Summary: C-GSZY, a Bell 206B operated by Apex Helicopters, was conducting survey operations near Timmins, Ontario, when the pilot reported abnormal noise and vibration in flight. While preparing for a precautionary landing, a loud noise was heard, followed by a loss of engine power to the main rotor. The pilot conducted an autorotation and landed downwind. During the landing, the main rotor contacted the tail boom, partially severing it approximately four feet forward of the tail rotor gearbox. There were no injuries reported. A post-landing inspection determined that the K-Flex driveshaft had separated aft of the main rotor transmission.

C-GITP, an Airbus A319-112 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting a non-revenue flight crew-only IFR flight ROU7096 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the climb phase at approximately 4000ft, the flight crew detected an electrical smoke odor, that was intensifying, but with no visible smoke. A quick reference checklist was executed, which prompted to apply ventilation that expelled the smoke. The aircraft returned to CYWG and was inspected by airport fire rescue personnel and found no abnormalities. An inspection by the operator's maintenance found a defective blower motor, which was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFMX, an amateur-built T51 Mustang replica, privately owned, was conducting a local flight from Windsor International Airport (CYQG), ON, with the pilot/owner and one passenger on board. During the approach, the pilot selected the landing gear down and observed indications showing the landing gear was down and locked. Upon touchdown, the main landing gear collapsed, and the aircraft slid to a stop on the runway. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The two occupants were not injured.

C-GTIM, a Swearingen SA-226TC operated by Skycare Air Ambulance as flight PHX274, was conducting a flight from Kingston Airport (CYGK), ON, to Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON. En route, the flight crew observed a decrease in No. 1 engine oil pressure, followed by illumination of the left engine oil pressure warning light. The crew shut down the affected engine and diverted to Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON, where a single-engine landing was completed successfully without further incident.

C-GLQC, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 operated by Porter Airlines Inc. as flight PTR2214, was conducting a flight from Ottawa Macdonald–Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. Just prior to descent into CYTZ, the flight crew observed smoke in the flight deck originating from behind the captain’s seat. The crew actioned the applicable quick reference handbook procedures and declared a MAYDAY. The flight crew reported that the smoke dissipated after the recirculation fan was selected to the OFF position. The aircraft landed uneventfully at CYTZ with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby. Maintenance inspection resulted in the replacement of the recirculation fan and the fan electronic module. Cabin air filters were also replaced.

C-GJWS, a Westjet B737-800 was operating flight WJA2565 from Vieuxfort/ Hewanorra International Airport (TLPL), Saint Lucia, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During preparation, before departure, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-GNBE, an Airbus A220 operated by Air Canada as flight AC744, was conducting a flight from San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the climb, the flight crew received a Left Brake Fail message. The crew actioned the applicable quick reference handbook (QRH) procedures and declared a PAN PAN while approaching CYYZ. The aircraft landed uneventfully with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) on standby. Maintenance inspection resulted in the replacement of the No. 3 brake assembly.

C-FEKJ, an Embraer 170-200 operated by Air Canada Express as flight AC8554, was conducting a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), NY. During the climb, at approximately FL220, the flight crew received a PACK 1 OFF message. The crew observed the cabin altitude continuing to increase, followed by a CABIN ALTITUDE warning. The crew initiated an emergency descent to FL010. While at that altitude, moderate icing was encountered, and an ANTI-ICE WING FAIL message was received. The crew declared a PAN PAN and continued the descent to 4 000 feet ASL to exit icing conditions. During the descent, the oxygen masks did not deploy.

C-GEWR, a Westjet Encore DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was being operated as flight WEN3614 from Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the climb to cruise altitude, the flight crew observed an amber warning light that indicated the left main landing gear door was open. The crew actioned the checklist in the quick reference handbook (QRH). The QRH noted that airspeed was restricted to 185 knots indicated airspeed (KIAS) and nose wheel steering would be inoperative on landing. The crew alerted air traffic control and company of the situation. As the aircraft approached CYYC, the crew declared a PAN PAN and advised that the aircraft would require a tow on arrival. The aircraft landed safely and was shut down on the taxiway. The aircraft was then towed to the gate. Maintenance found excessive air in the No. 2 hydraulic system. The left main landing gear solenoid sequence valve was replaced, and the No. 2 hydraulic system was bled. The landing gear retraction/extension system was function checked serviceable.

C-FIUA, an Air Canada B777-200 was operating flight AC34 from Sydney/Kingsford Smith Airport (YSSY), Australia, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-FNNH, an Air Canada B777-200 was operating flight AC34 from Sydney/Kingsford Smith Airport (YSSY), Australia, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, a cabin crew member sustained a minor injury and was unable to continue duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-GDEN, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was operating as flight WEN3458 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, with 4 crew members and 71 passengers on board. Shortly after reaching cruising altitude of flight level (FL)210, the flight encountered sudden and severe turbulence. As a result, control of the aircraft was briefly lost; the aircraft climbed and the autopilot disengaged. Two cabin crew members, who were standing, were injured after hitting the ceiling. The captain informed air traffic control and company dispatch. After landing, medical personnel assessed the injured cabin crew members, who were then taken to the hospital for further evaluation. No passengers were injured and no damage to the aircraft was reported.Maintenance reviewed the flight data recorder and determined the aircraft had been subjected to severe turbulence. A severe turbulence inspection was conducted, as per the aircraft maintenance manual, with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWJK, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was operating as flight WEN3675 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, under instrument flight rules, to Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC. While flying the RNP Y 15 approach to CYXT, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence and was difficult to control. The autopilot disconnected and flight crew initiated a missed approach which they flew by hand. The flight crew decided to divert to their planned alternate airport at Prince Rupert Airport (CYPR), BC, where they landed without further incident. There were no injuries reported. Maintenance reviewed the information from the flight data recorder and determined the aircraft had been subjected to severe turbulence. A severe turbulence inspection was conducted as per the aircraft maintenance manual with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FANB, an Air North Charter and Training Limited Boeing 737-400, was conducting flight ANT721 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen International Airport (CYXY), YT. On a previous flight the Constant Speed Drive (CSD) disconnected and the APU was required on subsequent flights for electrical power. During deicing at CYEG, deicing fluid was inadvertently sprayed into the APU inlet. The crew did not observe any abnormalities or unusual indications and continued to taxi to the runway after deicing was completed. The aircraft departed with the APU bleed air on and the engine bleed air off. During the initial climb the cockpit and cabin began to fill with smoke. The flight crew detected the smell of deice fluid within the cabin. The aircraft was reconfigured to use engine bleed air, and the smoke began to dissipate. The flight crew communicated with the lead flight attendant and made several passenger announcements to explain the situation to the passengers. The flight crew contacted ATC and continued to perform the quick reference checklist items. Once the smoke had cleared, the aircraft continued to CYXY without further incident. After landing at CYXY, company maintenance personnel found visual indications of glycol ingestion in the APU inlet and an SMS was filed to help prevent re-occurrence.

C-GCAM, a Westjet B737-8 was operating flight WJA2045 from Cozumel Aeropuerto International Airport (MMCZ), MX, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Air Traffic Control held the aircraft at FL270 in cloud for an extended period, during which ice formed on the windshield. After being cleared to climb, the aircraft exited the clouds through FL280 and shortly after experienced elevated engine vibrations (ENG 1 VIB 4.0, ENG 2 VIB 4.5). The flight crew completed the High Vibration Non-Normal Checklist. Reducing thrust slightly lowered ENG 1 vibration, while ENG 2 vibration decreased with a 20% N1 reduction however increased again with thrust increase. The crew declared a PAN PAN and leveled at FL310, where the Fan Ice Removal procedure was successfully completed. The flight then climbed to FL370 and continued uneventfully to destination.

C-FSFO, a Cessna 525B operated by AirSprint Inc. as flight ASP668, was preparing to depart Timmins/Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON, for Cleveland Hopkins International Airport (KCLE), OH, when it was struck by a de-icing truck during de-icing operations. The de-icing truck contacted the elevator and horizontal stabilizer, resulting in damage to both components.

C-FIVM, a Boeing 777-300 operated by Air Canada as flight AC859, was conducting a flight from London Heathrow Airport (EGLL), United Kingdom, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, when a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue performing safety-related duties.

C-GUFU, an Airbus A330 operated by Air Transat as flight TSC426, departed Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, bound for Cancún International Airport (MMUN), Mexico. During the climb, cabin crew detected a glycol odour in the cabin, which subsequently developed into a burning plastic smell. Shortly thereafter, the flight crew received an AIR ENG 2 BLEED FAULT ECAM message.The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and actioned the applicable quick reference handbook procedures for smoke, fumes, or avionics smoke. The aircraft diverted back to CYYZ, where it landed uneventfully and was met by aircraft rescue and firefighting.Maintenance personnel suspected that a significant quantity of glycol had been ingested by the No. 2 engine during de-icing.

C-FZZJ, a Seair Seaplanes Limited De Havilland DHC-2 MK.I floatplane, was being flown, under visual flight rules, from Vancouver International Water Aerodrome (CAM9), BC, to Ganges Water Aerodrome (CAX6), BC, with the pilot and 1 passenger onboard. Just after lift-off, through approximately 100 feet above ground level (AGL), the engine fuel pressure light flickered and the engine (Pratt & Whitney-USA, R-985-AN-14B) began running roughly. The pilot manually operated the fuel wobble pump and declared a PAN PAN. The engine regained full power at approximately 300 feet AGL. The pilot then requested a return to CAM9. The pilot continued to climb to 700 feet AGL before turning back and landing safely at CAM9. The aircraft was taxied to the dock. Maintenance inspected the fuel system including the carburetor filter, fuel lines, wobble pump, and fuel system check valve. The fault could not be duplicated and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKQM, a Porter Airlines Embraer ERJ 190-400, operating as POE606, had landed at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, on Runway 24R in a dual operation (6nm), exited on Taxiway C4 and came to an almost complete stop on Taxiway C4 short of the hold line without talking to the ground controller. The ground controller instructed C-GKQM to expedite and not to stop that side of the hold line as the south tower controller had C-FIVR, an Air Canada Boeing 777-333ER, operating as ACA890, starting its takeoff roll.There was a loss of separation at 23:50:36 when south tower controller cleared ACA890 for takeoff from Runway 24R while POE606 was on Taxiway C4 and still in the protected area of Runway 24R. POE606 was still moving at a reasonable speed at the time with the expectation they would comply with the south tower’s taxi instruction “Charlie Four join Delta”. However, POE606 slowed to a near stop in the runway protected area after ACA890 began their take-off roll. POE606 was clear of the protected area prior to ACA890 operating abeam C4.

C-GLQB, un Bombardier DHC-8-402 exploité par Porter Airlines, effectuait le vol PTR2464 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport Billy Bishop Toronto City - Toronto, ON (CYTZ) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 67 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, l'aéronef a rencontré un turbulence de sillage sévère à 5 milles derrières un gros porteur. À environ 1300 pi. ASL L'équipage a dû effectuer des mouvements important des contrôles de vol afin de briser le roulis vers la gauche. L'aéronef a éventuellement atterri à destination sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GDDR, a Westjet B737-8 was operating flight WJA2091 from Bahías De Huatulco International Airport (MMBT), MX, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned to remaining flight attendants.

C-GZQK, a Porter Airlines Embraer E190-400 aircraft, operating as flight PD591 from Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL, was boarding passengers at the gate when the flight crew received an intermittent APU FIRE EICAS message with an associated APU shutdown. The quick reference handbook procedures were followed and the crew called for a rapid deplanement and contacted ATC requesting aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF). After deplanement the ARFF reported no indications of fire or hot spots. After maintenance checked LOOP A and B, the input/output module and fire bottle were replaced.

N640GT, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Atlas Air was conducting IFR flight GTI8713 from Frankfurt-Hahn Airport (EDFH), Germany, to Boeing Field/King County International Airport (KBFI), WA. During cruise near southern Greenland at FL350, a left outboard spoiler deployed fully, resulting in a rolling action. The captain disconnected the autopilot and corrected the roll manually; recorded flight data revealed a maximum roll of 18.63 degrees before recovery. The flight crew declared a MAYDAY with ATC and advised company dispatch via ACARS that they were diverting to Keflavík International Airport (BIKF), Iceland. The spoiler remained extended until approximately FL190, then retracted. The aircraft landed safely at BIKF at 19:31Z. Maintenance replaced the #2 spoiler power control actuator and the 1L spoiler control module, with operational and leak checks satisfactory.

C-GSNR, a Beech 200 aircraft operated by SkyNorth Air was conducting an IFR flight from Winnipeg/James A. Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to the Island Lake Airport (CYIV), MB. The first officer was performing the takeoff. During the takeoff roll at 85 Kts, the aircraft experienced an un-commanded pitch-up, and the aircraft became airborne. The captain took control with heavy pitch and yaw forces required to maintain control of the aircraft. The autopilot was switched off but the pilot continued to have difficulty controlling the aircraft. An emergency was declared and the aircraft returned to CYWG for the RNAV 31 approach with vectors provided by ATC. Aircraft rescue and firefighting was standing by. The aircraft landed without further incident. The aircraft was placed in a heated hangar, and it was noted that water drained out of the elevator. The operator's maintenance department inspected the flight controls and autopilot system without finding any faults.

C-GGNZ, a Jazz Dash 8-400 was operating flight JZA807 from Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (KSEA), WA, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Shortly after take-off, the crew received a No. 2 engine FADEC warning (Full Authority Digital Engine Control). The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and elected to continue to destination. Both KSEA and CYVR centers were advised and an emergency was declared. The aircraft landed safely in CYVR with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby.

C-GUBO, an Air Transat A330-300 was operating flight TSC110 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France. During descent, a PAN PAN was declared after the crew received a Slat/Flap Control Computer fault (SFCC 1 & 2 INOP FAULT). The flight crew requested radar vectors for RWY 27L. The aircraft landed safely in LFPG without further incident.

C-GENU, a Westjet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400 was operating flight WEN3582 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, enroute to Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK. Shortly after takeoff, the flight crew attempted to raise the landing gear. The flight crew observed a right red main landing gear unsafe indication and a right door amber caution light. The flight crew actioned the quick response handbook and elected to return to CYEG. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency and aircraft rescue and firefighting personnel were placed on standby. The aircraft landed and taxied to the ramp without further incident.See also A25W0173 for similar event.

C-GENU, a Westjet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400 was operating flight WEN3562 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, enroute to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. Shortly after departure, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency due to a landing gear door issue. The flight crew elected to return to CYYC and landed safely. After landing, the aircraft was towed clear of the runway.

C-FSFP, an AirSprint Inc. Cessna 525B departed from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, enroute to Great Falls International Airport (KGTF), MT. Onboard were 3 pilots and 1 passenger. Shortly after takeoff, the flight crew attempted to retract the landing gear. When the landing gear was selected up, the red landing gear unlock light remained illuminated. The flight crew extended and retracted the landing gear multiple times to troubleshoot. When the landing gear lever was selected down (extended), the landing gear indication would show the wheels down and locked and the landing gear unlock light would extinguish. With the landing gear lever switch was selected to the up (retracted) position, the landing gear unlock light remained illuminated. As a precaution, the flight crew returned to CYYC and requested that aircraft rescue and firefighting personnel be placed on standby for the landing. The aircraft landed without further incident.The company is investigating.

C-GTIM, a Swearingen SA226-TC operated by SkyCare Air Ambulance, was conducting an IFR flight from the Pikangikum Airport (CYPM), ON, to the Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON. The first officer was flying the aircraft during the approach and landing at CYXL. While on the landing roll on Runway 16, the aircraft veered to the right. The captain took control to correct the right turn and the aircraft then veered sharply to the left. The captain continued the left turn and applied power to exit the left side of the runway surface to avoid hitting a runway light. The aircraft then taxied to the ramp.    The operator's maintenance department was notified of an erroneous left engine torque reading during a subsequent start attempt. Upon inspection, it was noticed that the left-hand propeller blades were out of track but had no damage to their leading edges. It was also noted that the right main landing gear tires exhibited skidding damage.

C-GFWX, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A320-214 was operating as ROU1511 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON. After landing on Runway 25 at CYQT and as the aircraft exited onto Taxiway D at low speed, the aircraft experienced a loss of control on the ground due to icy conditions. Steering and braking inputs were ineffective, and the aircraft slowly slid toward the edge of Taxiway D before coming to a stop on the edge of the taxiway.The flight crew notified ATC and requested a tow, as further movement under its own power was deemed unsafe. Engines were shut down, and the aircraft remained on APU power while airport personnel applied de-icing chemicals on the asphalt and prepared for towing. The aircraft was towed to the gate approximately 90 minutes after landing, without further incident.

C-GDRU, a Carson Air Limited Beechcraft King Air 300, departed Dease Lake Aerodrome (CYDL), BC, operating as flight CRN411, under instrument flight rules, to Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC. The aircraft was being flown on the ILS Y 33 approach to Runway 33 and the crew had the required runway visual reference approximately 150 feet above the approach minima. Due to snow and limited forward visibility, it was decided to leave the landing light turned off. At approximately 20 feet above ground, the crew realized the aircraft had drifted to the left of the runway centreline and made a correction. When the aircraft touched down, it began skidding on the wet runway surface and contacted a runway light on the left side. The aircraft remained on the paved surface and was taxied to the ramp. It was noted that the left inboard main landing gear tire was flat and airport personnel confirmed that a runway light had been damaged. There were no reported injuries.Maintenance personal determined that the tire’s sidewall was damaged. The tire was replaced, and an abnormal occurrence inspection was conducted which did not reveal any other damage. The aircraft returned to service the next day.

C-GTSW, a WestJet Airlines 737-8 (Max 8), was being operated as flight WJA1721, under instrument flight rules (IFR), from Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), CA, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. C-FCZF, an Air Canada Airbus A320-214, was being operated as flight ACA245 under IFR, from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to CYVR. Both airplanes were intercepting the final approach course for Runway 26R, the Airbus from the north and the Boeing from the south. The Boeing was vectored by air traffic control (ATC) to intercept ahead of the Airbus and a loss of separation occurred. The aircraft were separated by 600 feet vertically and 2.5 nautical miles laterally where 1000 feet vertically or 3 miles laterally was required. ATC issued airspeed instructions to both aircraft and the required separation was re-established. Both airplanes landed without further incident.

C-GYXL, a Perimeter Aviation Swearingen Fairchild SA-227-AC was operating from North Bay Airport (CYYB), ON, to Kitchener/Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON. On the take-off roll after V1, the flight crew received an airspeed mismatch message on the Garmin 700. Once airborne, both Air Data Computers were giving incorrect airspeed and altitude readings. The captain looked at the standby attitude and standby airspeed, and noticed the altitude showed incorrect information as well. The only information that was correct was their attitude information. The flight crew advised ATC, requested a return to the airport (CYYB) and for emergency services to be on standby for any issues upon landing. The crew consulted the quick reference handbook (QRH) and referenced the Garmin 700 airspeed mismatch. The QRH directed the flight crew to refer to the standby instruments however, this proved ineffective as these instruments were also providing incorrect information. The captain elected to switch to the alternate static source and both airspeed and altitude indications returned to approximate normal indications. The flight crew then briefed the approach back into CYYB and landed without any further incident.

C-FYJG, an Airbus A319 operated by Air Canada Rouge as flight ROU1910, was conducting a flight from Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the cruise phase of flight, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue performing safety-related duties. Cabin crew duties were redistributed in accordance with company procedures, and the flight was completed without further incident.

C-GHPD, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A312, operating as ROU1812 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Cancun International Airport (MMUN), Mexico, elected to return to CYYZ due to an odd smell in the cabin which resulted in flight attendants feeling sick. The flight crew declared an emergency and requested that EMS meet the flight on arrival. ROU1812 landed safely at 2353 EDT.

C-GEPF, experienced a Dutch roll condition in environmental conditions on the initial climb from Runway 24R out of Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. The severity reduced after the climb to cruise altitude. After landing at Montreal/Pierre E. Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, the aircraft was inspected, the yaw damper replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FBCL, a Carson Air Limited Beech (Textron) B300C (King Air 360ER), was conducting medevac flight CRN222, under instrument flight rules, from Dawson Creek Airport (CYDQ), BC, to Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC. Approximately 16 nautical miles southwest of CYDQ, climbing through 15 000 feet above sea level (ASL), the flight crew received a Door Unlocked CAS (crew alerting system) message. The Door Unsafe emergency checklist was actioned and the flight crew requested to descend to 11 000 feet ASL. The flight crew decided to continue to CYXS, requested the standing by of emergency response services, and landed without further incident.Maintenance personnel inspected, cleaned, and dried the door, switches and seals. The microswitch operation function tested serviceable in accordance with Aircraft Maintenance Manual 52-30-09 and 52-30-17. The aircraft was returned to service.

EI-EIK, an Airbus A333-302 aircraft operated by Aer Lingus UK, was conducting flight EUK94R from John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), NY, to Manchester Airport (EGCC), England. During cruise, the First Officer noticed the number 1 Integrated Driven Generator (IDG 1) was displaying higher temperature than IDG 2 however, was below the advisory limit. Soon after an ECAM advisory for IDG 1 appeared. The flight crew consulted the quick reference handbook, shed electrical loads, and shut off GEN 1 to affect IDG 1 cooling. When GEN 1 was reconnected the IDG 1 advisory quickly reappeared, and GEN 1 was again shut down. Because the APU was inoperative it was decided the flight was unsuitable for ETOPS and a PAN PAN was declared, and a diversion return to KJFK was coordinated with ATS. On initial approach to KJFK Runway 31 the flight crew also received ECAM messages for AIR ENG 1 BLEED FAULT and AIR ABNORMAL BLEED CONFIG. The crew carried out ECAM actions and landed at KJFK without further incident.  The deferred APU was rectified (low pressure fuel shut-off valve actuator) and the number 1 IDG was subsequently replaced, as was the number 1 engine bleed pressure regulating valve.

C-FCOO, a Carson Air Limited Beech (Textron) B300C (King Air 360ER), was conducting flight CRN333, under instrument flight rules, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC. On final approach for Runway 33, the flight crew selected the landing gear handle to the down position and observed that the left main landing gear did not indicate down and locked. The flight crew decided to conduct a missed approach to troubleshoot the issue. The aircraft returned for an approach to Runway 15 and, when the landing gear handle was placed in the down position, the indications showed that the gear was in the down and locked position. When power was reduced during the touchdown, the left wing dropped abruptly and the aircraft touched down hard on the left main landing gear. The aircraft then rolled to the right and the right propeller contacted the runway. After landing, the flight crew taxied the aircraft to the company hangar and shut down. The flight crew then noticed that the right propeller was damaged. There were no injuries.The aircraft was removed from service and repairs are ongoing.

C-GDSS, an Aerospatiale ATR 42-300 operated by Calm Air International LP, was conducting IFR flight CAV3001 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Rankin Inlet Airport (CYRT), NU, with 1 passenger and 4 crew members on board. Shortly after departure from CYWG, when the bleeds were selected ON during the climb sequence, the crew noticed a smell of smoke in the cockpit. After confirming with the flight attendant that the smell was present in the cabin, a decision was then made to return to CYWG as a precautionary measure. The crew requested a diversion back to CYWG where they landed safely without further incident. There were no injuries. There was no fire. There was no damage to the aircraft.The operator's maintenance consulted the aircraft fault isolation manual and high-power engine ground runs were performed for 10 minutes with no odour observed. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKQL, a Porter Airlines Embraer 190-400 was operating flight POE653 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, NV. During descent, the crew declared an emergency due to interoperable steering and inoperable vertical navigation. The aircraft continued to KLAS, where it landed safely without further issue. The aircraft taxied to the apron under its own power.

C-FKRF, a Westjet B737-8CT was operating flight WJA2113 from Licenciado Gustavo Diaz Ordaz International Airport (MMPR), Puerto Vallarta, MX, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. During cruise, the crew declared an emergency due to an electrical issue and elected to divert to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, where the aircraft landed safely.

N147LM, an Air Methods LLC Airbus Helicopters AS350-B2 helicopter, was conducting local maintenance test flights, under visual flight rules, from Langley Regional Airport (CYNJ), BC, with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. During an autorotation check, the pilot adjusted the fuel control lever and the engine (Safran-Turbomeca Arriel 1D1) subsequently flamed out. The pilot continued the autorotation to the ground and the helicopter bounced and slid on Runway 01 before coming to a stop on the runway. The emergency locator transmitter (ELT) activated on landing and the pilot turned it off. The pilot restarted the engine, and hover taxied the helicopter back to the hangar. Maintenance conducted a tail boom stinger deflection check with no faults found. The aircraft departed on another test flight for main rotor track and balance before being grounded for a hard landing inspection due to the ELT activation. During the inspection, maintenance found minor distortion in the fuselage center frames, rubbing on the aft firewall which was the result of tail rotor driveshaft contact, and cracks in the cabin sliding door supports. The scope for the aircraft repair and component overhaul is being evaluated.

C-FXMY, a Beechcraft BE200 operated by Keewatin Air LP, was conducting IFR flight KEW209 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Churchill Airport (CYYQ), MB with one passenger and 2 crew members on board. While in cruise at approximately 62 nautical miles north of CYWG, the crew noticed that the left fuel cap had dislodged, and fuel was leaking out of the tank. The flight crew declared an emergency and requested a diversion back to CYWG where they landed safely without further incident. There were no injuries. There was no fire. There was no damage to the aircraft.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft upon landing and found that the left main fuel cap tab was open. Upon further inspection, it was noticed that the left main fuel cap tab was looser than normal. The left main fuel cap was replaced and a precautionary inspection carried out of the anti-siphon valve and surrounding area and no faults were noted. The fuel cap function was checked for proper locking operation, and no further faults were noted.

C-GPGA, un Bombardier CL600-2B16 (Challenger 604) exploité par Acass Canada LTD. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Naples, FL (KAPF) avec 9 passagers et 3 membres d'équipage à bord. Au départ de CYUL, l’équipage a noté que l’indicateur d’angle d’attaque (AOA) n’était pas fiable, que les indices de basse et de haute vitesse sont apparues simultanément et que les paramètre de vitesse ne correspondaient pas à la combinaison attitude et puissance. L’aéronef est demeuré contrôlable en tout temps. En raison des paramètres non fiables, une urgence a été déclarée, et l’équipage a demandé à retourner à CYUL. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Suite à une inspection au sol, il a été déterminé que la sonde AOA était gelée.

C-GKIV, a Cessna C560 Citation Ultra operated by Keewatin Air LP, was conducting IFR flight KEW502 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Churchill Airport (CYYQ), MB, with one passenger and 2 crew members on board. At approximately 32 nautical miles north of CYWG, the crew heard a loud bang, then 2 more in close succession accompanied by some vibration. The crew also detected a burning smell in the cockpit. The flight crew declared an emergency and requested a diversion back to CYWG where they landed safely without further incident. There were no injuries. There was no fire. There was no damage to the aircraft.The operator's maintenance conducted a detailed inspection of the ACM installation and associated ducting and no visual defects were found. They also inspected the water separator sock and drains, with no faults noted. An inspection was carried out on all exterior structures, and no structural damage was observed. Upon speaking with the pilots, they suspected the loud noise could have originated from the nose section but were not certain. As a precaution, the aircraft was placed on jacks and gear swings carried out. Landing gear extension and retraction checked for operation, no faults found. An inspection was carried out on all flight controls and no defects were noted. Ground runs were carried out and general engine parameters found in normal range. Pressurization function, ECS function and tailcone bleed air system leak all checked okay. The operator's maintenance subsequently released the aircraft.

C-GSIA, a Northern Air Charter Beech 200 was operating as flight NLI373 from Peace River Aerodrome (CYPE), AB, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During cruise, approximately 112 NM SE of CYPE, the flight crew received a No. 2 engine fire warning. The flight crew determined that all engine indications were normal, and there was no visual sign of fire. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and shutdown the No. 2 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-41) as a precaution. A PAN PAN urgency was declared and the aircraft returned to CYPE and landed without incident. There were no injuries. Company maintenance inspected the RH engine, and no evidence of leaks or fire were noted. The RH engine fire detection system was inspected and tested serviceable. The aircraft was released for continued service.

C-FSWE, a WestJet Encore Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), departed Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, operating as flight WEN3455, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. N494UA, a United Airlines Incorporated, Airbus A320-232, was being operated as flight UAL2259 from San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA, under instrument flight rules, to CYVR. Both aircraft were turning onto the extended centreline for the final approach to Runway 26R when the required separation was lost; the Airbus was in front of the Dash 8. The separation between the aircraft was reduced to approximately 1.9 nautical miles (NM) laterally and 700 feet vertically when 3 NM laterally or 1000 feet vertically was required. Both aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GAIG, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit Ltée sous l'indicatif AIE705 allait effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de La Grande, QC (CYGL) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 67 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors du roulage sur la voir de circulation B1 suite à l’atterrissage sur la piste 06L, il y a eu une indication et une alerte sonore de feu moteur droit. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification d’urgence (QRH), a déclaré la situation à l’ATC et a ordonné l’évacuation de l’aéronef. Lors de l’évacuation, 3 passagers ont subi des blessures mineures. Les passagers ont été transportés au terminal en autobus. Les services de sauvetage et de lutte contre l'incendie des aéronefs (ARFF) n'ont trouvé aucune trace d'incendie.

C-GMXB, un Boeing 787-8 exploité par Westjet sous l'indicatif WJA8958 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL), à destination de l'aéroport de Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). Au départ de CYUL, l’indication de vitesse de droite n’indiquait aucune donnée, l’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification d’urgence (QRH) et a déclaré une d'urgence. Un retour à CYUL a été demandé et l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre. Suite à une inspection, le capteur d'angle d'attaque a été trouvé brisé.

C-FHRC, a de Havilland DHC-8-102 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting IFR flight PAG215 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Gods River Airport (CZGI), MB. While holding short of Runway 36 at CYWG, the crew simultaneously received a call from the flight attendant and the ground controller advising them that the aircraft was on fire. The captain checked all indications in the flight deck, but there was no fire indication. The crew completed the engine fire drills on the ground and triggered the extinguisher bottles, followed by an evacuation drill. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) responded and extinguished a fire in the right wheel assembly. All of the passengers were safely brought upwind of the aircraft where a headcount was completed. The passengers were then transported by bus to the terminal. There were no injuries. Damage was limited to the right-hand wheel assembly.The operator has submitted a Service Difficulty Report (SDR) with Transport Canada.

C-GLQK, un Dehavilland DHC-8-400 exploité par Porter Airlines sous l'indicatif POE2237, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW) à destination d’Halifax/Stanfield Int’l, NS (CYHZ) avec 68 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de la montée entre 10 000 pieds et le niveau de vol 180, le voyant « caution light » de la pompe hydraulique du moteur #2 s’est allumé. L’équipage a identifié qu’il ne restait plus de liquide hydraulique dans le système #2. L'équipage a suivi la liste de vérification d’urgence (QRH) et a déclaré une d'urgence. Ils ont effectué un palier au niveau de vol 210 et ont demandé un déroutement vers l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Après avoir effectué la sortie manuelle du train d’atterrissage, l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre et s’est arrêté sur la piste. Les moteurs ont été arrêtés et suite à une inspection par les services d’urgence, l’aéronef a été remorqué à la porte d’embarquement. Suite à une inspection, une fuite hydraulique a été identifiée au niveau du tuyau coudé au collecteur de filtre.

C-GLQO, un Dehavilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Porter Airlines sous l'indicatif POE1284, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Halifax/Stanfield Int’l, NS (CYHZ) à destination de Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport, ON (CYTZ) avec 25 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage à bord. En vol de croisière, environ 50 minutes avant la descente, une agente de bord n’a pas été en mesure de poursuivre ses fonctions en raison d’une condition médicale. L’équipage a informé l’opérateur afin d’avoir du support au sol à l’arrivée. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GJZA, un Dehavilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7891, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Moncton International, NB (CYQM) à destination d’Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW). C-GHQP un Dehavilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Hydro-Québec sous l'indicatif HYD144 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL), à destination de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY). L'espacement entre les deux aéronefs a été réduit à 600 pieds sur le plan vertical alors que l'espacement requis était de 1000 pieds. Les 2 appareils se sont posés sans encombre.

C-FWST, un MHI RJ Aviation ULC CL-600-2B19 (CRJ200) exploité par Pivot Airlines (2746904 ONTARIO INC) sous l'indicatif LSJ821, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Val d’Or (CYVO), Qc à destination de Rouyn-Noranda (CYUY), QC avec 17 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage sur la piste 26, il y a eu une indication de défaillance du système d’antiblocage et vers la fin du roulage lors de l’atterrissage, l’équipage a eu des difficultés à maintenir la maîtrise de l’aéronef. L’aéronef a dérapé et s’est immobilisé sur la piste. Des crevaisons au 4 pneus des trains principaux ont été constatés. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. La piste a été fermée jusqu’au lendemain à 15 :44z.

C-GHPQ, an Air Canada B787-8 was operating flight AC1348 from Licenciado Gustavo Diaz Ordaz International Airport (MMPR), Puerto Vallarta, MX, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. On departure the right landing gear and door disagree EICAS remained on. The crew declared a PAN PAN and requested a return to departure airport. The aircraft landed without incident and taxied to the gate.

C-FYKN, an Alkan Air Beech 350 was operating on a flight as AKN036 from Mayo Airport (CYMA), YT, to Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen International Airport (CYXY), YT. During final approach to Runway 14R, the flight crew selected the landing gear to the down position and only 2 green lights were observed with the nose landing gear light not illuminated and the landing gear selector handle light red. A missed approach was conducted, and the landing gear was cycled. Upon gear extension there was no change. The flight crew actioned the manual gear extension checklist, manually extended the landing gear and requested for aircraft rescue and firefighting to be on standby. The aircraft landed without further incident. Company maintenance is conducting troubleshooting.

C-GWLK, a WestJet Boeing 737-8 (MAX) was operating flight WS1086 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, NV. Shortly after takeoff a cabin crew member experienced a medical event. The cabin roles and responsibilities were reassigned to assure continued cabin service and safety. MedLink was contacted for guidance, and the incapacitated crew member was secured in the last row seating for landing. The crew member was released to their own care upon arrival and pursued medical treatment.

N287TA, a Tecnam P2012 Traveller operated privately was conducting flight from Reykavík Airport (BIRK), Iceland, to Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL. During the flight, the flight crew declared an emergency due to low oil pressure. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FJYW, an Aerospatiale ATR 42-300 aircraft operated by Calm Air International, was conducting an IFR flight from Rankin Inlet Airport (CYRT), NU, to Baker Lake Airport (CYBK), NU. During the final approach, a propellor configuration increasing its RPM to max for the landing phase was not achieved when selected. Further propeller control input was not responsive; the crew elected to conduct a missed approach and consult with maintenance. The second approach was unstable due to gusty wind conditions and mechanical turbulence resulting in a missed approach. The crew elected to return to CYRT and requested emergency services as a precaution and landed without further incident.The operator's maintenance inspected components related to the propellor control and replaced connectors and verified lock mechanisms, which corrected the faults. The aircraft was released into service following a successful test flight.

C-FXMY, a Beech B200 operated by Keewatin Air LP, was conducting IFR flight KEW209 from Thompson Regional Airport (CYTH), MB, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. During cruise flight a right-hand bleed air warning light illuminated. The crew elected to shut off the bleed air switch; eventually extinguishing the indication by the landing phase. The crew declared a PAN PAN as a precaution and landed without further incident. The operator's maintenance inspected the bleed air system and found damaged duct tubing leaking air. The damaged tubing was replaced and, additionally, the operator has opted to conduct an inspection of its entire fleet.

C-FTRX, a Pilatus PC-12/47 operated by Air Bravo Corp, was conducting IFR flight AB743 from Nakina Airport (CYQN), ON to Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON. During the climb near level off altitude, the number 1 generator was being displayed as off. The crew confirmed that the generator was not online. While monitoring the electrical system, the number 2 generator was not maintaining sufficient power. The crew elected to declare a PAN PAN for arrival into CYQT and landed without further incident. An inspection by the operator's maintenance found the number 1 generator had failed. The generator was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GITP, an Airbus A319-114 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting an IFR flight ROU1901 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. While in cruise at FL360 and approximately 105 nautical miles west of Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, with the air conditioning PACK 2 deferred under MEL, air conditioning PACK 1 faulted due to an overheat. The flight crew requested descent, during which a CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT warning appeared. The cabin altitude peaked at approximately 11 000 feet. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, actioned the quick reference handbook emergency descent and donned their oxygen masks. The flight crew requested a diversion to CYWG where they entered a hold to reduce the weight and landed safely without further incident. There were no injuries. There was no fire. There was no damage to the aircraft.Following the occurrence, the operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft in accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual and replaced the air cycle machine and #2 engine pressure regulating valve. Subsequent serviceability tests were carried out with satisfactory result. The aircraft was subsequently deemed to be airworthy and returned to service.

N752YX, an Embraer E175LR owned by United Airlines Inc. and operated by Republic Airways, was conducting flight RPA3664 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Washington/Dulles International Airport (KIAD), VA, USA. When the crew selected the landing gear up, the gear failed to retract. They declared an emergency and returned to CYOW where they landed uneventfully.

C-GBJZ, a DHC8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8430 from Timmins/Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the arrival while descending through 8000 feet at approximately 200 knots, the right-hand windshield cracked, followed by a 2nd crack within 30 seconds. The flight crew declared PAN PAN and requested priority. The flight landed uneventfully.

C-FMHJ, a privately operated Pilatus PC-12/47E, was conducting a flight, under instrument flight rules (IFR), from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC. N138UP, a United Parcel Service Company Airbus A300 F4-662R was being operated as flight UPS499, under IFR, from CYVR to Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport (KSDF), KY. C-FSDL, an Anderson Air Limited Learjet 45 was being operated as flight ADS75, under IFR, from Scottsdale Airport (KSDL), AZ, to CYVR. The Pilatus was sequenced to take off first from CYVR on Runway 26L by the Vancouver Tower South controller. Following departure, the controller then cleared the Airbus for immediate takeoff from Runway 26L. At that time, the Learjet was on final approach 2.6 nautical miles (NM) from the threshold of Runway 26L. The controller informed the flight crew of the Learjet that the separation between them and the Airbus taking off was reduced. The Learjet flight crew opted to conduct a missed approach. The controller instructed the Learjet to climb to 1000 feet above ground level and maintain the runway heading followed by a further climb and left turn. Once the Airbus was airborne and on the initial climb, the separation with the Pilatus ahead was reduced to 2 NM when 3 NM was required laterally and the separation with the Learjet behind was reduced to 0.9 NM laterally and 200 feet vertically when 5 NM laterally and 1000 feet vertically was required.

C-FJZD, a Jazz Aviation LP MHI RJ CL600-2D24 (CRJ900), was being operated as flight JZA7121, for a positioning flight under instrument flight rules, from Saskatoon/ John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with only 2 flight crew members onboard. During final approach to Runway 26L, the flight crew selected the landing gear down, but it did not extend. The crew executed a missed approach and actioned the checklist during which, the landing gear extended. The crew declared a PAN PAN and landed safely. They were met on the runway by aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) services. The aircraft was then taxied to the gate under its own power. Maintenance replaced the landing gear selector valve and the No. 3 hydraulic system priority balanced relief valve. The system was successfully function tested and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWRE, a Westjet Encore Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was being operated as flight WEN3420, under instrument flight rules, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC. During the initial climb, the aircraft encountered moderate icing and, after levelling off at flight level (FL) 250, the flight crew detected a vibration on the aircraft. The flight crew set the condition levers for maximum propeller RPM and, with no indication of de-ice system faults, declared a PAN PAN with air traffic control. The flight crew diverted to Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, and during the descent, the vibration began to decrease until it stopped at lower altitude. The aircraft landed safely and there were no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft. Maintenance carried out a balance check on both propellers and the vibration parameters were within the manufacturer maximum limits. The right propeller was adjusted to optimize the balance. The aircraft was returned to service.

C- FKSL, un Saab SF340B exploité par Pascan Aviation, effectuait le vol PSC483 selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR), au départ de l'aéroport métropolitain de Montréal (CYHU) à destination de l'aéroport international Jean-Lesage de Québec (CYQB), avec à son bord 3 membres d'équipage et 9 passagers. Peu après le décollage de CYHU, suite à l’activation des « bleed valves » l'équipage a perçu de la fumée dans le poste de pilotage. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée. Les paramètres moteurs étaient normaux et il ne semblait pas y avoir de fumée dans la cabine. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et a amorcé un retour vers l'aéroport de départ. L'appareil a atterri sans incident à CYHU.

C-FSKX, a Beechcraft King Air B200 operated by Keewatin Air was conducting flight KEW205M from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, with 2 pilots and 1 medical crew onboard. In preparation for departure, the flight crew elected to deice the aircraft. During the deicing process with the engines running, the flight crew received a #1 engine fire indication. The flight crew completed the engine fire checklist and shut down both engines and declared a MAYDAY with air traffic services. Aircraft rescue and firefighting responded and confirmed that there did not appear to be an engine fire. The aircraft was towed to the hangar for further inspection.Maintenance confirmed that there was no fire in the #1 engine compartment but the fire detector photocells were contaminated with deicing fluid, resulting in the false fire indication. The fire detectors were cleaned, a ground run was performed, and no further anomalies were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

A loss of IFR–IFR separation occurred involving C-GGFP, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight JZA8067 from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to Ottawa/Macdonald–Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, and C-FFOP, a Boeing 737-8 MAX operated by Air Canada as flight ACA7077 from St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL, to CYOW.While both aircraft were inbound for their respective approaches to Runway 14 at CYOW, separation was reduced to 1.8 NM laterally and 800 feet vertically. At the time of the occurrence, both aircraft were under the responsibility of the Montréal Area Control Centre (ACC).

C- GLJZ, un CRJ900 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8823, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau international, QC (CYUL) à destination de Ronald Reagan Washington National aux États-Unis (KDCA) avec 58 passagers et 4 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors que l'aéronef était en montée initiale, une indication d'une défaillance du FADEC gauche (Full Authority Digital Engine Control) est survenue. L'équipage déclaré un état d'urgence. L'appareil est revenu se poser sans encombre à CYUL.

C-FOAI, un DeHavilland DHC8-314 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE803  selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Umiujaq, QC (CYMU) à destination de l'aéroport de Kuujjuarapik, QC (CYGW) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 45 passagers à bord. Lors de l'approche à CYGW l'équipage a initié une approche interrompue due à de la turbulence sévère. Durant la manœuvre, des difficultés de contrôle de l'aéronef ont été rencontrées par l'équipage qui a alors décidé de rediriger le vol vers l'aéroport de Val-D'Or, QC (CYVO) où celui-ci a atterri sans encombre. il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GGFV, a Cessna 172N operated by the Waterloo Wellington Flight Centre, was being flown by a licensed pilot as the sole occupant during hours of darkness, and was conducting a cross-country flight from the Kitchener/Waterloo Airport (CYKF), ON, with the intention to conduct low approaches to the Sarnia Chris Hadfield Airport (CYZR), ON, and the St. Thomas Municipal Airport (CYQS), ON, before returning to CYKF. After making an approach to runway 24 at CYZR, the pilot conducted a go-around and rejoined the downwind for runway 24 for a second approach. During the downwind leg, the pilot directed their attention outside the aircraft to monitor traffic in the vicinity of the airport. Shortly afterward, the aircraft began to bank slowly to the right and the rate of descent increased. Over the next 30 seconds, the aircraft continued to descend and accelerate before striking a row of cedar trees. The aircraft impacted a field beyond the trees and overturned. The pilot exited the aircraft and was able to walk to a nearby road for assistance. The pilot received minor injuries, and the aircraft was destroyed. The ELT operated as designed.

C-GEWR, a Westjet Encore Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was being operated as flight WEN3485, under instrument flight rules, from Fort St. John Airport (CYXJ), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise flight, at flight level (FL)230, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence and the autopilot disengaged. The pilot-in-command assumed manual control of the airplane and was able to keep within approximately 300 feet of the assigned cruise altitude. Following the turbulence, the flight crew advised air traffic control of the event and the flight continued to the destination without incident. The 2 cabin crew members sustained minor injuries. Maintenance inspected the aircraft after the flight and no faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

N918XJ, un appareil de type CRJ900LR exploité par Endeavor Air, effectuait le vol EDV5197 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport LaGuardia (KLGA), NY, à destination l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC. En approche de CYUL, l’équipage a effectué une remontée en rapportant un problème technique non spécifié. Après avoir effectué des circuits d’attente, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence et l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre à CYUL.

C-FNNW, un Boeing 777-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA923 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Cacun, Mexique (MMUN) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau international, QC (CYUL) avec 14 membres d'équipage et 353 passagers à bord. Durant la croisière, il y a eu une indication de bas niveau de quantité de fluide hydraulique du système central. L'équipage a complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a déclaré une urgence. L'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre avec les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) déployés. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l'aéronef. L’aéronef a ensuite été remorqué au terminal. Le personnel de maintenance a ensuite effectué une inspection et remplacé un boyau du système antiblocage de l’unité de frein #10. L’aéronef a été remis en service.

C-FDUY, an Airbus A220-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting IFR flight AC339 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. While in cruise approximately 5 nm SE of North Battleford (CYQW), SK, the first officer became incapacitated. The captain declared a medical emergency and continued the flight, single-pilot to CYEG. The flight landed at CYEG without further incident. EMS was dispatched and met the aircraft upon arrival.

C-GYLQ, an Air Canada A220 was operating flight AC702 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson international Airport (CYYZ), ON, to LaGuardia Airport (KLGA), NY. On arrival to KLGA, light turbulence was encountered, and a cabin crew member was unable to continue their duties due to an injury.

C-FGDX, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was operating flight AC843 from Frankfurt Airport (EDDF), Germany, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. After takeoff a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to continue their duties.

C-FPQQ, un Beech B200 exploité par Keewatin Air effectuait le vol KEW213 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Pond Inlet, NU (CYIO) à destination de l'aéroport d'Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 3 passagers à bord. À 25Nm au nord de CYFB. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence due à des indications du moteur gauche qui fluctuaient. Le moteur s'est arrêté de lui-même peu après et l'aéronef a atterri à CYFB sans encombre à 21h48z. Un prélèvement de carburant fut effectué après-le vol et analysé et celui-ci s'est avéré contaminé par de l'eau.

C-GDEW, a DeHavilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting an IFR flight from the Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, to the Winnipeg/James A. Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. While on approach to CYWG, the flight crew selected gear down and they observed 2 green lights on the main gear and a red light on the nose gear. The flight crew completed a go-around and actioned the quick reference handbook (QRH). Upon completion of the QRH the crew received 3 green lights. The crew declared PAN PAN and got a new approach clearance from ATC. The flight subsequently landed safely and was met by emergency services on the ground. The operator's maintenance department found a nose landing gear door actuator leaking from the piston and hydraulic line unions were found loose and leaking from the actuator. The nose landing gear door actuator was replaced. Gear swings were carried out with no faults found.

C-GVNY, a Top Aces Inc. Dassault-Breguet / Dornier Alpha Jet Model A, was operating on a training exercise from Cold Lake/Group Captain R.W. McNair Airport (CYOD), AB. While in flight the pilot observed the left-wing fuel tank empty light illuminate at a much earlier time than anticipated. The pilot elected to return to base, suspecting a possible fuel leak, and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without further incident.

A7-BAC, un Boeing 777-300ER exploité par Qatar Airways, effectuait le vol QR763 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Doha, Qatar (OTHH) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 19 membres d'équipage et 298 passagers à bord. Au départ de OTHH un membre d'équipage cabine qui ne sentait pas bien et a été relevé de ses fonctions. Le vol a poursuivi sa route vers Montréal, QC (CYUL) et Medlink a été consulté et après du repos, le membre d'équipage a pu reprendre ses fonctions, mais en approche de CYUL celui-ci a recommencé à ne pas se sentir bien et a de nouveau été relevé de ses fonctions. Un état d'urgence a été déclarée et une demande a été faite à ATC pour les services médical d'urgence à l'arrivée. A7-BAC a atterri sans incident à 18h38 Z (13h38 HE) et les services médicaux d'urgence (SMU) ont accueilli l'avion à la porte d'embarquement.

C-FDGK, a Guardian Helicopters Inc. Airbus AS350B3, was on a local maintenance flight from Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB. While returning to CYBW, the pilot observed a governor light and an uncommanded increase in main rotor RPM. A decision was made to use the active runway to allow for a safer landing. The helicopter landed on the runway without issue. The helicopter was shut down and towed to the company's ramp for troubleshooting. Company maintenance installed a new bleed valve and Z1 card. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FMEN, a privately registered Cessna 180C, was operating from Maple Lane Farms Aerodrome (CMF2), AB, to a farm field 9.3 nm SW of Bonnyville Aerodrome (CYBF), AB. The snow in the field was deeper than anticipated and the aircraft nosed over and came to rest upside down. The lone occupant was not injured and egressed on his own from the aircraft. A wingtip, the propeller, and the top of the vertical fin were damaged.

C-FEJY, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA7948 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Deer Lake Regional Airport (CYDF), NL. On approach to Runway 25 at CYDF, the aircraft encountered unexpected turbulence and very strong wind gusts, and the crew decided to go around. On the second approach the aircraft became difficult to control due to variations in speed and altitude caused by the unexpected turbulence and the crew received a windshear warning. On both approaches the aircraft also sustained flap overspeed exceedances. The crew elected to carry out a missed approach and divert to Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. The aircraft landed at CYHZ without further incident, and without any reported injuries.Maintenance carried out all recommended inspections based on the recorded flight performance variations and exceedances, with no faults or damage found.

C-GKQQ, an Embraer ERJ 190-400 operated by Porter Airlines Limited as flight POE441, was en route from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, when the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to an avionics failure. The flight crew elected to return to CYYZ, where the aircraft landed without further incident with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby.

C-FGKN, an Airbus A321-211 operated by Air Canada as flight ACA163, departed Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, bound for Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. Shortly after departure, the flight crew requested to stop the climb due to a hot brake indication. The crew subsequently declared a PAN PAN due to being overweight for landing and returned to CYYZ, where the aircraft landed with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) on standby.

C-GDUZ, a Boeing 767-300 operated by Air Canada as flight ACA7253, was en route from Jorge Chávez International Airport (SPJC), Lima, Peru, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, when the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to a leading-edge slat asymmetry indication.The flight crew discontinued the approach to complete the applicable checklist and subsequently landed on Runway 05 at CYYZ without further incident.

C-GUZJ, un Cessna 152 exploité par Orizon Aviation, effectuait un vol de formation selon les règles de vol à vue de l'aéroport Jean Lesage Intl de Québec, QC (CYQB) à destination de L'aéroport de Montmagny,Qc (CSE5) avec 1 élève pilote (assis à droite) et 1 passager à bord. Lors de l'atterrissage, l'aéronef a touché le sol enneigé une quarantaine de pieds avant le début de la piste 06. La roue de nez a arraché et l'aéronef a terminé sa course le nez contre le sol peu après. Le capotage moteur, le pare-brise et l'hélice on aussi étés endommagés. Les deux occupants on subit des blessures légères et ont été pris en charge par les services médicaux.

C-FVLX, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was operating flight AC36 from Brisbane Airport (YBBN), Australia, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. A cabin crew member became incapacitated and were unable to continue their duties.

C-GARO, an Airbus A319-114 operated by Air Canada Rouge as flight ROU1675, was en route from Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, when the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to an electrical or plastic burning odour in the flight deck. The aircraft landed without incident at CYYZ with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby.Maintenance inspected the aircraft in accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual and identified the source of the odour as a blower fan. The blower fan was replaced, and subsequent serviceability tests were completed with satisfactory results.

C-FYJH, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was operating flight ROU16557 from Tampa International Airport (KTPA), FL, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, unexpected turbulence caused a cabin crew injury, rendering them unable to perform safety-related duties. The duties were redistributed among the remaining cabin crew members and the flight continued to its destination without further incident.

C-GIBH, an Aero L-39C operated by the International Test Pilot School as flight SA62, reported engine-related issues and requested a landing at London International Airport (CYXU), ON. SA61, a second ITPS aircraft operating in formation with SA62, declared an emergency on behalf of SA62 and requested aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) to be on standby. SA62 landed on Runway 33 at CYXU without incident and taxied to Apron 3.A post-flight maintenance inspection identified a bleed air leak in the de-ice system. The de-ice system bleed air outlet port flange was found to be missing an attaching screw, and the gasket between the engine case and the pipe elbow had displaced and was leaking. The gasket was replaced, and the fuel-oil heat exchanger (FOHE) and fuel control unit (FCU) were bled as a precautionary measure.

C-GYRS, un Boeing 787-9 exploité par Westjet sous l'indicatif WJA33 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Léonard-de-Vinci de Rome Fiumicino, Italie (LIRF) à destination de l'aéroport de Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) avec 13 membres d'équipage et 321 passagers à bord. À environ 60 miles nautiques au sud de CYCY, l'appareil est entré dans une zone de fortes turbulences alors qu'il était au niveau de vol 380 avec des variations de vitesses de 25 noeuds et d'altitude de ±300 pieds. L'équipage a tenté de réduire la vitesse et s’est retrouvé en survitesse malgré l'application d'aérofreins. L'équipage a tenté de rejoindre le centre de contrôle d'Edmonton sans succès à de multiples reprises pour demander une réduction d'altitude de croisière pour le niveau de vol 360. Étant sans réponse du centre de contrôle et après avoir vérifié que la voie était libre en consultant le système d'avertissement du trafic, les pilotes ont déclaré une urgence et amorcé une descente d'urgence. Les turbulences sévères ont cessé à l'atteinte du niveau 370. Le pilote automatique est resté en fonction à tout moment de l'épisode. Le vol s'est ensuite poursuivi pour atterrir sans encombre à destination. Une inspection non planifiée suite à des turbulences sévères a été effectuée et l'appareil remis en service.

C-FYAI, un DeHavilland DHC8-314 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE2724  selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 34 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, l'aéronef a subi une défaillance de la pompe hydraulique du moteur droit après avoir initié la remontée du train d'atterissage. De plus, les portes de train sont demeurés ouvertes et déverrouillées. L'équipage a alors décidé de revenir à CYUL et a déclaré une urgence. Après avoir déployé le train d'atterrissage en mode alternatif, l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre sur la piste 24R à 17h11z, après quoi l'aéronef a dû être remorqué jusqu'à son hangar. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-FVNF, a Boeing 787-9 operated by Air Canada as flight ACA0057, was en route from Dubai International Airport (OMDB), UAE, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, when a flight attendant sustained an injury and was unable to continue safety-related duties.

C-FAMS, un Piper PA31-325 Navajo exploité par le Collège d'enseignement général et professionnel de Chicoutimi (CQFA), effectuait un vol local de formation selon les règles de vol aux instruments à partir de l'aéroport St-Honoré/Chicoutimi, QC (CYRC) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 2 passagers à bord (élèves observateurs). Lors de la remontés suivant une approche d'entraînement à l'aéroport de Bagotville ,QC (CYBG), l'indication de pression d'admission du moteur gauche (Avco-Lycoming LTIO-540-F2BD, s/n L253568C)a rapidement baissé et est reste figée. Une légère diminution de la puissance a été observée et le moteur s'est mis a vibrer légèrement. Ces paramètre se sont maintenus jusqu'à CYRC où le pilote a pris la décision d'arrêter le moteur par précaution et a déclaré un Pan Pan. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre et il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GBAP, a Coywolf Aviation Pilatus PC-12 was operating flight WPK521 from Richmond International Airport (KRIC), VA, to Savannah/Hilton Head International Airport (KSAV), GA. An emergency was declared due to a de-icing equipment issue. The crew elected to divert to Myrtle Beach International Airport (KMYR), SC, where they landed safely.

C-FEKH, a Jazz Aviation Embraer ERJ 170-200 was operating flight JZA870 from Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (KDCA), VA, to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. Right after departure out of KDCA, a slat fail caution message was received. Flight was continued to CYOW and emergency was declared on descent into CYOW. Flight landed uneventfully.

C- FUWS, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-700, was operating as flight WJA1462 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), CA. Shortly after take-off a cabin crew member experienced a medical event. Cabin responsibilities were reassigned and the flight continued to its destination. The cabin crew member was transferred to emergency medical services upon arrival.

C-GPQO, a DeHavilland DHC-8-314 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting an IFR flight from Winnipeg/James A. Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to the St. Theresa Point Airport (CYST), MB. As C-GPQO was descending to CYST, Thunder Bay Radio advised the crew of C-GPQO that C-FTYO, a Beaver Air Services (dba Missinippi Airways) Beech 200, was departing the Island Lake Airport (CYIV), MB, with a destination of CYWG. At about 8000 feet ASL in uncontrolled airspace, the flight crew of C-GPQO were advised by the TCAS of "TRAFFIC". The captain put the aircraft into heading mode and steered the first officer's heading bug to an easterly direction. Soon after, the TCAS advised "CLIMB". The required climb gradient was 2000 fpm. The captain took control and pitched the aircraft "nose up" to avoid the traffic. Once clear of the traffic, the captain continued the descent to CYST and handed control back to the first officer. The captain of C-GPQO subsequently tried to contact C-FTYO on 126.7 MHz, without response. C-GPQO landed safely at CYST.

C-GIAF, a Conair Group Limited Cessna 525B (Citation CJ3), was being operated as flight FGD116 from Spokane International Airport (KGEG), WA, U.S., under instrument flight rules to Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, with 1 flight crew member and 1 passenger on board. During approach to CYXX, when the landing gear was selected down, the left main gear down indicator light did not illuminate. A missed approach was conducted and the applicable checklist was performed. An emergency was declared as a precautionary measure. The aircraft landed without further incident. Following the flight, the left main landing gear light bulb was found to be burnt out. The lightbulbs for all gear lights were replaced and the system was function tested with no faults found.

C-FGEW, an amateur built Gray RG12 (Piper 12 replica) was attempting to land in high winds on runway 28 at Southwest Michigan Regional Airport (KBEH), MI, and winds at the time were from 240° at 27 knots, gusting 43 knots. The aircraft veered off the runway and became inverted. The pilot was transported to the hospital for evaluation. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FIOH, a Swearingen SA227-AC aircraft operated by Skycare Air Ambulance, was conducting an IFR flight from the Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON, to the Opapimiskan Lake Aerodrome (CKM8), ON. While on the landing roll, the aircraft began to veer to the left when the nose gear touched down. At 60 knots, the captain attempted to regain directional control with an increase in left engine power; however, the aircraft continued to steer off the runway. The aircraft came to rest to the left of the runway surface. It was reported that the green nose wheel steering light remained illuminated steady green during the event.The aircraft was ferried to the operator's base at Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON. During troubleshooting, it was discovered that the servo valve for the nose wheel steering was faulty. The servo valve was replaced, and the nose wheel steering system was tested with no further faults.

C-GEND, a Harbour Air Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-3T (Turbo Otter), was being operated as flight HR321 from Vancouver Harbour Aerodrome (CYHC), BC, under visual flight rules, to Victoria Harbour Airport (CYWH), BC, with 1 flight crew member, and 8 passengers on board. During cruise, the engine (Pratt & Whitney-Can, PT6A-34) oil pressure indication suddenly dropped to 72 psi, the minimum operating oil pressure is 85 psi. The pilot declared a PAN PAN urgency to air traffic control and diverted to Vancouver International Water Aerodrome (CAM9), BC, approximately 10 nautical miles northeast. The engine oil pressure indication increased and stabilized at 81 psi prior to landing. The aircraft landed at CAM9 without further incident.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and conducted troubleshooting in accordance with the Pratt & Whitney maintenance manual. They inspected and replaced the oil transducer, adjusted the oil pressure, and replaced the oil pressure shim. They then tested the engine and could not duplicate the low oil pressure indication.

C-GDFE, a Diamond Flight Centre Diamond DA40-180 and C-FXZI, (callsign Stallion 36), an International Test Pilot School Canada Aero L-29 Delfin had a near miss within Class C controlled airspace while both aircraft were on straight-in approaches to the active Runway 15 at the London International Airport (CYXU), ON.C-GDFE, flown by a solo pilot, was established along the extended centerline of Runway 15 at 1900 feet ASL.
