Stallion 36, with an instructor pilot in the rear seat and a student test pilot flying in the front seat, was returning from the northwest but displaced well left of the extended centerline to Runway 15. As Stallion 36 approached, the student test pilot could not identify the runway given the sunlight conditions and snow-covered terrain. The instructor pilot, realizing the aircraft was improperly positioned, took control at approximately 4.5 nm and initiated a right turn to realign the aircraft. The turn created separation from downwind traffic but placed Stallion 36 on a converging track with C-GDFE on approach. During the turn, the student test pilot identified C-GDFE inside their turn and informed the instructor pilot.Multiple radio communication issues followed, including garbled and simultaneous transmissions, misidentification of the Stallion 36 callsign and aircraft type, and use of non-standard phraseology. Various traffic warnings and instructions to both aircraft to change course were issued and eventually, evasive instructions were issued with C-GDFE being told to descend, and Stallion 36 instructed to climb. NAV CANADA radar data indicates the two aircraft were at the same altitude as they converged. C-GDFE’s descending turn and Stallion 36’s climb increased the vertical separation to 200 feet and then 400 feet. As Stallion 36 passed behind C-GDFE, they came within a horizontal separation of approximately 1200 to 1800 feet. At no point did any pilot confirm visual contact with the other aircraft over the radio. Following the near miss, both aircraft were instructed to exit the control zone. They both subsequently returned and landed safely.

C-GWJG, a Boeing 737-700 operated by WestJet, experienced increased vibration during the takeoff roll from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. After landing gear retraction, a Leading Edge Flap Transit light illuminated. The flight crew notified ATC of a possible blown tire and requested vectors. The flight crew completed the applicable checklist, coordinated with maintenance and dispatch, and briefed the cabin crew before entering a holding pattern to burn fuel in preparation for a return to CYYZ. ATC subsequently advised the crew that tire debris had been observed on the runway. The cabin was prepared for a non-normal landing.The aircraft landed below maximum landing weight and stopped on the runway for inspection by emergency vehicles. Due to damage, the aircraft was towed to the gate. Damage was found to the right inboard tire, wheel well area, and the right inboard leading-edge and aft flaps.

C-FHNI, a Canadian North Boeing 737-700 was operating as flight AKT1700 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Fort MacKay/Horizon Aerodrome (CYNR), AB. After departure, while climbing through 7000 feet ASL, the lead cabin flight attendant observed a slowly increasing smell of burning plastic; a sweet smell in the cabin. The FWD lavatory smoke detector also activated. No visible smoke was observed. The flight crew levelled the aircraft at 8000 feet and actioned the quick reference handbook checklist. An emergency was declared and the aircraft returned to CYYC. During the return, the smoke smell slowly began to dissipate. The aircraft landed uneventfully, stopped on the runway and was met by aircraft rescue and firefighting before returning to the apron.Company maintenance inspected the APU inlet, both pack inlets and coalescer bags for contamination; nothing was found. An engine ground run was performed with no smoke or smell of deice fluid noticed throughout cabin or lavatories. All lavatory smoke detectors tested OK. The aircraft was released for continued service.

C-GNLE, un Boeing 737-248C exploité par Nolinor Aviation, effectuait le vol NRL942 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Mirabel, Qc (CYMX) à destination de l'aéroport de Val-D'Or, Qc (CYVO). Une vibration a été ressentie au moment du toucher du train principal sur la piste. Le contrôle directionnel a été maintenu et un freinage normal effectué. Les vibrations se sont fait sentir jusqu'à l'arrêt complet de l'appareil sur la piste. L'équipage a informé les autorités de l'aéroport qui ont dépêché les services d'urgence qui ont alors informé l'équipage que le train d'atterrissage droit était endommagé. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé et les passagers ont été débarqués normalement par la porte avant et ont pris place à bord d'un autobus qui les a transportés jusqu'au terminal.

N411DX, a Delta Airlines Airbus A330-900, operating as DAL162 from Minneapolis-St Paul International Airport (KMSP), MN, to Amsterdam Schiphol Airport (EHAM), Netherlands, had a fuel leak enroute while in Canadian airspace. The crew conducted a precautionary engine shutdown, declared an emergency, diverted and landed safety at Detroit Metro Wayne County Airport (KDTW), MI.

C-GMSY, un Learjet 45 exploité par Aviation Starlink inc. sous l'indicatif TLK822 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ). Lors de la montée à environ 13 000 pieds ASL, une réduction du régime du moteur droit (Honeywell TFE731-20BR-1B) est survenue et le système d'affichage des paramètres moteurs et d'alerte de l'équipage (EICAS) a généré le message « R ENG Computer Fail ». L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et est revenu se poser sur la piste 24R à CYUL sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’aéronef.

C-GUPG, an Air Canada Airbus BD-500-1A11 (A220), operating as ACA454, was enroute from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, when the flight crew declared an emergency due to smell of fumes in the flight deck. The crew elected to return to CYYZ where the aircraft landed safely at 1956 UTC.

C-GCWJ, a Boeing 737-700 operated by Westjet Airlines Inc., was operating as flight WS4037 from Fort MacKay/Firebag Airport (CYFI), AB, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. After boarding was complete, ground personnel reported what appeared to be flashes or sparks in the vicinity of the horizontal stabilizer. The flight crew shut down both engines, ordered a rapid deplanement of the aircraft out the main cabin door and requested assistance from aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF). All passengers de-planed without incident. Observation concluded that the apparent flashes were caused by snow and de-icing fluid interacting with the logo light. Company maintenance reviewed video and pictures to confirm the assessment. The passengers were boarded and the flight continued without further issues.

C-FNPJ, a Boeing 767-316 aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd., was conducting flight CJT2457 from Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While configuring for approach into CYYC, the flight crew observed a TRAILING EDGE FLAP DISAGREE message. The flight crew completed the appropriate checklist, declared a PAN PAN, and conducted a flap 20 landing without issue. Company maintenance completed troubleshooting and found a right-hand outboard flap rotary actuator overload trip indicator (#8) tripped. The indicator was reset, and the flap system was checked serviceable. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GFYW, a Sealand Flight Limited Cessna 172M, departed Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, on an unscheduled flight of which the aircraft owner was unaware. Only the pilot was on board. The aircraft departed Runway 34 at CYCD at approximately 0300 Pacific Standard Time (PST) and collided with terrain at approximately 0304 PST. The pilot received fatal injuries. The aircraft was destroyed. The aircraft emergency locator transmitter (ELT) did not produce a signal that was relayed to the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre.The occurrence pilot was a Sealand employee. The pilot held a commercial pilot license with a class 3 instructor rating, and a valid category 1 medical. The pilot had approximately 511 hours total documented flight time.Video evidence showed that the aircraft took off without the pilot activating the aerodrome lighting. After takeoff, the aircraft climbed on runway heading for approximately 35 seconds before turning west. The aircraft then traveled 4.3 nautical miles (NM) west before it impacted terrain. A security camera, located approximately 550 m from the crash site, recorded the sound of the aircraft engine at high rpm, with engine sound increasing as the aircraft approached the ground. The audio recording indicated the aircraft struck terrain at 0304:31 PST. The aircraft wreckage was found approximately 4.5 NM WNW of CYCD near a public street and several houses. Wreckage was consistent with a high energy impact, and the aircraft propeller showed signs that it was producing power at the time the aircraft collided with terrain. The smell of aviation fuel was noted at the site, and it was determined that the occurrence aircraft had been fully fueled following its previous flight, the day before the occurrence. The investigation could not establish control continuity due to the degree of damage suffered by the aircraft. The aircraft ELT was found separated from the airframe at the crash site, with the ELT switch in the off position, but it is not known when or how the switch came to be in that position.

C-GPCR, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited Beech 1900D, departed Bella Bella (Campbell Island) Airport (CBBC), BC, on flight PCO1294, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew members and 19 passengers on board. Before departure, the aircraft was parked in conditions of heavy rain. During the climb to cruise altitude, the elevator trim was set for a nose-up attitude. Upon reaching their cruise altitude of flight level (FL) 210, the crew found that they could not adjust the elevator trim. The aircraft could not be trimmed electrically nor manually to achieve a cruise attitude. The crew suspected pitch trim had frozen. Significant force was required on the controls to maintain level flight and to prevent the aircraft from climbing. The flight crew requested a lower altitude and initiated a descent from FL210. Pitch trim was found to be functional below the freezing level, and the aircraft continued to CYVR without further incident under visual flight rules, at approximately 3000 feet above sea level.Following the flight, the aircraft elevator trim tabs were lubricated and tested for serviceability before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FYJE, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was operating flight ROU1833 from V.C. Bird International Airport (TAPA), Antigua and Barbuda, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, fumes were reported in the cabin affecting multiple flight attendants. One flight attendant became unresponsive during taxi-in after diversion to Punta Canada International Airport (MDPC), Dominican Republic. Medical assistance was provided on arrival. The flight was cancelled and the passengers were deplaned.

C-GFCH, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A320-214 was operating flight ROU1702 from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), NV, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During taxi out of KLAS, fumes were reported in the cabin and persisted during the climb, affecting both passengers and crew. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks and PAN PAN was declared. The flight diverted back to KLAS, where it landed overweight without further incident.

C-FULJ, a Westjet B737-8 was operating flight WS2615 from Licenciado Gustavo Diaz Ordaz International Airport (MMPR), Puerto Vallarta, MX, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-FERF, un Piper PA-23-250 exploité par Cargair Ltée. effectuait un vol local de formation depuis Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU), QC selon les règles de vol à vue avec un instructeur et un élève à bord. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, des flammèches sont apparues sous le moteur de droite (Avco Lycoming IO-540-C4B5).  L’instructeur a demandé un retour à CYHU, a déclaré un état d’urgence et a fermé le moteur droit. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-FCJZ, un CRJ900 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8962, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Chicago O’Hare, É.-U. (KORD) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau international, QC (CYUL) avec 64 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’aéronef était en descente à CYUL, une indication de défaillance des déporteurs intérieurs et des spoilerons intérieurs est survenue. L’équipage déclaré un état d’urgence. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 06L.

C-GNLQ, un B737-33A exploité par Les Investissements Nolinor Inc. sous l’indicatif NRL630 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à destination de Port Meunier, QC (CYPN) avec 36 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en croisière au niveau de vol 230, un problème d’instrument de vol du côté du commandant est survenu. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et est revenu se poser sur la piste 24 à CYQB sans encombre.

C-FSLU, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight AC518 from Daniel K. Inouye International Airport (PHNL), Honolulu, HI, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-FRQM, a Jazz Embraer 175 was operating flight JZA542 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to LaGuardia Airport (KLGA), NY. On the descent into KLGA the crew received a MAU 3B FAIL (Modular Avionics Unit). Message relayed by NY Center as ACARS was not functioning (to and from/ no ACK). The crew elected to return CYYZ (ALTN), for longer runway (aircraft was also carrying 1 REV INNOP). Declared PAN PAN inbound CYYZ. Flight landed without any further issue.

C-GGNY, a Jazz Aviation LP DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was being operated as flight JZA810 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (KSEA), WA, U.S. under instrument flight rules. Shortly after liftoff, the flight crew selected the landing gear handle to the up position. The amber light in the landing gear handle remained illuminated and the landing gear inoperative caution light illuminated. The flight crew communicated with company dispatch and maintenance, actioned the appropriate checklists, and conducted an alternate landing gear extension procedure. The flight crew decided to return to CYVR and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed safely with aircraft rescue and firefighting crews on standby. The aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.Maintenance crews inspected the proximity sensor electronic unit (PSEU) and determined there was a fault with the nose landing gear 2 (nglk2) proximity sensor. They replaced and rigged the alternate nose landing gear harness assembly in accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual. The harness tested serviceable and the PSEU fault codes cleared. Landing gear primary retraction and extension system were checked to be serviceable and service difficulty report (SDR) 20251125009 was submitted. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GLQH, a De Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight PTR2616 from Timmins Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. While on the ground at CYTS, a ''Flap Power'' caution light illuminated. The flight crew successfully reset the indication and took off with no further indications. After takeoff, the same caution light re-illuminated, and the flaps became stuck at the 0 position. The crew subsequently executed the ABNORMAL FLAP LANDING procedure from the quick reference handbook (QRH), notified Air Traffic Control (ATC), declared an emergency, and diverted to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. PTR2616 landed safely at CYYZ runway 23 with no flaps, with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) vehicles standing by. ARFF inspected the aircraft, and the brake temperature was found to be normal. Fluid was observed leaking from the engines and the bottom of the fuselage, resulting in the closure of Runway 23 and the redirecting of approximately 15–20 departing aircraft to Runway 33R. The fluid, initially suspected to be hydraulic fluid, was later determined to be de-icing fluid. The aircraft was towed to the gate with all passengers and crew remaining on board. An inspection from maintenance revealed that the flap lever was not sending proper data to the flap control unit (FCU). The flap lever module was replaced, and the system was tested serviceable, restoring proper data transmission.

C-GXZM, an Air Tractor AT-502B, operated by Zimmer Air Services Inc, was performing a VFR Flight from Dauphin/Lt. Col W.G. (Billy) Barker, VC Airport (CYDN), MB to Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON. During touchdown on Runway 34 at CYXL, the aircraft veered to the left and departed the paved surface of the runway. The aircraft did not sustain any damage, and it was taxied to the apron without further incident; however, it was slightly difficult to steer due to an apparent brake failure of the right brake.The aircraft was inspected by the operator's maintenance for damage, and none was found. The right brake reservoir was found empty. The reservoir was refilled to normal level and taxi tests confirmed the brakes worked as expected. The aircraft was released for a flight to the operator's home base where further inspection revealed a defective O-ring on the right wheel brake assembly causing a slow leak. The part was replaced.

C-GELU, an Air Canada B737-8 completed flight AC583 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport CYUL), QC, to George Bush Intercontinental/Houston Airport (KIAH), TX. At the gate, ground crew advised pilots of flames in number 2 engine tail pipe after shutdown. Passengers completed a rapid deplanement. The crew completed all checklists, including engine motor procedures and the flames were extinguished.  ATC was advised and emergency services attended to inspect the aircraft.

C-FREQ, a Chartright Cessna 560 was operating flight HRT421 from George Bush Intercontinental Airport (KIAH), TX, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, the crew declared an emergency due to a door indicator light and elected to divert to Nashville International Airport (KBNA), TN, where the aircraft landed safely.

C-GXNS, a Cessna 172N operated by The Toronto Shuttle Inc., was conducting a local VFR flight from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. ATC instructed C-GXNS to pull up, go around, proceed toward the Western Gap, and remain north of Runway 26 while on right base. These instructions were issued to ensure appropriate sequencing ahead of JZA7921, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 (C-GJZA) operated by Jazz Aviation LP on an IFR approach to Runway 26.Contrary to the instruction, C-GXNS began an eastbound turn toward JZA7921. The Toronto City (TZ) controller identified the developing conflict and immediately issued deconfliction instructions to both aircraft. At the closest point, separation was reduced to 1.7 NM laterally and 200 feet vertically. Nav Canada reported the required separation was 1 mile laterally or 500 feet vertically.

C-GFJM, a WestJet Boeing 737-8 was operating flight WJA2965 from Cancún International Airport (MMUN), MX, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During takeoff on runway 12R in MMUN, the flight crew felt an unusual bump. The Tail Strike Non-Normal Checklist (NNC) was reviewed and it was decided to continue to CYUL. During the post-flight walk around, it was discovered that the tail skid shoe had been scraped and the cartridge was slightly compressed. Maintenance replaced the skid shoe and tail skid cartridge.

C-GLQZ, a DeHavilland DHC-8-402, operated by Porter Airlines Inc., was conducting flight PTR2487 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Montreal Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. The flight crew rejected the takeoff at 50 KIAS when, after applying takeoff power, the No. 1 engine produced 85% torque while the No. 2 engine produced 106% torque. An emergency was declared with Air Traffic Control (ATC), and the aircraft taxied back to the gate without further incident.A maintenance inspection and data review revealed that engine No. 2 exceeded 100% torque (peaking at 106%) for approximately 6 seconds while the main propeller (NP2) RPM remained fixed at 850. This condition required replacement of the right-hand Engine Pitch Control Unit Beta Feedback Transducer (BFT). Following part replacement, calibration, and operational testing, no further faults were identified.

C-GVIJ, a Cargojet Airways Boeing 767-328 was operating flight CJT920 from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (KCVG), KY, to Don Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla International Airport (MMGL), MX. During ILS 29L in MMGL, the right main landing gear light did not illuminate when the gear was selected down. A missed approach along with the published hold was performed as required and PAN PAN was declared. The quick reference handbook checklist was executed for Alt Gear Extension however the light still did not illuminate. Changed light bulbs for the gear positions and the right hand light main gear light illuminated. A second ILS 29L approach was performed and aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-GTLS, a Kississing Lake Lodge Ltd. (dba Wings Over Kississing) Beech 100, was conducting training flight WN16T under instrument flight rules (IFR) from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. A loss of separation occurred when the Winnipeg Tower controller prematurely cleared C-GTLS for takeoff behind C-GPQO, a Perimeter Aviation LP De Havilland DHC-8 conducting IFR flight PAG 117 from CYWG to Cross Lake/Charlie Sinclair Memorial Airport (CYCR), MB. The separation was reduced to 3.0 miles, where 4.0 miles was required.

C-GKUG, an Airbus A330-343 operated by Air Canada, was operating an IFR flight ACA327 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB.  During the cruise phase of flight, a burning smell was detected in the flight deck, followed by an indication alerting that a circuit breaker had been tripped. The flight crew then observed smoke emitting from the centre column below the standby compass. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks, declared an emergency, and diverted to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, where the aircraft landed without incident. The operator's maintenance found the standby compass exhibited heat damage to an electrical connector. The instrument was replaced, tested, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWJO, a Boeing 737-700 operated by WestJet Airlines was conducting flight WJA1086 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), NV. During the initial climb after take-off, the captain noticed flashing around the left windshield. Shortly after, a series of large cracks appeared and the heating element briefly burned. The flight crew requested to stop the climb with ATC and elected to return to CYYC. The flight crew then completed the appropriate checklist and declared a PAN PAN with ATC. The aircraft completed an uneventful landing in CYYC. Company maintenance replaced the captain's windshield and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FCCJ, a Cargojet B767-323 was operating flight CJT943 from Hamilton Airport (CYHM), ON, to Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (KCVG), KY. As the aircraft levelled off, the left engine surged and banged approximately 4 times and yaw was felt. There was a slight N1 fluctuation. Thrust was reduced on the affected engine to approximately 65% N1 with no more issues felt or seen. QRH was carried out, and the thrust on #1 engine was left at reduced power. Dispatch and maintenance were advised and MCC requested a return to CYHM. A PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GTXE, a Top Aces Incorporated Learjet 35A, was operating as flight BRUSR02 from Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, on a local Naval Support Mission flight, under instrument flight rules. The aircraft was equipped with a target tow reeling pod, mounted on a pylon under the left wing. When the aircraft returned to CYYJ, the crew experienced a launcher arm malfunction and were unable to reel in the towed target. The crew completed the applicable checklist and declared a PAN PAN. The crew then consulted with air traffic control about where to release the target being towed by the aircraft. The crew descended to an altitude of 1000 feet above sea level over the Haro Strait, visually cleared the area below the aircraft of all traffic, and completed a cable cut procedure to release the TRX-9 towed target and 129 feet of cable. The aircraft then landed at CYYJ without further incident. There were no injuries.The Royal Canadian Navy Air Component Coordination Element was informed of the Tow Target release coordinates.

C-FTEN, a WestJet Encore Ltd. De Havilland of Canada DHC-8-402, was conducting flight WEN3547 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. During cruise en route to CYXE the flight crew received a #2 engine oil pressure warning light. The crew checked the engine display to assess and noticed a rising oil temperature with no reading for oil pressure. Shortly after they received a #2 Propeller Electronic Control caution light. The flight crew began completing the applicable checklist in the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH). During this time, they noted the aircraft yawing and shaking. After completion of the checklist, the flight crew completed a precautionary #2 engine shutdown at FL220. The crew then made a MAYDAY call with Air Traffic Control (ATC) and, after further assessment of the situation, elected to divert to Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK. The flight crew advised ATC of their intentions and were given vectors for the diversion. Approximately 7.5 nm from Yorkton Municipal Airport (CYQV), SK the flight crew began their decent to FL100 and turned to CYQR. The flight landed with one engine operating on Runway 13 in CYQR without further incident and came to a stop for ARFF to inspect the aircraft. After inspection, the flight crew was given clearance to taxi the aircraft. While attempting to taxi, the captain was unable to keep the aircraft straight with tiller input, rudder deflection and differential braking and received a Nose Wheel Steering caution light. The aircraft was brought to a stop, and a tow was requested to the gate during which time the Nose Wheel Steering caution light extinguished.The operator's maintenance has replaced the #2 engine, and the aircraft was released back to service.

C-GBBB, a Bombardier CL-600-2B16 operated by Chartright Air Inc. as flight HRT556, was conducting a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Denver Centennial Airport (KAPA), CO. During the climb, at approximately FL315, the flight crew received a Master Warning ICAS “R ENGINE OIL” along with an aural “engine oil” alert, accompanied by a low oil pressure indication of 25 psi on the No. 2 engine (GE CF34-3B). The crew reduced the climb rate and retarded thrust on the No. 2 engine while actioning the quick reference handbook. Oil pressure temporarily recovered. The flight crew advised ATC of the situation and elected to return to CYYZ. The No. 2 engine remained at idle for the return; however, at approximately FL240, the low oil pressure indications and accompanying symptoms reappeared. The crew shut down the No. 2 engine and declared a MAYDAY. The aircraft landed uneventfully at CYYZ with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby.

C-GLQK, a Porter Airlines Inc. De Havilland DHC-8-402, was conducting flight PTR2350 from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. After being cleared for takeoff on Runway 30 and accelerating through approximately 40 knots, the flight crew received a takeoff warning horn. The crew conducted a rejected takeoff and declared a PAN PAN. The crew taxied off the runway onto Taxiway A and informed Air Traffic Control that no assistance was required. The operator's maintenance performed a reset of the elevator trim indication system. The takeoff warning horn then tested normal. The aircraft was released back into service and completed the trip to CYOW.

C-FQNG, a VIH Helicopters Limited Sikorsky S-61N, was conducting heli-logging operations with a longline and grapple approximately 72 nautical miles northwest of Tofino-Long Beach Airport (CYAZ), BC, with 2 flight crew members on board. While in flight, the aircraft suffered an uncommanded release of the longline assembly and grapple. The equipment fell into a forested area. There were no injuries reported and the aircraft was not damaged. A maintenance inspection was conducted after the longline assembly and grapple were recovered. Cotter pins in the manual release assembly were found to be worn and that was determined to be the cause of the release.

C-GJZA, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was preparing for a flight from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During boarding, the flight crew received a fire warning for the aft cargo compartment. The crew discharged the fire extinguishing bottles, initiated a rapid deplanement, and requested aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) services. There was no visible evidence of fire or smoke, and no engines were running at the time of the occurrence. No injuries were reported.

LN-RKM, an Airbus A330-343 aircraft operated by Scandinavian Airlines, was conducting IFR flight SAS910 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), New Jersey, to Copenhagen/Kastrup International Airport (EKCH), Denmark. While in cruise at FL370 over Labrador, the flight crew received a master caution and a flashing low oil quantity indication on engine No. 2, with the indicated quantity decreasing from approximately 3.7 quarts toward zero while oil pressure and oil temperature remained normal. After consulting company technical support via SATCOM, the crew declared a PAN PAN with air traffic services, reduced thrust on engine No. 2, and requested a diversion to Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), Newfoundland and Labrador. The aircraft landed at Goose Bay without further incident. After parking, ground personnel observed oil leaking from engine No. 2. There was no reported damage, and there was no impact on airport operations.The operator reported that maintenance replaced the engine No. 2 oil pressure transmitter hoses (part numbers AE711312-2 and AE711312-1) in accordance with the Rolls-Royce engine maintenance manual. An idle-run leak check was completed with no further discrepancies noted.

C-GGXP, a Cessna 172N and C-GBJJ, a Piper PA-44-180, both operated by Cornwall Aviation Ltd., were conducting local flights from Cornwall Regional Aerodrome (CYCC), ON. At approximately 1057 local, the two aircraft collided midair approximately 9 NM north-northwest of CYCC.Following the collision, C-GBJJ, with 2 pilots onboard, was able to continue flight and landed safely at CYCC. C-GGXP, with one pilot onboard, descended uncontrolled and impacted terrain in a forested swampy area. There was no post-impact fire. The aircraft’s emergency locator transmitter did not transmit a detectable signal.The pilot of C-GGXP was fatally injured. There were no injuries to the occupants of C-GBJJ. C-GGXP was destroyed, and C-GBJJ sustained significant damage.

C-GLWJ, a WestJet Encore DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was being operated as flight WEN3629 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, under instrument flight rules, to Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC. During cruise, while 90 nautical miles east of CYKA, the crew noted a change in engine sound. Shortly afterwards, the No. 1 engine hydraulic pump caution light illuminated. The crew began to conduct the applicable checklist from the quick reference handbook (QRH).  Before they completed the checklist, the crew observed illumination of the caution lights for the No. 1 hydraulic isolation valve, No. 1 rudder hydraulic, and the roll spoiler inboard hydraulic. The crew then noticed that the No. 1 hydraulic system showed zero pressure and zero fluid. The flight crew then began the loss of all fluid from the No. 1 hydraulic system QRH checklist. The crew declared a PAN PAN and elected to return to CYYC. The crew completed a flapless landing without further incident. Upon arrival, the aircraft was met on the runway and inspected by aircraft rescue and firefighting crews. It was then taxied to the gate under its own power. There were no injuries.Company maintenance inspected the hydraulic system and located a loose hydraulic fitting inside the left (No. 1) engine nacelle with the hydraulic fluid quantity being very low. The fitting was repaired, the engine driven hydraulic pump and system filters were replaced, and the fluid was replenished. Leak checks were completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GCEF, a Diamond DA 42 operated by Journey Air Ltd., was conducting a flight test for licensing purposes with a student pilot and an examiner on board. The aircraft remained within the Windsor International Airport (CYQG), ON, area for the duration of the flight. While on approach, approximately 7–8 NM from the runway, the student was performing a single-engine approach with one engine set to idle. During the approach, the landing gear remained retracted and the landing gear warning horn sounded continuously. The aircraft subsequently touched down on Runway 12/30 with the landing gear retracted. The aircraft sustained substantial damage; however, there were no injuries to either occupant.

C-GXTB, a Pilatus PC-12 operated by North Star Air, was conducting a flight from Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON, to Fort Albany Airport (CYFA), ON, with two crew members on board. While in cruise, approximately 20 NM southwest of Fort Albany Airport, the crew observed smoke in the cabin and flight deck. An emergency was declared, and the crew continued to destination, where the aircraft landed uneventfully with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by.After landing, the crew reported oil on the windshield. Maintenance determined the source to be a leaking propeller oil shaft seal.

N17TJ, a Cessna 441 Conquest II registered to Southern Aircraft Consultancy Inc. Trustee, was conducting a flight from Taber Airport (CED5), AB to Lethbridge Airport (CYQL), AB with only the pilot on board. During the final approach into CYQL the pilot elected to use approach flap for landing due to the gusty wind conditions. The aircraft touched down with all landing gear retracted. The pilot intentionally drifted the aircraft into the grass off the right side of Runway 24. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The pilot exited the aircraft and was uninjured.With the flaps in the approach position, the landing gear warning horn is disabled and as such, did not activate/warn the pilot when the power levers were reduced for landing.

C-FLQZ, a Boeing 737 Max 8 operated by Flair Airlines was conducting flight FLE600 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Approximately 49 nm SW of Lethbridge, AB, the captain observed some electrical arcing on the R1 windscreen, and the outer panes of glass appeared to start to crack. The flight crew requested a lower altitude with ATC and proceeded to complete the appropriate checklist. A PAN PAN was declared and the crew elected to divert to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, where an uneventful landing was completed.

C-GOUM, a privately registered Piper PA-28R-200, was conducting a local flight from Medicine Hat Airport (CYXH), AB, with the pilot and one passenger on board. After departure, the cabin door became unsecured, and the pilot remained in the circuit for a return to land. During the approach to Runway 21 in CYXH, the pilot observed a loss of engine power. During the final approach, the aircraft encountered a downdraft. When the pilot attempted to increase engine power, the engine (Lycoming IO-360) did not respond but remained running. The aircraft landed short of the runway threshold and during the landing roll, impacted the runway centerline lighting standard with the left wing and was substantially damaged. The pilot and passenger were not injured and exited the aircraft.

C-FIJZ, a Jazz CRJ900 was operating flight JZA822 from Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (KDCA), DC, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During cruise, the crew received a brake overheat indication. The crew actioned the quick reference handbook and the light extinguished. MTC was advise and met the aircraft after the flight landed in CYUL. Aircraft rescue and firefighting were put on standby as a precaution. The flight landed without any issue.

C-GTTM, a Swearingen SA227-AT operated by Carson Air was conducting flight CRN7081 from Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, with 2 flight crew members on board. C-GJWD, an Airbus Industries A321 operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA149 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to CYYC. ACA149 was on the final approach for Runway 29 while CRN7081 was being vectored from the southwest to follow ACA149 for Runway 29. CRN7081 was instructed to fly a heading of 030 and ATC observed the aircraft flying a heading of 020. Separation between CRN7081 and ACA149 reduced to 1.8 NM where 3.0 NM is required. ATC subsequently instructed CRN7081 to perform a left 360 turn to increase spacing and both aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-GWEF, a WestJet Encore Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was being operated as flight WEN3445 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC, under instrument flight rules. During cruise, the flight crew heard unexpected sounds which were followed by the landing gear inoperative caution light illuminating and the landing gear warning horn activating. The flight crew reduced aircraft power and decided to return to CYVR. They conducted the quick reference handbook (QRH) procedures for landing gear inoperative and weight on wheels caution lights. When the aircraft approached CYVR, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and used the alternate landing gear extension procedure. To confirm the landing gear was extended, the crew flew past the control tower at 300 feet above ground level. Various sources on the ground at CYVR reported that the aircraft’s landing gear appeared to be down and locked. The aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident where it was met by emergency services, inspected, and towed to the gate.Maintenance personnel found a fault with the aircraft’s Proximity Sensor Electronics Unit (PSEU) and a broken wire on a configuration plug. The PSEU and the wire were replaced, numerous landing gear swings were carried out successfully, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FPCZ, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited, Saab 340B, was being operated as flight PCO1775, under instrument flight rules, from Quesnel Airport (CYQZ), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. While on approach to CYVR, the crew was descending to 10 000 feet above sea level when the aircraft encountered severe turbulence. The indicated airspeed fluctuated from approximately 140 knots to 185 knots and the attitude varied from 10° nose up to 5° nose down. The aircraft landed safely. No injuries were reported. The aircraft was not damaged.A severe turbulence inspection and pressurization tests were carried out, and no faults were found.

C-FGSJ, a Cargojet B767 was operating flight CJT918 from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (KCVG), KY, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the takeoff run, thrust was set, the crew received an EICAS warning for Main Deck Cargo Fire. The takeoff was rejected at approximately 60 knots. Mayday was declared. Warning extinguished after thrust retarded to idle. The checklist was actioned, then the aircraft turned on to taxiway M3. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) responded, checked aircraft for any smoke or fire indication and used a FLIR camera to detect any heat source with no smoke visible. Aircraft returned to the ramp with ARFF following.

C-GEET, a privately registered Robinson R44 Clipper II helicopter, was conducting a local VFR flight from Lake Douglas, Newfoundland and Labrador, with a pilot and three passengers on board. During a landing to a bog area near 47°56'N 057°03'W, the helicopter was hovering in ground effect and the pilot applied right pedal to position the tail rotor over a clear area. The helicopter yawed rapidly to the right and settled. The pilot then pushed the cyclic forward in an attempt to fly away; the nose of the helicopter contacted the ground and the helicopter rolled onto its right side a short distance from the intended landing spot. The ELT did not activate and the helicopter was destroyed; there was no post-impact fire.All four occupants exited the helicopter and moved to a sheltered area. The pilot used a satellite messenger to send the occurrence coordinates to a flight follower, who notified the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre. About two hours later, a CH-149 Cormorant recovered the occupants and transported them to hospital in Corner Brook, Newfoundland and Labrador. The pilot suffered minor injuries.

C-FWJS, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-8CT, was operating as flight WJA667 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. C-GTWE, a WestJet Encore Bombardier Inc. De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402, was operating as flight WEN3338 from Grande Prairie Airport (CYQU), AB, to CYYC. Both aircraft were on the RNAV "Y" approach to Runway 29 when separation was reduced to 2.8 NM where 3 NM separation is required. There were no further issues and the flights landed safely.

C-FHNL, a Canadian North Inc. Boeing 737-752, was operating as flight AKT1749 from Horizon / Fort Mackay (CYNR), AB, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. On a visual approach into CYEG, for Runway 02, the flight crew reported a flap asymmetry issue. The flight crew completed the Trailing Edge Flap Asymmetry QRH and the Trailing Edge Flaps Up Landing QRH procedures. A PAN PAN was declared and the flight landed safely a short time later. Company maintenance found that the flap torque tube was sheared.

C-FWSO, a WestJet Boeing 737-7CT (B737-700), was being operated as flight WS845 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, under instrument flight rules, to Abbotsford International Airport (CYXX), BC. Shortly after departure from CYEG, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to perform their duties. A physician onboard the aircraft provided medical attention and the flight was expedited to CYXX where the crew member was transferred to emergency medical services.

C-GHLM, an Air Canada A330 was operating flight AC845 from Frankfurt Airport (EDDF), Germany, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. On departure the crew received an ECAM indication for bulk avionics smoke. A PAN PAN was declared with ATC, and a return to EDDF was initiated and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GOKG, an Air Transat A321 was operating flight TSC681 from Lisboa/ Humberto Delgado Airport (LPPT), Portugal, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-GEHY, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 was operating flight AC1246 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Sarasota Bradenton International Airport (KSRQ), FL. On approach to KSEQ Rwy14 at 2000 feet, the crew received a TCAS RA and the crew followed the operating procedures. ATC provided vectors away from the traffic 500 feet below. Aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GFVN, a Boeing 737-8 Max operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA147 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. A loss of IFR separation occurred when the Winnipeg tower combined Airport and Ground (WG) controller-in-training, under the supervision of the WG controller, cleared WJA147 for takeoff prematurely behind SKW3871, an Embraer E175LR, N310SY operated by SkyWest Airlines from CYWG to Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport (KMSP), MN. The separation between both aircraft was reduced to 2.5 miles. There were no injuries. There was no damage.

C-GMIQ, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 was operating flight AC976 from Los Cabos International Airport (MMSD), MX, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, the cruise experienced +/- 1000 feet and +/- 30 knot changes. Crew requested ATC for block altitude and after they were through an area of severe turbulence, requested descent to FL330. Autopilot remained engaged, cabin was secure with seatbelt signs on and no injuries reported.Air Canada maintenance completed the required inspections and no faults were found. Aircraft was returned to service.

C-FPSA, a Summit Air Ltd Dornier D228, was operating as flight SUT1023 from Gahcho Kue Aerodrome (CGK2), NT, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. During the approach into CYZF the No. 2 engine (GARRETT, TPE331-5-252D) performance began to degrade. A precautionary engine shutdown was conducted, and an emergency was declared. The flight landed safely in CYZF.The maintenance team found an issue related to the FCU.

C-GYKI, an Air Tindi Beechcraft B200GT was operating as flight TIN510 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. C-GMPY, a RCMP Pilatus PC12 was operating from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to CYEG. C-GYKI and C-GMPY, both on arrival into CYEG, lost separation on approach to RWY 02 and RWY 12 respectively. Separation was reduced to 2.4 miles where 3 miles is required. There were no further issues and both aircraft landed safely.

C-FRSO, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC57 from Dubai International Airport (OMDB), UAE, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-FWGB, un Learjet 45 exploité par Aviation Starlink inc. sous l'indicatif TLK811 effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC avec 2 membres d’équipage et 1 passager à bord. Lors de l’approche au retour, après avoir sorti le train d’atterrissage, un message rouge « Norm Brake Fail » est apparu sur le système d'affichage des paramètres moteurs et d'alerte de l'équipage (EICAS). L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a complété la liste de vérification pour un atterrissage avec le système de freinage d’urgence. L’aéronef s’est posé et s'est immobilisé sur la piste 06R sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’aéronef.

C-FXCA, un Boeing 767-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA7302 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Chicago O’Hare, USA (KORD) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau international, QC (CYUL) avec 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Lorsque l’équipage a sélectionné les volets en approche, un message d’asymétrie des becs de bord d’attaque est apparu. L’équipage a effectué une remonté, a complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et l’aéronef s’est posé sur la piste 06L sans encombre avec les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) déployés. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’aéronef.

C-FEXH, a Morningstar Air Express Incorporated, Cessna 208B (Grand Caravan), was being operated as flight MAL8070, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, with only the pilot onboard. During final approach to CYYJ, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence and wind shear. Indicated airspeed fluctuated more than 40 knots on multiple occasions. The pilot had difficulty holding the attitude required to maintain the alignment for the approach and experienced an altitude loss of between 400 and 700 feet. The aircraft was grounded, and a severe turbulence inspection was carried out. The inspection revealed no issues with the aircraft.

Au décollage de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL), il y a eu perte d'espacement entre C-GLQF, un DHC-8-402 exploité par Porter Airlines à destination de l'aéroport Billy Bishop Toronto City - Toronto, ON (CYTZ) et C-GOPW, un Boeing 737-275C exploité par Air inuit à destination de l'aéroport de Puvirnituq, NU (CYPX) lorsque C-GLQF a reçu l'autorisation de décollage piste 24L sans avoir reçu l'information trafic à propos de C-GOPW qui venait de décoller piste 24R lors de l'application d'espacement visuel appliqué par le contrôleur.

C-FAKF, un Autogyro Cavalon en exploitation privée effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aérodrome de St-Apollinaire (AirPro), QC (CAA4) avec un pilote à bord. Lors du décollage en condition de vent traversier, le pilote a perdu la maitrise de l’aéronef, le rotor principal a percuté le sol et l’aéronef s’est renversé sur le côté de la piste. Le pilote n’a pas été blessé, toutefois l’aéronef a subi des dommages importants.

N771XF, an American Airlines Airbus A321 was operating as flight AAL511 from Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (KDFW), TX, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. On approach into CYYC the flight crew had a notification of a flap issue. The flight crew discontinued the approach. It was determined that there was a fault with slat no. 2. The flight crew requested an approach into CYYC and declared a MAYDAY. The flight landed safely with no other issues.Following the flight, the maintenance removed and replaced the LH flap track #1 actuator due to actuator torque limiter fault. No maintenance history was found on this system preceding this event, and no repeats have occurred following the event.

C-FCTK, a Westjet Boeing 737-8 (Max 8) departed Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, was being operated as flight WJA2194, under instrument flight rules, to Cancun International Airport (MMUN), Mexico. While taking off from CYYJ, the aircraft suffered multiple bird strikes while passing through a flock of seagulls. The crew leveled the aircraft at 3000 feet above sea level and advised CYYJ tower controllers of the bird strike. After assessing the situation, a decision was made to divert to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. A PAN PAN was declared with air traffic control. The aircraft performed an overweight landing in CYVR without further incident. Company maintenance performed an overweight landing inspection and a bird strike inspection. The remains of multiple birds were found. The aircraft was undamaged and was returned to service.

C-GSCL un hélicoptère Robinson R44 en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis un lac situé à environ 10 miles nautiques au nord de la pourvoirie du Lac-Paul, Qc à destination de l'aéroport de St-Honoré, Qc (CYRC) avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Peu après le décollage, à environ 10 pieds du sol, une rafale a causé la perte de maitrise de l'appareil qui a alors percuté des arbres et s'est écrasé. L'appareil a subi des dommages importants mais les 2 occupants ont pu sortir sans blessures.

C-GAXV, a float equipped Cessna 172M operated by Red River Aviation Services Ltd. was conducting a training flight from Selkirk Water Aerodrome (CKC5), MB. During landing at CKC5 and at touchdown, the left float dug into the water causing the plane to pivot to the left and roll to the right. The propeller and the right wing contacted the water and the aircraft came to rest upright on the floats. The pilot, and sole occupant, reported no physical injuries and taxied the aircraft back to the dock. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FKGY, a Bombardier CL-600-2B16 (Series 604) operated by I.M.P. Group Ltd., was conducting a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Int'l Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Iqaluit Airport (CYFB), NU. During the climb through FL300, the flight crew received a "HYD 1 LOW PRESS" CAS message, followed by other related CAS messages. The flight crew levelled off at FL330 and declared PAN PAN, conducted the appropriate checklists, and elected to divert to Montreal/Trudeau Int'l Airport (CYUL), QC. The flight crew requested delaying vectors in order to burn off fuel in order to reduce the aircraft weight to below the maximum landing weight. The flight landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by.

C-GFJQ, a Westjet B737-8 was operating flight WJA2705 from Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), DR, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, the crew declared an emergency due to #2 engine oil issue. The crew elected to divert to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL, where the aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GLQB, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 operated by Porter Airlines as flight PD2237, was departing from Runway 14 at Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ). Shortly after takeoff, at approximately 500 feet AGL, the flight crew reported a near-miss with a remotely piloted aircraft system (RPAS) approximately 30 feet off the left wing.

C-GJYA, an Airbus A220-300 operated by Air Canada as flight AC542, was en route from Seattle–Tacoma International Airport (KSEA), WA, to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the flight, the crew declared a PAN PAN due to slat/flap and nose wheel steering issues.The aircraft landed at CYYZ with Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) on standby, then taxied to the gate without further incident.

C-GZYO, an Air Nunavut Ltd. Beechcraft King Air 200, was conducting a flight from Arviat Airport (CYEK), NU, to Rankin Inlet Airport (CYRT), NU. After takeoff from CYEK, the flight crew completed landing gear retraction and noticed that the landing gear had quit cycling. The flight crew contacted tower and requested Airport Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) to be on standby. They then attempted to cycle the gear with no change in gear position. The flight crew entered a hold on the inactive downwind side of the runway to complete the Emergency Landing Gear Extension checklist which included pulling the Landing Gear relay circuit breaker. They then completed an emergency gear extension at which time they received the three green lights indicating landing gear down and locked. After consultation with the Chief Pilot, the decision was made to return to CYEK. They landed on Runway 15 and stopped where the aircraft was met by ARFF. After an inspection of the landing gear the flight crew taxied off the runway onto the ramp.The operator's maintenance completed an inspection of the aircraft and found the landing gear motor to be unserviceable. The motor and hydraulic pump were replaced and function checks completed satisfactorily. The emergency gear extension system was bled and reset, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GZQV, an Embraer ERJ 190-400 operated by Porter Airlines as flight PD365, departed Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, for Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the climb, while passing through 8500 feet, the pilot monitoring (PM) observed the cabin altitude decreasing. The PM advised Air Traffic Control (ATC) of a pressurization issue and requested a level-off at 10 000 feet. The flight crew then received a CABIN DIFF PRESS FAIL EICAS message and actioned the applicable quick reference handbook (QRH) procedures. A decision was made to return to CYYZ and conduct an overweight landing in accordance with the QRH. The crew declared a PAN PAN. During the arrival, the crew was advised that a passenger was experiencing a panic attack, and medical assistance was requested upon landing. The aircraft landed and taxied to the gate without further incident.  Maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft and replaced both the outflow valve and the Air Management System (AMS) controller. The aircraft was functionally checked, found serviceable, and returned to operation without further issue.

C-GJZD, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was being operated as flight JZA8058 from Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Shortly after takeoff, the nose landing gear unsafe advisory light was illuminated. This was followed by the illumination of the landing gear inoperative caution light. The applicable checklist was actioned and the aircraft entered a hold before returning to CYKA. No emergency was declared, but the crew requested that aircraft rescue and firefighting services to be on standby for their arrival. An alternate landing gear extension procedure was performed and the flight landed without further incident in CYKA.The aircraft was subsequently flown, with landing gear extended under minimum equipment list relief, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, for maintenance. A damaged proximity sensor was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FRQA, an ATR-72-200 operated by Canadian North, was conducting flight AKT5858 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Taloyoak Airport (CYYH), NU. Shortly after departure the flight crew observed an Electric Smoke Warning light. The crew declared Pan Pan and subsequently shut off air conditioning pack 1 and 2. The Electric Smoke Warning ceased. The aircraft returned to CYZF and landed without further incident.  Company maintenance removed and replaced the smoke detector and the aircraft was returned to service.

N816AA, an American Airlines Boeing 787-8 aircraft was operating as AAL780 on a flight from Philadelphia International Airport (KPHL), PA, to Naples/Capodichino International Airport (LIRN), Italy. During the flight at approximately 43°55' N, 059°23' W, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform their duties. A decision was taken to divert back to KPHL where the aircraft landed without further incident. Emergency medical services were standing by to meet the aircraft and attend to the ill cabin crew member.

C-GKYS, an Embraer E195-E2 (ERJ 190-400) aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight JZA8118 from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. As the aircraft began the descent into CYHZ, air traffic control advised that light to moderate turbulence had been reported. The flight crew illuminated the seat belt signs and had the cabin crew secure the cabin. Severe turbulence was encountered as the aircraft descended through FL250 and autopilot disconnected. The crew experienced difficulty controlling the aircraft airspeed and descent rate for 2 to 3 seconds. The crew recovered control and confirmed with cabin crew that the cabin was safe and that no injuries had occurred. The aircraft continued the approach and landed at CYHZ without further incident. Maintenance carried out all recommended inspections based on the flight performance variations and exceedances, with no faults or damage found.

N913AN, a Boeing 737-800 operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL511 from Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport (KDFW), TX, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. After landing and while at the gate, sparks were observed coming from the auxiliary power unit (APU). Aircraft rescue and firefighting were requested and attended the aircraft. There was no fire noted, and there were no injuries.

C-FWSX, a Westjet B737-700 was operating flight WJA1427 from Nashville International Airport (KBNA), Tennessee, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-GJFZ, un Bombardier CRJ900 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA506 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport Lester B. Pearson International, ON (CYYZ) à destination de l'aéroport de Fredericton, NB (CYFC) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 74 passagers à bord. À 4NM au sud de Saint-Jean, QC, l'agent de bord responsable a avisé l'équipage de vol qu'elle ne se sentait pas bien. Celle-ci a transféré ses tâches à l'autre agent de bord et elle est allé s'asseoir à l'arrière de l'appareil tout en restant en fonction. L'équipage de vol a décidé de rediriger le vol vers l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) en déclarant une urgence "médicale" et a demandé à avoir la présence des services médicaux d'urgence sur place à l'arrivée à la barrière où l'agent de bord affecté a été prise en charge. L'agent de bord a été remplacée et le vol a redécollé sans encombre vers sa destination prévue.

C-FTPQ, a Chilliwack Flight Centre Inc., Cessna 172M was conducting circuits at Chilliwack Airport (CYCW), BC, on a visual flight rules night training flight with the pilot and a student on board. The aircraft had a bird strike on final. The instructor took control and landed the aircraft without further incident. There was significant damage to the front cowlings.

C-GJNZ, a Jazz Aviation LP MHI RJ Aviation CL-600-2D24 (CRJ 900), was being loaded to operate as flight JZA168 from Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 2 pilots, 2 cabin crew, and 10 passengers on board. During the passenger boarding and baggage loading process, a vehicle towing a baggage cart was manoeuvring around the left side of the aircraft. The vehicle drove under the left wing tip and collided into the outside trailing edge of the left wing. At the time of the collision, the vehicle driver was looking to the rear to ensure the baggage carts were in the correct place for the baggage loader. There was no high visibility cone placed at the end of the wing at the time of the collision. There were no injuries. The passengers deplaned and continued their flight on a different aircraft. The aircraft was ferried to CYVR for repair and landed there without further incident.

C-GPDJ, a Cargojet Airways Boeing B767 was operating flight CJT943 from Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, to Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (KCVG), KY. Shortly after leveling off at FL340, an ACARS message in red indicated Cabin Altitude. The cabin was climbing at 1200 fpm, and the outflow valve was fully open. An emergency descent was initiated, and ATC was advised with a MAYDAY call. The aircraft descended to 10 000 ft. After completing the checklist, the flight continued to KCVG and landed without further incident.

C-GPIM, a Mitchinson Flying Service Ltd. Cessna 310R, was conducting a training flight from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. Approximately 33 NM North of CYXE, the flight crew observed a reduction in performance from the right engine. They initiated a return to CYXE and declared a PAN PAN. While attempting to troubleshoot, the engine continued to lose power and oil pressure dropped to zero. As a precaution, the flight crew shut down and feathered the right engine and declared a MAYDAY. The aircraft landed on Runway 15 without incident but was unable to turn left and exit at the end of the runway due to asymmetric thrust. The aircraft was shutdown on the runway and was met by Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF). The operator's maintenance vehicle was escorted to the aircraft which was able to tow the aircraft back to the hangar.

C-GWHO, a Gogal Air Services Ltd. Bell 206LR, was conducting a flight from Norway House Airport (CYNE), MB, to a remote location 22 nautical miles WNW of CYNE. Upon landing in an open dry swamp, the pilot let 3 passengers out. The passengers then walked approximately 150 meters from the helicopter. When the pilot checked that the doors were closed before liftoff, he noticed that the passengers had left one of their shovels behind. The pilot tried to signal them to come back to the helicopter but was unable to get their attention. The pilot then got out of the helicopter while the engine was still running to try and signal them more effectively while standing on the skid. He then slipped off the skid, and the helicopter began to tilt backward and rolled over onto its side. There were no injuries, and the helicopter was substantially damaged.

C-GZQV, a Porter Airlines (Canada) Limited Embraer E190-400 was operating flight PD273 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While in cruise in vicinity of Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue safety duties. An onboard doctor provided medical care in flight, and another flight attendant assumed their duties for the remainder of the flight. Medical staff met the aircraft upon arrival at CYYC.

C-FGYL, a Top Aces A-4N was operating a flight from Nordholz Airport (ETMN), Germany. When the pilot selected the landing gear handle up, it resulted in the right-hand main gear indicating “in transient/not locked in position”. The nose and left-hand main gear did indicate up and locked. The landing gear handle was then lowered which resulted in all landing gear indicating down and locked. Fuel was then burnt down to landing weight. After 30 minutes, the right-hand main gear changed from down and locked, to “in transient/not locked in position.” A chase aircraft confirmed all landing gear to be down and appeared locked. An emergency was declared and a straight in, full stop landing was flown without further incident.

C-FETR, a Chinook Helicopters (1982) Limited Bell 47G-2 helicopter, departed Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, to conduct local training flights, under visual flight rules, with 1 student pilot and 1 flight instructor onboard. The student successfully completed 2 circuits with the instructor onboard and then dropped the instructor off on the airport infield to begin solo exercises. The student successfully completed a solo circuit and landed. For the second solo circuit, as done in the previous 3 flights, the student lifted into a hover at approximately 5 feet above ground level and initiated a 360° clearing turn to the left in preparation for departure. During the latter part of the turn, the helicopter suddenly accelerated in the left turn. The student maintained a left tail rotor pedal input and the left turn continued to accelerate. Control was lost; the aircraft contacted terrain and came to a rest on its left side. The student turned the throttle off and crawled through the left door. The instructor arrived on scene, checked on the student and turned off the main battery. Aircraft rescue and firefighting crews arrived on scene. There was no post impact fire. The emergency locator transmitter (ELT) had activated on impact and was turned off by company maintenance personnel. The student received minor injuries. The helicopter was substantially damaged.The helicopter was recovered to the company hangar and the TSB examined the wreckage. Both main rotor blades were destroyed and the aft tail boom had broken as a result of the impact with terrain.

C-GWEQ, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 operated by WestJet Encore was conducting flight WEN3566 from Cranbrook (CYXC), BC to Calgary Intl. Airport (CYYC), AB. C-GQHL, a Cessna T-310P operated by Orthoshop Geomatics Ltd. was conducting a photo survey flight from Calgary/Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB. Approximately 45 nm SSW of CYYC, WEN3566 was cleared on an initial decent for the approach into CYYC. While descending through approximately 16 000 feet, a loss of separation occurred between WEN3566 and C-GQHL. Lateral separation was reduced to 4.2 nm where 5.0 nm is required.

C-GJTX, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was operating flight ROU1882 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Cancún International Airport (MMUN), Mexico. Prior to top of descent, three cabin crew members began to feel unwell. No unusual odour was present at the time. However, the flight crew noted a moderate soapy odour during departure and a brief musty smell during descent through 13 000 feet. One of the cabin crew members was unable to perform duties for landing.

C-FJZL, a Jazz CRJ900 was operating flight JZA717 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Minneapolis-St Paul International/Wold-Chamberlain Airport (KMSP), MN. During climb the crew had a complete loss of the #3 hydraulic system. They declared a PAN PAN and elected to return to CYYZ. The crew confirmed they needed to do an alternate gear extension and originally requested a tow however the aircraft was able to taxi to the gate after landing.

C-GPOJ, a PAL Airlines de Havilland DHC-8-402 was operating as PVL921 from Gander International Airport (CYQX), NL, to Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL. While climbing through 17 000 feet, the crew observed a cabin pressure warning light indication and requested an immediate descent to 10 000 feet. The crew performed their memory items, consulted the quick reference handbook checklist, and briefed the passengers. The crew then declared a PAN PAN and coordinated a diversion back to CYQX where a landing was made without further incident.The post-flight maintenance inspection found ruptured air conditioning pack ducts related to a faulty Pack Flow Control & Shutoff Valve.

C-FXMS, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-800 was operating flight WJA229 from Halifax Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. C-FWSY, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-700 was operating flight WJA113 from CYYC to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, and was holding short of Runway 17L at Taxiway Z, 3600 feet from the threshold of Runway 17L. Another aircraft was holding short of Runway 17L on Taxiway D by the threshold. The Calgary Tower controller cleared WJA229 to land Runway 17L and when WJA229 passed the aircraft holding on Taxiway D, cleared WJA113 to line up. WJA113 did not follow the instruction and advised the tower controller of their position and WJA113 was subsequently instructed to hold short of Runway 17L.

C-FWKQ, a North Star Air Pilatus PC12/47E, was conducting a flight from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, to Webequie Airport (CYWP), ON. On climb-out through 10 000 feet, the flight crew noticed that both electric fuel boost pumps were indicating ON and momentarily turning off at a regular cadence of approximately every ten seconds. There were no Central Aural Warning System (CAWS) notifications nor low fuel pressure indications. Fuel flow and all engine indications were normal and appropriate for the power setting. The flight crew actioned the Fuel Pressure Low checklist, declared a PAN PAN and requested priority vectors to remain within glide distance of CYQT. The aircraft landed, taxied and shutdown without further incident.The operator's maintenance replaced the Fuel Low pressure switch, cleaned the airframe fuel filter and replaced the engine fuel filters. Ground runs and leak checks were completed with no faults found and the aircraft was released to service.

C-GTUK, a Nolinor Boeing 737-200, was being operated as flight NRL514 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, under instrument flight rules, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. C-FWZV, an Air Tindi De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-7-100, was being operated as flight TIN702, under instrument flight rules, from CYZF to Hay River Airport (CYHY), NT. Near CYZF, the aircraft were separated by 900 feet vertically and 4 nautical miles (NM) horizontally where 1000 feet and 5NM was required. Both aircraft proceeded without further issues.

C-FGYL, a Top Aces McDonnell Douglas A-4N was operating SKYHWK1 for a local training flight from Cuxhaven/Nordholz Airport (ETMN), Germany. After takeoff, the Oil Level High caution light remained illuminated. The pilot declared an emergency after troubleshooting having had no impact on the oil level high light. Fuel was reduced to landing weight and aircraft landed uneventfully.

N193DN, a Boeing B767-332(ER) aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL45 from Dublin International Airport (EIDW), Ireland, to John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), NY. While at FL350 in cruise flight at about 55°13' N, 031°03' W, the flight crew detected an audible thump and observed the number 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney PW4060) decelerate and shut down. The flight crew then disconnected the autopilot and autothrottles and performed the quick reference handbook procedure for Engine Failure or Shutdown which included one attempted restart on the number 1 engine. The crew noted the high engine EGT and elected to continue with the number 1 engine shut down. The crew declared an emergency and initiated a diversion to Reykjavík/Keflavík International Airport (BIKF), Iceland. The crew contacted company dispatch and maintenance using ACARS and landed at BIKF without further incident. Airport emergency response crews inspected the aircraft with no anomalies noted. Maintenance personnel discovered metal in the tailpipe. A borescope inspection identified significant damage that required the replacement of the number 1 engine.

C-FBPQ, a Delta Helicopters Ltd. Airbus AS350 B-3 helicopter, was conducting sling load operations approximately 16 miles east-northeast of Lac La Biche Aerodrome (CYLB), AB, with only the pilot on board. While transporting mechanical equipment in a sling, the sling assembly failed and the cargo fell to the ground below. A search for the load was unsuccessful. There was no reported damage to the helicopter or environment, and there were no injuries.

C-FERJ, a Summit Air BAE Systems (Operations) Limited Avro Series RJ85, was on an IFR flight from Diavik Aerodrome (CDK2), NT, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. During the climb through 10 000 feet, the crew heard a banging noise and noted a vibration along with the #3 engine ENG VIB warning illuminated, the EGT climbing, and the N1 dropping. The crew actioned the checklists, shut down the engine (AVCO Lycoming USA LF-507-1F), and declared a MAYDAY. The decision was made to divert to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. The crew downgraded to a PAN PAN, and landed at CYZF without further issue. Aircraft rescue and firefighting followed the aircraft to the ramp. There was no fire, and no injuries were reported.Company maintenance determined the #2 bearing scavenge line failed resulting in oil loss and failure of the affected engine. The engine manufacturer will be providing a teardown report.

C-GJYC, un A220-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif AC515431 s’apprêtait à effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l’aéroport international de Seattle-Tacoma, USA (KSEA). Alors que l'aéronef était stationné à la barrière, au sol à CYUL, une fuite de carburant a été signalée. Un débarquement rapide a été effectué et les services d’urgence ont été appelés. Les passagers ont été débarqués en toute sécurité vers le terminal. Une composante du système de carburant a ensuite été changée et l’aéronef est retourné en service.

C-GLHO, a Beech 1900D operated by Latitude Air Ambulance, was conducting flight HTT192 under instrument flight rules (IFR) from Greater Sudbury Airport (CYSB), ON, to Timmins (Victor M. Power) Airport (CYTS), ON. While inbound CYTS runway 03, HTT192 reported a traffic collision avoidance system (TCAS) resolution advisory (RA) at approximately 5000 feet and 20 nautical miles south of CYTS. C-FJUM, a Diamond Aircraft DA40 operated by Waterloo-Wellington Flying Club under visual flight rules (VFR) was about 500 feet below HTT192. The traffic was not passed by Air Traffic control (ATC).

C-GPDB, a Learjet 45 operated by Sunwest Aviation Ltd. was conducting flight CNK678 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Boeing Field/King County International Airport (KBFI), WA. Departing CYYC the flight crew received a CKPT DUCT OVHT alert message and noticed rising cabin temperature. The crew elected to return to CYYC and declared an emergency. On descent, the crew also received multiple warning messages related to the duct system as well as the rudder boost. The aircraft landed uneventfully and was shut down on the runway. The crew and airport rescue and firefighting conducted inspections finding no evidence of fire. The aircraft was restarted and taxied back to the apron. There were no injuries.Company maintenance conducted troubleshooting and located a faulty servo air pressure regulator. It was determined that other alert messages were related to the high interior temperatures caused by the faulty regulator. The systems were ground tested as serviceable, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTVO, a Boeing 737-200 operated by Buffalo Airways Ltd. was conducting flight BFL202 from Goose Lake Aerodrome (CGS2), NU, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. Passing approximately 5000 feet during the initial climb, the crew noted an uncommanded extension of the nose gear and heard sounds consistent with the nose gear banging against the fuselage. The crew actioned the emergency checklists, contacted company operations, and declared an emergency with ATC. The flight continued to CYZF where aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) were on standby. During the landing roll, the nose gear collapsed rearward. The aircraft remained on the runway, there was no fire, and there were no injuries.Company maintenance is investigating the cause of the failure.

C-GJIZ, a Jazz Aviation CRJ900 was operating flight JZA929 from Philadelphia International Airport (KPHL), PA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While taxiing at KPHL, the aircraft was cut off by a ground vehicle, and the flight crew had to aggressively apply the brakes to avoid a collision. A cabin crew member sustained an injury and was subsequently removed from the flight.
