C-FYRH, un Pilatus PC12/47 exploité par Panorama Fixed Wings Ltd. sous l'indicatif PNO729, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aérodrome de Saint-Augustin (CYIF), QC à destination de l'aéroport Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU). Environ 45 minutes après le début du vol, à environ 60nm ENE de l'aéroport de Mont-Joli (CYYY), QC, l'équipage a remarqué un problème avec le générateur #1 et que la batterie se déchargeait. L’équipage a dérouté vers CYYY et la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée. Plusieurs systèmes de l’aéronef ont ensuite commencé à être hors fonction. Lors de la sortie du train, uniquement le train principal a complètement sorti, l’équipage a dû utiliser la procédure alternative de sortie du train afin de sécuriser la roue de nez. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et l’aéronef s'est posé sans encombre à CYYY. Le démarreur-générateur et la batterie ont été remplacés par la suite.

C-GCGU, a Cessna 560XL operated by Chartright Air Inc. as flight HRT247, was conducting a flight from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON. During departure from CYYZ, HRT247 was issued takeoff clearance from Runway 23 as a successive departure following ENY3993 (N298FR), an Embraer 175LR operated by Envoy Air. Both aircraft were cleared in sequence for departure from the same runway.A loss of separation occurred during the climb-out phase. The minimum separation achieved was 1.8 nautical miles, which is below the required minimum standard of 3 nautical miles.

C-GWJO, a Westjet Airlines Boeing 737-7CT, was operating flight WJA310, under instrument flight rules from Comox Airport (CYQQ), BC, to Calgary International (CYYC), AB. During cruise flight, the flight crew observed a low oil quantity indication on the right engine (CFM International CFM56-7B22E) and reduced the engine thrust to idle. The crew contacted maintenance, and during the call, they observed a continued decrease in oil quantity in the right engine combined with low oil pressure and high oil temperature indications. The crew consulted the quick reference handbook and shut down the right engine. The crew declared an emergency and requested emergency services to be on standby at CYYC. The aircraft landed safely, and the engine was inspected before the aircraft taxied to the gate. There were no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft. Maintenance found metal debris in the right engine accessory gearbox. The engine was removed and sent to the manufacturer for teardown and assessment. Three days earlier, on 17 October 2025, the right engine had a low oil quantity indication after start-up at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (KSEA), WA. The engine was shut down, and a third-party maintainer serviced the engine adding 13 quarts of oil. The engine was ground run and leak checked with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FCZF, an Air Canada Airbus A320-214 (A320-200) was operating flight ACA1048 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Chicago O'Hare Airport (KORD), U.S. C-FBWI, a Westjet Boeing 737-8CT (B737-800), was operating flight WJA2060, under instrument flight rules, from CYVR to Los Cabos Airport (MMSD), MX. Vancouver Tower air traffic control (ATC) cleared the 2 aircraft for takeoff from Runway 08R with the Airbus departing first. The initial horizontal separation between the aircraft was approximately 3 nautical miles (NM). Once both aircraft were airborne and in their initial climb, a loss of separation occurred when the separation between the aircraft reduced to 2.7 NM when 3.0 NM was required. Vancouver Terminal ATC directed the aircraft on course and the required separation was re-established.

C-GUBC, an Air Transat A330-243 was operating flight TSC251 from Paris Charles De Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Shortly after take-off, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-GSKB, a Beech 1900D operated by Kenn Borek Air Ltd., was operating as KBA901 from Ulukhaktok Airport (CYHI), NT to Inuvik Mike Zubko Airport (CYEV), NT. During the approach to CYEV, the crew reported a potential landing gear issue, requested a low pass for a visual confirmation, and proceeded to orbit north of the field to perform checks. A second low pass confirmed that the landing gear appeared down. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) were requested on standby. The aircraft landed without incident.Company Maintenance completed troubleshooting and determined the issue was caused by a faulty landing gear down and locked switch. The affected switch was replaced, the system tested, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GUBL, an Air Transat A330-243 was operating flight TSC695 from Athens Eleftherios Venizelos Airport (LGAV), Greece, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-GFOL, a Beech 200 operated by Keewatin Air LP (dba Kivalliq Air Nunavut Lifeline) was conducting an IFR flight from Island Lake Airport (CYIV), MB, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. When approximately 60 nm north of CYWG, the aircraft experienced a rapid depressurization at 23 000 feet and the cabin differential pressure reduced to zero. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and continued to descend. At approximately 5000 feet the aircraft began to re-pressurize. The aircraft subsequently landed safely in CYWG. The operator's maintenance found the cabin door seal was deformed and a left-hand rudder cable seal was leaking. The seal was replaced and the main cabin door latching mechanism was rigged as per the maintenance manual. The aircraft was pressurized on the ground to max differential with a pressurization cart and released subject to satisfactory test flight.

C-GFOL, a Beech 200 operated by Keewatin Air LP, was conducting an IFR flight as KEW210 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Airport (CYWG), MB, to Norway House Airport (CYNE), MB. During the approach into CYNE, the flaps did not extend when selected. The crew referenced an abnormal checklist and elected to return to CYWG. A PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft landed without further incident.  The operator's maintenance replaced a faulty switch and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GAAS, an AirSprint Cessna 525B was operating flight ASP567 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Providenciales International Airport (MBPV), Turks and Caicos Islands. During cruise, the crew declared an emergency due to a pressurization issue and elected to divert to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL, where the aircraft landed safely.

C-GSGA, a Sander Geophysics Ltd. Cessna 208B was conducting survey operations from Khajuraho Airport (VEKO), Madhya Pradesh, India. During the flight, the aircraft experienced an in-flight electrical anomaly when the crew detected a faint smell of smoke in the cockpit, initially uncertain whether it originated from inside or outside the aircraft. Within approximately ten minutes, visible smoke developed, prompting the pilots to execute the “Electrical Fire in Flight” memory items and initiate a diversion to the nearest suitable airport which was Bilaspur Airport (VEBU), Chhattisgarh, India. Upon shutting down electrical power, the smoke ceased, but the crew continued toward VEBU as a precaution. Attempts to establish contact with VEBU Tower and Raipur ATC were unsuccessful, leading the crew to squawk 7700 and transmit blind on 121.5 MHz. The aircraft landed safely and without incident at VEBU, where it was met by airport authorities for inspection.

C-GOIE, an Airbus A321-271NX(LR) aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC260 from Montréal/Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Josep Tarradellas Barcelona/El Prat Intl (LEBL), Spain. While cruising at FL330 at about 49°19' N, 046°06' W, the flight crew requested descent to FL320 via Controller pilot data link communications (CPDLC) due to moderate turbulence. The crew received "UNABLE DUE TO TRAFFIC" CPDLC message. The turbulence level increased, and the crew declared a PAN PAN on radio frequencies 123.45 and 121.5 and initiated an offset descent to FL310. No traffic was observed on the TCAS during the descent and air traffic control subsequently cleared the flight to FL310. The aircraft continued to the destination and landed without further incident. Maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft in accordance with manufacturer instructions and no damage was found.

C-GUPL, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300, was holding short of Runway 05 on Taxiway Hotel at Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. N589FX, a Bombardier Challenger 350 business jet was lined up on Taxiway Hotel 6. The crew of C-GUPL responded to a clearance to enter the active runway, without any correction from ATC, and believed it was for their flight number. The crew started to move and passed the hold short line for Runway 05. ATC then told the crew to hold their position. N589FX was then cleared for takeoff and C-GUPL was then subsequently cleared for their departure without further incident.

C-FYJG, an Air Canada Rouge LP Airbus A319-114, enroute from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), NV, towards Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, declared an emergency due to two flight attendants and three passengers feeling ill. There were reports of dizziness and nausea. The crew of the aircraft continued towards CYUL and was given priority. The aircraft landed safely at 1053 UTC. Medical staff met with the five individuals at the gate.

C-FIUL, an Air Canada Boeing 777-300, was taxiing for departure at Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, when a Flight Attendant reported an illness and was unable to continue their duties. The aircraft returned to the gate and was met by EMS.

C-GQBQ, un Bombardier CL600-2B16 (Challenger 601-3A) exploité par le Gouvernement du Québec, service aérien gouvernemental effectuait un vol d'évacuation médicale selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC  à destination de l'aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, Qc (CYMT) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 2 passagers à bord. En approche finale sur CYMT, le train d'atterrissage a été descendu. L'indicateur de verrouillage du train principal droit ne s'est pas illuminé. La liste de vérification pour un "GEAR DISAGREE" a été effectuée. Une urgence a été déclarée, le train a été rentré et la décision de retourner à CYQB a été prise. À l'approche de CYQB, le train a été redescendu et environ une minute plus tard, tous les voyants indiquant les trains déployés étaient illuminés. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre.

C-GFJM, a WestJet Airlines Limited Boeing 737-8 (Max 8) was conducting flight WJA707 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. While on short final (between 700 and 300 feet above ground level), the No. 1 engine (CFM LEAP-1B27) experienced a loss of engine power. While on autopilot, the aircraft drifted slightly to the left and a loss of thrust was felt. The loss of thrust was confirmed by a simultaneous 7 knot speed reduction. The crew then observed an auto throttle caution light and an engine fail warning light. The captain announced an engine failure and the crew elected to continue the approach. Concurrently, the engine stabilized to normal performance parameters and the landing was conducted without any further incident and taxied to the gate with both engines operating. There were no injuries.The aircraft was removed from service and company maintenance completed numerous activities to troubleshoot the power loss. During the fuel nozzle check, a loose B-nut was located which was retorqued to the approved specifications. The fuel metering unit (FMU) was also replaced during the troubleshooting. Engine runs proved successful and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKXM, a Porter Airlines (Canada) Limited Embraer ERJ190-400, was conducting flight POE481 from John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 5 crew members and 129 passengers on board. On approach, the flight crew observed an AVNX MAU 2A FAIL (modular avionics unit 2A) warning message. The crew completed the applicable quick reference handbook (QRH) checklist and advised air traffic control (ATC) that upon landing, the aircraft may experience a potential loss of nose wheel steering. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) was requested to be placed on standby. Just prior to landing, the warning message in the aircraft cleared. The aircraft landed without further incident and exited the runway without difficulty.Company maintenance inspected the aircraft after landing but were unable to recreate the fault. All service checks passed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GGNC, a Chinook Helicopters Bell 206B, was being operated on a local training flight from Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, under visual flight rules. During the approach to CYXX, the transmission oil chip detector caution light (XMSN CHIP LT) began to flicker on and off. The pilot monitored the light while continuing to CYXX. On long final for Pad A, the XMSN CHIP LT illuminated continuously. The pilot declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed without further incident with aircraft rescue and firefighting crews on standby. There were no injuries reported.A post-flight maintenance inspection found a small amount of magnetic debris on the transmission oil chip detector. The chip detector was cleaned and reinstalled without further illumination of the light.

C-GOIM un Airbus A321-271NX exploité par Air Transat sous l'indicatif TSC538 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport Cancún Intl, Mexique (MMUN) avec 6 membres d'équipage et 182 passagers à bord. Peu après le décollage de la piste 06R avant d'atteindre 1000 pieds, le moniteur électronique centralisé de bord (ECAM) a affiché le message NAV ADR 1+2 FAULT indiquant un problème avec le système d'indication de la vitesse et de l'altitude. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) et a suivi la procédure de la liste de vérification et est revenu se poser sans encombre sur la piste 06L. Les passagers ont été transférés dans un autre appareil et le vol a été effectué avec un retard d'environ 3 heures.

C-FEKD, a Jazz Embraer 175 was operating flight JZA735 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Cleveland-Hopkins International Airport (KCLE), OH. On the approach after putting the gears down, the crew got a warning they had no #2 hydraulics. They did a missed approach, declared a PAN PAN and went through their checklist. Landed in KCLE with only #1 hydraulics, half the brakes and no nose wheel steering. The aircraft stopped on the runway to assess the situation and let the breaks cool down, proceeded to the taxiway and aircraft rescue and firefighting met the aircraft to do an inspection. Then taxied to the gate without further incident.

C-GDSG, un Beech 1900D exploité par Sky Jet M.G. Inc. sous l'indicatif LSJ607 effectuait un vol d'essai local après maintenance selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à destination de l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), Qc avec 2 pilotes et un technicien d'entretien. Au moment de virer en finale lors du premier circuit, la manette de train a été descendue et le train principal a commencé à descendre. Les 2 voyants indiquant que le train principal était bien verrouillé se sont illuminé mais l'indicateur du train avant ne s'est pas illuminé. Une revue des coupe-circuits du système d'indication a été effectuée mais tout était bien en place. L'indication du train avant ne s'étant toujours pas illuminé, une remise des gaz et une remontée ont été effectuées. Un passage près de la tour de contrôle confirme que le train avant n'est pas complètement déployé. Après plusieurs tentatives de déployer le train et avoir consommé le plus de carburant possible, les services de secours sont déployés et l'atterrissage est effectué avec le train avant partiellement sorti. Les moteurs sont coupés tout juste après le toucher des roues du train principal. Le train avant est resté dans cette position tout le long du roulage sur la piste et l'appareil a même pu dégager la piste en virant sur la voie de circulation. Les occupants sont sorti sans problème.

C-GNRC, an Execaire Aviation Challenger 604 (CL-600-2B16) was operating a flight from Verona/Villafranca Airport (LIPX), Italy, to Milano/Malpensa Airport (LIMC), Italy. During descent, the flight crew experienced a rollback on the No. 1 engine, accompanied by an engine overheat indication. In response to the abnormal indications and degraded engine performance, a PAN PAN was declared with ATC. The engine securing checklist was promptly executed in accordance with the quick reference handbook. A single-engine approach and landing were carried out without further incident. The aircraft came to a stop on the runway. After a brief hold, the aircraft was cleared to taxi off the runway under its own power. The affected engine area was visually inspected by aircraft rescue and firefighting personnel, who reported no visible signs of fire or external damage.

C-FTIQ, un Aerospatiale ATR 42-500 exploité par Bradley Air Services sous le nom de Canadian North, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport d'Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) à destination de l'aéroport de Hall Beach, NU (CYUX) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 34 passagers. Au moment où l'appareil a atteint la vitesse V1, l'équipage a senti une odeur s'apparentant à du caoutchouc brulé. L'odeur s'est intensifiée lors de la rétraction du train d'atterrissage. Le train a aussitôt été ressorti et une urgence a été déclarée. L'appareil a effectué un circuit et est revenu se poser en surpoids sans encombre. L'équipage a aussi rapporté que les freins semblaient mous. Le personnel de maintenance n'a pas pu reproduire l'odeur lors de l'essai moteur. Le système d'aération a été inspecté sans problème décelé. L'inspection non planifiée pour un atterrissage en surpoids a été effectuée, ainsi que le remplacement de l'unité de frein numéro 1. L'appareil a été remis en service à la suite d'un vol d'essai.

C-IFES un Ultra Léger Delisle CADI en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'hydrobase Piché Dubuisson QC (CTA5) à destination du lac Langis situé à 1 mile nautique au sud-est de l'aéroport de Val d'or Qc (CYVO). Au moment de l'amerrissage, pour une raison inconnue, l'appareil s'est renversé sur le lac. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé.

C-FGZH, a Top Aces A-4N was operating flight SKYHAWK3 from Nordholz Airport (ETMN), Germany. After an hour of flight, the pilot had the fuel low level light unexpectedly illuminate indicating approximately 1100 lbs of fuel left in the fuselage tank. All other fuel quantities and transfer indications were normal. The pilot declared an emergency with ATC and diverted to Rostock-Laage Airport (ETNL), Germany, and landed safely without further incident.

C-FNND, an Air Canada B777-200 was operating flight AC33 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Sydney/Kingsford Smith Airport (YSSY), Australia. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-GKOD, an Air Canada Airbus A320, was conducting flight AC259 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB with 108 passengers and 5 crew members on board. At 500 feet above ground level while on final approach to CYWG, the aircraft encountered 15-20 medium size birds, and the crew had indications of contact. The number one engine encountered a compressor stall for 10 seconds. The crew continued the approach after the engine power recovered. During the landing, the number one engine thrust reverser malfunctioned. After landing, the aircraft was checked by ARFF and proceeded to taxi to the gate without further incident. The operator's maintenance completed a bird strike inspection and an engine change.

C-GJTE, a privately registered Piper PA31-310 (Navajo) was on a flight from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, with a fuel stop in Lac La Biche Aerodrome (CYLB), AB. After fuelling, the aircraft departed CYLB and the pilot noticed that fuel was leaking from one of the fuel caps and returned to CYLB to tighten the fuel cap. The aircraft landed without extending the landing gear. The propellers, engines and the belly were damaged as a result. The pilot, the sole occupant on board, was not injured and egressed out of the plane on their own.

N126LS, a privately registered Cessna 210M was performing a recreational flight from Port Hardy Airport (CYZT), BC, to Kitimat Aerodrome (CBW2), BC, with the pilot and 3 persons on board. As the aircraft was flared for landing, the pilot observed 2 deer sprint across the runway from right to left. The pilot attempted to avoid a collision by popping the airplane up and was able to avoid 1 of the 2 deer. The other deer was struck by the propeller and impacted the nose gear. The pilot was able to settle the aircraft onto the runway without further incident and taxied to a nearby hangar. There were no injuries reported. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The aircraft suffered damage to the propeller, nose gear doors, exhaust pipe and cowl flaps. The aircraft is being assessed for further damage.

C-FYNP, a Bell 407 helicopter operated by Edge Helicopters Canada Inc., was conducting a local VFR flight near Cow Head, NL, transporting a hunting group from a ridge back to base camp. After returning to the staging area and refueling the aircraft, the pilot performed a post-flight walk-around and observed paint chipping and impact marks on both tail-rotor blades. No abnormal vibration, pedal feedback, or control issues had been noted during the flight. Maintenance, subsequently confirmed evidence of a minor, glancing tail-rotor strike. The helicopter was removed from service for maintenance inspection. No property damage were reported. Maintenance ActionFollowing the occurrence, a field inspection confirmed minor tail rotor blade damage with no structural or gearbox defects. The helicopter was transported by ground to the company hangar for maintenance, where the tail rotor blades will be replaced and balanced before return to service.

C-GAZD un Cessna 185F sur flotteurs en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le lac Helluva Qc. à destination de l'hydrobase du lac Pau (CTP4) Qc avec un pilote et un passager à bord. L'appareil était en mouvement vers l'aire de décollage quand une bourrasque de vent a soulevé une aile. Le pilote a perdu la maitrise de l'appareil quand une combinaison de facteurs comme le flotteur et le bout d'aile sous le vent sont passés sous la surface de l'eau. L'appareil s'est renversé et les occupants ont pu s'extirper rapidement. Ils n'ont pas subi de blessures. En fin de journée, C-GAZD n'étant toujours pas arrivé, les personnes à CTP4 ont alerté les autorités que l'appareil manquait à l'appel. Les occupants ont été retrouvés sains et saufs 2 jours plus tard.

C-GITR, an Air Canada Rouge A319 was operating flight ROU1622 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL. During cruise phase of flight, the flight crew received a BLUE HYD SYS LO PR ECAM, followed shortly by a BLUE HYD RSVR LO LVL indication. ECAM actions confirmed a complete loss of blue hydraulic fluid. Landing performance was assessed for KFLL, with sufficient runway available. The flight crew coordinated with Dispatch and MOC, who advised continuing to destination. No ATC notification was made at the time. A PAN PAN was declared with Miami Center, and aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) was requested for landing as a precaution. The aircraft landed uneventfully and an ARFF inspection revealed no visible fluid leak. The aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power, where the flight was completed without further incident. Post-flight inspection identified the source of the leak as the blue hydraulic pump.

C-FWXI, a Beechcraft B200 operated by Beaver Air Services LP (dba Missinippi Airways) was conducting an IFR flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport, MB. (CYWG) to the Flin Flon Airport, MB. (CYFO). During the climb out of CYWG at an altitude of 19800 feet, the aircraft's cabin pressure began to fluctuate. The captain experienced mild dizziness and the crew donned oxygen masks. An emergency descent was initiated. The flight crew activated the manual passenger oxygen system but the masks did not deploy. An emergency was declared, the Quick Reference Handbook checklist for depressurization was completed, and the aircraft returned to CYWG without further incident.The operator's maintenance department conducted tests of the cabin pressurization system and could not duplicate the fluctuation. The cabin oxygen system was inspected and a faulty passenger oxygen valve was found. The valve was repaired and tested serviceable. A satisfactory flight test was conducted for cabin pressurization.

F-RARF, a France - Air Forces Command Airbus A330-200 was departing as flight CTM001 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, for Paris Orly Airport (LFPO), France. C-FJWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-400 was arriving to CYYC from Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK. While F-RARF was still on the take-off roll on Runway 35R, C-FJWE had crossed the threshold of the runway and a loss of runway separation occurred. There were no further issues with the departing and arriving aircraft.

C-GARO, an Airbus A319-114 operated by Air Canada Rouge as flight ROU1711, was conducting a flight from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) to Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (KMSY). Shortly after takeoff, when the landing gear and flaps were retracted, the flight crew received an ECAM HYD G ENG 1 PUMP LO PR message, followed by a HYD G SYS LO PR message.The crew actioned the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) procedures and determined that the Green Hydraulic System had lost fluid. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight returned to CYYZ, where it landed uneventfully with Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) on standby. Due to a disabled nosewheel steering system, the aircraft was towed from the runway to the gate.Maintenance inspection revealed a damaged brake pressure line and broken support brackets beneath the aft cargo floor panels, which contributed to the Green Hydraulic System fluid loss.

C-GNAS, an AirSprint Cessna 525B was operating flight ASP642 from Lynden Pindling International Airport (MYNN), Nassau, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While at cruise altitude of FL450, the flight crew heard a rush of air, then noted a climbing cabin altitude and the "CABIN ALT" CAS message. The crew donned their oxygen masks and initiated an emergency descent. The passenger's oxygen masks deployed automatically. The aircraft diverted to Raleigh-Durham International Airport (KRDU), NC, and landed safely.

C-FXCA, a Boeing 767-300 operated by Air Canada as flight ACA7255, was on approach to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, when the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to a flaps asymmetry fault. The crew conducted a go-around to complete the appropriate checklist procedures and subsequently returned for a second approach. The aircraft landed without incident and was escorted to the gate by Fire and Emergency Services.

C-FHTO, a Top Aces Alpha Jet Model A was operating flight RUSTY1 from Laage Airport (ETNL), Germany. During the flight, the pilot encountered strong vibrations. Engine indications were normal and stable, the pilot checked engine response by reducing power to idle and then selecting approx. 85%, however the vibrations continued. The pilot declared an emergency and diverted to Nordholz Airport (ETMN), Germany. During the descent, the vibrations eventually ceased, and the aircraft landed safely.

C-FKOJ, an Airbus A320-200 operated by Air Canada as flight ACA7081, was conducting a flight from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Montréal/Saint-Hubert Longueuil Airport (CYHU), QC. Shortly after takeoff, the flight crew received a #4 Hot Brakes indication and declared an emergency. The crew elected to return to CYYZ, where the aircraft landed at 12:57Z (08:57 EDT). Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) attended and inspected the brakes before the aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.

C-FBAN, a privately registered, amateur built, Bushmaster floatplane, was conducting a recreational flight, under visual flight rules, from a lake located at 59° 48.23' N, 133° 46.32' W to Katina Lake, BC, (59° 12.60' N, 132° 55.25' W). The pilot took off from the lake southbound. Immediately after lifting off, the left wing dropped and contacted the water. The pilot reduced the throttle and the left wing contacted the water a second time. The aircraft spun 180° and came to an abrupt stop facing north with the nose pitched down in the shallow water. The right front door could not be opened; both occupants exited the left front door. A witness arrived at the aircraft within a few minutes to provide assistance. The pilot sustained minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. No ELT signal was received however police dispatch received an alert from a smart phone that was on board the aircraft. Emergency medical services and police attended the scene.The aircraft was recovered from the lake and will be assessed for damage.

C-GPRY, a Pilatus PC-12/45 aircraft operated by Transwest Air Limited Partners (dba Rise Air), was conducting an IFR flight from Southend/Hans Ulriksen Field Airport SK. (CKA9) to Pelican Narrows Airport (CJW4), SK. Shortly after takeoff from CKA9, the flight crew was alerted by a Central Advisory and Warning System (CAWS) with a Flap and Pusher failure indication followed by a flap asymmetry aural warning. The flight crew followed the Quick Reference Handbook and Standard Operating Procedures for flap asymmetry. After communicating with the operator's operations department, the flight crew elected to divert to La Ronge/Barber Field Airport (CYVC), SK. A PAN PAN was declared with Air Traffic Services and the aircraft landed uneventfully at CYVC.The operator's maintenance department inspected, and function tested the flap system and were unable to determine the cause of the warning indication.

C-GZII, a privately registered amateur-built Foll RV (Vans RV-6) was conducting a recreational flight from Camrose Aerodrome (CEQ3), AB, to Olds-Didsbury Aerodrome (CEA3), AB, with the pilot and one passenger on board. During the landing on Runway 10 in CEA3, the pilot was unable to maintain directional control of the aircraft and the aircraft departed the left side of the runway and impacted a farm field on the north side of the airport property. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the forward and aft fuselage, landing gear, propeller and left wing.

C-GUBF, an Air Transat A330-200 was operating flight TSC695 from Eleftherios Venizelos Airport (LGAV), Greece to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-FWWP, a Bell 206L helicopter operated by Prairie Helicopters Inc. was conducting a VFR flight from Gimli Industrial Park Airport (CYGM), MB. to the Thompson Regional Airport (CYTH), MB. During landing at the operator's helipad at CYTH, the aircraft experienced a dynamic rollover. The pilot and sole occupant was not injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The adjacent hangar door sustained damage from debris. There was no fire or fuel leakage. The Emergency Locator Transmitter (ELT) was activated, and its signal was received by the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre. CYTH Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) responded.

C-FBBT, a Black Tusk Bell 214B-1 helicopter, departed Squamish Municipal (Don Patrick Field) Airport (CYSE), BC, under visual flight rules to conduct slinging operations from the dam at Henriette Lake, BC, to Squamish, BC. The pilot was seated in the left-seat. Upon reaching the pick-up site, radio contact was established with the lead person on the ground and the crew attached a 4700-pound load to a 125-foot longline. As the pilot began to lift the load, the cargo hook opened, and the load detached. The ground crew reattached the load and a second lift was attempted. When the load reached approximately five feet above the ground, the helicopter descended due to a loss of engine power and the load struck the ground. The helicopter then moved to the right, descended, and collided with terrain on the sloped shoreline. The helicopter came to a rest on its right side. One of the main rotor blades struck the tail boom, separating the tail gearbox from the body. The pilot was seriously injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged. No emergency locator transmitter signal was received by the Canadian Mission Control Centre (CMCC). A nearby company helicopter transmitted a Mayday call that was relayed to the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) in Victoria, BC, and a Canadian Armed Forces Search and Rescue helicopter responded.

C-GANN, a privately registered Piper PA28-180 aircraft was conducting a VFR flight from Winnipeg/St. Andrews Airport, MB. (CYAV) to Erickson Municipal Airport, MB. (CKQ6).  Due to low light conditions upon arrival at CKQ6, the pilot diverted to Brandon Muni Airport, MB. (CYBR). While approaching Runway 08 at CYBR, the aircraft descended and struck the ground short of the runway in an adjacent field. The pilot and sole occupant was not injured. The aircraft's landing gear, propeller and engine compartment were substantially damaged. No leakage of fuel or oil was reported.

C-GWBT, a Boeing 737-7CT operated by WestJet, was preparing for IFR flight WJA607 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Shortly after the boarding process had ended, the passenger seated in 7E reported a broken reading light to the cabin crew. During troubleshooting, a large amount of water leaked from the overhead bin where a passenger's insulated tumbler was located. Moments later, a passenger noticed steam coming out of the light fixture and a strong smell of burning plastic was noted by the crew. After advising the pilot-in-command, it was decided to proceed with a rapid deplanement and to request that airport rescue and firefighting services attend the aircraft. The rapid deplanement took approximately 4 minutes and no injuries were reported.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft, confirmed intermittent smoke odor but no heat. The overhead Passenger Service Unit (PSU) panels from row 3 to row 8 were opened for access. All panels were inspected for water and evidence of overheating and no damage was found. The PSU panels were closed and PSU lights functions were checked serviceable in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual and the aircraft was released for service.

C-GBFU un Britten Norman BN.2A-27 exploité par Montmagny Air Service Inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Montmagny, QC (CSE5) à destination de l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) avec un pilote et un passager à bord. À environ 20 miles nautiques au nord-ouest de l'aéroport de Baie-Comeau, Qc (CYBC) le pilote a remarqué une baisse de tour moteur sur le moteur gauche. Le pilote a décidé de dérouter le vol et atterrir à l'aéroport de Baie-Comeau, Qc (CYBC) où il s'est posé sans encombre. Un essai moteur subséquent a révélé que le magnéto de gauche était défectueux. Le magnéto a été remplacé et les bougies associées ont été nettoyées. L'appareil a été remis en service.

C-GAQP, un Piper PA-12X sur flotteurs en exploitation privée effectuait un vol depuis le réservoir Pipmuacan, QC à destination d'un lac non identifié situé à environ 10 miles nautiques au nord du point de départ avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Lors de l'approche, le pilote a perdu la maitrise de l'appareil et a percuté le sol presque à la verticale, les flotteurs amortissant le choc. Les 2 occupants ont été sérieusement blessés. La balise d'urgence s'est déclenchée et les services de recherche et sauvetage ont été rapidement déployés. Les blessés ont été évacués et transportés à l'höpital.

C-ICLO, a privately owned Zenair CH-701 on floats, was conducting a takeoff from Whalley Lake, Ontario, with one pilot on board. This was the pilot’s first attempt at a full-flap takeoff. The aircraft became airborne after approximately 200 feet of takeoff run; immediately afterward, the left (port) wing dropped, and the wingtip contacted the water. The aircraft flipped to the left and came to rest submerged. The pilot, wearing a flotation vest, exited the aircraft and stood on a float while awaiting rescue. The pilot was not injured; however, the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GHQZ, a DeHavilland DHC-8-314 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways LP, was conducting an IFR flight from the Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, to the Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON. Shortly before commencing final approach into CYXL, a flight attendant became ill. A repositioning flight attendant that was onboard assumed the safety duties. The flight crew declared an emergency and continued the approach to CYXL for an uneventful landing. The cabin attendant was taken to a local hospital for medical evaluation.

C-FNNU, an Air Canada B777-300 was operating flight AC899 from Eleftherios Venizelos Airport (LGAV), Greece, to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. On the take-off, the crew rejected at high speed due to bird activity and possible engine ingestion. The crew declared a PAN PAN and requested aircraft rescue and firefighting to inspect the aircraft. On inspection a tire fuse plug had deflated a wheel.Air Canada maintenance inspected the aircraft for a high speed rejected take-off and possible bird strike. Two main wheel units replaced, and remnants of bird strike found on left wing leading edge. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJXV, an Air Canada A220 was operating flight AC1039 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Denver International Airport (KDEN), CO. On approach to R16L the crew received a TCAS RA. The procedure was followed and completed a missed approach. The aircraft landed uneventfully on the second approach and informed ATC.

C-ILLP, an RSULTRA Inc. Kangook MF was being operated on a recreational flight with another pilot also operating a powered parachute. The two aircraft departed from a field 8 nm NNE of Lethbridge Airport (CYQL), AB, flew to Taber, AB, and then returned to the departure field following the Old Man River. During the approach back to land at the departure field, the pilot encountered an unanticipated gust of wind and lost control of the powered parachute. The pilot was unable to regain control of the parachute prior to collision with terrain. The accident occurred at approximately 1915 MDT. The pilot was fatally injured.

C-GMWJ, a Boeing 737-7CT operated by WestJet Airlines, was preparing to conduct flight WJA1460 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), NV. While boarding passengers, ground personnel noticed fuel leaking from the number 2 engine, leading to a spill approximately one square meter in size. Airport operations were notified, the passengers were deplaned, and aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) were notified and arrived at the gate to monitor the situation. There were no injuries.Company maintenance determined there was a static fuel leak from the high-pressure turbine active control drain. The engine was ground run to rectify the problem, it was tested as serviceable, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPAK, an Iskwew Air Incorporated Piper PA-31-350 (Chieftain) airplane, was operating as flight SG466, under visual flight rules, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC. On approach, the pilot selected landing gear down and noticed that the gear extended slowly. The pilot flew to a nearby area to troubleshoot the issue. The pilot was able to retract and extend the landing gear normally however, the left main landing gear down and locked indicator light did not illuminate. The pilot conducted 2 low passes at CYCD and the Flight Service Station reported that the main landing gear appeared to be down. The pilot declared a Mayday and landed safely with aircraft rescue and firefighting crews standing by. The aircraft stopped on the runway, the landing gear was confirmed to be down and locked, and the aircraft taxied to the apron.Maintenance found the right engine hydraulic pump fittings were leaking and replaced the gaskets. They also found the left main landing gear microswitch sticking and replaced the microswitch. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FIUD, a privately registered, owner maintained, Cessna 170B X, was conducting circuit training at Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, with an instructor and a student pilot on board. After 3 circuits on Runway 09, the instructor exited the aircraft and the student pilot continued to conduct solo circuit practice. The first circuit was uneventful. During the second take-off roll, the pilot felt a vibration on the right side of the aircraft and reduced the power to idle. The aircraft abruptly swung 180° to the left, the right wing tip and right elevator struck the ground. The aircraft came to rest north of the paved runway surface with the nose of the aircraft facing opposite the original direction of travel. There were no reported injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FELO, a privately registered Enstrom 480B helicopter, was conducting circuit training at Tillsonburg Regional Airport (CYTB). While on approach to land during the second circuit, the two pilots on board heard an unusual external noise but were unable to determine its source. As the flight continued, a vibration developed throughout the cockpit, and the noise increased, consistent with a possible bearing malfunction.The more experienced of the two pilots assumed control and initiated a rapid descent toward the runway. During the landing, as collective input was applied, the helicopter made a hard touchdown, causing the main rotor blades to strike the tail boom. The helicopter rotated just above the runway surface before coming to rest upright.The two occupants were not injured; however, the helicopter sustained substantial damage. C-FELO is reported to be the only Enstrom 480B of its type registered in Canada.

C-FENJ, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400 operated by WestJet Encore was conducting flight WEN3217 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Fort McMurry Airport (CYMM), AB, departing Runway 12. C-GWEJ, a DeHavilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400 operated by WestJet Encore was conducting flight WEN3485 from CYEG to Grand Prairie Airport (CYQU), AB, and departed CYEG after WEN3217. During the departure, lateral spacing was reduced to 2.7 nm where 3.0 nm is required.

C-FLBV, a WestJet Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737-8CT departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, on an instrument flight rules flight to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During the takeoff, the flight crew identified that the aircraft was making uncommanded right roll inputs. The flight crew hand-flew the aircraft through 10 000 feet ASL and then the autopilot was engaged. The uncommanded right roll continued. The flight crew was able to counter the roll tendency through the use of rudder trim. In consultation with WestJet's maintenance control centre, the decision was made to burn off some fuel and then return to CYYC. Due to thunderstorms building up in the area, the decision was made to carry out an overweight landing. The aircraft landed without any further issues. Airport rescue and firefighting personnel checked brake temperatures and then the aircraft taxied to the gate.Post-maintenance activities did not identify a cause of the uncommanded roll. There have been no reoccurrences since the occurrence on 21 July 2025.

C-GPAH, a privately registered Mooney M20B, had departed Kakabeka Falls Aerodrome (CKG8), ON, on a local visual flight rules flight with only the pilot on board. After approximately 30 minutes of flying in the area of the airport, the aircraft's engine began losing power and the pilot attempted unsuccessfully to return to CKG8. The pilot executed a forced landing in a field adjacent to and just short of CKG8. The emergency locator transmitter (ELT) was activated on impact. There were no injuries. There was no fire. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GASR, a Cessna 525A operated by Airsprint Inc. was conducting flight ASP510 from Halifax Standfield International Airport (CYHZ) NS to Saint John Airport (CYSJ). During the approach, the flight crew selected flaps, however they did not move resulting in a missed approach. The checklist was reviewed and planned to land flapless. On the second approach the landing gear did not extend. The flight crew declared an emergency and completed a manual gear extension. The aircraft landed without further incident and stopped on the runway. ARFF responded and a large amount of hydraulic fluid was discovered on the runway and the aircraft was towed. The aircraft remains unserviceable and waiting for maintenance to investigate the cause.

C-FLGD, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 operated by Flair Airlines Ltd., was conducting flight FLE642 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Int'l Airport (CYWG), MB, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Int'l Airport (CYYZ). During cruise, the flight crew received a caution light for tire pressure. The crew actioned the appropriate checklist and consulted the company via ACARS. During arrival, the crew requested ARFF to be standing by as a precaution. The aircraft landed uneventfully and taxied to the assigned gate.

C-FKBT, a privately registered, Piper Aircraft Corporation PA-14 (Family Cruiser) floatplane, departed an area approximately 1.5 nautical miles east of the Fraser Lake Water Aerodrome (CBJ8), BC, on a recreational flight, under visual flight rules, to Fleming Lake, BC, with the pilot and 1 passenger onboard. This was the second flight of the day. The pilot arrived on Fraser Lake from Drywilliam Lake and beached the aircraft near White Swan Park. The pilot picked up 1 passenger and their baggage. It was reported that the beach area was rocky. After loading, the aircraft was taxied and began a 58 second take-off run. After liftoff, it was observed that the aircraft was climbing very slowly and seemed heavy. At about 200 feet above ground level (AGL), the pilot carried out a left turn onto the downwind. The aircraft was not climbing and seemed to have difficulty maintaining altitude. Approximately 35 seconds after takeoff, the aircraft appeared to stall, and the left wing dropped abruptly. The pilot was able to level the aircraft's wings just before impacting the lake. The aircraft came to rest partially submerged. The pilot swam to shore while the passenger stayed with the aircraft. Both were rescued by persons with a boat. The pilot suffered minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The aircraft was recovered from the lake and transported to a maintenance facility. An inspection determined that the aircraft’s left float had been punctured. This likely occurred during the beaching and loading process on the shore of Fraser Lake. The puncture allowed water to enter a float compartment which likely caused the aircraft to be heavier than anticipated and resulted in the inability to maintain altitude and the ensuing stall.

C-GYEO, Airbus Helicopters AS350-B3 (AStar), operated by Contour Helicopters, departed a remote work site, 37 nautical miles north of Bella Coola (CYBD), BC, under visual flight rules, for Dean River Lodge, BC, with 1 pilot and 5 passengers on board. The passengers had been preparing the wooded hillside to prepare it for a ski run. After lifting off, the pilot completed 3 slow passes over the slope to allow the workers to assess the job they had completed. At the completion of the 3rd pass, the helicopter was brought into a high hover above the site. On completion of the inspection, the pilot turned towards the centre of the valley to transition to forward flight. The helicopter started an uncommanded descent at a high vertical speed. The pilot was unable to arrest the descent and the main rotor blades impacted a tree and the helicopter started to spin counterclockwise. The pilot rolled off the throttle and the aircraft landed upright and then rolled onto its right side. The work crew that had been left at the departure point responded and assisted in recovery. The company's emergency response plan was initiated by radio. One person was seriously injured and 3 people had minor injuries. The aircraft was significantly damaged.Helicopters from other companies working in the area extracted the occupants.

C-GGDU, a Jazz Aviation DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was being operated as flight JZA8151, under instrument flight rules, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, with 37 passengers onboard. When the landing gear was selected down during final approach to CYYJ, the left landing gear indication did not indicate down and locked. The flight crew performed a missed approach and returned to CYVR. They declared a PAN PAN and used the alternate landing gear extension system to successfully lower the landing gear. The aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident.Maintenance personnel found that the left landing gear downlock-1 wiring harness had an intermittent fault and connector J23 and a solder splice were shorting to ground. The harness and connector were replaced, and the solder splice was repaired. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPCE, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited Beech 1900D, was operating flight PCO334, under instrument flight rules, from Anahim Lake Airport (CAJ4), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise flight, the captain’s electronic attitude direction indicator (EADI) screen began to glow and sparkle. This was followed by an electrical burning smell within the cockpit. The flight crew isolated the captain’s EADI and electronic horizontal situation indicator (EHSI) and the electrical burning smell dissipated. The flight crew contacted air traffic control to declare a Mayday and diverted to Campbell River Airport (CYBL), BC, where the aircraft landed safely. No injuries were reported. Maintenance personnel replaced the Captain’s EADI and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWEJ, a WestJet Encore DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), departed Kelowna International Airport (CYLW), BC, operating as WEN3331, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During the approach to CYVR when the landing gear was selected down, the nose landing gear indicator did not indicate down and locked. The flight crew carried out a missed approach and entered a holding pattern to carry out the quick reference handbook (QRH) procedure for a landing gear malfunction. The flight crew informed air traffic control (ATC) of their intentions and advised that the aircraft was at minimum fuel. After completing the QRH procedure all three landing gear lowered successfully and indicated down and locked. ATC then provided vectors for another approach during which the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to their fuel state. The aircraft landed safely. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) crews inspected the landing gear and found no issues. The aircraft arrived at the gate with approximately 118 pounds of fuel in excess of the fuel reserve requirement. Maintenance personnel carried out landing gear retraction and extension tests and did not find any faults with the indication system.

C-FZFY, un Cessna 180H sur flotteurs en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le lac Augusta, QC à destination du lac Kaupitatim, QC avec seul le pilote à bord. Alors qu’il était en vol de croisière à environ 45 miles marins au nord-est de Nemiscau (CYHH), QC un cylindre du moteur (Teledyne Continental O-470-U) s’est détacher, causant une panne complète du moteur. Le pilote a tenté de se rendre à un lac tout près, mais l’aéronef a percuté des arbres juste avant le lac. Le pilote a subi des blessures sérieuses et l’aéronef a subi des dommages importants. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée, et le signal a été reçu par le Centre conjoint de coordination de sauvetage à Trenton, ON.

C-GTHI, a Dassault Falcon 900EX operated by Skyservice Business Aviation Inc. as SYB607, was conducting a repositioning flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Shortly after takeoff, the crew received an ENGINE FIRE indication. The crew continued to climb to 5000 feet, declared MAYDAY, and requested a return to CYYZ. While actioning the appropriate checklist, the ENGINE FIRE indication was extinguished when the #1 thrust lever was brought to idle. The crew elected to leave the engine running at idle after completing the checklist and made an uneventful landing. Maintenance revealed a failed high pressure bleed air pipe (PN FGFB721531100D3) which had caused heat damage to nearby fuel lines and blistering to the top of the aft tail cone. The affected parts will be replaced, and Dassault will be consulted regarding repairs to the tail cone.

C-GBHO, un Airbus 319-114 exploité par exploité par Air Canada Rouge LP sous l’indicatif ROU1617 était en descente pour 3000 pieds, sous guidage radar pour intercepter l’axe de l’approche finale de la piste 24L à l'aéroport international de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC. Une perte d’espacement est survenue lorsque ROU1617 interceptait l’axe d’approche finale à 3400 pieds alors qu’un Airbus 330-200 exploité par Air Algérie sous l'indicatif DAH2700 qui était déjà établi en approche finale à 4000 pieds s’est retrouvé à 2,5 miles marins derrière le ROU1617. L’espacement requis était de 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical et 3 miles marins sur le plan horizontal. Les 2 appareils se sont posés sans encombre.

C-FIVR, an Air Canada B777-300 was operating flight AC01 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Haneda Airport (RJTT), Japan. During the flight a cabin crew member sustained an injury after tripping over a bag and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-FNNQ, an Air Canada B777-300 was operating flight AC833 from Brussels Airport (EBBR), Belgium, to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During cruise, a cabin crew member sustained a minor injury and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-FSCY, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight AC971 from Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International Airport (MMPR), Puerto Vallarta, MX, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Prior to departure, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned to the remaining flight attendants.

N339PL, a Boeing 737-800 operated by American Airlines, was operating flight AAL1993 from Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (KDFW), TX, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. The flight crew were concerned about the possibility of damage to one of their right main tires and declared PAN PAN during their arrival into CYYZ, requesting runway 33R for landing. The flight received priority handling and landed uneventfully on runway 33R with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by.

C-ILPY, an Airborne Windsports XT-582 Outback weight-shift basic ultra-light, was operating from private property approximately 12 NM south of Grande Prairie Airport (CYQU), AB. During ground maneuvers (intent for flight unknown) directional control was lost and the ultra-light struck a trailer. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, died from his injuries.

C-GFJZ, CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA582 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport (KDTW) aux États-Unis, à destination de l'aéroport international de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC. C-FDJZ, un CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA822, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Ronald Reagan Washington National aux États-Unis (KDCA), à destination de l'aéroport international de CYUL. Alors que les 2 aéronefs étaient à 3000 pieds en guidage pour l’approche finale, l'espacement entre les deux aéronefs a été réduit à 2,5 miles marins sur le plan horizontal alors que l'espacement requis était de 1000 ou 3 miles marins. Les 2 appareils se sont posés sans encombre.

C-GGFP, a Dehavilland DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA7954 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. After selecting the landing gear up, the flight crew received an indication that there had been a landing gear malfunction. They maintained a speed below VLE, conducted the appropriate checklists, and elected to continue the flight to CYUL. During their descent, the flight crew declared an emergency and actuated the landing gear using the alternate gear extension checklist. The flight landed uneventfully at CYUL.

C-GTUK, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Les Investissements Nolinor inc sous l'indicatif NRL796 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX) à destination de l'aéroport d’Iqualuit, Nu (CYFB). L’équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison de multiples impacts d'oiseaux au décollage. L'équipage de l'avion a décidé de retourner à CYMX. Une inspection de la piste a été effectuée avant atterrissage de NRL796 et l'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre par la suite.

C-GURG, un Canadair CL60 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, sous l'indicatif QUE10, effectuait un vol d'évacuation médicale selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Puvurnituq, QC (CYPX) à destination de Québec/Jean-Lesage Intl., QC (CYQB). Alors que l'appareil était en rapprochement de CYQB, l’équipage a déclaré un problème de contrôle du tangage en raison d’un canal numéro du compensateur en tangage indiquait une survitesse, l’autre canal a alors été utilisé. Par précaution, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence avant l’atterrissage. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre.

C-GWNQ, a privately registered, amateur-built Bushmaster Super 22 airplane departed Lillooet Aerodrome (CYLI), BC, on a visual flight rules recreational flight to Chilliwack Airport (CYCW), BC, with only the pilot on board. Shortly after takeoff, the aircraft’s engine (Aerosport Power, O-375-A2A) lost power. The aircraft levelled off at approximately 400 feet above ground level (AGL) and turned back toward CYLI. While in the descending turn, the aircraft struck trees at a height of approximately 35 feet AGL and then impacted level terrain. The aircraft came to rest inverted. Local first responders attended the scene and provided medical assistance. The pilot was fatally injured. There was no post-impact fire. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The TSB deployed to the site.

C-FFLC, a Flair Airlines Limited Boeing 737-86J (737-800), was being operated as flight FLE758, under instrument flight rules, from Kelowna International Airport (CYLW), BC, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. C-FSNY, an Airsprint Incorporated Embraer EMB-550 (Legacy 500) was being operated as flight ASP858, under visual flight rules, from CYLW to Boundary Bay Airport (CZBB), BC. Both aircraft departed Runway 16. The Boeing took off first. During the initial climb out of CYLW, the Boeing was through approximately 12 000 feet above sea level (ASL), when the crew received a traffic alert and collision avoidance system resolution advisory (TCAS RA) directing them to level off and descend. The TCAS RA was triggered by the proximity of the Embraer at approximately the same altitude. Air traffic control (ATC) had passed the traffic information to the Embraer who reported that the Boeing 737-86J was in sight. ATC did not pass traffic to the Boeing. The Embraer was levelled off and turned to avoid the Boeing as its crew followed the TCAS RA direction. The two aircraft passed at a lateral distance of approximately 1 nautical mile (NM) while at approximately 12 000 feet ASL. Both aircraft then continued to their destinations without further incident.

C-FFLC, a Flair Airlines Limited Boeing 737-86J (737-800), operating as flight FLE759, departed Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, under instrument flight rules, to Kelowna International Airport (CYLW), BC. C-GTRI, a privately registered Piper PA-24-250 (Comanche) was flying from Vernon Airport (CYVK), BC to Medicine Hat Airport (CYXH), AB. During final approach to Runway 16 at CYLW, the Boeing was descending through approximately 5500 feet above sea level (ASL) when the crew received a traffic alert and collision avoidance system resolution advisory (TCAS RA) directing them to climb. The TCAS RA was triggered by the proximity of the Piper that was climbing through 5200 feet ASL. The two aircraft passed approximately 1 nautical mile (NM) laterally and 200 feet vertically from each other. The Boeing conducted a missed approach and then returned to CYLW where it landed without further incident.

C-FYAO, un Cessna 185 sur flottes en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis la rivière Moisie, Qc, à destination du lac Costebelle, Qc. Durant la montée initiale, à environ 200 pieds AGL, le moteur (Teledyne Continental IO-520-D) a eu des ratés. Le pilote a immédiatement tourné vers la rivière et le moteur s’est complètement arrêté. La hauteur n’a pas permis de planer jusqu’à la rivière et l’aéronef est entré en collision avec des arbres. L’aéronef a subi des dommages importants et les 2 occupants ont subi des blessures mineures. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s'est déclenchée.

C-FAUA, an Insignia College Ltd. Piper PA-34-200T (Seneca II) was performing circuit training, under visual flight rules, at the Boundary Bay Airport (CZBB), BC, with 1 instructor and 1 student on board. During the 6th circuit, simulated single engine operations were demonstrated. When the aircraft settled on Runway 25, the propellers struck the runway, and the aircraft came to an abrupt halt on the paved surface resting on its belly. The 2 occupants were able to egress without incident. Post-occurrence, it was determined that the landing gear selector was in the up position. There were no injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. There was damage to the propellers, flaps, and underside of the aircraft. It was lifted from the runway and the landing gear was extended normally. The aircraft will be assessed for damage.

LN-RKN, an Airbus 330-343X aircraft operated by Scandinavian Airlines, was conducting flight SAS910 from Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ to Copenhagen/Kastrup Intl (EKCH), Denmark. During cruise flight a DOOR L AFT CABIN message was received by the flight crew indicating an unsafe door 4L. At the same time, both the captain and first officer sensed a cabin pressure drop. The flight crew donned oxygen masks, started an emergency descent, and declared an emergency with ATS. Shortly after initiating the descent the captain observed normal cabin pressure indication and levelled the aircraft at FL320. The captain consulted with maintenance personnel via SATCOM and it was determined that a faulty 4L door sensor was likely responsible for the warning message. The emergency was cancelled with ATS and the aircraft was climbed to FL370 and continued to destination without further incident. Maintenance personnel replaced the faulty 4L door proximity sensor.

TALN28, a military variant of the Sikorsky S-92 helicopter (CH-148 Cyclone), operated by Royal Canadian Air Force, was conducting a local IFR flight from Shearwater Heliport (CYAW), NS. C-FLFN, a Sikorsky S-76C operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited, was conducting a VFR MEDEVAC flight from Halifax (QE II Health Sciences Centre) Heliport (CHQE), NS to Halifax/Stanfield (CYHZ), NS. TALN28 was returning to CYAW for landing and was inbound for the COPTER RNAV 16H approach. Communications for TALN28 was transferred from the YHZ Terminal controller to the CYAW Precision Approach Radar (PAR) controller, however TALN28 had not established communication with the PAR controller. TALN28 was tracking a 256 degrees true heading at 1900 feet above sea level (ASL) and at about the same time C-FLFN departed CHQE and was tracking a 026 degrees true heading at 1700 ASL. C-FLFN initially was communicating with the CYAW Advisory controller before being transferred to YHZ Tower. C-FLFN was then given the information for TALN28 and reported having the traffic visual. C-FLFN began a descent, and the 2 helicopters passed at 0.5 NM horizontally and 400 feet vertically. The Directorate of Flight Safety of the Royal Canadian Air Force is investigating.

C-FCAE, a Cargojet B767 was operating flight CJT1801 from Narita International Airport (RJAA), Japan to Hangzhou International Airport (ZSHC), China. Prior to the initial departure, the Left Bus TIE tripped, resulting in the left and center IRS going offline and triggering an audible horn warning. The aircraft returned to the gate and the issue was rectified. The subsequent departure was completed without further incident.During climb, at approximately FL230, the Left Bus TIE tripped again. The associated checklist was actioned, and the APU was started. A Left Gen message was then displayed on the EICAS. A PAN PAN was declared and the crew elected to return to RJAA. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GZHF, un Cessna 152 exploité par Lachute Aviation, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à destination de l’aéroport de Lachute, QC (CSE4) dans le cadre de pratiques solo sous l’autorisation d’un pilote-instructeur. Lors d’un atterrissage, l’aéronef a touché durement et la roue de nez s’est brisée. L’aéronef s’est immobilisé sur la piste et il n’y a eu aucun blessé. L’aéronef a subi des dommages au train avant, au mur pare-feu, au moteur et à l’hélice. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée.

C-GKSP, a KASI Aviation Services Inc. Piper PA-31-350 (Chieftain) departed Merritt Aerodrome (CAD5), BC, on a survey flight, under visual flight rules, to Pitt Meadows Airport (CYPK), BC, with 1 flight crew member, and 1 survey operator on board. During descent in the vicinity of Hope Aerodrome (CYHE), BC, a decrease in the right engine's (Lycoming LTIO-540) oil pressure was observed. The pilot elected to divert to Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, and advised air traffic control (ATC) they were having a technical issue. On approach to Runway 25 at CYXX, the pilot noted that the oil pressure for the right engine had decreased further and then shut down that engine as a precaution. The pilot did not declare an emergency. The aircraft landed without further incident at 1258 Pacific Daylight Time, with aircraft rescue and firefighting services, called out by CYXX ATC, standing by. The aircraft was taxied to parking under its own power. The aircraft has been grounded pending a maintenance investigation.

C-FDCH, a Canadian Helicopters Ltd. Sikorsky S-61N was operating on a local fire suppression mission to wildfire SWF-092-2025 U18, approximately 61 NM NNW of Slave Lake Airport (CYZH), AB. During firefighting operations, the helicopter was 1.9 hours into the first 3.3-hour tanking cycle of the day. While on short final to the dip site, the flight crew noticed a burning smell that entered the cabin, which was shortly thereafter followed by the No. 2 engine (General Electric CT58-140-2) fire light illuminating. A climb was initiated as the dip site was not suitable for landing. The flight crew actioned the engine fire checklist, extinguished the fire and shut down the No. 2 engine. A PAN PAN was declared and the helicopter returned to CYZH where it landed uneventfully on the runway. There were no injuries. Company maintenance removed the No. 2 engine, and it has been routed to an engine shop for examination.

C-GOIM, an Airbus A321- 271NX aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC155 from Brussels Intl (EBBR), Belgium to Montréal/Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. During the flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform their duties. A supplementary crew member was on board and available to assume the jump-seat position and safety-related duties of the ill crew member. The fight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FEUJ, un Piper Pa12 sur flotte en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à destination du le lac des 2 Montagnes dans le cadre de pratiques solo sous l’autorisation d’un pilote-instructeur. En virage en finale, il y a eu un bris dans la manivelle de commande du compensateur de l’élévateur. Le pilote a tenté de se poser et a perdu la maitrise, le bout de l’aile gauche a touché l’eau, l’avion a ensuite basculé partiellement vers la droite et l’aile droite a frappé l’eau. Le pilote a réussi à ramener l’avion au quai et a constaté des dommages à l’aile droite et au saumon de l’aile gauche. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FLDO, un hélicoptère Airbus AS350 B3 exploité par Innukoptères Inc., effectuait un vol avec une charge à l'élingue selon les règles de vol à vue environ 10 WNW de Saint-Urbain, QC. Durant une opération d’élingage (short-line), après avoir déposé le cargo, une rafale de vent a fait déplacer l’aéronef vers l’arrière et le rotor de queue est entré en contact avec un arbre. Le pilote a ressenti des vibrations anormales dans les palonniers et a immédiatement effectué un atterrissage de précaution dans un endroit sécuritaire. L’aéronef a subi de dommages et il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GMSL un hélicoptère Robinson R44 en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue au départ une propriété privée située aux abords de la ville de Sainte Marie, QC, en direction de Magog, QC, avec le pilote seul à bord. Durant le vol, dans le secteur de St Severin, l’hélicoptère a été observé en piqué vers le sommet d’une colline boisée d’érables. L’hélicoptère a percuté la cime des arbres et s’est écrasé. Un incendie s’est déclenché. Le pilote est décédé et l’aéronef a été détruit.

C-GLQX, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight PTR2284 from St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL to Halifax/Stanfield (CYHZ), NS. While in cruise the fight crew observed a FLAP POWER caution message, actioned the QRH and reset the flap system. When about 20 minutes prior to descent the FLAP POWER caution message illuminated a second time. The flight crew actioned the ABNORMAL FLAP LANDING checklist and declared a PAN PAN with ATS. The flight crew conducted a flapless landing at CYHZ and stopped on the runway for emergency services to inspect the aircraft before taxi to the gate. Maintenance personnel replaced the Flap Control Unit and rigged the left-hand Rotary Variable Differential Transducer.

C-FCCJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing B767-323 (B767-300) departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, on flight CJT2389, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew members on board. While climbing through flight level 330 (FL330) the pilots felt a slight rumble. Prior to levelling off at FL360, the green nose gear light illuminated, indicating that the nose gear was extended. A LDG GEAR MONITOR status message was subsequently received. The flight crew advised maintenance of the issue via the Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS). The flight continued to CYVR, and the nose gear extended indication extinguished. While on approach to Runway 26L at CYVR, when the landing gear was selected down, both green main landing gear lights illuminated, but the green nose landing gear light did not. Neither gear disagreement indications nor configuration warnings were observed with flaps selected at 25. A missed approach was conducted and the landing gear indication issue was communicated to air traffic control (ATC). The aircraft was vectored to the south of the airport while flight crew performed troubleshooting activities. A low approach was then conducted to Runway 26L to allow for a visual inspection by the tower controller. The controller confirmed the nose landing gear was extended. Before landing, the flight crew declared a Mayday. The aircraft landed without further incident and was taxied to the gate under its own power.A post-flight maintenance inspection identified multiple faults with the Proximity Switch Electronic Unit (PSEU). The PSEU was replaced along with proximity sensors, and the nose gear down annunciator light. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GVIX, a Vancouver Island Air Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-3T (Turbo Otter), was preparing to depart Campbell River Water Aerodrome (CAE3), BC, for Knight Inlet Lodge, BC, under visual flight rules, with 1 flight crew member, and 14 passengers on board. After engine start, the aircraft was untied from the dock by a ground handler. The aircraft began to move forward, parallel to the dock, and the pilot had difficulty stopping the aircraft. The pilot signaled the ground handler to retie the aircraft to the dock, but the ground handler did not respond to the signal. The pilot then exited the aircraft in an attempt to arrest its forward movement from outside the aircraft. A second company pilot entered the aircraft after the first pilot had exited and turned off the aircraft engine. Before the aircraft engine was shut off, it had moved approximately 20 feet forward along the dock and collided with a second company Turbo Otter that had been parked in front of the occurrence aircraft. The pilot of the occurrence aircraft sustained minor injuries when exiting the aircraft. No passenger injuries were reported.C-GVIX sustained minor damage, limited to the engine and propeller. C-GVIR sustained substantial damage to its elevators and vertical stabilizer.

C-FPWP, a privately registered Diamond DA-62 was operating on a local flight from Josephburg Aerodrome (CFB6), AB. During cruise the flight crew received a #2 engine (Austro, E4P) ECU A and B caution indication. The aircraft returned to CFB6 using a low power setting on the right engine. The aircraft landed uneventfully and during rollout, the right engine began to shake and was immediately shut down. The aircraft was undamaged and there were no injuries.

C-GGWV, un Boeing 737-4Y0 exploité par Les Investissements Nolinor Inc. sous l’indicatif NRL665 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Wabush, NL (CYWK) à destination de Bagotville, QC (CYBG) avec 90 passagers et 7 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en croisière au niveau de vol 340, il a subi la perte du système hydraulique B. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et l’ATC a autorisé le vol à procéder directement vers sa destination. L’équipage a complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et l’aéronef s’est posé sur la piste 11 sans encombre avec les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) déployés.

N622EL, un Cirrus SF50 en exploitation privé effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Sherbrooke, QC (CYSC) à destination de Montréal Intl (Mirabel), QC (CYMX). Lors de l’approche vers la piste 24 une indication anormale du train d’atterrissage est apparue. Le pilote a fait une remise des gaz et a déclaré un état d’urgence. Par la suite, le pilote a fait un circuit VFR et est revenu se poser sur la piste 24 sans encombre.

C-GMIU, un Boeing B737-800 (Max) exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA324 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) à destination de l'aéroport international de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC. C-FJFZ, un CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA824, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Ronald Reagan Washington National aux États-Unis (KDCA), à destination de l'aéroport international de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC. Alors que l’ACA324 était établi en approche finale pour la piste 24L, le JZA824 était en guidage radar pour intercepter l’approche finale de la piste 24R. L’espacement entre les deux aéronefs a été réduit à 900 pieds sur le plan vertical et 2,2 miles marins sur le plan horizontal alors que l’espacement requis était de 1000 et 3 miles marins. Les 2 appareils se sont posés sans encombre.

C-FCJZ, a Jazz CRJ900 was operating flight JZA596 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Sacramento International Airport (KSMF), CA. During the descent, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties. EMS was requested, the flight attendant walked off the aircraft with the assistance from EMS.

CF-CWL, a privately registered, amateur built, Piel Emeraude CP 301 airplane, was taxiing for departure for a local recreational flight from the Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, with only the pilot onboard. While taxiing for takeoff, control of the aircraft was lost when it yawed inadvertently to the left and ground looped on Taxiway A. No injuries were reported. The aircraft was substantially damaged. Both main landing gears broke off at their mounts and there was damage to the propeller and an aileron. The aircraft was recovered to the hangar and will be assessed for damage.

C-FEUR, un ATR 72-202 exploité par Summit Air sous l’indicatif SUT7394 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Kuujjuarapik, Québec (CYGW) à destination de Puvirnituq, QC (CYPX). Un Dash-8 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE880 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) à destination de Puvirnituq, QC (CYPX).
