Alors que SUT7394 était en croisière à 16 000 pieds dans l’espace aérien non contrôlé à environ 60 miles marins (nm) au nord de CYGL, l’équipage a remarqué l’AIE880 environ 10 nm devant passant 15 000 pieds en montée. Pendant l’échange de communication avec AIE880, l’équipage du SUT7394 a reçu et a suivi l’avis de résolution du système de surveillance du trafic et d'évitement des collisions (TCAS RA). L’AIE880 a fait un palier et il est passé 400 pieds sous SUT7394.

N189DN, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL154 from Boston Logan Intl, MA (KBOS) to Dublin Intl, Ireland (EIDW). While in cruise near position 44°20'N / 063°44'W, the crew received an EICAS L OIL FILTER message. The crew completed the QRH for OIL FILTER procedure and coordinated with dispatch. As the procedure did not permit an oceanic crossing with the indication displayed, the crew declared an emergency and elected to divert to New York, John F. Kennedy Intl, NY (KJFK), where it landed without further incident with the left engine runningPost Occurrence actions/Maintenance:Maintenance inspected the magnetic chip detectors and carried out the following corrective actions: removed and replaced the left engine oil filter, removed and replaced the differential pressure switch, and confirmed the fault message cleared. The aircraft was subsequently returned to service.

C-GHJU, a Helijet International Inc. Learjet 31A, departed King County International Airport (KBFI), WA, operating as flight JBA381, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew and 3 passengers on board. During the takeoff roll at KBFI, a severe vibration was felt which became worse as the aircraft’s speed increased. The flight crew suspected a nose gear issue and contacted air traffic control (ATC) to coordinate a low-level fly past at CYVR to check for damage to the front wheel prior to landing. A PAN PAN was declared by the flight crew and emergency services were requested to be on standby. No damage was noted during the fly past and the aircraft proceeded to land safely at CYVR. During landing the nose wheel was held off the runway until approximately 70 knots and no vibrations were felt after it touched down.Maintenance personnel found the source of the vibration to be an internal balancing weight had de-bonded within the nose landing gear tire. The tire had recently been replaced and had only accumulated 2.4 hours of airtime. The company has submitted a service difficulty report (SDR).

C-FFEL, a Flair Airlines Limited Boeing 737-8 (Max 8) departed Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, operating as flight FLE601, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. C-FGWJ, a WestJet Boeing 737-7CT (737-700), was being operated as flight WJA107, from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, under instrument flight rules, to CYVR. Both aircraft were on final to Runway 26R with the WestJet flight ahead of the Flair aircraft. During the approach, the required separation was lost. The separation between the aircraft was reduced to approximately 2.8 nautical miles (NM) laterally when 3 NM was required. Both aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FIQI, a Cessna 182 operated by Skydive S.W.O.O.P., departed Dundas Air Plaza (CPG4) on a parachute drop flight. While climbing through 7800 feet ASL, the engine began to shake violently. The pilot applied carburetor heat, reduced engine power, enriched the mixture, and noted engine indications of 18 inHg at 2500 RPM, with oil pressure and temperature remaining within normal limits. Engine RPM was reduced to 2200, and the pilot instructed the jump door to be opened. A normal jump run was completed at 8300 feet ASL.After the jump, the door was closed and the pilot initiated descent, attempting several actions to reduce the vibration. The pilot contacted Toronto Centre to report the descent and was handed off to Toronto Terminal. Shortly afterward, oil pressure was observed near the bottom of the normal range, with temperature remaining normal. During a turn toward the drop zone, the engine vibration increased significantly. The pilot pitched for 70–80 mph and elected to keep the engine running until overhead the drop zone.The pilot declared an emergency with Toronto Terminal, reporting a partial engine failure. Although Hamilton International Airport (CYHM) was offered as an alternate, the pilot determined the aircraft could not glide that distance and elected to return to Dundas Air Plaza. The pilot selected Runway 18, squawked 7700, conducted left-hand orbits over the threshold, and shut down the engine prior to landing. The aircraft landed without further incident and was removed from the runway using a towbar.A subsequent inspection revealed that the engine crankcase had failed above the No. 3 cylinder, resulting in separation of the cylinder from the crankcase. The engine was removed for detailed inspection and overhaul

C-GFCI, an Airbus A320-214 operated by Air Canada Rouge as flight ROU1715, was taxiing for departure when the flight crew received an ECAM ENG 2 FAIL message. At the same time, ATC reported visible flames coming from the No. 2 engine. The flight crew stopped the aircraft, actioned the ECAM procedures, and shut down the No. 2 engine. Although there were no fire indications in the cockpit, the associated fire bottle was discharged as a precaution. Aircraft rescue and firefighting responded and inspected the aircraft, confirming residual heat but no active fire. The aircraft taxied back to the gate using the No. 1 engine, and the flight was terminated.

C-FRJV, an Airbus Helicopter AS350B2 operated by Heli-Recon Aerial Support Services Inc., was conducting a local survey flight from Carswell Lake Camp, SK. While conducting low altitude operations the helicopter contacted the water surface of Lake Carswell in a level attitude and the helicopter was quickly submerged in the water. Both the pilot and passenger were able to egress from the sinking aircraft and swam to shore before being rescued by bystanders. It was reported that the lake water was glassy and there was reduced visibility due to the setting of the sun.The helicopter is still resting at the bottom of the lake and the operator is coordinating resources to recover the aircraft and assess the damages.

C-FYFB, a privately registered Piper PA-28R-200, was departing on Runway 33 at Sarnia Chris Hadfield Airport (CYZR), ON, for a local flight. During the takeoff roll, the aircraft veered off the left side of the runway onto the grass due to a rudder issue. The aircraft came to rest in the infield approximately 150 feet left of the Runway 33 centerline, near the 1000-foot marker. The nose and right main landing gear collapsed, and the right wing sustained damage. There were no injuries reported.

C-FXGC, a privately registered Piper PA-28-140, departed Orillia Airport with a pilot and two passengers on board, destined for Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ). The aircraft climbed to 3000 feet.During descent, when the throttle was retarded, the engine stopped producing power. The pilot attempted a restart without success, advised Toronto City Tower, and elected to conduct a forced landing in an illuminated soccer field. The flight was being conducted during the hours of darkness.The aircraft struck a chain-link fence before reaching the intended landing area and came to rest nearby. The occupiable space remained intact, and there were no injuries to the occupants. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.A post-occurrence examination of the wreckage revealed no mechanical anomalies that would have precluded normal engine operation. Sufficient uncontaminated fuel was on board, and a subsequent ground run of the engine demonstrated normal performance. Examination of the carburetor heat control indicated it was in the cold position at the time of impact.Meteorological data for CYTZ at the time indicated a temperature of 18°C and a dew point of 15°C, conditions conducive to moderate carburetor icing at cruise power, serious carburetor icing at descent power.

C-GKKC, a SA226-TC operated by 2080061 Ontario Inc. (dba SkyCare Air Ambulance), was conducting IFR flight PHX370 from Kenora Airport (CYQK), ON, to Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON. While on short final, the flight crew observed a flock of seagulls crossing the runway and, immediately prior to touchdown, one of the seagulls was ingested by the number 2 engine (Garrett TPE331-10UA-511G). Upon applying reverse thrust, the pilot flying felt that the number 2 engine was losing power and saw the RPM and torque indications were decreasing rapidly. The flight crew decided to do a precautionary shutdown of the number 2 engine while taxiing to the apron. There was no further incident.The operator's maintenance found that a bird had been ingested through the intake of the right-hand engine. The number 2 engine was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTSJ, an Airbus A330 operated by Air Transat as flight TSC309, was departing Rome–Fiumicino International Airport (LIRF), Italy, for Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During climb-out, the crew received an ECAM WHEEL TIRE LO PR message associated with the No. 8 wheel, which was indicating 150 psi. Over the course of the flight, the tire pressure dropped to 0 psi.On approach to CYYZ, the crew declared a PAN PAN due to the flat tire indication. The aircraft landed on Runway 15L, where aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) confirmed one flat tire, intact. The aircraft taxied off the runway under its own power but subsequently became disabled on a taxiway and required towing to the gate.

C-FCME, a Central Mountain Air Ltd. Beechcraft 1900D was operating flight GLR2704 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, under instrument flight rules with 2 flight crew onboard. On approach to CYYJ, the flight crew declared minimum fuel to ATC. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FXNJ, a privately registered Cessna 172B, was landing on Runway 08 at Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON, with winds reported from 360 degrees, creating a left crosswind. During the landing roll, the aircraft veered left, the right main landing gear failed, and the right wing contacted the runway surface, resulting in a 180-degree ground loop. The aircraft came to rest at the intersection of Runways 08/26 and 14/32. The aerodrome was temporarily closed until the aircraft was removed, causing delays to local general aviation traffic. There were two persons on board, and no injuries were reported.

C-FEWJ, a WestJet Boeing 737-8 (Max 8) was being operated as flight WJA113 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. C-GGBY, a Central Mountain Air Limited Beech 1900D was being operated as flight GLR9173, under instrument flight rules, from Campbell River Airport (CYBL), BC, to CYVR. Both aircraft were on final to Runway 08L with the Beech 1900 ahead of the Boeing 737-8. Air traffic control (ATC) instructed the Boeing 737-8 flight crew to slow to final approach speed, but they were unable to so before lateral separation with the Beech 1900D was reduced to approximately 1.8 nautical miles (NM). The planned separation was 4 NM, so the Boeing 737-8 crew was directed by ATC to conduct a missed approach. Both aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GOKE, an Air Transat A321-271NX was operating flight TSC955 from Holguin/Frank Pais International Airport (MUHG), Cuba, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During climb, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst remaining flight attendants.

C-GUFR, un Airbus A330-243 exploité par Air Transat A.T. sous l'indicatif TSC309 effectuaient un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport international Léonard de Vinci, Rome (LIRF) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Peu après le décollage de LIRF, l’équipage a remarqué un message sur l’ECAM indiquant que le pneu de la roue #7 avait une pression basse de 170 PSI. La pression a continué à diminuer durant le vol pour atteindre zéro. L’équipage a appelé la compagnie pour les aviser de la situation et a déclaré une urgence au centre de contrôle aérien. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre et s’est immobilisé sur la piste. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs ont inspecté le train d’atterrissage et l’aéronef a été remorqué jusqu’à une porte pour le débarquement des passagers.

C-GOKH, an Air Transat A321-271NX, was operating flight TSC153 from New Jorge Chávez International Airport (SPJC), Peru, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-GTSJ, un Airbus A330-243 exploité par Air Transat A.T. sous l'indicatif TSC309 effectuaient un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport international Léonard de Vinci, Rome (LIRF) à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ). Peu après le décollage de LIRF, l’équipage a remarqué un message sur l’ECAM indiquant que le pneu de la roue #8 avait une pression basse de 150 PSI. La pression a continué à diminuer durant le vol pour atteindre zéro. L’équipage a décidé de poursuivre le vol jusqu’à sa destination et a déclaré une urgence au centre de contrôle aérien. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 15L où il s’est immobilisé. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs ont inspecté le train d’atterrissage et l’aéronef a été remorqué jusqu’à une porte pour le débarquement des passagers.

C-GMXB, a Boeing 737 Max operated by WestJet Airlines Ltd, flight WJA408, was conducting IFR flight from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Moncton/Greater Moncton Romeo Leblanc International Airport (CYQM), NB, with 129 passengers and 6 crew members onboard. At FL390, approximately one hour from Moncton display unit indicated fluctuating vibrations on the No. 2 engine (CFMI LEAP-1B). The vibration reached 4.1, the flight crew completed the High Engine Vibration checklist, declared a Mayday and initiated a drift-down to FL240. After communicating with dispatch and maintenance control, the crew elected to continue to destination. The cabin crew were advised of the engine indication anomaly, and a normal landing was conducted in CYQM with no damage and no injuries.

C-FDPW, a float-equipped De Havilland DHC-2 MK.1 operated by MHA Enterprises Ltd., was conducting a VFR flight from St. Theresa Point, MB float base to Makepeace Lake, MB, with a pilot and 4 passengers on board. When the aircraft was approximately 0.5 NM from Makepeace Lake, the aircraft collided with terrain. The aircraft ELT did activate. The pilot was able to contact emergency services using his mobile phone. Island Lake RCMP and Search and Rescue Technicians deployed to the site. The pilot sustained serious injuries, and 4 passengers were fatally injured. There was a post-crash fire. TSB deployed to the site.

C-GUIC un Cessna 185 privé sur flotteurs effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue proche du lac Weldie (N46 43 18, W76 39 35), QC, 40 milles marins au nord-ouest de Maniwaki, QC (CYMW), avec le pilote et 2 passagers. En raison de problèmes de moteur le pilote a tenté un atterrissage forcé sur le lac Weldie. Aucune blessure n'a été signalée. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence s'est déclenchée. Le Centre conjoint de coordination des opérations de sauvetage (JRCC) de Trenton a dépêché un hélicoptère pour récupérer le pilote et les passagers car le lieu de l'accident étant situé dans une zone isolée et inaccessible par la route.

C-GUJZ, un Dehavilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l’indicatif JZA7955, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Toronto/City Centre Airport, ON (CYTZ). Lors de la montée initiale, l’équipage a rencontré un problème de contrôle du roulis lors d’un virage. Une fois l’aéronef stabilisé, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence au centre de contrôle aérien et a décidé de revenir se poser à CYUL où il a atterri sans encombre.

C-FDSN, a VIH Helicopters Ltd. Sikorsky S61N was conducting a flight in support of firefighting operations from Lac La Biche Aerodrome (CYLB), AB, to a remote site approximately 50 nm north of CYLB. Early in cruise, the flight crew observed noticeable main rotor vibration and commenced a precautionary landing. Prior to touchdown, the bucket and longline assembly were released from the helicopter to facilitate the landing. The helicopter landed uneventfully, there were no injuries.After landing, it was determined that a fault in the automatic flight control system (AFCS) was the cause of the vibration. The fault was rectified, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FGWJ, a Boeing 737-700 operated by Westjet, was operating as flight WS104 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While on approach, the crew observed, but were unable to avoid, a flock of birds on the approach path. The aircraft landed normally and taxied to the gate with the flaps extended. After engine shutdown, leaking hydraulic fluid and smoke from the right main brake assembly were observed. Airport rescue and firefighting (ARFF) were called to assist. There was no fire observed, the smoke subsided without intervention, and the passengers deplaned normally. There were no injuries.Company maintenance found damage to the right-hand leading-edge slat and a hydraulic return line. The aircraft was repaired, checked for faults and within tolerances, and returned to service.

C-FWVJ, a Westjet Boeing 737-800, was operating as flight WS1536 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, under instrument flight rules, to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (KPHX), AZ. During departure from CYYC at approximately 30 000 feet, a stabilizer out of trim caution illuminated and both pilot electric trim switches were found inoperative. The crew completed the appropriate checklist, declared a PAN PAN, and elected to return to CYYC. The aircraft completed an uneventful non-normal landing. There were no injuries.Company maintenance replaced the stab trim motor, completed a function test, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYFW, a privately registered, Cessna A185F floatplane departed Ootsa Lake, BC (53º 48' N, 126º 03’ W) on a recreational flight to Nadsilnich Lake, BC (53º 42' N, 122º 52’ W) with only the pilot on board. In preparation for landing at Nadsilnich Lake, the pilot conducted 2 inspection passes and noted that the water was glassy but clear of any obstacles. Visibility was approximately 6 statute miles due to smoke in the area. During final approach, the aircraft touched down on the water sooner than the pilot expected. The aircraft overturned and came to an abrupt halt. The pilot egressed underwater through the pilot’s door and climbed onto the aircraft’s floats where they were able to flag down and get assistance from fishers in a nearby boat. The emergency locator transmitter (ELT) did not activate. The pilot received minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The aircraft was recovered from the lake, and transported to a facility where the damage will be assessed.

C-GECG, a privately registered, Cessna 525B (Citation CJ3), departed Masset Airport (CZMT), BC, under instrument flight rules, for Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise flight, approximately 5 minutes prior to the top of descent, the pilot reduced engine power as a result of an airspeed increase caused by turbulence. After approximately 5 seconds, the thrust levers were advanced, and the No. 1 engine (Williams International FJ44-3A) flamed out. The pilot completed the engine failure procedures outlined in the emergency checklist and the aircraft flight manual (AFM) and declared an emergency with air traffic control (ATC). The pilot confirmed there was no fire or structural damage to the engine and noted that the N1 and N2 engine sections were still rotating, and that oil pressure was present. The pilot then initiated the single engine restart procedure. The engine restarted successfully, and all engine parameters returned to normal. The aircraft continued without further incident and the landed safely at CYVR.Maintenance personnel analyzed data from the Full Authority Digital Engine Control (FADEC) and determined that there was a fault with a fuel valve in the No. 1 engine Fuel Control Unit (FCU). The FCUs in both engines were replaced following guidance from a Williams International service bulletin which addressed engine flameouts at high altitudes following power reduction.

C-GEFA, an Air Canada Airbus A330 was operating flight AC73 from Mohammed V International Airport (GMMN), Morocco, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During take-off a cabin crew member became ill, and duties were redistributed to remaining cabin crew members.

N787UA, a Boeing 777-200 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL927 from Frankfurt Airport (EDDF), Germany, to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA, U.S. While in cruise, the flight crew observed multiple Engine Indication and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) messages associated with an electrical fault. The flight crew coordinated with company operations maintenance control and dispatch and determined the messages could not be resolved by accomplishing the non-normal checklist. The crew declared a MAYDAY, diverted to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, and landed uneventfully. Maintenance completed troubleshooting and identified a faulty Overhead Panel Bus Controller (OPBC) as the direct cause of the disruption. Repair was completed, and after the aircraft was tested without a recurrence of faults, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GXPM, an Air Tractor AT-502A, operated by Bradley Airspray, was landing at Lloydminster Airport (CYLL), AB, after a flight to conduct aerial application work. Upon landing, the aircraft encountered a gust that lifted the right wing and caused the left wing to strike the runway. The aircraft remained on the runway and the pilot was not injured. Damage was limited to the left wingtip and spray assembly.The affected parts were repaired, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKKB, a Kenn Borek Air Ltd. Douglas DC-3C Basler BT-67, was conducting a visual flight rules flight in support of firefighting operations from the Fort St. John Airport (CYXJ), BC, to a remote site approximately 57 nm southwest of CYXJ. While in a holding pattern waiting for guidance from the bird dog aircraft, the flight crew noticed a decreasing oil pressure indication on the number 1 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-67R). The crew elected to divert back to CYXJ and declared a PAN PAN. The crew then observed oil streaks on the nacelle of the affected engine, actioned the appropriate checklists to shut down the engine, and declared a MAYDAY. The aircraft conducted an uneventful single-engine approach and landing.Company maintenance determined a cracked vent tube was leaking oil. The affected part was replaced, the engine ground run, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GNKG, a General Lee Aviation Cessna 172M was being operated by a student pilot who was carrying out take-off and landing exercises on Runway 30 at the Wetaskiwin Regional Airport (CEX3), AB. During a landing attempt, the aircraft ballooned. The pilot initiated a go-around, during which the aircraft entered a stall and a loss of control occurred. While still airborne, the aircraft veered left (west) off the runway, where the nose wheel and propeller struck the grass. The aircraft came to rest approximately 280 feet from the runway centerline near the Bravo Taxiway intersection. The pilot exited the aircraft without assistance and, once clear, called for help. The student pilot received minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FGYN, a Top Aces Inc., McDonnell Douglas A-4N, was taking off from Cold Lake/Group Captain R.W. McNair (CYOD), AB. As the aircraft was accelerating through 100 knots, the pilot heard a popping noise and observed the canopy seal deflate and daylight becoming visible around the front section of the canopy. A takeoff abort was initiated. Moments later, the canopy departed from the aircraft. The aircraft taxied back to parking under its own power. The pilot was uninjured. Subsequent inspection of the aircraft revealed damage to the left horizontal stabilizer, the engine and the spine of the aircraft. The aircraft has been quarantined pending an ongoing internal investigation.

C-GPDJ, a Cargojet Airways Boeing B767-3Q8 operating as CJT2386, was climbing out of Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, enroute to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON. The flight crew observed an engine surge (General Electric, CF6-80C2B6F) and levelled the aircraft off at 13 000 feet. The crew declared a PAN PAN, ran the appropriate checklists and requested vectors to return to CYYC. The aircraft subsequently landed without further incident.

C-GPJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight JZA928, departed Runway 05 at Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, bound for Philadelphia International Airport (KPHL), PA. Shortly after departure, the flight crew received a landing gear disagreement, with all three indicator lights remaining green. The crew declared a PAN PAN, actioned the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) procedures, and requested a return to CYYZ. When the landing gear was selected down, a PROX SYS FAULT 1 warning was displayed; however, the aircraft continued to show three green gear indications. The aircraft landed successfully at CYYZ without further incident.

C-GPWE, a Westjet Encore Dehavilland DHC-8-402 (Q400) was operating flight WEN3628 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Portland International Airport (KPDX), OR. During cruise, at FL240 the left windshield cracked suddenly. The crew had ice protection on, declared a PAN PAN and ran the QRH. The crew reduced speed to less than 210 kts and descended to 14 000 feet initially as per QRH. The crew continued safely to KPDX where the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FWAU, a Beech 1900D operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting IFR flight WSG1656 from Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON, to Bearskin Lake Airport (CNE3), ON. When shortly after departure from Runway 34 in CYXL, the flight crew noticed some smoke in the cockpit. The flight crew elected to remain visual and completed a visual circuit for Runway 34. The aircraft landed a few minutes later without further incident.The operator's maintenance discovered that during a previous maintenance procedure, a small amount of engine oil was inadvertently allowed to enter the inside of the bleed air pre-cooler which caused smoke to appear in the cockpit shortly after takeoff. The bleed air system was cleaned and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYRW, a Cessna 172N operated by Durham Flight Centre Inc., was conducting a local training flight from Oshawa Executive Airport (CYOO), ON, with one student pilot and one instructor on board. Shortly after rotation during takeoff from runway 12, the engine experienced a loss of approximatively 250 RPM. A rejected takeoff was initiated, and the aircraft landed straight ahead. During the rollout, it struck a barricade and broke through a fence before coming to a stop. At the time of the occurrence, the available length of runway 12 had been reduced from 4750 feet to 4000 feet due to construction work at the runway end. Emergency services responded to the scene. Both occupants were uninjured, but the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GJZV, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting IFR flight JZA110 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. During climb through flight level 220, the flight crew received a Brake Overheat alert for the left main gear. The flight crew decided to return to CYWG and elected to declare a PAN PAN. The flight crew requested some delaying vectors to get below maximum landing weight and then landed without further incident shortly after. The aircraft stopped on the runway to have aircraft rescue and firefighting services inspect the aircraft and, after the firefighters gave their all clear, the flight crew taxied to the gate.The operator's maintenance inspected the brake system of the aircraft and found that the indication was due to the Left-Hand Inboard Thermocouple. It was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTSJ, an Air Transat A330-200 was operating flight TSC122 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to London Gatwick Airport (EGKK), UK. Shortly before descent, an ECAM (HYD G SYS LEAK) appeared. It briefly disappeared and reappeared. The crew declared a PAN PAN and executed the ECAM actions, and the aircraft landed safely in EGKK without further incident.

C-GWSR, a WestJet Boeing 737-800, was operating IFR flight WJA2276 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Philipsburg/Princess Juliana International Airport (TNCM), Sint Maarten, with 157 passengers and 6 crew members on board. Upon touchdown during landing on Runway 10 at TNCM, the aircraft’s right main landing gear collapsed and the right engine nacelle contacted the runway. The aircraft stopped on the runway surface and the occupants evacuated via the left side emergency slides. It was reported that one passenger received minor injuries during the evacuation. The aircraft’s right landing gear structure was substantially damaged. The Sint Maarten Civil Aviation Authority has delegated the investigation to the TSB under provisions of ICAO Annex 13 and the TSB deployed to the site.

C-GISZ, un Beech B200 exploité par Max Aviation sous l'indicatif MAX220 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) à destination de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU), avec 2 membres d’équipage et 8 passagers à bord. Lors de la monté initiale, le moteur de gauche a perdu de la puissance. L’équipage a constaté 2 retours de flamme, il a effectué la liste de vérification d'urgence et a fermé le moteur. L’aéronef est revenu atterrir à CYVP sans encombre. Aucune urgence n’a été déclarée.

C-GXAI, un De Havilland DHC8-314 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE802 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Kuujjuarapik, QC (CYGW), avec 3 membres d'équipage et 37 passagers à bord. Alors que l'aéronef était en vol de croisière, l’agent de bord a senti un malaise et n'a pu continuer d'exercer ses fonctions. Des membres d’équipage de la compagnie voyageant comme passager ont pris en charge la gestion de la cabine. L’équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence médicale et a demandé un déroutement vers Chibougamau, QC (CYMT). L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre avec le service ambulancier en attente.

C-GYRQ, un Cessna 208 Caravan exploité par Parachutisme Adrénaline inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à destination de l’aérodrome de Farnham, QC (CSN7). Lors de l’approche finale pour la piste 29, l’aéronef était en peu à gauche de l’axe de piste et l’aile gauche a percuté la cime d’un arbre. Le pilote a maintenu le contrôle de l’aéronef et a effectué un atterrissage normal. Le bord d’attaque de l’aile gauche a été endommagé, il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FFBJ, a privately registered, amateur built, Kitfox S7 STI airplane, departed Vernon Airport (CYVK), BC, on a recreational flight, under visual flight rules, with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. The pilot conducted an off-field landing to an unprepared grass meadow that had an uphill slope. On touchdown, the left wheel sheared off the axle and the aircraft bounced. The aircraft came to rest approximately 20 metres after the initial contact. The right-wing tip contacted the ground and was damaged. The pilot contacted the responsible person via a satellite based communication device. The responsible person contacted Nav Canada who relayed the information the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC). A Canadian Armed Forces search and rescue helicopter was dispatched to rescue the 2 occupants. There were no reported injuries. The aircraft was recovered for assessment and repair.

C-GYHF, a Yellowhead Helicopters Ltd. Bell 212 was conducting a crew transfer flight in support of firefighting operations. While on approach to a remote landing site, the pilot observed the number 1 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6T-3B) RPM begin to roll back to idle. Suspecting a governor failure, the pilot aborted the landing, issued a MAYDAY call, and activated the ELT. The aircraft was switched to manual mode, returning the engine to operation. The aircraft returned to Red Earth Creek Aerodrome (CEH5), AB, uneventfully. There were no injuries.Maintenance completed troubleshooting and found a faulty torque control unit (TCU). The affected part was replaced and tested, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GZCF, a Lockheed L188C operated by Air Spray (1967) Ltd., was operating as ASB490 engaged in forest fire suppression operations based out of Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB. After the second drop of the day, while returning to base, the crew observed that the No. 2 engine (Allision/Rolls Royce 501-D13) had fluctuating then dropping oil pressure and quantity. The flight crew consulted the quick reference handbook and shutdown the No. 2 engine, declared an emergency, and returned to CYMM. The 3-engine landing at CYMM was uneventful.Company maintenance is evaluating and troubleshooting the engine.

C-GNGN, un Van’s RV 8 en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol de formation selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport d’Ottawa/Gatineau, QC (CYND) avec 1 pilote et 1 instructeur à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage au retour à CYND, le pilote a perdu la maitrise en lacet de l’aéronef, qui a fait un cheval de bois et a terminé sa course sur la piste à 180 degrés de sa trajectoire initiale. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé, toutefois le train d’atterrissage droit s’est affaissé et il y a eu des dommages à l’aile et à l’hélice.

C-GOFJ, a Flightpath Charter Airways Ltd. Dassault Falcon 7X was being operated as flight KNT7, from Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport (KDFW), TX, U.S., under instrument flight rules, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While approaching CYYC, the flight crew noticed multiple crew alert messages due to a modular avionics unit failure. The crew declared a PAN PAN then completed the quick reference checklist items, including shutting down the hydraulics system. A manual landing gear extension and non-normal landing was completed without incident, and the aircraft was towed to the hanger. There were no injuries. The aircraft was inspected by maintenance, and the faulty avionics components were replaced. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FHXP, a Bradley Airspray 502XP Air Tractor, was conducting an aerial spray application flight from Lloydminster Airport (CYLL), AB, to a field approximately 5 nautical miles northwest of Neilburg Aerodrome (CJV2), SK. After completing the main spraying operations on a field, the pilot decided to conduct trim passes between a power line and the southern road edge of the field. As the pilot descended into the field and focused on the left-wing tip to avoid colliding with the power line poles the pilot inadvertently struck a wire running perpendicular to the main power line. The wire extended southward and was not visible to the pilot. The pilot was able to discharge the remainder of his load into the field and return to CYLL. There was no emergency declared, and aircraft landed uneventfully.After inspection by the operator's maintenance, the right-hand spray boom assembly, left-hand wheel and tire, and the left-hand wire cutter assembly were replaced.

C-GYLP, a Boeing 737-8 operated by WestJet, was conducting IFR flight WJA520 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the takeoff from Runway 36 at CYWG, the aircraft collided with a flock of seagulls. The aircraft continued the takeoff and the crew declared a MAYDAY after identifying that the First Officer's flight instruments were indicating incorrectly. The aircraft returned and landed uneventfully on Runway 31 at CYWG.Upon inspection by the operator's maintenance, evidence of bird strikes were found on the left-hand upper winglet, left-hand engine inboard inlet cowling, the left-hand landing gear and the left-hand inboard trailing edge flap with no damage found at any of those locations. The First Officer's pitot tube was found to be clogged with bird remains. The pitot tube was replaced, checked serviceable and returned to service.

C-FYKW, an Airbus A319 operated by Air Canada Rouge as flight ROU1675, was conducting a flight from Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the initial approach into CYYZ, a cabin crew member became ill, affecting their ability to perform safety-related duties. The approach and landing were continued, and the flight was completed without further incident.

C-GGDU, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was being operated as flight JZA151, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. C-GNAS, an Airsprint Incorporated Cessna 525B (Citation CJ3) was operating as flight ASP642 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, under instrument flight rules, to CYYJ. During the approach, the Citation was sequenced behind the Dash 8 and both aircraft were cleared to land without further instruction from the CYYJ tower air traffic controller. Separation between the aircraft was reduced to 3.5 nautical miles (NM) where the required wake turbulence separation was 4 NM. Both aircraft landed without incident.

C-GLQK, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 operated by Porter Airlines as flight PTR2293, was en route from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Greater Moncton Roméo Leblanc International Airport (CYQM), NB. At the same time, JY-BAB, a Boeing 787-8 operated by Royal Jordanian Airlines as flight RJ272, was enroute from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Montréal–Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Approximately 6 NM east of CYTZ, while both aircraft were transiting through 6000 feet ASL, a loss of separation occurred. The two aircraft came within 2.6 NM laterally, which was below the required minimum separation.

C-GSJB, an Air Canada Rouge A319 was operating flight ROU1830 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Owen Roberts International Airport (MWCR), Cayman Islands. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst remaining flight attendants.

C-FWEW, a Westjet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, operating as flight WEN3433, under instrument flight rules, to Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC. The pilot executed a missed approach due to weather and diverted to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Enroute the crew declared minimum fuel to air traffic control. While on approach into CYVR the crew observed the fuel to be below minimum reserve landing requirements and declared a Mayday. The aircraft landed without further incident and taxied to the gate.

C-FYHA, a Yellowhead Helicopters Limited Airbus AS350 B-3 helicopter, was conducting sling load operations between diamond drill pads in Mitchell Valley, BC, with only the pilot onboard. While transporting equipment in a cargo net, a bag dislodged from the net and fell approximately 75 feet to the riverbed below. The bag was empty and was later retrieved. There was no reported damage to the helicopter or environment.

C-FSHC, a Sierra Helicopters Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 departed Squamish Municipal Airfield (Don Patrick Field)(CYSE), BC, on a British Columbia Wildfire Services (BCWS) tasking, to a fire on Mount (Mt) Currie under visual flight rules with 1 pilot and 3 passengers on board. The 3 passengers on board were an initial action firefighting crew deploying to fight the fire on Mt Currie. The pilot gave a safety briefing, and the crew lead a hover exit walk through prior to takeoff. The pilot and the crew lead were in the front seats, and the other two members were in the rear left and rear center seat. The equipment was strapped in the rear right seat. The drop off location was a steep talus field on the northern face of Mt Currie. The pilot and crew lead agreed on a large flat rock for the drop off position. The pilot did an overhead recce and completed an approach to the rock. He repositioned once for a more stable position and had the toe of both skids resting on the rock. The crew member in the left rear seat removed his headset, put on a hardhat, and exited the aircraft. The second crew member in the back removed his seatbelt and headset, put on his hardhat, and began passing equipment to the outside member in packages that were less than 20lbs. All crew members heard a sharp noise, and the aircraft pitched nose high and to the left. The outside person leapt down and away from the aircraft. The helicopter turned 180° and rolled down the slope. During the roll down the slope, the crew member in the back seat was ejected from the helicopter and the pilot's helmet came off. The helicopter came to rest in an upright, nose down attitude. The pilot and passenger were both able to exit the aircraft prior to the airframe being engulfed in flame. The crew member who had been outside the aircraft called a Mayday on his handheld radio and started downhill toward the wreckage. The four members grouped together and started to climb back up the slope, away from the burning helicopter. The crew lead used his cell phone to call in to dispatch and advise the status of the helicopter and crew. A BCWS team was dispatched for the rescue and recovered the crew to the Pemberton Aerodrome (CYPS), BC. All four occupants had minor injuries. The helicopter was destroyed.

N821DX, a Boeing 757-200 operated by Delta Airlines was conducting flight DAL 179 from Reykjavik - Keflavik International Airport (KEF) Iceland to Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County International Airport (KDTW) USA. During the cruise, the flight crew adjusted the left environmental (enviro) pack for temperature, moments later, the right enviro pack failed and then the left. The flight crew initiated an emergency decent due to a loss of cabin pressurization and declared an emergency. Once the aircraft leveled off maintenance and flights operations were contacted, and a plan was made to divert to Montreal Trudeau International Airport (CYUL) QC. The flight crew communicated with the cabin crew about the diversion, and they indicated the cabin was hot and could smell a burning odor. The right enviro pack was restarted and the aircraft landed in CYUL without incident Maintenance personal are in the process of inspecting the aircraft.

C-GITY, an Airbus A321-200 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA117 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Shortly after departure, the flight crew was unable to pressurize the aircraft. They declared an emergency and completed applicable checklist items while circling in the area, before electing to return to CYYZ. The aircraft landed without further incident. Air Canada maintenance conducted an inspection and determined that the avionics vent valve was faulty. The valve was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GPGB, a Bombardier Challenger 300 operated by Chartright Air Inc., was conducting flight HRT260 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Washington Dulles International Airport, USA with 2 crew members and 6 passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff, upon selecting the landing gear up, the flight crew received a Crew Alerting System (CAS) message: GEAR DISAGREE. The crew confirmed the issue, noting the absence of the normal gear retraction sound. The flight crew advised Air Traffic Control (ATC) of the situation and proceeded to complete the appropriate checklist and troubleshooting procedures. After multiple unsuccessful attempts to resolve the issue, the crew elected to return to CYYZ, declaring an emergency. Flight HRT260 landed safely on Runway 23 without further incident. Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) personnel and equipment met the aircraft at the Signature FBO ramp upon arrival. Post-flight inspection by company maintenance personnel revealed a fault with one of the nose landing gear weight-on-wheel sensors. The sensor was readjusted to proper specifications, and the system was tested and found to be serviceable.

C-FQGG, a Boeing 737-800 operated by WestJet as flight WJA627, was on approach to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, when the flight crew requested a go-around due to a landing gear indication. The crew declared an emergency and requested aircraft eescue and firefighting (ARFF) to be on standby for arrival.The aircraft conducted a second approach and landed uneventfully. However, while exiting the runway, the crew reported a loss of nose wheel steering and subsequently requested a tow to the gate.

N821DX, un Boeing 757-200 exploité par Delta Airlines Inc. sous l'indicatif DAL179 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Keflavik (BIFK), Islande à destination de Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County (KDTW), États-Unis avec 6 membres d’équipage et 184 passagers à bord. À 1220z à environ 108 miles marins (nm) au nord de Natashquan (CYNA), Québec, l'équipage a remarqué que la température dans le cockpit était plus chaude, l’équipage a ajusté le pack de gauche et peu après, le pack de droit a failli suivi de celui de gauche 30 secondes plus tard. L’équipage a enfilé les masques d’oxygène et a déclaré une urgence en raison d’un problème de pressurisation, a effectué une descente d’urgence vers 10 000 pieds et a demandé un déroutement vers l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Lors de la descente, en passant le FL280, l’altitude de la cabine a dépassée 14 000 pieds et les masques se sont déployés automatiquement dans la cabine. Durant le déroutement, le pack de droit a recommencé à fonctionner, mais pas celui de gauche. L'aéronef s'est posé à CYUL sans encombre.

C-GYBB, a privately registered float-equipped Piper PA-22-150X, operating under a special certificate of airworthiness - owner maintenance, was conducting a flight from Flin Flon/Channing Water Aerodrome (CJK8), MB, to Moose Jaw, SK. While in cruise approximately 1000 feet above ground level, C-GYBB experienced a rudder post failure above the upper hinge attach point. The aircraft became uncontrollable and turned left 90 degrees and, shortly after, went nose down. The aircraft crashed into a forest approximately 16 nautical miles west of Cumberland House Aerodrome (CJT4), SK. The pilot and sole occupant was able to exit the aircraft and transmitted an SOS through a satellite tracking device. The signal was received by the satellite tracking company who then contacted the RCMP. The ELT was also triggered in the accident and JRCC Trenton coordinated with Saskatchewan RCMP who were able to locate the aircraft and rescue the pilot. The pilot was subsequently taken to hospital with a serious injury. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The Piper Aircraft company released a mandatory Service Bulletin 1379B on 7 May 2024 to inspect and/or replace a rudder post manufactured from 1025 carbon steel. The FAA later released Airworthiness Directive 2025-02-11 on 20 March 2025 due to reports of non-fatal accidents that were caused by rudder posts manufactured from 1025 carbon steel that structurally failed above the upper hinge in flight.

C-GJYI, an Airbus A220-300 operated by Air Canada as flight AC1398, was departing Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, for Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, USA, with 122 passengers and 5 crew members on board. C-FFPT, a Bombardier Global 7500 (BD-700-2A12), was conducting a ground test with two Aircraft Maintenance Engineers (AMEs) and one inspector on board.While AC1398 was on its takeoff roll on Runway 23, C-FFPT was taxiing northbound on Runway 33L and had been instructed to hold short of Runway 23. Air Traffic Control (ATC) observed C-FFPT crossing the hold-short line and reminded the crew to stop; however, the aircraft continued to move toward Runway 23 until ATC issued an urgent instruction to stop.C-FFPT came to a full stop well past the hold-short line, with its nose approximately 35 feet onto Runway 23. AC1398 became airborne just before reaching the intersection point. Both aircraft continued operations without further incident.

C-GLQR, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 operated by Porter Airlines Inc., was conducting flight POE2476 from Montréal–Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, with 67 passengers and 4 crew members on board. Shortly after initiating descent to CYTZ, the flight crew received a FUSELAGE DOORS master warning while passing through FL180. The indication briefly extinguished and reappeared multiple times before being identified as related to the forward baggage door. The crew completed the applicable checklist and confirmed that the aircraft pressurization remained normal. A PAN-PAN emergency was declared with Toronto Centre. The crew also advised CYTZ Tower to request a precautionary runway inspection. Flight POE2476 landed without further incident. Maintenance personnel conducted an inspection and determined that the warning system had issued a false alert due to a misadjusted vent flap and a wiring issue with the door lock sensor. The faulty components were replaced, and the system was adjusted and tested satisfactorily before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FLFU, un hélicoptère privé Robinson R44 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Maniwaki, QC (CYMW) au lac des 31 miles, QC avec un pilote à bord. Lors de l’approche au-dessus du lac en condition d’eau miroitante, l’hélicoptère est descendu plus bas que perçu et a touché la surface du lac. Le pilote a tenté de remonter, mais l’hélicoptère s’est mis à tourner sur lui-même, le pilote a alors redescendu l’hélicoptère à l’eau et l’a fait incliner sur la gauche afin d’arrêter le rotor avec l’eau. Le pilote a subi des blessures légères. L’hélicoptère a subi des dommages importants. La radiobalise d‘urgence ne s’est pas déclenchée. Le pilote a ensuite été secouru par un riverain.

N661UA, a Boeing 767-300ER operated by United Airlines Inc was conducting flight UAL934 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, to London Heathrow International Airport (EGLL), UK. During the climb the flight crew were notified by the cabin crew that the aft galley had lost electrical power. After communication with flight operations and maintenance control, the flight crew decided to return to KEWR, and an emergency was declared due to an overweight landing. The aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance action completed a fault isolation procedure, and the electrical system was reset. An overweight landing inspection was carried out and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GMFA, un ultraléger de type évolué KitFox IV en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aérodrome de Casey, QC (CSQ4), à destination d’une piste privée à Sainte-Eulalie, QC, avec 1 pilote et 1 passager à bord. Lors du décollage de la piste 22, l’aéronef a été vu en virage prononcé vers la droite (vers le nord) et la maîtrise a été perdue. L’aéronef a percuté le sol et un incendie s’est déclenché. Les 2 occupants ont subi des blessures mortelles et l’aéronef a été détruit.

C-GCBK, a De Havilland DHC-8-314 operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting flight PAG629 from Island Lake Airport (CYIV), MB, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. While in cruise at 20 000 feet, the flight crew observed the #1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW123) oil pressure gauge fluctuating between 50 and 40 psi. The flight crew elected to complete a precautionary engine shut down on the #1 engine. The flight crew declared an emergency and advised Winnipeg Center that they were shutting down the #1 engine due to low oil pressure. They executed the Engine Fail/Fire/Shutdown Quick Reference Handbook checklist and shutdown the #1 engine. The aircraft landed on Runway 18 at CYWG where they stopped and were inspected by Airport Fire and Rescue. Once given all clear, the flight crew taxied back to Apron 4 with no incident.

C-FLWQ, a privately registered Cessna 170B, was conducting a recreational flight, under visual flight rules, from Guess Lake, BC, (54°43.776'N, 126°43.859'W) to a private airstrip located approximately 6 nautical miles northeast of Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC, (54º32.266'N, 128º27.399'W) with only the pilot onboard. During the landing, the aircraft briefly touched down at a high rate of speed and the pilot determined that the aircraft could not stop within the remaining runway. The pilot initiated a go-around and the aircraft clipped nearby trees during the initial climb. The pilot lost control of the aircraft and collided with terrain. Bystanders assisted the pilot in egressing the aircraft. The pilot sustained minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FRQN, a Jazz Aviation Embraer 175 was operating flight JZA954 from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (KATL), GA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During climb, the flight crew advised dispatch that there was smoke detected from the galley oven, there was no fire. The flight attendant pulled the circuit breaker (CB) and the flight crew elected to return to KATL. After the CB was pulled, the smoke slowly dissipated. The flight crew initially declared a PAN PAN however, that was upgraded to Mayday. The aircraft landed overweight at 34 700 kg and the rate of descent was less than 350 feet per minute. The aircraft stopped on the runway to allow aircraft rescue and firefighting to do an inspection and was able to taxi to the gate once they got cleared.

C-GUFR, an Air Transat Airbus A330 was operating flight TSC765 from Porto Airport (LPPR), Portugal, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Shortly after take-off, a cabin crew member became incapacitated. Duties were reassigned to a supernumerary crew member.

C-FJZS, an Air Canada Boeing 777-300 departed Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, operating as flight ACA303, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, a cabin crew member opened a galley bin and was incapacitated and received a minor injury. The flight continued to CYVR where emergency medical services met the aircraft.

C-GMQZ, un Pilatus PC-12/45 exploité par Chrono Aviation Inc. sous l'indicatif NDL432 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB)à destination de l'aérodrome Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU). C-GUWW, un Short Brothers SC-7 Skyvan Series 3 exploité par WM aviation effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis CYHU à destination de l’aérodrome de St-Jean Chrysostome, QC (CSG5). Alors que NDL432 était en palier à 4000 pieds en rapprochement de CYHU, l’équipage a reçu un avis de trafic TCAS d’un aéronef convergeant à la même altitude. L’équipage a repéré l’aéronef et a initié une descente d’environ 300 pieds afin de maintenir la séparation. Après que les aéronefs se soient croisés, l’ATC (terminal de Montréal) a informé NDL432 du trafic convergeant et l’a autorisé à descendre à 3000 pieds. Les 2 vols ont continué à destination sans encombre. L’ATC a confirmé par la suite que C-GUWW évoluait en VFR en dehors de l’espace aérien de class C et qu’il n’était pas en contact avec l’ATC.

CF-EOL, a privately registered Cessna 170B, was conducting a local training flight, under visual flight rules, from Qualicum Beach Airport (CAT4), BC, with 1 flight instructor, 1 student, and 1 passenger onboard. After lining up to take off from Runway 11, the student in the forward left seat applied full throttle and began the takeoff roll. The aircraft began drifting to the right and the flight instructor took control of the aircraft. The aircraft momentarily became airborne and immediately rolled and yawed to the left. The aircraft lost altitude, contacted the runway, and came to rest on the right wingtip and right horizontal stabilizer. The aircraft was in the airport infield between the runway and Taxiway A. The occupants egressed the aircraft through the left door. There was 1 minor injury reported and the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GSHJ, a Helijet International Incorporated Sikorsky S-76C++ helicopter, was operating as flight JBA707 from Vancouver/Harbour Heliport (CBC7), BC, to Victoria Harbour (Camel Point) Heliport (CBF7), BC. During cruise flight, the crew observed that the indication for the No. 2 hydraulic system pressure was low. The crew declared a PAN PAN and requested a diversion to the Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. The crew consulted the emergency checklist, decreased the helicopter forward speed, and lowered the landing gear. The helicopter landed safely at CYVR near the company hangar.  Maintenance replaced the No. 2 hydraulic pump and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FLUM, a Cessna 150 operated by the Leamington Community Flying Society, was conducting a flight from Chatham-Kent Airport (CYCK), ON, to Leamington Aerodrome (CLM2), ON, with two souls on board. While landing on Runway 01 in crosswind conditions, control of the aircraft was lost, and the right side of the stabilizer struck a runway landing light.A subsequent inspection in the hangar revealed that the left wing had also sustained damage after scraping the runway during the landing. Neither occupant was injured, and the ELT did not activate. The pilot later reported that the narrow runway made it difficult to maintain directional control under crosswind conditions.

N832MH, a Boeing B767-432ER aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL9893 from London/Heathrow Intl (EGLL), England to New York/John F. Kennedy Intl (KJFK), NY. When in cruise flight at about 60° 02' N, 031°11' W, the flight crew received a momentary left display processing computer (DPC) status message and then noticed a vibration that was felt as a brief shudder in the aircraft. The DPC status message and subsequent vibration/shudders occurred momentarily about every 15 minutes, though there were no aircraft controllability issues. The flight crew conferred with company maintenance control and decided to carry out a diversion to Reykjavík/Keflavík Intl (BIKF), Iceland. The flight crew declared an emergency and coordinated with the ATS for the diversion to BIKF where a landing was made without further incident.The DPC was replaced. Additionally, connector pins were repaired at electrical connector number D3853 and software was updated before returning the aircraft to service.

N344KD, a Boeing 747-446 (BCF) aircraft operated by Western Global Airlines, LLC, was conducting cargo flight WGN4196 from Brussels Intl (EBBR), Belgium to Chicago O'Hare Intl (KORD), IL. When in cruise at about 57°00' N, 045°00' W, the flight crew observed an EICAS message that number 3 engine oil quantity was decreasing. The crew conferred with company maintenance via satellite communication and decided to shut down the number 3 engine, declared an emergency and coordinated with ATS for a diversion to Portsmouth Intl (KPSM), NH where a landing was made without further incident.Maintenance personnel removed and replaced a cracked lubrication scavenge pump discharge manifold.

C-GGMZ, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP was conducting flight JZA143 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the initial climb, the flight crew attempted to retract the landing gear and received an amber gear in transit light followed by the red gear unsafe light. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook, declared a PAN PAN with ATC and elected to return to CYEG. The alternate landing gear release was actuated, the landing gear extended, and flight crew observed three green landing gear down and locked indicator lights. During the landing roll, the aircraft experienced a significant vibration from the nose landing gear. The aircraft came to a stop on the runway and the flight crew shut down the engines and secured the aircraft. All passengers deplaned and were bussed to the terminal. There were no injuries.Post flight examination found the left nose wheel assembly partially separated the nose landing gear due to a failure of the outer wheel bearing. At the time of the accident the nose wheel assembly had accrued a total of 273 hours and 341 cycles since last repair. A web service difficulty report (WSDR) has been submitted.

C-GTBY, a Cessna 208 operated by Superior Airways Limited, was conducting a VFR flight from Hansen Lake, ON, to Red Lake (Howey Bay) Water Aerodrome (CKS4), ON. Normal flight control feedback required for the initial takeoff run was observed. When the airplane became airborne, the pilot continued to apply aft input and limited elevator travel was experienced; inhibiting the desired pitch attitude for climb. The pilot made an immediate left turn into the wind for a landing. With limited elevator control input for the flare phase, the plane contacted the water at a harder than normal rate resulting in substantial damage to the airplane. The were no injuries.  The operator's maintenance noted the right elevator was deformed, and a brief test found flight control pitch input to be obstructed consistent with a visual observation of limited elevator travel. It was reported that the damage to the elevator was consistent with a collision with an object prior to the takeoff run. A flight control check was performed during the first flight of the day by the pilot but not on subsequent flights. The operator now requires their checklist items to be read and do action, including a flight control check prior to all takeoffs.

C-FYPB, a Boeing 737-8CT (B737-800) operated by WestJet Airlines Limited, was conducting flight WJA164 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. During the initial climb, the cabin crew noticed a strong smell which resembled propane throughout the cabin. The flight crew also noticed the odour in the cockpit but were unable to confirm the source. The flight crew made the decision to return to CYVR and requested priority handling from air traffic control. Some members of the cabin crew reported feeling lightheaded as the aircraft descended into CYVR. The aircraft landed without further incident and aircraft rescue and firefighting personnel met the aircraft at the gate. The cabin crew initiated a rapid deplanement when the aircraft arrived at the gate. There were no injuries.Company maintenance discovered that the source of the strong odour was a shipment of Durian fruit in the cargo compartment. The fruit shipment was removed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBIM, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was operating flight ROU1637 from Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL, to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Airport (CYUL), QC. While cruising to CYUL, the crew received the message "HYD G RSVR LO LVL" from the Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitor (ECAM) indicating a low fluid level in the green hydraulic system and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed and was towed to the gate. Maintenance replaced the engine 1 pump pressure switch.

C-FKGE, un Pilatus PC12/47 exploité par Kudlik Aviation sous l’indicatif KUK761, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à destination de l'aéroport de Schefferville, Québec (CYKL). Après environs une heure de vol, l'équipage a constaté un problème avec le système de navigation automatique. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) et décidé de revenir vers CYQB où il s'est posé sans encombre.

N671UA, a Boeing 767-322 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL967 from Naples/Capodichino International Airport (LIRN), Italy, to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ. While in cruise at about 44°36' N, 042°37' W, the flight crew noticed a burning odour. The flight crew conferred with company maintenance control and completed the Cabin Air Quality checklist, after which the odour reduced in intensity. The flight observed an EICAS message related to the Forward Equipment Exhaust Fan. The flight crew declared an emergency and coordinated a diversion to St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL, with ATS. The aircraft landed at CYYT without further incident.Maintenance personnel replaced the faulty Forward Equipment Exhaust Fan.

N787FZ, a privately operated Bombardier Global 7500 (BD-700-2A12), was conducting an IFR flight from Teterboro Airport (KTEB), NJ, to Olbia/ Costa Smeralda Airport (LIEO), Sardinia, Italy. While in cruise flight at FL410 near 47° 42'N, 052° 00'W, the flight crew received two caution messages: L REVERSER FAIL and L REVERSER LOCK FAIL accompanied by a number 1 power reduction to flight idle. The crew completing the appropriate checklist, which required the reduction of indicated airspeed to 170 KIAS and to land at the nearest suitable airport. The crew reduced airspeed to 170 KIAS, declared an emergency and coordinated with ATS to descend to 10 000 feet. They flew an extended pattern enroute to achieve a landing weight below maximum limits and coordinating with ATS for a diversion to Gander Airport (CYQX), NL where a landing was made without further incident.The operator coordinated troubleshooting with General Electric to identify a faulty EEC.

C-GPOW un Airbus Helicopters AS350B2 effectuait un vol de transport de marchandise à l'élingue entre la tour 198 de la ligne de transport haute tension près du poste Montagnais (CSF3) Qc. et le poste de ravitaillement Premio situé le long de la voie ferrée entre Sept-ïles et le poste Montagnais. Peu après le décollage, à son altitude et vitesse de croisière, le pilote a ressenti un cognement suivi d'une vibration dans le palonnier. Ralentissant sa vitesse, il a remarqué une augmentation des vibrations. Le pilote a alors effectué un largage de son chargement et s'est posé par précaution dans un espace dégagé. Une inspection a révélé des dommages aux pales du rotor de queue, au stabilisateur horizontal et à une pale du rotor principal. Les dommages correspondaient avec une pièce de bois qui serait sortie du chargement.

C-GUTI, an Aerospatiale AS 350B3 operated by Canadian Helicopters was conducting operations approximately 27 nm ENE of Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. The pilot had landed the helicopter at a remote worksite where one of the workers was kneeling on a "mega bag" to prevent it from blowing away in the rotor wash of the helicopter. When the worker got up to board the helicopter, the bag blew away and into the rotor system. The pilot experienced a severe vibration and the helicopter rolled onto its right side. The pilot was uninjured, shut down the helicopter engine and was able to extricate himself from the helicopter. There was no fire, but the helicopter was substantially damaged.

C-242456464, a SwissDrones SDO 50 V3 drone system operated by the Southern Alberta Institue of Technology was being flight tested approximately 19 nm WSW of the Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB. The flight was in accordance with the conditions of the special flight operation certificate issued by Transport Canada. Part way through the second flight of the day, the drone suddenly lost altitude and impacted terrain. There was a post-accident fire, and the drone was destroyed. Ground crew extinguished the fire and emergency services were notified and attended the scene to ensure no hot spots remained.

C-FEYP, un Beechcraft A100 exploité par Propair Inc. sous l’indicatif PRO4230, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) à destination de Nemiscau, QC (CYHH) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 1 passager à bord. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, de la fumée est apparue dans le poste de pilotage. L’équipage a effectué un retour à CYUY, aucune urgence n’a été déclarée et l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GKIT, a privately-registered Cessna 337E aircraft, was conducting a local VFR flight from the Brandon Municipal Airport (CYBR), MB, with the pilot and three passengers. While returning for landing at CYBR on Runway 32, it was reported that the landing gear selector was placed in the down position. The pilot did not confirm the down and locked indication prior to touchdown and the main landing gear collapsed during the landing roll. The aircraft skidded to a stop in the center of the runway. The aircraft was substantially damaged. There were no injuries.

C-GNCJ, a Central Mountain Air De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8–102 (Dash 8 100), was conducting flight GLR9326 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Bella Bella Airport (CBBC), BC. During the initial climb out of CYVR, the pilot observed an "ATT" (attitude) flag on the left electronic attitude director indicator. The crew declared a PAN PAN and returned to CYVR where the aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance replaced the left side electronic attitude director indicator, and the aircraft was checked serviceable.

C-GJAZ, a Jazz Aviation MHI RJ Aviation CL-600-2D24, operating as JZA238, had landed on Runway 06L at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, and was instructed to taxi off the active runway at Taxiway C3. Meanwhile, C-FWJS, a WestJet Boeing 737-800, operating as WJA708, was on approach to Runway 06L and crossed the threshold to Runway 06L with JZA238, still on the runway. The distance between the threshold and the turnoff to Taxiway C is approximately 4700 feet. There were no injuries or aircraft damage, however Nav Canada has initiated an investigation into the loss of separation.

C-FIGS, a Cessna 337 aircraft operated by MAG Aerospace Canada Corp. was conducting a local VFR fire patrol flight from La Ronge/Barber Field Airport (CYVC), SK. When approximately 40 NM North-northwest of CYVC, the pilot observed an RPM fluctuation on the front engine which worsened over time. The pilot then turned back toward CYVC and consulted the quick reference handbook emergency checklist (QRH). While actioning the "propeller overspeed/governor" checklist, the front engine was inadvertently shut down. The pilot restarted the front engine and was unsure of the front engine's performance. He declared a PAN PAN to receive priority through restricted airspace and the aircraft landed at 0048 UTC in CYVC without further incident.The operator's maintenance department found a broken tachometer wire on the right magneto of the front engine. The wire was repaired with a new terminal end, and a satisfactory function test carried out. The aircraft was returned to service. The operator will be amending the QRH to have the "low, high/fluctuating RPM gauge" checklist appear before the propeller "overspeed/governor failure" checklist.

C-GENK, a WestJet Encore DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was operating as flight WEN3627 from Portland International Airport (KPDX), OR, under instrument flight rules, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During cruise, a No. 2 hydraulic isolation valve (HYD ISO VLV) caution light illuminated and the hydraulic fluid quantity on the No. 2 hydraulic system indicated 10%. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist and declared a PAN PAN. While being vectored by ATC, the flight crew actioned the alternate gear extension as detailed in the quick reference handbook. A normal landing was completed and, when the aircraft was clear of the active runway, the flight crew requested a tow to the gate because the nose wheel steering was inoperative. Maintenance personnel installed nose landing gear lock actuator hydraulic flex hoses and bled the No. 2 hydraulic system. Landing gear system checks were completed with no further faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBHJ, a Helijet International Incorporated Sikorsky 76C++, was being operated as flight JBA726 from Victoria Harbour (Camel Point) Heliport (CBF7), BC, to Vancouver Harbour Heliport (CBC7), BC, under instrument flight rules. During cruise, at 5000 feet above sea level, the No. 2 engine (Turbomeca Arriel 2S2) chip light illuminated. The emergency checklist was consulted and the flight crew reset the chip circuit breaker. The chip light re-illuminated immediately. After completing the emergency checklist, the flight crew reduced the No. 2 engine power setting to 70% N1, declared a PAN PAN, and requested radar vectors to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. On short final, the flight crew returned the No. 2 engine to flight power and performed a run-on landing on Runway 32. After landing, the flight crew shut down the No. 2 engine and taxied to parking.A post-flight maintenance inspection found significant magnetic debris on the Electric Magnetic Chip Detector and the MO-1 Chip Detector. The MO-5 Chip Detector was found to be clean. The engine manufacturer was consulted, and the engine was removed from service. A replacement engine was installed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOGJ, a Custom Helicopters AS350 B2 helicopter, was conducting a geological survey flight, under visual flight rules, from a camp located approximately 52 NM northwest of Stewart Aerodrome (CZST), BC, with only the pilot on board. During the flight, the pilot noticed the geological survey "bird" equipment had departed the 75-foot longline. The helicopter returned to the camp safely. The survey equipment was later found in a forested area and recovered.Post-flight inspection by maintenance personnel revealed that the manual release cable sheathing had separated from its attachment point on the cargo hook. A new cargo hook was subsequently ordered and installed.

C-FMFD, a privately registered Piper PA-18-150, was conducting a VFR flight near Stormer Lake, ON, to Red Lake (Howey Bay) Water Aerodrome (CKS4), ON. While enroute, the airplane was flying at approximately 500 feet above ground level and slowed to an estimated 70 miles per hour at an idle power setting, over a lodge near Stormer Lake to observe damage conditions of the area from a recent forest fire. When power was applied to regain airspeed, the inability to move the throttle from its idle position was reported. The airplane was unable to maintain altitude and struck terrain. There were no injuries, and the airplane was substantially damaged.  After the accident, a maintenance facility inspected the function of the throttle linkage and found it to move freely.

C-FYJG, an Airbus A319-100 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1926 from Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise phase of flight, the flight crew encountered spurious and random failures including cockpit displays, lighting, and communications. Communication with ATC was initially disrupted but was re-established after the crew started the APU. PAN-PAN was declared, and maintenance was consulted via VHF radio. IDG 1 was identified as the source of the issue and was subsequently switched to OFF, which resulted in systems returning to normal. The PAN-PAN was then cancelled and the flight continued safely to CYYZ, where it landed without further incident. Maintenance replaced IDG 1 and the aircraft was returned to service.

N711AL, a Gulfstream G650ER aircraft operated by FLEXJET LLC, was conducting flight LXJ672 from Santa Barbara Airport (KSBA), CA, to Beja Airport (LPBJ), Portugal. At about 49°00' N, 040°00' W a thin crack appeared in the right-side windshield. The crew referenced the quick reference handbook (QRH) and determined that insufficient fuel remained to continue to destination based on the altitude restriction in the QRH procedure. The crew decided to divert to Gander International Airport (CYQX), NL. They then declared an emergency and coordinated the diversion with ATS and landed at CYQX without further incident.

C-FOOU, a Principal Air Limited Cessna 152, was conducting a cross-country training flight from Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, under visual flight rules, to South Cariboo/108 Mile Aerodrome (CZML), BC, via Squamish Municipal Airport/Don Patrick Field, (CYSE), BC, and Pemberton Aerodrome (CYPS), BC, with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. The pilot completed the first legs of the flight without incident. While en route to CZML the pilot made a landing and short stop at Echo Valley Aerodrome (CBJ4), BC. CBJ4 was not on the flight plan, and no prior notice was provided to the aerodrome operator as required and noted in the Canada Flight Supplement (CFS). The airport elevation is 3650 feet, the temperature was greater than 20°C and the first 2000 feet of Runway 07, used for takeoff on the occurrence flight, had a 4° upslope. The pilot taxied into position with approximately 250 feet of runway behind the aircraft and used a short field take-off technique. Shortly after liftoff, the aircraft stalled, collided with trees, and impacted terrain approximately 300 meters beyond the paved end of the runway. The electronic locator transmitter (ELT) signal was relayed to the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre Victoria. Two aircraft were dispatched to assist but were recalled when it was determined that local first responders arrived on scene. Both occupants were seriously injured; the pilot was taken to hospital in Kamloops by air ambulance, and the passenger was taken to the hospital by ground ambulance. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FIRS, a Forest Protection Limited Air Tractor AT8T, operating as TKR229 was enroute from Miramichi Aerodrome (CYCH), NB, to Fredericton International Airport, (CYFC), NB. Departing CYCH after reloading with water and foam for one additional suppression 9 NM north and then the occurrence aircraft with an additional 3 other Air Tractors were returning to CYFC.
