The flight of 4 aircraft were enroute to CYFC when at the hallway point, the occurrence aircraft received a low fuel annunciator. At this point the pilot activated the fuel boost pump and engine igniters. The pilot informed the team lead of the situation, and it was decided TKR229 would have priority to land. While maneuvering to enter the control zone the aircraft’s engine flamed out. The pilot declared an emergency and conducted a forced approach on to a roadway 8 NM north from CYFC. On landing the aircraft struck construction signs during the rollout. The pilot was uninjured.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and noted leading edge damage to both wings, two areas of the fuselage and damage to one propeller blade. Both wing tanks were drained, and it was determined that there was approximately 25 liters in the RH wing tank and 150 liters in the LH wing tank. Maintenance removed both wings and transported the aircraft back to the base via road. The damaged area of each leading edge was then removed to facilitate inspection of the wing spar. No wing spar damage was evident.

C-GKYN, an Embraer ERJ 190-400 operated by Porter Airlines as flight POE154, was departing from Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. The aircraft was instructed to line up only on Runway 25. At the same time, C-FGXH, a Beech C90A operated by the Aerospace Engineering Test Establishment as Transport Canada flight LOGC987, was on short final for Runway 32.POE154 read back the instruction to line up, but subsequently began its takeoff roll on Runway 25. Ottawa Tower identified the conflict and instructed POE154 to reject the takeoff. LOGC987 landed without further incident, and POE154 later departed at 12:11 ETD.

B-LXA, an Airbus A350-1000 operated by Cathay Pacific, was conducting flight CPA805 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Hong Kong International Airport (VHHH), HK. Upon reaching FL250, the flight crew received indication of an issue with the hydraulic system, declared PAN PAN, and requested to dump fuel before returning to CYYZ. After dumping fuel for approximately 1 hour, the aircraft returned to CYYZ and landed uneventfully on Runway 15L.

C-FGKJ, a Cargojet Airways Boeing 757-200 was operating as flight CJT937 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the initial approach to CYYC, the flight crew received a TE FLAP DISAGREE message, displayed on the EICAS. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and declared a PAN PAN. The approach and landing were uneventful and without further issues; there were no injuries. Company maintenance replaced the LH IB Flap OB transmission and RH IB Flap IB transmission.

C-FWKQ, a Pilatus PC12/47E operated by North Star Air, was conducting an IFR flight BF705 from Lansdowne House Airport (CYLH), ON, to Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON with 2 crew members on board. While on approach to Runway 25 at CYQT, the crew selected the gear down, but the left main gear indicated unsafe. They conducted a low approach and asked the tower if they could see the gear. The tower controller advised all three gear appeared down. The crew executed a missed approach and requested delay vectors with ATC while they conducted the emergency landing gear extension checklist. The issue could not be rectified following the checklist. The crew elected to conduct another low approach to see if the gear was down but ATC advised they could not tell. The crew prepared for landing with a potential unsafe left main gear and requested the emergency vehicles on standby. After touchdown, the aircraft felt stable and the crew elected to exit on taxiway Golf to shutdown the aircraft and be towed in. There were no injuries. There was no damage to the aircraft.After troubleshooting the landing gear system on C-FWKQ, the operator's maintenance was found that the left hand main landing gear actuator microswitch had failed. The main landing gear actuator was replaced, extension/retraction/leak checks were carried out and the hydaurlic system was serviced. No faults were found following the function checks.

C-FJPI, an AS350-B2 operated by Expedition Helicopters Inc., was conducting external load operations out of a temporary staging area in Matachewan, ON. The pilot was picking up a slung load weighing approximately 1500 lbs using a 100-foot longline. Almost immediately after taking up the slack in the line and lifting the load off the ground, the engine (LTS101-700-D2) failed abruptly. The pilot conducted a forced landing on a road. The result was a hard landing; there was significant damage to the helicopter as the tail boom bent downwards, the tail rotor blades were destroyed, and the skids were damaged, although the helicopter remained upright. The pilot was uninjured. Initial examination of the engine revealed that the compressor section of the engine was seized, while the turbine section was free to rotate. The engine will be disassembled to determine the cause of the engine failure.

C-GMOC, an Alkan Air Beech 200 was operating on a MEDEVAC flight as AKN513-M from Whitehorse International Airport (CYXY), YT, to Watson Lake Airport (CYQH), YT. During climb after departing CYXY, the flight crew noticed that the landing gear motor “running” light remained illuminated. After the aircraft climbed clear of cloud at approximately 10 000 feet ASL the flight crew actioned the abnormal checklist for the landing gear motor light. During this time the captain noticed that the nose landing gear had not retracted. The crew attempted to cycle the landing gear. The main landing gear extended and showed down and locked. The landing gear was then selected up and did not retract. The landing gear select handle was replaced to the down position and left there. The landing gear indication panel still showed 3 green landing gear down indication lights with no unsafe landing gear indication. The flight crew advised ATS that they were returning. The flight crew conducted a visual approach and landed on Runway 14L. During rollout as the flaps were being retracted and the weight of the aircraft settled onto the landing gear, the landing gear unsafe horn sounded, and the landing gear unsafe light illuminated.  As power was reduced to idle and the aircraft slowed, the right main landing gear collapsed. The flight crew carried out the emergency shutdown procedures for both engines. The aircraft skidded to a stop on the runway surface. There were no injuries. Damage was limited to the belly pod and right propeller. During the aircraft recovery, the left gear subsequently collapsed, and the resulting damage was minor.

CF-FVN, a privately registered Aeronca 7BCM, was one of two aircraft conducting a local flight from Straffordville/Bushhawk Creek Aerodrome, (CBH5), ON, with one pilot in each aircraft. This was the first flight for each aircraft after annual inspections which had been completed on 13 August 2025. After departing toward the south, the pilots turned northward as they continued to climb. Approximately 2 NM north of the airport, the pilot of CF-FVN reported engine trouble (Continental C85, fuel injected) to the pilot of the other aircraft, and after checking the engine gauges and controls, began to look for a landing site. The engine power gradually diminished over a period of 30-45 seconds before it failed completely. The aircraft was too high and fast to land at the originally chosen landing site, and the pilot changed direction to line up with a corn field. Upon first impact with the corn, the aircraft spun 180 degrees and fell through the crop. The pilot received injuries as a result of the impact forces but was able to exit the aircraft; he was taken to hospital for treatment by first responders. The aircraft was substantially damaged, with the engine displaced into the cockpit area and significant damage to the floor, firewall and instrument panel. The cause of the engine failure has not been determined.

C-FCNU, a Range Helicopters Inc. Bell 212, was operating on a local fire suppression mission to wildfire HWF 106, approximately 39 NM northwest of High Level Airport (CYOJ), AB. The helicopter was engaged in transporting firefighters from the fire back to the abandoned Zama Airport, AB (N59 09 W118 42). The helicopter landed at HWF 106 wildfire pickup location and loaded 9 firefighters onboard. During departure, 200 meters away, the No. 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada, PT6T-3B) experienced a complete power loss. The pilot initiated the engine out emergency procedures and turned back intending to land at the departure location. The pilot quickly realized that the intended landing site was not achievable, and a secondary landing zone was identified. The pilot executed the single-engine emergency landing without issue. The helicopter was undamaged and there were no injuries. The pilot stayed with the helicopter and the firefighters were picked up by another helicopter.

C-GLQK, a Porter Airlines Dash-8-400, was conducting flight PTR2363. The tower controller at Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, cleared PTR2363 to depart Runway 07 with the expectation that they would begin a right turn towards AVVON upon reaching 2500 MSL. Approximately 80 seconds later, C-FXGO/HRT242, a Chartright Air CL30, was cleared for takeoff on runway 07. In the meantime, the Ottawa Terminal controller had instructed PTR2363 to maintain runway heading. The required IFR separation of 3 NM horizontally was briefly lost as C-FXGO climbed on runway heading to their assigned altitude of 5000 feet MSL; spacing between aircraft reduced to 2.6 NM while the aircraft were within 1000 feet vertically. PTR2363 was given a right turn to prevent a further reduction in spacing. There were no reported TCAS alerts from either aircraft.

C-GFNJ, an Aero Vodochody L39C operated by ITPS (Canada) Ltd., was conducting a training flight from London International Airport (CYXU), ON, with 2 pilots on board. While initiating a descent, the pilot pulled back the thrust lever but observed that the RPM had remained at 100%. The training flight was discontinued and ATC was advised of the situation, and a return to CYXU was requested. An emergency was declared as there was a high likelihood of the aircraft brakes becoming hot or overheated during the landing roll. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) was dispatched to be present for the landing. The pilot made a shallow and fast approach, shutting down the engine on short final. The aircraft landed on runway 33, using approximately 7000 feet of runway, and came to a stop with heavy smoke observed from the main landing gear, but no fire was observed. ARFF inspected the brakes and did not observe any damage to the aircraft. Post flight inspection did not reveal any issues with the throttle linkage, further inspection revealed that the Fuel Control Valve (FCV) had failed. The FCV will be replaced, and the aircraft will be returned to service.

C-GZNR, an Airbus Helicopters AS350 B3e operated by the Nova Scotia Department of Natural Resources and Renewables, was conducting aerial fire suppression operations near Five Finger Lake, NS (44°40'26"N, 065°11'19"W). While refilling the water bucket from the lake and beginning to lift off with the load at approximately 75 feet above the lake surface, the pilot reported hearing a loud bang followed by a loss of power. The helicopter subsequently impacted the water and became partially submerged. The pilot sustained serious injuries and was transported to hospital for medical treatment. The TSB is investigating.

C-GJZY, a De Havilland DHC-8-402 operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight JZA17, was conducting a flight from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. While en route, the first officer became partially incapacitated. The captain actioned company procedures, completed the appropriate checklists, and continued the flight with priority handling to CYOW. The aircraft landed uneventfully, and Emergency Medical Services (EMS) met the aircraft at the gate. The First Officer was transported to hospital.

C-FPWE, an Air Canada A320 was operating flight AC584 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ. During cruise a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-GRUU, a Carson Air Limited Raytheon Beechcraft B300 (King Air 350) aircraft, was operating flight CRN555, under instrument flight rules, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Williams Lake Airport (CYWL), BC. Approximately 10 minutes after departure, climbing through 10 000 feet above sea level, the flight crew noticed a yellow HYD FLUID LOW annunciator. The appropriate checklist was actioned and the flight crew decided to return to CYVR. Air traffic control (ATC) was informed of the issue and company dispatch was updated on the situation. On descent, the flight crew heard the hydraulic system attempting to pressurize and the landing gear relay circuit breaker popped. Without resetting the circuit breaker, the flight crew placed the landing gear handle in the down position and received no indications on the landing gear position. When they were on final, approximately 15 nautical miles from touchdown, the flight crew manually pumped the landing gear into the down and locked position with 3 green indication lights illuminated. The flight crew declared an emergency to ATC. The aircraft landed without incident and the airplane was taxied to the hangar under its own power. After shutdown, hydraulic fluid was seen under the right main landing gear.Maintenance personnel found the right main landing gear (MLG) hydraulic actuator was leaking and it was removed and replaced with a serviceable unit. The required rigging, adjustments, and testing were completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FPIJ, a Cargojet B767 was operating flight CJT588 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON. After deviating around a line of thunderstorms, the pilot heard the Autopilot Disconnect aural warning and noticed a few EICAS messages: AUTOPILOT DISC, IAS DISAGREE, RUDDER RATIO, AILERON LOCKOUT. After completing the IAS DISAGREE NNC there was an additional GND PROX SYS EICAS message pop up. The crew completed all the checklist items. Unable to restore any of the Autopilots, they declared PAN PAN and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GQXD, a Piper PA-31-350 operated by 2080061 Ontario Inc. (dba SkyCare Air Ambulance) was conducting IFR flight PHX 2009 from Gillam Airport (CYGX), MB, to South Indian Lake Airport (CZSN), MB. C-GQXD was preparing to land at CZSN and were told a company aircraft was parked at the edge of the taxiway due to a flat tire. The flight crew continued the approach but did not notice that the aircraft did not have 3 green landing gear lights on. During the landing flair, the flight crew became aware that the gear had not been extended and performed a go-around. They configured the aircraft for landing and the aircraft landed safely on the next approach. The aircraft taxied off the runway. After shutdown, the flight crew discovered that the communication antenna on the bottom of the fuselage had made contact with the runway. No other damage was found. Pieces of the communication antenna were recovered from the runway.

C-ILNH, un paramoteur Air Conception Nitro 200 effectuait un vol privé depuis Saint-Cutbert, QC avec seul le pilote à son bord. Au retour à Saint-Cuthbert après environ 1 heure 30 minutes de vol, le pilote a ressenti de la chaleur et a réalisé que l’aéronef était en feu. Il s’est posé immédiatement dans un champ alors que ses vêtements étaient en feu. Il a réussi à se retirer du feu et enlever ses vêtements, mais a subi des brulures graves. Le paramoteur a été détruit par le feu.

C-IHVW, un ultra-léger de type évolué Bilsam Enterprises Sky Cruiser en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Charlevoix, QC (CYML) à destination de Neuville, QC (CNV9) avec seul le pilote à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage sur la piste 24, le pilote a perdu la maîtrise en lacet, a fait une sortie latérale de piste du côté droit et la roue de nez s’est brisée. Le pilote n’a pas été blessé, toutefois l’aéronef a subi des dommages importants.

C-FTGD, un Beechcraft C24R Sierra 200 en exploitation privée, effectuait des posés-décollés depuis l’aérodrome de Lachute (CSE4), QC, en conditions météorologiques de vol à vue avec seul un pilote à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage, l’aéronef a glissé sur le ventre puisque le train d’atterrissage était rentré. Il n’y eut aucun blessé et l’appareil a subi des dommages structurels au fuselage.

C-GOIE, an Air Transat A321-271NX was operating flight TSC117 from Paris Charles De Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France, to Québec /Jean Lesage International Airport (CYQB), QC. During cruise a cabin crew member sustained a minor injury and was unable to perform duties. These duties were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-FZQS un Airbus A320-214 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA302, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Vancouver, BC (CYVR), à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Lors de l’approche initiale, l’équipage a reçu le message « F/CTL FLAP LOCKED » du moniteur électronique centralisé de bord (ECAM) lorsque les volets ont étésélectionné à la position numéro 2. L’équipage a interrompu l’approche et effectué une remontée. Suite à l’évaluation du problème de volet, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN). Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été avisés et l’aéronef a atterri sans encombre sur la piste 06L. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé. Un roulement défectueux dans le système de volets a été remplacé et l'appareil remis en service.

C-GKOE, an Air Canada A320 was operating flight AC1093 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to San Diego International Airport (KSAN), CA. During climb, above 15 000 feet, the flight attendants in the rear galley reported an oil smell and both were unable to continue their duties. The crew completed the relevant quick reference handbook checklists and elected to returned to CYYZ. The crew declared a Pan Pan with Cleveland center. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 33R, completed a hot brake inspection before taxiing to the gate. Both ill flight attendants were met by EMS.Air Canada maintenance completed their inspection, the right-hand engine lower pressure turbine plug was replaced. A further engine inspection was completed without further issues and the aircraft was returned to service.

The Air Tindi De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltc. DHC-7-103, C-GCEV, was operating as TIN107 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT to Hay River Airport (CYHY), NT with 3 flight crew and no passengers. While enroute to CYHY, the flight crew observed erratic turbine inlet temperature (T5) indications on the No.1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada, PT6A-50). The flight crew actioned the QRH, contacted operations and returned to CYZF. While on approach to CYZF the flight crew elected to shut down the No. 1 engine as a precaution. The aircraft conducted a 3-engine approach and landing without further incident. Company maintenance is troubleshooting and will advise TSB of their findings.

Le British Aerospace 125 (BAe-125-1000) immatriculé N868WU, exploité par 868WU LLC effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis Sullivan County International Airport (KMSV), NY aux États-Unis à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC. En approche finale à CYUL, le pilote a déclaré un état d’urgence en raison d’une indication que la roue de nez n’était pas verrouillée. Une approche basse a été effectuée et la tour de contrôle a observé que le train semblait sorti. Lors de la remontée, l’indication de la roue avant a changé au statut verrouillé. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 24L sans encombre.

C-FDND, a de Havilland DHC-8-102 operated by PAL Airlines, was operating as PVL927 on an IFR flight from St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL, to Deer Lake Airport (CYDF), NL. C-GCIQ, a Bell 429 helicopter operated by the Canadian Coast Guard, was operating as CTG434 on a local VFR flight from CYYT. C-FDND departed CYYT Runway 28 and received a Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) Traffic Advisory (TA) followed by a Resolution Advisory (RA). The TCAS RA was due to C-GCIQ who had been cleared right downwind for Runway 28 at CYYT. C-FDND reacted to the RA and then visually acquired C-GCIQ. The helicopter was opposite direction and about 0.5 NM north of the PAL Airlines’ C-FDND departure path. The helicopter traffic had not been passed to C-FDND on departure. NAV CANADA assessed the incident as an operational irregularity and is investigating.

C-GHPJ, an Air Canada Rouge A321-200 was operating flight ROU1812 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Cancun International Airport (MMUN), MX. During cruise, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-FXCA, un Boeing 767-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA7309 et C-GJTH, un Airbus 321-211 exploité par Air Canada Rouge LP sous l’indicatif ROU1523 effectuaient leur vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, tous les deux à destination de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL). ACA7309 était à 4000 pieds en interception de la piste 24R et ROU1523 était à 3300 pieds en descente pour 3000 pieds en interception de la piste 24L lorsque l’espacement entre les 2 aéronefs a été réduit à 2,5 miles marins sur le plan horizontal et 700 pieds sur le plan vertical. L'espacement requis était de 3 miles marins et 1000 pieds.

On 10 August 2025, at 1652 MDT a Porter Airlines Inc. Embraer E295 (POE408, C-GZQM) was cleared for take-off from Runway 30 at Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. A few moments later, a Westjet Airlines Inc. Boeing B737 (WJA152, C-GJLZ) was instructed to line up on Runway 30 at CYEG. At 1653:27 WJA152 was cleared to take-off from Runway 30 at CYEG. When WJA152 became airborne, spacing behind POE408 was 2.4 NM where 3 NM was required.

C-GKKN, a Westjet B787-9 was operating flight WS9 from Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During cruise, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst remaining cabin crew members.

C-GCUQ, a Government of Canada, Department of Transportation Bell 412EP helicopter, departed Prince Rupert/Seal Cove (Coast Guard) Heliport (CBY5), BC, on flight CTG948, under visual flight rules, to Maitland Island (53° 44' 05" N, 128° 56' 02" W), BC, with 1 flight crew member on board. The helicopter was carrying a slung basket of construction materials. During the initial climb at an airspeed of approximately 60 knots, the pilot observed that the slung basket was oscillating and beginning to spin. The pilot elected to return to CBY5 to rectify the load. On short final, part of the load exited the basket. After landing, it was reported that additional parts of the load had exited the basket undetected during the departure. The load had been inspected prior to takeoff with nothing abnormal noted. No injuries or damage was reported. The flight was conducted over an unoccupied forest and water. A vessel was dispatched to look for the debris that splashed down on short final.

C-GUFU, an Air Transat A330-200 was operating flight TSC691 from Eleftherios Venizelos Airport (LGAV), Athens, Greece, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During cruise, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-GJIX, an Airbus Helicopters AS 350 B-2 aircraft operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd., was conducting local external load wildfire fighting operations from Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL. The helicopter departed the company hangar at CYYR and crossed Runway 15/33 heading south with a slung long line and Bambi Bucket attached. The helicopter was in the departure climb below 500 feet above ground when the long line and bucket detached. The slung load fell in the CYYR airport midfield, and no persons or structures were in the area where the load fell. The minor damage to the bucket from the unintentional release was repaired. A full inspection and test of the external hook, long line and bucket was conducted with no faults found. It is considered that the external load was not adequately secured before the departure on the occurrence flight.

C-GUKF, a privately registered Cessna C150, was taxiing, as cleared by ATC after landing, to Apron 1 via Taxiway B at Winnipeg/St. Andrews Airport (CYAV), MB. Staff 24, a CYAV Maintenance truck, was proceeding to Apron 1, as cleared by ATC, via Taxiway A. C-GUKF's ground speed while taxiing was observed as being higher than the typical taxi speed. C-GUKF and Staff 24 collided at the intersection of Apron 1, which is uncontrolled, and Taxiway B. The pilot shut down the aircraft and exited to assess the damage with the driver of Staff 24. After inspecting the damage, the pilot started the aircraft and continued to taxi to Apron 1 under its own power. There was no fire. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

On 11 August 2025, a Loon Air Inc. Cessna U206G (C-FJST) on floats was flying at 800 feet AGL on a visual flight rules flight, returning from South Leland Lake, NT to 4 Mile Lake, ON. The pilot was the sole occupant. At approximately 13 NM ESE of the Fort Smith Airport, NT (CYSM), at around 1140 MDT, the engine began to sputter due to fuel depletion in the left wingtip tank. The pilot selected the right wingtip tank and turned the boost pump on; however, the engine (TCM IO 550-F) continued to sputter and eventually shut down due to fuel starvation. Due to the aircraft's height above ground, the pilot shifted his focus to picking a forced landing spot. The pilot carried out a forced landing in a marsh. The aircraft sustained minor damage and there were no injuries. The ELT did not activate. The pilot was recovered by a helicopter and returned to a camp on 4 Mile Lake.

C-GFSA, a Summit Air ATR-72, was conducting flight BF7514 from Naujaat Airport (CYUT), NU to Thompson Municipal Airport (CYTH), MB with 3 crew members on board. Approximately 100 nautical miles north-northeast of CYTH, while in cruise flight, the crew received a LO LVL alert for the blue hydraulic system. The crew carried out the appropriate QRH checklist. The crew declared a PAN PAN with Winnipeg ATC stating that they would potentially leak hydraulic fluid onto the airport surface and that ground maneuverability was affected by the failure but that no assistance was required. Winnipeg ATC relayed the message to CYTH radio, who had ARFF on standby. The crew performed a flapless landing at CYTH without incident and taxied to the ramp followed by the fire trucks.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and found the RH spoiler valve block leaking from splines and hydraulic unions. The RH spoiler valve block (part number BHC1201) was replaced. They serviced the hydraulic reservoir and an operational test and leak check was carried out. No other faults found and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FHOZ, a Robinson R44 II operated by Zimmer Air Services Inc., was conducting aerial spray operations over a corn field approximately 9.5 NM west of Windsor International Airport (CYQG), ON, with the pilot as sole occupant. While descending through approximately 150 feet AGL while entering the field for a spray run, the low rotor RPM horn sounded, and the gauges confirmed that the engine was no longer producing power. The pilot nosed down to gain airspeed and then began a cyclic flare over the corn field. The helicopter contacted the top of the corn stalks with minimal rate of descent and forward speed, but the first contact with the corn resulted in the helicopter yawing to the right. The tail boom became severed during the landing sequence, and the helicopter came to rest on its left side. The pilot, who had been wearing a seatbelt and flight helmet, was able to exit the helicopter unassisted and was not injured. There was no fire, and no leakage of fuel or chemical in the field itself. The ELT activated and the signal was detected by the JRCC. The operator will examine the engine and helicopter to determine the cause of the engine failure.

C-GFAH, an Airbus 330-343 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA667 from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During the pre-flight, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform the duties of the position. Safety-related duties were reassigned accordingly amongst remaining crew for the remainder of the flight. The aircraft continued and landed at CYUL without further incident.

C-GAZB, un Cessna 180J en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le lac Alexandre situé à environ 80 miles nautiques au nord ouest de sa destination, l'hydroaérodrome du Lac-des-Rapides, Sept-îles (CSM8), QC, avec un pilote et un passager. Au moment de l'amerrissage, l'appareil a percuté la surface miroitante du lac entrainant la perte de contrôle latérale où les deux embouts d'ailes ont été lourdement endommagés. L'appareil s'est immobilisé sur ses flotteurs qui n'avaient pas de dommages apparents. Le passager a été légèrement blessé et transporté à l'hôpital pour examen.

C-FRQW, a Jazz E175 was operating flight JZA585 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Pittsburgh International Airport (KPIT), PA. During cruise, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-FLWJ, a Westjet Boeing 737-700, was operating as flight WS133 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew members, 3 cabin crew members, and 96 passengers on board. During the arrival into CYVR, a stabilizer out of trim caution illuminated. The crew performed the applicable checklist and continued the flight without the use of auto throttle or autopilot. The flight crew requested that emergency services be on standby for their arrival at CYVR. No emergency was declared. The flight landed without further incident.

C-GENU, a WestJet Encore Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, on flight WEN3592, under instrument flight rules, to Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies Airport (CYXC), BC. When the aircraft began its descent from cruise altitude, passengers reported seeing flames and/or sparks coming from the left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW150A). A flight attendant looked at the left engine nacelle and reported the presence of flames to the flight deck approximately 21 minutes before landing in CYXC. All engine indications seen on the flight deck were normal. The flight crew asked a cabin crew member to look at the engine to verify what was being seen. Approximately 1 minute later, it was reported that flames were no longer visible by the cabin crew member but were still visible to a passenger. The aircraft subsequently began deviations to avoid thunderstorms in the area. The passenger had taken a photo of the engine nacelle and reported that they believed there was small hole in the left engine nacelle, with sparks being visible within the hole. A visual inspection of the engine nacelle was not performed by either pilot, nor was the photo taken by the passenger seen by either pilot during the flight. Approximately 10 seconds after the hole was first reported, it was concluded that it was a normal feature of the nacelle and that the reported sparks were engine exhaust. Communication between the cabin and flight deck regarding the reported flames and sparks concluded approximately 2 minutes after the first report of flames to the flight deck.Engine indications on the flight deck remained normal, and the flight landed without further incident in CYXC. After landing, oil was found dripping from the left nacelle. A maintenance inspection discovered that the left engine oil cooler was leaking oil. The investigation determined that the reported hole in the engine nacelle was a dark patch of engine oil which had collected on the lower side surface of the engine nacelle during flight. The left engine oil cooler was replaced, and an engine ground run was performed without occurrence of sparks or flames. The aircraft was subsequently returned to service.

C-GYJW,  an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 (Dreamliner) was preparing to depart Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, on flight AC7, under instrument flight rules, to Hong Kong International Airport (VHHH), Hong Kong, with 4 flight crew members, 9 cabin crew members, and 288 passengers on board. Before departure, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to continue their duties. The cabin crew member was replaced, and the flight departed without further incident.

C-FMFP, a Rockwell 690A aircraft operated by the Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency as flight BD166, was conducting a local VFR flight from the Prince Albert/Glass Field Airport (CYPA), SK. While returning to CYPA, the crew observed the "low fuel" warning. In anticipation of a fuel shortage, an emergency was declared and an engine was shutdown to conserve fuel. The aircraft landed uneventfully at CYPA with aircraft rescue and firefighting services standing by.The operator's maintenance department discovered that the fuel indicating system was reading high. The aircraft was ferried to a maintenance base and the fuel indicating system was recalibrated.

C-FNAG, an Aspen Air Charters Inc., PA-31-350 was on an IFR flight from Burlington Airpark (CZBA), ON, to Rhode Island TF Green International Airport (KPVD), RI. The pilot observed that the fuel quantity in the RH tank was depleting faster than expected and elected to divert to Albany International Airport (KALB), NY, where the flight landed without incident and taxied to the CBP ramp for customs clearance. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) were aware that the aircraft had diverted due to a fuel quantity issue, waited for the aircraft as it landed, and then followed the aircraft to the CBP ramp. Upon shutdown, the RH engine caught fire. Aircraft rescue and firefighting extinguished the fire, and the passengers and pilot evacuated the aircraft safely. R/H engine and cowling received fire damage.Maintenance determined that the source of the fire was a cracked fitting from the Electronic Instruments FT60 Red Box fuel transducer.

C-GYLP, a Westjet B-737 Max 8 was operating flight WS2923 from Holguin/Frank Pais International Airport (MUHG), Cuba, to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Shortly after take-off, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-GNBE, un Airbus A220 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA416 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Lester B. Pearson de Toronto (CYYZ), ON à destination de l'aéroport international de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC. C-GEJL, un Boeing 737-8 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA374 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Winnipeg (CYWG), MB, à destination de l'aéroport international de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC. Alors que ACA374 était en finale pour la piste 24L, ACA416 qui était en vent arrière a reçu l’instruction de tourner à droite sur un cap de 080, de descendre à 3000 pieds et de réduire à 190 nœuds. Le AC416 semblait sur une trajectoire qui le rapprochait de l’approche finale et un cap de 090 lui a été assigné. L’espacement entre les deux appareils a été réduit à 800 pieds sur le plan vertical et 2,3 miles marins sur le plan horizontal alors que l’espacement requis était de 1000 et 3 miles marins. Les 2 appareils se sont posés sans encombre.UPDATED 14 August 2025

C-GDJZ, un Bombardier CRJ 900 exploité par Jazz Aviation Lp sous l'indicatif JZA7774 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC. C-FFQO, un Cessna 152 exploité par Orizon Aviation Inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport Cornwall Regional (CYCC), ON à destination de l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC. JZA7774 était en descente pour 3000 pieds, vent arrière. C-FFQO traversait la zone du terminal à une altitude de 3500 pieds, à environ 2nm au sud sur un cap parallèle à JZA7774. Alors qu'il dépasse C-FFQO, JZA7774 est instruit de virer sur sa droite pour intercepter ILS piste 24R. Au moment où sa trajectoire d'interception convergeait avec celle de C-FFQO et qu'il questionnait le contrôleur sur la proximité de l'autre appareil, JZA7774 a reçu un avertissement de résolution TCAS (RA) avec une indication de trafic 300 pieds au-dessus. Le JZA7774 a suivi le RA du TCAS et est descendu pour éviter l'autre appareil. Au point le plus rapproché, le radar indiquait une distance horizontale de 0.8 nm et verticale de 500 pieds. JZA7774 est remonté pour intercepter l'ILS en finale, C-FFQO a poursuivi sa route vers sa destination. Les 2 appareils ont atterri sans encombre.

C-GYEZ un autogire de type Autogyro Cavalon en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport d'Alma, QC (CYTF) à destination de l'aérodrome de St-Apollinaire, QC (CAA4) avec un pilote et un passager à bord. L'appareil a décollé de la piste 13 et lors de la montée initiale il a tourné vers la droite. Le pilote a remarqué que la vitesse diminuait et par le fait même, l'altitude. Le pilote a appliqué la pleine puissance et le moteur a répondu comme prévu, mais la perte d'altitude se poursuivait. Juste avant de percuter les arbres le pilote a réduit la vitesse à zéro et l’aéronef est descendu verticalement dans le boisé situé à droite de l'axe en bout de piste 13. Le pilote et le passager sont sortis de l'appareil et le pilote a contacté les services d'urgence. Les 2 ont subi des blessures légères.

C-FXHS, a Yellowhead Helicopters Limited AS350 B2, departed Mason Creek, BC, to pick up an external load for a client. The client’s external load rigging was attached to the aircraft’s long line. Shortly after departure, 2 of the 4 lanyards broke on the rigging and the load fell to the ground in a remote and wooded area. No injuries were reported. The helicopter was not damaged. Subsequent loads and straps were inspected by the client and the pilot prior to slinging.The dropped load was retrieved and moved by external load to a staging location.

C-FGYN, a Top Aces Inc., McDonnell Douglas A-4N, was operating approximately 30 nm NE of Group Captain R.W. McNair - Cold Lake (CYOD), AB at FL260 when the pilot increased the throttle. A popping noise was heard from the engine accompanied with a noticeable airframe shake. The pilot then reduced the throttle to a lower power setting which initially cleared the engine stall; however, the event occurred again. Following the second event, the pilot reduced the throttle setting yet again, declared an emergency, and conducted a powered on precautionary approach leaving the throttle in a fixed position until landing was assured. The aircraft landed safely shortly afterward.

C-GCGB, an Airspan Helicopters Ltd. Bell 212, was transporting wildfire crews near Bison Lake, AB, approximately 49 nm ENE of Manning Airport (CFX4), AB. While transiting to a fire suppression area NE of Bison Lake the pilot observed a 'TRANS OIL PRESSURE' light accompanied by a drop in transmission oil pressure. The pilot reduced power and landed immediately and shut down the aircraft. The pilot and passengers disembarked the aircraft without further incident.Following the flight the maintenance team found a ruptured transmission oil line. The line was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GXNV, a Vans RV9A, was operating on a local flight from Wetaskiwin (CEX3), AB to Linden, AB, a private nonregistered grass airstrip. During the landing the aircraft struck a fence and flipped upside down. Both occupants were assisted out of the aircraft. The pilot received minor injuries, and the passenger received serious injuries. There was no post impact fire. The aircraft had performed as required for the flight.

C-FAPL, a privately registered Piper PA-31 Navajo, departed Kashechewan Airport (CZKE), ON, on a flight with another pilot on board. While on short final to Runway 28 at Timmins Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON, the Flight Service Specialist (FSS) observed that the aircraft’s landing gear did not appear to be extended. FSS radioed C-FAPL to confirm the gear status, but the aircraft landed gear-up. The aircraft skidded along Runway 28 through the intersection with Runway 03/21 before coming to a stop on the runway. There were no reported injuries; however, the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FSIQ, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 (Max 8) airplane, was conducting flight AC105, under instrument flight rules, from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. C-GKFB, an Air Canada Rouge LP Airbus A321-211 airplane, was conducting flight ROU1901, under instrument flight rules from CYYZ to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. A loss of separation occurred 37 nautical miles (NM) north-northeast of Castlegar/West Kootenay Regional Airport (CYCG), BC, while both aircraft were in cruise. The Airbus was in trail of the Boeing and 2000 feet lower at flight level FL340. The Airbus was cleared to climb to FL360 which was the same altitude as the Boeing. At their closest, the aircraft were separated by 4.2 NM horizontally at the same altitude. The minimum required separation was 5 NM horizontally or 1000 feet vertically.The Airbus was subsequently turned right and the appropriate separation was re-established.

C-GENV, a Westjet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC–8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was conducting flight WEN3162 from Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. When the aircraft was at flight level 250, approximately 30 minutes after takeoff, the flight crew observed a CABIN ALT master warning. The quick response checklist was actioned for a rapid de-pressurization and the pilot started an emergency descent. The flight crew declared a mayday and received vectors from ATC and were able to descend below 10 000 feet above sea level. The aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance replaced the pack flow control and shutoff valve, and pressurization checks were successfully carried out and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWUE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was conducting flight WEN3146, under instrument flight rules, from Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the take-off roll, the flight crew observed #1 and #2 bleed hot caution lights and a deice pressure caution light. The flight crew executed a low speed rejected take off and declared a MAYDAY. The flight crew taxied off the runway and returned to the gate.Company maintenance replaced the LH wing duct check valve, the pack control shut off valve, and the RH high pressure shut off valve. Operational tests of the bleed air system and the deicing system air supply were carried out with no faults.

C-FONK, WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-8CT was operating as flight WJA215 from Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), ON. to Calgary International (CYYC), AB. ATC had been step descending WJA215 into CYYC due to departing traffic and was levelling off at FL190. C-FWIJ, a WestJet airlines Boeing 737-8CT, operating as flight WJA268 from CYYC to James Armstrong Richardson International (CYWG), MB was cleared to FL180 but misheard the clearance to be FL190. The flight crew attempted to verify the clearance with ATC and ATC stated the clearance of FL190. Approximately 33 nm ESE of CYYC, C-FONK responded to a TCAS RA. Separation was reduced to 2.4 nm, where 5 nm horizontally and 1000 feet vertically is required. Once separation was regained, both flights continued to their destinations.

C-GCEV, a De Havilland Canada DHC7-100 operated by Air Tindi, was conducting IFR flight TIN701 from Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON, to Webequie Airport (CYWP), ON. While in cruise the aircraft experienced a number 1 hydraulic system failure. The crew completed the actions of the quick reference handbook checklist and elected to divert back to CYQT. After an uneventful approach and landing, the flight crew requested a tow to the apron.The operator's maintenance investigated and found the #1 and #2 hydraulic pump shafts had sheared which caused the flow of hydraulic fluid in the #1 hydraulic system to stop. Aircraft maintenance engineers flushed the system and the component seals, the hydraulic reservoir, the #1 and #2 hydraulic pumps, and all filters were all replaced. The system was then replenished and the system was tested serviceable with no leak detected. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOIR, an Airbus A321neo operated by Air Transat was conducting a flight from Manchester International Airport (EGCC), UK, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) ON. During cruise, the aircraft experienced wake turbulence from an opposite direction Airbus A380, 1000 feet above. Two cabin crew members sustained minor injuries and one of these members was considered incapacitated and unable to perform their duties. First aid was provided, and the flight continued to the destination without further incident.

C-GIWJ, a Westjet B737-8 was operating flight WS1853 from Kahului Airport (PHOG), HI, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During climb, a vape pen in a passenger's bag malfunctioned and there was smoke with an electrical burning smell. A flight attendant put the device in a metal container and fully submersed it in water. The flight crew was advised of the situation, and the decision was made to continue to destination where the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GHEZ, a Zenair 701 operated privately was conducting solo training flight from the owner’s grass strip. On landing the pilot experienced a bounce and then a hard landing which resulted in the aircraft nosing over and coming to rest on its back. The aircraft received substantial damage, and the pilot received minor injuries. First responders attended the scene, and the aircraft was released to the owner.

C-GGAS, a Bell 206B helicopter operated by Apex Helicopters Inc., was conducting aerial application of fungicide on a corn field in the vicinity of Thamesford, ON, approximately 6 nautical miles NE of London International Airport (CYXU), ON. The pilot was the sole occupant of the helicopter. During a reversal of direction following a spray run, the helicopter began to yaw to the right. The right yaw continued until the helicopter touched down with a high rate of descent before rolling over onto its right side. The helicopter had landed in a field of wheat stubble, and a post-crash fire began almost immediately. The emergency locator transmitter activated. Two people who had been driving in the opposite direction witnessed the crash from their cars, parked near the crash site, and ran to the helicopter to help the pilot out of the wreckage. The pilot received serious injuries and was airlifted to the hospital.

C-GCJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ9), was operating as flight JZA113 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT. On approach into CYZF the flight crew received an anti-skid indication and requested vectors to carry out the emergency check list. A longer runway was required due to the inoperative anti-skid system. The flight crew requested to divert to Grand Prairie (CYQU), AB. The flight crew declared a Pan Pan and requested AARF to stand by. The flight landed safely in CYQU at 2259 MDT.

C-FNOG, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC846 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Frankfurt Airport (EDDF), Germany. On approach to Runway 25R, a go-around was initiated due to a TCAS RA on short final at 1000 feet. ATC was informed of a police helicopter south of the runway.

C-GTGP, a Beech B200 operated by Transwest Air Limited (dba Rise Air), was conducting an IFR medevac flight from North Battleford Airport, SK (CYQW) to Stony Rapids, SK (CYSF). While in cruise the power was reduced from 1500 foot-pounds to 1000 foot-pounds. When the power reached 1000ftlbs, the number 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-42) started to surge. Torque and Ng gauges showed increases and decreases related to the surges. The flight crew reduced the power lever to the idle detent to try to stop surges but had no success. They decided to perform an in-flight shutdown of the engine. Once the engine was shutdown and the checklist completed, the crew diverted to La Ronge/Barber Field Airport, SK (CYVC) and the airplane landed uneventfully.The operator's maintenance completed a General Visual Inspection (GVI) as well as a Boroscope Inspection (BSI) but did not find any fault. Both High Pressure (HP) and Low Pressure (LP) bleeds were removed for inspection and the HP bleed was found to be sticky and not moving freely. Both bleed valves were replaced and ground runs were conducted and successful. The aircraft was released for a test flight which ended up being unsuccessful as the surges reappeared at altitude as soon as the power lever was moved. A Blow Off Valve (BOV) opening test was conducted and the valve was found to be opening at 4-5% lower than specifications. The unit was re-orificed to achieve the Maintenance Manual test specifications for ground runs. The compressor was found to be dirty and a compressor wash was performed. The aircraft was released for a second test flight, which was successful, and it was subsequently returned to service.

C-GUXN, a privately registered Grumman American Aviation Corporation AA-5A, was conducting a local visual flight rules flight from Gatineau–Ottawa Executive Airport (CYND), QC, with one pilot and two passengers on board.At approximately 1748 EDT, while at 3000 feet ASL over the city of Ottawa, ON, the aircraft sustained a catastrophic engine failure. The pilot turned southbound and received clearance to land on Runway 14 at Ottawa/Macdonald–Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON.At approximately 1752, the aircraft descended below airport elevation into lower terrain near the Rideau River. The aircraft collided with trees in a residential area approximately 960 metres short of Runway 14 and came to rest suspended in trees atop power lines. There was no post-impact fire; however, the emergency locator transmitter (ELT) activated, and its signal was received by the appropriate authorities.The pilot was fatally injured. The two passengers sustained serious injuries and were transported to hospital.

C-GRYI, an ATR 42-500 operated by Transwest Air Limited (dba Rise Air), was conducting IFR flight RS280 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport, SK (CYXE) to Stony Rapids Airport, SK (CYSF). When on approach into CYSF, the flight crew selected the gear down but couldn't confirm normal extension of the landing gear. They elected to abort the approach and entered a hold to troubleshoot the issue. After consultation with the operator's maintenance and operations department, it was decided to divert to CYXE. A PAN PAN was declared with ATC. On descent into CYXE, the flight crew conducted a gravity gear extension and received indication that it had extended. The flight landed without further incident.Operator's maintenance conducted a functional test of the landing gear extension and retraction. The retraction of the landing gear was found serviceable but the extension was found unserviceable with all UNLK (unlock) lights from primary and secondary landing gear indicator illuminated and no movement of the landing gear. They performed several inspections and replaced a selector valve. A subsequent functional test of the normal landing gear extension and retraction was found serviceable for both actions as well as the functional test of emergency extension. The aircraft was returned to service after a successful test flight.

C-GBHY, un Airbus 319 exploité par Air Canada Rouge sous l'indicatif ROU1653 et N17317, un Boeing 737-8 MAX exploité par United Airlines sous l'indicatif UAL587, effectuaient leur vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, tous les deux à destination de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). ROU1653 et UAL587 étaient en train d’intercepter l’approche finale de la piste 24L, l'espacement a été réduit à 2,4 NM sur le plan horizontal et 400 pieds verticaux. L'espacement requis était de 3 NM et 1000 pieds. Les 2 aéronefs ont atterri sans encombre.

A7-CGL, a Gulfstream G650ER operated by Qatar Executive, was conducting IFR flight QQE217 from King County International/Boeing Field Airport, USA (KBFI) to Amsterdam/Schiphol International Airport, Netherlands (EHAM). While in cruise 128NM south-southwest of Coral Harbour, NU (CYZS), the flight crew received an alert for a flight control malfunction (Spoiler Panel Failure) and, shortly after, an IRS power interruption. The flight crew did the related checklists, declared a PAN PAN with ATC, and elected to divert to Washington/Dulles International Airport, USA (KIAD) as a precaution. The aircraft landed uneventfully KIAD.The operator's maintenance completed several checks of both systems but could not replicate the faults. They swapped the inboard and midboard spoiler Remote Electronics Unit (REU) to further troubleshoot. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTSW, a WestJet Boeing 737-8 (Max 8), was operating as flight WS1865, under instrument flight rules, from Daniel K Inouye International Airport (PHNL), HI, U.S., to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During the final descent to CYVR, a cabin crew member became unwell and was unable to perform their duties. The flight landed safely and emergency medical services personnel assessed the cabin crew member.

C-FWRM, un Beech King Air A100 exploité par Propair Inc, sous l'indicatif PRO4200 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) à destination de Wemindji, QC (CYNC) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 1 passager à bord. Lors de la montée après le décollage une indication anormale de porte est apparue. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a effectué un retour à CYUY. L’avion s’est posé sur la piste 26 sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

N2471A, a privately registered Piper PA-22-135, was on a flight from the Ponoka Airport (CEH3), AB, to a private airstrip 18 NM northwest of the Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, with only the pilot on board. After touching down at the private airstrip, the aircrafts brakes were ineffective, and the aircraft impacted a fence at the end of the airstrip, coming to rest inverted. The aircraft's emergency locator transmitter (ELT) activated and remained on after the accident. An RCMP helicopter responded to the ELT signal and once located turned off the ELT. The pilot suffered minor injuries and was able to self-extricate from the aircraft. The aircraft was substantially damaged.After the accident the pilot inspected the brakes and noted that there was no brake fluid in the system.

C-FTMY, a Morningstar Air Express ATR-72-202, was operating as flight MAL7059 from Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During cruise at FL200 the crew observed the cabin heat increase to full hot. The crew actioned the quick reference handbook but were unable to stop the heating of the cockpit and declared a Pan Pan, requesting a descent. During the descent to 10 000 feet, the crew turned off the pack valves which stopped the heating and both a cabin alt high, and duct over temp light illuminated. The flight continued to CYYC and landed uneventfully.Company maintenance personnel replaced the flight compartment temp controller.

N850EC, a Hawker 850XP operating as flight RVJ850, was conducting a flight from Pittsburgh International Airport (KPIT), PA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During landing on Runway 05, the left main landing gear failed.Shortly after the main landing gear touched down, and as the nose landing gear contacted the runway, the left main landing gear began to vibrate and shimmy, followed by a loud noise. Moments later, the bottom of the left main landing gear strut fractured, causing the wheels, axles, and chrome oleo strut to separate from the gear assembly.Unaware of the failure, the crew initially believed a tire had blown and continued the landing rollout. As the aircraft decelerated, increased control inputs were required to maintain directional control. ATC instructed the aircraft to expedite a left turn onto Runway 33R. During the turn, the crew observed that the left wingtip was contacting the runway. The aircraft came to rest on Runway 33R, north of the intersection with Runway 05.There were two persons on board, and no injuries were reported. Aircraft rescue and firefighting and airport emergency services responded.

C-FBWS, a Boeing 737-8 operated by Westjet, was conducting IFR flight WJA585 from Hamilton Airport, ON (CYHM) to Calgary International Airport, AB (CYYC). During cruise, approximately 30nm SE of Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport, SK (CYXE),A flight attendant became unable to carry out their duties. The crew member occupied a passenger seat for the remainder of the flight and their duties were distributed amongst the remaining crew members. The flight landed uneventfully at CYYC.

C-FJQD, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was operating flight ROU1790 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), Dominican Republic. During cruise, the flight crew was advised of an electrical smell in the cabin and no visible smoke was observed. The flight crew carried out the SMOKE checklist. The odour dissipated after approximately 20 minutes, and no source was identified. During descent, a second distinct odour was observed in vicinity of one of the lavatories. As a precaution, a PAN PAN was declared with ATC. The approach and landing were completed without further incident. Aircraft rescue and firefighting conducted an external inspection with no abnormalities reported.

C-GCJN, a Cargojet Airways Boeing 767-316 was operating flight CJT991 from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (KCVG), KY, to Mirabel Airport (CYMX), QC. CJT991 departed under minimum equipment list with one generator and the APU pneumatics inoperative. Shortly after takeoff, the crew declared an emergency because the APU shut down, leaving the aircraft powered by a single electrical source (left generator). Upon successful restart of the APU, the crew canceled the emergency and elected to continue to the planned destination.Maintenance replaced a permanent magnet wire which had chafing. MEL placard removed.

C-FAPL, a privately registered Piper PA-31-350, was conducting a flight from Kashechewan Airport (CZKE), ON, for the purpose of familiarizing another pilot with the aircraft. While on approach to Runway 28 at Timmins Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON, the pilots configured the aircraft for landing, including lowering the landing gear, but did not confirm three green “down and locked” indications.On short final, the Flight Service Specialist (FSS) observed that the landing gear did not appear to be extended and radioed C-FAPL to confirm gear status. The aircraft subsequently landed gear-up, skidding along Runway 28 through the intersection with Runway 03/21 before coming to a stop.The two pilots on board were not injured. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the propellers, engine nacelles, and underside of the fuselage.

C-FUJE, an Embraer 175 operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight JZA875, was conducting a flight from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. After landing and during taxi to the gate, the flight crew reported hot brakes and requested the assistance of aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF). Following an inspection by ARFF personnel, the aircraft was cleared to continue taxiing to the gate, accompanied by ARFF vehicles.

C-GMIW, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 operated by Air Canada as flight ACA1158, and C-GJZH, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight JZA252, were both inbound to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. A loss of separation occurred when ACA1158 was not given timely instructions to turn and intercept the localizer. As a result, separation was reduced to 1.5 NM laterally and 700 feet vertically, below the required minimum of 3 NM laterally and 1000 feet vertically. ACA1158 executed a missed approach. Both aircraft subsequently landed without further incident.

C-FNVV, an Air Canada Airbus A320-211 was operating flight AC2311 from Melbourne Orlando International Airport (KMLB), FL, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the flight, the crew declared a PAN PAN due to a smoke smell in the cockpit. The flight continued to destination and landed uneventfully at CYYZ with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) standing by.

C-GWEJ, a Westjet Encore DHC 8-402, was operating flight WEN3628 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Portland International Airport (KPDX), OR. During the approach, the crew declared an emergency due to flight control issues (elevator). The aircraft landed safely in KPDX.

C-GFLA, a Pilatus PC12/45 operated by Wasaya Airways Limited Partnership, was conducting an IFR flight WSG1652 from Poplar Hill, ON (CPV7) to Deer Lake, ON (CYVZ). While on approach into CYVZ, the crew did not get the 3 green gear lights. They conducted a missed approach, declared a PAN PAN, and diverted to Sioux Lookout, ON (CYXL). They carried out the checklist and requested a low pass at CYXL to confirmed the gear was in the down position. The aircraft subsequently landed uneventfully.The operator's maintenance completed several gear swings but could not replicate the fault. A subsequent inspection found a faulty wire on the actuator switch, the wire was repaired, and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FWTY, a Bell 412 aircraft operated by Wildcat Helicopters, departed the Surmont Camp [Fort McMurray International Airport (CYMM), AB, 26 NM southeast] to support firefighting operations in the area. While in cruise the pilot heard a loud bang as the helicopter yawed. The pilot observed that the #2 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6T-3D) failure caution light had illuminated. The pilot ran the appropriate emergency procedure and diverted to CYMM for an emergency single-engine approach landing. The landing was completed without incident.

C-GGSG, a Cameron Air Services Cessna TU206G equipped with amphibious floats was conducting a VFR flight from Mill Lake, ON, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, with only the pilot on board. Shortly after takeoff during cruise flight, the oil pressure gauge indicated a reading below the green arc. As all other engine parameters remained within normal limits, the pilot elected to continue the flight. However, en route, the pilot heard approximately four loud banging sounds before the oil filler access panel opened unexpectedly. Oil subsequently began leaking from the engine, spraying the windshield and obstructing visibility. The pilot declared a Mayday to Air Traffic Control (ATC) and directed the aircraft toward a farmer’s field near Linton, ON, for a forced landing. After extending the landing gear, the aircraft landed in the field. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the tail and floats, and a fence on the farm property was also damaged. The pilot was not injured. Post-incident inspection by the company’s maintenance team revealed a large hole in the top crankcase of the Teledyne Continental IO-550-DCF engine, specifically in the area of cylinders 5 and 6.

N345NW, a Delta Air Lines Airbus A320-212, was operating flight DAL2525 from Bradley International Airport (KBDL), CT, to Minneapolis–Saint Paul International Airport (KMSP), MN. Approximately 30 minutes after takeoff, the flight crew received an ENG 2 COMPRESSOR VANE ECAM (Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitor) message, though engine parameters remained within normal limits. After consulting with maintenance, the crew elected to continue the flight. Roughly 30 seconds later, an ENG 2 STALL ECAM message was displayed, followed by an ENG 2 EGT OVER LIMIT message. The crew subsequently shut down engine number 2 after completing the appropriate quick reference handbook (QRH) procedures. A Mayday was declared, and the flight diverted to Buffalo Niagara International Airport (KBUF), NY, where the aircraft landed without further incident.
C-GPDZ, a RAVIN 500 was flying from Preston, MN, to Wittman Regional Airport (KOSH), WI. During landing roll, the left main gear collapsed. There were no injuries to the 2 occupants.

C-FNJZ, a MHI RJ Aviation ULC CRJ-900 operated by Jazz Aviation LP was conducting flight JZA783 from Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (KDCA), U.S., to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Shortly after departure from KDCA, the flight crew was informed of tire debris found on the departure runway and subsequently suspected a blown tire. The crew elected to continue the flight to the planned destination and declared an emergency with Air Traffic Control (ATC). Flight JZA283 landed safely on Runway 05 at CYYZ with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) services standing by. Upon post-flight inspection by maintenance personnel, it was determined that a portion of the tire tread had separated. The affected tire was identified as a retreaded tire. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) was submitted to Transport Canada.

C-FRTN, a Cessna TP206D operated by Sky Dive Vancouver Island, was conducting a local skydiving flight from Qualicum Beach Airport (CAT4), BC, with the pilot and 4 skydivers onboard. At approximately 12 450 feet above sea level (ASL), the 4 skydivers exited the aircraft and the pilot began their descent. As the aircraft approached 10 000 feet ASL, the pilot observed a strong burning smell in the cabin that was followed by smoke, a rough running engine (Teledyne Continental TSIO-520-C), and a loss of engine power. The pilot followed the emergency checklist for an engine fire, shutdown the engine, and turned the master power switch off. The pilot declared an emergency on the mandatory frequency using a handheld radio and conducted an emergency power-off landing, with flaps retracted, on Runway 29 at CAT4. The aircraft touched down approximately 1000 feet beyond the runway threshold. The pilot applied the brakes but the aircraft continued off the end of the runway and stopped approximately 150 feet past the paved surface where it collided with the airport perimeter fence. The pilot was not injured. There was no post impact fire. The aircraft was substantially damaged.Maintenance found that there was a hole in the top of the engine crankcase near the No. 4 cylinder and the crankshaft had fractured. The engine will be removed and sent to a maintenance facility for teardown and evaluation. The engine had a total time since new of 1898.3 hours and was being maintained on an approved on-condition maintenance program in accordance with Transport Canada Airworthiness Notice B041 Edition 4. The engine manufacturer recommends an engine overhaul at 1600 hours with more frequent overhauls for stressful applications such as parachute operations.

C-GYYP, a Piper PA-31 aircraft operated by Kisik Aerial Survey, departed from Runway 25 at Deer Lake Regional Airport (CYDF), NL. After takeoff, the aircraft completed a full circuit and then turned southeast. Approximately 1/2 nautical mile south of the threshold of Runway 07, the aircraft collided with the Trans-Canada Highway (Route 1) and continued toward the side of the highway, entering a ditch approximately 12 to 15 feet deep. The aircraft came to rest on its side 200 feet from the initial point of impact. Both occupants sustained fatal injuries.

C-IEBK, a privately registered amphibious-equipped Quad City Challenger II advanced ultra-light, departed Winnipeg/Lyncrest Aerodrome (CJL5), MB, on a local VFR flight. During the flight the aircraft was observed to pitch nose down and collide with terrain. The pilot was fatally injured. Provincial 911 dispatched RCMP, fire rescue and EMS. There was no post impact fire. The TSB deployed to the occurrence.

C-GHQI, un Airbus 321-211 exploité par exploité par Air Canada Rouge LP sous l’indicatif ROU2385, effectuait un vol de mise en place selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Trois-Rivières, QC (CYRQ) à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ) avec 2 pilotes à bord. Lors de la montée après le décollage, le moteur gauche (CFM International, CFM56-5B3/3) a subi un décrochage réacteur. L’équipage a complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH), a déclaré un état d’urgence et a fait une diversion à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). L’avion s’est posé sur la piste 24R sans encombre.

C-FGKO, an Airbus Helicopters AS350 B-2 helicopter operated by Custom Helicopters Limited, was conducting a local flight, under visual flight rules, from a remote camp in northern BC to pick up 5 passengers on a mountainside with only the pilot onboard. While manoeuvring at approximately 1 foot above ground level for a hillside toe-in landing, the tail rotor contacted rising terrain. The pilot executed an overshoot, landed approximately 1000 feet downslope, and conducted an emergency shutdown and secured the aircraft. There were no reported injuries. The helicopter was substantially damaged.After shutting down the aircraft, a visual inspection determined that the tail rotor was damaged. The aircraft was recovered to a maintenance facility where repairs to the tail rotor, tail rotor gear box, tail boom, and other components will be carried out.

C-FCYX, an Air Canada Airbus A320-214, was conducting flight AC1058, under instrument flight rules, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, NV. C-FYUL, a Monarch Air Limited Cessna 560XLS (Citation Excel), was conducting a flight, under instrument flight rules from CYVR to Medicine Hat Airport (CYXH), AB. A loss of separation occurred while both aircraft were on the initial climb out from Runway 26L. The Cessna Citation accelerated and flew faster than anticipated by air traffic control. At their closest, the aircraft were separated by 1.2 nautical miles (NM) horizontally and 600 feet vertically where the minimum required separation was 3 NM horizontally or 1000 feet vertically.

C-GXNR, un B737-2S2C exploité par Glencore Canada Corporation sous l’indicatif RAG240 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) ) à destination de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) avec 49 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage à bord. Après le démarrage des moteurs au stationnement, une indication de feu du groupe auxiliaire de bord (APU) est apparue.  L’équipage a effectué les items de la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH), toutefois l’indication de feu est demeurée. Une urgence auprès de l’ATC a été déclarée, les moteurs fermés et puisqu’il n’y avait aucune apparence de fumée à l’intérieur ni à l’extérieur, les occupants sont sortis par les escaliers habituels. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’aéronef. L’inspection post événement a déterminé que la fausse indication avait été causée par une boucle de détection d'incendie défectueuse.

C-GCWO, a float-equipped Cessna 185F operated by Gogal Air Services Ltd., was conducting a flight from Snow Lake Water Aerodrome (CKM5), MB, to Lac du Bonnet (North) Water Aerodrome (CJS9), MB. The aircraft landed safely at CJS9 and began taxiing to the dock. After approximately 400 meters into the taxi, the right front float began to dig in under the waves and, shortly after, the left front float followed. The aircraft then slowly nosed over and sank becoming inverted with the floats keeping it afloat. The pilot, wearing his undeployed inflatable personal flotation device, was able to open the door and get out of the aircraft with no injuries.The aircraft was flipped back onto the floats and removed from the water in the following days by a contract maintenance facility. Upon inspection, it was noted that there was no structural damage to the aircraft.

C-FSTY, a privately registered Cessna 172E, equipped with amphibious floats, was conducting a round robin flight from Campbell River Airport (CYBL), BC, via Choelquoit Lake and Anahim Lake Airport (CAJ4), BC. While en route to CAJ4, the engine (Avro Lycoming O-360-A3A) lost power due to fuel starvation and the pilot conducted an emergency landing in a swamp approximately 1 NM south of Nimpo Lake Seaplane Base (CAF8), BC. The pilot activated the emergency locator transmitter (ELT) and shutdown the aircraft. The pilot was called by and spoke to personnel at the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC). They discussed the extent of his injuries and the rescue plan. JRCC requested that the pilot turn off the ELT. The pilot egressed out the left front door and walked to a nearby road where transportation had been arranged. The pilot sustained minor injuries; the aircraft was substantially damaged.The aircraft was recovered and transported to Campbell River for repair.

C-GNVJ, un Piper PA-31-325 exploité par SAB Aviation Inc., effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Rimouski, QC (CYXK) à destination de Port Meunier, QC (CYPN) avec un pilote et 4 passagers à bord. Environ 6 minutes après le décollage, une panne du moteur droit (Avco Lycoming TIO-540-F2BD) est survenue. Le pilote a sécurisé le moteur, déclaré un état d’urgence et est revenu se poser à CYXK. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 25 sans encombre.

C-IKDH, un ultra léger de type évolué Just Aircraft LLC Escapade privé, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Saint-Mathieu-de-Beloeil, QC (CSB3) avec seul le pilote à bord. À l’atterrissage, l’aéronef a effectué un rebond et a atterri sur la roue de nez qui s’est affaissée. Les hélices ont touché le sol, l’aéronef a dévié de sa trajectoire et s’est immobilisé hors-piste. Le pilote n’a pas été blessé et a pu évacuer l’aéronef sans difficulté. L'aéronef a subi des dommages importants.

C-GOIE, un Airbus A321-271NX exploité par Air Transat A.T. sous l'indicatif TSC155 effectuaient un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Bruxelles-National, Belgique (EBBR) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). N20HQ, un Bombardier BD-700-1A10 en exploitation privée par P2 Aviation Management LLC effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Trois-Rivières, QC (CYRQ) à destination de l’aéroport international de Portland, ME (KPWM) aux États-Unis. N20HQ a décollé de CYRQ et a monté jusqu’au niveau de vol 250 où il s’est établi en croisière environ à 29 milles nautiques ESE de CYRQ. TSC155 qui se trouvait dans le même secteur et stable au niveau de vol 260 se dirigeait vers l’ouest. Le TCAS de TSC155 a détecté la montée de N20HQ et a émis un avis de résolution de monter. L’équipage a suivi l’avis de résolution en procédant à une montée.

C-FEXB, a Morningstar Air Express Inc. Cessna C208B, was conducting flight MAL8060 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON. During approach into CYQT, the aircraft missed due to minimum weather conditions. On an attempted second approach, ATC declared an approach ban and the pilot diverted to an alternate, Dryden Regional Airport (CYHD), ON, but missed the approach again due to weather. The pilot then requested a return to CYWG and declared minimum fuel with priority handling as a precaution. The aircraft landed safely in CYWG with the fuel gauge indicating 450 lbs of fuel remaining on board.

C-FNND, a Boeing 777-200 operated by Air Canada, was operating flight AC881 from Zurich Airport (ZRH), Switzerland, to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, with 273 passengers and 11 crew members on board. After landing at CYYZ, while being marshalled to the gate, the aircraft's engine intake came into contact with a stationary bridge, resulting in a dent to the nacelle. Air Canada maintenance conducted an inspection and subsequently repaired the damaged area.

C-FCQD, an Air Canada A320-214 was preparing for flight AC1063 from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, NV, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. The crew experienced an odor event on the ground in KLAS, an engine run was done without isolating the issue. The first officer became unwell due to the odor and in turn the flight was cancelled.After a maintenance inspection, the recirculation fan was found to have popped a circuit breaker, and the APU bleed generated an odor. The fan was replaced.

C-GJXY, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300 was operating flight AC169 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. Shortly after departure from CYYZ, the flight crew received a Brake Overheat indication following the landing gear retraction. They completed the applicable checklist, although the warning continued to appear intermittently. The crew subsequently decided to return to CYYZ and requested aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) services to be on standby. Flight AC169 landed without further incident. An inspection by Air Canada Maintenance determined that the left inboard brake temperature sensor was damaged. The sensor was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFUL, a privately registered Piper PA-14 (Family Cruiser) on straight floats, was conducting a flight, under visual flight rules, from Dease Lake, BC, to a remote lake in northern BC with only the pilot and cargo onboard. During cruise flight, at approximately 5000 feet above sea level, the engine (Lycoming O-320-A2B) started running rough with a coincident power reduction.
