The pilot applied carb heat, which had no effect, and elected to conduct a forced landing in a swamp. On touchdown, during the landing slide, the aircraft floats caught vegetation which spun the aircraft and caused the left wing to contact the ground. The pilot manually activated the emergency locator transmitter and communicated with the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) using a Garmin inReach satellite communication device. There were no reported injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The aircraft was recovered by helicopter. Maintenance found 1 engine cylinder head had cracked. The engine will be removed and sent to a maintenance facility for examination.

C-GTTH, a privately registered Robinson R44 II (Raven) helicopter, was conducting a recreational flight, under visual flight rules, from Tatogga Lake Resort, BC, to Smithers Airport (CYYD), BC, with 1 pilot and 1 passenger onboard. The pilot elected to make an unscheduled stop near Teigen Peak, BC, which is at approximately 5000 feet above sea level (ASL). While on final approach, the helicopter encountered a tailwind and the pilot attempted to overshoot. The low rotor RPM warning light and horn turned on, and the pilot carried out a forced landing. The left skid dug into terrain causing the helicopter to pitch forward and roll onto its left side. The main rotor blades struck the ground and also severed the tail boom from the helicopter. The emergency locator transmitter (ELT) activated, and the signal was relayed to the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC). The occupants egressed the aircraft and used a satellite tracking device and a satellite phone to request assistance. A nearby RCMP helicopter was dispatched to the site and picked up the pilot and the passenger. The pilot and passenger sustained minor injuries. The helicopter was substantially damaged.

C-GYXL, a Perimeter Aviation LP Fairchild SA227-AC, was conducting flight PAG117 from Norway House Airport (CYNE), MB, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. While cruising at 21,000 feet, the flight crew heard a high pitch noise which appeared to come from the cabin door. As the noise got louder and more intense, the first officer noticed that the cabin altitude was rising, the cabin differential was dropping, and the cabin altitude light came on shortly after. The flight crew contacted ATC and requested immediate descent due to a loss in pressurization and descent was granted. The flight crew completed the memory checks and conducted an emergency decent to 9000 feet where the cabin altitude light went out. They continued to CYWG unpressurized with no further issues and landed uneventfully.

N1200K, a Boeing 767-332 aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL245 from Catania/Fontanarossa Intl (LICC), Italy to New York/John F Kennedy Intl (KJFK), NY. While in cruise flight about 500 NM east of Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL, the flight crew was contacted by the flight attendants who reported an odour in the aft galley described as a burning electrical smell. The flight crew referenced the quick reference handbook (QRH) and contacted dispatch and maintenance via SATCOM. The cabin crew reported that the smell had begun to dissipate, however the flight crew followed the QRH and decided to declare an emergency and divert to CYYR. The aircraft landed at CYYR without further incident and was inspected by airport emergency services who reported no anomalies. Maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft and subsequently replaced the number four and number five galley ovens.

C-GRAG, a Westjet B737 Max 8 was operating flight WS2061 from Los Cabos International Airport (MMSD), MX, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining cabin crew.

C-GHOA, an Airbus Helicopters AS 350 B3 operated by Hydro One Networks Inc. was conducting powerline work in Island Falls, ON, at approximately 32 NM NNW of Cochrane Aerodrome (CYCN), ON. While slinging a crossarm onto a two-pole powerline, the pilot experienced an unintentional release of the load from the remote hook. As the crossarm was being lowered through the phase conductors, it became caught on the middle phase. While the pilot was holding the load in position, awaiting the lineman to reach the end of the arm, the load unexpectedly detached from the remote hook and fell to the ground. No injuries were reported.

C-GTMW, a privately-registered De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-3T (Turbo Otter) airplane, equipped with amphibious floats, was conducting a local flight under visual flight rules from Harrison Hot Springs (CAE7), BC with 1 pilot and 6 passengers on board. After starting the engine, the rope that had been securing the aircraft to the dock detached. The airplane then moved forward. The pilot feathered the propeller and shut down the engine and, as the engine and propeller were slowing, the aircraft struck a boat that was parked at the dock. The 1 person on board the boat sustained minor injuries; all occupants on board the aircraft were uninjured. The boat and aircraft sustained minor damage.

C-GVKC, a Pilatus 12/45 aircraft operated by North Star Air Ltd. was conducting an IFR flight from the Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, to Angling Lake Airport (CKB6), ON, as flight BF708, and C-GLQV, a De Havilland DHC-8-402 operated by Porter Airlines Inc. was conducting an IFR flight from the Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON to Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON as flight PTR 2636. BF708 was given clearance to take off with instructions to contact the terminal frequency.  Meanwhile, the Winnipeg Area Control Centre had requested Thunder Bay Tower to stop the takeoff of PTR2636 next in sequence until BF708 was identified on radar.  At the time of the request, PTR2636 had already taken off; creating a loss of separation less than 1 mile. Both aircraft continued flight without further incident.

C-GITP, an Air Canada Rouge A319-112 was operating flight ROU1661 from Tampa International Airport (KTPA), FL, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the cruise phase of flight, prior to top of descent, the flight crew received a Master Caution followed by ECAM messages: HYD G LO LVL and HYD G LO PRESS. ECAM and quick reference handbook procedures were actioned, and a PAN PAN was declared. The flight crew coordinated with ATC for an approach to Runway 33R due to wind conditions and system status. Landing gear was manually extended at 3000 feet. The aircraft landed and came to a stop on the runway. Aircraft rescue and firefighting conducted an external inspection with no abnormalities reported. Engines were shut down, and the aircraft was towed to the gate.

C-GEZD, un Airbus A321-211 exploité par Air Transat A.T. sous l'indicatif TSC398 effectuaient un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de l’aéroport international de Punta Cana, en République dominicaine (MPDC).  N96LA, un Dassault Falcon 900EX en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de l’aéroport Centennial aux États-Unis (KAPA). TSC398 a reçu en premier l’autorisation de décoller de la piste 24R. N96LA a reçu l’autorisation de décoller de la piste 24L après le décollage de TSC398. Après ce dernier décollage, l’espacement horizontal entre les 2 aéronefs a été réduit à 2.6 NM alors qu’il devait être d’au moins 3 NM. Le contrôleur aérien a instruit N96LA de rester à 2000 pieds jusqu’à ce que l’espacement vertical soit de 1000 pieds entre les 2 aéronefs. Une fois l’espacement minimal respecté, les 2 aéronefs ont été dirigés sur leurs routes respectives.

C-GCBL, an AC Airways Limited Cessna 210 airplane, was conducting a local forestry flight, under visual flight rules, from Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. During the landing roll, the nose gear fork failed, the nose wheel broke off, and the nose gear collapsed. The nose of the aircraft tipped forward and the propeller contacted the runway. The aircraft stopped and remained on the runway. All occupants exited the aircraft and there were no injuries reported. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The aircraft was moved to a maintenance facility for repair.

F-HTYB, un Airbus 350-941 exploité par Air France sous l'indicatif AFR348 et F-GZNO, un Boeing B777-228ER aussi exploité par Air France sous l’indicatif AFR344, effectuaient un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle, FR (LFPG) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). AFR348 était en rapprochement pour atterrir sur la piste 24L suivi de AFR344. AFR344 qui avait réduit sa vitesse d’approche au minimum, a rattrapé AFR348 plus lent lors de l’approche finale. Ceci a réduit l’espacement entre les 2 aéronefs sous le minimum requis de 4 NM. Le contrôleur aérien a instruit AFR344 d’effectuer une remontée à 3000 pieds car il se rapprochait trop de AFR348. A ce moment, l’espacement était de 3.4 NM.

C-FRQN, un Embraer 170-200 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA609, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl - Boston, MA aux États-Unis (KBOS) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). C-GLQD, un Dehavilland DHC-8-400 exploité par Porter Airlines Inc. sous l’indicatif PTR2473, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Billy Bishop Toronto City, ON (CYTZ) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). PTR2473 était en rapprochement pour atterrir sur la piste 24L suivi de JZA609. Alors que PTR2473 était à environ 10 NM E de CYUL, l’espacement entre les 2 aéronefs a été réduit à 2,8 NM alors que l’espacement horizontal minimal requis est de 3 NM. Le contrôleur aérien a instruit JZA609 de tourner à droite sur un cap de 010 pour augmenter l’espacement entre les 2 avions. La perte d’espacement a duré 15 secondes.

On 21 July 2025, a privately owned Cessna 185E aircraft (registration: C-FEPK, serial number 185-1430) departed on a visual flight rules flight from Rocky Mountain House (CYRM), AB to McBride/Charlie Lake Field (CAV4), BC. The pilot was the sole occupant. During the flight to CAV4, deteriorating weather due to clouds and ground fog were encountered. The pilot elected to deviate toward Edson Airport (CYET), AB and encountered further deteriorating weather and visibility, eventually deciding to visually follow a service road. The pilot lost visual reference and was unable to avoid contact with the rising terrain. The pilot was able to exit the wreckage and notify police via cell phone. The pilot received minor injuries. There was no post-impact fire, and the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FJQH, un Airbus A321-211 exploité par Air Canada Rouge LP sous l’indicatif ROU1954 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Toronto/Lester B.Pearson, ON (CYYZ) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Durant la phase de descente à environ 20 mille marins à l’ouest-sud-ouest de CYQB, l’équipage a reçu un avis de résolution « CLIMB » du TCAS alors que l’aéronef était en descente à environ 6500 pieds. L’équipage a suivi l'instruction RA, a effectué une montée et identifié visuellement un avion Cessna 152. Il a ensuite avisé l’ATC et a poursuivi sa route vers l’aéroport où il a atterri sans encombre.

C-GNJZ, un Bombardier CL-600-2D24 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JAZ631 effectuaient un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de LaGuardia aux États-Unis (KLGA) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL).  N2LG, un Piper PA-46-701TP exploité par Academy Aero LLC effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport métropolitain de Montréal, QC (CYHU) à destination de Burlington International Airport (KBTV), VT aux États-Unis. Au décollage de la piste 24R à CYHU, l’équipage de N2LG a relu l’instruction de monter pour et maintenir 3000 pieds. Rendu à 3000 pieds, N2LG a poursuivi sa montée. En dépassant l’altitude instruite, l’espacement minimal requis de 1000 pieds et 3 milles n’a pas été maintenu avec JZA631 qui était rapprochement à 4000 pieds pour CYUL. L’espacement a été réduit à un minimum de 600 pieds et 0,5 mille.

C-FJAC un DeHavilland DHC-2 MK.I (Beaver) sur flotteurs exploité par Air Tunilik inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue de jour depuis le lac du Poisson Blanc (N51 13.8, W077 29.3), QC, à destination du lac Evans, QC, avec le pilote et 4 passagers à bord. Après le décollage, suite à la réduction de puissance, le moteur (Pratt & Whitney-USA R985-AN-14B) a perdu de la puissance et le pilote a tenté de se poser dans la portion du lac restant. La surface de l’eau était miroitante, car il n’y avait aucun vent et alors que le pilote tentait de se poser, l’aile droite a décroché et l’avion a heurté la surface de l’eau en piqué vers la droite. Les occupants ont tous réussi à sortir et ont nagé jusqu’à la rive est du lac. Un passager a subi des blessures mineures. L’aéronef a subi des dommages substantiels. La radiobalise de repérage d’urgence s’est déclenchée.

C-FTXD, a privately registered Denney Kitfox IV 1200, was conducting touch and go landings at the Guelph Aerodrome (CNC4), ON, when it experienced a hard landing. Upon landing on the grass strip, the impact caused the right and left main gear axles to collapse which resulted in the wheel struts digging into the ground, the aircraft nosing over, cartwheeling and coming to rest on its back. The pilot was uninjured and egressed on his own. The aircraft sustained substantial damage and was subsequently turned over and removed from the runway area.

C-FTUZ, un Boeing 737-800 exploité par Air Inuit Ltée sous l’indicatif AIE731 allait effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP). Lors du roulage sur la piste 24L, l’équipage a observé l’illumination des lumières d’avertissement « ALT » pour les 2 moteurs lorsque la vitesse était à environ 85 noeuds. L’équipage a poursuivi le roulage en vue du décollage étant donné que l’indication ne présentait pas une menace immédiate pour le vol. Lorsque la vitesse de roulage a atteint 120 nœuds, un message « AIRSPEED DISAGREE » est apparu. Après une vérification rapide, le commandant de bord a instruit le copilote qui était aux commandes d’interrompre le décollage. Peu de temps après, l’équipage a senti une odeur de pneu en surchauffe. Le contrôleur de la tour a informé par radio l’équipage que de la fumée provenait du train d’atterrissage principal. Le PIC a demandé la présence des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) et a arrêté l’aéronef dans la baie d’attente à la fin de la piste 24L. Une fois l’événement sécurisé par les SLIA, le service de maintenance de la compagnie a inspecté le train d’atterrissage et a remplacé 2 pneus avant de remorquer l’aéronef au hangar.

C-FCDB, an Ultravia Pelican Sport 600 Amateur Built aircraft on amphibious floats, was on a local flight with two souls on board. The aircraft had departed from Scugog Charles Landing Water Aerodrome and was returning to land after completing the short flight. The landing was performed with glassy water conditions and the pilot decided to stay near the shoreline and use the landscape as a reference for the height above the water. The aircraft skipped on the water at least twice prior to the pilot reducing power. The landing was aborted and the pilot applied full power to go-around. The aircraft pitched nose up and veered to the left where it impacted two docks with the left float. One individual was on the second dock when they were struck by the aircraft and fatally injured. The aircraft then struck a moored pontoon boat and came to rest in an inverted position on the pontoon boat. The aircraft was substantially damaged during the impact sequence. Both occupants exited the aircraft with some difficulty. One of the occupants returned to the aircraft to switch off electrical power and turn off the fuel valve. The Emergency Locator Transmitter did not activate during the impacts.

C-FITU, an Air Canada B777-333 was operating flight AC861 from Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining cabin crew.

C-FVLX, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC904 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Leonardo da Vinci International Airport (LIRF), Italy. The crew was provided by ATC a heading directly into a significant thunderstorm cell, the crew requested a turn to deviate and due to ATC language misunderstanding, declared a PAN PAN in order to avoid the cell for safety of flight. Next controller confirmed the crew declared the PAN PAN and they explained why and there was no issue. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GXWA, a float-equipped Cessna A185F, was on a local flight from Coe Hill, ON, to Baptiste Lake, ON, with the pilot and two passengers. Flying over Baptiste Lake the engine began to lose power (TELEDYNE CONTINENTAL, IO-520-D) and the aircraft began to lose altitude. The pilot selected an area on the lake for the landing. The aircraft landed hard on the water resulting in substantial damage to floats and wings. The three occupants exited the aircraft and swam to shore. The emergency locator transmitter activated, and the pilot contacted Search and Rescue stating that they would not be required. The pilot determined that although the fuel selector was in the "BOTH" position, the right tank was empty, and the left tank had substantial fuel. The aircraft had departed Coe Hill with a total of two hours of fuel in the tanks.

C-GCHZ, a Custom Helicopters Bell 206L, was conducting a sling load flight from a staging area 9 nautical miles (NM) northwest of Whale Cove Airport (CYXN), NU, to BG Gold camp, 22 NM west-northwest of the staging area. The aircraft had a 100-foot longline attached, and a 650-pound toolbox attached with 2 straps. At 1800 CST approximately 10 NM into the trip, the toolbox slipped out of the straps and fell approximately 1000 feet to the ground. There were no personnel injuries or damage to the aircraft.

C-FJFL, an Atleo River Air Service Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-2 MK I (Beaver) floatplane, was conducting a flight, under visual flight rules, from Hot Springs Cove, BC, to Tofino Harbour Water Aerodrome (CAB4), BC. While landing westbound at CAB4, just prior to the intended touchdown, the left float contacted a water peak where two boat wakes had collided. The aircraft bounced and the nose yawed slightly to the left. The right float then touched down and the subsequent side load caused the right wing to dip and contact the water. When the wing tip contacted the water, it acted as a pivot point around which the floatplane spun 180 degrees. The floatplane came to an abrupt stop and remained upright. The pilot was able to then taxi to the dock. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the right wing and flap.

C-GLRR, an Ootsa Air Limited Piper PA-31-325 (Navajo) aircraft, was conducting a cargo flight, under visual flight rules, from Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC, to Tsay Keh Aerodrome (CBN9), BC, with only the pilot on board. After reaching a cruising altitude of 12 500 feet above sea level, the pilot set the cruise power setting. When the mixture was leaned, the pilot noticed a vibration and low exhaust gas temperature (EGT) in cylinder 2 on the left engine (Avco Lycoming TIO-540-F2BD). The pilot completed the engine roughness emergency checklist. The vibration did not stop, and the pilot decided to return to CYXS. Shortly thereafter, the manifold pressure on the left engine reduced suddenly, the RPM dropped, and the EGT for all of the cylinders dropped. The pilot followed the procedure for an engine failure and secured the left engine. No oil or fire was observed. The pilot declared an emergency, returned to CYXS, and landed without incident. The aircraft was taxied to the company hangar.Maintenance personnel checked the compression and injectors on the engine and conducted ground runs but could not replicate the issue. The aircraft fuel tanks were checked, and some water was found. The fuel tanks were then drained. The aircraft completed a satisfactory test flight and was returned to service.

C-GWUE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) airplane, was conducting flight WEN3576, under instrument flight rules, from Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During the takeoff roll, the flight crew observed #1 and #2 bleed hot caution lights and a deice pressure caution light. The flight crew executed a low speed rejected take off and declared a MAYDAY. The flight crew taxied off the runway and actioned the quick reference handbook, which cleared the faults. The aircraft returned to the gate where the passengers were offloaded.Maintenance personnel reset the system in accordance with the supplemental procedure ground reset guide. The caution light did not return, and the system was found serviceable. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FTGS, a privately registered Cessna 182D aircraft, was conducting a VFR flight from Grand Prairie Airport (CYQU), AB to Jasper Airport (CYJA), AB with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. Approximately one hour into the flight, while in cruise, the engine (Teledyne Continental O-470-L, serial number 814280L4) began to run rough and then lost power. The pilot declared a MAYDAY, activated the ELT, and conducted a forced landing. The aircraft contacted trees and came to an abrupt stop on a service road. None of the occupants sustained injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GVNO, un Cessna 172M sur flotteurs en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’hydrobase de St-Mathias, QC (CSV9) à destination de la baie des Quenouilles du lac Taureau, QC avec seul le pilote à bord. Alors que l’avion approchait la surface de l’eau, il a amorcé un virage à gauche à basse altitude. Lorsqu’il a quitté l’effet de sol en virage avec un vent de dos, il a subi un décrochage aérodynamique et a percuté la surface de l’eau. L’aile gauche s’est retrouvée dans l’eau et le moteur était affaissé. L’avion est resté à l’endroit sur les flotteurs, mais a subi des dommages importants. Le pilote n’a subi aucune blessure.

C-FASA, a privately-registered De Havilland DHC-2 Mk. III (Turbo Beaver) airplane, equipped with amphibious floats, was conducting a flight under visual flight rules from Qualicum Beach Airport (CAT4), BC, to False Bay Water Aerodrome (CAT7), BC, with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. The aircraft landed on the water at CAT7 with the gear down. Immediately after touchdown, the float wheels dug into the water, the aircraft pitched forward, and the aircraft flipped upside down. The aircraft settled nose low in the water at an approximately 30-degree angle. When the aircraft came to a full stop, the pilot released his seatbelt and went back through the cabin to assist the passenger. The pilot removed 2 personal flotation devices (PFD) from under the middle row seats. The pilot unfastened the passenger's seatbelt and assisted him out the left cabin door. The pilot assisted the passenger in donning a PFD and inflated it. The passenger called 911 from his cellphone. Within 1 minute, a boat arrived at the aircraft and the pilot and passenger boarded the boat. Ropes from the boat were used to tie the aircraft and was towed to the dock. The Canadian Coast Guard, Canadian Forces Search and Rescue, and local emergency medical services attended the scene. The emergency locator transmitter transmitted a signal. The pilot sustained minor injuries; the passenger was uninjured. The aircraft was substantially damaged.The aircraft was recovered from the water the following day and barged to a hangar for repair.

C-GBEO, un motoplaneur Brasov IS282M en exploitation privée effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) avec seul 1 pilote à bord. Lorsque l’aéronef était établi dans une ascendance dans la région des monts Valin, le pilote a arrêté le moteur et a mis l’hélice en drapeau. Un effort inhabituel sur le levier a été ressenti, donc le pilote a tenté de remettre l’hélice (Hoffman propeller HO-V62R/L160T) en marche, sans succès. Il s’est ensuite dirigé vers CYRC, mais sans moteur ne pouvait s’y rendre en vol plané. Il a déclaré un état d’urgence et s’est posé dans un marais à environ 8 miles marins au nord-est de CYRC. Il n’a subi aucune blessure, toutefois l’aéronef a subi des dommages importants.

C-FUJE, an Embraer 170-200 SU operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight JZA8732, was conducting a flight from Cleveland Hopkins International Airport (KCLE), Ohio, to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During descent, the flight crew reported a flap failure to company dispatch. The flap position indicated 0, while the slats remained at position 3.The crew declared a PAN PAN and advised that Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) be requested to inspect the brakes following landing due to a higher Vref. The aircraft landed uneventfully on Runway 05 and came to a stop on the runway. After the brakes were inspected by ARFF, the aircraft continued to the gate.

C-FRHQ un Dash-8-311 exploité par Hydro-Québec sous l’indicatif HYD310 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC) à destination d’Havre-St-Pierre, QC (CYGV) avec 8 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage à bord. À environ 5000 pieds en montée, une indication de fumée est apparue dans le poste. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a amorcé un retour à CYBC. Une vérification de la cabine et de la soute à bagages n’a révélé aucune fumée à bord. L’aéronef s’est posé sur la piste 28 sans encombre.

C-GDJZ, un CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7901, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Gander international, NL (CYQX) à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 31 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Alors que l’aéronef était à environ 15000 pieds en descente à CYUL, une indication de panne des volets (FLAPS FAIL) est survenue. L’équipage déclaré un état d’urgence et les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 24R.

C-GOIM, un Airbus 321-200 exploité par Air Transat sous l'indicatif TSC680, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL), à destination de Lisbon International/Humberto Delgado (Portela de Sacavem), Portugal (LPPT) avec 197 passagers et 7 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors que l'aéronef était en montée, l’équipage a reçu une indication de fumée dans les toilettes. L'équipage a arrêté la montée et a déclaré une urgence au contrôleur aérien.  L’indication s’est éteinte et toutes les toilettes ont été inspectées. Aucune trace de fumée ou de feu n’a été trouvée. L’urgence a été annulée et l’aéronef a poursuivi son vol jusqu’à destination sans encombre.

C-GOKF, an Air Transat Airbus A321, was operating from Toronto/Lester B Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, when a cabin crew member became ill shortly after take-off. The cabin crew member was removed from their assigned duties. Safety-related duties were reassigned accordingly amongst remaining crew for the remainder of the flight. The aircraft continued and landed at CYUL without further incident.

C-GAGE, a private Cessna 441 Conquest II, was conducting a local training flight and had completed multiple training sequences and landings. After landing on Runway 36 at Muskoka Airport (CYQA), ON, the copilot applied reverse thrust, and the aircraft began to lose directional control and veer to the left. Attempts to correct the lateral drift with pedal input was unsuccessful and resulted in a runway excursion. The aircraft made a 180-degree right hand turn as it came to rest in the grass/sand. There was damage to the right main landing gear and right propeller. The airport staff closed Runway 18/36 and attended to the aircraft. The pilot and others on board indicated they did not require medical attention. The airport was towed to the main apron. Airport staff performed a runway inspection for foreign object debris (FOD) related to the event and reopened Runway 18/36.

C-GYPC, a private Piper PA-11 floatplane, suffered a hard landing on East Lake, ON, approximately 5 NM southwest of Picton Airport (CNT7), ON. During the approach, it was reported that the aircraft lost lift at approximately 10 feet above the surface, resulting in a hard landing. Following touchdown, the aircraft listed to the right as the right wing dropped and made contact with the water. The aircraft came to rest with the right wing partially submerged and resting on the lake bottom. The pilot and passenger were uninjured. EMS and fire services responded to the scene.

C-GESH, a De Havilland DHC-8-102 operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was taxiing on the maneuvering areas of Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB to conduct maintenance grounds runs at the runup bay of Runway 13. At approximately 23:30 CDT, the operator's maintenance personnel contacted the ground controller to request taxi from Apron 4 to the bay of Runway 13. They were given instruction to taxi Taxiway Charlie, Runway 31 and hold short of Runway 18; however, they were seen crossing the hold short line of Runway 18. The tower controller noticed the incursion and instructed C-FFNF, a Boeing 737-406 operated by Bradley Air Services Limited (dba Canadian North) as flight AKT153, to pull up and go around as they were on short final for Runway 18. The crew of AKT153 executed the go around at approximately 100ft above ground level (AGL). C-GESH was then instructed to continue taxi to runup bay of Runway 13. AKT153 remained VFR in the circuit for Runway 18 and landed without further incident 10 minutes later.The operator's maintenance personnel was given verbal coaching on the event and will be receiving additional training before they are allowed to reposition aircraft onto maneuvering areas.

C-GHVJ, un Cessna 182R exploité par Exact Air inc. effectuait une patrouille de feu selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) avec seul le pilote à bord. Après environ 5 minutes de vol, une odeur inconnue est apparue dans la cabine, et quelques minutes plus tard, de la fumée a commencé à sortir autour du transpondeur. Le circuit électrique a immédiatement été fermé et un retour à CYMT a été amorcé. Ayant isolé le transpondeur, l’électricité a été rétablie pour sortir les roues et les volets, et par la même occasion déclarer un état d’urgence. L’aéronef s’est posé sur la piste 04 sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GASI, a Beech A100 operated by Thunder Airlines as flight THU102, departed Timmins Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON. Shortly after departure, the flight crew reported smoke in the cockpit. During the climb, a smell of burning plastic was detected near the co-pilot’s side panel. An emergency was declared, and a return to CYTS was initiated. The aircraft had climbed to 8,600 feet ASL before the crew elected to return.During the return, the crew observed that the landing gear circuit breaker had tripped, and the landing gear would not extend normally. A manual gear extension was completed, and the aircraft landed uneventfully on Runway 21 at CYTS with emergency services on standby.

C-GKXH, an Embraer E190-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines (Canada) Ltd. was conducting an IFR flight from Hamilton/John C. Munro International Airport ON (CYHM) to the Vancouver International Airport, BC (CYVR) while enroute approximately 150 nm East of Regina International Airport SK.(CYQR), the crew observed a burning odour in the cabin. A PAN PAN was declared with a diversion to CYQR; however, the smell dissipated. The diversion was then updated to proceed to Calgary International Airport, AB. (CYYC). Approximately 10 minutes later, the odour was apparent again and the diversion was changed back to CYQR. After landing at CYQR, and the passengers and crew disembarked. The aircraft was inspected by ARFF and no evidence of fire was found, but an elevated heat signature was found around the floor in a specific seat bank.Extensive post flight maintenance inspections did not reveal a cause for the odour. Aircraft was to be repositioned to a maintenance base for further investigation.

C-GTHU, a Summit Helicopters Limited Bell 407 helicopter, was conducting slinging operations in the vicinity of the former Bronson Creek Airstrip, BC, (56°40'47"N, 131°05'15"W) with only the pilot on board. While transporting drilling rods to a drill site, the load began to move excessively. To control the load, the pilot pulled back hard on the cyclic to correct the unwanted motion. The load was delivered after this flight maneuver and the pilot continued with normal operations. After the pilot shutdown the helicopter for a scheduled break, they, observed damage to the top of the left finlet which had been contacted by the main rotor blades. There were no injuries.Company maintenance performed inspections, completed non-destructive testing (NDT) on the main rotor blades, and replaced the damaged finlet. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWRC, an Airbus Helicopters BK117-D3 (H145), was being operated by Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service (STARS) on a training flight at the Wetaskiwin Regional Airport (CEX3), AB. During a simulated instrument approach at CEX3, the flight crew observed a No.1 generator overheat warning light. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist and shutdown the No. 1 engine (Safran Arriel 2E). The flight crew declared a MAYDAY with ATC and diverted to the Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, where an uneventful single-engine approach and touch down was completed.Company maintenance determined that the No. 1 generator overheat switch was faulty.

C-GWPS, a De Havilland DHC-8-102 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting an IFR flight from Thompson Regional Airport (CYTH), MB, to Tadoule Lake Airport (CYBQ), MB. During cruise, two passengers became unruly, resulting in intervention by the cabin crew. The captain entered the cabin to inform passengers of the return to CYTH. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and received priority handling by ATS. The aircraft returned to CYTH and landed.

C-FVKO, a Cessna 172M operated by Spectrum Airways, was en route from Windsor International Airport (CYQG), ON to Parry Sound Area Municipal Airport (CNK4) with two souls on board. While in cruise at 5,500 feet ASL, the engine (Lycoming O-320-E2D) began to shake violently. The pilot applied carburetor heat, set the mixture to full rich, and performed a magneto check; however, no change in engine performance was observed.A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft diverted to Centralia/James T. Field Memorial Aerodrome (CYCE), where it landed uneventfully.

N732YX, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 LR operated by Republic Airlines as flight RPA3499, was departing from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Chicago O’Hare International Airport (KORD), IL. RPA3499 was cleared for takeoff on Runway 23 behind an Airbus A350-900, registration ET-AZN, operated by Etihad Airways and departing for Bole Addis Ababa International Airport (HAAB), Ethiopia.The required wake turbulence separation was reduced to 3.8 NM, below the minimum required 5.0 NM for this aircraft pairing.

C-GDUZ, an Air Canada B767-300 was operating flight AC7252 from Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL, to Jorge Chávez International Airport (SPJC), Peru. During cruise the crew received a Leading-Edge Slat Asymmetry message and then actioned the quick reference handbook. The warning remained on throughout the flight. During the approach, the crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC. The aircraft landed without incident.

C-GJWN, an Airbus A321 operated by Air Canada as flight AC130, was en route from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While in cruise, the flight crew received an ECAM Nose Wheel Steering Fault indication. The crew completed the applicable quick reference handbook checklist, declared a PAN PAN, and requested a tow from the runway upon landing.The aircraft landed uneventfully at CYYZ with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by and was towed to the gate. Maintenance replaced the nose wheel servo control, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFVZ a De Havilland DHC-3 aircraft operated by Kississing Lake Lodge Ltd. (dba Wings Over Kississing), was conducting a VFR flight from Wollaston Lake Airport (CZWL), SK, to La Ronge Water Aerodrome (CJZ9), SK. Upon landing at CJZ9, while taxiing into the docking area, the pilot misjudged the position of a parked DHC-2 aircraft (C-FIFJ) and collided with it. The propeller of C-FFVZ, which was feathered but still turning, made contact with the trailing edge of the parked aircraft's right aileron. The parked aircraft (C-FIFJ) sustained damage to its right aileron. C-FFVZ sustained minor damage to its propeller. There were no injuries reported.

C-FHEP, a DeHavilland DHC-2 float equipped aircraft operated by Bamaji Air Inc. was conducting a VFR flight from Slate Falls, ON, to Sioux Lookout/Pelican Lake Water Aerodrome (CKA6), ON, with the pilot and one passenger. While flying enroute at a low level, at approximately 22 nm North of CKA6, the aircraft contacted the water surface of Lac Seul, in the vicinity of Chamberlain Narrows, and nosed over and broke apart. The pilot and passenger, both having minor injuries, exited the aircraft and inflated their personal flotation devices. They were picked up by another Bamaji Air aircraft that was also in the area and were transported to CKA6 for medical aid. C-FHEP has sunk.

C-GSHF, a Bell Helicopter Textron Canada Ltd. 206L-3, operated by Great Slave Helicopters 2018 Ltd., was conducting external load operations in support of tree planting 5.5 NM E of Rae/Edzo Aerodrome (CRE2), Northwest Territories. The helicopter collided with terrain and the pilot, who was the sole occupant, was fatally injured. There was no post impact fire.

C-FGOV, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-7 operated by Air Tindi was conducting flight TIN707 from Wekweeti (CYWE), NT, to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT. TIN707 was on final approach for Runway 28. C-FEXZ, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-300, operated by Voyageur Airways, requested taxi instructions to conduct a maintenance run on the button of Runway 28. C-FEXZ was instructed to taxi and hold short of Runway 28. The crew of C-FEXZ stopped the aircraft beyond the hold short line for Runway 28, consequently entering the runway protected area. TIN707 conducted a missed approach/go-around. C-FGOV subsequently completed an uneventful landing.

C-FATA, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-7-100, operated by Air Tindi Ltd., was conducting flight TIN708 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Bathurst Inlet, NU. Shortly after departure and approximately 59 NM south of CYZF, the flight crew observed torque fluctuations in the #1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-50). The flight crew actioned the applicable checklist and standard operating procedure, reduced power on the engine and elected to return to CYZF. A PAN PAN was declared with ATC. An uneventful approach and landing were completed in CYZF.

C-GESH, a De Havilland DHC-8-102 Aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LLC was conducting an IFR flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to the Pikangikum Airport (CYPM), ON. While descending toward CYPM, the TCAS system displayed a resolution advisory (RA) due to a target that was in conflict with their planned route. The unknown traffic was spotted in VFR conditions, and the autopilot was disengaged by the flight crew to slow the descent rate. The TCAS RA ended after two seconds. The flight continued to CYPM without further incident.

C-GRXD, a Pilatus PC-12/47 aircraft operated by Ornge Global Air Inc., was conducting an IFR flight from Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON, to Pikangikum Airport (CYPM), ON. During the initial climb at an altitude of FL220, the First Officer (FO) began to feel ill. The captain levelled off at FL220 and engaged the onboard paramedics to assess the FO. The FO was moved to the cabin so the medics could monitor and manage their symptoms. The captain returned to CYQT and landed normally. The FO was taken to hospital for treatment.

C-FJBO, a Jazz Embraer 175 was operating flight JZA879 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. On the taxi out, the cabin crew noticed smoke coming from the oven. They turned off the oven and pulled the circuit breakers. They notified the flight crew, and the smoke started dissipating. It was decided to go back to the gate. No emergency was declared. They told the ramp control that there was smoke earlier but was not an issue anymore. No emergency vehicles were involved. Passengers were deplaned upon arrival at the gate. No adverse passenger reaction was noted. Maintenance found a problem with the seal of the oven, and it was put under MEL. The flight was cancelled.

C-GBIM, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1652 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL. During approach, while on final for the ILS Runway 26L, ROU1652 was advised of helicopter traffic at the 2 o’clock position, expected to cross behind. The helicopter reported visual contact; however, the flight crew did not have the traffic in sight. At approximately 900 feet AGL, a TCAS TA was received, followed by a TCAS RA: LEVEL OFF. The flight crew followed the RA and initiated a go-around. ATC was advised, and vectors were provided for a subsequent RNAV approach to Runway 09, which was completed without further incident.

C-FNWD, a WestJet Boeing 737-8 (Max 8) departed Tampa International Airport (KTPA), FL, as flight WJA1285, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Shortly after arriving at the gate at CYVR, the flight crew was alerted by the ground crew to the presence of flames coming from the number one engine (CFM International LEAP 1B27). The flight crew was unable to visually verify the engine fire due to the passenger boarding bridge blocking their view. The flight crew checked the cockpit for indications of an engine fire. The cabin crew, having been made aware of the fire, initiated evacuation procedures to get the passengers off the plane after receiving confirmation from the flight crew. The flight crew gave the order to evacuate through the aircraft’s public address system and conducted the Engine Fire on Ground checklist and the Evacuation checklist. As part of the first checklist, the aircraft’s left engine halon fire suppression system was activated. Sixty-five passengers egressed the aircraft using the passenger boarding bridge while the remaining fifty-six passengers egressed the aircraft using the rear emergency slides located at the rear aircraft doors. Aircraft rescue and firefighting crews were dispatched to the scene and inspected the aircraft; however, the tail pipe flame had extinguished prior to their arrival. There were no reported injuries. There was no damage to the aircraft.Maintenance found that the center vent tube extension (CVTE) had a significant amount of oil coking which caused the oil to pool in the exhaust nozzle. The pooled oil ignited after the engines were shut down due to the heat in the exhaust cone and this created the tail pipe fire. An inspection for engine exposure to fire and extinguishing agents was carried out successfully. The CVTE, exhaust tube support, and injection nozzle were all removed and cleaned. The CVTE extension was replaced. The rear aircraft emergency slides were replaced as was the left engine halon fire bottle. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GRHH, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B2 operated by Heli Source Ltd. was conducting a flight from Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB, with a pilot and two passengers on board. C-FXCL, a Cessna 208B Caravan operated by McMurray Aviation was conducting a flight from CYMM to Fort Chipewyan Airport (CYPY), AB, with a pilot on board. As the helicopter was operating in the Oil Sands North airspace, the pilot was communicating on the North Oil Sands ATF of 123.50 MHz broadcasting his position and intentions. Approximately 8 NM northwest of the Fort MacKay/Firebag Airport (CYFI), AB, a risk of collision event occurred between C-GRHH and C-FXCL. The aircraft were flying at approximately the same altitude, the pilot of C-FXCL never made visual contact with C-GRHH. The pilot of C-GRHH visually acquired C-FXCL at a distance of approximately 1/4 sm. The pilot of C-FXCL was monitoring both 123.50 MHz and 126.70 MHz and heard radio calls to "Caravan traffic" but did not understand that the calls were directed to him as no registration was included with the radio call. The pilot of C-GRHH eventually made radio contact with the pilot of C-FXCL on the VFR enroute frequency of 126.7 MHz and informed him of the near miss / risk of collision. The pilot of C-FXCL had previously turned off the traffic collision alerting system due to nuisance ground traffic alerts and had not turned the system back on once airborne.

C-FXDM, an Aerospatiale AS 350 FX2 operated by Airborne Energy Solutions Inc., was conducting long line firefighting operations utilizing a bucket out of a remote location approximately 48 NM south-southeast of High Level Airport (CYOJ), AB. After returning to the camp for the day, the pilot placed the water bucket on the ground behind the landing pad and was positioning the helicopter to the landing pad. During the reposition, the rotor downwash inflated the bucket, and the bucket made contact with the tail rotor. The helicopter gained approximately 15 feet of altitude and completed one revolution before contacting the ground and rolling onto its right side. Company maintenance personnel immediately responded, shut down the helicopter and extricated the pilot from the cockpit through the roof window. There were no injuries, but the helicopter was significantly damaged.

G-VSPY, a Boeing 787-900 operated by Virgin Atlantic Airways Ltd. was conducting flight (VIR156) from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), U.S., to London Heathrow International Airport (EGLL), UK. While in cruise the flight crew received left and right PACK EICAS message and lost pressurization. An emergency descent was conducted, and a MAYDAY was declared. When the aircraft was passing through FL250, the left pack returned online, along with the pressurization. The flight crew completed the required checklists and requested to climb to FL350 and continued to EGLL without further incident. Maintenance found the General Process Module (GPM) had failed and the unit was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPWE, a De Havilland Canada DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, departed the Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON, on an IFR flight to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. After takeoff and passing through 1000 feet AGL, the flap drive caution light illuminated. The flight crew observed the flaps were stuck between the 10- and 15-degree position. They advised ATC and proceeded to complete the appropriate checklist in the quick reference handbook (QRH). After completing the checklist and consulting the company operations department, the flight crew decided to return to CYQT. After setting up the aircraft for the approach, the captain declared an emergency. The aircraft landed in CYQT uneventfully, with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by.The operator's maintenance department inspected the aircrafts flap and hydraulic systems and found no faults. Operational checks were carried out and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKQH, a Porter Airlines Q-400 was operating flight PTR2406 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, to Ottawa International Airport (CYOW), ON. During climb, after selecting flap '0', the caution light illuminated, and the flap indicator was stuck at 4 degrees. The quick reference handbook was actioned, and a PAN PAN was declared. The crew elected to return to KEWR where the aircraft landed safely and stopped close to taxiway B4 for an inspection. The aircraft then taxied to the gate.

C-GORI, an Exploits Valley Air Services Beech 1900D aircraft was conducting a medevac flight EV101, from Deer Lake Airport (CYDF) to St. John's Airport (CYYT), NL. During climb, at approximately 1500 feet AGL, the crew received a Right Bleed Air Fail master warning. The system was secured per company procedures, and System Operations Control (SOC) was notified. All other systems were normal.The flight continued to FL210. After 4 to 5 minutes at cruise, the cabin altitude indicated approximately 16 000 feet, though no warning was triggered. The crew coordinated a descent with ATC, initially to 13 000 and then 10 000 feet, and descended at approximately 3000 feet per minute. The flight continued to destination without further incident.The flight crew did not report any symptoms of hypoxia. Members of the medical crew reported feeling unwell and used medical oxygen prior to descentPost occurrence maintenance action: Following the occurrence, maintenance personnel found a separated EVA tubing at the right-hand inboard leading edge, which was resecured. A faulty PCB A141 was also identified and replaced. Functional tests of the pressurization and cabin altitude warning systems were completed, confirming both were serviceable. Service Difficulty Reports submitted to Transport Canada.

C-FEAI, un DeHavilland DHC-8-314 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE807 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de la Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Alors que l'aéronef était en croisière à environ 170 NM au sud-sud-est de CYGL, l'équipage a reçu une indication de perte de fluide hydraulique du système #1. L'équipage a déclaré un état d'urgence (Pan Pan) et a atterri à CYUL sans encombre à 0126Z. L'appareil s'est immobilisé sur la piste et a été remorqué au hangar.

C-FGCN, a Canadian North Boeing 737-300 was operating as flight AKT245 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. At approximately 250 NM north of CYEG at FL370, the flight crew received a master caution warning for the No. 1 engine cowl anti-ice. The crew actioned the quick reference handbook, however; the warning light remained illuminated. The crew requested and was cleared to descend to FL250. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN urgency and continued to CYEG. The aircraft landed without further incident and there were no injuries.Company maintenance found the No. 1 inlet cowling thermal anti-ice (TAI) overheat switch shorted and the switch was replaced before the aircraft was released for continued service.

A Cessna 172R aircraft (registration C-GZKA) and a Cessna 152 aircraft (registration C-GGPE), both operated by Harv’s Air Service, were conducting local training flights from Steinbach (South) Aerodrome (CKK7), Manitoba, with 1 pilot on board each aircraft. While on final approach for Runway 36 at CKK7, the 2 aircraft collided mid-air. They then collided with terrain approximately 1/4 statute miles (SM) from the runway threshold. There was a post-impact fire. Both pilots were fatality injured. The TSB deployed and is assessing the occurrence.

C-FTJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP Bombardier CRJ 900 aircraft, operating as flight JZA970 from St. Louis Lambert International Airport (KSTL), Missouri, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the initial descent from FL310 the crew received a L BLEED DUCT message. During the quick reference handbook procedures, the right bleed valve closed resulting in both packs being inoperable. The crew requested a lower altitude and commenced descent to FL240. The cabin rate of climb increased from 2300 to 3000 feet per minute and climbing. The crew donned their oxygen masks, and the masks dropped automatically in the cabin. The flight crew configured the aircraft for unpressurized flight and declared PAN PAN with ATC. The aircraft landed uneventfully with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by. Maintenance found the Bleed Air Manifold duct cracked at a welded joint above the wing anti-ice SOV. The result was a protective shutdown of the bleed air system. The operator submitted a service difficulty report (SDR) for this event. All cabin oxygen generators were replaced.

C-GTHU, a Summit Helicopters Limited Bell 407 helicopter, was conducting helicopter slinging operations in the vicinity of Bronson Creek Airstrip, BC, with only the pilot on board. While moving a load of core samples on a long line, the pilot inadvertently pressed the load release button located on the cyclic control. The long line and load released from the helicopter belly hook and landed in the nearby Iskut River. The long line was not located. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft or property.

C-GENO, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-8-402, was operating flight WEN3348 from the Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to the Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While descending through 12 500 feet ASL on the initial approach into CYYC, WEN3348 encountered severe turbulence. The flight crew reported large and abrupt changes in aircraft attitude and altitude. The aircraft momentarily became unresponsive to control inputs, and the auto pilot disconnected. Moments later, the flight crew was able to regain positive control of the aircraft. The flight continued to CYYC and landed without further incident. There were no injuries, and the aircraft received no damage.

N805NW, an Airbus A330-300 operated by Delta Airlines was conducting flight DAL127 from Adolfo Suárez Madrid–Barajas International Airport (LEMD), Spain, to John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), NY. While in cruise, the flight crew felt a shudder and yaw to the left. The ECAM indicated a No.1 engine stall and a N1 drop. The thrust lever was reduced to idle while the EGT continued to increase, and the checklist was completed resulting in the engine being shut down. The decision was made to declare an emergency and divert to Lajes International Airport (LPLA), Portugal. The flight landed without further incident. Maintenance was deployed and the No.1 engine will be replaced, and the aircraft will be ferried. The cause of the engine failure is under investigation.

C-FYJD, a Westjet Boeing 737-800 operating as flight WJA2425, from Cancun International Airport (MMUN), MX, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, was on descent to CYYZ when the crew received an Airspeed Disagree message. Quick reference handbook procedures were followed, and a PAN PAN was declared. The crew determined the First Officer's instruments were providing the correct information, so control of flight was transferred from the Captain to the First Officer. The aircraft landed uneventfully and taxied to the gate. Maintenance performed several fault isolation tasks including a flushing of the pitot static system, and a pitot static check, but no faults were found. Aircraft was returned to service.

C-FXJC, a Jazz Aviation Embraer ERJ 175 was operating flight JZA943 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During the climb from KEWR, a cabin crew member advised the flight crew about smoke coming out of the oven. After pulling the breakers, the smoke dissipated, and the crew decided to turn back to KEWR. No emergency was declared but firetrucks were waiting for them at the gate.

C-FGCH, a privately registered Robinson R44 Raven II helicopter, was on a recreational flight from Clearwater, BC, to Lone Butte, BC, with 1 pilot and 3 passengers onboard. During the final approach to a clearing beside a restaurant in Lone Butte, at approximately 70 feet above ground level, the aircraft encountered a wind gust while the pilot was initiating a right turn. A loss of tail rotor effectiveness followed, and the aircraft began to yaw to the left. Control of the aircraft was lost, and the helicopter collided with the surrounding terrain. The aircraft came to a rest on its side, on top of a large rock in a forested area. The emergency locator transmitter (ELT) activated. Emergency services responded to the scene. One passenger was seriously injured and was airlifted to hospital. The pilot and another passenger received minor injuries. The helicopter was substantially damaged.

C-GKVX, a commercially registered Bell Textron 206L-4 Long Ranger was conducting a private flight under visual flight rules, from The Lodge at Panther River, AB to the Hespero/ Safron Residence Heliport (CTS6), AB with the pilot and one passenger on board. At approximately 1220 MDT the pilot conducted his second approach to a grass strip attached to the heliport. The helicopter impacted the ground and the skid gear collapsed.  One main rotor blade struck the tail boom, cutting off the tail rotor gear box. The second main rotor blade was sheared off by the upper wire cutter. The pilot was seriously injured, and the passenger received fatal injuries. There was no post-accident fire.

C-FZUG, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was operating flight ROU1623 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise at FL330, the aircraft encountered unexpected turbulence, resulting in an initial 200 feet climb followed immediately by a 500 feet descent to FL327 triggering a TCAS RA. The crew actioned the RA and stabilized the aircraft. ATC was advised and the flight continued without further incident.

C-GAAJ, a Cargojet Airways Boeing B767 was operating flight CJT5457 from La Aurora International Airport (MGGT), Guatemala, to Ramón Villeda Morales International Airport (MHLM), Honduras. During the visual approach to Runway 04 at MHLM, an EICAS message LE SLAT ASYM was received. A go-around was executed, vectored to a hold, checklist was followed, and a PAN PAN urgency was declared. Aircraft circled back for visual approach and the aircraft landed uneventfully. #4 INBD target re-secured IAW AMM 27-81-02. #4 OUTBD sensor was replaced IAW AMN 27-88-01. System tested serviceable.

C-GBHR, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was operating flight ROU1878 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Hewanorra International Airport (TLPL), Saint Lucia. During cruise, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue their duties. Duties were redistributed amongst remaining cabin crew members.

C-ISYG, a privately registered Pipistrel Alpha Trainer advanced ultralight, was on a local flight from Delta Heritage Air Park (CAK3), BC, with only the pilot on board. After touching down at CAK3, the aircraft bounced and then veered off the runway into nearby bushes. The aircraft’s emergency locator transmitter (ELT) activated and remained on after the accident. The Civil Air Search and Rescue Association (CASARA) responded to the ELT signal and turned it off. There were no injuries reported. The aircraft was substantially damaged.The propeller, nose and left main landing gear were damaged. The left wing and empennage were broken off the aircraft. The pilot will be conducting training with a flight instructor.

C-GARJ, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was operating flight ROU1707 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), NV. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to continue their duties. Duties were redistributed amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-IFHK, un ultra léger de base Fly Italia MD3 Rider d'immatriculation privée, effectuait un vol local à partir d'une piste privée située à environ 10.75 NM au Sud-Est de l'aéroport de St-Hyacinthe, QC (CSU3) selon les règles de vol à vue avec seul le pilote à bord. Au moment de l'atterrissage, il y avait des orages à l'horizon et alors que celui-ci tentait de s'aligner pour revenir atterrir sur sa piste privée, l'aéronef a rencontré de la turbulence sévère au point d'être difficile à contrôler et a été plaqué au sol par une rafale de vent dans un champ de maïs à environ 800m du seuil de la piste. Au contact avec le sol l'aéronef a basculé vers l'avant et s'est retourné sur le dos. Il n'a pas eu de blessé mais l'aéronef a subi des dommages substantiels.

C-FRAX, a Boeing 737-8 MAX operated by WestJet as flight WJA2481, was en route from Norman Manley International Airport (MKJP), Kingston, Jamaica, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While in cruise, the flight crew received a LOW PRESS indication for the System A hydraulic pump. The crew contacted company operations and declared a PAN PAN.  The flight continued to CYYZ and landed uneventfully on Runway 23. The crew retained control of steering and braking, and the aircraft taxied to the terminal after stopping briefly on Taxiway H to be cleared by aircraft rescue and firefighting.Maintenance subsequently replaced the System A hydraulic pump. Following a successful operational check, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GIUF, an Airbus A321 operated by Air Canada as flight AC982, was preparing to depart from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Sangster International Airport (MKJS), Jamaica, when a flight attendant became ill. The crew member was replaced prior to departure, and the flight continued without further incident.

C-FDJZ, a Jazz Aviation CRJ900 was operating flight JZA768 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to San Diego International Airport (KSAN), CA. During climb, the crew smelled electrical fumes and lost comm #2. Checklist was followed but source of the smell could not be determined. Crew declared PAN PAN and headed back to CYVR. Upon landing they stopped on the taxiway and since the smell was still present, a rapid deplanement was executed.

C-FSEQ, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 was operating flight AC1322 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Providenciales International Airport (MBPV), Turks and Caicos Islands. After departure, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue their duties. Other cabin crew took over duties.

C-FITW, an Air Canada Boeing 777-300 was operating flight AC890 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Leonardo da Vinci International Airport (LIRF), Italy. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to continue their duties.

C-FEJF, a Jazz Aviation Embraer ERJ 175 was operating flight JZA671 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Raleigh-Durham International Airport (KRDU), NC. Shortly after take-off, a cabin crew member advised there was a burning smell in the galley area. The circuit breakers for the oven were pulled out and the crew declared an emergency and diverted back to CYUL. The aircraft was met by aircraft rescue and firefighting who came onboard to check for fire/air quality. Reported that sandwiches wrapped in plastic were found in the oven. The aircraft landed approximately 3500 kg overweight.

C-FYFD, a privately registered Van's RV-6A departed Duncan Aerodrome (CAM3), BC, on a recreational flight, under visual flight rules, to Courtenay Airpark (CAH3), BC, with 1 pilot, and 1 passenger on board. Prior to departure, the aircraft fuel gauges indicated 12 US gallons of fuel. After approximately 30 minutes of flight, while approaching CAH3, the aircraft experienced an engine (Avco Lycoming O-320) power loss due to fuel exhaustion. A forced approach was conducted and the aircraft landed on a mudflat approximately 1 nautical mile east of CAH3. The suspected cause of the fuel exhaustion was reportedly a fuel leak. The aircraft was fuelled with 5 US gallons of 100LL Avgas which was brought to the aircraft in a jerry can from CAH3. The pilot subsequently attempted a takeoff from the mudflat, without his passenger, to complete the flight to CAH3. During the takeoff roll on the mudflat, mud accumulated in the wheel fairings of the landing gear. This resulted in the takeoff ground run being longer than anticipated. The aircraft traversed a depression in the surface of the mudflat, approximately 1000 feet from the beginning of the takeoff roll, and the nose gear experienced structural failure. The aircraft nosed-over to an approximately vertical nose-down attitude before falling back onto its main landing gear. The aircraft emergency locator transmitter activated, and a signal was received by the Canadian Mission Control Centre. The pilot was able to exit the aircraft without issue and no injuries were reported. The aircraft was substantially damaged.Following the occurrence, the aircraft was pushed to the shoreline by the pilot and a number of bystanders. The aircraft was subsequently recovered by a helicopter. A post-crash inspection of the aircraft found that a gasket seal on the carburetor had degraded. This would have allowed fuel to leak when the aircraft engine was running.

C-GZVJ, a Wasaya Airways LP Beech 1900 was conducting flight WSG1633 from Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON to Muskrat Dam Airport (CZMD), ON with 2 crew members and 7 passengers on board. Approximately 48 nautical miles north-northeast of CYXL, just after reaching the cruise altitude of flight level 230, the crew noticed an issue with the pressurization. The crew carried out the "Cabin Alt Hi Drill" and descended to 10 000 feet ASL. The crew declared a MAYDAY during the descent and diverted to CYXL. Following the descent, a passenger suffered a medical issue, so the crew requested an ambulance to meet the aircraft on arrival. The aircraft landed uneventfully. Following the occurrence, the operator's maintenance replaced a bleed air valve and computer board.

C-GCHU, a Chinook Helicopters Cessna 172S was operating from Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, to Langley Regional (CYNJ), BC, and N196SY, a Skywest Airlines Embraer 175 was operating flight SKW3400 from Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (KSEA), WA, to Bellingham International Airport (KBLI), WA. During the descent for SKW3400, there was a loss of separation in the vicinity of KBLI with a separation of 2.9 miles laterally and 400 feet vertically.

C-GJFZ, a Jazz Aviation CRJ900 was operating flight JZA783 from Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (KDCA), VA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Internation Airport (CYYZ), ON. Enroute, the brake overheat warning message illuminated. The crew actioned the quick reference handbook and a PAN PAN was declared. Aircraft landed uneventfully and brake temperature was back to normal. The emergency crew did a brake inspection, and all indications were good. Emergency vehicles followed the aircraft to the gate.

C-GESH, a Perimeter Aviation LP De Havilland DHC-8-102, was conducting IFR flight PAG209 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Oxford House Airport (CYOH), MB. Approximately 30 nautical miles northeast of CYWG, upon reaching the cruise altitude of flight level 190, the PIC noticed the #1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW121) oil pressure indicating 10 PSI. The PIC confirmed this information with the first officer and the crew proceeded with a precautionary engine shut down as per the standard operating procedure and quick reference handbook. The crew then declared a PAN PAN and returned back to CYWG. The aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-FUEY, a privately registered Cessna C180, was conducting a VFR flight from Pistol Lake, ON to Pickerel Lake, ON with one pilot on board. During the flare, the aircraft encountered gusty conditions and touched down on the right float. The aircraft continued rolling to the right until the wingtip contacted the water; resulting in the aircraft cartwheeling on the water. The aircraft came to stop facing in opposite direction of the approach, upside down with the cockpit submerged. The pilot exited aircraft through the passenger door. There was no fire. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.A retired firefighter/paramedic was first on scene with a boat followed almost immediately by a second boat. The aircraft was towed submerged to a sand beach with the bottom of the beach on a gradual incline to land. The aircraft was secured to shore and marked with buoys for visibility as only the bottom of the floats were visible from above water line. Paramedics, volunteer firefighters and OPP also attended the scene.

C-GJWN, an Air Canada Airbus 321, was conducting flight AC153 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, with 6 crew and 182 passengers on board. Prior to descent, the flight crew received a "NOSEWHEEL STEERING FAULT" message on their ECAM. The flight crew declared a Pan Pan and began their descent to CYYC. After an uneventful landing, the flight crew were able to successfully reset the Nose Wheel Steering Fault and taxi to their gate under the aircrafts own power. Company maintenance personnel replaced the nose wheel servo control valve, and the aircraft was returned to service without further issue.

C-FMFA, a privately registered Cessna 190 was operating from the Edmonton/Josephburg Aerodrome (CFB6), AB. During the landing roll the right brake became ineffective and the aircraft veered to the left side of the runway. The aircraft exited the runway and ground looped. The landing gear collapsed, and the aircraft came to rest in the grass. There were no injuries to the pilot. The aircraft was substantially damaged with both the wing and fuselage bending during the ground loop. The aircraft was subsequently removed from the runway.

C-GOYY, an amateur-built Willy's 140 taildragger, was conducting a flight from Kitchener/Waterloo Airport (CYKF), ON, to Guelph Aerodrome (CNC4), ON, with the pilot as the sole occupant. During touchdown on Runway 32, the aircraft flipped over. The aircraft sustained substantial damage, and the pilot sustained minor injuries. The pilot reported encountering gusty wind conditions at the time of landing.

C-GFQP, a Bell 212 HP helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited, was conducting external load operations 129 NM NNE of Goose Bay, NL (53.55°N, 56.83°W), with 1 crew member on board. The helicopter was slinging a load of roof sheeting when, approximately three minutes after departure, the long line cable detached, and the load fell to the ground. No injuries were reported, and there was no damage to the aircraft or surrounding property.Maintenance action: a post-occurrence inspection determined that the manual release was not properly rigged. The system was set too tight, with insufficient slack when in the closed and locked position. As a result, the manual release was partially pulled open even while at rest, potentially leading to an uncommanded release of the sling load.

C-GOFJ, a Sunwest Aviation Limited Dassault Falcon 7X was being operated as flight CNK7, from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, under instrument flight rules, to Masset Airport (CZMT), BC. While on short final to Runway 13 in CZMT, the crew initiated a go-around in response to bird activity near the runway touchdown zone. Several birds were struck while the aircraft flew the published missed approach. Subsequently, multiple landing gear fault indications were received by the crew. After performing the appropriate checklists, it was determined that the nose landing gear was not locked down, and the gear doors were in the open position. The crew elected to divert to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, and a PAN PAN was declared. The aircraft landed without further incident. There were no injuries. The aircraft will be inspected to determine what damage occurred.

C-GBJZ, un De Havilland of Canada DHC-8-402 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7986 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international Montréal-Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV). En croisière dans le secteur de Québec, l'équipage a déclaré une situation d'urgence (PAN PAN) avec le service de circulation aérienne en raison d’un problème avec le système de dégivrage. Une descente vers 10 000 pieds a été demandée. Une fois à 10 000 pieds, le PAN PAN a été annulé et l’aéronef a poursuivi son vol. L'atterrissage s'est déroulé sans encombre.

C-FIUW, an Air Canada Boeing 777-333ER was operating flight AC2 from Haneda Airport (RJTT), Japan, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. On departure, a cabin crew member fell ill prior to departure. They were unable to continue their duties and were removed from the aircraft.

C-FGDX, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was operating flight AC60 from Kansai International Airport (RJBB), Japan, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, the aircraft passed through an area of turbulence, a passenger found a cabin crew member with a minor head injury in the galley. The cabin crew member was unable to continue duties.

C-FEGI, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was operating flight AC879 from Toulouse-Blagnac Airport (LFBO), France, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During cruise, a flight attendant became incapacitated and was unable to continue duties.

C-GITP, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-112 was operating flight ROU1672 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL. During approach, on descent to 3000 feet for the ILS 18R, a TCAS TA was received for traffic 800 feet off the left wingtip. An RA: LEVEL OFF followed at approximately 3200 feet, as the aircraft was leveling for the approach. Flight directors commanded a pitch-up before the "clear of conflict" alert. ATC was notified and the flight subsequently landed without further incident.

C-FMAK, an ATR42-320 operated by Calm Air International LP, was conducting IFR flight CAV120 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to The Pas Airport (CYQD), MB. During the starting procedure of the number 1 engine, the flight crew saw smoke starting to billow into the cockpit from behind the First Officer seat. The flight crew stopped the starting sequence, shut down the number 2 engine and proceeded with a rapid deplanement of the passengers. The crew entered a snag in the journey log and maintenance personnel rectified the snag by replacing the Recirculation Fan contactor. However, when the flight crew started number 1 engine for the second time, smoke began billowing into the flight deck once again. The crew interrupted the engine start and a second rapid deplanement was initiated. During both events no injuries were reported, and no emergency services were requested.The operator's maintenance replaced a Recirculation Fan contactor, the DC External Power contactor, as well as the wiring and terminals of the DC External Power system. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-FLKY, a 2106701 Ontario Inc. (dba NovaJet) Mitsubishi CL-600-2B19 (CRJ100) was flying from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Providenciales International Airport (MBPV), Turks and Caicos Islands. Approximately 1 hour prior to landing at MBPV, the FLAPS FAIL amber caution message illuminated. Crew followed the appropriate quick reference handbook. The crew requested priority handling by ATC and requested fire trucks on landing. Crew performed a Flap 0 degree landing uneventfully. Maintenance determined the issue is most likely the flap computer. Flap computer has been ordered.

C-GXAF (test flight registration), a Bombardier BD-700-2A12 operating as test flight BBA02, departed Runway 23 at Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, following C-FUJA, an Embraer ERJ-170-200 operating as Jazz Aviation LP flight JZA686. While under the control of South Departure, BBA02 was observed overtaking JZA686. The controller issued a turn to the north for BBA02; however, separation had already deteriorated to 2.2 NM laterally and 900 feet vertically.

C-GKQC, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 operated by Porter Airlines as flight PTR2248, and C-GSJZ, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight JZA7123, were both on approach to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ). A loss of separation occurred when JZA7123 failed to sufficiently reduce speed to maintain the required 3 NM spacing behind PTR2248. The minimum separation between the two aircraft was 1.7 NM.

C-GRSB, a Douglas C-47 operated by the Canadian Warplane Heritage Museum, was on final approach to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, when the flight crew feathered the left engine due to backfiring and a loss of power. The aircraft continued the approach and landed without further incident.

C-FABH, an Anderson Air Dassault Falcon 2000EX was operating from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Van Nuys Airport (KVNY), CA. C-FABH was cleared for visual approach for RWY 16R. the aircraft manoeuvered to avoid high terrain and while descending on 5-mile, 70-degree right base, an RA was issued due to VFR traffic converging. The conflicting traffic was acquired visually, and no aggressive manoeuvring was required. Minimum separation was about 300 feet vertically and 1/4 SM laterally.

C-FJZL, a Jazz Aviation Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) was conducting IFR flight JZA8110 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. When the aircraft was at FL370, significant turbulence was encountered north of Lake Superior. The aircraft suffered a momentary loss of aircraft control, the autopilot was disengaged, and the flight crew were unable to maintain altitude. JZA8110 descended to FL350 and control of the aircraft was regained. No aircraft limitations were exceeded and no unsecured items tossed.
