There were no reported injuries, and the seatbelt sign was on at moment of turbulence encounter. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft before further flight.

N78002, a Boeing 777-200 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL879 from London Heathrow Airport (EGLL), United Kingdom, to George Bush Intercontinental Airport (KIAH), Texas, U.S. N879FD, a Boeing 777 aircraft operated by FedEx, was conducting flight FDX10, from Memphis International Airport (KMEM), Tennessee, U.S., to Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France.While in cruise at FL340 within Gander FIR, UAL879, requested a climb to FL360 and was advised by ATC to stand by. During this time, the controller issued a CPDLC clearance direct to TOPPS, which inadvertently included a level change to FL360. The controller immediately recognized the error and issued a voice instruction to the crew to maintain FL340 and disregard the CPDLC clearance.Approximately two minutes later, UAL879 was observed climbing. ATC instructed the crew to descend back to FL340, reiterating that the level change clearance had been cancelled. The crew reported receiving a TCAS alert during the climb. The conflicting traffic, FDX10, was eastbound at FL350.UAL879 climbed 500 feet above its cleared altitude before returning to FL340. A loss of vertical separation occurred when the required 1000 feet in reduced vertical separation minimum (RVSM) airspace was reduced to 500 feet, but separation was re-established within seconds. Both flights continued to their destinations without further incident.

C-GLQR, a De Havilland Dash 8-400 operated by Porter Airlines as flight PTR2248, was enroute from Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON at FL220. Approximately 10 minutes prior to top of descent, the flight crew received a #2 HYD PRESS caution, followed shortly by a #2 HYD QTY caution. The crew observed a rapid loss of pressure and quantity in the No. 2 hydraulic system.The flight crew actioned the No. 2 Hydraulic System Failure checklist and declared a PAN PAN. The alternate landing gear extension checklist was completed, and the flight diverted to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ). The aircraft landed without further incident and, following an inspection by ARFF, taxied to the gate under its own power.Maintenance inspection revealed a leaking hydraulic line, which was replaced along with the No. 2 hydraulic pump. A hydraulic system flush was completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GLQL, a De Havilland Dash 8-400 operated by Porter Airlines, was scheduled to operate flight PTR2133 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. During preflight preparations, the flight crew was advised of a potential issue with the right-wing fuel tank. Upon inspection near the No. 2 engine nacelle, the captain observed a minor fuel drip from beneath the fuel panel. The captain notified ATC, who in turn advised ARFF, and the crew promptly offloaded the passengers.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and determined the fuel leak to be abnormal. The aircraft was grounded for further evaluation. Porter maintenance identified a leaking fuel line just aft of the refuel/defuel adapter. The O-rings on the pressure refuel line couplers were replaced, with the fault traced to a cut O-ring at the Master Fuel Valve Coupler. A pressure fueling test was conducted with an additional 300 lbs of fuel added; no leaks were observed. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GQTA, a Dornier Alpha Jet operated by Top Aces, was conducting flight CHETA18 from North Bay Airport, Ontario (CYYB) to Winnipeg, Manitoba (CYWG). During the takeoff roll on Runway 26, the crew initiated a high-speed rejected takeoff due to a suspected incorrect flap setting. The aircraft exited the active runway and came to a stop on the taxiway, where it was shut down.Following the stop, both main wheel tires deflated, and the left main wheel brake assembly caught fire. The fire was extinguished, and the aircraft was secured without further damage.

C-GRQH, a Kîsik Aerial Survey Incorporated Piper PA-31 (Navajo) departed Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC, for a local aerial survey flight, under visual flight rules, with only the pilot on board. Approximately 2 hours into the flight, the left engine (Avco Lycoming TIO-540-I2B) began running rough and losing power. The pilot subsequently shutdown and feathered the affected engine, declared a Mayday, and diverted to Mackenzie Aerodrome (CYZY), BC. The pilot was able to restart the engine during the descent into CYZY and landed without further incident. There were no injuries, and the aircraft was not damaged.The aircraft was inspected and the flight data was reviewed. It was determined that an overly lean mixture setting on the left engine caused the roughness. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GIVV, un hélicoptère Bell 206B exploité par G.D.G. Aviation Inc. effectuait un vol d’épandage aérien selon les règles de vol à vue dans un secteur à environ 25 milles nautiques au sud de l’aéroport d’Alma, QC (CYTF). L’hélicoptère était en approche finale vers un camion ravitailleur quand soudainement, le pilote a perdu la maîtrise en lacet (perte d’efficacité du rotor de queue). L’hélicoptère a basculé en touchant le sol et s’est immobilisé sur le côté gauche à quelques mètres du camion. Le pilote a pu évacuer sans difficulté et a subi des blessures mineures.UPDATED: 18 June 2026

C-GBIJ, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was operating flight ROU1673 from Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise at FL380, the aircraft encountered sudden and unexpected severe turbulence near the JOHNN RNAV fix while in IMC conditions. The aircraft experienced a rapid downdraft lasting approximately 10 seconds, resulting in an altitude loss of 700 feet. The crew selected engine ignition mode. The turbulence produced near-zero gravity conditions and a vertical speed of -3700 feet/minute. The autopilot and autothrust remained engaged, and the aircraft returned to assigned altitude without further incident.

C-GUWJ, a WestJet Boeing 737-7CT was operating flight WS1315 from Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), CA, U.S., to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue duties. Duties were assumed by another cabin crew member.

C-GJZX, a Jazz Aviation LP de Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was conducting flight AC8652 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Portland International Airport (KPDX), OR. During the initial climb, the gear up selection was made and the weight on wheels caution light subsequently illuminated. After discussions with flight operations, the decision was made to return to CYVR. During the approach to final, under VMC (visual meteorological conditions) the first officer noticed flames at the bottom of the right windshield. The sparking ceased as soon as the windshield heat was selected to off. The outer windscreen showed some discoloration and had cracked. The aircraft continued and landed without further incident. Maintenance personnel found and replaced a broken wire in the weight on wheels system and the cracked window was replaced. Jazz safety found no wiring connection between the weight on wheels and the windshield heat systems.

C-FSQX, an AirSprint Cessna 525B was operating flight ASP556 from Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport (KOPF), FL, to Midland International Airport (KMAF), TX. While at FL450, the crew reported hearing a pressurization related sound coming from the door area. They initiated a normal descent and observed that the cabin pressure was normal. Shortly after, the sound became louder and the cabin altitude began to climb. Approximately 80 NM east of George Bush Intercontinental Airport (KIAH), TX, at FL430, the AirSprint operations centre received an automated alert notification from the aircraft of "Cabin Altitude". Aircraft initiated an emergency descent with oxygen masks on and diverted to KIAH. The passenger masks deployed automatically.Aircraft is grounded for maintenance.

C-FGKO, an Aerospatiale AS350 B-2 operated by Custom Helicopters was conducting a VFR local flight that included firefighting duties and external load operations in vicinity of Lynn Lake, MB. C-FGKO departed the Eldon Lake Fire Base (ELFB), located near Lynn Lake/Eldon Lake Water Aerodrome (CKD3), MB. C-FGKO was returning from the fire with a 100-foot-long line and a 16-foot x 16-foot net that weighed approximately 380 pounds. The helicopter approached ELFB into wind from the south. The drop zone was on the north end of a pad area near where C-GLBJ, a Wildcat Helicopters Inc. Airbus AS 350 B3, was parked. The pilot attempted to stabilize the load but drifted closer to the parked helicopter and elected to go around. On the second approach, ground crew arrived to help marshal the helicopter. On the final approach to the drop site, the load made contact with the water, short of the dock. Engine power was increased to gain altitude and bring the helicopter into a hover; however, the load had lateral and longitudinal movement. During the attempt to regain control, the load made contact with 2 of C-GLBJ's rotor blades. The pilot released the load at a height of 2 to 3 feet above the ground. The pilot landed the helicopter safely and shut down.Wildcat Helicopters' maintenance removed the 2 blades from C-GLBJ for inspection.

C-GFHZ, a privately registered Shinn Engineering Inc. (Varga) 2150A was operating on a local sightseeing flight from the Vermilion Aerodrome (CYVG), AB. The occurrence flight had departed from CYVG at approximately 1145 MDT. After approximately 40 minutes, the aircraft returned to land at CYVG. The aircraft approached the airport and joined the mid-left downwind for Runway 10. Wind at the time (Lloydminster CYLL METAR – 28 NM E) was reported as 050°T at 12 gusting to 22 knots. During the initial approach for Runway 10, the pilot discontinued the approach for unknown reasons and conducted a go-around. The pilot rejoined the circuit on the downwind left for Runway 10. At 1225 MDT, while turning from the base leg to final, the aircraft stalled. The left wing dropped, and the aircraft entered a spin to the left. The aircraft completed one and a half rotations before impacting the ground. The aircraft came to rest approximately 0.9 NM NW of the airport. The pilot and passenger were fatally injured, and the aircraft was destroyed in a post-impact fire.

C-GDGP, un hélicoptère BK117 exploité par Airmédic effectuait un vol d’évacuation médicale selon les règles de vol à vue de nuit depuis une pourvoirie au lac Watshishou situé à environ 47 MN NE de Havre-Saint-Pierre, QC à destination a l'aeroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV), avec 2 membres d’équipage, 2 membres du personnel médical et un patient à bord. Peu de temps après le décollage, l’hélicoptère s’est abimé dans le lac. Un témoin qui a vu l’hélicoptère percuter l’eau s’est dirigé en chaloupe vers l’endroit où l’aéronef a coulé. Un des pilotes a pu s’extirper et il a été embarqué à bord, toutefois les autres occupants n’ont pu être localisés. L’hélicoptère et les 4 autres occupants ont été localisés dans le lac plusieurs jours plus tard. Il n'y a eu aucun autre survivant.

C-GLRR, an Ootsa Air Limited Piper PA-31-325 (Navajo) departed Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC, on a charter flight, under visual flight rules, to Tsay Keh Aerodrome (CBN9), BC, with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. When the aircraft was level at 10 000 feet above sea level, the pilot noticed an unsafe nose gear indication on the annunciator panel. The pilot visually confirmed that the nose gear doors were open and slowed to the landing gear extension speed. The landing gear was selected down and all 3 landing-gear down and locked lights illuminated. The pilot saw that the nose gear steerage linkage appeared to be disconnected. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft was turned back to CYXS and landed without further incident. The aircraft was inspected and the landing gear was found to be serviceable. The aircraft has a supplemental type certificate for a quick disconnect pin for the nose gear steering linkage. That pin was connected to the landing gear by its lanyard but was not installed in the steering linkage. The quick connect pin was replaced with standard steering linkage hardware. Maintenance conducted gear swings and the aircraft was returned to service.

Un système d’aéronef télépiloté (SATP) de plus de 25 kilogrammes en exploitation par ING Robotics Aviation, effectuait un vol d’essai dans un champ dans le secteur de Shawville, Québec. À environ la moitié du trajet de 2 kilomètres, le moteur du côté droit a eu une défectuosité et la maitrise du SATP a été perdue. Le SATP a roulé sur sa droite et s’est écrasé au sol. Un incendie s’est déclenché à l’impact et a rapidement été maitrisé. Le SATP a été détruit par l’incendie. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GBHZ, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was operating flight ROU1636 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL. During approach to RWY 18R, ROU1622 received a TCAS RA:  LEVEL OFF. The crew followed the RA, levelled off and ATC was advised. No traffic was visually acquired. TCAS indicated 700 feet separation. Aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GLJV, a Beech B200 operated by Fast Air Ltd., was operating IFR flight PBR640 from Norway House Airport, MB (CYNE) to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Airport, MB (CYWG). After landing Runway 36 at CYWG, PBR640 exited the active runway and the ground controller instructed PBR640 to taxi on Runway 13 then Taxiway C to Apron II. OPS 3, a Winnipeg Airports Authority vehicle, was on Taxiway C conducting a field check with an acknowledged clearance to hold short of Runway 36 only. OPS 3 then proceeded Taxiway C towards Runway 13. As PBR640 was starting its right turn onto Taxiway C from Runway 13, the First Officer had to abruptly apply the brakes as OPS 3 vehicle was proceeding from Taxiway C onto Runway 13. The approximate distance between the aircraft and the vehicle was 90 feet. Once OPS 3 was clear of the aircraft, PBR640 continued taxiing to Apron II without further incident.The operator of OPS 3 vehicle reported not being able to see PBR640 as they were in his blind spot. The operator of OPS 3 was given verbal coaching and additional training trough the Winnipeg Airport Authority AVOP program.

C-GSLF, un hélicoptère Airbus AS350 B2 exploité par Les Hélicoptères Canadiens Limitée, effectuait un vol avec une charge à l’élingue selon les règles de vol à vue depuis un camp situé à 50 milles nautiques à l’est-sud-est de l’aéroport de Kuujjuarapik, QC (CYGW) à destination de CYGW. Deux moitiés de remorque ont été préparées pour le transport à l’élingue par le client avec des sangles de type Maxiflex. Le pilote a décollé avec la charge en direction de CYGW. La charge à l’élingue est devenue instable et a commencé à tourner sur elle-même dès que l’hélicoptère a atteint une vitesse de 60 nœuds. Le pilote a exécuté un demi-tour pour revenir au point de départ. Peu de temps après, une des sangles s’est brisée et le pilote a réduit la vitesse à 40 nœuds. La charge est tombée au sol avant que l’hélicoptère soit arrivé à destination. Personne n’a été blessé. L’observation des sangles faite par le pilote suite à l’événement indique qu’une des sangles s’est cassée et que les 2 autres ont été endommagées suite au frottement de celles-ci entre des pièces métalliques et le bord tranchant de la remorque coupée.

C-FCAS, un Osprey II de construction amateur et d'immatriculation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue à partir de l'aéroport de St-Jean, QC (CYJN) avec seul le pilote à bord. Au moment du toucher de roues à l'atterrissage, la jambe de train droite s'est affaissée dû au bris d'un boulon de la contrefiche et l'aéronef s'est immobilisé sur la piste peu après. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GORN, un Beech 1900D exploité par Propair, effectuait le vol PRO4895 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport Jean Lesage International de Québec, QC (CYQB) à destination de l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 9 passagers à bord. À environ 110NM au sud-est de l'aéroport de Val-D'Or, QC (CYVO), l'équipage a perçu une odeur de brûlé ainsi qu'une légère fumée dans le poste de pilotage. Le pilote a alors décidé de détourner le vol vers CYVO où les services d'urgence ont été mis en alerte. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre à 1827Z. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés ni d'incendie.Une inspection de maintenance a révélé une défaillance du moteur du ventilateur avant.

C-FLTS, un Beech A100 exploité par Exact Air, effectuait le vol ET823 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport St-Honoré/Chicoutimi, QC (CYRC) à destination de l'aéroport Jean Lesage International de Québec, QC (CYQB) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 2 passagers à bord. Quelques instants après le décollage les pilotes ont été avertis par la tour qu'une trainée blanche sortait de l'avion. Ils ont fait demi-tour pour revenir se poser à CYRC. Une inspection après-vol a révélé que le bouchon du réservoir de carburant auxiliaire gauche était manquant et celui-ci a été retrouvé près des réservoirs de ravitaillement, celui-ci a été remis en place par un technicien suite à une inspection visuelle de l'aile et du bouchon.

C-GURG, un Bombardier Challenger CL600-2B16 exploité par le Gouvernement du Québec, Service aérien gouvernemental, effectuait le vol QUE10 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport Jean Lesage International de Québec, QC (CYQB) à destination de l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP). À environ 170NM au sud de CYVP, le voyant de déverrouillage d'inverseur de poussée du moteur gauche (GE CF34-3A1) s'est illuminé. L'équipage a déclaré un état d'urgence et l'aéronef est retourné se poser à CYQB. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés ni dommage.

C-FYJE, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was operating flight ROU2375 from Lake City Gateway Airport (KLCQ), FL, U.S. to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, the crew received a HYD G RSVR OVHT ECAM. ECAM actions were completed, resulting in the green hydraulic system and PTU being isolated. Approximately 20 minutes later, the OVHT indication extinguished, however the system remained isolated as a precaution. The crew declared a PAN PAN urgency with ATC. While descending through 8000 feet, the green hydraulic system was reactivated, with all systems restored. The aircraft landed uneventfully, and no abnormalities were identified when aircraft rescue and firefighting carried out their external inspection.

C-GOWD, a Piper PA-30 (Twin Comanche) aircraft operated by Annapolis Valley Flight Training Centre Inc., was conducting a local training flight from Greenwood Airport (CYZX), Nova Scotia, with one instructor and one student on board. During the landing on Runway 26, the aircraft veered suddenly to the left after touchdown. The aircraft slid perpendicular to the runway, resulting in the collapse of the right-hand main landing gear. There were no reported injuries.Tire marks showing an alternating pattern right, left, right, left suggest possible overcorrection during rollout. Skid marks from both main landing gear extended approximately 300 feet, indicating that brakes may have been applied throughout the slide. According to the operator, the right main landing gear collapsed after the aircraft began sliding sideways. It is believed that the right tire likely blew due to lateral forces and friction on the grooved runway surface. No mechanical malfunction has been identified.

N757AN, a Boeing 777-223 (ER) operated by American Airlines was conducting flight AAL333 from Athens International Airport (LGAV), Greece, to John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), NY, U.S. Just over 8 hours into the flight, the fuel imbalance checklist was illuminated which led the flight crew to action all items and to shut down engine No.2. The flight crew declared a PAN-PAN and requested a diversion to Bangor International Airport (KBGR) ME, U.S. and landed without incident. Maintenance found a broken fuel tube, which was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GSGK, a Bell 205A-1 operated by Guardian Helicopters Inc., was operating a VFR flight from Bak Lake Forward Attack Base, ON conducting aerial firefighting activities near Sandy Lake Airport, ON (CZSJ). At approximately 17:51 CDT, shortly after scooping a load of water from a lake, the engine (Avco Lycoming T5313B) stopped producing power. The pilot (sole occupant) released the water load and conducted an autorotation landing in a shallow part of the lake. The pilot was uninjured. The ELT activated and another helicopter in the area responded to the site and rescued the pilot. The operator's maintenance went on site to rig the aircraft to lift it out of the water. They discovered some metal debris in the engine exhaust and the engine couldn't be turned by hand. The helicopter was recovered and shipped back to the operator's hangar to remove the engine for a teardown. After consultation with the helicopter manufacturer, it was found that the airframe suffered extensive damage while resting in the water and during the lift operation. The TSB is awaiting the engine tear down report.

C-GNAM, an Air Canada A220 was operating flight AC1051 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (KAUS), TX, U.S. In cruise, the captain became ill and was unable to continue their duties. A company A220 pilot was onboard the flight and commenced the flight duties. The crew decided to return to CYUL without further incident.

C-FSLU, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 was operating flight AC1071 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport (KDFW), TX, U.S. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue their duties.

PH-AOF, an Airbus A330-200 operated by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, was conducting flight KL695 from Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (EHAM), Netherlands, to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON with 265 passengers and 10 crew members onboard. During takeoff from (EHAM), the temperature of brake #3 rose to 315°C. To allow the brake to cool, the aircraft continued its climb with the landing gear extended before retracting it and proceeding normally to its destination.On approach to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), the flight crew requested Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) services to be on standby. Flight KL695 landed without further incident and was escorted to the gate by ARFF. During taxi-in, brake #3 was found to be stuck and recorded as the hottest among all brakes. It was subsequently deactivated for the return flight and replaced once the aircraft was back at EHAM.

C-GYQY, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by Maritime Air Charter, was conducting a local IFR training flight from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. C-FPQI, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines, was preparing for takeoff for IFR flight PVL2563 from CYHZ to Boston/Logan International Airport (KBOS), MA, U.S. C-GYQY was cleared for CYHZ Runway 05 approach with circling procedure to Runway 32 by the Halifax Terminal controller. The Tower Release Authority was not cancelled by the Halifax Terminal controller and PVL2563 was subsequently released for departure by the Halifax Tower controller. The separation between PVL2563 and C-GYQY became 2.9 NM horizontally and 700 feet vertically where the required separation was 3 NM and/or 1000 feet vertically. There was no other operational impact.

C-GFOF, a Flair Airlines Limited Boeing 737-8 (Max 8) was operating flight FLE820 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. C-GGCI, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 was operating flight JZA293 from CYVR to Sandspit Airport (CYZP), BC. FLE820 departed from Runway 26L, and JZA293 was subsequently cleared for takeoff from the same runway. During the initial climb, horizontal separation between the two aircraft was reduced to 1.8 nautical miles when 3.0 nautical miles was required.

CN-RGS, un Boeing 787-8 exploité par Royal Air Maroc, effectuait le vol RAM208M selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Casablanca/Mohammed V International, Maroc (GMMN) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). À environ 21 NM à l'est de Québec (QC), l'équipage a déclaré une urgence médicale pour un membre d'équipage cabine. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre à CYUL à 2334Z.

C-GKQN, an Embraer 190-400 operated by Porter Airlines Inc, was conducting flight POE308 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. On initial approach, the flight crew declared an emergency with Air traffic Control (ATC) due to a nose wheel steering issue. The aircraft landed safely in CYYZ with aircraft rescues and fire fighting (ARFF) vehicles on standby.  The aircraft was subsequently towed to the gate.

C-GSYL, un Zenair Zenith CH-300 de construction amateur et d'immatriculation privée effectuait un vol local à partir de l'aéroport Ottawa/Gatineau , Gatineau, QC (CYND) selon les règles de vol à vue avec seul le pilote à bord. Peu après le décollage le moteur s'est arrêté (Avco Lycoming O-320-B3B) et le pilote a effectué un atterrissage d'urgence dans un champ. Lors de l'atterrissage, les trois jambes de trains se sont arrachées et l'aéronef a terminé sa course sur le ventre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés ni d'incendie.

C-IPKC, un Quad City Challenger 2 sur flotteurs amphibies d'immatriculation privée, effectuait un vol de plaisance selon les règles de vol à vue de l'aérodrome de St-Lazare, QC (CST3) à destination de Vankleek Hill, ON, avec 1 pilote et un passager à bord. Au moment du décollage, le pilote a ressenti une perte de puissance moteur (Rotax 582) et l'aéronef a commencé à perdre de l'altitude. Le pilote a alors tenté un atterrissage dans un champ environ 0.6 NM au sud de la piste. Lors du contact avec le sol, l'aéronef s'est retourné sur le dos. Les deux occupants, quoique blessés, se sont extirpés d'eux-mêmes de l'aéronef et les secours sont arrivés peu de temps après. Il n'y a pas eu d'incendie.

C-FIBW, a Boeing 737-700 operated by Westjet Airlines Ltd., was conducting flight WJA658 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON with 133 passengers and 5 crew members onboard. During the takeoff roll at CYYC, the flight crew heard a loud noise followed by noticeable aircraft vibration just prior to reaching V1. After confirming that there were no engine malfunctions and upon reaching Vr, the crew proceeded with rotation and began the initial climb. The vibration ceased once the aircraft became airborne.Shortly after takeoff, the crew received information via Air Traffic Control (ATC) from another pilot who reported witnessing a tire blowout and debris on the runway. The flight crew consulted with company maintenance and operations, and after assessment, opted to continue to CYYZ. Upon handoff to Toronto ATC, the crew declared an emergency. ATC acknowledged and was already aware of the situation. Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) vehicles were positioned on standby for the aircraft’s arrival. WJA658 landed safely on runway 33R at CYYZ.Following a preliminary inspection on the ground, the aircraft was towed to the gate. Maintenance personnel conducted the applicable inspection and replaced the #3 and #4 main landing gear tires and brakes before returning the aircraft in service.

C-GURG, un Bombardier Challenger CL600-2B16 exploité par le Gouvernement du Québec, Service aérien gouvernemental, effectuait le vol QUE10 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Mont-Joli, QC (CYYY) à destination de l'aéroport Jean Lesage International de Québec, QC (CYQB) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 6 passagers à bord. À environ 62 NM au nord-est de CYQB. Un voyant de déverrouillage d'inverseur de poussée s'est illuminé. L'équipage a déclaré un état d'urgence et l'aéronef s'est posé à CYQB à 2245z. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-IJVF, un ultraléger de base Bird-Fly privé effectuait un vol local à partir d’une résidence privée de Rimouski, QC avec 2 personnes à bord. Alors que l’aéronef était à une altitude de 1500 pieds, le moteur a cessé de développer de la puissance, mais continuait de fonctionner. Le pilote s’est dirigé vers un champ pour effectuer un atterrissage d’urgence. L’aéronef a touché les roues à la fin du champ et a traversé une route en direction du champ de l'autre côté de la route. L’aéronef a basculé vers l’avant en raison du fossé qui longeait la route et aurait effectué des tonneaux. Il s’est immobilisé environ 78 pieds plus loin. Les 2 occupants blessés ont pu s’extirper de l’aéronef et ils ont été transportés à l’hôpital.

C-GCJZ, a Jazz Aviation CRJ900 was operating flight JZA640 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to LaGuardia Airport (KLGA), NY, U.S. Crew noticed brake overheat on landing and request was made to have aircraft rescue and firefighting inspect. Firetrucks escorted JZA640 to gates after being cleared.

C-FGWJ, a Boeing 737-7CT operated by WestJet, was operating IFR flight WJA1549 from Minneapolis-St Paul International/Wold-Chamberlain Airport (KMSP), MN, to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. When on final approach at CYXE, at around 400 feet AGL, the crew received a Master Caution alert. The crew elected to execute a missed approach and determined the alert was caused by a Left IRS fault. The crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC and completed the appropriate quick reference checklist (QRC). Subsequently, they received alerts for Auto Brake Disarm and Speed Trim Fail. The crew completed both QRC and set up for another approach and the aircraft landed without further incident on the second attempt.The operator's maintenance carried out several tests on the Left IRS, Auto Brake and Speed Trim, in accordance with Boeing Fault Isolation Manual (FIM). All systems were serviceable and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJYZ, a De Havilland DHC-8-314 operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was operating IFR flight PAG 1510 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Elk Island Aerodrome (CKZ3), MB. During the approach into CKZ3, the crew brought the power below 5-10% torque and the #1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW123) propeller (Hamilton Standard 14SF-23) RPM started fluctuating between 800-1200 RPM. The crew elected to discontinue the approach and, after consulting their maintenance and dispatch departments, decided to divert to Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB. They declared an emergency with ATC to have emergency services on standby upon arrival. The approach and landing at CYTH were uneventful.The operator's maintenance crews found the #1 engine PCU to be at fault. They replaced it, performed a test flight which was satisfactory, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GDON, a Cessna 172K operated by Insignia College Limited, was conducting a local flight from Boundary Bay Airport (CZBB), BC, visual flight rules, with only the student pilot on board. The aircraft taxied to the run-up area for Runway 25. The pilot executed a right turn to position the aircraft into the wind and the left wing struck a retaining wall. The aircraft taxied back to the hangar. The left wing was substantially damaged and was removed for repair.

C-FYJE, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was operating flight ROU1801 from San Salvador International Airport (MYSM), Bahamas, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During cruise at FL370, the flight crew received a HYD G RSVR OVHT ECAM message. The crew actioned the ECAM, shutting down the green hydraulic system. The crew declared an emergency (PAN PAN) and decided to divert to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL, U.S. The OVRHT condition was cleared during descent, allowing partial system restoration. The aircraft landed uneventfully with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) on standby. A general visual inspection was conducted by ARFF with no abnormalities identified. With green hydraulic pressure restored, the aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.

C-GMOW, a Seair Seaplanes Limited Cessna C208 (Caravan) floatplane, was conducting a flight under visual flight rules from Nanaimo Harbour Water Aerodrome (CAC8), BC, to Vancouver Harbour Water Aerodrome (CYHC), BC. On approach to landing westbound, the air traffic controller advised the pilot of the aircraft that there was a pleasure craft located near the ball which marks a corner of the landing area. The aircraft landed and while it slowed, the pleasure craft turned toward the aircraft and began to increase speed. The pleasure craft then turned northbound and continued to increase speed, moving away from the aircraft. The aircraft taxied to the dock without further incident.

C-GMDY, a privately registered Waco YMF F5C aircraft, was conducting a local flight under visual flight rules from Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, with a pilot and passenger on board. On landing, as the aircraft touched down on Runway 16, the aircraft began to yaw left and right, and the pilot had difficulty maintaining control. As the aircraft slowed, it ground looped, the main wheels sheared off, and the propeller struck the runway. The aircraft slid and came to a stop on the runway. The pilot and passenger exited the aircraft and emergency vehicles arrived at the aircraft. There were no injuries; the aircraft was substantially damaged. Initial inspection of the aircraft showed that the springs connecting the rudder chain had slipped out of the chain.

C-GGWF, un Boeing 737-400 exploité par Les Investissements Nolinor inc sous l’indicatif NRL310 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX) à destination de l’aéroport international de Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT). Une fois l’aéronef décollé, l’équipage a rentré les trains d'atterrissage, mais l’indicateur de position du train principal gauche est demeuré rouge. L’équipage a maintenu une vitesse de 200 nœuds et a tenté de recycler la rentrée du train d’atterrissage sans succès. Après avoir suivi la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et contacté le centre de contrôle de la maintenance de la compagnie, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence et a exécuté un demi-tour pour revenir atterrir à CYMX. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre. Après une vérification, le service de maintenance a découvert que le capteur de proximité de verrouillage du train d’atterrissage principal gauche était sale. Ce dernier a été nettoyé selon les instructions du manufacturier et l’aéronef a été remis en service.

C-GYJZ, un Dehavilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l’indicatif JZA7122 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Halifax/Stanfield international, NS (CYHZ) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Lors de l’approche, l’équipage a abaissé les trains d’atterrissage. L’indicateur lumineux a allumé 3 lumières vertes et 1 ambrée pour la porte du train avant. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence au service de contrôle aérien. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

N708RF, a privately registered Cessna 172E, was conducting a flight from High River Aerodrome (CEN4), AB, to Whitecourt Airport (CYZU), AB, with the pilot and one passenger onboard. The pilot elected to use Runway 07 at CEN4 for the takeoff attempt. As the aircraft was not accelerating at a rate the pilot was anticipating, the decision was made to abort the take-off run. The available runway remaining was insufficient to stop the aircraft, and the aircraft exited the end of the runway surface. The nose landing gear subsequently collapsed, the prop struck the ground and there was significant damage to the cowling and forward fuselage. There were no injuries to the pilot or passenger.

C-FIVX, un Boeing 777-300 exploité par Air Canada était en préparation pour effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Après le refoulement de l’aéronef, l’équipage a demandé au contrôleur de retourner à la porte d’embarquement, car un agent de bord a subi une blessure à la tête lorsqu’un bagage est tombé de son compartiment. L’agent de bord n’a pas pu continuer de remplir ses fonctions.

C-FKLF a privately registered Piper J3C-65 was conducting a local recreational flight from Lacombe Aerodrome (CEG3), AB, with only the pilot onboard. During the take-off roll on Runway 35, directional control of the aircraft was lost. The aircraft swerved left and right of the runway centerline, ultimately departing the west side of the runway. The aircraft travelled across the grass area and made contact with the ditch and the airport perimeter fence. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The pilot was uninjured.

C-FJQL, an Air Canada Airbus A321-211 was operating flight ROU1873 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Daniel Oduber Quirós International Airport (MRLB), Costa Rica. During cruise, a cabin crew member became unwell and was unable to continue their duties. Duties were redistributed amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-GJZA, un Dehavilland DHC-8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l’indicatif JZA7969, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport, ON (CYTZ). Juste après le décollage environ à 2000 pieds, l’équipage a ressenti des vibrations au travers de la structure de l’aéronef. Les passagers ont également ressenti les vibrations. Par mesure de précaution, l’équipage a décidé d’effectuer un demi-tour et revenir atterrir à CYUL après avoir brûlé du carburant. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence au centre de contrôle aérien et les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été mis en alerte. L’aéronef a atterri sans encombre.

C-GUPK, an Air Canada Airbus A220 was operating flight AC747 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA, U.S. On approach to RWY28R at 2700 feet, a TCAS RA was received by the flight crew due to an aircraft infringing the parallel approach centreline. The crew performed a go-around and landed without further incident.

C-FERF, un Piper PA-23-250 exploité par Cargair Ltée, effectuait un vol d’entraînement local selon les règles de vol aux instruments simulé depuis l’aéroport de Montréal / MET, QC (CYHU) avec un instructeur et un élève-pilote à bord. La séance d’entraînement terminée, l’équipage revient à CYHU et effectue l’approche RNAV Piste 06L. Une fois l’arrondi complété et au moment habituel du toucher des roues, l’instructeur constate que l’hélice de droite touche le sol. Ce dernier coupe l’arrivée de carburant et ferme les moteurs. L’avion termine son atterrissage sur le ventre et s’immobilise sur la piste. Les occupants n’ont pas été blessés et ont pu évacuer l’aéronef sans difficulté. Aucune défaillance du train d’atterrissage n’a été signalée et l’événement est relié à un oubli de l’équipage d’abaisser le train d’atterrissage lors de l’approche.

C-GZSL, un Beech C23 exploité par le Collège d’enseignement général et professionnel de Chicoutimi, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) avec seul un élève-pilote à bord. L’élève-pilote a effectué une approche pour la piste 14 à l’aérodrome de Charlevoix, QC (CYML). Au moment de poser les roues, l’aéronef a rebondi et l'élève-pilote a remis de la puissance. L'aéronef a effectué d'autres rebonds et la roue de nez s'est brisée, l'hélice a touché le sol et l'aéronef a dévié vers la gauche et est sorti de piste. L'aéronef s'est immobilisé et l'élève-pilote, non blessé, a pu évacuer sans difficulté. La piste a été fermée jusqu'à ce que l'aéronef ait été déplacé.

C-GRDY, a privately registered Cessna 180 was conducting a flight from Melfort/Miller Field Aerodrome (CJZ3), SK, to Yorkton Regional Airport (CYQV), SK. While conducting a landing on Runway 22 at CYQV with a 6-knot crosswind, the aircraft's tail swung around to the left on touchdown causing the left wing to contact the runway, the left-wing fuel tank to rupture, the left landing gear to fail, and the propeller to strike the ground. The fuel tank leak was plugged and remaining fuel contained by airport rescue and firefighting. There was no post-accident fire. Both the pilot and the passenger were able to exit the aircraft with no injuries.

C-FVLZ, un Boeing 787-9 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA864 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Londre/Heathrow, Royaume-Uni (EGLL). Lors de la montée initiale, l'équipage a eu un message EICAS indiquant un problème avec le système hydraulique C. L'équipage a complété les listes de vérification applicables et effectué un retour à CYUL sans encombre. Les services d'urgence ont inspecté l'appareil au sol et celui-ci a été remorqué à la barrière.Une inspection de maintenance a révélé une conduite déconnectée au niveau de la pompe hydraulique C1.

C-GZEH un Dassault Alpha Jet exploité par Top Aces, effectuait le vol Cheta 12 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Thunder bay, ON (CYQT) à destination de l'aéroport de Bagotville ,QC (CYBG) avec seul le pilote à bord. À environ 25 NM au nord-ouest de CYBG, le voyant OIL R s'est illuminé. Le voyant a continué de clignoter alors que le pilote a réduit la puissance du moteur droit au ralenti. Le pilote a alors fermé le moteur par précaution et l'appareil a atterri peu après sans encombre à CYBG. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés. Une inspection de maintenance subséquente à l'évènement a révélé une sonde de pression d'huile défectueuse sur le moteur droit.

C-GKQC, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 operated by Porter Airlines Inc., was conducting flight PTR2637 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON. While cruising at FL240, the aircraft encountered sudden and severe turbulence. The turbulence caused the autopilot to disengage, followed by a brief Vmo overspeed of approximately 5–10 knots and a temporary altitude deviation of about 250 feet. The First Officer assumed manual control, stabilized the aircraft, and returned it to FL240 before re-engaging the autopilot and advising Air Traffic Control (ATC).Two cabin crew members were thrown from their seats and sustained minor injuries. One passenger also sustained a minor injury after striking their head on a ceiling panel. The flight continued to CYQT and landed without further incident.Company maintenance conducted both a Vmo overspeed and severe turbulence inspection. No faults were identified, apart from cosmetic damage to the ceiling panel above the seat of the injured passenger.

C-FZWS, a WestJet Boeing 737-8 was operating flight WS2315 from Cancún International Airport (MMUN), México, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During cruise, a cabin crew member started to feel unwell and was unable to continue their duties. Duties were reassigned amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-FYOS, a privately registered, amateur-built, amphibious float equipped Bearhawk aircraft, was conducting a local flight under visual flight rules from Langley Regional Airport (CYNJ), BC, with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. The flight included 3 stops at lakes with the third stop being 45 minutes in length. While in cruise over Harrison Lake, on the return leg to CYNJ, a minor, intermittent roughness was noticed with the engine (Avro Lycoming O-540-EXP) and the pilot decided to divert to Chilliwack Airport (CYCW), BC. On the downwind leg at CYCW, the landing checks were completed, the landing gear was lowered, the power was reduced, and the prop was set to full fine. On final approach, when the pilot set the mixture to full rich, the engine completely lost power. An attempt to restart the engine was made without success. The pilot tried to retract the landing gear but it could not be retracted prior to landing. The pilot conducted a forced landing onto a farmer's field approximately 1 nautical mile northeast of CYCW. The aircraft touched down in a nose high attitude, at minimum speed, nosed over, and came to rest inverted. The 2 occupants exited the aircraft. Emergency services attended the scene, and the aircraft occupants were transported to the local hospital. The passenger received minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The aircraft will be assessed for repair. The cause of the engine power loss is unknown.

C-FDDG, a De Havilland Dash 8-100 operated by PAL Aerospace Ltd. was conducting flight SPR08 from Gander International Airport (CYQX), NL, on a DFO patrol. After departure the flight crew received an indication of a Hydraulic system No. 2 lost quantity. The quick reference handbook was completed, and the decision was made to divert to St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL, which was the location of a maintenance base. A manual landing gear extension was completed, and the aircraft landed without further incident. The aircraft was towed from the runway by maintenance and after post occurrence it was discovered a pressure switch was found faulty and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FWEW, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 was operating as flight WEN3295 under instrument flight rules, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. During takeoff from CYVR, the flight crew received an inboard anti-skid caution light and rejected the takeoff at a speed below 50 knots. The flight crew declared a Mayday, taxied off the runway, and returned to the gate.Maintenance found the inboard anti-skid inoperative, and the item was recorded in accordance with the minimum equipment list. The aircraft was returned to service.

N49RP, a privately registered Piper PA-18 Super Cub, was conducting a flight from Beaver Creek Aerodrome (CYXQ), YT, to Discovery Yukon Lodgings, Koidern, YT, with only the pilot onboard. During the landing roll at Discovery Yukon Lodgings, the aircraft drifted to the left side of the grass runway, and the left wing made contact with tall vegetation which pulled the aircraft into the bush and trees. The aircraft received substantial damage but there were no injuries.

C-GYGU, an Airbus A321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA174 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. C-GJEN, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore was conducting flight WEN3217 from CYEG to Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB. Both aircraft departed Runway 30 in sequence. During departure, lateral separation was reduced to 2.8 NM when 3.0 NM is required. The aircraft were subsequently vectored to maintain the required lateral separation and both aircraft continued to their destinations.

N812GS, a Pilatus PC-12 business aircraft was conducting flight from Reykjavik Airport (BIRK), Iceland, to CFB Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL, for a fuel stop. On the landing the aircraft ballooned due to overcontrol of the elevator resulting in a secondary balloon with the nose gear and prop striking the runway and then the main landing gear. The flight crew used reverse and then taxied off the runway to park. The flight crew noted the blade tips had been curled. Company operations and maintenance were contacted and the aircraft propellor and engine will be replaced.

C-FKWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-402, was operating as flight WEN3417 from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. During the descent phase the flight crew observed the first officer's windshield crack. They declared a PAN PAN and continued the descent to CYWG. Once on the ground, the aircraft taxied to the gate followed by aircraft rescue and firefighting and was inspected. The windshield was replaced by the operator's maintenance and released to service.

C-GRTL, an Aerospatiale AS 350 BA operated by 1000367123 Ontario Ltd. (dba Heli-Worx Aviation), was conducting fire suppression work from Savant Lake FAB (48.35 NM ENE of Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON), to SLK003 (49.94 NM NE of CYXL). While suppressing a spot fire at SLK003, the pilot unintentionally pushed the external load release and the bucket disconnected from the aircraft. The bucket was approximately 100 feet from the ground and no ground personnel were injured. There was no damage to the aircraft.

G-ZBJB, un Boeing 787-8 exploité par British Airways, effectuait le vol BAW6NC selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Londre/Heathrow (EGLL) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Lors de l'approche, a 11NM au NE de CYUL, l'équipage a déclaré un état d'urgence (Pan Pan), invoquant des problèmes de radar altimètre. L'avion s'est posé en toute sécurité sur la piste 24R à 23h58. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GGGA, a Beech 1900 operated by Propair was conducting flight 109443 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Val-d'Or Airport (CYVO), QC. During the climb, the flight crew detected an unusual smell in the aircraft. An emergency was declared, and the crew elected to return to CYTZ, where the aircraft landed uneventfully with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by. Maintenance later determined that the source of the smell was a failure of the flap motor, which had produced smoke.

C-GTXM, a Top Aces Inc Learjet 35A, aborted its takeoff in North Bay Airport (CYYB), ON, on Runway 26 at 71 knots when a parachutist was observed running across the runway. A NOTAM for parachute activity for the Canadian Armed Forces Skyhawks had expired at 2030Z. C-GTXM taxied to hold short of Runway 26 at 2035Z. While listening to North Bay Radio frequency, it was heard and observed that all parachute jumpers were on the ground at approximately 2037Z. At 2040Z, C-GTXM took the runway. At approximately 71 knots and 900 feet down Runway 26, the Pilot Flying (PF) observed a human looking obstruction on the right side of the runway (north side of Runway 26) and called for the abort. The Pilot Monitoring (PM) observed a black object, which initially looked like wildlife, and both PF and PM carried out the aborted takeoff actions, with the PM making a radio call to North Bay Radio that they were aborting for a parachutist on the runway. The aircraft aborted the takeoff, having come to a stop by taxiway E (3400 feet down Runway 26). The parachutist was observed continuing to run across Runway 26 from north to south, a few thousand feet in front of C-GTXM. C-GTXM carried out the Approved Flying Manual procedure for Aborted Takeoff between 40 and 80 knots (hot brake check and 20 min wait) without further incident and continued the mission at 2102Z.This incident has been reported to the Canadian Armed Forces, 3 Wing Flight Safety Office.

C-GLQL, a Porter Airlines Inc. De Havilland DHC-8-400, was operating as PTR2942 from Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS), MA, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. Upon landing on Runway 26 in CYTZ, the aircraft experienced a bounced landing during which the “Touched Runway” warning light activated. The crew initiated a go-around from the balked landing. The warning light was noted during the initial climb, and a return to CYTZ was coordinated with ATC. A second approach was discontinued after the aircraft passed the touchdown zone limit (1000-foot touchdown markers). A third approach and landing was completed without further incident. Following the flight, company reporting obligations were completed by the crew and the defect was entered in the Journey Logbook. Upon initial evaluation by Porter maintenance the Touched Runway (tailstrike) Sensor was found to have sheared off. The sensor unit and associated fairing have been replaced. Flight Data Recorder (FDR) analysis indicated a 2.87G landing, triggering a Level 2 hard landing inspection. The hard landing inspection was completed with no additional findings. The aircraft has returned to service.

C-GNWM, a Cessna 550 operated by Beaver Air Services (dba Missinippi Airways), was conducting IFR flight MCB410-M from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. During the flight, a fuel imbalance condition occurred two times, requiring the flight crew to cross-feed fuel twice in order to correct the imbalance. While in the descent, the first officer noted another fuel imbalance, but the pilot-in-command opted not to cross-feed fuel during the descent. While on a visual approach, the pilot-in-command noticed a dust-like odor, followed by a momentary low fuel indication, then selected the fuel boost pumps ON. Shortly after, the first officer noticed the odor, which had become stronger. After the airplane had landed in CYWG and was taxiing, white smoke was observed in the flight deck. The pilot-in-command elected to evacuate in front of a hangar. All occupants safely exited the airplane and there were no injuries. Fuel was observed dripping from the #1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada JT15D-4). The operator's maintenance found the #1 engine fuel pump was leaking and it was replaced. Engine oil was found in the #1 engine exhaust cone. The operator's maintenance noted that it was over-serviced, and 1.5 litres of oil was removed. A subsequent test flight was performed but was unsatisfactory; noting an odor of smoke was still present. Further inspection found the #1 engine coalescer (condenser) in the water separator for the air cycle machine was contaminated with oil and was replaced. A second test flight was performed satisfactorily, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FYHL, a Bell 427 operated by Prairie Helicopters Inc., was conducting firefighting support operations from Rennie Fire base, MB to Whiteshell Provincial Park, MB. While conducting a toe-in hover landing in order to drop off two wildland firefighters at a rock outcropping site on the upper northwest corner of Mantario Lake, MB, the pilot heard a loud continuous noise while the aircraft was being unloaded. The helicopter then pitched nose down and the tail moved up and to the right. The pilot corrected down and to the left and the back of the skids contacted the rock surface. The pilot then rolled off the throttle, closed the two emergency fuel valves and pushed the cyclic forward and left. Once settled on the rock surface the aircraft slid backwards where it hit a rock ledge and came to rest. The aircraft was slung out of the location back to the operator's base for inspection.During inspection by the operator's maintenance, it was found that the aircraft experienced a blade strike and required a sudden stoppage inspection.

C-GTUJ, un biplan de construction amateur Stolp SA750 Acroduster Too d'immatriculation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue de l'aérodrome de Neuville, QC (CNV9) à destination de l'aérodrome de St-Lambert-de-Lauzon (CST7) avec seul le pilote à bord. À environ 5.7NM de son point de départ, l'aéronef s'est écrasé dans un boisé. Le pilote a été blessé. Il n'y a pas eu d'incendie. Des témoins ont rapporté avoir entendu le moteur fonctionner de façon intermittente juste avant l'écrasement. L'épave était recouverte d'huile moteur et l'hélice n'affichait pas de signes caractéristiques de rotation au moment de l'impact.

C-FKSV, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC986 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), Dominican Republic. On approach, a cabin crew member sustained an injury and was unable to continue their duties.

N782TW, a Ameristar Air Cargo Incorporated McDonnell Douglas DC-9, was operating as AJI9202 from Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport (PANC), AK, under instrument flight rules, to Great Falls International Airport (KGTF), MT, with 2 crew on board. While in cruise at flight level (FL) 340 the aircraft suffered a loss of cabin pressurization with the cabin altitude reaching 25 000 feet. The crew completed the Cabin Altitude Warning / Rapid Decompression checklist, informed air traffic control, and initiated an emergency descent. The crew managed to re-establish sufficient cabin pressure, manually, at FL230 where they leveled off. The crew elected to divert to Glacier Park International Airport (KGPI), MT, where they landed without further incident. There were no injuries.The aircraft was flown, with a restricted altitude, to Detroit Willow Run Airport (KYIP), MI, where company maintenance found that the right air condition pack was unserviceable.

C-GWEU, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was operating as flight WEN3591, under instrument flight rules, from Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies Airport (CYXC), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During final approach into CYVR, the flight crew observed that the right main landing gear did not indicate green, red, or amber. The flight crew executed a missed approach, actioned the applicable checklist, and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without further incident on the second approach. Airport emergency vehicles met the aircraft and inspected the landing gear. The aircraft then taxied to the gate under its own power. There were no injuries. Company maintenance found that both light bulbs at the right-hand main landing gear green indication light socket were burnt out. The bulbs were replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GARJ, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was operating flight ROU1602 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL, U.S. During the descent, passing through approximately 6300 feet on the CUDDA 3 arrival, the flight crew received a TCAS TA followed by an RA. Flight crew complied with the TCAS RA command, while ATC simultaneously issued a climb instruction to 7000 feet. According to ATC, the conflict was caused by a medevac aircraft that had deviated from its assigned altitude. ROU1602 continued to destination and landed without further incident.

C-FOEG, a Bombardier BD-700-2A12 (Global 7500) was operating as Aurora Jet Partners from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Dallas Love Field Airport (KDAL), TX, U.S. During taxi into US Customs ramp at KDAL, the right winglet of C-FOEG contacted the trailing edge of the left wingtip of N650FX, Gulfstream G650, which was parked on the ramp.

C-FIVK, an Air Canada Boeing 777-233LR was operating flight AC43 from Indira Gandhi International Airport (VIDP), India, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to continue their duties. Aircraft was diverted to Schiphol International Airport (EHAM), Netherlands.

C-GNRT, un Eurocopter AS350-B2 exploité par Nunavik Rotors Inc, effectuait un vol local d'évaluation selon les règles de vol à vue à partir de l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) avec 1 pilote évaluateur et un jeune pilote à bord. Lors de la simulation d'une autorotation, le pilote évaluateur a tenté de ralentir l'aéronef à l'approche du sol en en remettant les gaz afin que le jeune pilote conclue l'autorotation en vol stationnaire sans nécessiter de contact avec le sol. Ne sentant pas de réponse du moteur (Avco Lycoming LTS-101-700D2) tel que prévu, le pilote évaluateur a repris les commandes et a atterri l'aéronef avec très peu de RPMs rotor restants. Au contact du sol, le rotor principal a contacté et endommagé la poutre de queue ainsi que la tête rotor. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-FEAI, un De Havilland DHC8-314 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE802 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Kuujjuarapik, QC (CYGW), avec 3 membres d'équipage et 39 passagers à bord. Au moment du refoulement, le personnel au sol n'avait pas relié la barre de traction au train d'atterrissage avant de l'appareil, celle-ci est entrée en contact avec le bras oscillant inférieur et l'a endommagé. Les passagers ont été débarqués, et le vol annulé. Le bras oscillant inférieur du train avant a été subséquemment remplacé et l'appareil retourné en service.

C-FBSX, a Cessna 414 operated by First Base Solutions Inc., was conducting a local training flight from Brampton-Caledon Airport (CNC3), ON. Approximately 25 minutes into the flight, at an altitude of 9000 feet, the pilot observed significant oil leakage from the right engine (Teledyne Continental, TSIO-520-NB). The flight was under flight following, and the pilot advised ATC of the engine issue and requested an immediate return to CNC3. During the return, the oil leakage decreased; the pilot reduced power on the affected engine but did not shut it down. Airport personnel requested aircraft rescue and firefighting be on standby for the landing.

C-FMOD, a Diamond DA 42M-NG operated by Trans Capital Air Ltd., was en route from Kingston Airport (CYGK), ON, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. During the flight, the pilot observed a fuel leak from the right engine. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft continued to CYTZ, where it landed uneventfully with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by. Maintenance determined that the fuel leak was caused by a failed fuel fitting. Fuel fitting was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOIK, an Air Transat Airbus A321-271NX was operating flight TSC153 from Jorge Chávez International Airport (SPJC), Peru, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Approximately one hour prior to arrival at CYYZ, one of the pilots became incapacitated. No impact on flight safety as there were 3 pilots on board.

C-FTAD, a privately registered, Schleicher ASH 31 Mi powered glider, was on a local flight from Invermere Aerodrome (CAA8), BC, with only the pilot onboard. While climbing through approximately 500 feet above ground level after takeoff, the aircraft’s engine (Austro Engine IAE50RAA) shut down unexpectedly when the secondary fuel pump had been turned off. The pilot restarted the engine and noticed fuel quantity now indicated the fuel tank was empty. Shortly afterwards the engine stopped again, and the pilot smelled smoke. The pilot immediately turned the aircraft back to the aerodrome, engaged the propeller lock to reduce drag, and landed on Runway 15. The cockpit then started filling with smoke, so the pilot evacuated the aircraft and saw flames engulfing the aircraft. Persons nearby attempted to use handheld fire extinguishers to put out the fire, but the extinguishers had little effect. A nearby water truck was able to extinguish the flames, and a firetruck arrived about 10 minutes later. The aircraft engine and fuselage section around the engine sustained severe fire damage. No injuries were reported.

C-GCIQ, a Government of Canada, Department of Transport Bell Textron Canada Limited 429 helicopter was being operated as flight CTG434, under visual flight rules, from Campbell River Airport (CYBL), BC, to a remote mountainous location near Tahsis, BC, with the pilot and 2 passengers on board. While approaching the unprepared, snow-covered landing site, the helicopter was using high power to arrest the descent rate. A run on landing was conducted and during touchdown the helicopter broke through the snow and the pilot heard an unidentified noise. After shutting down, the pilot inspected the aircraft and found damage to all four main rotor blades. The main rotor blades had come in contact with the upper wire strike blade. There were no injuries. The ELT did not activate.A second helicopter was sent to retrieve the occupants while maintenance staff began planning repairs.

C-FTIR, a Canadian North ATR 42-500 was operating as flight ATK676 from Cambridge Bay Airport (CYCB), NU, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. During cruise the flight crew noted a "Side Windows Anti-Icing Fault" followed by smoke emanating from the base of the tiller. The side windows anti-icing was selected off and the smoke dissipated. The flight crew actioned the smoke checklist and the anti-icing side windows fault checklist. The flight landed safely in CYZF with no further issues. An emergency was not declared, nor was priority handling requested.Following the flight the maintenance team found that a relay and associated wiring for the side window anti-ice were burned, and another relay showed signs of heat damage. The electrical components and wiring were replaced and tested. The aircraft was released back into service.

C-FGHZ, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was operating flight AC90 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Guarulhos International Airport (SBGR), Brazil. In cruise, the crew received multiple EICAS messages with lost indications of brakes and tire pressure on wheel units 3/7. The crew declared a PAN PAN and landed on runway 10L. Aircraft rescue and firefighting completed a landing gear inspection, and the aircraft taxied to the gate with no issues. Maintenance replaced the brake system control unit, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GUWX, a Campbell Helicopters Ltd. Bell 212 was operating on a local fire suppression mission to wildfire SWF-083, approximately 100 NM NW of the Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB. The staging area for the SWF-083 wildfire was established in the vicinity of the wildfire in a muskeg area adjacent to a watercourse and swamp. After finishing a bucket cycle, the pilot proceeded to set the Bambi bucket down at the staging area to pack it up and wait for the arriving fire crew. As the pilot set the bucket down and was laying out the long-line while maneuvering to land, the pilot felt an impact from the tail and the helicopter entered an un-commanded turn. The pilot rolled both throttles to idle and the helicopter settled to the ground. The engines were shut down and the helicopter secured before the pilot exited the helicopter. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured. The helicopter received significant damage as the tail rotor had departed and struck the tail cone and right horizontal stabilizer. Examination of the Bambi bucket revealed that the tail rotor struck near the top of the bucket.

C-FJQD, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was operating flight ROU1841 from Grantley Adams International Airport (TBPB), Barbados, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, a cabin crew member sustained an injury, and their duties were redistributed amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-FGSQ, a Sea to Sky Air Limited Cessna C172M departed Squamish Municipal Airport (CYSE), BC, on a local sightseeing flight, under visual flight rules, with the pilot, 3 adults, and one infant on board. The pilot initiated the takeoff by applying the brakes and adding power to check the engine parameters. The brakes were released, and the aircraft began the take-off roll. Once airborne, at approximately 50 feet above ground level, the engine (Avco Lycoming, O-320-E2D) was heard to make a popping sound and engine power was lost. The aircraft descended back onto the runway and subsequently bounced. The pilot landed, set the flaps to full down, and applied the brakes. The aircraft came to a full stop approximately 75 metres off the end of the paved surface. There were no injuries.The aircraft had visual damage to the main landing gear legs. The aircraft is grounded and will be inspected to determine the extent of the damage.

C-GPOJ, a De Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines, was operating as PVL2594 from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL. While enroute in cruise, the flight received indications that the number 1 hydraulic system fluid quantity was decreasing. The flight crew consulted with company operations and discussed the possibility of diverting to Gander International Airport (CYQX), NL, where a longer runway was available in case flaps became unavailable. At about 47°33' N, 054°17' W (62 NM west of CYYT) the flight crew declared an emergency and coordinated the diversion to CYQX with ATS. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYQX using flaps 15.Maintenance personnel discovered minimal signs of hydraulic fluid loss. The number 1 engine driven pump inlet line was found to be weeping fluid; the fluid line was torqued, and the hydraulic system was bled of excess air. It is suspected that air in the number 1 hydraulic system resulted in the low fluid quantity indication experienced in flight.

C-FVLZ, un Boeing 787-9 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA864 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de London Heathrow, United Kingdom (EGLL). Peu après le décollage, lors de la montée initiale, l'équipage a noté un problème avec un des 3 systèmes hydrauliques. Une urgence mécanique (PAN PAN) a été déclarée. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre après quelques longs circuits d'attente.

C-GVQA, un Cessna 172K sur flotteurs en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le lac Gravel, Qc à destination du Lac-des-Écorces (CTV2) Qc. Au moment de l'amerrissage, le pilote a percuté la surface du lac et a perdu la maitrise de l'aéronef causant des dommages aux flotteurs et aux ailes. L'appareil a terminé sa course en se renversant dans l'eau. Le pilote a évacué et n'a pas subi de blessure

CS-TXA, an Airbus A321-251NX-LR (A321neo) aircraft operated by TAP Air Portugal was conducting flight TAP211 from Porto/Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport (LPPR), Portugal, to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ. During cruise, at FL340, the cabin crew noticed a strong smell coming from the forward galley area. A few minutes later the same smell was also noticed in the aft galley. The flight crew was advised, who carried out the SMOKE/FUMES/AVNCS SMOKE checklist. At about 47°50' N, 048°00' W the flight crew declared an emergency with ATS and coordinated a diversion to St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL. During descent the flight crew donned oxygen masks and applied the FUMES/SMOKE REMOVAL checklist procedure. The aircraft landed at CYYT without further incident.Maintenance personnel inspected both engines, the APU, environmental packs, as well as all galley equipment and lavatory waste baskets. Operational runup checks were carried out on APU and both engines. The smell fault could not be duplicated, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GVVI, a privately registered amateur-built American Affordable Aircraft (Pro Composite) Vision was operating on a local flight from Calgary/Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB. The pilot had concluded a 2-hour engine break-in flight and was attempting to land at CYBW on Runway 26. The winds were 300° True at 12 gusting 17 knots. The pilot made 3 attempted landings with associated overshoots as the aircraft floated, and the pilot was unable to land on the available runway. During the fourth landing attempt, the aircraft once again floated and tracked to the right of the runway's paved surface. The aircraft touched down on the grass and continued where it then struck a drainage ditch and then came to rest. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured. The aircraft received significant damage, and the 406 MHz ELT activated.

C-FPQB, an Air Canada Boeing B787-9 was operating flight AC35 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Brisbane International Airport (YBBN), Australia. In descent from 16 000 feet, the plane encountered turbulence on the TEBOT arrival and two cabin crew members sustained minor injuries and were unable to continue their duties.

C-GAMN, an AAA Aviation Cessna 172K operated by Acadia College, departed Langley Regional Airport (CYNJ), BC, under visual flight rules (VFR) for a student navigation trip returning to CYNJ with only the pilot on board. The flight planned route was a round trip that followed the VFR flight path to Princeton Aerodrome (CYDC), BC, and returned via the same route. The en route clouds were slightly lower than forecasted and, when the student arrived overtop of Hope Aerodrome (CYHE), BC, the pilot elected to return to CYNJ. Shortly after turning back, the pilot noted smoke in the cockpit that appeared to be coming from the floor area on the left side of the cabin accompanied with the mild smell of burning plastic. The pilot landed intact in a field on the north side of the Fraser River, 12 nautical miles northeast of Chilliwack Airport (CYCW), BC. Once on the ground, the pilot egressed the aircraft and used the fire extinguisher in an attempt to douse the flames. It had little effect, and the aircraft began to burn. The pilot returned to the aircraft to turn on the emergency locator transmitter (ELT) and then moved to a far end of the field. The Canadian Mission Control Centre (CMCC) received the ELT signal. The pilot contacted 911 and first responders attended the scene. The pilot suffered minor injuries. The aircraft was destroyed.

N627AS, an Alaska Airlines Incorporated Boeing 737-790, was operating as cargo only flight ASA7040, under instrument flight rules, from Seattle–Tacoma International Airport (KSEA), WA, to Juneau International Airport (PAJN), AK. Shortly after levelling at an altitude of approximately 40 000 feet above sea level (ASL), the aircraft cabin altitude warning annunciation illuminated, and the accompanying warning horn sounded. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks and accomplished the quick reference checklist (QRC). The flight crew then declared an emergency with air traffic control (ATC) and requested a lower altitude. A rapid descent to 10 000 feet ASL was made approximately 17 nautical miles southeast east of Comox Airport (CYQQ), BC. The flight then diverted back to KSEA and landed without further incident. No injuries were reported.Maintenance personnel accomplished a built-in test (BIT) check of the No. 1 Digital Cabin Pressure Control System (DCPCS) which revealed fault code 107. The aircraft’s aft outflow valve assembly and cabin pressurization controller module were replaced to rectify the fault. Operational checks were performed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GZOP, a privately registered Cessna A185F on amphibious floats was landing at the Edmonton/Cooking Lake Aerodrome (CEZ3), AB. The pilot was conducting a landing on Runway 10 with a prevailing southerly wind. The aircraft touched down on the north side of the runway on the right-hand float. The aircrafts right float bounced off the runway and the right wing continued to rise as the aircraft departed the paved surface of the runway. The left wing contracted the infield as the pilot applied full power. The aircraft continued to veer northward, impacting a fence and tree on the airport's perimeter, where the aircraft came to rest in a drainage ditch, facing south. There was a post impact fire. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was seriously injured and was extricated from the aircraft by first responders. The pilot was subsequently medevaced by helicopter to a nearby hospital. The aircraft was destroyed in the post impact fire.

N797UA, a United Airlines Boeing 777-222(ER) operating flight UAL194 from San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA, to Munich International Airport (EDDM), Germany. While in cruise about 5 1/2 hours into the flight (at 53°28' N, 063°52' W), the first officer experienced symptoms of food poisoning. The international relief officer (IRO) was called up from the crew rest bunk to take over the first officer's responsibilities. A decision was made to divert to Washington/Dulles International Airport (KIAD), VA. A medical emergency was declared, and the diversion was declared with ATS. The aircraft landed at KIAD without further incident.

C-GBHY, an Air Canada Airbus A319-114 was operating flight ROU1823 from Cancún International Airport (MMUN), México, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise at FL370, the flight crew received an ECAM alert indicating AIR ENG 2 BLEED ABNORM PR, accompanied by fluctuating cabin temperatures and intermittent PACK 2 faults. Initial troubleshooting cleared the alert. To further assess the issue, the crew reduced the aircraft's Mach number. Following the power reduction, engine 2 failed to respond to subsequent thrust commands, remaining limited to approximately 50% N1. This was accompanied by significant airframe vibrations and a decay in airspeed. A Mayday was declared, and during the descent, the crew was able to restore normal engine performance by executing the compressor stall procedure for engine 2. The emergency was cancelled and the flight continued to CYYZ where it landed without further incident. Following occurrence, the PRV was removed and replaced with a serviceable unit. Subsequent serviceability tests were conducted with satisfactory results. It is suspected that bleed configuration at high altitude induced the compressor stall event.

C-GCIJ, a Boeing 767-306 (ER) aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd., was conducted flight CJT625 from St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL, to Moncton/Roméo LeBlanc International Airport (CYQM), NB. As the flight crew selected flaps 1 in preparation for the approach at CYQM, they received the LE FLAP ASYM EICAS message. The flight crew requested vectors to carry out quick reference handbook checklist items. The flight crew then declared PAN PAN and carried out the approach and landing on Runway 06 at CYQM without further incident. Maintenance personnel replaced the faulty FLAPS SLAT ELECTRONIC UNIT.

C-FMYW, a Pilatus PC-12/45 operated by Air Bravo Corp, was conducting IFR flight AB1237 from Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON, to Sudbury Airport (CYSB), ON. After departing Runway 25 and climbing through 2700 feet ASL, the flight crew felt a decrease of engine power (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-67B) and observed an abnormally high engine torque indication. The flight crew initiated a turn back for Runway 07 and elected to shut the engine down. The aircraft landed on Runway 07 and came to a stop. There were no injuries. The aircraft's right tire was flat, but there was no other damage to the aircraft.Following the occurrence, the operator's maintenance replaced the engine torque pressure transducer and followed up by conducting an engine performance test.
