The aircraft was then released to service. During subsequent flights over a few days, the aircraft experienced other events, such as an uncommanded reduction in power during taxi, a frozen torque indication on an approach with loss of power lever control for approximately one minute, and, while on the ground, a false torque indication was observed. The operator's maintenance conducted follow-ups after each event. The airframe fuel filter was replaced, and PY lines and bleed air lines rigging was inspected and deemed serviceable. They also replaced the propeller governor, beta carbon block, and torque limiter; followed by engine parameter testing within serviceable limits. After the last event, an engine service facility inspected the engine torque meter system and found debris intermittently blocking the oil bleed port from the torque system. Post-repair engine parameters tested normal and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GDAF, an amateur-built float equipped Murphy Rebel was being operated on a local flight 20 NM NW of Bonnyville Aerodrome (CYBF), AB. The pilot was landing towards the west on Conn Lake and during touchdown directional control was lost. The aircraft subsequently overturned. The pilot was able to egress and stood on the aircraft while rescue was arranged by an eyewitness. The pilot was uninjured. It was noted that the winds were from the southeast at the time of the landing.

An unregistered, privately operated basic ultralight, Kangook RS Ultra (powered para-glider) was conducting a recreational flight approximately 14 NM east of the Grand Prairie Airport (CYQU), AB. While overflying a farmer's field, control was lost and the para-glider struck the ground. The pilot was seriously injured and the para-glider was substantially damaged.

C-FRQM, a Jazz Aviation Embraer ERJ 170-200 was operating flight JZA611 from General Edward Lawrence Logan International Airport (KBOS), MA, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott International Airport (CYUL), QC. During the flight, a cabin crew member became unwell and was unable to perform their duties. The duties were reassigned to another cabin crew member.

C-FMGW, a privately registered Cessna 140X was operating from Clearwater River Aerodrome (CFS8), AB, to Rocky Mountain House Aerodrome (CYRM), AB. As the pilot was completing the preflight of the aircraft, frost was noted on the aircraft, and it was left in the sun with the intent to melt the frost. With the preflight complete, the pilot departed CFS8. The aircraft gained approximately 50-60 feet of height when the right wing dropped, and the aircraft began a turn to the right. The pilot briefly regained control before the right wing dropped again. Subsequently the right wing and right main landing gear contacted trees, and the aircraft collided with terrain. The pilot (sole occupant) was uninjured and was able to egress from the aircraft. The aircraft received substantial damage.

C-FLTS, un Beechcraft A100 exploité par Exact Air sous l’indicatif ET823, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Havre-St-Pierre, QC (CYGV) à destination de l’aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) avec 7 passagers et 2 pilotes à bord. Alors que l’aéronef était en vol de croisière, une odeur de brulé est apparue. L’équipage a remarqué de la fumée qui s’échappait d’une section de la finition du côté gauche dans la cabine. L’avion se trouvait à environ 65 miles marins au sud-est de l’aéroport Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV), l’équipage a amorcé une diversion à destination de CYZV et a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH). Après la fermeture des systèmes électriques non essentiels, la fumée a cessé de s’échapper dans la cabine. L’aéronef s'est posé à CYZV sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni autre dommage. L’inspection après l’envolée a révélé qu’un court-circuit d’un fil d’une lampe de lecture a causé la surchauffe de la finition de cabine, entraînant l’émanation de fumée.

C-FMMX, un Diamond DA 20-C1 exploité par Collège iFly Inc. effectuait un vol d’entraînement selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Int, QC (CYQB) avec un instructeur et un élève-pilote à bord. Après plus d’une heure de vol, l’aéronef se situait à la pointe est de l’Île d’Orléans à 3500 pieds. L’instructeur a demandé au contrôleur aérien de monter à 4500 pieds. Après avoir reçu l’autorisation de monter, l’élève-pilote a appliqué la pleine puissance et le moteur s’est éteint. L’instructeur a pris les commandes et a débuté le diagnostic de la panne. Le moteur a redémarré, mais il n’a pas développé une puissance suffisante pour maintenir l’altitude malgré les différentes interventions de l’instructeur. Ce dernier a déclaré un message de détresse (MAYDAY) au contrôleur aérien et s’est dirigé vers CYQB. Réalisant qu’il ne pourrait pas rejoindre l’aéroport, l’instructeur a évalué la possibilité d’atterrir sur une route de l’île, mais le trafic routier était trop important. Un chemin de terre rectiligne dans un champ a été choisi comme lieu d’atterrissage d’urgence. Lors de l’approche, à environ 400 pieds, un cisaillement de vent positif a interrompu la descente de l’avion sur l’approche. L’instructeur a exécuté une glissade pour que l’avion reprenne la descente. L’avion a touché le sol à la moitié de la longueur du chemin de terre. L’instructeur a appliqué les freins. Le train principal droit s’est enfoncé dans le terrain plus mou et l’aile droite a percuté un arbre provoquant une rotation de l’avion qui a terminé sa course dans un fossé. Les 2 occupants ont évacué l’avion sans difficulté et sans blessure. Les services d’urgence sont arrivés rapidement sur les lieux peu après.

C-GBBX, an Avalo Air Incorporated, privately operated, Cessna Citation 510, departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, for Campbell River Airport (CYBL), BC. During cruise flight at 10 000 feet above sea level, the aircraft master warning light illuminated and the crew altering system (CAS) displayed a left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW615FA) low oil pressure message. The pilot brought the left engine to idle as instructed by the emergency checklist, but the engine oil pressure remained low. Consequently, a left engine precautionary shutdown was performed and the pilot contacted air traffic control to declare a PAN PAN urgency. The flight continued to CYBL and landed without further incident. After landing, the aircraft was towed to a hangar where maintenance personal determined that the left engine oil pressure transducer was faulty. The transducer was replaced, tested satisfactorily, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-IMQI, un paramoteur Kangook AK (Amaruk) effectuait un vol local en exploitation privée à Cap Santé, QC avec seul le pilote à son bord. Après environ 5 minutes de vol, alors qu’il survolait des résidences il a rencontré de fortes turbulences et a eu de la difficulté à garder la maîtrise de l’aéronef. Le régime moteur a été diminué et une descente rapide a été amorcée. Le paramoteur s’est retrouvé sur le toit d’une résidence avant de tomber et percuter une structure en bois dans la cour. Le pilote a subi des blessures graves et l’appareil a subi des dommages importants.

C-GUBF, an Air Transat Airbus A330-243 was operating flight TSC764 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport (LPPR), Portugal. While in cruise, one cabin crew member became ill. Duties were redistributed amongst remaining cabin crew members.

C-GFCH, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A320-214 was operating flight ROU1739 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (KAUS), TX. During descent, passing through approximately 9000 feet on SEWZY6 arrival, flight crew received a TCAS TA for VFR traffic intruding into the arrival path. VFR traffic was reported to have been NORDO and not under ATC control. ATC issued immediate vector and altitude hold to ROU1739. During the maneuver. ROU1739 received TCAS RA: CLIMB. Flight crew complied and informed ATC. Flight continued to KAUS and landed without further incident.

C-FWSE, a WestJet B737-8CT was operating flight WS1426 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Nashville International Airport (KBNA), TN. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated. Duties were reassigned amongst remaining crew members.

C-FKIW, a Westjet Boeing 737-7CT was operating flight WS1232 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL. During cruise, a cabin crew member became unwell. Duties were reassigned amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-FJJG, a privately registered, Piper Aircraft Corporation PA-28-151 (Piper Warrior) departed the Williams Lake Airport (CYWL), BC, on a cross-country flight, under visual flight rules, to Fort St. John Airport (CYXJ), BC, with only the pilot on board. While cruising at approximately 8000 feet above sea level (ASL), above mountainous terrain, the aircraft’s engine (Avco Lycoming O-320-E3D) power output began to decrease. The weather at the time was scattered and broken cloud with mist and an outside air temperature of approximately -2 degrees Celsius. A short time after the initial power decrease, the engine RPM further declined to approximately 800 RPM. The pilot increased the throttle setting but there was no increase in engine power. Within a few minutes after that, the engine stopped. A Mayday call was broadcast on radio frequency 121.5 MHz and the pilot set the aircraft up to conduct a forced approach. The pilot began to glide toward a clearing in the valley below. Ice accumulated on the aircraft’s wings, the airspeed indicator stopped functioning, the aircraft began to lose lift, and the stall horn sounded. The pilot lowered the nose of the aircraft several times to regain lift during the glide, but the aircraft stalled into the treetops short of the intended landing site. During the collision, both wings separated from the aircraft. One wing remained suspended in the trees and the other wing fell to the ground below. The aircraft fuselage impacted the ground a short distance away and came to rest on its left side. The aircraft’s emergency locator transmitter (ELT) did not activate during the accident. The pilot sustained serious injuries. The aircraft was destroyed.The exit door was jammed closed during impact which hindered egress from the aircraft. Additionally, a large suitcase was blocking the right middle window which also hampered the pilot’s attempts at exiting the aircraft. After about an hour, the pilot was able to egress through a rear window that had broken during the accident. The pilot activated the SOS signal on a GPS tracking device which alerted emergency services. Canadian Armed Forces search and rescue and RCMP aircraft and personnel were dispatched to the scene. The site was eventually located, and the pilot was airlifted to hospital for treatment.The investigation found no indication that a component or system malfunction played a role in this occurrence.

C-GYWX, un DHC-8-102 exploité par Air Creebec inc, venait d'effectuer le vol CRQ251 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Val-D'Or, QC (CYVO). Lors du débarquement des passagers à CYVO, une odeur de brûlé a été détecté par l'équipage. Au même moment, de la fumée a été rapporté dans la cabine près de la sortie de secours de gauche par le personnel de bord. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'aéronef a été évacué sans encombre.Il n'y a pas eu de blessés. Une inspection de maintenance a révélé la défaillance d'une lumière de cabine à la rangée 5.

C-GHCP, un ATR 42-300 exploité par Bradley Air Services Ltd. (Canadian North), effectuait le vol AKT823 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport d'Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) à destination de l'aéroport de Qikiqtarjuaq, NU (CYVM) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 11 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée hors de CYFB, alors que l'aéronef atteignait 15000pi, le pilote a remarqué une odeur de brûlé dans le poste de pilotage. Il a alors vu de la fumée émanant du panneau de contrôle de la maintenance du côté gauche. Une urgence a été déclarée (Pan Pan) et l'aéronef a rebroussé chemin. La fumée s'est atténuée et l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre à CYFB avec les Services de sauvetage et de lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs en attente.Une inspection du service de maintenance a révélé une défaillance interne d'un voyant d'alerte sur le panneau de maintenance de gauche.

C-GUFZ, an Air Transat Airbus 330-243 was operating flight TSC574 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Lyon-Saint-Exupéry Airport (LFLL), France. In cruise over the Atlantic, one cabin crew member became incapacitated. Remainder of the flight was operated without further incident.

C-GOIO, an Air Transat Airbus A321 was operating flight TSC434 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Marseille Provence Airport (LFML), France. During flight, a cabin crew member became incapacitated. Minimum crew complement was maintained, and the remainder of the flight was operated uneventfully.

C-GWUX, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-8CT operating as flight WJA1501 was on a flight from Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), CA, U.S., to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. C-FENU, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400 operating as flight WEN3100 was on a flight from Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC, to CYYC. On approach into CYYC, separation reduced to 2.5 NM between WJA1501 and WEN3100 when 3.0 NM was required. WJA1501 was pulled out of the sequence by ATC and vectored for another approach. Both aircraft landed safely with no further issues.

C-FHNC, a North Cariboo Air DHC-8-311 was operating as flight NCB4080 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Primrose Aerodrome (CFN6), AB. During departure, as the aircraft was passing through 10 000 feet ASL, a loss of oil pressure was observed on the #1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW123). The engine was shut down and an emergency was declared. The flight returned to CYYC and landed safely a short time later. The aircraft was inspected by emergency equipment and then taxied to the apron.

C-GUAT, an Air Tindi De Havilland Canada DHC-7-103 was operating flight 805 from Kashechewan Airport (CZKE), ON, to Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON. During taxi to the runway, the aircraft’s right wingtip contacted a light pole, resulting in minor damage to the pole and damage to the right navigation light assembly. A company maintenance engineer on board inspected the wingtip and determined the aircraft was safe to continue to CYQT. This was a non-revenue flight with only company personnel on board.

C-FCXY, a privately owned Mooney M20E, touched down on Runway 32 at Kitchener/Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON. Upon reaching the intersection of Runway 32 and Taxiway Alpha, the aircraft veered left, exited the paved surface, and struck the hold short sign for Runway 26. Both the sign and the aircraft's left wing sustained substantial damage. The pilot was not injured. While on final approach, the pilot was advised by the tower of wind conditions: 340 degrees with gusts up to 16 knots.

C-GTNE, a CorilAir Charters Limited Cessna 185E departed Campbell River Harbour (CAE3), BC, under visual flight rules, for a sight-seeing trip with the pilot and two passengers on board. The flight planned route was a round trip that included three stops, following the traditional mail delivery route in and around the Discovery Islands. The first stop was Refuge Cove on West Redonda Island. The southerly winds outside the cove were strong with whitecaps evident and the pilot elected to land inside the cove where it was more protected. The pilot flew over the intended landing site to assess its suitability. Once complete, the pilot initiated a southbound landing. While on short final, it was reported that the aircraft’s sink rate increased. The aircraft touched down and bounced 4 times on the water. The pilot initiated a go around by applying full power but the aircraft rolled to the left, the left wing struck the water, the aircraft flipped, and came to rest upside down with the cabin submerged. The pilot and both passengers egressed the aircraft. The pilot inflated his personal flotation device (PFD) and assisted the two passengers in inflating their PFDs. One passenger required assistance to remove a headset cord that had wrapped around their neck. Rescue boats were on site quickly and recovered the survivors to shore. A Coast Guard vessel arrived approximately twenty minutes after the accident and transported the occupants to Campbell River. They were transported by ambulance to the local hospital where they were treated for injuries. Both the pilot and the rear passenger had received underwater egress training which contributed to the survivability of the accident. The front passenger was able to follow the direction provided during the passenger briefing and successfully open the right front door. The pilot and front passenger were wearing a lap belt with a shoulder harness and the rear passenger was wearing a lap belt.The electronic locator transmitter (ELT) signal was not received after the impact likely as a result of the antenna being submerged. After the aircraft was recovered onto a barge the following day, an ELT signal was received by the Canadian Mission Command Centre. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GWBX, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-7CT was operating as flight WJA222 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. C-FAFF, a Sunwest Aviation Beechcraft King Air 350, was operating as flight CNK381 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to CYYC. At the RNAV waypoint ADVOX, separation between the aircraft was reduced to 4.4 nm and 700 feet when 5 nm and 1000 feet vertically is required. There was no risk of collision, no TCAS alerts and both flights landed safely.

C-GXIV, an amateur-built Vans RV-14A, was intending to conduct a maiden flight after construction. The pilot made an initial attempt at take-off from Runway 17 at Calgary / Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB. The pilot elected to abort the initial attempt due to lower than anticipated aircraft performance during the take-off roll. The pilot then taxied back to the threshold of Runway 17 and a second attempt was made at 0724 MDT. The aircraft gained approximately 10-20 feet of height during the initial portion of the take-off. The pilot elected to abort the take-off as aircraft performance, once again, was lower than expected. The aircraft descended and contacted the runway, nose landing gear first. The aircraft subsequently bounced back in the air and entered a pilot induced oscillation drifting left of the runway paved surface. The aircraft descended and impacted the grass area on the left side of Runway 17. The right main landing gear was broken free from the aircraft, the nose landing gear collapsed, the prop contacted the ground, and all three prop blades were broken off and the left main landing gear was folded back under the fuselage. The forward fuselage sustained significant damage as well. The pilot received serious injuries but was able to extract himself from the cockpit. There was no post-accident fire.

C-FMEZ, a Boeing 757-2B7 operated by Morningstar Air Express Inc., was conducting flight MAL7062 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise approximately 90 nautical miles east-southeast of Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, the crew noticed a decay in the right engine fuel flow indication. When an input was made to the thrust lever there was no response. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC and requested a diversion back to CYWG. The aircraft landed safety in CYWG. There was no fire. There were no injuries. There was no damage to the aircraft.

C-FDYL, a Harbour Air Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-6-300 (Twin Otter) floatplane was operating as flight HR2169, under visual flight rules, from Vancouver Harbour Water Aerodrome (CYHC), BC, to the Victoria Harbour Water Aerodrome (CYWH), BC. When the flight crew advanced the aircraft’s power levers for takeoff, white smoke came from the overhead power lever control quadrant and spread into the cockpit. The flight crew rejected the takeoff and declared an emergency with air traffic control (ATC). The aircraft was taxied back to the CYHC floatplane dock. The flight crew conducted an emergency shutdown, and the passengers were evacuated without incident. After the aircraft was evacuated, the Fire Department personnel arrived and inspected the aircraft. There was no evidence of fire or smoke. Maintenance personal performed an inspection and found that a recently replaced windshield wiper motor resistor had failed. This was the source of the smoke. No evidence of a fire was found. The air operator's maintenance is following up with the part supplier.

The Jazz Aviation Bombardier CRJ-900 (CL-600-2D24), C-FJFZ, was operating as flight JZA8113 from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT. After takeoff the flight crew received a SKID fault message. The flight crew contacted company dispatch, and the decision was made to return to CYEG, as possible minimum equipment list (MEL) requirements would require maintenance action. ATC was contacted and the flight crew requested ARFF to be on standby. The aircraft made an uneventful landing and ARFF carried out a visual inspection of the aircraft with no issues noted. The aircraft returned to the gate. Company maintenance replaced the #1- and #4-wheel speed transducers and carried out brake bleeding. Further troubleshooting found the LH OB antiskid harness faulty, and the harness was replaced.

C-GOKN, a De Havilland DHC-8-102 operated by Wasaya Airways Limited was conducting flight WSG1401 from Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON, to Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON. Approximately 72 nautical miles southeast of CYXL, one of the attitude and heading reference systems (AHRS) failed. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC and requested a diversion back to CYXL. The aircraft landed safety in CYXL and taxied to the apron. The operator's maintenance re-racked the system to rectify the issue.

C-GMOC, an Alkan Air Ltd. Beech 200 was operating on an air ambulance flight as ANK513 from Dawson City Airport (CYDA), YT, to Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen International Airport (CYXY), YT. While conducting a visual approach to CYXY RWY 14L, the landing gear was selected down. The left landing gear down and locked light did not illuminate. The pilot conducted an overshoot and flew an extended circuit while actioning the quick reference handbook. After following the checklist, the left landing gear down and locked light remained off. The flight crew requested aircraft rescue and firefighting to standby and approached to land on RWY 14L. The aircraft landed uneventfully and there were no injuries. Company maintenance found damaged wiring on the left landing gear down lock switch.

C-GVCS, an Aerospatiale AS332L helicopter operated by Coldstream Helicopters Ltd., was conducting a firefighting flight approximately 35 nautical miles (NM) northwest of Kenora Airport (CYQK), ON, with 2 crew members on board. During the flight, the aircraft experienced an electrical short circuit in the DC master box (1 Alpha). This short circuit caused a number of issues in the aircraft. The aircraft was in the process of executing a water drop on the fire at approximately 250 feet radar altitude. After initial diagnosis of the problem, the crew jettisoned the bucket and long line using the manual emergency release (electrical release not usable with loss of electrical power) and then focused on recovery of altitude and airspeed. They then continued diagnosis and used the emergency range of the number 1 throttle to recover more rotor rpm. The aircraft then turned towards base. After a short period en-route, the crew decided to land the aircraft. They landed in a gravel clearing approximately 9 NM from the fire near a small settlement. There were no injuries. There was no fire. There was no damage to the helicopter.

C-FGXR, un BEECH B200 exploité par Air Nunavut Ltd, effectuait le vol BFF203 selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR), au départ de l'aéroport d'Arctic Bay (CYAB), Nunavut, à destination de l'aéroport d'Iqaluit (CYFB), Nunavut. En descente vers CYFB, le couple (torque, tq) du moteur gauche est tombé à zéro, et le moteur a commencé à fluctuer, indiquant un couple variant entre 0 et 1000 lb/tq. L’équipage a déclaré une situation d’urgence et a procédé à un arrêt préventif du moteur, avant d’atterrir sans encombre sur la piste 16.Une inspection effectuée par le personnel de maintenance a révélé la présence d’eau et de matières étrangères dans le filtre à carburant.

C-GKXT, a Porter Airlines Limited Embraer ERJ 190-400 (E195-E2), was operating as flight POE308, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. N500XX, a Stephenson Air Services LLC, Gulfstream Aerospace Corporation GVII-G500 (Gulfstream G500), was operating from CYVR, under instrument flight rules, to Seattle–Tacoma International Airport (KSEA), WA, U.S. The Embraer was climbing through 6800 feet above sea level (ASL) at a groundspeed of 210 knots. N500XX was climbing in trail with a groundspeed that accelerated to 250 knots as it climbed through 6100 feet ASL behind C-GKXT. The separation between the 2 aircraft was reduced to approximately 2.3 nautical miles (NM) laterally and 700 feet vertically when 3 NM horizontal or 1000 feet vertical separation was required. Separation was re-established shortly afterwards and both aircraft continued to their destinations without further incident.

C-FDHK, a Conair Group Inc. Air Tractor AT-802A was operating flight FGD680 on a fire suppression mission from Lac La Biche Aerodrome (CYLB), AB, to Janvier Aerodrome (CEP5), AB. The aircraft was operating as part of a 4 aircraft group conducting fire suppression activities in the vicinity of Bohn Lake approximately 2 NM east of CEP5. During a water scooping run on the lake, the aircraft experienced a porpoising event and made firm contact with the surface of the lake in a nose high attitude. The pilot brought the aircraft to a stop on the water, jettisoned the water load and then commenced a takeoff with no further issues. Another 5 scooping runs and water dumps were completed before the aircraft returned to Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB, to refuel. After arrival at CYMM the pilot noticed the damage to the empennage and the missing ventral fin. The aircraft is currently undergoing repairs.

C-GPWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-8-402 was operating as flight WEN3307 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Fort St. John Airport (CYXJ), BC. The aircraft was cleared to 9000 feet ASL after departure and was observed by air traffic control climbing to 9300 feet. The aircraft subsequently received a TCAS RA with the WestJet Boeing 737-700, C-GGWJ, which was operating as flight WJA1565 from San Diego International Airport (KSAN), CA, to CYYC. WJA1565 was on arrival to CYYC and descending to 10 000 feet. Separation between WEN3307 and WJA1565 eroded to 700 feet vertically and 0.5 NM horizontally where 1000 feet and 3 NM are required.

C-GWRC, a Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service (STARS) Airbus H145 (MBB-BK 117 D-3) was operating on an air ambulance flight from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to a scene call at Goodfish Lake, 3 NM Northeast of Lamont/Health Care Centre - Heli (CLM4), AB. While en route, in the vicinity of Lamont, the Air Medical Crew (AMC) reported the smell of electrical smoke in the cabin. Moments later the AMC reported heavy smoke in the aft cabin area. The pilot flying actioned the Fire/Smoke emergency checklist. An immediate high-rate descent (2000 FPM) was initiated with a left turn into wind toward Lamont. The pilot declared a MAYDAY emergency and proceeded to land at the Lamont Hospital heliport. While on short final to land, the pilot downgraded the emergency to a PAN PAN urgency. The 2-flight crew and 2 AMC crew members were uninjured. The smoke was found to have originated from medical equipment that was brought onboard by the AMC personnel.

C-GEZO, an Air Transat A. T. Airbus A321 was operating flight TSC685 from Cancún International Airport (MMUN), MX, to Halifax/ Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. Shortly after take-off from MMUN, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue their duties. The minimum required cabin complement was not maintained but the remaining cabin crew reassigned positions. The remainder of the flight continued and landed without further incident.

C-GJRH, a Piper PA-31-350 operated by 2080061 Ontario Inc. (dba SkyCare Air Ambulance), was conducting a VFR flight from Red Lake Airport (CYRL), ON to Winnipeg/St. Andrews Airport (CYAV), MB. During the taxi after landing at CYAV, the right engine (Avco Lycoming TIO-540-J2BD) experienced an uncommanded shutdown. The aircraft was taxied off the active taxiway on power from the left engine and the flight crew attempted to restart the right-hand engine but was unsuccessful. The operator's maintenance subsequently towed the aircraft to the apron.The operator's maintenance conducted an inspection of the right engine but could not identify any issues. The aircraft was ground run and checked serviceable.

Location: São José dos Campos, São Paulo
Summary: C-GHLV, an Air Canada Boeing 767-333 was operating flight ACA7078 from Professor Urbano Ernesto Stumpf International Airport (SBSJ), Brazil, to Jorge Chávez International Airport (SPJC), Perú. On departure at 6000 feet, the crew received a TCAS RA to descend. The crew executed the resolution advisory and reported the TCAS event to ATC.

C-FGGR, un aéronef amphibie de construction amateur de type SeaRey exploité à titre privé, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue de l’aéroport Roland-Désourdy (CZBM), QC, avec le seul pilote à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage, au moment du toucher des roues, la roue de queue s’est détachée, ce qui a provoqué un déport de l’appareil vers la gauche. L’aéronef est alors sorti de piste. Le train d’atterrissage principal gauche s’est arraché et l’appareil a terminé sa course en bordure de piste. Aucun incendie ne s’est déclaré, aucun blessé n’a été signalé, et la radiobalise de détresse (ELT) s’est déclenchée.

C-GUPK, an Air Canada Airbus A220 was operating flight ACA959 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Juan Santamaría International Airport (MROC), Costa Rica. On landing, a cabin crew member reported a minor injury and was unable to continue their injuries. The crew reported a suspected hard landing.A phase 1 inspection was completed with no issues found and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FKWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 was operating as flight WEN3339 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Comox Airport (CYQQ), BC. Shortly after takeoff, during the climb, the flight crew selected the landing gear handle to the up position. As the landing gear retracted the landing gear selector indicated three red lights, accompanied by the landing gear inoperative caution light. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and the main landing gear indication then showed all three lights in both green and amber. The floor indication panel displayed only the right main and nose landing gear as green. The flight crew elected to return to CYEG and declared a PAN PAN emergency. The aircraft landed without further issue and came to rest on the runway, where it was met by aircraft rescue and firefighting before returning to the gate. The aircraft was removed from service for troubleshooting and repair.

C-GFAL, a Beech B200 operated by Fast Air Ltd., was conducting IFR flight PBR625 from Grand Rapids Aerodrome (CJV8), MB, to Pukatawagan Airport (CZFG), MB. During the flight to CZFG, the aircraft experienced a degradation of the aircraft electrical systems. During the descent from 16 000 feet in visual meteorological conditions, the flight crew cancelled their IFR flight plan and, shortly thereafter, the aircraft avionics were reduced to standby instruments only. The flight crew continued the descent to 3500 feet to maintain VMC and an operational decision was made to divert to Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB. While enroute to CYTH, power was restored by following the quick reference handbook procedure for a dual generator failure. When avionics were restored, the flight crew declared an emergency and carried out a normal approach to CYTH. The aircraft landed safely in CYTH. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft's electrical system, including conducting gear swings, flaps extensions, and generator load sharing. No faults were found, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GXFC, a Lockheed 188C operated by Buffalo Airways Ltd., was conducting IFR flight BFL1227 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Hope Bay Aerodrome (CHB3), NU, with 4 crew members on board. On arrival at CHB3, the flight crew conducted an approach to Runway 01 and noticed a glare coming from the sun and overflew the runway to conduct an approach to Runway 19. The aircraft flew the approach, and touchdown was on the Runway 19 centerline. Shortly after touchdown, the aircraft started to swerve off to the east side of the runway and the number 1 propeller impacted a snowbank and the left main gear impacted several runway lights. The flight crew applied rudder and reverse thrust to counteract the swerve and the aircraft returned to the runway centerline. The aircraft taxied to the apron and the flight crew shut down the engines. The operator's maintenance found the number 1 gearbox housing sheared within the engine housing. The number 1 engine, propeller and regulator were replaced. The aircraft was subsequently inspected for a ferry flight to CYZF.

C-GRDU, un Saab SF340B exploité par Pascan Aviation, effectuait le vol PSC702 selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR), au départ de l’aéroport international Jean-Lesage de Québec (CYQB) à destination de l’aéroport métropolitain de Montréal (CYHU), avec à son bord 3 membres d’équipage et 10 passagers. Peu après le décollage de CYQB, l’équipage a perçu une odeur suspecte dans le poste de pilotage. Il a ensuite constaté la présence d’étincelles provenant de l’entrée d’air du moteur droit. Le système antigivrage a alors été désactivé, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence et a amorcé un retour vers l’aéroport de départ.L’appareil a atterri sans incident sur la piste 06 de CYQB à 23 h 04 UTC. Aucun blessé ni incendie n’a été signalé. La piste a été brièvement fermée pour inspection.Une défaillance du système antigivrage de l’entrée d’air du moteur droit a par la suite été diagnostiquée par le personnel de maintenance.

C-GNWU, a Cessna 208B operated by Northway Aviation was conducting a VFR flight from Winnipeg/St. Andrews Airport (CYAV), MB, to Little Grand Rapids Airport (CZGR), MB. During the taxi to the runway, the pilot received an engine fire warning. The pilot stopped the aircraft and shut down the engine in the runup bay. The pilot informed the passengers to evacuate the aircraft. There were no injuries. There was no smoke or fire evident. The operator's maintenance determined it was a faulty engine fire indication.

C-FTBA, an Air Tractor AT-504 operated by Air Andrew Ltd. was conducting a VFR local training flight from Virden (CYVD), MB with 2 crew. When the aircraft touched down on Runway 08, a tail wheel shimmy was detected. The aircraft swerved right, exited the runway surface and ground looped. There were no injuries to the 2 crew. There was substantial damage to the aircraft. The ELT did not activate. The operator's maintenance found no defects with the tail wheel or the tail wheel lock.

C-GFAF, an Air Canada Airbus A330-343 was operating flight AC829 from Copenhagen/Kastrup Airport (EKCH), Denmark, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue their duties.

C-FRJY, a Summit Air Ltd. British Aerospace Avro RJ100 was operating as flight SUT8253 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Ekati Aerodrome (CYOA), NT. At the top of climb, at approximately FL260, during a scan of the engine parameters, the flight crew noted low oil pressure on the #3 engine (Honeywell LF507-1F). The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and performed a precautionary engine shutdown. The aircraft diverted to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, and landed without incident. No emergency was declared and there were no injuries. Company maintenance determined an oil leak at the #4/5 bearing pack (P/N 2-143-930-04). The engine was replaced before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GAZF, a Cargojet Airways Limited Boeing 767-338, was operating as flight CJT2389 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During final approach to CYVR, the aircraft's engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS) displayed a slat caution message (LE SLAT ASYM) as the flight crew selected flaps to position 25. The flight crew conducted a missed approach and retracted the flaps to position F1 to avoid movement of the slats. A hold clearance was obtained from air traffic control (ATC) and the required checklists and calculations were completed. The flight crew discussed contingencies and communicated with company dispatch and maintenance. After burning off excess fuel, another approach to CYVR was initiated and the flight crew requested that aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) equipment to be on standby for the aircraft's landing. The aircraft landed without further incident and taxied off the runway and stopped. ARFF conducted an inspection, and the aircraft then taxied to the ramp with flaps extended and was shut down.Maintenance personnel cycled the aircraft’s flap slat electronics unit (FSEU) circuit breaker then completed FSEU tests using the build-in test equipment (BITE) which revealed no faults. A new FSEU was installed and tested. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GVDG, un pilatus PC-12/45 exploité par Chrono Aviation Inc. sous l'indicatif NDL321 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) à destination de l'aérodrome Pourvoirie Mirage, QC (CPM3). En croisière, environ 45 minutes après le départ, l'équipage a remarqué un problème d'indication des paramètres moteur. Une urgence mécanique (PAN PAN) a été déclarée et le vol a été dérouté vers l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) où il est atterri sans encombre. Il a été confirmé que le problème d’indication ne provenait pas du moteur, mais bien du système d'indication moteur (EIS).

C-GEPG un Boeing 737-8 Max exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA0305 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC à destination de l’aéroport de Vancouver (CYVR), BC. Au moment du refoulement à partir de la barrière 47, le bout de l'aile gauche est entré en contact avec la clôture. L'aéronef est retourné pour inspection des dommages. Une réparation a été effectuée à l'embout d'aile et l'appareil remis en service.

C-GIUB, an Air Canada Airbus A321-211 was operating as flight AC186 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Shortly after take-off, the aircraft’s No. 1 air data inertial reference unit (ADIRU) failed which prevented the flight management system (FMS) from coupling to the autopilot. The flight crew contacted air traffic control (ATC) to declare a PAN PAN emergency and returned to CYVR. The aircraft landed without further incident.After conducting a heavy landing inspection, maintenance personnel replaced the No.1 ADIRU. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-FWEP, a Westjet Encore Ltd., De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd., DHC-8-402 operating flight WEN3190 departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, en route to Prince George Airport (CYXS), AB. Shortly after takeoff, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to a blown tire on the right main landing gear. The flight crew elected to return to CYYC where the aircraft landed safely. There were no injuries.

C-FWZK, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited, Beech 1900D was operating flight PCO1606, under instrument flight rules, from Tofino/Long Beach Airport (CYAZ), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. C-FOEN, a WestJet Encore, De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 was operating flight WEN3576, under instrument flight rules, from Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, to CYVR. During the approach to CYVR, air traffic control (ATC) instructed PCO1606 to turn right to a heading of 050°. The crew read back the ATC instruction correctly but flew a heading of 350°. That heading put the aircraft on a track toward WEN3576 which was on approach to Runway 26L. As a result, the separation between the aircraft was reduced to 2.6 nautical miles (NM) laterally and 800 feet vertically when the required separation was 3 NM laterally/1000 feet vertically. ATC instructed PCO1606 to turn back to an easterly heading and expedited the decent of WEN3576. This action re-established the required separation.

C-GDEW, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was operating as flight WEN3331 under instrument flight rules from Kelowna International Airport (CYLW), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Air traffic control (ATC) had just cleared the flight for takeoff when a cabin crew member became incapacitated. The flight crew declined the take-off clearance and the aircraft taxied back to the gate where the crew member received medical assistance. The flight was cancelled, and the aircraft was repositioned to CYVR.

C-GIUF, an Air Canada A321-211 was operating flight AC983 from Sangster International Airport (MKLS), Jamaica, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While parked at the gate, the aircraft had a fuel system issue and maintenance was in attendance. During the maintenance procedure, a significant fuel leak started. The crew declared a PAN PAN with the ground controller and requested safety vehicles. The crew called for a rapid deplanement and to leave their belongings behind. Passengers exited thru the L1 door. Maintenance inspected the fuel system for the source of the leak and fuel control valve actuator was replaced. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GHPV, an Air Canada Boeing 787-8 was operating flight AC900 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Schiphol International Airport (EHAM), Netherlands. During cruise, the relief pilot became incapacitated and was relieved of their duties for the remainder of the flight.

C-FNVV, an Air Canada Airbus A320 was operating flight AC7023 from Denver International Airport (KDEN), CO, to Dallas Love Field Airport (KDAL), TX. On approach to KDAL, runway 13R, a TCAS RA message was received. AC7023 was at 2000 feet and helicopter traffic was 600 feet below the left side of the aircraft. ATC was advised and AC7023 completed the standard operating procedure for the TCAS. ATC vectored flight for second approach and aircraft landed without further issue.

C-FNOI, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 operating flight ACA967, had landed on Runway 24R at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, and was proceeding to exit at Taxiway C4. Shortly after, C-FIUV, an Air Canada Boeing 777-300 (ER) operating flight ACA890, was issued a takeoff clearance on the same runway. At this time, ACA967 was physically off the runway but was observed by Air Traffic Services personnel in the CYYZ tower still not past the hold short line and not moving away from Runway 24R. As ACA890 was conducting its take-off run, ACA967 was instructed to keep moving clear of the runway and to move past the hold short line. ACA890 was one nautical mile off the departure end of Runway 24R and in the climb when ACA967 was fully across the hold short line. NAV CANADA filed this occurrence as a non-air traffic services operating irregularity but has initiated an investigation into this occurrence.

A7-CGM, a Qatar Executive Gulfstream G650ER (serial number 06A1D1) departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, en route to Ningbo Lishe International Airport (ZSNB), China. Shortly after takeoff at approximately 1108 MDT, the flight crew reported a flap issue and declared a PAN PAN. The flight crew then requested, and obtained permission, to hold in order to burn fuel to reduce weight for a flapless landing back at CYYC. The aircraft landed safely at 1555 MDT. The aircraft was inspected on the runway and then taxied back to the apron. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft.

C-GFJZ, a Bombardier CRJ900, operating as Jazz Aviation LP flight JZA582, had been cleared to FL370 in the vicinity of waypoint NUBER when the flight crew advised ATC they were responding to a TCAS resolution advisory (RA). ATC had previously issued traffic information regarding opposite-direction traffic at their 12 o’clock position, 1000 feet above—UAL958, cruising at FL380. JZA582 reported the traffic in sight and climbed to FL372 in response to the RA. The aircraft passed with 2.7 NM lateral and 900 feet vertical separation.

C-FZQS, an Air Canada Airbus A320-200 was operating as ACA457 from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. On approach to CYYZ Runway 24L at 2000 feet, the landing gear was selected down, and the flight crew saw no associated movement and they received landing gear not locked down ECAM. The crew completed a missed approach to complete the quick reference handbook checklist. During the completion of the checklist the crew received landing gear full locked down indications. The crew declared a PAN PAN emergency and landed on Runway 23 without further incident. The fire trucks did meet the flight on arrival.

C-FEJF, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU, operating as Jazz Aviation LP flight JZA556 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), NY, declared an emergency due to a landing gear issue. The crew elected to return to CYYZ, where the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GHKX, an Air Canada Airbus A330 was operating from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Josep Tarradellas Barcelona-El Prat (LEBL), Spain. During the flight, a cabin crew member was unable to continue their duties due to illness. The remaining cabin crew members assumed their duties.

C-GTCY, an Air Transat A.T. Inc Airbus A321-211 was operating as flight TSC341 from Felipe Carrillo Puerto International Airport (MTLL), Mexico, to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During boarding a cabin crew attendant member became ill. Another flight attendant who was travelling was requested to work the flight, replacing the ill cabin crew member. The remainder of the flight was uneventful.

C-FYNT un DeHavilland DHC-2 MK.I (Beaver) sur flotteurs exploité par ETA Aviation & Cesar Camp du nord Inc. effectuait un vol local depuis la rivière Richelieu devant devant l'hydroaérodrome de St-Mathias, QC (CSV9) avec 2 personnes à bord. Lors de la course au décollage, il y a eu perte de maitrise de l'appareil en roulis. L'aile droite s'est détachée au moment de l'impact avec la surface de l'eau et l'appareil s'est retrouvé renversé sous la surface de la rivière. Le pilote est décédé et l'autre a subi des blessures mineures. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) ne s'est pas déclenchée.

C-GHZN, an Airbus AS350B was being operated by Horizon Helicopters Ltd. on a training flight that originated from the Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen International Airport (CYXY), YT, with 2 pilots on board. After conducting several different training exercises over the course of about an hour, the pilots performed several autorotations to a large clearing. During the fourth autorotation, the aircraft collided with the ground, fatally injuring one of the pilots.

C-FMKZ, a Cirrus SR22, was enroute from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Pembroke Airport (CYTA), ON. The pilot departed without issue from Runway 26. While climbing through 4000 feet, the engine (Teledyne Continental IO-550-N, S/N 1000467) shuddered and began running rough. The pilot reported engine trouble to ATC and initiated a return to the airport.Descending through 2000 feet, the engine shuddered again and failed completely. Realizing he could not reach the airport, the pilot ditched in Lake Ontario near Woodbine Beach. The aircraft’s ballistic parachute was deployed at low altitude, fully inflating just before impact and slowing the descent. The aircraft dropped into the water; the pilot exited onto the wing, called 911, and was rescued by a nearby boat.A preliminary inspection revealed a hole in the top of the engine between cylinders 1 and 2. Both magnetos were broken at the mounting ears, with gear drives found atop the engine. Cylinder 2’s connecting rod was broken and located on top of the engine alongside the piston pin and part of a piston ring.

C-GASB, a De Havilland DHC-8-102 operated by Summit Air Ltd., was operating as flight BF1810 from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, to Fort Hope Airport (CYFH), ON. During the climb out after departure from CYQT, the flight crew observed a decrease in oil pressure on the left-hand engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW120A). The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and preformed a precautionary left-hand engine shut down. The aircraft returned to CYQT and landed without incident.Upon investigation by the operator's maintenance, an oil leak at the inboard line coupling on the oil cooler was found. The O-ring was replaced, ground runs and leak checks were completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FENJ, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Inc. DHC-8-400, was operating as WestJet Encore flight WEN3140 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the take-off roll the flight crew rejected the take-off due to a TCAS FAIL message on the primary flight display. The flight crew informed the tower of the rejected take-off and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft exited the runway and taxied to the gate. Company maintenance completed a Built-in Test Equipment (BITE) check and as a result replaced the bottom transponder antenna. The TCAS system was tested and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GLWJ, a WestJet Encore, De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 was operating flight WEN3590, under instrument flight rules, from Comox Airport (CYQQ), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. C-GGBF, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 was operating flight JZA299, under instrument flight rules, from Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies Airport (CYXC), BC, to CYVR. During the approach to CYVR, air traffic control (ATC) instructed WEN3590 to turn right to a heading of 095°. The crew readback the heading correctly but turned to a southerly heading towards JZA299 that was on the approach for Runway 26L. As a result, the separation between the aircraft was reduced to approximately 1.9 nautical miles (NM) laterally and 800 feet vertically when 3 NM lateral or 1000 feet vertical separation was required. ATC instructed WEN3590 to turn back to an easterly heading and to climb to 4000 feet above sea level (ASL). The required separation was re-established. WEN3590 was then re-sequenced for an approach. Both aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FJKG, a Coywolf Aviation Limited Dassault Falcon 900EX was operating a flight from Milan Rastislav Stefánik Airport (LZIB), Slovakia, to St. John's International Airport (CYYT), NL. Upon reaching cruise altitude, the aircraft experienced a stuck No. 2 engine (Honeywell, TFE731-60-1C) throttle. The crew ran the checklist and contacted company maintenance. The crew elected to divert to Humberto Delgado Airport (LPPT), Portugal. Upon commencing the approach, the No. 2 engine was shut down in accordance with the quick reference handbook. Aircraft landed uneventfully. Upon inspection, pooled water was found in the aircraft belly. It was found that the internal water drains were covered by tape. The water was removed, the tape was removed, and the aircraft was inspected and returned to service.

C-GBHZ, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1878 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Hewanorra International Airport (TLPL), Saint Lucia. During climb and through FL250, the flight crew encountered intermittent faults in the PFD/ND, VHF radios and an intermittent un-commanded roll and yaw and associated ECAMs were transient. Flight crew disconnected the autopilot and requested return to CYYZ from Cleveland ARTCC. Mild un-commanded yaw and roll occurred until the flight descended through 17 000 feet ASL. During descent, FAC 1 ECAM was received and actioned by the flight crew. PAN PAN was subsequently declared as a precaution. Autopilot was reengaged after the un-commanded yaw and roll ceased during descent. The aircraft landed above MLW on CYYZ Rwy 33R with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby. The flight taxied to the gate. Maintenance inspected the aircraft in accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual and found the #1 IDG to be defective. The unit was removed and replaced with a serviceable unit. Subsequent serviceability tests were carried out with satisfactory result.

C-GNCF, a De Havilland DHC-8-314 operated by Perimeter Aviation LP., departed Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, on an IFR flight to Sandy Lake Airport (CZSJ), ON. While on final approach to CZSJ, as the landing gear and flaps were selected "down", the #1 Hydraulic Isolation Valve light flashed, followed by a FLAP POWER caution light. A missed approach was initiated. When the flaps were selected "up" during the missed approach, they remained in the previously selected 15 degrees position. After completing the quick reference handbook (QRH) procedures and assessing fuel and weather, a decision was made to declare a PAN PAN and divert to Thompson Regional Airport (CYTH), MB. The aircraft landed at CYTH uneventfully and was towed to the apron.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and found the rudder damper (P/N 237400-3001) cracked and leaking fluid. The rudder damper was replaced, and the hydraulic pump dry-run operation inspection was completed. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) has been submitted.

C-GTLF, a Victoria Flying Club Cessna 172S was operating a local night training flight, under visual flight rules, from Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, with only the pilot on board. After landing, the pilot taxied from the runway to the parking area on the Victoria Flying Club ramp. While maneuvering to enter the apron, the aircraft struck a fencepost with the leading edge of the wing. A maintenance inspection determined that a wing stringer and part of the wing skin was damaged.

C-FEJF, a Jazz Aviation Embraer 170-200 was operating as JZA540 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to LaGuardia Airport (KLGA), NY. After departing Runway 23 in CYYZ, JZA540 requested to return to CYYZ due to their landing gear being stuck in the down position. Upon selecting the gear up, the landing gear lever disagree emergency light illuminated. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook. After cycling the landing gear, the 3 green lights illuminated. The flight crew elected to return to CYYZ. They did not declare an emergency but did request to have aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby. JZA540 landed Runway 23 without incident at 1345. Once flight crew received all clear from fire services, the aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.

C-FGKH, an Air Canada Airbus A320 was operating as ACA460 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. During the descent the crew received a Cabin Pressure Excess Altitude ECAM Indication. The crew followed the OEB CABIN PRESSURIZATION EXCESS ALT and started an emergency descent from 21 000 to 8000 feet, declaring a Mayday with ATC. The aircraft landed safety in CYOW. After inspection by Air Canada maintenance, the number 1 Cabin Pressure Controller was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FNNW, un Boeing 777-300ER exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA871 et C-GLQD, un DeHavilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Porter Airlines sous l'indicatif PTR2473, effectuaient leur vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, tous les deux à destination de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). ACA871 et PTR2473 étaient en approche finale de la piste 24L, l'espacement a été réduit à 2,7 NM sur le plan horizontal. L'espacement requis était de 3 NM et 1000 pieds. Les 2 aéronefs ont atterri sans encombre.

C-GCHZ, a Bell 206-L1 aircraft operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd. was conducting a post-maintenance test flight from Thompson Regional Airport (CYTH), MB, with the pilot and two maintenance personnel on board. While performing an autorotation RPM check, the pilot inadvertently rolled the throttle past the idle detent and the engine (Allison 250-C30P) shut down. The pilot informed ATC of the situation and continued the autorotation to Runway 24 where the aircraft landed uneventfully. There was a delay to other air traffic while the aircraft was restarted and taxied to the apron.The operator's maintenance department inspected the aircraft, including the throttle idle detent button, and no damage or faults were found.

C-GNCH, a Boeing 737-81D aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines Inc., was conducting flight SWG346 from Fredericton International Airport (CYFC), NB, to Abel Santa Maria International Airport (MUSC), Cuba. Following departure from RWY09 at CYFC on a standard instrument departure (SID), the controller issued an instruction to Turn Left, heading 295, climb FL280, the flight crew readback Heading 295, Climb 280, but subsequently executed a right turn instead of the instructed left turn. As a result, the aircraft was observed to come within less than 5 NM (minimum required lateral separation) of CYR724. The aircraft continued the flight without further incident.

C-GJWO, an Air Canada A321-211 was operating flight AC2123 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During taxi for departure, a general aviation aircraft cut in front of AC2123, subsequently an abrupt stop was required, a flight attendant fell and were unable to continue their duties.

C-GOSR, a Spectrum Airways Piper PA-34-200 aircraft, was on a local training flight from Burlington Executive Aerodrome (CZBA), ON, with a student and instructor on board. The student was a licensed pilot, and this flight was for their multi-engine rating. After performing simulated single engine approaches the aircraft was on final approach to runway 32. The landing gear was not extended and the aircraft touched down with the landing gear retracted. The aircraft received substantial damage, but no injuries were reported to the two occupants on board.

C-GPCT, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited, Saab 340B was operating as flight 8P557 under instrument flight rules from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Williams Lake Airport (CYWL), BC. Approximately 30 minutes prior to arrival at CYWL, an intermittent master warning indication began due to an oil pressure issue with the left engine (General Electric CT7-9B). The flight crew reviewed the aircraft quick reference checklist (QRC) and discussed their options in case they needed to shut down the affected engine. Shortly thereafter, the master warning indication illuminated again and remained illuminated. The flight crew monitored the oil pressure and noted that it was gradually decreasing. When the oil pressure dropped below 30 psi, the flight crew shut down the left engine in accordance with the QRC and contacted air traffic control to declare an emergency. As a precaution, emergency services were requested to be on standby upon landing. The aircraft's flight attendant and passengers were briefed on the situation. The flight landed at CYWL without incident.The flight crew determined that the left engine oil level was low and noted oil leaking from the engine cowling. Maintenance personnel investigated and found that an O ring was missing from the left engine generator axis bearing seal which had recently been replaced. The O ring was installed and after a satisfactory leak check, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOSD, a privately registered Lancair 235, was being flown on a local recreational flight from Vernon Airport (CYVK), BC. During the take-off run, the aircraft inadvertently veered to the left and off of the runway surface into the grass. The aircraft struck an embankment causing the landing gear to collapse and a subsequent propeller strike. The emergency locator transmitter (ELT) activated. There were no injuries reported but the aircraft was substantially damaged.The aircraft was recovered from the field and transported for assessment.

C-GXTH, un hélicoptère Eurocopter AS350 B2, exploité par Heli-Inter Inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis la base d'Hydro-Québec La Grande-1 (LG1), QC à la base d'Héli-Inter à La Grande-2 (LG2), QC avec seulement le pilote à bord.  Alors que l'aéronef était en approche finale à environ 1 NM à l'ouest de la base LG2, une odeur de brûlé est survenue dans le cockpit suivie d'une légère fumée blanche provenant du tableau de bord prêt de l'emplacement de la boussole. Le pilote a effectué la procédure d'urgence pour feux électriques et la fumée s'est dissipée peu après la fermeture des interrupteurs électriques du tableau de bord. Le pilote a continué l'approche pour atterrir sans encombre à LG2. Après vérification du technicien, il a été confirmé que le conservateur de cap était défectueux et avait causé l'odeur et la fumée.

C-GUBC, an Air Transat A330-243 was operating flight TSC803 from Jardines del Rey International Airport (MUCC), Cuba, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, the crew received an ECAM warning of LOW OIL QUANTITY, followed a while later by LOW OIL PRESSURE message. The engine was shut down as per the standard operating procedures, a PAN PAN was declared and the flight was diverted to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL. The aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-GFWX, an Air Canada Rouge A320-214 was operating flight ROU1734 from Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), CA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated, and their duties were redistributed amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-FIUL, an Air Canada B777-300 was operating flight AC861 from to London Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK, Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, a passenger's cell phone started melting and emitted smoke. The crew were able to contain the cell phone in the personal electronic device bag.

C-GNZR, a Canadian Helicopter Limited, Bell Helicopter Textron 206L, was conducting a flight from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT to the Bluefish Dam, NT. While levelling off in cruise the pilot observed the pilot side door of the helicopter open. The pilot declared Pan Pan and elected to return to CYZF. The helicopter landed without further incident.Subsequently company maintenance personnel tightened the door closing mechanism.

C-GLUT, a CanWest Air Beechcraft King Air 200 was operating as flight CWA925 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB. C-GATK, an Air Tindi Beechcraft King Air 200, was operating as flight TIN511 from CYEG to Lutselk'e Airport (CYLK), NT. On departure from CYEG separation between CWA925 and TIN511 was reduced to 2.6 NM horizontally where 3.0 NM is required, there was no risk of collision. Both aircraft continued to their respective destinations without further incident.

C-GGWJ, a Boeing 737-700 operated by WestJet Airlines, was conducting flight WJA267 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the approach into CYYC the first officer observed a yaw damper master caution and a trailing edge flap asymmetry, with the flaps between 0 and 1. The flight crew advised ATC and began conducting the non-normal checklist for both the yaw damper and for the trailing edge flap damper. The first officer declared PAN PAN with ATC. Upon touchdown the crew observed a proximity switch electronic unit (PSEU) light illumination. The aircraft taxied off the runway on Taxiway D4 and then stopped to be inspected by aircraft rescue and firefighting. The aircraft subsequently taxied under its own power to the gate.The operator's maintenance conducted a yaw damper operational test and system test with no faults found. Maintenance also carried out a service check non-routine to rectify the trailing edge flap asymmetry, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJXE, un Airbus A220-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA405 et un Embraer ERJ 170-200 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA959 effectuaient leur vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, tous les deux en départ de l'aéroport international Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Les 2 aéronefs étaient en montée peu après leur départ de la piste 24D alors que l'espacement latéral a été réduit à 2.1 NM à la même altitude. L'espacement latéral requis était de 3 NM et 1000 pieds vertical.

C-FYBK, a Westjet B737-800 was operating flight WJA1433 from Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), CA, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. During climb out, the lower display unit illuminated, and the engine gauges showed low oil pressure indications in the yellow band. A return to KLAX was requested and checklists were completed. Oil temperature spiked into red and the crew shut down the engine and declared an emergency. Aircraft landed safely and was able to taxi to gate under its own power. At the gate, maintenance found a pool of oil under the No. 1 engine at the integrated drive generator drain. Damaged gearbox seal was identified. Pressure and scavenge filters were replaced. Metal found in No. 1 AGB/TGB screen, starter was replaced. Debris in No. 1 engine found in magnetic chip detectors (MCDs). Due to level of disassembly required for RDS inspection, company elected to proceed with an engine replacement.

C-GFAJ, un Airbus A330-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif AC832 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport nationale de Bruxelles, Belgique (EBBR). L'aéronef a frappé un oiseau de grande taille durant la monté initiale peu après le décollage de la piste 24R. L'équipage a ensuite déclaré l'état d'urgence et le vol est revenu atterrir sans encombre sur la piste 24L à CYUL. Le service de maintenance de la compagnie a effectué l'inspection de l'aéronef et a constaté des dommages au radôme et au radar météo nécessitants le remplacement de ceux-ci.

C-GSJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP DHC-8-402, was conducting flight JZA362 from Windsor International Airport (CYQG), ON, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While on climb out at FL040, the wind screen developed a crack. The crew declared a PAN PAN and returned to CYQG. The aircraft landed uneventfully with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by.

C-GLQZ, un DeHavilland DHC-8-400 exploité par Porter Airlines sous l'indicatif PTR2327, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport international Stanfield d'Halifax, NS (CYHZ) avec 73 passagers et 4 membres d'équipage à bord. À environ 17 500 pied, pendant la montée initiale, l'équipage de conduite a détecté une odeur de brûlé dans le poste de pilotage. L'équipage cabine a ensuite confirmé que la même odeur était présente dans la cabine. Aucune indication n'indiquait la présence de feux ou de fumée et aucune source visible n'a pu être identifiée. L'équipage de conduite décidé de revenir se poser à CYUL par mesure de précaution. Le vol PTR2327 est ensuite atterri sans encombre sur la piste 24D où les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. L'aéronef a circulé à la barrière et les passagers ont procédé au débarquement sans autre incident. Le système d'air conditionné et de pressurisation a été inspecté et testé avec les moteurs en marche par le service de maintenance de la compagnie. La condition n'a pas pu être reproduite et l'appareil a été remis en service.

C-GLQK, a Porter Airlines Dash 8-400 was operating flight PTR2125 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, was on climb-out when the crew noticed the flaps remained at Flap 5 during retraction. The crew declared a Mayday and diverted to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, where it conducted an uneventful landing with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by.

C-GLQZ, a Porter Airlines Dash 8-400, conducting flight PD2941 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS), MA, was on the climb out when the flight crew received a fuselage door warning light. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and returned to CYTZ. The aircraft performed an uneventful landing with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by.

C-GNSS, a Kisik Aerial Survey Incorporated Piper PA-31-325 (Navajo), was conducting a survey flight from Boundary Bay Airport (CZBB), BC, with only the pilot on board. During the approach back to CZBB, the aircraft’s flaps was stuck in the fully down position. The pilot contacted air traffic control and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed at CZBB without further incident. Maintenance personnel checked the aircraft’s flap system and found that the flap selector up switch was sticking. The switch was cleaned, and the subsequent operational testing showed the aircraft to be serviceable.

C-GWFE, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited DHC-8-400 operated by WestJet Encore was operating as flight WEN3217 from Edmonton International Airport (CEYG), AB, to Fort McMurray International Airport (CYMM), AB. While on the initial climb out from CYEG the flight crew observed a landing gear retraction malfunction. The flight crew declared Pan Pan and returned back to CYEG. The aircraft landed without further incident. Upon arrival it was discovered that the nose landing gear ground lock (NLG) was engaged, preventing the retraction of the landing gear. A landing gear swing was carried out by company maintenance personnel, and no faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJQL, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was operating flight ROU1702 from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), NV, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, the flight crew noted vibration from under the floor of the flight deck followed by a loud abnormal noise and an electrical burning odour. No smoke was observed. Flight crew declared a PAN PAN, requested descent to 10,000 feet and a diversion to Des Moines International Airport (KDSM), IA. During descent avionics vent blower extract ECAM was received and actioned by the flight crew. The flight subsequently landed full-stop with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) on standby. ARFF did not detect any abnormalities when a general visual external inspection was conducted. Aircraft was taxied to gate under its own power.

C-FXOK, a privately registered Zenith CH-750, was conducting a flight from Alliston Airport (CNY4), ON, to Collingwood Regional Airport (CNY3), ON, with the pilot as sole occupant. During cruise flight, approximately 2nm E of CNY3, the engine (General Motors, 2700CC) failed, idling down from 2700RPM. The pilot selected a farm field and conducted a forced approach. During the landing roll, the nosewheel dug into the soft ground and collapsed, and the aircraft overturned. The pilot exited the aircraft and was not injured. The aircraft received damage to the nosewheel, propeller spinner, engine cowling, both wing leading edge slats, and the vertical stabilizer. The ELT activated. During recovery of the aircraft, 6.5 gallons of fuel was drained from the tanks. The propeller and engine were observed to rotate freely, and the cause of the engine failure has not yet been determined.

C-GLQV, un deHavilland DHC-8-400 exploité par Porter Airlines sous l'indicatif PTR2287, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Billy Bishop de Toronto, ON (CYTZ) à destination Aéroport International Stanfield d'Halifax, NS (CYHZ). Alors que l’aéronef était en vol de croisière au niveau de vol 250, une fissure est apparue dans le pare-brise. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a effectué une diversion vers l'aéroport international Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). L'aéronef se trouvait à environ 60 miles marins à l’est-sud-est de CYUL au moment de l'évènement.  Le vol PTR2287 s'est posé sur la piste 24L sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte.

C-FBVC, a privately registered Cessna 335, was conducting a flight from Timmins/Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON, to Kitchener/Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON, with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. While in cruise flight, the alternator failed, followed by the right-hand engine (TSIO-520-EB) failing when one of the pistons broke through the crankcase. There was a brief fire originating near the propeller hub, which extinguished shortly after the pilot shut off the fuel flow to the engine. The pilot elected to divert to the Parry Sound Area Municipal Aerodrome (CNK4), ON. The pilot landed at CNK4 without further incident. There were no injuries to either occupant, and damage to the aircraft was limited to the engine and its cowling.

C-FJBO, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA874 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, USA. While climbing through approximately 11 000 feet, the flight crew observed a master caution light with an indication that the slats had failed at 0. After consulting with maintenance, the decision was made to return to CYYZ. Aircraft landed with slat 0 and flap 2; aircraft rescue and firefighting was on standby to monitor the brake temperatures after landing. The aircraft landed without incident and taxied to the assigned gate.

C-GDON, an Insignia College Limited Cessna 172K was being operated on a local training flight from Boundary Bay Airport (CZBB), BC, with only the pilot on board. After touching down on Runway 31 at CZBB, the aircraft bounced a number of times causing the propeller and a wing tip to strike the runway. The aircraft then veered left off the runway and came to a stop in the grass. The propeller and nosewheel assembly were damaged during the occurrence. No injuries were reported.C-GDON was removed from service for inspection of the attachment points for landing gear and wing structures. The propeller and the nose gear assembly were removed for replacement. The engine was removed for a teardown and inspection.

C-GKUG, an Airbus A330, operating as Air Canada flight AC0841, landed at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, and during a post flight inspection, Air Canada maintenance discovered damage consistent with ground contact of the rear fuselage.Air Canada maintenance completed after flight inspection and external skin panels found damaged. Nondestructive testing was completed, no cracks or further faults found. Aircraft skin thickness was found within limits between frame 72-75 after inspection. Airbus engineering was consulted for further information and recommendations.

C-GIFO, a privately registered Cessna 150M, was conducting a round-robin solo recreational flight from the Smithers Airport (CYYD), BC, to a number of aerodromes which included Woodcock Aerodrome (CBQ8), BC. Just after the touchdown of a touch and go at CBQ8, the pilot smelled smoke. Shortly after, as C-GIFO lifted off, the aircraft cabin started to rapidly fill with smoke. The pilot set the aircraft back down on the runway and braked hard. The aircraft came a stop on the right side of the runway. The pilot then turned off the aircraft’s master switch, moved the engine mixture control to cutoff, and switched off the ignition. After evacuating the aircraft, the pilot attempted to access the aircraft’s fire extinguisher but was unable to because it was underneath the cargo and smoke was quickly filling the cabin. Within two minutes, the aircraft was engulfed in flames. The flames were reported to be coming from the cargo area where the pilot had stored containers with approximately 34 liters of 100LL Avgas. The fuel was intended to be used to refuel the aircraft during the planned trip. The cargo area also contained a plastic survival kit bag which contained emergency flares.  Emergency services attended the scene but by the time of their arrival most of the aircraft had been destroyed by the fire.

C-FIUJ, an Air Canada Boeing 777-200, was departing Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, operating as flight AC33, under instrument flight rules, to Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport (YSSY), Australia. While the aircraft was being taxied to the runway, a cabin crew member was injured. The aircraft returned to the gate where the injured crew member received medical treatment.

C-FLUT, a Boeing B737-8, operating as Flair Airlines flight FLE1600, was departing Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, when the tower controller issued a takeoff clearance from Runway 15L, but did not modify the departure heading to turn away from Porter Airlines flight PTR2942, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 (C-GKQB), inbound to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. Separation was reduced to 2.3 miles laterally and 900 feet vertically with PTR2942.

N655RW an Embraer ERJ170, operating as Republic Airways flight RPA3627 was inbound to Toronto/Lester B.
