Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, when ATC gave the flight crew a clearance to turn to 260 degrees and descend to 3000 feet. The readback from the flight crew was correct, however, RPA3627 continued to turn past 260 degrees. ATC immediately re-cleared RPA3627 to a left turn, but not before separation was reduced to 2.5 miles laterally and 700 feet vertically with C-GKXF, a Porter Embraer ERJ190 operating as flight POE552.

C-GIQP, a privately registered Cessna R182 was conducting a local flight from Lac La Biche Aerodrome (CYLB), AB, with only the pilot on board. On initial approach to CYLB, the pilot extended the landing gear and received a green down and locked indication and visually confirmed that the main landing gear was extended. On final approach the pilot once again confirmed the green landing gear down and locked indication, as well as visually verifying the position of the main landing gear. During the landing roll out on the runway, both main landing gears collapsed, and the aircraft exited the runway surface on its belly. There was significant damage to the right horizontal stabilizer, main landing gear and belly of the aircraft. There were no injuries.

C-GJZD un DeHavilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7721 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis depuis l’aéroport de Bathurst, NB (CZBF) à destination l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre-Elliott-Trudeau Int'l, QC (CYUL). C-FEKH un Embraer ERJ170-200 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA247 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Halifax/Stanfield Int’l, NS (CYHZ) à CYUL.Alors que JZA7721 se trouvait en réduction de vitesse en courte finale de la piste 24L, JZA247, lui aussi en finale pour la 24L s'est rapproché derrière JZA7721. Le contrôleur a demandé à JZA247 d'interrompre l'approche et remonter afin de maintenir l'espacement. L'espacement a été réduit à 2.7nm horizontalement et 900 pieds verticalement alors que les minimums d'espacement pour la zone sont de 3.0 nm et 1000 pieds. Il n'y a pas eu de risque de collision.

N370EL, a Bombardier Challenger 300 operated by Jet Linx Aviation LLC as JTL370, and C-GUPK, an Airbus A220-300 operated by Air Canada as ACA418, were under the control of Toronto Centre while being sequenced for arrival into Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Both aircraft were eastbound and had been cleared to descend to FL270, and both were reaching that altitude in the vicinity of waypoint MIGLO. N370EL was the lead aircraft and had been assigned a speed of 280 knots, C-GUPK was trailing and assigned a speed of 250 knots. The minimum separation was 4.2 NM horizontally (5 NM is the required separation), while the aircraft were 100 feet apart vertically. ATC did not give a traffic advisory to either aircraft; it is not known whether either crew had the other aircraft in sight. Both flights continued to CYUL.

CS-GLB, a NetJets Europe Bombardier BD-700-1A10 (Global 6000) was conducting positioning flight NJE913G, under instrument flight rules, from Miami Opa-Locka Executive Airport (KOPF), FL, U.S. to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. While in cruise, the aircraft's Crew Alerting System (CAS) displayed a slat – flap caution message (SLAT-FLAP HALFSPD). During the approach into CYVR, a flap failure CAS message appeared when the flight crew selected flaps position 16. The flaps were stuck at position 13. The flight crew decided to abandon the approach and were given vectors from air traffic control so they could execute the required checklist tasks. The flight crew completed their tasks, declared a PAN PAN due to the partial flap deployment, and flew another approach to Runway 08R. Emergency services were requested to be on standby and the aircraft landed without further incident.  Following the landing, the flight crew performed a system reset which resolved the flap issue.  Maintenance personnel later determined that the aircraft’s flap resolver was defective and replaced that component.

C-GMKS, a Westjet B787-9 was operating flight WS19 from Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GENV, WestJet Encore DHC-8-400 was operating flight WEN3271 from Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. C-FENU, a WestJet Encore DHC-8-400 was conducting flight WEN3280 from Penticton (CYYF), BC, to CYYC. WEN3271 was performing the RNP Y arrival for Runway 35R, while WEN3280 was also on final approach for Runway 35R. Separation between WEN3271 and WEN3280 was reduced to 2.6 NM horizontally where 3.0 NM is required. Both aircraft continued with the approach sequence, and uneventful landings were conducted.

C-FFIP, a Boeing 737-8 operated by Air Canada as IFR flight AC266, was departing from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Prior to departure, AC266 was taxiing out in heavy snow and required deicing prior to takeoff. During the deicing procedure in a quartering tail wind, the aircraft suffered an engine auto shutdown that was followed by the second engine auto shutdown. The crew completed the quick reference handbook checklist and the aircraft was towed back to the gate.The operator's maintenance conducted a visual inspection of both engines. A borescope of the engine found ice accretion in the engine cores that restricted airflow. Engine performance runs were subsequently completed with no faults found and the aircraft was returned to service. The operator continues to consult with the aircraft and engine manufacturers. During the deicing procedure, the CYWG weather was reported as winds of 040 degrees true at 11 knots, gusting to 17 knots, in heavy snow conditions, a temperature of minus 4 degrees Celsius, and a dew point of minus 5.

C-FGYS, a McDonnell Douglas A-4N, operated by Top Aces Inc., was conducting aerial work out of Cold Lake/Group Captain R.W. McNair Airport (CYOD), AB. The aircraft sustained a generator failure while operating approximately 90 NM north of CYOD. The pilot deployed the ram air turbine (RAT) and completed the associated checklist, subsequently declaring an emergency with ATC. The aircraft returned to CYOD and landed without further incident.

C-GXFC, a Buffalo Airways Ltd. Lockheed L188C was operating as BFL808 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Hope Bay Aerodrome (CHB3), NU. During cruise the flight crew observed a #4 propeller indication; the flight crew then performed a precautionary shutdown of the #4 engine (Allison 501-D13). The aircraft returned to CYZF and landed without further incident.Company maintenance replaced the #4 Propeller Regulator and the #4 FCU, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GDEN, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited DHC-8-400 operated by WestJet Encore was operating as flight WEN3299 from Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While on approach for Runway 17L the flight crew observed an intermittent left main landing gear unsafe indication. The flight crew initiated a go-around to conduct the alternate landing gear extension checklist and requested vectors for a right hand downwind for Runway 17L. The flight crew declared Pan Pan and completed the checklist. After the checklist was complete the landing gear indication initially showed safe, but then the left main landing gear indicator briefly flashed unsafe. The captain instructed the first officer to continue pumping the hydraulic pump handle during the approach, and the landing gear indication remained safe. The aircraft landed without further incident, exited on Taxiway D3 and was escorted to the gate by aircraft rescue and firefighting. Company maintenance found that the left hand landing gear down and locked proximity sensor connector was contaminated. The sensor was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FXMY, a Keewatin Air LP Beech B200 operating as flight KEW209, was conducting a Medevac flight from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Kugluktuk Airport (CYCO), NU, with 2 crew and 2 passengers (medical team) on board. During the approach into CYCO the flight crew selected gear down and the nose gear down indication did not illuminate. The flight crew completed a missed approach and selected the landing gear up. The main landing gear transitioned to the up position; however, the nose landing gear indication remained illuminated red (gear unsafe, in transition). The flight crew contacted company operations, and it was determined that the best course of action was to return to CYZF and conduct a manual landing gear extension. Upon returning to CYZF the flight crew conducted a manual landing gear extension which resulted in the main landing gear indicating down, and the nose landing gear position unknown. The flight crew executed a fly-by of the tower, which confirmed that the nose landing gear appeared to be deflected about 30 degrees rearward of the normal down and locked position. The flight crew declared an emergency and entered a hold until aircraft rescue and firefighting was activated. As the aircraft landed, the nose landing gear collapsed. The aircraft came to rest on the centerline of the runway. The flight crew and the passengers were uninjured and exited the aircraft.

C-FXBP, an Aerospatiale AS350 BA/FX2 helicopter operated by Expedition Helicopters Inc., was conducting a local flight from Fort Albany Airport (CYFA), ON. Shortly after lifting off, while maneuvering for departure, the pilot felt an uncommanded pull to the left through the cyclic, and was unable to use the cyclic control to compensate as it could not be moved to the right. The helicopter continued to bank to the left and began to pitch up, causing the airspeed to reduce. The pilot shut off the hydraulic system using the collective-mounted switch, and although control was briefly lost during the transition from hydraulic control to manual control, he managed to regain control of the helicopter before making a successful approach and landing. There were no reported injuries. Several maintenance checks were performed, and the left hand main rotor servo control (P/N AC67244) was identified as the cause of the control difficulties, as there was a defect in the servo slide valve causing intermittent binding to occur. This part had been in service for approximately 350 hours since its last overhaul, with approximately 1450 hours remaining until its next overhaul. The company submitted a Service Difficulty Report to TC, and the defective servo will be dismantled to determine the reason for the failure. The servo control was replaced, and the helicopter control system was tested before returning it to service.

C-FCJP, a Boeing B757 operating as CargoJet flight CJT2402, was on approach to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, Runway 24. The flight crew selected flap “1” and received EICAS alert TE FLAP DISAGREE with no movement indication. The flight crew requested vectors from ATC and actioned the quick reference handbook which led to a flap “20” landing utilizing the alternate flaps. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and landed on Runway 30 without further incident.Maintenance found obstruction/foam in #2 flap track/transmission, removed and inspected per AMM 27-51-00. Found #4 transmission overload indicator tripped.

C-GBIN, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319 was operating flight ROU1771 was on the initial approach to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, at 3000 feet ASL when the flight crew received an ECAM F/CTL FLAPS LOCK - WING TIP BRAKE ON following selection of FLAP 2 from 1. ATC was notified and the approach was discontinued. The applicable ECAM actions and quick reference handbook were carried out, and preparations were made for a reduced flap landing. A PAN PAN was declared and a full stop landing on Runway 23 was carried with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) on standby. The aircraft was inspected by ARFF with no faults found, the flight taxied to the gate without further incident.Maintenance inspected the aircraft in accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual and found the right-hand position pick up unit to be defective. The unit was removed and replaced with a serviceable unit. Subsequent serviceability tests were carried out with satisfactory result. The aircraft was subsequently deemed to be airworthy and returned to service. A service difficulty report (SDR) was submitted to Transport Canada.

C-FKMG un Beech King Air 300 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif AIE552 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Puvirnituq, Nunavik, QC (CYPX) à destination de l’aéroport d’Akulivik, QC (CYKO) avec 2 pilotes à bord. Au moment du roulage vers la piste, l'hélice gauche a touché un cone orange qui se trouvait tout juste devant le moteur. Le vol a été annulé et l'hélice inspectée par le personnel de maintenance. Il n'y a eu aucun dommage observé à l'appareil durant l'inspection préliminaire.

C-GVVZ, a Sunwest Aviation Learjet 45 was operating flight CNK645 from Scottsdale Airport (KSDL), AZ, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. While on approach to Runway 20, a LR INBD BRK FAIL amber CAS message was received. The flight crew initiated a missed approach, and the appropriate quick reference handbook (QRH) checklist was carried out; the flight crew declared an emergency. The aircraft subsequently landed and taxied to the apron without issue.Company maintenance subsequently inspected the aircraft and suspected that one of the four weight on wheels switches had an intermittent fault.

C-FCSX, a Westjet B738 was operating flight WS1770 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (KPHX), AZ. During cruise, the first officer became incapacitated. The captain declared a medical emergency and initiated a return back to CYVR. Aircraft landed uneventfully.

HI1078, un appareil de type B737 MAX 8 exploité par Arajet effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments à partir de l'aéroport de Punta Cana (MDPC), République Dominicaine à destination de l'aéroport international de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC sous l'indicatif DWI5900. L'équipage a été instruit par le contrôleur du tablier de se stationner à la barrière 77. En se présentant sur les lieux, il s’est aligné sur la ligne de guidage de la barrière 77B et a été guidé sur le poste de stationnement 77B. Un autre aéronef de type Boeing 737 max 8 exploité par Air Canada en préparation pour le vol ACA763 était stationné à la barrière adjacente (76). Les distances entre les postes de stationnements 77B et 76 ne permettent pas un dégagement suffisant pour deux aéronefs de type B737 max 8. Alors que le vol DWI5900 effectuait son entrée au stationnement 77B, le bout de l'aile gauche de l’aéronef est entré en collision avec le bout de l'aile droite de l’aéronef du vol ACA763. Les passagers du vol DWI5900 ont pu être débarqués normalement par la passerelle 77. Aucune urgence n’a été déclarée. Seulement des dégâts aux bouts des ailes des aéronefs respectifs ont été constatés.

C-FYKC, an Air Canada A319, was conducting flight AC705 from La Guardia International Airport (KLGA) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. ATC cleared the aircraft to turn right to a heading of 260 degrees magnetic, and although the readback was correct, the aircraft continued the turn and was approaching 360 degrees. A loss of separation occurred with WJA324, a Westjet Airlines Boeing 737-800, registration C-FYPB. ATC immediately turned AC705 away from WJA324, however loss of separation had already occurred. The normal required separation in this airspace is 3 miles laterally, and 1000 feet vertical. The aircraft involved were separated by 2.7 miles laterally and 200 feet vertically.

C-GHCC, a Chinook Helicopters (1982) Limited Cessna 172S aircraft departed Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, on a local visual flight rules training flight to return to CYXX. There was an instructor and a student on board. The purpose of the flight was simulated instrument flight training. At approximately 1230 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), the aircraft departed CYXX and flew east. The aircraft was last visible on radar at approximately 1239 PDT. At that time, it was in the Chilliwack River Valley at an altitude of approximately 2125 feet above sea level. Another source of tracking data was recovered from the aircraft wreckage and analyzed by the TSB laboratory. The aircraft was flying eastbound in a narrow valley toward rising terrain. The aircraft was in a turn when it collided with the terrain. An emergency locator transmitter signal was received by the Canadian Mission Control Centre and the signal was relayed to the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre in Victoria, BC, at approximately 1306 PDT. The crash detection notification feature of an Apple device (either watch or phone) sent a message at approximately 1308 PDT. The instructor and student were fatally injured. The aircraft was destroyed. There was no post-impact fire.Chilliwack Search and Rescue and Canadian Armed Forces Search and Rescue personnel deployed to the site and the bodies were recovered. A TSB team deployed on 09 April 2025, and the wreckage was recovered to the Pacific Regional office on 14 April 2025.

C-GZRJ, a Summit Air British Aerospace Avro 146 (RJ100), was conducting flight SUT8131 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Hope Bay (CHB3), NU. On departure, the flight crew selected flaps up and immediately the FLAP INOP and FLAP FAULT caution lights illuminated, with the flaps remaining at the 18-degree position. The flight crew completed the quick reference handbook. The flight crew elected to return to CYEG and requested emergency services to standby as a precaution. The aircraft approached and landed safely, remained on the runway, and emergency services assisted in cooling the brakes. The aircraft taxied to the gate uneventfully.Maintenance inspection found that the Left Hand PSU was slightly out of range. The appropriate maintenance was completed, the system was reset, and the flaps tested successfully before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FXWJ, a Westjet Boeing 737-8 was operating flight WS2262 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Daniel Oduber Quirós International Airport (MRLB), Costa Rica. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to continue their duties. Duties were reassigned amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-GPIM, a Cessna 310R operated by Mitchinson Flying Service Ltd., was conducting a local VFR training flight from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. When approximately 40 NM southeast of CYXE, the flight crew observed a reduction in performance from the right engine (Teledyne Continental, IO-520-MB). C-GPIM requested a return to CYXE and declared a PAN PAN. Shortly thereafter, the oil pressure on the right engine indicated zero. The flight crew carried out a precautionary engine shutdown, feathered the right propeller, and declared a MAYDAY. The aircraft landed safely at CYXE and taxied to the operator's hangar. The operator's maintenance observed that the oil level was at 6 quarts when the pre-flight oil reading was 9 quarts. The engine was removed for further inspection.

C-GFVE, a Boeing 737-800 operated by WestJet was conducting flight WS491 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Los Cabos International Airport (MMSD), MX. After take-off, a flight attendant began to feel unwell. The flight crew contacted a remote doctor, and the crew member was removed from duty and treated. The duties were reassigned amongst the operating cabin crew. The flight continued to MMSD with no issues.

C-GWJF, a Westjet Boeing 737-7CT was operating flight WS1232 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Southwest Florida International Airport (KRSW), FL. The aircraft was vectored an early descent due to weather and were also instructed to hold. The flight crew declared a fuel emergency and requested vectors to their planned alternate at Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL. The flight landed uneventfully with the minimum reserve fuel of 3000 lbs.

C-FLQZ, a Flair Airlines Boeing B737-8 was operating flight FLE1848 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA. During approach into KSFO for 28R RNAV, aircraft was vectored to the north by ATC. As aircraft was vectored onto final, they were told to turn to heading 270 and cleared for the visual approach 28R with traffic on the parallel runway for 28L. Traffic was in sight and shallow out the intercept was instructed. At that moment, the TCAS RA command of TRAFFIC TRAFFIC LEVEL OFF appeared. The autopilot was disconnected and TCAS provided guidance was followed as instructed. After the CLEAR OF CONFLICT call, the approach was continued. At approximately 40' before being back on the VNAV path, a second RA command of CLIMB CLIMB message was received. Crew decided to go-around and notified ATC. Aircraft came back around and landed without further incident.

C-GFOF, a Flair Airlines Boeing 737-8 was operating flight FLE1876 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), NV. In the vicinity of San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA, the Oakland Centre instructed the aircraft to descend from FL390 to FL370 with at least 1500 feet per minute. While the aircraft was descending a traffic advisory (TA) was indicated. Before the decent could be stopped, a RA STOP DESCENT warning was received. The autopilot was disconnected and the TCAS RA was actioned. Once CLEAR OF CONFLICT was indicated, the autopilot was re-engaged and ATC was informed. The flight continued to land uneventfully in KLAS.

C-GRSZ, un Diamond DA40NG privé effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'Aéroport de Saint-Honoré (CYRC), QC avec seul un élève-pilote à bord. Au moment de l'atterrissage, l'élève-pilote a perdu la maîtrise de l'aéronef et celui-ci a quitté la surface de la piste du côté gauche. Il s'est immobilisé dans la neige, sur le nez. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé. L’aéronef a subi des dommages substantiels.

C-FCJF, a Cargojet Boeing 757-223 was operating flight CJT571 from Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. The aircraft declared an emergency over Minnesota due to a pressurization issue. Once level at 14,000 feet, the pilot reduced emergency to a PAN PAN and informed ATC that no assistance would be required. Aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GWSN, a Westjet Boeing 737-700 was being operated as flight WJA118 under instrument flight rules from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the take-off roll, when nearing the takeoff decision speed (V1), the flight crew noted a mismatch between the Captain’s and First Officer’s airspeed indications. Consequently, the takeoff was rejected, and the aircraft was brought to a stop on the runway. A PAN PAN call was then transmitted to air traffic control (ATC) and airport emergency services were dispatched. When the flight crew attempted to taxi the aircraft off the runway, they discovered that the brakes had seized due to the high speed rejected takeoff. Attempts to free the brakes were unsuccessful. As a result, the runway was closed, the passengers were disembarked, and the aircraft’s brakes were replaced. There were no reported injuries, and the aircraft was not damaged.After the brakes were replaced, the aircraft was moved off the runway. Maintenance personnel then conducted a test of the air data inertial reference system (ADIRS) using the build-in test equipment (BITE) which revealed an airspeed disagree message. The main pitot static lines were flushed and inspected, and various other tests and inspections were carried out. No further discrepancies were found, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSJJ, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 (Max 8) was being readied for departure on flight AC598 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to the John Wayne/Orange County Airport (KSNA), CA, U.S. While a flight attendant was arming a cabin door for departure, they were injured and were unable to continue their duties.

C-FGDZ, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 (Dreamliner) was departing Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, operating as flight AC39 under instrument flight rules to Auckland International Airport (NZAA), New Zealand. While taxiing out from CYVR, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to perform their duties. The aircraft returned to the gate and disembarked the crew member.

C-FNVU, an Air Canada A320, was conducting flight AC425 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Prior to the top of descent, as the flight crew was reducing engine power, the number 1 engine indicated a stall condition (CFM56-5A1). A PAN PAN was declared with ATC. The aircraft landed uneventfully with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by. Maintenance examined the engine and removed it for repair.

C-GYXL, a Fairchild SA227-AC operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting IFR flight PAG384 from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, to Sault Ste. Marie Airport (CYAM), ON. During the climb out after departure from CYQT, the flight crew observed torque fluctuations on the left-hand engine (Garrett, TPE331-11U-612G) with associated yawing, oil pressure fluctuations, and engine sounds. The flight crew referenced the quick reference handbook (QRH) and shut down the engine. They declared an emergency and returned to CYQT where the aircraft landed without further incident. Upon inspection by the operator's maintenance, the torque signal conditioner was found to be unserviceable.

C-FRSE, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC57 from Dubai International Airport (OMDB), UAE, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, the left low hydraulic quantity caution illuminated. The crew declared a PAN PAN and elected to divert to Frankfurt Airport (EDDF), Germany. The aircraft landed and taxied to the gate without further incident.After an Air Canada maintenance inspection, a leak was found in the engine driver pump return line. The engine driven pump, return line and filter were replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GLWJ, a Westjet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 was departing Kelowna International Airport (CYLW), BC, operating as flight WEN3750 under instrument flight rules to the Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (KSEA), WA, USA. After applying takeoff power, the flight crew received a PITCH TRIM caution light. The flight crew performed a low speed rejected takeoff and declared a MAYDAY. After approximately 2 seconds, the caution light extinguished without any inputs. The flight crew cancelled the MAYDAY and taxied the aircraft off the runway to consult the aircraft quick reference handbook (QRH).After reviewing the QRH the flight crew verified that the pitch trim was operative and was set within the takeoff range. The maintenance department was consulted, and it was determined that the aircraft was safe to continue operations. The subsequent takeoff was normal, and the flight continued without issue.

C-GZQK un Embraer ERJ 190-400 exploité par Porter Airlines sous l'indicatif POE135 venait d’effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl., QC (CYUL). Suivant l'atterrissage et le débarquement des passagers au quai #6, l'équipage de conduite a reçu une indication de feu du groupe auxiliaire de puissance (APU). La présence des services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) a été demandée afin de vérifier s'il y avait une présence de fumée ou de flammes à l'arrière de l'appareil. Aucune flamme n’a été détectée, mais un peu de fumée blanche s’échappait de l’APU.

C-FSBV, un Boeing 787-9 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif AC303 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Vancouver, BC (CYVR) avec 298 passagers et 10 membres d'équipage. Après le refoulement, un agent de bord a été victime d'un malaise l'empêchant d'accomplir ses tâches. L’avion est retourné au quai d’embarquement.

C-GBKB, a Bombardier Challenger 605 (CL-600-2B16) operated by Aurora Jet Partners was conducting a maintenance test flight departing from and returning to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. During the flap cycling tests, the flaps failed in a 16-degree setting. The crew actioned the Flaps Fail checklist and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft conducted an uneventful landing into CYEG. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) were requested to meet the aircraft after landing and confirmed the brake temperature was appropriate to taxi back to base. Company maintenance completed the Flaps Fail troubleshooting checklist, completed necessary repairs and checks, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FRTW, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC39 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Auckland Airport (NZAA), New Zealand. During the flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was not able to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-GPWG, an Air Canada Airbus A320 was operating as flight AC265 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. During the cruise portion of the flight, the crew observed a left engine (CFM International CFM56-5A1) low oil pressure indication on the Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitor (ECAM). The flight crew completed the associated checklists, including a left engine shutdown. They declared a MAYDAY and diverted to Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON. The aircraft landed safely, and after an inspection, the aircraft taxied under its own power to the gate.Following an inspection by the operator's maintenance, the left engine was replaced.

C-GVIJ, a Cargojet Boeing 767-328 was operating flight CJT5231 from Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL, to Juan Santamaría International Airport (MROC), Costa Rica. On ILS approach into MROC on 07, as the landing gear and flaps 20 was selected, the crew got EICAS LE SLAT AASYM message. A go-around was declared and the crew maintained flaps 1 and went for a hold. A PAN PAN was declared and diversion to Daniel Oduber Quirós International Airport (MLRB), Costa Rica, was decided as the landing distance on onboard performance tool showed that max auto was sufficient. During the transit, the crew elected to request a hold at ROMKO to burn fuel in order to lower landing weight. Crew decided to raise emergency to MAYDAY. Aircraft landed uneventfully. AUTOBRAKE got scale down as the crew rolled down the runway. The crew accepted a tower request to taxi to HOT BRAKE stand 7 for inspection. Aircraft rescue and firefighting cleared the aircraft.

N216UA, a Boeing 777-222ER, operated by United Airlines Inc, was conducting a flight from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, to Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (EHAM), Netherlands. During cruse at FL350, an electrical odor was detected emanating from the mid-galley area. The odor was traced to the 408 zone B galley oven. The flight crew pulled the circuit breakers, deactivating the unit. After consulting with Dispatch and Technical Operations Maintenance Control, the pilots elected to return to KEWR. An emergency was declared as a precaution, and the aircraft landed safely without further incident.Maintenance teams conducted an inspection of the aircraft, during which evidence of plastic debris was found in the exhaust fan of the galley oven. Following the completion of the necessary maintenance, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GURG, un Bombardier CL600-2B16 Challenger 601 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait le vol QUE10 selon les règles de vols aux instruments au départ de l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 2 pilotes, 2 personnels de cabine et 4 passagers à bord. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en croisière après 20 minutes de vol, l’indication ambre du « thrust reverser unlock » du moteur #1 s’est allumée. L'équipage a effectué la liste de vérification d'urgence. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et a poursuivi son vol vers CYUL où l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte.

C-IMCR, a privately operated basic ultra-light aircraft on floats was conducting a local flight from Petpeswick Lake, NS. After takeoff, at an altitude of about 150 feet above ground level (AGL), the engine had a power loss. The pilot initiated a forced landing. The aircraft contacted the water and experienced a hard touchdown, resulting in the collapse of the left and right float strut. The propeller struck and pierced the left float, causing the aircraft to take on water. The pilot received minor injuries.

C-FUJE, an Embraer EJR 170-200 SU aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation was conducting flight JZA93 from J.A. Douglas McCurdy Sydney Airport (CYQY), NS, to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC.  During cruise, a crack developed in the Captain’s windscreen. The crew referenced the quick reference handbook (QRH) and initiated a gradual descent from FL360 to FL100. After assessing the situation, they determined there was sufficient fuel and continued to their destination. The flight crew declared an emergency, and Moncton Centre coordinated with CYUL to provide the aircraft with priority handling. Emergency services were requested to meet the aircraft upon arrival. The aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-GVVZ, a Sunwest Aviation Limited Learjet Incorporated 45 (Lear 45), was conducting medevac flight CNK645 under instrument flight rules, from Scottsdale Airport (KSDL), AZ, U.S., to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During their approach to CYVR the flight crew configured the flaps and turned on the auxiliary hydraulic system in accordance with the landing checklist. The landing gear was extended, and the crew alerting system (CAS) then displayed an amber right inboard brake failure (R INBD BRK FAIL) message. The flight crew then advised air traffic control (ATC) that they would be conducting a missed approach. ATC instructed the crew to climb to 3000 feet ASL and then vectored them for a long downwind approach close to CYVR. During the vector, the crew completed the items directed by the aircraft quick reference handbook (QRH). The QRH advised that the aircraft would not have normal brakes for landing, so the flight crew contacted ATC, declared a PAN PAN, and requested that emergency services be on standby. The medics and patient onboard were advised of the situation. Upon landing, the pilot in command (PIC) actuated the thrust reversers which did not deploy immediately. The PIC then applied brakes, but the left brake felt abnormal. Shortly thereafter, the thrust reversers deployed. The first officer (FO) then applied their brakes which operated normally. The aircraft was stopped and, as the FO’s brakes were functioning, the aircraft was taxied off the runway. Emergency services personnel inspected the aircraft and found neither fluid leaks nor hot spots around the brakes. The aircraft taxied to parking and shut down.When the aircraft was restarted, a taxi and brake check were performed. The brakes functioned normally and the brake system CAS message did not reappear. Maintenance personnel cleaned the right landing gear squat switches and brake control unit connectors. They conducted various function checks and tests on the brake system and the thrust reversers with no faults found. The aircraft was released for service and no similar issues were reported.

C-GEPB, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 departed Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, operating as flight AC195, under instrument flight rules, to Kelowna International Airport (CYLW), BC. During the approach to CYLW, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to perform their duties.

C-GWSZ, a Westjet Boeing 737-800, was conducting flight WJA419, from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intenational Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. During the take-off roll, the pilot flying engaged the Take-Off Go-Around system (TOGA) but immediately noticed a discrepancy between the left and right thrust levers. Recognizing the discrepancy, the flight crew rejected the take-off when the aircraft was below 60 knots. The aircraft remained under control and the flight crew declared a MAYDAY. The aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power and was met by maintenance.Maintenance deferred the auto-throttle system under the MEL and replaced the Total Air Temperature (TAT) probe.

C-FTXQ, an Air Transat A321 was operating flight TSC650 from Québec/Jean Lesage International Airport (CYQB), QC, to Cancún International Airport (MMUN), MX. During cruise, over the Gulf of Mexico, the aircraft encountered sudden severe turbulence during which a cabin crew member sustained a minor injury and was unable to perform duties. A deadheading pilot was briefed and occupied the cabin crew jumpseat for landing. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GPWE, a Westjet Encore Ltd. De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 operating as flight WEN3195 was on a flight from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, en route to Grande Prairie Airport (CYQU), AB. At 1032 MDT, while at FL240, the captain's side window developed a large vertical crack. Side window heat had been on for at least 15 minutes prior to the crack developing. The crew declared a PAN PAN and turned back towards CYYC. The aircraft was slowed to 200 KIAS and a slow descent was carried out to prevent additional strain on the aircraft. The aircraft landed safely at 1108 MDT on Runway 17L. Aircraft rescue and firefighting followed aircraft to the gate.

C-GFCI, an Air Canada Rouge A320-214 was operating flight ROU1831 from Owen Roberts International Airport (MWCR), Cayman Islands, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During climb to cruise altitude, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining crew members.

C-FFYG, a Jazz Aviation LP Embraer ERJ170, was conducting a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to LaGuardia Airport (KLGA), NY. While at Gate 162 with the bridge attached and passengers on board, the flight crew noticed a sulfur odour. The ground crew reported sparks exiting the APU exhaust. At that moment the aircraft began to shake followed by a loud banging noise. The flight crew shut down the APU, commenced a rapid deplanement and aircraft rescue and firefighting was requested. Maintenance removed the aircraft from service and after extensive checks could not duplicate the odour but placed the APU on minimum equipment list (MEL) and returned the aircraft to service. The APU was replaced five days after the event.

C-GYFY, an Air Canada A321-211 was operating flight AC1202 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL. During the descent, the aircraft encountered light turbulence during which, a cabin crew member sustained a minor injury. The flight attendant was unable to perform safety duties. These safety duties were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FIUA, an Air Canada B777-200 was operating flight AC33 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Sydney Airport (YSSY), Australia. During the flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned to remaining crew members.

C-GCPW, un Dornier 328-300 exploité par Pratt & Whitney Canada sous l’indicatif PWC404, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ) à destination de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU). Alors que l’aéronef est établi sur l’approche RWY 24R, les pédales de la gouverne de direction se sont bloquées causant la désactivation du pilote automatique et de l’amortisseur de lacet. L’équipage a déconnecté les 2 systèmes et a confirmé que le jeu dans les pédales de la gouverne de direction était restreint. L’équipage a poursuit l’approche en utilisant les ailerons pour aider à contrôler le mouvement de lacet. À environ 100 pieds au-dessus du sol, le contrôle de la gouverne de direction est revenu et la restriction des pédales a disparu au même moment qu'un de relâchement mécanique a été entendu par l’équipage. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre à CYHU. La servocommande de l’amortisseur de lacet de l’autopilote a été remplacée.

C-GVGA, un Beechcraft 1900D exploité par Propair Inc. sous l’indicatif PRO4810 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY). Lors de la montée vers FL150, l’équipage a remarqué que la lumière d’alerte « CABIN DOOR » s’allumait de façon intermittente et est restée allumée à partir du FL180. La montée a été arrêtée à FL190 et l’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide. Il a ensuite contacté l‘unité de contrôle aérien pour déclarer une urgence et demander une descente pour 10 000 pieds et un retour à CYUL. L’aéronef s’est ensuite posé sans encombre à  CYUL.

C-FPQB, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC1088 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL. During the flight, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst remaining cabin crew.

C-FVLQ, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC79 from Dubai International Airport (OMDB), UAE, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-FKIW, a Westjet Boeing B737-700 was operating flight WS1511 from Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), CA, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated. Duties were reassigned amongst cabin crew members and aircraft landed without further incident.

N838AM, an Air Mexico Boeing 737-900, was conducting flight AMX 693 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Aeropuerto Internacional Benito Juárez (MMMX), Mexico. C-FSNQ, an Air Canada Boeing 737-800, was conducting a flight from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to CYYZ. AMX693 took off from Runway 33R following MIXUT7 SID but deviated off course toward arriving ACA160 on the downwind for Runway 33L, resulting in a loss of separation. ATC stopped ACA160 descent and turned AMX693 away to assure separation.

C-GKPX, a Swearingen SA-226-TC operated by 2080061 Ontario Inc. (dba SkyCare Air Ambulance), was conducting IFR flight PHX264 from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, to Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON. The aircraft taxied for takeoff from Runway 07, lining up with centre of the runway at the intersection of Runway 12/21. The power levers were advanced, the flight crew saw 2 positive torques, the BETA lights extinguished, and takeoff power was set. The aircraft accelerated to 80 knots normally. The pilot flying applied up elevator to reduce the weight on the nose wheel. Shortly after raising the nose wheel, the flight crew felt the aircraft pull hard left and a call was made to reject the takeoff. During the recovery with slippery runway conditions and reduced traction, the aircraft started to swerve. The aircraft turned to the right, then back to the left, and back to the right. Control of the aircraft was regained with the use of braking, nose wheel steering and reverse power. The flight crew at some point in the recovery process felt a thud on the left main gear. The aircraft came to a stop on the runway centreline. The flight crew asked Thunder Bay Radio to close their flight plan and advised that they were returning to the apron. On the apron, the flight crew shutdown the engines and exited the aircraft. Upon exiting the aircraft, the flight crew noticed a significant amount of fuel leaking from the left inner wing and gear area. The crew requested assistance from the operator’s maintenance and the airport refueller to control the fuel leak.The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and found structural damage to the left nacelle area skins and the left main gear attachment points. An airfield inspection found no runway lights were damaged. A runway condition report issued 1 hour before the event reported that Runway 07’s centre 100-foot width had 30% coverage of 1/8 inch dry snow and the remaining runway width reported as 6 inches in dry snow. A runway condition report issued approximately 45 minutes after the event reported that Runway 07’s centre 120-foot width was 20% coverage of 1/8 inch dry snow and 30% coverage of frost with the remaining runway width reported as 11 inches in dry snow.

C-FGAJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing B767 was on a flight from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (KCVG), KY, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the descent out of FL400, the crew received an EICAS of "FWD EQPT OVERHEAT" almost immediately followed by "CABIN ALTITUDE". The crew actioned the checklist, including donning oxygen masks and declaring an emergency. The crew carried out an expedited descent to 10,000 feet ASL. At that point CABIN ALT extinguished. Maximum cabin altitude was between 10,500 feet and 11,000 feet ASL. The aircraft landed without further incident.

N518FX, a Flexjet LLC Bombardier Challenge CL300 operating as flight LXJ518) was on an instrument flight rules flight from Boeing Field/King County International Airport (KBFI), WA, to Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen International Airport (CYXY), YT. Onboard were 2 pilots and an unknown number of additional crew and passengers. During the arrival, the flight crew reported a flap indicator issue and requested to level off. A few moments later, the flight crew declared a Mayday and advised that they would be landing on Runway 32L without any flaps. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) personnel were advised and standing by. The aircraft landed safely at 09:20 MST.

C-GFVY, a Cessna C185F operated by MHA Enterprises Ltd. (dba Alair), was conducting a VFR flight from Winnipeg/St. Andrews Airport (CYAV), MB, to St. Theresa Point Airport (CYST), MB. During the landing roll at CYST, directional control was lost, and the aircraft experienced a ground loop resulting in the collapse of the left main landing gear with the left wing striking the runway surface. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. There were no injuries.

C-GHKW, un Airbus A330-343 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA866 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de London Heathrow, Angleterre (EGLL) avec 298 passagers et 11 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, le bouton poussoir associé aux détecteurs de fumée au niveau du système d’avionique s’est allumé. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence au contrôleur aérien et a demandé de revenir atterrir à CYUL. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre et a été inspecté par le service de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). Après une inspection de l'aéronef par le service de maintenance d’Air Canada, les détecteurs de fumée ont été remplacés.

C-GQXX, a PA-31-350 operated by 2080061 Ontario Inc. (dba Skycare Air Ambulance), was conducting an IFR flight from Dryden Regional Airport (CYHD), ON, to Bearskin Lake Airport (CNE3), ON. Shortly after departing CYHD, the flight crew noticed that the right hand propeller RPM was decreasing despite attempting to increase the RPM. The flight crew contacted Sioux Lookout Radio requesting a return to CYHD and conducted a right engine precautionary shut down. The flight landed safely. The operator's maintenance found the right propeller governor shaft had failed. The governor was replaced, ground runs completed, and the aircraft was returned to service. A service difficulty report (SDR) was submitted by the operator.

C-FPVJ, un de Havilland DHC8-402 exploité par Provincial Airlines sous l'indicatif PVL831, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) avec 52 passagers et 4 membres d'équipage à bord. Pendant le dégivrage de l’aéronef avant le démarrage des moteurs, du liquide de dégivrage s’est introduit dans le système d’air de prélèvement du groupe auxiliaire de bord (APU), qui s’est soldé par de la fumée qui s’est répandue dans la cabine. L’ordre d’évacuation a été donné, et après quelques instants, il a été changé pour un débarquement rapide. Les passagers ont marché pour se rendre au terminal, ou les agents de bord les ont rejoints. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. Il a été établi que la fumée provenait du liquide de dégivrage qui s’est introduit dans le système de conditionnement d’air de l’appareil et les SLIA ont confirmés qu’il n’y avait pas de danger d’incendie. La cabine de l’aéronef a été aérée et les passagers sont revenus à bord. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’aéronef.

C-GQWJ, a Boeing 737-700 operated by WestJet Airlines, was conducting IFR flight WJA326 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During enroute climb between flight level FL190 and FL250, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence, making it difficult to control the aircraft. The flight continued to CYUL where an uneventful landing was conducted. There were no injuries.The operator's maintenance conducted a severe turbulence encounter inspections and no faults were found. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-GBQP, a privately-registered Piper 601P was conducting a flight from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, to High Level Airport (CYOJ), AB. During the climb, the pilot observed non-normal left-engine (Avco Lycoming IO-540-S1A5) cylinder head temperature indications. The pilot then observed oil streaking from the left-engine nacelle and completed a precautionary shut down of the left engine. The aircraft returned to CYXE for an uneventful landing.

C-GYRS, a Westjet B787-9 was operating flight WJA2426 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Cancún International Airport (MMUN), MX. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst remaining flight attendants.

C-GKQG, a Porter Airlines Dash 8-400 was operating flight PTR2137 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ. In the vicinity of MEMMS waypoint, ATC advised the crew to expect significant turbulence at FL210 and suggested FL190 as a better alternative. Shortly after descending to FL190, the aircraft experienced sudden and violent turbulence. The crew reduced the airspeed to 210 KIAS (rough air speed). While the autopilot remained engaged, the crew reported difficulty in controlling airspeed due to the severity of the turbulence and reported severe turbulence to ATC. Upon further descent to 17 000, they encountered smoother air. The aircraft landed without further incident.The severe turbulence inspection was carried out by maintenance. Flight data and landing weight data was reviewed with no faults found. The aircraft was released back into service.

C-GHKR, an Air Canada A330 was operating flight AC872 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France. During cruise, the crew noticed the yellow hydraulic quantity had fallen outside the green band and an associated low level ECAM caution. On decent into LFPG a PAN PAN was declared with ATC and the aircraft landed without further incident.After a maintenance inspection was completed, the number 4 spoiler servo was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBJV, a Pilatus PC-12/45 operated by Air Bravo Corp, was conducting IFR flight AB237 from Timmins/Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON, to Dryden Regional Airport (CYHD), ON, with 2 pilots on board. During the cruise portion of the flight and approximately 60 nautical miles North of Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, the aircraft entered severe turbulence. The captain, who was the pilot monitoring and had removed his shoulder harness for a portion of the cruise phase, hit his head on the overhead panel and was injured. The crew declared an emergency and began a descent to exit the turbulence. The captain tended to his injury while the first officer flew the aircraft and diverted to CYQT where an uneventful landing was conducted. Aircraft rescue and firefighting followed the aircraft to the apron and administered medical assistance to the captain.The operator's maintenance subsequently inspected the aircraft for damage and no faults were found. The aircraft's interior was cleaned and was then returned to service.

C-GOIJ, an Air Transat Airbus A321-271NX was operating flight TSC680 from Montreal (CYUL), QC, to Humberto Delgado Airport (LPPT), Portugal. In cruise over the North Atlantic, a cabin crew member became incapacitated. The duties of the cabin crew member were redistributed amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-GVDQ, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300 was operating flight AC1169 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. Approximately 58 nm SE of CYZF, the first officer (FO) fell ill and was not able to perform their duties. A deadheading flight crew member was able to assume the FO's duties. The flight continued to CYZF with no issues. EMS was requested to meet the flight at the gate.

C-GOJQ, an Air Transat Airbus A321-271NX was operating flight TSC301 from Daniel Oduber Quirós International Airport (MRLB), Costa Rica, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the descent into CYYZ, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to perform safety duties. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GBCH, a Central Mountain Air Limited DHC-8-311 (Dash 8), was conducting flight GLR562 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Quesnel Airport (CYQZ), BC. During the initial climb out of CYVR, the No. 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW123) oil pressure warning light illuminated. The flight crew levelled the aircraft at 5000 feet above sea level (ASL), consulted the aircraft quick reference handbook (QRH), and then performed a precautionary shut down of the No. 2 engine. A MAYDAY was declared with air traffic control (ATC) who provided the crew with vectors to return to CYVR. The aircraft landed without further incident with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) personnel standing by. ARFF inspected the aircraft after it landed and did not notice any leaking fluids or other anomalies. There were no injuries reported and the aircraft was not damaged. Maintenance inspections found debris in the oil that was drained from the No. 2 engine reduction gear box. It was determined that the debris was likely the cause of the oil pressure warning and was thought to have come from an AC generator failure that had occurred previously. The No. 2 engine oil system was flushed, and the aircraft was released to service after a satisfactory test flight.

C-FRSR, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was operating flight AC40 from Auckland Airport (NZAA), New Zealand, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Prior to departure, a cabin crew member sustained a personal injury and consequently was deplaned.

C-GGFJ, un Dash-8 Q400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7721, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Bathurst, NB (CZBF) à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 35 passagers à bord. Lors de la sortie du train d’atterrissage en approche finale, une indication anormale du système hydraulique est survenue. L’équipage a effectué une remise des gaz, a déclaré un état d’urgence et a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH). Par la suite, un atterrissage sans encombre a été effectué sur la piste 24R avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte.

C-GTSD, un Airbus 330-343 exploité par Air Transat sous l'indicatif TSC539, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport international de Cancún (MMUN) au Mexique à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL), avec 340 passagers et 11 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’aéronef était en approche pour la piste 24R, le premier officier a subi une incapacité physique partielle. Le commandant a poursuivi l’approche et l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GTYX, un Twin Otter (DHC-6) exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE616 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Kuujjuaq QC (CYVP) à destination d’Apaluk, QC (CYLA) avec 2 pilotes et un passager à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage en condition de vents traversiers sur la piste 04, le pilote a perdu la maîtrise de l’aéronef et celui-ci a quitté la surface de la piste du côté gauche. L’aéronef a terminé sa course dans la neige à environ 350 pieds du centre de la piste. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni autre dommage.

C-GBKB, a Bombardier CL-600-2B16 (604 Variant) operated by Aurora Jet Partners from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), CA. After takeoff from CYYC, when the flaps were selected to 0, the flight crew observed CAS message "Flaps Fail". The flaps had not retracted to 0 and remained at 20. The flight crew reported the problem to ATS and requested vectors to run the quick reference handbook checklist. Needing to burn a substantial amount of fuel to be able to land under maximum landing weight, the crew decided to divert to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, and held for approximately one hour before landing. A PAN PAN was declared to air traffic control, and aircraft rescue and firefighting was requested to standby in order to check brake temperatures after landing. The flight landed in CYEG with no additional issues.Following the flight, maintenance determined that an identical failure occurred with this aircraft on 8 February 2025 on a flight departing CYEG (A25W0014). Maintenance complied with AD CF-2024-31R1; troubleshooting continues.

C-FUCL, a privately registered Rans Coyote II S-6S was on a recreational flight from Kuskanook Harbour, (49º 18' 08" N, 116º 39' 53" W) to Creston Aerodrome (CAJ3), BC, under visual flight rules, with the pilot and one passenger on board. Immediately after lifting off from the water, the right wingtip dropped and came in contact with the surface. The aircraft came to an abrupt halt and settled upright on the water with the right float strut having collapsed. The occupants egressed from the aircraft without injury and paddled to the nearby beach. The aircraft was substantially damaged.The aircraft had damage to the landing gear supports, a cracked wing tip, and a bent propeller blade. The aircraft was towed from the beach and transported back to its hangar. It will be assessed for damage.

C-FYJE, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1696 from Ottawa International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL. During cruise, the aircraft encountered moderate turbulence during which, a flight attendant sustained a minor injury and was unable to perform safety duties. These duties were reassigned amongst remaining cabin crew. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GJAN, a Jazz CRJ900 was operating flight JZA765 from San Diego International Airport (KSAN), CA to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise at FL360, the crew received a Right Outboard Brake warning message. The Temps slowly went from 10 to 20 so the crew were unsure if they had a fire. They performed a rapid descent and then extended the gear. The crew elected to divert to Sacramento International Airport (KSMF), CA. The warning message went out but re-appeared on approach. The flight landed with no further issue. The crew did not declare an emergency however, the fire trucks were on standby. The flight was able to taxi to the gate and there was no adverse passenger reaction.

C-FJZN, a Jazz Aviation LP Bombardier CRJ900, was conducting a repositioning flight as JZA7125 from Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During descent the crew received a SMOKE AFT LAV warning message. The flight crew donned the oxygen masks and declared a PAN PAN with Toronto ATC. The quick reference handbook procedures were followed and the aircraft landed on runway 24L with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by to inspect the aircraft when it came to a stop. There were no visible signs of fire or smoke, and the aircraft was cleared to the terminal. After extensive checks maintenance determined that it was a faulty aft lavatory smoke detector. The unit was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GAEW, a Beech King Air B200 operated by Voyageur Aviation Corp. was conducting flight VAL791 from Moncton Romeo LeBlanc International Airport (CYQM), NB to Miramichi Airport (CYCH), NB. When the aircraft was climbing through 10,000 feet, the flight crew noticed smoke coming from the right circuit breaker (CB) panel. The flight crew leveled off and turned off the overhead and side panel lighting. The checklist was actioned, and a decision was made to return to CYQM. The flight crew briefed the nurses onboard and the aircraft landed without incident. Maintenance inspected the aircraft and heat from the backlighting of the right circuit breaker panel was the cause of the smoke and odor. The CB for the panel was isolated and the aircraft was placed back in service.

C-GWZY, a Dassault-Breguet / Dornier Alpha Jet operated by Top Aces Inc., was operating as CHETA 62 from Cold Lake Canadian Forces Base (CYOD), AB. During take-off, at rotation speed, the pilot heard a loud ‘machine gun like’ banging noise from the right-hand engine (SNECMA Turbomeca Larzac, 04C6). The take-off was continued and, once safely airborne, the pilot completed the Engine Fire/Failure During Takeoff checklist. A compressor stall was diagnosed, and an emergency was declared. A single-engine approach was completed at CYOD without further incident.

C-FCSK, un DeHavilland DHC-8-102 exploité par Air Creebec, effectuait le vol CRQ238 selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR), depuis l'aéroport de Chibougamau, QC (CYMT) à destination de l'aéroport international de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 35 passagers à bord. À mi-parcours, l'équipage de conduite a remarqué que la pression d'huile du moteur droit a baissé sous le seuil permis. Suivant les procédures associées aux symptômes, le moteur droit a été éteint et une urgence a été déclarée avec le service de circulation aérienne. L'aéronef a poursuivi sa route vers CYUL où il s'est posé sans encombre.Une inspection a révélé une fuite d'huile provenant du refroidisseur d'huile. La pièce défectueuse a été remplacée et l'aéronef remis en service par le personnel de maintenance.

C-GWJE, a Westjet B737-800 was operating flight WJA9145 with only the 2 pilots onboard from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, to L.F. Wade International Airport (TXKF), Bermuda. While at 39 000 feet, the Master Caution light illuminated, which led to the Auto Fail non-normal checklist. The crew began an early descent into TXKF, and at 37 000 feet, the Cabin Alt Warning light illuminated. The crew donned oxygen masks and initiated an emergency descent. They declared a MAYDAY to ATC, ran the emergency descent checklist, and descended safely to 10 000 feet. The flight landed safely without further incident.Maintenance Actions: CPC bite was carried out, and fault codes 050, 090, and OFV messages were found. Both pressure controllers were replaced and tested serviceable. The outflow valve was also replaced and tested. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTSJ, an Air Transat A330-200 was operating flight TSC399 from Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), DR, to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Shortly after take-off, a cabin crew became incapacitated and was unable to perform safety duties which were reassigned amongst remaining crew members.

C-GAEM, an Airborne Energy Solutions Inc. Cessna 172S was operating on a local pipeline survey flight from Edmonton/Villeneuve Airport (CZVL), AB. When entering the CZVL control zone, the pilot was cleared for the left downwind on Runway 26. While at approximately 1000 feet AGL, less than a mile from Runway 34 (short left base) tower asked if the pilot wanted to land on Runway 34 instead of Runway 26. The pilot accepted and clearance was given to land Runway 34. The pilot reduced power, set flaps and entered a forward slipping turn to quickly reduce altitude in order to get established on the approach to Runway 34. While over the midpoint of the runway, the speed of the aircraft was 76 KIAS and the pilot began to flare. The pilot considered the option to conduct an overshoot; however, another Cessna 172 had just taken off from Runway 26. The pilot added a small amount of throttle to ensure the aircraft cleared the runway edge lighting and a soft field landing was made on the grass beyond Runway 34. After the aircraft came to a stop the pilot requested clearance to taxi back to Runway 34. Taxi clearance was given and C-GAEM was subsequently cleared back to the apron. The aircraft received no damage and there were no injuries.

C-FHCW, a Nolinor Aviation Bombardier Learjet 45 was operating as flight NRL430 from Mirabel Airport (CYMX), QC, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. During final approach to CYEG, the flight crew received the CAS message "Normal Brake Fail". A go-around was conducted, the flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and were vectored for a second approach. After completing the checklist items, the brake issue remained, and the flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency.  The aircraft landed without further issue and was met on the runway by aircraft rescue and firefighting. The aircraft was inspected and was cleared to taxi to the apron. Company maintenance inspected the aircraft and no faults were found. The aircraft was released for continued service.

N865FD, a Boeing 777-FS2 aircraft operated by FedEx Corporation, was conducting flight FDX1 from London/Stansted International Airport (EGSS), England, to Memphis International Airport (KMEM), TN.  While in cruise at about 57° 03' N, 048° 27' W the flight crew experienced smoke in the cockpit. The flight crew completed the quick reference checklist, declared an emergency, and coordinated with company dispatch and with ATS for a diversion to Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL. The aircraft landed at CYYR without further incident.Maintenance personnel determined the cause of the smoke was a faulty equipment cooling fan.

C-FEAI un Dehavilland DHC-8-314 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif AIE866 effectuait un vol d'essai local selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Qc (CYUL) avec 3 membres d'équipage. Peu après l'atterrissage, une perforation sur le revêtement du fuselage arrière a été remarquée par le personnel de maintenance. Il a été déterminé que l'appareil a heurté un petit poteau électrique sans que l'équipage le remarque lors d'un virage serré en se dirigeant vers la piste avant le vol.

C-GEMV, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight AC1323 from Providenciales International Airport (MBPV), Turks and Caicos Islands, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, a cabin crew became incapacitated and was unable to perform safety duties which were reassigned amongst remaining crew members.

C-FNOE, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC851 from Indira Gandhi International Airport (VIDP), India, to Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK. During the cruise phase of flight, a cabin crew member was incapacitated and unable to continue with duties which were reassigned amongst remaining flight attendants.

C-FIUA, an Air Canada B777-233LR was operating flight AC43 from Indira Gandhi International Airport (VIDP), India, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, approximately 2.5 hours to arrival, a pilot became incapacitated and was unable to continue with their duties. The flight was completed without further incident.

C-GPCI, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited, Saab 340B was conducting flight PCO1308 under instrument flight rules from Penticton Airport (CYYF), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. While in cruise at flight level (FL) 200, the right engine intake (R INTAKE) amber warning light and master caution light illuminated. Soon afterwards, the flight crew noticed a burning smell and saw sparks around the right engine intake. As a precaution, the flight crew turned off the right engine anti-ice and after reviewing the quick reference checklist and decided to keep it off for the remainder of the flight. The flight crew coordinated with air traffic control (ATC) to minimize their flight time in icing conditions during the flight to CYVR.While being vectored for approach, the flight crew was informed by ATC that several aircraft ahead of them had conducted missed approaches due to the wind shift (a gusting tailwind of 13 to 22 knots). The flight crew initiated a missed approach. ATC then instructed the crew to climb to 3000 feet above sea level (ASL). While in the climb, the aircraft began to accumulate significant ice. The flight crew contacted ATC to declare an emergency and requested a descent to 2000 feet ASL where there was no icing. The flight crew was cleared for a visual approach and landed safely without further incident. Maintenance personnel found that the aircraft’s right engine lower inlet duct had burn damage. The lower inlet duct was replaced and systems tests were performed successfully.

N338JE, a TVPX Aircraft Solutions Incorporated Trustee (Jet Select LLC doing business as Vista America) Bombardier BD-100-1A10 (Challenger 300), was operating flight VJA338, under instrument flight rules, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Teterboro Airport (KTEB), NJ. Approximately 25 minutes after takeoff, the flight crew noticed an electrical burning smell coming from the galley area. The flight crew contacted air traffic control (ATC) to declare an emergency, returned to CYVR, and landed without further incident.    Maintenance personnel determined that a malfunctioning microwave oven had caused the electrical burning smell. The microwave oven was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

N12003, a Boeing 787-10 operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL881 from Chicago/O'Hare International Airport (KORD), IL, USA to Haneda Airport (RJTT), Tokyo, Japan. While cruising approximately 217 nautical miles (NM) North-northeast of Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, the crew declared an emergency due to a fuel leak and requested a diversion to Minneapolis–Saint Paul International Airport (KMSP), USA. The aircraft landed uneventfully KMSP at 2258z.

C-GJZX, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was operating flight JZA8060, under instrument flight rules, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC. During the approach to CYKA, the aircraft experienced severe turbulence between 10 000 and 8000 feet above sea level (ASL) which made the aircraft difficult to control. The turbulence also resulted in large airspeed and vertical speed fluctuations. The flight crew aborted the approach and returned to CYVR without further incident. There were no injuries to persons on board nor damage to the aircraft reported.

C-GPCN, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited Saab 340B, was operating as flight 810T, under instrument flight rules, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR) BC, for a local maintenance test flight, with 2 flight crew members and 1 aircraft maintenance engineer on board. While climbing through flight level 235, the flight crew heard a loud pop and noticed that the outer right front windshield pane had cracked. The flight crew initiated a descent and checked that the aircraft cabin had maintained pressure. They contacted air traffic control to declare an emergency and requested an immediate return to CYVR. The aircraft landed without further incident.The aircraft was held out of service until company maintenance replaced the window. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-FWGV, a privately registered amateur-built Bearhawk with the pilot and one passenger on board, was departing for a flight from a private airstrip located 10 nautical miles east-southeast of Winnipeg/St. Andrews Airport (CYAV), MB, to Gimli, MB. During the takeoff sequence from the private airstrip, the pilot was unable to maintain runway heading and the left wing came into contact with small trees along the south side of the east/west oriented airstrip. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. There were no injuries. There was no fire.

C-FNND, an Air Canada Boeing 777-233LR, was preparing to depart from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Zurich Airport (LSZH), Switzerland, when a plastic bag was ingested into the right-hand engine during engine start. The aircraft returned to the gate and the flight was cancelled. Air Canada maintenance completed the engine foreign object damage checks as per the AMM and no fault was found.

C-FRSE, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC66 from Suvarnabhumi International Airport (VTBS), Thailand to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Shortly after departure, the crew received a SLAT/Drive fault message. The crew elected to return to VTBS, dump fuel and declare PAN PAN. The aircraft landed in VTBS without further incident.Maintenance replaced the number 7 inboard Slat skew sensor, completed a wiring functional check and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FGNZ, a privately registered Piper PA-20 Pacer with only the pilot on board, was on a flight from Souris Glenwood Industrial Air Park (CJX5), MB, to Russell Airport (CJW5), MB. During the landing sequence at CJW5, lateral control was lost and the aircraft departed the runway to the left. During the runway excursion, the aircraft encountered soft snow conditions causing it to overturn on its back. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. There were no injuries. There was no fire.

C-GZCN, a Canadian North Boeing 737-300 was operating from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Iqaluit International Airport (CYFB), NU, when the flight crew observed visible smoke/vapor from the captain’s and FO’s windshield air vents during the take-off roll. The smell was of burnt deice fluid. The aircraft climbed normally, the gear was retracted, and the flight path was stable as it climbed to 400 feet AGL while smoke continued to flow out of the air vents. At 400 feet AGL the crew configured the bleeds. When the APU bleed switch was selected off and replaced by the Engine #1 bleed, the visible smoke/vapor and strong odor began to dissipate. The flight path remained stable, the flight deck air quality continued to improve, flaps were retracted and the After Take-off checklist was completed. Once AKT103 climbed above the 100nm safe altitude approximately 7000 feet, communication was established with the cabin crew and the cabin air quality was assessed and confirmed to be unaffected.The flight crew assessed the events, the risk of continuing the flight and agreed that it had been an abnormal occurrence, but that the aircraft air conditioning had returned to a normal state and that it would be safe to continue the flight to destination. The flight crew contacted dispatch and advised of the occurrence and the need for maintenance at destination. AKT103 landed without further incident.Post flight maintenance inspection found evidence of de-ice fluid ingestion within the APU inlet. The APU was run, and an ops test of pack systems was carried out. The system operated normally, with no odors or vapors present, and checked serviceable.

C-GPTS, an Air Transat Airbus A330-200 was operating flight TSC601 from Daniel Oduber Quirós International Airport (MRLB), Costa Rica, to Montréal/ Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to complete their duties. Duties were redistributed amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-GFSJ, an AirSprint Inc. Cessna 525B was operating flight ASP501 from Witham Field Airport (KSUA), FL, USA, to Lynden Pindling International Airport (MYNN), Bahamas. After starting the engines and completing required checklists, the crew was delayed leaving the ramp due to ground traffic. The crew noted an "Aft Baggage Smoke" CAS message and referenced the emergency quick reference handbook. The crew shut off the air conditioning and shut down the engines. The first officer exited the cabin and opened the aft baggage compartment. When the door was opened, smoke came out and flames were visible in the rear compartment. The captain declared an emergency on the ground frequency and the flames stopped before the fire extinguisher was used by the crew. When the emergency crew arrived, they inspected the aircraft visually with IR cameras and confirmed the fire was out. The aircraft manufacturer inspection found the damage isolated to the Vapour Cycle Cooling System (VCCS) motor and wiring on the drive assembly. The motor drive assembly was removed and replaced with an overhauled unit. Airframe structure, wiring and close proximity components were unaffected.
