The Canadian North ATR 42-500, C-FTID, was operating as flight AKT677 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Cambridge Bay (CYCB), NU. During the initial climb, the flight crew received an AFT SMOKE warning. The aircraft levelled off at 4000 feet ASL and the flight crew actioned the QRH. The flight attendant was contacted and confirmed there was no evidence of smoke or fire in the aft compartment. The crew then completed their checklist and attempted to contact the flight attendant but discovered the PA and interphone were not working. The First Officer indicated that the autopilot had kicked off. The flight crew utilized the ordnance signs to communicate with the flight attendant, who took their seat. A PAN PAN  was declared, and the flight crew requested an immediate return to CYZF. The aircraft landed without further issue and was met on the runway by ARFF. The aircraft was inspected and there were no signs of smoke. The aircraft taxied back to the gate under its own power. There were no injuries. Company maintenance inspected the aircraft. The autopilot system could not be faulted. The aft smoke detector was replaced and plumbing cleaned. The remote-control audio unit (RCAU) was replaced for the PA and interphone issues. The aircraft was returned to service.

UR-82007, un Antonov An-124-100 Ruslan exploité par Antonov Airlines sous l'indicatif ADB5293 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Keflavík International Airport, Islande (BIKF) à destination de Toronto/Lester B.Pearson, ON (CYYZ). À environ 15 NM NNE de Val-d’Or (QC), l’aéronef a rencontré des turbulences. À la suite, un problème avec les commandes de vol est survenu et l’équipage a déclaré une urgence au service de contrôle aérien. Il a demandé un déroutement vers l’aéroport de Montréal Intl (Mirabel), QC (CYMX) où l’aéronef a atterri sans encombre.

C-GHKX, un Airbus A330-343 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA835 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas en Espagne (LEMD) à destination de l'aéroport international Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 286 passagers, 2 membres d’équipage de conduite et 8 membres d’équipage de cabine à bord. À environ 50 NM au sud de Gaspé, QC, un membre de l’équipage de cabine a subi une incapacité physique l'empêchant de continuer ses tâches. Le vol s’est poursuivi jusqu’à destination où il a atterri sans encombre.

C-FSDQ, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 was operating flight AC1323 from Providenciales International Airport (MBPV), Turks and Caicos, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, the crew A system hydraulic contents indicated zero and the engine driven pump low pressure illuminated. PAN PAN was declared with Cleveland ATC. The crew completed their quick reference handbook checklist and continued to destination. The landing was uneventful, and the aircraft was checked on the runway by aircraft rescue and firefighting. The aircraft required a tow back to the gate.

N890LJ, un Learjet 35A privé exploité par TVPX Aircraft Solutions Inc effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Greenville Downtown Airport aux États-Unis (KGMU) à destination de l'aéroport de Goose Bay, NL (CYYR). À environ 35 NM est-sud-est de l’aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV), le copilote a subit une incapacité physique. Le commandant de bord a déclaré un signal de détresse (Mayday) au centre de contrôle régional de Moncton (ACC). Il a demandé une autorisation pour l’approche et l’atterrissage à CYYR et qu’une ambulance soit envoyée sur les lieux. L’aéronef a atterri sans encombre.

C-GUBH, an Air Transat Airbus A330-200 was operating flight TSC1301 from Daniel Oduber Quirós International Airport (MRLB), Costa Rica, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Shortly after takeoff, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and their duties were distributed amongst remaining cabin crew members.

C-GVUO, un A220-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA431 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Toronto/Lester B.Pearson, ON (CYYZ). Immédiatement après avoir décollé de la piste 24L, une indication de surchauffe des freins est apparue. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence au contrôleur aérien et a demandé de revenir se poser sur la piste. L’aéronef a atterri sans encombre et sans surcharge. L’équipe de maintenance a fait une vérification et il s’agissait d’une erreur d’indication.

C-GXAX, a WestJet Boeing 737-8 was operating flight WS2162 from Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, to Cancún International Airport (MMUN), MX. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and their duties were reassigned amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-GYJW, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was operating flight AC79 from Dubai International Airport (OMDB), UAE, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. In cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to continue their duties.

C-FIAS, an AirSprint Inc. Cessna 525A was operating flight ASP511 from Hamilton Airport (CYHM), ON, to Naples Municipal Airport (KAPF), FL, USA. In descent from FL430 the right-hand engine flamed out. The flight crew noted there was still N1 and Oil Pressure so they tried a restart which was unsuccessful. A Mayday was declared and the aircraft was diverted to Orlando International Airport (KMCO).No abnormalities were noted during multiple ground run checks which were completed following the event. FDU was replaced as directed.

C-GJTX, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1674 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL. During cruise phase of flight, at FL320, in the vicinity of CAE VORTAC, the flight crew received ELEC AC BUS 1 FAULT followed by ELEC GEN 1 FAULT and BLUE HYD SYS ECAMs. A/P and A/T disengaged automatically, and the captain's side PFD and ND briefly failed before coming back online. A PAN PAN was declared with ATC and a vector requested while the flight crew carried out ECAM actions. The APU was started to regain electric generating redundancy. The nature of the failure resulted in the loss of a number of associated systems including: SPLR3, L/R/ TK PUMP 1, ALTN BRK, AUTO BRK, and REVERSER 1. The flight continued to KMCO where the longest runway was requested and granted. Full-stop landing was carried out with ARFF on stand-by who carried out external GVI with no faults found. Aircraft subsequently taxied to the gate where the flight was completed without further incident

C-GGMI, a DeHavilland DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation, was conducting flight JZA359 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Windsor International Airport (CYQG), ON. After takeoff, the flight crew observed a nose gear unsafe indication after retracting the gear. The flight crew conducted the alternate gear extension procedure and observed that all 3 landing gear were indicating down and locked. An emergency was declared and the aircraft returned to CYYZ for a safe landing. Due to the alternate gear extension having been employed, the aircraft needed to be towed off the runway.The operator's inspection of the aircraft post-occurrence indicated that the nose landing gear lock had been inadvertently activated during the GPU disconnect procedure.

C-GMIW, a Boeing 737-8 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA422 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During the climb, a flight attendant was hit on the legs by a service trolley and was unable to continue their duties. The flight continued to CYUL uneventfully with the other flight attendants assuming the safety duties.

C-GVUN, an Airbus Canada Limited Partnership BD-500-1A11 (A220-300) operated by Air Canada, was operating flight ACA1102 from Nashville International Airport (KBNA), TN, USA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While in cruise, the flight crew observed a BRAKE CAUTION light. A PAN PAN was declared, and ACA1102 continued to CYYZ where an uneventful landing was completed with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby.The operator's maintenance conducted a post-occurrence inspection and the left brake assembly was replaced.

C-GSGV, a Sanders Geophysics Limited Cessna Caravan 208B, sustained a left main tire rupture on landing at Sanford Raleigh Executive Jetport Airport (KQTT), NC. Upon landing, after the tire ruptured, the brakes locked up. Further deceleration was accomplished through reverse thrust to stop the aircraft. The aircraft veered left, departed the runway surface laterally and came to a stop with the left main landing gear 1 foot off the runway into the grass. The single runway was closed for 1 hour and 50 minutes as a result. There were no injuries or damage to airport property. The only damage observed on the aircraft was the ruptured tire.

C-GJXV, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300 was operating as AC1286 from Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (KPHX), AZ, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise at FL350, approximately 1 hour prior to landing, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency due to a passenger medical emergency. The aircraft landed safety at CYYZ and was met by medical services.

On 26 January 2025, a privately-owned Chinook Plus 2 ultralight (registration: C-IGRK, serial: 02190XS) departed on a visual flight rules flight from a remote cabin approximately 75 NM North of the Faro Airport (CZFA), Yukon eroute to CZFA. Onboard was the pilot and 1 passenger. During the flight to CZFA, strong winds and moderate turbulence were encountered. The pilot elected to fly at lower altitudes (approximately 800 feet AGL) to avoid the strong winds near that tops of the surrounding hills. Approximately 13 NM NNW of CZFA, the aircraft encountered a severe downdraft that caused a rapid, uncontrolled descent. The aircraft began a gradual left turn. At approximately 400 feet AGL, the aircraft experienced a severe updraft that caused the aircraft to stall and to flip inverted. The pilot was unable to recover before the aircraft collided with terrain. The pilot was seriously injured. The passenger had minor injuries. Both occupants were able to exit from the wreckage and notify search and rescue personnel via a satellite messenger. After several hours, the occupants were rescued by a US military helicopter from Anchorage, Alaska. Both occupants were transported to Faro, Yukon for medical treatment.

C-GDJZ, a Mitsubishi CRJ-900 operated by Jazz Aviation was conducting flight AC7780 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB with 4 crew members and 76 passengers on board. During the final approach into CYEG, when the flight crew selected the flaps to 45, they received a FLAPS FAIL caution message. A missed approach was conducted, the QRH was reference, the flight crew requested ARFF to be placed on standby and declared PAN PAN with ATS. An uneventful flap 30 landing was conducted, and the aircraft taxied to the gate without further incident.

C-GHKC, an Air Canada A330 was operating flight AC841 from Frankfurt Main Airport (EDDF), Germany, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Shortly after takeoff a cabin crew member became incapacitated and the other cabin crew members assumed their duties.

C-GHLV, an Air Canada Boeing 767-333 was operating cargo flight AC7231 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD), IL. After thrust reduction for descent into KORD, the LH engine experienced a compressor stall. The LH engine was set to idle power for the remainder of the flight. A PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft landed uneventfully. The aircraft taxied to the gate, the LH engine was shut down and a ENG1 CTRL message was noted.

C-GPDB, a Learjet 45 operated by Sunwest Aviation Ltd. was conducting flight CNK678 from Fort St. John, B.C. (CYXJ), to Calgary Intl., AB. (CYYC) with two crew and four passengers onboard. Departing CYXJ the crew received a "L R OUTBD BRK FAIL" Amber CAS message after gear retraction. The flight crew reviewed the applicable QRH procedure for the fault and approximately 21 NM NW of Sundre, AB (CFN7) contacted ATS and requested ARFF on standby for landing in CYYC. The crew briefed the passengers prior to the landing and an uneventful landing was subsequently completed.

C-GWBF, a WestJet Boeing 737-7CT was operating flight WS1237 from Southwest Florida International Airport (KRSW), FL, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise at FL370, the flight crew observed a traffic advisory (TA) from JZA836 500 feet above, descending through FL370 and positioned at their 1 o'clock position. Aircraft WS1237 did not receive an ATC traffic report. The TA then escalated into a resolution advisory (RA) necessitating a descent. WS1237 initiated the descent and through the maneouvre, the first officer spotted the traffic at a perceived distance of 200 feet above the right-wing tip. WS1237 advised ATC and continued their flight. Occurrence was reported to NTSB and FAA. Pending review to validate contributing factors and actual separation.

C-FGKJ, a Boeing 757-200 operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd, was conducting IFR flight CJT2402 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Hamilton/John C. Munro International Airport (CYHM), ON. While in cruise at flight level 390, the flight crew observed a "CABIN ALT" engine indicating and crew alerting system message and the associated aural warning chimed. The flight crew confirmed that the cabin altitude was greater than 10 000 feet on the pressurization panel and actioned the quick-reference-handbook checklist. An emergency descent to 10 000 feet ASL was coordinated with air traffic control and the aircraft subsequently landed at CYHM without further event.The operator's maintenance replaced the #1 cabin pressure controller. The system was function checked serviceable and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FIPY, un hélicoptère privé Robinson R44 II effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à l’aéroport de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC) avec un pilote et un passager à bord. À environ 24 NM au NE de CYQB, le signal sonore de bas régime du rotor principal s’est activé. Le pilote a baissé le collectif et entendu le moteur s’arrêter. Le pilote a effectué une autorotation et atterri dans la cour d’un chalet à environ 2 NM à l’ouest du Mont Sainte-Anne (QC). Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. L’hélicoptère a subi des dommages au train d’atterrissage.

C-GUWJ, a Westjet Boeing 737-700, was operating as flight WS461, under instrument flight rules (IFR), from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC. At the time of the occurrence, the weather at CYLW was ceilings of 1100 feet above ground level with and visibility of 2 ½ statute miles. The IFR weather required air traffic control (ATC) to maintain a minimum of 12 nautical miles horizontal distance between aircraft. The ATC that controlled the initial approach of the flight consisted of a controller in training under supervision from the Vancouver Area Control Centre (ACC). The pilot requested the RNAV X 16 approach via the EBLEL intersection but was given vectors to the north due to the spacing requirements. ATC briefly cleared the crew to intercept the NORIP FIVE standard arrival procedure before the flight was put back on vectors for their approach. After ATC determined there was adequate spacing, the flight crew were given a southerly vector and cleared to conduct the RNAV X 16 approach. The aircraft was flown west of the initial way point for the approach. The flight crew then turned left and intercepted a direct track to the threshold of Runway 16 and continued to descend. The aircraft was 1 nautical mile west of track when the ACC passed the pilot to the CYLW tower controller. When the aircraft was approximately 10 nautical miles north of the threshold of Runway 16, the supervising ACC controller advised the CYLW tower controller that the aircraft was 600 feet low on the approach. The CYLW tower controller relayed to the crew that they were 600 feet low on the approach. The crew acknowledged the radio call. The aircraft continued and landed without incident. Westjet Airlines and Nav Canada are both investigating the incident.

C-GWBU, a Westjet Boeing 737-800, was conducting flight WJA2177 from Cancún International Airport (MMUN), MX, to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC. On approach, while the flight crew were selecting initial flaps, they received a Trailing Edge Flap Disagree caution message. The flight crew conducted a missed approach and requested vectors to complete the non-normal checklist. Once the checklist was completed, the aircraft approached and landed safely with flaps set to 15. Maintenance inspection found that the Proximity Switch Electonic Unit had an existing fault landing flap disagree. Maintenance carried out the Fault Isolation Manual task and then cycled the flaps several times with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GGNZ, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was conducting flight JZA8462, under instrument flight rules, from Smithers Airport (CYYD), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During the initial climb from CYYD, the aircraft experienced severe turbulence between 5000 and 12 000 feet above sea level (ASL) which affected aircraft controllability and caused the autopilot to disengage. As a result of the turbulence, the minimum airspeed could not be maintained during climb, so the flight crew leveled the aircraft until they were able to climb again. No injuries were reported.The aircraft was removed from service for a turbulence inspection which found that the tension of the left and right aileron control cables was low. The cables were tensioned, an independent inspection was completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

N226AF, a Pilatus PC-12/47E operated by PlaneSense Inc., was operating a flight from Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Bedford/Laurence G Hanscom Field Airport (KBED), MA, USA. Shortly after takeoff from CYTZ, the aircraft's stick shaker and stall warning systems activated. The pilot flying reduced the angle of attack and increased the airspeed; however, the stick shaker and stall warning continued. The flight crew declared an emergency and returned to CYTZ for an uneventful landing. The stick pusher did not activate and the pilot flying pressed and held the stick pusher interrupt button until landing. Following the occurrence, the operator's maintenance arranged an inspection, and the left angle-of-attack probe was tested unserviceable. The probe was replaced, and the aircraft was subsequently returned to service.

C-FXRJ, un Avro 146-100 exploité par Summit Air Ltd , effectuait le vol SUT8083 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport d'Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) à destination de l'aérodrome de Mary River, NU (CMR2). En voie de retour à CYFB pour cause de mauvaise météo à CMR2, un voyant "Low Fuel Feed" s'est illuminé. L'équipage a alors déclaré une urgence afin d'obtenir une priorité d'atterrissage à CYFB. L'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre avec encore 2020 lbs de carburant à bord.

C-FZNQ, an Air Nunavut Beechcraft 200 was operating flight BFF202 from Baker Lake Airport (CYBK), NU, to Rankin Inlet Airport (CYRT), NU. When the flight crew selected gear up after takeoff from CYBK, the main gear stayed down but the nose gear retracted. The flight crew continued to climb and once clear of obstacles, cycled the landing gear. The main gear remained extended, but the nose gear went to a partially extended position. The flight crew then attempted to use the alternate gear extension system; however, there was no change in gear configuration. The flight crew declared an emergency and the aircraft continued to CYRT. The flight crew conducted a low pass at CYRT and ground-based staff reported that the nose landing gear appeared to be only partially down. The aircraft subsequently landed on Runway 31 with the main landing gear down and locked and the nose landing gear partially extended. Upon touchdown, the flight crew shut down the engines. The aircraft came to a rest halfway down the runway. The two flight crew members and 6 passengers were able to egress the aircraft with no injuries. Aircraft rescue and firefighting were on scene and assisted with the aircraft evacuation. The left and right propellers sustained damage to two blades each and the nose gear doors were damaged.Upon inspection, the operator's maintenance found a shredded O-ring in the landing gear selector valve and a broken wire in the cannon plug connection for the landing gear hydraulic system pressure switch. The selector valve and cannon plug were replaced. The gear extension and retraction system were tested, as well as the emergency extension system with no faults found.

C-FFFX, a Boeing 737-8 (Max 8) aircraft operated by Flair Airlines Limited, was conducting flight FLE802 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. On the takeoff roll, just prior to rotation, a loud bang was heard from the area near the nose gear. The aircraft rotated normally, and after landing gear retraction, the red light for the nose gear remained illuminated. The crew levelled the aircraft at 3000 feet above sea level to assess the situation. The Gear Disagree checklist was accomplished however the problem was not rectified. The crew decided to return to CYVR, and a PAN PAN was declared. While being vectored by air traffic control (ATC), a traffic collision avoidance system resolution advisory (RA) occurred. The flight crew initiated a climb as per the RA instructions, and ATC was advised. In preparation for landing, the landing gear was extended normally with 3 green lights which indicated that all landing gear was down and locked. After landing, emergency vehicles inspected the aircraft and noticed fluid leaking from the nose gear area. The aircraft taxied slowly to the gate and emergency vehicles followed. Maintenance found the nose oleo fully compressed and a seal leaking. The nose wheel seals were replaced as per Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) 32-21-11 and a nose wheel function test was performed in accordance with AMM 32-51-00. The nose wheel strut servicing pressure was re-checked and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FERF, un Piper PA-23-250 exploité par Cargair Ltée, effectuait un vol local d'entraînement selon les règles de vol à vue à partir de l'aéroport MET - Aéroport métropolitain de Montréal, QC (CYHU) avec 1 instructeur et 1 élève-pilote à bord. Lors de la descente du train d'atterrissage en approche de CYHU seulement deux voyants verts se sont illuminés. Après quelques tentatives infructueuses de régler le problème, le pilote a décidé de remettre les gaz et a déclaré une urgence. Lors de la deuxième approche, le voyant manquant s'est illuminé de lui-même. L'aéronef a ensuite atterri sans encombre. Une inspection subséquente par la maintenance a révélé un microcontact défectueux.

C-GPCL, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited Beech 1900D, was operating flight 8P8994, under instrument flight rules, from Anahim Lake Airport (CAJ4), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew members and 1 aircraft maintenance engineer on board. During cruise flight, in light icing conditions, the master caution light illuminated due to a right-hand pitot heat failure. The flight crew was able to reset the pitot heat and continued cruise flight. During decent to CYVR in moderate icing conditions, moderate turbulence, and poor weather, the right-hand pitot heat failed again. Subsequently, multiple electrical system failures occurred which affected the aircraft’s communication, stabilization, and navigations systems. As a result of the failures, the flight crew contacted air traffic control and declared a PAN PAN and requested a lower altitude to get out of the icing conditions. The aircraft landed safely at CYVR.Maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft and found moisture in the right-hand pitot system and in the battery bay. They also found 2 corroded battery switch diodes. The defects were rectified, function checks were carried out and the aircraft was returned to service. The flight crew was provided a stand-down period of 24 hours as a precaution against any physical or mental post-occurrence issues.

N360FX, a Flexjet LLC, Embraer Executive Aircraft Incorporated EMB-505 (Phenom 300) conducted flight LXJ360, under instrument flight rules, from Jackson Hole Airport (KJAC), WY, USA, to Kelowna International Airport (CYLW), BC. During the approach to CYLW, the flight crew received a flap fail message and observed that the flap indication on the multi-function display (MFD) was different than the flap setting selected by the flight crew. The flight crew executed a missed approach and consulted the flap failure checklist. They then contacted air traffic control and declared an emergency. After determining that the aircraft’s flap configuration was suitable for landing at CYLW, the crew landed without further incident.Maintenance personnel performed an electrical reset and then carried out multiple operational checks of the flaps system with no faults found.

C-GTJX, a Transwest Air Ltd. (dba Rise Air) SAAB 340B, was on a flight from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK to Fond-du-Lac Airport (CZFD), SK. While on route, the flight crew noticed a stiff right power lever. While troubleshooting, the right engine torque dropped to 0 and the engine appeared to auto-coarsen. The flight crew conducted the precautionary shutdown procedure of the right-hand engine and declared an emergency. The flight crew diverted to Stony Rapids (CYSF), SK where the aircraft landed safely.Upon inspection by the operator's maintenance, it was noted that the stiff control linkage was likely caused by moisture ingression and freezing. They noticed that during the cleaning and purge of a right-hand cable segment from the nacelle to the engine, a black residue was noted. The segment was replaced and all engine controls were subsequently inspected and tested, with no further faults were found.

C-GDEW, a DeHavilland DHC-8-400 aircraft being operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting and IFR flight from Regina International Airport (CYQR) SK. to Calgary International Airport (CYYC) AB. During the climb out from CYQR at 2000 feet, the fuselage door warning light illuminated. The First Officer, who was the pilot flying, stopped climbing at 6500 feet and descended to 6000 feet after the Captain declared a PAN PAN. The flight crew went through the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) and determined that the best option was to return to CYQR. Air Traffic Control was notified and provided vectors for the return to CYQR. During the return to CYQR the fuselage door warning light intermittently flashed on and off. The aircraft landed safely back at CYQR.The operator's maintenance department inspected the forward baggage door proximity switches. They warmed and dried the switches to remove moisture. An operational test of the forward baggage door was conducted and was deemed serviceable.

C-GTWE, a DeHavilland DHC-8-400 aircraft being operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting an IFR flight from Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK. to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the takeoff roll, the First Officer's Primary Flight Display (PFD) failed to indicate airspeed. The takeoff was rejected with a MAYDAY declared as per company Standard Operating Procedure (SOP). The aircraft taxied off the runway and the crew contacted the operator's maintenance department. The flight crew was advised by maintenance to attempt another takeoff. On the second takeoff attempt, the FO's PFD failed to indicate airspeed. The takeoff was rejected with another MAYDAY being declared. The crew canceled MAYDAY and returned to the gate.The operator's maintenance department conducted an inspection of the #2 Air Data Unit (ADU) and discovered a fitting was not fully seated. The fittings were removed and reinstalled. Subsequent testing of the #2 ADU revealed no other faults.

C-FZQE, a Cessna 150M registered to Millennium Aviation Ltd., was performing training circuits at Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. While performing a touch-and-go landing on Runway 27, the aircraft veered left off the runway and came into contact with a snowbank. The nose gear collapsed and the aircraft came to a stop off the runway. The sole occupant of the aircraft was able to egress the aircraft without injuries. The ELT did activate. ARFF attended the scene. The aircraft's right wing and propeller were substantially damaged.

C-FEJF, a Jazz Aviation Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU was operating flight JZA553 from John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), NY, USA, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. After departure, the crew was selecting flap setting 1 to 0 when the crew received an ICAS message. The crew performed the quick reference handbook checklist, with no fix. Aircraft requested to return to KJFK where they landed uneventfully with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby. The fire department checked the brakes and followed the aircraft to the gate.

C-FYJE, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was operating ROU1879 from Hewanorra International Airport (TLPL), St. Lucia, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Shortly after takeoff, flight crew detected a fuel odour that gradually intensified. The cabin crew also reported the fuel odour. The climb was discontinued at 15 000 feet to diagnose the issue. Fuel calculations showed no indication of a leak. The fumes checklist was actioned, and a return to TLPL was planned. Flight crew declared PAN PAN, completed the overweight checklist and requested emergency trucks for a visual inspection on the runway. Aircraft landed uneventfully and fire trucks inspected the aircraft upon landing and no leaks were found.

C-FTCA, a Boeing 767-375 operated by Air Canada, was conducting an IFR flight from Chicago/O'Hare International (KORD), USA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International (CYYZ), ON. On approach to CYYZ, the flight crew observed a "Leading Edge Slat Disagree" Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) message. The flight crew conducted a missed approach and declared a PAN PAN with air traffic control. The flight crew completed the relevant quick reference handbook checklist and completed a second approach at CYYZ where the aircraft landed without further incident.The operator's maintenance subsequently completed an inspection and functional test of the flap/slat system, and no faults were found.

C-FNNW, an Air Canada B777-300 was operating flight AC870 from Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Charles-de-Galle Airport (LFPG), France. During cruise a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to continue their duties; their duties were distributed among remaining cabin crew.

C-GFAF, an Air Canada Airbus A330-343 was operating flight AC865 from London Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK, to Montréal / Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. A cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to perform duties; their duties were assigned to remaining cabin crew.

C-GBKG, a Cessna 172N registered to Mitchinson Flying Service Ltd., was on a local training flight from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK to Birch Hills Airport (CJD3), SK. C-GBKG was conducting a low approach into CJD3 when the aircraft completed an unintended touch down onto Runway 09. The aircraft veered off the left-hand side of the runway and came into contact with deep snow. The aircraft began a skid which resulted in the aircraft contacting a windrow of approximately 3 feet in height located on the runway edge. The aircraft subsequently flipped over and came to rest inverted. The instructor and the student were able to egress the aircraft without injury. The ELT activated. There was no post-impact fire or rupture of the aircraft fuel tanks.A post-accident inspection by the operator revealed the engine and propeller were damaged from the sudden stoppage. There was substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and tail of the aircraft.

C-GVDU, un Cessna 150M exploité par Aéroclub de Montréal Inc. effectuait un vol local d'entraînement selon les règles de vol à vue partir de l'aéroport MET - Aéroport métropolitain de Montréal, QC (CYHU) avec un instructeur de vol et un élève-pilote à bord. Alors que l'aéronef se trouvait au-dessus de St-Bruno de Montarville, QC, en vent arrière pour la piste 24 gauche, le moteur de l'aéronef (Continental O-200-A) a commencé à subir des ratés. Le pilote a déclaré une urgence et a tenté de rallier CYHU. Le régime moteur a continué de varier autour des 1000 RPM malgré la manette des gaz à fond avant de s'arrêter complètement. Déjà à basse altitude, le pilote a alors décidé d'effectuer un atterrissage d'urgence dans un champ enneigé en bordure de l'autoroute 30. Au moment du toucher des roues, l'avion a piqué du nez et s'est retourné sur le dos. Les deux occupants ont évacué l'aéronef promptement et n'ont pas été blessés. Un hélicoptère qui se trouvait tout près a recueilli les occupants et les a ramenés aux installations Aéroclub de Montréal Inc. à CYHU où ils ont été vus par des ambulanciers. Il n'y a pas eu d'incendie et la balise (ELT) s'est déclenchée et son signal a été capté par le centre conjoint de coordination des opérations de sauvetage (CCCOS) de Trenton, ON. Une inspection subséquente par la maintenance a révélé la défaillance d'une valve du cylindre no. 1.

C-GJLZ, a Westjet B737-800 was operating flight WS1631 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During cruise a cabin crew fell ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst remaining crew.

C-FYJP, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1659 from Tampa International Airport (KTPA), FL, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During climb, the In-Charge Flight Attendant notified the flight crew via intercom of a fuel odour in the forward galley. Initial efforts to isolate/determine the source of the odour were inconclusive and decision to return to origin was made. The flight and cabin crew donned supplemental oxygen masks, requested return to KTPA, descent to 10 000 feet and subsequently declared MAYDAY as a precaution. During descent, the flight crew carried out applicable quick reference handbook procedures including REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES which resulted in an increase of cabin pressure altitude in excess of 9000 feet as the flight descended through FL220. Flight crew then expedited descent to 10 000 feet and manually deployed passenger supplemental oxygen. The aircraft subsequently landed at KTPA RWY 19R with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby and taxied to the gate without further incident.

C-FTJC, a Carson Air Limited Cessna 560 Citation Encore was conducting a medevac flight as CRN999, under instrument flight rules, from Smithers Airport (CYYD), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. While cruising at flight level (FL)390, the flight crew noted that the cabin altitude was 7000 feet and the cabin pressure differential was below the maximum, which was abnormal. As a precaution, the flight crew contacted air traffic control (ATC) and requested a lower altitude. They were cleared and then descended to FL290. When the aircraft reached FL290, the cabin pressure differential decreased further, and the cabin altitude climbed to 8000 feet. Shortly after, the high cabin altitude (CABIN ALT HI) warning light illuminated as the cabin altitude had increased to 10 000 feet. In accordance with procedures, the flight crew donned their oxygen masks, deployed the passenger oxygen masks, and declared a PAN PAN with ATC. The crew requested a routing towards lower terrain. When the aircraft was able to descend below 12 000 feet above sea level, the flight crew removed their oxygen masks. Emergency and normal checklists were completed, and the aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident. Maintenance personnel conducted various functional tests and inspections but were unable to find any defects with the aircraft that would have caused the pressurization issue experienced. The aircraft was released to service after a satisfactory pressurization test flight.

C-GZNS, a Mitsubishi MU-2B-60 aircraft operated by Thunder Airlines, was conducting an IFR flight from Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON, to Sandy Lake Airport (CZSJ), ON. During the climb at approximately 60 nautical miles north-northwest of CYXL, the right-hand engine began indicating oil pressure and torque fluctuations. Shortly thereafter, the oil pressure and torque indications both dropped to zero, and the flight crew shut down the right-hand engine. The aircraft diverted to Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON, where airport emergency response was standing by. The aircraft made an uneventful landing at CYQT.The operator's maintenance department observed that the right-hand engine oil filter housing was cracked and is replacing the engine.

C-GLQL a Porter Airlines Dash 8 (POE260) on a flight from Greater Moncton Roméo LeBlanc International Airport, NB (CYQM) to Ottawa Macdonald–Cartier International Airport, ON (CYOW) with 62 SOB declared an emergency during descent due to an indications of zero oil quantity on the #2 engine. The crew elected to shut down the engine. The aircraft landed safely at CYOW at 2227Z (1727 EST). Upon landing, the aircraft was taxied clear of the runway and inspected by emergency vehicles on site. After emergency crews confirmed that the engine was secure, the aircraft was taxied to just before the gate, and was towed to the stop line by the ground crew. All passengers exited the aircraft normally.

N932XJ, a CL-600-2D24 (CRJ-900) manufactured by Bombardier Inc, was operating as Endeavor Airlines flight EDV4819 from Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport (KMSP), MN, USA, to Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the landing on Runway 23, the aircraft impacted the runway, the right wing detached and a fire ensued. The aircraft overturned, and slid down the runway inverted, coming to rest near the intersection of Runway 23 and 15L. Aircraft rescue and firefighting responded, and all passengers and crew evacuated.

C-FYJE, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1833 from V.C. Bird International Airport (TAPA), Antigua and Barbuda, to Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Shortly after takeoff, as the flight climbed through approximately 800 feet AGL, the flight crew began to receive multiple successive aural alerts related to the RADALT system, specifically aural automated callouts related to landing gear position and throttle position which would normally be annunciated during the flare and landing phases of flight. The flight crew determined the alerts to be erroneous, stopped the climb at 11 000 feet AGL and elected to return to TAPA. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft entered the published hold at EMALI in order to troubleshoot. After consulting with Maintenance Operations Control (MOC), the flight crew pulled the RALT 2 circuit breaker that ceased the continuous aural alerts and resolved the condition. The aircraft carried out a full stop landing in TAPA RWY 07, overweight, with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby.

C-FTXE, a Sunwing B737-8 was operating flight SWG4167 from Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), DR to Winnipeg Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. During cruise, a flight attendant became incapacitated and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned with the remaining cabin crew.

C-GAAS, an AirSprint Cessna 525B, was operating flight ASP567 from Tampa International Airport (KTPA), FL, to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. At the start of descent into CYUL, passing through FL400, the First Officer (FO) heard a loud hiss coming from the door. The FO immediately called for oxygen masks and the flight crew proceeded to put the oxygen masks on. The FO noticed the cabin altitude climb at a rate from 2500 fpm to 3500 fpm. The FO selected the mic to oxygen mask and began to execute an emergency descent and informed Boston center. Boston center cleared the aircraft to 8000 feet. The FO could not hear the captain through the intercom as they later found out his mic cord for his oxygen mask was not fully plugged in. During descent, the FO requested priority handling in the event they would have to divert. During the descent the crew identified a master warning "cabin altitude" light come on. Once the crew leveled at 8000 feet the cabin pressure altitude matched the aircraft altitude, and they elected to take off the oxygen masks and put their headsets on. The crew noted that they had enough fuel to continue to CYUL. The flight then continued without further incident.

C-FJGZ, a Jazz Aviation LP, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries CL-600-2D24 (CRJ 900) departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, operating as flight JZA480, under instrument flight rules, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. During cruise flight, a flight attendant became incapacitated. A medical emergency was declared and the flight diverted back to CYVR.

N437YX, an Embraer ERJ 170-200LR operated by Republic Airways Inc., was conducting flight RPA4438/AA4438 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Int'l Airport (CYYZ), ON, to New York/La Guardia (KLGA), NY, USA. Shortly after departure from Runway 23, the flight crew encountered an issue with the bleed air system. After actioning the appropriate checklists, the crew elected to return to CYYZ and declared an emergency. ARFF was present for the landing, which was uneventful.

C-FZCV, a Skyservice Business Aviation Inc. Gulfstream G280, was on a flight from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the take-off in CYEG, the crew heard a loud noise coming from the area of the nose landing gear. The crew received no warning messages, and after contacting CYEG tower, they reported no debris on the runway. The flight crew elected to continue to CYYZ but on approach declared a PAN PAN as a precaution. Maintenance performed a visual inspection of the nose landing gear and surrounding area and found no damage. A pressure check of the nose landing gear strut was performed and the aircraft was returned to service.

N12MF, un Fairchild SA226-T(B) exploité par Kenmore Crew Leasing Inc Trustee, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport international de Bangor, ME, USA (KBGR) à destination de l'aéroport de Goose Bay, NFL (CYYR). Alors que l'aéronef était en vol de croisière à environ 20 miles nautiques de Gaspé, QC , l'équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison d'un pare-brise fissuré et à avisé d'un changement de destination sans demandé assistance. L'aéronef est retourné attérir à son point de départ.

C-GAIW, un DeHavilland DHC-8-300 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif AIE885, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Radisson La Grande-Rivière , QC (CYGL) à destination de l'aéroport de Umiujaq, QC (CYMU) avec 3 membres d'équipage à bord. Après le décollage de CYGL, l'équipage a observé la quantité du système hydraulique #2 diminuée. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) avant de revenir vers CYGL. L'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre à CYGL attendu par les services d'urgence et a sorti de piste sur son propre pouvoir.

C-GWJO, a Westjet B737 was operating flight WJA1448 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), NV. While in cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and did not occupy jumpseat for landing.

O-KTVJ, a Boeing 737-NG operated by Sunwing Airlines Ltd. was conducting flight SWG464 from Halifax / Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to Gregorio Luperón International Airport (MDPP), Dominican Republic. C-FSXG, Beech King Air C-90A operated by Moncton Flight College was on a training flight from Fredericton International Airport (CYFC), NB, to CYHZ and returning to CYFC. C-FSXG was on the ILS approach to Runway 23 and planned to conduct a missed approach, while SWG464 was departing the adjacent Runway 32. After take-off and the initial climb there was a loss of separation laterally (actual distance 2.5NM / required separation was 3.0NM) and risk of collision between SWG464 and C-FSXG as they completed the missed approach.

C-FSCY, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight AC933 from Cancun International Airport (MMUN), MX, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. On departure, the crew received a Master Caution light, with the associated Hydraulic Eng 2 low pressure light. The crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC, completed the relevant checklists and elected to return to MMUN where the aircraft landed uneventfully and was towed to the gate.

C-FDHU, an Air Canada A330-343 was operating flight AC1275 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, NV. During cruise, approximately 50 NM east of Dove creek, Colorado, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence at FL400. The crew requested and descended to FL360, the seat belt signs were illuminated at the time and two passengers sustained minor injuries. The crew requested EMS as a precaution for the injured passengers after landing in KLAS.

C-GSUI, a North Cariboo Flying Service Ltd British Aerospace Avro 146 Series RJ100, was operating flight NCB1540, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC. During the initial descent, the flight crew noticed that the No. 3 engine (Avco Lycoming LF-507-1F) oil pressure was below the operating range and that the pressure continued to drop with the reduction of engine power. The crew actioned the quick reference handbook checklist and performed a precautionary inflight shutdown of the No. 3 engine. The crew continued the approach, notified the cabin crew, passengers, and air traffic control. The aircraft landed safely. Maintenance found that the No. 3 engine oil pressure indicator had failed and was deferred under the minimum equipment list (MEL). The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FYJH, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was operating flight ROU1784 from Cancun International Airport (MMUN), Mexico, to Halifax / Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. On the landing roll out, the aircraft experienced nil braking action due the runway surface conditions, and the wind began to weather-vane the aircraft 20 degrees into the wind and the flight crew had difficulty controlling the centerline. The flight crew regained control with manual braking and reverse thrust. A secondary controllability issue occurred, and the flight crew completed a similar technique to regain directional control. The aircraft exited the runway and taxied to the ramp without further incident.

C-FGQE, a Top Aces A-4N was returning to Mesa Gateway Airport (KIWA), AZ, to land after completion of Functional Check Flight. Following ‘Landing Gear Down’ selection, an intermittent RH Main Landing Gear UNSAFE gear indication presented. The approach was discontinued, and an emergency was declared with ATC. A low approach with visual inspection by the tower and Top Aces maintenance was performed. The landing gear visually appeared down and the Wheels Warning light in the cockpit was extinguished providing indications the LG was down and locked. The pilot completed associated emergency checklist procedures, then landed in KIWA without further incident. The aircraft stopped on the runway where the gear was pinned, then taxied to the ramp for parking.

C-GNRL, a Piper PA-28-140 operated by General Lee Aviation, was conducting a local student pilot solo flight from Lacombe (CEG3), AB. During the landing back at CEG3, directional control of the aircraft was lost, and the aircraft exited the west side of the runway approximately 1200 feet from the threshold of Runway 35 and entered the accumulated snow on the side of the runway. The nosewheel fork broke, and the propeller/engine cowl and remaining nose gear components made contact with the ground. The pilot exited the aircraft, there were no injuries.

C-GZBW, a privately operated Piper PA-28RT-201T was conducting a private local flight from Josephburg Aerodrome (CFB6), AB, with a pilot and three passengers on board. This was the third flight of the day, and the previous flights had been uneventful. During the initial take-off roll, the right landing gear retracted/collapsed. The right wing made contact with the runway as well as the aircraft entry step on the right side. The aircraft came to a stop on the runway and all personnel evacuated the aircraft; there were no injuries. Subsequent investigation found damage to the right flap, aileron and wingtip, as well as the lower right side of the fuselage.

C-GBKB, a Bombardier Challenger 605 (CL-600-2B16) operated by Aurora Jet Partners was conducting a flight from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Palms Springs International Airport (KPSP), CA, USA. During the initial climb after take-off, the flight crew attempted to retract the flaps and received a Flaps Fail message and the flaps did not retract. The flight crew requested a hold at 6000 feet to complete the required checklists and burn sufficient fuel to be at the aircraft maximum landing weight for the return to CYEG. During the approach into CYEG, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATS and requested emergency services on standby for the arrival. An uneventful landing was completed. Company maintenance reset the flap system, ground checks were successfully completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

N402LC, a Lockheed L382G (C-130) operated by Lynden Air Cargo, was conducting flight LYC402 from Santa Maria International Airport (LPAZ), Azores, Portugal, to St. John’s international Airport (CYYT) NL. On the approach into CYYT, the flight crew received a propellor No. 1 warning. As a result, the engine was shut down as a precaution. The flight crew declared an emergency and based on the weather and runway conditions, a decision was made to divert to Halifax Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. The flight landed without further incident. Maintenance was performed on the aircraft and the aircraft was returned to service.

N642FE, a Federal Express Corp. McDonnell Douglas MD-11F was operating flight FDX247 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Memphis International Airport (KMEM), TN. The crew declared an emergency during departure due to an engine failure on the number 3 engine. The flight crew elected to return to (CYYZ). The aircraft landed without further incident and taxied to the gate under its own power.Maintenance is currently examining the engine to determine if an engine change will be required.

C-FZXI, a Sunwing Airlines Boeing 737-8, flight SWG7182, was being pushed back from the gate at infield terminal when the tail cone hit a blast fence. The flight and ground crew were not aware of the impact until after the aircraft had been pulled forward and a normal engine start. The damage to the tail cone was noticed by the ground crew. The tug was disconnected and the aircraft taxied back into position at the gate. Sunwing maintenance found damage to the aircraft tail cone, the APU exhaust duct muffler, and the lower aft heat blanket. The aircraft is undergoing repairs to the affected areas.

C-GJZR, a Jazz Aviation De Havilland DHC-8-400 operating as flight JZA7714, was on the approach to Ottawa/ Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. The flight crew selected the landing gear down and received a nose gear red unsafe light, yellow nose gear door open, and an irregular noise coming from the nose gear. The flight crew carried out a missed approach, referenced the quick reference handbook and did a manual gear extension. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed on RWY 25 without any further issue.

C-FSJR, AirSprint flight ASP877, an Embraer EMB-550 was inbound to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, when the "BRAKE LH FAULT" and "FLT CNTRL NO DXP" CAS messages were displayed almost simultaneously. The flight crew conducted the relevant checklists and declared a PAN PAN to have emergency equipment standing by in case of a runway excursion. Landing was on RWY32 due to winds and longest runway available. The flight crew elected to use reverse thrust only to slow the aircraft to approximately 20kts then gently test brakes before attempting to vacate the runway. The CAS message cleared itself at about 60kts. The captain performed the landing and once aircraft controllability was assured, cancelled aircraft rescue and firefighting assistance and taxied to Skyservice normally.

C-GNCD, a Beech B200 operated by SkyNorth Air, was operating IFR flight SN867 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB. While on approach to Runway 24 at CYTH, the flight crew noted that the right-hand main landing gear light was not illuminated upon gear extension. A go-around was conducted and the aircraft held north of the airport. The crew referenced the quick reference handbook (QRH) and changed light bulbs; however, the light remained extinguished. After consulting with the operator's maintenance by phone, the crew further troubleshot the situation and noted that the gear horn and the TAWS warnings could not be heard. A low pass was conducted and Thompson Radio indicated that they could see both main gears. The flight crew declared an emergency, aircraft rescue and firefighting was placed on standby, and the aircraft landed uneventfully at CYTH.

C-FNSV, a North Cariboo Flying Service Beech 1900D was operating as flight NCB260 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Fort Smith Airport (CYSM), NT. After departure from CYEG, as the aircraft climbed through 10 000 feet ASL, the first officer noticed a fuel trail originating from the right wing. The crew declared an emergency and the aircraft was given vectors to return to CYEG. Upon completing an uneventful landing, the crew consulted with fire response personnel and then taxied back to the apron under escort from aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) vehicles.Once the aircraft was secured, it was inspected by company maintenance personnel, who determined that there was no fuel leak, and that the fuel was being vented from the main wing tank vent as per design parameters.

D-AIKB, an Airbus A330-343 operated by EW Discover GmbH, was operating flight OCN77 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Frankfurt Airport (EDDF), Germany. Shortly after take-off the flight crew observed a smell similar to diesel in the cockpit. After confirming with the cabin crew that the smell existed throughout the cabin, the flight crew elected to return to Calgary. A Pan Pan was initiated by ATC. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks, and the aircraft made an uneventful overweight landing in CYYC. Upon landing the brakes were inspected by ARFF and then the aircraft taxied back to the gate under its own power.

C-GTWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3566 from Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International Airport (CYXC), BC, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While intercepting the ILS for Runway 35L, the crew observed the #1 AC GEN caution light illuminate, which was accompanied by an increase of torque and a decrease in propeller RPM on the number 1 engine. Before the quick reference handbook could be actioned by the crew, the engine parameters returned to normal. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and conducted a missed approach. The aircraft was vectored to conduct the ILS 35L approach and landed without further incident. Following the flight, company maintenance replaced the NR-4 and NR-7 PEC and the PCU. The aircraft was ground run, and no further faults were found.

C-GENK, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 was operating as flight WEN3198, under instrument flight rules, from Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. During initial climb, the aircraft encountered a flock of birds and 1 bird struck the windshield. The crew inspected the windshield and identified a potential crack on the right windshield. The crew followed the quick reference handbook and decided to return to CYLW. The crew descended and advised the cabin crew and air traffic control. No emergency was declared and the aircraft landed safely. Maintenance replaced the right windshield and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GGNZ, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, operating as flight JZA441, under instrument flight rules, to Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC, with 2 flight crew members, 2 flight attendants, and 72 passengers onboard. During the takeoff from Runway 08R, the crew observed an abnormal vibration in the aircraft and suspected a blown tire. The crew contacted Vancouver Area Control Centre and requested an inspection on Runway 08R for tire debris. CYVR ground crews confirmed that tire debris was found on the runway during snow removal. The crew elected to return to CYVR and declared an emergency. A passenger advised the crew that the damaged tire could be on the left main gear. On final approach, the company dispatch asked CYVR tower to advise the crew that a checklist for a main landing gear tire failure needed to be completed prior to landing. The crew initiated a missed approach, confirmed the checklist was completed, and landed without issue. The aircraft was inspected by aircraft rescue and firefighting services before it taxied to the terminal. Maintenance found the left inboard main landing gear tire had blown and had caused minor damage to the inboard landing gear door and the lower panel of the engine nacelle. Maintenance replaced both tires, the inboard brake, and the inboard speed transducer on the left main landing gear. Temporary repairs were completed on the landing gear door and engine nacelle.

C-GGNF, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, operating as flight JZA8089, under instrument flight rules, to Prince Rupert Airport (CYPR), BC, with 2 flight crew members, 2 flight attendants, and 75 passengers onboard. During the approach, the aircraft encountered moderate turbulence at approximately 6000 feet above ground level (AGL). The turbulence became severe at approximately 1000 feet AGL. The flight crew momentarily lost control of the aircraft with significant fluctuations in pitch and airspeed. The crew elected to go around and diverted to Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC. The aircraft landed safely and there were no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft. Maintenance downloaded the flight data recorder and determined that the severe turbulence event was within the aircraft limitations. No further maintenance action was required.

C-FMIJ, a Cargojet B767 was operating flight CJT372 from East Midlands Airport (EGNX), UK, to Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (KCVG), KY. At an altitude of approximately 8000 feet, the crew got a Flap Disagree EICAS message and consulted the Flap Configuration quick reference handbook (QRH). The MCC advised to turn back to EGNX. The crew declared a PAN PAN and squawking 7700, proceeded with fuel jettison procedures to decrease the weight to below the maximum landing weight necessary for the return to East Midlands. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FSLU, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight AC1035 from Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise the flight encountered moderate turbulence. A flight attendant sustained an injury and was unable to continue their duties. Medlink was contacted by the crew. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

OK-TSR, a Sunwing Boeing 737-800 was operating flight SWG720. The crew reported a tail strike on departure from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. The flight crew requested a return to CYYZ and carried out an overweight landing without further incident. No emergency was declared, and no assistance was requested.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and found only minor scrapping damage to the tailskid that was within limits. An overweight landing check was completed and the aircraft departed for the original destination.

C-FJZN, a Jazz CRJ900 was operating flight JZA901 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD), IL. On final, smoke AFT LAV warning and fire alarm went off. A Pan Pan was declared and the flight landed without incident. No smoke was noticed. A flight attendant checked the lav door, it was cool to the touch, then the captain investigated and noticed the mirror was warm and removed it. He found the heat duct was not attached. Contract maintenance contacted to re-attach duct. No adverse passenger reaction to report.

C-FMIJ, a Boeing 767-328 (ER) aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd, was conducted flight CJT372 from Nottingham/East Midlands International Airport (EGNX), UK, to Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (KCVG), KY. During cruise flight at FL 340 the left forward window began arcing and the crew received EICAS message L FWD WINDOW. As the crew began the checklist, the window cracked. The crew immediately began a descent to 10 000 feet, declared a MAYDAY with Gander Centre, and squawked 7700. The crew completed the L FWD WINDOW checklist while in the descent and initially advised their intent to divert to Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL. Following an analysis of fuel load, the weather and the situation generally, a decision was made to instead divert to St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL, which was coordinated with ATS. The diversion to CYYT was flown at 10 000 feet with normal pressurization and no requirement for mask use. The aircraft landed at CYYT without further incident. Maintenance personnel replaced the left forward window and replaced both left and right window heat controllers.

C-GBCG, a Carson Air Ltd Beech (Textron) B300C, was conducting medevac flight CRN811, under instrument flight rules, from Fort St. John Airport (CYXJ), BC, to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC. During cruise, the aircraft had a double engine bleed failure, and the aircraft was unable to pressurize. The crew declared an emergency, donned oxygen masks, requested an emergency descent, and executed the descent to 13 000 feet above sea level. The flight crew requested diversion to the Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC, and requested aircraft rescue and firefighting services to be on standby. The aircraft landed safely with no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft. Maintenance found holes in the left and right tubing of the bleed air system and the cockpit blower circuit breaker was popped.  The tubing was repaired, and the cabin heat venturi plumbing was secured. The cockpit blower circuit breaker was reset, and the blower was function checked with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FGQE, a Top Aces A-4N Skyhawk was conducting a Functional Check Flight (FCF) in the vicinity of Mesa-Gateway Airport (KIWA), Arizona, when the aircraft was subject to an uncommanded rolling motion to the right during a checklist procedure. The pilot regained control of the aircraft by applying left aileron, slowing to 170 KIAS, and raising the flaps to the up position. Fuel was burned down to reach maximum landing weight. The pilot declared an emergency due to a flight control malfunction and completed a controllability check with the gear down and the flaps up. The aircraft returned to KIWA for a visual straight-in, flaps-up approach to RWY 12C. The aircraft landed safely and taxied back without further incident.

C-FNWD, a Westjet Boeing 737-8, was operating flight WS2043 from Mazatlán International Airport (MMMZ), Mexico, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During the boarding process, a cabin crew member sustained an injury and was unable to complete their duties. Duties were re-assigned among the other cabin crew members. Aircraft landed without further incident at CYVR.

C-IDGE, a privately registered Beaver RX550 departed the shoreline of Stave Lake, BC, on a recreational flight under visual flight rules to a private airstrip located approximately 6 nautical miles east-southeast of Langley Regional Airport (CYNJ), BC, with only the pilot onboard. Shortly after takeoff, the engine (Rotax 503) stopped producing power and the pilot initiated a forced landing on the shoreline. The aircraft landed hard which caused the right landing gear to separate from the aircraft and the right-wing tip to contact the ground. The pilot was uninjured. The aircraft was salvaged by the pilot the following day. The pilot inspected the aircraft and found that the fuel was contaminated with water. The aircraft was being operated with MOGAS.

C-GSWK, a Swearingen SA-226-TC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, departed the Swan River Airport (CZJN), MB, on an IFR flight to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. While enroute in cruise flight, one of the passengers noticed a chemical odor and smoke coming from the right-side floor approximately mid-cabin. The first officer investigated and found the right-side floor was hot to the touch but found no fire. The air conditioning was selected to cold which eliminated the hot spot. The flight continued to CYWG and landed uneventfully. There were no injuries. There was no fire and no damage to the aircraft.

C-FYKC, an Air Canada A319 conducting flight AC1112 from Regine International Airport to Toronto Lester B Pearson International airport had a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform duties. The remaining cabin crew took over duties.

C-GWBU, a Westjet Boeing 737-800 departed Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, operating as flight WS161 under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew members, 4 cabin crew members, and 105 passengers onboard. During the initial descent into CYVR, the first officer (FO) was incapacitated. The captain called the lead flight attendant into the flight deck to assist the FO and to contact Medlink. The captain declared a PAN PAN and the aircraft landed safely. Emergency services met the aircraft on arrival and the FO was transported to hospital.

C-GOJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (Series 900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting an IFR flight JZA7793 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. After takeoff from CYWG, the left main and nose wheel retracted when the gear-up selection was made; however, the right main did not. The flight crew advised ATC, levelled the aircraft at 4000 feet ASL, and accepted delaying vectors to allow time to troubleshoot. The flight crew completed the appropriate checklists and was able to get all 3 gears in the down-and-locked position. The flight crew elected to burn fuel to reduce the aircraft weight to the max landing weight, requested that aircraft rescue and firefighting be on standby, and made an uneventful landing on Runway 18 at CYWG. The aircraft subsequently taxied to the gate.The aircraft was ferried to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, for troubleshooting. The operator's maintenance found the right-hand main landing gear uplock sensor was out of range. The sensor was re-adjusted, functional checks were completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWJO, a Westjet Boeing 737-7CT was operating as flight WJA649 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. An emergency was declared with FAA Minneapolis Air Route Traffic Control Center due to a pressurization issue. The crew elected to divert the aircraft to Winnipeg/ James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. The aircraft circled to burn fuel, emergency services were on standby and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FSIL, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight AC1326 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Princess Juliana International Airport (TNCM), St. Maarten. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue duties.

C-FSJR, AirSprint Embraer Legacy 500 was conducting flight ASP877 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While on approach to CYYZ, and while extending the flaps, the crew received a Flap Disagree message. Unable to lower the flaps for landing, the crew conducted a go-around and requested vectors while they performed the flap fail checklist. Unable to resolve the fault, the crew declared a PAN PAN and requested a longer runway for their landing. A flapless landing was performed on runway 23 with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by. Maintenance performed troubleshooting procedures as per the aircraft manufacturer's guidance. Unable to duplicate the fault, maintenance completed a lubrication of all actuator screw jacks and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FYAG, a Fairchild SA227-AC operating as Bearskin Airlines flight BLS385, was on a flight from Sault Ste. Marie Airport (CYAM), ON, towards Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON, and declared an emergency due to a hot indication on the right battery. The aircraft was given priority and landed without further incident in CYQT. Emergency vehicles were on standby.

C-FIVW, un Boeing 777-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA871 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle, France (LFPG) à destination de l'aéroport Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 15 membres d'équipage et 443 passagers à bord. Lors du vol en croisière, un agent de bord a éprouvé des problèmes médicaux affectant sa capacité à effectuer ses tâches et l'agent a été considéré incapable de poursuivre ses tâches reliées au vol. Une assistance médicale a été demandée pour l’arrivée à CYUL.

C-FTPN, a Cessna U206F operated by EON Airborne Inc., was conducting a VFR survey flight with 2 pilots on board from the Swift Current Airport (CYYN), SK. On touchdown during the landing at CYYN, the aircraft began porpoising and, after the third bounce, the nosewheel collapsed. The aircraft came to rest on its nose on the side of the runway. There was no fire. There were no injuries.

C-FNOH, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC57 from Dubai International Airport (OMDB), United Arab Emirates, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, when a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue their duties.

On 24 January 2025, a Centennial Flight Centre Inc. Cessna C-172, registration C-GXAA, was on a visual flight rules (VFR) flight cross-country. On board was the pilot and 1 passenger. The aircraft departed Villeneuve Airport (CZVL), AB towards Whitecourt Airport (CYZU), AB for the first leg of the flight. During the descent for landing on Runway 29 at CYZU, the engine power reduced unexpectedly (AVCO LYCOMING, O-320-E2D). The pilot confirmed carburetor heat was on. The pilot tried pushing and pulling both the carburetor heat and the throttle; however, the engine continued to lose power. The pilot declared MAYDAY, made a sharp turn to avoid trees, and executed a forced landing. The aircraft came to rest after impacting a barbwire fence and trees along the edge of a tree line. Both occupants were uninjured. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.The company is investigating.

C-FSLZ, a Swearingen SA-226-TC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, departed Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB, on an IFR flight to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. While enroute in cruise, the flight crew noticed smoke coming from the cabin floorboard vents. The flight crew ran through the quick reference handbook but were unable to isolate the source of the smoke. They shut off both bleed air systems and descended while ventilating the cabin. The smoke dissipated. After declaring an emergency, they continued to CYWG and landed uneventfully. Emergency vehicles followed the aircraft to the ramp and checked for overheats after shutdown.

C-GKNR, a Sikorsky S-92 operated by Cougar Helicopters Inc., was conducting flight CHI151 from St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL, to the Hibernia Oil Field. While enroute at 7000 feet altitude, the crew received a tail rotor deice fail indication. The crew attempted to reset the tail rotor deice system without success and climbed to 9000 feet in an effort to clear icing conditions. The helicopter remained in icing conditions and the crew conducted a diversion to return to CYYT and declared a PAN PAN for priority landing. The helicopter landed at CYYT without further incident.Maintenance personnel inspected the helicopter and replaced 2 tail rotor blades and 2 tail rotor deice system electrical harness assemblies.

C-GWWD, an ATR 42-300 aircraft operated by Transwest Air LP (dba Rise Air), was conducting an IFR flight from the Prince Albert/Glass Field Airport (CYPA), SK, to the Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. A lead sweeper vehicle contacted the CYXE ground controller to request clearance to sweep Runway 15/33. The ground controller cleared the lead sweeper (plus 2 other sweepers) to work on Runway 15/33 and to hold short of Runway 09/27. The hold short clearance was acknowledged by the lead sweeper. While on final approach to Runway 27 at CYXE, the CYXE Tower Controller issued a go-around instruction to C-GWWD as the sweeper vehicles had crossed over the hold-short line for Runway 09/27 at the intersection with Runway 15/33. C-GWWD conducted a missed approach and subsequently landed on Runway 27 without further incident.

C-FMAI, a Boeing 757 aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express Inc. was conducting an IFR flight from the Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, as flight MAL7070. C-GCJT, a Boeing 757 aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd. was conducting an IFR flight from Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK, to CYWG, as CJT590. C-GNCH, a Boeing 737 operated by Sunwing Airlines Inc. was conducting an IFR flight from Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), Dominican Republic, to CYWG, as flight SWG121.  While the three aircraft were being vectored for approach for Runway 31 at CYWG by ATC, minimum separation between the 3 aircraft in succession was lost. The separation between CJT590 and MAL7070 deteriorated to 4 miles. The separation between SWG121 and CJT590 deteriorated to 4 miles. SWG121 was subsequently pulled from the approach by the CYWG Tower Controller and conducted a second approach. All 3 aircraft landed at CYWG without further incident. Separation requirements for these aircraft was 5 miles.

C-FXYK, a Westjet B737-8 was operating flight WS2431 from Licenciado Gustavo Diaz Ordaz International Airport (MMPR), Puerto Vallarta, to Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK. Approximately, 25 minutes prior to landing, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue their duties. Cabin safety duties were re-assigned amongst the remaining flight attendants.

C-FLQO, a Boeing 737-8 operating as Flair Airlines flight FLE600, was in cruise flight on route to Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, when a flight attendant reported a strong smell of burning rubber or plastic localized around seat 20E/F. The smell diminished soon after, but a faint odor remained. Both the Captain and First Officer individually investigated the cabin and found no problems. Flight attendants inspected all luggage and personal electronic devices in the area and found no problems. The flight crew decided to continue to CYYZ. Upon landing, what appeared to be smoke, was observed in the cabin around seats 19E/F. CYYZ ground control was made aware of the issue and aircraft rescue and firefighting met the flight at gate C33. Firefighters entered the aircraft via the bridge and cleared the aircraft for a normal deplaning. Maintenance found condensation in the overhead passenger service unit (PSU) at seats 19 E/F.

C-FTHU, un DeHavilland DHC-8-102 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif AIE850, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Muskoka, ON (CYQA) à destination de l'aéroport international Montréal-Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors que l'aéronef se trouvait en vol de croisière, l'équipage a observé une baisse de la quantité de liquide hydraulique du système #2 suivi d'un voyant d'avertissement #2 HYD ISO VALVE. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) et a suivi la liste de vérification d’urgence (QRH). L'aéronef a continué vers CYUL où il s'est posé sans encombre.

C-GVVZ, a Sunwest Aviation Learjet 45 was operating flight CNK645 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Scottsdale Airport (KSDL), AZ. While on base to runway 21 into KSDL, a R INBD BRK FAIL Amber CAS message was received. The landing clearance was cancelled by the flight crew and the appropriate quick reference handbook (QRH) checklist was carried out. A BRAKE FAULT Advisory CAS remained and vectors were requested while the next QRH checklist was carried out. An emergency was declared and aircraft rescue and firefighting were on standby. Aircraft landed without further incident. BRAKE FAULT CAS message was cleared with a full shutdown.

C-GWEJ, a WestJet Encore DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC. While on the RNAV Y approach for Runway 15 in CYXT, at approximately 7000 feet above sea level, the flight encountered severe turbulence. The pilot monitoring called for a go-around and the pilot flying executed the missed approach. Due to the turbulence, the crew elected to climb to the 100 nautical mile minimum safe altitude. The flight crew advised air traffic control and, once clear of the turbulence, requested a vector and a clearance back to CYVR. The aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident. Maintenance inspected the aircraft and no damage was found. Aircraft was returned to service.
