C-FWEP, a WestJet Encore DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was conducting flight WEN3107 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, under instrument flight rules to Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC. After conducting a missed approach at CYXT, the crew selected flaps up and the “elevator asymmetry” caution light illuminated. The flight crew completed the related quick reference handbook checklists but the light did not extinguish. The crew determined the reduced aircraft performance meant they did not have the required navigation performance to complete a second approach into CYXT. The crew elected to divert back to CYVR. They declared a PAN PAN for potential control problems and for a minimum fuel situation. They had the minimum reserve requirement but not the minimum diversion fuel. During the diversion to CYVR, the flight crew as directed by the checklist, did not engage the autopilot and maintained an airspeed of less than 200 knots. The aircraft landed without further incident and taxied to the gate.  The elevator asymmetry light extinguished on touchdown at CYVR. Maintenance completed an inspection but could not determine the cause. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GEKH, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight AC113 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. In cruise at FL360, the aircraft encountered moderate turbulence and then severe turbulence which disconnected the Autopilot. Flight descended to FL320 and continued to destination without further incident. Maintenance conducted a severe and unusual turbulence check with no findings.

C-FIUA, an Air Canada Boeing 777-200, was conducting flight AC34 from Sydney International Airport (YSSY), Australia, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 4 flight crew members, 12 flight attendants, and 298 passengers on board. One flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform their duties.  The aircraft landed at CYVR without incident.

C-FSDQ, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 (Max 8) conducted flight AC274 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC. After landing in CYLW, during the taxi to the ramp, one flight attendant became unwell and was unable to perform their duties.

C-FYAI, un Dash-8-300 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE867 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) à destination de l'aéroport d’Aupaluk, QC (CYLA) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 6 passagers à bord. C-GSPW, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif AIE781 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Puvirnituq, QC (CYPX) à destination de CYVP avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. AIE867 était en palier à 8000 pieds à la suite de son départ de CYVP. AIE781 était en descente vers le point XOTAR, l’équipage avait été informé du trafic au départ de CYVP et l’avait sur le système de surveillance du trafic et d'évitement des collisions (TCAS). L’équipage a planifié arrêter la descente à 8500 pieds sur l’autopilote, mais avec l’inertie, l’avion est descendu jusqu’à 8350 pieds et les équipages des 2 avions ont reçu un avis de résolution du TCAS et ont respectivement effectué les manœuvres d’évitement. Les 2 vols ont été poursuivis sans encombre.

C-FTAX un Dornier Alpha Jet exploité par Top Aces Inc. effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis et à destination de l'aéroport militaire de Bagotville, QC (CYBG). Lorsqu’il était en vol à 18 000 pieds, l’indicateur d’huile du moteur droit s’est allumé. Le pilote a suivi la liste de vérification d’urgence (QRH) et a éteint le moteur droit. Une urgence a été déclarée et l’avion est revenu se poser à CYBG sans encombre. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FCQX, an Air Canada Airbus A320-214, completed flight AC272, under instrument flight rules, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC. While the aircraft was deplaning in CYLW a fuel truck contacted the right engine. There were no injuries. Maintenance inspected the engine and completed the needed repairs to return the aircraft to service.

C-FGDT, un Boeing 787-9 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA865 et N371NB, un Airbus A319 exploité par Delta Airlines sous l'indicatif DAL2665 effectuaient leur vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, tous les deux à destination de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). ACA865 était en approche finale de la piste 24R et DAL2665 a été instruit trop tôt en étape de base, ce qui a fait que lorsqu’il a intercepté l’approche finale de la piste 24L, l'espacement a été réduit à 2,1 NM sur le plan horizontal et 500 pieds sur le plan vertical. L'espacement requis était de 3 NM et 1000 pieds. Les 2 aéronefs ont atterri sans encombre.

C-GEZO, an Air Transat Airbus A321 operating flight TSC880 departed London Airport (CYXU), ON, on a flight to Cancún International Airport (MMUN), MX. During the initial climb out of CYXU the PIC reported not feeling well. Later during the flight, the PIC became incapacitated and was unable to continue flying duties. Following a discussion with Medlink, it was decided to continue to destination. The first officer flew the aircraft to destination and aircraft landed without incident.

C-GJWD, an Airbus A321, operating as Air Canada flight ACA791, was climbing out of Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, en route to Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), CA. During the climb through 14 000 feet, the flight crew received a bleed 1 and 2 message on the ECAM. The flight crew followed ECAM and the quick reference handbook checklists and the fault did not clear. A PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft returned to CYYZ and landed without further incident.

C-GCML, a Central Mountain Air Beechcraft 1900D was operating as flight GLR9156 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Conklin Aerodrome (CET2), AB. Shortly after departure, after turning the bleeds on and blowers on, the crew noticed a strong smell of smoke that seemed to be increasing. After a few seconds, the cockpit and cabin became hazy with the smell of smoke intensifying. The environmental system was shut down and the flight crew elected to return to CYEG. The flight landed safely with no further issues. Other than some passengers experiencing some headaches, there were no injuries. All of the passengers and crew declined medical attention.Following the flight, the maintenance team found that the forward evaporator blower motor was unserviceable. The blower motor was replaced with a new unit and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSDW, an Air Canada Boeing 737 Max 8 departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. The aircraft encountered severe turbulence climbing through flight level 315 resulting in an uncommanded airspeed loss of up to 25 knots, bank angles in excess of 20 degrees, and vertical speed changes. The turbulence subsided quickly, and the crew reported the occurrence to air traffic control. There were no injuries, and the flight continued without further incident.

C-GKWH, a Bell 407 helicopter operated by Churchill Falls (Labrador) Corporation Ltd, was conducting external load operations about 18 NM south of Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL, with 1 crew member on board. The helicopter was slinging a pole designed to be used for electrical power line ice removal operations. The pole became snagged on the power line and the additional stress on the sling gear caused the designated weak link to break, allowing the sling gear to fall free from the helicopter as designed. There were no injuries. The sling gear and pole were retrieved, and there was no damage to equipment or property. After the incident, the pilot and crew halted operations to fully brief crew and inspect the equipment.

D-ABYF, a Boeing 747-830 aircraft operated by Lufthansa, was conducting flight DLH463 from Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL, to Frankfurt International Airport (EDDF), Germany. While enroute in cruise flight, the Captain became ill in the flight deck crew rest area. The pilot-in-command duties were assumed by the Senior First Officer (SFO) and the first officer (FO) was summoned to the cockpit. Subsequently 2 flight attendants provided first aid. Weather was considered and Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, was selected for the diversion location. At about 48° 25' N, 058° 06' W the crew declared an emergency, advised that the captain had become incapacitated, and requested a diversion to CYUL. Fuel dumping was required and took place enroute to CYUL where a landing was made without further incident.

C-GSOC, a Sunwest Aviation Cessna C680 was operating flight CNK771 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), CA. While on the downwind leg for runway 13R at KPSP, a 90-degree wing drop was experienced, roughly 5 nm in-trail of an Airbus A320. Aircraft recovered and landed without further incident.

C-GCPW, a Pratt & Whitney Canada Corp. Dornier 328-300 was operating PWC328 from North Central West Virginia Airport (KCKB), WV, to Aéroport Métropolitain de Montréal (CYHU), QC. During climb, through 16 500 feet for FL230, ATC advised of un-verified traffic at 17 500 feet. Almost simultaneously, TA and RA warnings were sequentially triggered. Climb was continued as per TCAS resolution commands and ATC was advised that the conflicting traffic had been visually acquired. Vertical separation when crossing path of un-verified traffic was 1100 feet.

C-GSAB, a Record Hound Aviation (2018) Limited, Cessna C510 (Citation Mustang) departed Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Lloydminster Airport (CYLL), AB. While in the initial climb, the pilot observed a crew alert system warning for low oil pressure on the No. 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney-Can PW615F-A). The pilot conducted the abnormal checklist, shutdown the No. 2 engine, and advised tower they would return to CYLW with one-engine inoperative. Air traffic control provided vectors to final for Runway 16 and the aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance investigated and replaced the oil pressure transmitter and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOIK, an Air Transat Airbus 321 was operating flight TSC518 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Sangster International Airport (MKJS), Jamaica. While in flight, the Pilot-in-Command became incapacitated. A decision was made to divert the flight to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), Florida. The aircraft was piloted by the Second-in-Command and landed without further incident.

C-FNND, an Air Canada B777-200 was operating flight AC33 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport (YSSY), Australia. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to continue duties which were reassigned amongst remaining flight attendants.

C-FRED, a Helicarrier Aerospatiale AS 332L was operating in the vicinity of General Bernardo O'Higgins Airport (SCCH), Chile, for wildfire operation when the cargo hook was inadvertently released upon water pickup. Maintenance inspected cargo hook, mechanical and release system and mission selector for damage or defect. Electrical release disengaged and mechanical release fully functional. The mission selector will be replaced and tested.

C-GAGP, un Cessna T206H privé effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport d’Ottawa/Gatineau, QC (CYND) avec un pilote seul à bord. Après environ 1 heure de vol, le pilote s’est dirigé vers CYND avec l’intention d’effectuer un posé décollé sur la piste 27. Lors de l’arrondi, le pilote a senti l’aéronef remonté de quelques pieds avant de redescendre causant un rebond de l’aéronef après le touché des roues. À la suite du rebond, le pilote a décidé de faire une remise des gaz. Il a appliqué plein gaz au même moment où les roues touchaient une seconde fois la piste. L’aéronef a dévié rapidement vers la gauche. Le pilote a tenté sans succès de conserver la direction de l’aéronef. En constatant que la sortie de piste semblait inévitable, il a reculé la manette des gaz au ralenti. L’aéronef s’est immobilisé au sud de la piste 27. L’hélice est entrée en contact avec le terrain après l’affaissement du train d’atterrissage avant. Le pilote n’a pas été blessé.

C-FNYA, an Air North Boeing 737-800 was operating flight ANT772 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen International Airport (CYXY), YT. Approximately one hour into the flight, the first officer became ill. Control was transferred to the captain for the remainder of the flight. The aircraft landed uneventfully at CYXY, and the crew member received medical attention.

HB-JHG, a Swiss Air Airbus A330 aircraft was conducting flight SWR23A from John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), NY, to Geneva Airport (LSGG), Switzerland. N815AA, an American Airlines Boeing B787-8 was conducting flight AAL92 from Philadelphia International Airport (KPHL), Pennsylvania, USA, to Zurich Airport (LSZH), Zurich, Switzerland.While both enroute at FL390, the two aircraft were separated by 17 miles longitudinally. The required separation for that airspace was 10 minutes longitudinally for unidentified aircraft, and 5 miles longitudinally for identified aircraft.Separation was not assured during the transition from Boston ACC. Although both aircraft were within Canadian airspace, they were not displayed on the ATC radar, had not been handed over from Boston, and no flight plan had been forwarded.Both aircraft continued their flights without further incident and landed safely at their respective destinations.

C-GEEN, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 was operating as flight WEN3358 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During cruise, one of the flight attendants (FA) felt ill and could not continue with their duties. A deadheading FA assumed the duties of the ill flight attendant and the flight continued on to CYYC. On arrival into CYCC, the FA exited the aircraft without assistance.

C-GVGX, an Air North ATR 42-300 was operating as flight ANT352 from Old Crow Airport (CYOC), YT, to Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen International Airport (CYXY), YT. During cruise, the flight crew observed a low oil pressure alert for the #2 engine (Pratt & Whitney-Can, PW121). The checklist was followed, resulting in shutting down the engine and restarting it. Shortly after starting the #2 engine a CCAS alert sounded, requiring the engine to be shut down again. An emergency was declared and the flight continued to CYXY without any further issues. The flight crew conducted a single-engine approach and landing with no issues.Following the flight, the maintenance team replaced the #2 oil cooler and associated filters. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOIR, an Air Transat Airbus A321-271 was operating flight TSC681 from Humberto Delgado Airport (LPPT), Portugal, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. While in cruise, the first officer became incapacitated. Another first officer was available to take over flight duties. The flight landed without further incident.

C-FKMA, a Piper PA-31 operated by Aries Aviation, was conducting a VFR flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Calgary/Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB. There was only a pilot on board. After departure from YWG, the pilot was unable to retract the landing gear. The pilot contacted company maintenance, and the decision was made to continue to CYBW with the landing gear extended. During the approach to CYBW, the pilot requested aircraft rescue and firefighting to be placed on standby as a precaution. An uneventful landing was conducted.Subsequent investigation by company maintenance found that when the aircraft had maintenance work performed in CYWG, the hydraulic reservoir had not been correctly serviced as the hydraulic fluid level was below the required limits. The low hydraulic reservoir level was not observed prior to take-off and as a result, there was inadequate hydraulic fluid to perform the landing gear retraction operation when the aircraft departed CYWG.

C-FNNH, an Air Canada B777-200 was operating flight AC43 from Indira Gandhi International Airport (VIDP), India, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the cruise portion of flight, three flight attendants became ill and were unable to continue duties. The aircraft continued to CYYZ and landed without further event.

C-GEPG, un Boeing 737 Max 8 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA481 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport International Montréal-Trudeau , QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport international Pearson de Toronto, QC (CYYZ) avec 114 passagers et 6 membres d'équipage. Lorsque l'équipage a sélectionné la rétraction du train lors de la montée initiale, le train n'a pas bougé et est resté en position baissé. L'équipage a ensuite déclaré une situation d'urgence avec l'unité de circulation aérienne avant de revenir vers CYUL. ACA481 s'est posé sans encombre à CYUL où les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) étaient en attente pour inspecter l'aéronef. Une inspection de l'aéronef a ensuite été effectuée par le service de maintenance et l'unité électronique de détecteur de proximité (PSEU) a été remplacé.

C-GSJZ, un De Havilland of Canada DHC-8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7988 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international Montréal-Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV). Peu après le décollage de CYUL, lors de la rétraction du train d'atterrissage, celui-ci est resté en position baissé. L'équipage a déclaré une situation d'urgence avec le service de circulation aérienne et l'aéronef est revenu atterrir à CYUL où les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) attendaient en retrait de la piste. L'atterrissage s'est déroulé sans encombre. L'aéronef est en inspection par le service de maintenance pour en déterminer la cause.

C-FGWR, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by Keewatin Air LP, departed Little Grand Rapids Airport (CZGR), MB, on an IFR flight to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. Upon departure from CZGR, after the landing gear was selected up, the left main landing gear (unsafe) transition light remained on. The left main landing gear was visually confirmed partially retracted. After reaching an altitude of 1000 feet AGL, the pilots completed the checklist for unsafe landing gear. The landing gear circuit breaker was noticed in the open (popped) position. The flight crew continued the climb to the enroute altitude and completed the appropriate checklists while proceeding as planned to CYWG. A PAN PAN was declared with CYWG air traffic control. The pilots reset the circuit breaker and selected the landing gear down. All three indicators for the landing gear where green, indicating a down and locked condition. The passengers were briefed for safety instructions. The landing at CYWG was uneventful. The aircraft was taken out of service.The operator's maintenance department conducted troubleshooting. Along with chafing and exposed wires, it was discovered that due to insufficient routing and clamping of the landing gear safety switch wiring harness, the left main landing gear drag brace was creating undue strain on the wires. The wiring harness was repaired and re-routed, and the safety switch was replaced. Subsequent retraction tests and a test flight were performed with satisfactory results.

C-GSAT, a Sunwest Aviation Challenger 604 was operating flight CNK91 from Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport (PANC), AK, to Teterboro Airport (KTEB), NJ. On approach into KTEB flaps failed at 7 degrees when selected. ATC was advised and the longer runway was requested. The quick reference handbook procedures for FLAP FAIL CAS message were followed and a PAN PAN was declared. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GWFM, a Skyservice Business Aviation Dassault Falcon 900EX, was descending toward Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, as flight SYB888, when the flight crew noticed that the #1 throttle did not retard and the auto throttles didn't disconnect. The flight crew disconnected the auto throttles, actioned checklist and shut the engine down. The flight crew advised ATC, but did not declare an emergency and landed without further incident.

C-GUSM, a Learjet 45 operated by Wal-Mart Canada Corp., was conducting a flight from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Orange County Airport (KORG), TX, USA. During the climb though FL300, the crew received an indication of a bleed air failure affecting their anti-icing protection system. The crew declared PAN PAN and requested a return to CYYZ where they landed uneventfully. Aircraft rescue and firefighting inspected the aircraft after landing before the aircraft was taxied to its parking area.

C-GIAB, un De Havilland DHC-8-300 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif AIE864 était en préparation pour un vol depuis l'aéroport international Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Mont-Joli, QC (CYYY) avec 1 passager et 3 membres d'équipage. Pendant le dégivrage de l'aéronef à CYUL, le préposé au dégivrage a contacté l'équipage pour aviser que l'hélice du moteur droit aurait frappé une composante du camion de dégivrage. L'équipage a immédiatement éteint le moteur et vérifié l'hélice qui ne présentait pas de dommages apparents. L'aéronef a été remorqué au hangar pour une inspection plus approfondie par le service de maintenance.

C-FYIY, an Air Canada Airbus A319, was conducting flight AC687 from St. John's International Airport (CYYT), NL, to Toronto/ Lester B. Peason International Airport (CYYZ), ON. On route, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform their duties.

C-GLQH, a DHC-8-400 operated by Porter Airlines Inc., was at the gate following boarding for flight PTR2691, which was to fly from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Sault Ste. Marie Airport (CYAM), ON. The auxiliary power unit (APU) was on to provide temperature control in the cabin, and the flight crew requested that the wing leading edges be sprayed with de-icing fluid to remove some ice which had accumulated on the wing. As the de-icing was nearing completion, both the flight crew and cabin crew noticed smoke in their respective areas of the aircraft. The crew initiated a rapid deplanement and all occupants exited the aircraft without incident. Due to the APU bleed air being on while the de-icing was taking place, some of the de-ice fluid had been able to enter the air conditioning system, resulting in foul smelling smoke. Maintenance conducted a smoke and odor purge from the aircraft before completing an operational check and releasing the aircraft back into service.

C-GXAI, un DeHavilland DHC-8-314 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif AIE866, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de La Grande-Rivière, QC (CYGL) à destination de l'aéroport international Montréal-Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 6 passagers et 3 membres d'équipage. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en vol de croisière après environ 1 heure et 13 minutes de vol, le moteur gauche s'est éteint par manque de carburant. L'équipage a alors déclaré une situation d'urgence avec l'unité de circulation aérienne et dérouté le vol vers l'aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) où l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre.

C-FKMG, un Beech B300 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif AIE550 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Puvirnituq, QC (CYPX) à destination de l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP). En approche pour la piste 07 à CYVP, l'équipage a sélectionné l'extension du train d'atterrissage pour ensuite constaté que celui-ci restait rentré et que la lumière rouge du voyant désaccord restait allumée. L'équipage a interrompu l'approche et s'est mis en circuit d'attente pour la recherche de panne. L'équipage a déclaré une situation d'urgence et demandé la présence des services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). Le train a pu être abaissé avec le système alternatif manuel et l'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre avec le service SLIA en attente. L'aéronef a été remorqué jusqu'au hangar de maintenance pour inspection.

C-GITU, an Air Canada Airbus A321 operating flight ACA163 departed Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, on an instrument flight rules flight to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. While enroute approximately 50 nm ESE of Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON, a passenger became ill. The flight was diverted to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with request for aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by, due to an overweight landing condition. The aircraft landed uneventfully in CYWG.The operator's maintenance department conducted a heavy landing inspection and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GARO, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1731 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (KPHX), AZ. During descent, at approximately 8000 feet, the flight crew received HYD G RSVR LO LVL and HYD G SYS LO PR ECAM. Flight crew carried out associated ECAM actions and selected PTU and Green pump off. PAN PAN was declared followed by Mayday. Upon approach, the ECAM instructed the flight crew to restore the pressure of the Green hydraulic system. Following this action, the system parameters returned to normal. Landing gear was extended normally and flight subsequently landed without further incident.Maintenance inspected the aircraft in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual and found the associated hydraulic level to be at full level. The associated low-level switch was determined to be defective, removed and replaced, and subsequent satisfactory serviceability tests were carried out.

C-FRZA, an amateur built Lancair-ES, was conducting a local flight from Springbank, AB (CYBW) with the pilot and one passenger on board. Shortly after take-off from Runway 35 and during the initial climb, the pilots side cabin entry door opened and broke free from the aircraft. The door went over the top of the fuselage striking the right-wing flap and causing minor damage. There were no injuries, and no reported damage from the falling door. The pilot declared a Mayday, joined the downwind leg of the circuit and completed a successful landing back onto Runway 35.

C-FSCY, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight AC517 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport (PHNL), Honolulu, HI. During the flight, the crew received a leading-edge light 5, indication. The crew declared Pan Pan and on descent below FL200 the light cleared. The crew completed all relevant checklists and landed without further incident.

C-GMXD, un Pilatus PC-12/47E exploité par Airmedic Inc. sous l'indicatif AM438 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport métropolitain de Montréal - St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) à destination de l'aéroport La Romaine, QC (CTT5) avec 4 membres d'équipage. L'équipage de conduite a perdu l'indication de couple moteur alors que l'aéronef était en croisière à une altitude de 22602 pieds au sud-ouest de la ville de Québec. Le moteur fonctionnait toujours et les autres paramètres étaient normaux. L'équipage a ensuite déclaré une situation de détresse (mayday) avec le service de circulation aérienne pour un atterrissage immédiat à l'aéroport international Québec - Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre sur la piste 29. Le service de maintenance a été avisé de la panne.

C-GEPF, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight AC971 from Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International Airport (MMPR), Puerto Vallarta, MX, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform duties. Duties were reassigned to the remaining cabin crew members.

C-GBCG, a Carson Air Limited Beechcraft B300C (King Air 350) was being operated on flight CRN811M from Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, under instrument flight rules, to Smithers Airport (CYYD), BC. En route, the aircraft experienced a partial electrical failure, and the crew decided to return to CYLW. When they approached CYLW, there was no gear down indication. This was likely connected to the partial electrical failure. The flight crew conducted the emergency gear extension checklist and then flew by the control tower to have the controllers visually confirm that their landing gear was down. The crew requested emergency vehicles to be on standby for their landing. The aircraft landed without incident.A maintenance inspection determined that a 30 amp circuit breaker, outside of the cockpit, had tripped. The circuit breaker was reset and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GRTB, a Westjet B737-800 was operating flight WS1229 from Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the safety demonstration a cabin crew became ill and was unable to perform duties. These duties were reassigned among remaining cabin crew members.

C-GKQG, a Porter Airlines De Havilland Dash-8-400, operating as PTR2691 from Billy Bishop/Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Sault Ste. Marie Airport (CYAM), ON, reported a pressurization issue on departure. The aircraft returned to CYTZ and landed without further incident.

C-GKQG, a Porter Airlines DeHavilland DHC-8-400 operating flight PD2939, departed from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, bound for Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS), MA. During cruise, the flight crew observed a Prop Deice Caution light illuminating. The quick reference handbook was actioned, however, the light remained illuminated and the crew elected to return to CYTZ. The aircraft was cleared for the RNAV RNP Y RWY 08 approach into CYTZ; however, when the landing gear was deployed, only two green landing gear down and locked lights illuminated. The crew requested vectors to maintain 1900 feet to avoid icing conditions. The flight crew then elected to divert to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, where an alternate landing gear extension was completed, resulting in three green lights on the alternate panel but still only two on the main indicator. The flight crew declared a MAYDAY and the aircraft landed safely and without further incident.Porter Maintenance found the main RH gear bulb burnt out, the bulb was replaced and checked serviceable. The prop deice harness was also replaced for original Prop Deice Caution light. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FXCA, an Air Canada B767-300 was operating flight AC7247 from Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, the crew reported a center system hydraulic quantity and pressure loss. A PAN PAN was declared, the crew requested the long runway in CYYZ and a tow off the runway.After an Air Canada maintenance inspection, the Electro-hydraulic servo valve for the Elevator Autopilot servo found leaking and was replaced.

C-FGEO, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC47 from Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (VABB), Mumbai, India, to Frankfurt Airport (EDDF), Germany. During the cruise phase of flight, a cabin crew sustained an injury while performing duties and was unable to continue working. The duties were reassigned to remaining flight attendants. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GVDP, an Air Canada A220-300 was operating flight AC1073 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Denver International Airport (KDEN), CO. During cruise, over the state of Michigan, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to a suspected fuel leak in the right wing. The crew elected to divert to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, where the aircraft landed safely.

C-FIIK, a Cessna 172N operated by Harv's Air Service Ltd., was preparing for a local flight to be conducted by a student pilot. The student pilot followed the startup checklist and attempted to start the engine. The engine would start, sputter, then quit. A Harv’s Air employee noticed that the student was having difficulty and walked over to offer assistance. The employee hand-rotated the propeller and was subsequently struck by the propeller. The operator called 9-1-1 and requested an ambulance. EMS transported the employee to a hospital with serious injuries.

C-GENU, a Westjet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 was conducting flight WEN3304 from Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, under instrument flight rules. During the take-off roll, as the aircraft approached 50 kts, the flight crew received No. 1 Bleed Hot, No. 2 Bleed Hot, and Deice Pressure caution lights. The flight crew rejected the takeoff and declared a MAYDAY. The aircraft was still on the ground with no hazard, the flight crew cancelled the MAYDAY and taxied clear of the active runway.  Company maintenance was contacted and the crew conducted the recommended supplemental procedure ground reset guide. The error was cleared and the flight departed without further incident.

C-GHPW, a VIH Helicopters Limited Bell Textron Canada 206 B3, departed Gold River (49 North Heli) heliport (CGR2), BC, under visual flight rules, to conduct tree planting operations in a cut block located 11 nautical miles to the southwest with the pilot and 1 forestry worker on board. The pilot was performing a toe-in hover exit to deliver the forestry worker to the site. While the passenger was deplaning, the rotor blade struck a tree stump that was at the helicopter's eight o’clock position. The pilot lifted off and landed at a nearby suitable landing site to inspect the blades. He assessed the damage to the blades as minor and flew back to the base. The pilot reported that he did not experience any sign of a rapid acceleration or deceleration during the event.  The area near the work site was determined to be unsafe for landing and the forestry worker walked out.On return to base, the helicopter was grounded. Bell Textron Canada was contacted to determine the extent of the inspection to be carried out. It was determined that, based on the description and the images of the main rotor blades, the incident did not constitute a main rotor stoppage.

C-FRHQ un Dash-8-311 exploité par Hydro-Québec sous l’indicatif HYD152 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Bagotville, QC (CYBG) avec 3 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’aéronef se trouvait à environ 39 miles marins au nord-est de CYUL à 15 000 pieds ASL, une fissure est apparue dans le pare-brise du côté droit. L’équipage a déclaré l'état d’urgence et est retourné à CYUL. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 24R sans encombre.

N745YX, an Embraer ERJ 170-200LR operating as United Airlines Inc., flight RPA3698, was on a flight from Ottawa/ Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, towards Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD), IL, when the flight crew declared an emergency due to a trim failure. The flight crew elected to return to CYOW and landed without further incident.

C-GVWJ, a Westjet Boeing 737-700, was at the gate in preparation for flight WJA193 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC. While boarding, the cabin crew reported an unknown type of fumes present in the passenger cabin. The crew completed a rapid deplanement, and airport firefighting arrived. It was determined that an external combustion heater was being used to thaw an aircraft water panel and was responsible for the fumes. The heater was disconnected, and an air quality test was completed. The crew returned to the aircraft, and the flight boarded, departed, and was completed uneventfully.

C-GALL, an Alpine Helicopters Incorporated Bell Textron 206L-3 (LongRanger) departed Galena Lodge (50° 39.8’ N, 117° 23.6’ W), BC, on a local snow safety mission, under visual flight rules, with the pilot and one guide on board. On the third task of the flight, the pilot dropped the guide off on the top of an alpine ridge. The guide was to ski down and establish a landing site for a Bell 212. The pilot flew an approach to a treed bench landform to await the guide. After the initial approach, while maneuvering to a second landing spot, the pilot lost visual reference and the rotor struck the snow on the left side of the helicopter. The mast sheared at the main gear box and the mast and rotor blades departed the helicopter. The aircraft settled upright in the snow with a slight nose up attitude. The pilot shut down the engine, egressed from the helicopter, and called an airborne helicopter with his handheld radio. The emergency recovery plan was activated, and the pilot and guide were recovered.The helicopter was recovered and the mast was sent for analysis.

C-FYXF, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1857 from Robert L. Bradshaw International Airport (TKPK), Basseterre, Saint Kitts and Nevis, to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue safety-related duties. The duties were redistributed amongst the remaining cabin crew in accordance with company policy and procedure. The flight was completed without further incident.

C-FIUR, un Boeing 777-300ER exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA832, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Bruxelles-National (EBBR), Belgique. Lors de la montée à environ 70 miles marins au nord-est de CYUL, une odeur et de la fumée sont apparues dans l’office arrière de la cabine. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence est retourné vers CYUL. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 24R sans encombre.

C-GUPG, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300 was conducting flight ACA609 from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the climb, the crew noticed that the pressurization was not stabilizing and they received a cabin altitude caution message. The crew then levelled off at 10 000 feet and held 50 nm NW of CYHZ to investigate the cabin pressurization issue. The crew completed all checklists but were unable to adjust the cabin altitude in manual control. The crew then declared a PAN PAN and diverted back to CYHZ. The aircraft landed safely at 1732 UTC (1332 AST) without further incident. An Air Canada maintenance inspection found that the aft cargo vent flap idler bearing was sheared, and the vent was in the open position. The idler bearing was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJZG, a Jazz Aviation De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 departed Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, on flight JZA283, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew members, 2 cabin crew members, and 54 passengers on board. The crew departed CYLW with a selection of Flaps 5 for takeoff. When the flaps were selected up on departure, the flaps did not retract and the power caution message illuminated. The quick reference handbook (QRH) checklist was actioned with no change to the flap position. The aircraft was leveled at 14 000 feet above sea level and an airspeed of 190 knots or less was maintained to comply with the flight limitations for Flaps 5. The flight crew elected to continue to CYVR due to the marginal weather in CYLW. An emergency was declared and aircraft rescue and firefighting crews were standing by. The aircraft landed without incident.The maintenance inspection found the right flap torsion bar had failed and the flap was no longer connected to the flap drive power unit. The torsion bar was replaced, and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FPLS, a WestJet Boeing 737-8CT, was conducting flight WS324 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Shortly after departing CYXE, 2 flight attendants in the aft cabin began to feel unwell. The cabin safety duties of these 2 flight attendants were re-assigned among the remaining flight attendants. The aircraft landed safety in CYYZ.

C-GOFW, un Airbus A330-343 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA2358 et un Embraer ERJ 190-400 exploité par Porter Airlines sous l'indicatif POE570 effectuaient leur vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, tous les deux à destination de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Les 2 aéronefs étaient en approche finale de la piste 24L et de la piste 24R alors que l'espacement a été réduit à 2,2 NM sur le plan horizontal et 600 pieds sur le plan vertical. L'espacement requis était de 3 NM et 1000 pieds.

C-GGGA, a Beech 1900D operated by Propair Inc., as flight PRO4383 was instructed to maintain 4000 feet while on approach to Runway 05 at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, but descended to 3000 feet. As a result, vertical separation was lost with C-FLJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP, Bombardier CRJ900, operating as JZA329 that was parallel traffic on approach to Runway 06R.

C-GHDQ, a Central Mountain Air Beech 1900 operating as flight GLR2727, on route from Sudbury Airport (CYSB), ON, to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, declared an emergency due to equipment issues. The aircraft continued to destination and landed without incident.

C-GAXD, un Cessna C-172M exploité par l’Académie de l'aviation de Saint-Hyacinthe inc. effectuait un vol d’entrainement dans le circuit à l’aéroport de St-Hyacinthe, QC (CSU3) avec un instructeur et un élève à bord. En montée après le décollage de la piste 02, une panne du moteur a été simulée et un demi-tour a été effectué pour se poser sur la piste 20. Après l’atterrissage, l’avion n’arrivait pas à freiner suffisamment pour arrêter avant le bout de la piste et l’instructeur a repris les commandes pour interrompre l’atterrissage et redécoller. L’avion a survolé la route au sud de la piste avant l’impact avec le sol à environ 500 pieds du bout de la piste. Un occupant a subi des blessures mineures et l’avion a subi des dommages importants. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée et le signal capté par le système de satellites Cospas.

C-GFDU, an Air Canada Rouge A320-214 was operating flight ROU1830 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Owen Roberts International Airport (MWCR), Cayman Islands. During climb, the flight crew received HYD Y RSVR LO LVL and HYD Y SYS LO PR ECAM messages. The associated ECAM actions were carried out in accordance with company policy and procedure. The flight crew elected to return to CYYZ when in the vicinity of Pittsburgh International Airport (KPIT), PA. A PAN PAN was declared, and an overweight full-stop landing was completed with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby. Due to associated loss of nose wheel steering, the aircraft was towed to gate.

C-GCJT, a Boeing 757-223 operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd., was conducting flight CJT462 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Iqaluit Airport (CYFB), NU. After takeoff from CYWG, the flight crew observed a "TE Flap Disagree" light and completed the associated checklist. The flight crew contacted the operator's maintenance and decided to return to CYWG. CJT462 declared a PAN PAN and held south of CYWG for approximately 2 hours to reduce the aircraft weight to maximum landing weight. Aircraft rescue and firefighting was requested and was on standby. The aircraft landed safely in CYWG. This was a repeat of a similar occurrence on the same aircraft from 2 January 2025 (TSB occurrence A25W0001). The operator's maintenance troubleshot the fault over a few days and replaced the trailing edge flap control valve and the inboard aft roller bearing on flap track #5. Subsequent operational checks were conducted successfully and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GVCH, a Cougar Helicopters Sikorsky S-92A was conducting flight CHI881, on an IFR flight from St. John's International Airport (CYYT), NL, towards the SeaRose Offshore Floating Production Platform. While 70 NM offshore from CYYT and in cloud, a loud bang was accompanied by a bright flash, followed by a burning smell and a TR Deice Fail indication. The crew descended to exit icing conditions and to attain VMC. The emergency checklist was carried out, and a PAN PAN was declared. Passengers were briefed, and the aircraft turned back to CYYT and was able to maintain VMC for the remainder of the flight. The aircraft landed without further incident. There were no injuries reported. Environment Canada confirmed that a lightning strike occurred on January 3, 2025, at 17:20 UTC. The strike was recorded approximately 135.8 km (73 NM) from CYYT, with coordinates N46.2885, W50.9227.Sikorsky and Cougar Helicopters engineers conducted a joint inspection of the aircraft. The inspection revealed lightning damage to major components, including two main rotor blades, two main rotor yokes, the main rotor deice harness, tail rotor blades, the tail rotor gearbox, and the tail rotor pitch beam.Damaged components were removed and replaced or overhauled per manufacturer procedures. After assessing the strike as low-to-medium severity and confirming the main gearbox (MGB) serviceability, the aircraft is being repaired and will return to service following successful test flights.

C-GCJT, a Boeing 757-223 operated by Cargojet, was operating as flight CJT566 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. During flap retraction on departure, the flight crew received a "TE FLAP DISAGREE" EICAS message. The flight crew requested to stop the climb at 9000 feet ASL. The flight crew contacted company maintenance and carried out the appropriate procedures for an "ALTERNATE FLAPS" and "FLAPS 20" indications and elected to return to CYYC. A PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft returned uneventfully. After exiting the runway, the aircraft was inspected by aircraft firefighting personnel and was released to taxi to the gate.Company maintenance followed the fault isolation manual and found the 4L, 2L, and 3R transmission overload tripped during troubleshooting. The mechanical flap system was inspected and found free of binding or resistance. The indicators were reset, and the fluids were serviced. The flaps were cycled, no faults were observed, and the aircraft was returned to service.The same aircraft was involved in a flap related occurrence on 06 January 2025, reference TSB report A25C0001.

C-FWSV, a Westjet B737-700 was operating flight WJA1540 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to George Bush Intercontinental Airport (KIAH), Houston, TX. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants. The flight continued without further incident.

C-FBYG, un Beech B200 exploité par Max Aviation sous l’indicatif MAX230 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) à destination de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU). En approche pour CYHU, l’équipage a abaissé le train d’atterrissage et a constaté un problème d’indication avec le train droit. L’équipage a effectué une remontée et a abaissé le train d’atterrissage à 2 reprises. L’indication lumineuse associée au train de droite n’indiquait pas que celui-ci était sorti. L’équipage a contacté la tour de contrôle pour effectuer un passage à basse altitude pour une confirmation visuelle. Le contrôleur aérien a confirmé que ce dernier était sorti. L’équipage a demandé un circuit d’attente pour compléter la liste de vérification d’urgence et demander la présence des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre et a pu circuler jusqu’aux installations de la compagnie. Une vérification par le service de maintenance a révélé que les lumières d’indication étaient brûlées. Le problème a été corrigé et aucune anomalie n’a été identifiée lors des essais d’extension et rétraction du train d’atterrissage.

C-GWCM, a Westjet B737-700 was operating flight WJA2051 from Bahías De Huatulco International Airport (MMBT), MX, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, a cabin crew became ill and was unable to continue duties which were reassigned to the remaining crew. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GHBO, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1735 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), CA. During cruise, just prior to Top-Of-Descent, in the vicinity of EED VORTAC, at FL360, the cabin crew identified smoke in the aft galley. The flight crew were immediately notified and then executed the associated checklist disabling power to the aft galley in the process. Smoke subsequently dissipated. The flight continued to destination without declaration of PAN PAN nor MAYDAY. The flight landed without further incident.Following the occurrence, a defect was entered in the Aircraft Defect Log in accordance with company policy and procedure. Maintenance inspected the aircraft and found a broken wire associated with aft coffee maker 3.

C-GCBK, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 operated by Perimeter Aviation was conducting flight PAG401 from Oxford House Airport (CYOH), MB, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. PAG401 was cleared to land Runway 13 at CYWG. A Winnipeg Airport Authority plow truck, identified as TR84+1, requested clearance to travel from the de-ice bay to the maintenance facility. The CYWG ground controller issued instructions for TR84+1 to the maintenance garage via taxiway Kilo, across Runway 18 but to hold short of Runway 13. TR84+1 read back the clearance and proceeded on taxiway Kilo. The ground controller issued a "Stop-Stop" command to TR84+1 when it was observed on the Airport Surface Detection Equipment (ASDE) that TR84+1 had failed to stop at the Runway 13 hold-short line. TR84+1 stopped just passed the hold-short line when PAG401 was on the landing roll; passing through the intersection.  Reported weather at the time indicated that visibility was reduced to 5/8 of a mile. A post-occurrence inspection of the taxiway and hold-short markings and lighting indicated that they were all in serviceable condition.

C-GVWA, a Westjet B737-800 was operating flight WS1940 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (KATL), GA. During descent, a cabin crew became ill and was unable to continue duties. The flight crew notified ATC and requested priority handling. The cabin crew duties were reassigned amongst the remaining flight attendants. The paramedics met the aircraft at the gate.

C-GGOY, a Jazz Aviation DHC-8-402 departed Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC on flight JZA346, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. On vectors for final approach into CYVR, a flight attendant noticed a burning smell in the galley with no indication of smoke. It was determined that the smell was from the inboard coffee maker and noted that the power light was not on. The flight crew was advised and they pulled the circuit breaker for the affected coffee maker. The smell dissipated. The flight crew advised air traffic control, declared a PAN PAN, and requested emergency vehicles be standing by for their landing. The aircraft landed without incident and after a visual inspection by the emergency vehicles, the flight crew taxied to the gate.  The coffee maker was deferred through the minimum equipment list, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPCI, a Pacific Coastal Saab 340 B, departed Penticton Airport (CYYF), BC, under instrument flight rules to operate flight PCO1386, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. The aircraft encountered continuous light to moderate icing during the flight and the flight crew selected the de-ice boots which cycled successfully. In the descent through 10 000 feet above sea level (ASL), when the de-ice boots were selected on again and the flight crew noted that none of the corresponding green lights illuminated. The crew attempted to manually inflate the de-ice boots but the system did not show inflation. The moderate icing continued and flight crew contacted company operations to troubleshoot the system.  A PAN PAN was declared and air traffic control gave the flight crew priority descent from 8000 feet ASL to 3000 feet ASL. The ice was shed in the warmer air and the flight landed without further incident.Maintenance was carried out and a hole was found in the de-ice boot, the boot was replaced and aircraft returned to service.

C-GKVV, un Boeing 737-86N exploité par Sunwing Airlines Inc. sous l'indicatif SWG5220 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport international de Cancún, Mexique (MMUN) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Lors de l’approche finale pour CYUL, l’équipage a sélectionné les volets à 15 degrés, mais il n’a pas constaté un abaissement des volets. Une remise des gaz a été effectuée et une urgence a été déclarée. L'équipage a vérifié la liste de contrôle pour une situation de volet de bord de fuite asymétrique et appliqué la procédure d’extension alternative des volets. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre. Les services d’incendie et de maintenance ont effectué une vérification de l’aéronef sur la piste avant que celui-ci ait circulé en direction de l’aérogare.

C-GPNA, a De Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines, was operating as PVL2259 from St. John's International Airport (CYYT), NL, to Halifax Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. During the takeoff from CYYT, the number 1 main wheel tire (left outboard tire) failed, leaving tire portions on the runway. Neither the blown tire condition, nor the tire debris on the runway at CYYT was noticed during the flight, and the aircraft continued to destination. Following touchdown on Runway 23 at CYHZ the blown tire imbalance led to a vibration that caused the left main landing gear stabilizer brace to become unlocked and allow the left main landing gear to collapse. As the landing gear collapsed, the left propeller contacted the runway surface. There was a left engine fire, and the crew activated the engine extinguisher system. The aircraft came to rest on the runway and 73 passengers and 4 crew members evacuated with no reported injuries. The TSB is investigating.

C-FWCN, a Westjet Boeing 737-700 departed Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), CA, on flight WJA1723 under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During the approach, initial flaps were selected down and the crew received notification of a trailing edge flap disagreement. The crew requested radar vectors and completed the corresponding checklists. A PAN PAN urgency was declared, and the crew conducted a non-normal flap position approach with flaps set to fifteen. The aircraft landed safely with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) vehicles standing by. After landing, the flight crew taxied clear of the runway, ARFF conducted a visual inspection, and the aircraft was taxied to the gate under its own power.Maintenance replaced the flap position indicator, flap position transmitter, and connector D40024P/J. The necessary function checks were carried out and the aircraft returned to service.

N801UA, a United Airlines Airbus A319-131 departed San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA, on flight UAL2051 under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, the pilots observed the right brake pressure indication on the yellow system brake triple indicator, indicating residual pressure. The pilots contacted company dispatch and technical operations maintenance control. A PAN PAN urgency was declared with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) crews requested to be standing by. Non-standard procedures were used during the landing and the aircraft landed without further incident. ARFF confirmed that there were no issues and the aircraft taxied under its own power.Maintenance deferred the indicator for the right brake system indicator in accordance with the minimum equipment list and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FGLX, a privately registered Mooney M20J was departing from Calgary/Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB, for Lethbridge Airport (CYQL), AB. After take-off the aircraft climbed to approximately 50 feet AGL and then settled back to the runway. Mixture was full rich; the throttle was full, the propeller control was full fine for the take-off and the engine instruments were indicating in the correct range. The aircraft exited the left side of the runway and contacted an airport sign damaging the left wing and collapsing the left main landing gear. The pilot and passenger were able to exit the aircraft without any assistance. The aircraft was moved off of the runway with assistance from airport staff.

C-FSFP, an Airsprint Inc. Cessna 525B was operating flight ASP686 from Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), CA, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Avionics overtemp warning was received on arrival into CYVR in instrumental meteorological conditions. Crew consulted quick reference checklist which led them to cut off GIA 1. In doing so, crew lost autopilot, electric trim, GPS 1, NAV 1, COM 1, localizer/glideslope along with GIA 2 and some others. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed safely at CYVR.Failure cleared on the ground with a power reset. Maintenance team sent diagnostic information to Garmin/Textron for analysis. Same issue arose on December 6, 2024, as occurrence A24W0151.

C-FSUP, a Cessna 525B operated by Airsprint Inc., was conducting flight ASP653 from Collingwood Aerodrome (CNY3), ON, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. Approximately two hours into cruise flight, the crew noticed the RH engine (Williams FJ44-3A) oil pressure start to fluctuate. The crew continued to monitor and noted it dropped below 44 psi before settling at 44 psi. The crew followed the checklist and continued with a precautionary engine shut down. At 23:39Z, 136 nautical miles east of the Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, the crew of ASP653 declared an emergency and advised ATC that they would be diverting to CYXE. The aircraft landed safely at 00:15Z with emergency services on standby. There were no injuries. There was no fire.A post-occurrence inspection by the operator indicated that the starter/generator failed and caused damage to the engine. The engine will require replacement. A Service Difficulty Report was submitted to Transport Canada.

HI1078, an Arajet Boeing 737-800 aircraft, was conducting flight DWI5801 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), Dominican Republic. During the rotation on take-off from Rwy 05, the tail section contacted the runway. The flight crew received an indication of ground contact and advised ATC they would be returning to CYYZ. No emergency was declared and the aircraft landed uneventfully on Rwy 06R. Maintenance inspected the aircraft at the gate, and found evidence of runway contact on the skid plate. A visual indicator on the skid plate, showed that the contact was minor and there was no structural damage to the aircraft. The flight was cancelled due to crew flight time limits.

C-FYKW, an Airbus A319-114 aircraft operated by Air Canada Rouge, was operating as ROU1522 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL. When enroute in the vicinity of Greater Moncton/Roméo Leblanc International Airport (CYQM), NB, the first officer became incapacitated and was unable to continue their duties. The first officer’s condition improved, and it was decided to continue to CYYT and have emergency medical services meet the aircraft at the gate. The landing was made at CYYT without further incident.

C-FARY, an Alberta College of Aeronautics Cessna 172 M, was on a training flight from Cooking Lake Aerodrome (CEZ3), AB, to Villeneuve (CZVL), AB, for a touch and go and back to CEZ3. Winds at CZVL were 180 Degrees at 10 kts and the winds at the Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, the closest airport with weather information, were 180 degrees 15 kts gusting to 21 kts. On approach to Runway 10 at CEZ3, the pilot encountered some turbulence between 3000 feet ASL and 2600 feet ASL. The pilot touched down on Runway 10 with up to 12 knots of crosswind component. The aircraft drifted to the left side of the runway and contacted the snow windrow and was further pulled into the snow as the pilot attempted a go-around. The aircraft came to rest after contacting the VASIS lights, breaking the nose wheel, left wing strut and damaging the left main gear. The pilot was not injured and was able to exit the substantially damaged aircraft without any assistance.

C-GEIV, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 departed Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, on flight AC253 under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. The flight crew anticipated turbulence and made a passenger announcement to have cabin crew and passengers seated during descent. While descending through flight level 310, severe turbulence was encountered and caused an uncommanded 30-degree bank and changes in airspeed. The flight crew reported the turbulence to air traffic control. The flight continued and landed at CYVR without further incident.  Maintenance completed the severe or unusual turbulence inspection and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FWRM, un Beech BE10 exploité par Propair, effectuait le vol PRO4700 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Rouyn, QC (CYUY) à destination de l'aéroport Jean Lesage Intl de Québec, QC (CYQB) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 9 passagers à bord. À 105 Nm au nord de Montréal, QC, l'équipage a observé l'indicateur de quantité d'essence du réservoir de gauche diminuant jusqu'à 150 lbs alors que le droit indiquait 800 lbs. Suspectant une fuite de carburant, l'équipage a alors déclaré une urgence et procédé à un déroutement vers l'aéroport La Macaza - Mont-Tremblant international, QC (CYFJ) où l'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre. Une inspection subséquente du service de maintenance a révélé un connecteur desserré sur l'indicateur de quantité de carburant gauche.

C-GPGH, an De Havilland Dash 8-402 operated by PAL Airlines Ltd was conducting a flight PVL2284 from Ottawa MacDonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, and C-GYGU an Airbus A321 operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA664 from Montréal Pierre Elliot Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, both landing at Halifax Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. During the arrival in the CYHZ terminal control area (TCA), Nav Canada ATC was required to have separation of 3 nm laterally and 1000 feet vertically, however there was a loss of separation between the aircraft and reduced to 2.7 nm laterally and 600 feet vertically. Both aircraft landed in CYHZ without further incident. Nav Canada is conducting their own internal investigation.

N658UA, a Boeing B767-322ER aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UA3 from Chicago O’Hare International Airport (KORD), Illinois, US, to Zurich Airport (LSZH), Switzerland. While in cruise, a flight attendant became ill. The pilots declared a medical emergency and diverted to Gander International Airport (CYQX), NL.

C-GWWJ, a Westjet B737-800 was operating flight WS2210 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International Airport (MMPR), Puerto Vallarta, Mexico. During cruise a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue duties. The positions were reassigned amongst remaining crew members. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FZAA, a Helijet International Sikorsky 76A departed Vancouver Harbour Heliport (CBC7), BC, on flight JBA785, under instrument flight rules, to Victoria Harbour/Camel Point Heliport (CBF7), BC. While conducting the cruise checks, level at 5000 feet, the flight crew detected a faint electrical odour. Engine anti-ice and pitot heat were both on when the two pilots noticed smoke emitting from above the instrument panel. Smoke was also seen coming from the upper left corner of the pilot's monitoring window. The flight crew declared a MAYDAY, and requested vectors to descend through the cloud. They followed the emergency checklist procedures and turned off the AC generator and all anti-ice equipment. The smoke dispersed. The flight crew were visual with Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, and elected to decrease the emergency to a PAN PAN and they landed without further incident.Maintenance investigated and determined the cause was an automatic flight control system amplifier pitch segment internal failure. The segment was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FDRZ, a Carson Air Limited B300 (King Air 350), departed Dawson Creek Airport (CYDQ), BC, on flight CRN444, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During the approach to CYVR, the gear handle was selected down but no corresponding green lights illuminated to indicate the landing gear was down and locked. The crew conducted a missed approach and continued under visual flight rules to run checklists and troubleshoot the issue. They manually extended the landing gear and requested that aircraft rescue and firefighting crews be standing by. The aircraft landed without further incident. The occurrence aircraft also had a gear indication failure 3 days prior to this incident, on 17 December 2024 (A24W0154). Maintenance replaced a number of parts and switches and conducted landing gear checks. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GFJZ, a Jazz Aviation CRJ900 departed Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, on flight JZA479, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Approximately 1 hour and 20 minutes into the flight, a flight attendant became ill. A doctor and nurse, on board as passengers, were able to attend the ill flight attendant. The flight crew requested through their company dispatch that emergency services meet the aircraft in CYVR. The crew requested priority but did not declare an emergency with air traffic control. After landing, the flight attendant was taken to the hospital for assessment.

C-GKAO, a Pilatus PC-12/47E operated by Keewatin Air LP (dba Kivalliq Air), was conducting flight KEW404 from Morden Regional Aerodrome (CJA3), MB, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. After departing and at approximately 5000 feet, the flight crew engaged the autopilot. The autopilot engaged, then disengaged, and "autopilot fail" and "yaw damper fail" messages were illuminated. The flight crew determined the aircraft was in a slipping attitude and ascertained that the rudder trim was fully deflected to the left and the aileron trim was fully deflected to the right. Control of the aircraft was maintained through physical strength on the flight controls and the aircraft was retrimmed. The flight crew engaged the autopilot again and the rudder trim deflected to the left again. The crew immediately disconnected the autopilot, retrimmed the aircraft and continued by hand-flying the aircraft. The flight crew referred to the quick reference handbook and found there was no published procedure to address this failure. The flight continued under visual meteorological conditions at a reduced airspeed and landed safely in CYWG. The aircraft was removed from service and the operator replaced the trim adapter unit.

C-GCBK, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting flight PAG607 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to St. Theresa Point Airport (CYST), MB. On descent into CYST in uncontrolled airspace, the flight crew received an advisory from Thunder Bay Radio that C-GXHS, a Beech 200 operated by Beaver Air Services Limited (dba Missinippi Airways), had departed Island Lake Airport (CYIV), MB. The flight crew was able to locate the aircraft on the TCAS display but was not able to make radio contact with the traffic. PAG607 leveled at 9000 feet ASL and continued trying to contact the traffic on 126.7 MHz, with no response. The conflicting traffic continued to climb through 8000 feet ASL. The flight crew disconnected the autopilot and conducted a right turn for conflict resolution. During the turn a TCAS RA was issued, requiring that the aircraft remain level or descend. The flight crew followed the RA and, after completing the turn, visual passage of the conflicting traffic was confirmed. PAG607 resumed the descent and landed safely in CYST.

C-GXAX, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-8 (Max) was operating as flight WJA114 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. On approach into CYYC, the flight crew requested the emergency vehicles to be on standby as they had blown a nosewheel tire on departure from CYVR. After the landing, the aircraft was inspected for damage and taxied to the gate with no further issues.

C-FCJP, a CargoJet Boeing 757-200, was operating as flight CJT2402 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Hamilton Airport (CYHM), ON. While in cruise, the aircraft began to lose cabin pressure and in response the flight crew conducted an emergency descent. A Mayday was declared and the flight crew diverted to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, and landed without further issue.

C-FHEN, a Westjet Encore DHC Dash 8 Q400 departed Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC, on flight WEN3106, under instrument flight rules to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. As the aircraft climbed through approximately 14 000 feet above sea level, the cabin pressure warning light illuminated. The crew donned oxygen masks declared a PAN PAN urgency and requested descent to the minimum radar vectoring altitude. During the descent, the captain determined that the bleed air was off. The bleed air was turned on and the cabin began to pressurize. The crew levelled the aircraft at 12 000 feet above sea level while normal pressurization was regained. The crew cancelled the emergency, climbed to cruise altitude, and landed at CYVR without further incident.

C-GULU un ATR 42-320 exploité par Canadian North sous l'indicatif AKT805 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Pangnirtung, NU (CYXP) à destination de l'aéroport d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) avec 20 passagers et 3 membres d'équipage. Au moment de l'atterrissage à destination, l'agent de bord a été victime d'un malaise l'empêchant d'accomplir ses tâches. Elle a demandé l'aide d'un employé de la compagnie qui volait comme passager. Le processus de débarquement a été effectué par le commandant de bord alors que l'agent de bord attendait l'ambulance pour être transporté à l'hôpital.

C-FHNF un Boeing 737-700 exploité par Canadian North sous l'indicatif AKT163, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Kuujjuaq QC (CYVP) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) avec 45 passagers et 5 membres d'équipage. Peu de temps après le décollage de la fumée sortant du four de l'office de bord arrière a été détectée. Le circuit électrique du four a été coupé et la fumée s'est dissipée. Le four ouvert a révélé que la fumée provenait d'un liquide ayant coulé d'un plat. Le tout a été nettoyé et le vol s'est poursuivi sans encombre.

C-FOJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP Bombardier CL600-2D24 (Series 900) was operating as flight JZA114 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. During the descent the flight crew reported to ATS that they may have a nose wheel steering issue and declared an emergency. The flight landed and taxied off the runway with no issues.

C-GLUQ, a Can-West Air Beechcraft King Air 200, operating as flight CWA926 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to High Level Airport (CYOJ), AB, had just departed Runway 30. At about the same time, C-GKXQ, a Porter Airlines E295, operating as POE407, was arriving on Runway 02. Separation was reduced to less than the required 2 nm. There was no risk of collision. There were no further issues with either flight.

C-GTVO, a Chrono Jet Inc. Boeing 737-200, was operating as flight BFL218 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Goose Lake Aerodrome (CGS2), NU. During the approach to CGS2, the flight crew noticed the hydraulic quantity in System "A" decreasing to "0" but the pressure remained normal. The crew diverted back to CYZF. During the approach, the Hydraulic System A LOW PRESSURE light illuminated. A Pan Pan was declared, checklists consulted, and the flight successfully landed on Runway 34 in CYZF. The flight crew stopped the aircraft on the runway and requested a tow back to the ramp.Following the flight the maintenance team performed maintenance to the hydraulic system and returned the aircraft to service.

C-GKWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402, was operating as flight WEN4074 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Fort Mackay/Firebag Airport (CYFI), AB. During the take-off roll the flight crewed received a pitch trim caution light and immediately rejected the take-off. An emergency was declared. The aircraft came to a stop safely. Company maintenance did not find any faults and returned the aircraft to service.

C-GGWX, un B737-400 exploité par Nolinor Aviation, sous l'indicatif NLR661, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Wabush, NL (CYWK) à destination de l'aéroport de Bagotville, QC (CYBG) avec 131 passagers et 7 membres d'équipage. À la suite d'une approche interrompue à cause de la mauvaise météo, le vol a été redirigé vers l'aéroport international Québec - Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Alors que l'aéronef était établi en approche LPV sur la piste 06 à CYQB, l'appareil s'est mis à tourner vers la droite. L'équipage a alors remarqué un problème de volets asymétriques avec une indication du volet de gauche à 25 degrés et celui de droite à 14 degrés. Une situation d'urgence a été déclaré en effectuant une remontée. La procédure pour cette situation a été suivie et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre après un circuit pour la piste 06.

C-GWRG, a Boeing 737-8CT operated by Westjet was conducting flight WS408 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Moncton / Greater Moncton Roméo Leblanc International Airport (CYQM), NB. At approximately 81 nm north-west of Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, a cabin crew member was unable to perform their flight duties. Cabin flight duties were reassigned and aircraft landed without incident at CYQM.

C-FTXF, a Sunwing B737 Max 8 was operating flight SWG626 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Juan Gualberto Gómez International Airport (MUVR), Varadero, Cuba. During climb, the crew declared an emergency due to a burning smell in the cockpit. The crew elected to return to CYYZ, where the aircraft landed safely and was met by emergency services.

C-GKQC, a Porter Airlines De Havilland DHC-8-400, operating as PTR2704 from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, declared a MAYDAY emergency on final for Runway 24L due to smoke in the aft cabin. The aircraft stopped on the runway as fire trucks met the flight for passenger evacuation procedures. After evacuation, the aircraft was towed off the runway.

C-FYKX, a Sunwing B737-800 was operating flight SWG774 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Rio Hato Scarlett R. Martinez L. Airport (MPSM), Panama. During the approach into MPSM, the flight crew selected flaps 1 and subsequently identified a flap asymmetry. ATC was advised and the crew requested a hold to complete the checklist. A PAN PAN was declared and a trailing edge flaps up landing was completed without further incident.

C-GSHJ, a Helijet International Incorporated S-76C++ helicopter departed the Vancouver/Harbour Public Heliport (CBC7), BC, on flight HJ983, under visual flight rules, to Nanaimo Harbour Heliport (CDH5), BC. The helicopter conducted a visual approach to the final approach and take off (FATO) area and then hover taxied to Helipad B. During shutdown, the pilots were informed that a pedestrian had been knocked over by the rotor downwash. The pedestrian had disembarked from the Hullo Ferry and was walking from the terminal (300 feet north-northwest of the FATO) to the parking lot (150 feet south of Helipad B). The walkway between the 2 points runs parallel to, and between 10 and 20 feet from, the fence on the east side of the heliport; 60 to 70 feet east of the 2 helipads. Paramedics were called and the individual was taken to hospital to treat a serious injury.Helijet is installing a new perimeter fence to mitigate the effects of rotor downwash.

C-GPWG, an Air Canada Airbus A320-211 was operating flight ACA584 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ. Shortly after departure, at approximately 0814 MST, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency due to a fuel indication issue. The flight crew elected to return to CYYC and landed safely at 0845. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft.

C-FXYK, a Westjet Airlines Boeing 737-8 departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, on flight WS129, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, the first officer reported feeling ill and was unable to continue their duties. One of the passengers on board was a Westjet pilot who was able to assume the first officer's duties. The incapacitated first officer sat in the cabin for the remainder of the flight. The flight crew did not declare an emergency or request a priority handling. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FDRZ, a Carson Air Ltd. Beech BE30 operating as CRN444-Medevac, was on an instrument rules flight from the Smithers Airport (CYYD), BC, to Fort St. John Airport (CYXJ), BC.
