During the approach to CYXJ, the landing gear handle was selected down but no corresponding green lights illuminated to indicate the landing gear was down and locked. At approximately 1922 MST, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency, requested aircraft rescue and firefighting vehicles be dispatched, and then manually lowered the landing gear. The aircraft landed safely at 1927 MST.The aircraft was inspected and tested but maintenance was unable to duplicate the error. The aircraft was returned to service.NOTE: ON 20 Dec 2024, the occurrence aircraft experienced another landing gear indication issue (TSB investigation A24P0153).

C-FYKX, un Boeing 737-8K5 exploité par Sunwing Airlines Inc., effectuait le vol SWG9771 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport Scarlett Martínez Intl - Rio Hato, Panama City, Panama (MPSM) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec seul 8 membres d'équipage à bord. En passant 4000 pi. lors de la descente de CYUL, l'équipage a reçu une indication d'assymétrie du système de volets empêchant ceux-ci de se déployer. L'équipage a averti ATC, suivi les procédures normalisées et déclaré une urgence. L'aéronef a ensuite atterri sans encombre avec les volets rentrés. Les actions suivantes ont été prises par la maintenance: Remplacement de l'indicateur de position des volets, lubrification des volets, inspection et nettoyage du connecteur du transmetteur de position des volets (aucune anomalie trouvée à ce niveau), inspection et essai du système de volets (aucune anomalie trouvée à ce niveau) et vol d'essai post-maintenance satisfaisant, après quoi l'aéronef a été remis en service.

C-GEHY, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 aircraft, was conducting flight AC113 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During the flight, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to carry on their duties.

C-GGMI, a Jazz Aviation DHC-8-400 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Timmins Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise the flight crew received a Flap Power caution warning, the flight crew followed the quick reference handbook, and the light extinguished. The caution light returned as the flight continued, and the crew declared a PAN PAN and prepared for a flapless landing. The aircraft performed an uneventful landing on runway 23 with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by. Maintenance replaced the Flap Power switch and performed an operational test without further faults.

C-FMHA, a Boeing B757 aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express Inc., was conducting flight MAL7054 from Greater Moncton Roméo LeBlanc International Airport (CYQM), NB, to Halifax Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. Just after rotation from CYQM, the crew received multiple electrical failure indications, including airspeed indication, vertical speed indication, wind shear, left and right engine EEC EICAS, Mach/Trim EICAS, and radio EICAS. The crew performed all required quick reference handbook procedures and declared PAN PAN with ATC. Additional failures and alerts occurred enroute to CYHZ. The crew landed the aircraft safely.Once on the ramp, maintenance began troubleshooting the issues. Water was found in the electrical bay under the main cargo door. Once the system was checked and the water removed, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWUU, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 departed Bangkok/Suvarnabhumi International Airport (VTBS), Thailand, operating flight AC66, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, the crew received engine indication and crew alerting system (EICAS) message to conduct a spoiler checklist. The crew completed the checklist and spoiler number 11 was isolated. A PAN PAN was declared with air traffic control and emergency vehicles were put on standby. The aircraft landed without incident and there were no injuries.An inspection on the spoiler rigging was carried out and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GEEN, a Westjet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Dash 8 Q400 departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, on flight WEN3297, under instrument flight rules, to Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC. The flight crew conducted a missed approach in CYXS due to weather and diverted to CYVR. The flight crew informed air traffic control (ATC) that they were at minimum fuel. En route to CYVR, the crew reduced airspeed and set bleed air to minimum to reduce fuel consumption.  The crew contacted ATC and requested a shortened routing and steeper than usual descent into CYVR. Prior to descent the flight crew calculated that they would land with less than the required minimum fuel reserve and declared a Mayday. The aircraft landed without further incident with 1200 pounds of fuel on board.

C-FKEX, un BE20 exploité par Keewatin Air LP, effectuait un vol d’évacuation médicale entre l'aéroport de Cape Dorset (CYCT), NU et l'aéroport d'Iqaluit (CYFB), NU avec 3 passagers et 2 membres d'équipage. L'aéronef était dans sa phase de montée lorsque l’équipage a été confronté à une dépressurisation rapide au niveau de vol FL200. L’équipage a exécuté les procédures d’urgence mémorisées et amorcé une descente. Une fois à une altitude sécuritaire, ils ont complété la liste de vérification associée, confirmé que les passagers n’étaient pas blessés, effectué un calcul progressif de carburant pour une altitude de route inférieure et déterminé que la meilleure décision était de poursuivre le vol vers Iqaluit. Le reste du vol et l’atterrissage se sont déroulés sans incident. Une inspection a révélé que le joint de la porte de cabine s'était déplacé de son assise supérieure. Le joint a été replacé selon le manuel de maintenance et un essai de pressurisation a été effectué avec succès.

C-GHQQ, an Air Canada B787-8 was operating flight AC878 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Toulouse-Blagnac Airport (LFBO), France. During cruise, prior to top of descent (TOD), a flight attendant became ill and was unable to carry duties. The duties were reassigned to the remaining flight attendants. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FCQX, an Air Canada A320-214 was operating flight AC562 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA. On arrival into KSFO, the crew selected gear down and received an ECAM gear not locked message. The crew did a missed approach and went through the quick reference handbook and cycled the gear which cleared the fault. ATC declared a PAN PAN on the crew's behalf. The flight landed and stopped on the runway for aircraft rescue and firefighting to inspect, the aircraft then taxied to the gate under its own power without further issue.

C-GOIX, an Air Transat A321-200 was operating flight TSC112 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Juan Santamaría International Airport (MROC), Costa Rica. After the second approach into MROC, the crew were unable to land due to poor visibility and elected to divert to the alternate Tocumen International Airport Panama (MPTO), Panama. The crew declared minimum fuel and the aircraft landed safely.

C-FDWO, un Dash-8-106 (DH8A) exploité par Air Creebec Inc. sous l’indicatif CRQ921, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Eastmain, QC (CZEM) à destination de l'aéroport de Wemindji, QC (CYNC) avec 16 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait à environ 20 miles marins au sud de CYNC, une indication de basse pression d’huile du moteur droit est apparue. L’équipage a réduit la puissance au ralenti et quelque temps plus tard, lorsque la pression d’huile a diminué sous 40 psi, le moteur (Pratt & Whitney-Canada, PW121) a été fermé. L’aéronef s’est posé sur la piste 10 à CYNC sans encombre. L’inspection post-envolée a révélé une fuite d’huile du côté droit du moteur de droite.

C-GKQD, un DeHavilland DHC-8-400 exploité par Porter Airlines sous l'indicatif PTR2473, et C-GHKX, un Airbus A330-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA823 effectuaient leur vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, tous les deux à destination de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL). PTR2473 venait de compléter un virage a droite pour l'approche de la piste 24L alors que ACA2483 était lui aussi en rapprochement pour l’approche de la même piste. La séparation entre les deux aéronefs a été réduite à 2.2 miles nautiques (NM) à la même altitude alors que la distance latéral minimum était de 3 NM et la séparation verticale prescrite était de 1000 pieds.

C-FQGB, a privately registered Mooney M20C, was conducting circuits at Taber Aerodrome (CED5), AB, with a pilot and one passenger on board. On the initial climb for the third circuit, the pilot and passenger began discussing the CHT and EGT indication, and the landing gear was not retracted. The aircraft is equipped with a manual type landing gear retraction mechanism. On the downwind leg of the circuit, the pilot observed that the indicated airspeed was slower than normal but did not correlate that to the landing gear still being extended.  Turning base leg, the pilot attempted to configure the aircraft for landing by turning on the boost pump and operating the gear extension lever. The landing gear was now retracted, and the gear unsafe light was illuminated on the instrument panel. At this point, there was another conversation in the cockpit about the runway approach lights no longer being operable, and the gear unsafe light went unnoticed. The approach was continued and the aircraft made contact with the runway with the landing gear fully retracted, approximately 1/3 to 1/2 way down the runway. The aircraft skidded to a stop on the runway, and the pilot and passenger exited the aircraft. There were no injuries and no reported mechanical issues with the aircraft prior to the accident.

C-GKXQ, a Porter Airlines E190-400, was conducting flight POE265 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue with their assigned duties. An off-duty flight attendant took over their duties and the flight continued to destination.

C-GVTA, a Top Aces Alpha Jet, was operating flight TONIC2 from Nordholz Airport (ETMN), Germany. After 50 minutes of flight, one of the internal tank groups appeared overfilled on the main fuel gauge indicating a fuel transfer abnormality. An airborne inspection by the wingman observed that fuel was venting overboard from the main fuel vent mast. An emergency was declared due to abnormal fuel venting, and the mission was aborted. The aircraft returned for a straight-in approach at ETMN without further incident. The aircraft was taxied clear of the runway and shut down in-place to minimize potential runway/taxiway surface contamination due to fuel venting. Runway inspection by airfield services indicated no runway/taxiway surface fuel contamination.

C-GVCO, un Cessna C-172F en exploitation privé effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Rivière-Du-Loup, Québec (CYRI) avec seul le pilote à bord. Environ 20 minutes après le décollage, alors que l’aéronef était en vol de croisière à 2500 pieds ASL, le pilote a sélectionné le réchauffage du carburateur. Lorsque le pilote a fermé le réchauffage du carburateur, le régime du moteur est passé de 2300 RPM à 1000 RPM et la puissance ne pouvait pas être augmenté. Le pilote a remis le réchauffage du carburateur, mais la puissance ne pouvait toujours pas être augmentée. Le pilote a effectué un atterrissage d’urgence dans un champ. Toutefois, une fois au sol la roue de nez s’est brisée et l’avion a glissé sur le nez, passé le bout du champ à basse vitesse et a percuté un arbre. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé, toutefois l'aéronef a subi des dommages importants. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée et le signal a été captée par le système de satellites Cospas-Sarsat, qui a relayé les renseignements au Centre conjoint de coordination de sauvetage à Halifax (Nouvelle-Écosse). Le pilote a fermé l’ELT quelques minutes après l’accident.

D-AFYR, an Airbus 330 aircraft operated by Discover Airlines, was conducting flight OCN3 from Punta Cana International Airport (MDCP), Dominican Republic, to Frankfurt Airport (EDDF), Germany. G-YMMB, a Boeing 777-200 aircraft operated by British Airways, was conducting flight BAW25K from Norman Manley International Airport (MKJP), Jamaica, to London Gatwick Airport (EGKK), England. During cruise, OCN3 requested to deviate right of track due to weather. The aircraft later requested deviations left of track and FL380. The controller did not update the profile and kept protecting for a deviation right of track. OCN3 was eventually cleared to FL380. Due to the sudden increase in workload due to weather deviations, the controller’s tasks were split with another controller. The new controller recognized that OCN3 was deviating towards BAW25K, also at FL380. A loss of separation occurred when only 10 NM of separation was established where 14 NM is the required separation. BAW25K was cleared to FL370 to regain separation. NAV CANADA is conducting an internal investigation into this loss of separation.

C-GUFQ, a privately registered Yakovlev Yak 18 was conducting circuits at Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, under visual flight rules with only the pilot on board. The pilot had conducted several circuits at CYCD with no issues. On the final circuit, the pilot selected flaps and gear down. The pilot felt the aircraft land on the main gear as normal but the nose wheel subsequently collapsed followed by the main gear. The propeller struck the surface, and the aircraft came to rest on its belly, on the runway. The annual inspection had been completed the month prior to the occurrence and had included a complete check of the operational and emergency operation of the landing gear. Both main gear wheels had been replaced. The aircraft was cleared from the runway and a propeller strike and engine inspection will be conducted.

C-GYSR, a Beechcraft King Air 200 operated by Keewatin Air, was conducting flight KEW208 from Gjoa Haven Airport (CYHK), NU, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. During cruise flight, approximately 80 nm NE of CYZF, the flight crew noticed the left and right bleed air fail annunciator flickering intermittently prior to receiving a dual bleed air fail warning light. The flight crew completed the appropriate checklist items and determined that the warning was likely related to the warning system itself. A PAN PAN was declared with air traffic services and priority handling requested. As the left engine temperature was indicating a slightly higher temperature than previous, the crew elected to turn off the left bleed air for the remainder of the flight. An uneventful landing was completed in CYZF.Subsequent investigation by company maintenance determined that the cockpit/cabin bleed air valve assembly was partially detached which allowed hot air to melt the EVA tubing for the bleed air warning system, and illuminate the bleed air fail warning annunciator. The valve was correctly installed and the tubing repaired in accordance with the manufacturer's maintenance manual. A ground check was performed and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FSFP, a Cessna 525B operated by Airsprint Inc., was conducting flight ASP686 from Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), CA, USA, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Approximately 104 nm SSE of CYYC, the flight crew received an avionics overtemp CAS message with a GIA2 overtemp. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist and began a slow decent into the CYYC area. Approximately 10 minutes later, the flight crew received a GIA1 overtemp CAS message. The flight crew referenced the checklist again and contacted ATS to request priority handling. At this point, C-FSFP was approximately 5-10 minutes from landing. The flight continued to CYYC where an uneventful landing was completed.Subsequent investigation by company maintenance found the avionics fault cleared with an aircraft power reset. Diagnostic information was sent to Textron for further analysis. This is a known issue with the aircraft avionics system, and Textron has published guidance material for operators regarding the erroneous condition/indication.

C-FYKW, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114, was conducting flight ROU1692 from Ottawa/Macdonald–Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), Florida. During the taxi to the active runway, a flight attendant became ill. Their safety-related duties were distributed to other cabin crew members for the remainder of the flight.

C-FMXG, a Sunwing B737-8 was operating flight SWG6204 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Cayo Coco/Jardines Del Rey Airport (MMUC), Cuba. During cruise a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue with duties. These duties were redistributed amongst remaining crew members.

C-GOWG, a Sunwing B737-8 was operating flight SWG378 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Juan Gualberto Gómez International Airport (MUVR), Varadero, Cuba. During cruise, the AFT cargo warning light illuminated with associated fire warning bell and light. The crew executed the non-normal checklist for cargo fire and decided to return to CYUL. ATC was advised and initiated the air turnback. After landing, the aircraft stopped on the runway for inspection by aircraft rescue and firefighting. The cargo hold was opened, and no smoke or fire was observed. The aircraft taxied to the gate and passengers deplaned.

RP-C7782, an Air Philippines Corporation (dba Philippine Airlines) Boeing 777-300ER departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, on flight PAL5117 under instrument flight rules, to Ninoy Aquino International Airport (RPLL), Manila, Philippines. Approximately 40 minutes into the flight, the crew reported a burning smell in the aircraft to air traffic control (ATC). The crew declared a PAN PAN and requested a return to CYVR. The crew dumped fuel and landed safely. The aircraft was taxied to the gate under its own power.The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GNGM, a privately registered ski-equipped Piper PA-20X, departed from Candle Lake Airpark (CCL2), SK, for a VFR flight to Torch Lake, Saskatchewan. The pilot was completing takeoffs and landings on Torch Lake and the first landing was uneventful. On the second landing, the aircraft touched down and experienced a right-hand gear failure immediately after touchdown. Upon hearing a loud bang and feeling the right wing drop, the pilot pulled the mixture lever to stop the engine. The wing tip contacted the snow and the wing dragged approximately 30 feet. The pilot maintained directional control until the aircraft came to a stop.A post-incident inspection by the pilot revealed a failure crack on the right-hand landing gear which connects to the bungee assembly. The engine, propeller, and gear attachment points were also inspected and no additional damage was found.

C-GELD, a Piper PA-31 Navajo registered to Adventure Aviation, was conducting VFR circuits at the Grand Prairie Airport (CYQU), AB, with the pilot and one passenger onboard. During the initial climb after take-off, the pilot observed an abnormal landing gear indication. The pilot climbed to circuit altitude and attempted to cycle the landing gear.  It was observed by both the pilot and passenger that the landing gear was neither retracting nor extending and the landing gear handle was not returning to the "neutral" position with either selection. The manual extension hydraulic hand pump was operated in an attempt to extend the landing gear, and a flyby of the tower was performed. It was observed that only one main landing gear was in a partially extended position and the remaining landing gear were retracted. The pilot continued to operate the manual hydraulic pump, and the landing gear eventually indicated down and locked. The pilot then performed additional tower flybys to confirm that the landing gear appeared to be fully extended and requested emergency services be placed on standby. The aircraft completed an uneventful landing approximately 20 minutes after take-off. Subsequent investigation by aircraft maintenance found nothing abnormal. Multiple landing gear operational checks were performed, and a test flight was successfully completed.

C-GWEJ, a Westjet Encore DHC-8-400 (Dash 8 Q400) departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, on flight WEN3367, under instrument flight rules, to Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC. WEN3367 conducted a missed approach in CYCD due to weather conditions and initiated their flight to their alternate at Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC.  Due to traffic at CYLW, the requested approach was not immediately available to the flight crew. They determined that the situation would result in a fuel critical situation and declared a Mayday. The aircraft landed safely in CYLW.  The aircraft landed with approximately 200 pounds less fuel than had been determined to be the minimum fuel reserve.

C-FYPN, un Boeing 737-2T4 exploité par Chrono Jet inc. sous l'indicatif MBK50, effectuait un essai en vol après maintenance local selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis de l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU). Durant le décollage, l’équipage a dû appliquer un maximum de pression vers l’avant du manche et actionner la pleine compensation électrique vers l’avant pour réduire l’angle de montée. La puissance a été réduite pour aider au contrôle du tangage et l’avion s’est stabilisé à 5000 pieds. Le vol a été annulé et l’équipage est retourné à CYHU pour un atterrissage sans encombre. Des éléments du connecteur de la commande de compensation ont été trouvés rompus. Le connecteur a été changé et le système remis à l'essai avec succès.

C-GGDC, a Thunder Airlines MU-2B-60, was conducting flight THU880 from Sudbury Airport (CYSB), ON, to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. While on descent to CYOW the crew received a low oil pressure indication for the number 1 engine. The fault appeared to be indication only and the crew decided to return to CYSB and declared an emergency. Aircraft landed uneventfully with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by. Maintenance replaced the engine 1 oil pressure gauge, and after completing subsequent run-up, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GLQX, a Porter Airlines DHC-8-400 aircraft, was conducting flight PD2124, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, and was in a hold at LINGG at an altitude of 9000 feet ASL, when a loss of separation occurred with a photo survey aircraft which was being controlled by Buffalo Approach. Separation was reduced to 0.5 NM lateral and 400 feet vertical.

C-FWJS, a Westjet Airlines Boeing 737-800 departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, on flight WJA114, under instrument flight rules, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the take-off roll from Runway 26L, the aircraft struck a bird. The impact was near the captain's pitot tube and angle of attack indicator. The aircraft was travelling at approximately 90 knots, takeoff was rejected and a MAYDAY was declared. CYVR tower air traffic control did not acknowledge the transmission and aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) crews were not deployed. The crew taxied the aircraft to the gate under its own power without ARFF assistance.   A bird strike and a high energy stop inspection were carried out with no damage found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FWVJ, a Boeing 737-800 operated by WestJet Airlines, was conducting flight WJA147 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. (CYWG) to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. N16234, a Boeing 737-800 operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL1029 from Denver International Airport (KDEN), CO, to CYEG. The active runway at CYEG at the time was Runway 12. UAL1029 was on approach for runway 12 behind WJA147. Due to eroding separation, UAL1029's approach was discontinued, and aircraft was vectored for a second approach. IFR separation was reduced to 2.2 NM on final where 3 NM is required.

C-GSWU, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by Miccar Aerial Ltd. was conducting an IFR flight from Key Lake Aerodrome (CYKJ), SK, to the Flin Flon Airport (CYFO), MB. During the approach into CYFO, the landing gear down indicators were three green as confirmed by both the captain and first officer. After landing on Runway 01 at CYFO, the right main landing gear collapsed during rollout. The aircraft came to rest on the runway. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained damage to the right wing and right propeller.The operator's maintenance department moved the aircraft off the runway and is examining the aircraft to determine the cause.

C-FRJZ, an IAI Astra SPX (Gulfstream G100) aircraft operated by Latitude Air Ambulance, departed the Gander International Airport (CYQX), NL, on a flight to Hamilton/John C. Munro International Airport (CYHM), ON. As the aircraft climbed through 10 000 feet the crew observed the right side and backup airspeed indicator readings become erratic, which was accompanied by multiple warning flags for airspeed, pitch, and attitude indications. The crew successfully transferred left airspeed data to the right system. The crew felt the aircraft buffeting and conferred with air traffic services (ATS) to obtain groundspeed values to evaluate the indications. They also monitored engine power and angle of attack readings. The aircraft buffeting continued, and the crew declared an emergency with ATS and requested a long final return to CYQX. During the return to CYQX the aircraft displayed annunciations related to air brake and automatic slat functions, although neither system deployed. The crew tried various flap settings at higher altitude to test for effect and decided to use flaps at 20 degrees for the landing at CYQX which was made on Runway 03 without further incident. There were no injuries.Maintenance personnel inspected and found moisture in the aircraft right pitot system. Both pitot systems were inspected and cleaned, and the air data computer was removed and replaced as a precautionary measure.

C-GACM, a Western Aerial Applications Limited SA 315B (Lama) was operating from a staging area approximately 10 nautical miles north of the Squamish Aerodrome (CYSE), BC, with only the pilot on board. The pilot was conducting operations in support of an aerial fertilization project under visual flight rules. Pelletized fertilizer was loaded from a truck/auger into the spreader bucket slung beneath the helicopter. The fertilizer was then spread over the forest. After receiving the tenth load of the day, the pilot applied power to depart. A loud noise was heard and the helicopter began to vibrate abnormally. While backing the helicopter away from the loading auger, the aircraft began an uncommanded yaw. The pilot immediately landed the helicopter on the forest road behind the auger. On landing, the main rotor blades contacted a raised berm beside the road and the helicopter was majorly damaged. There were no injuries.The helicopter was trailered to an aircraft maintenance facility, where the main rotor gearbox will be disassembled and inspected to determine the cause of the inadvertent yaw.

C-FMPD, an Inland Air Charters Limited De Havilland DHC-2 MK.I (Beaver) was departing from Dolphins North Lodge, BC, on a visual flight rules flight to Eagle Point Lodge, BC, with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. The aircraft was pushed off from the dock at Dolphins North Lodge for departure. Subsequently a gust of wind turned the aircraft back towards the lodge. The pilot started the engine in an attempt to taxi away from the lodge for takeoff. The wing tip struck the deck of the lodge and the pilot shut down the engine. The pilot allowed the aircraft to drift away from the dock before restarting the engine and parking back at the dock. There were no reported injuries. The aircraft had minor damage to the left wing tip. A company aircraft maintenance engineer (AME) was dispatched to the lodge. The AME confirmed that the left wing tip and the left wing rear attach point were damaged. The aircraft was eventually taxied back to Seal Cove Water Aerodrome (CZSW), BC, where maintenance replaced the left wing assembly. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJZY, un DeHavilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA7971 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Billy Bishop de Toronto, ON (CYTZ) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). C-FTQR, un Beech 1900D exploité par Propair Inc, effectuait le vol PRO4925 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de CYUL à destination de l'aéroport de Rouyn Noranda, QC (CYUY). JZA7974 était en descente vers 6000 pieds lorsque l’équipage a reçu un avis de résolution du système de surveillance du trafic et d'évitement des collisions (TCAS) en raison de PRO4925 qui était en palier à 5000 pieds.

C-GVUE, a privately registered Cessna 340A, was operating an IFR flight from Fond-du-Lac Airport (CZFD), SK, to La Ronge/Barber Field Airport (CYVC), SK. On descent to CYVC, the aircraft encountered unexpected freezing drizzle and the ice accretion was in excess of what the aircraft de-icing system was capable of shedding. The aircraft subsequently stalled onto the runway in the landing flare.  The right propeller and right wingtip made contact with the runway and were damaged. The aircraft has been removed from service pending repairs.

C-FJQI, an Eagle Air Enterprises Ltd. Piper PA-31-350, was operating a VFR flight from Winnipeg/St. Andrews Airport (CYAV), MB, to Red Sucker Lake Airport (CYRS), MB. Upon touching down on Runway 09 at CYRS, the aircraft veered to the left and struck a snow windrow that was adjacent to the runway. The nosewheel collapsed and the aircraft sustained damage to its left wing, both propellers, and fuselage. There were no injuries.A subsequent inspection by the operator revealed a frozen left brake.

C-FJIC, a Chrono Aviation Cessna 750 was operating flight NDL10 from Montréal/St-Hubert Airport (CYHU), QC, to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. The crew observed a flap malfunction indication. After assessing the malfunction, the crew declared a PAN PAN and continued on to CYXE; where they carried out an uneventful landing.After landing the flaps were reset and the warning cleared.

EI-GEY, an Aer Lingus A330-200 aircraft, was conducting a flight EI126 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International (CYYZ), ON, to Dublin International (EIDW), Ireland. During pushback from the gate at CYYZ and after engine #1 start but during engine #2 start, the crew received an ECAM for a GEN 1 Fault. The crew performed two GEN 1 resets without success. The flight crew noted an electrical burning smell entering the cockpit and opened cockpit windows and shut down both engines. The smoke dissipated but the crew requested a return to the gate. Cabin crew confirmed no smoke in the cabin. The flight crew switched off the APU bleed air and the passengers were deplaned at the gate. Both pilots attended the hospital as a precaution.

C-GWSZ, a Westjet Airlines Boeing 737-800 aircraft, was conducting a flight WJA714 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While being vectored for an approach to CYYZ a loss of separation occurred with Caribbean Airlines BWA600. The controller took corrective action by turning WJA714 left but there was not sufficient time to prevent the loss of separation. Separation was reduced to 2.2 NM lateral and 500 feet vertical.

C-GHPJ, an Air Canada Rouge A321-200, was conducting flight ROU1675 from Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform their normal duties. Their duties were distributed between other flight attendants in accordance with company policies and procedures.

C-FFFX, a Flair Airlines B737-8 was operating flight FLE2811 from Cancún International Airport (MMUN), MX, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, the first officer momentarily fell ill and became incapacitated. A flight attendant was brought to the flight deck to assist and Medlink was contacted. The first officer was administered oxygen, felt better and showed no further signs of distress and in consultation with Medlink the decision was made to continue the flight to CYVR. No further issues occurred during the remainder of the flight and the first officer was able to perform their duties.

C-GDAB, a Sealand Flight Limited Cessna C172M departed Courtenay Airpark (CAH3), BC, on a local training flight, under visual flight rules, with only pilot onboard. The pilot was practicing short field landing techniques and on the occurrence circuit, they landed long. The aircraft skidded off the end of the runway and impacted the perimeter fence. The pilot egressed without injury. The aircraft was substantially damaged.   The aircraft had damage to the nose gear and propeller. The aircraft will be taken to an approved maintenance organization for assessment and repair.

C-FWSK, a WestJet Boeing 737-700 departed Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, on flight WJA194, under instrument flight rules, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the climb out, the cabin crew observed white smoke coming from the aft galley oven; no flames were visible. A cabin crew member used the fire extinguisher on the oven as a precaution. The smoke dissipated, the flight crew was informed, and the flight continued to CYYC without further incident. There were no injuries and the aircraft was not damaged.Company maintenance is investigating the cause. The oven has been de-activated and deferred as per the minimum equipment list and the aircraft has been returned to service.

C-FYMN, un Pilatus PC-12/47 exploité par Chrono Aviation inc. sous l'indicatif NDL987, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Bagotville, QC (CYBG) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 1 passager. Lors de la montée initiale, en passant 2500 pieds, la commande de compensation (trim) s’est emballée et a causé une montée abrupte qui était difficile à contrôler. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et coupé l’alimentation à la commande de compensation avant de regagné le plein contrôle de l’avion. L’avion est revenu se poser à CYQB sans encombre. Durant la recherche de panne, le service de maintenance a trouvé le relais K21 défectueux. Le relais a été remplacé et le système mis à l'essai avec succès.

C-FENU, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, on flight WEN3185 under instrument flight rules, to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. During the take off roll, the aircraft had an AC GEN 2 caution light illuminate. During the initial climb, the No. 2 propeller (Dowty Rotol R408/6-123-F/17) rpm was lower and the No.2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW150A) torque reading was higher than normal. The propeller electronic control (PEC) caution light illuminated. The crew conducted the checklist items, declared a PAN PAN, and requested vectors to return to CYVR. The crew shut down the No. 2 engine and completed the one engine inoperative landing checklist. The aircraft landed safely with the aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) vehicles on standby. The aircraft was taxied off of the runway and, after being inspected by ARFF, continued to the gate under its own power. There were no injuries and the aircraft was not damaged.Maintenance crews found that the No. 2 alternating current generator had failed. The engine and will be replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GTUK, un Boeing 737-200C exploité par Nolinor sous l'indicatif NRL251 était en préparation pour effectuer un vol depuis l'aéroport d'Iqaluit (CYFB), NU à destination de l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC avec 42 passagers et 5 membres d'équipage. Alors que l'embarquement se terminait, de la fumée a été détectée à travers la cabine et le poste de pilotage. Le commandant a alors ordonné une évacuation. Le groupe auxiliaire de bord (APU) qui était resté en marche a été stoppé et l'appareil sécurisé. Les sorties de secours sur les ailes ont été utilisées. Quelques passagers sont sortis sur les ailes et la majorité sont sortis par la porte arrière gauche où l'escalier était encore présent. Les passagers sur les ailes ont été assistés par les employés au sol pour descendre. Après avoir confirmé que la source de la fumée était bien l'APU, celui-ci a été placé sur la liste des problèmes différés et l'appareil a pu effectuer le vol de retour vers CYQB avec quelques heures de retard. L'APU a été remplacé par les techniciens au retour à la base. Le roulement de turbine de l'APU a été identifié comme la source de la défaillance.

C-GMUK, an Airbus Helicopters AS350-B2 operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited, was conducting a flight, under visual flight rules, from Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC, to a remote powerline right-of-way with a work crew. The pilot dropped off the work crew, and then flew to refuel the helicopter. The pilot then conducted reconnaissance and landings at newly identified landing sites near the powerline right-of-way. While lifting off from a site, the pilot felt a bump from the rear of the aircraft. He had no control issues but landed as a precaution at a nearby helipad. After shutdown, damage to a main rotor blade and to the top of the vertical stabilizer was found. There were no injuries.A maintenance team was flown to the aircraft to complete an assessment and to repair the helicopter. BC Hydro dispatched an assessment and repair crew to repair the damaged powerline.

C-FCJU, a Cargojet Airways Limited Boeing 767-316 departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, on flight CJT2384, under instrument flight rules, to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, with 2 flight crew members and 3 jump seaters on board. During the climb out of CYVR, while approaching 10 000 feet above sea level (ASL), the right engine (Pratt & Whitney, PW4060(-3), SN 727767) suffered a compressor stall followed by a large increase in internal temperature. The crew completed the engine limit surge stall checklist, retarded the right engine throttle to idle, and declared a MAYDAY. The crew continued to monitor the engine while descending to 9000 feet ASL. The right engine began vibrating and loud noises began to emanate from it. The crew continued to run the appropriate checklists and shut down the engine as a precaution. In an effort to avoid an overweight landing, the aircraft was flown west while maintaining 9000 feet ASL and entered a hold over Vancouver Island for approximately 2 hours. Once sufficient fuel had been used to achieve a normal landing weight, the aircraft turned back to CYVR. With aircraft rescue and firefighting crews standing by, the aircraft made an uneventful one engine inoperative landing. There were no injuries. Company maintenance carried out a visual inspection of the right engine. Metal was found in the exhaust area indicating an internal engine failure. An engine change is ongoing.

C-GZPA, a Perimeter Aviation De Havilland DHC-8-102, was enroute from Thompson Regional Airport (CYTH), MB, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. During cruise, the flight crew observed a decrease of fluid level on the gauge of the #2 hydraulic system. Based on the flight crew's rough calculations that they were losing 1/2 quart of fluid every 15 minutes, the flight crew determined that the fluid quantity would be depleted prior to landing in CYWG. The flight crew performed the quick reference handbook for a complete #2 hydraulic system failure in preparation for landing and declared an emergency. On final, caution lights illuminated indicating a complete #2 hydraulic system failure. The aircraft landed safely in CYWG where they were met by emergency services.A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed a leaking #2 hydraulic pump. The pump was repaired, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSKA, a Kississing Lake Lodge Ltd (dba Wings Over Kississing) Beech 100, had departed Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, on an instrument flight rules flight for Gods Lake Narrows Airport (CYGO), MB. While climbing through 18 000 feet, the crew observed the fault warning light illuminate along with the left engine chip detector light. The crew ran the emergency shutdown drill for the #1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-28). They then requested a clearance to return to CYWG. They declared an emergency and carried out an uneventful landing on Runway 31 with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by.The operator's maintenance discovered a sliver of metal in the chip detector during a post-occurrence inspection and the aircraft was removed from service.

C-FJQH, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-200 was operating flight ROU1661 from Tampa International Airport (KTPA), FL, to Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the takeoff roll, after V1 and prior to rotation, the aircraft experienced a thud and associated adverse yaw of the nose to the right, which was promptly corrected by flight crew. No abnormal engine parameters were observed and takeoff was continued without further incident. Near the top of descent, flight crew elected to declare Pan Pan as a precaution due to potential nose wheel damage. Aircraft rescue and firefighting were on standby and aircraft landed uneventfully. Aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.

C-FIUR, an Air Canada Boeing 777-300 aircraft, was conducting a flight from London Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. After levelling off at cruise altitude, the flight crew received an EICAS tire pressure warning. After reviewing the checklist, the crew confirmed the fault was with #10 tire. Tire pressure continued to decrease during the flight, and during the descent the flight crew declared a PAN PAN. ATC upgraded it to a MAYDAY due to possible runway closure. The aircraft landed uneventfully with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by and was cleared to taxi to the gate. Maintenance replaced the #9 and #10 mating wheels. They found evidence of FOD on the #10 tire. All other tires were checked for damage, but no faults were found.

C-GBZS, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800 aircraft, was conducting a flight as SWG602, was being pushed back from gate 528 at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Airport (CYYZ), ON, when after the number 2 engine start (CFM International CFM56-7B) a fuel leak was noticed by ground personnel. The flight crew completed the shutdown procedures and requested aircraft rescue and firefighting. With maintenance in attendance, the number 2 engine was restarted but the fuel leak continued. The aircraft was towed back to the gate and the passengers were deplaned.

C-FWEP, a Westjet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q 400) departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, on flight number WEN3208, under instrument flight rules, to Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC. During the final approach to CYKA, the flight crew selected landing gear down and the No. 2 hydraulic isolation valve (HYD ISO VLV) caution light illuminated and the hydraulic quantity indicator dropped to 0. The crew conducted a missed approach and entered the published hold while completing the checklist from the quick reference handbook. The crew diverted to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, and declared a PAN PAN. The crew conducted a manual landing gear extension and the aircraft landed safely. Emergency services attended and there was no reported damage to the aircraft. Maintenance replaced the No. 2 hydraulic engine driven pump and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FALQ, un Learjet 45 exploité par Skyjet (fonctionnant comme Air Liaison) effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments entre l'aéroport international Jean Lesage - Québec, QC (CYQB) et l'aéroport international de Gander, NL (CYQX).  Lorsque l'aéronef était en montée vers 41 000 pieds, l'équipage a reçu une indication que le système de pressurisation de la cabine était passer en mode de pressurisation d'urgence lorsque l'aéronef passait 38 000 pieds. L'équipage a affiché 7700 sur le transpondeur et effectué une descente d'urgence après avoir mis les masques à oxygène. La décision de revenir vers CYQB à été prise et l'aéronef c'est posé sans encombre sur la piste 24.

C-FKEX, un Beech B200 exploité par Keewatin Air LP avec l'indicatif KEW217, conduisait un vol selon les règles aux instruments depuis l'aéroport d'Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) à destination de l'aéroport de Pangnirtung, NU (CYXP).  Lorsque l'appareil était en montée passant vers une altitude de 15 000 pieds, l'aéronef a rapidement perdu sa pression cabine. L'équipage a déclaré un état d'urgence (PAN PAN) et décidé de revenir vers CYFB où l'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre. Le personnel de maintenance a déterminé qu'un crochet de verrouillage de la porte principale ne s'engageait pas correctement. Le crochet a été ajusté et le joint d'étanchéité de la porte a été remplacé avant la remise en service de l'aéronef.

C-FPIJ, a Cargojet B767-300 was operating flight CJT3525 from Arturo Merino Benitez International Airport (SCEL), Chile, to Ministro Pistarini/Ezeiza International Airport (SAEZ), Buenos Aires, Argentina. Just prior to top of descent, the aircraft encountered moderate turbulence, hail, and lightning, there was weather around, however the descent path was not painting any weather of concern. The Captain was the Pilot Monitoring while the First Officer was the Pilot Flying. ATC did not mention of any weather and the radar was not depicting any returns. The crew anticipated for some turbulence and slowed down to turbulent penetration speed prior to descent. From FL 350, the aircraft started down the descent into SAEZ. Around 28,000 to 25,000, they encountered moderate turbulence with hail and lightning. The hail was felt for around 10 seconds or so. The turbulence was felt a bit longer. Once out of the weather, there was no visible damage observed however the weather radar failed. Upon landing and taxi to the gate, the ground crew noticed the nose cone was damaged.

C-GGWX, un Boeing 737-400 exploité par Nolinor Aviation, sous l'indicatif NLR662, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international Québec - Jean lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de l'aéroport de Saguenay-Bagotville, QC (CYBG) avec 87 passagers et 7 membres d'équipage. Suite à un problème de volet alors que l'aéronef était en approche à CYBG, l'équipage a signalé l'état d'urgence et dérouté l'aéronef vers l'aéroport international de Montréal-Mirabel, QC (CYMX). Lors de la décélération après l'atterrissage avec les volets en position rentré à CYMX sur la piste 24, le train d'atterrissage principal gauche s'est affaissé jusqu'à ce que le moteur de gauche touche le sol. L'aéronef a continué sa course supporté par le moteur jusqu'à un arrêt complet sur la piste. L'équipage a lancé un appel de détresse au service de circulation aérienne et le service de lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs a immédiatement été déployé vers l'aéronef. Il n'y a pas eu d'incendie et les passagers et l'équipage ont évacué par les glissières d'évacuation. Il n'y a pas de blessé rapporté lors de l'évacuation. L'aéronef a subi des dommages importants.

C-GUBH, an Air Transat A330-200 was operating flight TSC326 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Cancún International Airport (MMUN), MX. The aircraft reached minimum fuel due to thunderstorms at destination and planned alternate. The crew initially declared MIN FUEL situation to the ATC followed by a PAN PAN before being cleared for an approach into Mérida International Airport (MMMD), MX, where the aircraft landed safely. While in-flight, the aircraft was struck by lightning twice which took no part in the PAN PAN declaration and did not affect the aircraft systems or performance.

C-GEHM, a Piper PA28-180 registered to Millennium Aviation Ltd., was conducting a VFR flight from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, to North Battleford Airport (CYQW), SK. Weather conditions enroute were reported to be conducive to carburetor icing and the carburetor heat function had been used during the flight. At 23:17Z and approximately 21 nautical miles west-northwest of CYXE, while enroute to CYQW, C-GEHM experienced a loss of engine power. The carburetor heat function was reported to not have any effect on the loss of power. The pilot declared an emergency and proceeded to land on a road. During the landing roll, the aircraft drifted into the snow filled ditch. There were no injuries. There was no fire but the aircraft sustained substantial damage.A post-occurrence inspection of the aircraft by the operator revealed the fuel selector was selected to the left tank and an inspection of the left tank indicated that there was no fuel.

C-GKIX, un Pilatus PC-12/45 exploité par Keewatin Air Lp effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport d'Iqaluit (CYFB), NU à destination de l'aéroport de Artic Bay (CYAB), NU avec 2 pilotes et un passager à bord. En croisière au niveau de vol 260 à environ 310 miles nautiques au nord-ouest de CYFB, les voyants d'alerte principal et de pression cabine se sont allumés. L'équipage a confirmé que la pression différentielle de la cabine descendait et que l'altitude cabine approchait 10000 pieds. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et effectué une descente d'urgence jusqu'au niveau de vol 100 tout en rebroussant chemin vers CYFB. Une évaluation médicale sommaire des occupants n'a révélé aucune blessure et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre à CYFB. La bride de serrage du tuyau de sortie du séparateur d'eau a été trouvée déserrée et le tuyau déconnecté créant une fuite majeure d'air compressé. Le tuyau a été reconnecté, la bride serrée et le reste du système a été inspecté et testé selon le manuel de maintenance du fabricant. L'appareil a été remis en service.

C-GKLB, un ATR 42-300 exploité par Canadian North sous l'indicatif AKT814 était en attente au sol pour un vol de l'aéroport d'Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) vers l'aéroport de Clyde River, NU (CYCY). Alors que l'aéronef était à l'écart de la voie de circulation GOLF, l'équipage a fait la demande pour un départ VFR depuis la piste 34. Immédiatement après avoir approuvé la demande, le service de circulation aérienne a avisé AKT814 de l'approche d'un Boeing 737 à 6 miles et 3 minutes de temps de vol pour la piste 34 au lieu de la piste 16. AKT814 à été demandé d'exécuter un virage à droite immédiatement après le décollage. AKT814 a procédé et effectué ce virage avant de se diriger vers sa destination. C-GVZB, le Boeing 737-800 en approche pour la piste 16 était exploité par Chrono Jet Inc. sous l'indicatif MBK900 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG). L'équipage de MBK900 a reçu une alerte de trafic du système d'avertissement de trafic et d'évitement d'abordage (TCAS) avec le trafic en visuel à moins de 1 mile nautique. MBK900 a continué et procédé à l'atterrissage piste 16. Nav Canada revoit présentement l'évènement.

C-FYXF, an Airbus A321, operating as Air Canada Rouge flight ROU1505 from Greater Moncton Romeo Leblanc International Airport (CYQM), NB, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the cruise phase of flight, a Flight Attendant sustained an injury and was unable to continue safety related duties. The duties were redistributed among the cabin crew in accordance with company policies and procedures. The flight was completed without further incident.

C-FXCA, an Air Canada B767-300 was operating flight AC7220 from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (KATL), GA, to Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport (TJSJ), Puerto Rico. On final, the flight crew detected an odour and smoke appeared in the cockpit. The smoke began to intensify, and the flight crew immediately donned their oxygen masks and turned off the packs. A MAYDAY was declared and the flight landed without further incident. Emergency vehicles met aircraft on arrival, and flight crew was taken to the hospital. Maintenance initial finding identified a broken hydraulic line in the electronic bay.

S2-AJY, a Biman Bangladesh Airlines Boeing 787-9 operating as flight BBC305, landed at Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, and requested aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) due to hot brakes after landing. The flight crew waited for the aircraft brakes to cool down before taxiing to the gate. ARFF followed the aircraft during the taxi to the gate without further incident.

C-FYJH, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319 was operating flight ROU1827, from Queen Beatrix International Airport (TNCA), Aruba, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While in cruise, just prior to the top of descent when intermittent self-clearing ENG2 THR LEVER DISAGREE ECAM messages were received by the flight crew. During descent through approximately FL220 in the vicinity of WOZEE the ECAM message appeared again and remained. ECAM actions were carried out which did not resolve the ECAM message, aircraft handling and throttle response was normal. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN as a precaution and the flight landed without incident. Aircraft rescue and firefighting were on standby but did not identify any abnormalities and the flight taxied to its assigned gate without further incident.

C-FGDZ, un Boeing 787-9 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA8XC effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC à destination de l'aéroport Lester B. Pearson de Toronto (CYYZ), ON. CN-RGT, un Boeing 787-8 exploité par Royal Air Maroc sous l'indicatif RAM209M, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Casablanca/Mohammed V, Maroc (GMMN) à destination de CYUL. Alors que C-FGDZ était en montée vers son altitude croisière au départ de la piste 06R à CYUL, CN-RGT était en approche pour atterrir sur la piste 06L. À environ 5nm au nord-ouest de CYUL, l'espacement entre les 2 appareils a été réduit à 1.3 MN horizontalement et 700 pieds verticalement alors que les minimums sont respectivement de 3 MN et 1000 pieds. Les 2 appareils ont poursuivi leur vol sans encombre.

C-GCLQ, un Beech King Air B200 exploité par Sky Jet M.G. Inc effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Trois-Rivières, QC (CYRQ) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec 2 membres d'équipage. En descente vers CYQB, à une altitude de 4000 pieds, le voyant principal d'alarme (Master Warning) s'est déclenché indiquant un feu sur le moteur gauche. Une vérification visuelle du moteur et des paramètres n'a rien révélé d'anormal. Quelques minutes suite à ces vérifications, le moteur en question a subi une perte de puissance avec une flamme visible à la sortie d'échappement. La procédure d'urgence a été effectuée et le moteur a été sécurisé. Une urgence a été déclarée et une approche vers une piste plus longue a été effectuée. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre sur la piste 24. Des vérifications ont été faites sur le moteur et le système de carburant. Rien qui aurait pu causer la situation n'a été découvert. L'exploitant est en communication avec le fabricant du moteur et Transport Canada. Le fabricant du moteur suspecte un décrochage du compresseur. Le moteur a été testé et déterminé comme fonctionnant dans les paramètres prescrits. L'appareil a été remis en service sans anomalies depuis.

C-GULM, a privately operated Piper PA 31 350 aircraft, was conducting an IFR flight from Rimouski Aerodrome (CYXK), QC, to Wabush Airport (CYWK), NL. While in cruise about 45 nm south of CYWK the pilot noticed that number 2 engine manifold pressure was indicating a 3 to 4 in Hg fluctuation. The pilot noted that all engine temperature and pressure parameters were normal, however the number 2 engine fuel flow indication varied in correlation with the manifold pressure fluctuations. The pilot continued to monitor engine parameters and carried out the ROUGH RUNNING ENGINE procedure which provided no improvement. As the flight neared the initial approach fix the manifold pressure fluctuation increased, however the pilot kept the engine running as it was still producing some power. When on the final approach for runway 36 at CYWK, the number 2 engine began losing all power and the pilot carried out the engine shutdown procedure and declared a PAN PAN for landing priority. The aircraft landed at CYWK without further incident.Maintenance personnel replaced the engine-driven fuel pump on the number 2 engine.

C-GJZS, a Jazz CRJ900 was operating flight JZA783 from Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (KDCA), VA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During taxi for take-off, smoke was coming from the oven, passengers were deplaned on the taxiway ALPHA. Aircraft rescue and firefighting was called for assistance, and the passengers were bussed back to the gate. No injuries and no adverse reactions reported.

C-FFLZ, a Flair Airlines Limited Boeing 737-800 departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, on a flight, under instrument flight rules, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. C-GMJJ, a Central Mountain Air Limited DeHavilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-102 departed Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, on a flight, under instrument flight rules, to CYVR. A loss of separation occurred when the Boeing aircraft departed CYVR and the DeHavilland was on approach. At the closest point, the aircraft were separated 2.9 miles laterally at the same altitude. The requirement is 3 miles laterally or 1000 feet vertically.

C-FRSE, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight ACA812 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Humber Delgado Airport (LPPT), Portugal. During cruise, a crew member was unable to continue their duties, and these duties were reassigned to the other cabin crew members.

C-GFAJ, an Air Canada A330 was operating flight ACA841 from Frankfurt Airport (EDDF), Germany, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the flight, the flight crew was advised of a cabin crew injury. The cabin crew member's duties were reassigned to remaining cabin crew.

C-GEOJ, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight ACA1317 from Cancún International Airport (MMUN), MX, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, the flight crew was advised of a cabin crew illness. Cabin crew member was unable to continue duties, and the flight continued without further incident.

C-GURP, a WestJet Airlines B789 was operating flight WS19 from Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Approximately 30 minutes into flight, the aircraft passed the wake turbulence from a Boeing 747 and a cabin crew member was injured. Duties were reassigned among remaining crew members and a deadheading cabin crew member was activated to sit in jumpseat for landing. Aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FFQF, a Conair Group Inc. Dehavilland DHC-8-402 was operating from Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, to Oakland International Airport (KOAK), CA, US. The aircraft was equipped with a TC-approved ferry fuel system composed of eight fuel bladders and systems necessary to supplement on-board fuel for a series of trans-Pacific flights to Australia. While enroute to KOAK, the aircraft mechanics travelling on board detected an increased odour of jet fuel. They found that refueling ventilation valves on two of the fuel bladders had been left open. The fuel vents were closed and the ferry system was energized in an attempt to draw the fuel remaining in the vent lines back into the fuel system. The flight crew were advised and they notified the destination FBO of the possibility of some fuel leaking after shutdown and requested assistance in dealing with a spill.Upon arrival, jet fuel began to drain from the aft fuselage drain vent. The fuel was contained using spill management media. The estimated fuel quantity lost was 30 US gallons.

7T-VJV, un Airbus A330-200 exploité par Air Nigeria sous l'indicatif DAH2700 et C-FEKD, un embraer 170-200 exploité par Jazz sous l'indicatif JZA858 effectuaient leur vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, tous les deux à destination de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL). DAH2700 était en rapprochement pour l'approche de la piste 24G et JZA858 était en rapprochement pour l'approche de la piste 24D. Des vents forts ont contribué à une perte d'espacement entre les deux aéronefs qui ce sont rapprochés a 2.5 milles nautiques l'un de l'autre alors que l'espacement prescrit est de 3 milles nautiques. L'ATC a pris rapidement des actions afin de rétablir la séparation. Les 2 aéronefs ont atterri sans encombre.

C-GNLN, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Nolinor sous l'indicatif NRL950, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Montréal - Mirabel, QC (CYMX) à destination de l'aéroport de Val d'Or, QC (CYVO). Après avoir reçu et relu correctement l'autorisation de descendre au niveau de vol 150, NRL950 a été observé en descente au travers le niveau 150. Une perte de séparation est alors survenue avec C-GIAB, un DHC-8-300 exploité par Air Inuit en tant que vol AIE863 qui était au niveau de vol 140 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl - Montreal, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport Amos/Magny, QC (CYEY). La distance de séparation a été réduite à 4.6 NM alors que le minimum prescrit est de 5 NM.

C-FRQK, a Jazz Aviation Embraer ERJ 170-200 was operating from LaGuardia Airport (KLGA), NY, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Upon selecting gear up, the crew received a Landing Gear Unsafe message. Crew ran checklists and decided to declare a PAN PAN and requested to return to KLGA. Aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GPDB, a Sunwest Aviation Ltd. Learjet 45, operating as flight CNK678 departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, en route to Whitecourt Airport (CYZU), Alberta. Shortly after takeoff, at approximately 0805 MST, the flight crew of CNK678 declared a PAN PAN emergency due to a pressurization issue. The flight crew elected to return to CYYC. The aircraft landed safety at 0820. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft.

C-GCRD, a privately registered Murphy SR2500 (Super Rebel) departed Powell River Airport (CYPW), BC, on a local recreational flight under visual flight rules with only the pilot on board. After departing CYPW, the aircraft took part in a flypast related to Remembrance Day ceremonies. In order to increase drag during the flypast, the pilot extended the landing gear of the aircraft's amphibious floats. After the flypast, the pilot proceeded to perform a water landing near a private dock approximately 16.5 nautical miles north of CYPW. During landing, the extended landing gear caused the aircraft to nose over, and the aircraft propeller struck the water. The pilot was able to egress the aircraft and swim to shore. The aircraft sustained damage and subsequently sunk. There was no ELT activation. The pilot was located by a search and rescue helicopter approximately 2 hours after being reported overdue, and approximately 8 hours 45 minutes after the occurrence.The aircraft was subsequently recovered from the water and is undergoing repairs.

VT-AEO, a Boeing 777-300ER aircraft operated by Air India, was conducting flight AIC191 from Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (VABB), Mumbai, India, to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), US. The aircraft diverted to Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL, due to a fuel shortage. No emergency was declared. The aircraft refueled and departed about 1.5 hours later.

N180DN, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL125 from General Humberto Delgado Airport (LPPT), Lisbon, Portugal, to Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS), MA, US. N12006, a Boeing 787-10 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL65 from LPPT to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, US. During cruise, around the BOBTU waypoint, there was a loss of separation between the aircraft. The required separation is 30 NM on either side of the track or 10 minutes longitudinal. The aircraft came 8NM inside the 30 NM protected airspace.

C-GAZI, a Cargojet Airways Limited Boeing 767-338 departed John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, on flight CJT2387, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew members and 1 jumpseater on board. During the descent into CYVR, the crew received a slat asymmetry warning. The crew leveled off, notified air traffic control, and declared a PAN PAN. The crew then completed the applicable checklist and prepared for a faster than normal approach and landing speed due to the slat issue. CYVR aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) crews were placed on standby. After touching down, the crew applied the brakes and pulled the thrust reverse handles however, neither engaged. The aircraft continued along Runway 08L, and departed the runway end at approximately 120kts. The aircraft collided with numerous approach lights and sunk into the soft muddy ground. The airplane came to a stop approximately 1250 feet past the end of the paved surface. The crew declared a MAYDAY and completed the shutdown checklist. The crew and jumpseater egressed with the assistance of ARFF personnel. There were no injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The aircraft was recovered from the muddy ground 2 days later. An aircraft damage assessment is ongoing by the operator. CYVR has repaired the lighting system.

C-FFGZ, an Air Canada Airbus 321-211, was conducting flight AC279 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Erik Nielsen Whitehorse International Airport (CYXY), YT, when a cabin crew member was injured and unable perform their duties. These duties were reassigned to the remaining cabin crew members. The aircraft returned to CYVR due to weather at destination.

C-FTJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP Bombardier CRJ900 was on a flight from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency due to a landing gear indication problem. The flight crew requested that aircraft rescue and firefighting personnel be placed on standby. The aircraft landed on Runway 30 without incident.

C-GLJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP Bombardier CRJ 900, was operating as JZA110 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, when approximately 1 hour into the flight, the flight attendants advised the pilots of a burning smell in the cabin. The First Officer entered the cabin to verify the smell as there was no indications in the cockpit. Once the smell was verified the flight crew declared a Pan Pan emergency. Given the location of the flight, it was decided to continue to CYOW.

C-FASR, a Cessna 525A operated by AirSprint Inc., was conducting flight ASP524 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. During the descent into CYWG, the flight crew reduced the engine power; however, the right engine (Williams International FJ44-3A) N1 would not reduce and no other abnormal indications were identified by the flight crew. ASP524 notified ATC, requested a hold, and contacted the operator's maintenance. The flight crew were unable to rectify the issue and planned their arrival at CYWG. As the aircraft descended, the split between the two engines' N1 values reduced allowing for normal aircraft handling. When the aircraft was on approach, the flight crew noticed a slight fluctuation in the right N1 and, upon landing, the right engine failed. The flight crew requested aircraft rescue and firefighting and taxied to the ramp. The flight crew and passengers exited the aircraft at the apron. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft.The operator's maintenance downloaded the FADEC data for troubleshooting. The Fuel Delivery Control Unit was replaced and the aircraft subsequently completed a successful test flight.

VT-ALO, an Air India Boeing 777-337 departed Indira Gandhi International Airport (VIDP), New Delhi, India, on flight AIC185 under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, approximately 1 hour northwest of CYVR, the crew received a “FIRE CARGO AFT” warning through the engine-indicating and crew-alerting system (EICAS). They completed the required checklist, contacted their company, and determined the nearest suitable airport was their planned destination, CYVR. They declared a MAYDAY and expedited a direct route to CYVR. Shortly after, the cargo fire warning message ceased and the crew cancelled the MAYDAY and declared a PAN PAN with air traffic control. The aircraft landed, taxied clear of the runway, and was inspected by aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) personnel. With no indication of fire, the aircraft was taxied to the gate under its own power. After all the passengers and crew had deplaned, ARFF personnel opened and inspected the cargo holds. There was no evidence of smoke or fire found. There were no injuries and the aircraft was not damaged.Maintenance completed their inspection and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FNAS, an AirSprint Incorporated Cessna 525B (CitationJet CJ3) was on the ramp at Smithers Airport (CYYD), BC. During the start of the No. 1 engine (Williams FJ44-3A), it was noted that the engine’s acceleration was abnormal and that there were indications of a hung start. The crew aborted the start and exited the aircraft. It was reported that there were flames coming from the engine’s tail pipe during the aborted start sequence. The flight crew advised company maintenance and the aircraft was grounded pending an inspection. There were no injuries. The aircraft had minor damage.It was determined that there was heat damage to the left side of the empennage and the tail cone area. The aircraft will be disassembled and sent for repair.

C-GEPF, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 was operating as ACA 464 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. On approach to Rwy 07 into CYOW, the flight crew was required to deviate for isolated thunderstorm cells. The isolated cells joined, preventing the flight crew from commencing the final approach. During a second approach, the aircraft suffered a possible lightning strike, which affected VHF number 1 radio for a short period of time. The flight crew elected to conduct a missed approach, in radio contact with YOW Tower and terminal, declared a PAN PAN emergency and diverted to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC.

LN-RKS, an Airbus A330-300 aircraft operated by Scandinavian Airlines, was conducting flight SAS957 from Stockholm Arlanda Airport (ESSA), Sweden, to Miami International Airport (KMIA), US. During cruise, the flight experienced turbulence while in Reykjavik’s airspace that caused the indication of ENG 1 Low Oil Pressure. The crew shut down the left engine as per the quick reference handbook and started a descent. The crew was able to restart the engine at around FL280 and proceeded to climb back to a cruise altitude of FL360. Once in Gander’s airspace, the crew declared an emergency and requested to turn back and landed at Copenhagen Airport (EKCH), Denmark, without further incident.

C-FZUG un Airbus A319-114 exploité par Air Canada Rouge, effectuait le vol ROU1977 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport Jean Lesage Intl de Québec, QC (CYQB) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 5 membres d'équipage et 113 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée, alors que l'aéronef se trouvait à environ 19NM de CYQB, l'équipage a reçu un message ECAM "ENG2 BLEED FAULT" (dysfonction de la soupape de prélèvement d'air #2). La montée a été arrêtée à 15000 pi. et les services de contrôle de la circulation aérienne ont été avisé de la situation. Des tentatives de rectifier la situation furent faites sans succès. L'aéronef ne pouvant se pressuriser, est redescendu à 8000 pi. Une urgence a été déclaré et l'aéronef a continué vers sa destination où il a atterri sans encombre. À noter que la soupape de prélèvement d'air #1 était déjà hors-service et l'anomalie différée d'après la liste d'équipement minimum (MEL). Une inspection après-vol a révélé la défaillance de la valve de surpression du moteur no.2.

N661UA, un Boeing 767-300ER exploité par United Airlines, effectuait le vol UA909 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport O'Hare Intl, Chicago, IL (KORD) à destination de l'aéroport Schiphol, Amsterdam, NL (EHAM) avec 8 membres d'équipage et 149 passagers à bord. Alors que l'aéronef se trouvait à 95 NM au nord de Montréal, QC, l'équipage a reçu un message EICAS "C HYD QTY" (Central Hydraulic Quantity). L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et a, de concert avec le personnel de répartition des vols, élu de retourner à KORD où l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre.Une inspection après-vol a révélé une fuite de fluide hydraulique au niveau du système des volets.

C-GOXD, un Bombardier CL3500 exploité par Bombardier Inc, effectuait un vol d'essai local selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Un problème avec les volets est survenu pendant une manœuvre en vol. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence au centre de contrôle aérien et demandé un retour à CYUL. L’aéronef est revenu atterrir sans encombre.

C-GUTA, a Top Aces, Dornier - Alpha Jet Model A, was on final approach into Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, when the pilot received a Master Caution for a HYD 1 failure. The pilot actuated the emergency landing gear extension system and declared a PAN PAN emergency with ATC. The pilot conducted a low approach to enable Ottawa Tower to confirm that the gear appeared down. Upon confirmation that the gear appeared down, the pilot landed in CYOW and taxied back to the ramp without further incident. The aircraft was removed from service to determine the cause of the issue. Maintenance was able to determine that the HYD 1 transducer had failed and thus causing the issue.

C-FPAL, un DeHavilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 exploité par Pal Airlines Ltd, effectuait le vol PVL3061 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport Jean Lesage Intl de Québec, QC (CYQB) à destination de l'aéroport de Bagotville ,QC (CYBG) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 52 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, l'équipage a senti une odeur de fumée et été avisé du déclenchement du détecteur de fumée du compartiment toilette. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et décidé de revenir à CYQB où l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre. Une inspection de l'équipe de maintenance a révélé la présence d'huile dans le système de climatisation.

C-GQXD, a Piper PA-31-350 operated by 2080061 Ontario Inc. (dba SkyCare Air Ambulance), was conducting flight PHX2063 from Kenora Airport (CYQK), ON, to Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON. During the descent into CYXL, the flight crew experienced a loss of aileron control. The flight crew used rudder and differential power to conduct a flapless landing. The aircraft landed safely and did not require assistance.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and found the right aileron control cable had completely failed at F.S. 58.5, where the cable is redirected 90 degrees by a pulley from the vertically positioned aileron interconnect chain. The aileron cable was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) was filed with Transport Canada. The operator conducted a fleetwide campaign to inspect the other PA-31-350s for the same fault, but none were found.

C-GHQZ, a De Havilland DHC-8-314 operated by Wasaya Airways LP, was conducting an IFR flight from Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON, to Big Trout Lake Airport (CYTL), ON. While in cruise at FL230, the Cabin Pressure High annunciator illuminated. The flight crew verified the cabin pressure gauge, which indicated 15 000 feet. The crew initiated the associated memory items, donned oxygen masks, and conducted an emergency descent. The crew decided to divert to Pickle Lake Airport (CYPL), ON, where an uneventful landing was completed. There were no injuries.The pressurization system was deferred per the aircraft's MEL for further flights.

C-FWEP, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3205 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Grande Prairie Airport (CYQU), AB. During cruise the flight crew observed a 'Flap Power' caution light. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook, declared a Pan Pan and returned to CYYC. The aircraft conducted a flapless landing without incident and taxied to the gate under its own power. Following the flight company maintenance replaced the Flap Control Unit and the left hand flap transducer. The aircraft flaps were tested, and no further defects were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJTV, an Air Canada Boeing 737 Max 8 departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, on flight AC545 under instrument flight rules, to Ellison Onizuka Kona International Airport (PHKO), HI, U.S. After takeoff, a flight attendant experienced a medical issue and was unable to continue their duties. The flight continued to its destination without further incident.

C-GOFW, an Air Canada A330-343 was operating flight AC877 from Lyon-Saint Exupéry Airport (LFLL), France, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During the cruise phase of the flight, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue duties. No medical attention was required and the flight continued to CYUL without further incident.

C-GFUR, an Air Canada A330 was operating flight AC873 from Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, a flight attendant sustained a personal injury and was unable to continue duties. The flight was completed without further incident.

C-FLQY, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 operated by Porter Airlines Inc., was conducting flight PD2639 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Thunder Bay Int'l Airport (CYQT), ON.
