Shortly before reaching cruising altitude of FL220, the CABIN PRESS warning light illuminated. The flight crew began an emergency descent and declared PAN PAN. While actioning the checklist, the flight crew realized that the bleed switches had not been selected ON during the after-takeoff checks. They selected the bleed switches ON and the aircraft began to pressurize normally. The crew elected to return to CYTZ for operational reasons and landed uneventfully.

C-GLQO, a Porter Airlines Dash 8-402, was conducting ferry flight PTR9813 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Int'l Airport (CYOW), ON, to St. Thomas Municipal Airport (CYQS), ON. After departure from CYOW, when the landing gear was selected up, the Main Landing Gear Door lights remained illuminated. The crew coordinated with dispatch and maintenance, and elected to continue the flight to CYQS, declaring PAN PAN as a precaution. The crew used the alternate gear extension procedure before landing uneventfully at CYQS, and they were towed to the hangar. It was discovered that the main landing gear door pins had not been removed before the flight.

C-FYNS, an Air Canada Airbus A319-114, operating as ACA619 enroute from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, reported low hydraulic pressure and a failed hydraulic system. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency and requested landing on Runway 23 at CYYZ. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GMMN, a private Cessna 182 overturned while landing in a private field at approximately 24 nm SW of London International Airport (CYXU), ON. There were 4 souls on board, 3 of which were taken to the hospital as a precaution. Emergency services were on site. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GAGL, a private Maule M-7-235C, on a local flight out of Edenvale, ON (CNV8), ground-looped on landing, departed the runway off to the left approximately 1000 feet past the threshold. The aircraft came to rest approximately 150 feet left of the Runway 31 centerline and suffered extensive damage. There were no injuries amongst the 2 souls on board.

C-GBHZ, an Air Canada Rouge A319, was conducting flight ROU1715 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Int'l Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Nashville Int'l Airport (KBNA), TN, USA. During the initial climb, the flight crew received an "ELEC GEN2 FAULT" ECAM message. After actioning the appropriate checklists which included an unsuccessful attempt to reset the generator, the crew started the APU, declared PAN PAN, and requested a return to CYYZ, where they landed uneventfully.

C-GFSA, an ATR 72-202 operated by Summit Air Ltd as flight BF7514, was conducting an IFR flight from Naujaat (CYUT), NU to Thompson (CYTH), MB with 2 flight crew members on board. While in cruise at FL240 and approximately 28 nautical miles south of Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU, the captain's windscreen cracked. The flight crew actioned the QRH, declared a PAN PAN, and made a descent to 10 000 feet ASL. There was no loss of pressurization and the aircraft continued to CYTH for an uneventful landing.

C-FYIY, an Airbus A319 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA163 from Toronto/Pearson Int'l Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Edmonton Int'l Airport (CYEG), AB. During the initial climb, the flight crew were advised by cabin crew that there was a strong odor in the cabin. After consulding with dispatch and maintenance, the decision was made to return to CYYZ. The flight crew declared PAN PAN and requested to return to CYYZ, where the flight landed and taxied to their gate. Maintenance conducted a thorough inspection but was unable to find the source of the odor, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GEEN, a WestJet Encore Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Dash 8 Q400 was scheduled to depart Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, on flight WEN3227, under instrument flight rules to Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC. During taxi for departure, the takeoff warning horn test indicated that the aircraft was not correctly configured for takeoff. The crew double checked the aircraft configuration and determined the aircraft was configured properly. Maintenance personnel were advised, and the flight crew were directed to perform a ground reset, after which the system tested normally and the flight continued.During the takeoff roll on Runway 08R, as the aircraft accelerated through approximately 70 knots, the take-off warning horn sounded again. The crew rejected the takeoff and declared a MAYDAY with air traffic control. After the aircraft was brought to a stop, the MAYDAY was cancelled, and the aircraft returned to the gate without further issue. The aircraft was removed from service, and flight WEN3227 continued after changing the aircraft.A maintenance inspection of the occurrence aircraft found the elevator trim indicator out of range. The elevator trim control system was replaced and the aircraft was subsequently returned to service.

C-GMBT, a Pilatus PC-24 aircraft operated by Keewatin Air LP, was operating an IFR flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Lynn Lake Aerodrome (CYYL), MB. Prior to the approach to CYYL, the flight crew received the latest automated weather report indicating the winds were 210° at 6 knots in VMC conditions. The flight crew calculated a landing distance with Flaps 15 at 3136 feet and conducted an approach to Runway 17. On final approach, the runway was observed as clear with some snow skiffs. The aircraft touched down in the touchdown zone, the lift dump devices were deployed, and brakes were were applied. It was noticed that there was limited braking action due to the runway being slippery and the flight crews deployed the flaps to 33 degrees. The aircraft slowed down, but overran the end of the 5004 foot runway at a speed of less than 10 knots, into a grassy area. The flight crew then taxied back onto the runway and to the apron, and then advised the operator of what had occurred. There were no injuries.The operator's maintenance was sent to CYYL and inspected the aircraft. No damage was identified and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOCR, a Synergy Aviation Ltd. operated Robinson R44 II, was conducting a survey 10 nm south-southwest of Rainbow Lake Aerodrome (CYOP), AB. During the survey the pilot observed the low rotor RPM horn, and confirmed that the RPM had lowered to approximately 95%. The pilot lowered the collective, but the rotor rpm continued to decrease. The pilot performed a power-on forced approach to a nearby service road. The pilot conducted a run-on landing on the service road, there were no injuries, and the helicopter was not damaged during the landing. Once on the ground the engine continued to run at idle and the pilot was unable to increase the throttle setting.Company maintenance crews were dispatched to the site and determined that a loose FCU arm nut had allowed the arm to over-rotate, restricting throttle movement. The arm nut was missing a cotter pin post overhaul allowing the nut to loosen.

C-FWZV, a Dehavilland DHC-7-103, operated by Air Tindi Ltd., was conducting flight TIN802 from Bathurst Inlet (CJN6), NU, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. During cruise the flight crew observed oil pressure fluctuations on the #2 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-50). The flight crew ran the appropriate checklist and performed a precautionary shutdown of the #2 engine. The flight continued to CYZF, and an uneventful 3 engine approach and landing was completed.Company maintenance investigated the cause of the fluctuating engine oil pressure indication and found that the oil filler cap on the #2 engine was loose.

N816AA, an American Airlines B787-8 was conducting flight AAL742 from Philadelphia International Airport (KPHL), PA, to Barcelona El Prat International Airport (LEBL), Spain. Approximately 1 hour in the flight, the crew declared a medical emergency due to the first officer expressing discomfort. Medlink was consulted and a physician onboard attended to the first officer. The relief pilot assumed the duties of the first officer for the remainder of the flight. The flight crew discussed the situation with company operations center and determined that returning to KPHL was the best course of action due to the minimum crew requirements. Gander ACC was notified about the situation, and they subsequently provided a direct routing to KPHL.

C-GBIN, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1711 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (KMSY), LA. During the initial approach, in the vicinity of RAYOP, at approximately 3000 feet ASL, the flight crew selected FLAP 2 in accordance with company policy and procedure. F/CTL FLAP LOCK ECAM was subsequently received. The approach was discontinued, ECAM actions carried out and PAN PAN was declared as a precaution. The aircraft returned to KMSY and carried out a zero-flap landing on RWY 11 without further incident. The aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.

C-GRUU, a Carson Air Limited Raytheon B300 departed the Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, on a flight to the Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, under instrument flight rules with 2 crew members and 2 passengers on board. After takeoff from CYVR, the crew, after selecting landing gear up, were unable to get a gear up and locked indication. The crew conducted a visual inspection and determined the gear was retracted. They continued the flight to CYLW at a safe gear extended speed. Once nearing CYLW the crew began to troubleshoot the issue and after cycling the gear, they received a 3 gear green down and locked indication. The crew communicated their gear issues to the CYLW control tower who placed aircraft rescue and firefighting assets on standby. The flight landed without incident. After inspecting the aircraft and cleaning the landing gear switches, company maintenance was unable to recreate a fault in the system. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GLBR, un Piper PA-31 exploité par le Collège d'enseignement général et professionnel de Chicoutimi était sur un vol de formation entre Jean-Lesage Intl - Québec, Qc (CYQB) et St-Honoré/Chicoutimi, Qc (CYRC) avec 2 élèves-pilotes et un instructeur à bord. Alors que l'aéronef atteignait 6000 pieds, en monté vers 7000 pieds, une vibration semblant provenir du moteur gauche a été ressenti par l'équipage. À 7000 pieds, le moteur a subitement cessé de produire de la puissance. L'instructeur a repris le contrôle de l'aéronef et a procédé selon la liste de vérification applicable avec l'élève-pilote. Le moteur de gauche a été arrêté par mesure préventive, une urgence a été déclarée et la décision de revenir à CYQB a été prise. L'appareil c'est posé sans encombre sur la piste 29 à CYQB. Un désassemblage du moteur défectueux a révélé une fracture du vilbrequin au niveau du cylindre #1.

C-FEXE, a Cessna 208B (Grand Caravan), operated by Morningstar Air Express Incorporated, was conducting flight MAL8072 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. When approximately 15 nautical miles south of CYVR, during cruise at 4000 feet ASL, the aircraft's autopilot failed. The pilot requested vectors to return to CYVR and declared a PAN PAN urgency. The aircraft landed without further incident while aircraft rescue and firefighting personnel were on standby.The aircraft was sent to company maintenance for repairs.

C-FIBW, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-700, was operating as flight WJA160 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. C-GGMU, a Jazz Aviation LLC Bombardier Inc DHC-8-402, was operating as flight JZA128 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to CYEG. Instrument meteorological conditions existed as both aircraft were on approach into CYEG. Spacing was reduced to 2.8 NM when 3.0 NM is required. Tower instructed C-GGMU to pull up and go around. There were no further issues and both aircraft landed safely.

C-GPTW, a Cessna 172M registered to the Smiths Falls Flying Club, was conducting night circuits on runway 24 at Smiths Falls-Montague Airport (CYSH), ON, with one pilot as the sole occupant. During the third circuit, just after turning onto the base leg for runway 24, the engine failed. The aircraft was not within gliding range of the runway, and the pilot was forced to land in a rough field approximately 650 feet short of the threshold of runway 24. Shortly after touching down in the field, the aircraft overturned. The pilot was uninjured and managed to get out of the aircraft unassisted.

C-FLTS, un appareil de type Beech King Air A100 exploité par Exact Air, effectuait le vol ET823 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYEY) à destination de l'aéroport de Port-Meunier, QC (CYPN) avec 2 pilotes à bord. Alors que l'aéronef était en croisière à 13 000 pieds ASL, la pression d'huile du moteur droit indiquait le minimum. La pression est ensuite redevenue normale avant de chuter sous le seuil minimum de 40 PSI.  L'équipage a effectué l'arrêt du moteur (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-28) de droit par mesure de précaution. Une urgence a été déclarée avec le service de circulation aérienne et un déroutement a été effectué vers l'aéroport de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC) où l'aéronef est atterri sans encombre.Le personnel d'entretien de l'exploitant a effectué des vérifications et le niveau d'huile a été trouvé bas. Le système d'indication était fonctionnel et il n'y a pas eu de fuites ou de contaminants détectés. De l'huile a été ajoutée et le moteur mis à l'essai avec succès.

C-GDCG, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Transwest Air Limited Partnership (dba Rise Air) was conducting a VFR repositioning flight from La Loche (CJL4) SK. to Buffalo Narrows (CYVT) SK. with two flight crew and no passengers. During the approach into CYVT, the left engine's (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-67D) indications were anomalous when the propeller speed was increased, which was followed by a loud bang. The crew performed a precautionary engine shutdown, continued the approach, and landed uneventfully at CYVT. The operator's maintenance examined the left engine which revealed fractured blades at both power turbine stages. There was no apparent damage to the gas generator section. The cowling and exhaust ducts were damaged from blade debris. The engine is being replaced.

C-GPNE, a PAL Airlines de Havilland DHC-8-402 was operating as PVL2267 from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ. The aircraft departed CYHZ Runway 23 and during the initial climb a passenger reported a left main gear wheel fire to cabin crew. The flight crew was alerted, who declared an emergency with ATC and coordinated a return to CYHZ where a landing was made on Runway 23 without incident. The aircraft made a full stop on runway and aircraft rescue and firefighting inspected the wheel area before the aircraft taxied back to the ramp. Maintenance personnel made repairs related to a left main gear inboard wheel bearing failure, including the replacement of left main landing gear components that received heat damage.

C-GMIW un Boeing 737 MAX 8 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA1147 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC, à destination de l’aéroport Lester B. Pearson de Toronto (CYYZ), ON. C-FSYX un Embraer Legacy 450 (EMB-545) exploité par Airsprint Inc. sous l'indicatif ASP844 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC, à destination de l’aéroport Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU). C-FSYX qui était en montée initiale et plus rapide que C-GMIW, se trouvait sur une trajectoire convergente à celui-ci. Alors que C-GMIW se trouvait à environ 5 miles nautiques à l'ouest de CYQB, l'espacement a été réduit à 2,1 miles nautiques latéralement et 800 pieds verticalement alors que les minimums étaient de 3 miles nautiques latéralement et 1000 pieds verticalement. L'espacement a été rétabli alors que C-FSYX a reçu l'instruction de maintenir 4000 pieds et que C-GMIW  passait 5000 pieds en poursuivant sa montée vers 13000 pieds.

C-GTZH, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300 was operating flight AC1162 from Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB, to Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. When the landing gear was selected up on departure from CYMM, the flight crew reported hearing a loud bang and observed a weight on wheels (WOW) and a 'gear fail' message. The crew actioned the quick reference handbook checklist and elected to divert to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, with the gear extended. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight landed without incident.Company maintenance found the nose gear oleo deflated, completed the associated repairs, tested the nose gear operation and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FNNH, an Air Canada B777-200 was operating flight AC43 from Indira Gandhi International Airport (VIDP), India, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During boarding, a flight attendant sustained a minor injury and was unable to continue with duties.

C-GUAC, an Air Canada A220-300 was operating flight AC730 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to LaGuardia Airport (KLGA), NY. During descent, the flight crew received an EICAS message “R Elevator Fail”. In discussion with ATC, the flight crew declared a Pan Pan and the flight landed without further incident.

C-GWJK, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-8-402 was being operated by WestJet Encore as flight WEN3371 from Saskatoon / John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, to the Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. WEN3371 was cleared for the RNAV Y RWY35L approach. Weather was clear, the winds were light out of the northeast and the approach was uneventful. The initial touchdown occurred during the hours of darkness at 2130 Mountain Daylight Time. During the initial touchdown the pitch attitude of the aircraft achieved 7° nose up and the aircraft became airborne. The attitude was lowered and a subsequent touchdown occurred 6 seconds later. A pitch attitude of 7° was attained by the time the main landing gear contacted the runway a second time. The flight data recorder recorded a 2.17g vertical acceleration force on the second touchdown. The flight crew observed a TOUCHED RUNWAY advisory light. The aircraft was taxied to the gate where the quick reference handbook was actioned and ATS was advised of the runway contact. There were no injuries to the crew or the passengers. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the lower side of the empennage. See TSB class 4 air safety investigation report A24W0038 for a similar occurrence.

C-FMVO, a privately registered Beech C35 aircraft, was conducting a visual flight rules (VFR) flight from Saskatoon/Banga Air Aerodrome (CJN5), SK, to Rocky Mountain House Aerodrome (CYRM), AB, with the pilot and one passenger on board. While on route, the pilot decided to do a touch-and-go landing at Biggar Aerodrome (CJF8), SK. On final approach, the pilot selected the landing gear down and noted that he had a down and locked indication. Prior to landing in gusty conditions, the pilot attempted to adjust the flaps selection; however, he mistakenly selected the landing gear up. The aircraft subsequently landed with the gear retracted and sustained damage to its propeller, lower fuselage and wings. There were no injuries. The runway was closed until the aircraft could be moved.

C-GJAN, a Jazz Aviation CRJ900 was operating flight JZA931 from Philadelphia International Airport (KPHL), PA, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. When leveling out at FL170, the crew got an elevator split caution message, a PAN PAN was declared and crew opted to return to KPHL. Aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-GMJS, a West Coast Helicopters Maintenance and Contracting Limited Bell 206L (LongRanger) was operating from a staging area approximately 4 nautical miles (NM) east of Scott Cove on Gilford Island, BC, in support of logging operations under visual flight rules. The pilot had dropped off 11 loggers at different helipads in a valley east of the staging area on the morning of the occurrence. A few hours after dropping them off, the pilot received a call from the logging crew leader requesting the fallers be picked up due to deteriorating weather conditions. The weather at the time of the accident was forecast to be broken clouds with ceilings of between 2000 and 4000 feet above sea level. The visibility was forecast to be from 3 to more than 6 statute miles in rain showers and mist, with patchy ceilings between 800 to 1500 feet above ground level. Weather on the south side of the valley was seen to be better than on the north. The pilot flew 2 round trips from the staging area to helipads on the north and the south sides of the valley, picked up 4 loggers, and returned them to the staging area. The occurrence flight was the third retrieval flight, from a pad on the north side of the valley. When the pilot landed on the pad and picked up 2 loggers, the weather had deteriorated. He backed the helicopter out of the pad and, using a line of old growth forest as a visual reference, descended into the valley. As the flight continued, visual reference was lost, the pilot inadvertently entered instrument meteorological conditions, and began having difficulties controlling the aircraft. The helicopter descended out of the clouds approximately 0.5 NM horizontally south of and approximately 800 feet lower than the helipad. The helicopter was about 10 feet above the treetops and in a steep left bank attitude. The pilot attempted to return to straight and level flight but the helicopter contacted the trees and control was lost. The aircraft rotated approximately 540° before coming to rest on the forest floor (50° 44' 22.74" N, 126° 17' 53.94" W) in a nose low attitude. All 3 occupants egressed and it was noted that a small fire had begun which extinguished itself as the pilot finished shutting down the helicopter. The pilot activated the alert button on the Spidertracks aircraft tracking system. A company helicopter was dispatched and landed on a logging road approximately 500 feet north of the crash site. The 3 occupants were able to walk out to be picked up. The pilot and 1 passenger suffered minor injuries and the remaining passenger was uninjured. The aircraft was substantially damaged.The aircraft was recovered and will be assessed for damage.

C-GPSQ un Pilatus PC-12 exploité par Chrono Aviation Inc. sous l'indicatif NDL765 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de New York/John F Kennedy (KJFK), NY à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Qc (CYUL). C-FJQL un Airbus A321 exploité par Air Canada Rouge sous l'indicatif ROU1637 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Orlando International, FL (KMCO) à destination de CYUL. Les 2 aéronefs volaient l'approche STAR CARTER CINQ, où il y a une restriction de vitesse au point SILDO de 210 KT et une restriction d’altitude de 4000’. Alors que ROU1637 rattrapait NDL765, le contrôleur a instruit NDL765 de virer à gauche sur un cap de 290 et ROU1637 de virer à droite sur un cap de 090. Lorsque le contrôleur a questionné ROU1637, l’équipage a avisé qu’ils étaient trop haut et n'ont pu réduire suffisamment la vitesse lors de la descente. L’espacement entre ROU1637 et NDL765 a été réduit à 2.7 NM alors que 3 NM est requis. Il n'y a pas eu de risque de collision.

C-GMSY, a Learjet 45 aircraft operated by Starlink Aviation Inc., was conducting flight TLK822 from Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL, to Keflavik International Airport (BIKF), Iceland. During cruise, the flight crew noticed N1, N2, ITT and fuel flow fluctuations on engine #2. The crew elected to return to CYYR, declared a PAN PAN and landed without further incident.The aircraft was ferried to a maintenance base where they continue to troubleshoot with the assistance of the manufacturer.

C-GTNZ, an amateur-built Murphy Yukon, was conducting a series of flights beginning and ending at Midland/Huronia Aerodrome (CYEE), ON. The pilot initially flew alone to Haliburton/Stanhope Municipal Aerodrome (CND4), ON, picked up a passenger, and proceeded to Orillia Rama Regional Aerodrome (CNJ4), ON. The passenger, a licensed pilot, was not operating the aircraft, however during cruise flight at 115 knots he reportedly applied alternating rudder inputs, causing considerable varying yaw to the left and right. The aircraft later experienced unexpected yaw during landing at CND4 but attributed it to wind. On a subsequent solo flight from CND4 to CYEE, the aircraft experienced unexpected left yaw, followed by violent rudder flutter. The pilot regained rudder control and safely landed at CYEE. A post-flight examination revealed that the fairing alongside the left side of the tail cone had pulled away from the fuselage. Upon removing the fairing, which covered the intersection of the fuselage and both the horizontal and vertical stabilizers, the pilot discovered that the forward and aft mounting structures for the vertical stabilizer had both failed, and the vertical stabilizer had remained attached to the aircraft only by the fairings. The rudder skin was creased at the location of the break in the rear vertical fin spar, indicating that it had bent significantly to the left during the occurrence.The vertical fin assembly from the occurrence aircraft was compared with the Murphy Aircraft SR2500 plans from which this aircraft was built, dated 2002. It was observed that there were discrepancies with the spar caps which act as doublers for the vertical stabilizer spar. The external spar cap was not installed while the internal spar cap was smaller than indicated in the plans. The aircraft had been inspected by a MD-RA inspector, both in 2007 during the pre-cover inspection, and in 2013 during the final inspection. The owner of the aircraft intends to repair the damage and add extra support to the assembly before returning the aircraft to service.

C-FCJZ, a Jazz CRJ 900 was operating flight JZA721 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Minneapolis–Saint Paul International Airport (KMSP), MN. During cruise, at FL360 the crew had a low-speed cue and high-speed cue message come on, on the captain's side. Due to these messages, the stick shaker engaged and the auto pilot disengaged. Also, the captain was unable to see speeds, however the speeds on the FO and standby displays appeared normal. On descent, the crew had the stall fail message illuminate. The crew declared a Pan Pan and actioned the quick reference handbook. The flight landed without further issue and there was no major passenger reaction.

C-GJUN un Piper PA-28R en exploitation privé effectuait un vol selon les règle de vol à vue depuis un aérodrome privé à Laval, QC (piste Contant) à destination de l'aéroport de Joliette, Qc (CSG3) avec 2 personnes à bord. Le Pilote a effectué ses rapports de position radio à l'entrée de zone, vent arrière, base et finale pour la piste 15. Lorsqu'établi en finale, le pilote a remarqué un appareil circulant en sens inverse au bout éloigné de la piste. Évaluant qu'il pouvait peut-être atterrir devant l'autre appareil qui allait sortir à la mi-piste, le pilote est descendu sous la pente  pour effectuer un atterrissage court. L'appareil est entré en collision avec des fils basse tension situés à environ 1300 pieds avant le seuil de la piste. Le premier impact avec le sol s'est produit à environ 450 pieds du seuil, les 3 parties du train d'atterrissage se sont brisées et l'appareil a terminé sa course à environ 150 pieds du seuil de la piste 15. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé, la radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée, mais il y avait déjà assistance sur les lieux.

C-FVLU, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC62 from Icheon International Airport (RKSI), South Korea, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. While in cruise, moderate turbulence was encountered, a cabin crew reported an injury, and they did not continue their duties.

C-FCNW, a WestJet B787-8CT was operating flight WJA1430 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), CA, U.S. While over Montana, a medical emergency was declared due to a flight crew incapacitation. A diversion to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, was requested. The flight landed without further incident.

C-FLKO, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 operated by Flair Airlines Ltd., was conducting flight FLE641 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Winnipeg/James A. Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. After departing runway 15L, and while climbing through approximately 4000 feet, the aircraft encountered a flock of geese, at least one of which hit the captain's L1 windscreen, causing it to shatter. Portions of the windshield glass entered the flight deck as a result. The flight crew declared PAN PAN and requested to return to CYYZ, where they landed without further incident. As the captain was unable to see forward through the windscreen, the crew requested to be towed to their gate. The captain received minor injuries due to the shattered glass entering the flight deck.

The Orthoshop Geomatics Ltd. Cessna T310P, C-GQHL, was operating on a local VFR flight from Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB. While conducting prelanding checks the flight crew lowered the main landing gear and the right main gear indication light did not illuminate down and locked. The light was checked serviceable. A low pass was requested for the tower to visually observe the gear position; tower confirmed the landing gear was down. Time to troubleshoot was requested by the flight crew and airspace was blocked overhead CYBW between 6000 and 6500 feet ASL. While troubleshooting, the landing gear was cycled several times without success. The flight crew requested to return to land and to have aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by. The aircraft landed on Runway 17 with no further issues and exited on Taxiway C. After turning to exit on Taxiway C, the flight crew heard a clunk and the main landing gear light illuminated. Company maintenance found the right main landing gear position switch to be dirty and loose. The switch was re-adjusted, and the aircraft was released for continued service.

C-FKJZ, a Jazz CRJ900 was operating flight JZA717 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Minneapolis–Saint Paul International Airport (KMSP), MN. During the cruise phase of flight, the crew got an ELEVATOR SPLIT caution message. A PAN PAN was declared and the crew elected to divert to Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD), IL. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GTXM, a Learjet 35A aircraft operated by Top Aces Inc., was conducting a flight from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, to Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. D-AXGF, an Airbus A330-203 aircraft operated by Discover Airlines, was conducting flight OCN74 from Frankfurt Airport (EDDF), Germany, to CYHZ. C-GTXM was sequenced behind D-AXGF on approach to Runway 05 at CYHZ and encountered a wake turbulence event when 6 NM behind the heavy airliner. The wake turbulence was encountered by C-GTXM at 3000 feet ASL while travelling at 170 KIAS and caused C-GTXM to enter an uncontrollable roll to the right and a sudden drop of altitude (right roll reached 45 degrees and C-GTXM lost between 100 to 200 feet of altitude). The crew of C-GTXM regained control and initiated a go-around. The aircraft landed on the second approach to Runway 05 at CYHZ without further incident.The wake turbulence event was reported to the TSB and air traffic services. The operator entered the event into their internal safety program and communicated the circumstances with all aircrew.

C-GFNK, an Aero Vodochody L-39C, operated by the International Test Pilot School (ITPS) as flight SA62, took off from London International Airport (CYXU), ON, in a 2 ship L-39C formation with C-GFNO to conduct a training exercise north of Centralia/James T. Field Memorial Aerodrome (CYCE), ON. After approximately 20 minutes of flight and 5 NM north of CYCE at an altitude of 15 000 ft, the engine RPM (N1) in C-GFNK dropped to 10%, whereas the throttle setting was at Max RPM position (106%). Engine instruments were checked but found no abnormality with EGT, Oil Pressure and physical thrust. With a suspected engine malfunction, an emergency was declared by the pilots of C-GFNO for C-GFNK with ATC. A priority landing at CYXU on Runway 33 was carried out without further incident.Maintenance determined the Tach Generator for N1 RPM had failed and was causing bad readings. The part was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FZXI, a Sunwing B737-8 was operating flight SWG4582 from Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), DR to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Shortly after take-off, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue duties. The incapacitated flight attendant occupied a passenger seat for the rest of the flight.

C-FHIA, a privately registered Sundance SBA90 hot air balloon, was conducting a recreational flight from the Hespero Aerodrome (CFB3), AB, with the pilot and one passenger onboard. During the approach to land the winds at 75 to 150 feet above ground level were approximately 13 knots. The winds at the surface were approximately 5 to 7 knots. During the landing sequence, the decent rate was observed to be high, so the pilot used both burners to add heat and slow the decent rate.  The decent rate didn't appear to change, and the balloon impacted terrain and bounced back into the air. To arrest the ascent, the pilot elected to dump the hot air out of the Balloon. The envelope deflated and the mouth closed so the pilot was not able to use the burners and add more heat. This significantly increased the decent rate of the balloon, and it impacted terrain. Both the pilot and passenger received serious injuries. The ground support crew were onsite immediately, and EMS was called to respond to the scene. Both the pilot and passenger were transported to hospital with serious injuries.

C-GFSR, an amateur built Zenair CH750 operated privately, was conducting a local flight 20 nm SE of Halifax. After a 40-minute flight the pilot noticed the engine was running rough and planned to return to the owner’s private air strip. A short time later the engine failed, and the pilot completed a forced landing and attempted to land on a beach on the East side of a lake. The aircraft landed short of the shoreline and into the lake. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, egressed without incident and no injuries. Local fire and police responded. The cause of the engine failure is being investigated by the operator/owner.

C-FFLW, un Lake LA-4 en exploitation privé effectuait un vol à vue local à partir de l’aéroport de Neuville, QC (CNV9) avec le pilote et un passager à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage sur la piste 06, l'aéronef est entré en collision avec 2 chevreuils. L’aéronef a subi des dommages à l'aile droite et à la porte de droite. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FAFJ, a Cessna 208 B operated by Superior Airways Limited was conducting flight SR607 from Red Lake Airport (CYRL), ON, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, with one crew member and no passengers on board. Approaching CYWG, SR607 was initially cleared for a right-hand base to Runway 31. The clearance was then changed to a right-hand downwind to Runway 31, which the pilot read back. The pilot then proceeded to turn base and SR607 flew through the final approach course of Runway 31 resulting in a loss of separation with N520QS, a Cessna 680A operated by NetJets conducting flight EJA520 from the Chicago/Midway International Airport (KMDW), USA, to CYWG, who was established on final approach for Runway 31.

C-GUDH, a WestJet B789 was operating flight WJA81 from Tokyo-Narita International Airport (RJAA), Japan, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Approximately 15 minutes into the flight, unanticipated turbulence was encountered. Two cabin crew members were injured and were considered incapacitated for the remainder of the flight. Duties were reassigned among crew members.

C-GENV, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 operated by WestJet Encore Ltd. was conducting flight WEN4703 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. At approximately 16 nautical miles southeast of Yorkton Regional Airport (CYQV), SK, while in cruise flight at flight level (FL) 240, the windshield on the first officer's side cracked. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook (QRH) checklist, declared a PAN PAN, and slowed the aircraft to between 180-200 knots while descending to 14 000 feet. WEN4703 continued towards CYXE and landed safely on Runway 27 at 14:03Z.The operator's maintenance replaced the windshield and the aircraft was returned to service.

G-VIIJ, un Boeing 777-200ER exploité par British Airways sous l'indicatif BAW4EA, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Seattle-Tacoma International, USA (KSEA) à destination de London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK. Au-dessus du détroit de Davis à l’est de la terre de Baffin, l’équipage a rapporté avoir rencontré de la turbulence sévère pendant environ 11 minutes. Le vol a continué vers sa destination.

C-GLQH, a DHC 8-400, operating as Porter Airlines flight PTR2487, departed Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, for a flight to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Shortly after leveling off in cruise at FL230, the CABIN PRESS warning light illuminated. The flight crew declared an emergency, initiated an emergency descent drill and then actioned the quick reference handbook, where it was discovered that the bleed air valves had not been selected ON as part of the after-takeoff callouts and checks. Pressurization was restored after the bleed air was turned on and the flight continued to CYUL.

C-FFCU, un Beech 1900D exploité par Sky Jet Aviation M.G., sous l'indicatif LSJ613, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Chevery, QC (CYHR) à destination de Lourdes-de-Blanc-Sablon, QC (CYBX). À environ 5 nm en finale, les 3 voyants verts de position du train n’ont pas allumé lors de l’extension du train d’atterrissage. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et a effectué la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour la sortie d’urgence du train. L’aéronef a fait une passe pour une inspection visuelle par du personnel au sol. Malgré la confirmation par le personnel au sol que les roues étaient sorties, l'équipage n'a pas eu d'indication que le train était sorti et verrouillé. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GBHO, an A319-114 operating as Air Canada Rouge flight ROU1534, departed Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, and shortly after takeoff, at approximately 3600 feet, the flight crew received green hydraulic system failure ECAM with PTU fault. The flight crew leveled off at 7000 feet and carried out the quick reference handbook procedures. A PAN PAN was declared and flight returned back to CYYZ. The aircraft landed without incident and was inspected by aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) with no faults found. The aircraft was towed to the gate without further incident.Maintenance inspected the aircraft in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual and found the green hydraulic low-level switch to be defective. The hydraulic low-level switch was removed and replaced with a serviceable component. Subsequent serviceability tests were carried out with satisfactory result. The aircraft was subsequently returned to service.

C-FARV, a privately operated, amateur-built Van's Aircraft RV-3A was conducting crosswind landing practice at Olds-Didsbury Aerodrome (CEA3), AB. On the third touch and go, the pilot lost directional control during the take-off. The pilot attempted to abort the take-off and the aircraft departed the left side of the runway and nosed over onto its top and came to a stop. The pilot received serious injuries, and the aircraft received substantial damage. The pilot was extricated from the aircraft by bystanders and was subsequently assessed by emergency services when they arrived on site.

C-FTIR, an ATR-42-500 operated by Canadian North, was conducting flight AKT658 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Cambridge Bay Airport (CYCB), NU. Shortly after departure a cabin attendant smelled a burning rubber smell in the forward cabin. The flight crew were made aware of the issue and elected to return to CYZF. During the return, a PAN PAN call was made with ATC. An uneventful landing was completed.Subsequent inspection by company maintenance was performed. However, maintenance personnel were unable to duplicate the fault, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPIX, a De Havilland Dash 8-402 operated by PAL Airlines Ltd., was conducting flight PVL2250 from Halifax/ Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL. During the climb, the number 1 propeller electronic control (PEC) caution light illuminated, and the engine perimeters indicated a propeller over speed and the RPM increased to 1080 RPM. The flight crew actioned the checklist and this provided direction to complete a precautionary engine shut down. An emergency was declared and the aircraft returned to CYHZ. The flight landed without further incident with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby.

C-GURP, a WestJet B789 was operating flight WJA81 from Tokyo-Narita International Airport (RJAA), Japan, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Cabin crew members were showing passengers the safety demonstration when the aircraft came to a sudden and unexpected stop. One of the cabin crew members was injured when they lost balance. The crew member was considered incapacitated for the remainder of the flight and occupied a passenger seat for both takeoff and landing. Crew positions and crew member duties were reassigned prior to takeoff.

C-FPBJ, a de Havilland DHC-7-103 operated by Air Tindi Ltd., was conducting flight TIN806 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, to SeaBee Mine Aerodrome (CCB2), SK. At approximately 87 nautical miles north-northeast of CYXE, while enroute to CCB2, TIN806 experienced an unexpected inflight shutdown of the #4 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-50). The crew actioned the quick reference handbook (QRH), notified company operations and elected to return to CYXE. The crew declared a PAN PAN. The crew completed an uneventful three engine approach and landing in CYXE with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby. The operator's maintenance is investigating the cause of the engine shutdown.

C-GTRK, a Bell Helicopters 412 SP operated by TRK Helicopters, was conducting a VFR flight to pick up and relocate a group of 8 forestry workers from Alberta Forestry heli-spot AB6-1 to the Zama City, AB heli-base. The pilot had flown into AB6-1 previously and was familiar with the location. During the approach into AB6-1 on this occasion, the pilot felt a momentary vibration as he descended into the landing site, but the helicopter did not require any abnormal control inputs or exhibit any other unusual characteristics. After landing, the pilot set the engines to ground idle and locked the flight controls so he could exit the right side of helicopter and complete an inspection. The pilot inspected the right of the tail boom and horizontal stabilizer as well as looking at the surrounding trees and foliage for evidence of contact with the helicopter. As none was observed, he boarded the helicopter and loaded the passengers for the return flight. During the flight back to the Zama City, AB heli-base the pilot observed a slight vibration in the tail rotor pedals. The helicopter landed uneventfully at the Zama City heli-base where the passengers were unloaded. The pilot subsequently shut down the helicopter to perform a more thorough inspection. The subsequent inspection by company maintenance revealed damage to the left side of the horizontal stabilizer and tail boom, as well as impact damage to the tail rotor blades. The helicopter was deemed unserviceable and was subsequently transported by truck back to the company's facility for repair.A follow up aerial inspection of the AB6-1 landing site by company personnel revealed broken treetops on the approach into the landing zone.

C-GBYN, a Beech B200 operated by Keewatin Air LP, was conducting medevac flight KEW201 from Arviat Airport (CYEK), NU, to Rankin Inlet Airport (CYRT), NU. At 0000z, while in cruise, the crew noticed the illumination of the left engine fire light along with the correlating warning system activation. The crew then completed the applicable checklist items and declared an emergency. Aircraft landed safely on Runway 13 in CYRT at 0012z. Upon confirmation that no fire existed, the operator's maintenance towed the aircraft to the ramp.

N808PD, a privately operated Embraer E-545, was conducting an IFR flight from Teterboro Airport (KTEB), NJ, U.S., to Shannon Airport (EINN), Ireland. While in cruise flight near 50° 50' N, 045° 00' W, the flight crew received the CAS messages AHRS FLTCTRL FAIL and FLTCTRL NO DISPATCH. The crew determined that an Attitude and Heading Reference System (AHRS) fault had occurred and declared PAN PAN with air traffic services. The crew coordinated a diversion to Bangor International Airport (KBGR), ME, U.S., where a landing was made without further incident.Maintenance technicians determined that a wiring fault in a power distribution harness related to number 3 AHRS system had occurred.

C-FLAD, a Robinson R44 helicopter operated by JoinAir Helicopters Inc., was conducting a local training flight from Chilliwack Airport (CYCW), BC, under visual flight rules, with an instructor and a student on board. The helicopter was on approach to land on a helipad beside a building. Prior to being positioned fully over the pad, the collective was lowered abruptly. The forward portion of the helicopter's skids were in contact with the helipad with the aft portion off the paved surface of the helipad, above the grass. The helicopter rocked backwards and forwards and, in the attempt to correct the nose high attitude, the helicopter yawed to the right and pitched forward. The helicopter rolled left and the main rotor blades struck the ground. It came to rest on the left side. Both occupants sustained minor injuries. The helicopter was substantially damaged.After the helicopter was recovered, it was determined that it was beyond economic repair.

C-FECI, an ATR-42-320 operated by Calm Air International LP, was conducting flight CAV224 from Rankin Inlet Airport (CYRT), NU, to Baker Lake Airport (CYBK), NU. While conducting the RNAV approach for Runway 16 at CYBK, the aircraft encountered 50 knot winds when flying from the initial approach waypoint to the intermediate approach waypoint. When the aircraft turned final, the winds slowly decreased. The pilot flying initially had difficulty spotting the runway due to the large crab angle and moderate rain. The aircraft crossed the threshold at about 50 feet, flared, and the touchdown was slightly left of the center of the runway. The aircraft drifted to the left side of the runway and made contact with 2 runway lights. The aircraft taxied to the terminal where a post flight inspection revealed damage to the left main landing gear door and weight on wheel switch.

C-GPIM, a Cessna 310R operated by Mitchinson Flying Service Limited, was flying from North Battleford Airport (CYQW), SK, to Stony Rapids Airport (CYSF), SK. At 17:05Z, 69 nautical miles west of the La Ronge/Barber Field Airport (CYVC), SK, the pilot of C-GPIM declared a MAYDAY due to a right engine (Teledyne Continental Motors IO-520-MB) failure. The pilot advised that they would be diverting to CYVC, where the aircraft landed safely at 17:46Z. Emergency services attended the landing. There were no injuries. There was no fire.A post-occurrence inspection by the operator indicated that the #4 connecting rod came through the engine case.

C-GMFW, a Bombardier CL-215-6B11 (Series CL-415) operated by Air Spray (1967) Ltd., was conducting a VFR flight from Fire 20; located approximately 70 nautical miles NW of Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB to CYTH. C-GMFW was southeast bound at 3500 feet, monitoring and making position reports on 126.7 MHz, and monitoring the BirdDog frequency. Two accompanying aircraft, C-GMFY and C-GJFO, were flying the same route at 1500 feet ASL and ahead of C-GMFW. C-GMFY notified C-GMFW that a De Havilland DHC-2 aircraft was overhead their position at an unknown altitude. C-GMFY attempted to communicate with the DHC-2 aircraft but there was no response. C-GMFW subsequently observed the DHC-2 as it passed 90 degrees of their track and a few hundred feet off their right wing. The visibility at the time was hazy in smoke and the color of the DHC-2 was white.

C-GCVS, un Beechcraft B200 exploité par Max Aviation inc. sous l’indicatif MAX210, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à destination de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors qu’il était en approche initiale pour la piste 24D, entre TAKIN et MAIRE en direction SW à 5000 pieds, l’ unité de circulation aérienne (ATC) a avisé l’équipage d’un trafic VFR à 12 heures à la même altitude. L’équipage a vu C-GAXD, un Cessna C-172N exploité par l’Académie de l'aviation de Saint-Hyacinthe inc. qui effectuait un vol d’entrainement selon les règles de vol à vue en direction nord à 5000 pieds. L’équipage du vol MAX210 a dû amorcer une descente immédiate afin d’éviter C-GAXD. Les 2 aéronefs se sont croisés avec un espacement vertical d’environ 200 pieds.

C-GTMX, un planeur monoplace de marque Burkhart Grob CLUB ASTIR III en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol solo local supervisé selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aérodrome de Saint-Raymond, QC (CSK5). Après avoir effectué un vol de près de 45 minutes, l’élève-pilote a effectué son approche à l’aérodrome. Au moment d’atterrir, ce dernier a mal évalué sa hauteur et le planeur a touché le sol durement provoquant un rebond et un deuxième touché dur. L’élève-pilote n’a pas été blessé et a pu s’extraire sans difficulté du planeur. Le planeur a été remorqué jusqu’au hangar où les dommages au train d’atterrissage et au fuselage ont pu être constatés. Le planeur a été retiré du service pour évaluer les réparations.

C-GPJN, a private Piper PA-28-151 was on a visual flight rules flight from Goderich Municipal Airport, ON (CYGD) to Ethel Airport, ON (CPD2). The pilot, sole person onboard, performed a circuit and landing in a field 1.4 nm SW of CPD2. During the landing roll, the pilot elected to go-around. During the go-around the aircraft was unable to climb and the aircraft collided with terrain at the end of the field, bounced, crossed over a county road and came to rest approximately 100 feet past the road in an adjacent field. The pilot was injured and taken to a local hospital. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The ELT activated and the signal was received by JRCC Trenton. There was no fire. Local Police and Fire attended the scene. The investigation revealed that the pilot misidentified a similar looking field as the airport runway at CPD2 and conducted a circuit, approach and landing to a field instead.

C-FRQN, un Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8411 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Gander international, NL (CYQX) à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ) avec 60 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Alors que l’aéronef était en vol de croisière au niveau de vol 340, une indication de basse pression d’huile moteur est apparue. L’équipage a fermé le moteur applicable, a déclaré une situation d’urgence et a fait une diversion à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). L’aéronef s’est posé sur la piste 24R sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte.

C-FCEU, an Air Canada Airbus A321, was operating as flight ACA257 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. In the climb to cruise altitude at approximately FL260, the aircraft experienced severe turbulence. There were no controllability issues and no adverse passenger reaction, however one cabin crew reported an injury and was unable to continue their duties. The flight crew elected to continue to CYWG and the aircraft landed safety in CYWG.

C-GUBH, an Air Transat Airbus A330, was operating as TSC213 from Zagreb/Franjo Tudman International Airport (LDZA), Croatia, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. On final approach into CYYZ, the flight crew received a F/CTL RUD TRV LIM FAULT ECAM message. The flight crew consulted the status page, declared a PAN PAN emergency and decided to continue with the approach. The flight crew did not report any controllability issues. Emergency vehicles were present as a precaution due to concerns about brake temperatures but were not needed as brakes were within normal operating temperatures. The aircraft landed safely and taxied to the gate under its own power.

C-GKKR, an ATR 42-320 operated by Calm Air Intl. LP, was conducting flight CAV118 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB. After an uneventful landing at CYTH, the aircraft taxied to the terminal. After stopping, ground personnel observed smoke coming out of the number 2 brake. The crew were notified and emergency services were requested. The flight attendant performed a rapid passenger deplanement. Aircraft rescue and firefighting attended the scene but no fire was observed.The operator's maintenance replaced the number 2 brake assembly and inspected the number 1 brake assembly. The aircraft completed a taxi test and was returned to service.

C-FWEM, a Piper PA-46-310P operated by Geodesy Group Inc., was conducting a photo survey flight within a block altitude from FL 220 to FL 240 approximately 110 nm north of Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. C-GURF, a Beech 1900D operated by Transwest Air Ltd. (dba Rise Air), was conducting flight RS194 from Cigar Lake Aerodrome (CJW7), SK, to CYXE. ATC cleared C-GURF to an altitude of FL 240 in the block of airspace assigned to C-FWEM and separation was not ensured. At their nearest point, the two aircraft were separated by 1400 feet vertically and 0.4 nautical miles laterally.

C-GDEN, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3628 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Portland International Airport (KPDX), Oregon. While in climb during departure, the flight crew received a pitch trim caution light and an auto trim fail message. A larger input force was required for pitch. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook, turned back to CYYC and declared a PAN PAN. The flight landed safely with no further issues.Company maintenance determined that the flight control electronic control unit had failed. The unit was replaced, operational tests carried out and the aircraft was returned to service.

A WestMET RPAS operator was seeding with a DJI AGRAS T40 unmanned aircraft system (UAS) near the Obed Mine, approximately 11 nm NE of Hinton / Entrance Aerodrome (CEE4), AB. The T40 was programmed to seed autonomously for several flights. During the occurrence flight the operator noted that the seeding operation had been interrupted and had some control issues. The UAS then flew into the side of a hill and was damaged during the impact. No one was injured.

C-FVKN, a VIH Helicopters Limited Sikorsky S-61N departed on a local visual flight rules flight from a staging area near Southgate River, BC, to conduct heli-logging operations. The helicopter was equipped with a grapple that was suspended on a 270-foot longline. While the grapple was lowered in tall trees, the cloud ceiling lowered and there was no longer sufficient altitude for the grapple to clear the trees without the helicopter entering cloud. The pilot released the load from the grapple and then maneuvered the grapple through the trees into an open cut block. The pilot laid down the grapple and longline in the cut block, released the line from the helicopter, and flew back to the staging area without incident.

C-GPVQ, a float-equipped De Havilland DHC-6 Series 100 operated by Osprey Wings Ltd., was departing Points North Landing Water Aerodrome (CKC2), SK, for La Ronge Water Aerodrome (CJZ9), SK. Shortly after C-GPVQ was airborne from CKC2, smoke and an acrid smell was noticed in the cabin. The flight crew levelled off at circuit altitude and circled back to land at CKC2. The aircraft landed safely. There were no injuries. The operator's maintenance was dispatched to CKC2 to inspect the aircraft. They identified that a landing light wire was burnt at connector J45. Wire was secured and system tested serviceable.

C-FODL, un DeHavilland DHC-8-100 exploité par Air Creebec était en préparation pour le vol CRQ217 à partir de l'aéroport de Val d'Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de l'aéroport de Chisasibi, QC (CSU2) avec 3 membres d'équipage à bord. Avant l'embarquement des passagers, l'équipage a détecté de la fumée émanant du plafond de la cabine. Le pouvoir électrique a été coupé et la fumée s'est dissipée. Une bulbe de lumière défectueux a été trouvé lors de l'inspection par le service de maintenance.

C-GKXR, a Porter Airlines Embraer E190-400, was operating as flight PD271 from Ottawa/ Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Several hours into the flight, the aircraft developed an AVNX MAU 1A fault causing a loss of normal braking and potentially a loss of nose wheel steering. The crew elected to continue to CYYC. Prior to the top of descent, the crew declared a PAN PAN. The flight landed using emergency braking and MAX reverse thrust. The flight was able to exit the runway, as nose wheel steering was functional, but was towed to the gate following an inspection of the brakes for high temperatures. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft.Company maintenance determined the power supply to MAU 1A had failed. The unit was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FTQR, un Beech 1900D exploité par Propair Inc, effectuait le vol PRO4900 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport Billy Bishop de Toronto, ON (CYTZ) à destination de l'aéroport de Val d'Or, QC (CYVO) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 5 passagers à bord. Alors que l'aéronef était en vol de croisière, la pare-brise de droite s'est fissuré sans raison apparente. L'équipage a effectué la liste de vérification d'urgence et déclaré l'état d'urgence (pan pan) avec l'unité de circulation aérienne pour ensuite dérouté vers l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) où l'atterrissage s'est déroulé sans encombre.

C-FIUR, un Boeing 777-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA0874 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments à partir de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport Paris Charles de Gaule, France (LCDG) avec 325 passagers et 12 membres d'équipage à bord. Peu après le départ de CYUL, l'équipage a reçu une indication de faible quatité d'huile sur le système hydraulique de gauche. L'équipage a revue la liste de vérification applicable et a déclaré une urgence (pan pan) avec l'unité de contrôle de la circulation aérienne. L'équipage est ensuite revenu se poser à CYUL attendu par les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronef. Après vérification, ACA0874 a circulé à la porte d'embarquement sur son propre pouvoir. Le service de maintenance a découvert une fuite de liquide hydraulique sur un joint torique endommagé de l'unité de contrôle extérieure de l'aileron de droit lors de l'inspection.

C-GZEW, un DHC-8-300 exploité par Air Creebec sous l'indicatif CRQ5376, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international Jean-Lesage de Québec, QC (CYQB) à destination de l'aéroport métropolitain de Montréal (MET), QC (CYHU). Alors que l'aéronef était en descente à 5200 pieds, l'unité de circulation aérienne a informé CRQ5376 d'un trafic se dirigeant vers leur trajectoire. L'équipage a ensuite reçu un avertissement du système d'alerte de trafic et d'évitement de collision (TCAS) de réduire la descente. L'équipage a désengagé le pilote automatique puis effectué la manoeuvre prescrite par le système. C-GAXD, un Cessna 172M qui effectuait un vol local à partir de l'aéroport de St-Hyacinthe, QC (CSU3) selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) à été observé légèrement sous leur position à une distance d'environ un mile nautique.

C-FYAI, un DeHavilland Dash-8-300 exploité par Air inuit Ltée, effectuait le vol AIE705 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) à destination de l'aéroport International Montréal-Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 38 passagers à bord. Alors que l'aéronef était en vol de croisière, le copilote a senti un malaise et n'a pu continuer d'exercer ses fonctions. Le commandant et l'agent de bord ont initié la procédure pour un pilote subissant une incapacité et un membre d'équipage de la compagnie, qui était passager sur le vol, est venu prêter assistance au commandant de bord pour le reste du vol. Une urgence a été déclaré et le vol a continué vers CYUL où l'aéronef est atterri sans encombre.

C-GWRC, an Airbus Helicopter H145 aircraft operated by Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service (STARS) was on a night VFR flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Dauphin/Lt. Col. W.G. Billy Barker Airport (CYDN), MB. While enroute approximately 14 nm southeast from CYDN, the aircraft's right front windscreen was struck by a bird; causing a large hole and subsequently entering the flight deck. No injuries were sustained by the flight crew or passengers. The flight crew completed the emergency checklist and landed safely in CYDN.The operator's maintenance department inspected the aircraft and determined that there was no damage beyond the right front windscreen. The windshield was temporarily secured and the aircraft was ferried under an authorized permit to CYWG for windshield replacement.

C-GUDH, a WestJet Boeing 787-9, was operating as flight WJA81 from Tokyo-Narita International Airport (RJAA), Japan, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. C-FSNP, an AirSprint Cessna Citation 525B, was operating as flight ASP675 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to CYYC. Both aircraft had been cleared to 10 000 feet at RNAV waypoint ADVOX. Separation between WJA81 and ASP675 reduced to 5.2 miles where 6.0 miles was required for wake turbulence separation. ATC instructed ASP675 to stop descent at 12 000 feet. Separation was restored and both aircraft landed safely in CYYC.

C-GCIJ, a Cargojet Airways Boeing 767-300 was operating as flight CJT301 from Hamilton Airport (CYHM), ON, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While landing on RWY 35R, CJT301 experienced a loss of runway separation with C-FNAX, a WestJet Boeing 737 MAX, which was operating as WJA502 from CYYC to St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL. As CJT301 touched down on the runway, WJA502 ahead was still on the takeoff roll. Seconds after CJT301 touched down, WJA502 became airborne.

C-GWBI, un appareil de type Cessna 180 sur flotteurs en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue à destination du lac Parent à Senneterre, Qc avec seulement le pilote à bord. Lors de l’amerrissage sur le lac Parent, une rafale a déplacé l’appareil et le pilote a perdu le contrôle. L’aile droite a touché l’eau et l’avion s’est renversé. Le pilote a pu évacuer l’appareil et a été secouru par des résidents locaux. Le pilote n'a pas été blessé et l'appareil a reçu des dommages importants.

C-GLQX, un De Havilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Porter Airlines, effectuait le vol PTR2303 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON à destination de Fredericton, NB (CYFC) avec 66 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage à bord. En vol de croisière, le voyant d’avertissement de la pression d’huile du moteur #2 a commencé à s’allumer de façon intermittente pour ensuite rester allumé. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée et le moteur a été éteint. Une urgence (MAYDAY) a été déclarée et un déroutement vers l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) a été effectué. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre à CYQB. Le personnel de maintenance a confirmé que le refroidisseur d’huile du moteur #2 était fissuré.

C-GJLJ, un Beech A100 King Air exploité par Propair sous l'indicatif de vol PRO4215 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda QC (CYUY) à destination de l'aéroport de Waskaganish, QC (CYKQ) pour un vol d'évacuation médicale avec 2 pilotes et 1 membre d’équipage de cabine. L'appareil s'est posé et sur le roulage au sol, le train principal gauche s’est partiellement affaissé. L’hélice a heurté le sol à plusieurs endroits, mais l’équipage a maintenu le contrôle directionnel et a été en mesure d’arrêter l’avion sur la piste. Ils ont ensuite procédé à une évacuation. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. Il a été constaté que la plaque de barrure du train n'était plus en place, car les boulons qui la maintenait en place se sont rompus.

C-GFUR, an Airbus A330-343 operated by Air Canada was conducting flight AC306 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During pushback, the flight crew received a generator fault message on the No. 2 engine. The aircraft came back to the gate, and maintenance was able to defer the fault under minimum equipment list (MEL). After the second departure, and shortly after reaching cruise altitude, the flight crew received an auxiliary power unit (APU) fault message. The quick reference handbook (QRH) required the flight crew to turn the APU off, but, since the APU was required to run for the deferred generator fault, the decision was made to divert to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. A PAN PAN urgency was declared and the aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance replaced the APU General Control Unit as per the aircraft maintenance manual and carried out the requisite ground tests. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GCHT, a Mustang Helicopters Incorporated Bell Textron 212 was conducting a flight, after maintenance procedures had been performed, approximately 6 nautical miles east of Vanderhoof Aerodrome (CAU4), BC. During the autorotation check, the pilot brought both engine throttles to the fully open position; neither engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6T-3) responded and remained at idle power. After recognizing the issue, the flight crew carried out a full-on autorotation and landed safely. There were no injuries and there was no damage to the helicopter.The engines were removed and sent to the engine manufacturer for examination.

C- GTMM, a Friendly Fast Foods Inc. Piper PA-31T1, was conducting a flight from Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, to High Level Airport (CYOJ), AB. While in cruise at FL220, the aircraft experienced a pressurization loss and conducted an emergency descent to 13 000 feet ASL. Once at the lower altitude the emergency checklist was carried out. The flight continued to CYOJ without any further issues and landed safely.The maintenance team determined that an air supply line had blown off a fitting. The line was reinstalled, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GQSS, a Pacific Professional Flight Centre Ltd Cessna 152 departed Vancouver/Boundary Bay Airport (CZBB), BC, for a local flight under visual flight rules with 1 student pilot onboard. During the first attempted landing on Runway 25, the aircraft bounced twice on the runway and the pilot performed a successful overshoot. On the second landing, the aircraft touched down hard on the runway and bounced back into the air. The pilot added partial power and the aircraft bounced a second time. The aircraft nose gear collapsed and the aircraft veered to the right before coming to a stop off the edge of the runway. The pilot was uninjured and egressed the aircraft. Air traffic services dispatched Delta Fire and Emergency Services to the scene. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.The company intends to assess and repair the aircraft.

C-GRXE, a Pilatus PC-12/47E aircraft operated by Ornge Air was conducting an IFR flight from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, to Webequie Airport (CYWP), ON.  While climbing northbound from CYQT through 13 000 feet, the engine torque indication began to fluctuate. All other engine parameters were normal. The aircrew elected to return to CYQT. As they returned to CYQT the torque fluctuations continued to get worse. The pilot-in-command declared a PAN PAN in order to receive priority clearance for landing. After a normal landing, the torque indication became a red X.The operator's maintenance department repaired a wire on the cannon plug for the engine torque pressure transducer. Subsequent engine torque indication checks were serviceable.

C-FBTR, a Carson Air Limited Beech 1900D departed Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, on flight CRN511, under instrument flight rules, to Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies Airport (CYXC), BC. On arrival at CYXC, the crew were unable to get a nose gear down and locked indication. The crew completed the required checklists and were able to get confirmation that the gear was down and locked. They decided to return to CYLW and requested that aircraft rescue and firefighting crews be on standby for their landing. The flight landed without incident. There were no injuries and the aircraft was not damaged.After inspecting the aircraft, maintenance replaced the landing gear indicator assembly.

C-GPAK, an Iskwew Air Inc. Piper PA-31-350 (Chieftain) aircraft, was conducting flight SG467, under instrument flight rules, from Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. After reaching their cruise altitude of 3000 feet, while setting cruise power and completing the cruise checklist, the flight crew noticed the left engine (Avco Lycoming TIO-540-J2BD) was showing abnormal indications. The oil temperature and cylinder head temperature were reaching the red line and the engine rpm was dropping significantly. The flight crew declared a MAYDAY, informing air traffic control that they had an engine failure. After considering their options, the flight crew decided to continue the flight to CYVR. While the engine continued to lose power, the flight crew chose not to shut down the engine because the remaining power was necessary to maintain altitude and a safe airspeed. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 08R at CYVR with aircraft rescue and firefighting crews on standby. During the landing rollout, the left engine seized with a loud bang, and the propeller stopped abruptly. The flight crew noticed smoke coming from the affected engine compartment, prompting the flight crew to order all occupants to evacuate the aircraft. The passengers were transported to the South terminal. After the aircraft landed at CYVR, airport personnel inspected the runway for foreign objects; an oil dipstick belonging to the occurrence aircraft was found. There were no injuries and no other damage to the aircraft. The engine was removed and sent to an engine shop to determine the cause of the failure.

C-GPMX, a privately registered float-equipped Maule M5-235C aircraft, was conducting a VFR flight from Moosehorn Lake (58° 09' 31" N, 132° 07' 32" W), BC, to Kennicott Lake (58° 10' 26" N, 131° 33' 04" W), BC, with only the pilot on board. While en route, the aircraft conducted a low pass over a lake and while in a left turn, the aircraft's airspeed reduced, the left wing stalled, and the aircraft impacted terrain. The pilot was able to egress the aircraft; he received minor injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The ELT signal was relayed to the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre in Victoria, BC.The pilot was able to walk to a nearby camp and the aircraft will be recovered from the accident site.

C-GFCH, an Airbus A320-214 aircraft operated by Air Canada Rouge LP as flight ROU1937, was operating an IFR flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. While on approach to CYXE at approximately 4500 feet ASL, and immediately after the flight crew selected Flap 2, the electronic centralized aircraft monitor (ECAM) annunciated a flight control - flaps locked message. The flight crew discontinued the approach, informed ATC, and declared a PAN PAN. The quick reference handbook procedures were followed and the flight crew conducted an uneventful slats-only landing on Runway 27 at CYXE.The operator's maintenance subsequently inspected the aircraft and identified that the right-hand position pick-off unit (PPU) and the right-hand flap actuator were defective. The units were replaced, a serviceability test was completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKXR, a Porter Airlines Embraer E195-E2 was operating flight POE670 from San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, the crew declared an emergency due to navigational issues/brake failure and elected to divert to Salt Lake City International Airport (KSLC), UT, where the aircraft landed safely.

C-FDMB, a Westjet B737-8 was operating flight WJA1591 from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (KATL), GA, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During climb, a cabin crew became ill and was unable to perform safety duties which were reassigned amongst the remaining cabin crew members.

C-GBTJ, a Wilderness Seaplanes Ltd Cessna A185F departed Port Hardy Water Aerodrome (CAW5), BC, under visual flight rules to a logging camp in Warner Bay, BC, with 1 pilot and 2 passengers onboard. On landing, after the aircraft contacted the water, control was lost. The aircraft came to rest with the fuselage underwater. The pilot and 1 passenger egressed the aircraft. The second passenger was unable to egress and was fatally injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GORC, a Propair Inc. Beech 1900D, operating as PRO4371 en route from Wawa Municipal Airport (CYXZ), ON, to Sudbury Airport (CYSB), ON, declared a PAN PAN emergency due to a nose gear indication. The flight crew consulted their checklists, conducted a low pass in front of the FSS tower to confirm the position of the landing gear, and then landed safely at approximately 1820 UTC. The aircraft was stopped and shut down on the runway before being towed to the gate.

N788UA, a United Airlines Boeing 777-200ER was operating as flight UAL949 from London Heathrow Airport (EGLL), United Kingdom to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), United States. While en route in cruise, approximately 148 nm NW of Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, the flight crew noticed a faint but consistent electrical odor. Checklists were actioned, and the pilots made an assessment of electrical devices in the cabin with no immediate findings. The flight attendants and passengers reported that the electrical odor was coming from the forward cabin area. The flight crew declared an emergency and diverted to CYYC where the aircraft landed without further incident. Company maintenance is conducting troubleshooting and will advise TSB of findings.

C-GELD, an Adventure Aviation Piper PA-31 was operating on a flight from Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC, to Fort Grahame Aerodrome (CBW3), BC. Shortly after departure, while climbing to cruising altitude, the pilot observed oil leaking from the #1 engine (Lycoming TIO-540-A2B) cowling. The pilot cross referenced the oil loss with the oil pressure gauge and observed the oil pressure decaying. While climbing through 8000 feet ASL a turn back to CYXJ was initiated and the pilot contacted Fort St. John Radio to declare a PAN PAN. The pilot decided not to shut down the engine and continued to the airport. The aircraft landed without further incident. Once clear of the runway, before coming to a stop, the pilot shutdown and secured the #1 engine. When the aircraft came to a stop, the pilot shutdown and secured the #2 engine. There were no injuries. Company maintenance found the #1 engine vacuum pump seal to be leaking. The seal was replaced, and the aircraft was released for continued service.

C-FMCN, a Beechcraft 1900D, operated by Pacific Coastal Airlines, was conducting flight PCA558 from Williams Lake Airport (CYWL), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During descent from 10 500 feet above sea level (ASL) to 10 000 feet ASL, approximately 41 nautical miles northwest of CYVR, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence and control of the aircraft could not be maintained. The crew regained control at approximately 9700 feet ASL and were then able to climb back to their cleared altitude of 10 000 feet ASL. The aircraft continued to CYVR in moderate turbulence and landed without further incident. There were no injuries.Maintenance conducted a severe turbulence inspection and found loosened rivets in the right elevator torque tube. The right elevator was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FLRZ, a privately registered Champion 7GC was operating on a local flight from Lacombe Aerodrome (CEG3), AB. While on final approach for RWY 35, the pilot experienced WNW winds which were approximately 15 knots gusting to 25 knots. The pilot landed the aircraft and during the rollout, the aircraft began veering to the left. The pilot responded using full right rudder and full right brake but was unable to maintain the runway centerline. The aircraft ran off the west side of the runway and came to rest when it collided with a fence, approximately 112 feet from the edge of the runway. The pilot and passenger were uninjured. The aircraft received significant damage to the wings, wing struts and landing gear.

C-FWZV, an Air Tindi De Havilland DHC-7 was operating as flight TIN802 from Bathurst Inlet (CJN6), NU, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. While being vectored for approach into CYZF, TIN802 experienced a loss of separation with the Nolinor Aviation Boeing 737, operating as NRL117 from Diavik Aerodrome (CDK2), NT, to CYZF. Lateral separation reduced to 3.5 miles where 5 miles was required.
