C-GGOK, a Jazz Aviation De Havilland DHC-8-400 was operating as JZA421 from Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During departure, while in climb to cruising altitude, the flight crew received a BAG DOOR warning indication. The quick reference handbook was actioned and the flight crew elected to remain at FL160 to reduce cabin pressure. ATC was advised, a PAN PAN emergency was declared, and the flight continued to CYYC. The aircraft landed without further incident and taxied to the gate. Upon arrival at the gate, company maintenance inspected the baggage door to find the latch was not completely closed. The latch was inspected and lubricated before the aircraft was released for continued service.

C-FCTK, a Westjet B737-8 was operating flight WJA2738 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to St. John's/V.C. Bird International Airport (TAPA), Antigua and Barbuda. During cruise a cabin crew became ill and was not able to perform safety duties and occupied a passenger seat for landing. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-FSIP, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight AC1338 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Argyle International Airport (TVSA), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. On route, the flight crew reported left engine rapidly losing oil pressure and oil quantity dropping. In discussion with MOC, the decision was made to divert to Luis Muñoz Marin International Airport (TJSJ), Puerto Rico. Indications continued to drop and the flight crew declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed without further incident

N27958, a United Airlines Inc. Boeing 787-9 aircraft was operating an IFR flight from Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), CA, U.S., to London/Heathrow International Airport (EGLL), UK, as flight UAL231. While enroute at FL350 over Hudson's Bay, the captain's primary flight display and navigation display failed to a blank display and both flight management computers entered a degraded mode with limited capabilities. Lateral navigation (LNAV) was unavailable; however, heading and track select modes remained available, as was communication via VHF and SATCOM. An emergency was declared. The aircraft diverted to Chicago/O'Hare International Airport (KORD), IL, U.S., via alternate navigation and vectors, where it landed uneventfully.

C-FYJH, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319, operating as ROU1855 from Tulum International Airport, (MMTL) MX, to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, declared an emergency due to a nose steering issue. The flight continued to CYYZ and landed safely on Runway 15L.

C-FTXE, a Sunwing Airlines Boeing 737 Max 8, operating as SWG438 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), DR, reported an onboard medical emergency after departure from CYYZ. The flight crew elected to return to CYYZ and declared a PAN PAN emergency due to an overweight landing condition. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 05 and remained on the runway for a few minutes to conduct checks before taxiing to the terminal.

C-FOJZ, a Jazz Aviation CRJ900, operating as JZA785, from Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (KDCA), VA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, declared a MAYDAY emergency due to a landing gear indication. On final, when the landing gear was selected, a gear disagree warning illuminated. The approach was discontinued, the aircraft leveled off at 3000 feet and the aircraft quick reference handbook checklist was actioned. The aircraft conducted a missed approach so that tower could inspect their landing gear, but the tower could not verify that the landing gear was extended. The flight crew carried out an alternate gear extension and landed safely on Runway 05.

C-FSIL, an Air Canada Boeing 737 Max 8, operating as ACA348, was enroute from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. During the latter stages of the flight, approximately 280 nm W of CYOW at FL390, the flight crew were advised of a cabin crew attendant that was unable to continue their duties. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GWQF, a privately registered, amateur built Sonex aircraft departed Abbotsford International Airport (CYXX), BC, on a recreational flight to Chilliwack Airport (CYCW), BC, with only the pilot on board. During the approach to land at CYCW the engine (Aerovee) began to surge and then stopped producing power. The pilot quickly raised the flaps to reduce drag and determined they were too low to make it to the runway. They selected a nearby field onto which a forced approach would be conducted. The pilot observed powerlines in his intended glide path and attempted to fly under the wires prior to the selected field. During this manoeuvre, the aircraft struck the ground and collided with a fence, approximately 0.4 nautical miles west of the airport. The pilot was able to call for assistance on his cell phone and egressed with the assistance of first responders. The pilot was treated in hospital for serious injuries. The aircraft had substantial damage.The aircraft was disassembled and transported to a nearby hangar for further assessment.

C-FRBD, an Aero Commander Rockwell 500S aircraft operated by Mag Aerospace Canada Corp., was parked on the apron at the Dryden Regional Airport (CYHD), ON. The pilot of C-FDBD, a Commander 690A aircraft operated by Mag Aerospace Canada Corp., contacted the fueling agent and requested JET-A fuel for C-FDBD. The contracted fueling agent subsequently began fueling C-FRBD with Jet-A (the aircraft requires AVGAS). The fueling was stopped when 20 litres of JET-A was added to C-FRBD. C-FDBD was parked nearby and has similar registration markings to C-FRBD. The pilot of C-FRBD was immediately notified and the aircraft was blocked from moving by a fuel truck. C-FRBD was removed from service for fuel removal by the operator's maintenance.

C-GUBD, an Air Transat Airbus A330-200, operating as TSC123 from London Gatwick Airport (EGKK), UK, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, declared a PAN PAN emergency while inbound into CYYZ due to a landing gear indication. TSC123 landed safely on Runway 05 in CYYZ but required a tow to the gate due to the loss of nosewheel steering.

C-FSJH, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight AC568 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA. On climb the aircraft experienced a right roll. The crew disengaged the auto pilot, took manual control, and declared a PAN PAN. No bank angle exceedance was triggered, and it was minimal. The flight crew advised dispatch and local maintenance. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GZRJ, a Summit Air BAE Avro RJ100, was operating as SUT8152 from Ekati Aerodrome (CYOA), NT, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. The aircraft landed on RWY 10, touching down approximately 1600 feet beyond the threshold. The runway had puddles of standing water from medium to heavy rains that had fallen recently before the aircraft landed. During rollout, the aircraft experienced decreased braking action due to hydroplaning while going through a large puddle. The pilot flying applied maximum braking for the duration of the landing roll, per the recommended procedure for hydroplaning and the anti-skid system worked normally. While decelerating, the aircraft exited the end of the runway, stopping approximately 20 feet beyond the paved edge of the runway on a gravel surface. The aircraft taxied under its own power to return to the gate. The aircraft received no damage. There were no injuries or property damage.

C-GWUT, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300, operating as ACA1169 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, declared a Pan Pan emergency while enroute at FL340, approximately 190 nm NW of CYYZ, due to a foul odor in the cockpit. The flight returned to CYYZ and landed without incident.

C-FMXG, un Boeing 737-8 exploité par Sunwing Airlines inc. sous l'indicatif SWG349 a effectué un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Jardines del Rey/Cayo Coco (MUCC), Cuba à destination de l'aéroport international Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC avec 188 passagers et 6 membres d'équipage. À l'approche du quai de débarquement, l'extrémité de l'aile gauche est entrée en collision avec un véhicule de service stationné. L'équipage a complété la procédure d'arrêt et les passagers ont débarqué à cet endroit. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé.

N957TX, a Cessna C750 (Citation X) operated by Mountain Aviation, was conducting flight WUP957 from Port Hawkesbury Aerodrome (CYPD), NS, to Teterboro Airport (KTEB), NJ, U.S. During cruise, the flight lost pressurization. The crew declared an emergency and completed an emergency descent. Once at a safe altitude, the flight crew cancelled the emergency and asked to divert to Rhode Island T.F Green International Airport (KPVD), RI, U.S. The flight landed without further incident.

N663UA, a Boeing 767-300ER operated by United Airlines Inc was conducting flight UAL956 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), U.S., to London Heathrow International Airport (EGLL), UK.  During cruise, cabin crew reported that they could smell a burning smell mid-cabin. The flight completed the non-normal procedure, declared an emergency, and coordinated with flight dispatch and requested a diversion to St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL. The flight landed without further incident. The aircraft was taken out of service and currently maintenance is trouble shooting the issue.

C-GSBD, a privately registered Murphy Rebel floatplane, was on a flight from Dry Pine Bay, French River, ON to Lake Temiskaming, ON. The water was a little rough for the landing at Lake Temiskaming and the aircraft landed hard, bounced and experienced a structural failure of the engine firewall on the second touchdown. There were no injuries, the pilot and passenger were transported by boat to a marina by a local boater and were assessed by EMS. The aircraft sank except for one wing was protruding the water.

C-GJHZ, a CL 600-2D24 (CRJ-900) operating as Jazz Aviation LP flight JZA931, landed on runway 24L at Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, and was cleared to taxi to the apron via taxiways DELTA 4 and DELTA, with clearance to cross runway 33R (15L). At that time, runway 24L was active for landings and runway 23 for departures. However, a Boeing 777, operating as Air India flight AIC188 (registration VT-ALO) had requested runway 15L for departure due to performance requirements. As AIC188 was on the takeoff roll on runway 15L and accelerating through approximately 110 knots, JZA931 was crossing runway 15L at the DELTA intersection, which is located near the end of the runway. The ground controller instructed JZA931 to expedite across the runway. As JZA931 cleared the runway, AIC188 was accelerating through approximately 135 knots; the two aircraft were about 6700 feet apart at this time.

C-IJGU, a privately registered float-equipped Zenair CH701SP, had departed the Catchacoma Marina for a training flight, with an instructor and the student pilot/aircraft owner on board. After conducting some airwork in the vicinity of Catchacoma Lake, the instructor planned to demonstrate a landing on glassy water. During the approach, the aircraft unexpectedly contacted the water with a relatively high rate of descent, and the aircraft overturned. Both occupants exited the aircraft and were uninjured and were rescued by nearby boaters. The floats of the aircraft had become mostly detached, and the aircraft eventually sank. It was later recovered from the lake and is substantially damaged.

C-GYJZ, a DeHavilland DHC-8-402, operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight JZA233 departed Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Sudbury Airport (CYSB), ON. Shortly after departure the aircraft nose landing gear door began to cycle on its own. The flight crew contacted maintenance, performed an alternate gear extension, declared an emergency and returned to CYYZ. They subsequently landed without further incident.

N52MG, a Piper Aerostar 600 operated by Castle Aviation Inc., was conducting a flight from John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, to Akron-Canton Regional Airport (KCAK), OH, U.S. Shortly after takeoff from runway 12, the top portion of the clamshell main entry door became detached from the aircraft. The flight crew declared an emergency and requested an immediate return to CYHM. They landed shortly afterward on runway 12 without further incident.

C-GFKA, a Pilatus PC-12/45 operated by Air Bravo Corp. as flight AB182, was conducting an IFR flight from Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON, to Attawapiskat Airport (CYAT), ON. While climbing through FL 235, the crew heard a loud bang and noted that the left windscreen had disintegrated and there was a loss of cabin pressure. The crew donned oxygen masks and established communications. They carried out an emergency descent, declared an emergency, and requested a clearance to return to CYQT where the aircraft landed safely. There were no reported serious injuries. A subsequent inspection by the operator revealed that the left windscreen had shattered, but its frame was still in place. The aircraft was removed from service and all of the other operator's PC-12 aircraft were inspected for similar damage; but no anomalies were found.TSB update 16 April 2025:The TSB Laboratory examined the remaining glass and window frame but could not determine a cause of the windshield failure. On 7 March 2025, a similar event with different PC-12/45 occurred near Sleetmute, Alaska, USA, which the United State’s National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating (ANC25LA027). The TSB is in contact with the NTSB to offer support to their investigation.

C-FYJH un Airbus A319 exploité par Air Canada Rouge sous l'indicatif ROU1553 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport international de Fredericton, NB (CYFC) à destination de l'aéroport international Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). En approche initiale vers la piste 24 gauche, l'équipage a reçu un avis de résolution du système de surveillance du trafic et d'évitement des collisions (TCAS RA) de maintenir son altitude. ROU1553 était en direction de l'axe de piste 24 gauche alors que JZA852 était en rapprochement vers l'axe de piste 24 droite. Les 2 trajectoires convergentes ont déclenché le TCAS RA. Les 2 appareils se sont alignés en parallèle sur l'axe de leur piste respective et se sont posés sans encombre.

C-FTBC, (s/n U20602047), an Amber Airways Inc. float-equipped Cessna U206F departed from the Faro/Johnson Lake Water Aerodrome (CFC9), YT, on a visual flight rules flight to Upper Macmillan River, YT. During the initial climb (approximately 500 feet AGL) the aircraft experienced an engine failure (Teledyne Continental Motors Model IO-520-F, s/n 8188-76R). The pilot subsequently conducted a forced landing on Johnson Lake Road, YT. The aircraft suffered minor damage to the bottom of the floats. There were no injuries and the emergency locator transmitter did not activate. The pilot's SAR contact advised the Joint Coordination Rescue Centre of the forced landing and that no assistance was required.Post-occurrence: The company is investigating the cause of the engine failure.

C-GOFV un Airbus A330 exploité par Air Canada roulait en direction de la piste pour effectuer un vol depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC à destination de l'aéroport international d'Alger - Houari-Boumédiène, (DAAG) Algérie, lorsqu'un membre d'équipage cabine a eu un malaise l'empêchant d'accomplir ses fonctions. L'appareil est revenu au terminal où le membre a pu débarquer.

C-FJZN, a CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) operating as Jazz Aviation LP flight JZA734, was inbound to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, at FL 190 when the aircraft's #1 yaw damper suddenly disengaged. When the flight crew attempted to reengage it, the aircraft veered abruptly to the left. The same incident occurred about 10 seconds later. The autopilot was then disengaged, and the #2 system was utilized. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and landed on runway 33 at CYYZ without further incident. Aircraft rescue and firefighting met the aircraft upon landing and escorted it to the gate.

C-FOWK, a Bombardier CL-600-2B16 aircraft operated by Image Air Charter Ltd., was on a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Bagotville Airport (CYBG), QC, when, the flight crew declared an emergency shortly after departure due to a flap issue. The crew decided to return to CYYZ, where the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GELJ, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight AC996 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Benito Juárez International Airport (MMMX), Mexico. During the flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue with duties. Flight landed without further incident and EMS met the aircraft on arrival.

C-GYSM, an amateur-built Avid Flyer MK IV STOL, was on a VFR flight from Selkirk Aerodrome (CKL2), MB, to Atikokan Municipal Aerodrome (CYIB), ON, with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. Upon landing on Runway 22 in CYIB, the aircraft experienced a gust of wind from the left and it ground-looped. The aircraft exited the runway; striking adjacent trees. The aircraft sustained damage to its wing tips, propeller and landing gear. There were no injuries to those on board.

C-GMCH, a Sikorsky S-92 helicopter operated by Cougar Helicopters Inc., was conducting a flight from St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL, to Hibernia Oil Platform (North Atlantic Ocean) with 2 crew and 15 passengers. After the initial departure, at approximately 300 AGL, the FADEC #1 and #2 CAUTION SEGMENTS illuminated on the EICAS. The flight crew completed the checklist, declared a PAN-PAN, and returned and landed at CYYT without incident. Maintenance verified there was an inadvertent signal from the FADEC 1/2 channel B that occurred momentarily during the take-off. The circuit was verified, and the helicopter was returned to service.

C-GYRS, a WestJet Boeing 787-9 was operating flight WS33 from Fiumicino/Leonardo da Vinci International Airport (LIRF), Italy, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During boarding, a cabin crew member sustained a minor injury and was not able to perform safety related duties for the remainder of the flight. The other cabin crew members assumed their duties.

C-FYNP, a Bell 407 Helicopter operated by Raven Helicopters Canada Inc, was conducting a flight with a 100-foot longline of lumber from Swift Current, NL, to Hungry Grove Pond, NL. During the trip, due to gusty winds, the helicopter dropped, resulting in the load becoming loose and the lumber scattering across the ground. The helicopter landed without further incident.

C-FDAO, un DeHavilland Dash-8-102 exploité par Air inuit Ltée, effectuait le vol AIE842 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) à destination de l'aéroport de Puvirnituq, NU (CYPX) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 10 passagers à bord. Suite au décollage, le voyant d'avertissement "ouvert" de la porte de train principal gauche s'est illuminé. Après avoir tenté sans succès d'abaisser le train de façon conventionnelle, celui-ci a dû être déployé en utilisant la procédure alternative. L'équipage est revenu vers CYVP et a demandé la présence des services d'urgence avant de posé l'aéronef sans encombre.

C-GARO, un Airbus A319-114 exploité par Air Canada Rouge LP, effectuait le vol ROU1954 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport Lester B. Pearson Intl, Toronto (CYYZ) à destination de l'aéroport Jean Lesage Intl de Québec, QC (CYQB) avec 5 membres d'équipage et 134 passagers à bord. Au moment d'amorcer la descente vers CYQB, une agente de bord a subi une blessure due à une turbulence subite et n'a pas été en mesure de continuer à exercer ses fonctions. Ses tâches ont été redistribuées entre les autres membres du personnel de cabine en accord avec les procédures de l'exploitant. Le vol s'est poursuivi sans autre incident.

C-GSYH, a Piper PA-23-250 Aztec operated by Kanata Aviation Training Inc., was conducting a runup after starting the engines when the student and instructor observed thick white smoke emanating from the cabin vents. The crew shut down the engines and evacuated the aircraft. The student pilot of the aircraft called the fire department shortly after evacuating. After evacuating, the smoke turned black and visible flames began to appear. Maintenance personnel attended the scene with fire extinguishers; however, they were unable to stop the fire. The fire department arrived at approximately 0825 MDT and extinguished the fire. The aircraft was destroyed, there were no injuries.

C-GMZN, an Air Canada A220 was operating flight AC740 from San Francisco International Airport (KFSO), CA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the cruise phase of the flight, a flight crew member became ill and was unable to continue flying duties. A dead heading captain assisted for the remainder of the flight. A PAN PAN was declared on arrival and EMS were requested to meet the flight. The flight was completed without further incident.

C-GBHY, un Airbus 319-114 exploité par Air Canada Rouge en tant que vol ROU1516, venait de compléter le refoulement de la barrière lorsque l'équipage a reçu un message du ''Electronic Centralised aircraft monitor'' (ECAM) indiquant GEN#1 FAULT. Durant l'exécution de la procédure du manuel de référence rapide, la présence de fumée a été observé en cabine et dans le poste de pilotage. Une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée par l'équipage. L'aéronef a ensuite été inspecté par le service incendie de l'aéroport et repositionné à la barrière pour le débarquement des passagers. Le personnel de maintenance a par la suite identifié un conducteur électrique qui causait des arcs électriques.

C-GORN, a Beech 1900D operated by Propair Inc. was conducting flight PRO4381 from Wawa Aerodrome (CYXZ), ON, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. At approximately 40 NM south southwest of Timmins Airport (CYTS), ON, while climbing through FL 180, PRO4381 received a right engine bleed air failure. The flight crew shut down the right engine bleed air system, declared a PAN PAN and diverted to Rouyn-Noranda Airport (CYUY), QC. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance found the fuse plug on the right engine bleed system was missing, a leak at the right-hand engine bleed air pre-cooler. The bleed air fuse and the right-hand engine bleed air pre-cooler were replaced, and the over-temperature sensor screws were tightened. The bleed air system was checked during a ground run and no further problems were found.

C-FULE, an ATR-72-200 operated by Calm Air International LP, was conducting flight CAV470 from Rankin Inlet Airport (CYRT), NU, to Taloyoak Airport (CYYH), NU. At approximately 250 NM south of CYYH, while cruising at FL 200 in uncontrolled airspace, CAV470 received a TCAS traffic advisory (TA). The flight crew looked out and identified the traffic (CGREJ), another ATR-72-200 operated by Calm Air International LP, conducting flight CAV488 from Kugaaruk Airport (CYBB), NU, to Thompson Airport (CYTH) MB, at FL200. Shortly after the TA, the flight crew of CAV470 received a TCAS resolution advisory (RA) to descend and the crew of CAV488 received a TCAS RA to climb. Both aircraft complied with their respective RAs until they were clear of conflict.

C-FDMT, a privately registered Piper PA-18-150 (Super Cub) departed the Upper Cache airstrip (56° 24' N, 121° 30' W), BC, on a recreational flight, under visual flight rules, for the abandoned airstrip at Prophet River (57° 58’ N, 122° 47’ W), BC, with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. After completing their runway inspection, the pilot set up for a landing. During the flare, the aircraft lost lift which resulted in a hard landing. The landing gear collapsed and the aircraft came to a stop on its belly. The pilot secured the aircraft and both occupants egressed without injury. The aircraft was substantially damaged.In addition to the damage to the landing gear, there was a propeller strike and damage to the left wing tip.

CF-KMD, a privately registered Globe Aircraft Corporation GC-1B (Swift) departed Qualicum Beach Airport (CAT4), BC, on a local recreational flight, under visual flight rules, with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. As part of the landing sequence, the pilot leveled the aircraft above the runway in the flare prior to touchdown. Shortly after the level off, the aircraft descended rapidly to the surface. The main gear contacted the runway and then collapsed. The aircraft came to a stop on the runway and the occupants evacuated. The pilot attempted to extinguish the post-crash fire with the aircraft’s on-board fire extinguisher but was unsuccessful. The post-crash fire consumed the cockpit area. Neither occupant were injured. The aircraft was destroyed.Emergency Services responded to the occurrence site and the fire department extinguished the flames. The wreckage was removed by the airport authority and repairs were required to area of the runway damaged by the fire.

C-GLQQ, a de Havilland Dash 8-400 operated by Porter Airlines Inc., was conducting flight PTR2486 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, with 4 crew and 42 passengers on board. During the climb through 14 000 feet, the flight crew observed that the LH engine oil pressure was on the lower end of normal and fluctuating. Before they were able to action the appropriate checklist, the oil pressure went below normal, and the crew elected to conduct a precautionary engine shutdown. They declared MAYDAY and announced their intention to return to CYUL, where they landed uneventfully. Before they taxied off the runway, ARFF inspected the aircraft and there were no leaks noted. Maintenance determined that one of the bolts securing the oil pressure regulator cover had become loose due to a failed helicoil.

C-GVRA, an Avro Lancaster MK X aircraft operated by Canadian Warplane Heritage, was conducting a local VFR flight from John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON. While on downwind for runway 30 the landing gear was selected down, but the right main landing gear indicator did not indicate that it was down and locked. After re-cycling the gear and actioning the appropriate checklist, the indicator was still not showing it down and locked, although it was observed to be in the extended position by the flight crew and there were no accompanying issues with the hydraulic system indications. The crew declared PAN PAN and made an uneventful landing on runway 30 with ARFF standing by. During the post-flight inspection, a broken electrical wire was discovered on the right main landing gear down lock.

C-GTNT, un Mooney M20F exploité privément, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue de l'aéroport de La Sarre, QC (CSR8) à destination de l'aéroport de Saint-Georges-de-Beauce, QC (CYSG) avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Alors que L'aéronef se trouvait à 126 NM ESE de CSR8, en croisière à 9500 pi, le moteur (Lycoming IO-360-A1A) a perdu en puissance et le pilote a déclaré une urgence. Le pilote a alors procédé à un atterrissage d'urgence sur une chemin forestier près du Lac Vimy. L'aéronef a heurté des arbres avec l'aile droite et s'est retrouvé sur le bas-côté à gauche de la route. Le pilote a été légèrement blessé et l'aéronef a subi des dommages importants. Il n'y a pas eu d'incendie.

C-GISS, a Cessna 172M operated by Integrated Sensing and Surveillance, was conducting a surveillance flight from Red Deer Regional Airport (CYQF), AB, to Edmonton Parkland Airport (CPL6), AB, with a pilot and passenger on board. While in the traffic pattern at CPL6 prior to landing, the pilot attempted to reduce the throttle in preparation for landing; however, the pilot observed the engine RPM increase. The pilot attempted to manipulate the throttle, but the engine did not respond and remained at high power. The pilot elected to divert to the Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, and declared an emergency with ATS while enroute. During the final approach for Runway 30 at CYEG, at a height of approximately 50 feet, the pilot intentionally shut down the engine and performed a glide to an uneventful landing. There was no damage to the aircraft and no injuries. Subsequent investigation by company maintenance found that a cotter pin for the throttle control had not been installed, and the nut securing the throttle control to the carburetor backed off during flight.

C-GJAN, a Jazz Aviation Bombardier CRJ900 was operating flight JZA931 from Philadelphia International Airport (KPHL), PA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. On the climb out, the elevator split caution message illuminated. Crew declared PAN PAN and returned back to KPHL. TCAS RA was received when routing back to KPHL. Flight landed without further incident.

C-GHNH, an Airbus Helicopter AS 350 operated by Newfoundland Helicopters Ltd, was conducting a flight from a remote camp which is approximately 74 nm NE of Goose Bay International Airport (CYYR), NL to Postville Airport (CYSO), NL. Shortly after take-off, the helicopter had an engine failure and the pilot was able to land upright, however the impact with terrain resulted in substantial damage. The pilot was the only occupant and egressed without incident, sustaining minor injuries. The ELT activated and JRCC Halifax was notified and then contacted the operator and TSB.Maintenance assessed the damage and identified that there was significant water and debris from the fuel drums, fuel filter and samples from the helicopter. The damage was significant, and the helicopter was slung to CYYR to determine a repair plan.

C-FGAQ, a Villers Air Services Britten Norman BN2A Islander departed Lower Prairie Airstrip (58° 04' 40" N, 123° 50' 55" W), BC, on a flight, under visual flight rules, to the Gathto Basecamp Airstrip (58’ 04' 05" N, 124’ 07' 39" W), BC. Immediately after takeoff, the aircraft experienced an engine (Avco Lycoming O-540-E4C5) power loss. The pilot initiated a forced landing and put the aircraft down into an area southwest of the airstrip that was partially cleared. The aircraft came to rest approximately 200 metres from the airstrip and both the pilot and passenger egressed without injury. The aircraft was substantially damaged. Damage included bending of the airframe and wings, with damage to both engines and propellers. The aircraft was recovered to Fort Nelson for assessment

C-FXUN, a privately registered De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-2 Mark 1 Beaver departed Courtenay Airpark (CAH3), BC, on a recreational flight, under visual flight rules, to a private airstrip on Nootka Island, BC, with the pilot and 2 passengers on board. Shortly after touchdown, the aircraft collided with vegetation along the edge of the landing area. There was damage to the undercarriage and to the wings. There were no injuries. Aircraft was disassembled and transported to Campbell River for assessment and repairs.

C-GFAJ, un Airbus A330-343 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA885 et N862RW, un Embraer E170SE exploité par Republic Airways sous l'indicatif RPA3459 effectuaient leur vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, tous les deux à destination de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Les 2 aéronefs étaient guidés au radar par le contrôleur de la circulation aérienne, ACA885 pour intercepter l'approche de la piste 24R et RPA3459 celle de la piste 24L. Alors que les 2 aéronefs se trouvaient à environ 10 miles marins (NM) à l’est de CYUL, l'espacement a été réduit à 2,6 NM sur le plan horizontal et 700 pieds sur le plan vertical alors qu'un espacement de 3 NM et 1000 pieds était requis.

C-FUHS, un hélicoptère Robinson R44 exploité par Attitude-Hélicoptère Inc. effectuait un vol d’entraînement depuis l’aéroport de Neuville, QC (CNV9) avec un élève-pilote seul à bord. Pendant les vérifications du moteur au sol, un mouvement de lacet à gauche a commencé. Dans la tentative d’arrêter le mouvement, l’élève-pilote a perdu la maîtrise de l’hélicoptère qui a décollé momentanément avant que les pales du rotor principal percutent le sol. Le pilote n’a pas été blessé et l’aéronef a subi des dommages importants.

C-GZAU, a privately registered Maule M-7-260C, was conducting a flight from a private grass runway in Caledon, ON, to Brussels Aerodrome (CPD4), ON, with the pilot and one passenger on board. Following a normal approach to runway 22, the aircraft touched down hard on the runway. The pilot was unable to maintain control of the aircraft, which exited the right side of the runway into a plowed field, where it spun 180 degrees as the right main landing gear collapsed. The pilot was uninjured, while the passenger received a minor injury. The aircraft was substantially damaged; the right landing gear had collapsed, the right wing tip was damaged, the right wing strut was bent, and the propeller was damaged from contact with the ground.

C-GYLP, a Boeing 737-8 operated by WestJet Airlines as flight WJA305, was conducting a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. During the descent into CYWG, the flight crew noticed smoke and sparks from the L3 window heat sensor. The crew disabled the window heat sensor and the smoke and sparks stopped. The crew declared a MAYDAY and the aircraft landed safely with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby. The aircraft then taxied to the gate. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft upon arrival. The electrically heated windshield L3 was deferred and aircraft is now operating under MEL.

C-GJUZ, a Jazz Aviation LP MHI RJ Aviation CL-600-2D24 (CRJ 900) for flight JZA766 was pushing back at Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to San Diego International Airport (KSAN), CA, with 4 crew members, and 73 passengers on board. While the aircraft was being pushed back from the gate, smoke was seen coming from the No. 2 engine (General Electric CF34-8C5) during engine start. The crew shut down the engine and the smoke dissipated. Aircraft rescue and firefighting personnel confirmed that there was no fire and the aircraft was towed back to the gate. There were no injuries and the aircraft was undamaged.A maintenance inspection determined that a hydraulic line leak was the cause of the smoke. The aircraft was repaired and returned to service.

C-GJAN, a Jazz Aviation CRJ900 was operating flight JZA879 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While climbing out of KEWR, the crew received an 'Elevator Split Caution' message. The quick reference handbook was actioned requiring minimal elevator movements to avoid turbulence and excessive crosswinds. Weather was passed via ACARS and decision was made to continue to CYYZ. Stopped climbing at 16 000 feet to meet the reduced airspeed. Crew asked for emergency response trucks to be on standby as aircraft landed. Aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GITP, an Air Canada Rouge A319-112 was operating flight ROU1709 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, NV. During the cruise phase of the flight, a Flight Attendant became ill and was unable to continue safety-related duties. The duties were redistributed among the cabin crew in accordance with company policy and procedure. The flight was completed without further incident.

C-GIBH, an Aero Vodochody L-39C, operated by ITPS (Canada) Ltd., as flight SA49, was on a VFR training flight, performing a simulated ILS approach to London International Airport (CYXU), ON, at 3000 feet ASL. The London Air Traffic Control Tower reported traffic, C-GGUI, a Cessna A150M, 4 miles ahead at 3500 feet. SA49 acknowledged but could not locate the traffic and requested clarification. Tower advised turning toward TUDAR. SA49 began climbing and was informed that C-GGUI was now at their 3 o'clock position, 2 miles away. SA49 still could not visually or instrumentally (TCAS) detect C-GGUI. Tower then advised C-GGUI to stop climbing, the traffic was directly above them. Radar showed SA49 at 3400 feet and C-GGUI at 3500 feet. SA49's ADS-B and TCAS did not display or alert to the other aircraft, and they never saw it visually.

C-GCJT, a Boeing 757-223 operating as Cargojet flight CJT2458, was on the approach to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, when the flight crew received a TE FLAPS DISAGREE EIACS message after selecting Flap 1. The flight crew carried out the quick reference handbook procedure and conducted a flapless landing. The flight crew requested emergency vehicles to be on standby in case the brakes overheated. The aircraft landed without further incident and was inspected by emergency vehicles after landing. No smoke or fire was found.Maintenance inspection found that the coupling for the #7 transmission was disconnected. The flap torque tube was replaced and during rigging and final check of flaps, two bolts were missing and the securing hardware was loose for the outboard RH flap control rod. The aircraft had recently came out of C-check.

N905G, a privately operated Gulfstream G-280 was conducting a flight from Eugene F. Kranz Toledo Airport (KTOL), OH, U.S., to Gander International Airport (CYQX), NL. During the approach phase when the landing was extended, the right main land gear did not provide an indication that it was down and locked. The gear in transit light stayed illuminated and the flight crew conducted a missed approach and requested vectors to provide time to review the checklist. The emergency landing extension was completed; however, it did not resolve the situation. The flight crew declared an emergency and aircraft rescue and firefighting was placed on standby. The aircraft landed without further incident and the landing gear safety pins were installed on the runway. Due to a delay in equipment availability, the flight crew taxied the aircraft to the ramp.Maintenance inspected the right main landing gear and determined that the down lock switch had failed.

C-GIJY, un Cessna 185F sur flotteurs en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’hydro-aérodrome de Ste-Anne du lac, QC (CSP9) à destination de Constance Lake (CNQ5), ON avec 1 pilote et 3 passagers à bord. Alors qu’il survolait le flanc de la montagne du diable, il a été rapporté que le moteur ne fournissait pas la puissance nécessaire pour éviter un impact avec les arbres. Trois occupants ont subi des blessures graves et un des blessures mineures. L’aéronef a subi des dommages importants.

C- GJXE, un Airbus A220 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA416, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ) à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 138 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage. Lors du roulage au sol après l’atterrissage, un message du système d'affichage des paramètres réacteurs, de mise en garde et d'alarme (EICAS) avisait d’une panne du moteur de gauche (Pratt & Whitney 1524G-3). L’appareil a pu circuler normalement à la barrière. L'analyse des paramètres enregistrés a confirmé le calage du moteur de gauche.

C-GUFU, an Air Transat A330-200 was operating flight TSC516 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Bordeaux–Mérignac Airport (LFBD), France. During the cruise phase of flight, a flight crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties. ATC was notified and the pilot remained seated in the full AFT position with seatbelt and shoulder harnesses secured. A cabin crew assisted the incapacitated pilot until the aircraft reached the gate.

C-GITR, an Air Canada Rouge A319 was operating flight ROU1709 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, NV. During the cruise phase of the flight, a Flight Attendant became ill and was unable to continue safety-related duties. The duties were redistributed among the cabin crew in accordance with company policy and procedure. The flight was completed without further incident.

C-FDHG, an Air Canada A330 was operating flight AC95 from El Dorado International Airport (SKBO), Bogotá, Colombia, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. On takeoff, the flight crew reported an engine 1 stall as thrust was being applied. The flight crew reviewed the quick reference handbook checklist and returned to the gate for further inspection.

C-GMYU, an Air Canada A220-300 was operating flight AC766 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS), MA. On initial approach, the flight crew experienced a sudden and unexpected flight handling event followed by FLT CTRL DIRECT EICAS MSG along with other flight control messages. The flight crew conducted a missed approach and switched to direct mode. A PAN PAN was declared and flight continued the second approach without further incident.

C-FKZO, a Cessna U206F operated by KBM Forestry Consultants Inc., departed Kindersley Regional Aerodrome (CYKY), SK, to conduct a VFR aerial powerline inspection flight. While executing a right-hand turn 7 nautical miles south-east of the Lloydminster Airport (CYLL), AB, the aircraft descended and struck the terrain. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The pilot and passenger received fatal injuries. There was no fire. The TSB deployed to the scene.

C-GQWJ, a Boeing 737-7CT operated by WestJet as flight WJA210, was at the departure gate at Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON. There were 5 crew members on the aircraft but no passengers had boarded yet. The aircraft was being refueled. After transferring 8500 pounds of fuel to each wing, the fueler switched to the center tank, activated the dead man switch, and returned to the truck to engage high idle. When the fueler returned to the wing panel, the number 2 gauge read 8810 pounds. The fueling was stopped and the flight crew were informed of the issue. The operator's maintenance instructed the flight crew to shut down the power to the gauges, carry out a reset, then restart the fueling to the center tank. As soon as the flight crew pressurized the system, fuel began to vent from the right side. The fueler stopped the refueling process and contained the spill. The size of the spill was contained to an area of 6 feet by 6 feet. ARFF responded to the spill.

N377FX, an Embraer EMB-505 (Phenom 300) aircraft operated Flexjet LLC, was conducting flight LXJ377 from Saint John Airport (CYSJ), NB, to Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD), IL, U.S. After takeoff from CYSJ, the flaps would not retract from the takeoff position. The crew performed the appropriate quick reference handbook actions, declared an emergency, and returned to CYSJ where a landing was made without further incident. Maintenance personnel conducted operational checks in accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual with no recurrence of the flap retraction defect.

C-GJUZ, un Bombargier CRJ900 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA644 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport New York/LaGuardia, NY (KLGA) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 71 passagers à bord. Lors du démarrage du moteur #2, durant le refoulement de la porte d'embarquement, le personnel de cabine a avisé l'équipage de vol qu'il y avait de la fumée dans la cabine provenant des évents de la cuisinette avant. L'équipage de vol a contacté l'unité de contrôle au sol pour l'informer de la situation après quoi les véhicules d'urgence ont été appelés. Le commandant de bord a alors ordonné l'évacuation rapide de l'appareil. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés ni de personnes incommodées par la fumée.

N583UP, a United Parcel Service Company Boeing 747-400 departed Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport (PANC), AK, U.S., on flight UPS509 to Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport (KSDF), KY, U.S., with 2 flight crew members and 2 passengers on board. During cruise at flight level 350 approximately 64 nautical miles east of Dease Lake Aerodrome (CYDL), BC, the flight crew received a status message indicating zero oil quantity in the No. 4 engine (General Electric CF6-80C2B1F). Subsequently, the oil pressure steadily decreased from 17 psi to 10 psi and then fluctuated between 13 psi and 10 psi. Eventually, the oil pressure fell below the lower limit (red line) of 10 psi. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with air traffic control, accomplished the "ENG 1, 2, 3, 4 OIL PRESS" emergency checklist and subsequently shutdown and secured the No.4 engine. The aircraft continued to KSDF without further incident.Post flight inspection revealed oil pooled in the exhaust area of the No.4 engine. The engine was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GSJZ, un DeHavilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA7720 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Bathurst, NB (CZBF) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 44 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, l'équipage a reçu une alerte de perte de pression du circuit hydraulique no.2. L'équipage a fait demi-tour vers CYUL et a déclaré une urgence. La procédure de déploiement alternative du train d'atterrissage a été effectuée avec succès. Lors de l'approche, la pression hydraulique est revenue. L'aéronef a ensuite atterri sans encombre.

C-GSPW, un B737-200 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif AIE705, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Puvirnituq, QC (CYPX) à destination de l'aéroport de La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) avec 56 passagers et 4 membres d'équipage à bord. Après avoir possiblement été frappé par la foudre en cours de vol, l'équipage a décidé de faire diversion vers l'aéroport International Montréal - Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) pour des raison d'inspection. Avant d'atteindre CYUL, l'équipage a déclaré une situation de carburant minimum par mesure de précaution. L'unité de circulation aérienne (ATC) a ensuite pris AIE705 en charge pour une approche directe et sans délais. AIE705 s'est posé sans encombre.

C-GDPI, un Beech King Air A100 exploité par Propair Inc, effectuait un vol d'évacuation médicale sous l'indicatif de vol PRO4245 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Wemindji, QC (CYNC) à destination de l'aéroport de Chisasibi, QC (CSU2) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 3 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, l'aéronef a amorcé une descente et a percuté des arbres à environ 700m du bout de la piste 28. L'équipage a rétabli la montée et est revenu atterrir sur la piste 10. L'aéronef a subi des dommages importants aux ailes, à l'hélice, à la nacelle et moteur droit ainsi qu'au stabilisateur horizontal du côté droit. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FDAO, un De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd DHC-8-102 exploité par Air Inuit Ltd, effectuait un vol d'essai concernant des problème de portes de train à partir de l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) avec deux pilotes à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, suite à la rétraction du train, une perte de liquide hydraulique du système #2 est survenue. L'équipage a déclaré l'état d'urgence (Pan Pan) et a effectué la procédure alternative de déploiement du train. L'aéronef est revenu atterrir sans encombre.

C-FDAO, un De Havilland DHC-8-102 exploité par Air Inuit Ltd, effectuait le vol AIE 851 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Kangiqsualujjuaq, (Georges River), QC (CYLU) à destination de l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 12 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée initiale au départ de CYLU, l'équipage a reçu une alerte de porte de train ouvert après la rétraction du train. Lors de l'exécution de la procédure du manuel de référence rapide pour un malfonctionnement du train, le train principal gauche ne s'est pas déployé. Le vol s'est poursuivi vers CYVP où une urgence a été déclarée. La procédure alternative de déploiement du train a été effectuée avec succès et l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre.

C-GKFS, a Kelowna Flightcraft Air Charter Limited Convair 340/5800 departed Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, on flight KFA 574 to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Approximately 6 minutes after takeoff, the main entry door unlock light illuminated followed by a decrease in pressurization. The crew subsequently conducted a precautionary shutdown of the No.1 engine (Allison 501-D22G). The aircraft landed in CYVR without further incident. There were no injuries and the aircraft was not damaged.Maintenance conducted an inspection and could not find any fault with the door rigging or operation. The aircraft was pressurized during ground runs to confirm that the main entry door was serviceable, and the aircraft was subsequently returned to service.

C-FQFU, a privately registered Champion 7GCAA (Citabria) was being operated out of the Peace River (CYPE), AB with the pilot and one passenger. on board. Shortly after take-off from Runway 22, the aircraft was observed to bank approximately 70 degrees, right to left, several feet above the runway, then climbed up to approximately 200 feet and flew a left downwind for Runway 22. The aircraft was then observed in a steep descending left turn over the runway, flew down the center of the runway at approximately 10 feet for several seconds, pulled up and initiate a roll. At the completion of the roll the aircraft stalled and collided with terrain on the north side of the runway. The occupants were fatally injured during the impact and the aircraft was destroyed in a post-impact fire.

C-FRQY, a privately registered Piper PA-22-150 departed Springhouse Airpark (CAQ4), BC, on a recreational flight, under visual flight rules, to an unnamed private airstrip (52 30 33.3 N, 122 28 39.47W), BC, with only the pilot on board. While landing at the destination, the aircraft bounced due to the uneven surface of the grass runway. When the aircraft touched down after the bounce, braking was applied and the aircraft nosed over. The aircraft came to rest inverted on the runway. The pilot was able to egress the aircraft without assistance. There were no injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The aircraft sustained damage to the propeller, spinner, engine cowling, vertical stabilizer, and rudder. The aircraft was removed from the runway and will be assessed.

C-FXAA, a privately registered Cessna 180H, was on a local VFR flight in the Fort Vermillion, AB area. While attempting to land on a rural road, during the final approach, the aircraft contacted a power line and flipped over and impacted the road. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, received fatal injuries; there was no post-impact fire. The pilot had landed on this road several times previously. The powerline was illustrated on the VFR navigation chart (VNC).

C-GTWE, a Westjet Encore DHC-8-402 departed Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, on flight WEN3260 under instrument flight rules to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC. Before top of descent into CYLW, severe static was experienced over the captain's headset, and the captain was unable to communicate with air traffic control (ATC) or with the first officer through the aircraft intercom. The first officer took over communications with ATC while the captain performed the appropriate checklist from the aircraft quick reference handbook. Due to concern about a complete communications failure, a PAN PAN was declared. The aircraft continued to CYLW without further incident.After the flight, company maintenance replaced the #2 VHF radio transceiver, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GMGD, a Viking DHC-2 Beaver floatplane operated by Simpson Air Limited, was on a VFR flight from Rabbitkettle Lake, NT, to Fort Simpson Island Water Aerodrome (CEZ7), NT. Approximately 6 nm from CEZ7, the aircraft suffered a complete loss of engine power (engine: Pratt & Whitney-USA, R-985-AN-14B). The pilot conducted a forced approach onto the Wrigley Highway. During the landing, the left wing sustained minor damage due to contact with small shrubs along the side of the road. There were no injuries and the emergency locator transmitter did not activate.The TSB is conducting a Class 4 investigation.

N574DZ, an Airbus A350-900 operated by Delta Airlines was conducting flight DAL176 from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (KATL), GA, U.S., to Dublin International Airport (EIDW), Ireland. During cruise a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to complete their duties. The flight crew contacted operations and a decision was made to divert to Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, at which point the crew declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without further incident and medical services met the aircraft.

C-GGIO, a privately registered Cessna C150M was on a local recreational flight under visual flight rules to and from Pitt Meadows Airport (CYPK), BC, with only the pilot on board. While landing on Runway 26L at CYPK, the aircraft bounced and became airborne. During the subsequent touch down, the aircraft was landed hard and the nose gear then collapsed. The aircraft came to a stop on the runway. The pilot egressed and was uninjured. In addition to the nose landing gear damage, the propeller was also damaged.The aircraft was recovered and will be assessed for damage.

C-GOKC, an Airbus A321-271NX operated by Air Transat was conducting flight TSC245 from Glasgow International Airport (EGPF), Scotland, UK, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON.  During the cruise phase, one of the cabin crew members reported not feeling well and was unable to perform their duties. An additional crew member onboard was able to take over the duties and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GSJB, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus 319-112 operating as flight ROU1922 departed Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK, on a IFR flight to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While enroute, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue their safety related duties. These duties were distributed among the cabin crew in accordance with company policy and procedures. The flight was completed without further incident.

C-FCHE, a Bell Helicopter 205A-1 operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd. departed the Wekusko Fire Base, MB, on a VFR flight to perform water bucketing on a nearby fire. During the tenth water bucket run, the water bucket unintentionally released from the helicopter. The water bucket was recovered but sustained significant damage. There was no damage to property or the environment.The operator's maintenance replaced the cargo hook assembly and tested it before returning the aircraft to service.

C-GMLB, a De Havilland DHC-3T floatplane operated by NDK Air Limited departed the Armstrong Water Aerodrome (CJF6), ON, on a VFR flight to Kashishibog Lake, ON. While on final approach to Kashishibog Lake, the aircraft struck a tree and subsequently landed hard onto the water. The pilot and passengers successfully egressed the aircraft. Two of the passengers received minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged and became submerged.

C-FXUS, a Fairchild SA227-CC, operated by Perimeter Aviation as Bearskin Airlines flight BLS377, was on route from North Bay Airport (CYYB), ON, to Sudbury Airport (CYSB), ON, at 8000 feet, and a had a near miss with a red and white Cessna on floats. C-FXUS had just emerged out of some clouds when the Cessna was observed through the right window flying directly at them in a southerly direction. C-FXUS took evasive action and descended rapidly and the Cessna was observed to bank sharply to the left. The flight crew of C-FXUS estimates the Cessna came within 200 feet of the aircraft. TCAS and ADS-B traffic systems were operating normally and there was no warning of the float plane until the visual sighting.

N77022, a Boeing 777-200 operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL120 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), USA, to Barcelona-El Prat International Airport (LEBL), Spain. During cruise one flight crew member was unable to complete their duties due to an injury. An air turn back to origin was conducted and the flight landed without further incident.

C-GRYW, a Delta Helicopters Ltd Airbus AS350B2, was conducting operations 6 nm east of Grist Lake (CFY2), AB. Upon landing at a remote location, in a confined area, the tail rotor contacted a tree branch. The helicopter continued the landing without any issues. There were no injuries.Following the flight the maintenance team found that the tail rotor trim tab was damaged and replaced the tail rotor. The helicopter was returned to service.

C-GYFM, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211, operating as flight ROU1545, from Charlottetown Airport (CYYG), PE, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the descent phase of flight, a flight attendant sustained an injury and was unable to continue safety related duties. The duties were redistributed among the cabin crew in accordance with company policy and procedure. The flight was completed without further incident.

C-GBZS, a Sunwing Airlines Boeing 737-800 was operating flight TFL2WD from Tenerife South Airport (GCTS), Spain, to Amsterdam Schiphol Airport (EHAM), Netherlands. When climbing through FL260, a cabin crew member noticed a burning smell, as they were using the forward galley oven to prepare food. The cabin crew member opened the oven to inspect it and observed glowing embers and a lot of dark grey smoke. The oven door was closed and the cabin crew and flight crew were notified of the issue. A halon fire extinguisher was taken, the seal was broken and the pin was pulled and was ready for use. When the oven was opened again, no glowing embers were observed as they had been extinguished in the closed oven. The cabin crew aired out the forward galley and the flight crew were notified accordingly. Once the oven was cooled down, the oven was inspected and two crew meal labels were found to be burnt. The flight continued without further incident.Maintenance removed the oven inserts and cleaned the oven elements.

C-FCRH, a Eurocopter AS 350 B2 operated by Foothills Helicopter Training Academy Ltd. (dba Exploration Helicopters), was conducting a local flight from Uranium City Airport (CYBE), SK, with one pilot and 2 passengers. During the walk around, the pilot noticed dew on the windscreen and wiped the dew off twice prior to starting the helicopter. After starting the helicopter, completing the checklist, and turning on the demister, the pilot again noticed dew on the windscreen. The engineer wiped the windscreen from the outside prior to the aircraft departing. C-FCRH departed to the southwest and climbed above the tree line. After flying approximately half a mile, the pilot was unable to see outside due to fogging of the front windscreen and side window. The pilot could see out the passenger-front windscreen. C-FCRH began making a right turn to remain over land and return to CYBE. After completing the turn, the passenger-front windscreen fogged over. The pilot used the passenger chin window to see the trees below but there was no reference indicating that the helicopter was descending. The pilot noticed that the trees appeared to be getting closer and tried to stop the descent by pulling up on collective. The helicopter settled into the trees, partially rolling on its left side but was still propped up by the trees. A horn was sounding and the engine was still running. The pilot shutdown the engine and crawled into the back seat to help unbuckle the rear passenger. The passengers and the pilot exited out the right-hand door. There were no injuries to the pilot or passengers. The helicopter sustained substantial damage. The ELT did not activate. There was no fire. The pilot used a portable radio to call for help. The pilot and passengers walked to the shoreline and returned to CYBE by boat.

C-FRXL, an Air Tractor AT-502A agricultural aircraft operated by Pembina Air (1999) Ltd. departed a private airstrip at Niverville, MB, on a VFR flight to perform aerial application of a field 1 nm East of Tourond, MB. While turning at a low altitude to start the spray run, the aircraft inadvertently descended and struck the terrain. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The pilot sustained minor injuries.

C-GEGI, an Air Canada Airbus A330-343 aircraft was conducting flight ACA306, under instrument flight rules, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During taxi at CYVR, the flight crew reported a flight attendant was unwell and requested a return to the gate. The flight attendant disembarked the aircraft and the flight subsequently departed with no further issue.

C-GRAL, a privately registered Ayres (Thrush) S2R-G6, was conducting local crop spraying operations from a private airstrip approximately 18 nm S of Lloydminster Airport (CYLL), AB, with only the pilot on board. During the third takeoff from the 2055 foot gravel runway, the aircraft became airborne but did not gain altitude. Immediately at the end of the runway was a mature canola crop. There were 2 tracks indicating where the aircraft tires had dragged through the top of the crop. The aircraft proceeded through the crop at times alternating between main landing gear, tail wheel and portions of the wings and spray booms for approximately 750 feet before making a slight 5° turn to the left for an additional 595 feet. Clumps of crop were periodically found along the flight path which was shed from the landing gear and spray booms. The aircraft struck an approximately 15-foot-tall embankment at the end of the field in a nose high attitude. Following the impact, the aircraft cleared the embankment, and subsequently impacted the ground in a steep nose down attitude and came to rest inverted 75 feet beyond the first point of impact. The pilot was fatally injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged. There was no post-impact fire and the 406 MHz ELT activated.The aircraft, engine, propeller and hopper dump system were examined. The investigation did not identify any issues that would have prevented these systems from operating normally during the occurrence flight. The investigation was unable to determine the actual fuel load on board C-GRAL prior to departure, or the actual hopper load, as fuel and aerial application product upload records were not available to the investigation. It was common practice for the pilot to depart with full fuel tanks. Upon return from the flights, only the left tank would be refueled to capacity. With these criteria as a guide and the aircraft departing for the third flight of the day, during the occurrence flight, it is estimated that the aircraft departed with 546 pounds of fuel on board. The investigation recovered notes from the pilot which indicated field location, size of the field in acres and that the product Glyphosate was being applied. These notes were used to determine that the field to be sprayed on the occurrence flight required approximately 320 USG (2872 pounds) of product. The empty weight of the aircraft was 4204 pounds. The Aircraft Flight Manual states the maximum operating weight limitation for the aircraft is 6000 pounds. The takeoff weight of the aircraft at the time of the occurrence was estimated to be 7872 pounds.

C-GAIS, un DHC-8-102 exploité par Air Creebec inc. sous l'indicatif CRQ921, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Val-d'Or, QC (CYVO) avec 15 passagers et 3 membres d'équipage à bord. À environ 75 nm ouest-nord-ouest de CYUL, en atteignant l’altitude de croisière, l’équipage a noté que l’altitude de la cabine descendait à 1500 pieds par minute. En tentant de régler la situation, l’équipage a entendu un bruit de dépressurisation provenant de l’avant du poste de pilotage. Ils ont immédiatement effectué une descente d’urgence et sont revenus atterrir à CYUL sans encombre.

C-GVUO, un Airbus A220-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA1050 et C-GTSR, un A330-200 exploité par Air Transat sous l'indicatif TSC111 effectuaient leur vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, tous les deux à destination de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL). ACA1050 était en rapprochement pour l’approche de la piste 06R et autorisé à descendre et maintenir 4000 pieds jusqu’au point de cheminement FULFO. ACA1050 est descendu sous 4000 pieds et est entré en conflit avec TSC111 qui était sur l’approche pour la piste 06L. L’ATC a pris rapidement des actions afin de rétablir la séparation. Les 2 aéronefs ont atterri sans encombre.

C-GRTB, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-800 was enroute from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, when a cabin crew member experienced a medical emergency. The crew member was unable to continue assigned duties and those duties were reassigned to remaining cabin crew members. The cabin crew member occupied the jumpseat for landing and was released into their own care after the flight. EMS was not requested or required upon arrival.

C-GJXY, an Air Canada A220-300 was operating flight ACA741 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA. Approximately two hours into the flight, the flight crew had a “HYD 1 QTY LO” EICAS advisory. In discussion with Maintenance and Dispatch, the decision was made to divert to Denver International Airport (KDEN), CO. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight landed safely without further incident.

C-GYGU, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1647 from Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the cruise phase of flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue safety-related duties. The duties were redistributed among the cabin crew in accordance with company policy and procedure. The flight was completed without further incident.

C-GHZL, a Cessna 150 operated by Island Air Flight School & Charters Inc., was on the right base for Runway 08 at Toronto Billy Bishop Airport (CYTZ) and instructed by ATC instructed to pull up, go around and stay south of Runway 08. The pilot of C-GHZL continued on base and was told again by ATC to comply, the pilot turned left towards Porter flight PTR2632, a DHC-8-400 (C-GLQX) on final for Runway 08. ATC ordered PTR2632 to go around. C-GHZL flew through the arrival path for Runway 08 then was instructed by ATC to perform a right turn through the western gap north of Runway 08.

C-GFCH, an Air Canada Rouge A320-214 was operating flight ROU1702 from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, NV, and was in the descent to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON when the flight crew requested to hold due to widespread storms in the Toronto area. The flight crew declared minimum fuel and revised their alternate airport from Detroit Metropolitan Airport (KDTW), MI, to London Airport (CYXU), ON, to extend their hold time, allowing them to cancel the minimum fuel declaration. Another hold was issued due to a new storm cell forming, at which point, the flight declared another minimum fuel and diverted to the alternate CYXU. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYXU with 1.8T of fuel remaining.

C-FLCA, un hélicoptère Robinson modèle R66 exploité par Attitude Hélicoptère Inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) dans le secteur camp 4 à 20 nm au nord-est de la pourvoirie du lac Ternay, Qc avec un pilote et 3 passagers à bord. Lors de l'approche finale pour une zone restreinte, l’hélicoptère a commencé à perdre de l’altitude malgré l’augmentation de la puissance par le pilote. Le pilote a maintenu le contrôle directionnel, mais l’hélicoptère a touché durement le sol principalement avec le patin droit qui s’est brisé, et a rebondi. Le pilote a repris le plein contrôle dans l’effet de sol suite au rebond et est allé se poser à l’endroit visé. La radio balise de repérage (ELT) a été déclenchée et le pilote l’a éteint rapidement car il n’y a eu aucun blessé. L’appareil a subi des dommages aux patins et haubans ainsi qu’à la carlingue.

C-GBHO, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-100, operating as ROU1938 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, was in a descent cleared to 8000 feet. The flight crew were advised by ATC of N565DR, a privately registered Cessna-525C Citation CJ4, that had just departed from CYYZ enroute to Nassau/Lynden Pindling International Airport (MYNN), Bahamas was in a climb and restricted to 7000 feet. The flight crew of C-GBHO had N565DR in sight and noticed a high climb rate. As C-GBHO was levelling off at 8000 feet the flight crew received a TCAS TA alert immediately followed by a TCAS RA. The flight crew climbed to 8400 feet, received a clear of warning alert and was advised by ATC that N565DR had overshot their cleared altitude of 7000 feet by 100 feet. Traffic information was passed to both aircraft. Resolution was followed. Both aircraft complied with ATC instructions and the flights were completed without further incidents.

C-GJFO, a Rockwell International Commander 690 operated by Air Spray (1967) Ltd. as flight ASB192, was conducting a local VFR flight from Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB. When the aircraft was at 2500 feet and 23 nautical miles south of CYTH, a large bird struck the left-side horizontal stabilizer. ASB192 returned to CYTH but experienced control difficulties when full flap was selected for the landing. The pilot performed an overshoot and conducted a second approach with a reduced flap setting. The aircraft landed safely. A visual inspection of the aircraft determined that the horizontal stabilizer sustained significant damage and it will be replaced.

C-FJQL, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211, operating as flight ROU1549, was enroute from Deer Lake Airport (CYDF), NL, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, and was in the descent phase of flight and holding at TADMO due to widespread storms in the Toronto area. After holding for approximately 50 minutes, the flight crew advised ATC that priority handling was required to commence the approach to CYYZ due to the remaining fuel on board the aircraft, or the aircraft would have to divert to an alternate airport. ATC provided the aircraft with a direct routing and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FKOP, a Wisk Air Helicopters Bell 407 was on a flight from Makokibatan Lake Lodge, ON, to Lamon Lake Camp, ON. While landing at Lamon Lake Camp the main rotor wash blew a piece of plywood, which struck and damaged the tail rotor blades. The tail rotor blades were damaged to the extent that the helicopter was not flyable. There were no injuries.

C-GGFJ, un Bombardier DHC-8-402 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7932, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport international Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec 64 passagers et 4 membres d'équipage. À la suite de l’atterrissage sur la piste 06, l’aéronef allait sortir par la voie de circulation A. À l’approche de celle-ci, la vitesse était à environ 40 nœuds et lors que le virage a été tenté, l’avion a continué tout droit pendant un moment. Le pilote a tenté de tourner vers le centre de la piste mais l'avion a continué tout droit. Le pilote a alors tenté d'arrêter l'avion rendu à basse vitesse sans autre option que de terminer dans le gazon. L'avion est sorti dans le gazon à basse vitesse juste après la voie de circulation A. L’avion s’est enlisé et les véhicules d’urgence ont été déployés. Les passagers ont été débarqués rapidement dans le gazon et transportés au terminal. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. L’avion a été remorqué par la suite.

C-GLQZ, a De Havilland DHC-8-400, operating as Porter Airlines flight PTR2280, was on a flight from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. While on approach to CYTZ, the flight crew selected FLAP 5, the FLAP POWER caution light illuminated. The flight crew discontinued the approach and actioned the quick reference handbook with no resolution. The aircraft diverted to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. The crew actioned the "abnormal flap landing" checklist and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed without incident.Maintenance checked for fault codes and a "hydraulic pressure loss" code was indicated. The code was cleared and multiple operational checks were conducted. The fault did not return. As a precaution, maintenance replaced the flap power unit hydraulic pressure switch. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJVE, a Sunwing B737-800 was to operate flight QS1016 from Václav Havel Airport (LKPR), Prague to Vincenzo Bellini Catania Airport (LICC), Italy. At the gate in LKPR, the flight crew started Engine No.1 with an air start unit. After pushback, the flight crew performed the Engine Crossbleed start procedure for engine No.2 which resulted in a hung start. The flight crew aborted the engine start. During a second attempt to start the engine, the ENG OVERHEAT light illuminated. The flight crew completed associated checklists for the condition and discharged a fire bottle in engine No.2. The flight crew declared a MAYDAY and made a passenger announcement. The cabin crew subsequently reported that no signs of fire were observed. Fire services arrived and reported no fire. Passengers were deplaned normally via air stairs.

C-GIQG, a Perimeter Aviation LP Swearingen SA226-TC, was conducting flight PAG02 from St. Theresa Point Airport (CYST), MB, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. When approximately 35 minutes from CYWG, the flight crew noticed both left and right hydraulic annunciator lights illuminated. The flight crew completed the checklist and declared an emergency. A manual gear extension was performed and the crew completed a flapless landing at CYWG. The aircraft subsequently taxied to the apron and a post-flight walk-around revealed hydraulic fluid leaking from the left engine nacelle. The operator's maintenance found a cracked hydraulic line. The line and the left and right hydraulic pumps were replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FYJH, an Airbus A319-114 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1921 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK. After landing Runway 13 at CYQR, C-FYJH was instructed to exit at Taxiway A and hold short of the Runway 26 approach. C-FYJH was subsequently observed crossing the hold short line. C-GTOQ, a Cessna C172 operated by the Regina Flying Club, was conducting a local VFR flight from CYQR and was on a short final for Runway 08. ATC instructed C-GTOQ to pull up and go-around. C-GTOQ conducted the go-around and C-GYJH was subsequently cleared to taxi to the gate without further incident.

C-FYKW, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1903 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. During cruise phase of flight, shortly after reaching TOC, flight crew identified lower than nominal oil level indicating possible oil leak in ENG2 and commenced monitoring of the condition. When ENG2 oil quantity reached 6.0 quarts, the decision was made to initiate diversion to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, while overhead Grand Forks International Airport (KGFK), ND, following consultation with Maintenance Operations Control. ENG2 oil quality levels continued to fall during descent and at approximately 10 000 ft ASL, with 4.0 quarts remaining, and intermittent associated OIL QTY ECAMs, the flight crew elected to execute a precautionary In-Flight Engine Shutdown (IFSD) and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft subsequently carried out full stop landing over MLW (~+1.2T) on CYWG RWY 31 with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) on standby. ARFF conducted general visual inspection noting unassociated water on the belly of the aircraft but no external leaks in the vicinity of ENG2. The aircraft taxied under its own power to the gate where the flight was completed without further incident.

C-GGLM, un hélicoptère AS350 B2 privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis un terrain privé à Mirabel, QC à destination de Launey, QC. L’hélicoptère a décollé à 9h57 et s’est dirigé en direction nord avec un pilote et 2 passagers à bord. Il a atterri à l’aéroport de Mont-Laurier, QC (CSD4) pour ravitailler. Une fois le plein de carburant fait, le pilote a décollé et a poursuivi sa route en longeant la route 117 en direction nord. Les conditions météorologiques dans le secteur nord de Mont-Laurier n’étant pas favorables, le pilote s’est posé à Le Domaine - Sépaq dans la réserve faunique La Vérendrye. L’hélicoptère a redécollé en direction nord moins d'une heure plus tard. Le Centre conjoint de coordination des opérations de sauvetage (JRCC) a été avisé en soirée que l’hélicoptère était porté manquant. Celui-ci a été retrouvé le lendemain matin submergé dans le lac D’Elvert près de la route 117. Aucun des occupants n’a survécu à l’accident.

C-GYFY, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1676 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL. During descent, a flight attendant advised the flight crew of a strong odor described as burning rubber, in the AFT galley. Out of caution, the flight crew elected to declare PAN PAN. The aircraft landed safely and carried out a full stop landing. Aircraft rescue and firefighting conducted an external visual inspection with no faults found. The aircraft subsequently taxied under its own power to the gate.

N828AX, a Boeing 777-2U8 registered to Omni Air International, was conducting flight OAE2408 from Perot Field/Fort Worth Alliance Airport (KAFW) TX, USA, to Istres-Le Tubé Airport (LFMI), FRA.
