Approximately 163 nm SE of Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, while cruising at flight level 330, the aircraft encountered an area of severe turbulence and began experiencing significant oscillations in airspeed and uncontrollable altitude changes. The turbulence lasted for approximately 6 seconds. The flight crew, in conjunction with operations, determined the safest course of action was to divert to CYHZ and have the aircraft inspected. The aircraft landed without further incident. There were no reported injuries to anyone on board.Post flight maintenance inspections revealed no damage to the aircraft.

C-GJZS, a Jazz CRJ900 was operating flight JZA725 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Dulles International Airport (KIAD), VA. During descent, the crew was informed that they had 7750 lbs of fuel on board. Due to weather and air traffic control reroute, they needed to change their alternate airport from Pittsburgh International Airport (KPIT), PA, to Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (KDCA), VA, which was closer given their current position. However, dispatch advised the crew that KDCA was under a ground stop due to thunderstorms and provided the fuel numbers for the alternate change to KDCA as requested by the crew. The crew diverted to KDCA due to further ATC holdings and reroutes, and they declared a fuel emergency with ATC to prioritize the landing. The flight landed safely without any incident. No adverse passenger reactions were observed. The aircraft landed with 4770 lbs of fuel on board.

C-FZHG, a privately registered Piper PA-31 Navajo operated by Airborne Energy Solutions Inc. was conducting a round robin instrument flight rules flight from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Hinton/Entrance Aerodrome (CEE4), AB, and back to CYYC with only the pilot on board. The plan was to conduct the flight without refueling in CEE4. Prior to departure from CEE4, the pilot determined there was sufficient fuel for the return flight to CYYC. While in cruise, with the left engine being supplied by the left outboard tank, the pilot observed the left engine fuel pressure start to fluctuate, and the engine operation became erratic. The pilot then selected the left engine to run on the left inboard fuel tank. Concerned about the fuel quantity in the left-wing fuel tanks, the pilot elected to cross feed the left engine from the right-side fuel system. During the final approach into CYYC the right engine stopped running. The pilot secured the right engine, feathered the propeller, declared a Mayday with ATS and elected to continue the approach. Two to three minutes later, the left engine stopped operating, and the pilot proceeded to perform a forced approach onto a golf course located directly south of the approach end for Runway 35R. The aircraft came to a rest approximately 1/2 nm south of the threshold for Runway 35R. The pilot received minor injuries; however, the aircraft was substantially damaged. There was no post-accident fire. CYYC aircraft rescue and firefighting, the CYYC airport authority and the Calgary Police Services attended the scene.On site post-accident examination of the aircraft found the left-hand fuel selector in the outboard position, the right-hand fuel selector in the off position and the cross-feed valve in the off (normal) position. The aircraft was subsequently removed from the golf course and transported to a secure location for further investigation. The investigation found that there was no fuel remaining in the left inboard, left outboard and left nacelle fuel tanks. The right nacelle tank was empty, however approximately 24 USG were recovered from the right inboard, and approximately 29 USG were recovered from the right outboard fuel tanks.

C-GKQF, a Dehavilland DHC-8-400 operated by Porter Airlines Inc., was conducting flight PTR2617 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Timmins Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON. While cruising at FL250, the crew received a master warning and CABIN PRESS warning. The crew noted the cabin altitude was increasing and initiated a decent to 12 000 feet, donned their oxygen masks, actioned the appropriate checklist, and declared PAN PAN. As the aircraft descended through 17 000 feet, the CABIN PRESS light extinguished as the cabin had begun to re-pressurize. The aircraft landed without further incident.While troubleshooting, maintenance discovered that the three-position (AUTO/MAN/DUMP) pressurization control switch was in the manual (MAN) position. Prior to the occurrence flight, maintenance had replaced the pilot's windshield, which required them to conduct a pressurization check using the MAN mode for pressurization control. The switch had not been returned to the AUTO position prior to flight, and its correct position (AUTO) had not been verified during pre-flight checklists.

C-IEUW, un Quad City Challenger II (équipé de flotteurs amphibies) en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local depuis le lac Bécancour situé à côté de l’aérodrome de Thetford Mines, QC (CSM3) avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Alors que l'aéronef était en vol de croisière, le moteur (Rotax 582) s’est arrêté. Le pilote a effectué un atterrissage d’urgence dans une forêt et lors de l’impact avec les arbres, l’aéronef a subi des dommages importants aux ailes, au fuselage et aux flotteurs. Un des occupants a subi des blessures mineures.

C-GXAJ, a Cargojet B767-300, was operating flight CJT1801 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Narita International Airport (RJAA), Japan. During cruise, a "fuel disagree" EICAS displayed. Intermittent calculated fuel and total fuel difference of 4000 lbs. The crew declared a PAN PAN for routing priority. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GWCT, an Airbus AS350-B2 helicopter operated by West Coast Helicopters Maintenance and Contracting Ltd., was conducting passenger and equipment transportation operations from the Port McNeill Aerodrome (CAT5), BC. After delivering a group of passengers, the aircraft commenced external load operations with only the pilot on board.When the aircraft was reported overdue for another crew transfer, the operator diverted another helicopter in the area to search. C-GWCT was found to have impacted terrain near the equipment transfer location. The Joint Rescue Coordination Center was contacted and subsequently dispatched a rescue helicopter to the site, where they determined the pilot had sustained fatal injuries. The aircraft was destroyed and there was no post-impact fire.

C-GOLC, a Harbour Air Limited De Havilland DHC-2 MK.I (Beaver) floatplane departed Ganges Water Aerodrome (CAX6), BC, on flight HR5221, under visual flight rules, to Victoria Harbour Water Aerodrome (CYWH), BC, with 1 pilot and 4 passengers on board. During the approach to CYWH, the aircraft flaps would not extend. The pilot could not resolve the issue and declared an emergency as per company procedures. The aircraft was successfully landed without flaps.  Maintenance could not duplicate the fault. The hydraulic flap system was bled and the aircraft was returned to service. The aircraft then departed CYWH on the return flight to CAX6 with the pilot and 3 passengers on board. During the approach to CAX6, the aircraft flaps would not extend and the aircraft was again successfully landed without flaps. No emergency was declared on this occasion. The operator obtained a ferry permit and the aircraft was relocated to Vancouver International Water Aerodrome (CAM9), BC, for further maintenance.The flap system ratchet valve was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FQWA, a Beech 1900D operated by Wasaya Airways Limited, was conducting flight WSG1633 from Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON, to Muskrat Dam Airport (CZMD), ON. At 52 nautical miles north of CYXL, during the climb to cruise altitude, the gear unsafe light illuminated. The crew tried cycling the landing gear, but the gear did not come down. The crew declared an emergency and requested to return to CYXL. The crew then contacted company maintenance, manually extended the gear, and did a low approach to visually confirm 3 gears down. The aircraft subsequently landed safely in CYXL with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby. The operator's maintenance towed the aircraft off the runway. There was no damage to the aircraft. There were no injuries.

C-GTSJ, an Air Transat A330-243 was operating flight TSC691 from Athens International Airport "Eleftherios Venizelos" (LGAV), Greece to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During cruise, the crew received "AUTO FLT FM 1+ 2" fault message on ECAM. A PAN PAN was declared and the crew elected to return to LGAV with hand flying and no auto thrust. The crew conducted an overweight landing and aircraft rescue and firefighting inspected the brakes. The aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.

C-GEVI, a privately registered Valentin Taifun 17E powered glider was conducting a local flight, under visual flight rules out of Vancouver/Boundary Bay Airport (CZBB), BC. After engine start, the aircraft was taxied from the apron towards Runway 13 to do a run up. Upon completion of the runup, the aircraft was taxied towards the hold short line for Runway 13. Prior to reaching the hold short line, the tower cleared the aircraft for takeoff. The pilot applied power and continued onto the runway while completing some remaining pre-takeoff checklist items. Rolling on to the runway, and with the aircraft ready, the pilot applied full power. The aircraft then veered 45 degrees to the right while it accelerated. The aircraft left the paved surface of the runway with the engine operating at full power. It struck tall grass and came to a sudden stop facing the opposite direction of the takeoff roll. The pilot shutdown the engine and secured the aircraft before exiting with the passenger. There were no reported injuries.The aircraft received minor damage to the propeller, landing gear, and belly skins. An evaluation of repairs is ongoing.

C-GIKY, a Cessna 172 operated by Integrated Sensing & Surveillance Inc. (ISSINC), was conducting a flight from Lloydminster Airport (CYLL), AB, to conduct some survey work and then proceed to Kindersley Regional Aerodrome (CYKY), SK, with 2 souls on board. After finishing the survey work, the pilot noticed that a storm had developed between their position and CYKY. The pilot proceeded east to avoid the cell. Checking the weather report, the pilot determined that the winds favored Runway 17 and proceeded to join a left base for Runway 17. When established on final approach, rain started adhering to the windshield and made it difficult for the pilot to see the runway. The pilot then decided to cross overhead to join a left hand downwind for Runway 26 instead. At this point the storm was approaching from the north. The pilot turned base and tried to slow down to the approach speed and set full flaps. The pilot ended up high and fast and floated quite far in the flare; touching down approximately 2/3rds of the way down the runway. The pilot then retracted the flaps and tried to stop the aircraft as quickly as possible without locking the brakes. The aircraft overran the end of Runway 26 by approximately 20 feet. The pilot then turned the aircraft around and taxied back to the apron, shut down the aircraft, and inspected it for damage. There was no damage. There were no injuries.

C-FMDN, a Sunwest Aviation Ltd. Gulfstream G150 was operating flight CNK9 from Kalispell Glacier Park International Airport (KGPI), MT, to Sacramento International Airport (KSMF), CA. During climb, the crew declared an emergency due to a flap issue and elected to return to KGPI. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GWWD, an ATR 42-300 operated by Transwest Air (dba Rise Air) as flight RS422 from La Ronge/Barber Field Airport (CYVC), SK, to Cigar Lake Airport (CJW7), SK, was on descent for the RNAV Runway 17 approach. Approximately 3 NM SE of CJW7, as the aircraft was heading towards MEPSO, the east T-Fix for the RNAV Runway 17 approach, and descending through approximately 10500', a TCAS target appeared about 1200' below at 1-2 o'clock position within approximately 2 NM. The TCAS alerted with a traffic advisory (TA) alert followed a few seconds later by a TCAS resolution advisory (RA) which instructed the crew to climb. The crew established the aircraft into a climb and about 300-400' of altitude gain later, the TCAS announced clear of traffic. There was no visual or radio contact with the traffic.

C-FTFT, a Beech B100 operated by FLYGTA Inc., departed Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, with 2 crew and 1 check pilot on board. The flight was to be conducted in the vicinity of Lake Simcoe Regional Aerodrome (CYLS), ON, and was to be a PPC check flight for the left seat pilot. During the majority of the check flight, the check pilot was seated on a divan behind the pilots so that he could observe the flight crew and flight instruments by leaning into the cockpit area, but during the takeoff and landings he would sit on a forward-facing seat at the rear of the aircraft where he could wear a seatbelt. From this position, he listened to the crew and issued instructions through the intercom system using his headset.The second approach, which was an RNAV approach to Runway 28 at CYLS, included a simulated engine failure, and was planned to continue to a full stop landing. The approach was proceeding normally, and the check pilot went to sit in the back of the aircraft once the crew had become established on their final approach path. Although the before landing checklist was conducted, the landing gear was not extended during the approach, and the propellers contacted the runway during the landing flare, after which the engine nacelles and the rear fuselage contacted the runway. The aircraft slid to a stop on the runway approximately 2500 feet after the first propeller strike.Shortly after coming to a stop, the crew observed smoke and an electrical smell coming from the area behind the left-hand edge of the instrument panel. The crew shut down the aircraft and used an onboard fire extinguisher in an attempt to prevent a fire, but the smoke continued and increased in intensity. All 3 occupants exited the aircraft and were uninjured. Within a few minutes, flames became visible inside the aircraft. The local fire department arrived and doused the fire before it spread to the wings; although the entire upper fuselage and aircraft interior was consumed by fire and the aircraft was destroyed. The cause of the fire has not been determined.

C-GWJF, a Boeing 737-700 operated by WestJet Airlines, was conducting flight WJA120 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB with 6 crew and 132 passengers. A cabin crew member became unable to perform their duties due to a medical issue. They did not occupy the assigned jump seat for landing and their duties were reassigned to the remaining cabin crew members. The aircraft landed in CYYC without further incident. The cabin crew member was released to their own care.

C-FNRP, a Rockwell Aero Commander 690C, operated by Buffalo Airways, was conducting a positioning flight as Bird Dog 104 from Inuvik Airport (CYEV), NT, to Fort Simpson Airport (CYFS), NT, with the pilot and one passenger onboard. Approximately 24 nm northeast of Norman Wells Airport (CYVQ), NT, the pilot observed smoke in the cockpit. The pilot turned off the generators and electrical system but could see and smell smoke continuing to enter the cockpit. The pilot completed the appropriate checklist, temporarily turned electrical power back on, declared PAN PAN with ATS and elected to divert to CYVQ where an uneventful landing was completed. Aircraft rescue and firefighting attended the aircraft; however, no smoke or flames were observed.Subsequent inspection by aircraft maintenance determined that the air cycle machine for the environmental/pressurization system had failed. The air cycle machine was deferred, and the aircraft continued to CYFS.

C-GRDD, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-6-100 operated by North-Wright Airways was conducting flight 286 from Norman Wells, NT (CYVQ) to Coleville Lake, NT, (CYVL) with 2 flight crew and 3 passengers onboard. Approximately 27 minutes into the flight, the flight crew received a low oil pressure warning on the right engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-20). The flight crew performed the applicable QRH procedure and company SOPs and completed an intentional shut down of the right engine. The flight crew elected to return to CYVQ and while en route, declared a PAN PAN. Upon arrival at CYVQ, an uneventful single engine landing was completed.Subsequent investigation by company maintenance determined that the engine oil dipstick for the right engine was not secured and allowed the engine oil to escape. The engine was inspected and serviced, ground runs were performed, and no further anomalies were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTCY, an Airbus A321 operated by Air Transat A T Inc., was conducting flight TSC186 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Punta Cana International Airport (MDCP), DR. Shortly after takeoff, the cabin crew reported a burning electrical smell in the cabin. The flight crew declared an emergency and requested a return to CYYZ. The aircraft landed uneventfully and stopped on the runway to be inspected by emergency vehicles before taxiing to their gate.Maintenance replaced an oven in the galley, as well as the LAV/Galley extract fan, and an overweight landing inspection was completed before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJYI, an Air Canada A220-300 was operating flight ACA595 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Houston George Bush Intercontinental Airport (KIAH), TX. During cruise, the flight crew received an EICAS brake ON message. The flight crew completed quick reference handbook checklist and spoke to MOC and dispatch. The flight continued to KIAH, where a PAN PAN was declared. The EICAS message cleared, the flight landed without further incident and aircraft rescue and firefighting followed the aircraft to the gate.

C-GUJZ, a Jazz Aviation Dash 8-400 was operating flight JZA651 from Portland International Airport (KPDX), OR, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During descent, the crew received a FADEC warning message and shut down the #1 engine as a precaution. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed safely without further incident and taxied to the gate.

N810DN, a Boeing 737-900 operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL563 from Anchorage/Ted Stevens International Airport (PANC), USA to Minneapolis-St Paul International/Wold-Chamberlain Airport (KMSP), USA. While cruising at flight level (FL) 330, approximately 50 nautical miles (NM) west of Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, the crew declared an emergency due to a cracked windshield and requested a descent to 10 000 feet. The crew initially leveled the aircraft at FL200 and after discussion with their dispatch, the crew elected to continue to KMSP at FL310.

C-GZWF, un Cessna 337H exploité par Sasair Inc., effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Deer Lake, NL (CYDF) à destination de Sydney-J.A. Douglas McCurdy, NE (CYQY) avec 1 pilote et 3 passagères à bord. L’aéronef a décollé de CYDF vers 13h30 derrière un autre aéronef de la compagnie qui se dirigeait aussi vers CYQY. Après avoir parcouru 37 milles marins en direction sud-ouest, C-GZWF a modifié sa trajectoire de vol pour voler à basse altitude dans une vallée. L’aéronef est entré en collision avec le terrain ascendant au bout de la vallée. L’aéronef a été détruit et aucun feu après impact ne s’est déclaré. La radiobalise de détresse s’est déclenchée et le pilote du second aéronef a immédiatement contacté CYDF pour rapporter l’accident. Le pilote et 2 passagères ont été gravement blessés et une passagère a subi des blessures mortelles.

C-FHAA, a Harbour Air Limited De Havilland DHC3T (Turbo Single Otter) seaplane departed Vancouver Harbour Water Aerodrome (CYHC), BC, on a charter flight to a lodge on the Westcoast of Vancouver Island, under visual flight rules, with only the pilot on board. During cruise, approximately 20 nautical miles west-northwest of the Sproat Lake Water Aerodrome (CAA9), BC, the pilot observed a sudden and uncommanded rise in engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-34) temperature and power. Manipulation of the power lever did not change the engine parameters. The aircraft was turned eastbound to remain within gliding distance of water and entered a climb to maintain an airspeed below the maximum operating speed. The pilot communicated the difficulties with Harbour Air dispatch and contacted the Comox Terminal air traffic controller to get clearance to enter their airspace. Once over a suitable landing area, the engine was shut down as a precaution and the pilot executed a forced approach at CAA9. There were no injuries. The aircraft was not damaged and was towed to a dock for evaluation. Company maintenance reviewed the engine data log. The engine data revealed that the engine was operating beyond its tolerances, and it would need to be removed and shipped to an overhaul facility. The cause may have been associated with the fuel control unit. Repairs are currently underway.

C-GNME, a Yellowhead Helicopters Limited Airbus Helicopters AS 350-B2, was conducting forestry operations 61 nautical miles northwest of Fort St. John Airport (CYXJ), BC, under visual flight rules, with 1 flight crew member, and 1 passenger on board. While conducting a hover entry with the passenger, the aircraft yawed and dipped to the right. The pilot continued the flight returning to CYXJ. Once on the ground, the pilot conducted an aircraft walk around and observed damage to the tail rotor and grass attached to the vertical stabilizer. There were no injuries. There was minor damage to the helicopter.Maintenance was informed and after completing an inspection of the damaged areas, the tail rotor was removed. The tail rotor was found to have delamination.

N401DZ, an Airbus A330-941 aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL224 from Boston/Logan Intl (KBOS), MA to Paris/Charles de Gaulle Intl (LFPG), France. While taxiing the captain (CAPT) noted discomfort in his eyes and the first officer (FO) detected a slight odour. After takeoff the flight attendants (FA) notified the CAPT of an odour detected mid-cabin and the relief first officer (RFO) was tasked to investigate. The RFO did not notice any odour. Several minutes into the flight the FA notified the CAPT that several FA were ill and that passengers were complaining about the odour. The flight crew carried out the quick reference handbook checklist items for smoke / fumes and recalled the RFO to the cockpit so that the CAPT could assess the cabin. The CAPT assessed the cabin, and at about position 43°02' N, 065°03' W the flight crew coordinated with ATS to return to KBOS. The overweight checklist was carried out and the aircraft landed at KBOS without further incident. The aircraft was met at the gate by emergency medical technicians and the CAPT, FO, and five FA were transported to the hospital. All were released after medical evaluation. Maintenance personnel inspected both engines and the auxiliary power unit for oil leaks and conducted engine run tests to isolate bleed air sources. No odours were detected. The forward recirculation filters were replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJLJ, un Wheeler Express CT de construction amateur en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue à partir de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) avec seulement le pilote à bord. À quelques pieds du sol après le décollage, le pilote a perdu la maitrise de l’aéronef et a percuté la surface de la piste avec une assiette à piquer. Le pilote n’a subi aucune blessure et l’aéronef a subi des dommages importants.

C-FGRM, un DH8A exploité par Air Creebec sous l’indicatif CRQ5873, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Éléonore, QC (CEL8) à destination de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) avec 30 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’avion était en étape d’approche finale, une mise en drapeau imprévue de l’hélice du moteur gauche est survenue. L’équipage a fermé le moteur et a poursuivi l'approche et l’atterrissage sur la piste 22 sans encombre.

C-GRJZ, un Raytheon B300 (King Air 350) exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif AIE570M, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) à destination de Puvirnituq, QC (CYPX) avec seulement 2 pilotes à bord. Peu après le décollage, l'hélice du moteur numéro 2 s'est mise en drapeau sans être commandée. Le moteur numéro 2 a été coupé en vol et une urgence a été déclarée. L'appareil est revenu se poser sans encombre à son point de départ. Le câble de commande et la valve bêta du moteur droit ont été trouvés désajustés. Le système a été ajusté selon le manuel de maintenance et l'avion remis en service conditionnellement à un essai en vol.

C-GSPW, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE704 effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) avec 5 membres d'équipage et 70 passagers à bord. Environ une heure après le départ, une indication de basse quantité du système hydraulique A a été constaté. L'équipage a décidé de revenir vers CYUL par mesure de précaution. Une urgence a été déclarée (Pan Pan) avec l'unité de contrôle aérien et l'appareil est revenu se poser sans encombre. Une inspection a révélé une fuite hydraulique dans la région du nez de l'appareil.

N832AA un Boeing 787-9 opéré par American Airlines sous l'indicatif AAL160 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Chicago O’Hare, États-Unis (KORD) à destination de l’aéroport international d’Athènes en Grèce (LGAV). Environ 2 heures après le décollage, alors que AAL160 était dans l'espace aérien canadien, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence médicale concernant un des membres d'équipage. AAL160 s'est redirigé vers l'aéroport Boston Logan Intl, Boston, MA, États-Unis (KBOS) où l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre.

An unregistered (previously registered in the United States as N13RR) Golden Circle Air, T Bird II ultralight was allegedly stolen and subsequently crashed approximately 6 nm ESE of the Grand Prairie Airport (CYQU), AB. The pilot fled on foot after the accident and was not detained by RCMP responding to the site at the time of the occurrence. There was substantial damage to the ultralight.

C-FRYJ, a privately registered Cessna 210E departed Williams Lake Airport (CYWL), BC, on a local maintenance test flight, under visual flight rules, with the pilot and a maintenance engineer on board. Shortly after takeoff, the gear was selected up but the gear up light did not illuminate. Visual inspection confirmed that the left main landing gear was still down. The landing gear handle was cycled but there was no change to the landing gear configuration. They used the emergency hand pump to manually extend the landing gear and that made no change either. The pilot and the maintenance engineer then spent approximately one hour troubleshooting the issue. Despite varied attempts, the left main gear remained extended, with the right main and the nose gear retracted. The pilot then contacted the CYWL Flight Service Station and declared an emergency. First responders were contacted and were present when the aircraft arrived. The pilot landed on Runway 30 with only the left main landing gear extended. The aircraft came to rest on the runway and both occupants egressed with no injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.The aircraft was recovered to a hangar and the extent of the damage will be assessed.

C-GMPY, a RCMP Pilatus PC-12/45 was operating from Edmonton International (CYEG), AB to Fox Creek (CED4), AB. C-GSWX, a Sunwest Aviation Beech 1900D, was operating as flight CNK99 from Edmonton International (CYEG), AB to Calgary International (CYYC), AB. GSWX had been cleared to take off approximately 34 seconds after GMPY, both from Runway 20. During the climb out separation was reduced to 2.8 nautical miles when 3 nautical miles is required.  Tower provided instructions to both aircraft in order to regain the required separation; there was no risk of collision.

C-FXYK, a WestJet Boeing 737-8 was operating as WJA436 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While WJA436 was on the takeoff roll from Runway 30, the Edmonton tower controller cleared the WestJet Boeing 737-8CT (C-FLSF) operating as WJA1547 from Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport (KMSP), MN, to CYEG, to land on Runway 30. A loss of separation occurred when WJA1547 touched down on Runway 30 while WJA436 was still in their takeoff run..

C-FJOU, un Airbus A321-211 exploité par Air Canada Rouge effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC à destination de l'aéroport de Miami, Floride, É-U (KMIA). Au moment de rentrer le train d'atterrissage après le décollage, l'équipage on eu un message ''L/G not Uplocked'' du système d'indication électronique du poste de pilotage (ECAM). Après une tentative infructueuse de réinitialisation du train, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence et est revenu se poser à CYUL où l'aéronef était attendu par l'unité de de sauvetage et de lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). Le personnel de maintenance a remplacé un relais, une valve et un roulement de porte. L'inspection après un atterrissage en surpoids n'a révélé aucune anomalie et l'aéronef a été remis en service. Un rapport de difficultés en service (SDR20240805002) a été soumis à Transports Canada.

C-GJWF un appareil sur flotteurs de construction amateur de type Moose en exploitation privée effectuait un vol depuis le lac Duchamp Qc, (CST6) à destination du réservoir Baskatong, Qc. Le pilote, accompagné de 3 passagers, a effectué un décollage à partir du fond d'une baie en induisant un léger dérapage pour éviter une pointe qui était sur sa trajectoire de montée. En arrivant à la hauteur de la pointe, le pilote a senti l'appareil décrocher sur la gauche suivi d'un contact du flotteur et de l'aile gauche avec la surface de l'eau mettant fin abruptement au décollage. L'appareil s'est ensuite retrouvé submergé. Les occupants ont pu évacuer sécuritairement malgré 2 passagers légèrement blessés. Le pilote était formé pour l'évacuation subaquatique et aurait effectué son exposé de sécurité en cas d'évacuation sous l'eau au début du vol.

C-FSCE, un appareil Cessna R182 effectuait un vol de positionnement selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, Qc (CYRC) à destination de l'aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, Qc (CYMT) avec seulement le pilote à bord. À son altitude croisière à 4500 pieds, environ 15 minutes après le décollage, le pilote a noté une température de sortie des gaz élevée. Croyant avoir trop appauvri il a ajusté la manette de mixture pour enrichir le mélange. Peu après, une forte odeur d'essence a été décelée et le pilote a décidé de se rediriger vers l'aéroport Dolbeau-Saint-Félicien, Qc (CYDO). En descendant à 3500 pieds pour éviter un nuage, le moteur a commencé à perdre de la puissance. Le pilote a continué à enrichir le mélange, mais le moteur a continué de perdre de la puissance. Le pilote a trouvé un endroit pour se poser de force et a coupé complètement le moteur tout juste avant le toucher pour minimiser les dommages. L'appareil s'est renversé peu après avoir touché la surface molle de la tourbière. Le pilote est sorti sans blessure et a contacté les secours. L'appareil a subi des dommages importants et il n'y a pas eu d'incendie.

C-FTKG, a Diamond DA42 operated by Cygnet Aviation Academy LP, was conducting a training flight towards a multi-engine rating, with an instructor and 2 students aboard. The aircraft had departed the Kingston Norman Rogers Airport (CYGK), ON, and proceeded to the training area to conduct various air-work exercises. The final planned exercise was a simulated engine failure followed by a single engine approach and landing. To simulate a failed engine and feathered propeller, the simulated failed engine was set to 15% load; under this condition the landing gear warning horn sounds continuously until the landing gear is selected down, which would normally be done only when landing is assured during a single engine approach and landing. The student completed the pre-landing checks, including the gear/fire test, but the gear handle was not placed in the down position before landing. The aircraft landed on Runway 07 with landing gear in the retracted position, the propellers contacting the runway first approximately 1200 feet along Runway 07 and the aircraft then sliding on its belly before coming to a stop on the runway. The instructor and 2 students exited the aircraft with no injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

N2004L, an unregistered Weatherly 620B aircraft, was performing aerial application 8 miles southeast of Birch Hills Aerodrome (CJD3), SK. While maneuvering at a low altitude, the aircraft stalled, and aircraft control was lost. The aircraft collided with level terrain. The pilot was airlifted to hospital with serious injuries. The aircraft was destroyed.

C-FBDS, a BDK Air Inc. Dassault Mystere Falcon 50 was conducting a flight from Villeneuve, AB (CZVL) to Kelowna, BC (CYLW) with 2 crew members onboard. In the vicinity of Rocky Mountain House, AB (CYRM), the flight crew observed heat and smoke originating from the passenger oxygen control panel located on the flight deck. As the smoke and smell of electrical equipment intensified, the crew requested a diversion to Edmonton Intl., AB (CYEG) and shortly after, declared a MAYDAY due to smoke in the cockpit. The aircraft landed uneventfully approximately 14 minutes later where they were met by aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) and thermal imaging was performed to confirm the aircrafts condition.Subsequent investigation by aircraft maintenance technicians determined that internal lighting in the recently replaced passenger oxygen control panel had shorted and caused some plastic to melt causing the smoke and burning smell observed by the flight crew.

C-GKWA, a Boeing 737-800 operated by WestJet Airlines was conducting flight WJA201 from St. John's International Airport (CYYT), NL, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. During the cruise portion of the flight, one of the cabin crew had a personal medical event and was unable to perform their duties. The individual was released from duty and their responsibilities were distributed among the remaining cabin crew. The flight continued to the intended destination uneventfully.

C-FWZV, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-7, operated by Air Tindi Ltd., was conducting flight TIN802 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Goose Lake Aerodrome (CGS2), NU. During the approach into CGS2, when the flight crew extended the landing gear, they did not receive a nose landing gear down and locked indication. The back up gear indication system indicated that the nose landing was down and locked; however, in the interest of safety, the flight crew elected to return to CYZF. A control tower fly past was performed, and the landing gear looked to be down. An uneventful landing was completed.

C-FUYS, un hélicoptère Robinson modèle R44 II effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis un terrain privé à Shawinigan, Qc à destination d'un terrain privé dans la municipalité de Percé, Qc avec un pilote et 3 passagers à bord. Lors de l'approche finale, une rafale de vent a causé une perte soudaine d'altitude et l'appareil a touché lourdement le sol malgré la correction appliquée au collectif. L'appareil s'est posé et est resté en position debout. Des dommages au train d'atterrissage, au devant de la cabine et le bout des pales ont été constatés. Les occupants n'ont pas été blessés et ont pu débarquer normalement. La radio balise de repérage (ELT) a été déclenchée.

C-GGBF, a DeHavilland DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA257 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to London International Airport (CYXU), ON. Upon departing CYYZ and during the initial flap retraction, the flight crew received a flap power caution message, and the flaps were stuck at position 5. The crew actioned their quick reference handbook and performed a successful reset, after which they retracted the flaps. Following discussion with maintenance and dispatch, the flight continued to CYXU. During approach into CYXU, the flight crew attempted to select flaps, but the flaps did not move. The crew elected to divert back to CYYZ and declared a PAN PAN before conducting an uneventful zero flap landing at CYYZ.

C-FJBO, a Jazz ERJ 170-200 SU, was operating flight JZA629 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Charleston International Airport (KCHS), SC. Approximately 30 minutes into the flight, the crew received a "#2 Hydraulic Low Quantity" EICAS message. The quantity was at 22% and was dropping 2% per minute. The crew actioned the quick reference handbook and decided to return to CYYZ. The crew entered a low-level holding pattern to bring the landing weight within structural limits. A PAN PAN was declared. The passengers were informed of the situation with no adverse reactions. The aircraft landed safely and was towed to the gate from the runway.

C-FZWS, a Westjet B737 Max 8 was operating flight WJA1402 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (KPHX), AZ. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to perform duties. These duties were reassigned to remaining crew. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FOXG, a privately registered Luscombe 8C departed Quamichan Lake Aerodrome (Raven Field (CML2)), BC, on a recreational flight, under visual flight rules, to Vancouver/Boundary Bay Airport (CZBB), BC, with only the pilot on board. On arrival at CZBB, the pilot was cleared to land on Runway 07 and approached on a slant final for a crosswind landing. The initial touchdown resulted in a bounce from which the pilot continued the landing. When the airplane touched down the second time, it veered and began to ground loop. The brakes were applied to prevent a runway side excursion and the airplane subsequently nosed over. The aircraft came to rest inverted on the runway. The pilot secured the airplane and was able to egress without assistance. There were no injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.The aircraft sustained damage to the propeller, windshield, vertical stabilizer, and the left wing tip. First responders righted the aircraft and airport operations personnel towed it clear of the runway. The airplane will be assessed for damage.

C-GGHB, a Cessna 172N, which was privately registered to the Salmon Arm Flying Club, was being flown in the circuit at the Salmon Arm Airport (CZAM), BC, with only the pilot on board. After touching down approximately 750 feet past the threshold of Runway 32, the pilot configured the aircraft and applied full power for the next takeoff. The aircraft lifted off at 55 knots and, when it was climbing through approximately 15 feet above ground level, the pilot felt the aircraft was descending. The pilot reduced power and attempted to land on the remaining runway. The aircraft floated along the runway and then touched down near the end of the runway. Runway 32 has a 1.9% downslope for the first 1400 feet. Brakes were applied but the aircraft departed the end of the runway, crossed the gravel, and entered the brush approximately 270 feet past the end of Runway 32. The aircraft nosed over and came to rest inverted. The pilot egressed and had minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.The aircraft sustained damage to the nose, both wings, and the tail. It was recovered and moved to a hangar where it will be assessed for repairs.

C-GMZN, an Air Canada A220 was operating flight ACA958 from Juan Santamaría International Airport (MROC), Costa Rica, to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. After takeoff, the flight crew experienced a left engine fault advisor above 80 kts. Subsequently, while continuing takeoff, the crew encountered multiple faults and were unable to select altitude or speed around 400-500ft. The flight crew manually flew with ILS guidance, the decision was made to return to MROC. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight landed without further incident.Maintenance findings: removed and replaced adaptive flight display (AFD) mounting fan IAW AMM.

C-FYPO, an Ayres S2R-R1340 operated by Precision West Ag Corp (dba Provincial Airways), was conducting a VFR aerial application flight from Rosetown Aerodrome (CJX4), SK. While spraying a field 27 miles west of CJX4, the aircraft's left landing gear struck a powerline while climbing out of the field. The wire was cut by the left landing gear wire cutter and the pilot maintained control of the aircraft. The aircraft then returned to CJX4 for an uneventful landing.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and it was observed that there was a scratch on the left wing leading edge and minor damage to the left wingtip fairing.

C-FDJZ, a Jazz CRJ900 was operating flight JZA766 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to San Diego International Airport (KSAN), CA. Shortly after touchdown in KSAN, the crew got auxiliary power unit (APU) fire indication. Fire push switch was engaged, and message was reverted back to APU fault caution message, and they carried on and taxied to the gate. The crew said that there was a strong smell of exhaust once they left the runway. Police and fire trucks met them at the gate however the crew did not call for them. It's unknown who did. Passengers were advised of the situation but there was no adverse reaction.

C-GSJB, un Airbus 319-100 exploité par Air Canada Rouge sous l'indicatif ROU1975, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international Jean-Lesage de Québec, QC (CYQB) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Une perte de séparation est survenue alors que ROU1975 avait été demandé de ralentir par le service de circulation aérienne (ATC) pour JZA724, un Embraer ERJ170-200 provenant de l'aéroport international Dulles aux États-Unis (KIAD), qui avait effectué un virage tardif pour une approche visuel sur la piste 24G. ROU1975 a été instruit par l'ATC de remettre les gaz pour interrompre l'approche. La séparation a été réduite à 2.5 miles nautiques (NM) alors que la distance latéral minimum était de 3 NM. Les 2 aéronefs sont attérris sans encombre.

C-GOKG, an Air Transat Airbus 321 was operating flight TSC680 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Humberto Delgado Airport (LPPT), Lisbon, Portugal. After two go-arounds at LPPT, the aircraft was about to reach minimum fuel, so the flight crew decided to divert to Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport (LPPR), Porto, Portugal. The flight crew declared PAN PAN while enroute to LPPR due to fuel situation. The aircraft reached the gate at LPPR with fuel quantity just above minimum fuel reserve.

C-GPGB, an I.M.P. Group Limited Bombardier Challenger 300 on a flight from Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL, to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, declared a PAN PAN emergency due to a nose gear issue. The aircraft was given priority, and aircraft rescue and firefighting services were on standby. The aircraft subsequently landed safely in CYYZ on Runway 33L without further incident.

C-GFKT, a, private registered, LA-4-200 amphibian Lake aircraft was landing on the water at Sawlog Bay, on Lake Huron.  During the landing, shortly after touchdown, the aircraft suddenly veered to the left, and subsequently spun around. There was substantial damage to the aircraft wings, however it stayed upright. There were no injuries.

C-GGMQ, a Jazz Aviation LP DeHavilland DHC-8-402, operating as flight JZA7962, from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, declared an emergency due to smoke in the cockpit while enroute at FL230. The crew elected to divert to Canadian Forces Base Trenton (CYTR), ON. On descent it appeared that the smoke/smell was not getting worse and may even have been dissipating. Upon landing the aircraft was met by fire services. Upon opening the main cabin door, the fire chief advised the cabin crew that it would be best to have the passengers removed from the aircraft. A rapid deplanement was carried out and all passengers exited through the main cabin door. No emergency exits were used.Prior to the start of this flight, the flight crew reportedly had issues with the air conditioning system. The captain had been utilizing the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) bleed to help cool the aircraft. While doing so, he noted a duct temperature spike, that stabilized. After engine start, there was another very brief temperature spike that then again stabilized. During the climb, when the pack control was switched to auto mode, a temp rise was noted. MTC was contacted and the defect was written in the logbook.MTC inspections did not find any fault and a satisfactory test flight was carried out. For the bleed/temp defect, that was cleared with an operational test with no faults found. Four flight legs after this event, on 03 August 2024, on approach when bleeds selected to min, cabin temp became uncomfortably hot, with a spike in duct temp when the APU bleed source was selected. The aircraft was removed from service. MTC action resulted in a bleed air check valve, pack flow control valve and the Environmental Control System (ECS) Electronic Control Unit (ECU) was replaced.

C-IFQU, the Inner Peace Flight Zenair 601 was conducting flight training at La Crête (Jake Fehr Memorial) Aerodrome (CFN5), AB. Onboard was an instructor and a student pilot. After a hard landing during a touch and go at CFN5, another aircraft in the circuit advised the pilot of C-IFQU that the right main landing gear wheel had fallen off. C-IFQU then proceeded to the Fort Vermilion (Wop May Memorial) Aerodrome (CEZ4), AB. At approximately 0327Z, the aircraft touched down on Runway 26 at CEZ4. After touching down, the aircraft veered right and exited the runway onto the grass. The aircraft suffered substantial damage and an aerodrome runway edge light was also damaged. There were no injuries.Post-occurrence inspection: the left main landing gear was found cracked in the same area as the right main landing gear. There was also minor damage to the right wing.

C-GJAN, a Jazz Aviation LP Bombardier CRJ900, was operating as flight JZA851, from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Minneapolis–Saint Paul International Airport (KMSP), MN. During the climb out of CYUL, at FL160, the flight crew received an elevator split caution light. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, actioned the quick reference handbook and elected to return to CYUL. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GEYL, a privately registered Piper PA-28-180 was on a visual flight rules flight from the Olds-Didsbury Aerodrome (CEA3), AB to the Okotoks Air Ranch Airport (CFX2), AB. The pilot was the sole occupant. Upon touchdown on Runway 34, the aircraft bounced and the plane veered left and the aircraft exited the runway onto the grass. During the runway excursion the left wing struck the Alpha Taxiway sign. The leading edge of the left wing had substantial damage and the taxiway sign was also damaged. The pilot, who was uninjured, taxied the aircraft to the apron and shut down.

C-FSEF, un Cessna 525B exploité par Airsprint Inc, effectuait le vol ASP574 selon les règles de vol aux instrument de l'aéroport de Port-Menier, QC (CYPN) à destination de l'aéroport de Rimouski, QC (CYXK) avec seulement 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Durant la montée initiale de CYPN, le voyant d'avertissement ''FUEL BOOST ON L'' s'est allumé dans le poste de pilotage. L'équipage a ensuite continué la montée et déclaré une urgence avec l'unité de contrôle aérien lorsque l'aéronef passait les 8000 pieds. L'équipage a demandé une diversion vers l'aéroport Michel-Pouliot de Gaspé, QC (CYGP) et est remonté à 18 000 pieds. En route pour CYGP, l'équipage a reçu le message ''ENGINE CONTROL R''. La liste de vérification rapide a été actionné et le message s'est éteint. ASP574 s'est ensuite posé sans encombre sur la piste 10 à CYGP. Le service de maintenance a remplacé le ''Fuel Oil Heater'' de gauche qui a été trouvé contaminé par des croissances microbiennes. Les réservoirs ont été inspectés et le ''Fuel Oil Heater'' de droite changé par précaution.

C-GGFJ, a DHC-8-402, operating as Jazz Aviation flight JZA7709, was on the approach at Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON when the cargo door warning illuminated. The aircraft was at an altitude of about 3000 feet and lost pressurization. The flight crew declared an emergency, diverted to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON and landed without further incident. Once on the ground, emergency personnel found the cargo door closed, but the handle had become dislodged from its secured position.

C-FWEP, a Westjet Encore Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Dash 8 Q400 was operating flight WEN3323 from Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During the take-off run at CYLW, the aircraft sustained multiple bird strikes. The crew rejected the takeoff at 65 knots and declared a Mayday with air traffic control. The Mayday was subsequently cancelled and the aircraft taxied clear of the runway under its own power. Airport operations reported dead birds found on the runway. A maintenance inspection found the aircraft undamaged.

C-FDSN, a VIH Helicopters Limited Sikorsky S-61N departed Tatelkuz Ranch, BC, on a flight under visual flight rules to Vanderhoof Aerodrome (CAU4), BC, with 2 flight crew members on board. While in cruise flight, the No. 1 engine chip light illuminated. An emergency checklist was performed, followed by a crew initiated shut down of the No. 1 engine (General Electric, CT58-140-2). The flight continued to CAU4 without further incident. Prior to landing at CAU4, the No. 1 engine was restarted to supply additional power while landing the aircraft. A post flight maintenance examination discovered a sliver of metal on one engine chip detector. The aircraft was ground run, test flown, and re-examined, with no further issues found. The aircraft was subsequently returned to service.

C-GPZS, un Cessna A185E sur flotteurs amphibie en exploitation privé effectuait un vol à vue depuis le Lac St-Charles à Saint-Charles-de-Bellechasse, QC à destination de l'aéroport de Dolbeau-St-Félicien, QC (CYDO) avec le pilote et un passager à bord. Lors de l'approche à CYDO lorsque l'appareil était à une altitude d' environ 1200 pieds, le pilote a ressenti une perte de puissance moteur et a été incapable de remettre la puissance. Le pilote à ensuite tenté un atterrissage forcé. L'aéronef est entré en contact avec le sol à approximativement 1000 pieds du seuil de la piste 29 et a été lourdement endommagé. Le pilote n'a pas été blessé et le passager a subi des blessures mineures. L'aéronef s'est immobilisé sur le côté droit et du carburant s'égouttait de l'évent de l'aile. Environ 10 gallons de carburant ont été récupérés de l'aile droite et l'aile gauche était vide. Le selecteur de carburant était à la position ''Both'' et le contenant du drain du filtre à carburant avant était vide lorsque vérifié.

C-GUCT, un Cessna A185F exploité par le Collège d'enseignement général et professionnel de Chicoutimi, effectuait un vol de formation local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Chicoutimi - Saint-Honoré, QC (CYRC) avec 2 élèves pilotes et 1 instructeur à bord. Une panne moteur est survenue alors que l'aéronef était en approche base gauche pour la piste 12 à une hauteur d'environ 600 pieds. L'instructeur a repris les commandes d'un des élèves pilotes à ce moment et a exécuté les procédures de pannes moteur sans réponse du moteur. L'instructeur a alors effectué un appel d'urgence avec le service de circulation aérienne et a avisé les élèves pilotes de prendre la position de sécurité pour un atterrissage forcé dans les arbres. L'instructeur a fait une ouverture complète des volets et a posé l'aéronef dans les arbres où il s'est immobilisé dans une position inclinée vers la droite à environ 15 pieds du sol. Les 3 occupants n'ont pas été blessés et ont pu sortir par eux-mêmes. L'appareil a subis des dommages importants. Un des bouchons du réservoir d'essence a été trouvé ouvert et environ 5 gallons d'essence ont pu être récupéré des réservoirs de l'aéronef. Un essai moteur a été effectué une fois l'aéronef récupéré et le moteur a été en mesure de démarrer normalement.

C-FFHP, a Conair Group Incorporated De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Dash 8 Q400 was operating flight FGD549 under instrument flight rules from Penticton Airport (CYYF), BC, to Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC. While climbing through 13 000 feet above sea level, both aircraft alternating current (AC) electrical generators tripped offline after the crew activated the aircraft propeller heating systems. A Pan Pan was declared with air traffic control, and the crew performed the applicable checklist from the aircraft quick reference handbook. Power to the AC generators was subsequently restored and the aircraft landed without further incident at CYXX.A post-flight maintenance inspection discovered an electrical short within the wiring harness of the propeller heater system. The wiring was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FHPX, a privately registered Cessna 170B planned to depart the Laslui Meadow airstrip (57° 02' 53” N, 127° 35' 49” W), BC, on a recreational flight, under visual flight rules, to the Grafton Airstrip (54° 00' 49” N, 122° 58' 13” W), BC, with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the takeoff roll, a downdraft was encountered, and the takeoff was aborted. As the aircraft rolled out, a shrub was struck with the right landing gear. The aircraft was inspected, and modifications made allowing the plane to be flown out the following day on a ferry permit. There were no injuries. The aircraft had substantial damage.The right landing gear box suffered structural damage. The aircraft will be dismantled and trailered to a repair facility.

C-FPPQ, a privately registered Cessna 170A was on a visual flight rules flight from the Swift Current Airport (CYYN), SK, to the High River/Foothills Regional Airport (CEN4), AB. On board was the pilot and 1 passenger. During the landing roll on Runway 25 at CEN4, an unexpected sudden crosswind from the south was encountered. The aircraft veered left and exited the runway (approximately 30-45 degrees of the runway heading) onto the grass. As the aircraft slowed, it veered further left. As this happened, the right landing gear separated from the aircraft causing the right wing to strike the ground, bending the right wing strut and causing damage to the leading edge near the right wing cap.

C-GPDT, a privately registered, amateur built, Coot A Amphibian departed the Merritt Aerodrome (CAD5), BC, for a local recreational flight, under visual flight rules, with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. After an approximate 20-minute flight, the aircraft was returning to CAD5 for a full stop landing. As the pilot turned onto final for Runway 21, the left wing separated from the aircraft. The aircraft subsequently pitched nose down and descended into terrain. Both occupants were fatally injured. There was no ELT signal as the ELT was significantly damaged during the impact. The aircraft was destroyed.TSB investigators deployed to the accident site and located the left wing, mostly intact, laying in a grassy area 330m east of the main wreckage location. Numerous parts were retrieved for further evaluation however, not all the left wing attach parts were accounted for in the wreckage or in the surrounding area.The investigation discovered that approximately 27 flight hours before the accident, the aircraft had been damaged in an incident while attempting to depart a lake. The damage was mostly to the keel and the tail section. The aircraft was repaired by the owner.After an analysis of the recovered parts was completed, it could not be determined what caused the wing to depart in-flight.

C-FJZL, un Bombardier CRJ900 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JAZ850 et C-GBIJ, un A319-114 exploité par Air Canada Rouge sous l’indicatif ROU1569 effectuaient leur vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, tous les deux à destination de l’aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Les 2 aéronefs étaient guidés au radar par le contrôleur de la circulation aérienne pour intercepter l’approche de la piste 06R. Un autre aéronef exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l’indicatif JAZ858 était aussi en rapprochement. Au moment de donner une instruction, le contrôleur s’est trompé dans l’indicatif d’un des aéronefs de Jazz. Il en a résulté une perte d’espacement entre JAZ850 qui était à une altitude de 4000 pieds et ROU1569 qui était à une altitude de 3300 pieds. L’espacement horizontal a été réduit à 2.1 NM et l’espacement vertical à 700 pieds. Les espacements horizontal et vertical minimaux devant être respectés sont de 3 NM et 1000 pieds. Les 2 aéronefs ont atterri sans encombre.

C-FKFR, a privately registered PA-22-160 equipped with floats was reported to have been damaged during a landing at Lillabelle in Cochrane, Ontario. Afterwards, the aircraft was found parked on land at the seaplane base and appeared to have sustained substantial damage.

N50LQ, a private US registered Cessna 560, was landing on runway 03 at Wawa (CYXZ), ON. The runway is 4420 feet in length and has a displaced threshold of 689 feet at the end of runway 03. Upon touchdown the flight crew began moderate braking and increased to heavy braking nearing the end of the runway. Both main landing gear tires blew, the aircraft skidded to a stop and came to rest at the end of the runway.

C-GHPB, a privately registered Cessna 182M, equipped with floats, was landing on the water at the Arnprior Water Aerodrome (CNB5), ON. During the landing, one of the floats dug in, the pilot lost control of the aircraft, and the right wing struck the water surface. The aircraft remained upright, but the wing was substantially damaged. There were no injuries to the two occupants.

N830NW, an Airbus A330-302 aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was enroute from Amsterdam Schiphol (EHAM), Netherlands, to Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport (KDTW), MI. When the aircraft was approximately 135 NM NW of Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL, the crew noted that the #1 engine oil quantity and pressure indications had begun to decrease. Subsequently, the flight crew received an electronic centralized aircraft monitor (ECAM) indication for low oil pressure. They then completed the associated ECAM action items and shut down the engine. Gander ACC was contacted, and the crew declared an emergency then requested and received clearance to divert to CYYR.  The aircraft landed safely in CYYR at 1741 UTC.  Maintenance discovered the presence of an oil leak around the accessory section. On further investigation they noted that the starter mount had broken into several pieces. There was also damage present on two oil lines and to the engine accessory case. Maintenance is assessing the damage to determine next steps in order to return the aircraft to service.

C-FCUR, a privately registered amateur built Lancair Legacy RG aircraft, departed Oshkosh/Wittman Regional (KOSH), USA, for Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. On approach to Runway 13 at CYWG, as aircraft were landing ahead of C-FCUR, the tower requested that C-FCUR land on the numbers to maintain separation. The pilot was looking outside for traffic and the aircraft landed with the gear retracted. There were no injuries to the pilot or passenger. Damaged was limited to the propeller, the belly fuel tank, and the ventral fin. Aircraft rescue and firefighting did respond and CYWG was closed for approximately 1 hour while the aircraft was removed.

C-FIBW, a Westjet B737-7CT was operating as flight WJA1579 from Detroit Metropolitan Wayne Country Airport (KDTW), MI, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During departure the aircraft struck a bird and the flight crew declared an emergency. The aircraft returned to KDTW where it landed without further incident.

C-FCAE, a Cargojet B767 was operating flight CJT1801 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Narita International Airport (RJAA), Japan. During cruise, the crew received a "Cabin Hi Altitude” indication on the EICAS followed by a Master warning. The cabin altitude was approximately above 10 000 feet and was climbing at 1000-1500 feet/min. The crew followed the quick reference handbook (QRH) memory items after donning oxygen masks. The cabin altitude was still climbing, the "Man Mode” was selected however, there were no reposts for approximately 20 seconds (the valve was not moving and was in 50% position). At this time, the cabin altitude was close to 13 000 feet. The crew sent the emergency message for descend as the cabin altitude was still climbing. Just before initiating the descend, the crew noticed the outflow valve movement and the cabin altitude was slowly descending (with approximately 500 feet/min). Tokyo radio was contacted on HF immediately and cancelled the MAYDAY but requested to descend to FL320 (as a precaution as the valve was closed partially - approximately 3/4). The crew were given the descend clearance about 1 minute after. By then, cabin pressure was steady in descend mode with about 1000 feet/min and was going below 10 000 (still had the Cabin Alt High warning). ATC was advised that cabin pressurization was stable and requested to stay at FL360. After the cabin altitude reached below 8000 feet and the warning message was cleared from the EICAS, the crew performed the QRH for "CABIN AUTO INOP" followed by a phone call to MCC. The cabin pressurization was kept in Manual Mode until landing at RJAA. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FJFH, a privately registered Zenair Zodiac suffered a nose gear collapse while landing on runway 14 in Williston Basin International Airport (KXWA), North Dakota. The two souls on board sustained minor injuries. The extent of the damage to the aircraft is unknown.

C-GCXG, a privately registered Lake 250, modified to a Lake LA-270 Turbo Renegade, amphibious aircraft, on a local flight out of Orillia Rama Regional Aerodrome (CNJ4), ON, crashed while performing a water landing and touch and go at CNJ4. During the touch and go, as power was applied, the right sponson hit the water which induced a left turn and resulted in the right wing tip to contact the water and to overturn the aircraft. The aircraft came to rest inverted in the water and approximately 180 degrees from its original heading. Bystanders reached the aircraft by boat and rescued the pilot who incurred minor injuries.

C-GWYO, a Cessna 172M operated by the Prairie Bible Institute, was conducting a training flight from Three Hills Aerodrome (CEN3), AB. A student pilot was practicing circuits on their second solo flight. On touchdown during the first circuit on Runway 12, the aircraft veered to the right and exited the runway, crossing through the grass and across a taxiway, coming to a stop in a field adjacent to the taxiway. The student pilot exited the aircraft on his own and was uninjured.Inspection of the aircraft by maintenance personnel showed that the aircrafts nose wheel fork had been damaged and 2 bulkheads located below the centre pedestal had buckled during the runway excursion.

OO-ACE, a Boeing 747-412BCF, registered to Challenge Airline BE, was conducting flight CHG533 from Liege Airport (EBLG), Belgium to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, USA. While in cruise flight at FL320, the flight crew noted a pressurization problem, declared an emergency and began a descent. At a lower altitude of FL100, the system was stabilized and the flight continued to destination.Maintenance replaced the right outflow valve actuator and carried out ground tests on packs 1, 2 and 3 and the pack temp controller and zone temp controller systems. The defect could not be reproduced on the ground. It is suspected that the problem is within the zone temp controller and/or pack temp controller and both are scheduled to be replaced.

C-GWRH, a Bell Textron Inc. B407 operated by Capital Helicopters (1995) Inc., was operating in support of geological exploration 115 NM NE of Ross River Aerodrome (CYDM), YT. The morning flight was to drop geologists at several locations. During the third drop off, the helicopter had toed into the mountain to facilitate a hover exit out the left side of the helicopter. Weather conditions were described as excellent with little wind or turbulence. The geologist exited without issue but had difficulty retrieving their bag from the rear left cargo door of the helicopter. The pilot repositioned the helicopter 2 times, moving small distances, to facilitate retrieval of the bag. It was shortly after the last reposition that the main rotor blades contacted a rock face of the mountain. The pilot eased away from the rock face but ensuing vibrations in the helicopter necessitated an immediate landing. The pilot set the helicopter down on a scree rock slope and from there the helicopter slid/tumbled down the slope and in doing so, the main rotor blades severed the tail boom and then detached from the mast. When the helicopter came to rest, partially inverted, the pilot and 2 passengers were able to egress quickly with only minor injuries. The geologist that had exited received a minor cut from flying debris. There was a small fire in the vicinity of the engine area which extinguished on its own. Rescue was facilitated with the use of satellite telephones. The 406 MHz ELT did activate; however, the pilot turned it off once contact was made with the company and the location given.

C-FWCN, a Westjet B737 was operating flight WJA1449 from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, NV, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. During initial climb, the engine #2 overheat light illuminated. Thrust was reduced as per the QRC and QRH, and the light extinguished. A MAYDAY was declared, and the aircraft returned to land in KLAS with reduced thrust. The aircraft landed overweight. Emergency services met the aircraft on the taxiway and confirmed that engine #2 was stable. The aircraft proceeded to the gate under its own power.

C-GJQN, a Sikorsky S61N, was being operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited in support of forest firefighting activities near Conklin, AB. While working a fire 13 NM NW of Conklin (Leismer) Aerodrome (CET2), AB, the flight crew observed an intermittent "compass fail" caution light. During an approach to refill at the water source, the aircraft began to shake laterally. The approach was abandoned and the flight crew diverted to CET2. The shaking went away but then returned with no shaking in the controls. The flight elected to do a precautionary landing in a bog and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed with no issue. The flight crew were retrieved by another helicopter and returned to CET2. Maintenance personal attended the helicopter and discovered a malfunctioning gyro that was providing input into the yaw channel of the automatic flight control system. The yaw channel was disengaged and the helicopter was ferried without issue to CET2 for further troubleshooting.

N520NA, un Gulfstream Aerospace G-1159A exploité par Nasa Langley Research Center sous l’indicatif NASA520, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport international de Bangor, Maine (États-Unis). Alors que NASA520 volait au niveau de vol (FL) 410, l’équipage a demandé de descendre au FL370 puis au FL210. Le contrôleur aérien a autorisé NASA520 à descendre jusqu’au FL290 afin de coordonner la descente avec le contrôleur qui s’occupait du niveau de vol inférieur. Entre-temps, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence en mentionnant avoir un problème avec le système de pressurisation et a amorcé une descente vers le FL210. Le contrôleur aérien a autorisé la descente et l’équipage a contacté le centre de contrôle approprié. L’avion a été observé sur le radar et a effectué un virage en direction de l’espace aérien de Boston d'où il a quitté l’espace aérien canadien.

C-GFCH, an Airbus A320, operating as Air Canada Rouge flight ROU1546, was taking off from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, on a flight to Deer Lake Regional Airport (CYDF), NL, when a vibration was noticed in the nose landing gear. The vibration intensified during rotation and the initial climb but stopped when the landing gear was up and locked. The flight crew discussed the issue with maintenance and because there was no maintenance in CYDF the decision was made to return to CYYZ. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed without further issue.Following the occurrence maintenance found the excessive play in the bearing of right-hand nose wheel. Both nose wheels were replaced and the aircraft was released back into service after the appropriate checks.

C-GYXQ, a Zodiac CH 601 XL, flown by a student pilot, was on a local flight for the purpose of practicing touch and go landings at the Hanover/Saugeen Municipal Airport (CYHS), ON. On the pilots third landing the aircraft touched down harder than expected breaking the bungee cord suspension on the nose gear. As the aircraft slowed down the nose gear collapsed, and the propeller struck the ground causing significant damage.

C-GJXY, an Airbus BD-500-1A11, operating as Air Canada Flight ACA758, received an EICAS 'Hyd 3 low pressure' caution during descent into Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and landed without further issues on Runway 23. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) inspected the aircraft landing and the aircraft taxied to the gate. Maintenance found a crack on the vertical stabilizer hydraulic supply tube.

C-GBIM, an Airbus A319-114, was conducting Air Canada Rouge flight ROU1552 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Fredericton International Airport (CYFC), NB.  After ROU1552 landed at CYFC on Runway 27, they commenced a backtrack to exit Taxiway A as requested by Saint John Radio. At that time, CYFC TWR was closed and C-FNJW, a Diamond DA-20 aircraft registered to CANLink Aviation Inc., was holding short of runway 27 on Taxiway A. During the backtrack, just prior to ROU1552 reaching the intersection of Runways 09/27, Runways 15/33 and Taxiway A, C-FNJW entered Runway 27 and taxied toward ROU1552 along the north edge of the runway. The ROU1552 flight crew stopped the aircraft as it appeared that C-FNJW was intending to taxi under the left wing of ROU1552. The flight crew of ROU1552 intervened on the radio and C-FNJW came to a stop roughly abeam the nose of ROU1552. The pilot of C-FNJW subsequently executed a 180 degree turn and exited the runway. ROU1552 then taxied to the gate where the flight was completed without further incident.

C-GBIJ, an Airbus A319, operating as Air Canada Rouge flight ROU1924, on route from Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, declared an emergency on final approach due to an APU fire discharge indication light in the flight deck and fuel odor in the aft cabin. The aircraft landed without further incident.Following the occurrence, maintenance inspected the aircraft and carried out serviceability tests with no faults detected. Suspected intermittent fault.

C-FNND, a Boeing 777-200, operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA42 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Indira Gandhi International Airport (VIDP), India. While in cruise flight, the flight crew received multiple system related indications. After discussions with maintenance and dispatch, the decision was made to return to their departure point, CYYZ. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and the aircraft safely landing at CYYZ at 18:40 UTC with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by. Maintenance found the ALT gear down dispatch switch not in the normal position. In accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual, the switch was replaced, the switch guard installed and an operational test carried out.

G-VIIB, a Boeing 777-236 aircraft operated by British Airways, was conducting flight BAW298 from Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD), US, to London Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK. During cruise, passengers and crew detected an acrid smell in the vicinity of door 4L. Shortly after, the in-flight entertainment (IFE) system shut down in a row nearby, with reports that the screens were hot to the touch, and faint wisps of smoke were observed above the seats. The crew completed their drills to try to identify the source of fumes. The decision was made to divert to Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL, and the crew declared an emergency. The aircraft completed an overweight landing without further incident.Maintenance found a quad seat electronics box (QSEB) with a strong metallic acrid smell, indicative of a capacitor failure. The QSEB was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSNP, an Airsprint Inc. Cessna 525B (Citation CJ3) departed Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, on flight ASP675 to Fairmont Hot Springs Aerodrome (CYCZ), BC. On landing at CYCZ, the aircraft encountered an unanticipated tailwind and the aircraft touched down more than 1000 feet past the threshold of Runway 16. The crew was unable to stop the aircraft on the remaining runway. The aircraft overran the runway and came to a stop in the runway end safety area (RESA) approximately 100 feet past the end of the pavement. The crew and the passengers egressed with no injuries. The aircraft had minor damage to the nose wheel tire. Maintenance crews successfully moved the aircraft from the RESA to the ramp. The nose wheel was replaced and the aircraft was ferried to the company’s main base where a maintenance inspection found no further damage and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GJZF, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) operated by Jazz Aviation, was conducting flight JZA368 from Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC. Shortly after departure, the flight crew observed caution messages for pitch trim, elevator feel, roll spoiler inboard, rudder control, and No. 1 rudder hydraulics. The crew actioned the quick reference handbook and elected to divert to Prince George (CYXS), BC. A PAN PAN was declared and emergency vehicles placed on standby. The aircraft landed uneventfully and there were no injuries.Company maintenance traced the issue to a faulty electronic flight control unit that had recently been installed. The unit was replaced, and the aircraft was tested then returned to service.

C-FTWJ, a Westjet B737-800 was operating flight WJA9145 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, to L.F. Wade International Airport (TXKF), Bermuda. After takeoff, the flight crew received signs of unreliable airspeed on the captain’s primary flight display (PFD). The flight crew ran the associated non-normal checklists, declared PAN PAN and initiated a return to KEWR. After receiving a momentary stick shaker, the crew then declared Mayday. The First Officer airspeed indications remained reliable. The aircraft landed safely and taxied to the cargo apron under its own power.

C-FEJD, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU, operated by Jazz Aviation LP, as flight JZA690 from Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD), IL to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. While in cruise, the right-hand front windscreen cracked, and flames were observed between the windowpanes. The flight crew requested a descent with Cleveland ATC to 10,000 feet, however the request was declined. As a result, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and diverted to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FCHE, a Bell 205A-1 helicopter being operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd., was performing water bucketing drops at a forest fire located 12 NM south of Snow Lake, MB. The aircraft had previously performed 21 water bucket drops. On the 22nd drop, while slowing to position for the target area, the water bucket released from the cargo hook. The pilot returned to base and the aircraft was inspected. The water bucket fell into an unpopulated area and has not been recovered.The operator's maintenance determined that interference between the electrical cord and the manual release on the hook caused an inadvertent release of the water bucket. The cargo hook was inspected, and no faults were found. The electrical cord was repositioned, and the aircraft continued to perform water drops on the fire with another water bucket.

C-GAUW, a Pipistrel SW128 (Velis Electro) was landing on runway 23 at the Brantford Airport (CYFD), ON with only the pilot on board. The aircraft bounced twice, and the nose-wheel subsequently collapsed. The aircraft came to rest on the runway and sustained substantial damage; there were no injuries.

C-GWBT, a WestJet Boeing 737- 7CT, operated as flight WJA621 departed Ottawa/Macdonald–Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. During the flight, a cabin crew member was injured due to intermittent turbulence. The cabin crew member was unable to perform their assigned duties and was not in their assigned jump-seat for landing. These duties were reassigned to the remaining cabin crew members. EMS was required upon arrival.

C-GOKC, an Airbus A321-27NX, operated by Air Transat A.T. as flight TSC206 departed Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON; shortly afterwards a cabin crew member became ill and was subsequently removed from duties. The remainder of the flight was operated uneventfully.

N662FE, an Airbus A300F4-605R, operated by Federal Express, was conducting flight FDX140 from Memphis International Airport (KMEM), Tennessee, to the Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, with 2 flight crew on board. During the initial stages of the approach during initial flap extension, the flight crew received a SLAT SYS 1+2 FAULT. The flight crew performed the ECAM actions, complied with the quick reference handbook and planned for a slats 0/flap 40 landing. An emergency was declared with ATS and aircraft rescue and firefighting was on standby for the landing.
