The aircraft arrived with no further issues.Maintenance follow up: The right hand wing #3 slat screw jack and the left hand wing #3 and #6 slat screw jacks were serviced. The system was tested and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GITP, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-112, departed Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, destined for Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During the cruise phase of flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue duties. The duties were redistributed among the remaining cabin crew and the flight was completed without further incident.

C-GMPY, a state operated, Government of Canada RCMP Pilatus PC-12/45, was on an IFR flight from Wabasca Aerodrome (CEE5), AB, to the Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, with just the pilot on board. During the climb to cruise altitude, the pilot heard a fluttering noise and after reducing power, the engine began to compressor stall with a resultant loss of torque (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-67B). While trouble shooting the problem the pilot commenced a turn to return to CEE5. With engine temperature increasing, the pilot feathered the propeller. After a short period of time the pilot conducted an inflight relight and the engine returned to normal operation. The pilot continued the climb and proceeded to CYEG where visibilities were VFR. The aircraft arrived in CYEG without further difficulty.

C-GTJB, a privately registered Piper PA46-350P, was conducting an IFR flight from Edmonton/Villeneuve Airport (CZVL), AB, to Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB, with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the rollout after touchdown on Runway 08 in CYMM, the aircraft veered to the right. Despite full left rudder and left brake, the aircraft departed the runway surface. Shortly after departing the paved surface the nose landing gear collapsed and the propeller struck the ground. The pilot and passenger egressed from the main cabin door with no injuries.

C-GEZN, un Airbus 321-211 exploité par Air Transat A.T. Inc. sous l’indicatif TSC821, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport international d’Orlando en Floride aux États-Unis (KMCO) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL). TSC821 était à 3000 pieds en approche finale et interceptait l’axe de la piste 24R. N664AW, un Airbus 320-200 exploité par American Airlines sous l’indicatif AAL1963 était également en approche pour CYUL. AAL1963 a été instruit de maintenir 4000 pieds par l’ATC pour intercepter la piste 24L. Environ 14 NM au nord-est de CYUL, AAL1963 est descendu sous 4000 pieds au moment d’intercepter l’axe de la piste 24L. Ceci a causé une réduction de l’espacement horizontale et verticale entre AAL1963 et TSC821 à 1.1 mille et 600 pieds. L’espacement réglementaire à respecter lorsque 2 aéronefs sont établis en approche sur les axes parallèles des pistes 24L et 24R est de 3 milles et 1000 pieds.

C-GZFU, a privately registered Cessna 188 aircraft departed Arborg Aerodrome (CJU6), MB, for a local aerial application VFR flight. Upon completion of the application, the aircraft returned to CJU6. While turning from base to final approach for Runway 35, there was a loss of control when the aircraft experienced a stall. The aircraft collided into terrain with trees. The pilot received minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FMUB, un Cessna 182 RG exploité par Exact Air Inc., effectuait un vol privé selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Rimouski, QC (CYXK) à destination de Saint-Honoré, QC (CYRC) avec un pilote et 2 passagers à bord. Au premier toucher des roues pour atterrir sur la piste 30, l’aéronef aurait remonté en raison d’une rafale soudaine. Le pilote a manœuvré pour poser l’aéronef qui a rebondi lors du deuxième touché des roues. Le pilote a remis les gaz pour interrompre l’atterrissage, mais l’aéronef a touché les roues une troisième fois au sol et le train d’atterrissage avant a cédé. L’avion a basculé sur le nez, l’hélice a touché le sol et l’avion a poursuivi sa course dans cette position avant de s’immobiliser. Les 3 occupants ont pu évacuer sans difficulté et n’ont subi aucune blessure. La piste 12/30 a été fermée temporairement.

C-FASQ, an Airsprint EMB-545 was operating flight ASP821 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Charleston International Airport (KCHS), SC. During flight, the crew declared a PAN PAN while in Cleveland (ZOB) airspace due to electrical issues. The crew elected to return to CYYZ and landed on runway 23 with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) standing by.

C-IRAY, an Earthstar eGull 2000 basic ultralight, was conducting a local flight out of Weyman Airpark (CCG3), NB. The aircraft was seen doing several turns at low level before rapidly descending into a cornfield. The pilot was fatally injured. The TSB deployed a team to the accident site.

C-FGYS, a McDonnell Douglas A4-N, was being operated by Top Aces Inc. out of Cold Lake/Group Captain R.W. McNair Airport (CYOD), AB. During rollout after landing on RWY31L, while decelerating through 50 knots, the aircraft began to veer to the right. The pilot added more left brake but this had no effect and eventually the left pedal was on the floor. The pilot activated nose wheel steering and continued to use right brake. This worked until about 10 knots ground speed when directional control was lost; no steering and only right brake. The pilot continued to use right brake to slow and the aircraft departed the right side of the runway coming to rest in grass about 150 feet off the runway. There was no damage to the aircraft and the pilot was uninjured.

C-GILZ, an Airbus Helicopters AS350B2, was being operated by West Coast Helicopters on a wild fire 31 NM west of the Slave Lake Airport (CYZH), AB. While translating into forward flight, just after picking a load of water with an external bucket from a beaver pond, the pilot heard the horn and observed the red HYDR warning light with the helicopter entering a left descending turn. The pilot jettisoned the load and turned the hydraulics off. Controllability did not improve and the pilot managed to set the helicopter down into the trees such that it remained mostly upright. The cabin sustained substantial damage and the pilot's seat broke free from the floor during the impact. This allowed an easy egress and he acquired no injuries. The helicopter sustained substantial damage; there was no post-impact fire.

C-GPRO, an Ayres S2R-R1340 equipped with a Walter M601E engine and operated by Precision West Ag Corp (dba Provincial Airways), departed the Rosetown Aerodrome (CJX4), SK, to conduct an aerial application flight of a field near Birsay, SK. After the first application pass of the field, the aircraft collided with the level terrain. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The pilot was fatally injured. There was no post-impact fire and the ELT activated. The TSB deployed to the site.

N264DC, a privately registered Cessna 421C departed Tofino/Long Beach Airport (CYAZ), BC, on a recreational flight under instrument flight rules to Portland International Airport (KPDX), USA, with 1 pilot, and 2 passengers on board. The aircraft departed Runway 16 at approximately 1242 Pacific Daylight Time and experienced a right engine fire shortly after takeoff. The aircraft leveled off at approximately 400 feet above sea level as it performed a left turn to return to the airport. The aircraft impacted terrain on the airport infield between Runway 25 and Taxiway G. Immediately after ground contact, an explosion and post-crash fire engulfed the aircraft. The aircraft came to rest approximately 93 m north of the centerline of Runway 25. Of the 3 people on board, 2 received fatal injuries, while the 3rd was able to evacuate the aircraft via the left rear exit.  The aircraft was consumed by fire and destroyed. There was minimal damage to the environment. The aircraft emergency locator transmitter did not activate. A team of TSB investigators deployed to the occurrence location, and the investigation is ongoing.

C-GEXB, an Air Transat A321 was operating flight TSC715 from Abel Santamaria International Airport (MUSC), Cuba, to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. After take-off the FCM selected the Packs ON, after a few seconds the crew got an ECAM message AIR PACK 2 Fault. The crew actioned the ECAM and tried to put the pack back on, but the same ECAM reappeared a few minutes later therefore the crew left Pack #2 OFF. In cruise, about 100 NM east-southeast of Raleigh-Durham International Airport (KRDU), NC, during a routine fuel check, the crew verified the PRESS page and noticed that the cabin altitude was high, about 7500 feet and that the cabin was climbing at around 100 feet/min. The crew requested lower, but ATC had to give them vectors to descend the flight. In the meantime, the ADV appeared on the ECAM, and the crew noticed that the inlet, extract and outflow valves were closed. The cabin altitude was now passed 9000 feet therefore the crew commenced an emergency descent while declaring a MAYDAY with Washington ATC. The oxygen masks were not donned by the flight crew members nor deployed in the cabin as the cabin altitude never passed 9300 feet.  Once at 10 000 feet ASL the cabin pressurization system was recovered, and the situation downgraded to a PAN PAN. The flight diverted to Dulles International Airport (KIAD), VA.

C-FMKB, a Douglas DC-3T aircraft operated by Kenn Borek Air, departed Resolute Bay (CYRB), NU, on an IFR flight to a decommissioned airport at Rea Point, NU. While on final approach, the aircraft deviated from the centreline of the runway by a wind gust. While attempting to regain the centreline, the aircraft was banked right, then left, which resulted in the left wingtip and outboard section of the aileron making contact with the runway surface. The crew initiated a missed approach and returned to CYRB. Upon landing at CYRB, it was discovered that the left wingtip and outboard section of the left aileron were damaged. The aircraft was removed from service for repair.

D-AALN, a Boeing 777-F operated by Aerologic GmbH, was operating as cargo flight BOX585 from Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport (PANC), Alaska to Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (KCVG), Kentucky, with 3 flight crew on board. While in cruise at FL330, 61 NM SE of Peace River, AB, smoke was observed emanating from captain's aft side window area. The flight crew donned oxygen mask and summoned the relief pilot to assist with procedures. The QRH was actioned and company maintenance was consulted. The smoke dissipated and a decision was made to continue to destination. Company maintenance could not replicate the issue on the ground and troubleshooting continues.

C-GAIS, un DHC-8-102 exploité par Air Creebec inc. sous l'indicatif CRQ921, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Wemindji (CYNC), QC à destination de l'aéroport de Chisasibi (CSU2), QC avec 12 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage à bord. Durant la montée initiale sous 1000 pieds AGL, une indication de fumée dans le compartiment cargo a été affichée dans le poste de pilotage. La montée a été interrompue et l'appareil est revenu se poser sans encombre à CYNC. Le compartiment cargo a été inspecté et aucune trace de feu ou de fumée n’a été détectée. Le système de détection a été réinitialisé, mais l’indication de fumée est restée allumée.

C-FJWE, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Inc. DHC-8-400, was operating as WestJet Encore flight WEN3317 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. During the take-off roll the flight crew rejected the take-off due to a POWERPLANT message on the engine display. The flight crew informed the tower of the rejected take-off and declared an emergency, stopping the aircraft on the runway. The emergency was cancelled, and the aircraft taxied back to the gate. Company maintenance replaced the PEC#2 and completed engine ground runs with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

N858CD, a Cirrus SR22 aircraft, was on a flight from Montréal/St-Hubert Airport (CYHU), QC, and landing at the Rideau Lakes Aerodrome (CRL2). The aircraft touched down on the grass/gravel runway, slightly left of the centerline and began to drift left. The pilot was unable to maintain directional control of the aircraft and it exited the left side of the runway. The aircraft travelled in an arc through some tall grass and collided with some trees. The pilot and passengers were able to egress the aircraft and there were no injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged from the impact with the trees.

C-FAMC, a Fairchild SA227-AC operated by Perimeter Aviation, was en route from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Red Lake Airport (CYRL), ON. At approximately 50 miles northeast of CYWG, the first officer observed a low oil pressure indication on the left engine. The flight crew carried out the emergency checklists and subsequently shutdown the left engine. They declared an emergency and requested a clearance return to CYWG; where they carried out an uneventful landing. The aircraft has been removed from service by the operator's maintenance for inspection.

C-GUAI, un appareil de type De Havilland Dash 8-314 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE881 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Tasiujaq, QC (CYTQ) à destination de l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) avec 3 membres d'équipage. Lors de la montée initiale à la rétraction des roues, la lumière ambre s’est allumée indiquant que la porte de la roue de droite du train principal n'était pas fermée. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée, le train d'atterrissage a été descendu et la lumière rouge indiquant que le train d'atterrissage droit était non sécurisé s'est allumée. L'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence et s’est dirigé vers CYVP. La liste de vérification pour la sortie alternative du train a été complétée et l’avion s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GFBR, a privately registered Antonov AN-2P, was enroute from Greenbank Aerodrome (CNP8), ON, to Haliburton/Stanhope Municipal Aerodrome (CND4), ON. The pilot reported engine issues as oil sprayed on the cockpit window reducing forward visibility. The aircraft returned to CNP8 where the pilot landed by looking out the side window. The aircraft bounced on landing and subsequently skidded off the side of the runway hitting a berm across a drainage ditch. The aircraft came to rest over 100 m from the runway edge. There were 5 persons on board and only minor injuries. There was significant damage to the aircraft.

C-FGKN, an Air Canada A321-211, was operating as flight ACA124 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. After landing at CYYZ, the flight crew felt the aircraft start to shake once on the taxiway. The flight crew stopped on the taxiway for inspection and observed no damage. The flight crew attempted to taxi but the aircraft did not move. Maintenance advised that the #4 brake was seized. The passengers were offloaded and transported by bus and the aircraft was subsequently towed to gate.A post-occurrence maintenance inspection was carried out and found #4 brake damage. The damaged #4 wheel and brakes were replaced as per the AMM and the aircraft was released for service.

An XAG P100 Pro UAV was being used to apply shade paint to a series of greenhouses. Before beginning the application, the site was surveyed, including a physical walkaround, and obstacles were identified, including a tall tower structure adjacent to one of the greenhouses. The route that the UAV was to fly was entered into the software and uploaded to the controller, which would fly the UAV automatically during the application; a significant buffer was programmed around the tower that was identified during the walkaround. The first flight went smoothly, and the first coat was successfully applied to both areas that were to be sprayed. During the second flight, during which a second coat of shade paint would be applied, the UAV began to fly its path normally, and the projected flight path on the controller was identical to that during the initial coat, however the UAV did not avoid the mapped obstruction and flew directly into the tower. The UAV was substantially damaged, there were no injuries to persons on the ground. The operator determined that a software bug was the likely cause of the collision and has changed their procedures to ensure greater clearance from obstacles, and additional time for pilots to intervene in case the UAV deviates from its programmed flight path. The UAV was repaired and returned to service.

C-FMAI, a Boeing 757 operated by Morningstar Air Express Inc., was conducting flight MAL7054 from Montreal/Mirabel International Airport (CYMX), QC, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During final approach for runway 05, the crew encountered an issue with the flaps, and initiated a missed approach. The crew requested that aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) be dispatched to monitor the brake temperatures after their subsequent landing. The flight landed without incident and taxied to the FedEx facility after ARFF inspected the brakes.

C-GXJZ, a DH8D operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA7711 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. Shortly after departure, the flight crew received an indication of low oil pressure on the #1 engine. They actioned the appropriate checklists and elected to shut down the #1 engine, declaring PAN PAN and requesting a return to CYOW. After landing, the aircraft was inspected by aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) before they taxied to their gate. Inspection of the aircraft revealed that there was oil leaking from the #1 engine.

C-FSBV, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA864 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Heathrow Airport (EGLL), United Kingdom. During cruise, the flight crew was advised of a strong burning smell in the mid-galley. They declared a PAN PAN and requested to divert to Gander International Airport (CYQX), NL. The aircraft landed without further incident in CYQX.Maintenance found that the lower R/H recirculating fan had failed. The fan was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GVVZ, a Sunwest Aviation Ltd., Learjet 45, was conducting an IFR flight CNK645 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Churchill Airport (CYYQ), MB. Approximately 30 minutes into the flight at an altitude of FL410, the crew smelled burning wire along with smoke in the cockpit and cabin. The crew donned their oxygen masks and goggles and then actioned the "smoke in the cabin" checklist. Upon investigation, the crew observed that the smoke was more intense in the cabin and suspected it to be coming from under the rear facing seat. They declared an emergency and requested a clearance to return to CYWG. While in the descent to CYWG, it was observed that the smoke in the cabin started reducing and the aircraft landed uneventfully. The aircraft was removed form service pending a maintenance inspection.

C-GHKR, an Airbus A330-343, operated by Air Canada as flight ACA301, was enroute from Montréal–Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, declared an emergency due to a hydraulic issue. The crew elected to return to CYUL, where the aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance found the yellow rudder servo control filter cap loose and the o-ring damaged. A new o-ring was installed on filter cap as per the aircraft maintenance manual (AMM). Leak check carried out satisfactory. It was also noted that hydraulic fluid leaked inside auxiliary power unit (APU) inlet causing a smell. The APU was decontaminated as per the AMM and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GDJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) operated by Jazz Aviation, was conducting flight JZA7730 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Shortly after takeoff, while passing through 600 feet with the autopilot engaged, the crew received an elevator split caution message. The quick reference handbook (QRH) checklist was accomplished and a return to CYXE was initiated.  Due to the possible flight control issue and the overweight landing, the crew requested aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF).  The landing was uneventful. The aircraft stopped on the runway and was met by ARFF and inspected for possible overheated brakes. With no issues identified by ARFF, the aircraft then taxied to the gate.The operator's maintenance initial inspection found no current or historic fault codes and were unable to fault the system.  Operational checks of the elevator control, servo and position indication and were carried out with no faults found. An overweight landing inspection completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GIUR, an Air Nootka Limited Cessna A185F floatplane departed Nootka Island Lodge (49° 37' 26" N, 126° 37' 23" W), BC, for Gold River Water Aerodrome (CAU6), BC, under visual flight rules. On approach, the pilot elected to land on Gold River due to the high wind observed in the Muchalat Inlet. The aircraft touched down near the river mouth in a south-southwest direction. During the landing slide, the aircraft veered towards the right riverbank and the pilot attempted to correct back to the left. Subsequently, the right wing contacted the water. The aircraft came to a stop on the right riverbank and was towed to the nearby company dock. The occupants were checked by emergency health services and there were no reported injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The aircraft will be assessed.

C-GFOF, a Flair Airlines Boeing 737-8 was operating flight FLE7677 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Nevada. On the RNAV VISUAL 19R, a TA was received, traffic was visual and approach continued. At approximately 1100 feet AGL, an RA was received with MONITOR VERTICAL SPEED. The VFR traffic was visual and the rate of descent was arrested to adhere to the TCAS RA. Another VFR traffic TA was received with traffic in sight on short final. The rest of the RNAV visual was completed and aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GNLK, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Nolinord, effectuait le vol NRL251 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Rankin Inlet, NU (CYRT), à destination de l'aéroport Jean Lesage Intl de Québec, QC (CYQB) avec 5 membres d'équipage et 40 passagers à bord. À environ 26 NM au nord de LaTuque, QC (CYLQ), alors que l'aéronef se trouvait à environ 35 000 pi. d'altitude et que l'équipage s'apprêtait à amorcer sa descente vers CYQB, l'aéronef a subi une perte de pressurisation dû à un problème d'alimentation en air provenant du moteur droit. L'équipage a alors déclaré l'état d'urgence (Mayday), initié une descente d'urgence et déclenché le déploiement des masques d'oxygène dans la cabine. L'aéronef a atterri sur la piste 24 de CYQB sans encombre.

C-GXNF, a Kisik Aerial Survey Incorporated Piper PA-23-250 (Aztec) departed Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies Airport (CYXC), BC, on an aerial survey flight under visual flight rules to Vancouver/Boundary Bay Airport (CZBB), BC, with 1 flight crew member and 1 survey equipment operator on board. Approximately 30 minutes after beginning descent from 8500 feet above sea level, the right engine (Avco Lycoming TIO-540-C1A) began to surge. The pilot switched the fuel selector to the inboard fuel tanks, switched the boost pumps on, and enriched the fuel mixture for the engine. The pilot attempted to restart the right engine without success. The pilot declared a PAN PAN urgency and diverted to Pitt Meadows Airport (CYPK), BC, where they landed safely with one engine inoperative. Maintenance inspected the right engine fuel system and performed a ground run on the engine with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service and was re-positioned to CZBB.

C-GDUZ, an Air Canada Boeing 767-38E was operating as flight ACA7260 from Miami International Airport (KMIA), Florida, to El Dorado International Airport (SKBO), Colombia. At approximately 20 000 feet, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to a cabin altitude high warning. The flight crew followed the quick reference handbook procedures and took over in manual mode. The flight landed without further incident. Maintenance replaced the cabin pressure controller.

C-GVFK (serial number E2268), a Conair Group Incorporated BAE Systems (Operations) Limited Avro Series RJ85 planned to depart Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, on flight number FGD564 for firefighting under visual flight rules with 2 flight crew members on board. During the takeoff roll on Runway 27, the crew observed an excessive exhaust gas temperature on the number 4 engine (Avco Lycoming LF-507-1F). The pilot monitoring reduced the thrust setting on the engine, but there was no change. The crew rejected the takeoff and applied the brakes. Once the aircraft came to a stop, the crew noted that the brake temperatures had reached 750 degrees Celsius and declared an emergency with a request for aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) services as a precaution. The aircraft was shut down in the turnaround bay at the west end of the runway and the runway was temporarily closed. Once the brakes cooled sufficiently, the aircraft was towed back to the company tanker base and the runway was reopened. Maintenance replaced the fuel control assembly on the number 4 engine and completed a power verification run. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GZWS, a Westjet operated Boeing 737-800, was operating flight WJA201 from St. John's International Airport (CYYT), NL, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. While in cruise, a cabin crew member experienced a medical issue and was unable to continue with assigned flight duties. Duties were reassigned amongst the other cabin crew members. The flight landed without further incident at CYEG.

C-GEIV, an Air Canada Boeing 737 Max 8 was operating flight ACA196 from Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During cruise the flight crew observed a high engine oil temperature on the #1 engine (CFM Leap - 1B). The flight crew followed the quick reference handbook checklist and completed a precautionary engine shutdown. The flight diverted to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, and a Pan Pan was declared by the crew. Emergency vehicles met the aircraft on arrival and the aircraft subsequently taxied to the gate under its own power. Company maintenance replaced the #1 engine oil pressure temperature sensor and carried out mid-power engine runs with no fault found. An inflight wind milling inspection was carried out. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GCKV, a Thrush Aircraft S2R-H80 operated by Fly'N Dutchman Ag Ltd., was conducting aerial application operations 5.7 nm southwest of Melfort/Miller Field (CJZ3), SK. On an application leg, the aircraft gained altitude to avoid a power line. After clearing the power line, the pilot initiated a descent to resume spraying. The descent was not arrested in time and the aircraft struck the level terrain. The pilot received minor injuries and was transported to hospital. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GAAJ, a CargoJet Airways Ltd. B767 was operating as flight CJT926 from El Dorado International Airport (SKBO), Colombia, to Miami International Airport (KMIA), Florida. After packs off takeoff, the auto control for the pressurization system did not work and the cabin kept climbing. The cabin altitude went above 10 000 feet. Cabin altitude warning was received, and a Pan Pan was declared. The aircraft was leveled off while the checklist was completed. Once in manual mode, the pressurization system was corrected. The Pan Pan was cancelled, and the aircraft was cleared to a higher altitude and back enroute. The aircraft landed at KMIA without further issues.

C-FGYD, a McDonnell Douglas A-4N, operated by Top Aces Inc., was conducting aerial work out of Cold Lake/Group. The pilot observed that both external fuel tanks were not transferring. The pilot completed the DROP TANK TRANSFER FAILURE procedures, which failed to rectify the problem. An emergency was declared, and the pilot proceeded to burn down internal fuel to the maximum landing weight of the aircraft. The aircraft was landed without further incident with 1000 pounds of internal fuel onboard. The aircraft was removed from service to determine the cause of the issue.

C- GRIQ, un Aerospatiale AS350B3 exploité par Helicarrier Inc s'apprêtait à effectuer un vol local à partir du camp Chukotat situé à 50NM au sud de l'aéroport de Salluit, QC (CYZG) selon les règles de vol à vue avec seul un pilote à bord. Après un ravitaillement en carburant provenant de barils entreposés sur place, le pilote a démarré le moteur et après que celui-ci eut été réglé à la position "Flight Idle", le moteur s'est éteint. De l'eau a été trouvé dans le réservoir de carburant de l'aéronef. Des conduites et des filtres de carburant ont aussi été trouvés contaminés d'eau et d'une matière gélatineuse blanchâtre. Le réservoir de carburant de l'aéronef ainsi que le baril de carburant devant servir au ravitaillement avait été vérifié pour de la contamination le matin même et aucune anomalie n'avait été détectée. Selon l'exploitant, une pièce d'équipement servant au ravitaillement pourrait être à l'origine de la contamination.

C-GNZQ, un Piper PA-23-250 Aztec exploité par Les Levés Aeroscan Inc., s'apprêtait à effectuer un vol de convoyage selon les règles de vol à vue de L'aéroport de Magny-Amos, QC (CYEY) à destination de l'aéroport Jean Lesage Intl de Québec, QC (CYQB) avec seul le pilote à bord. Au moment de la course au décollage, le pilote a ressenti une baisse de puissance et a décidé d'interrompre le décollage. L'aéronef s'est finalement immobilisé dans le gravier à quelques mètres au-delà du bout de la piste. L'aéronef n'a pas été endommagé et il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GUTA, un Dornier Alpha Jet Model A exploité par Top Aces Inc, effectuait un vol local sous l'indicatif "Fishbed18" selon les règles de vol à vue à partir de l'aéroport de Bagotville ,QC (CYBG) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors du retour à la base, le train d'atterrissage a été déployé et l'indicateur du cockpit avant n'indiquait aucun voyant vert tandis que celui du cockpit arrière indiquait les 3 voyants vert. Une inspection visuelle a été effectuée depuis un autre aéronef en vol et le train apparaissait déployé et verrouillé. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre.Une inspection subséquente a indiqué que l'interrupteur du mode "Jour/Nuit" du cockpit avant avait été placé en mode "nuit" par inadvertance.

C-FLRD, un Beechcraft A100 exploité par Exact Air sous l’indicatif ET712, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC) à destination de Manic-5, QC (CMN5) avec 5 passagers et 2 pilotes à bord. Lorsque le train d’atterrissage a été baissé à destination, une indication que la roue de nez n’était pas verrouillée est apparue. L’équipage a effectué une diversion à Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) et a fait un survol de la tour à basse altitude afin de faire confirmer que la roue de nez était bien sortie et verrouillé, sans succès. L’équipage a ensuite décidé de se poser à l'aéroport de Bagotville, QC (CYBG) en raison de la disponibilité des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) et a déclaré un état d’urgence. L’avion s’est posé sans encombre. L’inspection après l’envolé a révélé un fil du contacteur de verrouillage train sorti qui était sectionné.

The Jazz Aviation De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400, registration C-GGNF) departed Victoria International (CYYJ), BC, on flight JZA154 under instrument flight rules to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew members, 2 cabin crew members, and 76 passengers on board. On approach to Runway 26L, after the landing gear was selected down, the nose wheel did not indicate in the down and locked position. The flight crew conducted a missed approach and completed the Landing Gear Malfunction and the Alternate Gear Extension checklists. The nose wheel then indicated in the down and locked position. The flight crew declared an emergency with ATC, landed safely on Runway 26L, and taxied to the gate.   Company maintenance found the nose landing gear indication light bulbs burnt out. The bulbs were replaced, and the primary and alternate gear operation checks were carried out. The aircraft was returned to service.

G-XLEC, a British Airways Airbus A380-800 was conducting flight BAW292 from Washington Dulles International Airport (KIAD), VA, to London Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK. During cruise, the flight crew noticed an overpowering scent, described as a strong smell of laundry detergent. Cabin and flight crew was affected by the smell, with reports of dizziness, nausea and headaches. The flight crew actioned the smoke/fire/fumes checklist. The crew declared a PAN PAN and diverted to Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS), MA. The aircraft landed without further incident in KBOS with aircraft rescue and firefighting and paramedics standing by. Upon inspection, it was discovered that the smell came from 5 pallets of fresh scented laundry beads in the cargo hold.

C-GKUK, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-8-402, was being operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight JZA127 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. When the landing gear was selected down on arrival into CYYC, the flight crew observed the right hand main landing gear light flickering between green and red. A missed approach was conducted and the flight received delaying vectors for 42 minutes while the flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and prepared the cabin for an abnormal landing. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and aircraft rescue and firefighting was on standby for the landing. The aircraft landed without issue and taxied to the gate.Company maintenance replaced the connector on right hand main landing gear down lock sensor, completed landing gear function tests and returned the aircraft to service.

A mid-air collision occurred between a L R Helicopters Inc. Bell 212, C-FTLR, and a Namao Flying Club Cessna 172, C-GJJL. C-FTLR was en route from Fort McMurray, AB, to Rocky Mountain House, AB, at an altitude of 3500 feet ASL and on an approximate course of 200°M; only the pilot was on board. C-GJJL was conducting a proficiency training flight with one instructor and a privately licensed pilot on board. They had completed their exercises and were returning to Villeneuve Airport (CZVL), AB, and on a track of 145°M level at 3500 feet ASL.The collision occurred 13 NM northwest of CZVL. The pilot of C-FTLR set down in a farm field shortly after the collision. C-GJJL continued on to CZVL and landed with no issue. The outer portion of the leading edge of the right wing of C-GJJL had contacted the right side of C-FTLR's tail skid/stinger.

C-GJTZ, a Lockheed L188C operated by Air Spray (1967) Ltd., was operating as ASB492 engaged in forest fire suppression operations based out of Loon River Airport (CFS6), AB. While in flight the crew observed that the No. 3 engine had low TIT, no horsepower, low fuel flow and high propeller RPM. The flight crew consulted the QRH and shutdown the No. 3 engine (Allison/Rolls Royce 501-D13) and diverted to Red Deer Regional Airport (CYQF), AB. The flight crew advised ATS of their situation and completed an uneventful 3 engine landing into CYQF.Company maintenance will be replacing the engine and will report to the TSB their findings.

C-GNDO, un DeHavilland DHC-6 série 300 Twin Otter exploité par Air Inuit Ltée, effectuait le vol AIE685 selon les règles de vol à vue de l'aéroport de Kuujjuarapik, QC (CYGW) à destination de l'aéroport de la Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de l'approche pour la piste 31 de CYGL, l'équipage a détecté une fuite hydraulique causant une perte totale de pression hydraulique. L'équipage a ensuite complété les procédures applicables et déclaré un état d'urgence (Pan Pan) avec l'unité de circulation aérienne. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre pour être ensuite remorqué de la piste au hangar. Une inspection subséquente a révélé une fissure dans l'évasement d'une conduite hydraulique.

C-GJYE, un Airbus A220-300 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA2129 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport San Diego Intl. San Diego, CA (KSAN). Alors que l'aéronef se trouvait à 21NM au nord-ouest de CYUL, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison d'un problème système non-spécifié. L'aéronef est alors revenu atterrir sans encombre à CYUL où les véhicules d'urgence avaient été déployés.

C-GMKS, a Boeing 787-9 operated by WestJet, was operating as flight WJA33 from Leonardo da Vinci-Fiumicino Airport (LIRF), Italy to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. After arriving at the gate in CYYC, before deplaning the passengers, the flight crew observed a Brake Temp EICAS message. The brake temperature readings were observed to be trending downwards. The ground crew noticed that the No. 8 tire on the right hand main landing gear was flat and that the brakes were smoking. This information was relayed to the flight crew who in turn requested aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) to the gate. ARFF arrived and put fans on the main wheel assemblies and monitored the situation while the cabin crew conducted a normal deplanement of the passengers.Company maintenance replaced the No.8 brake assembly and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FCJF, a Boeing 757-223, operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd., was operating as flight CJT1574 from Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. In the initial climb, the left and right airspeed indications diverged, with a maximum split of 80 kts. The left airspeed indicator and the standby airspeed indicator stabilized at 230 kts, the right airspeed indicator indicated 310 kts. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency and requested vectors in order to consult checklists for Airspeed Unreliable, Mach/Speed Trim and Rudder Ratio. The crew advised ATC of their intent for a normal landing and did not require response vehicles. The aircraft was given priority handling and returned to CYHM without incident.Post-occurrence maintenance troubleshooting identified a blockage in the line between the right-hand pitot tube and the ADC. The blockage was located and removed, the right-hand pitot tube and ADC were replaced IAW maintenance manuals and the system was ground tested with no faults found. The aircraft defect was rectified, and the aircraft returned to service.Revised 17 July 2024 as per Jean-Pierre

C-GVVZ, a Sunwest Aviation Ltd. Learjet 45 departed the Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, operating as flight CNK645. When on final approach to Runway 33 at CYXE, the flight crew selected the landing gear down and noticed that the nose gear indication was not illuminated "down and locked". The crew tried wiggling the light to see if it might be loose and attempted a LTS test and found the white hash lines (gear unsafe) lights illuminate on the nose gear but again, no green light showing "down and locked". The crew executed a go around but kept the gear selection in the down position. The crew obtained a holding clearance at 5000 feet and proceeded to execute the UNSAFE gear indication checklist from the quick reference handbook (QRH). Upon completing this checklist, the crew noted that they did not have any white hash (advisory indication) but noted the nose steering light was illuminated which is a secondary indication of a "down and locked" nose gear. The crew contacted ATC and requested to do a low approach for the tower controller to inspect visually that the gear was down. The tower controller confirmed that the landing gear appeared that it was down. The crew continued the circuit and on the downwind leg for Runway 33, the tower controller offered ARFF to respond and the crew accepted the offer. CNK645 then landed uneventfully on Runway 33 and taxied off the runway.Once they landed in CYXE, the crew completed a full power down of the aircraft. After powering the aircraft back up, the nose green light was illuminated. Subsequently, the operator's maintenance investigated and found one out of the two bulbs burnt out in the nose gear down and lock annunciator. They replaced all light bulbs in the nose gear down and lock, and gear unsafe annunciator.

C-GSMR, a Dassault Falcon 2000, operated by Skyservice Business Aviation was enroute from Grand Junction Regional Airport (KGJT), Colorado, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Approximately 90 mins prior to landing, the flight crew noticed fluctuations with the hydraulic pressure and quantity on system 2. The crew followed the quick reference handbook (QRH) procedures and continued the flight as per the checklist. The system eventually failed and all hydraulic fluid was lost. The crew elected to turn off the standby pump to prevent burning it out and continued to destination for emergency services, maintenance and a long runway. A PAN PAN emergency was declared with Toronto Centre, given the aircraft had lost air brakes, flaps, emergency slats, emergency parking brake and braking system 2. After a short hold for weather, the aircraft landed at CYYZ as planned without further incident with emergency services standing by. Post flight inspection revealed hydraulic fluid on the outside of the tail and all over the inside of the aft service compartment.

C-FSOU, a DeHavilland DHC-8-311, operated by Summit Air Ltd., was enroute from Ogoki Post Airport (CYKP), ON, to Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON. Approximately 100 nm northeast of CYQT the flight crew started smelling a very faint smell of burning plastic. The smell got stronger and at approximately 40 miles from CYQT the crew started seeing wisps of smoke coming from the dash. The flight crew referred to the quick reference handbook and by the time they donned their oxygen masks the smoke had dissipated. The crew continued to CYQT and landed without incident.A post occurrence maintenance inspection found the righthand aircraft flight control system (AFCS) with multiple burnt diodes on the circuit board. The unit was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

Suite à un changement de piste, l'espacement entre C-GJZS, un Bombardier CRJ 900 exploité par Jazz Aviation sous l'indicatif JZA582 qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County- Detroit, MI (KDTW) à destination de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC. et C-FJZL un autre CRJ 900 exploité par Jazz Aviation en provenance de l'aéroport Philadelphia Intl, Philadelphie, PA (KPHL) a été réduit à 2,6 milles nautiques (NM) et 500 pi alors qu'un espacement de 3 NM et 1000 pi était requis.

C-GERI, an Exploits Valley Air Services (EVAS) Beech 1900D aircraft, was operating as flight EV602 from Gander Intl (CYQX), NL, to Halifax Intl (CYHZ), NS. When the crew selected gear down on approach, the gear did not extend. The crew discontinued the approach, referenced the QRH and completed a manual gear extension. They received confirmation that the gear was down and locked and requested that ARFF be on standby. The aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance determined that the landing gear electric motor had failed. The motor was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKUK, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-8-402, was being operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight JZA8394 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB with 4 crew and 62 passengers on board. When the landing gear was selected down on arrival into CYYC, the flight crew observed an amber light for the main landing gear door and a red light for the right main landing gear. A missed approach was conducted and the flight crew held south of the airport for 45 minutes to consult with company maintenance and complete checklists. A manual landing gear extension was completed and the No. 2 engine was shutdown and feathered for the landing. Passengers were moved to the left side of the aircraft where possible. An emergency was declared and ARFF was put on standby for the landing. JZA8394 landed with no issues and stopped on the runway. Company maintenance installed landing gear safety pins before the flight crew shutdown the No. 1 engine. The aircraft was then towed to the gate.

C-GKQB, a Porter Airlines Dash-8-400 was operating flight POE2342 from Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS), MA, to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. Approximately 15 minutes into cruise flight the pilots heard a loud pop, and the front RH windscreen cracked. The crew completed the appropriate quick reference handbook (QRH) checklist. They declared a MAYDAY with the ATC facility and requested a descent. There was no loss of pressurization. The request for a lower altitude was in accordance with the QRH checklist, which requires they reduce the cabin altitude pressure differential. The crew continued to their intended destination of CYOW.

N657UA, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL934 from Newark Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ to London Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK. During cruise, the pilots received a HYD QTY – L light. After consulting the QRH and maintenance, the crew shut down the left hydraulic system, declared an emergency and requested to return to KEWR. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance found a faulty left hydraulic quantity transmitter. After replacing the transmitter and performing an operational check, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYCV, a DHC-8-314 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines, was conducting flight PVL924 from Deer Lake (CYDF), NL to St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL. During the climbout, the crew noticed a gradual loss of torque on the #2 engine. As the torque continued to drop to 0, they shut down the engine and declared a MAYDAY. The crew returned to CYDF and landed without further incident. ARFF inspected the aircraft on the runway, and the aircraft then taxied to the apron on its own. Maintenance discovered a faulty fuel control unit. The part was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FPVJ, a DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines, was conducting flight PVL2255 from St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. On descent into CYHZ, smoke started filling the flight deck, coming from the first officer’s air vent. As the crew were donning their O2 masks and completing their checklist, the flight attendant advised them of smoke in the cabin.   The crew declared an emergency with ATC. The smoke started to dissipate. The aircraft landed and stopped on the runway where ARFF inspected the aircraft. The aircraft subsequently taxied to the gate without further incident.Maintenance found that the circuit board associated with the recirc fan had overheated. After replacement, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GHLM, an Air Canada Airbus A330-343 operating as flight ACA155 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Climbing through FL340, the flight crew received a cabin altitude ECAM warning. The cabin altitude had exceeded the normal range and was continuing to climb. The crew stopped the climb and levelled off at FL350, completed their memory checklist action items, declared a MAYDAY emergency, set the transponder to 7700, donned their emergency oxygen masks and completed an emergency descent. Upon reaching 10 000 feet, the crew removed their masks, completed the diversion guidance checklist and cancelled the MAYDAY. The aircraft returned to CYYZ and landed on Runway 23 without further incident.

C-GSUJ, an Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Rockwell 690A, was conducting forest fire fighting operations approximately 45 NM NW of the Fort McMurray Airport (CYYM), AB. About 1 hour and 45 minutes into the flight, the pilot observed low oil pressure and fluctuating power indications on the left engine (GARRETT, TPE331-10T-516K). There were no asymmetrical power affects on the aircraft and the engine temperatures remained normal. The pilot decided to return to CYMM and conducted a visual approach for Runway 26. While in the flare the aircraft yawed and rolled fairly abruptly. The pilot brought both power levers to idle and set the aircraft down on the runway. Directional control was difficult and the aircraft departed the right side of the runway and came to rest in the grass. The aircraft was shut down and the pilot and fire attack officer egressed with no issue and no injury. There were no observed damages to the aircraft.Company maintenance found that an O-ring was missing on the oil filter housing for the left engine resulting in a significant oil leak.

C-GJTX, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was operating as flight ROU1705 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Nevada. On RNAV visual approach for runway 19R, a TCAS RA command was received due to helicopters in the vicinity. Flight crew complied with the maintain current descent rate command and landed without further incident. ATC was informed upon landing.

C-GWWD, an ATR 42-300 operated by Transwest Air (dba Rise Air) as flight RS422, was departing from Runway 27 at Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, to Prince Albert/Glass Field Airport (CYPA), SK. After receiving their takeoff clearance from the tower controller, RS422 began the takeoff roll when the flight crew noticed a truck moving at high speed from taxiway B and crossing the runway with a clearance from the ground controller. RS422 rejected the take-off at a low speed without incident and exited the runway. RS422 then received instructions to taxi back to Runway 27 and a second take-off clearance was received. RS422 departed without further incident the second time around and proceeded along its planned route.

C-GKQK, a Porter Airlines EMB 190-400 aircraft operating as flight POE245, was conducting a flight from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON, to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. C-FOOX, a NovaJet Astra SPX aircraft operating as flight NOJ10, was conducting a flight from Moncton Romeo Leblanc Intl (CYQM), NB to CYHZ. Both aircraft were being vectored for Runway 23 in CYHZ. A loss of separation occurred when the aircraft came to within 2.5 NM of each other at the same altitude. Separation was reestablished without further controller action as C-GKQK passed behind C-FOOX. The minimum required separation was 3 NM horizontally and 1000 feet vertically. Both aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FEJP, a Jazz Aviation E175SU was operating flight JZA839 from Raleigh–Durham International Airport (KRDU), NC, to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. After takeoff from KRDU, the landing gear failed to move, and the crew pressed the down lock release red button. The gear went up however they had a landing gear "WEIGHT OF WHEEL" (WoW) system fail message. The crew actioned the QRH and in discussion with maintenance continued to destination. During descent, the crew declared PAN PAN with ATC. The landing gears lowered normally with all three green indications and the landing gear message "WoW" went out. After landing ARFF followed the aircraft to the gate.

C-FGYS, a Top Aces Inc. McDonnell Douglas A-4N, was conducting aerial work out of Cold Lake/Group Captain R.W. McNair (CYOD), AB. When the landing gear was extended on approach to CYOD, the pilot observed an unsafe condition for the nose landing gear. The pilot conducted a missed approach and completed the gear unsafe/gear handle down checklist. A visual inspection was completed by the wingman and the nose landing gear appeared to be down. The pilot declared a PAN PAN and ARFF was placed on standby. The aircraft landed without further issue.Company maintenance determined that a microswitch in the nose landing gear was misaligned.

C-GLQF, a Porter Airlines De Havilland DHC-8-402 was preparing for flight PTR2634 from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, to Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. During the passenger boarding process, the flight crew observed that the aft baggage compartment fire suppressant bottle was indicating low. There was no indication of smoke, fire or fumes. The captain called for the passengers to disembark the aircraft and requested aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) to inspect the aircraft. Upon inspection by ARFF, there was no indication that a fire had occurred.The operator's maintenance inspected the bottle and there were no notable reasons for the depletion of the bottle. The system was deferred under the aircraft's MEL and the aircraft was released to reposition to CYTZ for rectification. On the subsequent repositioning flight, the aircraft pressurization did not function properly and the aircraft returned uneventfully to CYQT. The operator's maintenance subsequently discovered that the primary heat exchanger outlet duct clamps were not secured causing the environmental control system (ECS) bay to overheat. The clamps were subsequently re-secured.

C-GJBG, a Terraquest Ltd., Piper PA-31 was operating flight JGB515 from Madera Municipal Airport (KMAE), California, for a local flight when the engine started to sputter due to low fuel. The aircraft was diverted to the closest runway at Lemoore Naval Airport (KNLC), California, but could not make the runway and slid into a security fence.

N7007R, a privately operated Bell 407 helicopter (serial number 54839) departed a private ranch approximately 5 nautical miles west-southwest of Fairmont Hot Springs Aerodrome (CYCZ), BC, under visual flight rules for a local flight to an unnamed lake with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board and a slung load. On arrival at the lake, the slung load was set onto the ground next to the shoreline and the 100-foot-long line was released from the helicopter belly hook. At approximately 1720 pacific daylight time (PDT), while still in a hover, the aircraft struck trees and the pilot lost directional control. The helicopter collided with forested terrain and the fuselage came to rest on its right side. E-Comm 911 services received a satellite I-phone crash notification and the Garmin Response Center received an SOS from a Garmin inReach device. No signal was received from the onboard Emergency Locator Transmitter (ELT). The Columbia Valley Royal Canadian Mounted Police and the Columbia Valley Search and Rescue team responded and were on scene at approximately 1930 PDT. The helicopter occupants were assessed by a paramedic. The pilot was fatally injured, 1 passenger received minor injuries and 1 passenger was uninjured. The 2 passengers were transported by helicopter to the Invermere Aerodrome (CAA8), BC, and then by ground ambulance to the Invermere and District Hospital for further assessment. The helicopter was destroyed.UPDATED: 10 January 2025

C-GPJJ, a Morningstar Partners Limited (dba Aurora Jet Partners) Bombardier BD100-1A10 (Challenger 350) departed Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, on a positioning flight under instrument flight rules to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. After takeoff, the aircraft experienced a flap system failure indication. The flight crew completed their required checklist procedures and opted to return to CYLW. A PAN PAN was declared as the aircraft would be landing at a higher-than-normal airspeed. The aircraft landed without further incident. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft.After landing, in consultation with maintenance, the flight crew reset the flap failure indication system. The reset cleared the fault and the aircraft returned to service. During the next maintenance check, the flap control unit will be replaced.

C-GONT un Cessna 414A en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC, à destination de l’aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec seulement le pilote à bord. En descente vers la destination à environ 15 miles nautiques au nord-est des installations de CYHU, le pilote a remarqué de la fumée provenant du moteur droit dans le poste de pilotage. En approche finale, la fumée s'est intensifiée et le pilote a alors sécurisé le moteur pour l'atterrissage. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre sur la piste 24 et le pilote n'a pas été blessé ni incommodé. L'inspection mécanique subséquente a révélé la présence d'une fissure près de la base du cylindre numéro 1. Le moteur a été déposé pour réparation.

C-ILWQ, a Fly Products Luna LU0003 powered parachute trike (ultralight), operated by Air Adventure Flight School Ltd., was conducting a discovery flight with one passenger on board at the company's location approximately 6.5 nm NNW of Drayton Valley Industrial Aerodrome (CER3), AB. Shortly after takeoff the ultralight veered left and collided with trees. The passenger received minor injuries. The aircraft was damaged.After the flight it was determined that a pulley was broken in the right brake (a chute flight control) and was not operational.

C-GJIX, a Custom Helicopters Aerospatiale AS350 B-2 helicopter was conducting external load operations from Somerset Island, NU. Shortly after departing with a sling load consisting of 3 barrels of diesel fuel, 1 barrel fell from the 4-barrel sling. The helicopter travelled approximately 2 miles from the departure point when the pilot noticed the missing barrel. The barrel was located near the departure point. The spill was reported and a clean-up was initiated. There were no injuries.

C-FPMR, a Great Slave Helicopters 2018 Ltd., Bell Textron Inc. 212 was operating in support of forest fire suppression activity near Fort Good Hope, NT. Shortly after lift off from the Fort Good Hope Airport (CYGH), NT, the helicopter experienced a separation of one main rotor blade from the head. Shortly thereafter, the remaining rotor blade and head separated from the mast. The helicopter subsequently collided with terrain. The pilot, who was the only occupant, received fatal injuries. There was a post impact fire. The TSB Edmonton office deployed 2 investigators.

C-GLQP, a Porter Airlines, DeHavilland DHC-8-402 (Dash 8) was conducting flight PTR2375 from Ottawa MacDonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Fredericton International Airport (CYFC), NB. During approach to landing phase, the aircraft experienced a hard landing and a tail strike which resulted in the flight crew conducting a low energy go around. Returning to the airport, the flight completed a visual circuit and landed without further incident. The TOUCHED RUNWAY sensor was illuminated, and the flight crew contacted company operations to advise of the occurrence. Ground crew personal discovered that the underside of the fuselage near the rear cargo door was substantially damaged and reported it immediately.The TSB deployed two investigators to gather information and examine the aircraft.

C-GYNG, an AugustaWestland AW139 helicopter, operated by 7506406 Canada Inc., (dba Ornge Global Air), was on an IFR flight from John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, to London International Airport (CYXU), ON, in IMC conditions, when the co-pilot's Primary Flight Display (PFD) failed. The Multifunctional Flight Display (MFD) unit automatically switched to composite mode. Shortly after a smell of smoke was noted in the cockpit. The co-pilot switched off the PFD and the crew followed the quick reference handbook procedures for a failed PFD. The flight continued to destination without further events. A maintenance inspection was conducted, and the PFD was replaced.

C-GYNO, an AugustaWestland AW139, operated by 7506406 Canada Inc., (dba Ornge Global Air) was starting up at the London International Airport (CYXU), ON, for a flight to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, with 2 flight crew members and 3 paramedics on board. All personnel on board noticed smoke in the cabin; the flight crew shut down the helicopter which included the fuel valves and battery off. The smoke immediately stopped after shutdown. Maintenance determined that the smoke was coming from a no smoking advisory sign in the cabin. On the previous flight, the helicopter had encountered heavy rainfall while parked on the ramp and water had penetrated into the sign resulting in a short circuit and smoke. The sign was replaced, and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GKQR, an Embraer ERJ 190-400, operated by Porter Airlines as flight POE177, was on the climb out from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Ottawa Macdonald–Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, when the aircraft encountered moderate turbulence. It was reported to the captain that a flight attendant had received an ankle injury and required medical assistance. Medical assistance was requested upon arrival in CYOW, but while on approach to CYOW, thunderstorm activity precluded a normal arrival and the flight crew decided to divert to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. On arrival at CYUL, paramedics met the aircraft. Crew member received medical care at a nearby hospital.

N1291T, a privately registered Beechcraft B300 was enroute from Bangor International Airport (KBGR) ME, USA to Reykjavik Airport (BIRK), Iceland when the flight crew detected a fuel leak, declared an emergency and requested to divert to Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL. The crew subsequently changed their diversion destination to Gander International Airport (CYQX) NL. The aircraft landed safely at CYQX.

N29124, a Boeing 757-224, operated by United Airlines Inc., was conducting flight UAL317 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, USA, to Dublin International Airport (EIDW), Ireland. While enroute, the flight crew noted that the autopilots and auto throttle were intermittent.  The flight crew made the decision to return to their point of departure. The crew declared an emergency for their landing at KEWR as they expected to land overweight. The flight landed safely.Maintenance personnel, after trouble shooting, replaced the right-hand flight management computer.

C-GDEW, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3182 from Grande Prairie Airport (CYQU), AB, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Shortly after takeoff the flight crew observed a #2 HYD ISO VLV caution light, roll spoiler OUTBD and 10% quantity in the #2 HYD system. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook, returned to CYQU and declared an emergency. The flight landed safely. The aircraft had to be towed back to the gate. Following the flight the maintenance team determined that a hydraulic line was leaking. The line was replaced, the fluid was topped up and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWLK, a Boeing 737-8 aircraft operating as WestJet flight WJA290 was on route from Winnipeg / James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Halifax / Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. When the aircraft was overflying Timmins, Ontario, a cabin crew experienced a medical issue and was not able to continue their duties. The flight crew were advised, and the cabin duties were distributed amongst the remaining flight attendants. Upon landing in CYHZ the flight attendant received medical care.

C-GEHQ, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 Max aircraft was operating flight ACA344 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. In the vicinity of Wawa Aerodrome (CYXZ), ON, the captain's windshield shattered. After the flight crew completed the quick reference handbook checklist procedures, they diverted to Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON, and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed without further incident with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by.

C-GZED, a privately registered Van's RV-14 aircraft, was conducting a visual flight rules (VFR) flight from Sherbrooke Aerodrome (CYSC), QC, to Summerside Aerodrome (CYSU), PE. Upon arrival at CYSU, C-GZED joined the circuit and conducted an approach for Runway 05. Recognizing that the aircraft was positioned too high on the approach, the pilot conducted a go-around to better set-up for a second approach. The second approach was on speed and profile however, the pilot noted that at approximately 30 feet above the runway, more crab was required to maintain the runway centerline. The aircraft touched down on the left side of the runway and the pilot applied full right rudder and brakes in an attempt to regain the runway centerline. The aircraft continued to drift left with the left main wheel contacting the grass along the edge creating more drag, which forced the aircraft off the left side of the runway into the grass. When the aircraft contacted the long grass, the aircraft’s nosewheel buckled backwards and the aircrafts' nose dropped and contacted the ground. The nose landing gear, propeller and engine suffered substantial damage. After the aircraft came to a stop, the pilot exited the aircraft uninjured. The pilot also observed that the wind was favoring Runway 23. Emergency services were contacted and arrived shortly afterwards to provide assistance.

C-GSHI, an AirSask Aviation Limited was operating from Kansas City International Airport (KMCI), Missouri, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the second leg of the day, the aircraft encountered a low oil pressure light indication and master warning on the climb after takeoff from KMCI. Climb was initiated and setup was made for a VFR circuit return. During the climb out, a burning oil smell was experienced throughout the entire cabin, prompting mask donning and engine shutdown. Emergency vehicles were on standby, and aircraft landed without further incident. No external damage was observed by emergency ground crew.

C-FZRM, a WestJet Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight WJA1572 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to George Bush Intercontinental/Houston Airport (KIAH), Texas. During aircraft rotation on takeoff from CYYC, the tail of the aircraft made contact with the runway surface. When the aircraft was established in cruise at FL350, the flight crew consulted with company maintenance and the decision was made to return to CYYC. The flight crew ran the checklist for a tail strike and depressurized the cabin, declared a PAN PAN with air traffic services and requested aircraft rescue and firefighting for the landing. The aircraft completed an uneventful approach and overweight landing.Company maintenance conducted a tail strike inspection and overweight landing inspection with no issues found.

C-FGWT, un McDonnell Douglas TA-4J Skyhawk exploité par Top Aces Inc, effectuait un vol d'entraînement local à partir de l'aéroport de Bagotville, QC (CYBG) avec un instructeur et un élève-pilote à bord. Une trentaine de minutes après le décollage, alors que l'aéronef se trouvait à une quarantaine de milles-marins à l'est de CYBG, le voyant "LOW FUEL" s'est allumé de façon intermittente. L'instructeur a alors demandé à l'élève-pilote de monter à vingt-mille pieds et de revenir directement à CYBG. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et 5 minutes plus tard, le voyant "LOW FUEL" s'est allumé de nouveau. L'équipage a initié une approche RNAV sur la piste 29 où l'aéronef est atterri sans encombre en utilisant le câble d'arrêt.Une inspection subséquente a révélé que le réservoir de carburant externe gauche était encore plein et n'avait pas alimenté le réservoir de l'aile.

C-GOKN, a De Havilland DHC-8-102 operated by Wasaya Airways Limited was conducting  flight WSG8161 on a special flight permit from Sioux Lookout (CYXL) ON. to Thunder Bay (CYQT) ON. The flight was to reposition the aircraft for further troubleshooting after a gear issue on the previous flight (see TSB occurrence A24C0060). During the flight the Weight on Wheels (WOW) light illuminated. The flight crew declared an emergency. The aircraft subsequently landed safely in CYQT with ARFF on standby.The operator's maintenance inspected the right WOW switch and found a rock jammed between the proximity switch and the scissor link. The rock was removed, the proximately switch gaps were checked and cleaned. All checks were completed with no faults found and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOKN, a De Havilland DHC-8-102 operated by Wasaya Airways Limited was conducting flight WSG1679 from Pikangikum Airport (CYPM), ON, to Keewaywin Airport (CPV8), ON. After departing CYPM, the flight crew made a gear up selection and received a "Weight On Wheels" (WOW) illumination. The flight crew continued the climb, reviewed the QRH, contacted ATC and requested a diversion to Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON. WSG1679 declared an emergency and requested for emergency services to stand by in CYXL. The flight crew notified the flight attendant and a cabin briefing was completed. The aircraft landed safety and taxied to the apron. The WOW light extinguished during touchdown or taxi. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and tested the PSEU; however, CYXL did not have the ability to jack the aircraft. The aircraft was ferried to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON, for further troubleshooting.

C-GUAL, a Sunshine Coast Air Cessna 180J floatplane was conducting a flight from Vancouver International Water Aerodrome (CAM9), BC, to Porpoise Bay at Sechelt, BC under visual flight rules. The flight took off eastbound and was cleared for a left turn over the river to do a North Arm departure.  The pilot accepted the departure instructions and once the aircraft reached 500 feet above sea level (ASL), the aircraft, instead of continuing north-northeast, was turned to the northwest. As the aircraft approached the threshold of Runway 26L of Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, the pilot observed a Beech B300 (King Air 300) aircraft (registration C-GRXX) operated by Carson Air Limited that was departing from Runway 08R as flight CRN611. The pilot of the Cessna turned to the east and contacted air traffic control (ATC) for instructions. Vectors were provided to guide the Cessna away from the King Air 300. Both aircraft continued to their destinations without further incident. ATC considered this a risk of collision.In response, Sunshine Coast Air conducted an internal investigation which included reaching out to ATC for clarification on the miscommunication. The guidance obtained was shared with the pilots of Sunshine Coast Air.

C-FQVP un Piper PA20X sur flotteur en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis un camp sur la rivière Aguanish au nord d’Aguanish, Qc à destination d’Aguanish avec le pilote et une passagère à bord. Lors de l’amerrissage par vent de travers, l’aéronef a frappé un cap rocheux. Les personnes à bord ont subi des blessures légères et l’avion a subi des dommages importants.

C-GUAJ, a Cargojet B767-300 was operating flight CJT569 from John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During descent, the crew declared PAN PAN due to hydraulics issue. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-IJKR, un Paramoteur Per Il Volo miniplane en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol de formation solo selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis l’aérodrome de St-Apollinaire, QC (CAA4). Lors du décollage, l’aéronef a commencé à osciller. L’instructeur a prodigué des conseils par radio de réduire la puissance. L’oscillation s’est amplifiée et la pilote a perdu le contrôle en raison de torsions entre la pilote et la voile causant une chute d’environ 40-50 pieds ralentie par la voile. L'appareil a ensuite percuté le sol et la pilote a subi des blessures graves.

C-FWEW, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400 was conducting flight WEN3627 from Portland International Airport (KPDX), Oregon, USA, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the landing on Runway 29 in CYYC, the aircraft touched down with a recorded vertical acceleration of 2.47 g with the longitudinal axis of the aircraft not aligned with the runway track.Company maintenance completed a Phase 2 inspection on the aircraft, and subsequently replaced the right-hand main landing gear assembly due to the side load experienced during the landing.

C-GWEJ, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC8-400 was conducting flight WEN3111 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC. Shortly after departure, the flight crew experienced a #1 engine over torque event. The crew actioned the appropriate quick reference handbook procedure and completed a precautionary inflight shutdown of the #1 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW150A). A MAYDAY was declared, and the flight returned to CYYC where an uneventful landing was completed. The maintenance investigation is ongoing.

C-FWSI, a Boeing 737 operated by WestJet Airlines was conducting flight WJA145 from Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC) to Fort McMurray, AB (CYMM). N103RM, a Cessna T310 was conducting a night VFR forest fire mapping flight southwest of the Fort McMurray Airport, AB (CYMM). During the RNAV Y approach into CYMM, the flight crew of WJA145 was made aware of VFR traffic in the vicinity of CYMM by ATS. The pilot of N103RM was operating outside of the CYMM control zone and monitoring 126.7 MHz. However, ATS was unable to make any radio contact with N103RM on any of the designated frequencies. Approximately 11 nm SW of CYMM, WJA154 took evasive action to avoid traffic by performing a right hand race track pattern before continuing the approach for an uneventful landing in CYMM.Separation was reduced to 2.3 nm laterally and 200' vertically, when 3 nm laterally or 1000' vertically are required.

C-FEYK, a privately registered Stinson 108-3, collided with terrain under unknown circumstances near Bowsman, MB. The aircraft was found substantially damaged in a field and was reported to local emergency services. An individual was found fatally injured outside the aircraft. There were no reported witnesses who had seen the aircraft being operated.TSB investigators deployed and attended the site. Information gathered indicated that the aircraft had impacted the level ground in a left-wing low attitude and that the aircraft subsequently nosed over. The collision with terrain resulted in substantial damage to the aircraft fuselage, wings, landing gear, engine, and propeller. Damage to the engine and propeller was consistent with a collision at a low engine power setting. It was observed that seatbelts had not been worn by its occupant. Fuel samples indicated the aircraft had been fueled with dyed fuel.

C-GLQV, a Porter Airlines Dash 8-400 was operating flight POE2304 from Fredericton International Airport (CYFC), NB, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. The aircraft departed CYFC with FMS #2 under MEL relief. While enroute to the DERDO fix, FMS #1 failed, causing the autopilot to revert to basic mode. The flight crew informed Boston Centre of a dual FMS failure and declared a PAN PAN. Due to convective weather at CYTZ, the crew decided to divert to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GTWE, a Westjet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) departed Prince George Airport, (CYXS), BC, on flight WEN3130 under instrument flight rules to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. C-GGOY, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, on flight JZA272 under instrument flight rules to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC. The crew of WEN3130 descended below their cleared altitude of 8000 feet above sea level (ASL). The separation between the 2 aircraft was reduced to 2.6 miles horizontally and 500 feet vertically when 3 miles and 1000 feet is required. There was no risk of collision.

N522JP, un Beechcraft C90A en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Goose Bay, NL (CYYR) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). À environ 15 mille marins à l’est de CYUL, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence au service de la circulation aérienne due à une défaillance d'indication du niveau de carburant. L'équipage a demandé d’atterrir sur la piste 24L. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployé. L’aéronef a atterri sans encombre.

C-FRSO, a Boeing 787-9 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA020 from Changi Airport (WSSS), Singapore, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC with with 4 flight crew members, 10 cabin crew members, and 280 passengers on board. During the descent to CYVR, while passing through 10 000 feet above sea level (ASL), the flight crew received a fire detection warning message for the left engine. Soon thereafter, while passing through 8000 feet ASL, the crew observed a fire warning message for the left engine (General Electric GENX-1B74/75/P2). The flight crew completed an engine fire drill, shut down the left engine, and declared a PAN PAN with air traffic control. While completing the checklist items, additional fire handle warnings occurred, fire bottles were extinguished, and the flight crew declared a MAYDAY. The flight landed without further incident. Aircraft rescue and firefighting crews met the aircraft on the runway for an inspection, there was no indication of fire. The aircraft taxied to the gate without further incident. Company maintenance inspected the aircraft and carried out a wiring check on the left engine fire warning system. A wiring fault was located and two wiring harnesses were replaced. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FKMG, un Beechcraft B300 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE551, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Kangiqsujuaq, QC (CYKG) à destination de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP). Durant l’approche vers CYVP, les trains d'atterrissage ont été abaissés. La lumières verte du train d’atterrissage principal de gauche ne s'est pas allumée indiquant que ce dernier n’était pas verrouillé. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence (pan pan) au service de contrôle aérien par mesure de précaution. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 31.
