C-GOOO, a Eurocopter (now Airbus Helicopters) AS 350 B2 helicopter, was conducting long lining operations in support of exploratory drilling. The helicopter was temporarily based at the mine site where the operations were taking place, approximately 26nm west of Wawa Airport (CYXZ), Ontario. During the second lift of the day, while flying at approximately 300 feet AGL, the pilot began a gradual descent and soon afterwards felt a strong jolt which caused a change in the attitude of the helicopter. He attempted to regain control of the aircraft, but after a subsequent and more severe jolt, he jettisoned the load, which fell clear of the helicopter onto a wooded area. The helicopter began to yaw to the left and attempts by the pilot to correct this yaw were unsuccessful. The pilot attempted to gain some forward speed to reduce the yaw but did not have enough remaining altitude to complete the maneuver. He made an emergency landing into a wooded area, the main rotor blades contacted trees while the helicopter was still yawing to the left, and the helicopter was destroyed, coming to rest on the lower right side of the fuselage. The pilot received minor injuries and was able to crawl out of the helicopter. Personnel who were waiting to receive the slung load heard the helicopter in distress and the impact with trees, and made their way to the site to assist, arriving approximately an hour after the occurrence. The 406 ELT activated as designed, prompting JRCC to deploy assets to the site. The pilot had a satellite phone and was able to contact the helicopter's owner and relay his coordinates to them. The pilot was airlifted from the site later in the afternoon by JRCC and brought to a nearby hospital, and he was released the following morning. The TSB deployed 2 investigators to the site of the occurrence.

C-FYWX un Cessna 120 sur flotteur en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’hydro-aérodrome du Lac Louise, Qc (CSH8) à destination de Fermont, Qc avec seul le pilote à bord. Lors de la course au décollage sur l’eau miroitante, le pilote a tenté de lever une flotte avant l’autre et une aile a touché l’eau. Le pilote a réussi à revenir au quai avec l’hydravion, mais l’aile de celui-ci a été lourdement endommagée. Le pilote n’a pas été blessé.

C-GITP, an Air Canada Rouge A319 was operating flight ROU1708 from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Nevada, U.S., to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During the cruise phase of the flight, a cabin crew became ill and was unable to perform duties. The duties were redistributed amongst the other crew members and the flight was completed without further incident.

C-FNND, an Air Canada Boeing B777-233LR departed Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, on flight ACA33 under instrument flight rules to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. At approximately 2143 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), during descent through 20 000 feet above sea level, a flight crew member became unwell and was unable to perform their duties. A PAN PAN was declared, and a cabin crew member who held a pilot license occupied the flight crew member's station for the remainder of the flight to perform monitoring duties. The flight landed at CYVR without further incident at approximately 2200 PDT.

C-GJVT, an Air Canada Airbus A320 was operating flight ACA144 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During departure from Runway 35R, the flight crew rejected the takeoff due to crosswinds. The flight crew initiated the rejected takeoff at 132 KIAS and exited the runway under its own power. The aircraft stopped on the taxiway to cool the brakes and advised of a possible blown tire. ARFF was dispatched and inspected the aircraft. No tires were blown; however, the #1 tire had deflated. Upon return to the gate, the aircraft stopped on the apron and had both #1 and #2 tires replaced before taxiing back to the gate. The aircraft was removed from service to have a high energy stop inspection conducted.

C-GLQC, a Porter Airlines DHC-8-402, operating as flight PTR2485 departed from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, and was climbing through approximately 16 000 feet, when a rapid depressurization occurred. The flight crew initiated an emergency descent, declared a PAN PAN, and descended down to 7 000 feet. Attempts to troubleshoot the problem in co-ordination with maintenance were unsuccessful. The flight crew returned to CYTZ and landed safely.

C-GKQI, a Porter Airlines DHC-8-402, operating as flight PTR2719 departed Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. During the initial climb out, the flaps were selected up, however shortly after a "FLAP DRIVE" caution light illuminated. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and consulted with maintenance for troubleshooting, including attempting a flap extension. The “FLAP DRIVE” light extinguished, however the “FLAP POWER” caution light illuminated. The flight crew diverted to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, and declared a PAN PAN; the aircraft landed without further incident on runway 05 with aircraft rescue and fire fighting standing by.

C-GMWJ, a Westjet Boeing B737-7 operating as flight WJA471 departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, under instrument flight rules to Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC. C-GWEJ, a Westjet Encore DeHavilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 operating as flight WEN3115 departed Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, under instrument flight rules to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. A loss of separation occurred after WJA471 was cleared to descend from flight level 380 to flight level 250. WJ471 descended below the cleared altitude of flight level 250 by approximately 500 feet. This created a loss of separation with WEN3115, which was operating at flight level 240. At their closest, the aircraft were separated by 4.4 nautical miles (NM) horizontally and 500 feet vertically. The minimum required separation was 5 NM horizontally and 1000 feet vertically. WJA471 returned to flight level 250, and both aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FGSJ, a Cargojet Airways B767 was operating flight CJT1801 from Narita International Airport (RJAA), Chiba, Japan, to Hangzhou Xiaoshan International Airport (ZSHC), Zhejiang, China. During climb out passing FL310 the crew experienced multiple EICAS messages. After consulting with MCC in an effort to resolve the issue in flight, the decision was made to return to RJAA. The crew declared PAN PAN. The flight was cleared to land and arrived safely. After landing the Standby Inverter was found to be unserviceable. The Standby Inverter was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GSMY, a Selkirk Mountain Helicopters Limited Aerospatiale AS350 B-2 departed the Big Mouth Repeater site, BC, conducting long line operations under visual flight rules to Mica Creek, BC, with one crew member on board. During cruise flight at approximately 2000 feet above ground level, the slung load was unintentionally released. The released load was later recovered. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft or the environment.

C-FHKU, a Kootenay Valley Helicopters Limited Sikorsky S-61N departed Fort Nelson Airport (CYYE), BC, for a local flight to conduct long line operations under visual flight rules, with 2 crew members on board. The crew observed a No. 1 engine fire warning, accompanied by the smell of smoke. The long line was jettisoned, and an auto-rotation was performed from approximately 400 feet above ground level. Upon landing, the aircraft engines were shut down and the fire bottles were discharged, extinguishing the fire. There were no injuries, and the aircraft sustained minor damage.The helicopter was dismantled and transported to a repair facility.

C-GDUA, a privately registered Cessna 441 was operating on an IFR flight from Edmonton/Cooking Lake Aerodrome (CEZ3), AB, to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC. After engine start, the aircraft taxied from the ramp and held short of Runway 28. During taxi, the pilot used reverse power to slow down the taxi, as well as to stop the aircraft at the hold short line at Runway 28. After traffic landed and cleared the runway, C-GDUA entered the runway and back tracked to the left side of the threshold of Runway 28. Left engine power was used to complete the turn to the center line and hold. The pilot completed the before takeoff checklist, applied takeoff power and released the brakes. The takeoff began normally, then while accelerating through 30 KIAS, the aircraft started to veer to the left. The pilot corrected with nose wheel steering, but this became ineffective. The pilot applied mostly right brakes attempting to hold the runway centerline. The power levers were pulled back to the idle position, as the aircraft exited the left side of the runway onto the wet grass. The pilot then moved the condition levers to the first stop. The aircraft collided with a drainage ditch where it came to rest with the nose gear collapsed. The pilot shutdown and secured the engines before exiting the aircraft. The pilot and 1 passenger were uninjured. Aircraft examination and troubleshooting are in progress and the owner of the aircraft will advise TSB of the maintenance findings.

C-FPAE un DeHavilland DHC-8-315 exploité par PAL Airlines ltd. sous l’indicatif PVL847, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Wabush, TN-L (CYWK) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC. Lors du passage du point MAIRE sur l’arrivée, C-FPAE a rencontré de la turbulence de sillage. C-GOFW, un Airbus 330-343 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA813 qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Lisbonne, Portugal (LPPT) à destination de CYUL était 10nm devant et avait passé MAIRE 500 pieds plus haut que C-FPAE. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GDJZ, a Jazz Aviation CRJ900 was operating flight JZA719 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Minneapolis–Saint Paul International Airport (KMSP), Minnesota, U.S. Enroute, LH bleed air duct warning message illuminated. The aircraft lost pressurization. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and advised ATC they required an immediate descent to 10 000 feet. An emergency descent was not carried out, however, the captain advised they descended at a moderate speed. The flight crew donned their mask for 2 minutes until they reached an altitude of 9 900 feet. The passengers advised flight attendants they were getting very warm. The captain then made a passenger announcement to advise of the mechanical issue and why the cabin temperature was increasing, as well as, passed along an updated ETA for KMSP. The aircraft landed without incident.

C-GBZH, a float-equipped De Havilland DHC-2 aircraft operated by Canadian Fly-in Fishing (Red Lake) Ltd. was departing the Chukuni River, ON, on a VFR flight to Thicketwood Lake, ON, with the pilot and four passengers. While climbing out shortly after takeoff, aircraft control was lost and it collided with the shoreline. Two of the passengers received serious injuries. The remaining occupants were medically evaluated at a local hospital and released. One of the seriously injured passengers subsequently died while in hospital. The ELT was activated. The aircraft was destroyed. The TSB deployed and is investigating.

C-GKXA, a Porter Airlines Ltd. Embraer E190-E2 was conducting flight POE670 from San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA, USA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Prior to descent, the crew received multiple EICAS messages related to the failure of a modular avionic unit (MAU), some of which suggested that the aircraft braking may be affected. During their descent into CYYZ, the crew advised ATC of the issue and declared PAN PAN. The flight landed on runway 05 with ARFF standing by, and after a brief delay for brake cooling, they proceeded to their gate. Maintenance inspected the aircraft and determined that the power supply for MAU 3B had failed. This component was replaced before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FLKJ, a Flair Airlines Boeing 737-800 was operating as flight FLE700 from Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. After landing in CYEG, the aircraft was being marshalled to gate 68. The marshalling crew observed that the left wingtip of the aircraft was in close proximity to a parked fuel truck. While marshalling the aircraft in, the gate marshaller lost sight of the left-wing tip and wing tip marshaller. While the left wing was obscured by the aircraft fuselage, the gate marshaller had to rely on signals from the lead marshaller. It was during this time that the left lower winglet collided with the fuel truck. No additional signals to stop were given and the aircraft continued to be marshalled in until the final park signal was given.  Company maintenance removed the lower winglet and installed a blanking plate. The aircraft was dispatched under configuration deviation list (CDL) for continued operations.

C-FXRJ, a Summit Air Ltd. British Aerospace Avro 146 (RJ100) was operating as SUT8073 from Goose Lake Aerodrome (CGS2), NU, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. After departure from CGS2, while climbing through 3000 feet AGL, the aircraft struck a bird and the flight crew heard a bang, followed by the #2 engine (Avco Lycoming LF-507-1F) vibration warning indication on the master warning system panel. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and the #2 engine was shut down and secured. An emergency was declared and the aircraft diverted to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, and landed without further incident.

C-GWBL, a WestJet Boeing 737-800 was operating as WJA172 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. The flight crew requested vectors to final with the Edmonton Terminal controller. The controller cleared WJA172 direct to SUVAT. The aircraft initiated the turn early to the approach before SUVAT. A loss of separation occurred with a WestJet Encore de Havilland DHC-8-402, C-GDEW, operating as WEN3145 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. Separation was reduced to 2.3 miles, where 3.0 miles is required.

C-FCAW, a privately registered Cessna 182P equipped with amphibious floats was operating on a recreational pleasure flight from Edmonton / Cooking Lake Aerodrome (CEZ3), AB, to Fort Smith Airport (CYSM), NT. While enroute the aircraft stopped at Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB, to refuel. After refueling, the aircraft departed for CYSM. Approximately 30 nm SSE of CYSM the engine quit. The pilot declared a MAYDAY emergency and conducted an emergency landing in muskeg. Before coming to a stop, the right wing contacted a tree and damaged the leading edge near the wing tip. The pilot and passenger were uninjured. The flight crew were subsequently rescued by a Parks Canada helicopter. The engine failure was determined to be fuel exhaustion. The fuel quantity uploaded was provided in Litres rather than US Gallons.UPDATED 13 November 2024

C-GYNR, a Nova Scotia Department of Natural Resources and Renewables (DNRR) Airbus H-125 helicopter, was conducting a local flight from the Shubenacadie, NS DNRR heliport (CSU4). The flight had the pilot and 3 passengers on board and was to conduct an inspection of another facility 25 nm south southeast of CSU4. On final approach to the confined area at the facility, the main rotor blades struck a fir tree on the left side of the helicopter. The pilot shut down the helicopter, inspected the main rotor blades, and elected to return the helicopter to CSU4. Subsequent action by maintenance personnel identified the requirement to follow airframe and engine manufacturer special instructions related to the blade strike. This required the removal of main rotor blades, gearbox, various other main rotor components and the removal of the engine. The components will be sent out for evaluation and action as required.

C-GEXE, a privately registered Cessna P210N was operating on a local flight from Ponoka Aerodrome (CEH3), AB. The aircraft was conducting a test flight following a top engine (Teledyne Continental TSIO-520P) overhaul. During the initial climb, while at 80 KIAS, the engine RPM began to decrease. The pilot was unable to maintain altitude and executed an emergency gear-up landing in a farm field approximately 1.5 nm from the runway. The pilot and passenger were uninjured. The aircraft fuselage received substantial damage. The owner will advise TSB of the maintenance findings.

C-FJQH, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1791 from Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), DR, to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During the initial climb phase of flight, after thrust reduction, the flight crew received ENG 1 FIRE warning for approximately 15 seconds. The indication disappeared but was then followed by intermittent indications of ENG 1 FIRE LOOP A FAULT. The flight crew declared MAYDAY, stopped the climb at 3000 feet and began preparations to return to origin. The flight crew subsequently brought the affected engine thrust to idle for the remainder of the flight following which, the indications ceased. The aircraft subsequently carried out a full stop landing at MDPC with ARFF on standby. The aircraft was towed to the gate.

9H-VJE, a VistaJet Ltd. Global Express 6000 (BD-700-1A10) was operating as VJT741 from San Francisco Bay Oakland International Airport (KOAK), USA, to London Luton Airport (EGGW), UK. At approximately 300 nm north of Winnipeg, MB, the crew was alerted by a hydraulic system 2 low quantity (HYD 2 LO QTY) crew alerting system (CAS) message. Whilst going through the electronic checklist (ECL), the crew observed that the hydraulic quantity was dropping steadily. The quick reference handbook (QRH) procedure was followed which suggested monitoring the quantity and pressure. Shortly after, the crew received a hydraulic system 2 low pressure (HYD 2 LO PRESS) CAS message. The QRH procedure for HYD 2 LO pressure was followed. 2B pump was selected on as per the procedure but then the HYD 2 quantity was indicating zero, as was the HYD 2 pressure. The QRH then suggested turning off the 2B pump, review HYD and flight controls (FLT CTRL) synoptic pages, and land at the nearest suitable airport.As Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, was one of the planned en-route diversions airports, the crew checked the weather again and reviewed the performance before declaring a PAN PAN. They requested a diversion with ATC and VJT741 landed safety in CYWG. The aircraft 9H-VJE was then grounded in CYWG for maintenance.

C-FJJZ, a Jazz CRJ900 was operating flight JZA7121 from Sacramento International Airport (KSMF), CA to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. The crew advised dispatch that they had the L FADEC (Full Authority Digital Engine Control) caution message. The crew actioned the QRH checklist and advised dispatch that they will return to KSMF. The crew powered back the engine to idle and was kept at idle for the remainder of the flight. The flight declared a Pan Pan and requested emergency vehicles for their arrival. The flight landed safely with no further issues. There were no passengers on board as this was a positioning flight.

C-GGVI, a privately operated Gulfstream GVI (G650ER), was conducting an IFR flight from Paris/ Le Bourget Airport (LFPB), France, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While in cruise flight at FL450 near 53° 03'N, 061° 22'W, the flight crew noticed rapidly fluctuating engine indications although the engines remained steady. The crew also experienced an autothrottle disconnect and multiple crew alerting system messages. The crew was unable to manipulate the Multi-Function Control and multiple systems went offline including navigational capabilities, which were reduced to heading only. The crew declared PAN PAN and coordinated with ATS to divert to Sept-Îles Airport (CYZV), QC, where a visual approach and landing was made without further incident. A repair team attended the aircraft and after analyzing the available data files, the technicians identified the AIOP1B fault and the TNIC (Timing Network Interface Controller) #2 card as the likely faults. The cards were replaced. The historical fault history databases are also currently being analyzed to pinpoint the root cause of the failures. The aircraft has been returned to service.

N794UA, a Boeing 777-222B aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL915 from Washington/Dulles Intl (KIAD), VA to Paris/Charles de Gaulle Intl (LFPG), France.  While in cruise about 4 hours into the flight (at 46°21' N, 048°01' W) the flight crew received a Reserve Brake Steering EICAS message followed by a Center Hydraulic System Low indication. The flight crew coordinated with ATS for a diversion to Gander Airport (CYQX), NL. As the diversion progressed, the flight crew observed that the center hydraulic quantity continued to decrease and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed at CYQX without further incident. Maintenance personnel identified a hydraulic leak coming from the aft electric hydraulic pump in the right wheel well.

C-GRSA, a Cessna U206G operated by Rocking Star Adventures Ltd. was conducting a sightseeing flight of the Kluane National Park area. During the downwind leg for landing at the Haines Junction Aerodrome (CYHT), YT, the engine (Teledyne Continental IO-520F) suffered a complete loss of power. The pilot attempted to conduct a 180 degree turn to land into wind, during which the aircraft struck the ground in a slight right wing low, flat attitude. The aircraft came to rest upside down on the infield of the runway. First responders extricated all on board from the aircraft and began administering first aid and CPR. The pilot and 4 passengers sustained serious injuries; 1 passenger was fatally injured during the accident.

N241MA, a privately registered Aviat A-1C-180 (Husky) was operating on a cross-country flight from Teslin Aerodrome (CYZW), YT, to Watson Lake Airport (CYQH), YT. Immediately after touchdown in CYQH, the aircraft encountered a gust of wind and began to deviate from the runway track. The right-wing tip contacted the surface of the runway, and the aircraft entered a ground loop. The right main landing collapsed and the propeller contacted the ground. The aircraft came to a rest on the runway. The pilot and passenger were uninjured and egressed from the aircraft. The aircraft was removed from the runway and brought to the tie down area of CYQH.

C-GVDX, un giravion de marque AutoGyro modèle Cavalon en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Baie-Comeau, Qc (CYBC) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, Qc (CYHU) avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Dans les environs des Escoumins, Qc, le pilote a rencontré des conditions météorologiques de vols aux instruments (IMC) et a pris de l'altitude pour tenter d'éviter la météo. Ayant de la difficulté à prendre de l'altitude, le pilote a rapporté voir du givrage sur son rotor principal et a donc amorcé une descente d'urgence. Arrivé à la cime des arbres, l'appareil a décroché et le pilote a perdu la maitrise de celui-ci et percuté le sol. Les occupants ont pu sortir de l'épave et contacter les services d'urgence. Le passager a subi des blessures mineures et a été transporté vers un établissement hospitalier. La balise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s'est déclenchée à l'impact.

C-FDIN, a Slate Falls Air float-equipped de Havilland DHC-2 aircraft was on a VFR flight from Cat Lake, ON, to Sioux Lookout/Pelican Lake Seaplane Base (CKA6), ON. While enroute, approximately 20 nm north of CKA6, engine oil began to leak onto the windshield. Shortly thereafter, the engine (Pratt & Whitney USA R-985-AN-14B) began to shake, the engine cowling became detached, and the engine subsequently failed. The pilot performed a forced landing on Lac Seul, ON. There were no injuries to the pilot and five passengers. The aircraft sustained damage to the cowling and propeller.

C-FKHL, a privately registered float-equipped Cessna 180 aircraft was departing South Gull Lake, ON, on a VFR flight to Cedar Lake, ON. Shortly after takeoff, the aircraft became difficult to control. The aircraft descended into a stand of trees adjacent to the lake. The sole occupant was not injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged. It was reported that there was a thunderstorm in the vicinity.

C-FIJZ, a Jazz Aviation CRJ900 was operating flight JZA768 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to San Diego International Airport (KSAN), CA. While over Oregon, the crew advised dispatch via ACARS, that they were turning back to CYVR after a passenger reported a fuel leak coming from the right-hand side wing fuel cap on take-off. The crew considered it to be an abnormal landing and declared PAN PAN and requested ARFF to be on standby. The aircraft landed safely without any further incident.

C-FFHA, a Harbour Air Limited DHC-2 MK. I Beaver aircraft was conducting a local sightseeing flight from Vancouver Harbour (water aerodrome) (CYHC), BC, with 1 pilot and 5 passengers on board. During the takeoff, the aircraft and a pleasure craft with 1 driver and 7 passengers on board collided. The aircraft and pleasure craft were substantially damaged, and the aircraft began to sink shortly after the collision. The pilot and aircraft passengers were able to egress. The occupants of the aircraft and the vessel were assisted to shore by first responders. Two passengers on the aircraft sustained minor injuries and 2 passengers on the pleasure craft sustained serious injuries. The aircraft was recovered 3 days after the occurrence. The TSB investigation is ongoing.

C-GARJ un Airbus A319-114 exploité par Air Canada Rouge sous l'indicatif ROU1521 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de St-John's, NF (CYYT) à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 5 membres d'équipage et 116 passagers à bord. Lors du vol, un agent de bord a éprouvé des problèmes médicaux affectant sa capacité à effectuer ses tâches. Lors de l'arrivée à CYUL, l'agent a été considéré incapable de poursuivre ses tâches reliées au vol.

C-GDQX un appareil de construction amateur de type Pégazair-100 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Maniwaki, QC (CYMW) à destination d'un terrain privé dans la municipalité de Bois-Franc situé à environs 13 miles nautiques au nord de CYMW avec 2 personnes à bord. Lors de l’arrivé au terrain privé, le pilote aux commandes a effectué un premier arrêt complet et est revenu au début de la piste pour effectuer un décollage. Lors de la course au décollage, l'aéronef n'a pas pu atteindre la vitesse de décollage requise et est sorti en bout de piste avant que le pilote ne puisse interrompre la course. L'aéronef s'est ensuite enfoncé dans un fossé rempli de branches. Le pilote était à son premier décollage de ce champ et les conditions rapportées indiquent que la masse de l'aéronef était élevée, que le gazon était long et la piste en pente ascendante. L'appareil a subi des dommages mineurs et les 2 occupants n'ont subi aucune blessure.

C-GQAJ, a Perimeter Aviation LP., Swearingen SA226-TC was conducting an IFR flight from Brandon Municipal Airport (CYBR), MB, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. While on approach to CYWG, the right battery temperature hot light illuminated. The flight crew performed the memory items and quick reference handbook checklist. The battery was disconnected from the electrical system and an emergency was declared. The aircraft landed uneventfully at CYWG with airport emergency services standing by.

The privately registered Aeronca 11BCX floatplane (registration C-FOYV, serial number 11AC-272X) was conducting a recreational flight under visual flight rules from Porpoise Bay (49° 28.98' N, 123° 45.46' W), BC, to Skaha Lake (49° 25.2' N, 119° 35.4' W), BC, with only the pilot on board. During cruise flight, the engine (Teledyne Continental O-200 series) RPM started to fluctuate. The pilot applied carb heat and adjusted the fuel mixture with no results. The pilot elected to make a precautionary landing at Lightning Lake (49° 03.68' N, 120° 49.87' W), BC. During the landing slide, the aircraft overran the end of the lake and collided with trees on the shoreline. The pilot was not injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged. BC Parks officials attended the scene and determined there was no environmental damage. The aircraft was disassembled and removed the following day.

N9710B, a privately registered Cessna 172RG was operating on a cross-country flight from Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen International Airport (CYXY), YT, to Discovery Yukon Lodge, YT. Upon landing on the wet grass runway, the pilot observed minimal braking effect and the aircraft slid to the left-hand side of the runway. The left-hand wing contacted a small tree and the aircraft turned sideways with right wing tip and propeller striking the runway. The aircraft came to rest on the runway; the pilot and passenger exited the aircraft uninjured.

C-GNLK, un B737-2K2C exploité par Les Investissements Nolinor Inc. sous l’indicatif NRL950 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Intl (Mirabel), QC (CYMX) à destination de l'aéroport de Val-d’Or, QC (CYVO) avec 84 passagers et 6 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en croisière au niveau de vol 320, un groupe de conditionnement d'air s’est mis hors-ligne et une dépressurisation est survenue. L’équipage a effectué une descente d’urgence, déclaré un état d’urgence (pan pan) auprès de l’unité de contrôle aérien (ATC) et déployé les masques à oxygène de la cabine selon la liste de référence rapide. L’équipage a poursuivi le vol à destination, où l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-GJZD, un Dash-8 Q400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7692, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Saint Jonh, NB (CYSJ) avec 53 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Alors que l’appareil est en croisière au niveau de vol 250, une dépressurisation est survenue. L’équipage a effectué une descente d’urgence et a déclaré un état d’urgence (pan pan) auprès de l’ unité de contrôle aérien (ATC). L’équipage a poursuivi le vol à destination à 12 000 pieds asl, où l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil. Le service de maintenance a trouvé le contrôleur de pression de la cabine avec un code d'erreur et un joint d'étanchéité de porte délaminé. Le contrôleur et le joint d'étanchéité ont été remplacé et l'aéronef remis en service.

C-FIUV, an Air Canada Boeing 777-300ER was operating as flight ACA872 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Paris Charles-de-Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France. Shortly after departure from CYYZ, while climbing through 400 feet AGL, there was a bang and reduction of power with a vibration from the right engine (General Electric GE90-115B). Passengers observed momentary flames from the back of the engine. The flight crew conducted the quick reference handbook for an engine surge/stall, the engine responded to engine commands, but was not producing the expected power. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight returned to CYYZ with the right engine set to idle. The aircraft was able to taxi under its own power to the gate without further incident.

C-GEFA, un Airbus 330-343 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA301 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Vancouver (CYVR), BC avec 299 passagers et 9 membres d’équipage. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, l'équipage n'était pas en mesure de sélectionner le levier du train d'atterrissage en position rentré et une indication anormale du train est apparue sur le moniteur électronique centralisé de bord (ECAM). L’équipage a décidé de revenir se poser à CYUL et a déclaré un état d’urgence (pan pan) auprès de l’unité de circulation aérienne (ATC). L’avion s’est posé sur la piste 24R sans encombre avec les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte.

C-GFCP, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A320-214 was preparing for flight ROU1704 from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), NV, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Prior to departure, a cabin crew member became incapacitated due to illness and was unable to operate the flight. The cabin crew to passenger ratio was respected and the flight departed without further incident.

C-FHRT, a Silver Mountain Commercial Distributors Ltd. dba Gulf Island Seaplanes float equipped De Havilland DHC-2 was conducting a training flight from Vancouver Harbour Aerodrome (CYHC), BC, with 1 pilot on board. The aircraft took off from CYHC and flew a short training circuit, returning for a westbound approach. A gust caused the left wing to lift, causing the right wingtip to impact the water. This caused an oscillation that led to the left wingtip, left float tip, and propeller to contact the water. The aircraft came to a stop in an upright position and was subsequently towed to the dock. The aircraft was removed from service to assess the damage. There were no injuries.

C-FTHD, a Summit Helicopters Limited Bell 407 departed Bronson Creek, BC, under visual flight rules for a local flight to support drilling operations with 1 crew member on board. At an unknown point in approximately 5.3 hours of flight, the helicopter main rotor contacted the tail finlets. Both finlets were damaged, and a portion of one finlet penetrated through the tail rotor shaft shroud, denting the shaft. The aircraft landed normally at Bronson Creek. The damage was noted after the flight, and the aircraft was removed from service for maintenance. There were no injuries.

C-GFXA, un Cessna 310R exploité par Mitchinson Flying Service Ltd., effectuait un vol d’aéropointage dans le cadre d’une opération d’arrosage selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Val d’Or, QC (CYVO) avec un pilote et un coordinateur des opérations à bord. Pendant la course au décollage sur la piste 18, l’avion a dévié vers la gauche et l’hélice du moteur de gauche a percuté une lumière de piste avant son décollage. Au retour du vol, le pilote a été avisé de la présence de verre jusqu’à 25 pieds de la bordure gauche de la piste. Une inspection après le vol a révélé des dommages à une des 3 pales du moteur gauche.

C-GLQL, a Porter Airlines Inc. DHC-8-402 was conducting flight PTR2327 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, USA. Shortly after takeoff, when the crew retracted the flaps to zero, the "FLAP POWER" caution light illuminated, and the flaps were observed to be stationary at 4 degrees. The crew actioned the appropriate checklist and requested to return to CYOW for a reduced flap landing, asking that ARFF stand by during the landing. They landed uneventfully, and after having ARFF inspect the brakes, they continued to their gate. Maintenance replaced the Flap Control Unit and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GXAI un Dash-8-314 (DH8C) exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE802 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Kuujjuarapik, Québec (CYGW) avec 34 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage à bord. En vol de croisière à 157 miles marins au sud-est de CYGW, l’équipage a remarqué une perte de fluide hydraulique du système numéro 2 et a décidé d’effectuer une diversion à destination de La Grande, Québec (CYGL). Une urgence a été déclarée (pan pan), le train d’atterrissage a été descendu manuellement et l’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 31 à CYGL sans encombre.

C-FZWS, a Westjet B737 Max 8 was operating flight WJA16 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Edinburgh Airport (EGPH), UK. While in cruise, a cabin crew became ill and was unable to perform duties which were redistributed amongst remaining crew. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GYNF, an Agusta AW139 helicopter operated by Ornge Rotor, had departed Sturgeon Falls Heliport (CNM3), ON, on a training flight with the intended destination of Sudbury Airport (CYSB), ON. There were 2 pilots and 3 cabin crew (paramedics) on board. The purpose of the flight was to conduct training for the cabin crew which included hover exits and entries, which would take place in the vicinity of Wanapitei Lake. During a hover exit, a trainee was struck by a large piece of debris dislodged by the rotor downwash, and although they were wearing a helmet, they were knocked briefly unconscious. The injured trainee was assisted back into the helicopter and transported to the Sudbury Airport (CYSB), then transported to the Sudbury hospital by ground.

N846PW, a corporate-registered Pilatus PC-12/47 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl Airport (CYWG), MB, to Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON. N846PW was cleared to taxi to Runway 31 and to hold short at the VFR line. C-FUNF, a Fast Air Beech 200, was conducting flight PBR650 from Attawapiskat Airport (CYAT), ON, to CYWG. PBR650 was cleared to land on Runway 31. As N846PW was taxiing to Runway 31, it crossed the VFR hold short line and entered into the runway protected area. At approximately 1 mile final, ATC instructed PBR650 to pull up and go around due to the runway incursion. N846PW turned around prior to proceeding onto the runway, exited the runway protected area, and held short of the VFR hold line. PBR650 completed a VFR circuit and landed safely.

C-FIUA, an Air Canada B777-200 was conducting flight ACA042 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Indira Gandhi International Airport (VIDP), Delhi, India. During climb to their cruising altitude, the crew heard a loud bang from the left engine, accompanied by an EICAS message indicating smoke in the crew rest area. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklists leading them to shut down the left engine. The crew declared PAN PAN initially, then upgraded to MAYDAY after the engine shutdown. They requested a return to CYYZ and jettisoned some fuel before landing on runway 23 with ARFF standing by. The left engine was replaced before the aircraft returned to service.

N14120, a Boeing 757-224 registered to United Airlines Inc., was conducting flight UAL977 from Shannon Airport (EINN) Ireland to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR) NJ, USA. During cruise at FL360, the pilots observed a R HYD QTY, a R HYD PRIM PUMP and a R HYD DEM PUMP annunciations. The pilots performed the relevant non-normal procedures, contacted dispatch and United Airlines Inc. Technical Operations Maintenance Control. The decision was made to continue to destination. An emergency was declared, and the flight landed safely at KEWR.Maintenance personnel performed fault isolation procedures which identified a leaking hydraulic coupling on the #2 engine and the coupling was replaced.

C-GXIH, an Excel Flight Training Inc. Piper PA30 was conducting a local visual flight rules training flight from Lethbridge Airport (CYQL), AB. Onboard was a flight instructor and a student pilot. Following a normal approach and landing on Runway 06 at CYQL, the throttles were retarded to idle. When the #1 throttle was retarded to idle, the #1 engine stopped running. The aircraft was brought to a stop on the runway and an engine restart was attempted. The restart attempt was unsuccessful, and the aircraft was taxied off the runway with the one operative engine and then the aircraft was shut down. The aircraft was then towed back to the ramp.Post-occurrence maintenance: it was determined that the idle speeds on both engines #1 and #2 were set too low. The idle speeds were adjusted and the aircraft was returned to service with no further anomalies noted.

N360DL, a privately registered Cessna U206G aircraft equipped with floats, was departing from Silver Falls Water Aerodrome (CKJ5), MB, for a flight to Dogskin Lake, MB. During the takeoff run, the aircraft became airborne prematurely and the pilot attempted to gently allow the aircraft to settle back on the rough water. The aircraft then entered a stall and contacted the water with the left wing low and transverse to the wind and waves. The left float contacted the water first and the hard impact broke the left float attachment allowing the fuselage to pivot to the left side. The left wing then impacted the water and the aircraft spun to the left and came to rest upright. There were no injuries. Pilot exited the aircraft and was met by a local seaplane operator with rescue boats. The aircraft was towed back to shore where emergency personnel were waiting. No services were needed or given to the pilot. The aircraft was pulled from the water in order to secure it and prevent any further damage. The damage to the aircraft was substantial. It was reported that the winds at the time of the occurrence were westerly at approximately 25 knots with gusts over 40 knots.

C-FEKG, a privately operated Cessna A185E on amphibious floats, departed Arnprior Aerodrome (CNP3), ON, with two pilots on board to conduct water landings on Lake Madawaska, which is adjacent to the CNP3 airport. After approximately an hour of circuits, the pilot joined the circuit for runway 28, and extended the landing gear in anticipation of landing on the runway. While on final, at 300-400 feet, the pilot noted that he was a bit slow and increased the throttle, only to realize that the engine had failed. He elected to land the aircraft in the water ahead, but there was not sufficient time to retract the landing gear before the landing, and the aircraft overturned after contacting the water. Both occupants exited the aircraft and were helped out of the water by boaters who had witnessed the event. The aircraft was mostly submerged and sustained significant damage to the propeller, engine cowling, and left wing.

During initial climb out of Calgary International Airport (CYYC), Alberta, the flight crew of MorningStar Express Inc's ATR 72-202 (flight number MAL8067) received an intermittent to steady flap asymmetry caution light and the autopilot disconnected. This was followed by an intermittent pitch asymmetry caution light. The flight crew stopped the climb, requested a return to CYYC, and declared a PAN PAN due to the nature of the problem and the increased approach and landing speeds. Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) vehicles were on standby and inspected the brakes for overheating. Aircraft taxied back to the hangar without further incident.Maintenance follow up: Morningstar Express Inc. maintenance personnel replaced the multi-function computer (MFC) #1 and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FRSE, a Boeing 787-9 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA062 from Incheon International Airport (RKSI), South Korea, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the arrival, the flight crew received a "SLAT DRIVE" ECAM message. After actioning the appropriate checklist, the flight crew declared PAN PAN and continued with a flap 20 landing with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by. After landing, a "HOT BRAKES" indication appeared on the EICAS. The aircraft remained on the runway until the brakes cooled to a normal temperature, after which they taxied to their gate. Maintenance replaced the #7 inboard slat skew sensor before returning the aircraft to service.

C-FDFK, a Calm Air International LP ATR 72-212A operating as flight CAV2401, was parked at gate 20 at the Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, preparing for departure to Sanikiluaq Airport (CYSK), NU. Due to the unavailability of air conditioning carts and the high cabin temperature, the crew elected to run the number 2 engine in hotel mode (propeller brake engaged) in order to utilize the air conditioning pack to cool the cabin. It was reported that a lightning/rainstorm was passing through at the time with wind gusts as high as 37 knots. The wind direction was a tailwind for the aircraft. Near the end of the storm, the crew observed a NAC OVHT warning followed by an engine fire indication on the right engine. The crew shut down the right engine and declared an emergency with ATC. The aircraft was evacuated at the terminal, and ARFF responded and inspected the aircraft; however, they did not find any signs of a fire. There were no injuries. A post-occurrence inspection of the aircraft by the operator's maintenance revealed no indications of fire and all related systems were tested and were deemed to be operating normally.

C-FNEN, a WestJet Encore Ltd. De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-8-402 (serial number 4453) was operating as WEN3630 on a flight from Calgary Intl. Airport (CYYC), AB to Portland International Airport (KPDX), OR. Onboard were 4 crew members and 18 passengers. On departure, the flight crew selected flaps to zero and the flap drive motor caution light illuminated. The flight crew carried out the appropriate checklist procedure, declared a PAN PAN and informed air traffic control that they would be returning to CYYC. The aircraft landed safety with emergency vehicles standing by. The aircraft taxied back to the gate without further incident.Maintenance actions: WestJet Encore replaced the pressure switch on the flap power unit and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FMXC, a privately operated Sportine Aviacija LAK-17B FES was participating in a gliding competition at the Cu Nim Aerodrome (CEH2), Black Diamond, AB. After flying for approximately 30 minutes the pilot bailed out of the glider; his parachute did not open and he subsequently died from his injuries. The glider impacted terrain, 1.8 NM SE of CEH2 and sustained significant damage.

OY-GRM, an Air Greenland De Havilland DHC-8-202 taxied back to the hangar after landing from a post-maintenance check/acceptance flight. Once stopped, the parking brake was set and the engine shutdown carried out. During this time, the right-hand main landing gear brakes caught on fire. Ground personnel, who were watching the aircraft shutdown, noticed the fire and used fire extinguishers to put out the fire. Both tires on the right-hand main landing gear deflated and there was a hydraulic leak. Heavy smoke was also observed from the left-hand main landing gear brakes; however, there was no fire.It was subsequently determined that the anti-skid transducer wiring had been installed incorrectly, during previous maintenance activities at a different facility. The brakes on both main landing gear were replaced.

C-FDTH, an Air Spray Ltd. Lockheed L-188A was conducting aerial firefighting operations as ASB498 locally from Manning Aerodrome (CFX4), AB, on Alberta wildfire #PWF037, (23 NM W of CFX4). On the second flight of the day, while on short final for the second drop, the fire reached a taller tree patch, which rapidly increased the intensity of the fire. This resulted in a rapid increase in fire activity and temperatures on the left side of the aircraft. The captain called for an increase in power. While power was being advanced, a temperature spike of 1040° F was noticed on the # 1 engine and was identified by the co-pilot. The flight crew observed the # 1 engine propeller speed drop and the captain called for an engine failure drill on the # 1 engine (Allison 501D-13). While securing the # 1 engine, the # 2 engine temperature spiked to 1040° F. The captain noticed the decreased performance, confirmed with power lever application and observed no change. The flight crew determined that the engine de-coupled and conducted the engine failure drill on the # 2 engine. Both engines were confirmed shutdown and propellers feathered. Once at a safe altitude, the emergency checks were completed, and a 2-engine landing was briefed. An emergency was declared and the aircraft returned to CFX4 where the aircraft landed without further issue.

C-GSNR, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by Sky North Air Ltd., was conducting an IFR flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to the Island Lake Airport (CYIV), MB. While on approach to Runway 30 at CYIV, upon lowering the landing gear, the flight crew noticed the left main landing gear was not indicating down and locked. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft returned to CYWG. While on final approach to CYWG, the left main gear indication was still not showing down and locked. The aircraft entered a hold and the crew performed the quick reference handbook checks. After a manual extension of the landing gear, the indication remained the same. The aircraft landed at CYWG without further incident.The operators' maintenance replaced the left main landing gear down-lock switch.

C-FMEP, a Morningstar Air Express Inc. Boeing 757-200 was operating as MAL7051 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. On approach to Runway 35R in CYYC, the flight crew selected Flaps 1 and the flight crew noticed the Trailing Edge Flap Disagree EICAS message had appeared along with a Trailing Edge annunciator light. The flight crew advised ATC of the flight control issue and declared a PAN PAN emergency. The aircraft continued the approach and landed on Runway 35R without further issue. Company maintenance serviced the #4 flap transmission and replaced the #1 Flap/Slat Electronic Unit (FSEU).

The Carson Air Limited Beech B300 (King Air, registration C-GRXX,) departed Kamloops (CYKA), BC, on medevac flight CRN711, under instrument flight rules to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew members, and 3 passengers on board. While climbing through 17 000 feet above sea level (ASL), the crewmembers observed the "cabin altitude" annunciator light illuminate. The aircraft was leveled off at 18 000 feet ASL where the crew next observed the "Cabin ALT HI" annunciator light illuminate. The crew donned oxygen masks: the oxygen masks in the cabin automatically deployed for the passengers. The crew requested a lower altitude from air traffic control and initiated a descent. During the descent, an emergency checklist was performed by the crew. A PAN PAN was declared with air traffic control. The crew leveled the aircraft at 13 000 feet ASL approximately 5 minutes after initiating the descent from their original cruise altitude. 16 minutes after their initial level off, the crew subsequently descended to 10 000 feet ASL. The flight continued to CYVR and landed without incident. There were no injuries.A maintenance inspection was conducted however the pressurization issue could not be duplicated. The masks were repacked, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSJJ, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight ACA1054 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (KPHX), Arizona, USA. On approach at KPHX, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to climb. The RA was actioned and a go-around was conducted. Flight landed without further incident.

C-GVUH, an Air Canada A220-300 was operating flight ACA763 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA, USA. On approach at KSFO, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to climb. RA was actioned and flight landed without further incident.

C-FNEN, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 was operating as WEN3630 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Portland International Airport (KPDX), Oregon, USA. After departure from CYYC, the flight crew selected flaps zero and the flap drive caution light illuminated. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and determined that a flap zero landing was required. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft returned to CYYC where it landed uneventfully. There were no injuries. Company maintenance replaced the pressure switch on the flap power unit and the aircraft was released back into service.

C-GRSX, a privately registered Cessna 305A (L-19 Bird Dog) was operating on a cross-country flight from a private airstrip 15 NM E of Peace River, AB, to Red Deer Regional Airport (CYQF), AB. An en-route stop was planned at Valleyview Aerodrome (CEL5), AB. While touching down on Runway 25 at CEL5, the aircraft began to drift to the left. The pilot was unable to regain control and the aircraft departed the left edge of the runway. While the left main landing gear transitioned from the paved runway surface to the grass, the aircraft began to ground loop. Subsequently the right main landing gear collapsed, and the right wing contacted the ground and fractured as the aircraft came to rest. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured.

N644UA, a Boeing 767-300ER operated by United Airlines Inc. was conducting flight UAL102 from George Bush/Houston Intercontinental Airport (KIAH), Texas, USA, to Franz Josef Strauss International Airport (EDDM), Munich, Germany. During cruise, the flight crew observed a series of Engine Indication and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) alerts of the forward, aft, passenger and emergency doors. The cabin pressure indications were unreliable. The ab-normal checklist was consulted, and the flight crew declared an emergency and diverted to Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. The aircraft landed without further incident.  Maintenance removed and replaced the Proximity Switch Electronic Unit (PSEU) and replaced both Cabin Pressure Controllers 1 and 2 to resolve the faults. The aircraft was ground tested and returned to service.

C-FTWO, a privately registered amateur built Murphy Rebel departed Squamish Municipal Airport (CYSE), BC, on a recreational flight under visual flight rules to Courtenay Airpark (CAH3), BC, with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. At approximately 1721 PDT the aircraft struck terrain 13 NM south southwest of CYSE. The pilot and passenger were fatally injured. The aircraft ELT activated, along with an automatic cellphone emergency notification system. The aircraft was destroyed. There was a post-crash fire, with minimal damage to the environment.The TSB deployed to the site and is investigating the occurrence.

C-GELJ, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight ACA1070 from Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (KDFW), Texas, to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Prior to departure, a passenger's vape battery combusted due to liquid leaking into it. Battery was contained by cabin crew and flight departed without further incident.

C-GCPX, a Swearingen SA226-AT operated by 2080061 Ontario Inc. (dba SkyCare Air Ambulance), was conducting flight PHX-011 from Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON, to Atikokan Muni Aerodrome (CYIB), ON. The aircraft flew the approach to Runway 04 and touchdown occurred on the wet runway at approximately 1300 feet beyond the threshold; therefore, there was approximately 2195 feet remaining. The flight crew applied reverse, and at 70 knots, the propeller speed levers were selected to the low position. The captain applied the brakes to slow the aircraft; however, the aircraft overran the end of the runway by approximately 15 feet. The flight crew assessed the situation and attempted to turn the aircraft around on the grassy area beyond the end of the runway; however, the aircraft became stuck. The flight crew shutdown and the 5 occupants disembarked from the aircraft. There was no damage to the aircraft. There were no injuries.A post-occurrence review of the weather indicated that the automated weather observations at CYIB recorded surface winds at 21:00z were 330 @ 17 knots. The operator's maintenance was dispatched to CYIB to free the aircraft. They inspected the aircraft and returned it to service.

C-FFYG, a Jazz Aviation LP Embraer 175 was operating flight JZA942 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), New Jersey. During the descent phase of flight, moderate turbulence was encountered and cabin crew member and a passenger received a minor injury. Cabin crew member was unable to complete duties for landing. EMS was requested to meet cabin crew member and passenger upon arrival. Aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FYWS, un Cessna 172K sur flotteurs amphibies en exploitation privée effectuait des décollages et amerrissages mandataire sur le fleuve Saint-Laurent à la hauteur de Sainte-Anne-De-La-Perade, QC. Lors d'un amerrissage, le pilote a perdu le contrôle de l'aéronef dans une condition d'eau miroir. Au contact avec l'eau, l'aéronef s'est renversé. Le pilote, seul occupant, a été secouru par un plaisancier et n'a pas été blessé. L'aéronef à subi des dommages substantiels. La balise 406 mhz ne s'est pas activé.

C-GNTG, a Buffalow Airways Ltd. Air Tractor AT-802A (Fireboss) on amphibious floats, was conducting training from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. The pilot reported a landing gear issue on approach and conducted a low pass to have a visual confirmation that the landing gear was down. The pilot requested aircraft rescue and firefighting to be on standby and landed without further issue.The maintenance team found that the left-hand nose gear track rods were overtightened. The track rods were adjusted in accordance with the maintenance manual and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GANU, an Air North Charter & Training Ltd Boeing 737-55D was operating flight ANT3712 from Fairbanks International Airport (PAFA), Alaska, to Dawson City Airport (CYDA), YT. While in cruise at 17 000 feet, ANT3712 received multiple TCAS RAs due to reported military aircraft activity in the area. The flight crew complied with the resolution alerts. The flight was completed without further incident.

C-FPVN, un Zenair Zodiac CH600 TD de construction amateur venait de décollé de l'aéroport de Maniwaki, QC (CYMW) pour un vol local avec deux personnes à bord lorsque le pilote a observé une perte de puissance moteur. Un état d'urgence (MAYDAY) a été déclaré et un retour vers CYMW a été initié. Devant l'impossibilité d'atteindre la piste, le pilote a effectué un atterrissage forcé dans un petit champ à proximité de l'aéroport . Le contact avec le sol a causé des dommages substentiels à l'aéronef. Aucun des occupants n'a été blessé.

C-FMLV, a Northern Air Spray Ltd. Thrush S2R-T34, was conducting a training flight at the Peace River Aerodrome (CYPE), AB. Upon landing on Runway 04, directional control was lost during the landing roll. The aircraft went off the right side, struck a runway light and damaged one propeller blade. There were no injuries. The aircraft was moved to the company's hangar.

C-FSDQ, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight ACA728 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to LaGuardia Airport (KLGA), New York. On approach at KLGA, the flight crew received a TCAS RA. RA was actioned and flight continued to land without further incident.

C-GNCF, a De Havilland DHC-8-314 Aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP., was conducting IFR flight PAG611 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to St. Theresa Point Airport (CYST), MB. While PAG611 was on final approach to Runway 04 at CYST, C-FZTA, a Eurocopter AS350-B2 helicopter operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd., took off from CYST and crossed the approach path to Runway 04. PAG611 continued its approach and landed without incident. It was reported that the aircraft were separated by approximately 1/4 mile and 100 feet vertically. In response, both operators have held coordinated meetings and SMS reviews of this occurrence.

C-GKUH, an Air Canada Airbus A330-300 was operating as flight ACA819 from Venice Marco Polo Airport (LIPZ), Italy, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. The flight crew received ECAM message for green hydraulic system level drop. Decision was made to divert to Dublin International Airport (EIDW), Ireland, and a Pan Pan was declared. The flight landed without incident and aircraft rescue and firefighting met the aircraft on the runway. Aircraft was towed to gate due to nose wheel steering limitations. During investigation, found leakage spot on bolt cap seal, location FR42 RHS FWD RIB1 lower #1 bolt on dry bay side. Lower bolt on inner tank side repair carried out by applying sealant.

C-FTIQ, a Canadian North ATR42-500, was operating as flight AKT677 from Goja Haven Airport (CYHK), NU, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. After landing and during the taxi to the apron, the flight crew received a "pack fault" caution light that was followed by smoke entering the flight deck and cabin. The flight crew also received an electrical smoke indication. An emergency was declared, and the flight crew requested to taxi to the ramp area. The flight crew ran the smoke and electrical smoke checklists, the aircraft was shut down and the passengers deplaned without further issue.Following the flight, the maintenance team found that the fans for the air-conditioning system were seized. Maintenance was performed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJYE, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300 was operating flight ACA580 from George Bush Intercontinental Airport (KIAH), Texas, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. In cruise, the flight crew received an EICAS message: EFIS Miscompare and indicated airspeed/altitude fluctuations, which triggered an indicated overspeed. The flight crew declared PAN PAN. Quick reference handbook checklist was actioned, and the indications cleared. PAN PAN was cancelled by flight crew and flight continued without further incident.

C-FJOK, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 aircraft was operating flight ROU1602 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), Florida. During the descent, while carrying out the CUUDA3 RNAV arrival, at 6000 ft ASL, the flight crew received TCAS RA CLIMB due to conflicting traffic climbing below. The flight crew complied with the RA and the flight was subsequently completed without further incident.

C-GYGU, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was operating flight ROU1645 from Miami International Airport (KMIA), Florida, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the cruise phase of flight at FL350, in the vicinity of Pittsburgh International Airport (KPIT), Pittsburgh, the flight crew observed an abnormal noise behind and below them followed by vibrations and odour in the flight deck. There were no associated ECAMs. Flight crew donned oxygen masks as a precaution and following unsuccessful troubleshooting, declared a PAN PAN. The flight landed uneventfully at CYYZ with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby. The aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and found the avionics blower fan to be defective. Component was removed and replaced.

N767AJ, an American Airlines Boeing 777-223ER was operating as AAL108 on a flight from Boston/Logan International Airport (KBOS), MA, to London Heathrow International Airport (EGLL), England. During the climb to cruising level the flight crew was advised that a section of the cabin was noticeably warm causing passenger discomfort. About 30 minutes later the flight crew received an EICAS message SMOKE CREW REST which cleared immediately. The crew verified that there was no smoke in the rest area and 20 minutes later the crew received a SMOKE CREW REST F/D message. Again, the flight crew verified the absence of smoke in the crew rest area. Shortly after, the cabin crew reported a burning odour in first class. The crew notified their operations and maintenance departments, declared a PAN PAN, and returned to KBOS.Maintenance determined that the odour was caused by oil contamination near the APU. The APU was removed and replaced, as well as oil-contaminated air conditioning pack components.

C-FLXT, an Air Spray (1967) Limited Lockheed L188C (Electra), was conducting a practice fire mission as flight ASB481, 35 nautical miles west of Williams Lake Airport (CYWL), BC. During the flight, the No.1 engine (Allison 501-D13) RPM increased to rate above operational limitations. The crew performed a precautionary shutdown of the engine as per the quick reference handbook. The aircraft returned to CYWL and landed without further incident.Company maintenance replaced propeller No.1 rotary actuator, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWIY, a privately operated Aviation Artur Trendak gyroplane, was taking off runway 13 at Woodstock Aerodrome (CCD3), NB, for a local flight with a flight instructor and a student pilot onboard. Their earlier flights in the day revealed that the aircraft engine was not achieving full RPM on takeoff (200 to 300 RPM below specified takeoff RPM), though they determined that aircraft climb performance was adequate. For the occurrence flight the student pilot conducted the takeoff from the right seat, and the initial climb was uneventful. When just a few hundred feet of altitude was achieved, the engine RPM began to decrease, and the aircraft began to descend. The flight instructor requested and was given aircraft control. The flight instructor lowered the nose and began a left bank, however the aircraft continued to descend. The aircraft descended into trees, coming to rest in the wooded area east of the runway.  The occupants both were wearing the aircraft 4-point safety harnesses and were initially assessed as uninjured by first responders. The flight instructor later visited medical facilities with back pain and was assessed with a minor injury. The aircraft was substantially damaged and was subsequently recovered.

N759AN, an American Airlines Boeing 777-223ER was operating as AAL56 on a flight from Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL, to London/Heathrow International Airport (EGLL), England. While in cruise, the flight crew received a FIRE FWD CARGO warning message, along with the fire bell. The flight crew immediately declared an emergency and coordinated with ATS for a diversion to St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL. The FIRE FWD CARGO message displayed intermittently through the remainder of the flight, which made an overweight landing at CYYT without further incident, damage or injury. Airport emergency services met the aircraft, inspected the cargo hold and did not detect any heat or signs of fire.Maintenance personnel carried out the overweight landing inspection and no damage was noted. The fire bottles were replaced, and a complete inspection and test of the fire detection system was accomplished with no faults found.

C-GUNB, a Cessna 172 aircraft operated by Gander Flight Training, was on a local solo training flight at Gander International Airport (CYQX), NL, when directional control was lost while landing on Runway 03. The aircraft departed Runway 03 on the east side, struck and damaged a runway light, after which the left wing struck the ground as the aircraft veered to the right. The aircraft came to a stop in a drainage ditch east of runway 03 and sustained substantial damage to the left wing, nose landing gear and forward fuselage, including the propeller. The emergency locater transmitter activated. The pilot was not injured. The winds reported at the time of the occurrence were 050°M at 12 knots gusting 17 knots.

C-GHPU, an Air Canada Boeing 787-8 was conducting flight ACA876 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Lyon/Saint Exupéry Airport (LFLL), France. While in cruise flight about 28 nm southwest of Deer Lake Regional Airport (CYDF), NL, the crew received an annunciation indicating that the L1 cabin air compressor (CAC) had failed, concurrent with an electrical burning odour which dissipated quickly. The crew declared PAN PAN, descended to 10 000 feet, and coordinated with ATS to enter a hold while waiting for weather to improve at nearby airports. About 30 minutes later the R2 CAC failed and subsequently the right air conditioning pack failed, leaving the aircraft unable to maintain cabin pressure. The crew consulted with company maintenance and operational control and coordinated with ATS to return to CYUL, where a landing was made without further incident.Maintenance personnel replaced both left and right-side air cycle machines.

C-GZTE, an Academie De Pilotage Internationale Inc. Cessna 172N was a on cross-country flight from Gatineau-Ottawa Airport (CYND), QC, to Cornwall Regional Aerodrome (CYCC), ON, with a student pilot on board. During the touchdown the aircraft bounced and as the student pilot applied engine power, the aircraft bounced a second time. Directional control was lost, and the aircraft veered off the runway. The nose landing gear dug into the soft mud and the aircraft flipped over. The student pilot was not injured but the aircraft received damage to the left wing and propeller.

C-IRIC, a Tecnam P92 Echo, advanced Ultra-light, was on the climb out after departure from Greenbank Aerodrome (CNP8), ON, with a pilot and passenger on board for a local flight. At a height of approximately 500 feet AGL the engine began to lose power (Rotax 912). The pilot carried out a forced landing in a farmer's field; the aircraft sustained damage, however both occupants evacuated the aircraft. There was a post impact fire, and the aircraft was destroyed. The two occupants were taken to hospital, and although the pilot was not injured, the passenger received a serious injury.

C-GQAJ, a Perimeter Aviation Swearingen Aircraft SA226-TC operating as flight PAG01, departed Swan River Airport (CZJN), MB, on a flight to Dauphin (Lt. Col. W.G. (Billy) Barker, VC) (CYDN), MB. After landing at CYDN, the flight paramedic observed a haze in the cabin and notified the flight crew. The flight crew also noticed the haze and shut down both engines. The flight crew then opened the cabin and cargo doors to allow the haze to escape. The patient then disembarked uneventfully and no further haze or smoke was observed after the engine shutdown.Post-flight, the flight crew contacted the operator's maintenance. In consultation with them, it was requested that the flight crew perform a ground run to help determine the source of the haze. It was determined that the source was the left-hand air conditioning system; which was deferred per the aircraft's MEL for the next flight. Subsequently, the left-hand mixing valve was replaced and the MEL was cleared.

C-GFXP, a Zimmer Air Services Inc. Sikorsky S-58T wheel equipped helicopter was conducting training with two pilots on board. The aircraft was being taxied on an inactive runway when the tail wheel went off the tarmac and onto the grass. At this time the aircraft began to oscillate and almost instantly went into a state of ground resonance, at which time one of the blades contacted the tail boom and then another contacted the ground. One of the aircrafts struts also broke, causing the aircraft to roll onto its right side and sustained substantial damage. Both occupants exited the helicopter safely, one received minor injuries.

N29LJ, a privately operated Learjet 60, was conducting an IFR flight from St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL, to Québec/Jean Lesage International Airport (CYQB), QC. While in cruise at FL380 a flight crew member became ill. At approximately 120 nm northeast of Moncton/Greater Moncton Roméo LeBlanc International Airport (CYQM), NB, an emergency was declared and the aircraft diverted to CYQM where it landed without further incident.

C-GNSF, a privately registered, amateur-built Murphy Radical, equipped with amphibious floats, was on a local flight from Squamish Municipal Airport (CYSE), BC, under visual flight rules, with the pilot and one passenger on board. After conducting a full stop landing in Princess Louisa Inlet, BC, the aircraft took off and completed several touch and goes. During the final touch-and-go, the approach was made to an area of water that was described as a glassy water surface. The aircraft contacted the water in a nose down attitude and one of the floats dug into the water. The aircraft nosed over. The pilot and passenger, who were wearing personal flotation devices (PFD), egressed out the left door and sat on the floats for a few moments before the aircraft began to sink. They both removed their PFD and began swimming for the shoreline. As they approached the shore, a private boat arrived and pulled them from the water. There were no injuries. The emergency locator transmitter did not activate.The following day, the TSB was contacted by the Sunshine Coast detachment of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police who had received numerous calls from boaters in Princess Louisa Inlet about a damaged, partially submerged, floatplane in the inlet. The aircraft was subsequently recovered from the inlet.

C-FEIQ, un Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU exploité par Jazz Aviation, effectuait le vol JZA8606 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl - Boston, MA (KBOS) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 54 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, un oiseau a heurté le moteur droit (GE CF34-E5A1 s/n 193389). L'équipage a alors déclaré une urgence et est revenu atterrir à CYUL où les services d'urgence étaient déployés. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre et il n'y a pas eu de blessés. Les services de maintenance ont constaté que des pales de la soufflante étaient endommagées. L' aéronef a ensuite été retiré du service.

C-GXZD, an Airbus A330-343 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA812 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Lisbon International/Humberto Delgado Airport (LPPT), Portugal. When the aircraft was approximately 80 NM NNW of St. John's International Airport (CYYT), NL, the crew declared a Pan-Pan due to the loss of both autopilot systems and multiple other failures. The crew contacted Gander ACC, requested and were cleared to return to CYUL. A short time later the systems affected came back online. The aircraft landed uneventfully in CYUL at 0639 UTC.Company maintenance at CYUL determined that the #1 Air Data and Inertial Reference Unit was faulty and required replacement.

C-FGZI, a Top Aces Inc., A-4N was operating a flight from Neuburg Air Base (ETSN), Germany, to Cuxhaven Nordholz Airprot (ETMN), Germany. While climbing through FL160, the aircraft was subject to an electrical failure. The pilot reset the generator in accordance with the quick reference handbook procedures which was unsuccessful, and then actuated the electrical Ram Air Turbine, which was also unsuccessful. The pilot declared an emergency and did a straight-in approach and landing at ETSN.

C-GEXB, an Air Transat Airbus A321-211 was operating flight TSC359 from Frank País Airport (MUHG), Cuba, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. The cabin crew noticed white smoke emanating from an oven. The oven was turned off and it was noticed two meals were overheating. The flight continued without further incident.The oven temperature setting was adjusted to 150C by maintenance following the flight.

C-GNGV, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300 was operating flight ACA506 from Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD), Illinois, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While en route, an emergency was declared as smoke was detected in the aft galley. The crew elected to return to KORD and the aircraft landed safety without further incident.

C-GPUR, un aéronef de construction amateur de type Searey en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol récréatif selon les règles de vol à vue partir une piste privé près de Val-des-Sources, QC, à destination du lac Les Trois Lacs à Val-des-Sources, QC. Lors de l’amerrissage, les roues étaient descendues et au contact avec la surface de l’eau, l’aéronef s'est renversé. Le seul pilote à bord a subi des blessures mineures. L’avion a subi des dommages importants.

The privately registered Quad City Challenger II basic ultralight, C-FOXR, was conducting circuits at the Foremost Aerodrome (CFD4), AB with just the pilot on board. During landing, the aircraft contacted the runway at a high rate of descent resulting in significant damage to the aircraft. The pilot, who was wearing a helmet and a 4 point harness, was not injured.

F-HRBB, am Air France Boeing 787 operating as AF338, was conducting an IFR flight from Paris/Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France to Seattle-Tacoma Intl (KSEA), USA. When the aircraft was approximately 120 nm south west of Iqaluit (CYFB) NU, the cabin crew reported an acrid smell of burning in the cabin between rows 15 and 17 and notified the flight crew. The flight crew carried out the "Smoke, Fire, or Fumes" emergency checklist; however, the source of the fumes could not be ascertained. The crew declared a MAYDAY and requested a diversion to CYFB where they carried out an uneventful landing on Runway 34.  At the time of landing the fumes had dissipated. There were no injuries to crew or passengers. During a subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance, the left and right AC packs were inspected with no faults found. The overhead ceiling panels between rows 15-17 were also inspected with no electrical faults found and no evidence of fire. The aircraft was subsequently returned to service.

N939AE, a Piedmont Airlines Embraer ERJ-145 was operating as PDT5913 from Albany International Airport (KALB), NY, to Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD), IL. During cruise at FL300 in the vicinity of London, ON, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency due to an engine icing issue and elected to divert to Frederick Douglass Greater Rochester International Airport (KROC), NY. The aircraft was cleared to KROC and exited Canadian airspace without further incident.

C-GVAJ, un Boeing 757-200 exploité par Cargojet Airways Ltd sous l'indicatif CJT575, se préparait à effectuer un vol cargo selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Montréal Intl (Mirabel), QC (CYMX), à destination de Hamilton, ON (CYHM) avec seuls 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors qu’il circulait vers la piste, l’équipage a reçu une indication de feu sur le moteur gauche. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été exécutée et le moteur a été fermé. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés et l'aéronef a été inspecté. Il n'y avait aucune trace de feu ni de fumée. Une inspection effectuée a déterminé 2 pièces fautives.
