Une boucle de détection d'incendie moteur a été repositionnée et la carte #1 du ''Automatic Fire and Overheat Logic and Test System'' (AFLOTS) a été remplacée. L’avion a été remis en service.

C-GHPX. Un Boeing 787-8 exploité par Air Canada était en préparation au sol pour effectuer le vol ACA814 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport Nice, France (LFMN). Après l’embarquement des 231 passagers, la barrière a été bougée et est entrée en contact avec le moteur #1 causant des dommages mineurs. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et les passagers ont été transporté en transbordeur (PTV). Le vol a été annulé.

C-GEEV, un Piper PA-32-260 Cherokee Six d'immatriculation privée, effectuait un vol de selon les règles de vol à vue de l'aéroport de Saint-Georges-de-Beauce, QC (CYSG) à destination de l'aéroport de Sherbrooke, QC (CYSC) avec 1 pilote et 1 passager à bord. À mi-chemin entre CYSG et CYSC, le pilote a noté une perte de pression d'huile et une augmentation de la température de celle-ci. Le pilote a alors déclaré l'état d'urgence (Pan Pan) et a tenté de rallier CYSC. À environ 2NM de CYSC le moteur de l'aéronef a saisi et le pilote a dû effectuer un atterrissage d'urgence sur un terrain gazonné adjacent au terminal de l'aéroport. L'aéronef a ensuite terminé sa course au sol dans les arbres. L'aéronef a été détruit et les occupants ont été blessés. Il n'y a pas eu d'incendie.

N408LC, a Lynden Air Cargo LLC Lockheed L382G (C130) was operating as flight LYC408 from Goose Lake Aerodrome (CGS2), NU, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, with 6 crew on board. While in cruise, approximately 115 NM from CYZF, the flight crew observed that the No. 1 engine (Allision 501-D22A) propeller was out of RPM limits. The flight crew shutdown the No. 1 engine in accordance with the QRH. LYC408 continued to CYZF and performed an uneventful 3 engine approach and landing.Company maintenance changed the No. 1 engine propeller valve housing and released the aircraft back into service.

C-FAVO, a Buffalo Airways Ltd. Curtiss-Wright C46D was operating as flight BFL302 from Déline Airport (CYWJ), NT, to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, with 3 crew on board. While in cruise the number 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney-USA, R-2800-51M1) backfired; temperatures and pressures were normal. The flight crew elected to shut down the engine. BFL302 completed an uneventful single-engine approach and landing onto Runway 10 at CYZF. BFL302 stopped on Taxiway C and was towed to the Buffalo Airways Ltd. hangar.

C-FEQW, a Summit Air Ltd. Dornier DO228-202, was operating as training flight SUT01T at the Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. During a crosswind landing, after brake application, the left main landing gear tire burst and directional control was lost and the aircraft veered off the side of the runway. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft.

F-GSPE, Un Boeing 777-228ER exploité par Air France, effectuait le vol AFR021 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport Los Angeles Intl , Los Angeles, CA (KLAX) à destination de l'aéroport Paris-Charles de Gaulle (LFPG). À 123NM NW de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL), l'équipage a déclaré une urgence dû à la présence de fumée dans la cabine et a dérouté l'appareil vers CYUL où les véhicules d'urgence ont été déployés. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre à 0203Z. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

N679AE, un Embraer ERJ-145LR exploité par Piedmont Airlines sous l'indicatif PDT5796, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Philadelphie Intl (KPHL), PA, à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC. C-GLQV, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-402 exploité par Porter Airlines sous l’indicatif PTR2473, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON, à destination de CYUL. L’unité des services de la circulation aérienne (ATS) a assigné un cap de 30 degrés plutôt que de 260 degrés à PDT5796 et l’espacement avec PTR2473 a été réduit à 2,4 milles nautiques (NM) et 700 pi alors qu'un espacement de 3 NM et 1000 pi était requis.

C-GPAV, un Piper PA-23-250 exploité par Cargair Ltée., effectuait un vol d'entraînement local selon les règles de vol à vue de l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU), QC. C-FXPR, un Diamond DA42 exploité par Cargair Ltée., effectuait un vol d'entraînement local selon les règles de vol aux instruments de CYHU. Alors qu'il était sur un guidage radar sur un cap de 060, C-GPAV s’est rapproché à 0,5 nm de C-FXPR qui était en approche aux instruments pour la piste 24 droite alors que l'espacement requis était de 3 nm. L'espacement requis était de 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical et 3 nm sur le plan horizontal.

N670UA, a United Airlines Boeing 767-322 (ER) departed as flight UAL3 from Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD), IL, USA, to Zurich Airport (LSZH), Switzerland. On departure, the flight crew suspected a blown tire after hearing a loud bang but continued the climb to enroute altitude; at 2331 UTC, when the aircraft was approximately 25 nm south of North Bay, ON, the flight crew declared an emergency and requested to return to KORD. The aircraft was cleared to KORD and exited Canadian airspace without further incident.

C-GCBK, a De Havilland DHC-8-314 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP., departed Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, on an IFR flight to Island Lake Airport (CYIV), MB. During the climb after takeoff, the #2 engine oil pressure gauge was fluctuating and then went to zero. The red oil pressure annunciator light did not illuminate. The flight crew followed the quick reference handbook, shut down the #2 engine and declared an emergency. The aircraft returned to CYWG and landed without further incident. The operators' maintenance department discovered a faulty connector on the #2 oil pressure gauge.

C-FACX, a Cessna 182G operated by Airborne Petawawa, was being flown on a local flight from Pembroke Airport (CYTA), ON, within a 25 nm-radius of the airport. The aircraft was in a skydiving configuration and equipped with a “jump-door” STC modification on the right side. The pilot-in-command was flying and executing a parachute jump from 12 000 feet ASL. An experienced flight instructor was also on board to observe the pilot and to provide feedback to the parachute jump school. After the three jumpers exited the aircraft, the pilot was unable to close the jump door in accordance with the instructions of the associated STC. The pilot and the flight instructor struggled with handling and closing the door. During that time, for reasons undetermined, the aircraft’s airspeed increased beyond the certified limitation for operation of the aircraft with the door open. Very shortly after (1-2 seconds), the jump door was ripped from the aircraft and departed the fuselage. As a result, the right wing received damage (punctures), which caused fuel to leak for the remainder of the flight. The right-wing flap received a significant dent. The aircraft landed without further incident. The aircraft, from top-of-descent to being parked on the ramp, leaked approximately 50 litres of avgas and was still leaking fuel onto the ramp after shutdown.

C-FBZN, a Geotech Aviation Eurocopter AS 350 B3 helicopter, was returning from a local survey flight with the intended destination of Thunder Bay Intl (CYQT), ON, with a broken survey loop as a slung load. When C-FBZN was approximately 1.6 miles from CYQT, the cables on the loop broke and the survey loop fell in a field near Fort William Historical Park. There was no damage to persons or property on the ground. The load has since been recovered by the operator.

C-GSJB, an Airbus A319 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1550 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QB, to Fredericton International Airport (CYFC), NB. The aircraft was being operated with the APU deferred per the MEL. During the descent, the flight crew received an ECAM alert related to the integrated drive generator (IDG) No.2 low oil pressure. After actioning the QRH, the crew declared a PAN-PAN and continued to CYFC without further incident.Maintenance removed and replaced the IDG and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FYXF, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1634 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL. During cruise phase of flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue duties. The duties were redistributed among the cabin crew and the flight was completed without further incident.

C-FKGE, a Kudlik Aviation Pilatus PC-12/47 conducting flight KUK761, departed from Chesterfield Inlet Airport (CYCS), NU to Rankin Inlet Airport (CYRT), NU. Shortly after starting the descent from 4000 feet ASL, the flight crew heard noise from the engine and then the engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-67B) lost power. The flight crew completed the associated memory items for the engine power loss, declared a MAYDAY, and landed the aircraft on the sea ice with the gear in the retracted position approximately 5 miles east of CYRT. The ELT did not activate automatically but was manually activated. There were no injuries to the 2 crew and 1 passenger. The local RCMP and fire department responded and arrived on site for rescue approximately 1 hour 20 minutes after the landing.

C-GISM, a Westjet B737 Max 8 was operating flight WJA1532 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (KPHX), AZ. During cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue with assigned duties. These duties were reassigned to the remaining cabin crewmembers. The flight attendant did not occupy their jumpseat for landing. EMS met the aircraft on arrival.

C-GNLE, a Nolinor Aviation Boeing 737-200 operating as flight NRL943, had departed Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU for an IFR flight to Val D'Or (CYVO), QC. During the climb after takeoff from CYRT, the left engine (Pratt & Whitney USA JT8D-17) was shut down due to low oil quantity indications. The flight crew completed the associated checklists and a PAN PAN was declared. After burning fuel for 45 minutes, the aircraft returned to CYRT for an uneventful landing. There were no injuries to passengers and crew.The aircraft was removed from service and the operator's maintenance is conducting an inspection to determine the cause of the low oil quantity.

C-GPCJ, a Pacific Coastal Airlines SAAB 340B was conducting flight WS3003 from Lethbridge Airport (CYQL), AB, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the approach into CYYC, when the flight crew selected the landing gear down, they observed a landing gear indication light anomaly. The flight crew aborted the approach, completed the appropriate quick reference handbook procedure, declared an emergency and returned for an uneventful landing at CYYC. There were no injuries.

C-GPGH, un De Havilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Provincial Airlines sous l'indicatif PVL831, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Au départ, lors de la rétraction du train d'atterrissage, le voyant d’avertissement (caution light) du train d’atterrissage s’est allumé et la lumière ambre de l’indicateur du train avant est resté allumée malgré une rétraction du train. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée. L'équipage a déclaré l'état d'urgence (PAN PAN). Un déroutement vers CYQB a été effectué et l'extension du train a été fait en mode alternatif avant que l'avion se pose sans encombre sur la piste 06. L’avion a ensuite été remorqué jusqu’au terminal.

C-GZJC, un Dehavilland Dash-8-103 exploité par Air Creebec sous l'indicatif CRQ270, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Waskaganish, QC (CYKQ) à destination de Val d'Or, QC (CYVO) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 13 passagers à bord. À environ 80 nm au nord de CYVO, l’équipage a remarqué une baisse de pression d’huile du moteur numéro 2. Le moteur a été éteint et la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée. L'équipage a déclaré l'état d'urgence (PAN PAN) et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre à CYVO.

C-GIZT, un planeur monoplace de marque Rolladen Schneider LS-4 privé, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aérodrome de Saint-Dominique, QC (CSS4). Après avoir effectué un vol d’environ 2 heures, le pilote a joint le circuit vent arrière gauche de la piste 15 à 1600 pieds ASL pour atterrir sur la partie gazonnée côté gauche de la partie asphaltée. Après avoir effectué les procédures de vérification habituelles, établi une vitesse de 57 – 60 KIAS et sorti le train d’atterrissage, le pilote a déterminé qu’il était un peu haut sur l’approche. Le pilote a manœuvré pour perdre un peu plus d’altitude. Après être établi en base, le pilote a observé que l’altitude diminuait trop rapidement. Il a effectué un virage vers la gauche pour se rapprocher de la piste et a effectué les corrections nécessaires pour corriger le taux de descente. Une fois établi en approche finale et à environ 200 pieds du seuil de piste, le pilote a regardé son anémomètre qui indiquait une vitesse de 51 nœuds. Il a poussé le manche pour reprendre de la vitesse et entrer les aérofreins. En très courte finale, au moment où le planeur s’est retrouvé à la même hauteur que la cime des arbres qui bordent le côté ouest du seuil de la piste 15, le planeur s’est soudainement enfoncé et a percuté le sol brisant le train d’atterrissage. Le planeur a poursuivi sa course sur le ventre sur une distance approximative de 150 pieds. Une fois le planeur immobilisé, le pilote est sorti sans difficulté et n’a pas subi de blessure.

The Conair Group Incorporated Aero Commander 690A (registration C-GGAA) departed Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, on flight FGD138 under instrument flight rules to High Level Airport (CYOJ), AB, with 2 flight crew members on board. While in cruise flight at Flight Level 230, the right engine (Garrett, TPE331-10T-516K) power and fuel flow indications began to fluctuate. The crew declared an emergency with air traffic control and initiated a descent with the intention of diverting to Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC. Once power was reduced on the affected engine, the fluctuating engine indications stabilized. The crew consulted with maintenance and elected to return to CYXX where the flight landed with emergency services standing by. During the landing roll, after reverse thrust was commanded, the aircraft departed the runway centreline to the right, but remained on the paved surface of the runway. There were no injuries. The tire on the right main landing gear had a 7 cm tear on the inner sidewall. There was no other damage to the aircraft, which was towed from the runway to a company hangar. There were no injuries.A maintenance inspection determined that the engine fluctuations were caused by a faulty T2 temperature sensor located in the right engine inlet. The sensor was replaced, an engine ground run was conducted, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FYHN, a Custom Helicopters Ltd. Bell 206L departed from Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL, to Pangnirtung (CYXP), NU, on a VFR flight. The pilot was the sole occupant, and the trip would require planned fuel stops along the route, the first one planned for Nain Airport (CYDP), NL. About 75 nm north of CYYR, the visibility decreased due to snowfall and the pilot turned from the planned route to evaluate if visibility would improve. Visibility was poor and the pilot made multiple turns, began a descent, made a left turn, and struck the frozen surface of Lewis Lake (54°33.85' N, 060°16.23' W) while travelling parallel with the north shoreline of the lake. The helicopter rolled after striking the ice surface and came rest inverted. The pilot was able to egress through the right front door and activated the SOS feature of a portable satellite communicator that was pre-programmed to send a message to the company operations department. The pilot also ensured that the ELT was selected ON, directly at the ELT unit. The pilot changed out of wet clothes and sheltered in the helicopter wreckage to wait for the search and rescue services. JRCC Halifax received the ELT signal and dispatched a SAR helicopter which transported the pilot to CYYR. The pilot received medical attention for minor head and hand injuries and was released. The melting ice conditions at Lewis Lake necessitated an immediate wreckage recovery, and the TSB did not deploy. The operator documented site and wreckage information on behalf of the TSB during the wreckage recovery operations on 4 and 5 May 2024.

C-GJZD, a De Havilland DHC-8-402, operated by Jazz Aviation LP, as flight JZA7709 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, declared a PAN PAN emergency due to an engine issue. A No. 1 Engine Low Power Caution illuminated on approach. The flight crew elected to go-around, troubleshoot and found no faults. The crew attempted a second approach and the same caution light illuminated. The crew declared a PAN PAN emergency and elected to divert to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. The aircraft landed safely in CYYZ on Runway 24L. Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting attended the arrival; the aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.

C-GILZ, a West Coast Helicopters Maintenance and Contracting Limited Airbus 350 B2 helicopter, departed the Port McNeill Aerodrome (CAT5), BC, under visual flight rules to conduct heli-slinging operations approximately 45 nautical miles to the east with only the pilot on board. During the second slinging lift of the day, the pilot intended to communicate with the ground crew via radio but unintentionally squeezed the remote hook release instead of the push to talk button. The net of equipment fell into a forested area. There were no injuries, and the helicopter was not damaged.

C-GFEH a Sunwing B737-800 was operating flight SWG6553 from Varadero - Juan Gualberto Gómez International Airport (MUVR), Cuba to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Following engine start, the cabin crew reported that a momentary billow of heavy white smoke came from the forward galley oven. The circuit breaker for the oven was pulled and the quick reference handbook checklist was actioned.The aircraft returned to the gate where maintenance inspected the oven and placed it under NEF deferral. Due to the duty day restrictions, the flight was rescheduled for later that day and departed without further issue.

An Aerospatiale AS 350 BA helicopter (registration C-FXEJ) operated by Aberdeen Helicopters Limited, took off from Vernon Airport (CYVK), BC, on a local training flight under visual flight rules with 2 crew members and 1 passenger on board. After a short time in flight, the hydraulics were shut off to accommodate a training exercise. A few minutes later, the helicopter began to pitch nose down. The pilots were able to mitigate, but not stop, the nose-down attitude. The helicopter hit the ground nose-down but remained upright. The aircraft was substantially damaged. There were no injuries.The TSB is continuing its investigation.

C-GPNE, a Pal Airlines Ltd. De Havilland DHC-8-402 was conducting a charter flight, PVL3072, from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL. During the roll out phase after landing, the aircraft overran Runway 10. Once the aircraft stopped St. John's ATC made contact with the flight crew to determine if they required assistance to which the flight crew confirmed they did. ARFF responded. No injuries were reported and there was minimal damage to the aircraft. TSB deployed two investigators.

C-GKVL a Sunwing Airlines B737-800 was operating flight SWG259 from Abel Santamaria International Airport (MUSC), Santa Clara, Cuba to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During cruise, the right flight management computer failed. The quick reference handbook checklist was completed and approximately 20 minutes later, the left flight management computer also failed, and the checklist was completed again. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC. The right flight management computer was recovered, and the flight crew downgraded the PAN PAN; ATC maintained priority for the aircraft's arrival in CYUL and the flight was completed without further incident.

C-GXCN, un Dehavilland Dash-8-106 exploité par Air Creebec sous l’indicatif CRQ703, était stationné sur la rampe d’embarquement à l’aéroport de Val d’Or, QC (CYVO) avec à son bord 3 membres d’équipage et 21 passagers en préparation pour un départ à destination de Moosonee, ON (CYMO). Une fois les documents signés par les pilotes et remis à un membre du personnel au sol, ce dernier a quitté l’avion par la porte-escalier. Au même moment, l’équipage a entendu un bruit de claquement provenant du compartiment servant de penderie à l’agent de bord. De la fumée a commencé à apparaître sous la porte. L’équipage a ordonné l’évacuation de l’aéronef et a fermé l’alimentation électrique. La fumée a cessé et s’est dissipée. Une première évaluation de la situation par la compagnie a permis de constater qu’un des câbles qui retient la porte-escalier a été brisé et qu’il serait entré en contact avec 2 connecteurs électriques sous tension.

C-FXYK, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-8 was operating as flight WS2164 from Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, to Puerto Vallarta/Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International (MMPR), Mexico, with 6 crew members and 100 passengers on board. During cruise, approximately 19 minutes into the flight, a flight attendant became unwell and was unable to perform their duties. The crewmember's duties were distributed to the remaining crewmembers and the flight proceeded as planned. The affected crew member did not occupy their jump seat for landing in MMPR.

C-FXMY, a Keewatin Air LP Beech B200 operating as flight KEW209, was taxiing for a flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to the Sanikiluaq Airport (CYSK), NU, with 2 crew and 2 passengers (medical team) on board. As the aircraft was taxiing on taxiway Hotel, the smell of electrical smoke was identified by the crew. After a scan of the cockpit, smoke and arcing could be seen emanating from the pneumatic pressure gauge on the copilot side. The emergency evacuation procedure and memory items were conducted. The passengers and the pilots completed a non-eventful evacuation without injuries. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) responded and personnel identified a warmer than normal temperature coming from the right-hand circuit breaker panel. Shortly thereafter, and upon confirmation from ARFF that no threat existed, the aircraft was towed to the ramp.

The flight crew of NXT Jet Inc, flight KPO455, a Gulfstream Aerospace Gulfstream IV 4, on a flight from Naples Municipal Airport (KAPF), Florida to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, declared an emergency due to a pressurization issue. The flight crew of the aircraft elected to continue towards CYYZ; supplemental oxygen was used in the flight deck. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GJZT, un Bombardier CRJ900 (CL-600-2D24) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA958, effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport international O’Hare de Chicago (KORD), IL à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Une fumée grise est apparue dans la cabine de pilotage alors que l’aéronef était à 3000 pieds en descente pour atterrir sur la piste 24R à CYUL. L’équipage a avisé le contrôleur aérien et déclaré une urgence. L’aéronef a atterri sans encombre et a quitté la piste pour s’arrêter sur une voie de circulation où un véhicule des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) l’a rejoint. La fumée dans la cabine de pilotage s’est dissipée et l’avion a pu circuler vers une porte de débarquement une fois l’inspection complétée. Le débarquement s’est déroulé normalement et sans encombre.

OH-LTM, un Airbus 330-302 exploité par Finnair sous l’indicatif FIN10, effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport international O’Hare de Chicago (KORD), IL à destination de Helsinki-Vantaa (EFHK), Finlande. Environ 1h30 après le décollage, l’équipage a observé un message indiquant que le niveau d’huile du moteur no 1 diminuait vers 0.6 QT. La pression et la température d’huile étaient dans les limites normales. Après un certain temps, l’équipage a observé que la pression d’huile a commencé à fluctuer et à graduellement diminuer. Environ 1 heure plus tard, la pression d’huile du moteur no 1 a atteint 10 PSI activant un message d’avertissement de fermer le moteur no 1. L’équipage a procédé à l’arrêt du moteur no 1 et a déclaré une urgence au service du contrôle aérien. Un déroutement vers l’aéroport international John F. Kennedy aux États-Unis (KJFK) a été effectué et où l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre. L’inspection du moteur no 1 par un service de maintenance a révélé qu’une fuite d’huile est survenue au niveau d’un joint du démarreur.

C-FJFW, a Chartright Air Inc. Falcon 2000EX was operating flight HRT223 from Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), CA, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Shortly after takeoff, the crew declared an emergency due to a left engine failure. The crew elected to return to KPSP. The aircraft landed safely on runway 31L and taxied under its own power. Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) responded, and a runway sweep was conducted by operations.

C-GCPJ, a Bell B429 operated by the Canadian Coast Guard, was conducting slinging operations as flight CTG438 in the area of Drum Head Harbour, 32 nm SE of Port Hawkesbury Aerodrome (CYPD), NS. After departing the sling staging area, while over the water at approximately 300 feet ASL and 0.6 nm S of the staging area, the pilot checked the net load from the long line window. While reaching to reduce the collective for controllability, the pilot inadvertently activated the remote cargo release button on the top of the collective. The load was jettisoned from approximately 300 feet into the ocean.

C-FLQY, a DeHavilland DHC-8-402 registered to Porter Airlines Inc., was conducting flight POE2370 from Moncton/ Greater Moncton Roméo Leblanc International Airport (CYQM), NB, to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. While enroute in level cruise, the flight crew noticed that an engine start select light was illuminated. The flight crew completed the quick reference handbook checklist which directed the flight crew to land immediately at the nearest suitable airport. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC and requested to divert to Fredericton International Airport (CYFC), NB. The aircraft landed safely at 11:14Z with ARFF standing by.Maintenance conducted an inspection and was not able to duplicate the fault. As a precautionary measure, the RL1 contactor, the K1 contactor and the engine start control panel were replaced. The system was checked serviceable, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GUPG, an Air Canada A220 was operating flight ACA1334 from Ixtapa-Zihuatanejo International Airport (MMZH), Mexico, to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Enroute, the flight crew received EICAS advisory for hydraulic system 2 loss of pressure and fluid. The flight crew completed the checklist, and the decision was made to divert to Nashville International Airport (KBNA), Tennessee. A Pan Pan was declared and nosewheel steering was lost on arrival. Aircraft was stopped on runway and towed.Maintenance investigation is ongoing. #2 hydraulic rudder PCU's return line identified, line is cracked. 3B ACMP circuit breaker was reset.

C-GJTH, an Air Canada Rouge A321 was operating as flight ROU1937 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. During the cruise phase of flight, a flight attendant was injured and unable to continue their assigned duties. The duties were redistributed among the cabin crew and the flight was completed without further incident.

C-FFHB, a Geodesy Group Inc. Piper PA-31 (serial number 31-40) was conducting aerial photography in the vicinity of the Grand Prairie Airport (CYQU), AB, just above flight level 180 when the pilot declared an emergency due to an engine failure (Lycoming TIO-540-J2BD). The pilots completed the appropriate checklist procedure and landed safely on Runway 12 at CYQU. The aircraft was then taxied to the ramp. Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) personnel responded and escorted the aircraft until the pilot advised that no further assistance was required.The company is currently investigating the cause of the engine failure.

C-GBIJ, un Airbus 319-114 exploité par exploité par Air Canada Rouge LP sous l’indicatif ROU1965, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 98 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage. Lorsque l’avion a fait un palier au FL220, la puissance des moteurs a été réduite et le moteur gauche (CFM International, CFM56-5A5) a démontré les symptômes d'un décrochage du réacteur. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et réduit la puissance du moteur affecté au ralenti résolvant ainsi la condition avant de poursuivre son vol vers CYUL. L’avion s’est posé sur la piste 24R sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil. Une inspection boroscopique du réacteur a révélée des dommages aux ailettes à plusieurs niveaux du compresseur haute pression.

C-GJZC, un Bombardier DHC-8-402 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7971, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport, ON (CYTZ) avec 23 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Lors de la montée après le décollage, l’équipage a constaté un écart important entre les commandes de vol de gauche et celles de droite. L’équipage a ensuite déclaré un état d’urgence et a avisé l'unité de contrôle aérien (ATC) d'un retour à CYUL. L’appareil s'est posé sur la piste 24R sans encombre. Une inspection par le service de maintenance a déterminé que la tension des câbles de contrôle des ailerons était hors limite. La tension a été ajustée et l'appareil remis en service.

C-GAWS, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-800 operating as flight WJA271, departed Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, on an IFR flight to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While in cruise, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue with their assigned duties. The flight continued uneventfully to CYYC.

C-FSWE, a Wesjet Encore Ltd. De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-8-402 (serial number 4517) was operating as WEN3145 on a flight from Calgary Intl. Airport (CYYC), AB to Edmonton Intl. Airport (CYEG), AB. At 1721 Mountain Daylight Time, while on approach to Runway 30, the crew declared a PAN emergency due to a landing gear indication issue. The flight crew carried out a missed approach to troubleshoot the problem. The flight crew verified via tower and other observers that the landing gear was extended. The aircraft landed safely at CYEG.Post-occurrence maintenance: WestJet Encore Ltd. found the problem to be a burnt out bulb; it was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GJZC, un De Havilland DHC8-402 exploité par Jazz Aviation, effectuait le vol JZA7130 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport l'aéroport MacDonald-Cartier Intl, Ottawa (CYOW).Lors d'un départ autorisé de la piste 06L pour une altitude de 3000 pieds et un cap à 350 degrés, JZA7130 a tourné rapidement à ce cap après le décollage, venant en conflit avec le départ précédent. L'autre aéronef C-GLQG, un De Havilland DHC8-402 exploité par Porter Airlines sous l'indicatif de vol PTR2472 à destination de l'aéroport Billy Bishop Toronto City - Toronto, ON (CYTZ) qui virait vers un cap de 300 degrés. JZA7130 a répondu a l'avis de résolution de conflit du système d'alerte de trafic et d'évitement de collision (TCAS RA).  L'espacement minimal atteint entre les deux aéronefs a été de 700 pieds et 0.2 mille nautique (NM) alors que la norme est de 1000 pieds et 1.0 NM.

C-GWMO, an Aerospatiale, AS-350BA helicopter, operated by Heli Explore Inc., departed from the Attawapiskat Airport (CYAT), ON, destined for a remote camp, located 23 NM to the east on Akimiski Island, NU. The helicopter landed in an open area near the camp and left the engine running while a passenger deplaned. The passenger and another person from the camp were unloading the helicopter, when the passenger walked into the tail rotor and was fatally injured. The tail rotor and tail rotor gear box separated from the helicopter.

C-GAIG, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE753 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à destination de Kattiniq/Donaldson, QC (CTP9) avec 50 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en approche initiale au sud-est de CTP9, l’équipage a sélectionné les volets à la position 1. À ce moment, une alerte de pression faible de la pompe hydraulique A est survenue, et la quantité hydraulique du système A indiquait zéro. L’équipage a décidé d’effectuer une diversion à destination de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) et a déclaré une situation d’urgence auprès de l’ unité de contrôle aérien (ATC). L’avion s’est posé sur la piste 07 à CYVP sans encombre et s’est arrêté sur celle-ci. Il a ensuite été inspecté et remorqué au tablier. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-GEGC, an Air Canada A220 was operating as flight AC935 from Punta Cana International Airport (MDCP), Punta Cana, Dominican Republic, to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Toronto, ON. During the initial descent phase of flight, the flight crew received a Master Warning Light, along with stab control fault message, prim 1 pitch fault, prim 2 pitch fault, prim 3 pitch fault ECAM message. The flight crew followed the ECAM action and declared a PAN-PAN. The aircraft landed in CYYZ without further incident.Maintenance carried out an operational test of the pitch trim actuator and everything tested serviceable, bite test of the EFCS ground scanning checked serviceable. Detailed visual inspection of the pitch trim actuator IAW AMM checked serviceable. Suspect pitch trim actuator unit, actuator to be removed and replaced.

C-FIUA, an Air Canada B777-200 was operating flight ACA33 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Sydney/Kingsford Smith Airport (YSSY), Australia. During cruise, a flight crew member became ill and was unable to continue duties. The decision was made to return to CYVR due to crew duty constraints. An emergency was not declared, and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GDUZ, an Air Canada Boeing 767-38E was operating as Flight ACA7258 from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (KATL), Georgia, to El Dorado International Airport (SKBO), Bogotá, Colombia. During descent, the flight crew received a cabin altitude warning. Masks were donned and a PAN PAN was declared. Cabin pressure was regained and the flight crew cancelled the emergency declaration. The flight landed without further incident.Maintenance determined that the outflow valve required replacement.

C-GNGV, an Air Canada A220 was operating flight ACA1092 from San Diego International Airport (KSAN), CA, to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON.  In cruise, the flight crew conducted a LH engine shut down due to low oil quantity. After the quick reference handbook checklist was carried out, the RH bleed failed and lost both packs. The decision was made to divert to Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD), IL. A PAN PAN was declared, the aircraft landed without further incident and aircraft rescue and fire fighting followed aircraft to gate.

C-GISM, a WestJet Boeing 737 Max 8 conducting flight SWG9291, had departed Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, to Cancún International Airport (MMUN), Mexico. SWG9291 was cleared to climb from flight level 310 to flight level 410 on a southeast heading. C-GZQV, a Porter Airlines (Canada) Ltd. Embraer ERJ 190-400 conducting flight POE352, had departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. POE352 was level at flight level 330 and heading east. The air traffic controller had calculated SWG9291 to climb in behind POE352 with approximately 6 miles of separation. A conflict alert was triggered when separation was reduced to 700 feet vertically and 4.7 miles laterally when 1000 feet or 5 miles is required.

C-GNAM, an Airbus Canada Limited Partnership BD-500-1A11 (A220) was operating as Air Canada flight ACA1204, from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) Toronto, ON, to Miami International Airport (KMIA), Miami, FL. During the climb to the cruise phase of flight, the aircraft struck a flock of birds on the left side of the aircraft. The flight crew could feel light aircraft vibrations following the impact, declared a PAN-PAN and returned to CYYZ. The initial maintenance inspection found 3 blades damaged on the left engine and are continuing the engine inspection.

C-FDML, a Saab 340B aircraft operated by Pascan Aviation, was conducting IFR flight PSC584, from Îles-de-la-Madeleine Airport (CYGR), QC, to Québec/Jean Lesage International Airport (CYQB), QC. During cruise, the windshield cracked. An emergency was declared and the aircraft diverted to Montréal/St-Hubert Airport (CYHU), QC, where it landed without further incident.

C-FTHD, a Summit Helicopters Limited Bell 407 departed Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, under visual flight rules for a local training flight with 3 crew members on board. While in a low hover practicing fire suppression using a long line and a water bucket, the trainee pilot inadvertently selected the hook release instead of water release and inadvertently dropped the bucket and long line from approximately 15-20' feet above ground level. There were no injuries; the helicopter was not damaged.

C-GFCH, an Air Canada Rouge A320 was operating as flight ROU1662 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Southwest Florida International Airport (KRSW), Fort Myers, FL. During the climb to the cruise phase of flight, through 4000 feet ASL the flight crew selected Flaps 0 and received an ECAM "FLAPS LOCKED" message. The flight crew carried out the quick reference handbook procedures, declared a PAN-PAN and returned to CYYZ.

C-FRQA, a Canadian North ATR 72-212A was operating as AKT5858 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Cambridge Bay Airport (CYCB), NU. Upon landing in CYCB and decelerating through 70 knots, the aircraft began to veer to the left. The flight crew attempted to maintain the aircraft along the runway centerline but were unable to do so. The aircraft continued to the left and the aircraft excited the side of the runway at approximately 30 knots. The aircraft came to rest with the nose and left main landing gear in the snow along the side of the runway. The right main gear remained on the runway surface. The aircraft was shut down and eventually towed back to the apron. There were no injuries. The aircraft was undamaged. Company maintenance will advise TSB of the maintenance findings.

C-GJVO, a Perimeter Aviation Fairchild SA227-DC aircraft, was conducting flight BLS371 from Sault Ste. Marie (CYAM) ON. to Thunder Bay (CYQT) ON. While enroute to CYQT, the flight crew received a right-engine (Garrett TPE 331-12UHR) low oil pressure annunciation. The flight crew confirmed the oil pressure indication was below 40 PSI on the separate oil pressure gauge. The flight crew elected to continue running the engine for the remainder of the flight. After landing, the right engine torque would not reduce to flight idle, and the aircraft pulled to the left. The flight crew pulled the right engine stop, feather and shutdown the engine while maintaining runway center line with the application of brakes. The aircraft stopped on the runway, the other engine was shut down, and the everyone evacuated the aircraft via the main cabin door. There was some residual smoke from the right engine and from the 2 tires on right landing gear. There were no injuries to the 11 passengers and 2 crew. ARFF response was activated but there was no fire. The 2 right landing gear tires were deflated and will be replaced. The operator's maintenance found the right engine rear turbine bearing scavenge pump had failed and the right engine oil quantity had depleted.

F-GSQP, un Boeing 777-300 exploité par Air France sous l'indicatif AFR345, était second en ligne pour le décollage  depuis l'aéroport Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport International de Paris Charles de Gaulle, France (LFPG) ainsi que C-GITR, un Airbus A319-100 exploité par Air Canada Rouge sous l'indicatif ROU1640 qui était premier en ligne pour le décollage de CYUL à destination de l'aéroport internationale d'Orlando en Floride (KMCO). Alors que ROU1640 restait à l'écart de la ligne sud de l'aire d'attente de la piste 06 gauche, l'équipage n'a pas été en mesure d'accepter l'autorisation de décollage car plus de temps était nécessaire pour préparer la cabine pour le départ. L'unité de contrôle du trafic a ensuite demandé au prochain aéronef en ligne (AFR345) s'il pouvait passer ROU1640 sur la ligne nord de l'aire d'attente. AFR345 a confirmé et l'unité de contrôle l'a authorisé à s'aligner et se préparer pour décollage immédiat. Lors du dépassement, le bout de l'aile gauche de AFR345 est passé directement au-dessus du bout de l'aile droite de ROU1640. L'unité de contrôle a été informé et les 2 aéronefs ont ensuite décollés.

N22S, un Cessna Citation M2 en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Page Field Airport à Fort Myers, FL (KFMY) à destination de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec 1 pilote et 1 passager. Lors de l’atterrissage sur la piste 24R en conditions de vents traversier de la gauche à 23 nœuds avec rafales à 34 nœuds, le pilote a perdu la maîtrise directionnelle et l’avion a fait une sortie de piste à droite. L’avion a parcouru environ 550 pieds dans le gazon, le train principal droit s’est affaissé et l'avion s'est immobilisé en bordure droite de la piste à 2800 pieds du seuil. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FTAR, a Morningstar Air Express ATR-72 was operating as MAL7059 from Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK, to Calgary (CYYC), AB. The Image Air Charter Beech 200, C-FPNX, was operating from Cranbrook (CYXC), BC to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During final approach to CYYC Runway 17L, C-FPNX was sequenced to land following MAL7059. A loss of separation occurred just before MAL7059 touched down on the runway due to the closure rate of C-FPNX. Separation was reduced to 3.6 miles where 4 miles is required for wake turbulence spacing.

C-GJWE, a WestJet Encore Bombardier Inc. DHC-8-042 was operating as flight WEN3136 from Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Upon landing the aft fuselage / tail of the aircraft contacted the runway, illuminating the” TOUCHED RUNWAY” warning light in the master caution panel. There were no injuries. The aircraft taxied to the gate and deplaned the passengers and unloaded the baggage as normal. Following the flight company maintenance determined that there was a substantial amount of damage to the lower rear portion of the fuselage. The aircraft was removed from service.UPDATED 15 AUGUST 2024

C-GBYN, a Beech B200 King Air registered to Keewatin Air LP, was conducting flight KEW201 MEDEVAC from Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL, to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, with a planned enroute fuel stop at Québec/Jean Lesage International Airport (CYQB), QC. Shortly after departure from Runway 26, the flight crew received a LH engine fire indication. The crew arrested their climb, actioned the appropriate checklist memory items which led them to shut down the LH engine. The crew then declared an emergency with ATC and requested to return for Runway 08. While maintaining visual contact with the ground, the crew navigated and conducted a single engine landing on Runway 08. Upon landing on the wet runway, the aircraft continued beyond the end of the runway, striking two runway end lights and coming to a stop on the paved surface, approximately 30 feet beyond the runway end lights. Both flight crew and 3 passengers were uninjured.

C-GFHG, a Super T Aviation Beech 95-B55 was operating on a local training flight from Medicine Hat Airport (CYXH), AB. Upon completion of the training flight, the aircraft was returning to CYXH for a full stop landing on RWY 03. Upon touch down, the nose gear began to collapse and the student pilot executed a touch and go. Control of the aircraft was transferred to the flight instructor, who remained pilot flying for the remainder of the flight. The aircraft flew to the North of the airport to troubleshoot the issue and the flight crew declared an emergency. The aircraft returned to the airport and conducted 3 low passes while activating the emergency landing gear extension. The manual extension was not successful. The aircraft conducted a landing with aircraft rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) standing by. After touchdown, as the aircraft was rolling out, the nose gear collapsed, and the aircraft came to rest on the runway. ARFF immediately arrived on scene. There were no injuries.Company maintenance will advise TSB of the maintenance findings.

C-GKKN, a Westjet B787-9 was operating flight WJA2056 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Cancún International Airport (MMUN), MX. During the cruise phase of flight, a cabin crew member became ill. The cabin crew member was unable to perform their assigned duties and was not in their assigned jumpseat for landing. These duties were reassigned to the remaining cabin crew members.

C-GJXE, un Airbus A220-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif AC1208, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport international de Miami, FL, (KMIA) avec 5 membres d'équipage et 136 passagers à bord. Lorsque l'aéronef était en monté après un décollage depuis CYUL, l'équipage à reçu un message ''Engine nacelle overheat'' sur le moteur numéro 2. Les procédures du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) ont été effectuées mais le message a persisté. L'équipage a procédé à l'arrêt du moteur 2 et a déclaré l'état d'urgence (PAN PAN). L'appareil est revenu se poser à CYUL sans encombres avec les services d'urgence de l'aéroport en attente. Le personnel de maintenance a conduit des inspections et remplacé les pièces suivantes: ''Buffer Air Pressure sensor (BAPS), Buffer Air Valve Selenoid and Valve Assy - Buffer Shut Off''.  L'aéronef a été remis en service après avoir conduit un essai de ''windmilling'' de façon satisfaisante.

C-GFDU, an Air Canada Rouge A320 was operating flight ROU1705 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, NV. During descent, on approach for runway 19R, the flight crew was issued a traffic advisory for a helicopter in vicinity. Upon configuring and arming the approach, the flight crew received a TCAS RA - Monitor Vertical Speed command. The flight crew complied with the command and the alert subsequently cleared. As a result, the aircraft was too high on approach, and the flight crew conducted a go-around. The flight was subsequently completed without further incident.

C-GCIV, a Transport Canada Bell 429 helicopter departed Port Hardy Airport (CYZT), BC, as flight CTG435 under visual flight rules to Scarlett Point (CBJ7), BC, with only the pilot on board.  The helicopter was helislinging a load consisting of a bundle of rebar and a white bag containing 300 pounds of steel mounting brackets which was attached and suspended below the bundle of rebar. Approximately 1 nautical mile SE of Scarlett Point, ground personnel heard a splash and when the helicopter arrived at Scarlett Point, the white bag was empty. There were no injuries; the helicopter was not damaged.

C-FEYP un Beech King Air A100 exploité par Propair sous l'indicatif PRO102T effectuait un vol d'entrainement local selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, l'équipage a eu une alerte de fuite d'air de prélèvement moteur provenant du côté gauche. Le moteur associé a été éteint et l'hélice mise en drapeau. Peu de temps après, le même signal est apparu pour le côté droit. L'état d'urgence (mayday) a été déclarée et l'appareil a été redirigé directement vers CYUY où il s'est posé sans encombre. Les services d'urgence de l'aéroport ont été mis en attente. Le circuit d'avertissement du système d'air a été trouvé brisé au collecteur. La ligne a été remplacée, le système a été testé et l'appareil remis en service.

C-FIAI, un De Havilland DHC8-314 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE859 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Kingston, ONT (CYGK) avec 30 passagers et 3 membres d'équipage. En montée initiale, l'équipage a noté que le levier de puissance du moteur numéro 1 devait être plus avancé que le numéro 2 pour obtenir un couple de montée acceptable et que la consommation de carburant était beaucoup plus élevée. L'agent de bord a rapporté qu'il y avait une fuite de liquide sortant de la nacelle gauche. Le moteur numéro 1 a été éteint en vol et l'équipage a déclaré l'état d'urgence (pan pan) avant de revenir se poser à CYUL. Le personnel de maintenance a trouvé la fuite sur le répartiteur de débit de carburant où un joint torique était endommagé. Tous les raccords de tuyauterie dans cette région ont été inspectés et les joints toriques ont tous été remplacés. L'appareil a été remis en service.

C-FWZK, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Beechcraft 1900D, was operating as flight PCO1146 from Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. On approach into CYYJ, after selecting landing gear down, the landing gear safe lights did not illuminate. The crew conducted a missed approach and received vectors away from the airport during which the crew completed their checklists and communicated with their company maintenance. The crew observed that the landing gear circuit breaker was popped, and they reset it. The crew elected to divert to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, for operational reasons. The crew completed a manual gear extension and received 3 landing gear safe lights. The aircraft landed with aircraft rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) crews standing by. ARFF inspected the aircraft and then followed it as the crew taxied to the South Terminal. There was no damage to the aircraft and no injuries.Company Maintenance inspected the landing gear system and found the service valve contaminated and some corrosion on the time delay circuit breaker. The issues were addressed, and gear swings were successfully completed. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GENU, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DH8C-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3146 from Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB, to the Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While taxiing to the runway in CYMM, the flight crew braked abruptly to avoid a taxiway incursion. The cabin crew were standing in the cabin completing the safety briefing when the braking occurred and one of the cabin crew members fell and was injured. The flight crew taxied back to the gate and the injured cabin crew member was taken to the hospital.

C-GFKA, an Air Canada Rouge A321 was operating flight ROU1708 from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, NV, to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During the cruise phase of flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue duties. The duties were redistributed among the remaining cabin crew. The flight was completed without further incident.

C-FSDQ, a Boeing 737-800, operating as Air Canada flight ACA600 was in the process of boarding passengers at Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, Terminal 1, Gate 128, when a tractor pulling luggage carts struck the #1 engine nacelle. The tractor driver was seriously injured during the impact, but none of the passengers and crew received injuries. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN on apron frequency and requested ARFF. The flight was cancelled, and the aircraft was removed from service for inspection and maintenance.

C-GBQD, a Aero Commander 690A aircraft operated by Conair Group Incorporated, was conducting flight FDG135, a local training flight from Abbotsford International Airport (CYXX), BC, with 2 flight crew on board. While in a simulated hold southwest of the airport, the cockpit temperature became hot and the cockpit began to fill with smoke. The crew donned their oxygen masks and advised air traffic control (ATC) of their situation. No emergency was declared. They requested vectors for a visual approach to the airport. The crew began to run the quick reference handbook (QRH) checklist and elected to shut down the air cycle machine.  During the descent as power was reduced, the smoke dissipated. When power was increased to level off on the downwind, the smoke returned. The aircraft continued the approach and landed on Runway 19 without further incident. The aircraft was shutdown on the taxiway and was met by aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) trucks which had been placed on standby by ATC. After a visual inspection, the aircraft was towed to the company hangar by maintenance staff. There were no injuries.Company maintenance found that the ground blower, which provides cooling air for the air condition and pressurization system, failed. This resulted in hot bleed air flowing to the air cycle machine. The heat caused the atomization of residual oils in the air lines and created the smoke. The ground blower was replaced. Following a successful test flight and ground checks, the aircraft was returned to service.

N663UA, a Boeing 767-300 operated by United Airlines was conducting flight UAL921 from London Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK, to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), USA. During the cruise portion of the flight, the flight crew were notified of a security threat. After reviewing the company procedures, the flight crew declared an emergency and advised company personnel. The company corporate security was involved and deemed the threat non-specific and non-credible. The flight continued to KEWR and landed without further incident.

C-FTCA, an Air Canada B767-300 was operating flight ACA7258 from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (KATL), GA, to El Dorado International Airport (SKBO), Bogotá, Colombia. On takeoff, the flight crew received a master caution “C HYD SYS PRESS”. The quick reference handbook checklist was completed however the SYS pressure did not extinguish. In discussion with Dispatch and MOC, the decision was made to return to KATL. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GTJX, a Transwest Air Limited Partners (dba Rise Air) Saab 340B aircraft departed Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, on a visual flight rules post-maintenance flight with a return to CYXE. During the flight, a power reduction was initiated and the right engine abruptly lost power with torque indications dropping to zero. The emergency checklist was followed and an emergency was declared. The aircraft returned to CYXE and landed without further incident. Airport emergency services were standing by and followed the aircraft back to the apron.The operator's maintenance department replaced the Digital Engine Control Unit (DECU) as per the manufacturer's troubleshooting recommendations. A satisfactory test flight was conducted and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FOEW, de Havilland DHC0-2 MK3 (Turbo Beaver), equipped with amphibious floats and operated by the Province of Ontario, Ministry of Natural Resources, was on a Pilot Competency Check (PCC) flight with two pilots on board. After completing training, which included water landings and take-offs, the aircraft departed from the Killarney area destined for the North Bay Jack Garland Airport (CYYB), ON. The landing at CYYB was the final exercise, and to be performed as a flapless landing. The aircraft landed on runway 36 with the wheels in the up position, and after touchdown came to a stop. Although the Land/Sea switch was on Land position, the landing gear handle remained in the up position. The aircraft received damage to the keel on both floats but there were no injuries. It was reported that due to the flaps being up, the landing gear warning system was not operational. The operator reviewed their training criteria for this type of flight test and have decided to eliminate the flapless landing exercise for all their fixed wing aircraft.

C-GBKA, a Bamaji Air Inc. Cessna 185 was preparing to depart Slate Falls Airport (CKD9), ON, on a visual flight rules flight to Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON. While the pilot was attempting to start the aircraft's engine by manually turning the propeller, the engine started but the pilot was unable to enter the aircraft in time. The unoccupied aircraft proceeded across the apron and collided with trees and a snowbank. The pilot received minor injuries while attempting to arrest the movement of the aircraft. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GLNL, a Learjet 35A, operated by Latitude Air Ambulance, departed the Hamilton John C. Munro International Airport (CYHM), ON; during the initial climb out, it was reported that the flight crew experienced difficulties with the pitch trim and autopilot systems, and that the aircraft became difficult to control. The aircraft returned to the airport where it landed without further incident. There were no injuries.

C-FWEW, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-400 was operating as flight WEN3186 from Grande Prairie Airport (CYQU), AB, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the take-off roll the flight crew rejected the take-off due to the #1 propeller (Dowty Rotol R408/6-123-F/17) auto-feather not arming. The flight crew declared an emergency and stopped the aircraft on the remaining runway. The aircraft taxied back to the gate and deplaned the passengers.The maintenance team replaced the propeller electronic control unit for the number one propeller. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWBJ, a WestJet B737-700 was operating flight WJA2211 from Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International Airport (MMPR), Puerto Vallarta, MX, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. During cruise, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue performing the assigned duties which were re-assigned to the remaining crew members. EMS was requested by the flight crew. The ill flight attendant did not occupy a jumpseat for landing.

C-GTLS, a Kississing Lake Lodge Ltd. (dba Wings Over Kississing) Beech 100 was departing Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, on a visual flight rules training flight to Morden Regional Aerodrome (CJA3), MB. During the takeoff roll on Runway 18, as the power on both engines reached the propeller governing range of 2000 RPM, the right engine emitted a loud pop accompanied with asymmetric thrust and a large increase in the right interstage turbine temperature (ITT). The flight crew performed a rejected takeoff procedure, followed by an immediate shutdown of the right engine due to elevated ITT. When the pop occurred, the pilot-in-command observed a peak ITT of 820C. The aircraft returned to Apron 2.

C-FAFU, a privately registered Bearhawk Model B taildragger aircraft, was on the landing roll on runway 06/24 at Smith Falls-Montague (Russ Beach)(CYSH), ON, when the aircraft ground looped to the left and went off the runway. The aircraft's right main landing gear subsequently collapsed, and the aircraft came to rest on its right wing. All three occupants exited the aircraft without reported injuries. During a subsequent walk around of the aircraft it was noted that the control cables for the rudder had become disconnected. Pilot/Owner reported that the right rudder pedal was not attached to the brake system.

C-FIRN, a Sunwing B737-8 was operating flight SWG596 from Cancún International Airport (MMUN), MX, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During cruise, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue their duties for the remainder of the flight. The flight landed safely in MMUN without further incident.

C-GGTM, a Regina Flying Club Cessna 172N departed Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK, on a night visual flight rules rental flight to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, with a return to CYQR. During the return flight, in the vicinity of the community of Liberty, SK, the aircraft's engine experienced a partial loss of power. The pilot contacted CYQR ATC advising of the engine issue. ATC provided directions to the Regina Beach Aerodrome (CKL9), SK. The runway at CKL9 was not lighted and it was after dusk, so the pilot had difficulty locating the runway. The aircraft landed 0.3 NM beyond the departure end of Runway 14. During the landing roll, the nose wheel dug into the soft ground and the aircraft nosed over, coming to rest inverted. The pilot and two passengers exited the aircraft. The pilot and front passenger received minor injuries. The ELT activated. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GERR, a Zlin Z242L aircraft, operated by The Sault College of Applied Arts and Technology was conducting flight training at the Sault Ste. Marie Airport (CYAM), ON, with a student pilot and instructor on board. The instructor was demonstrating a simulated engine failure during take-off, with a high angle of climb. During the maneuver the aircraft reportedly stalled, and subsequently crashed onto the runway surface. The student received a serious injury and the aircraft was substantially damage.

C-GTSJ, un Airbus A332 exploité par Air Transat était en préparation au sol pour effectuer le vol TSC890 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport Gregorio Luperón Intl, Puerto Plata, République Dominicaine (MDPP) avec seulement  les 11 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors que l'aéronef était stationné à la barrière, un convoyeur à bagages est entré en collision avec l'aéronef endommageant la partie inférieure du fuselage arrière.  L'aéronef a été retiré de service et envoyé au hangar pour évaluation et réparation.

C-CGWRE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3242 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Brandon Municipal Airport (CYBR), MB. Shortly after take-off the flight crew noted an abnormal landing gear position indication. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and returned for landing in CYYC. The flight landed with no further issues.Following the flight, the maintenance team inspected the aircraft and found several rigging and servicing issues with the landing gear. These items were corrected and the aircraft was returned to service.

N309PQ, an Endeavor Air Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) operating as Delta flight EDV4986, was on route from Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport, (KMSP), MN, to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. The flight crew declared an emergency due to a loss of speed indication and reduced visual separation minimum (RVSM) indicators. The aircraft continued to its destination and landed without further incident.

C-GGNW, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland DHC-8-402 was operating as JZA7976 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. When departing CYTZ at FL230 the aircraft experienced a loss of pressurization. The flight crew performed an emergency descent and advised ATC. The aircraft subsequently continued to CYUL unpressurized and landed without further incident.

C-GDPI, un Beech King Air A100 exploité par Propair sous l'indicatif PRO102T effectuait un vol d'entrainement local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY). Lors de l'approche, le train d'atterrissage n'est pas sorti. L'équipage a procédé à la sortie manuelle du train tel que prévu par le manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et l' aéronef a atterri sans encombre. Le système a été inspecté et testé fonctionnel par le personnel de maintenance. Les interrupteurs de la boite de transmission ont été nettoyés et le contrôleur du moteur de la transmission a été nettoyé et testé fonctionnel. L'aéronef est retourné en service par la suite.

C-GGUH, a Can-West Corp Air Charters Ltd. Cessna 208B was conducting a charter flight from Fox Lake Aerodrome (CEC3), AB, to High Level Airport (CYOJ), AB. The aircraft lined up for takeoff on Runway 26, which is 3600 feet long and constructed of sand and gravel. During the takeoff roll, the pilot observed the airspeed reach approximately 65 knots. The pilot assessed that it was taking longer than usual for the aircraft to lift off and was concerned about climb performance and the presence of trees approximately 2000 feet past the end of the runway. Due to these concerns, the pilot elected to abort the takeoff by reducing power to flight idle then max reverse, selecting the flaps up and applying maximum braking. During the abort, the aircraft overran the runway onto the frozen, snow-covered ground. During the overrun, the aircraft crossed over a dirt berm and then veered to the right before coming to rest approximately 165 feet from the end of Runway 26. There were no injuries.

C-GZEW, un De Havilland DHC-8-314 (Dash-8) exploité par Air Creebec inc. sous l'indicatif CRQ5366, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aérodrome de Renard, QC (CFX5) à destination de l'aéroport de Chibougamau, QC (CYMT) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 23 passagers à bord. Au moment du décollage, une odeur de surchauffe électrique et de la fumée ont été constatées dans le poste de pilotage. L'équipage est revenu vers CFX5 pour se poser sans encombre sur la piste 06. Un fil relié à l'interrupteur de consigne de ceinture a été trouvé surchauffé. Le panneau de contrôle a été remplacé et l'appareil remis en service quelques heures plus tard.

C-GKMO, a Heli Source Ltd. Airbus AS 350 B2 helicopter was conducting external load operations in support of a construction project approximately 50 nautical miles north-northwest of the Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB. One of the external loads consisted of a mix of 2x4 inch boards and some 4x8 foot sheets of plywood. During the transit from the staging area to the remote construction site, some of the 2x4 inch boards fell out of the load. There were no injuries or damage to ground-based assets.

C-FYJP, an Air Canada Rouge A319, was conducting flight ROU1693 from Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL, USA, to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. During the approach in gusty conditions, and below approximately 50' AGL, the nose of the aircraft pitched down. The flight crew corrected the pitch but due to the proximity to the ground, the aircraft was subject to a hard landing. One passenger reported an injury to airline staff in the terminal; they were assessed at the local hospital and released later that evening. Additionally, a member of the cabin crew reported an injury but did not seek further treatment. The aircraft was subject to a detailed inspection, there were no faults found relating to the hard landing and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYSR, a Keewatin Air Beech B200 departed Sanikiluaq Airport (CYSK), NU, on an IFR flight to Churchill Airport (CYYQ), MB. When the aircraft was on approach to CYYQ and the landing gear was extended, the flight crew observed that the nose gear indicator did not show a down-and-locked indication while the main gear did. A missed approach was conducted and the flight crew flew a VFR hold while completing the quick reference handbook (QRH) checks and actions. The flight crew declared an emergency and consulted via satellite communication with the operator. The aircraft subsequently landed uneventfully at CYYQ. After landing, the flight crew shut down the engines on the runway and the aircraft was then towed to the apron.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and observed damaged wires in the undercarriage area.

C-FYSD, a Sunwing B737-800 was operating flight SWG7392 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Sangster International Airport (MKJS), Montego Bay, Jamaica. Approximately 300 miles from MKJS, the flight crew identified a fuel imbalance on the #1 fuel tank. The fuel leak and fuel imbalance checklists were completed however, the fuel imbalance was not rectified. The flight crew elected to divert to Cayo Coco/Jardines del Rey Airport (MUCC), Cuba. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.No leaks or faults were found by maintenance.

C-GHQL, un DHC-8-402 exploité par Hydro-Québec sous l'indicatif HYD142, effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC à destination de l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY). Durant la montée vers l'altitude de croisière, une odeur anormale ressemblant à du chlore a été détectée dans la cabine et dans le poste de pilotage. Presque au même moment, une indication de fumée dans la toilette a été affichée dans le poste de pilotage. La montée a été interrompue à 5000 pieds et une urgence PAN PAN a été déclarée. L'appareil est revenu se poser sans encombre à CYUL. L'équipe de maintenance a constaté qu'un nettoyage du compresseur du groupe auxiliaire a été effectué avant le vol et qu'un résidu de produit nettoyant aurait pu rester dans les conduits.

C-GAIW, un appareil de type De Havilland Dash 8-314 Cargo exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE885 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de la Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) à destination de l'aéroport de Kangiqsujuaq/Wakeham Bay, QC (CYKG) avec seulement 3 membres d'équipage. Au moment du toucher des roues à CYKG, la partie inférieure du train d'atterrissage principal gauche s'est détachée. L'avion a fait un rebond et a retouché le sol avec seuls les trains avant et droit. Le contrôle directionnel a été assuré et l'aéronef s'est immobilisé sur la piste. L'aéronef a subi des dommages substantiels au fuselage, à la nacelle, au moteur et à l'hélice. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GITP, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus 319-112 was operating flight ROU1633, from Sarasota Bradenton International Airport (KSRQ), FL, USA to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the cruise phase of flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue their duties. The duties were redistributed among the cabin crew, and the flight was completed without further incident.

C-GSJZ, a DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA362 from Windsor Airport (CYQG), ON, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the downwind, the flight crew observed a FLAP DRIVE caution message. They declared PAN PAN and continued their planned approach. They conducted an uneventful flapless landing, with ARFF standing by.

PH-BKC, a Boeing 787-10, operated by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines as flight KLM204, was departing from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, and was holding short of runway 06L. Meanwhile, SP-LSB, a Boeing 787-9, operated by LOT Polish Airlines, as flight LOT 5E was landing on runway 06L. After LOT 5E touched down, KLM204 taxied to position in preparation for take-off from runway 06L. When LOT 5E was about to exit the runway at taxiway C5, KLM204 was then cleared for immediate take-off. However, shortly afterwards, LOT 5E announced they would exit runway C7 instead (near the end of the runway). The Tower subsequently instructed KLM204 to abort its takeoff. At this time, the speed of KLM204 was about 110 knots; KLM204 aborted the take-off and vacated the runway at taxiway D1. The minimum distance between the two aircraft was approximately 5400 feet. Wet snow conditions were reported on the runway.

N770JM, an Embraer E-170 operated by American Eagle, was conducting flight ENY3641 from Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD), IL, USA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the downwind leg the flight crew encountered an issue with their trailing edge flaps. They declared an emergency and continued with their planned approach. The flight landed uneventfully with aircraft rescue and firefighting standing by.

C-GJAN, a Jazz Aviation CRJ900 was operating flight JZA823 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (KDCA), DC. On route, a fuel imbalance required quick reference handbook action. The imbalance was not able to be rectified therefore, the crew elected to divert to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GZXK, a privately operated Zenair CH701, was conducting a local recreational flight from the Edmonton Cooking Lake Aerodrome (CEZ3), AB, with one pilot and one passenger on board. On the return to CEZ3, the pilot's intention was to perform a touch-and-go on Runway 28. The initial landing was successfully completed, and power was applied to commence the subsequent take-off. Approximately 1600 feet of runway remained when the aircraft became airborne. After gaining approximately 50 feet of altitude, the pilot perceived a significant decrease in the aircrafts performance and made the decision to abort the take off and attempt to land on the remaining runway. The aircraft touched back down on the grass past the end of Runway 28, impacted an airport property perimeter fence and came to a stop in a ditch. Both occupants were uninjured and exited the aircraft. The aircraft received substantial damage.

C-FHZP, a Bell Helicopter Textron Inc. model 206 Jet Ranger operated by Airborne Energy Solutions Inc. was being operated in support of annual recurrent training of company pilots. On the occurrence flight, there was one flight instructor and one company pilot on board, and the exercise being performed was a 180-degree, descending auto-rotation with a planned power-on recovery. The maneuver commenced on the downwind leg of the traffic pattern. The power was reduced by the flight instructor and the pilot entered the auto-rotative descending turn with the intention of landing on the first third of Runway 11. After completion of the 180-degree turn and as the helicopter approached the runway surface, the pilot under instruction pulled aft on the cyclic in order to reduce the helicopters forward velocity, and up collective to reduce the rate of decent. Concurrently, the flight instructor re-applied engine power with the intention that the helicopter would not contact the runway surface but enter into a hover condition. As these events occurred near simultaneously, the helicopters tail boom made contact with the runway surface. When this occurred, the main rotor struck the aft section of the tail boom and severed it from the helicopter. The fuselage of the helicopter skidded approximately 20-30 feet along the runway while remaining upright with the engine running. Not knowing that the tail boom had been severed, the instructor pilot attempted to lift the helicopter into a hover; however, it was then immediately realized that there was a problem with the tail rotor control. The instructor pilot reduced power and shut the helicopter down. There were no injuries to either pilot. The helicopter was significantly damaged.

C-GJWN, an Air Canada Airbus 321-211 aircraft was conducting flight ACA601 from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. As ACA601 was preparing for pushback from a gate at CYHZ, a catering truck struck and damaged the rear fuselage of the aircraft aft of door 4L. The passengers were deplaned, and the aircraft was removed from service for maintenance. There were no injuries.

C-FIAI, un Dash-8-314 (DH8C) exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif AIE851, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL), à destination de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) avec 3 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de la montée en passant le niveau de vol 200, le pare-brise de droite s’est fissuré. Le pare-brise est demeuré en place et l’équipage a déclaré une urgence pour revenir à CYUL. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé et aucun autre dommage à l'appareil.

C-GEHY, an Air Canada Boeing 737-800 departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, on flight ACA970 under instrument flight rules to Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International Airport (MMPR), Puerto Vallarta, MX. Shortly after takeoff, the crew observed a dual autopilot fault. After discussions with airline operations, the decision was made to return to CYVR. Due to an overweight landing condition, a PAN PAN was declared, and the flight continued to CYVR where it landed without further incident. There were no injuries.The aircraft was removed from service and during troubleshooting, a corroded elevator pressure switch was found and replaced as well as a pressure switch electrical connector. The aircraft was tested as serviceable and returned to service.

C-GJZK, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 departed Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, on flight number JZA34 under instrument flight rules to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. After take-off, the crew selected the landing gear up and observed the nose gear light indicating amber and determined that the gear had retracted but the door remained open. The crew conducted the manual gear extension procedure, and 3 green down and locked lights illuminated. The crew declared a PAN PAN and completed the landing at CYVR without further incident.
