There were no injuries. Maintenance completed troubleshooting and replaced the nose landing gear solenoid sequence valve. Gear swings were carried out and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GENK, a Westjet Encore Limited de Havilland DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was operating as flight WEN3282 from Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Prior to top of descent, the crew observed a No.2 HYD ISO VLV (hydraulic isolation valve) caution light illuminated, and the No.2 hydraulic quantity indicated 10%. The crew actioned the appropriate checklists, declared a PAN PAN, and requested a vector for appropriate altitudes and speeds to conduct a manual gear extension. The crew conducted a manual gear extension and landed at CYVR without further incident.Maintenance determined the right main landing gear retraction actuator was leaking. The actuator was replaced, the aircraft was tested and returned to service.

C-IKRX, un paramoteur DTA combo 912 en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol local de posés-décollés selon les règles de vol à vue à un aérodrome privé à Saint-Bernard-de-Michaudville, Qc. Lors de la dernière approche, un câble de commande aurait subi une défectuosité, le pilote a tenté d’atterrir, mais a perdu le contrôle et s’est écrasé. Le pilote a subi des blessures mineures et l’aéronef a subi des dommages substantiels.

C-GHQI, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1746 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Juan Gualberto Gómez International Airport (MUVR), Matanzas, Cuba. During the cruise phase of the flight at FL300, the flight crew received a "BLUE HYD SYSTEM SERVICED" ECAM. ECAM actions were carried out and following consultation with Dispatch and MOC, the decision was made to return to CYUL. ATC was advised and routing back to CYUL was initiated. Subsequently, a PAN PAN was declared as a precaution. HYD B pressure was not available for the remainder of the flight. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and removed and replaced the B HYD electric pump with a serviceable unit.

C-FYMN, un Pilatus PC-12/47 exploité par Chrono Aviation inc. sous l'indicatif NDL987, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Quaqtaq, QC (CYHA) à destination de Kangirsuk, QC (CYAS) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 4 passagers. Lors de l’atterrissage par vent de travers (vents rapportés du 280 vrai à 26 kts avec des rafales à 36 kts), l’équipage a sélectionné l’inversion de poussée, mais rien ne s’est produit. Environ 5 secondes plus tard, au moment où le pilote allait remettre les gaz, l’inversion de poussée s’est enclenchée au maximum. L’équipage a perdu le contrôle et l’avion a fait une sortie latérale de piste à environ 20 kts et s’est immobilisé dans la neige. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé. L’avion a subi des dommages.

9H-ELF, an Air X Charter Ltd., Boeing B737-700 BBJ aircraft was conducting flight AXY536G from Birmingham Airport (EGBB), United Kingdom to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL. While in cruise flight at FL340 at about 57°07' N, 030°00' W the flight crew noted that fuel from the auxiliary fuel tanks was not transferring into the main tank. An option to land in Iceland was rejected because it would require an overweight landing, and the flight crew decided to divert to Gander International Airport (CYQX), NL, since there was sufficient fuel for that option. After leaving NAT High Level Airspace the flight crew coordinated with ATS for a diversion to CYQX where the flight landed without further incident. Maintenance personnel determined that 2 circuit breakers for the Auxiliary Tanks Transfer Channels A and B tripped due to a faulty Wing Spar Fuel Valve actuator.

C-FCMU, a Central Mountain Air Ltd. registered Beech 1900D was operating as flight GLR564 under instrument flight rules from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Quesnel Airport (CYQZ), BC. When near the initial approach fix, the crew selected flaps to 17°. The flaps did not extend from the retracted position. The crew entered a hold while they cycled the flap lever and checked the flap circuit breaker in an effort to troubleshoot the issue. The crew concluded that a flapless landing was required and made the decision to divert to Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC. In the diversion, the crew declared a PAN PAN. They completed a flapless landing with no further issues. There were no injuries reported and no damage to the aircraft.Maintenance conducted an inspection of the flap assembly and found the left safety switch was sticking in the open position. The aircraft has returned to service.

N845MH, a Boeing B767-432ER aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL1 from New York/John F. Kennedy Intl Airport (KJFK), NY to London/Heathrow Intl Airport (EGLL), England. When in cruise flight at about 50°57' N, 050°11' W, the flight crew observed an indicated airspeed disagree message. The flight crew referenced the quick reference handbook, identified the malfunctioning air data computer and contacted company operations and maintenance departments. The flight crew decided to return to KJFK, then declared an emergency and coordinated with the ATS for the air turnback to KJFK where a landing was made without further incident. Maintenance replaced the first officer side air data module, conducted a pitot static system test, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWRE, a Westjet Encore DeHavilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3205 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Grand Prairie Airport (CYQU), AB. During the initial climb after take-off, when the crew selected landing gear up, the flight crew received an amber nose landing gear door advisory light indication. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist, elected to return to CYYC and declared a PAN PAN with ATC in accordance with company SOPs. The flight crew completed the alternate landing gear extension checklist, and all three landing gear indicated down and locked. The aircraft completed an uneventful landing. There were no injuries.Company maintenance replaced the nose landing gear door actuator and released the aircraft back into service.

C-GNVR, un appareil de type Boeing 737-800 exploité par Sunwing Airlines Inc. sous l’indicatif SWG428 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport international de Punta Cana (MDPC), République Dominicaine. Peu après le décollage, un membre d'équipage de cabine n'était plus en mesure d'exercer ses fonctions en raison d'une incapacité physique. L'équipage de vol en a été informé et a demandé la présence des services médicaux à l'arrivée. L’avion s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GLQG, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-402 exploité par Porter Airlines, effectuait le vol PTR2205 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport d'Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW) à destination d’Halifax/Stanfield Int’l, NS (CYHZ). Alors que l'appareil passait 10 000 pieds en montée, l’équipage a constaté que la pression différentielle de la cabine était de 3,2 psi au lieu de 3,6 psi anticipé. L’équipage a vérifié que les contrôles de la pressurisation étaient normaux et a continué de surveiller la pression. Au niveau de vol 230 à environ 20 milles nautiques (nm) à l’ouest-sud-ouest de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL, l'équipage a fait un palier et remarqué que l’altitude de la cabine continuait d’augmenter. L’équipage a alors initié une descente d'urgence et a déclaré une urgence pour revenir atterrir à CYOW. L’altitude maximale atteinte par la cabine a été de 11 500 pieds. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé. Le personnel de maintenance a changé le contrôleur de la pression de la cabine et l’avion a été remis en service.

C-FTJX, a 2080061 Ontario Inc. (dba SkyCare Air Ambulance) Piper PA-31-350 was departing Big Trout Lake Airport (CYTL), ON, on a visual flight rules flight to Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON. During the application of power and forward movement of the aircraft for takeoff from CYTL, the main gear doors opened and the nose gear retracted. There were no injuries to the 5 passengers nor to the 2 crew members. The aircraft received substantial damaged. A post-occurrence cockpit survey indicated the nose landing gear handle was in the up position. Information gathered indicated a portable GPS yoke mount's clamp adjusting screw (installed on the left yoke) had white paint transfer from the landing gear handle. The operator's maintenance lifted the aircraft and removed the aircraft from the runway.The operator reported that the GPS mount's clamp is normally mounted with the adjusting screw on the left side of the yoke; however on this aircraft, the clamp's adjusting screw was mounted on the right side of the yoke. Control column movement on C-FTJX allowed the clamp's adjusting screw handle to contact the landing gear handle. The operator's maintenance also found that the aircraft's anti-retraction safety system had failed.

C-FGZO, a Top Aces Inc. A4N was operating a flight from Rostock–Laage Airport (ETNL), Germany to Nordholz/Cuxhaven Airport (ETMN), Germany. After take-off from ETNL, passing FL120, the fuel transfer light and fuel level low light illuminated. The fuel indicator indicated 1000lbs. An emergency was declared and a return to ETNL was conducted. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GVGA, un Beech 1900D exploité par Propair Inc. effectuait le vol PRO4800 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda (CYUY), QC, à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC. Peu après le décollage, en montée vers l'altitude de croisière, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence due à un problème avec le système avionique de l'appareil. Un retour vers CYUY a été effectué et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GWCM, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-700 was conducting flight WJA611 from Ottawa Macdonald–Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During a missed approach due to vehicles still on the runway, the crew contacted departure control and informed them that they did not have enough fuel to go-around again. This was acknowledged by the departure controller. No emergency was declared, and the aircraft landed without further incident. On touchdown the aircraft had approximately 7400 pounds of fuel onboard and was holding Saskatoon / John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK, as an alternate.

C-FVFN, a Vanguard Air Care Beech 200 departed the Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB, on an instrument flight rules flight to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, as flight VN06. While on approach to CYWG, the right gear down safe indicator did not illuminate when the landing gear was selected down. The flight crew cycled the gear twice but received the same indication. A missed approach was conducted and during the climb to a safe altitude, the right gear down safe indication illuminated as desired. The crew secured the cabin and prepared for landing with considerations for a gear failure. Aircraft rescue and fire fighting were notified and requested to be held on standby. The aircraft subsequently landed uneventfully at CYWG, and then taxied to the apron.The operator's maintenance identified a loose gear indicator connector. The connector was re-secured and several gear swings were performed with no further faults.

C-GJCT, a Boeing 757 aircraft, operated by Cargojet Airways, was conducting a maintenance test flight after engine work was carried out. The aircraft departed Hamilton John C Munro International Airport (CYHM) and shortly after the flight crew selected the flaps up, the left engine began to surge. The flight crew reduced engine power on the associated engine and declared a PAN PAN. The bleed air for the engine was shut off and no further surges occurred. The flight crew informed ATC that they would like to continue with the test flight and rescind the PAN PAN status. The aircraft climbed to flight level 340, then completed a descent, approach and landing without any further surges.

C-FUSM, a Westjet B737-800 was operating flight WJA2214 from Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, to Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International Airport (MMPR), Puerto Vallarta, MX. During the flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue performing the assigned duties which were re-assigned among the remaining crew members. Medlink was contacted for medical/treatment support. The cabin crew member did not occupy the jumpseat for landing.

C-FGWO, a 49 North Helicopters Limited Robinson R22 Beta departed Tofino / Long Beach Airport (CYAZ), BC, on a training flight under visual flight rules flight to Campbell River Airport (CYBL), BC. During an off-field landing attempt, the helicopter’s low rotor RPM warning horn sounded. The training pilot took control but the helicopter landed hard and rolled over onto its left side. The helicopter sustained substantial damage including damage to the airframe, tail boom, and main rotors.The crew telephoned for assistance and were extracted. The helicopter was subsequently airlifted to the company’s facility in CYBL. It was determined that the helicopter is beyond viable economic repair and has been written off.

C-GGOY, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 was operating as flight JZA655, was conducting an instrument flight rules flight from Portland International Airport (KPDX), OR, USA to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. The flight was cleared to land on Runway 26L. C-GYJW, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9, was conducting flight ACA345 under instrument flight rules from Ottawa International Airport (CYOW), ON, to CYVR. Air traffic control instructed ACA345 to follow JZA655 and was cleared to land on Runway 26L. Before landing, the horizontal separation between the aircraft had reduced to 2.7 nautical miles where 3 nautical miles was required. Vancouver Tower instructed ACA345 to pull up and go around. There were no injuries reported and no damage to either aircraft.

G-VIIP a Boeing 777-236 (ER) aircraft operated by British Airways was conducting flight BAW2JA from John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), New York, USA, to London Gatwick Airport (EGKK) England, UK. At 04:42 UTC, a flight crew member contacted Gander ACC to declare a medical emergency for a flight crew member who was unable to continue with flight duties. A clearance was requested to divert to St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL. Gander ACC issued the clearance and the aircraft landed safely at CYYT at 05:59 UTC with paramedics standing by.

C-GHPD, an Air Canada Rouge LP Airbus A321-211 was operating flight ROU1600 from Montréal / Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), Florida. During the initial approach at 6 000 feet, ATC advised flight crew of a VFR traffic proceeding northbound at 5 500 feet. Flight crew received a TCAS TA, followed shortly by a RA to monitor vertical speed and a command to maintain flight level. Flight crew complied with the command and informed ATC. Flight crew had conflicting traffic in sight throughout the incident. Flight landed without further incident.

C-FKEJ, a Keewatin Air Beech B200 departed the Norway House Airport (CYNE), MB, on an instrument flight rules flight to The Pas Airport (CYQD), MB, as flight KEW202. Shortly after reaching the cruising altitude of 16 000 feet ASL, the left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-42) torque increased to an over-torqued state without crew action. The crew confirmed higher than normal N1 and fuel flow indications and reduced the throttle lever, but no change in torque occurred. The propeller setting was then adjusted with normal results for that action. The crew then completed a left-engine shutdown and checks. They advised ATC, declared an emergency, and diverted to the Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB.  The aircraft landed uneventfully at CYTH, and the aircraft was shutdown and towed to the apron.

C-FFAP, a Vanguard Air Care Inc. Beech 200 departed the Poplar River Aerodrome (CZNG), MB, on an instrument flight rules flight to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, as flight VN02. When on final approach to CYWG, the flight crew observed that the nose gear indication was not illuminated "down and locked". The flight crew changed the light bulb, but the nose gear indication remained not illuminated. The flight crew executed a go-around and declared an emergency. The aircraft did a flyby of the tower to confirm that the gear was down. The aircraft remained VFR and the flight crew troubleshot the malfunction while speaking with the operator's maintenance. The gear was suspected down and locked as the taxi light was operating. The flight crew then conducted a manual gear extension and the aircraft landed uneventfully at CYWG with aircraft rescue and fire fighting on standby. The aircraft then taxied to the apron.The operator's maintenance found that the nose gear down and locked light bulb was unserviceable. The bulb was replaced with a new bulb then gear swings and emergency extension were completed with no further faults found.

C-GZWS, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-8CT was operating flight WJA1463 from Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (KPHX), Arizona to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. In the vicinity of Salt Lake City, Utah, a cabin crew member was incapacitated. The cabin crew member was unable to perform their assigned duties and did not occupy their assigned jumpseat for landing. Duties were re-assigned to remaining cabin crew members.

C-GCJT, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 757-223 was operating as flight CJT584 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Hamilton Airport (CYHM), ON. During cruise at FL390, the exhaust gas temperature (EGT) was noticed to be exceeding 700 degrees and in the amber band on the left engine. Power was reduced to stabilize the engine EGT into the normal range. Other indications on the engine at the time seemed normal but the EGT continued to fluctuate. Flight crew turned off electronic engine controls and descended to FL350. The engine seemed to stabilize for about an hour but then it was noted that the left engine was reading considerably higher than the right with respect to EGT, N2, N3 and Fuel Flow, despite setting an identical engine pressure ratio on each and lower N1 on the left engine. Due to fluctuations and the concern of decrease rate of oil pressure, a Pan Pan was declared. The aircraft landed in CYHM without further incident.Maintenance follow-up indicated that the engine was tagged unserviceable and LH engine was replaced. No further faults noted since engine replacement.

C-FLWK, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-8K5 was operating as flight WSG764 from Montréal / Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Princess Juliana International Airport (TNCM), Sint Maarten. During the approach to TNCM, the LAVATORY SMOKE light illuminated in the flight deck. There were no visible signs of smoke reported by the cabin crew. The flight crew declared an emergency for priority landing with ATC. After landing, emergency services reported that no smoke was observed outside the aircraft. The aircraft taxied to the gate without further incident.

C-GIUF, an Airbus A321-211, operated by Air Canada as flight ACA0107 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, was involved in a ground incident. Prior to pushback, the aircraft rolled back approximately 6-8 ft with the parking brake showing set. The L1 door made contact with the bridge. The passengers were deplaned, and the aircraft was taken out of service for inspection and maintenance.

C-FWSO, a Boeing 737-700, operating as Westjet flight, WJA714, was on route from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) when a cabin crew member became sick due to a personal medical event. The cabin crew member was unable to perform their assigned duties for the remainder of the flight. These duties were reassigned to the remaining cabin crew members. The aircraft continued to CYYZ and landed without further incident; EMS met the flight upon arrival.

An Air Canada Boeing 737-8 (registration C-GEKZ) operating as flight ACA395, was conducting an IFR flight from Quebec City/Jean Lesage International Airport (CYQB), QC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. While in cruise, the flight crew received an airspeed (IAS) disagree message. After completing the Quick Reference Handbook checklist, it was determined that the captain's IAS indicator was in error. The flight crew declared an emergency and diverted to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Airport emergency services was on standby and the aircraft landed safely at CYYC. The operator's maintenance replaced the pitot probe, pitot/static probe, Air Data Inertial Reference Unit (ADIRU) and the total air temperature probe. Their fault investigation and troubleshooting is ongoing.

C-FRQP, a Jazz Aviation LP Embraer 175, was operating flight JZA543 from LaGuardia Airport (KLGA), New York, to Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the climb out of KLGA, the crew contacted dispatch and maintenance to report a crackling noise from the windshield area. No visual indications of windshield cracking or delamination and the crew decided to continue to CYYZ. A PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft landed in CYYZ without further incident.

C-GJXE, an Air Canada A220 was operating flight ACA748 from Montréal / Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS), Massachusetts. In descent, the flight crew received a TCAS RA. RA was followed and flight continued to land without further incident.

C-GPNL, a Canadian North Boeing 737-300 was conducting flight AKT1502 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC. While in cruise at FL340 the flight crew observed a cabin altitude warning light and verified that the cabin altitude gauge indicated approximately 12 000 feet. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and after advising air traffic control began a descent and air turnback to CYEG. A PAN PAN was subsequently declared. During the descent cabin altitude was maintained between 10 000 feet and 11 000 feet. The crew requested a hold to burn fuel down to below the maximum landing weight, cancelled the urgency, and then proceeded to land without further incident.

C-FCDF, a privately registered Beech King Air F90 was on a flight from Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the initial descent into CYYC, the aircraft experienced severe turbulence 20 NM west of CYYC. The aircraft rolled uncommanded to 90 degrees of bank and the autopilot disconnected. The pilot had slowed to maneuvering speed prior to the turbulence encounter. The aircraft continued to destination without further issues. A post landing inspection revealed no damage to the aircraft.

C-GKFA, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1624 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), Florida. During the descent from FL260 to FL240, the flight crew received a TCAS RA and subsequent Level Off command at FL247. The flight crew complied and informed ATC. ATC informed ROU1624 the conflicting traffic had leveled off at FL230. The flight was completed uneventfully.

C-FAWH, a privately registered Cessna 120 was conducting circuits on Runway 25 at the Grande Prairie Airport (CYQU), AB. During one of the landings the pilot elected to land in the grass north of the runway. The aircraft touched down on the snow-covered grass and subsequently nosed over onto its roof. The two occupants were able to exit the aircraft. The aircraft was substantially damaged.Maintenance Update: Aircraft was lifted back onto the wheels and removed from site to hangar where damage is being assessed.

C-GWBL, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-800 was operating as WJA456 on a flight from Abbottsford Airport (CYXX), BC, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the initial approach into CYYC, the flight crew reported a flap asymmetry issue. Vectors were requested to run the appropriate checklist and configure the aircraft for a flapless landing. A PAN PAN was subsequently declared and a safe landing was carried out on Runway 17L. Aircraft rescue and fire fighting was called to check the brakes and tires while stopped on the runway. The aircraft was towed to the gate where the tires and brakes were checked again.Maintenance Update: The aircraft was removed from service and maintenance replaced T530 trailing edge flap skew sensor 6 and connector due to corrosion in accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual. Due to the corrosion found at sensor 6, multiple connectors were tested and subsequently replaced. A flap skew system functional test was carried out in accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual with no defects found. Several function tests of the flap system carried out with no defects found and the aircraft was returned to service.

Truck 80 was conducting sweeping operations on Runway 18 at the Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, and was instructed by ATC to remain clear of Runway 31. C-FFJM, a Perimeter Aviation Fairchild Aircraft SA-227-AC departed Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB, on an instrument flight rules flight (flight PAG191) to CYWG. As C-FFJM was landing, Truck 80 was observed by ATC crossing the Runway 31 hold short line. The controller queried Truck 80, who stopped immediately and reversed the vehicle to the hold short line. C-FFJM landed uneventfully and exited on Taxiway V, short of the intersection of Runway 31 and Runway 18. A review of the Airport Surface Detection Equipment (ASDE) indicated that Truck 80 did not reach Runway 31 prior to stopping but did enter the runway protected area (RPA).

N468AX, a Boeing 767-300ER registered to Omni Air International LLC, was conducting ferry flight OAE1911 from Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport (KBWI), MD, USA to Ramstein Air Base (ETAR), Germany. While enroute, the number 1 engine thrust rolled back. After completing the required checklist items, the flight crew declared an emergency and requested a diversion to Bangor International Airport (KBGR), ME, USA. The aircraft landed safely at 04:22 EDT. Maintenance is attending to the aircraft with a planned borescope scheduled for the number 1 engine to determine the reason for the roll-back.

N688LB, an Adams Aviation Services Inc. Trustee Cessna 750, operating from Ottawa/Macdonald Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Sarasota Bradenton International Airport (KSRQ), FL, declared a PAN PAN emergency due to a cracked windshield. The flight crew elected to return to CYOW and landed safely.

C-FGJI, an Air Canada Airbus A320 was operating as flight ACA262 from Winnipeg/James Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While enroute, they declared a PAN PAN emergency due to a hydraulic issue. The flight crew received a Yellow Hydraulic below minimum ECAM message. In discussion with company dispatch, the crew elected to continue to CYYZ where the aircraft landed safely. Emergency services responded and the aircraft was confirmed to have a minor hydraulic leak. The aircraft was able to taxi to the gate afterwards. Post occurrence inspection and maintenance included the removal and replacement of the yellow power accumulator and replace O-rings IAW AMM. A leak check was carried out and no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FIUR, an Air Canada B777-300, was operating as flight ACA36 from Brisbane, Australia (YBBN) to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. While in cruise flight over the North Pacific Ocean in the vicinity of Hawaii, odour of smoke was noticed in the aft galley, when the ovens were turned on. The odour subsequently dissipated, and the flight continued without further incident. The oven smoke origin appears to be related to small paper debris which was found underneath the oven insert.

C-GBHZ, an Air Canada Rouge LP. Airbus A319-114 was operating flight ROU1619 from Tampa International Airport (KTPA), Florida to Montréal / Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During cruise at FL370, ENG2 N1 rolled back to 52% with associated rumbling and vibrations felt throughout the airframe. N1 ENG parameters were not normal and the airspeed began to decay. A PAN PAN was declared with a request for descent to a lower altitude. The ENG2 resumed normal operation when the flight leveled off at FL260. Aircraft rescue and firefighting were on standby. The aircraft taxied to gate under its own power uneventfully.

OK-TST, a Smartwings, Boeing 737-800 operating as Sunwing flight SWG2466, was being prepared for a flight at Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, at the area of gate 40. After conclusion of the water service, as the water cart was being towed away, it made contact with the aircraft causing damage to the cargo door.

C-GZQW, a Porter Airlines Embraer ERJ190-400, operating as flight POE424 from Winnipeg/James Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, declared an emergency enroute with nosewheel, braking and electrical issues. The flight crew requested Runway 05 for arrival in CYYZ, landed and stopped on the runway for inspection. The aircraft was then taxied to the gate under its own power.

C-FCPD, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 767-316 was operating flight CJT1508 from Jorge Chávez International Airport (SPJC), Peru to Mariscal Sucre International Airport (SEQM), Ecuador. During an intermediate level off at FL340 for traffic, EICAS message for AFT CARGO DOOR was displayed. Pressure loss was felt in crew's ears and the crew observed the cabin altitude climb initially at 700 feet per minute and then reduce to 400 feet per minute. The cabin altitude continued to climb until reaching 9000 feet. The flight crew requested a return to SPJC and declared a PAN PAN. The maximum cabin altitude reached was 9500 feet with accomplishment of associated non-normal checklist actions. Flight landed without further incident.

C-FKFZ, a Kelowna Flightcraft Air Charter Limited Convair 340/580 departed Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, on a return training flight via Penticton Airport (CYYF), BC, with 2 crew members on board. During the planned missed approach in CYYF, when the crew advanced the power levers, the right engine propeller (Aeroproducts, A6441FN-606A) RPM increased and exceeded limitations. The crew continued the climb, declared an emergency and, at a safe altitude, they conducted a precautionary engine shutdown. The crew decided to return to CYLW and landed there without incident. There were no reported injuries or damage.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and determined that the propeller rotary actuator was faulty and replaced it. The aircraft has returned to service.

C-GWLK, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-8 Max, was operating as WJA2228 on a flight from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Sangster International Airport (MKJS), Jamaica. Prior to departure, WJA2228 had entered the east deicing facility Bay 1 at CYYC for the application of type 1 and type 4 de-ice fluid. Meanwhile, WJA2286 was being deiced in Bay 3. The ICEMAN informed the flight crew for WJS2286 in Bay 3 that deicing was complete. The flight crew for WJA2228 acknowledged the call. The flight crew for WJA2286 confirmed the deicing complete call was for them and switched to PAD control. By this time the flight crew for WJA2228 had already switched to PAD control and they began to taxi away. WJA2228 was still undergoing the application of deicing fluids when the aircraft began to move. One of the boom units had to move out of the way to avoid a collision with the aircraft. While holding short of Runway 35R, the tower controller informed the flight crew of WJA2228 that their deicing was incomplete and that they needed to return to the deice facility. Subsequently WJA2228 returned to the deice bay.

A WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-700 aircraft (registration C-GWJG) departed Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK, on an IFR flight to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While enroute, smoke began to emit from the flight number display on the first officer's control column. The flight crew disconnected the power source to the display and the smoke stopped. The flight crew advised the operator's maintenance and the flight continued to CYYC without further incident.The operator's maintenance department replaced the control column memory device, which was found to be arcing internally. A detailed inspection of the wiring and interconnect terminals was also performed with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPIX, a DeHavilland DHC-8-402 operated by PAL Airlines Ltd., was conducting flight PVL3051 from St John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL to Deer Lake regional Airport (CYDF), NL. During the climb out, the aircraft experienced an engine failure and a fire indication on the No.1 engine. The crew completed the engine fire/failure procedure and secured the engine. The flight crew returned to CYYT and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed, was inspected by ARFF and taxied to the FBO without further incident.During further examination at the Pratt & Whitney Canada facility, it was discovered that the PW150A engine experienced a low-pressure compressor 2nd stage (LPC2) rotor failure. A similar LPC2 issue is already being investigated by the TSB (investigation A23P0020). This occurrence will be used to support that ongoing investigation.     UPDATED 22 JULY 2024

C-FSKX, a Keewatin Air LP Beech BE-20 was operating as KEW205-M departed the Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, en route to Cambridge Bay Airport (CYCB), NU. Shortly after reaching their planned cruise altitude, the flight crew carried out the mid-way check and realized that the flight had departed with approximately 945 pounds of fuel where 3000 pounds of fuel was required. The flight crew reduced power to achieve minimum fuel flow for cruise flight and diverted to the nearest suitable airport, which was Ekati Aerodrome (CYOA), NT. The aircraft landed with approximately 266 pounds of fuel onboard.

C-FAFH, an amateur built, AF Hamblin FEW TP-51 Mustang, experienced an engine fire and conducted a forced landing in a field 2 nm east of Edenvale Aerodrome (CNV8), ON. The pilot elected to land without flaps and with the landing gear retracted to prevent over-turning while the aircraft was on fire during the landing. The pilot landed into wind and the aircraft slid 78 yards on its belly coming to rest upright, with the fire still burning under the cowling. The pilot shut the fuel off and evacuated immediately. He was uninjured. The pilot extinguished fire with a portable fire extinguisher. The emergency locator transmitter did not activate but the aircraft was severely damaged due to fire and the gear up landing. The Police and local Emergency Medical Services attended the scene. Post occurrence examination determined that an exhaust valve in the left bank of the GMC LS1 V8 engine stuck in the open position. The heat led to melting through the aluminum head and then the rocker box, igniting the wiring and controls above. The melt hole is about the size of a human fist. The aircraft has been determined to be a write-off and has been salvaged from the accident location.

C-GXTB, a Pilatus PC-12/47 aircraft operated by North Star Air Ltd, was conducting an IFR flight from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, to Deer Lake Airport (CYVZ), ON. While levelling off at FL180, the cabin pressure continued to increase until it was in the caution range. Manual control of the pressurization was not effective as minor adjustments resulted in a maxed-out cabin pressurization to a depressurization and a cabin altitude above 10 000 feet reading. The crew advised ATC and requested a descent to 10 000 feet with a return to CYQT. The cabin pressure continued to fluctuate during the remainder of the flight. The aircraft landed safely at CYQT.The operator's maintenance department replaced the outflow valve controller, cleaned the outflow valve and removed moisture from the control lines. Aircraft was released to service subject to a satisfactory test flight.

C-FLLB, un Piper PA-18-150 en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol récréatif local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de de Lachute, QC (CSE4) avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Lors du roulage après l’atterrissage sur la piste 28, l’avion a dévié vers la gauche, a fait une sortie latérale de piste et a terminé sa course dans le fossé. L’avion a subi des dommages importants au train d’atterrissage, à l’aile droite et à l’hélice. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

N461AW, an Air Wisconsin Airlines, Bombardier CL-600-2B19, operating as flight AWI6021 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) to Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD) declared an emergency due to an engine indication. The flight crew of the aircraft elected to return to CYYZ. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 23 with ARFF standing by.

C-FWCN, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-700 departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to conduct flight WJA131, under instrument flight rules, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise at flight level 320 (FL 320), approximately 45 minutes prior to landing, the Captain felt sudden ear pressure and observed the cabin vertical speed indicator (VSI) was indicating a climb at the maximum rate position of       4 000 feet per minute. The Captain donned his oxygen mask, declared a MAYDAY, and requested an immediate descent with air traffic control. The Cabin Altitude Warning horn sounded and the oxygen masks in the cabin deployed. The pilots referred to the quick reference checklist (QRC) and initiated the procedures outlined in the Cabin Altitude Warning checklist. During the rapid descent the flight crew were able to regain control of the cabin pressure in manual mode on the mode controller. When the crew completed the emergency descent and the aircraft was level at 10 000 feet above sea level (ASL), they removed their masks and checked on the cabin crew members and the passengers. The aircraft continued at 10 000 feet ASL until they descended for CYVR. Concurrently, approximately 20 minutes before the landing, the cabin crew heard a smoke detector alarm sound in the right aft lavatory. The cabin crew investigated and did not observe any smoke or fire. The aircraft landed without further incident. Aircraft rescue and firefighting crews met the aircraft and after a brief inspection, the crew taxied to the gate. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft.Maintenance was unable to pressurize the aircraft the day after the occurrence. The air conditioning accessory unit was found to have failed and was replaced. An air check valve was also replaced. Following engine bleed system check and a successful flight test, the aircraft was returned to service. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) is being prepared for submission to Transport Canada.

C-GXJZ, a DeHavilland DHC-8-402 operated by Jazz Aviation LP. was conducting flight JZA8657 from Halifax Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), USA.  During the cruise phase, a flight attendant could smell a strong burning smell in the back galley and reported the coffee machine appearing much hotter than normal. The crew opted to return to CYHZ and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without further incident.

A Smartwings, Boeing 737-800, registration OK-TVM, operating as Sunwing Airlines flight 411, from Gregorio Luperon International Airport (MDPP) to Toronto/Lester B Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) advised ATC of a flap issue, requested to be re-sequenced for landing and declared a PAN PAN. During the approach and selection of flaps 5, the flight crew noticed that flaps stopped slightly behind position 2. In dealing with the Trailing Edge Flap Disagree checklist and during the turn to final, the crew noticed a low-speed alert. The crew cancelled the approach and entered a hold to troubleshoot and prepare for landing. The flaps could not be extended using the alternate flap extension. The crew declared a Pan Pan, was sequenced to land on Runway 23 and landed at without further incident.

C-FTXQ, un Airbus 321-211 exploité par Air Transat sous l'indicatif TSC821, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Orlando International aux États-Unis (KMCO) à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Alors qu’il était sur un guidage radar pour tourner en base pour l’approche finale 24R, un malentendu est survenu sur le cap. Une correction de cap a été donnée par l’unité de contrôle aérien (ATC), toutefois une perte d’espacement est survenue lorsqu’il s’est retrouvé 2,8 miles marins du vol LXJ561, un Bombardier Challenger 300 établis en approche finale de la piste 24L à environ la même altitude. L’espacement requis était de 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical et 3 nm sur le plan horizontal.

C-GMPW, a Pilatus PC-12/47E aircraft operated by the RCMP Air Services Branch, departed on a VFR flight from Wollaston Lake Airport (CZWL), SK, to Prince Albert (Glass Field) Airport (CYPA), SK, with a pilot and two passengers onboard. While on approach to CYPA, the left main landing gear indicated an "in-transit" warning.  The aircraft entered a hold to the southeast of the airport while the pilot performed checks. The pilot then performed a low approach for visual confirmation that the landing gear was down. Airport emergency services were requested and mobilized to the standby position. The aircraft landed uneventfully. The operator's maintenance replaced the landing left main gear actuator.

C-GKWH, a Bell 407 helicopter operated by Churchill Falls (Labrador) Corporation Ltd, was conducting a flight from Wabush Airport (CYWK), NL, to Menihek, NL. During the flight, the XMSN CHIP light illuminated. The pilot immediately landed the helicopter. Upon inspection, metal was found on the chip detector. The aircraft was subsequently returned to base after removal of the metal particles from the chip detector. As this was the 3rd occurrence of the chip light activation on that aircraft, the transmission was replaced.

C-FENJ, a WestJet Encore de Havilland DHC-8-402 was operating as flight WEN3394 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. The flight departed from CYEG and while climbing through 9 000 feet ASL, the flight crew received an R1 door unsafe warning indication. The flight crew actioned the QRH, declared a MAYDAY and advised ATC that they were returning to CYEG. The aircraft landed without further issue. Company maintenance replaced and rigged the R/H emergency door closed/locked sensor, and the aircraft was released for continued service.

C-GMPM, a Pilatus PC-12/47E aircraft operated by the RCMP, was conducting flight SST011 from St John's International Airport (CYYT), NL, to Greater Moncton Roméo Leblanc International Airport (CYQM), NB, with 1 flight crew member and 1 passenger on board. While in cruise at FL260 the pilot received an airspeed miscompare message and both copilot primary flight display and the electronic standby instrument showed an airspeed error, as well as failure messages related to autopilot functions. The pilot disconnected the autopilot, followed the QRH checklist, and requested a diversion to Sydney/J.A. Douglas McCurdy Airport (CYQY), NS. As the flight neared CYQY the pilot reviewed enroute and original destination weather and decided to continue to CYQM. The pilot requested priority at CYQM and landed without further incident.The RCMP Air Services are in the process of completing an investigation through their safety management system and maintenance department.

C-GGKP, a privately owned Beechcraft Sierra C24R was on a VFR night cross-country flight with the student pilot and an instructor. The purpose of the flight was to fulfill the requirements for the student's night rating. The aircraft departed Kitchener (CYKF) and was flying to Tillsonburg (CYTB), Goderich (CYGD) and return to Kitchener. When the aircraft was on the approach to runway 26 at CYTB the instructor observed trees on final, and as the aircraft was pulling up, the aircraft struck the treetops. The approach was aborted, and a decision was made to return to CYKF. During the return flight the engine was performing normally, and there were no difficulties with the flight controls, however the airspeed indication was erratic. The landing at CYKF was uneventful, but during the walkaround after the taxi it was noticed that the left wing, horizontal stabilator and left flap had several tree impact marks. The pitot tube was found partially plugged with tree debris. The repair to the aircraft included the replacement of the left wing.

The BC Ministry of Forests was conducting fire management operations 7 nautical miles northwest of Kamloops (CYKA), BC, with an Autel Evo II Enterprise V2 RPAS with an operator and an observer. Due to environmental conditions, the RPAS was being recovered using hand catches rather than landing on a surface. After landing on the observer's hand, the RPAS operator shut down the RPAS. During shutdown, the RPAS spun and a rotor struck the observer's hand causing a serious injury. The RPAS sustained minor damage.

C-FCJE, un De Havilland DHC-8-102 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE871 MEDEVAC, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) à destination de Kangirsuk, QC (CYAS). Lors de la montée initiale en passant 7000 pieds, la lumière d’avertissement « #2 Engine Manual » s’est allumée. L’équipage a complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a déclaré une urgence à l’unité de contrôle aérien. L’aéronef a effectué un demi-tour et s’est posé sans encombre à CYVP.

C-GRJZ, un Beech B350 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE551, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Kuujjuarapik, QC (CYGW) à destination de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP). En palier au niveau de vol 330, à environ 120 NM au nord-est de CYGW, l’indication « CABIN ALTITUDE » s’est allumée ainsi que l’alerte sonore. L’équipage a noté que l’altitude de cabine indiquait 11 000 pieds. Après avoir tenté de régler la situation en vain, une descente a été demandée et puisque la descente était autorisée seulement jusqu’au niveau de vol 290, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) afin de descendre plus bas. Au niveau de vol 250, l’altitude de la cabine a descendu sous les 10 000 pieds et restée stable. L’équipage a signalé que la situation était sous contrôle et a annulé l’urgence. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre à CYVP.

C-GJZD, un Dehavilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7976, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Billy Bishop Toronto City/Toronto, ON (CYTZ) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Lors de l’approche, l'équipage a sélectionné le levier de commande du train d'atterrissage en position sortie. La lumière verte d’indication du train avant ne s’est pas allumée. L'équipage a effectué une remise des gaz, a complété les listes de vérification appropriées et a déclaré une urgence au contrôleur de l'unité de contrôle aérien. L’équipage n’a pas utilisé le moyen alternatif pour sortir le train, la cabine a été préparée pour un atterrissage anormal probable. L'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre.

C-FNEN, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), operated by WestJet Encore Limited, was conducting flight WEN3157 from Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. On initial climb after takeoff, the flight crew selected flaps to 0 at flap retraction altitude. The flaps travelled from flaps 10 to flaps 5 and then the Flap Power annunciator light illuminated. The quick reference checklist was completed, and the Flap Power annunciator light temporarily extinguished and then re-illuminated. The flight crew advised air traffic control, declared an emergency, and informed the flight attendants, passengers, and company dispatch. The aircraft landed safely in CYVR. Once on the ground, the flight crew cancelled the emergency and taxied to the gate. Emergency services personnel inspected the aircraft.Maintenance carried out a function test of the flap system and found no faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FIOH, a Swearingen SA227-AC operated by 2080061 Ontario Inc. (dba SkyCare Air Ambulance), was conducting a medevac flight from Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON, to Dryden Regional Airport (CYHD), ON. During the landing roll on Runway 12 at CYHD, directional control was lost at a low speed. The aircraft departed the runway to the south and entered the gravel surface. The aircraft was shutdown. There were no injuries and the patient was transferred to a waiting ambulance. The pilots subsequently inspected the aircraft and taxied to the apron. There was no damage to the aircraft.  The operator's maintenance verified there was no damage and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FXCA, an Air Canada B767-300 was operating flight AC7259 from Luis Muñoz Marin International Airport (TJSJ), Puerto Rico to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During take-off, the flight crew received a Main Cargo Door Open warning at V1. The flight continued take-off roll and declared a Pan Pan for an air turnback. The flight landed without incident, emergency vehicles inspected the aircraft and was cleared to taxi to the gate.

C-GJWE, a WestJet Encore de Havilland DHC-8-402 was operating as flight WEN3111 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC. The aircraft departed from CYYC and during landing gear retraction on the initial climb, the nose landing gear did not retract. The flight crew actioned the quick reference checklist and after landing gear extension, all landing gear were confirmed down with 3 green landing gear position lights illuminated. A PAN PAN urgency was declared and the aircraft returned to CYYC where it landed without further issue. The aircraft was met by ARFF on Taxiway C4 and inspected before returning to Gate 6. Company maintenance found the nose landing gear actuator to be faulty. The actuator was replaced, and the aircraft was released back into service.

C-FWSV, a WestJet B737-7CT was operating flight WJA2220 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to Cancún International Airport (MMUN), MX. During the flight, a cabin crew member became ill. The cabin crew member was unable to perform their assigned duties and did not occupy their assigned jumpseat for landing. Duties we re-assigned to remaining cabin crew members.

N47524, a United Airlines Boeing 737-9 operating as flight UAL1946 and C-FSWE, a Westjet Encore Bombardier DHC-8-400 operating as flight WEN3296 departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, en-route to their scheduled destinations. During the departure, UAL1946 was flying on a southeasterly heading climbing to flight level 210 and WEN3296 was on an easterly heading climbing to 12 000 feet ASL. While under the control of Calgary Departure, the aircrafts' tracks crossed approximately 11 nautical miles to the northeast of CYYC. Shortly after their tracks crossed, vertical separation between the two aircraft had reduced to 800 feet at 0.6 nautical miles horizontal distance. The required separation was 1 000 feet vertical or 3 nautical miles horizontal.

C-GPNA, un De Havilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Provincial Airlines sous l’indicatif PVL863, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Wabush, NL (CYWK) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) avec 11 passagers et 4 membres d'équipage. Au niveau de vol 240, l’équipage a observé un début de délamination dans le pare-brise du côté du commandant de bord. L’équipage a éteint le réchauffe pare-brise. Peu de temps après, l’équipage a entendu un son et plusieurs craques dans le pare-brise sont apparues ainsi que d’autres signes de délamination. L’équipage a avisé le contrôleur aérien et a amorcé une descente au niveau de vol 100 tout en réduisant la vitesse de vol. L’équipage a complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a déclaré une urgence à l’ATC. Un déroutement vers l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) a été effectué et l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GEDV, an Upper Valley Aviation Limited Beech B200 (Super King Air 200), was operating as a medical evacuation flight from the Phoenix-Mesa Gateway Airport (KIWA), Arizona, U.S., to the Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, with 2 flight crew and 3 passengers on board. During descent through approximately 20 000 feet above sea level, approximately 12 nautical miles southwest of CYLW, the oxygen masks deployed in the cabin. The flight crew declared an emergency and landed safely at CYLW.Maintenance found the cabin altitude on the pressurization controller was set to below field elevation and the rate knob turned to maximum. Inspections of the outflow valve, safety valve, and system lines were carried out with no defects found. The oxygen masks were repacked, a test flight was conducted, and the airplane was returned to service.

N87512, a United Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-824, was operating flight UAL460 from San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), California, U.S., to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. On final approach, the flight crew observed a trailing edge flap disagree indication. When flaps were selected beyond the 15° detent, in the trailing edge flaps would not extend further and the discrepancy was observed between the flap lever positions selected and the corresponding flap indicator. The flight crew conducted a missed approach and declared an emergency with air traffic control. After completing the missed approach procedures, the flight crew completed the Trailing Edge Flap Discrepancy checklist, and the flaps were extended to the landing configuration by completing the Alternate Flap Extension checklist. The aircraft landed safely at CYVR. Maintenance conducted a Built-in Test (BITE) on the Flap/Slat Electronics Unit (FSEU) and found an intermittent fault between the left-wing and right-wing flaps. The right flap position transmitter was replaced, and operational checks were conducted with no further faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FLIY, an Air Creebec Inc. Hawker Siddeley HS 748 2A, operating as flight CRQ650 was on route to Attawapiskat (CYAT), ON, from Timmins (CYTS), ON, when the flight crew noticed an excessive increase of fuel flow on the #2 engine. A visual inspection determined that there was a fuel leak from the #2 engine. The crew shut down the engine and completed the QRH procedures. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft returned to CYTS. The landing was uneventful with ARFF standing by. Maintenance determined that the fuel leak was from a transfer tube between the Engine Driven Fuel Pump and the Fuel Control Unit. The operator submitted an SDR and also completed an inspection of the #1 engine.

C-GCJY, a Cargojet Boeing 757-200 aircraft, operating as flight CJT1574, departed Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, on route to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, when the flight crew received a low oil pressure EICAS warning for the #1 engine. The quick reference handbook procedures were followed, and power was reduced but the warning remained. The flight crew shut down the engine, declared a PAN PAN and returned to CYHM. The aircraft landed uneventfully with aircraft rescue and fire fighting standing by. Maintenance performed an initial inspection, but no faults were found. The aircraft was removed from service for further troubleshooting and repairs.

C-FYXI, un hélicoptère Robinson R44 II privé, effectuait un vol local de nuit selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis un terrain privé à Carignan, QC, avec seul le pilote à bord. Les conditions météorologiques étaient favorables au vol VFR de nuit. À son retour vers Carignan, le pilote a survolé les installations de son entreprise et a aperçu un de ses véhicules semi-remorque en déplacement. Le pilote a décidé de se rapprocher pour tenter d’identifier le véhicule. Le pilote n’a pas aperçu les câbles paratonnerre d’une ligne électrique et les a heurtés. L’hélicoptère s’est écrasé dans un champ et a subie des dommages importants. Le pilote non blessé, a pu s’extirper de l'hélicoptère. Aucun feu après impact ne s’est déclaré. Le Centre conjoint de coordination des opérations de sauvetage de Trenton, ON a reçu un signal de détresse de la radiobalise à 18 h 52. Les services d’urgence ont été avisés.

N809NW, an Airbus A330-300 operated by Delta Air Lines Inc., was conducting flight DAL137 from Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (EHAM), Netherlands, to Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport (KDTW), Michigan, U.S. During initial descent from FL380, the flight crew declared an emergency with ATC (Toronto Centre), citing a hydraulic issue. The flight continued to the planned destination.

C-FPCZ, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Saab-Fairchild 340B, was operating as flight PCO100 from Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. On final into CYVR, after selecting landing gear down, the left main gear light did not illuminate. The crew conducted a missed approach and received vectors during which the crew completed their checklists and communicated with their company maintenance. A second approach was flown with the same result. After the second missed approach, the crew completed a manual gear extension, declared a PAN PAN, and requested a low pass by the CYVR tower so that the controllers could look at the landing gear. The controllers stated that the 3 landing gears looked to be down. The aircraft landed with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) crews standing by. ARFF inspected the aircraft and then followed it as the crew taxied to the South Terminal. There was no damage to the aircraft and no injuries.Company Maintenance inspected the landing gear system and determined that the left main gear up-lock cannon plug was disconnected. The plug was inspected, cleaned and re-installed. Landing gear extension and retraction function checks were carried out with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSEZ, a privately registered, amateur built, Murphy Moose was taxiing to depart Delta Heritage Air Park (CAK3), BC, on a local visual flight rules flight with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the taxi on the grass maneuver area, the aircraft nosed over with the left wing striking the turf and came to rest inverted. There were no injuries to either occupant. The aircraft sustained substantial damage including the left wing tip, right wing strut, empennage, and propeller.The aircraft will be inspected to determine the extent of the damage.

C-GTVL, Bell 206-B3 helicopter, operated by Quantum Helicopters, was conducting a local animal survey flight, under visual flight rules, from Williams Lake Airport (CYWL), BC. While flying at approximately 9 300 feet above sea level (ASL) the pilot heard a loud bang and the helicopter yawed. The engine (Rolls Royce Allison 250-C20B) indications showed that the engine had lost power. Concurrently, there was smoke in the cockpit, a warning horn, and the engine chip warning illuminated. The pilot broadcast a MAYDAY call and turned on the emergency locator transmitter (ELT). The pilot executed a successful autorotation and landed in a meadow at approximately       6 800 feet ASL. Once the pilot and passengers egressed, the pilot used the satellite phone to contact the British Columbia Wildfire Service (BCWFS). The BCWFS dispatched 2 helicopters to recover the pilot and passengers and relayed to the Joint Rescue and Coordination Centre that the pilot was turning off the ELT and that further support was not required. There were no injuries, and the helicopter was not damaged.The helicopter was airlifted from the landing site, and it was determined that the engine failure may have initiated at the top mounting structure at the exhaust collector. Internal engine damage was consistent with the turbine being out of alignment and there were indications of blade rub. The engine was sent for further examination.

C-GBHR, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1780 from Ottawa MacDonald Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), Dominican Republic. During the climb to cruise phase of flight, a Flight Attendant became ill and was unable to continue their duties. The duties were redistributed amongst the cabin crew, and the flight was completed without further incident.

C-GOJN, a Sikorsky S-61N aircraft operated by VIH Helicopters, was conducting heli-logging operations approximately 57 nm north-northwest of Bella Bella (Campbell Island) Airport (CBBC), BC. During the approach to the log drop off area, the logs being carried as longline load contacted trees. The longline and load of logs released and fell into the forest. The helicopter returned to the service barge uneventfully. There were no injuries or damage to people or objects on the ground. The helicopter and the rigging were inspected by maintenance personnel and were found to be free of damage or malfunction. The helicopter was returned to service. The longline was recovered, inspected and found to be undamaged.

C-GUAI, un DHC-8-314 exploité par Air Inuit Ltée, effectuait le vol AIE884 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de la Grande Rivière (CYGL), QC  à destination de l'aéroport de Kangiqsujuaq/Wakeham Bay (CYKG), QC avec 3 membres d'équipage à bord. À environ 20 miles nautiques au nord de CYKG, l'équipage a déclaré un état d'urgence (Pan Pan) en raison du train d'atterrissage qui refusait de se déployer. Les voyants de train en transition et de train non sécuritaire étaient allumés. L'équipage a alors fait diversion vers l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq (CYVP), QC où des services de maintenance seraient disponibles. Le train a été déployé manuellement et l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre sur la piste 25. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GXAI, un DHC-8-314 exploité par Air Inuit Ltée, s'apprêtait à effectuer le vol AIE854 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Tasiujaq (CYTQ), QC  à destination de l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq (CYVP), QC  avec 4 membres d'équipage et 15 passagers à bord. Au moment de quitter la barrière d'embarquement, le pilote a lentement fait pivoter l'aéronef vers la gauche, guidé par du personnel au sol. Le premier officier a ensuite vu le guide au sol pointer vers le bout de l'aile droite indiquant un contact entre le bout de l'aile de C-GXAI et le gouvernail de direction de C-FDAO, un DHC-8-102 appartenant aussi à Air Inuit Ltée qui était tout près et sur lequel de la maintenance était effectuée.Le bout de l'aileron droit de C-GXAI a subi une abrasion et une fissure et le gouvernail de direction de C-FDAO a subi une bosse de sur son bord de fuite.

N585NN, un Bombardier CRJ-900LR exploité par PSA Airlines, effectuait le vol JIA5029 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport Charlotte/Douglas Intl, Charlotte, NC (KCLT) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 76 passagers à bord. Suite au départ de CYUL, alors que l'aéronef se trouvait à environ à 8000pi., l'équipage a observé une indication vibration de 1.7 sur le N1 du moteur gauche (GE CF34-8C5) qui a ensuite continué à augmenter. L'équipage a alors déclaré une urgence et a décidé de revenir à CYUL où l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre. Les broches d'ailettes de soufflantes du moteur gauche ont été remplacées et l'aéronef a été remis en service.

C-FJVE, un Boeing 737-8DC exploité par Sunwing Airlines, effectuait le vol SWG6488 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination de l'aéroport Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl de Varadero (MUVR), Cuba avec 6 membres d'équipage et 188 passagers à bord. Après le départ de CYUL, l'indication d'altitude s'est "gelée" a 16 500 pi. sur le panneau de contrôle de mode du pilote automatique et sur l'écran d'affichage primaire. L'équipage a alors décidé de revenir à CYUL et a déclaré l'état d'urgence (Pan Pan). L'aéronef, en surpoids, a atterri sécuritairement. Après l'atterrissage, l'aéronef s'est immobilisé sur la voie de circulation où les services de sécurité incendie ont inspecté les freins et les pneus. L'aéronef a ensuite pu circuler jusqu'à une barrière et procéder au débarquement des passagers. Le panneau de contrôle de mode du pilote automatique a été remplacé.

F-GSQC, a Boeing 777-328ER operated by Air France, was conducting flight AFR004 from Charles de Gaulle International Airport (LFPG), France to John F Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), USA.  During the cruise phase, the crew received an EICAS caution message of hydraulic quantity low. The crew reviewed the QRH and contacted company operations and the decision was made to continue to KJFK. A PAN-PAN was declared with ATC and the flight landed without further incident.Maintenance discovered a crack on hydraulic return line at a 45 degree elbow fitting and a contractor made the repair to return the aircraft to service.

C-FPQQ, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by Keewatin Air LP as KEW213-M, departed Rankin Inlet Airport (CYRT), NU on an IFR flight to Gjoa Haven (CYHK), NU. While climbing thru FL220, a passenger noticed a loud whistling sound emanating from the door. Approximately 10 seconds later, the cabin rapidly depressurized. The crew deployed the oxygen masks for all occupants and initiated an emergency descent to 10 000 feet. The aircraft returned and landed uneventfully at CYRT. The operator's maintenance found a damaged door seal and determined that the pneumatic valve was not maintaining correct pressure. The door seal and pneumatic valve were replaced. The aircraft was released subject to a satisfactory test flight. This aircraft had similar previous events (TSB occurrence A24C0016 and A24C0017).

C-GFMX, a PAL Aerospace Ltd. DHC-8-315 was on a RNP Y approach to Lydd Airport (EGMD), UK.  Standard RA recovery executed followed by a missed approach.  The aircraft was on an IFR flight plan in IMC conditions under procedural IFR control.  The TCAS target was not seen due to IMC conditions.  Traffic was unknown to EGMD ATC.  Aircraft successfully completed a subsequent approach and landed safely.

On 12 February 2024, the Hanley Heli Service Inc. Bell Textron Inc. 206L helicopter (registration C-GCHM, serial number 45083) was conducting aerial geo-survey operations in the western area of Lake Athabasca near the Fort Chipewyan Airport (CYPY), Alberta. At approximately 1311 Mountain Standard Time, the occurrence helicopter departed from CYPY on a day visual flight rules (VFR) flight, with 1 pilot on board. The helicopter was conducting external load operations consisting of a geo-survey sensor package on a 300-foot longline. At approximately 1429, a company pilot who was on the ground at CYPY advised the occurrence pilot that the weather was deteriorating rapidly, with reduced visibilities in snow, and that he should return to the airport. As the occurrence aircraft approached CYPY, the pilot attempted to line up for final on Runway 22. On short final, the occurrence pilot activated the aircraft radio control of aerodrome lighting (ARCAL) system for visual guidance. Approximately 0.4 NM from the threshold of Runway 22, the occurrence pilot encountered reduced visibility and reversed course and then turned towards Lake Athabasca. A few minutes later, at approximately 1518, the aircraft collided with the ice-covered surface of Lake Athabasca. The pilot was fatally injured. The aircraft was destroyed by the impact forces. There was no post-crash fire. The emergency locator transmitter activated and search and rescue personnel were dispatched. The wreckage was located at approximately 1810 by the RCMP and local first responders.

C-FULI, a Lynx Air Boeing 737-8, operating as flight DAT112, was conducting a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International (CYYZ), ON, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, and was on final approach to Runway 26R. C-FPCX, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited Beech 1900D, was conducting flight PCO9191 from Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, to CYVR, BC and was being manoeuvred to the final approach for Runway 26L. While manoeuvring, the Beech 1900D came within 2.3 miles laterally and 500 feet vertically of the Boeing 737-8 where a separation of 3 miles laterally and 1000 feet vertically was required. Air traffic control cancelled the clearance for the Beech 1900D and vectored that aircraft for a second approach to Runway 26L. The Boeing 737-8 continued the approach for Runway 26R and landed without incident.

N485PX, un appareil de type CRJ900LR exploité par Endeavor Air, effectuait le vol EDV5263 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY  à destination l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC avec 4 membres d'équipage et 64 passagers à bord. À 15Nm en approche de CYUL, l'équipage reçu une alarme "SMOKE FWD LAV". Les listes de vérification d'urgence ont été complétées et une urgence a été déclaré alors que le personnel de bord informait l'équipage d'une "odeur de brûlé". Les véhicules d'urgence ont été déployés et l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre à 2148Z. L'aéronef s'est immobilisé sur la piste 24R où les passagers ont été évacués par la porte principale. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés. Le passager se trouvant dans la salle d'aisance avant au moment où l'alarme a retenti dans le poste de pilotage a admis avoir vapoté dans celle-ci et a été pris en charge par les forces de l'ordre à l'arrivée...................Au moment de toucher le sol à CYSK, la visibilité est devenue nulle et l'appareil a dévié vers la gauche et a terminé sa course à une cinquantaine de pieds du bord de la piste.        Une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil s'est posé sans problème à C***.. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-FSVU, a privately registered Piper PA-28-140, was conducting a recreational flight from the Red Deer Forestry Aerodrome (CFR7), AB to Lacombe Aerodrome (CEG3), AB. The pilot elected to conduct a sightseeing overflight of Burnstick Lake, AB (25 NM NE of CFR7), and on the second pass, descended low enough that the aircraft wheels made contact with the snow-covered lake surface. The aircraft came to an abrupt stop, and ultimately flipped over on to its top. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The pilot, who was the sole occupant of the aircraft, was wearing a seatbelt and was able to exit the aircraft out a side window. He sustained no injuries.

C-GEOC, a Geotech Aviation AS350B3 was conducting an aerial survey with a magnetometer in the vicinity of Sonora, MX. The aircraft was at 5560 ASL surveying along a track line of rising terrain while maintaining the contour lines at 100’ AGL. The pilot looked inside the cockpit to change the setting on the Aerocomp unit in order to determine the number of tracks remaining. When the pilot looked outside again, the terrain had risen faster than anticipated and an evasive maneuver was necessary to minimize contact with a tree. An abrupt pull up/left turnout was made as the helicopter struck the tree. The helicopter began to vibrate and the pilot landed uneventfully in a nearby clearing. The helicopter sustained the following visible damage: slight damage to the belly/mirrors, damaged to the horizontal stabilizer, damage to the tail boom, damage to the tail rotor blades (opened up on the trailing edges). The abrupt maneuvering resulted in a torque exceedance that will require replacement of the engine and possibly some dynamic components. The pilot was not injured.

C-FGZO, a Top Aces A-4N was operating a flight out of Nordholz/Cuxhaven Airport (ETMN), Germany. After 35 minutes of flight at FL320 and the wings leveled with engine operating at 82% RPM, the pilot observed abnormal vibrations and a high-pitch noise. The cabin pressure system was set to RAM AIR resulting in the vibration and noise no longer present. An emergency was declared, and a descent below FL250 was initiated. Upon achieving desired landing weight, the aircraft returned to ETMN and landed without further incident.Similar incident from occurrence A24F0033.

C-FIVS, an Air Canada Boeing 777-333ER was operating as flight ACA1 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON, to Haneda Airport (RJTT), Tokyo, Japan. Due to severe turbulence on planned airway, crew requested a lower flight level from ATC. ATC was unable to accommodate request due to traffic. PAN PAN was declared and Special Procedures for In-Flight Contingencies in Oceanic Airspace. After procedure and FL change was complete a new clearance from ATC was received and PAN PAN was cancelled. Aircraft landed at RJTT without further incident.

C-GWUQ, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300 was operating flight ACA0763 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA. The crew received a TCAS RA notification to descend while on approach. This resulted in the aircraft being too low to continue. The aircraft did a go-around and landed uneventfully.

C-GJAN, a Jazz Aviation CRJ900 was operating flight JZA954 from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (KATL), GA to Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During climb at 10 000 feet the 'Elevator Split Caution' message illuminated. The crew leveled off at 10 000 feet and actioned the quick reference handbook. There was no visible split on the controls and no difference was felt in the aircraft handling. Crew declared Pan Pan for priority handling and elected to return to KATL. Landing required longest runway and 20º of flap. Aircraft landed without incident.

C-GJXV, an Air Canada Airbus A220, flight ACA470, departed Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, on a flight to Ottawa Macdonald–Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. Shortly after takeoff, at approximately 500 feet AGL the right-hand windshield cracked. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and the aircraft returned to CYYZ where it landed without further incident.

C-GOIX, an Air Transat A321-271 NX was operating flight TSC616 from Québec / Jean Lesage International Airport (CYQB), QB to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL. TSC616 was required to reroute several times due to ATC requests in Orlando, Florida. While in descent to KFLL, the flight crew declared a minimum fuel emergency. TSC616 was given priority and landed without further incident.

C-GBIJ, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1662 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Southwest Florida International Airport (KRSW), FL. During the descent phase of flight, ATC cleared ROU1662 to descend to 4000' and advised the flight crew to observe VFR traffic at 3500'. While descending to 4000', the flight crew received a TCAS RA followed by a climb command. Flight crew complied with command and the flight was completed without further incident.

C-GKQM, a Porter Airlines (Canada) Limited Embraer ERJ 190-400, was preparing for flight PD260 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Ottawa International (CYOW), ON, with 5 crew and 42 passengers onboard. After being pushed back from the gate, the crew started the right engine (Pratt & Whitney-USA, PW1921G) and a flight attendant observed brief smoke and flame coming from the engine. The flight attendant alerted the flight crew, and the right engine was shut down. The flight crew requested an external inspection by aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) personnel and no damage or fire was visible. The aircraft returned to the gate and the passengers were deplaned. Maintenance inspected the right engine and conducted an engine ground run with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTSY, an amateur-built Just Aircraft Highlander, was conducting a local flight from a private grass airstrip approximately 4 nautical miles east-southeast of Langley Regional Airport (CYNJ), BC, with only the pilot onboard. While landing with a slight tailwind, aircraft nosed over after brakes were applied during the landing roll. The aircraft came to a rest inverted. The emergency locator transmitter activated and a signal was received by the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre. The pilot exited the aircraft and was not injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FRJY, a British Aerospace Avro 146 Series RJ100 registered to Summit Air Ltd., was conducting flight SUT8292 from Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, to Prince Rupert Airport (CYPR), BC. After conducting an approach for Runway 31 at CYPR, the aircraft touched down, started to slow and as it was nearing the button of Runway 13, the aircraft started to slide sideways and exited the end of the runway, skidding to a stop approximately 30 meters past the end, facing a NE direction. There were no reported injuries to anyone on board and there was no visible damage to the aircraft. One runway end light was damaged when the aircraft exited the runway. The passengers were transported by bus to the airport terminal and the aircraft was eventually taxied to the apron under its own power.

C-GEZX, un Airbus 321-211 exploité par Air Transat sous l'indicatif TSC972, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL),QC à destination de l'aéroport international Samaná/El Catey (MDCY), République Dominicaine. Le départ suivant était C-GJXM, un Embraer EMB-550 exploité par Skyservice Business Aviation inc. sous l'indicatif SYB999 qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de CYUL à destination de l'aéroport Teterboro (KTEB), États-Unis. Une perte d'espacement est survenue lors de la montée initiale, lorsque SYB999 s'est retrouvé momentanément à 2,3 miles marins (nm) derrière le TSC972. L'espacement requis était de 3 nm sur le plan horizontal. Les 2 appareils ont poursuivi leurs vols à leurs destinations respectives sans encombre.

C-FPQQ, a Beech B200 operated by Keewatin Air LP, was performing a post-maintenance test flight (following TSB occurrence A24C0016) from the Rankin Inlet Airport (CYRT), NU.
