As the aircraft was climbing to the intended altitude of FL280, the crew heard a loud squeal and levelled off at FL230. After leveling off at FL230 the aircraft cabin rapidly depressurized. The crew followed depressurization procedures, including setting the transponder to 7700. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft returned to CYRT for an uneventful landing. The aircraft remains out of service pending the operator's investigation and maintenance. This aircraft had a similar subsequent event (TSB occurrence A24C0019).

C-FPQQ, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by Keewatin Air LP as flight number KEW213-M, departed Rankin Inlet Airport (CYRT), NU on an IFR flight to Kugaaruk Airport (CYBB), NU. As the aircraft leveled off at the intended cruising altitude of FL270, the crew noticed the cabin altitude began to increase. The crew donned oxygen masks and initiated depressurization checks, including confirming that the passengers were wearing their oxygen masks. The transponder code was set to 7700 and they began an emergency descent with a return to CYRT. Due to difficulties encountered with the oxygen mask microphones, radio communication was not established until the aircraft was at a lower altitude. The aircraft made an uneventful landing at CYRT.The operators' maintenance personnel found the main cabin door seal was out of position (out of its track). Ground checks were performed, and the aircraft was released to service subject to a satisfactory test flight. This aircraft had similar subsequent events (TSB occurrence number A24C0017 and A24C0019).

C-GPCE, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited Beech 1900D was conducting flight PCO1858 from Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, on an instrument flight rules flight to Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC. The crew added takeoff power to both engines for departure and heard a loud bang from one engine. The crew rejected the takeoff, exited on Taxiway B and entered Apron 2 where the left engine was shut down. The crew observed smoke coming from the left engine and requested aircraft rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) services while monitoring the engine for fire. The smoke dissipated and ARFF arrived to inspect the aircraft. Once deemed safe, the passengers deplaned and were transported to the terminal in 2 airport vehicles. The aircraft was towed to a fixed base operator for further inspection.Visual inspection revealed that some of the second-stage power turbine blades had failed on the left engine. The engine power section module had been overhauled 17 hours before the occurrence during which all second-stage power turbine blades had been replaced with new blades. The manufacturer reported 2 other second-stage power turbine blade failure events that occurred on 2 different engines during testing at the manufacturer's facility. The manufacturer is still investigating the root cause for the blade failures and has issued Alert Service Bulletins (ASB) for different engine models to identify and remove the suspect blades. Transport Canada issued Emergency Airworthiness Directive (EAD) CF-2024-05 on 16 February 2024 that aligned with the ASB and required the replacement of the suspect second-stage power turbine blades on the specified engines before further flight. The EAD is an interim action until the root cause of the blade failure can be determined.

C-GZSG, a Boeing 737 Max 8 operated by WestJet Airlines Ltd., was operating as WJA445 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl. Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. WJA445 was approaching from the north on the RNAV Y for Runway 12. Concurrently, C-FQGG, a Boeing 737 Max 8 operated by WestJet Airlines Ltd. was operating as WJA237 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to CYEG. WJA237 was on vectors from the south for an approach to Runway 12. A loss of separation occurred when separation decreased to 2.2 miles and 500 feet when 3 miles or 1000 feet are required. WJA445 was pulled from the approach and issued vectors to follow WJA237 at the appropriate distance. Both aircraft landed safely with no further impact to operations.

C-FATM, a de Havilland DHC-6 operated by Air Tindi Ltd., was operating as flight TIN604 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT to Hay River Airport (CYHY), NT. While enroute, the No. 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney-Canada PT6A-27), shutdown on its own. The flight crew actioned the QRH, notified operations, and elected to continue their approach to CYHY. An uneventful single-engine landing was conducted.Maintenance update: Engine teardown revealed a failure of the 1st stage sun gear in the reduction gear box (RGB) which led to a decoupling of the RGB and the power turbine (PT) resulting in a PT disc overspeed causing the PT blades to fail. There was evidence of arcing on the sun gear which typically is a result of a lightning strike at some point in the life of the engine. The entrance and exit points of the lightning strike on the sun gear could have been the initiating points of failure. The engine was removed from service.

N320PQ, an Endeavor Air, Bombardier CL-600-2D24, operating as flight EDV4826, departed Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, on a flight to John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), NY, and was climbing though 8000 feet when the flight crew noticed a burnt electrical smell in the cockpit. The flight crew were checking the cockpit when the captain's side windshield electrical heater control unit began to emit sparks/flames. The flight crew donned oxygen masks, declared an emergency and requested a return to CYYZ. The flight crew turned off the windshield heat and the sparks/flames stopped. The flight crew conducted a normal approach and landed without further incident.Maintenance found arcing on the left windshield power terminal block into the inner surface of the windshield and no damage to the wires. The windshield will be replaced.

CF-VDJ, a privately registered Cessna 150G, was being flown in the circuit at Pitt Meadows Airport (CYPK), BC, with only the student pilot on board. The approach to landing was low and the pilot corrected by adding power. The airspeed increased and the pilot reduced power resulting in a loss of altitude followed by a hard landing and propeller strike before the aircraft bounced back into the air. On the second ground contact, the nose wheel broke and the aircraft slid to the left of the runway with the propeller still striking the pavement. The aircraft hit the grass edge of the runway where the nose gear collapsed, and the aircraft came to a rest with its tail in the air. The pilot was uninjured. He secured the airplane and exited without assistance. The aircraft was substantially damaged with dents in the right wing and damage to the propeller and nose gear.The aircraft was removed from the runway and will be assessed by maintenance.

C-FWZK, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited Beech 1900D, operating as flight PCO8992, was conducting a test and repositioning flight from Port Hardy Airport (CYZT), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew and 2 company maintenance personnel onboard. During flight tests at 21 000 feet above sea level (ASL), the aircraft control column made an uncommanded abrupt forward movement and pitched the aircraft in a slightly nose down attitude. The crew opted to descend to 7 000 feet ASL and declared a PAN PAN. Once level at 7 000 feet, the crew observed a second uncommanded abrupt forward movement on the control column and declared a MAYDAY. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 08R at CYVR and aircraft rescue and firefighting personnel inspected the aircraft before it continued taxiing to the company hangar. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft. Maintenance carried out a detailed inspection of the elevator trim control system and replaced both the left and right elevator trim actuators, the electric elevator trim motor and 2 elevator pulleys under the floor. Maintenance performed a rigging and functional check of the elevator system on the ground. The aircraft was test flown with no defects noted.

C-GVJT, a Chartright Air Inc. Cessna C560 was operating flight HRT373 from Sault Ste. Marie Airport (CYAM), ON, to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ). On approach to Runway 23, the flaps failed to extend after flap 15 was selected. The flight crew attempted to cycle the flaps, however there was no change. A go-around was carried out, and an emergency was declared. The aircraft landed without further incident and taxied to the ramp.

Le 31 janvier 2024, vers 15 h 54 heure normale de l'Est, l’aéronef Cessna 172G (immatriculation C-FSSJ, numéro de série 17253659), avec à son bord le pilote, a décollé de l'aéroport d'Ottawa/Rockcliffe (CYRO), ON, pour effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol à vue à destination de l’aérodrome de Maniwaki (CYMW), QC. Dans la nuit du 1er février 2024, à 0 h 35, le pilote a décollé de CYMW pour un vol en direction de CYRO. Après le décollage, le pilote a fait 2 tours inégaux au-dessus de CYMW à des altitudes instables qui variaient entre 1800 et 2800 pieds au-dessus du niveau de la mer (ASL). Après ces 2 tours, le pilote s'est dirigé vers le sud-sud-est, en direction de CYRO. Son altitude a continué d'être instable et en arrivant à 20 milles marins (NM) au sud-sud-est de CYMW, il est descendu et a volé au-dessus du relief ascendant, puis à des altitudes variables, près du sol, pendant environ 5minutes, parcourant environ 6 NM. À environ 26 NM au sud-sud-est de CYMW, alors que l'avion était en virage d'un cap sud-sud-est vers un cap sud-ouest, l'aile gauche de l'avion a percuté un arbre et s'est rompue. L'avion est ensuite entré en collision avec le relief ascendant. Le pilote, dont la ceinture de sécurité a été trouvé détachée, a été mortellement blessé. L'avion a été détruit par la force de l'impact. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) de 406 MHz ne s'est pas déclenchée, cependant les services d’urgence ont reçu une alerte d’accident provenant du téléphone du pilote à environ 1 h 23 et ont avisé le Centre conjoint de coordination de sauvetage de Trenton, ON, qui a lancé les recherches et a découvert l’appareil. Selon le message d’observation météorologique régulière d’aérodrome (METAR) émis à 1 h  pour l’aéroport international Macdonald-Cartier d’Ottawa en Ontario, situé à 32 NM au sud-sud-est du lieu de l’accident, des vents de 6 nœuds soufflaient du 200° vrai avec une visibilité de 10 milles terrestres, un plafond couvert à 1500 pieds au-dessus du sol, une température de 2°C et un point de rosée de 0°C.

C-GKQP, a Porter Airlines, Embraer E190-400 was operating flight POE402 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON.  During cruise at FL410, the flight crew observed a number of EICAS messages, and the autopilot disconnected. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook for AVNX MAU 1A Fail, which indicated increased landing distance and potential loss of nose wheel steering. The flight crew continued to CYYZ and selected runway 15L based on available length and wind conditions. The aircraft landed normally and stopped on the runway for inspection by aircraft rescue and fire fighting in case of brake overheat. No issues were observed, and the aircraft taxied to the gate normally. Porter Airlines maintenance replaced the power supply for the MAU 1 and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GVIB, a Skyservice Business Aviation Inc. Falcon 2000EX, was operating flight SYB123 from Naples Airport (KAPF), FL to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON. At around FL300 the crew observed engine “banging” which they identified as a compressor stall. The crew reduced the thrust, initially banging stopped then started again. The decision was taken to shut down the engine as a precautionary measure and divert to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed in KMCO without further incident.

C-FGZO, a Top Aces A-4N was operating a flight out of Nordholz/Cuxhaven Airport (ETMN), Germany. After 30 minutes of flight at FL100 and the wings leveled with engine operating at 85% RPM, the pilot observed abnormal vibrations and a high-pitch noise. The cabin pressure system was set to RAM AIR resulting in the vibration and noise no longer present. An emergency was declared, and upon achieving desired landing weight, the aircraft returned to ETMN and landed without further incident.

C-IERZ, un ultraléger de base de type Cosmos Phase II sur skis de propriété privée, effectuait des ajustements de carburateur au sol à l’aérodrome de St-Cuthbert, QC (CCU2). Alors que le moteur a été démarré, il est allé à pleine puissance. Le pilote qui était à côté de l’aéronef a tenté de l’arrêté mais l’aéronef a passé sur lui et s’est envolé par lui-même. Le pilote n’a pas été blessé. L’aéronef a volé pendant environ 20 minutes pour ensuite s’écraser dans un petit boisé à environ 1sm au nord est de l’aérodrome.

XA-GJC, an AirLink Air Ambulance Cessna 650, was conducting a flight as PPQ268 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Houston William P. Hobby Airport (KHOU), USA, with 4 crew members on board. On the initial climb out, the crew attempted to select the landing gear up, but the landing gear lever did not move. The crew requested a hold to burn fuel down to the maximum landing weight of the aircraft and subsequently requested a return to CYYC for landing. Aircraft rescue and fire fighting was deployed and the aircraft landed without further incident.Inspection by maintenance personnel found that the centering solenoid cannon plug wire was broken. The wire was replaced, and the handle was tested serviceable on the ground.

C-GNZR, a Canadian Helicopter Limited, Bell Helicopter Textron 206L, was conducting a test flight from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT with 2 crew members on board. While returning to land at CYZF the pilot noted an increased Nr and an abnormal noise from the engine. The pilot declared Pan Pan and elected to land the helicopter in an open area short of the airport. There were no injuries and no damage to the helicopter.Subsequent inspection by company maintenance personnel revealed a loose nut on the engine Pr line.

C-FICU, a Beech 200 operated by Beaver Air Services (dba Missinippi Airways), was conducting a VFR re-positioning flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Winnipeg/St. Andrews Airport (CYAV), MB, with only the pilot onboard. The aircraft entered the circuit on a right-hand downwind for Runway 18 at CYAV and was cleared to land Runway 18. The aircraft landed on Taxiway B; to the right of the Runway 18. A maintenance sweeper was cleared to work west of Runway 18. The aircraft landed safely. The incident occurred during daylight hours.

C-GSGV, a Sander Geophysics Ltd. Cessna 208B was on a low-level survey operations out of Cochise County Airport (P33), Wilcox, AZ. Three hours into the flight, a quiet squealing was heard which lasted for 10-15 seconds. The captain noticed the noise and mentioned it, but at the time it was inaudible to the first officer (FO). At about the same time the noise stopped, smoke was seen coming from in front of the glare shield, and a terrible odour was smelt. The FO first noticed the smoke, then the captain, and drill actions were followed for an Electrical Fire. 10-15 seconds later, the smoke stopped and cleared over the next minute or so. The decision was made to return to base, P33, with a reduced electrical load. Tucson Departure was informed of a systems issue and VFR Flight Following to P33 was requested.

C-GENO, a WestJet Encore Limited de Havilland DHC-8-400 was operating as flight WEN3108 under instrument flight rules from Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. While on the arrival to CYVR, the aircraft encountered severe icing leading to difficulty controlling the aircraft. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and requested a change in altitude. While changing altitude to avoid the icing conditions, further difficulty controlling the aircraft was experienced and the crew then declared a MAYDAY. During the descent on approach, severe turbulence was also encountered. The crew managed to intercept the approach to CYVR and proceeded to land without further incident. There were no injuries reported. The aircraft was inspected after the occurrence. The maintenance crew did not find any damage and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJQH, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1894 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to V.C. Bird International Airport (TAPA), Antigua. During the final approach phase of flight inside the final approach fix (FAF) at approximately 1300' ASL, the flight crew received a TCAS TA for traffic 700' below followed by TCAS RA Climb command. The flight crew complied with the RA and conducted a go-around. The flight was completed without further incident. ATC was questioned about the traffic after landing, however was unaware of the intruder aircraft.

C-FYAG, a Fairchild SA277-AC operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting flight PAG117 from Norway House Airport (CYNE), MB, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl Airport (CYWG), MB. When the gear was selected gear down on the approach to CYWG, the flight crew observed 3 red in-transit lights followed by 2 green down-and-locked lights. The left main gear did not show a green down and locked position. ATC was notified and an emergency was declared. The flight crew completed the quick reference handbook (QRH) checklist, completed an emergency gear extension, conducted a fly-past inspection by the CYWG tower to confirm gear position, and the first officer went back to visually confirm the gear position. Prior to landing, the QRH action included briefly selecting flight idle to check for a landing gear warning horn, which didn't sound. The first officer briefed the passengers and the aircraft landed safely with aircraft rescue and fire fighting on standby.

C-GCHJ, a Helijet Airways Incorporated Sikorsky 76-C+, was conducting a medevac flight from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to the Abbotsford Regional Hospital Heliport (CAB5), BC, with 2 flight crew and 2 cabin crew on board. While on final for CAB5, the pilots observed a "1 AHRS" (attitude and heading reference system) caution illuminated. Shortly after, the No. 1 autopilot (AP) was observed to be off, the 'AP1' caution light illuminated, concurrent with a strong electrical burning smell in the cockpit. The co-pilot very high frequency omnidirectional range (VOR), and the No. 1 AHRS circuit breakers had popped. The aircraft landed normally at CAB5. Maintenance determined that the burning smell was coming from the avionics bay and that it originated in the co-pilot navigation unit.  The unit was replaced, and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FTEN, a WestJet Encore Ltd. de Havilland DHC-8-400 was operating as WEN3317 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. C-GYKI, an Air Tindi Ltd. Beechcraft Corporation B200GT was operating as TIN510 from Hay River/Merlyn Carter Airport (CYHY), NT to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. During approach into CYZF, WEN3317 informed ATC that they were unable to continue the RNAV Y approach and were given vectors for the RNAV Z approach. A loss of separation occurred during the vectoring as TIN501 was on approach for landing. Separation was reduced to 700 feet vertically and 4.6 NM horizontally when 1000 feet and 5 NM were required. There was no risk of collision and no impact to operations.

C-GKQX, an Embraer E195-E2 operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight PD157 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson Int'l Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. During the initial climb, the flight crew received an "APU FIRE" EICAS indication. They actioned the appropriate checklist(s) and declared PAN PAN before requesting a return to CYYZ. ARFF was standing by while the crew conducted a normal landing on runway 23. After taxiing clear of the runway, the ARFF personnel inspected the tail of the aircraft and relayed to the flight crew that there were no indications of fire or damage, after which the crew taxied to the gate. Maintenance replaced a fire sensing loop, a generic I/O card, and the APU fire bottle before returning the aircraft to service.

C-FYJP, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114, was operating flight ROU1878 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON and was climbing through 8500 feet ASL when the cabin crew advised the flight crew of an abnormal odour in the cabin. The aircraft levelled at 10 000 feet ASL, advised ATC and proceeded with the QRH procedures. The flight crew did not declare a PAN PAN or a MAYDAY; the aircraft returned to CYYZ for an overweight landing. The landing was uneventful, and after ARFF completed an external inspection, the aircraft taxied to the gate. Maintenance reported the source of the odor was a contaminated filter element in the Air Cycle Machine #2 and replaced the filter.

C-GKQM, a Porter Airlines E190-400 was operating flight POE521 from Toronto Lester B Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Tampa International Airport (KTPA), FL. Approximately 30 minutes prior to top of descent into KTPA, the crew smelled acrid smoke and detected hazy smoke on the right side of the flight deck. The pilots actioned the SMOKE/FIRE/FUMES checklist and the fumes dissipated. The crew elected to continue to KTPA. The crew reported smoke to ATC and requested aircraft rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) vehicles on the ground, but declined to declare an emergency however, ATC elected to declare an emergency. The aircraft landed safely and ARFF vehicles met the aircraft. The emergency personnel inspected the aircraft for hot spots and also noted the acrid smell.

C-FWEW, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3394 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While climbing through 10 000 feet, the flight crew heard a bang, and observed a right DC generator light and abnormal torque indications from the right-hand engine. The crew actioned the quick reference handbook and shut down the number 2 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW150A). ATC provided vectors for a return to CYEG. The aircraft conducted a single-engine approach and landed without further incident. Emergency vehicles met the aircraft on the runway and the aircraft subsequently taxied to the gate under its own power.Subsequent inspection from company maintenance revealed that the number 2 engines 2nd stage Low Pressure Compressor (LPC2) had failed.

C-GEXB, an Air Transat A T Inc. was operating flight TSC880 from London Airport (CYXU), ON to Cancún International Airport (MMUN), Mexico. An emergency was declared in Boston airspace due to a blocked fuel filter. Crew elected to divert to Montréal / Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. Emergency services were on standby. Aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GDSS, an ATR 42-300 operated by Calm Air International, was conducting flight CAV111 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. While climbing through FL220 the flight crew observed a Master Warning light with a CCAS "Excess Cabin Altitude" message. The flight crew contacted ATC and requested a descent to 13,000 feet ASL. In the descent, the warning went away and the cabin pressure levels returned to normal. The flight continued to CYWG where it landed uneventfully.A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed a jet pump needed replacement. The jet pump and 2 pneumatic outflow valves were replaced and an inspection of the electrical connections and the cabin controller wiring was conducted. Pressurization runs and operational test of the manual pressure control system were completed. A test flight was completed and the aircraft was returned to service. C-GDSS had 2 previous similar events; TSB occurrences A24C0008 and A24C0009.

C-GFAE, a Beech B200 operated by Vanguard Air Care Ltd. as flight VN11, was conducting a flight from The Pas/Grace Lake Airport (CJR3), MB, to Brandon Muni Airport (CYBR), MB. At approximately 150nm NW of CYBR, level at 15 000 ASL, the #2 bus feeder circuit breaker tripped. The flight crew completed the checklist, declared an emergency, and diverted to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl Airport (CYWG), MB. The system fault required a manual landing gear extension and manually flying the ILS instrument approach to Runway 13 in CYWG. The aircraft landed safely with ARFF on standby. The aircraft stopped on the runway where the patient was off-loaded to a waiting ambulance. The operator's maintenance subsequently towed the aircraft to the hangar. The operator's maintenance found that the #2 bus connections had loose wires on the breakers; causing the circuit breaker to trip. The #2 bus area was inspected and the circuit breakers were replaced.

C-GOWG, a Sunwing B737-800 was to conduct flight SWG785 from Juan Manuel Gálvez International Airport (MHRO), Roatán, Honduras to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the #2 engine start sequence and with the engine start lever (fuel) remaining in the "CUT OFF" position, the flight crew observed smoke from the engine. The captain immediately turned the engine start switch to the "OFF" position and the smoke dissipated. The flight crew requested emergency services and the aircraft was towed back to the gate where the passengers were offloaded.

C-GDSS, an ATR 42-300 operated by Calm Air International, was conducting flight CAV240 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Sanikiluaq (CYSK) NU. While climbing through FL200 the flight crew observed a Master Warning light with a CCAS "Excess Cabin Altitude" message. The flight crew contacted ATC and requested a descent to 10,000 feet ASL and a clearance to return to CYWG. In the descent, the flight crew carried out the QRH checklist and was able to decrease the cabin altitude in manual mode. The aircraft landed uneventfully in CYWG.A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed a the flexible hose connected to the T-fitting on the jet pump to be seized. The flexible hose and check valve were replaced. The operator's maintenance also replace the digital pressurization controller. Pressurization runs and a test flight was completed and the aircraft was returned to service. The previous and a subsequent flight of C-GDSS had similar events; TSB occurrences A24C0008 and A24C0012.

C-GDSS, an ATR 42-300 operated by Calm Air International, was conducting flight CAV127 from The Pas (CYQD), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. While climbing through FL200 the flight crew observed a Master Warning light along with a CCAS "Excess Cabin Altitude" message. The flight crew stopped the climb, observed that the cabin altitude was just over 10 000 feet with a high climb rate, and initiated an emergency descent. ATC was advised and the QRH items were carried out. The flight leveled at 9000 feet ASL and the flight crew requested a clearance to proceed to CYWG at 9000 feet. During the flight to CYWG at 9000 feet, the auto pressurization system appeared to be working again and the manual mode was tested but only provided 400 feet per minute descent in the full descent selection. CAV127 subsequently landed uneventfully at CYWG.The operator's maintenance performed fault isolation for excess cabin altitude, performed functional test on the ground of the cabin pressure control in automatic and manual modes. The fault could not be duplicated and the aircraft was returned to service. Subsequent flights of C-GDSS had similar events; TSB occurrences A24C0009 and A24C0012.

C-FGRC, a Perimeter Aviation LP de Havilland DHC-8-102 was conducting flight PAG1519 from Pukatawagan Airport (CZFG), MB, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl Airport (CYWG), MB. While enroute, the flight crew observed a cargo smoke indication. The flight crew performed the quick reference handbook checklist and the flight attendant checked the cargo compartment. No smoke or fire was observed, an emergency was declared, and the aircraft diverted to Flin Flon Airport (CYFO), MB. The aircraft landed uneventfully.The operator's maintenance examined the aircraft and the defect was deferred per the operator's minimum equipment list (MEL). The aircraft subsequently departed CYFO and the flight to CYWG was uneventful.

N445YX, un appareil Embraer ERJ 170-200LR exploité par Republic Airways Inc, effectuait le vol RPA4772 entre l' Aéroport LaGuardia (KLGA) NY, États-Unis et l' Aéroport internationale Pierre Elliott Trudeau de Montréal (CYUL), QC. En approche pour CYUL, l'équipage a demandé que les services d'urgences soient en attente durant l'atterrissage en raison d'un problème avec les volets. RPA4772 a atterri sans encombre piste 24D avec les véhicules d'urgences en attente.

C-GUPL, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300, was conducting flight AC1003 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), USA to Montreal - Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC with 5 crew and 71 passengers onboard. While landing in CYUL, the aircraft experienced a right hand engine flame out followed by multiple associated Engine Indicating and crew Alerting System (EICAS) messages. The crew accomplished the shutdown procedure for the right engine and taxied to the gate without further incident. The aircraft was removed from service for further investigation by the engine manufacturer and the company maintenance department.

C-FPQQ, a Beech B200 operated by Keewatin Air LP., was conducting flight KEW213-M from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl Airport (CYWG), MB to Churchill Airport (CYYQ), MB. Shortly after takeoff, the #2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-42) torque rolled back. The flight crew feathered the #2 propeller, declared an emergency, ran the appropriate checklists, and shut down the #2 engine. The aircraft returned to CYWG and landed uneventfully.The operator's maintenance reviewed the engine trends from an onboard recording device and noted the #2 engine torque slowly decreased to idle over a 28 second span after takeoff power was applied. All other recorded data was reported to have remained in the normal parameters. The operator's maintenance inspected/cleaned the firewall and engine high pressure fuel pumps filters and replaced the low-pressure fuel filter. No faults or excessive contamination was reported to have been found. During a follow-up ground run, the operator's maintenance could not duplicate the fault but noted that the #2 engine power lever friction lock was not engaged. The aircraft was returned to service subject to a satisfactory flight test.

C-FNAA, a BAE Systems Jetstream model 3212, operated by Northwestern Air Lease Ltd., was conducting flight PLR738 from Ft. Smith Airport (CYSM), NT to Diavik Mine Airport (CDK2), NT with 2 flight crew and 5 passengers on board. Shortly after take-off from Runway 30, the aircraft impacted trees at the end of the runway clearway and subsequently collided with terrain. There was a post impact fire, and the aircraft was destroyed. Both flight crew members and 4 passengers received fatal injuries, 1 passenger was ejected from the wreckage during the accident sequence and received minor injuries.

C-GENK, a WestJet Encore DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3125 from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Kelowna (CYLW), BC. During the take-off roll an unknown alarm sounded. The flight crew rejected the takeoff and declared a MAYDAY emergency as per SOP, and subsequently cancelled the emergency while taxiing off the runway. The aircraft then departed uneventfully on the second attempt.Upon further inspection by the flight crew, the unknown alarm was coming from a cellular telephone.

C-GEEN, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), operated by WestJet Encore Ltd., was conducting flight WEN3185 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. On final approach, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence and control of the aircraft could not be maintained. The flight crew initiated a missed approach and the rapid changes in airspeed that the crew had experienced continued until approximately 3500 feet above sea level. The aircraft returned to CYVR and landed safely.Maintenance conducted flap overspeed and severe turbulence inspections and no faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

The Agusta AW119 Koala helicopter (registration C-GSLY) owned by Skyline Helicopters and leased to Northern Escape Heli Skiing, was conducting heli-skiing operations 21 nautical miles (NM) northwest of Terrace Airport (CYXT), British Columbia (BC) with a pilot, a ski guide, and 5 passengers on board. During the flight, the helicopter impacted terrain. The pilot and 2 passengers were fatally injured, and the ski guide and 3 passengers received serious injuries. The helicopter was destroyed. The emergency locator transmitter (ELT) did not transmit a signal. Three helicopters that were conducting heli-skiing operations nearby responded to the accident and airlifted the ski guide and 3 passengers with serious injuries to ambulances that transported them to hospital. One passenger later died as a result of their injuries.

C-FENY, a WestJet Encore de Havilland DHC-8-402 was operating as flight WEN3341 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Canadian Forces Base Comox (CYQQ), BC. During the take-off roll the take-off warning horn sounded at 125 KIAS, which is 5 kts below the intended V1 speed. The flight crew rejected the take-off and declared a MAYDAY emergency. The aircraft returned to the gate where company maintenance conducted troubleshooting. There were no injuries.Company maintenance will advise TSB of the findings.

F-HTYH, an Air France Airbus A350-900, operating as Air France flight AFR356, from Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France to Toronto/Lester B Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, was on approach to Runway 24L; just after touchdown a go-around was initiated. The aircraft suffered a tail strike during the go-around, but the climb out was uneventful, and the aircraft subsequently landed safely. The aircraft sustained substantial damage, there were no injuries.

C-GZEW, un De Havilland DHC-8-314 (DH8C) exploité par Air Creebec inc. sous l'indicatif CRQ5375, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de l'aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) avec 14 passagers et 3 membres d'équipage à bord. Durant la phase de croisière du vol, le personnel cabine a demandé aux pilotes d'augmenter la température en cabine. Le sélecteur étant déjà au maximum, le pilote, voulant mettre le groupe de climatisation en mode manuel a plutôt sélectionné la position "OFF" par inadvertance. Quelque temps plus tard, le voyant d'alerte de pressurisation cabine s'est illuminé. L'équipage a immédiatement initié une descente d'urgence et a déclaré l'état d'urgence. Durant la descente, le pilote a réalisé l'erreur et a remis le sélecteur en position "AUTO". La pression cabine a été restaurée et le vol s'est poursuivi jusqu'à son atterrissage sans encombre à destination.

C-GWPS, a de Havilland DHC-8-102 operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting flight PAG117 from Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl Airport (CYWG), MB. While enroute, the flight crew observed a #1 ENG OIL PRESS warning light flickering intermittently and there was a corresponding flicker between 50-60 psi on the #1 Oil Pressure gauge. The flight crew performed the Low Oil Pressure (40-55 PSI) checklist from the quick reference handbook (QRH), resulting in feathering the #1 propeller; but not requiring to shut down the engine. The oil pressure was monitored per the QRH. The flight crew declared an emergency and the flight continued to CYWG for an uneventful landing. The aircraft has been removed from service pending inspection.

C-FNEN, a WestJet Encore de Havilland DHC-8-402 was operating as flight WEN3397 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Grande Prairie (CYQU), AB. During climb, while departing from CYYC, the flight crew received an R1 door open indication. An emergency was declared. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and the aircraft returned to CYYC. Upon landing, the door indication extinguished. There were no injuries. Company maintenance found the R1 door proximity sensor to be faulty and the sensor was replaced.

C-GOIW, an Air Transat A321 was operating flight TSC153 from Jorge Chávez International Airport (SPJC), Peru to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Shortly after takeoff, a cabin crew member became ill. The cabin crew member was unable to perform their assigned duties. Duties were reassigned amongst remaining cabin crew members.

C-FAKW, an Alkan Air Limited Beechcraft 300 (Super King Air) aircraft, was conducting a flight from Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, to Bellingham International Airport (KBLI), WA, USA. After departure, the crew selected the gear up and though the gear handle came up, the gear did not. The gear indication continued to show 3 green lights. The crew observed that the landing gear circuit breaker had tripped. The aircraft returned to CYCD and flew a low approach over the runway and requested that ATC visually observe the position of the landing gear. The aircraft landed without further incident with aircraft rescue and fire fighting on standby. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft.Company maintenance investigated the gear issue. A diode on a relay was replaced and the gear was swung several times without fault. The aircraft has returned to service.

C-GURJ, an Anderson Air Ltd. Bombardier CL-600-2B16 (Series 604) departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC for McClellan-Palomar Airport (KCRQ), California. When level at 3600 feet in the downwind approach, aircraft was advised to climb to 4000 feet. Upon level off at 4000 feet, the aircraft was advised to climb another 1000 feet. TCAS RA received at 5000 feet. Aircraft able to level off at 5000 feet in accordance with the RA. C-GURJ landed without further incident.

C-FGDZ, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight ACA856 from London Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK to Mumbai Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport (VABB), India. On departure, EGLL tower advised that smoke was observed from C-FGDZ. Aircraft was showing brake 5 fault and zero pressure on that tire. Decision was made to return to EGLL and a Pan Pan was declared. Aircraft landed and emergency vehicles met aircraft on runway for inspection. Aircraft was cleared to taxi to the gate without further incident.Maintenance found #5 wheel assembly damaged with burst tire and correlating faults to anti skid 5, auto brake and brake #5. Wheels #5 and #6 were replaced.

C-GEKX, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 was conducting flight AC1035 from Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 6 crew and 142 passengers on board. During the approach to CYVR, the crew observed an Asymmetric Trailing edge flap warning. The flight crew completed the appropriate checklist and declared a PAN PAN. The landing was completed without further incident with the aircraft stopping on the runway for a brief inspection by Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF). After the inspection, the aircraft taxied to the gate. There were no injuries.Maintenance replaced the left hand flap position transmitter and completed ground checks. The aircraft was returned to service.

N464AW, an Air Wisconsin Airlines LLC. CL-600-2B19 (CRJ-200LR) was conducting flight AWI6086 from O'Hare Intl Airport (KORD), IL, USA, to Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the approach to CYYZ, the flaps failed to extend when selected. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklists and declared an emergency with ATC before continuing with an approach and uneventful flapless landing and taxiing to their assigned gate. ARFF was standing by for the landing. Maintenance reset the flap system and tested the flap system before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FLPA, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 757-200, was operating as flight CJT1574 from John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON to Ottawa MacDonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. Climbing through 7000ft, the flight crew received an EICAS message "L FWD ENTRY DOOR". The flight crew stopped the climb at approximately 11000ft. They were unable to ascertain at that altitude whether pressurization was normal and completed the appropriate checklist. The crew then declared a PAN PAN emergency and requested to return to CYHM. The aircraft landed on Runway 30 without further incident.Post occurrence, a Detailed Visual Inspection (DVI) of the door mechanism and indication system was carried out and the fault could not be duplicated. As a precaution, MEL 52-71-01-01 was applied and M# procedure to verify the door is closed, latched, and locked before each departure was accomplished. The aircraft was returned to service. On 17 January, the door and indication system were inspected, function checked and door system lubricated as per the AMM. No faults were present and the MEL was resolved. The aircraft subsequently flew, three flight legs with no faults.

C-GFDH, an Island Air flight School & Charters Inc., Cessna 150M experienced an engine failure while on a VFR, round robin flight from Billy Bishop Toronto City Center Airport (CYTZ), ON. After having departed from the Oshawa Executive Airport (CYOO), ON control zone, and on the return leg to CYTZ, the pilot noticed a drop in oil pressure which was shortly followed by the engine failure. The pilot declared a MAYDAY and conducted a forced landing on a Bayly Street in Ajax, ON, approximately 6NM southwest of CYOO. The pilot was uninjured; during the landing roll the aircraft's left wing sustained substantial damage as the aircraft collided with a street pole.

C-GPNL, a Boeing 737-300 operated by Bradley Air Services, dba Canadian North, was conducting flight AKT107 from Ottawa Int'l Airport (CYOW), ON, to Iqaluit Airport (CYFB), NU, with 5 crew and 47 passengers on board. The aircraft was de-iced with type 1 and 4 before departure, and the flight crew conducted engine clearing procedures before beginning the takeoff roll. During the takeoff roll at approximately 125 knots, smoke was detected on the flight deck and the flight crew conducted a rejected takeoff. The flight crew stopped the aircraft on the runway and ARFF responded to evaluate the aircraft and check the temperature of the brakes, which were reported to be hot. The crew requested a tow from the runway and shut down the engines. Maintenance did not find a cause or source for the smoke, and after conducting a procedure to remove contamination from the air conditioning and pneumatic systems, the aircraft was returned to service subject to a satisfactory test flight.

C-GJOL, privately registered Diamond DA62, was on a local flight as part of a Civil Air Search and Rescue Association search from the Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC. While on final approach, the pilot noted that the 3 green landing gear down and locked indication was not illuminated. The pilot initiated a missed approach and was cleared to airspace south of the airport where they completed the gear indication checklist. Once the checklist was completed, there was still no change to the indication and the pilot declared an emergency and requested a low and over to have the landing gear checked visually. During that approach, it was noted that the panel lights had been dimmed for improved visibility and when the illumination was increased, the 3 green indication was visible. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FPCU, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited Saab 340B, was conducting flight PCO120 under instrument flight rules from Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. C-FIUJ, an Air Canada Boeing 777-233LR, was conducting flight ACA123 under instrument flight rules from Toronto International Airport to CYVR. A loss of separation occurred while both aircraft were on approach to Runway 08L. At their closest, the aircraft were separated by 2.1 nautical miles (NM) at the same altitude where the minimum required separation was 3 NM horizontally or 1000 feet vertically. The Saab 340 was directed to conduct a missed approach. Both aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FGOV, an Air Tindi de Havilland DHC-7-100 was operating flight TIN807 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT, to Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB. While in cruise the aircraft exhibited two large vibrations. After the vibrations the crew observed that the #2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-50) had a higher-than-normal T5 temperature and a lower-than-normal torque indication. The quick reference handbook items were carried out, which called for a precautionary shutdown of the #2 engine. The aircraft returned to CYZF and landed without further incident.A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed a damaged power turbine compressor. This aircraft had a previous precautionary engine shutdown due to vibrations, high T5 temperatures and low torque on 08 January 2024 (TSB occurrence A24C0001), after which the engine was removed and replaced. This was the aircrafts first flight post engine change.

C-GOIF, an Air Transat Airbus 321-271 NX was operating flight TSC284 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Princess Juliana International Airport (TNCM), Saint Martin. At FL330, between waypoints KAYYT and BOVIC, the aircraft encountered a zone of turbulence resulting in an altitude deviation of 600 feet and a significant reduction of airspeed. The crew advised ATC and the aircraft returned back to FL330 without further incident. No injuries were reported.

C-GEJN, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight ACA1056 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (KPHX), AZ. On final, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to descend. RA was followed and flight was cleared to continue to land. The aircraft landed without further incident.

N662FE, a Federal Express Corporation Airbus A300-600, was conducting a flight from Memphis International Airport (KMEM), USA, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, with 2 flight crew onboard. During the in-range computation for landing data, the flight crew found that the Aircraft Performance Software (APS) would not compute valid landing information with an OAT of colder than -40 degrees Celsius. The crew reviewed the aircraft flight manual and determined that the aircraft is capable in landing at temperatures as cold as -60 degrees Celsius. After consulting with dispatch the crew declared an emergency and opted to continue to CYEG. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYEG.

C-FLPA, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 757-200 was conducting flight CJT626 from Moncton Roméo LeBlanc International Airport (CYQM), NB to Halifax Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. During the approach phase, the crew received an EICAS caution message of a flap disagree between 15 and 20 degrees. The crew broke off the approach, declared a PAN-PAN, reviewed the quick reference handbook and were able to reconfigure with flaps 20. The flight landed without further incident.The aircraft was grounded, and maintenance is waiting for parts based on trouble shooting the issue.

C-GWEU, a WestJet Encore Ltd. Dehavilland DHC-8-402, was operating as flight WEN3329 from Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. Following two missed approaches in CYVR due to wind shear and severe turbulence, the flight continued to the flight planned alternate of Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While en route to CYYC, the flight crew calculated that the aircraft would land with approximately 100 pounds less than the minimum reserve fuel. On approach into CYYC the crew declared a MAYDAY as per their standard operating procedures. The flight landed safely with no other issues.Following the flight, the maintenance department completed a severe turbulence inspection. There were no issues found with the aircraft and it was returned to service.

C-GLMT, a de Havilland DHC-3T operated by Kississing Lake Lodge Ltd. (dba Wings Over Kississing), was conducting a flight from Wollaston Lake Airport (CZWL), SK to Points North Landing Airport (CYNL), SK. After takeoff from CZWL, the pilot was unable to reduce the engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-34) power setting to climb power. All further attempts to reduce power had no effect. The pilot activated the emergency power lever, but it also had no effect. The pilot initiated a climb in an attempt to manage the airspeed. The aircraft then proceeded to CYNL; however, the airspeed increased to over 140 MPH and the pilot's side window shattered. When in range of CYNL, the pilot shut down the engine at approximately 4000 feet ASL with the condition lever. The aircraft decelerated more quickly than anticipated and the aircraft struck trees on final approach and the aircraft came to a stop beside the runway. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left wing, nose, and landing gear. There were no injuries.

C-FMAI, a Boeing 757-2B7 operated by Morningstar Air Express Inc., was conducting flight MAL7090 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While enroute at FL380, the crew observed a "Cabin Altitude, Cabin Auto" EICAS message. The crew then selected manual pressurization; however, they could not get the cabin to pressurize correctly. The crew further received an "Oxygen ON" EICAS message. While descending through FL250, the cabin altitude started descending and stabilized at 8000 feet when the aircraft was at FL200. They then declared an emergency and diverted to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB; where an uneventful landing was conducted.A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed that the cabin outflow valve had iced up causing a pressurization leak. The ice was removed, checks were completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FKAC, a Found Aircraft Canada Inc. FBA-2C1 operated by Bamaji Air Inc., was conducting a VFR flight from Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON to Slate Falls Airport (CKD9), ON. On touchdown at CKD9, C-FKAC ground looped and swerved to the right; coming to a rest approximately 6 feet from the runway edge lights. The aircraft's tailwheel was damaged by the hard snow windrow at the edge of the runway. The aircraft was removed from the runway and was subsequently repaired.

C-GNVR, un Boeing 737-800 exploité par Sunwing Airlines Inc. sous l’indicatif SWG689 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Juan Gualberto Gómez International Airport (MUVR), Varadero, Cuba à l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC. Lors de l’approche à destination, un message de volets bloqués est survenu avant la position 10. L’équipage a discontinué l’approche, a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide et les volets ont été baissés à la position 15 avec le système alternatif. Un état d’urgence a été déclaré et l’atterrissage a été effectué sur la piste 06L avec les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs en alerte. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre et il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FGOV, a de Havilland DHC-7-103 operated by Air Tindi Ltd, was conducting flight TIN807 from Gods River Airport (CZGI), MB to York Landing Airport (CZAC), MB. While enroute to CZAC, the crew noticed vibrations from the #2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-50), after which they noted an increase in T5 and reduction in torque. The quick reference handbook items were carried out, which called for a precautionary shutdown of the #2 engine. The crew declared a PAN PAN and diverted to Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB for an uneventful landing. A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed a damaged power turbine compressor. The aircraft was ferried to the operator's maintenance base for a #2 engine change. This aircraft had a previous precautionary engine shutdown due to low oil pressure on 04 December 2023 (TSB occurrence A23C0112).

C-GLQO, a Porter DHC-8-400 was operating flight P3 2394 from Chicago Midway International Airport (KMDW), IL, USA to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. During the climb, the flight crew was notified by the KMDW tower that sparks were seen out of the left wing and asked for the flight crew's intentions. The crew had no abnormal indications and conducted a visual inspection of the wing from the flight deck. The crew elected to return to KMDW where the aircraft landed safely with ARFF on standby.The inspection of the wing found no damage or anything abnormal.

C-FLPA, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 757-200 was conducting flight CJT619 from Halifax / Stanfield Intl Airport (CYHZ), NS, to Hamilton Airport (CYHM), ON, with 2 crew members on board. During the approach, the flight crew received an EICAS message TE FLAP DISAGREE. The crew conducted a go-around and actioned the appropriate checklists resulting in an alternate flap extension procedure. The crew conducted a second approach and landed uneventfully. Maintenance was unable to replicate the fault, and the aircraft has returned to service. The aircraft had been de-iced in CYHZ before the occurrence flight.

N617TT, a privately operated Bell 206B helicopter, was conducting a flight from High River Aerodrome (CEN4), AB, to a property in Sicamous, BC, with only the pilot onboard. While en route, the helicopter collided with terrain 11 nautical miles east-northeast of Revelstoke Aerodrome (CYRV), BC. The aircraft was destroyed and the pilot was fatally injured. The TSB deployed and is investigating.

C-FNEN, a WestJet Encore Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was conducting flight WEN3435 under instrument flight rules from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC, with 4 crew members and 52 passengers on board. On approach into CYXT, when the flight crew selected flaps to 5, a flap drive caution light illuminated. The crew discontinued their approach and conducted the published missed approach procedure. The crew requested a hold from air traffic control (ATC) where they completed the necessary steps outlined in the aircraft’s quick reference handbook. On completion of the checklist, the crew decided to divert to the Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC. En route, a PAN PAN was declared. The aircraft landed at CYXS without incident with aircraft rescue and firefighting crews standing by. The aircraft taxied to the ramp under its own power.Maintenance are conducting inspections to determine the fault.

C-FHTO, a Top Aces Inc. Alpha Jet Model A was conducting a local flight from Rostock-Laage Airport (ETNL), Germany. While at FL320, the pilot detected an unusual rumbling noise. The engine parameters were observed to be normal. A chase aircraft verified that no fluid was visible on the fuselage. As a pre-caution, the pilot declared an emergency with ATC. A descent was initiated and while passing FL250, the noise disappeared. The aircraft returned to ETNL without further incident.

C-GJZS, a Jazz Aviation LP CRJ900 was operating flight JZA596 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Sacramento International Airport (KSMF), CA. On descent into KSMF, a FADEC fault message was received. Engine was brought to idle as per quick reference handbook. All other indications were normal. PAN PAN was declared to ATC. Aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FEKH, a Jazz Aviation LP ERJ 170-200 was operating flight JZA877 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Once at FL300, the flight crew noticed the ITT as being high on #2 engine. The thrust lever was brought back, bringing the ITT into the yellow range. In the vicinity of Attica, Buffalo, NY, the crew declared PAN PAN with ATC. The aircraft landed at CYYZ safely, where the aircraft rescue and fire fighting met them as a precaution.

C-GJWE, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) owned by Westjet Encore Limited, was operating as flight WS3340 from Comox Airport (CYQQ), BC to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, with 4 crew members and 65 passengers on board. During cruise, approximately 45 minutes into the flight, a flight attendant became unwell and was unable to perform their duties. The affected crew member did not occupy their jump seat for landing in CYEG.

C-GGFJ, un Dehavilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l’indicatif JZA16, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport d’Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Après le décollage, l’équipage a sélectionné le levier de commande du train d’atterrissage en position de rétraction. Les indications des portes et d’avertissement du train d’atterrissage droit se sont allumés. L’agent de bord a confirmé à l’équipage que le train droit était en position rétractée, mais que les portes étaient restées ouvertes. L’équipage a complété les listes de vérification appropriées et a déclaré une urgence au contrôleur de l’unité de contrôle aérien. Le vol s’est poursuivi jusqu’à CYUL où l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GFCI, an Air Canada Rouge A320-214 was operating flight ROU1795 from Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), DR to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the climb phase of flight, in the vicinity of GOSUL waypoint, climbing through 10,000 ft. ASL, the flight crew identified the cabin was not pressurizing. Followed closely thereafter by an associated ECAM: CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT. Climb was arrested at 12,000ft and the flight crew requested and was granted descent to 5,000 ft. ECAM actions were carried out with no effect so the decision was made to return to origin. A MAYDAY was declared by the flight crew as a precaution to ensure aircraft rescue and fire fighting was on stand-by upon landing. The flight attendants were briefed and the flight subsequently landed safely, over Maximum Landing Weight (MLW).Maintenance inspected the aircraft and found the outflow valve to be defective. The component was removed and replaced.

G-CKWD, a Boeing B787-9 aircraft operated by Norse Atlantic UK Ltd., was conducting flight UBT78T from Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL to London Gatwick Airport (EGKK), England. While in cruise flight at FL390 at about 45°33' N, 060°00' W the flight crew heard a loud bang accompanied by a flash at the left windshield. The windshield outer layer was shattered, and the flight crew carried out the window damage checklist. Pressurization was normal, and after a discussion with company operational control center the flight crew decided to continue the flight. The flight crew declared PAN PAN with air traffic services as a precaution and continued to destination EGKK without further incident.

C-FLQY, a Porter Airlines DHC-8-402 was operating flight PD2234 from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS to Ottawa/Macdonald Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. During departure climb from CYHZ the crew noted that the landing gear was not retracting. The crew made a PAN call with ATC and requested a hold to troubleshoot the landing gear issue. The crew actioned the ALL LANDING GEAR FAIL TO RETRACT checklist and called company maintenance control to troubleshoot. It was determined that the LANDING GEAR ALTERNATE RELEASE DOOR was not fully closed, and resetting the door allowed normal landing gear retraction to occur. The crew cancelled the PAN with ATC and continued to CYOW where the flight landed without further incident.The LANDING GEAR ALTERNATE RELEASE DOOR had been opened during preflight checks to open the main landing gear doors for access to the parking brake hand pump in the right main landing gear wheel well.

N827JS, a Cessna 560XL, operated by Fly Exclusive, flight JRE827, was on route from Chicago Executive, IL (KPWK) to Toronto, Lester B. Pearson International Airport, ON (CYYZ), when the flight crew declared an emergency due to an altimeter issue. The flight crew elected to divert to London International Airport, ON (CYXU) where the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FJFR, un Dehavilland DHC6-300 exploité par Air Inuit Ltée sous l’indicatif AIE670M, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) à destination de Tasijuaq, Nunavut (CYTQ) avec 2 membres d’équipage et 1 passager à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, une fumée s’est propagée dans la cabine. L’équipage a complété la liste de vérification d’urgence et a identifié que la fumée provenait du système de chauffage. L’équipage a fait demi-tour pour retourner à CYVP où l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre. Le service de maintenance a trouvé une certaine quantité de liquide de dégivrage à l’intérieur des compartiments des moteurs.

C-FTEN, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 operated by Westjet Encore Ltd, was conducting flight WEN3389 from Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Shortly after takeoff from CYQR, the flight crew received a cabin door unsafe light and stopped the climb. The flight crew declared an emergency with ATC and requested a return to CYQR. The flight subsequently landed without incident.

C-GBHJ, a Helijet International Incorporated Sikorsky S-76C++, was conducting a flight under visual flight rules from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Vancouver Harbour Heliport (CBC7), BC, with 2 crewmembers on board. At 0751 pacific standard time (PST), the aircraft was struck by a blue laser, emitted from a building approximately 500 metres south of the helipad. The laser strike incapacitated the pilot flying, and a missed approach to CBC7 was conducted. Aircraft control was transferred to the non-flying pilot and the crew then returned to the heliport to land. After landing, details of the laser strike were reported to Vancouver Harbour control tower, Transport Canada, and the Vancouver Police Department.

C-GVWE, a WestJet Encore Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was conducting flight WEN3283 under instrument flight rules from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC, with 4 crew members and 41 passengers on board. When the crew selected the landing gear up after takeoff, they observed an intermittent nose gear indication. The crew actioned the applicable procedure from the quick reference handbook (QRH) and declared a PAN PAN with air traffic control. A decision was made to return to Vancouver, and the flight entered a holding pattern to perform a manual landing gear extension. The flight then proceeded to Vancouver and landed without further incident on Runway 08L. After landing, emergency crews inspected the landing gear before the aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.Company maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft and adjusted a nose landing gear door proximity sensor. A nose landing gear swing was carried out, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GDRU, a Carson Air Limited Beech B300 (King Air), was conducting medevac flight CRN811 under instrument flight rules from Masset (CZMT), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 2 crewmembers and 4 passengers on board. While enroute at 27 000 feet above sea level (ASL), a hissing sound was heard by crewmembers, and a rise in cabin altitude was indicated on the aircraft's pressurization control panel. The crew donned oxygen masks and manually deployed oxygen masks for the passengers. A cabin altitude annunciator illuminated, and an aural cabin altitude warning system sounded. The crew requested a lower altitude from air traffic control and initiated a descent. During the descent, an emergency checklist was performed by the crew, but no emergency was declared with air traffic control. The crew leveled the aircraft at 13 000 feet ASL approximately 6 minutes after initiating the descent from their original cruise altitude. The crew subsequently descended to 10 000 feet ASL 20 minutes after their initial level off. The flight continued to CYVR and landed without incident. A maintenance inspection discovered that the left engine main bleed air supply line was disconnected from the pneumatic manifold to which it should have been attached. The connection was repaired, the pneumatic system was tested, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FWTO, un Cessna 177 d'immatriculation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue de l'aéroport de St-Jean-Chrysostome, QC (CSG5) à destination de l'aéroport de Neuville, QC (CNV9) avec le pilote et un passager à bord. Une quinzaine de minutes après le décollage de CSG5 alors que l'aéronef se trouvait à 1500pi. au-dessus du fleuve St-Laurent à la hauteur de St-Laurent de l'Île-d'Orleans, le pilote et son passager ont entendu un bruit fort ressemblant à une détonation et l'aéronef s'est mis à vibrer violemment. Le pilote a alors déclaré Mayday et effectué un atterrissage d'urgence dans un champ de l'Île D'Orleans. Suite à l'arrêt du moteur, le pilote a constaté qu'il manquait environ 6po. à l'extrémité d'une des pales de l'hélice de modèle McCauley 1C172/TM. Il n'y a pas eu de dommages ni de blessés. Un examen sommaire de la surface fracturée de l'hélice montrait des marques de picotement noires à l'intérieur.

C-GWEJ, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was conducting flight WEN3287 under instrument flight rules from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC, with 4 crew members and 44 passengers on board. During cruise, a No. 1 DC GEN HOT caution light illuminated, indicating an overheat condition detected in the starter/generator unit associated with the left engine. In response to the indicated fault, the crew consulted the quick reference handbook (QRH). They QRH instructed them to turn off the No.1 DC Generator but, as the No.1 DC Generator was inoperative and deferred under the operator's minimum equipment list (MEL), the switch was already in the off position. Shortly thereafter, the flight crew were notified that passengers had observed sparks near the left engine nacelle. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN requesting priority landing and emergency services. The aircraft landed on Runway 15 at CYXS with aircraft rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) services standing by. The aircraft was stopped on the runway and inspected by the ARFF crew. No fire was observed, and the aircraft was then taxied to the gate using the right engine. Maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft and replaced the No. 1 DC starter/generator unit; the No. 1 starter/generator remained deferred under the operator's MEL.

C-GWEU, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 operated by Westjet Encore Ltd, was conducting flight WEN3275 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. During the taxi from the gate to the active runway at CYWG, the flight crew received a check fire detection warning light. They declared a MAYDAY, actioned the quick reference handbook and requested that aircraft rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) come inspect the aircraft. ARFF found no signs of smoke/fire or heat. There was no smoke or fumes in the cabin or flight deck. Both fire bottles were indicating LOW. The aircraft taxied back to the gate under its own power. The operator's maintenance replaced the low-rate extinguisher. Operational checks were completed with no faults found.

N78001, a Boeing 777-224 aircraft operated by United Airlines Inc., was conducting flight UAL57 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), US to Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France. During cruise, as the aircraft was entering oceanic airspace, smoke was observed emanating from a passenger’s cell phone. The crew declared an emergency and ATC cleared them to the St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL. During that time, flight attendants discharged halon fire extinguishers and placed the cell phone in a thermal containment bag. No damage or injuries were reported. About 9 minutes after declaring the emergency, the crew cancelled the emergency and requested a clearance back to their original destination. The aircraft continued to LFPG without further incident.

C-GMAS, a Viking Air DHC-6-300 Twin Otter, operated by Air Tindi Ltd., was conducting flight TIN601 from Margaret Lake, NT to Lac De Gras, NT with 2 flight crew and 8 passengers on board. The charter was in support of winter road construction activities. On the approach into Lac De Gras, the aircraft impacted terrain. There were 2 serious injuries, 6 minor injuries, and 2 persons with no injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. JRCC Trenton deployed assets and 3 search and rescue technicians parachuted into the area to provide medical and survival assistance overnight. Additionally, emergency response personnel were deployed from the Diavik Diamond Mine located approximately 7 NM to the NW; they arrived on scene the evening of the accident. All personnel were recovered from the accident site the next day and received the appropriate medical attention.

C-FYJI, an Air Canada Airbus 319-114, was conducting flight AC248 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. Approximately mid-way through the cruise portion of the flight at 35 000 feet above sea level, the left engine (CFM56-5A5) exhibited signs of a compressor stall. The crew reduced power and the engine stabilized. After declaring a PAN PAN with air traffic control, the flight continued to CYEG and landed safely.Company maintenance will conduct required engine stall inspections and assess the engine's operation.

A privately registered Bell 206B, C-GPPW, departed a farm site 22 nautical miles (NM) east south-east of the Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, for a VFR flight to a cabin 40 NM NW of Sundre (CFN7), AB. On arrival at the landing site the pilot flew over the landing area multiple times trying to assess speed and direction; there was a windsock on the cabin. After multiple passes the pilot attempted to land. As the helicopter slowed to land the wind changed direction and the helicopter experienced a loss of tail rotor effectiveness (LTE) and completed one rotation to the right. The aircraft struck the ground in a forward motion, spread the landing gear and the main rotor blade severed the tail boom. The aircraft was shut down and all passengers and the pilot exited the aircraft. The ELT activated and was subsequently turned off. There were no injuries and there was no fire.

The privately registered Piper J3 Cub, C-FEGF, was doing circuits at the Whitehorse International Airport (CYXY), YT. On the last approach to Runway 14L the pilot was unable to differentiate the runway from the infield to right of the runway. During the flare the aircraft drifted to the right and touched down in snow that was deep enough to result in a rapid deceleration. The aircraft nosed over and came to rest on its back. The pilot was uninjured and was able to extricate himself from the aircraft. There was no fire, and the ELT did not activate; ARFF did respond. Flat light and blowing snow conditions were prevalent at the time of the occurrence.

C-FKIW, a WestJet B737-700 was operating flight WJA2810 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON to Sangster International Airport (MKJS) Montego Bay, Jamaica. During the flight, a cabin crew member became ill. The cabin crew member was unable to perform their assigned duties and was not in their assigned jumpseat for landing. These duties were reassigned to the remaining cabin crew members.

C-FFPH, un appareil de type Boeing 737-800 exploité par Sunwing Airlines, s'apprêtait à effectuer le vol SWG348 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport Jean Lesage Intl de Québec, QC (CYQB) à destination l'aéroport Jardines del Rey Intl - Cayo Coco, Cuba (MUCC) avec 6 membres d'équipage et 191 passagers à bord. Pendant le refoulement de l'appareil à la barrière, après que les deux moteurs eurent été démarrés, l'équipage a été informé par le personnel au sol que du carburant fuyait du moteur droit (CFM56-7B26 s/n 657841). Le voyant "Fuel Filter Bypass" du moteur de gauche (CFM56-7B26 s/n 658808) s'est aussi allumé. L'équipage a alors éteint les moteurs et l'aéronef a été ramené à la barrière. Peu après, les services d'urgence de l'aéroport sont arrivés sur les lieux et les passagers ont été débarqués. Des tests ont été effectués sur le moteur droit sans qu'aucune anomalie ne soit identifié et le filtre de carburant du moteur de gauche a été remplacé. L'aéronef a ensuite été remis en service et a décollé 1à 3h45Z.

C-GAGT, a Cessna T206H (Stationair) airplane registered to 2115828 Ontario Incorporated, doing business as First Base Solutions Incorporated, was conducting a flight under visual flight rules from Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC to Calgary/Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB. During cruise approximately 40 nautical miles east of CYXX, the pilot experienced burning smell followed by smoke in the cabin. Cabin vents were closed, and the smoke dissipated. The pilot selected non-essential equipment off and returned to CYXX. The aircraft landed safely in CYXX. Maintenance attempted to troubleshoot the issue and the aircraft underwent test flights. Eventually, maintenance found the cabin heat air ducting hose resting intermittently on the engine block. The hose was replaced and re-secured. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GITU, an Air Canada A321-211 was operating flight ACA552 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), California. Flight was given a long re-route, vectored around weather, and had to perform a go-around at KLAX due to aircraft on the runway. ACA552 declared MAYDAY due to fuel emergency and for priority handling to the diversion airport Ontario International Airport (KONT), California.

C-GBHO, an Airbus A319-114 operated by Air Canada Rouge as ROU1923, departed Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. Airport (CYYZ), ON for an IFR flight to Regina Intl. Airport (CYQR), SK. During cruise at FL360 in the vicinity of waypoint GERTY (CJA5, 10 nm NE), the aircraft entered a region of turbulence. Shortly thereafter, the #2 engine (CFM International CFM56-5A5) experienced instability, vibration, and reduced N1. As the airspeed began to decay, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and requested a descent to FL300. The engine parameters returned to normal after resetting the power settings. The flight crew cancelled the emergency after consulting company procedures. The flight continued to CYQR without further incident.The operator's maintenance removed and replaced the ENG 2 ECU. Subsequent serviceability tests were conducted and the aircraft was returned to service. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) was filed in reference to this occurrence.

C-GPAW, a Pratt & Whitney Canada Cessna 560XLS was operating a flight from Montreal Saint-Hubert Airport (CYHU), QC to Dulles International Airport (KIAD), Washington, DC. During descent, between 16000 and 15000 feet, the aircraft encountered significant wake turbulence from a preceding aircraft on the same track, 2000ft above and 12NM ahead resulting in a pitch and roll upset. The flight altitude abruptly changed from a few degrees nose up and 30 degrees bank. The autopilot disconnected and a Master Warning light illuminated. After the crew successfully recovered and reestablished the aircraft on its nominal flight path, the ATC was advised and a 3.5NM offset track was subsequently flown. The flight landed without further incident.

C-GBIN, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1758 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON to Cancún International Airport (MMUN), MX. During the cruise phase of flight, while at FL360, ROU1758 was experiencing continuous LGT to MDT turbulence for the majority of the flight. In the vicinity of OLABI, the flight encountered a sudden vertical shear which caused the aircraft to abruptly descend 500 ft. The altitude control was reestablished, ATC was advised and the flight returned to FL360. The flight was subsequently completed without further incident. At the time of the occurrence, the seatbelt sign was illuminated and all passengers and crew were seated in their seats. There were no injuries reported nor aircraft damage.

C-GWBU, a Boeing 737-800 operated by WestJet Airlines Ltd., was conducting flight WJA213 from Montreal/Pierre-Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB with 6 crew members and 169 passengers. During the cruise portion of the flight, a flight attendant became ill. The duties of the ill flight attendant were assumed by the other 3 flight attendants. The flight continued to CYYC uneventfully.

C-FFAP, a Beech 200 operated by Vanguard Air Care Inc., was conducting flight VN06 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl Airport (CYWG), MB to Island Lake Airport (CYIV), MB. When the aircraft was en route to CYIV, C-GFFAP experienced a right hand electrical bus failure. An operational decision was made to return to CYWG. On arrival at CYWG, the flight crew were unable to electrically extend the gear, therefore, they performed a manual gear extension. Due to the electrical failure, the landing gear indicating system was inoperative, so a fly-past inspection was completed to determine gear position. The aircraft subsequently landed without incident with aircraft rescue and fire fighting on standby. The operator's maintenance found burnt diodes and feed wires on the #2 bus feeder. They replaced the defective parts, conducted a #2 electrical bus serviceability check, landing gear system check, and confirmed the avionics systems were serviceable.

C-GAWP, a Pilatus PC-12/45 aircraft being operated by NorthStar Air Ltd. as flight BF707, was conducting an IFR flight from Thunder Bay Intl. Airport (CYQT), ON. to Poplar Hill Airport (CPV7), ON. While enroute, the master caution light illuminated, indicating a low fuel pressure condition. Both fuel pumps were confirmed to be running. After completing the emergency checklist, the flight crew declared an emergency and returned to CYQT with Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting Service (ARFF) on standby. The aircraft landed at CYQT without further incident.The operators' maintenance replaced a faulty low fuel pressure switch.

N23GX, un Aero Vodochody L-39 expérimental enregistré au nom de TVPX Aircraft Solutions Inc.
