Trustee effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis de l'aéroport militaire de Bagotville (CYBG), QC, pour ensuite continuer pour un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments à l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU), QC. L’aéronef a obtenu l’autorisation d’effectuer une approche pour la piste 29 à basse altitude et a été observé volant à environ 20 pi au-dessus du sol (AGL), le long de la piste , train d’atterrissage en position rentré. À environ la moitié de la piste, l’aéronef a frappé plus de 35 petits oiseaux, a sorti son train d’atterrissage et a atterri directement devant lui. Il a fait une sortie en bout de piste, a brisé un feu d’extrémité de piste et a poursuivi son chemin sur l’herbe. Il est retourné sur la voie de circulation par ses propres moyens et a circulé jusqu’à l’aire de stationnement. Le pilote a inspecté l’aéronef et a décidé de décoller de Bagotville environ une heure plus tard.

C-GYRS, a WestJet B787-9 was operating flight WS1867 from Daniel K. Inouye International Airport (PHNL), Honolulu, HI to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the flight, a cabin crew member became ill. The cabin crew member was unable to perform their assigned duties and was not in their assigned jumpseat for landing. These duties were reassigned to the remaining cabin crew members. EMS were not required upon arrival.

C-GNLK, un Boeing 737-2K2C exploité par Les Investissements Nolinor Inc. sous l'indicatif NRL945 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Rankin Inlet, NU (CYRT) à destination de Val d'Or, QC (CYVO) avec 77 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de l’approche pour la piste 36 à CYVO, l’équipage a effectué une remontée en raison du train d’atterrissage droit qui ne s’était pas déployé. L'équipage a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et suivi les procédures établies par la compagnie, cependant le train n’a pas sorti.  L’équipage a décidé de se diriger vers leur aéroport de dégagement, Montréal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX) et a déclaré un PAN PAN. En arrivant à CYMX, l’équipage a suivi la QRH pour une sortie manuelle du train d’atterrissage. Le train d’atterrissage a sorti et l’avion s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GIQK, a Swearingen SA-226-TC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP., was conducting an IFR flight from Dauphin/Lt. Col W.G. (Billy) Barker, VC Airport (CYDN), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. Airport (CYWG), MB. During the cruise portion, approximately 70 nautical miles NW of CYWG, the #1 engine (Garrett TPE 331-IOUA-511G) chip detector annunciator illuminated. The flight crew was also notified by a crew member in the cabin of the presence of smoke. The #1 engine was shut down and secured. The flight crew declared an emergency at 46 nautical miles from CYWG with request for airport rescue and fire fighting service (ARFF) on standby. The aircraft landed uneventfully at CYWG and ARFF escorted the aircraft to the apron.

C-GANR, un SAAB 340B exploité par Pascan Aviation sous l'indicatif PSC581, s’apprêtait à effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de l'aéroport des Îles-de-la-Madeleine, QC (CYGR). Lors de l’embarquement des passagers, de la fumée a été aperçue près de l’aile droite, où une unité de chauffage était située. L’équipage a déterminé que la fumée venait de l’unité de chauffage, le personnel au sol a été avisé et a déplacé l’unité loin de l’avion. Un déversement de liquide rouge a été observé où se tenait l’unité de chauffage. L’embarquement a été arrêté, car de la fumée a été observée provenant du système de ventilation de l’avion. À ce moment, il y avait 9 passagers à bord et un débarquement rapide a été effectué sans encombre. Une urgence a été déclarée et le service de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été appelés. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GSNF, a Beech 200 operated by SkyNorth Air Ltd., was conducting flight SN898 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl Airport (CYWG), MB to Lynn Lake Aerodrome (CYYL), MB. During the initial approach into CYYL, the flight crew reduced power and received a "RH Fuel Pressure" master warning. The flight crew referenced the quick reference handbook and turned on the standby boost pump. There was no change to the warning light. Due to weather and icing conditions in the area, the crew elected to divert to Thompson Airport (CYTH), MB. ATC was notified and SN898 declared an emergency. On the climb out from CYYL, the "RH FUEL PRESSURE" light extinguished. The aircraft subsequently landed safely in CYTH and taxied to the hangar. The operator's maintenance conducted grounds runs and 2 engine starts, and no fault was found. The operator's maintenance replaced the right hand fuel pressure switch as a precautionary measure.

C-GENO, a WestJet Encore DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was preparing for flight WEN3318 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC. While still parked at Gate A6, the catering truck arrived at the aircraft and collided with the aft service door. There were no reported injuries and the flight was delayed for inspection. Maintenance found no damage to the door and performed a successful operational check. The aircraft was returned to service for the scheduled flight.

C-FPIJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd Boeing 767-33A, was operating as flight CJT1926 from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (KCVG), U.S., to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During approach, when the flaps were selected to 20 degrees, the crew received an 'LE SLAT ASYM' (Leading Edge Flap Asymmetry) warning on the Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System (EICAS). The crew executed a missed approach to complete the quick reference checklist. The checklist directed the crew to conduct a high-speed approach and the crew declared a PAN-PAN. The aircraft was vectored to the approach for Runway 08R. The aircraft landed without incident. Maintenance followed the fault isolation manual and found an outboard slat sensor disagree. Maintenance replaced the flap/slat electronics unit (FSEU) and a slat proximity switch. The defect was placed on monitor with no further issues reported.

C-FLWJ, a Westjet Airlines Boeing 737 was operating flight WJA1422 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Nevada. While enroute at flight level (FL) 390, in the vicinity of Calgary, Alberta, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to severe mountain wave activity, and requested an immediate descent to FL370. The aircraft received clearance to FL370 and continued to destination without further incident. There was no damage to the aircraft or injuries to the flight crew or passengers.

C-GFSX, an AirSprint Inc. Cessna 525B was operating flight ASP609 from Naples Municipal Airport (KAPF), FL to Charleston International Airport (KCHS), SC. During cruise at FL400 and 15NM WNW of Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL, the crew received a BAGGAGE SMOKE AFT RED CAS message. All parameters were stable and no smoke or odour was noticeable. The quick reference handbook checklist was completed within one minute with the mention of landing as soon as possible. A MAYDAY call was declared with Jacksonville Center and the decision was made to land at KMCO. The crew advised ATC of the nature of the emergency and asked for vectors towards KMCO. The approach was normal and landing was conducted at 195 LBS overweight. Once the aircraft came to a stop on the runway, emergency evacuation procedure was conducted as per standard operating procedures, without firing the bottle. The aircraft was towed to the Service Center.

C-GDDJ, a Wilderness Seaplanes Limited Grumman G-21A aircraft (serial number 1184) was conducting a flight under visual flight rules from Bella Bella (CBBC), British Columbia (BC) to Port Hardy (CYZT), BC, with 1 pilot and 4 passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff from Runway 13, the left engine surged and lost power. A few seconds later, the right engine lost power. The pilot communicated a Mayday call on the aerodrome traffic frequency and conducted an emergency landing in a forested area approximately 0.5 nautical miles southeast of CBBC. All occupants received minor injuries and were able to exit the left cabin door. The occupants walked to a nearby road where local residents transported them to the Heiltsuk Hospital in Bella Bella, BC. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FEQX, a Summit Air Ltd. Dornier 228-202 was departing from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), Northwest Territories to Fort Simpson Airport (CYFS), Northwest Territories on an instrument flight rules (IFR) flight. During the departure from CYZF, at approximately 0908 Mountain Standard Time, the flight crew observed the #2 (right-hand) engine RPM was approximately 94-95%. The flight crew advised air traffic control that they needed to level off at 2500 feet above sea level to do some troubleshooting. The flight crew reduced the throttles to cruise power setting. The #2 engine was not responding to throttle changes so the flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook (QRH) and shutdown the #2 engine (Garrett TPE 331-5-252D) as a precaution. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed back at CYZF without further incident.Maintenance is investigating.

C-FMKJ, an ATR-72-212A aircraft operated by Calm Air International LP., was conducting an IFR flight from The Pas Airport (CYQD), MB to Flin Flon Airport (CYFO), MB. While en route at 11000 feet ASL, the flight crew received a TCAS warning and a descent Resolution Advisory (RA). The pilot-in-command disconnected the autopilot and turned westward while descending 400 feet. Shortly thereafter, the flight crew observed a Beech King Air aircraft approximately 1/2 mile away, passing on their starboard side. The flight continued to CYFO uneventfully.

C-GJYZ, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation Ltd. was departing Island Lake Airport (CYIV), MB for an IFR flight to Red Sucker Lake Airport (CYRS), MB. During the takeoff roll, C-FGTI an Airbus AS350-B2 helicopter operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd. departed from the apron at the same time and drifted towards the side of the runway in use by C-GJYZ. The pilot of C-GJYZ delayed rotation to avoid conflicting with the helicopter. Once clear of the helicopter, C-GJYZ rotated and climbed out without further incident.

C-GKQI, a Porter Airlines Inc. DeHavilland DHC-8-402, operating as flight POE2466 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. POE2466 had a "#1 HYD ISO VLV" caution light indication, with one other associated light while in cruise at FL240. A #1 Hydraulic Failure was confirmed, the crew actioned the appropriate quick reference handbook checklist, notified their company and declared a Mayday emergency. The aircraft diverted to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, and landed on Runway 23. The flight crew used max reverse on landing and then applied parking brake pressure to further slow the aircraft. After landing, aircraft rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) indicated the aircraft was safe to taxi off the runway. Once off taxiway, ARFF updated their inspection and indicated that hydraulic fluid was leaking from the aircraft. The flight crew elected for an evacuation, and an all-exits evacuation was completed where 6 passengers left the plane using the aft exits and the remaining passengers used the 1L door. No injuries were reported. The aircraft was later towed to a ramp parking spot. Post occurrence inspection found the Balance Relief Valve leaking. The part was replaced, a fluid service was carried out and no further leaks were noted. A BRV ops check was required but due to a lack of a Hydraulic power cart available at YYZ (where the aircraft maintenance was carried out), the aircraft was authorized for a ferry flight to CYTZ to carry out that task. No further faults were noted and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FHBX, an ATR 42-500 operated by Transwest Air (dba as Rise Air), was conducting flight RS102 from Prince Albert/Glass Field Airport (CYPA), SK to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. C-GGCA, a Beech 1900D operated by Transwest Air (dba as Rise Air), was conducting flight RS193 from Key Lake Aerodrome (CYKJ), SK to CYXE. During the IFR approach to Runway 33 at CYXE, C-GGCA was sequenced behind C-FHBX. The separation between C-FHBX and C-GGCA deteriorated to less than the required minimum. C-GCCA was instructed to overshoot and was given vectors to return for another approach to Runway 33.

C-GJTX, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1628 from CYYZ to KFLL. During EN ROUTE, climb to cruise phase of flight, through FL270 to a cleared altitude of FL340, in a managed speed auto-throttle mode, the aircraft began to accelerate toward an overspeed condition as a result of sudden vertical shear and quartering tailwind increase of 10 knots. Flight crew disconnected the autopilot in order to manage airspeed through the use of increased rate of climb. Through FL310, the autopilot was reengaged however the aircraft did not level until FL344. TCAS RA was triggered due to crossing traffic at FL370. Flight crew complied with the RA, notified ATC and returned to FL340 and resumed normal navigation after the conflict was resolved. The flight was subsequently completed without further incident.

C-GRAG, a WestJet B737-8 was operating flight WS1867 from Daniel K. Inouye International Airport (PHNL), Honolulu, HI to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the cruise phase of the flight, a flight crew member became ill and could not perform the duties. There was a deadheading pilot onboard who performed the duties for the remainder of the flight. There was no emergency declared. The flight landed without further incident.

C-GJXY, an Air Canada A220 was operating flight AC745 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA. During descent, the flight crew received a TCAS RA. The RA was actioned, and a go around was initiated. The flight landed without further incident.

C-GWUT, an Air Canada A220-300 was operating flight AC1204 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL. During descent, the flight crew notified dispatch that they received an EICAS “R ENG OIL PRESS” message. The checklist was completed, a Mayday was declared and RH engine was shut down. The decision was made to divert to Palm Beach International Airport (KPBI), FL and the flight landed without further incident.An initial inspection by Contracted Maintenance revealed no external leaks and the oil quantity level was full. Suspect an oil indication issue. Maintenance investigation is underway.

C-FIUR, an Air Canada B777-300 was operating flight ACA36 from Brisbane Airport (YBBN), Australia to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. In cruise, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence with stick shaker activated, shear +/- 20 knots, unable to maintain altitude with momentary loss of control. The aircraft descended and remained at FL270, all passengers were seated and no injuries were reported. The flight continued to CYVR without further incident.

C-GPDB, a Sunwest Aviation Ltd. Learjet 45 was operating flight CNK678 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Scottsdale Airport (KSDL), Arizona, USA. In the vicinity of Provo, Utah, USA the crew received a HYD QTY LOW CAS message. The crew elected to return to CYYC for ease of logistics. During the approach into CYYC, the crew received a second CAS message, this time in amber, and declared an emergency with ATS. The aircraft landed without further incident.Following the flight, the maintenance team found a cracked hydraulic line, which was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

Une perte d’espacement longitudinal est survenue à environ 13 milles nautiques (NM) au nord-est de l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl QC (CYUL) entre un DHC8-400 exploité par Hydro Québec sous l’indicatif de vol HYD171 C-GHQP et un BD-100-1A10 (CHALLENGER 300) exploité par Netjets Aviation sous l’indicatif de vol EJA755 N755QS. La perte de séparation est survenue lorsque l’équipage de conduite du EJA755a tourné sur le cap 175 degrés alors qu’il avait été assigné et relu le cap 075. L’espacement a été réduit à 2,7 milles alors que la norme est de 3 milles.

C-GKLB, a Canadian North ATR42-300, was operating as flight AKT620 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Kugluktuk (CYCO), NU. Prior to departure, the crew had carried out a pre-flight inspection on the aircraft, noting the 1/8 inch of ice on the exterior of the aircraft from the freezing rain. The AOA vanes were also checked for freedom of movement. The aircraft was de-iced prior to departure. Immediately after rotation the captain’s stick shaker activated as well as master caution / chime sounded, and a FLT CTRL indication was observed on the CCAS. The issue was identified as a stick shaker fault. The climb was stopped at 1 500 feet ASL and the flaps and landing gear were retracted; however, upon landing gear retraction, the right main landing gear showed a gear unsafe indications. The landing gear was selected down and the flight crew observed a down and locked indication for all three landing gear. The flight crew left the landing gear down for the return to CYZF. The crew declared a “PAN, PAN” and landed safely back a CYZF.Following the flight, the maintenance team conducted a landing gear retraction overspeed inspection, replaced the right-hand main landing gear uplock box, replaced the crew alerting computer and cleaned the AOA sensors. A satisfactory verification flight was completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GVYZ, a North-Wright Airways Beechcraft 1900D, was operating as flight NWL125 from Norman Wells airport (CYVQ), NT to Tulita airport (CZFN), NT. While departing from CYVQ a security event occurred involving a passenger. A Mayday was declared, and the flight returned to CYVQ where the passenger was arrested by RCMP. There were no injuries.

C-GLLS, A STARS Aviation air ambulance helicopter MBB-BK117 D-2 (AH 145), was operating from Edmonton international airport (CYEG), AB to the hospital in Two Hills, AB. The flight was stood down 20 minutes from the destination and returned to CYEG. As the helicopter began the right turn to return to CYEG, the flight crew experienced an issue with the autopilot. The recovery mode was selected in order to switch from NAV mode to HDG mode. Expecting a turn to the right the aircraft immediately began a turn to the left with a greater than normal roll rate. The pilot flying (PF) allowed the un-commanded left roll to continue, guarding the cyclic.  Through 30 degrees of bank, the PF began to over-ride the roll while allowing some more bank to develop.  As bank approached 60 degrees (and upon completion of the 180 degree turn) the PF manually rolled out with normal over-ride indications displayed.  Some altitude was lost. Significant lateral force on the cyclic was required to keep the aircraft straight, recovery mode was again engaged. The pilot in command (PIC) took control to confirm the control issue, and again a significant roll rate to the left began, stopped by manual pilot override as the bank angle approached 60 degrees. A while later the autopilot was set up the same way with no unusual responses from the autopilot. The flight landed safely at CYEG.Following the flight, the FDR was downloaded, and the manufacturer (Airbus Helicopters) was consulted.

C-GPAK, an Iskwew Air Incorporated Piper PA-31-350 (Chieftain) aircraft, was conducting a flight under instrument flight rules from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Qualicum Beach Airport (CAT4), BC. While on initial descent for CAT4, the right engine (Avco Lycoming LTIO-540-J2BD) began running rough and reduced fuel flow was observed. The pilot selected the emergency fuel pump on with no change to the fuel flow. The pilot declared an emergency and decided to divert to their alternate airport of Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. On approach to CYYJ, the vibration in the right engine increased and the pilot conducted a precautionary engine shut down. The aircraft landed safely at CYYJ.Maintenance found a faulty cylinder in the right engine. The cylinder was replaced, and the aircraft returned to CYVR. The engine underwent a thorough inspection and was removed from the aircraft for overhaul.

C-GRAX, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-MAX 8, operating as flight WJA1624, was operating from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, NV. Icing conditions were encountered during the climb from 13 000 feet to FL230. At approximately FL240 a vibration in the number 2 engine (CFM INTERNATIONAL, LEAP 1B27) was noticed. The quick reference handbook was actioned (QRH) for 'Engine High Vibration' and the climb rate was reduced. ATC was advised and a request was made to return to CYYC. The vibration was minimized with low thrust in the decent. During the arrival, a Pan Pan was declared and aircraft rescue and fire fighting was requested. The flight landed with no further issues and stopped on Taxiway D3 for emergency crews to inspect the engine. No damage was found and the aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.Following the flight, the maintenance team carried out FOD and bird strike inspections and various other maintenance actions on the engine. Engine maintenance runs were conducted and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GFCP, an Airbus A320-214, registered to Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1998 from Moncton/ Greater Moncton Romeo Leblanc International Airport (CYQM), NB. to Sydney/J.A. Douglas McCurdy Airport (CYQY), NS. ROU1998 was cleared for the RNAV Z Rwy 24 at CYQY. While on the approach, light turbulence was encountered below 4000ft with intensity increasing to MDT by approximately 3000 ft. Due to the turbulence, the flight crew increased the approach speed in accordance with company policy and procedure. Descending through 900 ft, the decision was made to abandon the approach due to turbulence and high potential for windshear. During the missed approach, a minor flap airspeed limitation exceedance occurred as a result of the increased approach speed. The flight climbed to smoother air at 8000 ft and entered a hold to assess the situation. Following consultation with dispatch and maintenance, the decision was made to divert to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Once the diversion was initiated, FMGC (Flight Management Guidance Computer) fuel planning indicated the flight would land at minimum reserve fuel. As such, a minimum fuel declaration was made with ATC as a precaution. Expedited routing was provided and the aircraft landed safely at CYYZ with fuel above the required minimum reserve fuel onboard.Following the occurrence, the flap airspeed exceedance was entered in the aircraft journey log in accordance with company policy and procedure. Maintenance inspected the aircraft in accordance with the AMM and found no faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GGAH, a De Havilland DHC-8-402 registered to Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA658 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, to Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. After conducting an approach at CYHZ for Runway 23 and due to the weather conditions, a missed approach was conducted and crew elected to divert to Deer Lake Airport (CYDF), NL. While on initial approach to CYDF, the flight crew requested priority handling with air traffic control due to not being able to hold because of the diversion. JZA658 landed safely at CYDF at approximately 09:05 UTC.

C-GFLN, un Pilatus PC 12/47 exploité commercialement par les Chantiers Chibougamau lte effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Chibougamau Qc(CYMT) à destination d'Amos/Magny Qc (CYEY). Lors de l'extension du train d'atterrissage à l'approche de CYEY le pilote a entendu un bruit anormal suivi d'une indication de train avant non verrouillé. Un second cycle du train d'atterrissage donnant le même résultat, le pilote a déclaré une urgence et à choisi de faire diversion vers l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert Qc où l'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre.

C-FFLJ, a Flair Airlines B737 was operating flight FLE1621 from Orlando Sanford International Airport (KSFB), FL to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. The crew declared an emergency while pushing back from the gate after one of the engines ingested an absorbent pad. The aircraft was towed back to the gate and the passengers were deplaned. There were no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft.

C-GNLW, a Nolinor Boeing 737-200 was operating as flight NRL100 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Goose Lake (CGS2), NU. The crew received a Flight Indicating System malfunction message. The crew elected to return to CYZF and an emergency was declared. The flight landed with no further issues.Following the flight, the maintenance team replaced the No. 1 Vertical Gyro. The aircraft was released back into service.

N811NW, un Airbus A330-323 exploité par Delta Air Lines Inc sous l’indicatif DAL135 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Amsterdam Schiphol, aux Pays-Bas (EHAM) à destination de Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County in Michigan, aux États-Unis (KDTW) avec 270 passagers et 13 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors qu’il était en vol de croisière, une indication d’anomalie du système d’anti givrage du moteur gauche est apparu. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et la décision a été prise d’effectuer une diversion à destination de l’aéroport de Goose Bay, NL (CYYR). L’équipage a ensuite déclaré un état d’urgence auprès de l’ATC et a fait part de leur intention de diversion. L’avion se trouvait à environ 35 miles marins au nord-est de l'aéroport Michel Pouliot de Gaspé, QC (CYGP). Il s’est ensuite posé sur la piste 26 à CYYR sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FDSN, a VIH Helicopters Ltd. Sikorsky S-61L, was conducting heli-logging operations approximately 60 nautical miles west-northwest of Pemberton Aerodrome (CYPS), BC, with 2 flight crew members on board. On approach to delivering a load of logs to the log loader, the aircraft yawed, and a large torque split was observed between the 2 engines. The No. 2 engine (CT58-140-2) torque read 0, and the master caution light illuminated. The flight crew released the load, confirmed the emergency, and jettisoned the external line from the belly hook of the aircraft. An emergency single-engine landing was accomplished without further incident. There was no damage to the helicopter and there were no injuries.The engine will be recovered to a maintenance facility for an inspection.

C-GLQF, a Porter DHC 8-402 was operating flight PD2721 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON to Dulles International Airport (KIAD), Virginia, USA. During the cruise portion of the flight, pilots noticed FUELING ON C/L illuminated. The quick reference handbook checklist was actioned. Company was contacted via ACARS; maintenance department responded that continuing to KIAD was acceptable and that the CA was to check the refuel/defuel panel upon landing in KIAD. ATC was advised that C-GLQF had a small chance of a loose cover and that a runway inspection should be conducted after landing as a precaution. ATC advised that they were elevating report to emergency status and requested fuel, souls on board, and dangerous goods. Upon landing on 1R in KIAD, PD2721 was instructed to exit the runway at K4 and stop on the taxiway for an inspection. Emergency vehicles were standing by; one of them conducted an inspection. Inspection revealed no abnormalities and the aircraft was cleared to taxi to the gate, with one emergency vehicle following.

C-GRJO, un Airbus Helicopter AS350-B2 exploité par Héli Express, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de La Tabatiere, QC (CTU5) à destination de Chevery, QC (CYHR) dans le cadre d’un contrôle de compétence pilote (CCP) avec un pilote et un pilote vérificateur agréé (PVA) à bord. Lors de l’approche vers la piste 25 en conditions de vents traversiers de la droite, une panne hydraulique a été simulée. Au moment de l’atterrissage, une perte de maitrise en lacet est survenue, le PVA a pris les commandes et l’hélicoptère a percuté le sol en bordure gauche de la piste. Un occupant a subi des blessures mineures et l’hélicoptère a subi des dommages importants. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée.

C-GYJZ, a De Havilland DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA169 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. After landing and while taxiing to the gate, a crew member was medically unable to perform their duties.

C-GKFS, a Convair 340 aircraft operated by Kelowna Flightcraft Air Charter Limited, was conducting flight KFA575 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. C-GLGA, a Cessna C208B operated by Skylink Express Incorporated, was operating flight SLQ520 from CYVR to CYYJ. A loss of separation occurred when C-GKFS deviated from the assigned heading as published in the Vancouver 2 standard instrument departure (SID).

N716UW, an Airbus A319-112 aircraft, operating as American Airlines flight AAL1246 was on the approach to runway 33R at Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON; as the flight crew selected the flaps down, they failed to move, due to an asymmetry fault. The crew followed the electronic centralized aircraft monitor (ECAM) and quick reference handbook procedures and declared a MAYDAY. The approach was continued, and the aircraft landed with slats at 2 and flaps retracted; aircraft rescue and fire fighting were standing by. Maintenance reset the right-hand flap interconnecting strut as per aircraft maintenance manual (AMM) and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBHR, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-100 was conducting flight ROU1820 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Puerto Plata Gregorio Luperon International Airport (MDPP), Dominican Republic. Shortly after takeoff, the flight crew noticed an abnormal odor in the flight deck. The flight subsequently leveled at 15 000 feet for troubleshooting the source of the odour. After an unsuccessful attempt to rectify the condition, the flight crew elected to return to CYYZ. An emergency was declared with Cleveland Air Route traffic Control Center (ARTCC) as a precaution. ROU1820 returned to CYYZ where it landed without further incident. Maintenance is investigating the source of the odor.

C-GMCP, un Learjet 45 exploité par Starlink Aviation Inc. sous l’indicatif TLK833 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l’aéroport de St John's, NF (CYYT) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). En approchant de CYUL, l'équipage a eu un ECAS MESSAGE : BREAK FAIL et a déclaré une urgence. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre et les freins ont été efficaces. Le même événement s’était produit à CYYT le 4 décembre 2023 (A23A0075), l’aéronef avait été remis en service, mais le message s’est de nouveau affiché. Le département de maintenance travail à résoudre la problématique.

C-GWBF, a WestJet B737-700 was operating flight WJA1540 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to George Bush Intercontinental/ Houston Airport (KIAH), TX. At 37 000 feet, the autopilot and autothrottle were disengaged. Flight crew lost both flight directors and the altitude alerts started to go off continuously. An emergency was declared due to equipment limitations. Aircraft was vectored in for the ILS 26L approach. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GTRG, a Gulfstream 200 aircraft operated by Chartright Air Inc., was conducting flight HRT024 from Boise Airport (KBOI), Idaho, USA to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While enroute to CYYZ, the flight crew received a number of warning messages. The crew subsequently declared an emergency (Pan Pan) with Air Traffic Control (ATC) due to electrical issue and possible loss of flap and communication upon landing. The flight crew requested the longest runway due to the possible flap malfunction during landing. HRT014 landed with a partial flap extension on CYYZ runway 05 with emergency services standing by. The company grounded the aircraft, and the maintenance department is investigating the issue.

C-GBHY, un Airbus 319-114 exploité par Air Canada Rouge sous l'indicatif ROU1597, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l’aéroport d’Halifax/Stanfield Int’l, NS (CYHZ) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Alors qu'il était en approche finale à CYUL, une perte d'espacement est survenue lorsqu'il s'est retrouvé à moins de 2,1 miles marins derrière C-GWUT, un Airbus A220 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA1074 en approche finale alors que l'espacement requis était de 3 nm.. Lors de la descente, ROU1597 a rencontré du givrage modéré entre 8000 et 2200 pieds avec une augmentation significative d’accumulation au travers de 3000 pieds. Alors qu’ACA1074 qui était devant a ralenti, le contrôleur a demandé à ROU1597 de réduire sa vitesse et a finalement instruit à ROU1597 d’effectuer une remise des gaz alors qu’il passait 2200 pieds et de monté à 3000 pieds afin d’assurer l’espacement. En raison des conditions de givrage, l’équipage a demandé à continuer l’approche pour des raisons de sécurité et l’ATC a permis à ROU1597 de continuer l’approche et de l’aviser lorsqu’il aurait ACA1074 en vue. ROU1597 était toujours dans des conditions IMC à ce moment, mais avait ACA1074 sur leur écran TCAS, ROU1597 a par la suite avisé avoir le trafic en vue et a été autorisé à poursuivre avec une approche visuelle. Les 2 aéronefs se sont posés sans encombre.

C-FXMY, a Beech B200 operated by Keewatin Air Ltd., was conducting a medevac flight from Baker Lake (CYBK), NU. to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. Shortly after takeoff, the medical crew noticed smoke in the cabin and alerted the flight crew. The flight crew confirmed the presence of smoke, carried out the required emergency procedures, and returned to CYBK. The aircraft landed safely. The flight crew, the medical team and the patient deplaned. There were no injuries. The flight crew carried out a visual inspection of the aircraft and secured it on the ramp. The operator's maintenance were dispatched to CYBK and were unable to duplicate the fault. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FWRR, un MHI RJ Aviation ULC CL-600-2B19 (CRJ200) exploité par Pivot Airlines (2746904 ONTARIO INC) sous l'indicatif GGN9200, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU), Qc à destination de Sept-Îles (CYZV), QC.          C-FKNQ, un hélicoptère de type AS355 N, exploité par Hélicoptères Canadiens Limitée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis CYZV. Une fois posé à CYZV, l’équipage de GGN9200 a avisé que durant l’approche à 200 pieds AGL, il avait reçu un avis de résolution du système de surveillance du trafic et d'évitement des collisions (TCAS) en raison de C-FKNQ. C-FKNQ était en stationnaire à la verticale de son point d'atterrissage à ce moment.

C-GMCP, a Learjet 45 aircraft operated by Starlink Aviation Inc., was conducting flight TLK833 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl Airport (CYUL), QC to St. John’s Intl Airport (CYYT), NL. While on approach to CYYT, the flight crew selected the landing gear to the DOWN position which was immediately followed by the illumination of a crew alerting system (CAS) message BRAKE FAULT. The flight crew decided to conduct a missed approach to trouble shoot the indication, and when the landing gear was lowered on the next approach the BRAKE FAULT CAS message illuminated again. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN as a precaution to have emergency services stand by and the aircraft landed at CYYT without further incident.Maintenance personnel replaced the defective brake shuttle module.

C-GWUQ, an Air Canada Airbus A220 was operating flight ACA1359 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Monterrey International Airport (MMMY), Mexico. After departure, the flight crew heard and felt a loud bang when the landing gear was being retracted. Subsequently, multiple technical faults were indicated. The crew elected to return to CYYZ and declared a Pan Pan. The aircraft landed without further incident.

G-VBOW, a Boeing B787-9 aircraft operated by Virgin Atlantic Airways Ltd., was conducting flight VIR23X from London Heathrow Intl (EGLL), England to Los Angeles Intl (KLAX), CA. While in cruise at FL380 at about 42°38' N, 060°44' W the flight crew received a EICAS PACK L alert. The aircraft had dispatched with R1 cabin air compressor (CAC) inoperable, and a descent would be required because the aircraft had only one CAC available. The flight crew requested descent with Iceland air traffic services (ATS), who could not accommodate the request. The flight was handed over to Montreal ATS and the flight crew declared PAN PAN and requested FL340, which was approved. The flight crew descended to FL340 and conducted troubleshooting by communication with their maintenance control center. Resetting the air pack was unsuccessful and the flight continued to destination KLAX at FL340 without further incident.

C-GWEJ, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was operating as flight WEN3184 from Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During the flight, a cabin crew member became unwell and was unable to continue performing their duties. The crew member was removed from the jump seat. A deadheading crew member took over the duties and occupied the jump seat for landing. The aircraft landed without further incident. There were no injuries.

C-GBHJ, a Helijet International Incorporated Sikorsky S-76C++, was conducting flight JBA717 from Vancouver Harbour Heliport (CBC7), BC, to Victoria Harbour Heliport (CBF7), BC, with 2 pilots and 12 passengers on board. While levelling off at 4000 feet ASL, the crew observed a gear box oil pressure warning indication. The flight crew followed the emergency checklist, declared a PAN PAN, and diverted to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. The aircraft landed without further incident. There were no injuries and there was no damage to the aircraft.Maintenance identified a faulty main gear box pressure switch. The switch was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FBWI, a WestJet B738, was operating flight WJA1401 from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Nevada, USA to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During cruise, a cabin crew member was unable to continue performing assigned flight duties; these duties were re-assigned.

C-FWIJ, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight WJA198 from Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Shortly after takeoff, the crew selected the flaps up however the flaps did not fully retract. They stopped at "5" as indicated on the flap gauge. The flight crew conducted the "Trailing edge flap disagree" checklist from the quick reference handbook (QRH) and elected to divert to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. On approach into CYVR, the airport tower controller deployed the aircraft rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) crews and equipment as a precaution. The aircraft landed without incident and was inspected by ARFF on the taxiway before proceeding to the terminal. There were no injuries. Maintenance inspected the aircraft and found a defect in the left trailing edge flap transmitter connector. The connector was replaced, and ground tests determined the flaps were functioning as designed. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GSKA, a Beech 1900C operated by SkyLink Express Inc., was conducting flight SLQ735 from Windsor International Airport (CYQG), ON to John C. Munro/Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON. During the approach, when the flight crew selected the landing gear to the down position, there was no movement of the landing gear. It was observed that the "landing gear relay" circuit breaker had been tripped, and attempted a reset, which was unsuccessful. After advising ATC of the issue, the crew completed a manual gear extension procedure which resulted in an indication that the landing gear was down and locked. The crew elected to conduct a fly-by of the control tower in order to have the tower controller verify that the landing gear appeared to be extended; the tower controller could not verify that the nose gear was extended. The tower controller asked the crew whether they would like to have aircraft rescue and fire fighting on standby, and the crew confirmed that they would. The flight landed uneventfully on runway 30 and taxied to the apron. Maintenance action included replacement of the gear solenoid diodes and the gear handle cannon plug. Gear swings were successfully completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

PH-BQE, a KLM Royal Dutch Airlines Boeing 777-200, was operating as flight KLM677 from Amsterdam Schiphol Airport (EHAM), Netherlands to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During arrival the flight crew informed Calgary Arrival of a high temperature indication on the right rear aft tire on the main landing gear and requested a runway inspection and aircraft rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) to check the tire temperatures. ARFF was notified and the aircraft landed uneventfully and taxied to the gate.

C-FCRZ, un appareil de type ATR-72-202 exploité par CALM AIR INTERNATIONAL LP, effectuait le vol CAV784 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport d’Iqualuit (CYFB), NU à destination l'aéroport de Clyde River (CYCY), NU. Un appareil inconnu effectuait un vol de CYCY à CYFB. L’équipage de CAV784 a reçu un avis de résolution TCAS RA en palier au niveau de vol 190. L’autre appareil qui était en sens inverse avait choisi la même altitude de vol alors qu’une altitude « pair » était normalement exigée. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

N3757D, a Boeing 737-832 aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines Inc, was conducting flight DAL1394 from Salt Lake City International Airport (KSLC), US to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While in cruise, the flight crew observed an intermittent stabilizer trim indication which disappeared while consulting the quick reference handbook (QRH). Approximately 20 minutes later, during the initial descent, the indication returned. The flight crew followed the QRH procedure and tested both the electric and manual trim operation which were found inoperative. The flight crew subsequently declared an emergency with air traffic control (ATC) and planned for a flap 15 landing as per the QRH. At approximately 12 000 feet, the flight crew requested the assistance in the flight deck to a Boeing 737 deadheading captain who was sitting in the cabin. The flight crew noted that the aircraft controllability remained normal during descent before the aircraft landed without further incident into CYYZ.

C-GCEV, a De Havilland DHC-7-103 operated by Air Tindi Ltd., was conducting flight TIN801 from Prince Albert Glass Field airport (CYPA), SK. to Saskatoon John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK. When the flight crew selected gear down for the landing in CYXE, they did not receive a gear down and locked indication on the nose gear. TIN801 conducted a missed approach and troubleshot the indication with maintenance and flight operations. The landing light bulbs were replaced with no change to the gear indication. The alternate landing gear extension was completed and a flyby inspection was conducted that indicated the gear appeared to be down. The flight crew completed an uneventful landing with ARFF on standby.The operator's maintenance is investigating the landing gear system.

C-FGOV, a de Havilland DHC-7-103 operated by Air Tindi Ltd., was conducting flight TIN807 from Red Lake Airport (CYRL), ON to Sachigo Lake Airport (CZPB), ON. While en route to CZPB, the flight crew observed a low oil pressure indication on number 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-50). The flight crew made an operational decision to return to CYRL and completed an inflight shutdown of #2 engine. The operator's maintenance is investigating the engine oil system.

C-FULE, an ATR 72-202 operated by Calm Air international, was conducting flight CAV770 from Thompson (CYTH) MB to Island Lake (CYIV) MB. As CAV770 was on final approach for CYIV, the flight crew was communicating with a helicopter on 122.2. The helicopter indicated a liftoff and departure on the east side of town and staying east of the runway center line. The flight crew had the helicopter in sight; however, the flight crew received a TCAS resolution advisory (RA) and flew the recommended climb rate to clear the traffic. C-FULE conducted a second approach and landed safely in CYIV.

C-FDIJ, un Boeing 767-39H exploité par Cargojet Airways Ltd. sous l’indicatif de vol CJT470 venait de décoller aéroport d’Iqaluit (CYFB), NT à destination de l’aéroport international Macdonald-Cartier (CYOW), ON lorsque l’équipage a entendu un bruit sourd suivi d’une perte de puissance sur le moteur droit réduisant de façon significative les performances de monté. Une fois en palier à 15 000 pieds asl, une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil est retourné à CYFB où il s’est posé sans encombre. Le personnel de maintenance a inspecté le moteur droit et confirmé des dommages internes importants. Le moteur sera changé avant de remettre en service.

C-GTWF, a Bell 412 operated by Wisk-Air Limited, was conducting slinging operations from Pipestone Camp, ON (approximately 7 nm northwest of Wiebenville Aerodrome [CXX2], ON) to the Kingfisher Lake, ON area. The helicopter departed with a slung load into a westerly wind of approximately 15-20 knots and turned northeast towards Kingfisher Lake. A mile into the flight, the pilot noticed the helicopter was flying at 40 knots. and the pilot slowed the helicopter to 35 knots. Seconds later the pilot felt a jerk from the load and looked out the bubble window to inspect the load when a second jerk was felt. At this point, the #1 engine decelerated (Pratt & Whitney PT6T-3B) and #2 engine (Pratt & Whitney PT6T-3B) decreased in power. The pilot jettisoned the load 2 miles north of Pipestone Camp and accelerated to one engine inoperative (OEI) speed. The pilot noticed a mine road approximately 1 mile away and turned towards the road. During the turn, the pilot noticed the pedals were stiff and the throttles were jammed. C-GTWF made a radio call to a Bell 407 that was working in the area indicating the intentions of C-GTWF. C-GTWF landed in small vegetation 20 feet short of the road. The pilot shut down the helicopter using the fuel shutoff valves. There were no injuries to the pilot. The ELT did not activate. The operator indicated that there was damage to the belly of the helicopter caused by the cargo hook. Damage to the helicopter is being assessed by the operator's maintenance.

C-GLTO, a Top Aces Inc. Alpha Jet Model A was operating as AMBUSH73 for a local flight at RAF Lakenheath Airport (EGUL), Brandon, United Kingdom. Shortly after takeoff, the pilot noticed smoke in the cockpit as well as a strong odor that would be indicative of an electrical source. The pilot climbed to a safe altitude and declared an emergency. Using the emergency checklist, the pilot was able to clear the cockpit of smoke. The pilot burned off fuel to achieve landing weight and landed safely at EGUL without further incident.Maintenance was unable to recreate the fault. Following consultation between the aircraft certification authority, person responsible for maintenance and the fleet manager, the jet was returned to service and flown without recurrence.

C-FGDX, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA824 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl Airport (CYYZ), ON to Adolfo Suárez Madrid–Barajas Airport (LEMD), Spain. While in cruise flight about 250 nm southwest of St. John’s Intl Airport (CYYT), NL an electrical burning odour was noticed by the flight crew, concurrent with a RECIRC FAN UPPER caution annunciation. The crew declared a PAN PAN with ATS and requested clearance to divert to CYYT. An amended route clearance was issued, and the flight landed at CYYT without incident. Maintenance found that the recirculation fan had a failed bearing and replaced the recirculation fan in accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual.

C-FSDW, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 was conducting flight AC342 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Ottawa/ Macdonald - Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. On departure, the crew observed a "Stab Out of Trim" fail message. After discussion with dispatch and maintenance the decision was made to return to CYVR. The crew declared a PAN PAN for the overweight landing and Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) was placed on standby. The landing was completed without further incident. There were no injuries.Maintenance replaced a stabilizer position sensor and carried out ground checks. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FVTL, a Piper PA31 operated by Exact Air Inc., was conducting a VFR aerial survey flight as flight ET703 from Red Deer (CYQF), AB in an area 105 nm ENE of CYQF with 2 crew on board. While conducting the survey work the left engine (Avco Lycoming TIO-540-A2C) began making intermittent unusual sounds. Soon, oil was seen leaking from the left engine cowling. The pilot conducted the appropriate checklist, shut down and secured the left engine, changed course to Edmonton (CYEG), AB and declared an emergency with ATS. A successful single-engine approach and landing was conducted on Runway 30 at CYEG. The engine will be removed for examination.

A6-EBQ, a Boeing B777-300ER aircraft operated by Emirates, was conducting flight UAE36K from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ to Athens International Airport (LGAV), Greece. While in cruise flight at about 47°34' N, 052°22' W an overspeed warning activated while in smooth air at FL350. A descent to FL 330 was made while troubleshooting was carried out. The airspeed indications were compared and the QRH was consulted. The flight crew consulted with their maintenance control center, and it was decided that airspeed was unreliable and a diversion to Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS), MA would be taken. The flight crew declared PAN PAN and diverted to KBOS to land without further incident. Maintenance inspection determined that a faulty VMO switch caused the unreliable airspeed readings.

C-GEKZ, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight ACA0559 from Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), California to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. On climb, flight crew received a TCAS RA. The RA was followed and the flight continued without further incident.

G-VGBR, an Airbus A330-343 aircraft operated by Virgin Atlantic Airways Ltd., was conducting flight VIR75L from Manchester International Airport (EGCC), England to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL. While in cruise flight at about 42°38' N, 060°44' W the aircraft encountered severe turbulence lasting approximately 5 minutes. During the period of severe turbulence, the aircraft altitude varied +/- 100 feet, rolled +/- 7 degrees with speeds varying +/- 25 knots and vertical G varying between +0.63 G and +1.23 G. The aircraft was at FL400, and the crew declared PAN PAN and requested FL380 where conditions were smooth. The flight continued to destination and landed with no further incident. There were no injuries. The flight data was analyzed, and a special maintenance inspection was carried out before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBHO, an Air Canada Rouge LP A319-114 was operating flight ROU1637 from Orlando International Airport (KMCO), Florida, USA to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC. In the vicinity of Norfolk International Airport (KORF), Virginia, USA during cruise at FL370, the flight crew identified ENG 2 had rolled back un-commanded with an associated slight vibration. There were no associated ECAMs. The engine power was reduced in an attempt to reset however the issue persisted. ENG 2 was reduced to idle for the remainder of the flight and descent was initiated to a lower altitude. A PAN PAN was declared as a precaution. The flight continued to CYUL with Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting on standby. The aircraft was able to taxi under its own power to the gate without further incident.

C-GHQZ, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 operated by Wasaya Airways LP, was conducting flight WSG1640 from Sioux Lookout (CYXL) ON to Big Trout Lake (CYTL) ON. C-FAQR, a Piper PA-31-350 operated by 2080061 Ontario (dba Skycare Air Ambulance), was conducting a flight from Angling Lake/Wapekeka (CKB6), ON. During the decent into CYTL, WSG1640 made a call on 126.7 through FL 200 indicating an ETA for landing on Runway 32 in CYTL. Another aircraft responded to the call on 126.7 indicating that WSG1640 would be number 2 for the landing in CYTL. When WSG1640 was below FL 180, the flight crew made numerous calls on 135.15, 123.2 and again on 126.7 indicating position, altitude and time for the 10 mile fix (OTREV) for Runway 32 at CYTL. The other aircraft then indicated that they were 7 min ahead of WSG1640 and that they were commencing the approach for Runway 32. At approximately 5 nm from OTREV, the flight crew of WSG1640 noticed the TCAS indicated 2 targets on final for Runway 32. Shortly thereafter, WSG1640 heard C-FAQR call off CKB6 Runway 30 and that they were climbing to 10 000 feet on their way to Sioux Lookout (CYXL) ON. The WSG1640 flight crew made 2 calls on 123.2 and 126.7 to alert C-FAQR of their position. As WSG1640 approached OTREV, the flight crew received a yellow target TCAS advisory and decided to stop the descent until past the traffic. The TCAS issued a traffic advisory, followed by an resolution advisory (RA) with a climb command. The TCAS indicated that C-FAQR was 900 ft. below and climbing. During the WSG1640’s manoeuvre to comply with the RA, both engines were inadvertently over-torqued. WSG1640's crew subsequently tried again to contact C-FAQR, but there was no response. WGS1640 landed safely in CYTL.The operator's maintenance was dispatched to perform inspections as per the manufacturer's maintenance manual.

C-GKNR, a Sikorsky S-92 helicopter operated by Cougar Helicopters, was conducting flight CGR31 from St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL to the Hibernia offshore platform (HIB). On descent, the crew made a call on 126.7 MHz and received a call from a PAL Aerospace aircraft stating that they were 7NM to the NW of HIB at 1,500 feet and leaving the area. At about 4,000 feet, C-GKNR received a TCAS RA. The crew stopped the descent and started a turn away from the traffic. They spotted the other aircraft climbing out of a cloud layer which was below them. The aircraft passed in opposite directions by approximately 0.5 NM at an altitude of 4,500 feet. No other communication from the PAL Aerospace was received by C-GKNR.

C-FZHI, un Cessna 170 d’exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue de l'aéroport de Sorel, QC (CSY3) à destination de l'aéroport de Sainte-Hyacinthe, QC (CSU3) avec seul le pilote à bord. Lors de l’approche finale de CSU3, l’aéronef s’est écrasé dans un champ situé à .35 NM du seuil de la piste 20. La radiobalise d'urgence de l'aéronef a été déclanchée. Le pilote a été grièvement blessé et l'aéronef a été détruit. Il n’y a pas eu d’incendie.

C-GXTB, a Pilatus PC-12 Aircraft operated by North Star Air Ltd. was conducting an IFR flight from Keewaywin Airport (CPV8), ON to Round Lake Airport (CZRJ), ON. During the landing on Runway 03 at CZRJ, the aircraft bounced and landed hard on the nose gear. A visual inspection by the pilots of the main wheels and nosewheel indicated that all appeared normal without damage. The aircraft was flown to Thunder Bay Intl. Airport (CYQT) ON and after further inspection, it was noticed that the landing gear and all four blades of the propeller were damaged. The operator's maintenance performed a hard landing inspection along with replacing the engine, propeller and numerous landing gear components.

C-FNSV, a North Cariboo Air Beech 1900D was operating as NCB4094 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to Primrose Aerodrome (CFN6), AB. After departure from CYEG, approximately 31 NM NE, as NCB4094 was approaching the top of climb at 19 000 feet ASL the flight crew observed the CABIN ALT HIGH warning light illuminate. The cabin altitude was noted to be above 10 000 feet. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist and were cleared to descend to 8 000 feet ASL. An emergency descent was performed. The crew did not declare an emergency as the issue self-rectified once the aircraft leveled off at 8 000 feet ASL. The aircraft returned to CYEG where the aircraft landed without further issue. There were no injuries. At the time of the occurrence, one of the bleed air valves were deferred under MEL authorization. Troubleshooting of the pressurization system is ongoing. The company will advise TSB of maintenance findings and follow-up.

C-GPNV, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines, was operating as PVL412 from St. John’s Intl Airport (CYYT), NL to Gander Intl Airport (CYQX), NL. When on the approach for CYQX, the flight crew selected the flaps however they would not extend. The flight crew consulted the QRH and couldn’t resolve the flap issue. The flight crew declared an emergency and coordinated with ATS to return to CYYT where the aircraft carried out a flapless landing on runway 28 without further incident. Maintenance personnel replaced the faulty flap control module.

C-GBHZ, an Airbus A319 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1941 from Toronto/Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Fort McMurray International Airport (CYMM), AB. While climbing through FL230, the cabin crew notified the flight crew of an abnormal odour in the aft cabin. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist and the odour did not dissipate. They decided to return to CYYZ, declared PAN PAN, and made an uneventful overweight landing with aircraft rescue and fire fighting standing by.

C-GYUA, a Mitsubishi Aircraft Intl. Inc. MU-2B-60 operated by Thunder Airlines Limited, was conducting flight THU890 from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON to Wawa Aerodrome (CYXZ), ON, with 2 crew and one medic on board. During landing on Runway 03, which was snow covered, the aircraft departed the right side of runway and slid down into the drainage area beside the runway. The aircraft was substantially damaged. There were no reported injuries.

C-GGOR, a privately registered Piper PA-28-180, was conducting a flight from Vanderhoof Aerodrome (CAU4), BC, to Invermere Aerodrome (CAA8), BC, under visual flight rules with one pilot on board. It was determined that at approximately 1555 PST, the aircraft was in a nose-down attitude, approaching the ground at high speed. The aircraft reportedly raised its nose abruptly to a level attitude, then rolled to the right as the nose dropped. The aircraft then collided with terrain. The pilot was fatally injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The Canadian Mission Control Centre did not receive a signal from the aircraft’s emergency locator transmitter.Canadian Armed Forces Search and Rescue aircraft deployed to the area but were unable to locate the site. The crash site was found by Columbia Valley Search and Rescue and was also attended by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police. There was no post-crash fire.

C-FKIW, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-700 airplane was operating as flight WJA456 from Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. The aircraft was parked with the doors closed and was set for departure. The aircraft was being sprayed to remove frost prior to departing. The de-ice truck had completed spraying on the left side of the aircraft and was moving to spray the right horizontal stabilizer.  When the truck drove in toward the aircraft, aft of the right wing, the de-icing bucket struck and punctured the right winglet. The vehicle came to a halt. The operator in the de-icing bucket received minor injuries. WestJet maintenance replaced the right winglet and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FENU, a WestJet Encore de Havilland DHC-8-400, was operating as WEN3433 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC. While on the takeoff roll on Runway 35L, during the “Power Set” call the flight crew heard a single chime. The captain observed the “OUTBD ANTISKID” caution light, rejected the takeoff at approximately 80 knots and took control. The first officer declared MAYDAY. During the rejected takeoff, when the power levers were brought to disc, the caution light extinguished. Upon coming to a stop on the runway, the flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and verified that the ANTISKID switch was set to on. As there were no further applicable checklists to run, the flight crew advised ATC that the aircraft would return to the gate. There were no injuries. The company will advise TSB of maintenance findings and follow-up.

F-HTYO, an Airbus 350-941 aircraft operated by Air France, was conducting flight AFR694M, from Paris / Charles de Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France, to Houston / George Bush Intercontinental Airport (KIAH), TX. At flight at about 46°55' N, 051°04' W (80 nm SE CYYT) the flight crew received an electrical DC voltage system fault message accompanied by multiple other system fault messages. The flight crew consulted with their company maintenance control center and a decision to divert to New York / John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), NY was taken. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and diverted to and landed the aircraft at KJFK without further incident as aircraft rescue and fire fighting stood by as a precaution. Maintenance tests were conducted, and a faulty emergency electrical network management unit was replaced.

C-GUBD, an Air Transat A330-243 was operating flight TSC186 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), Dominican Republic. A flight crew member became incapacitated approximately 3 hours into the flight. A company qualified pilot who was flying as a passenger replaced the incapacitated flight crew member and the aircraft continued to the intended destination without further incident.

C-FGZI, a Top Aces Inc. Mcdonnell Douglas A-4N was operating a local flight as Skyhawk1 and departed Cuxhaven/Nordholz Airport (ETMN), Wurster Nordseeküste, Germany. After climbing to FL260, the pilot observed the cabin altimeter rise past approximately 20 000 feet and a rushing sound was heard. A request was made to ATC for an immediate descent to 10 000 feet which was authorized and the pilot declared an emergency. The aircraft returned to ETMN and entered a holding pattern to achieve landing weight. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FLBG, a Flair Airlines Boeing 737-8 was operating as FLE1600 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), Florida. While descending on the CUUDA2 arrival, the aircraft received clearance to descend to FL230. A King Air was cleared to FL220. B737-8 received a "Level Off" RA at FL233 and the level off was actioned. B737-8 informed ATC of the level off at FL233 and continued to descend once clear of conflict.

C-GMZN, an Air Canada A220 was operating as flight ACA1039 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Denver International Airport (KDEN), Colorado. On approach, the aircraft received a TCAS RA from a fast-climbing aircraft departing from KDEN. The RA was followed and C-GMZN landed without further incident.

C-GVDP, an Air Canada A220 was operating as flight AC1073 from Montréal / Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Denver International Airport (KDEN), Colorado. On approach, the aircraft received a TCAS RA. The RA was followed, and the aircraft continued with a missed approach. The landing was uneventful.

C-GSNR, a Beech B200 operated by SkyNorth Air Ltd., was conducting an IFR flight as SN852 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. to Thompson Regional Airport (CYTH), MB.  While enroute at FL260, the flight crew started to smell a strong burning odor. The flight crew declared an emergency with an immediate return to CYWG. The aircraft landed at CYWG and was escorted by fire/rescue to the apron.The operator's maintenance replaced a faulty bleed air bypass valve.

C-GEOW, a Pilatus PC-12/45 aircraft operated by North Star Air Ltd., was conducting a flight from Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON to Kasabonika Airport (CYAQ), ON. During the landing on Runway 03, the aircraft experienced a runway excursion when it overran the end of the runway. The aircraft came to rest approximately 350 feet past the departure end of the runway and the aircraft was substantially damaged. The pilots and passengers were uninjured. The ELT activated.

C-GBIA, an Air Canada Airbus A319-114, was conducting flight ACA235 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, under instrument flight rules with 5 crew members and 114 passengers on board. Approximately 138 nautical miles northeast of CYVR, the aircraft experienced a loss of pressurization. An emergency descent was conducted to an altitude of 10 000 feet, and the crew declared a MAYDAY. The aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident. There were no injuries to passengers or crewmembers. There was no damage to the aircraft. After being inspected by emergency services, the aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.Company maintenance inspected the aircraft and replaced the ram air outlet actuator for the number 1 air conditioning pack. The aircraft was returned to service.

RP-C3508, an Airbus A350-900 operated by Philippine Airlines, was conducting flight PAL126 from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (RPLL), Manila, Philippines to John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), New York, USA. Approximately 127 nm NW Whitehorse International Airport (CYXY), Yukon while cruising at 38 000 feet, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence and requested a descent to 37 000 feet. ATS granted the request, the aircraft descended, and the flight continued to the intended destination.

C-GBHO, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating ROU1735 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), California. In the vicinity of Grand Canyon, Arizona, a cabin crew member became ill and their duties were redistributed. The flight continued uneventfully.

C-GVJZ, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA7705 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. After retracting the landing gear, the flight crew received a caution message "LANDING GEAR INOP". The flight crew declared an emergency and stated their intentions to return to CYOW. After the landing gear was extended using the alternate gear extension procedure, the flight landed uneventfully. Maintenance inspection found that there was an issue with the nose landing gear lock wiring harness, which was replaced before the aircraft returned to service.

C-GAAJ, a CargoJet Airways B767-323 was operating flight CJT926 from Bogota El Dorado International Airport (SKBO), Colombia to Miami International Airport (KMIA), Florida. During the initial climb, after conducting a "PACKS-OFF" takeoff at SKBO, a CABIN ALTITUDE EICAS warning was received. The cabin altitude climbed to 12,000 feet. The cabin was still uncontrolled after conducting the quick reference handbook checklist therefore, the crew requested a clearance to descend to 10,000 feet with a radar heading. While descending, the crew received a TCAS traffic alert, and ATC provided a revised heading. While flying the revised heading, the crew received a TERRAIN caution alert and the crew took corrective action. After that, ATC notified them that they would need to climb to clear the low level airspace or land back at Bogota as they did not have a safe zone to give them a HOLD at those altitudes, due to departure and arrival traffic. Therefore, the crew elected to land back at SKBO slightly overweight. On final runway 14L, as the cabin altitude became under control, the PAN PAN was cancelled. The aircraft taxied back to the gate for maintenance assessment. No malfunction was found and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FWSE, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight WJA1565 from San Diego International Airport (KSAN), California, USA to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. On approach into CYYC, the flight crew attempted to extend the flaps, but the trailing edge flaps did not appear to move. The flight crew aborted the approach and requested vectors from ATC in order to action the appropriate checklist. In the process of performing the checklist, the crew observed movement of the trailing edge flaps. The aircraft was set-up for another approach, at which point the flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC. An uneventful landing was conducted in CYYC with airport rescue and firefighting on standby and the aircraft taxied to the gate.Maintenance inspected aircraft and noticed the trailing edge flaps were extended 25 degrees. Aircraft was removed from service for inspection.

C-GWJK, a WestJet Encore DHC8-402, was conducting flight WEN3242 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Brandon Municipal Airport (CYBR), MB. During the initial take-off run at CYYC, the flight crew received a baggage door warning indication. The take-off was aborted, and a MAYDAY call was made with ATS. The aircraft returned to the gate where company maintenance determined that baggage door handle had been secured incorrectly. The door handle was inspected, stowed correctly, and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FNEN, a WestJet Encore DHC-8-402 was conducting flight WEN3120 from Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. On approach to CYEG, the left main landing gear down and locked indicator did not illuminate when the flight crew selected the landing gear down. A missed approach was conducted, and the flight crew actioned the appropriate quick reference handbook procedure. Upon completing the alternate gear extension procedure, the left main landing gear down and locked light still did not illuminate. The flight crew subsequently performed the landing gear indicator malfunction procedure and verified that they did have three landing gear down and locked indications. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC as a precaution, and on second approach landed without incident. Company maintenance personnel replaced an unserviceable bulb in the landing indication panel.

C-GXNL, a DeHavilland DHC8-402 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines, was conducting flight PVL2258 from Halifax/ Stanfield International (CYHZ), NS to St. John’s International (CYYT), NL. The crew had been instructed to fly heading 100° after departure off of Runway 05. C-FLFT, a Sikorsky S-76C helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters Ltd, was conducting a VFR medevac flight from Truro (Colchester Health Centre) Heliport (CEH9), NS to Halifax (South End) Heliport (CHS7), NS and was transitioning through the CYHZ control zone at 2500 feet ASL. C-FLFT was advised of the traffic on departure and acknowledged having them in sight. C-GXNL turned to the assigned heading and was climbing when they received a TCAS RA. The range between the two aircraft decreased to 0.1 miles laterally and 600 feet vertically. NAV CANADA is conducting a safety investigation into the occurrence.

C-GYCV, a DeHavilland DHC8-314 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines Ltd., was conducting flight PVL923 from Moncton/Greater Moncton Roméo Leblanc Intl (CYQM), NB to Mont-Joli Airport (CYYY) QC. During the flight a cabin crew member experienced a medical issue and was unable to continue performing their duties. The flight crew was made aware of the situation and the decision to return to CYQM was made. No emergency was declared. The flight landed in CYQM without further incident.

C-FLUT, a Flair Airlines Boeing 737 Max 8 was conducting flight FLE801 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC with 6 crew members and 168 passengers on board. After departure from the terminal gate and taxiing for the departure runway, one of the cabin crew members became ill and was unable to perform their duties. The flight crew elected to return to the gate and seek medical attention for the affected cabin crew member. The flight subsequently departed after a delay.

The WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-400, C-GDEN, was operating as WEN3135 on a flight from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. During landing gear retraction after take-off, a nose gear door malfunctioned, and the flight crew observed a landing gear INOP caution light. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook checklist and manually extended the nose landing gear. All landing gear indicated down and locked. The aircraft returned to CYYC, and the flight crew requested the airport rescue and firefighting units to attend the landing. The landing was uneventful, and the aircraft stopped on the taxiway for inspection before taxiing to the gate. No leaks were found during inspection.Maintenance update: Maintenance crews replaced the wiring harness for the nose gear door actuator. Functional checks were carried out and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOIW, an Air Transat A321-271 aircraft was operating flight TSC123 from London Gatwick Airport (EGKK), United Kingdom to Toronto Pearson Intl Airport (CYYZ), ON. While in cruise at flight level 320, the aircraft entered an area of severe clear air turbulence causing the aircraft to climb 280 feet and descend 2200 feet before stabilizing. The flight continued to destination uneventfully and no injuries were reported. Post severe turbulence maintenance inspection was carried out.

C-FSIQ, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating flight ACA0598 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to John Wayne/Orange County Airport (KSNA), California. On arrival into KSNA at 5000ft, the flight crew received a TCAS RA with VFR traffic. Traffic cleared and flight continued to land without further incident.

C-GFAJ, an Air Canada A330 was operating flight ACA0875 from Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During taxi for departure the aircraft taxied off the taxiway while making a left turn. The left gear was stuck in the mud and was unable to move. Passengers deplaned safely and the aircraft was removed using a crane.Inspections of the main landing gear were carrier out by maintenance in accordance with the AMM. Main landing gear wheels replaced and ops checks of the braking system performed with no faults found.

C-FYIY, an Air Canada Rouge A319 was operating flight ACA1104 from Nashville International Airport (KBNA), Tennessee to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During take-off, the flight crew received a TCAS RA for traffic at 1500 feet. The crew followed the RA and the flight continued without further incident.

C-GKQQ, an Embraer E190-400, operating as Porter Airlines flight POE157, arrived at Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON and taxied to gate 20. Upon engine shutdown the ground crew advised the flight crew of an engine #2 tailpipe fire. The flight crew actioned the "Tailpipe Fire" quick reference handbook checklist, and dry motored the engine. The flight crew contacted ATC to request emergency vehicle support as a precaution. Aircraft rescue and fire fighting confirmed with the flight crew that the fire was extinguished. The bridge was then connected, and passengers disembarked normally. Porter Maintenance personnel conducted an engine run, which revealed oil leaking from bearings #5 and #6. The affected engine was removed and replaced.

C-GIZX, un Beech A100 exploité par Propair Inc, sous l’indicatif PRO100T, effectuait un vol d’entraînement depuis l’aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda (CYUY), QC vers l'aéroport de Val-d'Or (CYVO), QC. Après avoir décollé de CYUY, l’aéronef s’est dirigé vers CYVO et a effectué un premier arrêt-décollé sur la piste 18. Après le décollage, l’équipage a effectué un virage par la gauche pour exécuter l’arc DME de l’approche ILS piste 18. Lors de l'approche, le train d’atterrissage a été abaissé et l’illumination des 3 lumières vertes indiquant que les trains d’atterrissage étaient sortis et verrouillés avant le posé a été confirmée. Quelques secondes après le posé des roues, l’aéronef s’est affaissé du côté droit et du côté gauche par la suite. L'aéronef a dérapé et est sorti de piste pour s’immobiliser dans la neige à environ 50 pieds du bord de piste du côté est. Les 2 pilotes ont pu évacuer l’aéronef sans difficulté et n'ont pas été blessés. Aucun incendie ne s’est déclaré mais l'aéronef a subi des dommages importants. L'examen des trains d'atterrissage n’a révélé aucune anomalie et a permis de constater que le système de verrouillage du train d'atterrissage était en position déverrouillé et que la rétraction des trains était amorcée lorsque l'affaissement s'est produit.

C-FLDX, a Flair Airlines B737-8 was operating flight FLE1300 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), Florida, USA. 25 minutes prior to top of descent, the Master Caution light illuminated at FL400 and the autopilot disconnected. Number 2 IRS Fault was identified. The IRS FAULT non normal checklist was completed. A PAN PAN was declared, and a request was made to exit reduced vertical separation minimum airspace. The aircraft was cleared to and descended to FL280. The manual approach was flown to KFLL without further incident.

C-GLQC, a Porter Airlines Inc. DHC 8-400 was operating flight POE2345 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON to Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS), USA. While taxiing to the terminal following landing, the aircraft struck a runway guard light with the right main landing gear. No injuries were reported and there was no damage to the aircraft.
