C-GGBZ, a Canwest Corporate Air Charters Ltd. Cessna U206G, was departing Fort Vermilion Aerodrome (CEZ4), AB on a flight to Fox Lake Aerodrome (CEC3), AB. At approximately 200 feet above ground level (AGL), the engine lost power (Teledyne Continental Motors IO-520F). The pilot, realizing that a return to the airport was not possible landed in a farmer's field. There was no damage to the aircraft, there was no fire, and the ELT did not activate. Maintenance update: A fuel leak was found at the B nut where the fuel line attaches to the fuel distribution block for the fuel injection system. Further inspection found an anomaly in the B nut assembly that allowed installation torque to be reached when the assembly was not fully seated, leading over time, to a fuel leak large enough that full power on the engine could not be attained. A new fuel line was installed, run-up checks completed, and the aircraft was returned to service. Modifications to the maintenance quality control process are being considered.

C-GKQD, a Dehavilland DHC-8-402 operated by Porter Airlines Inc., was conducting flight POE2463 from Toronto / Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Montréal / Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, with 4 crew and 66 passengers on board. After receiving a report from ATC about moderate turbulence ahead on their route, the flight crew began an early descent from their cruise altitude of FL250 and suspended in-flight beverage service. While descending through FL215, they encountered severe turbulence, which caused the autopilot to disengage and resulted in momentary difficulty controlling the aircraft. The encounter lasted for approximately two seconds, after which the pilot flying took control and re-engaged the autopilot. The flight continued uneventfully to the intended destination, and there were no reported injuries. A maintenance inspection for severe turbulence was carried out and no faults were found, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FIUV, a Boeing 777-333ER, operating as Air Canada flight ACA2, was landing at Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON and encountered wind shear just prior to touch down during gusty wind conditions. A hard landing ensued, the aircraft rolled out normally and taxied to the terminal. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft.

C-FSCY, a Boeing 737-8, operated by Air Canada as flight ACA2350, was on a post maintenance positioning flight from the Windsor Airport (CYQG), ON to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the climb out of CYQG the number 2 engine hydraulic EDP light illuminated, the flight crew carried out the checklist and the light extinguished. While in cruise a number 2 engine oil bypass message was received, the flight crew carried out the checklist and carried a precautionary shutdown of the engine. A PAN-PAN was declared and the flight crew was given priority handling and landed without further incident. Emergency vehicles were on standby for the landing.

C-GCFR, un Dehavilland DHC-7-100 exploité par Transports Canada sous l'indicatif TGO922, effectuait un vol de reconnaissance local selon les règles combinées de vol aux instruments et de vol à vue au départ de l'aéroport de Moncton/Greater Moncton Roméo LeBlanc International, NB (CYQM). Alors que l'aéronef se trouvait à environ 17 milles nautiques (NM) au sud-sud-ouest de l’aéroport de Sept-Îles, Québec (CYZV), l'équipage a remarqué que l'indication de pression d'huile du moteur numéro 2 était en baisse. L'équipage a pris la décision de fermer le moteur par mesure de précaution. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) et revenu à CYQM où il s'est posé sans encombre. Il a été estimé que 5 pintes d’huiles ont été perdues. Le département de la maintenance a découvert une fuite du joint de transducteur de pression d'huile.

C-GGDU, un DeHaviland Dash-8 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7988 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC à destination de l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV). Sélectionnant les volets à 5 degrés lors de l'approche à CYZV, l'équipage a eu une alerte de mauvais fonctionnement des volets. Les volets étant bloqués à 3 degrés, les pilotes ont effectué une remontée. Après avoir calculé la distance de piste, ils ont opté pour changer de destination et se diriger sur l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) où l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé. Le personnel de maintenance a effectué l'ajustement de l'indicateur de la position des volets à gauche.

N758AN, un Boeing 777-200 exploité par American Airlines sous l'indicatif AAL717, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Munich (EDDM), Allemagne à destination l'aéroport de Charlotte Douglas International (KCLT), NC. À environ 35 miles nautiques à l'est-sud-est de l'aéroport de Bagotville (CYBG), Québec, une indication d'un problème avec le système d'huile du moteur gauche est apparue dans le poste de pilotage. Une urgence a été déclarée et le vol a été dérouté vers l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Québec (CYUL). Les services d'urgence ont été déployés et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé. Une demande afin d'obtenir des détails supplémentaires a été soumise à l'exploitant.

D-ABUC, a Boeing 767-330ER operated by Condor, was conducting flight CFG2198 from Rhein-Main Frankfurt (EDDF), Germany to Juan Gualberto Gomez Intl - Varadero (MUVR), Cuba. During cruise, the crew had difficulty in controlling the aircraft due to severe turbulence, with deviations +/- 600 feet and roll up to 30 degrees. The crew requested an altitude block, however when they did not receive a response from ATC, they declared a PAN PAN and followed the NAT contingency procedure. The crew then received a clearance to climb to FL340. The turbulence decreased, and eventually became light. The PAN PAN was cancelled and the aircraft continued to destination without further incident. Two passengers received minor injuries, they did not require medical assistance. The crew was aware, through weather charts and ACARS information, that the possibility of turbulence existed.

C-FGYD, a Top Aces Inc. McDonnell Douglas A-4N was operating a flight from Phoenix-Mesa Gateway Airport (KIWA), AZ, to Falcon Field Airport (KFFZ), AZ. The pilot elected to return back to KIWA, as an airspeed indicator anomaly was observed. Upon landing at KIWA, the pilot commenced braking, following which, the pilot suspected that the left tire was damaged and released the brakes. The pilot continued the landing rollout maintaining directional control, and at the subsequent application of the brakes, the pilot noticed that there was no perceptible braking action available to stop the aircraft. The pilot informed the Tower that the aircraft had a blown tire and exited the runway onto Taxiway Golf. The aircraft was stopped prior to the hold short line for the parallel runway. Emergency services were requested as the left-hand brake assembly was smoldering. Aircraft was towed back to the hangar without further incident.

C-FJOU, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1707 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), NV. During the descent phase of flight, while flying the RKSTR 3 RNAV arrival into KLAS in accordance with ATC clearance, ROU1707 was descending to 8000ft ASL. As the flight descended through 11000ft ASL, approximately 3.9NM NW of RKSTR flight crew received TCAS RA: CLIMB. At the same time, ATC issued clearance to stop descent at 11000ft however, aircraft was already below the altitude to initiate climb in accordance with RA instruction. The flight crew reported that the observed minimum vertical separation was reduced to approximately 500ft during the occurrence. The conflict was subsequently resolved, and the flight was completed without further incident.

C-FGXR, un Beechcraft KingAir 200 exploité par Air Nunavut en tant que vol BFF203 entre Nuuk airport (BGGH) Groenland et Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) était en vol de croisière lorsque l'équipage a observé une baisse anormale du niveau de carburant. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil a pu complété son vol pour atterrissage sans encombres à CYFB. Le personnel de maintenance a déterminé que la fuite était causée par un bouchon de drainage qui s'est séparé du moteur en vol.

C-GYKN, un Bombardier CL-60-2B16 exploité par Starlink Aviation sous l'indicatif de vol TLK622 venait de décoller de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de Newark, NJ (KEWR) losque l'équipage de conduite a constaté que le train d'atterrissage ne rétractait pas. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil est revenue se poser sans encombres à CYUL.

C-FMHR, a Mark Anthony Group Inc. Pilatus PC-24 departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, for an instrument flight rules flight to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC. After passing FL240 while in the climb at 280 KIAS to the selected cruise altitude of FL270, the flight crew felt a brief shudder followed by a loud bang. The aircraft yawed to the right, nosed down and began to accelerate. The pilot-in-command retarded both engine thrust levers, applied left rudder pedal, and requested the second-in-command to apply nose left rudder trim in an attempt to correct the sudden yaw. Attempts to control the yaw with rudder trim were unsuccessful. Aircraft control was passed to the second-in-command. Directional control was achieved by reducing airspeed and applying differential engine thrust while both pilots applied pressure on the left rudder pedal. The flight crew advised Vancouver Center of the flight control difficulty, declared an emergency and requested that airport emergency services stand by for the landing at CYLW, where the aircraft landed without further incident at 2139 PDT. Neither pilots, nor the passenger were injured. Company maintenance conducted an initial inspection and found that the rudder mass balance weight arm had broken off and became lodged in a position that prevented full movement of the rudder. Further inspection found that the rudder trim tab control rods had become separated aft of the rudder trim actuator.

C-FHCM, a WestJet Airlines B737 MAX was operating flight WJA2152 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Licenciado Gustavo Diaz Ordaz International Airport (MMPR), Mexico. In the vicinity of the Grand Canyon National Park, Nevada, a cabin crew member became ill.. The cabin crew member was unable to perform their assigned duties and was not in their assigned jumpseat for landing. These duties were reassigned to the remaining cabin crew members.

N879UA, an Airbus A319-132 operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UA1684 from George Bush International Airport (KIAH), USA to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While on descent to CYYZ below 10000 feet, the flight crew reported indications of the loss of both packs and an auxiliary power unit (APU) bleed air leak. The cabin continued to hold the pressurization during the remainder of the descent. The flight crew declared an emergency with air traffic control (ATC) and subsequently landed the aircraft into CYYZ without further incident. The cabin oxygen masks did not deploy during the occurrence. The maintenance department performed a reset of both aircraft bleed monitoring computers (BMC) as per the aircraft maintenance manual and the APU bleed air and pack systems operated normally.

N416AW, un CL 600-2B19 exploité par Air Wisconsin sous l’indicatif de vol AWI6147 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Montréal/ Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l’aéroport international de Philadelphie (KPHL), PA. L’appareil venait de décoller de CYUL lorsque l'équipage a observé une indication d'alarme du système de dégivrage. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil est revenu se poser sans encombre à CYUL.

C-GXCD, a Kammer Ag Services, Thrush Aircraft S2R-H80 was operating a flight from Four Corners Regional Airport (KFMN), New Mexico towards Hector International Airport (KFAR), North Dakota. In the vicinity of Cherry, Arizona, an emergency was declared due to an alternator failure and loss of radio communications. The pilot of the aircraft elected to return to KFMN. The aircraft landed safely and taxied to its parking location without any further incident.

C-GJJF un Beech A100 King Air exploité par Propair sous l'indicatif de vol PRO4215 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda QC (CYUY) à destination de l'aéroport de Wemindji, QC (CYNC) pour un vol d'évacuation médicale avec 2 pilotes et 3 passagers à bord. L'appareil s'est posé légèrement décalé sur le côté gauche du centre de la piste. Le moteur gauche a alors frappé un banc de neige qui était présent sur la longueur de la surface de piste. L'appareil a dévié de sa trajectoire en dérapant et est sorti du côté gauche de la piste pour s'arrêter dans la neige à environ 8 mètres du bord de piste. Un passager a été légèrement blessé mais pouvait se déplacer sans aide. Une inspection sommaire de l'appareil a révélé des dommages aux hélices et aux volets.

N28912, a Boeing 787-8, operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UA946 from Washington Dulles International Airport (KIAD) Washington DC, USA to Amsterdam Schiphol Airport (EHAM) NL. While enroute, over the North Atlantic within Gander airspace, the flight crew received a low oil quantity EICAS message for the left engine. After consulting with maintenance control, a decision was made to divert to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, USA. During the diversion to KEWR, the left oil quantity continued to decrease. The flight crew made the decision to divert to Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, and declared a PAN PAN with Moncton ACC. The aircraft landed safely at 08:20 utc.Upon aircraft inspection, maintenance technicians found the oil cap on the left engine unsecured. The cap was re-secured, oil was cleaned from the cowl area and the engine was serviced. A leak check was performed on the engine and no defects were noted. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GMOB, a Piper PA-31-350 operated by Eagle Air Enterprises Limited, was conducting a VFR flight from Sachigo Lake Airport (CZPB), ON. to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. with one pilot and six passengers. When the aircraft was enroute and approximately 25 minutes north of CYWG, a fuel level concern was identified, and a decision was made to divert to Winnipeg/St. Andrews Airport (CYAV), MB. During the diversion to CYAV, the left engine ran out of fuel. ATC was notified and, at approximately 5.5 nm north of CYAV, the right engine started to sputter. The pilot conducted a landing on a gravel road. There were no injuries to the passengers and no damage to the aircraft. RCMP, the local fire department and EMS attended to the scene.

C-GVUO, an Air Canada Airbus 220-300 was operating flight AC431 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the flight, the flight crew received a "Brakes On" message. In discussion with maintenance, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN. As the flight crew selected Flaps 5, the "Brakes On" message disappeared. The aircraft landed without further incident and was inspected by ARFF; afterwards it taxied to the gate without further incident.

C-GLQP, a DHC-8-402, operating as Porter Airlines flight POE 2541, departed the Toronto Billy Bishop Airport (CYTZ), ON,  destined for the Sudbury Airport (CYSB), ON. While on final approach, a cabin crew member notified the flight crew of a loud bang, followed by the sound of leaking air. The flight crew observed the pressurization was fluctuating and elected to declare a PAN PAN. After touchdown, the flight crew stopped the aircraft on the runway and an external inspection was conducted by ARFF. The aircraft proceed to the gate under its own power and maintenance was notified. A post-flight maintenance inspection revealed a tear in the aft baggage door seal.

C-GMCP, a Starlink Aviation Learjet 45 was operating flight TLK833 from L.F. Wade International Airport (TXKF), Bermuda to Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS), Massachusetts. Upon landing in KBOS, the flight crew declared an emergency due to overheating brakes. The aircraft was towed to the ramp without further incident.

C-FHCW, a Learjet 45 operated by Les Investissements Nolinor Inc, was conducting flight NRL43 from Montréal International (Mirabel) Airport (CYMX), QC to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON with only 2 pilots onboard. While on approach into CYHM with the landing gear extended, the crew received a red ''NORM BRK FAIL CAS'' message accompanied by a red master warning indication. The flight crew declared a Pan Pan and initiated a go-around. The flight crew subsequently followed the quick reference handbook (QRH) and elected to return to CYMX where the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FIOJ, a Swearingen SA227-AC (Metroliner) operated by SkyCare Air Ambulance, was conducting flight PHX-594 from Kitchener / Waterloo Airport (CYKF), ON to Ottawa / Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. While on route to CYOW, the crew received an intermittent illumination of the R/H Engine Chip detector annunciator. The crew subsequently elected to return to CYKF where the R/H engine flamed out on approach. The crew declared emergency, secured the engine and landed into CYKF runway 26 without further incident. The company maintenance department is investigating.

C-FYNI, un hélicoptère Robinson R44 exploité par Richcopter Inc. effectuait un vol d’entraînement depuis l’aéroport de Gatineau, QC (CYND) avec seul un élève pilote à bord. Au décollage une perte de maîtrise est survenue, l’hélicoptère a fait 2 rotations de 360 degrés et la queue a percuté le sol. L’élève-pilote a repris la maîtrise de l’hélicoptère et a réussi à effectuer un atterrissage. L’appareil a subi des dommages importants, mais le pilote n’a subi aucune blessure.

C-FGZT, a Top Aces Inc. A-4N was returning to base from D323 airspace to RAF Lakenheath Airport (EGUL), UK when the aircraft lost all communications. The pilot selected Mode 3 squawk to 7600 and set ADS-B callsign to "NORDO". The pilot gradually descended for the ILS Y RNY 24 approach as per EGUL local NORDO procedures. The aircraft landed without further incident. Wing Operations declared an emergency on behalf of the pilot due to lost communications.Maintenance discovered a failure with the pilot's helmet communications wire/connector.

C-FXRJ, an Avro RJ100 operated by Summit Air, was conducting flight SUT8042 from Diavik (CDK2), NWT to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with 4 crew members and 59 passengers on board. Shortly after departure from CDK2, the flight crew observed an airspeed comparator indication. The crew declared PAN PAN as a precaution. The crew subsequently completed the QRH checklist and switched the Air Data Computer (ADC) from NORM to BOTH 1; the system was restored, and the PAN PAN cancelled. The flight landed in CYZF without further incident.

C-GKQB, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 operated by Porter Airlines Inc., was conducting flight POE2461 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During the initial climb, the flight crew noticed a lag of 0.6 PSI in differential cabin pressure; the climb was continued. Upon actioning the 10 000 feet checks, the differential cabin pressure was still noted a bit lower than normal, lagging by approximately 0.4 to 0.6 PSI. The flight crew subsequently noted that the rate controller was locked at 250 Feet Per Minute (FPM) instead of 500 FPM in normal condition and elected to continue the climb to FL250. Shortly after level off, the Cabin Press warning light came on with a differential cabin pressure indication of 4.8 PSI and the cabin altitude at approximately 11 000 feet. The flight crew subsequently donned oxygen, declared Mayday and initiated an emergency descent to 10 000 feet. The quick reference handbook (QRH) checklist was actioned. After leveling at 10 000 feet, the crew continued an unpressurized descent for an Instrument Landing System (ILS) landing into CYUL runway 06R where the aircraft landed without further incident. The maintenance crew were unable to replicate the fault, the pack flow control and shutoff valve were replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FLSX, un DH8A exploité par Air Creebec sous l’indicatif CRQ238, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Chisasibi, QC (CSU2) à destination de Val-d’Or, QC (CYVO) avec 28 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’avion était en étape d’approche finale de l’approche RNAV (GNSS) PISTE 18, une alerte TAWS est survenue. L’équipage a effectué une remise des gaz, a fait une deuxième approche et l’avion s’est posé sur la piste 18 sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FJZS, an Air Canada B777-300 operating flight ACA892 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Leonardo da Vinci–Fiumicino Airport (LIRF), Italy. On arrival, the ramp crew advised the flight crew via intercom that the left main gear brake was smoking. An extinguisher was used to discharge the fire. No indication of hot brakes reported by flight crew. ARFF wasn’t called to the scene. Local maintenance carried out an inspection of the gear.The Main Landing Gear (MLG) #5 brake assembly was replaced as per AMM. Inspection carried out and no further faults or damage found.

C-FAQB, un Bombardier CL600-2B16 en exploitation privé sous l’indicatif CDR695, effectuait un vol d’essai (pré-certificat de navigabilité) selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC avec 2 pilotes à bord. Le C-FAQB se trouvait dans la zone d’essai de Montréal Bravo et effectuait une descente depuis le niveau de vol 370. En quittant le niveau de vol 320 l'équipage a reçu une indication de compensation de la gouverne de direction vers la gauche ainsi qu'un mouvement intempestif de lacet dans la même direction. L’équipage a gardé la maîtrise de l’avion, a déclaré un état d’urgence et a amorcé un retour à CYUL. Durant le retour l’équipage a actionné le compensateur de sorte qu'une réduction de la force exercée sur le palonnier a été réduite. Toutefois, l'indicateur affichait toujours une pleine déflexion à gauche. L’avion s’est posé sur la piste 24L sans encombre. Une fois au sol, l'indicateur s'est replacé à la position neutre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FJBO, an Air Canada Express EMB175 was operating flight JZA556 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), NY. While at FL200, the crew received Bleed 1 and Bleed 2 Fail Caution lights. The crew declared an emergency and did a rapid descent from 20000ft to 10000ft. There was no negative passenger reaction and the flight landed in KJFK without further incident.

C-FKOE, a privately-registered Cessna A185F aircraft, was conducting a VFR flight from Nanaimo (CYCD), BC to a private airstrip in Surrey, BC with only the pilot on board. While descending for landing, a catastrophic, uncontained engine failure (Teledyne Continental IO-550-D) occurred. The pilot conducted an emergency landing in a vacant bog area of a park. The aircraft contacted trees and impacted the terrain in a nose-down attitude; a post-impact fire began on impact. The pilot egressed out the front right door. The pilot received serious injuries. The aircraft was destroyed. The emergency locator transmitter did not activate.

C-GGOY, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 was operating flight JZA445 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC. After leveling at 24 000 feet above sea level, approximately 50 nautical miles northwest of CYVR, the crew received a No.1 DC GEN HOT caution message and sparks were seen exiting the No.1 engine cowl vent. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft returned to CYVR, landed safely on runway 08R, and exited on taxiway D5. The No.1 engine was then shut down. The aircraft was taxied to the gate with the airport fire services following as a precaution. Company maintenance found the No.1 generator inlet duct had been broken off. The generator and associate generator control unit were replaced. Operational checks were carried out and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GCGX, a privately registered float-equipped Cessna A185F aircraft was conducting a post-maintenance test flight from Gods Lake, MB, approximately 3 nm east of Gods Lake Narrows Airport (CYGO), MB. The aircraft was being operated on the left fuel tank only due to minimum fuel. While turning to a final approach to the lake, the aircraft was banked sharply to the left and the engine (Teledyne Continental IO-520-D) abruptly lost power. The aircraft landed short of the intended landing area in a stand of trees. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was not injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

LX-VCD, a Cargolux Airlines International Boeing 747-8R7F operating as flight CLX37F, enroute from Luxembourg Findel Airport (ELLX), Luxembourg to Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), California. LX-VCD reported a technical issue with its fuel system while over the Hudson Bay, Ontario. The flight crew elected to divert to Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD), Illinois. No emergency was declared. The aircraft landed at KORD without further incident.

C-GDDR, a WestJet B737 Max 8 was operating flight WJA2251 from Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International Airport (MMPR), Puerto Vallarta, MX to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During climb out from MMPR through approximately FL350, the flight crew encountered the LH PACK Caution light illumination. QRH - NNC 2 - PACK checklist was called. During which, the flight crew encountered the RH PACK Caution light illumination. While the checklist was being actioned, the cabin altitude warning illuminated. The captain took control and QRH - NNC 2 - Cabin Altitude Warning or Rapid De-pressurization checklist was actioned. The flight crew donned the oxygen masks and established required communication. As the cabin altitude was uncontrollable, the flight crew as per procedures actioned the QRH - NNC 0 - emergency descent checklist, declared an emergency and started descent to 24000ft. The oxygen masks did deploy in the cabin. The aircraft gradually got cleared down to 14,000ft and then to 13,000ft. The flight crew contacted ATC / company and decision was made to divert to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (KPHX), AZ. The flight crew conducted a normal landing into KPHX and landed safely. The aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power where maintenance met the aircraft.

C-FWRB, a privately registered Piper Arrow PA-28R-180 aircraft, departed from Grand Falls Airport (CCK3), NB for a local flight after the pilot had conducted a walkaround inspection and pre-flight engine run-up. The takeoff was from CCK3 runway 16, and the winds were approximately 220 true at 6 to 9 knots. Shortly after takeoff as the aircraft reached about 700 feet above ground in the climb, the aircraft engine began to run with reduced power available and the pilot immediately lowered the aircraft nose and banked slightly left to avoid a wooded area. The aircraft made a forced landing into a soft, farm field about 1.5 statute miles SE of CCK3 with the wings level and the landing gear extended. The right main landing gear separated, and the left main and the nose landing gears collapsed as the aircraft skidded to a stop. All 4 occupants egressed without injury. The emergency locator transmitter activated, and emergency responders attended. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. No fuel was released in the forced landing.

C-FHNM, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft was operated by Nolinor Aviation, was conducting flight NRL581 from Allentown/Lehigh Valley Intl (KABE), USA to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. While on approach to CYWG, the aircraft experienced a flap extension failure. A go-around was performed and, after completing the fault checklist, the aircrew manually extended the flaps to 15 degrees. An emergency was declared and the aircraft subsequently landed uneventfully at CYWG.Initial inspection by the operator's maintenance did not identify the reason for the flap extension failure and further inspections are ongoing.

C-GETX, a Cessna 172N, operated by Envirotech Aviation Inc., was on a flight from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB returning to CYEG with 2 crew members on board. Just prior to commencing a descent, the pilot-in-command briefly applied carburetor heat to the engine. During the initial power reduction for descent, the engine RPM decreased to approximately 700 rpm. Initial attempts to restore power to the engine were unsuccessful and the crew declared an emergency. Engine power was restored at an altitude of 3500 feet ASL with the application of full power. The crew then contacted Edmonton Tower, who offered priority handling, which was declined by the crew. Once established on a base leg for Runway 30 the power was reduced from full to cruise, which resulted in a second sudden power loss to approximately 700 rpm. Power was restored when full power was re-applied, and the crew elected to request priority handling and continue to the runway at full power. Once landing was assured, power was reduced, and the aircraft landed without further incident.Following the flight, the engine was inspected and no faults in either the engine or the carburetor heat system were found. It was determined that the pilot had only momentarily applied carburetor heat and that the power loss was likely due to carburetor icing.

C-FDOD, a Wisk Air Helicopters Bell 412 experienced a main rotor blade strike while enplaning passengers at a mining exploration drill site. Due to the presence of drilling equipment on the helicopter landing pad, the helicopter landed on the edge of the pad with the drill equipment under and within the rotor disk. The pilot maintained some power with collective input as the passengers embarked. As the third passenger boarded the helicopter, the pilot heard a noise that sounded to be coming from behind his chair and felt a couple of vibrations from the floor or skid area. The pilot did not observe any additional abnormalities, continued with the flight and returned to the base camp. After shutdown, 2 of 4 main rotor blades were found damaged. The following day, it was determined that the main rotor blades had contacted the drill mast. The 2 damaged blades were replaced.

G-GQPC, un SAAB 340B exploité par Pascan Aviation sous l’indicatif de vol PSC373 était en route de Montreal Saint-Hubert Longueuil Airport (CYHU),QC à destination de l'Aéroport de Bonaventure (CYVB), QC, lorsque l’équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence médicale pour un agent de bord qui a subi un malaise l’empêchant de poursuivre ses fonctions. L’appareil a dérouté vers l’aéroport Régional de Mont-Joli (CYYY), QC, où il s’est posé sans problème. Un agent de bord qui effectuait une vérification de compétence de l'agent de bord affecté a pris la relève du service de cabine.

C-FLTS, un Beech A-100 exploité par Exact Air en tant que vol ET823 entre Baie-Comeau, Qc (CYBC) et La Romaine, Qc (CTT5) était en croisière à 30 milles nautiques à l'est d’Havre-St-Pierre, Qc (CYGV) lorsque les pilotes ont observé une fluctuation de l'indication de pression d'huile du moteur numéro 2. La décision de faire diversion vers CYGV a été prise par précaution et une urgence a été déclarée. L'aéronef s'est posé sécuritairement à CYGV. Le personnel de maintenance a identifié un indicateur de pression d'huile défectueux.

C-GKQK, an Embraer ERJ 190-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting an IFR flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. While enroute, approximately 5 NM North of the Regina Intl (CYQR), SK, a cabin crew member became ill. The ill crew member's duties were assumed by another cabin crew member for the remainder of the flight. The flight continued to CYYC without incident. The ill crew member was attended to by medical personnel upon arrival.

C-FNED, a GCS Aviation Beechcraft B90A, was operating from Red Deer (CYQF), AB to Penticton (CYYF), BC. Approximately 67 nm SW of CYQF the flight crew was alerted to a low oil pressure on the right engine (PRATT & WHITNEY-CAN, PT6A-28). The flight crew elected to shut down the engine as a precaution and returned to CYQF. The aircraft landed safely with no further issues. An emergency was not declared.Following the flight, the maintenance team found that the "B" nut on the oil pressure transmitter line was loose. The line was tightened, engine cleaned, ground run, leak checked and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FYWP, a Buffalo Airways Ltd. Canadair Ltd. CL215-1A10, was conducting forest fire fighting operations in the vicinity of Gordon Lake, NT, 53 NM NE of Yellowknife, NT. During a scooping run on Gordon Lake, the aircraft struck an object. The take-off was rejected and the captain water taxied to the shore to park the aircraft. A helicopter picked up the flight crew to return them to Yellowknife. Damage to the lower forward section of the hull was substantial.UPDATED 02 NOVEMBER 2023

C-GJEN, a WestJet Encore DH8D-Q400, was operating as flight WEN3281 from Calgary International (CYYC), AB to Penticton (CYYF), BC. After the aircraft took off and landing gear retraction, the flight crew observed that the left main landing gear light remained illuminated green. The flight crew completed the takeoff checklist and requested to level off at 7000 feet. ATC was notified of the issue and vectors were requested to remain in the vicinity of the airport while the flight crew actioned checklists. The flight crew actioned the LANDING GEAR INDICATION MALFUNCTION QRH. The crew declared a PAN PAN and landed back in CYYC safely.Company maintenance team replaced the landing gear control panel, tested it and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FKGL, a Douglas DC3C operated by North Star Air Ltd. as flight BF102 departed Wunnumin Lake (CKL3), ON, to Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON. The aircraft was landing on Runway 27 at CYPL when the flight crew experienced a loss of control due to a flat left main tire. The aircraft veered to the left and experienced a runway side excursion. The left main wheel dug into the soft turf causing the aircraft to enter a rapid tight left turn. The aircraft damage was limited to the left main wheel assembly. There were no injuries.

C-GVIJ, a Cargojet B767 was operating flight CJT925 from Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL to Viracopos International Airport (SBKP), Brazil. Shortly after take-off, the crew received a "FLAP DISAGREE" message. After troubleshooting with MCC and QRH actioned, the crew elected to return to KMIA. A PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft landed slightly overweight without further incident.

C-GXHJ, a Helijet International Incorporated Sikorsky S-76C++ operating as flight JBA705, was conducting a flight from Vancouver / Harbour Heliport (CBC7), BC, to Victoria Harbour Heliport (CBF7), BC, with 2 flight crew and 12 passengers onboard. During cruise flight, the aircraft was struck by lightning and entered an uncontrolled descent. The pilot-in-command regained control of the aircraft following a loss of approximately 2900 vertical feet. The aircraft continued the flight to CBF7 and landed without further incident. There were no reported injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The post-landing inspection revealed that 2 tail rotor blades had separated from the helicopter and there was impact damage found on the main rotor blades, the left horizontal stabilizer and the left engine cowl. The aircraft was disassembled to the degree necessary for ground transport to a hangar at Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC for detailed examination.

C-FTMB, an Aviation Unlimited (1990) Inc. Cirrus SR22, was operating a flight from Oshawa Executive Airport (CYOO), ON to Chicago Midway International Airport (KMDW), IL. At approximately 1100 CDT, the pilot declared an emergency due to loss of engine thrust 10 miles south of South Bend, IN. The pilot attempted to glide to South Bend International Airport (KSBN) but had to deploy the parachute 4 NM south of the airport. The aircraft landed in a corn field and there were no reported injuries. FAA:At this point the FAA, have concluded our investigation of this incident. We are closing it out as an airworthiness issued due to loss of oil, and recording the fact that the left waste gate oil line was found loose. Because the aircraft is maintained under Canada’s civil aviation regulations, our action taken is that we are relaying our findings to the Transportation Safety Board of Canada for appropriate action.

C-GBIA, an Air Canada Airbus A319-114 operating as flight ACA243, was conducting a flight from Edmonton International (CYEG), AB, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise, the No.2 engine (CFM International CFM56-5A5) compressor stalled. The pilots actioned the quick reference handbook (QRH), switched off the auto throttle, and reduced the No.2 engine throttle. The No.2 engine anti-ice was turned on, the throttle was re-applied, and the engine operated normally. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and continued the flight to CYVR without any further issues. The aircraft landed safely at CYVR and with aircraft rescue and fire fighting assets on standby. The aircraft taxied to the terminal and a normal shutdown was completed on both engines. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft.   Maintenance conducted troubleshooting on the No.2 engine and replaced the high pressure (HP) bleed valve and the hydro-mechanical unit (HMU). A compressor wash was carried out followed by a successful power assurance run and leak check.

C-FFPH, a Sunwing Airlines Boeing 737-81D was operating as SWG5146, from Cancun International Airport (MMUN), Mexico to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the takeoff roll, the flight crew and cabin crew smelled burning rubber that dissipated approximately 1 minute after rotation. The flight proceeded to destination but the flight crew, suspecting tire damage, requested to have emergency services on standby upon arrival in CYYZ. The landing was completed without incident and no damage was reported by emergency services. Following the incident, maintenance inspected the aircraft, no faults were found, and the tires were deemed serviceable.

C-GHPJ, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was operating as flight ROU7098 from Saskatoon/ John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. This flight was a non-revenue positioning flight with only the two pilots on board. During cruise at flight level 390, approximately 15 NM N of Sault Ste. Marie, while operating with a PACK 1 INOP (MEL 21-52-01-D), the flight crew received AIR (R) WING LEAK; AIR BLEED; AIR PACK 1 2 FAULT ECAM messages.  With PACK 1 on MEL, the failure of the other PACK resulted in the inability to maintain cabin pressurization. The crew donned their oxygen masks, declared a PAN PAN emergency and initiated a descent to 10,000 feet above sea level (ASL) in accordance with company policy and procedures. Cabin altitude reached 9,000 feet ASL as the aircraft leveled at 10,000 feet ASL. The flight continued to destination and was completed without further incident.

C-FIVK, an Air Canada B777-200 was operating flight AC42 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Indira Gandhi International Airport (VIDP), India. During cruise, the flight crew shut down the number 1 engine due to low oil pressure. After consulting with maintenance, the crew elected to divert to Heydar Aliyev International Airport (UBBB), Azerbaijan. A Mayday was declared, and the aircraft landed approximately 20 KG overweight. The aircraft taxied to the gate without further incident.

C-GKKR, an Aerospatiale ATR 42-320 operated by Calm Air International LP was conducting flight MO121 from Flin Flon (CYFO), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. During the flight, a flight attendant was unable to perform the duties due to an illness. The flight continued to CYWG and landed without incident.

C-GAKI, an Alkan Air Dornier 228 was operating as flight AKN100 from Dawson City (CYDA), YT to Erik Nielsen International Airport (CYXY), YT. On approach into CYXY, the flight crew observed low oil pressure on the number 1 engine (GARRETT, TPE331-5). The engine was shut down as a precaution in accordance with the company's standard operating procedures (SOPs) and a PAN PAN was declared with ATS. The flight landed without further issue.Company maintenance determined the oil cooler was leaking.

C-GKHX, a Kestrel Helicopters Limited Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 (AStar) helicopter, was conducting longline operations under visual flight rules, 8 nautical miles east of Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, with one pilot on board. At 1348 pacific daylight time, 10 metal sheets, 4 feet by 8 feet in size, came loose from the slung load and fell into the water below the helicopter. The aircraft continued its flight and dropped off the remainder of the slung load before returning to its staging area without further incident. There were no reported injuries, and there was no damage to the aircraft or to property. The Coast Guard determined that there was no environmental impact, and no pollution report was required as a result of the occurrence.

C-GOIH, an Air Transat A321LR was operating flight TSC729 from London Gatwick Airport (EGKK), UK to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Shortly after take-off, a flight attendant sustained a minor injury. The cabin crew was incapacitated and could not resume duties. The safety-related positions and responsibilities were reassigned in order of jumpseat priority. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GMEX, an Air Canada B737-8, was operating flight ACA990 from Mexico City International Airport (MMMX), MX to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Approximately 30 minutes after departure the crew reported cabin decompression and oxygen masks deployed. A MAYDAY was declared, and the flight descended to 8000ft, the decision was made to divert to George Bush Intercontinental/Houston Airport (KIAH), Texas. The aircraft landed without further incident, EMS met aircraft on arrival and no injuries were reported.L/H PACK Air conditioning computer (IASC) replaced in accordance with AMM.

C-GDUZ, an Air Canada B767-300 was operating flight AC7253 from Jorge Chavez International Airport (SPJC), Peru to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the take-off roll, the main deck cargo and master warning light came on. The flight crew went through the quick reference handbook and in discussion with MOC and dispatch, the decision was made to declare a Pan Pan and return to SPJC. The aircraft landed with aircraft rescue and fire fighting on standby and the aircraft taxied to the gate without further incident.The aircraft was inspected on arrival in SPJC and it was determined to be an upper deck Cargo door indication issue. Maintenance applied an MEL for the Cargo door indication and the flight continued to destination without issue.

N653UA, un appareil de type Boeing 767-322ER exploité par United Airlines, effectuait le vol UAL925 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Londre/Heathrow (EGLL) à destination de l'aéroport Washington Dulles Intl - Washington, DC (KIAD) avec 10 membres d'équipage et 125 passagers à bord. À environ 210 NM ENE de Sept-Îles, QC, un des deux premiers officiers a commencé à se sentir malade vers la fin de sa période de repos et a été incapable de retourner au poste de pilotage. Le capitaine et l'officier de relève ont complété le vol sans encombre.

C-GOIK, an Air Transat A321-271NX was operating flight TSC251 from Aéroport de Paris-Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Approximately 35 minutes prior to landing, a cabin crew became incapacitated. The safety related responsibilities were reassigned in order of jumpseat priority. The flight landed without further incident.

C-FTXF, un appareil de type Boeing 737-8 exploité par Sunwing Airlines, s'apprêtait à effectuer le vol de positionnement SWG9762 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport Lester B. Pearson Intl, Toronto (CYYZ) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors que l'aéronef était en préparation à la barrière, le bord d'attaque de l'aile droite a été heurté par un véhicule de service au sol. L'appareil a été retiré du service pour réparation. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-FDFK, an ATR-GIE 72-212A operated by Calm Air International LP, was conducting flight MO117 from Thompson (CYTH) MB. to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB. After the flight attendants completed the safety demonstration, a flight attendant felt ill. The flight crew were notified and the aircraft departed CYTH and landed safely in CYWG with one flight attendant assuming the duties. No medical attention was required in CYWG.

C-GGFJ, a Jazz Aviation LP DeHavilland DHC-8-400, operating as flight JZA7711 from the Ottawa Macdonald - Cartier International airport (CYOW), ON to the Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, declared a PAN PAN due to an indication that the right service door not closed. The flight returned to CYOW and landed without incident.  Airport Fire Fighting was on standby.

C-FNWD, a Westjet Airlines Boeing 737-800, was conducting flight WJA1723 under instrument flight rules from Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), CA, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 6 crew members and 144 passengers on board. During departure from KPSP, the flight crew reportedly experienced a strong vibration or shimmy, 10 seconds in duration, felt in both the control column and rudder pedals. The crew briefly left the landing gear extended to ensure that the vibration did not persist. With no further abnormalities observed, the landing gear was retracted, and the aircraft proceeded to its destination. Prior to landing at CYVR, a PAN PAN was declared as a precautionary measure. The aircraft landed without incident at 1551 PDT, and was inspected by aircraft rescue and firefighting personnel. The aircraft subsequently taxied to the gate under its own power.Post flight maintenance action included replacement of the left and right nose landing gear wheel assemblies, service and lubrication of the nose landing gear lower end components, serviceability checks of the replaced and serviced components, and a general visual inspection of the aircraft exterior. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) was submitted to Transport Canada, and the aircraft was subsequently returned to service.

C-FWFJ, an Eurocopter EC-130 B4 was taking off for a private flight from Collingwood (Wilsons) Heliport (CCW2), ON to Collingwood Airport (CNY3), ON with only 1 pilot onboard. Shortly after takeoff from the helipad, the pilot initiated a left pedal turn to turn into wind which was reportedly at 12 knots gusting to 22 knots from the North. The left yaw subsequently accelerated past the intended heading and the helicopter started rotating. As the helicopter was still rotating and drifting south, the main rotor blades hit a tree. The helicopter subsequently stopped and came to rest against a house. The pilot shut down the engine and exited the helicopter with only a minor injury. The Emergency locator transmitter (ELT) activated, and the signal received by the Joint Rescue Coordination Center (JRCC) in Trenton, ON. The helicopter and the house were substantially damaged.

C-GTVO, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Chrono Jet inc., effectuait le vol MBK793 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, de l'aéroport de Mary River, NU (CMR2) à destination de l'aéroport d'Iqualuit, NU (CYFB) avec 5 membres d'équipage et 39 passagers à bord. Lors de l'approche pour la piste 16 de CYFB, l'équipage a rencontré un problème de volets et a effectué une procédure de remise des gaz. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'aéronef a ensuite atterri sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés. Une inspection mécanique subséquente effectuée par l'exploitant a révélé un transmetteur de position des volets défectueux.

C-GQXD, a Piper PA-31-350 operated by 2080061 Ontario Inc. (dba SkyCare Air Ambulance), was conducting a flight from Pickle Lake Airport (CYPL), ON to Winnipeg/St. Andrews (CYAV), MB. The aircraft was fuelled by a local fuelling company in CYPL. As the aircraft was departing from CYPL, the fueller realized that the aircraft was fuelled with Jet A instead of AVGAS and called NAV CANADA to relay a message to the flight crew of C-GQXD. The engines continued running and crew diverted to Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL), ON, where the aircraft landed without incident.

The Carson Air Swearingen SW4 (Metro III), C-FJKK, was operating as CRN7081 from Kelowna (CYWL), BC to Calgary (CYYC), AB. The aircraft landed on Runway 35L in CYYC. On the roll out the flight crew smelled smoke inside the cockpit. The aircraft was stopped on Taxiway W and the flight crew requested the ground controller to dispatch aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) equipment. The aircraft was shut down and secured, then the flight crew evacuated onto the taxiway. The cargo from the aircraft was unloaded on the taxiway, under supervision of ARFF. During the unloading, ARFF monitored for hot spots. When the cargo was unloaded, company maintenance confirmed that there was a cargo fire under the floor cargo rollers. The aft heat duct had previously been isolated to direct all bleed air heat forward to the cockpit and a paper strip (sticker backer) had gotten blown forward to FS197 and pinned against the heat duct. The paper strip was heated, smoldered, and subsequently ignited some sawdust, cardboard box “fuzz”, and wood scraps. Maintenance inspected the cooling turbines, duct overheat, and bleed air system with no further faults noted. The aircraft will undergo a scheduled cleaning maintenance task. The aircraft received no damage. The flight crew were the sole persons onboard, and they received no injuries.

The WestJet Encore de Havilland DHC-8-400, C-GENK, was operating as WEN3317 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Edmonton (CYEG), AB. The WestJet Boeing 737-800, C-GWJS, was operating as WJA167 from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Vancouver (CYVR), BC. A loss of separation occurred approximately 5 NM NW of CYEG as WEN3317 was on approach for landing while turning on the right base for Runway 12 and observed traffic on TCAS. Moments later the flight crew visually identified the traffic. WJA167 was departing Runway 02 (Gabet 1 departure) and was given a left turn on radar vectors. A further left turn was provided due to traffic. The flight crew received a TCAS RA aural alert and had traffic in sight. Once clear of traffic, WJA167 was cleared direct to the en-route waypoint. Separation reduced to 2.5 miles where 3 miles is required.

N336QS, an EMB-505 operated by Netjets Sales, was conducting flight EJA336 from Chicago/Midway Intl (KMDW), USA to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. N336QS was cleared for the RNAV Z RWY 36 at CYWG. C-GAMI, a Fairchild SA227-AC operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting a local VFR training flight as flight PAG958T. C-GAMI was conducting a simulated RNAV Z RWY 36 approach behind N336QS. ATC instructed PAG958T to reduce speed to 150 knots or less and a further reduction to minimum approach speed. The wake turbulence separation requirement between the aircraft was 4 nm; however, the separation was reduced to 3.4 nm. C-GAMI landed safely.

C-FAMS, un Piper PA-31-325 exploité par le Collège d’enseignement général et professionnel de Chicoutimi effectuait un vol de maintenance selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) avec un pilote et un technicien d’entretien d’aéronef à bord. Au moment de la remontée, après avoir effectué une approche IFR simulée à l’aéroport de Bagotville, QC (CYBG), le pilote a observé une indication que le train d’atterrissage n’était pas complètement rétracté. Le pilote a annulé la seconde approche IFR simulée prévue et a reçu l’autorisation de monter à 3000 pieds pour procéder à des vérifications. Le pilote a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) mais l’indication que le train de gauche n’était pas totalement sorti ou verrouillé est restée allumée. Le pilote a demandé au contrôleur aérien de CYRC l’autorisation de faire un passage bas devant la tour pour une vérification visuelle de la position du train d’atterrissage. Le contrôleur aérien a confirmé que les roues étaient descendues. Le pilote a suivi la procédure d’urgence applicable et a demandé les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d’aéronefs (SLIA). L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GAIW, un Dash-8-314 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE884 était en préparation pour effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) à destination de Kangiqsujuaq, QC (CYKG) avec 3 membres d’équipage de conduite à bord. Pendant la séquence de démarrage des moteurs, l’équipage a identifié une fumée jaune qui provenait du panneau de disjoncteurs de gauche (EXHUST FAN1). L’équipage a arrêté la séquence de démarrage et a demandé par radio le véhicule d’incendie. L’équipage a évacué l’aéronef sans encombre et aucun incendie ne s’est déclaré. L’inspection visuelle du panneau a permis de trouver un fil électrique et le disjoncteur associé, brûlés.

C-FVHW, a Valley Helicopters Ltd. Bell 206L-4 (LongRanger IV) helicopter, was conducting longline operations under visual flight rules 12 nautical miles east-northeast of Hope Airport (CYHE), BC, with one pilot on board. At 1000 PDT, while operating at 400 feet above ground level, the pilot inadvertently pushed the longline cargo release button. The slung load of trees was released from the longline. The released external load landed in a heavily forested area. There were no reported injuries. There was no damage to the aircraft or to property.

C-GJZX, un Dash 8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l’indicatif de vol 7952 venait de décoller de Billy Bishop Toronto City/Toronto, ON (CYTZ) à destination de  Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl- Montréal QC (CYUL) lorsque l'équipage a observé une indication de porte de train d'atterrissage avant non fermée. Les procédures QRH ont été suivies et le vol a continué vers CYUL. Avant l'atterrissage, une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre.

C-FIDZ, un avion de construction amateur privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis la rivière de la Croix, QC vers la rivière Matonipi, QC avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Le pilote avait décollé d’un camp de chasse environ 30 minutes avant d’amerrir sur la rivière de la Croix pour un court arrêt. Au décollage, alors que l’avion avait une hauteur d’environ 5 pieds au-dessus de l’eau, le moteur a perdu momentanément de la puissance et l’avion n’a pas pu continuer sa montée. Le pilote a conservé la trajectoire de l’avion au-dessus de la rivière pour y effectuer un amerrissage. Cependant, l’avion n’a pas pu être arrêté avant la fin du plan d’eau. Le flotteur de gauche a percuté une roche et les ailes de l’avion ont été endommagées par des arbres. Les 2 occupants n’ont pas été blessés.

C-GENK, a DeHavilland of Canada DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore was conducting flight WEN3522 from Grand Prairie, AB, (CYQU) to Calgary International, AB (CYYC) and conducting an IFR approach for Runway 17L. WEN3522 was being followed by two other aircraft on the RNAV Yankee approach, also for Runway 17L, C-FBWJ, a Boeing 737-700 operated by WestJet Airlines conducting flight WJA263 from Saskatoon, SK (CYXE) to Calgary International (CYYC), and C-FRAX, a Boeing 737 Max 8 also operated by WestJet conducting flight WJA1537 from Pheonix Sky Harbor, AZ (KPHX) to Calgary International (CYYC). The terminal arrival controller discontinued the approach for the second aircraft, WJA263, due to spacing on final with preceding arrival WEN3522. While repositioning for another approach, WJA263 came within 2.6 NM and 900 feet of WEN3255 and 2.5 NM and co-altitude with WJA1537 when 3 NM or 1000 feet separation was required.

C-FRQN, a Jazz Aviation E175 was operating flight JZA973 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to St. Louis Lambert International Airport (KSTL), Missouri. The crew had a HYDRAULIC NO:2 SYSTEM FAILURE, the crew actioned their quick reference handbook, maintenance and dispatch advised they continue to KSTL. The crew used an alternate gear extension and advised ATC of an emergency landing in KSTL.

C-FHCW, a Nolinor Aviation Learjet 45 was operating flight NRL480 from Minneapolis–Saint Paul International Airport (KMSP), Minnesota to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, Nevada. After take-off from KMSP, the crew noticed a R PYLON OVERHEAT. The crew followed the appropriate quick reference handbook checklist and declared a PAN PAN and received priority to return to KMSP. The crew landed without further incident and confirmed with aircraft rescue and fire fighting as well as tower that no smoke or fire was visible from RH engine.

N41140, a Boeing 757-224 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL317 from Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ to Dublin Intl (EIDW), Ireland.  While in cruise about 2 hours and 40 minutes into the flight (at 52°23' N, 055°01' W) the flight crew heard a bang and noted a momentary yaw of the aircraft. The flight crew noted the EICAS message for number 1 engine (Rolls-Royce RB211-535E4B) vibration, consulted the QRH, reduced left engine power until the vibration decreased below the amber range, and declared an emergency. The flight crew consulted with company maintenance control personnel and decided to return to KEWR. The diversion was coordinated with ATS, and the flight landed at KEWR without further incident.Company maintenance identified a crack at the 1 o'clock position on the number 1 engine exhaust nozzle and removed and replaced the engine.

C-GSPW, un Boeing 737-275C exploité par Air Inuit Ltée sous l’indicatif AIE753 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL), à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). En approche pour CYQB, l’équipage a sélectionné la position 1 des volets, mais l’indicateur des volets est demeuré à 0. L’équipage a contacté le service de maintenance de la compagnie et la décision de retourner à CYUL a été prise. L’équipage a avisé l’unité de contrôle de la circulation aérienne (ATC) et a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour se préparer à effectuer un atterrissage avec les volets rétractés. En rapprochement de CYUL, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence. Les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d’aéronefs (SLIA) ont été avisés. L’aéronef s’est posé et s’est arrêté sur la piste 24R. À la suite d’une inspection visuelle de l’aéronef au sol par le SLIA, l’aéronef a pu circuler pour quitter la piste et se rendre à son aire de stationnement dédié. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

C-FEJP, a Jazz Aviation E175 was operating flight JZA940 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), New Jersey. There was already one air conditioning pack unserviceable when the aircraft was climbing through 24,000 feet. The aircraft picked up icing and lost the other air conditioning pack. The crew carried out an emergency descent to 10,000 feet. All passengers and crew donned their oxygen masks and the aircraft returned to CYUL. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GNLN, un Boeing 737-2B6C exploité par Les Investissements Nolinor Inc. sous l’indicatif NRL951 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Val d’Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de Montréal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX). En route vers CYMX, plusieurs erreurs d’indication sont apparues sur l’écran de vol principal (PFD) dont des erreurs sur la vitesse indiquée, l’altitude et le variomètre. Des messages d’avertissement sont également apparus dont un faux message provenant du système avertisseur de proximité du sol (GPWS). L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et suivi les procédures établies par la compagnie. La décision de poursuivre le vol jusqu’à CYMX a été prise et l’équipage a déclaré une urgence auprès de l’unité de contrôle de la circulation aérienne (ATC). L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre à CYMX.

C-FJZS, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC897 from Eleftherios Venizelos Intl - Athens (LGAV), Greece to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During the flight, a flight attendant was unable to continue their duties due to a medical issue. The flight landed without further incident.

C-GBZS, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. B737-800 was operating flight TOM7572 from Belfast International Airport (EGAA), UK to Corfu International Airport "Ioannis Kapodistrias" (LGKR), Greece. On descent into LGKR, the ATC cleared TOM7572 to FL370 from FL410. The ATC then cleared TOM7572 to descend to FL350. At FL358, the flight crew received a TCAS TA for traffic below them, followed by a TCAS RA with command to level off. The flight crew disconnected the autopilot and levelled off at FL353. They then received a "clear of conflict" aural alert. The autopilot was re-engaged and the aircraft descended to FL350 as cleared by ATC. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GTYH, a SkyQuest Aviation Ltd. Piper PA-34-200 Seneca aircraft (serial number 34-7250160) departed Langley Regional Airport (CYNJ), BC, on a visual flight rules training flight with one instructor, one student, and one passenger on board. After conducting some maneuvering exercises and one circuit at Chilliwack Airport (CYCW), BC, the aircraft commenced a missed approach. During the attempted missed approach, the aircraft rolled into a right bank, continued the roll until it struck trees and terrain in a nose down and inverted attitude. The three occupants were fatally injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged and there was no post-impact fire. The TSB deployed investigators and the investigation is ongoing.

The Jazz Airlines LP DeHavilland DHC-8-400, C-GGNZ, was operating as JZA7124, repositioning on a flight from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Winnipeg (CYWG), MB with 2 flight crew on board. As JZA7124 commenced the take-off roll on Runway 17R, two ground vehicles/tugs that had been holding short of Runway 17R on Taxiway C2, drove onto Runway 17R and proceeded from C2 to Taxiway U. They then turned onto Uniform and cleared Runway 17R. The flight crew of JZA7124 noticed the vehicles as the aircraft approached the take-off decision speed (V1) and elected to continue the take-off. Minimum lateral distance was 1800 feet. The aircraft passed overhead the tugs through 300 feet as the tugs exited the runway at Taxiway U.

C-GSPW un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments sous l'indicatif AIE754 depuis l'aéroport de Val-d'Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC. Lors de l'approche finale, alors que le déploiement des volets a été commandé, une indication d'un problème de volets est apparue dans le poste de pilotage. L'approche a été interrompue, l'appareil est remonté et une urgence a été déclarée. La liste de vérification a été effectuée et l'appareil est revenu se poser sans encombre environ 20 minutes après l'approche interrompue. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé.

C-GSPW, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif de vol AIE753 avec à son bord 32 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage effectuait un vol entre l’aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau international (CYUL), Qc à destination de Val-d’Or Qc (CYVO). À l’approche de CYVO, un membre d’équipage de cabine  s’est blessé l’empêchant de continuer ses tâches en tant que membre d'équipage. L’appareil a poursuivi sa route vers CYVO où il s’est posé sans problème.

C-GMAI un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Val-d'Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC avec 20 passagers et 4 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de l'approche initiale en virage à droite pour intercepter l'ILS de la piste 24R l'équipage a ressenti une secousse brusque et le roulis vers la droite s'est rapidement accentué. Le pilote a remarqué que les commandes étaient au neutre ou presque, mais que le taux de roulis s'accentuait. Le pilote automatique a été désengagé et le pilote a tourné les commandes complètement à gauche. Le roulis vers la droite a persisté un bref moment malgré la commande du pilote pour ensuite reprendre une assiette normale. L'approche s'est poursuivie sans problème et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Un Boeing 787-9 précédait l'appareil en cause, l'espacement avec le lourd était au minimum prescrit de 5 miles nautiques.

C-GXQX un hélicoptère Eagle Helicycle de construction amateure en exploitation privée, effectuait une activité de maintenance dans l'aire de stationnement de l'aéroport de St-Mathieu-de-Beloeil à Beloeil Qc, (CSB3). La turbine était en fonction avec les rotors engagés. Le pilote casqué était aux commandes dans le siège du pilote. Un mécanicien ajustait la turbine qui était alimentée en carburant par un bidon externe. À un certain moment, la turbine s'est subitement emballée causant un début de basculement dynamique. Le pilote, ne sachant pas que les pieds du mécanicien étaient sur le patin a tenté d'empêcher le basculement en appliquant du collectif, causant le décollage de l'appareil. Gagnant de l'altitude, le bidon alimentant la turbine s'est déconnecté et la turbine s'est arrêtée alors qu'il était à environ 30 pieds du sol. L'appareil est redescendu et a lourdement touché le sol. Le pilote et le mécanicien ont subi des blessures légères.

C-GJHZ un Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ-900) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP effectuait le vol JZA94 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis  l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC à destination de l'aéroport J.A. Douglas McCurdy/Sydney, NE (CYQY). Quelques minutes après le décollage, passant le niveau de vol 100, l'équipage a remarqué une fumée accompagnée d'une odeur de brulé dans le poste pilotage. Les pilotes ont enfilé leurs masques à oxygène, déclaré une urgence et amorcé un retour vers CYUL. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre à 17:39 UTC sur la piste 24R où les véhicules d'urgence ont été déployés. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé. La source de la fumée et de l'odeur était une connexion électrique du pare-brise de gauche. Le pare-brise a été remplacé par le personnel de maintenance et l'appareil est retourné en service.

G-ZBKN, a British Airways Boeing 787-900, operating as BAW8 on a flight from Tokyo Haneda International Airport (RJTT), Japan to London Heathrow Airport (EGLL), England experienced smoke in the cabin due to a portable device (phone) being stuck down the side of a passenger seat. The cabin was vented, and a Pan Pan was declared. The aircraft diverted to Anchorage Ted Stevens International Airport (PANC), Alaska, USA.

C-GJTX, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1709 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, Nevada. During the final approach phase of flight, descending through 1000ft ASL while conducting a visual approach to KLAS RWY 19R, the flight crew determined stable approach criteria could not be met and requested go around instructions from ATC. ATC issued instructions to climb runway heading to 7000 and go around was initiated. Shortly thereafter TCAS RA: CLIMB was annunciated. The flight crew complied with the RA in accordance with company policy and procedure. The flight crew attempted to notify ATC during the RA but was unable due to frequency congestion. The flight was subsequently completed without further incident.

OK-HAR, a Cessna Citation 560XL was conducting an IFR flight from Reykjavik Airport, (BIRK), Iceland to Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL. C-GIED, a de Havilland DHC-6-300 operated by Air Borealis as Northlight 483 (LGH 483), was conducting a VFR flight from Cartwright Airport (CYCA) NL to CYYR.LGH 483 was instructed by ATC to join a left base for Runway 26 and that they would be number 2 to Citation OK-HAR, that was cleared straight-in approach for Runway 26. When OK-HAR was in final approach for Runway 26, LGH 483 reported abeam the VOR and was instructed by ATC to turn right to fly the base leg for Runway 26 in an attempt to visually acquire OK-HAR and they were to follow. LGH 483 advised they did not have OK-HAR in sight. ATC advised LGH 483 to join the downwind for 26 from their current position but the radio transmission got stepped on and the instruction was not heard by LGH 483. They subsequently flew through the final approach for Runway 26 in front of OK-HAR at the same time they made visual contact with OK-HAR.OK-HAR was in visual contact with LGH 483 and arrested their approach descent profile, anticipating a potential conflict, and climbed slightly to remain above LGH 483. Simultaneously, OK-HAR received a TCAS-RA warning as they were passing by LGH 483. OK-HAR then continued their approach to a safe landing on Runway 26 at 15:22 ADT. LGH 483 safely landed approximately 2 minutes later.  A loss of separation occurred when both aircraft came within ½ nm horizontally and 200 feet vertically.

C-FIVR, an Air Canada B777-333ER was conducting flight ACA80 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Tel Aviv Ben Gurion Airport (LLBG), IL. Approximately 62 nm NNW of Sydney/J.A. Douglas McCurdy Airport (CYQY), NS, the crew declared a PAN PAN and requested to return to CYYZ due to a hydraulic system failure indication. The other two hydraulic systems onboard operated normally for the duration of the flight and ACA80 landed uneventfully at 0132 UTC.After troubleshooting, maintenance confirmed that the left rudder PCU was leaking. The PCU was replaced as per the AMM and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FGXR un Beech B200 exploité par Air Nunavut effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Naujaat, NU (CYUT) à destination de l'aéroport d'Iqaluit, NU (CYFB). Suite à une approche manquée, le pilote a rapporté que son niveau de carburant était bas et a déclaré une urgence pour éviter le déroutement vers son aéroport de dégagement. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre à CYFB.

C-GUTA un Dornier Alpha Jet exploité par Top Aces Inc. effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à destination de l'aéroport militaire de Bagotville, Qc (CYBG) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de l'approche finale, alors que la sélection de sortie du train d'atterrissage a été effectuée, les feux verts indiquant que le train est sorti et verrouillé ne se sont pas illuminés. L'indicateur rouge avertissant le pilote que le train n'est pas sorti malgré la commande de sortie ne s'est pas non plus illuminé. Une inspection visuelle a été effectuée par un autre appareil accompagnateur. Un test du système d'anti blocage (anti-skid) a été effectué avec succès et poursuivant l'approche, l'avertisseur de train non sorti ne s'est pas déclenché, rassurant le pilote que le train était probablement sorti et sécuritaire. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Pas de blessé. L'appareil a été retiré du service et une inspection plus approfondie sera effectuée.

C-GYJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP de Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was preparing to conduct flight JZA416 under instrument flight rules from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Penticton Airport (CYYF), BC, with 4 crew members and 20 passengers on board. Prior to pushback, cabin crew reportedly detected the smell of electrical smoke. While investigating the source of the fumes, a passenger approached a cabin crew member with an external battery that showed signs of being abnormally hot. The external battery was placed inside a lithium-ion battery incident kit (LIBIK). The LIBIK containing the battery was removed from the aircraft and retrieved by fire crews for disposal of the battery inside. Prior to departure, the empty LIBIK was returned to the aircraft. There were no injuries, and no damage to the aircraft was reported.

C-FJQZ, a CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900), operating as Jazz Aviation LP flight JZA729, departed from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ). Shortly afterwards the flight crew observed the nosewheel steering inoperative caution light illuminate. The flight crew actioned the QRH, communicated with maintenance and dispatch, and subsequently returned to CYYZ. The crew declared a PAN PAN, landed without further incident and was towed to the gate.

C-GPCF, a Pacific Coastal Airlines SAAB SF340B was operating as flight PCO3056 from Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International Airport (CYXC), BC to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While on arrival to CYYC, PCO3056 encountered severe turbulence while passing through 12 000 feet ASL. The crew was able to bring the aircraft back under control and landed safely. There were no injuries.Maintenance update: The aircraft is grounded pending a maintenance inspection.

C-GRDI un hélicoptère Aérospatiale AS350 B-2 exploité par Héli-Express inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis un chemin près de La Forge 1 situé à environ 50 miles nautiques au nord-est de l'aéroport de La Grande 4, Qc (CYAH) Lors de travaux d'élinguage, peu après le décollage, l'indicateur du bas niveau de carburant s'est allumé. Le pilote est allé déposer sa charge au point prévu à environ 3 miles et est revenu vers le point de ravitaillement. À l'approche du point, la lumière de la pompe de carburant s'est illuminée. Le pilote a effectué un atterrissage d'urgence sur un chemin à proximité. Au moment de l'arrondi, la béquille de queue a touché la surface du chemin et les patins se sont enfoncés dans la surface meuble du chemin. L'arrêt soudain a créé un basculement vers l'avant et ensuite vers l'arrière déformant le revêtement de la poutre de queue. Une inspection sommaire n'a pas révélé de dommages aux patins du train principal, aucune pale (rotor principal, ni queue) n'a percuté le sol. Une inspection plus approfondie sera effectuée. La radio balise de détresse s'est déclenchée mais le pilote n'a pas été blessé.

C-ILPT, a privately registered advanced Ultralight was taking off from Runway 30 at Wetaskiwin Regional Aerodrome (CEX3), AB when the aircraft experienced an engine (Rotax 582) failure as it was turning crosswind at approximately 450 feet above ground. The pilot attempted one restart and then set up a glide into a field of unharvested canola. On touchdown the aircraft flipped forward and came to rest on its back in the canola. There were no injuries and there was no fire. There was no ELT onboard.

C-GKQH, a De Havilland DHC-8-402 operating as Porter Airlines flight POE2484, on route from Montreal Pierre Elliott Trudeau International-Airport, QC (CYUL), to Toronto Billy Bishop, ON (CYTZ) declared an emergency due to a cargo door indication. The flight crew carried out the QRH procedures and elected to divert to Ottawa Macdonald–Cartier International Airport, ON (CYOW). While descending through 4500 feet there was a bang in the back of the aircraft and the remaining cabin pressure dropped rapidly. The aircraft landed without further incident, stopped on the runway and was inspected by aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF). ARFF found the baggage door handle had popped out.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and found the door handle out, but no mechanical deficiencies were found. The door handle and a blowout panel were re-secured and a pressurization run was conducted with no issues. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GUBO, an Air Transat A330-343 was operating flight TSC434 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Marseille Provence Airport (LFML), France. Approximately two hours prior to arrival at destination, a cabin crew member became incapacitated. The emergency positions and safety responsibilities were reassigned to the remaining crew and the flight continued without further incident.

C-FPWE, an Air Canada A320 was operating flight AC566 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA. On approach, the flight crew received a TCAS RA. The RA was followed and a missed approach was conducted. The second approach was uneventful and the flight landed without further incident.

C-GMWT, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 operated by Goldcorp Canada Ltd. operating as flight WSG88, departed Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT), ON for Opapimiskan Lake Aerodrome (CKM8), ON. While on approach into CKM8 the flight crew selected gear down and observed illumination of the #2 Standby Power Unit light. The crew declared an emergency and returned to CYQT. The aircraft landed safely in CYQT with aircraft rescue and fire fighting on standby. The operator's maintenance found that the #2 standby power unit and drain was leaking. The #2 standby power unit was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GDJL, a privately registered Cirrus SR22 G2, was conducting a VFR flight from Edmonton/Villeneuve Airport (CZVL), Alberta to the Westlock Aerodrome (CES4), Alberta with the pilot and 2 passengers on board. The aircraft departed CZVL and flew northbound for a short time. The pilot decided to return to the airport and as a result of deteriorating weather, the pilot could not complete a visual approach to the airport. After maneuvering in the vicinity of the airport for some time, the pilot activated the Cirrus airframe parachute system (CAPS). The aircraft came to rest in brush 1.4 nm SW of the airport. There were no injuries; the 406 MHz ELT activated.

C-FGAJ, a Boeing 767-223 operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd., was conducting flight CJT917 from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB.
