The aircraft started a descent 100 nm northwest of Winnipeg from FL410. Through approximately FL370, the flight crew received a "FWD EQT OVHT" EICAS message followed by a "OVHT" caution light. The first officer was flying and called for the QRH. At the same time, the flight crew noticed the cabin pressurization rate was climbing at 1000 to 1500 feet per minute, followed by a CABIN ALTITUDE warning. The captain called for the cabin altitude warning memory actions and both crew members donned their oxygen masks and established communications. The captain took control and instructed the First officer to complete the drill and checklist. CJT917 declared a MAYDAY and continued the emergency descent to 9000 feet ASL. When the cabin altitude was below 10 000 feet, the flight crew removed their oxygen masks. The aircraft subsequently landed safety in CYWG. The operator's maintenance identified that the equipment cooling fan had malfunctioned. The operator's maintenance followed a MEL procedure that locks the equipment cooling valve in the closed position and a ground pressurization check was completed and tested serviceable. The aircraft will be ferried to a maintenance facility for further troubleshooting and repairs.

C-GLYX, a Boeing 737 Max 8 operated by Lynx Air, was conducting flight DAT2042, a positioning flight from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, with 6 crew members on board. Upon reaching cruise altitude, the flight crew noticed a fuel imbalance. There was no sign of a leak, as the total quantity was correct, and the fuel flows were indicating normal. The crew attempted a fuel balancing procedure, but the imbalance continued to worsen, so they discontinued the procedure. The crew requested priority with YYZ Centre and asked to have ARFF standing by for their landing. Shortly before landing, the flight crew noticed that the fuel cross feed valve was open, and had likely been open for the entire flight. They closed the cross feed valve and the flight landed uneventfully on runway 23, aircraft rescue and fire fighting inspected the aircraft and no leaks were noted, and the aircraft taxied to the gate. Fuel balancing was completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKQP, an Embraer E190-400 operated by Porter Airlines Canada Ltd. was conducting flight POE237 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to St. John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL with 5 crew and 55 passengers on board. During the cruise portion of the flight, an updraft and moderate turbulence was encountered from convective activity below. This resulted in a loss of 1000 feet from the cleared altitude and exceedance of the maximum cabin altitude. When the crew recovered, the aircraft exceeded Vmo by approximately 6 knots. The aircraft continued to destination without further incident and reported no injuries.

C-FGEL, a privately registered Murphy Rebel on floats, was preparing to conduct a takeoff from Long Gull Pond, approximately 4nm ENE of Stephenville Airport (CYJT) NL with 3 persons onboard. While maneuvering on the water, just prior to take-off, the left Full Lotus inflatable float deflated, filled with water and the aircraft rolled and became inverted in the water. The occupants onboard were able to egress the aircraft and clung to the floats and were later rescued by RCMP. There were no injuries.

N589FE, a Federal Express Corporation McDonnell Douglas MD-11F, was conducting a flight from Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (KSEA), USA, to Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport (PANC), USA, with 2 flight crew onboard. During cruise, the crew received a HYD 3 ELEV OFF alert followed by a decrease in the hydraulic fluid quantity in the No. 3 hydraulic system. The crew declared an emergency and opted to return to KSEA. The crew attempted a normal gear extension without success and consulted the quick reference handbook (QRH). The crew performed an alternate gear extension and landed at KSEA without further incident. The aircraft was towed into the ramp from Taxiway Alpha. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft. Maintenance retorqued the hydraulic B-nut, replaced both engine driven hydraulic pumps, and replaced 4 hydraulic manifold filters.

On 26 September 2023, the Buchanan & Son Aviation Limited Bell 206L (LongRanger) helicopter (registration C-FHKJ, serial number 45116) was travelling on a forestry survey flight originating from a private property 27 nautical miles east of the Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC, during daylight hours, with the pilot and 5 silviculturists on board. Shortly after departure, at 0735 Pacific Daylight Time, approximately 100 feet above ground level, the helicopter began spinning, lost altitude, and collided with trees. The pilot and passenger, located in the front 2 seats of the helicopter, were fatally injured. The remaining 4 passengers all received minor injuries. The helicopter was substantially damaged. There was a post-impact fire located near the engine exhaust which was extinguished by one of the passengers using the aircraft's fire extinguisher. There were no dangerous goods on board. The 406-megahertz emergency locator transmitter activated however the antennae was damaged in the accident sequence and the signal was not received by the Cospas-Sarsat search and rescue satellite system.The TSB deployed investigators and the investigation is ongoing.

C-FQMV, a privately registered Cessna 210, was landing at a private aerodrome near Morris, MB. The aircraft landed hard and short of the runway with the nose gear contacting first. The nose landing gear fork broke and the propeller contacted the ground. There were no reported injuries to the 1 occupant on board.

C-GDPG, a Bombardier BD-700-1A11 (Global 5000) aircraft operated by I.M.P. Group Limited, was conducting a flight from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC. C-FPCX, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Beech 1900C aircraft was operating a flight from CYVR to Trail (CAD4), BC. A loss of separation occurred when C-GDPG deviated from the assigned Fraser Seven Departure route and C-FPCX departed behind C-GDPG on the Vancouver Two Departure. Separation was reduced to 2.5 miles horizontally and 800 feet vertically where 3 miles horizontally and 1000 feet vertically is required.

C-FGMH, a privately registered Lake Amphibian A-4 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Canyon Lake (56° 16’ N, 128° 10’ W), BC to Quesnel Airport (CYQZ), BC, with only the pilot on board. When landing on Runway 13, the aircraft touched down hard, and the left main landing gear collapsed. The aircraft departed the runway to the left and came to a rest in the grass, approximately 200 feet from the runway. There were no injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.The aircraft has been disassembled and recovered to a maintenance facility for repair.

C-FSFS, a Cessna Citation C25A aircraft operated by Airsprint Incorporated, was conducting a flight from Santa Barbara (KSBA), California to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC. N833NN, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting a flight from Dallas Fort Worth International (KDFW), Texas to CYVR. On approach, C-FSFS deviated from the course which resulted in a loss of separation with N833NN. The required separation was 3.0 miles laterally or 1000 feet vertically; at the aircraft`s closest point, the separation was reduced to 2.4 miles laterally and 600 feet vertically. Both aircraft landed without incident.

C-GKHI, a Beech King Air 200 operated by Transwest Air (dba as Rise Air), was conducting flight RS240 from North Battleford Airport (CYQW), SK to La Ronge/Barber Field Airport (CYVC), SK. While in the descent to CYVC, the flight crew observed left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-42) torque anomalies. The flight crew conducted the quick reference handbook procedure and performed a precautionary engine shutdown. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft landed in CYVC without further event with aircraft rescue and fire fighting vehicles waiting.

N422DZ, an Airbus A330-900 aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL291 from Paris/Charles de Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France to Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), USA. While enroute to KLAX, one of the flight crew became medically incapacitated. The ailing pilot was moved to the cabin for care and the duties of the incapacitated pilot were assumed by the pilot that was on crew rest. The flight crew declared an emergency and diverted the flight to Minneapolis-Saint Paul International/Wold-Chamberlain Airport (KMSP), USA. The aircraft landed without incident and the pilot was transported to hospital for examination.

C-FIML, a private Cessna 310Q, was conducting a flight from Ottawa/Carp Airport (CYRP), ON, to Kingston/Norman Rogers Airport (CYGK), ON, with 2 people on board. Shortly after takeoff, when the pilot retracted the landing gear, he heard a loud popping sound from the nose of the aircraft and observed a gear unsafe indication. A visual check in the nacelle mirror indicated that the nose gear was still partially extended. After cycling the landing gear and conducting other troubleshooting, the issue was not resolved. The pilot declared an emergency with the Ottawa Terminal controller and requested a tower fly-by to verify the gear position, during which it was confirmed that the nosewheel was partially retracted with the main gear appearing to be down and locked. The pilot decided to circle near the Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, while burning off fuel, and with 20 gallons of fuel remaining he requested an approach at CYOW. He was cleared for a visual approach to runway 14, where Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting would be standing by for the landing. The nose gear fully collapsed upon touchdown, and both propellers were still spinning when they struck the runway, despite the engines having been shut down on short final. Both occupants exited the aircraft and were uninjured. The underside of the forward fuselage, and propellers were damaged due to contact with the runway. The cause of the gear failure has not yet been determined.

C-GAEB, a float-equipped de Havilland DHC-2 MK1 operated by Elk Island Air, was conducting a flight from Rurke Lake, MB to Red Sucker Lake (CKT4), MB with 1 pilot on board. During the descent through 600 feet AGL for a final approach to CKT4, the pilot observed that the engine (Pratt & Whitney USA R-985-AN-14B) was running roughly. Moments later, 2 loud bangs were heard and the engine quit operating. The pilot conducted a forced approach and landed in a beaver pond located 2.7 nautical miles north-northeast of CYRS. The aircraft overran the pond and the aircraft sustained damage to a float. There were no reported injuries and no post-impact fire. The pilot was able to communicate the situation via radio with another aircraft in the area and was subsequently airlifted by a local helicopter operator.

C-GLDE, an ATR 42-320 operated by Transwest Air (dba Rise Air), was conducting flight RS424 from Prince Albert/Glass Field Airport (CYPA), SK to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), SK. During the takeoff from CYPA, the aircraft experienced an aggressive yaw to left at 90 knots. Control of the aircraft was maintained, and the aircraft rotated at 94 knots. The crew elected to keep the landing gear extended; suspecting the yaw was caused by a blown tire. The aircraft returned to CYPA and conducted a fly-by to determine the tire condition. Ground to air visual inspection determined that there was no visible damage to the tire. The gear was left extended, and the decision was made to continue the flight to CYXE. A PAN PAN was declared, and aircraft rescue and fire fighting were on standby for the uneventful landing in CYXE. The aircraft then taxied to apron without issue.The operator's maintenance conducted various tests and no issues with the aircraft was identified. The aircraft was returned to service and it has been reported the issue has not reoccurred.

C-GYDQ, an Beech King Air 200 aircraft operated by Transwest Air (dba as Rise Air) as flight RS220, was preparing to taxi to the runway in Fond-Du-Lac Airport (CZFD), SK for Wollaston Lake Airport (CZWL), SK with two flight crew and two passengers on board. Shortly after start-up, the flight crew could smell electrical smoke in the cabin. The crew shutdown the engine and observed smoke coming from under the floors. The aircraft occupants deplaned uneventfully. The operator's maintenance found a defective flap motor and the aircraft was ferried to a maintenance base for service.

C-FSES, un Boeing 737M exploité par exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA913, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis Keflavik International en Islande (BIKF) à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Alors qu’il était en approche finale pour la piste 06R une perte d’espacement est survenue lorsqu’il s’est retrouvé 2,4 miles marins derrière N875RM un GL7T (Global 7000) en approche finale sur la piste 06R et qui avait réduit sa vitesse. L’espacement requis était de 3 nm. Les 2 aéronefs se sont posés sans encombre.

C-GCPU, a privately registered Cessna 150M, was conducting circuits at the Stoney Point (Le Cunff) Aerodrome (CRML), ON. The pilot was the sole occupant of the aircraft. During landing on runway 19, a wind shift was encountered, and the aircraft touched down hard on the runway and became airborne again. The pilot had difficulty controlling the aircraft, and on the ensuing landing it veered to the right into a ditch beside the runway. The nose wheel collapsed resulting in a propeller strike, and the aircraft came to rest on its nose. The pilot was not injured.

C-GBLR, un Cessna 152 exploité par Cargair Ltee effectuait un vol d’entrainement selon les règles de vol à vue à partir de l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec 1 élève-pilote à bord. Alors que l’avion se trouvait à environ 3 miles marins au nord de CYHU en palier à 1100 pieds au-dessus du niveau de la mer (ASL), le moteur (Lycoming O-235-L2C) s’est vidé de son huile et s’est arrêté brusquement. Un atterrissage forcé en bordure de l’autoroute 20 a été effectué et l’avion a culbuté dans le fossé. L’élève-pilote n’a subi aucune blessure, l’avion a subi des dommages importants. La radiobalise de détresse (ELT) s’est déclenchée et a été captée par le système d’aide à la recherche et au sauvetage par satellite (SARSAT).

C-GJNZ, un CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7912, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Bagotville, QC (CYBG). Après le décollage l’équipage a reçu un message d'alarme indiquant un problème avec le gouvernail de profondeur. Un état d’urgence a été déclaré, l’équipage a effectué un retour à CYUL et l’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 06R sans encombre.

C-GJLN, un Challenger 604 exploité par Aviation Jolina SEC, effectuait un vol de l'Aéroport International Montréal-Trudeau (CYUL), QC à destination de l'Aéroport International de Nashville (KBNA), TN. L'aéronef était en croisière au niveau de vol 400, quand l'équipage a remarqué une baisse ainsi qu'une fluctuation de la pression d'huile sur le moteur de gauche. L'équipage a ensuite suivi les étapes de la liste de controle ''checklist'' du Quick Reference Handbook 2. Suggéré par le QRH, ils ont ensuite descendu au niveau de vol 29000 et réduit la puissance du moteur de gauche au minimum (idle). La pression ne ce stabilisait toujours pas, ils ont donc continué la descente jusqu'à 12000'. Par précaution, l'équipage de vol a ensuite déclaré un Pan Pan avec le centre de contrôle de Nashville puisque qu'ils n'étaient pas en mesure de stabiliser la pression durant la descente avec le moteur #1 au régime minimum. Les contrôleurs aériens de Nashville ont pris l'aéronef en charges et les ont dirigé pour une approches visuelle sur la piste 02R. L'approche a été effectué selon la checklist d'atterrisage sur un moteur et sans ambûches.

C-GWGA, un Beech 1900D exploité par Sky Jet M.G. Inc sous l’indicatif LSJ641, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de La Romaine, QC (CTT5) à destination de Natashquan, QC (CYNA) avec 9 passagers et 2 membres d’équipage. Après avoir sélectionné la sortie du train d’atterrissage en approche pour la piste 32 à CYNA, l’équipage a entendu le mouvement du train, mais il n’y a pas eu d’indication que le train était sorti et verrouillé. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification d’urgence pour la sortie manuelle du train d’atterrissage, mais l’indicateur de position des roues ne confirmait toujours pas que toutes les roues étaient sorties. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a effectué une diversion à destination de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV). Avant d’arriver à CYZV, une vérification des disjoncteurs du côté droit a révélé que celui de l’indication du train d’atterrissage était sorti. L’équipage l’a réenclenché et l’indication de la position des roues est revenue à la normale. L’équipage a avisé qu’il n’y avait plus de situation d’urgence et l’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 09 sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GSBA, a Sealand Aviation Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-2 (Beaver) was conducting a local flight under visual flight rules from Campbell River Airport (CYBL), BC, with two pilots on board. After conducting a stall exercise in the landing configuration, the throttle was increased, however, the aircraft engine (Raikhlin Aircraft Engine Developments GmbH, RED A03-005) responded abnormally to the input. The thrust generated by the engine and propeller system was insufficient to maintain altitude, and a forced landing was initiated. The target touchdown point could not be reached, and the aircraft collided with terrain in a heavily forested area. At 1032 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) a MAYDAY was declared by the crew, and an Emergency Locator Transmitter (ELT) activation occurred at 1034 PDT. When the airplane came to rest, the crew were able to egress without assistance. Search and rescue services deployed a helicopter from Comox Airport (CYQQ), BC, and the two crew members were recovered by search and rescue personnel and taken to a local hospital. The two crew members sustained minor injuries. The aircraft was significantly damaged. There was no post-crash fire.

C-FTJJ, un Twin Otter (DHC-6) exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE113 venait d’effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Poste Montagnais, QC (CSF3) à destination de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) avec 1 passager et 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Une fois stationnée et après avoir fermée les moteurs, la pompe hydraulique fonctionnait encore continuellement. Lorsque le personnel de la maintenance a ouvert le compartiment hydraulique, il a constaté la présence de fumée. Par mesure de précaution, l’équipage a demandé de faire venir les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). Après une vérification avec les SLIA, il a été déterminé qu’il n’y avait plus de risque d’incendie. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni de dommage à l’appareil.

C-FZXM, a Piper PA-23 (Apache) operated by St. Thomas Flight Centre Ltd., was on a training flight at the St. Thomas Municipal Airport (CYQS), ON, with an instructor and student on board. After departure from runway 27 the landing gear had been selected up. The instructor noted that the nose gear was not indicating up, and he could see in the mirror on the cowling that the nosewheel had not fully retracted. After cycling the gear and troubleshooting without rectifying the issue, the landing gear was extended, the indicator showed that it was down and locked. During the landing on runway 27, the nosewheel collapsed immediately as it touched the runway. The aircraft yawed abruptly to the left and exited the side of the runway, coming to rest in an adjacent bean field. Both pilots exited the aircraft without injury. Both propellers had made contact with the runway, and the nose of the aircraft was damaged.

C-GDIL, an Aurora Jet Partners Challenger 350 was operating flight 27642 from San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA to Van Nuys Airport (KVNY), CA. The aircraft was cleared for the ILS Z runway 16 right descending on the glideslope when ATC advised of unidentified traffic at their 11 o'clock 3 miles about 1000 feet below. The crew had the target on TCAS but not visual. Then, the other aircraft started a climb, and the crew received a TCAS RA to climb and followed the RA and ATC told the crew to level at 5000 feet turn right heading 250. The crew saw the small single engine plane pass on the left side about 300 feet below. The passengers were advised of the situation and the aircraft was vectored around for another approach to land.

C-GQWJ, a Boeing 737-700 operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA476 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, with 5 crew and 137 passengers on board. During the initial approach to CYYZ, the flight crew received an indication that the hydraulic system B had failed. The approach was abandoned, and the crew requested to hold while they conducted troubleshooting. Before requesting a second approach, the crew declared PAN PAN. They arrived on runway 06R with Aircraft Rescue Fire Fighting standing by. Due to a significant amount of hydraulic fluid leaking from the aircraft near the RH engine, the aircraft was towed from the runway and passengers were deplaned. Initial maintenance examination indicates that the RH engine driven hydraulic pump had failed.

N786UA, a Boeing 777-200ER aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL510 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), US to Leonardo da Vinci-Fiumicino Airport International, Rome (LIRF), Italy. During cruise, the crew observed a cabin altitude warning annunciation on the EICAS display. The crew completed the checklist and performed an emergency descent. The aircraft descended to 9,000 ft and entered a hold while running checks to determine the next course of action. The crew declared an emergency and decided to return to KEWR where they landed without further issue.Maintenance found ice in the ground air connection. The ground air connection duct valve was also found to be broken, not seated. The ground air check valve and associated gasket were replaced, checks were completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FMXB, a Thrush S2R-H80 aircraft operated by Agmax Ltd., was performing an aerial application flight 5.5 nm NE of Minnedosa (CJU5), MB, near the community of Polonia, MB. During a low pass, the aircraft inadvertently touched the crop. The landing gear was damaged and the aircraft belly landed onto the ground in an upright position in the field. The pilot was not injured. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the landing gear, lower fuselage, engine, and propeller.UPDATED 25 September 2023

C-FIAI un Dash-8-314 (DH8C) exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE803 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Umiujaq, QC (CYMU) à destination de Kuujjuarapik, QC (CYGW) avec 32 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de l’approche, l’équipage a sélectionné la sortie du train d’atterrissage et une indication anormale est survenue. L’équipage a fait une remontée et a effectué un circuit d’attente pour compléter liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour la sortie manuelle du train d’atterrissage. Lorsqu’il a été confirmé que le train était sorti et verrouillé, l’équipage a effectué un atterrissage à CYGW sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-FSNM, a privately owned Cessna 182Q, operating from a privately owned airstrip near Douglas, Ontario, experienced a hard landing, causing the nose wheel to break away. The aircraft nose gear dug into the ground causing the aircraft to flip over on its back. The two occupants received minor injuries and were both transported to a local hospital. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FAXD, a Sunwing B737 Max 8 was operating flight SWG2974 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to La Aurora International Airport (MGGT), Guatemala. On the ILS approach, the crew received a TCAS TA followed by a RA to descend at about 500ft above the airport elevation however more than 1000ft on the radar altimeter. The crew decided to continue the ILS approach since the traffic was in sight and their proximity to the ground. The flight landed without further incident.

C-FBWI, a WestJet B737-800 was operating flight WJA2315 from Cancun International Airport (MMUN), Mexico to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During cruise, the crew declared an emergency due to a water leak and elected to divert to George Bush Intercontinental/Houston Airport (KIAH), TX. The aircraft circled west of KIAH then landed safely without further incident.

C-GAKI (s/n 8100), an Alkan Air Ltd. Dornier 228 was on a visual flight rules flight from the Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen International Airport (CYXY), YT to the Watson Lake Airport (CYQH), YT. Approximately 5 minutes after levelling off at the cruise altitude of 11 000 feet above sea level (ASL), the #1 engine oil pressure light illuminated along with the master caution. The flight crew checked the oil pressure gauge, which indicated low oil pressure on engine #1. The flight crew observed oil was present on the exterior of the aircraft around the engine cowling area. The flight crew shut down the #1 engine (GARRETT TPE331-5), briefed the passengers, and returned for a single-engine approach and landing at CYXY without further incident. No emergency was declared. Following the occurrence, maintenance personnel discovered that the #1 engine oil cooler was cracked which resulted in the oil leak.

C-FNEH, a privately registered Cessna 140, registration C-FNEH, collided with two parked aircraft at Ottawa/Rockcliffe Airport (CYRO), ON, while attempting to takeoff from a taxiway. An individual was in the process of stealing the aircraft. As a result of the collision, the emergency locator transmitter (ELT) activated. The Rockcliffe Flying Club reported the occurrence to the Ottawa Police Services who responded with EMS. The sole occupant received minor injuries, was taken into custody and transported to a local hospital. There was extensive damage to the nose and left wing. The ELT activated.

C-GDKO, an Air Tractor AT-402B operated by Western Canadian Aerial, was conducting an aerial application flight from Gilbert Plains Airport (CJH2), MB. While on an application pass approximately 10nm to the northeast of CJH2, the aircraft's landing gear collided with a power line. The wire cutters on the gear legs severed the line. The pilot stopped spraying and returned uneventfully to CJH2. The pilot was uninjured. The aircraft sustained minor damage, limited to spray nozzles and the pump fan blades.

C-FYJD, a Sunwing B737-800 was operating flight TOM5248 from Norwich Airport (EGSH), UK to Palma de Mallorca Airport (LEPA), Spain. During descent to LEPA, TOM5248 was cleared to descend to FL220 and expedite the descent through FL230. When at FL230, the crew received a TCAS TA for traffic below and to the right, immediately followed by a TCAS RA with a command to level off. The crew levelled off and the TCAS RA subsided. The flight continued the descent as per clearance and advised Barcelona ATC of the alert.

C-GJTX, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1622 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL. During the descent phase of flight, passing through 12,000ft ASL, ATC instructed the crew to stop descent and the crew received a radar vector for traffic in reference to an uncontrolled military P8 aircraft 500ft below. The crew subsequently complied with a TCAS RA. ATC was advised and the flight was completed without further incident.

C-GJTX, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1628 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL. During the climb to cruise phase of flight, passing through FL280 to a cleared altitude of FL300, in the vicinity of Erie International Airport (KERI), PA, the crew received, and complied with, a TCAS RA: LEVEL OFF. The conflicting traffic was at level FL310. The ATC was advised, and the flight was subsequently completed without further incident.

C-GNCS, a Buffalo Airways Ltd. Canadair CL-215 (serial 1008) was departing Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), Northwest Territories on a local fire-fighting mission. On board were 2 pilots. After lining up for departure on Runway 28, the pilots carried out the remaining pre-takeoff checklist items. During that time, the engine RPM on the left-hand engine slowly began decreasing. The reduction of engine RPM on the left-hand engine went undetected until the engine stopped due to flooding. The crew of TKR291 then taxied off the runway and back to the company hangar. The engine was restarted, and the flight was completed without further incident. There was no damage and no injuries.

N583FX, un Challenger 350 exploité par Flexjet LLC sous l'indicatif LXJ583 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Dallas Love Field, Texas (KDAL) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). En rapprochement pour CYUL, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence au contrôleur aérien en raison d’un problème avec le train d’atterrissage. Les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d’aéronefs (SLIA) ont été avisés et des véhicules d’urgence ont été déployés. L’aéronef a atterri sans encombre sur la piste 06L. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GJOX, a Cessna 172S aircraft registered to Harv's Air Service, departed Steinbach/Steinbach South (CKK7), MB, on a VFR rental flight. While attempting to land in a mowed field one mile north of Stratton, ON, the aircraft touched down briefly and the pilot then initiated an overshoot. During the initial climb, the aircraft became uncontrollable, descended into power lines, and collided with terrain. The aircraft came to rest inverted. The three occupants were not injured. The aircraft was destroyed. It was reported that tailwinds were present at the time of the attempted landing.

C-GVWA, a WestJet B737-800 was operating flight WJA2702 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Sangster International Airport (MKJS), Montego Bay, Jamaica. During the flight, a cabin crew member became ill due to a personal medical event. The Cabin crew member was unable to perform their assigned duties and was not in their assigned jumpseat for landing. These duties were reassigned to the remaining cabin crew members. Medics were required upon arrival.

C-FOFV, a privately registered Cessna 180E, was conducting a ferry flight from Quesnel Airport (CYQZ), BC, to Calgary/Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB, with only the pilot onboard. The right wheel was out of alignment after a change from floats to tundra tires. The pilot inquired about the availability of a grass strip, and was informed by the tower that there is no designated grass strip at CYBW. The pilot did not declare an emergency and subsequently landed on Runway 35. During the landing roll, the pilot lost control of the aircraft and the aircraft flipped over on the runway. The pilot was uninjured and egressed from the overturned airplane. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GHLV, an Air Canada B767-300 was operating flight AC7222 from Halifax Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS to Liège Airport (EBLG), Belgium. During cruise, the flight crew received an Indicated Airspeed (IAS) disagree message followed by multiple other EICAS messages. The crew conducted the associated QRH checklists and were unable to pinpoint the fault. In discussion with MOC and Dispatch, the decision was made to divert to Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK and declare a Mayday. The aircraft landed in EGLL and cleared to taxi without further incident.

C-FANF, an Air North Ltd. Boeing 737-500, was being operated as flight ANT772 from Erik Nielsen Whitehorse International Airport (CYXY), YT to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. On approach, approximately 5nm from landing, the aircraft experienced a total hydraulic pressure loss on system "A". After landing in CYEG the aircraft became disabled on the runway and could not taxi to the gate. A tug was sent out to tow the aircraft to the gate. An emergency was not declared, but emergency vehicles followed the aircraft in tow as a precaution.Company maintenance determined that the #1 ground spoiler actuator cracked, resulting in the loss of the "A" hydraulic system. The actuator was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FYMK, a Cessna 208B operated by Superior Airways, was conducting a VFR flight from Red Lake (CYRL), ON to Pikangikum (CYPM), ON with 1 pilot and 6 passengers onboard. During the flare for landing on Runway 27 at CYPM, the aircraft entered fog and landed long. The aircraft experienced a runway excursion when it rolled off the end of Runway 27. The aircraft sustained damage to its propeller. There were no injuries. The ELT did not activate.

C-FRWA, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Westjet Airlines Limited, was conducting flight WJA360 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB, with 6 crew and 115 passengers on board. Approximately 30 minutes after departure a cabin crew member became incapacitated due to illness. The duties of the ill crew member were distributed among the other cabin crew members. The crew member could not occupy their assigned jump seat for landing. The aircraft landed without further issues. EMS met the aircraft at the gate and the ill crew member received medical attention.

C-FPWE, an Air Canada Airbus A320 was being operated as flight ACA0242 from Vancouver (CYVR), BC to Edmonton (CYEG), AB. While exiting the runway in CYEG, the crew received an ECAM message "Avionic Smoke". The quick reference handbook (QRH) check was completed, and the smoke couldn't be detected. A PAN PAN was declared, and emergency vehicles met the aircraft for inspection. No fire or smoke could be detected. The aircraft was cleared to the gate without further incident.Following the flight, the maintenance team carried out inspections and could not find any signs of smoke or overheat issues. The forward smoke detector was found faulty and replaced. The skin air outlet valve and AEVC computer were replaced as well. The aircraft was released back into service.

C-FEFN, an Edmonton Flying Club (EFC) Cessna 172S, was being operated on a student pilot's first solo flight at Edmonton Parkland Airport (CPL6), AB. During the flare for landing the aircraft ballooned and was corrected by pitching forward. The nose landing gear contacted the runway first, followed by 3 bounces. The aircraft remained on the runway and once at taxi speed the student pilot taxied the aircraft to the EFC ramp. Following the flight, it was noted that the propeller had contacted the runway, the nose wheel and firewall were bent, there was some damage to the fuselage skin, and the control yoke was jammed in the full aft position. The pilot was not injured.

C-GASB, a de Havilland DHC-8-102 aircraft operated by Summit Air, was conducting a flight from Lansdowne House Airport (CYLH), ON to Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON. During the descent into CYQT, the flight crew observed a pitch trim error annunciation on the Automatic Flight Control System (AFCS). The autopilot was disconnected to manually re-trim the aircraft. While manually re-trimming to the nose down position, the trim wheel stopped turning when the trim travel was about halfway. The flight crew actioned the QRH checklist and reported that they still had full control of the elevator and could trim to a nose up position. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft subsequently landed in CYQT uneventfully.The operator's maintenance identified that the PRC on panels 332AT and 334AT had deteriorated, allowing for water to ingress the trim actuator. The trim actuator was purged and lubricated, the panels were resealed and reinstalled, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GHQL, un DHC-8-402 exploité par Hydro-Québec sous l'indicatif HYD106, effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Bagotville, QC (CYBG) à destination de Quaqtaq, QC (CYAH). Environ à 90 milles nautiques au nord de CYBG au niveau de vol de 25 000 pieds, l’équipage a perdu l’affichage primaire des indications d’attitude et de direction. L’équipage a utilisé la source secondaire pour lire les indications et a suivi les procédures établies pour gérer la panne. Il a ensuite communiqué avec le service de maintenance et le répartiteur. Le contrôleur aérien de l’ACC de Montréal a été avisé de la situation par l’équipage, qu’un retour à CYBG était demandé et qu’une urgence était déclarée sans qu’aucun service d’urgence au sol ne soit requis. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre à CYBG.

C-FEAI, un Dash-8-314 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE803 effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Kuujjuarapik (CYGW), QC à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC. Une fois prêt pour le départ, l’équipage a avancé les manettes de contrôle des gaz des 2 moteurs à la position « puissance de décollage ». Le commandant de bord a aussitôt entendu un son anormal provenant du côté droit de l’aéronef et a observé qu’une lumière d’avertissement de température élevée d’un des moteurs était allumée. L’équipage a immédiatement arrêté la course au décollage. Une fois l’aéronef immobilisé, le commandant de bord a coupé l’alimentation en carburant du moteur #2 par mesure de précaution. L’aéronef a circulé au sol jusqu’au tablier principal où les passagers ont pu débarquer. L’aéronef a été retiré du service de vol temporairement pour qu’il soit inspecté par le service de maintenance de la compagnie.

C-GFFZ, a Cessna 172P operated by the Brampton Flying Club, was on a local flight with an instructor and two passengers on board. As the aircraft was returning to Brampton-Caledon Airport (CNC3), ON, the engine experienced a complete loss of power (Lycoming O-320-D2J). The instructor declared a MAYDAY and initially attempted a forced landing on a road. However, upon noticing approaching traffic, the decision was made to divert to a nearby hayfield for a safer landing. During the landing roll, the aircraft impacted a cluster of trees at the field boundary. All three occupants successfully evacuated the aircraft, although both passengers sustained minor injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage; notably, there was no fire despite some compromise to the integrity of the fuel tanks. The Emergency Locator Transmitter (ELT) was activated and subsequently deactivated by rescuers.

C-GTAA, a privately registered Cessna A185F amphibious aircraft, was conducting a round-robin VFR flight from Winnipeg/St. Andrews Airport (CYAV), MB. During the flight, the pilot conducted touch and go landings at Forbes Lake, MB. On the second landing, the aircraft yawed to the left then to the right at touchdown. The pilot attempted to correct the yaw; however, the right wing contacted the water. The aircraft remained upright, and the pilot was able to taxi the aircraft to shore. The pilot then relayed to an over-flying aircraft his situation and requested a relay for assistance. The pilot was not injured. The aircraft's right wing was substantially damaged.

C-GITR, an Airbus A319-112 aircraft operated by Air Canada Rouge LP, was conducting flight ROU1921 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International (CYYZ), ON to Regina International (CYQR), SK. While on the initial approach to runway 31 at CYQR, the flight crew received a FLAP FAULT ECAM. The approach was discontinued. The flight crew then carried out the ECAM actions which did not rectify the fault. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft returned to CYQR. The aircraft landed uneventfully with its flaps in the up position on Runway 31 with Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) on standby and then taxied to the gate.

C-FGAV, a Bell 407 helicopter operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd, was conducting an external load flight from a camp located approximately 20nm northeast of Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU. The external load (a tent floor) was lifted and when the helicopter was at approximately 200 feet AGL and at an airspeed of 10-20 knots, the external load was flying erratically. The pilot intentionally released the long line and the load fell to the ground in an open area away from the ground crew. The pilot then landed the helicopter and shut down without further incident. The operator inspected the long line and cargo hook, and no anomalies or damage were noted.

C-GQOA, a South Nahanni Aviation Services Inc. Cessna U206G was operating from Fort Simpson Island Aerodrome (CET4), NT to Wrigley Aerodrome (CYWY), NT. While in cruise, approximately 10 minutes after leveling off at 4500 feet ASL, the engine (Teledyne Continental 10-520-F) began to vibrate strongly, and smoke entered the cabin. The pilot turned toward a highway located 15 NM South and declared an emergency on 126.7 MHz with intentions to land on the highway. The distress call was answered by two other aircraft in the area. The pilot reduced engine power and observed oil coming over the cowling and onto the windscreen. Moments later the engine began to lose power. The pilot acknowledged that landing on the road would not be possible and conducted a forced approach and landing along a cut line. Upon touchdown, due to soft terrain, the aircraft nosed over, came to rest inverted and the ELT activated. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured and had no issues egressing the aircraft. The pilot was picked up by a local helicopter approximately 30 minutes following the incident. Company maintenance will report to the TSB regarding maintenance findings and follow-up.

C-GSUI, a North Cariboo Flying Service Ltd BAE RJ-100, was operating as flight NCB6064 from Hay River Merlyn Carter Airport (CYHY), NT to Prince Albert Glass Field Airport (CYPA), SK. During the initial climb from CYHY the aircraft's no. 4 engine (Avco Lycoming, LF-507-1F) began to vibrate and over-temp. The crew conducted a precautionary engine shutdown and discharged the fire bottles. An emergency was declared, and the flight diverted to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT. The flight landed safely without further incident.

C-GYCS, a Diamond Aircraft Industries Inc. DA 40 aircraft operated by Genesis Flight College, was in the process of landing at Kincardine Aerodrome (CYKM), ON with the pilot and three passengers on board. The wind conditions were reported as 12 knots from 330 degrees, and the aircraft was using Runway 31. During the touchdown, a gust of wind caused the aircraft to become airborne momentarily, resulting in a hard landing on the runway. The pilot aborted the landing and executed a go-around. Subsequently, a second circuit was completed, where the aircraft landed without further incident. Initial assessments of the aircraft revealed damage to the propeller and engine. However, upon transporting the aircraft to the operator's primary maintenance facility, further examination revealed additional damage to several components within the nose landing gear.

C-GJZF, a Jazz Aviation LP Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft was conducting a test flight JZA7190 at Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON following the replacement of a spoiler cable due to a previous defect. On board were the two flight crewmembers and two maintenance personnel. During the approach to Runway 24L, the landing gear was extended, and the flight crew received an unsafe indication for the Left Main Landing Gear. In response, the crew aborted the approach and initiated a climb to 5000 feet above sea level (ASL). They then followed the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) procedures and declared a PAN PAN emergency with Air Traffic Control (ATC).Despite completing the QRH procedures, the unsafe landing gear indication persisted. The flight crew made the decision to execute a landing with the landing gear in the unsafe condition, in accordance with the QRH. This procedure also required shutting down the number one engine. The aircraft executed a safe landing on Runway 15L. After coming to a stop on the runway, the flight crew shut down the right engine as Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) personnel approached the aircraft.Upon inspection on the runway, maintenance discovered a tool jammed in the left landing gear, preventing it from fully extending. Subsequent investigation determined that the tool found was an extension magnetic tool, not under the operator's control, and lacking any identification markings. The operator conducted research into prior maintenance in the area but found no documented reason for the tool to be located there.

C-GCWW, un Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 exploité par Canadian Helicopters Limited effectuait un vol de transport de chargement sous longue élingue selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Sept-Îles (CYZV), QC à destination d'une pourvoirie située à environ 28nm au nord de CYZV. Au moment de soulever la charge, pour une raison inconnue, le crochet de l'élingue situé sous l'appareil s'est ouvert et l'élingue est tombée au sol près de l'accrocheur. La cause de l'ouverture fait l'objet d'une enquête par l'exploitant. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé.

C-GJVW, a Fairchild SA227-DC operated by Perimeter Aviation as PAG/BL4330 was conducting a flight from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to North Bay/Jack Garland Airport (CYYB), ON and then to Detour Lake Aerodrome (CDT9), ON. During the first attempt to land on Runway 10 in CDT9, the crew conducted a missed approach due to the aircraft not being correctly positioned to land. Once past the threshold on the second approach, the right wing and nose contacted the runway, resulting in damage to the aircraft. The aircraft veered to the right and came to rest after sliding off the side of the runway, down an embankment. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the landing gear, engines, propellers, wings and fuselage. The was no post-crash fire.All 2 crew and 8 passengers egressed, some sustained minor injuries. The ELT did not activate. The Aerodrome and emergency personnel responded.

C-GFAF un Airbus A330-300 exploité par Air Canada effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Blagnac de Toulouse, France (LFBO) à destination de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). En descente vers CYUL à environ 30 miles nautiques au sud sud-ouest de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée en raison de la condition médicale d'un passager. L'appareil s'est posé à destination en priorité sans encombre.

C-FRJY, a Summit Air Ltd. Air British Aerospace Avro 146 (RJ100) was operating as SUT8191 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. N114SY, a Skywest Airlines Embraer ERJ 170-200 LR was operating as SKW4702 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to Denver International Airport (KDEN), Colorado. A loss of separation occurred after departure from CYEG when separation was reduced to 3.7 miles where 5 miles or 1000 feet is required.

OH-LTT un Airbus A330-300 exploité par Finnair sous l'indicatif FIN9 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Helsinki-Vantaa, Finlande (EFHK) à destination de l'aéroport de Chicago O'Hare, É-U (KORD). G-YMMG, un Boeing 777-200 exploité par British Airways sous l'indicatif BAW9CG effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de London/Heathrow, R-U (EGLL) à destination de l'aéroport international Sky Harbor de Phoenix, US (KPHX).Se rapprochant de OH-LTT à la même altitude avec une vitesse supérieure, le service de contrôle aérien a demandé à G-YMMG d'effectuer une descente du niveau de vol (FL) 380, vers le niveau de vol 370 pour le croisement des trajectoires. Avant le changement de niveau de vol, l'espacement horizontal minimum observé a été de 4.9 miles nautiques alors que l'espacement minimal requis est de 5 miles. Les 2 appareils ont poursuivi leurs vols à leurs destinations respectives sans encombre.

C-GXFA, an Icefield Discovery Tours Helio H-295 was conducting a local radar survey flight from Silver City Airport (CFQ5), YT. After departure from CFQ5, the aircraft climbed to 3500 feet ASL and conducted 2 survey lines. The aircraft climbed to 4500 feet ASL for the next line. As the third survey line was completed, while approximately 5 NM NNW from CFQ5, the pilot noticed a slight vibration from the engine (Lycoming GO-480-G1D6). The pilot began troubleshooting the issue and after 2 to 3 minutes the vibration became more pronounced and oil pressure dropped with an immediate loss of engine power. Smoke appeared from the windshield de-frost duct into the cabin. The pilot decided to conduct an emergency landing and diverted to return to CFQ5. While the aircraft approached the airport, the pilot acknowledged that it would not be possible to make the airfield and a forced landing was made on a gravel bed along Silver Creek. At approximately 60 mph, just before touchdown, the pilot shutdown the engine. The aircraft landed uneventfully with no damage to the airframe. The pilot and the 2 other individuals onboard received no injuries. The ELT did not activate. Company maintenance found that the #5 cylinder on the engine had failed.

C-GUBH, an Air Transat A330-243 was operating flight TSC573 from Lyon-Saint Exupéry Airport (LFLL), France to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During cruise, approximately 45 mins after takeoff, the flight crew noticed a suspicious smell (dirty socks) in the cockpit. An emergency was declared, and a decision was made to divert to Nantes Atlantique Airport (LFRS), France where the aircraft landed safely.

C-FRQA, a Canadian North Aerospatiale ATR-72, was operating as AKT5804 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NT. During departure, upon gear retraction, the flight crew received a cockpit emergency exit door unlock indication. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight crew advised CYEG departure that the aircraft was returning. The flight crew requested delaying vectors to complete the appropriate abnormal and normal checklists and setup for the approach. The aircraft landed uneventfully and was met by Aircraft Rescue Fire Fighting. The emergency vehicles followed the aircraft to the apron. There were no injuries. Company maintenance inspected the crew overhead emergency exit and latches. No defects were noted. A door warning MEL was raised, and the aircraft was released for continued service.

7T-VJX un Airbus A330-200 exploité par Air Algérie effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'Aéroport international d'Alger Houari Boumédiène, Algérie (DAAG). Peu après le décollage, une flamme sortant du moteur de gauche a été aperçue par le personnel de l'aéroport. L'équipage n'a pas noté de perte de puissance ou de feu moteur, mais a ressenti une vibration ponctuelle s'apparentant à un décrochage ou pompage du compresseur. L'équipage a décidé de faire un circuit et revenir se poser pour une inspection du moteur. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre avec les 2 moteurs en marche. Pas de blessé. Ayant subi un impact aviaire lors du décollage précédent, le moteur sera remplacé par précaution.

C-GKQV, a Porter Airlines E190-400 was operating flight POE309 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. During cruise at FL400, the #2 engine failed. A PAN PAN was declared and Drift Down procedures completed followed by actioning of the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH). A decision was made to divert to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB based on proximity and suitable weather. The aircraft landed safely with Aircraft Rescue Fire Fighting (ARFF) on standby.

C-FSFS, an AirSprint Inc. Cessna 525B (CitationJet) was conducting flight ASP654 from Abbotsford (CYXX), BC, to Kelowna (CYLW), BC, with 2 flight crew on board. In the climb out of CYXX, through approximately 11 000 feet above sea level, the crew received low oil pressure advisories. The crew declared an emergency with air traffic control and diverted to Vancouver (CYVR), BC. The engine (Williams FJ44-3A) was shutdown and the flight landed without further incident.The engine was sent to the manufacturer for inspection. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GNBN, an AIRBUS CANADA LIMITED PARTNERSHIP, BD-500-1A11 (A220-300), operating as Air Canada AC447 departed Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON destined for Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While on final approach, smoke and fumes were observed in the cabin and cockpit. The flight crew declared an emergency and the aircraft was met by ARFF on arrival. A post flight maintenance inspection revealed an issue with the right-hand PACK.

C-FSCY, a Boeing 737-8 operating as flight AC348 departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR) destined for Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW). During the flight (approx. 50 minutes to destination), a flight crew member advised that they were unwell and unable to continue duties. In discussion with dispatch and Stat MD, the decision was made to continue to CYOW. A PAN PAN was declared; the aircraft landed without further incident, and emergency services met the aircraft on arrival.

C-GTIP, a privately registered Beech F33A (Bonanza), departed Tobermory Airport (CNR4), ON, on a flight to Toronto / Buttonville Municipal Airport (CYKZ), ON. While climbing to 2500 AGL, the pilot noted a slight vibration coming from the engine. The pilot attempted to climb but found the aircraft was not able due to the engine performance. The pilot diverted to Wiarton Keppel International Airport (CYVV), ON but found the aircraft could not maintain altitude and was descending. A Mayday was declared, and the aircraft was ditched in Georgian Bay near Smoke Head - White Bluff Provincial Park. The pilot was not injured and was able to egress the aircraft and swim to shore. Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) Trenton tasked the Canadian Coast Guard to pick up the pilot. The aircraft sank in approximately 30 feet of water.

C-GBHO, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319, was operating as flight ROU1904 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Québec / Jean Lesage International Airport (CYQB), QC. During pushback from gate C31 at CYVR, the aircraft collided with C-GGNZ, a Jazz Aviation LP de Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) which was parked at gate C34 with engines running and waiting to taxi. C-GGNZ was being operated as flight JZA8031 from CYVR to Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC. The pushback required the tug to push the A319 south and then turn it right (west) to a position on the north taxi line where it could start engines. At approximately 1415 Pacific Daylight Time, the left wing fence of the A319 made contact with the right wing tip of the DHC-8. When the collision occurred, the DHC-8 was on it’s designated parking spot. The tug was right of the pushback line and the A319 was approximately 25 feet north of the taxi line when it contacted the DHC-8. Wing walkers on both wings of the A319 and the lead station attendant for the DHC-8 all signalled the tug driver to stop. The first stop hand signal was initiated approximately 9 seconds before the collision. Apron 6, where the aircraft were located is uncontrolled. There were no injuries. Both aircraft suffered minor damage.Maintenance conducted a wing tip after impact inspection of the A319 in accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual (AMM). The left wing fence was damaged beyond limits and was replaced. The aircraft was returned to service.For the DHC-8, the damage was limited to the right aileron and wing tip. The wing tip was replaced as was the aileron and all its bearings. Function tests were carried out and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GLIN, a Cessna 172M, with a solo student pilot on board, was conducting touch and go circuits at Smiths Falls-Montague (CYSH), ON. On the first touch and go landing the aircraft, the student reported the approach and landing was stable. While applying full power for the touch and go takeoff, the aircraft veered to the left, off the side of the runway into the trees. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The pilot was not injured.

TC-TFI un Cessna 172 exploité par la Turkish Airlines Flight Academy effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, Qc (CYVP) à destination de l'aéroport de Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) avec un pilote à bord. Lors de l'approche initiale, les conditions météorologiques se sont dégradées et le pilote a perdu le contact visuel avec le sol. L'unité de contrôle régionale de Montréal a donné une autorisation pour une approche aux instruments. À l'arrivée au seuil de la piste 16, étant trop haut pour compléter l'atterrissage, le pilote a alors effectué une remontée et un virage à droite se dirigeant à l'ouest de l'aéroport suivant un tracé erratique. 25 minutes plus tard, à l'aide du service de contrôle aérien et un autre pilote s'exprimant dans la langue du pilote, il s'est réaligné dans l'axe de la piste 16, à environ 4 miles nautiques du seuil. L'appareil a percuté le sol à environ 1 mile nautique du seuil de la piste 16. Le pilote a été légèrement blessé.

C-GOWG, a Sunwing Airlines B737-800 was operating flight TOM6720 from Cardiff Airport (EGFF), UK to Palma de Mallorca Airport (LEPA), Spain. During initial approach to LEPA, Air Traffic Control (ATC) cleared TOM6720 to FL200. While crossing FL207 the flight crew received a TCAS TA immediately followed by a TCAS RA. The autopilot and autothrottle were disengaged and the aircraft climbed to FL210. The flight crew attempted to notify ATC of the alert, but communications were busy.Following the alert and while in hold, the flight crew were notified that LEPA was closed and they diverted to Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport (LEMD), Spain.

C-GGNB, an amateur built Murphy Rebel on amphibious floats, was conducting circuits at Lake St. John with a pilot and instructor on board. During the occurrence landing, when the aircraft touched down normally, it suddenly veered to the right, due to a reported issue with a float attachment point. The aircraft stayed upright but had to be towed to the Orillia-Ramara Airport (CNJ4), ON. Both pilots received minor injuries.

C-FIUF, an Air Canada B777-233LR was operating flight AC43 from Delhi Indira Gandhi International Airport (VIDP), India to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Approximately one hour into the flight, the crew received "terrain pull-up" warnings. The flight crew followed checklist actions and the decision was made to return to VIDP. The crew declared a PAN PAN, emergency vehicles met the aircraft on the runway for assessment and was cleared to taxi to the gate without further incident.

C-GOKL, a Canadian Helicopters Limited Bell 212 helicopter was conducting a passenger flight from Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL to Cartwright Long Range Radar Site (LAB-6), NL with 1 passenger on board. When about 38 nm east of CYYR while operating with the automatic flight control system (AFCS) in attitude hold mode, the helicopter suddenly and abruptly rolled left. The pilot immediately pressed the trim release button and regained control of the helicopter. The flight continued to destination without further incident. There was no injury, and no damage to the aircraft occurred.Maintenance conducted extensive troubleshooting on the AFCS system but could not duplicate the problem.

C-FPWE, an Air Canada Airbus A320, was operating flight ACA242 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. After landing, the flight crew received an ECAM message “avionics smoke” while exiting the runway. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook and no smoke was detected. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft stopped on the taxiway where emergency vehicles met the aircraft for inspection. No fire or smoke was detected, and the aircraft was cleared to taxi to the gate. There were no injuries. Company maintenance found the forward avionics smoke detector to be faulty and the unit was replaced.

C-FXVH, a privately registered Piper PA-28-160 was on a flight from Toronto /Buttonville Municipal Airport (CYKZ), ON to East Linton (Kerr Field) Aerodrome, ON (CEL3). After touchdown, the aircraft went off the end of Runway 29, into a ditch. There were no injuries reported, the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GCEV, a Dash-7 aircraft operated by Air Tindi, was conducting flight TIN801 from Seabee Mine (CCB2), SK to Prince Albert (CYPA), SK. While enroute, the flight crew observed oil pressure anomalies on the number 3 engine. The flight crew conducted the QRH procedure, performed a precautionary engine shutdown, and diverted to Saskatoon (CYXE), SK, without further incident.

C-GYQK, a Beech A100 operated by Thunder Airlines, was conducting flight THU103 from Wunnumin Lake (CKL3), ON to Fort Hope (CYFH), ON. While on final approach CYFH, the flight crew selected the landing gear down and observed that the landing gear would not extend. The crew carried out a missed approach, requested emergency services and a diversion to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON. The crew conducted a successful manual gear extension during the approach into CYQT. Emergency services were on standby, and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FITW, un Boeing 777-333ER exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol AC6 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, de l'aéroport de Tokyo-Narita (RJAA) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Arrivé à la barrière 63 de CYUL, de la fumée et des flammes au niveau d'une des roues du train principal droit a été signalé par le personnel au sol. L'incendie a rapidement été maitrisé par les pompiers et les passagers on étés évacués par la passerelle d'embarquement. Il n'y a pas eu de déploiement des glissières d'urgence ni de blessés.Une inspection effectuée par l’exploitant a révélé que la cause de l’incendie était attribuable à la présence d’une quantité excessive de graisse sur l’essieu. Mis à jour le 18 octobre 2023

C-FTJJ, un DeHavilland DHC-6-300 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE127 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, de l'aéroport Poste Montagnais (Mile134) (CSF3) à destination de l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de l'arrivée à CYZV, l'aéronef a dû effectuer un virage serré sur le tablier et le bout de l'aile droite a heurté une porte de hangar. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GERL, a Qwest Helicopters (2020) Limited Aerospatiale AS350 BA (AStar) was conducting long line firefighting operations under visual flight rules from fire G90709 to a landing site located approximately 28 nautical miles south-southeast of Fort Liard Airport (CYJF), NT, with one crewmember on board. At 1633 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), while backing up to land on the helipad, the tail rotor of the helicopter struck a pack that had been left on the helipad. The tail rotor assembly subsequently departed the helicopter. There were no injuries. The helicopter was substantially damaged.The helicopter was recovered and was repaired in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. It has been returned to service.

C-GFAF, an Air Canada A330-343 was operating flight AC823 from Josep Tarradellas Barcelona-El Prat Airport (LEBL), Spain to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During the cruise phase of the flight, the crew received an ECAM message “BLUE HYD RSVR OVERHEAT”. The crew completed the checklist and subsequently received a “HYD B SYS LOW PR” message. In discussion with MOC and Dispatch, the decision was made to return to LEBL. A pan pan was declared, the flight landed without further incident and the aircraft was cleared to taxi to the gate.The blue hydraulic engine driven pump (EDP) and blue hydraulic EDP case drain filter element replaced in accordance with AMM.

C-GFCI, an Airbus A320-214 operated by Air Canada Rouge was conducting flight ROU1546 from Toronto Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Deer Lake Regional Airport (CYDF), NL. Once the aircraft landed the flight crew applied manual braking and felt a slight shudder and tire squeal. The aircraft taxied to the ramp and parked, then the flight crew were informed that smoke was observed to be coming from the left main gear with hydraulic fluid pooling around the tires. The flight crew requested the ARFF attendance at the aircraft.ARFF responded and once on scene noted that the smoke was dissipating. A dam was placed around the main wheels and absorbent applied to soak up the leaked hydraulic fluid. Once the smoke was no longer present the passengers deplaned uneventfully. Maintenance determined that the quick disconnect B-nut on the #2 brake was not lock-wired and found loose with the quick disconnect not locked in position. Maintenance secured and lock-wired the B-nut and locked the quick disconnect. A subsequent servicing and check of the yellow hydraulic system confirmed that the aircraft was serviceable, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFYO a privately registered Quicksilver Challenger II aircraft on floats was on a local area pleasure flight operating from Lake Deception, near Lower Ohio, Nova Scotia. During a glassy water landing the aircraft touched down hard and the fiberglass floats were immediately compromised. The aircraft sank below the lake surface. The uninjured pilot extracted himself from the aircraft and swam to shore. The pilot had taken aircraft egress training in the past year.In addition to damaged floats the aircraft received some structural damage due to the impact.

C-GPCT, a SAAB 340B operated by Pacific Coastal Airlines, was conducting flight PCO3026 under instrument flight rules from Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. B-16705, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by EVA Airways Corporation, was conducting flight EVA010 under instrument flight rules from Taipei/Songshan International Airport (RCSS) to CYVR. A loss of separation occurred while the aircraft were on approach. At 1920:48 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) PCO3026 was cleared for a visual approach onto Runway 26L at CYVR while EVA010 had been cleared for an instrument approach to Runway 26R. PCO3026 had previously reported EVA010 in sight, however the loss of separation occurred because air traffic control (ATC) did not instruct PCO3026 to maintain visual separation from EVA010.  At their closest, the aircraft were separated by 1.8 nautical miles (NM) and 900 feet. Both aircraft landed without incident at CYVR.

C-FMOC, a B757-2B7 aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express Inc., was conducting flight MAL7090 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. C-GITY, an A321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA113 from Lester B. Pearson International (CYYZ), ON, to CYVR. A loss of separation occurred while the aircraft were on approach. At 1616:50 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), ACA113 was assigned a speed of 160 knots while 6.2 nautical miles (NM) in trail of MAL7090, overtaking the preceding aircraft by 120 knots. At 1617:30 PDT, ACA113 was 5.3 NM in trail of MAL7090, overtaking by 100 knots, and was instructed to slow to final approach speed by air traffic control. At 1618:11 lateral separation between the two aircraft was reduced to 4.5 NM. The required lateral separation was 5 NM for wake turbulence. At their closest, the aircraft were separated by 4.5 NM laterally and 1300 feet vertically. Both aircraft landed without incident at CYVR.

C-GAQT, a Bell 407 aircraft operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited, was conducting external load operations at Hope Bay (CHB3), NU. Two external water bladders were slung through the eyelets of the bladders and hooked up to the cable connected to the helicopter. Shortly after departing, one of the bladders ripped through the eyelets and fell to the ground. There was no injury, and no damage to the aircraft or to the environment.

C-FBAF an Amateur Built Fenifox Alpha aircraft was on a local flight at Carp, ON (CYRP) with only the pilot on board. The takeoff was aborted due to a reported airspeed indicator issue; the aircraft overran the end of the runway. There were no injuries, the aircraft sustained substantial damage and the ELT activated.

C-FULE, an ATR 72-202 aircraft operated by Calm Air International, conducted a flight from Resolute Bay (CYRB), NU to Eureka (CYEU), NU. While taxiing on the ramp in CYEU, the aircraft's left wing came into contact with a parked semi-truck located on the apron. The aircraft's left wing scraped a semi-trucks exhaust stack, resulting in scratches to the wing and damage to the de-ice boot. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained minor damage.

C-GRCA, a privately registered Cessna 152, was being operated by AFS Aerial Photography in the vicinity of Claresholm Industrial Aerodrome (CEJ4), Alberta with one pilot on board. Shortly after take-off on Runway 03, the aircraft collided with terrain approximately 1 nm NE of the airport. The pilot sustained fatal injuries. The 121.5 MHz ELT did activate, and its signal was received by several aircraft in the vicinity. There was no post-impact fire.

C-FTQE, a privately registered Cessna 180H, departed Peterborough Airport (CYPQ), ON destined for Brockville Airport (CNL3), ON with only the pilot on board. During the landing on runway 04, just prior to touchdown, the aircraft drifted to the left and touched down in a soybean field. Both main landing gear collapsed, and the aircraft came to rest on its belly. There were no injuries; the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FTWN a privately registered Cessna 180H aircraft, was conducting a flight from Stoney Rapids (CYSF), SK to Lynx Lake, NWT, a private tundra strip located in NWT.  Shortly after touchdown the aircraft wheels rolled over rough terrain on the strip causing the aircraft to bounce. The pilot attempted to correct the landing, due to a 90-degree crosswind, the aircraft drifted to the sideways striking a barrel placed on the side of the runway. The aircraft left landing gear made contact with the barrel causing the left gear to collapse and left-wing tip and propellor to strike the ground. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The pilot exited the aircraft without injury.

C-FZNS, a privately registered Cessna U206D (Stationair) was conducting a flight from Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC, to a private landing strip located at 56°38'25.10"N, 123°23'41.62"W, known as Big Meadow, BC, under visual flight rules with one pilot and one passenger on board. Upon touchdown, the grass landing surface was found to be wet, and braking action was reported to be poor. The pilot elected to perform a go-around. They became airborne but collided with trees at the end of the runway. A 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter (ELT) on board the aircraft activated automatically at 0907 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), and a search and rescue aircraft was dispatched in response. The pilot was uninjured, but the passenger sustained minor injuries. There was no post-crash fire, but the aircraft was substantially damaged.The pilot and passenger were extracted by private helicopter prior to the arrival of search and rescue personnel.

C-GAKZ, a privately registered Cessna 172K aircraft was operating under visual flight rules from Squamish Municipal Airport (Don Patrick Field) (CYSE), BC, to Pitt Meadows Airport (CYPK), BC, with only the pilot on board. After descending to an altitude of approximately 1000 feet above ground level (AGL) in the valley north of Indian Arm, the aircraft experienced a partial loss of engine (Avco Lycoming O-320-E2D) power when the throttle was increased to climb. It was reported that the degraded power output of the engine was insufficient to maintain altitude, and the pilot began preparing for a precautionary landing. While the pilot was searching for a suitable landing site, the aircraft engine lost all power, but subsequently resumed generating power without pilot intervention. It was reported that the engine power output after the re-start was higher than before the initial power loss, but still less than normal. The engine performance then degraded further, and the engine stopped generating power a second time. The pilot successfully restarted the engine, however the engine continued to produce insufficient power to maintain altitude. After a brief period of operation, the engine quit a third and final time. At the time of the final power loss, the pilot had maneuvered to the vicinity of a gravel bar on the Indian River. A low-level turn was executed to align the aircraft with the landing site. Upon landing, the aircraft struck a log, which caused significant damage to the left elevator and horizontal stabilizer. The aircraft came to a stop on the gravel bar.The pilot was uninjured and egressed the aircraft without issue. A hand-held personal locator beacon (PLB) was activated at 1753 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), and a Canadian Armed Forces CH-149 Cormorant search and rescue helicopter retrieved the pilot at approximately 1958 PDT. The aircraft was removed from the landing site several days later via helicopter.Transportation Safety Board (TSB) investigators examined the aircraft after it had been recovered. Investigators examined the aircraft engine and found no abnormalities. Fuel samples from the engine gascolator were normal. Fuel samples taken from the aircraft wing tanks at the time of recovery were examined and found to be consistent with the conditions to which the aircraft had been exposed while awaiting recovery. With no abnormalities found with the aircraft engine, fuel supply lines were reconnected with a fuel source and a successful engine start was performed. It was determined that the condition that had caused the engine to quit during the occurrence was no longer present at the time the aircraft examination.

D-ABVW, a Deutsche Lufthansa Aktiengesellschaft Boeing 747-430 was conducting flight DLH493 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Frankfurt Main Airport (EDDF), Germany, under instrument flight rules. On departure from CYVR, a malfunction occurred with the aircraft landing gear system, preventing the crew from retracting the landing gear, and an emergency was declared. Air traffic control (ATC) directed the aircraft via radar vectors to an area appropriate for dumping fuel. The crew performed a fuel dump at 12,000 feet to bring the aircraft to a weight suitable for landing. The aircraft then returned to CYVR, where it landed without further incident.

C-FNSN, an ATR 72-212A aircraft operated by North Star Air, was conducting flight BF502 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Arctic Bay (CYAB), NU. When the aircraft was 60 NM North of CYTH, the flight crew observed oil pressure anomalies on the number 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW127M). The flight crew conducted the QRH procedure, performed a precautionary engine shutdown, and the aircraft then landed in CYTH without further event.The operator's maintenance was unsuccessful in determining the cause of the oil pressure anomalies. The aircraft remains out of service and further troubleshooting guidance is being provided by the engine manufacturer.

C-GJSD, a Bell 206B helicopter operated by Wetaskiwin Aerial Applicators, was conducting aerial application on a field with only the pilot on board. During an application pass, the helicopter struck a powerline and then collided with terrain. The pilot did not receive any injury and the helicopter was substantially damaged. There was no post-impact fire.

On 19 August 2023, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400 (C-GEEN/WEN4748) was on a scheduled flight from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), Alberta to Kamloops Airport (CYKA), British Columbia. On board were 4 crew members and 47 passengers. At 1100 Mountain Daylight Time, during the take-off roll, prior to the airspeed reaching 60 knots, the crew experienced a #2 bleed hot caution light followed by a deice press caution light. The flight crew initiated a rejected takeoff and declared a MAYDAY. The flight crew were then able to taxi the aircraft off the runway, complete the appropriate checklists and the aircraft returned to the gate.Maintenance actions: Maintenance replaced the left-hand nacelle shut off valve and completed an operational test of the bleed air system. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBEP, a Summit Helicopters Limited Bell 412EP helicopter, was conducting long-line firefighting operations in the vicinity of fire K21633 (Bush Creek East), BC, under visual flight rules with 1 crew member on board. At 1700 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), after departing a remote refueling point to return to the fire, a master caution light illuminated, indicating a system 1 hydraulic malfunction. Hydraulic pressure for the number 1 system indicated 0, and failure of the system was further confirmed via manipulation of the tail rotor pedals. The pilot diverted approximately 30 nautical miles southwest to the Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, and performed the required emergency checks. Upon arrival at the CYKA control zone, the pilot declared an emergency. The slung load was jettisoned onto the airport ramp and the helicopter landed without further incident. A maintenance investigation will be undertaken by the operator to determine the cause of the hydraulic system failure.

C-FTIQ, un ATR42-500 exploité par Canadian North / Bradley air services Limited sous l'indicatif AKT6365, venait d’arriver d’un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Pond Inlet, Nu (CYIO) à destination d'Iqualuit, NU (CYFB) avec 29 passagers et 3 membres d'équipage. Lors de la circulation vers l’aire de stationnement, l’équipage a reçu une alerte de fumée électrique accompagnée de senteur de fumée et de fumée dans le poste de pilotage. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et a demandé l'intervention des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). L’équipage a complété la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH). Après avoir arrêté l’aéronef, un débarquement rapide a été débuté suivi d’une évacuation amorcée par l’ouverture de la porte de service par un passager. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.
