Le personnel d'entretien d'aéronef a observé que le ventilateur gauche de refroidissement au sol était saisi. Le ventilateur a été remplacé et l'appareil remis en service.

C-IJYF, un Paramoteur Air Conception ultra moster 185 trike en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol de formation solo selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis un champ situé à 8 nm à l’est de l'aéroport de Gatineau, QC (CYND). Lors du décollage par vents faibles, la voile était en roulis et suite aux conseils par radio de son instructeur de réduire la puissance, le pilote a mis plein gaz et a donné du frein à la voile. Ceci a amplifié le roulis vers la gauche en soulevant l’appareil d’environ 4 pieds et l'appareil a ensuite percuté le sol. Le pilote a subi des blessures sérieuses.

C-GNEC, a Synergy Aviation Ltd. operated Robinson R44II, was conducting longlining work 30 nm East of Grande Cache, Alberta. While lifting off from an oil field site, the longline snagged a railing associated with the oil field infrastructure. The helicopter subsequently collided with terrain resulting in substantial damage to the helicopter. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was seriously injured. JRCC and RCMP responded to the accident site and worked to extract the pilot.

G-ZBKM, a British Airways B787-9 was operating flight BAW4MX from Mexico City International Airport (MMMX), MEX, to Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK. In the vicinity of Fredonia, NY, an emergency was declared due to an oil pressure issue. The crew of the aircraft elected to divert to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON where the aircraft landed safely.

C-GKCW, a Bell 206L helicopter operated by Gogal Air Services, was conducting a day VFR flight from Flin Flon (CYFO), MB to Yaskowich Lake, SK. Upon landing at Yaskowich Lake, the pilot positioned the aircraft's skids across a log to keep the tail rotor clear of terrain. The pilot got out to load some cargo with the aircraft idling. The center of gravity shifted, and the aircraft pivoted back onto its tail. The tail rotor contacted the ground while turning. The aircraft was substantially damaged. There were no injuries. C-GKCW was subsequently relocated by helicopter to Snow Lake, MB for repairs.

C-GKQF, a Porter Q400 was operating flight POE2722 from Dulles International Airport (KIAD), VA to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. When at approximately 100NM South of Toronto, in the vicinity of Silver Creek, NY, the #2 HYD ISO VLV M/C illuminated. The QRH was actioned. The #2 HYD fluid quantity was indicating zero. No other M/C were illuminated at this time. The ATC was given a PAN PAN call and advised of the situation. The crew elected to divert to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON where the aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance performed inspection and found the leak originating from the EDP Suction line union. It was found loose. Hydraulic engine driven pump and #2 system filters replaced. Aircraft returned to service.

C-FCAG, a Cessna C560, operating as Chartright Air Inc. flight HRT510, departed Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ), ON. Shortly afterwards, the flight crew noted that the pressurization system was over-pressurizing the cabin. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and elected to return to CYYZ. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GFFS, a Cessna 525B aircraft, operated by Airsprint Inc., was conducting flight ASP595 from Gander International Airport (CYQX), NFL to Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON with 2 crew and 2 passengers onboard. While on final RNAV approach in visual conditions, at approximately 10 NM ENE from CYKF, ASP595 received a Traffic Advisory (TA) which subsequently transpired as a Resolution Advisory (RA). Air Traffic Control informed the crew of a glider flying in the area. The crew followed the RA and flew under the target, ASP595 continued on a stable approach and landed in CYKF without further incident.

C-GKQS, an E195-E2 operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE303 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Int'l Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 5 crew and 126 passengers on board. During the initial climb, the crew received an EICAS indication of a LH inboard brake overheat. The crew actioned the appropriate checklist, which cleared the indication initially, but the same indication appeared twice more, followed by a LG Temp Exceedance message. The flight crew requested to hold in order to consume fuel and reduce the aircraft weight to below maximum landing weight. Before returning to CYYZ, the flight crew requested ARFF to be standing by for their landing and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed uneventfully and was inspected by ARFF before proceeding to the gate. Maintenance revealed a faulty brake temperature sensor, which was replaced before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJLH, a Jetlines A320-214 was operating as flight CJL503 from Cancun International Airport (MMUN), MX to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While in cruise, the crew declared an emergency due to a cracked windshield. The crew elected to divert to Charlotte Douglas International Airport (KCLT), NC where the aircraft landed without further incident.

D-ABPD, un Boeing 787-9 exploité par Lufthansa effectuait le vol DLH478 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Frankfurt/Rhein-Main, Allemagne (EDDF) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Québec (CYUL). Une fois stationné à la barrière 59, un incendie s’est déclenché au frein #2. Des extincteurs portatifs ont été utilisés et les pompiers sont arrivés et ont arrosé l’endroit. Le feu s’est éteint et les passagers ont été sortis normalement. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GHPD, an Airbus A321-211, operating as Air Canada Rouge flight 1813, was taxiing to the gate after landing at Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), when the flight crew received an "ENG 2 FAIL' ECAM message. The flight crew shutdown the engine and taxied to the gate without further incident. Maintenance was unable to determine the fault, the engine was scheduled to be removed and sent for an inspection/overhaul.

C-FKXY, a privately registered GC-1B (Globe Swift), was conducting a VFR flight from Plattsville/Lubitz Flying Field (CLB2), ON, to Guelph Airport (CNC4), ON, with two pilots on board. After takeoff from runway 25, a 1980' x 75' grass runway, the aircraft did not accelerate as expected. Without sufficient runway to reject the takeoff, the pilot attempted to gather speed while remaining in ground effect, but once the aircraft was over the corn field at the end of the runway the ground effect was diminished, and the aircraft began to decelerate. The pilot lowered the nose and landed in the cornfield. Both main landing gear collapsed, and there was also damage to the nose and leading edges of the wings. The ELT did activate following the emergency landing, there were no injuries.

G-ZBLA, un Boeing 787-10 exploité par British Airways sous l'indicatif BAW9EW, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK. Dans les environs de Carleton-sur-Mer, Québec, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence médicale en raison d'un membre d'équipage de cabine malade et qui a été blessé légèrement. L'équipage a demandé un retour vers CYUL où il s'est posé sans encombre.

C-GRGQ, a Bell 212 helicopter operated by Coldstream Helicopters, was conducting external load operations departing from Sandy Lake, ON with a fuel stop at Valard - Deer Lake Camp, Deer Lake, ON. While on final approach to Valard-Deer Lake Camp, the aircraft began to shake fore and aft. The pilot released the external load in a clearing from approximately 30 ft AGL. Once the load was released the shaking ceased. The aircraft landed at the Valard-Deer Lake Camp without further incident. The external load rigging was inspected by the operator found to be appropriate. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft, and it was returned to service.

C-FHAU, an AS-350 BA helicopter operated by Expedition Helicopters, was conducting external load operations near Wawa, Ontario, in support of a mining operation. The helicopter was positioning an external load attached by a long line onto a platform with the assistance of several ground crew members. During the positioning of the load, unbeknownst to the pilot, one of the ground crew members became entangled in the external load, and subsequently fell while the helicopter was being manoeuvred. The ground crew member was fatally injured; there were no other injuries. The helicopter was not damaged.

C-GGAH, a Jazz Aviation LP de Havilland DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was conducting flight JZA298 under instrument flight rules from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International Airport (CYXC), BC, with 4 crew members and 78 passengers on board. During approach to Runway 16 in CYXC, a missed approach was conducted due to high crosswind conditions. A second approach to Runway 16 was attempted, but also resulted in a missed approach. The crew subsequently diverted to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Nearing CYYC, the crew advised air traffic control that their fuel level was critical, and the flight received priority handling. The aircraft landed without incident.

C-GYWQ, a float-equipped Cessna U206G airplane operated by Interlake Aviation, was conducting a local VFR flight from Riverton (CKW4), MB with only the pilot on board. While in cruise approximately 20 NM north of CKW4, the engine (Teledyne Continental Motors IO-520F) began to run rough and then abruptly failed. The pilot conducted a forced landing without further incident on Lake Winnipeg, near the shore. JRCC was notified and a Canadian Coast Guard vessel was diverted to tow the aircraft to safety. There were no injuries.The operator's maintenance inspection indicated that the engine experienced a connecting rod failure.

C-GLQL, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par Porter Airlines, effectuait le vol POE2360 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Charlottetown, IPÉ (CYYG), à destination d'Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW). C-IEWU, un ultra-léger de type évolué Aerotechnik Sportstar effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue dans la région de Gatineau (QC). Après que l’ATC ait avisé des trafics et donné des autorisations de virage subséquentes à C-IEWU et POE2360, l’équipage de POE2360 a avisé qu’il devait répondre à un avis de résolution TCAS RA. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

N576DZ, an Airbus A350-941 operated by Delta Airlines Inc., was conducting flight DAL176 from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (KATL), GA, USA to Dublin International Airport (EIDW), Ireland with 14 crew members and 339 passengers. While in cruise flight, approximately 234 nm SSW of Gander International Airport (CYQX) NL, a flight attendant noted an electrical odor in the aft galley. The flight crew contacted dispatch and maintenance control to assist with identifying the source of the odor. It was decided to initiate a diversion to CYQX. The flight crew declared an emergency and landed safely at 0405 UTC.Maintenance personnel found the aft galley electrical inline heater was malfunctioning. They deactivated and deferred the heater and returned the aircraft to service.

C-GARO, an Airbus A319-100 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1543 from Charlottetown Airport (CYYG), PEI, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Int'l Airport (CYYZ), ON with 5 crew and 118 passengers on board. Shortly after beginning their descent, the flight crew received ECAM messages indicating low hydraulic pressure in the Yellow reservoir and system. The flight crew declared PAN PAN, and landed uneventfully at CYYZ. Maintenance revealed a leaking check valve tube assembly and elbow fitting, which were replaced and tested before returning the aircraft to service.

C-FUSE, a privately registered Piper PA-18 aircraft, was conducting touch-and-go at Saskatoon/Richter Field (CRF5), SK. On the third touchdown, the pilot lost control and the aircraft ground looped. The pilot sustained minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. It was reported that gusty crosswind conditions existed at the time of the occurrence.

C-GPWG, an Airbus A320-211 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA0271 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Winnipeg James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB with 6 crew and 138 passengers onboard. Shortly after starting the engine in CYYZ, a pilot felt unwell and was not able to continue with duties. A company pilot seating in the cabin for a repositioning flight offered to operate flight ACA0271 in replacement. In consultation with company dispatch and crew scheduling, he was authorized to take over the functions for the flight. ACA0271 continued to CYWG without further incident.

C-FCBK, a Thrush S2R-T34 operated by Kindersley Airspray, was performing aerial application of a field 7NM WNW of Luseland (CJR2), SK. During a turn at a low altitude, the aircraft's left wing contacted the ground. The aircraft subsequently collided with the terrain and it was destroyed. The pilot was injured and airlifted to hospital.

C-GDWM, a Canadian Helicopters Limited Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 helicopter was conducting a flight from Bear Claw Lodge, BC, (55° 36.67' N, 128° 07.43' W) to a passenger pick up area at 55° 17.48' N, 127° 41.83' W, under visual flight rules with only the pilot on board. At 1355 PDT, the pilot noticed a fluctuating engine torque indication (Turbomeca Arriel 1D1) followed by a drop in indicated oil pressure. Subsequently, the oil pressure annunciator light illuminated. The pilot maneuvered toward a valley, initiated a power-on autorotation, and declared a Mayday. The aircraft landed without further incident in a field near the town of Kispiox, BC.   A maintenance inspection found evidence of a significant oil leak caused by a crushed washer on the end of the torque transmitter. The aircraft was repaired on site and returned to service.

C-FROG, a Glacier Air Cessna 172N, was conducting local circuits at Squamish Municipal Airport (CYSE), BC, with only the student pilot on board. During the fourth circuit and approach for Runway 33, the aircraft was high and the pilot initiated a slip to reduce altitude. The aircraft floated down the runway and touched down with approximately 1000 feet remaining. The pilot applied the brakes and the aircraft veered to the right and departed the runway surface. The right wing tip contacted a tree and the aircraft came to a stop approximately 45 feet from the runway edge with an east-northeasterly heading. The pilot secured the aircraft before egressing and then contacted the supervising flight instructor for assistance. There were no reported injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.  Post occurrence, a tire skid mark was found on the runway surface that exited the right side of the runway and continued as a ground scar in the direction of the aircraft's resting position. During the recovery of the aircraft, both aircraft wheels were reported to rotate freely.

C-FUGU, a privately registered Cessna 172H, was returning to Michael's Bay Field, a private grass runway approximately 17nm SW of Manitoulin East Municipal Airport (CYEM), ON, after a local flight with only the pilot on board. During the landing flare on Runway 19, the pilot encountered an unexpected tailwind (winds were observed, based on the appearance of the water, to be from the west at approximately 20 knots), resulting in the aircraft floating along the runway. The pilot decided that he was too far along the runway to make a successful go-around due to obstacles, including a house, beyond the end of the runway. The pilot landed and used maximum braking before steering the aircraft into nearby trees to avoid colliding with the house. The nose aircraft received substantial damage to the nose, and the nose gear collapsed after hitting a rock. The left and right wingtips received damage from contact with trees. The pilot was not injured.

C-FASY, un Cessna 525B (Citation CJ3) exploité Airsprint Inc. sous l’indicatif ASP489, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis Toronto Pearson International Airport, ON (CYYZ) à destination des Îles-de-la-Madeleine, QC (CYGR) avec 2 pilotes à bord. En vol de croisière alors qu’il se trouvait à environ 19 miles marins à l’est de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC au niveau de vol 450, un problème de pressurisation est survenu. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence, a amorcé une descente rapide jusqu'au niveau de vol FL31 et a effectué une diversion à CYUL. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 24L à CYUL sans encombre et il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C- GNBN, un Airbus Canada Limited Partnership BD-500-1A11 (A220) exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA692, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ) à destination de St John's, NF (CYYT) avec 127 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage. Lors de la montée, un message du système d'affichage des paramètres réacteurs, de mise en garde et d'alarme (EICAS) avisait d’une faible pression du système hydraulique numéro 3. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et fait une diversion à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés et l’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 24R sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni de dommage à l’appareil.

C-GBHY, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1652 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to  Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL. During the flare on runway 8L, ATC instructed the flight crew to conduct an overshoot due to traffic on the runway. The main landing gear made contact with the runway before the aircraft climbed back up. There was no damage, the flight was completed without further incident.

0n 23 July 2023, an Air North Charter and Training Ltd. Aerospatiale-Alenia ATR 42-320 (C-GVGX/ANT326) was on a scheduled passenger flight from Dawson City Airport (CYDA), YT to the Erik Nielsen Whitehorse International Airport (CYXY), YT. On board were 3 flight crew and 42 passengers. As the aircraft began to taxi, the first officer called Dawson Airport Radio to announce their taxi instructions. No reply was received. As the aircraft approached Runway 21, the flight crew looked outside for traffic. Not seeing any aircraft on the runway or short final in either direction, they proceeded onto the runway, broadcasting their intentions to takeoff from Runway 21. Moments later, another aircraft announced that they were on final for landing. The flight crew of ANT326 immediately broadcast their position on the runway and the approaching aircraft  delayed their approach to allow ANT326 time to backtrack and depart from Runway 21. ANT326 departed and the other aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GOVT, the Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency (SPSA Air Operations) Gulfstream 695A was on a flight from the Erik Nielsen Whitehorse International Airport (CYXY), YT to the High Level Airport (CYOJ), AB. The aircraft was returning from a firefighting operation in Alaska. The pilot attempted to reduce power on both engines to commence the descent from FL190 into CYOJ. When the power levers were brought back, the right engine (Garrett TPE331-10) RPM sped up. The pilot noted that the right engine was doing the opposite of what was commanded using the power lever. The pilot declared an emergency and carried out the descent by reducing power on the left engine and leaving the right engine at cruise setting to reduce the risk of an engine RPM overspeed. Airborne troubleshooting proved unsuccessful, and the pilot elected to shut down the right engine for landing. The aircraft landed safely at CYOJ without further incident.Maintenance examined the engine and engine controls and carried out a ground run. No defects were found. A flight test was carried out with no defects found. The airplane was subsequently declared serviceable and returned to service.

On 07 August 2023, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400 (C-GDEW/WEN3268) was on a scheduled flight from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), Alberta to Regina International Airport (CYQR), Saskatchewan. On board were 4 crew members and 67 passengers. At 1410 Mountain Daylight Time, during the take-off roll, as the airspeed increased to 60 knots, the crew experienced a #1 AC GEN caution light. The flight crew initiated a rejected takeoff and declared a MAYDAY. The flight crew were then able to exit the runway and cancelled the MAYDAY. The flight crew attempted a second takeoff but the caution light illuminated again during the takeoff roll. The flight crew again rejected the takeoff and declared a MAYDAY. After exiting the runway, the flight crew cancelled the MAYDAY and returned to the gate. There were no injuries.Maintenance actions: The aircraft was inspected and the #1 AC GEN was replaced. The aircraft tested serviceable and was released back into service. No other faults were found.

C-GVCS, an Aerospatiale AS 332L helicopter operated by 618232 Alberta Ltd. (dba Val Air), was conducting external load operations near Pikangikum Airport (CYPM), ON. During the flight, the crew noticed that the sling load had shifted. The load was jettisoned in a remote area as a precautionary measure. The helicopter continued uneventfully to a landing and there was no damage to the aircraft.

C-GCJK, an Airbus A320-214 operated by Canada Jetlines Operations Ltd., was conducting flight WSW310 from Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Int'l Airport (CYYZ), ON, with 6 crew and 164 passengers on board. During approach to runway 24L, at 3000 feet ASL, the flight was intercepting the localizer when the crew noted traffic ahead on the approach that appeared closer than normal. The crew received an ATC instruction to turn to a heading of 290 degrees. Simultaneously, they encountered momentary uncommanded roll to the right due to wake turbulence from the aircraft ahead. The flight received vectors to rejoin the approach and continued to land without incident.

C-FSEO, un Champion Aircraft Corp. 7GCB Challenger (équipé de flotteurs) en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’hydro-aérodrome de Québec/Lac St-Augustin, QC (CNS8) pour effectuer des posés-décollés sur le fleuve Saint-Laurent à quelques milles marins au sud-ouest avec un instructeur et un pilote à bord. Après un posé-décollé, l’avion a fait un circuit par la gauche et quelques instants après avoir atteint 1000 pieds au-dessus du niveau de la mer en vent arrière, une descente rapide est survenue. L’avion a percuté la surface de l’eau avec une assiette verticale et l’appareil a coulé au fond du fleuve. L’appareil a été détruit et les 2 occupants ont subi des blessures mortelles.

C-IREX, un Quad City Challenger II en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport d’Amos/Magny, QC (CYEY) dans le but d'y faire des posés-décollés avec seul un pilote à bord. Lors du premier atterrissage, l’aéronef a rebondi et le pilote a fait une remise des gaz. Lors du prochain atterrissage, il y a eu un rebond suivi d’une remise des gaz et une importante déviation du côté gauche de la piste. L’aéronef a percuté l'indicateur de trajectoire d'approche de précision (PAPI) et a terminé sa course dans le fossé à gauche de la piste. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé, toutefois l’aéronef a subi des dommages importants.

C-FGXH, un Beechcraft C90A exploité par Transports Canada sous l'indicatif TGO987, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à destination de Drummondville, QC (CSC3) avec 2 pilotes à bord. Alors que l’aéronef circulait au sol avant le décollage, une indication de feu du moteur gauche est survenue. L’équipage a immobilisé l’avion et a fait la procédure de feu au sol et d’évacuation. Les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés et l’inspection de l’appareil n’a révélé aucun signe de feu ni de fumée.

C- FRSA, un Boeing 787-900 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA51, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Indira Gandhi International Airport en Inde (VIDP) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 263 passagers et 15 membres d’équipage. Pendant le vol l’équipage a remarqué la diminution de la pression du pneu gauche de la roue de nez. En approchant CYUL l’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. L’aéronef s’est posé sur la piste 24R sans encombre. Il fut immobilisé et inspecté sur la piste avant d’être remorqué à la barrière.

C-FEYP, un Beechcraft A100 exploité par Propair Inc. sous l’indicatif PRO4701, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Sioux Lookout ON (CYXL) à destination de Val-d’Or, QC (CYVO) avec 4 passagers et 2 pilotes à bord. Alors que l’aéronef se trouvait en vol de croisière à 17 000 pieds ASL, à environ 100 miles marins à l’ouest-nord-ouest de Rouyn le générateur gauche s’est arrêté, des fluctuations de puissance sont survenues et le générateur droit s’est arrêté. L’équipage a réussi à remettre le générateur gauche en marche, a déclaré un état d’urgence et a fait une diversion à destination de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY). L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 26, et il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GAIS, a DHC-8-100 operated by Air Creebec Inc., was conducting flight CRQ861 from Timmins/Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON, to Moosonee Airport (CYMO), ON, with 4 crew and 26 passengers on board. After departing runway 03, the LH engine torque began to fluctuate, lost power, and failed. The flight crew conducted the appropriate checklists and declared an emergency with Timmins FSS, declared their intention to return for landing on runway 03, and requested that the ARFF be present for their landing. The flight landed uneventfully. Maintenance completed ground runs and did not find any cause for the engine failure. As a precaution, they replaced the LH torque gauge and LH engine signal conditioner and conducted further ground runs before conducting a test flight. Five circuits were performed with no faults found, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GIWJ, a WestJet B737 Max 8 was operating flight WS2512 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Grantley Adams International Airport (TBPB), Barbados. During flight, a cabin crew member became sick due to a personal medical event. The Cabin crew member was unable to perform their assigned duties and was not in their assigned jumpseat for landing. These duties were reassigned to the remaining cabin crew members. EMS was required upon arrival.

C-GNMR, a privately registered amphibious float equipped Murphy Rebel, was conducting local flights from Chilliwack Airport (CYCW), BC, with the pilot and one passenger on board. Following a stopover on Harrison Lake in the vicinity of Silver Creek, BC, the aircraft took off and was flying low level southbound over the lake. The pilot opted to land near the middle of the lake. The aircraft landed hard which caused the left float to buckle and the left-wing tip to contact the water. The aircraft briefly spun on the water surface before overturning. The pilot and passenger removed their respective restraints, exited the right cockpit door onto the overturned wing and donned personal floatation devices. C-FOHT, a private amphibious Cub Crafters Carbon Cub EX, was accompanying the Murphy Rebel and landed on the lake to pick up the 2 occupants. The aircraft taxied to shore and offloaded the 2 occupants riding on the floats before departing back to CYCW. The occupants were assisted by a bystander and taken by private vehicle to the Chilliwack General Hospital. The pilot received minor injuries and the passenger was uninjured. The aircraft sank in approximately 860 feet of water and has not been recovered.

C-GGMQ, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting IFR flight JZA21 from Deer Lake airport (CYDF), NL to Halifax/Stanfield (CYHZ), NS. C-GUPW, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Services (EVAS), was conducting flight EV200 from Gander Intl (CYQX), NL to CYHZ. When about 47 north-northeast (NNE) of CYHZ, ATS advised JZA21 they would be following EV200 and gave instructions for JZA21 to reduce speed. About 2 minutes later EV200 was cleared for the CYHZ ILS23 approach and was instructed to maintain as high a speed as possible, which EV200 acknowledged. Shortly after JZA21 was also cleared for the CYHZ ILS23 approach. JZA21 was given and followed subsequent instructions to reduce speed when advised. Following hand off to CYHZ tower EV200 was about 8 nm NNE of CYHZ. JZA21 was about 3 nm behind EV200 and was given and complied with an instruction to turn right to provide spacing to EV200. However, EV200 had decreased speed more than ATS had anticipated, and separation between the aircraft was reduced to 2.6 nm momentarily, where 3 nm was the separation standard. JZA21 was recleared on the approach and both aircraft landed without further incident. NAV CANADA is carrying out an investigation into the occurrence.

C-GHCT, an Aerospatiale AS 350 BA operated by Foothills Helicopter Training Academy Ltd. (dba Exploration Helicopters), was conducting seismic mapping northeast of Hatchet Lake, SK with seismic gear slung on a long line. While mapping, the pilot heard a loud bang and noted that the seismic gear had become disconnected from the helicopter. The flight returned to its base at Hatchet Lake uneventfully.A subsequent inspection by the operator revealed that the soft-point sling gear had failed. The slinging gear was replaced and operations resumed.

C-ITNO, a privately registered US Aviation Cumulus ultralight aircraft, was conducting a local flight under visual flight rules from Hope Airport (CYHE), BC, with 1 pilot on board. The flight occurred following recent engine repairs and a new propeller being mounted. The aircraft departed Runway 25 and joined the circuit pattern and was the pilot’s third flight in the occurrence aircraft. On the turn from base leg to final approach, the aircraft reportedly experienced a severe and continuous vibration. The pilot attempted to keep the aircraft under control and continued westbound parallel to the runway until control was lost. At 0815 Pacific Daylight Time, the aircraft collided with terrain, nose-down, in a field approximately 4000 feet west of the end of Runway 25. The aircraft was substantially damaged, but there was no post-impact fire. Emergency medical services, Fire fighters, and RCMP attended the scene. The firefighters cut off the forward part of the aircraft to extract the pilot. The pilot was seriously injured and airlifted to hospital.The aircraft was recovered put into a storage trailer.

C-FTES, a privately registered Cessna 337G, was conducting an IFR flight from North Bay/ Jack Garland Airport (CYYB), ON, to St. Catharines/Niagara District Airport (CYSN), ON, with 1 pilot and 2 passengers onboard. During initial climb from CYYB, the pilot noticed that the left main landing gear door was still open after the gear retraction. Once in level cruise, the pilot unsuccessfully tried to deploy the landing gear. The pilot subsequently ran the applicable checklist from the flight manual and declared PAN PAN with ATC, stating his intention to continue the flight to CYSN. Once in range of CYSN, the pilot requested a descent into VFR conditions, after which he attempted a manual landing gear extension, which was not successful. After an hour of circling and additional troubleshooting in consultation with his AME via telephone, the pilot elected to land on the grass beside Runway 01 with ARFF standing by.  The pilot shut both engines off before touchdown and landed the aircraft on its belly. The aircraft sustained damage to the front propeller, the landing gear doors, and to the belly. The occupants exited the aircraft without injuries. There was no post impact fire. Preliminary maintenance information indicates a failure of the nose landing gear actuator which caused a loss of hydraulic fluid in the landing gear system.

An unregistered Robinson R44 helicopter was conducting a local flight in the vicinity of Mabel Lake, BC, with 4 occupants onboard. During low-level cruise flight over the Shuswap River, the pilot lost control and the helicopter collided with the riverbed. The occupants were assisted by local bystanders until emergency services arrived. Three occupants sustained injuries and the status of the fourth occupant was unknown. The aircraft was destroyed.     The following day, BC Hydro repaired a broken power line in the vicinity of the occurrence site. This occurrence is currently being investigated by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

C-FRZG, a Cooking Lake Aviation Academy Diamond DA20-C1, was operating on a training flight from the Cooking Lake Airport (CEZ3), AB for the private pilot license with a flight instructor and student on board. While in the local training in the vicinity of Bearverhill Lake (20 NM east of CEZ3), the aircraft collided with the lake. The aircraft came to rest in shallow water; the 406 MHz ELT did not activate. The aircraft was declared missing at 2100 MDT and JRCC Trenton commenced search activities. The aircraft was found shortly after midnight. One occupant was deceased and the other was seriously injured and was transported to an Edmonton hospital. The survivor subsequently died 2 days later from their injuries.

C-GGOF, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was conducting flight JZA269 under instrument flight rules from the Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, to the Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 4 crew members and 78 passengers on board. While on approach for Runway 08L at CYVR, as the aircraft was descending through 2100 feet, it experienced an un-commanded roll.  The occurrence flight was approximately 7 miles in trail of a Boeing 787-9 (Dreamliner). The crew of flight JZA269 disconnected the autopilot and countered the un-commanded roll via manual flight control input. The flight then landed without incident. There were no injuries and there was no damage to the aircraft.

C-GJCN, a Summit Air Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-311 (Dash 8), was conducting flight SUT2091, under instrument flight rules, from Bella Bella (Campbell Island) Airport (CBBC), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 3 crewmembers and 29 passengers on board. At 2007 Pacific Daylight Time, while on final approach to Runway 26R in CYVR, the flight crew selected the landing gear down, and observed that the right main gear green light did not illuminate. The crew carried out a missed approach and requested emergency services. The crew completed the Landing Gear Indicator Malfunction check list and determined that the right main gear green light was burnt out. The crew cancelled their request for emergency services and the aircraft landed without incident.

C-FANB, a Boeing 737-48E aircraft operated by Air North Charter and Training Ltd., was conducting flight ANT903 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl Airport (CYHZ), NS to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. Shortly after takeoff a flight attendant became incapacitated. Food poisoning was suspected, and the flight attendant’s duties were distributed among the cabin crew. The ill flight attendant’s condition improved and was able to resume minimal duties. The fight continued to destination without further incident.

On 10 August 2023, the privately registered Beechcraft Bonanza A35 (C-FKVI) was enroute from the Indus/Winters Aire Park Airport (CFY4), Alberta to the High River Airport (CEN4), Alberta for an annual maintenance inspection. Onboard was the pilot-in-command (PIC) and a second pilot. While on the downwind leg of the circuit at CEN4, the PIC initiated the pre-landing check, which was carried out by the second pilot seated in the right front seat. During the pre-landing check, the second pilot attempted to verify fuel selector position by feel since it was not visible due to the forward position of the PIC's seat. The second pilot inadvertently selected the fuel selector position to the OFF position. A few moments later, as the aircraft was turning final, at low altitude, the engine lost power due to fuel starvation. At 1543 Mountain Daylight Time, the PIC executed a forced landing in a farmer's field approximately 1 nautical mile east of CEN4. During the landing, the aircraft struck a fence, and sustained substantial damage. Shortly after the forced landing, police and emergency medical services attended the scene. Both occupants suffered minor injuries and were transported to hospital by ground ambulance. The emergency locator transmitter activated and a distress signal was detected by the search and rescue satellite system.

C-GJYZ, a DHC-8-314 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was preparing for flight JV1519 from Lansdowne House Airport (CYLH), Ontario, to Winnipeg International Airport (CYWG), Manitoba, with 3 crew and 27 passengers on board. The crew started engine #2 (RH engine), which is normally the first engine to be started. Although the parking brake had been set, the aircraft began to roll forward towards a chain link fence at the edge of the apron. The flight crew could not stop the aircraft from rolling forward using the aircraft normal braking system, which uses the hydraulic system which is powered by engine #1 (LH engine). The flight crew shut down the engine as the aircraft approached and fence, after which it struck and displaced the fence before making contact with a parked pickup truck on the other side of the fence. All passengers and crew safely deplaned, there are no injuries reported at time of deplanement. Damage to the aircraft was limited to the radome, and the fence and pickup truck were also damaged. Maintenance inspection revealed that there was a hole in the No. 4 brake flex line caused by chafing. The line has been replaced and the system serviced, bled and tested serviceable, and the radome was replaced before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FASB, a Beech King Air A100 operated by Thunder Airlines Ltd, was conducting flight THU101 from Timmins/Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON to Moosonee Airport (CYMO), ON with 2 crew and 7 passengers onboard. During the landing rollout following a normal landing on runway 24 at CYMO, the crew used propeller beta mode to slow the aircraft until approximately 60 knots before using the brakes, which is their normal practice. As the aircraft reached the last third of the runway, the brakes were applied. The pilot flying felt no pressure in the right pedal, and the left pedal felt spongy. The other pilot tried his brakes and experienced the same issue. The aircraft overran the runway and came to a stop in the grass approximately 40 feet from the runway end and just left of the extended centreline. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft. The maintenance personnel conducted an inspection and found a leak in the metal brake line at the brake caliper assembly. The brake line was repaired before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYSY, a privately registered Schweizer SGS 2-33 glider, was conducting a local training flight from Arthur/Walter's Field (CPC3), ON, with a solo student pilot onboard. During the base leg, the aircraft was observed to be pitching up higher than normal, causing the aircraft to slow down. The base-to-final turn was made at approximately 50 feet AGL, during which the aircraft was observed to bank suddenly to the right. The right wing made contact with the ground, followed by the nose of the aircraft, after which it came to rest in a normal upright position. The pilot was not injured. Damage to the aircraft was substantial, including damage to the right wing, nose cone, and fuselage.

C-FWSI, a WestJet Boeing 737-7CT, was conducting flight WJA346 from Comox Airport (CYQQ), BC, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. While taxiing, the aircraft had a ground collision with a parked Royal Canadian Air Force CC-130H Hercules aircraft (registration 130337). The Department of National Defence is investigating.

C-GUXZ, a Central Mountain Air Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-311 (Dash 8) was conducting flight GLR8570, under instrument flight rules, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Smithers Airport (CYYD), BC, with 3 crewmembers and 25 passengers on board. While enroute, the number 1 hydraulic system of the aircraft indicated a hydraulic fluid quantity of 0. There were no other indications of hydraulic issues with the number 1 system; it seemed to function normally. The crew completed the actions required to defer the number 1 hydraulic system under the provisions of the aircraft minimum equipment list (MEL). At 0920 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), the aircraft began to display intermittent secondary indications of a number 1 hydraulic system failure, including loss of hydraulic pressure and associated master caution lights. The crew actioned the items required by the aircraft quick reference handbook (QRH) for a number 1 hydraulic system failure and declared an emergency with air traffic control (ATC). At 0922 PDT, the crew initiated a diversion to Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC, where the aircraft landed without incident.Maintenance determined that the aircraft had a leak in the number 1 hydraulic system.

C-GUPL, an Air Canada A220-300 was operating flight AC543 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (KSEA), WA. On approach, the flight crew received a TCAS RA which was followed. After the maneuver, the aircraft was high on approach. A go-around was conducted, and the flight landed without further incident.

C-GYSJ, a Central Mountain Air Ltd. de Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-102 (Dash 8) was preparing to conduct flight GLR9316, under instrument flight rules, from Port Hardy Airport (CYZT), BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 3 crewmembers on board. At 1730 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), while on the apron in CYZT, the crew attempted to start the aircraft auxiliary power unit (APU). The start was unsuccessful, and the APU along with the aircraft batteries were cycled off prior to attempting a second start. During the second start attempt, ground crew observed black smoke coming from the tail section of the aircraft and informed the flight crew. A flight crew member exited the aircraft to visually observe the smoke and the crew concluded that they were experiencing an APU fire. The APU fault light inside the cockpit was illuminated, but the APU fire warning light was not. Manual discharge of the APU fire bottle was accomplished, and the fire department was called. Fire crews found high temperatures in the APU compartment but determined no further extinguishing agents were required.A maintenance inspection found no signs of fire within the APU but did find evidence of an APU generator overheat, along with damage to the APU generator. The APU generator was repaired, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GRDD, a North-Wright Aviation Inc. de Havilland DHC-6-100, was conducting a VFR flight in support of an outfitter located in the Godlin Lakes area of NWT. There were 2 crew, 4 passengers and cargo on board. Shortly after departure, the flight crew experience difficulty in roll control. The aileron control was stiff and required excessive force to move the control column. Rudder inputs were used and once at a safe height, the flaps were retracted and climb power was set. There was no change in the aileron control during the remainder of the flight to Norman Wells (CYVQ). The flight crew advised the company via satellite phone and on contact with CYVQ FSS, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN. A successful approach and landing was completed.Maintenance observations: The ceiling panel in the cabin, which covers the aileron cable run out to each wing, was removed and there were signs of distortion in the structure around the aileron quadrant. Groove marks were also noted where fuselage structure had interfered with the aileron quadrant.

C-GEGC, an Air Canada A330-343 was operating flight AC814 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Nice Côte d'Azur Airport (LFMN), France. In cruise, the flight crew received an ECAM “Green hyd low level”. The flight crew shut down the engine pumps as per checklist and a pan pan was declared. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GVFH, a Conair Group Incorporated BAE Systems RJ85, was conducting local firefighting operations as flight FGD561 under visual flight rules from Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, with 2 crewmembers on board. On the return to CYKA, on approach to Runway 09, during landing gear extension, a caution message indicating low fluid level in the GREEN hydraulic system occurred. The crew observed the associated hydraulic system quantity to be one third full and elected to continue the approach. After final flap selection, the associated hydraulic system quantity and pressure indicated zero. With selection of the airbrake, and with subsequent use of systems powered by the GREEN hydraulic system, the crew reported abnormal sounds, suspected to be hydraulic pump cavitation. After landing, the crew were able to clear the runway, onto Taxiway B, where the aircraft was shut down and towed to the tanker base. A maintenance inspection determined that there was a leak in a right-hand lift spoiler selector valve. The component was replaced, hydraulic fluid was replenished, and a successful ground function test was completed. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GUBH, an Air Transat A330-200 was operating flight TSC764 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport (LPPR), Porto, Portugal. During the cruise phase of the flight approximately 1200 nm west of LPPR, a cabin crew member sustained a minor injury and was unable to continue with duties. The safety related duties were redistributed amongst remaining crew and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FEKH, a Jazz Embraer 175, was operating flight AC8612 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS), MA. Just after top of descent, the aircraft encountered turbulence and a cabin crew member sustained a minor injury and was unable to continue duties. The remaining cabin crew assumed their duties and an Able-Bodied Passenger was briefed on the rear exits.

C-FYJH, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1820 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Puerto Plata International Airport (MDPP), Dominican Republic. During the cruise phase of flight, at FL350, HYD G RSVR LO LVL ECAM was received by the flight crew. The flight crew carried out ECAM actions, declared PAN PAN and initiated a return. The manual landing gear extension was carried out and a full-stop overweight landing was subsequently carried out on CYYZ RWY 33R with ARFF on standby. ARFF conducted a general visual inspection, and the aircraft was towed to the gate.

C-FRWK, an MU-2B-60 operated by Thunder Airlines Ltd., was conducting flight THU850 from Sault Ste. Marie Airport (CYAM), Ontario, to Greater Sudbury Airport (CYSB), Ontario. During the takeoff run at CYAM, shortly before rotation speed, the flight crew felt a vibration in the rudder pedals. They elected to continue to CYSB, and requested a low fly-by for a visual inspection of the landing gear, and that ARFF be standing by for their landing. The visual inspection did not reveal an obvious issue, and the crew made a normal approach and landing, and taxiied to their hangar. After shutdown, the crew observed that the nosewheel was completely deflated. The tire was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GLQD, a DHC-8-400 operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE2473 from  Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), Ontario, to Montréal–Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), Quebec. While enroute, in the vicinity of Cornwall, Ontario, the flight crew declared an emergency due to a medical situation with a passenger. ATC arranged to have EMS standing by at the gate, the aircraft landed safely at CYUL at 1913Z.

TC-LLG, a Boeing 787-9 operated by Turkish Airlines, was conducting flight TK134 from George Bush Intercontinental Airport (KIAH), VA, USA, to Istanbul Airport (LTFM), Turkey. During cruise at FL370 in the vicinity of Toronto, Ontario, the flight crew declared PAN PAN with the Toronto ACC due to an onboard medical emergency. The flight was given priority and vectored north of Toronto Lester B Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) where they dumped fuel to reduce weight, before being vectored for landing on Runway 23 at CYYZ.

CF-CEZ, un appareil de type American Aviation AA-5 d'immatriculation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue, de l'aéroport Ottawa/Gatineau, Gatineau, QC (CYND) à destination de l'aérodrome désafecté du lac Nilgaut situé à environ 97 Nm au nord ouest de CYND, avec à son bord le pilote et une passagère. Lors du vol de retour vers CYND, en descente à 4500 pi, le pilote a déclaré une urgence, suite à une panne de carburant, et a effectué un atterrissage dans un champs à environ 20NM au nord ouest de CYND. L'aéronef a subi des dommages substantiels mais les occupants n'ont pas étés blessés.

At 1951 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) on 3 August 2023, a privately registered Flight Design CTSW advanced ultralight (registration C-IPCT, serial number 06-08-19) departed the Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC, on a Nav Canada filed visual flight rules (VFR) flight plan with the pilot and one passenger on board. The flight planned route was a 132 nautical mile round trip that included 3 waypoints southeast of CYXS with no stops indicated. The first waypoint was 53° 15', 121° 25' W which coincides with the location of the Bowron Lake Lodge Airstrip. The second waypoint was the south end of Bowron Lake (53° 12’ N, 121° 18’ W), then east to a point south of Two Sisters Mountain (53° 10’ N, 121° 34’ W) and then northwest back to CYXS. The aircraft was seen as it approached the airstrip at Bowron Lake from the east. The Bowron Lake Airstrip is privately owned and requires prior permission for persons to land. The aircraft continued over the campground area of the Bowron Lake Lodge and witnesses observed the aircraft begin to fly at low level along the length of the airstrip from east to west. At approximately 2025 PDT, the aircraft impacted trees and level terrain approximately 300 feet beyond the western end of the airstrip and approximately 20 feet south of the extended centreline. There was a post impact fire, and the airplane was destroyed. Both occupants were fatally injured.Witnesses heard a bang, and a plume of smoke was seen coming from the west end of the runway. The descent and impact were not seen by any witnesses, no radar coverage was available of the occurrence, and the aircraft did not have a flight data recorder. People in the area went to the site and found the aircraft and the immediate surroundings in flames. A search was conducted in the vicinity with no survivors found. Emergency services attended the scene. The Canadian Mission Control Centre did not receive a signal from the aircraft’s 406 MHz emergency locater transmitter (ELT). Due to the nature of the impact and the post-impact fire, it could not be determined why no signal was transmitted.The trees surrounding the wreckage were between 20 feet and 60 feet high. Directly above the wreckage, 3 large tree branches had been broken off on 3 different trees. There was a broken branch near each wing tip and one above the fuselage. The aircraft was pointing in a northerly direction. The wreckage itself was contained within a circular area with a diameter of approximately 28 feet with the cockpit, landing gear, and engine confined to a circle approximately 4 feet in diameter. The aircraft's small debris field is indicative of a steep vertical descent.Local police conducted a search of the airstrip and the area surrounding the occurrence site and did not find any aircraft components. The aircraft was manufactured in 2006 and there were no recorded defects outstanding at the time of the occurrence. Due to the nature of the impact and the post-impact fire, it could not be determined if a component or system malfunction played a role in this occurrence. The pilot held a private pilot licence – aeroplane, endorsed with a blanket type rating for all single-pilot, non-high performance, single-engine, landplanes and had a valid Category 3 medical certificate. According to information gathered during the investigation, there was no indication that the pilot’s performance was affected by medical or physiological factors.UPDATED:16 February 2024

C-GOFU, un hélicoptère Robinson R44 exploité par Héli-Tremblant effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’héliport de Mont-Tremblant / St-Jovite Héli-Tremblant, QC (CHT3) à destination du Lac à l’Eau Claire, St-Alexis des Monts, QC avec 1 pilote et 2 passagers à bord. Après l’atterrissage en pente, l’appareil a basculé sur le sabot de queue. Le pilote a tenté de redresser l'appareil et le nez de l’hélicoptère a percuté le sol avant de se poser à nouveau. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé, toutefois l’hélicoptère a subi des dommages importants.

C-GYJJ, a Montair Aviation Incorporated Cessna 152, was conducting a local training flight under visual flight rules from Pitt Meadows Airport (CYPK), BC, with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. At 1336 Pacific Daylight Time it was reported that the aircraft engine (Lycoming O-235-L2C) began to run rough, with a vibration observed of the instrument panel. A gradual decrease in engine RPM followed. Full power was subsequently commanded via throttle input but was not achieved by the engine. The power produced by the engine was not sufficient to maintain altitude. The pilot contacted CYPK tower and advised air traffic control (ATC) that the aircraft was experiencing engine issues. ATC cleared the aircraft for a straight-in approach to Runway 18. The aircraft engine continued to lose power, and the pilot elected to perform a precautionary landing north of CYPK after determining they would be unable to reach the airport. The engine subsequently lost all power, and a forced landing was performed. The aircraft landed in a field, approximately 4.7 nautical miles northeast of CYPK. During the landing roll, the aircraft descended an embankment into a water filled ditch, nosed over, and came to rest upside-down. The pilot and passenger were able to egress the aircraft, and no injuries were reported. The aircraft emergency locator transmitter (ELT) automatically activated, and emergency services attended the scene. The aircraft was substantially damaged.The aircraft was recovered from the site and transported back to CYPK where the damage will be assessed.

C-GBZS, a Sunwing B737-800 was preparing for flight TOM7740 from Birmingham Airport (EGBB), UK to Tenerife Sur Reina Sofia (GCTS), Spain when a fuel spill occurred while boarding was taking place. The boarding was stopped and passengers subsequently deplaned. Fire services attended the aircraft and sweepers cleaned up the spill. Boarding re-commenced an hour later and the aircraft took off without further incident

C-GLQV, a Porter Dash 8-400 was operating flight POE2128 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. On departure from KEWR, awaiting next sector climb, in the midst of several frequency changes, the aircraft encountered a cell with other cells on either side. Unable to obtain deviation permission due to ATC workload, the flight crew elected to enter the cloud and started slowing down the aircraft. A "cabin crew be seated" PA was made and complied with; the passenger seatbelt sign was still on from departure. The aircraft experienced severe turbulence including momentary loss of control, which was promptly regained. A passenger, with seatbelt not fastened, sustained a minor injury when their head hit the overhead bin.Porter Airlines Technical Operations conducted a "heavy turbulence" inspection as per OEM. No faults were found.

C-FWTX, an Ayres S2R-T34 aircraft operated by FARR Air Inc., departed from a private strip in the area of Coronach SK. to conduct aerial application to crops. During an application run, the aircraft struck a power line. The pilot completed a precautionary landing on rural road 2251, located approximately 2 miles from the power line. There were no injuries to the pilot. RCMP, fire services and EMS attended the scene. There was minor damage to the aircraft. SaskPower was informed of the wire strike. The aircraft was inspected at scene by the operator's maintenance, a ferry permit was obtained, and the aircraft was flown to a maintenance base for further repairs.

C-GHSG, an amateur-built Vans Aircraft RV-9A, was conducting a local flight in the area of Humboldt, Saskatchewan. The pilot overflew a property at approximately 500 feet AGL in slow flight when the aircraft engine (Avco Lycoming IO-320-D2A[X]) started to run rough. The pilot advanced the mixture and throttle, and selected the boost pump to "on". The aircraft continued to lose power and altitude and the pilot decided to land the aircraft on a dirt road. Upon landing, the left wing made contact with a canola crop. The aircraft turned left, and the aircraft flipped over its nose. There was no fire and the ELT did activate. The pilot, who was trapped in the cockpit, made a cell phone call to someone so that they could call to activate an emergency response. First responders arrived within 1.5 hours of the occurrence and extricated the pilot from the wreckage. EMS attended to the pilot. There were no injuries.

N647RW, un Embraer 170-100 SE exploité par Republic Airlines Inc. sous l’indicatif RPA3451, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC à destination de Newark (KEWR) aux États-Unis. Lors du décollage sur la piste 24L une indication de feu au moteur gauche est apparue. L’équipage a rejeté le décollage et a circulé au centre de dégivrage pour effectuer des vérifications. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés et l’aéronef a été inspecté. Il n’y avait aucune trace de feu ni de fumée. Les passagers sont débarqués à l’aide de véhicule transbordeur (PTV), il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-GURM, un Dash-8-300 (DH8C) exploité par le service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, sous l'indicatif QUE40, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à destination de Roberval, QC (CYRJ). Alors que l’appareil passait 9000 pieds en descente, une perte d’espacement est survenue lorsqu’il s’est retrouvé à 4,7 miles marins du C-FWUF, un Piper PA-28R en palier à 9000 pieds en vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments en direction est. L’espacement requis était de 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical et 5 miles marins sur le plan horizontal. Les 2 appareils ont poursuivi leurs vols à destination sans encombre.

C-FGKP, an Air Canada Airbus A321, was operating as flight AC171 from Toronto Intl Airport (CYYZ), ON to Edmonton Intl. Airport (CYEG), AB with 10 crew and 142 passengers on board. During the taxi after landing in CYEG, the flight crew reported a brake failure and stopped for an inspection. ARFF was called as a precaution. Airstairs were used to deplane the passengers.Maintenance follow up: Air Canada maintenance found that the brake pistons for the number 2 brake system were damaged and seized.

C-GQJA, a Bombardier CL600-2B19 (CRJ-200) operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8197 from Toronto/Pearson Int'l Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, to Sault Ste Marie Airport (CYAM), Ontario, with 3 crew and 34 passengers on board. Shortly after landing gear up was selected, the crew received a "GEAR DISAGREE" warning message accompanied by messages related to weight on wheels faults. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist, which led to a manual gear extension. The alternate gear extension handle could not be stowed properly, and the flight crew declared PAN PAN and requested ARFF to be present for the landing. After coming to a stop on the runway, and after ARFF inspected the landing gear and determined that it was safe for them to taxi to the gate, the crew received a "HYD 3 HI TEMP" warning message. They actioned the appropriate checklist, which resolved that issue. After realizing that the nosewheel steering was inoperative due to the position of the alternate gear extension handle, the aircraft was towed to the gate where the passengers deplaned normally.  Maintenance determined that the nose gear oleo was not fully extended, resulting in the landing gear position sensors providing a fault message. The oleo was serviced with no further fault messages received. The "HYD 3 HI TEMP" message determined to be related to fluid bypass occurring because the alternate landing gear extension handle was not able to be stowed. Maintenance determined the manual release handle was unservicable and replaced it before returning the aircraft to service.

C-FNBP, un Cessna modèle 152 exploité par Orizon Aviation, effectuait un vol local d'entrainement selon les règles de vol à vue, à partir de l'aéroport Jean Lesage Intl de Québec, QC (CYQB) avec seul le pilote à son bord. Lors de l'atterrissage sur la piste 24, l'aéronef a rebondi sur la surface de la piste pour ensuite sortir de piste du côté sud. Le pilote a alors appliqué les gaz et l'aéronef a repris l'air en direction sud pour ensuite effectuer un virage à droite en direction nord perpendiculairement à l'axe de piste. Dans sa remontée, l'aile gauche de l'aéronef a décroché et celui-ci s'est écrasé sur la surface de la piste 24. Le pilote a été blessé et il n'y a pas eu d'incendie.

C-FXDE, un Beechcraft A100 exploité par Exact Air inc. sous l’indicatif ET828, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Havre-St-Pierre, QC (CYGV) à destination de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) avec 2 pilotes à bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en palier au niveau de vol 200, le voyant principal d'avertissement s’est mis à clignoter, mais aucune anomalie n’était perçue. Par la suite, l’autopilote a fait des corrections d’altitude intempestives. L’autopilote a été débranché et l’équipage a réalisé que la gouverne de profondeur était bloquée, mais que l’altitude pouvait être contrôlé avec le compensateur de profondeur. Une urgence a été déclarée. Lors de la descente, la gouverne de profondeur s’est débloquée et le contrôle de l’avion est revenu à la normale. L’appareil s’est posé à CYRC sans encombre et il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage. Une inspection a révélé qu’un drain dans la queue était bouché par des insectes, qui a causé une accumulation d’eau dans la queue, qui a pu geler et empêcher le mouvement d’une poulie sur le câble de la gouverne de profondeur.

C-GOFV, an Air Canada A330-343 was operating flight AC71 from Algiers International Airport Houari Boumediene (DAAG), Algeria to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. On take off, the crew reported hitting a flock of seagulls on R/H side of the aircraft. Subsequently, the crew received multiple ECAM messages. The crew began actioning the checklist, the decision was made to return to DAAG. A Pan Pan was declared and the flight landed without incident. ARFF met the aircraft and was cleared to taxi to gate.Engine #2 inspection performed and probe replaced as per AMM. Found blade fan 18 bent.

C-FGDT, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC826 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Copenhagen Airport (EKCH), Denmark. During descent, the flight crew reported a burning smell in the flight deck and cabin. The flight crew requested emergency services to meet the aircraft on arrival. The flight landed, stopped on runway and emergency services cleared the aircraft after inspection. The smell returned and smoke was visible, the aircraft shut down on the taxi way; airstairs were requested for passenger deplanement. No injuries reported.

N926FM, an Embraer EMB-135ER aircraft operated by RVR Air Charter LLC., was conducting a flight under instrument flight rules from Campbell River (CYBL), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC. While backtracking onto Runway 12 for departure, the aircraft experienced a nose wheel steering problem. The aircraft was subsequently towed off the runway.A maintenance inspection found that a microswitch in the aircraft steering system had failed. The microswitch was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTEM, an Alkan Air Limited Beech B300 (King Air), was conducting flight AKN236 under instrument flight rules from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Whitehorse/Eric Nielsen International (CYXY), YT, with 2 crewmembers and 3 passengers on board. At 0441 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) the crew received taxi clearance for a departure from Runway 08L from CYVR ground control. The issued taxi clearance was via Taxiway Alpha, Hotel, clearance to cross Runway 08R, Juliette, Mike, Mike 8 to Runway 08L. The aircraft began taxing at 0443 PDT. At 0446 PDT, the aircraft taxied onto a portion of taxiway Hotel that was closed via notice to airmen (NOTAM) C2398/23. The aircraft subsequently struck a lit barrier while travelling at a speed of approximately 30 knots. This sheared the nose gear below the torque link, and the aircraft propellers, subsequently, contacted the surface of the taxiway. The crew shut down the engines and reported a landing gear collapse to CYVR ground control before evacuating the aircraft. Emergency services attended the scene. There were no reported injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FMOC, a Boeing 757-200 operated by Morningstar Air Express was conducting flight MAL8062 from Toronto/Pearson Int'l Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, to Moncton/Romeo Leblanc Int'l Airport (CYQM), New Brunswick, with two pilots on board. The flight crew received a taxi clearance to taxi via taxiway J and hold short at the CAT I line. While holding short at the CAT 1 line, they received further clearance to continue on taxiway J and hold short of runway 05/23. The aircraft failed to hold short of the line, and an aircraft on approach was instructed to go around as a result.

C-FGZE, a McDonnell Douglas A-4N aircraft was operating a flight out of Nordholz/Cuxhaven Airport (ETMN), Germany. During straight and level flight with a steady power setting, an audible "bang" occurred combined with a perceived yawing movement to the left. The aircraft quickly returned to coordinated flight on its own and continued straight and leveled. The pilot monitored the engine and systems indications which were all normal. The same occurred again 5 minutes later. The pilot elected to abort the mission, declared an emergency and land the aircraft as soon as possible. The other formation member executed a visual inspection of the incident aircraft but no damage was noted. The aircraft landed in Royal Air Force Lakenheath (EGUL), Suffolk, England without further incident.

C-FNNP, an amateur-built amphibious-equipped Super 22 Bushmaster airplane, was conducting a VFR flight from Virden (CTVD), MB to Oak Lake Beach MB. While landing at Oak Lake Beach, the aircraft landed hard and became partially submerged.  There were no injuries to the pilot or passenger. The aircraft was substantially damaged. It was reported that glassy water conditions existed at the time of landing.

C-FCCY, a Piper PA-32R, was conducting a VFR flight from Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB to Salmon Arm (CZAM), BC with 1 pilot and 5 passengers on board. The aircraft departed CYBW at 2047 MDT on 28 July 2023 and was reported overdue early the following morning. A strong ELT signal was heard by overflying aircraft in the vicinity of Bow Valley Provincial Park, Kananaskis, AB. Search and rescue assets located the aircraft on the east slope of Mt. McGillivray, AB on 29 July. All 6 occupants were fatally injured and the aircraft was destroyed; there was a post impact fire.

C-FZVP, an Air Nootka Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-2 MK 1 (Beaver) aircraft on floats, was conducting a flight from Louie Lagoon, Nootka Island, BC, to Gold River (CAU6), BC, with only the pilot on board. During approach to land on the river mouth near the CAU6 dock, the aircraft entered an abrupt turn to the right, impacted the trees and came to rest in the forest approximately 50 meters from the river's edge. The pilot was seriously injured. The aircraft was significantly damaged. The aircraft was recovered to a maintenance facility at the Campbell River Airport (CYBL) for examination.

C-GYWJ, a Westjet Airlines Boeing 737-7CT, was conducting flight WJA385 under instrument flight rules from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, with 5 crew members and 86 passengers on board. At 1037 PDT, while on approach for Runway 26R at CYVR, the flight crew selected the flaps to 30, and then received an indication of a flap asymmetry. The crew advised air traffic control (ATC) that they would be conducting a missed approach and flew a missed approach procedure. While on radar vectors, the crew carried out the quick reference handbook (QRH) checklist for a trailing edge (TE) flap asymmetry. Upon completion of the checklist, a PAN PAN was declared with ATC. The aircraft landed on Runway 26R without further incident. The aircraft was inspected by aircraft rescue and fire fighting personnel and then taxied to the gate without assistance.A maintenance inspection of the aircraft was performed. They replaced and did maintenance on 4 flap skew sensors in the right wing. Additionally, they repaired damaged wiring and replaced the right flap position transmitter connector. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GRCA, a Cessna 152 operated by AFS Aerial Photography, was conducting a photo flight west of Lethbridge, Alberta (CYQL). After approximately 5 hours of flight time, the engine (AVCO LYCOMING, O-235-L2C) began to lose power and the aircraft started to descend. The pilot adjusted the throttle and mixture, applied carburetor heat but was unable to restore engine power. A forced approach and landing was performed on a gravel road approximately 26 nm WNW of CYQL. During the landing roll, the right outer wing made contact with a road sign post and significantly damaged the leading edge. Post occurrence, the aircraft was defueled for transport and revealed only unusable fuel in both the left- and right-wing fuel tanks.

C-FIYQ, a Cessna 414 owned and operated by ITPS Canada Ltd., was conducting a flight from Montréal-Mirabel International Airport (CYMX), Quebec, to London International Airport (CYXU), Ontario, with one pilot and one passenger on board. The aircraft had been recently purchased by ITPS Canada Ltd.; the purpose of this flight was to bring the aircraft to its new home base at CYXU. During cruise flight at 3000 feet ASL, and approximately 8nm NNE of CYXU, both engines stopped producing power. The pilot made a forced landing in a bean field, there were no injuries and no damage observed to the aircraft.Before leaving CYMX, the pilot had requested that the fuel tanks be filled, and records indicate that 46 gallons of fuel had been added to the fuel tanks by a fueler who was familiar with this particular aircraft, although the pilot had not checked the quantity before fueling took place. The pilot did not physically check the fuel levels before departure, and although the fuel gauges showed less than full tanks, the pilot proceeded under the assumption that they were displaying an incorrect quantity.Initial examination of the aircraft revealed no damage, and the aircraft was brought via ground transportation to a hangar at CYXU, where the maintenance is conducting a detailed check of the aircraft.The safety officer for the company has initiated an SMS investigation into this event.

N323BT, an amateur-built float-equipped OBT Sportsman airplane, was conducting a VFR flight from Rainy Lake, ON to Lake Winnipeg, MB. While enroute, the aircraft encountered turbulence followed by an unusual feeling in the flight controls. The aircraft abruptly entered uncontrolled flight. The pilot attempted to recover control but was unable to and the aircraft collided with terrain 19NM NNE of Silver Falls Airport, MB (CKB8). The ELT activated and search and rescue responded. The pilot was severely injured and was airlifted to hospital. The aircraft was destroyed. TSB investigators examined the aircraft wreckage after it was recovered. The right aileron control rod exhibited evidence of corrosion and the right aileron control rod end was found separated at its junction with the control rod tube. The right aileron control horn front attachment screw exhibited wear likely from interference with the control rod.

C-GFFG, a privately registered Cessna 150B aircraft, was conducting circuits at Alexandria, Ontario (CNS4) with two pilots on board: a private pilot and an instructor pilot. Shortly after taking off from Runway 25, the aircraft experienced a partial engine power loss. A 180-degree return was accomplished, and the aircraft was repositioned over runway 07, but significantly down the runway. Engine power was re-applied, and the aircraft began to climb again. Shortly afterwards, the engine power decreased more considerably; the aircraft entered a steep right bank, followed by a steep nose down attitude and impact with terrain. The aircraft was destroyed, one person was fatally injured, and one received serious injuries. TSB deployed to the site.

C-GWJF, a WestJet Boeing 737, was operating flight WJA778 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Windsor Airport (CYQG), ON. During climb on departure from CYYC, a loss of separation occurred with an overflying, privately registered Mooney M20R, N617DH which was on a flight from Fort St. John Airport (CYXJ), BC to Lethbridge Airport (CYQL), AB. Separation reduced to 2.5 miles laterally and 1000 feet vertically where 3 miles laterally and 1000 feet vertically is required.

C-GQHV, a Piper PA-31-350 aircraft operated by Eagle Air Enterprises, was conducting a day VFR flight from St. Theresa Point (CYST), MB to Winnipeg/St. Andrews Airport (CYAV), MB. As the aircraft was taxiing for departure on Runway 22, the pilot was informed by FSS that there were two service vehicles on the runway and that the vehicles were to report when exiting on the taxiway. Communications between the service vehicles and FSS was intermittent. The pilot proceeded to takeoff Runway 22. Once airborne, the pilot announced their departure. Shortly after, FSS stated that the second service vehicle was still in the runway environment during the aircraft's takeoff roll. The flight continued to CYAV without incident.

The Synergy Aviation Ltd Robinson R44II, C-FZQX, was departing Villeneuve Airport (CZVL), AB on a flight to Swan Hills (CEM5), AB with an apparatus containing a gas leak detector and a thermal camera attached to the cargo hook. The helicopter was cleared to the north, transiting over Taxiway Bravo, when a noise was heard from the rear seat area. Shortly thereafter Villeneuve Tower called to inform the crew that something had fallen from the aircraft, and it was laying on Taxiway Bravo. The flight crew requested a return and landed midfield to investigate. It was determined that the detection unit had fallen from the aircraft. Both flight crew confirmed that the manual release had not been activated during the departure. There was no damage to the helicopter or the detection assembly.Maintenance update: Upon further investigation it was determined that the cargo was not faulty; however, it was found that the manual release handle was not in the fully down position and may have allowed the hook to open due to vibration.

N55PJ, a Gulfstream IV aircraft operated by Pegasus Elite as PEG55, was conducting a flight from Farnborough Airport (EGLF), England to Teterboro Airport (KTEB), NJ. During cruise, the crew experienced a converter failure. The crew declared a PAN PAN and diverted to Gander Intl (CYQX), NL, where the aircraft landed without further issue.On the ground, in coordination with maintenance, the crew completed the converter reset procedure as per the Gulfstream AFM and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FVLX, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating flight AC091 from São Paulo-Guarulhos International Airport (SBGR), Brazil to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. In cruise, the left and right pack failed, the cabin temperature was at 31C. In discussion with dispatch and maintenance, the decision was made to return to SBGR. A PAN PAN was declared and the flight landed without further incident.

C-GUBT, an Air Transat A330-243 was operating flight TSC403 from Leonardo da Vinci International Airport (LIRF), Rome, Italy to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. In the cruise phase of flight, a flight attendant became incapacitated. Duties were redistributed and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

The Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Lockheed L188C, C-FLXT, was operating as ASB481 from Red Deer (CYQF), AB to Williams Lake (CYWL), BC. During the climb to cruise the flight crew observed large fluctuations on the #2 propeller (AEROPRODUCTS, A6441FN-606A S/N HC683) and a resulting pitch lock. The #2 engine (ALLISON, 501-D13 S/N CAE501265) was shut down as a precaution and the flight returned to CYQF and landed uneventfully. Maintenance Update: The #2 propeller regulator was found to be at fault. Regulator S/N R895 removed and regulator S/N R1145 installed. Ground run and pitch lock check completed with no faults found and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-IIJZ, a Quad City Challenger II equipped with wheels, took off from Guelph, Ontario (CNC4) for a local flight. While airborne, the pilot suddenly heard a loud noise emanating from the engine, which was followed by a loss of power. At that moment, the aircraft was flying over Lake Belwood, near Fergus, Ontario, at an altitude of approximately 900 feet AGL. Consequently, the pilot made a forced landing on the water. Shortly after touching down, the aircraft began to sink. The pilot egressed the aircraft and was later rescued by local residents. The pilot sustained only minor injuries and was taken to the hospital for evaluation.
