C-GDJU, a privately registered, amateur built Murphy Rebel airplane, was conducting a local flight under visual flight rules for the purpose of flying circuits at Vernon Airport (CYVK), BC, with only the pilot on board. At 1155 Pacific Daylight Time, the aircraft took-off from Runway 23 and conducted one left-hand circuit. The tail wheel equipped aircraft was landed in a 3-point attitude and touched down approximately 116 feet prior to the displaced threshold of Runway 23. A 15 knot crosswind, indicated by an airport wind sock at the time of landing, was reported. The maximum demonstrated crosswind component for the aircraft is 14 knots. The aircraft traveled approximately 700 feet from the point of touch-down, along the runway center line, slowing to a speed of approximately 45 knots before it began to veer left. Right rudder was applied but the aircraft departed the left side of the runway. After departing the paved surface of the runway, the left main landing gear collapsed, resulting in the left wingtip and the propeller striking the ground. The aircraft came to rest approximately 1000 feet from the threshold of Runway 23, and approximately 100 feet to the left of the runway centerline. There were no injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. Emergency services attended the scene.The aircraft was recovered and will be assessed for repairs.

C-FRQA, a Canadian North/Bradley Air Service ATR72-200, was operating as flight AKT5844 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Cambridge Bay (CYCB), NU. While in cruise the flight crew observed a loss of hydraulic oil with the illumination of the green hydraulic system low level indicator. An emergency was declared, and the crew elected to return to CYZF. An uneventful landing took place at CYZF.Maintenance update: The right-hand main landing gear lower #4 brake pressure feed flexible hydraulic hose was found chafed and leaking due to contact with an adjacent electrical connector. The hose was replaced and the brake lines were bled in accordance with the applicable maintenance guidance. The aircraft ground check serviceable and was returned to service.

N420PD, a Falcon 900EX aircraft operated by SC Aviation, was conducting a flight from Chicago Midway Intl airport (KMDW), IL to Milano Bresso airport (LIMB), Italy. During cruise, the crew requested a diversion to Gander Intl (CYQX), NL due to minimum fuel, where the aircraft landed without further issue. No emergency was declared.Maintenance determined that a fuel line break had occurred. The aircraft is awaiting repair before returning to service.

C-FHIW, a privately registered Cessna 182G, was conducting a flight under visual flight rules from Tofino/Long Beach Airport (CYAZ), BC, to Duncan Airport (CAM3), BC, with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. The aircraft landed on Runway 31, touching down at or near the threshold at a speed of approximately 70 knots. Heavy rain and wet runway conditions were observed at the time of touch-down. Upon landing, the pilot retracted flaps and applied brakes. The braking and the nose wheel steering appeared to be ineffective which is consistent with hydroplaning. With approximately 500 feet of runway remaining, the pilot attempted to steer the aircraft off the left side of the runway with the application of full left rudder, with no result. The aircraft exited the end of the runway surface on or near the centerline. The paved surface ends 75 feet after the runway threshold marking. A rough embankment, which drops approximately 10 feet over a distance of approximately 45 feet, begins approximately 15 feet after that. The airplane nosed over and came to rest inverted at the bottom of the embankment. There was no post-crash fire, and no activation of the aircraft emergency locator transmitter. The pilot and passenger were able to egress the aircraft via the pilot's door. There were no injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FQNS, an Airbus Helicopters AS 350 B-2 aircraft operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited, was conducting external load operations about 6 nm west of Wabush airport (CYWK), NL. While slinging drill rods to a remote site, rods came loose in the load bundle. Eventually, the entire load fell from the sling gear into forested terrain and a river about 7 nm west of CYWK. The external load operations were stopped, and the crew debriefed the occurrence. There was no injury, and no damage to the aircraft or to the environment occurred.

C-GNCH, a Sunwing B737-800 was operating flight TOM7795 from Málaga-Costa del Sol Airport (LEMG), Spain to East Midlands Airport (EGNX), UK. During descent at 8000ft, a flight crew member became ill and was temporarily unable to conduct pilot monitoring duties, but able to resume duties after interception of the ILS. The flight landed safely without issue.

C-FWSV, a Westjet Airlines Boeing 737-7CT, was conducting flight WS309 under instrument flight rules from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, to Comox Airport (CYQQ), BC, with 5 crew members and 120 passengers on board. At 1927 PDT, while on the Required Navigation Performance (RNP) Y approach for Runway 30 at CYQQ, the flight crew selected the flaps to 15 and then received an indication of a flap asymmetry. The flight crew conducted a missed approach, declared a PAN PAN, and entered the published hold. While in the hold, the flight crew carried out the quick reference handbook (QRH) checklist for a trailing edge (TE) flap asymmetry. The crew exited the hold and, while being vectored for a subsequent approach, declared a MAYDAY in response to a concern regarding remaining fuel quantity on board. They carried out the QRH fuel low checklist and then landed without further incident. The aircraft was inspected by the fire department on the runway before taxiing under its own power to the gate. On shutdown, the aircraft indicated 3300 pounds of fuel remaining.On inspection, maintenance found the trailing edge flap indicator and the alternate flap drive motor to be inoperative. Both were replaced, a successful function was conducted, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSWN, an Iskwew Air Piper PA-31-350 (Chieftain) airplane, was conducting flight SG309 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Qualicum Beach Airport (CAT4), BC, with the pilot an 2 passengers on board. After takeoff, the pilot selected gear up but the gear would not retract. It appeared that the the nose gear wheel was turned 90° to the airplane. The pilot requested an inspection pass by the air traffic control tower who confirmed that the nose gear was sideways to the aircraft. Aircraft fire fighting rescue (ARFF) crews and equipment were put on standby. The pilot landed the aircraft and sparks and smoke came from the nose gear wheel and tire. The aircraft was stopped on the runway and was met by ARFF. The passengers were deplaned and the aircraft remained on the runway for approximately 3.5 hours while a tow was being arranged. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained minor damage.It was determined that the nose gear's upper and lower torque link assemblies were not connected.

C-FLRJ, a BAE Systems RJ85 airplane, operated by Summit Air Limited, was conducting flight SUT101 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Masset (CZMT), BC, under instrument flight rules with 4 crew members and 62 passengers on board. Approaching CZMT, the crew conducted the Area Navigation (RNAV) Z approach to Runway 13 but were unable to achieve the necessary visual references to continue to the landing. A missed approach was conducted, and a second approach was attempted. During the second approach, approximately 2 miles from the intermediate fix, a fire warning light illuminated for the No. 2 engine. The engine fire drill was conducted, resulting in the discharge of both engine fire bottles, and the shutdown of the No. 2 engine. The fire warning light remained illuminated, along with an intermittent fire warning bell. The crew declared an emergency, and diverted to Sandspit (CYZP), BC. While on approach to CYZP, the fire warning light extinguished. The aircraft landed without incident with emergency services standing by.A subsequent maintenance inspection conducted by Summit Air Limited found that 2 pins of a connector in the fire warning system had partially shorted together. The connector was replaced, and the engine fire detection system was tested and found serviceable. The aircraft was returned to service.

N109DV, an amateur-built Durand Mark V, was operating on a VFR flight from Whetstone International, Del Bonita (CEQ4), AB to High River (CEN4), AB. During the take-off roll the prevailing wind resulted in a crosswind condition. Directional control was lost and the aircraft struck a barbed wire fence on the north side of the runway.  The aircraft came to rest in a farmer's field with extensive damage. There were no injuries to the lone occupant. The ELT did not activate and there was no fire.

C-FFNE, a Boeing 737-400 aircraft operated by Canadian North (Bradley Air Services Ltd), was conducting flight AKT129 from Ottawa Macdonald - Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON to Iqaluit International Airport (CYFB), NU with 4 crew and 72 passengers onboard. While on initial climb at approximately 400 feet, the #1 engine Exhaust Gas Temperature (EGT) exceedance light illuminated. The crew actioned their memory and the quick reference checklist (QRC) items, and the EGT exceedance light subsequently extinguished within a half inch of thrust lever movement. The flight crew declared an emergency (PAN PAN) with Air Traffic Control (ATC) and were provided holding instructions.  While in the hold burning fuel to the maximum landing weight, a passenger had a panic attack which precipitated a planned overweight landing. AKT129 landed into CYOW runway 32 where Airport Rescue and firefighting (ARFF) vehicles were standing by. ARFF inspected the landing gear, and the aircraft was cleared to the gate. Maintenance conducted a borescope inspection of engine #1 and found damage out of limits on a High Pressure (HP) blade. An engine change is scheduled.

C-FNPY, a privately registered Robinson R44 Raven II helicopter was on a visual flight rules trip from Vancouver/Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC, to Meager Creek Hot Springs (50º34'32" N, 123º27'53" W) with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. On final approach, at approximately 20 feet above ground level, the helicopter entered an uncontrollable decent. The main rotor hit trees and the helicopter collided with level terrain. The temperature at the time was approximately 33° C and there was a tail wind present of approximately 8 knots. There were no injuries. The helicopter was substantially damaged. The pilot and passenger were picked up at site by another helicopter whose pilot was contacted via a text from a satellite communication device.The helicopter was recovered to a maintenance facility at Fort Langley (CBQ2) to be inspected.

C-GXKQ, a float equipped privately registered Cessna 182P, was on a recreational flight from Bonnyville (CYBF), AB to Stoney Lake AB which is 13 NM to the SE of St. Paul (CEW3). On arrival overhead Stoney Lake, two passes were made to inspect the lake conditions for landing before the landing attempt was made. On the landing, the flare was misjudged due to glassy water conditions and the aircraft bounced 3 times. On the third bounce the nose of the floats caught the water and the aircraft tumbled forward which resulted in the aircraft being inverted in the water. The aircraft remained on the surface of the lake attached to the floats. Both occupants were able to exit the aircraft and a passing boater gave them a ride to shore. The ELT did not activate.

C-FGKN, an Airbus A321-211 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA139 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Shortly after takeoff from CYYZ, while climbing to cruise altitude, the flight crew declared emergency (Pan Pan) with air traffic control (ATC) due to a hydraulic system issue. The flight crew subsequently elected to return to CYYZ and landed runway 15L without further incident.

C-GDVF, an amateur built, Vincent Lane Scott Safari, departed the London International Airport (CYXU), ON, for an initial flight after construction. Shortly after becoming airborne, while the pilot was attempting to land back on the remaining runway, the aircraft landed hard, the landing gear collapsed, and the aircraft sustained substantial damage. There were no injuries.

C-GYFM, an Airbus A321-211 aircraft operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1910 from Kelowna International Airport (CYLW), BC to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON with 6 crew and 161 passengers onboard. While on-route, descending through approximately 8000 feet, flight ROU1910 penetrated an unexpected active frontal weather system where it encountered moderate turbulence and intense and heavy precipitation not previously detected by the onboard weather radar. The flight crew observed suspected external static discharge from the aircraft. Immediately thereafter, the captain's forward L1 flight deck window had cracked with an associated window heat fail message on the Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitor (ECAM). The flight crew carried out the ECAM actions and notified air traffic control (ATC) before continuing to destination without further incident. There was no emergency declared. Following the occurrence, a general visual inspection of the aircraft was conducted, hail damage was observed on the radome and on both the left-hand and right-hand horizontal stabilizer leading edge.

C-GAZI, a CargoJet B767-338 was operating flight CJT2384 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON. During the cruise phase of the flight, at FL350 the crew received multiple EICAS messages pop up. The crew started working down the list and got a LE SLAT DISAGREE. As the checklist reached changing flap configuration, the crew noted a STANDBY BUS OFF message. Figuring that is what was caused it, they started that checklist. In the meantime, the crew requested a descent out of RVSM airspace since the autopilot and autothrottle were INOP. A PAN PAN was declared. The crew also talked to MCC and Dispatch, finished the checklists and continued to destination without further incident.

C-GVJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP. Dash 8-400 was operating flight JZA659 from Halifax Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ. While on approach the crew selected gear down and showed the left main gear still in transit, when the nose and right main showed down and locked. The crew then did a missed approach, and retracted the landing gear. The crew then followed there landing gear malfunction check list and then passed by Teterboro Airport (KTEB), NJ tower after which the tower confirmed that they saw 3 gear down. The flight then returned to KEWR, where the crew requested that ARFF meet the flight. No emergency was declared. The crew advised the passengers of the issue and there were no adverse reactions.

C-GQPN, a Piper PA-28-140 registered to Winnipeg Aviation 2003 Ltd, was conducting a local flight from Winnipeg/St. Andrews (CYAV), MB with only the pilot onboard. The pilot was practicing forced approaches over a wheat field. During a practice forced approach, when power was applied for the go-around at a low altitude, the engine hesitated. The pilot subsequently landed in the field and attempted to takeoff but was unable to gain enough speed. The pilot then taxied from the field to a gravel road and started a takeoff run. Upon getting airborne, the pilot observed a power line crossing the road ahead of the aircraft. The pilot attempted to land on the gravel road but the aircraft had drifted laterally and the aircraft landed in a ditch. The aircraft overturned and was substantially damaged. The pilot received minor injuries. RCMP and ambulance responded to the scene.

C-FYAV, a Piper PA-28-161 registered to Winnipeg Aviation 2003 Ltd, was conducting a takeoff from the grass Runway 27 at Gilbert Plains (CJH2), MB. During the takeoff as the nose wheel lifted off the ground, the aircraft drifted to the left. The pilot pulled the throttle to idle to abort the takeoff but the aircraft's left wing collided with 3 runway edge markers and exited the left side of the runway. The aircraft came to a stop in a field. There were no injuries but the aircraft's was substantially damaged. The ELT did not activate.

C-FTIZ, a Canadian North ATR 42-500, was operating as flight AKT609 from from Hay River (CYHY), NT to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT. During the initial climb from CYHY, the first officer's EHSI and EADI failed (went blank) during the initial climb. Shortly after there was smoke in the cockpit. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft returned to CYHY uneventfully.Maintenance update: The #2 symbol generator burnt out causing the circuit breaker to pop. The #2 symbol generator was replaced, function tested as per the maintenance manual and the aircraft was released to service.

C-GJFJ un avion amphibie construction amateur de type Osprey 2 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport Bruce McPhail Memorial, On, à destination du lac Green dans la municipalité de Clarendon, Qc. Lors de l'amerrissage, une partie collée de la coque s'est détachée, ce qui a entrainé la perte de contrôle. Le bout de l'aile gauche s'est détaché lorsque celui-ci a frappé la surface de l'eau et l'appareil a pivoté sur lui même. Le pilote a pu regagner la rive avec l'appareil. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé. Des dommages à la coque et à l'aile gauche ont été constatés.

C-GRUV, a Valhalla Helicopters Inc. Bell 205A-1, was operating in support of forest fire fighting activities in the vicinity of Haig Lake, AB, 55 nm NE of Peace River Airport (CYPE), AB. Shortly after departure to commence bucketing operations the helicopter collided with terrain. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was fatally injured. The ELT activated; the helicopter was substantially damaged and there was no post-impact fire. The TSB Edmonton office deployed investigators to the site.

C-GCBL, an AC Airways Limited Cessna 210C (Centurion) aircraft, was conducting a flight from Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC, to Kamloops (CYKA), BC. On final approach to Runway 09 at CYKA, the pilot noticed an issue with the hydraulic system that operates the landing gear and flaps. The flap travel was limited and the landing gear did not extend. The pilot informed the flight service station that they were having gear issues and intended to troubleshoot the problem. After actioning checklists from the pilot operating manual and consulting with company, the situation was unchanged. The pilot decided to return to CYPK where they circled for approximately one hour to reduce the fuel onboard. The pilot then conducted one planned approach overshoot and then landed with the main gear retracted. City fire department crews and equipment were waiting on scene. The aircraft came to rest on the runway surface with only the nose gear extended. There was no fire and the aircraft sustained minor damage. There were no injuries.The aircraft was recovered to the company hangar where maintenance will inspect the aircraft.

C-GNAM, an Air Canada A220-300 was operating flight AC1039 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Denver International Airport (KDEN), CO. On approach, the flight crew received a TCAS RA, TA was followed and the flight continued to land without further incident.

C-GHLV, an Air Canada B767 was operating flight AC7263 from El Dorado International Airport (SKBO), Bogota, Colombia to Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), Dominican Republic. Approximately 1 hour into the flight, the flight crew experienced multiple flight system failure indicators. In discussion with dispatch and MOC, the decision was made to divert to the nearest airport which was Ernesto Cortissoz International Airport (SKBQ), Barranquilla, Colombia . The crew declared a May Day with ATC, with ARFF on standby. The flight landed without further incident.

C-GBHR, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1730 from Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (KPHX), AZ to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Just prior to Top Of Descent, in the vicinity of Watertown, NY, the Flight Crew received a Green Hydraulic System Low ECAM. ECAM actions were carried out in accordance with company policy and procedure. A PAN PAN was declared with ATC and the flight subsequently completed a full-stop landing in CYUL RWY 24L . The aircraft was unable to taxi to gate under its own power and as a result was towed to gate.

C-GPCI, a Pacific Coastal Airlines SAAB 340B, was conducting flight PCO3055 from Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International (CYXC), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 3 crew members and 33 passengers on board. During the takeoff roll, warning lights and a loss of left engine power (General Electric, CT7-9B) occurred between approximately 85 and 90 knots. Annunciator lights illuminated to indicate low oil pressure and an overtemperature associated with the left engine. Additionally, there was an accompanying reduction in torque on the same engine. The crew rejected the takeoff and brought the aircraft to a stop on the runway. Visual observation of the engine indicated no smoke or fire. A precautionary shutdown of the left engine was accomplished. The flight crew then taxied the aircraft back to the gate, where they shut down the aircraft and deplaned passengers. There were no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft.Pacific Coastal Airlines maintenance personnel will change the engine and the aircraft will be retuned to service. They will also examine the engine to determine the cause of the power loss.

C-FFBC, a Boeing 737-8, departed Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, destined for Winnipeg /James Armstrong International Airport (CYWG), MB. The aircraft was in cruise flight in the vicinity of the Sault Ste Marie Airport (CYSM), ON and had begun a descent from FL400 to FL380 due to turbulence; the aircraft was descending through level FL395 when the Master Caution illuminated and both PACK lights illuminated. The flight crew donned oxygen masks and initiated an emergency descent in coordination with ATC. While in descent the crew actioned the PACK non-normal checklist, and both PACKS were reset, and the aircraft began to pressurize. The cabin altitude exceeded 14 000 and the passenger oxygen masks automatically deployed. The crew leveled the aircraft at 20 000 and elected to return to YYZ.

C-GPNN, an Allstar-PZL Glider (SZD-51-1) departed the Rockton Aerodrome (CPT3), ON; after gliding for some time the aircraft performed a land-out on a farm field in the vicinity of Ayr, Ontario. The pilot intentionally ground looped the aircraft to avoid collision with obstacles and the aircraft spun around 180 degrees. A post landing inspection revealed stress striations and cracks on the tail-boom fuselage area. The aircraft was disassembled, removed from the field and transported to a maintenance shop for repair. There were no injuries.

C-GKQJ, an ERJ 190-400 operating as Porter Airlines flight POE119 was on a flight from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Montreal Pierre-Eliot Trudeau Airport (CYUL), QC, when the flight crew declared an emergency due to smoke in the forward cabin. The flight crew elected to return to (CYYZ) and landed without further incident.

C-GJZN, a DeHavilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight Air Canada Express 8357 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Windsor International Airport (CYQG), ON with 4 crew and 50 passengers onboard. While on route at approximately 12 000 feet, flight 8357 experienced severe turbulence. The captain and the first officer were dislodged from their seat and the autopilot disconnected resulting in an altitude gain of 300-500 feet. The first officer hit his head and a cart hit a flight attendant on her leg. Flight 8357 continued to destination and landed without further incident. The crew continued with the following leg back to CYYZ where the first officer and the flight attendant ended their day prior the next scheduled flight due to minor injuries. The company maintenance control department was notified and an inspection after severe and or extreme turbulence was conducted with no faults found.

C-GMRO un Learjet 45 exploité par Chartright Air Inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Goose Bay (CYYR), NL  à destination de l'aéroport Lester B. Pearson de Toronto (CYYZ), ON. En route, au niveau de vol 400, une alerte d'altitude cabine "CABIN ALT" est apparue dans le poste de pilotage. L'équipage a noté que l'altitude cabine montait rapidement. Ils ont enfilé leur masque à oxygène, déclaré une urgence, et effectué la procédure d'urgence consistant à déployer les masques à oxygène pour les passagers et amorcer une descente d'urgence. Le vol a été dérouté vers l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC où il s'est posé sans encombre. Pas de blessé. Des tests opérationnels de maintenance ont été complétés sans révéler d'anomalie.

C-GARO un Airbus A319 exploité par Air Canada Rouge effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC, à destination de l’aéroport de Vancouver (CYVR), BC. Durant la montée vers l'altitude de croisière une odeur anormale a été détectée dans la cabine et dans le poste de pilotage. La montée a été interrompue à 14 000 pieds et une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée. L'appareil est revenu se poser sans encombre à CYQB. L'équipe de maintenance ont trouvé la turbine du groupe d'air conditionné numéro un saisie. Le groupe numéro un a été désactivé selon la MEL et l'appareil a été remis en service.

C-FYKA, a Cessna 172 floatplane, was conducting flight training on Whitewater Lake, ON, with a student and an instructor on board. During the landing, the left wingtip made contact with the water, damaging the aircraft. The aircraft remained afloat. The wing was removed for structural repairs and subsequently reinstalled. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GREU, a Bell 205A-1 aircraft operated by Airborne Energy Solutions Inc., was conducting a flight from Peace River Regional Airport (CYPE), AB to Whitecourt Airport (CYZU), AB with 1 crew member on board. As the helicopter was lifting a water pump through approximately 4 feet AGL, the pilot inadvertently pressed the load release switch; dropping the pump and 60 feet of long line. There were no injuries to the ground crew and no damage to the helicopters.

C-FJQD, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1637 from Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During the climb to cruise phase of flight, approximately 9nm N of DUCEN, climbing through FL210,ROU1637 received TCAS RA initially to descend which changed immediately to a climb commanding +4500fpm. The flight crew complied with the RA, notified ATC and received a CLEAR OF CONFLICT annunciation as ROU1637 climbed through FL235. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GUBL, an Air Transat A330-200 was operating flight TSC251 from Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC when in cruise over the coast of Ireland, a flight attendant became ill. The emergency positions and safety responsibilities were reassigned to the remaining crew and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GCJT, a CargoJet B757-223 was operating flight CJT1918 from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (KCVG), KY to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. While in the vicinity of O'Hare International Airport (KORD), IL, the crew declared an emergency due to a pressurization issue and elected to divert to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON where the aircraft landed safely.

C-FOLB, an AS350-B2 operated by Helicopters Canada, was conducting VFR flight MNR718 for firefighting support from the MNR Base at Sioux Lookout, ON, to Arril Lake, ON. During the landing phase at Arril lake, the floating landing platform moved unexpectedly. The aircraft's tail rotor was struck by the platform structure. The pilot maneuvered the aircraft away from the platform and autorotated into the lake. The rotor brake was applied fully and the aircraft came to rest upright in 3 feet of water. One passenger sustained a minor injury. The ELT activated and MNR dispatch was notified immediately. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FMFG, a Boeing 757-2B7 aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express Inc, was conducting flight MAL7090 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 2 pilots on board. While climbing through 17 000 feet, the crew observed a L HYD QUANTITY EICAS message. The left hydraulic quantity subsequently dropped from 90 to 0; the QRH checklist was performed and the aircraft returned to CYYC. The captain declared a PAN PAN. Emergency vehicles were deployed and inspected the aircraft after landing without incident. The aircraft was towed back to the apron.

C-FWVJ, a Westjet Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737-8CT, was conducting flight WS2246 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International Airport (MMPR), Puerto Vallarta, Mexico, with 6 crew members and 164 passengers on board. During the initial climb out of CYYC, a cabin crew member became incapacitated. The remaining cabin crew members were reassigned for the duration of the flight. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GTSJ, an Airbus A330-243 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC403 from Rome/Fiumicino Intl (LIRF), Italy to Montréal/Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. At about 44°35' N, 045°47' W a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform their duties during the flight. A supplementary crew was on board and available to assume the duties of the ill crew member. The fight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GJEN, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (DASH 8 Q400), was being operated by Westjet Encore as flight WEN9876 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Masset (CZMT), BC, with 4 crew members and 22 passengers on board. After landing, the crew turned off the runway for the apron when the left main landing gear came off the pavement and onto the grass left main gear was in the grass. The crew brought the aircraft back onto the pavement under its own power and proceeded to park without further incident.Maintenance conducted an inspection of the left main landing gear and tire and found no damage. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWJF, a Westjet Airlines Boeing 737-7CT, was conducting flight WJA689 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International (CYXE), SK, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 5 crew members and 96 passengers on board. While configuring for landing, the crew received a flap asymmetry warning and a flap rollback. The crew elected to complete a flapless landing at CYVR, and declared a PAN PAN emergency with air traffic control. The airplane landed without further incident. Aircraft rescue and firefighting escorted the aircraft to the gate where the passengers deplaned normally.Maintenance determined a problem with the No. 4 flap inboard skew sensor. The sensor was replaced and tested as serviceable. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FNAZ, a British Aerospace Jetstream 32, was being operated by Northwestern Air Lease Ltd. as flight PLR904 from High Level (CYOJ), AB to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. C-GLUH, a Beech King Air 200, was being operated by CanWest Aviation as flight CWA924 from Grand Prairie (CYQU), AB to CYOJ. During PLR904's departure and CWA924's arrival, a loss of separation occurred when procedural separation limitations were reduced. A minimum separation of 15 nm is required and separation was estimated to have been 10 nm.

C-FIQR, un Aerospatiale ATR 42-300 exploité par Bradley Air Services Limited, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport d'Iqaluit (CYFB), NU à destination de l'aéroport de Artic Bay (CYAB), NU. À environ 150 miles nautiques de son point de départ, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) en raison d'un problème de basse pression et bas niveau du système hydraulique bleu. Un retour vers CYFB a été effectué. Les services d'urgence ont été avisés et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre sans les volets. Un tuyau hydraulique a été remplacé et l'appareil remis en service suite aux essais satisfaisants

C-GOIS, an Air Transat A321-271NX was operating flight TSC324 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (EHAM), Netherlands. Approximately 4 hours into the flight, a flight attendant became ill and unable to perform duties. The emergency positions were reassigned according to priority of occupancy and the flight continued to destination.

C-GWSP, a WestJet Boeing 737-700, was operating as flight WS557 from Waterloo (CYKF), ON to Calgary (CYYC), AB. C-GYRS, a WestJet Boeing 787-9 was operating as flight WS669 from Toronto (CYYZ), ON to CYYC. While the flights were being vectored for arrival, 52 nm SE of the airport, separation between the aircraft eroded to 4.6 nm horizontally and 100 feet vertically where 5.0 nm horizontally and 1000 feet vertically was required. There was no risk of collision. Both flights landed safely with no further issues.

C-GDAA, a Conair Group Incorporated Rockwell International Commander 690B, was conducting fire suppression operations as flight FGD136 out of Smithers (CYYD), BC, with the pilot and an air attack officer on board. While in cruise, the power of the No. 1 engine (Garrett TPE331-10T-516K) decreased to idle. Attempts to regain engine were not effective and the pilot completed an engine shutdown. A PAN PAN was declared with air traffic control and the flight returned to CYYD where it landed without further incident.Maintenance determined that the T2 temperature sensor probe had failed. The affected sensor was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service. Conair will work with the manufacturers of the engine and the T2 probe to determine the cause of the failure.

C-FTEN, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), operated by Westjet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3630 from Calgary International (CYYC), AB, to Portland International (KPDX), OR with 4 crew and 78 passengers on board. Approximately 25 minutes after takeoff, the First Officer was reported to be unwell. The crew accomplished their company medical procedures and made the decision to divert to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, and declared a PAN PAN with air traffic control. The flight continued without further incident. Emergency services met the aircraft at the gate and the affected crewmember was taken to hospital.

C-GJJM, un cessna Caravan C208, effectuait un vol local de transport de parachutistes selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Pintendre, Qc (CPT9). Lors du largage à 13500 pieds directement au dessus de l'aéroport, le moteur s'est soudainement arrêté. Le pilote a tenté en vain de redémarrer le moteur et a effectué une descente pour venir se poser sans encombre sur la piste. L'appareil a été ravitaillé et les tests moteurs ont été effectués normalement. Pas de blessé.

C-GTDK, a Cessna 172S operated by the Victoria Flying Club, was conducting a local flight from Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC, with 1 instructor on board. While holding short at Runway 09, the pilot requested takeoff from the 2000-foot line after the incoming aircraft had landed: C-FASP, a Cessna 525A (CitationJet CJ1) operated by Airpsprint Incorporated. The CYYJ tower controller instructed C-GTDK to continue to hold short and cleared C-FASP to land which it did without incident. As C-FASP rolled out after landing, C-GTDK was instructed to line up on Runway 09 and to prepare for a normal departure due to inbound and outbound traffic. The pilot acknowledged. C-GTDK lined up and began the takeoff roll without clearance and before C-FASP had exited Runway 09. The aircraft separation was reduced to 0.5 nautical miles on Runway 09 before C-FASP had exited the runway on Taxiway Sierra.

C-IKND, un ultra léger de base Air Creation Skypper 912 R, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de St-Lambert-de-Lauzon, Qc. Pour une raison inconnue, l'appareil a percuté le sol. Le pilote, seul à bord, a été mortellement blessé.

C-FHEN, a Westjet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was conducting flight WEN3108 from Terrace (CYXT), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 4 crewmembers and 30 passengers on board. After landing at CYVR, a passenger and cabin crew member observed what was suspected to be a brake or wheel fire on the left main gear. The captain requested aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) personnel to attend. The ARFF team that arrived found no evidence of fire and determined that the brake temperatures were within the normal range. The passengers deplaned normally and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GMAI, un boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit Ltée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC à destination de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 73 passagers à son bord. Environs 20 minutes après avoir atteint son altitude de croisière au niveau de vol FL310, une indication de vibration élevée accompagnée par une perte de puissance du moteur numéro 1 ont été constatées. L'équipage a actionné la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a déclaré une urgence. Un déroutement vers l'aéroport de Chibougamau, QC (CYMT) a été effectué. Le moteur a été sécurisé au ralenti selon la procédure pour la descente et l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre.

C-FITL, un Boeing 777-300 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Genève, Suisse (LSGG) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. QC (CYUL). Alors que les passagers avaient débuté le débarquement, un véhicule de service d'eau potable situé près de la porte de cargo arrière a pris feu. Les flammes ont atteint le revêtement de l'appareil et de la fumée a été détectée dans la cabine. Un désembarquement rapide a été commandé et tous les passagers sont sortis dans le terminal alors que l'incendie était maitrisé par le personnel au sol.

C-FYJE, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1737 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Portland International Airport (KPDX), OR. During the cruise phase of flight, approximately 160 NM WNW of Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, a flight attendant (FA) became ill and was unable to continue duties. The cabin safety duties were redistributed amongst the remaining cabin crew in accordance with company policy and procedure. The flight continued to destination and was subsequently completed without further incident.

C-FYKW, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114, was operating flight ROU1909 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC. During the descent phase of the flight, at 10,000ft ASL, ATC instructed ROU1909 to maintain the altitude due to a business jet leveling off at 9,000ft ASL. Shortly after, ATC instructed the business jet to climb. As a result, the flight crew of ROU1909 received and followed a TCAS RA command to climb. ATC was advised, the conflict was resolved and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GMDL, a privately registered PA-31-325 (Navajo), was on a visual flight rules flight plan from Victoria International (CYYJ), BC, to Abbotsford (CYXX), BC, with 2 crew on board. While departing CYYJ, the indication for manifold pressure of the No. 2 engine (Avco Lycoming TIO-540-F2BD) had decreased from full power to 24 inches, fuel pressure was fluctuating, and the aircraft had poor climb performance. The crew completed a precautionary shutdown of the affected engine, declared a MAYDAY, and diverted to Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC. After remaining in the circuit pattern at CZBB to await the arrival of emergency services vehicles, the aircraft landed without further incident. The aircraft stopped on the runway to be inspected and, after determining there was no fire, the crew started the engines and taxied to the apron.The aircraft was sent to a maintenance facility to be inspected. It was determined the the density controller was faulty. The part was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GMDL, a privately registered PA-31-325 (Navajo), was on an IFR flight plan from Campbell River (CYBL), BC, to Victoria International (CYYJ), BC, via Port Hardy (CYZT), BC, with 2 crew and 1 passenger on board. While preparing for descent into CYZT, the crew noticed the indication for the oil pressure of the No. 2 engine (Avco Lycoming TIO-540-F2BD) was in the cautionary range and decreasing. The crew decided to discontinue their approach to CYZT and proceeded to Abbotsford (CYXX), BC. While enroute to CYXX, the crew completed a precautionary shutdown of the No. 2 engine, then proceeded to CYXX where they landed without further incident.The aircraft was delivered to maintenance for evaluation. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJWE, a WestJet Encore de Havilland DHC-8-400 was operating flight WEN3199 from Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. While on approach to CYYC (35 NM NW), in the vicinity of BIRKO, WEN3199 was instructed to descend to FL210. The aircraft descended below FL210 and separation between WEN3199 and C-GBAP, a Coywolf Aviation Ltd. Pilatus PC-12, which was operating from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB to CYYC was reduced to 800 feet and 2.8 miles, where 1000 feet vertically and 5 miles horizontally are required.

C-FZKK, a Cessna 172N operated by Acadia College/AAA Aviation, was conducting circuit training at Langley (CYNJ), BC, with 1 student pilot on board. After touchdown, the pilot reported experiencing an unusual wobble in the landing gear and elected to attempt a full stop landing rather than the intended touch and go. The aircraft overran the end of the runway and traversed approximately 70 feet of grass before the nose gear collapsed and the aircraft collided with the airport perimeter fence. The pilot exited the aircraft without assistance. There were no injuries, but the aircraft was substantially damaged.Maintenance crews recovered the aircraft. They will examine the aircraft and assess the extent of the damage in general and in particular to the propeller, engine cowling, wing strut, and landing gear.

C-GQBQ, un Challenger CL600-2B16 exploité par le Service Aérien Gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait le vol QUE20 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, de l'aéroport depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Au départ de CYUL, les volets sont restés coincés à 20 degrés lors de la rétraction. L'équipage a alors déclaré une urgence et continué le vol vers CYQB où celui-ci s'est posé sans problème.

C-FVFN, a Beech 200 operated by Vanguard Air Care as flight VN06, was conducting a flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. to Churchill (CYYQ) MB, with 2 crew and 2 paramedics. On the approach to CYYQ, the flight crew selected the gear down. The gear traveled down but there was no green down and locked indication and no red unsafe light. The flight crew checked all lights and tested the system but no landing gear lights illuminated. The flight crew conducted a missed approach and completed a fly-past inspection to confirm gear position. The tower confirmed the gear appeared to be down. The operator's maintenance advised VN06 to return to CYWG. The flight crew confirmed fuel remaining, advised ATC, and returned to CYWG. When VN06 was en-route to CYWG, the flight crew advised ATC of a low fuel condition, gear issues, and requested ARFF. The aircraft landed without incident at CYWG and taxied to the hangar. The operator's maintenance placed the aircraft on jacks before the crew disembarked.The landing gear indication circuit breaker was replaced. Gear swings were completed with no faults and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FKWS, a WestJet Airlines B737-700, was operating from Puerto Vallarta, (MMPR) Jalisco, Mexico to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB as flight WS2247. After landing at CYYC on Runway 35L the flight crew were given clearance to taxi via Taxiway E to the apron. The flight crew was to enter the apron at their discretion and taxi to Gate D71. The flight crew were advised of another aircraft, WS1536, a Boeing 737-800, on Taxiway E that had just been pushed back from the apron preparing to start engines and taxi to the runway. At Gate D76, next to Taxiway E, was an Air Canada Boeing 787-9, AC850, that was being prepared for its next flight. Ground support equipment was operating within the vehicle service road (VSR) on the apron. Flight WS2247 elected to taxi between WS1536 and AC850. The right wings of WS2247 and the 787 came within approximately 10 feet of each other and WS2247's wing went over top of an operator and ground support equipment operating in the VSR. Once around the obstacles, WS2247 re-joined the yellow line and continued to the gate without further issue. There was no collision with any personal, ground equipment or aircraft.

C-GJKK, a Boeing 737-8 operated by Swoop Inc, was conducting flight WSW104 from Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB to Hamilton (CYHM), ON with 6 crew members and 163 passengers. During the cruise portion of the flight, a flight attendant became ill. The company was advised of the situation and the duties of the ill flight attendant were assumed by the other 3 flight attendants. The flight continued to CYHM uneventfully.

C-FIUY, The Upper Winds Air Ltd. de Havilland DHC-2, was departing from Spray Lakes, AB to Ghost Lake, AB. While conducting a water take-off, a crosswind gust lifted the left wing of the aircraft. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was unable to maintain control of the aircraft. The left-wing tip dragged on the water surface. Subsequently the nose and the right wing tip of the aircraft contacted the surface of the lake as the aircraft came to an abrupt stop. The emergency locator transmitter activated, and the aircraft returned to the shoreline. The pilot was uninjured and the aircraft received damage to the right-wing tip fairing and propeller.

C-GJZC, un De Havilland DHC-8-402 exploité par Jazz Aviation, effectuait le vol JZA7924 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport des Îles-de-la-Madeleine, QC (CYGR) avec à son bord 4 membres d'équipage et 55 passagers. Lors de la montée initiale, il y a eu découplement du système d'interconnection des commandes d'ailerons du coté co-pilote. L'équipage a alors déclaré un Pan Pan et l'aéronef est revenu atterrir sans problème à CYUL.

C-GOIE, an Air Transat A321LR was operating flight TSC189 from Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Approximately 35 minutes after take-off, a cabin crew member became incapacitated. The emergency positions and safety responsibilities were reassigned to the remaining crew and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GGMQ, un De Havilland Dash8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation, effectuait le vol JZA8045 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de St-John, NB (CYSJ) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec à son bord 4 membres d'équipage et 31 passagers. Lors de la descente vers CYUL, un membre d'équipage de cabine n'a pas été en mesure d'exercer ses fonctions en raison d'une incapacité physique. L'équipage de vol en a été informé et a demandé la présence des services médicaux à l'arrivée. Un pilote de la compagnie voyageant en cabine a été breffé sur les procédures de sécurité et a pris la relève de l'agent de bord affecté jusqu'à la fin du vol.

C-FPNB, a privately registered Christen Eagle II, was being flown on a local visual flight rules trip from Abbotsford International (CYXX), BC, with the pilot and one passenger on board. At Chilliwack (CYCW), BC, the pilot conducted 3 circuits. During approach to Runway 25 on the third circuit, the aircraft struck a lamp post adjacent to the westbound lane of the Trans Canada Highway. The collision occurred 1627 feet east of the beginning of the paved surface of Runway 25, at a height of approximately 30 feet above ground level. The lamp post was found on the ground near the impact location, severed from its base, with the lamp head separated from the post. The impact caused significant damage to the left lower wing and undercarriage of the aircraft. The aircraft continued flying from the point of collision to Runway 25. Upon landing, the aircraft undercarriage failed to support the weight of the aircraft, and the propeller contacted the runway. After the aircraft came to rest, the pilot and passenger were able to egress. The aircraft was substantially damaged and was leaking fuel. There was no fire, and no injuries were reported. First responders attended the scene.The aircraft was recovered to a local maintenance facility where the extent of the damage will be assessed.

C-GFHG, a Beech 95-B55 operated by Super T Aviation, was enroute from Geraldton (CYQG), ON to Regina Intl (CYQR), SK with 1 pilot onboard.  During the flight, the aircraft encountered headwinds and moderate turbulence. As the flight was approaching CYQR, both engines made an uncommanded roll back to idle power. The mixtures, throttles, and propellers controls were advanced to correct the condition without effect. The pilot elected to make a forced landing in a farm field approximately 8nm east of CYQR. The landing was uneventful. The engines remained at idle after touchdown and were shutdown. A post-landing inspection revealed that the aircraft's fuel tanks were empty. Fuel was added and the aircraft departed from a nearby road and landed in CYQR. Further inspection by the operator indicted that the aircraft was using 10 gallons per hour more than it should have for the planned flight. The aircraft has been removed from service.

C-GGPK, a privately registered Cessna T310R, was conducting a flight from Alert Bay Airport (CYAL), BC, to Vancouver/Boundary Bay Airport (CZBB), BC, with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. During cruise flight, the pilot turned the fuel selector valve for the left engine from the auxiliary fuel tank to the main tank and, after the left engine stabilized, repeated the process for the right engine. Shortly after that, the right engine (Teledyne Continental TSIO-520-NB) began losing power and while troubleshooting the right engine, the left engine power began to fluctuate. The pilot decided to divert to the Pitt Meadows Airport (CYPK), BC, and declared a MAYDAY. The pilot then turned the right boost pump on high and, after a momentary hesitation, the right engine power started to increase and the left engine stabilized. While on short final for Runway 08R, the pilot reduced power on both engines in preparation for landing and landed without incident. The aircraft exited on Taxiway C and the right engine stopped running. The pilot restarted the right engine and continued to taxi to Apron I.  An Aircraft Maintenance Engineer inspected the aircraft and checked the fuel for quantity and contamination with no faults found. An engine ground run was performed successfully and the aircraft returned to CZBB with no further issue.

C-FIGF, a de Havilland DHC-2 Beaver on floats, was being operated by Alkan Air from Mayo, YT float base (3 nm E of CYMA) to McClusky Lake, YT. The flight was transporting two passengers to the Wind River for a canoe trip. The pilot aborted the first approach, to the south, as the variable winds were not favorable. On the second approach, to the north, after touchdown on the water, the pilot attempted a go-around. The engine (PRATT & WHITNEY-USA, R-985-AN-14B) hesitated and did not produce power quickly enough. The pilot aborted the go-around and reduced power. During the deceleration on the water the aircraft didn't come to a stop until it had entered a marshy area. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft and all occupants were able to exit the aircraft unassisted. Following the flight, the company brought a maintenance team out to inspect the aircraft and pull it out of the marsh. There were no defects or damage found on the aircraft. The aircraft was returned to service and flew from McClusky Lake back to the float base in Mayo, YT.

C-GQBQ, un Challenger CL600-2B16 exploité par le Service Aérien Gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait le vol QUE100M selon les règles de vol aux instruments, de l'aéroport depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec 4 membres d'équipage à bord. Au départ de CYUL, les volets sont restés coincés à 20 degrés lors de la rétraction. L'équipage a alors déclaré une urgence et continué le vol vers CYQB où celui-ci s'est posé sans problème.

C-GQBQ, un Challenger CL600-2B16 exploité par le Service Aérien Gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait le vol QUE20 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Mont-Joli, QC (CYYY) à destination de l'aéroport de Matane, QC (CYME) avec à son bord 4 membres d'équipage et 1 passager. Au départ de CYYY, les volets sont restés coincés à 20 degrés lors de la rétraction. L'équipage a alors déclaré une urgence (Pan Pan) et dérouté l'aéronef vers l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) où celui-ci s'est posé sans problème à 2037Z. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GWGA, un Beech 1900D exploité par Sky Jet M.G. Inc, effectuait le vol LSJ641 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) à destination de l'aéroport de Port-Menier, QC (CYPN). Au départ de CYZV, suite à la rentrée du train d'atterrissage, l'équipage n'a pas eu de d'indication que le train était bien verrouillé. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'équipage a dérouté vers l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) où il s'est posé sans problèmes. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

N533NN, a MHI RJ Aviation ULC, CRJ-900LR aircraft operated by American Airlines Inc, was conducting Flight JIA5020 from Charlotte Douglas International Airport (KCLT), USA to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While on approach into CYYZ runway 06R, the crew declared emergency with Air traffic Control (ATC) due to smoke in the cockpit. JIA5020 continued its approach and landed safely runway 06R.

N301NB, an Airbus A319-114 aircraft operated by Delta Airlines Inc, was conducting flight DAL1394 from Salt Lake City International Airport (KSLC), USA to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport, ON (CYYZ). While on approach into CYYZ, the flight crew declared emergency with ATC due to a nose wheel issue. The aircraft subsequently landed runway 15L with emergency vehicles standing by and was escorted to the gate without further incident.

C-GJLZ, a WestJet B737-800 was operating flight WJA1510 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), CA. On final approach for runway 24R, the crew experienced a flaps malfunction when they would not extend from setting 25 to 30. The crew initiated a go-around to perform the associated non-normal checklists and declared PAN PAN. The aircraft landed safely with a flap setting of 25 and taxied to the gate under its own power. Once at the gate and with the support of maintenance, the flight crew completed a full flap cycle. Flaps went down to 40 with asymmetry identified and retracted fully with no issues.

C-FFLJ, a Boeing 737-86J operated by Flair Airlines, was conducting flight FLE661 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Abbottsford Intl (CYXX), BC. C-GEHI, a Boeing 737 Max 8 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA134 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. While enroute, FLE661 requested a step climb from FL360 to FL380. The ATC controller then cleared FLE661 to climb to FL380, which the crew of FLE661 read back. During the climb, FLE661 received a TCAS RA to descend, which the crew complied with. ACA134, who was level at FL370, also received a TCAS RA to climb, which the crew complied with. The ATC controller also issued a safety alert to FLE661 to descend. Separation between the two aircraft degraded to 400 feet vertically and 7.4nm horizontally. Once cleared of the conflicting traffic, both aircraft resumed their flights to their intended destinations uneventfully.NAV CANADA is conducting an investigation. While not in conflict with FLE661 and ACA134, there was a WestJet aircraft, flight WJA661 on the same frequency.

C-GJOG, a privately registered Mooney M20R, was conducting a flight from Vancouver/Boundary Bay Airport (CZBB), BC, to Chilliwack Airport (CYCW), BC, with only the pilot on board. The aircraft’s transponder was unserviceable, and the pilot obtained special clearance from CZBB tower to complete the flight. During lift off, the cockpit door, located on the right side of the aircraft, popped open. The pilot immediately radioed CZBB tower for permission to return to the airport, but the cockpit wind noise prevented the pilot from hearing the tower's response. The aircraft continued to climb and initiated a left turn into the circuit pattern at an altitude of approximately 640 feet above sea level (ASL). The pilot kept the engine controls in the takeoff configuration of full rich mixture and full fine propeller; the flaps were switched to landing configuration on the downwind leg. The pilot continued to radio CZBB tower 3 more times and, 47 seconds after the pilot's first transmission, the pilot heard the tower's fifth response and acknowledged that he was number 1 in the sequence for Runway 13. 50 seconds later, the tower cleared the aircraft to land on Runway 13 and provided the wind speed of 140 degrees at 10 knots; the pilot acknowledged the clearance. During final approach, the aircraft altitude was low and the pilot prepared for an overshoot by adding engine power. The aircraft impacted terrain approximately 132 feet short of the paved surface (840 feet short of the displaced threshold) of Runway 13 and came to rest 95 feet later on a heading of 232 degrees and in an upright position. Tower called 911 to dispatch local emergency services. The pilot radioed tower and advised he was not injured. The pilot egressed the aircraft before the Delta Fire Department and emergency medical services arrived on scene. No signal was transmitted or received from the emergency locator transmitter (ELT). There was no post-impact fire or fuel spill. The aircraft was substantially damaged. CZBB tower directed 2 aircraft to perform missed approaches for Runway 13 while a third aircraft was diverted to land on Runway 07. Runway 13 was temporarily closed and was reopened shortly after for takeoff only from the displaced threshold. The TSB deployed to the occurrence site.

C-GORP, a Swoop B737 Max 8 was operating flight WSW660 from Abbotsford International Airport (CYXX), BC to Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International Airport (MMPR), Puerto Vallarta, MX. During cruise, a flight attendant was injured and unable to continue duties. Other cabin crew members assumed their duties and the flight continued uneventfully.

C-GLVU, a Swoop B737 Max-8 was operating flight WSW745 from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), NV to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the cruise portion, a flight attendant became incapacitated and Medlink was called. The captain decided to divert to O'Hare International Airport (KORD), Chicago, IL and declared a MAYDAY. Once on the ground, the aircraft was met by EMS.

N840MH, a Boeing 767-432ER, operated by Delta Airlines, was conducting flight DAL130 from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (KATL), GA, USA to Munich Airport (EDDM), Germany. While enroute, approximately 45nm NE of Sable Island Airport (CSB2), NS, the flight crew requested to divert to Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS) MA, USA due to a flight attendant that became incapacitated. The flight landed safely at KBOS at 2:45 UTC, no emergency was declared.

C-GNAM, an Air Canada A220 was operating flight AC604 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Halifax Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. After experiencing multiple fault indications and a discussion with MOC and Dispatch, the decision was made to return to CYYZ and a pan pan was declared. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FQHB, a Bell Helicopter 206L-1 operated by Custom Helicopters, departed from Truelove Inlet, NU for Devon Island, NU with a pilot and 2 passengers on board. During the flight, the pilot lost visual reference and collided with the ice and snow covered terrain. The passengers and pilot received minor injuries. They were rescued and taken to Resolute Bay, NU for medical evaluation. The helicopter was destroyed. The TSB is investigating.

C-GKQQ, an Embraer 190-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines Canada Ltd. was conducting flight POE405 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. While in cruise, approximately 1 hour after departure from CYYZ, the crew received an ENG 2 OIL LO PRESS Engine Indication and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) message. The flight crew subsequently actioned the applicable quick reference handbook checklist (QRH) and initiated a descent from FL380 to FL250. During the descent with the engine #2 at idle, the EICAS message extinguished. After consultation with the maintenance department, the crew elected to return to CYYZ and declared Pan Pan with Air Traffic Control (ATC). POE405 landed in CYYZ without further incident. The engine #2 Oil pressure valve has been replaced.

C-GDEW, a Westjet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400 (Dash 8 Q400) was operating as flight WEN3337 from Calgary International (CYYC), AB, to Penticton (CYYF), BC, with 4 crew members and 43 passengers onboard. C-GDZQ, an Airhart Aviation Incorporated Cessna 172M (Skyhawk), was passed as traffic to WEN3337 and informed that the aircraft was climbing VFR to 4500 feet above sea level (ASL) and would remain east of the approach path. While descending through 5000 feet ASL, WEN3337 received a traffic alert (TA) notice and saw the other aircraft climbing. The TA was followed by a resolution advisory (RA) advising them to climb. The crew complied with the RA instruction. During the climb the Pitch Trim Caution Light illuminated. Once level and clear of the reported conflict, the checklist from the quick reference handbook for the pitch trim was completed. Air traffic control (ATC) was informed of the RA and that the crew flew the published missed approach path. ATC provided vectors for a second approach and the aircraft landed without further incident. There were no reported injuries and no damage to either aircraft.

C-GFAH, an Air Canada A330 was operating flight AC811 from Humberto Delgado Airport (LPPT), Lisbon, Portugal to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During climb, the flight crew received an ECAM Message for cargo door open, pressurization was okay. In discussion with Dispatch and MOC, the decision was made to return to LPPT. A pan pan was declared, the flight landed without further incident.

C-GBIJ, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1502 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Greater Moncton Roméo LeBlanc International Airport (CYQM), NB. The pilot declared an emergency due to a hydraulic issue. The crew elected to return to CYYZ where the aircraft landed safely on runway 33R.

C-FGWJ, a Westjet Airlines Boeing 737-700, was conducting flight WJA456 from Abbotsford International (CYXX), BC, to Calgary International (CYYC), AB, with 5 crew and 131 passengers on board. On rotation, departing from CYXX, the crew observed a master caution light. As they climbed through 500 feet above sea level (ASL). They saw the "Forward Entry Door Open" indication. The forward entry non-normal checklist was actioned and air traffic control (ATC) was advised. The cabin crew confirmed that the door handle of the forward entry door was in the closed position. The crew continued the climb with a requested maximum altitude of 10 000 feet ASL. While climbing through 9000 feet ASL, the crew observed that the aircraft was not pressurizing, and at 10 000 feet ASL, the non-normal checklist was completed. The crew elected to return to CYXX and declared a PAN PAN with ATC. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance completed an evaluation on the forward entry door with no faults found. An aircraft cabin pressurization check was completed with no leaks noted at the forward entry door. The aircraft was returned to service, boarded, and continued to CYYC.

On 20 June 2023, at 1351 MDT the flight crew of a Thompson Aviation Services Pilatus PC-12 aircraft (registration C-GTAI) advised Edmonton Tower that the aircraft was on the RNAV Z to Runway 02, level at 5000 feet ASL. The aircraft was sequenced number one for landing on Runway 02. At 1353, the Northwestern Air Lease Ltd British Aerospace Jetsteam Model 3212 (Callsign PLR905, registration C-FNAZ) was cleared for takeoff from Runway 30 with no delay. C-GTAI was subsequently cleared for landing on Runway 02. Due to the time that it took PLR905 to taxi past the displaced threshold markers, approximately 980 feet down Runway 30, it resulted in a loss of separation between the arriving light aircraft and the departing medium aircraft. At 1355, lateral separation had been reduced to 2.7NM. There was no other operational impact.NAV CANADA is conducting an internal investigation into this loss of separation.

C-FJGZ, a Jazz Aviation LP Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Limited CL-600-2D24 (CRJ 900), was preparing for flight AC8102 from Erik Nielsen Whitehorse International (CYXY), YK, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 4 crew members and 70 passengers on board. During pushback from the airport gate, the push tug began to emit smoke and then became engulfed in flames. The aircraft captain contacted air traffic control and declared a PAN PAN. Jazz Aviation ground staff used handheld fire extinguishers to battle the fire until airport aircraft rescue and firefighting crews arrived. The fire was extinguished, and the aircraft was disconnected from the tow bar. The pilot cancelled the PAN PAN. There were no injuries to anyone on the ground or onboard the aircraft. There was no damage to the aircraft.After a short delay, the aircraft departed on the scheduled flight.

C-FVVW, un ultra-léger de type évolué Delisle CADI sur flotteurs, effectuait un test à régime moteur médium sur le lac Kénogamichiche, QC avec le pilote seul à bord. Alors que le pilote avait augmenté le régime moteur et qu’il était toujours à basse vitesse avec le nez haut, l’aile droite s’est soulevée probablement en raison d'une rafale de vent, le bout de l’aile gauche a touché à la surface de l’eau et l’hydravion s’est renversé. Le pilote a réussi à sortir et n’a pas été blessé. L’hydravion a subi des dommages principalement en raison de l’immersion dans l’eau.

C-GJWS, a Boeing 737-800, operated by Westjet Airlines Limited, was conducting a flight from Las Vegas (KLAS), NV, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, as flight WSJ1789 with 6 crew members and 172 passengers on board. During descent into CYVR, passing through 13 000 feet above sea level, the flight crew observed a strong odour in the flight deck. Flight attendants confirmed a similar odour was also in the aircraft cabin. The fumes quick reference checklist was actioned, the flight crew donned oxygen masks, and a PAN PAN was declared with air traffic control. The aircraft landed without further incident. Upon arrival, the aircraft was inspected by aircraft rescue firefighting crews before taxiing to the gate under its own power. There were no injuries.During the subsequent maintenance inspection, staff confirmed an exhaust /oil burning smell inside the aircraft when the auxiliary power unit (APU) bleed was selected on. The APU middle drain was found to be leaking oil and in need of replacement. The APU was placarded as inoperative in accordance with the minimum equipment list and the aircraft was returned to service.

Location: Moose Jaw/Air Vice Marshal C.M. McEwen
Summary: N775AN, a Boeing 777-200 aircraft operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL139 from London/Heathrow International, United Kingdom (EGLL) to Los Angeles International, USA (KLAX) with 12 crew members and 273 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL380 overhead Moose Jaw (CYMJ) SK, the flight crew reported a collision with what is believed to be a weather balloon. The flight continued to destination and landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance conducted a visual external inspection of the aircraft, and no damage was found. The aircraft was returned to service.

N717LM, un Bell 206B en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis une résidence privée au lac du Huit à Adstock, QC situé à environ 3 miles marins (nm) au nord-est de l’aérodrome de Thetford Mines (CSM3), QC avec un pilote et 2 passagers à bord. Alors que l’hélicoptère était à environ 25-30 pieds au-dessus du lac et s’approchait de son lieu d’atterrissage, le moteur a perdu de la puissance. Le pilote a effectué un atterrissage d’urgence sans puissance dans le lac à environ 20 pieds de la rive. Après l’impact, les 3 occupants sont sortis alors que l’hélicoptère versait sur le côté droit. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. L’hélicoptère a subi des dommages importants en raison de l’immersion dans l’eau. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) se serait déclenchée.

C-GRAE et C-FUAE, deux Cessna 150M exploités par l’unité de formation au pilotage Collège Select Aviation (Richcopter Inc.), effectuaient des circuits de nuit piste 09 selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport d’Ottawa/Gatineau, QC (CYND). Chaque avion avait seul à son bord un élève-pilote et ils étaient sous la surveillance d’un instructeur superviseur resté au sol. Vers 21h20, C-GRAE et C-FUAE se préparaient à décoller avec 2 autres avions. C-FUAE était numéro 2 dans la séquence de départ et C-GRAE était numéro 4. Une fois en vol et leur premier circuit et posé-décollé effectués, C-FUAE était toujours numéro 2 dans le circuit et C-GRAE était numéro 3. Lors de l’étape du vent-arrière, l’élève-pilote de C-FUAE a étiré l’étape du vent-arrière pour conserver une distance suffisante avec l’aéronef devant lui et numéro à l’atterrissage. Il a communiqué à la radio sa position au moment de tourner en « base » et en « finale » sans mentionner qu’il était numéro 2. L’élève-pilote de C-GRAE a vu C-FUAE étirer l’étape du vent-arrière. Lorsqu’il a vu l’avion numéro 1 en courte finale, il a tourné en base en communicant sa position à la radio. Il a ensuite tourné en finale en croyant qu’il était le numéro 2 pour l’atterrissage et n’a pas vu C-FUAE plus bas devant lui. Alors qu’il était en descente, C-GRAE est entré en collision avec C-FUAE. Après avoir ressenti un choc, l’élève-pilote de C-GRAE a remis les gaz et a vu l’aéronef numéro 1 redécollé de la piste 09. L’élève-pilote a poursuivi son vol pour continuer les pratiques de circuits. L’élève-pilote de C-FUAE qui n’a pas vu C-GRAE au-dessus de lui a décidé d’atterrir à la suite du choc ressenti. Après l’atterrissage, des dommages à la dérive verticale ont été constatés et l’instructeur avisé. Un rapport d’incident a été complété. C-GRAE s’est posé environ 40 minutes après l’incident. Une fois au sol, l’élève-pilote a constaté des dommages au bord d’attaque d’un des stabilisateurs horizontaux. L’instructeur n’étant plus là, l’élève-pilote a écrit ses constatations dans le carnet de route de l’avion et est parti. Ni l’un ni l’autre des avions n’était muni d’un système anticollision embarqué.

C-GHQP un DeHavilland Dash-8 exploité par Hydro-Québec effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de de Rouyn-Noranda Qc (CYUY) à destination de l'aéroport de la Grande Rivière Qc, (CYGL). Lors du vol, une agente de bord a commencé à ressentir des symptômes similaires à une allergie alimentaire, mais a pu poursuivre ses fonctions jusqu'à destination. À l'arrivée, l'agente a consulté un professionnel de la santé qui a administré une médication comportant des effets secondaires. Le commandant de bord a confirmé l'incapacité de l'agente qui a été remplacée pour les vols subséquents. Aucune autre personne à bord n'a ressenti de symptôme.

C-FQNG, a Sikorsky S-61N operated by VIH Helicopters Limited, was conducting firefighting operations with a long line and bucket approximately 25 nautical miles northwest of Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC, with 2 flight crew members on board. While returning to CYXJ in level flight with an empty bucket, the pilot (who was flying from the LH seat) released the cyclic to adjust the trim. When his hand returned to the cyclic, he inadvertently pressed the cargo release button on the cyclic. The longline and bucket where jettisoned into the forest below. The aircraft continued to CYXJ. There were no injuries to anyone on the ground and the aircraft was not damaged.The company briefed flight crews on operational mitigations to reduce the likelihood of inadvertent load release.

C-GBHO, an Air Canada Rouge LP Airbus 319, operating as ROU1940 was on a flight from Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), Alberta to Toronto/Lester B Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) Ontario. During the descent phase of flight, while descending to 8000 ft in accordance with the BOXUM6 arrival, the flight crew received momentary TCAS RA for traffic below at 7000 ft. The flight crew complied with the RA and advised ATC. The RA only lasted for a few seconds before CLEAR OF CONFLICT was issued. The flight was subsequently completed without further incident.

C-GUAC, an Air Canada A220, was operating flight AC523 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Chicago O'Hare International Airport (KORD), IL. Enroute to KORD, the crew reported a burning electrical smell in the vicinity of row 35. A pan panwas declared for priority handling. The crew turned off IFE systems and smell dissipated, the flight landed without further incident.

The privately registered amphibious Savannah advanced ultralight aircraft (C-ISVG) was conducting a local flight, under visual flight rules, from the Chetwynd Aerodrome (CYCQ), British Columbia (BC), with only the pilot on board. The aircraft was reported overdue at approximately 1715 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) and a search began. The aircraft was found approximately 32 nautical miles southwest of CYCQ, near the shore of Simpson Lake (55° 32' 05" N, 122° 40' 24" W), BC. The pilot was fatally injured. The aircraft had substantial damage. The RCMP responded.The TSB was notified at 1811 PDT by the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre in Victoria, BC. The aircraft was recovered to Fort St. John, BC.

C-GIAA, an Aero Commander operated by Conair Group Incorporated, was conducting a local fire fighting flight from Smithers (CYYD), BC, with 2 crew and 1 passenger on board. During the takeoff roll, the pilot noticed some drift to the right and sensed a reduction in the acceleration rate. The throttle positions were confirmed as matched, but the right engine (Garrett TPE 331-10T-515K) power gauge was indicating 120 hp whereas the planned takeoff setting was 600 hp. The right throttle was advanced but no change in power was noted. The takeoff was aborted at 92 kts (critical engine-failure recognition speed, V1, was 95 kts) and aggressive braking was used to ensure a safe stop on the available runway remaining. After assessing the situation, the crew taxied clear of the runway. They then noted some smoke from the left main landing gear. To cool the brakes, they prolonged the taxi before parking. After parking, the brakes continued smoking and hydraulic fluid was seen running from the left main gear. Company maintenance personnel used fire extinguishers to douse the left and right main wheels. The crew requested emergency services to assist. There was no fire.After troubleshooting the engine issue, the cause of the power reduction was a failed (blocked) propeller governor reset orifice and check valve assembly. They also replaced the left and right main landing gear tires, wheels, and brakes.

C-GASB, a de Haviland DHC 8-102 operated by Summit Air, was conducting a flight from Muskrat Dam (CZMD), ON to Round Lake (CZRJ), ON with 3 crew members and 24 passengers onboard. Shortly after takeoff from Muskrat Dam (CZMD) the crew observed a loss of the #1 hydraulic system. The #1 HYD ISO VLV caution light illuminated with hydraulic quantity showing less than 1 quart. The crew completed the checklist in the QRH, declared an emergency, and diverted to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON. The aircraft subsequently landed safely at CYQT. There was no damage to the aircraft and no injuries.

C-GOWG, a Sunwing B737-800 was operating positioning flight TOM223 from Dalaman Airport (LTBS), Turkey, to East Midlands Airport (EGNX), UK. While flying in Austrian airspace, a flight attendant got injured. A decision was made to divert to Cologne Bonn Airport (EDDK), Germany, where an ambulance met the aircraft and took the flight attendant to the hospital.

C-IFKS, a privately owned SONEX advanced ultra-light, was conducting a visual flight rules flight from Kingston, Ontario to Westport Rideau Lakes (CRL2), Ontario. On landing, the aircraft bounced and drifted laterally away from the centerline to the left side of the runway. The aircraft port wing contacted tall grass which aggravated the drift and resulted in a runway excursion to the left. The aircraft rolled into the long grass and as it was slowing, cartwheeled, overturned and came to rest upside down. The pilot and the passenger egressed the aircraft safely. The aircraft received substantial damage. The ELT activated; there was no post impact fire. The aircraft was recovered and stored in a local hangar. JRCC Trenton dispatched a CH146 Griffon helicopter to locate the ELT signal. The CH146 landed at CRL2, and crew members found and turned the ELT off. Medical assessment indicates the passenger received serious injuries.

C-IIJK, un ultra-léger de base amphibie Aerodyne Stingray effectuait un vol local dans la région de Gatineau, (QC) selon les règles de vol à vue.
