Le pilote seul à bord a décollé d'une piste en gazon et a amorcé une approche 7 minutes plus tard pour amerrir sur la rivière des Outaouais non loin de la traverse Cumberland-Masson.  Lors de la manœuvre d’amerrissage, les roues qui n'avaient pas été remontées après le décollage ont touché la surface de l'eau et l'aéronef s'est renversé. Le pilote non blessé a pu s'en extirper et a été repêché des eaux par des plaisanciers. L’aéronef a été remorqué jusqu’à la rive par les services d'urgence.

N6598B, un Carbon Cub CCX-2000 privé et équipé de pneus toundra, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Rivière-du-Loup, QC (CYRI) à destination des environs de Val d’Or, QC (CYVO). Environ à 18 milles marins à l’est de CYVO, le pilote a effectué un vol de reconnaissance près d’une rivière dans le but d’atterrir le long de celle-ci afin d’y camper pour la nuit. Une fois l’endroit choisi, le pilote a effectué l’approche et a posé l’aéronef dans une zone dégagée d’arbres, mais couverte d’une végétation basse et dense. Alors que l’avion était encore en mouvement, ce dernier a arrêté sa course nette et a basculé vers l’avant pour s’immobiliser à l’envers. Le pilote seul à bord s’est détaché et a pu évacuer l’aéronef sans encombre. Il n’a pas été blessé. Les services d’urgence terrestres ont été avisés de l’accident, car la montre intelligente que portait le pilote a composé le 911. La radiobalise de repérage d’urgence de type 406 a émis un signal de détresse qui a été capté par le Centre canadien de contrôle des missions de Trenton (ON). Le pilote a été récupéré par les services d’urgence terrestre et conduit à Val d’Or.

HB-LEU, a Swiss privately registered Piper PA-34-200 Seneca, was taxiing to conduct a flight from Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL to Bangor International Airport (KBGR), ME, USA.  The CYYR tower controller had given HB-LEU taxi instructions for departure on Runway 08. HB-LEU appeared to have comprehension issues with the assigned routing, the taxiways to use as well as the instruction to hold short of Runway 08. After some confusion regarding the taxi clearance, upon reaching Taxiway Charlie, HB-LEU continued across the hold short line and onto Runway 08. At the same time, C-GJDE, a DHC-6 Twin Otter operated by Air Borealis as Northflight 955, was in the circuit and about to turn final for Runway 08. The controller, upon noticing that HB-LEU had entered the runway, told HB-LEU to immediately turn around, exit the runway and hold short of Runway 08 on Taxiway Charlie. HB-LEU complied with the instructions and Northflight 955 landed safely. HB-LEU departed on their flight shortly after.

C-FKKV, an Air Tractor AT-402B operated by Western Canadian Aerial, was conducting aerial applications flights from Neepawa (CJV5), MB to Whitewood (CKY2), SK. During the landing roll on Runway 09 in CKY2, the pilot inadvertently unlocked the tailwheel. The aircraft's tailwheel started to shimmy and the pilot then applied braking. The left-hand tire blew and, subsequently, the pilot lost directional control and the aircraft exited the left side of the runway. The aircraft sustained minor damage and there was no injuries to the pilot.

C-FNJZ, a Regional Jet 900 operated by Jazz Aviation Ltd, was conducting flight JZA7744 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK with 4 crew members and 63 passengers on board. While on approach to CYXE Runway 15, the tower advised C-FNJZ that the winds direction was 180° at 18 knots, gusting to 29 knots and cleared the aircraft to land. During the landing flare, the right wing dropped. The pilot flying and the captain both applied flight control inputs to correct the wing drop. The aircraft then landed with no further deviations. At the conclusion of the flight, one of the pilots conducted a pre-flight walk-around and a normal station turn was completed. The aircraft then flew uneventfully to CYVR.Once in CYVR, another crew was assigned the aircraft. Upon their pre-flight walk-around, damage was observed on the right wing tip and forward right edge of the leading edge lift device. The aircraft was removed from service for repairs. TSB analysis of the FDR data indicated that the roll exceeded approximately 12 degrees during the touchdown in CYXE.

N584FE, a Federal Express Corporation McDonnell Douglas MD-11F aircraft, operating as FDX247 on a flight from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Memphis International Airport (KMEM), TN, declared an emergency shortly after departure due to a reverse thruster issue. The crew elected to return to CYYZ and landed safely on Runway 05.

C-GIWJ, a WestJet Boeing 737 Max 8 (B38M) aircraft, operating as WJA734, collided with a fuel truck while being marshalled to the gate. The aircraft was on a scheduled flight from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB and had landed in London International Airport (CYXU), ON. The aircraft approached bridge 6 on apron 5 where a fuel truck was actively fuelling another aircraft at the adjacent gate. The wing walker noticed that the wingtip would come close to the fuel truck and signaled the marshaller to stop. The marshaller, in turn, signaled to the aircrew to stop. As the aircraft was slowing, the left-wing tip collided with the fuel truck. The winglet of the wing was then caught in the safety rails on the top of the truck. The aircraft was shut down, passengers were deplaned, and baggage was removed before the aircraft was pushed back from the truck. There was no fire, and no injuries were reported.

C-GKTX, a privately-registered Quest Kodiak 100 amphibious float-equipped aircraft, was conducting a flight from Masset (CYZT), BC to a cabin located approximately 60 nautical miles northwest of Tofino (CYAZ), BC with 4 persons on board. During a go around from a balked landing, the aircraft impacted the terrain. The pilot and 1 passenger were fatally injured, 1 passenger received serious injuries, and 1 occupant received minor injuries. The aircraft was destroyed. The emergency locator transmitter signal was received by the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre in Victoria, BC. Coast Guard, Search and Rescue, RCMP, and fire personnel responded. There was a post-crash fire.

N864AM, a U.S. registered Raytheon/Hawker 800XP aircraft operated by AirMed International, was conducting a MEDEVAC flight from Birmingham/Shuttlesworth Intl (KBHM), AL to Gander Intl (CYQX), NL. When on the ILS approach for Runway 13 at CYQX the crew noticed glide slope anomalies with the avionics and executed a missed approach. On the second attempt the crew opted for the RNAV approach for Runway 13 at CYQX however they continued to encounter avionics issues. The crew decided to divert to their alternate airport, which was Deer Lake airport (CYDF), NL. The crew noted that they would no longer have the required fuel reserves and declared minimum fuel. The flight landed at CYDF without further incident.Maintenance personnel consulted with the avionics manufacturer and determined that a corrupt database may have caused an internal issue that resulted in the approach anomaly. The database was reloaded, and the issue has not reoccurred. The approach information integrity continues to be monitored.

C-GKFB, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was operating flight ROU1674 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), FL. During the descent phase of the flight, while descending through FL290 in accordance with clearance to descend to FL280, ROU1674 received a TCAS TA to shallow descent rate, followed shortly thereafter by a TCAS RA to initially level off which then changed to CLIMB instruction. The flight crew complied with all instructions climbing to FL290 as a result. The ATC was advised, the conflict was resolved and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FYJP, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was operating flight ROU1879 from Hewanorra International Airport (TLPL), Saint-Lucia to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the descent phase of the flight, descending through FL300 in accordance with a descent clearance to FL280, in the vicinity of Frederick Douglass Greater Rochester International Airport (KROC), NY, while on ATC vector, ROU1879 received TCAS RA. The flight crew complied with the RA and leveled off at approximately FL296 and advised Cleveland ATC of the RA. Once the conflict was cleared, the flight continued to destination where it was subsequently completed without further incident.

C-GLQD, a Bombardier DHC-8-400, operating as Porter Airlines flight POE2249, departed Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, destined for Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to "check fire det" and "APU bottle low" annunciators. The flight landed on Runway 14 in CYOW without further incident.

C-FLKA, a Boeing 737-8 (MAX 8) operated by Flair Airlines, was conducting flight FLE620 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. During the flight, the First Officer became ill and the Captain diverted to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB where EMS support was requested. C-FLKA landed uneventfully in CYWG and the First Officer was taken to hospital for evaluation.

C-FDYS un hélicoptère Aérospatiale AS 350B opéré par Les Hélicoptères Panorama Ltée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis un site de chargement situé à environs 8 miles nautiques au nord-est de l'aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, Qc (CYMT) à destination de la mine Troilus. Peu après le décollage avec le chargement de barils de carburant Jet-A, la charge s'est soudainement décrochée d'une altitude entre 200 et 300 pieds sol et les barils se sont fracassés sur des rochers. Il y a eu déversement de carburant. Les autorités ont été contactées et la décontamination a été débutée. Un mauvais ajustement du câble d'ouverture manuelle a été diagnostiqué.

C-GNCH, a Sunwing B737-800 was operating flight TOM1472 from Belfast International Airport (EGAA), UK to Lanzarote Airport (GCRR), Canary Islands, Spain. During rotation for take-off, the tail of the aircraft made contact with the runway. The flight crew put the aircraft in holding while they ran the appropriate checklists and contacted the company. The flight was subsequently instructed to return to EGAA where it landed overweight. There were no reported injuries.

C-GNZQ, un Piper PA-23-250 exploité par Les levés Aéroscan Inc., sous l’indicatif SCANNER4, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Alors que l’aéronef était à 20 milles marins au sud-est de CYQB et en rapprochement, la réception des instructions de la tour sur la radio par l’équipage était difficilement compréhensible et évaluée à 1 sur 5. L’équipage a affiché le code de transpondeur 7600 et s’est posé sans encombre 12 minutes plus tard à CYQB.

C-FIVM, a Boeing 777-300 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA415 from Montreal Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. The aircraft was on approach for runway 05 with a strong crosswind (METAR reported wind: 33016G25); during the landing flare the Captain took control to ensure landing on the centreline, which required some relatively brisk control movements. Initially, three passengers who were seated towards the rear of the aircraft reported that they had been injured during the landing due to the aircraft yawing abruptly. The flight crew arranged to have EMS meet the aircraft at the gate. All three passengers who had reported an injury after the landing declined to be assessed by the waiting EMS personnel and walked away from the gate. The flight data was reviewed by engineers at the TSB laboratory: there was no indication of unusual yaw rates or lateral acceleration during the landing.

C-GJLI, a Beech 200 operated by Mag Aerospace Canada Corp., was conducting a flight from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON to Wapekeka/Angling Lake (CKB6), ON. The aircraft landed at Wapekeka/Angling Lake and, while maneuvering from the runway to the Apron, the left propeller struck a taxi light. The propeller strike went unnoticed by the captain and the aircraft conducted 2 additional flights, ending in Kenora (CYQK), ON. Once in CYQK, the captain noticed damage to the left propeller. It was subsequently reported that a taxi light in CKB6 was also damaged.The operator's maintenance conducted an inspection and replaced the left propeller and engine. The operator conducted an internal investigation and is undertaking short and long-term corrective actions.

C-GJWN, an Airbus A321-200 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA601 from Halifax Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), Nova Scotia, to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario. During the descent, the flight crew heard a noise and felt a vibration under the floor of the flight deck, which was followed by the smell of fumes on the flight deck. The crew donned their oxygen masks, declared PAN PAN, and continued the flight to CYYZ, landing uneventfully on Runway 24L with ARFF standing by. Maintenance inspection revealed a faulty avionics blower fan which was replaced before the aircraft was returned to service.

N711WS, a CL-600-2B19 (CRJ-200) operated by TVPX Aircraft Solutions Trustee, departed Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, at 1742 EDT, on a flight to Republic Airport (KFRG), NY, USA. While the operator did not submit a report, it appears that they made an approach at KFRG and conducted a go-around, followed by delaying vectors for approximately 8 minutes before initiating a return to CYYZ. During the arrival, the flight crew declared an emergency with Toronto Centre, stating that they were unable to cycle the main gear. After conducting two low approaches on Runway 33L in order for the tower controllers to assess the position of their landing gear, a third approach resulted in a normal landing at 2050 EDT.

C-GBZS, a Sunwing B737-800 was preparing to operate flight TOM7732 from Birmingham Airport (EGBB), UK to Kos International Airport (LGKO), Greece. A fuel leak occurred while refueling the aircraft because of high ambient air temperatures. The fuel spilled from the right wing overflow valve and under the fuel truck. ARFF and Maintenance were subsequently notified. ARFF attended the aircraft because the spill was classified as large. The crew disembarked the aircraft while the spill was being cleaned up. No passengers were onboard during the time of the spill. After the spill had been cleaned up, the crew proceeded to board passengers and the flight departed without further issues.

C-GTVV, a Talon Helicopters Airbus Helicopters AS365-N3 (Dauphin), was conducting Class B external load operations via a hoist at Saltery Bay (49º46'55 N, 124º10'33 W), BC with 2 flight crew members and 1 hoist operator on board. The crew was installing power line markers using an automated robot attached to the hoist hook. The robot is placed on the line and installs the marker balls on powerline crossings. While attempting to remove the robot from the powerline after the third marker ball was installed, the robot became stuck on the powerline and could not be removed using the hoist. The hoist operator used manual cable cutters to cut the hoist cable as outlined in the company’s standing operating procedures. The helicopter returned to the staging without further incident.The helicopter’s hoist cable will be replaced and a hoist inspection carried out. The robot was removed from powerline using an external load grapple hook.

C-GBKB, a Morning Partners Challenger 605 was conducting a flight from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), NV to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. After departing RWY 26R in KLAS, the aircraft experienced a flap failure. The flaps would not retract from the Flap 20 take off position. The crew contacted the departure controller and informed them that they would be returning to KLAS. The ATC offered an immediate return to RWTY 19L. The crew informed ATC that they would need time to complete the applicable QRH checklist. ATC provided vectors, offered any runway for landing and indicated that they had all the time they needed to complete the required checklists. Once landing data was calculated, the crew requested an ILS approach onto RWY 26L. The ILS approach was flown in the Flap 20 configuration, at the calculated ref speed. ARFF was requested to stand by to inspect the brakes after landing. An uneventful landing wascompleted with an emphasis on the caution note from QRH, page FCTM 07-6. The aircraft exited RWY 26L at intersection A7. The aircraft was stopped on taxiway A and a visual inspection was completed by ARFF. Once the all-clear was given by ARFF, the aircraft was taxied to SignatureAviation, with ARFF following as a precaution. After parking and shutdown, ARFF completed another brake inspection and reported a brake temperature of 680 deg on the left brake and 570 deg on the right brake. No further action was required or provided by ARFF.

C-GSGY, a Sander Geophysics Ltd. Cessna 208 Grand Caravan was conducting a ferry flight from Mallacoota Aerodrome (YMCO), Australia to Kempsey Airport (YKMP), Australia. During flight, the ADF #1 was turned on, shortly after turning it on, the system flickered on/off and then remained on. About 45 seconds later the co-pilot noticed white smoke coming from the on/off knob of the ADF. He promptly turned off the unitand informed the captain. After confirming the ADF was smoking, the captain pulled the ADF #1 circuit breaker. The flight was able to carry on to destination without further incident, and no emergency was declared.

C-GJXY, an Airbus A220-300 operated by Air Canada as ACA692 was conducting a flight from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to St John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL with 6 crew members and 125 passengers on board. During the flight, the First Officer became incapacitated. A deadheading Captain assumed the crew members duties and the aircraft landed without further incident. Emergency Medical Services met the aircraft at the gate upon arrival.

C-GJXV, an Air Canada A220 was conducting flight AC1039 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Denver International Airport (KDEN), CO when on approach the flight crew received a TCAS RA. The RA was followed and the flight continued to land without further incident.

N172AC, an Erickson Incorporated Sikorsky S-64E (Skycrane) helicopter, was conducting heli-logging from a remote gravel service landing pad in the vicinity of Port Douglas, BC, with 2 crew on board. As the aircraft entered the hover landing phase, the right main landing gear oleo and strut assembly decoupled from the helicopter. The assembly fell and struck the ground in the service landing area but did no damage to vehicles or equipment and caused no injury to ground personnel. Flight and ground crews communicated and coordinated their actions via radio and hand signals. The crew did a light landing on the nose and left main landing gear and kept the right main gear housing off the ground as they took on fuel. A plan was devised, and a pickup truck was maneuvered to support the helicopter in place of the decoupled landing gear. The pilot successfully landed the right gear housing structure in the bed of the truck and shut down the helicopter.The maintenance crew inspected and replaced the right landing gear with a complete oleo, strut, and housing assembly. The company will submit a Service Difficulty Bulletin for the aircraft type and model.

C-FWRI, un appareil construction amateur Super-Rocket sur flotteurs, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis un lac situé à 56 miles nautiques de l'aéroport de Chute-des-Passes,Qc (CYDG) à destination d'un autre lac situé à environs 10 miles nautiques au nord-est du point de départ. Lors de l'amerrissage sur la surface d'eau miroitante, le pilote a perdu le contrôle et l'appareil a capoté vers l'avant. Les occupants ont pu évacuer sans blessures et ont ramé jusqu'à la rive.

C-GNVJ un Piper PA-31-325 en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Port-Menier, QC. (CYPN) à destination de l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, Qc. (CYZV). Lors du séquencement pour l'approche à la piste 09, C-GNVJ a été instruit de se placer derrière C-GSAG un Pilatus PC-12/45 exploité par Univair Aviation Inc. en approche finale, qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC à destination de l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, Qc. (CYZV). Le virage serré de C-GNVJ a entraîné la perte d'espacement entre les 2 aéronefs. l'espacement a été réduit à 4.1 Nm à la même altitude alors que les minimums requis sont de 5 miles horizontalement et 1000 pieds verticalement. Le contrôleur a demandé à C-GNVJ de virer à gauche de 020 degrés. Aussitôt l'espacement récupéré, C-GNVJ a été autorisé à virer vers le nord pour joindre la finale 09 derrière C-GSAG. Les deux appareils ont atterri sans encombre.

The Villers Air Services Ltd. King Air C90, C-GCFB, was departing Fort Nelson (CYYE), BC on a pilot proficiency check (PPC) with two crew and a pilot examiner on board. While operating in instrument meteorological conditions (IMC) the flight crew observed smoke in the cockpit. Oxygen masks were donned, a MAYDAY call was made and an immediate return to CYYE was requested. An instrument landing system (ILS) approach was made to the airport and the aircraft landed uneventfully. Maintenance update: On investigation, it was found that the cabin florescent light dimming resistor was overheating.  Various wires in the vicinity of the resistor showed signs of combustion and overheating. The cabin florescent light circuit was disconnected, and damaged wires were repaired.  No further faults were found.

C-FEXG, a privately registered Cessna 120 was operating on a multi leg visual flight rules round trip from Delta Heritage Airpark (CAK3), BC, with only the pilot on board. The accident occurred on the leg from Langley (CYNJ), BC, to Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC. While on short final to Runway 26L at CYPK, the engine (Teledyne Continental Motors C-85-12-F) stopped producing power. The pilot determined that they would be unable to reach the runway and performed a forced landing into the grass on the runway's extended centreline, parallel and left of the line of omni-directional approach lights (ODAL). The aircraft touched down approximately 1400 feet from the displaced threshold of Runway 26L. The aircraft overturned and came to rest inverted. The pilot egressed and was not injured. Police, fire, and ambulance services all responded. At the time of the accident, the temperature / dew point at 2 airports within 19 nautical miles of CYPK were 19°C / 14°C at Vancouver International (CYVR) and 21°C / 14°C at Abbotsford (CYXX). The carburetor heat control was determined to be in the cold/off position. There was no post impact fire, but the aircraft was substantially damaged.The aircraft has been recovered and will be assessed by maintenance for repair.

C-FLQZ, a Flair Airlines Ltd. B737-8 conducting flight F8726 from Victoria International Airport (CYYJ), BC to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB declared an emergency in the vicinity of Birch Bay, WA, due to smoke in the cockpit. The crew elected to divert to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. The aircraft landed safely in CYVR. The aircraft was able to taxi to the first taxiway, where ARFF (Air Rescue and Fire Fighting) performed a survey of the aircraft.

C-GAHI un hélicoptère Aérospatiale AS350B-2 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue pour transporter des travailleurs depuis l'aéroport de Mary River, Nunavut (CMR2) à destination d'un site de forage situé à environs 55 miles nautiques au sud de CMR2. À environ 36 miles nautiques du point de départ, la visibilité s'est rapidement dégradée. Le pilote a amorcé une descente pour maintenir la visibilité et trouver un endroit propice à l'atterrissage. Peu de temps après, l'appareil a percuté le sol et s'est renversé sur le côté. La poutre de queue s'est séparée et a été projetée devant l'appareil immobilisé sur son flanc droit. Le pilote et les 2 passagers ont pu évacuer sans blessures et ont été secourus par un autre hélicoptère travaillant dans le même secteur. La balise de détresse s'est déclenchée.

C-FIEM. an Airbus Helicopters AS 350-B3 (AStar), operated by a Yellowhead Helicopters Limited, was conducting aerial firefighting operations in the vicinity of Pink Mountain, BC, with only the pilot on board. During an attempted water drop, the pilot inadvertently pressed the cargo release button which led to the bucket and the longline being released. They both landed in an un-populated area within the confines of the fire. The bucket and longline were both eventually recovered.

C-FCNB, a Cessna 172L operated by Truro Flying Club, was conducting a Canada Post mail flight from Debert Airport (CCQ3), NS to Pictou Island, NS with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the approach to landing phase, the right wingtip hit a tree branch just before the flare. This resulted in a yaw and slight roll to the right. The pilot added full power to attempt a go-around, however the right bank continued, and further contact was made with more tree branches, resulting in a speed decay. The aircraft sunk into the trees with the right wing low and the prop making further contact with the shrubs and trees. The aircraft pivoted 180 degrees of heading to the right and came to an abrupt stop, with the nose pitching downwards. The aircraft settled on top of a fence when it came to its final resting position. Once stopped the pilot secured the aircraft. Both the pilot and passenger exited through the right door and were  not injured. The ELT activated and JRCC was advised.

C-GHPD, an Air Canada Rouge A321-200 was conducting flight ROU1602 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL. During the cruise phase of the flight, a flight attendant sustained a minor injury during service delivery. The flight attendant was deemed incapacitated and unable to continue safety duties. The safety duties were redistributed amongst the remaining flight attendants in accordance with company policy and procedure. The flight was subsequently completed without further incident.

C-FPBJ, an Air Tindi de Havilland DHC-7, operating as TINDI 806 on a flight from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Ekati (CYOA), NT experienced a flap system failure on approach to CYOA. A missed approach was carried out and, after consulting with operations and maintenance, the aircraft returned to CYZF. A PAN PAN call was made and the crew informed ATC that emergency services were not required. An uneventful flapless landing was carried out and the aircraft taxied in to the Air Tindi facility. Maintenance Update: The flap power control unit (PCU) was found to be faulty. It was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GITR, an Air Canada Rouge A319 was operating flight ROU1795 from Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), Dominican Republic to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the climb to cruise phase of flight, through approximately 4000 ft. ASL, the flight crew received an ECAM PACK 2 Fault followed by PACK 1 + 2 Fault. The ECAM actions were carried out and the aircraft leveled at 10,000 ft. ASL in order to carry out troubleshooting activities. The aircraft held for a period of time until returning to origin where a PAN PAN was declared as a precaution and an overweight landing was carried out. The flight was subsequently completed without further incident.

C-GMYU, an Air Canada A220 operating as flight AC1016 from Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport (KMSP), MN to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON was taxiing for departure when a cabin crew advised that smoke appeared in the cabin and a strong electrical smell was present. A Pan Pan was declared and the aircraft returned to the gate as smoke dissipated. ARFF met the aircraft at the gate and the passengers were deplaned.

C-GYTO, an Alpha Jet Model A aircraft operated by Top Aces Inc. was operating as CHETA61 on a local flight from Fredericton Intl. Airport, NB (CYFC). During the approach to RWY27 at CYFC the pilot lowered the landing gear and then received an anti-skid abnormal indication. A missed approach was conducted to allow for time to analyze the fault. Subsequent testing of the brake system revealed no problem with the brake system. CYFC tower offered initiating aircraft rescue and firefighting trucks to position, and the pilot accepted.The aircraft landed uneventfully at 11:12 with ARFF standing by.

C-GOSX, a Piper Aerostar PA-60-600, operated by Forest Protection Limited as BD171 was on a positioning flight from Fredericton Intl. Airport, NB (CYFC) to Yarmouth Airport, NS (CYQI) for birddog duty in forest fire operations. On approach to RWY33 at CYQI the pilot selected gear down and noted that the nose landing gear (NLG) indicator did not illuminate. The pilot executed a go around and re-entered the circuit. On the downwind leg the landing gear was cycled two more times without a change in the NLG down indication even though the reflection of the NLG in the prop spinner showed that it was extended. The NLG bulb was checked and found to be serviceable after which the pilot elected to return to CYFC.On approach to RWY 33 at CYFC the gear was lowered, and the NLG not locked indication persisted. The pilot contacted CYFC tower and requested Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting be on standby. The aircraft landed safely at 14:29 AST. Maintenace determined that the NLG not locked indication problem was due to a broken wire.

C-GENU, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was conducting flight WEN3283 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Prince George (CYXS), BC. While conducting the pre-flight walk around, the first officer (FO) noticed smoke originating from the auxiliary power unit (APU). The FO advised the Captain. There were no cockpit indications of an APU fire. The APU had not been started and all the APU switches were in the off position. The Captain actioned the Quick Reference Checklist, notified air traffic control on the ground frequency, and requested aircraft rescue and firefighting services. Maintenance replaced the APU generator control unit and carried out an APU operational test with no defects noted. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWUU, an Air Canada B787-9 was operating as flight AC0005 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Narita International Airport (RJAA), Japan. While on approach, the flight crew received a TCAS RA.  The RA was followed and the approach was discontinued. The flight completed a go around and continued to land without further incident.

The WestJet Boeing 737-800, C-GWSX, was operating as flight WJA1536 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Phoenix (KPHX), AZ. During pushback from the gate, the flight crew had started both engines. Once the aircraft was on Taxiway BA, the pushback tractor stopped, and the ground crew disconnected the towbar. The aircraft started rolling forward towards the pushback tractor, where the lower nose of the aircraft collided with the roof structure of the tractor. A hole was punctured into the lower fuselage and the tractor became wedged in the fuselage. The windshield of the tractor was shattered. There were no injuries. The aircraft received damage to the lower fuselage and radome. After company maintenance assessed the aircraft damage, the aircraft was towed back to the gate and the passengers deplaned.

C-GELU, an Air Canada B737-8 was operating as flight AC1059 from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), NV to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC. After departure, the flight crew received a TCAS RA. The RA was followed and the flight continued to CYVR without further incident.

C-FHNJ, a Skyservice Business Aviation Inc Cessna 560XL operating flight SYB505 from Windsor International Airport (CYQG), ON to Nashville International Airport (KBNA), TN, declared an emergency due to a landing gear issue. The crew elected to continue to KBNA where the aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GBHZ, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was conducting flight ROU1622 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL. During the cruise phase of flight (vicinity of Virginia), a Flight Attendant became ill and was unable to continue safety duties. Cabin safety duties were redistributed amongst the remaining Flight Attendants in accordance with company policies and procedures. The flight crew declared a medical emergency and continued to KFLL where the flight was completed without further incident.

C-FRSB, a privately operated amateur-built Bushmaster Model B aircraft on amphibian floats was on a VFR flight from Greenwood Airport, NS (CYZX) to Lake George, NS. When the aircraft departed CYZX the landing gear was not retracted. Enroute to destination the pilot elected to do a touch and go on Aylesford Lake, NS and when the aircraft touched down it nosed over immediately, and the cabin space began to fill with water. The pilot was not injured and unstrapped the safety harness and utilized techniques learned from a recent floatplane dunker training course to exit the aircraft. Once outside and clear of the aircraft the pilot inflated the life vest and swam approximately one kilometer to the shoreline. The pilot then utilized a cellphone to contact the duty officer at CFB Greenwood and informed them of the accident. The 121.5 MHz emergency locator transmitter did not activate.C-FRSB was equipped with a Wipaire gear position warning system that consisted of four (4) hard surface green colored indicator lights and four (4) water surface blue colored indicator lights. Additionally, C-FRSB contained an aural gear advisory that indicated the gear position once the throttle was reduced below a set value. On the occurrence landing, the aircraft checklist and GUMP’s check, which were normally done, were not completed. The aural gear advisory, which stated that the gear was down, had been immediately silenced by the pilot prior to touchdown.The aircraft sustained water damage and impact damage to the windshield, left wing, tail and empennage.

C-GIED, a de Havilland DHC-6-300 operated by Air Borealis, was conducting flight LBR480 from Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL to Natuashish Airport (CNH2), NL. While on the initial take-off roll, upon application of takeoff power, smoke appeared from the power lever quadrant in the cockpit ceiling. The flight crew rejected the takeoff before becoming airborne and taxied clear of the runway. The flight crew opened their side windows for ventilation as the smoke appeared to be confined to the cockpit area. The crew taxied the aircraft to the gate, ran the appropriate checklist for shutdown and deplaned the passengers. Maintenance then towed the aircraft to the hangar for inspection. Maintenance determined that a wiring connector had shorted out in the cockpit ceiling producing the smoke.

C-GFRG, an Airbus Helicopters MBB-BK117 D-2 operated by Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service (STARS), was conducting a flight from Regina Intl (CYQR), SK. At approximately 53 nm North of CYQR, the #1 engine (Safran Helicopter Engines Arriel 2E) chip annunciator illuminated. The checklist was carried out and a unsuccessful fuzz burn was completed. The crew conducted a #1 engine shutdown and the aircraft returned to CYQR where a single-engine landing was conducted uneventfully. The operator's maintenance inspected the chip detectors and found multiple metallic particles.

C-GMHN, a Bell 206L helicopter operated by Churchill Falls (Labrador) Corporation Ltd., was conducting a flight from Churchill Falls (CZUM), NL. During start up, the engine failed to accelerate past idle during the start sequence. The pilot subsequently shut down the engine.Maintenance determined that the nut on the P3 line had loosened. Maintenance retorqued the line and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFMI, a Morningstar Partners Ltd. Challenger 650 was conducting a flight from Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS), MA to Teterboro Airport (KTEB), NJ when flying direct to DWURF for the RNAV Y 06 and leveled at 3,000', the aircraft encountered a VFR target that was 400' below and shortly after received a TCAS Resolution Advisory - 'Monitor Descent Rate'. Since the aircraft was leveled, no corrective action was needed/required by the crew. The traffic was visually confirmed and passed off the left side of the aircraft. The aircraft landed in KTEB without incident.

C-GPQO, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting flight JV209 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG) MB. to Gods Lake Narrows (CYGO) MB. In the vicinity of CYGO, the aircraft experienced a #1 hydraulic system failure. The flight crew declared an emergency and made an operational decision to return to CYWG. The aircraft landed safely in CYWG.The operator's maintenance found the #1 hydraulic pump inlet/outlet port O-ring blew out; allowing hydraulic fluid to escape. The upper 2 bolts were found to be backed out. An SDR was filed.

C-GLDE, an ATR 42-320 operated by Transwest Air Ltd (dba Rise Air) was conducting flight RS103 from Stony Rapids (CYSF), SK. to Prince Albert/Glass Field (CYPA), SK. When the aircraft was approximately 150 nm south of CYSF, the green hydraulic system low pressure warning light illuminated. The flight crew referenced the QRH and SOPs and notified the cabin crew. RS103 declared a PAN PAN with ATC and diverted to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl. (CYXE), SK. where more services were available. RS103 landed safely in CYXE.The operator's maintenance found the green hydraulic system circuit breaker was popped and suspected the hydraulic pump was seized. There was no fluid loss. The system was deferred under MEL.

C-GUKV, a Sikorsky S76C, operated by Helijet International Incorporated, was conducting a charter flight from Nanaimo (CYCD), BC, to Port Hardy (CYZT), BC, with 2 passengers and 2 crew on board. After landing on runway 29, the crew exited on taxiway Bravo and taxied to the apron. While maneuvering on the apron to park the helicopter, the left main landing gear fell in an uncovered drainage hole and collapsed backwards. The pilot-flying (seated in the left seat) immediately applied hard right control to the cyclic and the pilot-in-command (seated in the right seat) shut off the engines and applied rotor brake. The helicopter came to rest on the left side of its belly. There were no injuries. The main rotor blades did not contact the ground however, the aircraft was substantially damaged.The helicopter was recovered to the operator's maintenance base for assessment and repair.

C-IKBS, a privately registered Zenair CH701 basic ultralight was conducting a local flight from an unnamed airstrip in Surrey, BC, with only the pilot on board. The pilot departed eastbound and at approximately 500 feet above ground level, the engine (Yamaha) lost power. The pilot turned left to return to the airstrip and then conducted a forced landing northeast of the airstrip on an adjacent field. The aircraft landed hard and a post impact fire began. The pilot egressed unassisted but sustained serious injuries. The aircraft was destroyed. The fire department arrived shortly after and began to extinguish the airframe fire and the ensuing grass fire.

C-GBKB a Morningstar Partners Ltd dba was conducting flight 27350 from Seattle/Boeing Field/King County Intl. (KBFI), WA to Naples airport (KAPF), FL.  During cruise at FL410 vertical of Bay St-Louis/ Stennis Intl. (KHSA), MS, flight crew saw an unidentified object (estimated height six feet with white dome and red device attached under it) visible in the left-hand windshield and estimated at less than half a mile from the plane. Flight crew informed ATC (Houston Center) with location and description. ATC advised they were going to report the unidentified object.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GLWN, a North Cariboo Flying Service De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-311, was operating as flight NCA4080 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB, with 3 crew members and 20 passengers on board. After engine start, once the bleed air was selected on, the aircraft pressurization system started to pressurize the aircraft on the ground. The captain shut the bleeds off and set the pressurization system from Auto to Manual; which had no immediate effect. Both the first officer and the flight attendant showed signs of incapacitation and the aircraft was shut down on the ramp. The aircraft needed to be manually depressurized prior to opening the main cabin door. 2 crew members and 1 passenger suffered minor injuries. The aircraft was not damaged. Maintenance subsequently inspected the suction lines going into the pressurization controller and no defects were noted. Upon reconnecting the suction lines, it was found that in manual mode the pressurization controller would intermittently pressurize the aircraft on the ground. The Cabin Pressure Controller was replaced and the system was tested serviceable in both auto and manual mode. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJTX, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was conducting flight ROU1677 from Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During flight level change from FL330 to FL350 (as per ATC clearance) in vicinity of waypoint EMCET, flight crew received instruction from ATC to immediately return to FL340 for traffic. Flight crew complied with instructions but as the aircraft transitioned from climb to descent (approximately FL350) a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory) ''DESCEND'' was received and complied with. Once the conflict was resolved, flight crew was cleared to FL370 and the flight continued without further incident.

C-FEJT, a Cessna 172S aircraft operated by Toronto Airways Inc., was engaged in circuit training on Runway 27 at Peterborough Airport, Ontario (CYPQ), under the control of a student pilot. During the takeoff roll, the student pilot lost control of the aircraft, causing it to veer to the left and depart from the side of the runway. The aircraft then transitioned across the grass before ultimately coming to a stop in a muddy ditch. As a result of the incident, the aircraft sustained substantial damage, there were no reported injuries.

C-GOHP, un hélicoptère AS350 BA exploité par Les Hélicoptères Panorama Ltée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis un lieu de rassemblement pour aller récupérer une équipe sur le terrain, située à environ 60 milles nautiques à l’est de l’aéroport de La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL). Après avoir localisé les travailleurs au sol, le pilote a amorcé son approche face au vent pour aller se poser près de ceux-ci en bordure d’un lac. Le pilote a manœuvré l’aéronef de manière à positionner le rotor de queue au-dessus de la surface de l’eau et les patins sur la végétation. Durant la mise en charge du poids sur les patins de la phase finale de l’atterrissage, l’aéronef a basculé vers l’arrière et le rotor de queue est entré en contact avec la surface de l’eau. Le pilote a perdu la maîtrise de l’aéronef qui a basculé sur le côté. Une fois immobilisé, le pilote a fermé le moteur et s’est extirpé de l’aéronef. Ni le pilote ni les travailleurs au sol n’ont été blessés. La radiobalise de repérage d’urgence de type 406 MHz s’est déclenchée et le signal de détresse a été capté par le Centre de contrôle des missions de Trenton, ON à 15 h 45 heure avancée de l’Est. Un autre hélicoptère de la compagnie a été envoyé sur place pour aller récupérer les personnes.

C-GKVU, a Sunwing B737-800 conducting flight SWG751 from Cancun International airport (MMUN), Mexico to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON when in the vicinity of Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (KCVG), KY, the Cabin Crew alerted the Flight Crew to a passenger's e-Cigarette that was overheating and emitting some smoke. The Cabin Crew promptly placed the e-Cigarette in an ice bucket filled with water, which was then placed into a cannister. The Cabin Crew continued to monitor the e-Cigarette for the remainder of the flight, and the cannister was locked in the aft lavatory for landing. The Flight Crew reviewed the QRH for Smoke, Fire or Fumes and increased speed as a precaution. Theaircraft continued safely to destination and landed in CYYZ without further issue. At the conclusion of the flight, maintenance removed the cannister containing the e-Cigarette.

C-GWEN, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN9820 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Ft. Chipewyan (CYPY), AB with 2 flight crew and 2 flight attendants on board. During the initial climb after take-off from CYYC, the flight crew heard a bang and the aircraft yawed to the right. Both flight crew observed that the No. 2 ITT was reading 1100°C. The captain (pilot flying) turned off the autopilot and as both flight crew assessed the situation the engine fire aural warning sounded. Smoke and fumes were also detected in the flight deck and in the cabin. The captain asked for the engine fire quick reference checklist and the first office commenced the actions. The captain declared a MAYDAY with ATC and leveled the aircraft at 8200 feet ASL. When the No. 2 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW150A) was shutdown, the smoke and fumes dissipated. The No. 1 fire bottle was actuated and after 30 seconds, the fire light remained illuminated. The No. 2 fire bottle was actuated and the fire light remained illuminated. The captain requested a priority return for CYYC and ATC vectored WEN9820 back to the airport. The No.2 fire light extinguished a few minutes later and WEN9820 completed a single-engine approach and landing onto Runway 35R. ARFF inspected the aircraft on the runway prior to the aircraft continuing to the gate. The TSB Edmonton office has deployed 2 investigators to CYYC.

C-FLWD, an amateur-built Zenith CH-200 aircraft, was flying approximately 1-2 miles southeast of North Bay Jack Garland Airport (CYYB), ON at an altitude of about 2500 feet AGL when the engine experienced a loss of power. The pilot declared an emergency and initiated a forced approach toward the threshold of Runway 36. During the approach, the aircraft cleared the perimeter fence but was unable to reach the runway. Instead, it touched down on the soft grass before the runway. Upon landing, the nose gear collapsed, resulting in extensive damage to the belly of the aircraft. There were two occupants on board, with one of them sustaining a minor injury.

C-GJYC, un Airbus A220-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif AC337, se préparait à effectuer un vol au départ de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Qc (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport d'Edmonton, Ab (CYEG). Alors que l'aéronef était en phase de retrait de la passerelle d'embarquement avec 147 personnes à bord, la passerelle à endommagée l'aéronef. L'aéronef a été mis hors service et le vol a dû être reporté.

C-FYAI, un DeHavilland DHC-8-300 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif AIE802, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Qc (CYUL) à destination de Kuujjuarapik, Qc (CYGW). Peu après le décollage de CYUL, le moteur 2 s'est arrêté sans mise en drapeau de l'hélice. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'aéronef est revenu se poser sans encombre à CYUL. Une fois au sol, l'équipage a rapporté que le système d'orientation du train avant était non fonctionnel.

C-GYLP, a Boeing 737-800, was conducting Swoop Inc. flight WSW360 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. At the top of descent, one of the flight attendants became ill. Oxygen was administered to the flight attendant who was unable to perform their duties. Emergency medical services tended to the flight attendant upon arrival at the gate.

C-FHNL, a Boeing 737-752 aircraft operated by Bradley Air Services Limited, was conducting flight AKT1420 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB, to Fort Mackay/Albian (CAL4), AB. During the initial RNAV RWY31 approach into CAL4, the crew of C-FHNL observed VFR traffic (C-GWRK, a Cessna 208B aircraft operated by McMurray Aviation) on their TCAS. At the IGSAD fix, C-FHNL received and followed a TCAS RA command to climb. C-FHNL did not have visual contact with C-GWRK during the maneuver. The pilot of C-GWRK acquired the Boeing visually and descended. Spacing between the aircraft reduced to 2 nm laterally and 100 feet vertically. C-FHNL completed a right hand orbit to rejoin final approach for Runway 31 and landed without incident.

On 2 May 2023, the Durham Regional Police Service (DRPS) reported the discovery of an aircraft wreckage found by local landowners near Port Perry/Utica Field (CUT2). The DRPS deployed to the site, took photographs of the accident, and reported it to the Transportation Safety Board (TSB). The aircraft's condition, covered in leaves and branches, indicated it had likely been in that location for some time.Further investigation revealed that the accident occurred on 25 August 2022, involving a privately-owned amateur-built Zenair CH 601 HDS with registration C-FUBE. The aircraft was performing visual flight rules circuits at CUT2 when it encountered a fuel pressure-related engine issue after a touch and go. As a result, the pilot opted for a forced landing into the trees, resulting in a collision with the heavily forested terrain, approximately 0.8 nautical miles from the departure end of the runway. The aircraft came to rest inverted on the ground, the pilot was not injured. However, the aircraft itself was destroyed in the crash.

C-FTNH, un Cessna 310R exploité par Exact Air inc., effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) pour la Société de protection des forêts contre le feu (SOPFEU) au départ de l’aéroport de Roberval, Qc (CYRJ). Alors que l’aéronef effectuait l’inspection de la zone de feu située à 8 milles nautiques au nord de l’aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, Qc (CYRC), le pilote a remarqué une indication de surchauffe de température d’huile pour le moteur gauche. Le pilote a actionné la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a fermé le moteur. Une fois le moteur sécurisé, le pilote a demandé l’autorisation d’atterrir à CYRC. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre et a circulé vers les installations d’Exact Air sur son propre pouvoir.  L’inspection au sol a révélé qu’un connecteur desserré dans le faisceau de câble de la jauge de température d’huile était à l’origine de l’indication de surchauffe.

C-FFQV, a Conair Group Incorporated De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402AT air tanker, departed Abbotsford (CYXX), BC, as flight FGD547, to conduct firebombing training in the vicinity of Harrison Lake, BC with 2 crew members on board. After the fourth drop, the crew were alerted that the retardant tank doors did not close. The associated warning alarm could not be silenced and interfered with crew communication with air traffic control. The flight returned to the CYXX area and, after discussions with ground-based maintenance, the crew reset the retardant tank system which eventually silenced the tank door warning. When the crew lowered the landing gear, the gear warning horn became active and could not be silenced. The crew declared a "PAN PAN" emergency and conducted a low pass for a visual inspection by CYXX Tower controller. The controller confirmed the aircraft appeared normal and the crew landed without further incident.Maintenance personnel were unable to replicate the fault on the ground and a subsequent flight was conducted with no faults found. Maintenance and engineering have developed supplementary quick reference handbook procedures for resetting the tank door system and audio alerts. They are developing dedicated reset switches for the door and audio alert systems.

C-GIZX, un Beech King Air BE10 exploité par Propair Inc, effectuait le vol PRO4200M selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Chisasibi, QC (CSU2) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Alors que l’aéronef se trouvait en croisière au niveau de vol (FL)190 à la verticale du lac Evans, QC, une forte détonation et des vibrations ont été entendus et ressentis par l’équipage de conduite, accompagné du voyant « RIGHT GEN ». L'équipage a actionné la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a fermé le moteur droit. Une urgence a été déclarée (MAYDAY) et l’équipage de conduite a demandé un déroutement vers l’aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY). L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-FISO, a Skyservice Business Aviation Gulfstream G200 conducting flight SYB079, departed Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport, ON (CYYZ) for San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA. The flight crew received an APU Bleed Air Leak master caution light and corresponding EICAS message, while climbing through 11 000 feet. The flight crew carried out the QRH items and the fault remained. The crew declared a PAN PAN and elected to return to CYYZ, the aircraft landed overweight without further incident.

Un paramoteur Jean Mateos Macfly, de propriété privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis un champ privé situé à Béthanie, Qc. Pour une raison inconnue, le paramoteur a percuté le sol. Le pilote, seul à bord, a été mortellement blessé.

C-FENO, a WestJet Encore Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was operating as flight WEN3540 from Kamloops (CYKA), BC, to Calgary International (CYYC), AB, with 4 crew members and 67 passengers on board. During the takeoff roll, the “YD DISENGAGED” message illuminated just after 80 knots. The crew rejected the take-off, and a MAYDAY emergency was declared with air traffic control. After exiting the runway, the emergency was canceled. No one was injured and there was no damage to the aircraft.After actioning the quick reference handbook, the yaw damper appeared to re-engage. The crew reported this to company maintenance, and it was decided the aircraft could continue in operation.

C-FBLE, un Bernard L’Écuyer BE-12-LE de construction amateur, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis l’aéroport de Gatineau/Ottawa, Qc (CYND) avec un pilote et un passager à son bord. Lors de la course à l’atterrissage, le train principal gauche s’est affaissé causant un mouvement de cheval de bois. L’appareil s’est immobilisé sur la piste. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

C-GTOP, a privately registered Cessna C340A, was conducting an IFR training flight out of Calgary/Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB, with 2 pilots on board. C-GTOP commenced the RNAV RWY35 approach into Drumheller Municipal Airport (CEG4), AB. The aerodrome was closed via NOTAM for runway maintenance; IFR approaches to the airport were not authorized by NOTAM. There were 2 vehicles on the runway. The vehicle operators attempted to wave off the aircraft on final: however, C-GTOP conducted a touch and go landing on Runway 35 with both vehicles still on the runway. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft or vehicles.

C-GWJG, a Boeing 737-7CT operated by WestJet Airlines Inc, was conducting flight WJA303 from Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC with 5 crew members and 73 passengers on board. While level at FL400 the flight crew observed an illuminated #1 generator annunciator light. The light remained illuminated after the flight crew performed the non-normal checklist. The flight crew declared PAN-PAN and diverted to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. During the descent to FL230 the flight crew received a TCAS RA, which was complied with; there was no loss of separation or risk of collision. While the crew was hand flying the aircraft after the TCAS RA, the aircraft descended approximately 400 feet below FL230; they then corrected the deviation. The aircraft landed in Calgary without incident.The aircraft was removed from service for troubleshooting. The #1 Generator Control Unit (GCU and the Bus Power Control Unit (BPCU)) were replaced and tested serviceable. A service difficulty report (SDR) was filed with Transport Canada. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GSGF, a Viking Air Limited DHC-6-300 was conducting local survey flight approximately 272 NM North of Sohar Airport (OOSH), Oman.  During cruise, smoke started to accumulate behind first officer survey display screen.  Pilot broke off the survey line, climbed to a safe altitude and completed the emergency checklist.  Soon after the survey equipment was shut down the smoke dissipated.  Flight diverted back to OOSH without further incident.

C-GLQK, a Porter Airlines de Havilland DHC-8-402, was conducting flight PD2283 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON to Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. While PD2283 was being vectored for the approach to Runway 05, C-GMBL, a privately registered Beechcraft BE58 Baron, was also in the vicinity conducting practice instrument approaches at CYHZ. The loss of separation occurred when C-GMBL was being vectored for the required 4nm wake turbulence spacing behind PD2283. The turn issued to C-GMBL resulted in a 2.7nm lateral spacing from PD2283 where the minimum required lateral spacing is 3nm.

C-GIZF, a de Havilland DHC-6-300 operated by Air Borealis, was conducting flight 955 from Postville Airport (CCD4), NL to Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL. While C-GIZF was conducting a visual approach to runway 33 at CYYR, a CH-146440 Griffon helicopter, being operated by the Department of National Defense (DND), call sign VIPR40, was lifting off with a slung load from a ramp adjacent to and west of runway 33. VIPR40 was cleared to depart eastbound and did so as C-GIZF was turning final for runway 33. The crew of C-GIZF acquired the Griffon, assessed that their flightpath could potentially lead to a conflict on their approach and elected to conduct a precautionary overshoot. The crew of VIPR40 also altered their heading as a precaution once they acquired C-GIZF visually. C-GIZF safely landed on their second visual approach and VIPR40 continued with their departure.

C-GLVU, a Swoop Inc. B737-8 conducting flight WSW745 from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Las Vegas, NV to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, declared an emergency due to a flight attendant becoming ill. The crew elected to divert to O'Hare International Airport (KORD), Chicago, IL.

C-FZJS, a NovaJet DASSAULT F900, conducting flight NOJ91 from St. John's International Airport, NL (CYYT) to Hector International Airport North Dakota (KFAR) when the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to a low oil pressure warning on the left engine (GARRETT, TFE731-60-1C). The flight crew conducted the low oil emergency check list and shut down the engine. The aircraft diverted to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport, ON (CYYZ) where the aircraft landed without further incident on Runway 05.Maintenance found an oil pressure transducer line cracked, the cracked line was replaced, and the engine was run with no further faults.

C-FYJP, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114, flight ROU1954, departed Runway 24R at Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON and was climbing through 2500 ft ASL when the flight crew received a Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) Traffic Advisory (TA) indicating the presence of another aircraft to the right of their position, with a vertical separation of 300 feet and closing laterally. Simultaneously, N519XR, a LJ60, departed Runway 23 on the KEPTA3 SID; without adhering to the noise abatement procedures and without ATC authorization, N519XR deviated from the SID and initiated a turn towards the parallel departing ROU1954. ATC immediately issued instructions to ROU1954 to level the climb and turn left. ROU1954 complied with the instruction and stopped climb at 2800ft ASL.

C-FIAM, a Call Aircraft S-1B1X, was operating from a farm air strip approximately 15 nm N of Coronation (CYCT), AB. Check out instruction was being provided to a licensed pilot by an instructor. Upon touchdown the aircraft bounced and control was lost. The aircraft was landing west to east and departed the right side of the runway, contacted some trees and then came to rest. The occupants were uninjured and were able to exit the aircraft unassisted. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GFBE, a Parachutisme Adrénaline Inc. Cessna P206 was conducting sky diving operations from the Innisfail (CEM4), AB, aerodrome. Shortly after departure the aircraft engine began to run rough. The pilot switched fuel tanks and the engine (Continental IO-520-A) ran without issue and the pilot continued the climb to 12 500 feet ASL to let the sky divers out. After the first 2 skydivers jumped, the engine failed. The pilot got the remaining skydivers to jump out. The aircraft was set up for best glide and the pilot attempted to restart the engine multiple times without success. Several times during the forced approach the engine restarted on its own, but only for a short time. On short final to Runway 34 the engine started without input from the pilot and again it failed. The engine was secured and the flight path was corrected from the unanticipated engine restart. The pilot then lined up for a farmer's field 1/4 mile south of the runway as there was a risk of not clearing the trees on approach to Runway 34. The aircraft landed in the field. The pilot was not injured nor was the aircraft damaged.Following the flight, the aircraft was towed back to the ramp at CEM4. The maintenance team inspected the aircraft and performed several ground runs without issue.

C-FDJZ, a Jazz Aviation CRJ900, was operating as flight JZA8099 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC to Erik Nielsen International (CYXY) in Whitehorse, YT. While descending through 16 000 feet ASL, on approach to CYXY, the crew received a HYD 1 LO PRESS caution message. The emergency check list in the quick reference handbook (QRH) was carried out and the crew declared a PAN PAN. Some of the flight controls were affected; however, the flight crew did not have any trouble controlling the aircraft. The flight landed safely approximately 5 minutes later.Maintenance replaced the #1 engine driven pump (EDP) and a hydraulic suction line. Leak and function checks were carried out and the aircraft was release back into service.

C-FLJO, an Air Spray (1967) Limited Lockheed 188C (Electra) was conducting fire suppression operations as flight ASB482 approximately 28 nautical miles northwest of Williams Lake Airport (CYWL), BC, with 2 pilots on board. During the return flight to CYWL, to reload fire retardant, the crew observed the No. 2 engine (Allison 501-D13) oil pressure and associated reduction gear oil pressure fluctuate. The No. 2 engine lost all oil quantity and the crew performed a precautionary shutdown. The aircraft diverted to the operator's maintenance facility at Red Deer Regional Airport (CYQF), AB, and landed without incident. Maintenance found that the oil line on the rear turbine bearing carrier was broken due to a vibration. The rear turbine and bearing carrier were replaced.

C-GOJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP MHI RJ Aviation ULC CRJ900 was conducting flight 8840 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), CA.  During climb out in vicinity of Seattle-Tacoma Intl. (KSEA), WA, the flight crew noticed right hand engine oil temperature in amber arc.  Temperature briefly returned to normal during level off but then increased to amber arc and then red arc. The flight crew completed the QRH procedure for a #2 engine shutdown declared a PANPAN and returned to CYVR.  Flight landed in CYVR without further incident and taxied to the gate under own power.

C-GKIV, a Cessna Citation C560 aircraft operated by Keewatin Air LP, was conducting flight KEW502 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON. During the climb through approximately 6000 feet ASL, the crew observed the left engine N1 indication decrease to 0%; however, all other engine parameters remained normal and stable. The crew declared an emergency and the aircraft returned to CYWG where an uneventful landing was conducted.The operator's maintenance inspection revealed that wiring to the left N1 speed sensor was broken at the connector.

C-GUGZ, a privately registered Cessna 172M was in taxiing preparation for a Visual Flight Rules (VFR) flight from London International Airport (CYXU), ON to Burlington Executive Airpark Airport (CZBA), ON with only the pilot onboard. While taxiing with the assistance of Air Traffic Control (ATC) , the pilot became confused, turned the wrong direction and tried to takeoff from taxiway Alpha. ATC informed the pilot of the situation, and the aircraft eventually came to stop on Alpha. ATC suggested the pilot not fly, and requested he return to the parking area. The pilot taxied the aircraft back to Apron 3 where it was observed entering the Apron at high speed and striking C-FOBU, a parked Cirrus SR22T aircraft. C-GUGZ received substantial damages to the wing and C-FOBU received damage to its propeller. There were no injuries.SUMMARY UPDATED 08 JUNE 2023.

C-FRPX, a Fairchild Aircraft SA227-TT operated by Skycare Air Ambulance, was conducting flight PHX518 from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON, to Deer Lake (CYVZ), ON with 4 crew members and 1 passenger on board. Upon arriving at CYVZ, the crew conducted the RNAV approach to Runway 31. At minimums, the crew conducted a missed approach due to low visibility in fog. After the missed approach procedure, the crew decided to conduct a second approach to Runway 31 using a pilot monitored approach (PMA) technique with the First Officer flying and the Captain monitoring. During the second approach, upon selecting the landing gear down when established on the final approach course, the nose gear down and lock indication did not illuminate. The captain cycled the gear twice and achieved a nose gear safe indication after the second cycle. Upon arriving at minimums, the Captain acquired the runway lights and assumed control of the aircraft. The aircraft descended and struck the terrain in the clearway preceding Runway 31. The aircraft’s gear collapsed and the aircraft came to rest on its belly prior to the threshold of Runway 31. The occupants were able to egress through the over-wing exit. The captain sustained minor injuries. There was no fire and the 406-MHz ELT activated. TSB investigators deployed to the site.

C-GFAH, an Airbus A330-300 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC0490 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Montreal - Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. While climbing at approximately 11 000 feet, the cabin Service Director reported a burning electrical smell inside the cabin. The flight crew subsequently declared a Mayday with Air Traffic Control (ATC) and elected to return to CYYZ. Flight AC490 landed on runway 23 where it was met by the Airport Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) vehicles. AC0490 taxied back to the gate under its own power without further incident. The maintenance department conducted the required inspection and identified the In Seat Power Supply (ISPS) located under row 38D emitting an odor as described by the cabin crew. The failure of the unit has been confirmed and it will be sent back to the vendor for further investigation. A service difficulty report has been raised and submitted to Transports Canada.

C-GTYV, a Valley Helicopters Limited Bell 206B (JetRanger) helicopter, was conducting helicopter sling operations 34 nautical miles north-northwest of Pemberton (CYPS), BC, with only the pilot on board. While on approach to the drop zone with a cargo net full of tree seedlings, the pilot depressed the radio call switch on the cyclic to make a radio transmission and inadvertently contacted the belly hook emergency release switch which is also on the cyclic. The external load was released from the belly hook and landed in a forested area. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft or property. The cargo net was recovered.

D-ABTL, a Boeing B747-400 aircraft operated by Deutsche Lufthansa AG, was conducting flight LH492 from Frankfurt Rein-Mein (EDDF), Germany, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC. On final approach for Runway 26R, at approximately 4000 feet above sea level, the engine-indicating and crew-alerting system (EICAS) caution status message ANTISKID appeared. The flight crew requested vectors from air traffic control to complete the required actions. The gear page showed ANTISKID INOP on main landing gear wheels 6 and 8. The flight crew accomplished the ANTISKID checklist and the landing distance was recalculated. The flight crew requested emergency response vehicles to be on standby. On final approach, the alert message ANTISKID disappeared and a normal landing was performed. The emergency response vehicles accompanied the aircraft during the taxi to the ramp.Maintenance found no fault message in the central maintenance computer. A brake system ground test was performed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKQC, a Porter Airlines Inc. de Havilland DHC-8-402, was conducting flight PD2320 from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. While en-route, just after leveling off at altitude, the lead flight attendant in the cabin advised the flight crew that the other flight attendant suddenly became ill. The flight crew declared a medical emergency and requested to return to CYHZ. The flight safely landed at approximately 10:17 ADT and once at the gate, medical personnel attended to the ill flight attendant.

D-AIVB, un Airbus A350-900 exploité par Lufthansa German Airlines sous l'indicatif LH474 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de de Munich, Allemagne (EDDM) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Québec (CYUL). À l'amorce de la descente vers CYUL, l'équipage a noté un message de température élevée du liquide hydraulique du système jaune. Les pompes se sont alors automatiquement éteintes. Une urgence a lors été déclarée et le train a été sorti par gravité. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre et a pu sortir de piste sur son propre pouvoir et procéder à la barrière. Aucun blessé, aucun dommage.

On 15 May 2023, an Excel Flight Training Inc Piper PA-23-250 (registration C-FVIY) was conducting multi-engine flight training under visual flight rules. On board was a flight instructor and a student pilot. Several circuits had been successfully carried out. While conducting a simulated single-engine landing to Runway 24, the flight instructor and student pilot detected an odd vibration from the nosewheel on initial touchdown and attempted to go around. The flight instructor pitched the nose up in an attempt to raise the nose landing gear to assist with acceleration; however, the aircraft settled back on the runway and landed on the aircraft's belly. The aircraft came to a stop approximately halfway down the runway. The flight instructor and student pilot evacuated the aircraft, uninjured. The aircraft's propellers were bent and there was damage to the underside of the aircraft.Post-occurrence inspection and testing found no faults with the landing gear. This, in conjunction with CCTV footage of the final moments suggest that the landing gear (i.e., nosewheel) had not completed its down cycle at the time of initial touchdown.

C-GSKQ, a Convair CV580 aircraft operated by the Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency, was operating a fire suppression flight from Prince Albert/Glass Field (CYPA), SK to a fire in the Buffalo Narrows, SK area. After takeoff from CYPA, the crew noticed that the right propeller (Hamilton Standard 55H60-77) was in a pitch-lock condition. The crew conducted an intentional engine shutdown of the right engine and returned to CYPA for an uneventful single-engine landing. There were no injuries, nor any damage to the aircraft.The operator's maintenance reported that the right propeller controller failed and will be replaced prior to the aircraft returning to service.

On 04 May 2023, a Campbell Helicopters Ltd. Bell 212 helicopter was conducting water bucketing operations in support of forest fire suppression services in the vicinity of Utikuma Lake, Alberta (approximately 160 nautical miles north-northwest of Edmonton, Alberta). Onboard was the pilot. While transiting back to the water source, after the 9th water delivery, the long line and water bucket inadvertently released over a heavily wooded, non-populated area. The aircraft returned to its operating base.Maintenance action: Post-occurrence maintenance determined that an electrical short in the arming switch led to the release of the long line and water bucket. The switch, relay, and cargo hook were replaced.

On 15 May 2023, a Buffalo Airways Limited Lockheed L188C, callsign TKR 416 (registration C-FIJX, serial #2010), departed Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), Northwest Territories enroute to Hay River/Merlyn Carter Airport (CYHY), Northwest Territories to position the aircraft for the upcoming fire-fighting season. Onboard were 2 flight crew. Shortly after departure, at approximately 1150 Mountain Daylight Time, the flight crew of TKR416 observed a #1 Engine Prop Overspeed indication. The crew shut down engine #1 (Allision D501-D13) as a precaution, in accordance with standard operating procedures, and returned to CYZF. No assistance was required. At 1155, the aircraft touched down on Runway 34 at CYZF. During the landing, one of the tires on the left main landing gear blew. The flight crew shut down the aircraft on Taxiway Bravo and it was towed back to the apron. Post-occurrence maintenance: Some troubleshooting was completed and after changing the prop governor, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJXW, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300, was operating as flight ACA318 from Calgary International Airport, Alberta (CYYC) to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport, Quebec (CYUL). On board were 10 crew members and 122 passengers. At approximately 0638 Mountain Daylight Time, the #1 engine (Pratt & Whitney PW1524G-3) lost oil pressure. The flight crew of ACA318 carried out the checklist procedure, shutdown the engine and declared a PAN PAN emergency. The flight crew then returned to CYYC. The aircraft landed safely at 0725 on Runway 35R and was met by airport rescue and firefighting (ARFF) personnel. The aircraft then taxied to the gate. There were no injuries.Maintenance action:The #1 engine oil filter was removed. Small metal chips were found on the filter and coverplate. The particles were removed and sent for analysis. The filter was replaced, and power assurance test carried out with no faults found.

C-GPDB, a Sunwest Aviation Ltd. was conducting flight CNK678 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Seattle/Boeing Field/King County Intl. (KBFI), WA.  During approach under ATC vectors at 6000 feet, flight crew received a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory).  Flight crew followed the RA and advised ATC.  Flight landed without further incident.

On 10 May 2023, the Westjet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-400 (registration C-GENM, serial number 4456) began it's takeoff roll for a passenger flight from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), Alberta to Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), Alberta. Onboard were 4 crew members and 66 passengers. During the takeoff roll on Runway 02, at approximately 110 knots, the fuselage doors warning light illuminated. The crew rejected the takeoff and declared a MAYDAY in accordance with company standard operating procedures. The MAYDAY was subsequently cancelled after the fault was identified. The flight crew taxied the aircraft off the runway and returned to the gate for maintenance. Maintenance action: The aft baggage door handle was found incorrectly stowed. An operational check of the handle was carried out with no faults found. The aircraft brakes were also inspected and no faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBHJ, a Helijet International Incorporated Sikorsky Aircraft Corporation S76C helicopter, was conducting flight JBA717 from Vancouver Harbour (CBC7), BC, to Victoria Harbour, Camel Point (CBF7), BC, with 2 crew and 12 passengers on board. During cruise, while at 70% torque, minor torque oscillations were observed (Turbomeca Arriel 2S2) and a slight yawing was experienced. The flight crew reduced the torque to 60% to avoid the suspected problem torque range. To troubleshoot the issue, when the torque was increased to 65%, the main rotor speed dropped momentarily, yaw was experienced, the (one engine inoperative) light armed and the torque indications were showed a 15% difference between the two engines. There were no digital engine control unit faults. The flight crew decreased the torque to 50%, diverted to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, and declared a PAN PAN. The flight crew conducted an uneventful run-on landing on Runway 08R.Maintenance removed the unserviceable collective position transducer (CPT) (P/N 760900-01884-102 S/N 0409) and installed serviceable CPT (P/N 760900-01884-102 S/N 0168). The aircraft was returned to service.  Service Difficulty Report 20230504003 (previously submitted to Transport Canada on 04 May 2023) was updated to include this occurrence.See occurrences A23P0038 and A23P0048 in relation to similar events.

On 13 May 2023, a Conair Group Inc De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400AT air tanker (registration C-FFQG), operating as FGD542, departed the Grande Prairie Airport (CYQU), Alberta to conduct aerial firefighting operations in the local area; on board were 2 crew members. At approximately 1445 mountain daylight time (MDT), while preparing to drop water on a fire, the crew noticed that the #2 hydraulic quantity was below normal and just above the minimum for dispatch. A few minutes later, the quantity reduced below the minimum. The crew jettisoned the retardant load in the fire area and returned to CYQU. During the transit to CYQU, the crew lowered the landing gear and completed the appropriate emergency checklist procedure. As the crew completed the checklist, the associated #2 hydraulic CAUTION and ADVISORY lights illuminated. Upon initial contact with the CYQU flight service station specialist, the crew declared a "PAN PAN" emergency. The aircraft landed at 1453 MDT on Runway 30 without further incident and then towed off the runway.Maintenance actions: Maintenance personnel found a leaking hydraulic line connected to the right hand main gear "up" actuator. The line was replaced and the fluid level replenished. Additional checks were completed with no faults found and the aircraft was returned to service.
