C-IKQK, a privately registered basic ultralight North Wing Sport X2 aircraft, was conducting high-speed taxiing on the runway at 100 Mile House Airport (CAV3), BC, with 1 pilot on board. During a high speed taxi on Runway 08, the aircraft became airborne. The aircraft yawed left, lost control and collided with a tree, and then impacted the terrain. The pilot sustained serious injuries and the aircraft was substantially damaged.

In the days leading up to the day of the occurrence, the pilot of C-FKMX, an Aerospatiale AS350B3 had been conducting long line forest fire fighting operations in support of Wildfire 017 located approximately 6 nm NW of Valleyview, Alberta (CEL5) in co-ordination with C-FCCK, a Bell Helicopters model 412 operated by Summit Helicopters Ltd. On the day of the occurrence, at approximately 1234 MDT, C-FKMX had been dispatched to conduct long line bucketing operations in continued support of Wildfire 017 on the east side of Sturgeon Lake, Alberta (Sandy Bay). C-FCCK, had also been dispatched to conduct bucketing operations in support of Wildfire 017 approximately 3.5 nm SE of C-FKMX's location. In addition, C-FALI, a Bell Helicopters model 212 operated by Alpine Helicopters, was called in to assist C-FCCK in working the eastern flank of the fire line.After approximately 8-9 buckets drops in the Sandy Bay area, C-FKMX was repurposed to join C-FCCK, and C-FALI in firefighting operations on the eastern edge of the fire. Enroute to the new location, C-FKMX refilled the bucket and proceeded southeast to engage in operations. As C-FKMX approached the new area of operations; the flight crew of the three helicopters engaged in firefighting operations were all communicating on the same frequency. As C-FKMX approached the drop area from the northwest, visual contact was made with C-FALI, while communicating on the radio and broadcasting current position and intentions and trying to visually acquire the location of C-FCCK. C-FCCK responded to the radio call, but portions of the radio calls between the two pilots were not clearly understood. The pilot of C-FKMX believed that C-FCCK was clear of the immediate area, and the pilot of C-FCCK was not aware that C-FKMX was immediately joining the firefighting efforts at their location. The pilots of both C-FKMX and C-FCCK both unknowingly observed the same hotspot in the area and had elected to drop their water on it at almost the same time. Due to the pilots' seating position in each helicopter (right seat in C-FKMX, and left seat in C-FCCK) and the relative relationship of the two helicopters to each other in flight, the pilots of both helicopters did not visually acquire the other. In the process of lining up to deploy the water on the location, C-FCCK which was slightly below C-FKMX, made contact with, and severed the long line of C-FKMX approximately 28 feet below the helicopter's fuselage. The majority of the longline and bucket assembly impacted terrain in a non-populated area and both helicopters continued to fly.Departing the immediate area, the pilot of C-FKMX initiated a crab to keep the remaining portion of the severed long line from entangling the tail rotor and found a clearing to land in to complete a preliminary inspection of the helicopter. No damage was found, and the remaining portion of the long line was removed and placed in the cabin. C-FKMX repositioned to CEL5 to refuel and then return to the Valleyview firebase.The pilot of C-FCCK was unaware that his main rotor system had severed the longline of C-FKMX believing that C-FKMX had severed its own longline. C-FCCK continued to work the fire until notified by Alberta Forestry that the helicopter had been involved in an occurrence, at which time the helicopter returned to the Valleyview firebase for an inspection by company maintenance. No damage was found, and the helicopter was returned to service.A subsequent investigation by Alberta Forestry resulted in an amendment to the circuit joining procedures for aircraft joining a previously established firefighting circuit, and clarification of procedures for aircraft moving work areas.

C-FTXK, un Canadair CL-215 exploité par le Service Aérien Gouvernemental du Québec, avec à son bord 2 membres d'équipage de conduite effectuait un vol de combat de feu de forêt selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à destination de Roberval, QC (CYRJ). Lors du deuxième largage sur un feu situé sous une ligne de transport d'électricité à haute tension d'Hydro-Québec près du mont Wright, l'appareil a subit une perte d'altitude et les portes de largage ouvertes ont touché au câble supérieur de la ligne. L'appareil a dérouté vers l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Int, QC (CYQB) où il a atterri sans encombre. Des marques de contact ont été observées par le personnel de maintenance. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé.

C-GDTL, un Pilatus PC12/47 exploité par Panorama Fixed Wings Ltd. sous l'indicatif PNO782, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport d’Inukjuak (CYPH), QC à destination de l’aéroport de Mont-Joli (CYYY), QC. 30 minutes après le décollage, l'équipage a eu un voyant d'avertissement sur le système hydraulique. L'appareil est alors dérouté vers La Grande Rivière (CYGL), QC pour étudier le problème. Une urgence a été déclarée de façon préventive étant donné que la procédure pour le système hydraulique comporte une étape pour tirer les disjoncteurs de la pompe. L'urgence a été annulée lorsque le train a été complètement sorti. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre, pas de blessé. Le personnel de maintenance a trouvé un fil endommagé sur l'indicateur de pression du système.

On 12 May 2023, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 (registration C-FSOC) was operating as ACA702 on a flight from Toronto Lester B Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, towards Laguardia Airport (KLGA), NY. Shortly after departure, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency due to vibrations in the aircraft. The flight crew elected to return to CYYZ and landed safely on Runway 33R without further incident.

C-FCNW, a Westjet Airlines Ltd. was conducting flight WS1565 from San Diego Intl. (KSAN), CA to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB.  During cruise in vicinity of Los Angeles Intl. (KLAX), CA, a cabin crew became incapacitated.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FGZT, a Top Aces Inc. McDonnell Douglas A-4N was conducting local flight from Cuxhaven/ Nordholz-Spieka (ETMN), Germany.  Approximately 10 minutes after takeoff passing 20000 feet, flight crew noticed unexpected loss of cockpit pressurization.  Flight crew declared an emergency, advised ATC and descended below 10000 feet.  Fuel was burned under ATC control and flight landed without further incident.

C-FJQZ, a Mitsubishi Heavy Industries RJ Aviation ULC CRJ-900 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8193 from Regina International (CYQR), SK, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 4 crew members and 42 passengers. During descent, the captain felt unwell and the first officer assumed the flying duties.  The captain remained responsive and his health had improved upon landing. Emergency medical services met the aircraft on arrival and the captain was brought to the hospital as a precaution. The flight crew did not declare an emergency with air traffic control.

C-FPWE, an Air Canada Airbus A320 was conducting flight ACA297 from Winnipeg (CYWG), MB, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC. C-FFXD, a Morningstar Air Express Cessna 208B (Grand Caravan) aircraft was conducting flight MAL8073 from Victoria International (CYYJ), BC, to CYVR. ACA297 was on intermediate final for runway 26R. The controller instructed ACA297 to descend to 3000 feet above sea level (ASL) and cleared for the instrument landing system approach to Runway 26R. MAL8073 was at 3000 feet ASL and flying on a heading of 360 degrees anticipating a visual approach to Runway 26L. As MAL8073 neared the extended centreline for Runway 26L, they advised the air traffic controller that they no longer had the airport in sight and the controller instructed them to turn left to a heading of 260 degrees. The instruction was acknowledged by the crew who was undergoing line indoctrination. Approximately 45 seconds later, MAL8073 again stated that there was cloud between them and the airport. The controller reiterated the left turn instruction and MAL8073 began the turn. The crew of MAL8073 was unsure as to which aircraft the initial left turn instruction was directed and had the ACA297 aircraft is sight throughout the maneuvering. The controller advised ACA297 that their approach clearance was cancelled and instructed them to turn right to 050 degrees. ACA297 was cleared to 5,000 feet and later cleared to continue the right-hand turn to rejoin the final approach course for Runway 26R. Lateral separation was reduced to 2.0 nautical miles (NM) horizontally and 0 feet vertically where 3.0 NM horizontally or 1000 feet vertically was required.

C-FNTA, a Northern Thunderbird Air Incorporated Beech B300 (King Air 350), was operating as flight NTA201 on an air ambulance flight from Prince George (CYXS), BC, to Bella Bella - Campbell Island (CBBC), BC, with 2 passengers and 2 flight crew on board. During cruise at flight level 210, the red landing gear handle light illuminated and flashed on and off intermittently. After consulting the applicable checklists and discussing the issue, the flight crew decided to return to CYXS. The flight crew declared an emergency and aircraft rescue and firefighting crews were put on standby. The gear was extended on final for runway 15 with a green gear down and locked indication. The crew performed a normal landing without incident.Maintenance cycled the landing gear and adjusted the gear-up microswitches. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FDOD, a Bell Helicopter 412 operated by Wisk-Air Limited, was conducting an external load flight from a powerline structure located 17 nm northeast of Dear Lake (CYVZ), ON, to Knox Camp, ON, located 22 nm southeast of CYVZ. While on short final at approximately 200 feet AGL, as the pilot was transitioning his head to the bubble window to finish the approach and set the load down, the pilot felt 2 hard jerks from the longline and heard the low rotor horn. The pilot observed that the N1 on the number 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6T-3B) was at 75%. The pilot attempted to add throttle to the number 1 engine but was unable to do so. The pilot continued the approach with some slight forward momentum with partial power on the number 1 engine and full power on the number 2 engine. Once the load was on the ground, the pilot jettisoned the longline from the helicopter belly hook at approximately 30 feet AGL. The helicopter then landed safely at the helipad. There were no injuries.The operator's observations indicated signs that the rigging of the external load, consisting of a swamp mat, likely slipped while C-FDOD was on final. The belly paneling of the helicopter was observed to be wrinkled and impinging on the #1 throttle push tube. The helicopter has been removed from service pending repairs.

C-FJYW, an ATR 42-300 operated by Calm Air, was conducting flight MO214 from Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU to Arviat (CYEK), NU with 3 crew members and 21 passengers on board. During the landing roll at CYEK, the aircraft's right landing gear struck a dog that ran onto the runway. The aircraft continued the landing roll and taxi to the apron without any other issues.A post-flight inspection was conducted and some damage was identified on the right landing gear and some associated components. After consulting the manufacturer, the operator replaced the damaged right landing gear and affected components to allow further inspection and evaluation of the damage. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSDA, a Rockwell International Commander 690B operated by Mag Aerospace Canada Corp, was conducting a training flight at the Dryden Regional airport (CYHD), ON, with 2 pilots on board. When selecting gear down while conducting an approach to Runway 12, only 2 green gear down and locked lights illuminated. A go-around was conducted and the crew consulted the QRH. The gear was cycled and a failed bulb was suspected for the right main landing gear indication. Emergency services were requested as a precaution and the aircraft subsequently landed at CYHD without incident.The operator's maintenance replaced the gear bulb.

C-GIGK, a de Havilland DHC-6 aircraft operated by Transwest Air Ltd. (dba Rise Air), was conducting a flight from Seabee Mine (CCB2), SK, to La Ronge/Barber Field airport (CYVC), SK. While established enroute, the crew noticed a marginally low oil pressure and elevated oil temperature of the right engine (#2). They performed a precautionary engine shutdown in accordance with company standard operating procedures. An emergency was declared and they continued to their destination where the aircraft landed uneventfully.Post occurrence, the operator's maintenance identified that there was a wiring fault in the oil temperature indicating system. The oil pressure 'marginally low' was within manufacturers specifications.

C-GPAO, a De Havilland DHC8-402 operated by PAL Airlines Ltd as PVL 412 was conducting a flight from Goose Bay International Airport (CYYR), NL to Voisey’s Bay Airport (CVB2), NL with 4 crew members and 60 passengers on board. During the take-off phase, just at rotation, the crew reported a vibration. Shortly after the take-off, the flight attendant called the crew and advised that a passenger observed the inside left (No.2) main tire failed at take-off. A crew member left the cockpit and inspected and confirmed the blown tire. The crew advised ATC of the situation, declared an emergency and requested to return into CYYR. After reviewing the QRH, they entered a hold to burn fuel until they were at their landing weight. Upon landing the crew observed a vibration and used braking and reverse to slow. The vibration stopped and the crew taxied to the ramp without further incident.

C-FCJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP, Bombardier CL-600-2D24, Canadair Regional Jet CRJ-900, (flight 752), was enroute from John Glenn Columbus International Airport (KCMH), Columbus, OH to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Toronto, ON. Approximately 30 minutes back from CYYZ, the flight crew reported a right-hand Full Authority Digital Engine Control (FADEC) caution message to maintenance. The crew declared a PAN PAN emergency as a precaution and landed in CYYZ without further issue.

C-GLDE, an ATR 42-320 operated by Transwest Air (dba Rise Air), was conducting a flight from Cigar Lake (CJW7), SK, to La Ronge/Barber Field (CYVC), SK, with 3 crew members and 41 passengers onboard. At the top of descent, the Blue Hydraulic System low level alert annunciated. The crew completed the associated QRH items and declared a PAN PAN with ATC. The aircraft subsequently landed safely at CYVC. There was no damage to the aircraft and no injuries.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and identified a hydraulic leak at at fitting near the hydraulic pump. Repairs were made and the aircraft was returned to service.

On 04 May 2023, a privately owned De Havilland DHC MK 1, (registration C-GBUL) was given a taxi instruction to taxi along Taxiway F and hold short of Runway 04. The air traffic controller did not hear a readback and asked C-GBUL twice to confirm the hold short instruction. In the meantime, a Sault College, Zlin Z242L, (registration C-FHTU) was number 1 on final approach for landing on Runway 04. With still no response from C-GBUL and unsure of the status of the communication with the aircraft on the ground, the controller changed the plan to give C-GBUL the priority in crossing Runway 04. A pull up and go around instruction was intended to be given to C-FHTU but was issued to another Sault College aircraft (registration C-FVWT) by mistake. C-FHTU landed without a landing clearance on the threshold of Runway 04 with C-GBUL still crossing Runway 04 at Taxiway F. The distance from the threshold to the taxiway is approximately 3300 feet. NAV CANADA has initiated an internal investigation and classified the occurrence as an ATS-Operating Irregularity. NAV CANADA Tower and Ground controller services were combined and services were being provided to several aircraft. Based on preliminary data, NAV CANADA's initial assessment is that this occurrence could be classified as an ICAO Runway Incursion Category C Severity - An incident characterized by ample time and/or distance to avoid a collision.

C-GCEV, a Viking Air Ltd. DHC-7, operated by Air Tindi Ltd., was conducting flight TIN801 from Yellowknife NT, (CYZF) to the Colomac Mine airstrip, NT with 3 crew members and 4 passengers on board. During the decent into the Colomac Mine strip, the flight crew noticed low oil pressure in the #4 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-50). The flight crew ran the appropriate checklist and performed a precautionary shutdown of the #4 engine. The decision was made to return to CYZF, a PAN PAN call was made with air traffic services, and an uneventful 3 engine approach and landing was completed.Company maintenance is investigating the cause of the low engine oil pressure indication.

C-GJBV, un Beechcraft King Air 100 exploité par Skyjet Aviation M.G., sous l’indicatif LSJ512, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) à destination de Port-Meunier, QC (CYPN). Après le décollage, l’équipage a sélectionné le levier de commande du train d’atterrissage en position de rétraction et a observé que l’indication de train en transit est restée allumée. À 1000 pieds au-dessus du sol, la procédure du manuel de référence rapide et la liste de vérification d’urgence ont été complétées par l’équipage sans succès. Une urgence a été déclarée et une approche basse a été effectuée devant la tour de contrôle à CYZV ce qui a permis au contrôleur aérien de confirmer que le train d’atterrissage était à moitié sorti. L’équipage a décidé de modifier la route de vol pour atterrir à l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Une fois à CYQB, l’aéronef a effectué un circuit d’attente pour brûler du carburant tel qu’indiqué dans la procédure d’urgence. L’équipage a ensuite procédé à la sortie manuelle du train d’atterrissage qui a été satisfaisante. En approche finale, les moteurs ont été fermés par mesure de précaution et l’aéronef a atterri sans encombre. Les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d’aéronefs (SLIA) l’ont inspecté une fois à l’arrêt et il a pu être remorqué par la suite jusqu’au hangar de la compagnie. Il n’y a eu aucun dommage ou blessé. L’inspection visuelle a permis de déterminer qu’un pneu à plat était resté coincé dans la porte au moment où le train se rétractait.

C-FHCW, un Learjet 45 exploité par Les Investissements Nolinor Inc. sous l’indicatif NRL431, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). L’équipage a reçu un message d’alerte d’équipage (CAS message) LR EMER PRESS ON suivi du message CAB DUCT OVHT alors que l’aéronef était à une altitude d’environ 19 000 pieds et en montée. L’équipage a contacté l’unité de contrôle de la circulation aérienne (ATC) afin de demander l’autorisation d’arrêter la montée. La demande a été refusée. L’équipage a procédé à une mise en palier à 20 000 pieds et a déclaré une urgence à l’ATC tout en expliquant au contrôleur aérien la situation. La liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été effectuée et les messages d’alerte se sont éteints. L’ATC a été avisé que la situation d’urgence était résolue et a autorisé l’équipage à reprendre la montée vers le niveau de vol FL280. L’aéronef a poursuivi sa route jusqu’à destination sans encombre.

C-FFNF, un Boeing 737-406 exploité par Canadian North Limited, sous l’indicatif AKT163, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Kuujjuaq QC (CYVP) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Peu de temps après avoir atteint l’altitude de croisière, le moteur #2 s’est éteint. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) à l’unité de contrôle de la circulation aérienne. L’aéronef a fait demi-tour et s’est posé à CYVP sans encombre. L’équipe de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) a été déployée et a inspecté visuellement l’aéronef. Suite à l’inspection visuelle, l’aéronef a circulé jusqu’à l’aire de stationnement.

C-FNTA, a Northern Thunderbird Air Inc Beech King Air 350, was operating as NTA201 on a MEDEVAC return flight from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Prince George (CYXS), BC. During landing gear retraction on take-off from CYEG, the flight crew observed a "Hyd Fluid Low" annunciation with the landing gear handle light on. There was an immediate drop in hydraulic pressure. The flight crew requested a level off with a high probability of a return to CYEG. After briefing the paramedics, the manual gear extension system was used to pump the landing gear down to a "down and locked" position with a "3 green" indication.  The flight crew did not declare an emergency but did request emergency vehicles to standby as a precaution. A safe landing was carried out and the aircraft taxied into the hangar.Maintenance Update: On inspection it was discovered that the left-hand main landing gear actuator had cracked and failed resulting in an immediate loss of hydraulic pressure. The left-hand main landing gear actuator was replaced, and all hydraulic lines were inspected and found "satisfactory". The right-hand main landing gear actuator was found "not satisfactory", so a ferry permit was obtained to allow C-FNTA to fly from CYEG to CYXS with the landing gear in the down position. Further inspection and maintenance will take place in CYXS.

C-GJTX, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was conducting flight ROU1840 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Bridgetown/Grantley Adams Intl. (TBPB), Barbados.  During initial climb through FL240, flight crew noticed a possible crack/delamination on the first officer flight deck window.  Flight crew stopped the climb at FL270, declared a PANPAN and diverted back to CYYZ where an overweight landing was completed without further incident.

C-FLUJ, a Flair Airlines Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight FLE1601 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During initial climb (AGERS1 departure runway 10R) climbing through 4200 feet, Flight crew received a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory).  Flight crew followed RA and advised ATC which were unaware of traffic in the area.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GUXR, a Mustang Helicopters Incorporated Airbus Helicopters AS350 B3 (AStar) was conducting maintenance ground runs at Smithers Airport (CYYD), BC with a pilot on board.  While at flight idle, the helicopter began an uncommanded yaw and rotated approximately 540 degrees striking 2 maintenance staff who were on the ground beside the helicopter when it began rotating. The pilot was able to cut the fuel to shut down the engine. The helicopter remained upright. One of the maintenance workers was fatally injured, the other received serious injuries and was air lifted to a hospital for treatment.

C-FZTA, an Airbus Helicopter AS350B2 operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd., was conducting a flight from the community of St. Theresa Point, MB to the St. Theresa Point airport (CYST), MB. During the final approach, the pilot elected to land at a different location than originally planned due to limited parking on the apron. While on short final, the aircraft's tail rotor struck a runway sign and became severely unbalanced. The pilot immediately reduced collective and landed the aircraft. Upon inspection, the tail rotor was significantly damaged, and the fuselage was also damaged due to a departed tail rotor tip. The pilot was the only occupant and was not injured. There was no fuel spill or fire.

C-GAOC, un Beechcraft 35-C33 (Debonair) en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à destination de Port Meunier, QC (CYPN) avec un pilote à bord. Lorsque l’aéronef était en vent arrière gauche de la piste 29, le moteur (Teledyne Continental IO 470-N) s’est arrêté. Le pilote a manœuvré pour un atterrissage sur la piste 11, toutefois l’aéronef a percuté le sol à environ 200 pieds avant la piste. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé, toutefois l’aéronef a subi des dommages importants.

C-FAVX, a Range Helicopters Inc. Airbus Helicopters AS350-B2, was returning to the Edson airport (CYET), AB, from a staging area supporting firefighting operations to the east of Edson, AB. On approach to CYET the pilot elected to expedite his arrival routing due to incoming fixed wing air traffic. On the final approach to landing, the helicopter entered a descent that resulted in a hard landing and roll-over. The pilot survived with minor injuries; the helicopter was substantially damaged. Post impact, the engine continued to run and was subsequently shut down. The ELT activated; there was no post-impact fire.

C-GASE, an AirSprint Inc. Embraer 545 was conducting flight ASP846 from Portland Intl. (KPDX), OR to Seattle/Boeing Field/King County Intl. (KBFI), WA.  During approach being vectored for ILS 14R at 2000 feet, Flight crew received a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory).  Flight crew followed the RA, advised ATC and landed without further incident.

C-GQLL, a Bell 205A-1 helicopter operated by Helicopter Transport Services Inc., was operating on a VFR flight from La Ronge (CYVC) SK to Buffalo Narrows, (CYVT) SK. While enroute approximately 20 nautical miles southeast of CYVT, the aircraft experienced a hydraulic failure of the number one hydraulic system. An emergency was declared, and the flight continued to CYVT and landed uneventfully.An post-occurrence inspection by the operator revealed that the number one hydraulic system was out of fluid.

C-GSWQ, a Learjet 45 operated by Sunwest Aviation, was conducting MEDEVAC flight CNK657-M from Edmonton Intl. Airport (CYEG), AB to Winnipeg James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB with 2 flight crew and 5 passengers on board. Approximately 10 minutes after departure, while climbing to cruise altitude, (approximately 35 nm east of CYEG climbing through 22 000 feet ASL), the flight crew observed the interstage turbine temperature (ITT) on the left engine increasing above the redline limit. The throttles were reduced with a corresponding decrease in ITT indication. The flight crew then advanced the throttles and the ITT on the left engine exceeded the redline limit again. The flight crew elected to shut down the left engine (Garrett TFE731-20R), contacted ATC, declared a PAN PAN and requested a return to CYEG. An uneventful landing was performed approximately 30 minutes after departure. Initial investigation by company maintenance determined the likely source of the high ITT indication to be a fault with the ITT indication system.

C-GZCF, a Lockheed L-188C Electra, operated by Air Spray 1967 Ltd. was conducting forest fire fighting operations from the Fort McMurray, AB airport (CYMM). Shortly after departure, the flight crew received a #2 engine fire indication. The flight crew ran the appropriate check list, and shut down the #2 engine (Allison 501-D13). A PAN PAN was declared with ATC, and the aircraft returned to CYMM for an uneventful landing with aircraft rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) on standby.Subsequent investigation by maintenance determined that the #2 engine fire indication was a fault with the fire indication system, and not an actual engine fire. Repairs to the fire indication system were completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFHB a Geodesy Group Inc. Piper PA-31 had departed the Edson (CYET), AB airport on a photo survey. Approximately 3 hours into the flight the pilot initiated a change in fuel tank selection to the starboard inboard tank. Power was lost on the starboard engine (Avco Lycoming TIO-540-J2BD). A review of the fuel gauge showed 3/4 tank available, and the fuel pressure was not interrupted. Multiple attempts were made to restart the engine but to no avail. The engine was secured, propeller feathered, and ATC was informed of the need to return to CYET. A successful landing at CYET was carried out. Maintenance update: After landing the engine was inspected with no evident damage. The engine started as normal. Maintenance was consulted and testing could not replicate the problem. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBHY, un Airbus A319-144 exploité par Air Canada Rouge sous l'indicatif ROU1962, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec à son bord 5 membres d'équipage et 99 passagers. À environ 14 NM au nord-est de CYQB, à une altitude de 4500 pieds ASL sur l'approche pour la piste 24,   celui-ci a rencontré de la turbulence sévère qui a causé un mouvement de piqué inopiné. L'équipage a initié une remontée et demandé à être réacheminé à CYUL où l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GIDY, a privately registered Cessna 182P, was conducting a visual flight rules sightseeing flight from, returning to, Langley (CYNJ), BC, with the pilot and one passenger on board. When the aircraft returned to CYNJ, a straight in approach to Runway 25 was conducted. The aircraft was observed to be low on the approach. The aircraft struck a vehicle on the public road approximately 450 feet east of the runway’s displaced threshold. It then impacted the airport perimeter fence approximately 60 feet west of the initial impact and slid a further 30 feet, before it came to rest against a berm.  A post-impact fire started shortly after. The passenger and pilot were extracted from the aircraft with the assistance of bystanders. The driver of the impacted vehicle was transferred to hospital via ground ambulance with minor injuries. The pilot sustained serious injuries and the passenger sustained minor injuries; both were airlifted to hospital. Firefighters extinguished the aircraft fire and the associated grass fire; the aircraft was destroyed.

C-GBHJ, a Helijet International Incorporated Sikorsky Aircraft Corporation S76C helicopter was conducting flight JBA700 from Victoria Harbour, Camel Point (CBF7), BC, to Vancouver Harbour (CBC7), BC, with 2 crew and 11 passengers on board. During the initial climb out of CBF7, the torque settings on the No.1 engine (Turbomeca Arriel 2S2) intermittently varied by 10 percent with the collective set to approximately the 70 percent torque range. This was accompanied by uncommanded, intermittent aircraft yaw. The crew reduced the collective to the 60 percent torque range and the engines stabilized and synchronized. The crew communicated with company maintenance and decided to divert to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC. They declared a PAN PAN urgency to receive priority sequencing for Runway 26L but opted to land on Helipad C with a run-on into Taxiway F which was conducted uneventfully. Sikorsky issued Safety Advisory SSA-S76-23-0001 on 29 April 2023 and Alert Service Bulletin ASB 76-73-12 on 30 April 2023 addressing an issue with a Collective Position Transducer (CPT) which may cause torque fluctuations, and yaw kick. Helijet is awaiting parts and will replace the CPT as per the bulletin.See occurrences A23P0045 and A23P0048 in relation to similar events.

C-GBHR, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was conducting flight ROU1996 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL. During the final approach phase of flight to KFLL RWY 28L, in the vicinity of YOBUS the crew received momentary TCAS RA: DESCEND. Before the flight crew had time to react, the TCAS RA was resolved. The intruder aircraft were reported to have been a formation of F-18s related to the Blue Angels US Navy Flight Demonstration Squadron which had departed KFLL RWY 28R and immediately reversed course toward the approach path of ROU1996. The ATC was advised and the approach was continued. The flight was subsequently completed without further incident.

C-GJXE, an Air Canada A220-300 was conducting flight AC914 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON, to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL. In descent, the flight crew received a TCAS RA. The RA was followed, and the flight continued to land without further incident.

The Sunwing Airlines Boeing 737-800 (SWG 684, C-GFEH) was pushed back from Gate 527 at Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, shortly afterwards, the aircraft developed a technical issue and taxied back to the gate. During the return it appeared the wingtip made contact with a company aircraft parked adjacent to it. An SMS investigation by Sunwing determined that the marshaller directed the aircraft on to the wrong lead-in line. A post inspection determined there was no damage to either aircraft.

C-FIVQ, un Boeing 777-300ER  exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA854, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) à destination de l'aéroport de Londre/Heathrow (EGLL) avec à son bord 12 membres d'équipage et 399 passagers. Alors que l'aéronef se trouvait en vol de croisière à environ 55 milles nautiques au sud-est de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB), l'équipage a déclaré une urgence (Pan Pan) dû à la présence de feu et de fumée dans la cuisine de bord arrière. Le personnel de bord a réussi à éteindre les flammes en vol et l'équipage a demandé un déroutement vers l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre vers 0207Z. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-FFBC a Flair Airlines Inc. Boeing 737 MAX 8 was operating as FLE503 on a flight from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Abbottsford (CYXX), BC. During departure from CYYC, FLE503 experienced multiple bird strikes. After consultation with company operations and company maintenance the decision was made to return to CYYC. An emergency was declared and ARFF was requested. The aircraft landed safely and taxied back to the gate. Maintenance update: Multiple impact points were found on the nose of the aircraft with the largest being directly above the first officer's wind screen. The company is working with Boeing on a repair scheme including NDT of internal structures and possibly re-skinning the upper cockpit area. The aircraft is currently out of service and work is ongoing.

C-GWEQ, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 operated by WestJet Encore Ltd., was operating flight WEW3204 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB, to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON, with 4 crew members and 75 passengers on board. On arrival into CYQT, the crew attempted 2 approaches but were unable to land due to high winds and turbulence. After the second landing attempt, the flight returned to CYWG. While enroute to CYWG, the flight crew slowed the aircraft to long-range cruise power settings. At that power setting, the FMS indicated that the aircraft would land in CYWG with a fuel amount above the minimum reserve fuel of 1435 pounds. Midway through the return flight to CYWG, the crew received a revised flight plan from the operator's dispatch indicating an increase of the minimum reserve fuel to 1535 pounds. The crew requested ATC for a landing on Runway 31, instead of the active Runway 36, as it was closer. While on approach for Runway 31, the fuel level of the aircraft dropped below the revised minimum reserve fuel, and the flight crew declared an emergency. The aircraft landed Runway 31 uneventfully and ARFF followed the aircraft as it taxied normally to the gate. The fuel upon touchdown was 1460 pounds.

C-FJZS, a Boeing 777-333ER operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC311 from Montreal/Trudeau Intl. Airport (CYUL), QC, to Vancouver Intl. Airport (CYVR), BC with 14 crew and 440 passengers on board. During cruise at FL340, a passenger indicated that they could see something glowing on the wing surface. The First Officer observed what appeared to be a scorch mark accompanied by what appeared to be static discharge. The flight crew declared PAN PAN and requested a diversion to Toronto/Pearson Intl. Airport (CYYZ), ON, where they landed and were inspected by ARFF before taxiing to their gate. Maintenance inspection revealed that there were two locations on the wing where a rubberized sealant material from a seam in the wing panels had become loose and was pulled into the airstream, as well as two broken bonding straps in the same area, which allowed a static charge to build up. The sealant and bonding straps were replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FKWE, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 operated by Westjet Encore Ltd., was boarding passengers at Ottawa/Macdonald Cartier Intl. Airport (CYOW), ON, for flight WEN3469 to Toronto/Pearson Intl. Airport (CYYZ), ON. There were 4 crew members and 74 passengers on board. During the boarding process, a crew member observed smoke coming from the APU, and a rapid deplanement was initiated and completed without injury. The flight was canceled as a result. Following maintenance inspection, a DC contactor on the APU starter/generator was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service with the APU placarded as out of service per the MEL.

C-GTSZ, an Air Transat Airbus A330-200 was conducting flight TSC939 from Cancun Intl. (MMUN), Mexico to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC.  During flight preparation on the ground in MMUN, a cabin crew member became incapacitated.  Emergency positions where reassigned respecting minimum crew complement, and flight proceeded to destination without further incident.

C-GBHY an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was conducting flight ROU1799 from Cancun Intl. (MMUN), Mexico to Quebec/Jean Lesage Intl. (CYQB), QC.  During cruise at FL350 approximately 26 NM south of Savannah/Hilton Head Intl. (KSAV), GA, flight suffered a sudden onset of unexpected severe turbulence (600 feet loss, airspeed fluctuation 30 KIAS and VMO exceedance 10-15 Kts).  Seat belt sign was on due to previous convective activity and continuous light turbulence. ATC was advised, flight returned to FL350, and flight continued to destination without further incident.  There was no damage to the aircraft and no injuries to crews or passengers.

N14107, a Boeing 757-200 operated by United Airlines Inc., was conducting flight UAL311 from Boston/Logan Intl. Airport (KBOS) MA, USA, to Los Angeles Intl. Airport (KLAX) CA, USA. During cruise at FL280 in the vicinity of London Intl. Airport (CYXU), ON, the flight crew encountered an issue with the RH engine which required them to shut down the engine. The crew declared MAYDAY with Toronto Centre and requested a diversion to Cleveland/Hopkins Intl. Airport (KCLE) OH, USA, where they landed uneventfully.

C-GIGL, a privately registered Wag-Aero Sportsman 2+2, was on a local flight from the Elko/Lionel P. Demers Memorial Airpark (CBE2), BC, with the pilot and one passenger on board. The pilot flew for approximately 15 minutes and returned to CBE2 to conduct a simulated approach to Runway 21. A few seconds after the application of power to conduct the go around, the engine (Avco Lycoming O-360-A4K) sputtered and then quit. The aircraft was approximately 100 feet above the ground and the pilot turned to an opening in the trees. The aircraft collided with some trees and turned 180 degrees as it impacted terrain. The pilot and passenger undid their harnesses and egressed through the right door. Neither occupant was injured.Emergency services attended the scene, the aircraft was substantially damaged, and there was no post impact fire. The wreckage was recovered and removed from the site.

C-GGPR, un Piper PA 23-250 Apache exploité par Cargair Ltée, effectuait un vol de formation local selon les règles de vol à vue, depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec à son bord un instructeur et un élève pilote. Alors qu'il évoluait dans la zone de contrôle de CYHU, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence suite à un problème d'indication de train d'atterrissage. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre à CYHU et a circulé jusqu'à son hangar sans incident.

C-IGCI, a privately registered Quad City Ultralight Aircraft Corporation Challenger II advanced ultralight, was on a local flight from Salmon Arm (CZAM), BC with only the pilot on board. The aircraft departed approximately 0800 pacific daylight Time (PDT) and after approximately 15 minutes the engine (Rotax 503) stopped producing power. The pilot turned to attempt a landing on a nearby golf course but did not have sufficient altitude to glide to a successful forced approach. The aircraft collided with a fence in a yard adjacent to the the golf course. The pilot was not injured but the aircraft was substantially damaged.The aircraft was recovered to the owner's hangar where it will be inspected and repairs assessed.

C-GUIV, un Piper PA-28-140 de propriété privée, effectuait un vol d’entrainement selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de St-Mathieu de Beloeil, QC (CSB3) avec un instructeur et un élève pilote à bord. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage de la piste 33, le moteur a subi une perte de puissance rapide. L’instructeur a repris le contrôle de l’aéronef et a aligné l’aéronef afin d’effectuer un atterrissage d’urgence. L’aéronef s’est posé sur la surface gazonnée, environ 50 pieds passé le bout de la piste. Les freins ont été appliqués, mais, en raison de la surface mouillée, l’aéronef a poursuivi sa course, percutant une clôture avant de s’immobiliser dans la portion remontante d’un fossé situé sur l’accotement de l’autoroute 20.  La balise de repérage d’urgence (ELT) s’est activée. L’appareil a subi des dommages importants. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

C-FIUF, an Air Canada Boeing 777-233LR was conducting flight AC33 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Sydney/Kingsford Smith Intl. (YSSY), Australia.  After engine shutdown in YSSY, ground crew noticed bird strike and damage to left-hand leading edge. As per AMM, bird strike inspection completed and left-hand #5 slat and associated bleed air ducting will require replacement.

The Nolinor Aviation Boeing 737-800 (NRL 821, C-FHNM) was on approach to Runway 24L at Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. After the flaps were selected to FLAP 5, the flight crew selected landing gear down, followed by FLAP 15. The crew received no indication the flaps had moved and retried another selection with the same results. A Go-Around was performed and after completing the QRH procedures the flaps were extended to FLAP 15 using the Alternate Flap system. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. After coming to a stop ARFF inspected the aircraft for hot brakes and possible hydraulic leaks and released the aircraft to the gate.  Maintenance determined that a malfunction of the Flap/Slat Electronics Unit (FSEU) was at fault. A BITE check of the FSEU was performed with no further faults evident. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJAZ, a Jazz Aviation LP MHI RJ Aviation ULC was conducting flight 8931 from Philadelphia Intl. (KPHL), PA to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During cruise approximately 170 NM SSE of CYYZ, a Cabin crew became incapacitated.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FWGH, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight SWG283 from Moncton/Greater Moncton Romeo Leblanc Intl. (CYQM), NB to Cancun Intl. (MMUN), Mexico.  During cruise, a passenger's e-cigarette battery was found overheating under a seat and emitting smoke.  After the battery had burnt a hole in the passenger bag, Cabin crew retrieved the e-cigarette and transported using an empty dry coffee pot in the front galley.  Cabin crew elected to discharge a Halon fire extinguisher in the coffee pot, filled it with water and placed it into a larger metal container where it was monitored for the remainder of the flight.  There was no damage to aircraft or injury.  Flight landed to destination without further incident.

C-GJWD, an Air Canada Airbus A321, was operating as flight AC252 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB with 6 crew and 155 passengers on board. During arrival into CYEG, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform their duties. Duties were distributed among the remaining cabin crew. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and EMS was waiting at the gate upon arrival.

C-GLVE, a privately registered Sukhoi-26 departed Collingwood Regional Airport (CNY3) for a local flight.  After some ground runs the aircraft departed runway 31 and initially remained in the circuit, afterwards it proceeded over Georgian Bay of Lake Huron and performed airwork, followed by aerobatics. During this time the aircraft engine began to sputter and lost power. The pilot called a Mayday on the radio and glided the aircraft to a nearby field, to conduct a forced approach. A helicopter in the area heard the Mayday call, proceeded to the location and observed the aircraft on final approach for the field. During the touchdown the wheels dug into the soft ground and the aircraft overturned, the pilot received minor injuries but was trapped inside the aircraft. The helicopter landed in the field nearby the aircraft; the two occupants, along with the help of some bystanders, assisted the pilot to egress the overturned aircraft. The aircraft received substantial damage.

C-GJZT, a Jazz Aviation LP MHI RJ Aviation ULC CRJ900LR was conducting flight 8882 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Newark Liberty Intl. (KEWR), NJ.  During cruise approximately 165NM ESE of CYYZ, Flight crew received a left outboard hot brake warning message.  Flight crew completed applicable QRH, declared a PAN PAN and diverted back to CYYZ where it landed without further incident.

C-GWEJ, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was conducting flight WEN3366 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC, to Edmonton International (CYEG), AB, with 4 crew members and 71 passengers on board. After takeoff, the flight crew retracted the landing gear. Shortly thereafter, the landing gear inoperative caution light illuminated as did the nose gear amber light. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist and declared a PAN PAN to air traffic control. The flight crew returned to land in CYLW, stopped on the runway, and had aircraft rescue and fire fighting personnel inspect the aircraft. The crew was then taxied clear of the runway, shutdown, and were towed to the gate.Maintenance found the nose gear door closed proximity sensor damaged and short circuited. The sensor was replaced, and the function check determined it was serviceable. The nose gear extension and retraction were checked in accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual with no other faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GECD, a privately registered PA-31T2 (Cheyenne II), was on an IFR flight plan from Grand Prairie (CYQU), AB to La Crete (CFN5), AB with just the pilot on board. During landing gear retraction after take-off, the pilot observed 2 green landing gear lights (right main and nose) and a red light for the left main landing gear. After cycling the landing gear (no change to the indication) the pilot used the 'blow down' system which resulted in 3 green lights. The pilot elected to shutdown the left engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-135A) just in case the left main landing gear collapsed. ARFF was standing by for the single-engine approach and landing which was uneventful.

C-FWGF, un Cessna 150G privé, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis un terrain privé à St-Urbain-Premier, QC avec un élève-pilote et un passager à bord. Alors qu'il survolait à très basse altitude une maison située dans la municipalité de St-Rémi, QC, l'aéronef a effectué une manoeuvre à basse altitude avant de percuter une ligne de distribution d’électricité et s'est s'écrasé dans le stationnement d'une maison privée. Un incendie s'est déclaré et l'aéronef a été détruit. Les 2 occupants, grièvement blessés, ont été extirpés de l'aéronef et transportés vers un centre hospitalier.

C-GRXW, a Pilatus PC-12/47E aircraft operated by Ornge Global Air Inc, was conducting flight PUL106 from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON. During the departure off Runway 07, through approximately 800 feet AGL, the crew observed the engine chip detector warning light illuminate. The QRH items were actioned, and a emergency was declared. The crew returned to CYQT and carried out an uneventful landing.A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed debris in the reduction gear box. The aircraft has been removed from service and the engine chip and oil samples were sent to manufacturer for analysis.

C-GGOK, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400 (Dash 8 Q400) operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8272 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Kelowna (CYLW), BC, with 4 crew and 75 passengers on board. During beverage service, a flight attendant (FA) was injured. The FA continued the flight to CYLW but was unable to operate the return flight to CYVR and was replaced with a customer service representative. There was no effect on normal operations. The injured FA was able to resume work the following day.

C-GITU, an Airbus A321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA122 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Lester B. Pearson International (CYYZ), ON. C-FNJZ, a CL-600-2D24 (Regional Jet Series 900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation, was conducting flight JZA7776 from CYVR to Edmonton International (CYEG), AB. A loss of separation occurred while the aircraft were on initial departure. At 1630:19 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), the lateral separation was 2.2 nautical miles (NM), and the vertical separation was 900 feet; the requirement was 3 NM or 1000 feet. At their closest, the aircraft were separated by 2.2 NM and 400 feet. After a vector heading assignment to JZA7776, separation was regained laterally at 1630:38 PDT and both aircraft proceeded enroute.

C-GKFS, a Kelowna Flightcraft Air Charter Limited Convair 340 (Convair 5800) was operating as flight KFA575, from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Victoria (CYYJ), BC, with 2 crew aboard. During the arrival to CYYJ, the crew noticed a higher-than-normal turbine inlet temperature (TIT) along with a lower-than-normal horsepower (HP) indication on the No. 1 engine. The crew elected to return to CYVR. While on final approach, the engine RPM decayed below the allowable limits and the crew conducted an inflight shut down. The crew landed without further incident. Company maintenance determined that a compressor failure occurred and are conducting further inspections to determine the cause.

C-FEXB, a Morningstar Air Express Incorporated Cessna 208B (Grand Caravan) was operating as flight MAL7052 from Nanaimo (CYCD), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC. C-GEEN, a Westjet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was conducting flight WEN3284 from Prince George (CYXS), BC, to CYVR. A loss of separation occurred while the aircraft were transitioning to final approach with C-GEEN assigned runway 08L and C-FEXB assigned runway 08R. At 1628:49 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) the lateral separation was reduced to 2.9 nautical miles (NM) and the vertical separation was 200 feet; the minimum separation requirement was 3.0 NM or 1000 feet. At their closest point, the aircraft were separated by 2.0 NM and 200 feet. The approach clearance was cancelled for the Dash 8 and the crew was assigned vectors for another approach. The required minimum separation was regained at 1629:34 PDT. Both aircraft landed safely.

C-GSJB, an Airbus A319-112 aircraft operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting ROU1725 from Halifax Stanfield International, NS (CYHZ) to Tampa – Tampa Intl. (KTPA), FL. The aircraft was established in cruise flight and was overflying Yarmouth, NS when the flight crew reported that one flight attendant fell ill and was unable to continue duties for the remainder of the flight. Medical assistance was rendered to the individual by passengers onboard who identified as medically qualified. Safety related duties were redistributed between the remaining flight attendants. The flight was subsequently continued to destination without further incident.

C-GJZV, an MHI RJ Aviation CRJ-900 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA192 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Regina (CYQR), SK. N918TX, a Cessna 750 privately operated aircraft was flying from CYVR to King Country International (KBFI) Seattle, WA, USA. A loss of separation occurred while the aircraft were on departure from RWY 26L CYVR. At 1418:03 PDT the lateral separation was reduced to 2.9 nautical miles (NM) with a vertical separation of 500 feet; the requirement was 3.0 NM or 1000 feet. At their closest point, the aircraft were separated by 2.6 NM and 500 feet. Minimum lateral separation was regained at 1418:33 and both aircraft proceeded enroute.

C-FDCA, an Air Canada Airbus A320, was operating as AC236 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB with 5 crew and 144 passengers on board. While on descent for CYEG the aircraft struck 1 or more Canadian Geese. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and continued the approach to Runway 20 without further issue. Damage was sustained to the radome and left wing leading edge.Company maintenance replaced the radome and the No. 4 left hand slat.

C-GEHV, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight ACA1046 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Palm Springs Intl. (KPSP), CA.  During descent to KPSP, flight crew received a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory).  Flight crew complied with the RA and continued to destination without further incident.

C-GMZR, an Air Canada Airbus Canada Limited Partnership A220-300 was conducting flight ACA1323 from Providenciales Intl. (MBPV), Turks and Caicos Islands to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  On initial climb, the flight crew received a right-hand engine vibration warning.  No vibration was felt by the flight crew, but the right engine showed that the N2 vibration level had been exceeded. The flight crew completed the appropriate checklist, a PANPAN was declared, and the flight levelled at FL260.  Shortly after, the right-hand engine vibration warning caution cleared. After discussion with maintenance control, the flight crew cancelled the PANPAN and continued to destination without further incident.  Maintenance completed the required inspection upon arrival in YYZ and oil line was replaced as per AMM.

C-FXRJ, a British Aerospace Avro 146 Series RJ100 operated by Summit Air Ltd., was conducting flight SUT8093 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl. (CYXE), SK. to Kamloops (CYKA) BC. During the climb at approximately 8 000 feet, the flight crew received a #3 engine vibration warning light on the master warning system panel. While running the engine vibration checklist the engine fire warning light illuminated. The flight crew carried out the engine fire drill and the fire engine warning light went out. The crew declared an emergency with ATC and secured the engine. SUT8093 landed without incident at CYXE with ARFF on standby. The operator's maintenance inspected the engine after the occurrence and found that the oil tank was dry, metal was on the chip detector, and the fuel flow divider was found cracked. The engine was removed and sent for evaluation.

C-GBIJ, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was conducting flight ROU1778 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Cozumel Intl. (MMCZ), Mexico.  During descent approximately 47 NM NW at 14000 feet, flight encountered momentary turbulence and one cabin crew received minor injuries.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GWJF, a WestJet Airlines Ltd Boeing 737-700 was conducting flight WS1172 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Fort Myers/Southwest Florida Intl. (KRSW), FL.  During cruise in vicinity of Tallahassee Intl. (KTLH), FL, a cabin crew became incapacitated.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FYPB, a Swoop Inc. Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight 771 from Phoenix/Mesa Gateway Airport (KIWA), AZ to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB.  During cruise in vicinity of Rapid City Regional (KRAP), SD, a cabin crew member became incapacitated.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FGJI, an Airbus A320-214 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA299 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC. Shortly after departure from CYWG, a flight attendant attempted to turn on the coffee makers; however, one was not showing any power. The flight attendant subsequently noticed a burning smell, heard a loud pop, and smoke appeared in the galley. The flight crew were notified and ACA299 declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft returned to CYWG and landed without incident. The operator's maintenance found visible signs of damage to the forward galley coffee maker. The galley coffee maker tray and wire harness were inspected and no damage was found. The circuit breaker did not trip. The coffee maker was replaced.

C-GKJZ, a Bell Helicopter Textron Canada Limited 407, operated by Alpine Helicopters Incorporated, was conducting a passenger flight from Golden (CYGE), BC, to the Saskatchewan Glacier 53 nautical miles north-northwest of CYGE. After assessing the proposed landing site as unsuitable due to insufficient visual landing references, the pilot discussed an alternate landing area with the passengers. It was decided to land at a location that appeared to have more sunlight and better visual references. During the final approach to landing, the direct light was lost and the anticipated visual references deteriorated. The helicopter skids dug into the snow at low speed and the helicopter rolled onto its right side. The passengers evacuated the aircraft followed by the pilot. There were no injuries but the helicopter was substantially damaged.The helicopter was removed and is being evaluated by maintenance crews for the operator.

C-GMPX, a Royal Canadian Mounted Police Pilatus PC-12/47E, was operating on an IFR flight from Whitehorse (CYXY), YT to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with just the pilot on board. Shortly after departure on Runway 32L, the pilot declared an emergency and returned to the airport. The aircraft collided with terrain within the airport boundary. The pilot sustained serious injuries and the aircraft was substantially damaged. There was no post impact fire. The Edmonton TSB office is deploying to the accident site.

C-GBIJ, un Airbus A319 exploité par Air Canada Rouge sous l’indicatif ROU1953, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Toronto/Lester B.Pearson, ON (CYYZ). En palier au niveau de vol FL360, l’aéronef a rencontré une série continue de turbulences modérées. L’équipage a demandé une descente à l’unité de contrôle aérien et a été autorisé entre FL300 et FL360. Après avoir amorcé la descente, l’intensité des turbulences a augmenté brusquement et de façon significative au passage du FL355 pour devenir sévère, modifiant de façon importante l’attitude de l’aéronef en tangage et en roulis. L’équipage a eu de la difficulté à contrôler l’assiette de l’aéronef qui est néanmoins demeuré à l’intérieur de l’enveloppe normale de vol. Dès que l’aéronef est descendu sous le FL340, les turbulences ont cessé abruptement et le vol est devenu calme. L’équipage a stabilisé l’altitude à FL340 et a poursuivi sa route jusqu’à destination sans rencontrer d’autres turbulences. Aucun passager ou membre d’équipage n’a été blessé. L’aéronef a atterri sans encombre à CYYZ. L’aéronef a été inspecté par le service de maintenance avant d’être remis en service.

C-FHNM, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Nolinor Inc., was conducting flight NRL821 from Juan Gualberto Gomez International Airport (MUVR), Cuba to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON with 7 crew and 159 passengers onboard. During the approach into CYYZ runway 24L, the flight crew selected landing gear down and the Flaps from 5 to 15 without indication or movement of the Flaps. The crew reselected to 5 then 15 without success. The crew initiated a go around and completed the applicable checklist. The Flaps were subsequently extended to 15 using the alternate flap system and declared emergency (Pan Pan) with Air traffic Control. NRL 821 landed runway 23 where Airport Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) vehicles were standing by for an inspection. The aircraft subsequently taxied to the gate without further incident.

C-FGSK, an Ottawa Flying Club Cessna 150L on a local training flight from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON was conducting touch and go out of runway 04 with only the pilot onboard. While the aircraft was on the initial climb after the last touch and go, the engine reportedly started sputtering and lost power. The pilot initiated a descending right turn to avoid buildings and populated area. The aircraft subsequently completed a forced landing on the military base adjacent to the airport. The aircraft skidded and hit two trees before coming to rest against a third tree. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the nose and the wings. The pilot was uninjured. Airport Rescue and fire fighting vehicles were dispatched to the scene. The local and military police also attended the scene. The aircraft flew for approximately .7 hour before the occurrence and reportedly had fuel for approximately 2 hours. The aircraft has been moved to The Ottawa Flying Club for further inspection.

C-GLQB, a Bombardier DHC-8-402, operating as Porter Airlines flight 2691, departed Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), Ontario for a night flight to Sault Ste. Marie Airport (CYAM), Ontario. Upon arrival, the flight crew performed the RNAV approach for runway 12; however, after touchdown the aircraft overran the end of the runway. The aircraft came to a stop about 250 beyond the end of the runway and was stuck in soft grass/mud. There were no injuries, and no damage to the aircraft.

At 1025 Mountain Daylight Time on 14 April 2023, the Northwestern Air Lease Ltd. British Aerospace P.L.C. Jetstream Model 3112 aircraft (registration C-FCPE, serial number 825) departed Fort Smith Airport (CYSM), Northwest Territories, on a training flight (flight PLR732T) with the captain and the first officer on board. At 1227, the aircraft returned to the airport. Shortly after landing, the left main landing gear unit collapsed, and the aircraft veered off the runway. There were no injuries. The aircraft’s left main landing gear unit, engine, propeller, and wing tip, as well as its belly cargo pod, were significantly damaged.UPDATED 16 January 2026

The Canadian North, Boeing 737-36N, C-GPNL, was operating as flight AKT1748 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB. While in cruise, approximately 72 nm NNW of Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB the flight crew received a FWD lower cargo smoke warning. The crew actioned the non-normal checklist, declared a PAN PAN emergency and diverted to CYEG. The aircraft landed without further incident and was met by ARFF. ARFF inspected the FWD lower cargo compartment with thermal equipment and no hot areas were detected. The aircraft returned to the apron; there were no injuries.Company maintenance found no traces of fire or smoke. The cargo fire extinguishing filter/dryer was replaced, cargo fire extinguishing system was cleaned as per AMM and the cargo compartment fire bottle squibs were replaced.

C-FDMB, a WestJet Airline Ltd Boeing 737-8CT was conducting flight WS2051 from Huatulco/Bahías de Huatulco Intl (MMBT), Mexico to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC. During cruise, in vicinity of Nogales, Mexico, a flight crew member became incapacitated and was replaced by a deadheading flight crew member. Also, during cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was replaced by a deadheading cabin crew member.  Flight landed in CYVR without further incident.

C-FXWJ, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 operated by WestJet Airlines Ltd, was conducting flight WJ601 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE) SK. to Calgary Intl (CYYC) AB. During the flight, a flight attendant was unable to continue their duties due to a medical issue and was not in their assigned jump seat for landing. WJ601 landed safely in CYYC. EMS was required upon arrival and the flight attendant was released to their care.

The Federal Express Airbus A300, N685FE, was operating as flight FDX120 from Memphis Intl. (KMEM), TN to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB. During approach, while descending through 7000 feet ASL, the flight crew received a SLAT SYS 1&2 fault indication when flaps were selected down. The flight crew cycled the flaps, however the fault reappeared. The crew proceeded to action the Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitor (ECAM), Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) and declared a PAN PAN. The flight crew continued the approach and landed with slats near zero and trailing edge flaps at 40. ARFF followed the aircraft to the gate to monitor for hot brakes, and brake fans were utilized once the aircraft was parked at the gate to assist in cooling the brakes. There were no injuries. Company maintenance found the right torque tube limiter circuit breaker popped. The limiter breaker was reset and the right-wing flap gearboxes were inspected. Operational tests were carried out and the right-wing jackscrews were lubricated.

C-GBHR, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was conducting flight ROU1879 from St-Lucia/Hewanorra Intl. (TLPL), Saint-Lucia to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During cruise over the North Atlantic Ocean, a cabin crew became incapacitated.  Safety duties were redistributed, and flight continued to destination without further incident.

The privately owned Robinson R44 II helicopter (C-GGVW) was on route from London International Airport (CYXU), ON to Centralia/James T. Field Memorial Aerodrome (CYCE), ON with a student and instructor on board. The student was flying the helicopter, and as the helicopter was climbing through 1400 ft ASL, a loud bang was heard. The instructor immediately took control of the helicopter as it began to yaw to the right followed by a roll to the left. The instructor entered the helicopter into an autorotation but could not control the yaw. As the ground approached the instructor initiated a flare and noted the main rotor RPM dropping to 80%. During the landing the right skid dug into the ground and the helicopter rolled on its side. The instructor was not injured but the student received a minor injury to the right arm.

The Porter Airlines DHC-8-400 aircraft (PD2388, C-GLQD) was on approach to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ) runway 26 when the crew selected the landing gear down. After extension, only the Left and Nose Gear indicated green lights for down and locked. The Right Main Gear indicated an unsafe red light with an amber indication for the door. The crew abandoned the approach to CYTZ and advised ATC of the landing gear issue. The QRH procedures were followed for the Alternate Gear Extension, but the Right Main Gear unsafe indication remained. At this time the crew decided to divert to CYYZ and declared an emergency. After a fly-by to confirm the Landing Gear was down, the aircraft landed uneventfully on Runway 15 with ARFF standing by. Maintenance found that the Right Main Gear Downlock sensor 2 was flagged by the PSEU. After re-rigging the sensor all indications were normal.

Location: Moose Jaw/Air Vice Marshal C.M. McEwen
Summary: C-FMFG, a Boeing 757-2B7 aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express Inc, was conducting flight MAL7079 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 2 pilots on board. While in cruise at FL 360, approximately 10 nautical miles South of Moose Jaw, SK, the right engine hydraulic pump inoperative EICAS message annunciated. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and  continued the flight to CYVR, where an uneventful landing was conducted.The operator's maintenance replaced the right-engine hydraulic pump, case drain filter, pressure filter, return filter, and the hydraulic pressure line hose upper self-sealing coupling. Engine runs were completed with no further faults noted and the aircraft was returned to service.

On 04 April 2023, the Air Partners Corp. Beechcraft King Air 350 (registration C-GKHD, serial FL-1126) was operating as flight SDE300 on a positioning flight from Bonnyville Regional Airport (CYBF), Alberta to Calgary International Airport (CYCC), Alberta. On board were 2 flight crew members. Prior to the occurrence, the aircraft was parked at the northwest corner of the ramp at CYBF. At approximately 1940 mountain daylight time, while attempting to taxi between a parked aircraft and the hangar along the north side of the ramp, C-GKHD's left winglet struck the southwest corner of the hangar. The flight crew then shut down the aircraft. The impact caused the outer section of the wing, outboard of the fuel filler cap, to shear off, buckling the skin and damaging the aileron. There were no injuries.Maintenance action: Maintenance is assessing the damage and the manufacturer has been contacted to assist with the development of a suitable repair.

C-GFCI, un Airbus 320-214 exploité par exploité par Air Canada Rouge LP sous l’indicatif ROU1950, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB). ROU1950 a intercepté l’approche finale de la piste 06 à CYQB à environ 12 miles marins (nm), en descente à 3000 pieds. À ce moment, C-FCCC un Cessna C-172 exploité par Orizon Aviation Québec Inc. qui effectuait un vol de formation IFR de CYQB à CYQB, était sur un guidage radar en éloignement pour l’approche piste 06 à 4000 pieds. Peu après, une perte d’espacement est survenue avec C-FCCC qui se trouvait à environ 2,7 miles marins au sud de l’approche finale à 4000 pieds. L’espacement requis était de 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical et 3 miles marins sur le plan horizontal.

C-FSNU, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8, was operating as flight AC182 from Vancouver Intl. Airport (CYVR), BC to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON with 6 crew and 135 passengers on board. While in cruise, about 55 nm SW of Calgary, AB, the flight encountered severe turbulence associated with mountain wave activity. Control of the aircraft was briefly lost along with an overspeed warning. 2 flight attendants sustained minor injuries during the event. The flight continued to destination.

C-GZFE, a Buffalo Airways Ltd. Lockheed Electra L188C was operating as training flight BFL1403 from the Yellowknife (CYZF), NT. airport with 2 flight crew onboard. Approximately 30 minutes into the flight an engine fire indication on the number 1 engine in zone 2 was indicated. A visual check was conducted, and the number 1 engine (ALLISON, 501-D13) was shut down as a precaution in accordance with the standard operating procedures. An emergency was not declared. The flight landed in CYZF with no further issues.Following the flight company maintenance found that the number 1 engine zone 2-3 fire control relay plug was loose. The plug was cleaned and refitted in accordance with the maintenance manual and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GWLK, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737 Max, was being operated as flight WS613 from Ottawa (CYOW), ON to Calgary International (CYYC), AB.During descent, the flight crew of WS613 checked in with the CYYC arrival controller and advised having the RNAV (RNP) Y RWY17R approach set up. ATC then provided vectors to WS613 and asked if they could accommodate a visual approach instead. The flight crew accepted and continued the descent. Once the aircraft was close to intercept the centerline of Runway 17L, the captain looked up, disengaged the autopilot and started to turn the aircraft towards the centerline of Runway 17L. The First Officer identified the error and immediately alerted the captain. The controller instructed WS613 to turn right heading 200 and notified the flight crew they were lined up with the left side. The flight crew readback the instruction and corrected their course for runway 17R. Separation was reduced to 2 miles on a 9-mile final from CYYC with WS2311, a WestJet Boeing 787-9, C-GUDO, inbound from Cancun (MMUN), Mexico. Both flights landed with no further issues.

C-FJQZ, a CRJ900 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8689 from Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl Airport (KBOS), MA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl Airport (CYYZ), ON, with 4 crew and 75 passengers on board. After landing on runway 24L at CYYZ, the crew received an intermittent "Brake Overheat" indication. The crew requested ARFF to attend their location to monitor the brakes, the ARFF advised that there was no significant heat detected. Discussion with maintenance personnel led to a conclusion that this was likely a false indication, and the crew taxied the aircraft to the gate with ARFF following. Further inspection revealed a shorted wire in the LH MLG OUTBD wiring harness, which was replaced before the aircraft returned to service.

C-GZON, an Air Spray (1967) Ltd. Aero Commander 690 was conducting a training flight, as flight ASB055, out of Red Deer (CYQF), AB with 2 flight crew on board.  The aircraft started take-off roll from Runway 17. At approximately 60 knots the nosewheel began to shimmy and the aircraft veered towards the left side of the runway. The flight crew aborted the take off and tried to keep the aircraft on the centerline. The aircraft continued to the left and exited the runway. The aircraft came to a stop in a drainage ditch. The nose gear and left main gear collapsed and both propellers were damaged.  The flight crew were not injured and egressed from the aircraft on their own.

C-GXNL, a De Havilland DHC8-402 operated by PAL Airlines Ltd as PVL 921 was conducting a flight from Goose Bay International Airport (CYYR), NL to Wabush Airport (CYWK), NL. During the cruise phase, the crew received a No. 1 low oil pressure warning annunciator light, followed by a FADEC caution light. The crew advised ATC they would like to return to CYYR and declared an emergency. A loud popping noise was heard, and the crew completed the memory items and actioned the QRH. The No. 1 engine was shutdown and the aircraft landed without further incident. ARFF inspected the aircraft and the crew taxied to the gate.Maintenance continues to investigate the issue of the No. 1 engine and will follow up with more information.

C-GLQY, un hélicoptère Bell B206LR exploité par Canadian Helicopters Limited, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Port Cartier, QC, à destination du camp « Love » situé à 110 NM au NNW de Port Cartier avec 3 personnes et le pilote à bord. Alors qu'il se trouvait environ 49 nm à l'ouest-nord-ouest de l’aéroport de Sept-Îles, Qc (CYZV), la visibilité a réduit en raison de fortes averses de neige. Le pilote a tenté de maintenir ses références avec le sol et a ralenti l’hélicoptère tout en amorçant une descente. Alors qu'il tentait un virage de 180 degrés, le pilote a perdu les références visuelles et l’hélicoptère a frappé durement la surface gelée d’un lac. L’hélicoptère s’est ensuite renversé sur le côté et le pilote a activé la radiobalise d’urgence. Les 4 occupants sont sortis, et ont subi des blessures mineures. Un autre hélicoptère de la compagnie est allé secourir les occupants.MODIFIER LE 17 MAI 2023

C-FPCJ, a Boeing 767-306 operated by Cargo Jet Airways Ltd as CJT620 was conducting a flight from Greater Moncton Romeo LeBlanc International Airport (CYQM), NB to St John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL with 3 crew members on board. During the landing roll out, the crew received a cargo fire indication light. Within 15 seconds the indication light went out. ARFF was requested to meet the aircraft at the ramp and an inspection was carried out. Nothing was discovered and maintenance was advised.Maintenance carried out an inspection and ensured the upper deck detectors, main control panel and integrity/security of all connectors. No defects were noted, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FMHA, a Boeing 757-200 operated by Morningstar Air Express Inc., was conducting flight MAL7050 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), Ontario to Edmonton Intl Airport (CYEG), Alberta, with 2 crew on board. While climbing through FL310 in the vicinity of Wiarton Airport (CYVV), Ontario, the flight crew received a warning indication that there was vibration in the number 2 engine (RB211-535 E4). The leveled at FL320 and conducted the appropriate checklist(s), leading to a precautionary engine shutdown. The crew declared PAN PAN and requested to return to CYYZ, where they landed uneventfully approximately 44 minutes after they had departed. Maintenance troubleshooting revealed chafed wires leading to the Airborne Vibration Monitor (AVM), which resulted in a spurious indication of engine vibration. The wires were repaired, and the AVM unit replaced before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJWS, a WestJet Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737-800, was operating as flight WJA650 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON with 6 flight crew and 131 passengers on board. Shortly after departure, during initial climb, a passenger's e-cigarette/vape pen began to smoke and get hot. The passenger put it in a cup of liquid that they had on their tray table. The cup and e-cigarette were then transferred by cabin crew to a metallic container that contained water. The smoke and heat diminished soon after. A decision was made to continue to destination.

C-GWVE, a privately registered Piper PA-12 was operating from the Medicine Hat (CYXH), AB airport. The owner was receiving a tailwheel checkout, an insurance requirement, from an instructor. The flight departed the airport and conducted some basic upper air work maneuvers. Approximately 1 hour later the flight returned to CYXH to perform take offs and landings. During the second touch and go a wheel landing was attempted. During the landing roll, the aircraft started to drift to the right side of the runway. The control stick was pulled aft and the tail of the aircraft contacted the runway and the plane yawed to the left. Control of the aircraft was lost and the aircraft exited the right side of the runway. The aircraft came to rest in the grass, with a damaged fuselage, left wing, and horizontal stabilizer. There was no damage to the prop or the engine. The aircraft was taxied to the hangar. There were no injuries to the two occupants.

C-GHQZ, a De Havilland DHC-8-314 operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting a flight from Sioux Lookout, ON (CYXL) to Kingfisher Lake, ON (CNM5).
