When approximately 25 miles north of CYXL, the flight attendant alerted the flight crew that a passenger noticed a smell of smoke. The flight crew elected to return to CYXL and declared an emergency. One passenger reported feeling ill. An uneventful landing and shut down were carried out and, after a short cabin inspection, the passengers deplaned normally. An ambulance met the aircraft upon arrival. The operator's maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft. No faults were found during a post-occurrence run-up. No further smoke or smell of smoke was detected.

C-FASY, an Airsprint Inc. Cessna 525B was conducting flight ASP489 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Miami Intl. (KMIA), FL.  Flight crew was cleared CSTL2 arrival in KMIA but due to significant thunderstorm in Miami area ATC rerouted flight over the Bahamas.  After being vectored for several minutes with Freeport ATC, flight crew informed ATC that they needed to land to an alternate airport as KMIA was still delayed.  At this point flight crew decided to declare an emergency due to low fuel.  Dispatch informed that Stuart/Witham Field (KSUA), FL would be able to accommodate.  Flight crew requested direct LEBAN at FL180 and landed in KSUA with 500lbs remaining (20 minutes).

C-FXWT, a Morningstar Partners Ltd. dba Bombardier Challenger 605 (CL-600-2B16) was conducting flight 26380 from Tucson Intl. (KTUS), AZ to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB.  During initial climb, cleared to 17000 feet, flight received a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory) due to VFR traffic.  PF already noticed the traffic prior to the RA and as preemptive measure had already disconnected autopilot and increased rate of climb.  Flight crew complied with the RA and continued to destination without further incident.

C-GAKW, un Cessna 172L exploité par A.L.M. Par avion inc. effectuait des circuits (décollages et atterrissages) sur la piste 33 à l’aérodrome de St-Mathieu-de-Beloeil, QC (CSB3). Lors de l’atterrissage en conditions de vent traversier, l’aéronef a été déporté vers la droite par le vent. Par la suite, l’aéronef s'est retrouvé sur une partie gazonnée de la bande de piste avant de se retrouver dans de la neige granuleuse. La roue de nez s’est enfoncée dans la neige et l’aéronef s’est renversé, terminant sa course sur le dos. Le pilote, seul à bord, n’a pas été blessé. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée.

The Hop-a-jet Bombardier CL-600-2B16 (flight HPJ650, registration N650HJ) was cleared to climb to FL 210 when ATC observed the aircraft at FL214. ATC instructed HPJ 650 to descend and maintain FL210. A loss of vertical separation occurred with Porter Airlines DHC-8-400 (POE 2190, registration C-GKQI) flying in the same direction at FL 220.

C-FFLZ a Flair Airlines Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight FLE1601 from Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. After departure out of KFLL Runway 10L AGERS1 SID, the first officer was PF (Manually flown departure in VMC conditions). Just prior to the level off altitude of 5000', a TCAS ''Descend'' RA (resolution advisory) was issued. A descent to approximately 4100' was commenced and ATC was notified. Visual contact was made with traffic descending to 6000'. All passengers and crew were seated at this point as flight was below 10 000'. The altitude excursion was momentary as flight was clear of traffic within 10 seconds. ATC was advised flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FPCA, an Air Canada Boeing 767-375ER was conducting flight AC7261 from Bogota/El Nuevo Dorado Intl. (SKBO), Colombia to Panama City/Tocumen Intl. (MPTO), Panama.  After landing inspection by maintenance showed tail skid shoe was found damaged (scrape marks) and tail skid indicator was popped out.  Panama accident investigation bureau will not investigate this occurrence.

The privately owned Cessna T310R aircraft (registration C-GKWC) was on route from Niagara District Airport (CYSN), ON to Windsor International airport (CYQG), ON when the pilot declared an emergency after it was reported the #2 engine shut down. The emergency was declared approximately 30 NM SW of London airport (CYXU) and the pilot decided to divert to CYXU where it landed without further incident.

C-GLQE, a Porter Airlines Inc. De Havilland DHC-8-400 was conducting flight POE2942 from Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl. (KBOS) to Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON.  During initial climb, Flight crew declared an emergency (Pan Pan) with ATC due #2 engine indicated more RPM than commanded through 5000' feet. The Flight crew elected to do a precautionary shutdown of the #2 engine and diverted to KBOS. Flight landed in KBOS without further incident. There were no injuries reported.The engine data was downloaded and it was found that the #2 engine power lever exceeded the power detent during climb out. The Propeller Electronic Controller (PEC) logic assumes that the pilot needs full emergency power and correctly drove #2 propeller to 1020 RPM even though the propeller condition lever remained at 900 RPM.  Aircraft was returned to service with no fault found.

The Air Canada Rouge Airbus A320-214 (ROU1934, C-GFCI) was on approach to runway 05 at Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) at 3000 ft ASL, when during the left bank to intercept the localizer, the aircraft encountered suspected wake turbulence which resulted in an un-commanded right wing drop and subsequent roll to approximately 30 degrees right bank attitude. The aircraft recovered with autopilot input and continued with the approach.

The Air Canada Airbus A220 aircraft (AC 459, C-GJYE) was on route from CYOW to CYYZ when the flight crew was advised of an unusual odour in the cabin. The crew decided to continue the flight and declared a PAN PAN . The aircraft landed uneventfully in CYYZ with ARFF standing by. Maintenance performed engine runs with no fault found. Further checks revealed that both engines were overserviced with oil. Maintenance also replaced the #2 Air Cycle Machine and completed a pack decontamination check.

C-GJTX, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was conducting flight ROU1706 from Las Vegas (KLAS), NV to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau INTL. (CYUL), QB.  During cruise phase of flight at FL330, flight was cleared to climb to FL350 due to turbulence. Approximately three minutes later as flight was climbing through approximately FL340, ATC queried if flight would reach FL350 within the next twenty seconds to which the response was negative. ATC subsequently instructed flight crew to turn left 50 degrees. During the turn, ATC issued another instruction to flight crew to turn immediately to heading 360. Shortly thereafter, flight crew received and complied with TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to ''CLIMB'' however climb performance was limited given the aircraft configuration. The conflict was resolved several seconds later, and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GUPK, an Air Canada A220-300 was conducting flight ACA1323 from Providenciales Intl. (MBVP), Turks and Caicos Islands to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  In cruise approximately 100nm SE of CYYZ, Flight crew received a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory).  Flight crew complied with the RA and continued to destination without further incident.

C-FSLU, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight ACA1300 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Houston/George Bush Intercontinental (KIAH), TX. During descent, Flight crew received a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory).  Flight crew followed the RA and landed in KIAH without further incident.

C-FJCZ, a Cessna Citation C550, being operated by the Government of Canada, Department Of Transport as TGO858, was conducting a flight from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. After departure, the crew felt a momentary high frequency vibration while climbing through 5000 feet and requested to stop the climb at 6000 feet. The flight crew noted that the vibration seemed to stop with no abnormal cockpit indications and requested to resume their climb. Shortly after, the crew noted that the vibration resumed and seemed be associated with left engine when N1 was near 90%. The crew again requested to stop the climb at 12,000 feet and requested a diversion to Moncton/Roméo Leblanc Intl (CYQM), NB. As they leveled off and set course for CYQM, the vibration became continuous. The crew then declared a PAN PAN and requested to return to CYHZ. The vibration was steady at all power settings with no other abnormal indications. While on the approach, the vibration disappeared with the lower power setting being used. The aircraft landed safely at 1635 UTC with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) standing by and taxied to the ramp.Maintenance troubleshooting indicates a left engine generator failure. The generator was replaced, and the aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GWJF, a WestJet Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737-7CT was conducting flight WS1233 from Fort Lauderdale/ Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During cruise in vicinity of Richmond Intl. (KRIC), VA a cabin crew became incapacitated.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GJXN, an Airbus Canada Limited Partnership  A220-300 airplane, operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA199 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International (CYYZ), ON, to Victoria Intl. (CYYJ), BC. C-GYJZ, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) airplane, operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA169 from Vancouver Intl.(CYVR), BC, to CYYJ. A loss of separation occurred while the aircraft were transitioning to final approach at CYYJ. At 2303:34 PST, lateral separation was reduced to 2.8 nautical miles (NM) with a vertical separation of 500 feet: the requirement was 3.0 NM or 1000 feet. At their closest point, horizontal separation was 2.2 NM and 900 feet. Minimum vertical separation was regained at 2303:52 after air traffic control cancelled the approach for JZA169 and vectored the crew for another approach. Both aircraft landed without further incident.

The Rockcliffe Flying Club (1961) Cessna 172 S aircraft (C-GKSK) was on a local training flight with a student pilot on board at the Ottawa/Rockcliffe airport (CYRO), ON. While performing a touch-and-go exercise on runway 09, directional control difficulties were experienced, and the take-off was aborted. While attempting to stop the aircraft, the pilot continued to experience directional control difficulties and the aircraft departed the right edge of the useable runway surface at the departure end, impacting the snowbank.  During the impact there was substantial damage to the propeller and the left-wing tip.  The aircraft came to rest about 200 feet beyond the runway end, and about 75 feet south of the centerline. The student pilot sustained minor injuries and didn’t require immediate medical assistance.

C-FLRI, a privately registered Cessna 206, was conducting a VFR flight from Leader (CJD5), SK, to a private aerodrome 4 nautical miles southwest of Eatonia (CJG2) SK, with one person onboard. While enroute, the aircraft encountered low cloud/fog and the pilot descended to remain visual with the ground. In whiteout conditions, the aircraft's wing impacted the ground during the base leg turn to final. The aircraft came to rest in a field and sustained sustainable damage. The pilot was not injured. The ELT activated and the signal was received.

C-FSBV, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was conducting flight AC856 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to London/Heathrow (EGLL) UK.  During descent, flight crew received a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory).  Flight crew complied with RA and flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FXDP, a SkyCare IAL Westwind 1124 was conducting flight PHX303 Region of Waterloo Intl. (CYKF), ON to Daytona Beach Intl. (KDAB), FL.  During descent at 8000 feet, left generator disconnected.  While attempting to reset the generator, more electrical systems started turning off and circuit breakers popping on the RH (right hand) distribution bus.  Shortly thereafter, an electrical smell was present in the cockpit.  Flight crew isolated/disconnected the RH distribution bus circuit breaker and the smell dissipated.  With the remaining radio and transponder offline, flight crew declared an emergency with ATC to get priority in KDAB.  Flight landed without further incident.  Maintenance is troubleshooting.

N824AN, un Boeing 787-9 exploité par American Airlines inc. sous l'indicatif AA110, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Chicago O'Hare, US (KORD) à destination de l’aéroport Léonard-de-Vinci de Rome Fiumicino, Italie (LIRF). À environ 10 NM au sud de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL), l'équipage a déclaré une urgence médicale en raison d’un membre d’équipage malade. L’équipage a demandé un retour vers KORD où il s'est posé sans encombre. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé et l'appareil n'a subi aucun dommage.

A Piedmont Embraer E145 aircraft (flight PDT 6072, registration N669MB) destined for Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) ON, was following a Jazz Aviation LP., Bombardier CL-600-2D24 aircraft (flight JZA 716, registration C-GCJZ) over the NUBER intersection, and while transitioning into Toronto terminal airspace a loss of separation occurred.

C-FYJG, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was conducting flight ROU1731 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Phoenix/Sky Harbor Intl. (KPHX), AZ.  During visual approach, just prior to turning final runway 26, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to monitor vertical speed.  Flight crew complied with the RA as traffic was intercepting final 25R and flight landed without further incident.

C-GEPG, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight ACA1047 from Palm Spring Intl. (KPSP), CA to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC.  On departure, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory).  Flight crew complied with RA and continued to destination without further incident.

C-FRQW, un Embraer 175 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8815, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Dallas/Fort Worth International, US (KDFW), TX avec 45 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Lors de la montée, l’équipage a noté une perte de carburant du côté droit d’environ 200 kg. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et a demandé un retour à CYUL. L’appareil s’est posé en surcharge sans incident avec les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. L’appareil a ensuite circulé au terminal par la suite. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FQGG, a WestJet Boeing 737-8 MAX aircraft conducting flight WS4201, was levelling off at FL 360 after departing from Toronto Lester B Pearson airport (CYYZ), ON, when the flight crew received a hydraulic pump low pressure indication from the #2 engine driven pump (EDP). The Non-normal checklist (NNC) was followed, and the indication cleared. Shortly after, the #2 engine oil filter bypass caution light illuminated. The NNC procedures were followed but the light remained on. The flight crew then elected to shut down the engine, declare a PAN PAN and return to CYYZ. The landing was uneventful with ARFF standing by. The aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power. Maintenance found the hydraulic line quick disconnect between the #2 engine driven pump and the #2 engine pylon unsecured. Maintenance re-secured the line in accordance with the Boeing AMM. The operator started a fleet campaign on all B737-8 Max aircraft to verify that the hydraulic quick disconnect connectors are in their locked position. A recurring task to check the connectors was also initiated.

C-FKAB, a Pilatus PC-12/45 aircraft operated by Air Bravo Corp., was conducting flight PCO1414 from Kenora (CYQK), ON, to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON, with 2 crew onboard. During final approach into CYQT at approximately 9 nautical miles from Runway 12, the flight crew powered back the engine and the aircraft's engine started vibrating. The flight crew pitched the nose up to gain altitude and observed abnormally high engine internal turbine temperature (ITT) and high NG (gas generator) on the engine gauges with no corresponding increase in engine power. The crew acknowledged the abnormality, declared an emergency and manually shutdown the engine. The crew continued the glide and landed the aircraft safely on Runway 12. The pilot taxied off the runway with remaining momentum. There were no reported injuries and no further damage to the aircraft. The aircraft was towed to the hangar for further inspection.The operator's maintenance inspection indicated that blades separated from the PT2 disc at the root. The engine is being sent to Pratt & Whitney Canada for further inspection.

C-FLWK, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800 conducting flight SWG514 was at 3000 feet AGL and 10 miles from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, when the flight crew reported a momentary loss of control due to wake turbulence, resulting in the aircraft banking in excess of 45 degrees, pitching downward, and losing 300 feet in altitude. The flight crew regained control and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FPWR, a Beech B300 aircraft operated by Churchill Falls (Labrador) Corporation Ltd., was conducting an approach into Churchill Falls (CZUM), NL. During the flight, the crew experienced intermittent illumination of the right prop pitch light, indicating that a yaw could occur upon touchdown. The crew contacted maintenance, reviewed the procedure and then contacted company management. The decision was made to have emergency services on standby as a precaution. Upon landing, the aircraft experienced a slight yaw, but no further issues were reported. Maintenance found a defective proximity switch on the right engine. The proximity switch was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FPWR, a Beech B300 aircraft operated by Churchill Falls (Labrador) Corporation Ltd., was conducting a VFR approach into Churchill Falls (CZUM), NL. At about 500 feet AGL, with the aircraft fully configured for landing, the aircraft abruptly veered to the right when the power was reduced. The crew conducted an overshoot and troubleshot. The crew returned for another approach and landed without further incident at CZUM. Maintenance found a worn bolt on the ground idle solenoid, which was subsequently replaced. The company has entered this event into their SMS program.

C-FYPN, un Boeing 737-2T4 exploité par Chrono Jet inc., effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) à destination de l'aéroport d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) avec 6 membres d'équipage et 86 passagers à bord. Environ 12 minutes après le décollage de CYHU, alors que l'appareil était en montée vers son altitude de croisière, l’équipage a observé une indication de chute de pression d’huile du moteur numéro 2 (PW JT8D-17). Peu après, le voyant de pression d’huile (LOW OIL PRESSURE) s’est allumé. L'équipage a actionné la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a fermé le moteur par mesure préventive. L’aéronef est retourné à CYHU où il a atterri sans encombre.

C-FWZV, a Viking Air Ltd. DHC-7-100 series aircraft operated by Air Tindi, was conducting flight TIN242 from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Hay River, NT (CYHY) with 3 crew members and 11 passengers on board.  Approximately 24 nm NE of CYHY, the flight crew noticed that the #1 hydraulic system had failed. Air Tindi operations and maintenance were contacted, and the decision was made to return to CYZF.  During the approach into CYZF, the crew declared a PAN PAN with air traffic services and performed an uneventful flapless landing.

C-GJTX, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321 was conducting flight ROU1679 from Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  On initial climb in vicinity of BLOSM Waypoint, Flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to ''Level off''. Flight crew complied with the RA and had the traffic visual.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GCPI, a Bell 429 helicopter operated by the Canadian Coast Guard, was conducting external load operations to the Westhaver Island Lighthouse from a nearby shoreline staging area along Mahone Bay, NS. The helicopter was to sling a load of construction lumber using a 100-foot long-line. The load was secured with cargo and sling straps, and was inspected before slinging operations commenced. While in transit at about 40 KIAS approximately 10 two-by-four boards became loose in the straps and fell into the ocean. There were no injuries, and no damage to the helicopter.Transport Canada Aircraft Services Directorate is conducting an investigation.

C-GCNJ, a privately-registered Piper PA-28-140, was conducting a local flight from Winnipeg/Lyncrest (CJL5), MB with 1 person on board. During the landing at CJL5, C-GCNJ inadvertently landed on the unprepared surface parallel to Runway 09. The aircraft's nose wheel dug into the snow, collapsing the nose gear, and the propeller struck the ground. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the nose gear and propeller and there were no reported injuries.

C-IKGW, an Xstream Sport Aviation Tecnam P2004 Bravo (advanced ultralight) was on a flight with an instructor and student on board. The aircraft was landing on Runway 34 at the Midland Huronia Airport (CYEE), and the student was the flying pilot. After a hard touchdown the right main landing gear collapsed, and the aircraft came to stop on the runway. There were no injuries to either occupant.

N675BA, a Berry Aviation Inc. de Havilland DHC-6 Twin Otter, was on a flight from Great Falls (KGTF), MT to Calgary (CYYC), AB for a major refit, when the aircraft experienced a hydraulic failure affecting the nose wheel steering. The nose wheel had not centered on departure from KGTF due to an unrelated issue, so the tiller indicated that the nose wheel was 45 degrees to the left. On arrival to the CYYC area the crew did not declare an emergency but requested ARFF, and that the runway be foamed. The aircraft landed in the foam uneventfully, the nose wheel centered, and the aircraft taxied under its own power to the west hangar area. Maintenance Update: The aircraft was being ferried to CYYC for a complete refit at Regent Aircraft Services Inc. On arrival at the facility, it was noted that the there was a lot of hydraulic fluid in the "hell hole" area, where the hydraulic pump is situated. The aircraft will be out of service for some time undergoing a complete overhaul prior to going out on another deployment.

C-GJZH, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA7999 from Moncton/Romeo LeBlanc Intl (CYQM), NB to Montréal/Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. While enroute at approximately 25 nm northeast of Fredericton Intl (CYFC), NB, the flight crew was setting cruise power and inadvertently decreased the propeller condition levers briefly below the MIN/850 position. The crew then observed a number 1 propeller overspeed indication, and a #1 PEC annunciation (number 1 propeller electronic control malfunction). The crew then followed the quick reference handbook (QRH) instructions for PROPELLER OVERSPEED, and the number 1 propeller feathered. The crew then actioned the QRH instructions for ENGINE FAILURE/FIRE/SHUTDOWN, and shut down the number 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW150A). The crew declared an emergency (MAYDAY) and elected to divert to CYFC where the aircraft made a single-engine landing without further incident. There were no injuries.Company maintenance conducted overspeed governor checks, which tested serviceable. It was determined that the inadvertent decrease of the condition levers below the MIN/850 position caused the Automatic Underspeed Protection Circuit to activate for the number 1 propeller.

C-GJZZ, a Jazz Aviation LP MHI RJ Aviation ULC CRJ-200ER was conducting flight JZA839 from Raleigh/Durham Intl (KRDU), NC to Toronto/Lester b. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  On initial climb, flight crew declared an emergency due to anti ice issue.  Flight crew elected to burn fuel and returned to KRDU where it landed without further incident.

C-FGKN, an Air Canada Airbus A321 operating as flight AC192 was on approach into Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, when the fight crew received an ECAM message "Green Hydraulic Sys Low". A go around was initiated to troubleshoot the fault. During the second approach, a PAN PAN was declared and the flight landed without further incident.

C-FSIQ, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8, operating as flight AC737 departed Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Shortly after departure, the flight crew received a master caution #1 IRS Fault. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight returned to YYZ, where it landed without further incident.

C-GIJZ, un De Havilland DHC8-402 exploité par Jazz Aviation sous l’indicatif JZA8011, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination d’Ottawa/McDonald Cartier, ON (CYOW). Peu après le décollage, lors de la rétraction du train d’atterrissage, une indication de portes de train d’atterrissage ouvertes est apparue accompagnée du voyant du capteur de référence air-sol (weight on wheel). La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée et le train d’atterrissage a été déployé avec succès. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) et est revenu atterrir à CYUL, où l'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre.

C-FYBK, a Swoop Airlines Boeing 737-800 was operating as flight WSW101 from Hamilton (CYHM), ON to Edmonton (CYEG), AB. On approach into CYEG, a flight attendant sustained a burn to their hand while pouring hot water. First aid treatment was provided by the cabin crew; the injured flight attendant was not able to continue with their duties for the arrival. EMS met the aircraft, and the flight attendant was removed from service.

C-GEDV, an Upper Valley Aviation Limited Beech Aircraft Corporation King Air 200, was conducting a flight from Jackson Hole (KJAC), WY, U.S., to Kelowna (CYLW), BC.  Approximately 14 nautical miles (NM) northeast of CYLW, air traffic control (ATC) cancelled the standard arrival (STAR) and instructed the flight crew to maintain present heading for vectors to follow a King Air medevac from the north. C-GEDV was at an altitude of 9000 feet above sea level (ASL). C-FRRQ, a North Cariboo Flying Services Limited Beech Aircraft Corporation King Air 200, operating as flight NCB580, was conducting a medevac flight from Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC, to CYLW. At 1501:55 Pacific Standard Time (PST), C-FRRQ was approximately 30 NM north of CYLW at 12 600 feet ASL when the flight crew received a clearance to conduct the RNAV V RWY 16 approach to CYLW. At 1504:55, C-GEDV was to the east of and abeam the runway at 9000 feet ASL. When C-FRRQ was approximately 15 nautical miles on final, ATC directed C-GEDV to turn to a heading of 080°, which was acknowledged by the pilot. At 1505:17, the crew of C-GEDV was instructed to turn to a heading of 240° and to descend to 8000 feet ASL. At 1505:59, C-GEDV was directed to stop descent at 8500 feet ASL. At 1506:21, 20 nautical miles (NM) north-northwest of CYLW, a loss of separation occurred. Separation was 800 feet vertically and 4.9 NM horizontally when the required separation was 5 NM or 1000 feet. The required separation was regained at 1506:31 and maintained.

C-GKWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. Dash 8-400, operating as WEN3281 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Penticton (CYYF), BC was at the gate as the flight crew prepared the aircraft for the flight. As the first officer (FO) was doing their walk around, the FO noticed smoke coming from the auxiliary power unit in the tail of the aircraft. Flight crew members informed maintenance who used a portable fire extinguisher to douse the flames. The flight crew ensured that all power was turned off. Airport fire and rescue (ARFF) were called and attended the scene. There were no passengers onboard at the time. The aircraft was taken out of service. Maintenance update: The aircraft is out of service awaiting replacement of relay K26 (the auxiliary power unit start relay), which was found welded closed, and the cable assembly, which showed signs of heat stress. The operator is working with the manufacturer to complete the investigation and repairs.

C-GKIX, un Pilatus PC-12/45 exploité par Keewatin Air LP effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Arctic Bay, NU (CYAB) à destination d’Igloolik, NU (CYGT). En approche vers CYGT, l’équipage a sélectionné la position sortie du train d’atterrissage et la lumière d’avertissement du train d’atterrissage gauche au tableau de bord est restée allumée. L’équipage a sélectionné la position rentrée et à nouveau la position sortie dans le but de verrouiller le train d’atterrissage gauche sans succès. Une approche interrompue a été initiée et l’équipage a décidé de procéder vers Iqaluit, NU (CYFB), l’aéroport de dégagement. En route vers CYFB, 2 tentatives de verrouiller le train d’atterrissage selon la procédure d’urgence établie ont échoué. Après une consultation avec l’équipe de maintenance de la compagnie aérienne, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence au personnel du service d’information en vol (FSS) de CYFB et a demandé de confirmer visuellement la position du train d’atterrissage lors d’un passage bas avant d’atterrir. Le train de gauche étant sorti, un atterrissage de précaution avec un arrêt sur la piste 34 a été effectué avec succès. Les véhicules d’urgence et de maintenance de la compagnie aérienne ont été à la rencontre de l’aéronef qui a été remorqué par la suite. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FDWM, a Beech B200C operated by Keewatin Air LP, had departed from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB for a maintenance test flight following work regarding a landing gear issue (see TSB occurrence A23C0007). During the flight while testing the landing gear system, the nose gear did not come down when selected. The flight crew completed a manual gear extension with all three-landing gear now down and locked. The flight crew declared an emergency, returned to CYWG, landed safely and shut down on the runway. The aircraft returned to the maintenance base without incident. There were no injuries to crew or passengers and there was no damage to the aircraft. The operator's maintenance found that the landing gear power pack bleed air check valve was faulty and was not allowing bleed air pressure into power pack reservoir.  They replaced faulty check valve and the landing gear was cycled multiple times, including emergency extension system, and the system was functioning. A successful test flight was completed on March 4, 2023, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GNVR, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight SWG538 from Cancun Intl. (MMUN), Mexico to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC. During cruise over Gulf of Mexico, a cabin crew became incapacitated. Incapacitated cabin crew was replaced by cabin crew on staff travel for landing and flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GSPW, un Boeing 737-275C exploité par Air Inuit Ltée, sous l’indicatif AIE753, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Val d’Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de Kattiniq-Donaldson, QC (CTP9). Établi en vol de croisière à 31 000 pieds, l’équipage a observé l’apparition d’une craque dans le pare-brise du côté du commandant de bord. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence au contrôleur de l’unité de contrôle aérien (ATC) et a demandé d’amorcer une descente en direction de l’aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT). Après avoir effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et établi que le dommage se situait à la partie extérieure du pare-brise L1, la procédure spécifiait de continuer les opérations normales. L’équipage a donc contacté l’ATC pour annuler l’urgence et a décidé de dérouter le vol vers l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GQCL, a Springbank Air Training College Cessna C172P, was conducting a student flown solo cross country flight from Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB to High River Airport (CEN4), AB, with 1 crew member on board. During a crosswind landing the pilot experienced a loss of directional control which resulted in a runway excursion to the left side of the runway. The pilot attempted a go-around; however, the left main gear entered deep snow on the runway edge and the aircraft veered further to the left. The propeller and right wing struck the ground, and the aircraft was substantially damaged. There were no injuries.The aircraft was repaired by company maintenance personal and returned to service.

N825MH, Boeing 767-400 operated by Delta Airlines, was conducting flight DAL04 from London Heathrow International Airport (LHR), UK to John F. Kenndy International Airport (KJFK), New York, USA. During cruise, the crew observed a fluctuation of the command speed bugs and an increase in IAS on both PFD’s.  The crew actioned the QRH for unreliable airspeed and contacted maintenance control (MC). The crew was told to reset the thrust management computer, switch autopilot, and use VNAV mode. An hour later, while in Canadian airspace, the crew observed the same fault on the right PFD and the illumination of the Pitch Limit Indicator. The crew actioned the QRH and contacted MC and flight dispatch, making the decision to declare an emergency and divert to Bangor International Airport (KBGR), Maine, USA. Shortly after the crew observed a left hydraulic quantity low indication and completed the QRH procedure. On the approach to landing the crew notice flap asymmetry during flap extension and completed that QRH item. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance traveled to KBGR and found a hydraulic leak in the pump filter in the left engine pylon. Maintenance removed and replaced the right air data module (ADM). The aircraft remains unserviceable while the hydraulic leak is investigated.

C-FSBV, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was conducting flight AC64 from Incheon Intl. (RKSI), Republic of Korea to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC.  On initial climb, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory).  Flight crew complied with RA and continued to destination without further incident.

C-FYZS, a Pilatus PC-12/45 operated by North Star Air Ltd. was conducting flight BF706 from Thunder Bay (CYQT) ON. to Kingfisher Lake (CNM5) ON. The aircraft was leveling off at flight level 230 when the flight crew noticed both fuel pumps were cycling "ON" and "OFF" when in the "AUTO POSITION". There was no audible or visual indication of low fuel pressure. The flight crew selected both left- and right-hand fuel pumps to the "ON" position. An emergency was declared and a return to CYQT was requested. The aircraft landed without incident in CYQT. The operator's maintenance found during troubleshooting that the EFIS display unit had failed. The unit was replaced, and a successful test flight was completed. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTZU, an Airbus A220-300 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC205 from Calgary International (CYYC), AB, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 5 crew members and 138 passengers on board. During the landing roll, after touchdown, the crew observed an uncommanded shutdown of the No.2 engine (Pratt & Whitney-USA, PW1524G3) with multiple Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) messages. The crew completed appropriate checklists and taxied to their gate on the remaining engine. The passengers deplaned normally. Maintenance replaced the W03 and W04 harness wires, as well as the N2 sensor. The engine was then tested successfully and returned to service.

C-FRHZ, a Beech King Air B200 operated by PAL Aerospace Ltd. as Speed Air 02, was conducting a patrol flight from St John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL. During the takeoff, the crew received an IAS and shortly after an ALT mis-compare warning annunciator. Once the crew were airborne, they contacted maintenance and completed the QRH. The crew changed the air data source to ADC2 and requested to return to CYYT.  ARFF was placed on standby, and the aircraft landed without incident.

C-FRTW, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 (Dreamliner) was conducting flight AC64 from Incheon International (RKSI), Seoul, Republic of Korea, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 12 crew and 300 passengers on board. After landing in CYVR, with the aircraft at the gate and the passengers deplaning, the ground crew noticed the left main gear showing smoke with a small fire present. The crew was advised and a rapid deplanement was conducted for the remaining passengers. An aircraft rescue and firefighting crew attended the scene to monitor the situation. No retardant was used, and the smoke and fire extinguished on its own.Maintenance conducted an inspection and replaced the No. 5 wheel assembly and the No. 5 brake assembly. Both assemblies that were removed have been sent for further inspection.

C-GBJZ, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8140 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB with 4 crew members and 68 passengers on board. During final approach the Transformer Rectifier Unit (TRU) master caution illuminated along with several other lights. A pop was heard, and a flight attendant reported a puff of smoke coming from the Passenger Control Unit (PCU) above seat 15 in the passenger cabin. The flight landed without incident.Following the flight, company maintenance found the 9811 / J711 electrical connector in the left hand wing root area, part number MS3450L24-11S, was shorted / burnt through; the connector was replaced (in the left hand wing root area - JD's note). A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) was filed with Transport Canada.

C-GALH, an Alpine Helicopters Incorporated Bell Textron Canada Limited 206L-3 (Longranger III) helicopter, was conducting snow safety support for heli-ski operations 21 nautical miles southwest of Valemount, BC (CAH4), with 1 pilot and 1 ski guide on board. The snow safety support helicopter supports the primary helicopter that carries the ski guests, establishes landing sites and ski runs, and assesses snow conditions for the operation. Prior to takeoff, the pilot and the guide agreed to establish a new landing site to pick up skiers at the end of a specific ski run. On arrival in the area, the pilot and the guide surveyed the terrain for an appropriate landing site based on visibility, lighting conditions, reference objects, and profile. Being a new landing site, there were no reference stakes established. The pilot identified a landing site immediately right of a convex roll and flew 0.4 nautical miles northwest to set up a south-southeast approach to the site. The pilot maneuvered the helicopter in a low angle descent with a slow forward speed in anticipation of whiteout conditions on touchdown. The helicopter skids contacted the ground - first the left skid and then the right skid - and, as the pilot reduced the collective input to settle the aircraft, the aircraft leaned to the right. The pilot arrested the collective reduction. The helicopter was now engulfed in blowing snow with no visibility in the created whiteout. The aircraft rolled forward and to the right, coming to rest on its right side, perpendicular to the direction of travel. The main rotor contacted the ground and the engine stopped running shortly thereafter. The pilot turned off the master power, closed the fuel shutoff valve, and manually activated the ELT. The pilot and the guide egressed out the front windshield that had partially broken on impact. The pilot noticed some fuel spilling out of the airframe fuel vent and placed a plastic bin under the vent to capture it. The helicopter was substantially damaged. The guide contacted the heli-ski lodge personnel with a handheld FM radio to activate the emergency response plan and the primary helicopter operating in the area arrived on scene approximately 5 minutes later. The pilot received minor injuries from the impact and egress. Both occupants were wearing helmets and four-point safety belts.The helicopter was recovered to the company's hangar where the damage will be assessed.

C-FZAT, a privately registered Nanchang CJ6A, was conducting a flight from Langley (CYNJ), BC, to Duncan (CAM3), BC, with only the pilot on board. On arrival, the aircraft touched down approximately 350 feet past the threshold of Runway 31. During the landing roll, the pilot applied the brakes but was unable to stop the aircraft before reaching the end of the runway. The aircraft rolled off the end of the runway and down a short embankment before the nose impacted flat ground. The emergency locator transmitter activated and the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre was alerted. There were no reported injuries and no post impact fire. Emergency services were not dispatched to the site. The aircraft was substantially damaged and a minor fuel leak was contained.The aircraft was recovered by a crane truck and repositioned to the airfield for further assessment.

C-FZUG, an Air Canada Rouge A319-114 was conducting flight ROU1696 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL. During the descent phase of the flight, while operating on the CUDUA2 STAR in the vicinity of CUUDA, at approximately 8000 ft ASL, the flight crew received, and complied with, a TCAS RA "LEVEL OFF" instruction. The ATC was advised, and the flight was subsequently completed without further incident.

C-FHCM, a WestJet Boeing 737-8 MAX was operating as WJA1681 from John F Kennedy Intl Airport (KJFK), NY to Calgary Intl Airport (CYYC), AB with 6 crew members and 165 passengers on board. During the take-off roll the flight crew heard a noise coming from the nose wheel. On the initial climb out the flight crew selected the landing gear up and they observed an abnormal indication with the nose landing gear. The flight crew were able to trouble shoot the condition and continued to destination. Approximately 1 hour before landing, WestJet dispatch called CYYC tower to advise them of the landing gear issue on WJA1681. The flight crew subsequently declared a PAN PAN with a request to stop on the runway and to be towed to the gate after landing; ARFF was dispatched. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 17L and taxied under its own power to the gate.Company maintenance found that the nose landing gear pressure seals failed during the takeoff roll. Loss of pressure in the oleo kept the strut compressed and unable to center before retracting into the gear well. The seals were replaced and an SDR was submitted to Transport Canada. The aircraft was released for continued service.

C-GKFS, a Kelowna Flightcraft Air Charter Limited Convair 340 (Convair 5800) was operating as KFA581, a repositioning flight from Kelowna (CYLW), BC, to Vancouver (CYVR), BC, with 2 crew onboard. Approximately 50 NM northeast of CYVR, the crew noticed the No. 1 engine power section oil pressure indication was above limits. The crew completed the required emergency checklist and completed a precautionary engine shutdown of the No. 1 engine. The crew declared an emergency and continued to CYVR where they landed safely with aircraft rescue and firefighting teams on standby. Maintenance determined that the power section oil pump pressure regulator required adjustment as per the aircraft maintenance manual. After the adjustments were made, engine ground runs were accomplished and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBKB, an Aurora Jet Partners Challenger 605, was conducting a flight from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to Scottsdale Airport (KSDL), AZ. While on descent to KSDL, clearance was given to descend to 7000ft. ATC Vector was given to turn right to heading 210 to avoid traffic. Upon read back, pilot flying (PF) noted that the Vector turned the aircraft towards traffic on TCAS already. The pilot monitoring (PM) confirmed heading with ATC (Phoenix Approach) and ATC confirmed "Correct heading and stop descent for traffic". Approximately 5-10 seconds after the turn, a TCAS "traffic" warning was heard. PF could see closure with traffic, ATC advised "further right for traffic". The PF disconnected the autopilot, continued the right turn and then got a TA/RA "don't descend" followed by a climb indication and "climb" audible command. The PM saw the red traffic at 300ft below. Shortly after following the RA, a "clear of traffic" was heard. The ATC was busy on the radio, the PM was not able to advise ATC of TA/RA. ATC's next call was that the aircraft was clear of traffic and given heading 180 and descend to 5300ft. The PM called the field in sight and eventually passed to KSDL tower. The approach and landing were carried safely.

Icelandair flight FI603, a Boeing 737-9 (registration, TF-ICA) aircraft, was on approach to Toronto, ON (CYYZ) Runway 33R when a glide slope fluctuation caused the autopilot to disconnect. The flight crew continued flying the approach manually. The aircraft deviated above the glide slope (GS) in the later part of the approach, as a result the pilot flying (PF) increased the rate of decent. Just prior to the point of flare, the flight crew increased the nose up pitch to slow the aircraft, but the aircraft touched down hard and bounced. The PIC called for a go around after the bounce and the aircraft was brought around for a second approach. The aircraft landed without further incident. The next flight crew noticed that the tail skid was damaged on their walkaround. Maintenance confirmed the tail skid crush cartridge needed to be replaced, there was no other damage to aircraft.

C-FEIQ, un Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7122, effectuait un vol de mise en place selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Halifax/Stanfield Int’l, NS (CYHZ) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Alors que l’avion se trouvait en courte finale de la piste 24R, l’équipage a perçu l’alarme du détecteur de fumée de la toilette et a avisé l’ATC. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés et l’aéronef a été inspecté. Il n’y avait aucune trace de feu, de fumée, ni d’odeur. L’appareil a ensuite circulé normalement jusqu'à la porte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FCVD, un Pilatus PC-12/45 par exploité par Chrono Aviation inc. sous l’indicatif NDL543, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Lebel-sur-Quévillon, QC (CSH4) à destination de Bagotville, QC (CYBG) avec 8 passagers et 2 membres d’équipage. En passant le niveau de vol 190 en montée, l’équipage a noté que la pression de cabine s’approchait de 10 000 pieds. Le commandant a déclaré un état d’urgence et a demandé une descente immédiate auprès de l’ATC. L’aéronef a été mis en palier à 10 000 pieds et il a continué son vol à destination de CYBG sans encombre. Il n’y a aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GNVR, a Sunwing Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight SWG312 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON to Santa Clara/Abel Santamaria Airport (MUSC), Cuba. While flying in Washington Airspace at FL340, a TCAS RA was received by the flight crew, instructing to descend. The crew subsequently complied with the RA, descending by approximately 300-500 feet, where the "Level Off" command was received. At nearly the same time as the TCAS Descend command, ATC instructed the crew to turn to a 290-degree heading. After descending, the crew reconfirmed the heading with ATC and was advised a 250-degree heading, to which they complied and climbed back up to FL340. The flight continued safely to destination.

C-FWEZ, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was conducting flight WEN3298 from Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 4 crew and 78 passengers on board. During the initial climb, the crew received an indication that the left main gear had not retracted as required. The crew actioned the quick reference handbook, completed a manual gear extension and returned to CYXS. The crew requested Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting services to be on standby and landed safely. There were no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft. Maintenance installed the landing gear pins and the aircraft was ferried to CYVR with the landing gear extended for further inspection. Maintenance found air in both the number 1 and number 2 hydraulic reservoirs. The air was removed, the systems were serviced with hydraulic fluid and the landing gear retraction system was function tested serviceable. The landing gear pins were removed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

The crew of Jet Linx Aviation flight JTL904, a Learjet 45 (N904HD) aircraft, on a flight from Omaha, Nebraska (KOMA) to Toronto, ON (CYYZ) declared an emergency in Toronto airspace due to a left engine (Honeywell (Garrett) TFE731) shutdown. The crew had initially received a "LOW OIL" caution alert, and then a subsequent master warning "LOW OIL pressure" alert. After carrying out the QRH checklist the engine was intentionally shutdown. The flight crew elected to continue towards CYYZ and landed without further incident. Maintenance found the L/H engine oil fill cap was loose and O-ring damaged.

C- FRAM, un Boeing 777-300ER exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA51, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Indira Gandhi International Airport en Inde (VIDP) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 289 passagers et 16 membres d’équipage. En vol de croisière à environ 35 miles marins au nord-est de Baie-Comeau, QC, le commandant de bord est devenu malade et fut remplacé par le commandant supplémentaire de cet équipage de conduite renforcé. L’appareil s’est posé à CYUL sans encombre et il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GUBH, an Air Transat A330 was operating flight TSC357 from Holguin/Frank Pais Airport (MUHG), Cuba to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. About 22 minutes after takeoff from MUHG, upon reaching FL340, the cabin crew reported to the flight crew that floors seemed to be overheating and smell of electrical wires burning in the cabin. The flight Crew immediately initiated the Smoke/Fumes procedures, declared a PANPAN and diverted to Nassau/Lynden Pindling International Airport (MYNN), Bahamas and landed safely.

C-GVEN, a WestJet Encore de Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was conducting flight WEN3532 from Kamloops (CYKA), BC, to Calgary Intl.(CYYC), AB, with 4 crewmembers and 74 passengers on board. While transitioning from their climb to a cruise altitude of 25 000 feet above sea level (ASL), the crew heard a loud bang. The pilot disengaged the autopilot and the crew saw the No. 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney-Canada PW150A) torque was decreasing with the inter-turbine temperature (ITT) rising above limits. This was shortly followed by a No. 2 engine fire warning. The flight crew declared a MAYDAY emergency with air traffic control (ATC) and actioned the checklist from the quick reference handbook (QRH). The engine was shutdown and secured. The flight crew did not discharge the fire suppressant as there was no indication of fire. The crew requested a diversion to Kelowna (CYLW), BC. ATC cleared the flight CYLW where it landed safely. There were no injuries.

C-FSDQ, an Air Canada B737-8 was conducting flight AC991 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Mexico City International Airport (MMMX), MX. On approach, the crew received a TCAS RA. The Resolution Advisory (RA) was followed, and the aircraft continued to land without further incident.

C-GUBF, an Air Transat Airbus A330-243 was conducting flight 890 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Puerto Plata/Gregorio Luperón Intl. (MDPP) Dominican Republic.  In climb abeam Plattsburg Intl. (KPBG), NY, smoke could be seen coming out of forward galley #1 oven.  The power to the oven was turned off and circuit breaker pulled.  After getting the safety equipment nearby, flight attendant opened the oven door where more smoke was seen coming out.  After a few minutes first officer inspected the oven with nothing found.  The oven was not used for the reminder of the flight.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FGHZ, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 (Dreamliner), was conducting flight ACA004 from Narita/ New Tokyo Intl. (RJAA), Japan to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC, with 8 crew and 298 passengers on board. Approximately 4 hours 10 minutes into the trip, a flight attendant became ill. Cabin crew positions were reassigned according to standard operating procedures. The aircraft landed without further issues and was met by EMS.

C-FPQQ, un Beech KIng Air BE20 exploité par Keewatin Air LP sous l'indicatif KEW213, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport d'Arctic Bay, NU (CYAB) à destination de l'aéroport d'Iqaluit, NU (CYFB). Alors que l'aéronef se trouvait en vol de croisière, à environ 200 mn au nord de  CYFB, l'équipage a perçu des anomalies du moteur gauche, suivi d'une perte de régime. Lors de la descente vers le niveau de vol 175, une saute de régime moteur est survenue, suivie d'une perte de régime. Un arrêt préventif du moteur a été effectué. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et poursuivi le vol vers CYFB. L'atterrissage s'est déroulé sans encombre.

C-FNNC, a Beech Aircraft Corporation Beech 200 aircraft operated by North Cariboo Flying Service, was conducting flight NCB2093 from Medicine Hat Airport (CYXH), AB to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. C-FTMY, an Aerospatiale ATR 72-202 aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express Inc was conducting flight MAL8066 from Saskatoon John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (CYXE), AB to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. NCB2093 and MAL8066 were on parallel approaches to RWY 17R and 17L respectively. Separation decreased to 1.4 NM when not less than 2 NM is required during parallel runway operations. There was no risk of collision and no impact to operations.

C-GMVB, a C208B operated by Wilderness North Air, departed Nakina Airport (CYQN), ON, on 28 February 2023 at approximately 1245 EST on a VFR flight to Fort Hope Airport (CYFH), ON, with two pilots on board. At 1445 the aircraft was reported missing by the company, as it had not arrived at CYFH or returned to CYQN. JRCC was notified and a search for the aircraft began. The aircraft was located on 4 March 2023 approximately 30 miles north of CYQN, along the direct route to CYFH. The aircraft was destroyed and both occupants were fatally injured. The ELT had been removed for recertification.

C-FEKH, a Jazz Aviation LP Embraer ERL 170-200SU was conducting flight 8997 from LaGuardia Intl. (KLGA), NY to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During cruise at FL300 approximately 188nm ESE of CYYZ, flight crew received a ''BLEED 1 FAIL'' message.  As the #2 Bleed system was already deferred by maintenance, flight crew started a descent and started the APU.  Subsequently, flight crew declared a PANPAN at FL200 and initiated an emergency descent as cabin rose to FL100.  Flight crew stopped the descent at 10000 feet and requested priority handling as cabin was getting cold due to no heat.  Flight landed at CYYZ without further incident.

C-GDMP, a Swoop B737-8CT was conducting flight WSW646 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Kingston/Norman Manley International Airport (MKJP), Jamaica. When flying over Cuba, the crew reported a suspected fuel leak from #1 engine. The #1 engine was shut down in response to running the required checklist. A mayday was declared with a diversion plan to Varadero/Juan Gualberto Gómez International Airport (MUVR), Cuba. The flight landed safely in MUVR.The aircraft will remain grounded in MUVR until maintenance arrives to inspect and determine the required repairs.

C-GFXC, a Buffalo Airways Ltd. Lockheed L188 was operating as BFL1227 from Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), NWT to Goose Lake Airport (CGS2), NU with 3 crew members on board. During cruise the #2 Generator mechanical failure light illuminated; the crew then performed a precautionary shutdown of the #2 engine (Allision 501-D13) . The aircraft returned to Yellowknife and landed without further incident.Company maintenance replaced the #2 generator, and the aircraft was returned to service.

On 18 February 2023, an Air Canada Airbus A330-300 (registration C-GFAF) operating as ACA095, was enroute from El Dorado International Airport (SKBO) Bogota, Columbia to Toronto Lester B Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario. During the flight, the flight crew was advised of an unruly passenger on board. The decision was made to declare a Pan Pan emergency that required priority handling. ACA095 continued the flight to CYYZ and landed Runway 24R at 2028Z without incident. The aircraft was taxied to the gate where law enforcement authorities met the aircraft on arrival.

C-GDEW, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402, was operating as WEN3171 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Canadian Forces Base Comox (CYQQ), BC with 5 crew members and 78 passengers on board. After take-off the flight crew observed a loss of pressure in HYD #2 system, declared a PAN PAN and actioned the quick reference handbook (QRH). WEN3171 subsequently return to CYYC for an uneventful landing. Post landing inspection by company maintenance found both #1 and #2 HYD systems filled to the maximum level. Both systems were bled with multiple gear swings and flight control movements carried out; no pressure loss was noted. Aircraft returned to service.

On 16 February 2023, the WestJet Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737-7CT aircraft (registration C-GWCN, serial number 34157) was conducting flight WJA1447 from Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), Nevada, United States, to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), Alberta, with 5 crew members and 109 passengers. At approximately 1825 Pacific Standard Time, the aircraft took off while aligned with the right edge of Runway 01R, and its right nosewheel contacted 8 runway edge lights. The flight crew were unaware of the misaligned takeoff and subsequent contact with the edge lights, and the aircraft continued to CYEG, where it landed uneventfully. None of the passengers or crew members were injured. The next day, company maintenance noted minor damage to the right tire on the nose landing gear and replaced both nosewheel tires before releasing the aircraft back to service. The airport authority at KLAS discovered the damage to the runway edge lights 32 hours after the occurrence, and notified the operator of the damage to the runway edge lights 8 days after the occurrence. TSB investigated.

The privately registered, amateur-built, Zenair CH 601-XL-B, C-GHRG, was on a training flight at the High River (CEN4), AB with a student pilot and instructor on board. While conducting circuits,  a hard landing occurred during one of the touchdowns. The instructor took control and conducted a missed approach. Control was returned to the student pilot and the aircraft returned for a landing. The aircraft was taxied back to the hangar. Once the cowlings were removed it was noted that there was damage in the nose gear support structure requiring major repair before further flight. The necessary entries were made in the aircraft journey log. Maintenance Update: Replacement parts have been fabricated and repairs are underway.

C-GPCR, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited Beech 1900D aircraft was conducting a flight PCO1414 from Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC, to Victoria International (CYYJ), BC, with 2 crew and 15 passengers onboard. During final approach into CYYJ at approximately 500 feet above ground level and 1.5 nautical miles from runway 14, the flight crew received a master warning accompanied by a right engine oil pressure light on the warning panel. The crew acknowledged the warning and verified the oil pressure was rapidly decreasing on the right engine oil pressure gauge. The crew continued with the approach and reduced the right engine to idle. The aircraft landed safely and the pilot utilized partial reverse on the left engine and assertive braking on the right main wheel to bring the aircraft to a stop on the runway. The right engine (Pratt & Whitney-Canada PT6A-67D) was shut down and, with smoke and fluid evident on the right side, the crew requested emergency fire services. The left engine was shut down and the crew initiated a rapid deplanement on the runway. Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting services attended the aircraft and no fire was reported. The right engine was leaking significant oil and the right outboard tire had failed during the landing roll. There were no reported injuries and no further damage to the aircraft. A NOTAM was issued and the runway was temporarily closed to tow the aircraft, clean up the fluid, and inspect the runway. Maintenance found that the forward external oil pressure elbow was cracked on the right engine resulting in the engine oil loss and low oil pressure. An SDR has been submitted by the operator. Due to the low oil pressure, the engine will be removed for an overhaul as per the maintenance manual.

C-GOIS, an Air Transat A321-271NX was conducting flight TSC113 from San José/Juan Santamaría Intl. (MROC), Costa Rica to Toronto Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During cruise portion of the flight over the USA, Relief pilot became incapacitated and was unable to provide relief to flying crew.  Flight landed in YYZ without further incident.

C-FSBV, un Boeing 787-9 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA097 au départ de l'aéroport de Sao Paulo/Guarulhos-Governador André Franco Montoro, Brésil (SBGR) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) avec 116 passagers et 11 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en descente à environ 25 nm au sud-sud-ouest de CYUL, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) en raison d’une indication de défaillance du mode d'opération primaire des becs de bord d'attaque (primary slats failure). L’équipage a effectué des vérifications et avisé l’ATC qu’il pourrait aussi y avoir un problème de roue de nez. L’avion a atterri sans encombre à 11:39z sur la piste 06 gauche.

C-FLUT, a Flair Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight F8 226 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), CA. While being vectored for ILS 28R visual approach (with parallel runway ops active), flight crew received a brief TCAS RA (resolution advisory) with traffic mutually in sight.  Flight landed without further incident.

C-FJCZ, un Cessna C550 exploité par Transports Canada sous l'indicatif TGO858, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Roberval, QC (CYRJ), à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Lors de la montée vers l'altitude de croisière, à environ 21 nm au sud de CYRJ, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison d’une perte de donnée du « air data computer #1 » (ADC1) dans le systéme de gestion de vol (FMS). Par conséquent, la navigation FMS, le système de dispositif avertisseur de proximité du sol (GPWS), le systéme de surveillance du trafic et d'évitement de collision (TCAS) et mode C des transpondeurs sont devenus hors-service. Le vol a continué vers CYUL où il s’est posé sans encombre à 21:10z.

C-FJXO, a Skylink Express Inc. Beech 1900C was conducting flight SLQ721 from Regina Intl. (CYQR), SK to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB. During the approach, the flight crew declared an emergency as the nose gear did not indicate down and locked. The aircraft circled the airport for a period of time and subsequently landed Runway 36 in CYWG with the nose gear up. There was observed minor damage to the nose of the aircraft and to its left propeller. There were no injuries. TSB investigators subsequently witnessed gear retraction tests at the operator's facility and observed the nose gear nitrogen charge had decreased such that the oleo piston collapsed once the gear was retracted into the nose gear compartment. In the collapsed position, the nose gear will not extend to the down-locked position due to interference with the nose gear compartment structure. A crushed frame member with an impression of the landing gear was found at FS 69.2 in the nose compartment. The nose gear oleo was disassembled with TSB present and no visible abnormalities were observed. The operator submitted a Service Difficulty Report.

C-FBIM un Boeing 737-247 exploité par Chrono Jet inc sous l'indicatif MBK721 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport d'Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) à destination de Resolute Bay, NU (CYRB). En croisière au niveau de vol 320, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison d’une pression anormale du moteur numéro 1 et a éteint le moteur. L’équipage a demandé un retour vers CYFB à 17 000 pieds. L’avion s’est posé sans encombre à 18:40z avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en attente près de la piste.

C-GVUH, un Airbus 220-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA314, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Vancouver, BC (CYVR), à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Durant le vol, le message d'avertissement « rudder fail » est apparu et l'équipage a déclaré une urgence auprès de l'unité de contrôle de la circulation aérienne. Le vol a continué vers CYUL à vitesse réduite où l’aéronef s'est posé sans encombre.

C-GGND, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was boarding flight 8204 scheduled from Sault Ste. Marie Airport (CYAM), ON to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON with 4 crew members and 74 passengers onboard. During the fueling operation, the refueling operator contacted the captain to mention that a switch was loose on the refuel/defuel control panel, and he was unable to fuel the aircraft. The captain subsequently met the operator at the panel where smoke and burnt wire smell were noticed coming from the panel. The captain returned to the cabin and instructed the cabin crew in charge to deplane rapidly and subsequently ran the emergency drill in the cockpit which includes shutting aircraft systems down and calling emergency services. The aircraft was deplaned between approximately 90-120 seconds. The pilots remained at the aircraft until the fire department arrived. The flight was cancelled and there was no reported injury.

C-FNTJ, a Diamond DA20-C1 aircraft operated by Moncton Flight College (MFC), had departed for a local solo training flight from Moncton/Roméo Leblanc Intl (CYQM), NB. Following the rollout after landing on Runway 29 at CYQM, the student pilot attempted to turn the aircraft to exit the runway at Taxiway Bravo and went off the hard surface. Due to icy patches beyond the paved area, aircraft directional control could not be maintained, and the aircraft right wing struck a taxiway sign. The student pilot was not injured. The right wing sustained structural damage that required major repair as a result of the contact with the sign.

C-FPVH, a privately registered Cessna 180G, was operating on a VFR flight itinerary for a local flight from Thunder Bay Intl (CYQT), ON with only the pilot on board. Due to engine roughness during the flight, the pilot elected to land on the frozen surface of Black Bay of Lake Superior, near the community of Dorion, Ontario. While on the landing roll, the aircraft nosed over in soft surface conditions in the landing zone. The aircraft came to rest upside down. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The pilot was uninjured.

C-GDMC, a privately registered ski-equipped Aeronca 11ACX, was conducting a flight from Little Bear Lake (CKL6), SK to Alsmith Lake, SK. During the landing roll on Alsmith Lake, the aircraft settled into deep snow and nosed over onto its back. The aircraft was substantially damaged. There were no injuries to the sole occupant/pilot.

C-GWEQ, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, was operating as WEN3127 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to Fort McMurray Airport (CYMM), AB with 4 crew members and 75 passengers on board. During the descent through FL180 the pitch trim caution light illuminated accompanied by the AUTO TRIM FAIL message. The flight crew actioned the quick reference handbook (QRH). The flight then informed ATC, declared a PAN PAN and requested ARFF to be present for landing. The flight landed without incident.The fault could not be duplicated on the ground and the system was tested serviceable. Due to the nature of the failure, the flight control electronic control unit (FCECU) was replaced and checked serviceable. The aircraft was returned to service.

N515EV, a Cessna 525A aircraft operated by Everair LLC, was conducting a flight from Lynden Pindling International Airport, Bahamas to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While on descent for landing into CYYZ, the crew declared a fuel emergency with ATC. Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) were notified of the emergency and the aircraft landed on runway 24L without further incident. The aircraft taxied under its own power to the FBO.

C-GSGY, a Sander Geophysics Ltd. was conducting local survey flight from Orange/New South Wales (YORG), Australia.  During cruise approximately 25nm SW of Canberra (YSCB), Australia, flight crew noticed mild odor similar to exhaust followed by faint smoke.  Flight crew decided to divert to YSCB and landed without further incident.  ARFF met with the aircraft and found nothing unusual.  Maintenance found loose AC belt that came out the drive when touched. After maintenance inspection, aircraft ferried to YORG with system deferred.  The AC drive belt had been replaced 25 hours prior during last inspection.

C-GJXE, an Airbus A220-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was boarding flight AC420 scheduled from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Montréal - Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC with 5 crews and 93 passengers. While approximately 75 percent of the passengers were already on board, the cabin filled with a white smoke. After an unsuccessful try to call the fire department on the radio frequency, the crew declared emergency (Mayday). The flight attendants subsequently executed a rapid deplanement via the bridge. There were no injuries reported and no fire discovered on board. A preliminary investigation conducted by maintenance revealed that during application at the gate, the di-icing fluid entered the Auxiliary power unit (APU) intake resulting in fumes to enter the cabin. Maintenance found the APU compartment contaminated with glycol and the bleed and air conditioning system were cleaned before returning in service.

C-GHQG, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was standing at gate D26 at Las Vegas/Harry Reid Intl. (KLAS) NV with crew on board.   Flight crew received a ''Smoke forward cargo'' on ECAM (Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitor).  Flight crew complied with ECAM instructions and maintenance and ARFF inspected the forward cargo.  Maintenance replaced C1 fire bottle and all 4 C1 smoke detectors and aircraft was returned to service.

C-GHPY, an Air Canada B787-8 was operating flight ACA956 from Juan Santamaria Airport (MROC), Costa Rica to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. On departure, the flight encountered severe turbulence which lasted approximately 5 seconds and had negative G. In discussion with dispatch the decision was made to continue to CYYZ. The flight continued without further incident. No injuries.A severe or unusual turbulence condition inspection was carried out IAW AMM. No damage found. Flight control test passed.

C-FLRS, a Boeing 737-8 Max aircraft operated by Flair Airlines Ltd, was at gate #3 at the Region of Waterloo International airport (CYKF), ON, undergoing baggage loading for flight F8576 to Cancun International Airport (MMUN), MX with 6 crew members and 148 passengers onboard. A belt loader at the aft hold of C-FLRS, was inadvertently put into forward gear and maneuvered under the aircraft causing damage to the aircraft belly skin, the cargo door bear strap and the forward and aft scuff plates. The belt loader traveled completely underneath the aircraft with the agent on the unit and exited behind the wing on the left side causing the agent to fall off the loader. The belt loader continued forward across the ramp to gate #2 striking C-GFEH, a parked Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines. The agent received minor injuries.

C-GFAF, an Air Canada Airbus A330-300 was conducting flight ACA0094 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Bogota/El Nuevo Dorado Intl. (SKBO), Colombia.  During descent approximately 100NM north of SKBO, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) ''monitor vertical speed'' with no actions required.  flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FIAI, un De Havilland DHC8-314 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE802 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de de Kuujjuarapik, QC (CYGW), avec 3 membres d'équipage et 18 passagers à bord. En vol de croisière, un membre d'équipage de conduite est tombé malade. Après avoir contacté la compagnie, le vol a été dérouté vers La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL). Le membre d’équipage a été en mesure de poursuivre partiellement ses fonctions. L’avion s’est posé sans encombre à CYGL.

C-FJBO, a Jazz Aviation LP Embraer RJ 170-200 SU was conducting flight 8639 from LaGuardia (KLGA), NY to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC.  During initial climb at 12000 feet, flight crew heard a loud percussive bang and notice first officer's windshield had shattered.  Flight crew stopped the climb, declared a PANPAN with ATC and diverted back to KLGA where it landed without further incident.

C-FDWM, a Beech B200C operated by Keewatin Air LP, had departed from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB for a maintenance test flight. During the flight, the flight crew noticed that the HYD FLUID LOW annunciator illuminated for approximately five seconds and extinguished on its own. The crew consulted the aircraft Quick Reference Handbook and performed the necessary actions. On the return to CYWG, the crew attempted to lower the landing gear; however, the landing gear control red light illuminated and there were no green lights. The crew noted that the landing gear relay circuit breaker had popped. The crew performed required actions from the aircraft Quick Reference Handbook and were able to get the two main landing gear down and locked by pumping the alternate gear extension handle. The alternate gear extension handle would not build any resistance and they could not get the nose gear down and locked indication. The crew then elected to reset the landing gear relay circuit breaker and the nose gear then indicated down and locked. The crew declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport (CYWG), landed safely and shut down the aircraft on the runway. There were no injuries to crew or passengers and there was no damage to the aircraft.The aircraft was then towed to the operator’s maintenance base for troubleshooting. A subsequent test flight after maintenance produced similar results also requiring an emergency landing (TSB occurrence A23C0012). The operator’s maintenance troubleshooting is ongoing.

C-FLDX, a Flair Airlines Ltd. was conducting flight F8188 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Phoenix-Mesa Gateway Airport (KIWA), AZ.  During visual approach runway 12, ATC advised flight crew of a traffic on approach runway 12.  Flight crew did not have traffic visual and shortly thereafter received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to ''monitor vertical speed''.  Flight crew complied with RA and landed without further incident.

OK-TSU, a Boeing 737-8FZ operated by Smartwings, was conducting flight SWG486 from Puerto Vallarta/Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz Intl (MMPR), Mexico to Regina Intl (CYQR), SK. While on approach to land at CYQR, the crew conducted a missed approach. During the climb to the go around altitude of 5000 feet ASL, the reserve fuel warning annunciated. The crew declared a PAN PAN for fuel quantity. The original alternate airport for the flight was Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG); however, the crew determined that a closer alternate, Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK, was available due to favourable weather conditions at CYXE. The crew determined that they had enough fuel to attempt a second approach into CYQR. Another approach at CYQR was conducted and the aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-GKSH, un hélicoptère Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 exploité par Go Hélico inc., effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Tasiujaq, QC (CYTQ), à destination de Kangirsuk, QC (CYAS) avec 2 personnes et le pilote à bord. Alors qu'il se trouvait environ 10 nm à l'ouest de CYAS, du brouillard étant présent dans les environs de l'aéroport, le pilote a manoeuvré l'hélicoptère à vitesse réduite à environ 15-30 pieds du sol le long de la rivière pour tenter de se rendre à destination. Après avoir parcouru environ 2,5 nm, le pilote avait de la difficulté à maintenir le contrôle de l'hélicoptère et devait maintenir la puissance au-dessus du maximum permis pour maintenir l'hélicoptère en vol. Il a manoeuvré l’hélicoptère pour effectuer un atterrissage de précaution et, alors qu'il cherchait un endroit pour se poser, les patins ont percuté des blocs de glace. Le pilote réussi à atterrir l'hélicoptère en bordure de la rivière. Une fois au sol, de la glace a été observée sur les pales principales et celles du rotor de queue. Des dommages aux patins ont aussi été observés. Après avoir déglacé l'hélicoptère à deux reprises, le pilote a décollé et effectué une montée verticale pour sortir du brouillard. Il s'est ensuite dirigé vers Quataq, QC (CYHA). Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GFCH, un Airbus 320 exploité par Air Canada Rouge LP sous l'indicatif ROU1952, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Toronto/Lester B.Pearson, ON (CYYZ) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec 118 passagers et 6 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de l'approche pour la piste 24 à CYQB, une fois en finale sous 1000 pieds, l'équipage a reçu un avis de trafic TCAS RA DESCEND en raison d’un trafic VFR dans le circuit.
