L'équipage a immédiatement suivi les directives et l'avion s’est ensuite posé sans encombre. Aucun blessé.

C-GLQE a Porter Airlines de Havilland DHC-8-402 operating as Flight POE2284 from Halifax, NS (CYHZ) executed a missed approach at Billy Bishop, ON (CYTZ) due to a gear problem. The aircraft was placed in a holding pattern over Lake Ontario to trouble shoot. The flight crew declared an emergency, requested a diversion to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport, ON (CYYZ) and requested emergency vehicles on standby. The aircraft was given priority and landed without incident on Runway 23.

C-FMOC, a Morningstar Air Express Inc. Boeing 757-200 was operating as MAL7051 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB with 2 flight crew and 1 passenger on board. While on initial approach into CYYC several engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS) warnings were triggered. The flight crew was unable to silence some of the warnings. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with air traffic services on final approach for Runway 17R and conducted a missed approach. The aircraft subsequently landed on Runway 29 without incident. Company maintenance changed the proximity switch electronic unit (PSEU) and returned the aircraft to service.

C-GSJB, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-112 was conducting flight ROU1639 from Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL to Montreal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC.  Approximately 10 minutes after takeoff a cabin crew became incapacitated.  Order of priority was reassigned, and flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FHCJ, un Boeing 767 exploité par Cargojet Airways Ltd sous l’indicatif CJT470, effectuait un vol cargo selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW) à destination d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) avec seuls 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de la descente vers CYFB, l’équipage a remarqué que le poids maximal d’atterrissage serait environ 400 à 500 livres au-dessus de la limite, il a décidé de descendre plus tôt vers 6000 pieds afin de consommer plus de carburant pour atterrir sous la limite. À environ 35 nm, CJT470 a été autorisé pour l’approche ILS piste 34 et lorsque l’équipage se dirigeait vers le point initial d’approche, l’altitude de 2100 pieds a été entrée dans le sélecteur d’altitude. L’avion a continué sa descente sous 6000 pieds avec les volets à la position 1 et le train d’atterrissage sorti, peu après, l’équipage a reçu une alerte du système GPWS (Ground Proximity Warning System). L’équipage a immédiatement effectué les manœuvres de correction et a remonté à 6000 pieds. L’approche et l’atterrissage ont été poursuivis sans encombre.

On 16 February 2023, a privately operated Lake LA 4 200 (registration C-FFPB) was enroute from Marathon Aerodrome (CYSP), Ontario to Muskoka Airport (CYQA), Ontario, when the engine failed. The pilot conducted an emergency landing onto a frozen lake approximately 55 nm from the Greater Sudbury Airport (CYSB) ON. After landing safely, the pilot transmitted a Mayday call that was overheard by the CYSB Flight Service station and Air Canada flight ACA326 that was flying overhead. ACA326 relayed the position report through Toronto ACC.JRCC Trenton dispatched a CC130 Hercules that deployed 2 SAR Techs who located the pilot and passenger. After spending the night near the aircraft, all personnel were transported by ATV to the nearest town. No injuries were reported. The aircraft sustained no damage but remained on the Lake.

The Canadian North Boeing 737-300, C-GZNZ, was operating as AKT1731 on a flight from Fort Mackay/Horizon (CYNR), AB to Calgary (CYYC), AB. AKT1731 was inbound on the ADVOX STAR for Runway 35L and was cleared to 10000 feet by the arrival controller. On the downwind, south of OTMAG, AKT1731 descended through 9700 feet, eventually reaching 9400 feet. The arrival controller queried AKT1731 about their altitude and instructed them to climb to 10 000 feet. A loss of separation had occurred with a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. Dash 8-400, C-GJWE, that was operating as WEN3229 on a flight from CYYC to Edmonton (CYEG), AB. Separation reduced to 1.8 NM horizontally and 700 feet vertically where 1000 feet or 3 NM is required.

C-GXRW, a Swoop Inc. Boeing 737-800 operating flight WSW772 from Winnipeg James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB to Orlando Sanford Intl. (KSFB), FL, had a depressurization event at 37000 ft. near Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta Intl. (KATL) GA. The crew declared an emergency, initiated an emergency descent down to 10000 ft. and continued to destination where it landed safely. No injuries.The aircraft will remain in KSFB for a maintenance inspection and required maintenance actions.

C-GBAS, an Airsprint Embraer E-545 operating as flight ASP875 from Denver Intl. (KDEN), CO to Boca Raton Airport (KBCT), FL declared an emergency due to a landing gear issue. The crew elected to return to KDEN where the aircraft landed safely.

C-GEHY, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft operated by Air Canada as AC607, was on a planned flight from Halifax/Robert L Stanfield International Airport, NS (CYHZ) to Lester B. Pearson International Airport, ON (CYYZ). During push back the crew started #2 uneventfully and then proceed to start #1 engine. During #1 engine start the crew noted a fault and contacted company Maintenance Operational Control (MOC) to discuss. During the sequence a miscommunication occurred between the aircraft crew and the ground crew as to the status of tug connection to the aircraft. The aircraft crew requested that the aircraft be towed back to the gate and subsequently released the brakes thinking that the aircraft was still physically connected to the tug. The aircraft then rolled a short distance forward under idle power and collided with the roof of tug. Both the aircraft and tug were disabled on the taxi line of Apron 1 which resulted in delays to multiple aircraft proceeding to/from gates and the deice pads. The aircraft to tug contact resulted in minor damage with no injuries to persons.

C-FIJZ, un Bombardier CRJ 900 exploité par Jazz Aviation, effectuait le vol JZA481 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport J.A. Douglas McCurdy/Sydney, NE (CYQY) à destination de l'aéroport Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ). Alors que l'aéronef se trouvait en croisière, à environ 40 milles nautiques de l'aéroport de Shebrooke, QC (CYSC), l'équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) suite à un problème de train d'atterrissage. L'aéronef a poursuivi sa route vers CYYZ et a demandé la présence des services d'urgence ainsi que l'accès à la piste d'atterrissage la plus longue disponible. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre à 1253Z.

N478UA, a United Airlines Airbus A320-200, was operating as UAL108 from Denver International (KDEN), CO, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 5 crew and 136 passengers on board. While on approach to CYVR, the landing gear would not extend. A go-around was executed, a manual extension of the landing gear was completed, and an emergency was declared. The aircraft landed safely, exited the runway, and halted on the taxiway. The nosewheel steering displayed a fault and the aircraft was towed to the gate.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and conducted a series of tests and replaced the 62GA relay. Maintenance performed nose wheel steering and gear swing tests and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSES, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 operating flight ACA587 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Kahului Airport (PHOG), HI, declared an emergency in the vicinity of Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (KSEA), WA, due to water pooling in the rear of the aircraft. The crew elected to divert to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC where the aircraft landed safely.

C-GCJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Limited CL-600-2D24 (CRJ 900), was conducting flight AC7746 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Saskatoon International (CYXE), SK, with 4 crew members and 74 passengers on board. While in cruise, the aircraft experienced an abrupt, uncommanded change in altitude and speed. The altitude jumped up 1000 feet from the assigned altitude of 37 000 feet above sea level (ASL) and the aircraft speed increased by 30 kts. The aircraft overspeed warning alarm sounded in the cockpit as the aircraft over sped for approximately 5 seconds. The crew disconnected the autopilot. The aircraft speed slowed to the normal cruise speed and the crew manually descended to their assigned altitude. The crew attributed this loss of control to mountain waves in the area during the flight. The flight continued to CYXE without further incident. There were no injuries.UPDATED 07 MARCH 2023.

C-GHQZ, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG1640 from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON to Big Trout Lake (CYTL), ON. While on approach to CYTL, the Nose Wheel Steering crew alerting and warning system light illuminated when the crew selected the gear down. The crew verified that the nose wheel steering switch was in the correct position and consulted the QRH. After completing the QRH items, the light remained on. The crew elected to return to CYXL and a PAN PAN was declared as a precautionary measure. An uneventful landing was conducted. After the landing, the nose steering system was functioning normally and the crew taxied the aircraft to the apron.The operator's maintenance inspected and tested the nose wheel steering system following the occurrence and was unable to duplicate the indication.

On 14 February 2023, a Skylink Express Beech 1900C (registration C-GSKM), operating as SLQ727 was enroute to the Hamilton International airport (CYHM), ON. While at 13000 MSL, prior to commencing the approach, the flight crew saw a white flash, heard a loud noise, felt a yawing moment and suspected an issue with the No. 2 engine. The flight crew reduced power on the No. 2 engine, declared an emergency and proceeded to land at CYHM without further incident. ATC dispatched ARFF who was awaiting the aircraft upon landing.

On 12 February 2023, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A320-214 (registration C-GFDU), operating as ROU1950, was taxiing for a departure from the Lester B Pearson International Airport, (CYYZ) Toronto, ON. During the taxi, a following aircraft advised ROU1950 of fluid leaking from the #2 engine. ROU1950 held its position. Suspecting a fuel leak, the flight crew shut down the #2 engine which was effective in mitigating the fluid leak. ATC dispatched ARFF as a precaution. ROU1950 returned to gate under its own power. The aircraft was removed from service and the scheduled flight was completed with a different aircraft following the associated delays.Maintenance inspected the aircraft in accordance with the AMM and found an aft actuator line to be leaking. The fuel gear motor was removed and replaced with a serviceable unit in accordance with the AMM. Subsequent serviceability tests were carried out with satisfactory results. The aircraft was subsequently deemed to be airworthy and returned to service.

C-FANB, an Air North Charter & Training Limited Boeing 737-400, was conducting flight AN542 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Whitehorse International (CYXY), YT, with 5 crew and 102 passengers onboard. While in cruise altitude of 32 000 feet above sea level (ASL), the flight crew noted that cabin altitude was approaching 10 000' ASL. An emergency descent was initiated, and masks were donned. During the descent, a cabin altitude warning horn sounded. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with air traffic control and they were given radar vectors to return to CYVR. The flight crew began the rapid depressurization checklist from the quick reference handbook (QRH). While completing the checklist, the flight crew discovered that the engine bleed valves had not been switched on during the after take-off checklist. With the bleed valve switch selected on, the flight crew levelled off at 14 000 feet ASL, pressurization was regained and the cabin altitude began to descend. The PAN PAN was cancelled and, after a discussion with the cabin crew and fuel calculations, the flight crew received a new ATC clearance to continue the flight to CYXY. There were no injuries and the flight continued without further issues.

C-GFSV, a Central Mountain Air Beech B1900D aircraft, was conducting flight GLR708 from Terrace (CYXT), BC, to Prince George (CYXS), BC, with 9 passengers and 2 flight crew on board. During the arrival into CYXS, descending through 15 000 feet, the flight crew smelled a strange odour and passengers saw smoke in the cabin. The flight crew completed emergency procedures, advised ATC, and requested priority handling. Aircraft rescue and firefighting crews were standing by when the aircraft landed safely. The aircraft taxied to the fire hall; the flight crew and passengers exited the aircraft.Maintenance found the Cabin Vent Blower Assembly (part number 114-380028-11) was unserviceable. The assembly was replaced in accordance with MM21-20-01 and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FDAO, un De Havilland DHC8-102 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait un vol d'essai sous l'indicatif AIE857, depuis l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP). Lors de la rétraction du train après le décollage, l'équipage a noté une rétraction du train d'atterrissage plus lente qu'à l'habitude, suivie de l'illumination du voyant de pompe hydraulique du moteur numéro 2 (#2 ENG HYD PUMP). L’équipage a actionné la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH). Après avoir complété la procédure de rétraction du train, le voyant de pompe hydraulique du moteur numéro 1 (#1 ENG HYD PUMP) s’est illuminé. Une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée. Peu après, l'indication de la défectuosité de la pompe hydraulique du moteur numéro 1 est disparue et l'urgence a été annulée. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-FDAO, un De Havilland DHC8-102 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE871M depuis l’aéroport de Kangiqsujuaq, QC (CYKG) à destination de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP). Peu après le décollage de CYKG, une indication de portes de train d'atterrissage ouvertes est apparue, et les voyants de pompe hydraulique du moteur numéro 2 (#2 ENG HYD PUMP) ainsi que du système hydraulique associé se sont illuminés. L’équipage a actionné la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et le vol s’est poursuivi vers CYVP à une vitesse réduite. Une urgence (PN PAN) a été déclarée et les services d'urgence ont été déployés. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre.

C-GNUQ, un Cessna 150M exploité par Richcopter Inc., effectuait un vol d'entraînement local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport d'Ottawa/Gatineau, QC (CYND) avec seul un élève pilote à bord. Lors de de l'atterrissage, au moment du posé des roues sur la piste 27 à CYND, l'aéronef a dévié de sa course et est sorti de piste. L'aéronef a terminé sa course dans la neige, du côté sud de la piste, subissant des dommages substantiels à la partie avant de l'appareil. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé ni d'incendie.

C-GGDU, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8368 from Fort Saint John (CYXJ), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 4 crew and 66 passengers on board. While on final approach into CYVR, the flight crew selected landing gear down and they received a gear unsafe message with 3 red warning lights illuminated which indicated that the gear was not down and locked. The crew discontinued the approach and requested radar vectors from the air traffic controller so that they could complete the necessary checklists. The crew declared a PAN PAN and performed the alternate gear extension procedure. The landing gear lowered into place and the crew received 3 green lights indicating the gear was down and locked. The aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft.Maintenance crews inspected the Proximity Sensing Electronic Unit (PSEU) and confirmed fault codes. The PSEU and selector valve were replaced, function tests of the gear were carried out, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GGOF, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400 (Dash 8 Q400) aircraft, operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight AC8284 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Kelowna International (CYLW), BC, with 4 crew members and 66 passengers on board. As the aircraft neared CYLW, the crew received a revised weather forecast which was below their required landing minimums. The aircraft was placed in a holding pattern by air traffic control (ATC). When the fuel load on board the aircraft reached 150 pounds over the planned minimum diversion fuel, the crew elected to return to CYVR. During the return flight, at approximately 100 nautical miles northeast of CYVR, the flight encountered strong headwinds: 40 knots stronger than had been used for the flight's fuel calculations. The crew requested and were granted an altitude change to 19 000 feet above sea level in order to reduce the headwind. After revised fuel calculations were made, the crew determined that they had sufficient fuel to reach CYVR but, for added safety, declared a minimum fuel advisory and requested priority handling with ATC. The aircraft landed safely with a fuel load that was more than 200 pounds above the minimum reserve fuel required. There were no injuries.

C-GHPJ, an Air Canada Rouge A321-200 operating as flight ROU1721 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (KPHX), AZ was in the descent phase and was being vectored to the downwind by ATC for unconfirmed VFR traffic. The aircraft was then cleared to a waypoint and issued further descent. Shortly thereafter a TCAS RA: DESCEND command was issued and complied with by the flight crew. The ATC was advised and visual contact with an orbiting target was subsequently acquired. The flight was subsequently completed without further incident.

C-FOJZ, an MHI RJ Aviation ULC CL-600-2D24 (CRJ 900) operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting JZA954, from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (KATL), GA, USA, to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the flight, the crew received a FLAP FAIL indication with the flaps fully retracted. In anticipation of an abnormal landing due to flap failure, the flight crew declared PAN PAN with Toronto Centre. The flight landed uneventfully at CYYZ.

C-GNBE, an Air Canada Airbus A220, was conducting flight AC724 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to LaGuardia Airport (KLGA), NY when on approach, a flight attendant became ill. The aircraft landed safely and was met by EMS.

C-FIOJ, a SA227-AC operated by SkyCare Air Ambulance as PHX594, departed the Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON, on a VFR flight to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, with 2 crew and 1 passenger on board. While in the vicinity of CYTZ at 2500 feet, the left engine (Garrett TPE331) flamed out. The flight crew verified the engine failure and secured the engine per their checklist before attempting a restart. The engine did not restart, and the flight crew elected to return to CYKF, where they landed without further incident. Maintenance inspection revealed that a failed gear on the torque sensor shaft, which also drives the high pressure fuel pump, resulted in the flameout. The engine has been shipped to an overhaul facility for inspection and repair. A similar occurrence occurred on 26 January 2023, involving a TPE331 powered SA226-TC which was also operated by SkyCare (A23O0013). This failure mode is similar to that revealed in a 2011 TSB investigation, A11C0047, where a TPE331 torque sensor gear failure is detailed in section 1.9.4.

G-ZBLG, a Boeing 787-10 aircraft operated by British Airways, was conducting flight BAW238 from Boston/Logan Intl (KBOS), MA to London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK. While in cruise flight at about 55°00' N, 040°00' W, the flight crew informed Gander Area Control Center of smoke in the cabin and declared an emergency. The crew discussed diversion airport options with ATS, then decided on and were cleared to land at St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL. The aircraft landed at CYYT without incident. At CYYT, airport emergency services entered the aircraft to inspect for sources of heat or smoke. An acrid smell was detected at row 12 seat A; however, no source was found. As a precaution, 2 cabin crew members were taken to a local medical facility for an assessment related to inhalation of fumes and were later released.Maintenance personnel subsequently inspected the aircraft and found no evidence of heat or fire. Multiple passenger service units and ceiling panels were removed for the inspection in the area around seat 12A. Engine runs as well as Zone B and C trim air mufflers were inspected without any defect noted. Maintenance also carried out seat inspections as well as air conditioning pack, galley equipment, in-flight entertainment, and auxiliary heater operational checks with no faults noted. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GTZS, an Airbus A220-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA647 from Greater Moncton/Roméo LeBlanc Intl (CYQM), NB to Toronto/Pearson (CYYZ), ON. While positioned in the deice bay on the ramp at CYQM before departure, a de-icing vehicle struck the left wingtip of the aircraft. Maintenance inspection identified minor skin damage, as well as a damaged aircraft static wick.

C-GKOE, an Airbus 320-214 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA690 from Toronto/Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL.  When overhead Saint John, NB and cruising at FL350, the flight crew received a Yellow hydraulics system low level ECAM message. The crew declared a PAN PAN, completed the QRH checklist, and completed all performance calculations and landed at destination (CYYT) without further incident.Company maintenance personnel replaced a faulty hydraulic system pressure line.

C-GJXW, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300 was conducting flight AC1205 from Miami Intl. (KMIA), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During descent at FL320, flight crew received a TCAS TA (traffic advisory) followed by a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) due to traffic closure rate.  Flight crew followed the RA and contacted ATC.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GEHY, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight AC572 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), CA. On final runway 28 Right, ATC was vectoring another flight for an approach when flight crew received a TCAS TA (traffic advisory) and then RA (resolution advisory). Flight crew followed instruction and performed a go around.  ATC vectored flight back to land on runway 28 Right. Flight landed without further incident.

C-GJXW, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300 was conducting flight AC701 from New York/LaGuardia airport (KLGA), NY to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During descent at FL266, flight crew received TCAS RA (resolution advisory) ''Traffic Traffic''.  Flight crew made visual contact with traffic and ATC asked traffic to climb.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GEMV, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight AC1058 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Las Vegas/Harry Reid Intl. (KLAS), NV.  On approach runway 1 Left, Flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) for traffic on approach runway 1 Right.  There was no conflict and flight landed without further incident.

C-GMIQ, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight AC572 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), CA.  During approach runway 28R, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory).  The traffic on TCAS initiated a go around and plane landed without further incident.

C-FIUJ, an Air Canada Boeing 767-200 was conducting flight AC43 from New Delhi/Indira Gandhi Intl. (VIDP), India to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. During cruise over the Black Sea, flight crew advised maintenance control over SATCOM that the First Officer outer pane had shattered, and inner pane was intact. Flight crew declared a PANPAN with ATC and decided to divert to London/Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK.  Flight crew landed overweight in EGLL without further incident.  Maintenance found First Officer window inner ply shattered.  ACA engineering and manufacturer is engaged in analysis and inspection. An overweight inspection was also carried out with no fault found. Maintenance also replaces left and right window heat controller as per aircraft maintenance manuals.

C-GNJA, un Bombardier CRJ 200 exploité par Jazz Aviation, effectuait le vol JZA938 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Newark Liberty Intl, Newark, NJ (KEWR) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 28 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, le voyant "Stab Trim Fail" s'est illuminé. L'équipage a déclaré un "Pan Pan" et a effectué un retour à CYUL où l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre.

C-FPRP, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight SWG435 from Punta Cana Intl. (MDPC), Dominican Republic to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC. During cruise over the Atlantic Ocean a cabin crew became incapacitated.  Flight landed at CYUL without further incident.

C-GHKR, an Airbus A330-343, operating as Air Canada flight AC917 was inbound to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) when the Blue hydraulic system overheated, and there was low hydraulic pressure. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and continued to CYYZ, where the flight landed without further incident. Maintenance carried out an inspection after landing and no visible leaks were noted. Troubleshooting of the system revealed that the Blue system hydraulic pump had failed.

C-GRAI, a Dash 8-300 aircraft operated by Air Inuit, was conducting a flight from Montreal/ Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Miramichi airport (CYCH), NB.  On approach, while extending the gear, the crew received gear unsafe lights, the #2 ENG HYD PUMP caution light, and zero hydraulic pressure on the #2 main hydraulic pressure gauge. The crew conducted a missed approach and declared an emergency with Moncton ACC. While performing the emergency checklist, the gear extended on its own and indicated down and locked. The crew validated this by checking the alternate landing gear down lock verification lights. The crew cancelled the emergency and landed at CYCH without further incident. Maintenance inspected the aircraft, with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSNQ, a Boeing 737-8 (MAX 8) aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA607 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Toronto/Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. On departure, the crew received a leading-edge flap EICAS message, declared a PAN PAN, actioned the QRH, and landed at CYHZ without further incident. Maintenance personnel replaced a wiring connector related to the leading-edge flap fault and returned the aircraft to service.

The Air Canada Airbus A220-300, C-GJXW, was operating as ACA220 on a flight from Vancouver Intl. Airport (CYVR), BC to Calgary Intl. Airport (CYYC), AB. While on approach to CYYC, a loss of separation occurred with a Flair Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737 MAX 8, C-FLKC, operating as FLE1813 on a flight from Waterloo (CYKF), ON to CYYC. Separation reduced to 2.2 NM laterally and 700 feet vertically where 3.0 NM or 1000 feet are required. Separation was regained when the tower controller instructed ACA220 to conduct a missed approach. There were no other impacts to operations and both aircraft landed safely.

C-FFEL, a Flair Airlines Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight FLE2615 from Cancun Intl (MMUN), Mexico to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  Approximately 4 minutes after level off at FL370, LH PACK annunciator illuminated on EICAS (Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System).  Flight crew actioned corresponding QRH action items and while performing required action, RH PACK also illuminated.  Shortly thereafter the flight crew received CABIN ALTITUDE Warning light and associated horn.Flight crew immediately donned oxygen mask and attempted to contact Houston Center for descent clearance.  Flight crew was unable to contact ATC.  Flight crew initiated an emergency descent, squawk 7700 on the transponder and cabin/passengers' masks also deployed.  During the emergency descent, flight crew was able to reach Houston Center, received clearance to 10000 feet and decided to divert to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL.  There were no injuries.  Maintenance is troubleshooting.

C-FSNQ, a Boeing 737-8 (MAX 8) aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA612 from Toronto/Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. While on approach to CYHZ, the crew selected flap 1 position and received the LEADING EDGE TRANSIT EICAS message. The crew noted that all trailing edge flap indications were normal. The crew declared a PAN PAN, actioned the QRH, and landed at CYHZ without further incident. Maintenance personnel recorded a latched fault which required the replacement of the S171 sensor.

C-GTIM, a SA226-TC, operated by SkyCare Air Ambulance departed Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON destined for Toronto Buttonville Airport (CYKZ), ON. Approximately 20 minutes from CYKZ, and just prior to descent from FL230 the flight crew noted a 10 degree rise in EGT on one of the engines (Garrett, TPE331-10UA-511G). The flight crew adjusted the power lever, and shortly afterwards they noted another rise in EGT, followed by a power loss. The inflight shutdown procedure was completed, the crew advised ATC and requested a diversion to Waterloo Regional Airport (CYKF), ON. The aircraft landed in CYKF without further incident.

C-GANU, an Air North Training and Charter Boeing 737-500 was being operated as flight AN554 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Whitehorse International (CYXY), YK, with 5 crew and 88 passengers on board. During the climb, the cabin crew reported a noise coming from the area of door L1. The flight crew levelled off at 28 000 feet above sea level (ASL) and utilized the standby mode on the pressurization controller. The noise became quieter and more tolerable for the passengers and the crew continued to climb to the assigned cruise altitude of 30 000 feet ASL. While in cruise approximately 40 nm NE of Bella Coola, BC, the flight crew observed a gradual loss of cabin pressure. As cabin altitude reached 9000 feet, the crew began the "Auto fail or unscheduled pressurization change" checklist from the quick reference handbook (QRH). The crew then requested and were cleared to descend to 26 000 feet ASL by air traffic control (ATC). During the descent the cabin pressurization became uncontrollable.  The crew donned oxygen masks and the passenger oxygen system was manually activated by the flight crew. The 'Cabin Altitude' annunciation accompanied by the cabin altitude horn sounded. The flight crew began the 'Rapid descent' checklist, began an emergency descent, and declared an emergency with ATC. The crew requested vectors to the Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC. The aircraft was levelled off at 10 000 feet ASL with the cabin altitude reading 0 feet of pressure. The aircraft continued to CYXS and landed without further incident. There were no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft.Maintenance replaced the L1 door bulb seal found that the L1 lower hinge flapper assembly hinge pin was unseated. They reseated the L1 lower hinge flapper assembly.  Additionally, the forward water separator grooved coupling clamps on the right side had failed. This allowed the pressurization duct to separate so only the left pack was pressurizing the aircraft. The clamp was replaced and a pressurization test was successfully completed. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GHKR, an Airbus A330-343, operating as Air Canada AC1086 departed Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ). Shortly after departure the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to smoke in the flight deck and cabin. The flight returned to CYYZ where the aircraft landed without further incident. The aircraft was inspected by aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) personnel, and there were no anomalies found. Maintenance conducted their investigation and found deicing fluid in the APU intake plenum.

CS-TXK, an Airbus 321 operated by Air Portugal, was preparing to conduct flight TAP260, from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, to Lisbon Humberto Delgado Airport (LPPT), Portugal. Runway 23 was assigned for departure, and during taxi the crew requested to depart from taxiway Q. This request was approved, and they were instructed to hold short of taxiway Q, which is within the runway protected area for runway 23. TAP260 was observed taxiing across the hold short line without clearance. As a result, the tower controller instructed a WestJet B737 (C-GGWJ/WJA710), which was on the approach for runway 23, to go-around.

N667UA a Boeing 767-322 aircraft operated by United Airlines Inc was conducting flight UAL146 from Newark Liberty International Airport Newark, New Jersey, USA (KEWR) to London Heathrow, United Kingdom (EGLL). During cruise, the flight the crew detected vibration from engine #1 and also noted that the engine was not producing thrust accompanied by high an elevated exhaust gas temperature (EGT). The Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) procedures were accomplished, the engine #1 was shut down and an emergency was declared with Moncton ACC. The crew requested and received clearance to divert to Halifax/Stanfield Intl. (CYHZ), NS where the aircraft landed safely at 0629 UTC.The aircraft was examined by Aircraft Rescue Fire Fighting crews before taxiing to the gate under its own power. Examination of the #1 engine, a Pratt and Whitney PW4060-3, revealed small-size metal debris in the tailpipe and oil from the engine core area. The inboard side of the accessory gearbox had a crack extending from the top along the forward edge of the gearbox case. There was no evidence of an uncontained failure of the engine. As of 08 February 2023, the aircraft remains out of service in CYHZ awaiting engine replacement.

C-FMEU, a Boeing 757-200 operated by Morningstar Air Express Inc., was conducting a cargo flight from Vancouver Intl, B.C. (CYVR) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with 2 flight crew members on board. During the decent into the greater CYYC area, the aircraft encountered turbulence with associated airframe vibrations and the loss of the tail wind. A temporary loss of control and an abrupt increase in indicated airspeed was experienced along with a brief aircraft overspeed condition. Control of the aircraft was regained, and the flight continued to the intended destination where an uneventful landing was completed. There were no injuries.Subsequent inspection of the aircraft by company maintenance did not find any faults.

C-GMXD, un Pilatus PC-12/47E exploité par Airmedic Inc. sous l'indicatif AM267, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Sept-Îles (CYZV), QC à destination de Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU), QC avec 2 pilotes et 2 passagers. En vol de croisière à 4500 pieds au-dessus du niveau de la mer et à environ 35 miles marins est-sud-est de Trois-Rivières, QC (CYRQ), un tangage vers le bas est survenu. L’aéronef avait une forte tendance de tangage à piquer et l’équipage a complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour l’emballement du compensateur horizontal. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a fait une diversion à destination de Trois-Rivières (CYRQ), QC. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 31. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

N829AW, un Airbus 319-132 exploité par American Airlines sous l'indicatif AAL1964, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County (KDTW) aux États-Unis. Le départ suivant était N311PQ, un CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) exploité par Endeavor Air sous l’indicatif EDV4648 qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de CYUL à destination de New York John F Kennedy (KJFK) aux États-Unis. Une perte d’espacement est survenue lors de la montée initiale, lorsque l'EDV4648 s’est retrouvé momentanément à 2,7 miles marins (nm) derrière le AAL1964 à environ la même altitude. L’espacement requis était de 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical et 3 nm sur le plan horizontal. Les 2 appareils ont poursuivi leurs vols à leurs destinations respectives sans encombre.

C-GSPW un Boeing 737-275C exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE700 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Puvirnituq, QC (CYPX) avec 2 membres d’équipage et 36 passagers à bord. Lors de l’approche initiale, l’équipage fait la sélection des volets à la position 1 et les volets sont restés bloqués à la position 0. Un déroutement à La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) a été effectué et l’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés et l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 31. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GXJA, un MHI RJ Aviation ULC CL-600-2B19 (CRJ200) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA584, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County (KDTW) aux États-Unis à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 14 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Alors que l’aéronef était en approche finale vers la piste 24R à CYUL, une indication « Flap Fail » est apparue lorsque les volets ont été sélectionnés à la position 20 et ceux-ci sont restés bloqués à la position 8. L’équipage a effectué une approche interrompue, a déclaré un état d’urgence (PAN PAN) et est revenu se poser sur la piste 24R sans encombre. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FKPT, an Air Canada Airbus A320-200 was conducting flight AC7081 from Buffalo/Niagara Intl. (KBUF), NY to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC.  After level off engines operated normally and flight crew decided on a lower speed due to turbulence. At this point both engines began to spool back up and the number one engine stalled at 50-54%. There were no caution/warnings only a slight buffet. Flight crew followed their QRH procedures and retarded the #1 engine throttle below 50% and the engine stabilized. Flight crew declared a Mayday with ATC and flight landed without further incident. Based on fault and system reliability data, Variable bleed valve actuator will be replaced.  Maintenance is still troubleshooting.

G-ZBKL, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by British Airways was conducting flight BA216 from Washington Dulles Intl (KIAD), VA to Heathrow Airport London (EGLL), UK. At approximately 0100 Z (2000 EST, Feb 01) the crew informed Moncton Area Control Center of smoke in the cabin and declared an emergency. The crew requested and were cleared to divert to Halifax/Stanfield Intl. (CYHZ), NS. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 05 at 0140 Z (2040 EST). During the flight, the cabin crew discharged a portable halon fire extinguisher in the forward cabin at Row 10 seat D, E, F as a precaution. Further inquiry revealed that no smoke was present but there was an acrid smell around row 10 seat D, E, F (forward cabin).  Initial maintenance action consisted of removing a number of Passenger Service Units (PSU’s) and ceiling panels for inspection including in the area above and around the area where the acrid smell was noted. No fire, soot or smoke damage was noted in the area.The middle PSU in the forward cabin was inspected in detail, all middle PSU oxygen generators were found in the green band with no signs of heat or burning present. Further checks were completed in the premium economy cabin with the PSU and the recirculation pack area inspected and found ok. All packs were function checked and no acrid odor detected. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-FYJI, an Airbus A319-114 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA223 from Calgary International, AB (CYYC), to Vancouver International, BC (CYVR) with 5 crew members and 111 passengers on board. During the initial climb after departure from Runway 17R, the flight crew received a left-hand engine thrust reverser unlocked message on the electronic centralized aircraft monitor (ECAM) system. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist and elected to complete a precautionary shutdown of the left engine (CFM International, CFM56-5A5). The flight crew contacted ATC, informed them of the condition and returned to CYYC, where an uneventful landing was completed. Airport rescue and firefighting responded to the occurrence, no abnormalities were observed on the aircraft and the aircraft taxied to the gate where the passengers deplaned. There were no injuries.Subsequent investigation by company maintenance found the outboard upper blocker door of the #1 engine not stowed. The door actuator and latch assembly for the outboard, upper blocker were replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

The WestJet Encore, de Havilland DHC-8-400, C-FJWE, was operating as flight WEN8986 on a positioning flight with no passengers, from Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC to Calgary (CYYC), AB. During the initial climb, the flight crew retracted the landing gear. The nose landing gear door remained open and the amber N.DOOR light illuminated. The crew actioned the QRH and clearance was requested for WEN8986 to divert to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB. During the initial approach into CYEG the flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency. The aircraft landed safely. The nose landing gear door actuator was replaced and the aircraft was released for continued service.

C-GJZT, a Jazz Aviation LP CRJ900 was conducting flight AC8387 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl. (CYXE), SK.  During cruise at FL360 in the vicinity of Sault Ste Marie Airport (CYAM), ON, the flight crew reduced thrust to achieve cruise speed.  Shortly afterwards following the adjustment, the low-speed cue and angle of attack parameters were met resulting in momentarily stick shaker and stick pusher to activate. The crew reacted in a timely manner with minimal loss of altitude and continued to destination and landed with without further incident.

C-FJQD, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-200 was conducting flight ROU1637 from Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. The aircraft departed RWY 17R, and during the climb to cruise phase of flight, passing through approximately 1500ft ASL in the vicinity of KAAPE waypoint, a bird strike occurred, and the bird was ingested by ENG#2. The aircraft leveled at 3000ft ASL and ENG 2 power was reduced to idle. A PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft returned to KMCO for full-stop landing RWY 18R with ARFF on standby. ARFF conducted a general visual inspection externally and the affected engine was subsequently shut down. The aircraft subsequently taxied under its own power to the gate where the flight was completed without further incident. Preliminary info: ENG 2 (RH) approximately 6 fan blades sustained shingling and significant soft impact damage from mid to 3/4 span (from root) of the blades. Following the occurrence, defects were entered in the aircraft journey log in accordance with company policy and procedure. Maintenance is currently inspecting the aircraft and rectifying the defects in accordance with company policy and procedure. A biologist met the flight and suspected the bird species may have been a turkey vulture.

The WestJet Encore, De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, C-FSWE, was operating as flight WEN3103 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Nanaimo (CYCD), BC. After take-off, the flight crew received a main landing gear door indication fault. The left main landing gear door remained open after gear retraction. The flight crew actioned the QRH and declared a PAN PAN emergency. The aircraft returned to CYYC and landed safely. There were no injuries. Company maintenance adjusted the main landing gear actuator proximity sensor and conducted landing gear operational tests. The aircraft was released for continued service.

C-GGMZ, a Jazz Aviation, Dehavilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-8-400, was operating as flight JZA8402 from Grande Prairie (CYQU), AB to Calgary Int. Airport (CYYC), AB. As the aircraft taxied into position on the runway for takeoff, the flight crew noted that the aircraft was lined up to the left of the runway centerline. As the flight crew maneuvered the aircraft back to the centerline, they advised FSS that they would turn around and return to the threshold, to line up again. While backtracking, the crew saw the aircraft tire tracks in the snow showing that they had taxied onto the side of the runway, departing the runway surface. The flight crew did not observe that the aircraft had collided with any ground objects. Once the aircraft was lined up on the runway centerline, the aircraft departed uneventfully. During the initial climb, the flight crew advised FSS that the aircraft taxied off the runway surface prior to repositioning. FSS dispatched airport operations to inspect the runway and the inspection revealed that a runway edge light had been struck by the aircraft; FSS notified the flight crew. The aircraft continued to CYYC without issue. During approach to CYYC, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN in case of potential tire damage. The flight landed safely and taxied to the gate without issue; there were no injuries.Company maintenance inspected the tires and landing gear and found no issues.

C-FADS, a Coastal Pacific Aviation Piper PA-30 (Twin Comanche) aircraft, was conducting a local training flight near Abbotsford (CYXX), BC, with 1 instructor and 1 student on board. As part of the training, the pilot attempted to lower the landing gear. The Gear Motor CB tripped and the landing gear down and locked light did not illuminate. The pilot reset the CB and attempted to lower the landing gear a second time with the same result. The pilot did not reset the CB and completed the manual gear extension emergency checklist. The landing gear down and locked light still did not illuminate. The aircraft returned to CYXX and flew a low approach over runway 19 and requested that ATC visually observe the position of the landing gear. ATC advised that the landing gear appeared down but it could not be determined if they were locked. The aircraft landed on runway 07 and approximately 1 second after touchdown, the nose and main landing gear collapsed. The aircraft stopped on the runway and a small fire erupted under the left wing between the fuselage and the left engine. The 2 occupants exited the front right door and ARFF extinguished the fire. There were no injuries; the aircraft sustained substantial damage. The ELT did not transmit a signal.The aircraft was recovered from the runway and maintenance repairs are in progress.

C-GKVU, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-86N was conducting flight SWG732 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Montego Bay/Sangster Intl (MKJS), Jamaica.  During cruise approximately 200 NM south of CYYZ, flight crew declared an emergency (MAYDAY) due to abnormal right hand engine oil pressure and temperature.  Flight crew completed the appropriate checklist, shutdown the engine as precaution and diverted back to CYYZ where it landed without further incident.

C-GBHZ, an A319-114 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was taxiing at Toronto Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. During taxi from the runway the aircraft was southbound on taxiway B in accordance with its taxi clearance. Approaching taxiway C in the approximate vicinity of taxiway B and D intersection, the brakes were applied to slow the aircraft in preparation for the left turn onto taxiway C. Braking action was nil and the aircraft began to slide and weathercocked into the wind. Brakes and nose wheel steering were ineffective to control the aircraft. After a short distance, the flight crew regained control of the aircraft as it passed over bare pavement. The flight crew notified ATC and the flight was subsequently completed without further incident.

The Northern Air Charter, Beech 200, C-GNAG, was operating on a MEDEVAC flight as NLI239 from Saskatoon (CYXE), SK to Calgary (CYYC), AB. On descent to CYYC, approximately 25 nm NE, the flight crew observed a decrease in power from the #2 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-42). As the the #2 engine lost all power the #2 propeller auto feathered. The flight crew actioned the QRH and declared a MAYDAY. The aircraft landed safely; there were no injuries.Company maintenance reported that they found the air conditioner belts broke and lodged in the pulley housing. This subsequently prevented the accessory gear box from rotating. No additional damage was found to the accessory gear box, components, and accessories. The air conditioning shaft was removed and inspected by NDT. The aft air conditioning shaft support bearings and packings were replaced.UPDATED 25 JANUARY 2024

C-FYMM, a Chartright Air Inc. Cessna 560 Encore was conducting flight HRT705 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Fort Lauderdale Exec Airport (KFXE), FL. During flight over Canadian territory, the left engine cowlings detached resulting in loss of control and aircraft upset. After significant altitude loss, the flight crew regained control, declared an emergency and diverted to Buffalo/Niagara Intl (KBUF), NY. A partial portion of the lower cowl fell from the aircraft after landing. The remaining cowl sections were missing from the aircraft and have not been located. The aircraft received damage to sections of the aft fuselage and the horizontal stabilizer.

C-FNZZ, a Canadian Helicopters Limited Airbus Helicopters AS350 B3, operated by Topflight Elite Training and Charters, was conducting annual recurrent flight training at Penticton (CYYF), BC, with two pilots on board. During a practice autorotation, as the aircraft flared, the throttle was accidentally disturbed and sprung open. The crew decided to reduce the throttle and continue to the touchdown as previously briefed. The height of the helicopter was higher than anticipated and that, combined with the position of the collective, resulted in rotor rpm decay and a hard landing. There were no injuries, but the aircraft was substantially damaged.Maintenance inspection revealed wrinkling on the lower portion of the tail boom. Repairs are in progress.

C-FSCY, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX8 was conducting flight AC564 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), CA.  During the approach runway 8R, flight was cleared to the approach and received TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to climb.  Flight landed without further incident.

C-GVUN, an Air Canada Airbus Canada Limited Partnership A220-300 was conducting flight AC1039 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Denver Intl. (KDEN), CO.  During approach runway 16R in KDEN, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) with traffic in visual.  Flight landed without further incident.

C-FYXF, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was conducting flight ROU1671 from Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. Immediately after takeoff, a cabin crew became incapacitated.  Cabin crew was able to occupy assigned jump seat for approach/landing and carry out safety related duties.  Flight landed in CYYZ without further incident.

C-FUJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 aircraft, operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight 8172, was enroute from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Montreal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with a crew of 4 and 69 passengers on board. Shortly after reaching cruise altitude at FL 290, the crew received a brake overheat warning indication. The crew descended the aircraft to FL200, referred to the QRH and then lowered the landing gear. The crew lost brake temperature indication and were uncertain of the as to the status of the brake temperature. As a precaution, the crew decided to continue flight with the landing gear extended and divert the aircraft to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON. The crew declared an emergency (Pan Pan) and then landed the aircraft safely. Emergency vehicles determined that there was no smoke or fire, and then followed the aircraft to the gate.Inspection by the operator's maintenance of the brake overheat warning system revealed a short circuit and the right inboard proximity sensor harness was replaced.

The Summit Air, British Aerospace Avro 146 (RJ100), C-GZRJ, was operating as flight SUT8151 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT. During approach to Runway 34 (CYZF), the flight crew selected the flaps down. The flaps did not move and remained in the up position. At approximately 10 nm final approach and at 4000 ft AGL the flight crew requested to hold and actioned the QRH. The Runway 34 surface condition was determined to not be suitable for conducting a flapless landing. Clearance was requested for SUT8151 to divert to Edmonton (CYEG), AB, where the company maintenance base was located. While en route to CYEG the flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency due to the flap issue. The aircraft conducted a flapless landing in CYEG without further issue. Company maintenance determined that the flap control unit, green system, pulse generator was faulty. The flap control unit was replaced, and the aircraft returned to service. UPDATED 11 APRIL 2024

C-GLUD, a CanWest Beech King Air 350C, was operating as flight CWA935 from Edmonton International (CYEG), AB to Calgary International (CYYC), AB. CWA935 contacted the arrival controller at 1513:05 and the crew started the arrival procedure into CYYC for a visual approach to Runway 35L. At 1521 CWA935 was instructed to fly heading 110° and to descend to 6200 feet. At 1521:56 CWA935 was instructed to turn left to heading 080° and to descend to 5700 feet. CWA935 remained on a track of 110°. At 1522:25 CWA935 was instructed to turn left to a heading of 010° to intercept the final approach course for a visual approach to Runway 35L; CWA935 remained on a track of 110°. At 1522:56 CWA935’s clearance was cancelled as the flight was crossing the center line of Runway 35L. CWA935 was instructed to turn to a heading of 180° and maintain an altitude of 6000 feet. At 1523:12 CWA935 was queried by the controller if they could intercept the approach for Runway 35L. CWA935 advised they couldn’t due to traffic (an Air Canada B787, flight ACA851, on an RNP Y approach to Runway 35R) at their 10 o’clock position. At 1523:20, CWA935 crossed the centerline for Runway 35R and a loss of separation occurred with ACA851. Separation reduced to 1.7 NM and 300 feet where 3.0 NM or 1000 feet is required. There were no TCAS RAs issued from either aircraft.  Separation was regained when ACA851 was instructed to turn and complete a 360° orbit to the right and CWA935 turned to a heading of 180°. Both aircraft were subsequently vectored back on to their respective approaches and landed without further issue.

C-GHQI, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was conducting flight ROU1997 from Cozumel Intl. (MMCZ), Mexico to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During cruise approximately 250nm N of MMCZ flight crew received multiple successive faults on ECAM (Electronic centralized aircraft monitor) related to ELAC (Elevator and Aileron Computer), stabilizer, autopilot and yellow hydraulic system.  As a result, aircraft flight control reverted to ''ALTN LAW'' and subsequently to ''DIRECT LAW'' on approach as designed.  Flight crew declared a MAYDAY and diverted to Tampa Bay Intl. (KTPA), FL where it landed without further incident. Aircraft was towed to the gate due to loss of nose wheel steering.  Maintenance is investigating.

C-GOIO, an Air Transat Airbus A321-271NX was conducting flight TSC948 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL.  During cruise approximately 60 NM E of Charleston/West Virginia Intl. Yeager (KCRW), WV, a cabin crew was injured.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FHGG, un Beech A100 exploité par Propair Inc. sous l’indicatif PRO4200, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments  depuis l’aéroport de Nemiscau, QC (CYHH) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. QC. (CYUL), avec 3 membres d'équipage et un passager à son bord. Lors de l’approche finale à CYUL, l’équipage a sélectionné la sortie du train d’atterrissage sans résultat. Une urgence a été déclarée et les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. L'appareil a effectué un passage afin de confirmer la position du train qui a été confirmée rentrée. L'équipage a actionné la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et le train a alors été sorti manuellement sans problème par l'équipage. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre, il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage. Des tests de rétraction et extension ont été effectués par le service de maintenance, aucune anomalie trouvée.

N135EV, un Bombardier Inc. CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) exploité par Endeavour Air, effectuait un  vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta, USA (KATL) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Lors de la descente vers CYUL, l'équipage a senti une odeur de surchauffe électrique sans fumée visible. Une urgence a été déclarée. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre quelques minutes plus tard. Aucun dommage ni blessé.Le personnel de maintenance ont trouvé un terminal du système de chauffage du pare-brise mal connecté à celui-ci causant un arc électrique. Le terminal a été resserré et l'appareil remis en service.

C-FJGZ, a Jazz Aviation LP Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd. CL-600-2D24 (CRJ 900), was operating as flight JZA 8103 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Whitehorse (CYXY), YT, with 4 crew members and 35 passengers on board. After takeoff, while selecting the gear up, the GEAR DISAGREE warning message displayed showing an amber indication for the main landing gear and a red indication for the nose landing gear. The flight crew completed the quick reference handbook (QRH) checklist and the landing gear indications showed 3 down and locked. The Nose Wheel Steering Inoperative message was displayed and the nose wheel steering was considered to be unserviceable. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, returned to CYVR, and landed safely. The aircraft exited the runway using differential braking and, after being inspected by aircraft rescue and firefighting crews, the aircraft was towed to the gate.The nose landing gear (NLG) shock strut was found to be flat. When maintenance attempted to service the system with Nitrogen, fluid began to leak out. NLG seals were replaced and inspections completed as per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual. Gear swings were carried out and the NLG steering was tested and found to be serviceable. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GHPJ, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was conducting flight ROU1704 from Las Vegas/Harry Reid Intl. (KLAS), NV to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During departure sequence runway 26L on NIITZ3 SID through 4500 feet, ATC issued vector of 150 degree.  Through 6000 feet on the turn to 150, a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) was received.  Flight crew disconnected the autopilot, complied with TCAS RA and notified ATC. Traffic passed 2 to 3 NM and 300 feet above.  The conflict was resolved, and flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FDOF, a Bell Helicopter 212 operated by Wilderness Helicopters 2009 Ltd., was conducting long-line operations approximately 50 nm northwest of Fort Frances Muni (CYAG), ON. While hovering with a load (hydro pole) at 80 feet AGL, the pilot began to transition to forward flight but the pole movement affected the helicopter. The pilot released the load at 40 AGL. There were no injuries and no damage to the helicopter.

N954AF un Pilatus PC-12/47E exploité par Rigi Inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Boston Logan Intl, Boston, MA (KBOS) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. QC. (CYUL). Lors de son approche vers CYUL, l'appareil a subi une panne du système de dégivrage. Une urgence a été déclarée et il s'est posé sans encombre.

C-FLKX, an Airbus A321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC418 from Toronto Pearson Internatinal Airport (CYYZ), ON to Montreal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC with 6 crew and 190 passengers onboard. While Enroute to CYUL, the aircraft lost the green hydraulic system and the crew subsequently declared emergency with Air Traffic Control. The aircraft landed in CYUL without further incident and towed to the gate as the aircraft did not have nose wheel steering available. During a post occurrence walkaround, hydraulic fluid was noticed running down both sides of the tail. The Green hydraulic level was found just above minimum level. The Left Yaw Damper servo actuator was replaced, and the system tested serviceable with no further leak noted.

C-FGZH, a Top Aces Inc. McDonnel Douglas A-4N was conducting a local mission from Nordholz-Spieka/Cuxhaven airport (ETMN) Germany.  During the mission, the flight pilot discovered an imbalance between external wing tanks.  Additionally, a leak of the external wing tank fuel cap was visible.  The pilot completed the appropriate checklist, the RAT (Ram Air Turbine) was deployed as per checklist and a PanPan was declared. A controllability check was performed prior to landing and the aircraft landed at ETMN without further incident.

C-GAIG, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE753, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Val-D’Or (CYVO) QC, à destination de l'aéroport Katinniq/Donaldson, QC (CTP9). Lors du roulage vers la piste de décollage un membre d'équipage de cabine a eu un malaise l'empêchant d'effectuer le vol prévu. L'appareil est revenu au terminal et le membre d'équipage a été transporté à l'hôpital. Le vol a été retardé le temps qu'une remplaçante se présente et le vol prévu a été effectué avec un léger retard.

C-FDEB, a Beech 200 operated by Vanguard Air Care as flight VN08, was conducting a flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. to Island Lake (CYIV), MB, with 2 crew and one paramedic. After takeoff, when the flight crew selected gear up, the gear unsafe light illuminated and the gear failed to retract. A visual inspection from the aircraft indicated the landing gear had stopped half-way up. The flight crew advised ATC and performed a manual gear down extension; however, the manual gear down extension did not produce a safe gear down indication. C-FDEB requested a hold southwest of CYWG and contacted the operator's maintenance. The operator's maintenance instructed the crew to disengage/reset the emergency engage handle, verify that the gear handle was fully in the down position, pull the landing gear relay circuit breaker, reset a circuit breaker that had tripped, reset the landing gear relay circuit breaker and select gear down. The landing gear started to extend but stopped. The flight crew repeated the procedure a second time. The landing extended and indicated 3 green with the red light in the handle out. The flight crew conducted a fly-past inspection to confirm gear position and completed a safe landing with ARFF standing by. The aircraft was subsequently towed to the hangar. The aircraft was placed on jacks, the landing gear system was inspected and the left gear actuator was found to be binding. The actuator was replaced, gear swings were carried out, and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FNND, un Boeing 777-200 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA42 au départ de l’aéroport de Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) à destination de Indira Gandhi Intl - New Delhi (CIDP), Inde avec 307 passagers et 16 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en vol de croisière à environ 57 nm au sud-est de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB), l'équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) en raison de multiples messages concernant l'état du pack de climatisation gauche et du contrôle de l'altitude cabine (CABIN ALT AUTO L et ASCP PRIMARY CTRL L). L’équipage a décidé de retourner vers CYYZ et a dû larguer du carburant. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre à CYYZ. L’ASCPC (air supply and cabin pressure controller) de gauche a été remplacé.

C-FNXN, un De Havilland DHC-8-314 (DH8C) exploité par Air Creebec inc. sous l'indicatif CRQ5376, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aérodrome de Renard, QC (CFX5) à destination de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec 37 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que CRQ5376 a été autorisé par le terminal de Québec pour l’approche RNAV24, une fois en finale, l’équipage a reçu un avis de trafic TCAS TA qui se situait 500 pieds plus bas à l’avant gauche de l’aéronef. À 4 miles en finale sur l’approche, l’équipage a reçu un avis de résolution TCAS RA. L’équipage a immédiatement suivi les directives et a amorcé une montée à 3000 pieds par minute. L’indication du trafic était rendue à 200 pieds sous l’aéronef et à proximité. L’ATC a été notifié et l’avion est revenu se poser sans encombre. Aucun blessé.

C-GMCP, a Starlink Aviation Inc. Learjet 45 was conducting medevac flight TLK833 from Port of Spain/Piarco Intl. (TTPP) Trinidad and Tobago to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL.  During cruise approximately 75NM W of Puerto Plata/Gregorio Luperon Intl. (MDPP) Dominican Republic, the flight crew noticed the left gauge engine oil pressure falling. The flight crew shut down the left engine as a precaution, declared an emergency (PANPAN) with ATC and diverted to MDPP where it landed without further incident.

On 17 January 2023, the Air Canada A320-211 (registration C-FPWE, serial 175) was operating as flight ACA234 on a scheduled passenger flight from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), British Columbia to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), Alberta. On board were 6 crew members and 125 passengers. Shortly after departing CYVR, the crew noticed the Brake Hot indication on one brake. The climb was stopped and the landing gear was extended to allow the brake to cool down. After the brake cooled down, the landing gear was retracted and the flight continued to CYEG. At approximately 1045MST, during the descent into CYEG, the crew of ACA234 declared a PAN PAN and requested Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF). Upon landing, the brake began to heat up again so the crew brought the aircraft to a stop, allowed the brake to cool, and then taxied to the gate without further incident. There were no injuries. Maintenance action: The affected brake was changed in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) and no other faults were noted.

C-FYXF, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was conducting flight ROU1664 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Fort Myers/Southwest Florida Intl. (KRSW), FL.  During the initial visual approach on ATC vectors runway 24, descending through 5000 ft ASL to a cleared altitude of 2000 ft ASL, ATC issued a VFR traffic advisory regarding VFR traffic at 3500ft ASL ahead. ATC subsequently issued a further vector directly at the VFR traffic. The flight crew did not have the traffic visual although it was displayed on TCAS. After the turn was initiated, it became apparent that a conflict would exist which prompted the PF to immediately disconnect AP and increase descent rate. TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to ''DESCEND'' was simultaneously received and complied with. The PM subsequently acquired visual with the conflicting aircraft. The conflict was resolved, and the flight landed without further incident.

On 11 January 2023, the Sunwest Aviation Ltd. Fairchild SA227-DC (registration C-GSHY, serial DC-897B) was operating as flight CNK214 on a cargo flight from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB. Onboard were 2 pilots. The flight crew was conducting a hand-flown instrument landing system (ILS) approach to Runway 02 at CYEG. The weather was at minimums for the ILS approach and there was a 5 knot tailwind. At approximately 1.0 nautical miles from the threshold of Runway 02, the flight crew initiated a missed approach. During the hand-flown missed approach, the tower controller observed the aircraft turning 35 degrees to the left towards the flight path of an aircraft (Air Canada flight AC234, Boeing 737 Max 8, registration C-FSIP, serial 61215) conducting an ILS approach to Runway 12. Radar data shows that CNK214 continued to descend while deviating left of the localizer. ATC instructed CNK214 to fly heading 360 and climb to 5000 feet above sea level. At 1111:11, radar data shows CNK214 at 0.9 NM from the threshold of Runway 02, between 100 to 200 feet above ground level, 800 feet west of the localizer. During the missed approach, there was a loss of separation with AC234, established on the ILS for Runway 12. Separation reduced to (2.1 nautical miles lateral and 300 feet vertical spacing where 3 nm or 1000 feet is required. Neither aircrafts' flight crew had the other aircraft visual due to instrument meteorological conditions; AC234 did not receive a TCAS resolution advisory. After CNK214 levelled off at 5000 feet above sea level, CNK214 received radar vectors for the ILS to Runway 12. At approximately 1 NM from the threshold of Runway 12, CNK214 was approximately 475 feet south of the localizer and full-scale deflection below the glideslope. At 0.64 NM from the threshold, CNK214 had descended to approximately 100 to 200 feet AGL and remained at that height until 0.4 NM from the threshold of Runway 12, at which point CNK214 began to climb in the missed approach. Following the second missed approach, CNK214 returned to CYYC without further incident.

C-FGZO, a Top Aces Inc. McDonnell Douglas A-4N was conducting local flight out of Cuxhaven (ETMN), Germany as SKYHAWK1.  Approximately 40 minutes after takeoff, pilot noted indication of a left-hand external fuel tank transfer failure.  Return to base was initiated, external fuel transfer failure/ landing asymmetric load checklist executed, and emergency declared.  Flight landed at ETMN without further incident.

C-FCYG, a privately registered Slingsby T67C aircraft was conducting a VFR flight from Buttonville Municipal Airport (CYKZ), ON to Kawartha Lakes Municipal Airport (CNF4), ON with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. Shortly after takeoff from CYKZ on runway 15, the pilot experienced an engine loss of power, declared an emergency (Mayday) and immediately returned for landing on runway 33. The aircraft subsequently touched down on the last third of runway 33 and went off the end. The aircraft continued through the fence and came to rest on 16th Avenue; it was substantially damaged. The nose landing gear detached from the aircraft and slid under a car. There were no injuries to people on the ground. The pilot was uninjured, and the passenger received a minor injury to his hand while egressing the aircraft. The TSB deployed to the scene.

C-FLKX, un Airbus A321-200 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA418, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l'aéroport Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) à destination de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). En route vers CYUL, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) en raison d’un problème avec le système hydraulique. L’aéronef a continué vers CYUL et s’est posé sans encombre avec les services d’urgence en alertes. L’équipage a immobilisé l’aéronef sur la piste pour qu’une inspection soit effectuée avant de circuler vers le terminal.

C-GGND, a DeHavilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA256 from London International Airport (CYXU), ON to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON with 69 passengers onboard. While on initial climb, at approximately 1000 ft, the crew received a Flap drive Caution Light on flap retraction. JZA256 advised ATC they had a flap issue and required a hold to work their checklist. The flight crew subsequently declared a Pan Pan and requested equipment on standby for landing in CYYZ. JZA256 was given priority handling and conducted a flapless landing into CYYZ runway 05. The aircraft landed without further incident and taxied to the gate followed by Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting vehicles.

C-GDGP, un hélicoptère Messerschmitt MMB-BK117 B-2 exploité par AirMédic inc., effectuait un vol d’entrainement selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à destination de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec deux pilotes à son bord. En courte finale pour une zone restreinte dans le secteur du lac Beauport, Qc, les indications « Master Caution » et « ENG I LOW » se sont allumés. Le moteur #1 produisait peu de puissance alors que le #2 fonctionnait à pleine puissance. Le contrôle de l’hélicoptère a été maintenu et l’équipage a décidé de retourner à CYQB. La liste de vérification d’urgence a été effectuée et moteur #2 était en survitesse. La manette de puissance du moteur #2 a été mise au ralenti sans aucun effet. Le moteur a été fermé et un atterrissage sur 1 moteur a été effectué sur la voie de circulation ECHO. Il n’y a eu aucun dommage ni blessé.

C-GSJB, an Airbus A319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1510 from Thunder Bay Intl. (CYQT), ON to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. C-GOJZ, an MHI RJ Aviation ULC CRJ900 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA770 from Detroit Metro Airport (KDTW), MI to CYYZ. ROU1510 and JZA770 were on parallel approaches to RWY 05 and 06L respectively. Both flights were at 4000 feet descending and lateral separation decreased to less than 3 nautical miles. The minimum lateral separation reached 2.2 nautical miles. Both aircraft landed without further incidents.

C-GGOK, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland DHC-8-400 was conducting flight 8651 from Portland Intl. (KPDX), OR to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC.  On top descent approximately 28 NM SE of CYVR, flight crew received a #1 hydraulic pump caution light and shortly after the left-hand quantity indicator showed zero.  Flight crew declared a Pan Pan and landed in YVR without further incident.

C-GFVM, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-8FN was conducting flight SWG088 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Miami Intl. (KMIA), FL.  During initial climb approximately 50 NM south of CYUL, flight crew received a landing gear disagree message.  Flight crew followed the appropriate checklist, a level off was completed at 15000 feet and a decision was made to return to CYUL.  Flight crew requested ARFF to be present due to possible brake overheating following overweight landing.  Flight landed in CYUL without further incident. Maintenance found landing gears selector valve faulty and landing gear control system adjustment (tension of cables) was performed. Aircraft was returned to service.

CGSQL, un Bell 412 exploité par le Service Aérien Gouvernemental du Québec pour le compte de la Sûreté du Québec, effectuait le vol de recherches QUE150  selon les règles de vol à vue, depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, Qc (CYHU). Alors que l'appareil survolait les Îles de Boucherville, une indication "Chip light" est apparue et l'équipage a décidé de retourner à CYHU. Une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre à CYHU. Une inspection de maintenance a révélé un filament métallique  sur le détecteur de limaille du moteur droit  (PWC PT6D-3D s/n CPPSTH0384).

C-GLVU, a Swoop Incorporated Boeing 737-8, was conducting flight WSW111 from Hamilton (CYHM), ON, to Abbotsford (CYXX), BC, with 6 crew members and 177 passengers onboard. During cruise flight, a flight attendant became medically ill and the crew contacted Medlink. The flight attendant was removed from duty for the remainder of the flight and their duties were distributed amongst the remaining crew. The flight landed in CYXX without further incident.

C-FLOX, an Embraer EMB-500 operated by Flightpath Charter Airways Inc, was conducting flight KNT102 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. While on the approach for CYHZ, the flight crew selected flap, which failed to extend. The flight crew followed the QRH checklist and decided to conduct a flapless landing. The flight crew contacted CYHZ tower to request emergency services stand by and landed at CYHZ without further incident. Maintenance personnel could not reproduce the fault, and the Central Maintenance Computer download suggests a transitory condition may have caused the fault.

C-GHLM, an Air Canada Airbus A330-300 was conducting flight AC885 from Geneve-Cointrin (LSGG) Switzerland to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC.  During initial climb approximately 41 NM NNE of Lyon St-Exupéry (LFLL), France, Flight crew noticed navigation errors, was unable to fly planned waypoints and shortly thereafter lost all navigation.  Flight crew advised ATC, declared a PANPAN and diverted to LFLL where an overweight landing was performed.  Maintenance conducted a complete reset of the inertial reference system and aircraft completed flight to CYUL without further issues following maintenance.

On  07 January 2023, an Air Canada Jazz Airlines CRJ 900 (registration C-GJZT) was operating as JZA683 from Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport, MD (KBWI) to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport, ON (CYYZ). The flight crew declared an emergency for a gear indication issue and after running a checklist they requested ARFF and were re-sequenced to land. The flight crew performed a manual gear extension. The aircraft landed safely at CYYZ at 01:43Z (20:43 EST) with no further incident.

On 6 January 2023, a Jazz Aviation LP MHI RJ Aviation ULC CRJ 100-200 (registration C-GUJA, serial number 8011) was operating as JZA581 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport (KDTW), MI. During the descent, the flight crew reported a flap issue, declared an emergency (PAN PAN) and requested to divert to Toronto/Lester B Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. The aircraft landed Runway 23 at CYYZ at 2043Z without further incident.

C-FVKN, a VIH Helicopters Limited Sikorsky S-61N helicopter, was conducting heli-logging operations 39 nautical miles east-northeast of Port Hardy (CYZT), BC, with 2 flight crew onboard.
