During the fourth logging cycle of the day, the long line and grapple, containing a log, disconnected from the belly hook of the aircraft and fell approximately 50 feet into the pile of logs at the log landing. The pilots confirmed that the electrical release was not pressed on either cyclic and that the manual release between the pilots' seats was in the down (inactive) position. The aircraft returned to the service landing for inspection and landed without further incident. On inspection, maintenance found that the belly hook electrical release connector was loose. The cannon plug for the grapple and remote hook switch on the left collective was occasionally shorting when the connector was wiggled. Both issues were rectified, and the electrical belly hook release system was set to the unarmed (safe mode) position with a switch in the cockpit. The aircraft returned to logging operations using a spare grapple with no further incident.

C-FGEO, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 (Dreamliner), was conducting flight AC64 from Incheon International (RKSI), South Korea, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 13 crew and 299 passengers on board. Approximately 2 hours after takeoff, the crew received a Hydraulic Pressure C2 engine indicating and crew-alerting system (EICAS) message. Over the next 5 hours, the centre hydraulic system level declined from 0.79 to 0.49 where it stabilized. During the approach into CYVR, when the crew initially selected flaps down, they received a Slat Drive Fail message. They completed the appropriate checklist and continued their approach. When the landing gear was selected down, the crew received a Centre Hydraulic Fail message and declared a PAN PAN urgency. The aircraft landed without further incident. The crew stopped on a taxiway for inspection and then taxied to the gate under their own power.On inspection, company maintenance found hydraulic fluid on the lower fuselage fairing aft of the main landing gear wheel well where two centre hydraulic pumps are located. The C2 Hydraulic Pump had been leaking. The C2 Electric Motor Pump was replaced and a function check determined the system was serviceable.

C-FWGH, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight SWG518 from Cancun Intl. (MMUN), Mexico to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC.  During cruise approximately 125NM SE of Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON, ATC advised flight crew of a descending traffic 1000 feet above. Both aircraft reported each other in sight and flight crew received a TCAS TA (traffic advisory) followed by TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to ''descend''.  Before disconnecting the autopilot, flight crew received a second TCAS RA to ''level off'' due to a second traffic below.  Flight crew monitored the TCAS with first traffic 900 feet above and second traffic 1000 feet below and shortly received a ''clear of conflict'' message.  Flight crew notified ATC accordingly and continued to destination without further incident.

C-GIAW, a SkyCare Westwind IAL 1124A was conducting flight PHX395 from Naples municipal (KAPF), FL to Kitchener/Region of Waterloo Intl. (CYKF), ON.  During cruise in vicinity of Pittsburg Intl. (KPIT), PA, flight crew declared an emergency with ATC due to loss of hydraulic pressure and consequently would have to perform a flapless landing without thrust reversers.  Flight crew decided to continue to destination where it landed without further incident.  Maintenance found defective hydraulic line on left-hand thrust reverser supply system.

C-IFJU, un ultra-léger évolué CADI sur skis, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) à destination d'un chalet situé  60 NM au nord est de CYMT. Le lendemain, sans nouvelles de l'aéronef, les proches du pilote on déclaré l'aéronef disparu. L'appareil a été localisé à environ 1 NM de sa destination par une équipe de recherche et sauvetage des Forces Armée Canadiennes, mais les conditions météorologiques ne permettaient pas le parachutage de secours sur les lieux. Le personnel de secours a réussi à atteindre l'épave le surlendemain de l'accident. L'aéronef a percuté le sol enneigé dans une zone isolée peu boisée. Le pilote a subi des blessures mortelles. Il n'y a pas eu d'incendie.

C-FPAE, a De Havilland DHC-8-300 operated by PAL Airlines Ltd. was conducting flight PVL907 from St. John's Int'l, Newfoundland and Labrador (CYYT) to Gander Int'l, Newfoundland and Labrador (CYQX). A short time after departure, while in the climb, the flight crew observed that the oil pressure was below 40 psi on engine #2. The crew completed the QRH procedure, requested and was cleared to return to CYYT. During the descent the crew contacted ATC and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed safely at 0902 NST. Company maintenance discovered contamination in the #2 engine oil pressure transducer cannon plug (9811-9-P29/J29). The cannon plug was cleaned and metered then ground runs were completed. No defects were noted, and the aircraft was returned to service. The company has submitted SDR #20230103007 to Transport Canada.

On 04 January 2023, a WestJet Boeing 737-7CT (registration C-FWSV, serial number 32760) operating as WJA8975, was conducting a maintenance flight from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During the flight, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency due to a flap indication that required a no flap landing. WJA8975 landed CYYZ Runway 06L at 1541z without incident.The occurrence aircraft had a similar incident that morning on departure from CYHZ. During that incident the aircraft returned for landing to CYHZ. Maintenance inspected the aircraft and identified a dirty connector which was cleaned and checked with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service. (See occurrence A23A0001)For the occurrence flight, despite the asymmetry indication received at 10,000 ft after takeoff from YHZ, the crew validated that the flaps had retracted normally, and the aircraft was in a clean configuration. The flight crew elected to continue to destination and used the alternate flap extension to deploy the leading-edge devices. The flight crew performed a 0-flap landing with no airspeed or structural weight limitations exceeded.Maintenance personnel replaced the #5 flap skew sensor and connector. During the maintenance resolution, it was identified that such connector had short-circuited. The trailing edges flaps were then checked serviceable, and the aircraft returned to service. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) was filed to Transport Canada on 06-January-2023 to address reliability concerns with this particular skew sensor which was original equipment to the aircraft.

N330AP, a Gulfstream G-200 departed from runway 06L at Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, behind C-GMIW, a Boeing 737-800 (operating as Air Canada 418). N330AP exceeded a 250kt speed restriction by ATC, and flew the runway track instead of the runway heading, causing a situation where separation was not assured with C-GMIW. The ATC controller noticed the conflict and turned both aircraft, however by the time the aircraft turned, separation was reduced to 1.7 NM and 300ft.

C-FPNX, an Image Air Charter Limited Beech B200, was conducting a flight from Tri-Cities Airport (KPSC), Washington, to Calgary International (CYYC), Alberta, with 2 flight crew and 4 passengers onboard. During cruise flight, approximately 34 nautical miles south-southwest of Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International (CYXC), BC, the flight crew noticed a burning electrical smell in the cockpit with a flickering of light behind the right circuit breaker panel. The crew declared an emergency with Edmonton Area Control Centre and diverted to CYXC. The crew completed the emergency checklist, briefed the passengers on the diversion, and donned oxygen masks. The aircraft landed safely and shut down at the Flight Service building. The passengers disembarked and the Cranbrook Fire Department checked the aircraft with no hot spots found. There were no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft.Maintenance found a faulty circuit breaker in the #2 avionics system that had shorted internally. The circuit breaker was replaced and the aircraft was powered up with no faults found. The company filed a service difficulty report.

C-GTHU, a Summit Helicopters Ltd. Bell Helicopters Textron Inc. model 407 helicopter was conducting a visual flight rules (VFR) flight from the Terrace Airport (CYXT), British Columbia, to the Northern Escape Mountain Lodge, British Columbia, with one pilot and four passengers on board. While enroute, the pilot was informed that low-level fog had moved into the area; therefore, the pilot reduced descended to maintain visual reference to the ground but subsequently became disoriented due to reduced visibility. The helicopter contacted the frozen surface of Treston Lake, subsequently climbed above the fog and continued to its intended destination without further incident. After landing, an inspection of the helicopter revealed damage to the skid landing gear. There were no injuries.

C-GGCI, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight AC8298 from Vancouver International, (CYVR), BC, to Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International, (CYXC), BC, with 4 crew and 46 passengers on board. While on final approach into CYXC, the flight crew selected landing gear down and the indications showed a green light for each of the main landing gear but a red light for the nose landing gear (NLG). The red light indicates that the NLG was not down or locked. The crew discontinued the approach and requested radar vectors from air traffic control (ATC) so that they could complete the necessary checklists. The LANDING GEAR INOP caution light illuminated and the crew performed the alternate gear extension procedure which resulted in 3 green landing gear lights indicating all gear were down and locked. ATC asked the crew if they would like emergency services on arrival and the crew requested them to be on standby. The aircraft landed without incident.Maintenance conducted an inspection of the nose landing gear and replaced the NLG door actuator, NLG door solenoid sequence valve, and the NLG lock actuator. The landing gear was function tested and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GFUR, an Air Canada Airbus A330-343 was conducting flight AC914 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL.  During descent in KFLL through 12000 feet, one of the flight crew became incapacitated.  PanPan was declared with ATC and cabin crew helped assisting the ill flight crew.  Flight landed at destination without further incident.

C-FTXQ, an Air Transat Airbus A321-211 was conducting flight TSC617 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL to Quebec/Jean Lesage Intl. (CYQB), QC.  During the climb out of KFLL passing 10700 feet, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to ''descend'' and level off at 10300 feet due to traffic descending at 11000 feet.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FWSV, a Boeing 737-7CT operated by WestJet Airlines, was conducting flight WJA243 from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Shortly after departure, the flight crew communicated a flap issue to ATC and requested to be vectored while they assessed the situation. While trouble shooting the issue, the flight crew requested to return to CYHZ and to have ARFF standing by for their arrival. The aircraft landed safely at 06:46 AST.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and identified a dirty connector which was cleaned and checked with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FHEN, a WestJet Encore Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was operating as flight WEN3210 from Comox (CYQQ), BC, to Calgary International (CYYC), AB with 4 crew members and 78 passengers on board. During the initial climb, at approximately 14 000 feet above sea level, the flight crew observed a master warning followed by a CHECK FIRE DET warning light for the No. 2 engine. The crew actioned the appropriate checklist and completed a precautionary shut down of the No. 2 engine. The crew then declared a MAYDAY with air traffic control and turned back towards CYQQ. During descent, after both fire bottles had been discharged. the flight crew received a secondary master warning and fire indication for the No. 2 engine. The aircraft landed without further incident and was stopped on the runway while aircraft rescue and firefighting vehicles inspected the aircraft. There were no visual signs or thermal indications of a fire. The passengers were transported to the terminal and shortly afterwards the aircraft was towed to the apron. Maintenance found that 2 pins of a connector in the fire warning system had partially shorted together. The connector was replaced, and the engine fire detection system was tested and found serviceable. An SDR was submitted to Transport Canada. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FGKH, an Air Canada Airbus A320-200, was conducting flight AC1202 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Miami Intl. (KMIA), FL. During descent through 15 000 feet, flight crew briefly observed an unidentified RPAS in close proximity, between the captain's window and the left engine appearing to pass over the left wing. The flight crew advised ATC of the encounter, and the flight continued to KMIA without further incident. A post-flight walk-around inspection did not reveal any evidence of a collision with an object.

C-FSJH, and Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight AC1064 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Los Angeles Intl. (KLAX), CA.  During approach runway 26L in KLAX, flight crew received a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory) to ''Climb''.  Flight crew did not initiate a Go around as the alert lasted two seconds and the advisory cleared.  Flight crew advised ATC and was notified of the traffic (police helicopter).  Flight landed without further incident.

C-GEIV, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight AC558 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Los Angeles Intl. (KLAX), CA.  During initial phase of descent cleared FL370 to FL340, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to level off at FL345.  Flight crew complied with RA and advised ATC of a traffic at FL330.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FNNH, an Air Canada Boeing 777-200 was conducting flight AC51 from New Delhi/Indira Gandhi Intl. (VIDP), India to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC.  During cruise over the Atlantic Ocean within Shanwick FIR, one of the Flight crew became incapacitated as well as two cabin crews.  Flight crew was replaced by relief crew, cabin crew safety responsibilities were redistributed, and flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GJXY, un Airbus 220-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif AC1251, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport international Palm Beach – West Palm Beach en Floride aux États-Unis (KPBI) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Durant le vol, l’équipage a observé l’apparition d’un message d’avertissement « freins activés » de façon intermittente avant que celui-ci ne reste affiché en continu. L’équipage a contacté le service de maintenance d’Air Canada pour déterminer les actions à prendre. Au moment d’effectuer l’approche à CYUL, par mesure de précaution l’équipage a déclaré une urgence auprès de l’unité de contrôle de la circulation aérienne. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre et inspecté par le service de maintenance.

C-FEVD, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-8Q8 was conducting flight SWG538 from Cancun Intl. (MMUN), Mexico to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC.  At the gate in MMUN with all passengers, crew and luggage on board, Cabin Safety manager reported a strong smoke odor to the flight crew.  Captain inspected the outside of the aircraft for abnormalities and found dense black smoke coming from belt loader located near front cargo door.  First officer contacted fire services and notified ground crew which pushed the belt loader away from the airplane.  No damage noted on the aircraft and flight proceeded to destination without further incident.

C-FTXQ, un Airbus 321 exploité par Air Transat AT Inc. sous l’indicatif TS202, était en préparation pour effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Casa de Campo International Airport – La Romana (MDLR) en République dominicaine. Alors que les passagers et les membres d’équipage étaient à bord de l’aéronef stationné à la barrière numéro 66, un camion du service de restauration Sky Café a heurté la porte de soute avant lors d’une manœuvre. Un technicien d’entretien d’aéronef de la compagnie aérienne a été avisé. À la suite de l’évaluation des dommages, la décision de reporter le vol et de remplacer l’avion a été prise.

C-FGCN, un Boeing 737-300C exploité par Canadian North (Bradley Air Services Limited), sous l’indicatif AKT118, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Yellowknife, NWT (CYZF) à destination d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB). En préparation pour l’approche, l’équipage a sélectionné le train d’atterrissage en position baissée et la lumière d’indication rouge pour la roue de nez s’est allumée. Aucune autre indication lumineuse primaire pour le train d’atterrissage ne s’est allumée alors que les indications lumineuses secondaires étaient vertes. L’équipage a complété la liste de vérification d’urgence pour la sortie du train d’atterrissage et par mesure de précaution, a déclaré une urgence auprès du contrôle de la circulation aérienne. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre et des goupilles de sûreté ont été installées une fois l’aéronef immobilisé à la barrière.

C-GPCI, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Saab 340B, was operating as flight PCO3057 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC, to Nanaimo (CYCD), BC, with 25 passengers and 3 crew members on board. After touchdown in CYCD, the Anti-Skid master warning illuminated and, as the flight crew applied braking, the aircraft vibrated and pulled to the right. The flight crew used a combination of left braking and tiller to return the aircraft to the runway centerline. The aircraft taxied off the runway and was stopped on the taxiway. Airport personnel inspected the runway and the aircraft and advised the flight crew that both right main tires were substantially damaged, and that the left outboard main tire was flat. The passengers were transported to the terminal by vehicle.Maintenance inspected the aircraft structure with no damage found but all 4 main landing gear tires had to be replaced. An inspection of anti-skid transducers was then carried out and transducers in positions 1,2, and 4 were found to be serviceable. The No. 3 transducer was found to be missing a screw for the transducer drive key. This allowed the drive key to come off the shaft. The screw was found in the hub cap and was re-installed. A function test of the anti-skid system was carried out and found to be serviceable.

C-IFPS, a privately registered Buckeye Industries 582 Dream Machine powered parachute, was conducting a local flight near Endako, BC, with 1 pilot on board. During cruise, the engine (Rotax serial number 4890695) lost power and the aircraft emergency landed in a wooded area. The pilot was not injured; the aircraft sustained substantial damage. The aircraft wreckage was recovered and was not returned to service.

C-FAXD, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight SWG523 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Puerto Vallarta/Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz Intl (MMPR), Mexico.  During cruise, in the vicinity of Great Falls Intl. (KGTF), MT, a flight attendant became incapacitated.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GPCF, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Saab 340B, was conducting flight PCO3040 from Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International (CYXC), BC, to Calgary International (CYYC), AB, with 3 crew members and 30 passengers on board. During the initial climb, the crew observed a warning message indicating a hot tailpipe on the right engine (General Electric, CT7-9B). Once clear of cloud, at approximately 6000' ASL, the crew executed the relevant quick reference checklist (QRC). The hot tailpipe indication briefly extinguished but returned shortly thereafter. In accordance with the QRC, the crew shut down the right engine, declared a MAYDAY with air traffic control, and returned to CYXC. The flight landed without further incident with one engine operating. There were no injuries.Subsequent maintenance activities by the operator found that the hot tail pipe warning was a false indication that was triggered due to de-icing/anti-icing fluid contaminating the overheat detectors. The detectors were cleaned, resealed, and checked for serviceability. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-GSUR, a Government of Canada, Department of Transport DHC-8-102 (Dash 8 100) airplane, was operating as flight TGO951 from, and returning to, Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew and 2 cabin crew on board. While climbing through 21 000 feet above sea level, approximately 40 nautical miles east of Prince Rupert (CYPR), BC, a strong odour of electrical burning was smelled in the cockpit. The flight crew levelled off and turned towards CYPR in case a diversion was needed. All unnecessary electrical components were shut off, but the odour grew stronger. One pilot donned an oxygen mask as a precaution. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYPR. While shutting down the aircraft the crew observed that the weather radar screen was no longer functional, and neither was the recirculation fan.Maintenance crews were flown into CYPR to inspect the aircraft. Maintenance determined the weather radar display had failed internally. The unit was replaced. The aircraft was then vented and assessed for any other source of burning odour. No further faults were found, and the aircraft was returned to service.

The Innisfail Flying Club Cessna 150M, C-GQZM, was operating on a recreational round-robin cross-country flight from Innisfail (CEM4), AB. During landing, after the aircraft touched down and was rolling out, the aircraft contacted several snowdrifts that had blown across the runway. As the aircraft rolled through the snowdrifts, the aircraft drifted toward the left edge of the runway. The pilot added power in an attempt to gain greater rudder authority. The left main wheel contacted a windrow along the left edge of the runway and subsequently, the aircraft was pulled into the windrow and the left-wing tip contacted the ground. The nose of the aircraft and right-wing tip also struck the windrow before the aircraft came to rest. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured. The ELT did not activate; the aircraft was substantially damaged.

The Air Canada Airbus A321, C-GJVX, was operating as ACA321 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Toronto (CYYZ), ON. After departure, during climb, the flight crew observed numerous nuisance electronic centralized aircraft monitor (ECAM) messages. At FL250 the flight crew received a system 1 cabin pressure fault and excess cabin pressure warning. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency, descended to FL090 and proceeded to return to CYYC. The turnback and approach for landing were uneventful. The flight crew conducted an overweight landing and stopped the aircraft on the runway due to possible hot brakes. The aircraft brakes were inspected by ARFF and the aircraft was released to taxi back to the gate. There were no injuries. Company maintenance performed an overweight landing inspection with no fault found. The cabin pressure controller (CPC) was replaced, and the aircraft was released for continued service.

C-GBZS, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight SWG699 from Varadero/Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl. (MUVR), Cuba to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB.  During cruise in vicinity of Minneapolis-St. Paul/Wold-Chamberlain Intl. (KMSP), MN, a flight attendant became incapacitated.  Safety duties were redistributed, and flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GBIJ, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114 was conducting flight ROU1993 from Fort Myers/Southwest Florida Intl. (KRSW), FL to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC.  In vicinity of Franklin VORTAC (FKN), VA at FL350, ATC advised flight crew of a traffic climbing 1000 feet below.  Thirty seconds later, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) ''climb''.  Flight crew complied with RA and ATC was advised.  At FL355 flight crew received ''clear of conflict'' and continued to destination without further incident.

C-GLQH, a Porter Airlines Dash 8-400, was conducting flight POE9807 from Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. Shortly after takeoff, the flight crew selected the landing gear up, and observed that it did not retract. After the crew conducted some troubleshooting and checklists, they declared a PAN PAN and requested a return to CYOW, where they landed uneventfully. A post flight inspection revealed that the landing gear ground locks had not been removed before the flight.

C-FCAG, a Chartright Air Group Cessna 560 Citation Ultra was conducting flight HRT510 from Palm Beach Intl. (KPBI), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During cruise in vicinity of Savannah/Hilton Head Intl. (KSAV), GA, aircraft suffered rapid decompression.  Flight crew donned mask and dropped passenger's mask, initiate an emergency descent to 10000 feet and declared MAYDAY with ATC.  Flight crew elected to divert to KSAV where they landed without further incident.  Maintenance is troubleshooting the issue.

C-GLQH, a Porter Airlines Dash 8-400, was conducting flight POE 2285 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Halifax Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. Approximately 20 minutes after departing CYTZ, the flight crew received indication of #2 HYD LOW PRESSURE. After troubleshooting and completing the appropriate checklists, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and requested to divert to the Ottawa International Airport (CYOW), ON, which was approximately 100 nautical miles ahead of them. The flight landed uneventfully at CYOW.

C-GZVJ, a Beech 1900D operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG758 from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON to Red Lake (CYRL), ON. During the approach to CYRL, the landing gear was selected to the down position but there was no corresponding movement of the landing gear. The crew elected to return to CYXL and declared an emergency. The crew consulted the QRH and identified a tripped landing gear circuit breaker. They reset the tripped circuit breaker, the gear lowered normally, and an uneventful landing was conducted at CYXL.The operator's maintenance replaced the landing gear relay. Gear swings were carried out and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GGCI, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Q400), was conducting flight JZA8317 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Comox (CYQQ), BC, with 4 crew and 37 passengers on board. At the top of climb, the propeller speed was reduced to the cruise setting of 850 rpm. As the aircraft began to accelerate the No. 1 propeller (Dowty Rotol, R408/6-123-F/17) rpm increased to 1090 rpm, an overspeed condition, with concurrent aircraft yaw. The propeller electronic control (PEC) No. 1 caution light illuminated and the overspeed drill was carried out; the propeller was feathered and the left engine was shut down. The flight crew completed the required checklists and declared a "Pan Pan" urgency with air traffic control (ATC). The crew informed ATC that they required a return to CYVR. The aircraft landed without incident and, after being inspected by aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF), taxied to their gate without assistance.Maintenance confirmed that a propeller overspeed had occurred and replaced the No. 1 engine pitch control unit assembly and the No. 1 engine propeller electronic control unit. Function checks were carried out and the aircraft was returned to service. A Service Difficulty Report was submitted to Transport Canada.

C-GWEN, a de Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 operated by WestJet Encore Limited, was conducting flight WEN9961 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK, to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB, with 4 crew members and no passengers on board. During the takeoff roll, the “ENG ADAPT HEAT 2” caution light illuminated at approximately 30 knots. The crew rejected the take-off and a MAYDAY was declared with air traffic control.  Once the crew had diagnosed the cause of the warning, the emergency was canceled. The crew conducted a second takeoff, during rotation the “ENG ADAPT HEAT 2” caution light illuminated momentarily and then remained off. The pilots continued the flight and landed safely in CYYC. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft.The operator's maintenance replaced the intake heater and wire harness, and completed operational test of heaters with no faults found. The aircraft was then returned to service.

The WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, C-FQWE, was operating as WEN3181 from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Kelowna (CYLW), BC. During the take-off roll above 80 knots, the flight crew observed the fuselage doors warning light illumination. The take-off was rejected and the flight crew declared a MAYDAY. The aircraft exited runway with no issues and the flight crew cancelled the MAYDAY. WEN3181 returned to gate for maintenance troubleshooting. There were no injuries. Company maintenance found the Aft Service Door Locked sensor was unserviceable. The Service Door Warning annunciation was deferred under MEL on 21 December 2022 and the aircraft was released for continued service. The sensor wire harness was replaced on 22 December 2022.

C-FVNF, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was conducting flight AC5 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to New Tokyo Intl (RJAA), Japan.  During initial approach through FL120 with seat belt sign on and flight crew expecting a zone of turbulence, a passenger stood up to go to the lavatory.  When coming back, flight attendant signaled the passenger to proceed to assigned seat and fastened seat belt.  Passenger returned slowly to the seat and expected strong moderate turbulence was encountered.  Passenger fell on the floor and suffered serious injuries.  Flight landed without further incident and passenger was transferred to EMS care.

C-GGMN, a DH8D operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA7955 from Montreal Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, to the Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, with 4 crew and 76 passengers on board. During the enroute portion of the flight, the crew had received a #2 DC GEN caution message. The crew actioned the appropriate checklist, which led them to shut down the #2 generator. Approximately 25 minutes later, while setting up for the approach into CYTZ, the crew received a #2 GEN HOT caution message. The crew declared PAN PAN, and requested diversion to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, where the flight landed uneventfully.

The Airsprint Cessna C525B (CJ3), C-FNAS, was operating as ASP473 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Grande Prairie (CYQU), AB. The Calgary Tower combined East/West controller cleared ASP473 for takeoff on Runway 35L while the Air Canada, Boeing 737 MAX, C-FSDB, which was operating as ACA394 from CYYC to Halifax (CYHZ), NS, was already cleared for takeoff on Runway 35R. As AC394 lifted off, the flight crew did not initiate the 15 degree turn to the right as required by the COWBOY SID immediately after departure, to ensure a divergent flight path until 3 nm or greater separation was assured. As ASP473 lifted off RWY 35L it was 2.6 nm from ACA394 which had departed RWY 35R, which resulted in a loss of separation.

C-FONV, a Eurocopter EC130 B4 operated by the Province of Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources, was engaged in aerial survey work within the northwest portion of the control zone at Timmins Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), Ontario, with the pilot and three passengers on board. During the flight, while approximately 4nm to the NW of CYTS at 250 feet AGL, the pilot received an aural caution, followed by an indication of low engine (Arriel 2B1) oil pressure. The pilot turned towards CYTS and announced his intentions to return to the airport. During the next 30 seconds, accompanied by additional warnings, the oil pressure began to drop rapidly. The pilot elected to make a precautionary landing on a frozen swamp, where he landed the helicopter and shut down the engine without incident. The occupants were picked up by another Ontario MNR helicopter within 15 minutes and were brought back to the airport. Initial inspection showed that the oil tank was empty, and the tail of the helicopter was covered in oil. It was determined that the magnetic oil breather seal (P/N 9560115450) had failed, resulting in the loss of oil pressure. The presence of oil in the reservoir after the precautionary landing indicated that the engine had not been operated without lubrication during the landing. The seal was replaced before the helicopter was flown back to CYTS on 3 January 2023.

C-FYXF, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was conducting flight ROU1834 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Montego Bay/Sangster Intl. (MKJS), Jamaica.   During climb through FL230 approximately 100nm S of CYUL, TCAS target suddenly appeared which generated a TCAS TA (traffic advisory) followed by TCAS RA (resolution advisory) ''Climb''.  RA was complied with, and associated target disappeared several seconds later.  Flight crew advised ATC who was unaware of any traffic in that area.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FJKK, a Carson Air Fairchild Swearingen SA227-AC (Metro III) airplane, was conducting cargo flight CRN8064 from Calgary (CYYC), AB, toKamloops (CYKA), BC, with 2 crew members on board. After landing, the crew experienced loss of directional control which resulted in a runway excursion to the right of the runway. The right main landing gear departed the runway edge and the right propeller struck a runway light which resulted in damage to 2 of its 4 blades. There were no injuries.The aircraft remains in CYKA awaiting maintenance.

C-GEGG, a privately registered Cessna 172I was conducting a recreational visual flight rules trip from Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC, to Chilliwack (CYCW), BC, with only the pilot on board. The airplane landed on Runway 07 and the pilot planned to exit at Taxiway C. When the airplane was turned left onto the taxiway, the wind began to push it further left until the left main landing gear contacted the edge of the taxiway. A wind gust then lifted the right wing and the airplane flipped over on the snow-covered grass beside the taxiway. The pilot, wearing a 4-point safety harness, was uninjured and egressed from the overturned airplane. A local aircraft maintenance organization determined that there was damage to both wings, propeller, rudder, and the left wing strut.

C-FKTE, a Carson Air Limited Beechcraft B300 (King Air 350) was operating as flight CRN911+ from Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International (CYXC), BC, to Kelowna (CYLW), BC, with 2 crew members and 4 passengers on board. During the approach into CYLW, the crew selected gear down and the nose gear light did not illuminate indicating the nose gear was not down and locked. The crew conducted a missed approach and conducted the appropriate checklists. After manually extending the landing gear, they maneuvered for another approach and requested Airport Rescue Firefighting crews to be on standby. The aircraft landed safely and the crew was able to taxi it off the runway under its own power.Maintenance found the light bulb in the nose gear annunciator light was burnt out. They replaced the bulb and a test of the landing gear indication system was completed successfully. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-FGKJ, a cargo-configured Boeing 757-200 operated by CargoJet Airways Ltd., departed Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with a destination of Montreal/Mirabel Intl (CYMX), QC. Approximately 45 minutes after takeoff, the crew was alerted to a fire indication on the left engine (Rolls-Royce RB211-535E4-37). The crew carried out an in-flight shutdown of the left engine, declared an emergency, and, upon consulting company operations, elected to return to CYWG. The crew did not deploy the fire suppression system as the fire indication cleared when the engine was idled down during the shutdown procedure. The aircraft landed without further issues. The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and a defect in the fire detection system is suspected. Troubleshooting and maintenance is being performed with company and engine manufacturer resources.

C-GQPC, un SAAB 340B exploité par Pascan Aviation sous l'indicatif PSC414, effectuait un vol d'essai selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis et à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU). Lors de la descente pour le retour vers CYHU, une perte de puissance sur le moteur droit a été notée. La liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour "ENGINE FAILURE" et "ONE ENGINE INOPERATIVE" a été effectuée. Les pilotes ont pris la décision de sécuriser le moteur droit éteint et de déclarer une urgence. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre, pas de blessé. La maintenance a remplacé le regulateur de survitesse de l'hélice et retourné l'avion en service.

The Central Mountain Air de Havilland DHC-8-100, C-FVRJ, was operating as GLR9476 from Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB to Edmonton (CYEG), AB. After departure, during the initial climb, the flight crew selected landing gear up and the nose landing gear partially retracted. The landing gear unsafe light associated warning lights illuminated indicating that the nose landing gear was not up and locked. The flight crew attempted to extend the landing gear with no change to the nose landing gear. The QRH was actioned, and a manual landing gear extension was attempted; however, the nose landing gear remained partially extended. The flight crew declared an emergency and returned to CYMM. The aircraft landed with the nose landing gear in a partially extended position. On touchdown, the nose landing gear did not collapse, and the nose structure of the aircraft remained free from contact with the runway surface. The aircraft came to a stop on the runway and was shut down. The aircraft received minor damage to the nose landing gear doors. The passengers were deplaned and transported back to the terminal; there were no injuries. Company maintenance found the nose oleo to be flat. The aircraft was ferried to CYYC the next day for repair of the nose gear assembly. The nose gear is to be removed and set out for inspection

C-GREJ, an ATR 72-212A operated by Calm Air International LP, was conducting flight CAV788 from Big Trout Lake (CYTL), ON to Red Lake (CYRL), ON. While the aircraft was on the ramp at CYRL after the flight, the crew elected to back up the aircraft under its own power. While backing up, C-GREJ tail struck a privately registered Piper PA-23-160 aircraft that was parked on the ramp. Both aircraft sustained minor damage. C-GREJ was grounded in CYRL until the applicable repairs were completed by the operator's maintenance and has since been returned to service.

C-GHLV, an Air Canada Boeing 767-333 was conducting flight AC7261 from Bogotá/El Nuevo Dorado Intl. (SKBO), Colombia to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During cruise in vicinity of Charleston/West Virginia Intl. Yeager (KCRW), WV, Flight crew declared a PanPan with ATC due to a cracked windshield.  Flight crew elected to continue to destination where it landed without further incident.

C-FFLC, a Flair Airlines Ltd. B737-800, was conducting flight FLE176 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to the Harry Reid International Airport (KLAS), USA, with 6 crew and 149 passengers on board. During takeoff in gusty crosswind conditions on Runway 23, the tail skid made contact with the runway due to over-rotation. The aircraft continued uneventfully to its destination. Maintenance inspection of the crush cartridge indicated that it had not exceeded limitations, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FLIX un Boeing 737-8K5 avait un vol selon les règle de vol aux instruments prévu depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC à destination de l’aéroport de Juan Gualberto Gómez Airport, à Varadero, Cuba (MUVR). Lors du taxi vers la piste de décollage, un agent de bord a eu un malaise et n'était pas en mesure de faire le vol prévu. L'appareil est revenu à l'aérogare et l'agent de bord a été remplacé par un autre agent de bord de la compagnie. Le vol prévu a ensuite été effectué sans encombre.

C-GKPX, a Swearingen SA226-TC operated by 2080061 Ontario Inc (dba SkyCare), was operating a flight from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Toronto/Lester B Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During the takeoff roll on Runway 07, the aircraft veered to the right and the main RH landing gear tires ran into the berm of snow on the inside of the runway. The propeller remained clear of the snow and the crew managed to stop the aircraft while still on the runway surface. It was noticed that the right propeller’s start-lock was still engaged. There was no damage to the aircraft or injuries to the crew or passengers. The start lock was disengaged, aircraft was backtracked to the threshold, and was re-cleared for takeoff on the same runway. The flight continued without further incident.

C-GKIV un cessna 560 Citation Ultra exploité par Keewatin Air LP effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport d’Iqualuit, NU (CYFB) à destination de l'aéroport d’Ottawa/Macdonald Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW). À l'amorce de la descente sur CYOW au niveau de vol 200, la puissance des moteurs a été réduite au ralenti. Le moteur droit s'est éteint peu après que les pilotes aient noté que le N2 du moteur droit était descendu à 38%. La vérification de la liste des procédures d'urgence a été effectuée et le moteur droit a été redémarré avec succès. Les pilotes ont pris soin de ne pas redescendre la manette des gaz du moteur droit sur sa butée de ralenti. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre avec ses deux moteurs à sa destination initiale. Aucun dommage ni blessé. L'équipe de  maintenance ont ajusté le régime de ralenti et la tringlerie du contrôle de carburant dans les limites prescrites.

C-GLJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA7948 from Toronto/Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. While enroute to CYDF, a flight attendant began to feel ill and was unable to perform their duties. The remaining cabin crew member performed the duties during the flight. An able-bodied passenger was assigned a seat adjacent to the emergency exits and was briefed on their operation. Emergency medical services were called and met the flight after landing in CYDF.

C-FPLS, a Swoop Inc. Boeing 737-800 was operating as flight WO314 from Abbotsford (CYXX), BC, to Toronto International (CYYZ), ON, with 6 crew members and 183 passengers on board. During cruise, a flight attendant became ill and took a passenger seat for the duration of the flight and their duties were distributed amongst the remaining crew. The flight landed in CYYZ without further incident. Emergency Medical Services were not required.

C-GWWN, a Beech 200 operated by Transwest Air Limited Partners (dba Rise Air), was conducting a medevac flight from La Ronge/Barber Field (CYVC), SK to Wollaston Lake (CZWL), SK. Approximately 10 minutes after takeoff while climbing through 17000 ft ASL, smoke began to exit the floor vents in the passenger cabin. Shortly thereafter, smoke was observed in the cockpit. The crew switched off the cabin environmental control and the smoke began to dissipate. The crew requested ATC for a return to CYVC. The crew then completed the checklists for smoke/fire. The aircraft landed at CYVC without further issues. The operator has grounded the aircraft until it can be inspected, and the cause of the smoke determined.AMENDED 22 FEBRUARY 2023

C-GFAF, un Airbus 330-343 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA7140, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Toronto Pearson International, ON (CYYZ). Peu après le décollage, de la fumée a été observée dans la cabine et dans le poste de pilotage. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil est revenu se poser sans encombre à CYUL. Une inspection de l'appareil a été effectuée et la source de la fumée a été déterminée comme étant une ingestion de fluide de dégivrage.

C-FOGP un Beech 100 exploité par Max Aviation Inc. sous l'indicatif MAX120, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) à destination de l'aéroport de Wabush, NL (CYWK). Lors de l'approche pour la piste 36, l'équipage a sorti le train d'atterrissage. L'indication de la roue de nez montrait qu'elle n'était pas sécurisée. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'équipage a décidé de revenir atterrir à Sept-Îles pour des raisons opérationnelles. Le train a été sorti manuellement et l'appareil s'est posé à Sept-Îles sans encombre. Aucun blessé.

N744CK, a cargo-configured Boeing 747-400 operated by Kalitta Air, was conducting flight CKS636 from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky Intl (KCVG), USA to Anchorage/Ted Stevens Intl (PANC), USA. While enroute, the flight crew received multiple status messages for Cargo FWD 1 and 2, fire Protection loops A and B.  Subsequently, the EICAS (Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System) displayed FIRE CARGO FWD warning message, as well as a Master Warning message, and the audible fire bell. The crew completed the cargo fire procedures and discharged the fire suppression system into the forward cargo compartment.  The crew then declared an emergency with Winnipeg Center and initially turned toward Cold Lake/Group Captain R.W. McNair (CYOD), AB when the aircraft was approximately 25 NM south-southwest of Flin Flon, MB. Winnipeg Center suggested to the crew that Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE) was closer, and the crew agreed that was a better option.  The crew proceeded towards CYXE and jettisoned fuel in order to decrease the aircraft weight to the maximum landing weight.  The aircraft landed safely at CYXE. Airport Emergency Services then approached the aircraft and scanned for heat sources with a thermal detector. No heat sources were detected, and the crew and Airport Emergency Services agreed it was safe to taxi the aircraft to a parking area. Once the crew was safely off the aircraft, the forward cargo compartment was opened. The discharge of the fire suppression was confirmed, and no damage to aircraft was noticed. The operator’s maintenance later determined that the fire indication was due to a fault in the fire detection system as they found evidence of AFOLTS cards shorted due to water damage. The cards were replaced, a thorough check of the system was carried out, and the aircraft was returned to service.

N314TW, a Dassault-Breguet Falcon 20, operated by Ameristar (Sierra American Corporation), departed the Detroit/Willow Run Airport (KYIP) MI, destined for the London International Airport (CYXU), Ontario. It was a cargo flight with 2 flight crew members on board. The ILS runway 15 approach was conducted during the hours of darkness.  After touchdown, the aircraft started to deviate to the left; a runway excursion occurred onto the grass next to the runway. The aircraft continued travelling in the grass and mud, parallel to the runway for approximately 1100 feet before coming to a stop. The aircraft came to rest about 100 feet from the hard surface. There were no injuries.

C-FJZD, un CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7785, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de St-John's, NF (CYYT) à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 54 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Alors que l’aéronef était en approche finale vers la piste 06L à CYUL, une indication de fumée dans la soute avant est survenue. L’équipage a avisé l’ATC et les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. En courte finale, l’indication de fumée a disparu et l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre. Par mesure de précaution, les SLIA ont inspecté l’appareil et n’ont trouvés aucune évidence de feu ni de fumée. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FNOH, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was conducting flight AC848 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Frankfurt/Rhein-Main (EDDF), Germany.  During cruise over North Sea at FL370, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence resulting in an overspeed of 15 to 20 kts for 10-15 seconds and abrupt loss of altitude up to 400 feet. Seatbelt sign was off at the time as flight conditions were smooth prior to the event. No injuries were reported, and ATC was advised of altitude deviation/turbulence encounter. Flight continued to destination without further incident and maintenance inspected the aircraft with no defect found.

C-GSJB, un Airbus 319-112 exploité par exploité par Air Canada Rouge LP sous l’indicatif ROU1816, se préparait à effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à destination de Punta Cana en République Dominicaine (MDPC) avec 114 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage. Pendant le dégivrage de l’aéronef au sol, à la barrière avant le départ, le godet d'un camion de dégivrage a accroché un déperditeur de potentiel (Static Wick) sur l'ailette de bout d'aile gauche. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et les dommages ont été limités au dépertiteur.

C-FTIL, un ATR-42-500 exploité par Canadian North sous l’indicatif AKT818 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) à destination de Pond Inlet, NU (CYIO) avec 33 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage à bord. L'équipage a procédé au dégivrage de l'aéronef avant le décollage. Lors de la montée, l’équipage a ressenti une vibration continue sur les palonniers et le personnel de cabine à l’arrière de l’avion a aussi ressenti la vibration dans l’avion. L’équipage a décidé de revenir atterrir à CYFB et l’avion s’est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’avion. L’inspection après l’envolée a révélé une présence de glace sur la partie centrale de l’aile, au-dessus du fuselage de l’avion ainsi que sur certaines surfaces critiques de l'aéronef.

C-FJOK, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 operating as flight ROU1707 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ) to Las Vegas/Harry Reid Intl. (KLAS), NV. After landing on RWY 26L in KLAS, ATC advised flight the observation of white smoke from LH main landing gear. ARFF was dispatched by ATC to investigate, and the aircraft came to rest on TWY B. The affected brake temp did not indicate greater than 350C. After coming to rest, the brake temperature was stable and began to decrease. The aircraft continued to gate with ARFF in trail as a precaution, no further smoke was observed.

N5EQ, a privately operated Piper PA 46-350P (PT6A-35 powered JetProp DLX conversion) was conducting an IFR flight from Sept-Îles airport (CYZV), QC to Goose Bay airport (CYYR), NL. The aircraft was on the approach for Runway 08 at CYYR and had been cleared to land. The aircraft struck terrain at 10:02 AST, when about 2.5 NM southwest (53° 16' 46.931'' N, 060° 30' 18.013'' W) of the airport along the extended centerline for Runway 08. The 406 MHz ELT activated, and the signal was received by the JRCC. A helicopter was launched as an emergency response from Canadian Forces Base 5 Wing - Goose Bay and rescue medical personnel were hoisted down to the aircraft. The 2 occupants were airlifted to a waiting ambulance with serious injuries and were transported to the local hospital. The pilot later died due to injuries sustained. The aircraft was destroyed. Two TSB Investigators deployed to the site.

C-GWRI, a de Havilland DHC-8-103 aircraft operated by Summit Air, departed Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON for Fort Hope (CYFH), ON, with a crew of 3 and 24 passengers onboard. Shortly after takeoff, the #1 engine's (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW121) propeller began to overspeed. The crew consulted the QRH and then completed a shutdown of the #1 engine. An emergency was declared and the aircraft then returned to CYQT where the aircraft landed safely.

N729QS, a Bombardier BD-100-1A10 aircraft operated by NetJets Aviation, was conducting a flight from Westchester County Airport (KHPN), NY to Farnborough Airport (EGLF), England. During cruise, the crew heard a loud noise and hissing sound in the cabin. The crew elected to land as soon as practical, declared an emergency and diverted to St. John’s Airport (CYYT), NL, where the aircraft landed without further issue.Maintenance determined the noise to be a malfunction of the cabin audio equipment. The equipment was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FPBJ, an Air Tindi de Havilland DHC-7, was operated as flight TIN806 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON. Approximately 68 nm SE of CYZF the number 3 engine (PRATT & WHITNEY-CAN, PT6A-50) was shut down as a precaution due to high torque indications and fuel fluctuations. A Pan Pan was declared and the flight returned to CYZF with no further issues.

C-GUAC, an Air Canada, Airbus Canada Limited Partnership A220-300, was conducting flight ACA774 from Los Angeles Intl. (KLAX), CA to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QB. The aircraft was being operated with a deferred MEL for the oil debris above limits on the right-hand engine. After departure, the advisory message ''oil debris'' for the right-hand engine illuminated on the EICAS. While in cruise flight at FL350, the flight crew received a repeated but intermittent, right-hand ''engine vibration'' caution message, along with a right-hand ''Fan VIB'' indication. The flight crew completed the abnormal checklist, discussed the situation with dispatch and maintenance control and elected to continue the flight towards CYUL.  In the vicinity of Minneapolis-St. Paul Intl/Wold-Chamberlain (KMSP), MN, the right-hand engine failed and shut down automatically.  The system attempted an auto-relight as designed but failed. The flight crew completed the checklist, declared a MAYDAY with ATC and elected to divert to KMSP where it landed without further incident.  Maintenance at KMSP is investigating.

C- GFAF, un Airbus A330-343 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA301 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) avec 285 passagers et 10 membres d’équipage. Lors de la rétraction des volets en montée initiale après le décollage, ceux-ci sont demeurés bloqués à la position 2. L’équipage a décidé de revenir atterrir à CYUL et a déclaré un état d’urgence. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés et l’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 06L sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GOPW, un Boeing 737-275C exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE781, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Puvirnituq, QC (CYPX) avec 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, l’équipage a détecté une odeur de brulé et quelques instants plus tard le détecteur de fumée de la toilette s’est déclenché. Une inspection visuelle de la cabine a révélé la présence de fumée blanche dans la cabine. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a effectué une approche visuelle vers la piste 06L. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés et l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FTXQ, an Air Transat Airbus A321-211 was conducting flight TSC612 From Quebec City/Jean Lesage Intl. (CYQB), QC to Punta Cana Intl. (MDPC), Dominican Republic. During cruise over Burlington Intl. (KBTV), VT, a cabin crew became incapacitated. Emergency positions and safety responsibilities were reassigned to remaining crew and an active Air Transat cabin crew travelling for leisure occupied jump seat for landing. Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GMRB, a Cessna 172M, operated by Mitchinson Flying Service Limited, was taxing on taxiway Foxtrot at Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker (CYXE), SK with the intent to conduct a solo training flight with only the student pilot onboard. At the same time, C-FFEL a Boeing 737-800 operated by Flair Airlines as flight FLE290 was on a half mile short final at 300 feet AGL for Runway 27 at CYXE with a crew of six and 145 passengers onboard. ATC instructed C-GMRB to taxi and hold short of Runway 27 on taxiway Foxtrot. The pilot read back the instruction but continued to taxi and lined up the aircraft on the runway. The flight crew of C-FFEL noticed C-GMRB enter the runway, queried ATC, and received an instruction to conduct a go-around. ATC then instructed C-GMRB to exit the runway. C-FFEL commenced another approach and landed safely on Runway 27 a short time later.

C-GLQE, a Porter Airlines Inc. De Havilland DHC-8-402 was conducting flight POE2939 from Toronto / Billy Bishop (CYTZ), ON to Boston/ General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl. (KBOS), MA. During approach at KBOS and upon gear down selection, flight crew observed L/H Gear did not indicate green on the gear selector panel.  Flight crew declared an emergency and landed uneventfully at destination airport.

F-HSAS, a Dassault Falcon 7X operated by Global Jet Luxembourg, was conducting a flight from Paris Le Bourget Airport (LFPB) FR to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR) NY. While enroute cruising at FL400, the flight crew received a cockpit indication from the crew alerting system (CAS), of a high cabin altitude. The cabin altitude was crosschecked and was not out of parameters and the decision was to monitor and proceed at FL400. In the vicinity of LOMSI intersection, approximately 185nm E of CYYR, the cabin altitude started to rapidly increase and the decision was made to conduct an emergency descent. The flight crew declared a MAYDAY with ATC and donned their oxygen masks. The cabin crew also donned their masks. During the descent through FL250, the cabin altitude began to restore to normal indications and the flight crew requested to level off at FL200. The MAYDAY was cancelled, and the decision was made to continue to KEWR. The aircraft landed safely at 14:57 UTC.Maintenance conducted system checks and found that the electrical flow control unit (EFCU) was providing false information to the oxygen and pressurisation systems. The EFCU was replaced, tested and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FHTI, a privately registered Cessna 172 operated by Golden Ears Flying Club, was taxiing for a local flight with 1 pilot on board. While taxiing on the apron, the pilot turned right to pass an aircraft taxiing from the opposite direction on the apron. After passing the opposite direction aircraft, the pilot began turning left to continue his taxi. During this turn, the aircraft's right wing struck the terminal building. The pilot advised air traffic control, shut down the engine, and pushed the aircraft back to its parking spot to assess the damage. There were no injuries; the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GOIF, an Air Transat A321-271NX was conducting flight TSC233 and took off from Faro Airport (LPFR), Portugal for a second time following occurrence A22F0387, for Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. Approximately 15 minutes after takeoff, the flight crew received another ECAM message telling them to retard ENG number 2 thrust lever to IDLE. Thrust lever number 2 was put at idle, the crew declared a PAN PAN and the flight returned to departure airport LPFR and landed safely with no further incident. The aircraft was then grounded for maintenance.

C-GXFC, a Buffalo Airways Lockheed Electra L188, was operating as flight BFL1208 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Hope Bay (CHB3), NU.  At flight level FL190, approximately 60 nm NE of CYZF, the number 3 engine (ALLISON, 501-D13) fire bells sounded and fire light illuminated. A precautionary engine shutdown was conducted in accordance with the company's standard operating procedures (SOPs) and the flight returned to CYZF and landed with no further issues. An emergency was not declared.Following the flight the maintenance team found that the number 3 engine fire control relay for zone 1 was corroded and caused false indications. The relay was replaced and tested the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOIF, an Air Transat A321-271NX was conducting flight TSC233 from Faro Airport (LPFR), Portugal to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. Approximately 15 minutes after takeoff, the flight crew received an ECAM message telling them to retard ENG number 2 thrust lever to IDLE. Thrust lever number 2 was put at idle, the crew declared a PAN PAN and the flight returned to departure airport LPFR and landed safely with no further incident.

C-GPSK, un Jetstream BAE 3201 exploité par Pascan sous l'indicatif PSC787 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de l'aéroport Michel Pouliot de Gaspé, QC (CYGP) à destination de l'aéroport des Îles-de-la-Madeleine, QC (CYGR). Lors de la montée vers l'altitude de croisière, au travers de 7000 pieds, l’équipage a observé des fluctuations de puissance sur le moteur droit. L'équipage a actionné la liste de vérifications du manuel de référence rapide (QRH). Une réduction de la puissance du moteur affecté à permis de le stabiliser, mais l'indication du couple de puissance a alors affiché une valeur nulle. Considérant que l'indication de température et de pression d'huile était nominale, l'équipage a décidé de laisser tourner le moteur et de déclarer un PAN PAN avant de revenir atterrir sans encombre à CYGP.

C-GJJF, un Beechcraft King Air A100 exploité par Propair sous l'indicatif PRO4451, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) à destination de l'aéroport de La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL). Peu après le décollage, lors de la sélection du train à la position rentrée, une indication de position anormale du train d'atterrissage est apparue. Après avoir effectué un nouveau cycle de sélection du train, l'indication normale du train à la position rentrée a été obtenue. L'équipage a poursuivi le vol vers CYGL.  Durant le vol, les pilotes ont tenté de sortir le train d'atterrissage, et, à chaque tentative, une indication de position anormale du train est apparue. L'équipage a alors décidé d'effectuer un déroutement vers l'aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT). La liste de vérifications avant la descente a été actionnée et, en raison d'indications de train non sécurisé, la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été actionnée. Une fois la procédure de sortie d'urgence du train complétée, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence (MAYDAY). L'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre à CYMT.

On 06 December 2022, the Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400 (registration C-GGNY, serial 4386) was operating as flight JZA8139 on a scheduled passenger flight from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), Alberta to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), Alberta. Onboard were 4 crew and 75 passengers. After landing, the aircraft taxied to its assigned gate. At approximately 1940 mountain standard time, while holding short of its assigned gate, the flight crew heard the fire warning and observed flight deck indications of a fire on engine #1 (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW150A). The captain shut down both engines, pulled the #1 T-handle and discharged both extinguishing bottles. The first officer advised ATC to send airport rescue and fire fighters. The fire indication remained so the captain commanded a rapid deplanement. There were no injuries during the rapid deplanement. There were no visible indications of an actual fire. Maintenance follow up: Maintenance personnel found a faulty connector in the fire detection system. Parts were replaced and operational checks completed and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GOHX, a Novajet Bombardier Challenger 300 was conducting flight 105931 from St-John's Intl. (CYYT), NL to Tampa Intl. (KTPA), FL.  During cruise approximately 150 NM N of KTPA flight crew received EICAS (Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System) warning for fluctuating #1 engine hydraulic temperature that exceeded the limitation of the system.  Flight crew completed the appropriate checklist procedure which resulted in shutting down the #1 engine.  The flight crew declared an emergency and completed a single engine approach and landing at KTPA.  Nosewheel steering was affected as a result of the loss of #1 engine hydraulic system and although the Flight crew could safely exit the runway, a tow vehicle was required to reposition the aircraft to the fixed based operator.Update 9 December 2022: Maintenance team has determined the LH engine driven hydraulic pump malfunctioned which caused a hydraulic fluid overheat condition. The maintenance team is working on replacing the affected component and the other affected components with the support of Bombardier

C-FTJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP, Bombardier CRJ900, flight JZA780, departed Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, for Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (KDCA), DC. After takeoff, the flight crew selected gear up and received a proximity system fault message. The flight crew declared a Pan Pan, completed the QRH checklist and elected to return to Toronto, landing without further incident.

C-FXPR, un Diamond DA42 exploité par Cargair Ltée, effectuait un vol  selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Sherbrooke, QC (CYSC) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec à son bord un instructeur et un élève-pilote. Alors que l'aéronef survolait l'aéroport de St-Hyacinthe, QC (CSU3) le moteur droit ( Thielert TAE 125-02-99, s/n 020203903) a manifesté un rythme irrégulier suivi d'une indication "R ECU A & B FAIL". Le moteur a alors été fermé par mesure de précaution. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'instructeur a demandé une priorité d'atterrissage à CYHU où l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre.Suite à l'évènement, une inspection mécanique a révélé qu'un injecteur de carburant défectueux était à l'origine du problème.

N8903A, un Bombardier CRJ200 exploité par Endeavor Air, effectuait le vol EDV4997 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County, MI (KDTW) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Alors que l'aéronef effectuait un virage pour s'aligner en finale pour la piste 24R à CYUL, il y a eu une perte d'espacement avec C-GTJA, un Bombardier CJR200 exploité par Jazz Aviation sous l'indicatif JZA10, en provenance de l'aéroport d'Ottawa International, ON (CYOW) qui le précédait. L'espacement à été réduit à 2.8 milles nautiques alors que l'espacement requis est de 3 milles nautiques. ATC a alors donné une instruction à N8903A, modifiant sa trajectoire. L'aéronef s'est alors retrouvé trop près de ACA760, un Boeing A220-300 exploité par Air Canada en provenance de San Francisco, CA (KSFO) qui était lui aussi en approche pour la piste 24R.

On the evening of 05 December 2022, a privately owned Cessna 150G (registration C-FQCS) was conducting a night visual flight rules flight from Salaberry-de-Valleyfield Airport (CSD3), Quebec to Cornwall-Summerstown Regional Airport (CYCC), Ontario. It was reported that at approximately 2000 eastern standard time, the engine had a power loss and the pilot attempted to conduct a forced landing on or beside Highway 401, north of the Lancaster Airpark (CLA6), Ontario. Prior to landing, the aircraft collided with power lines that crossed the highway. The aircraft impacted terrain in the grassy median between the east- and west-bound highway lanes. The pilot and passenger were seriously injured and transported to a hospital in Ottawa, Ontario. The aircraft was destroyed. There was no fire. The aircraft ELT was activated.

C-GDPI, un Beech King Air A100 exploité par Propair Inc., effectuait le vol PRO4005 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Wabush, NL (CYWK) à destination de l'aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT). Après avoir relu correctement l'instruction du contrôleur de la circulation aérienne de voler la radiale 240 du VOR de YWK, PRO4005 est apparu 8NM au nord de celle-ci. Il y a eu une perte de séparation avec C-GORN, un Beech 1900D exploité par Propair Inc. qui effectuait un vol depuis l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) à destination de l'aéroport de Wabush, NL (CYWK) qui était établi en rapprochement sur la radiale 260 du VOR YWK.

C-GBMK, a Cessna 172I aircraft registered to Durham Flight Centre was on a rental flight from Oshawa Executive Airport (CYOO), ON to Kawartha Lakes (CNF4), ON with only 1 pilot onboard. While on approach for a touch and go into CNF4 runway 31, the pilot experienced strong crosswind and limited the flap deployment to 20 degrees and landed on the center of the runway with the left wheel touching first. As the aircraft slowed down, the flaps were being retracted in preparation for takeoff when a gust of wind from the left pushed the aircraft toward the right edge of the runway.  Subsequently, the right wheel rolled on the soft grass pulling the aircraft further to the right. As the right wheel dug into the soft grass, the aircraft flipped on its nose where it came to rest. The aircraft sustained substantial damages to both wings, propeller, engine and cowlings. Airport authority estimated to wind to be 220 degrees magnetic at 10 knots gusting to 15 knots at the time of the occurrence. The pilot was not injured.

C-FSPN, a Beech 200 operated by Keewatin Air Ltd., was conducting flight KEW216 from Thompson (CYTH) MB. to Brochet (CYBT) MB. During the climb out from CYTH, the flight crew noticed a gear in-transit/gear unsafe light on with no gear warning horn. KEW216 notified ATC and leveled off at 5 500 feet. The flight crew performed the necessary checks as per the QRH, performed a manual gear extension and confirmed the gear was down. KEW216 declared an emergency, requested a return to CYTH and carried out a successful normal landing. There were no injuries to the passengers or crew and no damage to the aircraft. The operator's maintenance inspected and cleaned the landing gear micro switches. Multiple gear swings were completed with no faults found. The aircraft was released subject to a satisfactory test flight.

C-FECI, an Aerospatiale ATR 42-320 operated by Calm Air International as flight CAV767, departed Churchill (CYYQ) MB. to Rankin Inlet (CYRT) NU. The aircraft was cold soaked prior to start. The pilot noticed oil pressure was high (70 PSI) on both engines (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW121) immediately after the starts. As the engines warmed up during taxi, deicing, and taxi out, the oil pressures came into the green arc. During the flight, the flight crew noticed number 1 engine oil pressure was reading near the barber pole. There were no warning alert and no master caution during the flight. After landing in CYRT, the flight taxied to the intended parking spot and, when the number 1 propeller was feathered, the flight crew received a master warning indicating engine 1 low oil pressure. The engine was shut down. The lowest oil pressure observed during the flight was between 50 and 55 PSI. The operator's maintenance is investigating.

C-GMEX, an Air Canada Boeing 737 Max 8 conducting flight AC1056 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (KPHX), AZ. During descent, Flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to ''descend'' while establishing on extended final due to traffic encroaching on their path. ATC was notified. Flight landed at destination without further incident.

C-GKVU, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-86N was conducting flight SWG410 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Puerto Plata/Gregorio Luperón Intl. (MDPP) Dominican Republic.  During cruise approximately 300 NM SE of Wilmington Intl. (KILM), NC entering WATRS airspace, Flight crew was informed of a security threat issued against the flight.  Flight crew declared a MAYDAY and diverted to KILM.  Flight landed without further incident.

On 21 November 2022 at Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, at approximately 1224 EST, 9Y-CAL, a Caribbean Airlines B38M conducting flight BWA607, was cleared for takeoff on runway 15L by Toronto Tower. The clearance was acknowledged, and the crew began to taxi into position on the runway. At the same time, Toronto Ground cleared C-FLDX, a Flair Airlines B38M which was taxiing to their gate following flight FLE149, to cross runway 15L at taxiway T, which is approximately 9200 feet from the threshold of runway 15L. The tower controller recognized that there was a loss of separation on the runway, and instructed BWA607 to abort their takeoff roll, which had just begun, and indicated to them that they had not been cleared to take off, although they had received such clearance. After FLE149 was clear of the runway, Toronto Tower re-cleared BWA607 for takeoff. From their respective positions, it would not have been possible for either aircraft to see the other, due to the geography of runway 15L, which slopes upward from each end.

C-GRXB, a Pilatus PC-12/47E operated by Ornge Global Air Inc. as PUL102, was conducting a flight between Sault Ste. Marie Airport (CYAM), ON, and Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON, with 2 crew and 2 passengers (paramedics) on board. During the initial climb, the passengers reported a burning smell accompanied by smoke in the cabin. The flight crew shut off the air conditioning system and declared PAN PAN, requesting an immediate return to CYAM, where they landed uneventfully. It was determined that de-ice fluid, which had been applied to the aircraft before this departure, had made its way into the engine and air conditioning system, resulting in the burning odor and smoke. The aircraft was ground run for 20 minutes to burn off residual de-ice fluid and returned to service; there was no smoke or odor detected during the subsequent departure.

C-GRXE, a Pilatus PC-12/47E operated by Ornge Global Air, was conducting flight PUL104 from Thunder Bay (CYQT) ON. to Moosonee (CYMO) ON. PUL104 was cruising at FL 250 when the flight crew heard a loud bang/bump from the rear of the aircraft and felt associated ear popping. The flight crew noticed a 2500 FPM climb and 12 000 cabin altitude with an associated CAS message. The QRH memory items were completed for cabin depressurization, crew donned their O2 masks, and instructed the paramedics to don cabin masks. ATC was notified and an emergency was declared. PUL104 started a descent to 10 000 feet and an operational decision was made to return to CYQT. PUL104 landed safely in CYQT.  The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and found the duct over temperature switch had failed resulting in the shutdown of the bleed air inflow.  This switch along with the over temperature sensor were replaced. A pressurization check was performed on the aircraft that indicated a leak at the elevator cable fairleads. This leak was rectified and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GNDR un Socata TBM-700 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de St-Georges, QC (CYSG) à destination de l'aéroport de Duluth, MN (KDLH) avec un pilote et 2 passagers à bord. Environs 15 minutes après le décollage, alors que l'aéronef se trouvait au niveau de vol (FL) 200, le pilote a reçu un message d'avertissement FUEL OFF suivi, quelques secondes plus tard, de l'extinction du moteur. Le pilote a actionné les items de mémoire de la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour une panne moteur et a remarqué que le sélecteur de carburant indiquait fermé (OFF). Le pilote a redémarré le moteur avec succès après avoir sélectionné le mode de carburant manuel. Quelques minutes plus tard, le sélecteur a été replacé en mode automatique (AUTO). Environ 2 minutes plus tard, le moteur s'est éteint de nouveau avec le sélecteur qui indiquait OFF à nouveau. Le pilote a redémarré le moteur et laissé le sélecteur en mode manuel. Un retour vers CYSG a été effectué. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre avec le moteur fonctionnel.

C-GRXM, Pilatus PC-12/47E operated by Ornge Global Air, was conducting flight PUL106 from Weagamow Lake - Round Lake (CZRJ) ON, to Thunder Bay (CYQT) ON. During the landing roll at CYQT on Runway 25, the aircraft was pulling left. Directional control was maintained and the aircraft came to a stop on the side of the runway. The flight crew suspected a frozen brake; however, when the aircraft was shut down, the crew identified the left main tire was blown. CYQT ARFF and the operator's maintenance responded to the aircraft. There were no injuries.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and found the left-hand brake unit was contaminated with ice. The brake unit was thawed and the left main wheel assembly was replaced. Aircraft was returned to service.

C-GECD, a privately registered Piper PA-31T2 (Cheyenne), was conducting a flight from La Crete (CFN5), AB, to Merritt (CAD5), BC. Approximately 12 nautical miles (NM) north of Kamloops (CYKA), BC, the pilot contacted the Vancouver Area Control Centre (ACC) to request a descent from 20 000 feet above sea level (ASL). C-FPCZ, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited Saab 340B, was operating as flight PCO3070 from CYKA to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC. During the initial climb, the flight crew of PCO3070 was advised by the Vancouver ACC controller of the approaching traffic and were instructed to proceed direct on course and climb to 14 000 feet ASL. At 1322:13 Pacific Standard Time (PST), the controller provided descent clearance for C-GECD to 15 000 feet ASL. The pilot of C-GECD read back that they were cleared to 5 000 feet ASL, and the controller acknowledged the read back. The controller then passed the position of PCO3070 and the pilot confirmed that they had PCO3070 on traffic collision avoidance system (TCAS). At 1324:24 PST, the Vancouver ACC controller advised PCO3070 of the Cheyenne traffic and the crew of PCO3070 confirmed they had C-GECD on TCAS.
