Immediately following that transmission, a different Vancouver ACC controller instructed C-GECD to maintain 15 000 feet ASL with traffic at the 3 o'clock position and approximately 2 NM southwest bound at 14 000 feet ASL. The pilot of C-GECD acknowledged and proceeded back up to 15 000 feet as instructed. A loss of separation occurred approximately 9 NM south-southeast of CYKA at 1324:49 PST when the aircraft separation had been reduced to 2.7 NM laterally and 800 feet vertically. The required separation was regained 53 seconds later when the lateral separation was increased to 5 NM. According to Manual of Air Traffic Services (MATS) 2.2 - Area Control Centre, the applicable standard aircraft separation is 5 NM laterally or 1000 feet vertically.

C-FXOA, un hélicoptère construction amateur de type Rotorway en exploitation privée effectuait un vol local depuis un terrain privé dans la municipalité de Lefebvre, Qc. Lors du retour vers son point de départ, à une altitude d'environs 200 pieds, l'appareil s'est disloqué et s'est écrasé dans un fossé entre 2 champs. Le pilote a subi des blessures mortelles.

C-FCHD, a Bell Helicopter 205A-1 operated by Custom Helicopters, was landing at the Valard Junction Camp, ON, approximately 40nm North of Red Lake, ON with 1 pilot and 3 passengers onboard. During the landing on an icy landing pad, the helicopter experienced an un-commanded spin around the vertical axis and the tail-rotor struck a structure. The pilot was able to shutdown the engines and everyone was able to exit the helicopter without injury. The helicopter sustained significant damage to the tail boom, gear box and tail rotor assembly. The operator has removed the helicopter from service.

C-GVCX, an Aerospatiale AS350B3 helicopter operated by Val Air, was conducting an external load flight from Kasabonika (CYAQ), ON to the North Caribou Camp, ON. Approximately 25 minutes into the flight at a speed of 65 to 75 knots, the pilot felt the single-item load drop at a location 18 nm west of CYAQ. The cargo net was observed to have failed. The pilot found the dropped item and flagged the area for retrieval. There was no damage to the helicopter, nor to the dropped load.The operator has taken the cargo net out of service.

C-GMXD, un Pilatus PC-12/47E exploité par Airmedic Inc., effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments sous l'indicatif AM267 depuis l'aéroport de Waskaganish, QC (CYKQ) à destination de Val-d'Or, QC (CYVO). À environs 20 miles nautiques au nord de l'aéroport de Lebel-sur-Quevillion , QC (CSH4) le pilote a remarqué que l'indication des pompes de carburant gauche et droite clignotait à un intervalle d'une dizaine de secondes. Suivant la liste du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour le clignotement des pompes, la section "FUEL PRESSURE LOW" est invoquée et donne l'instruction de se poser aussitôt que possible. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil a été dérouté vers CSH4 où il s'est posé sans encombre. Les tests de maintenance ont été effectués avec succès et ils ont déterminé qu'il est possible que le système d'équilibrage du carburant ait causé cette indication.

C-GGRY un Aero Vodochody L-29 Delfin en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’Aéroport d’Ottawa/Gatineau, QC (CYND) avec 1 pilote et 1 passager à bord. Au moment de circuler à l'écart de la piste après un arrêt complet, le train d'atterrissage principal droit s'est effondré. Le réservoir extérieur droit a été légèrement endommagé sans autres dommages rapportés. Aucun blessé. La maintenance a soulevé l'aile droite pour fixer le train solidement et remorquer l'appareil.

N306FE, a Federal Express McDonnell Douglas MD10-30F, was operating as flight FX141 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Memphis (KMEM), TN with 2 flight crew on board. At approximately 1930 MST (28 November 2022) the aircraft was pushed back from Apron VII onto Taxiway W for engine start. During number 1 engine start (General Electric CF6-50C2), the pushback crew advised the flight crew that the engine was on fire. The flight crew commenced the engine fire drill and related QRH checklists. Once those were complete the flight crew radioed the pushback crew to gain information on the condition of the engine, but they were no longer communicating and had left the area. With no information on the status of the engine the flight crew elected to evacuate the aircraft using the slide out the R1 door. The flight crew sustained no injuries. ARFF attended the scene and applied foam to the intake and tailpipe of the engine. The Edmonton TSB office deployed 2 investigators.

C-GLTN, un Cessna A185F en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de l'Isle-aux-Grues, Qc (CHS2) avec seul le pilote à son bord. Lors de la course à l'atterrissage, le pilote a perdu la maitrise de l'aéronef en raison d'une rafale de vent. L'aéronef s'est retourné et a subi des domages mineurs. Le pilote n'a pas été blessé.

C-FRQN, un Embraer 175 exploité par Jazz s’apprêtait à effectuer le vol JZA8642 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Québec (CYUL) à destination de l’aéroport de LaGuardia, NY (KLGA). Peu après le refoulement, le contrôle du tablier a donné l’instruction à l’équipage d’avancer, tout droit, d’environ 10 mètres. L’ailette de bout d’aile droite (winglet) du C-FRQN est entrée en contact avec le dessous du bout de l’aile du N774XF, un Airbus A319 exploité par American Airlines qui était immobile après avoir complété son refoulement en préparation pour un vol à destination de l’aéroport de Charlotte Douglas International, NC (KCLT). Les 2 aéronefs sont retournés à une porte d’embarquement et les passagers ont été débarqués. L’ailette droite du C-FRQN a été légèrement endommagée. Le bord de fuite de l’aile gauche du N774XF a été endommagé et un déchargeur statique de l’aile gauche s’est détaché.

C-FFLC, a Flair Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight FLE501 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to the Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON, with 6 crew and 134 passengers on board. Following touchdown on runway 26 the flight crew encountered some directional control issues, and the aircraft did not decelerate as expected. The aircraft overran the runway, coming to rest approximately 500 feet from the end of runway. There were no injuries, no observed damage to the landing gear, and some minor FOD damage observed on the LH engine. The crew and passengers stayed on the aircraft until airstairs were made available.

C-FLLH, an Amy’s Flying School Limited Piper PA-28-140 (Cherokee) was conducting circuit training at Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC, with only the student pilot on board. During the second touch and go, the aircraft bounced upon initial touch down, and then veered off the left side of Runway 27L on the subsequent touch down. The airplane traveled southwest through the grass, crossed Taxiway C, and then came to rest nose down in a ditch approximately 950 feet from where it originally left the runway. The pilot egressed without assistance and was uninjured. The airplane sustained substantial damage to the undercarriage, wings, and components forward of the firewall.The extent of the aircraft damage is being assessed.

C-GSQL, un Bell 412EP exploité par le service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, sous l'indicatif Q150, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols à vue depuis de l'aéroport de Montréal/Saint-Hubert, QC (CYHU) à destination des environs de St-Michel des Saints, Québec, avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors que l’aéronef se posait dans une zone restreinte pour secourir 4 personnes prises sur une île et incapables de quitter en raison de la glace, les patins arrière ont légèrement défoncé la mince couche de glace et un repositionnement a été entamé. Lors du repositionnement, l’aéronef a été manœuvré pour se rapprocher des arbres pour placer l’aéronef sur la terre ferme. Un arbre qui était soufflé par le rotor a repris sa position momentanément et le bout des pales du rotor principal l’a heurté. Aucune vibration n’a été perçue et l’équipage a décidé de retourner à CYHU. Les bouts des pales du rotor principal ont été trouvés endommagés. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FBMO, a float equipped Cessna A185E, operated by CBE Construction Ltd, was departing a logging camp in Strachan Bay, BC for Port Hardy Water Aerodrome (CAW5), BC, with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. During the initial climb, the aircraft reached an approximate height of 100' ASL before pitching nose down and colliding with the water. Staff at the logging camp called for emergency services. They scrambled a boat to the accident site and observed a large fire on the water's surface. Numerous aircraft, including Search and Rescue aircraft dispatched by the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre, converged on the area seeking to assist any survivors but none were found.The wreckage was located the following day by the RCMP who deployed a dive team to the site. The pilot and 2 passengers were located within the fuselage of the aircraft and removed. The TSB deployed to the site and oversaw the recovery and removal of the wreckage.

C-FWXI, a Beech B200 operated by Beaver Air Services (dba Missinippi Airways), was conducting a flight from South Indian Lake (CZSN), MB to Thompson (CYTH), MB. Shortly after takeoff from CZSN, the crew noted that the landing gear did not fully retract. The crew subsequently selected gear down and noticed that the nose gear and right gear indicated down and locked but the left gear indication did not. The crew completed the checklist, including a manual gear extension, but did not receive the left gear down and locked indication. After consulting with the operator's maintenance via satellite phone, the aircraft entered a hold near CYTH to troubleshoot. A low approach was then conducted at CYTH where FSS and the operator's maintenance personnel reported the gear appeared to be in the down and locked position. The crew then declared an emergency and requested emergency services. The aircraft landed uneventfully and taxied to the north apron without incident. Upon shutdown, the captain remained in the cockpit and continued to pump the manual extension pump handle until a jack was placed under the left wing.It was reported that during the previous flight's landing, there were snow drifts present on the runway in CZSN. The operator's maintenance inspection of the aircraft in CYTH following the occurrence found that the main wheel wells were packed with snow and found that the left-hand gear drag brace down lock was only 1/4 of the way over the down lock pin. Further inspection found that the down lock pin was bent, which may have prevented the down lock hook from fully engaging.

The privately registered Luscombe T8F-X, C-FHCA, was on a local flight departing, and returning to the Josephburg airport (CFB6), AB. The aircraft touched down in a 3 point attitude and on the roll out the pilot had difficulty maintaining directional control. The oscillations became progressively worse until it ground looped and nosed over. The aircraft was substantially damaged, the pilot was not injured, and the ELT did not activate. Maintenance Update: The aircraft was removed from the runway to a secure location. A log entry was made in the Journey log removing the aircraft from service pending extensive repairs.

C-GHXS, a Cessna 172M operated by 10113158 Manitoba Ltd. (dba LS Airways Flight Academy), was conducting a local flight in the vicinity of Gimli (CYGM), MB with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During straight and level flight at 5500 feet ASL, the pilot observed the engine running rough. Carb heat was selected to the fully open position; however, moments later, the engine quit operating. The pilot chose an area for a forced approach and landed 2NM west of CYGM. There were no reported injuries and no post-impact fire. The aircraft sustain substantial damage to its nose gear.

N375NC, a Delta Air Lines Inc. Airbus 320, was conducting flight DAL1228 from Hartsfield Jackson Atlanta International Airport (KATL), USA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, with 6 crew and 75 passengers on board. After extending the landing gear while on final approach for runway 24R, the flight crew received a "NOSEWHEEL STEERING FAULT" message on their ECAM. They abandoned their approach retracted the landing gear, and conducted troubleshooting using their QRH, in addition to consulting with dispatch and maintenance personnel. The flight crew declared an emergency, requesting that ARFF be present during their landing. During their next approach to runway 33R, the landing gear was selected down, and the ECAM message did not reappear. The flight landed uneventfully on runway 33R, and was escorted to the gate by ARFF.

C-FMXA, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight SWG699 from - Varadero/Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl. (MUVR), Cuba to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB.  Shortly after takeoff, a cabin crew became incapacitated.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GVEN, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) airplane operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3185 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Victoria International (CYYJ), BC, with 4 crew members and 71 passengers on board. During cruise at 4000 feet the flight crew received a fuselage door warning indication. The crew actioned the quick reference handbook (QRH) checklists and advised air traffic control of their situation. The crew requested an airport vehicle to follow them after landing to ensure that, if the door came open on landing, they could collect anything that fell onto the runway. The aircraft performed an uneventful landing with aircraft rescue and firefighting crews standing by. The operator's maintenance adjusted the door lock sensor. An operational check of the door revealed no further faults, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOFJ, a Sunwest Aviation Ltd Dassault Falcon 7X was conducting flight CNK7 from Bedfordshire/Luton Airport (EGGW), UK to Palm Spring Intl. (KPSP), CA.  On initial approach descending from 11000 to 7000 feet, Flight crew received a TCAS RA (Resolution advisory) to ''climb''.  Flight crew complied with RA and advised ATC.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

On 10 November 2022, after having boarded the passengers and while still at the gate at the Lester B Pearson International Airport, Toronto (CYYZ), ON, an Air Canada Airbus 321-200 crew noticed an ECAM - FUEL Right Wing Tank Overflow caution light. This was followed by the ground crew informing the flight crew of a fuel spill. A PAN PAN emergency was declared with ATC. All passengers and crew deplaned through the boarding bridge to the terminal gate area. GTAA emergency vehicles responded and dealt with the fuel spill. The aircraft was taken out of service.

On O5 November 2022, an Air Canada A320-200 (registration C-FXCD) was operating as flight ACA0686 from Lester B Pearson International Airport, (CYYZ) Toronto, ON to St John's International Airport (CYYT), ON. After departure from CYYZ, the crew were unable to pressurize the aircraft. The number 2 air conditioning pack was unserviceable as per the minimum equipment list (MEL) and the number 1 air conditioning pack was selected. The crew then received an ECAM - Pack 1 fault. The crew informed ATC and requested to return to CYYZ. The aircraft landed in CYYZ without further incident.Post-occurrence: Maintanance replaced Pack 1 flow control valve as per AMM 21-51-51-400-001-A. A leak and ops check was carried out with no faults found.

The Airborne Energy Solutions Inc. Cessna 172S, C-GFXS, was being operated on a pipeline surveillance flight 18 NM NE of the Edmonton International Airport (CYEG). While in cruise the flight crew noticed an odd odor in the cockpit. Thinking that it was electrically related, the pilot turned off the electrical system. The odor persisted so the crew turned the electrics back on to continue the flight. The emergency checklist for electrical fires was actioned as a precaution. By the time the checklist was complete the odor dissipated. Noticing no anomalies on the engine instruments they elected to climb and contact the terminal controller. An emergency was declared and a request to proceed directly to Villeneuve (CZVL), AB. As they were enroute to CZVL they began to notice oil on the windscreen and concluded that they had an oil leak from the engine (Avco Lycoming IO-360-L2A). A safe landing was carried out and the aircraft taxied to the hangar uneventfully.Maintenance Update: Maintenance cleaned the engine bay and did a test run and discovered an oil leak from the crankshaft seal. The seal was replaced, a successful test run carried out, and a test flight. The aircraft was released for service.

C-GMXD, un Pilatus PC12/47 exploité par Airmedic Inc. sous l’indicatif AM267 effectuait un vol MEDEVAC selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Chisasibi, QC (CSU2) à destination de Montréal/Saint-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec 4 passagers et 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage sur la piste 24 droite, les freins de la roue de droite étaient gelés et la roue n’a pas tourné. La maitrise directionnelle n’a pas pu être maintenue et l’aéronef est sorti en bordure de piste. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé, mais une ambulance a été appelée pour évacuer le patient à bord. L’aéroport a été fermé jusqu’à 0340z.

The Porter Airlines DeHavilland DHC-8-402 aircraft (registration C-GLQV, flight POE 611) departed from runway 26 at Billy Bishop Toronto City airport (CYTZ), ON and turned northbound enroute to Timmins Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS).  The Flair Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737-800 (registration C-FLUT, flight FLE 121) was descending for an approach to Runway 33L at Toronto Lester B. Pearson airport (CYYZ), ON. A loss of separation occurred between the two aircraft at approximately 7000 feet ASL. Separation was reduced to 2.7 NM laterally and 200 feet vertically. There were no evasive maneuvers from either aircraft.

L’aéronef Boeing 737-800 (immatriculation C-GFVM, numéro de série 37077) effectuait le vol SWG307 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Santa Clara Abel Santa Maria, Cuba (MUSC) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 6 membres d'équipage à bord et 191 passagers à son bord. Lors de l'approche à CYUL, l'équipage a actionné les volets et a noté une indication d'asymétrie. L'équipage a effectué une approche interrompue et a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN). Une deuxième approche, avec la configuration non-standard utilisant les volets à la position 15 (Flaps 15) a été effectuée et l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 24 droite.

L’aéronef De Havilland DHC-8-314 (immatriculation C-GIAB, numéro de série 296) exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 3 membres d’équipage et 10 passagers à son bord. Lors de la course au décollage de la piste 29 à CYQB, il y a eu un impact avec un renard. L’aéronef a poursuivi le vol vers CYUL et, par mesure de précaution, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN). L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre à CYUL.

Westjet Boeing 737-700, C-GWBN, was operating as flight WJA661 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. to Calgary (CYYC), AB with 5 crew and 117 passengers. While in cruise flight, a pilot briefly became incapacitated and was unable to perform their duties. As a precautionary measure, the flight crew utilized a deadheading pilot traveling as a passenger and elected to divert to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson (CYWG), MB. The flight landed without incident and was met at the gate by EMS. The pilot was assessed and cleared to deadhead as a passenger to CYYC.

C-GRJA, a Piper Navajo PA31-350 operated by Sandy Lake Seaplane Service, was conducting a flight from St. Theresa Point (CYST) MB. to Sandy Lake (CZSJ) ON. After departing CYST, the aircraft experienced a power loss on the number 1 engine (TIO-540-J2BD) and an abnormal engine sound. The pilot conducted a precautionary shutdown of the number 1 engine and diverted the aircraft to Island Lake (CYIV) MB.  A single engine landing was performed and the aircraft landed safely on Runway 12 at CYIV.The operator's maintenance is assessing the cause of engine power loss.

The Canwest Aviation Beech King Air B200CGT, C-GLUF, was operating as CWA922 from Medicine Hat (CYXH), AB to Calgary (CYYC), AB. After departure from CYXH the flight crew contacted the Edmonton Centre Calgary Enroute controller as the aircraft was climbing to FL200 direct to EBGAL. The controller identified the aircraft and cleared CWA922 to FL200. The controller’s situation display indicated an airspace warning for the CYR230 restricted airspace. The controller instructed CWA922 to turn left 20 degrees for vectors around the restricted airspace before being cleared direct to EBGAL. As the aircraft approached the CYR230 restricted airspace horizontal separation was reduced to 4.7 statute miles where 5 statute miles is required.

C-GTCJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 757-200 was conducting flight CJT1891 from Havana/José Martí Intl. (MUHA), Cuba to Panamá City/Tocumen Intl. (MPTO), Panamá.  During initial climb on selection of landing gear up, L HYD QTY indicated on EICAS (Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System), and hydraulic quantity was depleting slowly.  QRH was actioned, PAN PAN was declared with ATC and decision was made to divert to Miami Intl. (KMIA), FL. Alternate Gear and flap extension was carried out on arrival and flight crew cleared the runway with rudder control and differential thrust.  Aircraft was subsequently towed to the gate.  Maintenance found 2 nose gear door actuator flex lines leaking.

C-GWSR, a WestJet Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737-8CT was conducting flight 2419 from Cancun Intl. (MMUN), Mexico to Saskatoon/ John G. Diefenbaker Intl. (CYXE), SK.  During cruise at FL360 in vicinity of Baton Rouge Metro/ Ryan Field (KBTR), LA, flight crew received an indicated airspeed disagree alert on PFD (primary flight display).  Flight crew actioned abnormal checklist and determined the unreliable airspeed was on the Captain's side.  After descending to FL340 due to moderate turbulence, flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC and requested a block altitude.  Flight crew discussed with maintenance control via SATCOM and monitored an intermittent indication for the remainder of the flight.  Flight continued to destination using First officer and standby instruments without further incident.

C-GUAC, an Air Canada Airbus Canada Limited Partnership A220-300 operating as flight ACA1039 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Denver International Airport (KDEN), CO was on final for runway 16L when the crew received a TCAS RA "Descend", the crew followed the command. ATC was informed and the crew were told of converging parallel traffic on runway 16R. The flight continued and landed without any incident.

C-FSOI, an Air Canada B737 Max 8 operating as flight ACA1046 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), CA was on approach for runway 31L when the crew received a TCAS RA "climb". The crew carried out the SOP and continued the approach onto runway 31L. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GGMN, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8118 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to St. John's Intl (CYYT), NL. On approach to CYYT, the aircraft became difficult to control due to variations in speed and altitude caused by severe turbulence.  All passengers and cabin crew were seated and using safety belts, and there were no reported injuries. The crew elected to carry out a missed approach and divert to Sydney/J.A. Douglas McCurdy airport (CYQY), NS. Enroute to CYQY, the crew decided to divert instead to Deer Lake airport (CYDF), NL due to turbulence forecasted at CYQY. The aircraft landed at CYDF without further incidentMaintenance carried out all recommended inspections based on the recorded flight performance variations and exceedances, with no faults or damage found.

C-GKWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Q400) was operating as flight WEN3155 from Calgary International (CYYC), AB, to Kelowna (CYLW), BC, with 4 crew and 75 passengers on board. When the crew selected the gear down during the approach into CYLW, the left main landing gear (LH MLG) door and LH MLG indicators were red as was the landing gear handle light. The crew initiated a missed approach and subsequently completed the appropriate checklists with the same result. After consulting company dispatch, the crew requested a return to CYYC. On the approach to CYYC, the crew declared a MAYDAY, conducted a successful alternate landing gear extension and requested aircraft rescue and firefighting crews to be standing by. The aircraft landed without incident and was taxied to the gate unassisted.Maintenance conducted an inspection and found that the proximity sensor electronics unit showed a fault. 2 connectors, P21 and P23, were loose and had water contamination. Both connectors were cleaned and corrosion inhibitor was applied. The fault was cleared with a test of the gear extension and retraction. The aircraft was returned to service.

L’aéronef Aerospatiale/Aeritalia ATR-42-500 (immatriculation C-FTIL, numéro de série 579) exploité par Bradley Air Services Limited, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) à destination de l’aéroport d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB). Alors que l’aéronef était stationné à la barrière, au sol à CYFB, l’équipage de conduite a coupé le moteur numéro 2 pour que l’équipe au sol puisse connecter le groupe électrogène de parc (GPU). L’équipage de conduite a ensuite reçu une indication ELEC SMK sur le panneau d’alerte. De la fumée était visible dans le poste de pilotage, et une odeur de fumée était présente dans la cabine. Le commandant a immédiatement sélectionné le bus DC SVC UTILITY à la position fermée. L’équipage a actionné la procédure d’évacuation au sol et une urgence (MAYDAY) a été déclarée. Les passagers ont été évacués en toute sécurité vers le terminal. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

C-GOIF, an Airbus A321-271NX aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC123 from London/Gatwick Intl (EGKK), England to Toronto/Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON.  At about 60°37' N, 044°47' W the aircraft encountered severe turbulence with momentary difficulty of aircraft control. The aircraft experienced left and right banking variations up to 30 degrees, altitude variations of plus 1800 feet and minus 800 feet at rates of more than 3000 feet per minute, and a brief airspeed increase of plus 15 knots indicated. There were no reported injuries and the aircraft continued to destination and landed at CYYZ with no further incident.Maintenance carried out all recommended inspections based on the recorded flight performance variations and exceedances, with no faults or damage found.

C-FRLM, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by PAL Aerospace Ltd., was conducting MEDEVAC flight SPR811 from St. John's (CYYT), NL to Stephenville airport (CYJT), NL. The landing gear was selected down on the approach to CYJT, and the crew observed that the green, safe landing gear indication did not illuminate for the left landing gear down position. The crew reported the condition to ATS, requested clearance to return to CYYT, and declared an emergency. While enroute to CYYT the crew coordinated with company maintenance to troubleshoot the landing gear position indication system and replaced the effected down position indicator bulb with a serviceable bulb. When the landing gear was selected down on approach at CYYT, the landing gear position displayed the green, safe position for all 3 landing gear and the crew cancelled the emergency. The aircraft landed at CYYT without further incident.

C-GITU, an Air Canada Airbus 321 operating as flight ACA100 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON declared an emergency due to a hydraulic issue on arrival into CYYZ. During the cruise portion of the flight, the flight crew received an ECAM HYD Blue Elec Pump OVHT. The flight crew followed the QRH actions and declared a PAN PAN with CYYZ Toronto center. The aircraft landed uneventfully and taxied to the gate without further incident.

N635AE, a Piedmont Airlines Embraer ERJ-145 operating as flight PDT6110 from Philadelphia International Airport (KPHL), PA to Lester B Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON declared an emergency due to a flap issue on arrival into CYYZ. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 05 at 1453 without further incident.

C-GELJ, an Air Canada B737-8 operating as flight ACA1093 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to San Diego International Airport (KSAN), CA was climbing to FL380 passing FL377 when the aircraft encountered a sudden wake turbulence event, the crew reported the event to ATC and requested a descent to FL360. Two Flight Attendants received minor injuries during the event. The aircraft landed safely in KSAN.Air Canada maintenance performed a general visual inspection. No Damage or defects noted and aircraft ok for continued service.

An unregistered basic ultralight, Magal Holdings Copy Cub, was conducting a recreational flight with an untrained and unlicensed pilot at the controls. Shortly after takeoff, the pilot elected to attempt to land in a field, and during the landing, the pilot lost control of the aircraft and collided with terrain coming to a rest upside down. The pilot received serious injuries and the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FTPN, a Textron Aviation (Cessna) U206F operated by Eon Airborne Inc. was conducting aerial survey work North and Northeast of the Lethbridge, AB (CYQL) with 2 crew members on board. The majority of the survey work was being conducted at an altitude of approximately 500 feet above ground level (AGL). Just over 2 hours into the flight, the crew switched fuel tanks from the right tank to left tank. Shortly after the selection, the engine (TELEDYNE CONTINENTAL, IO-520-F) began to run rough, with an associated significant power loss, and the aircraft immediately started losing altitude. Before the flight crew could complete the appropriate emergency checklist procedure, the aircraft was at 100 feet AGL, and the pilot elected to prepare the aircraft for a forced landing in an open field. A successful forced landing was completed. There were no injuries to the flight crew, and the aircraft was not damaged. Subsequent external examination of the aircraft showed blue fuel staining down the upper left side of the fuselage.

C-GLWN, a North Cariboo Flying Service De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8 300, was operating as flight NCB2021 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Smithers (CYYD), BC, with 3 crew members and 15 passengers on board. While on approach, the flight crew disengaged the autopilot and steered the aircraft left to align with the runway. As the speed slowed and the aircraft was configured for landing, a significant pitch control issue was encountered by the flight crew. The pitch trim wheel was difficult to move and, when the flaps travelled to 15 degrees, both pilots were required to maintain the desired pitch angle. With pitch control significantly degraded, the crew executed a missed approach. While consulting the QRH, the pitch control improved enough to allow the flight crew to return for a landing. The approach and landing were uneventful but when the aircraft was parked, it required significant force to move the control column fully forward to engage the control lock. Approximately 10 minutes after shutdown, both the control column and pitch trim wheel moved freely. Company maintenance examined the aircraft and discovered pieces of melting ice in the area of the elevator actuating mechanism. The aircraft had been parked outside over-night in CYVR in light rain. At CYYD, the temperature was -9°C, with a wind chill factor of -17°C. After maintenance inspected the airplane, it was returned to service.

C-FJQH, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 was conducting flight ROU1722 from Phoenix Sky Harbor Intl. (KPHX), AZ to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl.  (CYYZ), ON. While in the cruise phase of flight in the vicinity of Gerald R. Ford International Airport (KGRR), MI, a Flight Attendant fell ill and was unable to carry out safety related duties for the remainder of the flight. For landing, a passenger was assigned acting flight attendant duties in accordance with company policy and procedures. The flight was subsequently completed without further incident.

N13954, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by United Airlines as flight UAL900 was conducting a flight from London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK. to San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), US. During cruise flight over northeastern Canada, the flight crew contacted United Technical Operations Maintenance Control and Dispatch regarding an airframe vibration in the aft/tail section of the aircraft. There were no reports of aircraft handling or controllability problems, and no engine or system abnormalities were identified in the flight deck. A flight crew member investigated by proceeding to the rear gallery area of the aircraft and noted an intermittent vibration. In coordination with the United Dispatch Centre, an operational decision was made to declare an emergency and divert to Iqaluit (CYFB) NU. The flight landing safely at CYFB. There were no injuries to passengers or flight crew.A visual inspection by a local airport maintenance company confirmed there were no identifiable defects to the aircraft or tail section. United Airlines field service maintenance personnel were dispatched to CYFB for an aircraft inspection and further troubleshooting. No defects were found. The operator's maintenance is currently coordinating repositioning the aircraft to a United Airlines maintenance base.

N8902D, a Piper PA-22-160, was conducting a private flight from Tok Junction (PFTO), AK to Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen Whitehorse Intl. (CYXY), YT with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. On approach into CYXY the aircraft lost engine power (Lycoming O-320), and the pilot performed a forced approach onto a road approximately 4 nm North of CYXY. The pilot and passenger were not injured; the aircraft was substantially damaged. There were no injuries to personnel on the ground, or damage to public property. During the subsequent removal of the aircraft from the road, it was found that each wing fuel tank contained 1 US gallon of fuel.

The Geotech Aviation Limited Airbus Helicopters AS 350 B3 (AStar) helicopter (registration C-FVCR) was conducting electromagnetic survey operations from a camp at Kitsault, British Columbia (BC), with only the pilot on board. An FM radio call from the pilot was received by the company’s geophysical equipment operator. Shortly after, a 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter (ELT) signal was detected by the Medium Earth Orbit Search and Rescue (MEOSAR) system and relayed to the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) in Victoria, BC. The site was accessed by Search and Rescue Technicians and they reported that the pilot had been fatally injured. The helicopter was destroyed and there was no post-impact fire.

C-GOIK, an Air Transat A321LR was operating flight TSC974 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Samaná El Catey International Airport (MDCY), Dominican Republic when in the vicinity of Currituck County Regional Airport (KONX), NC, a flight attendant became ill and unable to perform duties. The emergency positions were reassigned according to priority of occupancy and the flight continued to destination where an ambulance met the aircraft.

C-GEKZ, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA584 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Newark Liberty Intl. (KEWR), USA. During cruise at FL370 and approximately 180 nautical miles west of Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB, the flight crew received an airspeed disagree message. The airspeed disagree message came and went three times at then stayed on. The flight crew conducted the unreliable airspeed indication checklist and diverted to CYWG; declaring a PAN PAN followed by a MAYDAY call. The flight crew determined that the Captain's airspeed indicator was in error and that both the standby and First Officer's airspeed indications were normal. In the decent through approximately 10 000 feet, the captain's airspeed began to operate normally. The flight landed uneventfully in CYWG with ARFF on standby and taxied to the gate.The TSB downloaded and analyzed the FDR and CVR. A review of the FDR indicated there was no degradation of airspeed and no aircraft control issues were recorded. The operator's maintenance investigated the aircraft's pitot systems and replaced the left Air Data Module (ADM) and the left Air Data Inertial Reference Unit (LADIRU). A functional test/ferry flight to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC. was conducted and there were no faults reported. The operator's maintenance then replaced the left-hand pitot probe due to a suspected failure of the pitot heating element. A left pitot system leak test was carried out and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GFWX, an Airbus A320-214 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1995 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. to Regina Intl (CYQR), SK. On arrival at CYQR, the weather was below approach limits so ROU1995 held near CYQR for 32 minutes at 10 000 ft. The weather conditions did not improve; therefore, ROU1995 advised ATC of a minimum fuel condition and requested a diversion to the planned alternate of Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. The flight landed safely in CYWG.

C-GOJN, a VIH Helicopters Limited Sikorsky S-61N helicopter was conducting heli-slinging operations at Cypress Mountain Ski Hill in support of ski lift tower construction. The helicopter was positioning a load to be placed on top of a tower, challenges with bolt placement resulted in a hover of 5 minutes. The temperature was 0° C and there was snow on the hillside. The flight crew observed fog started to form and rolling upslope. They told the tower crew to release the tag lines and they planned to depart uphill to the upper station. As the flight crew departed the tower, the fog became thicker, and reference to the ground was lost. The flight crew assessed the situation and elected to release the load once they were clear of the ground crew. The pilot not flying (PNF) regained visual reference and took control and returned to the staging area. The load was damaged from impact with the ground. There were no injuries and no damage to the helicopterThe Company reviewed this occurrence and advised they are increasing their weather limits for performing precision helicopter long line work. The minimums will now be 1.5 statute miles visibility with a minimum ceiling of 750 feet above ground level.

C-FGKJ, a Boeing 757-223 was conducting Cargojet Airways Ltd flight 626 from Moncton/Roméo Leblanc Intl Airport (CYQM), NB to Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. While on descent for the approach, the flight crew received a LE SLAT DISAGREE message on the EICAS. The crew requested and conducted a hold prior to the approach to be able to trouble shoot and perform the checklist items. ARFF was advised and standing by when the aircraft landed safely at 1107 UTC. The aircraft was inspected prior to taxing to the ramp.The fault isolation manual (FIM) for LE SLAT DISAGREE was carried out. Maintenance checks were carried out with no fault codes present. The slats and flaps were tested and function checks completed with no faults found. The power drive unit (PDU) torque limiter was inspected and function checked with no faults along with the override and JAM functions. The items in the FIM were exhausted with no faults and a review of defects for the last 60 days was conducted with no noted faults for the LE SLAT system. Aircraft was returned to service and placed on monitor. The aircraft has completed subsequent flight legs with no repeat or noted faults reported.

C-GQDR, an Airbus Helicopters AS350 B2, operated by Remote Helicopters, was supporting flood debris clean-up operations and had departed Merritt (CAD5), BC, with only the pilot onboard. Approximately 3 minutes after take-off, the pilot noticed a burning smell and saw white smoke coming from the right side of the instrument panel. The pilot radioed another company aircraft to inform them that he was returning to CAD5. He then reduced the electrical load, opened the pilot side window to vent the cabin, and returned to CAD5. The smoke had dissipated from the cabin, and the pilot landed without further incident.  Company maintenance personnel determined that an internal failure in the directional gyro (DG) had resulted in a short circuit, which caused the melting of insulation and subsequent smoke. The system was isolated by disconnecting the DG and was listed as a deferred defect. The helicopter was returned to service.

C-GSNI, a Beech 200 privately-operated by Sifec North Inc., was conducting a flight from Cambridge Bay (CYCB) NU. to Rankin Inlet (CYRT) NU. with 2 crew members. When approximately 159 nm from CYRT, the flight crew requested a climb from cruise altitude of FL 210 to FL250. During the climb, the captain noticed a disparity between the engine instruments and pulled back the right throttle to test the engine power on the right engine (PWC PT6A-41). During this action, the right engine power went down briefly but then stopped at 1400 foot-pounds torque instead of decreasing. C-GSNI continued the climb to FL 250. While in cruise a second attempt was made to reduce power on the right engine and the power reduced to 1700 foot-pounds torque at an ITT of 685 degrees C. The flight crew determined that no action from the right power lever was able to bring the power down. The flight notified ATC, declared a PAN PAN, and conducted a precautionary right engine shutdown. The flight crew conducted a single engine landing at CYRT with ARFF on standby. The aircraft taxied to the apron and shutdown.The operator's maintenance is inspecting the right-hand engine.

C-FEGC, a privately owned Van's RV 7A aircraft, was on approach to Rideau Lakes - Westport airport (CRL2), ON after a flight from Peterborough, Ontario (CYPQ). On final approach to the grass covered runway 25, the pilot increased the airspeed to compensate for the higher winds and clearing of the hydro lines. After clearing the hydro lines, the aircraft descended quickly, and upon touchdown the nose landing gear dug into the soft grass surface and the aircraft flipped over. The aircraft was substantially damaged, and the pilot was seriously injured.

C-FMSX, an Air Canada Airbus A320-200 was conducting flight AC702 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to LaGuardia Intl. (KLGA), NY.  During initial approach at 5000 feet, flight crew received TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to level off and then climb.  Flight crew complied with RA and flight landed without further incident.

C-FNND, an Air Canada Boeing 777-200 was conducting flight AC791 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Los Angeles Intl. (KLAX), CA.  On initial approach, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to climb.  Traffic was visually in sight, crew advised ATC and aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FSNQ, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight AC566 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), CA.  During visual final approach runway 28L, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) at 1200 feet to ''descend'' due to another aircraft on a different profile landing runway 28R.  Flight landed without further incident.

C-GITU, an Air Canada Airbus A321-211 was operating as ACA162 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. At approximately 1012 MST, shortly after taking off from CYEG, the flight directors failed, and multiple warning messages appeared on the Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitor (ECAM). The flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency and diverted to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB. Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) personnel were dispatched. The aircraft landed safely at 1212 MST. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft.Company findings/corrective action: Air data inertial reference unit (ADIRU) #3 was replaced. Inspections of all 3 ADIRUs carried out serviceable. Angle-of-attack sensors and pitot probes inspected with no faults found. Leak test of principal static and total air data system carried out serviceable. No other faults found.

C-GBHR, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114, was conducting flight ROU1611 from Fort Lauderdale Intl (KFLL), FL to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC.  During takeoff roll runway 10L just prior to V1, flight crew observed small animal/large bird followed by loud noise and smell.  Due to speed, takeoff was continued, PanPan was declared, and aircraft diverted to Miami Intl. (KMIA), FL.  As flight crew suspected a blown tire, ARFF was requested, aircraft landed and was inspected by ARFF without any fault.  Flight taxied to the gate on its own power.  Following the occurrence, maintenance inspected the aircraft without evidence of blown tire and no damage identified.  Evidence of a bird strike on RH engine without core ingestion and evidence on RH Main Landing gear impact was found.

C-GKCY, a SAAB 340A operated by Transwest Air Ltd., was conducting a flight from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE) SK. to McArthur River (CKQ8), SK. Approximately 30 minutes into the flight at FL 200, the flight crew noticed a faint hot rubber smell in the cockpit. The flight crew scanned the cockpit instruments and circuit breakers, and reduced the cabin temperature; however, the smell continued to increase with an acrid melting plastic/hot metal with an ozone smell typical of an electrical short circuit. There was no visible smoke present at this time. As the flight continued and with the sun shining through the right-hand windshield, the pilot-in-command noticed that smoke was visible from the rear corner of the right front windshield. The memory checks for electrical smoke or fire were completed, the cabin seat belt sign was turned on, and the flight crew donned their O2 masks. An emergency was declared with a request to descend to 10 000 ft and divert to Prince Albert/Glass Field (CYPA) SK. The flight crew referenced the QRH and started the checklist when the right front windshield annunciator illuminated. The right-hand windshield circuit breakers were pulled and the smoke then began to dissipate. The First Officer (FO) notified the flight attendant of the situation, asked for the cabin to be secured for a landing in CYPA. The flight attendant informed the FO there was no smoke in the cabin, secured the cabin, and briefed the passengers. The aircraft landed safely in CYPA and taxied to the terminal with local firefighters and EMS on standby. The fire firefighters inspected the aircraft and found no active fire.The operator's maintenance conducted an inspection and confirmed the burnt terminal block on the windshield was the source of the smoke when power was applied. The aircraft was returned to service in accordance with a MEL. The aircraft was flown to a maintenance base for repairs.

C-FFLC, a Boeing 737-86J airplane, operated by Flair Airlines, was conducting flight FLE500 from the Region of Waterloo International (CYKF), ON, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 6 crew members and 146 passengers on board. On approach to CYVR, the flight crew selected flaps to 10 degrees and observed a momentary flap load relief light. As the landing gear was lowered, the flight crew observed the trailing edge flap was between 1 and 5 degrees without a green light.  The flight crew notified air traffic control (ATC), discontinued the approach, and received vectors to complete the associated Quick Reference Handbook checklists for trailing edge flap disagreements. Once the checklists were completed, the crew requested a second approach. ATC placed aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) crews on standby and the aircraft landed uneventfully.Company maintenance found a fault message and completed a successful trailing edge flap load relief ground test. No further faults were found, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GVJR, a Eurocopter AS 332 2L helicopter operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd. was slinging an external load from the Longdog Valard Camp, ON to Pipestone Valard Camp, ON with a crew of 2 on board. While in cruise in the vicinity of Big Trout Lake (CYTL), ON at approximately 1000 feet AGL, the crew felt a sudden jolt and noticed the load meter read "Empty Line". The crew flew the helicopter in a circle and confirmed that the external load had dropped. The crew then continued on to Pipestone Valard Camp, ON where the helicopter landed safely. An inspection completed by the operator revealed that the straps connected to the long line had failed.

An Aeolus Flight Academy Inc., Cessna 152 (registration C-GBZB), was cleared for a touch and go on Runway 15 at the London International Airport (CYXU), ON. Subsequently, a Waterloo-Wellington Flying Club Cessna 172S (C-GYEE), requested take-off clearance for Runway 15 from taxiway A intersection; C-GYEE was instructed to hold short RWY 15 by ATC. C-GYEE then proceeded to line up on Runway 15 in front of C-GBZB, who was touching down north of taxiway D. The tower controller observed the incursion and instructed C-GBZB to stop on the runway. C-GBZB came to a stop near the D intersection.

C-GVAJ, a Cargojet Boeing 757, operating as flight CJT 919, was enroute from Cincinnati Northern Kentucky International Airport (KCVG), USA to Calgary International Airport (CYYC) when the left engine had a momentary EGT exceedance. Maintenance requested the aircraft divert to Hamilton (CYHM), ON. On final for Runway 12, the thrust was increased from idle, and a bang was heard by the crew. The thrust lever was reduced to idle again and increased a second time, there was another bang and the engine failed. The flight crew continued final approach and secured the engine declaring a mayday. The aircraft landed without further incident, was inspected by emergency services and taxied to the ramp.Maintenance found the following: LH ENG ECC dedicated generator failed, LH engine BVCU failed test, TAT probe fault, all units were replaced, and function checked as per AMM.  A borescope inspection was carried out with no faults or findings. As an added precaution, the L ENG LP PUMP fuel filter was inspected and replaced, as well the LH ENG starter was replaced. Additional function check of the L GEN DRIVE was carried out with no faults. A functional check flight was carried out with no faults, aircraft was returned to service.

C-GUBL, an Air Transat Airbus A330-200 was conducting flight TSC309 from Rome/Leonardo da Vinci Intl. (LIRF), Italy to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  In vicinity of Genoa/ Cristoforo Colombo Airport (LIMJ), Italy, a cabin crew member became incapacitated.  Emergency position and safety responsibilities were reassigned, and flight continued to destination.

N358QS, an Embraer 505 operated by NetJets Aviation Inc. was conducting flight EJA358 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. to Buffalo/Niagara Intl (KBUF), NY. While climbing through FL 250 and approximately 65 nm Southeast of CYWG, the flight crew felt an engine vibration followed by a shutdown of the left-hand engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW535E). The crew completed the QRH procedure, declared an emergency and diverted to Minneapolis-Saint Paul Intl. Airport/Wold-Chamberlain (KMSP), MN for an uneventful landing. The operator's maintenance replaced the left-hand engine.

C-FEXW, a Morningstar Air Express Incorporated Cessna 208B Caravan airplane, was conducting flight MAL8074 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Victoria (CYYJ), BC, with one crew member on board. On approach to CYYJ, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence, wind shear, and strong gusting tailwinds. The pilot experienced a temporary loss of control and conducted a missed approach. Once clear of the turbulence, the aircraft diverted to CYVR and landed without incident. There were no injuries.Maintenance conducted a severe turbulence inspection as per the aircraft maintenance manual and found no damage. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFXD, a Morningstar Air Express Incorporated Cessna 208B Caravan airplane, was conducting flight MAL8072 from Victoria (CYYJ), BC, to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC, with one crew member on board. Upon departure from CYYJ the aircraft encountered severe turbulence. The pilot experienced negative G loading and temporary loss of control. Once clear of the turbulence, the aircraft continued to CYVR and landed without incident. There were no injuries.Maintenance conducted a severe turbulence inspection as per the aircraft maintenance manual and found no damage. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FLUT, a Flair Airlines Boeing 737 MAX 8, was operating as flight FLE151, from Edmonton International (CYEG), AB to Kelowna (CYLW), BC. While the aircraft was taxiing to the runway, the crew followed a portion of taxi line that was decommissioned. The leading edge of the left-hand wing tip struck a piece of ground support equipment that was stored outside of the taxi area. The contact with the equipment was reported by a passenger to the crew. The aircraft taxied back to the gate; the aircraft was grounded pending repair.

C-FLWJ, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-700 aircraft, operating as flight WS544, experienced a fire in the cabin after landing at the Region of International Waterloo Airport (CYKF), ON. The flight had arrived from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB and while taxiing to the gate at CYKF the cabin crew advised the flight crew that there was a fire in the cabin. The flight crew stopped the aircraft on the taxiway, shut down the engines, declared an emergency and requested Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) services. The cabin crew isolated the source of the fire to a passenger carry-on bag suspected to be either an e-cigarette or a battery and extinguished the fire. The flight crew started the engines and taxied the gate. ARFF followed the aircraft to the gate, where the passengers and crew deplaned normally. There was minor fire and smoke damage to the aircraft in the vicinity of seats 22 ABC. The source of ignition was identified as a spare Lithium-ion battery (IMREN18650) used for an electronic e cigarette. The battery, along with a metal tool were stored loosely in a backpack pocket. There were no injuries or evacuation.

C-FKTE, a Carson Air Limited Beech B300 (King Air), was conducting a flight from Penticton (CYYF), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 2 crew and 3 passengers on board. During the approach to CYVR, the landing gear was selected down, and the left main landing gear down and locked green indication did not illuminate. The crew advised the CYVR tower controller and requested holding instructions for troubleshooting. Once in the hold, the flight crew was able to switch one of the working landing gear light bulbs into the left landing gear indicator socket. The left landing gear light came on with the new bulb. The aircraft requested and then flew past the control tower for a visual inspection of the landing gear condition. The tower controller confirmed that the gear appeared down. The aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident. Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting crews were standing by. There were no injuries, and the airplane was not damaged.Company maintenance inspected the landing gear and found; the lamp assembly catch pins bent, damaged annunciator assembly, and the lighted overlay panel was not aligned correctly with gear handle/light assembly. The airplane was repaired and returned to service following operational checks.

C-GCFF, a Beech 200 aircraft operated by Skynorth Air Ltd. was enroute from Island Lake (CYIV), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB with a crew of 2 and 1 passenger onboard. While in cruise at 24000 feet ASL, the crew noticed the right engine's (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-41) torque indication began to fluctuate and the right engine oil pressure had dropped to 50 PSI. The crew decided to perform a precautionary shutdown of the engine and continued to CYWG. The crew declared an emergency and then landed the aircraft without further incident.

C-FNAX, a WestJet Boeing 737-MAX, was operating as WJA11853 from Maui (PHOG), HI to Vancouver (CYVR), BC with 6 crew and 170 passengers on board. While in cruise, approximately 850 nm SW of CYVR, the aircraft did not turn at waypoint ZAGER as expected. The flight crew was able to correct this and navigated the aircraft back on course. Shortly after, the flight crew received fuel alert messages from the fuel management computer. The flight crew checked and verified that all fuel indications were accurate. They then carried out the associated non-normal checklists to confirm there were no fuel leaks. The flight crew reached out to their company dispatch and maintenance control to consult about the difficulties they had encountered. The flight crew requested priority handling when they contacted the Vancouver center controller to avoid potential arrival delays. The aircraft arrived without further issues. There were no injuries.Company maintenance performed troubleshooting tasks. No further faults could be recreated, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FCVD, un Pilatus PC-12/45 exploité par Chrono Aviation, effectuait le vol NDL543 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montreal/St-HUbert, QC (CYHU) à destination de l'aéroport de Sanikiluaq, NU (CYSK) avec à son bord 2 membres d'équipage et 2 passagers. Lors de la course à l'atterrissage sur la piste 27, l'aéronef a percuté des feux de piste. Des marques ont étés retrouvées sur le flanc du pneu principal gauche lors de l'inspection après vol. Une inspection de piste a révélé que deux feux de piste ont été endommagées.

C-GEHY, an Air Canada B737-8 was conducting flight AC598 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Orange County/John Wayne Airport (KSNA), CA. On base leg at 3000ft, the crew received a TCAS RA, they followed resolution and climbed 400ft. The flight landed safely in KSNA without further issues.

C-GLKY, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 operated by Perimeter Aviation as flight PAG1519, was landing at Big Trout Lake (CYTL), ON with a crew of 3 and 23 passengers on board. During touchdown, the crew received a "touched runway" light on the annunciator panel. The crew taxied the aircraft to the ramp where the crew and passengers deplaned the aircraft safely. An inspection revealed that the "touched runway" light sensor on the aft belly of the aircraft was damaged.

C-GRFC, a Carson Air Limited Citation 560 Encore, was conducting flight CRN999 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Port Hardy (CYZT), BC, with 2 crew and 2 passengers on board. On final approach into CYZT, the crew lowered the landing gear and the green light which indicates that the right main gear was down and locked, did not illuminate. The crew conducted a missed approach and orbited over the water to troubleshoot the issue. They could not rectify the problem and decided to return to CYVR. They notified air traffic control of the issue and, when they arrived at CYVR, they conducted a fly-by of the tower where the controller confirmed that the landing gear appeared to be extended. The crew, landed without further incident with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) standing by. ARFF attended the aircraft after it stopped. After the landing, the right main gear green light illuminated. The aircraft was taxied to its hangar under its own power.Maintenance found that the right main gear green indicator light bulb was faulty and only came on intermittently. The bulb was replaced, gear swings were conducted, and the airplane was returned to service.

C-GUIM, a Canadian Flight Instructor Inc. Cessna 172M, was on a VFR flight from Claresholm Industrial Airport (CEJ4), AB to Rocky Mountain House (CYRM), AB and back to CEJ4. On board, were two private licensed pilots working towards their respective commercial pilot licenses. The flight departed CEJ4 with approximately 29 US gallons of fuel on board as indicated by the fuel gauges. The return leg of the flight was planned from CYRM direct to CEJ4 but deviated east of Calgary International (CYYC), AB, adding approximately 8 NM to the flight. When the flight was near Okotoks (CFX2), AB the pilot flying realized that the fuel quantity may not be sufficient to make CEJ4. The pilot descended the aircraft to 5500 feet above sea level and continued on to CEJ4. On short final to Runway 21 at CEJ4, the engine (Avco Lycoming O-320-E2D) lost power. During the forced approach the aircraft entered an aerodynamic stall and impacted the ground 400 feet short of the runway. The aircraft subsequently nosed over. The two pilots received minor injuries and the aircraft was severely damaged. The aircraft had been operating for approximately 3.3 flight hours at the time of the engine power loss.

C-FGWJ, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-700, was operating as flight WJA188 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Calgary International (CYYC), AB. On approach to landing the crew suspected a blown tire and requested emergency services to stand by. The flight landed without incident and taxied to the gate.Following the flight, maintenance personnel checked the landing gear and wheels; all were found serviceable. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GANH, an Air North Charter and Training Limited Boeing B737-505, was conducting flight ANT554 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Whitehorse (CYXY), YT, with 5 crewmembers and 110 passengers on board. As the aircraft was taxiing for departure, the crew noticed the A Hydraulic System was losing quantity and pressure. They stopped and turned off the A Hydraulic System pumps, informed air traffic control (ATC) and the flight attendants. The crew referenced the “Loss of System A” checklist and decided to return to the gate. When the alternate nose wheel steering was used, the B Hydraulic System quantity immediately reduced to 60% and a hydraulic mist was observed coming from nose wheel area. The crew requested Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) through ATC. The ARFF crews confirmed a hydraulic leak around the nose gear. The aircraft was shut down and towed back to the gate. Maintenance inspected aircraft and found a burst hydraulic line on the nose gear. The line was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPAK, an Iskwew Air Incorporated Piper PA-31-350 (Navajo Chieftain) operating as training flight SG100T from Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 2 pilots on board. During approach into CYVR, the flight crew selected the landing gear down and the left main gear green light did not illuminate, the red unsafe gear light did illuminate, and the landing gear handle remained in the down position. The crew aborted the approach and flew to the Vancouver VOR to troubleshoot the landing gear issue. The crew was unsuccessful in correcting the landing gear discrepancy and flew past the CYVR control tower.  The tower controller confirmed that the landing gear appeared to be in the down position. The crew returned to the Vancouver VOR and conducted an emergency gear extension procedure with no resulting change in the cockpit indications. The crew declared an emergency and proceeded to land at CYVR with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) crews on standby. The aircraft landed safely. After landing, the crew shutdown and inspected the landing gear down locks. Despite the cockpit indications, all landing gear locks were confirmed to be in place and the crew taxied to the hangar.  Upon inspection, maintenance found that the left landing gear squat switch had failed and the switch was replaced. The aircraft was returned to service.

N880BJ, a Boeing 777-800 operated by American Airlines, was operating as AAL754 from Philadelphia International Airport, Pennsylvania, USA (KPHL) to Charles de Gaulle/Roissy Airport, Paris, France (LFPG). During cruise, the cabin crew detected fumes/odour in the area of the 2R and 3R door. The odour was described as an epoxy smell that worsened as the flight progressed. The flight crew contacted Moncton ACC and requested to return to KPHL due to a mechanical issue. The flight crew accomplished the associated QRH items, and cabin crew checked overhead bins and lavatory trash bins for the source of the fumes/odour, but the source could not be determined. When the fumes/odour began to permeate the entire aircraft, the flight crew declared an emergency while in Canadian airspace and diverted to Bangor International Airport, Maine, USA (KGBR) where they landed without further incident.In KBGR contract maintenance could not determine the source of the fumes. A disinfectant cleaning was completed in the cabin between seat rows 10 thru 19. During the maintenance ferry flight to KPHL the odour was again present in the cabin between rows 10 and 19. Maintenance personnel in KPHL replaced the lower recirculation fan and both the left and right air purification filters and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBXU, un Cessna 177 sous immatriculation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue, depuis l'aéroport de Lachute, QC (CSE4) avec seul le pilote à son bord. Peu après le décollade de CSE4, le pilote a rebroussé chemin et a effectué une approche sur la piste 10. Alors qu'il se trouvait en approche finale, l'aéronef a percuté une clôture situé à environ 300 pieds du seuil de la piste. Par la suite, l'aéronef a basculé vers l'avant et percuté le sol terminant sa course sur le dos, à 150 pieds du seuil de la piste. Le pilote a été blessé mais il n'y a pas eu d'incendie. Aucun signal ELT n'a été capté.

VP-CFO, a Global Express BD-700, private operator, was on a flight from Juan Manuel Galvez International Airport, Roatán, Honduras (MHRO) to London Stansted Airport, London, England (EGSS). At approximately 1739 UTC the aircraft was in cruise at FL450, position 45°53N 056°50W, when the crew contacted Moncton ACC and declared a Pan-Pan due to a cracked windshield. The aircraft was cleared to descend to FL340 and then diverted to Montréal–Trudeau International Airport, Montréal, Quebec (CYUL). The aircraft landed uneventfully in CYUL at approximately 1935 UTC.

C-FHCW, a Learjet 45 operated by Nolinor Aviation was conducting flight NRL48 from Lexington, Kentucky (KLEX) to Mirabel, QC (CYMX), experienced cabin pressurization issues. At 41,000', the crew received a CAS (Crew Alerting System) message indication L R EMER PRESS ON, following this message a CAB DUCT OVHT also appeared.  The flight crew proceeded directly to the QRH checklist. A short time later, a CAS message illuminated displaying CABIN ALTITUDE. Not an extreme rate, but it still showed a positive rate. The flight crew donned oxygen masks and requested a decent from ATC and proceeded with established company procedures.  The aircraft levelled off at 15,000' and the Flight crew elected to declare an emergency with ATC. Considering remaining fuel and the pressurization system was not functioning properly the crew requested an alternate airport in the area. The crew was giving Erie International, Pennsylvania (KERI) and landed without incident.The cabin pressure controller was detected by maintenance as the issue.

C-GEPG, un Boeing 737-800 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA775, s’apprêtait à effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l’aéroport de Los Angeles International, CA (KLAX) avec 6 membres d’équipage et 131 passagers à son bord. Lors de la course au décollage, une indication de porte ouverte est survenue. L’équipage a interrompu le décollage et déclaré une urgence (MAYDAY). La défectuosité s’est résolue alors que l’aéronef circulait vers la barrière.

C-GNCD, a North Cariboo Flying Service Limited Beech B200 operating as flight NCB580M, was conducting a medevac flight from Fort Ware (CAJ9), BC, to Prince George (CYXS), BC. At 1020:03 pacific daylight time (PDT), the CYXS Tower/Ground controller cleared a ground maintenance electrician vehicle (ELC 43) to proceed to the intersection of Runway 15 and Taxiway D; approximately 4750 feet from the threshold of Runway 15. Approximately 10 minutes later, the pilot contacted the controller and reported they were on the ILS approach for Runway 15. The aircraft was subsequently cleared to land on Runway 15 at 1034:53 PDT. The airplane crossed the threshold of Runway 15 at a groundspeed of 130 knots and was approximately 130 feet above ground level (AGL) in a descent. The crew initiated an overshoot at approximately 30 feet AGL when the pilot saw the truck on the runway. The controller instructed ELC43 to exit Runway 15 and, after consultation with the pilot, directed them to perform a 180° turn and cleared them to land on Runway 33. The aircraft landed without further incident.  Nav Canada's Manual of Air Traffic Services - Tower requires that the intended runway and runway protected area are clear of vehicles before the landing aircraft crosses the runway threshold. Nav Canada wrote a Preliminary Safety Investigation Report on the occurrence.

F-GSPI, a Boeing 777-200 operated by Air France was conducting AFR379 from Vancouver Intl, British Columbia (CYVR) to Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport, France (LFPG). When the aircraft was in the vicinity of 61N 040W the aircraft was observed on ADSB descending from FL380 to FL365. The flight crew contacted Gander ACC to declare PAN-PAN due to encountering severe turbulence at FL380. AFR379 was issued a new routing and level clearance to FL370.The flight continued with no further issues.

The Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319, C-FYJE, operating as ROU1873, on a flight from Quebec City (CYQB), QC to Calgary (CYYC), AB was being vectored onto the approach for Runway 35R at CYYC. The Pacific Coastal Airways Saab 340B, C-GPCI, operating as PCO3019, on a flight from Medicine Hat (CYXH), AB to CYYC was being vectored onto the approach for Runway 35L at CYYC. A loss of separation occurred when during vectors separation reduced to 2.8 NM laterally and 400 feet vertically where 3 NM or 1000 feet are required. Lateral separation was regained within 1 minute and both aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GGZZ, a privately owned Rockwell Aero Commander 112, was conducting a local flight from the Midland/Huronia Airport (CYEE), Ontario, with only the pilot on board. Shortly after becoming airborne from runway 16, following landing gear retraction, the pilot detected an issue with the engine and elected to land on the remaining runway. He selected the landing gear down and attempted to keep the aircraft off the runway to allow time for gear extension, but the aircraft touched down with only the left main gear extended. The aircraft slid to a stop about 30 feet beyond the runway surface. There was damage to the propeller, nose gear doors, the right wingtip, and the right wing leading edge, which had struck two runway end lights during the overrun. The pilot was uninjured.

C-FMPN, an Embraer EMB-505 registered to Flightpath Charter Airways Inc. travelling from Westchester County, NY (KHPN) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) declared an emergency due to a generator issue. The crew of the aircraft declared the emergency approximately 50 NM South of Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ). The crew of the aircraft elected to continue towards CYYZ. The aircraft landed safely in CYYZ at 22:15 Z (18:15 ET). There were no impacts to operations.

C-FONK, a Swoop B737-800 was conducting flight WO646 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Norman Manley International Airport (MKJP), Kingston, Jamaica. While in the vicinity of Savannah/Hilton Head International Airport (KSAV), Georgia, USA, a flight attendant became ill. Medlink was contacted and the flight attendant's duties were redistributed. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

CF-ZPO, a privately registered Aero Commander 100-180, was conducting a visual flight rules trip from Prince George (CYXS), BC, to Vanderhoof, (CAU4) BC with only the pilot on board. Shortly after takeoff, in the climb through approximately 300 feet above ground level, the engine (Avco Lycoming, O-360-A2F) lost power. The pilot switched the fuel selector from the right tank (which had been left nearly empty) position to both tanks. This did not rectify the power loss. The airplane landed hard on the grass to the right of Runway 06-24, bounced, and slid onto the runway. It came to a halt near the center line. The left main gear leg was broken but there were no injuries. A signal from the emergency locator transmitter was not received by the Canadian Mission Control Centre.The owner is in communication with maintenance personnel and has ordered a replacement for the broken landing gear.

C-GELP, a British Columbia Helicopters Limited Guimbal Cabri G2 helicopter was conducting infield circuit training at Abbotsford (CYXX), BC, with only the student pilot on board. After conducting half an hour of training with his instructor, the pilot continued circuit training solo. Having completed 3 successful circuits, the pilot intended to land and pick up his instructor. As the helicopter was slowed below translational lift speed, it began to descend while in a slight left turn. The pilot raised the collective and the helicopter began to yaw to the left. More collective was pulled, and the helicopter began to spin. After a number of rotations, the right rear skid contacted the ground and the helicopter rolled onto its side. The pilot egressed and was uninjured. Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting attended the scene. The helicopter was substantially damaged.British Columbia Helicopters Limited recovered the helicopter to their hangar where the damage and maintenance requirements will be assessed.

L’aéronef Piper PA-30 Twin Comanche (immatriculation C-FFOW, numéro de série 30-1737) exploité par l’école d’aviation Rouyn-Noranda, effectuait un vol local d’entrainement selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda (CYUY) (Québec) avec 1 instructeur de vol et 1 élève pilote à bord. Alors que l’aéronef était en croisière une panne du moteur numéro 1 est survenue. Les pilotes ont tenté de redémarrer le moteur sans succès. Une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée et un retour vers CYUY a été amorcé. Peu après, une panne du moteur numéro 2 est survenue. Le pilote a lors tenté d’effectuer un atterrissage d’urgence sur la route 117, à environ 6 NM à l’est de CYUY. Au sol, l’aéronef a percuté un poteau électrique lors de la course à l’atterrissage. L’aéronef a subi des dommages substantiels mais il n’y a pas eu d’incendie. Les occupants ont reçu des blessures mineures.

C-GPCE, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited Beech 1900D, operating as flight PCO1206, was conducting a flight from Kamloops (CYKA), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC. At approximately 6.5 nautical miles north-northwest of CYVR, PCO1206 was assigned Runway (RWY) 08L by the Vancouver Terminal Low North (LN) controller. C-FFGA, a Skylink Express Inc. Cessna 208B (Caravan), operating as flight SLQ713, was conducting a flight from Victoria International (CYYJ), BC, to CYVR. At approximately 7.5 nautical miles southwest of CYVR, SLQ713 was assigned RWY 08R by the LN controller. Both aircraft were vectored and cleared by the LN controller for the approach on their assigned runway; PCO1206 was cleared for the RNAV approach on RWY 08L at 16:39:10 pacific daylight time (PDT) and 24 seconds later, SLQ713 was cleared for the ILS approach on RWY 08R. The aircraft spacing began to reduce and the LN controller cancelled the approach clearance for SLQ713 with a heading change to 110 degrees. A loss of separation occurred at 16:40:55 PDT when the aircraft spacing was reduced to 2.3 miles laterally and 900 feet vertically. The Nav Canada Manual of Air Traffic Services - Tower requires a separation of 3 miles laterally and 1000 feet vertically. Due to work occurring at the runway end safety area of Runway 08L, the ILS approach for that runway was unauthorized as published in a NOTAM.

L’aéronef Beech C23 Sundowner (immatriculation C-GBQI, numéro de série M-2264) exploité par le Collège d’enseignement général et professionnel (CEGEP) de Chicoutimi effectuait un vol d’entrainement local depuis l’aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré (CYRC) (Québec) avec un instructeur et une élève-pilote à son bord.  Alors que l’aéronef se trouvait en base droite pour un atterrissage simulant une panne moteur dans le circuit, celui-ci a percuté des arbustes situés à environ 1300 pieds du seuil de la piste 30 avant de percuter le sol. L’aéronef a subi des dommages substantiels mais il n’y a pas eu d’incendie. Les deux occupants ont été blessés. La radiobalise de repérage d’urgence (ELT) s’est activée à l’impact.

N814AG, an Airbus A321-251N, operated by Aviation Capital Incorporated was on a positioning flight with flight planned routing from Portland International Jetport, ME, USA (KPWM) to Cornwall Airport Newquay, England (EGHQ). The aircraft was approximately 2 hours into the flight when the crew noticed the #2 engine oil level had decreased from 12 quarts to 8 quarts and as the flight progressed the oil level continued to decrease. At approximately 1335 UTC, position 50N 036W, the crew informed Moncton (YQM) ACC that they were diverting to Bangor International Airport, ME, USA (KBGR) with a possible engine issue. The aircraft was 110NM from KBGR when the crew started the auxiliary power unit (APU) and carried out a precautionary shut down of #2 engine. The crew informed YQM ACC that one engine had been shut down and they were declaring an emergency. The aircraft exited Canadian airspace at 1550 UTC. The aircraft landed safely in KBGR at 1609 UTC.Maintenance determined the source of the oil leak was from a torn o-ring on the #2 engine starter shaft. Both o-rings on the starter shaft and one o-ring in the reduction gear box were replaced. Engine #2 was ground run with no leaks present; the aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GJYZ, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting a flight from Pikangikum (CYPM), ON to Sandy Lake (CZSJ), ON with 3 crew and 28 passengers on board. Upon landing Runway 29 at CZSJ, the tail contacted the ground and the "TOUCHED RUNWAY" annunciator illuminated. The aircraft subsequently taxied to the apron. The TSB is investigating.
