C-GJZN, un Dash-8 Q400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8011, s'apprêtait à effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination d'Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW) avec 64 passagers et 4 membres d'équipage. Lors de l’embarquement et du second démarrage de l’APU, une forte odeur de fumée a été constatée dans l’arrière de l’appareil et le système de détection de fumée arrière s’est déclenché. Les passagers ont été évacués par la porte principale sans encombre. L’équipage a demandé l’intervention des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) et aucune source de chaleur n’a été détectée. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

The Air Canada Boeing 737-8 MAX, C-GEPF, operating as ACA200 on a flight from Vancouver (CYVR), BC to Calgary (CYYC), AB was cleared to descend to FL220. The crew readback FL220 and proceeded to continue the descent through FL220 and at FL217 was queried by the controller. They were subsequently re-cleared to FL220, but the aircraft descended to FL212 before the aircraft climbed to the assigned altitude. A Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-8-400, C-GGCI, was operating as flight JZA392 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to CYYC. JZA392 was maintaining FL210 and was turned away from ACA200 by air traffic control. A loss of separation occurred when separation between the two aircraft decreased to 200 feet vertically and 3.8 nautical miles laterally where 1000 feet or 5 nautical miles is required.

The privately registered Cessna 172F, C-FSQH, was on a flight from Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB to Grande (CFA5), AB. After completing two inspection passes over Runway 21, the pilot entered a left-hand circuit for landing. It was noted that the wind was from left to right across the runway, but the strength could not be accurately determined because the windsock was not functional. On short final, approximately 10 feet off of the ground, a large gust of wind picked up the left wing and although the pilot responded with full left rudder the aircraft continued turning to the right. A go-around was initiated but by the time the aircraft responded, it had drifted to the edge of the airport clearing. During the climb the right wing began to hit the tops of the trees. The aircraft then turned further to the right and came to rest nose down, suspended in the trees 8 feet above the ground. The pilot and his passenger were uninjured in the crash. The ELT was turned on manually; there was no fire.

C-GPTS, an Airbus A330-243 operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC699 from Athens International Airport (LGAV), Greece, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario. During approach to runway 24L, while at approximately 5000 feet in the vicinity of waypoint LETAK, the aircraft flew through a rain cell and was struck by lightning. The strike was felt by the pilots through the rudder pedals and floor of the flight deck, however, there were no alarms, warning messages, or system issues noted. Approximately two minutes later, the flight crew detected a strong electrical burning smell which subsided after approximately 10 seconds. The flight crew advised ATC of the lightning strike and requested the presence of ARFF upon arrival in the event that an evacuation became necessary. The flight landed uneventfully following the approach, and was escorted by ARFF to their gate, where the passengers disembarked normally. Inspection by maintenance personnel did not reveal any visual damage, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FGZH, a Top Aces A-4N was conducting flight Skyhawk9 supporting a US Air Force - Europe mission out of Nordholz/Cuxhaven Airport (ETMN), Germany. During the Return to Base (RTB) phase of flight, the pilot noticed the master warning light illuminated. The pilot looked down at the emergency light panel and noticed the "Control Hydraulic" light on. The pilot communicated with the lead aircraft and actioned the flight control hydraulic systems failure checklist. The utility hydraulic system continued to power all systems, but the pilot elected to land ASAP with an arrested landing. The pilot declared a mayday with ATC and diverted to Hohn Air Base (ETNH), Germany for the arrested landing/cable engagement. The aircraft was towed off the runway to a hangar. Post flight inspection revealed hydraulic fluid on the right-hand fuselage and inboard of the right-hand wing. The aircraft was removed from service to determine cause of issue.

The Air Canada Airbus A320, C-FPWE, was operating as flight AC299 from Winnipeg (CYWG), MB to Vancouver (CYVR), BC with 5 crew and 118 passengers. While in cruise flight, a flight attendant became incapacitated and was unable to continue to perform their duties. With the incapacitated flight attendant, the cabin crew staffing requirement became lower than required. The flight crew declared an emergency and diverted to Calgary (CYYC), AB. The flight landed without incident and was met at the gate by EMS. The incapacitated flight attendant was taken to hospital for evaluation. A replacement flight attendant met the aircraft and the flight continued to CYVR.

The Pacific Coastal Airways Saab 340B, C-FPCZ, was operating as PCO3028 from Dawson Creek (CYDQ), BC to Calgary (CYYC), AB. Earlier in the day, the aircraft was ferried from Vancouver (CYVR), BC to CYYC following a major repair, including a right engine (General Electric CT7-9B) overhaul. Following the ferry flight, both engines were inspected with no faults found. The aircraft was released for service and conducted a flight from CYYC to CYDQ. The flight to CYDQ was uneventful, however the right engine inter-turbine temperature (ITT) was indicating 15 degrees Celsius higher than the left engine. The flight crew maintained the right engine torque below maximum cruise torque to maintain the ITT within operating limits. On the occurrence flight from CYDQ to CYYC, the flight crew again observed higher ITT on the right engine and maintained reduced cruise torque. Shortly after beginning the descent into CYYC, the flight crew heard a loud pop and observed the right engine ITT increase and engine torque fall to 20%. The flight crew performed the engine failure procedure and actioned the QRH before contacting Edmonton Centre to declare an emergency. The flight crew conducted an uneventful single-engine approach and landing on Runway 17R where it was met by ARFF. The aircraft was inspected by ARFF and released to taxi to the gate. The 3 crew and 19 passengers received no injuries. Company maintenance will follow-up with TSB regarding findings.

The privately registered Cessna 172C, C-FCJG, was operating on a pleasure flight from Athabasca (CYWM), AB. While in cruise flight, 35 nm NNE of CYWM, at approximately 1000 feet AGL, the pilot attempted to apply full throttle to initiate a climb. When the throttle was increased, the engine (Teledyne Continental O-300-D) remained at 1500 rpm. Mixture was increased to full rich with no change to rpm and carburetor heat was applied with a slight decrease in rpm. As the pilot was unable to climb to clear local terrain, the pilot elected to conduct a forced approach into a cleared cut block. On final approach the pilot secured the engine and shut off fuel. The aircraft collided with tree stumps and the aircraft received substantial damage. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was wearing the provided lap belt (the aircraft was not equipped with a shoulder harness) and was able to exit the aircraft once it came to rest. The pilot received minor injuries.  The 406 MHz ELT did not activate and was manually activated by the pilot. JRCC received the distress signal. A SAR helicopter was dispatched and retrieved the pilot approximately 2 hours later.

C-GIUF, an Air Canada Airbus A321-211 operating as Flight ACA1090 was travelling from Toronto/Lester B Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL. Shortly after departure, approximately 130 NM south of CYYZ, the crew declared an emergency (PAN PAN) due to a hydraulic failure and elected to return to CYYZ. The aircraft was given priority and landed safely on Runway 23 at 18:43Z (14:43 EDT). The aircraft stopped on the runway due to the loss of nosewheel steering. The aircraft was subsequently towed off the runway. Maintenance found right hand MLG bypass valve leaking.

The VIH Helicopters Kamov KA-32, C-FIGR, was conducting heli-slinging operations 22 nm N of Fort Liard (CYJF), NT. The helicopter was slinging 4 cut-up bridge structure sections. The first section was slung horizontally, using a 4-point rigging system, and was moved without issue. The second section was rigged on one end by the loadmaster to be moved in a vertical configuration. While moving this section the load became unsecured and dropped into the bush. There were no injuries, and the helicopter received no damage.

C-FFAL, un Boeing 737-2R8C exploité par Glencore Canada Corporation sous l'indicatif RAG100, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) à destination de Kattiniq/Donaldson, QC (CTP9) avec 72 passagers et 4 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de la montée, en passant le niveau de vol 280 à environ 150 nm au nord de CYUY, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison d’une indication de feu moteur gauche et a demandé à se diriger vers Val-d’Or, QC (CYVO). La procédure d'urgence a été exécutée et l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre à CYVO. L’avion a été arrêté sur la piste et une inspection a confirmée qu’il n’y avait aucun incendie. Une fois cela confirmé, l’équipage a tenté de déplacer l’avion, mais les freins avaient surchauffé et étaient bloqués. Les passagers ont été désembarqués et l’ingénieur de vol a fait relâcher les freins et l’avion a pu circuler jusqu’au terminal. Le filage des détecteurs de feu moteur a été trouvé endommagé et donnait de fausses indications.

The Aero Pacific Flightlines Gulfstream G-650ER, HL8299, was operating from Gimpo/Seoul (RKSS), South Korea to Cleveland (KCLE), Ohio, United States. During cruise flight at FL450, while approximately 125 nm WSW of Whitehorse (CYXY) YT, the flight crew reported experiencing severe turbulence and difficulty maintaining altitude. Vertical deviations of up to 500 feet in altitude were observed. The flight crew did not declare an emergency and no injuries were reported. The aircraft continued flight to KCLE.

At 0012 EDT on 15 October 2022, MTC31, a Greater Toronto Airports Authority maintenance vehicle which was westbound on taxiway Juliet, entered the threshold of runway 15R despite having recieved and read back a clearance to hold short of that runway. At the same time, C-GEOJ, an Air Canada B737 opearating as flight ACA174, had been cleared to land on runway 15R, and was inside 1 mile final. The tower controller noticed the incursion, and instructed ACA174 to go around. The ACA174 flight crew complied, received vectors to restart the approach, and landed on runway 15R at 0025 EDT. VFR conditions prevailed at the time of the incursion. The lowest altitude reached by ACA174 was approximately 150 feet AGL. The vehicle had entered the displaced portion of the threshold for runway 15R, and was approximately 400 feet from the displaced threshold.

N823AN, a Boeing 787-900 aircraft, operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL 87 from London Heathrow, London, England (EGLL) to Chicago O'Hare Intl, Chicago, IL (KORD).  At 1309Z the flight crew contacted Gander ACC, declared a MAYDAY and requested clearance to divert to Keflavik International Airport, Iceland (BIKF) due to a fuel valve and multiple electrical failures. Gander ACC cleared AAL 87 to BIKF and the aircraft exited the Canadian airspace at 1329Z. AAL 87 subsequently landed BIKF without incident at 1425Z.American Airlines dispatched maintenance to BKEF. A wiring check was completed with no findings. Maintenance discovered that remote power distribution units (RPDU 73 - M6 & M7) were faulty. The units drive the Primary Flight Display (PFD) and the Electronic Flight Instrument System (EFIS).  Both M6 and M7 units were replaced. In addition, the secondary power distribution card DC2 was replaced. All status messages cleared, and the aircraft was returned to service.

The Summit Air Dornier 228-202, C-FPSA, was operating as flight SU1023 from Hay River (CYHY), NT to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT. While on final approach, approximately 6 nm from Runway 28, the flight crew heard an audible click and observed a 'power light' for the standby attitude indicator had illuminated. Additionally, the right-hand engine indications all read zero, except for the inter-turbine temperature (ITT) gauge, which was operating normally. Additionally, the first officer’s communication radios were not working. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and continued the approach. Approximately 4 miles from the runway, the captain observed that the BW2 circuit breaker had tripped. The circuit breaker was reset and the issues were rectified. The aircraft continued on the approach and landed without further issues. There were no injuries. Company maintenance performed troubleshooting and found no faults. The aircraft was returned to service service.

C-GWCN, a Boeing 737-700 operated by WestJet Airlines, was conducting flight WJA649 from Toronto, Ontario (CYYZ) to Calgary AB, (CYYC). C-GLUN, a Textron Aviation Beech 200GT operated by Canwest Air was conducting MEDEVAC flight CWA928 from Fairview, AB (CEB3) to Calgary, AB (CYYC). The Calgary terminal arrival controller sequenced CWA928 first for an arrival on Runway 35R, with WJA649 sequenced behind. CWA928 was instructed to, and maintained 160 knots on final approach; WJA649 was maintaining approximately 230 knots. Due to the difference in approach speeds, and the reducing distance between the aircraft, the Calgary tower controller instructed WJA649 to pull up and go around as the lateral separation between CWA928 and WJA649 was reducing. CWA928 continued for landing on Runway 35R. WJA649 executed a go around and was sequenced back in for landing. Lateral separation was reduced to 2.8 nm where 3.0 nm is required, and 900 feet vertically where 1000 feet is required.

C-GKKB, a Kenn Borek Air Ltd. Douglas DC-3C Basler BT-67 was conducting a positioning flight under instruments flight rules (IFR) from Brownsville/South Padre Island Intl. (KBRO), TX to Liberia/Daniel Oduber Quirós Intl. (MRLB), Costa Rica. After RNAV approach runway 25, engines' throttles were brought to idle just before touchdown.  After uneventful touchdown, aircraft decelerated normally, and the tail came down.  Flight crew introduced beta as they thought the tail was down and the aircraft started veering to the right. PF applied more left beta and left brakes with no effect and the aircraft continued to veer harder right.  The aircraft started skidding and veered off runway into soft grassy field.  Aircraft came to a stop 10 feet from the edge of runway.  There was no damage to aircraft and no injuries. Aircraft was inspected with no defect noted by maintenance.

C-GKFF, a Kelowna Flightcraft Air Charter Limited Convair 580, was conducting flight KFA579 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC to Kamloops (CYKA), BC, with 2 flight crew on board. As the crew attempted to reduce power for the descent and approach into CYKA, the engine power would not decrease below approximately 1200 hp on either engine (Rolls-Royce 501-D13): 300-400 hp is typical and 0 hp is achievable. The crew attempted to rectify the issue without success. They diverted to their maintenance base in Kelowna (CYLW), BC. The same power issue occurred on the descent and the crew declared an emergency with Kelowna air traffic control. On touchdown, the horsepower on both engines remained at approximately 1000 hp with abnormal reverse indications. The crew shut down both engines on the runway during the landing roll. Emergency vehicles were standing by. The aircraft exited the runway on Taxiway E, the crew completed their shut down, and the aircraft was towed to maintenance.The operator's maintenance completed various engine and propeller checks with no faults found. Static engine runs with power cycles from flight range to flight idle to reverse power completed with normal response. High speed taxi tests were completed with all indications being normal except a slightly delayed beta light indication on one propellor; the beta switch was replaced. Engine runs and taxi tests repeated with normal response and indications. The airplane has been returned to service.

C-GUNL, a Blackcomb Helicopters Limited Partnership Eurocopter EC 130-B4, was conducting the second leg of a sightseeing trip from Ipsoot Lake (50° 21.2’ N, 123° 02.1’ W), BC, to Whistler Municipal (CBE9), BC, with the pilot and 2 passengers on board. Approximately 3 minutes into the flight, the pilot turned on the fan to cool the cabin. About 30 seconds after the fan noise stabilized, there was a loud "pop" and smoke from behind the dash filled the cabin. The pilot vented the cabin, shut off electrics, and transmitted a Mayday call. The passengers were briefed that they were going to conduct an emergency landing which was conducted without incident. The pilot shut down the helicopter, retrieved the fire extinguisher and survival kit, and moved the passengers to a safe area. There were no injuries and no fire. A company helicopter arrived approximately 40 minutes later to pick up the passengers and return them to CBE9. Another helicopter arrived and the crew conducted an inspection of the occurrence helicopter. With the fan circuit breakers pulled, the helicopter was flown back to CBE9.Maintenance removed the fan, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FZVX, a North Cariboo Flying Service Limited Beech Aircraft Corporation BE 200 (Super King Air 200), was conducting medevac flight NCB860 from Prince George (CYXS), BC, to Fort Saint John (CYXJ), BC, with 4 crew and 1 passenger on board. The airplane was climbing through 19000 feet above sea level when the No. 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-42) began surging. Torque gauge fluctuations were between 1600 to 800 foot-pounds of torque and the aircraft began to yaw. The crew declared a MAYDAY emergency and diverted back to CYXS. On reduction of power for the descent to CYXS, the fluctuation ceased and the crew landed safely without further incident.Maintenance determined that the primary propeller governor was faulty and replaced it. The aircraft was returned to service and maintenance is awaiting the results of the teardown report for the propeller governor.

C-GHQQ an Air Canada B787-8 was conducting flight AC854 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to London/Heathrow Airport (EGLL), UK. During the flight, a flight attendant became ill. The crew declared a PAN PAN with EGLL where the aircraft landed safely. EMS met the aircraft and transported the cabin crew to the hospital.

C-FJOU, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was conducting flight ROU1637 from Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC.  During cruise FL370 at waypoint MAGGO, flight crew received a TCAS TA (traffic advisory) followed shortly after with TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to ''climb more then 600ft per minute''.  Flight crew complied with the RA and climbed to FL 375 at which point the RA changed to ''monitor vertical speed''.  Flight crew advised ATC and made note of a Falcon jet climbing to FL360 below.  Minimum separation was reported around +/- 1500 feet.  Flight crew returned to FL370 once clear of conflict and continued to destination without further incident.

C-FYJE, un Airbus 319 exploité par Air Canada Rouge LP sous l’indicatif ROU1794, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Toronto/Lester B.Pearson, ON (CYYZ) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Lors de l’approche initiale à CYQB, l’équipage a reçu le message « F/CTL FLAP LOCKED » du moniteur électronique centralisé de bord (ECAM) lorsque le volet numéro 2 a été sélectionné. L’équipage a interrompu l’approche et effectué une remontée. Suite à l’évaluation du problème de volet, l’équipage a avisé le contrôleur aérien de la décision de dérouter le vol vers l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) et a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN). Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été avisés et l’aéronef a atterri sans encombre sur la piste 24R.

C-FDDX, a De Havilland DHC-3T float aircraft operated by True North Airways Inc., was conducting a flight from Mistissini Water Aerodrome, QC (CSE6) to Lac Pluto, QC. While maneuvering for a landing, the aircraft struck the surface of the water. The passengers, who were waiting nearby, transported the pilot to a nearby cabin, where he was later taken to hospital by a search and rescue helicopter. The pilot, who was the sole person on board, received serious injuries. The aircraft was destroyed. The TSB is investigating.

C-FGSJ a Cargojet Boeing 767-300 was conducting flight CJT926 from Viracopos International Airport (SBKP) São Paulo, Brazil to El Dorado International Airport (SKBO) Bogota, Colombia. At top of descent into Bogota, the crew experienced an unreliable airspeed indication on the captain's instruments with the EICAS message IAS DISAGREE. Approximately 2 minutes after the unreliable airspeed issue, the crew had multiple EICAS messages: Rudder Ratio / Aileron Lockout / GRD PROX SYS / L ENG EEC MODE / R ENG EEC MODE. The crew declared a mayday into SKBO and carried out appropriate QRH procedures and landed safely. A partial flap landing was conducted, the aircraft was inspected by Fire/Crash/Rescue. No issues noted and brake temps were not excessive.

C-GYSG, un Maule M-5-235C privé exploité par le Club de vol à voile de Québec, effectuait un vol de remorquage selon les règles de vol à vue depuis une piste en gazon privée située près de la marina de Baie Saint-Paul, QC. L’aéronef a décollé en remorquant un planeur et, peu de temps après, alors qu’il avait atteint une altitude d’environ 1800 pieds au-dessus du sol, le pilote a observé que de la fumée s’échappait sous le tableau de bord. Quelques secondes plus tard, le moteur a perdu toute sa puissance. Le pilote a largué le planeur et a manœuvré pour retourner atterrir sur la piste. Une fois établi en finale, l’aéronef n’a pas pu atteindre le seuil de piste et a dû atterrir environ 100 mètres avant celui-ci. L’aéronef a terminé sa course dans un bosquet d’arbres. Le pilote n’a pas été blessé et l’aéronef a subi des dommages importants.

C-FKMA, a Piper PA-31 operated by Aries Aviation, was conducting a survey flight from the Springbank Airport, AB (CYBW). During the survey portion of the flight, the pilot noticed a slight decrease in the right engine (Lycoming TIO-540) oil pressure indication. Continuing to monitor the right engine oil pressure, the pilot observed that the oil pressure had continued to decrease. The decision was made to abort the survey mission and return to CYBW. The pilot performed a precautionary shut down of the right engine and conducted a single-engine approach and landing at CYBW. Subsequent investigation by company maintenance found that the right engine only contained approximately 4.5 quarts of oil, and the oil scrapper ring for one of the pistons was broken into multiple pieces resulting in excess oil consumption during the flight.

C-GJAZ, a Jazz Aviation LP MHI RJ Aviation ULC CRJ900 was conducting flight 8897 from Phoenix/Sky Harbor Intl. (KPHX), AZ to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC. Shortly after take-off, KPHX tower advised flight crew that they appear to have a fuel leak.  Flight crew decided to return to KPHX with ARFF on standby.  Flight landed in KPHX without further incident.  Maintenance found fuel cap on top right hand wight installed backward.

C-FLQY, a Dehavilland DHC-8-402 aircraft, was conducting Porter Airlines flight POE293 from Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON to Moncton/ Greater Moncton Romeo Leblanc International Airport (CYQM), NB. After the flight had landed and all the passengers had deplaned, the pilots noticed a series of electrical faults in the cockpit. The start select light illuminated and the ground power unit (GPU) failed. The auxiliary power unit (APU) was then started however, within 25 seconds, the crew noted electrical fluctuations, and the APU generator warning light illuminated. The avionics were turned off to conserve battery power. In consultation with the company maintenance, a bus fault reset was done to eliminate the start select light that had illuminated however, this was unsuccessful, so all electrical power was turned off. With further consultation with maintenance, the batteries were turned on and the GPU was reconnected and maintaining voltage to the aircraft. Shortly after, a ramp agent informed the crew that smoke was coming from the #2 engine. The Captain then turned off all batteries and GPU power and exited the aircraft to inspect the #2 engine and subsequently observed thick smoke coming from the starter/generator vent of the #2 engine cowl. The Captain returned to the aircraft and activated both engine fire bottles into the #2 engine to extinguish the fire. ARFF arrived shortly after and sprayed water into the generator vent.The maintenance department found that the cause of the overheated starter/ generator was an overheating K2 relay. This relay should have opened upon engine shutdown however, it was found that it stuck in the closed position which allowed the buses to be powered which catastrophically overheated the starter/generator. The K2 relay and the starter/generator were replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FWEW, a WestJet Encore Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400), was operating as flight WEN3114 from Victoria International (CYYJ), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 4 crew members and 76 passengers on board. During the takeoff roll, the “No.2 AC GEN” caution light illuminated at a speed below 80 knots. The crew rejected the take-off and a MAYDAY emergency was declared with air traffic control. Once the crew had diagnosed the cause of the warning, the emergency was canceled, and the aircraft was taxied back to the gate without further incident. No one was injured and there was no damage to the aircraft.Maintenance replaced the No. 2 alternating current generator and conducted a function check before releasing it back into service.

C-FHWX, a Harvard 2 aircraft, operated by The Canadian Harvard Aircraft Association, was completing its 6th circuit at the Tillsonburg Airport (CYTB), ON. During the landing, the aircraft touched down on Runway 32 with the landing gear retracted. There were no injuries to the two occupants, but the aircraft was substantially damaged. It was reported that the warning horn for the landing gear did not operate.

C-IDNC, un ultra-léger de base Quad City Challenger II privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis une piste privée en terre battue située dans le secteur de Maria, QC avec seulement un pilote à bord. Les prévisions graphiques (GFA) pour la journée prévoyaient un ciel dégagé avec une visibilité de plus de 6 milles terrestres. Vers 16h, un citoyen a avisé la Sureté du Québec de la présence de l’aéronef dans un champ. L’aéronef semblait avoir heurté le sol en position de piqué. La cabine de pilotage était détruite et la queue de l’aéronef pointait vers le haut. Selon les informations recueillies, aucune autre trace au sol n’était présente. Toutes les composantes majeures de l’aéronef, c’est-à-dire les ailes, la queue, le train d’atterrissage, le moteur et la cabine étaient présents et liés ensemble. Une ligne à haute tension d’Hydro-Québec se situait à proximité du lieu de l’écrasement. Aucun fils électrique ou structure n’ont présenté des dommages après avoir été inspectés et il n’y a eu aucune coupure d’électricité dans le secteur. Le pilote a été trouvé à bord sans vie. L’heure, la direction du vol, l’altitude et la phase de vol, c’est-à-dire le décollage, la croisière ou l’atterrissage au moment de l’accident sont inconnus.

C-FYMV, a float-equipped de Havilland DHC-2 MK1 operated by Kississing Lake Lodge (dba Wings Over Kississing), was conducting a flight from Lynn Lake/Eldon Lake (CKD3), MB to Kovacs Lake, MB with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. Roughly 10 minutes into the flight, while in cruise at 2500 feet ASL, a loud grinding noise was heard from the engine (Pratt & Whitney - USA R-985-AN-14B) before it stopped immediately. The pilot made a rapid emergency descent towards Dunsheath Lake, MB and transmitted a MAYDAY call on 126.7 MHz, which was received from another aircraft flying in the area. C-FYMV landed uneventfully on Dunsheath Lake. The pilot immediately exited the aircraft and called the operator on satellite phone to report the incident and coordinate a rescue.

C-GTVO, a Boeing 737-219C operated by Chrono Aviation Inc., was conducting flight MBK795 from Mary River (CMR2) NU. to Iqaluit (CYFB) NU. After departing CMR2 at approximately 9000 feet, the flight crew received a warning indicating the #2 start valve was open. The QRH checklist was consulted and a precautionary shutdown of the number 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney USA JT8D-17) was completed. The flight attendants were notified and the passengers were briefed for an abnormal landing. The aircraft made a return to CMR2, a PAN PAN call was made, and emergency services were placed on standby. A single engine overweight landing was performed and the aircraft landed safely on Runway 30 at CMR2.This was the second similar occurrence for the aircraft (see TSB occurrence A22C0084). The operator's maintenance carried out extensive electrical wiring troubleshooting and discovered one flight deck connector pin shorting against its connector. The connector was replaced, test flights were conducted, and the issue was cleared.

N260DC, un De Havilland DHC-1 Chipmunk exploité par Ghoswriter Airshow LLC, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis Montréal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX) à destination de Burlington, VT (KBTV). Peu après le décollage de CYMX, le pilote a déclaré une urgence en raison de problème avec le moteur. Le pilote a demandé un retour vers CYMX et il s'est posé sans encombre.

C-FYAI, un De Havilland DHC8-300 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE832 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) avec 4 membres d’équipage et 22 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée initiale au départ de CYQB, après avoir sélectionné les volets à la position relevée, l’équipage a constaté qu’une perte totale de liquide hydraulique du système numéro #1 était survenue. La liste de vérifications du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour « Loss of Hydraulic #1 Quantity » a été effectuée. Une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée et l’équipage a demandé un déroutement vers l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d’aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés et, suite à une inspection, l’aéronef a circulé jusqu’à la barrière. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-FNVU, un Airbus A320 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA411, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). Peu après le décollage, alors que l’aéronef de trouvait à 28 milles nautiques (NM) à l’ouest de CYUL, l’équipage a reçu un message du moniteur électronique centralisé de bord (ECAM) indiquant un déverouillage du méchanisme d'inverseur de poussée du moteur numéro 2 (engine thrust reverse unlock). L'équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) et a demandé un retour vers CYUL. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

N3744G, a U.S. registered, privately-operated Cessna 310R aircraft, was conducting a photo survey flight over Nova Scotia from Bangor Intl (KBGR), ME. The aircraft was in cruise flight about 15 nm west of Trenton (CYTN), NS, and was climbing from 11 500 feet to a higher cleared altitude when the aircraft engines began running rough following an engine mixture control adjustment to both engines. The pilot conducted the emergency checklist while circling CYTN as a precaution. Unable to maintain altitude, the pilot declared an emergency with ATS. When at 10 000 feet the pilot returned engine controls to initial settings and the engine roughness subsided. The pilot cancelled the emergency with ATS and continued the photo survey flight. The aircraft returned and landed at KBGR without further incident.

C-FAJA, a WestJet Airlines Ltd. Boeing 787-9 was conducting flight WJA0004 From London/ Gatwick Intl. (EGKK), United Kingdom to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  On initial climb approximately 107 NM W of EGKK, Cabin crew members identified and reported to Flight crew a burning plastic smell/odor over the L3/R3 jump seats and aft galley.  Flight crew completed the appropriate checklist and shutdown power sources, cabin in-flight entertainment system and cabin lighting.  No improvement was noted with the smell intensity and decision was made to declare a PANPAN.   Fuel dump was conducted to reach applicable landing weight and flight diverted back to EGKK.  After uneventful landing, ARFF inspected the aircraft with no fault found.  Maintenance replaced mufflers on right hand air conditioning pack and aircraft was returned to service.

C-FTXE, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight SWG688 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Varadero /Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl. (MUVR), Cuba.  Approximately an hour from landing, a Flight crew member became incapacitated. The incapacitated flight crew member subsequently was able to assist during landing phase of the flight as symptoms subsided.  Flight landed in MUVR without further incident.

C-GWYM, a privately registered Cessna P210N, was taxiing past the hangar line at Weyburn (CJE3), SK when the aircraft nosewheel fell into a hole on the apron. The hole had been made by concrete repair crews associated with construction work that had been NOTAMed. The aircraft sustained damage to its nose gear, propeller, and forward belly section. It has been grounded pending repairs.

The FulcrumAir Corp. E7500 rotary wing RPAS was conducting test flying under a Transport Canada SFOC at the City of Calgary RPAS test facility. After a successful test flight and landing, the RPAS began to smoke and then caught fire igniting the LiPo batteries. The ensuing fire caused substantial damage to the RPAS. There were no injuries.

C-FVXT, a privately registered Cessna 150G, landed on a private aerodrome near Sovereign, SK. Upon touchdown, the left main wheel assembly came apart. The aircraft veered to the left and departed the maintained portion of the runway. The left wing contacted the ground. The aircraft sustained damage to its left wing and the propeller was bent. The pilot sustained minor injuries.

C-GPWG, an Air Canada Airbus A320-200 was conducting flight AC7031 from Buffalo/ Niagara Intl. (KBUF), NY to Philadelphia Intl. (KPHL), PA.  During the approach at KPHL runway 27R, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) at approximately 1300 feet AGL.  Flight crew conducted a go around and landed without further incident.  Aircraft in conflict was conducting banner towing.

C-GTZH, an Air Canada A220-300 was conducting flight AC734 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to New York/ LaGuardia Intl. (KLGA), NY. During the approach at 4000 feet, Flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to monitor vertical speed. Flight landed in KLGA without further incident.

C-FGKH, an Air Canada Airbus A320-200 was conducting flight AC714 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to New York/ LaGuardia Intl. (KLGA), NY.  During the approach at 4000 feet, Flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to monitor vertical speed.  ATC was advised and flight landed in KLGA without further incident.

C-GPCL, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited Textron (Beech) 1900D, was conducting flight PCO343 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Bella Coola (CYBD), BC, with 2 flight crew members and 16 passengers on board. During the climb to cruise altitude, the flight crew identified fuel flow fluctuations of between 100 and 450 pounds per hour to the right engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada, PT6A-67D). The flight crew requested a return to CYVR with air traffic control and noted the reason for the diversion was an indication issue. As a result, CYVR placed the airport rescue and firefighting crews on a precautionary standby. The flight landed without further issue and shortly after continued to CYBD using a different aircraft. Subsequent maintenance activities replaced the right-hand fuel flow transducer and following function testing the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJVE, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting Flight SWG423 from Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), Dominican Republic to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario with 8 crew members and 160 passengers onboard. During the approach the LE EDGE FLAP TRANSIT light illuminated as flaps were extended. The flight crew requested vectors from air traffic control (ATC) to allow them to run the appropriate quick reference handbook (QRH) checklists. The flight crew subsequently declared pan pan with ATC and configured the aircraft for landing. SWG423 landed without further incident into CYYZ runway 05 with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) vehicles standing by.                                                                                                               Maintenance found wire chaffing damage in a section covered with PRC sealant. A service difficulty report was filed with Transport Canada.

C-GUUL, a Boeing 737-8 aircraft operated by Lynx Air, was conducting flight DAT521 from Toronto/Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON, to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. On approach to CYHZ, the crew observed tire pressure indications for the nose wheel tires showing no tire pressures, and coordinated with ATS to have emergency vehicles stand by for the landing. The crew elected to conduct a missed approach due to cockpit configuration, and landed at CYHZ without incident on the second attempt. The nose tire pressures were found to be correct, and tire indications displayed correct tire pressures following the landing.

C-FFPH, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight TFL3042 from Antalya Airport (LTAI), Turkey to Rotterdam The Hague Airport (EHRD), Netherlands. While at FL360 the flight crew observed arcing on the R1 window which was followed by a Window Overheat Master Caution. The flight crew ran the Window Overheat checklist however a large crack developed across the window. The flight crew ran the Window Damage Forward checklist and requested a lower altitude. The window continued to crack so the flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC and diverted to Bucharest/Henri Coanda International Airport (LROP), Romania. Fire services met the aircraft on landing to conduct a brake inspection due to the overweight landing.

C-GVJR, an Eurocopter AS332L2 helicopter operated by Custom Helicopters, was conducting external long-line load operations from the Pipestone Valard Camp, ON to the Wapekeka Valard Camp, ON. While enroute, approximately 10 NM SSW of Big Trout Lake (CYTL), ON, the external load released from the helicopter. Chafed straps were observed hanging from the long line hook. The helicopter continued to the destination and landed uneventfully.

C-FBML, an amateur-built Superbear aircraft departed for a local flight from a private grass runway in Maynooth, Ontario with only the pilot onboard. The runway is approximately 1000 feet long and oriented in a north-south direction; the south end is approximately 60 feet higher in elevation than the north end. The aircraft flew locally for approximately an hour, during which the weather had reportedly changed, including strong gusty wind conditions. Family and friends attempted to contact the pilot without success, and subsequently initiated a search based on the pilot's cellular phone signal location. The aircraft was found in a forested area approximately 500 feet south of the runway, the pilot was fatally injured. On site examination indicated that the aircraft impacted large trees while flying in a southbound direction, beyond the south end of the runway, before contacting the ground and coming to a rest on its left side. Damage to the trees and propeller suggests that the engine was producing power at the time of impact; there were no pre-impact anomalies found with the flight control systems.The ELT (121.5 MHz) activated, but the signal strength was likely diminished due to the damaged antennae system. Weather forecasts and conditions obtained after the occurrence indicated a rapid temperature drop and moderate mechanical low-level wind shear turbulence at the approximate time and location of the occurrence. Although it was reported that the pilot had received some flight training, there were no records found to indicate he held an aviation document.

C-FRZK, a Rocking Star Adventures Ltd. Piper PA-18-150, was conducting VFR operations in support of a hunting camp in the Nisling River area of the Yukon. During a landing on a gravel bar on the Nisling River, the left wing contacted a stump and the aircraft veered left. During heavy braking the tail came up and the aircraft came to rest on its nose. The aircraft sustained damage to the left wing and propeller. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured.

C-FPCL, a Pilatus PC-12/45 operated by Timber Wolf Air as flight 1276, was conducting a flight from Thunder Bay (CYQT) ON. to Fort Hope (CYFH) ON. As C-FPCL was back tracking on Runway 25 at CYQT for departure and was turning around on the threshold, the crew heard a loud bang and felt the left-hand wing drop. The aircraft was disabled at the threshold, the crew shutdown the engine, and the 2 crew and 3 passengers exited the aircraft without injuries.The operator's maintenance was dispatched to the aircraft and found the lower trailing link on the left main landing gear had broken away from the upper gear leg at the axle pivot point. The aircraft was removed from the runway. The left main gear was replaced, gear swings were completed, the aircraft was inspected and returned to service. The operator indicated that a service difficulty report would be filed with TC.

C-GTSD, an Air Transat Airbus A330-300 was conducting flight TSC248 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Barcelona/El Prat Intl. (LEBL), Spain.  Approximately 215 nm SE of St-John's Intl. (CYYT), NL, a Cabin crew member became incapacitated.   Emergency positions and safety responsibilities were reassigned and flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GNSV, a Voyageur Airways De Havilland of Canada DHC-8-402 was conducting flight UNO517P from Bentui (HJBT), South Sudan to Malakal Intl. (HJMK), South Sudan.  During descent to HJMK,  “#2 HYD ISO VLV” caution light illuminated indicating low hydraulic quantity in the #2 system. The Flight crew actioned the appropriate QRH checklist and briefed the cabin crew in accordance with Standard Operating Procedures. The QRH directed the Flight Crew to use asymmetric braking and power to maintain directional control upon landing and to conduct an Alternate Landing Gear Extension. During landing roll and while decelerating through 80 kts the PIC became aware that braking was not effective. The PIC called for the SIC to assist.  Prior to the SIC assisting and while continuously applying toe brake pressure and asymmetric power the aircraft exited the right side of runway. The aircraft stopped with the left main wheel still on the runway and the nose and right main wheel in the soft clay soil. The engines were secured and Flight Crew communicated with the cabin crew and passengers. ATC and Emergency Services were advised and Passengers were escorted with no reported injuries. Damage to the aircraft is limited to nose landing gear doors. Maintenance is troubleshooting.

Le 23 septembre 2022, l'hydravion Wagaero Sportsman 2+2 (immatriculation C FFDA, numéro de série 792), avec à son bord le pilote et un passager, a décollé du lac Mylène, situé à 12 milles marins à l'ouest de l'aérodrome de Rivière-Bonard (CRB4) (Québec) pour effectuer un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR). Après 5 minutes en vol, à environ 4 milles marins au sud du lac Mylène, l'aile gauche de l'hydravion s'est détachée, s'en est suivi d'une descente non contrôlée avant de percuter le relief. Les 2 occupants ont été mortellement blessés. L'hydravion a été détruit par la force de l'impact. Aucun incendie ne s'est déclaré. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) de 406 mégahertz (MHz) s'est déclenchée et le système de recherche et sauvetage par satellite Cospas-Sarsat a capté le signal à 8 h 46.

C-GWLK, a WestJet Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight WS729 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC.  During cruise approximately 280 NM WNW of CYYZ, a flight crew member became incapacitated. Medical assistance was requested via sat phone and a deadheading flight crew member was able to take over the incapacitated flight crew's responsibilities. Flight crew elected to divert to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB where it landed without further incident.

C-GMWJ, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-700, was operating as flight WS8900 from and to Calgary International (CYYC), AB. WS8900 was on approach for Runway 17R. CYYC tower instructed WS8900 to overshoot due to a previous arrival still occupying the runway. WS8900 was instructed to fly runway heading to 7000 feet ASL. C-FCNW, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-800, was operating as flight WS1590 and had departed minutes earlier from CYYC Runway 17L. A loss of separation occurred when spacing between WS8900 and WS1590 reduced to 1.3 nm laterally and 900 feet vertically during the WS8900 overshoot.

C-GCMD, a Yellowhead Helicopters Limited Airbus Helicopters AS350-B2 (AStar) helicopter was conducting fire management operations with only the pilot on board. During drip torch operations, a weld failed on the suspended heli-torch and a piece of it and the associated fuel barrel fell into a previously burnt area. The equipment fell from a height of about 300 feet above ground. There were no injuries or damage to the helicopter.The fuel barrel and the part of the heli-torch were recovered.

C-FGWJ, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-700, was operating as flight WJA186 From Victoria International (CYYJ), BC to Calgary International (CYYC), AB. On approach into CYYC the flight crew received a flap position alert. The flight crew conducted an overshoot and then declared an emergency. The flight subsequently landed safely on Runway 17R.Following the flight, the maintenance team replaced the right-hand flap position transmitter and flap indicator.

C-FSAG, a privately registered Piper PA28-180, was operating from a dirt road approximately 64 nm NW of Ft. St. John (CYXJ), BC with the pilot and 3 passengers on board. During the take-off the aircraft collided with trees at a turn in the road. The pilot and passengers were able to extract themselves from the substantially damaged aircraft. The pilot sustained a serious injury and the front passenger a minor injury. The two rear seated passengers did not receive any injuries.

C-GJXE, an Air Canada A220-300 was conducting flight AC1097 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to San José/Juan Santamaria Intl. (MROC), Costa Rica.  Approximately 350 NM SW of Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL during cruise over the Gulf of Mexico, one flight crew became incapacitated. A Pan Pan was declared with ATC and decision has been made to divert to KMCO where the plane landed without further incident.

C-GLQX, a De Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines Inc., was conducting flight PD262 from Ottawa International Airport (CYOW), ON to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON with 4 crew and 30 passengers onboard. While climbing through 15000 feet, the flight crew observed excessive vibrations along with excessive engine internal temperature on the #2 engine. The pilots subsequently leveled the aircraft and reduced power on the #2 engine and observed that the vibration persisted with the interstage turbine Temperature (ITT) remaining excessive. The flight crew elected to shut the #2 engine down and declared Mayday with air traffic control (ATC). PD262 returned and landed in CYOW with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) standing by. After an initial inspection, the aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power. The engine #2 has been removed from the aircraft for further inspection by the engine manufacturer.

C-GWGX, a Pezetel PW-6U glider operated by the Winnipeg Gliding Club, was conducting a solo training flight at Starbuck (CKJ7), MB. Immediately upon touching down on landing in a wings level attitude, the pilot perceived a bounced landing and retracted the airbrakes. The nose of the glider dropped which resulted in an induced oscillation. On the third oscillation, the glider collided with the runway with a 20-30 degree nose down attitude. The glider sustained substantial damage to the nosewheel housing, lower fuselage skin, cockpit floor pan, and a cracked support bulkhead. The student pilot was uninjured.

C-GMZJ, a Cessna 188B operated by Accumark Aviation, was conducting a local flight from Nipawin (CYBU), SK. The aircraft landed safely at CYBU and was taxiing when the aircraft struck an unoccupied forklift on the taxiway. There was substantial damage to the aircraft and no injuries to the pilot.

At 1248, on 24 September 2022, a privately operated Quad City Ultralight Aircraft Corporation (Quad City) Challenger II advanced ultralight aircraft (registration C-IYDD, serial number CH2-0604-2481) departed a private grass runway near Yarker, Ontario, for a daytime visual flight rules flight to Westport/Rideau Lakes aerodrome (CRL2). The pilot was the sole person onboard.At approximately 1515, the aircraft was seen flying in a southerly direction near Bob’s Lake, east of Parham, Ontario. The aircraft engine was heard sputtering. The aircraft was then seen to slow and then drop vertically before turning over upside down. The engine lost power and the aircraft collided with terrain in a wooded area. The pilot was fatally injured, there was no post-impact fire but the aircraft was destroyed by impact forces. There was no emergency locator transmitter on board and none was required by regulations.At 1521, local residents called 911 to report the accident. At 1635, a Canadian Armed Forces CH146 Griffon helicopter located the aircraft and 2 Search and Rescue technicians were hoisted down from the helicopter to the accident site. Shortly after, local firefighters arrived and assisted with the recovery of the pilot.

C-FGZH, a Top Aces Inc. McDonnell Douglas A-4N was conducting tow target operations approximately 80 NM NW of Cuxhaven/ Nordholz-Spieka (ETMN), Germany.  During the gunnery exercise, pilot performed an intentional jettison of centerline mounted tow target reel system following procedure inside gunnery range operating area (North sea).  After landing, it was noticed that some of the system cable wrapped on the aircraft fuel vent mast and caused minor damage to the aircraft and to the runway lighting system.  Maintenance is assessing damage repair.

C-GTVO, a Boeing 737-219C operated by Chrono Jet Inc., was conducting flight MBK791 from Mary River (CMR2) NU. to IQALUIT (CYFB) NU. After departing CMR2 at approximately 11 000 feet, the flight crew received a warning indicating the #2 start valve was open. A visual check of the number 2 engine gauges indicated that the oil quantity reading was zero and the oil temp was 150 degrees. The QRH check list was completed and a precautionary shutdown of the number 2 engine was completed. The flight attendants were notified and the passengers were briefed for an abnormal landing. An operational decision was made to return to CMR2, a mayday call was made, and emergency services were placed on standby. A single engine overweight landing was performed and the aircraft landed safely on Runway 30 at CMR2.The operator's maintenance found the oil quantity gauge connector on the sending unit was broken. MEL 79-01 was applied and the connector was capped and stowed. The start valve and pressure switch were replaced. The aircraft was inspected for the overweight landing and was found serviceable.

C-FBCL, a London Air Services Limited Learjet Incorporated Learjet 45, was conducting a repositioning flight from Las Vegas (KLAS), Nevada, U.S., to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew members and 1 company maintenance engineer on board. When the flight crew lowered the aircraft's landing gear while on approach to CYVR, they received the warning message for NORMAL BRAKE FAIL. The flight crew discontinued the approach to assess the aircraft condition. The flight crew were unable to resolve the failure condition and subsequently requested aircraft rescue and fire fighting on standby for their arrival. The aircraft landed without further incident. Normal braking was available despite the warning message. Subsequent maintenance activities noted the auxiliary hydraulic pump pressure was higher than the normal operating range. The maintenance crew adjusted the hydraulic pressure, downloaded the computerized brake fault list for review by the manufacturer, and replaced the brake shuttle module and auxiliary hydraulic filters. The aircraft has since returned to service.

N638JM, an amateur-built non-aerobatic Arion Aircraft Lightning, was conducting a flight from Baudette International Airport (KBDE), USA to Roseau Municipal Airport/Rudy Billberg Field (KROX), USA on a VFR flight plan with a planned fly-by of a cottage located on Lake of the Woods, ON with only the pilot onboard. The aircraft conducted a low-level fly-by of the cottage and, once past the cottage, conducted a climbing 60° to 75° bank right turn. During the climbing steep turn, the left wing dropped and the aircraft descended rapidly in a nose-down attitude. The aircraft collided with terrain on an island located 15 NM south of Kenora (CYQK), ON. The pilot received fatal injuries. The aircraft was destroyed and there was no post-impact fire. A person who observed the accident reported it to emergency services. The OPP and the TSB deployed to the site.

On 19 Sep 2022, the Summit Air Ltd. British Aerospace Avro 145 Series RJ100 (registration C-FXRJ, serial number E3301) flight #SUT8042 departed the Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), Northwest Territories en route to Diavik Airport (CDK2), Northwest Territories. Onboard were 4 crew members and 60 passengers. While climbing through 15 000 feet above sea level (ASL), the flight crew felt a small bang that subsided. Moments later, another bang was felt and the #4 engine vibration indicator illuminated on the master warning system. The flight crew requested to stop the climb at 16 000 feet ASL. The flight crew carried out the checklist procedure for high engine vibration, and did a precautionary shutdown of the #4 engine, (Avco Lycoming LF 507-1F, serial number LF07393). At 1923, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and returned towards CYZF. At 1746, the aircraft landed on Runway 34 at CYZF without incident. There were no injuries.Company maintenance is investigating and the engine has been removed for examination.

C-FZQS, an Air Canada Airbus A320-200 was conducting flight AC724 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to New York/ LaGuardia Intl. (KLGA), NY. Approaching final approach fix runway 13 in KLGA at 1300 feet ASL, in a left hand bank, flight crew reported passing an unidentified object approximately 10 feet above Captain's window. Flight crew informed ATC but could not identify the object.  Flight landed in KLGA without further incident.

C-GARO, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319-114, was conducting flight ROU1764 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Santa Clara/Abel Santamaria (MUSC), Cuba. During cruise at FL340 approximately 150 nm east of Savannah/ Hilton Head Intl (KSAV), GA, flight suddenly and unexpectedly encountered a significant updraft and associated increase in turbulence intensity.  Flight crew was already operating in accordance with ATC reroute to avoid convective weather further west.  The updraft resulted in an uncommanded climb to FL347 over approximately 30 seconds.  Pilot flying assumed manual control with minimal inputs required, reported altitude deviation to ATC and returned to cleared altitude of FL340 with autopilot engaged.  Seatbelt sign was on the entire event with no injuries.  Flight landed at destination without further incident.  Maintenance inspection took place at MUSC with no fault found.

C-GUPK an Air Canada Airbus Canada Limited Partnership A220-300 was conducting flight AC732 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to LaGuardia Airport (KLGA), NY. During arrival in KLGA at 8000ft, traffic was climbing and initially got a Traffic Advisory (TA). The ATC advised the type aircraft and position but kept climbing at a low rate. AC732 then received a Resolution Advisory (RA) and only needed to climb less than 100ft to clear conflict. No further issues on arrival.

C-GZLU, a Cessna 172 operated by Airborne Energy Solutions, was conducting a pipeline inspection flight south of the town Shaunavon, Saskatchewan. The flight consisted of multiple legs to facilitate visual and electronic data collection of pipeline infrastructure, between Swift Current, Saskatchewan, and Estevan, Saskatchewan. At approximately 1015 Central Standard Time, approximately 6 nautical miles (NM) south-southwest of Shaunavon, the aircraft struck a 466-foot communications tower. A 4-foot section of the aircraft's right wing was shorn off. The aircraft then entered a steep descent and collided with the ground approximately 640 m southeast of the tower. A post-impact fire ensued, which consumed most of the wreckage. The 2 crew members were fatally injured. The aircraft was destroyed. TSB investigators deployed to the scene.

C-FGSJ, a Boeing 767-39H, operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd, was on a flight from Hamilton, ON (CYHM) to Halifax, NS (CYHZ) and was climbing through about 9000ft when there was a loud noise and vibration from the left engine. The flight crew leveled the aircraft at 10000 feet, declared a PAN PAN returned to CYHM, where the aircraft landed without further incident. A post flight maintenance inspection revealed damage to the LPT blades.

C-GOFI, a Bell 206L-1 helicopter operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd, was conducting a flight from Florence Lake, NL to Postville Airport (CYSO), NL.  During cruise, about 18nm west of CYSO, a PA31 Navajo aircraft (C-GPTB) flew directly under the helicopter at a 90-degree angle. The helicopter pilot was concerned with the close proximity of the PA31 aircraft and made a blind radio call on 126.70 MHz to advise that the traffic was in sight. No specific radio call was made from the PA31 aircraft. The helicopter was not equipped with TCAS and the transponder was deferred. Both aircraft continued without further incident.

C-FYCS, a privately registered Cessna A185E equipped with conventional landing gear, was conducting a flight from Springhouse Airpark (CAQ4), BC, to Williams Lake Airport (CYWL), BC, with 1 pilot onboard. During the touchdown on runway 30, the tailwheel began to shimmy and the pilot pushed the control column forward to lift the tailwheel off the ground. The shimmy stopped and the pilot pulled the control column back. The tailwheel touched the ground for the second time and the aircraft immediately entered a ground loop to the right. The left wheel and tailwheel broke free of the aircraft and the left wingtip contacted the runway. The aircraft came to a stop facing the opposite direction on the runway. The pilot shutdown the engine, exited the aircraft, and contacted the CYWL flight service station to request assistance. The pilot was uninjured, but the aircraft was substantially damaged. The airport issued a NOTAM to close the runway. The airport authority assisted the pilot in moving the aircraft from the runway to the apron in front of a private hangar located at the airport. The runway was re-opened approximately 2.5 hours after the occurrence.

C-GUBT, an Air Transat Airbus A330-200 was conducting flight TSC426 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Cancun Intl (MMUN), Mexico.  During the approach, a flight attendant became incapacitated.  Flight landed without further incident.

C-FSDB, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 aircraft operating as flight ACA555, was conducting a flight from Los Angeles International (KLAX), CA, to Vancouver International (CYVR), B.C, with 4 crew members and 152 passengers onboard. While vectoring for approach into CYVR, the crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) due to a privately registered Cessna 172S C-GZAA climbing VFR to 2400 feet in Class C terminal airspace. The crew responded to the RA and the aircraft landed without further incident. The minimum separation was 0.2 NM horizontally and 900 feet vertically. There were no reported injuries and no damage to either aircraft.

N898MJ, a Bombardier Global Express aircraft operated by Executive Jet Management, was conducting flight EJM898 from Teterboro, NJ (KTEB) to RAF Northolt, England (EGWU). During cruise, the crew received "R Oil Low QTY" amber message. The crew elected to divert and declared an emergency with ATC. During the descent, the amber message went away and the aircraft landed in Gander, NL (CYQX) without further incident.Shortly after shutdown, the flight crew added 4 quarts of oil to the right engine in accordance with the Cockpit Servicing Procedures. Maintenance personnel performed ground runs and no leaks were detected. The aircraft was found to be serviceable and was returned to service.

C-FJZD, a Jazz Aviation LP Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900), was operating as JZA392 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Calgary (CYYC), AB.  C-FLJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900), was operating as JZA243 from Regina (CYQR), SK to CYYC. Both aircraft were on approach into CYYC. JZA243 was instructed to descend and intercept final for Runway 35R. JZA243 was unable to descend as quickly as the controller anticipated due to VFR traffic in uncontrolled airspace. This resulted in a loss of separation with JZA392. Separation was reduced to 2.9 NM and 700 feet where 1000 feet or 3 miles is required. JZA243 was vectored away from traffic and re-sequenced onto the approach for Runway 35R. Both aircraft landed safely and there was no further impact to operations.

C-FYSA, un Piper PA-44 exploité par Richcopter Inc. et C-GNZK, un Beech 19 en exploitation privée, effectuaient des circuits selon les règles de vol à vue à l'aéroport de Gatineau, Qc (CYND). Alors que C-GNZK virait en vent de travers lors de sa montée initiale, il y a eu un risque de collision avec C-FYSA lorsque C-GNZK est passé devant C-FYSA qui était déjà dans le circuit. Les 2 pilotes n'ont pu établir de contact visuel. Le Spécialiste de l'information de vol a demandé à C-GNZK d'arrêter sa montée pour éviter la collision. Les 2 appareils se sont retrouvés à environ 100 pieds l'un de l'autre et ont pu atterrir sans encombre à CYND

C-GAJU, a Boeing 757-200 operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd. as flight CJT571, was enroute from Hamilton (CYHM), ON to the Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB with a crew of 2 on board. While climbing through 8000’ feet ASL at CYHM, the left engine's (Rolls Royce RB211-535E4) EGT spiked to 911 degrees momentarily and the auto-throttle disengaged. After coordinating with the operator's maintenance control centre, it was decided to continue the flight to CYWG. While on descent into CYWG at 10,000 feet ASL, the left engine became unresponsive and, after running the appropriate checklist, the EGT would spike each time power was applied. The crew decided to shut down the left engine and then declared a Pan Pan. The crew then completed an uneventful single engine landing. The operator is currently troubleshooting the left engine.

C-GGWX, un Boeing 737-408 exploité par Les Investissements Nolinor Inc sous l’indicatif d’appel NRL664 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de de Bagotville, Québec (CYBG) à destination de l’aéroport de Wabush, NL (CYWK). Lors de l'amorce de descente vers la destination, l'équipage a noté une perte de pressurisation et déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN). Le contrôle de la pressurisation a été rétabli quand le système a été transféré en mode manuel en effectuant la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH). L'urgence a alors été annulée et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. L'appareil n'a subi aucun dommage et il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FIFJ, a De Havilland DHC-2 MK1 aircraft operated by Transwest Air Limited, was enroute from the La Ronge water aerodrome (CJZ9), SK, to Southend (CKA9), SK, with only the pilot onboard. While in cruise, the pilot noticed irregular fuel pressure indications and then consulted with the company's maintenance control center. The pilot then decided to return to La Ronge/Barber Field (CYVC) SK. During final approach into CYVC, all fuel pressure was lost and the engine (Pratt & Whitney R985) lost power. The pilot declared a Pan Pan and then completed a successful forced landing. After troubleshooting the system, it was realized that the rear fuel tank was empty. The fuel tank was switched and the engine was then restarted successfully.

C-GUPL, an Air Canada A220-300 was conducting flight AC568 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to San Francisco Intl (KSFO), CA.  During the approach runway 28R in KSFO, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) due to Southwest Airlines B737 300 feet away.  Flight crew levelled off at 2000 feet and initiated a missed approach.  Flight was vectored back to runway 28L where it landed without further incident.

C-FJIS un Cessna 120X en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Charlevoix, Qc (CYML) à destination d'un terrain privé situé à St-Ambroise, Qc avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Lors de la course au décollage, l'appareil s'est incliné vers la gauche au moment où les roues ont quitté le sol. L'aile gauche a touché le sol et l'appareil est sorti du côté gauche de la piste 15. L'appareil a été lourdement endommagé et le pilote a subi des coupures mineures.

C-FZAA, a Helijet International Incorporated Sikorsky S-76A helicopter was operating as flight JBA908 from Nanaimo Harbour Heliport (CDH5), BC, to Vancouver Harbour Heliport (CBC7), BC, with 2 flight crew and 11 passengers onboard. Prior to the flight’s departure, 2 float planes broadcast flight intentions on the aerodrome traffic frequency for the Nanaimo Harbour water aerodrome which is the same frequency used for the 4 Nanaimo heliports. The helicopter departed on an east-northeast heading and advised traffic they would be climbing to 500 feet. The crew made visual and radio contact with 1 float plane which was to their north with no traffic conflict. The crew spotted the second float plane approaching from the 11 o'clock position at approximately the same altitude with a separation of approximately 0.25 nautical miles. The crew performed an evasive manoeuvre to the right and the flight was completed without further incident. There was no radio contact made with the second float plane.   The crew and passengers were debriefed immediately following the flight.

C-FPQQ, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by Keewatin Air as flight KEW213, was on a local maintenance test flight out of the Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB with a crew of 2 and 1 passenger on board. After selecting the landing gear lever down, the landing gear would not extend. The crew referred to the aircraft checklist and was able to extend the landing gear successfully using the manual gear extension. The crew declared an emergency and then landed the aircraft safely. An inspection of the landing gear system by the operator's maintenance personal revealed an unserviceable landing gear hydraulic power pack/motor assembly. The hydraulic power pack/motor assembly was replaced and, after a successful gear swing and a test flight, the aircraft was returned to service. The hydraulic power pack/motor assembly was newly installed prior to the first test flight. The operator has submitted a Service Difficulty Report with Transport Canada.

C-FJVL, an Arty's Air Service Ltd. Air Tractor AT-502B, was conducting agricultural application operations 18 NM S of Bawlf (CFR2), AB with 1 pilot on board. After completing spray operations on the field, the aircraft collided with terrain; the pilot was fatally injured. There was no post-impact fire, and the ELT did transmit. The Edmonton TSB office deployed 2 investigators to the accident site.

C-FVYW, un Piper PA-31 exploité par Exact Air sous l'indicatif ET870 effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à destination de l’aéroport de Montréal St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Au moment de réduire la puissance lors de la mise en palier, le moteur de gauche a subi une perte de puissance. Le pilote a déclaré une urgence. Lors de la procédure de vérification, la puissance du moteur a été rétablie. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre avec les 2 moteurs en fonction. La pompe de carburant et le moteur du contrôleur de carburant ont été remplacés par précaution.

N524TA, an Airbus A319-132 aircraft operated by Avianca, was conducting flight LRC627 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to El Salvador International Airport (MSLP), El Salvador. N1D, a Gulfstream G4 aircraft operated by Private FLITE, was conducting a flight from CYYZ to Teterboro Airport (KTEB), USA. Shortly after take off from runway 23, N1D overtook flight LRC627 to a minimum spacing of 1.7 Nautical miles lateral and 200 feet vertical. Air Traffic Control (ATC) turned N1D south to regain separation. Both flights continued to their destination.

C-GVEN, a DHC8-402 aircraft operated by Westjet Encore Ltd, was conducting flight WEN3471 from Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While climbing, the flight crew noted the ''RH MLG'' red and amber advisory lights not extinguishing after selecting the landing gear up. After completing the non-normal quick reference checklist associated with the condition, the crew elected to return to CYOW and declared emergency (Pan Pan) with air traffic control. The crew conducted an alternate landing gear extension for an uneventful landing into CYOW runway 07.  Maintenance Personnel were able to duplicate the fault while the aircraft was on jacks. It was observed that the gear would retract but not enter the up-lock. A complete rigging of the right main landing gear retraction actuator rod end was carried out and the aircraft subsequently returned to service.

C-FFIN a Cessna 152, operated by Lachute Aviation (6800009 Canada Inc.), was landing on runway 25 at the Alexandria Aerodrome (CNS4), ON. During the approach, the speed was reported to be higher than anticipated, and the aircraft touched down with about 2/3 of the runway remaining. The pilot initiated a go-around, however, before becoming airborne the go-around was rejected. The aircraft went off the end of the runway and struck an embankment located about 120 feet from the runway end. The aircraft came to rest on its nose; there were no injuries.

C-FHSP, a privately registered Beech B300C (Super King Air 350C) airplane, was operating from Victoria Int'l (CYYJ), BC, to Penticton (CYYF), BC, with 2 pilots and 6 passengers on board. During the climb through flight level (FL) 180, the flight crew noticed the right oil pressure indication was red and showing zero. Air traffic control was notified and the flight crew requested to level off at FL190. The flight crew discussed the situation, consulted the QRH, declared an emergency, and requested a return to CYYJ. While en route to CYYJ, the flight crew noticed that the right oil pressure circuit breaker had popped. They did not reset the breaker and landed safety in Victoria. Maintenance personnel inspected the engine and found no fault. The right oil pressure circuit breaker was reset and engine runs were performed. The aircraft was returned to service.

The 41-9 Aerial Ltd Robinson R44II, C-GGJS (S/N 12254), was carrying out spray operations on a canola field 18NM north of Boyle (CFM7), AB when on the last tank of the day, during one of the final passes, the helicopter came in contact with the canola crop. Control was lost and the helicopter tumbled forward, coming to rest inverted in the crop. The pilot was uninjured and was able to extract self from the wreckage. The helicopter was substantially damaged. There was no fire. The ELT did not activate.

C-GWEN, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited DHC-8-402 (DASH 8 Q400), was operating as flight WEN3335 from Calgary Int'l (CYYC), AB, to Comox (CYQQ), BC, with 4 crew members and 65 passengers. During the flight, a cabin crew member experienced a medical event and was unable to continue performing their duties. The flight crew was made aware of the situation and no emergency was declared.

C-FIVS, an Air Canada Boeing 777-300 was conducting flight AC801 from Dublin Intl. (EIDW), Ireland to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. During initial climb, flight crew was cleared to FL110 with another traffic cleared above them at FL120.  During level off, flight climbed to FL113 and received a TCAS TA (Traffic Advisory) while corrective actions were in progress.  Subsequently, a TCAS RA (Resolution advisory) to return to FL110 was issued which the flight crew complied with.  ATC also issued a transmission for the flight crew to return to the cleared altitude.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GWJK, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited DHC-8-402 (DASH 8 Q400), was operating as flight WEN3108 from Terrace (CYXT), BC, to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR) BC, with 5 crew members and 29 passengers. After boarding in CYXT, a cabin crew member experienced a medical event and was unable to continue performing their duties for the remainder of the flight to CYVR. The company was informed of the situation and no emergency was declared.

C-FEKS, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU, operating as Jazz Aviation LP flight JZA890, on a flight from George Bush Intercontinental Houston Airport, TX (KIAH) to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport, ON (CYYZ) declared an emergency due to a possible blown nose gear tire on departure. The flight crew of the aircraft elected to continue towards Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport, ON (CYYZ). The aircraft landed safely in Toronto. A post flight inspection revealed the tire was not blown.

C-GORN, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Propair Inc, was conducting flight PRO 4001 from Wabush Airport (CYWK), NL to Chibougamau Airport (CYMT), QC. Shortly after departure, Wabush FSS advised the crew that the ramp attendants had seen fluid or fuel leaking from the wing. The crew advised Montreal ACC that they wanted to return to CYWK and declared a PAN-PAN, with a request for ARFF to be placed on standby. The flight landed without further incident. Company maintenance is in the process of inspecting the aircraft.

N307FE, a Federal Express McDonnell Douglas DC-10-30F, was conducting cargo flight FDX140 from Memphis, Tennessee, USA (KMEM) to Calgary, Alberta (CYYC). During the cruise portion of the flight, the exhaust gas temperature for the #3 engine (General Electric CF6-50 series) increased to 1054° F, which resulted in an engine exceedance alert to the flight crew.  The flight crew reduced the throttle for the #3 engine and proceeded to execute the appropriate procedure in the QRH check list. As the aircraft descended into the greater CYYC area, the flight crew notified ATC that they were experiencing the #3 engine issue, and declared an emergency. An uneventful 2 engine landing was completed.Subsequent investigation by company maintenance found a loose EGT connector for the #3 engine.

C-GHTE, a Hiller UH-12E operated by Western Aerial Applications Ltd. departed Winnipeg/City of Winnipeg Heliport (CWG2), MB to the southwest of CWG2 to conduct local mosquito control work by applying biological control pellets. During this process, the pilot heard a loud bang and felt a vibration coming from the engine (AVCO Lycoming VO-540-C2A). The pilot noticed the engine was still producing power and carried out a precautionary landing. The operator's maintenance could not find an obvious cause for the vibration and a decision was made to place the helicopter onto a trailer for transport to the company's main base for further inspection.

Un Drone ARA-TR-RPAS en exploitation par ARA Robotique, effectuait un vol de configuration des paramètres du contrôleur d'attitude de l'autopilote depuis l’aéroport Alma, QC (CYTF). Lors de manœuvres à une hauteur d’environ 3 mètres au-dessus du sol, le drone est devenu incontrôlable, un atterrissage d’urgence a été effectué et l’appareil a subi des dommages importants. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage au sol.

C-FNXP, an amateur built Pegazair100 was landing on runway 24 at Guelph Airport, Ontario (CNC4). The aircraft touched down on the grass prior to the start of the runway and flipped over. The occupants were not inured, however the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FTXQ, un Airbus 321-211 exploité par Air Transat sous l'indicatif TSC893, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Gregorio Luperón Intl, Puerto Plata en République dominicaine (MDPP) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Alors que l’avion était établi à environ 9 miles marins en approche finale de la piste 06R, une perte d’espacement est survenue lorsque N842UP, un Beechcraft 350 exploité par Gama Aviation LLC sous l'indicatif GAJ842 qui était sur un guidage radar pour intercepter l’approche finale 06R, s’est retrouvé 2,6 miles marins derrière TSC893 à environ la même altitude. L’espacement requis était de 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical et 3 nm sur le plan horizontal.

C-FCGF, a Cessna 560 XL, operated by Chartright Air Inc, departed Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON when shortly after after take off, the flight crew received a R Bleed Overheat caution light. The climb was continued to 6000 feet and the flight crew then leveled off and reduced thrust on the affected side; the warning light extinguished once power was reduced. The aircraft returned to Toronto and landed without further incident. Upon shutdown maintenance staff inspected the aircraft and noticed smoke and a small flame inside the starboard service bay.
