The flame was extinguished with a portable fire extinguisher. Further inspection revealed that the bleed air line had become detached at a joint that is normally kept secure by a clamp.

C-GRSP, a Piper PA-25-235 operated by Miccar Aerial Ltd. departed Yorkton Muni (CYQV), SK. to conduct aerial application 7 nm miles south of CYQV. During the aerial application flight, approximately 1 hour 35 minutes after departure, the engine (AVCO Lycoming 0-540-B2C5) lost all power. While conducting a forced landing, the aircraft speed reduced and the aircraft entered a stall at a low altitude. The aircraft impacted the ground and sustained substantial damage. The pilot was not injured.An inspection of the aircraft by the operator determined that both fuel tanks were empty. There were no signs of fuel leaks.

The Jazz Aviation LP, Bombardier Dash 8-402 aircraft (flight 7711, C-GUJZ) was climbing to altitude when the captain (PF) noticed a stiffness in the aileron control system. The captain transferred control to the first officer who also felt the control stiffness. The aircraft was levelled off and the crew requested to return to Ottawa International airport (CYOW). The crew actioned the QRH procedures for ROLL JAM and ROLL CONTROL MALFUNCTION. There were no QRH procedures for aileron stiffness. The crew decided to activate the "PULL ROLL DISCONNECT" which identified the stiffness on the first officer's side. Since no control jam existed they reconnected the "PULL ROLL DISCONNECT" lever. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed uneventfully on Runway 07 with ARFF standing by. Maintenance completed a full inspection of the aileron control system including cable tension measurements, and after lubricating the right hand aileron hinges found the system to be operating normally.

C-FKWE, a Dehavilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore Ltd, was conducting flight WEN3419 from Moncton Romeo LeBlanc International Airport (CYQM), NB to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Shortly after departure, 25nm W of CYQM, the oil pressure indication on the No.2 engine started fluctuating. The crew actioned the checklist and feathered the No. 2 engine after discussion with dispatch and MCC.  The crew requested a diversion to Halifax Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. The aircraft entered a hold to burn fuel and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance found the No.2 oil quantity low, added 14 quarts of oil, and continues to investigate the cause of the loss of oil.

C-GLMX, a privately registered Bell 206L-1 (LongRanger II) helicopter, was preparing for a flight from Little Parker Island (CBK9), BC, to the Villa Eyrie Resort on Vancouver Island, BC, with 1 pilot and 3 passengers on board. A pre-flight walkaround was conducted and the main rotor blade tie-down was released from the marine cleat located on the helipad. The pilot and passengers boarded the helicopter and the pilot proceeded with a normal engine start. As the engine speed increased to 60% for the gas generator (N1) and the main rotor blades accelerated, a main rotor blade departed the helicopter near the blade root and the pilot immediately shut down the engine. The rotor blade was recovered with the tie-down strap attached to the tip of the blade. The main rotor continued rotating with 1 intact rotor blade attached and the imbalance violently rocked the helicopter off the helipad and over the adjacent embankment. The helicopter came to rest on the shoreline on its right side, partially submerged in shallow water. The front left passenger was ejected from the helicopter beside the helipad while the 3 remaining occupants were retained in their seats and able to egress through the left doors of the helicopter once all motion stopped. The pilot and the front left passenger were seriously injured and airlifted to hospital. The rear 2 passengers were not injured. The 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter (ELT) was activated during the occurrence and the signal was received by the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre. The aircraft was substantially damaged.The helicopter was recovered and taken to the owner’s hangar where the damage will be assessed.

C-GRGQ, a Bell 212 HP helicopter operated by Coldstream Helicopters Ltd. was conducting aerial work from Deer Lake (CYVZ) ON. to a power line right-of-way, located approximately 20 nm southwest of CYVZ. While C-GRGQ was en-route to the destination, the longline and load experienced an uncommanded release. The helicopter returned to CYVZ.The operator's maintenance subsequently found the top of the belly hook and the manual release cable had significant dust and debris that prevented the hook from being properly seated when in the closed position. A functional test produced a complete failure of the manual release cable at the attachment point. The aircraft was removed from service, a new manual release cable was installed and the aircraft was returned to service. A service difficulty report (SDR) was submitted to Transport Canada.

C-GHSC, a Bell 206B operated by Expedition Helicopters Inc. was conducting low-level agricultural aerial application approximately 11 nm north of Turtleford, SK. The pilot was spraying a field east to west. As the helicopter approached the end of the field, the helicopter struck an electric wire. The wire made contact with the helicopter's wire strike protection kit's upper cutter and the wire was severed. The pilot flared the helicopter and made a power on landing and shutdown. There was no damage to the helicopter and no injuries to the pilot. SaskPower was notified and the wire was repaired. The aircraft is grounded until inspected by the operator's maintenance.

C-GYDQ, a Beech 200 operated by Transwest Air Limited Partners (dba as Rise Air) was conducting a flight from Stony Rapids (CYSF) SK. to La Ronge (Barber Field) (CYVC) SK. with 2 crews and no passengers. After starting the right engine, the flight crew noticed the electrical load remained high; however, it did return to normal limits. The left engine start was normal. The flight crew then turned on the electrical and avionics systems. Sometime after connecting these aircraft systems, the crew could smell electrical smoke. The aircraft was shutdown and the crew deplaned; noticing smoke in the cabin area. Hangar staff at CYSF were alerted and ground crews provided fire protection. There was no visible fire. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and found the flap motor was the cause of the smoke. The flap circuit breaker did not pop.

C-GCQS un hélicoptère Bell 429 opéré par Transport Canada pour la Garde Cötière du Canada sous l'indicatif CTG444, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Puvirnituq, Nunavik (CYPX) avec un pilote à bord et deux membres d'équipage au sol. L'appareil était en approche pour effectuer du travail d'élingage à environs 2 miles marins au sud-sud-ouest de l'aéroport CYPX. Alors qu'il était quasi stationnaire au-dessus de la charge à accrocher, le pilote a perdu l'autorité des commandes en lacet et a effectué un atterrissage d'urgence. L'appareil s'est renversé sur la surface inégale du terrain et s'est immobilisé sur le côté. Aucun blessé.UPDATED 11 September 2025

C-GPTS, an Airbus A330-243 aircraft operated by Air Transat Inc, was conducting flight TSC690 from Montreal Pierre Elliot Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Athens International Airport (LGAV), Greece. During the cruise portion 175 nm E-SE of Goose Bay International Airport (CYYR), NL, a cabin crew member became incapacitated due to a minor injury. All safety related duties where reassigned and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GATY, an Air Tindi Ltd. Cessna 208 Caravan, was conducting flight TIN403 from Aylmer Lake, NT to the Yellowknife, NT float base (CEN9) with 1 pilot and 6 passengers on board. Shortly after departure from Aylmer Lake, the pilot noticed and smelled smoke in the cockpit that appeared to be coming from aircrafts avionics system. The pilot elected to return to Aylmer Lake, and conducted an uneventful landing. Subsequent investigation by company maintenance determined that the GPS radio was the source of the smoke. The GPS was replaced with a serviceable unit, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GZGK, a Bell 205A-1 operated by Guardian Helicopters Inc., was conducting a flight from La Ronge (CJX3) SK. to the north end of Lake Besnard SK. to drop off a forest firefighting crew. C-GZGK landed at Pad 9, located on the shore of Lake Besnard. The fire crew departed the running helicopter and were positioned at the 11 o'clock and 2 o'clock positions. Prior to departure, the doors were closed and secured, basket was closed, and pre-takeoff checks were completed. The pilot lifted the helicopter up into hover flight and started to slowly back the helicopter away from Pad 9. The helicopter tail rotor struck the water as the helicopter was backing up. A loud bang was heard coming from the rear of the helicopter followed by a nose pitch-up, an increase in the sound of the engine and main rotor rpm, and the helicopter started to spin to the right. The pilot closed the throttle and performed the procedure for a tail rotor failure. The helicopter landed upright close to the shore near Pad 9. The pilot shutdown the helicopter and exited. There were no injuries. The ELT did not activate.

C-GNWV a Cessna 208B operated by Northway Aviation Ltd., was conducting flight NAV831 from Poplar River (CZNG) MB. to Winnipeg/St. Andrews (CYAV) MB. At approximately 10nm north of CYAV, the pilot noticed the presence and odor of smoke coming from the pilot's side pedestal. The pilot carried out memory items for a cabin fire, declared an emergency, and continued to CYAV. During the approach to CYAV, the pilot noticed the smoke was dissipating. C-GNWV landed safely. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and found the air conditioning compressor belt had seized and broke; which was the source of the smoke.

The Jazz Aviation LP DASH-8-400 aircraft (C-GGMZ, 8259) was at 8000 feet ASL and beginning the descent to London International airport, Ontario (CYXU) when the #1 engine briefly lost 30% torque, RPM followed by a momentary flashing of a caution light. The flight crew requested that ATC allowed the aircraft to maintain their current altitude. While communicating with ATC the same event occurred with the #1 engine. This similar event occurred six times and the crew decided to shutdown the engine. The flight crew followed the QRH procedures, decided to divert to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed uneventfully on Runway 15L with ARFF standing by. After a ground inspection the aircraft was allowed to taxi to the gate. Maintenance replaced the #1 Propeller Electronic Control Unit and the #1 quadrant condition lever. The aircraft was returned to service.

The Air Canada Rouge Airbus A320-214 (C-GFWX) was on climb out from Fredericton, New Brunswick (CYFC) when the flight crew heard an abnormal noise from the mid-center of the cabin. This was immediately followed by a HYD OVERHEAT and GREEN HYD LO LVL ECAM messages. The crew followed the ECAM procedures and declared a PAN PAN. Upon arrival in CYYZ the crew manually lowered the landing gear and subsequently the aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The aircraft came to a stop on the runway and after ARFF inspection was towed to the gate due to unavailable nosewheel steering. Maintenance found a hydraulic leak in the system and a faulty PTU. After the leak was repaired and the PTU replaced the aircraft returned to service.

C-GHKC, an Airbus 330-343 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA894 from Montréal/Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Milan/Malpensa Intl (LIMC), Italy. When about 30 nm northeast of Goose Bay (CYYR), NL, the flight crew received a green hydraulics system low level message. The flight crew selected the green hydraulics pump off, declared a PAN PAN, and coordinated a diversion to return to CYUL. On approach to CYUL, the crew turned on green hydraulic system pump and selected the landing gear to the down position. The aircraft landed within landing weight limits on runway 24R at CYUL without incident. The aircraft shut down on the runway and was inspected by airport emergency responders. Due to nose wheel steering not being available, the crew requested a tow to the terminal. There were no injuries.Company maintenance personnel repaired a hydraulic leak at number 2 engine pulsation damper.

C-FIVQ, an Air Canada Boeing 777-300 was conducting flight AC105 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC.  Approximately 91 NM ESE from Thunder bay airport (CYQT), ON, Flight crew suspected a fuel leak.  After discussion with maintenance control, flight crew declared a PAN PAN, diverted back to CYYZ and jettison fuel at FL190 to avoid overweight landing. Flight crew completed QRH checklist to reduce tank imbalance (4000kg left wing low) and landed in CYYZ without further incident.Maintenance proceeded with fuel quantity processing unit (FQPU) replacement and completed checks and ground runs at 80% N1 (same fuel flow) for 30 min with cross bleed closed with no fault found.  Maintenance found that with cross bleed opened fuel transferred slowly to right hand side.   More troubleshooting is ongoing.

C-GEKZ an Air Canada B737-8 on route from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to San Diego International Airport (KSAN), CA when the crew requested vectors to deviate around some weather near Flagstaff Pulliam Airport (KFLG), AZ. Halfway through the turn, SkyWest was given vectors but also responded with deviations for weather. The controller gave vectors for a turn 30 degrees to the right (crew were in a 30 degree turn to the left). Still in the process of rolling out level to turn to the right, the crew received a TCAS TA and shortly after the controller told them to turn a further 15 degrees to the right. Immediately following that, the crew received a TCAS RA to descend. After descending around 1000 feet, received the CLEAR OF CONFLICT aural and started climbing back up to FL340.

C-GJVT an Air Canada A320-200 conducting flight AC585 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB was climbing through 7000ft on departure when the crew received a TCAS RA and descended 600ft to clear the alert. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

The Air Transat Airbus A321-211, C-GEZN, was operating as flight TSC865 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Toronto (CYYZ), ON. Shortly after take-off, the flight crew observed the ENG 1 EGT OVER LIMIT and ENG 2 EGT OVER LIMIT indications on the electronic centralized aircraft monitor (ECAM). The flight crew initiated a thrust reduction, and only the ENG 2 EGT OVER LIMIT warning remained. The crew elected to run engine #2 (CFM International CFM56-5B3/3) at idle power. A PAN PAN was declared and TSC865 returned to CYYC. An uneventful overweight landing was conducted and the aircraft came to a stop on the runway. ARFF met the aircraft and conducted an inspection before the aircraft taxied back to the gate. Company maintenance performed troubleshooting and visual inspections of both engines. Engine 1 was found to be serviceable. Engine 2 required a borescope internal inspection.

The Keewatin Air Beech 200, C-GYSR, was operating as flight KEW208-M from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Kugluktuk (CYCO), NU. On departure from CYZF the crew was unable to retract the landing gear, as the gear selector handle was restricted to half travel. The selector handle red GEAR UNSAFE light illuminated and the landing gear circuit breaker popped. The flight crew made 2 attempts to lower the landing gear; however, they were unable to get a left main landing gear green safe light. The flight crew actioned the QRH and manually lowered the landing gear. While holding, company operations were contacted via satellite phone and the decision was made for the aircraft to return. The flight crew declared an emergency and returned to CYZF. The aircraft landed without further issue and stopped on the runway. Company maintenance met the aircraft and confirmed the landing gear was down and locked before towing the aircraft back to the hangar. Company maintenance found the down lock latch on the landing gear selector handle was not disengaging in air mode. The right main gear safety switch was replaced.

C-FFAL, un Boeing 737-2R8C exploité par Glencore Canada Corporation sous l'indicatif RAG100, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) avec 35 passagers et 4 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de la rotation durant le décollage, l’équipage de conduite a entendu un bruit de détonation venant du côté gauche de l’aéronef suivi d’une odeur de caoutchouc. Un passager a observé de petites flammes sortant du moteur #1. L’équipage a suspecté une défaillance des pneus du train d’atterrissage gauche et a suivi la liste de vérification d’urgence (QRH). Le vol s’est poursuivi vers CYUL avec le train d’atterrissage sorti. L’équipage a contacté la station de service en vol (FSS) de CYUY pour aviser de possible débris sur la piste. Une fois en communication avec l’ACC de Montréal, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) et a rapporté avoir possiblement subi une ou deux crevaisons. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 24 droite à 22 :20z. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage. Le moteur #1 a été éteint et inspecté sur la voie de circulation et aucun dommage n’a été observé. Après vérification, il a été trouvé qu’un impact aviaire a eu lieu à CYUY.

C-FEJY, un Embraer 170-200SU exploité Jazz Aviation LP sous l’indicatif JZA994 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Dallas-Fort Worth Intl, TX (KDFW), à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). C-GAWP, un Pilatus PC12/45 exploité par Airmedic Inc. sous l’indicatif AM87 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT), à destination de CYUL. À 10nm au sud-ouest de CYUL, l'espacement minimal requis de 3 milles marins horizontalement n’a pu être maintenu alors qu’AM87 a été guidé à 2.4NM derrière JZA994 avec 200 pieds d'espacement vertical. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FUSM, a Boeing 737-8CT operated by WestJet Airlines Ltd, was conducting flight WJA9536 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Regina (CYQR), SK. During the approach for landing at CYQR, the flaps stopped at position 15 and would not select higher when commanded. The pilots conducted missed approach to troubleshoot the situation. After evaluating the situation and conducting the abnormal checklist, the pilots declared an emergency and elected to land with flap 15. The airplane landed safely without further incident. The operator's maintenance discovered a fault with the trailing edge flap sensor associated with the flap drive system on the right hand wing. It was repaired and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOKN, a de Havilland DHC-8-102 operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG8161 from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON to Muskrat Dam (CZMD), ON. During the taxi on the ramp after landing at CZMD, the aircraft's left wing tip came into to contact with a de-ice ladder. The aircraft received minor damage to the left hand aileron.The operator's maintenance replaced the left aileron and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FHGG, un Beech 100 (BE10) exploité Propair Inc. sous l’indicatif PRO4250, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Val-d'Or, QC (CYVO), à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). C-GOIS un Airbus A321-271 exploité par Air Transat A.T. inc. sous l’indicatif TSC399, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Punta Cana, République Dominicaine (MDPC), à destination de CYUL. À 10nm au sud-ouest de CYUL, l'espacement minimal requis de 3 milles marins horizontalement n’a pu être maintenu alors que PRO4250 a été guidé à 2.0NM derrière TSC399 avec 300 pieds d'espacement vertical. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FCRF, an Air Tractor AT-502B operated by Prairie Sky Crop Solutions, was conducting an aerial application flight near Niverville, MB. While applying pesticide on a crop, the aircraft's propeller blade and tail fin came into contact with a powerline. The pilot carried out a low-level recovery, jettison the remaining pesticide load and returned to Niverville, MB where the aircraft landed safely. The pilot was not injured and the aircraft sustained damage. Part of the tail fin and rudder remained lodged in the powerline until it was removed by Manitoba Hydro.The operator reported that the propeller blade, tail fin and tail rudder was to be repaired prior to returning the aircraft to service.

C-GUFR, un Airbus A330-243 exploité par Air Transat A.T. inc. sous l’indicatif TSC244, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ) à destination de Glasgow, Royaume-Uni (EGPF), avec 297 passagers et 11 membres d'équipages à bord. À environ 40 NM au nord-est de l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL), l’équipage a demandé un déroutement vers CYUL en raison d’une incapacité d’un membre d’équipage de conduite. Aucune urgence n’a été déclarée. TSC244 s’est posé à CYUL sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage.

C-GEWR, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-400 was conducting flight WEN3603 between Boston/ General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl (KBOS), MA and Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  At the gate after closing main aircraft door, cabin crew heard lavatory alarm going off and heavy smoke coming from lavatory.  Cabin crew closed the lavatory door, flight crew contacted emergency services and proceeded with a rapid deplanement through forward main cabin door to the jet bridge gate A1.  Passengers were held onto the jet bridge for a period of time before transferring to the terminal.  It was later found that a passenger had vaped in the lavatory before proceeding to his seat.  Aircraft was inspected and subsequently cleared for flight.

The Rouge Airlines Airbus A320-211 aircraft (C-FJQD) was on approach to CYYZ at an altitude of 6800 feet ASL when the crew received a SLAT FAULT ECAM message. The crew declared a PAN PAN and the flight entered a holding pattern while the crew actioned the ECAM actions. The fault remained and the crew followed QRH procedures and performed a slat 0, Flap 3 approach. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. Maintenance determined that the Left Hand Slat #11 track actuator was faulty. The actuator was replaced IAW AMM and after an operational check, the aircraft returned to service.

C-GICZ, an Air Tractor AT-502B operated by Arty's Air service, was conducting an aerial application flight near Ste. Agathe, MB. While applying chemical on a canola field, the aircraft's rudder struck a powerline. The pilot then carried out a low level recovery straight ahead over the town of Ste. Agathe and diverted to Winkler (CKZ7), MB where the aircraft landed safely. The pilot was not injured and the aircraft sustained damage.The operator reported that the right wing tip, the upper rudder cap, propeller blade, and pump blade fans were damaged and will be replaced prior to returning to service.

C-FWGN, Bell 206B operated by Helicopter Transport Services (Canada) Inc., was on a repositioning flight from La Ronge/Barber Field (CYVC), SK to Baker Lake (CYBK). While enroute, the pilot heard a whining and grinding noise coming from the engine. The pilot monitored the gauges and noticed the turbine operating temperature (TOT) started to increase with no adjustments to the power setting. Moments later, the TOT increased further to an abnormal operating range of 950°C, followed by a louder whining and grinding noise. The engine NR RPM then increased, annunciator warning lights illuminated, and aural alarms sounded. The pilot conducted a successful forced landing in a marsh clearing. The pilot was uninjured and was transported from the site by another helicopter. The occurrence helicopter sustained minimal damage.An external examination of the engine was conducted and there was no signs of distress to the compressor. The operator will follow up with the TSB as to their findings.

C-GNTM, an Air Tractor AT-802 operated by Forest Protection Limited, was conducting fire suppression training flights about 20 nm southwest of Fredericton (CYFC), NB. It was planned to have the aircraft land at Brockway (CCX3) Airport, NB for fuel, and as the aircraft touched down on Runway 22 at CCX3, the aircraft began to drift to the left. The pilot applied right rudder, and when the yaw to the left continued, the pilot began adding right brake pedal pressure in an attempt to arrest the left yaw. It was not possible for the pilot to arrest the left yaw with right rudder and brake pedal force, and the left yaw increased until the aircraft nose was 90 degrees left, relative to the runway. The tailwheel pylon separated during the skid to the left, and the aircraft came to rest with the main landing gear off of the runway surface. The pilot was uninjured. The left mainwheel tire was found deflated due to a shredded patch in the center of the tread. The tire came off its wheel bead, and allowed the wheel rim to cause minor gouging damage to the chip seal runway surface. A small amount of fuel vented onto the runway surface. The landing conditions for runway were described as a light, right crosswind.

C-GTSZ, an Air Transat Airbus A330-200 was conducting flight TSC207 from Manchester/ Ringway Intl. (EGCC), United Kingdom to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During initial climb to cruise altitude approximately 65 nautical miles WNW from EGCC, one cabin crew became incapacitated.  Flight continued to CYYZ without further incident

C-GVZB, a Chrono Jet Inc. Cargo Boeing 737-800, was conducting flight MBK780 from Winnipeg/ James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB to Louisville/ Muhammad Ali Intl. (KSDF), KY.  At top of climb, approximately 180nm SE of CYWG, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to right hand engine issues (EGT fluctuations) and elected to return to CYWG where they landed without further incident.Maintenance found right hand engine EGT probe S3 and S4 out of tolerance.

C-GIQG, a Swearingen SA-226-TC aircraft, operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was being fueled in Swan River (CZJN), MB. Prior to operating the engines, the flight crew realized that the aircraft was fueled with incorrect fuel as Avgas 100LL was used versus the required Jet A fuel. A defect was entered into the journey log book and the operator's maintenance personnel removed the Avgas 100 LL. The aircraft was subsequently returned to service.

C-FBNX, a Cessna 337G operated by Mag Aerospace Canada Corp., was conducting a flight from Buffalo Narrows (CYVT), SK to Ile-à-la-Crosse (CJF3), SK. Just prior to the approach to CJF3, the aircraft returned to CYVT due to weather conditions. On approach to CYVT, the landing gear failed to extend and the landing gear circuit breaker was tripped. The QRH was consulted and an alternate gear extension was attempted; however, only the nose landing gear extended while the main landing gear did not. The pilot subsequently landed the aircraft on the nose gear only and the aircraft sustained damage to its belly and rear propeller. The pilot exited the aircraft without injury.The aircraft was subsequently removed from the runway and the operator's maintenance personnel noted that a hydraulic leak was found in the nose landing gear actuator and that the hydraulic reservoir was depleted.

C-FIBW, a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-700 conducting flight WS660 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, was on climb out of CYYC when at 400 feet ASL the aircraft inadvertently turned to the left. The flight crew corrected the deviation and continued to climb to altitude. The crew determined that the deviation was a result of the Yaw Damper disconnecting. The flight continued to CYYZ, and on descent to CYYZ the yaw damper again disconnected without warning and the flight crew began experiencing flight control difficulties. The crew declared an emergency and the aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The aircraft was removed from service and maintenance continue to troubleshoot the flight control system and will report on the findings.Added on August 25th 2022: Maintenance determined that the rudder trim had an un-commanded left deflection of 5 units when departing CYYC after the yaw damper disengaged. After recentering and restoring the yaw damper, cruise operations continued. While on approach into CYYZ in turbulence conditions, the rudder trim deflected un-commanded 11 units, then 5 units with an associated yaw damper and auto pilot disengage.  Maintenance identified the associated circuit breakers tripped. Troubleshooting activities continue to correct and identify the cause.  Connectors within the system had evidence of discoloration indicating shorting inside the connector which maintenance replaced. A series of ground tests as well as a flight test flight will be performed, to determine when the aircraft will be released to service.

N128UP, a United Parcel Service Airbus A300-600, was operating as flight UPS499 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to - Louisville International-Standiford Field (KSDF) KY, U.S., with 2 crew on board.  The aircraft taxied approximately 3 nautical miles from Ramp IX to takeoff from Runway 26L. Immediately after takeoff, the crew received an electronic centralized aircraft monitor (ECAM) Brake Temp High message. Elevated temperatures were noted on all four left main landing gear wheels. The landing gear was extended to cool the wheels. After two minutes of flying with the gear down, the crew, after consulting their flight dispatch and maintenance control, declared a PAN PAN emergency and returned to CYVR. Aircraft rescue and firefighting personnel met the aircraft and conducted an initial inspection. The tires were not damaged and the brakes showed normal temperatures. The aircraft was then taxied to the ramp for further inspection.Maintenance inspected the brake temperature system and performed the required tests. No faults were found. The brake temperature sensors were cleaned and the brake temperature system was adjusted and tested. The aircraft was returned to service.

D-ABYK, a Boeing B747-8 aircraft operated by Lufthansa German Airlines, was conducting flight DLH403 from Newark Liberty International Airport, NJ, USA (KEWR) to  Frankfurt Rein-Mein, Germany (EDDF). While in cruise flight, the cabin crew reported an electrical smell with light smoke in the forward galley to the flight crew. The flight crew declared an emergency and initiated a diversion to Boston Logan International Airport (KBOS) where the aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance personnel conducted an inspection of the aircraft and identified an espresso machine in the forward galley as being the source of the electrical smell and smoke.

C-GFJX, a privately operated Dassault Falcon 10 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Toronto/Oshawa Executive, ON (CYOO) to Charlottetown, PE (CYYG). As the aircraft was descending for the approach, the crew received a TCAS warning for traffic with a subsequent resolution to climb. The crew complied by climbing, advised ATC and continued to land without further incident. The conflicting aircraft was a Royal Canadian Air Force, CP-140 Aurora which had just conducted a low approach at the CYYG airport and was proceeding to Debert, NS (CCQ3).

C-GATX, an Airbus AS350B2 helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited, was conducting external load operations from Lorraine Lake, NL to Wabush Lake, NL with 1 flight crew member on board. While in cruise flight, the full 400 litre diesel fuel tank that was being carried, inadvertently released and fell to the forest below. The fuel tank was substantially damaged, resulting in the majority of its contents being released onto the forest floor. The rigging was recovered and was found to be in serviceable condition. The operator is conducting testing on the remote hook assembly, in order to determine the cause of the inadvertent release.

C-GPSK, un Jetstream 32 exploité par Pascan Aviation, effectuait le vol PSC582 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport des Îles-de-la-Madeleine, QC (CYGR) à destination de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 14 passagers à bord. Alors que l'aéronef se trouvait en approche pour la piste 06 à CYQB, le moteur gauche (Garrett TPE-331-12 s/n 66145) s'est arrêté lorsque le premier officier a réduit la puissance. Celui-ci a alors appliqué pleine puissance avec le moteur de droite et transféré le contrôle de l'aéronef au commandant de bord. Une urgence a été déclaré et l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre peu après.

The privately owned Grumman G44 aircraft (C-FNGD) was on route from the Sarnia airport (CYZR), ON to the Stratford Municipal airport, Ontario (CYSA) with the pilot/owner as the only soul on board. The pilot had made previous arrangements with a maintenance facility at the airport to have the annual/100 hour inspection performed. Weather at CYSA was reported as poor visibility with fog patches surrounding the airport area. The last  communication from the pilot on the airport Unicom frequency, was that he was turning base leg for Runway 23. Witnesses in a farm near the airport, observed  the aircraft entering and exiting cloud cover, a lower speed than they expected to observe and a bank angle greater than 45 degrees. They observed the aircraft disappear into cloud, and a few seconds later a loud crash was heard. Although they did not observe the impact they did see smoke from a field across from their farm, and after approaching the site immediately dialed 911. The pilot was fatally injured and the aircraft was consumed by fire after the impact. The pilot was only VFR OTT rated, he did not hold an IFR rating. Weather reports for the cities of Sarnia, Kitchener and London, Ontario were obtained and all three cities were reporting visibilities greater than 9 SM.

C-GVUH, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300, was conducting flight AC573 from Los Angeles (KLAX), California, U.S., to Calgary International (CYYC), AB, with 6 crew members and 128 passengers on board. Prior to the top of descent into CYYC, the ground spoiler caution message illuminated and continued intermittently. The flight crew declared a PAN-PAN and continued to CYYC. The flight landed without incident. The spoilers operated in flight as commanded with no adverse flight control behavior.  Company maintenance conducted troubleshooting and carried out a system reset. The ground spoiler operations check was carried out in accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual with further faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FUWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3400 from Comox (CYQQ), BC to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. At 12 000 feet ASL during approach into CYEG the crew observed a fuselage door warning indication. The crew referenced the QRH and declared a PAN PAN. The flight landed without any further issues. There was no loss of pressurization.Following the flight the maintenance team inspected and rigged the door sensor. The aircraft was released back into service.

C-GVOM, a privately registered Piper PA 18A 150 (Super Cub), was conducting a visual flight rules trip from Grassy Lake (57° 55.18' N, 131° 29.41' W) to Level Lake (58° 29. 69' N, 131° 17. 07' W) with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. After liftoff, approaching the end of the lake, the aircraft encountered a downdraft and began to lose altitude. The pilot initiated a left turn to avoid terrain at the end of the lake. In the turn, the aircraft stalled and struck the water in a nose down, left wing low attitude. The occupants were able to quickly exit the aircraft and then swam to the nearby shore. The emergency locator transmitter did not function but a personal locator beacon was used to signal the emergency. A helicopter was dispatched from Dease Lake to evacuate the pilot and passenger. The passenger was uninjured and the pilot was taken to hospital for treatment.The aircraft was recovered from the lake and taken to Telegraph Creek. Maintenance will conduct an inspection and determine the repair requirements.

C-GJTH, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-211 was conducting flight ROU1837 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Phoenix/Sky Harbor Intl. (KPHX), AZ.  During descent through FL300 approximately 100 nautical miles ENE of KPHX, aircraft experiences un-commanded roll approximately 30 degrees followed by less aggressive rolling turbulence shortly thereafter.  Flight crew corrected the roll and suspected wake turbulence.  ATC advised the flight crew they were 10 nm trailing a Boeing 737.  Flight crew requested and was granted 2 nautical miles track offset and flight landed in KPHX without further incident.

An unregistered Challenger II ultralight aircraft on floats was taxiing on the surface of the water in the vicinity of Lower Shoal Harbour, NL when the aircraft unexpectedly became airborne with one person on board. While maneuvering in the air, the aircraft stalled and rolled to the left, resulting in the left wing striking the surface of the water and the aircraft capsizing. The pilot was able to evacuate the aircraft with minor injuries and was taken to shore via rescue boat. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GGMZ, a DHC-8-402 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA201, an IFR flight from Toronto/Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario to Sault Ste. Marie Airport (CYAM), Ontario, with 4 crew and 39 passengers on board. During the initial climb through 14000 feet, the flight crew received an indication of #1 propeller overspeed. Checklist items were completed, resulting in a precautionary shutdown of the #1 engine. The flight crew declared PAN PAN and requested a return to CYYZ, where the flight landed uneventfully. Maintenance replaced and ground tested the #1 engine Pitch Control Unit before returning the aircraft to service.

N762QS, a NetJets Aviation Limited Bombardier BD-100-1A10, was operating as flight EJA762 from King County International (KBFI), WA, USA, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 2 crew members and 3 passengers on board. Upon landing at CYVR, the flight crew observed smoke in the cockpit and cabin. The flight crew asked for aircraft rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) to meet them as they stopped on Taxiway H. The crew shut down the aircraft on the taxiway. With the ARFF crew on site, it was determined that the smoke was no longer a danger. The aircraft was then towed to the ramp in order to clear customs.A maintenance inspection found the Air Cycle Machine (ACM) had failed. The aircraft was repaired and returned to service.

C-IGSC, a privately registered float-equipped Spectrum Aircraft Beaver RX 550 basic ultra-light aircraft, was conducting a takeoff on Setting Lake, MB with only the pilot on board. During the initial climb at approximately 75 feet AGL, the engine (Rotax 503) completely lost power. While attempting to conduct a forced landing on the lake, a float dug into the water and the aircraft capsized. The pilot was able to evacuate the aircraft with a minor injury. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The pilot was pulled out of the water by local cottagers and then taken to hospital for observation.

C-GUPG, an Airbus Canada Limited Partnership A220-300, was conducting flight ACA1237 from Toronto Pearson International Airport(CYYZ), ON to Nashville International Airport (KBNA), USA with 5 crew and 131 passengers onboard. N685TA, an Airbus 320 operated by Avianca, was conducting flight LRC626 from El Salvador International Airport(MSLP), El Salvador to CYYZ. Shortly after takeoff from CYYZ, while climbing to cruise altitude, ACA1237 received a traffic and collision avoidance system (TCAS) resolution advisory (RA) with flight LRC626 at 7000 feet and took the applicable evasive action. Both aircraft continued to their intended destination.

C-GFQP, a Bell 212 helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited, was slinging a diesel electric generator at a radar site located 43 nm SSW of Igloolik (CYGT), NU with only the pilot on board. While manoeuvering at approximately 1700 feet, the pilot unintentionally activated the load release switch and the load dropped. The pilot was able to maintain control of the helicopter and then landed safely. There were no injuries and the helicopter did not sustain any damage.

C-FVNB, an Air Canada B787-9 conducted flight AC27 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Incheon International Airport (RKSI), South Korea. On arrival in RKSI, a passenger dropped a cellphone into a seat and tried to retrieve the phone by moving the seat. The phone was crushed by the movement of the seat causing a small fire/smoke. The flight crew was notified, and ARFF was dispatched to the aircraft. The captain requested a deplanement of all passengers. 4 extinguishers were brought out in total with pins pulled. 2 extinguishers were used. No injuries.

C-FCAE, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd, was conducting flight CJT302 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON. While on Instrument landing system (ILS) approach for runway 12, CJT302 took evasive action to the right to avoid an unknown VFR glider directly in front of them. The glider was not transponder equipped, therefore not visible on radar or the aircraft's Traffic and collision avoidance system (TCAS). The glider also made a turn in the north west direction. CJT302 passed the glider on its port side close enough to see the glider pilot and was able to shortly return to their approach profile and land on runway 12 without further incident.

C-FWKO, an Utra Magic Balloons T-210, was launching from Floradale Parkview Manors, Floradale, ON with 1 pilot and 7 passengers onboard. The hot air balloon initially climbed to a height of 300 feet with surface wind of approximately 5 to 7 knots and was flying over a corn field which had an ascending elevation. The pilot reported that the wind suddenly began to press the aircraft toward the surface. The pilot began to heat the envelope with two burners at once but the inertia and the wind did not make it possible to avoid contact with the ground. Passengers were advised to bend their knees before impact and the aircraft touched down in the middle of the corn field approximately 500-600 meters east of the launch position. After checking with passengers, the aircraft took off again and climbed to 1000 feet to find a safe place to land and subsequently landed in a farmers cut field at 20:10. Two of the passengers reported being sore after landing. The following morning, the company was reported that one of the passenger suffered from a fractured collar bone and one passenger had her knees, ankles and hip bruised and swollen.

C-FSNQ, an Air Canada B737 Max 8 was conducting flight AC598 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to John Wayne Airport (KSNA), Santa Ana, CA when inbound at 5000 feet, the crew received a TCAS RA for a Cessna 172 at 4600 feet ahead. The crew followed the resolution and maintained 5000 feet. The ATC instructed the Cessna 172 to descend. AC598 landed safely in KSNA.

C-GAMQ, a Westjet B737 Max 8 conducting flight WJA1540 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Houston Airport (KIAH), TX was taxiing to the gate in KIAH under marshalling direction when the underside lower winglet of the left wing struck the air stairs. There was no evacuation or rapid deplanement. There was minor damage to the winglet.

C-FYSZ, a privately registered Piper PA-28-180 aircraft was taking off from Canton Aerodrome (CTN7), ON for a Visual Flight Rule (VFR) flight to Ottawa/Rockcliffe Airport (CYRO), ON with 1 pilot and 1 passenger onboard. At approximately 20:15, the aircraft took off runway 14, then shortly after liftoff, the left wing hit a tree at approximately 1400 feet from the start of initial takeoff roll at a height of 26 feet and about 40 feet left from the runway centerline. The aircraft subsequently impacted other trees approximately 400 feet from the initial impact and crashed in a soybean field. The wreckage came to rest approximately 220 feet left of the runway centerline, about 150 feet from the departure end of runway 14. The 406 MGHZ emergency locator transmitter (ELT) activated during impact and the signal received by the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) in Trenton, ON. Emergency services attended the scene and both occupants were found fatally injured. The TSB deployed investigators to the scene.

C-GNLN, a Boeing 737-2B6C operated by Nolinor Aviation, was conducting flight NRL944 from Val-D'Or (CYVO) QC. to Rankin Inlet (CYRT) NU. When the aircraft was on final approach for CYRT, the flight crew observed a flap disagree indication, and flight instruments and aerodynamic feedback indicated that the flaps were not extending. The aircraft was diverted to Churchill (CYYQ) MB. which offered a longer runway for a partial flap or a no-flap landing. The flight crew carried out the appropriate checklists, declared a PAN PAN with ATC, and requested airport emergency services on standby. The aircraft subsequently landed safety. The operator's maintenance inspected and tested the trailing edge flap control system and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FMAI, a Morningstar Air Express Inc. Boeing 757-200, was operating as flight MAL7090 from Toronto (CYYZ), ON to Calgary (CYYC), AB with 2 flight crew and 1 passenger on board. While on approach into CYYC, when flaps were selected from 5° to 20°, the flight crew observed a TE FLAP DISAGREE EICAS message. The flight crew discontinued the approach and obtained delaying vectors in order to action the QRH. MAL7090 conducted a second approach with the trailing edge flaps set to 20° using the ALT FLAP system, declared an emergency and had ARFF standing by for the landing. After landing, ARFF inspected the brakes and the aircraft taxied on its own to the cargo ramp. Company maintenance cleaned the flap limit switches and returned the aircraft to service.

C-GTXM, a Learjet 35A aircraft operated by Top Aces Inc. as BRUSR01, was conducting a flight from Halifax Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Bagotville airport (CYBG), QC. During the takeoff run in CYHZ, the crew aborted the take off at about 120 knots due to fumes in the cockpit. ARFF responded. The aircraft taxied back to the ramp without further incident. Maintenance determined that the odour was caused by residual fluid from the compressor wash completed several days prior to the incident. Engine runs were carried out, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FXIA, a commercially registered Robinson R-44, was conducting a private flight from Grand Bend, ON to Ilderton, ON with 1 pilot and 2 passengers onboard. Shortly after take off, during the initial climb, the pilot realized that he didn't have enough forward speed and rate of climb to clear approaching hydro lines. As the aircraft was moving downwind the carb heat had opened and the helicopter didn't get the expected power and planned transitional lift. While slowing down to an almost stationary position, extra load was put on the rotor system and the lower rotor RPM horn came on. The pilot subsequently looked to find an area with no obstruction and pushed the collective down to get the rotor head to speed up. The aircraft was approaching a landing position close to a parking lot area when the pilot realized that he had to put the helicopter down immediately. The rotor head rpm was to low and the helicopter started to turn clockwise form the engine torque when the aircraft landed hard onto a grass area just off the edge of the asphalt. The landing gear collapsed and the tail rotor hit the ground. The pilot and passengers walked away without injuries.

C-FWTC, a privately registered Piper PA28R-180 was conducting touch-and-go on runway 33 at Toronto Buttonville Municipal Airport (CYKZ), ON. While coming for a third landing on the downwind part of the circuit, the pilot reported a slower aircraft joining the downwind in front. The pilot subsequently reduced power to maintain separation and continued for a shallow approach to maintain visual contact preceding traffic. The gear warning activated just before contacting the runway when power was reduced for landing. The aircraft contact the runway on its belly damaging the propeller, the strobe light and an antenna. The aircraft was lifted and the gear extended before towed off the runway. The pilot, sole occupant onboard, was uninjured.

C-FTXA, a Viking Air CL215 operated by Buffalo Airways, was conducting operations as Tanker 293 from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) with 2 crew members on board. During the cruise portion of the flight, the left engine (Pratt & Whitney R2800) quit operating. The flight crew performed the actions required by the emergency checklist, and elected to return to CYZF. An uneventful landing was performed.Subsequent inspection by company maintenance personnel determined that the engine driven fuel pump had failed. The fuel pump was replaced, ground runs were performed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GVRA, an Avro Lancaster MK X aircraft operated by Canadian Warplane Heritage, was conducting a local flight from John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON. While on takeoff from runway 30, blue smoke was observed streaming from the right outboard engine immediately after rotation. The observation was communicated to the crew and the aircraft proceeded in a left circuit pattern. Air traffic control asked the pilot if they had the intention to land and have emergency equipment on standby. The pilot agreed and the aircraft came back for landing with Aircraft Rescue and firefighting (ARFF) vehicles standing by. The aircraft landed without further incident and taxied back to the apron under its own power.

C-FMKJ, an ATR 72-212A operated by Calm Air International LP, was conducting flight CAV3071 from Rankin Inlet (CYRT) NU. to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. CAV3071 conducted the RNAV Z approach to Runway 18, joined final, and completed the landing gear checks. On short final at 500 feet agl, the crew observed a red gear unsafe indication. The indication was intermittent changing from green to red with noises and vibrations coming from the lower nose carriage. A missed approach was carried out and the crew completed the "landing gear unsafe indication" checklist. On the second approach, the gear down selection was made and three green lights illuminated on both landing gear panels with no vibrations or noises. ARFF was placed on standby at the request of the crew. CAV3071 landed without incident and taxied to the gate.The operator's maintenance found an indication problem on the secondary (overhead) gear indicating system. A proximity sensor was replaced and tests carried out as per the aircraft maintenance manuals. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-GHCS, a Beech 1900D operated by Sunwest Aviation was conducting flight CNK55 from Calgary International, AB (CYYC) to Masset, BC (CZMT). C-GLWJ, a De Havilland of Canada DHC8-Q400 operated by WestJet Encore was conducting flight WEN3453 from CYYC to Victoria International, BC (CYYJ). CNK55 departed CYYC Runway 35L on runway heading. When the aircraft was transferred from the CYYC tower to CYYC departure control, the aircraft was cleared for a left turn to the AGMAK intersection. Shortly after the departure of CNK55, WEN3453 departed Runway 35L. While still under CYYC tower control, the tower cleared WEN3453 for the left turn to a heading 310. A loss of separation occurred between CNK55 and WEN3453 when separation eroded to 2.3 nm laterally and 800 feet vertically, where 3 nm lateral separation, and 1000 feet vertical separation are required. When WEN3453 was transferred to departure control, they were issued a new heading of 210 to regain separation.

C-FPLJ, un Murphy Moose SR3500 (construction amateur) sur flotteurs, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis le lac Otis, QC à destination du lac Brébeuf, QC. Peu après le décollage du lac Otis, alors que l’aéronef se trouvait en montée sur un cap nord, l’aéronef a amorcé un virage à droite vers un cap est en direction du lac Brébeuf. Peu après, une panne de moteur (SC Motorstar M14PF) est survenue. Le pilote a effectué la procédure de panne moteur et s’est dirigé vers le lac à la Balle pour effectuer un amerrissage d’urgence. Le pilote a tenté, sans succès, de redémarrer le moteur. L’aéronef a fauché la cime des arbres alors qu’il se trouvait en courte finale pour l’amerrissage, et a par la suite percuté un cabanon. L’aéronef a été détruit et le pilote a été grièvement blessé.

C-GORA, a Chartright Air B1900D (BE02) was conducting flight HRT326 from John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON to Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (KATL), GA when approximately 20 minutes after departure the aircraft leveled off at FL240. The electric trim failed and the crew cut out the system and reverted to manual trim. When they attempted to trim manually the trim wheel would not move. The aircraft was still trimmed nose up and the PF had to apply moderate control force to hold the aircraft level. The crew declared an emergency and diverted to London International Airport (CYXU), ON. The flight landed at CYXU without further incident. Control force in the flare, given the position that the trim was stuck in, was close to normal and there were no issues on landing.

C-FEWJ, a Boeing 737-8 operated by WestJet Airlines, was conducting flight WJA252 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. Approximately 30 minutes after takeoff from CYYZ, the flight crew was informed by a deadheading cabin crew member traveling in the cabin, about a loud and abnormal noise coming from the left main gear. The flight crew contacted maintenance control for consultation as a main landing gear was suspected to be damaged initially. The flight crew did not receive any other abnormal indications in the flight deck and continued the flight. While on the descending through 10,000 feet for CYHZ, the loud noise was heard again. The flight crew elected to declare a PAN PAN and have aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) meet the aircraft on the runway after stopping. Once stopped, ARFF confirmed to the flight crew that there was no visible damage to the landing gear and the aircraft then taxied safely to the gate. Maintenance personnel performed an inspection on the left hand landing gear and did not identified any faults or damage. The aircraft was returned to service.

Fedex flight FDX132, a Douglas DC10 (N318FE) aircraft, on route from Memphis, TC (KMEM) to Toronto, ON (CYYZ) declared an emergency due to a cracked windshield. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FKIW, a Boeing 737-700 operated by WestJet Airlines was conducting flight WJA175 from Edmonton International, AB (CYEG) to Vancouver international, BC (CYVR) with 5 crew members and 128 passengers on board. During the climb to cruising altitude, the flight crew noticed a burning smell in the cockpit. The flight crew contacted the cabin crew, who also confirmed there was a similar smell in the cabin. The flight crew made the decision to return to CYEG. A PAN PAN call was made with ATS and airport rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) was activated. An uneventful landing was subsequently completed, and ARFF met the aircraft on the runway to perform an initial inspection. After determining there was no indications of a fire, the aircraft taxied to the gate were the passengers and crew deplaned.Subsequent investigation by company maintenance found an unserviceable cabin air recirculation fan. The fan was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

Porter airlines flight POE9806, a De Havilland DHC-8-402 (C-GLQG), was on descent to Toronto Billy Bishop Airport (CYTZ), ON and descending through 10000 feet when the aircraft had an uncommanded yaw to the left. The aircraft had another uncommanded yaw to the left 10sm from LENOG with a corresponding uncommanded change in torque of approximately 15%. One caution and warning light illuminated briefly, but the flight crew were unable determine which lights they were in the brief moment they were illuminated. The flight crew leveled the aircraft at 4000 feet and shut down the number 2 engine as per the QRH. The flight crew declared an emergency and diverted to Hamilton (CYHM), ON. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance replaced the number 2 Propeller Electronic Controller (PEC) IAW the maintenance manual the aircraft released beck into service.

C-GCFR, un Dehavilland DHC-7-100 exploité par Transports Canada sous l'indicatif TGO922, effectuait un vol de reconnaissance local selon les règles combinées de vol aux instruments et de vol à vue au départ de l’aéroport de Iqaluit, NU (CYFB). Alors que l’aéronef se trouvait à environ 140 milles nautiques (NM) au sud-ouest de CYFB en palier à 6000 pieds ASL, l’équipage a remarqué que l’indication de pression d’huile du moteur numéro 1 était en baisse. Alors que l’équipage effectuait la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH), la décision de fermer le moteur par mesure de précaution a été prise alors que la pression d’huile continuait de baisser et que le témoin de basse pression d'huile s'est allumé. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) et revenu à CYFB où il s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GKWE, a Dehavilland DHC-8-402 aircraft, was conducting WestJet Encore flight WEN3422 from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS to St. John's International Airport (CYYT), NL. While on final approach on Runway 34 at CYYT, the flight crew was alerted to smoke in the lavatory. The flight crew declared a MAYDAY with CYYT tower and advised them that the flight intended to stop on the runway after landing. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) met the aircraft when it stopped. The source of the smoke was traced to a passenger that was vaping in the lavatory. The aircraft then taxied safely to the gate.

C-FTHY, a Talon Helicopters Limited Airbus AS350-B2 (A-Star) helicopter, was conducting external load operations 46 NM NW of Vernon (CYVK), BC, in support of forest fire suppression operations with 1 pilot on board. During cruise, the empty net which was attached to the long line, inadvertently released onto a steep hillside within the fire area. There were no injuries.The hook was inspected and the keeper was found to be sticky. The keeper was lubricated and function tested. Ground crews received additional briefings on sling operations.

The pilot of C-GPLL, a Bakeng Duce aircraft, was taking off from Runway 07 at Lancaster Airpark (CLA6), ON and had just become airborne around 1000 feet down the runway when the aircraft encountered some unexpected wind from the left causing the aircraft to drift right. The pilot corrected for the right drift and then found the aircraft wanted to drift left then right. The pilot attempted to correct the drifting and ended up losing control of the aircraft and crashing on the south side of the runway near the windsock, there were no injuries. The aircrafts right land gear and tail wheel failed, the right wing was bent and the propeller was damaged.

C-FVOL, a privately registered Quest Kodiak 100 amphibious airplane, was conducting a flight from Atlin (CYSQ), BC, to Trout Lake, BC, with 3 passengers and 2 crew members on board. After landing, while taxiing the aircraft to a nearby shore, the aircraft was caught in a river current and grounded in shallow rocky water. There were no injuries. Three days later, a helicopter slung the aircraft to a nearby shore. The crew conducted a visual inspection of the aircraft. They then flew from Trout Lake to CYSQ with only the 2 pilots on board. The crew intended for maintenance personnel to conduct a more thorough inspection of the aircraft. During the takeoff run, the aircraft could not accelerate to the speed needed for liftoff and the crew rejected the takeoff. Following the rejected takeoff, the aircraft rolled to the right and became partially submerged. There were no injuries. The aircraft was substantial damaged. The emergency locator transmitter did not activate. The crew were airlifted to Atlin by a local helicopter company.The aircraft was recovered and transported to Atlin.

C-GELD, a Piper PA-31 operated by Adventure Aviation, was conducting a VFR flight from Fort Saint John, BC (CYXJ) to Fort Grahame, BC (CBW3) with only the pilot on board. During the approach into CBW3, the pilot extended the landing gear, but did not receive a down and locked indication for the right main landing gear. The pilot operated the emergency extension hydraulic pump, but the landing gear position indication did not change. The decision was made to divert to Grand Prairie, AB (CYQU) with the landing gear extended. On the approach into CYQU, the pilot declared emergency due to gear indicator not showing that the right main landing gear was down and locked. Airport rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) were dispatched, and 911 was advised. The pilot flew a low and over the field and FSS as well as ARFF confirmed all 3 landing gear appeared to be down. The aircraft completed and uneventful landing and shut down on runway to inspect the landing gear. The pilot inspected the landing gear and advised he was able to start up and taxi off the runway under the aircraft's own power. Subsequent investigation by company maintenance personnel found the downlock rods for the landing gear were contaminated. The actuating rods were cleaned, gear swings were successfully completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

N284UP a UPS MD-11F aircraft conducting flight UPS487 was climbing after take-off from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Louisville International Airport (KSDF), KY when reaching FL140 the crew heard a loud bang and moderate vibration. The number 3 engine (P&W PW4460) EGT immediately indicated in the red. The crew followed QRH procedures and shut down the engine. An emergency was declared and the aircraft returned to CYYZ. The landing was uneventful with ARFF standing by. Maintenance could not determine the cause for the failure, and replaced the engine before the aircraft returned to service.

C-GENO, a De Havilland of Canada DHC-8-Q400 operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3195 from Calgary International, AB (CYYC) to Grand Prairie, AB (CYQU) with 4 crew members, and 54 passengers on board. After take off from CYYC, the flight crew retracted the landing gear and received an amber nose landing gear door indication. The flight crew notified ATS and performed the appropriate QRH procedure. The decision to return to CYYC was made and a priority (PAN PAN) was declared. An uneventful landing was completed, and the passengers deplaned normally.

C-GBOW, a Canadair CL215-1A10 aircraft operated by Air Spray (1967) Ltd., was conducting fire suppression operations in the vicinity of Pukatawagan, MB. After a water pickup, the crew noticed excessive oil on the right engine cowl. The water load was dropped and the aircraft climbed to 5500 feet ASL. The right engine was shut down per the emergency checklist and the aircraft diverted to The Pas (CYQD), MB for an uneventful landing.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and identified an oil leak coming from the right engine nose case. The nose case was replaced and the engine was subsequently ground run with no further faults identified.

C-GLSD, Un Piper PA-28R-200 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) à destination de l’aéroport de Sherbrooke, QC (CYSC) avec un pilote et un passager à bord.  Le pilote utilisait une liste de vérification papier et n'a pas remarqué qu'il avait omis l'étape de la sortie du train. L'approche a été effectuée sans que les gaz soient complètement réduits. L'alarme ne s'est donc déclenchée qu'au moment de l'arrondi. L'appareil s'est posé sur le ventre en douceur et a glissé sur une courte distance, s'immobilisant dans l'herbe en bordure de piste. L'hélice a percuté le sol. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé. L'appareil a été soulevé et le train sorti pour le remorquage.

C-FBHF, a Canadian Helicopters Limited Bell 212 (Twin Huey) helicopter was conducting external load operations at Kemano Heliport (CBZ2), BC, with only the pilot on board. During the lift of a 1600 pound steel counterweight, the load inadvertently released from the aircraft belly hook at approximately 10 feet above the ground. There was no damage to property, the load, or the aircraft. There were no injuries reported. A similar occurrence with the same aircraft and lifting equipment occurred on 20 July 2022 under TSB investigation A22P0065. Maintenance has removed all associated parts of the lifting system for troubleshooting.

C-GWNG, un Aerostar en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de de l’aéroport de Lachute, Qc (CSE4) avec un pilote à bord. Lors de la sortie du train d'atterrissage, l'indicateur de sortie du train avant ne s'est pas allumé. Le pilote a décidé de se dérouter vers l'aéroport de Mirabel, Qc (CYMX) pour faire inspecter le train par le personnel de l'aéroport et une meilleure assistance. Le train a visuellement été confirmé descendu et lors de la deuxième approche, le voyant lumineux du train avant s'est allumé. L'avion a poursuivi vers sa destination originale où il est atterri sans encombre. Le personnel de maintenance ont diagnostiqué et remplacé un solénoïde intermittent.

C-FJYR un Cessna 172N sur flotteurs en immatriculation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le Lac Marjo, Qc à destination de l'aéroport d'Alma, Qc (CYTF). Environs 10 minutes après le décollage, alors que l'appareil se trouvait à environ 3000 pieds ASL, le pilote a positionné le sélecteur de réservoir d'essence sur l'aile gauche. Moins d'une minute plus tard, le moteur s'est subitement arrêté. Le pilote a effectué un amerrissage d'urgence sur un petit lac, et l'appareil s'est immobilisé dans la tourbière sur la rive éloignée. Le pilote a manuellement activé la radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT). L'appareil a été localisé par le Centre conjoint de coordination des opérations de sauvetage de Trenton (JRCC). Le pilote et le passager ont été récupérés par l'unité de sauvetage de la base des Forces armées de Bagotville. Les 2 occupants n'ont pas été blessés, mais le passager a été transporté à l'hôpital pour un examen de contrôle en raison de son âge.

C-ICTC, a Quad City Challenger II advanced ultra-light aircraft, took off from runway 02 at Manitowaning/Manitoulin East Municipal airport, ON. Video of the take-off shows that as soon as the aircraft became airborne the pilot had difficulty controlling the aircraft and the engine began to surge. The pilot attempted to return to land on runway 02, but aerodynamically stalled while attempting to maneuver at low altitude. The aircraft crashed near the windsock and main ramp area in a ditch. The pilot was not injured, but the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

The Air Sprint Inc. Cessna 525A, C-FASR, was operating as ASP510 on a flight from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Edmonton (CYEG), AB with 2 flight crew on board. During descent into CYEG, the flight crew observed a master warning light for the door seal which then led to a cabin depressurization during descent. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks, descended at an accelerated rate, and declared an emergency. The flight continued to CYEG and made a safe landing. Once on the ground the crew got a L PT2TT2 fail annunciator and a L ENG CTRL SYS fail annunciator. Maintenance update: Cabin entry door seal service line evacuated to remove moisture. Functional test completed on ground and no fault found. Left hand engine FADEC harness replaced with new to address coincidental illumination of L PT2TT2 fail and L ENG CTRL SYS fail annunciators.

C-FVFH, a Lockheed 188A (Electra) operated by Air Spray (1967) Ltd, was conducting aerial firefighting operations from West Kootenay Regional Airport (CYCG), BC, with 2 pilots on board. During takeoff, the No. 2 engine (Allison 501-D13) suffered a power loss when take off power was set. The flight crew rejected the take off at approximately 50 knots and taxied off the runway. There were no injuries.The operator's maintenance replaced the propeller governor and propeller regulator which were found to have malfunctioned. The engine was successfully run and the airplane was returned to service.

The Rideau Valley Soaring School Piper PA-25-235 aircraft (C-GGDK) was returning to Rideau Valley Airpark (CPL3) after a local flight. Approximately 3 Km South of the Airpark, and at height of 2200 feet AGL, the engine lost power (Lycoming O-540) and was unresponsive to the control inputs. The pilot attempted to return to the airpark but due to the loss of height selected a grass field nearby. During the landing the right main landing gear collapsed and the right wing dug into the ground resulting in the aircraft ground looping. The pilot was not injured and exited the aircraft. During a walk-around the pilot found fuel leaking from the rear of the carburetor.

C-GOKD, an Ayres S-2R operated by Pembina Air 1999 Ltd. C-GOKD departed Treherne/South Northfolk Airpark (CTN6) MB. to conduct aerial application operations approximately 12 NM to the north east of CTN6. The aircraft was conducting a race track spray pattern on the field and, while turning, the aircraft collided with the ground. The ELT activated and RCMP, EMS and the local fire department responded. The pilot was fatally injured. TSB is investigating.

C-FYJD, a Sunwing B737-800 was conducting flight BY5529 from Corfu Airport Ioannis Kapodistrias (LGKR), Greece to Norwich Airport (EGSH), UK. On departure, BY5529 deviated southbound due to weather and airspace restrictions. BY5529 was then delayed in returning to a northbound course to intercept flight plan track due to ATC frequency congestion. After establishing a northbound course, the flight crew subsequently received a "using reserve fuel" message on the Flight Management Computer (FMC) which indicated that the FMC was forecasting to arrive at destination with insufficient reserve fuel to fly to the planned alternate. The flight crew contacted dispatch and a decision was made to divert to Leonardo da Vinci International Airport (LIRF), Rome for fuel. After refueling, the flight continued to EGSH without further issue.

C-GTSR, an Air Transat A300-200 was conducting flight TSC308 from Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Leonardo da Vinci International Airport (LIRF), Italy. Approximately half way to destination, a cabin crew became incapacitated. All safety-related duties were reassigned for the remainder of the flight.

C-GOIK, an Air Transat A321-271NX was conducting flight TSC123 from Gatwick Airport (EGKK), UK to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Approximately 30 minutes into the flight, a cabin crew became incapacitated. Safety related duties were reassigned for the remainder of the flight.

C-FFQS, a Conair Group Incorporated Air Tractor AT-802A on amphibious floats, was conducting forest fire fighting operations from the Canadian Rockies International Airport (CYXC), BC, with 1 crew member on board. After releasing his payload on the Connell Ridge wildfire, the pilot applied power for the climb out but the engine power rolled back to idle. The pilot selected the Emergency Power Lever but no more power was produced. The pilot selected an area for a forced approach and landed in a logged area with newly planted trees. The pilot sustained minor injuries and was taken by helicopter to receive medical aid. There was no post impact fire. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FEIX, un Embraer ERJ 170-200 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA948 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport George Bush Intercontinental de Houston, USA (KIAH) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal Trudeau, Qc (CYUL). Au même moment, C-GOJC, un Airbus A321 NEO exploité par Air Transat sous l'indicatif TSC583 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Blagnac de Toulouse, France (LFBO). En approche finale, à environ 11 miles nautiques au nord-est de CYUL l'espacement entre C-FEIX et C-GOJC a été réduit à 2.7 miles nautiques et 400 pieds verticaux alors que le minimum requis était de 3 miles et 1000 pieds verticalement.

C-GHLM an Air Canada A330 conducting flight AC824 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Adolfo Suárez Madrid–Barajas Airport (LEMD), Spain was landing runway 32L on short final at 1500ft when the crew received a TCAS RA to monitor vertical speed. They kicked off the autopilot and hand flew the descent when they were told by ATC about an aircraft heading towards them in the opposite direction. The crew reported missing the traffic by 200ft. No evasive maneuver reported and the aircraft landed safely.Final report was received on 17th Feb 2023.

C-FMSX, an Air Canada A320 conducting flight AC584 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ when at around 800 feet on final, the crew received a TCAS RA due to a nearby helicopter. The crew performed a go around, climbed to 2500 feet and vectored back. The aircraft landed safely.

C-GJJF, un Beechcraft A100 exploité par Propair Inc. sous l’indicatif PRO4650, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) à destination de La Romaine, QC (CTT5). Durant la montée initiale, les passagers ont observé une fumée blanche avec une odeur de surchauffe. En raison des conditions météorologiques à CYZV, l'équipage a immédiatement déclaré une urgence et dérouté vers L'aéroport de Baie-Comeau, Qc (CYBC). La source semblant être dans le compartiment bagage, un passager a vérifié tous les bagages sans identifier de problème. L'appareil a atterri sans encombre à Baie-Comeau. Aucun blessé. Les services d'urgence incendie ont inspecté le compartiment ainsi que les baggages sans trouver la source. Des mécaniciens ont inspecté les moteurs et tout le système environnemental sans trouver de défaillance. Un test en vol a été effectué avec succès et l'appareil remis en service.

C-GDDJ, a Wilderness Seaplanes Grumman G21A (Goose), was conducting a passenger flight from Walbran Island, BC, (17 nautical miles southwest of Rivers Inlet [CAU8]) to Port Hardy (CYZT), BC, with the pilot and 8 passengers on board. After the aircraft began to taxi on the water for departure, the right wing float appeared to have lost buoyancy. The pilot maneuvered for another minute in an attempt to raise the float. Unable to raise the float, the pilot attempted a turn to return to the dock. During the turn, the right propeller struck the water and the pilot saw the right wing was sinking. He immediately shut down the engines and told the passengers to evacuate. The pilot assisted the passengers in exiting from the left rear emergency exit and the left side cockpit window; the right side exits were submerged. Boats from a nearby fishing lodge arrived to help and took the passengers on board. One passenger received minor injuries during the egress from the aircraft but there were no other injuries. All the passengers had been wearing PFD's, two passengers inflated them once out of the aircraft. The aircraft rolled inverted in the water and floated on the surface. Once recovered, an inspection found three float plugs for the right wing float were missing which allowed the float to fill with water.

C-IJAQ, un Air Création FUN-GTE 503 SL ultraléger de base (pendulaire) en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis un champ à Saint-Paul-d’Abbotsford, Québec avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Immédiatement après le décollage, l’aéronef a amorcé un virage à gauche, inhabituel et continu, à très basse altitude. Au deuxième tour, l’aéronef a percuté le sol avec le moteur à pleine puissance et a subi des dommages importants. Le pilote a subi des blessures mortelles et le passager a subi des blessures graves.

C-GEGI, an Airbus A330-343 was conducting Air Canada flight 823 from Josep Tarradellas Barcelona–El Prat Airport (LEBL), Spain to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. While enroute, approximately 100 nm NE of Moncton/Roméo Leblanc International Airport (CYQM), NB, the flight crew declared a medical emergency and requested to divert to CYQM due to a flight attendant who became incapacitated and was unable to perform their duties. The flight attendant was under the care of a physician that was on-board the flight. After landing, the flight attendant was transported to hospital.

C-FBHF, a Bell 212 helicopter, operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited, was conducting external load operations at Kemano Heliport (CBZ2), BC, with only the pilot on board. During a lift of 2 racks of oxygen bottles (4 bottles per rack), the load inadvertently released from the belly hook at approximately 10 feet above the ground and clear of the pad site. The load and long line were recovered and the load suffered minor damage. There was no property or aircraft damage and there were no reported injuries. On-site maintenance conducted an inspection and functional check of the long line and aircraft system with no faults found.

C-GRIL, a Bell 212 helicopter operated by Ascent Helicopters Limited, was conducting wildlife monitoring work in the vicinity of Sparwood/Elk Valley Airport (CYSW), B.C, with 1 pilot and 4 passengers onboard. While landing at an unprepared site on a mountain ridge, at approximately 7000 feet above sea level, the aircraft encountered down drafts while on short final. The helicopter settled onto the ground while moving forward. The pilot shut down the aircraft as per normal procedures and, after exiting the aircraft, observed the landing gear cross tubes had been deformed and had separated from the skid tubes in 3 locations. The ELT did not activate. There were no reported injuries. A second helicopter arrived at the occurrence site and transported the pilot and passengers to the operator's helicopter base in Fernie, B.C.A preliminary inspection was conducted on-site and found no damage to the main rotor, tail rotor, and associated drive shafts.
