The aircraft was slung out and transported to a maintenance facility for inspection and repair.

C-GBBG, un Cirrus SR22 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) et C-GNKW, un Socata TBM 700N en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport, ON (CYTZ) aussi à destination de CYQB. Le C-GBBG a eu des difficultés avec la procédure d'arrivée publiée pour CYQB et un cap lui a été assigné, par la suite les données radar ont disparu et ensuite réapparues. Un cap de correction a été assigné alors qu’il était à 4500 pieds, toutefois une perte d’espacement est survenue avec C- GNKW qui passait à 2,7 miles marins au sud en approche finale à 4000 pieds. L’espacement requis était de 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical et 3 nm sur le plan horizontal.

C-FNYA, an amateur built, DANA motor-glider, departed from runway 27 at the Conn Aerodrome (CCN4), Ontario for a local flight; the pilot was the sole occupant onboard. Shortly after lift-off, the aircraft turned to the right, descended, and struck a line of trees bordering a wheat field adjacent to the airport and subsequently impacted the ground. The aircraft was destroyed, and the pilot sustained fatal injuries. TSB investigators deployed to the scene. During examination of the flight control systems, the elevator was found disconnected from the elevator control pushrod. A bolt was found installed in the elevator control rod end, secured with a washer and a closed coiled tension safety pin, however the control rod end and related hardware were not connected to the associated elevator bracket. None of the prementioned components were damaged from impact, indicating the control rod was most likely not attached prior to the occurrence flight. The horizontal stabilizer and elevator were designed to be removed easily for storage and transport and were reportedly installed just prior to the occurrence flight.

N809AW, an American Airlines Airbus A319 aircraft (flight AAL1730) was en route from Charlotte Douglas International Airport (KCLT), NC to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON when the flight crew received an ECAM caution message LG LGCIU 1 Fault. The flight crew followed the QRH procedures and contacted maintenance; an emergency was declared due to the possible landing gear issues. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. Maintenance rectified the fault and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GCVV, a privately registered Piper PA-28R-180 (Arrow) was on a local visual flight rules trip from, and returning to, Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC, with only the pilot on board. The pilot checked in with the CYPK Tower air traffic controller and was cleared for the straight in approach to Runway 26L. The tower controller subsequently cleared the aircraft to land when the pilot reported over the Hammond Mill; approximately 3 nautical miles final. The aircraft struck terrain 2½ minutes later and stopped on the grass approximately 560 feet prior to the threshold of Runway 26L. On short final, the aircraft struck a number of obstacles; omni-directional approach light (ODAL) No. 4, ODAL No. 3, a hedge, and the airport perimeter fence before impacting the terrain. The aircraft collided with ODAL No. 2 37 feet after the initial impact and came to rest about 15 feet after that. The first obstacle hit, ODAL No. 4, was 1180 feet east and 23’ above the threshold of Runway 26L. The emergency locator transmitter (ELT) activated automatically.  The tower controller called 911 to request first responder services. The aircraft was substantially damaged but the pilot was not injured.  The aircraft was recovered from the field and taken to its hangar. It will be examined to determine the repairs required.

N404AN, an American Airlines Airbus A321-253NX, was operating as flight AAL1753 from Anchorage (PANC), AK to Chicago (KORD), IL. The crew declared a PAN PAN while in Vancouver airspace due to a LAV issue and diverted to Seattle (KSEA), WA. The PAN PAN was declared due to an anticipated overweight landing. There were no further issues during the flight.Following the flight the maintenance team determined that an overweight landing inspection was not required.

C-GKFG, a Convair 580 operated by Kelowna Flightcraft Air Charter Limited, was conducting flight KFA576 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with two crew members on board. Shortly after departure, the crew observed the Engine Driven Compressor (EDC) oil overheat annunciator illuminated; all other engine indications were normal. The crew accomplished the appropriate supplementary checklists and disconnected the EDC. The No. 2 engine (Allison 501-D13D) oil temperature then began to climb rapidly. The engine shut down checklists were accomplished and the crew shut down the No. 2 engine. The airplane returned to CYLW and landed without further incident.   An inspection by company maintenance personnel determined that a fault in the EDC had caused the No. 2 engine oil temperature rise. The EDC assembly was replaced no fault was found in the subsequent engine runs. The airplane was returned to service, a Service Difficulty Report has been filed with Transport Canada, and a report was entered into the company’s Safety Management System.

C-GJZT, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 CRJ 900 operated by Jazz Aviation as flight JZA 8192, was enroute from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Regina Intl. (CYQR), SK with 4 crew members and 63 passengers on board. When approaching the Medak Intersection at flight level 370, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence. The turbulence event resulted in an increase in airspeed and caused the auto pilot to disengage. Checklist items were carried out and the crew requested a lower altitude to escape the severe turbulence. Moderate turbulence was experienced in the descent through flight level 290. The captain and First Officer sustained minor injuries. One passenger holding an infant was thrown into a bulkhead near a window area; however, received no injuries. The flight continued to CYQR where, upon landing, the crew observed an outboard spoilers caution message, an ADS-B Fail message and EFIS COMP MON annunciation within a few minutes of each other. Taxi to the gate was uneventful. The aircraft was removed from service while the operator's maintenance carried out a severe turbulence inspection and downloaded the QAR for analysis. The severe turbulence event was classed as a type one event. The operator also noted that the pre-flight planning did not indicate any significant turbulence risk. The flight plan showed shear factor of 1 in that area. There were no PIREPs reported, nor were there any other aircraft in the vicinity.

C-GSWM, a Cessna 150L aeroplane operated by the Regina Flying Club, was conducting touch and go circuits during a solo Air Cadet student flight at Regina Intl. (CYQR), SK. On the third circuit, the aircraft landed hard and bounced resulting in a harder second touchdown and bounce. The student declared a partial MAYDAY advising ATC that a crash was imminent. During the final impact with the runway, the nose landing gear collapsed and the aircraft skidded nose down 50 to 75 feet to a stop. Airport emergency services were activated and the student was able to exit the aircraft uninjured. The aircraft sustained damage to the nose landing gear, propeller, engine, engine mount and cowling. A small amount of fuel leaked onto the runway. There was no fire. The DND Directorate of Flight Safety (DFS) is investigating.

N945AT, un Boeing 717-200 exploité par Delta Airlines sous l’indicatif DAL2416, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Hartsfield-Jackson Intl Airport, GA (KATL) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) avec 85 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors du débarquement des passagers à la barrière C84 à CYUL, le convoyeur à bagages a percuté le fuselage près de la porte-cargo arrière causant des dommages structurels. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FWVD, un Pathfinder de construction amateur (équipé de flotteurs) en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue à partir de Poltimore, QC à destination de Notre-Dame-du-Laus, QC avec 1 pilote à bord. Lors de la manœuvre en approche pour l’amerrissage, le pilote a perdu la maîtrise de l’avion et il a percuté la surface de l’eau avec une assiette en piqué prononcé près de la rive du lac. Le pilote a subi des blessures graves et l’avion a subi des dommages importants. Aucun signal de radiobalise de détresse (ELT) n’a été capté.

C-FNWD, a Westjet Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight WJA1215 from New York/ LaGuardia (KLGA) NY to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During climb to cruising altitude, flight encountered unexpected turbulence and one of the cabin crew became incapacitated.  Flight landed in CYYZ without further incident.

C-GOIH, an Air Transat Airbus 321 had an indication of smoke in the lavatory while taxiing for departure at the Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario. The flight crew stopped the aircraft, set the parking brake and declared an emergency. The cabin crew was called to investigate and found that the alarm had activated as a result of a passenger having sprayed something in the lavatory.  The flight crew cancelled the emergency, resumed normal operations and proceeded with the flight.

C-GGSN, a privately registered Cessna 172P, was conducting a visual flight rules flight from Victoria International (CYYJ), BC, to Qualicum Beach Airport (CAT4), BC, with only the pilot on board. As the aircraft neared CAT4 from the southeast, the engine (Avco Lycoming O-320-D2J) began to sputter and decelerated to approximately 1200 RPM. The pilot increased the throttle, but the engine did not respond. The pilot had been maneuvering to join the downwind leg for Runway 29 but opted to conduct an emergency landing on Runway 11, initiated a left turn, and a steep descent. The pilot reduced the engine throttle and added flaps. The aircraft briefly contacted the runway surface beyond the midpoint of the runway (less than 1850 feet of runway remained) and became airborne again. The pilot initiated a go-around and increased the engine throttle to full power and entered a climb. The pilot initiated a steep right turn immediately before reaching tree-covered down-sloping terrain and the aircraft began a rapid descent in a right bank and nose-down attitude. The pilot declared a MAYDAY before the aircraft impacted terrain in the trees along the edge of a farmer's field and came to rest approximately 1880 feet beyond the runway. The 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter (ELT) activated and local emergency services arrived on scene shortly after. The pilot received serious injuries and the aircraft was substantially damaged.AMENDED on 13 February 2023.

C-ILLZ, an Aeroprakt 22LS advanced ultralight operated by Flying Air Club Inc., was preparing for flight on Apron 1 at Pitt Meadows (CYPK), B.C with 1 flight instructor and 1 student onboard. Immediately after engine start, the engine speed rapidly increased and the aircraft launched forward. The pilot attempted to pull back on the throttle to reduce the engine power, but the throttle could not be moved. The pilot manipulated the rudder and the brakes before control was lost and the aircraft collided with a parked aircraft C-GYPN, a Cessna 172N operated by Island Coastal Aviation Inc. C-GYPN was not operating at the time and there were no occupants onboard. The pilot reported a minor injury while the passenger was uninjured. Both aircraft were substantially damaged. C-ILLZ was equipped with a modified hand control that combines the rudder, brake and throttle controls on 1 hand lever. After shutdown and egress from the aircraft, the pilot confirmed the throttle functioned normally as it did during the preflight checks. During a previous flight on 5 July 2022 with the same aircraft, the pilot experienced a temporarily stuck throttle in-flight that self-corrected and, after a normal landing, no fault could be identified.

C-GDCP, an Anderson Air Ltd. Cessna sovereign C680 was conducting a flight between Fairbanks Intl. (PAFA), AK and Kotzebue/Ralph Wien Memorial Airport (PAOT), AK.  During landing rollout shortly after touchdown, the aircraft travelled through standing water left of centerline.  Flight crew felt a bump as if the aircraft went over a dip (pothole) on the runway.  During the after landing check the flaps were selected up and failed at 15 degrees and could not be reset. After shutdown flight crew discovered substantial damage to LH inboard flap damaged and wing trailing edge.  During discussion with airport maintenance on duty personnel,  it was discovered that a NOTAM referencing standing water on runway was cancelled the previous day and therefore was unavailable to flight crew.  No hazard was signaled before landing by local FSS. Maintenance is investigating aircraft damages.

C-FQHJ, a privately registered Luscombe 8E, was conducting a training flight at Winters Aire Park - Indus (CFY4), AB. On short final for Runway 09 the instructor took control from the student to initiate a go-around. During the go-around the aircraft lightly contacted the runway surface so the instructor continued with the landing. During the roll out the right hand landing gear collapsed and the aircraft veered off of the right side of the runway. Winds were from the 150 degrees true at 10 knots (CYYC METAR). There were no injuries and the instructor and student exited the aircraft on their own. The plane was recovered to the student's hangar at the aerodrome.

C-GNSC, a Chartright Air Inc. Learjet 45 was conducting flight HRT237 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Austin-Bergstrom Intl. (KAUS), TX.  Approximately 275 NM SW of CYYZ, Flight crew received#1 engine oil pressure indication.  Flight crew completed QRH, shut down the engine, declared an emergency with ATC and diverted to CYYZ where it landed without further incident.  Maintenance found faulty filler cap oring on #1 engine.  Maintenance is investigating the cause.

C-GKFG, a Kelowna Flightcraft Air Charter Limited Convair 580, was conducting flight KFA577 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Kelowna (CYLW), BC, with 2 flight crew onboard. During cruise flight, the No. 1 engine (Allison 501-D13D) speed dropped below 13 400 rpm and the crew observed oil leaking from the No. 1 propeller. The crew completed an inflight shutdown of the No. 1 engine and declared an emergency with the Vancouver Area Control Center. The crew elected to continue the flight to CYLW and landed safely with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance found the #1 propeller filler plug assembly on the propeller regulator was faulty and caused the loss of the propeller fluid. The propeller filler plug assembly was replaced and function checked serviceable. The operator will file an SDR.UPDATED 04 AUGUST 2022.

D-ELAO, un Piper PA-46-500TP en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) et était au départ de la Piste 16 en montée pour maintenir 5000 pieds. Au même moment, un Boeing 737-436 exploité par Bradley Air Services Limited sous l’indicatif AKT6314 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier, ON (CYOW) à destination de CYFB, et était à environ 10 miles marins au sud de CYFB en circuit d’attente à 7000 pieds. Une perte d’espacement est survenue lorsque D-ELAO a tourné en direction sud et a poursuivi sa montée passé 5000 pieds. Il s’est retrouvé à 200 pieds et à 2,4 miles marins sur le plan horizontal du AKT6314, alors que l’espacement requis était de 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical et 3 nm sur le plan horizontal.

C-GUAC, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300 was conducting flight ACA1037 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Denver Intl. (KDEN), CO.  During Initial approach to KDEN, flight crew received a ''RH Elevator fail caution message''.  Flight crew completed checklist and landed without further incident.  Flight crew stated that they had not felt anything unusual with the handling of the aircraft.  Maintenance replaced the Aft remote electronic unit REU4 and released the aircraft back to service.

The Etihad Airways Boeing 787-900 aircraft (registration, A6-BLT, flight ETD 141) was en route from Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates (OMAA) to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to a loss of transponder and communications. The crew of the aircraft communicated with the Montreal ACC, then the Toronto ACC using CPDLC (Controller -Pilot Data Link Communications) and continued to its destination. The aircraft landed uneventfully at CYYZ.

C-FJDQ, un Beech 100 exploité par Max Aviation Inc. sous l’indicatif MAX100, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Trois-Rivières, QC (CYRQ) à destination de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY). C-GEDI, un hélicoptère EC120B privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Val-d’Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de Timmins (Victor M. Power), ON (CYTS). MAX100 était en descente vers CYUY pour atterrir. Le pilote de C-GEDI a contacté la station d’information de vol de Rouyn alors qu’il était en palier à 2800 pieds et 8 milles nautiques au sud-est de l’aéroport. Ce dernier a mentionné être passé à environ 200 pieds latéralement de MAX100 qui était en descente. L’équipage de MAX100 a également signalé au personnel de la FSS qu’ils étaient passé très proche de l’hélicoptère. MAX100 n'était pas équipé d'un système de surveillance du trafic et d'évitement des collisions (TCAS). Il s’est posé sans encombre et C-GEDI a poursuivi son vol.

C-FEXO, a Morningstar Air Inc. Cessna C208, operating as flight MAL7095, was on an IFR flight from Toronto Lester B Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) Ontario, to North Bay Jack Garland Airport (CYYB) Ontario. Shortly after departure, at 16:37 EDT, the pilot declared PAN PAN due to a fuel indication issue and requested a return to CYYZ. The aircraft landed without further incident.   The aircraft had a fuel quantity indicator snag that was being worked on the morning before its departure. A maintenance action was done, the aircraft was run up, and it appeared to be fixed. The gauges showed a fuel amount of 1000 pounds, which was the required amount for the flight. Around 30 minutes into the flight, the fuel gauges started to move simultaneously slightly low. The pilot assessed that he had more than enough fuel to fly the remaining minutes to the original destination (CYYB). The fuel gauges continued to show lower amounts, so the pilot changed the destination to Toronto. When the fuel indicator looked critically low, he declared an emergency.

C-FGZO, a McDonnell Douglas A-4N aircraft operated by Top Aces Inc., was conducting a local flight from Nordholz Air Base (ETMN), Germany. After two hours of flying, the generator failed and no reset was possible. The emergency generator (RAT) was deployed, the pilot declared an emergency and a return to ETMN was completed uneventfully. Maintenance found a faulty converter as the cause of the generator failure.

C-GSHD, a Skyline Helicopters Ltd. Agusta AW119 MK II (Koala), was conducting bucketing operations in support of wildfire management (wildfire MWF052) in the vicinity of Birch Mountains, Alberta. The pilot departed the fire area and was proceeding to refuel at Birch Mountain when he observed that the "Cargo Open Hook" caution light had illuminated. The collective load release switch was guarded and the manual floor release was fully down. The pilot started slowing down and that is when the external load (Bambi Bucket and longline) departed the helicopter. The pilot diverted to Ft. McMurray to assess the issue.Company maintenance observed that a crimp on the manual cable release had failed. The cable was removed and a serviceable unit installed and the helicopter was returned to service.

C-FYJD, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight BY1473/TOM2GC from Arrecife Canary Islands/ Lanzarote Airport (GCRR), Spain to Belfast/Aldergrove Intl. (EGAA), Ireland.  During cruise, flight crew received a ''using fuel reserve'' on Flight management computer (FMC) which indicates forecast to arrive at destination with insufficient fuel for planned alternate if need be.  Flight crew discussed the matter with dispatch and approximately 115nm NNW of Porto/ Francisco de Sá Carneiro Airport (LPPR) Portugal, decided to divert to LPPR for fuel.  After refueling in LPPR, flight proceeded to EGAA without further incident.  Company SMS investigation is in progress.

C-FBQJ, un LeVitation 4 sur flotteurs (constructeur amateur), effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le lac Lesage près de Nominingue, QC avec un pilote et 3 passagers à bord. Le pilote a effectué une approche au-dessus du lac Nominingue, QC en direction sud pour y effectuer un posé-décollé dans la baie de Bellerive (partie sud-est du lac). Lors de son survol de reconnaissance, le pilote remarque que l’eau est miroitante dans la baie et décide d’effectuer le posé-décollé plus au nord, là où il y a des ondulations visibles à la surface de l’eau. En approche à 70 miles à l’heure, l’aéronef a soudainement percuté l’eau et a basculé vers l’avant et s’est inversé. Le flotteur de gauche s’est brisé, le pare-brise et l’aile droite ont été arrachés sous la force de l’impact. Les 4 occupants portaient tous une veste de flottaison individuelle et ont pu évacuer l’aéronef par la porte de gauche. Une des barres de soutien de l’aile droite bloquait l’ouverture de la porte du même côté. Les vestes de flottaison du pilote et de la passagère avant ne se sont pas gonflées lorsque les ficelles ont été tirées. Malgré qu’il ait subi de graves blessures, le pilote ainsi que les 3 passagers ont nagé environ 15 minutes vers la rive la plus proche avant que des personnes dans une chaloupe vienne à leur rencontre pour leur porter secours.

C-GKRS, an Expedition Helicopters Inc. Bell 206L was slinging an inflatable Zodiac with an outboard motor on a 100 foot longline. The load was released without the pilot activating the release system and was dropped into the forest below. The operator suspects a mechanical failure of the hook or the roll-out ring that attaches the load to the hook. The load was located and removed in its entirety from the forest.

C-GSAO, a Beech 95-B55 aircraft operated by Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency, was conducting birddog flight BD154 from Buffalo Narrows (CYVT), SK. During the approach to CYVT, the aircraft landing gear would not extend. The flight crew conducted an emergency landing gear extension procedure, declared an emergency, and diverted to La Ronge (CYVC), SK. The aircraft landed safely and without incident.The operator's maintenance discovered the landing gear "gear down microswitch" was stuck. The switch was cleaned and tested, and the gear was cycled as per Aircraft Maintenance Manual. No additional faults were found and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTRJ, un Maranda S-14D sur flotteurs (constructeur amateur), effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le lac Ouareau à St-Donat, QC avec le pilote seul à bord. Une fois amerrit, le pilote a manœuvré l’aéronef pour se diriger vers la descente de bateau. L’aile gauche s’est soudainement levée et le pilote a réagi afin de ramener les ailes à plat. L’aile gauche s’est soulevée à nouveau sans que le pilote ait pu empêcher l’aéronef de basculer et de chavirer. Il a pu s’extraire de la cabine de pilotage et a nagé jusqu’à la rive. Il a subi des blessures mineures et a été récupéré par les premiers répondants avec l'aide d'une embarcation.

C-ITUK, a Chinook Plus 2 ultralight aircraft was landing on Runway 31 at Kincardine Municipal Airport (CYKM), ON; as the pilot adjusted engine power for the landing, the engine (HQS-700E) quit. The pilot lost control of the aircraft and it veered off the runway and crashed into a field adjacent to the runway. The pilot was not injured but the aircraft was substantially damaged. The pilot reported that the engine power loss was likely due to fuel starvation but did not find the cause of the fuel starvation. The pilot reported full fuel tanks prior to the half hour flight.

N815NW, an Airbus A330 operated by Delta Airlines, was conducting flight DAL 115 from Paris/Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France to Minneapolis-Saint Paul Intl (KMSP), US.  While enroute (255 nm W  of Whale Cove (CYXN), NU), the flight crew observed a cabin pressure indication and subsequently initiated an emergency descent to 12 000 feet ASL. The flight crew declared an emergency and elected to continue to KMSP. The aircraft landed without further incident. There were no injuries. The operator's maintenance replaced two damaged left pack duct boots and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJJF, un Beechcraft A100 exploité par Propair Inc. sous l’indicatif PRO4215, effectuait un vol d’évacuation sanitaire selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Kuujjuarapik, Québec (CYGW) à destination de Val d’Or, QC (CYVO). Durant la montée initiale, le pilote non volant (PNF) a senti une odeur de fumée. Peu de temps après avoir passé l’altitude de 1000 pieds, l’équipage et l’infirmière observent la présence de fumée dans la cabine et le poste de pilotage. L’équipage a décidé de poursuivre la montée jusqu’à 3000 pieds et de déclarer une urgence à l’unité de contrôle aérien pour revenir se poser à CYGW. La cabine a été dépressurisée ce qui a dissipé la fumée à bord de l’avion qui s’est posé sans encombre à CYGW. Aucun des occupants n’a été incommodé par la fumée. L’inspection de l’avion par le service de maintenance a découvert une légère odeur de brûlé émanant d’un des moteurs qui actionne les volets et il a été remplacé.

C-GJZS, a Jazz Aviation LP MHI RJ Aviation ULC CRJ 900, was conducting flight JZA647 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), CA.  During cruise approximately 200NM SSE of Portland Intl (KPDX), OR, flight crew became incapacitated.  Flight crew declared an emergency and continued to destination without further incident.

C-GOQZ, un Bellanca Citabria privé équipé de flotteurs, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Trois-Rivière (CYRQ), QC à destination d'un quai situé sur la rivière St-Maurice à Shawignigan. Durant un survol du lieu d'ammerrissage, l'aéronef a percuté le fil conducteur le plus bas d'une ligne de transport d'électricité qui traversait la rivière. Suite à l'impact, l'aéronef a percuté la rivière en position inversée. Le pilote a subi des blessures mortelles. L'appareil a été détruit.

C-GHKR, un Airbus 330-343 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA70, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Genève-Cointrin, Suisse (LSGG). Peu de temps après le décollage, l’équipage a remarqué un problème avec le transfert de carburant d’un réservoir à un autre et a décidé de retourner à CYUL. En raison du poids de l’aéronef, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence au service de contrôle aérien afin d’obtenir une inspection des freins sur la piste après l’atterrissage. L’aéronef a atterri sans encombre sur la piste 24R et a quitté la piste après l'inspection.

C-GIUB, an Air Canada A321-200 was conducting flight AC122 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON when at FL330 25nm north of DIK VOR the aircraft encountered moderate turbulence and requested a lower flight level. During the descent at FL310 the turbulence increased and the crew declared Severe turbulence with ATC. The aircraft continued descent to FL250. One crew member received minor injury during the event and the passenger seatbelt sign was illuminated. The aircraft landed safely in CYYZ.

C-FELO, a Thrush S2R-T34, operated by Provincial Airways, was conducting an aerial application flight near Glenavon, SK, located 15 miles south west of Grenfell (CKU6), SK. While applying chemical onto a canola field, the aircraft’s vertical fin struck a powerline. The pilot then carried out a hard landing straight ahead and the aircraft came to a stop in an upright position. The pilot was not injured and the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GIYV, a Tyax Air Service Limited, float-equipped De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC2 (Beaver), was conducting a flight from Tyaughton Lake, BC, to Lorna Lake, BC, with 1 pilot and 5 passengers on board. During cruise, the pilot attempted a course reversal in a valley and the aircraft collided with terrain. The pilot and 2 passengers received serious injuries and 3 passengers received minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter (ELT) activated but SAR efforts were delayed by approximately 3 hours due to low ceilings near the accident site.

C-GCJF, a Cessna A185F, was conducting a local post-maintenance test flight from the Olds-Didsbury (CEA3), AB airport with 1 pilot on board. Shortly after take-off the engine (TELEDYNE CONTINENTAL, IO-520-D) sufferred a catastrophic failure. The pilot conducted a forced approach and during the touchdown the aircraft sustained substantial damage and the pilot a serious injury. The 406 MHz ELT activated and there was no post-impact fire.A post accident inspection revealed that a portion of the oil filter gasket had moved out of position and a significant amount of engine oil had vacated onto the ramp during the start, taxi and runup.

C-FEJP,  a Jazz Aviation LP Embraer ERJ 170-200, (flight 8966,) was at FL290 when the flight crew received a "PRK BRK NOT RELEASED" EICAS message. The QRH procedures were followed but the issues were not resolved. The crew decided to continue the flight to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC and advised Toronto Centre they would be declaring an emergency prior to landing. On arrival, an emergency was declared, and the aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. Troubleshooting by the maintenance department resulted in the Emergency Parking Brake Accumulator #1 Transducer being replaced IAW AMM 32-44-17-400-801. Subsequent testing revealed no further faults.

C-GFDU, un Airbus 320 exploité par Air Canada Rouge effectuait le vol RV1791 depuis s'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ). Au décollage de CYQB, l'équipage a rapporté une possible collision avec une volée d'oiseaux lors de la rotation. Aucune anomalie ayant été notée, l'équipage a poursuivie la montée vers son altitude de croisière. Une fois en palier, l'équipage a reçu le message ECAM (moniteur électronique centralisé de bord) “Cabin Altitude” indiquant une diminution rapide de la pressurisation de la cabine. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence (Pan Pan) et a effectué une descente d'urgence pour une altitude de 10 000 pieds. Une fois en palier à 10 000 pieds, et après avoir évalué la situation, l'équipage a poursuivie son vol vers CYYZ. L'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre.

C-FSDB, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 completed flight AC991 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Mexico City International Airport (MMMX), Mexico and was taxing to the gate when the aircraft struck a portable air stairs, which was not entirely in the safe zone. The flight crew followed the lead in line and the aircraft had wing walkers. The crew was unaware of the strike until they deplaned the aircraft. The stairs caused damage to the leading edge of the right hand lower winglet (Sharklet).The aircraft was taken offline for Maintenance to review the damage and discuss the options for repair or MEL.

C-GEKZ, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 conducting flight AC1072 from Denver International Airport (KDEN), CO to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC was climbing to cruise altitude when, around 38,000', the flight crew heard a loud crack noise. They determined that the #3 window on the FO side had a crack in it. The aircraft descended down to 9,000', declared a PAN PAN and diverted to Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport (KMSP), MN. The crew reported that the cabin pressure was maintained the entire time and the masks did not deploy. The aircraft landed in KMSP without further incident.

C-FSNQ, an Air Canada B737-8 conducting flight AC759 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA was on approach to KSFO when the crew received a TCAS RA, no maneuvering required, they continued the approach and landed without incident.

C-FRSE, a Boeing 787-900 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA845 from Frankfurt, Germany to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) with 281 passengers and 11 crew members on board. While on approach to CYUL, when Flap 2 setting was selected, the crew received a Flat/Slat primary message. The crew declared an emergency (PAN PAN) and continued with the approach. When gear down was selected, the crew received a Centre Hydraulic message. The aircraft landed and stopped on Runway 24R and an inspection found hydraulic fluid on the aft belly of the aircraft. The crew taxied to the gate with no further issue.

C-FUAM, un Pilatus PC-12/47E exploité par Airmedic Inc. sous l’indicatif AM366, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'Aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda (CYUY), QC vers l'Aéroport de Montréal Saint-Hubert Longueuil (CYHU), QC. Lorsque le train d'atterrissage a été sélectionné en position sortie, l’équipage a reçu une indication anormale de position du train. Une urgence a été déclarée et l’équipage a effectué un survol de la piste afin de confirmer la position du train avec le contrôleur de la tour. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-IILH, a Zlin Aviation Savage advanced ultralight, was conducting a local sight-seeing flight from the pilot’s farm, approximately 7 nm SE of the Olds-Didsbury, AB airport (CEA3), with one passenger on board. At approximately 1015 MDT, 45 minutes after take-off, the aircraft collided with terrain 0.7 NM south of the farm strip. By 1530, the family began to search for the aircraft as it should have returned by then. A neighbor assisted in the search by conducting an aerial search with their aircraft. The accident aircraft was located during the aerial search at approximately 1645. Emergency services were on scene by 1700 and found both occupants deceased. The aircraft was not equipped with an ELT nor was it required by regulation.

On 12 July 2022, the Morningstar Air Express Inc. Boeing 757 (registration C-FMAI, serial 27199) departed Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), British Columbia enroute to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), Alberta for a cargo flight with 2 pilots onboard. During the arrival procedure at CYYC, the Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) displayed a trailing edge flap disagree ("TE FLAP DISAGREE") message when the flap selector was moved to the "Flaps 1" detent position. The flight crew carried out the appropriate checklist procedure and declared a PAN emergency. Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) personnel were notified. The aircraft landed on Runway 17L at CYYC at 0730 MDT. After landing, ARFF personnel inspected the aircraft's trailing edge flaps. No damage was noted and the aircraft taxied in from the runway. There were no injuries.

A United Airlines Inc. (UAL) Boeing 737-900ER, operating as flight UAL750 departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), Alberta en route to Houston International Airport (KIAH), Texas. This was the second attempt to complete the flight. The first attempt (see A22W0054) resulted in the aircraft returning to CYYC due to a #2 engine (CFM56-7B26/E) overheat indication. UAL750 departed Calgary a second time at 1813 MDT. As the aircraft climbed through 13 000 feet above sea level, at 1840 MDT, the #2 engine overheat caution light illuminated as it did during the previous flight. The flight crew completed the appropriate checklist procedure and reduced the #2 throttle to idle. The #2 engine overheat caution light extinguished. There was no engine gas temperature (EGT) exceedance. The flight crew declared an emergency (MAYDAY) and returned to CYYC. The aircraft landed at 1901 and taxied back to the gate without further incident.Maintenance follow up: During troubleshooting, high power runs following the second Air Return found faults with both loop A and loop B. Maintenance then replaced all #2 engine fire loops and engine core harnesses. The engine/APU fire detection module was replaced. An engine fire test and engine high power run was performed with no failures and aircraft was returned to service.

A United Airlines Inc. (UAL) Boeing 737-900ER, operating as flight UAL750, departed Calgary International Airport (CYYC), Alberta enroute to Houston International Airport (KIAH), Texas. At 1548 mountain daylight time (MDT), while climbing through 20 000 feet above sea level (ASL), the #2 engine (CFM56-7B26/E) overheat caution light illuminated. The flight crew completed the appropriate checklist procedure and reduced the #2 throttle to idle. The #2 engine overheat caution light extinguished. There was no engine gas temperature (EGT) exceedance. The flight crew declared an emergency (MAYDAY) and returned to CYYC. The aircraft landed at 1629 MDT and taxied back to the gate.After landing, maintenance performed a BITE test of the engine/APU fire detection control module, and found the #2 engine loop A faulty, but loop B was found with no faults. The #2 engine loop A was placed on MEL 2602B. See also - A22W0055 - subsequent event on same aircraft.

C-FOBO, a Robinson R44 helicopter operated by Hanley Heli Service, was conducting an aerial application flight near Bradwell Saskatchewan, MB. The helicopter departed from a road to spray an adjacent wheat field, loaded with 30 gallons of chemical. During the initial application pass, in a westerly direction, the helicopter struck a powerline and the pilot conducted a hard landing straight ahead. The pilot was not injured; however, the helicopter sustained substantial damage.

C-FHPD, a privately owned Van's RV-6 was landing on a private grass runway 3 nautical miles west of Paris, ON, lined on both sides by corn that was approximately 4 feet high. After touchdown, the aircraft's right wing contacted the corn on the right side and the aircraft ground looped and came to stop. The two occupants on board were not injured, but the aircraft received substantial damage to the left wing, propeller and left main landing gear. The ELT was automatically activated and JRCC responded to the scene. The wind was calm at the time of the accident.

C-FEKH, a Jazz Embraer 175 aircraft conducting flight JZA984 from Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to LaGuardia Airport (KLGA), NY was operating with one pack unserviceable which restricts the aircraft to 25 000 feet.  The crew lost their second pack and descended down to 10 000 feet as it had to fly unpressurized. The crew declared Pan Pan but did not do an emergency descent. The aircraft landed safely at KLGA.

C-FTXD, a Kitfox IV-1200 equipped with a tail wheel, was conducting a high speed taxi test at Shupe Field, a private unregistered grass strip approximately 16nm ESE of Saugeen Municipal Airport (CYHS), Ontario, with the pilot as the sole occupant. While taxiing at speed taxi in gusty crosswind conditions, control was lost, and the aircraft departed the runway into an area of long grass; both main landing gear failed, resulting in a prop strike. The pilot exited the aircraft and was uninjured.

C-FQPH, an amateur built Denney Kitfox IV equipped with tundra tires and conventional landing gear, was flying from Plattsville Airport/Lubitz Flying Field (CLB2), Ontario to Kincardine Airport (CYKM), Ontario, with the pilot being the sole occupant. During touchdown on runway 13 at CYKM with the wind calm, control was lost and the aircraft began to ground loop. An attempt was made to go-around, but the aircraft was already out of control. The aircraft came to rest in a field near the runway, where the pilot exited the aircraft with minor injuries. The aircraft was destroyed.

C-FFND, an amateur built, Champion L16 Replica (MS-L16A), was landing on a private runway near Mooretown, Ontario. During the approach, the pilot encountered gusty wind conditions, and had difficulty keeping the aircraft on the approach centerline. After touchdown, control of the aircraft was lost and the right main wheel went off the runway edge, into the soft dirt, causing the aircraft to ground loop. The aircraft sustained substantial damage; there were no injuries.

C-GLQB, a Porter Airlines Inc. DHC-8-402, was conducting flight POE246 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), Ontario to Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), Ontario, with 4 crew and 67 passengers on board. While climbing through 16000 feet approximately 20nm north of Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, the flight crew heard a popping noise and detected an electrical odour.  After actioning the appropriate checklist, the flight crew elected to divert to CYYZ, where they landed uneventfully. Although they did not declare an emergency, the aircraft was stopped on the taxiway and a rapid deplanement was completed with ARFF standing by. Maintenance determined that the #1 Air Cycle Machine had failed. The #1 Air Cycle Machine was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GITP an Airbus A319, operated by Air Canada Rouge (flight 1505), departed Greater Moncton Roméo LeBlanc International Airport (CYQM), NB   destined for Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While enroute the flight crew experienced a failure of some navigation equipment. A PAN PAN was declared the aircraft continued to CYYZ, where it landed without further incident.

C-FSOC, a Boeing 737-800, operated by Air Canada (flight 173) was preparing for pushback from a gate at Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON when a catering truck struck the left-hand lower winglet. The passengers were deplaned and the aircraft was removed from service for maintenance.

C-GJZA, a Bombardier Inc., DHC-8-402, operated by Jazz Aviation LP (flight 7958) departed Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ) destined for Montréal–Trudeau International Airport (CYUL). After departure the flight crew received an indication that a main landing gear door remained open. ATC was advised to have emergency equipment on standby as a precaution, in the event that an alternate gear extension was required. The flight crew actioned the QRH and elected to continue to CYUL where they performed an alternate gear extension as per the QRH.  The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FRQN, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU, operated by Jazz Aviation LP (flight 8543) departed Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), destined for the Regina International Airport (CYQR). When the aircraft was approximately 100 miles east of Thunder Bay, Ontario, the captain became ill. The aircraft returned to CYUL and EMS were requested to meet the flight. The aircraft landed without further incident.

N181DN, a Boeing B767-332 aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL211 from Prague-Václav Havel Intl (LKPR), Czech Republic to New York-John F. Kennedy Intl (KJFK), NY. When in cruise flight at about 56°35' N, 038°48' W, the flight crew was alerted to a flooding issue in the mid-cabin lavatories, followed shortly after with information that the forward left lavatory was also flooding. A short time after the flooding issue was discovered, the autopilot disconnected. The flight crew attempted to connect all 3 autopilot systems, but none would remain connected. The aircraft began to drift direction to the right, and correction to the left could not be made. The flight crew contacted company dispatch and maintenance control and completed the quick reference handbook (QRH) for a jammed flight controls state. The flight crew declared an emergency with Canadian air traffic services (ATS), began a descent and coordinated with ATS for a diversion to Goose Bay (CYYR), NL. At about 100 nm east of CYYR, while at an altitude of 12 000 feet, the aircraft flight control function returned to normal operation. The flight crew terminated the emergency and coordinated a diversion to Boston-Logan Intl (KBOS), MA. While enroute to KBOS at 11 000 feet a recalculation of fuel determined that the flight could continue to KJFK, where a landing was made without further incident.Maintenance personnel replaced both grey water drain masts, and replaced a seal in the left wheel well canted pressure deck above the aileron feel centering and trim mechanism. The entire roll control and related autopilot systems were inspected and repairs effected as required.

C-GHCE, a privately registered Hrycay Consulting Engineers Cessna 421C, was conducting a flight from Moberly/Omar N Bradley Airport (KMBY), MO to Winner Regional, Winner (KICR), SD. When over Jackson Township, MO (39.972N 93.293W) the right engine had a complete loss of power. The engine was secured and the flight diverted to Kirksville Regional Airport (KIRK), MO and landed without further incident.

C-GTBH, a privately registered amateur-built Thorp T-18 was conducting a local flight from Disley (CDS2), SK. On departure from the grass runway, a wheel caught the soft ground adjacent to the runway and the aircraft veered to the left. The aircraft departed the maintained portion of the grass runway and got airborne momentarily after passing through a small ditch. The aircraft bounced and, on touchdown, it nosed over in a nearby field coming to a stop inverted. The pilot sustained minor injuries and the passenger was uninjured. The aircraft was destroyed.

C-GVMP, an Aurora Jet Partners Hawker 900XP, was conducting a flight from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to King County International Airport (KBFI) Seattle, WA. Approaching KBFI, the aircraft was cleared to maintain 2200 feet until established final on the ILS runway 14. After levelling at 2200 feet, and prior to intercepting the glide slope, the crew received a TCAS RA with instruction to descend. The aircraft descended to approximately 2000’, cleared traffic, advised ATC and returned to the assigned altitude.

C-GVMP, a Aurora Jet Partners Hawker 900XP, was conducting a flight from King County International Airport (KBFI) Seattle, WA to Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. The airplane departed from RWY 32 with an assigned level off altitude of 1600’ as per the SID. While climbing through 1000 feet, the crew received an TCAS RA instructing to climb. The climb rate was increased, and the aircraft was able to level out at the assigned altitude and was clear of traffic.

C-GVDP, an Air Canada A220-300, was conducting flight AC759 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA. The flight crew received a TCAS RA on final into KSFO. The aircraft landed safely at KSFO.

C-GMIW, an Air Canada B737 MAX 8 was conducting flight AC759 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA when the crew received a TCAS RA on approach to KSFO RWY 28R, the aircraft did a go around and landed RWY 28L safely.

C-GTCY, an Air Transat A321-211, conducting flight TSC566 from Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Abel Santamaría International Airport (MUSC), Santa Clara , Cuba. Due to a passenger medical emergency onboard, a pan pan was declared by the Flight Crew in order to get priority for approach and landing. The aircraft landed normally with no further incident, taxied to its parking position where the passenger was met by medical staff.

C-GHJW, a Helijet International Incorporated Sikorsky S-76A, was conducting flight JBA916 under visual flight rules (VFR) from Nanaimo Harbour heliport (CDH5), BC, to Vancouver Harbour heliport (CBC7), BC, with 2 crew and 7 passengers on board. While in the initial climb through 500 feet above sea level, in the vicinity of Duke Point (1NM east of CDH5), the crew saw an opposite direction floatplane directly in front of them at the same altitude. The helicopter abruptly turned left to avoid the floatplane. CDH5 and the Nanaimo Harbour water aerodrome (CAC8), BC, use the same aerodrome traffic frequency but the helicopter crew had heard no radio transmissions from the floatplane. As the helicopter passed behind the floatplane, the crew made another radio call to which the floatplane replied that they had the helicopter in sight.The helicopter continued to CBC7 without further incident.

C-GGOJ, an Acro Sport II aircraft, landed at Fergus Juergensen Field (CPG7), ON with a 10-15 knot 90 degree crosswind. During the landing roll the aircraft began to weathercock, the pilot was unable to maintain control and the aircraft exited the right side of the runway into a wheat field. The right wing contacted the wheat spinning the aircraft and collapsing the left main gear. The left lower wing separated from aircraft and the fuselage broke near the lower left wing attachment. There were also indications of a possible prop strike. The pilot was not injured.

United Airlines flight UAL643, a Boeing 737-824 (registration N27205), on a flight from San Francisco, CA, USA (KSFO) to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport, ON (CYYZ) initiated a missed approach to Runway 23. After troubleshooting, the flight crew declared an emergency due to a flap asymmetry issue. ARFF were on standby for uneventful landing.

C-GNDQ, a Cessna 210-5 (205), operated by Niagara Skydive Centre Inc., was on a local flight with parachutists on board. The aircraft had just started a descent, after the parachutist's had jumped, when the engine (Teledyne Continental, IO-470-S) started to run rough and had a partial loss of power. The pilot declared an emergency and continued the descent to the airport. At approximately 7000 feet AGL the engine returned to normal operation. The aircraft landed without further incident.A post flight maintenance inspection found the shaft to the alternate air flapper valve had failed, reducing airflow to the engine. The shaft was replaced, a test flight was flown and the engine operated normally.

C-GUZN, un Cessna U206G privé, effectuait un vol  selon les règles de vol à vue, au départ de la rivière Sakami, QC à destination du lac Guyer. QC avec seul le pilote à son bord. Après avoir débarqué un passager dans un camp de chasse situé sur la rivière Sakami, l'aéronef a amorcé son décollage sur la rivière Sakami. Lors de la course au décollage, l'aéronef a heurté un banc de sable et s'est reversé sur le dos, dans l'eau, près de la rive. Le pilote a été légèrement blessé. Le passager est aller assister le pilote, et ceux-ci ont alors activé la radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT), alertant ainsi le centre conjoint de coordination des opérations de sauvetage (JRCC) de Trenton, ON, qui ont dépêché une équipe pour les secourirs et les transporter à l'aéroport de Val-D'Or, QC où ils ont étés pris en charge.

C-FYAI, un Dash-8-300 exploité par Air Inuit, s'apprêtait à effectuer le vol AIE861 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de l'aéroport de Port-Menier, QC (CYPN) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 41 passagers à bord. Lors du démarrage du moteur gauche, le voyant "#1 DC GEN HOT" s'est illuminé et le moteur à été fermé. Un membre du personnel au sol a signalé à l'équipage que de la fumée s'échappait du moteur gauche. Le commandant a alors ordonné l'évacuation de l'aéronef par les sorties situées sur le côté droit. Des membres du personnel au sol ont aidé à l'évacuation et les services d'urgence ont été appellés. Trois passagers on subi des éraflures légères lors de l'évacuation.

C-GGWX a Nolinor Aviation B737-400 conducting flight NRL951 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Frank País Airport (MUHG) Holguin, Cuba. The pilot declared an emergency with ATC and diverted to Jacksonville (KAJX), FL, after receiving an indication of  fire in the AFT cargo compartment. The indication was received 2 hours 30 minutes after departure while cruising approximately 200 NM east of KJAX. The crew followed company procedures and performed a safe landing on RWY 8. Once clear of the runway the emergency services inspected the aircraft and found no sign of fire. The aircraft was cleared to taxi to gate C5 where the emergency services were on standby until the passengers were all deplaned. The emergency services then inspected all the luggage of the cargo compartment to ensure there was no fire.The aircraft was then inspected by the flight engineer (ACA) and a maintenance release was signed. Considering two fire suppression halon bottles were discharged, the aircraft was released under MEL and ferried back to CYMX for further investigation of the fire detection system.

C-FSNZ, a privately registered Robinson R44 helicopter, was conducting a local flight at Abbotsford (CYXX), BC, with 2 pilots on board. The flight was operated under BC Heli rentals with the purpose of the Pilot-in-Command, acting as a Safety Pilot, to assess the ability of the other pilot and determine if they would be permitted to rent the owner’s helicopter. The helicopter was cleared by air traffic control (ATC) to perform circuits in the infield at CYXX. As the helicopter slowed for landing, it began to yaw to the right. Inputs by the crew did not arrest the yaw. ATC observed the helicopter on the ground, on its side. The two pilots egressed without assistance and ATC initiated the dispatch of aircraft fire and rescue crews and called for emergency services. The pilots were transported to the local hospital with minor injuries for observation. The helicopter was substantially damaged. It was removed to be stored at a local aircraft maintenance facility where a damage assessment will be conducted.

C-IVCT, un ultra-léger avancé fabriqué par Flight Design (modèle CTSW) opéré par Aviation Rou-Air, effectuait un vol local de familiarisation depuis l'aérodrome de Sainte-Hyacinthe, QC (CSU3) selon les règles de vol à vue, avec un instructeur et un élève-pilote à bord.Lors de l'atterissage, l'aéronef a décroché alors qu'il se trouvait à une dizaine de pieds au-dessus du sol, à proximité du seuil de la piste. L'aéronef a ensuite effectué un rebond sur la piste avant de terminer sa course sur le dos en bordure de piste. L'aéronef a subi des dommages majeurs. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.Amendé le 08 juillet 2022

C-GWEP, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Dash 8-400, operated by WestJet Encore was conducting flight WEN3147 from Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC) to Fort McMurry, AB (CYMM) with 4 crew members and 33 passengers on board. During the initial take-off roll in CYYC, the flight crew observed multiple birds on the runway. The flight crew rejected the take-off and declared a MAYDAY with air traffic control. Airport rescue and fire fighting was dispatched and completed an external inspection of the aircraft as a precaution. No abnormalities were observed and the flight crew received a revised take-off clearance. The flight subsequently departed CYYC and continued to the intended destination.

C-GDDJ, a Wilderness Seaplanes Grumman G21A (Goose) was conducting a passenger flight from Port Hardy (CYZT), BC, to the Wuikinuxv airstrip (60 nautical miles north of CYZT) with the pilot and 4 passengers on board. After touchdown at Wuikinuxv, when the tailwheel was lowered, the plan began to drift to the left. The pilot took corrective action but was unable to remain on the centerline and the plane veered into the soft shoulder as it slowed down. The passengers and the pilot disembarked from the aircraft without injury.Company maintenance were dispatched to inspect the aircraft and determined that the only damage was some scratches on the keel. The plane was recovered to the hard surface of the airstrip and returned to service.

C-GHXS, a Cessna 172M aircraft was on a pleasure trip from Gimli (CYGM), MB to Little Grand Rapids (CZGR), MB with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. During landing roll on RWY 36 at CZGR, the pilot lost directional control of the aircraft and veered off the right side of the runway into a ditch. The aircraft came to a stop in an upright position. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the right wing and propeller. The aircraft did not strike any runway lights.

C-GXRW, a Boeing 737-800 operated by Swoop Inc., was conducting flight WSW264 from Edmonton Intl., AB (CYEG) to Hamilton Intl., ON (CYHM) with 6 crew members and 157 passengers on board. During the take-off roll, the #1 main tire blew. After departure, the landing gear retracted normally. The flight crew felt a vibration and were subsequently advised by air traffic control that the tower witnessed the #1 tire blow, and debris was found on the runway. The flight crew then completed the QRH procedure, and the aircraft entered a hold for approximately 2 hours north east of the airport to burn off fuel before returning to CYEG. A PAN PAN was declared with air traffic service, and an uneventful landing was performed with airport rescue and fire fighting in attendance. The aircraft taxied to the gate without further incident.

C-FPBJ, a Viking DHC-7 operated by Air Tindi was conducting flight TIN806 from Bathurst Inlet, NU (CJN6) to Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) with 3 crew members on board. Approximately 50 nm N of CYZF the flight crew observed the #3 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-50) experience an uncommanded power roll back to idle. The flight crew elected to perform an intentional inflight shutdown of the #3 engine, and an uneventful landing was completed in CYZF.

C-FMAS, a De Havilland DHC2-MK1 aircraft, operated by Kississing Lake Lodge Ltd. was enroute from Kasba Lake (CJL8) NWT to Flin Flon (CYFO) MB with only the pilot on board. While in cruise, the engine (P&W R985) oil pressure dropped to 0 PSI. The pilot performed a precautionary shutdown of the engine and then completed a successful forced landing on a nearby lake (Reindeer Lake, SK). After landing, the pilot contacted the base using a satellite phone and informed them of his situation.

C-FDGA, an Aerospatiale AS350-B3 operated by Blackcomb Helicopters was conducting slinging operations on behalf of the Alberta Forestry service approximately 20 nm SW of Springbank, AB (CYBW) with only the pilot on board. The helicopter picked up a loaded propane tank on a long line from the staging area, and planned to deliver it to the Barrier Lake lookout tower facility at the peak of Yates Mountain. As the helicopter made a final approached to the lookout tower, the pilot was unable to arrest the descent of the helicopter, and elected to release the external load. The propane tank dropped approximately 25' into the bush. There were no injuries to any personnel located on the ground, and no damage to the environment or the propane tank.

C-GERX, a Blackcomb Helicopters Limited Partnership Bell 206L-4 (Long Ranger IV) was conducting long line operations near Lillooet (CYLI), BC, with only the pilot on board. The helicopter was slinging a load in a cargo net on 100’ long line with a remote hook. The pilot was adjusting the radios with his left hand when the flight encountered turbulence. As the pilot returned his hand to the collective, the remote hook release, an unguarded 2 position switch located on the far left of the cyclic, was inadvertently activated and the load was dropped in trees. The operator has reported that C-GERX is a leased helicopter and has not been modified to match the rest of the company’s Bell helicopter fleet.

C-GIAW, an Israel 1124A aircraft, operated by Skycare Air Ambulance departed Sioux Lookout (CYXL) ON with a crew of 2 and 2 passengers on board. During the initial climb, the horizontal stab trim became unresponsive and the crew then disconnected the auto-pilot. The crew declared an emergency and decided to return to CYXL where the aircraft landed safely. An inspection of the trim system by company maintenance personnel revealed a defective horizontal stab actuator. The horizontal stab actuator was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service. The operator has filed a service difficulty report with Transport Canada.

C-GFDU, an Air Canada Rouge A320-214 was conducting flight ROU1802 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Norman Manley International Airport (MKJP), Jamaica. Shortly after reaching the initial cruise altitude of 32000ft, the crew received a cabin altitude advisory with the cabin altitude reaching 9150. An emergency descent was initiated and masks were donned. The descent was coordinated with ATC and the cabin was advised of the situation as per company SOP. The crew declared a PAN PAN that was subsequently cancelled after levelling off at 15000ft. After consulting with the company MOC and dispatch, it was decided to return to CYYZ. The aircraft climbed to 21000ft and continued to CYYZ uneventfully.

C-GXHS, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by Missinippi Airways as flight MA05 was landing on RWY 06 in Thompson (CYTH) MB, with a crew of 3 and 1 passenger on board. During the landing roll, the pilot applied the brakes and did not receive any braking action of the left main wheel. The crew managed to slow the aircraft down using propeller reverse and then veered off the right side of the runway. The aircraft then came to a safe stop approximately 10 feet off the side just before the departure end. There were no injuries. The aircraft did not sustain any damage and did not hit any runway lights.

C-FWEW, a De Havilland of Canada DHC-8-400 operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3274 from Edmonton International, AB (CYEG) to John D. Diefenbaker Airport, SK (CYXE) with 4 crew members and 35 passengers on board. Shortly after take-off during landing gear retraction, the flight received a landing gear inop caution light, in addition to amber nose gear indication lights. The flight crew performed the QRH procedures for an abnormal gear condition and elected to return to CYEG. Priority was declared (PAN PAN) and airport rescue and fire fighting was put on alert. An uneventful landing was completed approximately 45 minutes after departure, and ARFF escorted the aircraft back to the gate.

C-FQDW, a privately registered Piper PA-32-300 aircraft was enroute from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG) MB to Regina Intl. (CYQR) SK with the pilot and 3 passengers on board. While in cruise at approximately 4500 feet ASL, the engine (Lycoming IO-540) lost complete power and the pilot conducted a forced landing on a grid road near Kipling (CKD5), SK. During the landing roll, the pilot lost directional control and the aircraft veered off the right side of the road, into a ditch. The aircraft came to a stop in an upright position and all occupants on board were able to evacuate without injury. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GLSI, a Partenavia P68C operated by Integrated Sensing & Surveillance Inc., departed Runway 25 from Deer Lake Airport (CYDF), NL for a local flight. On departure, the pilot detected smoke coming from the windshield heat vent. The pilot advised radio they would be returning for landing on Runway 25. After the aircraft safely landed and was shutdown on the apron, the pilot visually inspected the aircraft and no fire was observed.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and observed a small quantity of spilled engine oil on the exhaust heat shroud below the oil filter. It was determined that oil had spilled during maintenance. The exhaust heat shroud was flushed out in accordance with the maintenance manual. The aircraft was ground run with no further faults found and returned to service.

C-FGKH an Air Canada A320-214 was conducting flight AC702 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to LaGuardia Airport (KLGA), NY when they received a TCAS RA at 1000' 'traffic traffic' alert due to traffic 500' below on final for KLGA. The crew disconnected the autopilot and monitored vertical speed. ATC was advised, and the aircraft landed without further event.

C-GJXE an Air Canada A220 conducting flight AC761 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), CA was on final into KSFO when the crew received a TCAS RA. They had the traffic in sight the whole time, and the aircraft landed safely.

C-FRYP, un Cessna R182 exploité par Grondin Transport, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Havre St-Pierre, QC (CYGV). En circulant pour un départ de la piste 26, le pilote a avisé qu'il retournait au terminal en raison de la présence de fumée à bord. Aucune urgence déclaré, aucun blessé.

C-FAUE, un aéronef de constructeur amateur Commander 285 privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le lac Klemka, QC à destination de l’hydrobase du lac Sébastien, QC (CTD3) avec 1 pilote et 2 passagères à bord. L’aéronef a circulé vers la partie nord-ouest du lac afin d’y effectuer le décollage en direction sud-est. Lors de la course au décollage, l’aéronef n’a pas pris son envol à l’endroit où habituellement les flotteurs se soulèvent de l’eau. Le pilote a tenté de manœuvrer pour soulever le flotteur de droite afin de faciliter le décollage, mais le flotteur de gauche s’est soulevé brusquement. Le pilote a alors réagi pour ramener l’avion à l’horizontale. Ce dernier a pris son envol par la suite sans que le pilote n’ait commandé la manœuvre. Voyant que les distances avec le relief vers l’avant et le côté droit étaient trop courtes pour lui permettre de passer par-dessus, le pilote a effectué un virage vers la gauche. À la suite, le pilote a senti que l’aéronef descendait. Il s’est assuré que la commande de puissance du moteur était réglée à la pleine puissance et a baissé le nez de l’avion pour reprendre plus de vitesse. L’aile gauche s’est brusquement inclinée et l’aéronef ne maintenait plus son altitude. Le pilote a coupé le moteur et l’aéronef est entré en collision avec l’eau. Les 3 personnes à bord ont pu s'extirper et nager jusqu’à la rive la plus proche. Elles ont été secourues par des témoins qui sont allés les récupérer avec un bateau. L'aéronef a couléf. Deux hélicoptères ont été envoyés sur les lieux pour évacuer et transporter les 3 personnes blessées vers un centre hospitalier de Chicoutimi.

C-FGZD a Top Aces MD A4N on a flight from Cuxhaven - Nordholz-Spieka (ETMN), Germany to Rostock–Laage Airport (ETNL), Germany was 30 minutes into the flight when the pilot noticed the engine had a high vibration accompanied by a high pitched sound for about 30 seconds. After reducing power, the high pitched sound went away. Approximately 5 minutes later, the sound returned and remained. The pilot declared an emergency and burnt fuel to achieve landing weight. The aircraft landed in ETNL without further incident.

C-GPDB, a Sunwest Aviation Ltd Learjet 45 was conducting flight CNK678 from Albuquerque Intl. Sunport (KABQ), NM to Abbotsford (CYXX), BC.  During cruise, flight crew initiated a climb from FL430 to FL470.  At FL450, flight crew received a AP AIL MISTRIM CAS warning.  Flight crew suspected frozen control and completed QRH.  Flight crew slowed at Mach 0.78 and manually flown with degraded roll control.  Flight crew reengaged the autopilot but warning came back as autopilot had difficulty tracking.  Flight crew elected to hand fly the aircraft and descended to FL430 where the autopilot was reengaged with success. remaining of the flight was completed with autopilot and controllability check. Weather in KABQ was rainy for the two days prior to the flight, departure was completed during moderate rain and aileron controls were exercised on the ground and on climb out as recommended. Maintenance is troubleshooting.

C-GNLN, a Boeing 737-200 aircraft operated by Nolinor Aviation as flight NRL951, was enroute from Meadowbank (CMB2), NU to Churchill (CYYQ), MB with a crew of 6 and 92 passengers on board. After holding for an incoming medevac flight, NRL951 conducted a missed approach at CYYQ due to weather. The crew then determined they were below reserve fuel required for the alternate and the crew declared an emergency. After consultation with company dispatch and considering an improving weather report in CYYQ, the aircraft returned to CYYQ for an uneventful landing.

C-ILPM, a quad City Challenger 2 Ultralight, was departing from Carp, Ontario (CYRP) for a local flight. After take-off from Runway 10, during the initial climb, the engine (Rotax 503) began to sputter then quit. A forced approach to the field at the end of Runway 10 was conducted. It was reported that the aircraft was flared high, stalled and subsequently landed hard, collapsing the landing gear. There were no reported injuries.

C-FJJH, a Beech A100, operated by Thunder Airlines (flight THU104) departed Timmins/Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON for Moosonee (CYMO), Ontario and was approximately 20 minutes into the flight when the flight crew noted torque fluctuations and a decrease in oil pressure on the left engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6-28). The flight crew shut down the engine as per the checklist, declared an emergency and diverted to Cochrane (CYCN), Ontario. Emergency vehicles were on standby for the uneventful landing.Maintenance found the oil dipstick was not properly secured and there was no damage to the engine.

C-GZOX, a Dassault Falcon 20-F5, operated by Air Nunavut (flight BFF21), departed the Oshawa Executive Airport (CYOO) and was climbing through FL250 when the flight crew noticed smoke coming from the slat/flap controls. The flight crew carried out the emergency checklist, turned off the auxiliary bus and the smoke stopped. The flight crew selected 7700 on the transponder, declared an emergency and returned to CYOO. The aircraft landed without further incident.

N15969, a Boeing 787-9 was conducting United Airlines flight UAL27 from Denver International Airport (KDEN), CO, USA to London Heathrow Airport (EGLL), England, UK with 268 persons on board. At a position approximately 450nm NE of the Goose Bay Airport (CYYR) NL, the flight crew received EICAS heat warnings for the flight attendant crew rest area followed by the bulk cargo area. There was no smoke or fumes detected in either the cabin or the flight deck. The crew declared a Mayday and requested to divert to CYYR. The aircraft landed safely at CYYR at 05:08 UTC. Maintenance conducted tests and determined that the bulk cargo temperature sensor was found covered in lint. The sensor was cleaned and the system tested normal. As well, a smoke detector in the flight attendant rest area did not test properly and was replaced.

N1423P, a privately registered, Piper PA-14 (Family Cruiser), was conducting a 3-day flight from Arlington municipal airport (KAWO), WA, USA, to Dillingham airport (PADL), AK, USA, with only the pilot on board. After refueling in Abbotsford (CYXX), BC, the pilot intended to fly to Quesnel (CYQZ), BC, via the published visual flight rules (VFR) route from Hope, BC. He departed CYXX and climbed to approximately 3300 feet above sea level (ASL) and proceeded along the VFR route north towards Lytton, BC where the route turns east following the Thompson River. Approaching Lytton, the pilot’s iPad, which was being used as a GPS display and an electronic chart, overheated and became unserviceable. At Lytton, the pilot continued north following the Fraser River towards Lillooet (CYLI), BC. Upon recognizing the unintended navigation, the pilot turned east to regain the intended route. There were clouds at the eastern end of the valley into which the pilot turned and, due to rising terrain, the pilot attempted to reverse course. During the reversal, the aircraft struck trees on the northern slope of the valley. The aircraft impacted terrain coming to rest approximately 13 nautical miles southeast of CYLI at approximately 4700 feet ASL. The aircraft sustained substantial damage, and the pilot was seriously injured. There was no flight plan or flight itinerary filed for this flight. No signal from the aircraft's 406MHz emergency locator transmitter (ELT) was received, but the pilot activated a personal locator beacon (PLB) and this signal was received by the Canadian Mission Control Centre initiating the search and rescue response. The pilot was located approximately 5.5 hours after the impact and transported to hospital.

C-GEZD, an Air Transat Airbus A321, was operating as flight TSC865 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Toronto (CYYZ), ON. TSC865 departed CYYC on a standard instrument departure for Runway 35R and utilized Noise Abatement Departure Procedure (NADP) 1; ATC was not aware the flight crew were performing NADP1. Following TSC865 was a WestJet B737-MAX8 C-GXAX, flight WJA234. During the climb, WJA234 was faster than TSC865 and separation reduced to 2.3 NM where 3.0 NM was required. The departure controller regained separation by turning WJA234 to the left.

C-FBWE, a Hiller UH-12E helicopter operated by Western Aerial Applications Ltd., departed Winnipeg City Heliport (CWG2), MB to apply control pellets to a farmers field. While seeding and making a tight turn, the helicopter was unable to maintain altitude and the pilot attempted a forced landing. The pilot made an autorotation at 20 feet above the ground and landed hard; making contact with small tree branches and a pole guy wire. The helicopter sustained substantial damage to its skids. The pilot was not injured and the 406 ELT activated.

C-GAHI, an Airbus AS350-B2 operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited, was conducting a long line external load flight from a refueling facility in the vicinity of the Cartwright Airport (CYCA), NL to a lodge approximately 28nm SW of CYCA. As the aircraft was climbing to cross the rising terrain of Earl Island, strong downdrafts were encountered which caused the aircraft to descend. The external load struck the terrain and the cargo net was torn open. Four fuel drums were released from the cargo net and ruptured, spilling approximately 800 litres of aviation jet fuel onto the ground. The long line and net did not detach from the aircraft and the aircraft safely returned to the refueling facility. Arrangements are currently underway to clean-up the fuel spill.

C-GITY, an Airbus 321 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was standing at the gate prior to departure for flight AC741 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO), USA with 6 crew and 138 passengers onboard. While fueling the aircraft, it was noticed that fuel was flowing out of the left wing NACA duct. The fuel spilled on an area of about 15 meter diameter without affecting the airport drainage system. All passengers and crew were rapidly deplaned into the airport. The airport authority was notified and Airport Rescue and Firefighting services attended and monitored the situation until the clean up was completed. The maintenance department confirmed the aircraft center tank valve was operated manually and approximately 1000 kg of fuel was accepted by the aircraft when the fuel spill was observed from the left wing. The aircraft was removed from service for further investigation.

C-ILIN, a privately registered Walkerjet Simon Plus Paramotor, basic ultralight, was conducting a local flight from Queensville Rollick Airpark (CRA2) in East Gwillimbury, ON with only the pilot onboard. After being airborne for approximately 30 minutes, the pilot encountered unfavorable wind conditions and subsequently loss control of the parachute. The aircraft crashed into grassy field, the pilot landed on his feet first, and then on his shoulder and sustained serious but non life threatening injuries and was transported to the hospital by helicopter.

C-GTLQ, un Pober Pixie P9 de construction amateur, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue à partir de l'aéroport de Joliette, QC (CSG3) avec seul le pilote à bord. Lors du décollage de la piste gazonnée, le pilote a perdu le contrôle et l'aéronef a terminé sa course sur le dos dans les herbes hautes en bordure de piste. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés ni d'incendie. L'aéronef a subi des dommages importants.

C-FHGG, un Beech King Air A100 exploité par Propair Inc., effectuait le vol PRO4215  selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Waskaganish, QC (CYKQ) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 2 passagers à bord. Alors que l'aéronef se trouvait en vol de croisière à une altitude de 11 000 pieds ASL, à environ 40NM au sud-est de Matagami, QC (CYNM), une perte de puissance est survenue en raison de givrage. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et a ensuite descendu à 7 000 pieds ASL. Une fois en palier à 7 000 pieds, l'équipage a annulé l'urgence avec ATC  et a poursuivi sa route vers CYUL, où il a atterri sans encombre.

C-GMHZ, un Piper PA31 Navajo exploité par Les Levés Aeroscan Inc. effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue au départ de l'aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait à environ 9 milles nautiques à l'ouest de CYMT le moteur gauche a cessé de fonctionner. Le pilote a mis l'hélice du moteur affecté en drapeau et a déclaré une urgence. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre et il n'y a pas eu de blessés. Une erreur de gestion des réservoirs d'essence en vol aurait conduit à la panne sèche du moteur gauche.

C-GKUG, un Airbus A330 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA885 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Genève, Suisse (LSGG) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 10 membres d'équipage et 190 passagers à bord. Après avoir effectué un circuit d'attente en rapprochement vers CYUL en raison de météo défavorable, ACA885 a demandé à être ré-acheminé vers l'aéroport Boston Logan International, MA (KBOS). Alors qu'il se dirigeait vers KBOS, ACA885 a été avisé que KBOS n'acceptait plus de déroutements. ACA885 a alors demandé un réacheminement vers l'aéroport d'Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier, ON (CYOW).  Aprés avoir été avisé que CYOW n'acceptait plus de déroutements, ACA885 a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) en raison d'un bas niveau de carburant et l'appareil a atterri sans encombre à CYOW.

C-GGMU, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Q400) operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8323 from Vancouver International, (CYVR), BC, to Comox, (CYQQ), BC, with 4 crew and 60 passengers on board.
