While on final approach into CYQQ, the flight crew selected landing gear down and the left main gear unsafe advisory (red) light remained illuminated indicating that the left gear was not down and locked. The crew discontinued the approach and requested radar vectors from the air traffic controller so that they could complete the necessary checklists. The crew decided to return to CYVR and performed the alternate gear extension procedure. The left main gear alternate down lock verification (green) light on the floor panel did not illuminate, which indicated the left main gear was still not down and locked. The crew declared an emergency and the cabin crew prepared the cabin for an emergency landing. The aircraft landed safely in CYVR with aircraft rescue fire fighting personnel and equipment standing by. Maintenance installed the landing gear lockout pins and the aircraft was towed to the gate. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft. Maintenance conducted an inspection of the landing gears electrical system and found an electrical connector that was contaminated and corroded. The connector was replaced and the landing gear was function tested satisfactorily. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-FFJA, a Jazz Aviation LP, Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (flight 8729), departed Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON and was in the initial climb when both the Captain and First Officer lost all air data computer (ADC) information on the their respective instruments. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and elected to return to CYYZ. A short time later all effected instruments returned to normal operation. The flight crew elected to continue with the return to CYYZ and the aircraft landed without further incident.The left ADC was replaced and the system checked serviceable IAW the applicable manual procedures.

C-FVVR, un Aéropatiale AS350B exploité par Groupe CLR Inc., effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) au départ de l'aéroport de Trois-Rivières, QC (CYRQ), avec 1 pilote et 3 passagers à bord. Lors du décollage, alors que l'hélicoptrère se trouvait à quelques pieds du sol, le pilote a viré l'appareil face au vent et le rotor de queue a percuté un bollard de béton situé sur le tablier. Le pilote a atterri et constaté les dommages au rotor de queue. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé.

C-FCXB, un Aviation Normand Dubé Aerocruiser en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue à partir d'une piste privée située à environ 3.5NM au sud de la ville de Fermont, QC (14 NM au sud-ouest de l'aéroport de Wabush, NL (CYWK)) avec seul le pilote à bord. Lors du décollage, l'aéronef a gagné puis perdu de l'altitude avant de percuter le sol. L'aéronef est ensuite entré en collision avec une voiture abandonnée et a subi des dommages importants. Il n'y a pas eu d'incendie et le pilote a été légèrement blessé.

C-FPCA, an Air Canada Boeing 767-300 was conducting flight AC7214 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to San Juan/Luis Muñoz Marín Intl. (TJSJ) Puerto Rico.  While in New York Oceanic FIR, in HF (High Frequency) and CPDLC (Controller–pilot data link communications) communication range, Flight crew had to deviate around weather on their flight path.  Flight crew declared a PanPan on 121.5 as airspace was busy and deviated without ATC clearance.  Flight crew received clearance shortly thereafter and resumes track to destination without further incident.

C-GBAZ, a privately registered Bellanca 8GCBC aircraft operated by the Air Cadet League of Canada, was landing on the infield grass south of Runway 26 at the Brandon Muni (CYBR), MB airport with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the landing roll, the aircraft ran into a puddle of water, nosed over, and came to rest in an inverted position. The pilot and passenger were able to evacuate the aircraft without injury and were taken to a local hospital for observation, as a precaution. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The DND's Directorate of Flight Safety is investigating.

C-GSXJ, a Dassault Falcon 10 aircraft operated by Air Nunavut Ltd DBA SmoothAir Charter, was conducting flight BFF102, a medevac flight from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. At the same time, C-FGKJ, a Boeing B757-200 aircraft operated by CargoJet Airways Ltd, was conducting flight CJT626 from Greater Moncton Roméo LeBlanc Intl (CYQM), NB to CYHZ. A loss of separation occurred while CJT626 was being vectored for the RNAV Z Runway 05 behind the medevac aircraft and the lateral separation between both aircraft was reduced to 1.9 nm. The required lateral separation limit was 3 nm at the time of the occurrence.

C-FJJA, a privately operated De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-401, was operating as flight DHC4001 from Winnipeg James Armstrong Richardson International (CYWG), MB to Calgary International (CYYC), AB. Shortly after a power reduction for decent into CYYC, the FADEC caution light illuminated. The crew elected to conduct a precautionary engine shutdown of the number 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney PWC 150A). An emergency was declared; the flight landed without further incident.Following the flight, the maintenance team found anomalies with the P2.2 bleed valve and associated wiring harness.

C-FAXD, a Boeing 737 max 8 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines Inc, was conducting flight SWG443 from Punta Cana International Airport (PUJ/MDPC), Dominican Republic to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While on final approach into CYYZ runway 33L, the flight crew received a Traffic and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) resolution advisory (RA) with C-GJVT, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada conducting flight ACA264 from Winnipeg James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (CYWG), MB to CYYZ which was on final approach for runway 33R. SWG443 followed the TCAS RA and aborted the approach to the left. Both aircraft came to a minimum lateral separation of 0.6 Nautical Miles and a minimum vertical separation of 500 feet. SWG443 was at an altitude of 3500 feet and ACA264 at 3000 feet abeam to each other on approach runways 33L and 33R. SWG443 and ACA264 landed without further incident.

C-GKQB, a DHC 8-402 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines Inc, was conducting flight POE483 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON to Montreal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. At approximately midway between CYTZ and CYUL, flight POE483 diverted back to CYTZ as it could not land in CYUL due to the local weather conditions and surrounding airports only accepting a limited number of diverted flights. While on approach into CYTZ runway 26, the crew declared a fuel emergency as CYTZ is restricted to emergencies or medivacs only after 23:00 EDT. POE483 touched down at 23:02 EDT with approximately an hour of fuel remaining. The aircraft taxied to the gate and deplaned without further incident.

C-FTOM, a privately registered Cessna C-560 (Citation Encore+) airplane, was conducting a flight from Vernon (CYVK), BC, to Abbotsford (CYXX), BC, with 2 flight crew and 2 passengers on board. During cruise, approximately 5 minutes before starting the descent into CYXX, the flight crew noticed the battery temperature indicated higher than normal. During the descent, the battery temperature indication was erratic and then jumped to the maximum temperature indication and remained there for the duration of the flight. The master warning and the BATT O'TEMP annunciator did not illuminate. The flight crew consulted the abnormal procedures checklist and did not observe any secondary issues. Priority handling was requested as a precaution and the aircraft landed without further incident. As the aircraft taxied off the runway, the battery temperature had returned to a normal indication. The crew, in consultation with their company’s Director of Maintenance, conducted an inspection. It was determined that it was an indication issue that was resolved and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GAMJ, a privately registered Cessna 340 was conducting a flight from Elmira Corning Regional Airport (KELM), NY, USA to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM, ON. While on approach runway 30, the pilot received an unlocked gear indication and declared an emergency (Pan Pan) with Air Traffic Control (ATC). The pilot subsequently initiated a go around and flew over runway 30. The aircraft came back on approach for runway 30 and landed safely.

C-GJXN, an Airbus 220-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA664 from Montréal/Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. Immediately following departure from CYUL, the flight crew noted indication of low tire pressure. The flight crew discussed the low tire indication with the company maintenance control and operations departments, and decided to continue to destination. Once in radio communication with CYHZ, a PAN PAN was declared and a request to have airport emergency services standing by was made. The flight landed at CYHZ without further incident. Inspection by emergency services did not reveal any damage to landing gear. The aircraft taxied in and deplaned passengers at the gate. Further inspection by company maintenance revealed low tire pressure and tire tread damage consistent with FOD impact. The damaged tire was replaced, and no other damage was found.

N794AN, an American Airlines Boeing 777-223 was operating as AAL67 on a flight from Josep Tarradellas Barcelona/El Prat Airport (LEBL), Spain to John F. Kennedy Intl (KJFK), NY. While in cruise flight at about 46°00' N, 035°00' W, the first officer observed the right-hand windshield shatter. The crew followed the QRH, notified their operations and maintenance departments, declared a PAN PAN, and continued to KJFK where the aircraft landed without incident. Maintenance replaced the R1 windshield.

C-GPCQ, a SAAB SF340A operated by Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited, was conducting flight PCO1609 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Tofino (CYAZ), BC, with 3 crew and 14 passengers onboard. Shortly after takeoff, the flight crew experienced an uncommanded yaw and saw abnormal indications for the right engine (General Electric CT7-5A2). The crew determined the aircraft was experiencing a propeller under speed and declared a MAYDAY. They completed the propeller under speed checklist, which required an inflight engine shutdown, followed by the one engine inoperative checklist. The crew returned to the airport assisted by vectors from air traffic control. The airplane landed safely and the crew requested aircraft rescue and fire fighting personnel to inspect the right engine prior to taxiing back to the terminal. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft.The aircraft was grounded and maintenance inspections are being conducted to determine the cause.

C-GVUN, an Air Canada A220-300, was conducting flight AC355 from Ottawa/Macdonald–Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB with 6 crew and 132 passengers onboard. While in cruise at FL360, AC355 had a left engine oil pressure indication issue. The crew brought the left throttle back to idle, declared emergency (Pan Pan) and diverted the flight to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. The aircraft landed at CYYZ without further incident. Air Canada maintenance completed the fault isolation and replaced the LH Engine oil pressure sensor. A trend review was conducted and revealed the Low Pressure indication was an actual oil pressure drop and not an indication fault. The operator and the engine manufacturer are conducting further investigation.

C-FOTA, a Dornier Alpha Jet Model A operated by Top Aces Inc. as flight CHEETA71, was on a training manoeuver in the vicinity of Buffalo Narrows (CYVT), SK with only the pilot on board. While in the maneuver, the pilot noticed the HYD 1 pressure indication drop to 0 PSI and did not receive any associated warning lights. An annunciator panel light check revealed that all warning lights were operating. The pilot activated the speed brakes and found they did not deploy, confirming a HYD 1 failure. The pilot decided to return to Cold Lake/Group Captain R.W. McNair (CYOD), AB and declared an emergency. The aircraft burned off the necessary fuel on board to achieve the required landing weight and then landed safely.

C-GJJF, un Beechcraft A100 exploité par Propair Inc. sous l'indicatif PRO4651, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport d’Alma, QC (CYTF) à destination de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) avec 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, le voyant de feu moteur de droite s’est allumé, s'est éteint, pour ensuite s’allumer de nouveau et est demeuré allumé.  Aucune anomalie ou fumée n’a été perçue durant le vol. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée, l'équipage a éteint le moteur et a demandé un déroutement vers Bagotville, QC (CYBG), où l’avion s’est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. Une inspection a été effectuée par le personnel de l'entretien et une défectuosité a été trouvée dans le système de détection d’incendie, un capteur a été changé et l’avion a été remis en service.

C-GJLJ, un Beechcraft A100 exploité par Propair Inc. sous l'indicatif PRO4800, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) à destination de Montréal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX). Lors de la montée initiale après la rentrée des roues, l’équipage a senti un lacet vers la droite que s’est accentué au point où les palonniers se sont retrouvés à pleine déflexion vers la droite. L’avion a dévié de la trajectoire autorisée par l’ATC. Les pilotes ont tenté d’appliquer du palonnier vers la gauche, mais les palonniers n’ont pas bougé. L’équipage a réussi à stabiliser l’avion avec les ailerons et a déclaré une urgence. Ils sont revenus à CYUY et ont effectué l’approche pour la piste 08. L’avion est redevenu stable lorsque les roues ont été sorties et l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre. Une inspection a été effectuée par le personnel de l'entretien et une défectuosité a été trouvée dans le système d’autopilote ainsi que dans le système rattaché à l’amortisseur de lacet.

C-GQBQ, un Bombardier CL600-2B16 Challenger 601 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait le vol QUE20 selon les règles de vols aux instruments au départ de l'aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) avec 2 pilotes, 3 personnels de cabine et 1 passager à bord. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en montée initiale après le décollage de CYMT, la roue de nez n'a pas remonté. L'équipage a effectué la liste de vérification d'urgence pour GEAR UP DISAGREE et a déclaré une urgence. L'équipage a poursuivi son vol avec le train baissé et a déclaré une urgence en descente vers CYQB où l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l'appareil. L'inspection effectuée par le personnel de l'entretien le « centering prox switch » a été ajusté et l’avion a été remis en service.

C-GFUD, a privately registered, amateur-built, amphibious Seastar SP, was on a local flight from Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC, with 2 pilots on board. The aircraft completed a touch-and-go on Pitt River, BC and, on the second landing, the aircraft nosed over into the water. The pilots egressed and were rescued by a passing vessel. The vessel towed the aircraft to shore. The pilots sustained minor injuries and the aircraft sustained substantial damage. The ELT activated. After the accident, the pilots verified that the landing gear was in the down position.The aircraft was disassembled and transported to a hangar where an assessment will be conducted to determine the repair requirements.

C-FINB, an Aerospatiale ATR 72-202 aeroplane operated by Calm Air International, was being prepared for flight 506/507 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Gillam (CYGX), MB. The aircraft had been taxied from the CYWG terminal to the apron and the engines were shut down. While ground power was applied there was a strong electrical odour accompanied by smoke and haze in the cockpit. The operator's maintenance personnel determined that the No. 1 inverter was the source of the smoke and the inverter was replaced. However, during troubleshooting, unrelated damage was discovered and repaired on the DC ground-power-unit connector's positive wire located under the floor beneath the first officer's seat.

C-GREY, a privately registered Cessna C340A airplane, was conducting a flight from Kelowna (CYLW), BC, to High River (CEN4), AB, with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During cruise, at 19 000 feet above sea level, the left engine (Teledyne Continental TSIO-520-NB) oil pressure began decreasing slowly. Air traffic control was advised and the pilot decided to divert to Fairmont Hot Springs (CYCZ), BC. During the descent for landing, the oil pressure continued to decrease and the pilot shut down the engine and feathered the propeller as a precautionary measure. The aircraft landed without further incident.The engine was sent to an engine maintenance facility to investigate the issue.

The WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-8-400, C-FENJ, was operating as WEN3271 on a flight from Regina Intl. (CYQR), SK to Calgary Intl.  (CYYC), AB. During the flight a cabin crew member experienced a medical event and were unable to continue performing their duties. The flight crew was made aware of the situation and no emergency was declared.

C-FDOD, a Bell 412 helicopter operated by Wisk-Air Ltd., was returning 4 drums containing Jet A-1 (UN 1863) fuel from a cache near Prospect Lake, ON to the Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources (OMNR) fire base at Red Lake, ON. The pilot supervised the loading and the sling gear had been inspected and found serviceable prior to departure. After takeoff the pilot de-activated the electrical release on the cyclic control. Approximately 8 minutes later the load of 4 fuel drums fell to the ground. All of the drums were damaged and 3 released their contents. The remaining drum still held fuel. The fuel drums were retrieved by OMNR personnel on 12 June and remediation of the site was conducted. Details of the event were reported to CANUTEC. The operator reported that abrasion to the retaining strap connecting the load to the belly hook indicated that it had worked itself around and under the hook keeper. The hook and release mechanism were inspected and found serviceable. The emergency foot release had not been used. The operator's aircrews that used the same helicopter type and hook system were notified.

C-GJTX, an Air Canada Rouge A321-211 conducting flight ROU1987 from Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), Dominican Republic to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. During cruise in the vicinity of New York, NY, a cabin crew became incapacitated and was attended by medical professionals on board. The flight attendant was unable to continue their duties.An able-bodied passenger (ABP) was identified in accordance with company procedures and took the incapacitated cabin crew position for landing. The aircraft landed safely in CYUL.

C-GOCD, a Westjet B737-800 conducting flight WJA1468 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), CA. During cruise at approximately waypoint LAKRR, 74nm southeast of Las Vegas, NV, a cabin crew became unwell. The captain elected to have the flight attendant removed from duties.The cabin crew member was assessed by local EMS and was cleared to fly home.

C-FNWD, a Westjet Airlines Ltd Boeing 737 MAX8 was conducting flight WS1246 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Tampa Intl. (KTPA), FL.  In early descent, flight crew advised cabin crew to anticipate turbulence in later stages of descent and requested they secure the cabin early.  Approximately 5 minutes later going through 13000 feet, flight encountered light to moderate turbulence (TCU).  A flight attendant suffered serious injuries due to turbulence.  Flight landed in KTPA where flight was met by EMS.

C-GPCE, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Limited Beech 1900D, was conducting flight PCO218 from Powell River (CYPW),BC to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 2 crew members and 9 passengers on board. During the climb out of CYPW, through approximately 7500 feet above sea level, the airplane’s left engine (PT6A-67D) began to surge. The flight crew reduced power and the surging became manageable. After consulting with company maintenance, they decided to continue to CYVR at the reduced power setting. When the crew had CYVR in sight, they declared PAN PAN with air traffic control and were given priority handling to a safe landing. They taxied in to their parking location without further incident.Maintenance was unable to replicate the fault during ground runs but the fault returned the next day when the airplane was climbing out of CYVR. The flight control unit was replaced and the aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GEXK, un Viking Air Limited DHC2 (Beaver) enregistré au  nom du Pavillon du Lac Berthelot Inc. effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue dans la région du Lac Berthelot, QC avec 1 pilote et 2 passagers à son bord. Lors de l'amerrissage sur le lac, le pilote a perdu le contrôle directionnel de l'aéronef après avoir descendu les gouvernes des flotteurs. L'avion a percutée la rive du Lac et a subi des dommages importants. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé. Le pilote a rapporté qu'il était possible que l'arrière de l'un des flotteurs soit entré en contact avec le quai durant le départ précédent l'accident.

C-FEWM, un Cessna 185 sur flottes en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue au départ du Lac à la Tortue, QC (CSL3) pour se rendre à un camp de chasse situé au Réservoir Gouin. Suite au décollage, le pilote n'a pas été en mesure de prendre de la vitesse et de l'altitude. Un virage dans le vent a été effectué pour tenter de remédier à la situation, mais sans succès. Lors d'un autre virage subséquent, l'aéronef a perdu de l'altitude avant de percuter des fils électriques et de s'écraser à 2 milles nautiques au nord de l’aéroport du Lac-à-la-Tortue, dans un boisé dense situé en bordure d'une route fermée à la circulation. Aucun incendie ne s'est déclaré, mais l'aéronef a été détruit. Les deux occupants à ont réussi à sortir de l'épave. Le pilote n'a pas été blessé et le passager à subi des blessures nécessitant son transport en ambulance. L'examen sur le site a permis d'observer que les volets étaient toujours en position de décollage. L'appareil n'était pas en surcharge et des éléments démontrent que le moteur développait de la puissance au moment de l'impact.

The WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-800, C-FWSO, was operating as WJA1585 on a flight from Las Vegas (KLAS), Nevada to Calgary (CYYC), Alberta. While 40 NM from CYYC a flight attendant was unable to continue performing their duties. Emergency medical services were notified and met the aircraft at the gate. There were no other operational implications.

C-GXAJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 767-323ER, was conducting flight CJT824 from Shanghai/Pudong Intl. (ZSPD), China to Narita/New Tokyo Intl. (RJAA), Japan.  During initial climb, flight crew received EICAS C DEM HYD OVHT and C HYD SYS PRESS.  QRH procedures was completed, emergency was declared with ATC and longer runway was requested for landing in RJAA.  Flight landed without further incident where it was met by ARFF.  Post landing inspection reported no fluid or smoke emanating from the aircraft.  Maintenance confirmed no leak detected and hydraulic fluid within limits.  Further troubleshooting found ADP filter module hot and by-passing fluid.  Unit was subsequently replaced and aircraft returned to service.

C-FWGH, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800 conducting flight TOM6622 from Cardiff airport (EGFF), UK to Rhodes International Airport "Diagoras" (LGRP), Greece was on approach to LGRP when the flight crew received a trailing edge flap asymmetry warning when flaps 15 was selected.  The flight crew initiated a missed approach, executed the trailing edge flap asymmetry checklist and declared a PAN PAN with ATC. TOM6622 landed with no further issue on the second approach. Emergency vehicles checked brake temperatures and escorted the aircraft to the gate.

C-GFWX, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A320 (flight ROU1525, ) was on climb out from Fredericton International Airport (CYFC). As the aircraft was climbing through 10,000 feet ASL the flight crew received an ECAM hydraulic overheat message followed by a Green Hydraulic system Low Level warning. The QRH procedures were followed and the flight continued to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON where the crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. As a result of the Green Hydraulic system fault the aircraft had to be towed to the gate because nosewheel steering was not available. Maintenance found a hydraulic leak in the Green Hydraulic manifold. The leak was rectified and the PTU was also replaced. The aircraft returned to service.

C-FWXI, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by Beaver Air Services LP. (dba Missinippi Air-Care), was conducting medevac flight MA02 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Island Lake (CYIV), MB. During the approach to Runway 30 at CYIV, the flight crew selected the landing gear down; however, the green down-and-locked indicator for the right main landing gear did not illuminate. The flight crew cycled the landing gear to no effect and tested the indicator lamps. The flight crew elected to divert to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB and communicated their intentions to the company and Thunder Bay radio. While climbing to cruise level the flight crew declared an emergency with the area communications centre (ACC). The emergency landing gear extension procedure was conducted on the descent to CYWG; however, the right main landing gear down-and-locked indicator still did not illuminate. After a flyby of the tower the crew was informed that the right landing gear appeared to be down. The flight crew conducted a visual approach for Runway 18 and briefed the medic on the brace procedure and evacuation plan. The subsequent landing was conducted successfully with ARFF responding. The flight crew taxied the aircraft to the apron while applying constant pressure to the landing gear with the hand pump. The occupants exited the aircraft after the landing gear was visually confirmed to be down-and-locked.The operator's maintenance personnel replaced the down-lock switch on the right main landing gear and conducted successful landing gear swings.

C-GNLK, a Boeing B737-2K2C aeroplane operated by Nolinor Aviation, was preparing for flight NRL955 from Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU to Val-d'Or (CYVO), QC. After both engines were started the aft cargo "A loop" smoke detection warning illuminated. The flight crew shut down both engines and requested emergency fire services. The flight crew performed an inspection of the entire aircraft and did not find any smoke sources. The emergency fire services were released by the flight crew after informing them of the false alarm. The operator reported that the false smoke indication was caused by a fault in the cargo compartment smoke detection system.

On 08 June 2022, a Delta Airlines Boeing 767-300 (flight DAL562) was enroute from Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), CA to John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), NY and a Pratt and Whitney Cessna Citation 560X (registration C-GPAW) was enroute from Dallas Love Field Airport (KDAL), TX to Montreal Saint-Hubert Longueuil Airport (CYHU), QC. At approximately 2220 UTC, DAL562 was proceeding SE and C-GPAW was proceeding NE and both aircraft were at FL370 and in the vicinity of the London International Airport (CYXU), ON. DAL562 initiated an unanticipated right turn that increased the closure rate and resulted in a loss of separation for both aircraft.  The Air Traffic Controller noticed the irregularity and immediately provided both aircraft with deconflicting (climb/turn, descend/turn) instructions by turning and climbing DAL562 and turning and descending CGPAW. A loss of separation occurred when both aircraft came within 5 nm laterally and 700 feet vertically of each other. The separation minimums in that airspace are 5 nm laterally and 1000 feet vertically. During the deconflicting turns, the aircraft continued to within 3 nm and 1800 feet. Once separation was regained, both aircraft proceeded to their destinations. There was no damage. There were no injuries.

C-FRQW, a Jazz Aviation LP Embraer 170-200SU was conducting flight 8944 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Newark Liberty Intl. (KEWR), NJ.  During climb through 16000 feet, flight crew noticed cabin pressure was not increasing nor decreasing.  Also, Flight crew started to feel symptoms of hypoxia.  As a precaution, Flight crew donned oxygen masks, performed a emergency descent to 9000 feet and communicated with ATC.  Flight did not declare an emergency and then diverted to CYUL at 9000 feet where it landed without further incident.  Maintenance did not find fault leading to this event.

C-FVIA, de Havilland DHC-2 MK1, equipped with floats and operated by True North Airways Inc. was departing Pilgrim Lake, Ontario with 5 people on board. Shortly after getting airborne the pilot elected to abort the take-off, as the aircraft was approaching the shoreline and the rising terrain sooner than he had expected. During the landing, while maneuvering through a narrow section of the lake, it was reported that the left wing-tip struck a tree. The aircraft touched down on the remaining lake, which widened out after the narrow section, but the aircraft ran aground and struck trees at the end of the lake. There were no injuries,  but the aircraft received substantial damage to the floats and leading edges of the wings.

C-GJDD, un Piper PA-31 exploité par Eon Aéroporté Inc., effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Rimouski, QC (CYXK) à destination de Bromont (Roland Désourdy), QC (CZBM). À environ 18 nm à l’est-sud-est de l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB), l’équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison d’une panne du moteur gauche. L’équipage a demandé un déroutement vers CYQB et l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 29. Aucun blessé. Une basse pression d'huile constante ainsi qu'une température d'huile élevée avaient été notées la veille et après discussion avec leur organisme de maintenance agréé, l'exploitant a décidé d'effectuer ce vol pour amener l'avion à sa base (CZBM) pour vérifications.

C-GQBA, un Viking Air Limited CL215-6B11(CL-415) exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental sous l'indicatif GRFEU06/QUE240, effectuait un vol local d'entrainement selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Alors que l'appareil était en vol, les pilotes ont noté un problème du système hydraulique qui indiquait un bas niveau et une basse pression. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée et l'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN). L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre à CYQB. Aucun blessé. Une fuite au niveau d’une bague d’étanchéité sur le train d’atterrissage gauche a été trouvée.

C-GHLM, un Airbus 330-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif vol ACA812, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) en direction de l'aéroport de Humberto Delgado - Lisbonne, Portugal (LPPT). En vol de croisière, les pilotes ont noté un problème du système hydraulique vert. Le vol est retourné vers CYUL et l'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN). L'appareil est revenu se poser à CYUL sans encombre à 04:43z avec les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FXCL, a McMurray Aviation Cessna 208B (208EX), was operating on a VFR charter from Gipsy Lake Lodge, AB to Ft. McMurray (CYMM), AB with 1 pilot and 5 passengers on board. During take-off from Runway 04 (turf runway), the aircraft had not achieved performance targets by mid runway and the pilot rejected the take-off. During the roll out the aircraft exited the end of the runway by about 35 feet. There was no damage to the aircraft or injuries to the occupants. Company maintenance was flown out to the aircraft, conducted an inspection and engine run up and released the aircraft back to service. The aircraft subsequently departed the air strip and returned to CYMM.

C-FZTK, a Bell 205A-1 helicopter operated by Churchill Falls (Labrador) Corporation Ltd, was conducting external load operations about 35 nm south southwest of Churchill Falls, NL (CZUM) with 1 crew member on board. The helicopter was slinging electrical power transmission line components to and from a staging area locally known as Mile-35. On one of the trips, while departing a nearby area known as Tower-188, the slung load was 2 line-maintenance carts suspended from the helicopter’s belly hook using a 15-foot short line setup. During take-off the pilot inadvertently pressed the load release button, which is located on the cyclic control stick, and the slung load was unintentional released. The intent was to press the radio mic button to speak with a ground crew member. There was no injury to personnel, and no damage to the helicopter. The 2 line-maintenance carts were damaged.The incident has been entered into the operator’s safety management system for investigation and corrective action.

N219CY, a Boeing 767-383 freighter aircraft operated by ABX Air Services, was conducting cargo flight ANX956 from Brussels Intl (EBBR), Belgium to Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky Intl (KCVG), KY. When in cruise flight at about 56°03' N, 048°00' W, the flight crew observed cargo fire panel B6 and B8 amber illuminate, with no associated EICAS message. The crew consulted the QRH and then contacted maintenance department to discuss the fault illumination. The crew was advised that the amber indication represented failed smoke detectors, and decided to make a precautionary diversion. A PAN PAN was declared with ATS, and a diversion to Goose Bay (CYYR), NL was made, where the aircraft landed without further incident. Airport emergency services met the flight, and several airfreight unit load devices were removed to facilitate inspection with thermal imaging cameras and gas detectors. No evidence of combustion was detected. Maintenance personnel replaced the faulty B6 and B8 smoke detectors.

C-FDJA, a Jazz Aviation LP MHI RJ Aviation ULC CL-600-2B19 (CRJ200) was conducting flight JZA8837 from Raleigh-Durham Intl. (KRDU), NC to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. The aircraft was 150 NM south of CYYZ when the right hand reverser unlocked caution message illuminated. The Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) was actioned and the number 2 engine was shut down. A PAN PAN was declared and the crew elected to continue towards CYYZ. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FLEJ, a Flair Airlines Boeing 737-86N conducting flight FLE277 from Harry Reid International Airport, Las Vegas (KLAS), NV to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC while on climb at 6500ft, received a TCAS RA due to crossing traffic at 7000ft. Crew informed ATC and proceeded enroute to CYVR without further incident.

C-GWSZ, a WestJet Boeing 737-800, was operating as WJA1401 from Las Vegas (KLAS), NV to Calgary (CYYC), AB with 6 crew and 145 passengers on board. Approximately 1 hour after departure from KLAS, while in cruise a FL370, the flight crew observed a horizontal stabilizer out of trim indication. The appropriate checklists were performed and WJA1401 descended out of RVSM airspace to FL280. The flight continued to CYYC without further issue. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN when they contacted the Calgary arrival controller and they were vectored for the left hand visual for Runway 17L.Maintenance follow up: the horizontal stabilizer trim logic was reset with no faults found. A DFCS BITE was performed and returned maintenance message 22-11177. A SPD/STB trim test was performed and was passed; the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GVJZ, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA51 from Gander Intl (CYQX), NL to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. On approach to CYHZ, the crew received an amber nose door caution light. Although all 3 landing gear safe lights were illuminated on the landing gear selector panel, an inspection of the landing gear downlock verification lights at the alternate extension panel revealed no nose gear down light illuminated. The flight crew then received a landing gear inoperative caution, elected to carry out a missed approach and declare a PAN PAN with the CYHZ ATS. The crew carried out an alternate landing gear extension as per checklist, and returned to land at CYHZ without further incident.Company maintenance replaced a faulty nose landing gear indication wiring harness.

C-GKQA, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE262 from St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL to Halifax/Stanfield (CYHZ), NS. About 30 minutes after takeoff, the right side of the windshield cracked while in cruise flight at FL240. The flight crew completed the checklist items related to a cracked windshield and consulted with dispatch regarding weather at departure and destination airports, as well as fuel burn calculations for lower altitudes. The flight crew decided to continue to CYHZ at a reduced speed, declared PAN PAN, and received priority from ATS to slowly descend to a cruising altitude of 14 000 feet. The flight remained at 14 000 feet to maintain clear of clouds and icing conditions, and descended to 10 000 feet about an hour later. The flight crew remained on oxygen while at 14 000 feet altitude. The cabin crew remained on portable oxygen for the remainder of the flight, and provided portable oxygen as needed to 8 passengers who initially indicated feeling light-headed. The flight landed without further incident at CYHZ, and no passengers reported injury or the requirement of medical attention.

C-FGKZ, an Airbus A321-211 operated by Air Canada, was operating flight ACA1117 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON to Regina Intl. (CYQR), SK. On arrival into CYQR, the crew declared a PAN PAN due to receiving a Green Hyd ECAM message. During the approach to CYQR and upon selecting the landing gear down, the crew observed another ECAM message that the gears were not down. The crew conducted a missed approach, was vectored by ATC while they completed the associated checklist. The aircraft subsequently landed uneventfully at CYQR with emergency vehicles standing by.A subsequent inspection revealed a leaking hydraulic line on the right landing gear door. The line was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service

C-FFNF, a Boeing 737-406 operated by Bradley Air Services (dba Canadian North), was conducting flight AKT150 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB for Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU. Shortly after takeoff, the Captain's (who was the pilot flying) primary flight instruments failed except for the Attitude Director Indicator (ADI). Flight control duties were transferred to the First Officer.  The crew declared a Pan Pan and requested block altitudes to hold while burning off fuel to achieve maximum landing weight for a return to CYWG. Once the fuel burn was reached, the aircraft returned for an uneventful landing in CYWG.A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed faults in the #1 Air Data Unit (ADU). The unit was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

The PropAir Beechcraft 1900D aircraft (PRO4381) was on final approach to RWY 15R and began a descent without clearance. The Air Canada Rouge A320 aircraft (ROU1803) was on final approach to RWY 15L when in the turn it flew wide and went through the localizer. Due to technical difficulties and frequency congestion the controller did not take immediate corrective action. The aircraft separation was reduced to 300 feet vertical, and 0.6 NM lateral. Visibility was good, and neither aircraft reported TCAS warnings during the event.

C-FFYG, an Embraer 170-200 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8218 from Montreal Pierre Elliot Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Charlottetown Airport (CYYG), PEI. During the cruise portion, the pilots reported encountering moderate turbulence which resulted in a cabin crew member receiving a minor injury. The cabin crew member was unable to perform their duties and the duties were distributed among the other cabin crew. The crew made a joint decision to continue to the destination and requested emergency services to meet the aircraft. Medical personal assessed the cabin crew member and released the individual fit and ok to complete the return flight.

C-FSNQ, an Air Canada B737 Max 8 was conducting flight AC548 (on 24 May 2022) from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ. The flight crew reported getting a TCAS RA at 4000' going into KEWR from VFR traffic at 3500'. ATC was aware, and no deviation commanded.

C-FYHN, un hélicoptère Bell 206L sur flotteurs exploité par Custom Helicopters Ltd., effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP). Peu de temps après avoir décollé, le pilote a rencontré du givrage non annoncé dans les prévisions météorologiques, consultées par ce dernier avant le vol. Le pilote a effectué un demi-tour pour revenir à CYVP mais le pare-brise et les hublots bombés de chaque côté avaient accumulé suffisamment de givre pour réduire la visibilité du pilote. Celui-ci a manœuvré l’hélicoptère jusqu’au-dessus de l’aire de posé où il était stationné précédemment, tout en conservant une hauteur plus haute et a amorcé une descente verticale pour atterrir. À environ 5 pieds au-dessus du sol, une rafale de vent a déstabilisé l’hélicoptère et le rotor de queue est entré en collision avec une rampe d’escalier portative utilisée pour les avions. Les dommages au rotor de queue ont causé une perte de son efficacité créant une rotation incontrôlable vers la droite. Le pilote a baissé le collectif et fermé la manette des gaz pour arrêter le mouvement de rotation. L’hélicoptère s’est posé durement au sol. Le pilote n’a pas été blessé et a complété la procédure d’arrêt avant d’évacuer l’hélicoptère. Le rotor de queue, la poutre de queue et le train d’atterrissage ont subi des dommages importants.

C-GOIA, a SAAB 340B operated by Pacific Coastal Airlines was conducting flight PCO3065 from Lloydminster, AB (CYLL) to Calgary International, AB (CYYC) with 3 crew members and 22 passengers on board. During the departure from CYLL the flight crew felt an unusual vibration from the nose landing gear. The landing gear retracted normally, there were no other abnormal indications in the cockpit and the flight crew elected to continue to CYYC. While enroute, the flight crew were informed that airport personnel at CYLL had located a nose wheel assembly. The flight crew performed the QRH checklist, and approximately 74 nm NE of CYYC, the flight crew declared an emergency, and requested airport rescue and fire fighting be placed on standby. A flyby of the control tower was completed, and the the nose landing gear was observed in the down position and the right nose wheel assembly was confirmed to be missing. The appropriate passenger briefings were completed and an uneventful landing was carried out with the remaining nose wheel taking the weight of the nose of the aircraft. The aircraft taxied to the intended parking area.Initial investigation by company maintenance indicates that the right nose wheel outer bearing failed due to lack of lubrication, allowing the nose wheel assembly to depart the aircraft.

C-FWGH a Sunwing Airlines B737-800 conducting flight TOM6720 from Cardiff airport, UK (EGFF) to Palma de Mallorca Airport, Spain (LEPA), while the flight was being vectored into LEPA, the Flight Crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory - Climb. The Flight Crew immediately executed the Climb maneuver. The flight continued to destination and landed without further incident.

C-FPXA, a Cessna 152 aircraft operated by Exploit Valley Air Services Ltd/Gander Flight Training, was conducting a local training flight 25 nm N of Gander International Airport (CYQX), NL. In preparation for his commercial licence, the pilot was practicing simulated forced approaches to an access road. The first practiced approach resulted in the aircraft too high to make a successful landing. A second practiced approach was attempted and the pilot used a forward slip with 30 degrees of flap to lose altitude to obtain a successful profile. A few hundred feet above the tree line the pilot initiated an overshoot, however the aircraft continued to descend and the left wing impacted a tree, which caused the aircraft to pivot and come to rest into trees facing 180 degrees in the opposite direction.The pilot secured the aircraft, egressed and climbed down trees which were approximately 10-12 feet high. Local bystanders assisted the pilot, who called the operator's dispatcher and chief flight instructor. No injuries were reported. The aircraft was substantially damaged.The operator recovered the aircraft and maintenance completed a preliminary inspection of the power plant, with no anomalies discovered at this time. A third-party repair facility will inspect the engine at a later date.

A De-Havilland Dash 8-100 aircraft with no civilian registration, operated by PAL Aerospace Ltd, was conducting a test flight at St John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL. The crew were departing on Runway 29, when the number 2 engine failed just prior to 70 knots. The crew rejected the take off and brought the aircraft to a stop on the runway. Tower advised that they saw a small amount of smoke from the engine and the crew decided to evacuate as a precaution. ARFF responded and no fire was detected. Maintenance towed the aircraft back to the hangar ramp. The initial report from the operator indicates the engine is damaged beyond repair. The cause of the failure is under investigation.

C-GGAP, a privately registered Piper PA-22 aircraft, with an instructor and student pilot onboard was on the approach to land on Runway 09 at Stirling, Ontario (CPJ5). The instructor was the pilot flying; as the aircraft approached the tree tops, the approach became unstable due to mechanical turbulence and a reported tailwind. The instructor performed a go-around and brought the aircraft around for a second approach, this time into the prevailing wind on Runway 27. The instructor attempted to go-around again as it was determined the touchdown would be further down the runway than expected. The instructor added full power for a go-around, the engine sputtered, and lost power. The aircraft touched down on the remaining runway, went off the end of the runway, down a slope, through a fence and into some trees. Both occupants exited the aircraft without injury. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GQFA, a Cessna 172M aircraft with an instructor and student pilot were conducting circuits at Toronto Buttonville airport (CYKZ), ON. The aircraft was on the fourth approach to Runway 21, on the base leg, when the instructor noted weather rapidly closing in on the airport. The aircraft encountered light wind shear on approach, but was stabilized on short final. The instructor took control and landed the aircraft, the winds were estimated to be around 230@15-20kts. The aircraft touched down on runway 21 just passed Echo taxiway and came to a complete stop at Charlie taxiway.The instructor taxied the aircraft to exit the runway and passed control to student. The student taxied normally on taxiway Alpha and crossed runway 33. The winds picked up significantly from the rear left of the aircraft after exiting runway 33 on alpha, along with heavy rain and hail. The instructor took over and applied full input to the control column to counteract the wind. When the aircraft reached the last row of aircraft, a sudden strong gust of wind lifted the tail and the aircraft flipped over. The instructor secured the engine and both the instructor and student egressed the aircraft through their respective doors with minor injuries.

N711WS, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19, departed Lester B. Pearson International Airport, Ontario (CYYZ) en route to Los Angeles International Airport, California (KLAX). After departure, the crew declared a PAN emergency due to a nose gear indication. The aircraft returned to CYYZ where it landed safely. There were no injuries.

C-GBGJ, a float-equipped Cessna U206G registered to Sandy Lake Seaplane Service, was conducting a privately operated flight from the Sandy Lake Water Aerodrome (CKE5), ON, to an unnamed lake, located approximately 25 minute flight north of CKE5, and a subsequent return flight to CKE5. On the return flight, while on final for a southwest direction landing at CKE5, the aircraft collided with a communication tower in the Sandy Lake First Nation community. The aircraft subsequently collided with terrain, caught fire, and was destroyed. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was fatally injured. The Nishnawbe Aski Police Service and the Sandy Lake First Nation Fire Department responded. The TSB deployed to the site.

N591ER, a Diamond Aircraft Industries DA42, was conducting a first test flight following a major refurbishment at Diamond Aircraft Industries at the London International Airport (CYXU). During the takeoff roll everything appeared to be normal, however as the aircraft nose wheel came off the ground, and the aircraft became airborne it immediately veered to the left. The pilot attempted to correct for the un-commanded movement but was having difficulty maintaining direction control of the aircraft. The pilot declared an emergency and flew the aircraft around for an emergency approach to Runway 27. During the approach the pilot continued to have control difficulties and attempted to land on taxiway Alpha, however he ultimately elected to land straight ahead on the grass. The aircraft touched down hard on the grass breaking off the rudder and the left-wing aileron mass balance weight. The landing gear collapsed and the aircraft slid approximately 265 feet from the initial impact to a final stop. The pilot was not injured.TSB investigators deployed and conducted an examination of the aircraft. The examination found that the rudder cables had been installed incorrectly.

The American Airlines Boeing 737-823, N342PM, was operating as flight AA2517 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Dallas/Fort Worth (KDFW), TX. Shortly after departure the flight crew noticed a leading edge flap issue. The flight crew declared MAYDAY and returned to CYYC. The aircraft landed without further incident. There were no injuries.

C-GIZX, un Beechcraft A100 exploité par Propair Inc. sous l’indicatif PRO4450, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) à destination l'aéroport d'Amos, QC (CYEY).  Lors de la montée initiale, de la fumée est apparue dans l’appareil. L'équipage est revenu atterrir sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage. L’inspection après l’événement a révélé qu’une petite quantité d’huile à moteur avait été renversée dans le compartiment du moteur lors d'une maintenance précédente. Au décollage, le résidu d'huile a chauffé et dégagé de la fumée qui a été aspirée par l’entrée d’air. Le compartiment moteur a été nettoyé et l'appareil remis en service.

C-GUSC, un Jetstream 32 exploité par Pascan Aviation sous l’indicatif PSC736 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Wabush, QC (CYWK) à destination de l’aéroport de Mont-Joli, QC (CYYY). Alors que l’appareil était en finale à environ 20 miles nautique de la piste 24, l'équipage a noté une perte de puissance sur le moteur gauche. L'équipage a complété la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a coupé le moteur. Une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée et l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre. La vérification mécanique a révélé que la pompe de carburant à haute pression a cessé de fonctionner suite à un bris interne de la boite d'engrenage.

C-GPRB, a privately registered Pitts S1S (Pitts Special), was conducting a local aerobatic flight from Vernon (CYVK) BC, with only the pilot on board. During the flight, the runway at CYVK was closed due to an airplane having landed gear up. The pilot diverted to Salmon Arm (CZAM) BC, where, in a cross wind, the aircraft ground looped. The airplane departed the runway to the right, nosed down and came to rest on the propeller, left main gear, and the left wing. The pilot released himself from his harness and parachute system, and egressed. There were no injuries.A maintenance company recovered the aircraft which was disassembled for ground transportation. The initial inspection revealed that the left main landing gear was bent, the left-wing tip was scraped, the propeller was fractured, and both wheel pants were damaged. Further examinations will be conducted to determine the extent of the repairs that will be required.

C-GSPW, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE751 effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Val-D’Or (CYVO) QC, à destination de Kattiniq/Donaldson, QC (CTP9) Lors de la montée initiale, la température d'huile du moteur #2 a dépassé la limite maximale. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée et le moteur a été arrêté par mesure de précaution. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et est revenu se poser à CYVO sans encombre à 17h29 UTC. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. La procédure de dépannage a conclu que le moteur avait un dommage interne nécéssitant le remplacement de celui-ci.

C-FESM, a privately registered Mooney M20C, was on a local flight from Vernon (CYVK) BC, with only the pilot on board. The airplane landed gear up on runway 23 at CYVK. The aircraft skidded to a stop at taxiway Bravo sustaining damage to its belly and propeller. Airport Operations issued a NOTAM to close the runway and assisted the pilot in removing the airplane from the runway to the pilot's hangar. There were no injuries to the pilot or damage to the runway or airport infrastructure.A runway sweep was conducted, the NOTAM was cancelled, and the runway was re-opened.

C-FMJO, a Viking DHC-6-400 Twin Otter on amphibious floats, operated by Pacific Sky Aviation Incorporated, was conducting circuits at Victoria International (CYYJ) BC, with 2 crew members on board. On the fifth circuit, the front left nose gear indicator did not show down and locked. The crew conducted a missed approach and flew to a position southwest of the airport to troubleshoot the issue. After completing the necessary check lists, and confirming visually that the gear was in the down position, the crew declared an emergency and returned to CYYJ. The aircraft landed without further incident with aircraft rescue and fire-fighting standing by.A local aircraft maintenance organization investigated the gear indication issue. The proximity switches for both the left and right nose landing gear were adjusted and gear extensions and retractions were completed successfully. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-FTXK, un Canadair CL215-1A10 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental sous l’indicatif QUE231, effectuait un vol local d'entrainement selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis et à destination de l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Alors que l’appareil revenait du lac Montauban où des exercices d'entrainement à l'eau ont eu lieu, un retour de flamme s'est produit sur le moteur de gauche. Le moteur a été éteint par mesure de précaution et une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. La cause du retour de flamme est sous investigation par l'opérateur.

C-FIUJ, an Air Canada Boeing 777-200 was conducting flight AC42 from Toronto/Lester B., Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to New Delhi/Indira Gandhi Intl. (VIDP), India.  Flight was unable to land at VIDP due to severe thunderstorm in the area.  Flight crew decided to divert to Ahmedabad/Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Intl. (VAAH), India.  Flight crew advised of their intention to divert to VAAH but ATC informed the crew that VAAH was closed.  As the flight crew did not want to try an approach in severe turbulence/thunderstorm at VIDP, flight crew declared a MAYDAY and proceeded toward VAAH. During climb to cruise level, flight encountered severe turbulence with altitude variation of 200 feet.  Several crew and passengers received minor injuries.  Flight landed in VAAH without further incident where they met with EMS and Severe turbulence inspection was completed with no damage found.

C-FSNC, a Chartright Air Cessna 560 was conducting flight HRT676 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Houston William P. Hobby Airport (KHOU), TX when at approximately 19:43 ET, the pilot declared an emergency due to smoke in the cockpit and cockpit display issue. After the smoke dissipated, the pilot elected to continue to Houston with a remaining estimated flight time of 36 minutes. The aircraft landed without incident at KHOU at 20:25 EST.

C-GHKW, an Air Canada A330 conducting flight AC926 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Cancun International Airport (MMUN), MX, after reaching FL400 the flight crew were advised by the Flight attendants that an oven had an electrical odour and smoke was visible. Power to oven and galley were switched off but smoke was still visible. The flight crew contacted dispatch and elected to return to YUL where the flight landed safely.

C-GKNW, a Pilatus PC-12/47E aircraft operated by Northway Aviation, was conducting a flight from Winnipeg/St. Andrews (CYAV), MB to Gods Lake Narrows (CYGO), MB.  Shortly after takeoff from Runway 36 at CYAV, the aircraft's stick shaker activated and the stall warning alert sounded. The crew declared an emergency and returned for an uneventful landing on Runway 36 with emergency vehicles standing by.A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed a faulty angle of attack sensor.  The sensor was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GCMD, a Yellowhead Helicopters Ltd. Airbus AS350 B-2, was conducting pipeline inspection operations 60 NM NW of Fort St John (CYXJ), BC. After landing, while the engine and rotors remained turning, passenger #1 exited the left side of the helicopter. He retrieved his tools from the basket located on the left side of the helicopter, then proceeded around the nose of the helicopter, to the jobsite located approximate 15 m to the right side of the helicopter. Several moments later, passenger #2 exited the left side of the helicopter. He proceeded to the aft end of the helicopter where he crossed under the tail boom. While crouched and passing under the tail boom, the passenger was struck by the tail rotor. The passenger received minor injuries. The pilot shutdown and secured the helicopter. The helicopter tail rotor blades were damaged. The pilot and passengers were recovered from a nearby lease site. It was the first day on the jobsite for the injured passenger, as well as his first time flying in a helicopter.

C-GTVO, un Boeing 737-219C exploité par Chrono Jet Inc effectuait le vol MBK797 au départ d'Iqualuit, NU (CYFB) à destination de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec 3 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de la course au décollage, l'équipage a ressenti des vibrations provenant du train d'atterrissage avant. Les vibrations ont cessé après la rétraction du train d'atterrissage. L'équipage a décidé de continuer vers CYHU et a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) par mesure de précaution. L'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre à CYHU. Le personnel de maintenance a effectué une inspection du train d'atterrissage et a trouvé que les deux roues avants n'étaient pas parfaitement rondes. Les pneus ont étés remplacés et l'aéronef a été remis en services après un test de rétraction et une lubrification du mécanisme du train avant.

C-GNNR, a Beech 200 operated by SkyNorth Air Ltd. as SN01T was conducting a training flight in the vicinity of Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. While on vectors for a second approach to Runway 13 at CYWG, the flight crew noticed smoke coming out of the right engine (PT6A-61) cowl and noticed the engine was not able to produce normal power. The flight crew shutdown the right-hand engine and declared an emergency with ATC. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 13 with ARFF on standby. ARFF inspected the engine and indicated that there was no smoke or fire coming from the engine. The aircraft was towed to the hangar. The operator's maintenance inspected the right-hand engine and found evidence of fuel leakage around the fuel nozzle transfer tubes. They replaced 16 fuel transfer o-rings, conducted an engine ground run, and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FAKW, an Alkan Air Beech King Air BE300, operated under instrument flight rules, was conducting flight AKN183 for BC Emergency Health Services from Nanaimo (CYCD) BC, and Terrace (CYXT) BC with two crew members and two passengers onboard. The flight was experiencing moderate turbulence while in the climb to 14000 feet above sea level and the crew noticed that the top forward cowling on the the right engine had come unseated. The flight crew elected to divert to Vancouver and requested priority handling from air traffic control.  The airplane landed safely with aircraft rescue and fire fighting personnel on standby. The airplane taxied to the gate. Company maintenance tightened a cowling bolt and secured the latch holding the cowling in place.

C-GVZB, a Chrono Jet Inc. Boeing 737-8Q8 was conducting flight MBK784 from Iqaluit (CYFB), NU to St. Petersburg/St. Pete-Clearwater Intl. (KPIE), FL.  During final approach in VMC, ATC identified to flight crew a traffic 11 o'clock unverified altitude.  Flight crew received a TCAS TA (traffic advisory).  Flight crew visually identified the traffic and then, while descending through 3200 feet, received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to ''climb''.  Flight crew climbed to 3800 feet until clear of traffic and resumed approach subsequently landing in KPIE without further incident.

C-GTHX, a Piper PA-24-250 aircraft operated by KBM Resources Group, was conducting a local training flight from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON with 2 pilots on board. During air work exercises, the gear was selected down and the right rudder pedal locked in position. The gear light did not illuminate green and aircraft control was maintained in a slow slip to the left. The gear was selected up, but the landing gear did not retract as the breaker had popped. The breaker was reset and the gear successfully retracted. Rudder control was restored with the gear retracted. The gear was selected down once again, and the rudder control issue returned. The gear breaker did not pop and the gear was retracted. The crew subsequently conducted the emergency manual gear extension procedure while making full rudder deflections. The gear was lowered successfully, three green lights illuminated, and no rudder control issues were present. The crew requested to have emergency vehicles on standby and a low pass was conducted at CYQT. The aircraft landed without incident.The operator's maintenance conducted a post-occurrence inspection of the nose gear and indicated that the clamp holding the shimmy dampener in place had been installed incorrectly, causing a bolt on the clamp to catch the cowling while the gear was being extended. The clamp installation was rectified and gear swings were conducted successfully. The aircraft was then returned to service.

An AirMarkets Inc., Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS) Spektreworks, Cobalt 110 G-VTOL, serial number CB110-2B-1220-GVTOL-025, was operating from an open field approximately 2 nm East of Josephburg (CFB6), AB. During operation the RPAS 's VTOL motor failed and was not able to stow. The crew were required to leave the RPAS in "airplane" mode for landing, controlling its flight path into terrain. The RPAS was damaged and removed from service. The RPAS did not cause any damage or injury. The cause for the occurrence is being investigated by the operator.

C-GADO, un Piper PA-46-600TP en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Barrie Lake Simcoe Regional, ON (CYLS) à destination de l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en rapprochement pour CYQB, le pilote a déclaré une urgence en raison d’un problème avec le train d’atterrissage. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre.

C-FFXD, a Morningstar Air Express Incorporated Cessna 208B Caravan airplane, was conducting flight MAL8071 from Vancouver International (CYVR) BC, to Victoria International (CYYJ) BC, with one crew member on board. While in the climb out of CYVR, the flight encountered moderate turbulence from 3000 feet above sea level (ASL) up to approximately 4000 feet ASL. Upon levelling at 4000 feet ASL, the turbulence became severe. The pilot chose to return to CYVR. During descent, the severe turbulence continued until approximately 2000 feet ASL. The aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident and there were no injuries.Maintenance conducted a severe turbulence inspection as per the aircraft maintenance manual and found no damage. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GDIH, a privately registered Cessna 172RG, was conducting night VFR circuits on Runway 27 at Peterborough Airport (CYPQ), ON, with 2 pilots onboard. During the sixth landing, as the nose landing gear touched down, a severe vibration occurred. Both crew subsequently held the elevator control full back to minimize pressure on the nose and brought the aircraft to a stop on the runway. Upon exiting the aircraft, the pilot observed that the nose wheel was missing. The nose landing gear yoke had been damaged as it dragged on the runway during the landing roll. Runway 27 was closed by NOTAM until the aircraft was moved clear of the runway, and an inspection for FOD was carried out. There were no injuries and no other reported damage to the aircraft.

C-FLEJ, a Flair Airlines Boeing 737-86N was conducting flight FLE519 from Region of Waterloo Intl. (CYKF), ON to Orlando Sanford Intl (KSFB), FL.  During approach 09L, ATC advised of a helicopter hovering at threshold on runway 09R.  Flight crew had the traffic visual and receive a TCAS TA (traffic advisory).  At 700' AGL, Flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to ''Level off''.  Flight crew followed RA, confirmed traffic was not converging and landed without further incident.

N674UA, a Boeing 767-322ER aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL925 from London/Heathrow Intl (EGLL), England to Washington/Dulles Intl (KIAD), VA. About 3 hours before landing at KIAD (during cruise flight at about 50°18' N, 052°48' W), the first officer began feeling ill shortly after eating. The captain, who was on a crew rest break, was summoned to the cockpit to assume the flight duties of the ill crew member. The captain and designated international relief officer continued flying the aircraft and landed at KIAD without further incident. The first officer required no further medical attention as they reported feeling better upon landing in KIAD.

C-FNAX, a WestJet Airlines Ltd Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight WS272 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Halifax/ Stanfield Intl. (CYHZ), NS.  During cruise at FL350 approximately 90 nm SSW from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC, flight crew identified pressurization issues.  Flight crew actioned checklist and expedited descent to 10000 feet.  After consultation with flight dispatch, flight crew diverted to CYUL where they landed without further incident. Maintenance identified a fault associated with the APU bleed valve.

C-GNCU, a Beech King Air 200 aircraft operated by North Cariboo Flying Services was conducting flight NCB0860 from Dawson Creek (CYDQ) BC, to Abbotsford International (CYXX) BC with 2 crew and 2 passengers on board. During the descent, air traffic control (ASL) advised the crew there was a Cessna 172 (C-FCQC) operating at 3200 feet ASL which posed a possible conflict. The crew leveled off at 5000 feet ASL to wait for the traffic to pass. While level at 5000 feet ASL, the flight crew received a Traffic Collision Avoiding System (TCAS) resolution advisory (RA) message indicating the traffic was at 5000 feet ASL. The crew was unable to visually acquire the traffic and followed the TCAS instruction and climbed to 5900 feet ASL.  Once clear of traffic, the crew continued the approach and landed without further incident.

C-GEMV, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8M (737 Max) airplane, operating as flight AC235 from Edmonton International (CYEG), AB to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC with 6 crew and 123 passengers on board. While enroute, a passenger experienced what may have been a heart attack. A doctor onboard assisted the flight crew in caring for the passenger. The flight crew declared a Pan Pan emergency for priority handling into CYVR and the flight landed without further incident. Emergency medical services met the aircraft on arrival.

C-GPYW, an Air Pockets Adventures Ltd Cessna 172E, was conducting flight training operations at the Beiseker (CFV2), AB airport. A student and an instructor were performing circuits on Runway 34. After the third dual circuit the instructor had the student stop the plane and authorized the student to conduct several solo circuits. As the student lifted off it was noted that the wind speed had increase significantly as the plane had to be "crabbed" into the wind to maintain runway heading on the climb out. During the first attempt to land the student conducted a "go-a-round" due to the cross wind. On the second landing the student touched down, and then drifted to the left side of the runway and exited in to the grassy ditch. The plane came to a stop in the ditch only after the prop had contacted the ground and stopped the engine. The student was securing the plane when a gust of wind caused the plane to flip on to the roof. The student unbuckled the seatbelt, dropped to the roof and exited the plane un-injured. The plane was substantially damaged. There was no fire.

C-GJEN, a Westjet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited DHC-8-402 aircraft, was operating as flight WEN3154 from Nanaimo (CYCD) BC, to Calgary International (CYYC) AB, with 4 crew members and 39 passengers on board. In the initial climb, through approximately 11 000 feet above sea level (ASL), the cabin pressure warning light illuminated. The crew advised air traffic control that they would be descending to 8000 feet ASL while conducting the actions indicated in the quick reference handbook. The crew were unable to regain control of cabin pressurization and they chose to divert to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC where they landed without further incident.Subsequent maintenance inspections found the aft outflow valve got stuck by the canted bulkhead blowout panel. Maintenance reinstalled the blowout panel and conducted a function check of the outflow valve. The system functioned as designed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJWN, an Air Canada Airbus A321-200 was conducting flight AC1286 from Phoenix Sky Harbor Intl. (KPHX), AZ to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), On.  During take off run on runway 25R, flight crew received a FMGC (Flight Management Guidance Computers) fault.  Flight crew rejected take off at 25kts and declared a PanPan with ATC.  After discussion with Maintenance control, the fault was cleared and flight departed to CYYZ.

C-FLRS, a Boeing 737-800 operated by Flair Airlines, was conducting flight FLE149, from Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, with 6 crew and 157 passengers on board. While flying the STAR behind a B777-300ER, moderate buffet occurred, along with 'Roll Authority' warnings and loss of lateral roll authority, resulting in an uncommanded right bank up to 35 degrees before roll authority was regained. ATC was notified of the incident, and the flight continued, landing uneventfully on runway 06R.

C-GXAI, un Dash 8-314 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif AIE850, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) à destination de Val d’Or, QC (CYVO) avec 3 membres d’équipage et 8 passagers à son bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en approche pour l’atterrissage à CYVO, lors de la sélection du train d’atterrissage en position sortie, le voyant “Gear Unsafe” pour la roue de nez s’est allumé. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN). La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée et la procédure d’extension manuelle du train a été effectuée avec succès L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste sans encombre.

C-GFCP, an Airbus A320-314 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1502 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Moncton/Romeo LeBlanc International Airport (CYQM), NB, with 6 crew and 168 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL370, the flight crew received an ECAM for HYD B ELEC PUMP LO PR. The flight crew completed the appropriate checklist, declared PAN PAN, and elected to return to CYYZ. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by.Maintenance found that the Blue System hydraulic pump had failed. The pump was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GHKC, un Airbus A330-343 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA811 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Humberto Delgado/Lisbonne, Portugal (LPPT) à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ). Alors que l’appareil était en vol de croisière, à environ 313 milles nautiques (NM) au nord-nord-est de l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Qc (CYUL), l’équipage a rapporté avoir un problème avec le système hydraulique. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) et a demandé un déroutement vers CYUL. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre. La piste a été fermée pour permettre le nettoyage de celle-ci.

C-FUSE, a privately registered Piper PA-18-150 aircraft, was conducting a VFR flight to Lucky Lake (CKQ5), SK with only the pilot on board. During the attempted landing on Runway 26 in gusty wind conditions, the pilot conducted a go-around. While climbing through approximately 60 feet AGL, a wind gust caught the aircraft and the aircraft turned to the south. During this turn, the aircraft stalled and subsequently collided with terrain. The pilot, who was wearing a 4-point safety belt, was uninjured. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to its prop, flaps, right gear, and wing tip. The ELT did not activate.

A Laflamme Aero Remotely Piloted Helicopter (RPH) was conducting a test flight to and from a designated test site. While performing a development test flight, after the pilot initiated a slow turn to the right following a straight and level leg, the RPH went into an uncommanded pitch up attitude followed by a level off. The rapid attitude change induced a rupture of the forward rotor mast, following which the RPH struck the ground, The RPH was destroyed by a post impact fire.

C-FIBW, A WestJet Airlines B737-700, was operating as flight WJA461 from Calgary International (CYYC), AB to Kelowna International (CYLW), BC. Shortly after departure from CYYC on Runway 17R, on the BANFF 2 SID, WJA461 was ascending through 9000 feet ASL when the crew received a TCAS RA for conflicting traffic. Separation was reduced to 300 feet vertically and 1.2 nautical miles laterally when 1000 feet vertically and 3 miles laterally is required. The flight crew followed the TCAS RA command. Visual meteorological conditions (VMC) existed at the time of the occurrence, but the flight crew did not have visual contact with the traffic. WJA461 continued enroute to their destination with no further issues.The loss of separation was with SNBD5, a flight of 3 CL41 Department of National Defense Snowbird Air demonstration team aircraft that was inbound from Kelowna (CYLW), BC. SNBD5 was cleared for the IGVEP6 arrival for Runway 17R and was cleared to 10 000 feet ASL. SNBD5 had loaded the IGVEP6 STAR for Runway 35L and as a consequence deviated at VEGSA eastbound rather than continuing northeast bound. The arrival controller climbed SNBD5 back to 10 000 feet ASL and turned the flight to a heading of 070, towards the STAR. Weather conditions were VMC and SNBD5 had WJA461 visual. SNBD5 landed shortly after in CYYC with no further issues.

C-GDPI, un Beechcraft A100 exploité par Propair Inc. sous l’indicatif PRO4600, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Val-d’Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY). Lors de la course au décollage de la fumée est apparue dans l’avion et le décollage a été rejeté. L’avion est ensuite retourné sur l'aire de trafic. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage. L’inspection après l’événement a révélé qu’une petite quantité d’huile à moteur avait été renversée dans le compartiment du moteur et en chauffant a dégagé de la fumée qui a été aspirée par l’entrée d’air.

C-GJAZ, a Jazz Aviation LP MHI RJ Aviation ULC CRJ900 was conducting flight 8853 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Nashville Intl. (KBNA), TN.  During final approach in KBNA 500 feet above ground, Flight crew received a TCAS RA due to another aircraft on the runway.  Flight crew performed a go around and on the second approach received a bird strike on the right leading edge mid slat.  Flight landed in KBNA without further incident. Crew inspected the aircraft and found no damage.

C-FENJ, a DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Westjet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3218 from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON with 4 crew and 61 passengers onboard. While enroute at FL250, in the proximity of Chapleau Municipal Airport (CYLD), ON, the aircraft flew through an area of severe turbulence. The auto-pilot disconnected due to the turbulence, and the aircraft gained 200 feet of altitude. The crew took control of the aircraft and noted that the flight controls were initially slow to respond. Once the crew regained full control, they deviated further away from the weather displayed on their radar, and continued to their destination. The maintenance performed a severe turbulence inspection with no defects found.

C-FGSJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd Boeing 767-300, was conducting flight CJT302 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to  Hamilton/John C. Munro Intl. (CYHM), ON.
