During cruise at FL380 (to stay above weather) approximately 460nm west of Toronto VOR,  Flight crew received IAS DISAGREE amber EICAS (Engine-indicating and crew-alerting system) caution light.  While completing checklist items, flight crew received RUDDER RATIO and AILERON LOCKOUT amber EICAS caution light.  Flight crew informed ATC of issues, requested a block of altitude and deviations as required and declared a MAYDAY.  After completing IAS DISAGREE checklist, flight crew found that left hand airspeed was unreliable and PF was transferred to copilot.  Flight crew was able to restore right hand autopilot, right hand flight director but auto throttle was inoperative.  Flight crew decided to continue to CYHM given the stability of the malfunctions, weather enroute and at destination.  During descent in VMC at FL290, flight crew received R and L ENG EEC EICAS (Electronic Engine Controls) message.  Flight crew completed appropriate checklist which resulted in R and L ENG EEC in Alternate mode.  Also during descent RUDDER RATIO, AILERON LOCKOUT and GND PROX SYS (Ground Proximity Warning System) EICAS advisory appeared and kept reoccurring. Flight landed in CYHM without further incident and was met and inspected by ARFF.  Maintenance replaced LH and RH AOA sensors and also LH ADC.  This occurrence was previously reported as cargo door indication and emergency declaration.

C-GVTA, a Top Aces Inc. Dassault Dornier Alpha Jet, was conducting local training flight with German Air Force from Cuxhaven/ Nordholz-Spieka (ETMN), Germany.  Just after take off, Flight crew received a left-hand engine fire indication.  Flight crew secured engine as per checklist, aircraft was inspected by wingman with no indication of fire detected and PanPan was declared with ATC.  Fuel was consumed thereafter to achieve landing weight and flight landed in ETMN without further incident.Maintenance determined the cause of the issue was contaminant in the left hand engine wiring connector which produced a false indication.

C-GADI, a Beech B300 aircraft operated by Kreos Aviation, was conducting a flight from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl. (CYXE), SK to Regina Intl (CYQR), SK. On approach to CYQR, the nose gear down and locked indication did not illuminate. The flight crew tested the bulbs and they were serviceable. A missed approach was conducted, an emergency was declared, and the flight crew elected to return to CYXE. A manual gear extension procedure was conducted and the aircraft landed uneventfully at CYXE with ARFF standing by.A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance found the nose landing gear down and locked switch contacts were in the open position. A new switch was installed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYSC, a MEDEVAC equipped Beech B200 aircraft operated by Voyageur Aviation Corp., was conducting flight VAL791 from Greater Moncton Roméo LeBlanc Intl (CYQM), NB to Grand Manan Airport (CCN2), NB. While in the initial climb at CYQM, the nurses observed sparks coming from both exhaust ducts of the number 1 engine, and reported this to the flight crew. The flight crew noted that the number 1 engine parameters were normal, and leveled the aircraft at circuit altitude for return to CYQM. The sparks discontinued when power was reduced, and the flight crew contacted ATS to request airport emergency services stand by for the landing. The flight crew were advised by ATS that airport emergency services were not on duty, and would not be available. The flight crew conducted a safety briefing with the 2 nurses on board, and decided to make a full stop on the runway to assess the engine condition. The aircraft landed runway 06 at CYQM without further incident. The engine parameters remained normal, and no further unusual engine operation was noted. The crew taxied to the apron and carried out a normal shut down of the engines.Maintenance personnel carried out borescope inspection of the engine and found no evidence of damage or contact of rotating components.  All subsequent engine test runs reveal normal parameters and it is concluded that carbon buildup in engine hot section was released following this first flight following routine engine maintenance. The engine trend analysis will be continued to be monitored.

C-FRAL, a privately operated Corben Baby Ace homebuilt aircraft, was conducting a local flight from Summerside Airport (CYSU), PE. Upon landing on runway 23 at CYSU, the pilot planned to stop as short as possible so as to be able to quickly vacate the runway for another inbound aircraft. The pilot unintentionally applied asymmetric heel brakes and the tail-wheel aircraft yawed nose left at a rate that could not be arrested. The rapid yaw caused the landing gear to skid on the runway, and the right wing tip struck the runway surface. The subsequent return motion in the roll direction caused the left wing tip to also strike the runway, and the aircraft then nosed over causing a propeller strike and sudden engine stoppage. The aircraft came to rest about 30 feet to the left of the center of the runway. The pilot was the sole occupant, and egressed the aircraft without injury. The winds were from approximately 210 degrees magnetic at less than 10 knots windspeed.The aircraft sustained major damage, with a right-hand flying wire that failed in tension, substantial damage to the right wing tip, and the destruction of the propeller.

C-GNCJ, a Central Mountain Air Limited De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-102, was operating as flight GLR8016 from Smithers (CYYD) BC, to Dease Lake (CYDL) BC, with 3 crew members and 26 passengers on board. 15 minutes into the trip, the flight attendant advised the pilot of smoke in the passenger cabin. The flight crew declared an emergency with air traffic control, requested a return to CYYD, and asked for aircraft rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) to be standing by. The flight landed safely and the ARFF crew, after a rapid deplanement of the airplane, determined that the heat source was no longer present.A maintenance inspection found a connector for a light bulb in an overhead bin showed evidence of electrical arcing and overheating. The aircraft has returned to service.

C-GHKC, an Airbus A330 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA0110 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, with 10 crew and 152 passengers on board. During approach to runway 05, the ECAM (Electronic centralized aircraft monitor) "Brakes-Auto Brakes" fault light illuminated when the landing gear was selected down. The crew elected to go-around, actioned the appropriate checklist, and determined that only the alternate braking system was available for landing. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, requested an alternate runway, and landed uneventfully on runway 15L, with ARFF standing by.

C-GVJT, a Cessna 560 (Ultra) operated by Chartright Air Inc. as flight HRT373, had departed on a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, to Orlando International Airport (KMCO), USA, with 2 crew and 2 passengers on board. During the initial climb through 9700 feet, the crew received a #2 engine fire warning. They leveled off at 10000 feet ASL, actioned the appropriate checklist, which led them to reduce engine power to idle. The crew declared an emergency and requested a return to CYYZ, with a delay to burn enough fuel to reduce the weight below maximum landing weight before making their approach. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. Maintenance determined that there was no evidence of an engine fire, and that the warning was likely a result of a faulty indication.

C-GWEN, a DHC-8-400 operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3539 between Montreal/P.E. Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, and Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, with 4 crew and 74 passengers on board. While enroute at FL220, the crew received a caution tone followed by a #2 DC GEN Caution light. The flight crew declared PAN PAN, actioned the appropriate checklist, and elected to divert to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON. The flight landed uneventfully at CYOW with ARFF standing by. Maintenance replaced the #2 Generator and RL2 Relay. Subsequent tests revealed no further faults and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPCX, a Bell 206L-1 helicopter operated by Provincial Helicopters, was conducting a local flight in the vicinity of Little Grand Rapids (CZGR), MB with one pilot on board. While lining up for touchdown at the CZGR landing pad, the helicopter began to drift backwards. Upon landing the helicopter skids and tail boom made contact with the surface of the ground and the helicopter tail boom sustained damage. There were no injuries.The aircraft was inspected by the operator's technicians for further damage in accordance with Bell manuals. There was substantial structural damage limited to the tail boom skin (wrinkle) and an installation of a new tail boom was completed. The helicopter was tracked and balanced and returned to service.

The privately registered Cessna 185F, C-FCWN, was on a flight from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Nahanni Butte (CBD6), NT when it experienced an engine (Teledyne Continental IO 520D, S/N 22147973D) failure in cruise flight. The aircraft had departed CYZF with full fuel. When the engine stopped running it stopped abruptly without a stumble or roughness. The propeller continued to rotate driven by the airflow. The pilot attempted numerous strategies to restart the engine but was unable to do so. The aircraft was maneuvered to a landing onto the muskeg 43 NM ESE of Fort Simpson (CYSF), NT. The lone occupant, the pilot, was uninjured. Both the ELT and a Garmin Inreach unit broadcast the aircrafts position. Fort Simpson RCMP responded and the pilot was rescued unharmed using a helicopter to access the location.

C-GFWJ, un Cessna 150M exploité par Air Richelieu, effectuait des posés-décollés sur la piste 06R à l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec un élève-pilote à bord. Lors d’un atterrissage, l’appareil a rebondi, l’élève-pilote a tenté une remise des gaz et a perdu la maîtrise de l’avion. Celui-ci s’est retrouvé sur le gazon et a fait une culbute. L’élève-pilote n’a pas été blessé, toutefois l’appareil a subi des dommages importants.

C-GWSQ, un Boeing 737-700 CT exploité par WestJet sous l'indicatif WJA579, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ). Avant le décollage, une instruction de virage après le décollage a été transmise, toutefois le collationnement de l’équipage n’a pas été reçu. Le départ suivant était C-GVDQ, un Airbus Canada Limited Partnership BD-500-1A11 (A220) exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA401 qui effectuait aussi un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de CYUL à CYYZ. Une perte d’espacement est survenue lors de la montée initiale, lorsque l'ACA401 s’est retrouvé momentanément à 2,7 miles marins (nm) derrière le WJA579 à environ la même altitude. L’espacement requis était de 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical et 3 nm sur le plan horizontal. Les 2 appareils ont poursuivi leurs vols à destination de CYYZ.

C-GIAJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 757-200 was conducting flight CJT909 from John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON to Vancouver International airport (CYVR), BC, while climbing from FL290 to FL380 the crew experienced a climb in cabin altitude with the associated EICAS (engine indicating and crew alerting system) message 'Cabin Altitude'. An emergency was declared, the QRH was carried out and the crew descended to 10,000 feet. Decision was made to divert to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB. Upon arrival in CYYC the aircraft was removed from service and placed on AOG (Aircraft on Ground). Maintenance: While troubleshooting all possible systems that could have caused the fault, a DVI of the ECS bay was conducted and the right pack discharge duct coupling was found dislodged from clamp. As this was the first flight after ''C'' Check event, a complete DVI check was carried out on all clamps and duct connections. No additional faults were found.   As an additional measure a Function Check Flight (FCF) was conducted to ensure system confidence with the repair carried. No additional faults noted on the FCF. The aircraft was returned to service and no faults found on subsequent flights.

C-FIUF an Air Canada Boeing 777-200 was conducting flight AC43 from Delhi/Indira Gandhi International Airport (DEL), India to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. When the flight was over Pakistan at FL300 near a large SIGMET (Significant Meteorological Information ) area of thunderstorms, Flight crew reported altitude deviation of approximately 200ft and rapid airspeed fluctuations as a cell rapidly built below them. Flight encountered severe turbulence as a result without injuries to passengers or crew.  Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C- GJXV, un Airbus Canada Limited Partnership BD-500-1A11 (A220) exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA2335 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Montréal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX) à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ) avec 2 pilotes à bord. Lors de la rotation au décollage, l’équipage a ressenti que l’avion tournait anormalement vers la droite et l'équipage a décidé de revenir se poser sur la piste 06 à CYMX. Une urgence a été déclarée et les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre, il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GURG, un Canadair CL60 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec sous l'indicatif QUE10M, effectuait un vol d’évacuation médicale selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Bonaventure QC (CYVB) à destination de Québec/Jean-Lesage Intl., QC (CYQB). Alors que l'appareil était en montée à environ 14000 pieds, une indication de pression d’huile faible au moteur droit est survenue. Le moteur droit a été mis au ralenti et la pression est demeurée stable. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et s’est posé sans encombre à CYQB avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GMWJ, a Westjet Airlines Boeing 737-700 was conducting flight WS1100 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Los Angeles Intl. (KLAX), CA. During the approach phase to KLAX, the crew identified a Trailing Edge (TE) flap transit indication on the flight deck. As per company procedure, the crew actioned the associated Non-Normal checklist (NNC) with the condition. The Flight crew declared an emergency with the associated ATC unit and landed safely shortly thereafter.Maintenance personnel in KLAX performed a detailed visual inspection of the D40024P/D40024J and D275 connectors with NFF. The right hand flap position transmitter/FSEU and the flap position indicator were replaced. The aircraft was then released back to service.

Un Pilatus PC-12 exploité par Panorama Aviation sous l’indicatif PNO727 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Montréal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX) à destination de l’aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) et était en approche RNAV (GNSS) Piste 06L. Au même moment un Jetstream 32 exploité par Pascan sous l’indicatif PSC562 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB) à destination de l’aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU). Une perte d’espacement est survenue lorsque le PSC562 ayant passé le point de cheminement d'approche PIDRI, s’est retrouvé environ à la même altitude et à 2,7 miles marins sur le plan horizontal du PNO727. L’espacement requis était de 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical et 3 nm sur le plan horizontal.

N614FE, a McDonnell Douglas MD-11F operated by FedEx as flight FDX148 between Memphis International Airport (KMEM), USA, and Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario. During descent into CYYZ, the flight crew declared an emergency due to cracked windshield. The aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-GWJG, a Boeing 737-7CT operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA2767 between Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC), Dominican Republic, and Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, with 5 crew and 132 passengers on board. During approach to CYYZ, the flight crew received an annunciation on the flight deck that a LE flap was not in the commanded position. The flight crew elected to go-around and actioned the appropriate checklist before requesting that ARFF be standing by for landing. The aircraft landed uneventfully. Following maintenance inspection, the flap slat electronic unit (FSEU) unit was replaced, and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FPRP, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight SWG634 from Halifax/Robert L. Stanfield Intl. (CYHZ), NS to Varadero/ Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl (MUVR), Cuba.  During descent, flight crew member felt unwell.  After engine shutdown in MUVR, Flight crew member was transported to a local hospital.  Return flight was delayed.

C-GIJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Q400), was conducting flight JZA8350 from Prince George (CYXS) BC, to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR) BC, with 4 crew members and 36 passengers on board. After take-off, when the crew selected landing gear up, the No. 2 ENG HYD caution light illuminated followed by caution lights associated with a total loss of hydraulic quantity in the No. 2 system. The loss of all fluid from No.2 Hydraulic System quick reference handbook checklist was actioned. The crew contacted maintenance control and elected to return to CYXS. A PAN PAN was declared and an alternate gear extension was completed. The airplane landed without further incident.Maintenance found the engine-driven pump (EDP) pressure line elbow at the No. 2 hydraulic manifold was cracked. The No. 2 EDP was replaced and a leak check was carried out IAW AMM29-11-01-400-801 with no faults found. EDP pressure line was repaired IAW AMM20-20-21-350-801 and Service Difficulty Report #2022051014 was submitted.

C-GBHO, an Airbus A319-100, was being operated by Air Canada Rouge from Miami Intl airport (KMIA), FL to Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl - Montreal (CYUL), QC. While taxiing for departure for Runway 08R, ground cleared the aircraft to follow another aircraft via taxiway Q and to hold short of Runway 08R. The aircraft inadvertently crossed the hold line at Taxiway Q and came to a stop short of the M1 hold line and runway.

C-GLRN, a Boeing 737-800 was being operated as Sunwing flight SWG 2872 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Guatemala City/La Aurora Intl. (MGGT), Guatemala. During the RNP Y approach for RWY 02, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to level off. The Pilot Flying disconnected the autopilot and complied with the RA. Since this subsequently left the aircraft high on the approach, the Pilot Flying initiated a missed approach. During the missed approach the flight crew received a TCAS RA to descend. The Pilot Flying complied with the RA. Due to frequency congestion ATC was advised of the two RAs around waypoint GT590. ATC then cleared SWG2872 for the ILS approach. The approach and landing were completed uneventfully.

C-GHFL, a Hughes 369D helicopter operated by West Coast Helicopters Maintenance and Contracting Ltd., was conducting heli-slinging operations 42 nautical miles west northwest of Port McNeill Airport (CAT5), BC, with the pilot side door removed and only the pilot on board. At the pickup site for the load of cedar shake blocks, the pilot maneuvered the aircraft to deliver the empty cargo hook to the ground crew using a 50-foot longline. While hovering over the forestry cut block at approximately 65 feet above ground level, the pilot felt a severe vibration and conducted an emergency landing. The pilot rotated the aircraft 180 degrees and nosed the aircraft onto the hillside. During touchdown, the tail rotor contacted a pile of wood on the ground. The pilot proceeded with a normal engine shutdown with no further incident. The pilot was not injured. The aircraft tail rotor, tail rotor driveshaft, and tail boom were substantially damaged and the aircraft was disassembled for transport back to the operator's hangar facility.

C-FASP, an AirSprint Inc. Cessna 525A was conducting a flight between Raleigh-Durham Intl. (KRDU), NC to Fort Myers/Page Field (KFMY), FL.  After initial descent from FL400, cabin altitude was noted increasing rapidly.  Around FL380, the cabin altitude reached 10000 feet and annunciator CABIN ALT came on.  Flight crew actioned checklist memory items, donned oxygen masks, initiated emergency descent and declared a MAYDAY with ATC.  Internal cockpit communications became severely limited due to the loud squelching of the oxygen mask over the speaker. After checklist was completed, flight crew noted that cabin altitude climb stopped at 14,000 feet cabin altitude.  ATC provided step down descent altitudes incrementally down to 10,000 feet. Once level the flight crew discussed the situation/fuel status and determined that they would land at planned destination. The flight landed in KFMY without further incident.

C-GLYM, un Cessna 177 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Neuville, QC (CNV9) avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage de la piste 24, alors que l’aéronef était encore au-dessus de la piste, le moteur (Lycoming O-320-E2D) s’est arrêté. Une descente fut initiée pour atterrir devant avec un atterrissage prévu près du bout de la piste. À environ 20 pieds au-dessus du sol le moteur a démarré à nouveau et le pilote a pu remonter et éviter les arbres en bout de piste, toutefois le moteur s’est arrêté à nouveau et pilote s’est posé dans un champ situé à droite de l’axe de piste. Les 2 occupants ont subi des blessures mineures, l’aéronef a subi des dommages importants, mais il n’y a pas eu de feu après impact. La radiobalise de repérage d’urgence (ELT) n’a pas été captée par le système d’aide à la recherche et au sauvetage par satellite (SARSAT) et aucun signal d’ELT n’a été rapporté sur la fréquence de 121,5 MHz.

The Alberta Central Airways Beech King Air 200, C-GSWU, was on a flight from Lac LaBiche (CYLB), AB to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB when it experienced a high oil temperature indication on the No.1 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-42). The crew shut down the left engine and declared an emergency. An uneventful single-engine approach and landing was perform at CYEG with ARFF standing by. The crew elected to shutdown on a taxiway and was towed to the hangar.Maintenance update: Avionics technicians determined that the high oil temperature indication was due to a poor wire splice in the wiring harness. Repairs were made and the aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GMWJ, a Boeing 737-7CT aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA9575 from Santiago/Rosalía de Castro Airport (LEST), Spain to St. John's Intl Airport (CYYT), NL. During the approach to Runway 16 at CYYT, the crew received a leading-edge flap transit asymmetry indication. The crew actioned the non-normal checklist and declared an emergency with ATS. The crew conducted a flapless landing at CYYT without further incident.Maintenance personnel replaced the faulty flap position sensor, tested the system, and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FHCJ, a B767-200 aircraft was being operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd., as flight CJT 951 from  Benito Juárez Intl - México Cit (MMMX) to  Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (KCVG). While climbing out of MMMX, through FL290 the crew heard a thud noise coming from the main cargo compartment. The crew also felt a pressure bump in their ears. Both crew immediately looked to the pressure controller and noticed that the cabin rate of climb was well exceeding 1000 feet per minute. Within seconds the cabin pressure altitude climbed in excess of 10000 feet, causing the Cabin Altitude light to illuminate and horn to sound. The captain, already in the Pilot Flying Position, announced to the crew to don their oxygen masks and to establish communications. As the cabin was still climbing at a significant rate, the crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC and requested an immediate descent. Initial descent clearance was given to FL200. An emergency descent was initiated. The aircraft was flying over mountainous terrain at night, so considerations were made for this. The captain requested the QRH for Cabin Altitude. The crew discussed options and it was decided to return to MMMX. The captain utilized the PA to advise the ACMs to don their oxygen masks and advised them of the problem. ATC cleared the crew to PAZ and then to ENAGA for the ENAGA2B arrival for Runway 23L. This is the longest runway at MMMX. Further descent was given when safe and in accordance with the arrival procedure. The crew carried out the QRH procedures for Cabin Altitude and then Cabin Automatic Inoperative. These checklists did not prove able to establish any control of the aircraft pressurization, although the first officer was able to manually move the outflow valve but to no effect. Oxygen masks were removed when cabin altitude was at a safe altitude. Arrival ATC cleared the aircraft for an approach and to switch to tower. The first officer would advise each subsequent controller that they had declared a PAN. The Tower controller advised the crew to maintain 160kias until MX402, the Final Approach Fix. They were number two to the runway for landing. Normal aircraft configuration was done and the QRH Landing Checklist was completed. The tower advised to continue as the previous aircraft was still on the runway. For some reason, the previous aircraft decided to clear at the end of a 13000 runway. When the crew reached decision altitude, no clearance had been given. The first officer could not get a word in edgewise to obtain the clearance. The captain disconnected the autopilot with the hopes of a late clearance but also ready for a go- around. At approximately 100 feet the Captain initiated the missed approach procedure. Clearance to land was given while the aircraft was well established in the initial go around procedure. The crew carried out the published missed approach; ATC provided vectors for a subsequent approach. The missed approach altitude was 12000 feet which triggered the Cabin Altitude Warnings again. The crew donned their oxygen masks again until the aircraft descended as per the approach to a safe cabin altitude. The aircraft approached and landed uneventfully on Runway 23L.

C-GLKY, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 aeroplane operated by Perimeter Aviation LP., was conducting a flight from Oxford House (CYOH), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. While on approach into CYWG, the flight crew received a landing gear unsafe indication related to the nose landing gear. The flight crew carried out the vital actions in accordance with the aircraft flight manual and declared an emergency. The flight crew conducted an alternate extension procedure and were able to extend the nose landing gear. The subsequent landing was uneventful with ARFF standing by. The aircraft was taxied to the apron where the passengers were deplaned.The operator's maintenance personnel replaced the nose gear drag-strut actuator. The nose gear actuator was also replaced as a precaution.

The WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-700, C-GYWJ, operating as WJA170 on a flight from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB experienced a loss of separation with a Cessna 680 Sovereign, C-GHCV, inbound to CYEG from Chicago Midway Intl. (KMDW), IL. WJA170 requested and was cleared for the RNAV Y RWY30 approach. The pilot readback the clearance correctly. WJA170 continued on the downwind instead of turning on the RNAV Y arc. Separation eroded to 2.8 nm and 500 feet when 3.0 nm or 1000 feet was required. Both aircraft landed safely after vectors were given to final.

C-GWRS, a Beechcraft King Air B200 operated by Alberta Central Airways, was conducting a patient transfer flight from Edmonton, AB (CYEG) to Fort McMurray, AB (CYMM) with 2 pilots and 3 passengers on board. During the initial approach into the CYMM area, when the crew selected landing gear down, they did not receive a nose landing gear down and locked indication. The flight crew executed a missed approach, and entered a hold to execute the appropriate checklist. After consultation with company personnel, the decision was made to return to CYEG. During the approach into CYEG the flight crew again extended the landing gear and the nose landing gear did not indicate down and locked. The pilots subsequently performed a flyby of the control tower to allow for a visual indication that the nose landing gear was extended. The crew requested airport rescue and fire fighting to be on standby for the landing. An uneventful landing was completed.  Troubleshooting discovered a failed nose landing gear downlock switch. The switch was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GILY, a Piper PA-44 operated by the Cooking Lake Aviation Academy was conducting a local IFR training flight from Cooking Lake, AB (CEZ3) with an instructor pilot and student pilot on board. C-FWGA, a privately registered Canadian Car and Foundry Harvard 4, was conducting a local VFR recreational flight from CEZ3 with only the pilot on board. As the pilot of C-FWGA returned to CEZ3 from the Beaverhill Lake area, the pilot of C-GILY was conducting an IFR flight within 2 nm of the SAVID way point, which is approximately 10 nm East of CEZ3. The pilots of both aircraft were monitoring 123.2 MHz, which is the frequency for both CEZ3 and Tofield, AB (CEV7). The pilot of C-GILY was informed by NAV CANADA terminal controller of possible traffic in the vicinity. A radio call was made on 123.2 MHz, to which no response was received. The pilot of C-GILY subsequently visually spotted the traffic (C-FWGA) and performed avoiding maneuvers. The pilot of C-FWGA did not have visual contact with C-GILY and continued the approach and landing to CEZ3.

C-GLKD, a privately registered Piper PA-28-140, departed Dryden (CYHD), ON on a VFR flight to Marathon (CYSP), ON. The aircraft was reported overdue at 0539Z. JRCC subsequently found the aircraft had collided with terrain approximately 20 NM southeast of Sioux Lookout, ON (CYXL) and was substantially damaged. The 4 occupants of the aircraft were fatally injured. The TSB has deployed investigators to the site.

C-GUZD, a Pacific Rim Aviation Academy Textron (Cessna) 172N, was conducting circuit training at Pitt Meadows Airport (CYPK) BC, with only the student pilot onboard. The student pilot conducted 2 successful touch-and-go landings on Runway 26L. Immediately prior to the third touch-and-go landing, the air traffic controller reported winds to the pilot as 050° magnetic at 5 knots (a quartering tailwind from the right). The aircraft touched down approximately 650 feet past the runway threshold. During the landing roll, the student pilot retracted the flaps and closed the carburetor heat. The aircraft drifted left and departed the paved surface, striking an airport sign with the left wing strut, left main landing gear, and the horizontal stabilizer during the excursion. The aircraft came to rest in the vicinity of the Runway 36 threshold. The ELT did not activate. There were no injuries. Subsequent maintenance inspection by the operator found damage to the left wing strut, left wing main spar, horizontal stabilizer, left main landing gear wheel, and the engine firewall.

C-GDDJ, a Wilderness Seaplanes Limited Grumman G-21A (Goose) amphibious airplane, was conducting a local company training flight from Port Hardy (CYZT) BC with 2 flight crew members on board. During cruise flight, the right engine (Pratt & Whitney-USA R-985-AN-14B) began making abnormal exhaust noises. The engine was shut down as a precaution and the flight returned to CYZT. The flight crew declared an emergency with the CYZT flight service station and landed without further incident. There were no injuries.Subsequent maintenance actions found the right engine’s no. 5 cylinder exhaust segment flange was broken and had separated from the no. 5 cylinder exhaust stub. The segment was replaced and the aircraft returned to service. The operator has submitted a service difficulty report and is conducting a fleet campaign inspection of the remaining aircraft.

C-GJNL, un DHC-8-311 exploité par Hydro-Québec, effectuait le vol HYD400 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) avec 2 membres d’équipage et 2 personnels de maintenance à bord. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en montée initiale, l'équipage a constaté des fluctuations dans les paramètres du moteur droit. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée et le moteur a été éteint. Une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée et un retour vers CYUL a été effectué. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre à CYUL. Aucun blessé.

C-GNVJ, a Piper PA-31-325 aircraft, (138883 Canada Inc.) on a flight from Islesboro, ME, to Sanford, ME (KSFM) declared an emergency due to both alternators failing. The crew diverted the aircraft, landed, and taxied to the ramp uneventfully at Worcester, MA (KORH).

C-FZKH, a Piper PA-44-180, operated by CANLink Aviation Inc. was on initial approach for Runway 23 at Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS and was given a speed restriction of 150 knots inbound until reaching the MITIK final approach fix (FAF). After being handed over from Moncton Area Control Centre to the CYHZ tower, C-FZKH slowed below the 150 knot speed restriction prior to reaching the MITIK FAF. At the same time, C-GSLC, a Cessna 560XLS was inbound to land at CYHZ and was overtaking C-FZKH. The YHZ tower controller attempted to maintain separation by slowing and turning C-GSLC to the south. The loss of separation occurred with both aircraft at the same altitude and the lateral separation reduced to 1.6 nm before C-GSLC made the turn. The required separation limit is 3 nm laterally or 1000 feet vertically.

C-FIBW, a B737 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting a flight from Hartsfield - Jackson Atlanta Intl (KATL) to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. Near PEMDU waypoint, approximately 57nm NE of Havre City County airport (KHVR), the aircraft encountered moderate turbulence resulting in a minor injury to a cabin crew member, who then was unable to perform their duties. Other cabin crew assumed their duties for the remainder of the flight to CYYC.

The Porter Airlines Inc. DHC-8-400 aircraft (POE630, C-GLQE) was on route from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, and had just levelled off in cruise flight. Shortly afterwards, the flight crew received a #2 ENG HYD PUMP caution light followed by #2 HYD ISO VLV, ENG #2 HYD valve closed advisory light, PTU fail light, and a no hydraulic quantity indication for the #2 system. Hydraulic pressure on the #2 system was indicating zero. The flight crew actioned the QRH procedures for a complete #2 Hydraulic system failure and declared a PAN PAN and briefed the cabin crew. Following discussions with company the crew decided to return to CYQT. The crew requested for ARFF to meet and inspect the aircraft upon landing, and maintenance to tow and pin the landing gear. An alternate gear extension was performed and the landing was uneventful.Maintenance reported finding the bleed valve on the #2 reservoir in the bleed position, this resulted in the hydraulic fluid from the #2 system to be depleted. Maintenance replaced the bleed valve and the #2 EDP since it was operating for a period of time without hydraulic fluid.

C-GUAI, un De Havilland DHC-8-300 (DH8C) exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE866, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Salluit, QC (CYZG) à destination de La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL). C-FYAI, un De Havilland DHC-8-300 (DH8C) exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE802, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Umiujaq, QC (CYMU) à destination d’Inukjuak, Québec (CYPH). Alors que le vol AIE866 était en palier à 16 000 pieds en conditions de vol aux instruments (IMC), l’équipage a reçu un avis de trafic (TA) du système de surveillance du trafic et d'évitement des collisions (TCAS). L’équipage a alors communiqué leur position sur la fréquence 126,7 MHz. Au même moment, le TA est devenu un avis de résolution (RA). L’équipage a suivi les directives du TCAS et a immédiatement amorcé une montée. AIE802 qui était en montée pour 16 000 pieds, a reçu l’avis TA et lorsque l’équipage a entendu le rapport de position d’AIE802, le TA est devenu un RA et l’équipage a suivi les directives du TCAS et a immédiatement amorcé une mise en palier. Les équipages n’ont pas eu de contact visuel avec le trafic en conflit. Les 2 aéronefs se sont posés sans incident. Aucun blessé.

C-GEGP, an A330 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC833 from Brussels (EBBR) to Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl - Montreal (CYUL), QC. During the top of climb a cabin crew member became ill and discontinued duties; other cabin crew members assumed their duties for the remainder of the flight to CYUL.

C-FNND, an Air Canada Boeing 777-200 was conducting flight AC0048 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to New Delhi/Indira Gandhi Intl. (VIDP), India.  During approach, flight crew received a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory).  Flight crew followed the RA and continued to destination without further incident.

N436NA, a Lockheed HC130H was conducting National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) flight 436 from Stockholm Arlanda Airport (ESSA) Sweden to the Goose Bay Airport (CYYR) NL. Approximately 450nm NE of CYYR, the #4 engine experienced a loss of oil pressure. A secondary visual inspection of the engine confirmed the loss of oil which necessitated an immediate engine shutdown.  The engine was secured, a PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft descended to 21,000 feet, the three-engine cruise service ceiling, to continue to CYYR. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 26 at CYYR at 1558 UTC.Maintenance has identified that a shear stud on the accessory drive mounting plate for the external oil scavenge pump gave way leading to a blow out of an o’ring gasket and further shearing of a second left-hand stud.  The studs are meant to shear to prevent further engine damage.  Maintenance is awaiting parts for the repair.

C-GQBQ, un Canadair CL600-2B16 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Gouvernement du Québec sous l'indicatif QUE20, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en montée initiale, lors de la sélection des volets en position montés, une indication de « FLAP FAIL » est apparue et les volets sont restés à la position 20°. L'équipage a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée par précaution. L'appareil a continué sa route vers CYQB et s'est posé sans encombre. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

On 24 April 2022, a FLYGTA Inc. Embraer EMB-505 Phenom 300 (registration C-GNSB) was operating as flight TOR803 from Fort Lauderdale Executive Airport (KFXE), FL to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON with 2 crew and 4 passengers onboard. At approximately 2200 UTC, and approximately 100 NM S of Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) the flight crew noticed a Flap Fail Fault. After consulting the checklist,  considering runway length and available maintenance services between CYHM and CYYZ, the flight crew requested to divert to CYYZ. The crew requested priority handling but did not declare an emergency. The aircraft landed safely in CYYZ on Runway 33 Left at 22:37.The aircraft was inspected and a systems check confirmed a fault in software. The fault was rectified and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GQMS, a Mooney M20K, was operating on a round robin IFR flight plan from Springbank (CYBW), AB with two pilots on board. During the RNAV approach to Runway 35, the pilot in command contacted ATC and informed them that the aircraft was accumulating some ice and requested a lower altitude. The aircrafts altitude continued to decrease until the aircraft struck the ground approximately 0.6 nm short of Runway 35, on the extended runway center line. The pilot in the left seat sustained fatal injuries, the pilot in the right seat received serious injuries. There was no post-impact fire.

C-GTYV, a Valley Helicopters Limited Bell 206B helicopter, was conducting a local charter flight from Spius Creek 15NM WSW of Merritt (CAD5) BC, with the pilot and two passengers on board. As the helicopter lifted off, it began to shudder and had compressor stalls. The pilot immediately landed, shut down the helicopter, and egressed with the passengers. A small fire that ignited near a ruptured hydraulic line was extinguished by the pilot. There were no injuries.Maintenance inspected the helicopter and determined that the wire which connects the transmission chip detectors had chafed against the braided metal shielding of a hydraulic line. This caused electrical arcing which melted the hydraulic hose which led to the hydraulic leak and subsequent fire. The compressor stalls were likely a result of the melted debris from the particle separator and hydraulic fluid entering the intake. An inspection of the companies other Bell 206 helicopters was conducted to ensure appropriate routing of the chip detector wiring.

C-FMCN, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Beech 1900D was conducting flight PCO9192 from Victoria International (CYYJ), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 2 crew members and 5 passengers on board. Immediately after aircraft rotation, the aircraft experienced an electrical failure. Multiple annunciator lights illuminated, including the L GEN TIE OPEN, BATT TIE OPEN, and R GEN TIE OPEN caution lights. The flight crew continued the takeoff, but could not retract the landing gear and determined multiple flight instruments were providing erroneous indications. Following the checklists, it was determined that the electrical voltage of the aircraft's center bus was zero. After consulting with maintenance, the flight crew declared PAN PAN with air traffic control and continued to CYVR under visual flight conditions. The flight landed without further incident. There were no injuries.Subsequent maintenance activities by the operator could not duplicate the failure after aircraft electrical power was reset. The operator removed and replaced the main battery and the bus tie printed circuit boards for evaluation. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GEZJ, an Air Transat Airbus A321-211 was conducting flight TSC557 from Varadero/Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl. (MUVR), Cuba to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. Flight crew requested a descent due to turbulence in vicinity of Jacksonville Intl. (KJAX), FL. During the descent from FL310 to FL280 flight crew received a TCAS TA (Traffic Advisory) followed by RA (Resolution Advisory). Flight crew followed the RA and once cleared of traffic, ATC apologized due to confusion with another Air Transat flight. Flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GOIF, an Air Transat Airbus A321-271NX was conducting flight TSC928 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL.  During descent in vicinity of Jacksonville Intl. (KJAX), FL, flight crew received a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory) just before level off at the assigned altitude.  Flight crew followed the RA and flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GEKZ, an Air Canada Boeing 737 Max 8 was conducting flight ACA1054 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Phoenix Sky Harbor Intl. (KPHX), AZ.  During approach, flight crew received a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory).  Flight crew followed the RA and landed without further incident.

C-GMFG, a privately registered Cessna A185F was on a local flight from Toronto/Buttonville Municipal Airport (CYKZ), ON. The pilot was the sole occupant onboard. On final approach to runway 15, the engine reportedly lost power. The aircraft descended and the left wing struck a lamp post located on the east side of highway 404, separating from the fuselage. The aircraft impacted the ground, and came to rest approximately 750 feet before the start of the runway, near the off ramp for highway 404 and sustained substantial damage. There were no injuries.

The WestJet Boeing 737-8 (MAX), C-FRYV, was operating as flight WJA178 from Vancouver (CYVR), BC to Edmonton (CYEG), AB. While en route a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform their duties. The duties were distributed among the other cabin crew for landing. EMS was not required and no emergency was declared.

C-GANR, un SAAB 340B exploité par Pascan Aviation sous l'indicatif PSC478, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport des Îles-de-la-Madeleine, QC (CYGR) à destination de l'aéroport de Gaspé, QC (CYGP) avec 11 passagers et 3 membres d'équipage à bord. La météo se dégradant et suite à un problème avec le système de dégivrage, l'équipage ont pris la décision de dérouter vers l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). À environs 30 miles au sud de l'aéroport de Mont-Joli, Qc (CYYY) FL160, le moteur droit s'est arrêté sans indications ou fluctuations préalables. Une urgence mécanique a été déclarée (PAN PAN) et le vol a été redirigé vers CYYY. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Un redémarrage du moteur droit n'a pas été tenté avant l'atterrissage dù à la proximité avec l'aéroport. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.L'appareil a été cloué au sol et des techniciens ont décelé une défectuosité lors du test d'allumage automatique (AUTO-IGN)Le Digital Electronic Control Unit (DECU) du moteur affecté a été remplacé.

C-GJJK, an Air Tractor AT802 aircraft operated by Forest Protection Ltd was conducting a local training flight at Fredericton International Airport (CYFC), NB. The crew was conducting circuits on Runway 27 and on downwind, when checking the brake pressure, the right brake felt soft. However, the pressure came back to normal when the pilot pumped the pedal with toe pressure. On the landing rollout the aircraft slowed, however began drifting left due to weather-cocking. When the pilot corrected by depressing the right brake, the pedal went to the floor. The pilot used power and reverse to maintain directional control. The aircraft continued to drift left and exited the side of the runway into the grass, approximately 10 feet from the edge. The tower asked if the crew required assistance, and the decision was made to shut down and be towed back to the hangar by maintenance.Maintenance noted the O-ring was kinked on the right brake cylinder and fluid had leaked. The brake was secured and towed back to the hangar. No injuries or any other damage to the aircraft was noted.

The Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 757-200 cargo aircraft (CJT910, C-GTCJ) was on route from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR) to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM). While in cruise at FL390 and approximately 60 minutes before the beginning of the descent the crew noticed an abnormal difference in parameters between the two engines. The indications continued to get worse and after consultation with MCC and completing the QRH procedures, the crew declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. Maintenance determined that the #1 engine was indicating erroneous parameters. Troubleshooting led to the replacement of the P1 probe. Subsequent flights revealed no further faults, although MCC will keep monitoring the engine.

C-FAVO, a Buffalo Airways Ltd. Curtiss-Wright C-46, was operating as flight BFL311 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Hay River (CYHY), NT. BFL311 departed Runway 34 and declared MAYDAY shortly after take-off due to the left engine (Pratt & Whitney USA, R-2800-51M1) surging. The aircraft joined the circuit and landed on Runway 34 without further issues. The flight crew received no injuries. Company maintenance replaced the engine carburetor and fuel pump.

C-GVMP, a Morningstar Partners Ltd. dba Textron Hawker 900XP, was conducting flight 24782 from Palm Spring Intl. (KPSP), CA to Prince George (CYXS), BC.  During cruise approximately 80 NM south of Reno/Tahoe Intl. (KRNO), NV, flight crew observed right hand engine oil pressure at 56 psi (yellow band).  Within a few second it had dropped to 49 psi.  Flight crew actioned checklist, shutdown the right hand engine, declared an emergency and diverted to KRNO.  Flight landed without further incident.  After parking in KRNO, a large oil leak was observed under #2 engine cowling.

C-FFPA, un Jetstream 3212 exploité par Pascan Aviation sous l'indicatif PSC837, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) à destination de Bagotteville, QC (CYBG), avec 8 passagers et 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de l’approche pour la piste 11 à CYBG, l'équipage a tenté de sortir les volets sans succès. L’équipage a interrompu l'approche et demandé un espace de travail au nord de l'aéroport. Après avoir effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) associée et, après avoir confirmé que la longueur de piste disponible permettait un atterrissage sécuritaire sans volet, l'équipage a effectué une 2e approche. Une urgence a été déclarée (PAN PAN) et l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre à CYBG. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage.Lors de l'inspection effectué par la maintenance, le disjoncteur “FLAPS CONT” a été trouvé déclenché et le contrôle des volets a été remplacé.

C-GQBQ, un Canadair CL600-2B16 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Gouvernement du Québec, sous l’indicatif QUE20M, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Rimouski, QC (CYXK) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en approche, lors de la sélection du train d'atterrissage en position sortie, une indication de train avant non sécurisé est apparue. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et une urgence a été déclarée. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre après vérification visuelle de la tour. L'ampoule d'indication de train avant sorti a été remplacée par la maintenance. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GEWK, a privately registered PA-24-250 (Piper Comanche 250), departed Delhi Aerodrome (CDH6), Ontario, at approximately 1535 EST on 14 April 2022, with two private pilots on board, for a VFR flight to Marathon Airport (CYSP), Ontario; the first leg of a flight to Lethbridge Airport (CYQL), Alberta, where the aircraft would be based following a recent change in ownership. When the pilots did not report their arrival at CYSP, Nav Canada initiated steps to locate the overdue aircraft at airports along its proposed route of flight, and via telephone; they were not successful in locating the aircraft. The last known position of the aircraft was derived from ADS-B data; at 1803 EST the aircraft was approximately 15 nm south of Wawa Airport (CYXZ), Ontario. The JRCC took over, and searched over the next 10 days with a number of aircraft and helicopters, in addition to ground searches. The conditions were difficult, as the area included rough terrain with significant snow cover, and additional snowfall occurred during the early days of the search. On 24 April, JRCC suspended their search efforts. The search was turned over to the Ontario Provincial Police as a missing persons case.

The Cessna 182H (C-FGDJ) was landing in Smith Falls, Ontario (CYSH) after a flight from Gananoque, Ontario (CNN8). The flight was to reposition the aircraft for an upcoming 50 hour inspection. Crosswind conditions existed during the touchdown and the aircraft bounced and landed hard on the nose landing gear, resulting in propeller contact with the runway and substantial buckling in the nose gear area. The pilot was not injured during the event.

The Thunder Airlines Beechcraft A100 aircraft (THU103, C-GYQK) departed Moosonee, Ontario (CYMO) destined for Fort Albany, Ontario (CYFA). The flight was conducted under VFR conditions; during the approach the First Officer selected the landing gear down, however there was no movement from the landing gear and no gear lights illuminated. The flight crew followed the QRH procedures and manually lowered the landing gear, and observed three green lights, indicating the gear was down and locked. The flight returned to CYMO, and the passengers were briefed on the situation and a landing was performed on Runway 24. During touchdown, the flight crew heard an unusual noise from the left main gear location and felt the left wing begin to drop. The left main gear green indicator light also extinguished. The Captain immediately aborted the landing, applied engine power, and became airborne, reportedly without any other parts of the aircraft coming into contact with the runway. The flight crew decided to divert to Timmins Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON, a main base for the operator with emergency services, since the aircraft had sufficient fuel and VFR conditions existed throughout the route. The flight crew declared an emergency and proceeded to land on Runway 21. The aircraft touched down on the nose and right landing gear and settled on the left side of the belly pod. The aircraft skidded until it stopped at the intersection of Runway 10/28. All occupants exited the aircraft and no injuries were reported. The airport was closed until the aircraft had been removed to a local hangar. The TSB is coordinating with the operator on the cause of the landing gear malfunction.

C-FFXD, a Morningstar Air Express Incorporated Cessna 208B Caravan airplane, was conducting flight MAL8051 from Nanaimo (CYCD), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with one crew member on board. While in the climb, on the Ladysmith 2 Standard Instrument Departure (SID), the flight encountered severe turbulence from 2000 feet above sea level (ASL) up to approximately 5000 feet ASL. The pilot experienced negative G loading and temporary loss of control. Once clear of the turbulence, the aircraft continued to CYVR and landed without incident. There were no injuries.Maintenance conducted a severe turbulence inspection as per the aircraft maintenance manual and found no damage. The aircraft was returned to service.

VQ-BWM, a Boeing 747-406M freighter aircraft operated by Longtail Aviation International Ltd., was conducting cargo flight LGT5535 from New York/John F. Kennedy Intl (KJFK), NY to Maastricht Aachen Airport (EHBK), Netherlands. When in cruise flight at about 52°00' N, 035°00' W, the flight crew observed number 3 engine N1, N2 and EGT parameters becoming erratic, with large thrust lever movements commanded by the autothrottle. The crew noted no unusual vibrations and no engine limits were exceeded, however the number 3 thrust engine would not follow thrust lever manual inputs. The QRH memory actions for ENGINE LIMIT OR SURGE OR STALL were carried out and the number 3 engine was shut down in accordance with the checklist. The crew declared PAN PAN and examined weather for their diversion decision. The crew elected to continue toward Shannon, Ireland, with an eventual diversion to Liège Intl Airport (EBLG), Belgium where a landing was made without further incident.Maintenance personnel determined that the number 3 engine thrust lever resolver was unserviceable. The resolver was replaced, its wiring installation to the EEC was tested, and operational checks of the system were successfully carried out before returning the aircraft to service.

C-FNJH, a privately owned Colonial C-2X amphibious aircraft was on route from John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON, to Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON with two souls on board. While in cruise the aircraft lost electrical power. The pilot turned off all non-essential power and was provided priority for the landing at CYTZ. The landing gear was extended on approach and the pilot observed a landing gear down and locked indication. This was confirmed by the pilot visually checking the exterior mirror to confirm the landing gear was down. After touchdown the right hand landing gear collapsed and the aircraft slid to a stop on the grass by the intersection of Runway 26 and Foxtrot taxiway. There were no injuries but the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FKSL, un Saab 340B exploité par Pascan Aviation, effectuait le vol PSC581 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 12 passagers à bord. Après avoir activé le pilote automatique lors de la monté initiale, le voyant principal d'alarme (Master Warning) s'est déclenché suivi d'un avis de compensation automatique (Auto Trim). Le pilote a alors désenclenché le pilote automatique et repris le contrôle manuel de l'appareil. Une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclaré et suivi d'un "Standby". Après avoir pris conscience du problème et avoir stabilisé le vol, l'équipage a demandé un retour à CYHU où l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.Après inspection de l'aéronef par la maintenance, l'ordinateur de contrôle de vol a été remplacé.

C-GPEP, a privately owned PZL Wilga aircraft  was on route from Timmins, Ontario (CYTS) to Sault Ste Marie, Ontario (CYAM) with the pilot as the sole occupant. The aircraft had been filled with 52 gallons of fuel prior to departure and the pilot/owner determined it was sufficient fuel to reach CYAM. On route, the aircraft encountered head winds which increased fuel consumption. Power was reduced and mixture leaned to increase range but as the aircraft approached CYAM the pilot reported minimum fuel to the tower and was provided a straight in approach. Prior to the approach the engine quit due to fuel exhaustion and the pilot performed a forced landing in an area covered with small trees. The pilot was not injured but the aircraft suffered substantial damage. This was the pilot's first flight since obtaining the aircraft.

C-GJZG, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Q 400), operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8161 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR) BC, to Victoria Intl (CYYJ) BC, with 4 crew and 27 passengers on board. Shortly after take off, in the climb through approximately 1000 feet above sea level, the cargo door handle released which caused a loss of pressurization and the master caution light to come on. The crew declared an emergency, returned to CYVR and landed without incident.Maintenance determined that the cargo door handle had opened but the door hooks had remained on the latches. The door mechanism was tested and found serviceable.  No faults were found with the door handle or door assembly.

C-GMXD, un Pilatus PC12/47E exploité par Air Medic, effectuait le vol d'évacuation médicale AM267 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Chisasibi, QC (CSU2) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec 2 membres d'équipage, deux spécialistes médicaux, un patient et un accompagnateur à son bord. Suite à des fluctuations de pressurisation, l'équipage a quitté son altitude de croisière de       15 000 pieds au-dessus du niveau de la mer (ASL) pour maintenir 9000 pieds (ASL) afin de maintenir une altitude cabine de 2000 pieds pour le patient. À 1911Z, l'équipage a déclaré "Carburant Minimum pour CYHU" avec le Centre de contrôle de Montréal, la consommation de carburant étant plus élevée en raison de l'altitude de vol plus basse. L'équipage a demandé une priorité sans toutefois déclarer d'urgence. Suite à la résorbtion des problèmes de pressurisation, l'aéronef a pu remonter à 13000 pieds. L'appareil s'est posé sans problème à 1851Z. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GXNF, a Kisik Aerial Survey limited Piper PA-23-250 (Aztec), was engaged in aerial survey work on a return flight from Boundary Bay (CZBB) BC, with the pilot and a crew member on board. The pilot selected the fuel selector from the outboard to the inboard fuel tanks. Approximately 10 minutes later, the right engine (AVCO LYCOMING, TIO-540-C1A) began to surge. The pilot performed the action required by the aircraft checklists and, after selecting the fuel to cross-feed, restored smooth operation of the right engine. The pilot then advised the air traffic controller that they had an emergency, terminated the survey mission, and landed at CZBB. Once on the ground, when the cross-feed valve was closed, the right engine quit.A maintenance inspection found the lever in the cockpit from the fuel selector switch to the fuel tank selection valve was broken. The engine had continued to draw fuel from the outboard tank until it surged. The airplane has been removed from service pending delivery and installation of a replacement cable. A service difficulty report was submitted.

C-GFJZ, an JAZZ Aviation LP MHI RJ Aviation ULC CRJ900 was conducting flight 8772 from San Diego Intl. (KSAN), CA to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC. While boarding in KSAN, a flight attendant became incapacitated.  Duties were redistributed and flight left for CYVR without further incident.

C-GWRG, a West Jet Airlines Ltd Boeing 737-8CT was conducting flight WJA1877 from Maui/Kahului (PHOG), HI to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC.  Approximately 250nm SW of CYVR during cruise, a flight attendant became incapacitated.  Duties were redistributed and flight landed in CYVR without further incident.

C-GJBV, un Beech A100 exploité par Sky Jet M. G. sous l’indicatif de vol SJ512, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Qc (CYUL) à destination de Trois Rivières, Qc (CYRQ). Alors que l’appareil se trouvait à proximité du point SINRO (environ 27 milles nautiques au nord-nord-est de CYUL), l’équipage a demandé un retour vers CYUL en raison de fumée dans le poste de pilotage. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été mis en alerte. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre et il n’y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GVIM, un Learjet 45 exploité par Aviation Starlink Inc. sous l’indicatif TLK557, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Qc (CYUL) à destination de Teterboro, NJ (KTEB) aux États-Unis. En route vers KTEB, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) en raison d’une fissure dans le pare-brise. L’équipage a ensuite demandé un retour à CYUL. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre et il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FKEJ, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by Keewatin Air LP as flight KEW202, was enroute from York Landing (CZAC), MB to Thompson (CYTH), MB with a crew of 2 and 2 passengers onboard. While on descent into CYTH, the crew selected the landing gear down and did not receive a down and locked indication for the left main gear. The crew conducted a missed approach and elected to flyby the Flight Service Station (FSS) to confirm that the left main gear was extended. FSS advised that all three landing gear appeared extended. The crew completed a manual gear extension and then declared an emergency. The aircraft then landed safely and came to a full stop after roll out on the runway. The aircraft was inspected by the operator's maintenance staff and confirmed that the left main gear was locked. The aircraft was then towed off the runway and pulled to the operator's maintenance facility for further inspection. The operator advised that the left main gear down and locked microswitch was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJOU, an Airbus A321 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1662 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, to Southwest Florida International Airport (KRSW), USA, with 6 crew and 171 passengers on board. During the early part of the takeoff roll, the flight crew detected asymmetric thrust and rejected the takeoff at low speed. The flight crew exited the runway and carried out an assessment of the aircraft systems and configuration and departed normally shortly thereafter. An Airbus 330 had departed the runway just prior to the rejected takeoff.

C-FVFN, A Beech 200 aircraft operated by Vanguard Air Care as flight VN06, was enroute from Little Grand Rapids (CZGR), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB with a crew of 2 and 2 passengers onboard. While on decent through 4000 feet into CYWG, the crew received a fire indication of the right engine and then declared a MAYDAY. All engine indications in the cockpit appeared normal and, shortly after, the fire indication went out. The crew landed the aircraft with both engines running and after exiting the runway, shut down both engines. Emergency services responded and confirmed there was no evidence of fire. The aircraft taxied to the operator's facility for further inspection.

C-FTID, a Canadian North ATR 42-500, was operating as flight AKT601 from Merlyn Carter (CYHY) airport in Hay River, NT to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT. During cruise, approximately 30 NM from CYZF, the number 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney-Canada PW127F) began to exceed torque and the interstage turbine temperature (ITT) limits. The flight crew ran the applicable checklists and reduced power on the engine. While at the reduced power setting the engine power began to fluctuate. The crew completed a shutdown of the No. 1 engine, declared an emergency and completed a single-engine approach and landing in CYZF with no further issues. The aircraft taxied to the ramp.

C-GAGS, a privately registered Van's RV-4, was conducting a local flight from Pitt Meadows Airport (CYPK) BC, with the pilot and 1 passenger onboard. During a low altitude pass near North Beach on Alouette Lake, the aircraft impacted the water but was able to become airborne again. The propeller was damaged during the impact and the engine began vibrating. When the pilot reduced power, the engine (Avco Lycoming O-320-E2D) failed catastrophically. The pilot opened the canopy as he glided the aircraft to a ditching in the lake where it remained upright after impact. The pilot assisted the passenger in egressing from the aircraft. The airplane rapidly sank and the pilot and passenger swam approximately 40 feet to the shore. The occupants were initially assisted by nearby kayakers and subsequently were transported to South Beach by a recreational boater. They were met by BC ambulance service attendants. Both pilot and passenger were examined and transported to a local hospital with minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged and a recovery is being planned.

C-FCJD, a Dehavilland DHC-8-102 operated by Air Creebec Inc., was conducting flight CRQ 841, an IFR flight from Fort Albany Airport (CYFA), ON, to Moosonee Airport (CYMO), ON, with 3 crew and 16 passengers on board. During the RNAV approach to Runway 06 at CYMO, the number 1 (left) engine low oil pressure light illuminated. As the flight crew was actioning their checklist, which involved shutting down the engine, a TAWS warning occurred, after which they carried out a single-engine missed approach in instrument meteorological conditions. After levelling off at the missed approach altitude, the number 2 (right) engine low oil pressure light illuminated briefly. The flight crew discussed their options and set up to fly the RNAV to Runway 06 for a second time. A single-engine landing was carried out on Runway 06 without further incident.

C-GJLR, a Novajet Gulfstream G200, was conducting flight 95372 from Las Vegas/Harry Reid Intl. (KLAS), NV to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During cruise in vicinity of Denver Intl. (KDEN), CO, the flight crew noticed the cabin altitude was fluctuating between 7800 and 8700 with cabin climb rate of approximately 2000'/min while in cruise at FL370.  The cabin altitude reached 11,000', the ''Altitude high cabin altitude'' warning annunciated followed by cabin masks being deployed for the passengers.  The flight crew donned their mask, completed the appropriate checklists, declared an emergency, descended to a lower altitude and requested diversion to KDEN.  Flight crew visually verified the passengers masks were donned and flight landed in KDEN without further incident.  Maintenance is investigating the cause.

C-GJLC, a McDonnell Douglas 369D (Hughes 500D), operated by Kestrel Helicopters Limited, was conducting heli-slinging operations 25 NM ESE of Port McNeil (CAT5), BC with only the pilot on board. After releasing a bundle of cedar shake blocks, the pilot declared a Mayday on the FM radio to his ground crew. The groundcrew arrived at the helicopter shortly thereafter. The helicopter was substantially damaged. The pilot was fatally injured. The ELT activated and the signal information was relayed to the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre in Victoria, BC. A search and rescue helicopter was dispatched to the site and the RCMP responded.

C-GKLK, a Carson Air Limited Fairchild SA227-AC, was conducting an IFR flight from Calgary (CYYC), AB, to Kelowna (CYLW) BC, with 2 flight crew on board. During the cruise portion of the flight, approximately 110nm east of CYLW, the flight crew observed the left and right hydraulic pressure warning lights illuminate. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklists and declared a mayday. On approach into CYLW the crew manually extended the landing gear. The aircraft landed and taxied clear of the runway without issue.Maintenance found that a clamp bolt head was rubbing on the rigid "flap up" hydraulic pressure line. This caused a hole to be worn in the line resulting in a loss of all hydraulic fluid. The hydraulic "flap up" line was repaired and the clamp bolt was repositioned to prevent reoccurrence.

C-FTAB, a Pilatus PC-12/45 operated by Air Bravo Corp. as flight AB229, was conducting a flight from Thunder Bay (CYQT) ON. to Big Trout Lake (CYTL) ON. Prior to departure, the pilot noticed the outside air temperature was plus 2 and the wings were wet but clear of snow. The aircraft departed CYQT from Runway 07 on a normal departure. As the aircraft was climbing through 10 000 feet, the pilot noticed the aircraft started to porpoise up and down slightly and, as the flight continued, the pitching movement increased. The pilot disconnected the autopilot and realized that the elevator was difficult to move but pitch control was available with pitch trim system. The pilot requested a return to CYQT and declared an emergency. During the RNAV approach to Runway 07 the pilot regained some movement of the elevator. The aircraft landed safely and, while taxing to the hangar, full elevator control became available.The operator's maintenance carried out an flight control function test with no faults found. Inspection of the elevator and horizontal stabilizers found ice build up on top and between the rubber seals of the elevator and horizontal stabilizers. Ice was removed and elevator attach points were lubed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOIO, an Air Transat Airbus A321-271NX, was conducting flight TSC196 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QB to San José/Juan Santamaría Intl. (MROC), Costa Rica.  While level at 10000 feet as per ATC instructions, Flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory).  Flight crew followed the TCAS RA and landed at MROC without further incident.

N8064X, a Piper Archer PA28-181, was on a ferry instrument flight rule (IFR) flight from Bangor International Airport, Maine (KBGR) (United States) to Goose Bay, NL (CYYR). While the aircraft was approximately 45 nautical miles north-north-east (NNE) of Havre St-Pierre, QC (CYGV), the pilot made a MAYDAY call on the Montreal Centre (ACC) frequency reporting an engine failure (Continental CD-155). The pilot made an emergency landing on a frozen lake. Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) Halifax subsequently reported an Emergency Locator Transmitter (ELT) (406 MHz) activation and initiated a search. The aircraft was located and the pilot was taken to Halifax, NS.

C-FWEP, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3349 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Abbottsford (CYXX), BC with 4 crew and 67 passengers on board. While in cruise at FL240, 50 NM east of Kelowna, BC, a flight attendant became incapacitated. Their duties were distributed to the remaining cabin crew and the flight returned to CYYC. Emergency medical services met the aircraft on arrival in CYYC.

C-FJYW, an Aerospatiale ATR42-300 operated by Calm Air International LP, was conducting flight CAV213 from Arviat (CYEK) NU. to Rankin Inlet (CYRT) NU. At approximately 20 nm from the approach into CYRT, the flight crew received a "master caution" indicating the blue hydraulic system pressure was low. The flight crew completed the QRH and shut down the blue hydraulic system. As a result flaps, nose wheel steering, and other aircraft systems were inoperative. The flight crew declared an emergency, requested emergency vehicles, and continued the approach. The aircraft landed safely and was able to taxi and park without assistance. The operator's maintenance inspected and repaired a leak on the blue hydraulic system.

C-FGKZ, an Airbus A321 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1087 from Orlando International Airport (KMCO), USA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, with 6 crew and 196 passengers on board. During approach to runway 06L, the flight crew received a "Green Hydraulic Warning/Fail" message. The flight crew initiated a go-around, and declared PAN PAN. The flight landed on runway 33R with ARFF standing by. Maintenance inspection revealed a ruptured flex line attached to the LH MLG gear door actuator; this was replaced, and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GLTC, a Hawker Siddeley HS748 Series 2A, operated by Wasaya Airways LP, was conducting flight WSG801 from Pickle Lake (CYPL) ON. to Kasabonika (CYAQ) ON. On descent into CYAQ, the flight crew noticed the number 2 engine feathering pump light flicker. The number 2 engine was stable at 14 200 RPM, but the engine oil pressure was at 40 psi and moments later the engine failed (Rolls Royce GY, Dart 534-2). The flight crew carried out emergency procedures, notified ATC, and returned to CYPL and completed an uneventful single engine landing. The aircraft was shutdown on the runway and towed to the hangar. The operator's maintenance identified engine oil contamination and hot section damage during a post-event inspection.

C-GYML, an amateur-built privately registered Zenair CH200, was being flown by a student pilot with an instructor in the right seat. The purpose of the flight was to practice short field/obstacle clearance takeoffs and landings on runway 28 at Carp Airport (CYRP), Ontario. During the fourth circuit, while in the landing flare, the aircraft began to drift to the left of the runway centreline. The instructor called for the student to add power, and took the controls. During the maneuver, the pitch attitude of the aircraft increased, and the aircraft, which was configured for landing with full flaps extended, did not climb. The aircraft touched down in an area of long grass to the left of the runway, continuing for a couple hundred feet before the nosewheel collapsed, stopping the aircraft. Both pilots exited the aircraft uninjured. There was damage to both wings, the nosewheel, and the propeller.

C-GYNK, an Agusta AW139 helicopter operated by 7506406 Canada Inc. (dba Ornge Rotor Wing Operation), was conducting flight LF6-M from Kenora/Lake of the Woods District Hospital (CJG6), ON. to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. At approximately 5nm east of CYWG, the flight crew were performing the landing checks when they noticed an unsafe landing gear gear down indication. C-GYNK completed a fly-by inspection and CYWG tower informed the flight crew that all 3 gear were visible. The flight crew performed a lamp test, actioned the QRH, recycled the landing gear, and the left main landing gear down light did not illuminate. C-GYNK conducted a second fly-by inspection and CYWG tower informed the crew that all 3 gear were visible. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and ARFF was dispatched to Apron 2. When ARFF arrived at apron 2, C-GYNK carried out an uneventful vertical landing and evacuated the patient and paramedics safely. Shortly after the evacuation the flight crew noticed the landing gear locked light was illuminated. The aircraft was shutdown without further incident.The landing gear control and indicating system was deferred in accordance with the MEL. The landing gear lever was pinned in the extend position and placards were installed. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft in CYWG and found the #1 hydraulic PCM was low and serviced the system. The #2 hydraulic was found to be over filled and the excess fluid was bled off. The aircraft was flown to Kenora where the operator's maintenance performed landing gear system checks that included landing gear swings. They were unable to duplicate the fault and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FHSP, a Beechcraft B300C King Air was conducting Pacific Sky Aviation Inc. flight LVW357 from St. John’s International Airport (CYYT) NL to Québec/Jean Lesage International Airport (CYQB) QC. While enroute, the flight crew declared an emergency due to a loose cowl latch on the aircraft nacelle and diverted to the Stephenville Airport (CYJT) NL. The aircraft landed safely at 18:37 UTC.

C-GMYU, an Airbus Canada Limited Partnership A220-300 operated by Air Canada as ACA426, was departing Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, enroute to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC, with 10 crew and 121 passengers on board. During the climb, the flight crew observed 2 birds in close proximity to left side of the aircraft, after which significant vibrations were felt coming from the LH engine. The flight crew declared PAN PAN and requested a return to CYYZ, where they landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. Maintenance inspection of the LH engine revealed 4 damaged fan blades and 3 damaged exit guide vanes. The affected parts were replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GCHZ, a Bell 206L-1 operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd. was conducting long line operations from Little Grand Rapids (CZGR) to the First Nation community of Pauingassi, MB. C-GCHZ was approximately 2 NM north east of CZGR with an external load of groceries and dry goods when an unintentional release of the cargo net occurred. There were no injuries or damage to the helicopter.
