C-FVLZ, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was conducting flight AC849 from Frankfurt/ Rhein-Main Intl. (EDDF), Germany to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB. During cruise, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory). Flight crew complied with RA and continued to destination without further incident.

N78005, a Boeing B777-224 was conducting United Airlines flight UAL46 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR) NY to Frankfurt Airport (EDDF), Germany. While enroute, the aircraft developed a hydraulic leak and requested to return to KEWR. After changing course, the flight crew declared an emergency due to loss of hydraulic pressure and requested to divert to Halifax/Stanfield International Airport (CYHZ), NS. In preparation for arrival to CYHZ, the flight conducted fuel dumping. The aircraft landed safely at 05:48 UTC.Maintenance identified a faulty center hydraulic system low pressure switch. The switch was replaced along with the pressure transmitter O-ring. During the operation check, a hydraulic isolation valve status message was present on the flight deck. This item was deferred as per AMM procedures and the aircraft was returned to service.

N823LF, a Gulfstream Aerospace G-IV, was conducting a flight from Shannon Intl Airport (EINN), Ireland to the Treasure Coast Intl Airport (KFPR), Fl. While en-route, the flight crew declared a MAYDAY due to pressurization issues. The crew descended the aircraft from FL430 to FL120. After reaching FL120, the crew changed the Mayday to Pan Pan and elected to divert to the Gander International Airport (CYQX), NL. The aircraft landed safely.

C-FPQB, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was conducting flight ACA2343 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON to San Antonio Intl. (KSAT), TX.  During initial approach, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory).  Flight crew complied with RA and landed in KSAT without further incident.

C-GGNZ, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (Dash 8 Q400) was conducting flight JZA8348 from Prince George Airport (CYXS) BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR) BC, with 4 crew and 75 passengers onboard. During cruise, the in-charge flight attendant (IFA) felt unwell and was assisted by a passenger who was a nurse. The IFA's condition improved. The aft flight attendant assumed the role of the IFA and emergency services met the flight upon arrival. There were no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft.

Shortly after departure, the flight crew of Air Canada flight AC56, a Boeing 787-9 (C-FRTU) aircraft, received a Slat Drive Message, Slat #5 failed to retract. The flight crew, after consultation with dispatch and MOC, decided to return to CYYZ. The flight crew declared a Pan Pan, fuel was dumped to land below the maximum landing weight, and the aircraft stopped on the runway for brake inspection and taxied to gate without further incident.During the maintenance investigation, the slat skew detection outboard skew cable guide bolts on slat 5 were found to have been painted over and were not lock wired. Maintenance investigation is ongoing.

C-GNLW, a Boeing 737-200 aeroplane operated by Nolinor Aviation Inc., was conducting flight NRL951 from Meadowbank (CMB2), NU to Churchill (CYYQ), MB. While in the climb, 5 nm after departure, the No. 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney - USA, JT8D-17, serial number 657394) amber oil-filter bypass warning light illuminated. The flight crew conducted the associated checklist and performed a precautionary engine shutdown. The flight crew declared PAN PAN and diverted the flight to Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU. A successful landing was conducted with the No.1 engine inoperative.The operator's maintenance personnel determined that the engine's magnetic chip plugs and oil filter were contaminated with metal particles. In accordance with the engine maintenance manual, the chip plugs were cleaned and the filter replaced. After a satisfactory ground run the aircraft returned to Mirabel Intl. (CYMX), PQ. The engine will be replaced having accumulated roughly 164 hours since overhaul.

C-FWCA, an Airbus AS 350 B2 operated by West Coast Helicopters Maintenance and Contracting Limited, was conducting heli-ski operations from Bella Coola Airport (CYBD), BC. After dropping off a group of heli-ski passengers, the pilot was re-positioning the aircraft to an unmarked (un-staked) landing zone on the crest of a ridge. The pilot conducted a visual reconnaissance of the ridge from the east and west side before proceeding with the landing. During the approach from the west, the pilot lost visual reference with the snow surface immediately prior to touchdown and the aircraft drifted laterally to the right. The right skid touched down in the snow and the aircraft rolled over to the right. The main rotor blades made contact with the surface and the tail boom before the fuselage settled upright on both skids. The pilot pulled back on the throttle lever and the emergency fuel shutoff lever to shut down the engine before egressing through the right cockpit door. There was no post impact fire or loss of fuel. The 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter activated automatically and the satellite signal was received by the Canadian Mission Control Centre. The pilot was uninjured and the aircraft was substantially damaged with the tail boom severed from the fuselage. The pilot contacted the company dispatcher with a handheld radio and the company activated their emergency response plan. A second company helicopter was operating in the vicinity and returned all heli-ski passengers to CYBD followed by the occurrence pilot.

Shortly after takeoff from Sault Ste. Marie (CYAM), ON, the flight crew of Perimeter Aviation flight BLS384, a Fairchild SA227-DC (C-GJVC) aircraft, detected a burning electrical odor in the cockpit. The flight crew declared an emergency and the aircraft returned to land without further incident.

C-FEKJ, a Jazz Aviation LP Embraer 170-200 SU was conducting flight JZA608 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Boston/ General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl. (KBOS), MA.  During descent to KBOS around 9000 feet, flight crew received a Slat Fail message.  Flight crew actioned checklist and continued on the approach where they received a flap fail message at flap 2.  Flight crew decided to go around, declared an emergency due to higher landing speed and landed on the second approach without further incident.

TF-ICN, a Boeing 737-8 MAX aircraft operated by Icelandair, was conducting flight ICE623 from Keflavik Int'l (BIKF), Iceland to Boston/Logan Intl Airport (KBOS), MA. TF-ISW, a Boeing 767-319ER aircraft also operated by Icelandair Airlines, was conducting ICE631 from BIKF to Newark/Liberty Intl Airport (KEWR), NJ. ICE631 departed BIKF about 7 minutes after ICE623 and at about 60°00' N / 030°00' W, ICE631 encroached within 12 minutes separation behind ICE623 on the same track. Because the flights did not maintain the required longitudinal separation of 15 minutes, a loss of separation occurred.

C-GHKX, an Air Canada Airbus A330-300 was conducting flight ACA0900 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL. During descent, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory). Flight crew complied with RA and continued to destination without further incident.

C-FLFX, un Cessna 150 immatriculation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Drummondville, QC (CSC3). Lors l’atterrissage, une rafale de vent a provoqué un contact de l'aile gauche avec le sol. Le pilote a perdu la maitrise de l'appareil qui est alors sorti de piste. L'aile droite et l'hélice ont aussi touché le sol et le train principal droit a été arraché. Le pilote n'a pas été blessé.

N472AS an Alaska Airlines Boeing 737-990 operating under instrument flight rules as flight ASA715 was enroute from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ to Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA),WA. At 03:15 UTC and approximately 28 NM SSE from the Toronto/Lester B Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, the flight crew declared an emergency due to cracks on the windshield and requested a descent to 10000 feet. The flight diverted to Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport (DTW), MI and landed without further incident.

N703KW, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Eastern Airlines LLC, was conducting flight EAL3160 from Shannon Airport (EINN), Ireland to Hunter Army Air Field (KSVN), US. During cruise, while in Gander oceanic airspace, the crew requested to divert to Goose Bay Intl Airport (CYYR), NL due to smell of electrical wire burning/overheating in the cockpit. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance found the left hand nav display cooling duct clogged with dust and debris, causing arcing. Maintenance cleaned the duct, performed an operational check, and the aircraft was returned to service.

N545JN, a McDonnell Douglas MD-11F aircraft operated by Western Global Airlines, was conducting flight WGN7326 from Anchorage/Ted Stevens Intl, Alaska, USA (PANC) to Chicago/O'Hare Intl, Illinois, USA (KORD). During cruise the flight crew initially received an AC TIE 1 alert. Approximately 30 minutes to an hour later, the flight crew received additional multiple system warning alerts and failures, including the number 2 display unit, autopilot and flight director. The flight crew proceeded through several checklists and eventually restored electrical power and restored the failed systems. The crew initially declared a MAYDAY but later cancelled the emergency once the systems were restored. The aircraft continued to KORD with the AC TIE 1 and DC TIE 1 off and landed the aircraft without further incident.The operator's maintenance subsequently inspected the aircraft and replaced both flight control computers (FCC).

C-GOFD, a Cessna 172RG registered to the Brantford Flying Club, departed runway 29 at the Brantford Airport (CYFD), Ontario, at 1709 for a local visual flight rules (VFR) flight. A licensed private pilot, who had rented the aircraft, was the sole occupant. After a brief flight to the west, the pilot returned and entered the circuit for runway 29. During final approach, the left wing of the aircraft struck a tree. The aircraft yawed significantly to the left and entered a spin before crashing in an adjacent field. The pilot was fatally injured. There was no post-crash fire, and the ELT had been activated.

C-GKOE, an Air Canada Airbus A320-200 was conducting flight ACA1081 from Miami Intl (KMIA), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  On initial climb out of KMIA on radar vectors at 9500 feet, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory).  Flight crew complied with RA and  continued to destination without further incident.

C-FUJR, a Westjet Airlines Boeing 737-800 aircraft, was conducting flight WS2703 from Sangster International Airport (MKJS) Montego Bay, Jamaica to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. On descent to CYYZ, the cabin crew notified the flight crew of an acrid smell at mid-cabin that remained constant for 15 minutes. The flight crew elected to divert to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON after the smell became stronger and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. Maintenance conducted an inspection of the seat power boxes and potable water compressor with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

The Government of Canada King Air C90A (TGO997, C-FGXO) was on a training IFR flight when during the approach to Peterborough Airport (CYPQ) the flight crew were notified of a single engine aircraft that was on a downwind for Runway 09. Approximately 2 miles from the airport, C-FGXO received a TCAS TA indicating the other aircraft was at the same altitude with a one mile horizontal separation. The flight crew observed the other aircraft at close range and conducted a go-around. During the go-around the right engine was over torqued for approximately 3 seconds. C-FGXO commenced a second approach and the aircraft  landed uneventfully.

C-FFRB, a Found Aircraft Canada FBA-2C1 operated by Hoarfrost River Huskies Ltd., was on a maintenance flight from Hay River (CYHY), NT to Fort Nelson (CYYE), BC with only the pilot on board. During the landing roll in CYYE, the pilot experienced some tail wheel shimmy, and during the attempted control of the shimmy, directional control of the aircraft was lost, and a low speed ground loop ensued. The aircraft came to a rest in a snowbank beside the runway. There were no injuries, and the aircraft sustained minor damage.

C-FACJ, a Boeing 757-200 operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd., was conducting flight CJT462 from Iqaluit International Airport (CYFB), Nunavut, to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), Ontario, with two crew members on board. During the approach, an electrical smell was noted by the flight crew, who then declared PAN PAN. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF in attendance. A visual inspection by maintenance did not reveal any faults, although the RH Flight Control Computer was replaced as a result of troubleshooting another snag. The aircraft was returned to service and there have been no faults reported on subsequent flights.

C-GFBW, un hélicoptère Airbus AS350B2, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis les installations de la compagnie Héli-Boréal, situées 7 milles marins au nord-ouest de l’aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV), à destination de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC). Lors du décollage, le pare-brise de l’aéronef a givré soudainement. Le pilote a amorcé une descente vers la Baie de Sept-Îles, dont la surface était gelée, afin d’y atterrir. L’aéronef est entré en contact avec la surface gelée de la baie alors que l’aéronef avait encore une vitesse vers l’avant. Ce dernier a basculé et s’est immobilisé sur le côté. Le pilote et la passagère ont pu évacuer l’aéronef sans difficulté et ont été conduits au centre hospitalier de Sept-Îles. L’aéronef a été détruit.

C-GATX, un hélicoptère Airbus AS350B2 exploité par Les Hélicoptères Canadiens Ltée, effectuait un vol local de transport d’une charge à l’élingue selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le camp Elmer, situé à environ 35 mille marins ENE de l’aéroport Eastmain River, QC (CZEM). Alors qu'il effectuait plusieurs mouvements de barils de carburant sur de courtes distances, un baril de diesel s'est détaché et s'est déversé dans la neige. Les attaches utilisées ont été inspectées et étaient en bon état. Une défaillance du baril est suspectée. La procédure de déversement mineur a été appliquée et les autorités environnementales ont été notifiées.

C-GYSD, a Swoop Inc. Boeing 737-8CT was conducting flight WO601 from Puerto Vallarta/Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz Intl. (MMPR) Mexico, to Abbotsford Intl. (CYXX), BC.  During cruise, approximately 120 nautical miles ESE of Seattle-Tacoma Intl (KSEA), WA, a flight attendant became incapacitated.  Duties were redistributed and flight landed in CYXX without further incident.

C-GWTQ, an Airbus Helicopters AS 350 B3 helicopter, operated by Kootenay Valley Helicopters was conducting avalanche control operations with 1 pilot and 2 avalanche technicians on board. The operation consisted of dropping strategically placed explosive charges onto the slope from a height of approximately 20 feet. They were operating at an elevation of about 7000' ASL, about a hundred feet below a mountain slope ridgeline. The sparsely treed mountain side was covered in snow and ice. Very shortly after the technician released a charge, the helicopter encountered an area of reduced visibility. The pilot lost visual reference and the tail rotor contacted the sloping terrain or a tree. The helicopter shuddered and the pilot immediately performed a forced landing. The helicopter descended, impacted the hard snow pack and rolled over. In the process, the tail boom was struck and partially severed by the main rotor blades. The helicopter came to rest onto its side, approximately 25 feet from the explosive charge that had been released. The explosive detonated about a minute and a half after the forced landing but did not trigger a release of the snow pack. All occupants were able to extricate themselves from the wreckage and the pilot secured the electrical and fuel systems. The two avalanche technicians accounted for and recovered all remaining explosive charges from the helicopter. Using portable radios, they contacted a nearby skiing operation and a helicopter operator to arrange for transportation off the mountain. The ELT activated and the signal was received by the Canadian Mission Control Centre who relayed to information the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre in Victoria, BC. Search and rescue personnel were not deployed to the site. The helicopter has been removed from the mountain.

C-GEAG, a Emil Anderson Air Ltd. Beech 200 (King Air 200) aircraft, was en route from Victoria Int'l Airport (CYYJ), BC, to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC with only the pilot on board. Approximately 2 nautical miles west of intercepting the final approach course to Runway 16, the flight experienced severe turbulence in visual meteorological conditions while descending from 8000 feet above sea level. The flight continued to CLYW and landed without further incident. There were no injuries.Subsequent maintenance inspections found no aircraft damage related to the severe turbulence encounter.

C-GEAG, an Emil Anderson Air Ltd. Beech 200 (King Air 200) airplane, was en route from Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC, to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC with 2 crew and 3 passengers on board. While flying level at 8000 feet above sea level, approximately 2 nautical miles west of the final approach course to Runway 16, the flight experienced severe turbulence in visual meteorological conditions. The crew had difficulty controlling the airplane and a loss of altitude occurred. The flight continued to CLYW and landed without further incident. There were no injuries.Subsequent maintenance actions observed no aircraft damage related to the severe turbulence encounter.

The Can-West Corporate Air Charters Ltd. Beech B200GT, C-GLUF, was operating as flight CWA922 from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Calgary (CYYC), AB. During final approach to CYYC, the flight crew selected landing gear down and the right main gear down and locked indicator failed to illuminate. The flight crew elected to conduct a missed approach and requested vectors to allow time for troubleshooting. During the go-around the FO was able to visualize that the right main gear was not fully extended, and the landing gear circuit breaker had popped. In consultation with company personnel, the flight crew reset the circuit breaker and cycled the gear three additional times. The right main gear did not go to the down and locked position. The flight crew diverted and returned to CYEG while actioning the QRH. On approach to CYEG the flight crew declared an emergency and used the emergency extension hand pump to extend the landing gear. Just before touching down the captain secured the engines and feathered the propellers. On the ground roll the flight crew noticed the landing gear indicator displayed three green lights. The aircraft was stopped and shutdown on the runway for company maintenance to attend the aircraft. Once maintenance determined the landing gear was indeed locked, the aircraft was restarted and taxied back to the company hangar. The flight crew and one passenger received no injuries. Company maintenance found the RH main landing gear drag brace idlers to be installed backwards, which restricted the down-lock hooks motion when under air load during landing gear extension.

The WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-400, C-GWRE, was operating as flight WEN3613 from Seattle (KSEA), WA to Calgary (CYYC), AB. During descent through 13 000 feet asl, approximately 35 nm SW of CYYC, WEN3613 entered severe unexpected turbulence. The flight crew experienced a momentary loss of control and the auto pilot disengaged. As the aircraft penetrated the turbulence, the flight crew members struck their heads on the  ceiling of the flight deck. Both flight crew members were wearing the provided lap belts and shoulder harnesses. The captain received minor injuries. The lead flight attendant also received minor injuries from striking the L1 entrance door during the turbulence. Both crew members were able to continue to perform their duties for the remainder of the flight. The cabin crew and passengers were all wearing their seat belts. There were no passenger injuries. The flight continued to CYYC and landed without further issue. Company maintenance carried out a severe turbulence inspection. No faults were noted and the aircraft was released for service.

C-FSFS, a privately operated by AirSprint Inc. Cessna 525B, was conducting a flight from Hamilton/John C. Munro Intl. (CYHM), ON to Sarasota/Bradenton Intl. (KSRQ), FL. ATC vectored the flight to avoid reported severe turbulence, as well to descend to FL390, and then FL370 in the vicinity of the northern border of Florida. The flight crew accepted the clearance and informed ATC that they were getting close to a minimum fuel situation. ATC requested a 360 degree heading (directly away from the destination airport). The flight crew reiterated that they were getting low on fuel, and they were assigned other vectors over the west coast of Florida, and over the Gulf. The flight crew declared a MAYDAY after informing ATC multiple times that they were approaching critical fuel. ATC cleared the aircraft with a direct vector to KSRQ; they landed uneventfully with 500lbs of fuel remaining. The flight had been planned so that it would land with 250lbs of extra fuel above the minimum IFR fuel requirements.

C-FOWK, an Image Air Charter Limited Bombardier CL60 (CL-600-2B16 Series 604) was operating between Vancouver Int'l Airport (CYVR), BC, and Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, with 3 crew on board. After departing CYVR, the flight crew selected the flap to the 0-degree position. The flaps remained at the 20-degree position and the crew received a FLAPS FAIL EICAS message. The flight crew actioned the QRH items, declared an emergency, and returned to CYVR. The aircraft landed without further incident.Subsequent maintenance actions included a ground reset procedure, but no defect was found when conducting the inboard and outboard flaps operational test. The airplane has been returned to service with a flap monitoring unit installed to identify any reoccurrence.

C-FYKR, an Air Canada Airbus A319, was conducting flight AC7017 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB to Dallas/ Love Field  (KDAL), TX. On descent to KDAL, the flight crew received a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory).  They followed the RA and continued to KDAL without further incident.

C-FNOG, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9, was conducting flight AC0801 from Dublin Intl. (EIDW), Ireland to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. On initial climb, the flight crew received a TCAS RA (Resolution Advisory). They followed the RA and continued to CYYZ without further incident.

C-GKUH, an Air Canada Airbus A330-343, was conducting flight AC301 from Montreal Int'l Airport (CYUL), QC, to Vancouver Int'l Airport (CYVR), BC, with 10 crew and 256 passengers on board. During the normal deplaning process in CYVR a cabin crew member detected a smoke/electrical odor, accompanied by a perceived heat source, in the aircraft's row 31. The cabin crew member discharged 2 halon fire extinguishers into the area. There were no injuries.Subsequent maintenance actions determined the under-seat mounted electrical box (P/N RD-FA3871-01), used for the in-seat power outlet and the in-flight entertainment system, experienced an internal electrical short. The component was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GTSR, un Airbus 330-243 exploité par Air Transat A.T. Inc. sous l’indicatif TS399, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Punta Cana International en République Dominicaine (MDPC) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Peu de temps après le décollage, l’équipage a lu sur l’ECAM (Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitoring) un message de basse pression de pneu accompagné d’une indication similaire au tableau de bord pour la roue #4. L’équipage a contacté, en vol, le service de maintenance de la compagnie et la décision de poursuivre le vol jusqu’à destination fut prise. Lors de l’approche vers CYUL, une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée et l’aéronef a atterri sans encombre. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont inspecté le train d’atterrissage et l’aéronef a été remorqué jusqu’à l’aire de stationnement désigné.

N894FD, a Federal Express Corporation (FEDEX) Boeing 777F cargo airplane was conducting flight FDX6014 from Anchorage Int'l (PANC), AK, USA, to Indianapolis Int'l (KIND), IN, USA with 2 flight crew and 1 passenger on board. During cruise flight, the first officer experienced medical distress but was able to continue with flight crew duties. The flight crew declared an emergency with Vancouver Centre and requested diversion to Seattle Int'l (KSEA), WA, USA. The flight crew requested to dump approximately 20,000 pounds of fuel during the diversion. The aircraft exited Canadian airspace at approximately 0646 UTC, and continued to KSEA where it landed without further incident.

C-GXCA, un Beech 1900D exploité par Chrono Aviation Inc. sous l'indicatif NDL191, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Salluit, QC (CYZG) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Après environ 60 minutes de vol, l’équipage a observé que l’indicateur de pression d’huile du moteur de gauche fluctuait. L’inspection visuelle de la nacelle par la cabine n’a rien révélé d’anormal. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a coupé le moteur de gauche par mesure de précaution, car les fluctuations se rapprochaient et l’écart entre elles s’agrandissait. Un déroutement vers l’aéroport de La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) a été demandé au contrôle de la circulation aérienne où l’aéronef a atterri sans encombre.

C-FRTV, a privately operated Piper Cherokee PA-28-140, was conducting a local flight from Romeo Leblanc International Airport, Moncton NB (CYQM). While in cruise, the engine experienced a fuel starvation for undetermined reasons. The pilot conducted a forced approach into a field approximately 41 nm south south east of CYQM. The aircraft sustained substantial damage and the pilot reported no injuries. Two weeks prior to this occurrence, the aircraft had a power loss resulting in a forced landing, and the aircraft was not damaged. Subsequently, maintenance had inspected and replaced a carburetor heat hose before returning the aircraft to service.

On 18 February 2022, Tractor 244 was towing a Boeing 737 aeroplane to Terminal 3 at Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ). Tractor 244 was moving on taxiway Sierra and was instructed to hold short of Runway 33R due to a departing aircraft on that runway. The driver of Tractor 244 read back the restriction to hold short of Runway 33R. As Tractor 244 approached the holdshort line, the driver attempted to stop; however, the vehicle began sliding along the taxiway, crossing the holdshort line for Runway 33R. The air traffic controller, observing the snow-clearing vehicle going past the holdshort line, instructed the driver of Tractor 244 to stop. At that point, the individual in the aircraft being towed also applied the brakes in an attempt to prevent crossing the holdshort line. Tractor 244 subsequently stopped approximately 5 metres beyond the holdshort line. Once stopped, the driver of Tractor 244 indicated that the vehicle would not stop due to the slippery conditions. There was no impact to the departing aircraft's takeoff and no impact to operations. There were no injuries.

C-GUBC, an Air Transat Airbus A330-243 was conducting flight TS327 from Cancun Intl. (MMUN), Mexico to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. After takeoff, flight crew received a Brake Hot ECAM (Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitoring). The ECAM actions were accomplished, the brakes cooled down and the gear retracted. The ECAM warning reappeared 2 more times and each time the ECAM actions were accomplished. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC and requested a return to the departure airport (MMUN). Once landed, ARFF inspected the landing gear and released the aircraft for taxi to a parking position. Maintenance inspected Brake #8 on arrival and was found free and cold, no tire fuse plugs melted and the tire pressure was found normal. The #8 brake unit temp sensor was deactivated and put on MEL.

C-GIPR, a wheel-equipped Cessna C208 aircraft operated by Bamaji Air Inc., was conducting a visual flight rules (VFR) flight from Sioux Lookout (CYXL) ON, to an ice strip on Springpole Lake, ON with the pilot and 1 passenger onboard. Approximately 17 nm NNW of CYXL the aircraft impacted the frozen surface of Lac Seul. The ELT activated and was detected by the Search and Rescue Satellite-Aided Tracking (SARSAT) system. A DND aircraft that was conducting training in the area responded and SARTECHs parachuted into the site. The occupants suffered minor injuries and the aircraft sustained substantial damage. There was no fire. The TSB is investigating.

C-FJJT, A Honda Jet registered to Sky Service business aviation inc., was on an instrument flight rules (IFR) flight from Val d’Or, QC (CYVO) to Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU), with two pilot and 4 passengers on board. After touchdown following the approach to runway 06 left, the aircraft overran the runway, coming to a stop approximately 500 feet beyond the edge of the pavement. There were no injuries, and no damage to the aircraft.

C-FQHB, a Bell 206L operated by Custom Helicopters, was conducting external slinging operations with a 100 foot longline from St. Theresa Point (CYST) MB to the community of Wasagamack, MB. On the apron at CYST, there were 2 ground handlers preparing and attaching the external loads to the helicopter and an additional 2 ground handlers working nearby. During the lift, the helicopter was positioned in front and to the left of the external load. As the helicopter began the lift, the external load swung forward and to the left. The swinging load caused the helicopter to drift left. The pilot recognized the load might strike a ground handler and attempted to correct; however, the load swung and struck a nearby ground handler that was positioned 50 to 100 feet from the slinging area from behind. The pilot set down the load, ground handlers unhooked the load, and the pilot repositioned and shutdown. The struck ground handler was transferred to a Winnipeg hospital for assessment and was released with minor injuries. The operator investigated the incident and has made changes to its longline procedures and training.

C-GSUI, a North Cariboo Flying Service Ltd. Avro 146 Series RJ100, was operating as flight NCB2012 from Calgary International (CYYC), AB to Fort St. John (CYXJ), AB. During cruise at FL260 the flight crew reported a vibration on the number 4 engine. The QRH was actioned and the crew conducted an engine (Avco Lycoming, LF-507-1F ) shut down of the #4 engine. An emergency was declared and the flight returned to CYYC without further incident.

C-GDEV, a privately registered Mooney M20M, was conducting a fight from Regina Intl. (CYQR) SK. to Yorkton Muni (CYQV) SK. The aircraft landed at CYQV with the gear unintentionally in the retracted position. The aircraft was lifted and placed on its wheels. There were no injuries to the pilot or passenger. The aircraft sustained damage to the propeller and fuselage.

N718SK, un MHI RH Aviation CRJ-700 exploité par SkyWest Airlines sous l'indicatif SKW9898, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Chicago O'Hare, US (KORD). Immédiatement après le décollage, le message R MAIN/SCAV Ejector Caution est apparu sur le système d'affichage des paramètres moteurs et d'alerte de l'équipage (EICAS) et l'équipage a noté que du carburant était transféré du réservoir de gauche vers celui de droite. Lors de la montée en route, à 15 000 pieds et à environ 32 nm à l’ouest de CYUL, le message de débalancement de carburant a apparu et l'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence en raison d’un problème de débalancement de carburant et a demandé un retour à CYUL. L'équipage a suivi la liste de vérification d’urgence (QRH) et le débalancement semblait venir du système automatique de transfert de carburant. Au début de la descente, le débalancement est resté stable à environ 1200 livres et a réduit à plus basse altitude. L'équipage n'a pas eu de problème de contrôle ni de performance et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre à 18:13z avec les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FCDE, a Challenger CL-600, operated by Skyservice Business Aviation was on the downwind for Runway 13 at Northeast Florida Regional Airport (KSGJ) at 3000 feet. ATC requested that the aircraft climb to 4000' for a pop up VFR target that was no factor. A TCAS target appeared at the same altitude, 5 miles on the TCAS. The flight crew queried ATC, and since a controller change was taking place the crew was told to standby. When the target was approximately 2 miles, the crew received a climb RA, which they responded to and they notified ATC that they were climbing (to about 4800 feet). ATC responded and gave a 180 degree heading (a 90 degree heading change) to put C-FCDE on the base leg. The aircraft returned to 4000 feet, with an uneventful landing.

The Buffalo Airways Lockheed 188C, C-GZFE, was operating on a local training flight from Yellowknife (CYZF), NWT. After takeoff the flight crew noticed a number 4 engine (Allison 501-D13) abnormality. The flight crew actioned the QRH and shut the engine down as a precaution. ATC was notified of the engine shutdown and the aircraft returned to CYZF; no emergency was declared. The aircraft landed without further issue. Maintenance action: Company maintenance replaced the number 4 engine fuel control unit and the aircraft was released for service.

WestJet Encore flight WEN3405, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 (C-FWEZ) aircraft, was on final approach to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) Runway 24R at approximately 4000 feet when the flight passed by a remotely piloted aircraft (RPAS/drone) heading east approximately 100-200 feet above. The flight crew reported the RPA to ATC and landed without further incident.

C-GOWG, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. B737-800, was operating as flight SWG609 from Gregorio Luperón Intl - Puerto Plata (MDPP) to MacDonald-Cartier Intl - Ottawa (CYOW). During the initial climb, after passing through 10,000ft, a physical altercation broke out between two passengers. The in-charge flight attendant informed the flight crew and of the need to return to MDPP. The cabin was secured for landing. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, the aircraft returned to MDPP. The passengers involved in the altercation were removed by police. There were no injuries, minor damage occurred to one window shade and one seat back.

C-GMZN, a A220 -300, operated by Air Canada from Vancouver Intl (CYVR) to John Wayne Airport-Orange County - Santa Ana (KSNA) was on vectors  during approach when the flight crew received a TCAS/RA. The RA was actioned by flight crew, an uneventful landing ensued.

C-FPCA, a B767-300, was being operated as Air Canada AC7125 from Luis Muñoz Marín Intl - San Juan (TJSJ) to Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ). During the take off roll, the Main Cargo Door indication illuminated and a warning bell sounded. The flight crew conducted the QRH checklist, the indication remained. The flight crew decided to return to TJSJ, a Pan Pan was declared, and emergency vehicles met the aircraft for inspection. The aircraft taxied to the gate. Maintenance found 4 latches were showing partial red on the visual indicators. The door was manually operated and when closed went hard stop on the latches. All but one visual red indicator were then showing correct.

The Olds-Didsbury Flying Association Cessna 150M, C-GAJQ, was operating on a local flight 20 nm NW of Olds-Didsbury (CEA3) airport, AB with just the pilot on board. While flying at low altitude over Glennifer Lake, the aircraft contacted the snow-covered lake surface. The aircraft settled into the snow and the nose landing gear collapsed before the aircraft came to rest. The pilot was uninjured; the 406 MHz ELT activated.

C-FPLS, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Swoop Inc., was conducting flight WSW190 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. While in cruise at approximately 200 nautical miles northwest of CYYZ, the flight crew advised they had a passenger in medical distress. The crew requested priority handling and emergency medical service to meet at the gate. The priority handling was given and flight WSW190 landed Runway 23 without further incident.

C-GJAN, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (Series 900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8504 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR) B.C. to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl. (CYXE), SK. During cruise flight, a flight attendant experienced a medical condition and was unable to perform their duties. The remaining flight attendant was assisted by flight attendants who were repositioning. The flight continued to CYXE where an uneventful landing was completed. EMS was called to assist.

C-FQNG, a Sikorsky S-61N operated by VIH Helicopters Limited, was conducting heli-logging operations with a grapple approximately 29 nautical miles north-northeast of Port Hardy (CYAZ), BC, with 2 flight crew members on board. While on a return leg to the service barge, in level flight, the pilot felt a small bump and, upon checking the grapple position, saw the grapple fall into the ocean below. The aircraft continued to the service barge and landed safely. The aircraft was inspected and the mount for the grapple hydraulic quick disconnect fittings was found torn away from the fuselage. The quick disconnect fittings did release during the long line separation and no hydraulic fluid was lost. Maintenance found no other anomalies that may have contributed to the belly hook release. The aircraft was repaired and the quick disconnect bracket was re-attached. The belly hook was removed and sent to the manufacturer for further analysis. The grapple and long line were not recovered.

C-GMEX, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8, was conducting flight AC554 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Los Angeles Intl. (KLAX), CA.  During descent, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory).  Flight crew followed the RA and landed in KLAX without further incident.

C-GTCJ, a Boeing 757-200 aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd, was conducting flight CJT1573 from Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON with 2 crew members onboard. During cruise, at approximately 120 nm from CYHM, the aircraft experienced a LH hydraulic system fluid and pressure loss. The crew initiated the Quick Reference Handbook applicable checklist and declared a Mayday. CJT1573 landed on Runway 30 where ARFF vehicles were standing by. The aircraft stopped on the runway for a preliminary inspection and then towed to vacate the runway.The maintenance department inspected the left engine pylon area and found that an internal pylon panel had shifted and was chaffing on an hydraulic tube resulting in hydraulic fluid leakage. The chaffed hydraulic tube was replaced and the system fluid replenished. A service difficulty report (SDR) has been submitted.

C-FHGG, un BE10 exploité par Propair Inc. sous l’indicatif PRO4245, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) à destination de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) avec 1 passager et 2 pilotes à bord. Lors de l’approche à CYMT, l’équipage a sélectionné la sortie du train d’atterrissage et une indication anormale du train gauche est survenue. L’équipage a décidé d’effectuer une remontée et de retourner à CYUY. À environ 100 miles marins au nord-est de CYUY une urgence a été déclarée et les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre, il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GKFA, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-200, was conducting flight RV1655 from Tampa Intl (KTPA), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. During cruise approximately 150nm south of CYYZ, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) ''DESCEND'' command. Flight Crew complied with TCAS command as instructed. At approximately FL324, flight crew received the ''CLEAR OF CONFLICT'' advisory. Flight crew advised ATC and returned to their cleared altitude of FL330. The aircraft landed at destination without further incident.

C-GKFA, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-220 was conducting flight RV1638 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL.  During cruise at FL380 in vicinity of Jacksonville Intl. (KJAX), FL, ATC instructed flight crew to turn right 15 degrees and descend to FL340. Flight crew complied and initiated a 1000ft/minute descent. Shortly after, ATC instructed flight crew to expedite descent. RV1638 increased their rate of descent to 1800ft/minute. A TCAS RA (resolution advisory) ''CLIMB'' command was received at approximately FL355 and flight crew followed the command as instructed. At approximately FL363, flight crew received the ''CLEAR OF CONFLICT'' advisory, initiated a descent back to their cleared altitude and advised ATC. The aircraft landed at KMCO without further incident

C-GITP, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A319 conducting flight RV1650 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Miami International Airport (KMIA), FL. While descending to FL240 on the SLFSH1 RNAV STAR, approximately 20NM north of waypoint CIKEN, ATC advised RV1650 of opposite direction traffic instructed to level-off at FL230. The rate of climb of the opposite direction traffic triggered a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) ''CLIMB'' command. The flight crew followed the TCAS as instructed. After climbing approximately 200 feet, RV1650 received the ''CLEAR OF CONFLICT'' advisory and descended back to their cleared altitude. ATC was advised. The aircraft continued to destination without further incident.

The Federal Express Airbus A300-600, N692FE, operating as FDX121, was on a cargo flight from Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB to Memphis Intl.  (KMEM), TN. During initial climb on departure from CYEG the flight crew observed an open forward cargo door light. The flight crew stopped the climb, declared an emergency and returned to CYEG; the approach and landing were uneventful. Maintenance found that the forward door "closed and locked" indication displayed on the ECAM door page was faulty. A visual inspection confirmed that the door was indeed closed and locked and the aircraft was returned to service per the MEL.

C-FYPN un Boeing 737-2T4 exploité par Chrono Jet inc sous l’indicatif MBK791 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Mary River, NU (CMR2) à destination d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) avec 99 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, les volets ont été sélectionnés à la position 1 et les volets ont cessé de bouger entre la position 2 et la position 1. L’équipage a poursuivi la montée à une altitude sécuritaire et a complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH). Par la suite, après la confirmation du carburant requis pour se rendre à destination avec le département de la régulation des vols de la compagnie, l’équipage a décidé de poursuivre le vol à CYFB au niveau de vol 190. Une fois en contact avec le centre de contrôle régional d’Edmonton, un état d’urgence a été déclaré. L’appareil s'est posé sur la piste 34 à CYFB sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FCII, a Skyservice Business Aviation Gulfstream G450 was conducting a flight from Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport (KOPF), FL to Teterboro Airport (KTEB), NJ at 2-3nm north of position SBJ VOR the crew received a Resolution Advisory (RA). The clearance was to maintain 4000’ at heading 040 which was complied with. A target was observed on the TCAS at the 11:30 position maintaining 500’ below. Subsequently, flight crew received a RA, to which the crew complied with and ATC were advised with no reply from ATC.  As flight crew climbed to 4200’ they received a ''CLEAR OF CONFLICT'' message and returned to 4000 feet and advised ATC with “ CLEAR OF CONFLICT” maintaining 4000 feet . Flight crew received no reply from ATC. When the pilot managed to contact ATC, advised that they just had an RA and had returned to the assigned level at 4000 feet , there was no acknowledgment from ATC and they told flight crew to contact approach sector. As instructed, flight crew contacted approach and advised that they had just had an RA event in the last sector and Approach advised they would let them know. Flight landed without further incident.

C-FKRF a WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-800, operating as flight WJA1247, reported a Remotely Operated Aircraft Systems (RPAS) at FL180 enroute to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ). The RPAS was described as a shiny and silver, and was estimated to be approximately three wing lengths to the left side of the aircraft. Police were notified.

C-GJYC, un Airbus Canada Limited Partnership A220-300 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA334 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Edmonton international, AB (CYEG) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau international, QC (CYUL) avec 135 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage. Lors de la descente, aux environs du niveau de vol 250, une panne du système pneumatique droit est survenue, ce qui engendre une perte de la capacité d’anti-givrage en vol. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification et par la suite déclaré un état d’urgence en raison de la vitesse élevée requise pour traverser la zone de givrage. L’appareil s’est ensuite posé sans encombre avec les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) déployés. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

The Alkan Air Ltd. Dornier 228-202, C-FUCN, was on a flight from Dawson City (CYDA), NT to Whitehorse (CYXY), NT. During the approach, when the landing gear was extended, the nose landing gear failed to extend. A touch and go was performed on the main landing gear but the nose landing gear still failed to extend. While in the go around, an emergency was declared and the aircraft did a circuit to prepare for an emergency landing with the nose gear retracted. The aircraft landed successfully with ARFF attending. There were no injuries and only minor damage to the aircraft. The aircraft was removed from the runway within 45 minutes. The company will report their maintenance findings to the TSB.

C-GISZ, un Beechcraft B200 exploité par Max Aviation inc. sous l’indicatif MAX220, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) à destination de Teterboro, NJ (KTEB) aux États Unis avec 2 pilotes à bord. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, l’équipage a sélectionné la rentrée du train d’atterrissage et une indication anormale du train en transition est apparue. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a effectué un circuit d’attente pour compléter la liste de vérification et consulter la compagnie pour résoudre l’anomalie. Le train d’atterrissage a éventuellement été baissé et les indications sont revenues à la normale. Par mesure de précaution, l’équipage a effectué un survol de la piste afin d’obtenir une confirmation visuelle que le train était sorti et est revenu se poser sur la piste 06L à CYHU sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) déployés. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé ni de dommage.

C-GAAR, a Cessna 172S aircraft operated by Waterloo-Wellington Flight Centre, was conducting a local training flight from the Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON with one student pilot onboard. After a uneventful landing on Runway 08 and previously having completed 3 circuits, the student pilot re-applied power for takeoff. Upon the application of power, the aircraft veered to the left. The student pilot reduced the power and applied the brakes before the aircraft continued off the runway. The aircraft exited the left side of the runway and came to a sudden stop after the nose dug in, causing the propeller to strike the ground. The ELT activated and emergency services assisted at the site. There were no injuries, the aircraft sustained substantial damage to the wing tips and wing roots. The aircraft was towed to the company hangar, maintenance is conducting a further inspection.

C-GATK, an Air Tindi Ltd. Beech 200 GT, was operating as flight TIN511 from Sambaa K'e (CEU9), NT to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT. While on approach to CYZF, the flight crew did not observe a landing gear safe indication when the landing gear was lowered. An emergency was declared and the landing gear was extended using the manual gear extension system. Again there was no gear down indication. The flight crew circled until there was enough daylight to confirm that the landing gear was extended fully by flying, once past the tower, and then once past maintenance staff, who were using binoculars to observe the landing gear position as the aircraft flew past the hangar. Once satisfied that all observers concurred that the landing gear was down and locked, a safe landing and taxi-in was performed without further issue.Maintenance found the landing gear bay packed with snow which prevented the down lock from engaging completely which in turn prevented the landing gear proximity switch from engaging and activating the landing gear position indication lights. Maintenance thawed the snow and performed landing gear swings which were successful. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GMAI, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE700 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Puvirnituq, QC (CYPX) avec 26 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait à environ 150 miles marins (nm) au sud de La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL), l’équipage a remarqué une diminution de la quantité d’huile du moteur gauche (Pratt & Whitney USA JT8D-17) et a décidé d’effectuer une diversion à CYGL. À environ 30 nm de CYGL une baisse de pression d’huile du moteur gauche est survenue. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a demandé un circuit d’attente pour compléter liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH). Par la suite, l’équipage a poursuivi l’approche avec le moteur gauche au ralenti de vol et l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre. Une fois au sol, le moteur a été fermé, inspecté par le véhicule d’urgence et l’appareil a ensuite circulé jusqu'à l'aire de trafic. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

N171UP, un Airbus A300 F4-322R exploité par UPS Airlines inc. sous l’indicatif UPS473, effectuait un vol cargo selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Montréal/Mirabel (CYMX), QC à destination de Louisville/Muhammad Ali International (KSDF), KY aux États-Unis avec 2 pilotes à bord. Après le décollage, l’équipage a sélectionné la rentrée du train d’atterrissage et celui-ci ne rentrait pas. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et est revenu se poser sur la piste 06 à CYMX sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-FEMF, un Learjet 45 exploité par Fox Flight Inc, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Toronto/Lester B.Pearson, ON (CYYZ). Après avoir décollé de la piste 24L, l’équipage a reçu un message d’alerte d’équipage (CAS message) LR EMER PRESS ON alors que l’aéronef était à une altitude de 12 000 pieds et en montée. L’équipage a arrêté la montée à 15 000 pieds et a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH). Le message d’alerte est resté actif et l’équipage a alors avisé le service de contrôle aérien d’un problème avec le système de pressurisation, a demandé un retour vers CYUL et a déclaré une urgence. Le contrôleur aérien a assigné de nouvelles altitude et route pour CYUL où l’aéronef a atterri sans encombre.

C-FIWE, a DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Westjet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3651 from Nashville International Airport (KBNA), USA to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON with 4 crew and 19 passengers onboard. While on final approach for Runway 24R into CYYZ, the crew selected the landing gear down and noted there was no right main landing gear green light when the gear was extended. The crew initiated a missed approach and proceeded with the applicable Quick Reference Handbook procedure, that led to an alternate landing gear extension. The crew declared a Pan Pan and landed Runway 23 where ARFF vehicles were standing by. The aircraft stopped on the runway due to contaminated taxiways and aprons and no nose wheel steering as a result of the alternate landing gear extension, and towed to the gate. Maintenance replaced 2 light bulbs on the right hand landing gear indication and checked the system serviceable.

C-GRDU, un SAAB 340B exploité par Pascan Aviation sous l’indicatif PSC588, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de l’aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU). Un hélicoptère Bell 412 exploité par le Ministère de la Défense nationale sous l’indicatif FCON479, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’héliport de Valcartier, QC (CYOY). Alors que FCON479 était à 8 milles nautiques à l’ouest de CYQB en rapprochement et à une altitude de 4300 pieds, l’équipage a effectué un virage de 180 degrés puis une descente de 500 pieds sans aviser le service de la circulation aérienne. PSC588 était alors à la droite de FCON479 à une altitude de 2900 pieds. À ce moment, les espacements minimaux requis de 3 NM latéralement et de 1000 pieds verticalement non pas pu être maintenus et ont été réduit à 2.6 NM latéralement et 600 pieds verticalement. Le contrôleur aérien a contacté FCON479. En raison d'ennuis techniques, FCON479 a demandé l’annulation de son autorisation IFR pour poursuivre son vol selon les règles de vol à vue et retourner à CYOY où il a atterri sans encombre.

C-FXDP, a SkyCare Westwind II 1124 was conducting a flight from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Sarasota Bradenton International Airport (KSRQ) FL when in the vicinity of Charlotte/Douglas International airport (KCLT) NC, the aircraft experienced a loss of hydraulic pressure and declared an emergency. The crew elected to return to CYYZ however, due to poor weather in CYYZ, the aircraft diverted to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON where it landed safely.

C-GSJZ, a Dehavilland DHC-8-402 aircraft, was conducting Jazz Aviation LP flight JZA775 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Charlottetown Airport (CYYG), PE. After landing, clear of the active runway in CYYG and taxiing toward the gate, Nav Canada personnel informed the crew that they observed smoke coming from the right main landing gear. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) was notified by Nav Canada personnel as the aircraft taxied and stopped on the apron. The crew assessed that it was safe to taxi to the gate with ARFF standing by.  When at the gate and after shut-down, ARFF confirmed that it was safe to deplane the aircraft. After the passengers deplaned, maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft and determined that the origin of the smoke was from deice fluid dripping onto the brakes and burning off. The aircraft brakes had been deiced in CYUL prior to departure due to slush on the taxiway.

C-GURI, a Kamov KA-32A11BC helicopter, operated by VIH Helicopters Limited, was conducting heli-logging operations with a hook at Pitt Island, BC, with 2 flight crew members on board. The long line was switched on the aircraft's belly hook from a grapple to a hook, and the belly hook latch was manually checked with a pull test prior to departure. During the first unloading turn, there was an uncommanded long line release from the belly hook and the line coiled up on the ground. There were no reported injuries to ground or flight crew and no reported damage to the aircraft or ground equipment. Upon landing, the belly hook latch was found in the open position. Maintenance inspected the belly hook with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service and continued hook logging without further incident.

C-GYWJ, a Boeing 737-700, operated by WestJet Airlines Ltd., was enroute from James Armstrong Richardson Intl - Winnipeg (CYWG) to Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ) when a cabin crew member became incapacitated. Duties were redistributed, the aircraft landed uneventfully at CYYZ.

C-GCMA, a Beech 1900D operated by Central Mountain Air was operating as flight GLR9016 from Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). GLR9016 was on final approach for Runway 35L and was instructed to execute a missed approach on short final due previous traffic landing and exiting the runway. GLR9016 was instructed by CYYC West Tower controller to maintain runway heading and climb to 7000 feet. N318NB, an Airbus A319 operated by Delta Airlines was conducting flight DAL2621 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Minneapolis / Saint Paul, Minnesota USA (KMSP) and was cleared by the East Tower controller to take off from Runway 35R at the same time as GLR9016 was performing the missed approach. As a result, lateral separation was momentarily lost. Separation was reduced to 1.9 nm, where 3 nm was required.The published missed approach procedure for Runway 35L is maintain runway heading until 500 feet AGL, and then alter heading 30 degrees left while climbing to 7000 feet ASL.UPDATED ON 25 APRIL 2022

C-GVDP, an Airbus Canada A220-300 operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA321 from Montreal Intl, (CYUL), QC  to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 5 crewmembers and 132 passengers on board. After landing at CYYC, while taxiing to the gate, the flight crew noticed a burning rubber smell in the cabin and cockpit. The flight crew requested airport rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) meet the aircraft on the apron and conduct an inspection for abnormal conditions. None were noted by ARFF, and the aircraft taxied to its designated gate for passenger deplaning without further incident. Subsequent inspection by company maintenance personnel found the auxiliary power unit (APU) to be over serviced with oil. The APU was serviced to the correct level and operated. No further abnormal odors were noted, and the aircraft was released for service.

C-GVEN, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3172 from Comox (CYQQ), BC, to Calgary (CYYC), AB, with 4 crew members and 10 passengers on board. While boarding, as the crew started the APU, the "APU Warning" light did not illuminate as usual on completion of the start procedure. The crew shut off the APU. The aircraft then stopped accepting external power. As the crew started the APU the second time, ground personnel reported to the flight crew that smoke was coming from the APU. The crew declared an emergency and a rapid deplanement was completed. When ARFF arrived at the aircraft, there was no sign of fire and the smoke was dissipating.Maintenance found that the APU starter-generator would engage when external power was applied to the aircraft. The APU starter-generator was replaced. After the completion of a function check, the airplane was returned to service. A Service Difficulty Report was submitted for this defect.

C-GWFE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, was conducting flight WEN3540 from Kamloops (CYKA), BC, to Calgary Int'l (CYYC), AB, with 71 passengers and 4 crew on board. After takeoff when the crew selected the flaps to 0, the flaps stopped travelling at 5 and the FLAP POWER caution light illuminated. The crew completed the associated checklist but the issue did not resolve. The crew decided to continue to CYYC. On arrival, the crew completed the "Abnormal Flap Landing" checklist and declared a PAN PAN as a precaution. The aircraft landed safely and taxied to the gate.Maintenance carried out a functional test of the flap drive system and flap control system; both systems tested serviceable. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FNWH, a Beechcraft 1900D, operated by North-Wright Airways was conducting flight NWL141 from Fort Good Hope, NT (CYGH) to Yellowknife, NT (CYZF). While completing a 180 degree turn at the button for departure on Runway 07, the flight crew encountered difficulty manipulating the left engine in beta mode while completing the turn. The nose wheel departed the runway surface and the nose landing gear made contact with a windrow/snowbank on the side of the runway. The aircraft became stuck, the flight crew shut down the engines and the passengers were deplaned.Subsequent aircraft inspection by company maintenance found the L/H primary prop governor reset linkage disconnected. Maintenance reconnected the reset linkage, ground runs were successfully completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

Chartright Air flight HRT912, a Beech B300 (C-FGGE) aircraft, was en route from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport, ON (CYYZ) to Thunder Bay ON (CYQT), when the flight crew noticed the hydraulic motor running and an intermittent hydraulic flow annunciator light. The flight crew decided to return to CYYZ. On approach to CYYZ when the landing gear was selected down, the nose gear down and locked indicator did not illuminate. The flight crew declared an emergency, and successfully performed a manual gear extension. The aircraft landed without further incident..

C-GJEN, a de Havilland DHC-8-402, operating as Westjet Encore flight WEN3517, was traveling from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) to London, ON (CYXU). The flight was holding in light icing conditions at 10,000 feet and waiting for the runway surface conditions to improve in CYXU. While holding, the flight crew received a DEICE PRESS caution light. The flight crew completed the QRH, declared a PAN PAN and continued to destination landing without further incident.

C-FYBN, a 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines Inc., was conducting flight SWG 292 from Cancun (MMUN) Mexico to Saskatoon (CYXE), SK. During the descent, a flight attendant experienced a medical condition and was unable to perform the duties required.  The other cabin crew members assumed their duties for the remainder of the flight. An uneventful landing was completed.

C-GKUC, un Pilatus PC-12/47 exploité par Kudlik Aviation Inc. sous l’indicatif KUK848, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP). À l’approche de CYVP, l’équipage a effectué une approche visuelle vers la piste 25. Au moment de baisser le train d’atterrissage, une lumière d’avertissement du tableau de bord s’est allumée pour indiquer que le train de droit n’était pas verrouillé. L’équipage a alors suivi la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a utilisé le levier manuel d’urgence du train. Une approche interrompue a été effectuée et l’aéronef a fait un circuit en restant en vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR). L’aéronef a effectué 2 autres approches VFR interrompues en raison de problème avec le levier manuel d’urgence du train d’atterrissage. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et a décidé d’utiliser la piste 31 où l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GNLW, un Boeing 737-2R4C exploité par Nolinor Aviation, effectuait le vol NRL954 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Mirabel, Qc (CYMX) à destination de l'aéroport de Val-D'Or, Qc (CYVO). Alors que l'aéronef se trouvait en approche finale pour l'atterrissage à CYVO, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence du à un problème au moteur gauche (Pratt & Whitney JT8D-17). L'appareil a atterri sans encombre quelques minutes plus tard. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GYYR, un De Havilland DHC-8-402 exploité par PAL Airlines Ltd., effectuait le vol PVL1909 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Mont-Joli, QC (CYYY) à destination de l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Alors que l'aéronef se trouvait à 30 milles nautiques (NM) au nord est de Rivière du Loup (CYRI), en palier au niveau de vol (FL) 240, un problème est survenu avec la pressurisation de la cabine. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée et l'équipage a effectué une descente d'urgence. Le vol s'est poursuivi vers CYQB et l'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GJZR, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, was conducting flight JZA7132 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC, to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC, with 3 crew on board. After takeoff, the landing gear did not retract when selected up by the flight crew. The airplane had the following landing gear indications: 3 red unsafe and 3 amber lights. Additionally, the No.2 HYD ISO, No. 2 ENG HYD PUMP, No. 2 RUDD HYD and PTU CONTROL FAIL caution lights illuminated. The No. 2 hydraulic pressure was at 0 psi. The crew actioned the "Gear Failed to Retract" checklist. While the checklist was being completed, the No. 2 hydraulic pressure returned to normal, the caution lights extinguished except for the PTU FAIL light which remained illuminated, and the landing gear lights indicated 3 green (down and locked). The ELEV PRESS caution light illuminated momentarily and then extinguished. The flight continued to CYVR with the landing gear down. The crew did not declare an emergency but requested ARFF to be on standby for the landing. After landing, all caution lights extinguished and the system returned to normal with no faults present.Maintenance found a significant amount of air in the No. 2 hydraulic system. The No. 2 hydraulic system was bled and serviced IAW with the aircraft maintenance manual. Several gear swings were completed with no faults found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GUSC, un Jetstream 3212 exploité par Pascan Aviation sous l'indicatif PSC707 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Gaspé (Michel-Pouliot), QC (CYGP) à destination de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU). C-GJZZ, un Bombardier CL-600 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA7939, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Le contrôleur aérien a instruit PCS707 de descendre à 17 000 pieds et l'instruction a bien été relue par l'équipage. Une fois l'aéronef à 17 000 pieds, il a poursuivi sa descente. Le contrôleur aérien a rappelé PSC707 pour l'aviser de maintenir l'altitude précédemment désignée. À ce moment, les distances latérale et verticale avec JZA7939 sont descendues à 4.5 milles nautiques (NM) et 600 pieds. PSC707 a repris l'altitude pour s'établir à 17 000 pieds. Un espacement minimal de 5 NM latéralement et de 1000 pieds verticalement étaient requis.

C-FFLJ, a Flair Airlines Ltd Boeing 737-86J was conducting flight FLE238 From Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Burbank/ Bob Hope Airport (KBUR), CA. While on approach runway 08 at KBUR, flight crew received TCAS RA (resolution advisory) ''Level Off''. Flight crew complied with RA and landed at KBUR without further incident.

C-FLKC, a Flair Airlines Ltd Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight FLE230 From Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Burbank/ Bob Hope Airport (KBUR), CA.  While on descent to start the approach runway 08 at KBUR, flight crew received a TCAS TA (traffic advisory) followed by a TCAS RA (resolution advisory).  Flight crew complied with RA and landed at KBUR without further incident.

C-GAZI, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 767, was conducting a flight CJT2384 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR) BC, to Hamilton (CYHM) Ontario, with 2 flight crew on board. On takeoff, the "MN CARGO DOOR" warning light illuminated and the aural warning sounded. The flight crew declared an emergency with air traffic control and requested radar vectors. The MAIN CARGO DOOR quick reference handbook checklist was completed and the flight crew decided to return to land at CYVR. After landing, the aircraft stopped on the runway, aircraft rescue and firefighting conducted a visual inspection of the aircraft. The airplane then taxied to parking.Maintenance personnel visually inspected the main cargo door and tested the function of the door system. The system checked serviceable with no faults found and the aircraft was returned to service.

PH-AKE, a KLM Royal Dutch Airlines Airbus A330-303, was operating as flight KLM678 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Amsterdam (EHAM), Netherlands with 12 crew and 216 passengers on board. During take-off on Runway 29, the tail contacted the runway surface during rotation. The flight crew were unaware a tail strike had occurred. They had detected a burning odor immediately after lift off and suspected the APU; it was a "bleeds off" take-off and the APU had been supplying conditioned air at the time of take-off. The flight crew consulted the ECAM 'wheel page' and 'APU page' and observed no abnormalities. ATC was queried and they suggested a possible tail strike. The cabin crew were consulted and they did not note anything unusual. The flight continued to EHAM with no further issues. When the aircraft arrived at the gate in EHAM, ground servicing crew noticed the damage to the underside of the empennage and the aircraft was removed from service for damage assessment.

C-GTCJ, un Boeing 757-223 exploité par Cargojet Airways Ltd sous l'indicatif CJT626, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Hamilton/John C. Munro, On (CYHM), à destination Montréal/Mirabel, Qc (CYMX). Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en finale, l’équipage a reçu l’instruction d‘effectuer une remontée, car C-FLAJ, un Boeing 757-223 exploité par Cargojet Airways Ltd sous l’indicatif CJT952 était en train de décoller pour un vol vers Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International, KY, U.S.A. (KCVG). La norme d’espacement de 1000 pieds ou 3 milles nautique (NM) n’a pas été assurée.

A6-EQD, Boeing 777-300 ER operated by Emirates, was conducting flight UAE235 from Dubai (OMDB), UAE to Chicago (KORD), USA. While en-route in Reykjavik Airspace, the crew observed a "Caution Flight Controls" with left elevator locked out EICAS message. The flight crew conducted the checklist items, declared a PAN PAN and diverted to Winnipeg (CYWG) MB. The aircraft landed without further incident.Post flight inspection and tests (AFM Actuator Confidence Test# 27-02-00-400-801 and FIM task MM 27-11100) were conducted. The inspection is still underway, once a maintenance solution has been identified the operator will ferry the aircraft back to Dubai.

C-GEKZ, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight ACA120 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON.  During cruise over US territory, flight crew declared an emergency due to airspeed indication problem.  Flight crew requested priority handling to ATC and landed in CYYZ without further incident.

VT-ALJ, a Boeing 777-300ER operated by Air India as AIC187, was on an IFR flight from Delhi Indira Gandhi International Airport (VIDP), India, to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario. During the arrival, the flight crew received an indication that there was a fire in the aft cargo area. The flight crew declared an emergency, and the flight was given priority by ATC. The flight landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by.

C-FTMY, a Morningstar Air Express ATR-72-202, was operating as flight MAL8058 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Regina (CYQR), SK with 2 flight crew on board. During the initial climb, through 12 000 feet, MAL8058 encountered severe turbulence. The flight crew were unable to control the aircraft in pitch and roll on two separate occasions. In addition, both engine oil pressure warning lights illuminated briefly. Several loose items flew about the flight deck but neither pilot were injured. A decision was made to return to CYYC where an uneventful landing occurred. Company maintenance performed the necessary inspections related to the severe turbulence encounter and no damage was observed.

C-FORB, a Chartright Air Gulfstream G IV operated flight HRT336 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport (KOPF) FL. Shortly after departure from CYYZ during climb to FL400 the crew noted an acrid smell. They took a look back into the cabin and white smoke was visible. The crew was not able to identify the source of the smoke. A PAN PAN was declared in the vicinity of Cleveland, OH. The flight diverted to Cleveland Hopkins International Airport (KCLE) OH. Upon landing the fire crew inspected the aircraft and no fire was detected. The crew taxied the aircraft to the FBO and subsequently carried out a detailed inspection of the aircraft but were not able to identify the source of the smoke or any damage. The aircraft was snagged with an electrical fault and is undergoing maintenance.

C-FRDN, a privately registered PA-46-350P was conducting a flight from Charles B. Wheeler Downtown Airport (KMKC) Kansas City, MO  to  James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG) Winnipeg, MB. The aircraft was cleared to land on runway 36 at CYWG. Runway 36 was bare and dry, upon touchdown the aircraft unexpectedly and violently turned to the left and exited the runway. The aircraft made contact with compacted snow and sustained damage to the propeller and the nose gear assembly. There were no injures to the pilot or to the passengers. ARFF did attend.A local AMO is inspecting and assessing the damage to the aircraft.

C-GZQT, a Cirrus SR22 being operated by ITPS Canada Ltd. as SA29, was on a training flight in the circuit for runway 33 with three pilots on board; there was an instructor and a student occupying the front seats. During a normal landing, the aircraft was allowed to slow down unintentionally during the flare at approximately 5-10 feet AGL. The student attempted to correct by adding power, but moved the control stick in his left hand, mistaking it for the throttle. This resulted in the aircraft pitching down rapidly and contacting the runway, causing the nosewheel assembly to become detached from the aircraft. The instructor pilot intervened during this sequence, and landed the aircraft on the remaining runway. The aircraft came to rest on its nose. There were no injuries.

C-GFCG, a Bombardier CL-600-2B16 operated by Chartright Air Inc. as HRT623, was on a scheduled maintenance flight from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, to Muskoka Airport (CYQA), Ontario, with 2 crew and 2 passengers on board. Shortly after departure, the flight crew received an engine fire indication. The crew declared PAN PAN and requested a return to CYYZ, landing without incident at 1313 EST with ARFF standing by. Maintenance action revealed a faulty engine fire sensing loop, which was replaced before the aircraft was returned to service.

N408DX, a Delta Air Lines Airbus A330-900, was conducting flight DAL9770 from Seattle Int’l (KSEA) WA, USA, to Incheon Int’l (RKSI) ROK, with 13 crew and no passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff, the flight crew observed an 'ENG 2 BLEED STATUS FAULT' electronic centralized aircraft monitor (ECAM) message. They completed the ECAM actions and referenced the quick reference handbook (QRH) noting that the fault remained. Dispatch and maintenance were contacted and the crew was advised to conduct a computer reset after reaching cruise altitude. Before reaching cruise altitude, the flight crew observed an 'ENG 2 CTL SYS FAULT' ECAM message with several secondary faults. The flight crew completed the ECAM actions and noted that the QRH procedure required the affected engine to be shut down for approach and landing. The decision was made to declare an emergency return to SEA. During approach into SEA, the flight crew shut down the No. 2 engine (Trent 7000 SN 75143) at approximately 5000 feet above sea level and landed without further incident.Maintenance inspected the airplane and found a loose B-nut on the PS26 moisture trap. Maintenance personnel torqued the B-nut, performed an engine run, and completed an overweight landing inspection. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GHPW, a VIH Helicopter Ltd. Bell 206B helicopter, was supporting logging operations near Frisco Lake, BC, with 1 pilot onboard. While conducting long line operations, the pilot inadvertently activated the belly hook release when he transmitted on the radio to the supported logging crew below. There were no injuries. There was no damage to the aircraft. The saws and equipment that were being slung were damaged.

C-FQNG, a Sikorsky S-61N aircraft operated by VIH Helicopters, was conducting heli-logging operations approximately 30 NM south of Port Hardy (CYZT) BC, with 2 pilots on board. While operating, the helicopter began to shudder violently. The pilot reduced power and the shudder ceased. When power was reapplied, the shudder returned. Power was again reduced and the crew communicated their situation to their base of operations. A small amount of power was applied to enable a slow return to base and, as the vibration returned, the crew elected to drop the grapple by manual release. On final approach, the left attitude indicator failed as did the pitch and roll channels for the Automatic Flight Control System (AFCS). The helicopter landed without further incident.The operator's maintenance discovered the vertical gyroscope, which supplies information to the AFCS, had failed. The vertical gyroscope was replaced and the helicopter was returned to service.

C-GFJZ, a MHI RJ Aviation ULC CL-600-2D24 (CRJ 900 series) operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was operating flight JZA 8596 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. On departure out from CYWG, the crew of C-GFJZ observed a crossflow caution message and a fuel quantity imbalance that could not be controlled. The fuel imbalance was substantial enough that the crew elected to shut down the right engine. The crew requested a clearance to return to CYWG where they carried out an uneventful landing. A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed a failed cross-flow pump.
