C-GJDA, an Airbus A330-243 operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC038 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) to the Tarbes-Lourdes-Pyrénées Airport, France (LFBT). As the aircraft was climbing through flight level (FL) 330, the crew received a FWD Cargo Smoke and Land ASAP message from the Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitoring (ECAM) system. The crew carried out the ECAM procedures and returned to CYUL. No emergency was declared, but the aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) services were on standby. The aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance inspected the forward and aft cargo hold and no evidence of smoke, or events that would have caused a smoke indication, were found.  A faulty Smoke Detection Control Unit (SDCU) was suspected. Maintenance replaced the unit.

C-GBEP, a privately registered Gray-Sherick aircraft Special model, was conducting a flight between Puerto Plata/Gregorio Luperón Intl (MDPP) Dominican Republic to St-Barthélemy/ Gustaff III Airport (TFFJ), Guadeloupe.  During landing, the aircraft suffered a hard landing on runway 10. Consequently, left hand gear collapsed, aircraft veered to the left exiting the runway and impacted the airfield enclosure wall.  Aircraft sustained substantial damage and pilot suffered minor injuries.  BEA advised they will not conduct ICAO annex 13 investigation as the aircraft is registered as a Special Certificate Airworthiness Amateur built Aircraft (CARs standard 549).

C-GJPY, a Summit Air Ltd. Aerospatiale ATR 72, was operating as flight SUT7191 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Kugluktuk (CYCO), NU. On approach to CYCO the crew noted a low oil pressure indication on the No. 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW124B). The crew conducted a precautionary engine shutdown, declared an emergency and landed with no further issues.Following the flight, the maintenance department had found that the oil plug in the oil cooler had loosened off. The plug was replaced, ground runs were conducted and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FOKR, a privately registered Piper PA-46-600TP, was on a visual flight rules flight from the Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), Ontario, to the Stratford Municipal Airport (CYSA), Ontario, with the pilot as sole occupant. During the landing roll on runway 17, the pilot felt the aircraft swerving and attempted a correction before deciding to reject the landing. After he added power for the go-around, the right main wheel entered the snowbank beside the runway, causing the aircraft to exit the runway surface into an area of undisturbed snow. The aircraft collided with some airport signage before the nosewheel sheared off, the aircraft came to a stop upright in a snow covered area beside the runway. The pilot exited the aircraft uninjured, the aircraft had been damaged significantly. The propeller was destroyed, and there was damage to the wing, cowling, and engine mounts. The ELT was activated during the runway excursion.

C-GCJH, a Piper PA-31-350 aircraft operated by Skycare Air Ambulance, was enroute from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Poplar Hill (CPV7), ON with a crew of two on board. While in cruise, the left engine (Lycoming LTIO-540) began to run rough followed by a loss of power. The crew decided to do a precautionary shutdown of the engine and then diverted to Dryden (CYHD), ON, where a successful single-engine landing was completed.

C-FDHB, a Kenn Borek Air Viking DHC-6-200 was conducting a flight from Liberia/Daniel Oduber Quirós Intl (MRLB), Costa Rica to Houston/ William P. Hobby (KHOU), TX.  After landing in KHOU, the pilot applied brakes to exit on taxiway and felt that the airplane ''grabbed'' a bit more then usual on the left hand side.  After exiting the runway, the flight engineer on board called ''Fire'' on left hand side of the airplane.  The pilot stopped the airplane and shutdown engines.  Flight engineer jumped out and extinguished fire on left hand main landing gear with handheld onboard fire extinguisher.  After inspection, it was discovered that the left hand brake caliper had broken free from his mount and rotated forward severing the hydraulic lines.

C-GWSX, a Westjet Airlines Ltd Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight WS2060 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Los Cabos Intl. (MMSD), Mexico.  In the vicinity of Los Angeles Intl. (KLAX), CA, a flight attendant became incapacitated.  Flight landed at destination without further incident.

C-FZJA, a MHI RJ Aviation CL600-2B19 (CRJ200) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP was conducting flight JZA7116 from Calgary International Airport (CYYC), AB to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON with 3 crew and 16 passengers onboard. While on approach into CYYZ runway 05, the flaps failed to extend when the flight crew actioned the lever to lower the flaps. The flight crew completed the applicable procedure of the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH), conducted a missed approach and declared Pan Pan with Air Traffic Control (ATC). The aircraft performed a second approach with the flaps up into runway 05 where it landed without further incident with Airport Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) vehicles standing by. The company maintenance inspected the system and found the brake and positioning sensing unit (BPSU) sensing the RH flaps position at 46.6 degrees and a full lock of the LH flaps. Maintenance adjusted the RH flaps with the BPSU to 45 degrees and replaced all four LH flap actuators. The applicable rigging was completed and the system tested serviceable.

C-GAWS, a Boeing 737-8CT operated by Westjet was conducting flight WJA2507 from Puerto Plata Gregorio Luperon International Airport (MDPP), Dominican Republic to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON with 6 crew and 158 passengers onboard. While on approach into CYYZ runway 06L, the flight crew selected the flaps to 30 but subsequently noticed the flaps stopped and remained at 15. The flight crew went through non-normal procedure, performed a go-around  and declared Pan Pan with Air Traffic Control (ATC). The aircraft performed a second approach into runway 05 with the flaps at 15 where it landed without further incident with Airport Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) vehicles standing by.  The company maintenance inspected the aircraft, replaced the Trailing Edge (TE) Flap transmitters, the left TE Flap position transmitter connector, the Flap position indicator and tested the system serviceable.

C-GUBL. an Air Transat A330-234 aircraft (flight TSC 326) was at the de-icing facility in Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON prior to departure. While parked the #1 engine performed an auto-shutdown. While the crew were performing their procedures and with the APU not operating, the #2 engine also auto-shutdown (Rolls Royce Trent 772B) . The flight crew was able to re-start both engines and taxied to the gate. The aircraft was removed from service pending investigation by the operator and Rolls-Royce, the engine manufacturer.

N586FE, a Federal Express MD-11 aircraft (flight FDX 147) was on the climb out after departing from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. At approximately 10000 feet ASL, the flight crew received an indication for a U/L reverser #1 engine accompanied by vibrations. The crew followed QRH procedures and shut down the engine. They declared an emergency and returned to CYYZ. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. Upon inspection maintenance found the #1 thrust reverser outboard center drive unit brake handle not stowed. The handle was re-stowed and a windmill run inspection was performed IAW 72-00-05-200-831 with no further discrepancies found. The #1 thrust reverser was de-activated under MEL 78-30-01-A, Category C. The aircraft returned to service.

C-GUJA, a Jazz Aviation LP MHI RJ Aviation ULC CL-600-2B19 aircraft (flight 8234) was on final approach to Toronto Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON, when the crew started the APU and received an APU fault message followed by a fire warning indication. The APU then performed an auto shutdown. The cabin crew confirmed a burning smell in the cabin. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and continued with the approach. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The aircraft was met by ARFF but there was no evidence of fire. The aircraft was cleared and continued to the gate. Maintenance found the intake supply duct and bellows damaged. It appeared the APU door closed while the APU was operating at speed. Maintenance replaced the door actuator, potentiometer, and the Electronic Control Unit (ECU). The aircraft was then cleared to return to service.

C-GMAI, un Boeing 737-200 opéré par Air Inuit, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Kattiniq/Donaldson, QC (CTP9) à destination de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) sous l'indicatif AIE754 avec 52 passagers et 4 membres d'équipage à bord. Au niveau de vol 180, le bord intérieur du bec de bord d'attaque de l'aile gauche a été observé en asymétrie. Malgré que la manoeuvrabilité de l'appareil n'était pas affectée de façon importante, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence et dérouté vers l'aéroport de de Puvirnituq, QC (CYPX) où il s'est posé sans encombre. L’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage et il n’y a eu aucun blessé.Suite à l'inspection effectuée par le personnel de maintenance, l'actuateur intérieur du bec de bord d'attaque remplacé.

C-FNAI, un Daher (Socata) TBM 700 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU). Suite à un problème de train d'atterrissage, le pilote a déclaré une urgence et demandé un examen du train par le personnel de la tour de contrôle. L'avion s'est posé sans encombre.

C-GPAR, un Dash8-311 exploité par PAL Airlines Ltd. sous l'indicatif PVL3042, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. C-GRDU, un Saab 340B exploité par Pascan sous l'indicatif PSC311 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Mont-Joli, QC (CYYY) à destination de l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV). À environs 40 miles nautiques au sud-ouest de CYZV, l'espacement entre C-GPAR et C-GRDU a été réduit à 1.5 mile nautique horizontalement et 700 pieds verticalement alors que l'espacement minimal requis est de 5 miles nautiques horizontalement ou 1000 pieds verticalement.

The Simpson Air (1981) Limited U206G, C-GGHU, was on a flight from Fort Simpson Island (CET4), NT to Fort McPherson (CZFM), NT. Upon landing at CZFM the aircraft came into contact with a snow bank on the side of Runway 30 and became stuck; there were no injuries. Airport radio was notified and a maintenance crew came and cleared a path to extract the aircraft from the snow. The aircraft was repositioned to the ramp. An assessment of the aircraft was made by the pilot and the maintenance organization and no damage noted.

C-FENO, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-402 (flight WEN3202) was conducting an instrument flight rules flight from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Fort Saint John (CYXJ) BC, with 4 crew members and 17 passengers on board. When the flight crew selected gear up after take-off from CYVR, the annunciators displayed an amber “main left gear door” indication, and a red “left main gear” indication. The crew actioned the landing gear door malfunction checklist, completed the alternate gear extension procedure, and decided to return to CYVR. They did not declare an emergency but indicated a need for emergency response vehicles to be on standby. The airplane landed without incident and was met by aircraft rescue firefighting vehicles. Maintenance found the left retract actuator was bypassing internally and replaced the retract actuator. The inspection also found the right main landing gear alternate extension cam mechanism assembly and the alternate extension up-lock release cable were broken. Those were replaced and, after a rigging check, the airplane was returned to service.

N562GJ, un Bombardier RJ-550 exploité par GoJet Airlines Inc., effectuait le vol GJS4535 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC à destination de l’aéroport de Chicago O'Hare International, IL (KORD) avec 22 personnes à bord. Peu après le décollage, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison d'une indication de porte ouverte et est revenu atterrir à CYUL où il s'est posé sans encombre.

C-GROV, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300 (flight AC351) was on climb out from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON when the flight crew noticed a smell in the aircraft that intensified as the flight continued. The flight crew contacted maintenance and after discussion they decided to return to CYOW and declare a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed uneventfully and stopped on the runway for inspection, afterwards it taxied to the gate. Maintenance performed various tests and checked both engines and APU for possible inlet contamination. No faults were found and after high power runs were successfully completed the recirculation filters were replaced. No further smell were noted and the aircraft returned to service.

N587NN, a CL-600-2D24, operated by American Airlines as flight JIA5110 was on final approach into Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ). The flight crew selected the landing gear down, and received an outboard antiskid caution message. The flight crew conducted a go-around, followed the QRH procedures, and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. A post flight maintenance inspection tested the spoiler/stabilizer control units (SSCUS) and anti-skid control system and found no faults. The aircraft was subsequently returned to service.

C-FCQJ, a Bell 206B operated by Delta Helicopters was conducting an aerial wildlife survey approximately 23 nm East South East of Camrose (CEQ3), AB, with the pilot and three passengers on board. Approximately an hour and 25 minutes into the flight, while performing low level maneuvering to count wildlife, the helicopter experienced an uncommanded rotation to the right, due to a loss of tail rotor authority. In the process of arresting the rotation, the helicopter descended and impacted terrain. The helicopter remained upright, there was no post-impact fire, and the 406 Mhz ELT activated. The pilot and three passengers received serious injuries.UPDATED 12 AUGUST 2022

The GCS Aviation Ltd. (CAR604) Beech B300, C-FGSX, was operating on a flight from Victoria, BC (CYYJ) to Red Deer, AB (CYQF). Upon landing, the pilot engaged propeller reverse thrust and the RH engine engaged reverse before the LH engine. The asymmetric thrust condition created a directional control issue. The pilot attempted to recover using yaw control, braking and bringing the engines out of reverse thrust; however, the aircraft continued to yaw to the left and exited the west side of the runway. The aircraft skidded sideways and rotated approximately 270 degrees before coming to rest 50 feet from the edge of the runway surface. The airport authority assisted in transferring the passengers back to the hangar, and the aircraft was subsequently towed back to the hangar. The pilot and two passengers received no injuries. The aircraft damage was limited to a flat RH tire. Company maintenance performed engine ground runs and found the RH engine was entering reverse ahead of the LH engine. The LH engine beta valve and reverse pick-up rigging was adjusted and the aircraft released for continued service.

C-GVUE, a privately registered Cessna 340A, departed La Ronge/Barber Field (CYVC), SK for Stony Rapids (CYSF), SK. Shortly after takeoff, the pilot noticed the oil door of the left-hand engine nacelle was open and oil was streaming down the cowl. The left-hand engine (TSIO-520-NB) was shutdown and the propeller feathered. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft returned to CYVC where a successful single engine landing was completed.After landing an inspection by the operator of the left-hand engine found the oil dip stick was missing, the breather tube was plugged with frost, and the oil/air separator was blocked with ice/sledge. The operator's maintenance serviced the oil/air separator, insulated the breather tube, and replaced the oil dip stick. Ground runs and a test flight were completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GDKN, a Sikorsky S-92 helicopter operated by Cougar Helicopters Inc., was conducting flight CHI831 from the Hibernia offshore platform (HIB) to St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL. Shortly after departure from HIB, a haze was noticed in the aircraft interior. The flight crew selected the cockpit heating system off and actioned the Emergency Checklist items. The haze immediately dissipated, and the crew elected to return to HIB where the aircraft landed without further incident. There were no injuries. A heater system hose was found partially separated, and the hose was replaced. The helicopter was returned to service following heater system testing.

C-GMIU, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 was conducting flight ACA1046 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Palm Spring Intl. (KPSP), CA.  During approach, ATC informed flight crew of a traffic 2 nautical miles ahead.  Shortly after, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to ''climb''.  Flight crew followed the RA and landed in KPSP without further incident.

C-GORN, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Propair Inc., was conducting flight PRO4005 from Chibougamau-Chapais Airport (CYMT), QC to Wabush (CYWK), NL. While in cruise flight the crew received a master warning light, accompanied by a low right engine oil pressure indication. The crew conducted the memory items, and determined that the right engine oil pressure was indicating 60 psi. The flight was at the start of descent, and the crew reduced power. The right engine oil pressure continued to decrease and when at 50 psi the crew carried out the emergency checklist items, shut down the right engine, and declared PAN PAN with CYWK air traffic services. The crew utilized the single-engine landing checklist, and briefed the single-engine go-around checklist before landing at CYWK without further incident. The crew shutdown on the runway and coordinated with airport services for transportation of passengers and the towing of the aircraft.Maintenance personnel determined the loss of number 2 engine oil pressure was due to engine oil leakage caused by a faulted engine oil cooler.

C-FYJO, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-8K5, was conducting flight SWG407 from Punta Cana Intl. (MDPC) Dominican Republic to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During descent in Cleveland airspace, Flight crew was cleared to descent from FL357 to FL340 and was a few second later re-cleared to FL330 and to be levelled within 2 minutes or less.  At FL337, Flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to monitor vertical speed and showed traffic 700 feet below.  Flight crew responded to RA command with avoidance maneuver and climbed back to FL340 with autopilot re-engaged. Aircraft landed at CYYZ without further incident.

At 1620 Eastern Standard Time, a privately-owned Cessna 150G (registration C-FVGZ) departed Nixon Airport (CNX8), ON on a local visual flight rules (VFR) flight. Upon return, the pilot positioned the aircraft on final for Runway 12 at CNX8. Shortly after commencing the final approach, the aircraft experienced a power loss. The pilot verified the engine instruments, which were all indicating normal. The pilot recognized that he would be unable to reach the runway so elected to carry out a forced approach in a nearby farmer's field. The aircraft's main landing gear touched down first, followed by the nosewheel. When the nosewheel contacted the rough terrain, it broke off and the aircraft flipped over and came to rest inverted. The pilot was able to egress from the aircraft with minor injuries. There was no post-crash fire. The aircraft suffered substantial damage.

C-GNUE, a Cessna 172R aircraft owned by Brampton Flying Club, was on a rental round-trip visual flight rules (VFR) flight from Brampton-Caledon airport (CNC3), ON with a stop in Oshawa Executive Airport (CYOO), ON via Toronto City Center with one pilot and one passenger onboard.  At 2301, Toronto Terminal provided the occurrence pilot with a transponder code, and the pilot readback the correct code. The aircraft then entered Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON Class C controlled airspace without Air Traffic Control (ATC) clearance. At that point, the transponder code was not appearing on the ATC radar. The aircraft continued, crossing eastbound through the localizer of runway 05 at CYYZ where it appeared on ATC radar. The aircraft flew in front of flight ICE37B, a Boeing 737 Max 8 aircraft on final approach for runway 05, resulting in a minimum separation of 300 feet vertical and 1 nm lateral. Subsequently, the aircraft crossed the localizer for runway 06L at CYYZ in front of flight ROU1657, an Airbus A321 aircraft on final approach resulting in a minimum separation of 900 feet vertical and 0.3 nm lateral. After crossing the localizer for runway 06L, the occurrence pilot exited CYYZ control zone under the direction of Toronto Terminal, and the flight continued without further incident.

C-FDOD, a Bell Helicopter Textron 412 operated by Wisk Air Helicopters, was returning from a work site on a power line to the work camp at Kingfisher Lake, ON with the pilot and 6 passengers on board. While enroute the No. 1 "FUEL LOW" (quantity) caution annunciator illuminated. The pilot commenced a precautionary landing and planned for a possible single engine landing. During the descent, at approximately 200 feet above ground level, the No. 1 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6T-3B) lost power accompanied by illumination of the associated caution/warning annunciators. While on short final the No. 2 engine began to fluctuate and then lost power. A successful autorotative landing was conducted onto the frozen, snow covered surface of Kingfisher Lake with both engines inoperative. There were no injuries and the helicopter was undamaged. The helicopter was refueled the next day and flown to the Kingfisher Lake camp. After further inspection the helicopter was ferried to the operator's maintenance base under a flight permit.The operator's maintenance personnel subsequently discovered several discrepancies. Loose B nuts in the No.1 fuel tank prevented the ejector pump from transferring fuel aft, over the baffle, to the boost pump side of the fuel tank. The examination also determined that the No. 2 engine was starved for fuel due to leaking flapper valve plates that, in a normal flight attitude, allowed fuel to move forward, through the baffle, at a rate that exceeded the recapture capacity of the ejector pump. The effect of these discrepancies was to trap unusable fuel forward of the baffle in each fuel tank. Further discrepancies were noted such as a damaged No. 2 low level float switch and inaccurate fuel quantity indication systems. The operator is conducting checks on the remaining aircraft in the fleet.

C-FGHZ, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner was operating as flight ACA518 from Honolulu (PHNL) HI, to Vancouver (CYVR) BC, with 10 crew and 89 passengers on board. During cruise, the flight crew received an Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) "Slat Drive" message. In consultation with company dispatch and the Maintenance Operations Center (MOC), the flight crew decided to continue to CYVR. A Pan-Pan was declared due to the requirement for a higher than standard approach speed. The flight landed without incident with ARFF on standby. Company maintenance replaced the inboard slat skew 6 sensor as per the Maintenance Manual and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJNL, un DHC-8-311 exploité par Hydro-Québec, effectuait le vol HYD160 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Québec/Jean Lesage, Qc (CYQB) à destination de La Grande 4, Qc (CYAH). Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en palier à environ 130 milles nautiques (NM) au sud de La Grande Rivière, Qc (CYGL), l'équipage a constaté une perte totale du liquide hydraulique dans le système numéro 2. Une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclaré et un déroutement vers l'aéroport de CYGL a été effectué. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée et le train d’atterrissage a été déployé avec succès. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre à CYGL. Le personnel de maintenance a remplacé une ligne hydraulique qui fuyait et l'appareil a été remis en service.

C-GBJZ, un De Havilland Dash 8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation, effectuait le vol JZA7937 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Qc (CYUL). En route, à environ 92 milles nautiques (NM) à l'est-nord-est (ENE) de CYUL et à une altitude de 14 000 pieds ASL, une indication de porte-cargo arrière non sécurisée est apparue. L'équipage a amorcé une descente vers 8000 pieds durant laquelle l'indication a disparu. Une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclaré. L'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre à CYUL.

C-GHPF, un Pilatus PC-12/45 exploité par Panorama Fixed Wings Ltd, effectuait le vol PNO727 selon les règles de vol aux instrument depuis l'aéeroport de Sanikiluaq, Nu (CYSK) à destination d'Iqaluit, Nu (CYFB).  Alors que l'appareil se trouvait à environ 40 milles nautiques (NM) à l'ouest de CYFB, l'équipage à perçu une odeur de fumée dans le poste de pilotage, sans observer de fumée. Une urgence (Pan Pan) a été déclaré et l'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre à CYFB. Le personnel de maintenance a déterminé qu'une fissure dans le bord d'attaque de l'orifice d'induction d'air du moteur avait permis au gaz d'échappement de pénétrer dans le système de pressurisation de l'aéronef.

C-FJRX, a Cessna 680 registered to I.M.P. Group Ltd, was conducting a flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. When the crew selected the landing gear up after rotation, it did not retract. The gear was then selected down which resulted in a 3 green / safe indication. The crew completed the associated checklist, decided to return to CYWG, and requested a clearance to hold in order to burn off fuel to reach their landing weight. Once the aircraft reached the landing weight, the crew requested a clearance to return to CYWG where they conducted an uneventful landing on Runway 18 with emergency vehicles standing by. A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed a leaking nosewheel oleo. The oleo seals were replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FLRJ, an AVRO RJ85 operated by Summit Air, was conducting flight SUT8592 from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Edmonton International, AB (CYEG) with 4 crew members and 44 passengers on board. Shortly after departure from CYZF, the flight crew experienced an AC BUS #2 OFF annunciation. The flight crew elected to return to CYZF. On approach to CYZF, as the flight crew was extending the flaps, the flaps failed to extend beyond flaps 18 when flaps 24 was selected. A go around was initiated, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and proceeded to complete another approach. A second approach, and subsequent uneventful landing was completed. Post flight troubleshooting by company  maintenance determined that the AC BUS 2 contactor required replacement. Ground checks were completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GROC, a privately registered Cessna 182N was conducting a flight from Springbank (CYBW), AB to Bonnyville (CYBF), AB with one pilot on board. As the aircraft was taxiing to the departure runway, the wind caught the left wing and flipped the aircraft over upside down on the taxiway. The aircraft sustained significant damage; however, the pilot evacuated the aircraft uninjured. The METAR for the CYBW airport issued 20 minutes before the accident reported winds at 280°T 28 gusting 44 knots. A special observation issued just before the accident reported winds 280°T at 40 gusting 53 knots.

C-FDJZ, Bombardier CRJ 900 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation Ltd, was conducting flight JZA8930 from Thunder Bay (CYQT) ON to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON with a crew of four and 29 passengers on board. During the climb to enroute altitude, the lavatory smoke alarm sounded and cabin crew reported plastic burning smell with no sign of visible smoke. The flight crew conducted the emergency procedures and requested to return to CYQT. ARFF services were requested to be on standby and the aircraft landed without further event.An inspection of the aircraft by the operator's maintenance determined that the R/H pack internal failure produced smoke or vapor substantial enough to send off the lavatory smoke alarm. The R/H pack was deferred and a test flight conducted. The aircraft was routed to the operator's CYYZ maintenance base and is scheduled to have the R/H pack replaced prior to returning to service.

C-GGCA, a Beechcraft 1900D operated by Transwest Air, was conducting a commercial flight from Saskatoon, Saskatchewan (CYXE) to Edmonton International, Alberta (CYEG) with 2 crew and 7 passengers on board. As the aircraft was performing the initial descent into the greater Edmonton area, approximately 32 nm SE of CYEG, the crew experienced an uncommanded propeller RPM (Np) decrease on the right engine of approximately 200 RPM. Operation of the propeller control lever had no effect on the propeller speed selection. Shortly after the initial Np decrease, the Np speed decreased again to approximately 1000 RPM. The flight crew elected to complete a precautionary right engine shut down (Pratt and Whitney Canada - PT6A-67D), and declared an emergency with ATC. The flight crew then completed a passenger briefing, and an uneventful single-engine approach and landing was conducted.

C-GFAD, a Beech B200 operated by Fast Air Ltd, was conducting flight PBR635 from Wunnumin Lake (CKL3), ON to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG) MB, with 2 crew members and 1 passenger on board. While on approach for Runway 31 in CYWG, the flight crew selected landing gear down; however, did not receive the three landing gear down annunciator lights. After several unsuccessful attempts to lower the gear, the landing gear was manually extended. Emergency services were requested to be on standby as a precaution and the aircraft subsequently landed without further incident. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft.The operator's maintenance identified that the accumulator pack's level was low. The pack was serviced and the gear swings were completed. The aircraft has been released into service.

C-FNIJ, an ATR 72-212A operated by North Star Air, was conducting flight BF503 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Brochet (CYBT) MB. Shortly after takeoff from CYTH, the crew observed an intermittent master caution light related to low engine oil pressure on the right engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW127F). The crew opted to return to YTH. During their return, the oil pressure gauge indicated decreasing oil pressure and, after consulting the QRH, the crew shut down the right engine as a precautionary measure. An emergency was declared and an uneventful landing in CYTH was conducted.  A subsequent inspection by the operator revealed that the right engine's oil cap was not secured, which allowed oil to vent out. It was also noted that the check valve designed to prevent oil from venting out if the oil cap is not secure was not functioning. A fleet wide inspection of all North Star Air ATR aircraft is being conducted by the operator.

C-FYPB, a Swoop Inc. Boeing 737-8CT, was preparing for flight WSW419 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Int'l (CYYZ), ON, with 6 flight crew and 126 passengers on board. The aircraft was parked at the gate in CYLW and configured to be deiced by Executive Aviation. The doors were closed, engines were off, and the APU was running. The deice truck was parked outside the aircraft clearance zone near the left wing with 1 operator in the bucket. The driver of the deice truck exited the vehicle to push another aircraft. Approximately 5 minutes later, the truck began rolling towards the aircraft and stopped when it collided with the left hand engine nacelle. The aircraft was deplaned and there were no reported injuries. The aircraft sustained damage to the outboard leading edge of the left hand engine inlet cowl. Maintenance replaced the left engine inlet cowl and the aircraft was returned to service. The deice truck's braking system was inspected and function tested with no faults found. Executive Aviation is conducting an internal investigation.

C-FGSJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd Boeing 767-300, was conducting flight CJT979 from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky Intl. (KCVG) KY to  	Derby/East Midlands Airport (EGNX), UK.  On descent to EGNX passing through FL200 on radar vectors, flight crew noticed the autopilot was not able to follow assigned heading and received an ''Autopilot'' EICAS (Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System) message.  Flight crew disconnected autopilot and found that aileron input was restricted/jammed.  Flight crew consulted QRH for restricted flight control and without improvement declared a PAN PAN and continued approach for runway 27.  While on final at approximately 2600 feet above sea level, roll function appeared to return to normal and aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FYMQ, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. B737-800 conducting flight SWG451 from Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC) Dominica Republic to Toronto Pearson IntL.(CYYZ), ON. Shortly after take-off, a flight attendant became incapacitated for the flight however was able to resume all duties prior to landing. The flight landed in YYZ without further incident.

C-FQWA, a Beech 1900D operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG751 from Sioux Lookout (CYXL) ON. to Muskrat Dam (CZMD), ON, with 2 crew members and 5 passengers on board. While on approach for CZMD, the flight crew selected landing gear down; however, the gear remained up and the crew did not receive the three landing gear down annunciator lights. The flight crew decided to return to CYXL and requested emergency services to be on standby as a precaution. The landing gear was manually extended and the aircraft landed without further incident. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft.The operator's maintenance identified an issue with the aircraft bus tie control PC board and replaced these components. GCU's were adjusted, gear swings were completed on the ground, and a successful inflight test flight was completed. The aircraft has been released into regular service.Previous similar occurrences: A21C0113 and A21C0114.

C-GSUI, a North Cariboo Flying Service Ltd. British Aerospace Avro 146 Series RJ100, was operating as flight NCB1512 from Calgary Int’l (CYYC) AB, to Terrace (CYXT) BC, with 4 crew and 77 passengers onboard. On short final for an ILS approach, at approximately 400 feet above ground level, the aircraft encountered wind shear causing an aerodynamic performance degradation and deviation from the glideslope. The aircraft auto-throttle system compensated for the performance change and enabled the crew to regain the glideslope. The crew then observed a GEN 4 caution light for the No. 4 engine (Avco Lycoming, LF-507-1F) and noted the engine continued to produce power based on the associated gas producer speed (N1) indication. The crew proceeded with the landing and touched down without further incident. Once on the ground, the crew found the No.4 engine was now indicating a decrease in N1 with an exceedance in the exhaust gas temperature (EGT) limitation. The No. 4 engine was shut down on the taxiway with no additional indications or warnings. There were no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft.Following arrival, the crew inspected the engine and no damage or leakage was found. When weather permits, the aircraft will be ferried on the 3 remaining engines to CYYC for completion of the required maintenance actions.

C-GYNG, an AW139 helicopter operated by 7506406 Canada Inc. (Ornge) as LF4, was on a positioning flight from the Peterborough Airport (CYPQ), Ontario, to the Belleville General Hospital Heliport (CBV5), Ontario, with 2 pilots and 2 medical crew on board. After selecting the landing gear down, the RH main landing gear did not indicate down and locked. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist and decided to divert to the Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), Ontario, which was their main base. They requested ARFF to stand by during their landing, which would take place in a remote location at the CYOW airport. The helicopter landed without incident. The landing gear wiring harness was replaced, and the helicopter returned to service.

C-FVRJ, a De Havilland Aircraft DHC-8-102 operated by Central Mountain Air, was conducting flight GLR8292 from Kamloops (CYKA) BC, to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR) BC, with 3 crew members on board. After the landing gear was retracted on departure from CYKA, the flight crew received a landing gear unsafe advisory indication. The landing gear was subsequently lowered and the nose gear down-and-locked indication did not illuminate. The flight crew declared an emergency and anticipated having to extend the landing gear manually prior to landing at CYVR. The crew cycled the landing gear a second time and, on that extension, the indication showed that all the gear was down and locked. The flight landed without further incident. Subsequent maintenance actions found the nose landing gear shock strut assembly to be compressed. This prevented the landing gear from fully retracting and kept the nose gear doors from properly closing. Hydraulic fluid was added to the shock strut as per the aircraft's maintenance manual and landing gear test swings were successfully conducted. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJCQ, an ATR 72-200 operated by Calm Air, was conducting flight CAV468 from Goa Haven (CYHK), NU to Thompson (CYTH), MB. When the flight was approximately 150 nm west southwest from Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU, the crew observed an intermittent low oil pressure warning light on the left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW124B). The crew referred to the QRH and decided to divert to CYRT. While enroute to CYRT, the master caution light  for the engine low oil pressure illuminated. The crew shut down the left engine as a precautionary measure and continued to CYRT where they carried out an uneventful landing.

C-FYJO, a Boeing 737-8K5 operated by Sunwing Airlines Inc., was conducting flight SWG411 from Puerto Plata/Gregorio Luperón International Airport (MDPP), DR, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario. During the initial flap extension, the flight crew received a fault message. After actioning the appropriate checklists, the crew advised that they would be landing with flap 15, and requested to have ARFF standing by. The flight landed uneventfully at 0133 EST.

N391CA, a MHI RJ Aviation ULC CRJ700 operated by Endeavor Air, was conducting EDV5441, a flight from John F. Kennedy International Airport (KJFK), USA to Minneapolis-St Paul International Airport (KMSP), USA. During cruise flight at FL360, at approximately 0905 EST, the crew observed a delamination of the windshield, after which they requested a descent. During the descent, the windshield shattered and the flight crew declared an emergency, requesting an emergency descent to 10000 feet. The crew requested to divert to the Coleman A. Young International Airport (KDET), USA, and landed there uneventfully at 1050 EST.

C-FFLA, a Boeing 737-86N operated by Flair Airlines, was conducting flight FLE802, from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), Alberta, to the Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), Ontario. During the ILS approach into CYKF, the flaps failed to extend beyond 25 degrees. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist and requested a diversion to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, where they requested to have ARFF standing by to inspect the aircraft after landing, which would be performed at a reduced flap setting. The flight landed uneventfully at 0139 EST. The Flap/Slat Control Unit was found to have failed, and will be replaced before the aircraft is returned to service.

C-FTJP, a Canadair CL-600-2B16 (Series 604) operated by NovaJet as NOJ64, was departing Peterborough Airport (CYPQ), Ontario, for a local test flight following a heavy maintenance check. While in flight, the crew received an indication of a baggage compartment overheat. They completed the appropriate checklist, declared an emergency with Toronto Centre, and returned uneventfully to CYPQ. It was determined that sections of the cabin ventilation duct in the vicinity of the smoke detector had deteriorated. The ducting was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GFCP, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A320-214 was conducting flight RV1621 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl.(KFLL), FL to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During cruise, approximately 70nm south of Pittsburg Intl (KPIT), PA, Captain became incapacitated.  First officer assumed Pilot Flying (PF) duties and Captain was able to continue duties as Pilot Monitoring (PM). No emergency was declared. Aircraft landed to destination without further incident.

C-GHKR, an Air Canada A330-343 operating as flight ACA0099 from El Dorado International Airport, Bogota (SKBO) Colombia to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. On departure, there was a burning smell and the flight crew noticed smoke pouring out of the overhead ducts in the Flight Deck. At thrust reduction altitude, the flight crew selected climb thrust and selected the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) bleed off, smoke immediately dissipated. The cabin crew was advised, no fumes or smoke identified in the cabin. The flight continued to CYUL without further incident.

N687FE, A Federal Express Airbus A300-600, was operating as flight FDX121 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to Memphis (KMEM) TN. Shortly after departure the flight crew observed a "forward cargo door not locked ECAM message". The crew flight stopped the climb at 6000 feet ASL to assess the malfunction. The flight crew ran the ECAM and QRH procedures and determined that they could not adequately confirm that pressurization was normal in order to continue the flight. The flight crew elected to return to CYEG and declared an emergency. The flight landed without further incident.Following the flight the maintenance team inspected the cargo door and lock mechanism and determined that the cargo door was fully closed and locked and the fault was an indication issue. A MEL was granted for the cargo door lock indication system and the flight departed to KMEM without incident.

C-FSEP, an Image Air Charter Ltd. Bombardier CL-600-2B16 (604) was conducting a flight from Palm Beach Intl. (KPBI), FL to The Valley/Clayton J. Lloyd Intl. (TQPF), Anguilla.  On initial climb out of KPBI, flight crew received a gear disagree and the nose door open caution light stayed illuminated after gear retraction. Flight crew actioned QRH and completed a manual gear extension.  Manual gear handle would not stay up during the process due to the center button not releasing.  The nose gear retracted and nose gear door closed while trying to perform manual gear extension.  Flight crew declared a Pan Pan and returned to KPBI where they landed without further incident.

C-GWUE, a Westjet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft, was operating as flight WEN3312 from Kelowna (CYLW) BC, to Edmonton Int'l (CYEG) AB, with 4 crew members and 66 passengers on board. In the initial climb through approximately 10 000 feet above sea level, the cabin pressure caution light illuminated. The flight crew conducted the actions indicated in the quick reference handbook but were unable to regain control of cabin pressurization. The flight crew declared PAN PAN and returned to land at CYLW without further incident.Subsequent maintenance inspections found ice in the aircraft's cargo door pressurization seal and an unserviceable cabin pressurization controller. Further inspection found the blow-out panel between the passenger cabin and cargo compartment had blown out. The operator replaced the aircraft's pressurization controller, aft cargo blow-out panel, and removed the ice from the door seal. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GHDI, a privately registered Piper PA-28-151 Warrior, was conducting a flight from Vancouver/Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC to Langley (CYNJ), BC with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. When approaching the CYNJ control zone, the tower controller advised the pilot the runway had not been plowed since a recent snow fall and the runway remained partially snow covered with ice patches. The pilot overflew the airport and requested landing on Runway 19. The aircraft touched down with approximately 850 feet of runway remaining. While attempting to exit the runway onto Taxiway A, directional control of the airplane was lost and it departed the paved surface striking an airport sign with the right wing. The aircraft's right wing sustained substantial damage. There were no injuries, and the ELT did not activate.The aircraft was moved to the ramp and will be inspected to determine the extent of the repairs required.

C-FUSM, a Boeing B737-800 operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA656 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. While in cruise approximately 40 NM northeast of Kenora (CYQK), ON, the first officer became ill. A deadheading WestJet captain, who was on board the aircraft as a passenger, assumed the duties of the incapacitated first officer. After speaking with the operator's ground based medical support, the flight diverted to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB where an uneventful landing was conducted. The first officer was transferred to a local hospital for assessment.

C-FSDW an Air Canada B737-8 operating as flight ACA555 from Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), LA, USA to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR) Vancouver, BC - On departure from LAX runway 25R SUMMR2 behind an A321 at approximately 800ft, the flight crew felt the aircraft rolling in what was likely wake turbulence. The Auto Pilot was engaged and gave "Roll Authority" amber alert on the Primary Flight Display (PFD). The pilot flying disengaged the autopilot and flew until clear of the wake turbulence. The auto pilot re-engaged just above 1000ft, the flight continued to YVR without further incident.

C-GCNK, a Canadian North Boeing 737-300, was operating as flight AKT1490 from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Norman Well (CYVQ), NT. Shortly after departure on Runway 12, ATC cleared AKT1490 to FL210 on a heading of 330 degrees. While climbing through 7000 feet a loss of separation occurred with an arriving WestJet Encore DHC-8-400 flight WEN3209, C-GEEN, arriving from Saskatoon (CYXE), SK that had been cleared for the RNAV Y approach for Runway 20 via the GOPEV intersection. Separating eroded to 2.8 NM laterally and 800 feet vertically where 3.0 NM or 1000 feet is required.

C-GYSD, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Swoop Inc, was conducting flight WSW110 from Abbotsford International Airport (CYXX), B.C. to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON. C-GNSB, an Embraer EMB-505 Phenom aircraft operated by FLYGTA Inc, was conducting flight TOR803 from Lynden Pindling International Airport (MYNN), Nassau, Bahamas to CYHM. While both aircraft were on simultaneous approach in CYHM, the minimum spacing was not maintained while C-GYSD was on final approach for Runway 30 and C-GNSB on final approach for Runway 24. Air Traffic control instructed WSW110 to go around when the aircraft was at 2.5 miles from runway 30 threshold and 2.5 miles from C-GNSB. Both aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GFAF, un Airbus 330-343 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif ACA901, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl, aux États-Unis (KFLL) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Lors de l’atterrissage sur la piste 06L, l’équipage a observé une indication de mauvais fonctionnement du train d’atterrissage principal de droit. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été demandés par l’équipage qui a immobilisé l’aéronef sur la piste. Les 2 pneus avant du train principal de droit ont crevé et des dommages importants au bogie ne permettaient pas un remorquage de l’aéronef. L’autorité aéroportuaire a fermé la piste 06L et des véhicules ont été envoyés pour transporter les passagers et les membres d’équipage vers le terminal. La piste 06L a été rouverte le lendemain à 1030Z.

C-FBDD, a privately-registered Cessna 340, was conducting a maintenance flight at Penticton (CYYF), BC with only the pilot on board.  After departure from Runway 16, in the climbing for the circuit, the right engine (Teledyne Continental TSIO-520-K) lost power. The aircraft turned back toward the airport and landed safely on Runway 34. No emergency was declared and there were no injuries.The engine is being inspected to determine the cause of the failure.

C-GWWD, an ATR 42-300 operated by Transwest Air (doing business as Rise Air), was conducting flight RS281 from Prince Albert/Glass Field (CYPA), SK to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK and was cleared for landing on Runway 09 at CYXE. Maintenance 26, an airport inspection vehicle operated by the Saskatoon Airport Authority, requested a clearance to conduct an inspection of Runway 15/33. ATC provided a clearance with a hold short of Runway 09/27 instruction. Maintenance 26 read back the clearance with the hold short instruction but was subsequently observed by ATC crossing the hold short line of Runway 09/27. ATC made a radio call to confirm that Maintenance 26 was holding short of the runway. The flight crew of RS281 heard ATC's query, observed the vehicle entering the runway environment, and initiated a go-around at approximately 100 feet AGL. Maintenance 26 crossed Runway 09 and replied to ATC that they believed they were at Taxiway A. RS281 then completed another approach to Runway 09 and landed uneventfully.The airport operator subsequently inspected the lighting, signage, and hold short lines and reported that all were working properly and were visible.

C-FGZD, a Top Aces Inc. McDonnell Douglas A-4N was conducting local flight out of Wittmund/Wittmundhafen (ETNT), Germany.  Approximately 55 nm north of ETNT in climb for 30000 feet, pilot noticed an acrid smell inside the cockpit.  Shortly thereafter, the generator failed.  Pilot deployed the Ram Air Turbine (RAT), selected 100% oxygen and an emergency was declared with ATC.  The plane landed in ETNT without further incident.

C-GORN, un Beechcraft B1900D exploité par Propair Inc. sous l’indicatif PRO4600, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) à destination de Kattiniq/Donaldson QC (CTP9) avec seulement 2 membres d’équipage à bord. À environ 70 miles marins à l’ouest de Kuujjuaq QC (CYVP), l’équipage a rapporté un problème avec le système de train d’atterrissage, a avisé l’ATC qu’il voulait effectuer une diversion à destination de CYVP et a demandé la présence des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) à l’atterrissage. La procédure d’extension manuelle a été utilisée avec succès pour déployer toutes les roues et l’aéronef s’est posé à CYVP sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-FHGG, un Beech A100 exploité par Propair Inc. sous l’indicatif PRO4200 MEDEVAC, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) avec une infirmière et 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, après avoir rentré les volets, l’équipage a perçu une odeur étrange, mais aucune présence de fumée a été perçue. Cependant il a été constaté que le disjoncteur du moteur des volets s’était déclenché. À environ 40 miles marins au nord-ouest de CYUL, l’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a demandé de revenir à CYUL. Le PRO4200 s'est posé sur la piste 24L à CYUL sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-GRAI, un De Havilland DHC8-314 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE803 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Salluit, QC (CYZG) à destination de l'aéroport de Ivujivik, QC (CYIK) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 25 passagers à bord. Lors de l'approche à CYIK, le train d'atterrissage ne s'est pas déployé et une remontée a été effectuée. L'équipage a alors opté de se diriger vers l'aéroport de Puvirnituq, NU (CYPX) et a effectué la procédure d'extension manuelle du train d'atterrissage avec succès. Une urgence a été déclarée. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre à 17:07.

C-FJEP, un Saab 340B exploité par Pascan Aviation, effectuait le vol PSC343 selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR), depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 3 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de l'approche à CYUL, alors que l'appareil se trouvait en courte finale, le moteur de gauche (GE CT7-9B) a subi une panne de moteur et l'équipage a déclaré une urgence. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre et il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-FCWP, un De Havilland DHC-8-102 exploité par Air Creebec, effectuait le vol CRQ2921 selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR), depuis l'aéroport de Val-D'Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 9 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, à environ 2 NM au sud-est de CYVO, l'équipage a détecté la présence de fumée dans le poste de pilotage. Par mesure de précaution, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence et demandé un retour à CYVO où l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-FTOH a Sunwing Airlines B737-800 operating as flight SWG553 from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON to Cancun Intl. (MMUN), MX. During the flight, a cabin crew member became incapacitated. Medlink was consulted. The crew member was moved to a passenger seat for the landing at the destination.

C-FRJY, a British Aerospace Avro 146 RJ-100 aircraft operated by Summit Air Ltd, was conducting flight SUT8225 from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON to Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON with 4 crew and 31 passengers onboard. During the climb, when passing through approximately FL300, the flight crew got a high cabin altitude alert. At this point the cabin altitude was indicating just over 8000 feet. After verifying the pressure setting, the cabin altitude continued to rise. The flight crew requested a descent from ATC and started descent to 10 000 feet. As the cabin pressure continued to climb, both flight crew members donned their oxygen masks and increased their descent rate to an emergency descent as they completed the applicable checklist. The passenger oxygen masks deployed during descent. The flight crew attempted to control the cabin altitude but the #2 discharge valve was stuck open at approximately one third of the open position. The aircraft levelled at 10 000 feet and the flight crew requested a return to CYQT. After few more minutes at this altitude, the crew regained control of the #2 discharge valve and of the cabin altitude. The aircraft landed without further incident in CYQT.

C-GLXV, a Beechcraft 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Service Ltd., was conducting flight EV200 from La Romaine Airport (CTT5), QC to Gander Intl Airport (CYQX), NL. While conducting the ILS 13 approach in CYQX, the landing gear failed to extend after being selected down. The crew conducted a go-around, declared a PAN PAN and requested a hold to troubleshoot the issue. The QRH actions were completed, the landing gear was manually extended and the aircraft landed safely without further incident. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft. Maintenance staff conducted an inspection of the aircraft. No faults were found and they were not able to duplicated the failure on the ground. As a precaution, the landing gear relay was replaced and the aircraft was released for a test flight. The test flight was successful and aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTGK, un Beech Musketeer C23 de propriété privée, effectuait un vol  selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis l'aéroport de Miramichi, NB (CYCH) à destination de l'aéroport Cornwall Regional, ON (CYCC) avec seul le pilote à bord à bord. En route vers CYCC, C-GTGK a subi une panne de carburant et a atterri dans un champs à 6 milles nautiques au sud de Salaberry-de-Valleyfield, (CSD3), QC. L'appareil a subi des dommages substantiels et le pilote a été lègèrement blessé.

C-FNML, Simpson Air Ltd Piper Aztec, PA23-250, was preparing for a flight from Fort Simpson Island Airport (CET4), NT to Nahanni Butte (CBD6), NT. The combustion heater was turned on and immediately the gear horn sounded and the heater circuit breaker popped. Smoke was detected and the pilot shutdown and secured the aircraft. Following the incident the maintenance provider determined that the combustion heater was the source of the smoke and some of the heater components were heat damaged. The aircraft has been grounded until the repairs can be made.

C-FLFR, a Buffalo Airways Ltd. Douglas DC-3-CS1C3G, was operating as flight BFL721 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Hay River (CYHY), NT with two flight crew on board. At about 25 NM N of CYHY, after being cleared for an approach, the flight crew heard a big bang from the No. 1 engine. The flight crew commenced the engine failure in-flight drill and shutdown the No.1 engine (Pratt and Whitney USA R-1830-92). An emergency was declared with ATS and the aircraft performed an uneventful single-engine approach and landing into CYHY.The aircraft remains on the ground in Hay River and company maintenance is awaiting warmer temperatures before commencing maintenance activity to determine the reason for the engine failure.

C-FSEP, an Image Air Charter Ltd Bombardier Challenger 604, was conducting a flight between Palm Beach Intl. (KPBI), FL to Houston/George Bush Intercontinental (KIAH), TX.  During initial climb out of KPBI, flight crew received a gear disagree, nose door open and HYD 3 overheat message on EICAS (Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System).  Flight crew completed the appropriate checklist, declared a Pan Pan with ATC and completed an uneventful overweight landing in KPBI.MTCE update:  Upon inspection, maintenance found microswitch improperly rigged in nose wheel well compartment, NLG wow harness damaged and emergency gear handle pulled from pilot checklist.  Overweight landing completed.  Aircraft returned to service on 24th of December 2021.

C-GPCR, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Textron (Beech) 1900D, was conducting flight PCO453 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Trail (CAD4), BC with 2 flight crew members and 19 passengers on board. When climbing through 17 000 feet above sea level, the crew observed the right engine oil temperature was high, approximately 90° C. The right engine (PT6A-67D (S/N: PCE-PS0584) oil temperature continued to rise rapidly despite the crew's efforts to cool it by reducing power and leveling off. The crew shutdown the right engine as a precaution. They declared an emergency (MAYDAY) and requested a return to CYVR. The aircraft landed without further incident.Company maintenance discovered that the right engine oil cooler had some bent fins and some small rocks embedded therein. The overheated oil was the result. The oil cooler was removed and a new one installed. A successful test flight was completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GMOB, a Piper PA-31-350, operated by Eagle Air Enterprises Ltd. was conducting a VFR flight from Pukatawagan (CZFG), MB to The Pas/Grace Lake (CJR3), MB with the pilot and 5 passengers on board. The pilot carried out a visual approach and landing on Runway 17 at CJR3. After the aircraft touched down, the pilot realized the runway was covered in approximately 1.5 feet of snow. The nose gear subsequently collapsed, the aircraft veered right, and stopped on the edge of the runway. The pilot and passengers exited the aircraft by the main cabin door. The RCMP and EMS attended the scene. There were no injuries.The was no NOTAM runway condition report issued for Runway 17/35 at CJR3; however, the Canada Flight Supplement advises that Runway 17/35 at CJR3 has no winter maintenance.

On 19 Dec 2021, a Chartright Air Group Bombardier Challenger CL-600, operating as flight HRT085, from Turks and Caicos Providenciales International Airport (MBPV) to Ottawa/Macdonald–Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON initiated a missed approach and go around after a left main gear issue while on approach to Rwy 07. The flight crew conducted a go around and requested vectors for a second approach. All required checklists were carried out but the flight crew was unable to confirm if the left main landing gear was down and locked. The flight crew declared an emergency and completed an approach and landing without further incident.

On 18 Dec 2021 a Piedmont Airlines Embraer 145 (N692AE), operating as flight PDT6112 declared an emergency with the Terminal Control Unit shortly after taking off Runway 05 from the Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. The flight crew requested a return to CYYZ. The nature of the emergency was unknown. The aircraft landed on Runway 06L without further incident and was followed to the gate by ARFF.

On 16 Dec 2021, United Parcel Service Airbus 300 (N173UP), operating as flight UPS474 on an instrument flight rules (IFR) flight from Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport (KSDF) KY, USA to Montréal-Mirabel International Airport (CYMX), QC received authorization from the Montreal ACC to deviate due to weather. UPS474 was then on a converging track with a Jazz Aviation Ltd Bombardier CL600 (C-GJFZ), operating as flight JZA2 on an IFR flight from the Ottawa/Macdonald–Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON to the Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. A loss of separation occurred when the distance between both aircraft was reduced to 4.1 NM laterally and 600 feet vertically.

N632QS, a Cessna 680A aircraft operated by NetJets Inc., was conducting a flight from L.F. Wade International Airport (TXKF), Bermuda to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. Just prior to commencing the approach, the flaps were set to position 1 by the flight crew, but failed prior to reaching the selected position. The flight crew requested a delaying vector, completed the QRH items and declared an emergency with ATC. The aircraft landed without incident with ARFF on standby.Maintenance is troubleshooting the failure.

C-GPAJ, a Chartright Air Inc. Bombardier Challenger 601 was conducting positioning flight HRT056 from Saint Maarten/ Princess Juliana Intl (TNCM), Saint Maarten to Miami/Opa Locka Executive (KOPF), FL with 2 Flight crew and a mechanic on board.  The aircraft was operating under Chartright Air's MEL for a landing gear issue and landing gear was pinned down for the flight.  During Cruise at FL200 over the Island of Mayaguana, Flight crew received a Left engine oil pressure light on EICAS (Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System) accompanied by excessively high ITT indication.  The engine failed very soon after, flight crew completed the appropriate checklist, declared an emergency and diverted to Abraham's Bay/Mayaguana (MYMM), Bahamas.  the flight landed in MYMM without further incident.  Maintenance is troubleshooting the engine issue.

C-GUAC, an Air Canada A220-300 was conducting flight AC598 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Santa Ana/ John Wayne/Orange county (KSNA), CA. During descent, flight crew experienced abnormal bumps and autopilot control input in pitch axis.  Subsequently, flight crew received an EICAS (Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System ) R Elevator fail caution message.  Flight crew performed the appropriate checklist, a Pan Pan was declared and diversion was conducted towards Los Angeles Intl. (KLAX), CA.  Flight landed without further incident in KLAX.  Maintenance is troubleshooting.

C-GGOF, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, was operating as flight JZA457 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with 4 crew and 53 passengers on board. JZA457 had been in cruise for approximately 90 minutes (160 nm S of CYZF) when the flight crew observed a "No. 2 HYD ISO VLV" caution light and an associated loss of hydraulic fluid for the number 2 hydraulic system. Moments later the flight crew observed the "No. 2 RUD HYD" "No. 2 ENG HYD PUMP" and engine hydraulic "CLOSED" lights illuminate. The checklists were consulted and a decision was made to divert to Edmonton (CYEG), AB. A PAN PAN was declared and the destination was revised to return to CYYC. At the top of descent a manual landing gear extension was performed and JZA457 landed in CYYC without further issue.Maintenance replaced P/N 82974584-003 hydraulic line and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBKB, a Morningstar Air Partners Ltd. (dba Aurora Jet Partners) Bombardier CL600-2B16 (Challenger 605), was conducting a flight (CAR604) from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Vancouver (CYVR), BC with 2 pilots and 9 passengers on board. Shortly after take-off, when flaps were selected from 20 to up, the flight crew observed a 'flaps fail' caution and that the flaps did not move. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC and completed the QRH for a 'flaps fail' condition while maneuvering west of the airport. The aircraft returned to CYEG for an uneventful landing with ARFF standing by.Company maintenance, in consultation with Bombardier, replaced the flap control unit, conducted ground and air testing (no faults found) and returned the aircraft to service. See also A21W0107.

C-GOIK, an Air Transat Airbus A321-271NX was conducting flight TS326 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Cancún Intl. (MMUN), Mexico.  During cruise over Pittsburg Intl. (KPIT), PA, a flight attendant suffered an injury and was incapacitated.  Flight attendant tasks were redistributed and flight landed in MMUN without further incident.

C-GPAL, a de Havilland DHC-8-102 operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting flight PAG407 from Thompson (CYTH) MB to Oxford House (CYOH) MB. At approximately 17 NM south west of CYTH, the flight crew received a red annunciator light indicating low number 1 engine oil pressure (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW121). The flight crew carried out the QRH actions, conducted a number one engine shutdown, declared an emergency, and requested a return to CYTH. The aircraft landed safely in CYTH with local Fire and EMS on standby. The operator's maintenance subsequently replaced the number 1 oil light pressure switch.

C-FSKO, a Beech King Air BE20 aircraft operated by Keewatin Air under flight KEW204, was conducting a medevac flight from Winnipeg, MB (CYWG) to Sanikiluaq, NU (CYSK) with 2 passengers and 2 crew members on board. While conducting a missed approach on Runway 29, the aircraft deviated from the intended path and went off the side of the runway. One of the passengers sustained minor injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FJOK, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-200 was conducting flight RV1676 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL.  During cruise approximately 260nm south of CYYZ at FL380, the flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to descend at FL375.  The flight crew descended, advised ATC and returned to FL380 when cleared of conflict.  Vertical separation was reduced at 700 feet.  The aircraft continued to destination without further incident.

C-GYYR, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines Ltd., was conducting flight PVL902 from Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL to Deer Lake Airport (CYDF), NL. During approach into CYDF, the autopilot disconnected and the crew received a yaw damp failure and a warning horn that could not be silenced. Due to the winds and turbulence, the crew conducted a missed approach and initially elected to divert to their alternate, St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL. However, with the continuous horn and crosswind considerations in CYYT, the crew decided to divert to Gander Intl, (CYQX), NL, which was closer. The crew declared a PAN PAN for priority into CYQX. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance is conducting an inspection of the aircraft to determine the cause of the autopilot disconnect and associated issues.

C-FYJO, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-8K5 was conducting flight SWG422 from La Altagracia/Punta Cana Intl. (MDPC), Dominican Republic to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During cruise at FL350 in the vicinity of Elizabeth City Coast Guard Air Station/Regional (KECG), NC, ATC gave the  flight crew clearance to proceed direct to the OPHEA intersection. After the flight crew turned direct to OPHEA, ATC then instructed them to turn to the right of track heading 210. Shortly after, ATC instructed to descend to FL340. The flight crew began the descent, then ATC instructed to expedite the descent to FL340. During the descent the flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory). Flight crew complied with the RA and informed ATC.  Once clear of the conflict, ATC cleared Flight crew direct to OPHEA followed by a climb back to FL350. Flight proceeded to destination without further incident.

C-GKFF, a Convair 580 operated by Kelowna Flightcraft Air Charter Ltd., was conducting flight KFA579 from Vancouver Int’l (CYVR), BC to Kamloops (CYKA), BC with two crew members on board. Shortly after departure from CYVR, the flight crew observed a fire warning light for the number 1 engine (Allison, 501-D13D). The power was reduced on the affected engine, the warning light extinguished. The crew conducted a successful fire warning test to confirm integrity of the system and elected to return to CYVR. The flight crew completed an uneventful landing and taxied to the apron.After the aircraft was parked and the engines shut down, the crew were advised by maintenance that there was smoke was coming from the wheel well area and were instructed to discharge fire bottle. ARFF vehicles were requested and attended the aircraft to ensure there was no fire. On inspection, it was determined that a clamp associated with the number one engine exhaust duct had failed, allowing hot exhaust gases to be directed at the fire sensors. The flight was cancelled, the clamp was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GGOY, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland DHC-8-402, was conducting flight JZA8399 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Sandspit (CYZP), BC with 4 crew and 26 passengers on board. While climbing through approximately 12 000 feet above sea level with the autopilot engaged, the flight crew heard a noise from the right side of the aircraft followed by a sudden and significant yaw and roll to the right. The right engine was indicating zero torque. The propeller did not feather and was indicating approximately 700 RPM. The flight crew subsequently selected the “Alt Feather” switch and the propeller then feathered. The flight crew declared PAN PAN and returned to CYVR. The aircraft landed without further incident. 1 cabin crew member experienced a minor injury when they fell against an emergency exit in the aircraft's aft galley during the engine failure event.Subsequent maintenance actions by the air operator noted the propeller and low-pressure impeller rotated freely, but the reduction gear box could not rotate. The engine, a PW150A (S/N FA0878), was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FGZS, a Top Aces Inc. McDonnel Douglas A-4N, was conducting local training flight from Wittmund/Wittmundhafen (ETNT) Germany.  Just after take off rotation, bird impacted left hand main landing gear.  Pilot left gear and flap in down position, wingman inspected the left hand gear and fuel was burned to reach acceptable landing weight.  ATC put ARFF on stand by and plane landed without further incident.

C-GWYB, a DBA Novajet Learjet 45 was conducting a flight between Fort Myers/Page Field (KFMY), FL and Kitchener/Region of Waterloo Intl (CYKF), ON. During initial cruise, the crew noticed a slow but steady decrease in cabin temperature.  An attempt was made to increase the cabin temperature in both manual and automatic modes until the crew adjustments had no more effects.  During descent, approximately 110 nm south of CYKF, power was reduced and abrupt HP Bleed cycling was observed.  Descending through FL330, the crew started to notice smell of hot synthetic oil.  Shortly thereafter, passengers alerted the crew that smoke was visible in the aft cabin.  Temperature selectors were moved to cold but this had no effect on temperature or smoke. The crew donned oxygen masks and completed the appropriate checklists and discussed enroute alternates but the smoke had diminished.  The Flight crew asked Cleveland ATC for further descent, explaining the presence of smoke but not declaring an emergency. ATC declared an emergency on behalf of the crew and provided a direct routing to the destination airport.  The flight landed at CYKF without further incident. The crew did smell cyclical oil scents which was a possible indicative of an ECU oil leak. Maintenance is troubleshooting.

C-GRAX, a WestJet Boeing 737 MAX 8, was conducting flight WS2660 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Montego Bay/Sangster Intl. (MKJS), Jamaica. During cruise over Wilmington Intl. (KILM) NC, a flight attendant became incapacitated.  Flight attendant tasks were redistributed for the remaining of the flight and flight landed at destination without further incident.

C-GDKN, a Sikorsky S-92A helicopter operated by Cougar Helicopters Inc., was conducting flight CHI431 from St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL, to the Hibernia platform. After departure, passengers and crew noticed a haze in the cabin accompanied by a slight pungent odour. The haze and odour occurred immediately after the crew had completed the heater check. The heater was selected off and the crew elected to return to CYYT. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance determined that the issue involved a failed heater ducting. Maintenance will be replacing the ducting prior to returning the aircraft to service.

C-GVRJ, a privately registered amateur-built BRM Land Africa aircraft operating on tundra tires with the pilot and 1 passenger on board, was enroute from Winnipeg/Lyncrest (CJL5), MB to Rock Lake, MB. While in cruise, roughly 6 nautical miles from the destination, there was a grinding noise from the engine (Rotax 912ULS). The pilot pulled the carburetor heat control "ON", but the engine stopped abruptly. The aircraft was 800 to 900 feet above ground level and the pilot elected to land straight ahead. The pilot made a Mayday call on 123.2 Mhz as the aircraft descended into a gully. After a landing roll of about 8 to 12 feet, the aircraft was stopped by the bank of the gully. The 406 ELT activated and the pilot called 911 and NAV CANADA, and selected SOS on their SPOT Locator device. The SPOT operator relayed the occurrence location to 911 and DND Rescue Coordination Centre. A local pilot over flew the site and assisted emergency services in locating the aircraft. The pilot and passenger, who wore seatbelts and shoulder harnesses, sustained minor injuries and were transported to hospital. The aircraft was substantially damaged. There was no fire.

C-GUPL, an Airbus A220 (BD-500-1A11), operated by Air Canada as flight AC466, was on the climb out from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Ottawa Macdonald–Cartier International Airport (CYOW), ON when the flight crew experienced an odour in the cockpit and cabin. The flight crew donned the oxygen masks, declared a PAN PAN and returned to YYZ. The aircraft landed uneventfully and maintenance determined that the odour was a result of de-icing fluid ingestion and not an aircraft system fault.

C-GAMQ, a WestJet Boeing 737 MAX 8, was conducting flight WS1862 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Honolulu/Daniel K Inouye Intl. (PHNL), HI.  During cruise prior to ETOPS (Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards) approximately 430nm SW of CYVR, flight crew received an indication of oil filter bypass on left hand engine.  Flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist, declared a mayday with Oakland oceanic, performed a precautionary shutdown and diverted back to CYVR where it landed without further incident.

The Aurora Jet Partners Bombardier CL-600-2B16, C-GBKB (Challenger 605), was operating a flight from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Palm Springs (KPSP), California. On departure from CYEG the flight crew were unable to raise the flaps. The flight crew conducted the appropriate checklists and entered a hold to burn fuel to avoid an overweight landing on return to CYEG. A PAN PAN call was made and a request for ARFF to attend the landing. The landing was uneventful and no other aircraft were affected.Maintenance update: Replaced the flap PDU potentiometer IAW manufacturers AMM and subsequently conducted a local test flight. No defects on the test flight. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GGMI, a DH8D operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA936 between Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), Ontario, and Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, with 4 crew and 58 passengers on board. After holding for approximately 30 minutes, the aircraft was cleared for the ILS on runway 06L. During the localizer intercept at 3000 feet ASL, the flight crew noted sudden and significant airspeed fluctuations, and the stick shaker activated unexpectedly. The flight crew conducted a go-around using maximum power, and made the decision to divert to their alternate, Montreal-Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), Quebec, where they landed uneventfully at 2105 EST. The FDR data indicated that a severe turbulence inspection was required, and that the engines had been over torqued during the windshear recovery event.

C-GGMN, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland DHC-8-402 was operating as flight JZA8274 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Kelowna (CYLW), BC with 4 crew members and 78 passengers on board. While on approach, descending from approximately 6500 to 5500 feet above sea level, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence and wind shear of +/- 35 knots.  The flight crew had difficulties controlling the aircraft and conducted a missed approach. After a hold, the crew attempted a second approach into CYLW and encountered similar conditions.
