They again conducted a missed approach and diverted back to CYVR. There were no injuries.Maintenance conducted a severe turbulence inspection and found no faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GNLN, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Nolinor Aviation sous l’indicatif NRL950, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis Val-d’Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de l’aérodrome de Meadowbank, NU (CMB2). Alors que l’aéronef était en montée, au passage du niveau de vol FL250, l’équipage a reçu une indication d’altitude cabine trop élevée. L’équipage a immédiatement amorcé une descente d’urgence, mais n'a pas déclaré d'urgence au contrôle de la circulation aérienne. L'avion est revenu atterrir sans encombre à CYVO. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.Lors de l'examen sommaire du copilote, l'interrupteur du groupe d'air conditionné de gauche n'était pas complètement en position de marche et pouvait rester entre 2 positions. L'interrupteur a été remplacé par la maintenance et testé fonctionnel.

C-GGMU, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8122 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to St. John's Intl (CYYT), NL. On approach to CYYT, the aircraft became difficult to control due to variations in speed and altitude caused by severe turbulence. The crew elected to carry out a missed approach and divert to their alternate airport – CYHZ. There were no reported injuries. The aircraft landed at CYHZ without further incident.Maintenance personnel carried out a severe turbulence inspection in accordance with aircraft manufacturer manual instructions, with no fault found.  A review of flight data revealed that no parameters exceeded limitations, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FENO, a WestJet Encore DH8D, was operating as flight WEN3406 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, to Fredericton International Airport (CYFC), New Brunswick, with 4 crew members and 30 passengers on board. While in cruise flight approximately 25 NM ENE of CYYZ, the flight crew detected an odour and smoke on the flight deck and in the cabin. The flight crew donned their masks, actioned the appropriate checklist(s), and declared MAYDAY with air traffic control. The flight returned to CYYZ, landed uneventfully, and was inspected by ARFF personnel before taxiing to a gate. Maintenance inspection did not reveal a cause for the odour or smoke; the ECS was purged to flush out potential contaminants. As the aircraft had been de-iced before the departure from CYYZ, it is suspected that some de-ice fluid had gotten into the aircraft ECS. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSIL, an Air Canada Boeing 737 Max 8 was conducting flight ACA0519 between Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Honolulu/Daniel K Inouye Intl. (PHNL), HI.  During descent, flight crew received and followed a TCAS RA (resolution advisory).  Flight landed in PHNL without further incident.

C-GXAX, a WestJet Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737 Max 8, was operating as flight WS1590 from Calgary International (CYYC) to Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta (KATL), GA. After departure, at the top of the climb, the captain became medically incapacitated. The first officer initiated a returned to CYYC and a dead-heading captain took over the operating captain's duties. The flight landed in CYYC without further incident.

C-GTXE, a Top Aces Inc. Learjet 35A was on a ferry flight, operating as flight BRUSR02, from London (CYXU), ON to Victoria (CYYJ), BC. The flight was overhead Medicine Hat (CYXH), AB at FL380 when it experienced a pressurization issue. The crew donned oxygen masks and executed an emergency descent to FL130. An emergency was declared and the flight diverted to Calgary International (CYYC), AB and landed on Runway 35R without further incident.Following the flight, the maintenance team found that the emergency pressurization valve had failed. The unit was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service

C-GKOE, an Air Canada Airbus A320, was operating as flight ACA463 from Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW), Ontario to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, with 5 crew members and 119 passengers on board. While in cruise flight approximately 63 NM east of CYYZ, the flight crew detected an electrical odour in the flight deck and in the cabin. The flight crew donned their masks, actioned the appropriate checklist(s), and declared MAYDAY with air traffic control. The flight landed uneventfully and was inspected by ARFF personnel before taxiing to a gate. During maintenance, it was found that an avionics fan circuit breaker had popped, and that the fan had been the source of the odour. The avionics fan was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FZJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (CRJ200) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8046 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Saint John (CYSJ), NB. On the approach into CYSJ, severe turbulence and wind shear was encountered which resulted in difficulty controlling the aircraft. The crew elected to carry out a missed approach and diverted to CYUL. There were no reported injuries. Maintenance personnel reviewed the flight data from the FDR and determined that the turbulence did not cause the aircraft to exceed manufacturer limitations. No further inspection was required and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJIC - PAL Aerospace Ltd Cessna 750 operating flight SPR600 was on route from Naples, FL (KAPF) to Marathon, FL (KMTH) when the crew declared an emergency due to a hydraulic issue. The crew elected to divert to Orlando, FL (KMCO) and landed without incident.

C-GJVX, un Airbus A321-211 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA1075, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Miami, Floride, É-U (KMIA) à destination de l'aéroport MOntréal/Pierre-Elliot Trudeau, Qc, (CYUL). Une urgence PAN PAN PAN a été déclarée due à un problème de train d'atterrissage. En approche finale, le problème disparut, l'urgence a été annulée, mais l'avion était trop haut pour terminer l'approche et une remise des gaz a été effectuée. L'appareil est revenu se poser sans encombre.

C-GHKX, an Air Canada Airbus A330-300 was conducting flight ACA900 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL.  On final approach to KFLL, Flight crew declared an emergency due to minimum fuel.  The airplane landed without further incident.

C-FJOK, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321-200 was conducting flight RV1660 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Fort Myers/Southwest Florida Intl. (KRSW), FL.  During the approach at KRSW at level 10000 feet, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to monitor vertical speed for a VFR traffic at level 9500 feet.  Flight crew responded to the RA, advised ATC and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FRTU an Air Canada B787-9 operating flight ACA0990 from Benito Juárez Intl - México City, MEXICO (MMMX) to Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto, ON (CYYZ). The crew reported a TCAS R/A that occurred while in cruise in Cleveland Centre's airspace. Cleveland ATC cleared a descent from FL390 down to FL350, the crew initiated the descent and received a R/A for traffic below. R/A was followed and flight continued to YYZ without further incident.

C-FKOP, a Bell Helicopter 407 operated by Wisk-Air Ltd, was conducting slinging operations approximately 7 nm SSE of Opapisiskan Lake (CKM8) ON. During the operations, 3 propane tanks fell out of the cargo net. It was reported that the cargo net had an abrasion on the tether believed to be caused from the sharp edge of the collar of the tanks. The propane tanks were located and recovered.

C-FQWA, a Beech 1900D operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting a landing gear test flight in the vicinity of Sioux Lookout (CYXL) ON. with 2 pilots on boards. During the test flight, the landing gear would not extend. The flight crew elected to declare an emergency and return back to CYXL. The landing gear was manually extended and the aircraft landed safely without further incident. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft.The aircraft has been grounded pending further investigation by the operator's maintenance. This was a flight test following a previous occurrence on 4 December 2021 (see TSB A21C0113).

C-GFDU, an Airbus A320-214 was conducting Air Canada Rouge flight RV1620 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl Airport (CYYZ), ON. to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport (KFLL), FL. USA. Prior to departure and shortly after de-icing, the flight deck began to fill with smoke. The flight crew actioned the applicable checklists and declared a PAN PAN. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) attended the aircraft and performed an inspection. The aircraft was then cleared to taxi back to the gate. Air Canada Maintenance conducted a technical inspection of the aircraft with no faults found. Residual de-icing fluid is currently being investigated as the suspected cause of smoke on the flight deck.

C-FQWA, a Beech 1900D operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG1475 from Sioux Lookout (CYXL) ON. to Angling Lake (CKB6), ON, with 2 crew members on board. While on approach for Runway 30 in CKB6, the flight crew selected landing gear down; however, did not receive the three landing gear down annunciator lights. The flight crew decided to return to CYXL and requested emergency services to be on standby as a precaution. The landing gear was manually extended and the aircraft landed without further incident. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft.The operator's maintenance replaced the landing gear control and completed gear swings. The aircraft then conducted a test flight on 5 December 2021. See TSB report A21C0114.

C-FYAI, un DeHavilland Dash 8-300 exploité par Air Inuit Ltée sous l'indicatif AIE832, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, Québec (CYZV) à destination de l'aéroport de Schefferville, Québec (CYKL) avec 31 passagers et 3 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors que l'appareil circulait vers l'aire de débarquement, les pilotes ont noté une odeur non identifiée dans le poste de pilotage. Pendant le débarquement, une brume ressemblant à de la fumée était visible dans le poste de pilotage. Une fuite du système hydraulique a été trouvée dans le puits du train avant. Le tuyau a été remplacé par la maintenance.

C-GDQE, a privately registered Mooney M20C, was on a recreational flight from Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC to Duncan (CAM3), BC with the pilot and two passengers on board. The pilot conducted an initial approach to Runway 13, executed a go around, and set up for a second approach. After the second approach, the aircraft touched down with the pilot finding the braking to be poor. Runway 13 has a 70 foot displaced threshold, a 0.5% downhill slope, and was reported to have frost present on the morning of the accident. Skid marks were observed starting about 800 feet beyond the threshold of the 1494 foot runway. As the aircraft was not slowing as expected, the pilot applied full power in an attempt to conduct a go-around. The aircraft ran off the end of the runway. It bounced off of a small berm and came to rest, on its belly, in a gravel pit. All occupants were able to extricate themselves and suffered various degrees of injuries. The airplane was substantially damaged.The RCMP and EMS services attended the scene and the pilot and passengers were taken to hospital.

C-GMSG, a Murphy Rebel aircraft operated privately, was conducting a local flight around Flora Lake near Wabush-Labrador Airport (CYWK), NL. A short time after take-off, the aircraft impacted the frozen lake surface. The owner/pilot and a passenger were fatally injured and the aircraft was destroyed. The TSB deployed a team to the occurrence site.

C-GOPW, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE781 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Puvirnituq, Qc (CYPX) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). En rapprochement vers CYUL, AIE781 a été observé sur un cap de 130°, et le service de la circulation aérienne (ATS) a instruit l’aéronef de virer sur un cap de 060°.  L'espacement avec C-GYJZ, un Dehavilland DHC8 exploité par Jazz Aviation sous l'indicatif JZA715, qui effectuait un vol depuis Québec/Jean Lesage, Qc (CYQB) à destination de CYUL a été réduit à 2.6 nm sur le plan horizontal  alors que l'espacement requis était de 3 nm.

C-GOCJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 767-300, was operating as flight CJT581 from Hamilton (CYHM), ON to Vancouver Int’l (CYVR), BC with 2 crew members on board. While in cruise, they encountered severe turbulence over position KEETA (60 nautical miles west of Great Falls, MT.) at flight level (FL) 320. The turbulence lasted approximately 20 to 30 seconds, during which time, the aircraft airspeed reduced from Mach .81 to Mach .74 with a loss of altitude of about 150 feet. After the turbulence subsided, the Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) indicated a change in the auto land status with the "NO LAND 3" message displayed. The flight crew informed company maintenance at CYVR where the flight subsequently landed without further event. A severe turbulence inspection was carried out in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual. No faults were found and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FKCJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 757-236, was operating as flight CJT909 from Hamilton (CYHM), ON to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC with flight crew of 2 on board. In cruise at flight level (FL) 380, the flight crew heard a report on the radio of another cargo flight reporting severe turbulence at FL370, 60nm west of Great Falls, MT. The occurrence crew descended to FL340 which was reported by air traffic control (ATC) to be smoother. As a precaution, the crew initiated the severe turbulence supplementary checklist; slowed to MACH .78, turned the ignition on to continuous mode, and ensured their shoulder harnesses were on. A few minutes later they encountered severe turbulence with heading deviations concurrent with altitude and speed deviations of +/- 500 feet, +/-35 knots respectively. The crew advised ATC and requested an immediate descent to FL320, which was authorized with a heading change. The turbulence lasted 5 minutes with the aircraft at an estimated weight of 200 000 pounds. There were no injuries. Upon arrival at CYVR, the aircraft was removed from service so that a severe turbulence inspection could be conducted. The maintenance crew carried out the inspection as per the aircraft maintenance manual with no faults found. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-GIAJ, un Boeing 757 exploité par Cargojet Airways Ltd. flight CJT1951, effectuait un vol international selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Cincinnati, Kentucky, É-U (KCVG) à destination de l'aéroport international de Mirabel, Qc (CYMX). Lors du décollage, l'équipage a eu une indication de bas niveau de liquide dans le système hydraulique de gauche (L HYD QTY), suivi du message de basse pression du même système (L HYD SYS PRESS). Après avoir effectué la procédure du manuel de réponse rapide (QRH) et communiqué avec la maintenance, la décision de poursuivre le vol à destination a été prise. En approche pour la piste 24 à CYMX, lors de la sélection de sortie du train d'atterrissage, l'indication de roue de nez non sécurisée est apparue. À 300 pieds AGL, l'indication verte indiquant la sortie complète du train avant est apparue et l'avion s'est posé sans encombre. Lors de l'inspection effectuée après le vol, le tuyau flexible de l'actuateur de rétraction du train avant a été trouvé endommagé et remplacé. Les pompes hydrauliques électrique et motrice du système de gauche ont aussi été remplacées.

C-GCJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8530 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to St. John's Intl (CYYT), NL. As the flight descended below 800 feet on the approach to CYYT, severe turbulence was encountered which resulted in the approach becoming unstable during which the aircraft entered a 30-degree bank and pitched down. The crew elected to carry out a missed approach and diverted to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. There were no reported injuries.Maintenance personnel reviewed the flight data from the FDR and determined that the turbulence did not cause the aircraft to exceed manufacturer limitations. No further inspection was required and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJZR, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland DHC-8-400, was operating as flight JZA8377 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Kamloops (CYKA), BC with 4 crew members and 71 passengers on board. While conducting the instrument landing system approach to Runway 09, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence. The auto-pilot disengaged and there was difficulty with airspeed and roll control. The flight crew conducted a missed approach and diverted back to CYYC. There were no injuries.The aircraft was inspected by the company’s maintenance personnel and no damage was found.

C-GAEK, a Cessna U206B, operated by the Gananoque Sport Parachuting Centre, departed Smith Falls Airport, Ontario (CYSH) on a visual flight rules flight to Gananoque Airport, Ontario (CNN8) with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. The aircraft was being flown to Gananoque Airport following maintenance, where it was going to be stored for the winter. While enroute, at approximately 23 nautical miles southwest of CYSH, the aircraft engine experienced an internal failure; however, the engine continued to run. The pilot conducted a forced landing in a nearby corn field. The aircraft sustained minor damage and there were no injuries. The emergency locator transmitter did not activate.It was later identified that a connecting rod in the engine broke and ejected through the top of the engine block.

C-GRIA, an Embraer Phenom 300E registered to I.M.P. Group Ltd., was on an IFR flight from Montréal–Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), Quebec to Kingston Norman Rogers Airport (CYGK), Ontario, with two pilots on board. After touchdown following the ILS approach to runway 19, at approximately 1829 EST, the aircraft overran the runway, coming to a stop approximately 400  feet beyond the edge of the pavement. There were no injuries, no damage to the aircraft, and no damage to airport fixtures. The TSB deployed two investigators to the site.

C-FWSX, a Westjet Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737-700 was conducting a flight between Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB and Hartsfield/Jackson Atlanta Intl. (KATL), GA. During cruise over Nashville Intl. (KBNA), TN, a flight attendant became incapacitated.  Duties were redistributed and airplane landed without further incident.

C-GJZV, an MHI RJ Aviation ULC CRJ-900 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA787 from San Diego International (KSAN), CA to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC with 4 crew members and 69 passengers. The aircraft began its takeoff near the beginning of the runway - approximately 1500 feet prior the Runway 27 displaced threshold. The takeoff occurred to the left of the runway centerline during which the aircraft’s left main landing gear wheels contacted 3 runway edge lights before the aircraft’s trajectory began to correct towards the runway centerline. During the aircraft’s climb, a fuel imbalance was detected. The fuel imbalance was not able to be corrected and the right-hand engine was shut down by the flight crew. An emergency was declared and the aircraft diverted to Los Angeles Int’l (KLAX). The aircraft was stopped on the runway. Airport rescue and fire flighting (ARFF) personnel advised that the No. 1 tire from the left main landing gear was deflated and smoke was coming from the wheel. The left main landing gear was sprayed by ARFF and the smoke dissipated. Passengers were disembarked and transported to the terminal.Subsequent maintenance actions found the Fuel Quantity Gauging Computer (FQGC) was unserviceable. The No. 1 tire sidewall was damaged leading to the tire being flat on landing, and the left-hand flap with 2 punctures. The left-hand flap was temporarily repaired, and the FQGC and the No. 1 tire replaced. The aircraft was flown to Calgary Int’l (CYYC), AB under the authority of a ferry flight permit for further repairs. NTSB has delegated the investigation in accordance with the ICAO Annex 13 Section 5.1.2/3.

TF-ISV un Boeing 757-200 exploité par Icelandair, effectuait un vol international selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Denver, CO, É.-U. (KDEN) à destination de l'aéroport international de Keflavik, Islande (BIKF). Suite à un problème de système électrique, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence et demandé un déroutement vers CYUL pour ensuite poursuivre jusqu'à l'aéroport international Logan de Boston, MA, É.-U. (KBOS).

C-FQNG, a VIH Helicopters Ltd. Sikorsky S-61N, was conducting heli-logging operations from a remote base on the east side of Harrison Lake, BC, with 2 flight crew on board. During the flight, a torque split was noted between the main engines and the crew returned to their base and landed without incident. Company maintenance personnel removed and inspected the airframe and engine fuel filters. They found a paste-like material in the filters and in the helicopters fuel cells. The examination of the fueling equipment found that inside a recently installed T-fitting in the fuel line (installed downstream of the systems filters) was an excessive amount of pipe sealant. The liquid teflon pipe sealant was being carried to the helicopter during fueling. The aircraft fuel tanks were defueled and cleaned of all contaminates. The airframe fuel filters were replaced. The engine fuel filters were cleaned and re-installed. The refueling T-fitting in the fueling equipment was cleaned out and lines were flushed. A ground run of the helicopter was conducted and it was returned to service.

C-FLBV, a Boeing 737-800 operated by Swoop Inc. was conducting flight WSW204 from Abbottsford Intl. (CYXX), BC to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB with 6 crew members and 157 passengers on board. Approximately 114 NM SW of CYEG the flight crew received a "DISPLAY SOURCE #2 FAIL" message with the corresponding EEC (electronic engine control) overhead light illuminating. The flight crew completed the checklist for the EEC alternate mode and the 'display source fail' condition. As the flight crew were completing the checklist, the overhead fuel filter bypass lights illuminated for both engines. The flight crew then completed the appropriate checklist for the fuel filter bypass, and declared a "PAN PAN" with ATC. The flight continued to the intended destination of CYEG where an uneventful landing was completed. Company maintenance personnel replaced the #2 DEU, and the #1 and #2 engine fuel filters were inspected and replaced. After a satisfactory engine ground run, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FTIZ, an Aerospatiale-Alenia ATR 42 operated by Canadian North, was conducting flight AKT240 from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with 3 crew members and 27 passengers on board. Shortly after departure from CYEG the flight crew smelled a burning electrical odor in the cockpit. The flight crew performed the appropriate checklist, declared a priority with ATC and the decision was made to return to CYEG. During the descent in to CYEG the electrical smell dissipated, and an uneventful landing was completed in CYEG. Post flight investigation completed by company maintenance found an air recirculation fan had failed. The appropriate maintenance action was completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FIML, a privately registered Cessna 310Q, departed Sault Ste. Marie Airport (CYAM) ON., for a local flight. Upon return, the landing gear was selected to the down position and the pilot received a left main landing gear unsafe indication. The pilot declared an emergency with CYAM tower. A low approach and flyby past the CYAM control tower was requested and conducted and the tower personnel confirmed that the landing gear appeared to be in the down position. The aircraft landed without incident at 2140 utc.

C-FLPH, a Cessna 172N registered to Sault Academy of Flight Inc., was conducting a training flight approximately 25nm NW of Sault Ste. Marie Airport (CYAM) ON. While conducting training, the aircraft’s engine began to run rough and lose power.  The pilot applied full throttle, conducted some troubleshooting and the aircraft was able to start a slow climb. The pilot broadcast a mayday call on 126.70MHz, activated an SOS function on the flight tracking device installed on the aircraft and began to look for a place to land. The engine then began to run smoother and produce more power. The pilot then elected to return directly to CYAM. A mayday call was then made to CYAM tower. C-FLPH landed safely on Runway 22 at 2217 utc with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) standing by. The operator is investigating the cause of the engine issue.

C-FKAJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 757-23A, operating as CJT909, was conducting a flight from Hamilton Airport (CYHM), Ontario, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew on board. During cruise flight at FL360, the crew received a trailing edge light and a leading edge slat asymmetry message on the engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS). The crew advised ATC and initiated the QRH procedure which included an attempt to extend the slats and flaps in alternate mode. The slats and flaps failed to respond and the crew declared a PAN PAN with a request for ARFF due to a high speed flapless landing. The aircraft landed safely with no reported damage to the aircraft. Maintenance found the left inboard slat loss sensing switch had an internal short and was replaced. The system was tested serviceable.

EJ-JMMM, un Global Express XRS exploité par ACASS Ireland sous l’indicatif SON001, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l’aéroport de Lyon-Bron, France (LFLY) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). En approche pour CYUL, lorsque l’équipage a actionné la commande pour abaisser le train d’atterrissage, l’icône de l’écran du système d’indication du moteur et d’alerte (EICAS), qui représente le train d’atterrissage de gauche en transit, est resté allumé après que les indications des trains d’atterrissage avant et droit aient confirmé qu’ils avaient déployé et étaient verrouillés. Les messages d’avertissement de GEAR DISAGREE, L-R MAIN GEAR DOOR et NOSE DOOR se sont ensuite affichés sur le EICAS. L’équipage a suivi la procédure du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a déclaré une urgence auprès du contrôleur aérien. L’approche s’est poursuivie et l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre. Des goupilles de sécurité de verrouillage des trains d’atterrissage ont été installées aussitôt que l’aéronef s’est immobilisé sur la piste. Une fois les goupilles installées, l’aéronef a quitté la piste.

C-GNLN, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Nolinor Aviation sous l’indicatif NRL567, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l’aérodrome de Meadowbank, NU (CMB2) à destination de Val-d’Or, QC (CYVO). Alors que l’aéronef était en palier à FL350, l’équipage a reçu l’indication d’une dépressurisation. L’équipage a immédiatement amorcé une descente d’urgence vers 10 000 pieds et a déclaré une situation de détresse (MAYDAY) au contrôle de la circulation aérienne. Une fois l’altitude de 10 000 pieds atteinte, l’aéronef a poursuivi sa route vers CYVO. L’équipage a éventuellement annulé l’urgence et l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

C-FRJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (Series 900) aircraft, operated by Jazz Aviation LP (JZA7461), departed Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) ON, destined for Chicago O’Hare International Airport, Chicago (KORD). After leveling off at FL380 the flight crew observed a flap caution message. They actioned the appropriate QRH checklist, contacted maintenance and decided to return to YYZ. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN in order to ensure they would get runway 23 for a long final approach, and requested emergency equipment on standby. The aircraft landed without further incident. After exiting the runway, fire crews inspected the brakes and tires with no damage or heat concerns noted.

C-FKAJ, a Boeing 757-23A, operated by CargoJet Airways Ltd., (flight CJT910), declared a PAN PAN while on approach to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM) ON, due to a leading edge slat asymmetry issue. The flight crew requested ARFF for their landing; the aircraft landed without further incident

C-GWFE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-402 was operating as flight WEN3311 from Edmonton Int'l (CYEG), AB to Kelowna (CYLW), BC, with 4 crew members and 72 passengers on board. While descending on approach, at approximately 6000 feet above sea level, the aircraft encountered a wind shear of between 20 and 30 knots accompanied by severe turbulence. The flight crew had difficulties controlling the aircraft and decided to conduct a missed approach. The flight diverted to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC. There were no injuries. Maintenance conducted a severe turbulence inspection and found no faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOKN, a de Havilland DHC-8-102 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways LP as flight WSG740, was enroute from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON to Big Trout Lake (CYTL), ON with a crew of 3 and 16 passengers on board. While in cruise, the flight crew received a master warning of the right engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW120A) low oil pressure. The right engine oil pressure gauge indicated a drop to minimum limitations. The crew shut down the right engine and returned to CYXL. An emergency was declared and a successful single engine landing was completed.The operator advised that the right engine oil cooler was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

The privately operated Cessna 210B, C-FANX, was operating from High River, AB (CEN4) to Olds-Didsbury, AB (CEA3) with just the pilot on board. The aircraft landed on Runway 28 at CEA3 and during rollout the nose landing gear shimmy damper failed resulting in significant vibrations. As the shimmy oscillations increased, the nose landing gear fork fractured and separated from the nose landing gear strut. The aircraft came to rest on the nose landing gear strut, which remained down and locked. The pilot was able to maintain control of the aircraft on the runway surface. The pilot was not injured. Damage was limited to the nose landing gear assembly and propeller.

C-FRTU, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 operating as flight ACA2045, was conducting a flight from Indira Gandhi International (VIDP), India, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC. The Vancouver Terminal Arrivals (VTA) controller vectored C-FRTU for an approach to runway 26. C-GWAZ, a Westjet Boeing 737-7CT operating as WJA103, was conducting a flight from Calgary International (CYYC), Alberta, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, and was on approach to runway 26. At approximately 17 NM east-northeast of CYVR, a loss of separation occurred when C-FRTU passed 2.1 miles north and approximately 100 feet above C-GWAZ where the minimum separation requirement was 3 miles or 1000 feet. Both aircraft continued the approach to CYVR and landed safely.

C-FSKN, un Beechcraft 200 exploité par Keewatin Air LP sous l’indicatif KEW203, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Igloolik, NU (CYGT) à destination d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 4 passagers à son bord. En route vers CYFB à FL190, l’équipage a observé que l’indication de torque du moteur droit fluctuait de 2200 à 1200, et ce, toutes les 30 secondes à 1 minute. Par mesure de précaution, l’équipage a mis la manette des gaz du moteur droit à la position ralentie et mis l'hélice en drapeau. Une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclaré à la station d’information de vol d’Iqaluit. L’aéronef a atterri sans encombre. Les informations saisies par la carte de données G1000 indiquent que la perte intermittente de couple a coïncidé avec une réduction du débit de carburant. Le personnel de maintenance de l'exploitant a inspecté le système et a effectué plusieurs points fixes, mais n'a trouvé aucune anomalie. L'exploitant va remplacer l'unité de contrôle du carburant.

C-GNDB, a privately registered Beech B36TC aircraft departed a private aerodrome located 18 miles NW of Swift Current (YYN), SK with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. Shortly after takeoff, the aircraft returned to the aerodrome for non-technical reasons. The aircraft landed with the gear unintentionally in the retracted position. There were no injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GPJL, un Beech B100 exploité par Max Aviation Inc, effectuait un vol local de vérification après maintenance selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec deux pilotes à son bord. Lors du vol, les membres d’équipage ont observé que l’indication de puissance du moteur droit était imprécise. Par mesure de précaution, l’équipage a fermé l’arrivée de carburant au moteur droit et a déclaré une urgence au service du contrôle aérien de la tour de CYHU. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GHRJ, a de Havilland DHC-8-311 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines, was operating as PVL901 from Deer Lake (CYDF), NL to Goose Bay (CYYR), NL. On the initial climb at CYDF, the number 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW123E) lost power and the right engine torque indication reduced to zero. The crew immediately shutdown the engine as per checklist instructions, declared an emergency and coordinated with ATS for a return to CYDF for landing. The aircraft was able to stop on the runway at CYDF without further incident. Due to a loss of hydraulic power to the nose steering system, it was decided to conduct a full shutdown of the aircraft on the runway and receive a tow to the apron to deplane the passengers.Company maintenance personnel determined that an under-torqued fuel line fitting nut at the number 2 engine fuel flow divider led to a sudden drop in fuel pressure and subsequent engine power loss. A company safety management system investigation has been undertaken. Unrelated to the engine fuel pressure issue, a faulty number 2 hydraulic pressure regulator caused an overpressure situation that damaged the nose wheel steering manifold.

C-GAZF, a Boeing 767-338 aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd, was conducting flight CJT2384 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON with 2 crew members onboard. While on approach for landing in CYHM, a Trailing Edge Flap Disagree Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) message appeared when the First officer selected the flap lever to 5. The Flaps indicator was showing between 1 and 5. The crew cancelled the approach clearance, declared an emergency (Pan Pan) and actioned the appropriate checklist. The aircraft landed with the flaps at position 20 as per the aircraft Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) without further incident.The maintenance department could not duplicate the fault in a maintenance environment. The issue has been identified as recurrent and the company is monitoring the system. Several components have been replaced following the Fault isolation Manual (FIM) instructions. The system will stay under monitoring until the confirmation of the fault resolution.

C-GFNO, an Aero Vodochody L-39C aircraft, operated by the International Test Pilot School (ITPS), was departing the London International Airport (CYXU) ON, on runway 33. The aircraft was instructed to line up and was informed of a delay for departure due to 2 aircraft landing on runway 27. C-GFNO mistook this instruction as expedite departure and was observed on the take off roll as C-GDFQ, a Diamond DA 20-C1 aircraft, operated by the Diamond Flight Centre was crossing the threshold of the Runway 27 for a touch and go landing. Both aircraft continued without incident, but safety was not assured.

Air Canada Rouge flight ROU2368, an Airbus A320 (C-GFDU), a non-revenue ferry flight, departed Grissom, IN, USA (KGUS) and was climbing through 8000 feet, when the flight crew received an ECAM HYD Y RSVR OVHT indication. The relevant ECAM actions were completed and the yellow hydraulic system was deactivated. On approach to Toronto LBPIA (CYYZ), the system was reactivated for landing and a precautionary PAN PAN was declared with CYYZ ATC. The aircraft landed and vacated the runway without further incident.Air Canada Rouge maintenance is troubleshooting the cause of the indication.

N402UP, a Boeing 757-24APF operated by United Parcel Service, was conducting flight UPS495 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG) MB. to Minneapolis-St. Paul Intl/Wold-Chamberlain (KMSP), MN. Shortly after departing CYWG, UPS495 was unable to retract the landing gear. The flight crew declared an emergency and returned to CYWG and completed a successful landing.The operator's maintenance lubricated the nose gear trunnion and drag brace fittings and performed a gear retraction test. The landing gear operated normally and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FGWT, a Top Aces Inc. McDonnell Douglas TA-4J aircraft, was conducting a local flight from Wittmund/Wittmundhafen (ETNT), Germany. During the initial climb, the generator failed.  The emergency generator (RAT) was deployed and an emergency declared. The aircraft burned fuel to achieve landing weight and landed at ETNT without further incident

N595FE, un McDonnell Douglas MD-11F exploité par Federal Express Corporation sous l’indicatif FDX130, effectuait un vol cargo selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Memphis International Airport aux États-Unis (KMEM) à destination de l’aéroport de Montréal Intl Mirabel (CYMX), QC avec 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Lorsque l’appareil était en approche finale de la piste 24, une indication de perte de fluide hydraulique est apparue et l’équipage a complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH). Lors du roulage après l’atterrissage une indication de feu dans le compartiment cargo avant est survenue. L’équipage a arrêté l’avion sur la voie de circulation B-6 et a déclaré un état d’urgence. Les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés et l’inspection de l’appareil n’a révélé aucun signe de feu, de fumée, ni de chaleur. Par la suite, l’avion a été remorqué à sa destination sur l’aéroport. Il n’a subi aucun dommage et il n’y a eu aucun blessé. L’inspection post envolé a établi qu'il est probable que l’indication de feu a été provoquée par la détection des particules de fluide hydraulique qui se sont répandu lors de la fuite en approche.

C-GNCV a Beech 100 aircraft operated by Kississing Lake Lodge Ltd. (doing business as Wings Over Kississing) as flight WN11, was enroute from Gillam (CYGX), MB to Gods River (CZGI), MB with a crew of 2 on board. While on approach into CZGI, the crew heard a bang come from the right engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-28), followed by a fluctuation of the #2 torque gauge and a rising ITT. The crew pulled the #2 power lever back to idle and the ITT then stabilized. The crew then advanced the #2 power lever but engine power did not respond. The crew then decided to shut down the #2 engine and diverted the aircraft to Thompson (CYTH), MB. An emergency was declared and the crew then conducted a successful single engine landing.

C-FSES, an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8, was conducting flight ACA0745 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), CA. On approach to runway 28R at KSFO, a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) was received at 1000 feet during parallel runway operations. The flight crew selected TCAS TA (traffic advisory) and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GMYU, an Air Canada Airbus Canada Limited Partnership A220-300, was conducting flight ACA0948 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Pointe-a-Pitre/Le Raizet (TFFR), Guadeloupe. On descent to TFFR, a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to monitor vertical speed at 9000 feet was received. The flight crew observed a traffic 500 feet above and notified ATC. The aircraft landed without further incident.

N743CK, a Boeing 747-400 operated by Kalitta Air LLC., was conducting flight CKS950 from Anchorage/Ted Stevens Intl. (PANC) AK, to Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky Intl. (KCVG), KY. After departure from PANC the flight crew received a fuel filter message for the No. 4 engine. The flight crew completed the checklist and continued on course. Approximately 2 1/2 hours into the flight, a fuel filter message for the No. 3 engine was received. In the event of more than 1 fuel filter message, the checklist required a precautionary landing at the nearest airport. The flight crew communicated with ATC to coordinate a precautionary diversion and landing at Cold Lake/Group Captain R. W. McNair Airport (CYOD), AB. Fuel was dumped and the aircraft subsequently landed uneventfully at CYOD.The operator's maintenance personnel replaced the No. 3 and No. 4 fuel filters which cleared the messages. The aircraft then proceeded to KCVG where the operator replaced the No. 1 and No. 2 fuel filters as a precaution.

C-FJCZ, a Cessna 550 aircraft operated by the Canadian Government, Department of Transport, was conducting Instrument flight Rules (IFR) flight TOG858 from Greater Moncton Roméo LeBlanc Intl. (CYQM), NB to Ottawa/Macdonald–Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON. An Airbus A310 operated by the Royal Canadian Air Force was conducting local Visual Flight Rules (VFR) flight HUSK01 from CYOW. At approximately 2600 feet , while C-FJCZ was on approach for landing runway 25, the wake turbulence separation requirements were not maintained between HUSK01 and TGO858 with 3 NM separating the aircraft when 6 NM are required. There was 600 feet separation between both trajectories at the crossover point, with TGO858 below when more than 1000 feet were required. Both aircraft landed CYOW without further incident.

C-FMJO, a Viking Air Ltd. DHC-6 Twin Otter operated by Pacific Sky Aviation, was flying under instrument flight rules as LVW100 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Victoria Int'l (CYYJ), BC with 2 flight crew and 1 passenger on board. During cruise, the door unlock crew-alerting system (CAS) message appeared intermittently. The flight crew confirmed that the passenger was secured, completed the QRH checklist and declared an emergency with air traffic control. The aircraft continued to CYYJ and the CAS message went out. The aircraft landed without further incident.Company maintenance found the door operation and function tested satisfactorily. Air stair door contacts were cleaned and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FBKJ, a private Cessna R182, was on a flight plan for a recreational, visual flight rules trip from Nanaimo (CYCD), BC to Glacier Park Intl (KGPI), USA with the pilot and one passenger on board. The aircraft was lost on radar 17 nautical miles northeast of Hope (CYHE), BC. An emergency locator transmitter signal was received and search and rescue (SAR) assets deployed to the scene. Two SAR technicians were able to get to the site but had to remain there overnight due to the poor weather. They confirmed the 2 persons on board were fatally injured. There was no post-impact fire.

C-FVGY, an Air North ATR-42-300, was operating as flight ANT198 from Old Crow (CYOC), YT to Whitehorse (CYXY), YT with two flight crew on board. During taxi for take-off from CYOC, the flight crew smelled smoke and observed that the duct temperatures for the air conditioning system were on the high side. The cabin temperature controller was reduced with no change. The smell of the smoke increased and the flight crew observed a "electrical smoke" warning message. The flight crew exited the runway and executed the SMOKE check list. Once the aircraft was shut down it was apparent that smoke was throughout the aircraft. Company maintenance determined a fault with the left bleed air valve.

C-GQBQ, un Bombardier CL600-2B16 Challenger 601-3A exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait le vol QUE20 selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l'aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapis, QC (CYMT) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Alors que l'appareil effectuait sa monté initiale, lors de la sélection des volets à la position 0°, une indication de panne des volets « Flaps Fail » est survenue et les volets sont restés à 20°.  L'équipage a complété la liste de vérification d'urgence et a décidé de revenir à CYMT. Par mesure de précaution, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) et les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été mis en alerte. L'appareil a poursuivi le vol s'est posé à CYMT sans encombre.

C-GAZF, a Boeing 767-338 aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd, was conducting flight CJT2834 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON with 2 crew members onboard. While turning base leg on approach for landing runway 30, a Trailing Edge Flap Disagree message appeared when the crew selected the lever to 5. The crew actioned the applicable checklist and declared an emergency (Pan Pan). The aircraft landed without further incident and taxied to the gate under its own power. The company identified the defect as intermittent and monitored its operation after troubleshooting attempts. Systems components have been replaced and the cable tensions were found outside minimum limits. The Flap control cables were tensioned within limit and the system tested serviceable. The aircraft returned to service with still a monitoring on the flap control system.

C-GVIJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd Boeing 767-300 was conducting flight CJT1592 from Viracopos-Campinas Intl. (SBKP), Brazil to Miami Intl. (KMIA), FL.  On initial climb, passing flight level 270, the flight crew noticed that the cabin would not pressurize more than 5 psi and was unable to maintain cabin pressure.  They noted that both pressurization controllers failed, declared a Pan Pan, descended to lower altitude, and performed an overweight landing in SBKP.Maintenance update: Replaced the center RAD ALT Transceiver.  Lower positive pressure relief valve found opened by FOD, removed FOD and locked in closed position. Lower positive pressure relief valve replaced. Replaced Cabin Alt pressure controller. F/O DCP removed and rectified. Captains FMC tested serviceable. Overweight inspection completed and aircraft returned to service.

C-FWSI, a Boeing 737-7 aircraft operated by Westjet was conducting flight WJA706 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ). While on approach for runway 24L, the flight crew received a Traffic Collision Avoiding System (TCAS) resolution advisory (RA) message from departing VFR traffic from Downsview Airport (CYZD), ON. WJA706 climbed from 3000' to 3300' before continuing approach for runway 24L and landed without further incident.

C-GIXT, a CL600-2B19 (CRJ200) aircraft operated by Voyageur Aviation Corporation, was conducting flight VAL200 from North Bay/Jack Garland Airport (CYYB), ON to Muskoka Airport (CYQA), ON with only 2 crew members onboard. Shortly after departure from CYYB following a heavy maintenance check on the aircraft, the number 2 engine failed during the level off at 8000 feet above sea level. The failure was indicated by a rapid Inter Turbine Temperature (ITT) increase and a corresponding compressor stall. The flight crew immediately actioned the applicable checklist for Severe Engine Damage in-Flight. The crew declared Pan Pan with Toronto ATC and the aircraft was vectored to return to CYYB. The crew subsequently transitioned to a visual approach and landed without further incident on runway 26 where emergency vehicles were standing by. Emergency services inspection confirmed there was no visible smoke and fire and the aircraft taxied back to Voyageur Aviation ramp under its own power. The company maintenance conducted a preliminary inspection and found that the intake variable guide vanes on engine #2 were in full open position. The company is investigating the occurrence.

C-FMEZ, a Morningstar Air Express Inc. Boeing 757-2B7, was operating as flight MAL7090 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB with 2 flight crew on board. During the initial approach, when the flight crew selected flap 1, they observed that the flap indication stopped between flap 0 and flap 1 with an associated 'TE Flaps Disagree" EICAS (Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System) message. The flight crew requested delaying vectors and an alternate flap extension was attempted with no change. A flap and slat 0 landing was planned for Runway 35R. A PAN PAN was declared and ARFF were put on standby for the landing. When MAL7090 came to a stop on the runway, ARFF assessed the tires and brakes due to their temperatures, the aircraft delayed taxi for 5 minutes.Company maintenance determined that the flap transmission was at fault.

C-FEKJ, an Embraer 170-200 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA7462 from Chicago O'Hare Intl. (KORD), IL to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON with 39 passengers and 4 crew members onboard. After receiving a clearance to cross waypoint KNOOK at FL310 from Cleveland Center , the crew was handed off to Toronto Center prior to level-off and traffic was pointed out at FL300. The autopilot and auto-throttle were engaged to capture FL310 when the crew received a Traffic Collision Avoiding System (TCAS) traffic advisory followed by a resolution advisory (RA) with C-FSNQ, a Boeing 737 Max operated by Air Canada conducting flight ACA 995 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Benito Juárez/Mexico City Intl. (MMMX), Mexico to climb which was followed by the crew. Air traffic control (ATC) advised JZA7462 that they had traffic at both FL300 and FL320. The crew advised ATC of the RA and that the flight was recovering to FL310 after the clear of conflict message was received. JZA7462 continued to CYYZ and landed without further incident.

C-GTRG, a Chartright Air Group Gulfstream G200 was conducting flight HRT-024 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Fort Lauderdale Exec (KFXE), FL.  On initial approach to KFXE, the flight crew received numerous warning messages including Flap/Slat failure.  They declared an emergency and decided to divert to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL for longer runway length.  As they approached the KFLL area, a communication equipment failure occurred and flight crew squawked 7600 on the transponder.  The aircraft landed in KFLL without further incident.

C-FABA, a De Havilland DHC-8-102 operated by Wasaya Airways LP, was conducting flight WSG815 from Wiebenville aerodrome (CXX2) ON. to Fort Severn (CYER) ON. When the aircraft was north of CXX2, and climbing to FL210, the flight crew received a flashing master caution light and noticed the number 1 engine oil pressure was fluctuating. The flight crew stopped the climb at FL190. The oil pressure continued to decrease into the caution range. The flight crew referenced the QRH, notified ATC, and requested a division to Pickle Lake (CYPL) ON. A precautionary engine shutdown was completed on the number 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW120A). No emergency was declared. WSG815 landed safely in CYPL, taxied to the ramp and shutdown. The operator's maintenance subsequently discovered an oil leak in the left hand engine oil cooler.

C-FENJ, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Westjet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3523 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl.  (CYYZ), ON. While initiating approach to CYYZ , Air traffic Control (ATC) Terminal Arrival issued WEN3523 a heading of 240 degrees with a correct readback from the flight crew. Shortly afterward, the aircraft was observed to turn to a heading of approximately 140 degrees. The ATC controller noticed the error and re-cleared WEN3523 to avoid conflict. WEN3523 received a Traffic and Collision Avoiding System (TCAS) resolution advisory alert with N703SK, a CRJ700 aircraft operated by SkyWest Airlines conducting flight SKW3226 from Chicago O'Hare Intl. (KORD), IL to CYYZ.  Both aircraft landed runway 05 without further incident.

C-GVJT, a Cessna Citation 560 Ultra aircraft operated by Chartright Air Inc. was conducting flight HRT373 from Sarasota–Bradenton Intl. (KSRQ), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON with only 2 crew members onboard. While on final approach runway 05, the crew selected landing gear down and the nose landing gear down and locked indication light did not illuminate. The crew subsequently elected to initiate a go-around and completed the applicable checklist. The airplane came back and flew by the control tower to confirm the nose landing gear position. The air traffic controller could not confirm the position due to darkness.  The crew subsequently declared emergency and requested airport rescue and firefighting (ARFF) to standby. The aircraft landed runway 06R where the main brakes failed and the crew had to engaged the emergency brake to come to a stop on the runway with no further issue.The aircraft was inspected by ARFF and company maintenance personnel before being towed to the hangar for further inspection. The company maintenance department is investigating the cause of the occurrence.

C-GOIW, an Air Transat Airbus A321-271NX was conducting flight TSC186 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Punta Cana Intl. (MDPC), Dominican Republic. In short final at MDPC, the flight crew reported to the ATC that they flew underneath a RPAS. The aircraft landed at MDPC without further incident.

C-FSBV, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA0091 from Sao Paulo Guarulhos Intl. (GRU/SBGR), Brazil to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON with 11 crew members and 245 passengers onboard. Following departure from GRU/SBGR, the crew received an Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) message related to tire pressure. The crew completed the applicable checklist and subsequently observed the number 6 tire pressure slowly decreasing from 90 PSI to 0 PSI. The crew declared Pan Pan to CYYZ Air Traffic Control and landed without incident on runway 15L with ARFF standing by for a preliminary inspection. The number 6 tire was found deflated. The aircraft subsequently taxied to gate under its own power.

C-GNBE, an Airbus Canada limited Partnership A220-300 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA720 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY. During the approach runway 31 at KLGA, at approximately 2000 feet, the flight crew received an OE Factor (One Engine) on the Flight Management System (FMS) and the aircraft yawed at the same time. The flight crew performed a missed approach and completed the checklist. The right hand (RH) N1 rolled back to 30% and was unresponsive to the throttle movement. A precautionary shutdown on the RH engine was conducted, a Mayday was declared and the aircraft diverted to Newark Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ where the it landed without further incident.

C-FETG, an Airbus AS 350 BA Helicopter operated by Expedition Helicopters Inc, was conducting a flight from Ogoki Post (CYKP) ,ON to Geraldton (CYGQ), ON with 1 pilot and 5 passengers onboard. While hovering at slow speed and low altitude prior landing, the pilot felt an uncontrolled forward input on the cyclic followed by a strong restriction when trying to correct the attitude with a rearward input. The pilot immediately positioned the helicopter in a safe landing area and proceeded with landing. There was no injuries and the helicopter sustained only minor damage to the belly cowling. The pilot and passengers were retrieved by another helicopter and continued to Geraldton.A comprehensive inspection and tests of the hydraulic system and flight controls were conducted with no fault found. As precautionary measure, the relevant hydraulic servo was replaced and sent for further inspection. The helicopter was flown to Geraldton without further incident.

C-GVIJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd Boeing 767-300 was conducting flight CJT1592 from Viracopos-Campinas Intl. (SBKP), Brazil to Miami Intl. (KMIA), FL.  On initial climb passing flight level 260, Flight crew received a cabin altitude caution and was unable to maintain cabin pressure in any mode selected.  Flight crew declared a Pan Pan and descended to 10000 feet and received a red Cabin Altitude master warning.  Flight crew burned fuel to reach under maximum landing weight and flight diverted at SBKP where it landed without further incident.

C-FPAE, un De Havilland DH8C exploité par PAL Airlines Ltd, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis Sudbury, ON (CYSB) à destination de Moncton/Greater Moncton Roméo Leblanc, NB (CYQM). Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en croisière, l'équipage a remarqué une fluctuation de l'indicateur de pression d'huile du moteur numéro 2. Le voyant d'avertissement principal (Master Caution) s'allumait également pour une fraction de seconde avant de s'éteindre. Par mesure de précaution, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) et a demandé à être dérouté vers Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL). L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GFSA, un Aerospatiale ATR72-200 exploité par Summit Air, effectuait le vol SUT7572 selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l’aéroport de Kuujjuarapik, QC (CYGW) à destination de La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) avec 3 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors que l’aéronef se trouvait en vol de croisière, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence par mesure de précaution, en raison d'une défaillance présumée de l'ordinateur de données de vol (Air Data Computer) numéro 1 (ADC #1) qui a entrainé une perte des systémes du côté du commandant de bord. L’aéronef s’est posé à CYGL sans encombre. Lors de l'inspection après vol, le service de maintenance a confirmé que l'ADC #1 était en cause.

C-GEBN, a Heliqwest Aviation Inc. Bell 206B helicopter, was conducting forestry support operations approximately 9 NM southeast of Qualicum Beach Airport (CAT4), BC with 1 pilot on board. After placing a tree topper onto a nearby trailer, the helicopter, with the 3 suspension cables still attached, backed away to land behind the trailer. As the pilot descended to approximately 7 feet above ground level (AGL), the helicopter became unstable and began to tip over. The pilot ascended slightly to adjust and stabilize the helicopter. As the pilot again attempted to land, descending through approximately 2 feet AGL, the pilot felt a slight tug on the cables and the helicopter immediately began to tip. The pilot was unaware that the tree topper suspension cables were snagged on the fuel tank which was also located on the trailer. The helicopter dynamically rolled and the main rotor struck the ground. The helicopter rolled onto its right side and the pilot lost consciousness. The helicopter was destroyed.A few minutes after the accident, a company maintenance employee returned to the staging area and saw the helicopter on its side with the engine still running. He called for emergency services. Concerned about the potential for a fire, the maintenance employee unbuckled the pilot and pulled him from the wreckage. First aid attendants responded and assisted the pilot who was transferred to the local hospital with serious injuries. There was no fire.

C-GJPW, a Great Pacific Capital Corp. Dassault Falcon 2000 EX, was conducting an IFR flight from Pensacola International (KPNS), FL to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC with 2 crew members and 6 passengers on board. While on the ILS approach to CYVR with the auto-pilot on, the aircraft turned sharply to the right as it intercepted the localizer. The crew disconnected the auto-pilot and corrected the heading deviation before re-engaging the auto-pilot, the aircraft once again made a sharp right turn. The crew immediately disconnected the auto-pilot. The CYVR tower controller cancelled the landing clearance and commanded a go-around. The crew followed the instructions given and began a turn to a heading of 150 degrees and a climb to 3000 feet above sea level. During the rapid climb to the cleared altitude, the first officer became spatially disoriented and declared a MAYDAY believing that the aircraft was diving towards the water. The crew received vectors to again intercept the localizer and hand flew the aircraft to land without further incident. There were no injuries.On inspection, company maintenance found that the area navigation (RNAV) approach to KPNS, the previous destination, was loaded and armed in the Flight Management System (FMS). The crew was attempting to fly the instrument landing system approach (ILS) at CYVR. The FMS reverted to the RNAV approach for Runway 15 at KPNS. All crews reviewed the procedure and the airplane was returned to service.

C-FJFH, a privately registered Zenair Zodiac CH 601 HDS with the pilot and 1 passenger on board, was conducting circuits at Regina Intl. (CYQR), SK. During a planned touch-and-go on Runway 26, the nose landing gear collapsed following a hard landing. The aircraft became disabled on the runway and was removed approximately 30 minutes later. The occupants were uninjured. The aircraft sustained damage to the nose landing gear, propeller, and engine.

C-FZCC, an Airbus Helicopters AS 350-B3 operated by Custom Helicopters, was conducting external load operations 50 NM NE of Red Sucker Lake (CYRS) MB, with one pilot on board. While longlining an external load containing a steel sled, there was an uncommanded release of the load. The external load fell into a heavily timbered and uninhabited area. There was no damage to the aircraft and there were no persons in the vicinity of the load release.The operator determined that the load was hooked up incorrectly that may have led to the load release. The hook related to this event was removed from service and replaced.

C-GIAB, un De Havilland Dash-8-300 (DH8C) exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE852 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Inukjuak, QC (CYPH) à destination de Kuujjuarapik (CYGW), QC. Lorsque l’appareil était en approche et que le train a été sorti, l'indicateur de position du train indiquait qu’il n’était pas barré. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour sortir le train. Par la suite, toutes les roues étant descendues avec des indications normales, l’équipage a effectué un déroutement vers La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni de dommage à l’appareil.

C-GQBQ, un Bombardier CL600-2B16 Challenger 601-3A exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait le vol QUE20 selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Puvirnituq, QC (CYPX). Alors que l’appareil effectuait l'approche pour la RNAV 01 à CYPX, lors de la sélection des volets à la position 20°, une indication de panne des volets « Flaps Fail » est survenue. L’équipage a effectué une remontée et amorcé un circuit d'attente au repère KIPEG. L'équipage a complété la liste de vérification d’urgence et, après avoir confirmé que la quantié de carburant était suffisante, a décidé de dérouter vers CYQB. Par mesure de précaution, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) et les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été mis en alerte. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre.

C-FJDQ, un Beech King Air B100 exploité par Max Aviation, effectuait le vol MAX100 selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) au départ de l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) à destination de Plattsburg International, NY (KPBG) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 10 passagers à bord. Immédiatement après le décollage, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison de la présence de fumée bleue dans le poste de pilotage. L'aéronef est revenu à CYHU où il s’est posé sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.Lors de l'inspection post-envolée, l'équipe de l’entretien a découvert des conduits de chauffage en plastique fondus sous le plancher de la cabine

At 1748 Mountain Daylight Time on 01 November 2021, the Air Tindi Ltd. de Havilland DHC-6-300 Twin Otter aircraft (registration C-GNPS, serial number 558) departed Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), Northwest Territories, as flight TIN223, a visual flight rules flight to Fort Simpson Airport (CYFS), Northwest Territories, with 2 flight crew and 3 passengers on board. Approximately 40 minutes into the flight, the flight crew realized that there was insufficient fuel to continue to CYFS or to return to CYZF. The flight crew diverted the aircraft to Fort Providence Aerodrome (CYJP), Northwest Territories, and informed the company of their decision. The left engine was intentionally shut down to conserve fuel. The right engine then flamed out. A forced landing onto muskeg was performed at 1851 Mountain Daylight Time, 6.7 nautical miles (14 km) northwest of CYJP. A signal from the emergency locator transmitter was received by the Canadian Mission Control Centre shortly after. Approximately 4 hours after the forced landing, all occupants were recovered by rescue personnel. All occupants received minor injuries related to hypothermia. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GHNN, un Cessna 182B en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis l'aéroport d'Alma, QC (CYTF) à destination de Joliette, QC (CSG3). Alors que l'aéronef se trouvait en croisière entre les municipalités de St-Paulin et St-Alexis des Monts, une panne moteur est survenue en raison d'un manque de carburant. Le pilote, seul à bord, a effectué un atterrissage forcé sur la route 349. À une altitude d'environ 30 pieds AGL, l'aéronef a percuté des fils électriques avant de percuter le sol et a subi des dommages majeurs. Le pilote a été blessé légèrement.

C-GUAJ, a Cargojet Airways Inc. Boeing 767-300 was conducting flight CJT973 from Cincinnati-Covington/Northern Kentucky Intl (KCVG), KY to Derby/East Midlands (EGNX), UK. Shortly after departure from KCVG, a main deck fire warning was annunciated. All indications disappeared when the master warning was cancelled by the flight crew. The flight crew requested vectors to return to KCVG. An overweight landing was performed with ARFF on standby. After being cleared by ARFF, the aircraft taxied to the stand without further incident .Maintenance update: Maintenance was carried out on multiple defects. Replacement of the Main Cargo Fire/Overheat Logic Card M02026 was completed. The card was replaced and system function checked serviceable. Airplane will be placed on Non ETOPS list as a precaution.

CF-PHA, a privately registered Volmer Jensen Amphibian VJ 22, was conducting circuits at Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC with only the pilot on board. On landing, the aircraft bounced and on the second contact, directional control was lost and the airplane exited the side of the runway. The right wing struck a distance remaining sign which was knocked off of its base. The pilot was not injured but the aircraft sustained substantial damage. Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting attended the scene and assisted in moving the aircraft.The airplane will be assessed to determine the extent of the damage.

C-GEAR, a privately registered Mooney M20J, was conducting a local flight from Oliver (CAU3), BC with only the pilot on board. The pilot initiated the takeoff roll and, at approximately rotation speed, the aircraft shuddered. The pilot rejected the takeoff but was unable to come to a stop on the runway. The excursion off the end of the runway ended when the airplane collided with the airport perimeter fence. The overnight temperature was -3°C and conducive to ice or frost formation. There is an active radio-controlled model flying club at CAU3 and the airport has a NOTAM in place to that effect. The pilot was not injured but the airplane was substantially damaged.Maintenance has inspected the aircraft. Parts are being ordered from the manufacturer and repairs to the wings and spinner will be completed. The engine will be torn down, inspected, and repairs will be made as required.

XA-VXI, an MD82 operated by Aeronaves TSM as VTM558, was eastbound in the vicinity of waypoint APDAX, approximately 16nm north of London Int'l Airport (CYXU), ON, and had been cleared to climb and maintain FL330. The instruction was read back correctly and the flight initially leveled at FL330. Shortly afterwards, the aircraft was observed to be climbing, at which time the controller (Toronto Centre controller) repeated the instruction to maintain FL330. The aircraft returned to FL330, but had reached as high as FL335 and was within 3.6nm laterally and 500' vertically of N305PQ, a CRJ9 operated by Endeavor Air as EDV5344, which had been westbound at FL340. There was no reported TCAS RA, and both flights continued to their destinations.

The Cargojet Airways Limited Boeing 767-300, C-GAZF, operating as CJT2387 on a flight from Hamilton (CYHM), ON to Edmonton (CYEG), AB, experienced a flap malfunction on approach to CYEG. The flight crew were able to select 'flaps 1' but when 'flaps 5' was selected they got a 'trailing edge flap disagree' message. The flight crew requested vectors from ATC to run the various checklists. Using the QRH they were able select 'flaps 20' via the alternate flap extension procedure.  A 'Pan Pan' was called and an uneventful landing carried out with ARFF standing by to check brake temperatures. The flight taxied in with no further assistance required.Update: Company maintenance inspected the flaps and found no faults. The aircraft was released back into service and no further issues have occurred.

C-GLQL, a Porter Airlines DHC-8-400, was to operate flight POE133 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Newark Liberty Int'l Airport (KEWR), NJ. After starting the RH engine, the flight crew observed smoke coming from the engine and shut it down immediately. The captain called for a rapid deplanement, which was conducted without incident. Although there was no distress message declared by the crew, the ARFF attended the gate as a precaution. Maintenance action revealed that a faulty K2 contactor had caused the starter/generator to overheat and fail during the engine start.

C-GDPA, a Canadian North Boeing 737-200, was operating as flight AKT226 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Cambridge Bay (CYCB), NT. When AKT226 was 180 NM north of CYZF, the number 1 engine oil quantity dropped to 1.0g on the indicator. The flight crew asked the cabin crew to confirm a leak. The cabin crew confirmed there was oil leaking out of the number 1 engine. The crew decided to return to CYZF. In the descent through approximately 10 000 feet ASL, the oil pressure gauge started dropping towards the yellow radial, then shortly after started bouncing above and below the red radial line. The low oil pressure non-normal checklist was completed and the number 1 engine (Pratt and Whitney USA - JT8D-17A) was shutdown. The aircraft landed onto runway 34 in CYZF @ 1828z without further incident. Update: Company maintenance found an oil leak on the oil filter bypass switch transmitter inlet connection. An "O" ring was replaced. The threads on the fittings were also cleaned. Engine oil filters and magnetic plugs were also inspected as per the windmilling inspection.

C-FYWQ, a B60 (Beech Duke) operated by ITPS (Canada) Ltd. as flight SA22, departed runway 09 at London Airport (CYXU), Ontario, with three crew members on board. During the initial climb, the LH engine failed and was shut down per the checklist by the flight crew, who subsequently declared an emergency. The crew returned to land uneventfully on runway 09 and shut the aircraft down on the runway. Upon exit, they observed a large quantity of oil extending back from the LH engine cowl. Maintenance action revealed that the LH oil cooler had failed.

C-GGAH, a De Havilland Dash 8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP as JZA7974, was departing on a flight from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON, to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC. During the takeoff roll, the airplane began to yaw to the left, at which point the crew rejected the takeoff and brought the aircraft to a stop on the runway. The flight crew had observed a LH ENG 'FADEC' caution light and 'powerplant' message on their Engine Display, during what they realized had been an un-commanded shutdown of the LH engine (PW150A). Following checklist actions and visual observation of the engine confirming that there was no smoke present, the flight crew elected to taxi back to the gate where they shut down the aircraft. Initial maintenance action revealed the presence of metal shavings in the oil/chip detector of the failed engine. The engine has been replaced, the failed unit will receive a detailed inspection to determine the cause of the failure.

C-GEHS, a Beech 200 medevac aircraft operated by PAL Aerospace Ltd, was conducting flight SPR810 from Halifax/Robert L. Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Sydney/J.A. Douglas McCurdy Airport (CYQY), NS with 2 pilots, 2 patients and 2 paramedics on board. On approach into CYQY, when the landing gear was selected down, the crew heard a loud noise and the green down and locked light for the right hand main gear did not illuminate. After some troubleshooting, the crew elected to return to CYHZ and completed the QRH. The crew declared an emergency and completed a fly-by for an inspection by the tower before landing on Runway 14. Upon landing, the right main landing gear collapsed as the nose wheel touched down. The aircraft stopped on the runway. There were no injuries. The right flap, wing and gear incurred damage.Maintenance discovered that a taper pin had become dislodged from the gear torque tube, restricting the gear from achieving the down and locked position. The company will be filing a Service Difficulty Report (SDR).

C-GBDY, an Anderson Air Ltd. Dassault Falcon 900 EX, was conducting an IFR flight from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Las Vegas McCarran Intl (KLAS), USA with 3 crew members and 4 passengers on board. While in the climb, through approximately 8200 feet above sea level. The crew observed erroneous air speed indications on the number 1 side with an associated ‘MIS-COMPARE’ and ‘PITOT HEAT L FAIL’ crew alerting system (CAS) messages. With the left side pitot heat failure message, the crew reverted to the right system as per the checklist. The right seat pilot assumed flying duties, the failure was reported to air traffic control ATC with a PAN PAN urgency call. The aircraft returned to CYVR without incident.On inspection, company maintenance confirmed the number 1 pitot tube was not heating up. The system was reset and the pitot heat system was ground tested. No fault was found and the airplane was returned to service.

C-FEKD, a Jazz Aviation LP Embraer ERJ 170-200SU was conducting flight JZA8944 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Moncton/ Greater Moncton Romeo Leblanc Intl (CYQM), NB.  During cruise, 80 nautical miles SW of Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC, the Captain's side inner ply windshield cracked.  Flight crew declared a Pan Pan and diverted to CYUL where it landed without further incident.

C-GQBT, un Bombardier DHC-8-200 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Gouvernement du Québec sous l’indicatif QUE30, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) avec 5 passagers, 2 personnels de cabine et 3 membres d’équipage à son bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en croisière au niveau de vol 210 à environ 15 NM au nord-est de l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB), l’alimentation du circuit de distribution 26 volts AC de gauche a cessé et l’équipage a perdu les instruments du côté gauche accompagné de fumée le poste de pilotage et la cabine. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et a effectué la liste de vérification accompagnée d’une descente d’urgence. L’équipage a demandé un déroutement vers CYQB et l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FFNE, a Boeing 737-400 operated by Bradley Air Services Ltd. (dba Canadian North), was enroute from Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. While passing overhead Churchill, MB at 36 000 feet, the crew observed a "Cabin Altitude" warning which was believed to be the result of inadequate duct pressure from the number one engine. The crew declared an emergency and carried out the Cabin Altitude checklist, and an emergency descent was initiated. The aircraft was levelled off at 14 000 feet with the cabin altitude indicating below 10 000 feet. The aircraft continued to CYWG and landed without further incident.

C-GGNZ, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland DHC-8-400 airplane, was conducting flight JZA8243 from Terrace (CYXT), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 4 crew members and 51 passengers on board. In cruise flight, at 25 000 feet above sea level, the first officer’s windshield shattered. Windshield heat was on and remained operational throughout with no spark or electrical arcing at the terminal noted by the crew. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and requested priority handling into CYVR. The cabin pressure remained steady and the flight descended normally to land without further incident.Company maintenance replaced the first officer’s windshield, conducted tests of the anti-icing and pressurization systems, and returned the aircraft to service. A Service Difficulty Report was submitted to Transport Canada (SDR 20211028012).

C-FIPC, un appareil de type Pilatus PC12-47E exploité en opération privée par Soucy aviation inc., effectuait un vol d’entrainement selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis et à destination de Montréal/St-Hubert, Qc (CYHU). Alors que l'appareil se trouvait sur un cap de 310 degrés magnétiques à proximité du repère OKOPO à 5000 pieds dans l’espace aérien de classe E, l’équipage a reçu un avis de résolution du système de surveillance du trafic et d'évitement des collisions (TCAS), indiquant un appareil convergeant sur un cap de 020 degrés magnétiques à une altitude de 5000 pieds. L'équipage a suivi les directives du TCAS et a immédiatement amorcé une descente pour une altitude de 4700 pieds et un léger virage. Un avis de trafic avait été transmis par l'ATC, pour un trafic qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue à une altitude de 5000 pieds qui n’était pas en communication avec l’ATC et qui n’avait pas à l’être. L’espacement entre les 2 aéronefs a été de 0,4 NM avant la descente de C-FIPC.
