C-FIVM, un appareil de type Boeing 777-333ER exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA845 en provenance de Frankfurt/Rhein-Main, Allemagne (EDDF) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en vol de croisière dans la région de Rivière-Du-Loup, QC (CYRI), l'équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) en raison de l’état de santé d’un passager qui s’est aggravé et a demandé d'être acheminé en priorité. L'appareil s'est posé à Montréal sans encombre et les répondants médicaux d'urgence étaient présents à l'arrivée à la barrière.

C-GUAJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 767-300, was operating as CJT555 from Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC with pilots on board.  While on descent into CYVR, the flight crew saw a MAIN CARGO FIRE annunciation on the engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS), as well as fire warnings and the fire bell. When the Master Warning was cancelled, all other indications of a fire ceased. The flight crew advised air traffic control of the main cargo fire warning and that it had extinguished but requested priority handling and aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) on standby as a precaution. The airplane was stopped on the runway to have ARFF personnel inspect for any signs of smoke or fire. Once given the all-clear, fire vehicles escorted the flight to the ramp.  Company maintenance determined that this defect appeared to have some history and there was ongoing troubleshooting. They discovered an electrical short circuit in the wiring between the loop 1 main alarm and the loop 2 main alarm.

The Air Canada Rouge Airbus A321 aircraft (ROU1713, C-GHPD) was on approach to Runway 24L at Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ). While flying over Downsview (CYZD) at an altitude of 3000 feet ASL, the flight crew received a TCAS RA, due to a small aircraft conducting circuits at CYZD. The flight crew climbed the aircraft to 5000 feet ASL in response to the TCAS RA, was vectored off the approach and re-sequenced into the approach pattern. The aircraft conducting circuits was squawking 1200 on radar and the last known altitude and position 1200 feet ASL, approximately 1nm final for Runway15 at CYZD.

C-GMCP, a Starlink Aviation Inc. Learjet 45 was conducting flight TLK833 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Denver Centennial (KAPA) CO. During cruise approximately 90nm SSW of Wold-Chamberlain/Minneapolis-St. Paul Intl. (KMSP), MN, flight crew declared an emergency due to oxygen system issues.  Flight crew decided to divert to KMSP where the flight landed without further incident.

The Air Canada Boeing 777-300 aircraft (AC184, registration C-FITW) was on the approach to runway 24R at Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ) at 3800 feet ASL. While flying over the Downsview Airport (CYZD) the flight crew received a TCAS RA and initiated a go-around. The aircraft returned and landed uneventfully. The target was unidentified and flying at 1300 feet ASL, over CYZD.

C-GSFP, a privately registered amateur-built Mk 26 Spitfire was conducting a local flight at Springbank (CYBW), AB with one crew member on board. After an uneventful take-off, the pilot was climbing on the downwind leg when the engine coolant temperature was observed to be continuously rising. The decision was made to stay in the circuit and execute a landing. The pilot contacted ATC and proceeded to select the landing gear down. The left main landing gear indicated down and locked; however, the right main landing gear did not indicate down and locked. In this aircraft, the gear down lock is manually engaged. The pilot attempted to recycle and lock the right main landing without success. With the position of the right main landing gear unconfirmed, the pilot elected to land in the grass to the west of Runway 17. As the aircraft touched down, the right main landing gear collapsed. The pilot attempted to keep the wings level with aileron input but as the aircraft slowed the wing dropped and made contact with the ground. During the landing roll, the aircraft crossed a ditch and the left main landing gear folded/collapsed aft after making contact with the ditch. The pilot was uninjured.

C-FIVX, an Air Canada Boeing 777-300 aircraft was on approach to Runway 24R at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl.(CYYZ), ON. While flying over the Downsview Airport (CYZD), ON at 3100 feet ASL, the flight crew received a TCAS RA. The flight crew responded to the TCAS RA, conducted a missed approach and returned to land without further incident. The target was unidentified on radar and flying at 1300 feet ASL in the vicinity of CYZD.

G-GSJK, a Chartright Air Group Bombardier Challenger 300, was performing flight HRT433 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Teterboro (KTEB) NJ. During cruise over state of Montana, USA, one of the flight crewmember became ill. A Pan Pan was declared and the aircraft diverted to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB where it landed without further incident.

C-FEBE, a Viking DHC-2 Beaver floatplane, operated by Harbour Air Ltd., was on a VFR flight from Nanaimo Harbour (CAC8), BC to Sechelt/ Porpoise Bay (CAX3), BC with the pilot and 3 passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff, at about 300 feet above sea level, the fuel pressure warning light illuminated. The pilot completed the cause checks, and switched fuel tanks as a precaution but the fuel pressure indication remained at 0 psi. The airplane’s engine (PRATT & WHITNEY-USA, R-985) failed shortly thereafter. The pilot performed a forced landing straight ahead on the water and radioed for the company to prepare the Assist Boat. The pilot was able to restart the engine using the manual fuel pump and then taxied back to the dock unassisted. A company maintenance inspection determined that the engine driven fuel pump drive shaft had sheared. They filed a Service Difficulty Report (SDR) with Transport Canada. The fuel pump was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FIOL, a Grumman GA21 Goose, operated by Wilderness Seaplanes Ltd., was on a VFR flight from Ocean Falls (CAH2), BC to Bella Bella (CBBC) Campbell Island, BC with the pilot and 4 passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff, about 6 nautical miles from CBBC, the pilot noticed oil coming from the left engine (Pratt & Whitney R985N-14B). The oil pressure and temperature indications were normal and the engine ran normally. The pilot reduced power and flew a direct approach to the runway at CBBC. After landing the engine quit as the airplane exited the runway. There was a significant quantity of engine oil on the aircraft. A maintenance inspection revealed that a cylinder had separated. Broken studs were found where it was attached to the engine case. The company filed a Service Difficulty Report (SDR) with Transport Canada.

C-FUAZ, a Grumman GA21 Goose, operated by Wilderness Seaplanes Ltd., was on a VFR flight from Ocean Falls (CAH2), BC to Port Hardy (CYZT), BC with the pilot and 4 passengers on board. While in cruise flight at 2500' above sea level and approximately 29 nautical miles northwest of its destination, the left engine (Pratt & Whitney USA Model R-985-AN-14B) abruptly stopped. The pilot shut down and feathered the propeller of the left engine, completed the required emergency actions, and then contacted their company. The aircraft continued to Port Hardy where it landed safely. Company maintenance inspected the engine and determined that it had experienced a catastrophic mechanical internal breakdown. The engine had accumulated a total of 340 hours since it had been overhauled. This engine had accumulated approximately 250 hours since having been repaired following removal for generating metal when it was installed on a different airplane. The engine will be sent for a complete teardown examination at an engine shop. A Service Difficulty Report was submitted to Transport Canada.

C-FCGK, a Bell 206B helicopter operated by Heli-Recon Aerial Support Services Inc., was engaged in forest fire support approximately 18 nautical miles west of Hudson Bay (CYHB), SK. While reconnoitering a fire guard at low level, there was a loud pop and the engine (Rolls-Royce 250-C20) lost power. The turbine outlet temperature (TOT) spiked to full scale on the TOT gauge. The pilot initiated autorotation and maneuvered the helicopter to a creek south of the fire area. The pilot extended the glide and conducted a successful run-on landing onto a gravel bar. During the landing the helicopter rocked from the heels of the skids to the toes and a main rotor blade made light contact with the tail rotor driveshaft cover. The pilot and 2 passengers were uninjured. The helicopter was transported from the site and is undergoing repairs. Initial inspection by the operator's maintenance personnel identified damage to the compressor beginning near the 3rd or 4th stage .

C-FHGG, un Beechcraft BE10 exploité par Propair Inc., effectuait le vol PRO4210M selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Waskaganish, QC (CYKQ) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 3 passagers à bord. Lors du décollage, le moteur droit (P&WC PT6A-28) a subi une perte de puissance. L'équipage a complété la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et est revenu atterrir à CYKQ. La première approche étant instable, l'équipage a effectué une deuxième approche et l'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.L'inspection subséquente de l'aéronef n'a pas décelée d'anomalie mais a révélé que la friction du levier de puissance droit était molle.

C-FIVM, un Boeing 777-333ER exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol AC845 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Rhein-Main-Frankfurt (EDDF), Allemagne à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC avec 13 membres d'équipage et 191 passagers à bord.  Pendant le vol, un membre du personnel de la cabine a subi une incapacité physique et n'a pas été en mesure de poursuivre ses activités. L'équipage a déclaré un PAN PAN et l'aéronef s'est posé à CYUL où les services médicaux attendaient l'aéronef à son arrivée.

C-FODH, a Harbour Air Seaplanes Viking DHC-3T Turbo Otter, was operating as flight HR241 from Vancouver Harbour (CYHC), BC to Victoria Harbour (CYWH), BC with 1 pilot and 12 passengers on board. The pilot was on approach for an eastbound landing and was not able to deploy landing flap when selected. He confirmed the flaps had stopped travel at the takeoff flap position both visually and with reference to the flap setting indicator. The pilot declared an emergency and flew a missed approach to troubleshoot the situation. After evaluating the situation, he elected to land northbound with partial flap. The airplane landed safely and taxied to the dock. Maintenance discovered that hydraulic line had broken at the flange of the coupling. It was repaired and the aircraft was returned to service.

N652FE, a Federal Express Airbus A300F4-605R, was operating as flight FDX120 from Memphis (KMEM), TN to Edmonton (CYEG), AB with 2 flight crew on board. During the approach, a decision was made to go around due to weather. During flap retraction from flap 20 to flap 15 the flight crew observed a 'FLAPS 1+2' fault. The flight crew actioned the ECAM (electronic centralized aircraft monitoring) with no changes. The QRH was consulted and after selecting flaps to 40, the fault cleared. The aircraft completed a second approach with no issues. Maintenance conducted a variety of checks with no faults found. There had been no similar faults in the past 30 days and the aircraft was returned to service.

AP-BGY, a Pakistan Airlines flight PIA782 Boeing 777-240LR aircraft was taxiing for departure from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON to Islamabad Intl. (OPIS), Pakistan. The aircraft taxied onto Taxiway QUEBEC without clearance and passed the hold line entering into the runway Protected area (RPA) for Runway 23. C-FKAU, an Air Canada flight ACA7290 Boeing 777-333ER aircraft on approach on Runway 23 at CYYZ was instructed to Go-Around. ACA7290 landed Runway 23 at 2111z without further incident.

C-FMXR, a float-equipped Viking DHC-2 Beaver airplane, operated by Tofino Air, was returning to Tofino Harbour (CAB4), British Columbia, after a local sightseeing flight with 5 passengers and 1 pilot on board. During the water landing, after touching down, the aircraft and a water taxi (C12996BC known as the Rocky Pass) from Ahousaht BC, collided. The docking location for both the aircraft and water taxi destinations were in close proximity. The vessel had one operator and two passengers on board. After the collision, the aircraft nosed over and capsized. Everyone on board the aircraft egressed and was transported to safety by various boats that assisted in the rescue. Three passengers on the aircraft and one passenger on board the Rocky Pass sustained minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged, and the vessel sustained minor damage. The ELT did not transmit a signal.The airplane was recovered from the water and transported to the company’s facility.

C-GRWK, A Bell 205A-1 helicopter, operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd., was conducting a long line external load operation from Little Grand Rapids (CZGR), MB to Pauingassi, MB with only the pilot onboard. Shortly after departure from CZGR at approximately 1500 feet ASL, the external load was subject to an un-commanded release from the remote hook of the long line and dropped into a heavily wooded area adjacent to CZGR. The helicopter then returned to CZGR where it landed safely.    The operator's maintenance personnel replaced the remote hook and the helicopter was returned to service. The operator's safety management system has since completed and submitted a trend analysis report of un-commanded load releases to Transport Canada.

C-FSBV, an Air Canada flight ACA800 Boeing 787-900 aircraft, was taxiing for departure from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Dublin Intl. (EIDW) Ireland, when a flight attendant became incapacitated and was unable to continue with their duties. The flight crew requested a to return to the gate and for EMS to meet the aircraft.

C-GHPY, an Air Canada Boeing 787-8 was performing flight ACA0319 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QB to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB, when the flight declared a PAN PAN due to low oil indication on the left engine (General Electric GENX-1B67). The flight crew elected to divert to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON, where the aircraft landed without incident.Initial inspection by maintenance shows left engine oil cap lanyard trapped below cap preventing a good seal and allowing the engine oil to leak out under pressure. The area is to be cleaned and engine the oil qty to be serviced. Servicing records to be reviewed by Air Canada.

C-GOPW, un Boeing 737-275C exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE780 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Puvirnituq, Qc (CYPX) avec 4 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de l'approche à CYPX, l'équipage a actionné les volets et a noté une indication d'asymétrie. L'équipage a alors effectué un circuit d'attente afin d'évaluer la situation et l'équipage a alors noté que le coupe-circuit identifié "Trailing Edge Flap Indication" s'était déclenché. Une vérification visuelle a révélé que les volets ne semblaient pas être positionnés de façon asymétrique, mais ne semblaient pas non plus être à la position sélectionnée de 25 degrés. Le coupe-circuit a été réenclenché et l'indication de volets est demeurée erratique. Considérant l'indication non fiable et les forts vents latéraux, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence. L'appareil a ensuite atterri sans encombre.

C-FJDQ, un Beechcraft B100 exploité par Max Aviation, effectuait le vol MAX100 selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l'aéroport de Sept-Iles, Qc (CYZV) à destination de Mont-Joli, Qc (CYYY). Alors que l'appareil se rapprochait de CYYY, l'équipage a entendu un son inhabituel provenant de la structure de l'aéronef. L'équipage a alors constaté qu'un capot moteur droit s'était ouvert en vol. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre à CYYY.

C-GJZK, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland DHC-8-400 was conducting flight JZA630 from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON to Halifax Stanfield Intl. (CYHZ), NS. After departure, flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to an unsafe cargo door indication. The flight returned to CYOW and landed without incident. After landing the flight crew were informed by ARFF that the latch on the baggage compartment was popped out.

C-GJXN, an Air Canada Airbus Canada Limited Partnership A220-300 was conducting flight ACA0599 from Santa Ana/John Wayne Airport-Orange County (KSNA), CA to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC.  On initial climb, the flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) message. The flight crew followed the RA and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GMZY, an Air Canada Airbus Canada Limited Partnership A220-300, was conducting flight ACA0718 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to New York/ LaGuardia (KLGA), NY.  During descent to KLGA, the flight experienced severe turbulence due to weather.  Flight crew disconnected the Auto Throttle and was able to regain control while climbing. The flight continued to destination without further incident.  Maintenance analyzed DFDR (digital flight data recorder) data, inspected the aircraft and was subsequently returned to service

C-GPAJ, a Chartright Air Inc Canadair CL60 flight HRT056 en route from Palm Beach Intl. (KPBI), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl.(CYYZ), ON, declared a PAN PAN on downwind for Runway 24L at CYYZ due to intermittent engine interstage turbine temperature (ITT) indication on the left engine. The flight crew shutdown the engine as a precaution and landed without further incident.Maintenance is inspecting the aircraft to determine the cause of the indication.

C-GUAT, a de Havilland DHC-7-100 aircraft operated by Air Tindi Ltd. as flight TIN805, was enroute from Tadoule Lake (CYBQ), MB to Thompson (CYTH), MB with a flight crew of 2 and 1 cabin crew member onboard. During the descent into CYTH, the #3 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-50) suddenly rolled back to idle power. The flight crew performed a precautionary shut down of the engine and continued on to CYTH where a successful 3 engine approach and landing was conducted.  An inspection of the #3 engine by the operator's maintenance personnel revealed a broken Py line. The Py line was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYZR, a Cessna 177B, was operating on a VFR flight from Ponoka (CEH3), AB to High River (CEN4), AB with just the pilot on board. During the take-off roll the aircraft veered to the left and the aircraft departed the runway surface, crossed the taxiway and then nosed over in a ditch. The pilot was uninjured. There was substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer, wings, propeller and engine.

C-FJYW, an Aerospatiale - Aeritalia ATR-42 aircraft, operated by Calm Air International as flight CAV222 was enroute from Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU to Baker Lake (CYBK), NU with a crew of three and 12 passengers on board. While on approach into CYRT, the crew received an "ELEC" flashing light indication followed by a #2 DC generator flashing light indication. The pilot advanced engine power and then leveled off at 2500 feet ASL. It was determined that the aircraft had a #2 DC bus failure along with all associated electrical systems. The crew then declared an emergency (PAN PAN) and decided to return to CYRT, where the aircraft landed safely.An inspection of the electrical system by the operator's maintenance personnel revealed an inoperative #2 starter generator. The starter generator was replaced and the aircraft was then returned to service.

C-GDTB, an amphibious Viking Air Limited DHC2T MKIII Turbo Beaver operated by Pacific Sky Aviation, was conducting a VFR flight from Vancouver Harbour (CYHC), BC to Victoria Int’l (CYYJ), BC with 1 pilot and 3 passengers on board. During cruise, 1 of the 4 landing gear up indicator lights on the gear advisory panel extinguished. After troubleshooting the issue, the pilot found that a light bulb was burnt out. On approach to CYYJ, the landing gear was lowered and all 4 green landing gear down lights illuminated and a visual inspection with mirrors showed all 4 landing gear in the down position. The pilot slowed the aircraft and activated the Gear Position Advisory system; the system announced “Check gear” due to the burnt out gear up indicator light bulb. The pilot commenced a go around and, as the aircraft flew by the air traffic control tower, the air traffic controller advised that the landing gear appeared down. On the subsequent approach, the pilot attempted to manually extend the gear; the gear did not lower any further. The pilot requested ARFF to be on standby and the aircraft landed safely.Maintenance personnel changed the gear up indicator light bulb and completed successful gear swings. The aircraft has returned to service.

C-GAMI, a Fairchild SA-227-AC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP as flight PAG1030, was enroute from Island Lake (CYIV), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International (CYWG), MB with only a crew of 2 onboard. While in cruise, the crew received a fire light indication for the right engine (Garrett TPE331-12). The crew consulted the quick reference handbook (QRH) and shut down the right engine. An emergency was declared and the crew continued on to CYWG where an uneventful single engine landing was conducted. The aircraft was met by emergency vehicles who determined that there was no sign of any fire or smoke. The aircraft then taxied to the ramp.

C-FTMN, an Aerospatiale - Aeritalia ATR-72 aircraft operated by Morning Star Express Inc. as flight MAL7088, was enroute from Calgary International (CYYC), AB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International (CYWG), MB with only a crew of 2 onboard. While on descent into CYWG at flight level 230, the crew received an "EMERGENCY BATTERY CHARGE" fault indication. The crew consulted the quick reference handbook (QRH) and then selected the #2 DC bus. The crew declared an emergency (Pan Pan) and decided to to return to CYYC due to moderate icing in the CYWG area. The aircraft then landed safely in CYYC.Following an inspection of the electrical system, the operator's maintenance personnel replaced the emergency battery fault selector switch and then release the aircraft back to service.

C-FEKJ, a Jazz Aviation LP Embraer 170-200SU, was conducting flight JZA7667 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON to Dallas/Fort Worth Intl.(KDLW), TX.  During cruise approximately 80NM north of Memphis Intl. (KMEM), TN, flight crew declared a MAYDAY due to pressurization issues.  Flight crew donned oxygen mask, performed a rapid descent and diverted to KMEM.  Flight landed at KMEM without further incident. Maintenance is troubleshooting.Update: Maintenance replaced outflow valve, cabin pressure controller and found RH PACK outlet line disconnected from ACM causing a large loos of conditioned air.  Hose was replaced and test on the ground were completed.  Test flight was carried out but failed to maintain cabin altitude at FL320 in auto and manual.  CPCS controller was replaced and aircraft was returned to service.  SDR 20211019004 was filed with TC.

C-FXPC, a float-equipped de Havilland Beaver DHC-2 MK.1 operated by 3097448 Manitoba Limited (dba Adventure Air Ltd.), was conducting a flight from Owl Lake MB to Wasagamack, MB. At approximately 14 nm north west of Wasagamack, the pilot felt an engine vibration (Pratt & Whitney USA R-985-AN-14B) and broadcasted on 122.2 that a precautionary landing would be cconducted on Kamwich Lake. A nearby aircraft subsequently relayed that the aircraft and the pilot were safe on the water. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and found a cracked cylinder head. The cylinder was replaced and the aircraft was then flown to the company base.

C-GGYC, un Murphy Rebel d'immatriculation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Saint-Michel-des-Saints, QC à destination du lac Éloigné situé à environ 47 miles marins au nord de Mont-Laurier, QC avec 1 pilote à bord. Arrivé à destination, un amerrissage brutal est survenu et l’appareil a subi des dommages importants. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GGOK, un Dash-8 Q400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA708, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Québec Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec 66 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Lors de la descente, de la fumée est apparue dans le poste de pilotage et l’équipage a mis leur masque à oxygène. La fumée provenait du système électrique de réchauffage pare-brise du côté droit et lorsque l’équipage a éteint le système, la fumée s’est dissipée. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a atterri sans encombre à destination avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-GTVO, un Boeing 737-219C exploité par Chrono Jet sous l’indicatif MBK790, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) à destination de Mary River, NU (CMR2) avec 45 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, les volets ont été sélectionnés à la position rentrée et les volets ont cessé de bouger. L’indicateur montrait une asymétrie des volets qui n’était pas perçue lorsque l’autopilote a été débranché. L’équipage a décidé de revenir atterrir à CYFB et l’appareil a été placé dans un circuit d’attente pendant environ 75 minutes pour réduire le poids de l’avion en dessous du maximum autorisé à l’atterrissage. Pendant ce temps, l’équipage a complété la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour un atterrissage avec les volets de bord de fuite bloqués. Un état d’urgence a été déclaré et l’équipage a atterri l’appareil sur la piste 34 sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FOXA, un Bell 206B d'immatriculation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis une résidence située à Sainte-Mélanie, QC avec un pilote et 4 passagers à bord. Au retour au point de départ, le voyant de basse pression de la pompe de suralimentation en carburant s’est allumé brièvement. Le pilote a choisi d’effectuer un atterrissage de précaution dans un champ et alors qu’il était en approche finale, le moteur (Allison 250-C20) s’est arrêté. Le pilote a fait une autorotation et lors de l’atterrissage, la poutre de queue a été sectionnée par le rotor principal. L’hélicoptère est demeuré à l’endroit sur ses patins et il n’y a eu aucun blessé. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée et a été immédiatement fermée. L’inspection post envolé a déterminée qu’il ne restait plus de carburant à bord.

D-AIXN, an Airbus A350-940 operated by Lufthansa, was conducting flight DLH470 from Frankfurt Main Airport (EDDF), Germany to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl Airport (CYYZ), ON. While on descent for CYYZ, the flight crew advised air traffic control of a passenger medical emergency onboard and requested priority handling and medical assistance at the gate.  A physician on-board attended to the passenger prior to landing.

C-GOPW, un Boeing 737-275C exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE781, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) à destination de Puvirnituq, QC (CYPX) avec 3 membres d’équipage à bord. Lorsque les volets ont été sélectionnés à la position « FLAP 1 » en approche initiale à CYPX, un message d’asymétrie est apparu et les volets ont cessé de bouger. L’équipage a effectué une approche interrompue, et par la suite a complété la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour un atterrissage avec les dispositifs de bord d’attaque sortie et les volets de bord de fuite remontés. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a posé l’appareil sur la piste 19 sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GSYN, un Guimbal Cabri G2 exploité par Synergy Aviation Ltd, a décollé selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) avec 1 pilote à bord pour effectuer du travail de relevés magnétométriques à environ 200 pieds au-dessus du sol. Alors que l’hélicoptère survolait un lac en conditions d'eau miroitante, le pilote a effectué une correction de trajectoire et a percuté la surface du lac à environ 54 mille marins au sud-ouest de CYMT. Le pilote a subi des blessures graves et est sorti de l’hélicoptère submergé à l’envers. L’appareil a subi des dommages importants et a coulé. Le pilote a nagé jusqu’à la rive, a réussi à signaler son écrasement et, quelques heures plus tard, a été rescapé par l’hélicoptère de Recherche et sauvetage des Forces armées canadiennes.

C-GRJZ, un Raytheon B300 (King Air 350) exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE550, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Kangiqsujuaq, QC (CYKG) à destination de Tasiujaq, QC (CYTQ) avec 1 passager et 2 membres d’équipage à bord. En vol, l’équipage a perçu une légère fumée qui provenait du système électrique de réchauffage pare-brise, a éteint le système et la fumée a cessé. Par mesure de précaution, une diversion vers Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) a été effectuée. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre et il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GQWJ, a Boeing 737-7CT operated by Westjet, was conducting flight WJA422 from Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl Airport (CYYZ), ON. At 1530 UTC, the flight crew of WJA422 advised air traffic control that they had a passenger medical emergency on-board and would be continuing to CYYZ as planned, requiring priority handling. Two physicians attended to the passenger onboard and the aircraft landed at CYYZ at 1625 UTC.

C-GXAI, un Dash-8-314 (DH8C) exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE802 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Kuujjuarapik, Qc (CYGW) avec 24 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage à bord. En vol de croisière au niveau de vol 230 à environ 200 miles marins au sud de CYGW, un membre du personnel de la cabine a subi une incapacité physique partielle. L’équipage a vérifié son état et a décidé d’effectuer une diversion à destination de La Grande, Qc (CYGL). L’appareil s’est posé à CYVP sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FFYM, a privately registered Daher TBM700N (TBM910), was conducting an IFR flight from Vernon (CYVK), BC to Westlock (CES4), AB. The aircraft departed CYVK and flew to Springbank (CYBW), AB with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. The aircraft landed in CYBW and made a short stop to pick up 2 additional passengers. During this stop, the aircraft remained running and did not shut down. Moments later, the aircraft departed CYBW for CES4. During landing on Runway 28 at CES4, the aircraft landed hard on the right hand main landing gear, bounced and rolled inverted coming to rest on the south side of the runway. The passengers were assisted out the main entrance by witnesses; the passengers had minor injuries. The pilot was trapped in the cockpit for about 2 hours before first responders could get him safely out of the wreckage; he had serious injuries. An investigator from the TSB Edmonton office deployed to the site.

On 09 October 2021, the privately registered, amateur-built Cavalier SA102.5 aircraft (registration C-FBWF, serial number 6958) was conducting a local recreational flight from Lacombe Aerodrome, Alberta, with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. When the aircraft was 14 nautical miles east of the aerodrome, it entered an aerodynamic stall, resulting in a left-hand spin and collision with terrain. The pilot, who was seated in the left seat, was fatally injured; the passenger received serious injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged; there was no post-impact fire. The 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter activated. A satellite tracking device also helped locate the aircraft.

C-FZJS, a Dassault Falcon 900EX aircraft operated by 2106701 Ontario Inc. (dba NovaJet), was conducting flight number 91 from Halifax/Stanfield (CYHZ), NS to Gander (CYQX), NL. While in cruise flight at about 50 nm west of Sydney, NS, the crew observed a number 1 engine low oil pressure indication, associated Master Caution illumination, and subsequent Master Warning indication. The crew carried out checklist requirements, including the precautionary shut down of the number 1 engine. The crew decided to continue the flight, declared PAN PAN with ATS, and landed at CYQX without further incident.Maintenance personnel replaced the faulty number 1 engine oil filler cap o-ring, and returned the aircraft to service following cleaning, servicing and function tests.

C-FHGG, un Beechcraft 100 exploité par Propair sous l’indicatif PRO100T, effectuait un vol d’entraînement de compagnie selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY). Après avoir effectué une remontée de la piste 18 à l’aéroport de Val-d'Or, QC (CYVO) et être établi sur l’arc DME pour effectuer l’approche ILS 18 à CYVO, l’équipage a senti une forte odeur. Une inspection visuelle de la cabine de pilotage a permis à l’équipage de percevoir de la fumée du côté gauche. L’équipage a suivi les procédures afin d’isoler le circuit électrique défectueux et a avisé la station d’information de vol (FSS) de CYVO qu’il cancellait l’approche pour se diriger directement vers le seuil de piste 18 pour atterrir. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été avisés et l’aéronef a atterri sans encombre. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

N913CK, a Learjet 35 aircraft operated by Kalitta Charters, was conducting medical services flight (KFS161) from Rapid City Regional Airport (KARP), SD, to Penticton (CYYF), BC with 4 crew members and 1 passenger on board. At approximately 10 000 feet, while descending for CYYF, the flight crew noticed the Master Caution annunciator light flashing. After assessing the gauges, they determined that the right engine (Garrett TFE731-2-2B) had had an uncommanded deceleration (roll-back). As a precaution, the flight crew decided to shut down the right engine. An emergency was not declared and the aircraft landed safely at CYYF.Maintenance visually inspected the engine and performed ground power runs; the engine parameters were normal and no defects were found. The compressor inlet pressure sensor was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FBFI, an amateur built Super Cub, equipped with floats, was conducting a takeoff from Lillibelle Lake, ON for a local flight. After liftoff from the water, the aircraft climbed to an altitude of approximately 50 feet, at which time the pilot reached forward and down to check the fuel selector position; the aircraft leveled momentarily then descended and impacted water at a steep angle. The aircraft flipped inverted after striking the water surface. The pilot, the sole person on board, was able to egress the submerged aircraft and was then rescued by a boater in the area that responded quickly to the incident.

C-FRSO, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was conducting positioning flight ACA7263 from Atlanta/Hartsfield Jackson Intl. (KATL), GA to Miami Intl. (KMIA), FL with only 2 crew members on board. After departure from KATL, the flight crew received a ''loss of tire pressure'' message. After executing the checklist, the decision to continue to KMIA was elected. KATL tower reported no debris on the departure runway. Approaching destination, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN, conducted a normal approach and landed without further incident. Maintenance replaced #7 and #8 main landing gear wheel and tire assembly in KMIA.

C-GEHV, an Air Canada Boeing 737 Max 8 was conducting flight ACA0552 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Los Angeles Intl. (KLAX), CA. During the descent to KLAX, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory). Flight crew completed the maneuver and landed without further incident.

C-FKPT, an Air Canada Airbus A320-200 was conducting flight ACA1054 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Phoenix Sky Harbor Intl. (KPHX), AZ. During the approach, the flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) due to another aircraft turning opposing final. The flight crew completed the maneuver with the appropriate call to ATC. The aircraft was sequenced for another approach and landed without further incident.

N402KZ, a Boeing 747-481F operated by Kalitta Air LLC, was conducting cargo flight CKS652 from Anchorage (PANC), AK to Miami Intl. (KMIA), FL. Approximately 1 hour into the flight, the flight crew observed that the #1 engine was being fed fuel from the #1 main fuel tank instead of the inboard tanks as was selected. It appeared as though the #1 fuel crossfeed valve was in the closed position and the flight crew were unable to select it open, leaving the engines only source of fuel being the fuel remaining in #1 main tank. As this was insufficient to supply the engine for the duration of the flight, the flight crew contacted the company operations center for guidance, and the decision was made to shut down the #1 engine (GE CF6-80C2B1F) and continue the flight to destination. When the fuel remaining in the tank was sufficient to supply the engine for the remaining duration of the flight to the destination, the #1 engine was restarted and normal aircraft operations were resumed. An uneventful landing was completed in KMIA. Company maintenance subsequently replaced the #1 engine crossfeed valve actuator, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FZVM, a Black Tusk Helicopters Inc. Kaman Aerospace Corporation K-1200 (K-max) helicopter, was conducting heli-logging operations in the vicinity of Killam Bay, in Jervis Inlet, BC, with 1 pilot on board. Following a mid-day break, the pilot resumed transporting logs from a cut block to an ocean pen approximately 0.6 NM NW. About 1 minute after departing the cut block with a load of 3 logs in the grapple, workers at the cut block heard a loud noise that came from the area of the ocean pen. The pilot could not be contacted by radio nor did he return to the cut block. A company support helicopter was directed to search the area of the ocean pen where they found debris in the water and a sheen on the water. A search and rescue helicopter arrived on scene but was unable to locate the helicopter. Portions of 3 rotor blades were recovered by searchers on the water. The helicopter was located by sonar 8 days after the occurrence. It was approximately 150m west of the reported initial collision location at a depth of approximately 110m. The pilot was fatally injured.

C-GBUU, a de Havilland DHC-8-106 aircraft operated by Summit Air, was conducting a flight from Cat Lake (CYAC), ON to Sioux Lookout (CYXL) ON. During the climb the flight crew received a traffic collision alerting system (TCAS) alert that escalated to a resolution advisory (RA). The RA was generated by C-FRPX, a Fairchild SA227-TT aircraft operated by Skycare Air Ambulance, that was conducting a flight from CYXL to CYAC. The flight crew of C-GBUU disconnected the autopilot and initiated a left turn followed by a descent. They made a call on the mandatory frequency at which point the flight crew of C-FRPX responded that they had C-GBUU on TCAS. The flight crew of C-FRPX had observed potentially conflicting traffic on TCAS and had commenced a turn to the right. They made visual contact with the aircraft and maintained visual separation while establishing radio contact with the traffic. Once clear of the conflict both aircraft resumed course.

C-GGST, un Cessna 172 exploité par Paquin Aviation enr., effectuait un vol privé selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR), depuis l’aéroport de Sherbrooke, QC (CSSC) à destination de Lac-à-la-Tortue, QC (CSL3) avec 1 passager et un pilote à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage, il y avait un léger vent de dos et l’aéronef s’est posé loin sur la piste et la distance de piste restante était insuffisante pour que l’aéronef soit arrêté. L’aéronef est sorti en bout de piste, est entré dans un fossé et a subi des dommages substantiels. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GKKR, an Aerospatiale ATR 42-320 aircraft, operated by Calm Air International LP., was conducting flight CAV775 from Prince Albert/Glass Field (CYPA), SK to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK. The aircraft was in a right turn shortly after departure from Runway 08 on the VEPRI ONE standard instrument departure (SID). While at approximately 2200 feet above sea level, the flight crew observed traffic on the traffic collision avoidance system (TCAS) that was going to become a conflict. The traffic was C-FNWQ, a Cessna 172C inbound to CYPA that was operating under visual flight rules. The pilot of the Cessna had stated their position on the CYPA mandatory frequency just before entering the class E control zone about 5 miles south east of the airport. The flight crew of CAV775 received a resolution advisory (RA) from the TCAS and were advised of the traffic by CYPA radio. They followed the TCAS resolution to continue the climb. They had the Cessna in sight and turned left to avoid the traffic. The flight crew of CAV775 advised Winnipeg Center and CYPA radio of their deviation from the SID due to following the TCAS RA generated by the conflicting VFR traffic.

Le 2 octobre 2021, vers 17 h 45 (heure avancée de l’Est), l’aéronef Cessna 172M (immatriculation C-FFRV, numéro de série 17262394) exploité par Publicité AERO-GRAMME Inc., a décollé de l’aérodrome de St-Mathieu-de-Laprairie (CML8) (Québec) afin d’effectuer un vol de publicité aérienne selon les règles de vol à vue dans la région de Montréal (Québec). Il y avait 1 pilote et 1 passager à bord. Lorsque l’aéronef survolait le fleuve Saint-Laurent à proximité du pont de la Concorde, une perte de puissance du moteur est survenue. Alors que le pilote tentait d’effectuer un atterrissage d’urgence sur l’avenue Pierre-Dupuy, située dans l’arrondissement de Ville-Marie à Montréal, l’aile gauche a fauché la cime des arbres. L’aéronef s’est mis à faire la roue et a percuté le sol. Un incendie s’est déclaré après l’impact. Le pilote a été grièvement blessé, mais a réussi à évacuer l’aéronef. Le passager n’a pu évacuer l’aéronef et a reçu des blessures mortelles. L’aéronef a été détruit. Aucun signal de radiobalise de repérage d’urgence n’a été capté.

C-FASW, a Cessna 525A aircraft operated by AirSprint Inc., was conducting flight ASP503 from Ottawa/Macdonald Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. While the aircraft was on approach for landing in CYYZ runway 24R, the crew reported a black drone 100 ft. above the aircraft when they were 1 mile from runway. The aircraft landed runway 24R without further incident.

C-GJZS, a MHI RJ Aviation ULC CRJ 900 aircraft operated by Jazz LP Aviation, departed Washington Dulles Intl (KIAD), DC for Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During cruise, south of Buffalo Niagara Intl (KBUF), NY, a "R WINDSHIELD HEAT" caution message posted on the EICAS. At the same time the first officer (pilot flying) noticed charring around the heating element on the right forward windshield. The captain (pilot monitoring) consulted the QRH and began actioning the checklist for R WINDSHIELD HEAT. While completing the checklist, the right windshield cracked. The crew checked the inner pane and found it to be secure and cabin pressure was unaffected. The first officer called for the cracked windshield checklist and a PANPAN call was relayed to ATC, they were given clearance to descend, and continued to CYYZ, 29 minutes away. The captain advised the cabin crew and they secured the cabin, but decided there was no need to prepare for an emergency landing as the pressure vessel appeared to be stable. Dispatch was then notified. Before landing, control was transferred to the captain who had the clear windshield. Approach, landing, and taxi in were uneventful with the aid of the QRH.

C-GIJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland DHC-8-402 operating as flight JZA127, was conducting a flight from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC, to Portland Intl. (KPDX), OR. The aircraft was cleared to climb to 19 000 feet by air traffic control and subsequently instructed to stop climb and level off at 9000 feet. The flight crew acknowledged and responded to the altitude clearance change approximately 14 NM south-southeast of CYVR. Due to the vertical climbing speed, the aircraft reached an altitude of 9300 feet. C-GWBL, a Westjet Boeing 737-800 operating as flight WJA543, was conducting a flight from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC, to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC. The aircraft was in level flight approximately 16.5 NM south-southeast of CYVR at 10 000 feet. A loss of separation occurred when the distance between the 2 aircraft was reduced to 2.8 NM horizontally and 700 feet vertically when 1000 feet was required. Both flight crews received and responded to traffic collision avoidance system resolution advisories (TCAS RA) before continuing their intended flight paths.  NAV CANADA is conducting an air traffic services operating irregularity investigation.

C-GJWE, a Westjet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-402 operating as WEN3448, was conducting a flight from Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 4 flight crew and 10 passengers on board. During the initial climb out of CYXT, the hot duct warning for both the flight and the cabin compartments illuminated The pilots referred to the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) and initiated the procedures for a single hot duct warning while the aircraft continued to climb. At FL240, the flight crew received a master warning for cabin altitude. The pilots declared an emergency and executed a rapid descent. The flight and cabin crews initiated their respective depressurization procedures including donning oxygen masks. The aircraft returned to CYXT and landed safely with no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft. Maintenance replaced the compressor discharge overtemperature switch and operational checks were carried out successfully. The aircraft blowout panels were inspected with no faults found. The operator filed an SDR for the overtemperature switch and the aircraft was returned to service.  The QRH did not contain a procedure for hot duct warnings in both the flight and cabin compartments.

C-GUPG, an Airbus A220-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA0687 from St. John's Intl. (CYTT), NL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl.  (CYYZ), ON. While on approach in CYYZ runway 24L, the flight crew reported Engine Indication and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) messages ''HYD PTU FAIL and HYD 2B FAIL''. The crew subsequently initiated a go around and completed the applicable checklist. Both messages cleared during the climb out. The crew declared a ''Pan Pan'' requesting emergency vehicles standby as the nose wheel steering was in question. The aircraft landed on runway 24L where the emergency vehicles were standing by for an inspection. After approximately 10 minutes, ACA0687 taxied off the runway under its own power. Airport operations were shifted to a runway 23 only operation during the occurrence due to several runway closures.

C-FFSS, a Mitsubishi MU-2B-60 aircraft operated by Thunder Airline, was conducting flight THU860 from Greater Sudbury Airport (CYSB), ON to Timmins Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON with 2 crews and 1 medical personnel onboard. While in cruise, the flight crew noticed a large flicker in the oil pressure reading for the left engine followed by a engine torque reading fluctuation. The flight crew elected to perform a precautionary engine shutdown during the approach at approximately 20 NM from CYTS. After completion of the emergency checklists, flight THU860 landed uneventfully in CYTS. No emergency was declared. No fault found on the engine after a preliminary inspection by the company maintenance personnel. The engine was removed and replaced for further investigation.

C-FMBU, a Messerschmitt-Bolkow-Blohm BK-117 helicopter operated by Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service, took off from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Ashern Airport (CJE7), MB with a flight crew of 2 and 2 cabin crew onboard. Shortly after take off, the flight crew noticed the #2 engine (Textron Lycoming LTS 101-750B-1) chip light illuminate. Emergency procedures were carried out and the chip light remained on. A precautionary shut down of the #2 engine was carried out and the helicopter was then diverted back to CYWG where a successful landing was completed.

C-GJWN, an Air Canada Airbus A321-200, was conducting flight ACA940 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Nassau/Lynden Pindling Intl. (MYNN), Bahamas. During the approach, the flight crew received an ''Elec IDG #2 low oil pressure'' (Integrated Drive Generator) warning on ECAM (Electronic centralized aircraft monitor). The flight crew followed the instructions on ECAM, declared a PAN PAN and the aircraft landed without further incident. The maintenance replaced right hand IDG and APU generator and the aircraft was returned to service.

On 26 September 2021, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus A320-214 (registration C-GFCH, serial number 3160) operating as flight ROU1654 from Toronto/Lester B Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Tampa Intl. (KTPA), FL, encountered a flap issue on departure from Runway 33R at CYYZ.  The flight crew declared an emergency (PAN PAN), requested a return to CYYZ and that ARFF be on standby. ROU1654 landed on Runway 24L at CYYZ without further incident.

On 22 September 2021, a WestJet Boeing 737-700 (registration C-GMWJ, serial number 35985) operating as flight WJA579, enroute from Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Toronto/Lester B Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON declared a medical emergency and requested priority handing. Air traffic services provided priority handling and WJA579 landed on Runway 05 at CYYZ at 1208Z without further incident.

C-GXSX, a Piper PA-28-140 operated by Millennium Aviation, had departed Runway 15 at Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbacker Intl (CYXE), SK, for a local flight over the city. When the aircraft returned to CYXE, an approach to Runway 27 was selected as the winds had shifted to favour this runway. The aircraft configuration was set to flaps at 40 degrees and an approach speed of 75 KIAS for the landing with a left crosswind in gusty conditions (approximately 230 degrees at 15 gusting to 25 knots). The pilot attempted to correct for the crosswind; however, upon touchdown the left main landing gear collapsed followed by a collapse of the nose gear. The aircraft then skidded along the paved surface of the runway for approximately 100 feet. The aircraft was substantially damaged.  The pilot and single passenger were able to exit the aircraft with no injuries. Runway 27 was closed for approximately 1 hour while the aircraft wreckage was removed.

C-GJZF, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Dash-8-400, was operating as JZA8476 on a flight from Grande Prairie (CYQU), AB to Calgary (CYYC), AB. During departure from CYQU the flight crew observed a Flap Power Caution light after flap retraction. The flight crew ran the QRH procedure and elected to continue to CYYC. The decision was taken to declare an emergency and carry out a zero flap landing. Airport Rescue and fire fight crews were deployed for the landing which was uneventful. Maintenance Update: L/H FLAP POSITION TRANSDUCER REPLACED AND CONNECTOR CLEANED AS PER AMM 27-53-06-400-801. FUNCTIONALTEST OF THE FLAP CONTROL SYSTEM COMPLETED AS PER 27-51-00-720-801 CHECKED SERVICEABLE.

C-FSKO, un Beech 200 exploité par Keewatin Air LP, sous l’indicatif KEW204 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON à destination d’Iqaluit (CYFB), NU. En vol de croisière au niveau de vol FL270, l’indicateur lumineux de la vanne de prélèvement d’air du moteur droit s’est allumé. L’équipage a complété la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) qui a mené à la fermeture de la vanne. Dans les secondes qui ont suivi, l’équipage a observé une augmentation rapide de l’indicateur d’altitude-pression de la cabine. Une descente d’urgence a été effectuée jusqu’à 10 000 pieds. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence au centre de contrôle terminal et a demandé un déroutement vers l’aéroport de La Grande Rivière (CYGL), QC où il a atterri sans encombre.

C-FVPZ, un Piper PA-18S-150 sur flotteurs en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis la rivière du Lièvre (Ferme Neuve, QC) à destination de Parent, Qc avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Lors du décollage, le pilote a perdu la maitrise de l'aéronef et a percuté, inversé, la surface de la rivière. L'aéronef a subi des dommages importants et les 2 occupants sont décédés. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) ne s’est pas déclenchée.

C-FSDW, an Air Canada Boeing 737 Max 8 was conducting flight ACA0967 from Bridgetown/Grantley Adams Intl. (TBPB), Barbados to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. On take off run, flight crew received an L1 Door indication on EICAS (Engine-indicating and crew-alerting system). Flight crew declared a Pan Pan and rejected take off. The aircraft taxied to the gate without further incident. Maintenance replaced faulty L1 door sensor and the aircraft was returned to service.

N2019C, a Bombardier Global 6500 aircraft operated by Citigroup Inc, was conducting a flight from Westchester County Airport (KHPN), NY to Athens Intl Airport (LGAV), Greece. During cruise, while in Gander oceanic airspace, the crew received a Right Engine Oil Quantity Low caution message. The crew actioned the QRH, all engine indications were within normal parameters. The crew elected to divert to Gander Intl (CYQX), NL and requested clearance from ATC via CPDLC (Controller–pilot data link communications) and HF. Due to no response from ATC, the crew issued a CPDLC PAN PAN and initiated the North Atlantic contingency procedure. The crew eventually received clearance to CYQX, and the caution message extinguished on descent into CYQX. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance conducted an inspection of the aircraft and did not observe any leaks. In consultation with the manufacturer, the aircraft was cleared to return to KHPN, where maintenance replaced the engine oil quantity probe and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FASW, un Cessna 525A exploité par Airsprint Inc., effectuait le vol ASP503 selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l'aéroport de Toronto/Lester B Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON à destination d'Ottawa/MacDonald Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON. Une perte d'espacement est survenue avec C-FLKC, un Boeing 737-8 (MAX), exploité par Flair Airlines ltd, qui effectuait le vol FLE306 depuis l'aéroport Stanfield de Halifax (CYHZ), NE, lorsque que ASP503 a été autorisé pour une approche RNAV Z pour la piste 14 à CYOW derrière FLE3069. L'espacement entre les 2 appareils a été réduit à 3.6 milles marins (NM) alors alors que l'espacement requis est de 4 Nm. L'approche de ASP503 dans le sillage de FLE306 a été interrompue. ASP503 a atterris sans encombres à 15 :00Z.

C-FFWG, a privately registered Beech 35-33, was conducting a VFR flight from Souris Glenwood Industrial Air Park (CJX5), MB to Virden/R.J. (Bob) Andrew Field Regional (CYVD), MB, with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. In the downwind for Runway 08 at CYVD, the pilot selected the gear switch to the down position and then selected 2/3 flaps during the left base. The aircraft subsequently landed Runway 08 with the gear in the retracted position. Both occupants were uninjured and the aircraft sustained substantial damage to the flaps, belly skin, engine, and propeller.It was reported that during the recovery of the aircraft, the master switch was turned on and the landing gear started lowering.

C-FJWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Dash 8-400, was operating as flight WEN3196 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB, to Regina (CYQR), SK. Upon landing gear retraction on take-off, the flight crew observed multiple gear caution lights. The flight crew actioned the QRH and coordinated with ATC to conduct an air turnback to CYYC. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN for arrival and CYYC tower activated ARFF to be standing by. WEN3196 landed safely with no further issue.Maintenance Update: Nose gear door harness was found unserviceable. Nose gear door replaced and the system tested serviceable.

C-GVWJ, a WestJet Airlines Ltd. Boeing 737-700, was operating as flight WJA4020 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Fort Mackay (CYFI), AB. While in cruise at FL350, the #1 engine (CFM-56-7B24/3) experienced an un-commanded deceleration. The crew retarded the #1 throttle and brought it up again. The #1 engine reaccelerated and regained power with no further deceleration for the remainder of the flight. The crew elected to divert to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB. An emergency was declared and the flight landed at CYEG uneventfully. Maintenance Update: After extensive troubleshooting and analysis of the FDR, the #1 EEC was replaced. A successful test flight was undertaken and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FTID, an ATR 42-500, operated by Bradley Air Services Limited (dba Canadian North) as flight AKT677, was conducting a flight from Cambridge Bay (CYCB), NU to Taloyoak (CYYH), NU. Upon landing at CYYH, the PEC Fault Light illuminated on the #2 engine and the aircraft veered to the left, striking 3 runway edge lights before the aircraft was returned to the center of the runway. The aircraft taxied to the ramp without further incident and remains at CYYH until maintenance release.Update November 1st 2021: The operator’s maintenance conducted a fault test and replaced the PEC computer and Prop Valve Module (PVM). Damage to the nose landing gear was identified, both nose wheels, left nose wheel, taxi light, and right hand aft nose gear door were replaced. The Configuration Deviation List (CDL) was closed and the aircraft was returned to service. Upon landing a few days later on 21 October 2021, the PEC fault light re-illuminated upon landing, this time in Gjoa Haven (CYHK), NU. The crew landed the aircraft and was able to maintain directional control on the runway. The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft, no damage was found. System tests were conducted and relays FIN 102KH and 98 KH and the micro switch unit in the throttle/condition lever were replaced. The company conducted a series of flight tests; the fault did not reoccur and the aircraft was returned into service.  The company submitted a Service Difficulty Report (SDR) to Transport Canada. No further issues have been reported.

C-GJZT, a MHI RJ Aviation ULC CRJ 900 operated by Jazz Aviation LP was conducting Flight JZA8886 from Montréal-Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Deer Lake Regional Airport (CYDF), NL. When the aircraft was approximately 100 nautical miles west of Fredericton Airport (CYFC), NB, the crew contacted Boston Area Control center and requested to divert to Halifax Stanfield Intl(CYHZ), NS due to a left engine vibration. The crew reduced power to flight idle on the affected engine and declared Pan-Pan with ATC. The aircraft continued to CYHZ and landed without further incident.Maintenance crews replaced the left engine blade pins with a new set. The engine was ground run and function checks completed with engine vibration values within limits and the aircraft has been returned to service.

Le 12 septembre 2021, l’aéronef Pilatus PC-12/47E (immatriculation C-GIOX, numéro de série 1237) exploité par Airmédic Inc. effectuait le vol AM237 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport international de Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB) (Québec) à destination de l’aéroport de Sept-Îles (CYZV) (Québec) avec uniquement 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de l’approche finale pour la piste 09 à CYZV, la vitesse de l’aéronef a augmenté et il a franchi le seuil de piste à 200 pieds au-dessus du sol; son taux de descente était de 2000 pi/min, le train d'atterrissage était en transit et les volets étaient rentrés. L’aéronef s’est posé à environ 2525 pieds au-delà du seuil de la piste 09, qui était mouillée, à une vitesse indiquée de 159 nœuds. Environ 20 secondes plus tard, l’aéronef a fait une sortie en bout de piste à une vitesse sol de 57 nœuds, a parcouru environ 590 pieds dans l’herbe avant d’amorcer un virage à droite autour d’un feu d’approche puis de revenir sur la piste. Personne n’a été blessé. L’aéronef n’a subi aucun dommage.

C-GJWO, an Air Canada Airbus 321-200, was conducting flight ACA740 from San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), CA to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON.  During climb at approximately 18,000 feet, 200 nautical miles north east of KSFO, the flight crew declared an emergency due to hydraulic issues. The flight diverted to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC where it landed without further incident. Troubleshooting carried out in CYVR revealed a leak from a pin hole in a tee fitting below the B System HP Manifold.

C-FABA, a de Havilland DHC-8-102 operated by Wasaya Airways as flight WSG815, was conducting a fuel cargo flight from Wiebenville (CXX2), ON to Big Trout Lake (CYTL), ON. Just prior to touchdown at CYTL, the crew observed the landing gear indication change to the unsafe condition, heard the gear horn, and felt the nose gear retracting. The crew initiated a go-around and declared an emergency (Mayday) with Thunder Bay Radio. They requested to divert to Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON. Upon arrival at CYPL the crew did a low and over for ground crew inspection purposes. They then conducted an alternate gear extension, receiving a 3 green/safe gear indication, and carried out an uneventful landing. A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed 2 faulty nose gear proximity sensors. The sensors were replaced, gear swings were conducted, and the aircraft was returned to service

C-GJZR, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland DHC-8-402, was conducting flight JZA8029 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC to Victoria International (CYYJ), BC with 4 crew and 39 passengers on board. The airplane landed without incident but, as they taxied to the gate, the crew was advised to stop by the air traffic services. The tower controller had observed smoke coming from the front of the airplane and activated the Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) crew. After getting the all clear from ARFF, the crew attempted to continue the taxi but found the nose gear steering was inoperative. The aircraft was towed to the gate without further incident.The number 2 hydraulic system fluid quantity indicated empty and there was no hydraulic pressure. ARFF cleaned up hydraulic fluid on the taxiway. Maintenance replaced the Nose Landing Gear lock actuator hydraulic flex hose and the airplane was returned to service.

C-GZKI, a Cessna 152 aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Services/Gander Flight Training, was conducting night training circuits at Gander Intl, NL (CYQX) with 1 student pilot onboard. On landing, the aircraft bounced and subsequently landed on the nose gear, causing the nose gear to collapse. The aircraft came to a stop on the runway, resting on the nose and left wing. The pilot was not injured.Company maintenance towed the aircraft to the hangar. Initial inspection revealed damage to the propeller, engine, engine mount, nose landing gear and left hand wing. The aircraft has been removed from service pending further assessment.

C-FMAO, un Pilatus PC-12 exploité par Airmedic Inc, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) au départ de Kuujjuarapik, QC (CYGW) à destination de Val d’Or, Qc (CYVO) avec 5 passagers et 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’aéronef se trouvait en montée pour son altitude de croisière, le message «Autopilot Fail» est apparu. Peu de temps après, le pilote aux commandes (PF) a avisé le pilote surveillant (PM) que le compensateur ne fonctionnait plus. Le PM a pris les commandes de l'appareil et le PF a actionné la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH). L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et a effectué un déroutement vers La Grande Rivière, Qc (CYGL) où l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre. Une inspection effectuée par la maintenance a révélé un relais défectueux. Celui-ci a été remplacé et l’appareil a été remis en service.

C-FGJI, an Air Canada Airbus A320-214, was operating as flight AC2217 from North Peace Regional Airport (CYXJ), BC, to Kelowna Intl Airport (CYLW), BC. with 5 crew and 69 passengers on board. Shortly after departure, the crew observed an ECAM message associated with the nose wheel steering being inoperative. The crew made a decision to divert to Calgary Intl Airport, (CYYC) AB, referred to the quick reference checklist, and an emergency (Pan Pan) was declared. The aircraft landed at CYYC without further incident. There were no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft.Maintenance found a proximity sensor issue. The sensor was replaced, the aircraft jacked, rigging and function checks were completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKCP, a Canadian Pacific Railway Company Bombardier CL-600-2B16, was conducting a flight from Palm Beach (KPBI), FL to Lincoln (KLNK), NE for a scheduled heavy maintenance at KLNK.  During the approach, flight crew declared an emergency due to flap failure.  The aircraft landed without further incident.Update: As part of the flight, maintenance had to complete an Air Driven Generator test. While completing the test on a hold at KLNK, Flaps Fail EICAS was generated. The troubleshooting by Duncan Aviation revealed that incorporated SB 605-27-006R3 (installation of a flap onboard recorder system) induce the signal with power change and flap at 20 degrees. As Bombardier does not have a fix for the problem encountered, the SB and system was deactivated. The aircraft has been returned to service since.  SDR has been filed with Transport Canada, CPR SMS has also been filed.

C-FEIE, an Insignia College Limited Cessna 172M airplane, was conducting a cross country training flight on a round trip from Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC with only the student pilot on board. The pilot was on short final to Runway 11 in Sechelt (CAP3), BC with an airspeed of approximately 70 knots. The airplane’s flaps were extended to the landing position. The aircraft landed and bounced into the air. The pilot pushed the nose down resulting in a hard landing. The damage included a propeller strike, a flat nose wheel, and damage to the firewall. The pilot taxied from the active runway onto the apron. Airport staff assisted moving the aircraft to the parking area due to the flat nose wheel.The company’s maintenance arrived at CAP3 and, after inspecting the aircraft, had it shipped to CZBB by truck. The pilot has been debriefed and the airplane is in maintenance awaiting repairs.

C-GKOD, an Air Canada Airbus A320-214, was conducting flight ACA289 from Terrace (CYXT), BC to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC with 5 crew and 119 passengers on board. During the descent into CYVR, a Flap Warning System 1 Fault was indicated and was followed by a flap/slat indicator turning amber for several seconds. Subsequently, the flight crew noticed a strong, acrid smell in the flight deck. They then declared a PAN PAN emergency and air traffic services provided priority handling. Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting was put on standby and the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre was advised of the situation. The flight landed, the odour dissipated, and the crew taxied to the gate without further incident.Maintenance conducted troubleshooting and replaced the number 1 System Data Acquisition Concentrator as per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM). Additionally, the recirculation filters were inspected (due to the reported acrid smell in cockpit) and replaced as per the AMM. No other faults were found and the airplane was returned to service.

C-GJZX, a De Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8637 from Halifax/Stanley International, NS (CYHZ) to Ottawa/Macdonald–Cartier International Airport, ON (CYOW). The aircraft was in the climb approximately 38 NM West of CYHZ when the Input/Output Processor (IOP2 FAIL) caution message appeared on the engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS) display. The crew declared Pan-Pan with Moncton Area Control Center, completed the QRH and requested a VFR block of airspace to burn off fuel; ATC provided a vectored hold at 6000 ft. The aircraft landed without further incident on RWY 23 in CYHZ at 1843 ADT. Company maintenance replaced the IOP2 module (P/N C12432AB09) and returned the aircraft to service after the system tested serviceable. A service difficulty report was submitted to Transport Canada.

C-FXCD an Air Canada A320-214 conducting flight ACA552 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), CA. On descent into KLAX, the flight crew reported a TCAS RA and the crew completed the procedure. ATC informed and aircraft observed below. Flight continued to land without further incident.

C-GTJA, a MHI RJ Aviation ULC Regional Jet CRJ200, operated by Jazz Aviation LP was conducting flight 8858 from Philadelphia Intl (KPHL), PA to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl  (CYUL) QC. On departure, the flight crew selected gear up and received a nose gear disagree light. The flight crew declared an emergency and burned fuel to get to maximum landing weight. The aircraft landed without further incident, was met by ARFF and then taxied to the gate. Upon further inspection, the gear safety pin was left in the nose gear prior to departure.

C-FACD, a Bell 212 operated by Wildcat Helicopters Inc., was conducting a VFR repositioning flight from Chapleau Municipal Airport (CYLD), ON to Kelowna Wildcat Heliport (CWC2), BC. During an unplanned low level diversion, the helicopter contacted a residential power line on the forward transmission fairing. The pilot conducted an immediate landing into a grass field. The helicopter remained upright, however, the tail rotor struck ground during the flare and touchdown and the main rotor blade severed the tail boom. The pilot was uninjured. The helicopter was equipped with wire strike protection and suffered substantial damage. Company maintenance is assessing the damage and will provide and update.

C-FLJL, a privately registered Mooney M20J, was landing on runway 30 at the South River Airport (CPE6), ON. During the landing, it was reported that the aircraft bounced several times, and subsequently a go-around was conducted. The aircraft was observed climbing over the trees at the end of the runway. However, shortly afterwards the aircraft crashed into the bush, approximately 1300 feet from the departure end of the runway. Both occupants received fatal injuries, and the aircraft was destroyed. The TSB deployed investigators to the accident site.

C-GSPW, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE700 selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis La Grande Rivière (CYGL), QC à destination de Puvurnituq (CYPX), QC. Alors que l'appareil était en vol de croisière, à environ 125 NM au nord-nord-est de CYGL, l’équipage a observé un problème avec le système de carburant. Par mesure de précaution, l’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence (PAN PAN) et a effectué déroutement vers CYGL. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre.

C-FPSR, a privately owned Murphy Rebel equipped with amphibious floats, was being flown for the purpose of type training following the purchase of the aircraft, with the owner/pilot and an instructor on board. Numerous landings had been made on both water and land during the course of the flight before they flew to Lake Scugog, ON for a landing adjacent to Port Perry harbour. Immediately following touchdown, geese were observed ahead of the aircraft; the pilot attempted to avoid them with a turn to the right. The left float dug into the water, and the aircraft overturned. Both occupants exited the aircraft without difficulty, and were picked up by nearby boaters shortly after the occurrence. There were no injuries. Damage to the aircraft will be assessed after it is recovered from the water.

C-GDER, a privately registered Ayres S2R aircraft was applying pesticide to a canola field in the area of Lipton, SK. During a pass over the field, the pilot felt excessive engine (Walter M601) vibrations and flames coming out of the exhaust stacks; followed by a complete loss of engine power. The pilot then successfully completed a forced landing in the field. The pilot was not injured. The aircraft sustained minor damage. An inspection of the engine and cowling revealed an uncontained failure behind the propeller.

C-GCOQ, a 38252 Yukon Inc. (dba Rogue River Outfitters) Piper PA-18-150, on straight floats, was operating from the Stewart River, 90 NM east of Mayo, YT, with one pilot on board. During take-off from the river, the aircraft contacted the river shore and nosed over. The pilot egressed without issue and was attended to by bystanders. The 406 ELT activated and the pilot sustained no injuries.

C-GIKX, a Bell helicopter 206L-1 operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited (dba Acasta Heliflight) was conducting a flight from Hope Bay (CHB3) NU. to a drill camp located 8 nm SSW of CBH3 with only the pilot on board. Upon landing, the helicopter rolled over. The pilot subsequently shut down the engine and exited the helicopter uninjured. A person on the ground was fatally injured. The TSB is conducting an investigation.

VQ-BUC, an Aeroflot B777-300, was operating as flight AFL107 from Los Angeles (KLAX), CA to Sheremetyevo International Airport (UUEE), Russia. While in cruise, approximately 45 NM south of Lethbridge, AB, fumes were detected in the cabin. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATS and diverted to Edmonton (CYEG), AB. During the diversion fuel dumping occurred to ensure a proper weight for landing. The flight arrived in CYEG without further issue.

C-GCEV, a de Havilland DHC-7-100 aircraft operated by Air Tindi Ltd. as flight TIN801, was enroute from Ferguson Lake, NU. to Thompson, MB. (CYTH) with a flight crew of 2 and 1 crew member onboard. During the departure, the crew received a #1 hydraulic pressure loss indication followed by a loss of oil pressure indication of the #2 Engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-50). The crew completed a precautionary shutdown of the #2 engine and elected to continue the flight to CYTH. The crew declared a Pan Pan and then completed a 3 engine approach and landing without incident.

C-FOJZ, a MHI RJ Aviation ULC Regional Jet CRJ 900 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting Flight 8485 from Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC with 4 crew members and 58 passengers on board. The Captain was conducting a check ride and was the pilot monitoring. The First Officer was the pilot flying. The landing at CYVR was recorded as being 2.789g resulting in the requirement for a high load landing event inspection. The flight crew taxied to the gate and were unable to start the airplane’s auxiliary power unit. After shutting down the aircraft, the flight crew realized that a flight attendant (FA) was injured; paramedics were called to attend. The FA, who was seated in the aft jump seat during the landing, was seriously injured and, after first aid was administered, was taken to a local hospital. The other cabin crew member received minor injuries. Company Maintenance conducted an inspection and found that both main landing gear shocks showed evidence of having bottomed out. They then initiated a high load landing event (HLLE) inspection. The airplane remained on the ground at CYVR for 6 days while the HLLE inspection and related tasks were carried out. The subsequent maintenance included replacing both of the main landing gear. The airplane has been returned to service.

C-FSDW, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 Max was conducting flight ACA0740 from San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), CA to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON. On departure, Flight crew noticed an RPAS (black in appearance with red and white lights) 100 feet from the aircraft.  Flight crew advised ATC and continued to CYYZ without further incident.

C-GQJA, a Jazz aviation LP MHI RJ Aviation ULC CL-600-2B19, was conducting flight JZA7724 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON to Cleveland-Hopkins Intl. (KCLE), OH. During taxi in KCLE, flight crew declared an emergency due to smoke in the cabin reported by the flight attendant.  Flight attendant also noticed that she could not feel any heat anywhere.  The smoke dissipated in the cabin by the time ARFF arrived to the airplane and proceeded to the gate where passengers deplaned normally.  Fire crew inspected the aircraft and concluded that the white smoke was actually condensation.

The privately registered Cessna 182A, C-GWAW, was operating a recreational flight from Westlock, AB (CES4) to Josephburg, AB (CFB6). While conducting preflight checks of the aircraft, the pilot noted that the fuel gauges read below half and checked the fuel tank level with an ungraduated fuel dipstick. On the final approach to Runway 08 at CFB6, the engine (Teledyne Continental O-470-L) subsequently lost power and the pilot initiated a forced landing; the aircraft collided with trees 0.3 nm short of runway. The pilot and the two passengers evacuated the aircraft with no issues. The pilot received minor injuries; the two passengers were uninjured. The aircraft was substantially damaged and the ELT did not activate. The RCMP conducted a post occurrence examination of the aircraft and observed no fuel in either fuel tank.

C-GENM, a WestJet Encore De Havilland of Canada DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3210 from Comox (CYQQ), BC to Calgary (CYYC), AB with 4 crew and 55 passengers on board. When the landing gear was selected down on approach into CYYC, the flight crew observed 3 red landing gear unsafe indications. A missed approach was conducted followed by the completion of the appropriate check lists and an alternate landing gear extension. The flight crew observed 3 green landing gear safe indications and an uneventful approach and landing ensued with ARFF standing by for the landing.Company maintenance replaced the landing gear selector valve. The system was checked serviceable and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GDSS, an Aerospatiale ATR 42-300 aircraft operated by Calm Air International LP as flight CAV144, was enroute from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Churchill (CYYQ) MB with a crew of 3 and 28 passengers on board. While in cruise, the crew received a hot brake indication and decided to return to CYWG. The crew declared an emergency and then landed the aircraft without further incident. The operator's maintenance subsequently replaced the brake over temp monitoring unit and the aircraft was then returned to service.
