C-FMBU, a Messerschmitt-Bolkow-Blohm BK-117 helicopter operated by Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service, departed Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with a flight crew of 2 and 2 cabin crew onboard. Shortly after take off, the flight crew noticed the #2 engine (Textron Lycoming LTS 101-750B-1) chip light illuminate. Emergency procedures were carried out and the chip light remained on. A precautionary shut down of the #2 engine was carried out and the helicopter was then diverted back to CYWG where a successful long field landing was completed.

C-GJYI, an Air Canada Airbus 220-300, was conducting flight ACA763 between Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL) QC and San Francisco Intl (KSFO), CA. During cruise portion of the flight to KSFO, EICAS (Engine-indicating and crew-alerting system) showed a left hand engine low pressure warning briefly and went away. During the descent to KSFO, flight crew received an EICAS Low engine oil pressure on left hand engine.  Flight crew conducted QRH, precautionarily shutdown the engine and declared a MAYDAY with ATC.  Flight landed without further incident, was met by ARFF and taxied to the gate.  Maintenance is troubleshooting the occurrence.

CF-SVT, un hydravion Piper J3C-65 a décollé de la rivière Batiscan au niveau de la pourvoirie de la Seigneurie du Triton, située à 25 milles marins (NM) à l’est-nord-est de l’aérodrome de La Tuque (CYLQ) (Québec), pour un vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) à destination de l’hydroaérodrome de Saint-Étienne-des-Grès / Hydravion Adventure (CHA2) (Québec). À bord se trouvaient le pilote, assis en place arrière, et un passager, assis en place avant. Il était prévu qu’après le décollage, le pilote survolerait les chalets de la pourvoirie pour permettre au passager de prendre des photos. À environ 6300 pieds du point de départ, l’hydravion, toujours dans l’effet de sol, a monté légèrement à environ 100 pieds au-dessus de la rivière et a amorcé un virage de 180° par la gauche en direction d’un relief ascendant. Pendant le virage à gauche à 45° d’inclinaison, sa vitesse et son altitude ont diminué. Le pilote a perdu la maîtrise de l’hydravion, qui a subi un décrochage aérodynamique menant à une autorotation de mise en vrille et a percuté les arbres, puis le sol dans une assiette verticale. Le pilote a subi des blessures graves et le passager des blessures mortelles. L’aéronef a été détruit par la force de la collision. Aucun incendie ne s’est déclaré.

C-FBVH, a Hughes 369D helicopter, operated by Oceanview Helicopters Limited, lifted off from Toba Inlet after taking on fuel. Shortly afterwards, while in cruise flight, the pilot observed the fuel filter light illuminate intermittently (about 4-5 times). He reduced power but the flickering continued. The engine (Rolls-Royce/Allison 250-C20B) torque indication was also fluctuating by 10 to 15 psi. Upon seeing this, the pilot reduced power further and turned the helicopter 180 degrees. The engine quit shortly after the turn was completed and the pilot conducted a forced landing and autorotation to an open marshy area. During the flare and subsequent touchdown, the helicopter slid about 30 feet, snagged a ditch and came to an abrupt stop. The main rotor blades contacted the tail boom and severed it from the fuselage. The pilot was not injured and egressed. The helicopter was substantially damaged. The Company obtained fuel samples which appeared clear and bright. The helicopter was retrieved and transported to their maintenance facility where it was further inspected. Maintenance performed a vacuum leak test on the air side fuel system components and found the pressure differential switch was not air tight. They are planning to run-up the engine in a test cell to verify the complete operation.

C-FTFP, a privately registered Beech BE23 (Musketeer), was on a local pleasure flight from Sundre (CFN7), AB with one pilot and one passenger on board. During a take-off from the grass runway, Runway 24, the pilot rejected the take-off just beyond the mid point of the runway. The aircraft did not stop before it overran the end and went across a road and through a fence. The pilot and passenger were uninjured; however, the aircraft sustained damage to the wings, cowling, propeller and landing gear. The 121.5 MHz ELT activated.

C-FYAI, un Dash-8-314 (DH8C) exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE852, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments (IFR) depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage International, QC (CYQB) à destination de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) avec 21 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage à bord. En vol de croisière, au niveau de vol FL250, à environ 180 miles marins au sud-ouest de CYVP, une fluctuation de la pression d’huile du moteur droit est survenue. L’équipage a complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH), a fermé le moteur droit (Pratt and Whitney, Canada, PW123B) et a déclaré un état d’urgence (PAN PAN). L’appareil s’est posé à CYVP sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FVFV, un ballon Sundance SBA90 d'immatriculation privé, effectuait un vol depuis le Parc La Baie à Gatineau, QC à destination de champs dans la région de l’aéroport de Gatineau (CYND), QC, dans le cadre du Festival de Montgolfières de Gatineau, avec 2 passagers et 1 pilote à bord. Après environ une heure de vol, alors que le ballon se trouvait au-dessus de la ville, le pilote a effectué une approche vers un terrain vacant entre 2 résidences. En descente finale, le panier du ballon a percuté le toit d’une maison et s’est arrêté quelques secondes avant de reprendre l’envol. Par la suite, il s’est retrouvé en descente rapide et a effectué un atterrissage brutal. Les 2 passagers ont subi des blessures et ont été transportés à l’hôpital, le ballon a été légèrement endommagé.

C-GANH, an Air North Boeing 737-500, was operating as flight ANT702 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Whitehorse (CYXY), YT with 6 crew and 119 passengers on board. While on approach an APU start was attempted but not successful. During the taxi in to the gate, the APU was once again started and successfully brought on line; however, an APU fire alarm sounded shortly after and the APU automatically shut down. The flight crew stopped short of the gate and actioned the emergency checklist for an APU FIRE and activated the extinguisher for the APU. An emergency was declared and ARFF attended the aircraft. No heat, smoke or fire was observed and the aircraft continued to the gate where a normal deplanement occurred. Company maintenance found evidence of an APU tail pipe fire and the APU muffler experienced heat warping and cracking due to fire. The APU has been MEL'd.

C-GTRG, a Chartright Air flight HRT024 Gulfstream G200, was in cruise flight from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Keflavík (BIKF), Iceland when a L BATT OVRHT caution message illuminated. The flight crew checked the battery temperature and it was indicating normal and coded green. The L BATT OVRHT message then extinguished. A short time later the the flight crew received another caution indication and when the battery was checked it was indicating 170 degrees and coded red. The flight crew carried out the battery overheat checklist, declared an emergency and returned to CYYZ. The aircraft dumped 4000 pounds of fuel in preparation for landing and landed without further incident. The aircraft was checked by the flight crew and fire department after vacating the runway and there was no sign of fire, smoke and the battery was cold. The aircraft returned to the FBO ramp.Maintenance swapped the battery and the aircraft completed the flight.

Le Boeing 737-700 exploité par WestJet sous l’indicatif WJA212 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL). En approche finale pour la piste 24L à CYUL, une perte d’espacement de turbulence de sillage est survenue lorsqu’il s’est retrouvé à 4,5 nm derrière un Boeing 777 d’Air Canada en approche finale sur la même piste alors que la norme d’espacement est de 5 nm. Aucune turbulence de sillage n’a été rapportée et les 2 appareils ont poursuivi leurs approches et atterrissages sans encombre.

C-GJLS, a WestJet Boeing 737-800, was operating as flight WJA658 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Toronto (CYYZ), ON with 6 crew and 132 passengers on board. During the initial climb on departure the flight crew observed a flap asymmetry indication. The flight crew levelled off at 8000 feet ASL and obtained vectors from ATC to remain in the Calgary area. The appropriate checklists were completed, an emergency was declared with ATC and the aircraft arrived back in Calgary with no further issue.Company maintenance replaced the trailing edge FLAP SKEW sensor, cleaned the flap position transmitters and replaced the FLAP/SLAT electronics unit.

C-GWRI, an Aspire Aviation Limited De Havilland DHC-8-103 airplane, was conducting flight TSH1202 from Vancouver Int'l Airport (CYVR), BC to Masset (CZMT), BC with 3 crew members and 23 passengers on board. During cruise at 22 000 feet above sea level, multiple left-hand electrical bus system malfunctions occurred without annunciation indications. The pressurization indication panel became unserviceable and the cabin altitude began to climb. The flight crew decided to return to CYVR, descended to 11 000 feet, and completed the actions listed in the Quick Reference Handbook. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC. Maintenance found the left-hand transformer-rectifier unit undervoltage relay (part number 2431-K19) faulty. The relay was replaced and testing was completed in accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual. The system tested serviceable and the aircraft was returned to service.

On 04 September 2021, a Quad City Challenger Ultralight (C-IRGH) was conducting a daytime visual flight at the Carp Airport (CYRP),ON with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. On final approach to the runway, the aircraft collided with power lines on the approach path. The pilot lost control of the aircraft and the aircraft impacted the terrain short of the runway, just inside the airport property fence line. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. Both occupants received minor injuries and were transported to local hospital for medical attention.

C-GMZN, an Air Canada Airbus Canada Limited Partnership A220-300, was conducting flight ACA1040 from Denver Intl. (KDEN), CO to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During descent to CYYZ at approximately 15 000 feet, the Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) displayed ''L ENG OPER DEGRADED'' Caution message. The flight crew completed the applicable checklist and declared a ''Pan Pan'' to air traffic control. The flight crew maintained control of the engine and reported that the thrust did follow lever movement with a small N1 split between left and right engine. The aircraft landed on Runway 24R where emergency vehicles were standing by. After an inspection by ARFF, aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power without further incident.

C-GNTC, a privately registered Cessna 185F on floats, was on a recreational flight from Fort St. John / Charlie Lake (CEY7), BC, to Beattie Lake, BC, with the pilot and one passenger on board. The landing area is at an elevation of 4242 feet above sea level and located in a mountainous valley. While on final approach, along the north shore of the lake, a crosswind gust caused the aircraft to veer to the right. One float contacted the water, the aircraft came to an abrupt stop and nosed over. The pilot and passenger were both wearing shoulder harnessed seat restraints and life vests. After egress, they collected the survival kit, sleeping bags, and tool kit and stayed with the airplane.  When the airplane stopped drifting, the pilot and passenger swam 15 feet to the lakeshore and sheltered in a nearby cabin. The 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter was submerged as the aircraft inverted in the water and no signal was relayed to the Joint Rescue Coordination Center. The pilot had a satellite phone but it was in the overturned airplane's cabin and unrecoverable. Unsuccessful attempts were made to establish cellular communications. When the pilot failed to report in after landing, the responsible person arranged for a private helicopter to fly over the area. The pilot and passenger were found, picked up the following morning, and returned to Fort St. John.

C-GGBC, a PAL Aerospace privately operated Dassault Falcon 900EX, was conducting a flight between Ostend-Brugge Intl (EBOS) Belgium to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS.  Immediately after take off, flight crew got an EICAS (Engine-indicating and crew-alerting system) white fault code followed by a yellow code HP 3 FAIL. Flight crew proceeded with the appropriate checklist and received concerns from passengers of a burning/heat smell in the cabin.  Flight crew advised ATC and requested return to EBOS. Shortly after, another message was received on EICAS (HP 2+3 OVERHEAT) and Flight crew completed the appropriate checklist, declared an emergency with ATC and requested vectors for runway 08.  Flight landed in EBOS without further incident.  Aircraft stopped on the runway, ARFF inspected the airplane and then proceeded to the FBO.

C-GBHQ, a privately registered, amateur built, Zenair CH601 on floats was conducting a recreational flight from Quamichan Lake water aerodrome (CML2), BC to Cowichan Lake (Honeymoon Bay), BC with only the pilot on board. While landing in gusty wind conditions, the aircraft made hard contact with the left float and the surface. The right float then contacted the surface and control of the aircraft was lost. It pivoted to the right and came to an abrupt stop. The aircraft remained upright in the lake on its belly with both the left and right floats having separated from the fuselage. The pilot and local boaters attempted to tow the aircraft to shore but were unsuccessful. The aircraft remained afloat for approximately 10 minutes before sinking. The pilot received minor injuries during the egress. The aircraft's emergency locator transmitter did not activate.The recovery team deployed diver's to the site but were unable to locate the fuselage. A sonar unit will be deployed to aid in the search.

C-GBTJ, a Cessna (Textron) 185 on floats operated by Wilderness Seaplanes Limited, was conducting a scheduled cargo flight from Port Hardy water aerodrome (CAW5), BC, to Minstrel Island, BC and Kingcome Inlet, BC, with only the pilot on board. During the downwind leg of the approach to Kingcome Inlet, the pilot noted the odour of smoke in the cockpit. Approximately 1 minute later, the pilot noticed smoke coming from the engine cowling. The pilot immediately turned to a final approach for the inlet. During the final approach, the smoke became thicker and forward visibility was obscured. The pilot had to open his door to be able to see to land the airplane. After landing, the pilot evacuated the aircraft and discharged the on-board fire extinguisher into the engine cowling through an access panel. The fire was extinguished. He was brought to shore by a nearby boater and later the airplane was towed to shore. Subsequent maintenance actions found significant fire damage between the engine and the firewall. The area of greatest damage was in the vicinity of the left-hand intake manifold, oil pressure hose, alternator, and the associated wiring harness leading to the voltage regulator.

C-GUAJ, a Cargo jet Airways 767-300, was conducting flight CJT1328 between New Tokyo Intl. (RJAA) Japan and Vancouver Intl. (CYVR) BC.  After take off,  the EICAS (Engine-indicating and crew-alerting system) message "R TAIL HYD VAL" in amber appeared. RJAA Tower reported smoke from the tail section on rotation before switching the flight crew to departure frequency. After flaps retraction flight crew requested to level off at 10000 feet (cleared altitude was 23000 feet), then reached QRH which reads "R TAIL FLT CONTROL SHUTOFF SWITCH MUST BE ON FOR FLIGHT". Flight Control Shutoff Valves on P61 panel indicated R TAIL SHUTOFF VALVE "ON" in white as well as "OFF" in amber. The switch is guarded and says "GND USE ONLY". Flight crew then contacted Maintenance control via Sat phone. Maintenance  suggestion was to do nothing with the shutoff valve. Other systems which could have been affected if the tail strike has occurred, such as hydraulics and cabin pressure looked normal. Flight crew also concluded, after discussion with maintenance, that the lack of the ''TAIL STRIKE EICAS'' message made the flight safe to destination . Before landing in YVR and after extending the gears, EICAS message "TAILSKID" in amber appeared. QRH actions were performed and uneventful landing was completed. Post-flight inspection by the Maintenance crew revealed the orange paint on the tail skid was partially removed but the indication on the strut showed no sign of compression.  Aircraft was returned to service with tail skid repair deferred on MEL (Minimum equipment list).

C-GTYI, a Cessna (Textron) 152 operated by Skyquest Aviation Ltd, was conducting a local training flight from the Langley (CYNJ), BC airport with one student pilot on board. The student conducted the flights' initial takeoff from Runway 25 practicing a soft field technique. As the aircraft became airborne its' pitch attitude remained nose high. Control of the aircraft was lost and it suddenly banked left and pitched nose down. The aircraft struck the grassed area between Runway 25 and Taxiway E. The left wing tip was the initial contact point followed by the nose and the right wing. The aircraft came to rest on its nose. The pilot exited the aircraft without assistance and received only minor injuries. A signal from the emergency locator transmitter was not received.After a maintenance inspection of the aircraft, it has been deemed destroyed.

C-GAMI, a Fairchild SA227-AC operated by Perimeter Aviation LP., was being prepared for flight JV1020 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Island Lake (CYIV), MB. During the loading of 2 small drums of UN1193 Methyl Ethyl Ketone (MEK), one of the drums struck a D-ring in the cabin floor and was damaged. Approximately 125 ml of MEK leaked into the aircraft. The drums were off-loaded. The operator's maintenance personnel cleaned up the spill and inspected the aircraft before returning it to service.

C-GTIJ, a Mooney M20C, was on a VFR flight plan from La Crete (CFN5), AB to Saskatoon (CYXE), SK via Slave Lake, AB (CYZH) and Lloydminster (CYLL), AB. The flight plan filed with NAV CANADA did not indicate that the aircraft would be stopping in either CYZH or CYLL. At approximately 10:35 MDT, a 406 MHz ELT signal was received from a location approximately 12 NM N of CYZH. Due to weather, delays in the search were encountered; the aircraft was found on 2 September 2021. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was found deceased. There was no post impact fire.

Air Canada flight ACA 410, a Boeing 787-8 (C-GHPV) aircraft was on route from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL) , QC was overhead Trenton (CYTR), ON when the first officers windscreen cracked. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and continued to CYUL where the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GJLS a WestJet B737-800 was conducting flight WJA712, from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON, executed a missed approach while on approach to runway 24L in Toronto due to a flap failure. The flight crew identified a flap asymmetry indication and carried out the associated checklist. The flight crew declared an emergency and the aircraft landed without further incident on runway 23 with emergency equipment on standby.Maintenance found the flap position indicator at fault, the indicator was replaced and the flap system was checked serviceable.

C-GRSF, un Pietenpol AirCamper de construction amateur, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR), depuis Neuville, QC (CNV9) à destination de Thetford Mines, QC (CSM3). Après le décollage, un détachement partiel du pare-brise de l'appareil est survenu et le pilote a effectué un retour vers CNV9. Lors de l'atterrissage, une rafale de vent a causé un contact inattendu d’une des roues du train principal avec le sol. L’avion a piqué du nez et a terminé sa course sur le dos. Le pilote, seul a bord, n’a pas été blessé.

C-GDSG, un appareil de type Beech 1900D exploité par SkyJet M.G., effectuait le vol LSJ607 selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de l'aéroport de Chevery (CYHR), QC à destination de La Romaine (CTT5), QC avec 16 passagers et 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Au départ de CYHR durant la course au décollage, le hublot de la sortie de secours avant droite (siège 4F) s’est détaché. L’équipage a constaté que le hublot était manquant lors de la montée initiale et est revenu atterrir à CYHR sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. Selon le département de maintenance, le hublot aurait subi une déformation due à la chaleur des gaz d’échappement du moteur droit alors que celui-ci a tourné au ralenti pour une période prolongée avec l'hélice en drapeau. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé.

C-ILKY, an Aero 360 Latina Itali S5 Velocity basic ultralight, was being operated at the Westlock (CES4), AB airport with just the pilot on board. The pilot was conducting high speed taxi runs and during the third high-speed taxi run along Runway 30 the aircraft became airborne. Reported winds were 350 degrees true at 7 knots. The pilot attempted to set the aircraft down on the runway; however, the aircraft bounced and began to porpoise. The pilot applied full power and commenced a go-around. While climbing, the aircraft began drifting to the left. The pilot then initiated a left turn, and during that turn, the aircraft stalled and entered a spin to the right. The aircraft descended approximately 250 feet and crashed through the roof of a hangar. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, received serious injuries; the ultralight was substantially damaged.

C-ITMP, a privately registered Quad City Ultralight Aircraft Corporation (Quad City) Challenger II advanced ultralight aircraft equipped with amphibious floats, was on a local flight along the southwest coast of Lake Ontario, with only the owner/pilot on board. While in cruise flight, the engine suddenly lost power. The pilot safely landed the aircraft parallel to the waves on Lake Ontario, approximately 300 meters from shore. After landing, the pilot unsuccessfully attempted to restart the engine and then sailed the aircraft to a beach on the shoreline. While beaching the aircraft, the breaking surf damaged the elevator pushrods. The owner has removed the Rotax engine and has arranged for an inspection to determine the cause of the sudden engine failure.

C-GPSQ, a Pilatus PC-12/45 aircraft operated by Chrono Aviation Inc, was conducting flight NDL765 from St John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL to Montreal Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC. Shortly after take-off a passenger became unruly and the crew decided to return to CYYT. ATC advised them that they were number 5 in the sequence to land and the crew declared an emergency and priority to land. The flight landed without incident.

C-GZSG, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA717 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 6 crew and 171 passengers on board. While established in cruise at FL340 over Lake Superior, the flight crew observed an "OIL FILTER BYPASS" caution for the No. 1 engine (CFM INTERNATIONAL, LEAP 1B27). The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist and shutdown the No. 1 engine and diverted into Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON. An uneventful single-engine approach and landing was performed with no further issue. The operator's maintenance personnel replaced the No. 1 engine oil-filter cartridge and engine driven oil pump. The scavenge oil screens were inspected and the oil system was flushed. Oil samples were collected and sent for analysis. The accessory gearbox was inspected with nil defects noted. The aircraft was released for service after satisfactory ground runs were completed. The operator submitted a service difficulty report (SDR) to Transport Canada.

C-IMAK, an Ultralight Designs 1ET EGO TRIKE aircraft, was conducting a local recreational flight from Pemberton Airport (CYPS), BC with only the pilot on board. While level at 3500 feet, the aircraft encountered an unexpected updraft and lost control. The aircraft appeared to suffer some structural damage and subsequently spun to impact the terrain. The pilot sustained serious injuries; the aircraft sustained substantial damage.The owner is recovering the aircraft.

C-GDWM, an Airbus Helicopters AS 350 B-2 helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited, was conducting crew movements and slinging operations between Johanson Lake, BC, and Kliyul drilling camp. During routine daily operations, the aircraft was incorrectly refueled with automotive diesel from a fuel tank at Johanson Lake; once with 258 litres and a second time with 158 litres. The aircraft completed 7.3 hours of flight time including a medevac flight to Smithers Heliport (CAA6), BC, where the aircraft was correctly refueled with Jet A-1. During a conversation with the job foreman, the pilot recognized the fueling error and the aircraft was grounded at the Kliyul drilling camp approximately 20 hours after the initial diesel contamination. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft. The operator is consulting the engine manufacturer for the required maintenance actions. The diesel and Jet A-1 fuel tanks at Johanson Lake are identical in appearance and construction, and are in close proximity to each other. Additionally, the diesel fuel tank  was labelled with both a Jet A-1 written placard and a diesel fuel UN number placard (UN1202); the Jet A-1 fuel tank was labelled only with a turbine engine aviation fuel UN number placard (UN1863). Both fuel tanks were owned by another helicopter operator.The Jet A-1 written placard that was on the diesel tank has since been covered and the correct written placards with the fuel type will be added to each tank.Update: The operator completed all maintenance and testing requirements outlined by the engine manufacturer and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FATW, an Air Tindi de Havilland DHC-6 SERIES 300 Twin Otter, was conducting flight TIN606 from Whati (CEM3), NT to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT. While enroute the flight crew identified that the flaps had not fully retracted. The hydraulic pressure was indicating 0 and the flaps were retracted manually. The flight crew declared an emergency on approach to CYZF and conducted a successful flapless landing on Runway 10. The aircraft was shut down on the taxiway and towed to the ramp.

C-GCJT, a Cargo jet Airways 757-200 was conducting flight CJT1819 between Vancouver Intl (CYVR) BC to Los Angeles Intl (KLAX) CA.  During cruise at FL 410 in vicinity of Portand Intl. (KPDX) OR,  Flight Crew received a R ENG OVHT EICAS (Engine-indicating and crew-alerting system) message, shutdown the engine as per QRH procedure and declared a Pan Pan with ATC.  The flight diverted to CYVR where it landed on one engine without further incident.Maintenance update: Upon return to base the aircraft was removed from service. Through troubleshooting and inspections, the Pressure Relief Valve on the Bleed Air Pre-Cooler was at fault. The valve was installed and function checks were carried out with no fault. A Fleet Campaign Directive (FCD) will be issued to all the B757's to carry out a Detailed Visual Inspection (DVI) of the Bleed Air Pre-Cooler, Pressure Relief Valve installation. During maintenance troubleshooting the AME noted the RH strut reducer and pressure relief valve had backed out of cooler. An SDR was submitted 2021-0831016

C-GPWE, a WestJet Encore Bombardier DHC-8-402, was conducting flight WEN3232 from Abbotsford International (CYXX), BC to Calgary International (CYYC), AB. During the approach into CYYC the #2 Hydraulic ISO valve caution light illuminated in the flight deck. The pilots completed the QRH which led to a successful manual gear extension. A PAN PAN was declared with ATC and the flight was set up for a visual approach to RWY 17L. The flight landed safely and stopped on the runway for an ARFF inspection. The aircraft was taxied to the gate and was met by maintenance personnel.

C-FPMH, a Piper PA-44-180 registered to Waterloo-Wellington Flying Club, was conducting a local training flight at Kitchener/Waterloo Airport (CYKF), ON, with 2 persons on-board. While on the downwind leg for landing at CYKF, the landing gear was selected down however, it failed to extend and the gear unsafe warning light was illuminated. The pilot in command (PIC) performed a manual gear extension and the gear indication lights indicated that the gear was down and in the locked position. As a precaution the PIC asked for the emergency vehicles to be standing by for their landing. The aircraft landed safely at 1700 EDT and taxied to the apron. A maintenance inspection was completed and found that a gear motor brush solder joint failed. The joint was re-soldered and the aircraft was returned to service after successful gear testing.

C-FFJE, a privately registered Cessna 170B was conducting a flight from Fort St. John/ North Peace Regional (CYXJ), BC on Runway 12 bound for Fort Nelson/ Northern Rockies Regional (CYYE), BC. The take off was aborted during the take-off roll due to the crosswind. As the aircraft was coming to a stop the left landing gear collapsed and the aircraft came to rest on the left wing tip. There was a small fuel spill that was contained but there was no post incident fire. There were no injuries.

The Sunwest Aviation Ltd. Bombardier BD-100-1A10 (CL35), C-FMIX, was operating as CNK350 on a flight from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Calgary (CYYC), AB with 2 flight crew and 1 passenger on board. During the initial climb, the flight crew experienced a horizontal trim malfunction. Power to the horizontal trim was shut down and the STAB TRIM FAIL checklist was run. After all QRH procedures were carried out a PAN PAN was broadcast and ATS was made aware of the situation. Adjustments to loading were made in the cabin and the decision was made to continue the flight to CYYC. As the aircraft approached CYYC a request was made for a long downwind to configure the aircraft. A flaps 10, Vref plus 30 approach was carried out to an uneventful landing. ARFF met the aircraft and confirmed there was no issues with the brakes and the aircraft was taxied to the hangar.Maintenance findings: Maintenance determined that the Copilot trim was stuck in the nosed down position internally. They are still working with Bombardier to resolve the issue. AW300-27-0388 Rev 1 addresses a similar situation.

C-GVDG, un Pilatus PC-12/45 exploité par Chrono Aviation inc. sous l'indicatif NDL321, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aérodrome de Kirkland Lake (CYKX), ON à destination de Chute-St-Philippe (CCP3), QC avec 5 passagers et 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de l’approche pour la piste 15, l’équipage a entendu un bruit venant de la droite de l’aéronef. L’équipage a continué l’approche et une fois au sol, ils ont constaté que l’aile droite avait été endommagée. Il a été constaté que de grands conifères se trouvaient sous l’approche de la piste 15 et que ceux-ci étaient plus haut que ceux visibles près du seuil de piste 33. Une inspection a été conduite et l’aéronef a pu être amené à Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU), Qc sur un vol de convoyage.

C-FRQM, an Embraer ERJ 170-200SU aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA7460 from Montreal Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Charlottetown Airport, (CYYG), PEI. Upon landing the crew felt a shimmy when applying the brakes and deceleration was not as expected. When further brake application was applied, the brakes locked up briefly. The FSS reported seeing a puff of smoke coming from the landing gear. After shutdown, the groundcrew advised that there was smoke and fluid coming from the left main landing gear. ARFF responded to monitor the situation while the passengers deplaned. The crew inspected the left main landing gear and noticed that one of the pistons was bent and the disc had come off. Maintenance and dispatch were advised. Maintenance replaced the No.2 brake and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPCF, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Saab 340B (SF34) was conducting flight PCO3049 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Comox (CYQQ), BC with 3 flight crew members and 30 passengers on board. Approximately 10 minutes after departure, when in level flight at 6000 feet above sea level, the flight crew received intermittent indications of low oil pressure in the right engine (General Electric CT7-9B). Shortly thereafter, the oil pressure in the right engine decreased to less than 30 psi; the associated oil pressure warning light remained illuminated. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with air traffic control (ATC) and initiated a diversion to CYVR. The flight crew then shut down the right engine and declared a MAYDAY with ATC. The flight landed without further incident. There were no injuries.Subsequent maintenance activities by the operator found that the oil pressure loss was due to the oil lines leading to the engine's differential oil pressure sensor (P/N IPTE-119-1000-200D-1) having loose connections. The aircraft has since been returned to service.

C-GPGR, a Beech King air BE20 aircraft operated by Provincial Aerospace Ltd, was conducting surveillance flight SPR006 from St John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL to St Anthony Airport, (CYAY), NL. An hour and a half into the flight, the crew decided to return to CYYT, due to an onboard radar equipment issue. While planning the approach, the crew noticed fluid streaming from the No.1 engine, behind the propeller and the vent from the top of the cowling. All engine indications were normal. Due to another inbound aircraft who requested priority due to a medical emergency, the crew decided to declare an emergency to avoid a delay. The aircraft landed without incident and taxied to the ramp.Maintenance inspected the No.1 engine and discovered oil leaking from the engine torque transmitter and a damaged O-ring. The O-ring was replaced, a ground run was completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FPEN, a de Havilland DHC-3T equipped with tundra tires and operated by Ookpik Aviation Inc., was conducting a flight from Ferguson Lake NU to Baker Lake (CYBK) NU. During cruise flight at approximately 53 NM north east of Ferguson Lake, the pilot noticed the engine (TPE331-10R-511C) began to surge. The pilot turned on the continuous ignition, fuel pump and confirmed the fuel quantity in the front and center fuel tanks and the surging subsided. After approximately 30 seconds the engine started to surge again and quit. The pilot attempted to restart the engine on a different fuel tank but was unsuccessful. A forced landing was carried out on an esker with no damage to the aircraft and no injuries to the pilot and one passenger.The operator's maintenance is inspecting the aircraft and has removed the engine.

C-FLWX, a Cessna 650 aircraft, registered to Private Air Inc., was conducting flight FSY705 from Teterboro Airport (KTEB), NJ, USA to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl Airport (CYYZ), ON. While on approach for runway 24L at CYYZ, the flight crew selected the landing gear down and received a green safe indication on each main gear, however, did not receive a green safe indication for the nose gear. ATC was advised, a missed approach was conducted and the aircraft was vectored to allow the crew to trouble shoot the situation. After running through the items on the emergency checklist, the flight crew still did not have a green safe indication for the nose gear. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and requested that aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) be standing by for the landing. The aircraft was vectored for approach for runway 24L at CYYZ; touched down on the runway at 21:22 EDT and came to a stop on the runway. ARFF made a preliminary inspection of the landing gear and indicated they saw no issue. After completing the after landing checklist and shutting down the engines while on the runway, the nose gear was inspected by the crew. The aircraft subsequently taxied to the ramp. The green nose gear indicator light illuminated prior to shutdown at the FBO. Update: Maintenance replaced the nose landing gear down indication switch assembly in accordance with maintenance manual procedures.

C-GPIM, a Cessna 310 R operated by Mitchinson Flying Service, was conducting a flight from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE) SK. to Lynn Lake (CYYL) MB. At approximately 45 NM northeast of Prince Albert (Glass Field) (CYPA) SK., the pilot noticed a fuel leak from the right hand engine (IO-520-MB). The pilot requested a return to CYXE; however, after assessing the situation, the pilot declared an emergency, requested to land at CYPA, and shut down the right hand engine. The aircraft landed without further incident in CYPA with fire and EMS on standby. The operator's maintenance inspected the right hand engine and found a loose fitting on a fuel line. All fitting were inspected, a run-up was performed, and no further defects found. The aircraft was returned to service and flown back to CYXE without incident.

C-GNAJ, a Beech 1900D operated by Alkan Air Limited, was conducting a re-positioning flight from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, with 2 pilots on board. Immediately after takeoff, the crew smelled and saw smoke coming from the circuit breaker panel in the right hand footwell. The pilots opted to keep the landing gear down and the flaps in the takeoff position and returned to CYVR. The smoke dissipated and the aircraft landed safely with no reported damage to the aircraft and no injuries. ARFF met the aircraft on the ramp and completed an inspection of the cockpit using a thermal scanner with no fire indicated.  Maintenance inspected all instrument and circuit breaker wiring in the cockpit with no faults found. The aircraft was then powered up for 2 hours followed by a 15 minute ground run and the smoke could not be duplicated. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GMYU, an Airbus 220-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA612 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Halifax Stanfield International Airport, (CYHZ), NS. In cruise, the crew received an EICAS message for the hydraulic No.3 low pressure. The checklist was completed and the quantity and temperature were normal. In consultation with maintenance and dispatch, the crew declared a PAN-PAN. Upon landing the aircraft was stopped on the runway, while ARFF inspected. The aircraft taxied to the gate without further incident. Maintenance replaced the input / output line replacement module 12 and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-IWBN, a privately operated Murphy Rebel advanced ultralight, was conducting a flight from Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International Airport (CYXC), BC, to an abandoned airstrip at Sage Creek, BC, with 1 pilot on board. During a slow descent at 1300 feet AGL, the engine (Rotax 912ULS)  made an escalating high pitched whine that was followed by a complete engine failure within approximately 5 seconds. The pilot performed a forced landing on a logging road without engine power. The left wing contacted trees during the landing roll instigating a ground loop which caused the aircraft veer off of the logging road as it came to a stop. The pilot was not injured and the aircraft was substantially damaged.An engine teardown found that the piston failed in the #2 cylinder. The annual inspection, including an engine borescope and dynamic vibration analysis, was completed 3 flight hours prior to the accident with no faults found in the engine.

C-FCMR, a Central Mountain Air Beech (Textron) 1900D was operating as flight GLR728 from Prince George (CYXS), BC to Kelowna (CYLW), BC, with 2 crew members and 12 passengers on board. The initial approach, approximately 24 nautical miles North of CYLW, was in the vicinity of the White Rock Lake forest fire. The flight experienced severe turbulence in instrument meteorological conditions while in descent between 12000 feet and 11000 feet above sea level. The flight crew discontinued the approach. The flight diverted to Penticton (CYYF), BC, and landed without further incident. There were no injuries. See occurrences A21P0085 and A21P0086 in relation to the same turbulence event

C-GGFP, a Jazz Aviation LP. De Havilland DHC-8-402, operating as flight JZA416, was en route from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC, to Kelowna (CYLW), BC, with 4 crew members and 38 passengers on board. The initial approach, approximately 23 nautical miles North of CYLW, was in the vicinity of the White Rock Lake forest fire. During this approach, the flight experienced severe turbulence in instrument meteorological conditions while in descent through 10000 feet above sea level. The flight crew discontinued the approach. The flight diverted to CYVR and landed without further incident. There were no injuries. Subsequent to the flight, maintenance actions included a severe turbulence inspection with no faults being found. The aircraft was returned to service.See occurrences A21P0085 and A21P0087 in relation to the same turbulence event.

C-FQWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-402, operating as flight WEN3324, en route from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC, to Kelowna (CYLW), BC, with 4 crew members and 46 passengers on board. The flight's initial approach, approximately 24 nautical miles north of CYLW, was in the vicinity of the White Rock Lake forest fire. During the approach, the flight experienced severe turbulence in instrument meteorological conditions while in descent through 9500 feet above sea level. The flight crew discontinued the approach. The flight diverted to CYVR and landed without further incident. There were no injuries. Subsequent maintenance actions included a severe turbulence inspection; no faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.See occurrences A21P0086 and A21P0087 in relation to the same turbulence event

The privately registered Cessna 180K, C-GYXX, was departing Drumheller (CEG4), AB regional airport for a flight to Cooking Lake (CEZ3), AB. During the take-off roll, when the tail came up, control was lost and the aircraft performed a ground loop, coming to rest inverted on the edge of the runway. The two occupants were uninjured and able to exit the aircraft without assistance. There was no fire and the ELT did not broadcast and was switched to the off position.

C-FDCM, un appareil de type Piper PA-24 en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aérodrome de Burlington executive, ON (CZBA), à destination de l’aérodrome de Neuville, QC (CNV9) avec le pilote à bord. Lors de la première approche, la vitesse était élevée et le pilote a effectué une remontée. Lors de la deuxième approche, l'avertissement de train non descendu a sonné à quelques pieds au dessus de la piste et l’aéronef s’est posé avec le train rentré. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. L’appareil a subi des dommages.

C-GEFA an Air Canada A330 conducting flight ACA0910 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL) Florida - was on approach to KFLL when the flight crew received a TCAS RA to "Descend", the resolution advisory (RA) was followed and flight continued to land without further incident.

C-FSIQ an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 conducting flight ACA0515 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Chicago O'Hare International Airport- (KORD) IL, USA - While on approach, the flight crew received TCAS RA "Monitor Vertical Speed", The Resolution Advisory (RA) was followed and cleared and the flight continued to land without further incident.

C-GHNC, a private Cessna 172M, was en route to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON.  While in the vicinity of Ignace (CJN3), ON, the pilot needed to make a stop in Ignace. The landing in Ignace was uneventful. When the pilot returned to the aircraft, he was unable to start the engine. He exited the aircraft and was able to successfully hand prop the aircraft.  Once the engine started, the aircraft began to move rapidly across the ramp and the pilot was unable to re-board the aircraft.  The aircraft traveled across the runway, crashed through a gate and caught fire. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GLYO, an Airspan Helicopters Limited Bell 212HP, was conducting water bucketing operations 45 nautical miles east-northeast of Williams Lake Airport (CYWL), BC, with 1 pilot on board. During initial approach to a water source, the pilot felt stiffness in the tail rotor pedals and aborted the approach to diagnose the problem. Shortly thereafter, the pilot felt stiffness in the cyclic and collective that was followed by an audible bang and a squealing noise. The helicopter hydraulic caution light illuminated on the caution panel and the pilot confirmed the #1 hydraulic pressure gauge was indicating below normal operating pressure. The pilot communicated the hydraulic problem to a Bell 206 helicopter pilot operating in the vicinity and then selected the #1 hydraulic system switch to the OFF position. The stiffness felt in the cyclic and collective controls subsided while the tail rotor pedals remained stiff for the remainder of the flight. The Bell 206 pilot transmitted a MAYDAY message to the fire centre and assisted the incident pilot in finding a suitable landing location. The Bell 212 pilot performed a successful precautionary landing in a farmer's field and the MAYDAY was canceled. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft.Maintenance discovered a ruptured hydraulic pressure line immediately downstream of the #1 hydraulic pump. Additional investigation revealed metallic debris in the pressure and return ports of the #1 hydraulic integrated valve assembly.

The Delta Helicopters Ltd. Bell 206B, C-GOPF, was involved in longline operations 56 nm NNE of Slave Lake (CYZH), AB with one pilot on board. While slinging a 115 liter drum, the load was unintentionally released from a height of 75 feet, approximately 30 meters from the departure point. The pilot checked the position of the remote release switch which was in the appropriate position for flight. He then returned to the departure point and shutdown the aircraft. The longline hook was inspected by the pilot and no obvious reason for the release was apparent. The longline and hook have been removed from service and further investigation is being carried out. The spill site was contained and remediated.

Le Boeing 737-200 immatriculé C-GNLN exploité par Les Investissements Nolinor Inc. sous l’indicatif NRL951 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Val d’Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de Montréal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX). Vers la fin de la montée pour le niveau de vol FL230, l’équipage a entendu un « bang ». Peu de temps après, il a constaté que le moteur #1 était en perte de puissance et que l’indicateur de pression d’huile était à la baisse. L’équipage a décidé de fermer le moteur #1 par mesure de précaution et a déclaré une urgence au centre de contrôle terminal. L’aéronef a poursuivi sa route en direction de CYMX où il a atterri sans encombre. Lors de l'inspection visuelle du moteur #1, des dommages ont pu être observés et étaient limités aux sections T1-T4 de la turbine.

C-GATX, un hélicoptère Airbus AS350B2 exploité par Les Hélicoptères Canadiens Ltée, effectuait un vol local de transport d’une charge à l’élingue selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le camp Elmer, situé à environ 35 mille marins ENE de l’aérodrome Eastmain River, QC (CZEM). Après avoir déposé la charge au sol, le pilote a appuyé sur le bouton qui a ouvert le crochet électrique de l’hélicoptère au lieu d’appuyer sur le bouton déclenchant l’ouverture du crochet électrique au bout de l’élingue. L’élingue a donc été larguée et est tombée au sol sans autre conséquence.

C-GYLD, a Rockwell International Commander 690B aircraft operated by Mag Aerospace Canada as flight BD160, began its takeoff roll on Runway 12 at Thunder Bay (CYQT) ON with only the pilot on board. Shortly after rotation, the aircraft rolled into a left bank, continued to roll, and then struck the surface of Runway 07 in an inverted attitude. The pilot sustained fatal injuries. The aircraft was destroyed by the impact and a post-impact fire. AARF responded and Runway 12 and 07 were closed. The TSB deployed investigators and the investigation is ongoing.

C-IHJZ, un ultra-léger de base privé Airborne Windsports XT-912 effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue avec un passager à son bord depuis l’aérodrome de St-Georges, QC (CYSG). Alors que l’aéronef effectuait un survol à basse altitude, l’aéronef s’est mis à descendre et a percuté le sol. Après avoir rebondi, il est entré en collision avec le sol latéralement et s’est renversé. Le pilote et le passager ont subi des blessures mineures et ont été transportés à l’hôpital.

C-GGOX, un planeur Lange 18S privé effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à destination de l’aéroport de Hawkesbury, ON (CNV4) avec 1 pilote à bord. Lors du survol de la région d’Huberdeau, QC, les courants ascendants s’affaiblissaient et le pilote a décidé de revenir vers CNV4. Entre 6 à 8 NM au nord de CNV4, l’aéronef est entré dans un secteur de courants descendants et a perdu de l'altitude au point que la poursuite du vol vers CNV4 est devenue rapidement impossible. Le pilote a décidé de se poser dans un champ à environ 7 NM au nord-nord-ouest de CNV4. Lors de l’atterrissage en direction sud, l’aéronef a fait un bond à cause d'une crête qui n’avait pas été aperçue par le pilote et s’est reposé plus loin dans le champ. Face à la faible distance restante avant d'atteindre la bordure des arbres, le pilote a fait tourner l’aéronef pour tenter de minimiser l’impact avec ceux-ci. L’aile gauche a frappé les arbres et la roue principale s’est brisée. Le pilote a subit des blessures mineures et l'aéronef a subi des dommages importants.

C-GARI, un Piper PA-23-250 exploité par Cargair Ltée., effectuait un vol d’entraînement selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec un pilote en formation et un instructeur à son bord. Alors que l’aéronef était en approche pour effectuer un atterrissage sur la piste 24R, le moteur de gauche a commencé à vibrer. L’instructeur a constaté des variations de puissance importantes et a décidé de fermer le moteur de gauche par mesure de précaution. Une urgence a été déclarée lorsque l’aéronef était à 3 milles nautiques du seuil de la piste 24R. L’aéronef a atterri sans encombre et les services d’urgence ont été annulés.

C-GCIJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. B767-300, was operating as flight CJT980, a flight from London Heathrow (EGLL), United Kingdom, to Hamilton/John C. Munro Int'l Airport (CYHM), Ontario, with two crew members on board. During the initial climb the crew received an indication of low hydraulic quantity on the Centre hydraulic system. The appropriate checklists were completed, and in consultation with the operator, the decision was made to continue the flight to CYHM. During descent, approximately 30nm WSW of Ottawa, Ontario, the crew declared MAYDAY with Toronto Centre. The flight landed on runway 30 in YHM without incident at at 1944 EDT and was towed to the gate.An inspection of the aircraft revealed that a filter cap had failed on the Spoiler Power Control Actuator in position #8. The actuator unit, case drain, and pressure filters were replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GIPL, an Air Spray 1967 Limited Gulfstream Commander (Twin Commander) 695B, operating as flight ASB062, was conducting fire suppression operations from Prince George International Airport (CYXS), BC, with 2 crew members on board. During the operation southwest of CYXS, the crew became aware of a possible hydraulic failure. Within a short time, the hydraulic failure was confirmed with reference to the hydraulic pressure gauge. The crew completed the hydraulic failure checklist and decided to return to CYXS. As the aircraft approached CYXS, the crew completed the landing gear emergency extension checklist and declared an emergency with the CYXS tower. The aircraft landed safely with ARFF on standby. There were no injuries. A maintenance inspection determined that the auxiliary hydraulic pressure switch had a leak which caused a loss of hydraulic pressure. This pressure loss resulted in damage to the engine driven hydraulic pump due to lack of lubrication. The switch and pump were replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSQQ, a privately registered Backcountry Super Cubs LLC Mackey SQ2 with amphibious floats, was conducting a takeoff from Long Lake ON. with the pilot and one passenger on board. As the aircraft climbed above the height of the trees adjacent to the lake, approximately 40 feet above the water, the left wing dropped abruptly and the aircraft entered a steep descent and impacted the water nose first. The occupants exited the aircraft after it overturned and were soon picked up by local boaters. There were no injuries. The aircraft was significantly damaged.

C-FFUE, a privately registered Bushcaddy R80 floatplane, was conducting local flights from the Orillia/Lake St John Seaplane Base (CNV6), Ontario. After landing in a sheltered bay, the pilot taxied the aircraft into the main part of the lake to conduct a takeoff into wind. After applying power, and with the aircraft on the step, the pilot raised the right float, a technique used to facilitate a shorter takeoff run. As the right float came out of the water, the pilot lost directional control and the aircraft turned abruptly to the left, where the left wing struck the water as the pilot brought the throttle to idle. As the aircraft returned to a level attitude, the right float impacted the water and became detached from the aircraft. The pilot and passenger egressed from the left side of the aircraft and entered the water. They were rescued a short time later by nearby boaters. There were no injuries. The aircraft came to rest upside down in the water and was eventually towed to shore.

C-FNQL, un planeur Aviacija LAK-17B FES privé effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aérodrome Paquet/St-Raymond, QC (CSK5). Lors de son retour vers CSK5, l’altitude du planeur était insuffisante pour permettre d'atteindre le seuil de la piste 09 et le planeur a heurté les arbres à environ 700 pieds avant le seuil de la piste. Le pilote a été gravement blessé. Le planeur a été détruit.

Un ultra-léger de type évolué Norman Aviation - NORDIC II privé effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis une piste privée gazonnée de Roxton Falls, QC avec le pilote seul à bord. Selon les informations recueillies, le moteur de l’aéronef de marque Subaru aurait eu des ratés lors de la montée initiale et l’aéronef n’aurait pas pris d’altitude. Peu de temps après, l’aile droite de l’aéronef est entrée en collision avec la cime d’un arbre situé sur le terrain privé d’une ferme à 0.6 mille marin au nord-nord-ouest de son point de départ. L’aile droite s’est détachée et l’aéronef a percuté le sol près d’un bâtiment. Le pilote a été trouvé à l’extérieur de l’aéronef par les premiers répondants et la ceinture de sécurité était détachée. Une antenne de radiobalise de repérage d’urgence (ELT) était fixée sur le fuselage, mais aucune ELT ni fil de raccordement n’étaient installés. Du carburant était présent dans les réservoirs. Le fil d’une des bougies d’allumage et le fil de la bobine d'allumage ont été trouvés déconnectés. Les pales de l’hélice ne présentaient pas les dommages typiques d’une collision avec un objet alors qu’elles étaient en rotation. Il n’y a pas eu d’incendie. Le pilote a été mortellement blessé.

C-FMHQ, un Cessna P206A exploité par Parachutisme Adrénaline inc., effectuait un vol de largage de parachutistes depuis l’aéroport de Trois Rivières, Québec (CYRQ). Lors de la course à l’atterrissage, une perte de contrôle directionnel de l’aéronef est survenue et celui-ci a terminé sa course dans la partie gazonnée de la bande de piste. L’aéronef a subi des dommages à l’hélice et le pilote, seul à bord, n’a pas été blessé.

C-GURG, un Canadair CL60 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, qui effectuait le vol QUE10 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean-Lesage Intl., QC (CYQB) à destination de Val d'Or, Québec (CYVO). En approche pour l’atterrissage, lorsque le train d’atterrissage a été sélectionné en position baissée, l'équipage a reçu une indication anormale que le train principal droit n’était pas verrouillé. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été suivie et l'équipage a décidé de se diriger vers CYQB. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil s'est posé sur la piste sans encombre. Le personnel de l'entretien de l'exploitant  a changé les ampoules des indicateurs de position des roues et de rétraction.

C-GJJX, an Air Tractor AT-802 operated by Forest Protection Limited, operating as Tanker 624, was conducting forest fire fighting operations out of the Miramichi (CYCH), NB Airport with 1 crew member on board. At approximately 1553 ADT, while conducting the fourth bombing run of the day, the aircraft impacted the hillside of a heavily wooded area of northern New Brunswick. The pilot sustained minor injuries and was able to walk to a nearby road, where he was taken by helicopter and ambulance to a local hospital.There was no post accident fire, however, the aircraft was destroyed.UPDATED 05 AUGUST 2022

C-FDJA, a Bombardier CRJ 200 aircraft operated by Jazz was conducting flight JZA8790 from Montréal–Trudeau International Airport, QC (CYUL) to Saint John Airport, NB (CYSJ). At approximately 10:25 AST the aircraft was descending through FL250 at approximately 96 NM W of CYSJ when the crew noted a gradual loss of cabin pressurization. They made contact with the Moncton Area Control Center (YQM ACC) to declare PAN PAN and provided details on the nature of the problem. Working through the QRH and Emergency checklist enabled the crew to stabilize the cabin altitude by switching from Auto to Manual mode. Subsequent contact was made with YQM ACC to advise that the pressurization issue was under control and the crew requested to downgrade from PAN PAN status to regular flight status. The aircraft landed safely at about 10:55 AST. None of the passengers or crew were physically affected by the loss of pressurization control.Company maintenance determined that the RH Outflow Valve was not closing fully. The secondary outflow valve and the Cabin Pressure Selector Panel were replaced and the aircraft was returned to service. Maintenance has submitted an SDR to Transport Canada.

C-FYZF, a Aerospatiale AS350 B3 helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters Ltd., was conducting heli-slinging operations from the Yellowknife Airport, NT (CYZF) with one crew member on board. Approximately 1.5 nm SW of CYZF after departure, the ATC tower observed an object fall from the net to the ground and informed the pilot. The pilot returned to staging area at CYZF to confirm the rest of the load was inside the net and secure before departing again.

C-IMMS, a private float equipped Quad City Ultralight Aircraft Challenger II advanced ultralight with only the owner/pilot on board, departed from a floatplane base on the St. Mary's River (11nm East of the Sault Ste. Marie Airport, CYAM),ON for a local flight. While in cruise flight at approximately 1200 feet above ground, the engine lost power and the pilot attempted a landing along the shoreline of Lake George. During the landing, the aircrafts floats dug in and the aircraft overturned and sank.  The pilot egressed the overturned aircraft and was picked up by nearby boaters. The pilot received minor injuries.

During operations in support of police activity approximately 1.5nm NW of Toronto Buttonville Airport (CYKZ), Ontario, a DJI Matrice 210 RPAS operated by the York Regional Police, collided with C-GKWL, a C172 operated by Canadian Flyers International Inc., which was on final approach to runway 15 at CYKZ with an instructor and student pilot on board. The collision occurred along the approach path for Runway 15. There was minor damage to the propeller of the aircraft and the left hand side of the lower nose cowling was significantly deformed. The aircraft landed without incident. There were no injuries to the pilots or to persons on the ground. The RPAS was destroyed.

C-GPHQ, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B2 helicopter operated by Yellowhead Helicopters Limited, was conducting long-line operations with only the pilot on board. While moving an external load of two items in a cargo net, a rope on the net broke causing one item to release from the net and fall to the ground. No one was injured and the location was noted from GPS so the item could be retrieved.

C-FLKI, un Boeing 737-800 Max (B7M8) exploité par Flair Airlines sous l'indicatif FLE635, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ) avec 79 passagers et 6 membres d’équipage. Lors du refoulement de la barrière 47 au départ de CYUL, l’ailette Scimitar de bout d'aile droite a heurté une clôture. L’appareil a été ramené à la barrière et les passagers sont débarqués normalement. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et les dommages étaient limités à l’ailette de bout d’aile.

C-FCAG, a Cessna Citation 560 Ultra aircraft operated by Chartright Air as HRT510, was departing from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Philadelphia International Airport (KPHL), USA, with 2 crew and 1 passenger on board. During the takeoff roll on runway 23, the aircraft reached V1 speed and subsequently VR; when the pilot attempted to rotate the aircraft, there was no response to his pitch input. The crew aborted the takeoff, reduced thrust to idle, and activated the thrust reversers. Minimal braking was required and the aircraft exited the runway on taxiway J2 where they stopped the aircraft. The crew heard two popping sounds in succession, and felt the aircraft settle. They looked back at the wheels and observed a glowing red brake on the LH side, and fire on the RH main wheel and tire. The crew advised ATC that they were evacuating on the taxiway, and proceeded to exit the aircraft with the passenger. ARFF responded and extinguished the fire. Both main landing gear tires had failed, and there was significant heat damage to the brakes. There was no indication of any malfunction with the flight controls of the aircraft. The TSB deployed two investigators to the occurrence.

C-FSJH, an Air Canada Boeing 737 Max 8, was operating as flight ACA225 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Vancouver (CYVR), BC with 6 crew and 90 passengers on board. In cruise flight at 40 000 feet above sea level, the flight crew noticed an electrical odour in the flight deck. They followed the 'FUME EVENT CHECKLIST', donned oxygen masks, and declared a PAN-PAN emergency with air traffic services. ACA225 continued to CYVR and landed without incident approximately 35 minutes later. The aircraft stopped on the runway for an inspection by aircraft rescue and fire fighting. The aircraft was cleared and taxied to the gate. Company maintenance crews inspected numerous systems but could neither find any fault nor replicate the smell.

C-GZIV, an Aerospatiale AS350 B3 helicopter, operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited (CHL), was dispatched to fire #G12340 approx. 36nm SSW of Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC. Shortly after starting water bucketing operations on the fire, the pilot smelled an acrid smoke. He elected to terminate the operation and pulled out of the dip, released the water in the bucket, and the smell of smoke became stronger. He initiated a 360 degree turn to assess whether the helicopter was on fire, and as he pulled out of the turn, acrid smoke started to billow over the instrument panel. He immediately turned off all unnecessary electronics and headed for the cut-block area where he'd previously set down, and declared an emergency. Once over the cut-block (approx. 3/4-1 km from the fire), he set the bucket down, released the longline, landed, and shut down. After doing an initial inspection he contacted the CHL aircraft maintenance engineer. The directional gyro was discovered to have failed and the rear of the instrument was split. The Company will file a Service Difficulty Report (SDR) with Transport Canada.

C-FSIL, a Boeing 737-8 operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA133 from Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), Toronto, ON to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. During the cruise, at approximately 650 nm from their destination CYYC, the crew received an amber oil pressure indication and a drop in oil quantity on the right engine. The crew declared a PAN PAN and diverted to CYWG where it landed without incident.

C-IDFZ, a Progressive Aerodyne Searey-95 amphibious advanced ultralight, was departing Wetaskiwin, AB (CEX3) on a local flight. The aircraft was downwind when the engine (Rotax 912UL) began to lose power. The pilot chose to conduct an orbit on the downwind leg to allow another aircraft to take off before returning to land. The engine continued surging and the airspeed decayed. On high final for the runway the aircraft departed controlled flight and entered an incipient spin. Just prior to ground contact the aircraft clipped a tree which righted the aircraft and it struck the ground upright. The pilot was severely injured and the aircraft was destroyed. There was no fire and the ELT did not activate.

C-FSBV, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was conducting flight ACA1254 from Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) Toronto, ON to Norman Manley International Airport (MKJP) Kingston, Jamaica. While climbing through Cleveland-Hopkins (KCLE),OH, the flight crew received a TCAS RA "traffic, traffic". The flight crew levelled off at FL330, advised ATC and continued to MKJP without further incident.

C-GGGN, a Cessna 152 operated by the Pacific Flying Club, was conducting circuits at Vancouver / Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC with one student pilot on board. Immediately after touchdown, the aircraft began to porpoise. In the subsequent hard landing, the nose gear collapsed, the propeller struck the runway surface, and the aircraft came to a halt on the runway. The pilot was not injured.The aircraft was towed from the runway by company maintenance. The initial inspection revealed damage to the propeller, the engine and its mounts, and the nose gear assembly. The aircraft has been removed from service pending further assessment.

C-GKAJ, a Beechcraft A100 King Air was conducting Thunder Airlines flight THU107 from Timmins Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON to Moosonee Airport (CYMO), ON. After an unsuccessful first approach to land for Runway 06, THU107 conducted a second approach for Runway 24. After touchdown, the aircraft continued along the runway and came to a stop approximate 50 feet beyond the threshold of Runway 06. There were no injuries to the 9 persons onboard. Heavy rain was reported in the vicinity of the airport at the time of approach and landing.

C-FTXK, a Canadair CL-215 operated by Gouvernement du Québec (Service aérien gouvernemental), was conducting a flight from Dryden Regional (CYHD) ON. to The Pas (CYQD) MB. When applying power for takeoff, the right engine (Pratt and Whitney-USA R2800 CA3) shutdown, the propeller feathered, and the takeoff was discontinued.The operator's maintenance found that the accelerating pump on the carburetor was at fault. The unit was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GGNY, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Dash 8-402,was operating as flight JZA8281 from Prince Rupert (CYPR), BC to Vancouver (CYVR), BC with 4 crew and 42 passengers on board. While in cruise at 25 000 feet ASL cabin pressure was lost. The flight crew performed an emergency descent to 14 000 feet ASL, advised ATC, and vectors were given for terrain clearance. JZA8281 later descended to 10 000 feet ASL where they were able to regain pressurization and continued to CYVR.  A few passengers experienced discomfort with their ears popping. Jazz Aircraft Maintenance advised that a leak was found at the aft baggage door inflatable seal. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR 20210805003) was submitted to Transport Canada on 05 August 2021.

C-GNGV an Air Canada A220 operating flight ACA0524 from Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL), QC to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR) NY. At 4000 ft. while on approach for runway 29, the crew received a TCAS Traffic Alert. The crew was advised by ATC of VFR traffic and the crew did have a visual on the aircraft. The Traffic Alert came once the aircraft (single engine light airplane) was behind them.  Flight landed without further incident.

C-GFKT, a privately registered LA-4-200 was conducting a water takeoff from Georgian Bay, to the east of Giant's Tomb Island, ON (14NM north northwest of Huronia (CYEE), ON). During the takeoff run, the aircraft encountered a boat's wake, causing it to become momentarily airborne. The right wing dropped and the right wingtip float contacted the water and became detached from the aircraft. The resulting yaw to the left caused the left wingtip float to contact the water forcefully. The takeoff was abandoned and the pilot taxied the aircraft to shore. The pilot, who was the sole occupant of the aircraft, was not injured. A witness contacted the police, who responded along with a Canadian Coast Guard vessel. There was significant damage to the right hand flap, which exhibited a bend about halfway along the wingspan, and there was evidence of buckling to fuselage structure below the right wing attach point. The aircraft will be brought to a maintenance facility to further assess the damage. The ELT did not activate.

C-IEUY, a private Quad City Ultralight Aircraft Challenger II advanced ultralight with only the owner/pilot on board, was returning to its home airfield, an unregistered 3200' grass strip approximately 5nm NNE of Carleton Place Airport (CNR6), Ontario, following a local flight. While on short final approach to runway 32, the nosewheel contacted and severed hydro wires approximately 275 feet short of the runway threshold. The aircraft lost most of its forward momentum, rolled to the right, and fell to the ground approximately 50 feet from the wire strike location, with the right wing absorbing the ground impact. The pilot was uninjured, and the right wing of the aircraft was substantially damaged. There was a local power outage resulting from the severed hydro wires.

C-GBXQ, a Cessna 152 aircraft operated by Truro Flying Club, was conducting a solo student training flight in the circuit for Runway 27 at Debert airport (CCQ3), Nova Scotia. On the final circuit, the solo student realized that they were low on approach and corrected by adding power. When they were close to the runway, they decreased power and pitched down and the aircraft bounced and the nose impacted. The nose gear collapsed and the aircraft remained on the runway. The flight school dispatcher recognized that there was an issue and the monitoring flight instructor drove out to the runway. The student pilot was not injured. The nose gear collapse resulted in damage to the propeller and engine area.

C-GFAV, a Beech King Air 200 aircraft operated by Fast Air Ltd, was conducting a charter flight from Wunnumin Lake Airport (CKL3), ON to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International (CYWG), MB. When the aircraft was approximately 70 NM northeast of CYWG, the crew observed an "abnormal flicker" coming from the front exhaust of the right engine. The flight crew suspected the possibility of a small flame; however, there were no associated abnormal engine indications. The crew elected to level off at FL200 and conduct a precautionary engine shut down. An emergency was declared, and the subsequent landing was conducted uneventfully with the right engine inoperative.The operator's maintenance examination of the engine revealed a loose torque oil pressure line and and oil leaking into the exhaust. There were no signs of smoke or fire damage found to the engine. The applicable maintenance was conducted and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FLFE, a privately registered Cessna 560XL, was conducting a flight from Victoria Int'l (CYYJ), BC to Tofino (CYAZ), BC with 2 flight crew and 1 passenger on board. Shortly after takeoff, at approximately 1000 feet ASL, the main cabin door opened. The flight crew declared an emergency and returned to land at CYYJ. After landing, ARFF inspected the aircraft and the flight crew taxied the aircraft back to the hangar. There were no injuries; the aircraft sustained minor damage to the main cabin door.It was determined that, prior to departure, the door had been latched on the pre-catch only. The aircraft was ferried to the manufacturer for repair.

C-GABW, an Island Coastal Aviation Incorporated Piper PA 34-200T Seneca II, was conducting a post maintenance test flight with the pilot and another instructor on board. The crew recycled the gear three times in the air to confirm it functioned properly after maintenance replaced the nose gear assembly. The crew then decided to conduct circuits at Abbotsford (CYXX), BC to complete the test flight. On final approach the crew observed a landing gear down and safe indication and the aircraft landed on the runway on its main wheels. As soon as the nose wheel came down, the nose gear collapsed. There was damage to the nose of the aircraft and both propellers were damaged when they struck the runway surface. There were no injuries.A third party maintenance company inspected the nose gear assembly. The nose wheel down lock link was broken at the upper rod end.

C-FJZD a Jazz Aviation LP CRJ900, was operating as JZA8143 from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Calgary, AB (CYYC). During taxi for departure, a cabin crew member became incapacitated. The aircraft returned to the gate and the captain called for EMS to meet the aircraft at the gate. EMS personnel boarded the aircraft and removed the flight attendant to the terminal and carried out an assessment. The flight attendant did not go to hospital and the flight was cancelled.

C-GJHD, a privately registered Cessna 172 was on the take-off roll, at Tillsonburg, Ontario (CYTB), with only the pilot on board. As the aircraft became airborne the pilot's seat slid back on the rails and the pilot was unable to reach the flight controls. The aircraft stalled and struck the ground with the left wing and cartwheeled. The nosewheel collapsed and the aircraft came to rest in an inverted position. The aircraft was substantially damaged but the pilot was uninjured. The 121.5 ELT activated during the impact.

C-GURG, un Canadair CL60 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, sous l'indicatif QUE10M, effectuait un vol d’évacuation médicale selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Québec/Jean-Lesage Intl., QC (CYQB) à destination de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC). Alors que l'appareil était en montée initiale après le décollage le contrôle du tangage requérait une force inhabituelle. Une fois en palier à 4000 pieds ASL l’équipage a reçu un message que le canal numéro 1 du compensateur en tangage était inopérant et il a automatiquement changé au canal numéro 2. Le compensateur fonctionnait à nouveau et le contrôle de l’appareil est redevenu normal. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et est revenu se poser à CYQB avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre.Le personnel de l'entretien de l'exploitant a remplacé la boîte de contrôle du compensateur en tangage et l’actuateur du canal 1. Un vol de vérification a confirmé que le tout était réglé.

C-FVHS, a Bell 212 helicopter operated by Vortex Helicopters Inc., departed Kenora (CYQK), ON. to conduct forest firefighting duties approximately 35 NM north of Kenora equipped with a 150 foot long line and water bucket attached. The helicopter completed a cycle of bucketing and was returning to a staging area for fuel. During the return flight the pilot noticed the bucket was twisted. The pilot decided to stabilize the bucket by adding water from a nearby lake. During the process, the pilot lost sight of the bucket and the helicopter began to drift to the right. The pilot then felt a tug on the helicopter and seconds later the helicopter impacted the water. The pilot, who was seated in the left seat, exited the helicopter, swam to shore and was picked up by a passing helicopter and transported to the staging area and was then transported to the local hospital with minor injuries. The helicopter was substantially damaged. The visibility in the area was reported as being reduced to 2 to 3 miles in smoke and the winds were reported as calm.

C-FRMH, a Canadian Helicopters Limited Sikorsky S-61N, was conducting bucketing operations in support of forest fire suppression activity southeast of Penticton (CYYF), BC with 2 crew on board. After lifting the water bucket out of the lake, the helicopter transitioned into forward flight. As they accelerated through approximately 30 knots, at an estimated 100 feet above the lake, the crew felt the bucket release. They confirmed that both the bucket and the long line assembly had fallen in to the lake. The crew then returned to CYYF and landed. Maintenance examined the manual hook release cable assembly and found that it had been assembled incorrectly. This allowed for the cable assembly to inadvertently activate the manual release mechanism in the cargo hook. The manual hook release cable assembly was put together correctly and returned to service.

C-GRUN, a privately registered Cessna 185F on amphibious floats, was conducting a VFR flight from Kamloops (CYKA), BC to Vanderhoof (CAU4), BC with only the pilot on board. The pilot departed from Runway 27 at CYKA at approximately 0800 PDT and the visibility, from the weather observation, was 3 statute miles (SM). Approximately 6 miles west of CYKA, visibility became worse and the pilot descended seeking better conditions. The visibility was still very poor so the pilot decided to do a precautionary landing straight ahead on Kamloops Lake. The aircraft touched down on the lake with the landing gear in the down position. The aircraft subsequently nosed over and came to rest inverted on the lake. The pilot egressed out the window of the left cockpit door and climbed up onto the float. A passing train acknowledged that they had seen the pilot and a train crew came later in the morning and, after the pilot swam to shore (the pilot was not wearing a PFD), transported him to the town of Savona.
