The pilot sustained minor injuries and no signal was received from the 406 MHz Emergency Locator Transmitter (ELT).The aircraft was subsequently recovered and is awaiting a maintenance estimate. During the recovery, a signal from the ELT was received by the Canadian Mission Control Centre.

C-FPDP a privately registered Zenith CH601HD was taking off from a private grass strip surrounded by soya fields, near Chatham, Ontario. During climb out the engine (1.8L Subaru EA-81) lost power at approximately 100 feet AGL. The aircraft forced landed in an adjacent soy field, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft, but no injury to the pilot, who was the only occupant.

N486AX, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Omni Air International, was conducting a positioning flight, OAE7392, from Eielson Air Force Base (PAEI), AK to Boeing Field/King County International (KBFI), WA with 16 crew members on board. During cruise flight, 45 nautical miles west of Port Hardy (CYZT), BC at 35 000 feet above sea level, the leading-edge slat disagreement caution message illuminated (LE SLAT DISAGREE). The crew performed the appropriate QRH procedure which did not clear the message. The crew decided to land with slats up and landing flaps at position 20. For safety, they diverted to Seattle-Tacoma International (KSEA), WA due to its longer runway. An emergency was declared with the Vancouver Area Control Centre and the crew elected to dump fuel to reduce the landing weight and the landing distance required. The approach and landing were uneventful.Maintenance performed a check of the flap-slat electronic unit and found a fault in the center hydraulic system pressure transmitter. The transmitter was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

On 22 July 2021, C-GVRA, a Canadian Heritage Warplanes Lancaster MK X aircraft, was conducting annual pilot recurrent training at the Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), Ontario. On the climb out after takeoff, the pilots noticed zero hydraulic pressure. The pilots were able to successfully lower the landing gear but could only select partial flaps due to the loss of hydraulic pressure. The pilots declared a PAN PAN, completed the circuit and landed without further incident. The aircraft was shut down on the runway and towed in for inspection.The company completed an internal investigation and SMS report. A Service Difficulty Report was submitted to Transport Canada. Their post-flight inspection revealed that a flange connecting a hydraulic line in the right landing gear wheel well had failed which resulted in the loss of hydraulic oil. The part was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

On 23 July 2021, C-ITHR a Zenair 601 CH advanced ultralight, was landing on Runway 15 at the Buttonville Municipal Airport (CYKZ) with the pilot and one passenger on board. While crossing the threshold and during the flare, the nose inadvertently pitched up abruptly. The aircraft experienced a hard landing on the left main landing gear and bounced. Subsequently on the second touchdown, the nose gear collapsed and the aircraft came to rest on the side of the runway. The runway was closed by NOTAM. There were no injuries. Post occurrence examination indicated that the aircraft was damaged beyond economical repair.

C-GOKN, a de Havilland DHC-8-102 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways LP., was conducting flight WSG420 from Sandy Lake (CZSJ), ON to Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON. C-FYWG, a Fairchild SA227-AC aircraft operated by Perimeter Airways LP., was conducting flight BLS220 from CYXL to North Spirit Lake (CKQ3), ON. WSG420 was descending to CYXL in instrument meteorological conditions (IMC). The flight crew was alerted by Winnipeg Centre of BLS220 that was VFR at 10 500 feet above sea level (ASL). The flight crew of WSG420 levelled off at 11 000 feet ASL and noted that the BLS220 did not appear to be at the reported 10 500 feet ASL. They determined that BLS220 was actually 200 to 300 feet below WSG420, at which time they received a traffic collision alerting system (TCAS) resolution advisory (RA) to climb. The flight crew of WSG420 complied with the RA and, once clear of the conflict, continued their descent to CYXL. Flight BLS220 was northbound from CYXL in visual flight rules (VFR) conditions when the flight crew received a Traffic Collision Alerting System (TCAS) traffic alert with the opposing direction WSG420. The flight crew made visual contact with WSG420 and altered their altitude while maintaining a safe lateral distance. As the 2 aircraft passed each other the separation was estimated to be 1.5 NM horizontally, and approximately 500 feet vertically.

C-FBRG, a Cessna 337G aircraft operated by Mag Aerospace Canada, departed Dryden Regional (CYHD), ON to conduct a survey with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. Approximately 35 nautical miles southeast of CYHD, the pilot noticed the circuit breaker panel began to heat up, followed by a burning electrical smell. The pilot declared a Pan Pan with Sioux Lookout (CYXL) ON,  radio and then turned off the electrical system. The aircraft diverted back to CYHD without radio and the pilot turned the electrical system on twice to keep CYXL radio updated on their position. The aircraft then landed without further incident.

C-GYPA, un Beech B100 exploité par Max Aviation Inc. sous l'indicatif MAX190 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, Qc (CYHU) à destination de La Grande Rivière, Qc (CYGL). Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en vol de croisière, un problème d'indication de train d'atterrissage a été rapporté et l'équipage a déclaré une urgence. L'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre à CYGL à 17:17 UTC.

C-FLXP, a float-equipped de Havilland DHC-6 Series 200 aircraft operated by Transwest Air with only 2 crew on board, was conducting a flight from La Ronge (CJZ9), SK to pick up fire fighting personnel at the Bar Fire, 46 NM NW of CJZ9. Immediately after takeoff, the flight deck and cabin filled with blue electrical smoke. The flight crew initiated a 180 degree turn for an emergency return to CJZ9. When the aircraft had landed safely on the water, the crew communicated with operations and then turned the electrical master switch off. The flight crew step-taxied the aircraft back to the water-base and secured the aircraft.The operator's maintenance personnel determined that wiring near the heat mixing-valve motor was burnt. The damage was repaired and the aircraft was returned to service.

On 26 July 2021, the Atleo River Air Service Ltd. Cessna A185F seaplane (registration C-GYJX, serial number 18503187) was conducting a flight from Tofino Harbour Water Aerodrome, British Columbia, to the Hesquiaht First Nation community located at Hot Springs Cove, British Columbia, with 1 pilot and 4 passengers on board. During takeoff at approximately 1138 Pacific Daylight Time, the aircraft momentarily became airborne before control was lost and the aircraft cartwheeled and came to rest inverted in shallow water. The pilot and passengers were able to exit the aircraft onto a sandbar. One passenger received serious injuries; the remaining 3 passengers and the pilot received minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. No signal was received from the 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter.

C-GAAJ, a Boeing 767-232 operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd., was conducting flight CJT567 from Winnipeg James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with two flight crew. The flight crew reported a standby bus failure and declared a Pan Pan as multiple systems failed and the flight diverted to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. The aircraft landed safely and was met by emergency vehicles.

N627AS, an Alaska Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-700 operating as flight ASA7004, was conducting a cargo flight from Seattle-Tacoma Intl (KSEA), WA to Ketchikan Intl (PAKT), AK, with 2 pilots on board. Shortly after levelling off at FL400, the crew observed a 'Cabin Altitude' annunciation accompanied by the cabin altitude horn. The crew donned oxygen masks, referred to the quick reference checklist, and declared an emergency with Vancouver ATS while beginning an emergency descent. The crew selected manual mode on the Pressurization Mode Selector and observed the cabin pressure improving during the descent. The 'Cabin Altitude' light extinguished when the aircraft passed through FL100 and then leveled at FL90. The crew removed their oxygen masks and after contacting dispatch, returned to KSEA where they landed without incident. There were no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft.Maintenance found the aft outflow valve was not fully closing in both normal and manual selector modes. The aft outflow valve was replaced, an aircraft pressurization test was successfully completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-ILZL, un paramoteur Per Il Volo Miniplane, en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis un champ situé à 14 milles marin au Sud sud ouest de l'aéroport Jean-Lesage (CYQB), Qc. Lors d'une manoeuvre acrobatique, le pilote a échappé le frein droit. À l'altitude de reprise de contrôle le pilote a heurté un amoncellement de souches et a été blessé au dos. L'appareil n'a pas été endommagé et le pilote a été transporté à l'hôpital.

C-FVPA, a Robinson R44 Helicopter was performing aerial spray application on a corn field near Brantford, Ontario. During a spray run, the helicopter impacted a set of hydro wires at the edge of a corn field, and subsequently crashed. The helicopter came to rest approximately 270 feet from the hydro wires, and was destroyed, the pilot who was the sole occupant was seriously injured. The TSB deployed two investigators to the scene.

C-GMZR, an Air Canada Airbus 220-300, was conducting flight AC502 from Chicago O'Hare Intl. (KORD), IL to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC. On initial climb, the aircraft levelled at 5000 feet and was advised from ATC of a traffic ahead at 10 nautical miles circling at 5500 feet.  Flight crew then received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) monitor vertical speed.  Flight crew followed the RA and flight continued to YUL without further incident.

C-GFVH un Cessna 150M immatriculation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Gatineau, Qc (CYND) à destination d'un aérodrome privé situé près du Lac Nilgaut, Qc. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en vol de croisière, la pilote a déclaré une urgence suite à une panne moteur. Un atterrissage d'urgence a été effectué dans une zone boisée. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée, et l'appareil a été localisé par le Centre conjoint de coordination des opérations de sauvetage de Trenton (JRCC). La pilote a été légèrement blessée et a été hélitreuillée par les services de sauvetage et transportée à l'hôpital pour un examen de contrôle.

C-GKIQ, un planeur monoplace Schleicher ASK21 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Saint-Dominique, QC (CSS4). Lors du retour pour l’atterrissage, le pilote a touché la cime des plants de maïs. L'aile droite a alors percuté le sol et l'avion s'est brusquement retourné sur son axe vertical. La force de rotation a endommagé la poutre de queue. Le pilote n'a pas été blessé.

C-GRHJ, an Aerospatiale AS 350B2 SD-2 helicopter, operated by Remote Helicopters, was engaged in aerial fire suppression 42 NM WSW of Big River (CKX8), SK. While water bucketing, the engine (Avco Lycoming LTS-101-700D2) lost power. The pilot jettisoned the bucket and conducted a successful autorotative landing near a slough. The pilot was uninjured and was extracted from the site by another helicopter. The helicopter was undamaged.The operator's maintenance personnel identified a problem was with the engine airflow modulator. The helicopter was repaired temporarily and then flown to Meadow Lake (CYLJ), SK under a special flight permit. The airflow modulator actuator was replaced. A detailed inspection of the tail rotor system was conducted with nil damage noted.

C-FNIJ, an ATR 72-212A aircraft operated by North Star Air Ltd., was conducting flight BF503 from Churchill (CYYQ), MB to Pond Inlet (CYIO), NU. At approximately 400 miles north of CYYQ, during a climb from 17 000 feet to 18 000 feet, the flight crew observed a low oil pressure warning of the number 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW127F). The power lever was pulled back and the checklist was conducted, which included shutting down the engine. An emergency was declared and the aircraft diverted to Thompson (CYTH), MB, where an uneventful landing was conducted. The operator’s maintenance performed the tasks required after a low oil pressure indication and subsequent engine shutdown. The main and scavenge oil filters were inspected, and the chip detectors and oil level was checked. No faults were found. The engine was also inspected for external oil leaks and none were found. The operator is consulting with the engine manufacturer for further troubleshooting.Updated November 3rd 2021

C-FGCN, a Canadian North Boeing 737-300, was conducting flight AKT1402 from Edmonton International, AB (CYEG) to Fort Mackay/Albian, AB (CAL4) with 5 crew members and 44 passengers onboard. As the aircraft was on final decent into CAL4, the flight crew selected the landing gear down, and observed the primary gear indication lights and various other panel lights were not working; however, the secondary landing gear position indication lights indicated that the landing gear was down. The flight crew subsequently elected to execute a missed approach and contacted company dispatch to advise them of the current situation. The decision was subsequently made to divert/return to CYEG. While en route to CYEG the flight crew elected to declare an emergency with ATC. On approach to CYEG the crew selected the landing gear down and using secondary indication methods confirmed the landing gear was extended and an uneventful landing was completed.Company maintenance is investigating the cause of the faulty landing gear indication system.

C-GAZF, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 767-338, was operating as CJT584 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC to Hamilton (CYHM), ON with 2 crew members on board. On the climb out around 10 000 feet ASL, an engine-indicating and crew-alerting system (EICAS) caution alert "AUTOPILOT" advisory occurred.  The crew requested to level-off and consulted the appropriate Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) checklist. After approximately 45 seconds, the light extinguished and the crew resumed the climb. As they approached 16 000 feet ASL the "AUTOPILOT" advisory reappeared. The autopilot was observed straying from the flight director commands and with airspeed decreasing. The crew disconnected the RH autopilot and the aircraft abruptly pitched up due to being significantly out of trim. The crew requested to level off and initiated a turn back to CYVR while declaring a PAN PAN. During the descent, a "STAB TRIM" advisory EICAS message appeared. The aircraft landed without further incident. Emergency vehicles met the aircraft but were quickly stood down. There were no injuries.The aircraft was refueled and the RH autopilot was deferred. The LH and center autopilot had been deferred on previous flights. The aircraft was dispatched and flown manually to CYHM at 27 000 feet ASL. During the flight, the "STAB TRIM" advisory EICAS message appeared twice. Maintenance staff replaced the LH and RH stabilizer trim limit switches and tested the autopilot system to clear the defects. The LH stabilizer actuator motor was also replaced to address the recurring stabilizer trim issue. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GRWK, a Bell 205A-1 helicopter operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd., was transporting 5 members of a Helitac crew from the Gypsumville Fire Base, MB to a fire near Barker Lake, MB. When the helicopter was approximately 30 nm NW of Gypsumville, the occupant of the left cockpit-seat noticed smoke in the left chin bubble area. The pilot conducted a precautionary landing and contacted the operator's maintenance personnel. The No. 2 battery relay was determined to be at fault. The No. 2 battery was de-activated and the aircraft returned to service with the item deferred. The relay was replaced upon return to the Gypsumville Fire Base. The operator submitted a Service Difficulty Report (SDR) concerning the failed relay.

C-GDPL, a privately registered, amateur-built Savanah VG XL on amphibious floats, was on the second leg of a return VFR flight plan to Nanaimo (CYCD), BC with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. The aircraft departed Gillies Bay (CYGB), BC with the next stop being Princess Louisa Inlet (50° 11’ 42” N, 123° 46’ 27” W). The pilot confirmed that the landing gear was in the up position and selected a landing site approximately ½ NM from the dock at the east end of the inlet. The conditions at the time were reported to be no wind and glassy water. The aircraft landed and nosed over coming to rest inverted in the inlet. The landing gear strut connection points on the fuselage showed buckling and the connecting bolts in the floats were ripped loose. The pilot and passenger egressed, inflated their personal flotation devices and were quickly pulled from the water and taken to the dock by nearby boaters. A nurse from a nearby lodge attended and determined the pilot and passenger had not been injured. The aircraft was towed to and secured at the dock. The signal from the 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter was relayed to the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre – Pacific.

C-GSSK, a privately registered Aerospatiale (Airbus) AS 350 B3 helicopter, was conducting a local VFR maintenance test flight following a 144 month maintenance inspection from Pitt Meadows airport (CYPK), BC with the pilot and 2 maintenance personnel on board. Following the completion of hover checks the helicopter was transitioned to forward flight. At an airspeed of approximately 40 knots the pilot observed a fuel pressure warning followed by a reduction of engine power and main rotor decay. The takeoff was rejected and an emergency landing was made on Taxiway F. ATC was advised of the rejected takeoff and emergency. The ELT automatically activated on landing. There were no injuries.Subsequent maintenance activities found the loss of engine power was resultant from interrupted fuel flow by a piece of debris that remained in the helicopter's fuel cell following the inspection. Structural damage to the helicopter's tail boom was repaired and the helicopter was returned to service.

C-GIPL, an Airspray 1967 Ltd. Aero Commander 695B, was operating as ASB062 from Prince George International Airport (CYXS), BC with 2 crew members on board conducting fire suppression south of CYXS. During the operation, the crew became aware of a possible hydraulic failure. Within a short time, the hydraulic failure was confirmed through the hydraulic pressure gauge. The crew completed the hydraulic failure checklist and decided to return to CYXS. As the aircraft approached CYXS the crew reviewed the flapless landing and emergency braking procedures. The crew then completed the landing gear emergency extension checklist and declared a PAN PAN with the CYXS tower. The aircraft landed safely without further incident with ARFF on standby. There was no fire and no injuries.Upon inspection, the maintenance staff found the auxiliary hydraulic pump pressure switch leaking causing a loss of hydraulic pressure. The switch was replaced and the system tested successfully. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FVNS, a Douglas DC-3C-BT-67 aircraft operated by North Star Air as flight BF105, began take off on RWY 04 at St. Theresa Point (CYST), MB with a flight crew of 2 on board. At the same time, C-FWLE, a Piper PA32 aircraft operated by MHA Enterprises Ltd. was approaching RWY 04 on the taxiway. During the take off roll of flight BF105, the crew noticed C-FWLE suddenly accelerate forward on the taxiway. As a precaution, the crew of flight BF105 decided to reject take off. C-FWLE was able to stop before entering RWY 04 and immediately returned to the ramp. Flight BF105 then back tracked RWY 04 and departed shortly after.

C-FATM, a Viking Air Ltd. DHC-6 operated by Air Tindi was conducting flight TIN604 from Thor Lake, NT to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with 2 crew and 10 passengers on board. En route from Thor Lake, the crew reported to company operations that the nose wheel was not centered. Troubleshooting with company maintenance was unsuccessful in centering the nose wheel. The crew declared an emergency with ATS while on approach to CYZF and emergency services were put on standby. An uneventful landing was subsequently conducted. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft.

C-FPHN, a Taiga Helicopters Aerospatiale AS350D, was conducting operations in support of tree surveying with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. As the aircraft was maneuvering to land at the destination and drop off the passengers, at an altitude of 4-6 feet, the main rotor blades struck a tree. An uneventful landing was conducted and the pilot and passengers disembarked normally. A post flight damage inspection was completed.

C-FCAS, un Osprey II de construction amateur, devait effectuer un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue au départ et à destination de l'aérodrome de Dolbeau/St-Félicien, QC (CYDO). Lors du démarrage, le moteur s'est emballé et a produit la puissance maximale. Le pilote n'a pas été en mesure de contrôler l'appareil et a percuté la porte d'un hangar situé approximativement 300 pieds devant lui. L'appareil s'est retrouvé encastré dans la porte et a été détruit. Le pilote a subi des blessures mineures.

C-FQEH, a Cessna 172K on floats, departed from the Sudbury/Azilda Water Aerodrome (CNC5), ON and was landing at Wanapitei Lake, ON. When the aircraft touched down on the water, the tip of the left float dug in and the pilot tried to correct, however, the right wing tip then contacted the water and the aircraft cartwheeled, coming to a rest inverted. The pilot egressed the plane without injuries, was picked up by local boaters and taken to shore.

C-FHKF, a General Dynamics Convair 440 aerial fire fighting aircraft operated by Conair, was conducting flight TANKER455 from the Penticton airport (CYYF), BC tanker airbase with 2 flight crew members on board. C-FKFL, another General Dynamics Convair 440 operated by Conair, was not operating and was parked at the north end of the tanker base near Taxiway C. As TANKER455 was taxiing northbound for departure towards Taxiway C its left wingtip contacted the left wing of C-FKFL. There were no injuries. C-FHKF received minor damage. C-FKFL received substantial damage.

C-FCMU, a Textron (Beech) 1900D operated by Central Mountain Air, was conducting flight GLR708 from Terrace airport (CYXT), BC to Prince George airport (CYXS), BC, with 2 flight crew member and 4 passengers on board. Prior to landing the flight crew could not extend the landing gear. The flight crew declared an emergency and carried out a manual landing gear extension. The flight landed without further incident.Subsequent maintenance actions replaced a faulty landing gear motor relay (p/n: MS24171D1), and the aircraft was returned to service.

The Airco Aircraft Charters Beech King Air 100, C-FWYN, was operating as flight ARQ147 from Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC  to Edmonton (CYEG), AB with two flight crew and two passengers on board. ARQ147 was following ATC vectors for the approach to CYEG and while turning for final approach, the flight crew observed the R ENGINE fire annunciator and right fire extinguisher light illuminated. The first officer visually checked the right engine for fire and observed no indication. While established on final approach, the flight crew declared an emergency and continued to land without incident. While holding on taxiway B1 the aircraft was met by ARFF and confirmed no fire was present. The aircraft taxied back to the company hangar where the annunciator lights remained illuminated until shutdown. The passengers were deplaned and there were no injuries. Company maintenance found that one of the three photoconductive cells in the right nacelle to be faulty. The photoconductive cell was replaced and the aircraft released for service.

C-GRFZ, a Bell Helicopter 206L-1, operated by Prairie Helicopters Inc landed on a log pad 25 miles north of Grand Rapids (CJV8), MB with only the pilot on board. While loading the helicopter, and with the engine operating, the log pad shifted and the helicopter began to pitch nose up. The pilot attempted to level the helicopter using the collective and cyclic control but was unsuccessful and then shut down the engine. One of the landing pad logs was shifted by the weight of the helicopter and struck the tail boom. There were no injuries. The helicopter sustained minor damage to the tail boom.

C-FHAB, a Pilatus PC-12/47 aircraft operated by Air Bravo Corp., was conducting flight C2297 from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Keewaywin (CPV8), ON. While en route the crew observed a puff of smoke emanating from under the GPS unit, which was followed by a GPS Fail warning. Smoke in cockpit procedures were carried out, and an emergency descent was initiated. The crew requested radar vectors to Pickle Lake (CYPL) ON where they carried out an uneventful landing with ARFF standing by.During a subsequent inspection maintenance noted that the GPS unit had a burnt smell to it They then replaced the GPS unit. No other faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GVSK, a Convair 340/580 aircraft operated by the Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency-Air Operations, was en route from Buffalo Narrows (CYVT), SK to La Ronge (CYVC), SK via the Forks wildfire. After finishing wild fire suppression activities, while en route to CYVC, the crew of C-GVSK observed fluctuations in the propeller rpms and that the propellers were out of sync. They attempted to manually sync the props, which resulted in the right-hand propeller (Hamilton Standard 54H60-77) going into an overspeed condition and an associated pitch lock. The crew made attempts to recover from the pitch lock but were unable. They then shut down the right-hand engine (Allison 501-D22G) as per the checklist. The flight crew declared an emergency and carried out an uneventful landing in YVC with the right-hand engine inoperative.During a subsequent inspection,  maintenance crews troubleshot the snag and replaced the R/H valve housing on the prop governor and the propeller synchronization box.  The aircraft was returned to service the following day.

C-GIGO, a float equipped Cessna 208 aircraft operated by Seair Seaplanes Ltd., was preparing to conduct a flight from Ganges Harbour (CAX6), BC to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC with 1 crew member on board. Prior to the engine starting, the dockhand assisting the pilot untied the guide rope and held it in his hand. When the engine started the aircraft travelled forward pulling the rope from the dockhand. The aircraft began travelling forward until the propeller of C-GIGO struck the rear of C-GUTW, a float equipped DHC-3T operated by Harbour Air. After the initial prop strike, the pilot of C-GIGO quickly shut down the engine as the aircraft rotated 90 degrees striking C-GUTW with the RH wing. C-GUTW was tied to the dock with no one on board during the occurrence. There were no injuries; both aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GPAO, a DeHavilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines Ltd, was conducting flight PVL901 from St. John's International (CYYT), NL to Deer Lake Regional (CYDF), NL with 4 crew members and 46 passengers onboard. While in cruise flight, a flight attendant became ill and was no longer able to perform the duties of the position. The crew made the decision to return back to CYYT and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FGPC, a privately registered Cessna 185F on amphibious floats, departed Prince George International Airport (CYXS), BC  to Mackenzie (CYZY), BC  with 2 persons on board. The flight was occurring under special VFR with forest fire smoke in the area limiting the visibility to 2 1/4 sm. Upon departure, the visibility deteriorated as the aircraft climbed. CYXS ATC asked the pilot to deviate their heading to accommodate inbound traffic. The deviation placed the aircraft in an area with even less visibility so the pilot elected to descend and follow the Fraser River northbound. As the river became more difficult to follow, the pilot elected to land on it. The landing gear had not been retracted after take off and upon touchdown the aircraft flipped over. Both occupants managed to egress the overturned aircraft and climb onto one of the floats while waiting for rescue. The pilot received minor injuries and the passenger received serious injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FPER, an Airbus AS350 B2 helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited was conducting a flight from a remote fishing outpost to the fishing lodge’s main base in Eagle River, Labrador with 1 pilot and 5 passengers onboard. As the helicopter was lifting off, the tail rotor made contact with a large rock located on the shoreline. The pilot aborted the takeoff and was able to land the helicopter back down on the river bank. The helicopter was shut down without further incident. The tail rotor, horizontal stabilizer and vertical fin sustained damaged. There were no injuries.

C-GCLQ, un Beech 200 exploité par Sky Jet M.G. Inc., sous l’indicatif LSJ447, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à destination de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) avec 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait à une altitude de 5000 pieds ASL en montée, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison d’une indication de feu moteur gauche et a demandé à revenir à CYQB. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été exécutée et le moteur a été fermé, mais l'indication de feu moteur était toujours allumée. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre à CYQB à 12 :02 UTC. L’équipage a évacué l’aéronef sur la piste. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. Une inspection effectué a déterminé que le filage des détecteurs de feu moteur donnait de fausses indications lorsqu'il bougeait. Le filage a été réparé.

Voyageur Airways flight VAL103, a De Havilland DHC-8-102 aircraft, was on route from Hamilton /John C. Munro , Ontario (CYHM) to Montréal-Mirabel International Airport, QC (CYMX) when the flight crew advised ATC of a number 1 engine oil pressure indication issue and requested a diversion to Toronto / LBPIA (CYYZ) ON. The flight crew carried out the QRH procedure and attempted to feather the engine. The engine oil pressure continued to drop and the flight crew shutdown the engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW120A). An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed without further incident in CYYZ.Voyageur maintenance inspected the aircraft and the fault was determined to be an "O" ring connecting to the pressure tube to the oil cooler had failed. The defect was rectified and the aircraft was returned to service with no additional defects found.

C-FYLY, a privately registered Piper PA-12 Super Cruiser, was conducting a recreational flight from Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC to Hope (CYHE), BC with the pilot and 2 passengers on board. During the take-off roll, the aircraft began to veer to the right. The pilot attempted to correct the turn but the aircraft continued off the right side of the paved runway into the grass. The pilot attempted to stop the aircraft and, after it crossed a ditch, the landing gear collapsed and the propeller struck the ground. The pilot and passengers egressed from the aircraft and waited by the aircraft for assistance. There were no injuries to the pilot or passengers. The aircraft was taken to a maintenance facility where the extent of the damage will be assessed.

C-FFBU, un hélicoptère Airbus AS350-B2 exploité par Les Hélicoptères Canadiens ltée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Puvurnituq, QC (CYPX) à destination du camp minier Rex (60 NM ENE de CYPX), QC avec seulement un pilote à son bord. Un équipement de forage et une échelle étaient transportés avec l’élingue. Au départ de l’aéronef, l’équipement de forage, qui n’était pas bien sécurisé, a commencé à se détacher de l’élingue. Le pilote a senti la charge se détacher complètement et a ensuite remarqué que seule l’échelle était toujours attachée à l’élingue. La compagnie a constaté que l’équipement de forage avait été sécurisé avec des câbles élastiques flexibles qui ne permettaient pas de bien sécuriser l’équipement. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GPSK, un British Arerospace Jetstream 3212 exploité par Pascan Aviation sous l'indicatif PSC587, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Bonaventure, QC (CYVB). Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en vol de croisière, en passant le point de repère VODIX, le voyant "Duct Light On" du moteur droit s'est allumé. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée, et l'équipage a coupé le moteur. Une urgence a été déclarée et l’équipage a alors demandé à être dérouté vers CYQB. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre sur la piste 06 à CYQB.

C-GRGI, a de Havilland DHC-8-106 operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting flight PAG107 from from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Island Lake (CYIV), MB. When approximately 50 nm northeast of CYWG, the crew observed a cargo smoke warning. The crew carried out the associated checklist items, declared an emergency, and returned to CYWG for an uneventful landing. During a subsequent inspection, the operator's maintenance personnel replaced both cargo smoke detectors. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-FKTZ, a privately registered Piper PA-22-160, was conducting a flight from Villeneuve airport (CZVL), AB to Fort McMurray airport (CYMM), AB with one pilot and one passenger onboard. While landing on Runway 26, the aircraft veered sharply to right off the centerline and nosed over coming to rest in the grass near Taxiway Golf causing substantial damage to the propeller and main landing gear. There were no reported injuries.

C-GTJL, an Learjet 35A aircraft operated by Sunwest Aviation Ltd, was conducting a flight from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 2 crew on board. Shortly after takeoff, the flight crew received a loss of hydraulic pressure indication in the cockpit. The crew declared an emergency, the emergency gear extension and the no hydraulic pressure landing checklists were actioned and the decision was made to return to CYYC where the aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance replaced part S-4606116ABCHT000 braided flexible hydraulic lines and the aircraft will be returned to service.

C-GUAY, un Cessna 208 amphibie exploité par Air Tunilik Inc, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Puvurnituq, QC (CYPX) à destination du camp minier RexNord (60°16’49.8’’ N 075°21’17.5’’ W), QC avec seulement un pilote à son bord. Les roues n’ayant pas été rétractées avant l’amerrissage, lorsque les flotteurs ont touché l’eau, l'appareil s’est renversé. Le pilote a pu évacuer l’appareil. Des témoins de l’accident sont allés porter secours au pilote avec l’aide d’une embarcation. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

On 10 July 2021, C-IJGB, a Tundra, registered as basic ultra-light aircraft, departed a private grass strip located approximately 5nm southwest of Athens, Ontario, for a local flight with the pilot and one passenger on board. During the takeoff, in the initial climb, there was a loss of power to the engine, and the aircraft crashed into a swamp near the end of the runway. The pilot was fatally injured and the passenger received minor injuries. The TSB deployed a team of investigators to the accident.

C-FXQS, un Piper PA-12 sur flotteurs, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le Lac Cayamant, QC. Au décollage, lors de la montée initiale, le pilote a perdu le contrôle de l'aéronef et a percuté des arbres. L'aéronef a terminé sa course partiellement submergé sur la rive du lac. Le pilote et le passager ont été sérieusement blessés. L'aéronef a été détruit. Le pilote a plus tard rapporté avoir été surpris par des vents rabattant durant la montée initiale.

C-FRWN, a Canadian Harvard Association Mk2 was conducting an airshow demonstration as part of a formation of 4 aircraft in Geneseo airport (D52), NY. During landing as the aircraft decelerated, the tail wheel touched down and the aircraft veered left departing grass runway into a cornfield.  Right hand wing tip touched the ground and the owner reported damage to right hand wing tip, aileron and spar.  There were no injuries reported.

C-FLLL, a Northwestern Air Lease Ltd. amphibious float equipped de Havilland DHC-3T (Turbine Otter) was conducting a VFR flight from Ft. Smith (CYSM), NT to a lake 17 nm ENE of CYSM with 1 pilot and 4 passengers on board. The aircraft touched down on the lake with the landing gear in the down position. The aircraft subsequently nosed over and came to rest almost inverted on the lake. The pilot egressed out the left cockpit door and swam to the rear of the aircraft where the 4 passengers were waiting with the emergency exit open. 1 passenger entered the water and shortly after a boat came to gather everyone up. The pilot sustained a minor injury and the passengers were uninjured. The 406 MHz ELT transmitted.

C-GGRC, a Valhalla Helicopters Bell 206 helicopter was conducting the second leg of a wine tasting tour from a winery SW of Oliver, BC to one SE of Naramata, BC with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. Shortly after liftoff, while in a left turn climbing through approximately 100 feet above ground level, the helicopter began an uncommanded yaw to the right. Despite full left pedal input by the pilot, the helicopter spun several times before it impacted terrain approximately 275 feet SE of the liftoff point in a vineyard. Prior to the right-hand spin, a shuddering was felt in the aircraft. The helicopter impacted the right front and came to rest on its left side. The pilot egressed first and assisted the right rear passenger out of the helicopter then they both assisted the left rear passenger. The helicopter engine was still running and the occupants were assisted to safety inside the winery where they received first aid while awaiting paramedics. All 3 occupants were taken to hospital; the pilot and right rear passenger received minor injuries while the left rear passenger received serious injuries. Police and firefighters also responded to the scene. The helicopter's engine had stopped running but fuel was still leaking and a small post-impact fire began in the engine compartment. Fire personnel disconnected the aircraft battery and extinguished the flames. The 406 MHz ELT signal was relayed to the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre and the police on scene turned off the ELT. Maintenance personnel examined the aircraft and determined that all tail rotor driveshaft couplings were intact and witness marked. They could not determine any mechanical reason for the helicopter's loss of control. Weight and balance calculations indicated that the helicopter was below maximum takeoff weight when it departed. The temperature was approximately 30° C with a density altitude of about 3500 feet. The estimated wind at the lift off point was SSE at approximately 5 knots.Change:Location of passengersUPDATED 11 August 2021

N605LC, a Bombardier CL60 aircraft operated by Solairus Aviation, was conducting flight TWY35 from Hanscom Field (KBED), MA, US to Frankfurt (EDDF), Germany with 2 flight crew members onboard. While in cruise flight, the crew advised ATC that the aircraft had a fuel imbalance and requested a diversion to Bradley International (KBDL), CT, US. The crew actioned the associated QRH items, however, the fuel imbalance continued to increase. The crew declared an emergency and requested a diversion to Stephenville (CYJT), NL as a precaution. The aircraft landed without further incident.The operator's maintenance department determined that a faulty auxiliary tank transfer ejector pump was the cause of the fuel imbalance. The remaining fuel in the tail and auxiliary tanks was transferred to the main tanks, the main fuel tanks were balanced and the aircraft was flown to a Bombardier maintenance facility utilizing the air operator’s Minimum Equipment List.

A homebuilt Ultra-light Thatcher CX4 (C-IKXF) was conducting circuits from Stoney Point (Le Cunff) airport, ON (CRML). During a low speed final approach over a wheat field, following a wind gust, the aircraft drifted left of the center line. When the pilot re-applied power to go around, the left wing touched the terrain and flipped over in the field. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left wing tip, vertical stabilizer and propeller. The pilot, sole occupant onboard, sustained serious but non-life-threatening injuries.

C-FLXF, a 7795289 CANADA Ltd. (dba Artic Red River Outfitters) Piper PA-18-150, was conducting circuits at Whitehorse/Cousins airport (CFP8), YT. During one of the take-offs, the engine (AVCO LYCOMING O-320-A2B) stopped producing power at about 200 feet AGL. The pilot commenced a forced approach into the trees. The aircraft was substantially damaged but there were no injuries to the two occupants. The owner will report back to the TSB their findings once the aircraft is recovered.

C-FIKM, a Cessna 337G aircraft operated by Mag Aerospace Canada, was conducting fire detection/bird dog operations in the vicinity of Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON with only the pilot onboard. While in cruise, the rear engine RPM began to fluctuate. The pilot conducted a precautionary shutdown of the rear engine and returned CYPL. AARF was put on standby and the aircraft then landed safely. A subsequent inspection of the system revealed an indication issue with the RPM gauge.

C-GLDE, an Aerospatiale-Alenia ATR 42-320 aircraft operated by Transwest Air Ltd, departed Buffalo Narrows (CYVT) SK with 2 flight crew, 1 flight attendant and 7 passengers on board. After leveling off at 10500 feet ASL while enroute to John G. Diefenbaker (CYXE) SK, the crew began a descent to 7000 feet ASL. While descending through 8500 feet ASL, the aircraft entered a cumulus cloud and encountered severe turbulence and a sudden drop in altitude. The flight attendant sustained serious injury and one passenger sustained minor injury, both of whom were not wearing a seat belt at the time of the turbulence. The aircraft continued on to CYXE where it landed without further incident and was met by ambulance.The operator grounded the aircraft following the incident and an abnormal occurrence inspection was completed. There were no defects found and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYAC, un Nanchang CJ6A (appareil monomoteur démilitarisé de conception chinoise) effectuait un vol de loisir entre l'aérodrome de Joliette, Qc (CSG3) et l'aérodrome de St-Esprit, Qc (CES2). Durant la phase finale de l'atterrissage (arrondi), l'aile droite de l'aéronef est entré en contact avec un tracteur à gazon à cabine ouverte qui circulait sur la piste. Le pilote a réussi à maintenir le contrôle de l'aéronef qui a terminer sa course dans une section cultivée sur le bord de la piste. La conductrice du tracteur à gazon a subie des blessures mortelles. L'aéronef a subi des dommages importants mais son pilote n'à pas été blessé.

C-GYTQ, un Cessna 185 privé sur flotteurs qui était amarré à un quai privé sur la rivière des Prairies situé à environ 4 mille marins au nord-ouest de l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL), s’apprêtait à effectuer un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue. Lors de la circulation de l’aéronef sur l’eau, le pilote a suivi sa liste de vérification en préparation au décollage. La liste de vérification n’indiquait pas de vérifier l’enlèvement du dispositif de verrouillage des gouvernes et l’aéronef n’était pas équipé d’un dispositif approuvé. Cependant, un dispositif non approuvé avait été installé la veille et n’a pas été retiré lors de la préparation au décollage. L’aéronef a débuté sa course sur l’eau et le pilote s’est aperçu que les commandes de vol étaient bloquées. L’aéronef a pu se soulever au-dessus de l’eau mais n'a pu monter davantage. L’aéronef est redescendu et a piqué du nez vers l’avant au moment où les flotteurs ont touché la surface de l’eau puis il s’est renversé. Le pilote a été retenu à son siège par une ceinture à 4 points d’attache et portait son gilet de sauvetage. Il a pu évacuer l’aéronef rapidement et n’a pas été blessé. Une embarcation est venue récupérer le pilote pour l’amener sur la terre ferme.

C-GNTI, a Sundance Balloons Cameron A-300, was conducting a sight seeing tour over Edmonton (CYEG), AB with 1 pilot and 10 passengers on board. After 45 minutes of flight, the balloon touched down in a field 12NM NNW of Edmonton. During envelope deflation, the wind shifted and the basked started dragging eventually tilting to the point where 2 passengers fell out. 1 passenger sustained injuries that required hospitalization. There was no damage to the balloon or basket.

C-FCLB, a Pilatus PC-12/47 aircraft operated by Private Air Inc, was conducting a flight From Chibougamau/Chapais Airport (CYMT), QC to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON with 1 crew and 6 passengers onboard. Upon selection of the landing gear down during the approach for landing in CYYZ, the nose landing gear annunciator illuminated a red light indicating the nose gear was not down and locked. The pilot completed the applicable checklists and called the maintenance department, declared an emergency and decided to divert to the Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON for maintenance. The pilot flew by the tower to confirm the nose landing gear position, and then landed without further incident on runway 26, where emergency vehicles were standing by. The aircraft was immobilized on the runway where maintenance inspected the landing gear. Afterwards, the aircraft was taxied back to the airport parking area.After further inspection, maintenance found the nose landing gear Up-lock sensor connector broken. The damaged parts have been replaced and the system tested serviceable.

C-GTUF, a Chartright Air Inc. Challenger 300, was conducting flight HRT142 from Coleman A Young Municipal (KDET), MI to Santa Barbara Municipal (KSBA), CA. During cruise, approximately 40 minutes from KSBA received a warning for a left engine fuel bypass.  Flight crew followed checklist and continued flight.  Approximately 15 minutes later, flight crew received a warning for right engine fuel bypass.  Flight crew followed checklist, declared an emergency and diverted to Los Angeles Intl (KLAX), CA.  The flight landed without any further incident. Operator advised last two FBO's where fuel was picked up in CYYZ and KDET so they can carry their possible fuel contamination protocols.

C-FVAS, a Cessna 337 aircraft operated by Can-West Corporate Air Charters Ltd., was conducting an aerial fire detection/bird dog operation in the Stoney Rapids (CYSF), Saskatchewan area with the pilot and one passenger on board. After completing the aerial fire detection operation, the crew returned to CYSF where the pilot selected landing gear down during final approach to Runway 24. During initial touchdown, the landing gear collapsed and the aircraft came to a stop on the centerline of the runway. The pilot and passenger were able to evacuate the aircraft without injury. The aircraft sustained significant damage.

C-FTAX, a Top Aces Inc. Dornier Alpha Jet A, was on approach to land at Group Captain R.W. McNair-Cold Lake (CYOD), AB when the aircraft struck a bird with the left wing. Flight crew from a second aircraft visually inspected the aircraft and a controllability check was completed. An emergency was declared followed by an uneventful approach and landing. Maintenance follow up: The aircraft was removed from service to assess the damage.

On 26 June 2021, a Thunder Airlines Mitsubishi MU-2, operating as THU890 was conducting a flight from Buttonville Municipal Airport (CYKZ), Ontario to Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), Ontario. At approximately 06:55 UTC, 200 NM southeast of CYQT the right engine oil pressure decreased, followed by a loss of torque. The flight crew elected to shut down the engine as a precautionary measure and conducted a single engine approach and landing at CYQT. There were no injuries and no aircraft damage. Post flight inspection revealed that the engine oil filter housing was cracked.

C-FTYZ un Beech 100 exploité par Exact Air inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Poste-Montagnais, QC (CSF3) à destination de l’aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) avec 2 pilotes et 7 passagers à bord. À environ 10 miles nautiques à l'ouest de CYBC, le pilote a senti une odeur de brulé dans le cockpit et déclaré une urgence. En déroutement vers CYBC, le pilote a identifié la source de l'odeur et annulé l'urgence. L'avion s'est posé sans encombre à CYBC. Un élément de dégivrage du moteur droit a été remplacé par la maintenance.Aucun blessé 27 juin 2021

C-GECT, un Pilatus PC12 exploité par Cameron Air Service Ltd. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de La Macaza-Mont Tremblant (CYFJ), QC à destination de l'aéroport Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON. C-GECT avait reçu et relu correctement l’autorisation de monter au niveau de vol (FL) 230. L’ATC a constaté que C-GECT a poursuivi sa montée jusqu’au niveau de vol 234. Le contrôleur a interrogé C-GECT sur son altitude, l’aéronef a reconnu l’erreur et est redescendu au niveau de vol assigné. Il y a eu une perte de d'espacement avec C-GDEW, un de Havilland DHC-8-400 exploité par Westjet Encore sous l'indicatif WEN3409 qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC, à destination de l'aéroport Lester B. Pearson de Toronto (CYYZ), ON.  L'espacement entre C-GECT et C-GDEW a été réduit à 4.4 miles nautiques horizontalement et 600 pieds verticalement alors que l'espacement minimal requis est de 5 milles nautiques horizontalement ou 1000 pieds verticalement.

C-GMAI, a Boeing 737-200 operated by Air Inuit, was conducting flight AIE780 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) to Puvirnituq, QC (CYPX) with 2 crew members on board. While on approach to CYPX, when Flap 1 setting was selected the flaps did not respond. Due to weather concerns, the crew diverted to their alternate airport Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP). The crew declared an emergency. They performed the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) checklist, and the flaps were lowered with an alternate selection. The aircraft landed in CYPX and taxied to the terminal without further incident.

On 28 June 2021, the Yellowhead Helicopters Ltd. Bell Textron Inc. model 212 helicopter (registration C-GYHQ, serial number 30933) was conducting operations in support of forest fire fighting efforts approximately 4 nautical miles west-northwest of Evansburg, Alberta. At approximately 1800 Mountain Daylight Time, the helicopter departed the staging area to complete a series of 3 flights transporting groups of forest fire fighters back to the staging area. The first 2 trips were completed uneventfully. During the last trip, as the helicopter was approaching the landing area to pick up the final group of fire fighters, one of the main rotor blades separated from the rotor head assembly. The second rotor blade and rotor head assembly then broke free from the helicopter and the helicopter crashed. The pilot, the sole occupant on board, was fatally injured. There was a post-impact fire that destroyed the helicopter. A signal from the 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter was not received.UPDATED 02 JULY 2024

C-GVSM, a privately registered Beech G36 aircraft, was conducting a VFR flight from Sechelt (CAP3), BC to Victoria Int'l (CYYJ), BC with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the descent for landing, the engine (Continental IO-550-B) lost power. The pilot declared an emergency and conducted a forced landing. The aircraft contacted trees and came to an abrupt stop on residential property. Both occupants sustained serious injuries. The aircraft sustained serious damage. The ELT activated.

C-FFLC, a Boeing 737-86J aircraft operated by Flair Airlines, was conducting flight FLE513 from John G. Diefenbaker (CYXE) SK, to Vancouver Int'l Airport (CYVR), BC with 6 crew members and 141 passengers. On approach, the trailing edge flaps did not extend beyond 'Flap 5' and then moved uncommanded to the 'Flap 2' position. The flight crew notified ATC, discontinued the approach and received vectors to complete the associated QRH checklists and landing performance calculations. During the alternate flap extension, the trailing edge flaps remained at 2 degrees. ATC notified the flight crew that ARFF was on standby and the aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-FYQQ, a float-equipped Cessna C180H owned by Fort Langley Air Ltd., was privately rented for a VFR flight from a seaplane dock at Pitt Meadows  Airport (CYPK), BC to Fire Lake, BC with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. While en route, the pilot decided to divert to Thomas Lake, BC and on landing, control of the aircraft was lost and it overturned. The 3 occupants egressed; 1 passenger received minor injuries. The ELT did not activate. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GMCP, a Starlink Aviation Inc. Learjet 45, was conducting flight TLK833 between Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl.(CYUL), QC and Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl (KBOS), MA. In KBOS vicinity, Flight crew declared an emergency with ATC due to cracked windshield, requested a descent and diverted back to CYUL.  Flight landed without further incident.

C-GOLC, a de Havilland DHC-2 aircraft operated by Harbour Air, was being fueled at the dock at Vancouver International Seaplane Base (CAM9), BC. The person refueling the piston engine aircraft (Pratt & Whitney-USA R-985 Serial Number 4220855) used the Jet A nozzle instead of the Avgas nozzle. The fuel nozzle had been turned on but the fuel pump for the Jet A had not been turned on. An unknown amount of Jet A was added to the fuel tank.  The fuel tank was drained by company maintenance and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GVCS, an Aerospatiale AS 332L operated by VAL AIR, was conducting external load operations from North Spirit Lake Airport (CKQ3), ON. to Knox Lake Camp ON. Shortly after departing CKQ3 with an attached 100 foot synthetic rope long line, there was an uncommanded long line release. The synthetic rope long line departed the aircraft and fell into forested wilderness. The long line was not found. There was no damage to the helicopter and property, and no injuries. This helicopter had a similar event on 21 June 2021 (TSB occurrence A21C0056). The operator has suspended slinging operations pending a complete assessment and repair of the electrical release systems on both upper and lower hooks.

C-FIVS, an Air Canada Boeing 777-300 cargo flight AC7211 was taxiing to the gate after landing on runway 24L in Toronto Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON from Frankfurt (EDDF), Germany. During taxi, the crew received an EICAS message of low pressure on tire #5 and #6 on the left wheel assembly.  Upon arrival at the gate, maintenance reported metal debris on tires #1, #5, #9. After landing the aircraft's taxi route was from 06L to taxiway D3 then taxiway DQ to gate 177. A number of amber edge lights were found broken at the intersection if 06L and D3.Maintenance replaced #1, #5, #9 wheel assemblies. No other damage was found.

C-FXIH, un hélicoptère Airbus AS355N exploité par Les Hélicoptères Canadiens ltée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Sept-îles, QC (CYZV) à destination de l’hélisurface d’IOC à environ 4 mille marins (NM) au sud-ouest. Peu de temps après le décollage, l’indication lumineuse rouge « REG » s’est illuminée et éteinte en même temps que des fluctuations de Ng (générateur de gaz du moteur) sont apparues. Une alarme sonore intermittente s’est fait entendre indiquant une survitesse des tours rotors (RPM), cependant le pilote a constaté que les RPM étaient dans la plage normale d’opération. Par la suite, les indications lumineuses « ENG P » et « R/H GEN » sont apparues et l’indicateur "delta Ng" du moteur #2 a affiché zéro. Le pilote a suivi la procédure pour continuer le vol avec un seul moteur fonctionnel. L’aéronef a fait demi-tour et s’est posé sur la voie de service Bravo à CYZV sans encombre. Le service de maintenance a établi que le DECU (Digital Engine Control Unit) a réagi à une fausse indication de survitesse et a coupé l’alimentation en carburant du moteur #2.

C-FCRZ, an ATR72-200 operated by Calm Air International LP, was conducting flight CAV784 from Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU. to Thompson (CYTH) MB. CAV784 landed safely in CYTH. After engine shutdown, the flight crew noticed a smell of gasoline in the cargo area. Upon further inspection of the cargo, the crew discovered that an ATV's fuel line had become dislodged. An estimated 100 ml of fuel (dangerous goods UN 3166, vehicle flammable liquid powered) was spilled.  The spill was cleaned by the operator's personnel and reported to the Transport Canada Emergency Centre (CANUTEC).

C-FMVK, a privately registered Stinson 108 aircraft was landing at Edenvale Airport (CNV8) after a flight from Buttonville (CYKZ), Ontario. During the landing a gust of wing lifted the wing, as the pilot applied engine power for a go-around the aircraft veered to the left and went off runway 13, rolled into uneven ground and flipped over. The pilot was not injured but the aircraft was substantially damaged. The wind was reported from 180 degrees magnetic at 14 knots.

C-GERO, a Thrush Aircraft S2R-T34  operated by Precision West AG corp. was conducting an aerial application flight from and to Gaspé, Québec (CYGP) with one pilot on board. On short final, with engine at idle, the pilot moved the power lever to apply more power but there was no response from the engine. A high ITT warning quickly followed. The aircraft could not reach the runway and struck the ground approximately 200 feet short of the threshold of Runway 10, striking the perimeter fence before coming to a complete stop. The Emergency Locator Transmitter (ELT) was triggered. The pilot secured the airplane and was not injured.

C-FGDT an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 aircraft flight AC58,  was beginning an ETOPS flight from Toronto Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ) ON to Doha/Hamad Intl. (OTHH) Qatar. After pushback and on route to the runway the flight crew received an EICAS message for #1 engine L1 VFSG (variable frequency starter generator) fault. After contacting maintenance the flight crew turned off the associated generator. To continue the ETOPS flight without the generator required the APU to be operational during the entire flight. As a result the current fuel load was not sufficient for the flight and the flight crew started taxiing back to the gate to refuel and for maintenance to MEL the generator. During the taxi, the flight crew received a #1 engine fire warning. They stopped the aircraft on the taxiway and declared a MAYDAY, afterwards discharging one fire bottle. After a short period of time they received a message from a following aircraft that smoke was still visible from the engine, and as a result a second fire bottle was discharged. ARFF arrived at the aircraft and monitored the situation. The aircraft was eventually towed to the gate for inspection. The flight crew maintained contact with the cabin throughout the event and did not order an evacuation of the passengers.Upon inspection of the #1 engine, maintenance found substantial fire damage to the engine surrounding the area of the L1 VFSG. The electrical harnesses and inner cowlings were damaged and oil was dripping from the VFSG. Maintenance replaced the engine and shipped the VFSG for overhaul.

C-GXZW, un hélicoptère Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 exploité par Héli Explore Inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à l’aérodrome de la pourvoirie Mirage, QC (CPM3) avec un pilote à bord pour effectuer du travail local. En montée initiale lors du déplacement d'une plate forme avec une longue élingue de 100 pieds, le pilote a ressenti un soubresaut et a constaté avoir perdu son chargement en haut du crochet inférieur. Le pilote a relâché l'élingue qui s'est enroulée autour du rotor de queue. Un atterrissage d'urgence a été effectué. Le pilote est sorti sans blessure. L'hélicoptère a subi des dommages importants et les pales du rotor principal ont heurté la surface rocheuse lors de l'atterrissage sur la surface inclinée. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) ne s’est pas déclenchée.

C-ILFK, a Just Escapade Advanced Ultra-light (floats) was on a VFR flight from Dashwoods Pond, NL to Long Gull Pond, NL. The aircraft was in cruise flight at 3000 feet ASL when the engine shuttered and quit without warning at 15:50 NDT. The pilot attempted a restart that was unsuccessful and then transmitted a MAYDAY call to Stephenville FSS. Landing options were limited due to the nature of the barren terrain. The pilot attempted a final restart at about 200 feet AGL with the use of the choke and the engine started. The engine ran normally and a climb was initiated. The pilot planned to continue to a pond he could see in the distance however, the engine quit again and a forced approach was conducted. The aircraft touched down 50 feet from the shoreline of a small body of water. At touchdown, one float dug into the terrain and the aircraft flipped onto its back and sustained damage to the float attachments and structural damage to the tail. The pilot sustained minor injuries and exited the aircraft to make cellular contact with the flight itinerary designate. They informed Stephenville FSS that the pilot was ok and they would not require JRCC assistance as they had arranged to have the pilot picked up via a commercial helicopter. The pilot also carried a satellite communication device capable of live tracking which was useful in pinpointing the location of the accident site.Once the aircraft is recovered from the accident site, it will undergo an engine and related system examination in an attempt to determine the reason for the engine stoppage.

C-FCFX, a Cessna 172M owned by the Canadian Aviation College, was operated by a student while taxiing for the fueling location. The left wing struck a staircase structure alongside the fuel tank; the aircraft was spun towards the fuel tank, but it impacted a cement barricade with the propeller which resulted in engine and airplane sudden stoppages. The pilot was not injured and there was no fuel spill.

C-FWBL, a privately registered Robinson R44 II, operated by White Bear Industries Ltd. was enroute from Lakelse Lake, BC to Fort Nelson Airport (CYYE), BC, when the pilot with one passenger on board, received a low main rotor RPM warning horn and light, with both engine and main rotor tachometer needles decreasing. The pilot performed a forced landing on a mountain logging road approximately 15 NM NE of the Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC. He noticed while in the auto-rotation descent that the reciprocating engine RPM was fluctuating (Lycoming IO-540-AE1A5, 6 cylinder, fuel injected). During the flare to touch down with collective and aft cyclic application to arrest the descent and forward motion, the helicopter skidded forward for about 15 feet on the gravel road. The helicopter remained upright on its skids, and both the pilot and passenger exited with no injury. The helicopter suffered substantial damage when the main rotor struck the tail boom during touchdown. The tail boom remained only partially attached to the rest of the structure by the internal driveshaft assembly connected to the tail rotor gearbox. Maintenance was contracted to inspect the helicopter drivetrain and initially could not find or replicate any defect that would suggest a mechanical malfunction or explain the low main rotor RPM reported by the pilot.

C-GGZQ, a Bell 206LR helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited, was conducting a flight from Fredericton International Airport, (CYFC), NB to Grand Falls Airport (CCK3), NB. In cruise, the pilot noticed the engine oil pressure intermittently showing above the maximum pressures of 130 psi. The pilot planned to carry out a precautionary landing in a field to check the oil levels. On the approach to landing, as the pilot raised the collective, the main gear box (MGB) pressure dropped below minimum and the caution light illuminated for 4 seconds. At this point the pilot transitioned to a no hover landing. After landing, the collective was reduced to full down and the MGB pressure returned to the normal range.After shut down, the pilot noticed that the main gearbox had no oil in the sight glass. An AME checked the chip plugs and removed 3 quarts of oil from the engine oil reservoir as it was over full from the transfer of oil. The MGB was topped up with 4 quarts of oil and a ground run was completed before the helicopter transited to Woodstock NB. The company completed a full serviceability check on the MGB, chip plugs and freewheel unit.

C-FILF a privately registered Cessna R172K, was on a VFR flight from Lloydminster (CYLL), AB to Cardston (CEA6), AB. The first approach to CEA6 RWY 23 was aborted and the pilot conducted an overshoot. On the second attempt the aircraft bounced on initial contact with RWY 23. The pilot applied power to abort the landing, but the right wing dropped and the right landing gear contacted the runway. The aircraft skidded off the left side of the runway. The right wheel dug into the grass and the aircraft flipped over and came to rest inverted adjacent to the runway. There were no injuries to the pilot or passenger.

C-GMNL, un Beech B100 exploité par Max Aviation, effectuait un vol local depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU) QC sous l'indicatif de vol MAX180, avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, l'indication de température interturbine (ITT) du moteur droit (Garrett TPE331-6-252B) est montée au-delà de la limite permise, sans manipulation correspondante du levier de puissance moteur. Après avoir reculé le levier de puissance moteur, la température n'est pas redescendue et le moteur a été fermé par mesure préventive. Le moteur s'est éteint et l'hélice s'est mise en drapeau. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre à CYHU à 1806Z.

C-GSJG, un Cessna 182P privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue, depuis le Lac Long (QC) à destination de la rivière le Petite Décharge, Alma (QC) avec le pilote et un passager à bord. Lors de l'amerrissage, le bout de l'aile droite a heurté des branches d'arbre qui pendaient au-dessus de la rivière. L'aéronef a subit des dommages à l'aile et au flotteur.  Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GFWK, un Cessna 172M sur flotteurs privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue, au départ de l'hydrobase Sainte-Véronique, QC (CSW9) à destination d'un lac non identifié situé à 4NM SSW du lac Tassé (Qc) avec le pilote et un passager à bord. Au moment de l'amerrissage sur l'eau miroitante, l'aile gauche a levé à la suite d'une bourrasque de vent, l'aéronef a dévié vers la droite et a percuté les arbres.L'ELT s'est déclenché lors de l'impact et les recherches effectuées par le centre conjoint de coordination des opérations de sauvetage (JRCC) de Trenton ont permis de localiser l'appareil. Celui-ci a subi des dommages majeurs, mais les occupants n'ont pas étés blessés.

C-GVCS, an Aerospatiale AS 332L operated by VAL AIR, was conducting external load operations 13 NM SE of Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON with two crew on board. While longlining an external load containing a mini excavator, there was an uncommanded release of the load. The external load fell into a heavily timbered and uninhabited area. There was no damage to the aircraft and there were no persons in the vicinity of the load release. The operator conducted a check of the electrical system and the suspected cause was an electrical issue in the longline hook release relays and circuits.

The amateur-built Birdman Chinook 2S, C-ILIJ, was on a flight from a private airstrip at the North Fork Ranch, YT to a private airstrip at 40 Mile Creek, YT. When switching from the wing strut pod tanks to the wing tanks, the aircraft engine (HKS JAPAN, 700E) lost power. During the forced approach the aircraft collided with trees approximately 13 nm east of Dawson City (CYDA),  YT airport. A local helicopter crew found the wreckage and was able to drop two rescuers at the crash site. The helicopter found a landing site and once the lone pilot was extricated form the wreckage, he was transported to CYDA for transfer to the Dawson City hospital and later to Whitehorse, YT.

C-GCQZ, a privately registered Piper Comanche, PA24, was conducting a flight from a private airfield near Bergen, AB to Sundre (CFN7), AB. During the approach to CFN7 the pilot did not extend the landing gear. The aircraft landed on its belly and damaged some lower fuselage skin and the propeller. The pilot, the sole occupant of the aircraft, was not injured.

N401KZ, a Boeing 747-400 aircraft operated by Kalitta Air, was conducting flight CKS335 from Los Angeles Intl Airport (KLAX), US, to Brussels Airport (EBBR), Belgium. During cruise, while in Gander oceanic airspace, the EICAS displayed ENG OIL FILT 2 and ENG OIL TEMP. The crew consulted the QRH and shutdown engine number 2. The crew declared an emergency and requested a diversion to East Midlands Airport (EGNX), UK. The aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance determined that the engine had experienced internal damage. A 3-engine ferry flight to the company’s maintenance facility was conducted, where the engine was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-IITD, a Rans S-6 Coyote II advanced Ultralight (ULA) aircraft was on initial climb from the Grand Forks Airport (CZGF) BC, and at about 500 feet AGL the engine lost power (BRP ROTAX 503) and the pilot turned back towards the airport. During the descent an airstart was attempted but was unsuccessful. The renter pilot did not declare an emergency. The ULA descended and crashed into an orchard about 100m North West of the runway, just short of the airport periphery fence. He extricated himself and waved down a witness who called EMS. He was attended to by EMS who transported him to the hospital for observation.  Prior to the flight, the pilot had taken a fuel sample from the sump and considered it clear. The aircraft run-up was fine and the engine was operating normally during taxi and takeoff. Maintenance Follow-up: Owner's maintenance determined that the carburetor bowl contained a large quantity/ratio of water to fuel (MOGAS 91 Octane).

C-FGFY, a privately registered amateur built Rutan LONG-EZ, was on a flight from St. Thomas Municipal Airport (CYQS), Ontario, to Dutton Airport (CDT7) Ontario, with the pilot as the sole occupant. During the downwind for runway 21 the engine (Lycoming O-235-L2C) began running rough, and as the pilot turned base, the engine failed. The pilot flew directly to the threshold of the runway while attempting a restart and switching fuel tanks, but landed approximately 50 feet short, striking a stack of plywood on the unfinished main floor of a house under construction. The fuel tanks were not breached, and there was no post crash fire. A neighbor responded within minutes, and the local fire department arrived shortly afterwards. The pilot received serious injuries to both legs during the impact and was airlifted to hospital.

C-FMII, a Cessna 152 registered to Winnipeg Aviation, was to conduct a local flight at Winnipeg/St. Andrews (CYAV), MB. As C-FMII was taxiing to a pre-flight runup location on Runway 04, the right wing of C-FMII contacted the rotating propeller of C-GKTJ (a Cessna 152 registered to Harv's Air Service), that was stationary and conducting a pre-flight runup. C-GKTJ's propeller severed approximately 2 feet of C-FMII's right wing and aileron. There were no injuries.

C-FEAI, un DHC8-314 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE802 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Kuujjuarapik, QC (CYGW) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 13 passagers à bord. Peu après le décollage, l'équipage a demandé un retour à CYUL en raison d'une perte de fluide hydraulique du système no.2. Une urgence a été déclarée et la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée. L'appareil a atterri sans encombre à 1247Z et s'est immobilisé sur la voie de circulation A2. L'appareil a été remorqué à la barrière d'embarquement. Il n'y a eu aucun blessés.

C-GPBT, un Cessna 182 privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aérodrome de Drummondville (CSC3) QC à destination de Sept-îles (CYZV) QC, avec un pilote et un passager à son bord. En raison de la dégradation des conditions météorologiques en rapprochement de CYZV, le pilote a décidé de faire demi-tour et d'atterrir à l'aéroport de Baie-Comeau (CYBC) QC. Une communication radio a été établie avec la station d’information de vol de Mont-Joli en vue de l’atterrissage. Une approche vers la piste 10 a été effectuée alors que les vents de surface étaient du 260 degrés à 13 kts avec des rafales à 19 kts. Suite à un premier rebond à l’atterrissage, le pilote a constaté que sa vitesse était élevée et que le bout de la piste était proche. Il a augmenté la puissance pour tenter de redécoller mais n'a perçu aucune réaction du moteur. Les freins ont donc été appliqué mais l'aéronef a sortie en bout de piste. La roue de nez a été arrachée, l'aéronef a basculé vers l'avant et a terminé sa course sur le dos. Les 2 occupants ont évacué l’aéronef et n’ont pas été blessés. La radiobalise de détresse s’est déclenchée à l’impact.

C-FOES, a de Havilland DHC-2T MK 111 'Turbo Beaver' floatplane, operated by Air Cab of Port Hardy BC, was conducting a visual flight rules flight from Port Hardy Water Aerodrome (CAW5), BC to Campbell River Water Aerodrome (CAE3), BC. The final approach was in to the sun and when approximately 1 Nm from CAE3, at a height of approximately 20 feet above the water, the pilot focused briefly on adjusting the propeller. At the same time, the airspeed was decreasing and the stall warning system activated. The aircraft then stalled and impacted the water. An aluminum front float strut fitting broke and the propeller struck the water as the aircraft came to rest nose down in the water. There was no post impact fire and the ELT did not activate. The pilot, sole occupant, sustained no injuries and was rescued by the Coast Guard who towed the aircraft to a nearby maintenance facility.

C-FZQS, an Air Canada Airbus 320-200, was conducting flight AC900 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL. While performing holding pattern over West Palm beach Intl (KPBI) FL, Flight crew reported they lost between 1200 and 1300 feet of altitude, airspeed fluctuation of 15 knots and the auto pilot disconnected due to active weather in the area. In consultation with company dispatch the decision was made to divert to Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL. The remainder of the flight to the alternate destination was conducted without further incident.

C-FFSS, a Thunder Airlines Mitsubishi MU-2B-60, was operating as flight THU860 from Sudbury (CYSB) ON to Kashechewan (CZKE) ON. While on the approach to CZKE, the flight crew selected the landing gear down, however, there was no response to the gear down selection. The flight crew initiated a missed approach at CZKE and made the decision to return to CYSB. While on the approach to CYSB, the landing gear was selected down and the gear extended normally. The flight crew requested that emergency services be standing by as a precaution and a normal landing was carried out. Company maintenance reported that the landing gear selector was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

The Great River Aviation Ltd. Britten Norman Islander BN2A-27, C-GHRK, was on a flight from Dawson City (CYDA), YT to Burwash (CYDB), YT when the right engine (AVCO Lycoming O-540-E4C5) experienced a drop in manifold pressure followed by a decay in engine RPM. The right hand throttle control was found to be stuck in the full throttle position. The flight was diverted to Beaver Creek (CYXQ), YT and a precautionary shutdown of the right engine was carried out. Upon engine shutdown the throttle released. Due to mountainous terrain and turbulence the right engine was restarted and the aircraft was climbed back up to 6500 feet. The engine operated normally for the remainder of the flight and an uneventful landing was carried out at CYXQ.Maintenance follow-up: A post-flight inspection found significant amounts of water in the fuel system. Carburetor, fuel gascolator, and fuel tanks were drained of all contamination. The source of water ingress was found to be from the right wing tip tank. The sticking throttle was attributed to ice forming in the carburetor due to water in the fuel.

The Buffalo Airways Ltd. Curtis-Wright Commando C-46D, C-FAVO, was departing Norman Wells (CYVQ), YT for Yellowknife (CYZF), NT when the crew noticed the right engine (Pratt & Whitney-USA R-2800-51M3) running rough. The flight crew performed a precautionary shutdown of the right engine and returned to land at CYVQ. A single-engine approach and landing was conducted without further issue.Maintenance update: The right engine has been replaced due to a failed cylinder.

C-GCHJ, a Sikorsky S76C+ operated by Helijet International Inc. was on a MEDEVAC flight to a field 3.8 NM SW of Princeton Airport, (CYDC), BC with 2 flight crew and 2 paramedics on board. The aircraft crew flew 2 circuits above the landing site for reconnaissance prior to their approach to land. During the approach to land one of the paramedics, located in the rear of the helicopter, spotted a double set of power lines strung across the landing site that were not spotted during the reconnaissance. The paramedic alerted the flight crew who took evasive action by leveling off until they were clear of the power lines. The crew  then reestablished a descent and landed without further incident. There were no injuries or damage to the helicopter.The powerlines had been previously identified as a hazard by bystanders at the landing site and communicated to an ambulance crew on the ground. This information was not passed to the flight crew who were in communication with a dispatcher located in Kamloops, BC. Discussions with the ambulance crew revealed some confusion about which radio frequency should have been used. Both Helijet International Inc. and the BC Emergency Health Services are reviewing the incident.

C-GDRD, un Piper PA34-200T en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Bromont/Roland Désourdy, QC (CZBM).
