En approche pour l’atterrissage, lorsque le train d’atterrissage a été sélectionné en position baissée, le pilote a reçu une indication anormale que la roue de nez n’était pas verrouillée. Une urgence a été déclarée et un déroutement vers Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) a été effectué. La procédure d’extension du train par gravité a été tentée sans succès et l'appareil s'est posé sur la piste 29 à CYQB avec la roue de nez non verrouillée. L'appareil est demeuré dans l'axe de la piste jusqu'à son arrêt complet. Les hélices et le carénage de nez ont étés endommagés. Le pilote seul à bord n'a pas subi de blessure. La vérification mécanique après vol à permis d'identifier un boulon installé dans la direction opposée aux recommandations du manufacturier.

C-GJGP, un Cessna A185F, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue, depuis le lac Plamondon, QC à destination du lac Preissac, QC avec 1 pilote et 2 passagers à bord. Alors que l'aéronef était en vol de croisière à 7000 pieds, le moteur s'est arrêté soudainement et le pilote a tenté de rallier le lac Chicobi, QC. Alors qu'il se trouvait à une altitude de 3000 pieds, l'aéronef s'est mis à perdre de l'altitude rapidement et le pilote a dû tenter un atterrissage sur un terrain marécageux situé à environ 4NM au nord du lac Chicobi. L'aéronef a été endommagé mais ne s'est pas retourné et tous les occupants en sont sortis indemnes. L'inspection post atterrissage a révélé que le bouchon du réservoir de carburant de l'aile droite était manquant et que les réservoirs étaient vides. Le moteur a pu être démarré par la suite et semblait fonctionner normalement.

C-FNIJ, an ATR-72-212 operated by North Star Air, was conducting flight BF503 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU. At flight level 190 approximately 107 nm NNE of CYTH, the flight crew observed a low oil pressure indication on the number 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW127F). The associated checklist was subsequently completed and the engine was shut down. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and the aircraft returned to CYTH for an uneventful landing.The operator's maintenance completed the tasks required following a low oil pressure indication and in-flight engine shut down. The oil pressure switch for the number 1 engine was found to be faulty, and was replaced and tested. A test flight will be conducted prior to the aircraft being returned to service.

C-GJMA, un Aero Commander 500B exploité par MAG Aerospace Canada, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l’aéroport Greenstone Regional (CYGQ), ON à destination de l'aéroport de Maniwaki (CYMW), QC avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors que l'appareil était en vol de croisière, à environ 60 NM ouest de l'aéroport de Val-D’Or (CYVO) QC, l’équipage a observé une indication de chute de pression d’huile du moteur gauche (IO-540-E1A5). L’équipage a alors demandé à être dérouté vers CYVO . Lors de l’approche, la pression d’huile a continué de chuter et le voyant “Low Oil Pressure“ s'est allumé. L'équipage a fermé le moteur par mesure préventive. L’aéronef a atterri à CYVO sans encombre. Il n’y a pas eu de blessés.L’inspection au sol a révélé que la magnéto du moteur gauche s’était desserrée, ce qui a engendré une perte d’huile moteur. Aucun autres dommage ou anomalie n’a été détecté.

C-GMTA, a privately registered Beech A36 was on a training flight originating from St. Catharines/Niagara District (CYSN) ON. and was conducting an instrument approach to runway 24 at Hamilton (CYHM) ON. An Aeronaves TSM Fairchild SA227 was operating as flight VTM761 from CYHM to Willow Run (KYIP) MI and was departing runway 24. The conditions for departure of VTM761 were not fulfilled and a loss of separation occurred when VTM761 departed. Spacing between C-GMTA and VTM761 was reduced to 2.1 miles laterally in airspace that required 5 miles of lateral spacing.

C-FFRY, an Aries Aviation Piper PA31, was conducting an IFR flight from Edson (CYET), AB to Calgary/Springbank (CYBW), AB with only the pilot on board. Just as the aircraft levelled at 9000 feet ASL, the pilot observed that the No. 2 engine (Avco Lycoming TIO540-A2C) went to idle power. The pilot shutdown and feathered the engine. A short while later, the pilot was able to restart and operate the engine, abeit at a lower power setting (maximum 20 inches of manifold pressure). The aircraft arrived in CYBW uneventfully.Maintenance follow up: Company maintenance found that the No.2 engine turbo charger had suffered a bearing failure.

C-GWGJ, a privately registered Piper PA-23-250, was conducting a flight from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK to Thompson (CYTH), MB with the pilot and 2 passengers on board. Shortly after applying full power for take off on Runway 09 at CYXE, the aircraft's right gear collapsed. The right wing contacted the runway and dragged the aircraft to the right. The engines were shutdown and the aircraft came to a stop. ARFF responded and the occupants were uninjured. The aircraft sustained damage to the right wing and right propeller. Runway 09 was closed until the aircraft could be removed.During the aircraft recovery, the aircraft was lifted and the right gear was extended. During the subsequent attempt to tow the aircraft off the runway, the nose gear and right gear collapsed.

C-GBSC, un Cessna R182 exploité par Exact Air, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aérodrome de Lachute (CSE4) QC, à destination de Manic-5, QC (CMN5) avec seul le pilote à bord. Alors que l'appareil était en vol de croisière, à une altitude de 3000 pieds ASL, à environ 20 NM au nord-nord-ouest de La Tuque, le moteur a perdu de la puissance. Le pilote a effectué les vérifications d’urgence et déclaré un MAYDAY. Après avoir appliqué du réchauffe carburateur, le moteur a eu quelques ratées et la puissance normale est revenue. L’appareil s’est arrêté à l’aéroport de St-Honoré (CYRC) Qc, où une inspection a été effectuée et aucune anomalie n’a été détectée.

C-FKAN, un Bell 206B-1 exploité par Foxair Héliservice – Héli Pro Inc., devait effectuer un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Saint-Pierre de Broughton, QC (30 milles nautiques au sud de l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB)) avec 1 pilote à bord. Lors de la manœuvre de décollage, un patin est demeuré accroché au sol et l’hélicoptère s’est renversé. L’appareil a été endommagé et il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

C-GUNO, un ATR42-320 exploité par Bradley Air Services Limited sous l'indicatif AKT825, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Pangnirtung, NU (CYXP) à destination d'Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) avec 8 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage. Lors de la rétraction du train d’atterrissage au décollage de CYXP, le train ne s’est pas rétracté suivi d’une indication de basse pression et de bas niveau du système hydraulique vert. L’équipage a décidé de continuer vers leur destination avec le train en position sortie et une urgence a été déclarée. L'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre et a été remorqué au terminal.

C-GUSF, a Bombardier BD-700-1A10 (Global 6000) aircraft, was carrying out the engine relight portion of a standard production flight test. The aircraft was at FL310 in a test flight area, when the left engine (Rolls Royce BR700-710A2-20) was shut down as required by the test. Following the shutdown, the flight crew determined that a restart of the engine should not be attempted due to a FADEC fault indication. The relevant checklists were actioned, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and advised Air Traffic Control (ATC) that the aircraft was operating on a single engine and returning Downsview, ON (CYZD). The flight crew followed standard single-engine operations procedures and landed safely at CYZD.

At 1640 on 07 June 2021, the Helicopter Transport Services (Canada) Inc. (HTSC) Bell 214ST helicopter (registration C GDYZ, serial number 28109) with only the pilot on board departed from the Nipigon, Ontario, fire base on a forest-fire suppression flight to wildfire Nipigon 8, located approximately 28 nautical miles northeast of Nipigon. The pilot was flying the helicopter from the left seat and was wearing a lap belt and helmet. The aircraft was equipped with a 550-gallon collapsible water bucket on a 150-foot long line. The pilot conducted approximately 45 drops before informing the fire boss on board the bird dog/spotter aircraft that the helicopter was low on fuel and that the end of his duty day was nearing.The return trip from Nipigon 8 to the Nipigon fire base was flown at 3000 feet above sea level, about 1600 feet above ground level. The helicopter was travelling at 70 to 74 knots in a nose-down attitude of roughly 7° due to the empty water bucket when the pilot was alerted by a vibration in the tail rotor pedals and a grinding noise. Moments later, the 42° BOX OIL PRESS and 90° BOX OIL PRESS annunciators for the 2 tail rotor gearboxes illuminated, and there was an audible engine overspeed noise. The helicopter yawed to the right and the nose began to pitch down.The pilot lowered the collective control and moved the cyclic control aft to counteract the nose-down tendency, increase the main rotor rpm, and enter autorotative flight. As the helicopter began to spin, the pilot released the long line and water bucket by kicking the manual cargo release pedal. The pilot transmitted a Mayday call on the enroute frequency (126.7 MHz) and informed other aircraft working on the same fire that he had lost tail rotor control. While the helicopter was descending at approximately 1000 to 1500 fpm, the pilot made 3 attempts to use some engine power to fly the helicopter to a suitable landing area near a small lake. He was able to regain some control over the adverse yaw via airflow acting on the vertical stabilizer. As the helicopter descended below treetop height, he raised the collective control to cushion the landing, at which point the low rotor rpm horn activated. At 1924, the helicopter landed on its left skid gear with almost no forward speed. The emergency locator transmitter activated automatically and there was no fire. The helicopter was substantially damaged.The pilot shut down the engines and electrical systems and was able to climb out of the right-side cockpit door. Another helicopter with fire fighters on board responded to the Mayday call and, within a few minutes, landed near the accident site. The seriously injured pilot was transported directly to a hospital in Thunder Bay, Ontario.

N825SK, a Skywest Airlines Inc. MHI RJ Aviation CRJ900 (CL600-2D24), was operating as flight SKW3914 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Minniapolis (KMSP), MN with 4 crew and 39 passengers on board. During start of the second engine, smoke entered the passenger cabin. The startup was aborted and the smoke dissipated. The flight crew declared an emergency and requested ARFF to attend to the aircraft. When ARFF arrived at the aircraft they observed no signs of heat or fire and communicated that to the flight crew. The aircraft taxied back to the gate on the one engine, shutdown, and deplaned. There were no injuries to the crew or passengers.Maintenance follow up: The aircraft was inspected with no faults found. The aircraft was released back into service and departed approximately 2 hours later with no further issue.

N624AG, a Boeing 757-200ER aircraft operated by Delta Airlines Inc, was conducting flight DL9887 from Reykjavík–Keflavik International Airport (BIKF), Iceland to John F. Kennedy International Airport, (KJFK), New York, USA. After take-off, the crew noticed an electrical burning smell with no visible smoke. The crew decided to continue the climb and reference the smoke/fire/fumes checklist. No circuit breakers had tripped, and there were no EICAS alerts. Maintenance control was contacted through a satellite phone and since the source of the smell could not be determined, the decision was made to return to BIKF. The crew declared an emergency with Gander oceanic ATC and the aircraft landed without further incident. The night prior to the occurrence flight, maintenance had replaced the right side Multi Control Display Unit (MCDU), due to a reported snag. After the occurrence flight, the right side MCDU was replaced again. In addition, new recirculation filters were installed and the electrical harness and connectors were inspected. No arcing or damage was found.

C-FUNT, un appareil de construction amateur de type Superstol immatriculation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aérodrome de St-Mathieu-De-Beloeil, QC (CSB3) avec 2 personnes à bord. Lors du décollage de la piste 33, l’avion a dérivé vers la droite et est sorti de piste. Le pilote a mis plein volet et a ensuite décollé, mais l'avion est entré en collision avec un véhicule stationné et un hangar. Il y a eu 2 blessés mineurs et l’appareil a subi des dommages importants.

C-FKSL, a Pascan (9736140 CANADA INC.) SAAB 340B was conducting a ferry flight between Sioux Gateway/Brig General Bud Day Field (KSUX),Iowa and Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC.  After take-off, flight crew noticed a slight fluctuation in the left engine oil pressure. Flight crew decided to monitor the situation during climb. 15 miles west of Fort Dodge Regional (KFOD), Iowa, master warning for the low oil pressure on left hand engine came on.  Flight crew followed the QRH with the precautionary engine shutdown, declared the emergency and proceeded to return toKSUX. The flight landed safely on runway 13 without further incident.

C-GSPW, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif AIE780, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Puvirnituq, QC (CYPX). Lors de l’approche, AIE780 a effectué une remontée en raison de problème de volets et a effectué un déroutement vers Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP). En rapprochement de CYVP, AIE780 a déclaré une urgence et un état de carburant minimum. L'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre avec la présence de l'unité de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA).

The privately registered Cessna 172G, C-FTKN, was on a local flight from a 1500 foot grass airstrip located 32 NM NW of Lloydminster (CYLL), AB. During the initial touchdown for landing in a southeasterly direction, the aircraft skipped followed by a float which left the aircraft touching down the second time between one half to two thirds down the airstrip. The pilot elected to go around and proceeded to climb out. The departure to the SE required a slight left turn in the climb to avoid a machine shed and trees. During the left turn the pilot leveled the aircraft and struck a tree. The aircraft crashed almost vertically into a nearby slough. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was seriously injured and pulled from the wreckage by an eyewitness. The aircraft was substantially damaged, there was no fire and the ELT did not activate.

C-GXFC, a Buffalo Airways Ltd. Lockheed L188C (Electra), was operating as flight BFL1204 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Ekati (CYOA), NT with 3 crew on board. While on approach into CYOA, the No.1 propeller entered an overspeed condition. The No. 1 engine (Allison 501-D13) was shutdown and the flight returned to CYZF.Maintenance follow up: A failed "o" ring in the propeller govenor resulted in an oil leak. The "o" ring was replaced, the system tested and checked serviceable and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FNOE, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC898 from Montréal/Trudeau (CYUL), QC to Athens (LGAV), Greece. While in cruise flight about 370 nm east of Gander (CYQX), NL a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform the duties of the position. The crew declared an emergency with Gander Centre and requested clearance to divert to CYQX. An amended route clearance was issued and the flight landed at CYQX without incident. The flight attendant was transported to hospital, and the flight departed for original destination employing minimum cabin crew compliance procedures.

C-GJZX, un Dash-8 Q400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8975, s’apprêtait à effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination d’Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW) avec 5 passagers et 4 membres d'équipage. Lors du refoulement et du démarrage des moteurs, un membre d’équipage de conduite a subi une incapacité physique. L’avion est retourné à la passerelle et le membre d’équipage a été remplacé. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l'appareil.

C-FTNS, un Bell 206B exploité par Richcopter Inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le Lac Mountain (QC) à destination de Drummondville, QC (CSC3) avec 1 pilote et 3 passagers à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en croisière, le pilote a constaté une fluctuation de l’indication de la pression d’huile, suivi, quelques minutes plus tard, d’une fluctuation de l’indication de couple de l’arbre d’entrainement. Par mesure de précaution, le pilote a effectué un déroutement vers l’aéroport de La Tuque, QC (CYLQ). Alors se trouvait à environ 15 mille nautiques à l’ouest de CYLQ, le voyant « Chip Detector » s’est allumé. Une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée et l’appareil s’est posé dans un champ. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre et il n’y a pas eu de blessés. À la sortie de l’appareil, une fuite d’huile importante provenant du moteur et de la boite de transmission principale a été constatée. L’appareil n’a pas été en mesure de redécoller et a été conduit sur une remorque à un atelier de maintenance pour une vérification plus poussée.

C-GDPY, a Piper PA-34-200T aircraft operated by KBM Forestry Consultants Inc. was conducting a photo survey of an area approximately 50 miles north of the Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON. with only the pilot onboard. While conducting the survey, the pilot noticed the main fuel cells were low on fuel and selected the auxiliary fuel pumps on. Shortly after, the left engine began to sputter and then lost power. The pilot then selected cross-feed and was able to restart the engine. The pilot decided to conduct a precautionary landing on a logging road approximately 24 miles north of CYXL. After touchdown, the aircraft wings struck some bush and directional control was lost. The aircraft came to a rest off the right side of the logging road in an upright position, approximately 50 feet into the bush. The pilot was not injured. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. Shortly after, the pilot was picked up by a passing vehicle and taken to CYXL.It was reported that the left auxiliary fuel cell had fuel remaining after the occurrence, while the other auxiliary and main cells appeared empty. Post-occurrence examination and testing of the left auxiliary fuel boost pump indicates that it was defective. The operator has submitted a service difficulty report with Transport Canada.

N213F, a Cessna 525B aircraft operated by Desert Jet Center, was conducting flight L9M50 from Wenatchee Memorial Airport (KEAT), WA to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 2 flight crew on board. During the final approach into CYVR, upon selecting landing gear down, the right main gear down green light did not illuminate. The flight crew determined it was a light malfunction, verified the landing gear was safe, and continued the approach. The flight crew declared an emergency and requested ARFF on standby as a precaution. The aircraft landed safely with no further incident.A local maintenance organization replaced 4 light bulbs in the landing gear light module and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GGOG, un appareil de construction amateur Wag-A-Bond en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le lac Nominingue (QC) à destination du réservoir Kiamika, Qc avec 2 personnes à bord. Au début de l’approche pour l’atterrissage, en passant environ 1800 pieds ASL en descente et peu après la sélection des volets à 15 degrés, le pilote a senti l’aile de droite ralentir. L’appareil est ensuite entré en vrille, et la technique pour sortir de la vrille a été appliquée. Au deuxième tour, le pilote a repris la maitrise de l'appareil, mais l'altitude était trop basse pour éviter les arbres. L’aile gauche a touché les arbres et l’appareil s’est écrasé. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FAPW, a privately operated Cessna T210L, was conducting a recreational flight from Rocky Mountain House (CYRM), AB to Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB with 1 pilot and 2 passengers onboard. During the final decent into CYBW the pilot experienced a total loss of engine power (Continental TSIO-520-H). The pilot performed a forced landing adjacent to a golf course and the aircraft came to rest approximately  0.3 nm short of the threshold for Runway 17 at CYBW. The nose landing gear collapsed during the landing roll and the propeller made contact with the ground. The pilot and passengers evacuated the aircraft with no injuries. Despite fuel leaking from the airframe, there was no post-impact fire.Third party post accident examination of the engine and airframe did not reveal an obvious cause for the power loss.

C-GNUG, a privately operated amateur-built JUST AIRCRAFT SuperSTOL, was conducting a recreational local flight from Villeneuve Airport (CZVL), AB with one pilot and one passenger on board. The aircraft originally departed CZVL and returned to complete circuits. During the second landing on the grass infield landing area of Runway 26, the left shock absorber failed/collapsed and a ground loop ensued. The aircraft sustained damage to the left wing, left landing gear / fuselage and propeller. Both occupants evacuated the aircraft and there were no injuries.

C-GDPA, a Boeing 737-200 (combi) operated by Canadian North was conducting flight AKT228 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Kugluktuk (CYCO), NU with 4 crew members and 13 passengers on board. Shortly after take off from CYZF the flight crew experienced a compressor stall/surge followed by abnormal engine noises emanating from the #1 engine (Pratt & Whitney JT8D-19). The flight crew executed the appropriate checklist and elected to return to CYZF. The flight crew declared a priority and ARFF was activated. An uneventful landing was completed and the aircraft was met on the runway and inspected by ARFF which did not reveal any obvious signs of damage or fire to the #1 engine. The flight crew shut down the #1 engine and taxied to the terminal for deplaning.Subsequent inspection by company maintenance revealed evidence of a bird strike to the #1 engine, and the vortex dissipater for the #1 engine was damaged. Further engine inspection revealed significant damage to the first stage fan blades.

C-FXCD, an Airbus A-320-200 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA2329, a ferry flight from Melbourne Orlando International Airport (MLB), Florida, USA to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON with two crew members and no passenger onboard. While on approach for runway 05 at approximatly 3000 ft, the crew received ''ENG 2 THRUST LEVER DISAGREE'' message from the Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitor(ECAM) and the engine thrust on engine number 2 rolled back to idle. The flight crew actioned the ECAM and notified ATC that they were cancelling the approach and climbed to 4000 ft as per ATC request. The flight crew declared Pan Pan to ATC and returned for landing on runway 05 where Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) vehicles were standing by. ACA2329 taxied to the appron under its own power, escorted by ARFF, without further incident. ATC moved two arrivals to the departure runway (06R) during the event.

C-FABA, a deHavilland DHC-8-102 operated by Wasaya Airways LP., was conducting flight WSG815 from Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON. to Fort Severn (CYER), ON. When approximately 10 nm south of CYER, the flight crew received a "weight on wheels" annunciator light and master caution illuminated. The flight crew actioned the QRH and and elected to return to CYPL. After 15 minutes on the return flight to CYPL, the "weight on wheels" annunciator light extinguished. The crew requested that emergency services be placed on standby and C-FABA subsequently landing safely in CYPL. The operator's maintenance cleaned all the landing gear proximity sensor connections and tested the proximity sensors. No faults were found. The Proximity Switch Electronics Unit (PSEU) codes were checked and reset. Aircraft was tested serviceable and was returned to service.

C-FFAR, a Beech King Air B200 operated by Vanguard Air Care Ltd., was conducting flight VN03 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. to St. Theresa Point (CYST), MB. During the approach to CYST, the flight crew selected the gear down and received a main gear down and locked indication but did not receive a nose gear down and locked indication. The landing gear warning horn did not activate and there was no red warning light in the gear selection handle. The flight crew cycled the landing gear once and received the same indication. The flight crew carried out a missed approach and decided to return to CYWG.  Upon returning to CYWG, the flight crew declared an emergency, carried out a manual gear extension and completed a low pass by the CYWG tower. The tower indicated the nose landing gear appeared to down. The aircraft landed and the engines were shut down on the runway with ARFF on standby. The operator's maintenance confirmed the nose gear was down and towed the aircraft to the operator's hangar. This aircraft has a similar event on 21 May 2021 (TSB occurrence A21C0046). The operator's maintenance inspected the nose gear downlock switch, cleaned and checked the wiring harness, and completed a nose gear actuator spring check. Maintenance could not duplicate the fault. Aircraft was released subject to satisfactory test flight. Test flight was successful and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FNYF, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B2 helicopter operated by Mustang Helicopters Inc., was en-route from Smoothstone Lake, SK. to Blackfalds, AB with the pilot and 1 passenger onboard. While in cruise, the pilot received an audible warning horn followed by a hydraulic pressure warning indication. The pilot declared a MAYDAY and completed a precautionary landing on a highway approximately 10 statute miles south of Meadow Lake (CYLJ), SK. There were no injuries. The helicopter did not sustain any damage.An inspection of the hydraulic system by the operator revealed a false warning. Repairs to the warning system were made and a successful ground run was completed. The helicopter was then returned to service.

C-FATM, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-6-300, operated by Air Tindi, was conducting flight TIN604 from the Snare Hydro site NT, to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with 2 crew members and 1 passenger on board. During the landing roll on runway 10 at CYZF, the co-pilot, who was the pilot flying, experienced difficulty with the  directional control of the aircraft. The captain assumed control of the aircraft keeping the aircraft on the runway. As the aircraft slowed, the captain intentionally departed the runway surface on to the grass airport infield around a runway light and then back on to the airport movement area. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft.

C-FZAM, a privately registered Cessna 414A, was conducting a flight from Abbotsford Airport (CYXX), BC to Calgary/Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB with 1 pilot on board. While in cruise at 21 000 feet ASL, approximately 30nm East of Kelowna International Airport (CYLW), BC, the pilot observed a slight drop in fuel flow to the right engine, a Teledyne Continental Motors TSIO-520-NB (S/N: 504315). A short time later, the fuel flow dropped rapidly followed by reduced engine power. The pilot completed the emergency checklist for a suspected engine driven fuel pump failure, which calls for the Auxiliary Pump set to high, and this restored fuel flow and engine power to normal. The pilot elected to divert to CYLW and conduct a precautionary landing.During the descent to CYLW the aircraft experienced significant vibrations with the right hand engine power fluctuating. The pilot declared a MAYDAY, shut down the right engine, and proceeded with a single engine approach and landing. The aircraft landed without further incident. There were no injuries.Subsequent maintenance actions revealed the right hand engine driven fuel pump had experienced partially seized internals but the shaft was still intact which allowed the pump to cavitate and/or continue pumping fuel creating power fluctuations. The fuel pump was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GDTM, a Cessna 441 aircraft operated by Lake central Airways, was conducting a post maintenance test flight from Toronto Buttonville Municipal Airport (CYKZ), ON to Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON with two flight crew members onboard. After receiving the clearance to climb to 8000 ft from ATC, the flight crew started climbing from 6000 ft to 8000 ft. Once the altitude was reached, the pilot in command disengaged the autopilot and shutdown the first engine to start the test procedure. The pilot monitoring was reading the checklist and both the pilot in command and pilot monitoring noticed an altitude of approximatly 8450 ft and started to correct their altitude back to 8000 ft. At that same time ATC also asked C-GDTM to maintain 8000 ft as the altitude deviation resulted in a loss of separation with an other aircraft at 9000 ft, C-FEXF, a Morningstar Air Express Inc Cessna 208 B conducting flight MAL7056 from Greater Sudbury Airport (CYSB), ON to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. Afterwards, C-GDTM requested ATC a block altitude between 8000 and 9000 ft which was granted once traffic cleared the area. The crew completed their tests and landed in CYKF without further incident.

C-FFAR, a Beech King Air 200 operated by Vanguard Air Inc. as flight VN01 Trainer, was conducting a local training flight and departed Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG) MB. When the training was completed, the aircraft returned to CYWG. The flight crew made a gear down selection and received a gear down and locked indication. At approximately 1 mile final, the flight crew noticed the nose gear light was not illuminated and carried out a missed approach. There was no gear unsafe warning horn nor a red light in the gear handle. The tower indicated to the flight crew the nose gear appeared down. The flight crew cycled the gear and received a main gear down and locked indication but did not recieve a nose gear light. A manual gear extension was conducted and the nose gear down light came on momentarily, then went out. The flight crew did not declare an emergency but did request ARFF on standby. The aircraft subsequently landed without incident.The operator's maintenance replaced the landing gear indication light bulbs. Gear swings were completed and no faults were found. Aircraft was returned to service.

N2971M, a privately registered Piper PA-12 with 1 pilot on board, was conducting a VFR flight from Goldendale Airport (S20), Washington, USA to Merrill Field Airport (PAMR), Alaska, USA. After completing the leg from Abbotsford International Airpot (CYXX) BC, to the Kamloops Airport (CYKA) BC, and during the landing, the aircraft bounced on initial contact with the runway surface. During the second runway contact, as the aircraft was settling, the aircraft began an airframe shimmy which resulted in a loss of control. The aircraft veered off the centerline and towards the runway edge. As the aircraft approached the grass, the RH main landing gear folded under the fuselage and the aircraft rotated 180 degrees with the RH wing making contact with the ground. The aircraft came to rest in the grass alongside the runway on its belly. The pilot egressed the aircraft with minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GDUK, a Delta Helicopters Ltd. Bell 204B, was conducting external load operations 25 NM NW of Wabasca (CEE5), AB with only the pilot on board. On approach, while longlining a carousel load with sixty boxes of trees, two of four nets became snagged with a dead tree on the ground. The pilot released the load and returned to the departure site. There was no damage to the aircraft and there were no persons in the vicinity of the load release.

C-GRUU, a Beech B300 operated by Carson Air Ltd, was conducting a flight from Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International (CYXC), BC, to Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC, with 2 flight crew and 3 passengers on board. At approximately 25 minutes into the flight, the flight crew observed the red warning light illuminate on the landing gear handle and referred to the checklist while continuing the flight to CYLW. The flight crew confirmed there was sufficient hydraulic fluid in the system and at 10 miles from CYLW, they selected landing gear down. The landing gear did not extend and the crew proceeded with the landing gear manual extension checklist that successfully lowered the gear, illuminated the 3 green landing gear lights, and extinguished the red warning light on the landing gear handle. The flight crew advised tower of the landing gear issue and requested ARFF on standby. The aircraft landed safely with no reported injuries or damage to the aircraft. Maintenance found the electric motor that drives the landing gear hydraulic power pack assembly had failed. The operator filed an SDR (SDR# 20210520014) along with 2 previous SDRs in 2016 and 2017 for similar failures.

C-GDCC, a Starlink Aviation Inc. Bombardier BD-100-1A10, was performing a flight between Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON and Melbourne Intl. (KMLB), FL, USA.  During the flight, flight crew declared an emergency (PAN PAN) with US Air traffic control due to flap issues.  Flight crew elected to divert back to YYZ where the plane landed without further issues.

C-GAHR, a Bell 206B Helicopter was conducting main rotor blades track and balance checks at Langley Regional Airport (CYNJ), BC. As the helicopter was lifting off (with the intent to reposition on the apron), the helicopter pitched nose down and banked left so that the main rotor blades impacted the ground. The helicopter came to rest on its left hand side. Both occupants were able to egress themselves and sustained only minor injuries. There was no post-impact fire, and both firefighters and local police responded. The helicopter sustained substantial damage.

The Guelph Flight Centre Cessna 172 (C-FWAZ) was on a local training flight with the instructor and student on board. On approach to runway 24 at Guelph Airpark (CNC4), ON, with the instructor flying the aircraft, the aircraft landed long and suffered a runway excursion. The aircraft came to stop off the runway amongst trees and shrubs. The aircraft was substantially damaged and the student suffered from serious but non-life threatening injuries. Runway 24 is asphalt covered and 2006 feet in length and 40 feet in width. The runway has a displaced threshold of 730 feet. It was reported that weather and aircraft mechanical issues were not factors in this occurrence.

CF-NPM, a privately registered Cessna 150A, was conducting circuits at the Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, with 1 pilot on board. During the occurrence landing, the aircraft ballooned and bounced. The second runway contact was primarily with the RH main wheel followed by the LH main wheel. The left main landing gear collapsed causing the propeller and the left wing to contact the runway as the aircraft settled on its belly. The pilot egressed the aircraft and was later treated for minor injuries. The aircraft began leaking fuel which was contained by ARFF; there was no fire. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GJBV, un Beech A100 exploité par Sky Jet M.G. inc. sous l'indicatif LSJ512 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Port-Menier, Qc (CYPN) à destination de Havre St-Pierre, Qc (CYGV). Peu après le décollage, un problème de train d'atterrissage bloqué a été rapporté. Le vol a été dérouté vers Sept-îles (CYZV) puis vers Québec/Jean Lesage, Qc (CYQB), où une urgence a été déclarée. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée et le train d’atterrissage a été déployé avec succès. L'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre à CYQB à 15:56 UTC.Suite à l'inspection de l'appareil par la maintenance, l'actuateur du train principal de droite défectueux.

C-FYRH, un Pilatus PC12/47 exploité par Panorama fixed wings Ltd. sous l'indicatif PNO729 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Iqaluit (CYFB), NU à destination de Cape Dorset (CYTE), NU. Peu après le décollage, lors de la rétraction du train d'atterrissage, les indications ''HYD'' et "CAWS Light" sont apparues et les 3 indications de train étaient rouges. Le disjoncteur "HYD CTL" s'est déclenché. Un retour vers CYFB a été demandé. Après un délai en circuit d'attente, lors du retour vers CYFB l'équipage a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et le train a été sécurisé et confirmé avec 3 indications vertes, une urgence a été déclarée de façon préventive et l'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre sur la piste 34.Lors de la procédure de dépannage en maintenance, une diode défectueuse a été identifiée. La cause de la défectuosité de la diode est inconnue.

C-GCVS, un Beech 200C exploité par Max Aviation sous l'indicatif MAX210 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB), à destination d'Ottawa, ON (CYOW). Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en croisière au niveau de vol (FL) 200, une perte d'espacement est survenue avec C-GHQL, un Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par Hydro-Québec sous l'indicatif HYD181, qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, Qc (CYUY) et qui quittait le FL210 en descente vers l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Qc (CYUL). L'espacement entre MAX210 et HYD181 a été réduit à 4.6 milles marins horizontalement et 600 pieds verticalement alors que l'espacement minimal requis est de 5 milles marins horizontalement et 1000 pieds verticalement.

C-FAWJ, a Boeing 737-8CT aircraft was conducting Westjet flight WJA556 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Kitchener-Waterloo (CYKF), ON. A second aircraft, C-GGFR, a Cessna 152 being operated by the Waterloo-Wellington Flying Club, was on a VFR flight from Guelph Airport (CNC4) to CYKF. While WJA556 was on RNAV Runway 26 approach to CYKF, the flight crew responded by climbing in response to a resolution advisory warning of traffic (C-GGFR) below them and in close proximity. Once clear of the traffic, WJA556 was able to continue with the approach to landing. The flight crew of WJA556 was not advised of the traffic ahead of time. The separation was reduced to 0.4 nm laterally and 400 feet vertically.

C-GCUV, an amateur-built Zenith 750, was flying circuits on a local flight from Westlock (CES4),AB. While conducting a touch-and-go landing, the aircraft contacted the runway surface with a high rate of descent and bounced. Following the bounce, the aircraft descended again contacting the runway surface on the nose wheel and the nose landing gear collapsed. The aircraft came to rest on the runway. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured. The ELT did not activate.

The Jazz Aviation LP, DHC-8-400 aircraft (Flt 8287, registration C-GGAH) departed Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ) and was destined for Timmins Victor M Power Airport (CYTS), ON, when at approximately 10 000 ft ASL, the flight crew received a #2 hydraulic ISO Valve fault. After following the QRH the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and decided to return to CYYZ. The flight crew performed an alternate gear extension and landed without furthur incident with ARFF standing by.

C-FHPQ, un hélicoptère Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 exploité par Go Hélico inc effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) à destination d'une aire d'atterrissage aménagée à 145 milles nautiques au nord du point de départ, avec un pilote et quatre passagers à bord. Lors de la manoeuvre d'approche, l'appareil a perdu de l'altitude, le patin droit a accroché des arbres et l'appareil a poursuivi sa descente. Une fois au sol, l'appareil s'est renversé sur le coté droit. Les occupants ont évacué et n'ont subi aucunes blessures. L’appareil a subi des dommages importants, il n'y a pas eu de feu ni de renversement de fluides. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) a été activée manuellement par le pilote.

C-GTCG, a Piper PA-34-200T aircraft operated by KBM Resources Group, was conducting a survey flight from Dauphin/Lt Col W.G. (Billy) Barker, VC (CYDN), MB. When the aircraft was approximately 40 NM west of CYDN and 1 hour and 50 minutes into the flight, the right engine (Teledyne Continental LTSIO-360-EB1) began to run rough. The flight crew elected to return to CYDN. The oil pressure remained normal; however, the flight crew conducted a precautionary engine shut down. The subsequent landing was conducted successfully with the right engine inoperative. The operator's examination of the engine revealed a cylinder with broken stud on a rocker-shaft hold-down clamp. The operator submitted an SDR regarding the failed stud.

C-FCHD, a Bell 205A-1 helicopter operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd, was conducting water bucket operations near the fire base at Marchand, MB. The cargo-hook release switch had been de-activated prior to bucket operation in accordance with the operator's standard operating procedures. While in the climb at 70 knots, after releasing a full load of water onto a fire, the cargo hook released un-commanded. The water bucket fell into an open area and was retrieved un-damaged. During the previous 2 days the helicopter had made 129 drops with the occurrence hook and bucket. The operator's maintenance personnel duplicated the un-commanded release while testing with a spare bucket. The cargo hook was replaced and operations resumed without further incident.

The Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service Messerschmitt MBB-BK117 B-2D, C-GBNH, was operating on an local air ambulance flight as STAR5 from Grande Prairie (CYQU), AB. Shortly after takeoff from CYQU the flight crew noticed the #1 engine oil pressure was fluctuating. While climbing through 500 feet AGL, the pressure continued to increase and was observed to climb beyond the upper limit. The flight crew reduced power on the #1 engine (Avco Lycoming LTS-101-850B2) to stabilize the oil pressure. Power reduction provided no change to the high oil pressure. The flight crew actioned the QRH and shut down the #1 engine. The flight crew declared an emergency and returned to CYQU and conducted a single engine landing without further issue. The 4 crew members onboard received no injuries. Company maintenance found the oil pressure indication cannon plug in the engine accessory bay to be loose with evidence of water ingress. The contacts were cleaned and the cannon plug reinstalled. A post-maintenance engine run was carried out with no further indication issues and released for service.

C-FSPM, a Gulfstream American Corporation 690D Aero Commander aircraft operated by the Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency (Air Operations), was conducting flight BD161 from Prince Albert/Glass Field (CYPA), SK to La Ronge/Barber Field (CYVC), SK. During the initial climb after taking off from Runway 08, the cabin air became hazy and smoky. The flight crew communicated with Prince Albert Radio FSS and advised that the aircraft would perform a 180 degree turn and return to Runway 26. The flight crew conducted the actions for smoke in the cockpit and closed the bleed air valves. The smoke subsequently began to clear. The flight crew declined emergency services and the subsequent landing was uneventful. The operator's maintenance personnel determined that the environmental system turbocharger oil-pump seal had failed allowing oil mist to enter the cabin air system. The turbocharger was replaced. The operator submitted a SDR (20210514012).

C-GTYC, an Aviat A-1 (Husky) operated by Hoarfrost River Huskies Ltd, was conducting a VFR repositioning flight from the Yellowknife ice / float base (CEN9), NT to Ft. Nelson (CYYE), BC for maintenance. During the landing roll in CYYE the pilot applied brakes and the aircraft pulled to the left and ground looped. The aircraft departed the left side of the runway into the grass. The aircraft was able to taxi to the ramp.Following the flight the aircraft was inspected and the minor damage was repaired.

C-FTIR, a First Air, Bradley Air Services Aerospatiale ATR42-500, was operating as flight AKT237 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB with 3 crew and 13 passengers on board. C-GDEW, a Westjet Encore De Havilland Dash-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3351 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB with 4 crew and 29 passengers onboard. AKT237 was cleared to the LOBTI fix and to plan for the RNAV Z approach to Runway 30; however, the controller did not clarify whether the TETAG2 RNAV standard arrival procedure (STAR) was still active or cancelled. The LOBTI fix is common to both the RNAV Z approach and the TETAG2 RNAV STAR. Upon reaching LOBTI, AKT237 turned south and followed the approach procedure which resulted in a loss of separation with WEN3351 who had been cleared for the RNAV (RNP) Y approach for Runway 30. Lateral separation reduced to 1.3 NM where 3.0 NM was required. Both aircraft were at the same altitude. ATC separation was regained when the controller turned AKT237 to a heading of 310 degrees and WEN3351 to a heading of 250 degrees. Neither aircraft received or responded to a TCAS RA and the flight crew of AKT237 had visually acquired WEN3351. Both aircraft landed at CYEG without further incident.

The Quad City Challenger II Advanced Ultralight (C-IGMZ) was on a flight from Coldwater, Ontario to Stouffville, Ontario (CBB2) with the pilot as the sole occupant. During the initial climb the pilot encountered lateral control issues at 20 feet ASL but continued flight instead of trying to land due to proximity of trees. The aircraft climbed to 100 feet ASL and the pilot attempted to land in a farmer's field but due to the control issues impacted the ground. The aircraft was substantially damaged, and the pilot receivied minor injuries. Shoulder harnesses were available and the pilot was wearing them.

C-GHEX, un hélicoptère Aerospatiale AS350 B2 exploité par Héli-Express Inc., effectuait un vol d’élingage le long d’une ligne à haute tension à 1.7 NM au nord de Les Escoumins, QC. La boîte de transmission de rotor de queue et le rotor de queue se sont séparés de l’hélicoptère alors qu’il était en vol. Le pilote a largué la charge à l’élingue et s'est dirigé vers une piste en terre battu non loin de sa position pour y effectuer un atterrissage d'urgence. Lors de l'approche, il y a eu une décélération et l'hélicoptère s'est mis à tourner sur lui-même vers la gauche. Le pilote n'a pas pu reprendre le contrôle de l'hélicoptère et a décidé de couper l'arrivée de carburant pour arrêter le mouvement de rotation et tenter un atterrissage sans moteur. L'aéronef a percuté le sol durement en position verticale sans basculer sur le côté. La radiobalise de repérage d’urgence a été activée. Un deuxième hélicoptère s'est posé peu de temps après avec des secouristes et le pilote blessé a été transporté à l’hôpital.

C-GOSX, a Piper PA-60 aircraft operated by Forest Protection Limited, was returning to Fredericton Intl (CYFC), NB on a VFR flight after conducting night currency circuits at Saint John (CYSJ), NB with one pilot onboard. While on final approach to Runway 27 in CYFC, the pilot felt an impact on the left side of the aircraft and believed that a possible bird strike had occurred. After landing, company maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft and it was determined that the aircraft had come in contact with trees. The aircraft sustained minor damage. No injuries were reported.The operator’s maintenance department will be removing the left engine and propeller for inspection and making minor repairs to the left landing gear door assembly.

C-GTTW, a privately operated Beech C24R departed Delta Heritage Air Park (CAK3), BC for Boundary Bay airport (CZBB), BC to have maintenance performed on the braking system. The aircraft landed on Runway 07 and upon initial application of the brakes to exit at Taxiway 'C', the aircraft pulled to the left; nearing the taxiway he applied the brakes again, and the aircraft departed the runway surface veering into the grass where it struck the taxiway sign with the left wing leading edge. Damage included a crushing puncture of the sheet metal and exposure of the main wing spar. The aircraft was towed to a maintenance facility for further evaluation of structural damages incurred.

C-GIAC, a Nutrien Ltd. Gulfstream Aerospace GV-SP, was conducting flight from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Dallas Love Field (KDAL), TX.  During the approach 25 nm north of KDAL at 5000 feet, Flight crew experienced a TCAS (Traffic Collision Avoidance System) TA (Traffic Advisory) shortly followed by a TCAS RA “Climb”. RA (resolution advisory) was actioned by flight crew and they advised ATC. Flight continued and aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GMAI, a Boeing 737-200 operated by Air Inuit, was conducting flight AIE704 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) to La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) with 33 passengers and 4 crew members on board. While on approach to CYGL, when Flap 1 setting was selected the flaps did not respond. The crew performed the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) checklist, and the flaps were lowered with an alternate selection. The crew declared an emergency and briefed the cabin crew. The aircraft landed in CYGL and taxied to the terminal without further incident.

C-GWHM, a privately owned Bell 206L-3, was departing from the owner's property on a local flight with the pilot/owner and two passengers on board. In hover at approximately 50 feet AGL, the helicopter began to yaw to the right, completing at least two rotations. The pilot reduced power, descended vertically to make an emergency landing, and was able to stop the yawing motion before making contact with the ground. The landing was hard enough to significantly deform the skids, and resulted in a downward bend in the tail boom between the main fuselage and the horizontal stabilizer. There were no injuries. The helicopter will be moved to a maintenance facility for inspection and repair.

C-GKGS, an Atlantic Charters (legal name Manan Air Services Inc.) Piper PA-42, was conducting a flight from Fredericton airport (CYFC), NB to Grand Manan airport (CCN2), NB. The aircraft touched down on Runway 06 (paved surface 3009 feet long, 75 feet wide) at CCN2 at about 0423 ADT in rainy conditions. Following touchdown, the aircraft moved to the right side of the runway until the right landing gear main wheel began to roll along the turf beyond the edge of the paved surface. The crew was unable to regain directional control and the aircraft left the paved surface with all three landing gear wheels rolling in the soft, wet ground. The aircraft slid to a stop with nose pointing north. Both propellers sustained blade damage; the right landing gear outboard door assembly was also damaged. Two runway edge lights were damaged. The 2 flight crewmembers were the only occupants, and were not injured.

C-FCRZ, an ATR 72-202 operated by Calm Air, was conducting flight CAV484 from Thompson (CYTH), MB. to Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU with only 2 pilots on board. When abeam Churchill (CYYQ), MB at FL210, the crew observed a burning odour followed by smoke in the cockpit. They also noted a high ITT and erratic oil pressure indications on the #1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW124B). The crew carried out the engine shutdown checklist and declared an emergency with ATC. The aircraft diverted to CYYQ, where an uneventful landing was carried out with emergency vehicles standing by. The operator is sending maintenance personel to CYYQ to examine the aircraft.

C-FPCV, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Textron (Beech) 1900C, was conducting flight PCO866 from Port Hardy airport (CYZT), BC to Vancouver Int'l airport (CYVR), BC with 2 flight crew members and 9 passengers on board. When climbing through 16 000 feet ASL the aircraft began to yaw to the right. The aircraft's RH engine, a PT6A-65B (S/N: PCE32157), was indicating a significant reduction in torque and an increased interstage turbine temperature (ITT). As the ITT continued to increase, a burning smell was perceived in the cockpit. The flight crew carried out a precautionary engine shutdown. The pilot monitoring declared an emergency (MAYDAY) and made the request to return to CYZT. The aircraft landed without further incident.Subsequent maintenance actions revealed the engine's compressor turbine disk had experienced a blade failure, leading to other blades on the disk to fail. The operator's maintenance has indicated that with the compressor no longer turning at an optimal speed, the engine power was reduced and was accompanied by a build up of heat. The engine's abnormally hot bleed air entering the air cycle machine (ACM) likely created the burning smell. The operator has shipped the engine to the manufacturer for a comprehensive teardown.

C-GOIC, a Northern Thunderbird Air Textron (Beech) B300 (King Air 350) aircraft, was operating as flight NTA9490 from Prince George airport (CYXS), BC to Dease Lake aerodrome (CYDL), BC with 2 flight crew members and 5 passengers on board. During climb after departure, while in IMC, the flight crew received an annunciation for a LH GEN TIE failure. This was accompanied with a data processing unit (DPU) failure and LH electronic flight instrument system (EFIS) screen failures. Throughout the next 15 minutes the flight crew experienced multiple, at times compound, failures of LH GEN, LH GEN TIE, RH GEN, RH GEN TIE, BAT TIE, #1 and #2 Inverters, Autopilot, #1 and #2 heading reference systems, and avionics equipment including radios and transponders. The aircraft's RH attitude instrument remained unaffected and control of the aircraft was maintained at all times. The flight crew declared an emergency. The flight returned to CYXS and landed without further incident. The operator's maintenance has filed a service difficulty report (SDR - 20210429009) and continues to perform actions to identify the source of the faults. The operator’s subsequent maintenance actions revealed a failure of the RH generator control unit (Lucas GCU P/N 51538-001A, S/N 99465) created the series of electrical malfunctions on C-GOIC.

The North Cariboo Air de Havilland Dash 8-300, C-GLWN, was operating as flight NCB4098 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Primrose (CEN6), AB with 3 crew and no passengers on board. While climbing through 16 700 feet ASL, the flight crew observed an engine torque roll-back on the number 1 engine (PW123, S/N AE0129). There were no additional warnings, cautions or changes to other engine parameters. The flight crew carried out the QRH items and declared an emergency. The flight was diverted to Edmonton (CYEG), AB and ARFF was requested for the arrival. The flight landed safely and after an assessment by ARFF, taxied to the apron.Maintenance update: After extensive troubleshooting and analysis of the FDR data it was determined that the number 1 engine Engine Electronic Controller (P/N 798213-3-007, S/N C94120062) had an intermittent fault. It was replaced and all engine checks were carried out and found to be functioning normally. The aircraft was put back in service.

C-GOGH, a Canadair CL-215-6B11 (Series CL-415) operated by the Province of Ontario, Ministry of Natural Resources, was conducting a local training flight at the Sault Ste. Marie Airport, ON (CYAM). While conducting the third circuit on runway 12, the flight crew inadvertently landed the aircraft with the landing gear retracted. The aircraft came to a stop on the runway surface. There was significant damage to the belly of the aircraft. There were no injuries.

C-GFPM, un Cessna 180K sur flotteurs en immatriculation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue au départ du lac Sacacomie, QC à destination du réservoir Taureau, QC,  situé à 5 milles nautiques au nord-est de l’aérodrome de Saint-Michel-des-Saints (CSM5) avec 1 pilote à bord. Lors de l’amerrissage, une rafale a déplacé l’appareil et le pilote a perdu le contrôle. L’aile gauche aurait touché l’eau et l’avion s’est renversé. Le pilote a pu évacuer l’appareil. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GNLK, a Nolinor Aviation Boeing 737-200 was conducting flight NRL969 from Goose Lake (CGS2), NU to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with 3 crew members and 0 passengers on board. Approximately 150 nm NE of CYZF, the flight crew received a brief #2 engine fire indication. The crew initiated a descent to FL 240 in anticipation of shutting down the #2 engine. Once level at FL 240, the crew received the #2 engine fire indication continuously, and executed the appropriate checklist shutting down the #2 engine (Pratt and Whitney JT8D-17). The flight crew then declared a PAN PAN with ATC. The flight continued to its intended destination (CYZF), where an uneventful landing was completed. ARFF met the aircraft and an external inspection was completed. No evidence of fire was found, and the aircraft subsequently taxied to the company facility.Company mantenance inspected the aircraft and determined there was an erroneous fire indication due to a fault with a fire sensor loop on the #2 engine. The aircraft was repaired and subsequently returned to service.

C-GVXT, a privately registered Cessna 340A, was conducting a flight from Springbank (CYBW), AB to Grand Prairie (CYQU), AB with only the pilot on board. Approximately 40 minutes into the flight, the pilot observed an uncontrolled rise of the left engine (Teledyne Continental Motors TSIO-520-NB) turbine inlet temperature. In the process of troubleshooting the issue, the pilot noticed the EGT and CHT for the #5 cylinder on the left engine significantly below normal. The pilot then contacted ATC to inform them of the issue and elected to shut down the left engine. The decision was then made to divert to Red Deer, AB (CYQF). An uneventful single-engine approach and landing was completed at approximately 1452 MDT.

C-FDTV, a privately registered Robinson Helicopters R-44 II, was conducting a training flight with a student pilot and flight instructor onboard. The flight originated from a private acreage approximately 5.5 nm NE of Grand Prairie, AB (CYQU) and proceeded to Grand Prairie (CYQU), AB to take on fuel. The aircraft then departed on a navigation training exercise and proceeded SW of CYQU. Approximately 30 nm SW of CYQU the crew elected to land in an open field. After a short break, the student pilot attempted to depart from the field. During the lift-off, the helicopter began a rapid uncommanded roll to the left. The instructor subsequently assumed control of the helicopter and attempted to correct the beginning of the dynamic rollover and lift the helicopter into a hover. During the recovery, the tail rotor struck the ground and the helicopter began to yaw to the right. The instructor immediately landed the helicopter and shut down the engine. Both occupants subsequently evacuated the aircraft, there were no injuries.

C-GMOC, a Beechcraft King Air 200 aircraft operated by Alkan Air, was conducting MEDEVAC flight AKN513+ from Dawson City, YK (CYDA) to Whitehorse (CYXY), YK with 2 crew and 3 passengers on board. On the downwind portion of the circuit during arrival into CYXY, the flight crew selected the flaps to approach. The flaps subsequently fully extended. The flight crew selected the flaps to up, but the flaps did not retract. The aircraft completed an uneventful landing on RWY 32L. During the landing roll on the runway, smoke began to enter the cabin/cockpit. The flight crew declared an emergency and requested ARFF respond to the aircraft. The aircraft taxied clear of RWY 32L onto RWY 20, came to a stop, and the crew initiated an emergency evacuation in accordance with company standard operating procedures. ARFF arrived on scene and inspected the aircraft, no fire was observed.   Subsequent aircraft inspection by company maintenance found the cause of the smoke to be a failed electric flap actuator motor. The flap motor was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FIAY, an amateur-built SUPER 12 (on straight floats) was being operated on Fraser Lake (CBJ8), BC in glassy water conditions. While conducting a post-maintenance flight, low over Fraser Lake, the pilot entered a turn with the intent to return for landing. In the turn, the aircraft contacted the surface of the water and nosed over. The pilot egressed from the right door of the partially submerged and inverted aircraft. The pilot was rescued by locals who saw the crash and launched their boat to rescue the pilot. The pilot, who was sitting on one of the floats, was brought to shore where EMS and Fire services were waiting. The pilot was transported to Vanderhoof, BC hospital and treated for minor injuries.The pilot had never taken dunker training, but had watched videos and read related articles. He was able to release his seatbelt and egressed through the already open right side door (opened by itself during crash sequence). The floats were above water and the pilot was able to pull himself on top of a float where he waited for rescue. There was a PFD inside the aircraft, but the pilot did not access it.

C-GYLD, a Rockwell International 690B aircraft operated by Mag Aerospace, was conducting a local training flight from Dryden Regional (CYHD), ON as flight BD160 with 2 crew on board. During the initial takeoff, the crew selected landing gear up and heard a bang followed by an in-transit landing gear indication. The crew then decided to select the landing gear down and received an unsafe nose gear indication. The crew conducted a fly-by and received notification that the nose gear seemed to be extended. An emergency was declared and the crew proceeded to land the aircraft on Runway 30. During landing, the aircraft settled on the main gear and the crew then received a nose gear safe indication. As the nose gear settled the aircraft immediately veered to the right and came to a stop with the right main gear off the side of the runway. An inspection by the operator revealed that the nose gear wheel was turned to the right and did not centered.

C-GMWT, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 operated by Wasaya Airways under CARs Subpart 604, was enroute from Pickle Lake, ON (CYPL) to Opapimiskan Lake, ON (CKM8) with a crew of 3 and 1 passenger on board. While on approach into CKM8, the crew selected the windshield heat "ON" and heard arcing, followed by a flame and smoke coming from the first officer's windshield electrical interface. The crew immediately turned the windshield heat off and the flame and smoke dissipated. The crew then landed the aircraft safely and while taxing to the ramp, the first officer's windshield cracked. The operator will advise the TSB of their findings.

C-GJBV, un Beech A100 exploité par Sky Jet M.G. Inc sous l’indicatif 102 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de l’aéroport de Port-Menier, QC (CYPN) à destination de Havre-Saint-Pierre, QC (CYGV). Lors de l’atterrissage du premier officier, l’avion a été ralenti sans utiliser les freins jusqu’à environ 55 nœuds. Le commandant a alors pris les contrôles et appliqué les freins. L’avion a tourné subitement vers la gauche, le commandant a tenté de reprendre la maitrise de la direction en appliquant du frein droit et en renversant la poussée des moteurs. L’avion est sorti de piste en frappant une lumière de piste avec la roue de nez et lorsque le train d’atterrissage était sur le gravier, le contrôle directionnel est revenu à la normale. Le commandant a ensuite circulé l’avion jusqu’au tablier sans encombre. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé. Après vérification avec la maintenance, les assemblages du train d’atterrissage principal ont été remplacés ainsi que le pneu de la roue de nez. La qualité des freins a été vérifiée lors du démontage des roues des essais de freinage n’ont révélé aucune faute. L’avion a été remis en service.

C-GKON, Voyageur Airways flight VAL100, a De Havilland DHC-8-102 aircraft, was conducting a local flight near North Bay (CYYB) to carry out some maintenance checks. During a system check for the #1 propeller governing system, the #1 propeller could not be controlled while the power levers were at flight idle. A precautionary shut down of the #1 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW120A) was carried out in accordance with the Dash 8 QRH. The QRH items were completed and the aircraft returned to North Bay airport for a visual approach. North Bay Radio was advised of the single engine status, no emergency was declared nor required. The approach and landing were normal without any further occurrences.This is the second occurrence involving this aircraft and the propeller governing system, Voyageur is consulting with external service providers to troubleshot and rectify the problem.

C-GAJS, a Latitude Air Ambulance Learjet 35A, was conducting a flight between John C. Munro Hamilton Intl. (CYHM), ON and Lethbridge County (CYQL), AB.  During cruise 20 nautical miles east of Washington Island Airport (2P2), WI (USA) at Flight level 380, Flight crew declared an emergency due to power loss on left hand engine. The flight crew actioned emergency checklist and attempted restart was unsuccessful.  The flight crew diverted back to CYHM where it landed without further incident.

C-GCMB, un appareil de construction amateur Murphy Rebel en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue au départ et à destination de l’aéroport de Joliette, QC (CSG3) avec 1 pilote à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage, l’avion a freiné plus subitement qu’anticipé par le pilote et a fait un cheval de bois. Le pilote n’a subi aucune blessure. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée. L’appareil a subi des dommages.

At approximately 1550 Central Daylight Time on 25 April 2021, a Great Slave Helicopters' Airbus Helicopters AS350-B2 (registration C-FYDA) departed a remote camp located on Russell Island, Nunavut on a day VFR flight to Resolute Bay Airport, Nunavut (CYRB). On board was the pilot, an aircraft maintenance engineer, and a biologist. While flying over Griffith Island, approximately 12 nautical miles southwest of CYRB, the helicopter impacted the snow-covered terrain at approximately 1632 Central Daylight Time. The aircraft was destroyed; however, the emergency locator transmitter did not transit a distress signal to the search and rescue satellites. A post-crash fire consumed much of the fuselage area. There were no survivors.

C-FXRJ, a Summit Air Ltd. Avro RJ-100, was conducting a flight from Kelowna International Airport (CYLW), BC to Northwest Regional Airport, Terrace, BC (CYXT) . On approach for Runway 33 at CYXT, the flight crew was prepared for a 10 kts crosswind. While in the flare at approximately 50 feet, the aircraft started a rapid descent. The crew pitched the nose up slightly to arrest the descent and landed the aircraft. The aircraft taxied off the runway without further issues. Damage to the tail bumper fairing of the aircraft was observed by the flight crew on a post-flight walk around. The damage was indicative of a tail strike. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and verified the damage was localized to scrapes and missing paint. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GFFN, a Boeing 737-33A operated by Air Inuit Ltd., was conducting IFR flight AIE730 from Ottawa MacDonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW) ON. to Saskatoon / John G. Diefenbaker Intl. ( CYXE) SK. As C-GFFN was at 5000 feet and approaching the ALUTU waypoint on the RNAV 27 at CYXE, the aircraft's TCAS indicated a target at 4 miles, 1 o'clock position and 400 feet above. While turning and establishing the aircraft on the final course, C-GFFN received a TCAS resolution advisory (TA) for conflicting traffic and the crew descended the aircraft to approximately 4800 feet. C-GIQB, a Cessna 172 operated by Mitchinson Flying Service Limited was conducting a VFR flight from CYXE to Humboldt (CJU4) SK. C-GIQB was level at 5400 feet ASL on a east bound heading. The pilot was informed by ATC of the conflicting traffic, a Boeing 737 at the 1 or 2 o'clock position and instructed not to go south of their current track. C-GIQB had the traffic insight.

C-FAMC, a Fairchild SA227-AC operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting flight PAG190 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG) MB to Thompson (CYTH) MB. When approximately 100 NM south of CYTH, when the right-hand engine (TPE331-11U-612G) failed. The flight crew secured the engine and declared an emergency with ATC. The aircraft landed safely in CYTH with ARFF on standby.The operator's maintenance removed the engine driven fuel pump and observed that the reduction gearbox fuel pump drive gear had failed. An SDR has been submitted.

C-GSCE, a privately registered Cessna 170B, was conducting a proficiency training flight from High River (CEN4), AB with one pilot onboard. On landing RWY 15 (gravel surface) at CEN4, the aircraft nosed over at very low speed and came to rest upside down causing damage to the propeller, both wings and the empennage. The pilot exited the aircraft without injury.

Voyageur Airways flight VAL100, a De Havilland DHC-8-102 aircraft (C-GKON), was conducting a local flight near North Bay (CYYB) to carry out some maintenance checks. During a system check for the #1 propeller governing system, the propeller exceeded limitations (overspeed) and became uncontrollable. The #1 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW120A) was shut down IAW the Dash 8 QRH for propeller overspeed. During the shutdown sequence, the primary method to feather the propeller failed requiring use of the alternate feathering system. The QRH items were completed and the aircraft returned to North Bay airport for a visual approach. North Bay Radio was advised of the single engine status, no emergency was declared nor required. The approach and landing were normal without any further occurrences.After assessing the status of the aircraft after landing, the flight crew proceeded to taxi back to the Hanga. Maintenance personnel were on board during the systems check flight, and are investigating the problem.

C-GGOY, un Dash 8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation sous l'indicatif JZA8701, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean-Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Montréal/Pierre-Elliott-Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 3 membres d’équipage et 34 passagers à son bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en approche finale pour la piste 06R à CYUL, le voyant “Left Gear Unsafe” s’est allumé lors de la sélection du train d’atterrissage en position sortie. L’équipage a effectué une remontée et une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée et et le voyant est demeuré allumé. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 06R sans encombre et l’appareil s’est immobilisé. Le train d’atterrissage a été sécurisé et l’appareil a été remorqué à la porte d’embarquement.

C-GYUA, a Mitsubishi MU-2 aircraft operated by Thunder Airlines, was conducting flight THU890 from Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON to Timmins Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON under instrument flight rules (IFR). While on descent to CYTS, THU890 was cleared for a contact approach on runway 21, traffic appeared on the traffic collision avoiding system (TCAS) screen and was initially not conflicting. The aircraft was identified as C-GEON, a privately registered Cessna P210N aircraft, conducting a flight from Timmins Victor M. Power Airport (CYTS), ON to Greater Sudbury Airport (CYSB), ON under visual flight rules (VFR).C-GEON subsequently appeared to turn towards THU890; the flight crew reacted by levelling at 5000 feet to avoid traffic. While C-GEON continued  to climb towards THU890, THU890 initiated a turn to the right as an evasive measure to avoid traffic. C-GEON was observed on TCAS to pass at the same altitude at approximatly 2 NM lateral separation.  The crew informed Timmins FSS of the event upon landing. The crew reported no TCAS alert for this event and recorded a defect due to onboard system displaying ''TCAS inoperative or connection lost'' later the same day.

C-GJJF, un Beechcraft BE10 exploité par Propair sous l’indicatif PRO4230 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Alors que l’appareil était en vol de croisière, à environ 30 minutes de CYUL les paramètres d’un des 2 moteur (Pratt & Whitney PT6A-28) ont commencé à donner des indications erratiques. L’équipage a fermé le moteur par mesure préventive, et a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN). L'appareil s"est posé sans encombre à YUL. La maintenance a remplacé un FCU et l'appareil a été remis en service.

C-FDND, a DeHavilland DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines, was conducting flight PVL1925 from St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL to Goose Bay (CYYR), NL. During climb through approximately 12000 feet, the #2 engine reverted to manual mode with the ECU going off line. At approximately FL215 the crew noted a yaw and observed that the #2 engine torque indication had decreased. Shortly after, the engine oil pressure warning light illuminated and the crew noted a low oil pressure indication as the engine was shutting down. The QRH engine failure checklist was completed. The aircraft returned to CYYT and landed without incident with ARFF on standby. No injuries were reported and there was no damage to the aircraft.The operator’s maintenance department replaced various components, a test flight was carried out and the aircraft was returned to service. The operator is coordinating with the AMO to determine the cause of the engine power loss.

C-GHBM, a Cessna C-172M owned by BP Aviation Ltd., was on a round robin VFR cross-country flight from Penticton (CYYF), BC to Princeton (CYDC), BC with 1 student pilot on board. Shortly after C-GHBM lifted off from Runway 04 at CYDC, the aircraft  bounced on the right side of the runway. The pilot rejected the take-off and landed on the grass next to the runway. Despite power reduction and brake application, the aircraft went through the airport fence, down a small embankment, and came to rest on Highway 5A against a concrete barrier. The student pilot egressed approximately 30 seconds after the aircraft stopped; he sustained minor injuries. There was a fuel spill from the aircraft; however, no post-impact fire. The aircraft sustained substantial damage and the ELT did not activate.

C-GKUK, a Dash 8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA 7932 from Toronto Leaster B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON to Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT), ON with 4 crew members and 50 passengers onboard. While on initial climb, the nose landing gear (NLG) light remained green after selecting the gear retraction. The flight crew declared an emergency and elected to return to CYYZ and performed an alternate landing gear extension. On the first attempt, the nose landing gear indication was red and another aircraft confirmed the NLG still up. The crew then pulled the alternate release handle harder and suddenly the NLG doors opened and the gear locked down with the normal and alternate indications both showing green. JZA 7932 landed runway 24R without incident with emergency response vehicles standing by. The aircraft was towed to the gate from taxiway D4.Company maintenance conducted an inspection and found the nose gear light always on during gear swings. The selector landing gear control unit has been replaced and tested serviceable.

The pilot of a Victoria Flying Club Cessna 172S, C-FGIM, was following other aircraft in the circuit for Runway 09 at Victoria Intl. airport (CYYJ), BC when, on final approach to land, ATC advised winds were 220 at 06 knots. The pilot elected to continue the approach at 70 KIAS and 10 degrees of flaps. While in the flare, the propeller struck the runway. The aircraft veered toward the runway's edge, and the right wing tip contacted the ground before the aircraft came to rest. The pilot exited Runway 09 at Taxiway Golf. ATC advised ARFF who attended the scene. The pilot was wearing both lap and shoulder harness, and was not injured. The aircraft was towed to the flying club facility.

C-GRXV, a Pacific Professional Flight Center Cessna 172M, was on a local VFR flight to and from Boundary Bay Airport (CZBB), BC as part of the commercial pilot training program. Upon returning to the airfield, the winds reported at Vancouver International (CYVR), BC at 1100 PST, were 280 degrees true at 22 knots gusting 28 knots. On final approach to Runway 25 for a full stop landing, the aircraft was configured with 30 degrees of flaps. While in the flare, the aircraft was observed to veer to the left of the runway. The pilot initiated a go around, low and near the runway. During the go around, the right wing and nose dropped, resulting in the aircraft cartwheeling into the grassy area adjacent the runway. The pilot extricated himself from the wreckage. ATC called out the Delta / Boundary Bay Airport Fire Rescue to respond to the accident. A small post impact fire in the engine area was rapidly extinguished. The aircraft sustained significant damage to both wings, cabin, and engine area. The pilot, who was wearing both lap belt and shoulder harness, suffered only minor injuries. The pilot was taken to hospital for observation.

C-FASB, a Beech A100 aircraft operated by Thunder Airlines Limited, was conducting a local training flight near Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON. During departure the crew selected landing gear up and the gear would not retract. The flight crew cycled the gear and, moments later, noticed a smell of burning electrics. The crew turned off the electrics and pulled the landing gear circuit breaker. The electrics were then turned back on. The decison was made to return back to CYQT. Prior to landing the crew manually selected landing gear down and received 3 safe landing gear position indicator lights.  The aircraft landed safely and without incident.

On 09 April 2021, at 0540 UTC, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 767 (registration C-FGAJ) operating as CJT583 departed from John C Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), Ontario for an instrument flight rules flight to Calgary International Airport (CYYC), Alberta. Shortly after departure, as the flaps were moved from Position 1 to Flaps UP, the amber engine-indicating and crew-alerting system message LE SLAT ASYM (leading edge slat asymetry) appeared. The flight crew requested a level off to carry out the associated checklist and requested to return to CYHM. Due to landing weight requirements the flight crew entered a hold to burn off fuel. At 0612Z the flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency and requested that the aircraft rescue and firefighting personnel meet them after landing to check for hot brakes.
