The alternate trailing edge flap system was used to move trailing edge flaps for landing. The aircraft landed uneventfully at 0645 UTC.

C-GYRD, a Perimeter Aviation LP. Fairchild SA226-TC aircraft, was operating flight PAG07 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Lynn Lake (CYYL), MB with 2 crew members and 1 passenger on board. During approach, the landing gear did not extend. The flight crew decided to return to CYTH and requested emergency services to be on standby as a precaution. The landing gear was manually extended and the aircraft landed without further incident. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft.The operator's maintenance replaced the landing gear down actuator.

C-ILTX, un Nitro 200 (ultra-léger de base) en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis un champs dans la région de Pont-Rouge, QC. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en vol, celui-ci a percuté une ligne de distribution d’électricité avant de s’écraser au sol. Le pilote, seul à bord, a été blessé.

C-GFJK, an amateur built, Fokker DR1 tail dragger, triplane aircraft was landing at Brampton, Ontario (CNC3). During the landing roll, after the tail was lowered, the pilot applied the brakes, however, the left brake failed and the aircraft drifted to the right and went off the runway. The aircraft transitioned across the grass infield area before contacting the edge of a narrow taxiway, where the left wheel sustained damaged. The aircraft continued across the taxiway onto the grass where the left wheel dug into the soft ground and the aircraft came to rest on its nose. The aircraft sustained substantial damage; the pilot who was the sole occupant was not injured.

C-GURF, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Transwest Air Ltd, was conducting flight TW103 from Stony Rapids (CYSF), SK to Fond-du-Lac (CZFD), SK with 2 crew members and 9 passengers on board. During departure, when the crew selected gear up the main gear did not retract and the red gear handle light remained illuminated. The decision was made to return to CYSF. The crew manually extended the landing gear and received 3 safe landing gear position indicator lights. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed at CYSF without incident with ARFF on standby.The operator's maintenance subsequently inspected the aircraft and determined that the hydraulic power pack had failed.

C-GDSH, a Cessna 525C, operating under a Private Operator Registration Document (CAR604), was conducting a single-pilot IFR flight from Lethbridge (CYQL), AB to Regina (CYQR), SK with one passenger on board. The weather was VFR, and on departure from RWY23 at CYQL, the pilot was hand flying a climbing left turn for CYQR. While in the turn and nearing the assigned altitude of 7000 feet, the pilot received a TCAS alert. The alert drew his attention outside of the cockpit and the aircraft climbed through the 7000 foot altitude clearance. The pilot noted the altitude exceedance and was correcting the error when ATC advised and told the pilot to maintain 7000 feet.  The pilot engaged the autopilot and continued looking for the traffic. Once the conflict was clear, ATC issued a climb. Separation with an IFR C172 had reduced to 700 feet vertical separation and 4.4 nm horizontal separation where 5.0 nm or 1000 feet is required.

C-GGNW, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft, was conducting flight JZA262 from Nanaimo (CYCD), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 4 crew and 61 passengers on board. During the climb out of CYCD, the aircraft struck an eagle at 2500 feet above sea level. The impact was below the captain's front window. The crew advised ATC of the bird strike but did not declare an emergency. They continued the flight to CYVR at a reduced airspeed and, as a precaution, requested to have aircraft rescue and firefighting vehicles standing by when they landed. The aircraft landed and taxied to the gate without incident.During their post flight inspection, the only damage maintenance found was a dent below the captain's windscreen. After consultation with their technical operations and the manufacturer, the aircraft was determined to be serviceable for continued operation with added inspection criteria to monitor the defect.

C-GOEL, un Grumman AA-5 privé effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aérodrome de Saint-Jean Chrysostome, QC (CSG5). L’aéronef a effectué une approche en vue d’atterrir. Un peu avant d’atteindre le seuil de piste, la vitesse de l’aéronef a descendu et celui-ci a décroché. L’aile gauche a touché le sol en premier et l’aéronef s’est immobilisé à côté de la piste. Le pilote, seul occupant à bord, n’a pas été blessé. L'aéronef a subi des dommages importants.

LX-TCV a Boeing 747-400F aircraft operated by Cargolux Italia S.p.A., was conducting flight CLX46V / CV7756 from Calgary International (CYYC), AB to Luxembourg-Findel International Airport (ELLX), Luxembourg. Approximately 1 hour and 40 minutes into the flight there was a loud bang accompanied with vibration and an N1 rpm fluctuation. The pilot flying reduced the thrust lever of the No. 4 engine (Rolls Royce RB211-524H2-T-19/15). Initially the engine parameters were stable; however, the exhaust gas temperature began to increase until boxed red. The memory items for Engine Severe Damage were performed and the engine was shut down. The flight crew declared Pan Pan, and initiated a diversion to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. The flight crew coordinated with ATC to dump fuel. The situation was under control and after communication with company operations control, the flight crew elected to return to CYYC. A Mayday call was made and the crew confirmed the squawk code with ATC. Calculations were made for the landing at CYYC and additional fuel was dumped. The subsequent landing was uneventful with ARFF responding.The operators maintenance personnel replaced the No. 4 engine. During the previous 2 legs, ELLX to Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), and KLAX to CYYC, the flight crew had reported vibrations at various stages of the flights. The subsequent inspections at KLAX, and at CYYC before the occurrence flight, did not reveal any damage.

C-GKPX, a Swearingen SA226-TC aircraft operated by 2080061 Ontario Inc. (dba Skycare Air Ambulance), was conducting a flight from Fort Frances (CYAG), ON to Thunder Bay Intl. (CYQT), ON. Shortly after departure the aircraft lost hydraulic pressure. The flight crew declared PAN PAN and continued to destination. A manual landing gear extension procedure was performed and the subsequent landing was conducted without further incident. The operator's maintenance personnel replaced a hydraulic pump pressure hose in the left-hand nacelle.

C-GCBW, a privately registered Cessna 172D aircraft on conventional landing gear with straight skis, was conducting a flight from Little Bear Lake (CKL6), SK to Allan Lake, SK with only the pilot on-board. During the takeoff the pilot raised the tail and a gust of wind turned the aircraft to the left. The pilot pulled the control column aft to put the tail ski on the ground and applied full right rudder. The pilot moved the mixture control to idle cut-off which shut the engine down. The aircraft travelled to the left off the runway, struck a small tree; and came to a stop. The pilot was uninjured and the ELT did not activate. There was no fire. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left wing.

C-FLAJ, a Boeing 757-200 operated by Cargojet Airways, was conducting flight CJT9001 from Regina (CYQR), SK to Hamilton (CYHM), ON. During cruise, the crew heard a noise emanating from the upper cargo deck which was followed by a cabin altitude ECAIS warning and the Master Warning Light. An emergency descent manoeuvre was initiated and the quick reference handbook items were carried out. The crew also requested a diversion to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB, where they carried out an uneventful landing on Runway 18The operator's maintenance personel's inspection revealed a fault with the cabin pressure outflow valve. The flight departed CYWG under the provisions of the operator's MEL and was conducted unpressurized to its original destination of CYHM. The operator's maintenance subsequently replaced the cabin pressure outflow valve, function checks were carried out, and no additional faults were noted.

C-GBNX, a Cessna C-560 operated by Keewatin Air, was conducting a flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB to Meadowbank (CMB2), NU. While descending through FL370 the crew noted a loss of pressurization. They donned their masks, ran the rapid decompression ckecklist, declared an emergency, and diverted to Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU. During the diversion, it was noted that the pressure source was normal, the dump valve was closed, the cabin rate knob was in a normal setting, and the cabin altitude was set to the field elevation plus 500 feet. During the decent the cabin altitude warning light illumintated. The aircraft landed uneventfully at CYRT.The operator's maintenance personnel subsequently inspected the cabin door seals with no faults noted; however, they did find that the left hand main landing gear squat switch was loose. The left squat switch was resecured and checked for proper adjustment as per the C-560 Maintenance Manual. Ground run pressurization checks were carried out with no faults noted. A successful test flight was completed and the aircraft was returned to service

C-FPSC, un Jetstream 32 exploité par Pascan sous l'indicatif PSC582 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC à destination de Montréal St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec 3 passagers et 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Lorsque le train d'atterrissage a été monté, une indication anormale de position de la roue de gauche est apparue. La procédure d'urgence a été exécutée et l'équipage a déclaré un état d'urgence. L'indication s'est éteinte alors que l'équipage préparait un retour à CYQB. Ils ont alors annulé l'état d'urgence et procédé vers CYHU. L'équipage a effectué une approche basse et une remontée afin de confirmer avec la tour que le train était bien en position sortie. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé et l'appareil n'a subi aucun dommage. Le problème serait relié au microcontact et les conditions climatiques et aucune autre défectuosité n'a été trouvée.

C-GIUF, an Airbus A321 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA911 from Fort Lauderdale International (KFLL), Florida, USA, to Toronto/Lester B Pearson International (CYYZ), Ontario. During the approach into CYYZ, a flap fault was indicated following flight crew selection of Flaps 2. The approach was abandoned and the flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and received vectors to the North to allow time for troubleshooting. The aircraft landed uneventfully following a second approach. Maintenance adjusted some rigging in the flap drive system and the aircraft was returned to service.

N29961, a Boeing 787-9 operated by United Airlines Inc. as UAL79, was on a scheduled flight from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), USA, to Narita International Airport (RJAA), Japan. Approximately one hour into the flight, the flight crew observed an issue with the air conditioning system. Following troubleshooting, the decision was made to return to KEWR, and it was determined that fuel dumping would be necessary to ensure that the aircraft would be below maximum landing weight prior to arriving at KEWR. The flight crew arranged with ATC for fuel dumping to take place at 34000 feet between Petawawa, Ontario, and Sudbury, Ontario. Over a period of approximately 25 minutes, approximately 47000 lbs of fuel was released. The aircraft reversed course during the fuel dumping and returned to KEWR uneventfully.

C-FRHZ, a Beechcraft B200 aircraft operated by PAL Aerospace Ltd, was conducting flight SPR02 on a local area VFR flight from St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL with 4 people onboard. After departure from CYYT, the crew noticed that not all of the landing gear position indicator lights extinguished, after the landing gear was selected up. The decision was made to return back to CYYT. When the landing gear was selected down prior to landing, only 2 of the 3 landing gear position indicator lights illuminated. The landing gear appeared to be down using onboard optics equipment. The crew declared an emergency and the aircraft landed at CYYT without incident at 1630z with ARFF on standby.The operator’s maintenance department discovered that the landing gear position press-to-test switch was stuck in the on position, giving a false indication. Also, the LH gear indicator light was burnt out. Landing gear position switch (P/N 101-3175-1S) was replaced and function checks were carried out satisfactorily. The aircraft was returned to service and a Service Difficulty Report was submitted to Transport Canada.

C-FGKJ, a Cargojet Canada Ltd. Boeing 757 was operating as Flight CJT925,  from Vancouver (CYVR), BC to Cincinnati /Northern Kentucky airport (KCVG), KY  with 2 crew onboard. During the take off roll from runway 26L, at approximately 80 knots, the flight crew observed an EICAS message of "R HYD ENG PUMP" with an associated "PRESS" illuminated switch light. The flight crew rejected the take off, exited the runway at TWY 'E', and requested ARFF for brake inspection. The crew taxied to the gate and parked without further incident. Maintenance performed an inspection and engine run with systems test, then deferred the defect under 29-31-02-02 "Center and Right Pump Indication Systems Inoperative". The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FDLG, un De Havilland DHC-8-100 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE854, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Umiujaq, QC (CYMU) à destination de Kuujjuarapik, QC (CYGW). Après le décollage, la lumière d’avertissement «weight on wheels» s’est allumée. L’équipage a décidé de dérouter vers l’aéroport de La Grande, QC (CYGL) où est située la base de maintenance de la compagnie. En approche vers CYGL, lors de la sélection du train d’atterrissage en position sortie, une indication que la roue de nez n'était pas verrouillée est apparue. L’équipage a amorcé un circuit d’attente afin d’évaluer la situation. Une urgence a été déclarée au spécialiste de l'information de vol (FSS) de CYGL. La liste de vérification d’urgence a été complétée et le train d’atterrissage a été descendu manuellement par l’équipage. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

Shortly after departure from Wawa, Ontario (CYKZ), the crew of C-FDOU, a Beech A100 aircraft declared a PAN PAN due to a faulty left main gear brake indication. The flight diverted to it's home base at Rouyn-Noranda, Quebec (CYUY) and landed without further incident. Maintenance found the brake hose to the left landing gear inboard brake assembly to be leaking, the brake hose was replaced and checked serviceable IAW the appropriate maintenance manual.

C-GOIQ, a Cessna 172 aircraft, operated by the Waterloo Wellington Flying Club, with a student pilot on board was holding short of Runway 32 at Kitchener/Waterloo (CYKF) and requested a take-off clearance. Simultaneously, C-GOIG a Diamond DA-40 aircraft was cleared for the right downwind, and C-GLFX, a Piper PA-46-600TP aircraft, was on final approach to land on Runway 32. The student  pilot, confused with the clearance for C-GOIG (the registration being similar), taxied across the hold short line to line up for departure on the runway. Waterloo tower observed C-GOIQ moving onto the runway and instructed the aircraft to vacate the runway. C-GLFX landed without incident.

C-GLAZ, un Piper PA-31 privé effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Val d’Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de Sherbrooke, QC (CYSC) avec un pilote et 3 passagers à son bord. Après environ 40 minutes de vol à une altitude de croisière de 9000 pieds ASL, le pilote a remarqué une coulisse d’huile sur le capot du moteur de droite. L’indication de pression d’huile moteur était normale. Par mesure de précaution, le pilote a demandé à l’ATC un déroutement vers l’aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) et de monter à une altitude de 11 000 pieds. Peu de temps après, un des passagers a avisé le pilote qu’il voyait une importante accumulation d’huile sur le volet de l’aile droite de l’avion. L’indicateur de pression d’huile moteur affichait une pression plus basse. Le pilote a décidé d’arrêter le moteur droit par mesure de précaution. Étant donné la proximité de l’aéroport de La Macaza/Mont-Tremblant Intl, QC (CYFJ), le pilote a avisé l’ATC de la situation et de son intention de se poser à CYFJ en effectuant une approche visuelle. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 21.

C-GXWZ, a privately owned Cessna 182R, was conducting a flight from Penticton Regional Airport (CYYF), BC to a private grass strip 4 nm W of Westlock (CES4), AB with one pilot onboard. While landing to the west on the strip, the aircraft slid off the end of the strip and nosed over coming to rest in a snow bank. Damage included the propellor, engine cowling and nose landing gear. There were no reported injuries.

C-IEQD, a Fisher Super Koala Ultralight aircraft, with one person on board, crashed on to the frozen lake surface of Lake Simcoe near Lagoon City, Ontario, approximately 1.5 nm from shore. The pilot was fatally injured and the aircraft was destroyed by a post-crash fire. The TSB deployed a team to the accident site.

C-GHPX, an Air Canada Boeing 787-8 aircraft operating as flight AC128, was conducting a flight from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International (CYYZ), ON, with 10 crew members and 104 passengers onboard. During the initial climb at approximately 7 NM northwest of Princeton Airport (CYDC), BC, the right hand windscreen cracked and triggered a message for the windshield heating system on the engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS). The flight crew completed the emergency checklist, diverted back to CYVR, and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed without incident and no emergency vehicles were required. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft.Maintenance replaced the right hand windscreen and as a precaution, replaced the window heat controller.

C-FJZD, a Bombardier CL-600-2024 (series CRJ 900) operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8550 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC. to Regina Intl. (CYQR), SK. JZA8550 landed without incident and taxied to gate 4. During passenger deplaning, the flight crew noticed an electrical smell/smoke throughout the cockpit and cabin. As a precaution, the captain called CYQR tower and requested ARFF to standby. No emergency was declared and there was no evidence of visible smoke. All passengers deplaned though the main cabin door.The operator's maintenance found a recirculating fan fault on the EICAS. The #1 recirculation fan was replaced, funtional checks carried out, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FTMN, an ATR72-200 operated by Morningstar Air Express, was conducting flight MAL8066 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl. (CYXE) SK. to Calgary Intl. (CYYC) AB. When approximately 44 NM WSW of CYXE and in cruise at FL220, the flight crew received a master warning and a CCAS indication "EXCESS CAB ALT" message. The cabin altitude was at 10 000 feet and climbing at 300 feet per minute. The pressurization system was checked and no abnormal indications were observed. The flight crew advised ATC that they were commencing an emergency descent to 10 000 feet ASL. The flight crew carried out the emergency descent drill and associated checklist. The flight continued to CYYC and landed safely. The operator's maintenance completed an external walk around of the aircraft and found the document door was latched but not fully closed, and insulation was protruding from the opening. The door was closed and latched properly. An operational test of the pressurization system was performed in the manual mode and a leak test of the pressurization system completed. No faults were found. The aircraft was subsequently returned to service.

C-IENH, un Cosmos Chronos (ultraléger motorisé pendulaire) en exploitation privée, effectuait un posé-décollée à Saint-Hyacinthe (CSU3), Québec avec seul le pilote à bord. Lors de la montée initiale, le ski gauche a été observé en travers. Le pilote a effectué un atterrissage dans un champ, toutefois il a perdu la maitrise de l’aéronef. Il a subi des blessures graves et l’appareil a subi des dommages importants.

C-GNZS, un Airbus Helicopters AS355N Twinstar exploité par les Hélicoptères Canadiens Limitée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Sept-Îles (CYZV), QC à destination de l’hélisurface de l’IOC situé à 3 miles marins à l'ouest. Lors du vol stationnaire avant l’atterrissage (environ 2 m), le moteur numéro 2 (Turbomeca Arrius 1A) s’est arrêté. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre et il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GGAH, un DHC-8-400 exploité par Jazz sous l'indicatif JZA730 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en montée vers son altitude de croisière, une indication d'un problème hydraulique a été observée. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et a pris la décision de retourner se poser à CYUL. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre.

C-FXHE, un Airbus Helicopters AS355 F2 exploité par Héli-Intair effectuait une patrouille de ligne électrique entre Mirabel, QC et Gatineau, QC lorsque l'équipage a perçu une odeur de fil électrique brûlée suivie d'une indication de générateur du moteur de gauche hors ligne. Le pilote a déclaré une urgence et s'est dirigé vers l'aéroport de Gatineau, QC (CYND). L'appareil a atterri sans encombre sur la rampe à CYND.

C-GMOB, a Piper PA-31-350 aircraft operated by Eagle Air Enterprises Ltd, was conducting a VFR flight from Churchill (CYYQ), MB to St. Andrews (CYAV), MB. The aircraft entered the circuit on a left downwind for Runway 36 and was cleared to land by the tower. On final approach the pilot inadvertently lined up with Taxiway B that runs parallel to Runway 36. The aircraft landed to the left of Runway 36 on Taxiway B. The taxiway was unoccupied at the time and the aircraft landed without further event. The incident occurred during daylight hours in visual meteorological conditions.

C-GNYI, a Bell 212 operated by Airspan Helicopters Ltd. was travelling from Sechelt Airport (CAP3), BC to Cypress Mountain Provincial Park, located in West Vancouver, BC to support a BC Hydro project with 2 pilots on board. During the flight the aircraft experienced a sudden and dramatic right roll and nose down pitch. Both pilots attempted to regain control. After regaining control, the pilots observed warning lights indicating a hydraulic and an engine failure (Pratt & Whitney PT6T-3B) . A location on nearby Bowen Island was selected for an emergency landing however the aircraft was still difficult to control and the crew was unable to maneuver it to the desired location. During the descent, the aircraft began an uncommanded rotation to the right, leading to a loss of control. The aircraft collided with trees and came to rest on a rocky ridge approximately 270 feet ASL on the NW corner of Bowen Island. Both occupants received minor injuries. The helicopter sustained substantial damage. There was no post impact fire and the ELT functioned as designed.

C-FWXO, a privately registered Cessna 177 aircraft, with the pilot and 2 passengers on board, was conducting a local flight from Russell (CJW5), MB. During the takeoff from Runway 17, the aircraft did not attain a positive climb rate after the main wheels left the ground. The pilot rejected the takeoff. When the aircraft touched down, it bounced and turned to the left. The aircraft exited the runway and struck a snow drift. The nose landing gear collapsed and the propeller struck the ground. The occupants were uninjured and the ELT activated automatically. The aircraft sustained damage to the propeller, landing gear and left wing.

C-GANF, a de Havilland DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways LP, was conducting flight WSG814 from Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON to Kingfisher Lake (CNM5), ON. The aircraft was transporting unleaded gasoline in a collapsible tank installed in the cabin. Shortly after departing CYPL the flight crew noticed a strong odour of unleaded gasoline in the flight deck. The first officer entered the cabin to investigate and discovered that the 2 vent line valves were open and the line had been left un-capped allowing gasoline to spill into the cabin. The first officer closed the vent line and the flow of gasoline ceased. The flight crew depressurized and ventilated the aircraft, and elected to return to CYPL. An emergency was declared and the subsequent landing was uneventful. After shutdown some gasoline leaked from the aircraft fuselage onto the apron and prompted spill response procedures.

C-FMHA, a Boeing 757-200 aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express Inc., was conducting flight MAL7070 from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB, to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. While cruising at FL350 the flight crew received a "Cabin Alt" master warning. The cabin altitude was noted to have risen above 10 000 feet with the outflow valve fully closed. The flight crew declared PAN PAN, and requested a descent to 14 000 feet above sea level. As the aircraft descended through FL230 the flight crew reported normal pressurization and requested FL210. The flight continued to destination without further incident. The aircraft was operating with an inoperative right-hand air-conditioning pack that had been deferred in accordance with the minimum equipment list (MEL) which restricted operation to a maximum altitude of FL350. However, the aircraft was unable to maintain maximum cabin differential pressure at the flight planned FL350. The next leg of flight MAL7070 was cancelled pending the replacement of the air-conditioning pack and clearing the MEL item.

C-GBKB, a Bombardier CL-600-2B16 Challenger 605 aircraft operated by Aurora Jet Partners, was conducting a flight from Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) to Scottsdale, AZ (KSDL) with 4 passengers and 2 crew members on board. At 9000 feet in the descent into KSDL, the flight crew received a Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) Resolution Advisory (RA). The flight crew complied with the advisory and notified ATC. Due to the TCAS RA and close proximity to the airport, the aircraft was too high to safely conduct the approach. The crew coordinated with the tower to do an orbit at the threshold of runway 21 to lose the necessary altitude. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.

C-GKGX, un appareil de construction amateur de type Wag-A-Bond en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le lac Barron (QC) à destination de l’aéroport de Lachute, Qc (CSE4) situé à 10.5 milles marins vers le sud-ouest. Peu après le décollage, l’appareil a viré vers la gauche et s’est écrasé sur la surface glacée du lac s’immobilisant à la verticale. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s'est déclenchée. Le pilote, seul à bord, a subi des blessures mortelles.

C-GEWR, a WestJet Encore de Havilland DHC-8-400 was operating as flight WEN3210 from Comox (CYQQ), BC to Calgary International (CYYC), AB. The crew encountered severe turbulence between FL170-120 on decent into CYYC and reported that momentarily the aircraft did not respond to their inputs. The flight landed safely in CYYC with no injuries to passengers or crew. Following the flight the aircraft was taken out of service for an inspection.

C-GMEW, a Fairchild  SA-227-AC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting flight JV377 from North Bay/Jack Garland Airport (CYYB), ON to Sault Ste. Marie Airport (CYAM), ON. Shortly after takeoff from CYYB, the No. 1 engine experienced a loss of power while passing through 1000 feet above ground level. The flight crew conducted the applicable procedures and elected to perform a precautionary No. 1 engine shutdown and return to CYYB. The flight crew declared an emergency and landed back in CYYB without further incident. Emergency response vehicles dispatched, but were cancelled after flight crew advised there was no injury and no risk of fire upon arrival.

C-GKHI, a Beech 200 operated by Transwest Air, was conducting medevac flight TW911 from Stony Rapids (CYSF), SK to Saskatoon (CYXE), SK with 2 flight crew, 2 EMT, and 1 passenger on board. While enroute to CYXE, the flight crew observed an erratic fuel flow indication on the No. 1 (left hand) engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-42) and a uncommanded torque increase. The flight crew performed a precautionary engine shutdown, declared an emergency and requested a diversion to Prince Albert (CYPA), SK. An uneventful single-engine approach and landing was conducted with ARFF standing by. The operator's maintenance inspected the engine and no issues were found. Further investigation is being conducted by the operator.

C-GDON, a Cessna 172K aircraft operated by Insignia College, was on the first take-off for circuits at Boundary Bay Airport (CZBB), BC with one student pilot on board. The student took off from Runway 07 and during the climb realized the aircraft airspeed was decreasing. As the aircraft was nearing a stall at 300 feet AGL, the pilot regained control by lowering the nose to keep speed up. The pilot declared a MAYDAY and ATC gave the pilot the option of "any runway". Other traffic was cleared to allow GDON runway access. The pilot managed to make a 180 degree turn to land on Runway 25 without further issues. After landing, the pilot realized she had set "full flaps" and did not set them for take-off prior to departure, as required in the pre-flight checklist. Ground taxi clearances were obtained and the aircraft taxied back to the company facility.

C-GDDC, a ski equipped, Amateur Built RANS S6ES aircraft, was landing on Canal Lake, Ontario. During the touchdown the nose landing gear dug into the soft snow and the aircraft nosed over. The pilot was not injured but the aircraft received substantial damage to the lower engine cowl and vertical fin.

C-GCFB, a Beechcraft King Air C90 operated by Synergy Aviation Ltd, was conducting a flight from Villeneuve (CZVL), AB to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with two crew on board. Shortly after take-off low oil pressure was indicated on the right engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-21). The engine shut down, an emergency declared and the flight returned to CZVL with no further issues.Following the flight it was found that the oil had vented out of the right engine due to the oil cap flap not being completely seated. The oil was replenished and the engine ground run. No further issues were reported.

C-FGXT, a Transport Canada Beech C90A aeroplane, was being flown on a night training flight as TGO998 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Campbell River (CYBL), BC with 2 crew members on board. During circuits at CYBL the LH main gear light remained unlit. The crew completed a low pass over the airport where a Flight Service Specialist observed that the landing gear appeared down. An emergency was declared with ATC and the appropriate checklists from the QRH were actioned, and a request was made to return to CYVR. The aircraft landed at CYVR without further issues with ARFF on standby. The aircraft was inspected by emergency authorities and was then towed to the Air Services Directorate hangar for inspection.Company maintenance inspections revealed that the landing gear accumulator was low on pressure. The accumulator was serviced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFVZ, a deHavilland DHC3T operated by Kississing Lake Lodge (dba Wings Over Kississing), was conducting a flight from Kaskattama, MB to Gillam (CYGX), MB with 1 pilot onboard. During the takeoff from Runway 12 at Kaskattama, C-FFVZ struck wind-hardened snowdrifts and the aircraft became airbone soon after. The flight continued uneventfully to CYGX. Upon landing in CYGX, it was noted that the tail wheel and ski were missing. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to its rear fuselage and rudder.

At 15:14 EDT on 25 February 2021, an Aero Vodochody L39C aircraft (registration N88EA), operated by the International Test Pilot School Canada, was landing on Runway 33 at the London International Airport (CYXU). After touchdown, the aircraft came to rest on its belly.  There were no injuries to the instructor or student. The internal investigation found no evidence of physical malfunction of the landing gear system. While the warning system is not well designed, it did function as per expectations on the day of the incident. All evidence suggests that the student pilot was task saturated handling the arrival procedure and likely did not lower the landing gear. The instructor was actively monitoring the student pilot’s task management and arrival profile and did not notice that the student did not lower the landing gear.The company has decided to implement the following risk controls in efforts to minimize the chance of re-occurrence:1. Upgrade aircraft / gear unsafe warning system by maximizing all capabilities of the Garmin G3X multipurpose display in order to introduce an additional layer of protection; 2. Organization / staffing - Management is working to recruit additional qualified instructor pilots and to endeavour to schedule instructors for a maximum of two instructional sorties per day.3. Training - All pilots continue to receive periodic briefings on human factors and task / workload management.

C-FWER, a privately registered Piper PA-22-108, was operating on a local flight from Labrie Field - Ponoka Industrial, AB (CEH3). The aircraft departed CEH3 at 1350 and flew locally for approximately 35 minutes in cruise flight, at 4000 feet ASL, when the engine (Lycoming O-290-D) rpm suddenly decreased from 2300 rpm to 1500 rpm. The pilot applied carburetor heat, checked both magnetos and switched fuel tanks; however, the engine rpm did not improve. The pilot initiated a forced approach 21 nm NE of CEH3. While on approach to land, the pilot attempted to reapply power and the engine rpm increased to 1800 rpm, which lasted approximately 20 seconds before engine power reduced to 1300 rpm. The pilot observed oil pressure in the green band. While reapplying power, the aircraft overshot the intended landing area, and continued toward the next field. While approaching the next field the aircraft crossed under a power line and over a road. At this time, the pilot observed a loud thud as the vertical stabilizer struck the power line. The pilot continued to land on the field and slid into a high wire fence, striking a fence post. The fence wire slid over the cowling and broke the windshield before the wire sheared. The aircraft came to rest leaning to the right with the right wingtip resting on the ground. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured. The ELT was not activated. The aircraft received damage to the propeller, engine cowling, bent left wing strut and windshield. Inspection of the engine revealed oil on cylinder 1 and blistered paint at the base of the cylinder. The engine contained 3.5 qts of oil and it was observed that the engine exhaust was dripping engine oil.

C-FITW, a Boeing 777-300 was conducting Air Canada flight ACA7211 from Frankfurt Rein-Mein (EDDF), Germany to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  After departure just before leveling off at FL100,  ATC advised of traffic at FL110. Flight crew had the traffic in sight and received a TCAS RA. No evasive action was taken as the flight was just leveling off at FL110. ATC advised no conflict and flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FWUI, a Douglas DC3C-BT-67 aircraft operated by North Star Air, was conducting flight BF104 from Kashechewan (CZKE), ON to Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON. During the flight, the crew heard a noise and observed the left engine (Pratt & Whitney PT6A-67R) chip detector warning light illumnate. The QRH items were actioned, and the left engine was shut down. The crew declared an emergency and carried out an uneventful landing in CYPL. A subsequent inspection revealed metal on the gas generator chip detector. The aircraft has been removed from service and the engine was removed and sent out for overhaul.

C-FMUV, a CRJ-200 aircraft operated by Voyageur Airways, was conducting flight VAL200 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to North Bay (CYYB), ON. After departure, the nose gear failed to retract. The flight crew actioned the QRH and conducted a manual gear extension. The flight crew elected to return to CYHZ, and requested ARFF to standby as a precaution, since the nose-wheel steering would not be available during landing. The aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance replaced a faulty proximity sensor in the nose gear section and the aircraft was returned to service the following day.UPDATED: 03 March 2021

C-GXYD, an amateur-built Hummingbird 206L helicopter, was conducting a local flight near St. Paul (CEW3), AB under the "Initial Standard Operating Conditions - Amateur-built Aircraft" for the Special Certificate of Airworthiness - Amateur Built. The turbine powered helicopter was nearing the required 25 hours with no issues related to design or construction. During cruise, at an altitude of approximately 700 feet AGL, a loud bang was heard and the helicopter yawed to the left. An autorotation was carried out to an open snow-covered field. As the helicoper landed it broke through a snowdrift and rolled over on its right side. The pilot exited the helicopter un-injured.Following the flight, it was determined that a weld had failed on a reduction gearbox bracket and the coupling between the engine and reduction gearbox had failed. Engine power to the reduction gearbox was lost.

C-GWKI, the Academie Aeronautique Inc. Cessna 152 was on a training flight with a student and instructor on board. During the landing roll at Hawkesbury (CPG5), ON the nosewheel dug into soft snow and the aircraft flipped over. No injuries were reported but the aircraft was substantially damaged. The snow had not been plowed from the runway but was compressed by equipment to provide a hard surface for landing aircraft. Prior to the landing the aircraft flew over the runway to determine surface condition.

C-FHZH, a privately owned Piper PA28R-180 was doing circuits on Runway 04 at Brockville-Thousand Islands (CNL3), ON. During the second take off, prior to becoming airborne, directional control was lost; the aircraft veered to the left and exited the runway into deep snow. The pilot was not injured but the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FGXL, a Transport Canada Beech C90A aeroplane, was being flown on a night training flight as TGO996 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Williams Lake (CYWL), BC with 2 crew members on board. During the climb to cruise altitude, approximately 10 minutes after departure, a strong smell of electrical burning and some smoke was observed in the cockpit. An emergency was declared with ATC and the appropriate checklists from the QRH were actioned. A request to return to CYVR was made and, during the descent, the burning smell dissipated. After landing, the smell recurred and the crew deplaned on the taxiway. Neither of the crew required medical attention.The aircraft was inspected by emergency authorities and was towed to the Air Services Directorate hangar. Maintenance determined the source of the odour and the smoke to be the co-pilot side edge-light panel. One of the backlighting elements on the hour meter panel failed and there was a burned area on around the bulb contacts. The aircraft has returned to service.

C-GEVC, an amateur-built Lancair 360, was operating on a local flight from Josephburg, AB (CFB6). Prior to take-off the pilot completed the runup and preflight checks, which included checking that the flight controls were free and clear. The aircraft taxied and began takeoff on Runway 26. The aircraft accelerated, rotated and became airborne. During the initial climb, at approximately 100 feet AGL, the aircraft began an uncommanded roll to the right. The pilot was unable to maintain a level attitude and continued rolling to the right. The aircraft completed one roll before colliding with terrain while upright. The aircraft came to rest approximately 200 feet to the north side of Runway 26. The pilot received no injuries and the passenger received serious injuries. The ELT activated on impact and was turned off by the pilot. The aircraft was subtantially damaged.

CF-STT, a ski equipped Stinson 108-2, was operating from an unmaintained private airstrip 6.5 nm SE of the Glendon, AB aerodrome (CFP5) to Spencer Lake, AB. The airstrip was snow covered with the snow depth of approximately 6-inches. During the take-off run, the left ski contacted a 12-inch snow drift and the aircraft veered to the right and pitched nose up and left the runway surface. The aircraft banked right and the right wing tip contacted the ground. The pilot was unable to maintain control, while the propeller struck the ground and the landing gear collapsed. The aircraft came to rest approximately 200 feet to the right side of the runway surface. The pilot and passenger received no injuries. The ELT did not activate.

C-GJZA, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8991 from St John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. While in the climb through 10,000 feet, the flight attendant noticed white smoke coming from the floor at row 19 on the left-hand side, which had an oily smell. The flight crew was notified immediately and the decision was made to return to CYYT. Within a short time, the smoke disappeared. The flight landed with no further incident. Prior to departure from CYYT, due to winter conditions the aircraft was de-iced with Type 4 fluid. Maintenance inspected the aircraft APU and engine bleed system and determined that the fumes were from the de-ice fluid. The aircraft was released back to service.

C-GUMB, un hélicoptère de type Robinson R44 en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue au départ et à destination de l’aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Le pilote effectuait un vol en stationnaire à environ 20 ou 30 pieds du sol en face d’un chalet situé en bordure du lac St-Jean dans le secteur de Saint-Henri-de-Taillon. Alors que le pilote tournait vers la droite, l’hélicoptère a perdu de l’altitude, le pilote a tenté de soutenir avec le collectif, mais a dû poser l’hélicoptère dans la neige. Le patin de gauche s’est enfoncé et l’hélicoptère s’est renversé. Une fois l'appareil arrêté, le pilote a éteint le moteur qui tournait encore. Le pilote et le passager ont évacué et ont subi des blessures légères. L’hélicoptère a subi des dommages importants. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) ne s’est pas déclenchée.

C-FRQU, un Cessna 182P en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de St-Lazare, QC (CST3) avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Suite à l'atterrissage, alors que l'appareil roulait vers l'extrémité de la piste 20 afin de rejoindre la surface de demi-tour, celui-ci a dévié de sa course et il y a eu contact avec la neige bordant le côté droit de la piste, entraînant une glissade qui s'est terminée au-delà du bout de la piste, à proximité d'un fossé. L'appareil a terminé sa course en position perpendiculaire à l'axe de piste. Le train avant s'est brisé, l'hélice et le capot moteur ont été endommagés et le bout de l'aile gauche appuyé contre le sol de l'autre côté du fossé. Il n'y a eu ni blessés ni déversement de matières dangereuses.

C-GPUC, a EADS SOCATA TBM 700 (SERIES A) turboprop destined for Red Deer, Alberta (CYQF) was at FL310 near the Princeton (CYDC), BC VOR when the pilot declared an emergency due to a pressurization issue. The flight descended to 15 000 feet and returned to Boundary Bay, BC (CZBB).

C-GSGQ, a privately owned Cessna 340A, was conducting an IFR flight from Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier Intl Airport (CYOW), Ontario to Toronto/Buttonville Municipal Airport (CYKZ), Ontario, with one pilot and two passengers on board. During descent from 5000 feet, the RH engine (Teledyne Continental TSIO-520-NB) failed due to fuel starvation, as the RH auxiliary fuel tank had been emptied. Attempts to restart the engine after selecting the main tank were unsuccessful, and the pilot arranged with ATC to divert to nearby Peterborough Airport (CYPQ), Ontario, where an uneventful landing was made at 1543EST. Vapor lock was the suspected cause of the failed restart attempts while airborne. On the apron at CYPQ, the RH engine was restarted successfully and a run-up was conducted which revealed no anomalies. The pilot departed at 1615EST and arrived uneventfully at the planned destination (CYKZ).

C-GECO, a ski-equipped Cessna 185F, operated by Kississing Lake Lodge (dba Wings Over Kississing) was enroute from Egenolf Lake, MB to Thompson (CYTH), MB with only the pilot onboard. While in cruise, the engine (Teledyne Continental IO-520-D) lost complete power. The fuel selector was set to "both" and the pilot then attempted to restart the engine without success. The pilot then successfully forced landing the aircraft on Pine Lake, MB. The pilot was not injured. The aircraft did not sustain any damage. The pilot was subsequently picked up in a helicopter by the air operator.An inspection of the fuel cells after landing revealed that they were dry and excessive fuel staining/streaks were found coming from the outboard fuel caps and on the underside of the flaps.

C-GLBI, un Robinson R44 II en exploitation privée, se préparait à effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol à vue à partir d'un terrain privé situé à St-Eustache, QC à destination de St-Donat, QC (CSY4) avec seul le pilote à bord. Lors du réchauffement moteur, l'aéronef s'est mis à tournoyer sur la glace, et s'est retourné sur lui-même terminant sa course sur le dos. La ceinture-baudrier du pilote n'était pas attachée et celui-ci a été éjecté par la porte de l'appareil qui était ouverte. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s'est activée et il n'y a pas eu de blessé.

C-GGJA, a CRJ-200 operated by Jazz Aviation LP as JZA 7895, was on an IFR flight from Thompson Municipal Airport (CYTH), Manitoba to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), Ontario with 3 crew and 5 passengers on board. During descent through approximately 15000 feet, a FLAPS FAIL message appeared on the flight display. The flight crew actioned the appropriate QRH items, declared PAN PAN with ATC, and conducted an uneventful zero flap landing.

G-ZBKG, un Boeing 787-900 exploité par British Airways sous l’indicatif BAW49, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Londres Heathrow, UK (EGLL) à destination de Seattle–Tacoma International Airport, WA aux États-Unis (KSEA). Alors que l’aéronef était en vol de croisière au niveau de vol 380 à environ 120 miles marins au nord d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB), il a rencontré de la turbulence en air clair sévère. L’équipage a avisé le contrôle de la circulation aérienne, une descente a été initiée au niveau de vol 340 et la turbulence a cessé sous le niveau 360. Un membre d'équipage de la cabine a été blessé et un avis médical a été obtenu avant la poursuite du vol à sa destination. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre à KSEA et le personnel paramédical a évalué les blessures du membre d’équipage à la porte d’arrivée. L’appareil n’a pas subi de dommage apparent.

C-FDYN, a Central Mountain Air Dornier DO-328 aircraft, was conducting flight GLR8438 from Kelowna Airport (CYLW), BC to Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC with 3 crew members and 11 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL240 the flight crew noticed indications of oil pressure fluctuations on the right engine (PRATT & WHITNEY CANADA PW119B). ATC advised the flight crew that the flight would be required to hold prior to commencing the approach at CYXS due to traffic. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and landed as soon as practical without further incident. Subsequent maintenance actions revealed the engine's no.3 and 4 bearing labyrinth seals were leaking air and pressurizing the bearing cavity to the point where oil had been pushed out into the intercompressor turbine case and overboard into both the cowling and the exhaust burn off duct. The operator has coordinated with the engine manufacturer and has indicated that the engine requires replacement.

At approximately 1800 utc (13:00 EST) C-GPOT, a privately registered Blackshape Prime BS100 aircraft, was conducting circuits on runway 28 at Ottawa/Carp (CYRP), ON. After a touch-and-go, the aircraft was climbing runway heading and then started a left turn prior to the end of the runway. Approximately 240m south of the runway, the aircraft entered a near vertical descent and crashed into a wooded area. The pilot, the sole person onboard, was fatally injured. The aircraft was destroyed by a post impact fire.

C-FXED, un hélicoptère Airbus Helicopters AS350BA exploité par Heli Mistral Service, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Trois-Rivières, QC (CYRQ), avec 1 pilote à bord. Alors qu’il se trouvait en vol de croisière à environ 1000 pieds au-dessus du sol, le pilote a remarqué qu’un objet est passé à sa droite, mais n’a perçu aucun impact. Après l’atterrissage au retour à CYRQ, l’inspection post envolée a révélé des dommages près du bord de fuite de la partie inférieure d’une des pales du rotor principal. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé, et la pale en question a dû être remplacée.

C-FFPA, un Jetstream 32 exploité par Pascan sous l’indicatif PSC582 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport des Îles-de-la-Madeleine, QC (CYGR) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB) avec 8 passagers et 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Lorsque le train d’atterrissage a été descendu, une indication anormale de position de la roue de nez est apparue. La procédure d’urgence a été exécutée et l’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 24 sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage.

C-GNLN, a Boeing 737-200 operated by Nolinor as flight NRL950, was conducting a flight from Thompson (CYTH) MB to Val-D'or (CYVO) QC. During the climb out from CYTH the cabin altitude reached 14000 ft and the passenger cabin masks deployed. The flight crew carried out the emergency procedures and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft descended from FL296 to 16000 ft and returned to CYTH where the aircraft landed without incident.The operator's maintenance found the automatic pressurization system was unserviceable. The aircraft was released under MEL and ferried to Montreal/Mirabel Intl (CYMX) QC for repairs.

C-GFAV, a Beech King Air 200 operated by Fast Air Ltd. as flight PBR215, was conducting a flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Victor Mine (CVM2), ON. During the approach to CVM2, the flight crew selected gear down for landing and the gear did not extend. The flight crew carried out an overshoot, contacted flight operations and an operational decision was made to return to CYWG. Upon arriving in CYWG, the flight crew declared an emergency and successfully carried out a manual gear extension. C-GFAV landed safely with ARFF on standby. There were no injuries. The operator's maintenance found the landing gear would retract but the landing gear would not extend with the selection of gear down. The landing gear handle was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GJXV, an Airbus Canada Limited Partnership A220-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA317 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. While cruising approximately 193 NM west-north-west of Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB the flight crew received a No. 1 hydraulic system low-pressure-warning. The flight crew elected to divert to CYWG and declared Pan Pan with ATC. The subsequent landing was uneventful and the aircraft taxied to the gate. The operator's maintenance personnel replaced the No. 1 engine-driven hydraulic-pump-attenuator and seal.

C-FBTR, a Carson Air Beech 1900D aircraft, was operating flight CRN511 from Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC to Kelowna (CYLW), BC with 2 crew members and 3 passengers on board. During approach, the landing gear did not extend. The flight crew decided to hold, actioned the appropriate checklists, and requested emergency services to be on standby as a precaution. The landing gear was manually extended and the aircraft landed without further incident. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft.In the process of troubleshooting the landing gear system, maintenance found a broken wire going to the landing gear control circuit breaker. The wire was repaired and the landing gear system tested serviceable.

C-GLUT a Canwest Air Beech B200GT, was operating on a MEDEVAC flight from Grande Prairie, AB (CYQU) to Fort Vermillion, AB (CEZ4) with two flight crew and two medical crew on board. During the approach to CEZ4, the flight crew selected landing gear down and the RH main landing gear only partially extended. The nose and LH main landing gear extended fully. A low pass was performed over CEZ4 where company personal were able to confirm that the RH main landing gear was not fully extended. The flight crew actioned the QRC "Landing Gear Manual Extension", but the RH main landing gear failed to extend. Several acceleration manouvers were performed; however, the landing gear did not move. Company Operations was consulted and a decision was made to conduct a wheels up landing in CYOJ before dark. The aircraft then diverted to CYOJ. The flight crew advised CYOJ FSS and declared an emergency and emergency services were dispatched from the town of High Level. When the aircraft arrived over CYOJ, the flight crew selected gear up and the landing gear retracted normally. All 3 gear retracted and the red gear unsafe light went out. The flight crew attempted to extend the landing gear again but the RH main landing gear did not move. The landing gear was selected up and the landing gear, once again retracted normally. The flight crew prepared for a landing gear up landing. On short final the flight crew shut down the engines and feathered the propellers. The aircraft touched down at approximately the 1000 foot mark and maintained the runway centerline. After the aircraft came to rest, the passengers and flight crew evacuated out the main cabin door; there were no egress issues. Emergency services arrived as soon as the aircraft came to rest. There was no fire, no injuries and no fuel leak. Company maintenance will follow-up with TSB regarding maintenance findings and follow-up.

C-FDBN, a privately registered Aerostar 601P aircraft, advised ATC they were having electrical issues, and subseqently  squawked 7600 due to radio failure. Radio communication and transponder were both intermittent. When communication and radar identification was re-established, the pilot declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without further incident at Hamilton International / John C. Munro Airport (CYHM), ON.

C-GJZG, a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland DHC-8-402, was scheduled for a flight from Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 4 crew and 47 passengers onboard. During de-ice operations at the gate, the auxiliary power unit (APU) ingested de-ice glycol causing smoke and fumes to enter both the cockpit and the cabin. The captain shut down the aircraft and ordered an evacuation over the public announcement system. The cabin crew directed passengers through the front left main cabin door and both aft exits—boarding stairs were moved to the aft left exit part way through the evacuation. The ground crew observed the deplaning and ceased de-ice operations at the right wing. Emergency crews responded, but were not required. There was 1 minor injury reported by a passenger to the Nanaimo Airport Commission. Maintenance confirmed the smoke and fumes were from de-ice glycol entering the aircraft through the APU bleed system. The APU was ground run to purge all glycol from the system and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FIOC, a Fairchild SA227-AC aircraft operated by Skycare Air Ambulance, was operating a flight from Kenora (CYQK), ON to Cat Lake (CYAC), ON  with a crew of 2 and 2 passengers on board. After the nose wheel touched down during the landing roll on Runway 29 at CYAC, the crew experienced difficulty in maintaining directional control of the aircraft and it veered off the right side of the runway. The crew and passengers exited the aircraft without any injuries. There was no damage to the aircraft or runway lights. Subsequently, the crew was able to taxi the aircraft back to the apron.The operator's maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft and found the nose wheel steering amplifier had failed. The steering amplifier was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FWEP, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 operated by Westjet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3139 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB with 4 crew members and 25 passengers on board. During the initial climb out from CYYC, the flight crew observed a master caution #1 PEC light followed by an overspeed indication for the #1 propeller. A MAYDAY was declared to ATC, the reference section of the QRC was actioned, and the crew proceeded to shut down the #1 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW150A) as per the QRH. A single engine approach and landing was conducted to RWY 17L in CYYC, where the aircraft landed without further incident. Following a visual inspection by ARFF, the flight crew taxied the aircraft to the gate. Company maintenance replaced the #1 PCU as per AMM 61-20-11 and after a satisfactory test flight, the aircraft was released back to service. SDR file #202110127005 was submitted by the company to Transport Canada.

C-GWAS, a Cessna U206G, operated by Questor Aviation Ltd. was conducting a local flight from Montgomery County Airport (43A) Star, North Carolina. The flight departed 43A with between 75 and 80 gallons of fuel for the purpose of aerial survey. While flying at 250 feet above ground level the engine loss power and went at idle. A force landing was conducted in a field approximately 23 nautical miles West North West of 43A. On touchdown the nose landing gear (NLG) collapsed, the prop struck the ground and the NLG wheel assembly separated from the airplane. There was also damage to the fuselage bottom. It was reported that just after the airplane came to rest, fuel was spaying from the engine compartment.The National Transportation Safety Board is conducting an investigation. A Federal Aviation Administration's inspector deployed on the accident site. The inspector checked the throttle and mixture controls and both were connected. A strange sound (grinding/binding) was heard when moving the mixture control. Atlanta Air Salvage will recover the wreckage and was tasked to drain the amount of fuel in each fuel tank and segregate.

C-GJZS, a CRJ 900 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting Flight JZA 918 from Toronto Lester B Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Greater Moncton Roméo LeBlanc International Airport (CYQM), NB with 4 crew members and 16 passengers onboard. Shortly after take off, the flight crew noticed a small engine number 1 fan vibration of 1.4 Mil which is still within acceptable limit. As the aircraft continued climbing, the vibration slowly increased until the aircraft levelled off at FL390 where the vibration reached the yellow arc with an indication from 3.7 to a maximum of 4.0 Mil. The crew actioned the QRH and conducted the applicable trouble shooting. The captain requested a lower altitude from ATC to reduce power and try to stabilize the vibration. As the indication was still around 3.3 Mils, the crew declared a Pan Pan, turned back toward CYYZ and shut down the number 1 engine as directed by the QRH. The aircraft landed safely in CYYZ where emergency vehicles were standing by. Engine number 2 fan vibration remained steady around .04 and 0.5 Mil.Company maintenance conducted an inspection with no defects found. The number one fan blade retaining pins were replaced and the engine tested. Results were within acceptable limits.

C-GNLO, a Government of Newfoundland and Labrador Beech Super King Air 350, was conducting a flight from Deer Lake (CYDF), NL to Gander (CYQX), NL. On approach to CYQX the landing gear was selected down but the crew did not receive a left hand main landing gear down green indication. The crew cancelled their IFR clearance, carried out the checklist items, and consulted with their maintenance department. It was decided to divert to St. John’s (CYYT), NL where an emergency was declared to have emergency services standing by as a precaution. The aircraft landed at CYYT without further incident. A faulty left hand main landing gear down indication lamp was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service following operational checks.

C-GYDQ, a Beech 200 aircraft operated by Transwest Air as flight TWA911, was conducting a medevac flight from Wollaston Lake (CZWL), SK  to La Ronge Barber Field (CYVC), SK with a crew of 2 and 3 passengers on board. While on descent into CYVC, the left engine (Pratt & Whitney PT6A-41) began to surge. The crew noticed torque indications from 2000 to 0 Ft-Lbs. and surging fuel flow indications. The crew elected to shut down the left engine and declared an emergency. The aircraft then landed safely and came to a stop on Runway 36. Emergency services met the aircraft and the patient was offloaded and transported to the hospital. The aircraft was then towed off the runway. The operator's maintenance is investigating the engine issue.

C-FMXK, an amateur built Van's RV-7A was conducting a local private sightseeing flight from Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON with only the pilot onboard. While cruising northbound in the direction of Collingwood, ON, the engine lost power. The pilot made a 180 degree turn for a precautionary landing on Eugenia Lake, which was frozen and snow covered. During the landing the nose landing gear collapsed; however, the aircraft did not flip over. The propeller and wheel fairings were also damaged. The pilot exited the aircraft without injury. Police services attended the site.

C-FUTL, a Cessna 525 operated by Novajet as flight NOJ52, departed Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON with a crew of 2 and 2 passengers onboard. While climbing through 8500 feet ASL, the crew heard a loud bang from the right engine (Williams Intl FJ44-1AP turbofan) followed by airframe vibrations. The crew then noticed low oil pressure, high inter turbine and oil temperature indications of the right engine. The crew then consulted the appropriate checklist and shut down the engine. The crew declared an emergency and returned to CYQT. The aircraft then landed safely.It was reported that the engine chip plug exhibited a large amount of metal flakes. The operator's maintenance personnel continues to investigate.

Air Transat Flight TSC016, a Boeing 737-800 was conducting a local IFR flight from John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON. The aircraft was instructed to maintain 4000 feet and proceed to KEBDU, a waypoint located approximately 11 NM southeast of CYHM. ATC notified TSC016 of VFR traffic over KEBDU at 3600 feet. The conflicting traffic was a Near North Aviation Cessna 172M, (registration C-GDXE) doing flight training. ATC instructed TSC016 to descend to 3000 feet. At this point TSC016 was 6.3 miles from C-GDXE on an approximately reciprocal course with a closure rate of 320 knots. ATC issued TSC016 a right turn to avoid traffic and facilitate the approach. Shortly after ATC advised TSC016 that it didn't appear they were turning. TSC016 advised they were responding to a TCAS Resolution Advisory (RA) of a VFR aircraft located abeam them. TSC016 passed abeam C-GDXE with a spacing of 0.7 miles at the point of closest approach. TSC016 was at 3500 feet heading southbound and C-GDXE was descending through 3100 feet heading northwest bound. Both aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GSAX a Summit Air Charters Dornier 228, was operating as flight SU1022 from Gahcho Kue (CGK2), NT to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with 2 flight crew and 6 passengers on board. The aircraft had arrived from CYZF on an IFR flight in IMC with the engine inlet anti-ice on. After arriving, they were on the ground for 10 to 15 minutes unloading and loading with the aircraft parked into wind. There was blowing snow with the wind speed at 25 knots gusting to 30 knots. Once the passengers were loaded the aircraft was started and taxied to the button of the runway. The captain was not satisfied that he had sufficient runway visibility so he taxied back to the ramp and faced into wind again to await the arrival of an IFR inbound aircraft. After 15 minutes had passed the arriving aircraft landed and gave a pilot report that there was more than 1 mile visibility. SU1022 then took position on the runway and departed CGK2 with the bleed air on, the propeller and engine inlet anti-ice off and the engine ignition in the off position. At 400 feet AGL the power was set to climb power and the propeller and engine inlet anti-ice were turned on in anticipation of entering cloud at 700 feet AGL. As they passed 1000 feet AGL and commenced a turn towards CYZF, both engines (Garrett TPE331-5-252D) flamed out. The captain cycled the power levers back and forth and was about to feather the propellers in preparation to glide back to the field when he noticed that the engines still had temperature and oil pressure. He switched the manual ignition on and both engines relit. With engines parameters stabilized the crew elected to proceed to the destination and landed without further incident.   Maintenance update: Both engines were bore scoped for damage and none was found. All systems were checked and verified operational. An engine check run was completed with all systems functioning normally and the aircraft was returned to service.  Operations Update: In consultation with the engine manufacturer (Honeywell) and the airframe manufacturer (Ruag), Summit Air Charters has updated their Dornier 228 SOPs and checklists in regards to the definition of icing conditions. The updates apply to when the application of engine inlet heat and propeller heat occurs as well as when the ignitors are turned on and how long the ignitors remain on.

C-FUTR, a privately registered Beech 58 was conducting a flight from Thunder Bay (CYQT) ON. to Brampton-Caledon (CNC3) ON. At approximately 40 nm south of CYQT the cabin heater system failed. The pilot conducted a cockpit survey to troubleshoot the failure but was unsuccessful in restoring the cabin heater system. Flight conditions were not conducive to continue the flight without cabin heat; therefore, the pilot requested a return to CYQT and declared a PAN PAN. C-FUTR subsequently landed without incident.Maintenance personnel found the cabin heater system remote circuit breaker had tripped. The circuit breaker was reset, the heater was ground checked, and the aircraft was return to service.

C-FSNV, a Cessna 172P operated by Harv's Air Service was conducting a VFR night flight from Steinbach/Steinbach South (CKK7) MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG) MB. The aircraft was cleared into the CYWG Control Zone to maintain 2000 ASL, informed Runway 31 was active and to maintain present heading. C-GFOL, a Beech King Air operated by Keewatin Air as flight Blizzard 210 was conducting a flight from Thompson (CYTH) MB to CYWG was cleared for the right hand visual Runway 31. C-FSNV was instructed to make a left turn 270 degrees and then join left base Runway 31. C-FSNV was observed making a right hand turn. Blizzard 210 was on the approach for Runway 31 and was instructed to turn right to 090.  Both aircraft had confirmed they had each other in sight. Blizzard 210 was instructed to maintain 2000 ASL and turn right for the downwind for Runway 31. C-GWCY, a Boeing 737-6CT operated by WestJet as WJA475 was conducting a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ) ON to CYWG. WJA475 was cleared for the approach to Runway 31 and a loss of separation occurred when WJA475 was on the approach between Blizzard 210 and WJA475. The separation was 2 miles and 900 feet when 3 miles and a 1000 feet is required.

C-FDLG, un Dash 8-102 exploité par Air Inuit effectuait le vol AIE858 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Kangirsuk, QC (CYAS) à destination de l'aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) avec 3 membres d’équipage et 7 passagers à son bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en approche pour l’atterrissage à CYVP, le voyant “Gear Unsafe” pour la roue de nez s’est allumé lors de la sélection du train d’atterrissage en position sortie. L’équipage a effectué une remontée et une urgence a été déclarée avec la station d’information de vol (FSS) de Kuujjuaq. Une fois établie dans un circuit d’attente, la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée et le train d’atterrissage a été déployé avec succès. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 25 sans encombre.

C-GDDP, a Pacific Rim Aviation Academy DA20-C1, was conducting circuit training at Pitt Meadows Airport (CYPK), BC, with 1 instructor and 1 student onboard. The lesson was focused on short-field take-offs and soft field landings. During the 5th circuit, the crew observed a small vibration on touch down however the vibration was minimal due to the back pressure on the flight controls as part of the soft field landing procedure. Once flaps were selected to take-off, the vibration increased slightly and then the aircraft became airborne. On the cross-wind leg, the CYPK tower advised the pilot that he may have lost his nose wheel. The pilot conducted a low and over while the tower confirmed that the nose wheel had departed the aircraft. The aircraft was put into an orbit above CYPK while emergency crews were assembled on the ground and checklists were completed in the aircraft. Approximately 25 minutes later the aircraft landed. During the landing, the aircraft was operated at a reduced airspeed with the fuel and magnetos shut off. The front nose gear strut broke off the aircraft and the aircraft slid to a stop on the front lower engine cowl. There were no injuries and no fire.The nose landing gear was retrieved and sent to the TSB Laboratory for evaluation.

C-FGDZ, an Air Canada Boeing 787-9 was conducting flight AC0874 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC to Frankfurt Rhein-Main Airport (EDDF), Germany.  During the approach, flight crew received EICAS (engine-indicating and crew-alerting system) message "Slats Drive". Flight crew completed the appropriate checklist and advised cabin crew. A Pan Pan was declared with ATC and flight landed without further incident. Maintenance found right hand slats #8 to #12 not extended and slat #1 to #7 partially extended. Further inspection found torque tube disconnected at #8 slat.

C-GOGT, a Beech King Air 200 operated by Beaver Air Services as flight MA03, was conducting a flight from The Pas/Grace Lake (CJR3) MB. to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG) MB. After departing CJR3 the flight crew selected gear up. The nose gear started to retract and then the hydraulic pump stopped running. The main gear remained in the down and locked position. The flight crew continued the climb, declared a PAN PAN with ATC, and a the decision was made to continue to CYWG.  On final approach to CYWG, the flight crew completed the emergency landing gear extension checklist and received a nose landing gear down and locked indication. The aircraft landed safely with ARFF on standby and subsequently taxied to the apron. The aircraft was ferried to Winnipeg/St. Andrews (CYAV) for maintenance. The operator's maintenance replaced the power pack pressure switch.

C-GZVJ, a Beech 1900D operated by Wasaya Airways Limited, was conducting flight WSG1475 from Wapekeka/Angling Lake Airport (CKB6) ON. to  Big Trout Lake (CYTL) ON. During the approach at CYTL, the flight crew selected landing gear down and the down indicator light for the left main gear did not illuminate. A visual inspection from the cockpit indicated that the left main gear was down and there was no red light illumination in the gear handle. The crew discontinued the approach and diverted to Sioux Lookout Airport (CYXL) ON. WSG1475 declared an emergency with Winnipeg Center and contacted company maintenance to troubleshoot the landing gear fault. Upon arriving at CYXL, WSG1475 entered a hold and carried out a manual gear extension and lowerd the flaps to 35 degrees; however, the left main gear down light did not illuminate and landing gear warning horn did not sound. The flight crew conducted a fly past inspection and maintenance personnel informed the crew the left hand gear appeared to be down. WSG1475 made a second approach and landed with Fire and EMS on standby. The aircraft was shutdown on the runway, landing gear pins were installed and the aircraft was towed to the hangar. The operator's maintenance discovered that the left hand gear actuator cannon plug was loose. The cannon plug was cleaned, secured and gear swings were completed. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GZGL, a privately registered Piper PA-31T aircraft, was on final approach to Runway 13 at the Regina Intl. (CYQR), SK with only the pilot on board. During the landing, the aircraft landed with the landing gear retracted and came to a stop on the centerline of the runway. The pilot evacuated the aircraft without injury. The aircraft sustained substantial damage and the runway was closed by a NOTAM. The responding maintenance crew was able to lift the aircraft and extend the landing gear. A down and a locked indication was received in the cockpit. The aircraft was then towed off the runway.

C-GTJL, a Learjet 35A aircraft operated by Sunwest Aviation Ltd., was conducting flight CNK633 from Thunder Bay Intl (CYQT), ON to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. At about 10 000 feet altitude and 20 nm west of CYHZ, the flight crew noted a master warning and number 1 engine (Garrett, TFE731-2-2B) power loss accompanied by low number 1 engine oil pressure, as well as the illumination of left fuel pressure and left generator indications. The flight crew declared an emergency and carried out checklist actions for engine failure in flight and single-engine landing. The flight continued the approach to CYHZ where the flight landed without further incident.The operator is coordinating with the engine manufacturer to determine the cause of the engine power loss.

C-FTBT, a privately registered Piper PA-20 aircraft on skis departed from a farm strip located 20 NM south of Tisdale, Saskatchewan (CJY3) with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the initial climb at approximately 100 feet AGL, the right wing dropped/stalled and the aircraft then struck the ground. A passerby saw the wreckage from the highway and contacted 911. The pilot and passenger sustained serious injury. The pilot and passenger were then taken to hospital. The aircraft was destroyed by the impact forces and there was no post-impact fire.

C-FMBU, a Messerschmitt-Bolkow BK117-B2 helicopter operated by Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service (STARS) as flight SHOCK8T, was enroute from Portage La Prairie/Southport (CYPG), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB with a crew of 2 and 2 passengers onboard. While in cruise at approximately 2000 feet ASL, the crew received a #2 engine (Allied Signal Lycoming LTS101-750B-1) chip light and, before any action could be taken, the light extinguished. Approximately 30 seconds later the engine chip light illuminated again and the crew decided to shut down the #2 engine. The crew then declared a PAN PAN and continued on to CYWG where the helicopter landed safely. An inspection found slivers of metal on the #2 engine chip plug. The engine is undergoing further inspection.

C-FUJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8219 from Sydney/J.A. Douglas McCurdy Airport (CYQY), NS to Toronto/Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. On climb out of CYQY, the flight crew received an AFT LAV SMOKE warning message. The cabin crew reported a visible haze and strong odour in the vicinity of the aft lavatory, but no smoke. The flight crew carried out the required checklist items, including pulling circuit breakers to remove electrical power from the aft lavatory fan motor. The haze and odour was reported as dissipating, and the flight crew requested a diversion to Moncton Intl (CYQM), NB and declared an emergency as a precaution to ensure emergency service were standing by. The aircraft landed at CYQM without further incident. Maintenance personnel subsequently confirmed and replaced a faulty aft lavatory fan motor.

N810NW, an Airbus A330-323 aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL262 from New York/John F. Kennedy Intl (KJFK), NY to Paris/Charles de Gaulle Intl (LFPG), France. When in cruise flight at about 54°37' N, 034°44' W, the flight crew detected a loud noise and an aircraft vibration shudder, and also observed a high vibration indication for the number 1 engine. The flight crew referenced the quick reference handbook and incrementally reduced the number 1 engine to idle. The flight crew noticed number 1 engine stall ECAM messages when power was reduced, and passengers reported sparks coming from the number 1 engine. The flight crew declared an emergency, and initiated a diversion to Reykjavík-Keflavík Intl (BIKF), Iceland where a landing was made without further incident.Maintenance personnel replaced the number 1 engine and the aircraft was returned to service.

The privately registered Mooney M20F (registration C-GYGN) departed Airdrie Aerodrome (CEF4), Alberta, for an instrument flight rules (IFR) flight to Nelson Aerodrome (CZNL), British Columbia, with 1 pilot on board. At approximately 1206 Mountain Standard Time, when the aircraft was 29 nautical miles northeast of the Fairmont Hot Springs Aerodrome (CYCZ), British Columbia,  the pilot declared an emergency and informed air traffic control (ATC) that the aircraft’s attitude indicator had failed. ATC provided several instructions in an attempt to assist the pilot, who was flying in instrument meteorological conditions (IMC). During a left turn, the aircraft entered an unintentional descent and entered a valley in the vicinity of Kananaskis Lake, Alberta. The aircraft lost direct radio contact with ATC, but the pilot was able to continue to relay emergency communications through other aircraft flying in the area. The pilot was able to fly visually along Highway 40 to exit the valley. The aircraft returned to CEF4 without further incident.
