C-GFNJ, an Aero Vodochody L39C owned and operated by International Test Pilots School (ITPS) Canada Ltd., was conducting an aerobatic training flight with 2 pilots on board in the vicinity of London Intl (CYXU), Ontario. During the planned return to base, the aircraft was maneuvering in formation with a company L39C aircraft. After rolling out following a barrel roll, and possibly after a brief application of pitch trim, an uncommanded pitch up movement occurred, the student pilot released the controls under the assumption that the instructor pilot had initiated the pitch up movement and was taking control. The maximum force reached during the pitch excursion was approximately 3.8 G, before the instructor pilot took control of the aircraft. The instructor pilot completed a controllability check which resulted in no abnormal indications, after which an uneventful approach and landing was made. ITPS grounded their L39C aircraft pending an internal inquiry into the occurrence. Maintenance action did not reveal any mechanical deficiencies with the aircraft, and a subsequent test flight did not reveal any flight control abnormalities. It was determined that the most likely cause was the design of the control stick-mounted trim hat, which could be activated with minimal force, and had a tendency to continue trim inputs momentarily after it was released. This may have caused the initial excursion, which was possibly exacerbated when the student pilot released the controls. Following an extensive internal inquiry, including a review of transfer of control procedures, the L39C aircraft were returned to service. ITPS reported that the current pitch trim controls will be replaced with OEM controls.

C-GAQZ, an Airbus A319-100 operated by Air Canada as ACA0993, departed from Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), Ontario to Benito Juárez Intl (MMMX), Mexico. Near the top of climb at 30000 feet, the flight experienced severe turbulence, resulting in a momentary overspeed of 3 knots. There were no reported injuries, and the flight continued to its planned destination.

C-GEGP, an Air Canada Airbus 330-300 was conducting flight ACA0900 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL. On final approach in KFLL, the Air Traffic Control warned the Flight crew that a traffic was crossing the approach path.  Flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory). Flight crew followed the RA and the flight landed in KFLL without further incident.

C-GAQX, an Air Canada Airbus 319-100 was conducting flight ACA1421 from Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl. (MUVR), Cuba to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl.(CYYZ), ON. During cruise approximately 10 nautical miles NNW of Allen C Perkinson Blackstone AAF Airport (KBKT), VA, Flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to ‘'climb’’. Flight crew followed the RA and the flight landed in CYYZ without further incident.

C-GFSG, a Beech King Air 200 operated by Transwest Air, was conducting a medevac flight as TW911 from Wollaston Lake (CZWL) SK to La Ronge (Barber Field) (CYVC) SK. At approximately 60 nm north of CYVC, prior to descent, the left hand engine (PWC PT6A-41) produced multiple loud bangs, vibrations and large flames exited the engine exhaust. The left engine torque and oil pressure indications dropped to zero. The left propeller moved to the feather position and stopped abruptly. The flight crew carried out the engine shutdown checklist and declared an emergency. TW911 landed safely in CYVC with emergency services on standby. There were no injuries. The aircraft was towed from Taxiway A. The operator's maintenance inspection revealed that the left hand engine experienced a contained engine failure.

At 1941 Mountain Standard Time on 01 January 2021, the privately registered Robinson Helicopter Company R44 Raven II helicopter (registration C-FBGT, serial number 13801) departed a farm 6 nautical miles south of Eaglesham/Delta Tango Field Aerodrome, Alberta, on a night visual flight rules flight to DeBolt, Alberta, approximately 30 nautical miles to the south-southwest. The pilot and 3 passengers were on board. At approximately 1954 Mountain Standard Time, the helicopter collided with terrain 10 nautical miles southwest of Eaglesham, Alberta (25.5 nautical miles northeast of DeBolt). The 4 occupants were fatally injured. The helicopter was destroyed and there was a post-impact fire. An emergency locator transmitter signal was received by the search and rescue satellite system.

C-GKOD, an Air Canada Airbus 320-200 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC0902 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL. On short final in KFLL, a passenger approached the Service Director to advise that his cell phone battery charger had caught fire. The Service Director put the charger in the PED (Portable Electronic Device) containment bag and extinguished the fire with water. Due to the phase of flight, the Service Director advised the Flight Crew as soon as the landing was completed and the aircraft had cleared runway 28R. No emergency was declared and the aircraft taxied to the gate without further incident.

C-FNNQ, an Air Canada Boeing 777-300, operating as ACA2284, was enroute from Seoul (RKSI), Korea to Toronto (CYYZ), Ontario when it experienced severe turbulence in the climb from FL 370 to FL390, 49 nm north northwest of the Fort Liard Airport(CYJF), NWT . The flight descended to FL355 to smooth air. The aircraft was 10 knots into the overspeed warning area for approximately 30 seconds. The flight continued without further incident.Maintenance update: Sever turbulence inspection/speed exceedance inspection accomplished per AMM; no faults found.

C-GURG, un Canadair CL60 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, qui effectuait le vol QUE10 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, venait de décoller de l'aéroport de Bonaventure, QC (CYVB), pour un vol à destination de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean-Lesage, QC (CYQB). Lors de la sélection du train d'atterrissage en position rentrée, la roue de nez ne s'est pas rétractée. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été suivie et après vérification du carburant, l'équipage a décidé de se diriger vers CYQB. Une urgence a été déclarée. L'appareil s'est posé sur la piste sans encombre sur la piste 24. Le capteur de positions du train a été trouvé défectueux et a été changé.

N532CV, an amphibious float equiped de Havilland DHC-6-300, operated by Bridger Aerospace, was conducting a maintenance test flight from Calgary Int'l (CYYC), AB returning to CYYC, with two flight crew on board. In cruise flight, the crew experienced a loss of electrical power to numerous aircraft systems. Three of the main power distribution circuit breakers tripped simultaneously, causing a loss of power to avionics, including radios and navigational equipment, and the gear position advisory system.The main hydraulic power for the flaps, landing gear, pitot-static instruments, and the standby compass remained functional. The crew actioned each individual inoperative system checklist including Landing Gear Fails to Extend or Retract. The crew contacted CYYC ATC tower via cellular phone and declared an emergency. A flyby of CYYC tower was conducted to confirm the landing gear was extended and the crew completed a normal visual approach to landing. There were no injuries.

C-FSNQ, an Air Canada Boeing 737-8 MAX was conducting non-revenue positioning flight ACA2358 from Pinal Airpark Marana (KMZJ) AZ, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC. After departure from KMZJ, the crew received a Left Eng Hydraulic Low Pressure indication. Following QRH action and a discussion with Dispatch & Maintenance, the crew elected to continue to CYUL. Shortly thereafter, the crew was alerted to a fuel imbalance from the left wing and shut down the left engine as per the QRH. The crew then diverted to Tucson Intl. (KTUS), AZ, declared a PAN PAN and landed on runway 11L. The aircraft was brought to a stop and once cleared by safety vehicles they were escorted to the ramp without further incident.

C-FNTA, a Northern Thunderbird Air Beech B300 operating as NTA201, was conducting a medevac flight from Burns Lake Airport (CYPZ), BC, to Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC, with 2 flight crew and 3 passengers onboard. During the climb to cruise altitude, the captain observed an uncommanded power reduction on the right hand (RH) engine (PRATT & WHITNEY CANADA PT6A-60A). The crew manually applied full power to the RH engine with no change to the engine performance. The crew declared an emergency for partial power loss of the RH engine and requested ARFF to stand by. During the approach, the RH engine regained full power and the aircraft landed without incident. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft. Upon inspection, maintenance found the primary governor had failed on the RH engine. The governor was replaced and a test flight was completed satisfactory.

C-GPCJ, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Saab 340, was operating as flight PCO3042 from Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International Airport (CYXC), BC to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB with 3 crew and 9 passengers on board. C-GCWJ, a Westjet Boeing B737-7CT, was operating as flight WJA118 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB with 5 crew and 75 passengers onboard. A loss of separation occurred as WJA118, who was following ATC radar vectors, closed the distance on PCO3042 who was on approach to Runway 29 in CYYC. Separation deteriorated to 2.7 NM where 3.0 NM was required. ATC separation was regained when the controller turned WJA118 to a heading of 110 degrees. Both aircraft landed CYYC without further incident and there were no injuries.

C-GFSV, a Central Mountain Air Ltd Beech 1900D operating as GLR8480, was conducting a flight from Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC, to Terrace Airport (CYXT), BC, with 2 flight crew and 6 passengers onboard. During approach, the landing gear did not extend and the flight crew executed a missed approach. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist and manually extended the landing gear while in a hold. The flight crew contacted ATC for a second approach, ATC advised that there was an approach ban due to the weather. Due to inflight icing conditions and uncertainty of weather, the flight crew elected to divert to Smithers Airport (CYYD), BC, and requested emergency services to be on standby as a precaution. The aircraft landed at CYYD without incident. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft.Upon inspection, maintenance found the landing gear selector valve had failed in the up position. The selector valve was replaced, the landing gear was function checked satisfactory, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GNWZ, a Pilatus PC-12 operated by Northway Aviation as flight NAL890, was conducting an IFR flight from St. Andrews (CYAV), MB to Keewaywin (CPV8), ON. During the climb the pilot observed an electrical instrumentation failure, including the failure of the MFD 2 and right side PFD. The pilot requested a level off altitude for troubleshooting. Shortly after, the pilot declared an emergency, and requested VFR and diverting vectors to Portage La Prairie (CYPG), MB. A visual approach was conducted to Runway 13R at CYPG and the aircraft landed without further incident.The operator's maintenance inspection revealed that a high current circuit breaker had tripped. The circuit breaker was reset, the aircraft was ground run, and the aircraft subsequently returned to CYAV.

9H-PPE, an Airbus A340-642 aircraft operated by Maleth Aero, was conducting cargo flight MLT221 from Bournemouth Airport (EGHH), England to John F Kennedy Intl (KJFK), New York. While cruising at FL380, 9H-PPE reduced speed in anticipation of expected moderate turbulence. At about 55°30' N, 042°00' W the intensity of turbulence increased from moderate to severe, making it impossible for the crew to type a CPDLC (Controller–pilot data link communications) descent request. The crew was unable to contact Gander Oceanic on HF radio. However, the crew did broadcast a PAN PAN signal and descended to FL340. Gander Oceanic subsequently acknowledged and cleared the flight at the requested level. The crew cancelled the PAN PAN, continued to the destination and landed without further incident. The aircraft quick access recorder was downloaded, and flight data analysis determined that flight loads sustained were within limitations. Maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft, with no fault found.

C-FCGM, a Beechcraft King Air 200 operated by North Cariboo Flying Service Ltd, was conducting flight NCB2400 from Calgary International (CYYC), AB to Edmonton International (CYEG), AB with two crew and no passengers on board. After departure the crew selected the landing gear up, but the green nose gear light did not illuminate. The crew leveled at 7000 feet and recycled the gear, but was not successful. The emergency check list was completed and the crew performed a successful manual gear extension. The flight returned to CYYC, emergency services were requested and the flight landed safely on Runway 17R. Following the flight, maintenance on the landing gear system was conducted and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FVTL, un Piper Navajo PA31 exploité par Exact Air, effectuait un vol d’entrainement selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Val d’Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de l’aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC). Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en approche pour la RNAV piste 30, le voyant « R Alt INOP » s’est allumé. L’équipage a complété la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour une panne d’alternateur simple; une fois la liste de vérification complétée, l’équipage a eu une indication de double panne d’alternateur. Par mesure de précaution, l’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence (PAN PAN) et l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre.

The Air Canada Airbus 321, C-FJNX, operating as ACA214 on a flight from Vancouver (CYVR), BC to Calgary (CYYC), AB, experienced moderate turbulence on descent into CYYC. All passengers were secure but the cabin crew was still moving around the cabin. Three flight attendants fell and received minor injuries. They were able to return to their jump-seats for landing. EMS was not contacted and the flight landed without further incident.

C-GDME, a Diamond DA20-C1 aircraft operated by Journey Air Ltd, was conducting a local training flight from Windsor International Airport (CYQG), ON with only a student pilot onboard. Upon return,  during on an attempt to land on runway 25, the aircraft bounced; the student pilot recovered however, the aircraft bounced again. The aircraft propeller and nose landing gear contacted the runway. The student shut down the aircraft and contacted the tower for assistance. The company's Chief Flight Instructor was monitoring the tower radio and advised they were on their way to provide assistance. They found the propeller tips broken and the nose landing gear bent. The aircraft has been towed back to the operator hangar. There were no injuries.

C-GAPY, an Airbus A319 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA0996 from Vancouver Int'l Airport (CYVR), BC to Mexico City/Benito Juarez Int'l (MMMX), Mexico with 5 crewmembers and 110 passengers onboard. On departure, the aircraft struck a bird and the flight crew decided to return to land at CYVR. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and an overweight landing was carried out without further incident.The operator's maintenance conducted a bird strike inspection on the aircraft and a boroscope inspection on the right-hand engine. No damage was found. Overweight landing parameters were within limits as per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual.

C-FWPP, a privately registered ski-equipped Cessna 140, was conducting a VFR flight with only the pilot onboard from Nipawin (CYBU), SK to a private airstrip near Gronlid SK, following servicing of the aircraft. Shortly prior to arrival, the engine (Continental C-90-12F) started to sputter, and the pilot was required to carry out a forced landing. On approach the aircraft struck trees and overturned. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The pilot was treated for minor injuries.

C-GUSC, un Jetstream 32 exploité par Pascan Aviation sous l’indicatif PSC902 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean-Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de l’aéroport des Îles-de-la-Madeleine, QC (CYGR). Alors que l’appareil était en vol de croisière, à environ 198 milles nautiques à l’est de l’aéroport de Mont-Joli, QC (CYYY) les paramètres du moteur de gauche ont commencé à donner des indications erratiques. L’équipage a fermé le moteur (Garrett TPE331) par mesure préventive, et a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN). L’appareil a effectué un retour à CYQB où il s’est posé sans encombre.

C- FOWJ, a privately registered Piper Super Cub, PA-18, was operating from a private airstrip approximately 5nm SE of Dawson Creek (CYDQ), BC, near the town of Pouce Coupe, BC. Two days prior, on December 6th 2020, the pilot had completed a ferry trip from Nanaimo (CYCD), BC for the new owner of the aircraft. On the occurrence flight, following a complete preflight inspection, the pilot was taking the new owner on a local flight to demonstrate the aircraft. The owner occupied the front seat while the pilot flew from the aft seat. During the take-off roll, after the tail had come off of the ground, the pilots control stick in the rear seat became detached from the aircraft. Once the pilot realized he did not have complete control of the aircraft he tried to give the owner control, but there was not enough time to react to the situation. The aircraft subsequently collided with trees and brush at the end of the runway. Both occupants walked away from the aircraft without any injuries.Following the accident, it was found that the rear control stick was not installed in accordance with the manufacturer's requirements. The control stub socket and control stick had been modified in such a manner that allowed the stick to be installed or removed without removing any hardware, giving the appearance that the control stick hardware was installed securely.

C-FDSG, a float-equipped de Havilland DHC-2 Mk.1 Beaver aircraft operated by Wilderness Seaplanes Ltd., was scheduled for a flight from Port Hardy Water Aerodrome (CAW5), BC, to a local logging camp. During pre-flight preparations, the pilot was struck by the propeller and fell into the water. The passengers found the pilot face down in the water approximately 14 minutes later and, after recovering him, they began to administer first aid with the guidance from a 911 operator. First responders arrived and transported the pilot to hospital.  The pilot died from his injuries the following day.

C-GHQQ, a Boeing 787-8 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA0992 from Benito Juarez International Airport (MMMX), Mexico to Leaster B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON with 9 crewmembers and 76 passengers onboard. While on cruise, approximately 20 minutes after takeoff, the flight crew experienced an EICAS ''Slats Drive'' message. The flight crew completed the applicable checklist and after discussion with the maintenance and dispatch departments, the decision was to carry on to CYYZ and declare ''Pan Pan''. The aircraft landed on runway 33R with rescue vehicles on standby, exited the runway at a high speed taxiway and taxied to the gate without further incident. The maintenance department troubleshot the problem leading to the replacement of Slat 6 INBD SKEW Sensor. The maintenance performed an operational check and found the system serviceable.

The Sunwest Aviation Ltd. de Havilland DHC-8-200, C-GYUP, was operating as flight CNK22 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Conklin/Liesmer (CET2), AB with 3 crew and 15 passengers on board. While en route the aircraft experienced a hydraulic failure. The crew declared an emergency and returned to CYYC. The landing was uneventful with airport rescue and fire fighting units standing by.Company maintenance found a hydraulic line (at the hydraulic power transfer unit) ruptured and the engine driven hydraulic pump was found to have run in excess of 15 minutes with no hydraulic fluid. Both the engine driven and power transfer unit hydrualic pumps were replaced.

The Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Dash 8-400, C-GGOF, was operating as flight ACA8552 from Victoria (CYTYJ), BC to Calgary (CYYC), AB with 4 flight crew and 23 passengers on board. On descent into CYYC the flight encountered severe turbulence at about 13000 feet above sea level. All onboard were in their seats with seat belts fastened. The aircraft was difficult to control for approximately 20 seconds and an overspeed of 3 to 5 knots occurred. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft.

C-GLQY, un hélicoptère Bell 206L exploité par Les Hélicoptères Canadiens Limitée, effectuait un vol local d’entraînement selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’héliport Montréal/Les Cèdres, QC (CSH6) avec 2 pilotes à bord. Alors que l’aéronef était en courte finale pour l'aire d'approche finale et de décollage (FATO) à environ à 30 pieds au-dessus du sol, le moteur a soudainement décéléré. L’atterrissage a pu être complété sans encombre. Une fois au sol, le moteur s’est éteint lorsque la manette des gaz a été mise au ralenti. L’équipage a fermé la valve d’arrivée de carburant et a ventilé le moteur. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GCVS, un Beech 200C exploité par Max Aviation inc. sous l’indicatif MAX210 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) à destination d’Amos/Magny, QC (CYEY). Lors de la montée initiale, le voyant d’avertissement lumineux « Fire detector » s’est allumé. L’équipage n’a pas constaté la présence de fumée et les paramètres moteurs étaient normaux. Une urgence a été déclarée par mesure de précaution. L’aéronef est revenu vers CYVP où il s’est posé sans encombre. Le service de maintenance de la compagnie n’a détecté aucun signe de feu et l’aéronef a été remis en service le lendemain.

C-FUJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight JZA7936, was enroute from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON with a crew of 4 and 43 passengers onboard. While descending through 33000 feet, the crew received a #2 hydraulic low pressure caution indication and the #2 hydraulic fluid quantity indicator, indicated a complete loss of fluid. After referrencing the QRH and consulting with company maintenance personel by radio, the crew decided to continue to CYQT. During approach into CYQT the crew was able to extend the landing gear using normal procedures. The crew requested that AARF be put on standby and the aircraft then landed safely. The aircraft came to a stop on the runway and was inspected by AARF before it continued to the gate.The operator's maintenance subsequently replaced the #2 engine driven hydraulic pump and engine quick disconnect for the pressure line.

C-FWYO, an Airco Aircraft Charters Ltd. Beech A100, was operating as flight AR128 from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Kelowna (CYLW), BC with 2 crew and 3 passengers and 2000 pounds of fuel on board. The flight departed CYEG utilizing runway 20 at 1415 MST. After departure, the flight crew selected the landing gear up. The gear in transit light illuminated and the two green main landing gear inidicator lights extinguished, but the nose landing gear green light remained illuminated. The crew requested and received a block of airspace from air traffic services to trouble shoot the issue. The flight crew subsequently selected the landing gear down, to which they heard some abnormal mechanical sounds and the status of the landing gear indication lights remained unchanged. The captain elected to perform a flyby of the control tower in an attempt to get visual confirmation of the landing gear position. The tower reported that the landing gear appeared to be in the extended position. The flight crew then completed the manual extension of the landing gear in accordance with the abnormal procedures, but was unable to cycle the manual extension handle. The flight crew informed the passengers that they would be returning to CYEG and conducted a passenger briefing as there was a concern the landing gear was not fully extended and may collapse/retract on landing. At approximately 1505MST, an approach and touch down on Runway 20 was subsequently conducted. The captain felt the left side main landing gear collapsing and executed a go around. The flight crew then requested and received permission to enter a hold for further troubleshooting. Company maintenance was contacted and the decision was made to execute an emergency landing. At approximately 1515 MST the aircraft landed runway 20, the left main landing gear collapsed and the aircraft came to a rest near taxiway B1. Passengers and crew evacuated out the main cabin entrance door. There were no injuries and there was no fire. Subsequent inspection by company maintenance personnel found a taper pin for the nose landing gear drive sprocket and right main landing gear driveshaft not installed in the right side output shaft of the landing gear gearbox. This resulted in the landing gears becoming unsynchronized.

C-GOCJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd. Boeing 767-316, was operating as CJT584 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC to Hamilton (CYHM), ON with 2 crewmembers on board. Shortly after takeoff, an engine-indicating and crew-alerting system (EICAS) caution alert "R HYD SYS PRESS" occurred with the associated "SYS PRESS" light illuminated. An en route climb was established, the appropriate Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) checklist was actioned and the "SYS PRESS" light remained illuminated. The QRH checklist required the right hydraulic system to be disabled. The crew declared a PAN PAN and requested a return to CYVR. No fuel dump was required as the aircraft was projected to be within 2000 pounds of the maximum certified landing weight. The aircraft landed without further incident. Emergency vehicles inspected the aircraft after landing and no hydraulic leaks were found.Maintenance tested the hydraulic system and verified that the defect was an indication only issue. The applicable hydraulic pressure switch was replaced, an overweight landing inspection was completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GXZY, a privately registered Piper PA-28-200 Arrow II was conducting a recreational flight from and returning to, Langley (CYNJ), BC with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the landing roll, directional control was lost, and the aircraft went off the left side of Runway 01 and came to rest on the intersecting runway. During the excursion, the aircraft collided with two aerodrome signs, one per wing, and the aircraft sustained damage to the wing leading edges and the right flap. The aircraft was able to taxi to the apron under its own power; there were no injuries.The aircraft is being inspected by maintenance to confirm the extent of the damage.

On 02 December 2020, an Air Canada Airbus A220-300 aircraft (registration C-GJYE), intending to operate as flight ACA 624 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International airport (CYYZ), ON to Halifax/Stanfield International airport (CYHZ), NS was conducting a number 1 engine start after having been pushed back from the gate. While the tug was still hooked up, the flight crew started the number 1 engine, felt a vibration and heard an unexpected noise. The flight crew noticed the exhaust gas temperature rise and the engine N2 speed at around 10%. The attending ground crew indicated a fire on the intercom. The flight crew stopped the engine start sequence and called for fire trucks to come to the aircraft. No emergency was declared. The aircraft was towed back to the gate for maintenance inspection. Initial inspection revealed the presence of snow and ice at the front of the engine intake. A boroscope inspections was completed and no other faults were found. An EGT overtemp inspection revealed that the EGT reached 1050 C for 11 seconds. As per the maintenance manual, no further action was required.

The Sky Regional Airlines Embraer 175 (AC7505, C-FXJC) was parked at the gate in Ottawa/ MCIA (CYOW)and was boarding for the flight to Toronto/ LBPIA (CYYZ). Approximately half of the passengers were boarded when the flight crew heard "FIRE" from the cabin and noticed smoke coming from the heater attached to the bridge. Boarding was stopped, and the ground crew began to use fire extinguishers on the heater; ARFF also responded to the scene. The captain decided not to deplane the passengers due to the location of the faulty heater underneath the bridge, but had passengers deplane after it was safe to do so. The aircraft was covered on the left side with the retardant residue, and after company maintenance was contacted it was decided to remove aircraft from service until a thorough inspection of the aircraft was completed. No damage was found and after cleaning the aircraft it was returned to service.

C-FSAJ, a privately registered PA-28-140 Cherokee, was conducting a recreational flight from Courtney Airpark (CAH3), BC to Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC with the pilot and one passenger on board. They began the day in CYPK and were on the third and final leg of their round-trip flight. The aircraft departed CAH3 from Runway 13 and climbed straight out with no issues. When the aircraft was level at 2000 feet above sea level (ASL), the pilot requested a clearance through the Comox control zone toward Sechelt and a climb to 3500 feet ASL with Comox air traffic control (ATC). When the aircraft was climbing through 2200 feet ASL, there was an unplanned loss in engine power (AVCO Lycoming O-320-E3D); engine rpm reduced to idle. The pilot began a 180° turn to the right planning to return to CAH3. On seeing the deviation on radar, Comox ATC queried if everything was alright. The pilot stated that they were having engine trouble, planned to land, and were trouble shooting the problem. When asked if they were declaring an emergency, they stated that they were. During the attempts to regain power, the pilot and his passenger (also a trained pilot) noted that as they pulled the throttle in and out, it stuck a few times and then there was no resistance at all. The pilot determined that a return to CAH3 was not possible and decided to ditch just off the shoreline. The main gear touched the water first and when the nose gear contacted the surface, the aircraft flipped over coming to rest inverted in approximately 3 feet of water. The pilot and passenger undid their seatbelts, opened the latch but were unable to open the door. Persons from shore waded out and were able to open the door and both occupants successfully evacuated the aircraft. A police helicopter, local police, fire, and ambulance personnel attended the scene. The pilot and passenger were taken to the local hospital for observation; no injuries were apparent. The aircraft was substantially damaged in the accident and was recovered from the beach 2 days later. The aircraft maintenance engineer who recovered the aircraft determined the nut that connected the throttle cable to the throttle lever had backed off from its respective bolt.

C-FNJB, a Cessna 172P operated by Canadian Flight Centre, was conducting circuit training at Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC with 1 instructor and 1 student on board. The exercise being conducted prior to the occurrence was practice forced landings. The aircraft's profile on final was higher than the anticipated flight path and the aircraft touched farther down the runway than was desired. On touchdown, the instructor took control of the aircraft and applied the brakes but unlike the previous landing on the wet runway, the braking action was poor. The PIC determined that conditions did not permit a go around. The aircraft overran the end of the runway, traversed a 250 foot grass field, crossed a ditch, and came to rest in a field approximately 300 feet beyond the runway threshold. The pilot shut down the aircraft and evacuated with the student. There were no injuries but the aircraft sustained substantial damage to its propeller, engine cowling, windshield, lower fuselage, and landing gear.Maintenance crews recovered the aircraft and an aircraft maintenance organization will assess the extent of the damage.

C-FAFS, an ATR-42-300 operated by Calm Air, was operating flight CAV464 from Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU to Naujaat (CYUT), NU with 3 crew members onboard. During the landing on Runway 34 at CYUT, directional control was lost and the aircraft experienced a runway side excursion on the east side of the runway. The aircraft came to rest approximately 44 meters from the runway edge. The captain suffered serious injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The TSB is investigating.

C-FWAL, a Pilatus PC-12/47 operated by Air Bravo as flight AB1776 was on descent for Runway 25 at the Thunder Bay Airport(CYQT), ON with 2 crew and 3 passengers on board. During the initial descent, the crew heard a loud bang come from the nose of the aircraft followed by an immediate nose gear unsafe indication in the cockpit. During final approach, the crew selected the landing gear down and received a down and locked indication for the left and right main gear but the nose gear unsafe indication remained. Cycling of the landing gear and use of the emergency gear extension failed to get a nose gear down and locked indication. A fly-by the tower revealed that the nose gear was only partially extended. The crew conducted several firm touchdowns on the runway to try and force the nose gear down, but was unsuccessful. The crew then requested to land on Runway 12 and declared an emergency. While on short final, the engine was intentionally shutdown and the aircraft was force landed. During the landing, the nose gear collapsed completely and the aircraft came to a stop on the centre line of the runway. The crew and passengers then exited the aircraft  without injury. The aircraft sustained substantial damage and was subsequently removed from the runway.  An inspection of the aircraft by the operator's maintenance personel revealed that the right hand nose gear drag brace had failed.

C-GHJB, a Cessna U206E aircraft operated by WMK Holdings Ltd, was conducting a flight from Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB to La Loche (CYL4), SK with one pilot and 4 passengers onboard. Shortly after rotation during take-off on Runway 26, the stall warning horn activated, the aircraft yawed to the right and departed controlled flight. The nose contacted a snow covered grass area north of the runway resulting in the compression to the nose landing gear and damage to the propeller. Shortly after, the aircraft contacted the right main landing gear, followed by ground contact to the right wingtip and then rolled over to the left wingtip, veered further to the right and came to rest on a northeast heading. The aircraft was substantially damaged but no injuries were reported.A post-accident inspection by a third party maintenance provider found no pre exisitings issues with the aircraft.

An Air Canada B787-9, C-FRTG was conducting flight AC7201, an IFR flight from London Heathrow (EGLL), United Kingdom, to Toronto/Pearson Airport (CYYZ), Ontario, with 3 flight crew members on board. During cruise at approximately 21:54 EST, the crew received a 'SLAT DRIVE FAIL' message. The flight continued towards CYYZ, during the arrival the crew declared 'PAN PAN'. ARFF was dispatched, the aircraft landed uneventfully at 23:27 EST.

C-FZUH, an Air Canada Airbus 319-100, was conducting flight ACA1054 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Phoenix Sky Harbor Intl. (KPHX), AZ. During approach, flight crew received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) to ‘’descend’’. Flight crew followed the RA and the flight landed without further incident.

The privately registered Cessna 172F, CF-RVH, was operating from a private airstrip in Sexsmith, AB. Prior to takeoff, the pilot ploughed the field to clear the runway surface. During the takeoff roll, as the aircraft rotated, the left wheel contacted a windrow and the aircraft drifted left into the unploughed area adjacent to the runway. The left wing tip contacted the ground and while attempting to maintain directional control, the right wing contacted the ground and the nose landing gear collapsed before the aircraft came to rest. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured and the ELT activated.

C-GCTM, un appareil de type Cessna U206G exploité par Montmagny Air Service Inc., effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue au départ de l’aéroport de L’Île aux Grues, QC (CSH2) à destination de Montmagny, QC (CSE5), avec un pilote à son bord. Lors de l’atterrissage piste 26, l’appareil a été déporté vers la gauche en raison du vent traversier. Lors du touché des roues, l’appareil a ensuite dévié vers la droite et a sorti de piste. En voulant revenir vers la piste, le terrain mou a fait en sorte que l’hélice a touché le sol et l'appareil s'est immobilisé. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GCQJ, un Cessna 150F en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aérodrome de Joliette, QC (CSG3) avec une pilote à bord. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en approche pour un atterrissage, le moteur a calé et la pilote a effectué un atterrissage forcé dans le stationnement des aéronefs, situé au nord de la piste 15. Lors du contact avec le sol, la roue de nez s'est affaissée. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé, et l'appareil a subi des dommages à la roue de nez, au châssis et au capot inférieur du moteur ainsi qu'aux tuyaux des pots d'échappement. L'inspection des réservoirs de carburant après l'atterrissage a révélée que les réservoirs de carburant étaient vides.

C-FWAU, a Beech 1900D operated by Wasaya Airways LP, was conducting a flight from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON to Angling Lake (CKB6), ON. During the climb through 10 000 feet the cabin door light illuminated. The crew requested priority return to CYXL and landed the aircraft without further incident.The operator's maintenance personel inspected the door and confirmed serviceablilty; however, the inidcation system was found to be defective. The system was deferred and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FNVS, a Beech 1900D operated by North Cariboo Flying Service Ltd., was conducting flight NCB2911 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Prince George (CYXS), BC. An Airbus A310 operated by the Royal Canadian Air Force was conducting flight HUSK99 departing from and returning to CYYC. After departure northbound from CYYC, NCB2911 was cleared to turn left and fly direct to CYXS. HUSK99 had previously departed CYYC was proceeding on their route NNW. Approximately 15 nm WNW of CYYC, minimum separation between the two aircraft was lost. The separation deteriorated to 4.2 nm laterally and 100 feet vertically, where 5 nm laterally or 1000 feet vertically is required.

C-GJQN, a Canadian Helicopters Sikorsky S-61N was conducting a flight abroad when the right hand engine failed without warning while in cruise.  Flight crew conducted checklist and SOP, declared a PAN PAN and returned at departure airport for an uneventful run-on landing.

C-FKWE, a WestJet Encore DHC-8-400 aircraft, was conducting flight WEN3107 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Terrace (CYXT), BC with 4 crew members and 46 passengers on board. During a visual approach to CYXT Runway 33 the flight crew were unable to extend the aircraft flaps. The flight crew conducted a go around and advised ATC of intentions to return to CYVR. Enroute to CYVR the crew declared a PAN PAN. The flight landed without further incident. Subsequent maintenance actions revealed loose ground studs in the circuit breaker panel, including the ground for the flap control unit. The loose studs were tightened and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GXHW, un Cirrus SR22 privé effectuait un vol de nuit selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport Du Rocher-Percé (Pabok), QC (CTG3) à destination de Québec/Neuville, QC (CNV9) avec le pilote et 2 passagers à bord. L’aéronef a effectué une approche en vue d’un atterrissage sur la piste 06. Suite au touché des roues, l’aéronef a rebondi et le pilote a ressenti une instabilité de l’aéronef. Jugeant qu’il était préférable de redécoller, il a effectué une remise des gaz. Suite à la remise des gaz, l’aéronef a dévié vers la gauche et s’est incliné vers la droite malgré la déflexion maximale du palonnier de droite. L’aile droite aurait touché le sol et l’aéronef a terminé sa course dans le fossé du côté nord de la piste. Les occupants, non blessés, ont pu s’extirper de l’aéronef. Une fuite de carburant s’est produite suite à une fracture du réservoir, mais aucun incendie ne s'est déclaré. La radiobalise de repérage d’urgence s’est déclenchée à l’impact et a transmis le signal de détresse. Les pompiers ont été déployés sur les lieux de l’accident.

The privately registered Piper PA 28R-201T, C-GAZL, had just completed a touch and go on Runway 12 at Fort St John, BC (CYXJ) intending to turn right and return to Grande Prairie, AB (CYQU). WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-400, C-FOWE, operating as WEN3101 on a flight from Calgary, AB (CYYC) was setting up for the RNAV approach to Runway 30. C-GAZL was given the traffic, WEN3101, on approach to Runway 30 and acknowledged. The FSS specialist requested that C-GAZL remain east and then corrected the request for C-GAZL to remain north of the approach to Runway 30. C-GAZL replied they planned to turn south in front of the approaching traffic. The FSS reported WEN3101 was at C-GAZL’s 12 o’clock 3 NM opposite direction, descending out of 6 900 feet. WEN3101 called the PA28 in sight and C-GAZL reported seeing WEN3101. WEN3101 received and responded to a TCAS RA. Surveillance data indicated that spacing between C-GAZL and WEN3101 reduced to 0.6 miles laterally and 100 feet vertically.

C-GHJP, a Sikorsky S-76A operated by Helijet International Inc, was conducting night VFR flight JBA724 from Victoria Harbour Heliport (CBF7), BC, to Vancouver/Harbour Heliport (CBC7), BC, with 2 pilots and 6 passengers on board. Approximately 1 minute into flight, the engine chip annunciator illuminated for the No. 1 engine (Rolls-Royce Corporation, Model 250-C30). The pilots did not see any secondary engine indications and elected to return to CBF7. The pilot-in-command declared a PAN PAN and the aircraft landed without incident. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft. Upon inspection, maintenance found 2 ferrous flakes on the No. 1 engine upper magnetic chip detector. The No. 1 engine chip detectors were tested, cleaned, and reinstalled. The aircraft was ground run for 30 minutes with no further indications. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPSK, un British Aerospace Jetstream 32 exploité par Pascan Aviation, effectuait le vol PSC837 depuis Bagotville, Québec (CYBG) à destination de Sept-Iles, Québec (CYZV). Lors de la sélection du train d'atterissage à la position sortie, une indication que la roue de nez non sortie et verouillée est apparue sur le système d'indication. Une urgence à été déclarée et la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée. Suite à la procédure d'extension manuelle du train, l'indication de roue de nez non sortie et verouillée est demeurée. L'équipage a effectué la procédure d'atterrissage avec une roue de nez non verrouillée, procédant à l'arrêt des 2 moteurs au toucher des roues. L'atterrissage s'est déroulé sans encombre et a été immobilisé sur la piste. Les passagers ont été transportés au terminal et l'appareil a été remorqué.

C-GITA, a Top Aces Inc. Dassault-Dornier Alpha jet was conducting a fighter training mission from Wittmundhafen (ETNT), Germany.  During recovery phase of the flight at approximately FL280 with a cabin pressure set at 11000 feet, the pilot felt initial symptoms of hypoxia. The pilot immediately selected EMG (overpressure) and 100% oxygen on the regulator and symptoms went away. The aircraft landed back to ETNT without further incident.

C-GEEN, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-400, was conducting flight WEN3298 from Prince George (CYXS), BC to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC with 4 crew and 16 passengers on board. During cruise, the crew received a Hydraulic Caution Light. The crew declared a PAN PAN and used the quick reference handbook to troubleshoot. The landing gear was extended manually as the aircraft descended through 10 000'. The aircraft landed without further incident and was met by ARFF. There were no injuries.Maintenance found the nose gear down lock actuator flex line leaking. The part was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOTC, a commercially operated Cessna 172M aircraft, owned by Canadian Institute of Aviation Technology Inc., was conducting flight training at Kelowna International Airport (CYLW), BC with a student pilot on board, the sole occupant. When the aircraft was on final approach for Runway 34, the aircraft struck the elevated runway approach lights and then the grass area short of the runway. The aircraft came to a stop in the soft grass 279 meters from the runway threshold line with the nose gear collapsed. The pilot exited the aircraft with minor injuries. An ELT signal was not detected. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FMQG, a privately operated Cessna 206 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Anahim Lake (CAJ4), BC  to Bella Coola (CYBD), BC with a sole pilot on board. While the aircraft was flying at approximately 2000 feet ASL, over the Dean Channel, the engine (Teledyne Continental TSIO-520-C) experienced a complete power loss. The aircraft was ditched into the channel near the mouth of the Dean River. Upon entry into the water the aircraft began to sink and the pilot quickly exited. The pilot was wearing a manual inflation PFD which he inflated upon exit from the aircraft. The aircraft then sank below the water surface while the pilot, wearing his PFD, swam to the shore line where he was able to summon assistance from a nearby cabin. The pilot sustained minor injuries. An ELT signal was not received.

C-FXTG, a privately registered Weatherly 620B aircraft with only the pilot on board, was conducting a takeoff from a private strip northeast of Leader SK to conduct spraying operations. When the aircraft was approximately 3/4 of the way down the strip, a pick-up truck backed onto the strip and stopped in front of the aircraft. The pilot maneuvered the aircraft to avoid a collision. The aircraft departed the strip and was brought to a stop in tall crops. The pilot was uninjured. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the propeller, left wing, landing gear and spray gear.

C-FZYG, an Amateur Built, Glass Goose, was initiating a local flight from Pembroke (CYTA), ON with 1 pilot onboard. While on take off roll on runway 35, the aircraft nosed up quicker and at a higher angle of attack than expected. The pilot applied a forward pressure on the control stick to compensate resulting in a nose down attitude. The nose wheel struck the runway and the aircraft began to porpoise. On the third runway contact, the aircraft slid off the runway onto the grass surface. Emergency services deployed to the accident site and the airport closed runway 35 until all the debris were removed. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the nose landing gear, cockpit, undercarriage and fuselage. The pilot received only minor injuries.

C-FGZE, a Top Aces Inc. McDonnell Douglas A-4N was conducting training mission German air Forces from Wittmundhafen (ETNT), Germany. On takeoff roll accelerating through 135 kts, the aircraft struck a bird (buzzard).  The pilot continued takeoff and left gear down for visual inspection by wingman.  The pilot declared a Pan Pan, burned fuel to achieve landing weight and returned to ETNT for uneventful landing.  There was no damage found on the aircraft.

C-FRUZ, a De Havilland DHC-8-300 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight 8478 from Grande Prairie (CYQU), AB, to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. Upon selection of the landing gear down on arrival at CYYC, the flight crew observed 3 red gear warning lights along with an amber landing gear handle indication.  The flight crew conducted a go around, actioned the QRH and completed a successful alternate gear extension. For precautionary measures, the flight crew requested ARFF to standby for the landing. The flight landed without any further incident and the aircraft taxied to the gate. There were no injuries.The operator's maintenance replaced the landing gear selector panel with no faults noted. Gear swings were completed and the landing gear tested normal. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FDOU, un Beech Aircraft Corporation A100 exploité par Propair inc. (vol PRO4210) effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l’aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda (CYUY) (Québec) à l’aéroport de Chissasibi (CSU2) (Québec), avec 2 membres d’équipage et 2 passagers à bord. À 2245Z, alors que l’appareil était en approche initiale à environ 20 miles marins au sud de CSU2, une fluctuation de la pression d’huile du moteur gauche (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-28) est survenue. L’équipage a fermé le moteur, a déclaré un état d’urgence et a effectué un déroutement à destination de La Grande Rivière (CYGL) (Québec). L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre, et il ni a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FPCC, a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan operated by Wasaya Airways LP., was conducting flight WSG129 from Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON to Kasabonika (CYAQ), ON with only the pilot on board. Shortly after lift-off, there was a loud bang and a loss of thrust, accompanied by severe vibration. The pilot lowered the nose to maintain airspeed and conducted a forced landing, bringing the aircraft to a stop approximately 20 feet from the end of the runway. The pilot was not injured and the aircraft was not damaged; however, a propeller blade was noted to be at an odd angle. Preliminary inspection of the propeller indicated that one blade was free to rotate, uncontrolled, within the hub. Examination by the TSB revealed that the blade actuating pin of the No. 2 propeller blade had failed due to a fatigue fracture. Both the propeller owner and the operator filed service difficulty reports (SDRs) with Transport Canada (SDR No. 202001105014 and No. 20201202006, respectively). The TSB issued Safety Information Letter A20C0103-D1-L1 to stakeholders.

C-GSKF, a Cessna 172P aircraft operated by the Springbank Air Training College, was being used for a private pilot flight test originating from and returning to Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB with one pilot examiner and one student pilot on board. As part the flight test profile, an inspection pass exercise was being conducted on Runway 28 at Olds-Didsbury Airport (CEA3), AB. After the inspection pass, the student pilot performed a go around and at that time the engine (AVCO Lycoming O-320-DJ2) lost power. Control was passed from the student to the pilot examiner (PIC).The PIC elected to conduct an immediate left turn to join the downwind for landing on Runway 28. While maneuvering to land on Runway 28, the left wing tip contacted the snow covered grass area north of and adjacent to the threshold of the runway. Shortly after, the nose contacted the ground resulting in the collapse of the nose landing gear, and damage to the propeller. The aircraft continued to slide on a track of approximately 310°M until it contacted a ditch that runs parallel to and north of the runway. The aircraft came to rest facing in a near north direction. The aircraft was substantially damaged but no injuries were reported.Post-accident inspection by maintenance found little fuel remaining in the aircraft’s fuel system.

N806NW, an Airbus A330-323 aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL30 from Hartsfield/Jackson Atlanta (KATL), GA to London/Heathrow (EGLL), England. When in cruise flight at about 233 nm east-southeast of St. John’s (CYYT), NL, the flight crew smelled a wood smoke odour in the cockpit. The flight crew contacted cabin crewmembers, who confirmed smelling the odour in the cabin as well. The flight crew subsequently declared an emergency, began descending and completed the quick reference handbook (QRH) procedure for smoke and fumes; however, the odour did not dissipate. Following a discussion with company maintenance personnel, the flight crew decided to divert to CYYT where the flight landed without further incident. Maintenance personnel inspected the cabin, cargo, and avionics compartments and reported no finding of smoke or haze. No faults were recorded by aircraft systems. On 22 October 2020, multiple flights across eastern Canada reported the detection of smell related to smoke carried aloft at high altitude in Canadian airspace, which originated from ongoing wildfires in Colorado.

Bearskin flight BLS384, a Fairchild SA227CC (C-GYTL) aircraft, was on route from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Sudbury (CYSB), ON and approximately 40 NM N of Sault Ste. Marie (CYAM), ON when the crew noticed smoke in the flight deck. The flight crew carried out the checklist, declared a PAN PAN and diverted to CYAM. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and found that a center pedestal back lighting circuit panel had failed.

C-FGZI, an McDonnell Douglas A4N aircraft operated by Top Aces Inc., was conducting a local flight from Wittmund/Wittmundhafen (ETNT), Germany. During the initial climb, the generator failed. A reset was attempted and failed 30 seconds after. The emergency generator was deployed and an emergency declared.  The aircraft landed at ETNT without further incident.

C-GSPW, un appareil de type Boeing 737-275C exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE 752 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Val D'or, QC (CYVO) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 56 passagers à bord. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait à 50 NM au nord de CYUL, en croisière à une altitude de  22 000 pieds, une agent de bord s'est blessée et et n'a pas été en mesure de poursuivre ses activités. L’équipage a demandé un retour vers Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC où l’appareil s’est posé sans problème.

C-GJZJ, a Bombardier CRJ-200 operated by Voyageur Airways Corp. on behalf of United Nations, was conducting flight UNO-788 from Khartoum (HSSS), Sudan to El Fasher (HSFS), Sudan. During initial climb at about 8000 feet, 5 birds (African Black kites) were seen passing by the cockpit and then a ''bang'' noise and vibration followed.  EICAS ( engine-indicating and crew-alerting system) showing Right Hand engine fire, Flight Crew actioned SOP checklist, activated two fire extinguisher bottle and RH fire annunciation light extinguished.  Flight crew declared a MAYDAY and returned to HSSS on a visual approach for an uneventful landing.

C-FABA, a de Havilland DHC-8-102 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways LP., was conducting flight WSG815 from Big Trout Lake (CYTL), ON to Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON. When the flight was approximately 66 nm north of CYPL, the flight crew noticed that the master caution light illuminated momentarily. The flight crew observed that the number 2 engine oil pressure was fluctuating between 40 and 50 psi. The flight crew referenced the QRH and placed the engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW120A) controls in flight idle and start feather. Although the oil pressure remained above 40 psi the flight crew elected to conduct a precautionary engine shut down. The company was notified of the emergency via the satellite tracking system and a MAYDAY was declared with Thunder Bay Radio. The flight continued to CYPL where a successful landing was carried out with one engine inoperative. The operator's maintenance personnel replaced the oil cooler due to leakage and submitted an SDR.

F-GSQH, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air France, was conducting flight AFR347 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Paris/Charles de Gaulle, France (LFPG). Approximately 300 nm northeast of Goose Bay Intl, NL (CYYR), the crew declared an emergency due to a cargo fire indication. The crew followed the QRH and discharged the cargo fire bottles. AFR347 diverted to Goose Bay Airport, NL (CYYR) and landed without further incident, with ARFF standing by. Upon inspection, maintenance determined that it was a faulty indication.

C-GZGL, a privately registerd Piper PA-31T Cheyenne, was conducting a local flight from Regina International Airport (CYQR), SK. After takeoff another pilot reported that the left main landing gear was not retracted. The pilot flew to the west of CYQR to conduct troubleshooting. Regina tower inquired if an emergency was being declared. The pilot responded negative and asked the tower for a low-and-over for a landing gear inspection. After the fly past the tower reported that the landing gear appeared down. The pilot requested a full stop landing on the next approach. While on base leg the tower again inquired if an emergency was being declared to which the pilot responded negative. On short final the pilot declared an emergency and the subsequent landing was without further incident. Maintenance personnel replaced the hydraulic power pack due to internal leakage and conducted successful landing gear swings.

C-FWAF, a Pilatus PC-12/45 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways LP, was conducting flight WSG5514 from Big Trout Lake (CYTL), ON to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON. While en-route the flight crew noticed a fuel quantity imbalance with the right side indicating high. The flight crew selected the right hand fuel boost pump on and, after monitoring, noted that there was no improvement to the imbalance. The checklist was reviewed and the flight crew noted that there was no CAWS (Central Advisory and Warning System) light for the right boost pump. The flight crew checked the lamps and continued to monitor the imbalance. The flight crew consulted with maintenance. When the left quantity indication dropped by another LED bar, the flight crew declared PAN PAN, and elected to divert to Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON. The passengers were briefed and the subsequent landing was uneventful.The operator's maintenance personnel replaced the right hand fuel boost pump and submitted an SDR.

C-GKKS, a privately registered Piper PA-28R-201T was conducting a flight from Edmonton/Cooking Lake (CEZ3) AB to Fort Frances Municipal airport (CYAG) ON. When approximately 20 NM from CYXE, the pilot experienced a full panel electrical failure that resulted in no communications. The pilot selected 7600 on the transponder and made contact with CYXE tower with an onboard cellphone. During the final approach to Runway 27 at CYXE, the pilot selected gear down but did not hear the landing gear extend. The pilot decided to conduct a tower fly past inspection for a gear verification check. CYXE tower indicated there was no gear extension. The pilot completed the emergency gear extension checklist procedure that included aggressive left and right yaw movement in an attempt to lock the main landing gear down. A second tower fly past inspection indicated there was no gear extension. The pilot conducted a gear up landing with ARFF on standby. There were no injuries to the pilot or the passenger but the aircraft sustained substantial damage.During the recovery process the aircraft landing gear extended and locked when the aircraft was raised.

CF-WMJ, a privately registered Cessna 180J aircraft, was landing on a private grass strip at Balsam Lake, ON. The pilot first approached the strip from the south and found the winds were favoring a landing in southerly direction. The pilot setup to land on runway 15 and during final approach found there was a gusty tail and crosswind when landing. The aircraft touched down approximately halfway down the 1900 foot wet grass strip and was unable to stop at the end of the runway. The aircraft went off the end of the runway at a very low speed and the right wing stuck a small pine tree which bent the wing and wing strut. The pilot and 2 passengers exited the aircraft without injury.

C-GNQZ a Pilatus PC-12/47E operated by North Star Air, was conduting IFR flight BF711 from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON. While climbing through 7000 feet after departure in visual meteorological conditions, the aircraft experienced a Modular Avionics Unit (MAU) Channel A failure. Numerous avionics systems failed, including DPU 1, DPU 2, Auto Flight Control System, and Transponder #1. All ADHRS data was lost including airspeed tape and altitude. The MAU circuit breaker was observed to have tripped. QRH items were carried out; however, the QRH did not contain instructions for a tripped MAU circuit breaker. The pilot elected to cancel the IFR clearance and return to CYQT in VMC conditions where an uneventful landing was conducted.The operator's maintenance subsequently reset the MAU circuit breaker and no additional faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FTES, a private Cessna 337G, was conducting a mission flight for the Civil Air Search and Rescue Association (CASARA) from ST. Catharines/Niagara district (CYSN), ON with 2 crew members and 2 spotters onboard. The aircraft was on the return leg after the first track crawl when four large birds dove at the aircraft from above. One bird struck the left wing leading edge at approximately 2 feet outboard the wing root. The pilot declared emergency and continued his return leg to CYSN escorted by the Military Search and Rescue Aircraft C-130 Hercules as precaution. The aircraft landed safely without further incident. There was no injuries to the crew and passengers. The left wing leading edge sustained substantial damages.

C-FEYP, un Beech A100 exploité par Propair, effectuait le vol PRO4230 medevac depuis l’aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) vers La Grande Rivière, Qc (CYGL) avec 4 membres d'équipage à bord. En vol de croisière au niveau de vol 210 à environ 30 miles marins (nm) à l’ouest-nord-ouest de l’aéroport de Matagami, Qc (CYNM), l'appareil a subi une dépressurisation complète. L'équipage a notifié l’ATC qu’il amorçait une descente d’urgence en raison d’un problème de pressurisation. Une fois en palier à 8000 pieds ASL, l’équipage a annulé l’urgence et le vol a été complété jusqu’à CYGL. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GEEN, a WestJet Encore de Havilland DHC-8-402, was operating as flight WEN3171 from Calgary, AB (CYYC) to Comox, BC (CYQQ). While enroute to CYQQ, the flight crew observed the pitch trim, elevator feel, roll spoiler outboard ground, spoiler outboard, #2 rudder hydraulic and rudder control caution lights illuminate and empty hydraulic fluid indications on the PFCS panel. The flight crew consulted with company dispatch and maintenance. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and conducted an air turnback to CYYC. A missed approach was conducted due to an unsafe landing gear indication. The aircraft landed uneventfully on the second approach and taxied to the gate. Company maintenance replaced the Flight Control Electronic Control Unit (FCECU) and system tested serviceable.

C-GEQK, un Odyssée de construction amateur en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue dans la région de la Rivière Savane, QC (environ 180 NM au nord de Bagotville, QC (CYBG)), avec un passager et un pilote à bord. Alors que l’appareil effectuait un amerrissage sur la rivière Savane, lors du contact avec l’eau, l’appareil a été poussé vers le rivage par le courant et a terminé sa course dans les arbres. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé et l’appareil a subi des dommages importants.

C-FIBX, a Cessna 152 operated by Pacific Professional Flight Centre, was conducting circuits at Vancouver / Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC with one student pilot on board. In the flare, the aircraft began drifting to the right edge of the runway and the pilot elected to overshoot. After the application of full power, the left wing struck the runway and the aircraft pitched nose down. The propeller struck the asphalt right of the right edge line and separated from the engine. The nose gear collapsed and the aircraft came to a rest. The pilot shut down the aircraft and evacuated.The aircraft was towed from the runway. Subsequent inspection revealed that the aircraft had sustained substantial damage to the propellor, engine, nose gear, wing tips, and the interior floor.

C-FSTL, a Zenair CH-701 advanced ultralight aircraft was on a return flight from Goderich (CYDG), ON to Lubitz Flying Field (CLB2), ON, with only the pilot onboard. During landing on runway 07/25 (1980 feet turf runway), the aircraft did a ground loop at approximatly 50 mph after touchdown. It was reported that the front wheel locked up causing the aircraft to veer left and nose over on the right side. The aircraft sustained substantial damages to the right wing, rudder, landing gear and propeller. There was no injuries.

C-GPPS, un Jetstream 3212 exploité par Pascan Aviation sous l'indicatif PSC837, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) à destination de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC), avec 12 passagers et 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de l’Approche visuelle piste 10 à CYBC, l'équipage a observé l’indicateur vert du train d’atterrissage avant verrouillé ne s’allumait pas. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification associée et changé les lumières de l’indicateur, mais le problème est demeuré. La roue de nez a été observée sortie par du personnel au sol à CYBC. L’équipage a décidé de se dérouter vers Sept-Îles (CYZV), QC et une urgence a été déclarée. En route vers CYZV, l’indicateur vert du train avant verrouillé s’est allumé. L’urgence a été annulée et l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre à CYZV. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage. Le microcontact a été ajusté et aucune autre défectuosité n'a été trouvé.

C-GRYM, an amateur built Christavia Mark-1 was preparing to land on a private strip (Runway 02), located about 1 Nautical Mile South East of Millson Field, Port Hope (CMF4), ON. The tailwheel touched the ground at about 25-30 mph then the aircraft veered sharply to the left. The pilot could not control the left veer and struck a gravel embankment; he was not injured.  The aircraft sustained substantial damage; the right main landing gear folded in, the left main landing gear buckled out and the propeller struck the ground. The pilot found the tailwheel in full reverse position after the impact. A preliminary inspection from the pilot and an aircraft maintenance engineer revealed that one of the tailwheel control arms shown signs of wear.

N403KZ, a Boeing 747-400 operated by Kalitta Air, was conducting flight CKS815 from Anchorage/Ted Stevens Intl (PANC), USA to New York/John F. Kennedy Intl (KJFK), USA. When approximately 75 nm west of Thompson, MB (CYTH), the crew observed a decreasing oil quantity indication on the number 4 engine. Shortly afterward the oil pressure dropped out of limits, and the crew consulted the QRH and conducted a precautionary engine shutdown (General Electric USA CF6 series). The flight continued to its destination.

C-GEWM, un Diamond DA-20, exploité par l’école d’aviation Évolution Inc., effectuait un vol local d’entrainement depuis l’aéroport d’Ottawa/Gatineau, QC (CYND) selon les règles de vol à vue avec un élève-pilote à son bord. Lors d’un exercice de simulation d’atterrissage court, l’appareil a rebondi à plusieurs reprises et au troisième touché des roues, le train d’atterrissage avant a cédé et l’hélice a frappé la piste. L’appareil s’est immobilisé en bordure de piste dans le gazon. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé, toutefois l’appareil a subi des dommages principalement à l’hélice, le capot moteur et le train avant.

C-FSSU, a privately registered Robinson R44 II helicopter was returning to a privately owned runway/helipad after a local flight with a pilot and three passengers. During the downwind approach the pilot flew along the runway in a northbound direction, and visually checked the wind sock and observed the wind was from the south. The pilot rotated the aircraft to face the headwind and directional control was lost;the helicopter began to rotate uncontrolably. The pilot decided to lower the collective and the helicopter dropped from 20 feet in height. The helicopter landed hard and came to rest on its right side. All four occupants evacuated the aircraft with no injuries and there was no fire. The 406 ELT was activated and all of the occupants had been wearing harnesses. The helicopter was substantially damaged.

C-GCNK, a Boeing 737-300 operated by Canadian North Inc, was conducting flight MPE1729 from Fort Mackay / Horizon (CYNR), AB to Edmonton International (CYEG), AB with 5 crew and 25 passengers on board. After departure from Runway 35, while the aircraft was climbing through 3000 feet ASL and accelerating to 250 knots, the aircraft experienced a vibration in the No.1 engine (CFM International CFM56-3C1). The left engine's thrust was reduced to idle and an emergency was declared. The flight diverted to Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB.  ARFF was on standby for the landing and the flight landed safety without further incident.Following the flight, maintenance inspected the aircraft and found that several fan blades were damaged. The damage was consistent with hitting a large bird.

C-GMSO, an Air Tractor AT-802 operated by Wilderness North Air, was landing on Runway 09 at Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON. with only the pilot on board. During the landing roll, the aircraft veered off the right side of the runway and struck a runway light with the tailwheel. The pilot then regained control of the aircraft and taxied to the ramp. There were no injuries and the aircraft was not damaged.It was reported that the wind at the time was from 360 degrees at 10Kts gusting to 17Kts.

C-FSNB, a Wetaskiwin Air Services (dba Absolute Aviation) Cessna 172L, was being rented for a local pleasure flight from the Wetaskiwin (CEX3), AB airport with one pilot on board. During the initial climb after take-off, the aircraft collided with a Canada Goose at approximately 600 feet AGL. The pilot experienced some control difficulties and returned to land. Significant damage was noted on the leading edge of the right wing, outboard of the wing strut. The aircraft has been removed from service for repair.

C-GPCL, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Beech 1900D operating as flight PCO615, was conducting a flight from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International (CYXC), BC, with 2 pilots and 9 passengers on board. During approach to CYXC, the nose landing gear indicated it was not down and locked. The landing gear was cycled with no change and the pilots opted for a go around as per Standard Operating Procedure (SOP). The pilots notified CYXC tower of the landing gear issue and performed the manual extension checklist twice with no change to the nose wheel indication. The pilots requested ARFF to be on standby and, during the turn into the final approach, the nose gear indication changed to down and locked without any pilot input. The aircraft landed safely with no damage to the aircraft and no injuries.During initial inspection, the nose landing gear down lock switch was cleaned, lubed, and tested satisfactory. The aircraft was returned to service and the defect returned after 4 additional flights. Maintenance replaced the nose landing gear down lock switch which resolved the defect.

C-FAFG, an Air Tindi Ltd. Cessna 208B, was operating as flight TI223 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Ft. Simpson (CYFS), NT with 1 pilot and 3 passengers on board. While in cruise the pilot observed a standby power warning and elected to return to CYZF. While in the vicinity of Rae-Edzo (CRE2), NT the pilot observed fluctuating oil pressure with a 'low oil' warning. The pilot declared an emergency and diverted into CRE2 where the aircraft arrived without further issue. Company maintenance will report their findings to the TSB.Company maintenance found that the accessory gear box (AGB) oil scavenge pump output drive had sheared resulting in a loss of oil and the loss of standby power (belt driven alternator from the AGB). In addition, play was noted on the alternator pulley adapter bearing. A corresponding Pratt and Whitney Canada SB1811 (compliance level 5) addresses the issue of oil loss should the output drive shear. It requires the addition of a plug to prevent the oil loss. Maintenance will be issuing an SDR to Transport Canada. The engine (PRATT & WHITNEY-CAN, PT6A-114A) has been removed for overhaul.

C-GSKB, a Kenn Borek Air Ltd. Beech 1900D, was operating as flight KBA901 from Inuvik (CYEV), NT to Sachs Harbour (CYSY), NT with 2 flight crew and 19 passengers on board. On departure from CYEV, through 3000 feet ASL, the left side airspeed indicator began to under read followed by the failure of the left hand flight director. Moments later the right hand flight director failed along with the yaw damper. Additionally, the left hand altimeter was under reading several hundred feet. After verifying that the right side flight instruments were accurate, the captain transferred control to the first officer, an emergency was declared with ATS and the aircraft returned to land at CYEV. At the time of landing the weather was 300 feet AGL overcast and a visibility of 8 SM in light freezing drizzle.

C-FBMB, a float-equipped amateur-built Bushmaster, was conducting a local flight from a private pond approximately 5 NM southeast of Campbell River (CYBL), BC with only the pilot on board. After takeoff, the aircraft contacted trees at the end of the pond and slid down a ditch, coming to rest on the nose of the aircraft. The pilot sustained minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The 406 ELT did not transmit a signal.

C-FGKJ, a Boeing 757-200 aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd., was conducting flight CJT 1891 from John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON to  Jose Marti Int'l Airport (MUHA), Havana, Cuba with 3 crew members and 2 passengers onboard. Approximately 8 minutes after departure from CYHM, the flight crew advised ATC of a Flap issue (Flap Asymmetry message) requiring return to CYHM with a 45 minutes hold to burn fuel. The flight crew declared Pan Pan and landed safely; the aircraft was towed back to the gate due to high brake temperature, emergency vehicles were standing by.Company maintenance found that the flaps were locked out on arrival at approximately 1 degree. The left inboard flap outboard trailing edge was extended slightly more than the inboard edge. After troubleshooting, maintenance found a discrepancy with the flap drive torque tube on the left wing. The torque tube bearing assembly between the inboard and outboard flaps had failed. The bearing assembly has been replaced.

C-FZXS, an amateur-built Harmon Rocket II, was conducting a low level flight approximately 24 NM W of Edmonton (CYEG), AB with a pilot and one passenger on board. The aircraft struck a power line and then collided with terrain. Both occupants received fatal injuries and there was a post-impact fire.

C-FYRQ, un Cessna C550 en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Trois-Rivières, QC (CYRQ), à destination de St-Catherines/Niagara District, ON (CYSN). C-FYRQ avait reçu et relu correctement l’autorisation de monter à 6000 pieds. L’ATC a constaté que C-FYRQ a poursuivi sa montée jusqu’à 7000 pieds et celui-ci a été réautorisé à 6000 pieds. Après avoir relu correctement la nouvelle autorisation, C-FYRQ est descendu à 5000 pieds. Il y a eu une perte de séparation avec C-GTSQ, un Cirrus SR20 qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX) à destination de Charlevoix/La Malbaie, QC (CYML). L'espacement a été réduit à 3.1 milles marins horizontalement et 500 pieds verticalement alors que l'espacement minimal requis est de 5 milles marins horizontalement et 1000 pieds verticalement.

C-GFOIF, an Airbus 321 Neo operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC546 from Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) to Bordeaux-Mérignac, France (LFBD)  with 7 crew members and 47 passengers on board. Shortly after take-off, one of the cabin crew members became ill and was unable to continue duties. Positions were reassigned among the other cabin crew members for the remainder of the flight.

C-GPSK, a British Aerospace Jetstream 32 aircraft operated by Pascan Aviation, was conducting flight PSC473 from Quebec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC to Iles-de-la-Madeleine (CYGR), QC. After selecting the landing gear down during the approach to CYGR, 2 landing gear transit light remained illuminated with no associated down position indication. An emergency was declared and the crew coordinated with the CYGR flight service station personnel to visually confirm landing gear position as the aircraft was flown along runway in a low pass. The down position indication subsequently illuminated for all 3 lights and the aircraft returned for another approach to CYGR. When the flaps were selected for landing no flap movement was detected and the crew noticed that the hydraulic fluid level was low. The aircraft landed at CYGR without further incident. Airport emergency response services were standing by for the landing as a precaution.  Maintenance replaced a broken hydraulic line, serviced and tested the hydraulic system; and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FIJW, un aéronef de construction amateur Seawind 3000 s’apprêtait à décoller d’une piste privée pour effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol à vue dans les environs de La Sarre (CSR8), QC. Lors de la course au décollage, l’aéronef a roulé sur une section boueuse de la piste qui l‘a fait dévier de sa trajectoire et l’a conduit dans un fossé. L’aéronef a subi des dommages substantiels. Le pilote seul à bord n’a pas été blessé. La radiobalise de repérage d’urgence ne s’est pas déclenchée.

C GJXV, an Airbus A220-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting IFR flight ACA610 from Toronto/Pearson (CYYZ), ON to Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ).  C-FNTJ, a Diamond DA 20-C1 aircraft operated by Moncton Flight College, was conducting a VFR training flight from Moncton/Roméo Leblanc (CYQM), NB and was operating about 10 nm south of CYHZ control zone. Air traffic control observed C-FNTJ, but was unable to make contact with the aircraft. The controller discussed the position of C-FNTJ with the crew of ACA610, who were approaching the ODKAS waypoint south east of CYHZ and did not have visual contact with the VFR traffic. The crew of ACA610 then reported receiving and correcting their flight path in response to a TCAS resolution advisory. The crew of ACA610 requested a visual approach to CYHZ and landed without further incident. The pilot of C-FNTJ was able to contact CYHZ on the tower frequency, and it could not be determined why contact could not be made on CYHZ terminal frequency as required. C-FNTJ continued on the training flight and landed at CYQM without further incident. The separation between the aircraft was 400 feet vertically and 0.5 nm laterally, where a minimum of 500 feet vertical and 1 nm lateral separation is required.
