NAV CANADA is carrying out an investigation.

C-FVEG, a de Havilland DHC-6-300 operated by TransWest Air Ltd., was conducting a flight from Seabee Mine (CCB2), SK. to La Ronge/Barber Field (CYVC), SK. with 2 crew. The aircraft touchdown was normal on Runway 18 at CYVC but when the nosewheel touched down, the aircraft veered left and departed the runway coming to a stop approximately 50 feet in the grass. The aircraft subsequently taxied to the apron and shutdown. There was no damage to the aircraft or injuries to the crew.The operator's maintenance conducted an inspection of the aircraft and the nose wheel steering system. It was reported that the nosewheel deflection markings inside the flight deck indicated a locked and centered nosewheel position when it was not. Adjustments were made to the nosewheel deflection markings and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FKMA, a Piper PA-31 aircraft operated by Aries Aviation Services Corporation, was conducting an IFR positioning flight from Springbank Airport (CYBW), AB to Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB with one pilot onboard. The pilot was cleared the RNAV GNSS RWY 26 approach at CYMM and the 20:00Z METAR reported winds calm, visibility 9SM, clear, altimeter setting 29.81. At approximately 5NM from the threshold, the pilot transitioned to a visual approach and the aircraft landed on Taxiway Juliette. A diagnostic check of the aircraft’s instruments was conducted by company maintenance with no faults found.

CF-UPF, a privately registered Cessna 150F, was conducting a flight from Lloydminster (CYLL), AB to a private aerodrome located 4.5 NM NNW of Edam (CJU7) SK with only the pilot on board. During the first landing attempt, the aircraft bounced twice and the pilot elected to go around. On the subsequent landing attempt, the aircraft bounced and control of the aircraft was lost. The nose gear assembly collasped and the aircraft came to rest inverted. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The pilot did not receive any injuries. JRCC did receive a 406 ELT signal from the aircraft. The local fire and EMS did not attend.

C-GSAF, a Sunwest Aviation Fairchild SA227-DC was operating as flight CNK214 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB with two flight crew on board. Shortly after departing Runway 17R, the crew noted an excess amount of heat in the cockpit from the vents and then the left hand wing overheat steady annunciator was observed. The flight crew actioned the QRH, declared an emergency, and returned to CYYC. Emergency services were requested and the aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance determined that the environmental system left hand mixing valve was modulating/hunting in the open (hot) position during auto mode operation. The cabin temp controller P/N: HYLZ50434-1 was replaced, a flight test was conducted, and the aircraft was returned to service.

N776AG, a privately operated Gulfstream G280 aircraft was conducting a flight from Shannon Intl (EINN), Ireland to Burlington Intl (KBTV), Vermont. At about 45°49' N, 052°52' W the number 2 engine (Honeywell HTF7250G) automatically shut down without warning. The crew declared an emergency, reviewed weather, and coordinated with ATC for a diversion to Gander Intl (CYQX), NL. The crew completed the engine fail checklists and decided not to attempt a restart of the engine. The APU was started below FL350 to facilitate electrical, environmental, and bleed air sources, and the flight landed at CYQX without further incident.Subsequent troubleshooting determined that false number 2 engine N2 overspeed logic caused the automatic shutdown of the engine. Gulfstream and Honeywell are collaborating on an investigation into the engine shutdown. The engine control units are with Honeywell for further evaluation.

C-FEHB a private Piper Navajo PA 31-310 aircraft was on a VFR flight plan from Hopedale, Newfoundland and Labrador (CYHO) to Springdale Newfoundland and Labrador (CCD2). When the aircraft was 35 NM NNW of Springdale the #2 engine began to lose power while in cruise flight. The pilot completed an in-flight shutdown of the engine and continued toward CYHO. The aircraft had progressed another 10 NM toward destination when the #1 engine began to lose power and the aircraft could not maintain altitude. The pilot maneuvered the aircraft toward Route 412 and conducted a forced approach to the highway. At approximately 1620 NDT the aircraft landed successfully 26 NM NNW of CCD2 without injury to the occupants or damage to the aircraft. The aircraft was relocated to a gravel pit off to the side of the Route 412. An Aircraft Maintenance Engineer inspected the aircraft and found that all fuel tanks were empty. Fuel was added and both engines were run-up for approximately 20 minutes without issue. The aircraft was flown back to CCD2 without further incident.

C-GQGE, a privately registered Piper PA-28 aircraft, was on a local training flight from Smithers Airport (CYYD), BC. During the demonstration of a forced approach, at approximately 600 feet AGL, the instructor observed the aircraft was unable to out climb the rising terrain during the overshoot. Without other options, she flew the aircraft into the trees keeping the wings level. Both occupants received minor injuries and called 911 from a cell phone. There was no fire and the ELT was manually activated. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FDLJ, un Cessna 172N exploité par Grondin Transports Inc., effectuait un vol d’entrainement local depuis l'aéroport de St-Frédéric, QC (CSZ4) avec un élève-pilote seul à bord. Lors d’un exercice d’entrainement d’une simulation d’atterrissage de précaution, l’élève pilote a sélectionné un champ et a ensuite configuré l’avion pour une inspection à 500 pieds AGL. Les volets auraient été baissés à 20 degrés et la puissance a été réduite pour atteindre une vitesse d’environ 70 nœuds (kts). Après l’inspection, l’avion est remonté à environ 1000 pieds AGL et les volets auraient été remontés à 10 degrés. Vers la fin de l’étape du vent arrière gauche, l’élève-pilote a constaté une vitesse verticale de -1000 pieds par minutes (pi/min) sur l’indicateur de vitesse verticale (VSI) et la technique de recouvrement de décrochage a été appliquée en poussant sur le nez. L'appareil a été mis en palier et le VSI a été observé à -1000 pi/min à nouveau. La manœuvre de recouvrement de décrochage a été refaite, mais la situation est restée la même. La manœuvre a été répétée quelques fois et l’avion s’est retrouvé très bas. L’élève-pilote a vu 2 champs devant lui avec une lisière d’arbres les séparant. L’avion a été tourné à droite et ensuite à gauche afin de tenter de réduire la vitesse et permettre un atterrissage après la lisière d’arbres. L’avion a percuté la lisière d’arbres dans un virage vers la gauche. Environ 1,5 mètre de l’aile gauche s’est arraché en raison de l’impact et a causé une accentuation de la rotation de l’avion. La portion de l’aile gauche qui était toujours rattachée à l’avion a touché le sol sur une longueur d’environ 18 mètres. L’avion s’est ensuite retrouvé sur le dos, l’hélice a frappé le sol suivi du moteur. L’avion a rebondi pour ensuite retoucher le sol toujours sur le dos et a glissé sur environ 53 mètres et s’est immobilisé à environ 137 mètres de la lisière d’arbres. Il n’y a pas eu d’incendie. Le pilote a subi des blessures sérieuses. Il s’est détaché et a évacué l’appareil. Des résidents près de l’endroit sont venus à son secours et le pilote a été transporté à l’hôpital.

C-FGZE, a Top Aces Inc. Mcdonnell Douglas A-4N was completing his tactical training mission with German air force from Wittmund (ETNT), Germany when pilot noticed a strong noise and vibration from air conditioning system.  The pilot shut down the air conditioning system which stopped all noise and vibration. An emergency was declared with ATC and emergency descent was initiated.  The aircraft was then diverted to Neuburg (ETSN), Germany.  Fuel was burnt down to desired landing weight and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FPMH, a Waterloo Wellington Flight Centre, Piper PA44, was conducting a dual instructional flight for multi-engine training at the Kitchener/Waterloo Airport (CYKF) with 2 flight crew members and no passengers on board. While in the practice area southwest of CYKF, the right throttle control became stuck at cruise power setting. The pilot in command contacted the company maintenance department and being unable to move the control, contacted CYKF tower, declared an emergency, and set up for landing on runway 26. The right engine was shut down and feathered when the aircraft was approximatly 4 miles back on the extended runway centerline. The aircraft landed without incident and cleared the runway without assistance.Maintenance found the right engine throttle stuck at the engine side. Maintenance personnel freed the cable and lubricated it, returning it to normal function. The throttle control cable was replaced in February 2019 and had about 500 hours in service. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) has been submitted.

C-FCJZ, a CRJ 900 was operated by Jazz Aviation LP, flight JZA 7925 from Thunder Bay International Airport, (CYQT), ON to Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport, (CYYZ), ON. When the flight crew selected the flaps from 30 to 45 degrees on final approach to runway 05 a "Flaps Fail" caution message illuminated and the flaps remained at 30 degrees indicated position. A go around was initiated, the flaps were retracted to 0 degrees without incident and the caution message extinguished. ATC was advised and the flight crew prepared for an abnormal landing. Passengers, dispatch and maintenance were also notified. The flight crew elected to land as per the emergency checklist with flaps selected at 1 (slats at 20 degrees), the captain upgraded the status to a Pan Pan with ATC. ATC redirected the aircraft to land on runway 23 due to shifting winds. Emergency equipment was on standby and the aircraft landed without incident on runway 23; emergency vehicles followed the aircraft to the gate. An inspection of the flaps and slats was conducted with no faults found. There was no faults logged in the Maintenance Diagnostic Computer (MDC). The slat/flap control lever has been replaced and the system was tested serviceable.

C-GJZD, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada DHC-8-400, operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA 8375 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB with 4 crew members and 62 passengers on board. During the initial descent into CYMM, the flight crew heard what sounded like an engine surge, and shortly after received a #1 PEC caution light. The #1 propeller RPM had increased from approximately 850 to 1060 RPM.  The pilot flying called for the "prop overspeed drill #1" which was completed. As the prop was feathered during the drill, the crew shut down the #1 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW150A). A PAN-PAN call was made to ATS, cabin crew and passengers were briefed, and an uneventful single-engine approach and landing was completed at the intended destination. Company maintenance subsequently replaced the propeller electronic control unit (PEC), the propeller control unit (PCU) and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GMGA, un Beech 1900D (BE02) exploité par Sky Jet M. G. inc. sous l'indicatif VSL629 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB), à destination de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC). C-GJBV, un Beech 100 (BE10) exploité par Sky Jet M. G. inc. sous l'indicatif VSL512 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV), à destination de CYQB. VSL629 avait reçu et relu correctement l’autorisation de monter à 11 000 pied. L’ATC a constaté que VSL629 dépassait 11 300 pieds en montée et a immédiatement communiqué avec l’équipage afin d’arrêter la montée. VSL629 a atteint 11 500 pieds avant de redescendre à 11 000 pieds. L'espacement minimal requis de 3 milles marins horizontalement ou 1000 pieds verticalement n'a pu être maintenu avec VSL512 qui était en palier à 12 000 pieds. L'espacement a été réduit à 2.8 milles marins horizontalement et 500 pieds verticalement. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FNMF, un appareil de construction amateur Foster 001 (Seabee modifié) en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Saint-Hyacinthe QC (CSU3), à destination du lac Massawippi, QC avec 1 pilote à bord. Le pilote a amorcé sa descente finale au-dessus du lac Magog, QC, pour ensuite se poser face au vent en direction sud-est dans la portion nord du lac Massawippi. Lors de l’amerrissage, au moment où l’appareil touchait l’eau, le pilote a entendu un bruit fort et l’appareil s’est renversé. Le pilote a tout de suite évacué l’appareil et a été secouru par des riverains. Il a subi des blessures mineures. L’appareil a subi des dommages substantiels, et il a coulé dans la minute après le renversement et se trouverait dans 96 pieds d’eau. Aucun signal de radiobalise d’urgence (ELT) n’a été entendu.

C-GCJT, a CargotJet Boeing 757, was en route from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky Intl (KCVG), OH to Calgary (CYYC), AB.  Shortly after take-off upon acceleration to clean speed, uncommanded yaw occured continuously and intensified.  The flight crew completed a flight control controllability check and confirmed the aircraft was unsafe to fly over 230-240kts.   The flight crew declared an emergency, elected to return to KCVG and landed without incident.

C-FLZA, a Cessna C550 aircraft operated by Transport Canada (Aircraft Services Directorate), was conducting IFR flight TGO859 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON to Moncton/Roméo LeBlanc Intl. (CYQM), NB. The crew selected the landing gear down for the approach at CYQM and the nose landing gear light did not illuminate. The crew declared a PAN PAN, requested a hold to troubleshoot the landing gear issue, then referenced and completed the quick reference checklist items related to the landing gear indication. The nose landing gear indication did not change initially, but did illuminate later in the hold. After burning off additional fuel the crew returned to land on Runway 24 without further incident. Airport emergency rescue services remained on standby as a precaution. Maintenance personnel towed the aircraft off the runway. The nose landing gear actuator was subsequently replaced, a landing gear operational test was carried out, and a test flight was conducted before returning the aircraft to service.

C-FAHG, a Bell 212 operated by Alpine Helicopters was conducting operations in support of forest fire fighting in the vicinity of Ghost River, Alberta. The pilot was repositioning the helicopter to a location previously utilized. During the approach for landing, the pilot noticed a tree top that appeared to have been recently broken off. An uneventful landing and shut down was completed. Upon further inspection of the helicopter, the pilot noticed that the main rotor blades had sustained damage consistent with a tree strike. The aircraft was subsequently inspected by maintenance personnel, and ferried to a maintenance location for repair. There were no injuries.

C-GLTO, a Top Aces Inc. Dassault-Dornier Alpha jet was conducting a fighter training mission with German Air Force from Wittmundhafen (ETNT), Germany.  During take off from ETNT, the landing gear handle was brought up but landing gear remained down and gear doors operated normally. The pilot declared an emergency and burned fuel for landing.  Upon achieving the desired landing weight, the aircraft landed without further incident.  Maintenance is troubleshooting the issue.

C-GMUQ, un Cessna 172P exploité par Laurentide aviation, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue au départ et à destination l'aérodrome de Montréal/Les Cèdres, QC (CSS3), avec un pilote à son bord. Lors d’un posé-décollé sur la piste 25, le pilote simulait un atterrissage sur terrain mou et lors du roulage au sol, le pilote a senti l’avion s’enfoncer sur la gauche suivie d’un virage non commandé vers la gauche. Il a alors coupé la puissance motrice, appuyé sur les freins et a appliqué du palonnier côté droit pour tenter de reprendre le contrôle. L’aéronef n’a pas ralenti et a fait une sortie de piste près du seuil de la piste 07. Lors de la sortie de piste, le train d’atterrissage droit et le gouvernail de profondeur ont heurté une lumière causant des dommages à l'aéronef. Le pilote n'a pas été blessé. Une crevaison du pneu gauche a ensuite été constatée. Une inspection de piste a été effectuée et un grattoir à peinture a été retrouvé sur la piste.

On 14 July 2019, a privately registered Schempp-Hirth VENTUS BT (C-FMVA) moto glider, was soaring near Montebello, Quebec with a single pilot on board. At approximately 12:20 (EDT) the glider lost lift conditions and started to descend. The pilot deployed the electric motor and it ran for a short period of time, before it quit. The pilot crossed the Ottawa River in an attempt to gain lift, but was unable to maintain altitude. The pilot carried out a forced approach to farm field 2 NM W of Lefaivre, Ontario. The glider landed hard collapsing main gear which caused substantial damage to the glider. The pilot was not injured.

C-GEWF, a privately registered AURIGA S 90 amateur built aircraft, was taking off from a private grass strip near Orillia, ON. At approximately 15:30 the pilot was having difficulty controlling the aircraft during the take off roll due to uncommanded pull to the right. The pilot aborted the take off late and was unable to stop the aircraft before the end of the runway. The aircraft struck the fence causing substantial damage to the aircraft. The pilot who, was the sole occupant, was wearing a 4 point seat restraint and was not injured.

C-FOAI, un Dash-8-300 (DH8C) exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE851 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Kuujjuaq QC (CYVP) à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 3 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage des variations de couple du moteur gauche (Pratt and Whitney, Canada, PW123B) et du régime de l'hélice sont survenues. Le moteur ne répondait pas aux commandes normales et l'équipage a décidé de l’arrêter. Par la suite, l’équipage déclaré un état d’urgence et est revenue se poser à CYVP sans encombre. Il ni a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FOAI, un Dash-8-300 (DH8C) exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE822 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Kangirsuk, QC (CYAS) à destination de Quaqtaq, QC (CYHA) avec 24 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage des variations de couple du moteur gauche (Pratt and Whitney, Canada, PW123B) et du régime de l'hélice sont survenues. Le moteur ne répondait pas aux commandes normales et l'équipage a décidé de l’arrêter. Par la suite, l’équipage déclaré un état d’urgence et a effectué une diversion à Kuujjuaq QC (CYVP). L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre, il n'y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-IDSD, un Quad City Challenger II (équipé de flotteurs) en exploitation privée, effectuait des posés-décollés sur la piste 03 de l’aéroport St-André-Avellin, QC (CAA2) avec seul un pilote à bord. Lors de la montée après le décollage, le moteur (Rotax 582) s’est arrêté. Le pilote a effectué un atterrissage d’urgence dans un champ juste au nord de la piste. Lors de la course au sol après l’atterrissage, les flotteurs et le fuselage ont subi des dommages. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FUIM, un Cessna U206A (équipé de flotteurs) en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue du Lac Sébastien, QC (CTD3) à destination de la Rivière-des-Prairies, QC avec un pilote et 2 passagers à bord. Alors que l’avion était sur le redan pendant le décollage en direction ouest, un ponton qui se trouvait à la gauche de sa trajectoire a tourné juste devant lui. Le pilote a effectué une manœuvre d’évitement et a arrêté le décollage, toutefois l’appareil a frappé la rive d’une ile et a terminé sa course dans un marais. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil a subi des dommages importants.

C-FJDZ, an Air Partners Corp. Cessna 750, was operating as flight SDE755 (CAR604) from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Red Deer (CYQF), AB with 2 flight crew and no passengers on board. During landing gear extension on approach into CYQF, the flight crew received a hydraulic system caution light. They conducted a missed approach, completed the appropriate checklists and decided to return to CYYC. ARFF was put on standby for the arrival into CYYC and the aircraft landed uneventfully on Runway 17L. The aircraft stopped on the runway using emergency braking and the aircraft was towed clear.Maintenance found that a main landing gear hydraulic line had burst which in turn depleted the hydraulic fluid. The line was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FXOZ, a privately registered amateur built Piel Emeraude was conducting circuits at Stanley Aerodrome (CCW4), Nova Scotia. At approximately 1020 ADT the aircraft lifted off RWY 27 after a touch-and-go and began to climb. When the aircraft reached approximately 50 feet above ground level the engine began to vary in RPM and lost power. The aircraft made an immediate turn to the right toward RWY 02 which intersects RWY 27. During the turn, the aircraft lost altitude and the right wingtip made contact with the ground. The aircraft cartwheeled and came to rest in an upright position. The pilot, who was the sole occupant onboard, was wearing a seatbelt and shoulder harness and sustained non-life threatening injuries. Emergency Health Services Nova Scotia LifeFlight attended the scene and transported the pilot to hospital in Halifax.Impact forces destroyed the aircraft; there was no fire.

A Piper PA-28R-201 (C-FFTU) aircraft, operated by the Waterloo Wellington Flight Club was conducting a cross country flight from Kitchener Waterloo (CYKF) to Peterborough (CYPQ) with a single student pilot on board. At 12:45 EDT the aircraft landed on Runway 27 with landing gear in the retracted position. The aircraft slide to a stop on it's belly and the pilot was not injured.

C-FKXV, a privately operated Cessna 172, was on a cross country VFR flight from Qualicum Beach (CAT4), BC; Sechelt (CAP3), BC; Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC; Princeton (YDC), BC; Oliver (CAU3), BC; with an ultimate destination of Castlegar (CYCG), BC. Shortly after departure from CAT4 the pilot elected not to fly into Sechelt due to poor visibilities and low ceilings, and continued on to Pitt Meadows where the ceilings were about 1 500 feet AGL, and from there toward Hope, BC where the ceilings lowered to about 1 000 feet AGL. When 6.5 NM SE of Hope, BC the aircraft collided with trees. JRCC received a signal from the aircraft’s 406 MHz ELT and the pilot also triggered an SOS signal on the SPOT network and RCMP were dispatched to the accident site. The pilot received minor injuries and walked from the accident site to Highway 3 where the RCMP found her. The aircraft sustained substantial damage; there was no post-impact fire.

C-GGHS, an Air Tractor 502B operated by Helico Services Inc., was conducting spray operations approximately 36 nm north west of Moose Jaw Municipal airport (CJS4) SK. Prior to the start of application, the pilot conducted an inspection of the field to identify power line locations. The pilot made multiple passes above an identified power line; however, during the occurrence application pass, the aircraft hooked and broke the single power line with the right hand main gear. The aircraft sustained minor damage to the right hand wing, including two boom hangers and the right aileron. The aircraft returned to CJS4 and is undergoing maintenance. The power company was notified of the downed wire.

C-FFTZ, an amateur-built Bushmaster, was conducting a local flight from a private grass runway approximately 7 NM northwest of Shuswap Regional Airport (CZAM), BC with only the pilot on board. During the landing roll, the main landing gear contacted rough ground, the aircraft nosed down, and the aircraft overturned. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GEHS, a Beechcraft 200 King Air operated by PAL Aerospace Limited was conducting flight SPR810 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ) NS to Sydney/J.A. Douglas McCurdy (CYQY), NS.  During the climb, the crew noted that the #2 engine indications (fuel flow and torque) became erratic and flame pulses exited the engine exhaust. Engine #2 was intentionally shutdown and the crew declared an emergency. The crew elected to return to Halifax where the aircraft landed without further incident while airport rescue and firefighting trucks stood by. There was no impact to airport or ATC operations. Maintenance completed a borescope inspection of the engine, which did not reveal an internal failure within the compressor or turbine sections. The engine has been removed from service due to the possibility of an inter-turbine temperature (ITT) exceedance during the event. The fuel control unit (FCU), a Honeywell P/N 3244755-22 is suspected to have failed internally and was incapable of metering fuel flow accurately. The operator will send the FCU for teardown, inspection and analysis.

C-FSAO, a Beech 200 operated by Keewatin Air LP as flight Blizzard 214, was enroute from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Lac Brochet (CZWH), MB with a crew of 2 and 2 passengers onboard. While on approach into CZWH, the crew extended the landing gear and the aircraft experienced the loss of the following equipment: Nav 2, Com 2, AFCS, AHRS 2, Landing gear control/position indicators, PFD 2 radar altimeter, cabin temperature controller, pressurization controller, windshield wipers, right hand engine instruments and right-hand engine ice vanes. After conducting a missed approach, the aircraft entered a holding pattern to assess the issues. The crew decided to return to CYTH where an emergency was declared and the aircraft then landed safely.  An inspection of the aircraft by the operators maintenance personnel revealed an incomplete assembly and diode failure of the #2 dual fed bus. The system was repaired and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GHCS, a Sunwest Aviation Ltd. Beech 1900D, was operating as flight CNK055 from Ft. St. John (CYXJ), BC to Calgary (CYYC), AB with 2 flight crew on board. Prior to departing CYXJ, CNK055 was fueled. CNK055 arrived uneventfully into CYYC. After the flight concluded, the aircraft went into scheduled maintenance. When the aircraft was defueled it was noted that the fuel was foul smelling and contained unknown particulates. A second Sunwest Aviation Ltd. aircraft (C-FBOM) that had also fueled in CYXJ was checked and it too had fuel contamination. Fuel filters at the vendor met EI 1581 and 1583 specifications. Fuel samples from both aircraft and from the fueling trucks in CYXJ were tested in two independent tests.  In both laboratory tests, the fuel met the CGSB 3.23 (2019) JETA-1 chemical standard. For the visual inspection test (ATSM-D4176), one lab passed the sample the other failed the sample. Enough of the particulate was recovered for a particulate test and those results determined that the material consisted of oxygen and carbon.  The fuel vendor is working with the refinery to determine the origin of the particulate. There have been no reported engine issues related to fuel dispensed from CYXJ. See also A20P0086 - fuel contamination in Terrace, BC.

C-GHZI, a Air Spray (1967) Ltd Lockheed 188, was conducting aerial firefighting operations 20 NM North East of Chico Airport (KCIC), CA.  The aircraft inadvertently entered smoke in short final and dropped retardant load.  Exiting the smoke, flight crew observed trees tops near left wing level.  The aircraft performed a second bomb run without incident.  Evidence of tree strikes was discovered during maintenance port flight inspection.  Aircraft was ferried back to company's maintenance base for repair.

C-FENY, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3106 from Terrace (CYXT), BC to Vancouver Int'l Airport  (CYVR), BC with 4 flight crew and 59 passengers on board. Prior to departing CYXT, WEN3106 was fueled. WEN3106 arrived uneventfully into CYVR. After the flight concluded, the operator was informed that the fuel from CYXT was contaminated. The aircraft was taken offline for a maintenance inspection. Two other WestJet Encore aircraft (C-GPWE and C-GWFE) had also fueled in CYXT with contaminated fuel.Fuel filters at the vendor met EI 1581 and 1583 specifications. Fuel samples from the fueling trucks in CYXJ were tested in two independent tests.  In both laboratory tests, the fuel met the CGSB 3.23 (2019) JETA-1 chemical standard. For the visual inspection test (ATSM-D4176), one lab passed the sample the other failed the sample. Enough of the particulate was recovered for a particulate test and those results determined that the material consisted of oxygen and carbon.  The fuel vendor is working with the refinery to determine the origin of the particulate. See also A20W0086 - fuel contamination in Ft. St. John, BC.

C-FPQE, a Robinson R44 helicopter was approaching to land on a helipad on the shore of Lady Evelyn Lake, located approximately 20 NM SE of New Liskeard (CPX3), Ontario. As the helicopter was touching down on the helipad it bounced and then drifted laterally. A main rotor blade contacted a tree and the helicopter rolled over onto its side. The two occupants were not injured; the helicopter was destroyed.

C-GWUE, WestJet Encore flight WEN3456, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft, departed Toronto LBPIA (CYYZ), ON for Moncton (CYQM), NB. While on route the flight crew received a flap power caution light and elected to return to CYYZ. The flight crew declared an emergency as a precaution. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and could find no faults with the system. Maintenance suspects the that L7 Flap Control circuit breaker may have been inadvertantly pulled by a headphone cord. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FMIR, a Piper PA-30 Twin Comanche operated by Millennium Aviation, was returning to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK from a local training flight. Prior to landing the pilots observed the main gear landing indicator light flicker. On final approach to landing, the main gear indicator light indicated that the landing gear was down and locked, the nose gear was confirmed visually down and locked, and there were no further abnormal indications or warnings. Upon touchdown on Runway 27 at CYXE, the left wing of the aircraft dropped and the aircraft skidded to a stop. The pilots exited the aircraft and observed that the left landing gear was not extended. Emergency crews responded. There were no injuries, but a NOTAM was issued to close Runway 27 for approximately 1.5 hours until the aircraft could be removed. A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed a damaged landing gear teleflex cable.

C-FINV, a privately registered Beech Bonanza M35, was conducting a VFR flight from Penticton (CYYF), BC to Porcupine Plain (CKD2), SK. While on approach to CKD2, the pilot had difficulty sighting the airstrip, which resulted in a high and unstable approach. The aircraft touched down short of the runway and pitched over. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to its propeller and forward fuselage.

Canadian Flyers International College's C-GWYC, a Cessna 172M with an instructor and student onboard departed Toronto Buttonville Municipal Airport (CYKZ) Runway 33 on a flight to practice circuits. The student did the preflight walk around; an engine run-up and associated checks were carried out prior to departure with the instructor. During the take-off, the student pilot had control, and the aircraft accelerated normally on Runway 33. As the aircraft lifted off and began to climb, the engine started to lose power. The instructor took immediate control of the aircraft, and ensured full power was being applied, but the engine continued to lose power. The instructor kept the aircraft pointed straight ahead and carried out a forced approach to a short field, located just past 16th avenue and adjacent to the northbound lanes on Highway 404. The right main landing gear and wing tip struck the top of a hill, and spun the aircraft around. Both pilots exited the aircraft with minor injuries. The TSB deployed two investigators to the scene of the accident.

The pilot of C-FEMA, a Kitfox IV amateur built aircraft, departed from Picton, ON (CNT7), on a local flight to do some sight seeing and practice some circuits. After approximately 15 minutes of flying the pilot brought the aircraft in for landing. The aircraft bounced on touch down, the pilot attempted to correct and the aircraft started to deviate and head toward the runway edge. The pilot then applied full power in an attempt to overshoot and lost control of the aircraft. The aircraft went off the runway and the landing gear caught a rut in the field, causing the nose to hit the ground and the main landing gear to collapse.

C-FYHA, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B2 aircraft operated by Yellowhead Helicopters, departed a remote area located 13 NM northeast of Stewart (CZST), BC to conduct external load operations with only the pilot on board. Shortly after liftoff, the load of steel pipe that was being slung with nylon straps on a 50 foot external line using a Crosby-style hook, released due to an inadvertent opening of the keeper. There were no injuries.When the load was picked up, it was observed one strap had flipped over the end of the hook and came to rest on the safety keeper, forcing a side load on the keeper rather than resting in the hook throat. This resulted in one strap releasing from the hook. After the incident, the Crosby-style hook was removed from service and replaced with a Sure-lock style hook.

C-GCCF, a privately registered Cessna 421B, was conducting a flight from Vernon (CYVK), BC to Ponoka Industrial (Labrie Field) Airport (CEH3), AB with 2 pilots on board. At approximately 38 NM northeast of CYVK, during the climb to cruise altitude, the right engine (Continental GTSIO-520-H) failed. The engine was feathered, an emergency was declared to ATC, and the aircraft diverted to Kelowna (CYLW), BC without further incident.

C-GWSR, a Boeing 737-800, operated by WestJet as flight WJA662, was enroute from Calgary Intl, (CYYC), AB to Toronto/Lester B Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON with a crew of 6 and 121 passengers on board. While in cruise, a cabin crew member became ill and could no longer perform duties. The aircraft was then diverted to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB where it arrived safely was met by emergency services. The cabin crew member was then transported to a local hospital.

C-GTPU, a Northwestern Air Lease Cessna U206G, was operating on a VFR charter from Fort Smith (CYSM), NT to Taltson River (CFW5), NT with 1 pilot and 3 passengers on board. Attempts to land at CFW5 were unsuccessful due to gusty winds and so the flight returned to CYSM. During the landing in CYSM on Runway 12, the aircraft bounced twice and departed the side of the runway where it came to rest with a flat nose tire. The pilot and passengers egressed from the aircraft and returned to the terminal on foot. There were no injuries to the pilot or passengers.

C-GSLJ, a Skyline Helicopters Augusta A-119, was operating in support of fire fighting operations in the vicinity of High Level (CYOJ), AB with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. While en route, the helicopter collided with several birds. The pilot's bubble side window shattered during the collision. The pilot performed a precautionary landing in a cut block to assess the damage. It was determined that there was no other damage other than the bubble window and the helicopter departed for an uneventful flight to CYOJ.Maintenance replaced the bubble window and returned the helicopter to service.

C-GJPY, a Summit Air Aerospatiale ATR-72-202, was operating as SU7142 from Diavik (CDK2), NT to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with 3 crew and no passengers on board. During the descent in to CYZF, the flight crew observed fluctuating engine parameters on the No. 1 ( left hand) engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW124B). The flight crew performed a precautionary engine shutdown, declared an emergency and performed an uneventful single-engine approach and landing with ARFF standing by. Company maintenance is investigation the cause of the fluctuating parameters.

C-GJQB a Cessna 172M, registered to Canadian Flyers International and being operated by a student pilot (sole occupant) was conducting circuits at the Toronto Buttonville Municipal Airport (CYKZ), ON. After the aircraft touched down for landing on runway 33 it veered to the left. The pilot applied full power in an attempt to get airborne. However, the aircraft subsequently veered to the right, exited the runway surface near taxiway BRAVO 1 (B1) and transitioned across a grass infield area, a taxiway, and then collided with a hangar located on the apron. The aircraft was destroyed and the hangar sustained substantial damage. The student pilot was taken to the hospital for assessment, but received only minor injuries.

C-GRCT, a Bell 206B helicopter operated by Clayton Air Service, was applying herbicide to a wheat field 12 nautical miles NW of Porcupine Plain, SK. with only the pilot on board. After clearing a row of trees, the helicopter began a slight descent. While rounding out to continue the application pass, the spray boom made contact with the crop and the pilot lost directional control of the helicopter. The helicopter veered to the right and then collided with the terrain. The operator's ground loader responded to the accident site and brought the pilot to hospital for assessment. The pilot sustained minor injuries and the helicopter was destroyed by a post impact fire.

C-FCVD, un Pilatus PC-12/45 exploité par Chrono Aviation, effectuait le vol NDL543 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC) à destination de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 3 passagers à bord. De la foudre à été observée 5 NM à l'est de la piste. Immédiatement après le décollage de la piste 28, les voyants  ESNTL BUS et AV BUS se sont allumés; l'équipage a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour “ESNTL BUS”.  Alors que l'appareil se trouvait à une altitude de 2000 pieds en montée, une panne des instruments du côté gauche s'est produite, suite à laquelle l'équipage a été en mesure de récupérer partiellement le système électrique. L'équipage a complété la liste de vérification du QRH pour “AV BUS” suivi de celle pour un emballement du compensateur (runaway trim). L'équipage a déclaré une urgence (Pan Pan) et, en raison des conditions météorologiques à CYBC, a effectué un déroutement vers l'aéroport de Mont-Joli, QC (CYYY) et une descente a été effectuée afin de maintenir des conditions de vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR). L'équipage a dû déployer le train d'atterrissage manuellement et l'aéronef a atterri sans encombres à CYYY à 18h13Z. Après que l'aéronef fut garé, l'équipage a constaté une odeur de plastique brûlé dans la partie non-pressurizé de l'appareil.Le personnel d'entretien a subséquemment trouvé 3 coupe-circuits déclenchés, 2 régulateurs de tension désajustés et le moteur du groupe turbo-refroidisseur brûlé. Le radar météo et les compensateur d'ailerons et de gouvernail de profondeur indiquaient hors service.

C-GNZF, un Eurocopter AS350B2 exploité par Canadian Helicopters Ltd, effectuait un vol avec charge externe entre 2 lignes de transport d'électricité dans la région de Sacré-Coeur, QC lorsque le rotor pricipal est entré en contact avec et sectionné un câble électrique. Le pilote a ressenti des vibrations et a immédiatement déposé et relâché la charge externe au sol. L'appareil a été positionné à l'écart de la charge ou il s'est posé sans encombres. Le rotor principal a été endommagé et il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

N764CK, a Boeing 767-300 cargo aircraft operated by Kalitta Air, was conducting flight CKS1917 from Seattle-Tacoma Int'l (KSEA), WA to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC with 2 crew members on board. While on final approach to Runway 08R the flight crew received an EICAS caution message of 'Trailing Edge Flap Disagree' when the flaps were selected to the 30 position. The flight crew performed the missed approach, declared an emergency, and completed the appropriate checklists. A second approach was attempted and the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator's maintenance subsequently observed an issue with the right hand wheel well flap drive unit when the flaps transitioned between the 20 and 30 position. The drive unit was serviced and aircraft returned to service.

C-GSAC, a privately operated Cessna 172E, was conducting a local pleasure flight at Silver Valley, AB with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. During the landing roll, the pilot was unable to affect positive steering and the aircraft departed the side of the runway. The aircraft collided with a culvert in a ditch and the aircraft sustained substantial damage. The pilot and 2 passengers egressed without difficulty; there were no injuries.Maintenance follow up did not detect any problems or failures with the nose wheel assembly.

C-IMOM, a Quad-City Challenger II advanced ultralight, equipped with amphibious floats was climbing out after departure from Carleton Place (CNR6), ON., when the engine lost power (Rotax 582). The aircraft forced landed in a hay field and was unable to stop before striking a line of trees. The pilot was not injured and the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FLHA, a float-equipped Cessna 208B aircraft operated by Tantalus Air, was conducting a flight from Vancouver Harbour (CYHC), BC to Tofino Harbour (CAB4), BC with 1 pilot and 9 passengers on board. Upon landing in a westerly direction, a 20 foot water taxi vessel operated by Tofino Water Taxi, passed in very close proximity in front of the aircraft in a general southerly direction requiring the aircraft to use full reverse thrust to avoid a collision. Neither the pilot nor the vessel operator were aware of the other until in the immediate proximity of one another.

C-GHHA, a Harbour Air float equipped de Havilland DHC-6 aircraft, was conducting flight HR243 from Vancouver Harbour (CYHC), BC to Victoria Harbour (CYWH) with 2 crew members and 8 passengers on board. Shortly after departure the flight crew became aware of a burning smell and a squealing noise. The flight declared an emergency and returned to CYHC where the aircraft landed and taxied to the dock without further incident. The operators maintenance determined that a hydraulic pump had failed to build enough pressure to automatically shutoff and was operating continuously, subsequently overheating. The operator has filed a service dificultly report, replaced the hydraulic pump, and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GPZV, a Cessna 172S aircraft was practicing precision 180 (power-off) maneuvers in preparation for a commercial flight test at the Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF), ON. During a forced approach followed by a touch and go, the aircraft's right horizontal stabilizer and elevator struck a Runway 26 threshold light, causing structural damage.

C-FAHC, an Aberdeen Helicopters AS350-B2, was conducting long lining operations 45 nm NNW of Stewart, BC with 1 pilot on board. During initial lift off from a drill site located on a mountain, the pilot decided to set the load back down due to incoming weather. After the load was disconnected the pilot departed for a staging area. When communications were not established with the pilot, a search was conducted. The helicopter was found approximately 1200 metres west of the drill pad on the mountain side. The helicopter was destroyed and was nearly consumed by the post impact fire. The pilot did not survive.

The FulcrumAir RPAS E7500 (pre-production model, serial number 1), SFOC 930020, was operating from the East Shepherd RPAS Site, Calgary, AB. The objective of the operation was to conduct testing of new remote pickup hardware that had been designed to allow the RPAS to pick up payloads at a remote location. Three successful payload tests were conducted. While conducting the fourth test, the RPAS successfully retrieved the payload and was returning to the departure location. As the pilot conducted a turn to initiate the approach to land, the RPAS began a rapid spin and descent. During the descent, as the payload contacted the ground, the pilot disengaged the main rotor interlock switches which cut power to the main rotors. This resulted in a decreased rate of yaw and stabilized the RPAS as it landed hard on the skid landing gear. Once on the ground, the pilot, force disarmed the RPAS and the RPAS shut down. There were no injuries, and no damage to property. The RPAS received significant damage to both the upper and lower main rotor blades and bent the main rotor drive shaft.

C-FGYL, an Airbus 320 operated by Air Canada on approach in Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (KFLL) FL, the flight crew received TCAS RA (Resolution advisory) "Climb". RA was executed and subsequently a go-around was initiated. Flight landed without further incident.

C-GNKP a privately owned Amateur Built Stits Skycoupe was on final approach to Port Elgin (CNL4), ON when the aircraft touched down in a gravel pit 0.4 NM east of airport, struck a stone ridge and flipped over. The aircraft was substantially damaged and the two occupants received minor injuries. It was reported that there was difficulties with the flight controls systems, as a result, a forced approach was conducted into a gravel pit.

C-GSAH, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by Saskatchewan Air Ambulance, was conducting flight SLG2 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK to Regina Intl (CYQR), SK. Shortly after takeoff there was a loud bang during the landing gear retraction cycle. The master caution light illuminated and the red light in the landing gear handle remained illuminated. The "Hyd Oil Low" annunciator illuminated and the landing gear circuit breaker tripped. The flight crew notified ATC and consulted the QRH. The flight crew conducted a manual landing gear extension and obtained three green, down-and-locked lights. The flight crew elected to return to CYXE and declared an emergency. The subsequent landing was uneventful and, after consultation with maintenance, the aircraft taxied to the apron. The operator's maintenance personnel discovered that the right main landing gear actuator body had ruptured. The operator filed a Service Difficulty Report.

C-GTRG, Chartright Air flight HRT024, a Gulfstream G200 was in cruise flight and approximately 45 minutes out of Toronto / LBPIA (CYYZ), ON when the crew noticed some electrical issues with the aircraft. They subsequently lost the ability to transmit followed by a full communication (COMMS) failure. The flight crew squawked 7600 and continued on their flight plan. COMMS then came back temporarily and the flight crew informed ATC of the issue. COMMs were then lost once again and the crew received flap and slat error messages. Given the various systems that were affected the flight crew opted to declare an emergency by squawking 7700. A flapless approach was carried out and the aircraft landed at CYYZ without further incident. There was no indication of fire and no control difficulties.Chartright Air maintenance found that the Flight Digital Acquisition Unit (FDAU) had malfunctioned, a new FDAU is being installed.

C-GAST, un Cessna 310R exploité par Grondin Transports Inc., effectuait un vol local depuis l'aéroport de St-Frédéric, QC (CSZ4), suite à des travaux de maintenance sur l'appareil avec deux membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de l'atterrissage sur la piste 23, la jambe de train droite s'est affaisée et l'appareil a dévié vers la droite suivie d'une sortie latérale de piste. L'appareil a terminé sa course sur le ventre, adjacent à une tranchée de drainage à une centaine de pied de la piste. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé et l'appareil a subi des dommages importants.

C-FBRG a MAG Aerospace Cessna 337G aircraft, was returning from a fire detection patrol, to Chapleau, ON (CYLD) and joined the circuit for Runway 23. The aircraft bounced on touch down and the landing gear didn't feel correct after the bounce. A second approach and touchdown was conducted on Runway 23 and again the aircraft bounced and the pilot conducted an overshoot. C-FBRG left the zone to troubleshoot the situation and confirmed that the gear was down and locked. C-FBRG returned and conducted a normal full stop landing on Runway 28.After shutdown, a MAG Aerospace AME noticed that the front propeller had been damaged. A thorough maintenance inspection of the landing gear system was completed which included multiple swings of the landing gear with no faults found. The front propeller was damaged and no other structural damage was found. The front propeller and engine was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FWAC, a de Havilland DHC-2 aircraft operated by Harbour Air, was being fueled at the dock at Vancouver International Seaplane Base (CAM9), BC. The pilot quickly realized that they were inadvertently using Jet A instead of Avgas fuel for the piston engine aircraft (Pratt & Whitney -USA R-985 Serial Number 22265). The amount of Jet A added to the fuel tank was estimated to be less than two litres.  The aircraft was removed from service. The defect was recorded and reported to the Aviation Maintenance Organization (AMO). The AMO drained the fuel from the affected tank and refilled that tank with Avgas. The fuel drains were subsequently sampled and no evidence of Jet A fuel was found.  The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FTJS, an Airbus A320-211 operated by Air Canada flight ACA0913 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL, USA to Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. Airport (CYUL), QC, on departure flight crew experienced TCAS RA to maintain a rate of climb. RA manoeuvre carried out and continued to CYUL without further incident.

C-GOJA, a CRJ 100 was operated by Jazz flight JZA8022 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport, (CYYZ), ON to Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ, USA when the crew reported flap fail at 14 degrees on approach to Newark, advised ATC they had a maintenance issue to work through and broke off the approach. No emergency or pan pan declared, ATC elected to send the trucks out. Flight crew advised flight attendant and passengers that it would be an abnormal landing. Flight landed without incident.

C-FCDK, an amphibious Lake LA-4-200 aircraft was conducting a flight from Langley (CYNJ), BC to Nanaimo (CYCD) BC. During the flight the pilot flew over their personal airstrip they keep on their property in order to assess the feasibility of landing there. On the second inspection pass, the aircraft began to lose altitude while on final approach and the pilot decided to land the aircraft rather than attempt a go around. The aircraft impacted a few feet before the landing surface on the rising terrain. The aircraft briefly became airborne again and then contacted the ground in a level attitude approximately 50 feet from the threshold. The aircraft slid to a stop on the left side of the airstrip. The pilot shut down the aircraft, directed witnesses to turn off the fuel, and had them turn off the ELT, which had activated. Local fire, police, and ambulance attended the scene with the pilot being taken to the local hospital with serious but not life threatening injuries.

C-GQIF, a privately registered wheel-equipped Bellanca 8GCBC Scout aircraft, was conducting a flight from Minaki (CJA6) ON, to Estevan (CYEN) SK with the pilot and 1 passenger on-board.  Approximately 1/2 hour from CYEN the engine (AVCO LYCOMING, O-360-C2E) lost all power. The pilot conducted a forced landing onto a field. The occupants were uninjured and the aircraft sustained damage to its left wing and right side landing gear. The aircraft had just been purchased by the pilot. Prior to departure, the fuel quantity onboard had been calculated to be enough for 5 hours of flight while the flight planning indicated a 4 to 4.5 hour flight to the destination. It was reported that the fuel tanks were empty during a post-incident aircraft examination.

The privately registered Luscombe 8A, C-GKIB, was on a flight from Rocky Mountain House (CYRM), AB to Red Deer Forestry (CFR7), AB. On the landing roll out the aircraft struck a hole causing a veer to the right. The brakes were applied aggressively to correct the veer resulting in the aircraft nosing over onto its back. There were no injuries, the ELT did not activate, but the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FCJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 operated by Jazz Aviation as flight JZA7944, was enroute from Regina Intl (CYQR), SK to Toronto Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with a crew of 2 and 35 passengers onboard. During the climb out of CYQR at approximately 22000 feet ASL, the crew received a left anti-ice duct warning message. The crew decided to level off the aircraft at 24000 feet ASL to stay clear of cloud and then declared a PAN PAN due to icing. After remaining clear of clouds, the flight was able to resume to it's destination without further incident.

C-FUGX, a privately owned, float equipped Cessna A185E aircraft, with one soul on board, was on a VFR flight from Riviere de Milles Isles, approximately 12 SM North of Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (CYUL) to the Geraldton / Hutchison Lake Seaplane Base (CNE6), Ontario. Upon arrival at CNE6 the pilot was advised that no fuel was available and as result flew to Government Lake, located 5 nautical miles west of the Hornepayne Municipal Airport (CYHN). During the approach to Government Lake the engine failed (Continental IO-520) and the aircraft impacted trees approximately 200 feet prior to the shore line. The pilot was not injured but the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FATK, a privately registered American Aircraft AA-1, was conducting circuits at Prince George Airport (CYXS), BC with 1 instructor and 1 student on board. During one of the circuits a simulated engine failure was conducted with the plan to land on the runway and complete a full stop. On final, the instructor took control as he deemed the aircraft to be too high. During the attempted go around, power was not sufficient to prevent heavy contact with the runway surface. Directional control was lost and the aircraft departed the side of the runway and nosed over in the turf. The aircraft slid to a stop 10 feet from the edge of the runway. Both the instructor and student were able to egress from the aircraft and they both sustained minor injuries. There was no post-impact fire.

The amateur-built, Hatz CB-1, C-FHZB, was on approach at Springbank (CYBW), Alberta and landed hard on the left main landing gear after encountering a gust of wind.  The aircraft continued bouncing down the runway until the left main landing gear broke off. The aircraft departed the runway surface, coming to rest in the grass. The ELT did not activate and the pilot was not injured.

The Landcare Aviation Inc. Cessna 172S, N370JA, and Cessna 172P, N53134 were departing Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB on a flight to Rome (KRME), New York, USA. The two aircraft had filed instrument flight rules (IFR) flight plans and were both departing on the Fort Mac 2 Standard Instrument Departure (SID). N370JA departed first and climbed straight ahead as required expecting to climb to seven thousand feet as directed in the SID. At 2500 feet above sea level (ASL) the departure controller cleared N370JA for a right hand turn and released him from the SID before issuing a departure clearance for N53134. On departure N53134 did not follow the Fort Mac 2 SID departure by turning southbound early without authorization. Separation decreased to 3.6 nautical miles (NM) where 5 NM was required.

The Canadian Helicopters Bell 407, C-GAVF, was involved in a drill move on the Diavik mine site when the slung load was inadvertently dropped into the lake when the longline release button rather than the radio transmit button was depressed. No one was injured.

C-FSPN, a Beech 200 operated by Keewatin Air as flight KEW216, was enroute from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson INTL (CYWG), MB to Leaf Rapids (CYLR), MB with a crew of 2 and 4 passengers onboard. During the initial descent into CYLR, the elevator indicator light illuminated in the cockpit. While completing the appropriate checklist procedures, the crew found the electric elevator trim was unresponsive and the manual elevator trim wheel was locked in a nose up position. The crew decided to divert to Thompson (CYTH), MB and declared an emergency. Substantial force was required to maintain the descent profile and the aircraft then landed safely.

C-GTJZ, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by PAL Aerospace Ltd., was conducting patrol flight SPR04 from St. John's (CYYT), NL to Deer Lake airport (CYDF), NL. The aircraft descended to the mission altitude of 500 feet above sea level, and at about 75 nm south of Stephenville airport (CYJT), NL, the crew detected an electrical odour in the aircraft. The crew ceased the patrol and climbed to a safe altitude for troubleshooting.  The crew consulted the QRH, enlisted a cabin crewmember to investigate for signs of heat or smoke, and requested return to CYYT. Onboard mission equipment was unplugged and no source of the smell could be detected. The crew declared PAN PAN and shut off all non-essential electrical equipment. There was no change in the odour, and no sign of smoke or heat. The crew ventilated the cabin using ram-air and the flight landed at CYYT without further incident. Emergency services inspected the aircraft and no heat source could be detected. Maintenance personnel subsequently determined that a transistor on a fuel transfer system circuit board failed and overheated.

C-GCIY, a Bell BH429 aircraft operated by Transport Canada Aircraft Services Directorate, was on a supply delivery flight from Seal Cove (CBY5), BC to Green Island Lighthouse Station (CAQ2), BC. The aircraft was transporting a rectangular wooden box inside an external net at the end of a longline. On final for CAQ2, the long line release button was inadvertently engaged thereby releasing the slung load into the ocean. The load, primarily lumber and hand tools, fell approximately 500 feet into the water and was not retrieved. There were no injuries or damage. The aircraft belly hook was inspected by maintenance personnel and no defects were noted.

C-GNYI, a Bell 212 helicopter operated by Airspan Helicopters Ltd. was engaged in forest fire fighting operations at the end of Butte Inlet. C-GNYI departed the fire location for fuel in the Toba Inlet with a Bambi Bucket attached.  On short final to the fuel barge, the pilot unintentionally pressed the belly cargo release button and jettisoned the slung load (Bambi Bucket) short of the fuel barge.  The bucket landed in the water and could not be retrieved. The helicopter landed on the fuel barge without further event. There was no injury, damage to property or the environment, beyond the loss of the Bambi Bucket.

The private RAF 2000 GTX SE gyrocopter, C-GEDF, was departing on a local sight seeing flight from a farm strip 8 nm SW of Calmar, Alberta. The pilot had flown earlier in the day and successfully departed and returned. On the occurrence flight the ambient temperature had risen significantly and 4.5 gallons of fuel had been added to the aircraft. On take-off the pilot noted that the climb rate would not allow the aircraft to clear the power lines on the departure end of the runway. A hard right turn was initiated and the rotor system lost lift. The aircraft came down hard in a ditch at the end and to the right of the runway. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The pilot received minor injuries and was transported to hospital for observation. There was no fire and the ELT did not activate.

C-GKGA, a Beech 1900C operated by Skylink Express Inc. as flight SLQ720, was enroute from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson INTL (CYWG), MB to Regina INTL (CYQR), SK with a crew of 2 onboard. During descent into CYQR, the crew heard a thump followed by a split in engine RPM and a slight yaw movement of the aircraft. Efforts to correct the split in engine RPM revealed the right propeller lever was jammed. The crew noticed the right engine (PT6A-65B) cowling had dislodged and remained only partially in place. The crew declared a PAN PAN with CYWG center and continued on to CYQR. The aircraft landed safely and came to a stop on the runway where they were met by fire crew for inspection. The aircraft then taxied off the runway. An inspection of the aircraft confirmed the right upper engine cowl had dislodged and interfered with the propeller governor, jamming the propeller control arm.

C-FVOL, a privately registered Quest Kodiak 100 Amphibious aircraft was conducting a flight from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Unwin Lake (50° 07'N 124° 40'W), BC. On the downwind leg after take off, the oil temperature of the engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-34) began to rise rapidly and the high oil temperature light illuminated. The crew reduced power on the engine, declared an emergency, and returned to land. The aircraft landed safely and taxied in with ARFF following. Fire fighters checked the temperature of the engine and found it to be safe.A post flight inspection found that the red coloured oil cooler cover had not been removed prior to flight; it was  located in a red painted area of the aircraft. Maintenance inspected the oil both physically and with data provided by the Garmin G1000 and determined that it was not burnt. The oil was changed and the aircraft departed 2 hours later.

C-GXKS, a Piper PA-31 aircraft owned by Terraquest Ltd., departed the Santee Cooper Regional Airport (KMNI) USA, with 2 pilots on board. Each fuel selector was positioned to its respective inboard tank (main), providing 2.7 hours of endurance. After 2 hours 2 minutes, each fuel selector was positioned to the outboard tank. With approximately 3.5 hours total time since the departure, when the flight was about 5 miles south of Sumter Airport (KSMS) USA, there was sputtering from the left engine, which was annunciated on the manifold pressure gauge. The manifold pressure for the left engine went from 30 inches to 17 inches.  Each fuel selector was then switched back to the inboard tank position and the boost pumps were turned on, with the throttle, propellers and mixture controls moved forward. Both a climb and level flight were attempted unsuccessfully and the aircraft started to descend. While descending, the right engine started to sputter. An attempt was made to feather the left propeller when the manifold pressure was indicating 10 inches. The aircraft collided with an open field in a right wing low attitude, resulting in an explosion. The two occupants exited the aircraft sustaining minor injuries; the aircraft was destroyed. An FAA investigator on-scene noted that the fuel level in the left outboard fuel tank was full, and the fuel level in the left inboard fuel tank was ½ full. The NTSB investigated (ERA20LA270).

C-FZYZ, a privately operated Cessna 180, was conducting a VFR flight from a private grass airstrip at Blind Bay, BC to Nelson (CZNL), BC with 1 pilot and 1 passenger-pilot on board. During the landing on Runway 22, the aircraft encountered a strong cross wind from the North which resulted in the right wing rising. The pilot applied power to try and stabilize the aircraft and to avoid a ground loop; however, control of the aircraft was lost. The aircraft left the runway surface and went through the airport fence, across a road, and came to rest in a parking lot approximately 80 meters form the runway centerline. Both persons on board sustained minor injuries. There was no post-impact fire.

C-FSCT, a privately registered Piper J3L-65 on floats, was landing on Upper Island Lake, ON on glassy water. The aircraft bounced after touchdown, and on the subsequent contact with the water the right float dug into the water and the aircraft overturned. The two occupants were helped from the water by nearby boaters before being brought to the hospital. The aircraft remained inverted but floating, and was towed to shore and removed from the water the next day. The aircraft was substantially damaged and will not be returned to service.

C-GOJA, a Jazz Aviation LP CRJ-100 was conducting flight AC8491 from Ronald Reagan Washington National (KDCA), DC, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. During the initial approach at CYYZ, the flaps failed to extend and the flight crew received a FLAPS FAIL caution. The flight crew declared PAN PAN, discontinued their approach, and requested delaying vectors to enable them to conduct troubleshooting. The flight landed uneventfully on runway 24L at 1303 with ARFF standing by.

C-GTXE, a Learjet 35A operated by Top Aces Inc. as flight FURBAL01, was departing Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON with a crew of 2 onboard. During the take off roll on RWY 25, the left engine (Garrett TFE-731) ingested a bird. At approximately 120 kts airspeed, the crew aborted take off and the aircraft came to a stop at the 5200 feet point on the runway. AARF responded to inspect for hot brakes and then escorted the aircraft off the runway. An inspection of the left engine revealed deformation to several fan blades.

C-GGND, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8734 from Fredericton Intl airport (CYFC), NB to Îles-de-la-Madeleine airport (CYGR), QC. On approach to CYGR, the crew received a FLAP POWER caution indication and the flaps did not extend beyond 17 degrees. The crew declared PAN PAN with ATS and requested a diversion to Halifax/Stanfield, (CYHZ), NS. The aircraft landed at CYHZ without further incident.

C-IBTR, a Kasperwing Cascade Ultralite aircraft, experienced a loss of control during its initial climb at approximately 40 feet agl, approximately 8 nm northwest of Arlington Muni (KAWO) USA. The aircraft was in a left turn when it began to descend and then impacted terrain. The pilot received serious injuries, the aircraft was substantially damaged. The NTSB investigated (WPR20LA240).

C-GXMJ, a privately registered Aeromot AMT-200 motor glider with only the pilot on board was on final approach to runway 13/31 at the Regina International airport (CYQR), Sk. The aircraft landed with the landing gear retracted and came to a rest in an upright position on the center of the runway. The pilot was not injured and the aircraft sustained substantial damage. It was reported that the landing gear was not selected down prior to landing.

C-GHRN, a privately operated Van's RV6, was returning to the Arnprior/South Renfrew Municipal Airport (CNP3), Ontario, following a local flight. During the circuit for runway 28, at approximately 800 feet AGL, the engine failed. The pilot, realizing he would not be able to reach the runway, maneuvered to avoid a water landing and conducted a forced approach to a field adjacent to Highway 417, near County Road 29. The aircraft overturned during the landing roll. Emergency services attended the scene and helped the two occupants out of the aircraft, who were brought to hospital with minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FLLL, a De Havilland of Canada DHC-3T operated by Northwestern Air Lease was conducting flight PLR403 from Powder Lake, NWT to Fort Smith (CYSM), NWT with one crew member and 2 passengers on board. Upon departure from Lady Grey Lake, the pilot observed that both hydraulic pumps were running. The pilot attempted to extend the landing gear (amphibious floats) but the landing gear did not extend. The pilot then pulled the hydraulic pump circuit breakers. As the aircraft neared CYSM, the pilot attempted to manually extend the landing gear, but was only able to extend the main landing gear. The nose landing gear remained retracted. A flyby of the airport was performed to confirm the main landing gear was down, and recce the airport for an appropriate place to land the aircraft off of the runway. The pilot subsequently elected to land the aircraft in the grass on the approach end of RWY 21. A successful landing was completed, there were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft.Subsequent inspection by company maintenance found the right hand aft gear hydraulic line ruptured allowing the hydraulic reservoir quantity to deplete. The affected hose was replaced, gear swings completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GLHO, a Beechcraft 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Service (EVAS), was conducting a training flight at Gander Intl (CYQX), NL with 3 people onboard. While conducting a simulated single engine approach, and manipulating the power and propeller levers, the number 1 engine went into an uncommanded auto-feather. The crew could not unfeather the engine, and decided to shut down the engine as a precautionary measure. The crew declared an emergency and requested ARFF to be on standby. The aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance determined that with the autofeather system armed and either power lever brought back to idle, the low power setting engine would feather intermittently. The autofeather arming switch was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FKJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8011 from St. John's Intl (CYYT), NL to Toronto/Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. While in cruise flight the crew received an AUTO XFLOW INHIB message, followed by a XFLOW PUMP caution message and actioned the QRH to use gravity cross flow to correct a 300 pound left-right fuel imbalance. The crew continued to monitor the fuel quantity, and observed that the left side quantity was indicating as though it were decreasing in quantity relative to expected engine fuel burn. The crew discussed the issue with their maintenance control department, and at about 157 nm north-northeast of Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS they decided to divert to CYHZ. The aircraft landed at CYHZ without further incident.Maintenance personnel found a fuel quantity gauging computer fault, and a faulty left hand primary ejector crossfeed fuel line. The faults were corrected, their relative systems tested and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FCME, a Central Mountain Air Beech 1900D, was operating as flight GLC708, from Terrace (CYXT), BC to Prince George (CYXS), BC with 2 flight crew and 10 passengers on board. Shortly after extending the landing gear at top of descent for Runway 15 at CYXS, the flight crew received an indication of fire for the right engine. The flight crew completed the QRH checklist, actuated the fire extinguisher for that engine and declared an emergency with ATS. No sign of fire was noted but the annunciation remained. The flight landed with ARFF on standby. After landing the flight crew elected to stop on the runway and proceeded with a rapid deplanement of the passengers. The runway was closed for 36 minutes as the aircraft was towed to a company hangar.Maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft and engine; they determined that the fire loop detection system was defective which resulted in the erroneous fire warning indication.

C-GOFK, a privately operated Cessna 140, was conducting a VFR flight from the abandoned airstrip at Stave Lake, BC to Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC with 1 pilot and 1 passenger-pilot on board. During the takeoff roll, control of the aircraft was lost. The aircraft came to rest inverted and in the opposite direction of the attempted takeoff roll. The pilot sustained fatal injuries. The passenger-pilot sustained minor injuries. There was no post-impact fire. TSB investigators deployed to the site.

C-FGKP, an Air Canada Airbus 321-200, was operating as flight AC7080 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON  to Denver Intl. (KDEN), CO. During descent to KDEN, flight crew received a TCAS Resolution advisory (RA). The advisory was to level off and the crew complied.  Flight landed safely in KDEN.

C-GJFL, un appareil de construction amateur Ti-Beaver en explotation privée, effectuait un vol de plaisance selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le Troisième lac des Marais, QC  à destination du Lac Buteux, QC avec seul le pilote à bord. Lors de l'amérissage, le flotteur droit s'est posé sur l'eau en premier et l'appareil s'est retrouvé dans une assiette inclinée vers la droite. L'appareil a culbuté avant de s'enfoncer dans le lac. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé mais l'appareil a subi des dommages importants.

C-GNWN, un appareil de contruction amateur Wagaero Sportsman 2+2 (équipé de flotteurs), effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le Lac-des-îles, QC à destination réservoir Baskatong, QC avec seul le pilote à bord. À l'approche du Réservoir Baskatong l'aéronef a subi une perte de puissance moteur (Avco Lycoming O-360-C2E). Lors de l'amérissage, un flotteur a frappé un kayakiste qui se trouvait sur le réservoir Baskatong. Il n'y a eu aucun dommage à l'appareil, mais le kayakiste a été grièvement blessé. Un examen du moteur effectué peu après l'accident a révélé que la saillie de montage de la bougie du cylindre arrière droit était fracturée et que la bougie pendait au bout de son fil.

C-GRGO, a De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd DHC-8-100, operated by Canadian North was conducting flight MPE1797 from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 3 crew members and 11 passengers on board. During the cruise portion of the flight, the #1 ISO VLV (Left hand Isolation Valve) light illuminated. The flight crew confirmed a partial loss of the #1 system hydraulic quantity level, and referenced the appropriate QRH procedure.  Flight crew declared an emergency prior to landing and the aircraft completed an uneventful landing at the intended destination.

The pilot of C-IJQP, a Quad City Challenger II advanced ultra-light aircraft, had just conducted an approach to Picton (CNT7), ON and was heading back to Gananoque Airport (CNN8), ON when the engine (Rotax 503) lost all power. The pilot conducted a forced approach into a farm field approximately 4.5 NM N of Picton. The aircraft was not damaged during the forced approach. After some trouble shooting it was determined that the 2 ignition plug leads had come off the ignition plugs on one cylinder. The ignition leads were re-secured to the ignition plugs. After running the engine for approximately 8 minutes and checking the aircraft for any damage the pilot took off from the farm field to continue back to Gananoque. Shortly after takeoff at approximately 30-40 feet the engine lost power again and the aircraft stalled aerodynamically. The aircraft crashed in the field in a near vertical attitude. The pilot received minor injuries and the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FUCN, a Dornier DO-228 operated by Alkan Air was conducting a flight from Whitehorse (CYXY), Yukon to the Coffee Creek Airstrip, Yukon with 2 flight crew and 7 passengers on board. The touchdown zone of the Coffee Creek airstrip is marked by fuel drums placed along the edge of the runway. During the landing, the aircrafts right hand main landing gear wheel struck one of the touchdown zone marking fuel drums which subsequently struck the right side of the fuselage and right horizontal stabilizer. The remainder of the landing was uneventful. There were no injuries and the aircraft sustained minor damage.Subsequent to the occurrence, the fuel drums were replaced with high visibility plastic cones and the vegetation near the edge of the airstrip was cut to provide better visibility of the new touchdown zone markers.

C-GQNS, a Bell 206L helicopter operated by Expedition Helicopters Inc., was transitioning from one aerial application block to another near Medstead, SK when it struck a power line. The aircraft was equipped with a wire strike protection kit which cut the power line. The pilot subsequently landed in a nearby field. The helicopter sustained damage to its windscreen and main rotor blades. The helicopter has been removed from service pending repairs.

C-FOUA, un appareil de type Cessna 172R exploité par Collège iFly, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue au départ et à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) avec un posé-décollé à Victoriaville, QC (CSR3) avec un pilote à son bord. Lors de l'atterrissage sur la piste 06 à CSR3, le pilote a aperçu un animal sur la piste. Il a alors tourné vers la gauche afin de l'éviter et est sorti en bordure de piste. Il a ensuite tenté de revenir sur la piste, mais l’aéronef a passé dans un petit fossé où l’hélice a touché le sol et l'aéronef s’est immobilisé. Le pilote n'a pas été blessé.

C-GWSA, a Boeing 737-8CT aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA518 from Toronto/LBPIA, ON (CYYZ) to Deer Lake, NL (CYDF). The flight was cleared for the approach to runway 25 in CYDF, and the crew contacted CYDF FSS to report that they were unable to extend the flaps for the landing. The crew conducted a missed approach and were issued a hold. The crew completed checklist actions and contacted maintenance control regarding the flap condition. The crew determined they could not resolve the flaps issue, declared a PAN-PAN, briefed the lead flight attendant, and conducted a flapless landing without further incident.Maintenance personnel replaced the faulty flap SKEW sensor #4 connecter.

Air Canada Rouge flight ROU2384, a Boeing 767-300 (C-FIYA) aircraft, departed Toronto LBPIA (CYYZ) and was heading to Shannon, Ireland (EINN). Shortly after departure, during flap retraction, the flight crew received a Flap/Slat asymmetry warning. The flight crew actioned the QRH checklist, declared a PAN PAN and returned to CYYZ. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GGNW, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8862 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Gander Intl airport (CYQX), NL. Shortly after the departure from CYHZ, the No. 2 roll spoiler switch-light SPLR 2 PUSH OFF illuminated in-flight. The crew pushed the switch-light to select the system to off, followed QRH checklist instructions, and then discussed conditions with company maintenance control personnel. The crew then contacted ATC, requested return to CYHZ, and requested that airport emergency services stand by for the landing. The aircraft landed and taxied to the gate without further incident. Company maintenance carried out testing and inspection of the No. 2 spoiler system in accordance with fault isolation manual instructions and no faults were observed.

C-FVIY, a Piper PA-23-250 aircraft operated by the Excel Flight Training School, was conducting a training flight from Lethbridge Airport (CYQL), AB to Medicine Hat (CYXH), AB to Taber (CED5), AB returning to Lethbridge Airport (CYQL), AB. There was one instructor pilot and one student pilot onboard.
