On the missed approach in CYXH, the flight service specialist noted that the right main gear appeared extended, while the nose wheel and left main appeared retracted.The crew selected the gear up for the missed approach, and noted that the white all up light was not illuminated, indicating that the gear had not retracted fully. The gear lever was cycled; the white all up light illuminated briefly and then extinguished. A decision was made to return direct to CYQL, and the aircraft was flown at reduced speed below max landing gear extension (Vle). An emergency was declared with ATC, and the aircraft landed on Runway 23 without further incident.Maintenance determined that the hydraulic fluid reservoir was low, the landing gear system was serviced, a gear swing was conducted, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GDUK, a Bell 204B aircraft operated by Delta Helicopters, was conducting external load operations at N55°46.96' W114°17.29' near Wabasca, AB with only the pilot on board. During slinging of trees with a longline carousel, the net load load unintentionally released from the remote hook. There were no injuries. Post incident inspection of the cargo hook found that the hook keeper and hook number two were found to be in the open position. Maintenance repair actions were completed on cargo hook number 2.

The pilot of C-FYFY, a Cessna 172P aircraft departed Brampton (CNC3) ON, with one passenger, also a pilot onboard. The 2 pilots were going to fly locally and practice some inflight emergencies. The aircraft flew to Burbank Field (CNN3) near Shelburne, ON and conducted a simulated forced approach to Runway 08, but did not land. The aircraft came around again for a second approach and attempted to land on Runway 08. The aircraft floated approximately 1600 feet down the 2000 foot runway before touching down. The pilot realizing the aircraft could not be stopped in the remaining 400 feet applied full power and attempted to take off. It was reported that the aircraft speed was low during take-off, and near the aerodynamic stall speed as the pilot attempted to clear trees approximately 375 feet from the end of Runway 08. When the aircraft was just above the tree tops it stalled aerodynamically and crashed in the forest. Both pilots exited the aircraft with no injuries. There was significant damage to the aircraft.

C-FULE, an ATR 72-202 operated by Calm Air as flight CAV470, was conducting flight from Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU to Pond Inlet (CYIO), NU. While en route at approximately 200 nautical miles north of CYRT, the flight crew heard a "thump". Subsequently, the aircraft yawed, the engine torque dropped to zero which was followed by a Master Warning #1 Engine Oil indication. The flight crew carried out the applicable checklists and secured the engine. The crew declared an emergency and returned to CYRT. The aircraft landed safely with ARFF on standby. The operator's maintenance inspected the engine and reported that an engine change is required. The operator is investigating will advise the TSB of its findings.

C-FFVS, a Bell Helicopter 412 operated by Wisk-Air Ltd, was conducting slinging operations from Deer Lake (CYVZ), ON to Bak Lake, ON (approximately 100 NM N of Red Lake [CYRL], ON). While en route the cargo net inadvertently released a drum. It was reported that the cargo net had a large hole. The drum could not be found, CANUTEC was notified, and a spill response report has been issued.

C-FPXL, a Piper PA-31-325 aircraft operated by The Airborne Sensing Corporation, departed Summerside airport (CYSU), NS on an aerial survey flight. While in the climb at about 10 nm north of CYSU, an uncommanded left yaw occurred, and the pilot observed a reduction of No. 1 engine manifold pressure indication. The No. 1 engine continued to run with partial power, and the pilot coordinated with ATS to return to CYSU where a landing was made without further incident.Post flight, a loose turbocharger induction hose clamp on the No. 1 engine was discovered. Subsequent engine operational tests confirmed full power was available on the No. 1 engine.

C-GUSD, a Hiller UH-12E operated by Western Aerial Applications, departed the Winnipeg Heliport (CWG2), MB to conduct spray operations 5.8 nm northeast of Winnipeg. During the spray operation, the helicopter's engine experienced a loss of power (Avco Lycoming VO-540-C2A) at an altitude of approximately 100 feet AGL. The pilot initiated an auto-rotation and, upon touching down, the helicopter yawed to the right but remained upright. There were no injuries to the pilot. Local fire, EMS and RCMP responded. The helicopter suffered minor damage to the right skid gear.A visual inspection of the helicopter by the operator indicated that the engine crank case was cracked and oil was found on the engine deck. The helicopter was placed on a trailer and transported to the operator's maintenance facility.

The Canadaian Warplane Heritage Museum's Avro Lancaster MK X (C-GVRA) aircraft, was on an annual recurrent training flight near Toronto Billy Bishop Airport (CYTZ) ON when the number 3 engine (Rolls Royce USA 224 Packard) oil pressure began to fluctuate. The flight crew carried out the abnormal checklist and perfromed a precautionary shut down of the engine. The flight crew advised ATC of the problem and requested ARFF on standby for the return landing in Hamilton (CYHM). The aircraft landed in CYHM without further incident.Maintenance suspects an oil pressure indication fault, all other engine indications and parameters were normal.

C-GOVQ, un Beechcraft BE-55 en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec seulement le pilote à bord. Alors qu’il effectuait un posé-décollé à l’aéroport de Bromont (Roland Désourdy), QC (CZBM), le train d’atterrissage s’est affaissé et l’appareil a glissé sur son ventre sur la piste où il s’est immobilisé. Le pilote a évacué l’appareil et n’a subi aucune blessure.

C-GIAB, un De Havilland DHC-8-314 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE802 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Kuujjuarapik, QC (CYGW) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 9 passagers à bord. En vol de croisière au niveau de vol 250, à environ 10 miles marins (nm) au nord-est de CYPP, le voyant d’avertissement « Cabin Press » s'est activé. L’équipage a remarqué que l’altitude de la cabine était supérieure à 10 000 pieds et a amorcé une descente d’urgence. Une urgence a alors été déclarée et l'équipage a effectué la liste de vérification d'urgence (QRH). Une fois en palier à 14 000 pieds, l’altitude cabine s’est stabilisée à 7000 pieds. L’équipage a demandé un retour vers CYUL et l’urgence a été annulée. L’aéronef a atterri sans encombre et il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

Air Canada flight AC81, a Boeing 787-9 (C-FGDT) aircraft was on route from Tel Aviv, Israel (LLBG) to Toronto LBPIA (CYYZ) and approximately 214 NM NE of Quebec City when a flight attendant had a medical emergency. The flight crew declared PAN PAN and requested EMS meet the flight on arrival in Toronto. The aircraft landed without further incident in Toronto and the crew member was transported to hospital by EMS.

C-GDMI, un appareil de type Eurocopter EC120B en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Saint-Sylvestre QC, à destination du lac aux Rognons QC, avec le pilote et 3 passagers à bord. Le vent venait du sud et le pilote devait se poser sur la rive nord du lac. Il a donc effectué une approche par vent traversier et une fois en stationnaire au-dessus de sa zone d’atterrissage, il a tourné l’hélicoptère face au vent. Le patin droit s’est pris dans une racine et le pilote a perdu la maîtrise de l’hélicoptère qui s’est retourné sur le côté droit en frappant des arbres à proximité. Tous les occupants portaient leur ceinture de sécurité et il n’y a eu aucun blessé. L’hélicoptère a subi des dommages importants. Il n'y a pas eu de feu post-impact.

C-FPBL, a privately operated Robinson R44 helicopter, was on a multi leg cross-country pleasure flight. The helicopter departed Springdale Airport Newfoundland (CCD2) with the intent to refuel at an aircraft maintenance facility located on the north-east side of Thorburn Lake, Newfoundland (CCW5). Upon arrival at Thorburn Lake the helicopter completed a right turn toward the planned landing site; a gravel parking lot surrounded by trees. It descended to tree top level and entered a hover then a short time afterward it began to climb vertically. When the helicopter reached approximately 75 feet above tree top level it began small yaw and pitch movements which increased in amplitude over a short period of time. Control was lost and the main rotor blades made contact with and severed approximately four feet of the tail boom that included the tail rotor assembly. The helicopter and the tail rotor assembly fell vertically into a stand of trees and came to rest upright on the forest floor. The pilot and front seat passenger sustained multiple serious injuries and passenger in the RH rear seat was fatally injured. Witnesses close by provided first aid to the occupants and extinguished a small non-fuel fed fire in the area of the LH engine manifold. The helicopter was destroyed.Updated 4 September, 2020

C-FQZM, a privately registered Piper PA-28-180, was conducting a visual flight rules flight from Arnprior/South Renfrew Municipal Airport, ON (CNP3) to Toronto/Buttonville Municipal Airport, ON, (CYKZ) with the pilot and 2 passengers on board. While enroute, the pilot made a decision to divert and land at the Stirling Airport, ON, (CPJ5) due to inclement weather enroute. As the pilot attempted to land on Runway 27, the aircraft continued to float down the runway. A go-around was attempted however, the aircraft did not perform as expected in the hot weather. The pilot made the decision to reduce engine power and land straight ahead. The aircraft touched down with approximately 300 feet of runway remaining and overran the runway by approximately 200 feet, coming to rest in a wooded area. There were no injuries. The aircraft propeller and nose landing gear were damaged.

C-GOVX, un Piper Navajo PA-31 exploité par Les Levées Aéroscan Inc., effectuait un vol de photographie aérienne selon les règles de vol à vue sous l'indicatif SCANNER1 depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors que l'appareil volait en suivant une ligne de photographies aériennes à une altitude de 13 000 pieds, le pilote aux commandes a senti le manche de l'appareil se raidir soudainement dans l'axe de roulis. En forcant à deux mains afin garder le manche droit et empêcher l'appareil d'effectuer un virage, le pilote aux commandes a déclaré une urgence et l'appareil est revenu atterrir sur la piste 25 à CYQB. Une fois l'appareil stationné, il a été constaté que le bouton de la fonction "ROLL" de l'autopilote était enclenché. En le désactivant, les commandes sont revenues à la normale. Une inspection de la maintenance a conclu qu'il n'y avait pas d'anomalie technique au niveau du système de pilotage automatique.

C-GUMQ, un Piper Navajo PA-31 exploité par Orizon Aviation, effectuait un vol d'entraînement local selon les règles de vol à vue, depuis l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait à 15NM au sud de CYQB, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison d'un problème d'indication de train d'atterissage. L'appareil s'est posé sans problème à CYQB à 1732Z. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-FSKQ, un Beechcraft 200 exploité par Skyjet Aviation sous l'indicatif VSL443 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 8 passagers à bord. Lors de la rétraction du train d’atterrissage au départ de CYQB, l’équipage a entendu un bruit, mais celui-ci ne semblait pas préoccupant. En approche pour la piste 26 à CYUY, lorsque la manette de commande du train d’atterrissage a été actionnée pour sortir le train, il n’y a eu aucun effet. L’approche a été interrompue et la liste de vérification d’urgence a été effectuée. L’équipage a tenté de sortir le train manuellement, mais aucune pression dans le levier d’urgence n’a été perçue et le train n’est pas sorti. Une deuxième tentative a été effectuée et le train avant a été sorti et verrouillé cependant il ne restait plus de pression dans la pompe manuelle pour sortir complètement le train principal. Une approche basse a été effectuée afin que du personnel au sol puisse vérifier la position du train. Les 3 roues semblaient sorties et l’équipage a déclaré une urgence pour se poser sur la piste 26. Les passagers ont reçu les instructions d’urgence et l’appareil s’est posé. Le touché des roues a été normal, mais lorsque la vitesse a atteint environ 60 nœuds, le train principal droit s’est affaissé suivi de celui de gauche. L’appareil a été évacué et il n’y a eu aucun blessé. Une inspection sommaire de l'aéronef a permis de constater le le disjoncteur du système de train d'atterrissage était dans la position tirée.

C-GANH, an Air North Boeing 737-500 aircraft, was operating as flight ANT569 from Vancouver Int'l, BC (CYVR) to Kelowna, BC (CYLW) with 4 crew members and 75 passengers on board. While parked at Gate 7 in CYLW, the CYLW passengers were deplaned, and 23 passengers remained onboard for the subsequent flight to Whitehorse, YT (CYXY). Following the detection of an acrid smell in the passenger cabin and a haze in the air on the flight deck, the crew confirmed it was not coming from the aircraft ovens. The captain requested assistance by ARFF and commanded a rapid deplanement of the remaining passengers and crew. The operators' maintenance determined that oil was leaking from the APU cowl drain and creating smoke when contacting the APU exhaust. The aircraft was returned to service under minimum equipment list provisions, and the flight continued to CYXY without further incident.

The amateur-built Glasair SH-2R, C-FHBS, was operating on a local flight from Olds-Didsbury (CEA3), AB. While landing at CEA3, the aircraft set down on the runway with the landing gear in the retracted position. The aircraft came to rest on the runway surface. The pilot and passenger received no injuries and the ELT was not activated. The pilot and passenger egressed the aircraft without issue. The aircraft received damage to the propeller, aircraft belly and flaps trailing edge. There were no reported issues with the landing gear system.

C-GTBG, an Air Tractor AT-401B operated by CR AG Ventures, was conducting a local flight in the vicinity of Virden/R.J (Bob) Andrew Field Regional (CYVD), MB. During landing onto Runway 08, a thunderstorm approached the field with increasing winds and heavy rain reducing the pilot's visibility. The aircraft drifted on landing and the right main wheel broke and the strut dug into the runway surface. The aircraft spun 180 degrees and came to a rest facing west on the runway. The aircraft sustained damage to the wing, fuselage and landing gear. No injuries were reported.

C-GTBY, an amphibian-equipped Cessna 208 operated by Superior Airways, was conducting a local training flight at Red Lake (CYRL), ON. During landing onto Runway 26, the wheels were inadvertently left in the retracted position prior to landing. The aircraft touched down and came to a stop on the runway surface. The bottom of the floats received some damage, however the 2 occupants were uninjured.

C-GWXP, a Mcdonnell Douglas MD900 helicopter operated by Ascent Helicopters Ltd, was conducting longline operations 21 NM east of Kamloops Airport (CYKA), BC, with 1 pilot onboard. During short final for the staging area with a longline load connected, the pilot experienced a rush of air in the cockpit accompanied by vibration in the yaw control pedals. The pilot controlled the descent until the load touched the ground and then released the longline from the cargo hook. The pilot proceeded with a no hover landing without incident. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the load or property. Upon inspection, the NOTAR (no tail rotor system) access panel was found dislodged from the right hand side and 2 NOTAR blades had FOD damage. The 2 NOTAR blades were replaced, the access panel was reinstalled, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GEEU, a Cessna 150 aircraft, operated by College Air Richelieu, was on a cross country training flight with two privately licensed student pilots on board. The aircraft departed Brockville (CNL3) and was headed to Montreal/St-Hubert (CYHU). After departure the aircraft climbed to 2000 feet, then 4000 feet and finally to 5500 feet for the flight to CYHU; at each altitude a carburetor heat check was carried out. Once at 5500 feet the aircraft engine was leaned for best performance. The weather at the time was conducive to severe carburetor icing at cruise power so the pilot conducted carburetor heat checks every 3 minutes. Near Ingleside, ON, the pilot noted a 200 RPM loss, the carburetor heat was on at the time. The pilot decided to leave the carburetor heat on to eliminate any ice in the carburetor. Approximately every 30 seconds the engine RPM started to fluctuate with increasing severity. The pilot decided to divert to Cornwall (CYCC) and declared a PAN PAN with Montreal Centre. While descending through 3000 feet the engine lost all power, the pilot applied full power and the engine re-started. The engine lost power again at 2500 feet while over the airport and was restarted. While on final approach the aircraft was too high so the pilot increased the flaps 40 degrees and used side slip to lose altitude. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GFPP, a Rockwell International Aero Commander 690 operated by Air Spray (1967) Ltd., was conducting a local flight 17 nm east of Gimli Industrial Park Airport (CYGM) MB. During cruise the pilot noted a rapid rise in ITT on the number 2 engine. The pilot elected to shutdown the engine and returned to CYGM. The aircraft landed safely without further incident.The operator's maintenance identified the a fault in the engine temperature indicating system.

C-GUWF, a privately operated de Havilland DHC-2 MK 1 with EDO 4930 amphibious float landing gear, was conducting a flight from Sakinaw Lake, BC, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 1 pilot and 1 passenger onboard. During the water take-off, the aircraft collided with an object in the water and made an uncontrolled veer to the right. The take-off was aborted and the plane was beached on the shore. There were no reported injuries. Upon inspection, the bow of the right hand float was substantially damaged forward of the mounting strut. The aircraft is being disassembled and transported to Vancouver for inspection and repair.

C-FKNQ, a Eurocopter AS 355 N helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters Ltd, was on approach for landing at a worksite about 10 nm northeast of Wabush airport (CYWK), NL. The right engine chip light illuminated during the approach and the pilot conducted an overshoot, reduced power and then shut down the right engine (Turbomeca Arrius 1A) as per checklist. The pilot diverted to CYWK, and restarted the right engine for the landing. The helicopter landed without further incident. Company maintenance carried out the right hand engine inspection for chip light illumination as per the manufacturer instructions, and operated the engine with no recurrence of the engine chip light.

C-FPMD, a Piper PA-36-235 operated by Miccar Aerial Ltd., departed Yorkton Municipal Airport (CYQV), SK to conduct spray operations approximately 10 nm south of Yorkton SK. After completing the spray operation C-FPMD was returning to CYQV when the engine surged (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-20). The pilot turned on the Aux Fuel Pump which restored power; however, at approximately 2 nm from the airport while on final approach for Runway 31 the engine flamed out. The pilot conducted a forced approach and landed safely in a field. There was no damage to the aircraft and no injuries to the pilot.  Prior to departing CYQV, the pilot did visually check the fuel gauges and noticed the left fuel gauge indicated half a tank but did not visually check the quantity of fuel in the left hand fuel tank. The pilot added fuel to the right fuel tank only. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and found both left and right hand fuel tanks were empty. The aircraft was removed from the field and flown back to CYQV with no further incident.

PH-BQC, a Boeing 777-200 aircraft operated by KLM, was conducting flight KLM 763 from Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (EHAM), Netherlands to Quito/ Mariscal Sucre International Airport (SEQM), Ecuador. About 3.5 hours after takeoff (during cruise flight at about 46°58' N, 033°55' W), KLM 763 contacted Gander Centre and requested clearance to divert and return to their departure airport due to an ill cabin crewmember. An amended route clearance was issued and the flight diverted without incident.

C-GMBI, an Air Tractor AT-401 operated by Steinbach Aerial Crop Service, departed Altona Municipal Airport (CJL6), MB to conduct aerial application on a field approximately 3 nm North of CJL6.  During the spray run, the aircraft stuck a powerline. The pilot was able to return the aircraft to CJL6 and landed safely. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. There no injuries to the pilot.

C-GLKY, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 operated by Perimeter Aviation LP as flight PAG1551, departed Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB for St. Theresa Point (CYST), MB. During the approach into CYST, the flight crew selected the landing gear to the down position but did not observe a gear down-and-locked indication. The flight crew decided to return to CYWG. When the aircraft arrived at CYWG, the flight crew performed an emergency landing gear extension procedure and did not receive a nose gear down and locked indication. PAG1551 performed a flyby past the control tower and were informed the nose gear appeared down. The aircraft landed safely with ARFF on standby. The operator's maintenance found loose wires at the landing gear inhibit switch. The wires were re-secured and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FRWC, an Ayers S-2R operated by Fly'N Dutchman Ag Ltd, was conducting aerial application operations on a field 5 NM north of Melfort/Miller Field (CJZ3), SK. While the aircraft was in a turn, oil was released from an engine cylinder (Pratt & Whitney USA R-1340-S3H1) that covered the windshield. The pilot was unable to see out the windshield and had to release his seatbelt to see forward out the side window. The pilot elected to return to CJZ3. The aircraft landed short of the runway and came to rest on the side of the runway. There were no injuries to the pilot. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FLJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ 900) operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight JZA8568, departed Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC for Regina Intl (CYQR), SK. At approximately 25 NM WNW of CYQR, the flight crew received a low oil status message for the right hand engine (General Electric CF34-8C5). The flight crew noticed oil temperature and oil pressure were normal; however, on the descent, the oil temperature started to increase and oil pressure dropped. The flight crew carried out a precautionary right engine shutdown and declared an emergency. The flight landed safely with ARFF on standby and taxied to the gate. It was reported that there was no evidence of an external oil leak. The operator's maintenance inspected the engine and found the accessory gearbox scavenge inlet strainer was clogged with debris. The filter was cleaned, the low oil level sensor was replaced and a successful engine ground power run was completed. The operator has sent the debris for analysis.

C-GVST, a private Burkhart Grob G102 ASTIR CS 77 glider, was conducting a local flight from Invermere Airport (CAA8), BC, with 1 pilot onboard. At approximately 3.5 hours into the flight, the pilot became incapacitated and the glider collided with terrain. The pilot was seriously injured and the glider was destroyed.

C-FEKI, an Embraer E175 operated by Sky Regional Airlines as SKV7459, was in the initial stage of a scheduled flight from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. After the pushback began the ground crew advised the flight crew they were clear to start both engines at their discretion on the push. The Captain requested, and received, an all-clear from the ground crew to start engine #1. The engine start commenced with no engine indication anomalies noted. The aircraft then came to a stop and the ground crew advised that one of their crew had dropped a  handheld computer (Honeywell CN-80), which was ingested into the engine #1 during the start and ejected back out the front. The flight crew shut down engine #1 and had the aircraft towed back to the gate. All passengers were deplaned, company maintenance notified and the aircraft removed from service. The flight crew deactivated the Cockpit Voice Recorder to preserve data related to the event.The engine #1 FOD inspection found some blades that were damaged and required either repair or replacement. The aircraft was later returned to service.

C-GWWE, a Cessna A188B operated by Southeast Air Service Ltd, was conducting an aerial application flight from Altona Municipal (CJL6), MB. During the aerial application of a field adjacent to the Canada/U.S. border located approximately 9 nautical miles SE of CJL6, C-GWWE collided with terrain approximately 1/2 nautical mile south of the border. The pilot sustained serious injuries and the aircraft was destroyed by a post impact fire.The National Transportation Safety Board of United States is conducting an investigation.

C-FJVW, a Saab 340B operated by Transwest Air, departed Prince Albert/Glass Field (CYPA) SK. enroute to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK. At approximately 20 NM north east of CYXE and descending through 8700 feet, the flight crew made a power reduction and the right hand engine (General Electric CT7-98) failed. The flight crew completed the emergency checklist, briefed the cabin flight attendant and declared an emergency with ATC. The aircraft landed safely in CYXE with ARFF on standby and taxied to the hanger. The operator's maintenance performed troubleshooting and replaced the right hand engine mounted Digital Engine Computer Unit (DECU). Ground runs were completed. The aircraft was released subject to a satisfactory test flight and returned to service.

C-GEFA, an Airbus A330 aircraft operated by Air Canada was conducting a flight from Montreal/ Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Zurich Airport Intl (LSHZ) Switzerland. The aircraft was approximately two hours into the flight and prior to ETOPS entry when the crew observed a Y-system hydraulic pressure low warning. The crew consulted with company maintenance and then elected to return to CYUL. They contacted Gander Area Control Center, declared a Pan-Pan, and received clearance to return to CYUL. The aircraft landed uneventfully at CYUL.Company maintenance installed a new hydraulic accumulator and bled the Y-system of air; the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKUK, a De Havilland Dash 8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, departed St. John’s Intl, NL (CYYT) on a schedule flight to Halifax/Stanfield Intl NS (CYHZ). The aircraft was in the climb phase at 30 NM west of CYYT when the flight crew detected smoke in the cockpit simultaneous to a flight attendant report of haze in the cabin area. A short time after, the crew noted caution messages FLT COMP HOT and #2 BLEED HOT followed by a LAV smoke detector caution.The flight crew donned their oxygen masks and declared an emergency with air traffic control (ATC) at approximately 07:45 NDT. They then received clearance from ATC to return to CYYT. The aircraft landed without incident at 08:01 NDT while ARFF were standing by. ARFF confirmed there was no evidence of smoke or fire and the aircraft then taxied to the gate.The aircraft is currently undergoing maintenance.

C-GRTQ, a privately registered Piper PA-25-235, departed from a private strip near Fertile SK. to conduct a fungicide aerial application of a field located approximately 9 miles south of Gainsborough, SK. During the spray operation, the aircraft struck a powerline with a tire. The aircraft pitched nose down and impacted the field and sustained substantial damage. The pilot sustained minor injuries. No ELT signal was received and first responders were not notified nor did they respond.

C-GTVS, a privately operated Mooney M-20 TN, was conducting a flight from Buena Vista / Central Colorado Regional (KAEJ), CO, United States to Van Nuys (KVNY), CA, United States with one crew member onboard. Shortly after takeoff, the aircraft impacted terrain and came to rest on the runway surface. The aircraft was destroyed by the post-crash fire. The pilot was seriously injured.The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating [NTSB Ref: CEN20LA268]

C-GNAG, a Beechcraft King Air 200 operated by Northern Air Charter, was conducting a flight from Penticton (CYYF), BC to Calgary Int'l Airport (CYYC), AB with 2 crew members on board. While taxiing for departure in CYYF, smoke was noticed in the cabin. The aircraft stopped on Taxiway Alpha, the engines were shut down, and the captain investigated the cause of the smoke. The operator's maintenance was consulted and the flap motor was determined to be responsible for the smoke. The system was isolated and the aircraft flew to Calgary without further incident.

C-FZRV, an amateur-built Acro Sport II, was conducting test flight operations from Springbank (CYBW), AB under the "Initial Standard Operating Conditions - Amateur-built Aircraft" for the Special Certificate of Airworthiness - Amateur Built. The aircraft was nearing the required 25 hours with no issues related to design or construction. The aircraft had been airborne for less than two hours when the engine (Avco Lycoming O-320-H2AD) quit. A mayday was declared and a successful forced approach and landing was conducted into a field near the Wild Cat Gas Plant. During the roll out, the right main landing gear contacted a large rock damaging it and shearing off the tail wheel. The pilot was not injured and was able to egress from the aircraft.Following the flight, the owner determined that the fuel tank was nearly empty. Some fuel staining was found around the airframe fuel screen housing. The owner is continuing to determine the cause of the engine failure.

Perimeter Aviation flight JV377, a Fairchild SA227AC (C-GYRL) aircraft was departing Sudbury (CYSB), ON when the right engine (Garrett TPE331-11U-612G) lost power just before V1. The flight crew rejected the takeoff and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft did not require assistance and returned to the gate. The aircraft was conducting a continuous alcohol water injection (CAWI) when the power loss occurred.Maintenance inspected the aircraft, tested the CAWI system for correct operation and performed max power grounds. Maintenance was unable to find any problems with the engine or CAWI system. A successful test flight was carried out and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFAL, un Boeing 737-2R8C exploité par Glencore Canada Corporation sous l’indicatif RAG100, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Kattiniq/Donaldson, QC (CTP9). Après environ 1 heure et demie de vol, l’équipage a remarqué une indication basse de la pression d’huile du moteur #2. Par mesure de précaution, le moteur #2 a été coupé et l’équipage a avisé le contrôleur aérien qu’il faisait demi-tour pour revenir à CYQB. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés à la demande de l’équipage. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre. Le service de maintenance a découvert qu’une ligne de conduite d’huile était brisée.

C-FEFO, a privately operated Murphy SR3500 (Murphy Moose) on floats, was conducting a fight from Lake Melville, NL to Red Wine River, NL. During the takeoff, the aircraft hit several waves prior to the rotation speed and became airborne, approximately 6-8 feet in the air, before the left wing dropped and struck the water, resulting in the aircraft flipping over. The pilot, passenger and a dog egressed and were rescued by a boat operating nearby. The pilot and passenger received minor injuries.

The pilot of C-FLIH, a Nanchang CJ6A aircraft, was conducting local flights in the Cornwall area. On the first flight of the day the pneumatically operated landing gear did not completely retract. After several attempts, the pilot was able to successfully retract the landing gear and it functioned correctly for the first landing. On the second flight of the day the landing gear retracted normally after take-off, however, during final approach for landing one gear did not lock down completely. The pilot noted the discrepancy with the landing gear during the flare. As the aircraft touched down, the other two landing gear collapsed. The bottom of the fuselage, flaps and propeller were damaged during the landing. When a crane lifted the aircraft after the accident the landing gear came down and locked into place.

C-GNME, a Eurocopter AS 350 B2 helicopter operated by Yellowhead Helicopters Ltd, was conducting a slung load operation 16nm North of Mackenzie Airport (CYCY), BC. While slinging a cargo net with personal gear and equipment to crews on the ground, the net caught on a tree and ripped open spilling the contents. The helicopter returned to the staging area without further incident. The cargo net, work equipment, and some personal items were damaged. There were no injuries or damage to the helicopter.

WestJet Encore flight WEN3516, a Dehavilland Dash 8 Q-400 (C-GWJK) aircraft, on route from London, ON (CYXU) to Toronto /LBPIA (CYYZ), ON declared a PAN PAN due to flap issues. The aircraft continued to its destination where it landed without further incident. Maintenance found the Flap lever trigger found to be sticking. Flap lever selector trigger mechanism was lubricated and flap functional test carried out, checked serviceable. The aircraft was returned to service.

The pilot of C-FVOF, a Jodel D-11 amateur built aircraft, was conducting local flights near the Plattsville airport (CLB2), ON with one passenger on board. The aircraft took off from Runway 07 flew for approximately 30 minutes without any problems. The aircraft returned to the airport landed and took off again from Runway 07. Immediately after becoming airborne, the engine suddenly quit and the pilot was forced to land in the field directly east of the runway. The aircraft landed roughly in the field and nosed over. The pilot and passenger exited the aircraft without injury. The engine caught fire after the nose over and the pilot attempted to put out the fire with the onboard extinguisher. The extinguisher was not able to put out the fire and the aircraft was destroyed by the fire.

C-FKKZ, an Air Tractor AT-401B operated by Western Canadian Aerial, was to conduct a local fungicide application flight from Neepawa (CJV5), MB. On the initial part of the takeoff roll on Runway 22 in CJV5, the aircraft started drifting to the left. The pilot attempted to correct the drift but was unable to obtain full forward travel of the right rudder pedal. The aircraft experienced a runway side-excursion to the left of the runway and came to rest in a ditch that runs parallel to the runway. The pilot was uninjured and the aircraft sustained substantial damage to its wings, propeller, engine and tail wheel. A minimal amount of fuel leaked from the aircraft but none of the fungicide leaked. The ELT did not activate.A post-accident inspection revealed scratch marks and an indentation on the hopper by the right rudder pedal in line with the rudder pedal adjustment T-pin (P/N D5-10T-303).The manufacturer is amending the AT-401B  Illustrated Parts Catalogue (IPC) to be consistent with Service Letter #317. A reduced height T-pin (P/N D5-10T-303/MIN D) will be usable on the Model AT-401B aircraft. A service difficulty report has been filed by the company to Transport Canada.

C-GATR, an amateur-built amphibious float equipped Murphy SR3500 (Murphy Moose), was conducting a local seaplane training flight from the Cooking Lake (CEZ3), AB airport with 1 pilot, 1 training pilot and 1 passengers on board. Approximately 12 nm east of the Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), the aircraft collided with terrain. All occupants sustained fatal injuries; there was no post-impact fire. The aircraft's 406MHz ELT broadcasted a signal that was received by the JRCC in Trenton, ON.

C-GURG, un Canadair CL60 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, qui effectuait le vol QUE10 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, venait de décoller de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean-Lesage, QC (CYQB) pour un vol à destination de l’aéroport de Val d’Or, QC (CYVO). Lors de la sélection du train d’atterrissage en position rentrée, la roue de nez ne s’est pas rétractée. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée et le train d’atterrissage a été déployé avec succès. L’équipage a décidé de revenir à CYQB et, par mesure de précaution, a demandé à ce que les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) soient déployés. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste sans encombre. Une inspection a révélé la présence d’un linge blanc qui masquait les capteurs de positions du train.

C-GTCG, un Piper PA-34-200T exploité par KBM Resources Group, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Bromont, QC (CZBM) à destination de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT). Durant le vol, l’équipage a remarqué que le moteur droit semblait avoir des ratés et que l’aiguille de la pression d’huile du moteur oscillait. Après 30 minutes de vol, l’équipage a décidé d’annuler la descente pour CYMT et de dérouter vers l’aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC). L’indicateur de la pression d’huile moteur a rapidement descendu sous 30 PSI. L’équipage a donc fermé le moteur de droite par mesure de précaution et a déclaré un signal de détresse (Mayday) au contrôleur du terminal de Montréal. L’équipage a dérouté vers l’aéroport de Roberval, QC (CYRJ) où un atterrissage avec un seul moteur fonctionnel a été effectué, et ce sans incident. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé. Une inspection par la maintenance a révélé qu’une perte d’huile a été causée par le desserrement d’une ligne de référence de la pression d’huile du moteur.

C-FKON, un Cessna 140X privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis une piste en gazon privée près de Saint-Ours, QC à destination de Joliette, QC (CSG3), avec un pilote et un instructeur de vol à bord. L’aéronef a débuté sa course au décollage après que le moteur ait tourné au ralenti pendant environ 10 minutes. Le pilote-propriétaire qui était aux commandes éprouvait quelques difficultés à contrôler l’aéronef. L’instructeur de vol a donc pris les commandes pour compléter le décollage qui s’est effectué à mi-piste, soit environ à 1500 pieds. Quelques secondes après le début de la montée initiale, l’instructeur a remarqué que le tachymètre indiquait une rotation du moteur inférieure à la normale d’environ 300 tours par minute et que l’aéronef n’arrivait pas à conserver sa vitesse qui diminuait. Bien que la manette des gaz était pleinement ouverte, l’aéronef a cessé de prendre de l’altitude et est entré en collision avec la cime des arbres. Ceci a provoqué un arrêt brusque de l’aéronef suivi d’un piqué vers le sol. La radiobalise de repérage d’urgence (406 MHz) s’est déclenchée et son signal a été capté par le Centre de contrôle des missions (Cospas-Sarsat). L’aéronef a subi des dommages importants et une fuite de carburant s’est produite sans qu’un feu se soit déclaré. Les 2 occupants ont été gravement blessés et transportés à l’hôpital.

C-GAIG, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE764, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de la Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL). Une fois le décollage effectué, l’équipage a déterminé que la vitesse indiquée n’était pas fiable durant la montée initiale et a déclaré une urgence. L’aéronef est revenu se poser sans encombre à CYUL. Une inspection visuelle a révélé qu’une partie déchirée du couvre-pitot recouvrait le tube pitot.

C-FAIY, un DHC-6-300 exploité par Air Inuit, s'apprêtait à circuler au sol de la rampe vers la piste pour effectuer un décollage de l’aéroport de Kangiqsualujjuaq, QC (CYLU) avec 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Le seul agent au sol, situé devant l’aéronef, a montré son pouce aux pilotes pour leur indiquer que la voie était libre et qu’ils pouvaient commencer à rouler. Après que l’aéronef a débuté un virage vers la gauche et avancé de quelques pieds, l’agent au sol a fait des signes aux pilotes d’arrêter. L’aileron au bout de l’aile gauche est entré en collision avec un camion qui était stationné trop prêt du côté arrière gauche de l’aéronef. Le vol a été annulé et du personnel de la maintenance a été envoyé sur place afin d’évaluer les dommages causés à l’aileron.

C-GVUT, a privately registered Cessna 180B, was conducting a flight from North Knife Lake Lodge, MB to Thompson (CYTH), MB with one pilot and one passenger on board. During landing on Runway 06 in CYTH the aircraft bounced on touchdown. Subsequently, the aircraft bounced a second time and the right main wheel came off. The aircraft veered to the left of the runway, the propeller, right wing tip and right main strut came in contact with the ground. The aircraft stopped just prior to exiting the side of the runway. No injuries were reported and the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

Sky Regional flight SKV7115, an Embraer ERJ170-200 SU (C-FRQK) aircraft, arriving in Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ), ON from Muskoka (CYQA), ON conducted an overshoot just inside the Final Approach Fix (FAF) due to flap failure. The flight crew carried out the QRH for a flap fail and were unable to resolve the issue. The flight crew declared PAN PAN and conducted a no flap landing on Runway 24L without issue.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and found the LH #4 flap actuator torque limiter tripped and the actuator was making unusual noises. The flap actuator was replaced.

C-FSUD, un Aero Commander 690B exploité par MAG Aerospace Canada s’est posé à l’aéroport de Maniwaki, QC (CYMW) pour ravitaillement. Une fois l’aéronef stationné, le camion de ravitaillement s’est approché. Pendant que le pilote terminait de remplir des documents à l’intérieur de l’aéronef, le personnel au sol a débuté le ravitaillement. Lorsque le pilote est sorti de l’aéronef, il a remarqué le lettrage AVGAS sur le camion. Il a tout de suite demandé d’arrêter le ravitaillement, mais 53 litres de carburant avaient déjà été versés. Une lettre a été envoyée à la compagnie de ravitaillement pour les informer des différences entre un AC690 (moteur à turbine) et un AC500 (moteur à piston), 2 modèles opérés par MAG Aerospace Canada et demander que le personnel au sol confirme avec le pilote le type de carburant avant de débuter le ravitaillement. Un rappel a été envoyé aux pilotes de la compagnie leur rappelant qu’ils doivent superviser le ravitaillement et s’assurer que le type de carburant est adéquat.

C-FKOB, a privately operated Cessna 175 on floats, was conducting a leisure flight from Pitt Meadows Waterdrome (CAJ8), BC, with 1 pilot and 1 passenger. After landing the aircraft was water taxing to the ramp. The aircraft was unable to access the ramp due to the current of the river and the pilot initiated a turn to avoid colliding with a pylon in the water. The right hand wing struck a tree and pivoted the aircraft into the rocky shoreline. The pilot contacted Pitt Meadows tower for assistance. Local RCMP and emergency services responded. There were no injuries and the ELT did not activate. The aircraft suffered substantial damage.

C-FWXX, a privately registered Cessna 150, was conducting a local flight in the vicinity of Kelvington (CKV2), SK. During flight the aircraft encountered engine power degradation and the pilot landed the aircraft in a nearby field. Upon touchdown the aircraft bounced and the wing collided with a tree; pulling the aircraft into bushes. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was not injured. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The closest reported weather at Wynyard, SK reported a temperature of 16°C and a dewpoint of 14 at the time of the occurrence.

C-GWOX, a Beechcraft 1900D operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG 941 from Fort Severn, (CYER) ON, to Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON, with 2 flight crew members and 6 passengers onboard. During cruise, the crew observed a fuel light indication approximately 77nm north of the destination. The flight crew actioned the QRH, declared a PAN PAN, and diverted the aircraft to Kingfisher Lake (CNM5), ON. The aircraft landed safely and no emergency assistance was required.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft fuel system and identified that there was no issue with the fuel system. It was reported that a grounding fault had likely triggered the false fuel light indication.

C-GNNR, a Beech 200 operated by Skynorth Air as flight SN 861, was enroute from Churchill (CYYQ), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with two flight crew, one flight medic, and two passengers on board. While in cruise, the right engine fire warning light illuminated. The flight crew actioned the QRH Engine Fire Drill, declared an emergency, and diverted the aircraft to Thompson (CYTH), MB. Emergency services were arranged and the aircraft landed in CYTH without further incident. The operator's maintenance inspection of the fire detection system and found the fire wall upper detector ground wire broken. The wire was repaired and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FPCJ, a privately operated Aero Commander 100X, was conducting a training flight from Lethbridge Airport (CYQL), AB to Cardston Airport (CEA6), AB with one pilot on board. While on final approach for Runway 23 at CEA6 for a touch and go, the aircraft banked left un-expectantly in the flare and departed the runway laterally. C-FPCJ then impacted a barbed wired fence adjacent to the runway, slid on it's nose into a nearby farmer's field before nosing over and coming to rest upside down. There was extensive damage to the propeller, nose wheel, fuselage, empennage and wings. There were no reported injuries.

C-FMJM, un Diamond DA42 exploité par Trans Capital Air Ltée. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. En vol de croisière à une altitude de 7000 pieds, l’équipage a entendu deux "bang" immédiatement suivi des indications "ECU AFAIL et "ECU B FAIL" pour le moteur de droite. La température et la pression indiquée du moteur sont restées dans les limites opérationnelles. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et a demandé à retourner à CYQB. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre à 1901 utc. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

C-FEKY, a privately operated Cessna 150L, was conducting circuits at Cooking Lake (CEZ3), AB. Following the first successful circuit, the pilot came to a full stop on the runway prior to the first taxiway, approximately half way down Runway 28.  The pilot elected to commence a second take off from the intersection of RWY 28 and the taxiway, with approximately 1550 feet of runway remaining.  The aircraft became airborne just prior to the end of the runway. During the climb out the aircraft did not gain enough altitude to clear the trees that were approximately 3250 feet from the start of the take-off run (approx. 1650 feet from the end of the runway). The wheels contacted the top of the trees and the aircraft stalled just over the field. The aircraft impacted the wet ground and flipped over.  The pilot was able to get out of the aircraft on his own and was not injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GSNF, Beechcraft 200 aircraft operated by SkyNorth Air Ltd. was conducting flight SN898 from Winnipeg/James Armstron Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Thompson (CYTH), MB with 2 flight crew members and 1 flight paramedic on board. During cruise, the flight crew smelled electrical smoke, followed by a white smoke emitting from the right corner of the overhead panel and circuit breaker panel on the Captain's side.  The flight crew actioned the Quick Reference Checklist (QRC), declared an emergency and diverted the aircraft back to CYWG. After landing in CYWG, fire and rescue scanned the aircraft for heat signature. No evidence of fire was observed and the aircraft was escorted safely to the ramp.The operators maintenance identifed that the right hand side circuit breaker panel lighting resistor on the overhead panel was burnt and its transitor had failed. Both the transistor and resistor were replaced and the aircraft was subsequently ground tested as serviceable.

C-GZSH, a private amphibious float equipped Cessna A185F, utilized by Conair Aerial Firefighting, was conducting a flight from Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC, to Abbotsford (CYXX), BC, with 1 pilot and 1 passenger onboard. Shortly after takeoff, the pilot reported a loud bang followed by significant vibrations and abnormal handling characterisitics in the pitch axis. The pilot requested an immediate landing, performed a 180 degree turn, and landed without incident. There was substantial damage found on the leading edge of the horizontal stabilizer. Upon further inspection, the right hand float access hatch was missing and was presumed to have struck the horizontal stabilizer. The aircraft had recently undergone maintenance on the hydraulic system for the amphibious landing gear. The access hatch was recovered from the runway.

C-FCGM, a Beechcraft 200 operated by North Cariboo Flying Service Ltd, was conducting a flight from Prince George (CYXS), BC, to Fort St John (CYXJ), BC, with 2 flight crew and 2 passengers onboard. During initial climb at FL190, the aircraft master warning flashed with no associated annunciator light and the crew observed a high oil temperature with fluctuating oil pressure (between 60-70 PSI) on the #2 engine (Pratt and Whitney PT6A-41). The flight crew performed a precautionary shutdown of the #2 engine, actioned the emergency checklist, and declared a MAYDAY. The aircraft landed safely at CYXJ and was shut down on the runway before being towed to the company maintenance facility. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft.Maintenance determined the thermostatic bypass and check valve assembly in the #2 engine was defective. The engine will be removed and sent for light overhaul as per the Engine Maintenance Manual.

The privately owned Aeropro A220 Advanced ultralight (C-IVLE) was departing from a private grass strip, located 13 nm to the east of the Kitchener/Waterloo Airport (CYKF). Shortly after take-off as the aircraft was climbing through approximately 200 feet AGL, the engine (Rotax 100 ULS) lost power. Due to trees located ahead,  the pilot decided to turn left, back towards the airstrip. During the left turn the engine quit. The aircraft lost height quickly and struck the ground in a 20 degree left turn bank. The pilot received minor back injuries and was transported to a local hospital.

C-FLTS, un appareil de type Beech A100 King Air exploité par Exact Air sous l'indicatif ET410, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Val-d'Or, QC (CYVO). Alors que l'appareil se trouvait à une altitude de 8000 pieds en montée après le départ, l’équipage a observé une légère fuite de carburant venant de la nacelle du moteur de gauche. L’équipage a demandé un retour à CYQB en raison d’une fuite de carburant. À 15 milles marins à l’ouest de CYQB durant la descente pour la piste 06, l’équipage a déclaré un PAN PAN. L'appareil s'est posé sans problème sur la piste 06 à 1719 UTC avec la présence de l'unité de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). Le département de maintenance a découvert une fuite via la sonde de la nacelle (nacelle probe).

C-ILOS, un paramoteur Kangook XLITE, en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis un champ situé à 1 mille marin à l'ouest-sud-ouest de l’aérodrome de Rougemont (CTY5), Qc. Après un vol d'environ 30 minutes, alors en courte finale sans moteur, le pilote a effectué un virage vers la gauche afin de bénéficier du peu de vent. Le côté gauche de la voilure a alors perdu de la portance et le pilote a perdu le contrôle de l’appareil et s’est écrasé. Le pilote a subi des blessures mineures et l'appareil a subi des dommages importants.

The pilot of C-FULL, a float equipped, Piper PA 12 aircraft, departed Mississippi Lake near the Carleton Place airport (CNR6) on a local flight after replacing the muffler on the aircraft. The aircraft was returning to land when the engine gradually started to lose power and the pilot was forced to conduct a forced approach. The aircraft crashed into trees approximately 0.5nm southwest of the airport. The pilot and passenger were not injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged during the crash.

C-GDSG, un appareil de type Beech 1900D exploité par SkyJet M.G., effectuait le vol VSL607 selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de l’aéroport de Port-Menier (CYPN), QC à destination de Sept-îles (CYZV), QC avec 13 passagers et 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Au départ de CYPN, à environ 41 miles nautiques au sud-est de CYZV, l'équipage a observé un problème avec l’indicateur du train d’atterrissage. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification associée et une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée. L’équipage a descendu le train manuellement et a demandé les services d’urgences. L’appareil a effectué une approche basse au-dessus la piste afin que du personnel au sol lui confirme que le train est bien sorti. L’appareil a effectué un circuit et s’est posé à CYZV sans encombre. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé. Une inspection de piste a été faite après l’atterrissage et rien d’anormal n’a été rapporté.

C-IJBA, a Challenger II ultralight on amphibious floats, took off from Mattawa (CMA2), ON and flew a single circuit. After the circuit, the pilot departed for a local flight and decided to land on the Ottawa river by Mattawa. The pilot overflew the intended landing area on the river to make sure the area was clear before landing; the water was fairly muddy looking, but everything looked clear for landing. The pilot brought the aircraft around for the landing and just after touch down one of the floats hit a submerged log. The damaged float dug into the water and the aircraft overturned and sank. The pilot who was wearing a 4 point safety belt was not injured. The pilot was able to egress the overturned aircraft and was picked up by local boaters. The pilot had received some egress training approximately 1 year ago.

C-GLVK, a privately registered amateur built Murphy Moose SR3500 (amphibian floats) was on a pleasure flight from Florenceville Airport, NB (CCR3) to Saint John Airport (CYSJ), NB. The pilot departed CCR3 at approximately 2015 ADT with approximately 15 gallons of fuel per tank. The aircraft was in cruise at 3000 feet ASL over the Saint John River, abeam Morrisdale, NB when the engine began to run rough. The pilot checked the RH and LH fuel sight gauges and both tanks were indicating empty. All engine parameters were normal. The pilot planned a precautionary landing on the river between a powerboat operating in the area and a spit of land jutting out from the shoreline. At an altitude of 1500 feet AGL the engine roughness increased and a complete power lost occurred a short time afterwards. The descent rate increased to approximately 900 FPM and the angle of glide steepened, requiring the pilot to bank to the right to remain clear of the powerboat. The aircraft stalled and departed controlled flight at approximately 100 feet AGL. It struck the surface of the water in a steep nose down right wing low attitude at approximately 2115 ADT. The aircraft cabin quickly filled with water and the pilot released himself from the three-point safety harness and exited the aircraft with an available life vest. The powerboat operator was on scene within minutes and recovered the pilot from the water. The pilot received minor injuries. Impact forces destroyed the aircraft.The aircraft was equipped with four life vests and four Helicopter Emergency Egress Device (HEED 3) units. The pilot had exited the aircraft before use of a HEED 3 was required. The pilot suspects fuel exhaustion as the initiating factor for the engine failure. A private aircraft maintenance company recovered the aircraft from the Saint John River. They will inspect the aircraft for evidence of a fuel related problem.

C-FDBD, a Boeing 737-800 operated by Sunwing Airlines Inc., was conducting flight SWG9950 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Phoenix/Goodyear Intl. (KGYR), AZ. During descent into KGYR, flight crew received TCAS RA “DESCEND” and “LEVEL OFF” warnings due to other local traffic. Standard operating procedures were applied and no cleared altitudes were deviated. ATC was notified and the flight landed without further incident.

C-FJJH, a Beech A100 aircraft was performing Thunder Airlines flight THU104 from Timmins (CYTS), ON for Mossonee (CYMO), ON. During the climb, smoke was observed coming from under the instrument panel. The flight crew carried out the electrical smoke checklist and the smoke began to dissipate. The flight crew declared an emergency and requested a diversion to Cochrane (CYCN), ON. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance inspected the aircraft and found a transistor the for the cabin light lighting system was burnt out. The system was disabled and the aircraft was issued a ferry permit back to CYTS for repairs.

C-GUPP, a Beech A100 aircraft, was conducting Thunder Airlines IFR flight THU106 from Timmins (CYTS), ON  to Moosonee (CYMO), ON. Approximately 80nm north of CYTS the flight crew noted the left engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-28) torque was fluctuating and oil pressure was dropping. The flight crew carried out the low oil pressure checklist and reduced power to the left engine. The oil pressure continued to drop and the flight crew shutdown the engine, declared an emergency and returned to CYTS. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance checked the engine and found a significant oil leak. The engine was  removed and sent to manufacturer for teardown and investigation.

C-GJNL, un Dash-8-300 (DH8C) exploité par Hydro Québec sous l'indicatif HYD151, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de La Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) à destination de CFB Bagotville, QC (CYBG) avec 24 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage. Immédiatement après le décollage, une roue du train d’atterrissage gauche s’est détachée de l’appareil et est tombée sur la piste. L’agent de bord a avisé l’équipage de la situation. Comme le train était en position rentrée et en l’absence d’indication de défaillance, l’équipage a pris la décision de dérouter vers l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Qc (CYUL). L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste sans encombre avec 1 roue restant sur le train d’atterrissage gauche. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni autre dommage à l’appareil.

C-FFTV, un Cessna 180 équipé de flotteurs en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le Lac Tozer, QC à destination du Lac des Iles, QC avec 1 pilote et 1 passager à son bord. Alors que l’appareil était en vol de croisière à environ 10 miles nautiques au nord-est de l'hydroaérodrome du Lac Beauregard, QC (CTN3), le moteur a connu des ratées. La puissance a été ajustée à la position maximale; et une panne moteur est survenue peu de temps après. Le pilote a effectué les procédures applicables en cas de panne de moteur et l'appareil a été configuré pour la descente en vue d'un atterrissage d'urgence. Le pilote a déclaré une urgence (MAYDAY) et a atterri sur un chemin forestier. Une fois au sol, le pilote s'est assuré que la balise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) émettait un signal et a utilisé son téléphone satellite pour aviser une personne responsable de la situation et fournir les coordonnées de l'emplacement où se trouvait l'appareil. NAV CANADA a été avisé, et ceux-ci ont avisé le centre conjoint de coordination des opérations de sauvetage (CCCOS) de Trenton. L'appareil a été localisé rapidement et les occupants ont été évacués vers le Mont-Tremblant.

C-FOAW, a privately registered Stinson SR9FM float-equipped aircraft, was taking off from an unnamed lake located 2 kms north of Unity, Saskatchewan with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the initial climb at approximately 300 ASL, the engine (P&W R985) power began to degrade and the aircraft could no longer climb. The pilot then maintained an easterly heading to try and assess the issue. The aircraft began loosing altitude and the pilot began a forced landing procedure. The aircraft landed in a farm field approximately 6 Kms NE of Unity, Saskatchewan and flipped over onto its back. Both occupants evacuated the aircraft without injury and the aircraft sustained substantial damage. The engine was never shutdown.

C-FUJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP Mitsubishi CRJ-900, was conducting flight JZA7132 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Halifax/ Robert L. Stanfield Intl. (CYHZ), NS.  During cruise over Watertown Intl. (KART), NY, the flight crew declared an emergency in US airspace due to pressurization issues.  Flight landed in CYHZ without further issues.

C-GZAY, a Beechcraft A35 Bonanza, was conducting circuits at Cooking Lake, AB (CEZ3) with only the pilot on board. While executing a final approach and landing, the pilot did not extend the landing gear, and performed an unintentional gear up landing. The aircraft came to a stop on the runway. There were no injuries, and there was no fire. The aircraft sustained damage to the fuselage, wing flaps, propeller and engine exhaust.

C-GIOM, a privately registered Cessna 185F amphibious aircraft was conducting a takeoff at the Thunder Bay (CKE6), ON, water aerodrome with only the pilot on board. During the initial takeoff run and prior to getting onto the step, the bow of the right float dug into the water and the aircraft overturned. The pilot was able to egress the aircraft using the left cabin door. The aircraft did not sink and the pilot hung onto the floats until rescue arrived. The pilot was not injured and the aircraft sustained substantial damage. It was reported that all landing gear were retracted and that the lake does contain dead-heads. The weather conditions at the time of the occurrence were clear with a light breeze and glassy water conditions.

C-FNDY, un Piper PA-22 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis l'aérodrome de Joliette, QC (CSG3) avec un élève pilote et un instructeur à son bord. Lors de l’atterrissage, qualifié de dur, l'élève pilote a perdu le contrôle directionnel de l'appareil et l'instructeur n'a pu en reprendre le contrôle afin d'éviter une sortie de piste. L’appareil a terminé sa course, renversé, dans un fossé et a subit des dommages importants. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-IJUB, un Paratour SD-2 en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) depuis un champs situé à 1.8km au sud-ouest de l'aéroport de Montmagny, QC (CSE5). Lors du décollage par vents faibles, lors de la montée intiale, le pilote a perdu le contrôle du l'appareil en tentant d'éviter des arbres. L'appareil a percuté le sol et un incendie s'est déclaré. Le pilote a subi des blessures mortelles.

C-GOBI, un Ultravia Pelican de construction amateur en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC), avec un pilote à bord. L'appareil a effectué plusieurs orbites dans la zone de contrôle de St-Honoré et les appels des contrôleurs de la tour avec celui-ci sont demeurés sans réponse. Comme il était impossible de communiquer par radio avec l'appareil, celui-ci a été considéré comme étant NORDO. Afin d'éviter les conflits possible, les appareils se trouvant dans la zone de contrôle ont reçu l'instruction de dévier. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait à environ 2.6 nm à l’est de CYRC, celui-ci a percuté le sol. L’appareil a été détruit et le pilote a subi des blessures mortelles.

On 14 June 2020, a privately operated Cessna 172M aircraft (registration C-GEDC, serial number 172-65285) had departed Arnprior Airport (CNP3), Ontario, with the pilot and 3 passengers on board, for a daytime visual flight rules (VFR) flight in the local area. A privately operated Champion 7GCB aircraft (registration C-FPTR, serial number 149), equipped with floats, had departed Golden Lake, Ontario, for a daytime VFR flight to Constance Lake, Ontario. Only the pilot was on board. Both aircraft were flying along the Ontario side of the Ottawa river, at approximately 1500 feet above sea level. At 1447 EDT, both aircraft collided while flying over the river near Buckhams Bay, approximately 12 NM east north-east of CNP3.The Champion aircraft sustained damage to the tail, entered a descending left hand spiral, impacted the water and overturned. The pilot egressed from the aircraft and was rescued from the water by nearby boaters. The pilot received minor injuries. The emergency locator transmitter from the Champion aircraft activated. There was no fire. The Cessna aircraft sustained damage to the propeller, nose wheel fairing and engine cowl. The pilot of the Cessna saw the Champion aircraft impact the water, flew a few orbits to confirm that the other pilot had been rescued and then flew back to CNP3 without further incident.

C-FIAH, a Springbank Air Training College Cessna 172, was conducting a local training flight at Springbank, AB (CYBW) with a student pilot on board. The student pilot was practicing circuits on Runway 26 and on the 4th or 5th circuit, was intending to conduct another touch and go exercise when during the landing, the aircraft began to bounce/porpoise on the runway. As the bounces occurred, the aircraft drifted to the right side of the runway, and the aircraft departed the runway surface, ultimately coming to a rest in the ditch beside the runway. There were no injuries; however, the aircraft sutained damage to the forward fuselage.

C-FRWT, a privately operated Piper PA-24 Comanche, was conducting a VFR flight from Vernon, BC (CYVK) to Fairview, AB (CEB5) with only the pilot on board. During the downwind leg for landing in CEB5, the pilot extended the flaps and selected the landing gear down. Unbeknownst to the pilot, the landing gear did not extend, and a gear up landing was unintentionally performed. There were no injuries, but the aircraft sustained damage to the propeller and the lower aircraft fuselage. Subsequent investigation revealed that the landing gear electric circuit breaker was tripped. The aircraft was raised, the circuit breaker reset and the landing gear was subsequently extended.

N725FD, a FedEx Airbus 300B4-622R, was conducting flight FDX 140 from Memphis Intl. (KMEM), TN to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB.  At approximatly 170nm from CYYC, the flight crew declared an emergency with ATC due to hydraulic issues. The flight landed without further issues.

C-GSLX, Sunwest Aviation Ltd. Beech 1900D, was operating as flight CNK448 from Conklin / Leismer (CET2), AB to Lac la Biche (CYLB), AB with 2 crew on board. While on initial approach over the lake, the aircraft struck a Pelican at 1500 feet above ground. There were no handling or system anomalies and the aircraft continued to an uneventful landing. A post flight inspection revealed significant damage to the right wing inboard leading edge.

C-FYAG, a Fairchild SA227-DC, operated by Perimeter Airlines LP as flight PAG1000, departed Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG) MB, for St. Theresa Point (CYST) MB. When the aircraft was approximately 20 nm NNE of Winnipeg, the aircraft experienced a failure of the nose down pitch trim. The flight crew were able to control the aircraft and retuned to CYWG. The aircraft landed safely.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and found a pitch trim actuator had failed. The actuator was replaced, and the aircraft was successfully test flown and returned to service.

C-GSAF, a Fairchild SA227-DC, operated by Sunwest Aviation Ltd as flight CNK302, departed Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG) MB, for Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. When the aircraft was approximately 70 nm west of Winnipeg, the flight crew observed the right engine torque was indicating 120 percent (Garrett TPE331-12UHR-7) and observed torque fluctuatiuons between 80 and 120 percent. When the flight crew made power lever movements, the EGT and fuel flow decreased and the torque decreased initially to 80 percent then increased to above 120 percent. The right hand engine was shutdown as a precaution, the flight crew declared an emergency, and requested a return to CYWG. The aircraft landed safely and taxied to the ramp.The operator's maintenance found a defective torque bridge sensor. The engine is equipped with two internal torque sensors and the connector was connected to the second torque bridge sensor. Ground runs were completed and the aircraft was retuned to service.

The Air Canada Airbus A320-200, C-FMSX, was operating as flight ACA329 from Montreal, QC (CYUL) to Edmonton, AB (CYEG). During final approach, the flight crew received an ECAM BRAKES (Auto Brake) fault. A missed approach was conducted. The flight crew actioned the QRH and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed without incident and the flight crew used alternate braking. Company maintenance found an unserviceable brake servo valve, which was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FAPH, an amateur built, Davis DA-2A, was flying circuits for runway 33 at the Brampton-Caledon Airport (CNC3) ON. During the downwind turn on the third circuit, the engine began to lose power. The pilot elected to turn towards the nearest runway threshold, which was runway 15. The pilot landed the aircraft in a plowed field north of the airport perimeter fence, the nosewheel sheared off and the aircraft overturned following touchdown. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was not injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

On 06 June 2020, Cessna 172M (registration C-FCCV), operated by International Flight Centre Inc., was conducting a local training flight from Boundary Bay Airport (CZBB), BC, with 1 student and 1 flight instructor onboard. At 13:12 Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), the aircraft disappeared from radar over the Fraser River at approximately 11 NM ESE of Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC. The aircraft was last recorded travelling eastbound at an altitude of 200 feet above water with a ground speed of 80 knots. The aircraft remains missing and the fate of the crew is unknown; the RCMP is leading the search.

The Air Tindi Beech King Air 200, C-FCGU, was operating as flight TIN502 from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Edmonton, AB (CYEG). While en route, the flight crew noticed the landing gear in-transit light was illuminated. While assessing the situation the flight crew observed the main landing gear doors open followed by the landing gear starting to lower. The flight crew reduced airspeed and selected landing gear down as a precaution to prevent the loss of hydraulic pressure. The landing gear was confirmed down and locked. The flight crew declared an emergency and returned to CYZF. The aircraft landed without further incident. Company maintenance replaced the hydraulic landing gear system pressure switch. The system was ground tested and flight test satisfactorily and the aircraft was released for continued service.

The pilot of a corporate registered Cessna 525A (registration N21RA) on route from Oshawa, ON (CYOO) to Sault Ste Marie, ON (CYAM) declared an emergency shortly after departure due to a fuel pressure issue. The pilot shutdown the right engine (Williams, FJ-44), returned to Oshawa and landed without incident.

C-FDOS, un Beech A100 exploité par Exact Air Inc., effectuait le vol ET824 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis le Poste Montagnais, QC (CSF3) à destination de l'aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait en croisière vers CYRC, le voyant de la pompe hydraulique s'illuminait par intermittence. L'équipage a tiré le disjoncteur de la pompe afin d'éviter qu'elle surchauffe. Quelques minutes plus tard, les voyants "Gear Unsafe" se sont illuminés; l'équipage a sélectionné le déploiement du train d'atterrissage et le train est partiellement sorti. La pompe s'est éteinte et les voyants de transition sont restés allumés. L’équipage a effectué la procédure d’extension manuelle du train d’atterrissage avec succès. L'équipage a ensuite déclaré une urgence et demandé la priorité. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre à 1602Z. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés. Le personnel de maintenance a diagnostiqué une défaillance de la pompe hydraulique.

C-FMST, un Cessna 310R exploité par Grondair Aviation, effectuait un vol d'entrainement selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR), depuis St-Frédéric, QC (CSZ4) à destination de St-George-de-Beauce, QC (CYSG) avec un instructeur et un élève pilote à bord. Après avoir effectué un atterrissage simulant une panne de moteur à CYSG, l'aéronef a décollé et effectué un circuit en préparation pour un deuxième atterrissage; cette fois avec les 2 moteurs. Lors de l'atterrissage la queue de l'appareil a frappé le sol, suivi des hélices et l'appareil a glissé sur le ventre le long de la piste. La course s’est terminée approximativement à 300 ft après le point d'impact et légèrement à droite de l’axe de piste avec de la fumée cabine. Le train d'atterissage était en position rentré au moment ou l'aéronef a été dégagé de la piste plus tard en soirée. Il n'y a pas eu d'incendie, de déversement de carburant ou d'huile. Il n'y eu aucun blessé.

C-FTAR, un Aérospatiale ATR-72-202, exploité par Morningstar Air Express pour le compte de FEDEX, effectuait le vol MAL8069 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX) à destination de l'aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, à une altitude d'environ 12 000 pieds, le voyant ''Excess CAB ALT'' s'est illuminé. L'équipage a alors cessé la montée, une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée et l'appareil est descendu à une altitude de 10 000 pieds. Le commandant de bord a alors réalisé que la porte de documents du poste de pilotage n'était pas complètement fermée. Une fois la porte bien fermée, la pression de la cabine est devenue normale et l'équipage a annulé l'urgence. L'équipage a poursuivi le vol vers CYQB ou l'appareil a atterri  sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.La liste de vérification préenvol a depuis été modifiée pour inclure une double vérification de la porte de documents.

The privately registered, amateur-built, Rans S7 Courier, C-GHIK, was on a round robin flight itinerary from Fort St. John (CYXJ) British Columbia northwest bound into the mountains to check out some remote airstrips. The first leg took the aircraft to a strip called Cypress Creek Airstrip where the pilot dropped off some fuel for the return trip. He then proceeded 20 minutes northwest into the mountains to a meadow. After overflying the landing area to assess the field, a successful landing was conducted. The pilot got out of the aircraft to stretch his legs and then re-boarded for departure. The taxi to the departure end of the strip was normal. The aircraft turned around and accelerated down the strip. After rotation the wind blew the aircraft from right to left across the strip into an area that had 3 foot high willow bushes along the left side of the strip. The tires began to contact the brush and as the aircraft moved along the willows got taller. The aircraft began to slow until it could no longer sustain flight. The willows snagged the landing gear resulting in the aircraft flipping forward on to its back and coming to rest in a snow bank. The pilot shut down the engine and closed all fuel valves. The pilot was using a 4 point safety harness and a helmet; he sustained no injuries. The pilot made contact with family and friends using a satellite communications unit (Garmin inReach) and in turn, the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre was notified.

C-GIQK, a Swearingen SA226-TC operated by Perimeter Aviation LP., was conducting flight PAG13 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Oxford House (CYOH), MB. When the flight was approximately 50 nm southeast of CYTH the flight crew noticed a haze of smoke in the cockpit. The flight crew donned oxygen masks and carried out QRH functions for smoke in the flight deck. The flight crew notified ATC and elected to return to CYTH. An emergency was not declared and the flight crew declined ARFF services. The subsequent landing was uneventful. The operator's maintenance personnel found no evidence of a fire or source of smoke. Further inspection found the environmental system water-separator housing full of water. A drain tube was replaced. The #1 and #2 cooling turbine water separators were removed, cleaned, and re-installed.

C-FYKR, an Air Canada Airbus 319-100, was operating as flight AC992 from Mexico city/Benito Juarez Intl. (MMMX), Mexico to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl.(CYYZ), ON. During the takeoff run, Flight crew noticed left hand engine surge around 60-70kts.  Flight Crew rejected take off and taxied to the gate.  There was no injury and no emergency declared.

C-FKCJ, a Boeing 757-200 operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd, was conducting flight CJT920 from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky Intl (KCVG), KY to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. On initial climb, the left engine rolled back and was shut down. ATC was advised and it was requested for ARFF to meet the aircraft and assess for any damage. The flight has landed back in KCVG. There was no injuries. Maintenance is assessing potential engine damage.

C-FHIJ, a float-equipped Cessna 180 operated by Pacific Seaplanes, was conducting student solo circuits near Hudson Island, BC with one pilot on board. During the 4th landing roll, the aircraft briefly became unstable and the right wing tip contacted the water. The aircraft taxied to the shore without further incident. There were no injuries. The ELT did not activate. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the right wing structure and aileron.

An unregistered Airborne Windsports basic ultralight departed in the vicinity of Wapella, SK for a local flight.
