Approximately 200 yards from the takeoff point, the ultralight collided with powerlines at approximately 120 feet AGL. The RCMP contacted TSB and reported that the pilot had minor injuries and he was being transported to the hospital for further examination.

C-GMTY, a YMF Waco F5C aircraft, was landing on Runway 24 at the Chatham-Kent airport (CYCK), ON with an 8 knot 40 degree left crosswind. During the landing rollout the tail began to oscillate and the pilot lost directional control of the aircraft. The aircraft ground looped to the left collapsing the right main landing gear. The right wing was damaged and the there was a prop strike when the main gear collapsed. There were no injuries to the 3 occupants on board.

C-FKTG, a Zenair STOL CH-701 advanced Ultra-light aircraft, landed at Oshawa, ON (CYOO) and approximately halfway down the runway on the rollout the main landing gear collapsed. The aircraft came to rest on the runway there were no injuries.

C-GXAI, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-300 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE4812 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Ivujivik, QC (CYIK) à destination de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) avec 3 membres d’équipage et 2 passagers à bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en descente vers CYVP, l’équipage de conduite a remarqué une indication de fuite graduelle de liquide hydraulique du système #2. Par mesure de précaution, et pour assurer la disponibilité des services d’urgence lors de l’atterrissage, l’équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN). L'équipage a effectué une extension normale du train d’atterrissage et l’appareil s’est posé sur la piste sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-GPAL, a de Havilland DHC-8-102 operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting a flight from Oxford House (CYOH), MB to Thompson (CYTH), MB. Approximately 50 nm southeast of CYTH, the aircraft experienced a loss of hydraulic pressure on the number 2 hydraulic system. The crew conducted the appropriate QRH items and declared an emergency with Thompson FSS. The aircraft subsequently carried out an uneventful landing at CYTH.A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed a failed nose gear hydraulic hose. The hose was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

The flight crew of a NorthStar Air Douglas DC-3 aircraft, (registration C-FWUI), equipped with turbine engines, was backtracking on Runway 35 at Kapuskasing, ON (CYYU). As the flight crew attempted to turn around at the end of the runway; the right brake seemed soft and not responsive. They attempted to slow the aircraft down with reverse power and braking, which caused the aircraft to swerve to the left, and go off the edge of the runway. While attempting to turn around on the grass, the left main wheel dug in and the aircraft became stuck. The flight crew shut down the engines and radioed for assistance. The aircraft was unloaded and pulled back onto the runway.

C-GEHS, a Beech 200 aircraft operated by Provincial Aerospace, was conducting flight SPR810 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) to Sydney/J.A. Douglas McCurdy Airport, NS (CYQY). During the approach to CYQY the crew lowered the landing gear and noticed a nose gear unsafe condition. At approximately 15:07 AST, the crew conducted an overshoot and elected to return to CYHZ. The crew declared an emergency at 15:40 AST and ACC advised the Rescue Coordination Center and CYHZ Airport Rescue Firefighting (ARFF). The aircraft landed uneventfully at 16:15 AST with ARFF standing by. One aircraft was delayed for approximately 15 minutes before it could land.Maintenance examined the aircraft NLG system and determined that the nose gear down lock switch had failed. They installed a new switch, completed several successful landing gear swings and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FBVJ, a Cessna 172K aircraft, was landing on the grass strip at Alexandria, ON (CNS4), when control of the aircraft was lost. The aircraft went into the ditch by the runway breaking off the nose landing gear. The pilot was not injured; the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

N702DN, a Boeing 777-200LR operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL3343 from Frankfurt/ Rhein-Main (EDDF), Germany to Chicago O'Hare (KORD), IL. While the flight was in cruise at about 60 nm NNE of Moncton/Roméo LeBlanc Intl. (CYQM), NB, the first officer became incapacitated. The captain summoned the relief first officer and together they performed first aid, including the use of an automated external defibrillator (AED), to stabilize the first officer. The captain declared a MAYDAY, requested a diversion to the nearest airport, and was cleared to CYQM. The flight landed at CYQM without further incident and the first officer was transported for medical treatment.

C-FPIL, a Zenair STOL CH701 advanced ultra-light aircraft, was returning to Pembroke, ON (CYTA), after a local flight and landed hard. The nose gear collapsed causing a prop strike and the aircraft came to a stop on the runway. There was no injuries, but the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GTBK, a privately registered Piper PA-22-160X, was operating a VFR flight from St. Theresa Point (CYST), MB to Bloodvein River (CZTA), MB. Upon landing on Runway 18 at CZTA, the aircraft swerved and contacted rough ground and a runway light. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to its right wing and empennage. It was reported that there was mud on the runway that may have lead to the aircraft's left brake to seize on landing.

C-GIQK, a Swearingen SA226-TC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP., was conducting medevac flight PAG13 from Oxford House, MB (CYOH) to Thompson, MB (CYTH). While in cruise to CYTH, the left-hand wing-overheat warning light illuminated. The crew performed the checklist items in the AFM and notified ATC of the issue. Following the checklist the wing overheat light extinguished and did not re-illuminate for the remainder of the flight to CYTH. The flight crew informed ATC of the event, declared a PAN PAN and landed the aircraft safely.The operator's maintenance discovered a bleed air leak at the bleed air line/ turbine cooling fan attach point. The aircraft was repaired and returned to service.

C-GFKA, a Pilatus PC-12/45 aircraft, operated by Air Bravo, was instructed to climb and maintain 14000 ft approximately 60 nm north of Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. C-GFKA was observed climbing through 14000, and did not respond to several calls from the controller.  As the aircraft reached 14400 feet, the flight crew responded and acknowledged 14000 feet. Separation was not maintained with a passing Fox Flight Learjet 36A C-GIFF. Separation was reduced to 800 feet and 4.1NM where 1000 feet or 5NM are required.

LX-VCL, a Boeing 747-800 aircraft operated by Cargolux International, was conducting flight CLX7416 from Guadalajara/Don Miguel Hidalgo Y Costilla Intl. (MMGL), MX to Luxembourg-Findel Intl.(ELLX), LU. Upon entering the Gander Flight Information Region, the crew made a PAN PAN call due to a medical emergency. A relief crew member was becoming progressively ill. The crew requested and were cleared direct to Gander Intl (CYQX), NL. The aircraft landed uneventfully on RWY 21 at 1755UTC. Emergency Health Services met the aircraft on the ramp and transported the relief crew member to the hospital. The aircraft departed CYQX the following day.

C-ILQJ, a privately operated basic ultralight, Kangook, RS Ultra (powered paraglider) was conducting a recreational flight approximately 4.5 nm N of Gibbons, AB. During the approach to a farmer's field, prior to touchdown, a go-around was performed. During the go-around the aircraft encountered turbulence and the canopy partially collapsed. Control was lost and the paraglider struck the ground. The pilot was fatally injured.

C-GFJZ, un CL-600-2D24 (Series 900) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8831, effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC à destination de Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl.(CYYZ), ON avec 12 passagers et 3 membres d'équipage. Peu après avoir passé Ottawa en croisière, l’équipage a demandé un retour vers CYUL en raison de fumée dans la cabine. L’équipage a ensuite déclaré une urgence. Une fois en finale pour la piste 06 droite à CYUL, l’équipage a demandé la présence d’ambulances à son arrivée et a mentionné la possibilité de faire débarquer les passagers sur la piste. JZA8830 s’est posé sans encombre à 10:29 UTC et est resté sur la piste jusqu’à 11:10 UTC. Les passagers sont restés à bord et les services d’urgences ont inspecté l’intérieur de la cabine et vérifié l’état des passagers. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil a circulé jusqu’au terminal avec les passagers à bord. Il n’y a pas eu de fumée visible par contre une forte odeur de feu électrique était présente. Un ballast d’éclairage dans la cabine est à l’origine de l’odeur, il a ensuite été remplacé par le département de maintenance.

C-FAFR, a Fairchild SA227-AC operated by Carson Air Ltd, was conducting a cargo flight from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Kelowna (CYLW), BC with 2 flight crew members onboard. During descent into CYLW, the crew observed a hydraulic pressure annunciator light with a corresponding low pressure indication. The crew followed the emergency checklist, advised CYLW tower of a hydraulic failure, and requested ARFF on standby. The crew lowered the landing gear manually and carried out a flapless landing without incident. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft. Maintenance found the right hand hydraulic pump return line was chaffed through at the hydraulic reservoir. The rigid return line was temporarily replaced with a flexible line as per the AMM and the hydraulic system was ground tested satisfactory.

C-FKKN, an Air Tractor AT-401B agricultural aircraft operated by Western Canadian Aerial Ltd. was on approach to Runway 04 at Neepawa (CJV5), MB, with only the pilot on board. During the landing roll, the pilot lost directional control and the aircraft ground looped to the right. The aircraft came to rest on the runway in an upright position. The pilot was not injured and the aircraft sustained substantial damage.  It was reported that the tail wheel began to shimmy on touch down.

C-GARX, a Robinson Helicopters R-66 aircraft operated by Valley B Aviation, was conducting heli-slinging operations approximately 90 nm NE of Fort Saint John, BC (CYXJ) with one crew member on board. As the aircraft approached the remote work site, the long line and load (sheets of plywood) unexpectedly released from the helicopter. The pilot subsequently landed at the site to inspect the aircraft, which revealed no damage. The pilot took off and returned to the maintenance base for further examination. There was no damage to equipment on the ground, or any injuries.Subsequent examination by maintenance revealed that the routing of the manual release cable on the belly of the aircraft to be incorrect, which did not provide enough slack in the cable and subsequent hook movement resulted in the unintentional activation of the manual load release. Maintenance rerouted the cable, function checked the system and released the aircraft for service.

C-GJPL, un appareil de construction amateur de type Cyclone 180 sur flotteurs en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol récréatif local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à destination du lac Ouareau près de St-Donat, QC avec 1 pilote à bord. Le pilote effectuait le premier vol après le remisage de l'hiver. Avant le départ, il a drainé ses réservoirs d'essence et a circulé sur le lac pendant une quinzaine de minutes avant de décoller. Après 10 minutes en vol, le moteur a commencé à perdre de la puissance et s’est arrêté. L'avion se trouvait à environ 600-700 pieds AGL et le pilote a effectué un amerrissage d’urgence droit devant lui sur la rivière Ouareau entre le lac Blanc et le lac Archambault. Lors de l’amerrissage, une aile aurait frappé des branches et l’avion a piqué du nez dans l'eau peu profonde. Le pilote a été retenu par sa ceinture de sécurité à 4 points n’a subi aucune blessure et a pu évacuer l'appareil pour se rendre au rivage. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée. L’appareil a subi des dommages substantiels.

C-FEUR, an ATR72-200 aircraft operated by Summit Air was conducting flight 7311 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Island Lake (CYIV), MB. with a crew of 2 on board. During the initial climb out of CYTH, the crew selected the landing gear up but the gear would not retract. The crew declared an emergency and returned to the airport where the aircraft landed safely. An inspection of the system by the operator's maintenance personnel revealed a chaffed electrical wire.

C-GRID, a McDonnell Douglas Helicopter 369E (500E) operated by BI-Air Application Services Ltd. was en-route from Blackfoot, AB. to Buffalo Narrows, SK. with only the pilot on board. While in cruise at approximately 1500 feet above ground level, the engine (Allison 250-C20B) began to loose power and the helicopter started to loose altitude. The pilot immediately began an autorotation procedure and forced landed the helicopter in wooded area. The pilot evacuated the with a minor injury and the helicopter sustained substantial damage. The pilot walked to a clearing and used his personal GPS device to track his location. The pilot was then picked up by JRCC. The helicopter's 406 ELT did activate and was shut off by the pilot before he left the accident site. There was no post impact fire.  Subsequent inspection of the helicopter’s fuel system revealed an excessive amount of water.

C-FEMT, a Learjet 45 aircraft, was on final approach for runway 23 at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. The flight crew advised that they needed to go around due to an unspecified mechanical issue. Subsequently, a manual gear extension was carried out, which indicated down and locked; the flight crew requested aircraft rescue and fire fighting services (ARFF) on standby for their arrival. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GDOW, a privately registered amphibious-equipped Found Brothers FBA-2C1, was operating from Fort Frances Municipal (CYAG), ON to an unnamed lake located approximately 40 nm north of CYAG with the pilot and one passenger on board.  During the initial touch down on landing at the unnamed lake, the aircraft bounced and then overturned during the second touch down on the water. The pilot and passenger were able to evacuate the aircraft without injury and clung to the aircraft floats. The aircraft eventually drifted to shore where the two occupants walked to a cabin and called for help. It was reported that the landing gear was retracted. The winds were strong and gusting and the water surface conditions were choppy with large waves.

C-GSAE, a Beech B200 of Province of Saskatchewan Ministry of Central Services, was conducting Air Ambulance operations from Lloydminister (CYLL), AB to Saskatoon (CYXE), SK. Shortly after departure from CYLL and while climbing through 4000 feet ASL the flight crew heard a loud thump and the aircraft began shuddering. Using the wing de-ice inspection lighting, the flight crew was able to identify some damage to the left wing and assumed the aircraft struck a bird. The flight crew decided to return to CYLL and arranged a visual approach with the Area Control Center. An emergency was not declared. The aircraft returned to CYLL and landed uneventfully. There were no injuries. The aircraft received significant left wing leading edge damage due to a bird strike.

C-GSKW, un Beech 1900C exploité par Skylink Express, effectuait le vol SLQ738 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Mirabel (CYMX), QC  à destination de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl. (CYQB), QC  avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Au décollage de CYMX, l'équipage a détecté de la fumée dans le poste de pilotage et a noté que le disjoncteur du circuit d'alimentation des volets s'était déclenché. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et l'aéronef est retourné à CYMX ou il a atterri sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.L'équipe de maintenance a subséquemment découvert une surchauffe du moteur des volets vraisemblablement causé par le vérin de volets extérieur droit. Le moteur et le vérin en cause ont été remplacés.

C-GKCK, a Bell 412EP helicopter, operated by AOG Spa was conducting a fire fighting activity in the vicinity of Limache, Valparaiso Province, Chile with 2 crew members on board. The helicopter was performing water pick up with a bambi bucket in the Lliulliu reservoir, which is at 800 feet above sea level, when it crashed in the water. There were no injuries and the helicopter was substantially damage. According to premiminary information received, the weather was not a factor and there was no mechanical problems on the aircraft. The authorities are conducting an investigation.

C-GIAB, un De Havilland DHC-8-314 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE4802 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Kuujjuarapik, QC (CYGW) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 15 passagers à bord. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait à 8 nm en approche finale à GYGW, lors de la sélection du train d'atterrissage à la position baissée, la quantité de liquide hydraulique dans le système numéro 2 est descendue à 1 pinte. L'équipage a effectué une remontée et une urgence (PAN PAN) a été déclarée. L'équipage a dérouté vers l'aéroport de la Grande Rivière, QC (CYGL) avec la train en position baissée. L'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre à 1552z.

C-ILGM, a Quad City Challenger II, advanced ultra-light aircraft, departed the Midland/Huronia Airport (CYEE), ON and was flying in the vicinity of Port Severn, ON when it crashed into Georgian Bay. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, received fatal injuries.

VH-OEF, a Quantas Airways Boeing 747-438, was operating as flight QFA76 from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Sydney/Kingsford Smith (YSSY), Australia. QFA76 was instructed to line-up on Runway 08R by Tower South/Scan (TS) and the flight crew advised a 30 second engine run-up was required prior to takeoff. The aircraft proceeded onto Runway 08R and started the engine run-up procedure. C-FZUL, an Air Canada A319-114, was operating as flight ACA557 from Los Angeles Intl. (KLAX), CA to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC. ACA557 was approximately 5.9 NM for the ILS CAT III approach to Runway 08R when QFA76 was cleared for takeoff and commenced the take-off roll. The separation was reduced with ACA557 at approximately 2.8 miles final to Runway 08R when QFA76 overflew the LOC antenna for Runway 08R. ACA557 proceeded with the approach and landed without incident. A loss of separation occurred as per the Vancouver Tower Unit Operations Manual (UOM) and Manual of Air Traffic Service (MATS) Tower/ACC stating a departing aircraft has to pass overhead of the localizer site before the next CAT II/III arriving aircraft is at 4 NM final.

C-FIUV, an Air Canada Boeing 777-333ER was conducting flight AC 2286 from Shanghai/Pudong Intl. (ZSPD) China to Tokyo/Narita (RJAA) Japan. While loading cargo at ZSPD using APU power, the APU auto shutdown and the crew followed the QRH.  After all requirements were met, the crew attempted to restart the APU and shortly thereafter, the ground crew member ran into the flight deck to advise of possible sparks and/or flames exiting the APU.  The Crew had received no fire warning in the flight deck; however, the APU fire bottles were discharged and a Mayday was declared with ATC.

C-GZVJ, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways LP., was conducting flight WSG1480 from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON to Wapakeka (CKB6), ON. Shortly after departure the flight crew noted illumination of the left engine low-oil-pressure annunciator, accompanied by a slowly decreasing oil-pressure indication. The flight crew decreased the power of the left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-67D) and conducted the engine shutdown procedure. The flight crew elected to return to CYXL where a successful landing was conducted with the left engine inoperative. The aircraft was shutdown on the taxiway and then towed to the apron. The operator's maintenance personnel repaired a leak in the oil supply line to the torque pressure transmitter and inspected oil filter, screens, and chip plugs.

C-FGCP, un De Havilland DHC-8-100 exploité par Chrono Jet Inc. sous l’indicatif MBK810, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Schefferville, QC (CYKL) à destination de Montréal/Saint-Hubert, QC (CYHU). Environ 20 minutes après le décollage, 4 lumières d’avertissement du tableau de bord se sont allumées (RUD PRESS, ROLL SPLR INBD HYD, #1 RUD HYD and RUD FULL PRESS). L’équipage a effectué la procédure inscrite au manuel de référence rapide (QRH), a déclaré une urgence auprès de l’ACC et a demandé d’être dérouté vers l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre. Le service de la maintenance a identifié qu'un bris de ligne hydraulique du moteur #1 s'était produit.

On 28 April 2020, the Buffalo Airways Ltd. Beechcraft King Air A100 aircraft (registration C-FCBZ, serial number B-116) was conducting charter flight BFL666, under instrument flight rules, from Cambridge Bay Airport (CYCB), Nunavut, to Kugaaruk Airport (CYBB), Nunavut, with 2 flight crew members and freight on board. At 1350 Mountain Daylight Time, during the hours of daylight, the aircraft landed at CYBB on Runway 23. Immediately after touchdown the aircraft veered to the right and departed from the runway surface. The aircraft came to rest after colliding with a snowbank on the northwest side of the runway. The crew, who were not injured, egressed the aircraft via the main cabin door. There was no fire, but the aircraft sustained substantial damage. The 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter did not activate.

C-FBRH, un Cessna 337G exploité par MAG Aerospace Canada Corp effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Sudbury, ON (CYSB) à destination de Val-d’Or, QC (CYVO). Lors de son atterrissage sur la piste 18, une rafale de vent a contribué à faire rebondir l’aéronef sur la piste. Suite au rebond, l’aéronef a touché durement le sol ce qui a provoqué l’affaissement du train d’atterrissage avant causant le heurt de l’hélice au sol. L’aéronef s’est immobilisé sur la piste. Le pilote seul à bord n’a pas été blessé. L’aéronef a subi des dommages importants. La compagnie a temporairement suspendu les vols de ses autres Cessna 337G afin de procéder à une inspection détaillée des trains d’atterrissage avant et aucune anomalie n’a été rapportée.

C-FPSI, un Jetstream32 exploité par Pascan sous l’indicatif PSC581 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination des Îles-de-la-Madeleine, QC (CYGR). C-GTAQ, un Dash-8-300 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l’indicatif JZA726, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Durant la montée initiale, PSC581 a avisé le contrôleur qu’il devait retourner atterrir à CYQB. Le contrôleur a donc fourni à PSC581 des vecteurs radar à suivre afin de le guider et de le positionner derrière JZA726 en approche pour CYQB. Malgré que PSC581 a suivi les vecteurs assignés, ceux-ci n’ont pas permis de conserver l’espacement requis de 3 milles nautiques latéralement et 1000 pieds verticalement avec JZA726. Au minimum, les distances latérale et verticale sont descendues à 2.7 milles nautiques et 100 pieds.

C-GLTO, a Top Aces Inc. Dassault-Dornier Alpha jet was conducting a fighter training mission with German Air Force from Wittmundhafen (ETNT), Germany.  During approach to ETNT, the right hand main landing gear down and locked light remained extinguished while all other indication showed normal.  The approach was discontinued and landing gear was inspected by another company Alpha jet.  Emergency was declared as precaution and visual approach was conducted.  At approximatively 3 miles final, the right hand main landing gear indicated safely down and locked until touch down were indication again disappeared.  The airplane landing was uneventful.  Company's maintenance is investigating.

N640AE, un Embraer ERJ-145LR exploité par Piedmont Airlines sous l’indicatif PDT5011, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Philadelphie Intl, PA (KPHL). N762QS, un Bombardier Challenger 350 exploité par Netjets sous l’indicatif EJA762, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Bedford/Laurence G Hanscom Field, MA (KBED). PDT5011 a été autorisé à décoller de la piste 06R. Le contrôleur a par la suite instruit EJA762 de s’aligner sur la piste 06R avant de l’autoriser à décoller. Une fois décollé, EJA762 avait une vitesse-sol supérieure à PDT5011 ce qui a réduit l’espacement latéral entre les 2 aéronefs à 2.2 milles nautiques au plus près alors qu’un espacement de 3 milles nautiques était requis.

C-FAVT, a Bell 407 operated by Canadian Helicopters Limited, was conducting company water bucket training over the NW corner of Skaha Lake, BC, with 2 pilots onboard. During the first water load, the pilot flying (PF) in the left seat attempted a water release test without success. The PF asked the pilot not flying (PNF) in the right seat to verify functionality of the water release system and the PNF depressed the cargo release button. The water bucket was released from the cargo hook and landed on the lake. There was no damage to people or property from the release, and there was no damage to the equipment.Maintenance confirmed all the aircraft systems were operating correctly. The aircraft does not have a water release on the left seat cyclic controls due to aircraft modification for NVG training.

The amateur-built Sorenson 282 amphibious float-plane, C-GTET, was on a local flight out of Cooking Lake (CEZ3), AB when the engine, (Teledyne Continental TSIO-550-E) experienced a loss of power at approximately 2500 feet AGL. The pilot attempted a forced approach on to TWP road 524 between RR212 and RR213. Once on the road the pilot had to swerve to miss a car that entered the roadway from a private drive. The left wing struck a tree and the aircraft entered the ditch. There was substantial damage to the aircraft including the floats sheering off, and the wing being displaced to the point there was a resultant fuel leak. There was no ELT signal detected. There were no injuries to the pilot who was the sole occupant.Update: The owner/pilot had installed a new fuel sight gauge and was calibrating the system. When he ran the right fuel tank dry the engine lost power. He switched to the left tank which had 50 liters of fuel in it and for unexplained reasons the engine would not restart. When the owner checked the fuel distribution manifold there was fuel present.

C-FRJZ, a Gulfstream G-100 aircraft conducting Latitude Air Ambulance flight 5059 flight,  was landing at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON on Runway 23. With winds 210 at 12 gusting to 18 knots the aircraft flared and the right wing dropped requiring full left aileron to level the aircraft. The aircraft landed without further incident.A post flight maintenance inspection noted a scuff mark on the right wing tip. The flight crew were not aware that the right wingtip had contacted the runway during the right wing drop. Latitude Air Ambulance reviewed the flight data recorder information and no abnormalities were observed in any system and all systems checked serviceable on the ground. Latitude suspects turbulence from the gusty conditions caused the wing drop. There was no damage to the aircraft structure other than the paint scuff on the wing tip.

The privately operated Cessna 182P, C-FJFO, was 5.1 nautical miles north east of Tofield (CEV7), AB in the Beaver Hills training area when it experienced a bird-strike on the inboard section of the right wing leading edge. Damage was substantial and after a systems check a PANPAN was declared with Edmonton Center. An immediate diversion was undertaken to Cooking Lake(CEV3), AB where a uneventful landing was performed. The emergency was closed out via cell phone. On inspection by an aircraft maintenance engineer it was determine that the damage was severe with six wing ribs crushed and upper and lower wing skin deformation. It is also suspected that the spar, fuel bladder, and flight control cables are damaged. Early assessment indicates a requirement for a complete right wing replacement with ancillary repairs.

N3333U, a Bombardier BD-700-1A11 (Global 5000) owned by Wilmington Trust Company Trustee, was conducting a flight from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to Tokyo International (RJTT), Japan, with 4 crew members and 4 passengers onboard. During cruise flight at approximately 35 NM east of Port Hardy (CYZT) and FL398, the right hand cockpit windshield cracked. The crew declared a PAN PAN and performed an emergency descent to 12 800 ft as per ATC instructions. The crew followed the QRH and verified the cabin pressure remained stable when the aircraft passed through FL200. The crew cancelled the PAN PAN on return to CYVR and performed a 90 minute fuel burn. The aircraft landed safely with no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft.A third party maintenance vendor has been contacted to replace the windshield.

C-GAVH, a Bell 206L-1 helicopter operated by Custom Helicopters Ltd., was conducting slinging operations from St. Theresa Point (CYST), MB to Wasagamack, MB. While en route the cargo net, with contents, was inadvertently released approximately 1.5 nautical miles north-west of CYST. The net and contents were retrieved. The contents of the cargo net were substantially damaged. The operator is investigating the cargo hook and the type of switch that controls the cargo hook release.

C-GVRC, a privately registered Pegazair-100 ADAC aircraft, was conducting a local fight from Oak Hammock Air Park (CAV9), MB with only the pilot on board. On the downwind leg the pilot selected carburetor heat between mid and 3/4 travel. While turning from base leg onto a final approach for Runway 36 the pilot selected full carburetor heat. The engine power began to falter after reducing power from 2000 rpm to 1500 rpm. There was no throttle response and the engine (Teledyne Continental Motors O-200) stopped a few seconds later while the aircraft was roughly 200-300 feet above ground level. The pilot checked that the fuel tank was selected "on". Carburetor heat was "on". Magnetos were on "both". The pilot maintained control and conducted a forced landing into a field approximately 0.5 nautical miles from the runway. After the 3 point touchdown the aircraft decelerated rapidly due to the soft, muddy terrain. The tail rose and the aircraft overturned and came to rest inverted. The pilot was uninjured and was able to exit the aircraft. The pilot signaled to people at the airport and returned to the aircraft to shut of the fuel and electrical system. EMS responded to the scene and evaluated the pilot. The aircraft sustained damage to the wings, cowling, tail, and a wing strut. The aircraft was recovered back to the airport.At Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) the temperature and dew point were reported to be 15 C and 3 C respectively at 1900 UTC, shortly before the occurrence.

C-FNOH, a Boeing 787-9 operated by Air Canada was conducting flight AC2287 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Hong Kong International (VHHH), Hong Kong. Approaching VHHH, the flight crew were cleared to waypoint LOTUS for an ILS approach Runway 25L. When the aircraft arrived over LOTUS, the flight crew contacted Air Traffic Controller (ATC) and reported being established on the ILS. ATC advised the flight crew to change to the tower frequency. Just after, ATC observed the aircraft overshooting the localizer of Runway 25L and descending to 3900 feet above sea level (ASL), which is below the minimum sector altitude of 4300 feet ASL. ATC provided a terrain warning to the flight crew and the flight crew corrected the flight path to re-intercept the ILS Runway 25L. The aircraft landed at VHHH without further incident.The flight crew reported receiving a false capture of the ILS Runway 25L and being visual with terrain and the airport during the event. The operator is conducting an internal assessment in accordance with their safety management system (SMS).

C-FITU, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada as flight ACA2236, was conducting a flight from Tokyo/Narita Intl. (RJAA), Japan to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. During cruise the flight crew received EICAS message “TIRE PRESSURE”. The flight continued to CYYZ and a PAN PAN was declared. The aircraft landed without incident. ARFF met the aircraft on arrival, inspection was carried out and aircraft taxied to gate.

C-GOPW, a Canadian North Inc. Boeing 737-200, was operating as flight MPE228 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Kugluktuk (CYCO), NT with four flight crew and 4 passengers on board. During the initial climb on departure from CYZF, the flight crew smelled and then observed smoke on the flight deck. It was suspected to be associated with the captain's side window heat plug. The QRH was actioned and when power was removed from the window heat, the smoke dissipated. The flight crew declared an emergency and returned for a landing in CYZF with ARFF standing by.Maintenance identified a faulty window heater.

N227GJ, a Dassault-Breguet Falcon 50 operated by Black Falcon LLC, was conducting a flight from Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, to McCarran International (KLAS), NV, with 2 flight crew and 4 passengers onboard. The pilot applied engine power to initiate a climb to cruising altitude and the #3 engine (Garrett TFE731) experienced a contained internal failure. There was no fire indication and the aircraft returned to CYVR. Tower placed ARFF on standby and the aircraft landed without incident. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft.   A third party maintenance vendor from the USA replaced the engine and the aircraft returned to the USA.

C-GTOG, an Anderson Air Cessna C-680 Sovereign, was conducting flight from Palm Spring Intl. (KPSP), CA to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. During cruise, a light jolt was felt followed by a high pitched whining sound and shortly thereafter a ENG VIBRATION R EICAS (engine indicating and crew alerting system) message. After completing the applicable checklist, the decision was made to shut down the right hand engine and divert to Boeing Field/King County Intl. (KBFI), WA. A Mayday was declared initially and downgraded to a Pan Pan.  Aircraft landed without further issues.

C-FKZI, a privately registered ski-equipped Cessna 185, was departing from the frozen lake surface on McMurray Lake, MB. At the point of rotation, the pilot heard an abnormal noise. The pilot elected to place the aircraft back onto the ice surface to access the potential issue before continuing to destination. On touchdown, the right landing gear ski broke at the gear box and collapsed; causing substainal damage to the aircraft. The pilot and 1 pax did not sustain any injuries.

C-GYSK, a Convair CV340/580 aircraft operated by the Province of Saskatchewan/Northern Air Operations, was conducting a local flight as TKR475 from Prince Albert/Glass Field (CYPA), SK with 2 crew members on board. While joining downwind in the circuit, the flight crew noted an issue with the right engine propeller. The flight crew actioned the checklist, shut down and secured the right engine, declared an emergency and returned to airport. The aircraft landed safely with emergency services standing by. No impact on operations.The operator's maintenance identified that the control valve of the propeller controller unit had failed. The control valve was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

Morningstar Air flight MAL7056, a Cessna 208 B (C-FEXX), was halfway between Sudbury (CYSB), ON and Timmins (CYTS), ON when the pilot noticed the engine (PRATT & WHITNEY-CAN, PT6A-114A) torque indicator was stuck at 1400 psi. On approach to CYTS the pilot declared a PAN PAN due to the faulty torque indication. The aircraft landed without incident. Maintenance determined the torque gauge was faulty and replaced it with a serviceable unit.

C-GBIT, a privately registered amphibious Cessna 208, was conducting a flight from Lloydminster (CYLL), SK to Maurice Lake, SK. During the landing roll onto an ice strip at Maurice Lake, the aircraft began to drift to the left. The left wheel struck a three foot windrow bordering the ice strip. The aircraft sustained extensive damage; there were no injuries to the two occupants onboard.

Air Canada flight ACA403, an Airbus A319 (C-FYJI) aircraft, was on final approach to Toronto LBPIA (CYYZ) when the flight crew received a "LANDING GEAR NOT DOWNLOCKED" ECAM message. The flight crew executed a go-around, declared a PAN PAN and carried out the alternate gravity extension of the landing gear. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GGOF, un Dash-8 Q400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8732, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Québec Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC avec 65 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Pendant le vol un membre du personnel de la cabine a subi une incapacité physique. Le deuxième membre du personnel de la cabine a assigné un passager à la surveillance des sorties de secours à l’arrière de l’appareil pour l'atterrissage. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre à destination. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-FSKA, a Beech A100 aircraft operated by Kississing Lake Lodge, was on a local flight at the Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with a crew of 2 and 1 passenger on board. While on final approach to Runway 36 at CYWG, the crew extended the landing gear and received a nose gear unsafe indication. Following an emergency gear extension, the unsafe gear indication remained. The crew conducted a fly-by the tower to assess the gear position. The nose gear appeared down and an emergency was declared. Prior to touchdown, the crew shut down both engines and the aircraft then landed safely.

C-GKNR, a Sikorski S92 operated by Cougar Helicopters was on an IFR flight from St. John’s International, NL (CYYT) to the Hebron Oil Platform (CHBR) at 7000 feet ASL. The aircraft was 150 NM East of CYYT when the INLET #1-A-ICE FAIL illuminated along with the Master Caution light. The crew referred to the Emergency Check List (ECL) and reset the INLET #1 A-ICE. The INLET #1-A-ICE remained in a failed state. Due to the light icing experienced in cloud and a PIREP from a company aircraft inbound from the Hebron area the crew elected to return to CYYT. The crew contacted Gander ACC, declared a PAN-PAN, and requested clearance to CYYT at 2400 feet ASL. The aircraft remained in cloud and icing so the crew cancelled IFR and descended to 900 feet ASL where they were clear of cloud and icing. The aircraft conducted a VFR approach and landed safely in CYYT.Maintenance determined that the #1 Engine Inlet required replacement.

C-GXHK, a Piper PA-31-350 operated by Kisik Aerial Survey Inc, departed Nanaimo (CYCD), BC, to conduct survey work north of Lillooet (CYLI), BC, with 1 pilot and 1 survey operator on board. At approximately 26 nautical miles north-northwest of CYLI, the right  engine (Avco Lycoming TIO-540-J2BD) lost power and the pilot-in-command (PIC) secured the engine. The aircraft diverted to CYLI and performed a single-engine approach and landed without incident. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft. The pilot found the right hand inboard fuel cap was not correctly secured and the fuel tank contained approximately 1L of fuel despite the gauge indicating one quarter (approximately 53L). Maintenance replaced the right hand inboard tank inboard fuel sensor and conducted a fuel system inspection for condition, leaks, and operation. A successful ground run was completed, and the aircraft flew back to base at Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC.

C-FXXH, un appareil de type Cessna A185E sur roues-skis en exploitation privée, avec à son bord 1 pilote, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aérodrome de St-Mathias (CSP5), Québec à destination de Neuville (CNV9), Québec. Lors de la course au décollage, 40 à 50 pieds après que la roue de queue se soit soulevée, une rafale de vent traversier a fait tourner l’avion vers la gauche. Le pilote a coupé la puissance afin d’interrompre le décollage. L’avion est sorti de piste et le pilote a aperçu un fossé devant lui. Constatant que sa vitesse était trop élevée pour pouvoir arrêter avant celui-ci, il a remis pleine puissance afin de tenter de passer par-dessus puisqu’il y avait un champ après. Le ski droit a passé par-dessus, mais le ski gauche a frappé le bord du fossé. L’avion est tombé à plat et a subi des dommages importants. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. La radiobalise d’urgence ne s’est pas déclenchée.

C-GHBB, a privately operated Eurocopter 120B aircraft, was conducting a leisure flight with 3 persons on board, departing from Fort Langley (CBQ2), BC. The helicopter was the first of three helicopters planning to visit Thomas Crater, BC, 39nm N of Abbotsford Airport (CYXX). On approach to the landing area, the pilot surveyed several options. He selected a location that would allow the other two aircraft to land nearby. The aircraft touched down on the snow and stabilized. The pilot began to "pump the collective", in order to solidify the helicopter into the snow, however the LH landing gear skid broke through the snow. A dynamic rollover ensued and the helicopter came to rest on its left side with substantial damage. One person received minor injuries. The ELT did not activate.

C-GTCJ, a Cargojet Airways Ltd Boeing 757-223, was operating as flight CJT926 from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International (KCVG), USA, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 2 flight crew onboard. During approach to CYVR, Flap 1 was selected that resulted in a trailing edge flap disagree message on the Engine Indication and Crew Alerting System (EICAS). The flight crew requested a hold to complete the checklist. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed without incident. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft. The aircraft had 2 previous flap disagree incidents on 17 March 2020 (TSB A20P0037) and 25 March 2020 (TSB A20O0034). Maintenance adjusted the left hand and right hand slat position transmitters as per the Fault Isolation Manual and carried out the system operational checks with no faults found.

Bearskin Airlines flight BLS377, a Fairchild SA-227DC aircraft (C-GJVW), was on route from Sault St. Marie (CYAM), ON to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON when the right engine (GARRETT, TPE331-12UHR) fire lights illuminated. The flight crew performed the emergency procedures, shut down the engine and declared an emergency. The aircraft continued to Thunder Bay and landed without incident.No evidence of fire was detected during inspection, maintenance are investigating the cause of the fire indication.

C-FMGC, a privately operated Beechcraft B200GT aircraft, was conducting a flight under instrument flight rules from Saint John Airport (CYSJ), NB to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. On approach to CYHZ the crew selected the landing gear down; and the landing gear indication did not change nor did it move from the up position. The crew conducted a missed approach and communicated the condition to CYHZ tower. The crew followed the QRH for landing gear failure and conducted a manual landing gear extension, which successfully lowered the gear. The crew then received landing clearance from CYHZ tower and requested that emergency services standby. The aircraft landed at CYHZ without further incident.Maintenance personnel replaced a landing gear control relay to rectify the fault.

N908EV, a Bombardier CRJ200 operated by Skywest Airlines, was conducting flight SKW5493 from San Fransisco Intl. (KSFO),CA to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB with 3 crew members and 29 passengers on board. During the descent into the greater CYYC area, the flight crew were configuring the aircraft for landing and selected "FLAP 8". They immediately received a "FLAP FAIL" caution message. The approach was discontinued and the captain declared an emergency with ATS. The flight crew completed the appropriate QRH procedures, briefed the flight attendant, made the passenger announcements, and proceeded to an uneventful flap 0 landing in CYYC. There were no injuries.

C-FGWJ, a Boeing 737-700 operated by WestJet Airlines, was operating as flight WS112 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 5 crew members and 21 passengers on board. During the enroute portion of the flight, flight attendant #2 experienced a medical condition and was unable to perform the duties required. The captain was advised of the situation, and flight attendant #2 duties were distributed between the remaining flight attendants for the remainder of the flight. An uneventful landing was completed. EMS met the aircraft at the gate, assessed and subsequently released flight attendant #2.

C-GGFP, un Dash 8-400 exploité par Air Canada Jazz effectuait le vol JZA7977 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Toronto City/Billy Bishop, On (CYTZ). Lors de la montée initiale au départ de CYUL, suite à la sélection du train d'atterrissage à la position rentrée, le train s'est initiallement placé à la position rentrée; suivi peu de temps après par une extension non commandée de celui-ci. L’équipage a effectué la procédure d’extension manuelle du train d’atterrissage avec succès. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'équipage a demandé un retour à CYUL ou l'appareil s'est posé sans encombres. Le tableau de commande du train d'atterrissage a été changé et l'appareil a été remis en service.

C-FENO, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par WestJet Encore, effectuait le vol WEN3538 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC, avec 21 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en descente vers CYUL, le voyant « mistrim left wing low advisory light » s’est allumé. L’équipage a déconnecté l’autopilote et ils ont constaté que les commandes de vol étaient très raides. Ils ont tiré sur le levier de déconnexion du roulis, les contrôles du commandant sont devenus libres et ceux du premier officier sont demeurés raides. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) associée et une urgence a été déclarée. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GQCA, an Airbus A320-211 operated by Air Canada, was conducting a flight from Los Cabos International (MMSD), Mexico, to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC, with 5 crew members and 110 passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff, the flight crew received the HYD G RSRVR LO LVL message on the Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitoring (ECAM) system indicating a failure of the green hydraulic system. The flight crew consulted with Maintenance Operations Control (MOC) and elected to continue the flight to the destination. Prior to arrival, Air Canada dispatch contacted tower at CYVR and advised the aircraft would not be able to exit the runway due to the loss of nose wheel steering. Tower initiated emergency standby with ARFF and the aircraft landed without incident. The aircraft was towed off the runway. There were no reported injuries and no damage to the aircraft. Maintenance replaced the green hydraulic system leakage measuring solenoid valve and carried out the decontamination procedures on the environmental control system (ECS) as per the AMM due to hydraulic fluid ingestion.

C-FAJC, a Bombardier Challenger 300 operated by Aurora Jet Partners, was conducting flight from Kelowna Intl. (CYLW), BC to Denton Enterprise (KDTO), TX. During initial approach ILS Runway 18, shortly after being vectored on a 190 heading, Flight crew experienced a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) ‘'descend descend’’. Flight crew complied with RA. Flight landed without further incident.

C-IAAE, a privately operated basic ultralight, Bushcaddy R80, equipped with Full Lotus FL1260 amphibious floats, was conducting flights following maintenance (propeller pitch adjustments) approximately 16.5 nm WSW of the Edmonton International Airport (CYEG), AB. Following a successful maintenance flight the pilot landed back at the private snow covered field and picked up the owner of the aircraft to take him for a flight.  The aircraft just cleared the power line and trees at the end of the 2700 foot field used for the take-off.  Shortly after clearing the power line and trees the aircraft departed controlled flight and impacted the ground.  The pilot and passenger both received non-life threatening injuries. The aircraft was approximately 15% over the maximum take-off weight indicated on the Transport Canada aircraft register.

Flair Airlines flight FLE134, a Boeing 737-400 (C-FLHJ) was on final approach to Toronto /LBPIA (CYYZ) Runway 24R, when a master caution illuminated and a number of indications were lost, including: hydraulic, engine, electrical, flight control, and pneumatic. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and determined that it was only indication problems. The aircraft landed on Runway 24R without further incident, taxied clear of the runway, and had the aircraft inspected for hydraulic leaks.

Air Creebec cargo flight CRQ651, a Hawker Siddeley HS-748-2A (C-FLIY) aircraft, departed Timmins, ON (CYTS) and climbed to 9000 feet after departure. Due to icing conditions, the flight crew elected to climb on top of cloud layer, at 11,000 feet. Shortly after leveling off, the first officer, who was the pilot flying, felt ill and transferred control to the captain. The captain decided to turn back to CYTS. After landing, the first-officer seemed to feel better. No emergency was declared.

The separation between PSA Airlines flight JIA5698, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (N557NN) and Air Canada flight ACA447, an Embraer E-190-100 (C-FLWE) dropped to 2.3 NM, in airspace that requires 3 NM, while both flights were on base for RWY 23 at Toronto LBPIA (CYYZ), ON. The controller re-established separation and there was no further operational impact.

Flightexec flight QG5MLI, a Gulfstream G-200 (C-GRST), departed London (CYXU), ON and was climbing through FL230 when the "Master Caution" illuminated and CAS displayed "R BLEED AIR". The flight crew notified ATC and levelled off, after which the QRH checklist was completed. The flight crew decided to not shut down the affected engine; an emergency was declared and the flight was cleared back to CYXU. The flight crew informed ATC that they had to dump fuel and were told to dump while over the Lake Erie area. During the fuel dump process the "R BLEED AIR" indication went away. Subsequently the flight crew cancelled the emergency and returned to CYXU, and landed without furthur incident.

C-GZCZ, a Sunwest Aviation Ltd Gulfstream 150, was conducting flight from Scottsdale (KSDL), AZ to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB. During initial climb shortly after being vectored on a 260 heading, Flight crew experienced a TCAS RA (resolution advisory). Flight crew advised ATC and could not visually identify the traffic. Flight continued without further incident.

Cargojet flight CJT584, a Boeing 757-200 (C-GCJT) aircraft, was on the downwind for Hamilton International Airport (CYHM), ON and declared emergency due to flap issue. The flight crew, upon selecting approach flap, reported receiving a “flap disagree” message and the flaps were indicating between 0 and 1. The flight circled airport to conduct system checks then returned to land. Emergency equipment was requested. The flight landed in YHM without further incident and was met by the ARFF upon arrival as a precaution. There were no injuries or damage.This aircraft had same problem on the previous flight going into Vancouver (CYVR) on 17 March 2020 (TSB A20P0037) and maintenance were unable to duplicate the snag on ground. The aircraft was taken out of service. A verification flight was mandated upon rectification prior to placing it back in service. The aircraft carried out the verification flight on 22 March 2020 with no faults noted. Multiple components were inspected and replaced as a precaution. Maintenance is continuing to investigate the issue.

C-GFEH, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight SWG389 from Varadero /Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl. (MUVR), Cuba to Kelowna Intl (CYLW), BC. During cruise, a cabin crew became incapacitated and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight.  Order of priority for cabin crew was reassigned.  The flight landed uneventfully in CYLW.

C-FPCV, a Beech 1900C operated by Pacific Coastal Airlines, was conducting a flight from Victoria International (CYYJ), BC, to Prince George (CYXS), BC with 2 flight crew and 10 passengers on board. During climb at 18 400 feet, the forward cabin door annunciator illuminated in the cockpit. The flight crew confirmed the cabin pressure was holding, the door was latched, and the passengers were secure. The flight crew followed the QRH, declared a MAYDAY, and diverted to Vancouver International (CYVR), BC. ARFF was on standby and the aircraft landed without incident. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft. The door functioned normally for deplanement at the gate. Maintenance replaced a corroded sill switch, cleaned the main connector, and released the aircraft back into service.

The WestJet Boeing 737-800, C-FUMF, was operating as WJA1516 from Calgary, AB (CYYC) to Pheonix, AZ (KPHX). Shortly after takeoff from CYYC, the cabin crew notified the captain that there was an acrid smell in the cabin. The flight crew declared an emergency and diverted to return to CYYC. WJA1516 landed uneventfully on Runway 35L. The aircraft stopped on the runway, where it was met by ARFF. After ARFF determined that there were no signs of smoke or fire, the aircraft returned to the gate. Company maintenance inspected the aircraft and found no smell of fumes. The aircraft was serviced by maintenance the previous night, including an engine borescope inspection.

C-GTSO, an Airbus A330 was operating Air Transat flight TSC560 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QB, to Cancun Intl. (MMUN), Mexico. While on cruise FL400 60NM north of PSK VOR, the flight crew initially received a TCAS TA (traffic advisory) caused by an opposite traffic followed 10 seconds later by a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) ''climb''.  Flight crew climbed to 40700 feet and later descended back to FL400 after receiving ''clear of conflict'' message and completed TCAS company procedures.

C-GXTB, a Pilatus PC-12/47 aircraft operated by North Star Air Ltd., was conducting flight BF704 from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON. On final approach to CYXL the flight crew selected the landing gear down but did not receive a down and locked indication. The flight crew performed two flybys and the landing gear was observed to be extended. The flight crew declared an emergency and conducted the "Main Landing Gear Unlocked" checklist as per the QRH Emergency checklist. The subsequent landing was conducted safely and the flight crew shut down the engine on the runway. The passengers deplaned and the aircraft was towed to the apron. The operator's maintenance personnel replaced the left main-landing-gear down-lock switch and conducted successful landing gear retraction tests.

The Sunwing Airlines Boeing 737-800 aircraft (SWG374, C-FJVE) was on climb out from Sault Ste. Marie (CYAM), when the flight crew received a Fuel Imbalance Alert for the right tank. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and the aircraft levelled off at FL270. The crew initiated the fuel imbalance checklist and determined that the Crossfeed Valve was open. The checklist was completed and the fuel was allowed to balance the loads in the tanks. The flight continued to destination without further faults.

C-FFNC, a Boeing 737-406 aircraft operated by First Air Inc., was conducting flight FAB152 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU. While on approach to CYRT, the flight crew received an indication warning of a flap asymmetry condition. There was no roll associated with the warning and the flight crew initially elected to divert to Churchill (CYYQ), MB. During the diversion the flight crew decided to return to CYRT due to more favourable weather conditions. An emergency was not declared; however, the flight crew requested ARFF to inspect the aircraft after landing. The subsequent landing was conducted without further incident with ARFF standing by. The operator's maintenance personnel replaced the flap position transmitter.

N576FE, a McDonnell Douglas MD-11F aircraft operated by Federal Express, was conducting flight FDX5986 from Anchorage International Airport, Alaska, USA (PANC) to Memphis International Airport, Tennessee, USA (KMEM). During cruise the flight crew received a "Level 1 - battery discharge alert". At approximately 30nm south of Swift Current, SK (CYYN) and after serveral attempts to trouble shoot the battery issue, the crew elected to divert to Great Falls International, Montana, USA (KGTF). The crew declared an emergency and landed the aircraft in KGTF without further incident.The operator's maintenance found a defective shunt in the battery charging circuits.

C-GRGO, a de Havilland DHC-8-106 aircraft operated by Canadian North Inc., was conducting flight MPE656 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Kugaaruk (CYBB), NU. During the descent through 10 000 feet ASL smoke began to appear in the cockpit. The flight crew donned masks and followed QRH procedures. The smoke quickly cleared from the cockpit. The flight crew declared an emergency and elected to divert to Gjoa Haven (CYHK), NU. The flight crew requested ARFF and the subsequent landing was conducted without further incident. The passengers deplaned safely. There was no evidence of fire and the operator's maintenance personnel are investigating.

C-FYAG, un Fairchild SA227AC exploité par Perimeter Aviation LP sous l’indicatif PAG907, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) pour un vol local afin d’effectuer des tests en vol. Après avoir volontairement fermé un moteur, l’équipage n’a pas été en mesure de le redémarrer. L’équipage a donc demandé d'être redirigé vers Montréal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX) où il a déclaré une urgence. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-GXCA, un Beech 1900D exploité par Chrono Aviation inc. sous l'indicatif NDL191, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Timmins (CYTS), ON à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC avec 18 passagers et 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Environ 35 minutes avant d’atterrir, le commandant de bord (PIC) s’est senti mal après avoir terminé son repas. À ce moment, le premier officier (FO) était le pilote aux commandes et le PIC assumait les fonctions de pilot surveillant (PM). Peu de temps après, le PIC est tombé inconscient. Le FO a contacté le contrôleur aérien pour l’informer de la situation et a déclaré une urgence. Quelques minutes plus tard, le PIC a repris connaissance. L’avion s’est posé sans encombre à CYQB et le PIC a été transporté à l’hôpital en ambulance.

C-GWEN, a De Havilland DHC-8-402 operated by WestJet Encore Ltd, was operating as flight WEN3108 from Terrace (CYXT), BC, to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC, with 4 flight crew and 30 passengers on board. At approximately 60 NM ESE of CYXT, the crew received an aft baggage smoke indication in the cockpit. The QRH procedure was followed and the fire bottles were discharged. The aft baggage smoke indication remained visible in the cockpit. The flight crew declared an emergency and the aircraft returned to CYXT. The aircraft landed safely and an emergency evacuation was conducted on Runway 15/33. ARFF gained access to the aft baggage compartment and found no evidence of fire. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft. Maintenance replaced the aft smoke detector in the baggage compartment due to damage found on the casing and the guard. An SDR was submitted with Transport Canada.

C-GBHZ, un Airbus A319-114 exploité par Air Canada Rouge LP sous l’indicatif ROU1651 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Miami, FL (KMIA) à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Alors que l’aéronef était en approche finale à 3000 pieds, l’équipage a ressenti des vibrations et entendu de fortes détonations provenant d’un moteur. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et s’est posé sans encombre. Aucun dommage apparent n’a été rapporté par l’équipe de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs lors de l’inspection au sol une fois l’aéronef arrêté sur la piste. Celui-ci s’est ensuite déplacé sans autre problème jusqu’à la porte prévue pour le débarquement des passagers.

The WestJet Boeing 787-900 (Flight 658, C-GKKN) was on route from Calgary International Airport (CYYC) to Toronto /LBPIA (CYYZ), when the a flight attendant became ill and was removed from her duties. The aircraft continued to destination without further incident.

The Sunwest Aviation Learjet 35, C-GTJL, operating as CNK633 on a flight from Winnipeg (CYWG), MB to Edmonton (CYEG), AB was on a decent through 12 000 feet when the left hand engine (TFE-731-2-2B) started to lose power. The throttle was advanced to try and regain power but the engine power continued to decrease. As the engine continued to lose power the associated low oil press light came on and triggered the master warning. The crew declared a Mayday and asked for delaying vectors so they could run the associated checklists. Once the engine was secured the flight crew told ATC they could continue inbound for a single-engine approach and landing. ARFF was requested to stand by for the landing. The landing and taxi to the FBO happened without further incident.Update:  The engine was inspected and motored with no faults found. The digital electronic engine control (DEEC) had recorded the engine shutdown but there were no other indications of a fault. The aircraft had been over-wing refueled in Winnipeg (CYWG) MB by two trucks; one on each wing. The fuel request showd that additive was requested and both trucks were capable of providing the same. The aircraft was refueled after the maintenance checks in CYEG and engine test runs were undertaken with no faults found. The aircraft was then flown under a ferry permit back to Calgary (CYYC), AB for further investigation.

The WestJet Encore DHC-8-400 aircraft (WEN3461, C-GWUE) was on approach into Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ) when the flight crew initiated a go-around due to a FLAP POWER CAUTION light after selecting Flap 15. The flaps had remained at 10 degrees and did not reach selected position. The QRH procedures were followed and the caution light extinguished. During the second approach the caution light again illuminated, and the flaps stopped at 5 degrees. On the third approach the crew elected to continue with the landing with the flaps in the last position and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. Maintenance replaced the Flap Power Unit pressure switch IAW AMM 27-52-01-400-802. Subsequent operational tests revealed no further faults.

C-GGOF, un Dash-8 402 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l’indicatif JZA7960 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport, ON (CYTZ) à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL). Durant l’approche, l’équipage a perçu une légère fumée près du pare-brise du côté droit ainsi qu’une odeur de fils électrique brulé. Le système de chauffage du pare-brise a été éteint, ce qui a dissipé la fumée. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre.

C-FMAI, a Boeing 757-200 aircraft operated by Morning Star Express, was conducting flight MAL7050 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. During the approach into CYWG, the flight crew observed a "TE FLAP ASYM" EICAS message. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN PAN due to the asymmetrical flap indication and actioned the QRH. The aircraft subsequently landed the aircraft without further incident, and there were no injuries. After landing, the brake cooling chart was consulted and the aircraft was taxied to the ramp while being escorted by ARFF.

G-FKJZ, an Bombardier CRJ-900 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight Air Canada Express JZA8783 from Halifax Stanfield International Airport, NS (CYHZ) to Montreal Trudeau International Airport, QC (CYUL). When the landing gear was selected up just after take-off, the crew received a gear disagree message and the gear did not retract. The crew referenced their QRH and discussed with maintenance control and a decision was made to return to CYHZ. The crew requested ARFF be placed on standby. The flight landed without any further incident and the aircraft taxied to the gate.  Maintenance is currently assessing what was the cause of the disagreement message.

C-GSNM, a Beech E90 aircraft operated by SkyNorth Air Ltd. departed Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG) MB with a planned destination of Bloodvein River (CZTA), MB, with a crew of 2 and one passenger on board. During the initial climb, the crew noticed an odd smell accompanied by a haze in the cockpit and cabin area. The crew closed both bleed air valves and then noticed the #2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-28) oil pressure had dropped below 35 PSI. The crew then shut down the #2 engine and returned to CYWG. A mayday was declared and the aircraft then landed safely.An inspection of the #2 engine by the operator's maintenance personnel revealed an oil leak from the propeller governor secondary low pitch solenoid.

C-GGPU, a wheel-equipped Cessna U206G operated by 2320127 Ontario Inc. (dba Slate Falls Airways), was conducting a VFR flight from an ice strip at Sioux Lookout/Pelican Lake (CKA6), ON to Springpole Lake Mine, ON with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the flight, the oil pressure started decreasing but all other parameters, including oil temperature, remained normal. The pilot decided to climb from 3000 feet to 4500 feet ASL and to continue to the nearest suitable landing location which was the original destination. The pilot of C-GGPU was in contact with another company aircraft and advised them of the situation. The oil pressure continued to drop, eventually reaching 0 psi. Shortly after the pressure reached 0 psi, the engine (Teledyne Continental IO-550-F) failed. The pilot informed the other aircraft of the engine failure, declared a MAYDAY on 126.7 and performed a forced landing into a forested area near Jeannette Lake, ON. The pilot and passenger were uninjured. The pilot subsequently relayed their position by radio to the other company aircraft. The aircraft was substantially damaged and the ELT activated. The pilot and passenger were rescued by another company ski-equipped aircraft a few hours later.The operator's post-accident inspecton of the aircraft revealed the connecting rod to the #5 cylinder had exited through the crankcase and oil streaking was evident on the underside of the aircraft.

C-GGOK, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft was conducting Jazz Aviation LP flight JZA7963 from Montreal/Pierre Eliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC to Toronto Billy Bishop (CYTZ), ON  . During the approach, the flight crew received a low oil pressure indication on the number 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada, PW150A). The flight crew followed the QRH and shutdown the engine, declared a PAN PAN and diverted to Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ), ON. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FJZK, un Boeing 767-3Q8 exploité par Air Canada Rouge LP sous l’indicatif ROU1726, devait effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de l’aéroport international Pointe-à-Pitre Le Raizet en Guadeloupe (TFFR). En montée initiale, l’équipage a entendu un son sourd et a observé une élévation des vibrations d’un moteur. Le contrôleur aérien a fait part à l’équipage qu’il avait aperçu de probables flammes sortir du moteur gauche lors du décollage. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence, a fait demi-tour et s’est posé sans encombre. L’équipe de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) a été déployée et a inspecté l’aéronef sur la piste. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

C-GTMW, a privately operated De Havilland DHC-3T, was conducting circuits at Fort Langley (CBQ2), BC. During the second landing, the aircraft bounced and started an uncontrolled veer to the left. The aircraft departed the left side of the runway onto the adjacent ramp. The left wing tip contacted a parked trailer causing the aircraft to pivot left and impact a second trailer before coming to an abrupt stop. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. There were no injuries and no post impact fire. The ELT automatically activated and the signal was received.

C-GBJZ, a DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting IFR flight JZA584 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Saskatoon International Airport (CYXE), SK. C-GLVO, a Cessna 172 operated by Mitchinson Aviation Flying Service, was conducting a VFR training flight in vicinity of CYXE. During the circuit for Runway 27 in CYXE, C-GLVO reported to ATC that they had visual contact of JZA584 who was on the approach for Runway 27. Tower then instructed C-GLVO to turn base leg and, when C-GLVO turned base leg, JZA584 reported a TCAS resolution advisory (RA). The crew of JZA584 complied with RA directions and once the RA cleared, JZA854 continued the descent for landing. The aircraft were separated 400 feet vertically and 0.6 miles laterally at the closest point.

C-FFWM, un Airbus A320 exploité par Air Canada sous l’indicatif AC420, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport international Pearson de Toronto (CYYZ), ON à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC. Alors que l’aéronef circulait au sol pour se positionner près de la porte d’embarquement et de débarquement des passagers, le moteur droit (#2) s’est éteint par lui-même. L’aéronef a été mis hors service et l’unité de commande électrique (ECU) du moteur #2 a été remplacée.

C-GPSK, un Jetstream 32 exploité par Pascan sous l’indicatif PSC736, effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Wabush (CYWK), NL à destination de l’aéroport international Québec Jean-Lesage (CYQB), QC. Alors que l’aéronef était à 79 milles nautiques au nord-nord-ouest de Sept-Îles, QC, l’équipage a reçu une indication d’anomalie du système de prélèvement d’air du moteur droit. La liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée, le moteur droit a été fermé par mesure de précaution et l’équipage a déclaré une urgence. L’aéronef a dérouté vers l’aéroport de Sept-Îles (CYZV), QC où il a atterri sans encombre. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

C-GEZD, an Airbus A321-211 operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC742 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 6 crew members and 172 passengers onboard. Shortly after takeoff, the flight director (cabin crew) became incapacitated. The captain contacted Medlink, and the crew followed their recommendations and provided first aid. Another crew member assumed the role of cabin flight director and the flight was completed without incident.

N16183, un Embraer EMB-145XR exploité par CommutAir sous l’indicatif UCA4986 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC à destination de Newark (KEWR) aux États-Unis, avec 41 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage. Lors de la montée à environ 10 000 pieds, l'équipage a remarqué la présence d'émanations dans le poste de pilotage. Par la suite, l’équipage a mis leur masque à oxygène, a déclaré un état d’urgence et a demandé un retour à CYQB. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 06 sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en attente. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage. L'inspection de l'appareil a permis de déterminer qu'une fuite d'huile du moteur gauche (#1) était à l'origine du problème. Un vol de convoyage à destination de Albany (KALB), NY sera effectué afin d'effectuer une inspection plus approfondie.

N14143, un Embraer EMB-145XR exploité par CommutAir sous l’indicatif UCA4966 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC à destination de Newark (KEWR) aux États-Unis, avec 42 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, le système d'affichage des paramètres moteurs et d'alerte de l'équipage (EICAS) a généré un message de désaccord entre la position du levier de commande du train d’atterrissage en position rentré alors que le train d’atterrissage était demeuré en position sortie. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence, demandé un retour à CYQB et a complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH). L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 06 sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en attente. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GDUZ, un Boeing 767-375ER exploité par exploité par Air Canada Rouge LP sous l’indicatif ROU7096, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec uniquement 2 pilotes à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en montée, le système d'affichage des paramètres moteurs et d'alerte de l'équipage (EICAS) a diffusé le message « L AC BUS OFF ». L’équipage a demandé un retour à CYUL, a complété liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a déclaré un état d’urgence. Par la suite, la procédure a corrigé le problème. L'équipage a annulé l’état d’urgence et a choisi de procéder à la destination initiale de CYYZ. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre, il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni de dommage à l’appareil.

C-FYJE, an Airbus 319-114 operated by Air Canada Rouge was conducting flight ROU1890 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC to Phoenix Sky Harbor Intl. (KPHX), AZ. During cruise at FL390, Flight Crew identified increasing left hand engine (#1) vibration and spool back.  Flight Crew initiated QRH procedures, notified the ATC and declared a PAN PAN.  The flight descended to FL300 where the engine stabilized at 50% N1 and subsequently returned to normal operations.  The flight crew elected to divert to Denver Intl. (KDEN), CO as a precaution and the flight landed without further issues.

C-FYIY, un Airbus 319-114 exploité par exploité par Air Canada Rouge LP sous l’indicatif ROU1524, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON à destination de Fredericton (CYFC), NB avec 129 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage. En croisière, alors que l’appareil se trouvait à 77 miles marins au sud-est de Québec, QC, le moniteur électronique centralisé de bord (ECAM) a généré un message de faible quantité de liquide hydraulique du système vert. L’équipage a effectué une diversion à destination de l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC et a déclaré un état d’urgence. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 24 sans encombre, il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni de dommage à l’appareil.

C-FTXU, an Airbus A321 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC990 from Vancouver Intl airport (CYVR), BC, to Toronto Pearson airport (CYYZ), ON. While in cruise at FL330, 20nm west of Lethbridge (CYQL), AB, the aircraft encountered severe mountain wave turbulence resulting in a 700 foot altitude loss and speed variations approaching low and high speed limitations. The crew had to disconnect the autopilot to regain control of the aircraft in order to minimize altitude loss.The aircraft landed safely at CYYZ. Maintenance completed a severe turbulence inspection and the aircraft was released to service. There were no injuries reported.

C-GEZO, an Airbus A321 was operating as flight Air Transat TSC783 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL to Quebec/Jean Lesage Intl. CYQB), QB. During take-off roll at approximately 15 kts, Flight crew rejected take off due to loss of directional control.  The aircraft was brought to a full stop and flight crew declared a MAYDAY.  After assessment of the situation and inspection, flight crew taxied the aircraft to the ramp.

C-GCUL, a Canadian Utilities Dassault Falcon 7X, was conducting flight from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Washington Dulles Intl. (KIAD), DC.  During approach shortly after being vectored for runway 1C , Flight crew experienced a TCAS RA “Climb”. RA (resolution advisory) was actioned by flight crew and they advised ATC. Flight continued without further incident.

On 07 March 2020, at 0948 eastern daylight time, an Embraer 190-100 (E190), operated by Air Canada (registration C-FMZW) as flight ACA1037, was conducting a takeoff under visual departure procedures from Runway 06L. After the E190 began its takeoff roll, a Boeing 777-300 (B777), operated by Air Canada (registration C-FJZS) as flight ACA606, was instructed to position and hold onto Runway 06L. While the E190 was on the take-off roll, the Tower controller issued a takeoff clearance to the B777. Moments later, the E190 had a bird strike at approximately 135 knots. The E190 flight crew initiated a high-speed abort and made a radio call on the tower frequency that they were aborting the takeoff. As the E190 flight crew made their radio call, the B777 flight crew read back the takeoff clearance on the same frequency and commenced its takeoff roll. Shortly afterwards the B777 flight crew observed that the E190 was still on the runway and aborted the takeoff, reaching a maximum speed of about 110 knots. The B777 flight crew made a radio call on the tower frequency that they were also aborting the takeoff. Both aircraft exited the runway. The E190 returned to the terminal. The B777 waited on a taxiway for 45 minutes to allow the brakes to cool and then returned to the terminal. There were no injuries. There was no damage to either aircraft.
