C-GEFL, a Piper PA-24-250 aircraft, was on final approach to Runway 27 at the Burlington Executive Airpark when the aircraft reportedly encountered wind shear, and lost altitude; the right main lading gear contacted a short tree. The aircraft touched down short of the runway and the right gear contacted a concrete pylon, which spun the aircraft 180 degrees. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The pilot was not injured.

C-FIUW, an Air Canada flight AC001 Boeing 777-300 aircraft, was taxiing for departure from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Tokyo/Haneda (RJTT), Japan, when the flight crew noted a smokey smell. A pan pan was declared with ATC and ARFF was sent to meet the aircraft to assess the situation. The smoke was was coming from a forward galley oven that was turned on by cabin crew. The oven was turned off and the smoke dissipated, the aircraft returned to gate for clean-up without further incident.Maintenance removed the oven and ventilated the immediate area to remove residual burning odour. Galley power was re-established, and all other galley systems operated. No further smell or smoke were observed. The oven and controller were replaced, and operation checked serviceable.

C-GLCA, an Air Canada Boeing 767-300, was conducting flight AC984 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Cancún Intl. (MMUN), Mexico. During climb, flight crew experienced a TCAS RA “Level off level off”. RA (resolution advisory) was actioned by flight crew. Flight continued without further incident.

N612CZ, a Compass Airlines E175 conducting flight CPZ5778 from Seattle-Tacoma Intl (KSEA), WA to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC conducted a missed approach from the ILS 08L approach in CYVR due to birds. During the missed approach, Vancouver tower ATC did not provide missed approach instructions and N612CZ flew runway heading.  At the same time, C-GPCE, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Beech 1900D operating flight PCO551 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Williams Lake (CYWL), BC departed Runway 08R and an IFR loss of separation occurred. The published missed approach for ILS 08L initially instructs aircraft to climb to 420 feet on heading 083 degrees and then to conduct the climbing left turn to 3500 feet on heading 051 degrees.

C-GWRE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-400 was operating as flight WEN3289 from Saskatoon (CYXE), SK to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB with 4 crew and 68 passengers on board. While on departure from CYXE, as the landing gear was selected up, the nose landing gear door light remained illuminated. The flight crew requested to level at 5000 feet ASL to assess the problem. The landing gear was confirmed in the up position, the QRH was actioned and WestJet Encore maintenance was notified. It was decided to continue the flight to CYYC. While on approach to Runway 35R CYYC, the flight crew declared an emergency, the QRH was actioned for emergency gear extension and the aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. There were no injuries.Following the flight, maintenance replaced a proximity switch and the nose landing gear door actuator. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FNJZ a Jazz Aviation LP CRJ900 was conducting flight AC8839 from San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), CA to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR) BC.  Just after take off and gear retraction, the crew received a forward and rear smoke indication from the lavatories followed by reports of smoke in the cabin. Pilot declared an emergency and returned to KSFO. The passengers were evacuated on taxiway and there has been an initial report of a minor injury to a passenger. A bus was dispatched to pick up the passengers.

C-GPNL, a Canadian North Inc Boeing B737-36N operating as flight MPE1740 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Fort Mackay/Horizon (CYNR), AB with 5 crew and 129 passengers onboard departed RWY 35L on a heading of 360. Following MPE1740 was C-GJZF, a Jazz Aviation de Havilland DHC-8-402, operating as JZA8477 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Saskatoon (CYXE), SK with 3 crew and 34 passengers onboard took off and climbed on a heading of 335. A loss of separation occurred as JZA8477 closed the distance on MPE1740. Separation deteriorated to 25 degrees and 1.9 NM laterally where 30 degrees and 3 NM is required. Separation was regained without controller intervention when JZA8477 turned to a northeast heading.

C-GJVO, a Fairchild SA227-DC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation as Bearskin Airlines flight 312, departed the Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB. for Red Lake (CYRL), ON with a crew of 2 and 5 passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff, the crew received a fire warning indication on the right engine. The crew decided to shut down the engine and return to CYWG. An emergency was declared and the crew then completed a successful single engine landing. An inspection of the aircraft by the operator's maintenance revealed a faulty fire probe in the right engine bay area.

C-GJZG, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8236 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Terrace (CYXT), BC with 4 crew members and 77 passengers on board. The flight was held near CYXT for approximately 30 minutes due to winds, snow, and runway conditions before diverting to Smithers (CYCD), BC. After departure from CYCD the flight crew planned to conduct an approach at CYXT. While in descent through 14 000 feet ASL, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence causing a momentary loss of control. The aircraft's autoflight system disconnected and the flight crew noted large airspeed fluctuations. The flight crew decided to divert to CYVR. There were no injuries to crew or passengers. The aircraft was subsequently removed from service for inspection following severe turbulence, and no faults were found by the operator's maintenance.

C-FINA, a privately operated wheel/ski-equipped Piper PA-18-150, was conducting a flight from South Cariboo/108 Mile (CZML), BC to QUESNEL (CYQZ), BC with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During cruise, the aircraft encountered unexpected weather and the pilot elected to divert to Williams Lake (CYWL), BC. Prior to reaching CYWL, the aircraft encountered IFR meteorological conditions and the pilot made a precautionary landing in a field. On landing, the aircraft bounced due to rolling terrain and came to rest at a fence line. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

N73299 a United Airlines Boeing 737-824 was operating as flight UAL1965 from Denver Intl. (KDEN), CO to Calgary Intl.(CYYC), AB. While in the descent, the crew observed a stab out of trim indication. The crew accomplished the QRH, declared an emergency, and landed Runway 35R without further incident with ARFF standing by. There were no injuries.

C-GWWK, a Beechcraft 1900D operated by West Wind Aviation, was conducting flight WEW690 from Christina Lake (CCL3), AB to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK. During the approach into CYXE, the flight crew selected gear down and did not receive a nose gear down and locked indication. The flight crew requested an overshoot and entered into a hold to troubleshoot the landing gear system.The flight crew confirmed the gear lights were functioning, there were no warning horns, and no red light in the gear handle. The checklist was reviewed but no action was taken. After consulting with company maintenance, it was decided to pulled the landing gear relay circuit breaker and attempt to pump down the gear using the manual gear extension. WEW690 conducted a low pass to allow for a visual inspection of the gear. The gear appeared to be down and locked. An emergency was not declared, however, a request was made for ARFF to be on standby. The aircraft landed safely and taxied to apron. The operator's maintenance replaced the nose gear down position switch.

Jazz Aviation LP, flight JZA949, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 (registration C-GGNW) aircraft, landed at Toronto / LBPIA (CYYZ) on Runway 24L and was instructed by ATC to take a right turn onto D2 and then cross Runway 24R.  When the aircraft was approaching the holding position for Runway 24R the flight crew observed an Air Canada ERJ 190-100 (flight AC462, registration C-FMZB) departing runway 24R in front of them. AC462 had received clearance from ATC to depart Runway 24R, and was on the take-off roll. The flight crew of JZA949 queried ATC when they saw AC462 passing in front. NAV Canada is conducting an internal investigation.

C-GEZO an Airbus A321-211 operated by Air Transat flight TSC940 from Quebec Jean Lesage Intl. airport (CYQB) QC to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. airport (KFLL) FL responded to a TCAS RA while at 4000ft on approach for runway 10 in KFLL. The TCAS resulted in a 200ft climb and the aircraft returned to 4000ft immediately after.

C-GWRG, a Boeing 737-800 operated by WestJet Flight WS1864, from Vancouver Intl. Airport (CYVR) BC to Daniel K. Inouye Intl. Airport (PHNL) Hawaii USA experienced a medical incident during flight involving a flight attendant. The flight crew contacted Medlink. The duties were distributed among remaining cabin crew members.

N313FE, a McDonnell Douglas MD10 aircraft operated by Federal Express, was conducting flight FDX231 from Montréal/Mirabel (CYMX), QC to Memphis Intl. (KMEM), TN. During initial start for the #3 engine, the ground grew advised that flames could be seen coming from the engine. The crew shut off the fuel flow and the flames disappeared. Maintenance was called and carried out an inspection following which the crew attempted a second start. Again flames were seen coming out from the engine. The crew discharged the fire extinguisher bottle and asked for assistance from aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) services. After investigation, the operator’s maintenance confirmed that the engine had not been dry motored after the first start attempt, resulting in a fuel accumulation that caused the fire during the second start attempt. Maintenance replaced the fire extinguisher, the aircraft tested serviceable and was returned to service.

C-GFFT, a Learjet 45 operated by Flightpath Charters Airways Inc. was on an IFR flight from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Quebec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC. Upon touch down on Runway 06, the crew experienced high wind gusts and white out visibility. The aircraft drifted slightly into the right runway strip of Runway 06, and came into contact with a number of Runway Edge Lights during rollout. Inspection of the aircraft revealed that the right landing gear door suffered slight damage as a result of contact with the light fixtures.

C-FIVS, a Boeing 777-300 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC737 Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), CA. During the approach, flight crew leveled at 6000’ on vectors for FMS bridge visual to TRDOW. A TCAS TA (traffic advisory) for traffic at 6500' was received and ATC advised to descend. Flight was down through 5000' when they received TCAS RA (resolution advisory), flight 400' above. No action taken as traffic was already in descent and meeting what the RA was advising. Flight continued without further incident.

C-GPAT, an Airbus 310-300 operated by Air Transat, was preparing for flight TSC462 with a departure from Quebec/Jean Lesage airport (CYQB), QC to Punta Cana International Airport (MDPC) in the Dominican Republic. During boarding, one of the cabin crew members became ill and was unable to continue duties. The cabin crew member was provided with medical assistance. Positions were reassigned among the other cabin crew members and the flight operated with 6 cabin crew members, instead of 7; 6 being the minimum cabin crew complement on the A310.

C-GAQX an Airbus A319-114 flight AC574 operated by Air Canada from Vancouver Intl. Airport (CYVR) BC to San Francisco Intl. Airport (KSFO) CA, experienced a TCAS RA at waypoint CORKK on approach for KSFO. The crew had a visual on traffic and climbed 1000 feet and advised ATC. Continuing with the approach, the aircraft was high and fast causing a missed approach to be carried out resulting in a flap overspeed of 5-10 knots. The aircraft landed in SFO without further incident.

C-GPVS, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight SWG630 from Ottawa/ MacDonald Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON to Varadero /Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl. (MUVR), Cuba. At top of climb, flight attendant became incapacitated and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight.  Order of priority for cabin crew was reassigned.  After consulting with Company, a decision was made to divert to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC were flight landed uneventfully.

Thunder Airlines flight THU890, a Mitsubishi MU2B-60 (registration, C-GYUA) aircraft was on route from Thunder Bay International Airport (CYQT) ON to Toronto BBTC (CYTZ) ON, when the flight crew noticed the power output of the right engine (GARRETT TPE331-10-511M) was lower than expected. The flight crew contacted maintenance and a decision was made to continue to destination. During descent into CYTZ, the engine power dropped by 30%, despite the right engine power lever being at full power. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and advised ATC of the situation, and  the possibility of an engine shutdown in the event the situation degraded. The aircraft landed without further incident with both engines running. The flight crew carried out performance engine power runs and fuel control test later in the day and the results were normal. Thunder Airlines maintenance was sent to CYTZ to further troubleshoot the problem and it was determined that the Delta P Transducer was causing false indications and reducing the fuel flow to the right engine. The Delta P Transducer was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FNTA, a Beech King Air 300 operating as flight NTA201, operated by Northern Thunderbird Air, was on a MEDEVAC flight from Fort St. John (CYXJ) BC, to Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC.  During cruise, at 27 000 feet, approximately 80nm North of Prince George (CYXS), BC, the aircraft experienced a rapid decompression. The flight crew initiated a descent and donned their oxygen masks while completing the emergency checklist. The crew then declared an emergency with ATC and leveled off at 11 000 feet. The aircraft diverted to CYXS and landed without further incident or injuries. Maintenance found that the door seal was leaking and worn. The seal was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYUK a Boeing 737-8K5 operated by Sunwing SWG596 from Cancun Intl. (MMUN), Mexico to Calgary Intl. (CYYC) AB, declared an emergency due to smoke in the cabin while in US airspace at FL360. The aircraft diverted to Memphis International Airport (KMEM), TN and landed without incident. Suspected cause of smoke is a battery from an e-cigarette.

C-FKRF, a Westjet Airlines Boeing 737-800 was conducting flight WS2290 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Los Cabos Intl. (MMSD), Mexico. During cruise, flight attendant became incapacitated and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight.  Order of priority for cabin crew was reassigned.  Flight landed without further incident.

OK-TVM, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft owned by Smartwings and contracted to Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC 2651 from Holguin/Frank País Intl. (MUHG), Cuba to Halifax/Robert L. Stanfield Intl.(CYHZ), NS with 162 passengers and 6 crew. On approach to CYHZ the crew selected flaps 5 and they became lodged at flap 2. The flight crew overshot the approach and troubleshot the issue until deciding to land with flap 2 as they would not move. The crew requested ARFF to meet the aircraft when it stopped on the runway. The aircraft landed without further incident. Once the aircraft stopped on the runway the ARFF inspected the brakes and flaps including taking temperatures. Once the inspection was complete the crew taxied to the gate and the passengers were deplaned. Maintenance cleared the fault by resetting the flap computer and the aircraft was released to service.

C-GJVB, a Fairchild SA227-DC operated by Perimeter Aviation as flight Bearskin Airlines 344, was conducting a VFR flight from Dryden Regional (CYHD), ON to Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON with 2 crew members and 6 passengers on board. As C-GJVB started the takeoff roll on Runway 12, the aircraft directional control was lost and the aircraft exited the right side of the runway. The propellers subsequently contacted a snow bank and broke apart. Parts of the broken propellers penetrated the fuselage, injuring 1 passenger. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FGAN, a privately operated Robinson R-44 II helicopter, was touching down on snow-covered ice at Widgeon Lake, BC when the pilot lost control and the helicopter rolled onto it's side. The pilot and two passengers were not injured but the helicopter was substantially damaged. The 406 KHz ELT was manually activated and a Mayday call was made on 121.5 KHz to an overflying aircraft.

C-FFVJ, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800 was preparing flight SWG651 from Frank País Intl. (MUHG), Cuba to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC. During aircraft grooming on the ground in MUGH, black smoke and a burning smell was observed from the forward galley AC outlet. The flight crew immediately switched off the power to the IFE (in-flight entertainment) and cabin utility. A flight attendant unplugged the vacuum from the outlet at the time of the occurrence, the smoke stopped and doors were opened to ventilate the aircraft before boarding. The power to the AC outlet was removed and aircraft flew to destination without further incident.

C-GABO, un Dash-8-300 (DH8C) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8970, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport d'Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier (CYOW), ON à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC avec 48 passagers et 3 membres d'équipage. Après l'atterrissage, alors que l'appareil circulait vers le terminal, un passager a alerté l'équipage que des flammes se dégageaient du train principal droit. L’équipage a immobilisé l’appareil et demandé l’intervention des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). Le feu s'est dissipé rapidement et l'appareil a été remorqué jusqu'à la passerelle de débarquement. Un examen du train principal droit de l'appareil a révélé un bris des deux roulements de la roue intérieur.

C-GFCC, a Bell 407 helicopter operated by Blackcomb Helicopters was conducting heli-skiing operations with 1 pilot and 5 passengers on board in the vicinity of Brandywine Mountain, approximately 14 nm W of Whistler (CBE9), BC. After transporting a different group of skiers to the staging area due to deteriorating weather conditions the helicopter returned to the pickup spot on the mountain to collect 4 heli-ski guests and 1 guide. The pilot and guide reassessed the weather conditions as favorable to attempt another skiing run. At the top of the ski run the pilot was unable to approach the staked drop-off location due to reduced visibility and attempted to approach a nearby, lower altitude location that was not staked. The pilot entered a hover but soon lost visual reference with the surface due to deteriorating weather conditions and attempted to abort the landing. During the aborted landing attempt, the helicopter struck the snow-covered terrain, rolled to the right, and came to rest its right side. The 406 Mhz ELT activated. The guide exited the helicopter and assisted the 4 passengers with egress. The pilot retrieved the halon fire extinguisher mounted in the cockpit and extinguished a small post-impact fire located in the engine area. The heli-skiing guide contacted the company dispatcher using a handheld radio who initiated the emergency response plan. A company helicopter was unable to access the occurrence site due to low visibility. The pilot and 5 passengers skied to a lower portion of the mountain where the company helicopter transported them to the staging area. The guide received minor injuries and the helicopter was substantially damaged.

C-GOHI, an Airbus 321 operated by Air Transat was conducting flight TSC288 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to St.Maarten/Princess Juliana Intl (TNCM), Netherlands Antilles. After being cleared to land on Runway 10 in TNCM, TSC288 had to perform a go-around at approximately 100 feet because of the presence of a small airplane on the runway threshold. The airplane climbed to 2600 feet as instructed by tower and returned for a normal landing.The Sint Maarten Civil Aviation Authority is conducting an investigation.

C-FOWE, a De Havilland of Canada DHC-8-402, operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3156 from Vancouver Intl., BC (CYVR), to Edmonton Intl., AB (CYEG) with 4 crew and 73 passengers on board. WEN3156 was cleared for the visual aproach for RWY 20 following a Boeing 747 on final. The 747 traffic exited at the end of the runway and ATC subsequently cleared WEN3156 to land when it was on final approach at an altitude of approximately 500 feet AGL. WEN3156 continued the approach and at approximately 300 feet AGL the aircraft experienced an uncommanded roll. The pilot in command took control of the aircraft, corrected the roll and elected to continue the approach and landing. An uneventful landing was accomplished.

C-GKCP, a privately registered Bombardier Challenger 605, was conducting a flight from Palm Beach International Airport, Florida USA (KPBI) to Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC), with three crew members and 10 passengers on board. During the final descent into CYYC, the flight crew selected flaps 20 and immediately received a flaps fail caution message. The decision was made to abandon the approach, and the crew received clearance from ATC to proceed NE of the CYYC airport and troubleshoot the issue. The crew executed the applicable QRH procedure and subsequently received clearance from ATC to proceed with the landing. A flaps 0 landing was then executed. During the landing roll, after ground spoiler and thrust reverser deployment, the nose of the aircraft attained a significant nose high attitude. The rear fuselage of the aircraft struck the runway, and during the recovery, the nose landing gear subsequently impacted the runway. The aircraft taxied clear of the runway and to the intended parking area. Subsequent inspection revealed that the aircraft sustained significant structural damage to the forward fuselage and minor damage to the rear fuselage. There were no injuries.

C-GJYZ, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 aircraft, operated by Perimeter Aviation as flight PAG607, was enroute from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to St. Theresa Point (CYST), MB with 3 crew members and 43 passengers on board. While in cruise, the crew noticed the oil pressure dropped below 40 PSI on the left engine (Pratt & Whitney PW123B) and then conducted an intentional shut down. The crew decided to return CYWG and declared an emergency. The aircraft then landed without further incident. The operator's maintenance replaced the left engine oil cooler.

Sunwing flight SWG298, a Boeing 737-800 (C-GLZX) aircraft was on route from Thunder Bay (CYQT) ON to Varadero, Cuba (MUVR) and had just reached cruising altitude when a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue their duties. The flight crew decided to divert to Toronto LBPIA (CYYZ) and declared a medical emergency for a crew member. The aircraft landed in CYYZ without further incident and the flight attendant was taken to the hospital. A replacement flight attendant was sent to the aircraft and the aircraft continued to MUVR.

C-FADF, a De Havilland DHC-8-300 flight 8851 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was on approach to Ottawa/Macdonald–Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON; when the flight crew selected the landing gear down, they received a nosewheel red advisory light with an associated amber door light. The flight crew aborted the approach and followed the QRH procedures which did not rectify the fault. The crew subsequently declared an emergency and on the following approach as flaps were selected to 35 degrees, the nose landing gear extended and locked in the down position. The aircraft proceeded to land uneventfully with aircraft rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) standing by and came to a stop on the runway. Maintenance crew safetied the landing gear before towing the aircraft to the gate where passengers deplaned. Maintenance found the nose gear oleo strut was flat with no extension visible. There was no damage to the aircraft.

C-GWSH a Boeing 737-700 operated by WestJet flight WS1210 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to New York/LaGuardia Intl. airport (KLGA), NY experienced longer than anticipated holds into KLGA due to weather. Once on final, ATC instructed WestJet 1210 to go around due to loss of spacing to the slower traffic ahead on the approach. At that point, fuel on board was less than required minimum. Emergency was declared. Aircraft diverted to the planned alternate aerodrome, New York Stewart Intl. (KSWF), NY.

C-FSQY a Bombardier CL-600-2B16 flight SYB109 operated by Skyservice Business Aviation, was on final approach to Toronto/Lester B Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. Due to high rate of closure with the preceding arrival, C-FACT, a De Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP flight JZA330, SBY109 was instructed to pull up and go around. Spacing was reduced to 2.4 NM horizontal where 3 NM was required. SYB109 was instructed to fly heading 220 degrees and climb to 3,000 feet. The aircraft was observed in a right hand turn conflicting with departing traffic on RWY 23, C-GHPJ an Air Canada Rouge flight ROU1820 Airbus A321-211 aircraft. SYB109 was subsequently instructed to turn left to heading 150 degrees to correct the conflict.

C-GLAH, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 operated by Access Helicopters, was flying down a mountain near Stewart, BC to pick up skiers when the right-hand side cargo door departed the aircraft damaging the tail boom and the tail rotor blades. The pilot was able to land normally. The cargo door was equipped with hinges at the top and with a single latch in the bottom center (additional, after-market latches are available for this door). None of the cargo inside the compartment fell out. Airspeed at the time the cargo door departed was about 125 knots. It was not determined why the cargo door opened.

N618L a Learjet 60 aircraft operated by Pegasus Elite Aviation LLC flight PEG18, departed runway 24R at Toronto LBPIA (CYYZ) ON, and was given a clearance of 7000 feet, read back was correct. However, PEG18 climbed through 7000 feet. By the time the controller noticed the error and re-cleared PEG18 back to 7000 feet, PEG18 had passed behind Air Canada Rouge flight ROU1981, an Airbus A319-100 (C-GARO) aircraft from Mexico City/Benito Juarez International Airport (MMMX) MX to CYYZ. Separation was reduced to 1.3 NM and 900 feet where 3 NM or 1000 feet were required.

C-GAQL an Airbus A319-100 aircraft AC715 operated by Air Canada was taking off from New York, LaGuardia (KLGA) NY to Toronto Lester B Pearson (CYYZ), ON, when the #4 wheel assembly separated from the landing gear. ATC  informed the flight crew and the flight continued to CYYZ. On arrival at CYYZ the aircraft did a fly-by the tower which confirmed the #4 wheel was missing. The crew declared an emergency and the aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The aircraft stopped on the runway and damaged was assessed before the aircraft moved to the operator's maintenance facility. All Passengers were deplaned on the runway and transported by bus to the terminal. Photos taken of the landing gear showed that the outer bearing appears to have failed allowing the wheel assembly to slip out of the axle. The axle nut remained secure and safetied to axle. Subsequent reports from the FAA and NTSB stated the wheel had been found and retrieved fully inflated. The operator was notified that the wheel was available for further examination.

C-GBKA, a wheel/ski equipped Cessna A185F operated by Bamaji Air Inc., was conducting a flight from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON to Wawakapewin First Nation, ON. After touchdown on the ice surface runway on Long Dog Lake the aircraft began to list to the right. The pilot attempted to keep weight off of the right side landing gear by applying left aileron. While taxiing from the landing area the right side landing gear leg collapsed and the right wing contacted the ice. The pilot shutdown the engine and evacuated the 2 passengers. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained damage to the right landing gear leg and the right wing.

WestJet Flight WJA720, a Boeing 737-700 (C-FWSY) aircraft, was on route for Vancouver (CYVR) to Toronto LBPIA (CYYZ), when a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue duties. The flight attendant duties were distributed to the remaining flight attendants for landing.

C-GYEV, un Cessna 150M en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local de nuit selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aérodrome de Montréal/St-Lazare, QC (CST3), avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait à environ 1,75 nm à l’est de l’aérodrome de Montréal/Les Cèdres, QC (CSS3), celui-ci a percuté 2 lignes de transport d’énergie avant de s’écraser au sol. L’appareil a été détruit et les 2 occupants ont subi des blessures mortelles.

C-GPHO, an Ahmic Air Ltd. ski equipped Cessna 185F was operating from the Yellowknife Ice Strip (CEN9), NT to Whati (CEM3), NT.  The aircraft suffered a loss of engine power (Teledyne Continental Motors IO-520-D) shortly after take-off and conducted a forced approach into trees.  There were no injuries to the passenger or pilot.  The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GJYZ, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP., was conducting flight PAG109 from Island Lake (CYIV), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB. C-GJZT, a Bombardier CRJ900, operated by Jazz Aviation, was conducting flight JZA526 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON. Flight PAG109 was given clearance to descend to 7000 ASL and was given departing traffic information on JZA526 climbing to 6000 feet ASL. The flight crew of PAG109 correctly set, and engaged, the altitude selector to 7000 feet ASL. However, the altitude selector was subsequently inadvertently disengaged and PAG109 descended through 7000 feet ASL. PAG109 was instructed by ATC to stop the descent immediately and climb to 7000 feet ASL. Separation was reduced to 2 nautical miles and 600 feet where 3 nautical miles or 1000 feet is required.

C-GXNR, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Glencore Canada Corporation sous l'indicatif RAG200 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY). En vol de croisière, à 1515z à environ 145 miles marins (nm) au sud-est de CYUY, l’alerte « Cabin Altitude Warning Horn » s’est activée et l’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification d’urgence (QRH). L’équipage a ensuite déclaré un PAN PAN en raison du problème de pressurisation et a demandé une descente pour 10 000 pieds. En raison de délais de l’ATC, l’équipage a déclaré un MAYDAY afin d’accélérer la descente vers 10 000 pieds. L’aéronef a ensuite poursuivi son vol vers CYUY où il a atterri sans encombre à 1543z. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GINH, a C-172 operated by Victoria Flying Club, was on a sight-seeing flight south of Victoria International Airport (CYYJ) when smoke was noticed coming from the instrument panel. Shortly after, the engine (Lycoming O-360-A3A) began to run rough and the windscreen became covered in oil. The pilot declared a Mayday and began a return to CYYJ but the engine lost all power and a forced landing was conducted in a field about 9 nm south of CYYJ. The aircraft overturned on landing and was substantially damaged. The pilot and passenger received minor injuries.Company maintenance found the crankshaft had broken several inches aft of the propeller flange and the propeller departed the aircraft in flight.

N995DP, a Gates Learjet Corporation aircraft operated by Reva Inc., was conducting a flight from Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB to St. Louis/Lambert International (KSTL) Missouri, United States. The flight crew received an engine fire warning and shutdown the affected engine. An emergency was declared and the flight crew elected to divert to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker International (CYXE), SK. The aircraft dumped fuel while in a hold and the subsequent landing was conducted without further incident. The operator's maintenance personnel repaired the fire detection system.

C-FHLG a Northern Air Solutions Inc. Cessna 550 aircraft, was cruising at FL250 abeam CFB Trenton (CYTR), ON when the flight crew heard a bang and then the cabin 10,000' ALT light illuminated. The flight crew initiated crew and passenger oxygen, contacted ATC and started an emergency descent to 10,000 feet. The flight crew elected to divert to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON and landed without further incident.

N9029F, an American Airlines flight AAL2352 Airbus A319 aircraft, departed Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON for Chicago O'Hare Intl. (KORD), IL. On initial climb, Flight crew declared an emergency due to fumes in the flight deck area. The aircraft was given priority to return to CYYZ and landed uneventfully. Aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) met and escorted the aircraft to the gate. After landing and during maintenance evaluation, it was determined that the blower fan had malfunctioned and sent fumes into the cockpit impacting the ventilation.

Approximately 14 miles from Ottawa (CYOW), the flight crew of Jazz flight JZA8013, a De Havilland DHC-8-300 (C-GEWQ) aircraft, received a green laser strike in the cockpit which reportedly hit the First Officer (F/O) in the eyes. The F/O, who was the pilot flying, passed control of the aircraft to the Captain. The flight crew hit the Ident button to capture their position and advised ATC of incident, the RCMP were also made aware. The Captain requested EMS, because the F/Os' eyes were irritated. The fight landed normally and the F/O was met by EMS at the gate, and transported to the Ottawa General hospital for further observation.

C-GBHM, an Airbus A-319 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC1046 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR) BC, to Palm Springs Intl(KPSP), CA with 5 crew members and 113 passengers on board. While descending, the flight crew received a TCAS RA. The flight crew complied with the RA and continued to destination without further incident

C-GPAT, an A310 aircraft operated by Air Transat was conducting flight TSC412 from Quebec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC to Paris-Charles De Gaulle Airport (LFPG), France. Approximately 3 hours 30 minutes after departure, the aircraft had a pitch trim stabilizer fault. Three resets were attempted however unsuccessful. The flight crew decided to continu to LFPG with no emergency declared. The aircraft landed safely in LFPG.

C-FYJD, a B737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing was conducting flight SWG677 from Varadero Juan Gualberto Gomez (MUVR), Cuba to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. During cruise, severe turbulence was encountered in vicinity of Helena Regional (KHLN), MT while on descent from FL380 down to FL350. During the encounter there was a temporary loss of control of the aircraft which was subsequently regained. The seat belt sight was on and a PA was made to passengers to be seated. A passenger that was in the aft lavatory during the event and sustain minor injuries. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

EI-GAJ an Airbus 330-300 aircraft operated by Aer Lingus was conducting flight EIN104 from John F Kennedy (KJFK) airport, New York, to Dublin airport (EIDW), Ireland. While in cruise at FL310 and approximately 50 NM NE of Halifax, Nova Scotia, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence. The crew declared a MAYDAY and immediately began a descent to FL290. There were no injuries to the crew or passengers nor damage to the aircraft. The aircraft continued to destination.

C-GTAQ, a DHC-8-300 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight 8025 from Hartford-Springfield/Bradley Intl. (KBDL), CT to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. On taxi out for take-off, Flight crew noticed visible smoke coming from first officer’s windshield (from windshield heat lead wire).  Windshield heat was selected off and smoke dissipated. Fight returned to the gate. No emergency declared.

C-GARO, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus 319-114, was conducting flight ROU1617 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL to Ottawa/ Macdonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON. During take-off climb, the flight crew had issues with the trailing edge flaps.  Flight crew declared an emergency and landed uneventfully back to KFLL.  No injuries reported.

The Summit Air Ltd. SU8142 British Aerospace BAE-146 (Avro RJ100), C-GZRJ, was operating from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Diavik, NT (CDK2). Approximately 20 nm from the initial approach fix the flight deck was informed that a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to perform their duties. The aircraft landed without further incident and an ambulance met the aircraft. No emergency was declared.

C-GJSV, a de Havilland DHC-8-102 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways LP., was conducting flight WSG821 from Kingfisher Lake (CNM5), ON to Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON. After departure from CNM5 the flight crew noticed that the left engine oil temperature was climbing. All other engine indications were normal. When the aircraft levelled off in cruise, the oil temperature had increased to 115°-120° and was still climbing. The flight crew communicated with the operator's maintenance personnel and elected to divert to Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON. The oil temperature continued to climb to the maximum gauge indication. The flight crew declared an emergency and the landing in CYPL was conducted without further incident. Once on the ground the flight crew shut down the left engine and taxied to the apron. The operator's maintenance personnel cleaned the connection at the oil temperature probe.

C-GTQB, un Boeing 737-800 exploité par Air Transat sous l'indicatif TSC474, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson, ON (CYYZ) avec 172 passagers et 6 membres d’équipage. Lors du refoulement de la barrière 49 au départ de CYUL, l’ailette Scimitar de bout d'aile droite a heurté une clôture temporaire de construction. L’appareil a été ramené à la barrière et les passagers sont débarqués normalement pour prendre un autre appareil. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et les dommages étaient limités à l’ailette de bout d’aile.

The WestJet Airlines Boeing 737-600, C-GPWS, operating as WJA132, was on a flight from Vancouver (CYVR), BC to Calgary (CYYC), AB. While flying the RNP "Y" VESGA transition for Runway 35L at CYYC, WJA132 was pulled off the approach. A loss of separation occurred when WJA132 got within 2.5 NM laterally and 700 feet vertically of a WestJet Encore De Havilland Dash 8-400, C-FWEP, operating as WEN4077, which was on the downwind for Runway 35L at 8000 feet. WJA132 was turned right to a heading of 190 to regain separation and as a result got within 2.5 NM and 500 feet of a Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland Dash 8-400, C-GVJZ, operating as JZA408, which was on the left base for Runway 35L. 1000 feet or 3nm was needed in both cases.

NovaJet flight NOJ75, a Hawker Beechcraft Hawker 750 (C-FCFC) aircraft from Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport (KOPF), FL to Toronto Lester B Pearson (CYYZ), ON, reported a medical emergency and requested priority and EMS to meet them at the gate. NOJ75 reported flying single pilot due to the Captain being incapacitated. NOJ75 was given priority and landed Runway 23 at 05:17z without incident.

The Air Canada Airbus A320-211, C-FKCO, operating as ACA396 on a flight from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Montreal (CYUL), QC experienced an engine (CFM International CFM56-5A1 S/N 731775)  failure during taxi from the gate to the runway. The aircraft returned to the gate and passengers were offloaded.Company maintenance conducted a borescope inspection and noted damage beyond limits on stages 7 and 8 of the high pressure compressor. The engine was removed and findings during the teardown will be relayed to the TSB.

While cleaning RWY07, a snow removal vehicle was instructed and readback to hold short RWY14. However, the vehicle crossed the hold short line for RWY14. Porter flight POE202, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 (C-GLQJ) aircraft, which was cleared for take-off from RWY14 was told to abort takeoff.

FlexJet flight LXJ549, a Bombardier BD-100-1A10 (N549FX) aircraft, departed runway 24 at Toronto Leater B Pearson (CYYZ), ON behind Sky Regional flight SKV7527, an Embraer E175 (C-FEJD) aircraft. ATC Separation was reduced to 2 nm laterally and 600 feet vertically where 3 nm or 1000 feet were required.

C-FTJO an Airbus 320-211 operated by Air Canada AC796 was conducting a flight from Los Angeles Intl. (KLAX), CA to Toronto Lester B Pearson (CYYZ), ON. In the vicinity of Porter, CA, the crew suspected a fuel leak and shutdown the Left hand (#1) engine. The Flight crew declared an Pan Pan and elected to divert to Denver Intl. (KDEN), CO where the aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance in Denver opened the #1 engine cowlings and found fuel to be heavily pooled inside. Maintenance crew is investigating.

C-GIQG, a Swearingen SA 226-TC operated by Perimeter Aviation PAG02, was conducting a medevac flight from Cross Lake (CYCR), MB to Thompson (CYTH), MB. During the descent into CYTH, the paramedic attending the patient required assistance. The first officer left the cockpit to assist and the Captain made a PAN PAN indicating single pilot operations. Prior to landing, the first officer returned to the cockpit and resumed normal duties. The aircraft subsequently landed safely at CYTH.

C-FNJZ, a CRJ 900 operated by Jazz Aviation LP was conducting flight AC8670 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to San Diego Intl. (KSAN), CA. While on top at FL270 Vicinity of PASKE (Porter, CA), the crew encountered clear air turbulence. Airspeed fluctuated +/-30kts but did not over-speed nor did the Auto Pilot kick off. Turbulence and Ignition buttons were on. The turbulence made reading the instruments on the panel impossible as they were too blurry.  The motion was up/down as well as side/side. The seat belt signs were switched on about 2 min prior to the encounter.  Flight crew initiated descent to FL 250 where they had moderate to borderline severe turbulence.  Continuing descent to FL230 flight encountered a severe turbulence event that lasted approximately 5 minutes. Flight climbed to FL250 where the turbulent event ceased.  Maintenance is arranging for an inspection.

C-FGUO, un Cessna 150 en exploitation privée effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aérodrome de Joliette/St-Thomas, QC (CJO2) avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Une fois en croisière à environ 1300 pieds au-dessus du niveau de la mer et à environ 7 mille marins à l’est de l’aérodrome, le moteur a eu des ratés. Le pilote a actionné la commande du réchauffe carburateur. Le régime moteur a momentanément augmenté, mais a ensuite redescendu. Comme l’avion ne parvenait pas à maintenir son altitude, le pilote a manœuvré pour effectuer un atterrissage d’urgence dans un champ. Suite à l’atterrissage, l’avion a subi entre autres des dommages à l’hélice, au train d’atterrissage et au bout de l’aile droite qui a touché le sol. Les occupants n’ont subi aucune blessure.

The Air Sprint Inc. Embraer E550 Legacy, C-FJAS, operating as ASP822 on a flight from Indianapolis (KIND) IN, USA to Calgary (CYYC), AB experienced a Flt Control Fault CAS message associated with Side-stick RH Fault, Side-stick LH Fault, Elevator LH Fault, and Aileron LH Fault.  The flight crew completed the appropriate checklists. Maintenance was contacted and the decision was made to continue as everything appeared to working correctly. The crew declared a Pan Pan prior to commencing the approach into Calgary and the arrival was conducted without issue.  Update:  Once on the ground a power cycle was performed which corrected the issue. The condition was considered a spurious event and the aircraft was released back to service.

Shortly after takeoff from Runway 21 late in the afternoon, a Zenair CH 701 STOL advanced ultralight, C-IHAN, impacted the left side runway edge in a nose down attitude. The pilot was trapped in the cockpit due to crushing damage incurred to the forward cabin area. The ELT signal was not triggered and the time of the occurrence with reduced daylight, precluded a timely emergency response. The pilot was reported missing and the RCMP initiated a search of the Merritt area establishments, and 'pinged' the pilot's cell phone for location. The aircraft was eventually spotted on the runway edge at the airport in the early morning hours with its tail in the air. The pilot was alive, conscious, but suffering from the cold, and serious injuries. He was extricated from the wreckage and taken to hospital. This was the first flight in the aircraft after the pilot purchased it. The aircraft had been delivered and reassembled the previous day.

C-GURG, un Canadair CL-600-2B16 exploité par Service aérien gouvernemental sous l'indicatif QUE10 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Mont-Joli, QC (CYYY) à destination de l’aéroport international Jean-Lesage, QC (CYQB). C-FCVD, un Pilatus exploité par Panorama Fixed Wings sous l’indicatif NDL543 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis CYQB à destination de Wabush, NL (CYWK). QUE10 a initié une approche interrompue RWY 24 en raison d’un problème d’instrument. Il a reçu et relu correctement l’instruction de virer à gauche au cap 150 degrés et de monter à 3000 pieds. Au moment d’atteindre 2900 pieds d’altitude, l’espacement a été perdu avec NDL543 décollé précédemment. L’espacement a été réduit à 2.7 milles marin (nm) horizontalement et à 800 pieds verticalement alors que 3 nm horizontalement ou 1000 pieds verticalement étaient requis entre les 2 appareils. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

B-KPQ, a Cathay Pacific Boeing 777-367ER, was operating as CPA865D from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Chek Lap Kok Intl (VHHH), Hong Kong with 18 crew and no passengers on board. As the aircraft leveled at FL 320 , the crew detected smoke in the cockpit and the cabin. The crew declared an emergency and requested a return to CYVR. The aircraft dumped fuel to 84 000 kg 40 NM NW of CYVR. The aircraft landed without further incident at approximately 11 000 kg over the maximum landing weight. ARFF was standing by.Maintenance conducted an overweight landing inspection with no faults found. They verified that the smoke was in fact oil fumes/haze caused by an oil contaminated air conditioning system. They traced the origin of the oil source to the aircraft's APU. Numerous components of the air conditioning  system were replaced and the ducting was removed and cleaned. The APU was deactivated for the return flight to VHHH and the aircraft has returned to service.

C-GMPN, an Aerospatiale AS350-B3 operated by RCMP Air Services, was conducting policing activities 24nm SW of Houston (CAM5), BC with 3 persons on board. Also operating in the area were two RCMP operated RPAS units. During low level flight (below 300 feet AGL), the helicopter and 1 RPAS (FLIR SkyRanger R60 - 2.4 kg) collided. The helicopter suffered some initial vibration and the pilot completed a precautionary landing on a road without further incident. Maintenance staff found damage primarily to the main rotor blades along with superficial damage on the tail boom and tail rotor. The effected components were removed as per the maintenance manual for repairs or overhaul as required. The RPAS was destroyed. There were no injuries to persons in the aircraft or on the ground.

C-GWVB, a Boeing 737-800 operated by Sunwing Airlines Inc., was conducting flight SWG282 from Cancun Intl. (MMUN), Mexico to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC. During climb in vicinity of MMUN, a flight attendant became incapacitated and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight.  Order of priority for cabin crew was reassigned.  Flight landed without further incident.

C-FMWY, a Boeing 767-33ER operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1629 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. During cruise in vicinity of Columbia Metropolitan (KCAE), SC, a flight attendant became incapacitated and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight.  Order of priority for cabin crew was reassigned.  Flight landed without further incident.

C-GWSB, a Westjet 737-600, was operating as WS461 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Kelowna (CYLW), BC with 5 crewmembers and 99 passengers on board. When, at the top of descent for CYLW, the crew activated the #2 Engine Cowl Thermal Anti Ice (TAI), they got a warning indicating that the TAI was inoperative. The crew climbed out of icing conditions and ran through the appropriate checklists with no change. The flight crew made the decision to return to CYYC. With the TAI inoperative, the crew needed to avoid icing conditions and that was not possible if they complied with the normal descent profile. They declared a PANPAN to and received priority handling to avoid icing conditions. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance replaced the #2 engine cowl TAI valve and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSRY, a Jazz Aviation LP Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft, was conducting flight JZA8075 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC with four crewmembers and forty passengers on board. During the descent into CYYJ, the flight encountered severe turbulence with the captain reporting that the aircraft could not be controlled. Both pilots reported never having experienced such severe turbulence and made the decision to return to CYVR. The flight landed in CYVR with no injuries to the crew or passengers. Maintenance conducted a turbulence inspection and found no obvious defects. They downloaded the FDR data that showed that the aircraft had not exceeded any vertical or lateral limits. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-FBJZ, a Canadair CL-600-2D24 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation as flight JZA7132, was enroute from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 2 crew members on board. Shortly after departure from CYWG, the crew received a lavatory smoke/fire indication followed by the smell of smoke. The crew decided to return to CYWG and declared a MAYDAY. While completing the QRH procedures, the fire/smoke indication went out. The aircraft then landed safely and was met by ARFF on the ramp. Inspection of the aircraft by ARFF did not reveal any fire or smoke. Further inspection of the aircraft by the operator's maintenance personnel revealed a loose wire in connector PS97P1 to the FWD lavatory light dimmer (PS97).

C-FTEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3241 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Kamloops (CYKA), BC with 4 crew members and 77 passengers on board. During the descent into CYKA, the flight encountered severe turbulence and the crew initiated a missed approach; turbulence continued throughout the missed approach. The crew reported a momentary loss of control when the aircraft would not respond to their inputs. The crew decided to divert to their alternate destination (CYYC) due to the severity of the turbulence. The flight landed safely in CYYC with no injuries to crew or passengers.Maintenance completed a severe turbulence inspection with no faults found. De Havilland analyzed the flight data recorder information with no exceedances found. The aircraft has returned to service.

C-FSKQ, un Beechcraft 200 exploité par Skyjet Aviation sous l’indicatif VSL443 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) avec seulement 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Environ 64 milles nautiques au nord-est de CYQB, l’équipage a observé un problème d’indication de torque du moteur droit. La liste de vérification d’urgence fut complétée. L’équipage a rebroussé chemin vers CYQB et a déclaré une urgence. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FSRY, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA59 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC. C-FEXI, a Cessna 208B aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express Incorporated, was conducting flight MAL8070 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC. A loss of separation occurred while the aircraft were being vectored for final approach to CYYJ. Lateral separation reduced to 2.7 nm where 3.0 nm or 1000 feet was required. NAV CANADA is conducting an ATS operational irregularity investigation.

C-FEXW, a Morningstar Air Express Limited Cessna 208B aircraft, was conducting flight MAL7058 from Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with one crew member on board. During the climb out of CYYJ, the flight encountered severe turbulence from 500 feet ASL up to approximately 4000 feet ASL and the aircraft became difficult to control. Once clear of the turbulence, the aircraft continued to CYVR and landed without further incident. There were no injuries to the crew or damage to the aircraft. Maintenance conducted an inspection of the aircraft and found no damage. The aircraft was returned to service.

The North Cariboo Flying Service Ltd de Havilland Dash 8-300, C-FHNC, was operating as NCB1795 on a flight from Primrose, AB (CFN6) to Calgary, AB (CYYC). NCB1795 was climbing through 14 000 feet when the master caution light illuminated and the hydraulic pressure gauge showed zero pressure. ATC was notified and the aircraft levelled at 16 000 feet. The crew actioned the QRH and declared an emergency diverting to Edmonton, AB (CYEG). Emergency services attended the landing which was uneventful. After a visual inspection the aircraft taxied to a company maintenance hangar.Company maintenance identified that the loss of hydraulic pressure indication and fluid loss was caused by the failure of the "bushing" or adaptor PN 82970078-101.

N236RP, un Embraer EMB-505 exploité par TVPX Aircraft Services effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Keflavík International Airport, Islande (BIKF) à destination d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) avec seulement 2 membres d’équipage à bord. En approche pour l’atterrissage, lorsque le train d’atterrissage a été sélectionné en position baissée, l’équipage a reçu une indication anormale que la roue de nez n’était pas verrouillée. L’équipage a alors demandé au personnel de la tour de faire un survol bas au-dessus de la piste et de vérifier visuellement si la roue de nez était sortie. Après que le personnel de la tour ait confirmé que la roue de nez n’était pas sortie, l’équipage a procédé à une remontée pour compléter la liste de vérification applicable et a déclaré une urgence. Une fois la liste de vérification complétée, l’indication au tableau de bord confirmait que le train d’atterrissage était sorti et verrouillé. Par mesure de précaution, l’équipage a demandé une deuxième fois au personnel de la tour de vérifier visuellement que le train d’atterrissage était bien sorti, ce qu’il a confirmé. L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

C-GARO, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus 319-114, was conducting flight ROU1896 from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Las Vegas/McCarran Intl. (KLAS), NV. During descent, the flight flew into an area of wake turbulence while passing through FL 170-160 from a Boeing 777 causing the aircraft to bank 20 to 30 degrees in both directions.  Flight crew corrected undesired aircraft state and notified ATC.  The flight subsequently landed in KLAS without further issues.  No injuries reported.

C-GBJZ, a de Havilland Dash 8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8902 from Montreal Trudeau airport (CYUL), QC, to the Greater Moncton Romeo Leblanc airport (CYQM), NB. While in cruise at FL250 over Frederiction New Brunswick, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence. The autopilot disengaged, the aircraft banked left to about 40 degrees and lost approximately 1000 feet before the crew could regain control. The turbulence lasted for approximately 45 seconds before abating. The 77 passengers and 4 crew were wearing seatbelts and no one was injured. The aircraft landed safely at CYQM. Maintenance completed a severe turbulence inspection and the aircraft was released to service.

C-GJSV, a de Havilland DHC-8-100 operated by Wasaya Airways as flight WP843, was enroute from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON with 3 crew members and 28 passengers on board. During the initial climb from CYQT, the crew observed a roll spoiler outboard hydraulic caution light on the annunciator panel. As the airspeed increased above 140 knots the caution light extinguished. The crew then decreased the airspeed below 140 knots and the caution light returned. The crew completed the QRH procedures and elected to continue their flight to CYXL where a PAN PAN was declared. The aircraft then landed safely.An inspection of the aircraft by the operator's maintenance personal revealed a dirty hydraulic pressure switch located in the right main gear wheel well. The hydraulic switch was cleaned and a successful test flight was completed. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-GBHM, an Air Canada Airbus 319-100, was conducting flight AC1047 from Palm Springs Intl. (KSPS), CA to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC. During cruise at FL360 in vicinity of Mammoth Yosemite (KMMH), CA, Flight crew reported severe wind shear of +/- 30 knots and +/- 2000-3000 FPM with an altitude change of +/- 500ft, classified associated turbulence as moderate/severe. Flight continued without further incident. DFDR (digital flight data recorder) download showed vertical accelerations at 1.75G and lateral accelerations -.2G, within limit of Aircraft maintenance manual.

C-FYNS, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus 319-114, was conducting flight ROU1638 Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC to Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL. During cruise in vicinity of Block Island State (KBID), RI, flight attendant became incapacitated and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight.  Order of priority for cabin crew was reassigned.  Flight landed uneventfully in KMCO.

C-GEZJ, an Air Transat Airbus 321-200, was operating as flight TS939 from Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC. On departure out of MCO, on radar vectors, the Flight crew were initially given a heading of 030, then instructed to turn left heading 310. As they were passing 7000 ft they received a TCAS RA (resolution advisory) telling them to maintain vertical speed, which was 3000 ft/min.  Flight crew complied and flight landed in CYUL uneventfully.

C-GCPX, a Swearingen SA-226-AT operated by Skycare Air Ambulance was enroute from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON with two flight crew members on board. During the landing roll on Runway 16 at CYXL, the crew pulled the power levers in an asymmetric configuration and the aircraft veered off to the right side of the runway. While regaining directional control of the aircraft, the left propeller struck a runway light. The aircraft then taxied to the ramp without further incident. An inspection of the aircraft by the operator's maintenance revealed damage to one of the blades of the left propeller.

After departure from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON, one of the flight attendants on Sunwing flight SWG207, a Boeing 737-800 (C-GNVR) aircraft, became ill. The flight attendant was unable to continue with their duties. The flight continued to Los Cabos (MMSD), Mexico and paramedics were arranged to meet the aircraft on arrival.

C-GOIA, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Saab-Fairchild 340B, was operating as flight PCO3041 from Calgary International (CYYC), AB to Cranbrook (CYXC), BC. The crew encountered severe turbulence 52 nm SSW of CYYC, declared an emergency and returned to CYYC. Following the flight, maintenance inspected the aircraft for any anomalies that would have resulted from the flight through the turbulence. No defects were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GHOZ, a Boeing 767-300 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA837 from Madrid / Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Intl (LEMD), Spain to Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 8 crew members and 130 passengers onboard. During takeoff, rubber from the number 5 main landing gear tire detached. Some debris was found on the runway and others were ingested by the left engine. As a precaution, the flight crew performed an in-flight shut down of the left engine. After burning off fuel to avoid an overweight landing, the aircraft returned to LEMD for an uneventful landing. There were no injuries to the occupants. Preliminary inspection of the aircraft shows damage to the engine and left main landing gear.The Spanish CIAIAC is investigating [Ref: A-006/2020]

OK-TVT, a Boeing 737-800, operated by Smartwings as Sunwing Airlines flight SWG600, departed from Toronto Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON for Cayo Coco (MUCC), Cuba. During gear retraction the flight crew heard an unusual noise followed by a high vibration; a Pan Pan was declared and the aircraft returned to CYYZ uneventfully.Prior to departure there was an incident during push-back where the ground completed the push-back and disconnected the tow bar, but forget to tell the crew to set the brakes. The aircraft started to roll forward and the flight crew applied the brakes. The aircraft was checked for damage by the ground crew and no apparent damage was found. After landing, Sunwing maintenance inspected the aircraft at the gate and determined that the right nose gear door retraction lever was broken.

C-GANF. a de Havilland DHC-8-102 operated by Wasaya Airways as flight WSG814, was enroute from Wunnumin Lake (CKL3), ON to Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON with two flight crew members on board. While in cruise at 12000 feet, the aircraft experienced failure of the left side and overhead instrument panel. The crew was able to make radio contact with a nearby aircraft and advised them of their situation and that they would be diverting the aircraft to Kingfisher Lake (CNM5), ON. The nearby aircraft was able to activate the runway lights at CNM5 and relayed a MAYDAY to the Winnipeg ACC. While on base leg, the crew of WSG814 reported a strong smell of fumes in the cockpit. The aircraft then landed safely and was stopped on the runway where both engines were shut down and the master switch was turned off. There were no injuries and the aircraft was not damaged. It was reported that the following circuit breakers had tripped: #1 Air Data Computer, #1 Radar Altimeter, 3 separate lighting breakers and 2 annunciator breakers. An inspection of the aircraft by the operator's maintenance personal revealed an unserviceable left starter-generator. The starter-generator was replaced and the aircraft was flown to base under the authority of a ferry flight permit for further inspection.

C-GHLT, a Boeing 767-333ER operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1950 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Quito/Mitad del Mundo Intl. (SEQM), Ecuador.  During final approach, Flight crew received LE SLAT ASYM EICAS (flaps asymmetry on engine-indicating and crew-alerting system) following selection of flaps.  Go around was conducted and carried out as per QRH procedures.  ATC was advised and Mayday was declared.  Flight crew performed a reduced flap landing in accordance with policy and procedures. The flight landed uneventfully.  Aircraft remained on runway until brake temperature was adequate for towing to the gate.

On 31 January 2020, the WestJet Encore Ltd. De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Ltd. DHC-8-402 aircraft (registration C-FKWE, serial number 4467) was conducting flight WEN3107 from Vancouver International Airport, British Columbia, to Terrace Airport, British Columbia, with 4 crew members and 43 passengers on board. At 2106 Pacific Standard Time, during the landing roll on Runway 33, the aircraft drifted left from the snow-cleared area of the runway and the left main landing gear came into contact with a windrow. As a result, the aircraft was pulled to the left and the nose and right main landing gear also came into contact with the windrow. The aircraft travelled through the uncleared portion of the runway and the left main landing gear exited the runway surface, outside of the runway edge lights, travelling for approximately 400 feet before returning to the runway. During the runway excursion through the windrow and uncleared portion of the runway, the aircraft’s nose landing gear collapsed rearward. After the aircraft came to a stop, the flight crew requested the services of aircraft rescue and fire fighting. There were no injuries. The passengers were transported to the airport terminal by bus approximately 30 minutes after landing. The damage to the aircraft included the collapsed nose landing gear and damaged right propeller blades. The accident occurred in the hours of darkness with limited visibility due to snowfall.

C-GTTM, a Swearingen SA227-AT operated by Carson Air Ltd. was conducting flight CA8081 from Calgary Int'l (CYYC), AB to Kelowna (CYLW), BC, with 2 flight crew members on board. During cruise flight the pilot flying determined the right engine (Garret TPE 331-11U) was no longer responding to cockpit power lever movements. The flight crew actioned the emergency checklist for no response to power lever movement. With no change to the condition, the crew actioned the engine shutdown checklist. The flight crew notified ATC of the event, but did not declare a PANPAN or MAYDAY. The flight landed without further incident. Subsequent maintenance actions determined the propeller pitch control bracket became detached during flight. The hardware including the bolt and washer were located within the engine cowling, but the lock wire was not. The aircraft has since been returned to service.

C-GWJU, a Boeing 737-600 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA141 from Edmonton Int'l (CYEG), AB to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC with 5 crew and 80 passengers on board. The flight crew stopped short of the lead-in line for gate B15, with engines running, awaiting ground crew to marshal the aircraft to the gate. C-FZWS, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA717 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Int'l (CYYZ), ON to CYVR with 5 crew and 87 passengers on board. This aircraft was taxing eastbound on the apron towards the lead-in line for gate B13, when the left winglet contacted the right-hand horizontal stabilizer of C-GWJU. There were no injuries. Both aircraft sustained substantial damage.

The controller issued Endeavor Air flight EDV5536, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (registration N232PQ) aircraft, a line up on Runway 06L clearance with a visual departure. The clearance was acknowledged by WestJet Encore flight WEN3474, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 (registration C-GWEN) aircraft. Both EDV5536 and WEN3474 began to lineup Runway 06L. EDV5536 asked for clarification on who was departing when WEN3474 departed RWY 06L. Sky Regional flight SKV7531, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU (C-FRQW) aircraft, was overshot due to EDV5536 being across the hold short line.

C-GPRU, un Beechcraft B100 exploité par Max Aviation Inc. effectuait un vol depuis l'aéroport de La Grande Rivière (CYGL), QC à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC. Durant la montée, à environ 5000 pieds, les indicateurs de couple et de pression d'huile du moteur droit indiquaient des valeurs anormales. L'équipage a avisé les services du contrôle aérien et a effectué un retour vers CYGL. Après avoir effectué quelques vérifications, l'équipage a fermé le moteur (GARRETT TPE331-6-252B) droit et a déclaré une urgence. L'appareil s'est posé sur la piste 31 sans problème. Les techniciens sur place ont constaté que la soupape de dérivation d'huile pour le moteur droit était partiellement sortie du carter moteur. Les filets rapportés hélicoïdaux dans lesquels était vissée la soupape de dérivation d'huile étaient arrachés du carter moteur.

Sky Regional Airlines flight SKV7608, an Embraer E170-200 (registration C-FEIX) aircraft, departed Toronto /Lester B Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON for Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (KDCA). During the climb-out from CYYZ the flight crew received a "SLAT FAIL' EICAS message. The crew carried out the QRH checklist, but was unable to clear the message. The flight crew elected to return to CYYZ and declared a PAN PAN in the downwind for Runway 23. ARFF deployed and SKV7608 landed Runway 23 without incident.Maintenance determined the a Power Drive Unit (PDU) was at fault, the PDU was replaced as per the AMM and returned to service.

The Top Aces Inc. Dassault/Dornier Alpha Jets, C-GJTA and C-FHTO, were operating at CFB Cold Lake, (CYOD) AB. A fuel order was placed for both aircraft to be fueled with NATO F34 type fuel. A fuel truck identified as containing F34 fuel went to the aircraft and both Alpha Jets were refueled. The fuel receipts also identified the fuel type as F34. Approximately 20 minutes after refueling, the operator was notified that NATO F37 type fuel had been delivered and fueled into the Alpha Jets. The fuel truck was previously used to defuel a RCAF CF-188 which contained the F37 type fuel. Both Alpha Jets were defueled, prior to flight operations, without further incident. (See A19W0155).

C-GUBF, an Air Transat Airbus 330-243, was conducting flight TSC138 Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC to Santa Clara Airport (MUSC), Cuba. During cruise in vicinity of Orlando (KMCO), FL, a flight attendant (FA) became incapacitated and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight.  Order of priority for cabin crew did not have to be reassigned since the FA had a supplementary position.  Flight landed uneventfully in MUSC.

C-GTSJ, an Airbus 330-243 operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight ACA2426 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC to Cancún Intl. (MMUN), Mexico. During cruise, flight attendant became ill and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight. Cabin crew positions were reassigned in priority of occupancy. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

G-ZBKD, an Boeing 787-900 operated by British Airways, was conducting flight BWA293 from London Heathrow Intl. (EGLL), UK to Washington Dulles Intl. (KIAD), VA. The aircraft dispatched with the right air conditioning pack inoperative in accordance with the MEL. During the cruise portion while at FL410, the left air conditioning pack failed, resulting in a PACK ALTITUDE LIMIT warning. The checklist required a descent to FL340. At 195 nm NE of St John’s International Airport, NL (CYYT), the crew requested FL340, however it was denied by ATC.  The crew then declared a PAN-PAN due to the pressurization issue and a descent to FL340 was made.  Once the aircraft reached FL340 the crew reported the situation was normal and cancelled the PAN -PAN and continued to destination without incident.

C-FNBM a Bombardier CL600-2B16 aircraft was conducting Chartright Air flight HRT085 from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), NJ to Toronto/Leaster B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  On approach, the Flight crew executed a go-around due to a landing gear indication problem. After the go-around, HRT085 performed the checklist items to troubleshoot the problem and then requested fire trucks to stand by for landing. The aircraft landed without further incident in CYYZ and taxied to the gate.

C-GOJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP CRJ-900 aircraft, was conducting flight JZA8576 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Int'l (CYXE), SK with 4 crew members and 74 passenger on board. After take off and following the landing gear retraction, the crew received a nose wheel steering caution annunciation. The flight crew elected to return to CYVR, however entered a hold for approximately 40 minutes to reduce aircraft weight for landing. In consultation with the operator's maintenance a decision was made to land at a weight higher than the maximum landing weight using a minimum descent rate. The flight crew declared an emergency and the aircraft landed without further incident. Subsequent maintenance actions revealved an inoperative nose steering control module. The unit was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

WestJet flight WJA2641, a Boeing 767-300 (C-FWAD) aircraft, was on the approach to Toronto /LBPIA (CYYZ), ON and instructed to fly a heading 330 degrees. The aircraft was observed to turn through the assigned heading to 230. WJA2641 came into conflict with the preceding arrival, Jazz flight JZA652, a De Havilland DHC-8-300 (C-GNON) aircraft. Separation was reduced to 2.4NM and 600 feet where 3NM or 1000 feet is required.

C-GHPE, a Boeing 767 aircraft operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1602 from Montreal / Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Fort Lauderdale / Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL. In cruise,  in the vicinity of New York City, it was identified to have experienced a gradual loss of C hydraulic fluid. The crew declared a PAN PAN, diverted to CYUL, and subsequently declared a Mayday. The aircraft landed uneventfully and was towed to the gate.  Maintenance identified the brake surge accumulator pressure line to be chaffed and cracked and it was replaced. The C hydraulic system was serviced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWVB, a Sunwing Airlines Boeing 737-800 aircraft, was operating as flight SWG569 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to General Mazatlán/Rafael Buelna Intl (MMMZ). At FL330, approximately 135 nm east of Las Vegas/Mc Carran Intl (KLAS), NV a TCAS RA 'DESCEND DESCEND NOW' was received. The flight crew complied with the command and descended until clear of conflict at FL325. The flight continued to the destination uneventfully.

C-GSQA, un hélicoptère Bell 206-L4 en exploitation privée par le Gouvernement du Québec sous l'indicatif QUE49, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols à vue depuis l'aéroport d’Alma (CYTF), QC, à destination de La Tuque (CYLQ), QC. L’aéronef avait participé plus tôt à une opération de recherche et sauvetage pour des motoneigistes portés disparus. Huit minutes après son décollage, l’appareil s’est écrasé sur la surface gelée du lac Saint-Jean. Le pilote a subi des blessures sérieuses et a été secouru par un autre hélicoptère participant aux recherches. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée. L’aéronef a subi des dommages substantiels.

OK-TVY, un Boeing 737-800 exploité par Smartwings pour Air Transat sous l’indicatif TSC2527, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport El Catey Intl (MDCY), République Dominicaine à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC avec à son bord 178 passagers et 6 membres d’équipage. Au départ de MDCY à la vitesse V1, l’équipage a ressenti de la vibration modérée. Durant la montée, ils ont demandé aux personnels de l’aéroport d’inspecter la piste et des débris de pneus ont été retrouvés. Toutes les indications étaient normales dans le poste de pilotage et le vol a continué vers CYUL. À environ 30 nm au sud de CYUL, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison d’un possible problème avec le train d’atterrissage. À 2342z, l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre avec les services d’urgence en attente, mais une vibration modérée a été ressentie. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. L’aéronef s’est immobilisé sur la piste pour inspection et il a ensuite procédé vers le terminal. Une roue endommagée a été remplacée et l’appareil a été remis en service.

C-FJOU, an Airbus A321 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1730 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Basseterre / Robert L. Bradshaw Intl (TKPK), Saint Kitts and Nevis with 6 crew members and 181 passengers onboard. In cruise, approximately 45nm SE of New York / LaGuardia (KLGA), NY, a cabin crew member became incapacitated due to illness and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight. Order of priority for the cabin crew was reassigned to ensure all doors were manned for landing. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

N508DN, an Airbus A350-900 operated  by Delta Airlines, was conducting flight DAL159 from Detroit (KDTW) MI, USA to Seoul (RKSI), Korea. En route, about 735 nautical miles north of Yellowknife (CYZF), NT, the aircraft experienced surging in the #2 engine (Rolls Royce Trent XWB-84, S/N 21390) which led to a roll back and subsequent shutdown. The flight crew, in consultation with dispatch, elected to divert to Fairbanks (PAFA), Alaska. The aircraft landed without further incident and maintenance is inspecting the aircraft.

Sky Regional Airlines flight SKV7531, an Embraer E-170 (C-FEJD) aircraft, operating as Air Canada Express was descending into Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ) when the flight crew received parking brake not released EICAS message. The flight crew attempted was unable to clear the message. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and landed safely on runway 15L at CYYZ. Upon landing the flight was met by emergency and inspection vehicles. After preliminary inspection the aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.Maintenance found the Emergency/Parking Brake pressure switch to be at fault. The switch was replaced and the appropriate checks were completed as per the aircraft maintenance manual (AMM).

C-FYXF, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU 1827 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Palm Spring Intl (KPSP), CA with 6 crew members and 142 passengers onboard. During cruise, in the vicinity of Blue Earth Municipal (KSBU), MN, a cabin crew received minor injury and became incapacitated for the remainder of the flight. Order of priority for the cabin crew was reassigned to ensure all doors were manned for landing. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

WestJet Encore flight WEN3446, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 (C-GTWE) aircraft, departed Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON toward Ottawa /Macdonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON. Shortly after departure, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to a possible blown tire. A runway inspection found rubber debris, confirming the suspicion. The aircraft continued to Ottawa and landed on runway 25. ARFF were on standby for the uneventful landing and confirmed damage to the left inboard main wheel. The aircraft remained on the end of Runway 25 where maintenance crews could assess the damage. Passengers were off loaded onto buses and taken to the terminal.
