C-FSRW, a De Havilland DHC-8-400, operated by Jazz Aviation Ltd, was conducting flight JZA399 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC with 4 crew and 49 passengers on board. On the takeoff roll, the crew received an inboard anti-skid caution message and rejected the take off at less than 80 kts. When the aircraft came to a stop on the taxiway, a flight attendant reported smoke and flames coming from the left main gear assembly. The flight crew requested ARFF assistance. The wheel assembly fire extinguished prior to the ARFF arrival. ARFF inspected the aircraft and the aircraft was towed to the terminal.Maintenance personnel replaced the left main landing gear axle, the inboard left main tire, wheel speed transducer and brake in accordance with the aircraft maintenance manual.

Le 20 janvier 2020, l’aéronef de Havilland DHC 8 314 (immatriculation C GXAI, numéro de série 481) exploité par Air Inuit Ltée effectuait le vol régulier AIE820 depuis de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage (Québec) à destination de l'aéroport de Schefferville (Québec) avec 3 membres d’équipage et 42 passagers à bord. À l’atterrissage, au toucher des roues sur la piste 35 à 11 h 09, heure normale de l'Est, la partie inférieure du fuselage a heurté la piste. Après l'atterrissage, l’aéronef a circulé jusqu'au terminal pour le débarquement des passagers. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé; par contre, l’aéronef a subi d'importants dommages. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence ne s’est pas déclenchée.

C-GASL, an Embraer EMB-545 operated by Air Sprint Inc., was conducting flight ASP816 from Lexington (KLEX), KY USA to Calgary (CYYC), AB. Enroute, approximately 75 minutes from the destination, the Crew Alerting System (CAS) indicated an AVNX LH DU FAULT, and an AP FAULT. All navigation sources were lost on the captain's side along with multiple flags on the PFD and multiple failures associated with the multifunction keyboard pad. The #1 FMS failed, and the auto throttles disengaged. Control was transferred to the first officer and the QRH was actioned for the CAS items. Control of the pressurization was lost and the crew expedited descent while declaring a PAN PAN. ARFF was declined and the crew planned a shallow descent. A normal landing was carried out using the co-pilot instruments for reference.Maintenance rebooted the avionics system and all system resumed normal operation. Troubleshooting continues.

C-GLHU, a Hughes 369D (500D) aircraft operated by Heli Source Ltd, was doing external load operations in support of an aerial seismic program north of Fort McMurray, AB. Just after lift off from Firebag (CYFI), AB, one of three bags came loose from the external load and fell to the ground. There was no damage to people or property. The loads were being hooked up by the prime contractors loadmasters. It is not known whether the hook failed or if the hook was not latched properly. The hook assembly is being sent to the manufacturer for analysis.

C-GTHY, un appareil de type Aviat Aircraft Inc. A-1B (Christen) sur roues-skis en exploitation privée, avec à son bord 1 pilote, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le lac Mance situé à 8 milles nautiques (nm) au sud-sud-est de l’aéroport de La Sarre (CSR8), Québec. À environ 12,5 nm au sud de CSR8 l'appareil est entré en collision avec la surface gelée de la rivière La Sarre et a parcouru une distance d'environ 235 pieds avant de s'immobiliser. L'appareil a subi des dommages substantiels mais n'a pas pris feu. Le pilote a subi des blessures mortelles. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s'est déclenchée.

C-GNWD, a Cessna 208B Caravan operated by Northway Aviation Ltd. was conducting flight NAL845 from Poplar River (CZNG), MB to Winnipeg/St. Andrews (CYAV), MB with 1 pilot and 3 passenger on board. After landing, the aircraft was taxiing to the hangar when the pilot moved the fuel condition lever from flight idle to ground idle and, within a few seconds, the engine shut down. No attempt was made to restart the engine and the aircraft was towed to the hangar. The operator's maintenance found that the fuel and fuel filters were clean of contaminants. A minimum fuel flow check was completed and was found to be 17% below the target Ng of 45%. The FCU was replaced, ground checks completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWVH, a Fairchild SA227-AC operated by Perimeter Aviation LP as flight PAG415, departed Thompson (CYTH) MB for Shamattawa (CZTM) MB with 12 passengers and 2 crew members. During the landing rollout on Runway 19 at approximately 60 knots, aircraft directional control was lost and the aircraft encountered a runway excursion to the right and collided with a snow berm at a groundspeed of less than 20 knots. The right hand propeller (MT Propeller MTV-27-1) made contact with a snow berm and shattered upon impact. RCMP responded to the scene. The ELT did not activate and there were no injuries. A NOTAM was issued closing the airport until the aircraft was removed from the runway. The aircraft sustained damage to the left engine nacelle, nose gear doors, and right propeller. The reported runway condition at the time of occurrence was 100% compacted snow. Data retrieved from the aircraft's navigation system indicated the winds were 255 degress at 18 knots on short final prior to touchdown.

C-GLHO a Beechcraft 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Services (EVAS) was conducting flight EV121 from Gander Intl (CYQX), NL to Halifax Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS, which was a maintenance repositioning flight with crew only. After landing on runway 14 the EVAS crew was cleared to taxi "Delta" to hold short of runway 23 and read it back. C-GGNW, a de Havilland Dash 8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz, was conducting flight JZA8635 from CYHZ to Ottawa Intl (CYOW), ON, with 78 passengers. As JZA8635 accelerated on runway 23 for departure the crew noted that EV121 did not stop as directed and continued as if to cross in front of the departing aircraft. JZA8635 applied braking just as the tower controller told them to reject the takeoff. The ground controller also called EV121 directing them to stop. JZA8635 stopped about 30 meters from the intersection, EV121 stopped just short of entering the active runway. The Jazz flight taxied back to runway 23 and departed for CYOW. EVAS has conducted an internal SMS review.

C-FVEG, a de Havilland DHC-6-300 operated by West Wind Aviation Ltd, was conducting flight WEW120 from La Ronge/Barber Field (CYVC), SK to a private aerodrome at Laonil Lake, SK. At approximately 40 nautical miles northeast of CYVC, the flight crew noticed the indicated right engine oil pressure was low. The flight crew carried out the emergency checklist, performed a precautionary engine shut down, declared an emergency, and elected to return to CYVC. The aircraft landed safely in CYVC. The operator's maintenance is troubleshooting the oil indicating system.

N864DA, un Boeing 777-200 exploité par Delta Airlines Inc. sous l'indicatif DAL148 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Las Vegas/McCarran Intl (KLAS), NV à destination de Paris/Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France. À 0059z à environ 125 miles marins (nm) au nord-ouest de Havre-Saint-Pierre (CYGV), Québec, l’équipage a déclaré avoir un problème de pressurisation et a demandé une descente pour le FL300 ainsi qu’un déroutement vers l’aéroport de New York/John F Kennedy (KJFK), NY. À 0115z, lorsque l'appareil se trouvait à 25 nm au nord de CYGV, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence et a demandé d’être dérouté vers l’aéroport de Boston/ General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl (KBOS), MA. Le vol a ensuite été transféré au centre de contrôle de Boston à 0135z. L’aéronef s’est posé à KBOS à 0226z. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FFFS. a Hawker Siddeley HS-748-2A operated by Wasaya Airways as flight WP806, was enroute from Fort Severn (CYER), ON to Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON with two flight crew members on board. While in cruise, the right engine fire warning light illuminated. The flight crew reduced engine power and the fire warning light then went out. Inspection of the right engine/nacelle area from the cockpit window and engine indication systems revealed no anomalies. The crew elected to keep the right engine running and eventually advanced the power back to cruise without receiving a fire warning indication. The crew declared a Pan Pan and continued the flight to their destination where the aircraft then landed safely. The operator's maintenance inspection of the fire warning system revealed a faulty wire loop. The wire loop was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

L'Aero Vodochody L-29 Delfin immatriculé C-GGRP effectuait un vol récréatif local depuis l'aéroport de Sorel, Qc (CSY3) avec seul le pilote à son bord. Lors du retour à CSY3, en approche finale pour la piste, l'appareil a fait un atterrissage dur avant le seuil de piste. Le pilote n'a pas été blessé, mais l'appareil a subi des dommages importants.

OK-TVX, a Boeing 737-800, operated by Smartwings as Sunwing Airlines flight SWG600, departed from Toronto Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ) for Cayo Coco (MUCC). One flight crew member experienced a medical emergency; a Pan Pan was declared and the aircraft returned to CYYZ uneventfully.

C-FPWE, un Airbus A320 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif ACA2339, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Hamilton/John C. Munro Int’l Airport (CYHM). Le décollage de la piste 24L a été fait après C-GKTS, un Airbus 330 exploité par Air Transat sous l'indicatif TSC398 qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis CYUL à destination de Punta Cana International Airport en République Dominicaine (MDPC). Une perte d'espacement de turbulence de sillage est survenue lors de la montée initiale, lorsque le ACA2339 s'est retrouvé 4,1 miles marins (nm) derrière le TSC398 alors que l'espacement requis était de 5 nm. Aucune turbulence de sillage n'a été rapportée et les 2 appareils ont poursuivi leurs vols à leur destination respective sans encombre.

Air Canada flight ACA739, an Airbus A330 (C-GEGC) aircraft, was on route from Toronto (CYYZ) to San Francisco (KSFO), when the flight notified Cleveland Centre of a flap and hydraulic issue and requested a return to CYYZ. After arriving in Canadian airspace, the crew declared a PAN PAN in order to coordinate a landing with zero flaps. The crew requested aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) standing by in Toronto to inspect the brakes on arrival. The aircraft landed without further incident and taxied off the runway under its own power.Prior to departure aircraft had MEL “Flap Sys 2 INOP and Yellow HYD Pump Low Pressure Alert”. In cruise flight crew received yellow hydraulic low indication. The flight crew in consultation with MOC decided to return to YYZ.Maintenance found the pressure switch to be leaking. The pressure switch and o-ring were replaced and the aircraft was returned to service after the appropriate AMM service checks.

C-GGOK un Dash-8 Q400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif de vol JZA8716 était immobilisé dans la baie de dégivrage numéro 6 de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL). Lorsque l'opération de dégivrage fut terminée, le technicien s'est approché du stabilisateur horizontal pour effectuer une vérification tactile de la surface. La flèche du camion nacelle est entrée en contact avec le dessous du stabilisateur causant des dommages mineurs.  Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GYJZ a de Havilland Dash 8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation was conducting flight JZA8639 from Halifax Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Ottawa Intl (CYOW) ON with 43 passengers. On departure the crew selected the gear up and received a gear inop caution light and 3 red lights. The crew actioned the quick reference handbook and completed the alternate gear extension and got 3 green lights. The crew requested to return to CYHZ. The crew did not declare an emergency but did request that ARFF be on standby for landing. The aircraft landed without further incident, stopped on the taxiway and was towed to the gate. Maintenance did an analysis of the fault and located broken wires at 3261-J23. The wires were repaired, gear swings were performed and tested serviceable. The aircraft was released to service.

The Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service BK117, C-GNBH, had departed Hanna (CHD3), AB on a MEDEVAC flight to Calgary Foothills Hospital (CMT3) when, in the vicinity of Drumheller (CDH2), AB, they experienced an electrical burning smell. The flight immediately diverted to CDH2 where the patient was transferred to ground transportation services. After a discussion with maintenance a ground run was undertaken with the heater unit in the off position. After a successful ground run the aircraft was ferried to Calgary (CYYC), AB. Maintenance found the cold weather fan blades seized. The unit was MEL'd and a replace fan unit was installed.

C-GJWS, a WestJet Boeing 737-800, was operating as flight WJA209 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Victoria (CYYJ), BC. During short final at CYYJ the aircraft encountered a flock of geese and struck approximately 10 of them. The crew executed a missed approach and diverted to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. With ARFF on standby, the aircraft was given priority clearance and it landed without further incident. The aircraft nose cone had been punctured by the impact. There were no injuries.

C-FTUU, a Piper 44-180 aircraft operated by Canlink Aviation Ltd (Moncton Flight College) was conducting a training flight from Moncton Airport (CYQM), NB to Bathurst Airport (CZBF), NB and returning to CYQM  with one instructor and 2 students onboard. Upon completing a second landing (touch and go) at CZBF, the aircraft drifted left on the landing roll. The student pilot brought the aircraft back to the centerline. As the aircraft continued slowing, it started drifting left again and the instructor took control. The propeller began striking the runway at which point the instructor shutdown the engines and the aircraft came to a stop on the runway. The pilots evacuated. There were no injuries.  The aircraft had experienced a left main gear collapse caused by a failure of the piston tube. This damaged the left prop, left engine and left wing. There was a large spill of hydraulic fluid noted at the point of touchdown. The runway was NOTAMed closed until the aircraft could be removed. Piper has provided instructions on an inspection process using Eddy Current to check for corrosion or cracking through the bolt hole that is used to hold the lower plug of the piston assembly. Piper recommends this testing be started at 6500 hours time in service and every 700 hrs thereafter. There is believed to have been a pre-existing fatigue crack on this aircraft which had 7900 hours.

The Jazz Aviation LP de Havilland Dash 8-400, C-GJZF, operating as JZA133 on a flight from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Calgary (CYYC), AB experienced a flap control failure that precluded the deploying of landing flaps. The crew, in preparation for a zero flap landing, requested that ARFF be standing by for the landing. The aircraft carried out a zero flap landing and taxied to the gate.Update: Maintenance replaced a pressure switch and the L/H flap position transducer. The system was rigged and function tested. The aircraft was returned to service.c-g

C-GWJK, a de Havilland Dash 8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3260 from Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC to Kelowna Intl (CYLW), BC with 4 crew members and 23 passengers on board. The crew conducted a missed approach at CYLW due to poor weather conditions. After holding in the CYLW area for better weather it was decided to divert to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. During descent into CYVR the aircraft was below minimum reserve fuel and therefore the crew declared a MAY DAY. The aircraft landed without further incident and with ARFF standing by.

The Jazz Aviation LP de Havilland Dash 8-400, C-GJZX, operating as JZA552, on a flight from Victoria (CYYJ), BC to Calgary (CYYC), AB experienced a loss of pressure in the #1 hydraulic system. A PAN PAN was declared with Calgary terminal. The aircraft subsequently landed on Runway 35R at CYYC and was towed to the main terminal. Runway 35R was closed for cleaning for 25 minutes.Maintenance found that the #1 EDP PX Line was loose allowing hydraulic fluid to escape. Fluid filters were inspected and the #1 EDP and #1 Hydraulic SPU were replaced due to being run dry. The #1 hydraulic system was bled and leak checked and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FFFS, a Hawker Siddeley HS-748 Series 2A aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways LP, was conducting a flight from Wiebenville (CXX2), ON to Kingfisher Lake (CNM5), ON. The aircraft was on approach to Runway 30 in dim/flat light conditions. The touchdown was made on the unplowed overrun area, approximately 50 feet prior to the threshold. The aircraft completed the landing on the runway without further event. The aircraft sustained damage to a brake line and nose landing gear door. The operator's maintenance personnel conducted a rough landing inspection. The aircraft returned to Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON under an additional flight authority for further repairs.

C-GWVH, a Fairchild SA227-AC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP., was conducting flight PAG403 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Gods Lake Narrows (CYGO), MB. Shortly after levelling off in cruise at 15 000 feet ASL, the left engine fire warning light illuminated, followed by a CAS (Crew Alerting System) message for ENG FIRE. The flight crew performed the emergency checklist items for an engine fire warning and shut down the engine. The flight crew declared an emergency and elected to return to CYTH. The fire warning light extinguished after all checklist items were completed. The subsequent landing was conducted with the left engine inoperative. The flight crew brought the aircraft to a stop on the runway and ARFF responded. The passengers and crew deplaned and the aircraft was towed to the apron. There was no sign of fire. The operator's maintenance personnel inspected the fire detection system and replaced all 5 fire detection probes.

C-GPCE, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Beech 1900D, was conducting flight PCO615 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC, to Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies Intl (CYXC), BC, with 2 crew members and 12 passengers on board. During the approach into CYXC, when the crew selected “GEAR DOWN”, the landing gear in transit light remained illuminated and none of the landing gear down lights illuminated. The crew conducted a missed approach and requested radar vectors to allow them to conduct their abnormal landing gear indication checklists. On completion of their checklists and manual extension of the landing gear, they had heard the landing gear extend, had a green nose landing gear down indication and had no landing gear warning horn with the flaps in the landing configuration. The crew determined they were safe to land with the indications present and requested the approach to CYXC with ARFF to be on standby as a precaution. The aircraft landed without incident.Maintenance conducted a number of landing gear swings and did functional checks on the landing gear electrical systems with no fault found. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GUBH, an Airbus 330-200 operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC798 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Puerto Vallarta/Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz Intl. (MMPR), Mexico.  During cruise, flight attendant became ill and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight.  Flight crew communicated with Medlink and medical assistance was provided by onboard doctor. Cabin crew positions were reassigned in priority of occupancy.  The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GEOQ, a Boeing 767-300 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1665 from Fort Myers/Southwest Florida Intl. (KRSW), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During descent from cruise altitude, flight attendant became incapacitated due to injury and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight.  Order of priority for the cabin crew was reassigned to ensure all doors were manned for landing.  The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FJNX, an Airbus A321 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA119 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Vancourver Intl (CYVR), BC with 6 crew members and 190 passengers on board. During cruise in the vicinity of Gull Lake, SK, the flight crew detected a smoke odour in the cockpit and the cabin crew reported a burning smell in the forward galley. The flight crew turned off PACK 1 and 2, declared a PAN PAN, and diverted to Calgary, Intl (CYYC), AB. The flight landed without further incident. The operator's maintenance determined the source of smoke was from the left-hand recirculation fan. The fault was addressed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWSZ, a West Jet Airlines Boeing 737-800, was operating as flight WS4012 from Edmonton International (CYEG), AB to Fort Mackay / Firebag (CYFI), AB. During cruise the flight crew noticed a burning smell in the flight deck. The crew declared an emergency and diverted to Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB. The aircraft landed without further incident. Company maintenance found that the source of smoke was from the first officer's audio panel. The audio panel was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

N815NW, an Airbus A330 operated by Delta Airlines, was conducting flight DAL 162 from Minneapolis-Saint Paul Intl (KMSP), US to Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (EHAM), Netherlands. During the cruise portion of the flight, a flight attendant noticed smoke and sparks from a screw head on the aft galley heated floor and discharged a fire extinguisher. The flight crew were notified and they consulted the QRH and pulled the associated circuit breakers. After coordination with dispatch and maintenance, the crew declared a MAYDAY and diverted to Keflavik Intl (BIKF), Iceland. The flight landed without further incident. Maintenance found discoloration in portions of the galley floor replaced the floor panel. The aircraft was returned to service with the floor heat unserviceable in accordance with the Minimum Equipment List (MEL).

C-GYCV, a De Havilland DHC8-300 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines, was conducting flight PVL411 from Deer Lake (CYDF) , NL to St. John’s Intl. (CYYT), NL. When the aircraft was approximately 15NM final from RWY 16 the crew contacted Gander Area Control Center and declared an emergency due to a hydraulic failure. The aircraft landed uneventfully with airport rescue and firefighting standing by. Company maintenance determined that a flared fitting on the number one (#1) hydraulic system manifold had cracked which depleted the fluid level below the quantity required for the system to work. The aircraft was repaired and returned to service. The company has submitted a Service Difficulty Report to Transport Canada.

C-FKCK an Airbus A320-211 operated by Air Canada was conducting flight AC783 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Los Angeles Intl. (KLAX), CA when the flight crew reported a decrease in navigation performance and decided to divert to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. The flight crew declated a PAN PAN due to concern over possible hot brakes from an overweight landing. The aircraft landed uneventfully with Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) standing by.

C-FCMR, a Central Mountain Air Beech 1900D aircraft, was operating as flight GLR560 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Quesnel, BC (CYQZ) with two pilots and ten passengers on board. During the initial climb, the flight crew and the passengers noticed blue smoke in the cockpit and cabin that was both visible and odorous. The flight crew conducted trouble shooting to identify the source. This included checking the CB panels, turning off the blower vents, and reducing the cabin temperature. The crew requested and received a clearance to return to CYVR due to smoke in the cabin. CYVR tower initiated a precautionary ARFF standby but, with the smoke dissipating in the cabin, assistance was not required. The aircraft taxied in without further incident.Maintenance tested the air conditioning blower motors with no fault found. After multiple ground runs, the smoke or fumes condition could not be replicated. The aircraft has returned to service.

C-GMJJ, a de Havilland DHC-8-100, operated by Central Mountain Air, was conducting flight GLR730 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC, to Prince George (CYXS), BC, with 3 crewmembers and 20 passengers on board. During the takeoff roll, the crew set power at 90% torque. After rotation, the first officer noted the torque setting on the #1 engine had inadvertently risen to 101% torque. After gear retraction, the first officer pulled back the #1 power lever to reset it to maintain 90%. This resulted in a significant split between the #1 and #2 power levers. The torque setting then dropped close to zero and the captain felt a significant performance loss of the #1 engine concurrent with yaw. The captain called for the emergency procedure and the FO stated that the propeller did not feather. The crew then shut down the engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW120A) and the propeller successfully feathered. The aircraft returned to CYLW and landed safely. After extensive troubleshooting, maintenance replaced the #1 engine hydro mechanical unit and the aircraft has since been returned to service.

C-FIJZ, a Jazz Aviation LP CRJ-900 was conducting flight AC8624 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Ronald Reagan Washington National (KDCA), DC. During initial approach and prior to landing gear extension, flight crew received a brake overheat warning indication from right-hand outboard brake. Flight crew requested emergency services to be present upon landing. Fire department inspected the brakes prior to taxi in to terminal and found no indication of brake overheat.  Maintenance found faulty sensor was the cause of indication.

C-GVVH, un Boeing 737-800 exploité par Sunwing Airlines Inc. sous l’indicatif SWG555 était en préparation pour effectuer un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC à destination de l’aéroport international de Cancún (MMUN) au Mexique, avec 179 passagers et 6 membres d’équipage à bord. Pendant les préparatifs pré-envolée, un membre du personnel de la cabine a subi une incapacité physique et a reçu des soins médicaux à la barrière. La personne a été remplacée et le vol a quitté CYUL sans autre difficulté.

Jazz flight JZA7930, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (C-FZJA) aircraft, on route from St Louis, MO (KSTL) to Toronto, ON (CYYZ) received a flap fail message. The flight crew advised ATC of a flap failure and that they would be carrying out a flap zero landing, requiring full runway length. No emergency was declared however, they requested ARFF standing by on arrival. JZA7930 landed and taxied to the gate without further incident.

Jazz flight JZA612, a De Havilland DHC-8-300 (registration C-GTAT) aircraft, was on descent towards Toronto, Ontario (CYYZ) when the number 2 engine intake heater would not come on. The flight crew declared Pan Pan for preferential handling due to icing conditions and other flights holding to land. The flight landed without issue.

N695CA, un CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) exploité par Endeavor Air sous l’indicatif EDV5526 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC à destination de l’aéroport Hartsfield/Jackson Atlanta Intl. (KATL), GA aux États-Unis avec à son bord 76 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage de la piste 06R, une indication de surchauffe des freins est apparue. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence, est revenu se poser sur la piste 24L sans encombre et par la suite l’appareil a été remorqué à la barrière. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni de dommage à l’appareil. L’inspection post-envolée a établi qu’il s’agissait d'une indication erronée.

C-GIAB, un Dash-8-300 (DH8C) exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE852 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Val-d’Or (CYVO), QC à destination de Kuujjuaq (CYVP), QC avec à son bord 29 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage. Lorsque l’appareil était en approche et que le train a été sorti, le train d’atterrissage principal de droite indiquait qu’il n’était pas barré. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour sortir le train d'atterrissage manuellement. Par la suite, toutes les roues étaient descendues avec des indications normales et l’équipage est revenu se poser à CYVP sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni de dommage à l’appareil.

C-GNLN, un B7327-200 exploité par Nolinor Inc. sous l’indicatif NRL942 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Mirabel Intl. (CYMX), QC à destination de Val-d’Or (CYVO), QC avec 6 membres d’équipage et 61 passagers à bord. Lorsque le train d'atterrissage a été rentré après le décollage, l’équipage a reçu une indication de désaccord de la roue de nez. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH). Lorsque le train a été sorti, toutes les roues étaient descendues avec des indications normales. L’appareil est revenu se poser sur la piste 06 à CYMX avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre, il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni de dommage à l’appareil.

Un Boeing 767-300 exploité Austrian Airlines sous l'indicatif AUA74, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) à destination de Vienne-Schwechat, Autriche (LOWW). Le décollage de la piste 24L a été fait après l’Airbus 330-200 exploité par Air Transat sous l'indicatif TSC258 qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis CYUL à destination de Paris Charles de Gaule, France (LFPG). Une perte d’espacement de turbulence de sillage est survenue lors de la montée initiale, lorsque le AUA74 s’est retrouvé 3,7 miles marins (nm) derrière le TSC258 alors que l’espacement requis était de 4 nm. Aucune turbulence de sillage n’a été rapportée et les 2 appareils ont poursuivi leurs vols à leurs destinations respectives sans encombre.

C-GAPY, an Airbus A319-114 aircraft operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA229 from Calgary Int'l (CYYC), AB to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC with 5 crewmembers and 112 passengers on board. At 30 000 feet ASL, near Kelowna, BC, the #2 engine (CFM Int'l CFM56-5A5) began to stall with some visible sparking. The crew reduced power to idle on the affected engine and declared a PAN PAN with ATC. The aircraft landed safely at CYVR with ARFF standing by.Maintenance conducted an initial borescope that revealed wear to High Pressure Compressor (HPC) stages 6 and 7 that was beyond limits. The company stated that it was a high time engine with only 1100 cycles remaining and that an engine change was conducted to return it to service.

C-FFNC, un Boeing 737-400 exploité par First Air sous l’indicatif FAB101 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW) à destination d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) avec 44 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage à bord. Avant la descente, l’équipage a remarqué une anomalie d’indication des volets et a demandé la présence des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) pour l'arrivée à CYFB. En approche les volets n’ont pas bougé lorsqu’ils ont été sélectionnés. L’équipage a complété liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a réussi à baisser les volets à la position FLAP 15 avec le système de secours des volets. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre et il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil. Le transmetteur des volets (flap transmitter) a été changé et l'appareil a été remis en service.

C-GPWE, un de Havilland, Dash-8 Q400 exploité par WestJet Encore sous l’indicatif WEN3441 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Moncton/Greater Moncton Intl. (CYQM), NB à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON, avec à son bord 66 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en vol de croisière à environ 175 miles marins à l’est de l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC, une perte du fluide hydraulique du système numéro 1 est survenue. L’équipage a effectué une diversion à CYUL, a déclaré un état d’urgence et les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 06R sans encombre, il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni de dommage à l’appareil.

C-FSOU, un Dash-8-300 (DH8C) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8684, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC à destination de CFB Bagotville (CYBG), QC avec 49 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage. Immédiatement après le décollage de la piste 24L, la roue intérieure du train d’atterrissage gauche s’est détachée de l’appareil et est tombée sur la piste. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et est resté en vol environ 1 heure pour bruler du carburant et réduire le poids de l’appareil avant de revenir se poser à CYUL. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 24R sans encombre avec 1 roue restant sur le train d’atterrissage gauche. L’appareil a dégagé la piste sur la voie de circulation B2 et a été immobilisé. Les passagers ont été acheminés au terminal par autobus. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni autre dommage à l’appareil.

N824AE, un Embraer 135 exploité par Envoy Air Inc. sous l’indicatif ENY3989 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC à destination de LaGuardia (KLGA), NY aux États-Unis avec 44 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage. À environ 18 miles marins au sud-ouest de CYUL, alors que l’appareil passait 11 000 pieds en montée, l’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence en raison d’un problème de pressurisation et est immédiatement redescendu à 10 000 pieds. L’équipage a avisé l’ATC que la situation était stabilisée et qu’il poursuivait le vol à destination de KLGA.

N32WC a Piaggio Aero Industries P180 was on approach to Windsor Intl. (CYQG), ON when the pilot requested a flyby of the tower to check position of left main landing gear. The tower reported that the landing gear appeared to be extended and the pilot requested to fly an orbit near the airport prior to the final approach. When cleared to land, the pilot requested Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) to be on standby. The aircraft landed uneventfully, came to a stop on the runway and was towed to the hangar.

C-GVKC, a Pilatus PC-12 operated by North Star Air Ltd, was operating as flight BF708 from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON to Bearskin Lake (CNE3), ON, with 2 crew and 8 passengers onboard. During the climb through 5 700 feet ASL, BF708 was cleared by ATC to climb and maintain FL190. At FL190 the aircraft did not level off and continued the climb to FL196. ATC asked BF708 to verify the aircraft's current altitude at which time BF708 descended to FL190. A loss of separation occurred with aircraft C-FJJH, a Beech A100 operated by Thunder Airlines as flight THU104, that was enroute from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Deer Lake (CYVZ), ON at FL200. Vertical separation between the two aircraft reduced to 400 feet vertically where 1000 feet is required. There were no TCAS resolution advisories from either aircraft.

C-FUJR, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA248 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Halifax Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS with 172 passengers and 6 crew. During the landing on Runway 14, the aircraft overran the end of the runway and came to a stop approximately 250 feet from the end of the runway. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft. The tires and brakes were replaced as a precaution and the aircraft was returned to service. The TSB deployed investigators to the site.

C-GKFA, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus 321-211, was conducting flight ROU1823 from Puerto Plata/ Gregorio Luperón Intl. (MDPP), Dominican Republic to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC. During climb in vicinity of Providenciales Intl. (MBPV), UK, flight attendant became incapacitated and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight.  Order of priority for cabin crew was reassigned.  Flight landed uneventfully.

C-FKCO, un Airbus 320 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif de vol AC912 avec à son bord 5 membres d'équipage et 146 passagers s'apprêtait à effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau intl à destination de Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl - Fort Lauderdale (Floride). Suivant le démarage des moteurs, le moteur droit (CFM56-5A1) s'est arrêté. L'appareil a été ramené à la passerelle de débarquement. Plusieurs test on été effectué et aucune défectuosité n'a permis de déterminer la raison de l'arrêt du moteur. L'appareil a été remis en service et a effectué 19 secteurs depuis et aucune anomalie du mopteur droit n'est survenue. Personne n'a été blessé.

C-GVJV a commercially registered Embraer EMB-500 Phenom 100 aircraft was being operated by a single pilot, and was inbound to Lake Simcoe Regional (CYLS), ON from Columbia Metropolitain (KCAE), SC. On arrival at CYLS, the pilot initially conducted an instrument approach to Runway 10, but performed a missed approach due to a lack of visual references. Subsequently, an approach was performed for Runway 28. After touchdown, during the landing rollout, the aircraft went off the end of the runway into a field and came to rest 275 feet past the end of Runway 28. There were no injuries and no obvious visible damage to the aircraft. The TSB is investigating.

C-GSPW un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif de vol AIE752 avec à son bord 4 membres d'équipage et 28 passagers effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Montréal Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), Québec à destination de Val-d'Or (CYVO) Québec. Suivant l'atterrissage à CYVO l'équipage de conduite a reçu une indication de feu du groupe auxiliaire de puissance (APU) ainsi que l'indication que la bouteille extincteur s'était déchargée. Constatant que l'indication de feu était toujours présente, l'équipage de conduite a immobilisé l'appareil sur la piste et a demandé la présence du sauvetage et lutte contre le feu en cas d'accident (ARFF) afin de vérifier s'il y avait présence de fumée ou de flammes à l'arrière de l'appareil. N'ayant reçu aucune confirmation de présence de fumée ou flammes l'appareil a circulé jusqu'à son stationnement prévu et a procédé à un débarquement rapide des passagers puisque l'indication de feu était toujours présente. Tous les occupants ont évacué l'appareil. Le personnel ARFF est arrivé quelques minutes plus tard. Une vérification de l'APU a permis de constater qu'il n'y avait aucune trace d'incendie.Personne n'a été blessé et l'appareil n'a subi aucun dommage.

C-GWWJ, the WestJet Boeing 737-800, was operating as flight WJA1485 from Palm Springs (KPSP), CA to Edmonton (CYEG), AB. During cruise flight the cabin crew reported to the flight crew that smoke was coming from a coffee maker. The cabin crew turned off the coffee maker and the smoke dissipated. The flight continued to CYEG without further incident. No emergency was declared and there were no injuries. Company maintenance replaced the coffee maker unit.

Air Canada Boeing 777-300 aircraft (AC872, C-FITU) was on climb out from Toronto /Lester B. Pearson International (CYYZ), ON when the cabin crew reported an odour and smoke in the forward cabin. The crew isolated the smoke coming from the In-Flight Entertainment System (IFE) in seat 9D. The IFE was selected off and the smoke dissipated. There was no emergency declared and the flight continued to Frankfurt (EDDF), Germany. Upon arrival, maintenance replaced the screen in seat 9D IAW AMM. The unit was checked serviceable with no further smoke evident.

C-FZUJ, an Air Canada Airbus 319 aircraft was operating as flight ACA976 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Los Cabos Intl.(MMSD), Mexico. During cruise the flight crew felt the cabin pressure changing. The cabin pressure indicated 4300ft/minute and the cabin was climbing. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks and executed a rapid depressurization drill. No emergency was declared, the flight landed without further incident. Maintenance found a faulty automatic cabin pressure control unit.

C-FIYA, an Air Canada Rouge 767-300, was operating as flight ROU1714 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Bridgetown/Grantley Adams Intl. (TBPB) Barbados. In the vicinity of L.F. Wade Intl. (TXKF), Bermuda a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue duties. These duties were assumed by other cabin crew and flight landed uneventfully.

The Privately operated Cessna 510, C-GSAB, was operating from Springbank (CYBW), AB to Lloydminister (CYLL), AB. Shortly after a cross-generator start of the right engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW615F-A), the pilot received an Engine Control SYS R annunciator light. While completing the abnormal checklist, smoke entered the cabin. The engines were shut down and the aircraft was evacuated. No emergency was declared. The pilot and 3 passengers received no injuries. Maintenance personnel determined the engine overheated due to a lack of N1 rotation on the right engine. Carbon fiber engine components had burnt due to the heat and resulted in smoke entering the cabin.

C-GSWX, the Sunwest Aviation Ltd. Beech 1900D, was operating as flight CNK400 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Bonnyville (CYBF), AB. Following departure from CYYC Runway 35L, upon rotation, the flight crew noticed a 50 rpm split between the left and right engines (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-67D). The left propeller control was reduced 50 rpm to match the full forward right propeller control. Once confirmed, the left propeller control was returned to full forward. As CNK400 was climbing through 1000 feet agl, the master warning and right oil pressure annunciator lights illuminated. The flight crew noticed the right oil pressure gauge falling rapidly to zero, and excessive oil leakage from the right engine. The right engine was shut down, an emergency was declared and the aircraft was leveled at 6000 feet asl. The right engine was secured and the QRH was actioned. CNK400 returned to CYYC, landed normally and exited onto Taxiway A3. The aircraft was met by ARFF and shut down on the taxiway. Large amounts of oil continued to leak from the right engine. Company maintenance found the propeller governor feather tube retainer plate retaining plate screws damaged. Propeller governor replace and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FACF, a De Havilland DHC-8-311 operated by Jazz was conducting flight JZA724 from Gaspé Airport, QC (CYGP) to Îles-de-la-Madeleine, QC (CYGR). During the approach to CYGR a failure of the #2 hydraulic occurred. The flight crew declared an emergency at 02:38 AST and after consideration of the crosswind conditions at CYGR they elected to divert to Moncton Intl Airport, NB (CYQM). The aircraft landed without further incident at 03:29 AST with aircraft rescue and firefighting on standby.Maintenance determined that the nose gear down lock pressure line was leaking and the fluid level had depleted. The aircraft was repaired and then returned to service.

The privately owned Cessna 152 aircraft (registration N48522) was flying circuits at the Ottawa Rockliffe Airport (CYRO). When the aircraft was on final approach to Runway 27 the engine lost power (Lycoming O-235) and it was unable to maintain altitude; the aircraft collided with terrain just short of the runway. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, received a minor injury; the aircraft was substantially damaged.

G-TAWN un Boeing 737-800 exploité par Sunwing sous l'indicatif de vol SW614 s'apprêtait à circuler au sol au départ de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau intl à destination de Vilo Acuña Intl/Cayo Largo del Sur (Cuba) selon les instructions du signaleur au sol lorsque le moteur droit de l'aéronef est entré en collision avec un tracteur remorque immobilisé sur sa trajectoire. La nacelle du moteur a été endommagée, toutefois la nature exacte des dommages au moteur est inconnue pour l'instant. Personne n'a été blessé et les passagers ont été transférés à un autre appareil par l'intermédiaire de véhicules de transport de passagers.

N14148 un Embraer-145XR exploité par Commutair sous l'indicatif de vol UCA5005 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Newark Liberty Intl/Newark (KEWR) NJ aux États-Unis à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL) Québec. Lors de l'atterrissage sur la piste 24R à CYUL l'aéronef n'a pu s'immobiliser avant le bout de piste temporairement déplacé dû à des travaux de réfection sur la piste. La longueur de piste disponible était de 7068 pieds. Suit au dépassement de piste, l'appareil a été autorisé à circuler sur la portion de piste fermée afin de se rendre à la passerelle de débarquement. Des précipitations verglaçantes prévalaient au moment de l'atterrissage. L'appareil n'a subi aucun dommage et personne n'a été blessé.

C-FWJS, a WestJet Boeing 737-800, was operating as flight WJA1877 from Maui/Kahului (PHOG), HI to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC, with a crew of six and 148 passengers. During the approach one of the flight crew members was unable to perform duties. A PAN PAN was declared, the aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-GOIF, an Airbus A321 was operating as positioning flight Air Transat TSC377 from Liberia/ Daniel Oduber Quirós Intl. (MRLB), Costa Rica to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC. During the climb, passing through 14000 feet, the cabin crew experienced an issue with an emergency exit indoor panel. The flight crew received an indication for the right over wing exit unsecured, followed by a call from the cabin crew reporting that there was an aural alarm in the cabin that a large panel had fallen off of the exit door, and a hissing sound. The flight crew returned to MRLB, declared a PAN PAN, and briefed the cabin crew. The landing was uneventful.

C-FSOU un DHC-8-300 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l’indicatif de vol JZA857 avec à son bord 4 membres d’équipage et 45 passagers effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL) Québec, à destination de Rouyn (CYUY) Québec. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait à environ 75 milles nautiques au nord-ouest de CYUL, l’équipage de conduite a observé une diminution du liquide hydraulique du réservoir numéro 2. L’équipage de conduite a effectué la liste de vérification applicable, a transmis un message PAN PAN et a demandé un retour vers CYUL. Lors de l’approche de la piste 06R à CYUL, l’équipage de conduite a sorti manuellement le train d’atterrissage et l’appareil s’est posé sans problème. Personne n’a été blessé et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage.

C-GOJG, a Cessna 525 aircraft, operated by C-GHGR Holdings, was enroute from Casper (KCPR), WY to Western Nebraska Regional/William B Heilig Field/Scottsbluff (KBFF), NE, with the pilot and 4 passengers on board. During cruise at 25000 feet ASL, the pilot heard a bang followed by a sudden, slight change in pitch attitude. The pilot immediately regained pitch control and continued to destination. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed uneventfully. An inspection revealed that the right lower engine cowling departed the aircraft and struck the outer portion of the right horizontal stab. The aircraft remained in Scottsbluff, Nebraska for repairs. Post-accident examination of the airplane revealed the right engine lower cowl separated from the airplane, struck the right engine upper cowl, and damaged about a 1/3 third of the outboard side of the right horizontal stabilizer and elevator resulting in substantial damage. The cowl fastener assemblies were all quarter-turn fasteners. Two consecutive fasters located at the forward inboard corner of the right engine lower cowl (labeled receptacles 10 and 11 in Figure 1) were missing. A third fastener, which joined the right engine upper and lower cowls through an angle/tab, were missing (see Figure 1). The receptacles associated with these fasteners did not display tearing/fractures. All the remaining right engine lower cowl fasteners were in place. The NTSB investigated (CEN20LA041).

C-GSPW, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE753 effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Val-D’Or (CYVO), QC, à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC. Lors de la montée initiale, l’équipage a entendu un bruit répétitif et a ressenti une vibration. Ils ont noté une hausse de la température des gaz d’échappement du moteur #2 (EGT #2) et ont effectué la liste de vérification associée. Le bruit, la vibration et la température des gaz d’échappement n'ont pas changé et l’équipage a effectué une fermeture du moteur #2 (moteur droit). L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et est revenu se poser à CYVO sans encombre à 0127z avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. Suite à une inspection du moteur #2 sur la piste, le cône moteur a été retrouvé sur la piste, mais aucun autre danger immédiat n’a été observé et l’aéronef a été conduit au terminal sur son propre pouvoir.

C-GKTS, an Airbus A330-342 was operating Air Transat flight TS111 from Paris/Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QB. While on cruise 320 NM SSE of Reykjavík/ Keflavík (BIKF), Iceland, a Flight crew became incapacitated. Flight diverted to BIKF and landed without further incident.

C-GOCD, a Boeing 737-800 operated by WestJet Airlines Ltd., was conducting flight WJA1484 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Palm Springs International Airport (KPSP), California. While in cruise a  cabin crew member became incapacitated. The captain was advised and the duties were distributed to the other cabin crew members for landing. No further assistance was required.

C-FYAG, a Fairchild SA227-AC operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting a test flight while operating under a Transport Canada Experimental Flight Permit. The aircraft was equipped with a flight testing air data boom mounted to the left wing tip. Approximately 65nm north of Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB, the aircraft's boom started vibrating and the flight crew elected to terminate the test flight. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft returned to CYWG for an uneventful landing. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft, made adjustments to the boom equipment, and returned the aircraft to service.

C-GAWS, a Boeing 737-800 operated by Westjet, was conducting flight WS1882 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Kailua/Ellison Onizuka Kona Intl. at Keahole (PHKO), HI. During cruise, flight attendant #3 became ill and incapacitated. Captain was advised and Medlink was contacted. Duties were distributed to the remaining flight attendants for landing. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FYAG, a Fairchild SA227-AC operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting a test flight while operating under a Transport Canada Experimental Flight Permit. At approximately 70nm west of Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB, the flight crew conducted a scheduled engine shutdown. Subsequently the crew was unable to restart the engine (GARRETT, TPE331-11U-612G). The non-operating engine was secured, an emergency was declared, and an uneventful landing was carried out in CYWG.

C-FHZZ, a Boeing 737-800 operated by Sunwing Airlines Inc., was conducting flight SWG407 from Punta Cana Intl. (MDPC), Dominican Republic to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. During cruise at FL370, Flight crew received a TCAS TA followed by TCAS RA “Descend”. The flight crew complied and descended 350 feet. Once clear of conflict, ATC was notified and SWG407 resumed cruise at FL370.  The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GECG, a privately operated Cessna 172, was operating under VFR out of Courtenay Air Park (CAH3), BC with one person, the pilot, on board. While in the vicinity of Estevan Point, the aircraft struck trees and collided with the ground; the pilot did not survive. There was no post-impact fire and the 121.5/243 ELT produced a signal that assisted in finding the wreckage.

C-FGSJ, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by CargoJet, was conducting flight CJT301 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with two flight crew members on board. On final approach to CYVR, at approximately at 1400 feet ASL, the crew conducted a missed approach because of an unsafe landing gear indication. The crew had a Master Caution light with Landing Gear Disagree, Tail skid, and Right Gear Door Amber Lights illuminated.  The crew flew the published missed approach and completed the QRH Checklist items while they flew on vectors for landing. ATC initiated the ARFF response. As part of the checklist, the landing gear was cycled and all indications showed normal for the landing gear being down. The aircraft landed without further event. Maintenance inspected all landing gear and landing gear doors. The right main landing gear door was cycled on the ground and the snag could not be replicated. There were no faults found and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FPCE, a privately registered Cessna Citation Mustang (C510), was conducting a flight from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Springbank/Calgary, (CYBW), AB. C-FACO, a privately registered Cessna Citation Encore (C560), was conducting a flight from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to CYEG. C-FPCE departed Runway 20 ahead of C-FACO that was landing Runway 12.  Automatic control transfer was not in effect due to a ceiling that was overcast at 800 feet above ground.  As C-FPCE climbed out through the Runway 12 arrival path, separation between C-FPCE and C-FACO was reduced to 2.9 nm (where 3 nm is required) for 18 seconds before returning to greater than 3 nm.

C-GPNL, a Boeing 737-300 operated by Canadian North Airlines, was conducting flight MPE1725 from Fort MacKay/Horizon (CYNR), AB to Edmonton Intl. (CYEG), AB. C-GZOR, a Piper Seneca PA34-200T operated by Montair Aviation Inc, was conducting an IFR training flight originating from, and returning to Red Deer (CYQF), AB cruising at 8000 feet. On initial approach into CYEG, MPE1725 was instructed to descend to 9000 feet. Air traffic control observed MPE1725 descending to 8700 feet.  Separation between MPE1725 and C-GZOR reduced to 2.6 miles and 700 feet where 3.0 miles or 1000 feet are required. Separation was regained when MPE1725 climbed on its own back to 9000 feet.

C-GKFF, a Convair 580 operated by Kelowna Flightcraft, was conducting flight KFA579 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Kamloops (CYKA), BC with 2 crew members on board. After takeoff the flight crew were unable to retract the landing gear. The flight crew elected to return to CYVR and requested ARFF be placed on standby. The flight landed without further incident. Subsequent maintenance activity revealed a landing gear handle safety solenoid wiring fault. The defect was rectified and aircraft was returned into service.

C-FCJE, a Bombardier DHC-8-102 operated by Central Mountain Air, was conducting flight GLR8016 from Prince George (CYXS), BC to Dease Lake (CYDL), BC with 3 crew members and 26 passengers on board. After departure the flight crew retracted the landing gear but noted an abnormal sound and the landing gear door remained open. The flight crew actioned the QRH for the landing gear door malfunction and proceeded to the alternate landing gear extension. The flight crew returned to CYXS and conducted an initial fly past of the tower/ARFF, followed by a second fly past for a pilot on the ground, to visually inspect the position of the landing gear. The flight crew then conducted an uneventful landing. Subsequent maintenance actions by the operator indicated a broken wire associated with the nose landing gear doors.

C-GJAN, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ 900) operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting ferry flight JZA7134 from San Diego Int'l (KSAN), CA to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC with 2 flight crew members on board. During descent to CYVR the flight crew received an EICAS message for smoke in the aft lavatory. The captain left the cockpit and could visibly see smoke coming from the aft lavatory but did not open the door. The flight crew followed the QRH, which included pulling the lavatory circuit breakers, and the EICAS message extinguished. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and landed without further incident. The aircraft taxied to the hangar and was met by ARFF who came on board. ARFF did not see smoke but noted the smell of smoke was present. Subsequent maintenance actions found chaffing in the cabin overhead lighting wiring at row 27 D/F. The wires were contacting in the area of the lavatory enclosure. The wires were adjusted for clearance and protected from outside contact. Ground runs were carried out and could not duplicate the fault. The aircraft has been released into service.

C-GWRE, un de Havilland, Dash-8 Q400 exploité par WestJet Encore sous l’indicatif WEN3513 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QB à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON avec 78 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Lorsque le train d'atterrissage a été rentré après le décollage, l’équipage a eu une indication qu’une porte de la roue de nez n’était pas fermée. L’équipage a complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH), toutefois l’indication de porte ouverte est demeurée. L’équipage a décidé de revenir se poser à CYUL, a déclaré un état d’urgence et les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre, il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni de dommage à l’appareil. L’inspection post-envolée a trouvé que le détecteur de proximité de la porte du train était désajusté.

C-GLQC, a de Havilland DHC-8-402, operated by Porter Airlines Inc. was conducting flight POE459 from Windsor Intl. (CYQG), ON to Toronto/Billy Bishop (CYTZ), ON. After departure the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to an intermittent rear door warning indication. The aircraft returned to CYQG without further incident. It was determined that doorframe ice was affecting the door sensor. Heat was applied to clear the ice and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GURG, un CL60 exploité par le service aérien gouvernemental du Québec sous l’Indicatif de vol QUE10 MEDEVAC venait de décoller de Chibougamau/Chapais (CYMT), QC à destination de Val-d’Or (CYVO), QC lorsque l’équipage de conduite a reçu une indication FLAP FAIL et constaté que les volets étaient bloqués à 20 degrés. L’équipage de conduite a demandé une diversion vers l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC et a demandé la présence des services d'urgence pour l'atterrissage. L'atterrissage s'est déroulé sans encombre. Le personnel de maintenance à réinitialiser le système des volets et l'appareil a été remis en service.

C-GHKW, an Airbus A330 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA 809 from Casablanca/Mohammed V Intl. (GMMN), Morocco to Montreal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC . During the cruise portion of the flight the yellow hydraulic system showed a low pressure and the crew was unable to shut the pump off. The crew consulted with dispatch and maintenance and a decision was made to declare a PAN-PAN and divert to St. John's Intl (CYYT), NL . The flight landed without further incident in CYYT. Maintenance found in the right hand wheel well that the manifold hydraulic high-pressure line fitting was loose. The fitting was resecured and the aircraft was returned to service.

M-USIC, a privately operated Gulfstream G550, was on a flight from Teterboro (KTEB), NJ to London/Farnborough (EGLF), UK. During the cruise portion of the flight, while in Canadian airspace, the cockpit windshield cracked. The crew declared a PAN PAN and requested a diversion to Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl. (KBOS), MA . No other assistance was required.

C-FRSE, a Boeing 787-9 operated by Air Canada as flight AC031, departed Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON for Beijing/Capital International (ZBAA), China. While in cruise, approximately 74 nautical miles SW of Arctic Bay (CYYZ), NU, the left-hand engine commanded itself to increase thrust. The autothrust pulled the throttle back about 1.5 inches to compensate. The flight crew contacted the operator's dispatch and maintenance personnel, and a decision was made to return to CYYZ. A PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft subsequently landed safely in CYYZ with ARFF on standby. The operator's maintenance replaced the throttle quadrant module.

C-FFYG, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU, operated by Sky Regional Airlines Inc. was conducting flight SKV7614 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOW), ON. During the descent, the flight crew received an EICAS message indicating the parking brake was engaged. The crew completed the appropriate checklist and then declared an emergency. The aircraft landed on runway 32 at CYOW without incident with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) standing by. After an inspection by ARFF, the aircraft taxied normally to the gate.

C-FKOJ, an Airbus A320-211 operated by Air Canada as flight ACA7058, was on a repositioning flight from CYVR (Vancouver Intl) to CYYC (Calgary Intl) with two pilots and no passengers. Prior to dispatch a Cabin Pressure Controller #1 Fail fault was cleared. On climbout from CYVR the flight crew received ECAM message CAB PR SYS 1 FAULT. ECAM actions were completed but a subsequent message CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT displayed. The crew declared a PAN PAN and returned to CYVR without further incident. Maintenance replaced the #1 and the #2 system cabin pressure controllers and the outflow valve.

The Air North Charter and Training Ltd. Hawker Siddeley HS748, C-GANA, was operating as training flight ANT 1T, from the Whitehorse (CYXY),YK. In the initial climb at 100 feet above ground, the left engine (Rolls Royce Dart 534-2) failed and auto-feathered. The crew accomplished the engine failure and shut down procedure. The captain declared an emergency and the aircraft performed a visual circuit for an uneventful landing on Runway 14R. The aircraft was met by ARFF and inspected before taxiing in. A preliminary inspection by maintenance indicated that there was no oil in the left engine.

The Air Canada Express De Havilland Dash 8-400, C-GJZD, was operating as JZA374 from Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB to Calgary (CYYC), AB. While en route, the flight crew observed a 'Deice Pressure' caution indication. The crew flew an increased approach and landing speed and declared an emergency. ARFF was on standby for the arrival which was carried out without incident.Update: Wing boot and deice system checked in all modes by maintenance personnel. All systems checked normal and the aircraft was returned to service.

The Sunwest Aviation Ltd. de Havilland Dash 8-200, C-GYUP, was operating as CNK4852 on flight plan from Whitecourt (CYZU), AB to Calgary Int'l (CYYC), AB.  was on the approach for runway 35L. A WestJet Encore De Havilland Dash 8-400, C-FWEP, was operating as WEN3249 on a flight from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl. (CYXE), SK to Calgary Int'l (CYYC), AB. Both flight were on the approach for Runway 35R in CYYC. A loss of separation occurred when the controller mistook CNK4852 with another aircraft and cleared them down to 5500 feet when originally he had told them to maintain 6500 feet; 5500 feet was the altitude that WEN3249 was maintaining. Separation reduced to 2.0 miles and 300 feet where 3.0 miles or 1000 feet are required.  CNK4852 and WEN3249 were subsequently removed from the approach and vectored around for another attempt; both aircraft landed safely. There were no TCAS RA's.

C-GFCI, an Airbus A320-214 operated by Air Canada Rouge was conducting flight ROU1740 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON to Varadero/Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl (MUVR) Cuba. During the descent at FL210 approximately 50nm north of Cuba, the aircraft encountered sudden turbulence which strongly forced the aircraft up and down and lasted for approximately 5-10 seconds. At the time of the occurrence, the seatbelt sign was active however, 3 Flight Attendants located in the aft galley of the aircraft and 4 passengers distributed throughout the aircraft sustained minor injuries. The flight continued to MUVR where it was completed without further incident.

C-GBHZ, an Airbus 319-114 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1986 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC to Punta Cana Intl. (MDPC), Dominican Republic. During cruise at FL380 in light turbulence, the flight crew felt vibrations and observed the right hand engine N1 indication rolling back, while all other indications were normal including engine vibration indications. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and requested a descent. The aircraft descended to FL280 at which point the issue rectified. The flight crew decided to divert to the nearest suitable airport, which was Nassau/ Lynden Pindling Intl. (MYNN), Bahamas, where the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GEEN, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 operated by Westjet Encore as flight WEN3226 was conducting a flight from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK. WEN3226 was cleared for the RNAV Y Runway 27. C-FIPN, a Pilatus PC 12/47 operated by 1867829 Alberta Ltd., was conducting a flight from Regina Intl (CYQR) SK to CYXE. C-FIPN was sequenced behind C-GEEN and was cleared for RNAV Z Runway 27 by Winnipeg Centre. Both aircraft were cleared for the approach and switched to CYXE tower frequency. C-GTJX, a Saab 340B operated by Transwest Air Ltd, was conducting a flight from Prince Albert/Glass Field (CYPA), SK to CYXE. C-GTJX was sequenced behind C-GEEN and C-FIPN for the RNAV Z Runway 27.During the approach, a loss of separation for wake turbulence occurred between C-GEEN and C-FIPN. The required separation was reduced to 2.9 nautical miles when the required separation is 4 nautical miles. C-FIPN's approach clearance was cancelled and C-FIPN was asked to contact Winnipeg Center. The controller cleared C-FIPN to turn right to a heading of 360 degrees, bringing the aircraft north of the approach path for Runway 27. The controller subsequently cleared C-FIPN to turn further right to a heading of 270 degrees. During the vectoring of C-FIPN, lateral separation between C-FIPN and C-GTJX was reduced to 2 nautical miles when 3 nautical miles in required. The controller cleared C-FIPN to turn to a heading of 360 degrees again, followed by another clearance to turn right to a heading of 270 degrees. The crew of C-FIPN asked for confirmation of the last clearance and the controller corrected the clearance to a right turn to a heading of 090 degrees. C-FIPN subsequently conducted the RNAV Z Runway 27 uneventfully. All aircraft landed safely in CYXE.

C-FDSN, an Airbus A320-211 operated by Air Canada was conducting flight AC568 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to San Francisco Intl (KSFO), CA with 5 crew and 80 passengers on board. During taxi the right engine (CFM International CFM-56-5A1) flamed out. The aircraft returned to the gate. Subsequent maintenance actions, as per the operators maintenance manual, replaced the engine electronic control (EEC) unit. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKFF, a Convair 580 aircraft operated by Kelowna Flightcraft, was conducting flight KFA579 from Kamloops (CYKA), BC to Prince George (CYXS), BC with 2 crew on board. While in cruise flight, approximately 30 NM north of Williams Lake (CYWL), BC the crew experienced an increase in oil temperature into the caution range for the right engine (Allison 501-D13). The flight crew were unsuccessful in attempts to return it to the normal range. The crew shut down the right engine, declared an emergency, and diverted to Kelowna (CYLW), BC where the aircraft landed without further incident. Subsequent maintenance revealed fault with the engine oil cooler, which was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GKQC, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 operated by Porter Airlines Inc. as flight PD219, departed Thunder Bay (CYQT) ON for Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ) Toronto ON. After departure the flight crew selected gear up and noticed the nose gear light was red with no red light in the gear handle. The flight crew elected to slow the aircraft and requested a hold at 5000 feet. After consulting with the operator's MOC, the flight crew carried out the "nose gear door malfunction" checklist and the "alternate landing gear extension" checklist. The flight crew informed ATC , declared a PAN PAN, and requested a return to CYQT. PD219 completed a normal landing with ARFF on standby. After landing the flight crew noticed the nose wheel steering was inoperative. The aircraft stopped on the runway and was towed the gate. The operator's maintenance replaced the nose gear door actuator and retuned the aircraft to service.

C-GYYB, a privately-operated C.L.A.S.S. Bushcaddy L164 on skis, was taking off from the owner's property at Beaver Lake, BC. During the take-off run one wing struck a tree and directional control was lost. The aircraft veered into trees resulting in substantial damage. The pilot was not injured.

C-GOWG, un Boeing 737-800 exploité par Sunwing Airlines Inc. sous l’indicatif SWG386 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport international de Cancún (MMUN) au Mexique à destination de l’aéroport de Québec Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC avec 185 passagers et 6 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en descente à 85 miles marins au sud de CYQB, l’équipage a avisé le centre de contrôle de la circulation aérienne (ATC) qu’il désirait effectuer une diversion à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC en raison d’une fuite de carburant. Par la suite, l’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et l’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 24R à CYUL sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en attente. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage. L’inspection de la piste après l’atterrissage a révélé un déversement de carburant.

C-FWSV, a Boeing 737-7CT operated by WestJet Airlines Ltd., was conducting flight WJA2227 from Montego Bay/Sangster Intl. (MKJS), Jamaica to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB. During the flight a Flight Attendant was unable to continue cabin duties due to a medical condition. Priority landing was requested.  No further assistance was required.

C-GYSR, a Beech B200 operated by Keewatin Air LP, was conducting flight Blizzard 208 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. Shortly after rotation on takeoff, the aircraft experience a power roll back on the left hand engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-42). The flight crew continued the climb and declared an emergency. As the flight crew was assessing the situation, it was determined that the left-hand power lever had moved back from the takeoff power position. The flight crew advanced the power lever and engine power was restored. The flight crew consulted with company flight operations, cancelled the emergency, and continued to CYWG; where the aircraft landed safely.

Jazz Aviation flight JZA8285 (C-GABO), a DeHavilland DHC-8-311 aircraft, en route from Toronto Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Timmins (CYTS), ON requested a return to CYYZ due to hydraulic issues. The flight crew requested ARFF on stand-by for the landing. The aircraft landed without further incident.

Ornge Air flight PUL107 (C-GRXN), a Pilatus PC-12/47E aircraft, was en-route from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON and descending in terminal airspace to 3000 feet. Simultaneously, Delta Airlines flight DAL8846 (N649DL), a Boeing 757-200 aircraft, was on approach to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ) ON. A loss of separation occurred when separation was reduced to 2.5 nm horizontal and 600 feet vertical where 3 nm or 1000 feet were required.

C-FZAA, a Sikorsky S76A aircraft operated by Helijet International, was conducting flight JBA802 with 2 flight crew members and 11 passengers on board from Nanaimo Harbour Heliport (CDH5), BC to Vancouver Harbour Heliport (CBC7), BC. After departure, approximately 3 NM NE of CDH5 and approaching VFR reporting point "SNAKE ISLAND", the non-flying pilot of JBA902 spotted a float plane on a converging course. The flight crew of JBA902 made an evasive pull up maneuver to avoid the float plane. JBA902 continued to CBC7 and landed without further incident.

C-GKFG, a Convair 340 aircraft operated by Kelowna Flightcraft, was conducting flight KFA576 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 2 crew members on board. When 70 nm northeast of CYVR the captain became ill and could not continue with their duties. The first officer notified ATC of the situation and requested priority handling. ARFF was on standby for landing, which was uneventful. The flight was met by ARFF and BC Ambulance Service.

C-GOSA, an ATR-72-202 operated by Summit Air, was conducting flight SU7022 from Gacho Kue (CGK2), NT to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT. When approximately 60 NM ENE of CYZF, smoke entered the cabin of the aircraft. The Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) for air-conditioning smoke was actioned and the #1 air conditioning pack was shut off. The smoke began to dissipate but the flight crew elected to declare a Pan Pan. The aircraft landed without incident and taxied in with ARFF following. Company maintenance is investigating the cause.Update: As an update to this occurrence, maintenance determined the recirculation fan faulted. This unit will be scrapped as it is pre-mod unit and the company is moving to post mod units with better reliability.

C-GCCF, a privately operated Cessna 421B, was operating from Whitecourt (CYZU), AB to Ponoka (CEH3), AB.  Approximately fifteen minutes after takeoff the pilot noticed the right engine (Teledyne Continental GTSIO-520-H) was running rough. There was no EGT on the no. 6 cylinder, and adjustments to the mixture, RPM or manifold pressure did not correct the issue. The engine was shutdown as a precautionary measure. The flight continued on to the destination and landed without further event.Following the flight, maintenance found a blocked fuel injector on the right engine to no. 6 cylinder. The injector was cleaned and the fuel system was inspected for other issues. A ground engine run was conducted with no further defects.

The Sunwest Aviation Ltd. Learjet 45, C-GSWQ, was operating as CNK657 on a flight from Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB. During cruise smoke entered the cabin from the environmental system requiring the crew and passengers to don oxygen masks and declare an emergency. The flight crew selected full cold on the environmental system and the smoke began to dissipate as the aircraft landed. CNK657 was able to taxi in under it's own power with ARFF following.Update: Environmental control muffler (ECS) was exposed to higher than normal temps in manual mode leading to breakdown of adhesives in the packing. ECS was removed and replaced with new unit. The aircraft was ground tested and returned to service.

C-FQYW, a privately operated Piper Aerostar PA60-602P, departed Bishop Airport (KBIH), CA for a flight to Nanaimo (CYCD), BC with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. At approximately 1803 PST the pilot informed ATC that they had a mechanical issue and required a new heading. ATC supplied several instructions attempting to assist the aircraft, which was in IMC. Shortly after, the aircraft lost contact with ATC and struck terrain into a forested area on Gabriola Island, 8.5nm N of CYCD. The aircraft sustained a post impact fire; the ELT did not alert. The 3 persons on board were fatally injured.

C-GKVV, a Boeing 737-800 operated by Sunwing Airlines Inc., was conducting flight SWG640 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Holguin/Frank País Intl. (MUHG), Cuba. During the climb to FL340, a TCAS RA "level off" was received at FL335 due to crossing traffic at FL350. The RA was followed. The flight crew was advised of the traffic by ATC. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GBLJ, a Cessna C340A aircraft, privately operated was conducting a flight from Toronto Buttonville (CYKZ), ON to Fredericton Intl (CYFC), NB. On departure, while climbing to 3000 feet, the pilot contacted the ATC. The controller advised the pilot to maintain 3000 feet which was read back correctly. The aircraft's mode C transponder signal disappeared momentarily and C-GBLJ was next observed climbing through 3400 feet. When queried by the controller, C-GBLJ descended immediately back down to 3000 feet. C-GBLJ came in to conflict with Jazz Flight JZA926, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 aircraft (C-GGJA) on approach to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ ) ON. Separation was reduced to 1.2 nm and 600 feet.

KLM Royal Dutch Airlines flight KLM691, a Boeing 747-400 aircraft, registration PH-BFH, was being marshalled in to gate C31 at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON when the left engine struck a parked ground vehicle. There were no injuries. Maintenance inspected the aircraft and the engine cowling was replaced.

C-GNDR, un Piper PA-46-600TP en exploitation privée avec 1 personne à son bord, effectuait un vol depuis l'aéroport de Ponca City Regional Airport (KNPC), OK à destination de Montréal/Saint-Hubert (CYHU), QB. Lors de l'approche à CYHU le pilote a observé que les volets ont refusé de s'activer lors de leur sélection. Une remise des gaz a été effectuée et la liste de vérification complétée sans toutefois régler le problème. Le pilote a déclaré PAN PAN et demandé un déroutement vers Montréal/Pierre-Elliott-Trudeau (CYUL), QB où l'atterrissage s'est effectué sans incident.

C-FUJZ, a Bombardier CRJ-900 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8804 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Nashville Intl. (KBNA), TN with 4 crew members and 66 passengers. At approximately 150 nm NNE of KBNA while en route at FL320, hydraulic 3 Low Press caution and associated spoiler fault messages appeared. The flight crew completed the check list, found that the right hand generator was inoperative and faults for the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) Battery charger.
