The flight crew started the APU and shortly thereafter, the cabin crew advised them of a burning electrical smell in the cabin. The APU was shut down and the burning smell disappeared. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and the aircraft landed with no further issue in KBNA. The maintenance personnel is troubleshooting at KBNA.

C-GNON, a DHC 8-301 was being operated by Jazz Aviation as flight JZA842 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Hartford/Springfield/Bradley Intl. (KBDL), CT. While enroute the flight crew observed smoke/fire emanating from the upper left corner of the first officer's windshield. The fire was extinguished and an emergency was declared. The aircraft landed uneventfully at KBDL. There were no injuries and the aircraft sustained minor damage. The NTSB investigated. (ENG20IA006).

C-FWGH, a Sunwing Airlines Inc. Boeing 737-800, was operating as flight SWG487 from Edmonton International (CYEG), AB. to Cancun Intl.(MMUN), Mexico. Just after pushback from CYEG gate 62 the flight crew were notified by the ground crew of a fuel leak from right hand engine (CFM International CFM56-7B26E).  As a precaution the engine was shut down and the aircraft returned to the gate where maintenance inspected the engine and found a loose fuel line.  The line was tightened and an idle engine run was conducted. No further leaks were found. The aircraft departed to the destination without further incident.

C-GFYD, a private Robinson R-44 Helicopter, was conducting a flight near the Vanderhoof (CAU4) airport, to land on a flat-bed truck for transport with only the pilot on board. After the aircraft landed on the truck deck and power was reduced, the aircraft began to rotate to the right. To prevent falling off the deck, the pilot increased power and lifted off the truck. The aircraft began to spin, tipped onto its right hand side and impacted the ground on the right front quarter of the aircraft. The pilot sustained minor injuries. The ELT activated. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FNVS, a privately operated Piper PA28-160, was conducting touch and goes at Cooking Lake (CEZ3), AB. During the landing the aircraft landed slightly off center and veered to the left. A correction was attempted with right rudder and the addition of power. The aircraft was not at rotation speed and continued to veer to left and contacted a snowbank on the left side of the runway. The aircraft came back on the runway and then crossed to the right side where it came to rest in the grass. The propeller (Sensenich M74DM-0-61) and nose gear were damaged. The aircraft was towed off of the runway.

C-FYJE, an Air Canada Airbus 319-100 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1735 from Lima/Jorge Chávez Intl. (SPJC), Peru to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. During cruise at FL350, 45nm W of Jacksonville Intl. (KJAX) FL, the flight encountered turbulence and the flight crew noted the Left Hand (LH) engine N1 decreased. The flight crew requested a lower altitude in search of smoother air. The flight leveled of at FL310 and the LH engine resumed normal operation for the remainder of the flight. Maintenance inspected the engine and found the LH engine HMU (hydro mechanical unit) faulty. Replacement of the HMU took place and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GLQV, a De Havilland DHC-8-402 operated by Porter Airlines (POE460) was on a flight from Halifax Stanfield Intl. (CYHZ), NS to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QB. Shortly after departure, the crew contacted air traffic control to report that they were experiencing a nose gear problem. The aircraft held in the Halifax area to troubleshoot the issue and reduce the fuel load. After holding for over 2 hours, the crew declared a Pan-Pan then requested and were cleared to landing. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 32 while aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) were standing by. Runway 14/32 was closed for a short time while the aircraft was towed to the gate. The company reported that maintenance rectified an indication problem and returned the aircraft to service.

C-GBIN, an Airbus 319-100 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1746 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC to Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl. (MUVR), Cuba. During cruise in vicinity of Albany Intl. (KALB), NY, flight attendant became incapacitated and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight. Duties were distributed to the other cabin crew members, and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FNAI, an Embraer 190-100 IGW aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA146 from Calgary Intl (CYYC) AB to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. At approximately 85 nautical miles SSW of Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB, the #1 generator fail light illuminated. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and diverted to CYWG. The aircraft completed an uneventful landing at CYWG. The operator's maintenance replaced the #1 generator control unit and returned the aircraft to service.

C-GORI a Beechcraft 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Services was conducting flight EV7784 from Gander Intl (CYQX), NL to St John's Intl. (CYYT), NL with 2 crew and 11 passengers. On approach to CYYT, the aircraft was intercepting the final approach course at 3000 feet when severe turbulence was encountered. The crew had difficulty controlling the aircraft, however the turbulence abated as they continued their descent. A passenger fainted, and was treated by EHS upon landing. The turbulent air inspection was carried out by maintenance and no faults were found, the aircraft was released to service.

C-FXCA, a Boeing 777-375ER operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1915 from Barcelona Intl. (LEBL), Spain to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  During the climb to cruise altitude, a flight attendant became incapacitated and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight. The order of priority for cabin crew was reassigned.

C-FYKC, an Air Canada Airbus 319-100, was operating as flight AC569 from San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), CA to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC. Following departure from Runway 10 at SFO, the crew received a TCAS Resolution advisory (RA). The advisory was to level off, so crew leveled off at 1700 feet. The traffic was not identified as it was IMC conditions, but it was cleared in 3 seconds.  The flight continued and landed safely in CYVR.

C-GGNF, Jazz Aviation LP De Havilland DHC-8-400 was operating as flight JZA8382 from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB. While enroute to CYMM (100nm NNE YEG), the flight crew observed a cabin pressure indication and initiated an emergency descent. The aircraft descended to 14 000 feet ASL and was further cleared to descend to 10 000 feet ASL. The flight crew elected to return to CYEG. No emergency was declared and the aircraft landed without further incident. There were no injuries. Company maintenance replaced the cabin pressure controller.

A6EPY, a Boeing 777-300 operated by Emirates Airlines conducting flight UAE221 from Dubai Intl. (OMDB), UAE to Dallas/Forth Worth (KDFW), TX. HL8363, an Airbus 350-900 operated by Asiana Airlines, was conducting flight AAR223 from New York/John F Kennedy Intl. (KJFK), NY to Seoul/Incheon Intl. (RKSI), Republic of Korea. The aircraft were on a crossing track and were identified, but the controller did not have either aircraft on frequency. Due to a conflict alert, the controller issued instructions via controller/pilot data link communication (CPDLC). In accordance with the instructions, UAE221 descended to FL340, and AAR223 climbed to FL370, when the aircraft were approximately 21 NM apart. As the flights crossed, a loss of separation occurred. Separation was reduced to 1000 feet and 30 seconds, where 1000 feet and 10 minutes was required.

C-FDLG, un Dash-8 100 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE821 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments de Kuujjuaq (CYVP), QC à destination de Schefferville (CYKL), QC avec à son bord 3 membres d'équipage et 17 passagers. Lorsque le train d’atterrissage a été descendu à l'approche de CYKL, le train avant ne s’est pas déployé malgré plusieurs tentatives. L'équipage a suivi la liste de vérification applicable et descendu le train à l'aide du système de sortie alternatif. Compte tenu des conditions de piste et des conditions météorologiques existantes à CYKL, l'équipage a opté pour remonter le train d'atterrissage et retourner à CYVP et a demandé l’intervention des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). À l'approche de CYVP le train d'atterrissage a été sorti à l'aide du système alternatif et l'avion s'est posé sans encombre. L'appareil a été immobilisé sur la piste et a été remorqué sur la rampe. Personne n'a été blessé.

C-FIUW, a Boeing 777-300 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA849 from London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON.  After level off at cruise altitude, following a report of smoke in the lavatory, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC. Subsequently it was determined that a passenger laptop that was emitting smoke in cabin. As per cabin procedure, the laptop was contained in a bag and cooled with water. The PAN PAN was cancelled when the smoke source was confirmed to be the laptop and was subsequently controlled by cabin crew. The flight landed without further event at CYYZ.

N204SY, an Embraer EMB 175 was operating Skywest Airlines flight SKW5877 from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Chicago O’Hare Intl. (KORD), IL. During the climb to cruise altitude, SKW5877 developed a glycol-type odor within the cabin and flight deck. Some crew and passengers experienced eye irritation.  The flight crew donned oxygen masks and declared an emergency. SKW5877 returned to CYYC and landed without further incident. Paramedics met the aircraft at the gate. The flight crew and passengers were assessed during deplaning. There were no injuries.

C-GDIL, a Canadair Challenger 300 operated by Morningstar Partners Ltd., was conducting a flight from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Van Nuys (KVNY), CA. The flight crew experienced a TCAS resolution advisory (RA) while established on the ILS. The flight crew disconnected the autopilot, a level off was initiated and avoided the traffic.  Once clear of the traffic, although the ILS approach was destabilized, the flight crew was able to return to a stabilized visual approach and the aircraft subsequently landed without further event on Runway 16R.

C-FWVJ, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Westjet, was conducting flight 1882 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Kailua/Ellison Onizuka Kona Intl. at Keahole (PHKO), HI. During cruise, flight attendant #1 became ill and incapacitated.  Duties were distributed to the remaining flight attendants for landing.  The aircraft landed safely in PHKO.

C-FKAL, a Douglas DC-3C-BT67 operated by North Star Air Ltd, was conducting a cargo flight from Red Lake (CYRL), ON to Sachigo Lake (CZPB), ON, with 2 flight crew members on board. While on approach to CZPB, the aircraft collided with terrain approximately 500 metres southwest of the threshold of Runway 10. The 2 flight crew members received no injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The TSB is investigating.

C-GXTB, a Pilatus PC-12 aircraft operated by North Star Air Ltd, was conducting a passenger flight from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Fort Hope (CZFH), ON. During the climb approximately 30 nm northeast of CYQT at flight level 200, the crew received an illumination of the ''CABIN PRESSURE CAWS'' annunciator light. The flight crew actioned the appropriate drill, commenced an emergency descent, notified ATC, and returned to CYQT where it landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance replaced the outflow valve controller. Applicable operational tests were completed and aircraft was checked serviceable.

C-GHLV, an Air Canada Rouge Boeing 767-333ER, was operating as flight ROU1844 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC to San José (MROC) Costa Rica. In cruise, in the vicinity of Owen Roberts Intl. (MWCR) Grand Cayman, a flight attendant became incapacitated due to foot injury and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight. The order of priority for the cabin crew was reassigned to ensure all doors were manned for landing.

C- FKWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-400, was conducting flight WEN3239 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB with 4 crew and 65 passengers on board. After takeoff and the selection of gear up, the gear retraction annunciator light for the right main gear door remained illuminated. The crew declared a PAN PAN and stated their intent to return to CYLW.  They performed an alternate landing gear extension and landed without incident. Maintenance replaced the right main landing gear solenoid sequence valve and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FRJA, a Bombardier CRJ 900 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8833 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with 4 crew and 64 passengers on board. During the climb out of CYVR, the crew received a nose landing gear 'door open' message. The crew decided to return to CYVR. The aircraft was manoeuvered to burn fuel to reduce the load to the allowable landing weight. Vancouver Tower activated ARFF on stand-by as a precautionary measure.The aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance personnel adjusted the nose gear door proximity sensor and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPJZ, a CRJ-900 was on a repositioning flight (QK7139) for Jazz Aviation LP from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. Approximately 135NM west of CYQT in American airspace, the flight crew received a left full authority digital engine control (FADEC) caution indication. The flight crew elected to shutdown the left hand engine as a precaution and diverted to Minneapolis-St. Paul Intl./Wold-Chamberlain (KMSP), MN. An emergency was declared with ATC and flight landed in KMSP without further incident.

C-GEZO, an Air Transat A321 aircraft, was operating as flight TSC 508 from Quebec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QB to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL. On the left downwind for Runway 10L/R at 4,000 feet on the Fisel7 arrival, C-GEZO was given a heading of 276° for radar vectors for 5nm until being turned in for the approach. On the TCAS, the crew noticed traffic about 4nm in front of them and closing at 200 feet below them. The traffic was neither climbing nor descending. The flight crew queried ATC and after having to repeat their query, ATC instructed them to turn left heading 220° and climb to 4,500 feet immediately. ATC then revised their vector to 180° while the aircraft was in the turn and climbing. The aircraft then received a TA and the target aircraft passed by their right wing at about 300 feet below them and less than 1nm. Flight landed uneventfully.

C-GCQB, a Bell 429 helicopter operated by Transports Canada, was conducting sling operations from Beaupré, QC. While slinging lumber and two (2) stepladders, the pilot notices the stepladders shifting and attempted to return to the staging area. Halfway through the flight, the stepladders plunged into the St-Lawrence river approximately .75 NM north of the northeast tip of Île d'Orleans, Qc. The ratchet straps that initially secured the stepladders were not found upon the aircrafts's return to the staging area. The ground crew received additional training following the incident. There were no injuries.

C-FIJA, un CL-600-2B19 (CRJ2) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA30, effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC à destination de Philadelphia Intl. (KPHL), PA avec 46 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage. À la suite de la rétraction des roues en montée initiale après le décollage, le message de « Gear Disagree » est apparu sur le système d'affichage des paramètres moteurs et d'alerte de l'équipage (EICAS). L’équipage a placé la commande du train en position d’extension et a confirmé que toutes les roues étaient sorties et barrées. L’équipage a ensuite décidé de revenir se poser à CYUL et a effectué un circuit d’attente d’environ 45 minutes, afin de réduire le poids de l’appareil sous la limite maximale à l’atterrissage. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 24L avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-GHLU, an Air Canada Rouge Boeing 767-300 aircraft, was operating as flight ROU2383 from Shannon Intl. (EINN), Ireland to  Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. During the take off run, the right hand engine performance indication was not corresponding with the thrust setting; manual thrust inputs did not correct the issue. The take off was rejected at 100 kts. The aircraft cleared the runway and taxied to a maintenance hangar with a fire brigade escort. At the hangar the fire crew noted smoke and flame emitting from the left main gear assembly and extinguished it within 15 seconds; the aircraft is offline for investigation.

N521FL an IFL Group Inc. Dassault Falcon 20 was operating as flight IFL521 from Kansas City (KMCI), MO to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB. While on short final to Runway 35L, at approximately 3000 feet AGL, the flight crew lowered the landing gear and received a landing gear unsafe warning light. The flight crew conducted a missed approach and actioned the QRH. While on final to Runway 35R, the flight crew declared an emergency and landed uneventfully. Maintenance troubleshooting identified moisture in the landing gear position switch.

C-GMSY, un appareil de type Learjet 45 exploité par Aviation Starlink Inc. effectuait un vol de transport médical de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QB à destination de l'aéroport Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl. (KFLL), FL. Apres son décollage de la piste 24L, C-GMSY est demeuré plus lent et a été rattrappé par N185GJ, un CRJ900 de Go Jet effectuant le vol GJS6190 de CYUL à destination de l'aéroport Metro Wayne County de Détroit (KDTW), MI. et qui décollait de la meme piste (24L). En montée initiale de la piste 24L, une perte d'espacement est survenue lorsque la distance entre les deux appareils a été réduite à 2.4 milles nautiques alors que la norme est de 3 mille avant de se rétablir peu après.

The Top Aces Inc. Dassault/Dornier Alpha Jets, C-GJTA and C-FHTO (see TSB occurrence A19W0177 for C-FHTO), were operating at CFB Cold Lake, (CYOD) AB. A fuel order was placed for both aircraft to be fueled with NATO F34 type fuel. A fuel truck identified as containing F34 fuel went to the aircraft and both Alpha Jets were refueled. The fuel receipts also identified the fuel type as F34. Approximately 20 minutes after refueling, the operator was notified that NATO F37 type fuel had been delivered and fueled into the Alpha Jets. The fuel truck was previously used to defuel a RCAF CF-188 which contained the F37 type fuel. Both Alpha Jets were defueled, prior to flight operations, without further incident.

C-GWBT, a Boeing 737-700 performing WestJet flight WJA700 was on route from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON when a flight attendant became ill and was unable to continue their duties. The flight landed without further incident.

Sky Regional Flight SKV7612, an Embraer E175 (C-FEKD) aircraft, landed on Runway 24R at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON and declared an emergency due to a "BRAKE OVERHEAT" message on the EICAS. ARFF was dispatched to the aircraft, checked the brakes and found the left inboard brake assembly to be 600-650°C. Once the brake had cooled down into the green the aircraft started to taxi to the gate and the brake temperature began to rise immediately. ARFF followed the aircraft to the gate and ensured the brake was in the green before leaving. Maintenance found the left inboard brake assembly was seized. The brake was replaced and the aircraft was released back into service.

N50DK, PA-32-260 aircraft, which was privately registered in the United States, departed Toronto/Buttonville (CYKZ), ON destined for Quebec City/Jean Lesage Intl. (CYQB), QB, with 7 people on board.  During the flight, the aircraft established radio communications with the Flight Service Station (FSS) at Kingston/Norman Rogers (CYGK), ON indicating their intention to land at CYKG.  However, shortly afterwards, the aircraft disappeared off radar, and the ELT activated. SAR was notified, after which a ground and aerial search was conducted. The aircraft was located approximately 3 nm to the north of CYGK; it was destroyed from impact forces. All 7 occupants received fatal injuries, there was no post impact fire. The TSB deployed a team of investigators to the site.

F-GZCE an Airbus A330-200 aircraft operated by Air France, was conducting flight AFR027 from Washington Dulles International Airport, WA (KIAD) to Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport, (LFPG). During cruise, about 65NM SSW from Yarmouth Airport, NS, the flight crew contacted the Moncton Area Control Center and declared a PAN-PAN. The crew indicated that the aircraft had a technical issue and requested a return to KIAD. The clearance was issued and the aircraft departed the Moncton ACC area of responsibility at 0411 UTC.  AFR027 landed safely in KIAD at approximately 0548 UTC. The technical issue was a discrepancy in the fuel indicating system as compared to the fuel quantity expected to have been on board. Maintenance carried out tests and reset the system. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FMZW, an Air Canada Embraer 190 was conducting flight AC1039 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Denver Intl. (KDEN), CO. Flight crew reported a TCAS Resolution advisory (RA) going into the approach in KDEN. RA was to “Climb” which was actioned by flight crew. Once RA was resolved the aircraft was too high on approach, flight crew elected to execute a missed approach. Flight landed without further incident.

C-FCGC, a Beech Aircraft Corporation King Air 200 aircraft operated by North Cariboo Flying Service Ltd., was conducting flight NCB911 from Edmonton Int'l (CYEG), AB, to Terrace (CYXT), BC with 2 crewmembers and 2 passengers on board. During the initial approach to CYXT, the number 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-41 serial #PCE85035) fuel flow gauge indicated a drop followed by a spike and then began fluctuating. The number 2 oil pressure master warning light then illuminated followed by an oil pressure drop and fluctuation. Concurrently, the number 2 engine surged with torque fluctuations. Following SOPs and the QRH, the crew shut down the number 2 engine and initiated a diversion to Smithers (CYYD), BC. Vancouver Center was advised and the crew declared a Mayday. The crew did not request ARFF but the CYYD FSS ordered the emergency vehicles to standby. The aircraft landed safely, came to a stop, and was towed off the runway. Maintenance conducted troubleshooting and replaced  the #2 engine FCU and high-pressure fuel pump prior to the test flight.

C-FZAA, a Sikorsky S-76A helicopter operated by Helijet International, was conducting flight JBA905 from Vancouver Harbour Heliport (CBC7), BC to Nanaimo Harbour Heliport (CDH5), BC with 2 crew and 8 passengers on board. When the aircraft leveled off at 1000 feet ASL, the pilot flying (PF) felt binding in the cyclic (roll axis). Thinking it was an issue with the cyclic force trim, the PF attempted to clear the problem by engaging the R/H cyclic trim button several times and informed the pilot monitoring (PM) of the situation. The PM checked the pressure gauges and the caution system for abnormalities and found none. The PF passed rotorcraft control to the PM to confirm the binding and to check the force trim release on the L/H cyclic. After troubleshooting did not clear the binding in the cyclic, the crew decided to divert to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC and declared a PAN PAN requesting priority for a runway. In close proximity to the airport, the binding in the cyclic ceased and the crew chose to land on the helipad with the option of using the connected taxiway for a run on landing if necessary. The rotorcraft landed safely and taxied in.Upon inspection, Helijet maintenance found that the Magnetic Brake was sticking "on". They installed a serviceable Magnetic Brake assembly, conducted a satisfactory flight control freedom of movement inspection, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GHQY, a Boeing 787-8 was operated by Air Canada as flight AC0857 from London/Heathrow (EGLL), England to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. In cruise, approximately 340nm WNW of Dublin Intl.(EIDW), Ireland, flight crew heard a loud bang and the captain’s window shattered. QRH actions were completed, dispatch was advised and the decision was made to divert to EIDW. A PanPan was declared with Shanwick Oceanic, flight descended to FL250 and slowed to minimize pressure on window. Flight landed without further incident.

C-GDJR, a privately operated Piper Navajo PA-31-310 aircraft took off from Chilliwack, (CYCW) BC on a training flight with two pilots on board. When the gear was selected up, the crew observed a gear unlocked indication. The gear was cycled and a gear down and safe indication was achieved. The crew's intent was to return to CYCW, but when they selected flaps down there was no movement of the flaps and the landing gear down and locked lights faded out. The crew made the decision to divert to Abbotsford, (CYXX) BC because it had a long runway and emergency equipment. During the diversion to CYXX, all electrical power was lost and communications equipment failed. Using a cell phone, the crew contacted the Kamloops Flight Service Station and declared a Mayday. They explained the situation, stated their intention was to land in CYXX, and requested to have ARFF standing by. On short final, enough electrical power returned for the crew to see they had a landing gear down and locked indication. The aircraft landed uneventfully and taxied to the ramp.Maintenance determined via a continuity check that the RH alternator field wire had an intermittent fault caused by a broken wire and / or a bad terminal crimp. They also found the LH engine noise filter had been removed from the alternator circuit, and wire terminals were taped with automotive electrical tape.

C-GCGF, a Valley B Aviation Robinson Helicopter R66 was being operated for annual company training. The crew was simulating a jammed tail rotor pedal. Once the aircraft was on the ground the pilot reduced the engine power to idle where the engine (Rolls Royce 250-300/A1) flamed out. Following the flight, maintenance inspected the aircraft and has replaced several seals in the engine air system.  A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) has been submitted to Transport Canada.

C-GQCH, a Sikorsky S-92A helicopter operated by Cougar Helicopters, was conducting flight CHI51 from St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL to the Hebron oil platform. During cruise, the crew noted the #1 hydraulic pressure indicate high and then drop to zero. The crew declared a PAN PAN, and returned to CYYT with no further incident. Maintenance found that the heat exchanger had ruptured causing fluid to leak.

The Porter Airlines Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft (POE1250, C-GLQH) was on climb out from Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), as the flaps were retracted the flight crew received a FLAP POWER caution light. The flight crew requested a level off at 3000 feet ASL and performed the QRH procedures. Unable to extinguish the caution light, the crew declared a PAN PAN and contacted company maintenance. A decision was then made to divert to Hamilton/John C. Munro Hamilton Intl (CYHM) due to the longer runway. During the approach the Abnormal Flap Landing checklist was completed and the aircraft landed uneventfully.Maintenance performed a flap drive reset as per AMM and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GEJD, a Learjet 45 operated by Starlink Aviation, was conducting a flight from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ). The flight crew declared an emergency on final approach to CYYZ due to smoke in the cabin. The aircraft landed safely on runway 24R with ARFF standing by. Maintenance found a faulty light controller for the left hand number 2 passenger seat.

Transport Canada flight TGO996, a Beechcraft C90A aircraft, was on route from Hamilton (CYHM) to Ottawa (CYOW) at FL210, with the autopilot engaged when the pilot flying (PF) noted an object directly ahead. Before the PF could disconnect the autopilot and maneuver, the object passed by the right wing. The object appeared to the pilot to have been a Remotely Piloted Air System (RPAS), reddish brown in appearance and weighing approximately 10 lbs. (4.5 kg).

N613CZ, a Compass Airlines Embraer ERJ-175 was operating as flight CPZ5774 from Salt Lake City (KSLC), UT to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB with 4 crew and 63 passengers on board. While on approach to Runway 17L the crew observed a brake fault indication. The crew declared an emergency, and landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. There were no injuries.

C-GYHQ, a Bell 212 HP BLR aircraft operated by Yellowhead Helicopters, was conducting a training flight approximately 8 NM ENE of Blue River (CYCP), BC with the pilot and training pilot on board. The PIC was conducting a simulated power limited take off from a confined area. During the exercise, the training pilot monitored the torque gauges. As the aircraft was turned on ascent to give maximum clearance for the tail rotor, the main rotor struck the top of a fir tree at the aircraft's eight o'clock position. The aircraft was landed at the nearest suitable landing area to conduct an inspection. Damage was found on both main rotor blades, 2 inches inboard from the rotor tips.The main rotor blades were removed and sent for repair. The original equipment manufacturer (OEM) was consulted and replacement main rotor blades were installed.

C-FYKW, an Air Canada Rouge Airbus 319-100, was operating as flight ROU1897 from - Las Vegas/MC Carran Intl (KLAS), NV to Vancouver Intl - (CYVR), BC. During the takeoff run a HOT BRAKE ECAM annunciated and flight crew rejected the take off at approximately 80 KIAS and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft came to complete stop on the runway to assess and subsequently taxied to the gate under its own power. The brake temperature was observed after the rejected take off to have been 750 degrees and the right hand main landing gear (MLG) tires deflated on account that the tire over-temperature protection (fuses) mechanisms had activated. Maintenance inspected the aircraft and right hand inboard and outboard MLG tire assemblies were removed and replaced. The MLG axels were inspected and the right hand inboard and outboard brake assemblies were removed and replaced in accordance with AMM. The after brake emergency application or overheat inspection was carried out with no fault found; serviceability tests were conducted with satisfactory results.

A student pilot was returning to Brampton-Caledon (CNC3) from a cross country solo flight in a Cessna 172P (C-GOZD) aircraft and did not select the correct radio frequency for the Brampton Flying Club. Unable to reach anyone on the radio, the pilot did a precautionary fly over runway 33; runway 15 was active. The pilot then proceeded to land on runway 33. Simultaneously, C-GBBP, a Cessna 172S aircraft with an instructor and student on board had just touched down on runway 15 for a touch and go landing. The instructor observed the other aircraft in the landing flare in front of them, broadcast on the radio for the aircraft to go around, and told his student stop their aircraft. The pilot of C-GOZD continued with the landing and then noticed C-GBBP on the runway in front of him. The pilot of C-GOZD attempted to stop the aircraft with difficulty, so applied right rudder and exited off the side of runway 33 into the infield. There was no damage to either aircraft. There were no injuries.

N416MC, a Boeing 747-412F operated by Atlas Air, was conducting flight GTI8045 from Ramstein Air Force Base, Germany (ETAR) to Dover Air Force Base (KDOV), DE. During cruise, 82 nm NW of Goose Bay Airport (CYYR), NL the crew observed the right hand outboard engine oil quantity turn magenta on the EICAS.  The crew consulted with company flight dispatch and maintenance control. The crew completed a precautionary shut down of the right hand outboard engine but did not declare an emergency. The flight continued to KDOV where it landed without further incident. Maintenance has removed the engine and is being investigated for the original fault.

C-GCGF, a Valley B Aviation Robinson Helicopter R66 was being operated for annual company training. The crew was simulating an engine failure and were performing an autorotation when the engine (Rolls Royce 250-300/A1) flamed out and an autorotation was performed to the ground. The autorotation was successful and there were no injuries to the crew nor damage to the aircraft. The cabin heater was on during the simulated engine failure exercise.

C-GEZX, an Airbus A321-211 was operating as flight Air Transat TSC90D from Lake City Gateway (KLCQ), FL to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QB. While on climb at FL270, flight crew noted left hand engine low oil quantity advisory. The flight crew leveled off for troubleshooting at which point they observed left hand engine oil pressure fluctuation and higher than normal engine temperature. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with ATC, requested a return to land at KLCQ and kept faulty engine at idle until landing. The engine was shut down by flight crew after a safe landing at KLCQ. Inspection was conducted by emergency services once on the ground and oil was observed coming out of the left hand engine. After inspection, flight crew taxied the aircraft to the ramp. Maintenance found gearbox turning tool access cover loose and leaking oil.

C-GLQM, un de Havilland, Dash-8 Q400 exploité par Porter Airlines sous l'indicatif POE480, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC à destination de Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (CYTZ), ON. Le décollage de la piste 06L a été fait après C-FACT, un Dash-8-300 (DH8C) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA753, qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis CYUL à destination de Val-d’Or (CYVO), QC. Une perte d’espacement est survenue lors de la montée initiale, lorsque le POE480 s’est retrouvé 2,4 miles marins (nm) derrière et 600 pieds en dessous du JZA753, alors que l’espacement requis était de 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical ou 3 nm sur le plan horizontal. Un vecteur radar a été donné au JZA753 afin de rétablir la distance requise et les 2 appareils ont poursuivi leurs vols à leurs destinations respectives.

C-FTIQ, un ATR-42-500 exploité par First Air sous l’indicatif FAB883 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Arctic Bay (CYAB), NU  à destination d’Iqaluit (CYFB), NU  avec 8 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage à bord. Un malentendu sur l’autorisation de descente au niveau de vol (FL) 230 est survenue et l’appareil a poursuivi sa descente sous le FL230. À ce moment, C-FTIL, un ATR-42-500 exploité par First Air sous l’indicatif FAB871 qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis CYFB à destination d’Igloolik (CYGT), NU  avec 21 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage à bord, était en monté au niveau de vol 220. Le contrôle de la circulation aérienne a remarqué la descente sous FL230 du FAB883 et est intervenu par l’entremise de la station d'information de vol (FSS) de CYFB, en demandant au FAB883 de stopper la descente au FL200 et au FAB871 de stopper la montée au FL190.  En raison du temps requis pour émettre les autorisations par l’entremise de la FSS, le FAB883 est descendu au FL198 avant de remonter au FL200 alors que les deux appareils étaient environ 40 nm au nord de CYFB. L’espacement entre les deux appareils a été réduit à 800 pieds sur le plan vertical et 6 miles marins (nm) sur le plan horizontal alors que l’espacement requis était de 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical et 10 nm sur le plan horizontal. Les deux appareils étaient en contact radio sur la fréquence 126.7 MHz et étaient affichés sur leurs systèmes de surveillance du trafic et d'évitement des collisions (TCAS). Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FNOG, a Boeing 787-9 was being operated by Air Canada as flight AC25 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Shanghai/Pudong Intl. (ZSPD), China. – Approximately 450nm SE of Anchorage/Ted Stevens Intl. (PANC), AK, flight crew received EICAS message “FMC Verify position” followed shortly by ''Nav unable RNP’’ message. After discussion with dispatch and maintenance, the decision was made to return to CYVR. A PAN PAN was declared, fuel was dumped and flight landed without further incident.

C-FFPH, un Boeing 737-800 exploité par Sunwing Airlines Inc. sous l’indicatif SWG426 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC à destination de Punta Cana Intl. (MDPC) Republique Dominicaine, avec 189 passagers et 6 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors de la montée initiale a 8000 pieds, la lumière « Stabilizer Out of Trim » s’illumine, l'équipage désactive l'autopilote, effectue la compensation en tangage de l’avion manuellement et réactive l'autopilote.  Alors que l’appareil passe le niveau de vol 310 en montée pour le niveau de vol 340, la lumière « Stabilizer Out of Trim » s’illumine de nouveau.  L’équipage complète la liste de vérification, débraye l’autopilote, désactive l’automanette et fait la compensation en tangage de l’avion manuellement.  L’équipage descend au niveau de vol 280 afin de quitter l’espace aérien désigné comme ayant un minimum de séparation verticale réduit (RVSM) et effectue un retour à CYUL après discussion avec le controle de maintenance de Sunwing. L’appareil se pose en surcharge sur la piste 06R sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en attente. Les freins de l’appareil ont été inspectés par les SLIA et par la suite l’appareil a circulé à la barrière sans autre difficulté. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

The Toronto Tower controller observed sparks and possibly flames coming from Air Canada Rouge flight ROU1629, a Boeing B767-300 (C-GHLQ)  aircraft from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON after touching down on runway 05. The tower initiated aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) response. The flight vacated the runway and came to a stop on taxiway Hotel. During inspection, debris and damage to the runway was reported and runway 05 was closed. Following a visual inspection by ARFF which revealed nothing of concern, the aircraft was cleared to taxi to the gate. However, when the aircraft began to move, sparks were observed originating from the left main gear. A maintenance crew was dispatched and discovered that a broken linkage on the left main gear was dragging on the ground, causing the sparks. The linkage was secured and the aircraft was towed to the gate.

C-GARI, un Piper PA-23-250 exploité par Cargair Ltée. effectuait un vol local de formation depuis Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU), QB selon les règles de vol à vue avec un instructeur et un élève à bord. En croisière une vibration a été ressentie et de la fumée est apparue derrière le moteur gauche suivi d’une fuite d’huile sur le capot du moteur. Par la suite le moteur (Avco Lycoming IO-540-C4B5) a fait un bruit très fort et l’instructeur l’a arrêté et a mis l’hélice en drapeau. Le pilote a déclaré un état d’urgence et est revenu se poser sur la piste 24R à CYHU sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FYPN, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Chrono Aviation inc., effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) à destination de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec 88 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage. Lors du décollage, une crevaison d’un des 2 pneus du train principal gauche est survenue. L’équipage a décidé de poursuivre le vol à sa destination et lors de l’approche a demandé la présence des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA).  L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 24R sans encombre, des dommages mineurs ont été notés et il n’y a aucun blessé.

C-GMWJ, a Boeing 737-7CT aircraft was conducting Westjet flight WJA556. En route from Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB to Kitchener-Waterloo (CYKF), ON, flight crew declared a PAN PAN after conducting a missed approach due to a flap problem and requested a diversion to Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ), ON for a longer runway. The aircraft landed without further incident on runway 23 at CYYZ with aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) standing by.

C-FRAD, a Robinson R22 helicopter from Great Lakes Helicopters was landing at the company’s facilities at 0.6nm SSW from Kitchener/Waterloo (CYKF), ON with student pilot and instructor on board. During landing the student was controlling the helicopter with the cyclic and the instructor was operating the collective and anti-torque pedals. The helicopter wasn't quite on the pad after the landing. The instructor lifted the helicopter into a hover and turned cyclic control only over to the student. The helicopter drifted forward past the landing pad, so the student input aft cyclic to move back, but then added an aggressive forward cyclic movement. The helicopter began to rapidly approach the hangar and a tree beside the hangar. The instructor took control, but was unable to arrest the forward momentum. The main rotor blades contacted the tree beside the hangar and the helicopter rolled on its right side. The helicopter was substantially damaged. There were no injuries.

C-GTQC, a Boeing 737-800 operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC691 from Santa Clara/Abel Santamaria (MUSC), Cuba to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. In cruise at FL370, approximately 80nm north of Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL the flight crew noticed right hand ''Eng low oil quantity'' warning with the oil pressure slowly decreasing. A PAN PAN was declared with ATC and the flight crew requested a descent and turn towards KMCO. Shortly after initiating the descent, the oil pressure decreased to 25-24psi with a flickering amber indication and almost immediately the right hand engine failed with the ''ENG FAIL'' indication. The crew changed their status to MAYDAY with ATC and accomplished the required Non-Normal Checklists. The aircraft landed on RWY 36R at KMCO and once the aircraft was checked out by ARFF, the crew taxied to the terminal.

N280GU a Gulfstream G280 aircraft was conducting a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Los Angeles Intl. (KLAX), CA.  N280GU taxied to runway 23 as directed, crossed the hold short line for Runway 23 at Taxiway Q and stopped just past the hold short line. Philippine Air Lines PAL118, an Airbus A350-941 aircraft flying from Manilla/Ninoy Aquino Intl. (RPLL), Philippines to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON was on final for Runway 23 and was consequently instructed to initiate a missed approach.  PAL118 landed safely following the missed approach.

C-FGWJ, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet Airlines, was operating as flight WJA450 from Abbotsford (CYXX), BC to Calgary Intl.(CYYC), AB. WJA450 was on the initial descent into the greater CYYC area. C-GOIA, a SAAB 340B aircraft operated by Pacific Coastal Airlines was conducting flight PCO3040 from Cranbrook (CYXC), BC to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB. PCO3040 was also on the initial descent into the greater CYYC area. Approximately 42 nm SSW of CYYC the separation between WJA450 and PCO3040 eroded to 4.7 nm laterally and 700 feet vertically where 5 nm laterally or 1000 feet vertically is required. Separation was re-established 19 seconds later.

C-FNEN, un de Havilland Dash-8 Q400 exploité par WestJet Encore sous l’indicatif WEN3524 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Toronto/Lester B. Pearson (CYYZ), ON à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC avec 63 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Alors que l’appareil était en descente pour l’approche, de la fumée est apparue au-dessus de la barre collectrice du réchauffage pare-brise du côté droit. L’équipage a coupé l’alimentation électrique au réchauffage du pare-brise, a complété la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et la fumée a cessée. Une urgence a été déclarée et les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 24L, il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil. L’inspection post-envolée a trouvé des signes d'amorce d'arc électrique sur la borne annulaire (L2) du bloc de jonction du pare-brise du copilote et la borne fut remplacée.

C-GRXN a Pilatus PC-12/47E was performing Ornge flight 528707. Enroute to Fort Albany (CYFA), ON from Timmins (CYTS), ON  the Captain (Pilot Flying) experienced a sudden onset of nausea and dizziness. Unable to continue duties as Pilot Flying (PF), aircraft control was transferred to the First Officer, and the flight returned to CYTS where it landed succesfully.

C-GAAS, a Cessna 525B operated by Airsprint Inc., was conducting flight ASP567 from Buffalo Niagara Intl. (KBUF), NY to Charlottesville-Albemarle (KCHO), VA. During cruise at FL330 the Cabin alt hi cas msg illuminated on annunciator system. Flight Crew donned the o2 masks, initiated an emergency descent and noted the cabin alt was around 11000'.  Flight Crew actioned the emergency checklist, ATC was notified and a mayday was declared. Flight Crew was advised that Bradford Regional (KBFD), PA was nearby and asked for vectors for an approach into KBFD.  While being vectored, it was ascertained through the emergency checklist that the air source select knob was in the off position. Flight Crew decided to return to KBUF due to runway condition in KBFD and declined ARFF services.   The aircraft landed safely in KBUF.

C-GYJP, an Airbus 319-214 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1848 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Los Cabos Intl. (MMSD), Mexico. During cruise, one of the flight attendants became ill and was unable to continue duties. The duties were distributed to other cabin crew members and the flight landed uneventfully.

C-GXNW a Gulfstream 150 from Skyservice Business Aviation, flight 264, was arriving from Teterboro (KTEB), NJ into Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ), ON declared a PAN PAN while on final for Runway 05 due to an icing issue. Emergency Response Services were deployed and the aircraft landed safely.

N318FE a McDonnell Douglas MD-10 was conducting FedEx flight FDX132. On arrival in Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ) from Memphis Intl. (KMEM), TN, flight crew declared an emergency due to inoperable de-icing equipment. The aircraft landed without further incident.

N848AE Envoy Air flight ENY3386, an Embraer E135 aircraft, was taxiing for departure from Toronto / LBPIA (CYYZ), ON and was instructed by ATC to taxi to Runway 24 L but hold short of the Runway 24L approach line on taxiway D7. The flight crew read back the instructions correctly. However, ATC observed ENY3386 cross over the Runway 24L approach line, and instructed the aircraft to stop.  C-GBIM, an Airbus A319 aircraft performing Air Canada Rouge flight ROU1525, was on final approach for Runway 24L and was instructed to initiate a missed approach. Rou1525 flight landed without incident after missed approach.

C-FLRJ, a BAE Systems RJ85 operated by Summit Air Ltd. was conducting flight FAB239 on behalf of Canadian North from Bonnyville (CYBF), AB to Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU with 4 crew and 17 passengers on board. Approximately 150 nm east of CYRT, the "FLAP INOP" light illuminated on the flight deck. The flight crew conducted the appropriate checklist, reported the issue with the flaps to air traffic services and elected to divert to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT. The flight crew subsequently requested ARFF be placed on standby. An uneventful flap 0 landing was successfully completed at CYZF. Company maintenance completed the appropriate inspections and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FJZL, a Jazz Aviation CRJ-900 aircraft, was conducting flight JZA8670 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to San Diego Int'l (KSAN), CA with 75 passengers and 4 crew members on board. After take off, the crew received an anti-skid caution message as well as an outboard ground spoiler fault indication. The landing gear was unable to retract for several minutes before it eventually retracted. The flight crew decided to return to CYVR and declared a PAN PAN to ATC. The aircraft landed safely. ARFF inspected the tires, found no discrepancies and the aircraft taxied to the gate.Maintenance personnel replaced the main landing gear speed transducer and adjusted the main landing gear weight on wheels proximity sensor and target. Operational test of the component and sensor was carried out with no further faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPTL, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 aircraft operated by Yellowhead Helicopters, was on a local training flight from Prince George (CYXS), BC to conduct external load (longline) Hydraulic Off emergency training, with the pilot and training pilot on board. On final for the CYXS field, the long line release button was inadvertently engaged thereby releasing the slung load. The longline and simulated load landed in a field and were retrieved by vehicle. There were no injuries or damage. The aircraft belly hook was inspected by maintenance personnel and no defects were noted.

C-GDGD, a Pilatus PC12/45 flight BF710 aircraft operated by North Star Air Ltd., departed Kapuskasing (CYYU), ON for Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON and was climbing through 15000 feet when the flight crew received a cabin altitude warning. The flight crew donned oxygen masks and instructed the one passenger to put on an oxygen mask as well. The flight crew carried out the Cabin Pressure Fail checklist and found that the Environmental Control System (ECS) switch was in the ''off'' position. The switch was placed in the ''on'' position and pressurization returned to normal. The flight crew requested a lower altitude as a precaution and continued to CYPL. Flight landed safely.

G-CIVP, un Boeing 747-400 exploité par British Airways sous l’indicatif BAW44N, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK, à destination de San Diego Intl. (KSAN), CA. En vol de croisière, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison d’un problème avec l’indicateur de vitesse. À 2006z, l’équipage déclaré que la situation à bord avait été réglée et qu’ils annulaient l’urgence. L’appareil a poursuivi son vol sans encombre.

C-GSNM, a Beech King Air E90 operated by SkyNorth Air, was conducting flight SN696 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Island Lake (CYIV), MB. During the initial climb, at approximately 400 feet AGL, the flight crew noticed smoke in the cockpit. At 2000 feet AGL, the flight crew referenced the QRH and requested a return to CYWG. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF on standby. There was a strong order of jet fuel but no fire was observed in flight. The operator's maintenance found a loose fuel line on the left hand engine. This line was used to defuel the aircraft prior to the flight.

C-GAQN, a DHC-8-311 aircraft operated by North Cariboo Flying Service, was conducting flight NCB2806 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Kelowna (CYLW), BC with 3 crew members on board. During a level off at 9000 feet ASL, the flight crew observed #2 engine oil pressure drop and requested a return to CYVR. The oil pressure gauge began to fluctuate including dropping to zero. The crew declared an emergency, landed, and taxied clear of the runway at CYVR without further incident. Maintenance replaced the oil pressure transducer and the flight deck oil pressure indicator.

C-GLWJ, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3297 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Prince George (CYXS), BC with 4 crew and 78 passengers on board. During a hold over the Prince George VOR (YXS), the crew elected to return to CYVR after receiving a Runway Surface Condition report stating the runway was 70% ice covered with reported poor braking. Approximately 17 NM northwest of CYVR, the aircraft DEICE PRESSURE caution light illuminated. QRH procedures were conducted with the caution light extinguishing momentarily and then re-illuminating. Due to aircraft vibration and icing conditions, a PAN PAN was declared. The flight crew requested a lower altitude immediately. The aircraft was vectored for an approach and landed safely without further incident. The operator's maintenance conducted an inspection of the airframe pneumatic deicing boots and replaced the DeIce timer and monitor unit. Operational checks were carried out and no defects were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FTDW, a Boeing 737-800 operated by Sunwing Airlines Inc., was conducting flight SWG081 from Daytona Beach Intl (KDAB), FL to Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL. Flight SWG081 was cleared for takeoff from runway 7L and was advised by ATC of a Cessna departing from runway 7R. During the climb at about 700 feet, the flight crew received a TCAS TA followed by TCAS RA `Maintain Vertical Speed'.  The flight crew complied with the RA and had the traffic in sight. ATC was advised and the flight continued uneventfully.

C-FKMX, un Aérospatiale AS350 B3 exploité par Questral helicopters effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue (VFR) de levées aériennes dans la région située à 60nm ENE de Puvirnituq (CYPX), QC, depuis et à destination du camp REX (60°17'8.05"N 75°21'44.87"W), QC, avec 1 pilote à son bord. Durant le vol, le pilote a senti une odeur de brulé et peu après de la fumée est apparue dans le poste de pilotage. L’équipement de levées aériennes a été éteint et le pilote est retourné au camp sans encombre. Une fois au sol, il a été découvert qu’un branchement du circuit d’alimentation principal de l’équipement s’est débranché causant un court-circuit. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

N818UA, an Airbus A319 operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL1184 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Denver Int'l (KDEN), CO with 80 passengers and 5 crew on board. On the take off roll on Runway 08R, a blue heron bird hit the aircraft, near the right engine area. The flight crew rejected the take off, exited on taxiway Delta, came to a stop, and requested ARFF. Emergency personnel sprayed the main landing gear with foam due to reported high brake temperatures. The passengers and flight attendants deplaned via air stairs and were bussed to the passenger terminal. There were no injuries. Maintenance personnel cleaned the right engine cowl and pylon and found no damage. The main landing gear wheel fuse plugs melted as designed due to the high energy stop and the tires deflated. All 4 main landing gear brakes and wheels were replaced as per United Aircraft Maintenance Manual.

C-FGWR, a Beechcraft King Air 200 operated by Keewatin Air LP, was conducting a repositioning flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Thompson (CYTH), MB. During the approach into CYTH, the flight crew selected gear down but the landing gear did not extend nor display any gear indication position. The flight crew carried out a missed approach, requested a holding procedure to consult the QRH and declared an emergency with ATC. The flight crew conducted a manual extension of the landing gear and confirmed the gear was down and locked. The aircraft landed safely with EMS on standby. The aircraft was shut down on the runway and towed to the apron. The operator's maintenance subsequently inspected and tested the landing gear system and was unable to duplicate the fault. The aircraft was released subject to satisfactory test flight; which was completed satisfactory.

C-FLSU, an Airbus 320-211 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA664 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC to Halifax/Stanfield Intl. (CYHZ), NS. On approach to CYHZ, the crew noticed a slight vibration when flaps were extended to FLAPS 3 (20 degrees)position. Later in approach when the flaps were selected to FLAPS FULL (35 degrees), the vibration became stronger. The crew immediately reduced the flaps setting to FLAPS 2 (15 degrees), initiated a missed approach, and declared PAN PAN with air traffic services. The crew selected FLAPS 3 (20 degrees) for the second approach, and landed without further incident. Maintenance inspection found that the left hand spoiler servo rod end had separated from the servo assembly.

N182GJ, un Bombardier CRJ900 (CL-600-2D24) exploité par GoJet Airlines LLC sous l'indicatif GJS6283 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County (KDTW), MI à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QB.  N304PQ, un Bombardier CRJ900 (CL-600-2D24) exploité par Endeavor Air sous l'indicatif EDV5473 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de LaGuardia (KLGA), NY à destination de CYUL. Lors de l’alignement des aéronefs pour l’approche finale à CYUL, l'espacement minimal de 5 milles marins horizontalement a été réduit à 2.7 milles marins horizontalement et 700 pieds verticalement alors que la norme est de 3 milles sur le plan horizontal ou 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GHJK, a Sikorsky S-76C++ helicopter operated by Helijet International, was conducting flight JBA713 from Vancouver/Harbour (Public) (CBC7), BC to Victoria Harbour (Camel Point - CBF7), BC with 2 pilots and 11 passengers on board. In cruise at 4000 feet ASL, the left hand Engine (Turbomeca Arriel 252) Chip Light illuminated. The crew completed the required drill memory items, elected to divert to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC, and then completed the emergency checklist. The crew declared a PAN PAN and performed a run on landing without further incident. The crew shut down and secured the left hand engine while taxiing from the runway. Emergency vehicles followed the aircraft. Maintenance personnel inspected the engine chip plugs with no fault found, and replaced a chip detector.

N60125, a privately operated Beechcraft B300 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Narsarsuaq airport (BGBW), Greenland to CFB Goose Bay (CYYR), NL with 2 crewmembers on board. When about 158 nm northeast of CYYR, the crew received an amber master caution low right fuel warning (R FUEL QTY) and observed that fuel was not transferring from the right wing tank to the right nacelle tank. The crew declared an emergency and landed about 52 minutes later without incident.

C-GKOE, an Airbus 320-214 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC782 from Los Angeles Intl (KLAX), CA to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QB. On the take-off roll, the cabin crew reported the smoke and odor event to the flight deck right after rotation. The flight crew declared a Mayday, donned their oxygen masks and conducted a return to KLAX. Subsequently, the smoke and odor dissipated. Once on the ground, ERS conducted an exterior inspection before the taxi to the gate. Two cabin air recirculation filters were replaced and a compressor wash completed on both engines.

C-FASF, an Embraer 545 operated by AirSprint Inc. as flight ASP827, was on approach to Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ), ON when a flight crew member was ill and unable to continue their duties. The aircraft landed uneventfully. The company sent a reminder to flight crews to advise ATC in such a scenario.

N910SW a Skywest Airlines Bombardier CRJ200 was operating as flight SKW5491 from San Francisco Intl. (KSFO), CA  to Calgary Intl.(CYYC), AB. During the initial approach to CYYC, the flight crew selected flaps down from 0° to 8°. The flaps did not extend beyond 0°. The flight crew discontinued the approach, requested vectors and actioned the QRH. The flight crew then declared an emergency and proceeded to conduct a flaps up landing. The aircraft landed without further incident. There were no injuries.

C-GHPQ, a Boeing 787-8 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC125 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC. After conducting a missed approach due to low visibility the crew requested a CAT 3 approach to RWY 08L. On short final the crew received a No Autoland status and a go around was conducted, followed by a diversion to Seattle-Tacoma (KSEA), WA. In the go around, the crew received an Insufficient Fuel advisory so they declared a PAN PAN with KSEA in order to get a straight approach to one of the three parallel runways, 16L, 16C and 16R as opposed to RWY 34, which was in use at the time. The flight landed uneventfully on runway 16L. Fuel quantity on aircraft shut down fuel was 2800kg, 800kg above minimum.

C-FKPT, an Airbus A320 was operating as flight Air Canada ACA351 from Ottawa/MacDonald Cartier Intl.(CYOW), ON  to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB. While on the ILS approach to CYYC Runway 35R, at approximately 1000 feet agl, the flight crew experienced restricted rudder pedal operation. The rudder input felt heavier than normal. The aircraft landed without incident and no emergency was declared. There were no injuries. Company maintenance replaced the rudder artificial feel travel limit unit.

C-FCMR, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Central Mountain Air Ltd.(CMA), was conducting flight GLR587 from Campbell River (CYBL), BC to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC with 2 pilots and 10 passengers on board. After take-off, when the landing gear was selected up, the Landing Gear Relay circuit breaker (CB) tripped. The CB was reset and tripped again on a second attempt to raise the gear. The aircraft continued to CYVR with the landing gear extended and the crew requested ARFF to standby. The aircraft landed without further incident. CMA's avionics maintenance could not identify the cause of the CB tripping and the gear actuators were changed.

C-FXLH, a Bombardier CL600-2B19 operated by Voyageur Airways Corp., was conducting flight UNO196P from Sana'a Intl. (OYSN), Yemen to Aden Intl. (OYAA), Yemen. During descent through 14000 at 260 kias, with thrust levers at idle, the aircraft experienced an engine noise followed by a vibration.  The right hand engine ITT increased significantly; the engine was shut down in accordance with the Quick Reference Handbook.  ATC, dispatch and the five passengers were briefed in accordance with company emergency procedures. The aircraft diverted to Djibouti/Ambouli Intl. (HDAM), Djibouti and landed uneventfully.

C-FCMB, a Central Mountain Air Ltd. Beechcraft 1900D, was operating as flight GLR775 from Edmonton International (CYEG), AB to High Level (CYOJ), AB. After the aircraft had landed and taxied to the ramp, the aircraft was marshalled into a fuelling bay where the aircraft's left wingtip contacted a parked fuel truck and damaged the strobe light. The strobe light lens and bulb were replaced. No other damage was found on the aircraft.

N230NN, un Embraer ERJ-175 exploité par Envoy Air inc. sous l’indicatif ENY3981 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC à destination de l’aéroport Dallas-Fort Worth Intl. (KDFW), TX. Lors de la montée initiale, l’agent de bord a déployé accidentellement les masques à oxygène de la cabine des passagers. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence en préparation pour un atterrissage lourd et est revenu se poser sans encombre à CYUL sur la piste 24L. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. Le service de maintenance a remis en état de service les masques à oxygène déployés.

C-GKQB, a DHC-8-400 operated by Porter Airlines Inc., was conducting flight POE386 from Chicago/ Midway Intl. (KMDW), IL to Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON. On the takeoff roll, the #1 PEC Caution light illuminated. The crew cancelled the caution light and the take-off was continued. There were no abnormalities. In cruise the QRH checklist was completed and a white power plant #1 PEC caution light was observed. A PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft diverted and landed at John C. Munro Hamilton Intl. (CYHM) ON.

C-GBEH, a privately registered Piper PA17 was conducting a local flight from Russell (CJW5), MB. While conducting a low pass in the vicinity of a friend's house, the aircraft collided with a power line. The pilot subsequently maintained control of the aircraft but landed in a field. During the landing, the right gear sustained substantial damage. The pilot was uninjured and the ELT did not activate.

C-FADE, a privately operated Cessna 340A aeroplane was conducting a local VFR flight from Kelowna (CYLW), BC with one person on board. As the aircraft climbed through 9200 feet ASL, oil was seen on the left engine nacelle. The pilot advised the Vancouver Area Control Centre (ACC) of the situation and that a precautionary shut down of the left engine would be completed. The pilot stated they would return to CYLW and plan to land straight in on Runway 16. The ACC requested fuel on board and number of souls before passing the aircraft over to the CYLW control tower. ARFF was put on standby and followed the aircraft after it landed without incident. Maintenance personnel found the left engine (Teledyne Continental TSIO-520-NB, serial number L-276661-R) had leaked approximately five liters of oil and were unable to determine what caused the leak.

C-FIBW, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet Airlines, was conducting flight WJA701 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Int'l (CYYZ), ON to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC. During cruise, a flight attendant became incapacitated and could not complete their duties. The flight duties for landing were distributed amongst remaining flight attendants.

N506DJ, a Falcon 2000 airplane operated by Dumont Aviation as flight SDU506, deviated from KEPRA2 SID RWY 23 after departure from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ). This resulted in a loss of separation with Rouge flight ROU1764, an Airbus A319 (C-FYJE) aircraft, departing runway 24L. The separation was reduced to 1.8nm and 400 feet.

C-FKCJ, a Boeing 757-200 operated by Cargojet Airways ltd, was conducting flight CJT920 from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky Intl (KCVG), KY to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. During the climb, the aircraft experienced a pressurization loss. A PAN PAN was declared along with an emergency descent. The aircraft returned to KCVG at 10000 feet and landed uneventfully. On initial inspection, maintenance found that the upper cabin pressure relief valve was partially open and jammed with insulation. The debris was removed and the valve reset to the closed position, checked as serviceable and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSDK, a Diamond DA42 aircraft, was on a local IFR training flight from Abbotsford (CYXX), BC with an instructor and student on board. During a simulated single engine ILS approach to landing on Runway 07 at CYXX, vertical guidance from the avionics became inoperative and the flight continued as a localizer only approach. The aircraft landed with the landing gear retracted and slid to a stop on the fuselage. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FNNU, a Boeing 777-300 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC0891 from Leonardo da Vinci Intl. Rome (LIRF), Italy to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ) ON, with 15 crew members and 448 passengers on board.  After takeoff, the flight crew received a fire/smoke warning from the forward cargo hold, and the cabin crew advised of a chemical smell. The fire handle was pulled by the flight crew and an emergency declared. The aircraft returned to LIRF and an overweight landing was carried out. Fire trucks met the aircraft for an inspection; maintenance personnel were unable to find the source of the fault. The aircraft was released and during the next flight the cabin crew noticed an odor that was due to the galley area heater. After an uneventful flight to CYYZ, maintenance found a faulty smoke detector and door heater installed incorrectly (airflow in opposite direction).

C-GJCN, the Canadian North Dash 8-300, operating as MPE9855 on a flight from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Calgary (CYYC), AB, experienced smoke in the cockpit during engine start-up at the gate. Smoke entered the flight deck from the lower right hand duct vent, followed by instrument failures on the first officer's side panel. The crew initiated an immediate engine shutdown and evacuated the aircraft. The company was notified and the fire trucks were not called to the scene. No passengers were on board the aircraft at the time of the occurrence. The aircraft was removed from service pending an investigation and corrective action by maintenance.

C-FJZD, a Bombardier CRJ-900 operated by Jazz Aviation LP., was conducting flight AC8038, from Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC to Chicago/O'Hare Intl. (KORD), IL with 4 crew members and 64 passengers on board. While enroute the flight crew requested Emergency Medical Services (EMS) to meet the aircraft on arrival due to a passenger illness. An emergency was declared; the aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-FJZK, a Boeing 767-3Q8ER aircraft operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1854 from Las Vegas/McCarran Intl. (KLAS), NV to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. During cruise the cabin crew noted smoke emanating from the oven and they discharged the fire extinguisher. The flight landed in CYYZ uneventfully.

C-FMWV, a Boeing 767-333ER operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1852 from Las Vegas/McCarran Intl. (KLAS) NV to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. Upon reaching cruise altitude of FL350, the flight crew noted smoke and odor in the cockpit. Applicable QRH drills were completed and flight crew declared a MAYDAY. The flight subsequently landed in KLAS RWY 26L with ARFF on standby. After landing, the flight crew reported that the LH Brake was over 600 degrees Celsius. The aircraft taxied to a remote location on the airport to allow the brakes to cool. Once the brakes reached an acceptable temperature the aircraft taxied to the gate uneventfully.

C-GSIA, a Northern Air Charter (P.R.) Inc. Beechcraft B200 was operating as flight NLI373 from Calgary International (CYYC), AB to Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB. Just prior to descent into CYYM the flight crew noticed smoke coming from the co-pilot's subpanel. All non-essential electrics were turned off and the smoke cleared. An emergency was declared and ARFF was standing by for the landing in CYMM. The aircraft landed without further incident.Following the flight, maintenance determined that the smoke was caused by a defective blower motor. The motor was deferred and the aircraft was flown (crew only) to CYYC for further maintenance.

C-GFEH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight TOM2713 from Catania-Fontanarossa Vincenzo Bellini (LICC), Italy to Ringway Intl. Manchester (EGCC), England with 6 crew members and 169 passengers on board. During the approach, one of the flight attendants became ill and was unable to continue duties. The duties were distributed to other cabin crew members and the flight landed uneventfully.

N7025J, a Grumman HU16 from The International Test Pilot School's (ITPS), departed London Intl. (CYXU), ON RWY 27 and climbed to the north west. Approximately 4nm from CYXU the pilot requested priority landing on RWY 27 due to a smell in cockpit. ARFF was placed on standby. The  aircraft landed without incident and taxied back to the ITPS apron. Maintenance conducted a thorough inspection of the aircraft, but was unable to find any discrepancies. The aircraft was released the following day and was flown without further incident.

C-GMLF, un Pilatus exploité par Private Air inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) à destination de La Romaine (CTT5), QC . C-GURM, un Dash 8-300 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental sous l’indicatif QUE40 effectuait un vol d’évacuation médicale selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport des Îles-de-la-Madeleine (CYGR), QC  à destination de Sept-Îles (CYZV), QC. C-GMLF a décollé de la piste 09 et était en montée initiale lorsque QUE40 a été autorisé à effectuer son approche pour la piste 27. L’autorisation d’approche de QUE40 a été transmise avant que C-GMLF ait dégagé l’approche de la piste 27. L’espacement minimal requis de 5 milles marins horizontalement ou 1000 pieds verticalement n’a pu être maintenu. C-GMLF a reçu du contrôleur aérien des instructions afin de rétablir l’espacement qui a été réduit jusqu’à 3.6 milles marins horizontalement et 800 pieds verticalement. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FIUR, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC2311, from Singapore/Changi Intl. (WSSS), Singapore to Tokyo/Haneda Intl. (RJTT), Japan with 2 crew members and no passengers on board. The purpose of the flight was for repositioning due to maintenance work. During cruise, the flight crew received a Left main landing gear Brace L message on the EICAS. On descent to Tokyo airport, a PAN PAN was declared; the aircraft landed uneventfully. Maintenance is troubleshooting the left main landing gear.

C-GGNY, un Dash 8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l’indicatif JZA500 avec à son bord 4 membres d'équipage et 54 passagers effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL), QC à destination de Fredericton(CYFC), NB. Lors de la montée initiale, la lumière d’avertissement de porte de fuselage s’est illuminée. Les membres d’équipage ont suivi la liste de vérification appropriée et ont constaté que la lumière de la porte-cargo arrière était illuminée. Un PAN PAN a été déclaré et l’appareil est retourné se poser sans encombre à CYUL. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. Après vérification, il a été déterminé que la poignée de la porte-cargo arrière avait mal été sécurisée lors de sa fermeture.

C-FEMM, un Grumman Traveler exploité par Ottawa Biplane Adventures inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport d’Ottawa/Rockliffe (CYRO), ON pour un vol touristique local avec un pilote et 2 passagers à son bord. Alors que l’appareil était établi à 2000 pieds au-dessus du niveau de la mer et se dirigeait vers le centre-ville d’Ottawa pour un tour de ville, le pilote a actionné la manette du réchauffe-carburateur. Presque immédiatement après, les révolutions du moteur sont passées de 2300 à 1600 tours par minute accompagnée de fortes vibrations. Le pilote a immédiatement activé la pompe électrique d’alimentation en carburant et ouvert la manette des gaz au maximum sans aucune amélioration. Le pilote a déclaré une situation de détresse à la Tour de contrôle d’Ottawa et s’est dirigé vers le parc de la Baie pour y effectuer un atterrissage d’urgence. Une fois atterri, le pilote a appliqué les freins au maximum, mais n’a pu éviter la collision avec les arbres devant lui. La radiobalise de détresse a été activée par l’impact. Le pilote et les 2 passagers ont pu évacuer sans difficulté et n’ont pas été blessés. Les services d’urgence avaient été avisés et sont arrivés peu de temps après. Aucun incendie ne s’est déclaré.

C-GCGQ, a BH412, Bell Helicopter operated by Transport Canada (TC), Aircraft Services Directorate (ASD) for the Canadian Coast Guard, was conducting flight CTG944 from Hopedale Airport (CYHO), NL to Stripe Island (24nm ESE of CYHO), NL. During flight, the helicopter was long lining a tower and noticed a slow rotation of the load. Slowing down approximately 1nm from the site, the pilot checked the load and noticed it had stopped rotating. Within 5 seconds later and 200 feet away from the intended lay down area, the long line released at 150 feet above the ground. The helicopter landed without incident. After shutdown the pilot noticed the electric plug from the aircraft cargo hook was missing and the wire had a small tear in the outer cover, which lined up with the manual release. The TC ASD safety department, after completing a preliminary investigation, believed that due to the slow rotation during the flight, the long line may have kinked and contacted the manual release.  There was no swivel on the belly hook, which likely contributed to this occurrence.

C-GBTU, a de Havilland DHC-3T (powered by a GE/Walter M601E-11 turbine engine) operated by Blue Water Aviation Services, was conducting a flight from Bissett (CJY6), MB to Family Lake near Little Grand Rapids, MB with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. As C-GBTU was turning final for the water at Family Lake the right wing became detached from the fuselage. The aircraft entered an uncontrolled descent and collided with the water surface. JRCC and RCMP responded. The pilot and 2 passengers sustained fatal injuries.

C-GTAT a De Havilland DHC-8-300 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA604 from Sudbury (CYSB), ON to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. Shortly after departure from Sudbury, flight crew advised ATC of a landing gear issue and requested holding in the YSB area to troubleshoot. The flight crew advised ATC that they were unable to retract gear and requested return to CYSB. Emergency was declared and ARFF services were put on stand by. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GUON, a De Havilland DHC-8-300 airplane operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight JZA613, was en route from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Sudbury (CYSB), ON when the flight crew received a hydraulic system 1 low message. The flight crew elected to return to CYYZ, declared an emergency and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FBHF, un hélicoptère Bell 212 exploité par Hélicoptères Canadiens Limitée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Hall Beach (CYUX), NU à destination d’un site situé à 51 milles marins à l’est-nord-est de CYUX. L’hélicoptère transportait du carburant au site. En raison d’un problème en lien avec les réservoirs sur le site, le pilote ne pouvait pas atterrir sur l’hélipad désigné à cet effet. Il a donc choisi un autre endroit pour se poser. Lors du second décollage de cette zone d’atterrissage, le pilote a entendu un « bang » et ressenti des vibrations significatives. Il a atterri immédiatement et fermé les deux moteurs. Les pales du rotor principal sont entrées en collision avec la partie supérieure de la cage de sécurité de l’escalier d’un réservoir qui se situait dans l’axe de décollage. Le pilote seul à bord n'a pas été blessé.

C-GOWG, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines Inc., was conducting flight QS1055, from Valencia/Manises (LEVN), Spain to  Prague/Václav Havel (LKPR), Spain with 6 crew members and 186 passengers on board.
