The flight crew was asked to expedite to FL300; during the climb they received a TCAS RA to descend and level-off. They complied and informed ATC. Once the traffic was in sight, and they were clear of the conflict, they resumed the climb to FL300. The flight continued uneventfully.

C-GBZS, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines Inc., was conducting flight SWG764, Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL) QC  to St. Maarten/Princess Juliana Intl. (TNCM), Netherlands with 6 crew members and 176 passengers on board. A crew member became ill; after consultation with medical experts the aircraft continued with one of the flight attendants seated in the jumpseat as a precaution. The aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-GLRN, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines Inc., was conducting flight TOM1574, from Shannon Intl (EINN), Ireland to Reus (LERS), Spain with 6 crew members and 170 passengers on board. The flight crew was cleared to begin their descent into LERS, from FL390 to FL370. During the descent through FL375 a TCAS TA followed by a TCAS RA to level off was received. The crew complied with the instruction and advised air traffic control. The flight was then cleared to continue their descent, and the flight continued uneventfully.

C-GNZS, un hélicoptère Airbus Helicopters AS355N Twinstar exploité par Hélicoptères Canadiens, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue au départ de Sept-Îles (CYZV), QC à destination de la station Tika, avec 1 pilote et 4 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée initiale immédiatement après le décollage, le moteur de gauche (Turbomeca Arrius 1A) a subi une réduction de la puissance et l’hélicoptère a tourné vers la droite. Le pilote a posé l’appareil au point de départ, il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FYJH, an Airbus A319 aircraft operating as Air Canada Rouge flight ROU1640 was vectored within close proximity of Air Canada Rouge flight ROU1706, an Airbus A321 (C-GHQI) aircraft, resulting in loss of separation. Separation was reduced to 2.5nm where 3nm was required.

C-GSCA, an Air Canada rouge LP Boeing 767-375ER, operating as flight ROU1599, was holding short of runway 05 at Toronto/LBPIA prior to departure. The flight crew observed R HYD QTY and R HYD SYS PRESS EICAS messages and initiated the associated QRH checklists. The flight crew subsequently identified the R HYD quantity and pressure were indicating nil values. An aircraft behind ROU1599 reported to ATC that ROU1599 was observed to be leaking significant fluid from the right wing area, and that smoke was emanating from the right main landing gear. ARFF was requested and responded. The flight crew shut down the engines, after which company maintenance attended the aircraft. The aircraft was subsequently towed back to the gate; there were no injuries.

C-FDBD, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines Inc., was conducting flight TFL194, Kos Island Intl (LGKO), Greece to Amsterdam/Schiphol (EHAM), Netherlands with 6 crew members and 183 passengers on board. During the climb through FL300, ATC asked the flight crew if they could climb to FL360 and how long it would take. The flight crew replied in the affirmative and indicated it would take 4 minutes. While climbing the flight crew informed ATC that they would be unable to make FL360 within the 4 minutes. Leveling off at FL360 a TCAS RA (Monitor vertical speed) was triggered. No action was required, the flight continued uneventfully.

C-FABA, a de Havilland DHC-8-102 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG815 from Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON to Fort Severn (CYER), ON with 3 crew members on board. While enroute, the crew received a weight on wheels (WOW) caution light and decided to return to CYPL. During the return trip, the WOW caution light went out and then illuminated once more during approach into CYPL. The crew proceeded to land on Runway 09 at CYPL and then received several caution lights on touchdown. During the landing roll, the aircraft did not respond to tiller steering input. As the aircraft came to a slower speed (below 30 kts), the aircraft brakes were unresponsive and the crew then lost directional control and the aircraft then veered off the runway. The aircraft came to a stop approximately 100 feet off to the north side of the runway. There were no injuries and the aircraft sustained minor damage. An inspection of the landing gear system by the operator's maintenance revealed two faulty proximity sensors.

C-GUBC an Airbus A330 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC571 from Venice/Marco Polo (LIPZ), Italy to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QB with 11 crew members and 310 passengers on board. Approximately 45 minutes into the flight, a passenger notified a cabin crew member that some smoke and sparks could be seen in the vicinity of the R2 door floor. The flight crew were notified, declared a MAYDAY with ATC and diverted to Paris/Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks and performed the appropriate checklists. The smoke was accompanied with an electric smell and dissipated during the descent. During the final approach, some smoke and flames reappeared and the cabin crew discharged a portable fire extinguisher. Once on the ground the fire brigade inspected the aircraft and the aircraft was cleared to proceed to the terminal.An heated Floor Board was found at fault. This phenomenon is already known and monitored by Airbus with the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA). Airbus Support has requested the part for expertise and created a shared occurrence with EASA as part of Continued Airworthiness.  The Bureau d’Enquêtes et d’Analyses pour la sécurité (BEA) does not open an investigation into this occurrence.

C-FUFZ, the Canadian Harvard Aircraft Association Harvard 4 was landing at Tillsonburg (CYTB) after completing a local flight with the pilot in the front seat and the check pilot in the rear seat. The aircraft touched down normally on Rwy. 08. On the rollout at 40 to 50 knots ground speed, the aircraft drifted to the right. The pilot applied opposite rudder but found no response. Additional rudder input and left brake resulted in the aircraft ground looping to the left. The right wingtip struck the ground and right landing gear was damaged. There were no injuries.

HB-JHE, un Airbus A330-300 exploité par Swiss en tant que vol SWR87 avec à son bord 12 membres d'équipage et 206 passagers effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montral/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QB et Zürich-Kloten (LSZH) en Suisse. Suite au décollage l'équipage de conduite a observé le message ''L/G R LENGTHENING FAULT'' sur le moniteur électronique centralisé de bord (ECAM). Un PAN PAN a été déclaré et l'appareil est revenu se poser en surcharge sans encombre à CYUL. Le personnel d'entretien a observé que l'allongement du cylindre hydraulic du train d'atterrissage principal droit était endommagé.

C-GGMZ, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Air Canada Express, was conducting flight JZA8209 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Prince George (CYXS), BC with 4 crew members and 78 passengers on board. During the climb from CYVR, the flight crew observed a landing gear door caution indication for all doors. A short time later, the LH main landing gear door indicated closed however the other landing gear doors remained open. The crew conducted a successful alternate landing gear extension. The aircraft held for 40 minutes to burn fuel to meet the landing weight requirements.  The aircraft returned to CYVR and landed without further incident. ARFF was on standby for the arrival. There were no injuries. The operator's maintenance adjusted the rigging for the gear doors and changed a faulty proximity sensor. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBBP, the Brampton Flying Club Cessna 172S was returning to the Brampton - Caledon Airport, Ontario (CNC3) after a cross-country flight to Goderich, Ontario (CYGD) with the pilot and one passenger on board. During touch down on runway 08, the aircraft began to porpoise resulting in a propeller strike and substantial damage to the firewall. The aircraft went around and landed uneventfully.

C-GBDQ, un Cessna R172K amphibie en exploitation privé effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis la rivière Manouane (50°20'24.2"N 70°35'56.4"W) à destination d’Alma, QC (CYTF), avec 1 pilote et 1 passager à bord. Lors d’un virage à basse altitude après le décollage, le pilote a perdu la maîtrise de l’appareil, l’aile gauche et le flotteur gauche ont percuté la surface de l’eau, avant de s'immobiliser et a coulé quelques instants plus tard. Le C-GBDQ a subi des dommages importants. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) ne s’est pas déclenchée.

Sky Regional Airlines flight SKV7502 operated as Air Canada 7502, an Embraer ERJ 170 aircraft, departed from Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ), ON to Baltimore/Washington Intl. Thurgood Marshall (KBWI), MA. After departure the flight attendants noticed a strong smell of smoke in the cabin, however, there was no visual smoke in flight deck.The remains of food packaging debris was found in an oven. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to smell of smoke in the cabin and elected to return to Toronto where the aircraft landed safely and taxied to the gate. Firefighters came on board at the gate, there were no injuries.

C-GWEQ, a De Havilland DHC-8-400D aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3537 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, (CYYZ), ON to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QB. The flight crew declared an emergency due to a hydraulic failure and elected to return to CYYZ. The aircraft landed safely on runway 06L and and came to a full stop on the runway. The emergency services confirmed a leak from the #2 engine and the flight crew requested a tow to the gate.

CS-TUD, the Transportes Aereos Portugueses Airbus A330-941 aircraft operating as flight TAP259A, departed Lisbon (LPPT) to Lester B. Pearson Intl. Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ). The aircraft declared an emergency on approach to CYYZ due to flap issues. The flight landed uneventfully.

F-HLVM, un Airbus A330-202 exploité par OpenSkies en tant que vol BOS7 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Paris/Orly (LFPO), France à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QB. Lors de l'approche l'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence dû à des problèmes de volets. L'appareil a poursuivi l'approche et s'est posé sans encombre à CYUL.

The pilot of C-GBPI, Cessna P210N aircraft, was delivering the aircraft from Montréal/St. Hubert (CYHU), QB to Saskatchewan. The pilot had originally planned to land in Wawa (CYXZ) for fuel, but elected to continue to Marathon (CYSP). After landing in CYSP, it was discovered that the fuel pumps were unserviceable and a NOTAM had been issued. The pilot took off and attempted to return to CYXZ for fuel, while en route back to CYXZ the aircraft ran out of fuel. The pilot conducted a forced approach to Paint Lake Road, but the road was not wide enough and the aircraft's wings contacted the trees causing the aircraft to spin into the forest. The pilot and 2 passengers received minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FJWE, a De Havilland Dash 8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore was conducting flight 3428 from Halifax Stanfield (CYHZ) Nova Scotia to St John's (CYYT) Newfoundland and Labrador with 68 passengers and 4 crew. After departure the nose gear down indication continued after the gear selector was selected to up. The quick reference handbook was referenced and the alternate landing gear extension procedure was conducted. The crew declared a PAN PAN and returned to Halifax. The aircraft landed safely and after inspection by airport vehicles proceeded to the gate. Maintenance determined the landing gear control panel was faulty and replaced it. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTSY, un Airbus A310-304 exploité par Air Transat en tant que vol TSC253 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Malaga/Costa del Sol (LEMG), Espagne à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QB avec à son bord 9 membres d'équipage et 237 passagers. Lors de l'approche de la piste 24L à CYUL, l'équipage de conduite a observé un message du moniteur électronique centralisé de bord (ECAM) indiquant que les volets étaient bloqués lorsque ces derniers ont été sélectionnés à la position 15/15. La liste de vérification applicable a été effectuée et l'équipage de conduite a déclaré PAN PAN. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Les pompiers ont dû utiliser des ventilateurs pour refroidir les freins de l'appareil. Le personnel de maintenance a remplacé un détecteur d'asymétrie défectueux avant de remettre l'aéronef en service.

C-FFNC, un Boeing 737-400 exploité par First Air en tant que vol FAB868 avec à son bord 4 membres d'équipage et 5 passagers, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QB à destination de Kuujjuaq (CYVP), QB. Lors de l'approche à CYVP, l'équipage de conduite a constaté que les volets étaient bloqués entre 15 et 25 degrés suite à leurs sélections à 30 degrés. L'approche a été interrompue, la liste de vérification applicable a été effectuée et une urgence a été déclarée. L'appareil est revenu se poser sans problème. Le personnel de maintenance a remplacé l'indicateur de position des volets qui était défectueux et l'appareil a été remis en service.

C-GVTB, a privately operated Grummond GA-7, was conducting a flight from Olds-Didsbury (CEA3), AB with one pilot on board. After take-off on Runway 28, and approximately 1.0 NM northwest of CEA3, there was a complete loss of engine power on the left engine (AVCO LYCOMING, O-320-D1D). The pilot elected to force land the aircraft straight ahead. On ground contact C-GVTB contacted a copse of trees and substantial damage was incurred to the nose gear, left engine and propeller (HARTZELL, HC-F2YL-2UF), tail section and both wing surfaces. The pilot sustained minor injuries and an ELT signal was received by the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) Trenton. The owner will report to TSB findings for the loss of power.

C-FNFC, a private float-equipped Aeronca 11ACX aircraft, was conducting a flight from Horton Lake, Biencourt QC, to the Madawaska River, near Edmunston, (CYES) NB. During cruise, the aircraft experienced an engine failure due to carburetor icing. The aircraft landed in a field about 12 nm ESE of Edmunston, NB. The pilot, the sole occupant on board, was not injured. The aircraft sustained substantial damage, mostly to the floats and struts.

C-GBIN, an Airbus 319 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1522 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to St-John Intl (CYYT), NL. Just after reaching flight level 350, the flight crew received a CABIN PRESS ECAM (Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitor) message followed by a CABIN ALT ECAM. The flight crew conducted the checklist, donned their oxygen masks and descended to 9000 feet. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and returned to CYUL. The flight landed without further incident.

C-FVFN, a King Air Beech 200 aircraft operated by Vanguard Air Care Ltd, was conducting flight VN06 from Berens River (CYBV), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. On short final for Runway 36 at CYWG, the flight crew did not receive illumination of the left main gear light. The crew conducted a missed approach to troubleshoot the issue, during which time the left main gear light illuminated. During the second approach to CYWG the left main gear light extinguished. The crew executed a second missed approach, conducted a manual gear extension and recieved illumination of three landing gear lights. The crew requested ARFF on standby for precautionary measures and the aircraft landed safely without further incident. The operators maintenance found high resistance on the down lock switch. The unlock and down-lock switches were replaced on the left side main gear. The system was checked and returned to service.

C-FUWA, a privately operated Piper PA-22-135, was conducting a night proficiency flight from Innisfail Airport (CEM4), AB with one pilot on board. After take-off on Runway 16, and approximately 3 NM south of CEM4, there was a partial loss of engine power (AVCO LYCOMING, O-290-D2) and reduced climb performance. The pilot elected to force land the aircraft straight ahead into an agriculture field. On ground contact C-FUWA nosed over and substantial damage was incurred to the nose gear, windshield, and wing surfaces. The pilot was not injured and no ELT signal was received.

C-FGKZ, an Airbus A321-200 operating as Air Canada flight ACA117 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC was en route when a flight attendant became ill and could not continue their duties. The flight attendant's duties were distributed among other cabin crew members and priority was requested for landing at CYVR. The landing was uneventful and EMS met the aircraft at the gate.

C-GDEN, an Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN 3282 from Prince George (CYXS), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 4 crew members and 76 passengers on board. Shortly after departure from CYXS, the flight crew observed the Flap Power annunciator light illuminate due to the flaps not retracting after takeoff. The appropriate checklist was completed however the light remained on. The flight crew declared an emergency and returned to CYXS where they performed a flapless landing. The aircraft taxied to the gate upon landing and the passengers were deplaned. There were no injuries. The operator's maintenance completed the required inspections on the flap system and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GCIJ, a Boeing 767-300 operated by CargoJet Airways, was conducting a flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International (CYWG), MB to Iqaluit (CYFB), NU. During the takeoff roll at CYWG, the flight crew observed a red FLAP EICAS message and aural warning subsequently rejecting takeoff above V1. The aircraft stopped within the confines of the runway and the crew subsequently followed the recommended brake-cooling schedule. ARFF was requested for precautionary measures and emergency vehicles escorted the aircraft safely to the ramp. The operator's maintenance identified the flaps could not retract and was stuck at 1 with FLAP/SLAT ELEC status message. Water was found on FSPM cards, the FSPM cards were dried and FSPM M838 was replaced. The flaps were cycled and tested normal with no further faults.

C-GKQH, a De Havilland Dash 8 Q400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines Inc., was conducting flight POE487 from Montreal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport, QC (CYUL) to Halifax Stanfield International Airport, NS (CYHZ). During the cruise portion of the flight, the number 2 DC Generator light came on and the crew notified maintenance. Approximately 5 minutes later the #2 oil pressure began fluctuating and the oil pressure warning annunciator illuminated. The crew shut down the number 2 engine, declared an MAYDAY and landed without incident. Maintenance determined that the number 2 DC generator had become unseated, which caused a slow oil leak.

C-GZIK, a Eurocopter AS 350 B3 helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters LTD, was conducting slung load operations at Boston Camp, NU. While slinging an empty fuel container, the pilot inadvertently contacted the electrical release button; releasing the empty fuel container. There was no reported environmental damage due to the inadvertent release.

C-GFBE, un Cessna P206 exploité par Parachutisme Adrénaline, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de St-Jérôme (CSN3), QB, avec seulement le pilote a bord. À une altitude de 4200 pieds, un bruit inhabituel et des vibrations ont précédé une perte de puissance. Des tentatives pour redémarrer le moteur ont été infructueuses, le démarreur ne faisant pas tourner le moteur. Le pilote a déclaré une urgence et considéré un atterrissage sur l'autoroute 15, mais considérant la circulation dense et lente, il a finalement opté pour atterrissage sur un terrain de golf de Saint-Jérôme. L'atterrissage a été dur et s'est soldé par un affaissement du train avant ainsi que des dommages à l'hélice et au pare-brise. Le pilote n'a pas été blessé. L'appareil a été démonté et transporté dans un organisme de maintenance agréé pour évaluation.

C-FVNF, a Beech 200 operated by Vanguard Air Care Ltd, was conducting flight VN06 from Berens River (CYBV), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. During the climb in winter weather conditions, the flight crew observed incorrect airspeed indications. The crew declared an emergency, and landed in CYWG without further incident. ARFF was responded and escorted the aircraft to the ramp. A post-flight tactile inspection indicated that the pitot tube was not hot.The operator’s maintenance subsequently checked the pitot heat and no faults were found in the system. The aircraft was returned to service.

N35953, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL968 from San Francisco Intl (KSFO), CA to Amsterdam/Schiphol (EHAM), Netherlands. During cruise flight near Wabush (CYWK), NL at FL390, the crew was alerted to decreasing cabin altitude and noted that the right DC electrical bus had failed along with the right air conditioning pack. The left pack subsequently failed, and the crew declared an emergency, descended, and coordinated with ATS to divert to Bangor Intl (KBGR), ME.

C-GNPO, a float-equipped DHC-2 operated by Black Sheep Aviation & Cattle Company, was en route from Tuya Lake, BC to Watson Lake, YT when the propeller rpm increased beyond redline and engine vibration became severe. The pilot reduced the throttle but significant vibration continued so the pilot elected to conduct a precautionary, power-off landing on Bus Lake, BC. The aircraft landed successfully and remained upright but one float was damaged when it struck a tree on approach. The pilot and passenger were not injured, the aircraft sustained minor damage.Metal contamination was found in the engine oil sump and screen and the exhaust valve in the #9 cylinder was broken. The engine (P&W R985-AN14B, serial number 19366) will be removed and sent to an overhaul facility for inspection and repair.

C-GCRU, a Bell 429 helicopter operated by the Canadian Coast Guard, was conducting external load operations to the Machias-Seal Island Lighthouse from Southwest Head Lighthouse, Grand Manan, NB. The helicopter was slinging a crate of construction materials, and while in transit the load began to shift in the straps. The pilot made a radio call to ground crew, determined that the external load was secure, and decided to continue the flight. As the helicopter was about 500 meters from shore, the pilot saw the crate had partially opened and some material depart from it. The helicopter was slowed and a turn was made to return to the departure point. It was found that unsecured material inside the crate had shifted in-flight. The material was secured, and the crate was lifted using a cargo net to continue the external load operations.Transport Canada Aircraft Services Directorate is conducting an investigation.

C-FTJO, the Air Canada Airbus A320 aircraft (AC757) was on route to San Francisco International Airport (KSFO) from Toronto / LBPIA (CYYZ) when the flight crew received an ECAM message for Green Hydraulic Low Level. The flight crew decided to return to CYYZ and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by and taxied to the gate. Maintenance found the Green Hydraulic Pressure line union fitting leaking at the Green System HP Manifold. The packing was replaced and subsequent testing found no further leaks.

C-FRRQ, a Beechcraft 200 aircraft operated by North Cariboo Flying Service, was conducting flight NCB2105 from Grand Prairie (CYQU), AB to Calgary International (CYYC), AB. While climbing out of CYQU, the chip detector light illuminated for approximately 2 minutes. The flight crew consulted the QRH and continued the climb with all engine parameters indicating green. During cruise, the oil pressure on the left engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-42) increased and a surge was observed by flight crew. Engine oil pressure began to fluctuate along with continuous and abrupt engine surges. The right engine was shut down and an emergency was declared. The flight was diverted to Edmonton International (CYEG), AB and subsequently landed without further incident. Following the flight, maintenance found power turbine blade damage.

C-GTSY, un appareil de type Airbus 310-304 exploité par Air Transat sous l'indicatif de vol TSC253, avec à son bord 9 membres d'équipage et 237 passagers, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Malaga/Costa Del Sol (LEMG), Espagne à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. Lors de la sélection des volets à la position 15/15 en approche de la piste 24L de CYUL, l'équipage de conduite a reçu le message ''Flaps Stuck'' sur le moniteur électronique centralisé de bord (ECAM). La liste de vérification applicable a été effectuée et un PAN PAN a été signalé au service de la circulation aérienne. L'appareil a poursuivi l'approche et s'est posé sans problème. Après avoir libéré la piste, la température des freins a augmenté rapidement. À l'aide de ventilateurs les freins ont été refroidis et l'appareil a par la suite circulé jusqu'à la passerelle de débarquement

C-IMAG, an amphibious Titan Tornado II Advanced Ultra-light, was on a local flight when it performed a water landing near Port Franks, Ontario. Upon touchdown the aircraft immediately flipped over. The two occupants exited the aircraft without injury and were picked up by nearby boaters. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. An examination of the aircraft by the owner indicated there was extensive damage to the underside of the left float such that approximately half of the bottom surface had become detached.

C-FHRC, a de Havilland DHC-8-102 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting flight PAG209 from Oxford House (CYOH), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. C-GSNW, a Beech E90 (King Air) operated by Sky North, was conducting flight SN696 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Island Lake (CYIV), MB at 17 000 feet in uncontrolled airspace (controlled airspace in the area is 18 000 feet and above). During the climb in uncontrolled airspace, approximately 40 miles northwest of CYIV, PAG209 obtained an IFR clearance to CYWG and to maintain 16 000 feet in controlled airspace from Winnipeg ACC. The controller also provided traffic information regarding a King Air enroute from CYTH to CYIV at 17 000 feet; but the call sign was not provided. SN696 reported the initiation of a descent from 17 000 feet on radio frequency 126.70 and the Mandatory Frequency for CYIV. C-GSNF, a Beech B200 (King Air) operated by SkyNorth Air, was also conducting a flight from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Island Lake (CYIV), MB, as flight SN898. SN898 was at 19,000 feet in controlled airspace and approximately 5 nm in front of company SN696. Winnipeg ACC cleared SN898 to descend out of control airspace and traffic information was provided to SN898 regarding PAG209's position. Winnipeg ACC then asked PAG209 if they were in contact with SN696. PAG209 responded they were not, but that they had TCAS traffic indication indicating that SN696 would pass to the right of PAG209 shortly. Subsequently, PAG209 communicated with Winnipeg ACC that visual passage of SN696 had occurred. SN898 reported passing through 18 000 feet. Moments later PAG209 reported to Winnipeg ACC that traffic had past them and they had responded to a traffic alert / resolution advisory. Radar data showed PAG209 descending through 12 100 feet and SN696 descending through 12 700 feet. The range between the two aircraft decreased to 0.1 miles laterally and 600 feet vertically. Traffic separation was increased when PAG209 responded to the TCAS resolution advisory and executed the descent. All aircrafts landed uneventfully

C-GWEO, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3504 from London (CYXU), ON to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During the approach at CYYZ, the crew selected flaps down and received a Flap Power Caution Light. A go-around was conducted and the QRH procedures were performed which eliminated the Caution Light. During the second approach the crew selected FLAP 10 and the Caution Light returned. The crew declared a PAN PAN and proceeded to perform an uneventful landing. ARFF were standing by for the landing and checked the brakes for overheating due to the higher than normal landing speed. Once cleared the aircraft taxied to the gate. Maintenance found a faulty pressure switch within the Flap Power Unit and replaced it.

C-GPAR, un DHC8-300 exploité par PAL Airlines en tant que vol PVL1909 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Sept-Îles (CYZV) QUE à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB) QCC. Alors que l'appareil était environ 35 milles au nord-nord-est de Mont-Joli QC, l'équipage de conduite a reçu une alarme de dysfonctionnement de système Beta (contrôle de puissance moteur). Le disjoncteur du circuit a été ouvert pour arrêter l'alarme sonore. Par la suite, l'équipage a observé une fluctuation de l'indication de pression d'huile, mais sans alerte de pression d'huile. Une urgence a été déclarée par précaution et l'appareil a poursuivi sa route vers CYQB où l'appareil s'est posé sans problème. Le personnel de maintenance a remplacé les micro-interrupteurs sur les contrôles de puissance des moteurs 1 et 2 et réparé un faisceau de fils électrique.

C-FXJF, an Embraer ERJ170-200SU aircraft operated by Sky Regional, was conducting flight SKV7558 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. During cruise, about 30 minutes before landing, the crew received a “PRKG BRK NOT RELEASED” EICAS message. The crew consulted the QRH, the message would not clear. The crew prepared for an emergency landing due to the possibility of blown tires on landing. The flight crew declared a MAYDAY, instructed the passengers to brace for landing, and landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. ARFF inspected the aircraft on the runway and no abnormalities were noted. The crew taxied to the gate. Maintenance determined that it was a failure of the park brake switch and replaced the switch. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBHJ, a Sikorsky S-76C+ helicopter operated by Helijet International, was conducting flight JBA723 from Vancouver Harbour (CBC7), BC to Victoria Harbour (Camel Point) (CBF7), BC with 2 crew members and 12 passengers on board. During cruise flight the crew received a #1 HYD warning. While carrying out the QRH procedure the hydraulic pressure decreased to a zero. The crew declared a Pan Pan and diverted to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC. The crew carried out a running landing without further incident. Subsequent maintenance actions revealed a leak around an insert fitting of the hydraulic pump body. The operator has submitted a service difficulty report and the helicopter has been returned to service.

C-GUBL, an Airbus A330-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC704 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to London / Gatwick (EGKK), UK with 11 crew members and 257 passengers onboard. On approach to EGKK, upon the ILS interception, at about 3000 feet and approximately 14 nm from the threshold of runway 26L, C-GUBL received a TCAS/RA to “Climb Climb”. The crew performed evasive manoeuvre as advised, contacted the ATC for a heading to re-intercept the ILS, and proceeded to EGKK for an uneventful landing.

C-FRSA, a Boeing B787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA850 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to London / Heathrow (EGLL), UK with 10 crew members and 282 passengers onboard. When descending through 10,600 feet on approach to EGLL, C-FRSA received a TCAS alert and advisory. The crew followed the resolution advisory and the flight continued to EGLL for an uneventful landing.

C-GPPS, un appareil de type BA 32-12 exploité par Pascan Aviation avec à son bord 2 pilotes et 12 passagers effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU), QB à destination de Val-d'Or (CYVO), QB. Lors de l'atterrissage à CYVO l'appareil a fait une sortie sur le côté de la piste suite à une crevaison du pneu droit. L'appareil a subi des dommages mineurs. Personne n’a été blessé.

C-FEJB, un appareil de type Embraer 170 exploité par Sky Regional Airlines sous l'indicatif de vol SKV7590, avec à son bord 4 membres d'équipage et 71 passagers effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Chicago/O'Hare Intl (KORD) IL à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL) QC. Alors que l'appareil se trouvait au niveau de vol FL35O à environ 42 milles à l'ouest de CYUL, l'équipage de conduite a reçu le message d'une baisse du fluide hydraulique du système numéro 1 sur le système d'affichage des paramètres réacteurs, de mise en garde et d'alarme (EICAS). L'équipage de conduite a effectué les vérifications applicables et a déclaré PAN PAN. L’appareil a poursuivi sa route vers CYUL où il s'est posé sans problème. Une fois au sol, l'appareil a été immobilisé sur la piste et le personnel d'urgence a pu observer une fuite de liquide hydraulique sous la nacelle du moteur gauche. Le moteur a été coupé et l'appareil a circulé jusqu'à la passerelle de débarquement escorté par les véhicules d'urgence. La pompe entraînée par réacteur (EDP) du moteur gauche a été remplacée et l'appareil remis en service.

C-FHOY, an Embraer E-190 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA442 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON with 4  crew members and 60 passengers on board. Shortly after take-off from CYYZ, ACA442 declared a PAN PAN due to an odour in the cockpit. The aircraft returned to CYYZ and stopped on the runway to be inspected by ARFF, there was no sign of fire. The aircraft returned to the gate without further incident.Maintenance checked the aircraft and found the APU oil level on the high side. The APU oil level was adjusted to correct level. The APU intake cover and aft fuselage belly were found contaminated with oil, the areas were cleaned and the recirculating air filters replaced.

C-FSGM, a Diamond Twinstar DA-42 aircraft operated by Chinook Helicopters, was conducting a training flight from Abbottsford (CYXX), BC to Victoria (CYYJ), BC with 1 pilot and 1 student pilot on board. During cruise flight the pilot received a left engine fire annunciation. There were no secondary indications of a fire, and the fire indication warning extinguished without pilot intervention. The pilot declared an emergency and returned to CYXX without further incident. Subsequent maintenance actions verified the fire warning to be a false indication caused by water contamination on a sensor. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GVSO, a Piper PA-31 Aircraft operated by Okanagan Air Ventures Ltd. was conducting local skydiving operations out of the Innisfail (CEM4), AB airport with the pilot and 9 skydivers on board. Approximately 14 minutes into the flight, while the pilot was reducing the manifold pressure from 38" Hg to 35" Hg, the left engine manifold pressure dropped to 17" Hg. A precautionary Left hand engine (AVCO LYCOMING, TIO-540-J2B) shut down was completed and an emergency was declared with ATS. As the aircraft was at an altitude where the skydivers could safely exit the aircraft, 7 of the 9 skydivers exited the aircraft uneventfully. 2 parachutists elected to remain on board for the landing. The pilot diverted and landed uneventfullyat at Red Deer, AB (CYQF).Subsequent investigation by maintenance found an inadequately secured clamp on intake duct plumbing. Repairs were made and the aircraft was subsequently returned to service.

C-FDTC un Beech 300 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif de vol AIE591 avec à son bord 2 pilotes et 2 passagers circulait sur la voie de circulation B2 de l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC pour effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments à destination de Kuujjuaq (CYVP), QC. Alors que l'aéronef s'apprêtait à prendre position sur la piste 06L, le premier officier a observé la présence de fumée blanche s'échapper au-dessus du capot du moteur droit. Le commandant a immobilisé l'aéronef et a également observé la présence de fumée. Le moteur a été fermé par précaution et une urgence a été déclarée. Une fois le moteur arrêté la fumée s'est dissipée et aucune fumée n'a été observé par le personnel du service d'urgence. L'aéronef a été ramené chez l'exploitant afin d'être examiné. Personne n'a été blessé.

Le DHC-8 exploité par PAL Provincial Airlines effectuait le vol PAL1901 au départ de Wabush (CYWK), TN à destination Sept-Îles (CYZV), QC. Lors de la descente pour l'approche à CYZV, l'équipage de conduite a dû faire une manœuvre d'évitement suite à une cible non identifiée sur leur système de surveillance du trafic et d'évitement des collisions (TCAS). Les deux aéronefs sont passés à environ 200 pieds l'un de l'autre. Le PAL1901 a poursuivi sa route et a atterri à CYZV sans problème. L'autre aéronef serait un hélicoptère faisant du transport à l'élingue à environ 10 miles nautiques au nord de CYZV. Ce dernier n'était pas en communication radio avec Sept-Îles radio.

C-GLQH, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE217 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier (CYOW), ON to Fredericton (CYFC), NB. C-GTMB, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Services (EVAS), was conducting flight EV778 from Fredericton (CYFC), NB to Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ). When POE217 was about 10 nm northeast of CYFC and descending through 4500 feet for 4000 feet, ATS passed along the position information of an unknown VFR aircraft, which was at 4500 feet. At about the same time POE217 received and responded to a TCAS resolution advisory (RA), and descended to avoid the VFR traffic. EV778 had departed CYFC runway 09 and was climbing to 3000 feet. A loss of separation between EV778 and POE217 occurred when POE217 responded to the RA and descended to avoid the VFR traffic. POE217 came within 1.9 nm laterally and 700 feet vertically of EV778. The required separation between POE217 and EV778 was 5 nm laterally or 1000 feet vertically.

C-GTSI, an Airbus A330-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC249 from Barcelona/El Prat del Llobragat (LEBL), Spain to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. C-GPAJ, a Canadair CL600-2A12 aircraft operated by Chartright was conducting flight HRT056 from Philadelphia Intl. (KPHL), PA to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. A loss of wake turbulence separation occurred on approach to CYYZ while the terminal controller was sequencing HRT056 behind TSC249. The loss of separation occurred as terminal controller instructed HRT056 to contact the tower controller. HRT056 was less than the required 5 nm behind TSC249, coming up to 4.4 nm before the tower instructed HRT056 to go around.

C-ILWA, an Aeroprakt-22LS advanced ultra-light aircraft operated by Hart's Aviation flight training unit, was conducting a first solo flight at Langley (CYNJ), BC with only the student pilot on board. Following numerous missed approaches the student pilot landed hard and the nose gear collapsed. Damage was sustained to the nose gear and propeller from contact with the runway. The student pilot sustained no injuries.

C-FOVF, a privately registered amateur built Zenair CH30, was conducting a local flight at Chilliwack (CYCW), BC. During landing the aircraft first contacted the runway with the nose wheel approximately 300' prior to the runway threshold. The aircraft became airborne again, in a nose high attitude, followed by a hard landing on the runway surface. The nose gear separated from the aircraft. The aircraft came to a stop on the runway. The pilot sustained no injuries. There was no ELT activation. Aircraft sustained damage to the nose gear and propeller from runway contact.

C-GAKI, an Alkan Air Dornier 228-200 was operating from Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen Intl. (CYXY), YT to Don Camp, YT.  During landing gear extension on approach to Don Camp, YT, the nose landing gear extended and locked, but both main landing gear remained up.  A checklist was consulted and the aircraft diverted back to CYXY with the gear in the transit position. On approach to CYXY the crew used the emergency gear extension system to extend the landing gear.  The aircraft landed without further incident and the aircraft was towed back to the company's ramp. Following the flight, maintenance found that a fuse had failed. The fuse was replaced, the hydraulic system was reset and function tested in accordance with the Dornier Maintenance Manual.  The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FWSE, a Boeing 737-800 operated by WestJet as WJA1229, was arriving at Toronto/Pearson Intl (CYYZ), Ontario, following a flight from Orlando (KMCO), Florida, with 6 crew and 165 passengers on board. During the landing roll, the aircraft drifted significantly to the left of centerline, and following arrival at the gate, there was damage observed to the #1 (LH outboard main) tire and the lower anti-skid wiring conduit on the LH main gear. A runway inspection conducted the following day revealed that a runway edge light on the left side and about halfway down the runway length was missing. The broken light was found in the grass about 30 feet from its installed location. Convective weather and reduced visibility due to heavy rainfall were observed overhead CYYZ at the time of the landing. The #1 tire and anti-skid conduit were replaced.

N636QX, a Horizon Air Embraer ERJ 170-200LR, was operating as flight QXE2546 from Seattle-Tacoma International (KSEA), WA to Edmonton International (CYEG), AB. On approach, the flight crew reported a trim indicator failure and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without incident. Following the flight, maintenance checked the aircraft and noted that here were no error messages found in the aircraft's computer system and the problem could not be replicated.

C-FBOM, a Beech B200 operated by Sunwest Aviation Ltd., was operating as flight CNK297 from Creston (CAJ3), BC to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB with 2 crew and 6 passengers onboard. While enroute during cruise, the flight crew noticed the left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-41) torque indicator and oil pressure gauge fluctuating. No smoke, fire or oil was observed coming from the left engine. The flight crew actioned the low oil pressure emergency checklist and reduced power on the left engine to 1100 lbs torque; oil pressure continued to decrease. The left engine was shutdown and the flight crew declared an emergency with air traffic services. CNK297 continued to CYYC and performed an uneventful single-engine approach and landing. There were no injuries.

C-FVPC, a Pilatus PC-12 aircraft operated by North Star Air Ltd, was conducting a passenger flight from Sioux lookout (CYXL), ON to Sachigo Lake (CZPB) ON. While enroute approximately 100 nm south of CZPB, the aircraft temperature auto selection failed to produce warm air, the flight crew selected the manual temperature switch to hot. Shortly after the manual temperature selection, the flight crew experienced physiological symptoms of rapid pressure change and noted a cabin pressure indicator spike to approximately 4000 feet per minute climb with illumination of CABIN PRESSURE CAWS. The flight crew actioned the appropriate drill, commenced an emergency descent, notified ATC and returned the aircraft to CYXL.The operator’s maintenance identified the temperature control valve was unserviceable and the temperature valve was replaced. Applicable ground runs were completed and aircraft was returned to service.

C-GFOX, a Piaggio Avianti P180 aircraft operated by Westair Aviation Inc., was conducting a commercial flight from Vancouver/Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC to Kelowna (CYLW), BC with 1 pilot and 7 passengers on board. Approaching CYLW one of the landing gear indicator lights would not illuminate to indicate the gear was in the extended position. The pilot conducted a low pass where the tower visually observed the gear extended. The pilot then completed the QRH actions. The tower initiated an emergency response. The aircraft landed without further incident. Subsequent maintenance action revealed one landing gear indicator light bulb was burned out.

C-GHPD, a Airbus A321-211 aircraft operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ZX1797, from Québec/Jean Lesage Intl. (CYQB), QC to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. During cruise a flight attendant became incapacitated and was unable to continue duties. The remaining cabin crew assumed these duties and the aircraft continued uneventfully.

C-GETA, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-300 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol régulier JZA8745 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Bathurs (CZBF), NB à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL),QC avec 48 passagers et 3 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors qu'il se trouvait en descente à environ 60 milles marins à l’est-nord-est de CYUL, l'appareil a rencontré de la turbulence sévère et l’agent de bord a reçu des blessures mineurs. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence. L'inspection post envolée a révélé des dommages mineurs au plafond de la cabine.

C-GWCN, a Boeing 737-700 operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA475 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. G-CKOG, a Boeing 787-9 operated by Norwegian Air Shuttle, was conducting flight NRS7181 from London/Gatwick (EGKK), UK to Austin-Bergstrom Intl (KAUS), TX. A loss of radar separation occurred 50 nm NE of Sault Ste. Marie (CYAM) between C-GWCN and G-CKOG. The separation was reduced to 800 feet vertically where 1000 feet is required and the lateral spacing was reduced to 4.1 nm where 5 nm is required.

N189DN, a Boeing 767-332 aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL474 from New York/Kennedy Intl (KJFK), NY to Venice/Marco Polo Intl (LIPZ), Italy. While in cruise flight at about 230 nm SE of St. John's Intl. (CYYT), NL (45°27' N, 048°10' W), the cabin crew detected an electrical odour in the cabin, although no visible smoke was noted. The flight crew was notified, and the captain transferred aircraft control and commenced the smoke and fumes quick reference handbook procedure. The flight crew then received an EICAS message regarding the left recirculating fan, and secured the fan. The flight crew conferred with their company maintenance control, decided to divert to CYYT, and coordinated with air traffic services for the diversion. The crew declared an emergency and landed at CYYT without further incident. Emergency services at CYYT determined no fire was present.  Maintenance personnel subsequently inspected the aircraft and verified that the left recirculation fan was the source of the odour.

C-FFQT, a Diamond DA20-C1 aircraft operated by Moncton Flight College (MFC), had departed for a local solo training flight from Moncton/Roméo Leblanc Intl (CYQM), NB. When in the MFC training area about 35 nm east of CYQM, the pilot commenced an exercise to practice a departure aerodynamic stall. At about 4000 feet above sea level while operating at a low engine power setting and high angle of attack, the engine quit running. The pilot lowered the nose of the aircraft and attempted to restart the aircraft by engaging the starter. When a restart was not possible the pilot selected a landing area to conduct a forced landing. The pilot landed the aircraft successfully in a northeast direction of a straight section of the Trans-Canada highway, near the west approach of the Confederation Bridge in New Brunswick. As the aircraft was taxied to the side of the highway, the right wing struck a signpost. There was no reported injury to the pilot. The outer portion of the right wing of the aircraft sustained structural damage and was sent to a manufacturer approved repair facility for evaluation and repair.Subsequent inspection by company maintenance required that a faulty engine fuel distribution manifold was replaced. The maintenance inspection also discovered an intermittent electrical connection at the electric fuel pump that was subsequently repaired.

C-FERF, un Piper PA-23-250 exploité par Cargair Ltée. effectuait un vol local de formation depuis Trois-Rivières, Québec (CYRQ) selon les règles de vol aux instruments avec un instructeur et un élève à bord. Alors qu’il se trouvait dans le circuit, une urgence a été déclarée en raison d’un problème avec le train d’atterrissage. Le pilote a effectué une approche basse-remontée pour faire vérifier la position du train d'atterrissage. Il a ensuite fermé les moteurs et l'appareil s'est posé sans autres difficultés avec les services d’urgence en attente. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’avion.

C-FVVS, a Piper PA-31-350 aircraft operated by Island Express Air, was conducting flight IAX104 from Qualicum Beach (CAT4), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 2 flight crew members and 5 passengers on board. Upon selection of the landing gear down during approach to CYVR, the crew received an unsafe gear indication associated with the right main landing gear. The crew conducted the emergency gear extension checklist and performed a low pass for the tower controller to observe the position of the landing gear. The crew declared a Pan Pan. The aircraft landed without further incident. Subsequent maintenance action revealed a faulty main gear down lock switch. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FZAA, a Sikorsky S-76A helicopter operated by Helijet International, was conducting flight JBA711 from Vancouver Harbour Heliport (CBC7), BC to Victoria Harbour Heliport (Camel Point)(CBF7), BC with 2 pilots and 10 passengers on board. Shortly after departure the Main XSMN Chip light illuminated. The crew declared an Pan Pan and diverted to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC. The crew performed a running landing without further incident. The operators maintenance replaced the main gearbox (serial number A081-00351). The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GOJN, a Sikorsky S-61N aircraft operated by VIH Helicopters, was conducting heli-logging operations approximately 25 nm north of Bella Bella (Campbell Island)(CBBC), BC with 2 pilots on board. Following a log pick-up, the longline detached from the helicopter and landed in the water near the shoreline. The pilots were unaware of the released load and were notified by the chasers. The aircraft returned to the service barge uneventfully. The operators maintenance determined the aluminum fitting at the hook, associated with the emergency release, had broken which triggered the hook to release and the line to be dropped.

C-FLPU, a privately registered Cessna 172N was conducting a VFR flight from Winnipeg/Lyncrest (CJL5), MB to Steinbach/North (CJB3), MB. CJB3 is an uncontrolled aerodrome and pilots provide traffic advisory on a common frequency, 122.7. Upon arrival at CJB3, the aircraft conducted touch and go landings on Runway 32. On the second touch and go, the pilot noticed an aircraft holding short on a taxiway that intersect approximately at the midpoint of the Runway 32. The pilot of C-FLPU thought this aircraft  was going to enter the active runway and applied maximum braking in an attempt to stop the landing roll. The directional control was lost and the aircraft departed the paved runway to the left into wet grass and continued through a drainage ditch. The aircraft came to an abrupt stop and flipped over. The ELT did activate. RCMP, fire and EMS attended the scene. There were no injuries and the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GCJT, a Boeing 757-200 operated by Cargojet Airways, was conducting flight CJT919 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Covington/Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky Intl (KCVG), KY. Upon reaching cruising altitude, the cabin altitude climbed at 100' per minute and the “cabin altitude” warning sounded. The flight crew declared an emergency, initiated a controlled descent, and donned oxygen masks. The aircraft returned to CYYC and landed without further incident. There were no injuries.At the time of the occurrence, the Equipment Cooling Overboard Exhaust valve was deferred by company maintenance and locked in the SMOKE (partially OPEN) position as per the MEL requirements. Upon return to CYYC, company maintenance found the value in the fully open position. The equipment overboard cooling exhaust valve failed to the full open position while in the locked out position, which created the loss of cabin pressure. The valve was replaced and tested. The aircraft was returned to service.

C- GTAG, a De Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP was conducting flight AC8599, from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to London Intl (CYXU), ON with 3 crew members and 48 passengers on board. The aircraft was being pushed back from the gate when smoke was noted in the cabin and flight deck. The smoke started after the left engine was started, with bleeds on. The aircraft returned to the gate and a rapid deplanement was conducted. ARFF attended the aircraft and there was no indication of fire. There were no injuries.The operator's maintenance ran the engines and no smoke was noted.

N682D, a private Raytheon BAE H125 aircraft, was on an IFR flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to White Plains/Westchester County (KHPN), NY. PH-AKA, an Airbus A330-300 aircraft operated by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, was conducted flight KLM86 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ) to Amsterdam/Schiphol (EHAM) NL. Just after departure from CYYZ, N682D made an uncleared left turn towards PH-AKA, which had just departed off Runway 24R. The controller caught the deviation and recleared both aircraft to regain separation. The Aircraft came within 1 NM and 300 feet of each other.

C-GTLM, un appareil de type Beechcraft C-23 en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aérodrome de Saint-Hyacinthe (CSU3), QC à destination de l’aérodrome de Saint-Anselme (CTQ6), QC. Lors de l’atterrissage sur la piste en gazon, la rosée avait rendu la piste glissante et l’appareil n’a pas été en mesure de s’arrêter avant la fin de la piste. L'avion est sorti de piste et est entré en collision avec des arbres. Les deux occupants n’ont pas été blessés. L’appareil a subi des dommages à une aile.

N397AN, a Boeing 767-323ER aircraft operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL734 from Philadelphia Intl (KPHL), PA USA to Manchester Intl (EGCC), UK. Approximately 200nm east of St John’s Intl (CYYT), NL, the crew had an odor in the cockpit that would not dissipate. The crew declared an emergency and requested a diversion to CYYT. The flight landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. Maintenance completed an inspection of the engines and APU and no discrepancies where found. The oven in the first class galley was found to have aluminum foil stuck in the oven fan.  Maintenance placed the oven as non essential furnishing (NEF)and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FRJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ-900LR) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA 8207 from Sydney/J.A. Douglas McCurdy (CYQY), NS to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON.  Prior to boarding passengers, one of the flight attendants felt nauseous and vomited. Emergency medical services were called and the crewmember was transported to hospital. The flight reduced the amount of passengers to operate with one flight attendant and departed for destination without further incident.

On 27 September 2019, C-GGVC, a privately operated Piper PA18-150 (s/n 18-7609024X), was conducting a local flight near a farm 25 miles east of Camrose (CEQ3), Alberta. The aircraft had arrived at the farm earlier in the afternoon and picked up a passenger for a short flight. After landing in the field across from the main farm yard just south of the road, and dropping off the passenger, the aircraft took off heading eastbound. After a short ground run the aircraft lifted off and climbed out steeply. At 1645 Mountain Daylight Time, approximately 90 feet above the ground, the aircraft stalled and entered a spin to the left and struck power lines. The aircraft broke the top insulating wire and then bridged the next two conductor lines with the right wing. The aircraft  fell to the ground and burst into flames. The aircraft was consumed by the post crash fire. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was fatally injured. The aircraft was equipped with a 121.5 MHz emergency locator transmitter (ELT). No ELT  signal was received and the ELT was consumed in the post-impact fire.

C-GJZD, a De Havilland DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation, was conducting flight JZA8376 from Fort McMurray CYMM), AB to Calgary (CYYC), AB. While enroute in cruise, the flight crew observed that the #1 and # 3 hydraulic quantity was reading zero with no associated caution lights. The flight crew received multiple failure messages and decided to proceed to CYYC. On final approach to CYYC, the flight crew declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without further incident and there were no injuries. Company maintenance found the #1 input/output processor unserviceable. No hydraulic liquid loss occured. The processor was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-ISPW, an Airdrome Aeroplanes Sopwith Camel basic ultralight aircraft, was conducting a local VFR flight from Winnipeg/Lyncrest (CJL5), MB. Upon landing on the soft turf of Runway 17, the aircraft nosed over and flipped. The pilot was uninjured and was able to egress the aircraft. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to its rudder and left wing strut. There was no fire; local police, fire department, and ambulance responded to the scene.

C-FMDW, un appareil de type de Havilland Dash-8-300 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8987, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination d’Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON avec 48 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage. Après le démarrage des moteurs, l’équipage a mis en marche l’air de prélèvement et de la fumée est apparue dans le poste de pilotage. L’air de prélèvement a été coupé et l'avion est retourné à la barrière. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

F-FWWY, un Falcon 900LX en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Goose Bay (CYYR), NL à destination de Bill & Hillary Clinton National/Adams Field (KLIT), USA avec seul 2 pilotes à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en croisière au FL430 à environ 45 miles marins à l’ouest de YBC, une fissure du pare-brise central des 3 situé du côté droit est apparue. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a effectué un déroutement à Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre et il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FJLJ, un Wheeler Express CT en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol récréatif selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré (CYRC), QB à destination de Québec/Neuville (CNV9), QC  avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage, l’appareil a fait quelques bonds et le train d’atterrissage avant s’est partiellement affaissé. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. L’appareil a subi des dommages au train avant et au support du moteur.

C-FXJF, un Embraer 175 exploité par Sky Regional Airlines Inc. sous l'indicatif SKV7703 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau (CYUL), QC  à destination de George Bush Intercontinental / Houston Airport (KIAH), TX. Lors de la montée initiale, une odeur est apparue dans le poste de pilotage et dans la cabine. Par la suite, un message d’alarme LAV SMOKE du système d'affichage des paramètres moteurs et d'alerte de l'équipage (EICAS) est survenu. Le voyant du détecteur de fumée arrière était allumé et l'alarme sonore a retenti. L’équipage a décidé de revenir se poser à CYUL, et en raison de l’atterrissage en surcharge, a avisé l'ATC qu’il allait s’immobiliser sur la piste pour fin d’inspection. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés et l’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 24L sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-GXSU, a Diamond DA42 aircraft, was on an IFR test flight with a pilot and examiner on board. The pilot was conducting a simulated single engine landing on Runway 27 at London (CYXU). It was reported that all landing checks were completed and the landing gear was confirmed down with 3 green down-lock indicators. As the student pilot flared both propellers contacted the ground and the aircraft slid to a stop on the fuselage. Neither pilot was injured; there is substantial damage to both propellers and the lower fuselage. The operators maintenance organization is evaluating the damage and examining the landing gear system.

C-IGXG, a Quantum 912, basic ultra-light aircraft, was landing at the pilot's private grass strip near Picton, Ontario (CGB3). After touchdown, the pilot was unable to maintain directional control of the aircraft; it left the runway surface and overturned. There was substantial damage to the aircraft, the pilot was not injured.

C-FMAO, un appareil de type Pilatus PC-12/47, exploité par Pascan Aviation Inc. sous l'indicatif PSC360M, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Int, QC (CYQB) à destination de de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC). C-GJNL, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-300 exploité par Hydro-Québec, sous l'indicatif HYD341, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Havre-St-Pierre, QC (CYGV), à destination de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC). Après avoir effectué une approche pour la piste 28 et une remontée jusqu’à 3000 pieds, PSC360M a effectué une approche et une remontée de l’approche ILS pour la piste 10. Dans la remontée, l’équipage a communiqué qu’il passait 2800 pieds en montée alors que l’altitude publiée pour la remontée était de 2200 pieds. HYD341 qui était en circuit d’attente à 3200 pieds à l’est de CYBC, a dû effectuer une manœuvre d’évitement pour éviter un conflit avec PSC360M. L’espacement a été réduit sur le plan vertical sous la norme de 1000 pieds.

C-GWEF, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-400, was conducting flight WEN3227 from Regina Intl (CYQR), SK to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB.  After departing CYQR, the crew reported the right main gear door would not close. The flight was conducted at a reduced airspeed and a manual gear extension was required for landing. Emergency vehicles meet the aircraft on arrival in CYEG for a visual inspection before taxing to the gate. The aircraft taxied under its own power to the gate after arrival.Maintenance replaced the solenoid sequence valve in accordance with Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) . Further interrogation of the Proximity Sensing Electronics Unit (PSEU) revealed that both Main Landing Gear (MLG) Door proximity sensors were out of rig. The door sensors were rigged in accordance with the AMM. Operational tests were carried out with no further defects found.

On 24 September 2019, the E & B Helicopters Ltd. Bell 206B helicopter (registration C-GEBY, serial number 3375) was conducting a visual flight rules flight from the operator's base at Campbell River (E & B Heli) Heliport (CCR6) in Campbell River, British Columbia, to Moat Lake, British Columbia, with only the pilot on board. Shortly after departure, while flying southeast along the coastline, the helicopter briefly levelled off at 615 feet above sea level, then began a descent. When the helicopter was at 417 feet above sea level, it entered a right-hand climbing turn toward land and, following the turn, it began to descend again. During this descent, at 1103 Pacific Daylight Time, control of the helicopter was lost when it was about 200 feet above ground level and the helicopter fell to the ground, striking a building and 2 vehicles. The pilot was fatally injured. No one on the ground was injured. The helicopter was destroyed by the impact forces and a post-impact fire.

C-GQAJ, a Swearingen SA226-TC operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting a maintenance flight in the vicinity of Thompson (CYTH), MB. The flight crew conducted an NTS engine shutdown test but was subsequently unable to restart the engine (Garrett TPE331-10UA). The non-operating engine was secured, an emergency was declared, and an uneventful landing was carried out in CYTH.

C-GPWZ, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 helicopter operated by Gogal Air Services, was conducting a VFR flight from Snow Lake (CJE4), MB to Wekusko Lake, MB. On final approach for landing on an old logging road, the helicopter's rotor blade came in contact with a tree. The helicopter started vibrating and the pilot conducted an uneventful landing at the intended area. The aircraft was shut down.The operator's inspection of the aircraft revealed damage main rotor blades. The aircraft has been removed from service pending repairs.

C-FJYW, an ATR 42-300 aircraft operated by Calm Air International LP, was conducting a flight from Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU to Repulse Bay (CYUT), NU with 3 crew members and 14 passengers on board. In the descent through 4000 feet, the flight crew selected level 2 ice protection. At approximately 2500 feet, the flight crew smelled electrical smoke followed by a dark grey smoke emitting from the first officer's side window. Once clear of icing conditions, the crew reverted to level 1 ice protection, notified CYUT CARS of the cockpit smoke and declared an emergency. On landing, the crew observed that the first officer side window and electrical connection began to burn and melt. While the aircraft taxied off the runway small flames appeared. The crew notified the flight attendant, shut down the aircraft, and discharged the hand held fire extinguisher onto the burning portion of the window and associated electrical connection; extinguishing the fire. RCMP and volunteer fire department were dispatched to the aircraft and remained near the aircraft for 30 minutes post fire, to ensure no re-ignition of fire.

C-GPCJ, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Saab-Fairchild 340B, was conducting flight PCO3038 from Prince George (CYXS), BC to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 3 crew members and 32 passengers onboard. During the flight the aircraft encountered icing conditions and experienced vibrations. The crew declared a Pan Pan as a precaution because of the vibrations and degraded aircraft performance. The vibrations continued to short final where they ceased prior to landing. The aircraft landed without further incident.Following the flight, maintenance inspected the aircraft and did not find any faults with the engines or propellers.  A test flight was conducted and was found to be satisfactory.

C-GYUA, a Mitsubishi MU-2B-60 aircraft, operated by Thunder Airlines Limited, was conducting flight THU890 from Fort Frances Muni (CYAG), ON to Red Lake (CYRL), ON. At approximately 15 nautical miles North of CYAG, climbing through 7000 feet, the right hand fire warning light illuminated. The flight crew stopped the climb and carried out the engine fire checklist. The flight crew did not observe fire or smoke from the engine and a decided to return to CYAG with both engines operating. During the descent, the fire warning light extinguished and a flight medic reported smoke from the right hand engine. An emergency was declared and the right hand engine was shutdown. The aircraft landed safely in CYAG. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft in CYAG and a ferry flight was subsequently completed to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON. The operator's maintenance then replaced the right hand fire detector control unit.

C-GOZJ, a privately operated Cessna 185E on floats, was conducting a private flight from Conroe-North Houston Regional (KCXO), TX with 2 occupants onboard. Shortly after take-off, the aircraft experienced engine issues and attempted to return to KCXO. The aircraft impacted terrain on approach for runway 14. The 2 occupants on board were fatally injured, the aircraft was destroyed. The NTSB investigated (CEN19FA325).

C-FPRP, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG641 from Holguin/Frank Paris Intl (MUHG), Cuba to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 6 crew members and 187 passengers on board. During cruise, one of the flight attendants began to feel unwell and was unable to assume their service duties. Prior to descent, the flight attendant was able to resume their duties and the flight continued without further incident.

C-FJKP, an amateur built Kit Fox II, took off from a private airstrip. During the initial climb at approximately 300 feet AGL, the engine lost power. The aircraft was unable to maintain altitude and the pilot attempted to land in a nearby field. At approximately 100 feet above the ground, the engine (HKS 700E) stopped and the aircraft collided with trees during the flare. The pilot received minor injuries and the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GOWG, a Boeing 737-800 operating as flight TVS7212 from Katowice Intl - Katowice Intl (EPKT), Poland to Milas - Bodrum (LTFE) Turkey, was instructed by ATC to descend to FL330. While descending, the flight crew received a TCAS TA followed by TCAS RA `Monitor Vertical Speed' and `Level Off'. The flight crew had the traffic in sight and had already leveled off at FL330. The flight continued uneventfully.

C-ICWI, the Quad City Challenger II Special aircraft, was taking off from Camden East Airport (CCE6) when the cabin door opened. The pilot attempted to close the door and landed immediately; the aircraft bounced on touchdown, impacted the ground and nosed over. The pilot received minor injuries and the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GOSJ, un Partenavia P68 Observer exploité par Montmagny Air Service Inc. effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Montmagny, QC (CSE5) à destination de Havre St-Pierre, QC (CYGV). Après avoir effectué une escale à l’aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV), le C-GOSJ a décollé en direction de CYGV. Peu de temps après le décollage, le moteur de gauche a perdu de la puissance. Le pilote a fermé le moteur de gauche par mesure de précaution et a déclaré une urgence. L’avion est revenu se poser sans encombre à CYZV. Une inspection du moteur de gauche a été faite suite à l’événement. Une fuite de carburant a été détectée en raison d’une conduite qui s’était partiellement dévissée.

C-GSKK, an Airbus AS350-B3 aircraft operated by Selkirk Mountain Helicopters, was transferring Jet A1 fuel from a fuel truck at a staging site on Bugaboo Creek Road, BC to a remote fuel tank in Rory Creek, BC using a 1100 litre Fuel-Easy fuel container on a 100 ft long line with only the pilot on board. While climbing to fly over Bugaboo Pass, the load hit the ground just before the summit. The nose of the aircraft swung to the left and the pilot was able to manoeuver the aircraft to maintain control. The pilot released the long line and the aircraft returned to the staging site. The fuel container bladder tore open spilling approximately 1100 litres of fuel near the impact site. Spill kits were taken to the site and the incident was reported to the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change.

C-GTLS, a Beech A100 King Air aircraft operated by Wings Over Kississing, was conducting flight WN03 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Nejanilini Lake (CYNN), MB. During the climb through 8500 feet ASL, approximately 30NM north of CYTH, the flight crew noticed the right (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-28) hand engine oil pressure was fluctuating. The crew elected to return to CYTH. Subsequently, the aircraft's right engine torque began fluctuating and there was a decrease in oil pressure. The crew conducted a precautionary engine shutdown and landed the aircraft without further incident. The operator's maintenance identified that the right hand oil cap was not secured properly. Further checks are being performed by the operator's maintenance to ensure there is no damage to the engine.

N910LJ, a privately operated Learjet 45 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Horta airport (LPHR), Portugal (Azores Islands). After departure the crew received a Central Alert and Warning System warning message RHS BLEED OVERHEAT. The crew shut off right side engine bleed valve and reduced No. 2 engine power as per checklist. The crew contacted air traffic services to declare an emergency and request return to CYHZ. The aircraft landed without further incident a few minutes later with emergency services standing by. The crew coordinated with maintenance personnel to test and troubleshoot the right bleed system. The crew completed engine performance runs and a satisfactory test flight. It is suspected that an intermittent and faulty temperature sensor may be responsible for the overheat indication.

C-GQAJ, a Swearingen SA-226TC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting medevac flight PAG01 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Oxford House (CYOH), MB.  While in flight at 19,000 feet the aircraft experienced pressurization fluctuations. The flight crew requested a descent to 10,000 feet. While in the descent the cabin fully depressurized and the captain performed the emergency descent procedures, as per the QRH. The flight crew elected to return to CYWG where an uneventful landing was carried out.The operator’s maintenance identified a damaged cargo door seal.  The cargo door seal was replaced, the aircraft pressurization was ground tested serviceable, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GIUB, an Airbus A321 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA115 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with the number 2 Pack on MEL. During the climb out through FL230 the crew were unable to control the cockpit and cabin temperature. The aircraft was levelled off while the flight crew attempted to control the temperature. Unable to do so, the flight crew initiated a rapid descent to 10000 feet ASL. An emergency was declared and the aircraft was diverted back to CYYZ. The overweight landing was uneventful with ARFF standing by. During the descent the cabin oxygen masks did not deploy. Maintenance found damaged bellows downstream of the check valve and replaced the bellows. The number 2 Pack Flow Control was also replaced in accordance with the AMM. No other faults were found, and the MEL was removed from the number 2 Pack.

C-FLSU, an Air Canada Airbus A320 was conducting flight AC704 from Toronto/Lester B. Person Intl (CYYZ), ON to New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY. Upon arrival to KGLA, over the Hudson River, the flight crew received a TCAS RA with VFR traffic. The crew followed the TCAS resolution and climbed as required.

C-FKVT, a privately registered Aeronca 11AC, was making steep turns after takeoff in gusty wind conditions near French Narrows on Lake of the Woods, Ontario. The aircraft experienced an aerodynamic stall and contacted the rough surface of the lake. The pilot suffered minor injuries and the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FNQA, an Air Tractor AT-502B operated by Clayton Air Service, was en route from a field near Asquith, SK to Leask (CJH8), SK.  The pilot noticed a high engine oil temperature indication. The pilot elected to reduce thrust in the hope that the oil temperature would decrease; however, the power reduction was followed shortly with the illumination of a chip light. The pilot elected to shut down the engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-34AG) and made an uneventful forced landing in an open field. No injuries or structural damage encountered.  A post landing inspection on the engine revealed propeller was hard to rotate and grinding noise coming from compressor when rotated. The aircraft has been removed from service pending an engine inspection

C-GEOQ, a Boeing 767-375 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1566 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 8 crew members and 245 passengers on board. On the initial climb at approximately 7000 feet ASL, the flight and cabin crew noticed a strong odour throughout the aircraft. The flight crew attempted to clear the odour however with no success. The flight crew requested to level off at FL250 to troubleshoot the issue. Subsequently, the crew declared a PAN PAN, donned their oxygen masks and returned to land in CYVR without further incident. It was discovered that the cause of the strong odour was a shipment of Durian fruit in the forward cargo compartment. The fruit shipment was removed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBIP, an Air Canada Airbus A319 was conducting flight AC700 from Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) to LaGuardia International Airport, New York (KLGA). Upon arrival to KGLA the flight crew received a TCAS RA with VFR traffic. The crew followed the TCAS resolution and there was no conflict. ATC was advised of the traffic.

C-IFKK, a Zenair CH701 advanced ultralight, was conducting a VFR flight from Gimli, MB to Riverton, MB. While enroute, gusty headwind conditions were encountered to the point where the aircraft was moving backwards in relation to the ground and was losing altitude. As power lines were underneath the aircraft, the pilot lowered the nose in an attempt to avoid them. The aircraft subsequently stalled and struck the terrain below. The pilot sustained minor injuries and the aircraft was destroyed.

C-GILK, a Beech B300 operated by Carson Air, was conducting a flight from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Campbell River (CYBL), BC with 2 passengers and 2 flight crew on board. On take off, when the crew retracted the landing gear, both generator annunciator lights illuminated. The flight crew actioned the memory checklist items for a dual generator failure. The crew began to declare an emergency with ATC when the radios stopped working and the screens for the G1000 flight instrument system failed. All electrical annunciators, communications and instruments failed except for the emergency back-up standby attitude indicator and altimeter. The crew were able to remain in VMC and elected to proceed to Vancouver/Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC airport because the aircraft was already proceeding in that direction. The first officer called the CZBB ATC tower by cell phone and declared an emergency.
