The captain actioned the checklist to manually extend the landing gear and the aircraft landed in CZBB without further incident.The operator's maintenance found the aircraft's main battery (Concorde p/n RG-380E/44K, s/n 40819077) was hot and testing at 20 volts. The main battery was removed and replaced with cap tested battery (serial number 40885147).

C-GPIT, a privately operated, float-equipped Piper PA12 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Moosehorn Lake, BC to Telegraph Creek (CAH9), BC with only the pilot on board. Approximately 4 NM from CAH9, the aircraft experienced an engine power loss. The pilot attempted to restart the engine (Lycoming O-360-A2A) and the engine had one sudden, brief burst of full power before losing power again. The aircraft performed an emergency landing in a field, approximately 0.75 NM west of the water landing area. The pilot received minor injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The ELT activated. The cause of the loss of engine power is undetermined.

C-FRSO, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA26 from Shanghai/Pudong Intl. Airport (ZSPD), China to Vancouver Intl. (CYVR), BC with 12 crew members and 287 passengers on board. During cruise, the captain’s window cracked followed by significant electrical arcing. The crew declared a Pan Pan and diverted to New Tokyo Intl. (RJAA), Japan. The aircraft landed at RJAA without further incident. The window was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GSAU, a Beech B200 operated by the province of Saskatchewan, was conducting flight SLG3 from Regina International (CYQR), SK, to Saskatoon International (CYXE), SK.  Upon selection of the landing gear down on arrival at CYXE, the flight crew observed that there was no green light for the left main landing gear. The flight crew conducted a go around in VFR conditions to troubleshoot the issue. The flight crew was able to determine the landing gear was locked as the gear horn did not sound with appropriate power and flap settings. For precautionary measures, the flight crew declared an emergency and an uneventful landing was carried out with emergency vehicles standing by.The operator’s maintenance replaced the down lock light indicator assembly. Gear swings were completed and the landing gear tested satisfactorily. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GROW, an Air Tractor 402B, operated by Bonnyville Air Services (1980) Ltd., was conducting an aerial work flight 3 miles east of High Prairie (CZHP), AB when it struck a power line. Multiple passes had been made on the field and on this particular pass the aircraft had moved closer to a gas plant which featured a flare stack. The pilot was momentarily distracted by the possibility of guide wires that might support the stack. He had crossed the subject power line multiple times earlier during this flight, but this time pulled up late, leading to the strike.  The aircraft was able to continue flight and returned to the staging area at the Donnelly airport (CFM4). Damage was minor and was mainly focused on the spray nozzles. Maintenance inspected the aircraft, effected repairs, and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FSKO, a Keewatin Air LP Beech B200, was conducting a flight on a special flight permit from Cambridge Bay (CYCB), NU to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. During the descent from 27 000 feet above sea level, the flight crew heard thumping and felt vibrations in the flight deck. Shortly after the captain observed short bursts of flames coming out of the exhaust of the number 1 engine in sync with the noises and vibrations. The flight crew noted the noises and vibrations became more frequent and noticed the left torque was surging in relation to the short burst of flames. The flight crew actioned the QRH procedure and conducted a precautionary engine shutdown, declared an emergency, and an uneventful landing was carried out at CYWG. The operator's maintenance sent the engine for testing and it was identified that the high pressure bleed valve closing point was 1200 rpm below minimum. The high pressure bleed valve orificie was change from 0.056” to 0.054". The engine was re-tested and was assessed as meeting all performance requirements. This aircraft experienced a similar event on 12 September 2019. (TSB occurrence A19C0113).

C-GTAT, un DHC-8-300 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif de vol JZA8704, était en montée depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL) Québec en direction de Bathurst NB, lorsque l'équipage a perçu une odeur de circuit électrique en surchauffe dans le poste de pilotage. Une urgence a été déclarée et les masques d'oxygène des pilotes ont été utilisés. L'appareil est revenu se poser à CYUL sans encombre. Aucune fumée ou odeur n'a été rapportée dans la cabine.

C-GJVH, a Fairchild SA227-DC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting flight BLS318 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB, to Red Lake (CYRL), ON. During the climb the flight crew observed a number 2 engine fire light indication. The crew conducted a precautionary engine shutdown, declared an emergency and landed the aircraft in CYWG without further incident.

C-GWOX, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting a flight from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON, to Muskrat Dam (CZMD), ON.  During landing at CZMD, the aircraft experienced a gust of wind at approximately 10 feet AGL. The captain took control and landed the aircraft. A post-flight walk around identified minor damages to the aircraft tail strakes.  The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and verified the damage was localized to the strakes of the tail. The strakes were replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

F-GZCF an Airbus 330-200 aeroplane operated by Air France was conducting flight AFR159 from Dallas Fort Worth, Texas, (KDFW) to Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), Paris, France. While in cruise flight with 11 crew and 148 passengers the crew noted a drop in oil quantity and oil pressure on the number 2 engine. The crew contacted maintenance and referenced to their quick reference handbook. At position 5411N 4432W the crew declared an emergency and decided to divert to Gander Intl, Newfoundland and Labrador (CYQX). The engine was kept at idle for the descent and landing. Maintenance is determining the problem and repairs will be effected.

C-GOJN, a Sikorsky S-61, operated by VIH Helicopters for heli-logging, was in a hover with ground personnel cleared away from the immediate area when the long line attached to the helicopter belly hook released. The helicopter returned to the service barge and the belly hook was examined by engineers. The emergency release mechanism was found to have not reset itself. The company issued a notice to all pilots and engineers to detail the differences between the two SK61 helicopters operated.

C-GTQB, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Air Transat, conducted a charter flight from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Victoria (CYYJ), BC. While parked on the ramp in CYYJ, a passenger bus drove under the left wing and the roof of the bus scraped the underside of the wing. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained minor damage.

C-FSKO, a Beech B200 operated by Keewatin Air LP, was conducting flight KEW204 from Cambridge Bay (CYCB), NU, to Gjoa Haven, (CYHK), NU. Due to deteriorating weather conditions in CYHK, the flight crew conducted a missed approach and proceeded to CYCB, their alternate airport.  In the descent from 20,000 feet above sea level, the flight crew heard thumping and felt vibrations in the flight deck. Shortly after, short bursts of flames were observed coming out of the exhaust of the #1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-42) in sync with the noises and vibrations. The flight crew then noted that the frequency of the noises and vibrations were increasing and the left torque began surging. The flight crew actioned the QRH procedure and conducted a precautionary engine shutdown, and declared an emergency with CYCB Radio. An uneventful landed was carried out in CYCB.The operator's maintenance conducted a #1 engine inspection in CYCB. No faults were found during the engine inspection. A special flight permit was issued and the aircraft was flown back to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB, for further inspection.

C-GOFI, a Bell 206L-1 helicopter operated by Custom Helicopters, was on a flight with an externally slung load from a remote location near Split Lake, MB, to Kelsey (CZEE), MB. Approximately 32NM ESE of CZEE, the slung load inadvertently released. Minor damage occurred to cargo net contents.

C-GENV, a de Havilland DHC8-400 operated by WestJet Encore as WEN3504, was taxiing out following pushback for departure from London (CYXU), Ontario bound for Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ), Ontario. The flight crew detected a burning electrical smell, which the Flight Attendant also reported, followed by traces of visible smoke near the front of the cabin. Flight crew completed the appropriate checklist resulting in both engines being shutdown, and requested a tow back to the gate. The passengers were deplaned normally, and no emergency services were requested. Maintenance discovered a defective recirculation fan, applied the MEL, and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FLWE, an Embraer E190 operated by Air Canada was conducting ACA526 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Boston / General Edward Lawrence Logan (KBOS), MA with 5 crew members and 88 passengers aboard. On descent into KBOS, the flight crew received a spoiler fault. The crew declared a PAN PAN and proceeded to land at KBOS uneventfully. There were no injuries to the occupants. There is no damage to aircraft. Maintenance found corrosion dust on one of the spoiler actuators and its connector and is being replaced.

L’Embraer ERJ-175 exploité par Sky Regional Airlines Inc. sous l'indicatif SKV7684 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport George Bush Intercontinental, TX aux États-Unis (KIAH) à destination de Montréal Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) avec 65 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. En montée initiale, l'équipage à reçu un message de panne des volets (FLAP FAIL CAUTION). La procédure du manuel de référence rapide a été effectuée, mais le message d'alerte est resté allumé. L'équipage a continué le vol vers CYUL avec les volets en position rétractés et demandé la présence des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) pour l'atterrissage à CYUL. L'appareil a atterri sans encombre ni dommages.

C-GYNM, an Agusta AW139 helicopter operated by 7506406 Canada Inc. (dba Ornge Rotor Wing Operation), was operating flight LF7 from Marathon/Wilson Memorial Hospital (CPX2), ON to Thunder Bay/Health Sciences Centre (CTB2), ON. While enroute, the flight crew observed a MGB CHIP SUMP CAS indication. The Quick Reference Handbook was consulted and the chip burner was subsequently activated 3 times. Prior to the 4th indication, the flight crew elected to divert the flight to Thunder Bay Intl (CYQT), ON and declared a PAN PAN to obtain priority landing. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 25 with ARFF standing by.The operator's maintenance inspected the helicopter upon shutdown and found a silver magnetic chip on the right-hand sump chip detector. Parts were replaced and the aircraft was released for service after a successful 30 minute hover flight was completed.

C-GHLT, a Boeing 767-333ER aircraft was being operated by Air Canada Rouge as flight ROU1992 from Vancouver (CYVR) to Pierre Elliot Trudeau International Airport (CYUL). Shortly after take off in the vicinity of Kelowna (CYLW), the flight crew was advised that a cabin flight attendant became incapacitated due to illness. A replacement was assigned to the position and functions.

C-GXRW, a Boeing 737-800, operated by Swoop Airlines as flight WSW312 from Abbotsford (CYXX) for Edmonton (CYEG), struck geese on the initial climb and the flight crew declared an emergency. The crew informed ATC of a mechanical thrust issue (CFM INTERNATIONAL, CFM56-7B27/E) and elected to return to the point of departure. The aircraft landed without further incident at 15:42Z (11:42 EDT). The aircraft remained on the runway in order to facilitate an inspection by aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF).

C-FNTK, a Diamond DA20-C1 aircraft operated by Moncton Flight College, exited from runway 24 at taxiway Delta following landing after a local training flight at Moncton/Roméo Leblanc Intl (CYQM), NB. C-FUZG, another Diamond DA20-C1 aircraft operated by Moncton Flight College, was stopped on the right side of Delta while holding short of runway 24. As it taxied past, the left wing of C-FNTK struck the left wing of C-FUZG. There were no reported injuries to the occupants. The outer portions of the left wings of both aircraft sustained damage. Both left wings were removed and sent to a manufacturer approved repair facility for evaluation and repair.

C-GMRS, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by PAL Aerospace Ltd., was conducting flight SPR01 from St. John's (CYYT), NL to St. Anthony (CYAY), NL. After departure, the flight crew noticed fuel leaking from the left wing fuel filler cap, and coordinated with air traffic services for a return to CYYT. The crew requested airport emergency services stand by, and made an overweight landing without further incident. The CYYT airport initially closed all runways, and later limited the closures to runway 11/29, 02/20 and taxiway Bravo, which were closed for approximately 2 hours to allow spilled fuel to be cleaned up. An aircraft had its landing delayed, and 2 aircraft had their departures delayed due to runway closures.Company maintenance personnel inspected and tested the fuel cap and filler mount, and noted no defect. An overweight landing inspection was carried out. The company is further investigating the occurrence.

N410UA, a United Airlines Airbus A320-232, was operating as flight UA 2268 from George Bush Intercontinental Airport (KIAH), Houston, Texas, USA to Edmonton (CYEG), AB with 5 crew and 143 passengers onboard. UA 2268 was following an open Standard Terminal Arrival (STAR) IGSOX 2 and was instructed by the arrival controller to descend to 6000 feet ASL for the ILS RWY 12.  A loss of separation occurred when UA2268 deviated from the STAR and turned towards the initial fix, MIPOT. Separation deteriorated to 2.2 NM laterally and 700 feet vertically (3 NM or 1000 feet is required) with an arriving Canadian North, flight MPE445 that was cleared straight in approach RWY 12. Separation was regained when the controller instructed N410UA to turn right. There were no TCAS RAs from either aircraft.

C-FASV, an AirSprint Embraer E545, was operating as flight ASP812 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Calgary (CYYC), AB with 2 crew and 2 passengers on board. While en route to CYYC, the flight crew observed a steering failure indication. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist and the indication failed to clear. As a precaution, the crew requested emergency services upon arrival in CYYC. A successful approach and landing was conducted into CYYC with ARFF standing by. There were no injuries reported to the crew or passengers.

C-GKEX, a privately owned Hatz Classic biplane powered by a Rotec 9-cylinder radial engine, took off from Hanover Saugeen Municipal (CYHS), ON to conduct a second test flight. The pilot flew for nearly an hour before returning to CYHS. During the base turn on approach to runway 19, the engine failed and the pilot elected to land in a field nearby. During the landing rollout, the aircraft overturned and came to rest on its back. The pilot received minor injuries, which were treated by paramedics on scene. The aircraft was substantially damaged, with damage to the wingtips, vertical stabilizer, struts, and the upper fuselage.

CS-TKT, a EuroAtlantic Boeing 767-300 operating as NAX4PF, was enroute from Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR), USA to Rome Fiumicino Leonardo Da Vinci (LIRF), Italy. At position 49 50N / 054 00W the crew contacted Gander Area Control Center and declared a MAYDAY due to smoke in the cockpit that was emitting from the left Control Display Unit (CDU). The crew requested, and received clearance, to divert to Gander Intl (CYQX), Newfoundland and Labrador, where they landed uneventfully with ARFF on standby.Maintenance removed the LH CDU which showed evidence of overheating and soot buildup in the area of the box cooling vent. Maintenance replaced the LH CDU and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJQU, an Ayres S2R aircraft operated by Kindersley Airspray, was conducting an aerial application flight 16 nm NE of Kindersley Regional (CYKY), SK. During an application pass, the aircraft experienced an engine power loss (Pratt & Whitney USA R-1340-AN-1). The pilot attempted an engine restart that was unsuccessful and subsequently the pilot conducted a forced landing on a road. During the landing sequence, the right wing hit a hydro pole and the aircraft veered off the road. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the right wing and the right hand gear leg collapsed. The pilot was uninjured and there was no environmental damage.The operator conducted an post-accident examination of the aircraft and observed there was no fuel remaining on the aircraft.

C-GSEN, un Cessna 172 exploité par Cargair Ltée, effectuait un vol de nuit selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Montréal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX) à destination de Sherbrooke, QC (CYSC) avec une pilote à bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en croisière à 3500 pieds, à environ 20 nm à l’ouest de CYSC, celui-ci a perdu rapidement de l'altitude et a percuté des arbres avant de s’écraser au sol. La pilote a subi des blessures mortelles et l’appareil a été détruit.

The pilot of Airbus Helicopter AS350B2, C-FTHZ, was moving the helicopter forward of a rock outcropping that the tail had been hanging over and lifting off from the landing zone (staging site) to begin crew moves when during liftoff he felt a severe vibration, landed, and shut down. The site was assessed for any leak or spillage of fluids as the tail rotor blades, gearbox, vertical fin, and tail-boom were damaged. Maintenance personnel were flown to the site to prepare C-FTHZ to be airlifted for further inspection.

C-FSRY, a Dash 8 operated by Jazz as flight JZA239 from Terrace, BC entered taxiway Hotel 'H' without authorization. American Airlines feeder Compass Flight CPZ6023, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 LR, N213NN, destined for Los Angeles had to take action to prevent a collision.

C-FYBK, Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Swoop Inc., was conducting flight WSW537 from London (CYXU), ON to Edmonton International (CYEG), AB with 6 crew members and 173 passengers on board. During cruise, the cabin crew and flight crew recognized a smell of cigarette smoke in the aircraft. The 'Smoke in the Cockpit' procedure from the Quick Reference Checklist (QRC) was actioned, a MAYDAY declared with a diversion to Regina, International (CYQR), SK. After landing in CYQR, fire and rescue scanned the aircraft for heat signature, with no evidence of fire found. The flight crew taxied the aircraft to the gate for passenger deplaning.The operator's maintenance inspected both cargo pits, the electronics and equipment bay, and hydraulic levels with no evidence of smoke and no faults were found.

C-GSJZ, a Dash 8 400 operated by JAZZ as flight JZA8061 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR) to Victoria experienced on the take off roll just prior to rotation,a slight yaw to the left, that the crew corrected with rudder. The take off was otherwise uneventful and the pilot selected gear up. The flight crew thought they may have blown a tire on take off, advised ATC of such and extended the landing gear at 4000 feet for the flight attendants to inspect the landing gear; all tires seemed fine. The flight crew made an announcement to the passengers to advise they were returning to Vancouver. The crew did not declare an emergency, but requested ARFF on standby. The aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-FRUZ, a De Havilland DHC-8-311 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA9047 from Masset (CZMT), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 3 crew members and 44 passengers on board. During cruise, the flight crew noticed the #2 hydraulic quantity was low. The flight crew elected to use the alternate gear extension and declared an emergency for landing into CYVR. On approach, the #2 hydraulic ISO valve illuminated. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist and landed safely.The operator's maintenance found the hydraulic pump leaking from the case. A new pump was installed IAW MM29-10-11 and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FHRE, a privately owned Van’s RV-9A aircraft, was conducting a training flight from Olds-Didsbury, (CEA3), AB with one instructor pilot and one student pilot onboard. The student pilot was attempting to take off from Runway 04 and experienced difficulty with a nose high attitude and a left cross-wind. The instructor pilot took control as the aircraft started to settle and the main wheels contacted a berm at the end of the runway resulting in damage to the propeller and nose wheel. There were no injuries reported.

N11184, an Embraer EMB 145XR aircraft operated by ExpressJet, was conducting flight ASQ4147 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. On departure, the aircraft experienced a loss of separation with C-GONW, a de Havilland DHC-8-101 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP conducting flight JZA498, which is on arrival to CYYZ. A clearance had been issued to ASQ4147 to fly direct to RIKEM instead of SAVUR, causing separation to be reduced to 2.4nm laterally and 600ft vertically. A separation of 3nm laterally and 1000ft vertically was required. The aircraft were flying nearly parallel tracks when the loss of separation occurred.

C-GAPY, the Air Canada Airbus A319 (flight AC258) was on route from Winnipeg (CYWG) to Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ). During the descent the flight crew noticed a strong odor in the cockpit and donned their oxygen masks. They declared a PAN PAN and the aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power. Maintenance determined that the APU aft bearing oil pressure line was leaking and replaced as per company task card. They also performed a decontamination of the ECS and after an operational check of the APU the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FMSX, an Airbus A320 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC297 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 5 crew members and 142 passengers on board. Approximately 48 nm ENE of Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB, the pilots received a "Press Sys 1 and 2" ECAM message. The pilots elected to divert to CYYC and completed an uneventful landing. Company maintenance completed an inspection of the aircraft and found a protective cover installed on the vent port for the #1 outflow valve. The cover was removed, the aircraft was function checked for normal operation on the ground and subsequently returned to service.

C-GKQE, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE227 from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON to Saint John (CYSJ), NB. During cruise, the crew received caution lights for #1 HYD ISO VLV, and ROLL SPLR INBD HYD. The crew also noticed the #1 hydraulic fluid quantity dropping to zero. The QRH was actioned and the crew decided to return to CYOW. During the flight the caution light for #1 ENG HYD PUMP also illuminated. The crew declared an emergency and requested ARFF to be on stand by. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. Maintenance performed an #1 engine run and found fluid leaking from center bottom fuselage drain. They determined that the Balance Relief Valve was faulty and replaced IAW AMM 29-11-52. Subsequent testing revealed no further leaks and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FXIK, the Fox Aviation Cessna 180 H was returning from a sight seeing trip to Niagara Falls with the pilot and two passengers on board. After touchdown, the aircraft veered left and the pilot tried to correct the deviation by applying right brake. The right brake failed and the aircraft continued to the left and off the runway, ground looped resulting in the left main gear collapsing. The three occupants on board were not injured. Maintenance determined that a seal in the right brake system failed and all fluid was lost.

C-FPML, a float-equipped Cessna 180F operated by Westcoast Wild Adventures Ltd, was on approach to "the ditch", a water landing strip adjacent to runway 11/29 at CYAZ (Tofino, BC). The aircraft's right float struck a metal post on the land immediately prior to the ditch and the aircraft overturned in the water after touching down. The pilot was not injured but the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FTGZ, a Nanchang CJ6A, was participating in an air demonstration in the vicinity of Smith, AB. After the air demonstration was complete the aircraft struck terrain while returning to a private airstrip where the aircraft was based. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was fatally injured.Extended summary  (24 January 2020):On 31 August 2019, at approximately 1130 Mountain Daylight Time, a privately registered Nanchang CJ6A aircraft (registration C-FTGZ, serial number 1532014) departed a privately owned grass airfield located 7 nautical miles (NM) south of Smith, Alberta, to participate in an airshow at the fairgrounds in Smith.A special flight operations certificate (SFOC) was issued by Transport Canada for a 2-aircraft airshow to be conducted at the 2019 Smith Hondo Fall Fair. The occurrence aircraft was one of the 2 aircraft authorized. The investigation found that the airshow was performed in accordance with the limitations and requirements of the SFOC.The airshow concluded at 1207 as the aircraft completed its final south-to-north pass through the airshow box. As the aircraft departed the airshow box, it made a right turn to the east. At 1208, the aircraft was observed doing a rolling manoeuvre and impacted the ground in a wooded area, approximately 1 NM east of Smith, at 55°9.731' N and 114°0.853' W. The pilot, the sole occupant of the aircraft, was fatally injured.The aerodrome routine meteorological report (METAR) issued at 1200 for Slave Lake (CYZH), Alberta, indicated the following: calm winds, visibility 9 statute miles, no clouds,  temperature 15 °C. Weather was not considered a factor in this accident.The 121.5 MHz emergency locator transmitter (ELT) was found intact and was manually switched off by first responder personnel. The expiry date for the ELT battery was February 2020. The ELT had last been serviced in June 2018.The occurrence aircraft was equipped with a Garmin GPSMAP 196 global positioning system (GPS), which was recovered at the accident site and sent to the TSB Engineering Laboratory, in Ottawa, Ontario, for analysis. Flight data was recovered from the GPS. The recorded parameters included universal date and time, elevation, latitude and longitude position, and ground speed. The data for the occurrence flight spanned about 44 minutes. The final recorded GPS data point before impact indicated that the aircraft was at an altitude of 2636 feet above sea level (541 feet above ground level), at 118 mph ground speed.The aircraft impact attitude was approximately 65° nose-down and wings-level. The aircraft was destroyed on impact. All major components of the aircraft were accounted for at the accident site. The nature of the impact was not survivable. The flight control systems, engine, propeller, and flight instruments that were examined did not exhibit any failures that would have prevented normal operation.According to the records reviewed, the aircraft was certified and maintained in accordance with the existing regulations, and the aircraft was being operated within the weight and balance design limits.The pilot held a commercial pilot licence aeroplane rated for single and multiengine land and seaplanes, and a Category 1 medical certificate, both valid until 01 November 2019. The pilot’s flight hours at the time of the accident are unknown, because his personal log was not up to date. At 23 May 2016, the pilot had 4006.8 hours total flight time recorded in his log, and the pilot flew the occurrence aircraft for the first time on 06 October 2017. Since the aircraft was purchased, 60.9 hours had been flown on the occurrence aircraft, but it is unknown how many of those hours were flown by the pilot.

C-FMZR, the Air Canada Embraer ERJ 190-100 (flight AC1037) departed Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ) and was on route to Denver International Airport (KDEN) when the flight and cabin crew noticed an odour. The flight crew decided to return to CYYZ and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft performed an uneventful overweight landing with ARFF standing by. Maintenance determined that the #1 engine oil had been over serviced. Oil level was correctly serviced and subsequent engine runs revealed no further odor. Maintenance also performed an overweight landing inspection prior to releasing aircraft back to service.

C-FIQU, an ATR 42-300 operated by First Air, was conducting flight CJT587 from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. Shortly after take off from CYQT, the flight crew noticed the number 2 engine was not producing the expected thrust. The flight crew actioned the appropriate QRH procedure, declared an emergency and returned to CYQT. An uneventful landing was carried out with ARFF vehicles ready.The operator’s maintenance identified that the Electronic Control Unit (ECU) had failed. The ECU was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service

C-FUJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation, was conducting flight JZA8623 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 4 crew members and 71 passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff from CYWG, the flight crew received a gear disagree warning message. The flight crew conducted the QRH procedure and, upon completion of the procedure, the landing gear indicator showed three gear lights in the down position. The flight crew decided to return to CYWG, an emergency was declared, and an uneventful landing was carried out with emergency vehicles standing by. The operator's maintenance identified the AFT door drive bracket (where the weight on wheels switches are mounted) being loose in the nose landing gear assembly. The bracket was replaced, gear swing was completed, and the aircraft was returned to service. This aircraft had been involved in 2 similar occurrences in the previous few days (TSB occurrence numbers A19C0100 and A19C0098).

C-GUDO, a Boeing 787-900 operated by WestJet was conducting flight WJA009 from Paris / Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB, when a cabin crew member sustained a minor injury enroute. Their duties were distributed to the other flight crew members.

C-GYTL, a Fairchild SA-227 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting flight BLS373 from Sault St. Marie (CYAM), ON to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON.  Southwest of CYQT, the flight crew observed left engine RPM anomalies.  The flight crew conducted the QRH procedure and performed a precautionary engine shutdown.  An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed in CYQT without further event with ARFF vehicles waiting.  The operator’s maintenance found a defective propellor governor.  The aircraft remains out of service until a new propellor governor has been installed.

C-FQLO, a privately registered Cessna 150H, was conducting a VFR flight from Yorkton Muni (CYQV), SK, to North Battleford (CYQW), SK. On final approach for Runway 30 at CYQW, the engine (Teledyne Continental O-200-A) stopped. The pilot conducted a forced landing in a canola field approximately 1/4 mile prior to the threshold of Runway 30. On landing, the aircraft sustained substantial damage to the propeller and wings and the ELT activated. The pilot was uninjured.It was reported that a subsequent inspection of the fuel tanks revealed there was no fuel remaining.

C-FTIR, an ATR 42-500 operated by Bradley Air Services Ltd. doing business as First Air, was conducting flight FAB842 from Kugluktuk (CYCO), NT to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with 3 crew members and 25 passengers on board. Shortly after take-off during landing gear retraction, the flight crew heard two "pops". The flight crew elected to continue the flight to CYZF and on approach, declared an emergency and requested ARFF be placed on standby due to the possibility of having one or more blown main tires. An uneventful landing was carried out in CYZF and the aircraft taxied to the terminal under its own power.Subsequent investigation by company maintenance determined that the left hand engine intake throat deice boot had become disbonded from the intake duct. The oil cooler flap exhibited damage, and the first stage compressor exhibited foreign object damage. The aircraft was repaired and returned to service.

C-FRWK, a Mitsubishi MU-2B-60 aircraft operated by Thunder Airlines, was conducting flight THU850 from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Peawanuk (CYPO), ON. On approach into CYPO, the flight crew selected landing gear down; the landing gear did not function. The flight crew diverted to CYQT where an emergency was declared. On approach into CYQT, the flight crew attempted the normal landing gear selection once more and the landing gear still did not function. The flight crew conducted a successful manual landing gear extension and an uneventful landing was carried out with emergency vehicles standing by. The operator’s maintenance reset the landing gear system and changed the landing gear door motor. Landing gear system checks were completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GMWT, a privately registered de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG831 from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Opapimiskam Lake (CKM8), ON. The aircraft experienced a loss of hydraulic fluid on the #2 hydraulic system during the descent through 10,000 feet ASL (approximately 4nm ENE of Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON) when the flight crew turned on the Stand-by Power Unit (SPU) as part of the approach checks. The flight crew declared an emergency with the appropriate FSS and diverted to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON.  An uneventful landing was carried out with ARFF vehicles on standby.  The flight crew shut down the aircraft engines on the runway and the aircraft was towed off the runway by the operator's maintenance.The operator's maintenance replaced the #2 SPU, performed leak and ground checks, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWJF, a Boeing 737-700 operated by WestJet was conducting flight WJA1535 from Houston/George Bush Intercontinental (KIAH) to Calgary, AB (CYYC). While enroute in cruise, WJA1535 entered turbulence. At this time a flight attendant was at the back of a service cart near the aft galley. The flight attendant fell into the aft galley and the service cart followed and struck their hand. The flight attendant was unable to perform their duties and their duties were distributed among the other flight attendants for the remainder of the flight.

C-FDMB, a Boeing 737-800 operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA264 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL. During the takeoff roll, the flight crew observed a master caution cargo door alert. The flight crew elected to reject the takeoff at 90 KIAS. While taxiing back to the gate the flight crew called for ARFF due to hot brakes. Company maintenance found a bungee lanyard that interfered between the doorframe and warning switch. The lanyard was replaced.

C-GNZG, un appareil de type Cessna 180K sur flotteurs en exploitation privé effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le réservoir Gouin, QC, à destination du lac Surprise, QC, situé à 4 nm au sud-est de l’aéroport de Mont-Tremblant International - La Macaza, QC (CYFJ). Alors qu’il était en vent arrière en direction nord pour le lac Surprise, le pilote a constaté une hausse des températures d’échappements (EGT), le pilote a augmenté le mélange (mixture) et a activé le réchauffe carburateur, les températures ont descendu et ensuite, l’appareil a subi une panne de moteur. Le pilote a manœuvré l’aéronef vers le lac Macaza qui était devant lui, il a évité une habitation, mais une des ailes a percuté un arbre. Le pilote réussi à amerrir l’avion sur le lac et a terminé sa course sur un banc de sable. Le pilote seul à bord n’a pas été blessé. L’appareil a subi des dommages à l’aile.

M-ODEL, un appareil de type Gulstream GIV-X exploité par Hampshire Aviation LLP, effectuait un vol depuis l’aéroport de Farnborough, UK (EGLF) à destination d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB). C-FKGY, un Bombardier CL-600-2B16 (Series 604) exploité par ACASS Canada Ltd effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis CYFB à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB). Alors que M-ODEL a été autorisé pour l’approche à CYFB, l’espacement avec C-FKGY qui décollait de CYFB, a été réduit sous les 3 minutes prescrites.

C-GGNY, a Dash 8 Q400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA 8862 from Halifax Stanfield International Airport, NS (CYHZ) to Gander International Airport, NL (CYQX). During cruise the aircraft encountered turbulence that caused one of cabin members to sustain a minor injury and was unable to continue their duties. The other cabin crew members assumed their duties for the remainder of the flight.

C-FWEP, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par WestJet Encore, effectuait le vol WEN3510 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC, avec à son bord 49 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en croisière juste avant la descente à environ 115 milles nautiques (nm) de CYUL, le message « HYD SOV #2 » est apparu avec l’illumination du « master caution ». L’équipage a alors remarqué que la quantité de liquide hydraulique dans le système #2 indiquait 0%. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification associée et une urgence a été déclarée. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre et après n’avoir constaté aucun dommage par une inspection par un véhicule d’urgence, il a été remorqué jusqu’au tablier. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GHJW, a Sikorsky S76A aircraft operated by Helijet International, was conducting a VFR flight from Vancouver/Harbour (CBC7), BC to Nanaimo Harbour Heliport (CDH5), BC. In cruise, approximately 3 NM NE of CDH5, C-GHJW spotted N8397Q, a Cessna U206F floatplane in the opposite direction and at the same altitude, approximately 1500 feet ahead. C-GHJW made an evasive turn to the left and initiated a climb, while N8397Q also appeared to take evasive action. C-GHJW attempted to communicate with N8397Q several times without success. C-GHJW continued to CDH5 and landed safely.

C-FUJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation, was conducting flight JZA8526 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON. Shortly after takeoff from CYWG, the flight crew received a gear disagree warning message. The flight crew actioned the QRH and the landing gear was successfully extended. The crew declared an emergency and an uneventful landing was carried out with emergency vehicles standing by. The operator's maintenance identified that the proximity sensor was damaged. The sensor and the nose weight on wheels centre wiring harness was replaced. The aircraft was returned to service. This aircraft also experienced a gear disagree warning on 22 August 2019 (TSB occurrence A19C0098).

C-GLFH, a privately registered Cessna 177B aircraft, was on final approach to Salmon Arm (CZAM), BC with 2 persons on board. On short final, the pilot noticed he no longer had engine power. The aircraft rate of descent increased significantly and landed 20' short of the runway threshold. The landing gear collapsed and the aircraft came to rest on the edge of the runway. The pilot and passenger received minor injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The ELT functioned as designed. The aircraft was found to have minimal fuel in the LH & RH fuel tanks.

C-FOBV, a float-equipped de Havilland DHC-2 Beaver aircraft operated by Sapawe Air Ltd., was conducting a flight from Eva Lake (CKO2), ON to Cache Lake, ON. During taxi after landing, the pilot shut down the engine and coasted to the dock. Upon docking, a Park Staff member assisted in docking the floatplane without the request of the pilot. During docking, the attendant sustained a serious injury between the left hand float cleat and the rope that was attached to the dock. The attendant was taken to hospital.

C-GKGC, an Air Georgian CL-600-2B19 (CRJ 200) was conducting flight GGGN7306 from Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) to Pittsburgh Intl (KPIT). On the downwind for 28C the aircraft was cleared to descend to 4000 feet from 6000 feet and informed that there was a Skyhawk (Cessna 172) at 3500 feet. The flight crew responded that they had the traffic in sight. The traffic was also on the TCAS. In the turn to base they were level at 4000 feet when the crew saw that the traffic was now showing -0400 with amber on the TCAS at approximately 3nm. The TCAS then initiated an RA to climb. The aircraft climbed 300 feet before the RA announced clear of conflict; ATC cleared the flight down to 4000 feet as well as the the approach when able. The aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-FGKN, an Air Canada A331 aircraft was conducting flight AC712 from Lester B Pearson Intl airport (CYYZ) to LaGuardia - New York (KLGA). On approach the crew received a TCAS RA to monitor vertical speed. The command was followed and the aircraft had an uneventful landing.

C-GHKR, an Air Canada A330, was operating as flight AC7064 from Mohammed V Intl - Casablanca (GMMN) to Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl - Montreal (CYUL). After departure the flight crew reported engine #1 EGT fluctuations. The crew discussed with MOC and diverted to Heathrow-London (EGLL) landing uneventfully. As per the PFR ref Ata harness EGT faults, the fault was found on 3005VC green wire harness lug. The lug was replaced and tested, all EGT indications were normal.

C-GEEN, a de Havilland, DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore was conducting flight WEN3439,   from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON to London (CYXU), ON with 4 crew members and 39 passengers on board. During the approach, the flight crew selected FLAP 5 and the flap power and drive caution light illuminated. The flight crew performed a missed approach, actioned the QRH procedures and requested ARFF to be on standby. The aircraft performed an uneventful flapless landing and taxied to the gate.The Operator’s maintenance replaced the FLAP POWER UNIT PRESSURE Switch and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GSPW, un Boeing 737-200 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE704 avec à son bord 4 membres d'équipage et 35 passagers effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de La Grande Rivière, Qc (CYGL). Après 10 minutes de vol de croisière au niveau de vol FL340 avec l’autopilote, l’aéronef a eu un cabrage non commandé. L’équipage a déconnecté l’autopilote et on ressentit une vibration dans les contrôles de vol (buffet). Après avoir repositionné l’aéronef au niveau de vol FL340, ils ont demandé un bloc d’altitude et en réenclenchant l’autopilote, un deuxième cabrage non commandé s’est produit. L’équipage a déconnecté l’autopilote et a demandé à descendre au niveau de vol FL320. Un passager a été blessé légèrement et une ambulance a été demandée à CYGL. Il y avait 2 infirmières à bord qui ont assisté les agents de bord avec le passager blessé. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre à CYGL.Un passager et deux agentes de bord ont été blessés légèrement et une ambulance a été demandée à CYGL.

C-GENK, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3436 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ) ON to Moncton / Greater Moncton Intl (CYQM), NB. During climb out from CYYZ, the windshield on the captain's side cracked. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and returned to CYYZ. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. Maintenance replaced the cracked windshield and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GHUG, a Bell 206L helicopter operated by Sunrise Helicopters, was conducting aerial works flight with chemical spray equipment from a Mix Rig platform, en route for a final spray application. The pilot was watching the chemical load empty light to turn off, indicating tank empty, when the helicopter struck the trees. The helicopter received damage to the fuselage and rotor system. The  pilot was unable to control the aircraft after the impact with trees, and the helicopter impacted the ground. The pilot was not injured but the helicopter was substantially damaged.

C-FUJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation, was conducting flight JZA8600 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Montreal Pierre-Elliott-Trudeau International, QC with 4 crew members and 68 passengers on board . Shortly after takeoff from CYWG, the flight crew received a gear disagree indication due to the nose landing gear not retracting. The flight crew conducted the QRH procedure and, upon completion of the procedure, the landing gear indicator showed three gear lights in the down position. The decision was made to return to CYWG for a landing. To reach landing weight the crew flew for 45 minutes close to CYWG to burn off fuel. An emergency was declared and an uneventful landing was carried out with emergency vehicles standing by. The operator’s maintenance identified that the left and right hand nose landing gear lock sensors were out of rig. Sensors were re-rigged, gear swings and operational system checks were completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FDRH, un appareil de type Airbus A320 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA410 en provenance de Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. N813AE, un Embraer E135 exploité par Envoy Air sous l’indicatif ENY3383 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY à destination de CYUL. Alors que les 2 aéronefs allaient s’établir en finale pour les pistes 24 droite et 24 gauche, l’espacement a été réduit à 2,5 nm sur le plan latéral et 400 pieds sur le plan vertical alors que l'espacement prescrit était de 3 nm ou 1000 pieds.

C-GPPZ, un appareil de type Cessna U206G sur flotteurs exploité par Bel-Air Laurentien Aviation Inc., effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le Lac-à-la-Tortue (CSU7), QC. L’appareil a subi une panne de moteur alors qu’il était en approche finale en direction nord. L’appareil s’est écrasé au sud du lac dans les arbres à environ 1000 pieds du rivage. Le pilote et 1 passager ont subi des blessures mineures, les 4 autres passagers n’ont pas été blessés. L’appareil a subi des dommages substantiels. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée.

C-GSXN, un appareil de type Cessna 172 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue à destination de Drummondville, QC (CSC3). Lors de l’atterrissage, une rafale a déplacé l’appareil vers le côté de la piste. Le pilote a voulu éviter les lumières de piste et s’est posé dans le gazon et a terminé sa course dans un fossé. Le pilote, seul à bord, n’a pas été blessé, mais l’appareil a subi des dommages au moteur, à l’hélice, aux ailes et aux trains d’atterrissage. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée.

C-GKQE, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par Porter Airlines, effectuait le vol POE227 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport d’Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW) à destination de Saint-John, NB (CYSJ, avec 33 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en croisière à environ 130 milles nautiques (nm) de CYOW, le voyant d’avertissement « #1 hyd iso valve » s’est allumé indiquant une perte du système hydraulique. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et a décidé de revenir atterrir à CYOW. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre à 18h18z et a circulé jusqu’au tablier. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FWEP, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3123 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON. The aircraft was at cruise altitude when the flight crew noticed the cabin pressure was rising, and were unable to control it. The flight crew decided to return to CYYZ and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. Maintenance found the Re-heater Inlet Duct damaged. The duct was replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GJIB, an amateur built Searey amphibious aircraft, had taken off from a grass field and was flying over Conestogo Lake taking photographs of the local area. The landing gear was down as the pilot's intentions were to return and land back in the grass field. While flying over the lake the pilot decided to land on the lake, but had not retracted the landing gear. Upon touchdown the aircraft flipped over. Both occupants were rescued and the pilot received minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GJYZ, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting flight PAG107 from Island Lake (CYIV), MB to Sandy Lake (CZSJ), ON with 3 crew members and 17 passengers on board. Shortly after departing CYIV, the aircraft experienced a loss of hydraulic fluid on the #1 hydraulic system. The flight crew contacted the operator's Operational and Maintenance Control Centres, declared an emergency, and diverted to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. The aircraft subsequently landed with flaps up without further incident. The operator's maintenance identified damage to a #1 hydraulic system line. The hydraulic line and the #1 hydraulic pump was replaced.

C-GQJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (CRJ200) aircraft operated by Jazz was conducting flight JZA8627 from Charlottetown (CYYG), PEI to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON. While at the gate and about to depart the Captain was advised by the flight attendant that they were ill and unable to continue with their duties. The flight was cancelled.

C-FEXE, a Cessna 208B aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express, was conducting flight MAL8071 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Victoria Int'l (CYYJ), BC with 1 pilot and cargo on board. MAL8071 commenced taxiing to runway 08R from the uncontrolled apron 4. A Cargojet tug with 4 cargo containers in tow was proceeding in the opposite direction in the vehicle corridor south of apron 4. In the vicinity of taxiway DW, the tug departed the vehicle corridor into apron 4. The tug missed the aircraft but the first cargo container struck the aircraft's left wing. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left wing and associated wing structure. The nighttime weather conditions at the time of the occurrence were rain and 7sm visibility. There were no injuries. There was no post impact fire. The ELT did not activate.

C-FMAI, a Boeing 757-200 aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express, was conducting flight MAL7940 from Jacksonville / Cecil (KVQQ), FL to Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with two crew members on board. En route, the flight crew received high engine vibration indication on the N3 rotor of the left engine, which went into the caution band. In accordance with the non-normal checklist, the flight crew reduced thrust to idle. However, the vibration indication remained in the caution band. In accordance with the checklist, the flight crew shutdown the left engine, declared a Pan Pan, and returned to KVQQ for an uneventful landing.Maintenance found the left engine vibration accelerometer to be faulty.

C-GCLQ, un appareil de type Beech 200 exploité par Sky Jet M.G. Inc., effectuait le vol VSL447 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) à destination de l'aéroport Jean Lesage Intl de Québec, QC (CYQB).À environ 30 nm au nord-est de Rivière-du-Loup, QC (CYRI) le pilote a déclaré une urgence en raison d'un pare-brise fissuré. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre à CYQB. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GHQI, un appareil de type Airbus A321 exploité par Air Canada Rouge, effectuait le vol ROU1686 de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l'aéroport de Charlottetown, PEI (CYYG). Au décollage, l'espacement a été réduit à 2.5nm entre ROU1686 et ENY3903, un Embraer EMB-135 opéré par Envoy Air à destination de l'aéroport New York/LaGuardia, NY (KLGA) alors que l'espacement prescrit était de 3nm. L'espacement vertical a cependant été maintenu.Par conséquent, ENY3903 a été dévié au sud et au nord de l'axe de piste en raison de la turbulence de sillage générée par ROU1686.

C-GHQI, un appareil de type Airbus A321 exploité par Air Canada Rouge, effectuait le vol ROU1883 en provenance de Cancún Intl (MMUN), MX à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. Alors que ROU1883 était en approche à CYUL, il a été viré en base trop serré par le contrôleur aérien ce qui a résulté en une perte d'espacement avec C-FYIY, un Airbus A319 exploité lui aussi par Air Canada Rouge, qui était en approche finale pour la piste 24L. Les appareils se sont rapprochés à 2 nm sur le plan latéral et 800 pieds sur le plan vertical alors que l'espacement prescrit était de 3 nm ou 1000 pieds.

C-FGZE, an MD A4N aircraft operated by Top Aces Inc., was conducting a local flight from Rostock/Laage Airport (ETNL), Germany. On the initial climb at approximately 10000 feet, the "Oil Level High" Light which indicates engine low oil level, started to flicker. The pilot declared an emergency and returned to ETNL via a straight in approach and landed. The light stayed on from the beginning of the approach to the engine shut down. The aircraft has been removed from service for troubleshooting.

C-FGZO, an MD A4N aircraft operated by Top Aces, was conducting a local flight from Laage/Rostock-Laage AB (ETNL), Germany. After approximately 20 minutes of flight, overhead Hohn/Hohn Air Base (ETNH), Germany, the master caution and utility hydraulic lights came on. The pilot completed the checklist and declared an emergency. An airborne visual check was performed by an accompanied aircraft. The aircraft diverted to Wittmund/Wittmundhafen (ETNT), Germany where a precautionary approach end cable arrestment was conducted. The aircraft landed and taxied with no further event.  The aircraft has been removed from service to determine the cause of Master Caution and Utility Hydraulic Light.

C-FTOH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines on behalf of Travel Service Poland was conducting flight TVP747P from Katowice Intl (EPKT), Poland to Warsaw/Frédéric Chopin Intl (EPWA), Poland. During the takeoff roll, an IAS disagree message appeared on both PFDs. The flight crew continued the takeoff. While climbing through 400 feet, the flight crew completed the Airspeed Unreliable memory items and declared a PAN PAN. The QRH checklist was completed and the aircraft returned to EPKT uneventfully. Troubleshooting was carried out in accordance with FIM procedure. LH static ADM, LH AOA sensor, RH EFIS control panel, and both ADIRUS were replaced. The pitot static test was carried out and found satisfactory.

C-GSDX a Bushcaddy R-120 homebuilt aircraft operated by the owner/pilot was conducting a flight from a private lake to New Germany Water aerodrome (CCA2), NS with one pilot and one passenger on board. While on approach to landing the pilot descended early and struck unmarked powerlines crossing the north end of the lake. The aircraft descended into the lake entangled in the powerlines. The occupants suffered serious injuries and were assisted by witness who walked out to the plane as the water was shallow. They were both transported to hospital. Having flown numerous time into that lake, the pilot was familiar with the water aerodrome and aware of the powerlines.

C-FLOZ, a privately operated Zenair CH-701 float equipped amateur built aircraft, departed from Sturgeon Lake, Kawartha Lakes, ON. After the take-off run, the aircraft contacted the tree tops followed by contacting power lines at the intersection of County Road 24 and Scotch Line Road. The aircraft then impacted a ditch adjacent to the intersection. The pilot and 1 passenger were each wearing their 3-point harness and received minor injuries. The aircraft was destroyed.

C-FJVV, a de Havilland  DHC-8-311 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8608 from Sudbury (CYSB) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ). Just prior to descent, a cabin crew member detected a faint, acrid, electrical smell from the area near the cabin door. The flight crew completed an initial inspection, no issues were detected. After landing, the aircraft taxied to the gate where they held short to wait for ground crew to marshal the aircraft in. The cabin crew then detected a faint bluish-grey smoke and notified the flight crew. The flight crew shut the aircraft down, actioned a rapid deplanement and notified emergency services. The 49 passengers were deplaned and escorted into the terminal building. There were no injuries.

C-FJZK, a Boeing 767-3Q8ER, operated by Air Canada Rouge was conducting flight ROU1631 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport (KFLL) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ). While inbound to CYYZ, just prior to descent, the flight crew received an EICAS message pertaining to the aircrafts' antiskid system. The flight crew carried out the applicable QRH items and declared a PAN PAN. The flight landed safely at CYYZ with ARFF standing by.

C-FLRS, a Boeing 737-400 operated by Flair Airlines was conducting flight FLE102 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International (CYYZ), ON to Edmonton International (CYEG), AB.  During cruise, approximately 42 nm southeast of CYEG, the captain experienced a medical issue resulting in incapacitation and was unable to continue his duties. The first officer was given command. The flight continued to its destination without further incident. Emergency Medical Services met the aircraft at the gate to attend to the captain.

C-GHJJ, a Sikorsky S-76A helicopter operated by Helijet International, was conducting flight JBA723 from Vancouver Harbour Heliport (CBC7), BC to Victoria Harbour Heliport (CBF7), BC with 2 pilots and 10 passengers on board. While on approach to CBF7 the crew received an audible engine out warning with N1 oscillations, however there were no secondary indications of engine failure. The crew performed a missed approach, declared a Pan Pan, and diverted to Victoria Int'l (CYYJ), BC. The crew performed a running landing without further incident. The operators maintenance replaced the N1 gauge, associated wiring harness, and N1 sensor. The aircraft has been returned to service.

C-GUBT, an Airbus 330 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC176 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to London/Gatwick Intl (EGKK), United Kingdom. During cruise, in the vicinity of Stony Rapids (CYSF), SK, a cabin crewmember and was unable to continue their duties. The duties were assumed by the rest of the cabin crew.

C-FAVX an Airbus Helicopters AS350-B2, was dropping off work crews at a gravel bar on the side of a creek approximately 20nm S of Drayton Valley Industrial Airport (CER3), AB.  Workers exited both the left and right sides of the helicopter.  The worker on the left side gathered equipment from the left side baggage compartment, then attempted to cross under the tail boom to the right side and tripped and fell into the tail rotor. The worker sustained serious injuries was transported to hospital.

C-FYFA, a privately operated Piper PA32-300, was on a VFR flight from Claresholm Industrial Airport (CEJ4), AB to Edmonton / Twin Island Airpark (CEE6), AB. During the landing on Runway 24, the aircraft overran the runway by 200 feet. The aircraft entered a ditch  and the nose gear collasped breaking the engine mount and damaging the propeller. There were no injuries to the pilot or passenger.

C-FHDJ, a privately operated Cessna 305A, was on a VFR flight from Black Diamond Flying Ranch (CBD8), AB to High River (CEN4), AB.  The aircraft performed a flap 30 short field take off from Runway 08, and carried out gentle a left had turn to the north. Shortly after take-off the aircraft stalled and impacted the ground sustaining substantial damage. The pilot and passenger were seriously injured.

C-GQHU, un Cessna 150M exploité par Richcopter inc., effectuait un vol allé-retour de l'aéroport de Drummondville (CSC3), QC selon les règles de vol à vue avec le pilote et 1 passager à bord. Dans les environs de Saint-Jean-Port-Joli QC, le pilote a affiché 7700 sur le transpondeur et a déclaré une urgence en raison d'une perte de puissance moteur (Teledyne Continental 0-200-A). Le pilote a ensuite effectué avec succès un atterrissage de précaution sur l'autoroute 20 à environ 4 NM à l'est du village de Saint-Jean-Port-Joli. Il n'a pas eu de blessés ni de dommages. Une inspection de maintenance a conclu que du givrage dans le carburateur serait la cause de la perte de puissance.

C-FWOM, a privately registered float-equipped Cessna 180H, was enroute from Gun Lake, ON to Long Lake, ON. Upon reaching Long Lake, the east end of the lake was covered in fog.  The pilot subsequently made an approach to land on the water surface of Long Lake from the west. On short final, the aircraft momentarily entered fog and visual contact with the water surface of the lake was lost. Upon regaining visual contact, the aircraft touched down near the north shoreline. The left float struck the shoreline and the aircraft veered 90 degrees to the left. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to its left float and left wing tip. There were no injuries.The aircraft was transported to a maintenance facility for repair.

C-FXZS, un appareil de type Robinson R44 Raven 1 exploité par Services Hélicocorp Inc. , effectuait un vol privé selon les règles de vol à vue, de St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) à destination de Roberval, QC (CYRJ) avec le pilote  et un passager à bord. À l'approche finale à CYRJ, le moteur (Lycoming O-540-F1B5) a perdu de la puissance et le pilote a alors effectué un atterrissage en autorotation. Lorsque l'appareil a touché sol, le rotor principal est entré en contact avec la poutre de queue. L'aéronef a subi des dommages substantiels. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GTGB, a privately registered Schweizer SGS 2-33A glider, operated by the Air Cadet League Of Canada was being positioned to land and the student pilot had entered the circuit in a wider than normal position. After rolling out on base leg, the student pilot noted that the altitude in relation to the distance to the landing area may be insufficient and turned directly to the landing area. The aircraft did not clear a tree line and landed in a level attitude in the canopy of the trees. The pilot who was the sole occupant was not injured, the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-IEZH, un avion ultra-léger de base de type Cosmos phase 2 effectuait un vol local à partir d'un terrain privé situé le long de la rue Principale Nord à Sacré-Coeur, QC selon les règles de vol à vue, avec seul le pilote à bord. Lors de l'approche en vue de l'atterrissage, l'aéronef a soudainement perdu de l'altitude lors du survol d'un cours d'eau et est alors entré en collision avec le sol. L'aéronef a subi des dommages importants. Le pilote n'a pas été blessé.

C-GJZC, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8898 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Goose Bay (CYYR), NL. Shortly after the departure from CYHZ, the aircraft experienced a loss of number 2 hydraulic system pressure. The crew contacted ATC and requested return to CYHZ. An alternate landing gear extension was required to lower the landing gear, and the crew requested that airport emergency services stand by for the landing. The aircraft landed and taxied to the gate without further incident.

C-FIUR, a Boeing 777 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA883 from Copenhagen Kobenhavn/Kastrup (EKCH), Denmark to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. C-GKEJ, a Bombardier CRJ-200 aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7339 from CYYZ to John Glenn Columbus Intl (KCMH), Ohio. While taxiing for departure at CYYZ, C-GKEJ was instructed by Tower ATC to line up on Runway 33R and was given an amendment to their standard instrument departure (SID). C-FIUR, who just landed on Runway 33L, was instructed by the Ground ATC to cross Runway 33R at Taxiway H in order to taxi to the terminal. While C-FIUR was crossing Runway 33R, C-GKEJ began the take-off roll, without clearance. When the crew of C-GKEJ saw C-FIUR over the crest of the runway, they aborted the take-off, and exited the runway via taxiway Bravo2.

C-GAYF, an amateur built Aerocomp Comp Air 6, was conducting a flight from Bella Bella (CBBC), BC to 108 Mile (CZML), BC with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. The aircraft landed normally but lost directional control and departed the right side of the runway surface. The aircraft came to rest approximately 120 feet from the runway in soft ground. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. There were no injuries. The ELT did not activate.

C-FNJZ, a CL-600-2D24 operated by Jazz as JZA8016, was conducting a flight from Saskatoon Int'l (CYXE), Saskatchewan to Ottawa MacDonald-Cartier Int'l (CYOW), Ontario. During the approach, following the selection of landing gear down, the crew received a 'GEAR DISAGREE' indication. They discontinued the approach while proceeding to manually extend the landing gear, and requesting ARFF to be present for their landing. The flight landed without further incident and taxied off the runway, after which it was towed to the gate as a precaution. Maintenance personnel discovered contamination in the landing gear selector valve connector, which was replaced before returning the aircraft to service.

C-GTWT, an amateur-built North Star, was conducting a VFR flight from Clearwater River (CFS8), AB to Sundre (CFN7), AB with one pilot and one passenger on board. During the initial climb on take-off from Runway 22, just as the aircraft climbed above the tree tops, climb performance diminished to the point where the pilot elected to land straight ahead on the remaining runway. The aircraft landed heavily and ground looped to the right. The aircraft sustained substantial damage but neither occupant was injured.

C-FIYA, a Boeing 767-33AER aircraft operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight RV 1934 from Montréal/Trudeau (CYUL) to Athens (LGAV), Greece. While in cruise flight, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to perform the duties of the position. The cabin crew reassigned tasks and ensured all cabin doors were manned for landing in accordance with company policies and procedures.
C-GURP, a Boeing 787-9, was operating as flight WS2 from Gatwick -London (EGKK) to Calgary Intl - Calgary (CYYC). During cruise a cabin crew member became incapacitated and duties were redistributed.

C-FTOH, a Boeing 737-800 operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight TVS7363 from Faro (LPFR), Portugal to Katowice Intl (EPKT), Poland with 6 crew members and 180 passengers onboard. While refueling before departure, the right main tank was overfilled and fuel spilled out. The ground personnel cleaned up the spill with a fire truck standing by for safety purposes. The aircraft experienced 2 other fuel spills during the taxi. Each time the aircraft returned at the gate and the crew shut down the engines  for clean up and ground maintenance crew examination. Eventually the overflow stopped and the maintenance crew performed fuel balancing of the fuel tanks. The aircraft departed LPFR and proceeded without further incident.

C-GURP, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft, operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WS2 from London Gatwick (EGKK), UK to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB when a cabin crew member experienced an illness. The duties were distributed to the other cabin crew and the flight continued uneventfully.

C-GBZS, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG650 from Frank Pais Intl – Holguin, Cuba (MUHG) Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). While on approach for CYUL, the crew was cleared for an altitude of 5000 feet, and ATC advised of  VFR traffic, a Cessna 210 (NORM10). The flight crew then received a TCAS resolution advisory (RA). Spacing was reduced to 0.4 nm horizontally and 600 feet vertically. The flight crew notified ATC and continued the approach without incident.

N902XS, un Canadair CRJ900 (CL-600-2D24) exploité par Endeavor Air effectuait le vol EDV5503 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Minneapolis-St. Paul/Wold-Chamberlain, MN à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en rapprochement pour CYUL, lors du survol du repère AGNAG l’appareil n’a pas effectué le virage vers le repère TIDAS tel que prescrit et a continué sur son cap. L’espacement avec N513MJ un Canadair CRJ700 (CL-600-2C10) exploité par Mesa Airlines sous l’indicatif ASH6138 qui effectuait un vol depuis Washington Dulles Intl, Washington, DC (KIAD) à destination de CYUL a été réduit à 2.6 nm sur le plan horizontal et 400 pieds sur le plan vertical alors que l’espacement requis était de 3 nm sur le plan horizontal ou 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical.

C-GTSN, un Airbus A330-200 exploité par Air Transat effectuait le vol TSC646 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de l’aéroport Eleftherios Venizelos Intl-Athènes, Grèce (LGAV). Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, l’équipage a reçu une indication de température de la turbine interne excédant les limites. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) et effectué un retour à CYUL. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage.

C-GABP, a De Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8685 from Bagotville, Qc (CYBG) to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). As the aircraft was on approach to Runway 24R at CYUL behind a Boeing 767-300, operated by Air Canada Rouge flight ROU1533 it encountered wake turbulence, followed immediately by an uncommanded 30° roll to the left and an uncommanded roll to the right. The crew notified ATC, and continued the approach without further incident.

C-GSWJ, the WestJet Airlines Boeing 737, operating as WJA585 on a flight from Hamilton (CYHM) to Calgary (CYYC) experienced a cabin crew member incapacitation during the enroute portion. The captain was advised and the duties were distributed to the other cabin crew members for landing.

C-GQLG, the Delta Helicopters Ltd. Bell 205A, was on a flight from Steen River, AB (CFB7) to Petitot Forestry Tower, AB, with an externally slung net load of building blocks. Approximately 45 nm short of the forestry tower the net split and the load was lost. The pilot circled back but could not find the blocks in the bush. The flight continued to the forestry tower and the loss was reported to the client and operations. The longline and hook equipment was inspected and found to be in good condition. The damaged net was removed from service and returned to the base in High Level.

ASQ4228, an Embraer 145 operated by ExpressJet, was conducting a flight from Toronto/Pearson Int'l (CYYZ), Ontario, to Newark/Liberty Int'l (KEWR). Approximately ten minutes after departure the flight crew declared an emergency with ATC due to AC PACK 1 blowing hot air, and requested a return to CYYZ. Priority was given and ASQ4228 landed at 1041 EDT with ARFF standing by.

C-GVWA, the WestJet Boeing 737-800, operating as WJA660, was on a flight from Calgary (CYYC) to Toronto (CYYZ). During take-off the flight crew observed engine indications that would suggest a bird strike. The crew elected to return to CYYC, declared an emergency, and landed safely shortly thereafter; ARFF was in attendance for the landing. Company maintenance observed damage to the fan blades on the #1 engine ((CFM56-7B27/E).

C-FNVV, the Air Canada Airbus A320, operating as ACA151 on a flight from Toronto (CYYZ) to Calgary (CYYC) received multiple ECAM messages related to low hydraulic levels for the yellow system. In discussions with maintenance the decision was made to continue to CYYC, a PAN PAN was declared and on landing the aircraft was met by emergency vehicles. The landing was uneventful. Maintenance determined that the yellow hydraulic HP manifold was leaking. A replacement unit was installed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FENU, the WestJet Encore De Havilland Dash 8-400, operating as WEN3193 on a flight from Saskatoon (CYXE) to Calgary (CYYC) experienced a yaw to the left on departure. Suspecting a blown tire the captain elected to continue to the destination and requested ARFF to attend the landing. No May Day or Pan Pan was declared. Maintenance inspected the wheels on landing and no fault was found.

C-GCTS, an Airbus 330-300 operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC111 from Charles de Gaulle (LFPG) Paris to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. During the climb though 14000 feet, the cabin crew noted smoke emanating from the mid-galley oven. The flight crew was advised, the fire was extinguished by the cabin crew; a Mayday call was made with a return to LFPG. The flight landed uneventfully. The aircraft was met by fire crews after landing; 21 passengers and 2 crew members were treated on the scene by local emergency services and company maintenance is investigating.

C-FKCN, the Canadian North Boeing 737-300, was operating as MPE1720 on a flight from Edmonton (CYEG), AB to Fort MacKay/Horizon (CYNR), AB. While descending to 6000 feet, a traffic advisory call was made on the North Oil Sands ATF (123.5 MHz), 48 nm south of CYNR, and no aircraft responded. As MPE1720 continued to descend through 8000 feet, in visual meteorological conditions, MPE1720 cancelled IFR services and shortly thereafter a target appeared on the TCAS display. The target appeared to be right below MPE1720 by 400 feet and climbing. The flight crew then responded to a TCAS RA command and began to climb. As they climbed the flight crew achieved visual contact with a float plane out of the right side window.

C-FMJO, a Viking DHC-6 Series 400 Twin Otter on amphibious floats, operated by Pacific Sky Aviation Inc. was conducting a flight from Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Ottawa/Gatineau Airport (CYND), QC. On approach to CYND, the crew received a landing gear unsafe indication. The crew then declared an emergency and elected to divert to Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier Int'l Airport (CYOW), ON where the aircraft landed safely with ARFF standing by.

C-FWTT, a privately owned Pitts S-1T, was landing at Warren Field (CWF3), Ontario, a grass strip west of London, Ontario. The aircraft landed near the edge of the grass surface, and the wing made contact with corn growing alongside the runway. The aircraft was pulled into the cornfield where it nosed over and came to rest inverted. The aircraft was significantly damaged, the pilot was uninjured.

C-ILLE, the Quad City Challenger II Advanced Ultra Light (Amphibious) aircraft, was in cruise when the left cockpit door opened resulting in the aircraft entering a slow uncontrolled roll. The pilot was able to return to the lake but struck the water surface in a non level attitude. The aircraft was substantially damaged and the pilot, who was wearing a four point safety belt, received minor injuries.

C-GXJA, a Bombardier CL- 600-2B19 (CRJ) aircraft, operated by Air Georgian Ltd., was conducting flight GGN 7384 from Lambert Intl - St. Louis (KSTL) to Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto  (CYYZ). During cruise, in the vicinity of Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International - Covington (KCVG), the flight crew noted a right oil pressure low status. The engine was shut down, and an emergency declared with a diversion to KCVG. Maintenance found that the oil line was chafed.

C-FRBG, un Piper Cub en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à destination de l’aérodrome de La Sarre, QC (CSR8), avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait dans la région de Val Paradis, QC, une défaillance du moteur est survenue et le pilote a effectué un atterrissage d’urgence sur la route. Peu après le posé des roues, l’aile droite a percuté un arbre et l’appareil a fait quelques tonneaux avant de terminer sa course dans un fossé. L’appareil a subi des dommages importants et il n’y a pas eu d’incendie. Le pilote a subi des blessures mortelles, et le passager a été grièvement blessé.

C-GUFV, a Robinson R44 helicopter operated by Apex Helicopters, was conducting aerial spray operations when the pilot observed a power line in the path of the helicopter. The helicopter had been flying East at the time, and the sun was low and obscuring the pilots' forward vision to some degree. The tail of the helicopter made contact with a power line during an avoidance maneuver. The pilot made an immediate emergency landing in a field, and substantial damage to the skids, floor structure, and tail of the helicopter occurred, with the tail rotor becoming separated from the helicopter. The pilot was the sole occupant, and was uninjured. The ELT activated.

C-GEYP, a Cessna150M collided with terrain under unknown circumstances when the airplane struck trees in the vicinity of Roundup Airport, Roundup, MT (KRPX). The pilot, the sole occupant, was hospitalized with serious injuries; the aircraft was substantially damaged. The NTSB investigated (WPR19LA213).

N510MJ, the Mesa Airlines CL-600-2C10 (ASH6197) was on initial climb out from Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) when the flight crew received a GEAR DISAGREE EICAS message and was unable to retract landing gear. The flight crew declared an emergency and returned to CYYZ and landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The operator's maintenance placed the landing gear on MEL, pinned it in the down position, and the aircraft flew back to their maintenance facility in Washington Dulles Intl (KIAD) with landing gear extended.

C-GGMI, a Dehavilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA 8238 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Terrace (CYXT), BC with 4 crew members and 78 passengers on board.
