Shortly after takeoff, the flight crew observed a FWD baggage door warning light. The flight crew actioned the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH), and advised ATC. The flight crew requested ARFF as a precaution. The aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-GTAG, a Dehavilland DHC-8-301 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, had just completed the start sequence for the second engine for a scheduled flight (JZA 8519) from Sandspit, BC (CYZP) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 3 crew members and 45 passengers on board when the flight attendant noticed smoke in the middle of the passenger cabin. The flight attendant notified the flight crew; the crew opened the door and commenced a rapid de-planement. The passengers and crew exited the aircraft uneventfully. The fire department attended and did not find any hot spots. Maintenance personnel carried out engine runs as per the AMM, both air conditioning packs and pressurization function checks were completed with no faults noted. A test flight was carried out and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FMLV, an Air Canada rouge B767, was conducting flight ROU 1901 from Eleftherios Venizelos Intl (LGAV) Athens to Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ) Toronto. At approximately 300 nm of Dublin Intl (EIDW), in the vicinity of the SPY VOR/DME (SPIKJKERBOOR), NL, the crew received a HYD quantity ECAIS message. The checklist was actioned, a PAN PAN advised, and the crew intended to divert to Heathrow International (EGLL). EGLL would not accept the flight unless the crew declared a Mayday. Instead, the crew elected to divert to EIDW and landed uneventfully.

C-GOVT, a Rockwell Commander 695A operated by the Province of Saskatchewan as flight BD167, landed on runway 26 at Prince Albert/Glass Field (CYPA), SK with only the pilot on board. After turning off the runway onto taxi way Delta, the nose gear collapsed. The aircraft came to a sudden stop and the engines were then shut down. There were no injuries and the aircraft sustained substantial damage. The aircraft was removed from the taxi way and taken to the tanker base. The operator will advise of their findings.

C-GMHT, a Bell 206L helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters Ltd, was conducting forest fire control operations near Pasadena, NL. The pilot attached the water bucket to the hook and proceeded to pick up a bucket of water. The water would not release when the water release button was pressed. After landing and checking that the cables were not tangled, the pilot departed and decided to check if the release would work, but hit the cargo release button instead. The water bucket released and fell into a pond. It was later determined that the water release button was incorrectly wired.

C-GMWT, a privately registered de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG852 from Opapimiskam Lake (CKM8), ON to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON.  On approach into CYQT, the flight crew selected landing gear down and received an abnormal landing gear light indication. An emergency was declared, and the flight crew requested a visual inspection from ATC. The landing gear was observed in the fully extended position; however, the normal landing gear indicator light remained abnormal. Various attempts to troubleshoot the landing gear was made; the flight crew selected an alternate gear extension and received 3 green lights on the alternate gear extension light indicator. An uneventful landing was subsequently carried out with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance replaced pins and sockets at the left-hand down-lock switch cannon plug. Gear swings were carried out and a successful test flight was made. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FDRP, an Airbus A320 operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA757 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to San Francisco Intl (KSFO), CA with 5 crew members and 146 passengers onboard. The flight was operated with the pack number 1 inoperative under the MEL. During cruise, in the vicinity of Denver Intl (KDEN), CO, the flight crew noticed the cabin altitude was climbing. The flight crew initiated a descent to lower altitude and declared a Mayday. During the descent, the cabin altitude stabilized and the flight was diverted to Salt Lake City Intl (KSLC), UT for an uneventful landing. During the occurrence, the cabin altitude did not exceed 9600 feet, and no oxygen masks were deployed. There were no injuries.

C-FOJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA 8737 from Saskatoon Intl (CYXE), SK to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 4 crew members and 59 passengers on board. While in cruise flight, the flight crew observed a flap caution fail message. The flight crew actioned the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH), advised the Air Traffic Controller and declared a Pan Pan. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYVR.Maintenance personnel reset circuit breakers L5 and R1, operational test and ground test were carried out and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FBFB, a Aerospatiale AS355N aircraft operated by Blackcomb Helicopters, was conducting a hydro line inspection approximately 5 nm west south west of Squamish (CYSE), BC with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the return flight to CYSE the left engine chip light caution illuminated. The pilot established one engine inoperative (OEI) flight and shutdown the Left engine. The passengers were briefed, and the companies operation dispatchers were notified. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYSE.

C-FEKD, a Sky Regional Airlines Embraer E175, was conducting flight 7611 from Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ) Toronto to O'Hare Intl (KORD Chicago. During the landing on RWY 27R KORD the aircraft encountered a hard landing on touchdown. Emergency services were not required and the flight taxied to the gate under its own power. On walk-around, the crew observed damage to the tail and maintenance was advised. There was damage to the lower rear section of the fuselage. A damage assessment for the tail strike is being carried out by maintenance in KORD along with a Phase 2 hard landing inspection. A more complete report will be provided upon completion of their inspections.

C-GITS, an Airbus 330-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC309 from Leonardo da Vinci Intl. (LIRF), Rome to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON with 11 crew members and 305 passengers on board. During cruise, a cabin crew member sustained an injury and was unable to perform their duties. Cabin safety positions were reassigned, and the flight landed without incident.

C-GFDD, a privately registered, float-equipped, Murphy Rebel amateur built aircraft, departed Freshwater Pond near Marystown, Newfoundland and Labrador, for a local flight as part of the flight time required for the issuance of a special certificate of airworthiness following the aircraft’s construction. The pilot intended to conduct landings on various local bodies of water (ponds) before returning to Freshwater Pond. When the aircraft was in the initial climb following a touch-and-go at Grandys Pond, the pilot experienced aileron control difficulty. The pilot declared a mayday and then attempted to land straight ahead in a bog. Upon landing, the aircraft flipped over and came to rest upside down. The pilot was the sole occupant on board, and was not injured. Another pilot, who had heard the mayday call, came to assist the occurrence pilot. The aircraft was destroyed. A post-accident inspection revealed that a rod end bearing had fractured and separated, causing a discontinuity in the aileron flight control system.UPDATED: 17 March 2021

C-GFXK, a Piper PA-28-140 aircraft operated by the Calgary-Okotoks Flying School, was conducting a training flight from Calgary/Okotoks Air Park (CFX2), AB to CFX2 with one instructor pilot and one student pilot onboard. After take-off from Runway 34, at approximately 150 feet AGL, the aircraft experienced a substantive loss of engine (AVCO LYCOMING, O-320-E3D) performance. The instructor pilot took control of the aircraft and elected to perform a forced landing straight ahead into an agriculture field. There were no injuries reported to either pilot.

C-GOHJ, un appareil de type British Aerospace HS125 exploité par Hawker Limited Partnership effectuait un vol entre l'aéroport de Port-Menier, QC (CYPN) et l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). À 40Nm au sud-ouest de Québec, QC, celui-ci été autorisé et a relu correctement de descendre au FL280. C-GOHJ a poursuivi sa descente sous le FL280. Conséquemment, l'espacement entre C-GOHJ et N506KB, un Raytheon B300, qui effectuait un vol de Manassas Regional Airport/Harry P. Davis Field(KHEF) à destination de Goose Bay au Labrador (CYYR) a été réduit à 3NM et 800 pieds alors qu'il aurait dû être de 5NM ou 1000 pieds.

C-GTJL, a Learjet 35A operated by Sunwest Aviation Inc., was on a flight from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Calgary (CYYC), AB. While in cruise, the flight crew observed that the right hand thrust reverser (TR) "UNLOCK" light had illuminated. They did not initially notice any yaw and it did not feel like the TR had deployed. While the flight crew were reviewing the abnormal checklist, they were cleared to descend to 15 000 feet at their discretion. As part of the descent checklist, the TR test button was selected and they noticed the aircraft momentarily yawed to the right. After a brief moment, the aircraft yawed even harder to the right, to approximately 20-30 degrees. The flight crew responded by selecting idle thrust on the right engine, declared a PAN PAN, and actioned the abnormal checklist for "Inadvertent Thrust Reverser Deployment In Flight". They completed the abnormal checklist and the TR unlock light remained illuminated, so the right engine (Garrett, TFE731-2-2B) was shutdown in accordance with the checklist. A single-engine approach and landing was completed into CYYC without further issue.Company maintenance has ordered a replacement pneumatic latch control valve and solenoid.

C-GLQN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE616 from Timmins/Victor M. Power (CYTS), ON to Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON. During the approach to CYTZ, the flight crew encountered a hydraulic issue, declared PAN PAN, and elected to divert to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ), where they landed without incident.

C-GMDC un Viking DHC-6 exploité par Air Inuit circulait sur le tablier de l'aéroport de Kangirsuk, QC (CYAS), guidé par du personnel au sol afin de se garer derrière un DHC-8 d'Air Inuit stationné aux bornes de carburant lorsque l'aile gauche de C-GMDC a frappé le gouvernail de direction de C-FEAI. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés. Les deux appareils n'ont subi que des dommages mineurs. Il n'y a eu aucun déversement de carburant.

C-FNOI, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA836 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Madrid/Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Intl (LEMD), Spain with 10 crew members and 251 passengers on board. After departure from CYYZ, the flight crew received an EICAS message indicating low tire pressure on wheel no 6. After consultation with maintenance, the flight continued to LEMD, where a Pan Pan was declared for the deflated tire. The flight landed uneventfully. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft. The no 6 tire was found to be punctured and replaced.

C-GORI, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Service (EVAS), was conducting flight EV7777 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Fredericton Intl (CYFC), NB. On final, ATC advised the crew of traffic in the area. The crew could not locate the traffic and received a TCAS warning for traffic with a resolution to climb. The crew complied by climbing, advised ATC and landed without further incident.

C-GURP, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft, operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WS5 from Dublin Intl (EIDW), Ireland to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB when a cabin crew member sustained a minor injury. The duties were distributed to the other cabin crew and the flight continued uneventfully.

C-FNAJ, un appareil de type Embraer ERJ 190-100 IGW exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA 746 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, de l'aéroport New York/LaGuardia, NY (KLGA) à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 92 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée, l'équipage de conduite a noté des vibrations du moteur droit (GE CF-34-10E5A1). La puissance du moteur a été amenée au ralenti. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'équipage a demandé un retour à CYUL où l'appareil s'est posé sans problème à 1832Z. Une fois au sol, le message ''ENGINE FAIL'' est apparu sur l'EICAS. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés. Une inspection au sol n'a révélé aucun dommage apparent, mais un grincement pouvait se faire entendre lors de la rotation du moteur. Le moteur devra être changé.

C-GJVW, the Perimeter Aviation Fairchild SA227-DC aircraft (384) was on route from Thunder Bay airport (CYQT) to Sault Ste Marie (CYAM) at FL190 when the crew received a #2 ENGINE FIRE WARNING.  Although there were no visible signs of fire or smoke the crew shut down the engine as a precaution. The aircraft continued to CYAM where it landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. ARFF inspected the aircraft and found no evidence of fire and the aircraft to continue to the gate.

C-GFDI, a de Havilland DHC-2 aircraft operated by Harbour Air, was being refueled with Jet A fuel by dock staff at Tofino Harbour (CAB4), BC. During refueling, the pilot realized that the aircraft was being fuelled with the incorrect fuel. The fuelling procedure was stopped. Consequently, the center and rear fuel tanks contained Jet A fuel. The aircraft was repositioned using the front fuel tank to the operator's maintenance base at Vancouver Harbour (CYHC), BC with only the pilot on board. The operator's maintenance drained the center and rear fuel tanks. The center and rear fuel tanks were flushed with avgas including the fuel lines and fuel strainers. Fuel was drained at the fuel strainers to remove remnants of jet fuel. Fuel tanks and strainers were cleaned in accordance with DHC-2 Maintenance Manual (MM) Section 5.14.3. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FGDT, the Air Canada Boeing 787-900 aircraft (AC85) was at the top of descent when the flight crew received fault messages for left brakes, thrust reverser, and nose wheel bypass systems INOP. The flight continued the descent and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed uneventfully Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) with ARFF standing by. Maintenance replaced the #3 Remote Data Concentrator, and subsequent tests revealed no further faults.

C-FJNX, the Air Canada Airbus A321 aircraft (AC785) was on the climb out from Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) when the crew received a "HYD G RSVR LO LVL" ECAM message. QRH procedures were followed, the aircraft returned to CYYZ and flight crew requested ATC to have ARFF standing by for the landing. The aircraft landed uneventfully and was towed to the gate due to inoperative steering. Maintenance determined that the high pressure fitting on the #1 EDP was leaking allowing hydraulic fluid to leak out. The seals were replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GNZF, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B2 helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters Ltd, was conducting long lining operations near Wabush airport (CYWK), NL. While long lining a portable drill, 6 wooden floor boards, which were screwed to the frame of the drill, ripped away during flight. The 10X2X4 ft boards fell in a lake about 10 nm NE of CYWK. The flight continued uneventfully.

C-GJLZ, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1417, from Orlando Intl. (KMCO), FL to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB with 6 crew members and 156 passengers on board. In cruise at approximately 150 nm from Nashville Intl. airport (KBNA), the cabin crew reported the smell of fumes in the cabin. The flight crew conducted the checklist for smoke/fire/fumes and the smell dissipated. The flight crew decided to divert to KBNA where the aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance personnel found no fault with the aircraft, and aircraft was returned to service.

At 1101 Pacific Daylight Time on 06 August 2019, the Alkan Air Ltd. Cessna 208B Grand Caravan aircraft (registration C-FSKF, serial number 208B0673) departed Rau Strip, Yukon, on a visual flight rules company flight itinerary to Mayo Airport, Yukon. The aircraft had 1 pilot, 1 passenger, and cargo on board. At 1113, the aircraft entered instrument meteorological conditions and struck rising terrain in a box canyon shortly after. The crash occurred approximately 25 nautical miles east-northeast of Mayo Airport, at an elevation of 5500 feet above sea level. The Canadian Mission Control Centre did not receive a signal from the aircraft’s 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter. Eyewitnesses from a nearby exploration camp arrived at the site after approximately 1 hour. Royal Canadian Mounted Police and emergency medical services arrived on site approximately 90 minutes after the accident. The pilot and passenger received fatal injuries. The aircraft was destroyed; there was a brief post-impact fire.Updated 20 August 2020

HB-JMF, an Airbus A340-300 aircraft operated by Edelweiss Air, conducted flight SWR8010 from Zurich (LSZH), Switzerland to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. Upon arrival at gate 64, HB-JMF was marshalled into the gate area, signaled to stop and set the parking brake. The engines were shut down. The ground personnel connected a tug and were preparing to tow the aircraft to the final gate parking position. Meanwhile, C-GHPU, an Air Canada Boeing 787-800 aircraft operating flight AC566 from CYVR to San Francisco Intl (KSFO), CA was taxiing westbound on JA taxiway, abeam gate 64, when the left wing tip contacted the tail section of HB-JMF. There were no injuries. Both aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GBUD, a Cessna C-172 operated by Pacific Flying Club, was conducting a flight from Vancouver/Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC to Williams Lake (CYWL), BC. C-FLOR, a Beech C90A aircraft operated by Air West Charters, was conducting a flight from Calgary/Springbank (CYBW) to CZBB. A loss of separation occurred 53 NM NE of CZBB when C-GBUD was cruising at 9000 feet and C-FLOR descended below the cleared altitude of 11,000 feet. The separation between the 2 aircraft reduced to approximately 3.5 NM laterally and 500 feet vertically, when the required separation minima was 5 NM or 1000 feet.

C-GAXW, a Bell 206L-3 helicopter operated by Highland Helicopters Ltd, was conducting heli-slinging operations 9 nm NE of Debolt (CFG4), AB. Tree planting garbage was being loaded into nets on the ground while the helicopter, which was attached to the load, hovered off to the side. The electrical mechanism for the aircraft hook was inadvertently released, which resulted in the end of the line landing approximately 25 feet from the person on the ground. No injuries to personnel or aircraft damage was reported.

C-GPPJ, a privately operated Van's RV-6A was departing Saint John (CYSJ), NB for local circuits. During takeoff from Runway 05, as the aircraft reached approximately 60 knots, it began to track left and then departed the runway surface. The aircraft bounced several times before entering tall grass and overturning. When first responders arrived, the aircraft was lifted enough to facilitate extracting the pilot who was the sole occupant. The pilot had serious, but non-life threatening injuries and was transported to hospital by ambulance. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GTQB, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was operating flight TSC772 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Int'l (CYUL), QC with 178 passengers and 6 crew members on board. The aircraft taxied on taxiway Lima for departure on runway 08R. As TSC772 contacted the controller and advised that they were ready for departure, the aircraft was taxied past the hold short line. The air traffic controller instructed TSC772 to hold short of runway 08R and the aircraft read back the instruction. The aircraft stopped approximately 40 meters past the hold short line. Post incident examination found that there is a discrepancy in the location of the hold short line for runway 08R at Lima on the LIDO and Canada Air Pilot taxi chart compared to the physical location at the airport. TSC772 was referencing the LIDO taxi chart at the time of the occurrence and expected the hold short line to be closer to the runway. CYVR has input the issue into their SMS for review.

C-GTAT, a De Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8734 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Iles-de-la-Madeleine (CYGR), QC. When the crew extended the gear for landing, they initially received the 3 green indication, but then the nose gear started to retract and cycle. The crew executed a missed approach and performed an alternate gear extension. The crew did not declare an emergency but requested ARFF to be on standby. The aircraft landed uneventfully and was towed off the runway. Maintenance is investigating.

On 4 August 2019, a privately registered Cessna 185 E aircraft, equipped with amphibious floats, departed the runway at Orillia Ramara Regional Airport (CNJ4), Ontario, destined to Upper Raft Lake, located approximately 48 nm to the north of CNJ4 and the co-located Orillia/Lake St. John Water Aerodrome, with 7 people on board. During the landing, when the aircraft touched down on the surface of the water, it flipped over and came to rest in an inverted position. The aircraft sustained substantial damage; it was submerged in the water, but held afloat by the aircraft floats. The landing gear, which is normally up for a water landing, was observed to be in the down position. The 6 passengers egressed the aircraft and sustained minor injuries; the pilot was fatally injured. The aircraft was equipped with an emergency locater transmitter (ELT); however, no signal was received at the time of the occurrence by alerting services. The TSB investigated.

C-GKUK, a Jazz Aviation de Havilland DHC-8-402, was operating IFR flight JZA4592 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Saskatoon (CYXE), SK with 4 crew and 70 passengers onboard. On vectored descent into CYXE, C-GKUK was instructed by the terminal controller to descend and maintain 7000 feet ASL heading 040. A few moments later C-FWSX, a WestJet Boeing B737-700 operating as flight WJA452 travelling from CYYC to CYXE parallel to JZA4592, was cleared 6000ft heading 040. Soon after, WJA452 was instructed to turn to 020 degrees, slow to 230 knots and maintain 7000 feet.  Through 8000 feet, WJA452 was instructed to turn further left 360 degrees. Subsequently, JZA4592 was instructed to fly 120 degrees to intercept the inbound course for RNAV Z 09 approach. A loss of separation occurred when the arriving aircraft were approximately 24 nm west of CYXE. Minimum separation between the two flights was reduced to 2.3 nm laterally and 600 feet, where separation required is 3 NM or 1000 feet.  Separation was regained when the controller instructed WJA452 to climb and maintain 9000. WJA452 had received a TCAS traffic advisory but no resolution advisory (RA).

C-GDGK, un appareil de construction amateur de type Zenair CH701 effectuait un vol local  selon les règles de vol à vue, de Lachute, QC (CSE4) avec seul le pilote à bord. Au décollage de de CSE4, le moteur de l'aéronef (Jabiru 2200A) a commencé à avoir de ratées. Le pilote a décidé d'atterrir sur un banc de sable situé à l'est de l'embouchure de la Rivière Rouge. Après une vérification sommaire et un essai moteur au sol le pilote a alors décidé de redécoller du banc de sable afin de tenter un retour à CSE4. Au décollage le moteur a eu de nouvelles ratées et a perdu de la puissance. Le pilote a tenté de revenir atterrir sur le banc de sable, mais l'aéronef a perdu de la vitesse lors d'un virage vers la droite pour ensuite s'écraser dans une zone boisée. Le pilote, légèrement blessé s'est extirpé de justesse alors que le feu envahissait l'appareil.

C-FDCH, a Sikorsky S-61N helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters, was conducting a flight at an international location with 3 crew members and 2 passengers on board. As the helicopter started to ground taxi, the crew heard 3 bangs and the engine number 2 started to spool back. The crew reduced the engine power to idle and conducted an engine shutdown; then the crew shut down the helicopter and called maintenance.The operator’s maintenance installed a new engine and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FXLH, a Voyageur Airways CL-600-2B19 (CRJ 200) aircraft was conducting flight AG508 from Curacao/Hato Intl (TNCC), Willemstad to Reina Beatrix Intl (TNCA), Aruba. On departure, during a left climbing turn, at approximately 1500 feet, the flight crew heard a loud bang followed by vibrations in the airframe. It was identified as an R ENGINE SEVERE DAMAGE with indications of excessive ITT displayed in the engine monitoring page. The affected engine was shut down and the flight returned to TNCC where an emergency was declared. After landing, ARFF inspected the right hand engine and confirmed there were no obvious signs of damage, smoke or fire. Minor damage in the aft section of the right engine was later observed.

On 29 July 2019, the Beechcraft Bonanza V35B aircraft (U.S. registration N3804X, serial number D-10358) departed Wittman Regional Airport, Wisconsin, U.S., for a daytime visual flight rules flight to Danbury Municipal Airport, Connecticut, U.S., with only the pilot on board. While enroute to Danbury Municipal Airport, the pilot deviated north of his planned route and into Canadian airspace. At 1912 Eastern Standard Time, while in the vicinity of a line of rain showers, thunderstorms and lightning, the aircraft entered a right turn, descended rapidly and collided with terrain approximately 7 nautical miles northeast of Senneterre, Quebec. At 2331, the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre in Trenton, Ontario, was notified of a missing aircraft and initiated search-and-rescue operations. The accident site was found 4 days later, on 02 August 2019. The pilot was fatally injured. The aircraft was destroyed. There was no post-impact fire. No signal was detected from the aircraft’s emergency locator transmitter.

C-FIVW, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA008 from Hong Kong/Chek Lap Kok Intl (VHHH), Hong Kong to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 17 crew members and 442 passengers on board. On departure, the flight crew noted an EGT exceedance indication on No. 2 engine, and heard a popping noise. The flight crew were also advised by ATC that some debris had been found on the runway, and after discussion with maintenance, the aircraft returned to VHHH for an uneventful landing. There were no injuries to passenger. The aircraft received minor damage. Maintenance investigation is in progress.

The Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service Airbus H145 (MBB-BK117 D-2) helicopter, C-FLCI, was on a flight from Calgary Foothills (CMT3), AB to Calgary International (CYYC), AB when the flight crew experienced limited cyclic control while on a one mile final. The pilot flying aborted the approach and declared an emergency. On the go-around the crew noticed an electronic flight bag (EFB - tablet) had moved into a position to limit cyclic movement. It was secured and cyclic movement was restored. ATC was advised and a successful landing was completed.

C-FKOJ an Airbus 320 aircraft operated by Air Canada was conducting flight AC702 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY with 5 crew members and 146 passengers on board. During the approach at KLGA, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to descend. The instructions were followed and the aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-GFII, an amateur built privately operated Falconer F11 aircraft, was operating from a private grass strip located 10 nm south of the Moncton/Roméo LeBlanc Intl airport (CYQM), NB. While conducting a high-speed taxi, the aircraft became airborne. After realizing that rejecting the takeoff would result in contact with terrain, the pilot elected to continue. Once airborne, the aircraft impacted the top of trees, which resulted in the aircraft rotating and turning upside down. The pilot, the sole occupant on board, evacuated the aircraft uninjured. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GIHQ, un appareil de type Rockwell Commander 112TC avec à son bord un pilote détenant une licence de pilote privé-avion et un instructeur de vol effectuait des posés-décollés à l'aéroport Québec/Jean-Lesage Int (CYQB), QC. Dans le cadre du dernier atterrissage, l'instructeur de vol a simulé une panne du moteur alors que l'aéronef était en approche finale. L'appareil a poursuivi la descente planée vers la piste 29, mais la sortie du train d'atterrissage a été omise. L'appareil s'est posé sur le ventre et a subi des dommages importants. Les deux occupants n'ont pas été blessés.

C-ILIM un aéronef de type ultra-léger de base (paramoteur) effectuait une manoeuvre à basse altitude dans le secteur de Carignan, QC lorsque la voilure du paramoteur a touché le sol. Une perte de maitrise s'en est suivi. Le pilote seul à bord a subi des blessures sérieuses. Les dommages exacts de l'aéronef sont inconnus pour l'instant.

C-GFPA un aéronef de type Cessna 152 exploité par Grondin Transport Inc. avec à son bord un élève-pilote effectuait des posés-décollés à l'aéroport St-Frédéric, QC. Lors de l'arrondi pour l'atterrissage l'aéronef a dévié à gauche de l'aire d'atterrissage. En ramenant l'aéronef vers l'axe de piste l'aile droite a touché le sol. L'aéronef a été ramené sur l'axe de piste et a poursuivi son atterrissage. L'élève-pilote n'a subi aucune blessure. L'aéronef a subi des dommages importants à l'aile droite.

C-GZOX un Dassaut-Breguet Falcon 20 avec à son bord 2 membres d'équipage et 5 passagers effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON à destination de Mary River, NU. Alors que l'appareil était au FL370 environ 156 milles nautiques au nord de La Grande-Rivière (CYGL), QC, le moteur gauche (GARRET TFE731-5BR-2C) s'est arrêté. L'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence et demandé un déroutement vers CYGL où l'appareil s’est posé sans difficulté. Personne n'a été blessé. La compagnie est à investiguer la cause de l'arrêt du moteur.

C-GPZP, a privately operated, float-equipped DHC2 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Vancouver Int’l (CAM9), BC to Ruby Lake, BC with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. During cruise, the aircraft experienced engine (Pratt and Whitney R-985-AN-14B) power loss, declared an emergency, and forced landed approximately 3nm south of Sechelt (CAP3), BC. The aircraft sustained substantial damage and became submerged underwater. All occupants sustained minor injuries. The ELT activated.The cause of the engine power loss has not been undetermined.

C-GCGB, a Star Helicopters Ltd. Bell 212, was conducting forest fire fighting operations 92 nm NW of Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB with one pilot on board. While in the hover just prior to touch down, the tail rotor struck a tree damaging one tail rotor blade. The pilot landed the helicopter without further issues.

C-FEUO, a Cessna 172 aircraft operated by Super T Management Ltd. was on a night cross-country flight from Medicine Hat (CYXH), AB to Calgary Springbank (CYBW), AB to Hanna (CEL4), AB and then return to CYXH. On the approach into CEL4, the private pilot decided to commence a go-around and try another approach. On the go-around, control of the aircraft was lost. The aircraft crashed on airport property and a small fire erupted. The pilot was able to exit the aircraft with minor injuries and called for help; police, fire, and EMS attended the scene. The 406 ELT activated and was detected by overflying aircraft, as well as the Joint Rescue Coordination Center (JRCC). The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FNNQ a Boeing B777-300  aircraft operated by Air Canada was conducting flight AC880 from Charles de Gaulle (LFPG) Paris to Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ) Toronto. During the push back at LFPG, the tow bar fuse broke. The ground personnel agent tried to remove the tow bar, however the aircraft moved forward and the tow bar hit the agent, who sustained serious injuries. There was no damage to the aircraft. The Bureau d’Enquêtes et d’Analyse pour la sécurité de l’aviation civile (BEA) is investigating this accident.The final draft report has been received and saved in Izone Nov 5, 2020. the comments from AC have been sent to the IIC by AC. They are saved in iZone 1.6.5. waiting for the final report.

C-FJQD, an Airbus A321-211 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge LP was conducting flight ROU1536 from Toronto Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL. During cruise at FL350, 35 nm NW of Halifax Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS the flight crew received a fault message of an aircraft air conditioning PAC fault 1 and 2. One of the PACs was already deferred as per the MEL and the subsequent fault caused a loss of pressurization. The crew conducted the required checklists, declared a PAN PAN, and requested a descent and a diversion into CYHZ where it landed without incident.

C-FVRT un Astar 350 B2 exploité par Héli-Inter Inc. s'apprêtait à atterrir au camp Bélanger situé environ 17 milles nautiques au sud-ouest de Salluit, QC afin d'y faire embarquer deux travailleurs. Lors de l'atterrissage le rotor de queue a frappé le sol. Le pilote seul à bord n'a pas été blessé. Le rotor de queue et sa boite de transmission ont été changés. Un permis de vol de convoyage a été émis afin de ramener l'appareil à un centre de service pour examen.

C-GJZC un appareil de type DHC-8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif de vol JZA7974 avec à son bord 4 membres d'équipage et 36 passagers effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport Billy Bishop Toronto City/Toronto, ON à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL) QC. Peu avant de débuter la descente l'équipage de conduite a observé la panne du système hydraulique numéro 1. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil s'est posé sans volets sur la piste 24R de CYUL. L'appareil a par la suite été remorqué jusqu'à la passerelle de débarquement.

C-FTXJ, un Canadair CL-215 exploité par le service aérien gouvernemental avec à son bord 2 pilotes effectuait un vol local au départ de Val-d'Or (CYVO) QUE lorsque l'équipage de conduite a observé une indication anormale des paramètres du moteur droit sans perte de puissance. Le moteur (PWC R-2800) a été arrêté par précaution, une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil est revenu se poser à CYVO sans difficulté.

N699RS un appareil de type SR22 en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Wabush, TNL  à destination de Québec/Jean-Lesage Intl, QC à une altitude de 8000 pieds asl lorsque le pilote seul à bord a noté une baisse de la pression d'huile du moteur accompagné d'une température d'huile élevée. Le pilote a déclaré une urgence et demandé d'être dirigé vers l'aéroport de Sept-Îles (CYZV), QC. À environ 60 milles nautiques au nord de CYZV, le moteur (TELEDYNE CONTINENTAL MOTOR IO-550) s'est arrêté. Le pilote a fait planer l'appareil jusqu'à environ 4000 pieds avant de déployer le parachute de l'appareil. L'appareil s’est écrasé dans les arbres à environ 56 milles au nord de CYZV et a subi des dommages importants. Le pilote n'a subi aucune blessure. Le pilote a activé le mode SOS de son GPS portable Garmin Inreach. Il a été secouru environ 5 heures après l'événement par le service de recherches et sauvetage des Forces armées canadiennes.

C-FUCO, un Cessna 172P exploité par Orizon Aviation Québec Inc. était en phase de décollage à partir de l'aéroport Jean Lesage Intl/Québec (CYQB), QUE pour un vol d'initiation (pilote d'un jour) avec trois passagers à bord. Durant la course au décollage, l'avion s'est brusquement cabré et a amorcé un virage vers la gauche de façon non commandée. L'appareil a quitté l'axe de la piste pour violemment retomber au sol. Les passagers et le pilote ont évacué d’eux même l'avion et ont attendu les services d'urgences de l'aéroport. Les trois passagers ont subi des blessures mineures. L'avion a subi des dommages importants.

N674FE un appareil de type Airbus 300-600 exploité par Federal Express sous l'indicatif de vol FDX152 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Montréal Intl/Mirabel (CYMX), QC à destination de Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON. Peu de temps après le départ l'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence pour des problèmes de volets. L'appareil a poursuivi vers sa destination où il s'est posé sans problème.

C-GWSL, a WestJet Boeing 737-600, was operating as flight WJA124 from Vancouver (CYVR), BC to Calgary (CYYC), AB with 5 crew and 104 passengers on board. While in cruise, the aircraft experienced turbulence and one flight attendant was injured during the event. Duties were distributed to the remaining cabin crew and the flight arrived in Calgary without further issue.

C-FPZE, a Cu Nim Gliding Club Cessna 182N, was conducting tow operations at the Black Diamond/Cu Nim airstrip (CEH2), AB. C-FLTY, a Cu Nim Gliding Club Schleicher ASK 21 dual seat glider, was operating at CEH2 with an instructor and student on board. C-FPZE departed Runway 07 with C-FLTY in tow and proceeded to climb to 2000 feet above the aerodrome at which time C-FLTY released from the tow plane. Shortly after release, C-FLTY and C-FPZE collided 0.5 nm southwest of the threshold of Runway 07. The collision resulted in the vertical and horizontal stabilizers being separated from the glider. The glider entered a dive from which it did not recover. The tow plane sustained damage to the propeller and right wing; however, the pilot managed to perform a successful forced landing with idle power onto Runway 14. The student and instructor were fatally injured; the tow pilot was not injured.

C-GURL, a float equipped Cessna 208 (Caravan) aircraft operated by SeAir Seaplanes, departed Vancouver Int'l water aerodrome (CAM9), BC at 09:32 PST for a flight to a fishing lodge approximately 29 nm southeast of Bella Bella (CBBC), BC with 1 pilot and 8 passengers on board. At approximately 11:02 PST the aircraft collided with terrain on Addenbroke Island, BC. There was no post impact fire. An ELT signal was detected; Search and Rescue (SAR) were dispatched and found the aircraft in a heavily forested hillside of Addenbroke Island – 37 nm southeast of CBBC. SAR personnel transported 5 surviving passengers to Port Hardy (CYZT), BC for medical attention. The 1 pilot and 3 passengers were fatally injured. The TSB deployed 3 investigators to the accident site.

C-FGQK, a de Havilland DH8A aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was scheduled to conduct a flight from Sault Ste. Marie (CYAM), ON to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. While taxiing from the apron, the crew heard a clunking sound and then observed smoke in the flight deck and cabin areas. The aircraft returned to the gate where the 33 passengers were deplaned rapidly. There were no injuries, and the flight was cancelled.

C-FJQL, an Airbus A321-211 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge LP, was conducting flight ROU1683 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC with 6 crew members and 138 passengers on board. During cruise flight, a cabin crew member became incapacitated due to illness and was unable to continue duties. Duties were distributed to remaining cabin crew members for the landing.

C-FJJH, a King Air A100, operated by Thunder Air as flight THU104, departed Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Fort Hope (CYFH), ON. At approximately 15 nautical miles north CYQT, passengers noticed smoke coming from beneath the floor and notified the flight crew. The flight crew conducted the emergency procedure for smoke, pulled the flap motor circuit breaker, and declared an emergency. Subsequently, the smoke appeared to dissipate and a flapless approach was conducted into CYQT. The aircraft landed safely. The operator's maintenance replaced the flap motor.

C-GSWB, a Sunwest Aviation Ltd. Beech 1900D, was operating as flight CNK432 from Grande Prairie (CYQU), AB to Calgary (CYYC), AB with 2 crew members and 10 passengers on board. During the climb to cruise, the flight crew observed a caution light for a yaw damper/rudder boost failure. Coincidentally a passenger drew the crew's attention to fog/smoke coming out of the floor vents. The flight crew elected to declare an emergency and return to CYQU with ARFF on standby. During the approach, the fog/smoke dissipated and the flight landed without further event.Company maintenance determined that the fog/smoke was water condensate from the air conditioning system. The system fault that triggered the yaw damper/rudder boost failure caution light was determined to be unrelated to fog/smoke.

C-GPTL, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 helicopter operated by Yellowhead Helicopters, departed Ospika (CBA9), BC to transport forestry crews to a location 10 nm north of CBA9 with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. During climb out of a vertical landing area, the main rotor blades contacted a tree. The operator's maintenance found no visible damage to the main rotor blades; however, green marks were found on the blade endcaps. There were no injuries.

C-GLQO, a DHC-8-402, was being operated by Porter Airlines as flight PD939 from Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON to Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl (KBOS), MA. Near the vicinity of Albany Intl (KALB), NY, the crew experienced a pressurization issue with the cabin climbing at a very high rate, accompanied by the Cabin Press warning light. The checklist was actioned and an emergency descent was initiated;a mayday was declared. At 10,000 feet it was determined there was no structural damage, and the aircraft continued to KBOS. A post flight inspection revealed the aft baggage blowout panel was loose. Maintenance deferred the pressurization system and the aircraft was repositioned to YTZ for further maintenance.

C-GICB, a Sikorsky S-92A helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters Offshore (CHO), was conducting flight CDN131 from Stanfield/Halifax Intl Airport (CYHZ), NS to the Thebaud gas field platform (Thebaud) during daylight hours on an instrument flight rules flight. Onboard were 2 pilots and 11 passengers. Due to low clouds and visibility, 2 instrument approaches were attempted at Thebaud. During the missed approach following the second instrument approach, the flight crew became visual with the platform. The flight crew decided to discontinue the missed approach and to conduct a visual approach and landing to the platform, which was now visible above a layer of fog. Shortly after commencing the final descent, the crew lost contact with the platform in the fog. The helicopter airspeed then decreased and a high rate of descent developed. The helicopter began to rotate about the vertical axis. The crew carried out a missed approach. Both engines experienced an over torque condition, a low main rotor speed condition, and the generators came offline. The crew regained control of aircraft at low altitude in low visibility conditions. The crew elected to divert to CYHZ where a landing was conducted without further incident. There were no injuries. Aircraft damage as a result of transmission over-torque still being evaluated. The emergency locator transmitter did not activate.

C-GELN, a Cessna 172 owned by Stratford Air Services Ltd., had departed Stratford Municipal Airport (CYSA) for a flight to the Sexsmith /Exeter Airport (CSX7) with only the pilot on board. The aircraft landed long on runway 27, exited the runway end, and made contact with a wooden pole. The aircraft continued through a shallow ditch and came to rest on a road. There were no injuries to the sole occupant. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FDEP, an amateur built Just Aircraft Highlander, on amphibious floats, was conducting a takeoff from a private grass runway with two people on board. After take-off, the aircraft began to descend and settled into a cornfield; the aircraft nosed over and came to rest on its back. There were no injuries, the aircraft was damaged substantially. The ELT did not activate.

A deHavilland DHC-8-402, operated by Porter Airlines as flight POE252, was conducting a flight from Greater Moncton Intl (CYQM), New Brunswick, to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), Ontario. During the take off run, the inboard left main tire failed. The takeoff was continued, a Pan Pan call was made during the descent into CYOW; the aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-FPFH, a privately operated, float-equipped Piper PA12 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Cold Fish Lake, BC to Laslui Lake, BC with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During cruise, the engine (Lycoming 0-320-C1A) experienced a power loss. The pilote conducted an emergency landing in a wooded area and overturned. The passenger sustained minor injuries. The pilot used a satellite phone to coordinate a helicopter rescue. The ELT did not activate. The aircraft was substantially damaged.  The cause of the loss of engine power is undetermined.

C-GCFF, a Beech 200 operated by Skynorth Air as flight SN851, was on an IFR flight from Brandon (CYBR), MB to Island Lake (CYIV), MB. During the approach to Runway 30 at CYIV, the flaps did not extend when selected. The crew reselected the flaps up and noticed the flap circuit breaker was open. They followed the circuit breaker tripped checklist and reset the circuit breaker. When the flaps were selected to approach, the circuit breaker immediately opened and the flaps did not move. The crew carried out a missed approach and SN851 diverted to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International (CYWG), MB. The crew declared a PAN PAN while en route to CYWG, and completed the flapless landing checklist. The flight landed without further incident on Runway 18 at CYWG with flaps up. The operator's maintenance replaced the flap motor, brake relay, switches, and flex shafts. The aircraft was ground checked and returned to service.

C-GPTD, a private Mooney M20J aircraft, was conducting a flight from Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC to Chilliwack (CYCW), BC with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During cruise, the landing gear warning horn started to sound. The pilot could not determine the cause of the horn so the circuit breaker for the landing gear was pulled to stop the sound of the horn and the flight continued to CYCW. During approach for landing, the pilot completed the pre-landing checklist which included selecting the gear down. The aircraft landed with the landing gear retracted and came to a stop on the runway. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The ELT did not activate. The cause of the landing gear warning horn is undetermined.

C-GYNT, a Weatherly 620B operated by Fly'n Dutchman AG Ltd, was conducting a local aerial application flight from Melfort/Miller Field (CJZ3), SK. During an application pass approximately 2 nm south of Armley, SK, the aircraft struck a power line causing substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer. Subsequently, control of the aircraft was lost and during an attempt to land on a gravel road, the aircraft collided with terrain adjacent to the road. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The pilot, who was wearing a helmet and 5-point harness, was seriously injured but was able to egress the aircraft. Local police and emergency services responded.

GGN7266, a Bombardier CRJ100 operated by Air Georgian, departed runway 06L at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. On departure, GGN7266 was instructed to turn direct to the MOBEL fix. LXJ589, a Bombardier CL300 operated by Flexjet, that departed behind GGN7266, began a turn towards the MOBEL fix at the same time. The controller instructed LXJ589 to level at 4000 feet and to ensure that they had GGN7266 visual. The controller advised LXJ589 of the requirement to maintain runway heading until they are instructed to turn to the MOBEL fix. During the departure, the separation was reduced to 1.7 nm horizontally and at the same altitude where 1000 feet or 3 nm separation is required.

C-FPQL, the Consolidated-Vultee PBY-5A Canso airplane, was operating from Hamilton (CYHM), ON to Appleton International (KATW), WI with 4 operating crew and 2 other qualified non-flying crew members. During the initial approach, the aircraft experienced a partial loss of hydraulic pressure. The crew lowered the landing gear using the alternate landing gear method and requested emergency response vehicles on standby. The aircraft landed uneventfully and the hydraulic system was inspected by maintenance. A hydraulic supply line to the accumulator was found to be cracked; it was repaired and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GSTG, a Dassault Falcon 7x aircraft was being operated by Execaire from Monmouth Executive Airport - Farmingdale (KBLM) enroute to Genoa Cristoforo Colombo - Genoa (LIMJ). When leveling off at FL200, approximately 15 minutes into the flight, a loud bang was heard on the starboard side of the aircraft and immediately the aircraft yawed to the right and "HIGHT VIB #3" was displayed. The checklist was followed and the #3ENG was  shut down to secure the engine. A Pan Pan message was passed to New York Control and the crew diverted the aircraft to John F Kennedy Intl (KJFK) and landed on RWY 22L uneventfully. For precautionary measures the crew had the emergency vehicles escort the aircraft to the FBO. The aircraft was shut down as per the AFM, and the passengers disembarked. The downloaded engine date revealed an Uncommanded increase in fuel scheduling which in turn caused an overtemp out of limits.The engine was replaced in KJFK and the aircraft was returned to service on 24 July 2019.

C-GEFA, an Airbus A330-343 aircraft operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA863 from Dublin Airport (EIDW) to Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC with 11 crew members and 282 passengers on board. Prior arrival to CYVR, the flight crew reported that a cabin crew member was ill and duties were distributed among the rest of cabin crew. The flight crew declared an emergency, the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GKBN, a Beech King Air 200 operated by Kenn Borek Air, was conducting a flight from Port Hardy (CYZT), BC to Calgary Int'l (CYYC), AB with 2 pilots and 2 passengers on board. After a normal start on the right engine, the left engine was started. While having the left starter engaged but before introducing fuel to the left engine, a MASTER WARNING and Right Engine Fire light illuminated. The pilot turned off the left starter and completed the "Engine Fire On Ground/Start" checklist. There was no visible indication of fire or smoke. The flight crew completed a rapid deplaning. ARFF responded. The operator's maintenance determined there was no physical indication of a fire and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWML, a Bell Helicopters B206B operated by Delta Helicopters, was conducting operations in support of a tree planting project approximately 48 nm N of Slave Lake, AB (CYZH) with the pilot and 2 passengers on board. As the helicopter was lifting off from the tree planting camp, the helicopter made contact with fuel drums that were set up on site and subsequently rolled over, coming to rest on its right side. The pilot and 2 passengers evacuated the aircraft; there were no injuries. There was no fire; the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GFPL, an Air Tractor AT-504 operated by Forest Protection Limited, was conducting a training flight in the local area around Miramichi airport (CYCH), NB with two pilots on board. Once the upper air work was completed the aircraft returned to the airfield to conduct circuits on runway 09. The approach and landing phase was unremarkable until part way through the roll-out when directional control was lost and the aircraft turned abruptly to the right. The aircraft began to skip/slide sideways until the left main wheel tire rolled off the rim and the landing gear collapsed inboard toward the fuselage. The aircraft came to rest partially off the runway with resultant damage to the left landing gear, left outboard wing section, and the propeller. Both pilots exited the aircraft without injuries. ARFF responded and there was no post accident fire. The aircraft was removed from the runway edge and the runway was reopened a few hours later.

C-GWEQ, a Westjet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-400 flight WEN3409 was conducting a flight from Quebec/Jean Lesage Intl. (CYQB), QC to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON  and was approaching CYYZ. At the same time, N300PQ Endeavour Air a CRJ9 flight EDV5540 was inbound to CYYZ from New York/John F Kennedy Intl. (KJFK), NY. Air traffic control issued an instruction to END5540 to turn to a heading of 040 and the crew read back 040 to the controller. EDV5540 was observed continuing the turn to a heading of 340 and when questioned, replied that they were given 340 as a heading. The controller immediately gave EDV5540 a clearance to turn to a heading of 090 and to stop descent at 3500 feet above sea level. WEN3409 and EDV5540 came within 2.8 NM laterally and were at the same altitude. A minimum 1000 feet or 3 nm separation is required. Both flights landed uneventfully.

C-GOOY, a Piper Aircraft Corporation PA-18-150, operated by Gana River Outfitters, was conducting a private flight in the Mckenzie Mountains approximately 72 nm West of Norman Wells, NT (CYVQ) with only the pilot onboard. While executing a landing at a possible future landing site, the wind direction changed during the landing roll. As there was insufficient distance remaining to initiate a go around, the pilot applied hard braking which resulted in the aircraft nosing over and coming to a rest upside down on its roof. The pilot exited the aircraft and was uninjured. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FWJI, a CL-600-2B19, operating as Air Georgian flight GGN7345, from Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) to Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky Intl. -Covington (KCVG), KY had landed and was taxiing on Taxiway Hotel when the aircraft collided with a fuel truck. Both aircraft and truck were in motion at the time. The impact caused the aircraft to rotate 45 degrees. There were no reported injuries and passengers were deplaned and bussed to the terminal. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left wing.

C-FTJQ, an Airbus 320 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC706 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY. During descent, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to CLIMB. The instruction was followed until the alert was over; the aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-FMWN, a privately operated Harvard 4 aircraft, was conducting a local flight from Vancouver/Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During landing, the aircraft touched down long, overran the runway, and impacted the airport perimeter fence. There were no injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GVSU, a Grob 115 aircraft operated by Ottawa Aviation Services for a local flight, was on the take-off run, runway 32, at Ottawa MacDonald-Cartier International (CYOW) when directional control was lost. The aircraft exited the right side of the runway and struck a taxi-way sign prior to coming to a stop. There was substantial damage to the aircraft, there were no injuries.

C-GCEA, a Cessna 150J, was on a VFR flight itinerary from the Jasper Airport (CYJA) to Hinton, AB with one pilot and one passenger on board. Shortly after take-off the aircraft entered a departure stall and spin to the left. The aircraft impacted the Athabasca River approximately 0.5 nm from the departure end of the runway. The pilot sustained serious injuries and the passenger was fatally injured. The 121.5 Mhz ELT activated. Witnesses on Highway 16 were able to attend to both occupants within minutes of the accident.

C-GJSD, a Bell 206B aircraft operated by Blackcomb Helicopters Ltd., was conducting a sight seeing operation approximately 8 nm north of Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. The flight originated and was destined to the Grouse Mountain Helipad. During the flight, the pilot received an engine chip light indication. The pilot declared a mayday, selected a suitable landing site, and executed a precautionary landing uneventfully. The aircraft landed on the Dundarave Beach in West Vancouver, BC. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft.The operator's maintenance staff attended, cleared the chip indication, and returned the aircraft to service.

A6-EDO, an Airbus A380-800 aircraft operated by Emirates Airlines was conducting flight UAE242 from Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON to Dubai International Airport (OMDB), United Arab Emirates. Approximately 20 minutes after departure, UAE242 declared a PAN PAN with the #2 engine shut down. UAE242 requested to return to CYYZ and began dumping fuel. The aircraft landed uneventfully on runway 33R at CYYZ with ARFF standing by.

C-GOJN, a Sikorsky S-61N aircraft operated by VIH Helicopters, was conducting heli-logging operations approximately 21 nm northwest of Bella Bella (Campbell Island) (CBBC), BC with 2 pilots on board. During the log pick-up, the longline and grapple were inadvertently released into the logging block. The helicopter returned to the service barge uneventfully.

C-FNOI, a Boeing 787-9 was being operated by Air Canada as flight AC548 from Vancouver Intl - Vancouver (CYVR)  to Newark Liberty Intl (KEWR). During top of descent the flight crew experienced an EICAS message that indicated an unservicable primary right hydraulic system. A Pan Pan was declared and emergency vehicles were requested. The aircraft landed uneventfully and exited the runway; the emergency vehicles inspected the aircraft, then the aircraft taxied to the gate.

C-GUBC, an Airbus A330-243 aircraft operated by Air Transat was conducting Flight TSC337 from Lisbon International/Humberto Delgado Airport (LPPT) to Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ), ON. During final approach to runway 24R, the flight crew received 2 flap ECAM messages and initiated a missed approach and notifying ATC of a flap issue. The crew performed the checklist items, declared an emergency and landed uneventfully on runway 23 with ARFF standing by. ARFF inspected the aircraft when it had stopped on the taxiway, then the aircraft taxied to the gate.

C-GMBZ, an Air Tractor AT-502B aircraft operated by Western Canadian Aerial Ltd., was engaged in agricultural application approximately 8 nm WSW of Reston (CRP2), MB. The pilot had conducted an inspection of the field and had identified adjacent hydro wires. The second pass to the north was made beneath the hydro wires to limit chemical drift. The aircraft came into contact with an unidentified earth cable that was strung at approximately 2/3 of the pole height. Damage was sustained by the horizontal stabilizer that caused the elevator to become jammed in the neutral position. The aircraft began an uncommanded climb. The pilot was able to regain level flight by using the elevator trim control. The aircraft was flown back to the operating base. The landing was conducted without elevator pitch control by using elevator trim and power. The aircraft landed on the upslope portion of the runway and bounced. The aircraft impacted the runway and sustained substantial damage to the propeller and landing gear. The pilot was uninjured.

C-GDJZ, a Bombardier CRJ 900 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP  departed Newark Liberty International Airport (KEWR) for a scheduled flight to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (CYOW).  Approximately 15 min after departing KEWR, the crew received a brake overheat warning indication. The crew actioned the appropriate checklist, reduced their speed and lowered the landing gear to allow the brakes to cool. Once cooled, the gear was retracted and the flight proceeded as planned. While approaching CYOW, the crew declared an emergency and called for the emergency vehicles to be on standby for their arrival as a precaution for a possible blown tire. The flight landed in CYOW without incident and stopped on the runway to allow emergency personnel to verify that there were no issues with the tires. The flight then proceeded to taxi to the gate. There were no injuries.

C-GCMD, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 aircraft operated by Yellowhead Helicopters, departed from Prince George (CYXS), BC to conduct external load operations in a remote area located 42 nm east of CYXS with only the pilot on board. Shortly after takeoff, both straps failed and the load landed into a heavily forested area. There were no injuries. The operator found the load was attached to the longline with two endless straps that were in contact with the bare metal edge of the load which caused the straps to fail.

C-FKWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-402, was operating as flight WEN3362 from Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB to Edmonton (CYEG), AB with 4 crew members and 70 passengers onboard. During landing on RWY 12, the aircraft made abnormal contact with the runway. After clearing RWY 12 on taxiway A2, the flight crew became aware that the nose tires had burst. Due to thunderstorm activity, company maintenance were unable to attend to the aircraft to change both nose tires for approximately 40 minutes. After deplaning passengers at the gate, a more detailed inspection of the aircraft revealed wrinkled fuselage skins, left nose gear door damage, damage to the forward pressure bulkhead, and the nose gear assembly. There were no reported injuries to the crew or passengers.

C-FDFK, an Air Tractor 502B operated by Tarrickfic Aerial Ltd., was conducting aerial application operations on a field approximately 19 nm NW of Two Hills Airport (CEL6), AB with just the pilot on board. Following completion of the first spray pass along the edge of the field, the aircraft struck a single strand power line adjacent to the perimeter of the field. The aircraft was equipped with wire cutters on the main landing gear legs and the wire was severed. The pilot returned to base and an uneventful landing was completed. There were no injuries, and no damage to the aircraft.

C-FVFK, an Aerospatiale AS350B3 helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters Ltd, was conducting heli-slinging operations 118 nm NE of Faro (CZFA), YK. Water was being supplied to an outpost using a plastic 120 gallon water tank that was strapped to a pallet, which was subsequently suspended on external load rigging from the helicopter. Shortly after liftoff, at an altitude of approximately 300 feet, in the transition to forward flight, the strapping securing the water tank to the pallet failed and the water tank subsequently slipped through the external load rigging and fell to the ground. There were no injuries or damage to the helicopter. The water tank was subsequently recovered.

C-GAFT, an experimental Glasair 2ST, with the pilot as the sole occupant on board, departed Lee Gilmer Memorial Airport, (KGVL) Gainesville, GA, and landed at Bedford, Indiana (KBFR) where fuel was bought. The aircraft then departed for Wittman Regional, Wisconsin (KOSH). While enroute, approximately 15 minutes, it was reported that the aircraft experienced a full electrical failure and then the engine stopped producing power. The aircraft stalled, experienced a hard bounce and nosed over in a wooded area. The pilot sustained serious injuries and the aircraft was substantially damaged. The NTSB investigated (ANC19LA0306).

C-GEOL, a Piper PA-31-350 aircraft operated by KD Air Corporation, was conducting a maintenance flight in the circuit at Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC with 1 pilot and 1 aircraft maintenance apprentice on board. During the first circuit, on the downwind leg, fuel was observed leaking from the left wing inboard fuel port due to the fuel cap being missing. After configuring the aircraft and turning base leg, the pilot communicated to air traffic control that they had an emergency and needed priority landing. The aircraft landed uneventfully. The airport ground crew found the fuel cap at the departure end of the runway.

C-FGQC, a DHC-2 aircraft operated by Inland Air Charters, was conducting a flight from Dolphins Lodge, BC to Seal Cove (CZSW), BC with a pilot and 4 passengers on board. On arrival to CZSW, the pilot inspected the water landing area from overhead. On landing, the aircraft touched down farther than expected and the aircraft collided with a log. There were no injuries. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and found no damage.

C-FZRF, a privately operated, float-equipped, Cessna 185 was conducting a local flight from Nimpo Lake (CAF8), BC with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During touchdown in glassy water conditions, the aircraft lost control and overturned. Both occupants egressed and the pilot sustained minor injuries. The ELT did not activate. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FTEN, a De Havilland of Canada DHC8-402 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3209 from Saskatoon/John D. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB with 4 crew members and 22 passengers on board. On approach into CYEG, the flight crew executed a missed approach due to misreading a NOTAM and elected to divert to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. On approach into CYYC, the crew declared a "min fuel" state with ATS and requested priority handling. Another aircraft was pulled off the approach to accommodate WEN3209 and subsequently landed after WEN3209 had landed. WEN3209 completed an uneventful landing in CYYC. The aircraft landed in CYYC with more than the min fuel required for the flight.

C-GOMH, a Robinson Helicopters R44 Raven II, was conducting a private flight with the pilot and 2 passengers on board from Tincup Lake, YK, to Dogpack Lake, YK. Following an uneventful flight to Dogpack Lake, upon landing the pilot elected to reposition the helicopter as it was not level after the initial settling. During the lift-off and unbeknownst to the pilot, the rear "Bear Paw" on the aft end of the RH skid became entangled in a tree root and the aircraft moved to the right, instead of forward as desired. As more collective was applied, the bear paw released from the root and helicopter moved forward abruptly. The pilot was unable to arrest the forward movement in time to avoid the main rotor blades making contact with a tree and subsequently cutting off the top portion of the tree. The nose of the helicopter also made contact with the remaining portion of the tree trunk and was significantly damaged. The pilot was able to land the helicopter, and the pilot and passengers exited the aircraft. There were no injuries.

C-GJZR, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA7124 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with only the 4 crew members on board. Upon landing gear up selection after the departure from CYYZ, all landing gears remained down, and the flight crew received three red lights accompanied by a gear unsafe indication. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and requested to return to CYYZ. The emergency landing gear checklist was completed, which resulted in a successful gear down indication. The aircraft landed without incident on Runway 24R with ARFF in attendance.The operator’s maintenance found the steering control unit with both Rotary Variable Differential Transformers (RVDT) out of rig. The rigging was completed as per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) 32-51-00-830-801. The Nose Wheel Steering (NWS) hand control potentiometer was found within limits and was tested operational. The NWS centering mechanism was replaced, and operational test of the main landing gear primary extension and retraction checks were completed in accordance with AMM 32-31-00-710-801. No faults were found. The aircraft was returned to revenue service.

C-FQWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-402, was operating as flight WEN3296 from Calgary (CYYC), AB to Regina (CYQR), SK with 5 crew and 68 passengers onboard. On departure, C-FQWE was instructed by terminal controller to climb and maintain 9000 feet ASL. A few moments later WEN3296 inadvertently acknowledged another radio call from ATC meant for WEN3396, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-402. WEN3296 started a climb to a new clearance limit of FL250. A loss of separation occurred with an arriving aircraft, C-GKUK, a Jazz Aviation De Havilland 8-402 conducting flight JZA441, that was cleared to 10 000 feet ASL. Separation deteriorated to 2.6 nm laterally where 3 NM is required. Separation was regained when the controller instructed JZA441 to turn right. There were no TCAS RAs from either aircraft.

N143UP, un appareil de type Airbus 300-600 exploité par United Parcel Service CO. sous l'indicatif de vol UPS474, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Louisville International Airport-Standiford Field (KSDF), KY en direction de Montréal/Mirabel (CYMX), QC. Alors qu'il venait d’atterrir à CYMX, les pilotes ont noté une surchauffe des roues #3 et #7 du train d'atterrissage intérieur droit et ils ont déclaré une urgence. Un véhicule d'urgence a inspecté les trains d'atterrissage et aucune fumée n'a été notée et tous les pneus semblaient normaux. Les températures ont commencé à réduire et le N143UP a circulé vers son stationnement. Un aéronef circulant sur une voie de circulation a été redirigé pour laisser passer le N143UP. Une fois stationné, toutes les températures de roues du train droit étaient dans les limites raisonnables.

C-FPCU, a Saab 340B aircraft operated by Pacific Coastal Airlines, was conducting flight PCO871 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC, to Port Hardy (CYZT), BC, with 3 crew members and 14 passengers on board. During cruise, the AVIONICS SMOKE annunciator illuminated. The crew conducted vital actions, declared an emergency and completed the Quick Reference Checklist. The crew detected no signs of smoke. The crew returned to land at CYVR and the aircraft landed uneventfully. On landing, the CYVR Fire Services inspected the aircraft and no heat signal was detected. The operator's maintenance replaced the smoke detector.

C-GCMA, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Central Mountain Air, was conducting flight GLR563 from Quesnel (CYQZ), BC, to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC, with 2 crew members and 9 passengers on board. During the takeoff roll the crew observed a sudden jolt to the right and continued the takeoff. The after-takeoff checklist was completed and no abnormalities were observed so the crew elected to continued to Vancouver and requested that CYQZ airport operations personnel check the runway for debris. ATC advised that a spring attached to foam and rubber was found on the runway. The crew determined there was a possibility of a structural landing gear issue and requested emergency equipment on standby in CYVR. The aircraft landed uneventfully. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and determined that the items recovered in CYQZ were not from the occurrence aircraft.

C-FWAF, a Pilatus PC-12/45 operated by Wasaya Airways as flight WSG5514, was on a VFR flight from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON, to Cat Lake (CYAC), ON. The flight was on left base for a 5 mile final approach to CYAC, with flaps 15 and gear up, when it encountered severe turbulence. The pilots experienced difficulty in maintaining aircraft control, and the flap limit speed was exceeded. The crew terminated the approach and diverted back to CYXL uneventfully.The operator's maintenance carried out severe turbulence and flap overspeed inspections with no fault found, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GDUZ, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1935 from Athens/Eleftherios Venizelos Intl (LGAV), Greece, to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 9 crew members and 248 passengers on board. During the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from LGAV, the flight crew identified a slight fuel imbalance. The associated QRH items were executed in an attempt to rectify the issue, however it was subsequently identified that there was an uncommanded fuel transfer of 2.6 tons per hour from the L MAIN tank to the CENTER tank. The flight crew decided to divert to London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK, and declared a PAN PAN as a precaution. The aircraft landed without further incident.  The operator’s maintenance is currently inspecting the aircraft, and will release it back to service once the issue is fixed.

C-GAEF, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-2 MK. I Beaver exploité par Air Saguenay, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis la base d’opération principale du Lac Sébastien (CTD3), QC avec seul le pilot à bord. À son retour à la base, le pilote a observé une grande quantité d’embarcations nautiques sur le lac, et a décidé d’effectuer un survol à environ 200 pieds au-dessus de la surface afin de signaler aux plaisanciers sa présence avant d’amerrir. Alors que l’avion était à environ 15 pieds au-dessus du lac, une embarcation de type motomarine a coupé l’axe d’approche de l’avion de la droite vers la gauche. Le pilote a remis les gaz pour interrompre l'amerrissage, et est revenu compléter son amerrissage sans autre incident. Suite à l’événement, l’association des propriétaires du lac Sébastien a émis un rappel aux plaisanciers d’être vigilant, et de circuler autant que possible à l’extérieur du corridor établi pour les approches et les décollages des avions.

C-GKWP, a privately operated float-equipped Savannah Homebuilt aircraft was attempting to land at Francois Lake, BC with 2 persons on board. During the first attempt to land, the left float made contact with the lake harder than usual and the aircraft began to porpoise. The pilot aborted the landing and came around for a second attempt. During the second attempt to land, the left float collapsed and the aircraft dug in. After the aircraft veered to the left, the right wing tip contacted the water causing substantial damage and the aircraft began to sink. Both occupants escaped without injury and were retrieved by nearby witnesses. Neither occupant was wearing a personal floatation device. The ELT did not transmit a signal and there was no post-impact fire.

C-GVIQ, a Bell 206 aircraft operated by Helijet International, was conducting external load operations from Seal Cove (CBF6), BC to Green Island Lighthouse Station, BC with only the pilot on board. During the initial turn from CBF6, the load unintentionally released from the remote hook. There were no injuries. Post incident inspection of the cargo hook found the release roller had rust and flat spots. Rust was also found on the latch spring.

N768AA, un appareil de type Boeing 777-200 exploité par American Airlines, effectuait le vol AAL71 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Frankfurt/Rhein-Main (EDDF), Allemagne à destination de Dallas-Fort Worth Intl (KDFW), TX avec 13 membres d'équipage et 271 passagers à bord. Alors que l'appareil était environ 185 milles au nord-est de Schefferville (CYKL), QC, un membre d'équipage de cabine a subi une incapacité médicale, et n'a pas été en mesure de poursuivre ses activités. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence médicale, et a demandé un déroutement vers Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC où l’appareil s’est posé sans problème.

C-FDUZ, a Schweizer SGS 1-34 glider operated by the Rideau Valley Soaring School, was in the circuit upon its return to Kars/Rideau Valley Air Park (CPL3), ON with only the pilot on board. The aircraft’s approach was observed to be lower and slower than usual, and was followed by a hard landing which substantially damaged the aircraft. The pilot was not injured.

C-FYJE, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1861 from Las Vegas/McCarran Intl (KLAS), NV to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 5 crew members and 108 passengers on board. During the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from KLAS, the aircraft lost the GREEN HYD SYSTEM fluid. The flight crew declared a MAYDAY, and diverted the aircraft back to KLAS where it landed without further incident. The aircraft required to be towed off the runway after the landing.The operator’s maintenance identified an issue in a hydraulic line associated with the nose wheel steering.

C-FEUX, a privately owned Piper PA-12 aircraft, was conducting a local flight from a private grass strip near Eugenia, ON with only the pilot on board. Just before touchdown as the aircraft was returning to land, the pilot encountered a gust of wind, which caused the aircraft to float over the runway. The aircraft touched down long, overran the runway, and impacted a cedar fence. The aircraft was substantially damaged, and the pilot received minor injuries. The pilot was wearing a shoulder harness that prevented serious injuries during the impact.

C-FPWE, un appareil de type Airbus 320-200 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA485 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC en direction de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON avec 5 membres d’équipage et 125 passagers à bord. Alors qu'il venait de décoller de CYUL, l'équipage de conduite a noté une surchauffe des systèmes hydrauliques jaune et vert. L'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence, et l'appareil est revenu se poser à CYUL sans encombre avec les Services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé, ni dommage. Le service de l’entretien de l’exploitant a remplacé le groupe de transfert d'énergie (PTU) du système vert, ainsi que l'accumulateur. L’appareil a été remis en service.

C-FJKI, a DHC-2 Beaver aircraft on floats operated by Air Saguenay, had departed Crossroads Lake, NL for a day trip to Mistastin Lake, NL, for a fishing excursion with the pilot and 6 passengers on board. When the aircraft did not return in the evening, JRCC was contacted. SAR was dispatched and  the aircraft was found submerged in the Mistastin Lake the following morning. Three deceased occupants were recovered. The RCMP and military carried out a search for the remaining occupants and a fourth deceased passenger was recovered. The pilot and the remaining 2 passengers are still missing. For more information regarding this occurrence, please visit our website https://www.tsb.gc.ca/eng/enquetes-investigations/aviation/2019/a19a0052/a19a0052.htmlAir transportation safety investigation A19A0052 - tsb.gc.ca
