C-FACT, un Dash 8 100-300 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l’indicatif JZA907 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Moncton/Greater Moncton International (CYQM) NB à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL) QC, C-GEZO, un Airbus A321-211 exploité par Air Transat A.T. sous l’indicatif TSC811, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Varadero (MUVR), CUBA  à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International (CYUL) QC. JZA907 était en approche pour un atterrissage sur la piste 24R, suivi de TSC811. Le contrôleur aérien a demandé à TSC811 de réduire sa vitesse d’approche pour tenter de maintenir l’espacement requis de 3 milles marins entre les 2 aéronefs. Une fois que JZA907 a atterri sur la piste, le contrôleur aérien a avisé TSC811 que JZA907 se dirigeait vers B2 pour libérer la piste. TSC811 a accusé réception de l’information et a entrepris de lui-même une remontée. L’espacement à ce moment était de 2.6 milles marins.

C-GKQH, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-8-400 exploité par Porter Airlines, effectuait le vol POE473 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. N750DC, un appareil de type Mooney M20R en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Louisburg/Triangle North Executive (KLHZ), NC à destination de CYUL. Lors de l’approche à CYUL, N750DC a dépassé l’alignement d’approche, créant ainsi une perte d’espacement avec POE473. La distance latérale a été réduite à 2.6 nm, alors que la norme est de 3 nm.

C-GUHZ, un appareil de type Eurocopter EC-130 B4 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Ste-Sophie, QC avec 1 pilote et 3 passagers à bord. Le vol consistait à effectuer des recherches afin de retrouver un autre appareil disparu depuis quelques jours. Lors de l’atterrissage au retour à Ste-Sophie, le pilote a perdu le contrôle; l'appareil a effectué un tour sur lui-même, un des patins a touché le sol, et l’appareil s’est renversé sur le côté droit. Le pilote a subi des blessures mineures, alors que les 3 passagers n’ont pas subi de blessures. L’appareil a subi des dommages importants; il n’y a pas eu de feu post-impact. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée.

C-FJLH, un hélicoptère de type Robinson R44 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le lac De la Bidière, QC à destination de Ste-Sophie, QC avec 1 pilote et 1 passager à bord. L’aéronef n’est jamais arrivé à destination. Le Centre conjoint de coordination des opérations de sauvetage de Trenton a été avisé le lendemain de la disparition, et les recherches ont débuté. L’accident s’est produit dans les heures de clarté. Il n’y a pas eu d’incendie et aucun signal de radiobalise de repérage d’urgence n’a été capté. L’aéronef a été localisé le 25 juillet, soit 14 jours après avoir été porté disparu, dans un secteur boisé près du lac Valtrie (Québec). Les occupants ont été trouvés sans vie. L’aéronef a été détruit.

C-GJVD, un appareil de type Cessna 152 exploité par Cargair Ltee, effectuait un vol local d’entrainement depuis l’aéroport de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) selon les règles de vol à vue avec un élève-pilote à son bord. Lors d’un posé-décollé sur la piste 30 de CYRC, l’appareil est arrivé trop haut et trop vite et a rebondi. L’élève-pilote a ajouté de la puissance et l'appareil a touché le sol une deuxième fois. La roue de nez s'est brisée de sorte que l'hélice a touché le sol et l'avion est sorti de piste vers sa gauche avant de s’immobiliser dans le gazon. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. L’hélice, le moteur, la roue de nez et l'aile gauche ont subi des dommages importants.

C-GRHF, un appareil de type De Havilland DHC-2 Mk 1. (Beaver) sur flotteurs, en exploitation privée, avec à son bord 1 pilote et 3 passagers, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le réservoir Gouin, QC, à destination d’un lac au nord de Chibougamau, QC. À environ 43 miles au sud de Chibougamau l’appareil est entré en collision avec les arbres. Le pilote et 2 passagers ont subi des blessures mortelles et 1 passager a subi des blessures mineures. L’appareil a subi des dommages substantiels. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée. Le Centre conjoint de coordination des opérations de sauvetage – Trenton a évacué le passager à Chibougamau, QC.

C-FOPT, a privately owned Piper PA-28 aircraft, was conducting a local flight from Vancouver/Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC with 1 student pilot on board. The student pilot was practicing simulated forced approaches. During an overshoot, at approximately 300 feet AGL, the aircraft engine (Lycoming 0-540-B4B5) experienced a power loss. The pilot attempted to restore power but was unsuccessful. The pilot performed an emergency landing in a field 9nm NW of Abbotsford (CYXX), BC. The pilot sustained minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The ELT activated and a signal was received. The cause of the engine power loss has not been determined.

C-FSRY, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8241 from Terrace (CYXT), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 4 crew members and 71 passengers on board. During top of descent, the captain’s windshield cracked. No emergency was declared, however the flight crew requested priority for their approach and ARFF standby as a precaution. The aircraft landed uneventfully.The operator’s maintenance found the captain’s windshield outer ply cracked. No evidence of arcing or mechanical fatigue was found. The windshield was replaced in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual and tested with no further faults. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) was filed with Transport Canada. The aircraft was returned to service.

N809FD, an Airbus A310-300 operated by Federal Express as flight FDX137, was on an IFR flight plan from Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB, to Indianapolis (KIND), Indiana. Construction at CYWG required FDX137 to taxi from Apron 5 to Runway 36 via taxiways H and V and Runway 31. FDX137 had acknowledged an instruction to hold short of Runway 36 on Runway 31. As FDX137 was on taxiway H approaching taxiway V, Winnipeg ground inquired whether FDX137 could accept an intersection takeoff on Runway 36 with 7500 feet remaining, and FDX137 indicated they would need to look up performance data. FDX137 was switched to tower as the flight turned onto taxiway V. By the time FDX137 checked in with tower, the aircraft was on Runway 31 at the hold short line for Runway 36 and came to a stop within the runway protected area for Runway 36. At that time, an Airbus A320-200, C-FZQS operated by Air Canada on an IFR flight from Vancouver International (CYVR), British Columbia, to CYWG as flight ACA292, had been previously cleared to land on Runway 36 and was on short final for Runway 36. The Winnipeg tower controller instructed the ACA292 crew to go around and they did so.FDX137 was subsequently cleared to backtrack to the threshold of Runway 36 and departed without further incident. ACA292 landed uneventfully about 10 minutes later.

C-FBBG, a float-equipped De Havilland DHC-2 Beaver operated by Hawk Air (705833 Ontario Ltd.), collided with terrain shortly after departure from Hawk Junction Water Aerodrome (CNH6) at approximately 0900 EDT. The aircraft was destroyed, the two occupants were fatally injured. There was no post-crash fire. The TSB deployed three investigators to the site.

N72697, a privately registered Cessna 210H, was on a VFR flight from Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB, to Elk Island (CKZ3), MB. The first approach to Runway 24 at CKZ3 was unstable and the pilot carried out a go-around. The second approach to Runway 24 was also unstable, and the aircraft touched down with about 2000 feet of runway remaining. The aircraft departed the end of Runway 24 at about 10 knots and went down a small slope before coming to a stop. The pilot and 1 passenger received minor injuries, and the second passenger was uninjured. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left wingtip, propeller, and nose landing gear.

C-FTYI, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 aircraft operated by Yellowhead Helicopters, departed from Valemount Heli (CBV7), BC to conduct external load operations in a remote area located 56 nm southwest of CBV7, with only the pilot on board. During slinging operations, the pilot inadvertently depressed the cargo hook release button, resulting in the release of the net load. There were no injuries.

C-FOWE, a WestJet Encore De Havilland DHC-8-402, was operating as flight WEN3267 from Calgary (CYYC), AB, to Penticton (CYYF), BC, with 4 crew and 62 passengers onboard. On departure C-FOWE was instructed by the terminal controller to climb and maintain 8000 feet ASL. A loss of separation occurred with an arriving Canadian North Boeing 737-36N, flight MPE1741, that was also cleared to 8000 feet ASL. Separation was reduced to 1.7 nm laterally and 900 feet vertically where 3 nm or 1000 feet is required. Separation was regained when the controller instructed WEN3267 to turn right and maintain 7000 feet ASL. There were no TCAS RAs from either aircraft and the flight crew of WEN3267 had MPE1741 in sight.

C-GSPP, a Grumman G-164B operated by Smokey Burn Ag-Air, had just completed a VFR aerial application flight and was landing eastward on a gravel road 2 nm southeast of Brooksby, SK. During the landing rollout, the aircraft encountered soft gravel at low speed and departed from the road surface into soft terrain and overturned. The pilot was uninjured, and the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FJIC, a Cessna 750 Citation X aircraft operated by PAL Aerospace, was conducting flight SPR600 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to St John’s Intl (CYYT), NL. During the initial climb after the departure from CYHZ, the flight crew contacted ATC and indicated that they would be returning to CYHZ due to a hydraulic issue. The flight crew confirmed the loss of pressure in Hydraulic System “A”, consulted the QRH, and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without further incident, and came to a full stop on the runway. Due to the lack of nose wheel steering and limited braking, the aircraft was unable to exit the runway. ARFF informed the flight crew that hydraulic fluid was leaking from the tail of the aircraft. The flight crew shut the engines down, and the aircraft was towed to the ramp. The operator’s maintenance determined that the left elevator power control unit (PCU) hydraulic return line in the tail section of the aircraft had ruptured. The spiral wrap utilized to protect the hydraulic line from chafing had migrated away, allowing contact between the line and the upper surface of the PCU.  The hydraulic line was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FAQL, a privately registered float-equipped Cessna A185E, was departing from Fedirchyk Lake, MB for St. Andrews, MB with only the pilot on board. Upon takeoff from the water, a wind gust was encountered and control of the aircraft was lost. The aircraft subsequently collided with an island and was substantially damaged. A witness responded to the accident and pulled the injured pilot from the wreckage. A family member, who was contacted by the pilot via satellite phone to advise of the accident, contacted the RCMP and they responded to the site by helicopter. The pilot and witness were rescued by the helicopter.

C-GAVQ, a Bell 407 aircraft operated by Summit Helicopters, was conducting forest fire suppression operations 30 nm north of Terrace (CYXT), BC with only the pilot on board. While attempting to release the load of water on the fire, the pilot inadvertently depressed the cargo hook release button, resulting in the release of the bucket and longline. There were no injuries.

C-GJZT, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA43 from Sacramento Intl (KSMF), CA to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. JZA43 was being vectored onto the RNAV R26R approach, 8 miles ahead of C-GWSQ, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, who was conducting flight WJA127 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to CYVR, which was on the same approach. C-GGMZ, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA52 from Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC to CYVR, and was being vectored onto the RNAV R26R approach between JZA43 and WJA127. JZA52 intercepted the approach 3 miles ahead of WJA127. The separation between JZA52 and WJA127 was reduced to 2.3 nm, where 2.5 nm is required. The approach clearance for WJA127 was cancelled, and the aircraft was vectored for a second approach.

C-FNNH, an Air Canada Boeing 777-233LR was operating as flight ACA033 from Vancouver (CYVR), BC to Sydney (YSSY), Australia with 15 crew members and 269 passengers on board. Approximately 7 hours into the flight (ADOWA waypoint; 640 nm sw of Honolulu, Hawaii) the aircraft encountered severe turbulence at FL340 for 10 to 15 seconds. During the encounter several passengers and some cabin crew were thrown in to the ceiling of the cabin. In total, 37 people (31 passengers and 6 cabin crew) identified that they had sustained sprains, strains, cuts and bruises. The flight crew decided to divert to Honolulu (PHNL), Hawaii which was approximately 2 hours away. While en route to PHNL, first aid was given by the cabin crew and voluntary medical professionals that were passengers on ACA033. In preparation for landing, fuel was dumped and EMS was positioned to meet the aircraft.Maintenance conducted a severe turbulence inspection and no faults were found. There was damage to interior components and cabin furnishings where passengers and cabin crew had come into contact with those items.

C-GMYC, un appareil privé de construction amateur de type Murphy Rebel sur flotteurs, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue à partir du Lac Kénogami, QC, à destination d'un point sur la rivière Chicoutimi, QC, avec seul le pilote à bord. Suite au décollage, le pilote a noté qu'il avait omis de retirer la barrure des flaperons. L'appareil s'est incliné sur la droite, et a piqué du nez pour s'écraser dans les bois à proximité d'une résidence. L'appareil a subi des dommages importants. Le pilote a été légèrement blessé.

C-FQWE, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3107 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Terrace (CYXT), BC with 4 crew members and 78 passengers on board. Approximately 25 minutes before the landing at CYXT, one of the cabin crew members became incapacitated due to illness, and was unable to complete their duties. Duties were reassigned to the remaining cabin crew member for the remainder of the flight.

C-FACT, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-8-300 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA8705 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Sept-Îles (CYZV), QC à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC avec 4 membres d’équipage et 15 passagers à bord. Lors de la sélection du train d’atterrissage en position baissée pendant l’approche finale pour la piste 24 à CYQB, l’équipage a reçu une indication anormale que le train n’était pas descendu et verrouillé. L’équipage a tenté à nouveau de faire descendre le train d’atterrissage, toutefois sans succès. Une urgence a été déclarée, et une approche interrompue a été effectuée. L’équipage a suivi la procédure alternative d’extension du train avec succès, et a annulé l’urgence. L’appareil a atterri sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GZJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7378 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Providence/Theodore Francis Green State (KPVD), RI with 3 crew members and 43 passengers on board. As the aircraft reached 135 KIAS during the take-off run at CYYZ, the flight crew received a number 1 engine duct warning. The flight crew rejected the takeoff, applied the brakes, and exited the runway. As the aircraft was taxiing, both tires of the right main landing gear deflated due to the overpressure fuses release, because of the hot brakes. The flight crew stopped the aircraft on the taxiway, and declared an emergency. All passengers deplaned, and were bussed to the terminal. The operator’s maintenance replaced all wheels. It was determined that the 14th duct sensor had shorted, causing the erroneous warning.

C-GLSA, a de Havilland DHC-2 aircraft operated by Kabeelo Airways, was performing a series of tourist camp resupply flights and was enroute from Wavel Lake, ON to Bear Paw Lake, ON. Upon landing on the glassy water surface of Bear Paw Lake, the aircraft floats struck a submerged reef and overturned. The pilot was uninjured; however, the aircraft sustained substantial damage and sank.

C-FYJG, an Airbus 319 operated by Air Canada Rouge, was conducting flight ROU1539 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK. On descent into CYXE, in the vicinity of DUNEM waypoint, the flight crew observed a TCAS traffic advisory, which was quickly followed by the TCAS aural resolution to level off. The crew leveled off at approximately 5000 feet and observed VFR  traffic (C-GVLO, a Prairie Aviation Training Centre Cessna 172) approximately 500 feet below them. The flight was being controlled by the NAV CANADA's Winnipeg North Low Specialty controller, who had relieved the previous controller only 2 minutes before. NAV CANADA procedures require that VFR traffic be passed to IFR traffic as time and workload permits. NAV CANADA is conducting a safety investigation into the occurrence.

C-FAWQ, un appareil de type Canadair CL-215-6B11 CL251T exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental (SAG) du Gouvernement du Québec, effectuait le vol Q239 selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Roberval (CYRJ), QC à destination d’un feu de forêt situé environ 45 milles marins au nord-ouest de CYRJ, avec 2 pilotes à bord. Lors d’une manœuvre d’écopage sur un lac, la coque de l’avion est entrée en collision avec un haut-fond, causant des dommages à celle-ci. L’équipage a cessé les opérations de lutte contre les incendies, et est retourné à CYRJ où l’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre. Une fois les dommages évalués, un permis de vol a été délivré afin de ramener l’aéronef à la base d’opérations principales du SAG pour y être réparé.

C-GENK, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3421 from St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS with 4 crew members and 49 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL240, the first officer’s side windshield cracked. The flight crew executed the QRH, and descended to 14 000 feet ASL. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight continued to CYHZ without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced the windshield, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-IGPK, un appareil de type Ultra-léger évolué Quad City Challenger II en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Bonaventure (CYVB), QC avec 1 pilote et 1 passager à bord. Peu de temps après le décollage de la piste 31 à CYVB, le pilote a éprouvé des difficultés à maîtriser l’appareil, qui s’est mis à perdre de l’altitude. L’appareil a fait un premier rebond sur la piste, a par la suite repris de l’altitude, pour redescendre à nouveau et faire un deuxième rebond. L’appareil s’est déporté vers la gauche, mais le pilote a réussi à le ramener vers le centre de la piste. Au troisième toucher des roues sur la piste, le train d’atterrissage a cédé sous l’impact, causant un changement de direction de 90° vers la gauche. L’appareil a glissé sur le ventre, est sorti de piste, et a terminé sa course dans un fossé longeant le côté ouest de la piste. Le pilote et le passager ont pu évacuer l’appareil sans difficulté et n’ont pas été blessés. Le pilote avait acquis l’appareil récemment, et n’avait effectué que des essais au sol jusqu’à ce jour.

C-GTSO, an Airbus 330-300 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC154 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Brussels (EBBR), Belgium with 11 crew members and 324 passengers on board. During cruise flight at approximate position N54/W050, a cabin crew member became ill and could not perform duties. Positions were reassigned, and the aircraft continued to destination uneventfully.

C-GTQP, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC296 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Holguin/Frank País Intl (MUHG), Cuba. C-GKQA, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE533 from Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON to Sudbury (CYSB), ON. TSC296 was on the initial climb from CYYZ, and was authorized to 6000 feet ASL. POE533 was also on the initial climb from CYTZ, and was also authorized to 6000 feet ASL. A loss of separation occurred when the two aircraft came within 1.7 nm laterally and 500 feet vertically, in an airspace that requires a minimum separation of 3 nm laterally, or 1000 feet vertically.

C-FRKM, a privately owned Robinson R44 helicopter, had taken off from Oyama Lake, BC, with 1 pilot and 3 passengers on board. Shortly after the takeoff, the pilot experienced a loss of directional control, and executed an emergency landing in a wooded area. There were no injuries, however the helicopter was substantially damaged. The ELT did not activate. The pilot called 911, and the RCMP responded.

C-GEZJ, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC793 from Montego Bay/Sangster Intl (MKJS), Jamaica to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Inlt (CYYZ), ON with 6 crew members and 185 passengers on board. During the initial climb after the departure from MKJS, the flight crew received an ECAM warning for a number 3 hot brake. The flight continued to destination and, after being handed off to Toronto Centre (CZYZ) during the descent to CYYZ, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN as they suspected a possible wheel/tire damage. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by, and stopped on the runway. The landing gear was inspected, and the aircraft was cleared to taxi to the gate. The operator’s maintenance reset the Brake & Steering Control Unit (BSCU) and tested it in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM). The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPAC, a privately registered Weatherly 620B aircraft, was spraying fungicide on a pea field near Oxbow, SK with only the pilot on board. At the end of a spraying run, the aircraft collided with trees, damaging the leading edge of the right wing and resulting in the aircraft making a hard landing in a nearby field. There was no post-crash fire, and no injuries; however, the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

N29JW, a Gulfstream G150 aircraft operated by Schussboomer Systems, departed from Reykjavík/Keflavík (BIKF), Iceland to St John's Intl (CYYT), NL with 2 crew members and 7 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL320 approximately 45 minutes from CYYT, the flight crew received a Main Hydraulic Reservoir Low CAS message. A few minutes later, a Left Hydraulic Pressure Low message was received, followed a few minutes later by a Right Hydraulic Pressure Low message. The hydraulic pressure was observed to drop from a normal 3000 psi to 0, then to 500-600 psi. The flight crew declared an emergency. The landing gear was lowered, however it had to be pumped down in order to receive three green lights. The aircraft landed at CYYT, vacated the runway, and was towed to the apron. Maintenance personnel determined that the number 2 hydraulic pump suffered a seal failure, causing the loss of fluid. Both the number 1 and 2 pumps, as well as all filters, were replaced. The landing gear was cycled as required before returning the aircraft to service.

C-GZAJ, a privately registered Piper PA-34-200T aircraft, was conducting a flight from Sault Ste. Marie (CYAM), ON to Stratford Muni (CYSA), ON with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the landing on Runway 05 at CYSA, the aircraft touched down with the landing gear retracted. The two occupants were not injured, however the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FCJD, a de Havilland DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Air Creebec, was conducting flight CRQ441 from Timmins (Victor M. Power) (CYTS), ON to Victor Mine (CVM2), ON with 3 crew members and 18 passengers on board. During the flight, the flight crew noticed a high oil temperature on the number 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW120A). As the temperature continued to increase, the flight crew elected to return to CYTS. Since the high oil temperature was time limited, the flight crew shut the engine down during the diversion. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by.

C-FTBA, a privately registered Socata TB 10 aircraft , was conducting a local flight from Earlton (Timiskaming Regional) (CYXR), ON with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the initial climb at 200 feet after the takeoff from Runway 34 at CYXR, the engine (Avco Lycoming O-360-A1A) lost power. The pilot continued on runway heading, and executed a forced landing in a field. The aircraft was substantially damaged, however the pilot and the passenger were not injured.

C-GTSI, an Airbus 330-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC183 from Glasgow/Abbotsinch (EGPF), UK to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 11 crew members and 320 passengers on board. During cruise flight at approximate position N55/W020, a cabin crew member became ill and could not perform duties. Positions were reassigned, and the aircraft continued to destination uneventfully.

C-FEXH, a Cessna 208B aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express, was conducting flight MAL8052 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Nanaimo (CYCD), BC with only the pilot on board. During the approach to CYCD, the pilot experienced a burning electrical smell. The STBY PWR and the number 3 Bus 1 circuit breakers popped. No emergency was declared, and the aircraft landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance found the number 1 and 2 avionics switch terminal screws loose, causing arcing and the subsequent electrical smell. It was also noted that connectors PH16 and PH17, forward of the circuit breaker panel, overheated. The number 1 and 2 avionics switches and wires were replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJBO, un appareil de type Embraer ERJ 170-200 exploité par Sky Regional, effectuait le vol SKV7634 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination de New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY. N65TP, un appareil de type Learjet 45 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Goose Bay (CYYR), NL à destination de CYUL. Lors de la montée initiale, SKV7634 a été autorisé par l’ATC jusqu’à 7000 pieds ASL, et l’autorisation a été relue correctement. Cependant, l’équipage a poursuivi sa montée jusqu’à 7700 pieds ASL, ce qui a réduit l’espacement à 1.1 mille marin sur le plan horizontal et 300 pieds sur le plan vertical avec N65TP, qui était en rapprochement vers CYUL. L’espacement requis de 1000 pieds vertical ou 3 milles marins horizontal n'a pas été assuré.

C-GKWE, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN8987 from Greater Moncton/Romeo Leblanc Intl (CYQM), NB to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During the extension of the flaps on the approach to CYYZ, a Flap Power caution light illuminated and the flaps stopped at the 5° position. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance replaced the main, auxiliary and standby batteries. A test flight was conducted and, following ground checks, no further faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GCWX, a float equipped Murphy Rebel Amateur Built aircraft, was conducting a flight from Kashabowie/Upper Shebandowan Lake (CKF5), ON to Whisper Ice Lake, ON with only the pilot on board. During the landing at Whisper Ice Lake, the pilot lost control of the aircraft, which suddenly dropped onto the surface of the water very hard. The aircraft remained upright, and the pilot was not injured. The engine was shut down, and the pilot paddled the aircraft to the dock. The aircraft sustained damage to the floats, float struts and propeller. Reportedly, engine power was reduced prematurely prior to touchdown.

C-GCUU, a Zenair STOL CH750 amateur-built aircraft departed from Sussex Aerodrome (CCY3), NB with only the pilot on board. The pilot did not advise anyone that he was going flying, so the intent of the flight and the time of departure are unknown. A passer-by noticed the aircraft in a field while driving by and notified the airport owner. The aircraft was discovered around 1830 Atlantic Daylight Time, located about 300 feet west of the runway. The aircraft had impacted the ground in a near vertical position and the pilot, who was the sole occupant, was fatally injured.  The ELT did not activate and no signal was emitted.  For more information regarding this occurrence, please visit our website https://www.tsb.gc.ca/eng/enquetes-investigations/aviation/2019/a19a0047/a19a0047.html. Air transportation safety investigation A19A0047 - tsb.gc.ca

C-GLQJ, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE251 from Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON with 4 crew members and 33 passengers on board. During flap retraction on the initial climb after the departure from CYTZ, the flight crew received a Flap Power caution warning. The flight crew followed the QRH procedures, however the warning remained. The flight continued to CYOW and, since the warning would result in a flapless landing, a PAN PAN was declared. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by, and came to a stop on the runway. ARFF checked the brakes, and cleared the flight crew to taxi to the gate. The operator’s maintenance determined that the fault resulted in the flaps stopping at the 5° position during retraction. The circuit breaker was reset, and subsequent flap operation revealed no further faults; the aircraft was released back to service.

C-GJBB, a privately operated Piper PA-31 aircraft, was conducting flight training at Langley Regional (CYNJ), BC with 2 persons on board. Following multiple simulated engine failures, the pilot-in-command (PIC) and student-pilot noticed that the right engines’s oil pressure indication was in the caution range, with an associated high oil temperature indication. The PIC completed the precautionary engine shutdown, and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without further incident, and required to be towed from the active runway. Maintenance personnel found a pressure relief spring stuck in the open position. Following repairs, the aircraft has returned to service.

C-GUAT, a de Havilland DHC-7-100 aircraft operated by Air Tindi, was conducting flight TID805 from Diavik (CDK2), NT to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with 3 crew members and 31 passengers on board. As the flight crew was executing the pre-takeoff checklist while holding short of the runway, smoke was observed coming from the base of the captain’s control column. The smoke quickly dissipated, and the aircraft returned to the ramp. Passengers were briefed, and deplaned.

C-GVWC, un appareil de type Goodyear Corsair FG 1D en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Ottawa/Gatineau (CYND), QC avec seul le pilote à bord. Alors que le pilote effectuait un posé-décollé sur la piste 09 à CYND, une perte de contrôle directionnelle vers la gauche est survenue. Le pilote a tenté de conserver la maîtrise de l'appareil en utilisant la gouverne de direction ainsi que le frein droit à fond, toutefois sans succès. L'appareil est sorti de piste, et est entré en collision avec un fossé longeant la piste. Le pilote a subi des blessures sérieuses, et l'appareil a été fortement endommagé.

C-GISI, a Cessna 152 aircraft operated by Harv's Air Service, was performing circuits at Steinbach (South) (CKK7), MB with only the student-pilot on board. During one of the landings on Runway 36, the aircraft struck the runway surface with the nose gear first, and overturned. The student-pilot evacuated the aircraft without injury, however the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FWJF, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7267 from Pittsburgh Intl (KPIT), PA to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 3 crew members and 45 passengers on board. Passing FL227 during the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from KPIT, the flight crew received an aural DESCEND TCAS RA command. The flight crew complied with the RA, descended to FL224, and resumed the climb once the CLEAR OF CONFLICT aural message was received. The aircraft continued to destination without further incident.

C-FFWN, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA538 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Anchorage/Ted Stevens Intl (PANC), AK with 5 crew members and 106 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL360 approximately 158 nm north west of CYVR, the flight crew received an ENG 2 FAIL ECAM message. The flight crew completed the associated checklist, secured the engine (CFM56-5A1), declared a MAYDAY, and requested a return to CYVR where the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator's maintenance found metal contamination in the fuel pump, Hydro Mechanical Unit (HMU), fuel-oil heat exchanger, fuel flow transmitter, and servo fuel heater. The engine was changed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

N84GJ, a privately owned amphibious ICON A5 aircraft, was conducting a recreational flight from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Okanagan Lake, BC with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the landing on the lake, the landing gear, still in the extended position, contacted the surface of the water. The aircraft came to rest inverted, with the cockpit canopy detached. The pilot and passenger egressed the submerged aircraft unassisted. Both occupants were not wearing their hydrostatic personal flotation devices, which the pilot had placed in the aircraft. The pilot and passenger were brought to shore by nearby boaters. The pilot sustained minor injuries, and the aircraft was substantially damaged. The ELT activated and its signal was detected.

C-GWJK, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-8-400 exploité par WestJet Encore, effectuait le vol WEN3535 depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Int (CYUL), QC vers Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. C-GOIE, un appareil de type Airbus 321-200 exploité par Air Transat, effectuait le vol TSC546 depuis CYUL, vers Bordeaux/Mérignac (LFBD), France. Simultanément, les 2 appareils se sont positionnés pour leurs décollages respectifs, WEN3535 sur la piste 24R, et TSC546 sur la piste 24L. Les informations disponibles au contrôleur responsable des départs indiquaient que WEN3535 devait effectuer un virage de 30° vers la droite durant la montée initiale; toutefois, cette information n’a pas été transmise à l’équipage par le contrôleur en service. Après que les 2 aéronefs aient reçu leurs instructions de départ respectives, un changement de contrôleur est survenu. Lorsque le contrôleur remplaçant s’est aperçu que WEN3535 n’amorçait pas le virage à droite tel que spécifié dans le système de données, il a instruit l’équipage de virer à droite pour obtenir l’espacement requis. Les trajectoires de décollage étaient parallèles, et l’espacement a conséquemment été réduit à 1.3 mille marin horizontalement, et 900 pieds verticalement avant que WEN3535 n’amorce son virage.

C-GZNW, a privately registered, Amateur-built Safari helicopter, was conducting a second local flight of the morning from Steinbach (CJB3), MB with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. While in a hover taxi, the rotor RPM increased. The pilot attempted to land on the grass infield, however upon touchdown, the helicopter turned on its side. The pilot and the passenger were able to egress uninjured, but the helicopter was destroyed in a post-impact fire. Local EMS and RCMP responded.

C-GJSD, a Bell 206B aircraft operated by Blackcomb Helicopters, was conducting a repositioning flight from Blueberry Bowl, BC to the upper helipad on Grouse Mountain, BC with only the pilot on board. Shortly after takeoff, smoke started to fill the cockpit. The pilot turned off the battery, opened the side window, and made an emergency landing back at the point of departure. Once all electrical power has been turned off, including the generator, the smoke ceased. Subsequent maintenance inspection revealed a faulty directional gyro in the main instrument panel.

C-GZLV, un appareil de type Piper PA-30 Twin Comanche en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis La Crête (CFN5), AB à destination d’Amos/Magny (CYEY), QC avec seul le pilote à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en approche finale pour la piste 14 à CYEY, le pilote a oublié de sortir le train d’atterrissage. L’appareil s’est donc posé sur le ventre, et les hélices sont entrées en contact avec la piste. L’appareil s’est immobilisé après avoir parcouru une distance approximative de 1500 pieds. Le pilote n’a pas été blessé, et a pu évacuer sans difficulté. L’appareil a subi des dommages substantiels, toutefois aucun incendie ne s’est déclaré. Le service d'incendie de la municipalité d'Amos a été avisé, et un véhicule d'urgence ainsi qu'une ambulance ont été déployés.

C-FACT, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-8-300 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA8907 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Greater Moncton/Roméo Leblanc Intl (CYQM), NB à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC avec 3 membres d’équipage et 12 passagers à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en vol de croisière au FL240, un problème de pressurisation est survenu. L’équipage a déclaré un PAN PAN et a effectué une descente rapide jusqu'à 8000 pieds, toutefois sans que les masques d’oxygène des passagers soient déployés. Par la suite, l’équipage a annulé le PAN PAN, et l’appareil a atterri sans encombre à CYUL.

C-FJVV, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8612 from Sudbury (CYSB), ON to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 3 crew members and 22 passengers on board. During landing gear down selection on the final approach to Runway 23 at CYYZ, the right main landing gear indication remained red. The flight crew aborted the approach, executed the QRH, and extended the landing gear using the alternate extension system. Subsequently, a three green light indication was observed. ARFF was requested on standby as a precaution, and the aircraft landed uneventfully. The operator’s maintenance replaced the right gear uplock actuator. Subsequent landing gear operations revealed no further faults, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FPXT, a privately registered Cessna 180G aircraft, was conducting a local flight from North Battleford (CYQW), SK with only the pilot on board. During the landing on the infield grass at CYQW, the pilot applied brakes, and lost directional control. The aircraft ground looped, and came to a rest in an upright position. The pilot was not injured, however the aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left wing. Reportedly, the grass landing surface was wet at the time of landing.

N628FE, a McDonnell Douglas MD-11F aircraft operated by Federal Express, was conducting flight FDX5277 from Paris/Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France to Memphis Intl (KMEM), TN with 4 persons on board. During cruise flight approximately 100 nm north of Gander Intl (CYQX), NL, the flight crew received a number 2 engine Oil Filter Bypass indication. Approximately 30 minutes later, the number 1 autopilot and auto throttle systems disengaged due to the thrust roll back, and the aircraft entered a climb. The flight crew reengaged the auto flight systems, corrected the altitude, then observed an engine number 2 RPM Low indication; additionally, the oil pressure was below the red line, and indicating zero. The flight crew shut the engine down as per the QRH, and diverted the aircraft to Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl (KBOS), MA. Once at the top of the descent, the flight crew declared an emergency, and the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance removed the engine for investigation.

C-IIJJ, un appareil de type Ultra-léger évolué Rans S-6ES Coyote II en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis un aérodrome privé situé dans la région de Mont St-Grégoire, QC avec 1 pilote et 1 passager à bord. L'appareil a été observé en train d’effectuer des cercles à basse altitude au-dessus de vergers dans le secteur de Rougemont, QC, lorsqu'il a perdu de l'altitude. L’appareil s’est écrasé contre des arbres et a été détruit. Les deux occupants ont subi des blessures mortelles.

C-FUJE, an Embraer ERJ170-200 aircraft operated by Sky Regional, was conducting flight SKV7652 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ with 4 crew members and 73 passengers on board. As the flaps were selected during the approach to Runway 22L at KEWR, the aircraft experienced a flap failure. The flight crew abandoned the approach, declared a PAN PAN, and executed the QRH. The subsequent landing was executed with full slats, and flaps 2 without further incident. After the landing, the aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power. The operator’s maintenance replaced the left outboard actuator. The aircraft was released back to service.

C-GBEW, un appareil de type Lake LA-4-200 amphibie en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Montréal/St-Lazare (CST3), QC à destination du lac Biron, QC avec 1 pilote et 1 passager à bord. Lors de l'amerrissage au lac Biron, l'aéronef a effectué deux rebonds avant que le flotteur droit entre en collision avec la surface de l'eau, provoquant le renversement de l’appareil sur le dos. Les deux occupants ont réussi à sortir eux-mêmes de l’aéronef, et ont subi des blessures légères.

C-GTQF, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC971 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 6 crew members and 183 passengers on board. During cruise flight in the vicinity of Brandon (CYBR), MB, turbulence was encountered, and a cabin crew member sustained an injury that prevented from performing their duties. The flight crew was advised, and the flight continued to destination. The cabin crew member's duties were distributed among the remaining flight attendants for the landing.

C-FIRL, a privately registered Cessna 140 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Edmonton/Calmar (MapleLane Farm) (CMF2), AB to Edmonton/Parkland (CPL6), AB to do some circuits with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the rollout after the landing, the aircraft veered to the right. In an effort to control the aircraft, the pilot applied the brakes. The aircraft’s tail tipped up, until the left wing touched the runway and the aircraft rolled over onto its back. There were no injuries, and the ELT was not activated. There was damage to the left wing, vertical stabilizer, landing gear and propeller.

C-FKPT, un appareil de type Airbus 320-200 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA414 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. C-GKTS, un appareil de type Airbus 330-300 exploité par Air Transat, effectuait le vol TSC111 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Paris/Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France à destination de CYUL. ACA414 était sous guidage radar par l’ATC pour la piste 06R, derrière TSC111, en palier à 3000 pieds ASL et aussi sous guidage radar, pour la piste 06L. ACA414 a été autorisé à descendre à 4000 pieds, et a effectué une relecture correcte de l’altitude. L’ATC a détecté une déviation d’altitude alors qu’ACA414 se trouvait à une altitude de 3400 pieds, et a instruit l’équipage de conduite d’effectuer un virage afin d’éviter la turbulence de sillage de TSC111. L’espacement a été réduit à 4 nm sur le plan horizontal, alors que l’espacement requis est de 5 nm ou 1000 pieds. Le contrôleur a émis un avertissement de turbulence de sillage, et les deux appareils se sont posé sans encombre.

C-FHTS, a Bell 214ST helicopter operated by Héli-Transport, was conducting aerial firefighting bucket operations approximately 25 nm east south-east of High Level (CYOJ), AB with only the pilot on board. During the flight, the number 1 engine (General Electric CT7-2A) chip detector light came on briefly. All engine indications were normal, so the pilot continued the flight. Shortly thereafter, the number 1 engine chip detector light intermittently illuminated for 30 seconds, and remained illuminated. The pilot left the bucket circuit, reduced the power, and initiated a return to CYOJ. The checklist was actioned, and the number 1 engine was shut down. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft returned to CYOJ without further incident. There were no injuries to the pilot, and the helicopter received no damage. The operator’s maintenance found a carbon particle on the number 1 chip detector.

OO-SFL, an Airbus 330-343 aircraft operated by Brussels Airlines, was conducting flight BEL515 from Brussels (EBBR), Belgium to Washington/Dulles Intl (KIAD), VA with 10 crew members and 233 passengers on board. During cruise flight at position N5413/W04846, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and executed an oceanic track deviation procedure to return to EBBR. The procedure was elected by the operator since it was discovered during the flight that the required administrative documentation was not on board for the flight into the United States.

C-GMYQ, the Trans North Turbo Air Ltd Bell 206B helicopter, experienced a main rotor strike while uplifting an exploration crew from sloping terrain. The main rotor blades clipped a rock resulting in damage to the main rotor blades, including the tips, and slightly inboard from the blade tips. The pilot was able to safely maneuver the helicopter to a landing site close by, where the helicopter was grounded pending an engineering inspection. There were no injuries. The ELT was not activated.

C-GLPT, un appareil de type Escalade 2060 de construction amateur équipé de flotteurs, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue au départ de la Rivière La Blanche, QC à destination du réservoir Gouin, QC avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Peu après le décollage, le moteur (General Motors L94 Vortec 6.2L) s'est arrêté, et l'aéronef s'est écrasé dans la forêt. Les occupants ont été légèrement blessés, et il n'y a pas eu d'incendie.

C-GFHG, a Super T Aviation Beech 95-B55, was conducting a local training flight from Medicine Hat (CYXH), AB. While on final approach to Runway 27, the aircraft maintained a speed of 110 KIAS. The student pilot initiated a speed reduction; however, the aircraft floated before settling onto the wet runway. Upon touchdown, both the student and instructor applied full braking. The aircraft hydroplaned and was unable stop prior to overrunning the runway. The aircraft maintained centerline until it came to a stop approximately 200 feet beyond the end of the runway. The instructor notified FSS and the aircraft was shut down. The student, instructor and passenger received no injuries. The aircraft received no damage.

C-FHAU, an Aerospatiale AS 350 BA aircraft operated by Expedition Helicopters, was conducting aerial application on an east/west series of fields, 12 nm north northeast of Edam (CJU7), SK with only the pilot on board. The pilot had conducted a reconnaissance flight, and noted a north-south wire on the eastern edge of the second field, from the west. Earlier in the morning, the pilot had completed several east-west passes and had stopped at the mix rig to re-fill the spray tank. Later that evening, the pilot resumed the spraying operation and had completed 2 east-west passes. The pilot was flying to the east from the first field, over a ravine, and into the second field. The pilot noted that the aircraft was approaching the wire too quickly and attempted a quick stop and climb. However, the helicopter caught the wire under the nose. The wire eventually broke, and the pilot maneuvered the helicopter roughly 250 metres to the mix-rig and landed. There were no injuries. The helicopter sustained minor damage to the cargo mirror, lower forward canopy, and punctures of the lower forward fairing.

C-GAKI, a Dornier 228-202 aircraft operated by Alkan Air, was conducting a flight from the Casino Mine Airstrip, YT to Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen Intl (CYXY), YT with 2 crew members and 3 passengers on board. During the climb to cruising altitude after the departure, the flight crew observed a momentary indication of the Master Warning system. The indication did not remain on, and all indicators displayed normal parameters. After levelling off at cruise altitude, the flight crew received another momentary Master Warning system indication. Moments later, the Master Warning system activated again and the number 1 engine low oil pressure light remained lit. The flight crew confirmed that the number 1 engine oil pressure was decreasing, and actioned the emergency procedures checklist. The number 1 engine (Garrett TPE331-5) was shut down, and the propeller was feathered. The flight crew continued to CYXY and, during the approach, the flight crew requested ARFF to standby. A single-engine approach and landing was performed without incident. The operator’s maintenance removed the number 1 engine to conduct further investigation.

C-GHEY, a Cessna 172P aircraft operated by Langley Flying School, was conducting a solo training flight from Langley Regional (CYNJ), BC to practice normal and short field takeoffs and landings with only the student-pilot on board. After a successful stop and go on Runway 01, the student-pilot backtracked the runway in order to perform a soft field takeoff. During the attempt, the aircraft veered left into the grassy knoll abeam Hangar 33, bounced over the berm, and came to rest in a ditch. Soft field takeoffs had not been dual checked by the instructor, nor approved. There had been an apparent miscommunication between the instructor and the student-pilot. The student-pilot was not injured, however the aircraft was substantially damaged. A fuel leak at the side of the runway prevented the use of that portion of the airport for approximately an hour.

C-FRQN, an Embraer ERJ170-200 aircraft operated by Sky Regional, was conducting flight SKV7688 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ with 4 crew members and 67 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew received a GROUND SPOILER FAIL EICAS message. After executing the QRH, the decision to continue to KEWR was elected. Approaching destination, the flight crew requested the longest runway, 22R, and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed long without further incident, with ARFF standing by. The flight crew then notified ATC that everything was normal, and the aircraft taxied to the gate.

C-GKEP, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ100 aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7338 from Columbus/John Glenn Columbus Intl (KCMH), OH to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 3 crew members and 25 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from KCMH, the flight crew stopped the climb at 4000 feet, and requested a return to the airport due to a landing gear disagree. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed without further incident. Since the nose wheel steering was inoperative, the aircraft was towed to the gate.

G-VIIB, a Boeing 777-200 aircraft operated by British Airways, was conducting flight BAW40F from New York/John F Kennedy Intl (KJFK), NY to London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK with 15 crew members and 227 passengers on board. During cruise flight approximately 50 nm north of Gander Intl (CYQX), NL, the cabin crew reported an odour of smoke in the vicinity of the 2R door. The flight crew completed the checklist, and the odour abated after the APU bleed and recirculation fans were turned off. Approximately 45 minutes later, the odour was again noted in the same area, but spreading to the 2L and 2R doors and accompanied by high heat near the overhead lockers. A mist was also observed by the cabin crew. The checklist was run through without any change in conditions. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, requested a diversion to CYQX, and proceeded to jettison 3.5 tons of fuel in order to prevent an overweight landing. The aircraft landed without further incident. The aircraft was later ferried to Cardiff Intl (EGFF), UK, while the operator sent a relief aircraft to take the passengers to EGLL.

C-FRDS, a float-equipped, amateur built Taylorcraft Cub J2 aircraft, departed from Lake Rosseau, ON for a local sightseeing flight with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the initial climb shortly after the departure, the engine (Teledyne Continental C-85-12F X) lost power. The pilot executed a forced landing into a treed area on Tobin Island, and the aircraft was substantially damaged. There were no injuries.

C-GTYR, a Cessna 152 aircraft operated by Skyquest Aviation, was conducting a local training flight from Langley Regional (CYNJ), BC with an instructor and a student-pilot on board. Approximately 0.5 nm on the initial climb after the departure from Runway 19, the engine power reduced to 2000 RPM. The instructor advised ATC of a power loss as the aircraft was not climbing, took over control and prepared for a forced landing; the aircraft crashed into trees just off the end of the runway, across the road south southwest of the airport. Emergency services attended and assisted both occupants, who were uninjured. The aircraft received substantial damage. Fuel was observed leaking from a ruptured fuel tank, and was contained by local firefighters. The occurrence aircraft had been involved in a request for priority landing due to a loss of power event, the day before the accident.

C-GKEM, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7312 from Indianapolis Intl (KIND), IN to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 3 crew members and 36 passengers on board. During the intermediate approach at CYYZ, the flight crew received an Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) fire warning. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and the aircraft landed without further incident on Runway 24R with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance found the APU thermocouple faulty and replaced it in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) 49-61-03-04. Subsequent testing revealed no further indicating faults, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GZCF, a Lockheed 188C Electra aircraft operated by Air Spray (1967), was conducting ferry flight ASB490 from Slave Lake (CYZH), AB to Red Deer Regional (CYQF), AB with 2 pilots and 2 aircraft maintenance engineers on board. During landing gear retraction on departure from CYZH, the left main landing gear did not retract properly. As the flight crew continued the flight to CYQF, various attempts to extend the landing gear were made while troubleshooting, however none were successful. Subsequently, the decision to land the aircraft with all landing gears retracted was made. In preparation for the landing, the aircraft dumped fuel and ARFF was placed on standby for the arrival. The aircraft touched down on Runway 35, and came to rest approximately half way down the runway, with the right wing in the grass on the east side of the runway. The flight crew evacuated; there were no injuries or post-landing fire. There was some minor damage to the belly mounted retardant tank and to all blades on the four propellers.Update 5 July 2019. The operator's maintenance determined that the forward door mechanism (P/N 810265) and gear roller (P/N S14-7625) clearance were found to exceed the requirements described in service bulletin  88/SB-558 and maintenance manual 32-0, paragraph 1.C (f).

N987NN, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL1111 from Dallas-Fort Worth Intl (KDFW), TX to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. AAL1111 landed on Runway 24L at CYYZ, was instructed to exit on Taxiway D6 located at the end of the runway, and to hold short of Runway 24R. After exiting on D6, the aircraft crossed over the hold short line for Runway 24R, causing the stop bar alarm to activate in the tower; however the aircraft did not proceed onto the runway. At the same time, EJA545, a Cessna Citation Latitude aircraft operated by NetJets, was departing off of Runway 24R, but was airborne by the time it crossed Taxiway D6.

C-FWSK, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA662 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 5 crew members and 134 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the cabin crew noted an acrid odour, accompanied by haze in the cabin. The flight crew was advised, and checklist items for Smoke/Fumes were completed. The odour dissipated after the checklist was completed, however, the flight crew elected to divert to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. An emergency was declared, and the subsequent landing was uneventful. The operator's maintenance determined that a malfunctioning recirculation fan was the source of the odour and haze.

C-FTVJ, a privately owned, amateur built Maranda AMF S14 aircraft, was conducting a local pleasure flight from Thessalon Muni (abandoned), ON with only the pilot on board. During the initial climb at approximately 300 feet AGL after the departure, the engine (Avco Lycoming O-290-G) lost power. The pilot switched the fuel selector to the main fuel tank, however the engine did not regain power. The aircraft impacted trees approximately 300 feet from the end of the runway, and was substantially damaged. The pilot was not injured. The pilot had recently acquired the aircraft, and the previous flight on the same day revealed no faults with the engine.

C-FFJA a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ 200 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8797 from Fredericton Intl (CYFC), NB to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON with 3 crew members and 35 passengers on board. Climbing through 900 feet during the departure from CYFC, the flight crew received a right hand 14th stage duct master warning light. The flight crew climbed to a safe altitude, and requested vectors back to CYFC. At the completion of the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH), the light did not extinguish. The number 2 engine power was reduced to idle, a PAN PAN was declared, and vectors for the ILS Runway 09 were requested. The aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance replaced the number 2 engine bleed air leak control and the isolation shutoff valve. The aircraft was released back to service.

C-FCDT, a float-equipped de Havilland DHC-2 MK. I aircraft operated by Air Nootka, was conducting a flight from Mooyah Bay, BC to Gold River (CAU6), BC with only the pilot on board. During the take-off run, the aircraft's left float was punctured after contacting a partially submerged log. The pilot rejected the takeoff, and evacuated with a life vest as the aircraft overturned and partially sank. The pilot sustained minor injuries, and was transported to Gold River by a nearby Coast Guard vessel. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The ELT did not activate.

C-FJUU, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Campbell Helicopters, was conducting local aerial firefighting operations from High Level (CYOJ), AB with only the pilot on board. During the first flight of the day, the pilot inadvertently depressed the cargo release button. The Bambi bucket and longline jettisoned from the helicopter, and landed in a wooded area. There was no damage or injuries to any ground based structures, or personnel. The helicopter returned to CYOJ and was not damaged.

C-FKFM, a Convair 580 aircraft operated by Conair Group, was conducting local aerial firefighting operations as flight FDG454 from Whitecourt (CYZU), AB with only the 2 pilots on board. Shortly after the IFR departure in clouds, the flight crew noticed that the cabin started to fill with smoke. The cockpit remained relatively clear of smoke. The flight crew declared an emergency, and returned to CYZU. During the descent as power was reduced, the smoke was observed to reduce. When power was increased, the smoke began to increase again. The flight crew actioned the checklist, and conducted an uneventful landing. The aircraft was able to taxi back to the apron and shutdown normally. The operator’s maintenance found burnt duct tape on the insulation of the tail de-icing ductwork.

C-FWGH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG774 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Río Hato/Scarlett Martinez Intl, (MPSM), Panamá with 7 crew members and 145 passengers on board. Shortly after entering Panama's airspace at FL370, the flight was approaching an area of moderate convective weather and required to deviate to avoid it. As the frequency was extensively congested, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN in order to establish priority handling. Approximately 1 minute later, ATC contacted the flight crew and authorized the deviation. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FKGL, a Basler Turbo Conversion TP-67 equipped Douglas DC-3C aircraft operated by North Star Air, was conducting a flight from Fort Hope (CYFH), ON to Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON with 2 pilots on board. Shortly after the takeoff from CYFH, both engines (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-67R) lost power. The flight crew executed a forced landing on Eabamet Lake, ON and after the landing, evacuated the aircraft via the main cabin door and swam to shore. Nishnawbe Aski Police Service responded, and transported the flight crew back to the community. There were no injuries.

C-FRKG, a Piper PA-31 Navajo aircraft operated by the Rockcliffe Flying Club, was conducting touch & go’s on Runway 09 at Ottawa/Gatineau (CYND), QC with 2 pilots on board. During the initial climb following the third takeoff at approximately 400 feet AGL, the right engine lost power. The flight crew feathered the propeller, carried out the applicable checklist, and declared a MAYDAY. A single-engine approach and landing was carried out at CYND without further incident.  The operator’s maintenance performed an inspection and identified a faulty Fuel Control Unit.

C-FFJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8798 from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON to Fredericton Intl (CYFC), NB with 4 crew members and 49 passengers on board. During the descent into CYFC, the flight crew received a right hand 14th stage duct warning message. The flight crew executed the QRH, and the message cleared. An emergency was declared, and the flight landed without further incident with ARFF standing by.

C-GLQB, a DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE458 from Montreal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON. During the descent into CYTZ, the flight crew experienced hydraulic issues, and declared an emergency. A diversion to Hamilton (CYHM), ON was elected, and the aircraft landed on Runway 30. During the rollout after touchdown, all main landing gear tires blew, and the aircraft was disabled on the runway. There were no reported injuries.

C-FYSH, a privately registered Luscombe 8A aircraft, was conducting a local flight from Cornwall Regional (CYCC), ON with only the pilot on board. During the landing on Runway 28, the aircraft bounced and became airborne again. On the subsequent touchdown, the aircraft started to swerve to the left. The pilot countered right, and the aircraft swerved to the right, then departed the surface of the runway. The aircraft came to rest on its nose in a ditch, and received substantial damage. The left landing gear leg was damaged, however it is not known whether it was damaged during the landing, or the excursion. The owner is investigating the possibility that the left landing gear leg failed during touchdown, which could explain the initial swerve to the left. The aircraft was equipped with a 4 point safety belt, and the pilot was wearing the lap belt and shoulder harness portion at the time. The pilot was not injured.

C-FLJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 CRJ900 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8206 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Sydney/J.A. Douglas McCurdy (CYQY), NS with 4 crew members and 78 passengers on board. Upon flaps selection during the approach into CYQY, the flight crew received a flap fault caution message. The flaps stopped at 8 degrees and the slats at 20 degrees. No emergency was declared, however ARFF was on standby for the landing. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GCZS, an Aerospatiale AS 355 F2 helicopter operated by Zimmer Air Services, was conducting forestry application 20 nm north of Dryden/Best Western (Heli) (CKV3), ON with only the pilot on board. During the flight, there was a loud bang, followed by a number 2 engine (Rolls Royce 250-C20R) chip light. The pilot reduced the power, and began to manoeuvre to a cut block where a safe landing could be made. Approximately 10 seconds later, the pilot noted that the fuel filter warning light had illuminated. The pilot elected to jettison 150 litres of spray, and informed the company by radio that an emergency landing would be conducted. Approximately 30 seconds later, the engine fire warning light illuminated. Another helicopter in the area reported to the pilot that the aircraft was on fire. A safe landing was conducted, and the pilot exited the helicopter uninjured. The aircraft was subsequently destroyed by fire. Initial inspection revealed that the number 2 engine had sustained an uncontained failure of the 3rd stage power turbine. On site examination of the wreckage revealed that high velocity pieces of the power turbine section had penetrated the engine compartment fire-shield above the fuel tank.Examination of the 3rd stage power turbine wheel of the number 2 engine, revealed that a turbine blade had fractured. The liberated parts severely damaged the exhaust collector and penetrated a compressor discharge tube of the number 1 engine. Metallurgical examination of the 3rd stage turbines wheels of both engines revealed fatigue cracking in the trailing edge of a number of blades on both wheels. Both 3rd stage turbine wheels were post CEB-1365 (Commercial Engine Bulletin) “enhanced” turbine assembly configuration. The pattern and appearance of the blade fracture was similar to a number of other failures of post CEB-1365 3rd stage turbine wheels.

C-FENO, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3150 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 4 crew members and 53 passengers on board. During the initial approach into CYYC, one of the flight attendants was unable to perform their duties. The flight crew discontinued the approach to allow time for the other flight attendant to prepare the cabin for the landing. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GJJA, a Bell 206B aircraft operated by Qwest Helicopters, was conducting heli-slinging operations in support of a reforestation project, approximately 8 nm west of Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB with only the pilot on board. While maneuvering after setting down a load of tree saplings, the helicopter contacted a set of unmarked 240 kV power lines. The windshield and centre post were damaged, and one main rotor blade cut one of the power lines. The helicopter was not equipped with a wire strike kit. The pilot managed to maintain control, and set the helicopter down in a nearby cut block. The pilot was not injured, and was wearing a helmet with the visor in the down position. The helicopter sustained substantial damage.

C-FVBF, a Cessna 188 AGwagon aircraft, was departing from a local airstrip approximately 13 nm south of Lloydminster (CYLL), AB for a local pleasure flight with only the pilot on board. The aircraft take off towards the south, with an easterly wind. Directional control was lost during the take-off roll, and the aircraft came to rest beside the runway. Damage to the aircraft included the left wing, collapsed left landing gear, and propeller. The spray hopper was empty, and the pilot was uninjured.

C-GYJR, a Cessna A188B aircraft operated by Western Canadian Aerial, was on a local flight from Neepawa (CJV5), MB to conduct upper air-work and practice dry spray runs. The pilot selected a field, and circled to inspect the area to set up a dry spray pattern. The pilot flew passes at tree top height, before descending down to spray height for more passes. On the accident pass, the pilot pulled over a group of trees too late, and had to push the aircraft down harder to get back to spray height. However, the pull-up manoeuver was made too late; the aircraft contacted the ground, and slid to a stop. The pilot was uninjured, and exited the aircraft. The ELT activated and was detected by CMCC. There was no fire, and the aircraft was not carrying any chemicals. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FMWP, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1923 from Prague/Václav Havel (LKPR), Czech Republic to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 8 crew members and 248 passengers on board. During cruise flight over the Atlantic ocean in the vicinity of 62N/020W, one of the cabin crew members became incapacitated due to illness, and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight. Duties were distributed to the other cabin crew members, and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

Le 17 juin 2019, un aéronef Piper PA-23-250 (immatriculation C-GDUL, numéro de série 27-3986) exploité par Cargair ltée effectuait un vol voyage de nuit, selon les règles de vol à vue à partir de l’aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert (Québec) avec un survol de l’aéroport international de Québec/Jean Lesage (Québec) et l’aéroport de Trois-Rivières (Québec). Il y avait à bord 1 pilote et 1 passager, qui était aussi un instructeur. Lors de l’approche à l’aéroport de Trois-Rivières (Québec), la décision d’effectuer un posé-décollé a été prise. Pendant la course au décollage, les hélices des 2 moteurs sont entrées en contact avec la surface de la piste. L’aéronef a décollé, a viré vers la gauche et, par la suite, le pilote a perdu la maîtrise de l’aéronef. L’aéronef est entré en collision avec le sol à 222 pieds au sud de la piste 23 le 18 juin à 0 h 09, heure avancée de l’Est. Aucun signal de la radiobalise de repérage d’urgence émettant sur 406 MHz n’a été reçu. Suite à l’impact, un incendie s’est déclaré et l’aéronef a été détruit. Les 2 occupants ont pu évacuer l’aéronef. Le premier a subi des blessures légères et le deuxième, des blessures graves.

C-GHQY, a Boeing 787-8 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA895 from Milan/Malpensa (LIMC), Italy to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 11 crew members and 273 passengers on board. After the entry door was closed following completion of the boarding at LIMC, the bridge came into contact with the number 1 engine as it was being removed from the aircraft. The engine nacelle was punctured, and the aircraft had to be removed from service for repairs. The flight was cancelled. The nose cowl skin was punctured at the 02:00 O’clock position (aft looking forward). The aircraft was returned to service following repairs.

C-GBFH, a Bell 206B aircraft operated by Blackcomb Helicopters, was conducting mining support operation approximately 57 nm north west of Pemberton (CYPS), BC with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. While landing on a gravel road at approximately 6600 feet ASL, the helicopter touched down perpendicular to the road, with the tail out over the embankment. When the pilot was performing a seating check, it was noticed that the helicopter was tipping aft. The pilot pushed the cyclic forward to correct the tipping motion, however the skid gear was seated too far aft on the side of the road; as a result, the nose of the helicopter pitched up, the helicopter slid backwards approximately 25 feet down the embankment, then rolled onto its left side. The occupants exited the helicopter with only minor injuries. One of the passengers was taken to the hospital as precautionary measure. There was a small post-crash fire, which was extinguished with the onboard fire extinguisher. The 406 MHz ELT activated, and the signal was received by JRCC.

C-GFCC, a Bell 407 aircraft operated by Blackcomb Helicopters, was conducting external load operations approximately 30 nm north west of Pemberton (CYPS), BC with only the pilot on board. Shortly after the final load was placed on the ground, the pilot inadvertently released the belly hook. There were no injuries.

C-FVMV, a privately operated Piper PA-15X aircraft, was conducting a recreational flight north east of Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC with only the pilot on board. During the return flight to a private airstrip approximately 9 nm north east of Vancouver/Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC, the aircraft experienced a partial loss of engine performance, associated with high internal engine temperature indications. The pilot attempted a precautionary landing at the private airstrip, however the aircraft bounced on touchdown. A go-around was initiated, but engine power was insufficient to maintain flight; as a result, the pilot conducted an emergency landing in a field, just north of the airstrip. When the aircraft made contact with the long grass in the field, it nosed over and came to rest inverted. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. There were no injuries.

C-GEFA, an Airbus 330-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA828 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Lyon/St-Exupery (LFLL), France with 10 crew members and 218 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew received a F/CTL FLAP SYS 2 FAULT ECAM message. The flight crew executed the QRH and, upon arrival at destination, declared a PAN PAN. A flapless approach and landing was carried out without further incident, with ARFF standing by.The operator’s maintenance tested the Slat/Flap Computers 1 & 2, and checked the Torque Limiters. The flaps operated normally, and no further faults were found. The aircraft however experienced another similar event on the following flight (see A19Q0079).

C-FVTS, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Tasman Helicopters, was conducting forest fire-fighting operations near Steen River (CFB7), AB with 1 pilot on board. During bucketing operations at approximately 300 feet AGL, the pilot observed that the number 2 engine fire light had illuminated. The pilot followed the emergency procedures for an engine fire indication, and subsequently discharged both fire retardant bottles. The right engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6T-3) was shut down, and a successful single-engine approach and landing was completed.The operator’s maintenance found that a fire detector amplifier was unserviceable.

N12167, un appareil de type Embraer EMB-145XR exploité par ExpressJet Airlines, effectuait le vol ASQ4074 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination de Chicago/O'Hare Intl (KORD), IL. À environ 23 miles marins à l'ouest de CYUL, l'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence en raison d’une fuite de carburant, et a demandé un retour vers CYUL où un atterrissage a été effectué sans autre incident.

C-FENB, a float-equipped Noorduyn UC-64A aircraft operated by Wings Over Kississing, was conducting a flight from Thompson (CKD6), MB to Big Sand Lake, MB with only the pilot on board. During a glassy water landing, the aircraft impacted the water. Both pontoons failed, and the aircraft sank almost immediately. With difficulty, the pilot was able to exit the right hand rear door after unhooking some cargo netting, and swam to a damaged pontoon. Subsequently, the pilot was rescued by a boat. The aircraft was submerged and sustained substantial damage. The pilot received minor injuries.

C-FICU, a Beech 200 aircraft operated by Missinippi Airways, was conducting flight MA04 from Red Sucker Lake (CYRS), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with 3 crew members and 2 passengers on board. Shortly after the touchdown on Runway 18 at CYWG, a hand-held fire extinguisher accidentally discharged. The flight crew declared an emergency, exited onto Taxiway K, and brought the aircraft to a stop. The aircraft was evacuated, and towed to the apron. The operator's maintenance cleaned the fire extinguisher residue from the aircraft interior.

C-FDIZ, a float equipped de Havilland DHC-3 Otter aircraft operated by Osprey Wings, was conducting a flight from Stony Rapids (CKW5), SK to Points North Landing (CKC2), SK with only the pilot on board. The pilot had the middle rope untied after starting the engine, and the aircraft began to pivot away from the dock. After the aft rope was released, the aircraft proceeded to turn out. The current was stronger than anticipated, and the left wing tip dragged over the left horizontal stabilizer of C-FVOG, a de Havilland DHC-6 Twin Otter aircraft, that was secured to the dock. Both aircraft sustained minor damage.

N14198, an Embraer EMB-145XR aircraft operated by CommutAir, was conducting flight UCA4961 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ with 3 crew members and 48 passengers on board. During the initial climb out of CYUL, a bird was ingested into the left engine. The engine rolled back, then spooled back up to normal operation. The flight crew briefly smelled an odour, and proceeded to turn off the number 1 bleed; the smell dissipated. Both ignition switches were turned on, a MAYDAY was declared, and an immediate return to CYUL was initiated where the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance completed a compressor wash, along with a borescope inspection of the engine. The damages were within limits, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GONV, un appareil de construction amateur de type PITTS S-2E, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Saint-Jean-Port-Joli, QC à destination de Montréal/Aéroparc Île Perrot (CSP6), QC avec 1 pilote et 1 passager à bord.
