Suite au décollage de la piste 24 à Saint-Jean-Port-Joli, l'appareil a été observé prendre de l'altitude, s'incliner sur la gauche, perdre de l'altitude, et s'écraser dans un fossé en bordure d'une route à environ 120 mètres au sud de l'aéroport. L'appareil a été détruit par les forces de l'impact. Un début d'incendie s'est déclaré, mais a toutefois été rapidement maitrisé par des gens qui se trouvaient à proximité, et qui ont porté assistance aux 2 occupants. Le passager a subi des blessures mortelles, alors que le pilote a subi des blessures graves. La radiobalise d'urgence (ELT) s'est activée à l'impact.

CF-TDZ, a privately owned Consolidated Vultee Aircraft Corporation Stinson 108-1 aircraft, was departing from Fairview (CEB5), AB with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the take-off roll on Runway 22, directional control was lost, and the aircraft nosed over. The reported winds were out of the south at 8 to 12 knots. The aircraft sustained damage to the wings, tail and propeller. The two occupants received minor injuries. The 121.5 MHz ELT activated.

C-FBDT, un appareil de type Pilatus PC-12/47E exploité par Flightpath Charter Airways, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments en provenance de Teterboro (KTEB), NJ à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. EJA621, un appareil de type Cessna 680A exploité par Netjets Aviation, était en provenance de White Plains/Westchester County (KHPN), NY aussi à destination de CYUL. Avant de pénétrer dans l’espace aérien canadien à environ 30 nm au sud de CYUL, le Centre de contrôle de Boston (KZBW) a transféré le contrôle des deux appareils au Centre de contrôle de Montréal (CZUL), alors que l'espacement entre les deux appareils était réduit à 3.6 nm et 500 pieds, de sorte qu'une perte d’espacement est survenue lorsque les appareils sont entrés dans l'espace aérien canadien, la norme étant de 4 nm ou 1000 pieds.

C-GPAT, un appareil de type Airbus 310-300 exploité par Air Transat, effectuait le vol TSC639 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Nice/Côte d'Azur (LFMN), France à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC avec 9 membres d'équipage et 203 passagers à bord. Alors que l'appareil était à environ 175 nm au nord est de CYUL, un ordinateur de poche utilisé pour les ventes en cabine a été observé émanant de la fumée, et il a également été noté que sa pile était devenue chaude. L'appareil a été placé dans un contenant rempli d'eau, et le vol s'est poursuivi sans problème jusqu'à CYUL où l’appareil s'est posé sans difficulté. L'ordinateur de poche a été acheminé au fournisseur de service pour fin d’analyse.

C-GJAZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8892 from Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen Intl (CYXY), YT to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 4 crew members and 66 passengers on board. Approximately 45 minutes after the departure from CYXY, one of the cabin crew members experienced a medical incident, and was unable to continue duties. An employee from a parent company travelling as a passenger assisted with first aid. The aircraft continued to destination without further incident, and was met by paramedics at the gate.

C-FANF, a Boeing 737-500 aircraft operated by Air North Charter and Training, was conducting flight ANT536 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen Intl (CYXY), YT with 5 crew members and 104 passengers on board. After the engines were shut down and deplaning of passengers had begun at CYXY, smoke was observed in the cabin and the flight deck. The remaining passengers were rapidly deplaned via the L1 door, while the flight crew turned off the air conditioning packs, recirculation fans, and the APU. ARFF was requested by the flight crew, and arrived shortly afterward. The operator’s maintenance observed oil in the compressor section of the APU, and suspected an oil seal leak. The APU was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FQNG, a Sikorsky S-61N aircraft operated by VIH Helicopters, was conducting heli-logging operations approximately 25 nm north of Bella Bella (Campbell Island) (CBBC), BC with 2 pilots on board. During the heli-logging operation, the flight crew observed smoke in the cockpit, followed by a number 2 generator failure caution light. The flight crew found a suitable landing site, and executed a precautionary landing without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced the number 2 generator, and the helicopter was returned to service.

N403UA, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL2754 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to San Francisco Intl (KSFO), CA with only the 2 pilots on board. Shortly after the departure, the flight crew received a AC ESS BUSS fault on the ECAM, and a loss of the number 2 electrical bus. The flight crew declared an emergency, and initiated a return to CYVR where the aircraft landed without further incident. A post-flight maintenance inspection identified a faulty right engine Integrated Drive Generator (IDG).

C-FRCY, a private Jodel F-10 Amateur-Built aircraft, was conducting a flight from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK to Saskatoon/Richter Field (CRF5), SK with 1 pilot on board. The purpose of the flight was to conduct circuits and on the third landing, the aircraft bounced twice before the pilot attempted a go-around. However, the left wing touched the ground, and the aircraft crashed on the left side of the runway. The pilot sustained minor injuries, and was able to exit the aircraft. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FARE, a Bell 407 aircraft operated by Arrowhead Helicopters, was conducting an external load, long line operation from Points North Landing (CYNL), SK to Milton Lake, SK with only the pilot on board. Shortly after the takeoff out of CYNL at approximately 50 feet AGL, the pilot felt a sudden jerk, and the slung load dropped. The pilot maintained control of the helicopter, and landed without further incident.It was reported that the long line was incorrectly attached to the load.

C-FZRM, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA230 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with 6 crew members and 100 passengers on board. During cruise flight, turbulence was encountered and a cabin crew member sustained an injury that prevented from performing their duties. The flight crew was advised, and the flight continued to destination. The cabin crew member's duties were distributed among the remaining flight attendants for the landing.

C-GAWP, un appareil de type Pilatus PC-12/45 exploité par Pascan Aviation, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU), QC à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC avec 2 pilotes et 1 passager à bord. Lors de la descente pour l’approche de la piste 29 à CYQB, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison d’une fissure apparue dans le pare-brise du côté droit. L’appareil a atterri sans encombre et les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

C-FHOY, an Embraer ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA547 from Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 4 crew members and 80 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL320 in the vicinity of Albany Intl (KALB), NY, the aircraft experienced a failure of the L/H wing anti-ice system. The flight crew initially declared a PAN PAN, then elevated the emergency to a MAYDAY as there was potential for icing during the descent. The aircraft landed at CYYZ without further incident approximately 50 minutes later.The operator’s maintenance carried out tests in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) and the Fault Isolation Manual (FIM). The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GZIQ, un appareil de construction amateur de type Adventure Plane sur flotteurs, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le Lac Viceroy, QC à destination du Lac Itomamo, QC dans les Monts Valin avec seul le pilote à bord. Lors de l’approche finale sur le Lac Itomamo, le pilote a rencontré un cisaillement de vent important, ainsi qu’un vent traversier plus important que prévu. Après le touché initial des flotteurs sur la surface du lac, l’appareil a rebondi. L’aile droite a été soulevée soudainement par une rafale de vent, abaissant l’aile gauche qui est entrée en collision avec la surface de l’eau, et a provoqué le renversement de l’appareil. Le pilote a réussi à évacuer l’appareil submergé, et a nagé en direction de la rive. Le pilote a été secouru par une embarcation, et n’a pas été blessé. L’appareil était muni d’un ELT de type 406 MHz, mais aucun signal n’a été capté par le JRCC suite à l’impact.

C-FFPH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines on behalf of TUI Airways, was conducting flight TOM1585 from Kerkyra/Ioannis Kapodistrias Intl (LGKR), Greece to Aberdeen/Dyce (EGPD), UK with 6 crew members and 189 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from LGKR, a cabin crew member became sick. The flight crew contacted Medlink, and a nurse came forward to assist. The medical condition of the cabin crew member improved through the flight, however duties could not be performed. Positions were re-assigned for the landing, and the flight was completed without further incident.

N116DA, un appareil de type Cessna 560XL exploité par Contour Aviation, effectuait le vol VTE116 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination d’Atlanta/Dekalb-Peachtree (KPDK), GA avec 2 personnes à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en montée initiale à 1300 pieds ASL, la lumière d’indication bas niveau de la pression d’huile du moteur gauche (PW545A) s’est allumée. L’équipage a alors vérifié les indicateurs de niveau de pression et de température d’huile du moteur gauche, qui indiquaient également bas. Le moteur gauche a été fermé, et l’équipage a déclaré une urgence. La liste de vérification applicable du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée par l’équipage, et l’appareil est revenu se poser sur la piste 24L sans encombre. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

C-GUON, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-8-300 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA727 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. C-GSKU, un appareil de type Beech 1900C exploité par Skylink Express, effectuait le vol SLQ739 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis CYQB à destination de Montréal Intl (Mirabel) (CYMX), QC. Lors de la transmission de l’autorisation de décollage de la piste 29 par le contrôleur aérien, l’équipage du JZA727 a reçu et relu l’instruction supplémentaire d’effectuer un virage à gauche au cap 210°. Lorsque le contrôleur a observé JZA727 amorcer un virage à gauche, il a autorisé SLQ739 à décoller de la piste 29. Peu de temps après, JZA727 a amorcé un virage vers la droite. Le contrôleur a alors instruit JZA727 de tourner à gauche afin de libérer la trajectoire de décollage de SLQ739. Le radar a indiqué qu’au plus près, les 2 aéronefs étaient à une distance horizontale de 0.7 mille marin. L’espacement requis était que JZA727 soit en virage à gauche et dégagé de la trajectoire de décollage de SLQ739.

C-FNVV, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA717 from New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 5 crew members and 146 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew reported hearing loud noises in the cabin ducting. After consultation with the operator’s maintenance, the flight crew descended to 10 000 feet, and continued to CYYZ. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance found the number 1 pack downstream valve broken. The valve was replaced in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM), and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-IKFS, un appareil Ultra-léger de base de type Sky Raider II en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Roxton Falls, QC avec 1 pilote et 1 passager à bord. Environ 15 minutes après le décollage alors qu’il volait à 1000 pieds au sud et en rapprochement d’Acton Vale, QC, le moteur a présenté des ratés. Le pilote a activé le système de réchauffage du carburateur, a vérifié que la pompe d’alimentation électrique du carburant était fonctionnelle, et que les deux robinets d’arrêt carburant étaient ouverts. Après quelques ratés, le moteur s’est arrêté. Le pilote s’est dirigé vers un champ afin d’y effectuer un atterrissage d’urgence. L’appareil a percuté le sol, et le train d’atterrissage s’est cassé sous l’impact. Une fois l’appareil immobilisé, le pilote a fermé les deux robinets d’arrêt carburant. Le pilote et le passager ont été blessés sérieusement, et ont été transportés à l’hôpital. Un examen sommaire de l’appareil a permis de constater que le réservoir de carburant de l’aile gauche était vide, et que le réservoir de l’aile droite contenait environ 5 gallons. Le système de réchauffage du carburateur était fonctionnel, le filtre à essence ne présentait pas de signe de contamination, il y avait de l'essence dans les 2 carburateurs, et la pompe d’alimentation électrique était fonctionnelle. Au moment de l'examen, le réservoir collecteur de la cabine était vide.

C-GESS, a privately registered Cessna TU206A aircraft on amphibious floats, was conducting a flight from Cree Lake, SK to Cold Lake Regional (CEN5), AB with only the pilot on board. During the crosswind takeoff run from Cree Lake, the aircraft encountered severe wind and waves as the aircraft approached 2 islands. The pilot elected to abort the takeoff and, as the aircraft decelerated, the left wing rose and the right float dug in the water. The right wing contacted the water and the aircraft came to a stop in a nose down, vertical attitude. The pilot was not injured, released the lap belt and shoulder harness, exited the aircraft through the pilot's door, and inflated the personal flotation device. The aircraft was towed close to shore, righted, and then towed onto the shore. The aircraft sustained damage to the right wing.

C-FYKR, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA578 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Los Angeles Intl (KLAX), CA with 5 crew members and 104 passengers on board. During the downwind approach to Runway 24R at approximately 4000 feet ASL at KLAX, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to CLIMB. The flight crew followed the resolution advisory, and the aircraft continued for the landing without further incident.

C-GKEL, a privately operated, amateur built Van's RV-9A aircraft, was departing from Runway 08 at Stouffville (CBB2), ON, intending to join the circuit to conduct a few touch-and-go's. The owner of the aircraft, who was sitting in the right seat, was providing familiarization training to another pilot, seated on the left. The non-owner began the take-off roll and, mid way through the manoeuvre, the owner took control as he determined that the aircraft was not accelerating normally. The aircraft departed the end of the runway, still on the ground, struck a berm, and slid along the ground before flipping over. The canopy broke, and the two pilots were able to egress without significant difficulty. The owner was wearing a 5-point seatbelt and received significant injuries, whereas the other pilot was wearing 4 of the available 5 points, and received minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GWBU, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1229 from Orlando Intl (KMCO), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. Following the landing on Runway 06R at CYYZ, the flight crew exited on high-speed Taxiway D5, and received instructions from ATC to hold short of Runway 06L. As the tower controller perceived that the aircraft was approaching the hold short line too fast, WJA1229 was instructed to stop. When the aircraft came to a complete stop, it had crossed the hold short line and caused a STOP BAR alarm in the control tower. However, the aircraft did not enter the runway. Another aircraft was departing from Runway 06L at the time, but it was airborne by the time it reached Taxiway D5.

N645GT, a Boeing 767-324 aircraft operated by Atlas Air Inc. was conducting flight GTI8473 from Frankfurt-Hahn (EDFH), Germany to Portsmouth/Pease Intl (KPSM), NH. 450 nm north east of Goose Bay (CYYR), NL at position N58.0 W049.44, the flight crew smelled smoke in the cockpit, and requested a diversion to CYYR. After declaring an emergency, the aircraft landed without further incident. Upon investigation, it was discovered that the fault was the forward equipment cooling and exhaust fan.

C-GEFA, un appareil de type Airbus 330-300 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA829 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Lyon/St-Exupéry (LFLL), France à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC avec 10 membres d'équipage et 245 passagers à bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait à environ 60 nm à l’est de CYUL, l’équipage a déployé les becs de bord d’attaque et a reçu un message indiquant que les volets étaient verrouillés. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence, et l’appareil s’est posé sans autre difficulté avec les volets rentrés sur la piste 24L. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. Le personnel de l'entretien a remplacé le bras d'interconnexion (interconnecting strut) de l'aile droite et l'appareil a été remis en service. L’appareil a connu le même problème sur le segment précédant celui-ci (voir A19F0159).

C-GFEZ, un appareil de construction amateur de type Zenair CH250 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Sherbrooke (CYSC), QC avec 2 personnes à bord. Le pilote aux commandes de l'appareil effectuait son premier vol sur ce type d’appareil en compagnie d’un autre pilote, qui avait de l’expérience de pilotage sur ce même type. Après quelques circuits, le pilote aux commandes a effectué une approche stable en vue d’un atterrissage sur la piste 31. Lors de l'arrondi avant l'atterrissage, la vitesse de l’appareil est descendue sous la limite de la vitesse de décrochage. L’appareil s’est enfoncé, et a rebondi en touchant le sol. Une remise des gaz a été effectuée afin de tenter de récupérer la vitesse et la maîtrise de l’appareil, main en vain; l’appareil a dévié vers la gauche. Après le deuxième rebond, la roue de nez a été arrachée, et le train d'atterrissage principal droit s’est affaissé. L’appareil s’est immobilisé environ 100 pieds du côté sud à la mi-piste. Les 2 occupants n’ont pas été blessés. L’appareil a subi des dommages importants.

C-GUYQ, un hélicoptère de type Robinson R44 en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue au départ de Montréal/Les Cèdres (CSS3), QC, et prévoyait un retour au même endroit. À son arrivée à Ste-Barbe, QC, le pilote a effectué une approche au-dessus de l’eau, dont la surface était animée par des vagues. Le pilote a maintenu l’appareil en vol stationnaire à environ 200 pieds du bord de la rive, toutefois il a éprouvé des difficultés à maintenir la stabilité et à conserver la distance verticale au-dessus de l’eau en raison de rafales de vent provenant de la droite. Sentant que l’appareil se déportait rapidement vers la gauche, le pilote a appliqué du cyclique vers la droite afin de corriger la dérive soudaine. Cependant, l’hélicoptère a basculé et les pales du rotor principal sont entrées en contact avec la surface de l’eau. L’hélicoptère s’est renversé, et s’est immobilisé sur son côté gauche à moitié submergé. Le pilote a pu évacuer sans difficulté, et n’a pas été blessé. Aucun signal de la radiobalise de repérage d’urgence n’a été capté par le Centre conjoint de coordination des opérations de sauvetage (CCCOS).

C-GNJM, a Beech C 23 Sundowner aircraft operated by Aviation MH, was conducting a flight from Riviere-du-Loup (CYRI), QC to Grand Falls (CCK3), NB with only the pilot on board. As the private pilot was landing on the 40-foot wide asphalt portion of Runway 16 at CCK3, the left main landing gear exited the asphalt. There was a slight drop between the asphalt and the turf/gravel on the sides of the runway. As the pilot experienced difficulty controlling the aircraft, full power was applied for a go-around, however during the early stages of the climb, the aircraft started heading toward the hangars on the south-east end of the airport. The pilot attempted to avoid the hangars by turning to the left over a forested area and continuing the climb. The aircraft contacted treetops before the aircraft stalled and struck the ground. The pilot exited the aircraft, and was able to get to a passerby, who called for help. There was no fire, and the ELT activated. The aircraft was destroyed and the pilot sustained serious injuries.

C-FXCA, un appareil de type Boeing 767-300 exploité par Air Canada rouge, effectuait le vol ROU1572 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC avec 8 membres d’équipage et 170 passagers à bord. Alors que l’appareil était établi en approche finale pour la piste 06R avec les volets sélectionnés à la position FLAP 20, le système d'affichage des paramètres moteurs et d'alerte de l'équipage (EICAS) a diffusé le message LE SLAT ASYM. L’équipage a effectué une remise des gaz, déclaré une situation d’urgence, et a complété la liste de vérification avant de revenir poser l’appareil sans encombre sur la piste 06R. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé, ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-FJBS, un appareil de construction amateur de type Cyclone 180 en exploitation privé, effectuait un vol récréatif selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Rivière-du-Loup (CYRI), QC à destination de Forestville (CYFE), QC avec 1 pilote et 1 passager à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage sur la piste 27 à CYFE, le pilote a perdu la maîtrise de l’appareil, ce qui a causé une sortie de piste latérale du côté gauche. Le train d’atterrissage principal droit s’est rompu, et l’appareil a subi des dommages importants à l’aile droite et à l’hélice. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FFPH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines on behalf of TUI Airways, was conducting flight TOM1617 from Palma de Mallorca/Son Sant Joan (LEPA), Spain to Belfast/Aldergrove Intl (EGAA), UK with 6 crew members and 183 passengers on board. As the flight crew was following the DRAGO 3R departure from LEPA, a LEVEL OFF, LEVEL OFF TCAS RA message was received. The flight crew complied with the RA, and notified ATC. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FKSV, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA875 from Frankfurt/Rhein-Main (EDDF), Germany to Montreal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 10 crew members and 243 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL380 in the vicinity of N57/W025, the aircraft experienced a lost of the right hydraulic system pressure. The flight crew initially declared a PAN PAN as they were preparing to divert to London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK. However, it was subsequently determined that the issue was not affecting the safety of the flight or the ETOPS operation, as the system pressure and quantity was operating normally with the Electric Driven Pump on. The PAN PAN was cancelled, and the flight continued to CYUL without further incident.The operator's maintenance found that the Engine Driven Pump (EDP) was leaking, and proceeded to replace it.

C-GVSP, a Piper PA-31-350 aircraft operated by Peregrine Aerial Surveys, was conducting training flight SEE201T from Abbotsford (CYXX), BC with 2 persons on board. The 2 pilots were performing a simulated ILS with a missed approach for Runway 07 in VFR conditions at CYXX. As the aircraft was climbing through 1000 ASL during the missed approach phase, ATC instructed SEE201T to expedite the climb. At the same time, the flight crew observed a Piper PA-34-220T (C-GAKJ operated by Canadian Flight Centre) below them at their 2 o'clock position, who was turning onto the left downwind leg for Runway 19. ATC contacted both aircraft to ensure separation. The separation between the 2 aircraft was less than 200 feet vertically, and ¼ mile horizontally.

C-FHOS, an Embraer ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1074 from Denver Intl (KDEN), CO to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 4 crew members and 80 passengers on board. Less than one hour after the departure from KDEN in cruise flight, the flight crew received an ALT mis-compare flag on both altimeters, with a corresponding APPR 2 NOT AVAIL EICAS message. The flight crew consulted with the operator’s maintenance, and the decision to divert the flight to Minneapolis-St. Paul/Wold-Chamberlain Intl (KMSP), MN was elected. A MAYDAY was declared, and the aircraft landed at KMSP without further incident.The operator’s maintenance replaced the Guidance Panel in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM). Following an operational check, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GNYI, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Airspan Helicopters, was operating on a forest fire approximately 23 nm north west of Manning, AB. C-GNYI was dispatched along with 4 other medium size helicopters to rescue firefighters that had become trapped by a forest fire. While approaching the area, C-GFHP, an Aerospatiale AS350 B2 aircraft operated by Highpoint Helicopters, passed above C-GNYI with only 100 to 150 feet of separation. At the time of the occurrence, there were three radio frequencies in use with significant frequency congestion. Visibility varied from unlimited to 2-3 nm in smoke.

C-FFKA, an Aerospatiale AS350 B3 aircraft operated by Airspan Helicopters, was conducting operations in support of forest fire fighting in the vicinity of Manning, AB with 1 pilot and 4 passengers on board. While maneuvering near a fire, a risk of collision occurred with C-GIRZ, a Bell 212 aircraft equipped with a long line and bucket, operated by Alpine Helicopters. C-GIRZ was approximately 450-600 feet to the left and slightly higher than C-FFKA, who maneuvered to the right to reduce the potential for a collision.

C-GKQD, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE261 from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON with 4 crew members and 74 passengers on board. At approximately 6000 feet ASL during the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from CYQT, the flight crew received a fuselage door warning light. The cabin crew was advised, and was instructed to secure the cabin. Shortly after the flight crew requested to return to CYQT, the cabin depressurized and light vibrations could be felt. The flight crew declared an emergency, flew the visual approach to Runway 07, landed the aircraft overweight, and stopped on the runway. ARFF inspected the aircraft on the runway, and released it to taxi to the terminal. A post-flight examination of the aircraft determined that the baggage door handle had popped open, although the door remained closed. The aircraft was inspected and ground tested before being returned to service.

C-FRSK, a Messerschmitt BK117 B-2 helicopter operated by Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service, was conducting medevac flight STARS9 from Arcola, SK to the Regina General Hospital (CRQ2), SK with 4 crew members and 1 patient on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew received a number 1 engine (Avco Lycoming LTS-101-850B2) chip detector light. The flight crew decided to complete a precautionary shutdown of the affected engine, and diverted to Regina Intl (CYQR), SK. The flight crew advised medical dispatch of their situation, and arranged for an ambulance transfer to the General Hospital. No emergency was declared, and the helicopter landed without further incident. An inspection of the system by the operator's maintenance revealed that the forward chip plug was contaminated with debris. The debris was removed, and following a lengthy ground run, the chip detector light did not illuminate. The engine oil system was serviced, and replenished with new oil. Another ground run was completed with no chip detector light. The aircraft was returned to service.

LN-LNB, a Boeing 787-8 aircraft operated by Norwegian Air Shuttle, was conducting flight NAX7055 from Copenhagen/København Kastrup (EKCH), Denmark to Orlando Intl (KMCO), FL with 14 crew members and 227 passengers on board. During cruise flight approximately 265 nm north east of Goose Bay (CYYR), NL, the aircraft experienced an exhaust gas temperature exceedance, followed by a roll back and vibration of the number 1 engine. The flight crew requested a descent and a diversion to CYYR, and completed the QRH memory items and checklist. The aircraft dumped fuel, and landed with the number 1 thrust lever at idle without further incident.

C-FLAJ, a Boeing 757-200 aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways, was conducting flight CJT246 from Bermuda/L.F. Wade Intl (TXKF), Bermuda to Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ with 2 crew members on board. During the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from TXKF, the flight crew received a MAIN CARGO DOOR UNLOCKED indication. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and initiated a return to TXKF. During the descent to TXKF, the flight crew declared a MAYDAY as a secondary door advisory was received. Upon arrival, the emergency was cancelled.The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and found a fault with the indication system. The system was deferred per the Minimum Equipment List (MEL), and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FTOH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG9903 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Hamilton (CYHM), ON with 6 crew members and 9 passengers on board. As the aircraft was taxiing out for the departure at CYLW, the flight crew was advised by the flight crew of a WestJet aircraft that fire was observed coming from the number 1 engine drain mast. The flight crew stopped the aircraft, and shut the number 1 engine down. ARFF came to inspect the aircraft and, after inspection, the aircraft was cleared to taxi back to the hangar for further inspection.The engine was inspected and a ground run was carried out. Pooled engine oil was determined to be the probable cause. The aircraft was released by maintenance and the flight was conducted to CYHM without further incident.

C-FMXC, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1913 from Barcelona/EI Prat (LEBL), Spain to Montreal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 8 crew members and 230 passengers on board. During the cruise portion of the flight in the vicinity of Gander Intl (CYQX), NL, a flight attendant became incapacitated due to illness and was unable to perform duties. Positions were reassigned for the landing, and the flight landed at destination without further incident.

C-GSCA, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1901 from Athens/Eleftherios Venizelos Intl (LGAV), Greece to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 9 crew members and 189 passengers on board. Upon selection of initial thrust at the start of the takeoff phase on Runway 21L, the flight crew noted a slight yaw. As the engines spooled up to the selected thrust setting, an abnormal rumbling noise could be heard. Passing 80 KIAS, the right engine (General Electric CF6-80C2B6F) began to roll back and was unresponsive to thrust commands. The takeoff was rejected at 110 KIAS, the aircraft stopped on the runway and became disabled as 2 outboard main landing gear tires had blown. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and ARFF attended to the aircraft.

C-GJVW, a Fairchild SA227-DC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation (dba Bearskin Airlines), was conducting flight BLS362 from Red lake (CYRL), ON to Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON with 2 crew members and 4 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew received a number 2 engine fire light on the fire panel. The engine operating parameters appeared normal, so the flight crew decided to keep the engine running and continued to destination. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft landed without further incident. After the landing, the flight crew stopped the aircraft on the runway and shut the number 2 engine down. The aircraft taxied to the apron, and there was no indication of any smoke or fire. A subsequent inspection of the system by the operator's maintenance revealed loose terminal connections to the oil cooler fire detector. The loose terminals were repaired, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTSI, an Airbus 330-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC183 from Glasgow/Abbotsinch (EGPF), UK to Toronto/Lester B Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 11 crew members and 342 passengers on board. Approximately 4 hours into the flight, a flight attendant felt ill and could not continue to perform their duties. Positions were reassigned for the landing, and the flight landed at destination without further incident.

N461UA, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL460 from San Francisco Intl (KSFO), CA to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 5 crew members and 139 passengers on board. When the landing gear was lowered in preparation for landing at CYVR, the flight crew received an AUTO-BRAKE FAULT on Brake and Steering Control Unit (BSCU) channels 1 and 2. The flight crew declared an emergency, and ARFF was standing by for their arrival. The aircraft landed without further incident. A post-flight maintenance inspection identified a failure of the right inboard wheel speed tachometer.

C-GYJX, a float-equipped Cessna A185F aircraft operated by Atleo River Air Service, was conducting a flight from Tofino Harbour (CAB4), BC to Ahousat, BC with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. During the landing at Ahousat in gusty wind conditions, the pilot landed long, and the aircraft was unable to stop before running into shoreline rocks. There were no injuries. The aircraft received substantial damage limited to the aircraft's floats.

C-FHKF, a Convair 440 aircraft operated by Conair Group, was conducting flight FGD455 on a fire suppression mission from Calgary/Springbank (CYBW), AB with two crew members on board. Shortly after the departure from CYBW, the flight crew observed a fire warning light for the number 1 engine (Allison/Rolls Royce 501-D13D). The power was reduced on the affected engine, and the light extinguished; consequently, the flight crew elected to return to CYBW. The load of fire retardant was released into a forested area prior to the return. During the initial approach at CYBW, the fire warning light illuminated once again. The flight crew shut the number 1 engine down as per the QRH, and completed an uneventful single-engine approach and landing.The operator’s maintenance observed that a clamp associated with the number one engine exhaust duct had failed, allowing hot exhaust gases to be directed at the fire sensors in zone 1. The clamp was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FGRP, a de Havilland DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8676 from North Bay (CYYB), ON to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 3 crew members and 26 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew observed an overspeed indication for the number 2 propeller, and proceeded to shut the engine down as a precaution. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight continued to destination where the aircraft landed without further incident. Following a visual inspection by ARFF, the flight crew taxied the aircraft to the gate. A small puddle with the appearance of oil was observed below the number 2 engine. The operator’s maintenance replaced the Hydro Mechanical Unit (HMU), the Electronic Control Unit (ECU), and the fuel pump prior to returning the aircraft to service.

N808AW, an Airbus 319 operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL1876 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), Ontario, to Charlotte Douglas Intl (KCLT), North Carolina. Shortly after departing runway 06L at 1625 EDT, the aircraft flew through a flock of birds sustaining multiple bird strikes. The flight crew declared a mayday and returned to land at CYYZ uneventfully at 1641EDT.

C-FJOU, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1715 from Bridgetown/Grantley Adams Intl (TBPB), Barbados to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 6 crew members and 200 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL360 in the vicinity of Scranton, PA, the flight crew reported a collision with what is believed to be a weather balloon. The flight continued to destination and landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance conducted a visual external inspection of the aircraft, and no damage was found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFNE, a Boeing 737-400 aircraft operated by Bradley Air Services (dba First Air), was conducting flight FAB702 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU with 4 crew members and 50 passengers on board. During the climb after the departure from CYWG, the flight crew noticed that the number 1 bleed air valve would not activate, and that the associated circuit breaker had popped. The circuit breaker was reset, however it popped again. Following consultation with the operator’s maintenance, the flight crew decided to return to CYWG. During the return, the flight crew noticed that the cabin altitude had increased to 11 000 feet. The QRH was executed, and an emergency descent was initiated from FL310. A MAYDAY was declared, and an overweight landing was completed without further incident at CYWG.An inspection of the system revealed chafed wiring to the number 1 bleed valve. The wires were replaced, and the aircraft was returned back to service following an overweight landing inspection.

C-GBZV, a Cessna 172S aircraft operated by the Brampton Flying Club, was being flown in the circuit on a training flight at Brampton-Caledon (CNC3), ON with an instructor and a student-pilot on board. During the third full stop landing, the aircraft was observed in a nose high flare, which created a prolonged tail strike prior to a rejected landing being initiated. The aircraft was observed to bank to the left after becoming airborne, and continued to roll left in a nose high attitude until the left wing and elevator struck the ground. The nose landing gear dug in the soft earth, and the aircraft rolled longitudinally before coming to rest on its back. There was no fuel leak, and no fire. The student-pilot was removed from the aircraft immediately, and received minor injuries. The instructor received minor injuries as well, and was removed by EMS. Both occupants were taken to hospital as a precaution. The ELT did activate during the collision with terrain.

N9017P, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL2589 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Miami Intl (KMIA), FL. During the taxi out for the departure from CYYZ, Ground Control authorized AAL2589 to taxi for a departure on Runway 06L, which was read back correctly by the flight crew. After switching to the Tower frequency, AAL2589 reported that they were taxiing to Runway 06R. The incorrect runway read back was not noticed by the Tower controller, who continued on to state that they had one more aircraft to land prior to allowing AAL2589 to depart. AAL2589 proceeded to taxi across 06L and held short of the 06R ILS hold line, which resulted in the aircraft occupying Runway 06L. No clearance was given to AAL2589 to cross a runway, and the only south complex runway in use at the time was 06L. The Tower controller directed C-FYIY, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, conducting flight ROU1671 from Orlando Intl (KMCO), FL to CYYZ, to pull up and go around as there was traffic on the runway. When queried on the radio, the flight crew of AAL2589 stated that they believed they were cleared to taxi to Runway 06R, and were holding short of the ILS hold line as the weather conditions warranted.

C-GTXE, un appareil de type Learjet 35A exploité par Top Aces, effectuait un vol local au départ de Bagotville (CYBG), QC avec seulement 2 pilotes à bord. Peu de temps après le décollage, le moteur numéro 2 a subi une perte de puissance. Aucun bruit, aucune vibration et aucune indication n'ont été associés avec la perte de puissance. Le moteur numéro 2 a été mis au ralenti, et un PAN PAN a été déclaré. L'équipage de conduite a demandé une montée à 7000 pieds afin de larguer du carburant pour l’atterrissage. L'appareil s'est par la suite posé sans encombre à CYBG. Le personnel de l’entretien a déterminé que la perte de puissance était causée par un potentiomètre défectueux.

N500RM, a privately owned amateur built Rotorway Exec 90 helicopter, was conducting hover practice exercises from a private property located 9 nm east-southeast of Gananoque, ON. After approximately 30 minutes of hovering, the pilot made a turn and observed an obstacle in an unexpected location, which prompted him to land the helicopter immediately. The helicopter landed with lateral momentum, and the right skid low; a dynamic rollover ensued. The pilot exited the helicopter before a post impact fire consumed most of the aircraft. The pilot, the sole occupant, was not injured.

On 01 June 2019 at approximately 2235 (Mountain Daylight Time),  a privately operated American Aircraft AA-5B (registration C-GQIJ, serial number AA5B-0544), was on a visual flight rules (VFR) flight from Medicine Hat Airport (CYXH), Alberta to Moose Jaw/Air Vice Marshal C.M. McEwen Airport (CYMJ), Saskatchewan, with a pilot and 2 passengers on board. The aircraft departed during the hours of darkness; official night began at 2207. There were no records from NAV CANADA of a flight plan being filed or a weather briefing being given to the pilot. The exact weather information that the pilot obtained from other sources prior to departure is unknown. The aerodrome routine meteorological report (METAR) for CYXH at 2100 indicated calm winds, visibility 4 statute miles (SM) in smoke, broken clouds at 28 000 feet above sea level, and a temperature of 22 °C. At 2200, the visibility at CYXH improved to 6 SM in haze and by 2300, approximately 15 minutes after the accident, to 8 SM.At 0401 on 02 June, the joint rescue coordination centre (JRCC) Trenton received a call indicating that the aircraft was overdue. The aircraft was expected to arrive at CYMJ at 0030. The JRCC had not received any reports of signals from the emergency locator transmitter (ELT) being detected. A missing aircraft file was opened, and assets were assigned to the search. At 0934, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) ground search identified the occurrence aircraft. Minutes later, a military aircraft flew over the site and received a weak ELT signal. At approximately 0940, 2 search and rescue technicians parachuted into the site. They confirmed that the pilot and the 2 passengers had been fatally injured. The 121.5 MHz ELT was found intact and was manually switched off by first responder personnel. The aircraft struck the ground at high velocity on unworked farmland approximately 18 nautical miles east of CYXH in the vicinity of Irvine, Alberta. The aircraft attitude was approximately 45° nose down and some left bank because the left wingtip struck the ground first. The airframe had broken up completely; however, all aircraft parts were accounted for at the accident site. The impact was not survivable. The degree of breakup and damage from the impact precluded any detailed assessment of the flight control system and aircraft systems. The portions of the flight control system, engine, propeller, and flight instruments that were examined did not exhibit any failures that would have prevented normal operation.According to the records reviewed, the aircraft was certified and maintained in accordance with regulations. There were no outstanding defects noted in the journey log, and the aircraft was being operated within the weight and balance design limits.The pilot held a student pilot permit that had expired on 01 May 2014, and a Category 4 medical certificate that had expired on 24 June 2017. There are no Transport Canada records showing that the pilot held an aeroplane license or a rating to fly passengers at night. According to the pilot’s personal log, he began his private pilot training in Regina, Saskatchewan, in April 2010 and accumulated 83.1 hours of dual flight training time before his first solo flight in December 2011. The pilot’s flight hours at the time of the accident are unknown, because his personal log was not up to date. At 07 October 2012, the pilot had 142.3 hours of total flight time recorded in his log. The pilot first flew the occurrence aircraft on 30 April 2014. According to the aircraft journey log, the pilot had acquired approximately 40 hours of night flying with another pilot on board.

C-GIAT, a float-equipped Cessna A185F aircraft operated by River Air, was conducting a flight from Kenora (CJM9), ON to Minaki/Pistol Lake (CKP3), ON with only the pilot on board. While on final approach into CKP3, the aircraft struck and severed a set of power lines. The pilot continued to land without further incident. The aircraft sustained minor damage to the propeller. There were no injuries.

N310, a Gulfstream IV aircraft operated by Worldwide Jet Charter, was conducting flight WWI31 from Springfield-Beckley Municipal (KSGH), OH to London/Luton (EGGW), UK. While in cruise flight at FL430, the flight crew noted smoke in the cockpit. The flight crew were unable to pinpoint the origin of the smoke, but noted that it was blue with no noticeable odor. An emergency was declared, the oxygen masks were donned, the aircraft diverted to Gander Intl (CYQX), NL, and the flight crew started to descend to 15 000 feet. As the aircraft was descending, the smoke dissipated and one of the pilots removed their oxygen mask to enable clear radio communication. The aircraft landed without further incident 35 minutes after the incident started, with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance determined that the smoke was actually water vapour caused by the decompression. An operational flight was conducted, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GEOQ, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1912 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Barcelona/El Prat (LEBL), Spain with 8 crew members and 260 passengers on board. During cruise flight in the vicinity of Trenton (CYTN), NS, a cabin crew member became incapacitated due to illness and was unfit for duty for the remainder of the flight. The remainder of the cabin crew were reassigned to cover all doors as required.

C-GTAG, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8470 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Baltimore/Washington Intl Thurgood Marshall (KBWI), MD with 3 crew members and 32 passengers on board. After holding for 40 minutes because of thunderstorms east of KBWI, the flight crew elected to divert to Philadelphia Intl (KPHL), PA. While enroute to KPHL, the flight crew received a pressurization warning, and declared a PAN PAN. The indication subsequently went away, so the flight crew cancelled the emergency and proceeded to KPHL where the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GERF, an amateur-built RAF 2000 GTXEJ2.5 FI gyroplane, was conducting flight training operations out of a private airfield, approximately 6 nm north-northeast of Drayton Valley Industrial (CER3), AB with 2 persons on board. During a take-off roll, the aircraft contacted some bumps in the turf runway, and directional control was lost. The aircraft rolled onto its left side, resulting in significant damage to the main rotor, propeller blades, vertical stabilizer, and cabin structure. The instructor and student were not injured.

C-GOGZ, a Bombardier CL-415 water bomber aircraft operated by the Province of Ontario, was conducting fire suppression operations near Pikangikum (CYPM), ON with 2 pilots on board. While scooping water on a lake, the flight crew heard a bang and immediately received failure indications on the bomb system panel. The flight crew aborted the pickup, climbed out of the lake, and returned to Dryden Regional (CYHD), ON where the aircraft landed without further incident. The aircraft sustained minor damage to the hull and water bombing system.

C-GQHL, a Cessna T310P aircraft operated by Orthoshop Geomatics, was conducting a local aerial survey flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. Upon selection of landing gear down during the final approach into CYWG, the pilot did not receive a down and locked indication for the right main landing gear. A fly-by the tower confirmed that the landing gear was extended. ARFF was called out and the aircraft then landed without further incident.An inspection of the landing gear system revealed an unserviceable landing gear indication micro switch.

C-GORG, a privately registered Maule M-5-210C aircraft on floats, was on a local solo training flight out of Watson Lake, BC. During the return back to Watson Lake, the aircraft ran out of fuel. The pilot attempted a forced landing in a pasture at One Hundred Mile House, and sustained minor injuries; the aircraft sustained substantial damage when the propeller contacted terrain, and one of the floats collapsed.

C-FYDN, a privately registered Piper PA-12 aircraft on floats, was conducting a flight from an outpost camp at Domain Lake, ON to another outpost camp at Optic Lake, ON with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. The aircraft was reported overdue at destination, and was found near the shore of Domain Lake the following day by another aircraft. C-FYDN collided with terrain, and the accident caused a forest fire. The Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources responded to the forest fire, and the Ontario Provincial Police subsequently attended to the scene. The 2 occupants were fatally injured, and the aircraft was destroyed. No ELT signal was detected.

C-GTQC, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC873 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 6 crew members and 186 passengers on board. Approximately 30 minutes after the departure from CYYC during cruise flight, the cabin crew observed smoke coming from a galley oven that was heating meals. The cabin crew pulled the associated circuit breaker and, several minutes later, the oven door was opened. No sign of fire was observed, and the smoke began to dissipate. The flight continued to CYYZ without further incident. The operator’s maintenance found the oven contaminated with food spills.

C-FMXC, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1919 from Venice/Marco Polo (LIPZ), Italy to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 8 crew members and 237 passengers on board. During cruise flight approximately 90 minutes after the departure from LIPZ, one of the cabin crew members became incapacitated due to illness, and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight. Duties were distributed to the other cabin crew members, and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FYAG, a Fairchild SA227-AC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting flight PAG190 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to St. Theresa Point (CYST), MB with 2 crew members and 3 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure off Runway 31 at CYWG, smoke entered the cabin. The flight crew confirmed the source as cabin bleed air, initiated the QRH checklist, and requested a return to CYWG. The smoke was successfully cleared, and the aircraft returned for an uneventful landing back on Runway 31.An inspection of the bleed air system revealed a loose pneumatic line to the bleed air modulator valve. The line was secured, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FABA, a de Havilland DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG815 from Big Trout Lake (CYTL), ON to Pickle Lake (CYPL), ON with 2 crew members on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew received caution light indications for the primary and secondary inverters. At the same time, the captain and first officer instruments flagged off, followed by a strong electrical smell. The crew pulled the bus tie circuit breaker, and continued to CYPL using standby instruments. The electrical smell subsided, and the aircraft landed without further incident.The operator's maintenance inspected the system and replaced the secondary inverter and the inverter paralleling control box. The operator filed a Service Difficulty Report (SDR) with Transport Canada.

C-IJAI, a privately registered Aeroquest Everest Basic Ultra-light aircraft, was on a local pleasure flight from Erickson Muni (CKQ6), MB with only the pilot on board. Just prior to the touchdown during the landing sequence, the pilot lost directional control, and the aircraft collided with the surface of the runway. The pilot sustained minor injury, and the aircraft was substantially damaged.Reportedly, there were gusting crosswinds at the time of the occurrence.

N4512C, a privately owned Cessna 170B aircraft, was departing Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen Intl (CYXY), YT for Anchorage/Ted Stevens Intl (PANC), AK with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. Shortly after the takeoff from Runway 14R, the aircraft departed controlled flight and crashed into a wooded ravine approximately 2000 feet south of the runway. A post impact fire consumed the aircraft, and the 2 occupants received fatal injuries. An ELT signal was detected.

C-GRGO, a de Havilland DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Canadian North, was conducting flight MPE611 from Pond Inlet (CYIO), NU to Igloolik (CYGT), NU with 3 crew members and 10 passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff from CYIO, the flight attendant became ill and could no longer perform duties. A company employee travelling on board offered assistance, and carried out inflight service for the remainder of the trip. The flight crew elected to divert to Iqaluit (CYFB), NU, where the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GSLI, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Skyline Helicopters, was conducting aerial firefighting operations from a lease site located 22 nm south southwest of High Level (CYOJ), AB with only the pilot on board. After the operation was completed, the pilot returned to the lease site, placed the water bucket on the ground, and maneuvered the helicopter in a rearward direction to put the longline down. The helicopter began to descend, and the pilot increased the collective and power in an attempt to arrest the descent. The helicopter continued to descend and struck the ground. The landing gear skid tubes broke free of the cross tubes, and the helicopter began to pitch forward. The pilot was able to gain altitude, stabilized the helicopter, and released the longline. The helicopter was manoeuvered away from the detached skid tubes, and the pilot was able to settle it on its belly. The engines were secured, and the pilot evacuated. There were no injuries.

C-GHLT, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1628 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL with 8 crew members and 117 passengers on board. Shortly after reaching Top of Climb after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew received a RH GEN DRIVE EICAS message. The QRH was executed, a return to CYYZ was requested, and a PAN PAN was declared as a precaution. The aircraft landed back at CYYZ without further incident. The operator’s maintenance is currently inspecting the aircraft to determine the cause of the indication.

C-IULM, a privately registered DTA Voyageur II 912 S Basic Ultra-light powered hang glider aircraft operated by ULM Quebec, was conducting a training flight from St-Cuthbert (ULM Quebec) (CCU2), QC with 1 instructor and 1 student-pilot on board. For approximately 1 hour, the 2 occupants trained locally, and conducted multiple touch and goes at CCU2. At approximately 20:00 EDT, the aircraft took off from Runway 10, and crashed a few seconds later on a field adjacent to the runway. Both occupants sustained fatal injuries. The aircraft was destroyed.

C-GOGT, a Beech 200 King Air medevac aircraft operated by Missinippi Air, was conducting flight MA03-M from Baker Lake (CYBK), NU to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with 2 crew members and 2 passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff from CYBK, the flight crew received a left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-41) chip detector light. The engine was shut down out of precaution, and the flight crew elected to return to CYBK. A Mayday was declared, and the aircraft landed without further incident. An inspection of the engine by the operator's maintenance revealed metal contamination on the chip detector. The operator has submitted the metal contamination and an oil sample for analysis.

C-GURP, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA9 from Paris/Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 13 crew members and 298 passengers on board. During cruise flight, a cabin crew member experienced a medical event and became incapacitated. The flight crew was advised, and the flight continued to CYYC. Duties were distributed to the remaining flight attendants for the landing.

C-GHPX, a Boeing 787-8 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA548 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ with 10 crew members and 223 passengers on board. During the initial climb through 12 000 feet after the departure from CYVR, the cabin crew detected the smell of smoke, followed by the visible presence of smoke. The flight crew stopped the climb at 18 000 feet, declared a PAN PAN, and requested to return to CYVR. The aircraft conducted an overweight landing, and taxied to the gate. Upon opening the cabin door, the smoke dissipated. The operator's maintenance found a fault with the lower right recirculation fan. The aircraft was returned to service under Minimum Equipment List (MEL) provisions.

N45366, a privately operated Douglas DC3 aircraft, was conducting an IFR oceanic crossing flight from Narsarsuaq (BGBW), Greenland to Reykjavík (BIRK), Iceland. N103NA, a privately operated Douglas C-47B aircraft, was also flying the same route. At approximate position N62°/W040°, N45366 entered controlled airspace at 13 000 feet, instead of 11 000 feet as cleared by air traffic services. In doing so, a loss of separation with N103NA occurred. The required separation is 30 minutes in trail, while the actual separation was 18 minutes.

C-GJZF, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA7953 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination de Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON avec 4 membres d'équipage et 71 passagers à bord. Suite au décollage de CYUL, l'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence après avoir ressenti une forte vibration provenant de la roue de nez, accompagnée d'une odeur de caoutchouc. L'aéronef est revenu atterrir sans problème à CYUL. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé.

C-FNXN, un appareil de type DHC8-300 exploité par Air Creebec, effectuait le vol CRQ530 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Mont-Joli (CYYY), QC à destination de Sept-Îles (CYZV), QC avec 3 membres d'équipage et 43 passagers à bord. Peu de temps après le décollage de la piste 06 à CYYY, l'équipage a noté des fluctuations de couple et de puissance du moteur gauche (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW123B). L’équipage de conduite a fermé le moteur par mesure de précaution, et a déclaré une urgence. L'aéronef est revenu atterrir à CYYY sans encombre. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GSAE, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by the Province of Saskatchewan, was conducting flight SLG1 from Wollaston Lake (CZWL), SK to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK with 2 crew members and 4 passengers on board. Approximately 10 minutes after departing CZWL, the flight crew received a GEAR UNSAFE indication. The GEAR UNSAFE light extinguished after 30 seconds, and a second GEAR UNSAFE light appeared 5 minutes later and extinguished after a short period of time. 30 minutes into the flight, the GEAR UNSAFE light re-illuminated intermittently, and then remained on for the remainder of the flight. The flight crew notified ATC of the situation and requested ARFF on standby at CYXE. Upon selection of landing gear down on arrival at CYXE, the flight crew observed a gear down and locked indication. The aircraft landed without incident, and taxied to the ramp. The flight crew reported a G1000 advisory light indicating "Miscompare between weight on wheels inputs". The operator's maintenance replaced the nose gear uplock switch, adjusted all uplock switches, and replaced the right Weight On Wheels switch (WOW). A visual inspection of the WOW wiring revealed that one pin was misaligned; the pin was re-inserted and the left WOW relay was replaced. The aircraft was returned to service after a satisfactory test flight.

C-GHQI, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1816 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Nassau/Lynden Pindling Intl (MYNN), Bahamas with 6 crew members and 198 passengers on board. During the descent into MYNN, one of the cabin crew members became incapacitated due to illness, and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight. Duties were distributed to the other cabin crew members, and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GKVV, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG033 from Orlando Intl (KMCO), FL to Miami Intl (KMIA), FL with 6 crew members and 175 passengers on board. When Flaps 30 were selected during the approach at KMIA, a temporary airspeed increase caused the activation of the Flap Load relief system. As the flaps returned to 30° after the airspeed decreased again, the LE FLAPS TRANSIT light illuminated steadily. The flight crew executed a missed approach, and ran the LE FLAPS TRANSIT checklist. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight crew requested the approach and landing to Runway 9. After the landing, the aircraft stopped on the runway for inspection of wings and flaps for damage, as well as the condition of the brakes. No apparent damage was noted, and brake temperatures were within the normal range. The aircraft was authorized to taxi to the terminal, followed behind by ARFF as a precaution.

C-FGKN, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA702 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY with 6 crew members and 144 passengers on board. Crossing approximately 5500 feet during the descent into KLGA, the flight crew received a TCAS RA aural TRAFFIC message, followed subsequently by a MONITOR VERTICAL SPEED aural message. The flight crew climbed back by approximately 300 feet, and the alert cleared. The flight continued for an uneventful landing.

C-GJEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3450 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Montreal/Pierre-Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 4 crew members and 22 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYHZ, the cabin crew noticed an unusual odor in the cabin after the bleed air switches were selected on. The flight crew advised ATC, and requested a return to CYHZ with the presence of ARFF on standby. The aircraft landed without further event. The operator’s maintenance met the aircraft and determined that the odour was caused by residual fluid from the compressor wash that had been completed the night before. Engine runs were carried out, and no further faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GCGB, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Star Helicopters, was conducting bucketing operations in support of forest fire fighting activity, approximately 15 nm south east of Lac La Biche (CYLB), AB. During a lift of water from a pond, the pilot experienced difficulties in controlling the yaw. The collective was reduced, and a power loss of the number 1 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6T-3B) occurred. The pilot returned to the staging area, and conducted an uneventful single-engine approach and landing. The operator’s maintenance observed damage to the number 1 engine. The engine was removed for replacement. There was no other damage to the helicopter.

C-FZRM, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA4032 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Fort MacKay/Firebag (CYFI), AB with 6 crew members and 87 passengers on board. Just prior to the rotation during the take-off roll at CYYC, the flight crew experienced a significant nose wheel vibration, which was followed by a bang. While in the climb, the flight crew was advised by ATC of rubber debris on the runway. The flight crew elected to divert back to CYYC, and requested ARFF for the arrival. The operator’s maintenance replaced both nose wheel assemblies, the air-ground sensor, a wire bundle bracket and the Electronic & Equipment (E&E) bay door.

C-GSAE, a Beech B200 King Air air ambulance aircraft operated by the Province of Saskatchewan, was conducting patient transfer flight SLG1 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB with a total of 5 persons on board. Just prior to the descent into CYEG, the flight crew observed a gear unsafe warning light. Upon landing gear extension during the intermediate approach, the flight crew observed three green landing gear safe lights. The flight crew requested ARFF to stand by for the landing, which was executed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance adjusted the left hand main landing gear uplock switch, conducted a gear swing, and released the aircraft back into service.

C-GAAZ, un appareil de type Cessna A185F en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue à destination de Lachute (CSE4), QC avec seul le pilote à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage sur la piste 10, l’appareil a fait un atterrissage dur et l’hélice a touché le sol; l’appareil s’est immobilisé sur le nez. Le pilote n’a pas été blessé, toutefois l’hélice et le moteur ont subi des dommages importants.

C-GKVV, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG763 from St. Maarten/Princess Juliana Intl (TNCM), Sint Maarten to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 6 crew members and 165 passengers on board. Approximately one hour after the departure from TNCM, one of the cabin crew members experienced a medical issue, and was unable to continue duties. Duties were distributed to the other cabin crew members, and the aircraft continued to destination without further incident.

C-GMAF, a Canadair CL215 1A10 water bomber aircraft operated by Air Spray Air Tankers, was conducting flight Tanker 250 in support of firefighting/fire management activities in the area of West Hawk Lake, MB with 2 pilots on board. During an active firefighting operation at approximately 3 nautical miles east of West Hawk Lake, the left wing sponson struck the tip of a tall spruce tree as the aircraft was in a left hand turn. The aircraft departed the fire area, and landed without further incident at Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. There were no injuries.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and replaced the left wing sponson due to damage. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GQBQ, un appareil de type Bombardier CL600-2B16 Challenger 601 exploité par le Service aérien du Gouvernement du Québec, effectuait le vol QUE20E selon les règles de vols aux instruments à partir de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC vers Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC avec 2 pilotes et 4 passagers à bord. Alors que l’équipage a sélectionné le train d’atterrissage en position baissé lors de l'approche pour la piste 06 à CYQB, le train avant ne s’est pas déployé. Après avoir complété les listes de vérifications appropriées, une urgence a été déclarée et l’appareil s’est posé sans autre incident avec le Service de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d’aéronefs (SLIA) en attente. L’appareil n'a subi aucun dommage et il n’y a eu aucun blessé. L'équipe d'entretien a remplacé l'unité de contrôle du train d'atterrissage, et l'appareil fût retourné en service.

C-FCPM, un appareil de type Cessna 208B exploité par Parachutisme Nouvel Air, effectuait un vol local de parachutage à partir de St-Esprit (CES2), QC. Suite au largage de parachutistes, le pilote est retourné à CES2 et, lors de l’approche visuelle pour la piste 20, l'appareil a rencontré un cisaillement de vent en courte finale. L’appareil a perdu de l’altitude, et le pilote n'a pas été en mesure de freiner la descente; l'appareil est lourdement entré en collision avec le sol. La roue de nez s'est affaissée, et l'hélice a contacté le sol. Le pilote et le passager à bord n'ont pas été blessés.

C-FZUB, un appareil de type Airbus 320-200 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA307 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination de Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC avec 5 membres d’équipage et 146 passagers à bord. Alors que l'appareil circulait pour le décollage sur la voie Alpha, une fuite de carburant significative provenant du moteur droit a été observée par l'équipage de ROU1742, qui circulait derrière ACA307. Le contrôleur de la circulation au sol a alors dirigé ACA307 vers la voie de circulation A1, et a avisé le service de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). L'unité SLIA a rencontré l'appareil et a procédé au nettoyage du déversement. Les passagers ont joint le terminal à l'aide des véhicules de transport de passagers, pour être par la suite transférés à bord d'un autre appareil. L'origine de la fuite de carburant est pour l'instant inconnue.

C-FJDQ, un appareil de type Beech B100 King Air exploité par Max Aviation, effectuait le vol MAX100 selon les règles de vol aux instruments à partir de Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU), QC à destination de Sherbrooke (CYSC), QC avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Immédiatement après le décollage, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison de la présence d'une odeur de fumée provenant de la cabine. L'aéronef est revenu à CYHU où il s’est posé atterri sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.Lors de l'inspection post-envolée, l'équipe de l’entretien a découvert des conduits de chauffage en plastique fondus sous le plancher de la cabine.

C-GKQA, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE242 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON with 4 crew members and 72 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew noticed a fuel imbalance and initiated a fuel transfer from the right main tank, to the left one. Subsequently, the flight crew stopped the fuel transfer when it was realized that the left wing fuel quantity was indicating 200 lbs, and decreasing. No fuel leak could be observed by the cabin crew. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight diverted to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. During the approach, fuel quantity indications returned to normal; consequently, the emergency was cancelled. The aircraft landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance identified the left wing fuel indication system to be faulty.

C-FSWB, an Aurora Helicopters Aerospatiale AS350-B2 helicopter, was conducting water bucket training when the pilot inadvertently pressed the incorrect button causing the longline and bucket to release from the aircraft over the intended water drop location. There was no damage to the helicopter or property on the ground.

C-IIOB, a privately operated Quad City Challenger II Advanced Ultra-light aircraft, was conducting a local flight from a private strip approximately 22 nm south east of High Level (CYOJ), AB with only the pilot on board. Prior to the takeoff, the pilot completed preflight checks, and no anomalies were noted. Shortly after becoming airborne at an altitude of approximately 75 to 100 feet AGL, the engine (Rotax 582) stopped abruptly. The aircraft subsequently descended and impacted the ground, coming to a rest slightly to the right of the centerline on the airstrip. The aircraft was substantially damaged, and the pilot received minor injuries. The owner subsequently completed a preliminary investigation into the loss of power and believes that the cause was fuel starvation due to foreign material entering the fuel selector valve, blocking fuel flow to the engine.

C-GTGA, a Beech 1900C aircraft operated by Skylink Express Inc., was conducting flight SLG720 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG), MB to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl. (CYXE), SK. Shortly after departure, the flight crew noticed that the No. 2 propeller tachometer was indicating low at 1550 rpm. The flight crew elected to return to CYWG and requested ARFF response. The subsequent landing was uneventful. The operator's maintenance personnel found that the No. 2 over-speed governor test-solenoid was stuck in the test mode. The over-speed governor was replaced. After a satisfactory ground run, the aircraft returned to service.

C-FXCA, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1677 from Orlando Intl (KMCO), FL to Toronto/Lester B Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 8 crew members and 272 passengers on board. As the flight crew selected Flap 20 during the final approach, a LE SLAT ASYM EICAS message was received. The flight crew initiated a missed approach, and declared a PAN PAN as a precaution. The aircraft returned to land uneventfully with a lower flap setting. ARFF was standing by and completed an external visual inspection prior to the aircraft being allowed to taxi to the gate.

C-GTJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7266 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Pittsburgh Intl (KPIT), PA with 3 crew members and 35 passengers on board. While descending to 4000 feet and receiving vectors to final approach for Runway 28L at KPIT, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to descend at 2000 feet per minute. The flight crew observed a target on their TCAS, and continued their descent to 3000 feet. Once clear of conflict, ATC provided additional vectors and the approach was continued to an uneventful landing.

C-FEJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8856 from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON to Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ with 4 crew members and 28 passengers on board. During the descent into KEWR, the flight crew received a right thrust reverser unlocked icon. The flight crew immediately shut the associated engine down, however realized upon executing the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) items that the engine shutdown procedure was for the 900 series, not the 200 series. The number 2 engine was restarted, and the aircraft landed at KEWR without further incident.The operator’s maintenance performed a thrust reverser lock out, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-IKID, a private Basic Ultra-light Raven Soaring Trike aircraft, was conducting a flight in the vicinity of Blumenort, MB with only the pilot on board. The pilot was flying low over a friend's home and while manoeuvering, the aircraft struck a power line and came to rest in a tree. Local Emergency Medical Services and the police responded, as well at the power company. The pilot sustained serious injuries, and the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GZVJ, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG671 from Angling Lake/Wapekeka (CKB6), ON to Kasabonika (CYAQ), ON with 2 crew members and 13 passengers on board. During the initial climb after the departure from CKB6, the number 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-67D) torque indicator was fluctuating between 4 000 and 2 500 ft/lbs. As the aircraft climbed through 400 feet AGL, the flight crew adjusted the throttles to climb power setting. Consequently, the torque indication stabilized. During cruise flight at 4 500 feet ASL, the low oil pressure warning light began to flicker, and the oil pressure indication was fluctuating between 50 and 70 psi. The flight crew reduced the power to 2 000 ft/lbs, and the oil pressure remained steady at 45 psi. The flight crew elected to divert to Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON, and performed a precautionary shutdown of the number 2 engine. The passengers were kept informed throughout the event. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and ARFF was placed on standby. The subsequent single engine landing was performed without further incident. The aircraft was shutdown on the runway, and towed to the apron.The operator's maintenance determined that the torque fluctuation was caused by a loss of oil from the leaking oil pressure switch.

C-GKOB, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1622 from Toronto/Lester B. Person Intl (CYYZ), ON to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL with 5 crew members and 133 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew received a HYD G RSVR LO LVL ECAM message. The ENG1 HD Pump and PTU were deactivated as per ECAM procedures, and the flight continued to destination. Just before the descent into KFLL, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN for priority ATC handling due to a possible manual landing gear extension. During the approach, the flight crew reactivated the hydraulic pump, and the landing gear extended normally without incident. After the landing, the aircraft stopped on the taxiway so that ARFF could inspect it, then continued to the gate on its own power. The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and identified a defective spoiler actuator as the source of the hydraulic leak. The component was replaced, and the Green Hydraulic System was serviced in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM). Subsequent tests were carried out with satisfactory results, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTAQ, a Jazz Aviation LP DHC-8-300 aircraft (AC8613), was taxiing for departure from runway 05 at Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ) when smoke and flames were reported emanating from the left main brakes. The aircraft stopped on the taxiway and the passengers were evacuated. ARFF responded to the site but their services were not required as the fire had self extinguished. Maintenance found the left main landing gear brakes were seized and heat damaged; the wheel overpressure plugs melted and the tires went flat.
