Damage was limited to the brakes and wheels, however, the left main landing gear was replaced as a precaution.

N361PJ, a Learjet 36 operated by Premier Jets Inc. took off from Montreal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC on an IFR flight to Cleveland Hopkins Intl (KCLE), OH. After take-off, the aircraft deviated from the standard instrument departure (SID) procedure, which resulted in a loss of separation with C-FRQP, an Embraer 170 operated by Sky Regional airlines as flight SKV7685 that was also departing from CYUL. Separation between the two aircraft was reduced to 2.3 nm horizontally and 100 feet vertically while the required minimum separation is 3 nm or 1000 feet.

C-FFKV, a privately operated Hughes 269C helicopter, was conducting a local VFR flight from Dolbeau-St-Felicien (CYDO), QC with one student pilot and one instructor on board. After completing 3 normal circuits, the student pilot approached for a landing on Runway 11. While hovering prior to the landing, uncontrollable oscillations appeared, which developed into severe ground resonance upon contact of the skids with the ground. The helicopter received substantial structural damage. There were no injuries.

C-FSXG, a Beech C90A King Air aircraft operated by the Moncton Flight College, was conducting a training flight from Fredericton Intl (CYFC), NB to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS and return to CYFC with 2 pilots on board. During the approach to CYHZ, the captain noted a thud, accompanied by a momentary vibration of the aircraft. A visual inspection revealed that the cowling on the right engine had separated. The controllability of the aircraft was, however, not compromised. The flight crew declared an emergency, and the aircraft landed at CYHZ without further incident. The operator’s maintenance found no damage to the aircraft, and no reports of damage from the ground. The cowling will be replaced, and the aircraft will be returned to service.

C-FJXZ, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8615 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Sudbury (CYSB), ON with 3 crew members, 1 jumpseat occupant and 52 passengers on board. Because of bad weather at CYSB, the flight returned to CYYZ a little more than 2 hours after the departure. As the aircraft was taxiing to the terminal after the landing at CYYZ, a collision with a fuel truck occurred. Both the fuel truck and the aircraft received substantial damage. Crew members and passengers evacuated the aircraft, and ARFF services attended the scene. There was no fire. Five people were taken to hospital for observation. The collision occurred during the hours of darkness, and in rainy weather. The TSB deployed a team of investigators.

C-GDGP, an Airbus Helicopter BK117 B2 operated by Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service (STARS), was conducting a MEDEVAC flight from Brooks Hospital (CFV8) Brooks, AB, to the Peter Lougheed Hospital (CLC3) Calgary, AB. with 2 flight crew, 2 medics and 1 patient on board. During cruise the flight crew received a chip detector warning light for the #2 engine (Lycoming LTS-101-750B1). The crew consulted the emergency procedures checklist and completed a precautionary shutdown of the #2 engine. The crew elected to divert to Calgary Intl. (CYYC), AB where an uneventful single-engine approach and landing was completed. No emergency was declared.Company maintenance completed the appropriate maintenance actions and the aircraft was released for service.

C-GSCH, a Sikorsky S92 Helicopter operated by Cougar Helicopters as CGR11, was conducting a test flight from St John's Airport (CYYT) NL. After departure, the transponder was not picked up by air traffic control and an automation problem prevented the coupling of some aircraft instruments. The helicopter had to be hand flown, and when selected up, the landing gear remained green with a red indication. The crew selected the gear down and observed 3 green lights. A PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft returned to CYYT where the gear was blown down to ensure extension. The aircraft was hover taxied back to the taxiway where ground crew confirmed the landing gear position before landing. The aircraft was towed back to the hangar. Maintenance jacked the aircraft up and noted the left main gear did not fully extend which resulted in the weight on wheels switch not engaging and this subsequently caused the failure of the autopilot automation, gear selection indication and transponder activation. Repairs are being effected to the left main gear and the aircraft will be returned to service after a maintenance release.

C-FJZK, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA2377 from Melbourne Intl (KMLB), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Person Intl (CYYZ), ON with only the 2 pilots on board. Passing 110 knots during the takeoff from KMLB, the flight crew received a GEAR NOT DOWN aural master warning message. The flight crew rejected the takeoff, and declared a MAYDAY. ARFF met the aircraft on the runway, followed shortly after by maintenance personnel for an inspection. The aircraft was then authorized to taxi to the apron. The operator’s investigation is in progress.

C-GPPS, un Jetstream 32-12 exploité par Pascan sous l’indicatif PSC582, s'apprêtait à effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB), à destination de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU), avec 13 passagers et 2 membres d’équipage. Lors du démarrage, le moteur droit (GARRETT TP331-12UHR) a subi un faux démarrage (hung start) et l’équipage a perçu des flammes par la tuyère d’échappement du moteur. La procédure de feu moteur au sol a été effectuée et les passagers ont été évacués par la porte d’entrée principale. Un préposé au sol a demandé l’intervention des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). Les flammes ne se sont pas propagées et il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GAQZ, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA787 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Los Angeles Intl (KLAX), CA with 5 crew members and 82 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL320 approximately 150 nm south of Minneapolis-St. Paul Intl/Wold-Chamberlain (KMSP), MN, the flight crew received an APU AUTO SHUTDOWN ECAM message. Since the flight had taken off from CYYZ under Minimum Equipment List (MEL) provision with the number 2 engine generator inoperative, the flight crew consulted with the operator’s Operational and Maintenance Control Centres, and the decision to divert to KMSP was elected. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight landed at KMSP without further incident. ARFF met the aircraft after the landing for an inspection, and the aircraft was authorized to taxi to a gate.The operator’s maintenance replaced the APU De-Oiling Solenoid Valve and the APU Bleed Control Valve as per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM). The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-FHOY, an Embraer EMB-190 operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA317 from Pierre Elliot Intl., QC (CYUL) to Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC) with 4 crew members and 54 passengers on board. While in cruise flight approximately 264 nm ENE of CYYC , the flight crew received a "ANVX MAU 2B" fault message on the EICAS. The flight crew referenced the appropriate checklist, and subsequently declared a PAN PAN for ARFF to complete a brake inspection on landing. The aircraft completed an uneventful landing in CYYC and taxied to the gate.

C-FNVV, an Airbus A320-211 operated by Air Canada as flight ACA160, departed Edmonton Intl. (CYEG) AB for Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ) ON. At approximately 60 nautical miles north west of Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl. (CYXE) SK., the crew observed a low green hydraulic system quantity indication. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and an operational decision was made to divert to Calgary Intl. (CYYC) AB. The flight landed safely in CYYC. The operator's maintenance replaced the green hydraulic low level switch, completed a leak check, and returned the aircraft to service.

C-GUCA, a Piper PA-31-350 Navajo aircraft operated by Flightexec, was conducting flight FEX100 from Hamilton (CYHM), ON to Sudbury (CYSB), ON with 2 pilots on board. As the flight crew selected landing gear down during the approach into CYSB, the landing gear failed to extend. The flight crew cancelled the approach, and diverted to North Bay (CYYB), ON due to the increased runway length. Using both the normal and alternate procedures, the flight crew made several attempts to extend the landing gear, however unsuccessfully. The decision to land with the landing gear retracted was made, and an emergency was declared; ARFF stood by for the landing. The aircraft touched down on Runway 08, and came to a stop on the paved surface. There were no injuries. The operator’s maintenance determined that a hydraulic line fitting had failed, releasing most of the hydraulic fluid and preventing the operation of both the normal and alternate landing gear systems. The fitting failed where it attaches to the hydraulic power pack.

C-FPDN, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1410 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Cancún Intl (MMUN), México with 5 crew members and 24 passengers on board. Following the landing at MMUN, the flight crew experienced difficulty exiting the runway. Once on Taxiway A3, the flight crew stopped the aircraft and requested an inspection of the tires. A brake on the left main landing gear had seized and, in consultation with the operator’s Maintenance Control Centre (MCC), the flight crew was unable to reset the brake. The aircraft was shut down, and passengers were deplaned. The operator’s maintenance replaced the brake, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FVLU, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA879 from Zurich-Kloten (LSZH), Switzerland to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 11 crew members and 175 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from LSZH, the flight crew received a C1 Hydraulic Pressure message, followed a Generator Control L1 EICAS message, which caused the associated generator to trip offline. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and, after executing the checklist, the system successfully returned online. The flight crew cancelled the emergency, and continued to destination without further incident.The operator’s maintenance carried out Fault Isolation Manual (FIM) tasks, and the aircraft was returned to service.

N853AE, un appareil de type Embraer EMB-135KL exploité par Envoy Air inc. sous l'indicatif ENY4127, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC, avec 3 membres d'équipage et 39 passagers à bord. À 28 miles marins au sud de CYUL, l’équipage a remarqué que le niveau d’huile du moteur #2 avait descendu à 4 pintes. L'équipage a suivi la liste de vérification (QRH) et a déclaré une urgence. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre avec les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GPHF, an Airbus Helicopters EC 130 T2 aircraft operated by Phoenix Heli-Flight, was conducting sling load operations from Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB with an external load of plywood using a cargo net. Shortly after the departure, some plywood sheets were able to escape the net, falling onto undeveloped land. The plywood was retrieved and the entire load was then strapped together inside the net to prevent a re-occurrence.

C-GFAF, an Air Canada Airbus A330 aircraft (flight AC842) departed Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ). After taking off the flight crew experienced an unusual engine vibration. In discussion with maintenance the flight crew decided to return to CYYZ. A PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft landed uneventfully. ARFF met the aircraft on arrival and after inspection the aircraft taxied to gate. Maintenance identified a bird strike that resulted in damage to fan blades 22, 23, and 24. The blades were replaced and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GNDO, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-6-300 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE641 depuis un camp situé au N55°40.74 / W077°11.17, QC à destination de Kuujjuarapik (CYGW) QC, avec 2 pilotes à bord. Lors du décollage, un des skis s’est pris dans la neige, la roue de nez s’est arrachée, et l’appareil est sorti de l’aire de décollage. L’appareil s’est immobilisé en dehors de la surface préparée pour le décollage. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. Le nez de l’appareil ainsi que l’aile gauche, le train d'atterrissage, ainsi que le moteur et l’hélice de gauche ont tous subi des dommages substantiels.

C-GEEN, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 operated by Westjet Encore Ltd. as flight WEN3242, departed Calgary Intl. (CYYC) for Brandon Municipal (CYBR). At 53 NM east of Regina Intl. (CYQR) SK, the flight crew observed the "#1 HYD QTY" light illuminate, followed by a loss of #1 hydraulic system pressure. The crew actioned the QRH, declared an emergency, and diverted to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl. (CYWG). WEN3242 successfully completed a flapless landing on Runway 18 with ARFF on standby and taxied to the gate. The operator's maintenance found a leak at the ground service pressure fitting. A new o-ring was installed, the cap was re-torqued and ground runs completed. The aircraft was returned to service.

N112BD, un appareil de type Learjet 60 exploité par Black Diamond Aviation Group LLC, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC, à destination de White Plains/Westchester County (KHPN), NY. Après avoir été autorisé pour le décollage de CYUL, une perte d'espacement est survenue lors de la montée initiale avec C-FRQP, un appareil de type Embraer ERJ 170-200 exploité par Sky Regional Airlines, qui effectuait le vol SKV7727 depuis CYUL à destination de Dallas-Fort Worth Intl (KDFW), TX, qui venait de décoller devant N112BD. L'espacement longitudinal a diminué à 2.6 miles marins (nm), alors que 3 nm étaient requis. Un vecteur radar a été donné à l’équipage du N112BD afin de rétablir la distance requise. Les 2 appareils ont poursuivi leurs vols à leurs destinations respectives.

C-GMCP, a Bombardier Learjet 45 aircraft operated by Skyservice Business Aviation, was conducting a flight from Edinburgh (EGPH), United Kingdom to Reykjavik/Keflavik (BIKF), Iceland with 4 crew members onboard. During pushback at EGPH, the nose landing gear collapsed. There were no injuries. The nose landing gear and surrounding airframe structure were damaged.The UK AAIB investigation (Ref EW/G2019/05/01) concluded the NLG collapse was most likely caused by inadvertent brake application during pushback.The final report was published in AAIB Bulletin 1/2020 on 09th January 2020.

C-FRSO, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA093 from Santiago de Chile/Arturo Merino Benitez Intl (SCEL), Chile to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. A Boeing 737-8 aircraft operated by Aeromexico, was conducting flight AMX617 from CYYZ to Mexico City/Benito Juarez Intl (MMMX), Mexico. AMX617 was cleared to taxi to position for a departure off Runway 05; however, their take off clearance was delayed due to a previous arrival exiting the runway. When ACA093 was at 2.5 nm final, AMX617 was cleared for take off and shortly afterward, ACA093 was instructed to go-around, climb to 3000 feet and turn to a heading of 360 degrees. A loss of separation occurred when ACA093 climbed to 3000 feet but did not turn to the assigned heading while AMX617 had departed Runway 05 and was climbing runway heading to 5000 feet as per the standard instrument departure clearance. ATC instructed AMX617 to stop their climb and instructed ACA093 to turn to a heading of 320. The aircraft were separated vertically by 700 feet and horizontally by approximately 0.25 nm.

On 04 May 2019, the Lakes District Air Service Ltd. Cessna 182E (registration C-FLVN, serial number 18253755) was conducting a fire surveillance flight under daytime visual flight rules. The flight was being conducted on behalf of the BC Wildfire Service in the vicinity of Smithers, British Columbia, with the pilot and 3 crew members on board. Approximately 3 hours into the flight, the pilot transmitted a Mayday before communication was lost. The 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter activated on impact and its signal was received by the Canadian Mission Control Centre. A helicopter search was conducted and the aircraft wreckage was located in a forested area approximately 50 nautical miles north of Smithers, 500 feet north of the Babine River, 5.6 nautical miles east of the Silver Hilton Lodge airstrip. The aircraft had collided with trees and terrain. One crew member survived the crash and was transported to hospital by helicopter. The pilot and the other 2 crew members were fatally injured. The aircraft was destroyed; there was no post-impact fire.UPDATED: 26 MAY 2020

C-FRTG, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC37 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Melbourne/Tullamarine Intl (YMML), Australia with 14 crew members and 212 passengers on board. At approximately 80 kts during the take-off roll from Runway 26L at CYVR, the crew flight heard a loud bang coming from the right engine (General Electric GENX-1B74/75/P2), and the aircraft simultaneously torqued rapidly to the right. The flight crew rejected the takeoff, and stopped on the runway. Since a flame was observed coming from the engine, ARFF responded to meet the aircraft. The aircraft taxied back to the gate without assistance. There were no injuries. The operator's maintenance discovered that the right engine had suffered a compressor stall as a result of a piston ring seal migration. An engine change was facilitated, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJKM, a Douglas DC3C-S1C3G aircraft operated by Buffalo Airways, was conducting cargo flight BFL169 from Hay River/Merlyn Carter (CYHY), NT to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with 2 flight crew on board. During the climb to cruise altitude after the departure from CYHY, the number 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney-USA, R-1830-92) lost complete power. The flight crew elected to return to CYHY, however were unable to maintain altitude. As more power was added to engine number 2 to maintain airspeed, it started to run rough. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, subsequently followed by a MAYDAY; a forced landing was executed approximately 3.5 nm south east of CYHY. The aircraft was substantially damaged, but there was no post-impact fire or injury to either flight crew.

C-FLUJ, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG781 from Montego Bay/Sangster Intl (MKJS), Jamaica to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 6 crew members and 184 passengers on board. During the boarding at MKJS, a cabin crew member became incapacitated after a passenger accidentally dropped a carry-on bag onto her head. The crew member experienced dizziness, headaches, and vomiting, was removed from the flight and taken to the hospital. A decision was made to disembark the passengers, and to operate the aircraft as positioning flight SWG9871 to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC without passengers.

C-GGSX, a Bell 206B helicopter operated by Vision Air Services, was conducting wildlife flight survey operations 5 nm east of Trenton (CYTN), NS with 1 pilot and 2 technicians on board. While manoeuvering at low altitude, the helicopter struck and severed a wire that spanned Big Cove bay. The small, single conductor was green in colour, 0.23 inches in diameter, and supplied 7.2 kV electrical power to a small group of buildings north of the bay. The helicopter made a precautionary landing ½ nm north of the location of the collision. There were no injuries. The helicopter sustained impact and electrical arcing damage to the main rotor leading edge surfaces.

C-FUJE, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 aircraft operated by Sky Regional Airlines, was conducting flight SKV7675 from Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl (KBOS), MA to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. Just before activating the flap lever during the descent into CYYZ, the flight crew observed a SLAT FAIL EICAS message. The flight crew interrupted the approach and requested vectors in order to complete the checklist. Subsequently, ARFF was requested on stand by for the flapless landing, and the aircraft landed on Runway 05 without incident. The aircraft stopped on the taxiway for inspection, and was authorized to taxi to the gate, followed by ARFF behind.The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and determined that the number 2 Slat/Flap Actuator Control Electronics (SF-ACE) needed to be replaced.

C-FUEQ, un hélicoptère de type Bell 206L-4 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue à partir d’un hangar privé près de Manic 5, QC à destination de Baie-Comeau (CYBC), QC avec 1 pilote et 5 passagers à bord. Lors de la manœuvre pour le décollage, le rotor principal est entré en collision avec un des murs du hangar. De fortes vibrations ont été perçues par le pilote qui a immédiatement reposé l’hélicoptère, et fermé le moteur. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. Le rotor principal a subi des dommages importants.

C-GQVQ, un appareil de type Cessna 152 exploité par Orizon Aviation Québec, effectuait un vol d’entraînement local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC avec 2 personnes à bord. Lors du retour vers CYQB, le pilote de C-GQVQ a été autorisé à pénétrer dans la zone de contrôle à 2500 pieds ASL, en provenance du sud-est par la contrôleuse aérienne du Terminal VFR de Québec. Presqu’au même moment, C-FKGE, un appareil de type Pilatus PC-12/47 exploité par Kudlik Aviation effectuant le vol local KUK761 selon les règles de vol à vue depuis CYQB, avait été autorisé à décoller de la piste 06 avec une restriction d’altitude à 2000 pieds ASL. Quelques minutes plus tard, KUK761 a été autorisé à contacter le Terminal VFR, avant que le pilote de C-GQVQ contacte la Tour de contrôle de CYQB. La Tour de CYQB a autorisé C-GQVQ en rapprochement à 2500 pieds ASL afin d’intégrer le circuit de la piste 06, et transmis l’information quant à la présence de KUK761 à 2000 pieds en direction sud-est. Le Terminal VFR de Québec a autorisé KUK761 à monter jusqu’à 7500 pieds ASL, sans l’aviser de la présence de C-GQVQ en rapprochement. Quelques instants plus tard, les contrôleurs aériens ont instruit leurs aéronefs respectifs à exécuter une manœuvre d’évitement. À ce moment, la distance entre les 2 aéronefs était d’un mile marin, sur un cap convergeant. Au plus près, l'espacement a été réduit à 100 pieds sur le plan vertical et 0.5 mile sur le plan horizontal.

C-GSME, a privately owned Mooney M20J aircraft was on approach after completing a circuit at Markham, Ontario (CNU8). During the touchdown the landing gear collapsed, and the aircraft slid to a stop on the runway. The pilot was not injured.  Maintenance determined that the push pull rods for the nose landing gear operation had failed. One rod was severed at both ends and the second was bent, affecting the over center locking mechanism of the nose gear and the locking integrity of the main landing gear.

N757NY, a privately registered Piper PA 46-350P aircraft, had departed from Goose Bay (CYYR), NL on a VFR flight plan to Narsarsuaq (BGBW), Greenland with 2 pilots on board. At approximately 0824 ADT, the Joint Rescue Coordination Center (JRCC) detected an Emergency Locator Transmitter (ELT) signal from the aircraft. It was determined that the aircraft had crashed into a snow-covered hillside, approximately 31 nm north northeast of Rigolet, NL. Deteriorating weather conditions at the time were less than adequate for air search and rescue resources. Both occupants survived the initial impact, however, one individual later succumbed to their injuries. The survivor was transported to Makkovik, NL via snowmobile until the weather became suitable for an air transport to a hospital in Goose Bay. The individual sustained serious injuries. The TSB is investigating.

C-FMWY, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1805 from Montego Bay/Sangster Intl (MKJS), Jamaica to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 8 crew members and 278 passengers on board. During cruise flight in the vicinity of Freeport/Grand Bahamas Intl (MYGF), Bahamas, one of the cabin crew members became incapacitated due to illness, and could not continue duties. Duties were redistributed to the remaining cabin crew members for the rest of the flight, and the aircraft landed at CYYZ without further incident.

C-GLWJ, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3126 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB with 4 crew members and 52 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYLW, the aircraft hit a flock of birds. The flight crew contacted ATC, and initiated a return back to land at CYLW. No emergency was declared, however ARFF was requested on standby. The aircraft landed without further incident. After touchdown, the flight crew elected to stop on the runway where they were met by ARFF.

N501VJ, un appareil de type Bombardier BD-700-1A11 Global 5000 exploité par Vista Jet, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Minneapolis-St. Paul/Wold-Chamberlain Intl (KMSP), MN à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC avec 3 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors qu’il approchait le hangar d’Exécaire à CYUL pour le stationnement après l’atterrissage, l’équipage était dirigé par 2 membres du personnel au sol; l’un était situé à l’avant, et l’autre à 45° sur la gauche de l’aéronef. Avant d’effectuer le virage final à 90 degrés vers la gauche, l’équipage a complété une vérification visuelle par la droite, et a suivi les instructions du personnel au sol. Quelques minutes plus tard alors que l’équipage quittait l’aéronef, un membre du personnel au sol a avisé que l’aile droite est entrée en collision avec la clôture lors du dernier virage, à l’insu de l’équipage. L’inspection visuelle a révélé que l’ailette de bout d’aile (winglet) a subi des dommages mineurs.

C-FDSN, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA578 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Los Angeles Intl (KLAX), CA with 5 crew members and 104 passengers on board. As the aircraft reached the Top of Descent (TOD) into KLAX, the flight crew received a YELLOW HYDRAULIC RESERVOIR LOW/LO PRESSURE ECAM message. The QRH was executed, and the flight crew declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed without further incident on Runway 25L, and stopped on the runway in order for ARFF to carry out an inspection. The aircraft was then cleared to taxi to the gate.  The operator’s maintenance replaced the manifold assembly in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM). A leak check was done, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GRXM, a Pilatus PC-12/47E aircraft operated by Ornge Global Air, was conducting a flight from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON to Timmins (Victor M. Power) (CYTS), ON with 2 pilots and 3 passengers on board. Upon selection of landing gear down during the approach into CYTS, the flight crew received a landing gear unsafe indication. The aircraft was flown over the Flight Service Station (FSS) to confirm the landing gear position. The flight crew executed the QRH procedures, and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance performed several landing gear operations, however could not duplicate the fault. The data fault information was sent to the unit manufacturer for evaluation, and the response is pending.

C-FSWE, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3670 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Nashville Intl (KBNA), TN with 4 crew members and 54 passengers on board. During the initial climb through 1500 feet after the departure from CYYZ, the FLAP DRIVE and FLAP POWER caution light illuminated, and the associated circuit breaker popped. The flight crew actioned the QRH for an abnormal flap landing, declared a PAN PAN, and diverted back to CYYZ. A flapless landing was executed with ARFF standing by. After the landing, the aircraft stopped on the runway so that ARFF could inspect the brakes, then taxied to the gate.The operator’s maintenance reset the L7 circuit breaker and performed a flap control function test and a flap drive test. No faults were detected, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FEJY, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 aircraft operated by Sky Regional Airlines, was conducting flight SKV7740 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ with 4 crew members and 76 passengers on board. Passing through clouds during the descent to 6000 feet at KEWR, the aircraft encountered icing conditions. Simultaneously, the flight crew received ICE CONDITION and SLAT FAIL EICAS messages. The flight crew executed the QRH, notified ATC of the slat failure, and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft subsequently landed on Runway 4R without further incident, with ARFF standing by. After exiting on Taxiway P3 and assessing the brake temperatures to be in the green, the aircraft taxied to the gate. The operator’s maintenance performed a series of resets and operational checks, which resolved the issues. The aircraft was released back into service.

C-GTSI, an Airbus 330-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC627 from Varadero/Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl (MUVR), Cuba to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 11 crew members and 344 passengers on board. Prior to the departure for the return flight, one of the cabin crew members became ill and was unable to perform duties. Positions were reassigned, and the flight departed without further incident.

C-GXZZ, a privately registered Cessna 170A aircraft, was landing on a private airstrip near Bottrel, AB. During the manoeuvre, a gust of wind came up, and the pilot lost control of the aircraft. The aircraft landed heavily, and passed through a fence. Damage included a collapsed left main landing gear, wing damage and a propeller strike. There was no injury to the pilot, who was the lone occupant.

C-FGQH, a de Havilland DHC-6 aircraft operated by Harbour Air, was conducting HES222 from Victoria Harbour (CYWH), BC to Vancouver Harbour (CYHC), BC with 2 crew members and 10 passengers on board. During the initial climb through 2500 feet, the flight crew noticed an electrical smell in the cockpit. The flight crew leveled the aircraft at 3500 feet, contacted ATC, and requested a return to CYWH. After completing the emergency checklist, the intercom system between the 2 pilots failed. The captain continued the approach, and landed single pilot without further incident at CYWH. The operator's maintenance found a smoking resistor in the throttle quadrant area.

C-GDGP, a Messerschmitt MBB-BK117 B-2 helicopter operated by Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service (STARS), was conducting a post-engine change (Lycoming LTS-101-750B1) test flight from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. During the return to CYYC, the flight crew received a chip warning indication, and elected to shut down one engine. A precautionary landing was carried out, and the helicopter was then towed back to its hangar.

C-GLQM, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE687 from Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON to Sault Ste. Marie (CYAM), ON with 4 crew members and 56 passengers on board. During the approach into CYAM with the landing gear extended, the flight crew conducted a missed approach as the weather conditions were below landing limits. The landing gear was selected up, and the flight crew subsequently received several fault indications including a LDG INOP caution light. QRH procedures were followed and, due to weather conditions, the flight crew elected to divert to Sudbury (CYSB), ON. A MAYDAY was declared, and the aircraft landed in CYSB without further incident.The operator’s maintenance replaced the Nose Landing Gear (NLG) harness and, following landing gear swings, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBHO, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1704 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Deer Lake (CYDF), NL with 5 crew members and 119 passengers on board. After selecting landing gear down during the final approach to Runway 25 at CYDF, the flight crew received several ECAM messages related to the landing gear. The flight crew initiated a go around, and declared a PAN PAN. On the second approach, the flight crew did not receive any ECAM messages, and landed without further incident. After the landing, a L/G SYS DISAGREE message was received. The aircraft remained on the runway to allow ARFF to visually inspect the aircraft, and to troubleshoot with maintenance personnel. Under maintenance guidance, the flight crew conducted a Landing Gear Control Interface Unit (LGCIU) reset, which rectified the condition. The aircraft taxied to the ramp without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced a defective Nose Landing Gear (NLG) proximity sensor, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GFWI, a Bell 204B aircraft operated by Fireweed Helicopters, was conducting an external load operation in the vicinity of Rackla River, YT with only the pilot on board. A load of lumber was being slung, when one of the two nylon straps failed. The load was lost onto a hillside, midway between the point of departure and its intended destination. The decision was made to make an attempt to retrieve the load. When the pilot was conducting a toe-in landing onto the snow-covered hillside, the main rotor blades made contact with an unknown object and/or the snow. The helicopter was grounded, and maintenance staff were dispatched to the helicopter. The aircraft was hauled by road to the maintenance base for further assessment, repair and overhaul of affected components.

C-GFAV, a Beech 200 aircraft operated by Fast Air, was conducting local training flight PBR01T from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with 2 crew members on board. During the final approach for Runway 36, the left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-41) began to lose power and would not respond to power lever input. The flight crew decided to do a precautionary engine shutdown, and declared an emergency. The aircraft continued on final, and landed without further incident. The operator's maintenance inspection of the aircraft and subsequent engine run-up did not reveal any anomalies.

C-GVJZ, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8863 from Gander Intl (CYQX), NL to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS with 4 crew members and 71 passengers on board. During the descent into CYHZ, the flight crew advised ATC that they had a failure of the number 2 hydraulic system, and conducted an alternate landing gear extension. No emergency was declared, however ARFF was requested on standby. The aircraft landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance found a cross-threaded fitting on the number 2 Engine Driven Pump. After replacement of parts, the aircraft was returned to service.

N788UA, un appareil de type Boeing 777-200 exploité par United Airlines, effectuait le vol UAL56 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Paris/Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France vers Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ. C-FRTU, un appareil de type Boeing 787-9 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA879 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Zürich-Kloten (LSZH), Suisse à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. UAL56 était établi en palier au FL360, alors que ACA879 était aussi en palier au FL380. Les 2 appareils suivaient un cap similaire, mais divergent. Environ 30 nm au sud-ouest de Sept-Îles (CYZV), QC, UAL56 a été autorisé à monter au FL380. Une perte d'espacement est survenue lorsque UAL56 s'est établi au FL380, alors que la distance horizontale entre les 2 appareils a été réduite à 8.8 nm. L’espacement requis était de 10 nm sur le plan horizontal, ou 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical.

C-FRQW, un appareil de type Embraer ERJ 170-200 exploité par Sky Regional Airlines, effectuait le vol SKV7519 selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de Charlottetown (CYYG), PE à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. Environ 63 miles marins au sud-est de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC, l'équipage a été avisé d'une odeur de fumée en provenance de la portion arrière de la cabine. Aucune fumée n'était visible, toutefois l'équipage a décidé d'effectuer un déroutement vers CYQB. Aucune urgence n'a été déclarée, et l'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé.

C-FZUB, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA253 from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 5 crew members and 128 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL360, the flight crew observed a GREEN low hydraulic fluid pressure on the ECAM, followed by a hydraulic green number 1 engine low pressure. The flight crew turned off the Engine Driven Pump (EDP) and the Power Transfer Unit (PTU), and declared a PAN PAN. The landing gear was manually extended, and the aircraft landed at CYVR on Runway 26R without further incident, with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance found that the number 5 right-hand spoiler servo was leaking, and replaced it.

C-GOCU, a privately registered Schleicher ASW 28-18E glider, was conducting a flight from Black Diamond/Cu Nim (CEH2), AB with 1 pilot on board. During the flight, the aircraft descended at an altitude too low to make it back to the departure airport. The pilot attempted a forced landing in a farmers field and, during the landing, the aircraft ground looped. The pilot was not injured, however the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

N871NN, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL397 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Chicago/O’Hare Intl (KORD), IL. During the takeoff from Runway 26L at CYVR, one of the tires on the left main landing gear blew. The YVR Airport Authority reported tire fragments on the runway, as well as a hydraulic line support bracket. The flight crew was contacted and determined that the aircraft would be overweight if they returned to CYVR; therefore, the decision to divert to Seattle-Tacoma Intl (KSEA), WA, was elected. The flight crew reported that the hydraulic system A quantity was depleted to 23%, and the ANTI-SKID INOPERATIVE light illuminated after takeoff. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft proceeded to KSEA. After the landing, the number 2 tire was confirmed to have burst, which resulted in multiple severed hydraulic lines, supports, and wire harnesses in the left wheel well. There was additional damage to the left wing inboard flap, left horizontal stabilizer, and lower wing panels. The left main landing gear tires, damaged hydraulic lines, and canon plugs were replaced.

On 24 April 2019, the Keewatin Air LP Beechcraft B200 aircraft (registration C FRMV, serial number BB979), equipped to perform medical evacuation flights, was conducting an instrument flight rules positioning flight (flight KEW202), with 2 flight crew members and 2 flight nurses on board, from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson International Airport, Manitoba, to Rankin Inlet Airport, Nunavut, with a stop at Churchill Airport, Manitoba.At 1814 Central Daylight Time, when the aircraft was cruising at flight level 250, the flight crew declared an emergency due to a fuel issue. The flight crew diverted to Gillam Airport, Manitoba, and initiated an emergency descent. During the descent, both engines flamed out. The flight crew attempted a forced landing on Runway 23, but the aircraft touched down on the frozen surface of Stephens Lake, 750 feet before the threshold of Runway 23. The landing gear was fully extended. The aircraft struck the rocky lake shore and travelled up the bank toward the runway area. It came to rest 190 feet before the threshold of Runway 23 at 1823:45 Central Daylight Time. None of the occupants was injured. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter activated. Emergency services responded. There was no fire

C-GSGU, a Cessna 208B aircraft operated by Sander Geophysics, was conducting a photo flight from Jandakot (YPJT), Australia to Dampier (YPKA), Australia with 2 crew members on board. During the flight, a smell of hot electronics was noticed, followed by a small puff of smoke coming from behind the instrument panel. The flight crew carried out the Electrical Fire checklist, and diverted the aircraft to Mount Magnet (YMOG), Australia. During the return, electrical systems were restarted one at a time as per the checklist. There were no further signs of smoke or fire. The aircraft landed 30 minutes later at YMOG without further incident.The operator’s maintenance opened the instrument panel and inspected it; no faults were found.  Avionics were also verified, and no faults were found. When the autopilot was turned on, the elevator trim circuit breaker tripped. The autopilot and electric elevator trim systems were disabled, and aircraft was returned to service.

C-FMGM, a Kaman K-1200 helicopter operated by Heliqwest Aviation, was conducting heli-logging operations approximately 13 nm west of Campbell River (CYBL), BC with only the pilot on board. Shortly after lifting two logs from the cut block, the pilot felt a bump and observed the two logs dropping from the grapple, followed by the grapple itself. The load fell approximately 400 feet into a ravine. The pilot returned to the service landing area, and landed without further incident.

C-GORF, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7230 from Medicine Hat (CYXH), AB to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 2 crew members and 17 passengers on board. During the take-off roll out of CYXH, the flight crew observed a slower rate of acceleration; however, the take-off roll was continued. Approaching the Top Of Descent (TOD) into CYYC, the flight crew observed that the parking brake was on. The parking brake was released, and ARFF was requested for the arrival. After the landing, the aircraft was inspected on the runway, and two flat tires were noted on the left main landing gear. There was no other damage or injuries related to the occurrence.

C-FLHJ, a Boeing 737-400 aircraft operated by Flair Airlines, was conducting flight FLE482 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB with 6 crew members and 114 passengers on board. During the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from CYLW, the flight crew noted a decrease in fluid quantity and pressure for hydraulic system B. Approaching the Top Of Descent (TOD), the flight crew observed that the hydraulic quantity for system B had decreased to less than 30%. The appropriate QRH checklist was actioned, a PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed at CYEG without further incident with ARFF standing by. Smoke was observed after the landing due to hydraulic fluid dripping on the brakes. The aircraft taxied to the gate.

C-GETA, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8037 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Fredericton Intl (CYFC), NB with 3 crew members and 37 passengers on board. Upon selection of landing gear up after the departure from CYHZ, the flight crew advised ATC that they had lost the number 2 hydraulic system. The flight crew declared an emergency, and requested a return to CYHZ. The aircraft returned and landed without incident with ARFF standing by.The operator's maintenance found that the right hydraulic line to the nose landing gear drag strut actuator was leaking. The line was replaced and, after the system was bled and serviced, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPPS, a British Aerospace Jetstream 32 aircraft operated by Pascan Aviation, was conducting flight PSC582 from Iles-de-la-Madeleine (CYGR), QC to Quebec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC with 2 crew members and 13 passengers on board. During the take-off roll on the departure from CYGR, the number 2 engine lost power. The flight crew rejected the takeoff, and taxied back to the apron. The operator’s maintenance was unable to determine the source of the power loss. The aircraft was ferried to the operator's maintenance base for further maintenance inspection.

C-GKOB, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1803 from Kingston/Norman Manley Intl (MKJP), Jamaica to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 5 crew members and 135 passengers on board. During cruise flight in the vicinity of Raleigh/Durham Intl (KRDU), NC, the flight crew noted an odour in the flight deck described as dirty socks. The odour dissipated, however subsequently returned with stronger intensity. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks, declared a PAN PAN, and initiated a diversion to KRDU. The aircraft subsequently landed at KRDU without further incident, with ARFF standing by.A maintenance inspection identified the APU intake and plenum to be soiled, and were cleaned in accordance with (IAW) the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM). The APU condensers and pack number 2 were found to be contaminated as well, and were replaced. An engine wash was accomplished on both engines, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYSK, a Convair CV340/580 aircraft operated by the Province of Saskatchewan/Northern Air Operations, was conducting a local flight as TKR474 from Prince Albert (Glass Field) (CYPA), SK with 3 crew members on board. During the initial climb after the takeoff, the flight crew noted an issue with the number 1 engine propeller (Hamilton Standard 54H60-77), and decided to do a precautionary engine (Allison 501-D22G) shutdown. The flight crew declared an emergency, and returned to CYPA where the aircraft landed without further incident.An inspection of the propeller system by the operator's maintenance revealed defective o-rings inside the propeller hub. The operator has filed a Service Difficulty Report (SDR) with Transport Canada.

C-GLWJ, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3273 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Regina Intl (CYQR), SK with 4 crew members and 27 passengers on board. During the takeoff from CYWG, the flight crew received a NOSE LANDING GEAR DOOR caution light indication. The flight crew completed the QRH procedures, continued to CYQR, and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed on Runway 31 without further incident. An inspection of the landing gear indication system by the operator's maintenance revealed that the Proximity Sensor Electronic Unit (PSEU) was out of tolerance. The sensor was rigged, and gear swings were successfully completed. The aircraft was then returned to service.

N469UA, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL2292 from Denver Intl (KDEN), CO to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. During the approach to Runway 26R at CYVR, the flight crew executed a missed approach. During the manoeuvre, the flight crew did not follow the missed approach procedure, and flew the runway heading instead. C-GPCY, a Beech 1900C aircraft operated by Pacific Coastal Airlines, was conducting flight PCO203 from CYVR to Powell River (CYPW), BC, and had simultaneously departed off Runway 26L, on a runway heading. Both aircraft came within 1.2 nm and at the same altitude prior to ATC instructing a turn.

C-GJZF, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA538 from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. C-GMPO, a Pilatus PC-12/47E aircraft operated by the Government of Canada/Royal Canadian Mounted Police, was conducting a flight from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON to Kitchener/Waterloo (CYKF), ON. Approximately 26 nm north north-west of CYYZ, a loss of separation occurred when JAZ538 was level at 9000 feet ASL, while C-GMPO was descending as authorized through 8300 feet ASL, to 6000 feet ASL. The two aircraft came within 2.8 nm horizontally of each other in airspace that requires 5 nm or 1000 feet vertical separation. C-GMPO acquired JZA538 visually just prior to the closest point of separation. There were no TCAS alerts reported, and no alteration of flight paths required. A transfer of position briefing occurred with the involved Air Traffic Controllers while the situation was developing.

C-GRIF, a Bombardier CL600-2B16 Challenger 601 aircraft operated by Chartright Air, was conducting flight HRT093 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Kitchener/Waterloo (CYKF), ON with 2 crew members and 1 passenger on board. Shortly after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew requested a return to CYYZ due to an unsafe gear indication, and requested the emergency equipment (ARFF) on standby. The flight crew carried out the QRH items, and lowered the landing gear. The aircraft returned for an uneventful landing on Runway 05 with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance inspected the landing gear and discovered a faulty nose gear proximity sensor, which was replaced and tested before returning the aircraft to service.

C-FLSU, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA290 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with 5 crew members and 146 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the cabin crew advised that there was an odour and smoke coming from the aft galley. The flight crew declared an emergency, and decided to divert the aircraft to Regina Intl (CYQR), SK, where the aircraft landed without further incident.An inspection of the aircraft by the operator’s maintenance revealed a damaged coffee maker.

C-GKUK, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8909 from Greater Moncton Roméo Leblanc Intl (CYQM), NB to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 4 crew members and 61 passengers on board. During cruise flight at 16 000 feet, the aircraft experienced a loss of cabin pressure, accompanied by a loud popping sound heard from the back of the aircraft. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks, initiated an emergency descent to 10 000 feet, and declared a PAN PAN. The flight continued to destination without further incident. The operator’s maintenance identified a leak from a faulty cargo door seal.

C-FNNW, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA007 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Hong Kong Intl/Chek Lap Kok (VHHH), China with 17 crew members and 404 passengers on board. Approaching VHHH, ATC advised the flight crew of delays at destination due to weather, and that all alternate airports within the vicinity were also closed. The flight crew declared a MAYDAY, and landed at VHHH uneventfully with 6500 kgs of fuel remaining.

C-GQBQ, un appareil de type Bombardier CL-600-2B16 Challenger 601 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait le vol QUE20 selon les règles de vols aux instruments à partir de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC vers Kuujjuaq (CYVP), QC. Lors de la montée vers l’altitude de croisière, le voyant DUCT FAIL du système anti-givrage des ailes s'est allumé. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification d’urgence applicable et a demandé un retour vers CYQB. En raison du poids supérieur au maximum autorisé par le manufacturier de l’appareil, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence. L'appareil s'est posé sans problème à CYQB. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil. Une fuite d'air du système anti-givrage de l'aile droite a été détectée, puis réparée. L’appareil fût par la suite remis en service.

C-FGRP, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-8-100 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol de convoyage JZA9015 depuis Val-d'Or (CYVO), QC à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC avec 3 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en vol de croisière, le voyant d'avertissement AIR COND PACK HOT s'est allumé. L'équipage a complété la liste de vérification applicable, et est descendu à 14 000 pieds. Une urgence a été déclarée, et l'appareil s'est posé à destination sans encombre. Le personnel de l’entretien de l’exploitant a remplacé un contacteur de température excessive défectueux sur le groupe de conditionnement d'air. L'appareil a été remis en service.

C-FDJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8172 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Washington/Dulles Intl (KIAD), VA with 4 crew members and 48 passengers on board. During the descent for the approach to Runway 1R into KIAD at 4000 feet ASL, the aircraft encountered a near miss with a drone. The device passed at less than a wingspan away to the right of the aircraft, and at the same altitude. The flight crew described it as a 4-blade drone. ATC was advised. There were no injuries, and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FRON, a privately operated Cessna 340A aircraft, was conducting a recreational day-VFR flight from Peterborough (CYPQ), ON to Kawartha Lakes (Lindsay) (CNF4), ON with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. Approximately 200 feet after the touchdown on Runway 13, the left main landing gear collapsed during the landing roll, causing the propeller to contact the runway. The aircraft veered to the left, and exited the left side of the runway, onto the grass. There were no injuries; however, the aircraft sustained damage to the left flap, wingtip, and propeller. The airport was closed to all traffic until the aircraft was moved clear of the runway area.

C-FLUJ, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG534 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Val D’Or (CYVO), QC with 6 crew members and 154 passengers on board. During the boarding in CYUL, one of the cabin crew members sustained a medical incident, and was transported to the airport clinic. Another cabin crew member was called in to operate the flight, and the aircraft departed without further incident.

C-FYJG, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1848 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Los Cabos Intl (MMSD), México with 5 crew members and 133 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew noted a light odour in the flight deck. The cabin crew reported the same odour, however stronger in the cabin area. The flight crew leveled the aircraft off at 10 000 feet, declared a PAN PAN, and requested a return to CYYZ. Radar vectors were required to allow some time to complete QRH actions before commencing the approach. The aircraft then landed overweight on Runway 05 with ARFF standing by, and subsequently taxied to the gate.The operator’s maintenance found that the odour was noticeable when the right Air Conditioning Pack was running, and found the associated condensers to be contaminated with oil. The right pack has been deferred inoperative under MEL provisions, and, following an overweight landing inspection, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GPRU, un appareil de type Beech B100 exploité par Max Aviation, effectuait le vol de formation MAX130 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU), QC avec seul 2 pilotes à bord. Lors de la montée initiale après le départ de CYHU, de la fumée est apparue dans le poste de pilotage. L’équipage a décidé de revenir se poser à CYHU et a déclaré un état d’urgence. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés, et l’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 24R sans encombre. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé, ni de dommages. L’inspection post envolée n’a pas révélé de présence de fumée; la source de la fumée n’a pas encore été identifiée.

C-FRQM, un appareil de type Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU exploité par Sky Regional Airlines, effectuait le vol SKV7685 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination de Houston/George Bush Intercontinental (KIAH), TX. Lors du décollage de la piste 24L à CYUL, une perte d’espacement est survenue lors de la montée initiale avec JY-BAA, un appareil de type Boeing 787-8 exploité par Royal Jordanian Airlines, qui effectuait le vol RJA90G de CYUL à Détroit/Metropolitan Wayne County (KDTW), MI, et qui venait de décoller devant SKV7685. L’espacement longitudinal a diminué à 4,2 miles marins (nm), alors que 5 nm étaient requis. Un vecteur radar a été donné à SKV7685 afin de rétablir la distance requise, et aucune turbulence de sillage n’a été rapportée. Les 2 appareils ont poursuivi leurs vols à leurs destinations respectives.

G-VBEL a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Virgin Atlantic, was conducting flight VIR20 from San Francisco Intl (KSFO), CA to London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK. During cruise flight, the flight crew initiated a climb from FL390 to FL410. The flight crew noted that the cabin altitude started to rise at a rate of 600 feet per minute, deviating from the normal 6000 feet. Manual cabin pressure control was selected, and a PAN PAN was declared. The flight crew elected to descend back down to FL390. The aircraft had been dispatched under Minimum Equipment List (MEL) provision for an inoperative Cabin Air Compressor (CAC) on the left air conditioning pack. Section 2 of the B787 MEL notes that the cabin altitude, which is normally 6000 feet, may rise to 8000 feet with an inoperative pack or CAC in degraded operations. After review of this section of the MEL, the flight crew continued to destination without further incident.

C-GYJZ, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8993 from St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. During the final approach to Runway 32 at CYHZ, the flight crew received an aft baggage smoke indication. The flight crew followed the QRH, discharged the fire bottles, and declared a MAYDAY. The aircraft landed without further incident. ARFF met the aircraft and checked for smoke or fire. After determining that there were no signs of fire, the aircraft taxied to the gate. The operator’s maintenance replaced extinguishers and conducted operational tests of the system before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GLKY, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting flight PAG663 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Sandy Lake (CZSJ), ON with 3 crew members and 28 passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff, the flight crew received a lavatory smoke alarm, followed by the smell of smoke. The flight crew decided to declare an emergency, and returned to CYWG where the aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF responding. An inspection of the aircraft revealed a leaking compressor seal of the right engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW123), that introduced oil into the engine bleed air system. The aircraft was removed from service, and the engine was replaced.

C-IDRB, a privately operated Quad City Challenger Basic Ultra-light aircraft, was conducting a local flight from Edmonton/Cooking Lake (CEZ3), AB with only the pilot on board. During cruise flight at 1200 feet AGL approximately 8 nm south west of CEZ3, the engine (BRP Rotax 447) lost power. The pilot declared a MAYDAY, and conducted a forced landing in a farm field. During the rollout after the touchdown, the nose landing gear collapsed, and the aircraft came to rest. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured. Varnish fuel residue in the fuel tank became loose, and was ingested into the main fuel line. This resulted in a fuel blockage that caused the engine to stop because of fuel starvation.

C-GTJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7358 from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky Intl (KCVG), KY to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 3 crew members and 9 passengers on board. During the takeoff roll at KCVG, the flight crew heard a loud noise coming from the nose landing gear area. The flight crew suspected a blown tire, and contacted the operator’s Operational Control Centre (OCC), who contacted KCVG ATC to inquire whether debris had been found on or near the departure runway. During the arrival into the Toronto area, the flight crew notified ATC about the issue, and requested ARFF to be standing by; no emergency was declared. The aircraft landed uneventfully, and taxied to the gate. The operator’s maintenance performed a detailed inspection of all landing gear and associated components; no faults were found. The nose wheel tires were replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOGN, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA003 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to London/Gatwick (EGKK), UK with 9 crew members and 262 passengers on board. During cruise flight, a cabin crew member experienced a medical incident. The flight crew was advised, and Medlink was contacted. The affected cabin crew member was removed from duties, which were redistributed to the remaining cabin crew members for the landing.

C-FEXX, a Cessna 208B aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express, was conducting cargo flight MAL8071 from Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 1 pilot on board. As the aircraft was authorized for the visual approach to Runway 26L behind a Boeing 787-8, MAL8071 encountered light wake turbulence, followed immediately by an uncommanded roll to the right. The pilot applied full left aileron deflection in order to stop the roll at a 45° bank angle. The event lasted a number of seconds before the pilot was able to return to wings level. The separation at the time of the event was approximately 7 miles. The pilot notified ATC, and continued the approach without further incident.

C-GTVG, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG731 from Montego Bay/Sangster Intl (MKJS), Jamaica to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 6 crew members and 193 passengers on board. While being vectored for an approach to Runway 06L at CYYZ, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to CLIMB. The flight crew complied with the command, and advised ATC. ATC replied that the conflicting traffic was unidentified, and not in communication with ATC. SWG731 was vectored for a second approach, and landed without further incident.

C-FJCQ, an ATR 72-200 aircraft operated by Calm Air International LP, was conducting flight CAV111 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with 4 crew members and 41 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYTH, the flight crew noticed that the number 2 engine fuel flow indication was abnormally high. An employee of the air operator, who was seated in the cabin, noticed fuel leaking from the right engine, and notified the flight crew. The flight crew advised ATC, and requested a return to CYTH. During the descent through 5000 feet, the right engine (PW124B) lost power. The flight crew declared a MAYDAY, and the aircraft landed without further incident at CYTH. The local fire department was advised. The operator's maintenance found and replaced a defective fuel transfer tube.

C-GJZG, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA7962 from Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 3 crew members and 31 passengers on board. During cruise flight in the vicinity of Trenton (CYTR), ON, the flight crew received erratic oil pressure indications from the left engine. The flight crew feathered the left propeller, declared a PAN PAN and continued to destination. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GJYZ, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Perimeter Airlines LP, was conducting flight PAG209 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Gods Lake Narrows (CYGO), MB with 3 crew members and 32 passengers on board. Shortly after departing CYWG, the flight crew selected landing gear up and simultaneously received a #2 HYD ISO caution light, associated with pressure and quantity loss of the number 2 hydraulic system. The flight crew notified ATC, levelled off at 3000 feet, and referenced the QRH. After a discussion with the operator’s Operational and Maintenance Control Centres, the flight crew declared an emergency and returned to CYWG. The aircraft landed without further incident on Runway 18, with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance found that the number 2 hydraulic line had failed.

C-FDMH, a privately operated Cessna 140 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Carleton Place (CNR6), ON to Ottawa/Carp (CYRP), ON. As the aircraft was taxiing down-wind for the departure on a wet, grass covered runway at CNR6, the main landing gear sank through the soft grass, and into mud. The aircraft nosed over, came to rest upside down, and sustained substantial damage. There were no injuries.

N230PS, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by PSA Airlines, was conducting flight JIA5664 from Washington/Ronald Regan National (KDCA), DC to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During the descent into CYYZ, the flight crew declared an emergency due to a flap issue. The aircraft landed without further incident, and there were no injuries.

C-FZUG, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1653 from Miami Intl (KMIA), FL to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 5 crew members and 130 passengers on board. Approximately 10 minutes prior to the Top Of Descent (TOD) in the vicinity of New York City, NY, the number 1 engine (CFM 56-5A5) started to exhibit symptoms of a compressor stall with vibrations, N1 roll back, airspeed decrease, and high Exhaust Gas Temperature (EGT). The flight crew executed the QRH, and declared a PAN PAN. During the descent to CYUL, the engine parameters returned to normal values. The aircraft proceeded to land without further incident.The operator’s maintenance performed a borescope inspection on the engine, and no faults were found. The Fuel Pump/Hydro Mechanical Unit (HMU) package was removed, and replaced in accordance with (IAW) the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM). Serviceability tests were carried out satisfactorily, and the aircraft was returned to service. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) was also raised.

C-FXMY, a Beech B200 King Air aircraft operated by Keewatin Air LP, was conducting medevac flight KEW209 from Rankin Inlet (CYRT), NU to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with 5 persons on board. During the climb to cruising altitude through FL200, the right engine (PT6A-42) made a loud bang, followed by flames emitting from the exhaust. The flight crew conducted a precautionary engine shutdown, declared an emergency, and requested a return to CYRT. The aircraft landed without further incident, and taxied to the apron. The operator’s maintenance found a failed engine compressor blade.

C-FXWJ, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA602 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK with 5 crew members and 131 passengers on board. The flight crew was conducting an ILS approach to Runway 09 at CYXE, with a reported visibility of ½ mile in fog and an RVR of 1800 feet. During the landing flare, the aircraft descended into a layer of fog, and visual contact with the runway surface was lost; however, the runway edge lights were visible. The aircraft began to drift to the right, and the right main landing gear wheels struck 3 runway edge lights. The flight crew corrected the drift, returned to the runway centerline, and continued the roll out. The operator’s maintenance discovered tire damage, and replaced the right main landing gear wheel assemblies. CYXE airport personnel replaced the runway edge lights.

N928EV, un Bombardier CRJ-200 exploité par SkyWest Airlines sous l’indicatif SKW3130, avec à son bord 3 membres d'équipage et 44 passagers, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport international de Chicago O’Hare, US (KORD) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). En passant le niveau de vol 200 en rapprochement de CYUL, les indications de vitesses sont devenues incertaines, l'anémomètre du commandant signalait un drapeau avertisseur ambre (amber IAS flag), celui du copilote indiquait 40 kts et son altimètre fluctuait. L’équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre sur la piste 06R avec les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GCNK, a Boeing 737-300 aircraft operated by Canadian North, was conducting flight MPE1525 from Fort Mackay/Albian (CAL4), AB to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 5 crew members and 120 passengers on board. C-GYYE, a Cessna 172L aircraft operated by McMurray Aviation, was conducting a sightseeing flight from Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB, and was approximately 5 nm south of CAL4 at 3500 feet ASL.  MPE1525 departed off Runway 13 at CAL4 and, at approximately 400 feet AGL, the flight crew initiated a right climbing turn to proceed direct to the ETMAR waypoint. As the aircraft was climbing through 3000 feet ASL, the flight crew received a TCAS target. The auto throttle was disengaged, the power levers were brought back to idle, and the flight crew initiated a descent in an attempt to maintain a 1000-foot vertical separation with C-GYYE. During the process, the flight crew received several DON’T SINK Ground Proximity Warning System (GPWS) aural warnings. MPE1525 passed approximately 1200 feet below C-GYYE. Both aircraft were operating in Class G airspace at the time of the occurrence. Although both aircraft were communicating on the North Oil Sands ATF 123.5 MHz frequency, direct communication between the 2 aircraft was not established by the pilots.

C-FBRP, a Cessna 525B aircraft operated by Tricycle Lane Aviation, was conducting a private flight from Scottsdale (KSDL), AZ to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 2 pilots and 4 passengers on board. During the turn to final approach at CYYC at approximately 2000 feet AGL, the flight crew received a BAGGAGE SMOKE indication. The flight crew carried on with the approach, and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without incident, vacated the runway, and was met by ARFF. No smoke was present; the flight crew elected not to evacuate the aircraft. Fire crews inspected the aircraft and no heat source was detected. The operator’s maintenance inspected the forward and aft baggage compartment smoke detection system. No faults were found. The issue was entered into the operator’s Safety Management System (SMS) for tracking, and the aircraft was released back to service.

C-FZLW, a Bombardier BD-700-2A12 Global aircraft, was conducting production test flight BBA19 from Toronto/Downsview (CYZD), ON with 3 crew members on board. During the flight, the flight crew received an EICAS message indicating a fuel leak on the number 1 engine. The flight crew actioned the QRH which led to a precautionary engine shutdown, and returned to CYZD where the aircraft landed without further incident. A maintenance inspection determined that there was no fuel leak. An investigation is under way to determine the cause of the apparent erroneous EICAS message.

C-GQGF, a Piper PA-28-181 aircraft operated by Excel Flight Training, was conducting a student-pilot solo cross-country training flight from Medicine Hat (CYXH), AB to Brooks Regional (CYBP), AB. During the landing on Runway 30 at CYBP, the pilot landed long and decided to abort the landing after touchdown. The pilot applied full throttle, however the aircraft departed the end of the runway and struck the airport perimeter fence. The aircraft came to rest approximately 200 feet beyond the paved surface of the displaced threshold of the runway. There were no injuries, and the ELT did not activate. The aircraft received damage to the propeller, and the wing leading edges received substantial damage from contact with the airport perimeter fence posts.

C-GKEP, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7332 from Nashville Intl (KBNA), TN to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 3 crew members and 45 passengers on board. During the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from KBNA, the aircraft experienced a left engine 14th stage duct issue. The flight crew stopped the climb at FL250, requested a return to KBNA, and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed back without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced the number 1 BLCU. After a few tests, the aircraft was returned to service.

N826AE, un appareil de type Embraer EMB-135KL exploité par Envoy Air, effectuait le vol ENY3368 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC avec 3 membres d'équipage et 41 passagers à bord. Lors de l’approche finale pour la piste 06R à CYUL, l’ATC a donné l’instruction à l’équipage de conduite d’effectuer une remontée, dû à un aéronef encore présent sur la piste après l’atterrissage en raison de conditions glissantes. ENY3368 a déclaré une urgence et a demandé la priorité d'atterrissage pour cause de carburant minimum et de conditions météorologiques se dégradant rapidement. L'aéronef est revenu se poser sans encombre sur la piste 06R. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

N833AE, an Embraer EMB-135KL aircraft operated by Envoy Air, was conducting flight ENY3957 from New York/John F. Kennedy Intl (KJFK), NY to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 3 crew members and 42 passengers on board. Upon landing gear down selection during the approach to Runway 05 at CYYZ, the flight crew observed an abnormal landing gear indication. An emergency as declared, and the flight crew requested a fly-past inspection in order for ATC to observe the apparent position of the landing gear. ATC subsequently confirmed that the landing gear appeared to be fully extended. The flight crew conducted an approach to Runway 06R, and landed without further incident with ARFF standing by.The operator replaced the Landing Gear Electronic Unit (LGEU) and performed extension and retraction checks in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FCZZ, an Aero Commander 690A aircraft operated by Conair Group, was conducting a local IFR training flight from Abbotsford (CYXX), BC with 2 crew members on board. During the initial climb after the departure, the cockpit filled with smoke. The pilot cancelled the IFR flight plan, completed the emergency checklist, remained VFR, and returned to land. The cabin temperature was lowered, and the smoke started to subside. No emergency was declared, however ATC was notified of the situation. The aircraft landed back at CYXX without further incident. No injuries were reported. Maintenance personnel replaced the air cycle machine.

C-GGGQ, a B200 Beech King Air aircraft operated by Miccar Aerial (dba Good Spirit Air Service), was conducting flight GT1128 from Prince Albert (Glass Field) (CYPA), SK to Yorkton Muni (CYQV), SK with only the 2 pilots on board. During the descent through 12 000 feet approximately 40 nm north of CYQV, the flight crew noticed fluctuations in the fuel flow and gas generator speed (ng) for the left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-42). As the flight continued in the descent, the left engine parameters returned to normal, then followed by a dramatic engine rollback. The flight crew feathered the engine, noticed an increase in ITT, and performed a precautionary engine shutdown. The aircraft landed without further incident in CYQV with emergency services responding. The operator’s maintenance replaced the fuel control unit.

C-FDST, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA416 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Montreal/Pierre E. Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 5 crew members and 14 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYYZ, the cabin crew informed the flight crew that there was an oil/plastic burning smell in the cabin. The flight crew stopped the climb at FL190, executed the Smoke/Fumes checklist, and decided to return to CYYZ. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed at CYYZ without further incident. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft. The operator’s maintenance reported finding the APU intake plenum deteriorated, and partially collapsed. The aircraft was returned to service on Minimum Equipment List (MEL) provisions.

C-GJJT, a Beech 200 Super King Air aircraft operated by Wabusk Air, was conducting a flight from Iqaluit (CYFB), NU to Moosonee (CYMO), ON with 2 pilots and 3 passengers on board. As the aircraft started its descent, approximately 61 nautical miles north east of CYMO, the flight crew noticed fuel flow fluctuations and surging of the right engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-42). The surging then intensified, and an R FUEL PRESS annunciator warning light illuminated. The flight crew executed the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) procedure, however the problem persisted. As the flight crew prepared to shut the engine down, it flamed out by itself. The auto feather system was armed, and activated on its own. The flight crew declared an emergency and continued the flight to CYMO, where an uneventful landing was performed. Maintenance personnel found the standby fuel pump circuit board burnt. Troubleshooting of the standby and engine-driven boost pump is ongoing.

C-FSRW, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8064 from Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 4 crew members and 51 passengers on board. Prior to being cleared for the visual approach to Runway 26R at CYVR, JZA8064 was on an assigned heading and was level at 3000 feet ASL in Visual Meteorological Conditions (VMC). ATC advised the flight crew of a VFR traffic in the vicinity that was assigned an altitude of 3500 feet ASL (C-GZTI, a Cessna 172N aircraft operated by Pacific Professional Flight Centre, from Qualicum Beach (CAT4), BC to Vancouver/Boundary Bay (CZBB), BC with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board). Similarly, C-GZTI was notified by ATC of the presence and position of JZA8064. The flight crew of JZA8064 received a TCAS TA in response to the VFR traffic, followed by a TCAS RA to MONITOR VERTICAL SPEED. C-GZTI had been warned by ATC of possible wake turbulence from JZA8064, and was instructed to descend to 2000 feet when ready.
