C-GZTI initiated a descent, shown on radar passing 0.5 nm to the right and 400 feet above JZA8064 at its closest point. Although a TCAS RA activated, no avoidance manoeuver was initiated. The event was captured by Jazz’s SMS.

C-GTNV, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 helicopter operated by Trans North Turbo Air, was conducting a flight in the vicinity of Coldfoot, AK with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. During a routine caribou capture for Environment Yukon/Alaska Fish and Game, one of the net weights fired from the netgun by an employee struck the outer leading edge of one of the main rotor blades. The pilot landed the helicopter immediately and shut it down. The operator sent another helicopter to recover the crew and replace the damaged blade. After an inspection, the helicopter was flown to its base on a flight permit to perform a full inspection.

C-GGOY, un appareil de type DHC-8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA8639 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS à destination d’Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON avec 4 membres d'équipage et 28 passagers à bord. Alors qu’il était en vol de croisière, la quantité de liquide du réservoir hydraulique numéro 1 est descendue à 35%, suivi peu de temps après de 0%. L'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence lors de la descente vers CYOW, et un atterrissage a été effectué sans encombre. Suite à l’atterrissage, l’appareil a été remorqué jusqu’à la barrière.L'équipe d'entretien a découvert qu'une conduite hydraulique du circuit de drainage de la pompe entrainée par le moteur numéro 1, s'était partiellement rompue dû à de l'usure par frottement. La conduite a été réparée, et le système hydraulique fût remis en état de fonctionnement.

C-GLKY, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting flight PAG633 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Sandy Lake (CZSJ), ON with 3 crew members and 32 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYWG, the flight crew received a lavatory smoke alarm, followed by the smell of smoke. The flight crew declared an emergency, and returned to CYWG where the aircraft landed without further incident. An inspection of the aircraft revealed a defective recirculation fan, which is suspected to have been the source of the smoke. The fan was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYNF, an Agusta AW139 helicopter operated by 7506406 Canada Inc. (ORNGE Rotor Wing Operation), was conducting a flight from Kenora (CYQK), ON to White Dog, ON. During the taxi to the active runway for the departure at CYQK, the flight crew received a #2 ENGINE OIL TEMP warning illumination from the Crew Alerting System (CAS). While still on the ground, the flight crew confirmed the high oil temperature, initiated the QRH, and carried out a precautionary shut down of the number 2 engine (PWC PT6C-67C). The aircraft was taxied back to the apron.The operator's maintenance replaced the fuel oil cooler.

C-GTSY, an Airbus 310-300 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC099 from Punta Cana Intl (MDPC), Dominican Republic to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with only the 2 pilots on board. While passing 1500 feet during the initial climb after the departure off Runway 08 at MDPC, the number 1 engine (General Electric CF6-80C2A2) experienced compressor stalls. The flight crew executed the QRH procedure, and requested a return to MDPC. Initially, the number 1 engine was brought to idle, then back to 50% N1 for the landing. A MAYDAY was declared, and the aircraft landed on Runway 08 without further incident. ARFF inspected the aircraft after the landing, then cleared the flight crew to taxi to the ramp.The operator’s maintenance performed a borescope of the booster and High Pressure Compressor (HPC) STG1 and STG12 in accordance with (IAW) Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) 72-31-00. Minor blade nicks and dents were observed, all within AMM limits. The High Pressure Turbine (HPT), Variable Stator Vane (VSV) and the Oil Magnetic Chip Detector (MCD) were also inspected IAW the AMM, and nothing was found. The Intermediate Pressure (IP) check valve and Compressor Inlet Temperature (CIT) sensor were replaced IAW the AMM, and following engine power runs, the aircraft was returned to service. The aircraft returned to CYUL without further incident.

C-GHKX, an Airbus 330-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA824 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Amsterdam/Schiphol (EHAM), Netherlands with 10 crew members and 197 passengers on board. Upon landing gear up selection after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew received an ECAM brake indication. ECAM actions were completed, and in consultation with the operator’s Operational and Maintenance Control Centres, it was decided to continue the flight to destination. During the descent into EHAM, ARFF was requested as a precaution. The aircraft landed without further incident with normal braking. The flight crew taxied the aircraft to the gate.The operator’s maintenance replaced the Brake Pressure Triple Indicator and the Brake and Steering Control Unit (BSCU) as per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM). Following tests, all brake indications were normal. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FDJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 CRJ900 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA576 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK with 4 crew members and 67 passengers on board. Approximately 205 nm east northeast of CYVR during cruise flight, the flight crew received a brake overheat indication, and elected to return to CYVR. An emergency was declared, and ARFF were positioned on standby. The aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident. After the landing, the brake temperature was measured, and was assessed to be within limits. The aircraft was cleared to taxi to the gate. There were no injuries.The operator’s maintenance replaced the number 1 brake assembly and the brake temperature sensor in accordance with the maintenance manual. The system was successfully tested, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FNAA, a British Aerospace Jetstream 3212 aircraft operated by Northwestern Air Lease, was conducting flight PLR607 from Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB to Fort Chipewyan (CYPY), AB with 2 crew members and 13 passengers on board. When reverse thrust and braking were selected during the landing roll on Runway 04 at CYPY, the aircraft departed the left side of the runway surface, out to approximately 50 feet. The wind at the time was reported as variable from 260° to 330° magnetic at 17 knots, gusting to 29 knots, and the runway surface condition report was 100% bare and dry. As the aircraft slowed down, the pilot was able to steer it back onto the runway surface. There were no injuries, and no damage to the aircraft.

C-FLSU, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA351 from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 5 crew members and 146 passengers on board. Following the ignition of the number 1 engine after the pushback from the gate, the flight crew received a SEC 1 fault message and a GENERATOR #1 line smoke light. Subsequently, there was smoke in the cabin and the flight deck. Both engines were shut down, and the smoke dissipated. The aircraft was towed back to the gate. The operator’s maintenance determined that SEC1 showed evidence of overheating and was replaced. The unit is located in the avionics bay, which is directly below the flight deck.

C-GWEF, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3650 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Nashville Intl (KNBA), TN with 4 crew members and 76 passengers on board. During the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew noticed a decrease of the number 1 hydraulic system fluid quantity, followed by a #1 HYD ISO VLV and ROLL SPLR INBD HYD caution lights. The flight crew actioned the QRH, requested a return to CYYZ, and declared a PAN PAN. The landing was uneventful with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance found the number 1 anti-skid control valve assembly hydraulic union fittings cracked, and leaking. The fittings were replaced in accordance with (IAW) CMM 32-48-07 and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GNTA, a Dassault/Dornier Alpha Jet A aircraft operated by Top Aces, was conducting a Close Air Support (CAS) mission in the vicinity of Bagotville (CYBG), QC, along with another aircraft. During the flight, C-GNTA experienced an uncommanded power rollback of the right engine. A fuel stream coming from the right engine could also be observed by the pilot of the second aircraft. The pilot positioned the affected engine throttle to STOP, which also caused the fuel stream to stop. The pilot declared an emergency, and headed back to CYBG where the aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. The cause of the engine flameout is still under investigation. It was concluded that the vapor stream observed was fuel being purged from the combustion chamber after the flameout.

C-FMWQ, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1609 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 8 crew members and 132 passengers on board. Upon selection of the landing gear down during the approach to Runway 24L at CYUL, the flight crew received a GEAR DISAGREE and TAILSKID EICAS message. The flight crew initiated a missed approach, executed the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) procedures, and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft subsequently returned for a successful landing with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance later identified Relay K904 faulty, which was replaced with satisfactory results.

C-GVPA, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-8-300 exploité par PAL Airlines, effectuait le vol PVL1910 depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC. Peu après le décollage de CYUL, l'appareil a connu une défaillance du système numéro 2 de référence de cap et d'assiette (AHRS), accompagné par l'illumination de témoins lumineux du panneau d'avertissement central. L’équipage de conduite a demandé un retour à CYUL et, alors que des conditions de vol aux instruments étaient anticipées, l’équipage a déclaré un PAN PAN afin d'obtenir la priorité d'atterrissage. L'appareil s’est posé sans encombre.

C-ICMG, un avion sur ski immatriculé comme étant un Ultra-léger de base de type Zenair CH-701-L en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local à partir du Lac Malartic, QC selon les règles de vol à vue avec seul le pilote à son bord. Après avoir décollé du lac Malartic vers 13h20 locales, l’avion a effectué un survol à basse altitude au-dessus du chemin du lac Malartic, avant de disparaître derrière les arbres. Peu de temps après, des flammes et de la fumée ont été aperçues s'élevant du site de l'écrasement, situé à environ 50 mètres à l'est de la route 117, à la borne kilométrique 548. Un incendie post-impact a en partie consumé l'aéronef. Le pilote a initialement survécu à l’accident, toutefois il a succombé à ses blessures peu après son arrivée à l'hôpital. Selon les rapports d’Environnement Canada, les conditions météorologiques au moment de l’écrasement étaient propices au vol à vue, avec un ciel dégagé et des vents légers en provenance du nord.

C-FLDQ, a privately registered Piper J3C-65 aircraft on skis, was conducting a VFR flight from Minaki (CJA6), ON to Snowshoe Lake, ON with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. As the aircraft was on a low-pass prior to the landing, the pilot lost control and the aircraft collided with the frozen surface of the lake. The pilot sustained fatal injuries. The passenger sustained serious injuries, however succumbed to his injuries 6 days later. TSB investigators deployed to the site.

C-FIUR, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA15 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Hong Kong/Chek Lap Kok Intl (VHHH), Special Administrative Region of China. During the descent into VHHH, the flight crew received a SMOKE REST UPR DOOR 5 EICAS message. The QRH checklist was completed, and no smoke was found. The aircraft landed uneventfully. The airport and local maintenance were advised.

C-FSBV, a Boeing 787-9, was being operated by Air Canada as fight AC857 from Heathrow Airport (EGLL) to Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ). During cruise, the aircraft encountered continuous moderate turbulence, as well as a few moments of severe turbulence. All aircraft parameters were within limits. There were no injuries reported and flight continued to YYZ uneventfully. Maintenance completed the severe turbulence inspection and no faults were found.

C-FFWV, a privately registered Boeing A75N1 Stearman aircraft, was conducting circuits at Abbotsford (CYXX), BC with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. As the southwesterly wind had increased and started gusting during the third touch-and-go, control was lost and the aircraft ground looped to the right. The aircraft became perpendicular to the runway and began to skid, resulting in the collapse of the left main landing gear. The aircraft struck one runway edge light, and came to rest on the right hand edge of the paved surface of the runway, in the opposite direction. The pilot and the passenger evacuated the aircraft with no injuries. There was no post impact fire, however the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GTBY, a Cessna 208 aircraft operated by Superior Airways, was conducting a flight from Red Lake (CYRL), ON to Pikangikum (CYPM), ON with 2 crew members and 2 passengers on board. During the initial climb after takeoff from CYRL, the flight crew noticed an electrical smell, followed by smoke emitting from the transponder. The flight crew pulled the circuit breaker for the transponder, and the smoke subsided. The decision to return to CYRL was elected, and the aircraft landed without further incident. Reportedly, the transponder had recently been replaced. An inspection of the transponder revealed discoloration of an internal circuit board, which indicates heat distress. The operator will submit a Service Difficulty Report (SDR) to Transport Canada.

C-FTJQ, an Airbus 320-200 operated by Air Canada as flight AC948 with 6 crewmembers and 89 passengers on board was en route from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QUE, to Le Raizet - Pointe-à-Pitre, Guadeloupe, France (TFFR). During cruise at FL350 near Bermuda, the flight crew received an ECAM message with the FLT CONTROL page showing the left spoilers in the UP position. After discussion with the company, the decision was made to return to CYUL. When the aircraft was about 20 nm south of CYUL, the crew declared a PAN PAN and carried out an uneventful landing on Runway 24L at 16 h 43Z with ARFF on standby. Spoiler 1R actuator was replaced in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual and the aircraft was returned to service following a successful operational test.

C-GAQL, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1208 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to West Palm Beach Intl (KPBI), FL. While on radar vectors to the ILS Runway 10L approach at KPBI, the flight crew reported that they received a TCAS TA, followed quickly after by a TCAS RA to CLIMB. The flight crew followed the RA instruction until the alert was over, and the aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-GZKC, an American Champion 7ECA aircraft operated by Harv's Air Service, was conducting circuits at Winnipeg/St. Andrews (CYAV), MB with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. Following 2 uneventful touch-and-go circuits, the pilot was planning to land on Runway 31, and complete a full stop. Upon touchdown, the aircraft landed off the centre line of the runway. The pilot attempted to correct toward the centreline using right rudder input, and subsequently decided to abort the landing. As power was applied, the aircraft veered off the right side of the runway, and flipped upside down. Emergency Medical Services (EMS) responded to the accident. The pilot was uninjured, and the passenger received minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GJVX, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA342 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON with 6 crew members and 170 passengers on board. While on final approach to Runway 32 at CYOW, the aircraft hit multiple birds and ingested some into the number 1 engine (CFM56-5B3/P). Subsequently, the flight crew received an ENG FAIL ECAM message, followed by an engine flameout. A MAYDAY was declared, and the aircraft landed without further incident. The aircraft was towed to the gate due to the loss of the green hydraulic system. There were no injuries.

C-FCME, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Central Mountain Air, was conducting flight GLR651 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB with 2 crew members and 15 passengers on board. Upon landing gear down selection during the approach to Runway 02 at CYEG, the flight crew received green down and locked indications for the left and right main landing gear only. The GEAR UNSAFE light did not illuminate, and the GEAR UNSAFE horn did not sound. The flight crew carried out the appropriate checklist and, as no nose landing gear was visible in the propeller spinner, a manual extension of the landing gear was executed. Due to the weather conditions at CYEG, the flight crew decided to return to CYYC and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without further incident and taxied to the terminal. There were no injuries.

C-FLSW, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG508 from Cancun Intl (MMUN), Mexico to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB with 6 crew members and 177 passengers on board. During the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from MMUN, the flight crew received a HYDRAULIC SYS B ENG2 LOW PRESSURE indication. Subsequently, when the aircraft reached its cruising altitude of FL350, the corresponding fluid quantity began to drop. The flight crew contacted the operator’s Operational Control Centre (OCC) after following the QRH procedure, and the decision to divert to CYYZ was made. Upon being handed over to Toronto Centre (CZYZ) during the descent to CYYZ, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft proceeded to land uneventfully with ARFF standing by. After the landing, ATC requested that the aircraft hold its position on Taxiway H, whereupon ARFF reported continuous fluid leakage from the number 2 engine. The number 2 engine was shut down, and the aircraft taxied to the infield terminal on one engine. The operator’s maintenance replaced the number 2 Engine Driven Pump (EDP) and, after an operational check, the aircraft was returned to service.

N492UA, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL1799 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Denver Intl (KDEN), CO with 5 crew members and 71 passengers on board. During the initial climb after the takeoff from Runway 33R at CYYZ, the flight crew was unable to control the thrust on the number one engine. The flight crew shut the engine (IAE V2500) down in accordance with QRH procedures, declared an emergency, and returned to CYYZ. The aircraft landed back on Runway 33R without further incident; there were no reported injuries. The operator’s maintenance replaced the Fuel Metering Unit and the Electronic Engine Control. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-FUWS, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA2261 from Liberia/Daniel Oduber Quirós Intl (MRLB), Costa Rica to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 5 crew members and 107 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL380, a cabin crew member experienced a medical incident. The flight crew contacted Medlink, and the decision to divert to Houston/George Bush Intercontinental (KIAH), TX was elected. Duties were distributed to other cabin crew members for the rest of the flight, and the aircraft landed without further incident at KIAH. Once at the gate, the ill cabin crew member was taken to the hospital by Emergency Medical Services (EMS).

C-GLRR, a Piper PA31-325 operated by Ootsa Air Ltd., had departed Prince George, BC (CYXS) for Tsay Keh, BC (CBN9) and was climbing through about 5000 feet asl when the left engine (Lycoming TIO-540-A2C) backfired and quit. The pilot declared an emergency and returned to Prince George where the aircraft landed uneventfully. Maintenance found that the left engine's magneto P-lead was shorting out and the left and right engine P-leads were replaced.

C-GSGT, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Wildcat Helicopters, departed the Tyax Lodge (Tyaughton Lake, BC) with 1 pilot and 12 heli-skiers on board. While at low height above the treetops and climbing over rising terrain to the north west, the helicopter's airspeed dropped below 45 knots, while its rate of climb decreased. The pilot made a steep 180° right turn in order to avoid terrain. During the turn, the aircraft descended slightly and the main rotor blades struck a few tree tops. The pilot decided to return to the Tyax Lodge. There were no injuries, however there was damage to the main rotor blades. The operator’s maintenance removed the drivetrain and transmission for inspection and repairs.

C-GPWG, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1412 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Cayo Coco/Jardines del Rey Intl (MUCC), Cuba with 5 crew members and 145 passengers on board. As the aircraft exited the runway after the landing in MUCC, and following an uneventful flight, the flight crew experienced a nose wheel steering failure. ECAM actions were carried out, and the flight crew taxied to the gate using differential braking to steer the aircraft.The operator’s maintenance carried out troubleshooting, and replaced a number of parts associated to the steering system.

C-GHPT, a Boeing 787-8 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA309 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 10 crew members and 255 passengers on board. During the take-off roll on Runway 06R at CYUL, the pilot flying noticed that the aircraft was nose heavy on rotation, to the extent that the control column had to be pulled hard in order to complete the rotation. The takeoff was continued, and the autopilot was selected on during the climb. No emergency was declared, and the flight continued to CYVR where an uneventful landing was carried out. The operator’s maintenance replaced the left-hand elevator feel actuator as per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM), and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GCPZ, a Beech 1900C aircraft operated by Pacific Coastal Airlines, was conducting flight PCO456 from Trail (CAD4), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 2 crew members and 11 passengers on board. Passing through 20 000 feet during the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from CAD4, the aircraft experienced a rapid loss of cabin pressure. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks, initiated a rapid descent to 10 000 feet, declared an emergency, and diverted to Kelowna (CYLW), BC. The oxygen masks in the cabin deployed, and were used by passengers. The aircraft landed at CYLW on Runway 34 without further incident. There were no injuries.The operator’s maintenance replaced the main cabin door's lower seal, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FXHE, un hélicoptère de type Aerospatiale AS 355 F2 exploité par Héli-Inter, effectuait un vol d'inspection de lignes électriques pour le compte d’Hydro-Québec, dans la région de Saint-Sauveur (QC) avec 1 pilote et 3 passagers à bord. Lors de la vérification d’un pylône à 100 pieds au-dessus du sol, le moteur numéro 2 (Allison 250-C20R/2) s'est éteint. Le pilote a été en mesure de reprendre de la vitesse et de l'altitude, et s’est dirigé vers St-Jovite (QC) où il s'est posé sans encombre. Lors de la vérification faite par le personnel de l’entretien, il a été constaté que toutes les ailettes du troisième étage du compresseur étaient manquantes.

C-GPCL, a Beech 1900D, operating as Pacific Coastal flight PCO1537, departed Victoria, BC (CYYJ) for Kelowna, BC (CYLW). As the aircraft levelled off at 19,000 feet asl the crew noted a strong smell of burning plastic which appeared to be coming from the environmental system. The crew selected "left envir off" and the smell diminished but the cabin altitude began to climb. The crew declared a PAN PAN and diverted to Vancouver, BC (CYVR) where the aircraft landed uneventfully. Company maintenance found that the forward vent blower fan was seized and that the current limiter in the left engine nacelle had popped. The vent blower fan (p/n 114-380028-11) and the current limiter (p/n ACH30) were replaced and the aircraft returned to service. An SDR was submitted.

C-FKCO, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA700 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY with 5 crew members and 97 passengers on board. During the intermediate approach into KLGA, the flight crew received a NOSE WHEEL STEERING fault message. The flight crew carried the appropriate procedure, declared a PAN PAN, and landed without further incident. The aircraft taxied to the gate on its own power.The operator’s maintenance replaced the number 2 Landing Gear Control and Interface Unit (LGCIU) as per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM). After a few nose wheel steering tests, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTSN, an Airbus 330-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC141 from Punta Cana Intl (MDPC), Dominican Republic to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 11 crew members and 332 passengers on board. During the turn around time in MDPC, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to perform duties for the return flight. Duties were reassigned to other cabin crew members, the aircraft departed and completed its flight to destination without further incident.

C-FARC, a Cessna 172S aircraft operated by Mitchinson Flying Service, was on a local training flight from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK with only the pilot on board. Upon touchdown during the landing on Runway 09 at CYXE, the aircraft was struck by a gusting crosswind. The aircraft bounced twice, and then veered off the right side of the runway where it came to a rest in an upright position. A PAN PAN call was made on the tower frequency by the pilot. The pilot was not injured, however the aircraft sustained damage to the nose landing gear and propeller.

C-FEIQ, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 aircraft operated by Sky Regional Airlines, was conducting flight SKV7608 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Washington/Ronald Reagan National (KDCA), DC with 5 crew members and 39 passengers on board. During the initial climb through 1400 feet after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew received a lavatory smoke warning. The cabin crew confirmed an odour and smoke in the cabin. The flight crew declared a MAYDAY, and requested to return to CYYZ. The Lavatory Smoke and Smoke Evacuation checklist items were executed, and the aircraft landed uneventfully on Runway 23 with ARFF standing by. Following an inspection, the flight crew was cleared to taxi to the gate. The operator’s maintenance reported that a compressor wash had taken place the previous night, and residual liquid may have caused the smoke. Engine runs were performed, and no further smoke or odour were noted. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FLSW, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG597 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Cancún Intl (MMUN), México with 6 crew members and 187 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew received a SYS B ENG 2 low pressure light. The QRH was executed, and the flight crew communicated with the operator’s Operational Control Centre (OCC); the decision to continue to MMUN was taken, despite the SYS B hydraulic pressure fluctuating. Subsequently, as the SYS B hydraulic pressure was steadily decreasing, the SYS B ELEC 1 low pressure light came on. The QRH was once again referenced, OCC was contacted one more time, and the flight crew planned for a flaps 15 approach and landing at MMUN. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight was given priority handling. The aircraft landed without further incident on Runway 12L, and taxied to the gate.The operator’s maintenance found no leak, however the hydraulic pump and hose assembly were replaced. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FNEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3220 from Grand Prairie (CYQU), AB to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 4 crew members and 78 passengers on board. During the descent into CYYC, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue duties. The flight crew declared a medical emergency, and requested priority handling from ATC. Emergency Medical Services (EMS) attended to the cabin crew member upon arrival at the gate.

C-FUOW, a privately-registered Cessna 340A aircraft, was conducting a flight from Vernon (CYVK), BC to Ponoka Industrial (Labrie Field) (CEH3), AB with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. Passing through 16 000 feet after the departure from CYVK, the right engine (Teledyne Continental TSIO-520-NB) experienced an uncommanded shutdown. The pilot feathered the propeller, declared a MAYDAY, and diverted to Kelowna (CYLW), BC where the aircraft landed without further event.Maintenance personnel performed a ground run of the right engine, however were not able to determine the cause of the shutdown. Further investigation is ongoing.

C-FENJ, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3240 from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Grande Prairie (CYQU), AB with 4 crew members and 75 passengers on board. Shortly after reaching FL280 after the departure from CYEG, the aircraft experienced a leak in the number 1 hydraulic system. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and elected to return to CYEG. A flapless landing was conducted with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance found a broken O-ring on the number 1 hydraulic manifold. After appropriate repairs were done, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GGJA, un appareil de type Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA44 entre Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON et Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl (KBOS), MA. C-GDEW, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par WestJet Encore, effectuait le vol WEN3514 de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON vers Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. JZA44 avait été autorisé par l’ATC à monter au FL190. Bien que l’autorisation ait été relue correctement par l’équipage de conduite de JZA44, l’ATC l'a observé au FL194, et l’a ré-autorisé au FL190. En conséquence, l'espacement avec WEN3514 a été réduit à 600 pieds et 3 miles, alors que la norme est de 1000 pieds ou 3 miles.

C-FIOM, a Messerschmitt MBB-BK117 A-4D helicopter operated by Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service (STARS), was conducting medical emergency flight STAR5 from Grand Prairie (CYQU), AB with 2 flight crew and 2 medical personnel on board. While en route, the flight crew observed a CHIP light for the number 2 engine (Avco Lycoming LTS-101-750B1). The flight crew completed the appropriate check list, shut the number 2 engine down, returned to CYQU and declared an emergency. A uneventful single-engine approach and landing was performed to Runway 25. The operator’s maintenance observed no significant debris on either chip monitors for the number two engine, and returned the helicopter back into service.

C-GGNW, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA518, from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, (CYWG) MB with 4 crew members and 78 passengers on board. The flight was being operated at 9000 feet ASL under MEL provision due to a Cabin Pressure Control System, and at approximately 56 nautical miles west northwest of Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK, the flight crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory (RA), commanding a climb. ATC was advised, and the aircraft climbed to 9600 feet until a CLEAR OF CONFLICT aural message was heard. The flight crew then returned to 9000 feet, notified ATC, and continued to destination without further incident. The conflicting traffic was C-GCSS, a private Piper PA-32R-300 aircraft that was on a VFR flight from CYXE to Camrose (CEQ3), AB at 8500 feet.

N452UA, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL545 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Denver Intl (KDEN), CO with 5 crew members and 140 passengers on board. During the departure off Runway 26L at CYVR, the aircraft experienced multiple bird strikes. The flight crew subsequently declared an emergency, and requested a return to CYVR. The aircraft landed without further incident on Runway 26R with ARFF standing by, and the aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power. Runway 26L was closed for 15 minutes for cleanup.The operator’s maintenance found that several ducks hit the left side of the fuselage. An inspection found 5 damaged blades on the number 1 turbo-fan engine (International Aero Engines V2500 series). These blades were in the low pressure compressor section of the engine, and there was evidence of tip curl or missing tips on these blades. The blade damage warranted an engine replacement.

C-GRRD, a privately operated Cessna 510 Citation Mustang aircraft, was conducting a flight from Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB to Calgary/Springbank (CYBW), AB with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During cruise flight, the aircraft experienced a vibration in the number 2 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW615 FA). The pilot elected to shut the engine down, and secured it. No emergency was declared, the flight continued at a lower altitude and landed at CYBW without further incident.Subsequent investigation by maintenance personnel determined that the source of the vibration was the number 2 starter/generator. The unit was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FHIF, a privately operated, ski equipped Maule M-5-235C aircraft, was conducting a flight from MacKay Lake, NT to Yellowknife Water Aerodrome (CEN9), NT with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the take-off run from MacKay Lake, the aircraft struck an object on the surface with the left ski assembly. The impact sheared the left oleo upper attach bolt, resulting in the landing gear leg to swing freely. The pilot elected to change the destination from CEN9 to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT, due to the availability of emergency services. When the aircraft was inbound for CYZF, the pilot indicated to ATC that there were problems with the left landing gear/ski. The pilot declared an emergency, and ARFF was activated. A low pass was carried out over the airport infield, while a suitable landing area was decided upon. C-FHIF proceeded to land on the infield, north of Runway 28. During the landing roll, the left hand landing gear collapsed. There were no injuries.

C-GWBL, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA2382 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Ixtapa-Zihuatanejo Intl, (MMZH), Mexico. WJA2382 had departed CYYC off Runway 35R, and had been cleared to 9000 feet on a heading of 360°. N906EV, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by SkyWest Airlines, was conducting flight SKW1362 from CYYC to Denver Intl (KDEN), CO. SKW1362 had departed from Runway 35L, and had been cleared to FL210 on a heading 345°. WJA2382 was subsequently cleared to FL210 and to turn left to a heading of 250°, in front of SKW1362. During the process, the separation was reduced to 700 feet vertically and 2.23 nm horizontally, where 1000 feet or 3 nm is required.

C-GWRK, a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan aircraft operated by McMurray Aviation, was conducting a flight from Fort McMurray (CYMM), AB to Fort Chipewyan (CYPY), AB with only the pilot on board. The pilot was issued taxi instructions from the ground controller at CYMM to hold short of Runway 07 at the Taxiway C intersection, due to an airport maintenance vehicle on the runway. The pilot read back the instruction correctly, however the aircraft was observed taxiing past the hold short line, and onto Runway 07. Subsequently, the pilot contacted ground control to confirm he had take-off clearance, and was informed that take-off clearance had not been issued due to airport vehicle traffic currently on the runway. The pilot was then instructed to taxi clear of the runway, and to return to the ramp.

C-FYMK, a Cessna 208B aircraft operated by Superior Airways, was conducting a flight from Red Lake (CYRL), ON to Pikangikum (CYPM), ON with the pilot and one passenger on board. During the initial climb at approximately 400 feet AGL, the pilot received a traffic alert, and initiated a best rate of climb. The aircraft then climbed out, and missed a helicopter by approximately 300 feet. It was reported that the traffic was C-GBOU, a privately operated Robinson R44 II helicopter. The pilot of C-GBOU had reported its position 8 miles to the north east, during the initial takeoff roll of C-FYMK.

C-FTUA, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG455 from Punta Cana Intl (MDPC), Dominican Republic to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS with 6 crew members and 162 passengers on board. During cruise flight, one of the cabin crew members became ill and was unable to continue duties. Duties were distributed to other cabin crew members and, prior to the descent into CYHZ, the ill cabin crew member started to feel worse. Paramedics were requested to meet the aircraft upon arrival, and the aircraft landed without further incident. The ill crew member received medical attention at the gate.

C-GQWJ, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1152 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to San Juan/Luis Muñoz Marín Intl (TJSJ), Puerto Rico with 5 crew members and 126 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL370, approximately 470 nm east of Wilmington Intl (KILM), NC, a flight crew member was unable to perform flight duties due to illness. A medical professional travelling as a passenger administered first aid, while the other flight crew member initiated a return to CYYZ. Emergency Medical Services (EMS) were requested as a precaution on arrival, and the aircraft landed without further incident. The flight crew member was assessed by EMS personnel, and released shortly thereafter.

G-ZZZA, a Boeing 777-200 aircraft operated by British Airways, was conducting flight BAW174 from New York/John F. Kennedy Intl (KJFK), NY to London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK with 13 crew members and 196 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL370, at approximate location 51°05' N, 043°31' W, the flight crew received a CARGO FIRE FWD EICAS message. The emergency checklist was executed, and a MAYDAY was declared. The flight crew descended off the North Atlantic Tracks (NAT), and offset their route for a diversion to St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL. The cargo hold fire extinguishing bottles were discharged, however the fire warning persisted. The aircraft landed in CYYT and was met by ARFF. No heat or smoke was detected by emergency services, and the aircraft was cleared to taxi to the gate.Maintenance personnel subsequently inspected the aircraft and found no evidence of heat or fire. The fire warning system detector was considered faulty, and was replaced. The fire extinguishers were also replaced.

C-FOTM, a privately registered, ski-equipped Cessna 170A aircraft, was beginning its takeoff on Brownell Lake, SK with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the takeoff roll, the aircraft struck a snow bank, and tore out the right main landing gear. The aircraft came to an abrupt stop, and the pilot and passenger evacuated the aircraft without injury. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the landing gear, horizontal stabilizer, propeller and engine cowling.

C-FFPH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG746 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Nassau/Lynden Pindling Intl (MYNN), Bahamas with 6 crew members and 180 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL360, approximately 395 nm north of MYNN, the flight crew reported a near miss with a weather balloon. The event was reported to ATC, and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FACJ, a privately registered Cirrus SR20 aircraft, was rented by a commercially licensed pilot for the purpose of building flight time. As the pilot had limited experience on this aircraft type, in addition to no recent flying, the pilot hired an instructor to provide some training. The instructor was a Class 1 instructor, and a Transport Canada accredited Pilot Examiner.On 12 March 2019 at 1342 Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), the aircraft departed from Runway 33 at Toronto/Buttonville Municipal (CYKZ), ON, with the commercial pilot and the instructor on board, with the intention to conduct some circuits at CYKZ. The wind was light and variable, so the aircraft joined the left downwind leg of the circuit for Runway 33, and planned for a touch-and-go.At 1348 EDT on the initial touchdown, the aircraft bounced and full power was added to commence the takeoff portion of the touch-and-go. The nose of the aircraft was raised, the aircraft became briefly airborne, before returning to the surface abruptly. The nose was raised again, and the tail of the aircraft struck the runway as the aircraft became airborne again, albeit briefly.  As the aircraft contacted the ground the third time, the outer right flap hinge and right wheel contacted the ground outside of the runway surface laterally, approximately 1000 feet from the runway end. The nose was raised again, and the aircraft continued the take-off roll.As the aircraft left the runway surface longitudinally, still on the ground, it struck a 4 foot high fence, located 60 feet from the runway end. Past this fence, the terrain slopes down toward 16th Avenue, which crosses the departure path perpendicularly. The aircraft crossed 16th Avenue in the air, in a right bank, and dragging the right wing tip. The aircraft passed directly in front of a tow truck that was in the westbound lane, and the driver of the vehicle captured the event on dash-camera. North of 16th Avenue, the terrain rises rapidly; the aircraft collided with the ground, and came to a stop approximately 250 feet passed the end of Runway 33. The two occupants were wearing 4-point safety belts and received no significant injuries. The aircraft received significant damage to the wings, nose, tail, landing gear, and propeller.The aircraft was equipped with an Avidyne FlightMax Entegra flight display that recorded engine and GPS data. The unit recorded one data point every 6 seconds. This data was acquired and analyzed by the TSB following the accident. It was noticed that, following the initial touchdown on Runway 33, the engine RPM and manifold pressure increased to full, followed by a significant reduction, and then a return to full. During the touch-and-go attempt, the recorded ground speed steadily decreased from 61 kts at the initial touchdown point, to 52 kts shortly before impact.

C-GKEJ, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7333 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Nashville Intl (KBNA), TN with 3 crew members and 48 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew reported a nose landing gear issue, and requested to level off in order to accomplish the associated checklist items. Subsequently, the flight crew declared an emergency, and requested a return to CYYZ. The aircraft landed on Runway 23 with ARFF standing by, and taxied to the gate without incident. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft.

C-GAUA, a privately operated Robinson R66 helicopter, was conducting a cross country flight from Nashville/John C Tune (KJWN), TN to Fauquier, ON. The helicopter landed at several airports along the route, the last being Sudbury (CYSB), ON, after which it departed for a night VFR flight to its final destination. The helicopter was reported overdue, and an extensive search was conducted; the wreckage was located on 11 March 2019, approximately 18 nautical miles west northwest of Timmins (Victor M. Power) (CYTS), ON. The two occupants were fatally injured. The TSB deployed 3 investigators to the accident site.

C-FYHT, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Yellowhead Helicopters, was conducting heli-skiing operations approximately 13 nm north north-east of Blue River (CYCP), BC with 1 pilot and 11 passengers on board. After refueling the helicopter at a remote fuel cache, approximately 10 nm north of CYCP, the pilot returned to pick up the 9 skiers and 2 guides. Shortly after take off, the pilot encountered whiteout conditions caused by the low density snow disturbed by the rotor downwash. Control of the aircraft was lost, the helicopter impacted terrain, rolled to the left, and came to rest inverted in deep snow. The ELT activated. The passengers and a guide egressed the helicopter utilizing the interior roof mounted ladder system and the right side push-out window. The pilot and the other guide exited the helicopter through the right side pilot door. One of the guides contacted the operator’s dispatcher, who initiated the emergency response plan. A company helicopter was sent to the accident site, and all occupants were transported to the Albreda ski lodge. There were no injuries, however the helicopter sustained substantial damage. There was no post impact fire.UPDATE 22 March 2019: The operator reported that 4 passengers and one of the guides received minor injuries.

C-FJWE, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3368 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Saskatoon/John G Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK with 4 crew members and 67 passengers on board. During the approach into CYXE, the flight crew requested an ambulance to meet the aircraft due to a medical emergency involving a flight attendant. The aircraft landed without further incident, and Emergency Medical Services (EMS) offloaded the cabin crew member prior to deplaning the passengers.

C-GJAZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 CRJ900 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8014 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to St. John's Intl (CYYT), NL with 4 crew members and 39 passengers on board. As the aircraft descended below 3000 feet on the approach to CYYT, severe turbulence was encountered which produced large variations in speed and altitude. The flight crew elected to carry out a missed approach, and divert to the alternate airport (CYUL). There were no reported injuries.The operator’s maintenance reviewed the flight data from the FDR, and determined that the turbulence did not cause the aircraft to exceed the manufacturer’s limitations. No further inspection was required, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJRH, a Piper PA-31-350 aircraft operated by SkyCare Air Ambulance, was conducting a flight from Red Lake (CYRL), ON for Wunnumin Lake (CKL3), ON with 2 pilots and 5 passengers on board. Approximately 5 nautical miles north east of CYRL after the departure, the flight crew noticed a significant oil leak from the right engine (Avco Lycoming TIO-540-J2BD). The flight crew also noticed a drop in oil pressure for the same engine, and elected to conduct a precautionary engine shutdown, with a return to CYRL. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYRL. The operator's maintenance replaced the engine.

C-GKVU, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG689 from Varadero/Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl (MUVR), Cuba to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 6 crew members and 188 passengers on board. As the flight crew was taxiing for the takeoff at MUVR, ATC cleared SWG689 to LINE UP on Runway 06. Approaching the hold short line for Runway 06, the flight crew was given a revised clearance to HOLD SHORT. The flight crew reacted, however the aircraft came to a stop approximately 10 feet past the hold short line. The control tower was notified of their position, and the tower proceeded to clear another aircraft to land on Runway 06. After the other aircraft landed, SWG689 continued to CYUL with no further incident.

C-FGWJ, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1501 from Las Vegas/McCarran Intl (KLAS), NV to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 5 crew members and 134 passengers on board. During the boarding at KLAS, the cabin crew observed smoke in the cabin, and proceeded with a rapid deplanement of the aircraft. There were no injuries in the process. The operator’s maintenance found that the right Air Conditioning Pack was the source of the problem. The aircraft was released under Minimum Equipment List (MEL) provision for the flight to CYYC.

C-FSOI, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1046 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Palm Springs Intl (KPSP), CA with 6 crew members and 165 passengers on board. During the final stages of the descent into KPSP, ATC cleared ACA1046 to descend from 7000 feet to 6000 feet. However, there was a VFR traffic at 6000 feet flying in the vicinity, and the flight crew received a TCAS RA to CLIMB. The aircraft climbed back to 7000 feet, then continued once the message cleared. After 2 missed approaches due to high winds and turbulence, the flight diverted to Ontario Intl (KONT), CA.

C-FZUR, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG122 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Punta Cana Intl (MDPC), Dominican Republic with 6 crew members and 175 passengers on board. During cruise flight, a flight crew member started to feel sick, requiring repeated absences from the cockpit. Subsequently, the affected flight crew member was able to resume flying duties. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GGBC, a Dassault Falcon 900EX aircraft operated by NovaJet, was conducting flight 58343 from Saint John (CYSJ), NB to Teterboro (KTEB), NJ with 2 crew members and 6 passengers on board. During cruise flight approximately 30 minutes after takeoff, the flight crew observed a number 1 engine low oil pressure indication, associated Master Caution light illumination, and subsequent Master Warning indication. The flight crew carried out checklist requirements, including the precautionary shut down of the number 1 engine. A return to CYSJ was requested, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and the aircraft landed at CYSJ without further incident.Maintenance personnel replaced the faulty number 1 engine oil filler cap o-ring, and returned the aircraft to service following cleaning, servicing and function tests.

C-FCAE, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA888 from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON to London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK with 8 crew members and 174 passengers on board. After the landing at EGLL, smoke was observed by the control tower coming from the landing gear area, and ARFF was sent out as a precaution. No emergency was declared, and the aircraft taxied to the gate without further incident. The smoke was caused by hydraulic fluid leaking on the left main landing gear. The number 1 brake flex line was removed, and the aircraft was released under Minimum Equipment List (MEL) provisions.

N782CK, a Boeing 747-400 cargo aircraft operated by Kalitta Air, was conducting flight CKS962 from Chicago/O’Hare Intl (KORD), IL to Greater Moncton Romeo LeBlanc Intl (CYQM), NB with 7 crew members on board. After the landing on Runway 24 at CYQM, the aircraft taxied onto Taxiway Echo to the apron. As the aircraft entered the apron, the flight crew deviated off the taxi lane during the left turn onto the apron. The number one engine then contacted a snow bank, which caused damage to the engine. There were no injuries and no impact to airport operations. The subsequent flight was cancelled. Maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft, and the operator elected to ferry the aircraft on 3 engines the following day.

C-FMXC, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1713 from Punta Cana Intl (MDPC), Dominican Republic to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 8 crew members and 277 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from MDPC at FL320, a cabin crew member received a minor injury, and was deemed unfit for the remainder of the flight. Duties were distributed to the remaining cabin crew members, and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GTQG, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC942 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL with 6 crew members and 189 passengers on board. During cruise flight approximately 45 nm north northwest of Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ, the flight crew received an AFT CARGO FIRE WARNING indication. The Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) was executed and, in the process, the indication went away for a few seconds, then returned and stayed on permanently. The flight crew discharged the halon in the associated cargo compartment, and declared a MAYDAY. A diversion to KEWR was requested, and the aircraft landed and stopped on Runway 04R. The control tower confirmed that no smoke was visible, however when the fire crew opened the cargo door, smoke was visible, and an electrical odour was detected. All aboard were then evacuated via emergency slides.The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and removed all panels in the cargo area; no evidence of smoke or fire was found. Additionally, all bags were inspected, and no signs of smoke or fire could be found as well. Maintenance personnel also identified that the Cargo Smoke Detector Unit was defective. It is believed that the smoke and electrical smell detected by the fire crew was caused by the halon that was discharged in the cargo compartment during the diversion to KEWR. The aircraft was returned to service once all the required parts were replaced.

C-FWSX, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA2653 from St. Maarten/Princess Juliana Intl (TNCM), Sint Maarten to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 5 crew members and 74 passengers on board. During the final approach on Runway 24L at CYYZ, the flight crew observed a flap asymmetry warning while deploying the flaps. A missed approach was executed, and the flight crew performed the associated checklist items. An emergency was declared, and an uneventful flapless landing was carried out on Runway 23. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft.The operator’ maintenance replaced a skew sensor on the left trailing edge flap support, at the number 1 position. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-GNYZ, a Sikorsky S-92A aircraft operated by Canadian Helicopters Offshore, was conducting flight CDN3 between the Thebaud and Alma gas field platforms, west of Sable Island, NS with 2 pilots and 13 passengers on board. During cruise flight, an INPUT #2 CHIP caution light illuminated. The flight crew followed the emergency checklist, declared a PAN PAN, and diverted to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS where a landing was conducted without further incident.Maintenance personnel inspected the associated number 2 input gearbox chip detector, and metal particles were found. After laboratory analysis of the metal particles and consultation with Sikorsky Aircraft Engineering group, replacement of both number 1 and number 2 input gearboxes, as well as the replacement of the main gearbox, was carried out.

C-GPWG, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA573 from Los Angeles Intl (KLAX), CA to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 5 crew members and 131 passengers on board. During the climb out from KLAX, the flight crew received the ECAM message HYD Y RSVR LO LVL. ECAM actions were completed and, in consultation with the operator’s maintenance and operational control centres, the decision was made to continue to CYVR. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN with Vancouver ATC during the descent, and the aircraft was met by ARFF after landing. The aircraft was then towed to the gate.

C-GLRN, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG575 from Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC to Los Cabos Intl (MMSD), México with 6 crew members and 79 passengers on board. Approximately 3 nm on final for Runway 16 at MMSD, ATC cleared SWG575 to land. As the aircraft approached the runway on short final, the flight crew observed a small corporate jet on the threshold of Runway 16, and executed a missed approach. ATC was notified that there was a traffic on the runway, and the aircraft returned to land without further incident. The incident has been captured in the operator’s SMS.

C-FDCH, a Sikorsy S-61N aircraft operated by Canadian Helicopters, was conducting a flight in the Middle East (location undisclosed) with 3 crew members and 6 passengers on board. As the helicopter was in a 10 foot hover shortly after iftoff, the PNF called torque split; simultaneously, a loud roaring sound was heard, the aircraft started to settle as the NR dropped, and the PF landed the aircraft back as the hoist operator gave height calls. The aircraft landed softly on the ground without further incident. The PNF pulled the throttles off while the PF called for engine cut off due to a temperature exceedance of 860°C on the number 1 engine. The passengers were escorted off the aircraft as soon as the rotor blades stopped.  The operator suspects that the number 1 engine ingested a Foreign Object (FOD).

C-FYLD, a Gulfstream G100 aircraft operated by Latitude Air Ambulance, was conducting a Medevac flight from Dubai Intl (OMDB), UAE to Dubrovnik (LDDU), Croatia with 4 crew members and 1 passenger on board. Late into the approach to their fuel stop of LDDU at 2500 feet, the flight crew realized that they had misinterpreted the wind direction, and that the crosswind was exceeding their limitations. The approach was immediately discontinued, and the flight crew determined that their planned alternate airport was also exceeding their crosswind limitations. After a quick assessment, Split/Kastel (LDSP), Croatia was selected with an into wind runway, and the flight crew climbed to FL150. Approximately 50 nm south east of LDSP, the flight crew declared a fuel emergency as the quantity indicated 400 lbs (30 mns). The aircraft landed at LDSP without further incident.

C-GKVL, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG706 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Aruba/Reina Beatrix Intl (TNCA), Aruba with 6 crew members and 107 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure behind an Airbus 320 off Runway 23 at CYYZ, with a visual separation of approximately 2-3 miles, the aircraft encountered wake turbulence through 2000 feet ASL. An uncommanded roll to the right was halted with full aileron deflection, but only enough to maintain a bank angle of approximately 25° that lasted approximately 4 seconds. 6 seconds after returning to wings level, a second event of uncommanded roll took place, this time to the left; however this roll was controllable with aileron input and lasted approximately 2 seconds. The flight continued to TNCA without further incident.

C-GPVS, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG158 from Fredericton Intl (CYFC), NB to Cayo Coco/Jardines del Rey Intl (MUCC), Cuba with 6 crew members and 181 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL360, approximately 250 nm north of MUCC, one of the flight crew members began to feel unwell after consuming a meal. Within the next 10 minutes, the flight crew member started to feel ok and was able to resume duties of Pilot Monitoring (PM). The aircraft landed at MUCC without further incident. In case of a re-occurrence during the return portion (SWG159) from MUCC to CYFC, it was decided that the affected flight crew member would carry out the same duties (PM). The affected flight crew member felt unwell again for a brief period during the return flight, which resulted in a state of fatigue. Controlled rest was used, in conjunction with careful hydration. Prior to the arrival at CYFC, the affected flight crew member assumed PM duties, and the flight landed without further incident.

C-FJDQ, un appareil de type Beech B100 exploité par Max Aviation, effectuait le vol MAX100 selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré (CYRC), QC à destination d’Amos/Magny (CYEY), QC avec 2 pilotes à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en rapprochement pour CYEY, l’équipage a constaté que la pression d’huile du moteur gauche (Garrett TPE331-6-252B) était en baisse. La décision de fermer ce moteur par mesure de précaution a été prise alors que la pression d’huile continuait de baisser. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 32. L’appareil a été remorqué jusqu’à un hangar où une fuite d’huile importante a été constatée.

C-GAWS, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1876 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Kahului (PHOG), HI with 6 crew members and 150 passengers on board. Approximately 45 minutes after the departure from CYVR, the flight crew received an R1 WINDOW OVERHEAT message. An emergency was declared, and the flight crew returned to CYVR. In order to reduce the landing weight, the flight crew elected to hold for approximately 70 minutes prior to the landing.The operator's maintenance replaced the R1 window, which sustained minor damage.

C-GYZV, a privately registered Murphy Rebel amateur built aircraft, was conducting circuits on Runway 12 at McBride/Charlie Leake Field (CAV4), BC with only the pilot on board. During the first landing, the aircraft bounced twice. The pilot attempted to abort the landing and, as full power was applied, the aircraft veered to the right and contacted a snow bank to the right of the runway surface. The aircraft ground looped, and came to rest upright approximately 20 feet off the runway surface. The pilot was not injured, and was able to vacate the aircraft without assistance. There was no post impact fire. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FAFV, a Cessna 208B aircraft operated by Amik Aviation, was conducting a VFR flight from Winnipeg/St. Andrews (CYAV), MB to Little Grand Rapids (CZGR), MB with 1 pilot and 6 passengers on board. During the final approach for Runway 36 at CZGR, the aircraft collided with the frozen surface of Family Lake, approximately 0.75 nautical mile south of the threshold of Runway 36. The pilot and passengers egressed the aircraft, and were transported to the Little Grand Rapids nursing station for evaluation. The pilot suffered minor injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FTCA a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA614 from Toronto/Lester B. Person Intl (CYYZ), ON to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS with 8 crew members and 211 passengers on board. During the landing rollout on Runway 23, the aircraft encountered a slippery area on the runway and was pushed by the wind, causing it to turn approximately 45° to the right. The nose wheel entered a snow ridge on the edge of the runway, which caused the rear of the aircraft to slide approximately 180°, coming to a stop facing in the opposing direction of travel. Due to the weather conditions, the surface of the runway experienced a flash freeze from a wet condition, and became extremely slippery as ice formed quickly. Passengers were taken to the terminal by bus, and the aircraft was towed to the apron. There was no damage to the aircraft, and no injuries reported by the passengers or crew.

C-GPWS, a Boeing 737-600 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1207 from New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 5 crew members and 113 passengers on board. During the descent into CYYZ, the flight crew received an AIRSPEED DISAGREE message on the Primary Flight Display (PFD). The non-normal checklist associated with this indication was executed, and the flight crew declared an emergency. The flight was given priority handling, and emergency vehicles were standing by for the landing. There were no injuries, and no damage to the aircraft.The operator’s maintenance replaced the left and right pitot systems, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWFE, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3324 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Kelowna (CYLW), BC with 4 crew members and 78 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew received a FUSELAGE DOOR warning light. The flight crew actioned the QRH, and continued to CYLW. The pressurization remained normal, until the aircraft descended through 5000 feet, and subsequently depressurized. The flight crew declared an emergency and continued to land on Runway 34 without further incident. ARFF inspected the aircraft after the landing, and then the flight crew taxied to the gate. The aft cargo door handle was found to be in the extended position.

C-FZQS, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA386 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 5 crew members and 90 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL370, the flight crew declared a MAYDAY due to a disruptive passenger, requesting an immediate diversion to Val D’Or (CYVO), QC, as well as police for the arrival. ACA386 landed at CYVO without further incident, and police met the aircraft.

C-GEOU, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1811 from Cancun Intl (MMUN), México to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 8 crew members and 279 passengers on board. During the descent into CYYZ, the flight crew noticed that the Center Hydraulic System fluid and pressure was observed to be lost. The flight crew completed the QRH, and briefed the cabin crew. Upon entering the Toronto FIR (CZYZ), the flight crew declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed on Runway 33R with ARFF standing by. Due to the loss of hydraulic, the aircraft needed to be towed to the gate.

N118MT, a Bombardier CL-600-2B16 Challenger 601 aircraft operated by One World Aviation 118 LLC, aborted its takeoff on Runway 06L due to smoke in the cockpit. The aircraft exited at the end of the runway, and taxied back to the FBO without further incident. ATC asked the flight crew if emergency services were required, and the crew declined.

C-FLEJ, a Boeing 737-400 aircraft operated by Flair Airlines, was conducting flight FLE138 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with 6 crew members and 106 passengers on board. As the aircraft reached the top of climb after the departure from CYYC, a smell of acrid electrical smoke was detected in the cabin; however, there were no visible signs of smoke or fire. The flight crew was informed of the issue as the smell was increasing in intensity, predominantly near the centre of the cabin. As a precaution, the flight crew requested a return to CYYC, and declared a PAN PAN. The Smoke or Fumes QRH checklist was executed, and subsequently, the cabin crew informed that fumes were dissipating. The aircraft landed without further incident, and taxied off the runway to have ARFF perform an inspection before proceeding to a gate. The aircraft was then cleared to proceed, and passengers deplaned normally as fumes were no longer present. The operator’s maintenance removed the left hand recirculation fan and its associated components for examination.

C-GKTA, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8273, from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Nanaimo (CYCD), BC with 3 crew members and 40 passengers on board. Less than 30 mns after the departure from CYYC at FL240, the aircraft slowly started to lose pressurization. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, initiated a slow descent to FL140 due to terrain clearance, and requested to return to CYYC where the aircraft landed without further incident. The passengers were notified of the situation, and Emergency Medical Services (EMS) was requested after the landing for those who needed to be checked. 1 passenger was taken to hospital with minor issues.

C-GSWJ, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA192 from Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB with 5 crew members and 32 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL390 in the vicinity of Kamloops (CYKA), BC, one of the flight crew members became incapacitated and was unable to perform flying duties. A cabin crew member assisted the pilot to the rear of the aircraft, while MedLink was consulted. The flight continued to CYEG where it landed without further incident. The aircraft was met at the gate by Emergency Medical Services (EMS). The pilot was assessed, and released shortly thereafter.

C-GXAX, a Boeing 737-8 MAX aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1118 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Las Vegas/McCarran Intl (KLAS), NV with 6 crew members and 160 passengers on board. During cruise flight, a cabin crew member sustained a medical incident and was unable to continue duties. Duties were distributed to the remaining cabin crew members for the landing.

C-GWBX, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA476 from Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 5 crew members and 100 passengers on board. During the descent into CYYZ, the flight crew observed a flap asymmetry indication. The associated checklist was executed, and the flight crew contacted the operator’s maintenance. A PAN PAN was declared, and a successful flapless landing was made on Runway 05. The aircraft taxied to the gate on its own power.The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and rectified the problem.

N1127M, a Learjet 60 aircraft operated by Worldwide Jets, was conducting flight WWI28 from Teterboro (KTEB), NJ to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. N903XJ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 CRJ900 aircraft operated by Endeavor Air, was conducting flight EDV5508 from CYYZ to Detroit Metropolitan/Wayne County (KDTW), MI. ATC cleared WWI28 to descend to 8000 feet during the downwind leg of the LINNG9 arrival (landing east). The flight crew read the clearance back correctly, however the aircraft was observed on radar descending through 7500 feet. This resulted in a loss of separation between WWI28 and EDV5508, which was level at 7000 feet after its departure on the ANCOL3 Standard Instrument Departure (SID). The separation was reduced to 1.1 nm laterally and 500 feet vertically, in an area where 3 nm or 1000 feet is required.

C-FMWP, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1944 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Bogotá/El Nuevo Dorado Intl (SKBO), Colombia with 8 crew members and 248 passengers on board. During the takeoff roll on Runway 06L at CYYZ, the flight crew heard an abnormal noise, and noted a slight adverse yaw. Since the aircraft had reached Vr, the takeoff was continued. Once at cruising altitude, the flight crew requested that Runway 06L be inspected, as they suspected that they had a tire failure; however, no debris were found following the runway inspection. The absence of evidence on the runway led the flight crew to believe that they had experienced a compressor stall on one of the engines during the takeoff. Therefore, a return to CYYZ was requested approximately 40 minutes after takeoff, and a PAN PAN was declared as a precaution. An overweight landing was completed without incident with ARFF in attendance and, after an inspection, the aircraft was cleared to taxi to the gate.  The operator’s maintenance performed a borescope inspection on the number 1 engine, and no faults were found. However, a BITE test revealed a fault with fan bleed 2.5. The 2.5 bleed valve actuator was replaced, although it could not be determined if it caused the event. It is also suspected that something was ingested by the engine.

C-GIPM, an Aero Commander 690A aircraft operated by Air Spray (1967), was conducting an IFR flight from Casper/Natrona County Intl (KCPR), WY to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with one pilot on board. During cruise flight at FL220 south of Lethbridge (CYQL), AB, the pilot noticed a loss of oil pressure for the number 1 engine (Honeywell TPE-331-5-251). As the oil pressure continued to drop, the pilot elected to shut down and feather the engine. An emergency was declared, and the pilot diverted to CYQL where a single-engine approach and landing was performed without further incident.

C-GNLW, a Boeing 737-200 aircraft operated by Nolinor Aviation, was conducting flight NRL791 from Iqaluit (CYFB), NU to Montreal Intl (Mirabel) (CYMX), QC with 7 crew members and 98 passengers on board. After a normal flap retraction shortly after the departure from CYFB, the flight crew noticed a FLAP DISAGREE indication approaching 10 000 feet. The flight crew contacted ATC, and levelled the aircraft off at 14 000 feet, while reducing the speed to 210 kts. The corresponding checklist was executed, and the flight crew elected to return to CYFB. The aircraft circled in order to burn the excess fuel prior to landing in a flapless configuration, and ARFF was called out as a precaution. After the landing, the aircraft stopped on the runway and was inspected. Subsequently, the aircraft continued to the gate without any further issue. There were no injuries.The operator's maintenance found that the flap asymmetry problem was associated with a Data Acquisition Unit (DAU) within the flap indicator. The DAU induced a short to the flap position indicator wire, from the left flap position transmitter. This caused a flap asymmetry indication.

C-GTQC, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC358 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Orlando Intl (KMCO), FL with 6 crew members and 138 passengers on board. Climbing through 400-500 feet on the initial climb after the departure, the flight crew heard a series of bangs, associated with vibrations felt through the floor. After a brief pause, a second series of bangs were heard, which were consistent with compressor stalls. The flight crew retarded the thrust lever on the number 1 engine (CFM56-7B26), which stopped the bangs and the vibrations. The climb was stopped at 3000 feet, and a PAN PAN was declared. The flight crew executed the checklist, and requested a return back to CYHZ where the aircraft landed without further incident, with the number 1 engine power at idle. The operator’s maintenance could not find any fault with the engine. The engine was replaced, and will be sent to an engine shop for maintenance.

C-GOPP, a float equipped de Havilland DHC-3T aircraft operated by Harbour Air, was conducting sightseeing flight HES305 from Vancouver Harbour (CYHC), BC with 1 crew member and 9 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the pilot was unable to reduce the engine power setting while moving the power lever. The pilot entered an orbit over CYHC, and consulted with the operator’s maintenance. Subsequently, an emergency was declared, the engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-34) was shut down, and the pilot performed a successful power-off water landing. The aircraft was then towed to the Vancouver Harbour dock. There were no injuries. The operator's maintenance indicated a fault with the engine's fuel control unit.

C-GJCN, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Canadian North, was conducting flight MPE1550 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Primrose (CFN6), AB with 3 crew members and 23 passengers on board. During the climb through 18 000 feet ASL, the pressurization was lost. The flight crew initiated an emergency descent to 10 000 feet ASL, and requested a return to CYYC. Control of the pressurization was regained during the descent, through manual mode. The aircraft continued to CYYC where it landed without further incident.

C-GSKB, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Kenn Borek Air, was conducting flight KBA901 from Paulatuk (Nora Aliqatchialuk Ruben) (CYPC), NT, to Inuvik (Mike Zubko) (CYEV), NT with two flight crew members on board. Upon selection of landing gear down on arrival at CYEV, the flight crew observed that there was no green light for the nose landing gear. The appropriate checklist was completed, and a manual landing gear extension was performed. The flight crew declared an emergency, and landed without further incident.

C-GOSN, a Bombardier Challenger 604 aircraft operated by Flightpath Charter Airways, was conducting a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Bridgetown/Grantley Adams Intl (TBPB), Barbados with 2 crew members and 2 passengers on board. During the departure from CYYZ, the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) was being used as the bleed air source for pressurization, which can be done to improve takeoff and climb performance. During the climb at approximately 9000 feet ASL, the APU was shut down, however the engine pressurization valves were not opened manually as necessary to maintain the pressurization. As the climb continued, the aircraft depressurized slowly, until the CABIN ALTITUDE amber caution message illuminated, as the aircraft climbed through 18 000 feet. Approximately 20 seconds later, the CABIN ALTITUDE red warning illuminated, accompanied by the automatic deployment of the passenger oxygen masks. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks, requested an immediate descent, as well as a return to CYYZ. Descending below 9000 feet, the flight crew recognized that the bleed source switch was in the OFF position, and elected to continue toward CYYZ where the aircraft landed without further incident. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft reported.

C-FZRM, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA2152 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Puerto Vallarta/Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz Intl (MMPR), Mexico with 6 crew members and 128 passengers on board. Approximately 2 hour and 50 minutes into the flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue duties. The affected cabin crew member’s duties were reassigned to the remainder of the cabin crew for the rest of the flight. Upon arrival, the affected cabin crew member was transported to hospital by EMS.
