C-FDAO, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-8-100 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE846 depuis Kuujjuaq (CYVP), QC à destination de Puvirnituq (CYPX), QC avec 3 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors qu’il se trouvait à environ 200 nm au nord-ouest de CYVP, le voyant ambre #1 HYD ISO VLV s'est allumé, suivi d’une perte totale du liquide hydraulique du système numéro 1. L’équipage a effectué les procédures d’urgence appropriées, suivi de la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH), a déclaré une urgence, et a pris la décision de retourner à CYVP. L’appareil a effectué un atterrissage sans volets sur la piste 25, et l’équipage a utilisé l’inversion de poussée ainsi que le frein d’urgence afin d’immobiliser l’appareil sur la piste. L’appareil fût par la suite remorqué jusqu’au hangar.

C-FEKI, un appareil de type Embraer ERJ 170-200 exploité par Sky Regional Airlines, s’apprêtait à effectuer le vol SKV7597 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination de Chicago/O’Hare Intl (KORD), IL avec 4 membres d’équipage et 64 passagers à bord. Alors que l’appareil circulait pour le décollage à proximité de la voie de circulation Golf (G), un escalier de service mobile a été soulevé par une rafale de vent, et a percuté le moteur numéro 1 ainsi que le fuselage. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA), ainsi que le département de l’entretien de l’exploitant, ont effectué une inspection de l’appareil, suite à laquelle des dommages au moteur ont été détectés. L’appareil est retourné à la barrière afin de permettre aux passagers de débarquer. Une inspection plus approfondie a permis de déterminer que les dommages à la nacelle étaient dans les limites de tolérance du manuel de réparations structurales. Les réparations ont été effectuées, et l’appareil a été remis en service.

C-GTGA, a Beech 1900C aircraft operated by Skylink Express, was conducting flight SLQ720 from Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK with 2 crew members on board. During the final approach at CYXE, the left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-65B) torque began to fluctuate. The flight crew decided to decrease the power on the left engine, which stopped the fluctuations. The power on the right engine was increased to compensate, and the flight crew declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed without further incident. An inspection of the left engine did not reveal any anomalies. A ground run was completed, and no defects were noted. The aircraft was then returned to service.

INSP35, an airport inspection vehicle, was proceeding on Runway 23 at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON, to perform a runway inspection. INSP35 was instructed by ATC to hold short of Runway 33L, and the operator read-back the instruction correctly. As INSP35 approached the intersection of Runways 23 and 33L, ATC reminded the operator of the hold-short instruction, followed immediately by an instruction to STOP, and subsequently to BACK UP. C-FMZD, an Embraer ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA502 from Chicago/O’Hare Intl (KORD), IL to CYYZ, and was approximately 1.8 nm on final approach for Runway 33L at the time of the incursion. ACA502 landed on Runway 33L without further incident.

RED11, an Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) vehicle, was taxiing northbound on Taxiway Bravo at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON, and was instructed by ATC to cross Runway 23, then taxi via Taxiway Juliet, and hold short of Runway 15R. RED11 crossed Runway 23, turned left on Juliet, and crossed Runway 15L, on its way toward Runway 15R. At the time RED11 crossed Runway 15L, C-GRWS, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet and conducting flight WJA427 to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB, had just taken off from Runway 33R, and had not yet cross overhead the intersection of Runway 15L and Taxiway J.

C-FKSV, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA95 from Buenos Aires/Aeropuerto Internacional Ezeiza/Ministro Pistarini (SAEZ), Argentina to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 11 crew members and 267 passengers on board. Shortly after the aircraft reached its cruising altitude of FL330, the cabin crew advised the flight crew that a baby had been unconscious for a while and that doctors, travelling as passengers, were assisting. Stat MD was also contacted and, after consultation with the crew, the decision to return to SAEZ was taken. However, because of a language barrier with local ATC personnel, the flight crew had to declare a MAYDAY. The aircraft proceeded to land at SAEZ without further incident.

C-GJVW, a Fairchild SA227-DC aircraft operated by Bearskin Airlines, was conducting flight BLS345 from Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON to Kenora (CYQK), ON with 2 crew members and 4 passengers on board. During the final approach into CYQK, the flight crew selected landing gear down, however the landing gear would not extend. The flight crew decided to divert the aircraft to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB, where a successful emergency/manual landing gear extension was completed. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft landed without further incident. An inspection of the system by the operator's maintenance revealed a broken wire to the landing gear control valve.

N491RV, a Gates Learjet 35A aircraft operated by Aero Jet Aviation, was conducting a flight from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON to Fort Lauderdale Executive (KFXE), FL with 2 crew members and 3 passengers on board. Upon selection of landing gear up after the departure from CYOW, the nose landing gear light remained illuminated. The flight crew verified that the landing gear was in the down position, declared an emergency, and requested to return to CYOW after a brief 10 mns hold to burn fuel. The aircraft landed without further incident, and proceeded to the FBO. Upon exiting the aircraft, the flight crew noted that the nose wheel strut was compressed, and there were no signs of hydraulic fluid.

C-GHLV, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1658 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Tampa Intl (KTPA), FL with 8 crew members and 261 passengers on board. As the flight was preparing to begin the descent into KTPA, a cabin crew member became incapacitated due to illness. A qualified employee travelling as a passenger on the flight was assigned the duties for the landing, and the aircraft landed at KTPA without further incident.

C-FYJE, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1848 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Los Cabos Intl (MMSD), Mexico. After reaching FL260 during the climb to cruising altitude less than 20 minutes after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and advised ATC of a pressurization issue, requesting a return to CYYZ. The aircraft turned around, and landed without further incident with ARFF standing by.UPDATE 05 March 2019 from the operator:Climbing through FL250 PACK 1 OVERHEAT ECAM displayed. Flight Crew completed ECAM actions, levelled off and descent were requested from ATC. Flight returned to CYYZ and PAN PAN was declared with ATC. Overweight landing was carried out without incident.

C-GOGT, a Beech 200 King Air aircraft operated by Missinippi Airways, was conducting flight MA03 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Norway House (CYNE), MB with 2 crew members and 1 passenger on board. While climbing through 11 500 feet after the departure from CYTH, the left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-41) chip detector light illuminated. The flight crew elected to perform a precautionary shutdown of the engine, declared an emergency, and returned to CYTH where the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator will advise of their findings.

OO-SRO, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by TUI Airlines Belgium on behalf of Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG425 from Punta Cana Intl (MDPC), Dominican Republic to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON with 6 crew members and 177 passengers on board. Just prior to the top of descent into CYOW, the Hydraulic System B failed. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN when in range to the airport, and the aircraft landed without further incident on Runway 07.The operator’s maintenance replaced a hydraulic pump, and the aircraft was returned to service.

OO-SRO, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by TUI Airlines on behalf of Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG325 from Varadero/Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl (MUVR), Cuba to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON with 6 crew members and 190 passengers on board. Passing 15 000 feet shortly after the departure from MUVR, the flight crew received a Master Caution, with simultaneous ENG 2 Hydraulic System B low pressure light. The non normal checklist was executed, and the flight crew elected to continue the flight. During the descent to CYOW, the low pressure ELEC 1 on Hydraulic System B illuminated, along with the FLT Control B low pressure light. The associated system reading indicated zero. The flight crew ran the checklist again, declared a PAN PAN, and the aircraft landed without further incident with the flaps at position 15. The aircraft taxied to the gate normally.

C-FOST, a Beech B300 Super King Air aircraft operated by Chartright Air, was conducting an IFR flight from Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON to Toronto/Buttonville Muni (CYKZ), ON. Approaching CYKZ, the flight crew of C-FOST conducted the RNAV approach to Runway 33. Shortly after passing waypoint SINRU (2.6 miles from the threshold of Runway 33), the flight crew observed a high-wing aircraft on a tight base leg for their intended landing runway. The flight crew initiated a go-around, and entered a right hand circuit for Runway 33 in VFR Meteorological Conditions (VMC). As the aircraft turned to line up with Runway 33 on final approach, the flight crew observed the same high-wing aircraft departing on Runway 15, flying towards them briefly before making a right turn. C-FOST subsequently landed without further incident.

C-GNLW, a Boeing 737-200 aircraft operated by Nolinor Aviation, was conducting flight NRL791 under instrument flight rules from Mary River (CMR2), NU to Iqaluit (CYFB), NU with 7 crew members and 84 passengers on board. After the cabin crew had deployed the aft airstair following the arrival at CYFB, smoke started to appear in the cabin. The cabin crew discharged a fire extinguisher at the aft airstair mechanism, however dark smoke continued to enter the cabin. A rapid deplanement of the passengers was conducted, and the flight crew requested emergency services. The crew and passengers were then directed to the FBO. There were no injuries.The smoke ceased after the airstair's internal control toggle switch was positioned back to the OFF position. A maintenance investigation revealed that the aft airstair's internal control toggle switch was stuck in the EXTEND position, causing the AC motor to be continuously energized after the door was fully opened. The AC motor overheated, producing smoke in the rear cabin. The internal control toggle switch is normally spring loaded to the OFF position.

C-GZNS, a Mitsubishi MU-2B-60 aircraft operated by Thunder Airlines, was conducting flight THU860 from Kenora (CYQK), ON to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON with 2 crew members and 2 passengers on board. During the landing roll on Runway 07 at CYQT, the aircraft collided with a snow drift, and directional control of the aircraft was lost. The aircraft veered to the right, then to the left, however remained on the runway. There were no injuries, and the aircraft sustained minor damage to the landing gear fairings and doors.

C-GHLM, un appareil de type Airbus 330-300 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA878 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON à destination de Zürich-Kloten (LSZH), Suisse avec 10 membres d'équipage et 215 passagers à bord. Peu de temps après le départ de CYYZ, l'équipage a reçu plusieurs messages d'alerte. L'équipage a alors demandé un déroutement vers Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC, ainsi que la présence des véhicules d'urgence dans l'intention d'effectuer un atterrissage en surpoids. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre, et la masse à l'atterrissage s'est avérée être à l'intérieur des limites prescrites. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.Divers composants ont été diagnostiqués fautifs, et ont été remplacés (HP Bleed Valve #1, GPWC, FMGEC #1 et FCC #1).

C-GSKK, an Aerospatiale AS350 B3 aircraft operated by Selkirk Mountain Helicopters, was en route to Banana Hammock, BC, a ridge above the North Bowl ski area at Revelstoke Mountain Resort, BC, to pick up an injured skier. During the approach, the helicopter's main rotor struck and severed the Discipline Explosive Tramway cable, which was suspended across the North Bowl. The unmarked cable has been in place for approximately 5 years. The pilot was advised by radio that the main rotor blades had struck the cable. The pilot continued the approach, landed, and shut down. Inspection of the helicopter showed a small abraded area on the leading edge of one main rotor blade, approximately 12 inches inboard of the tip. The injured skier and a ski patroller boarded the helicopter and were flown to the Revelstoke (CYRV), BC. The patient was transferred to BC Ambulance Service, and the helicopter returned to Selkirk Mountain Helicopter's base in Revelstoke.

C-FKCO, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA567 from San Francisco Intl (KSFO), CA to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 5 crew members and 146 passengers on board. After engine start at KSFO, the flight crew received a NOSE WHEEL STEERING FAULT, and successfully performed a reset. However, shortly after take-off the fault re-occurred. The flight continued to CYVR, and the flight crew declared a PAN PAN on arrival. The landing was uneventful, and the aircraft was towed to the gate.The operator’s maintenance replaced the nose wheel steering servo control valve assembly, and performed functional checks. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FNWC, a privately registered Cessna 441 Conquest aircraft operated by The North West Company, was conducting a local training flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. Approximately 8 nm on final to the runway, the flight crew noticed that the right engine oil pressure was low. ATC was notified, an emergency was declared, and the right engine (Garrett TPE331-10N-515S) was shut down. The aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF on standby, and subsequently taxied to the apron.  The operator's maintenance has removed the right engine for further investigation.

C-GEOU, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1852 from Las Vegas/McCarran Intl (KLAS), NV to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 8 crew members and 282 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL350 approximately 90 nm NNW of Amarillo/Rick Husband Intl (KAMA), TX, the cabin crew reported smoke coming out of a coffee maker in the forward galley. A cabin crew member discharged a fire extinguisher in the affected area, and notified the flight crew. The QRH was executed, and after evaluating the situation, the decision to continue to destination was taken. The aircraft landed at CYYZ without further incident.An entry was made in the log book, and the event was captured in the air operator’s Safety Management System (SMS).

C-GUBD, an Airbus 330-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC560 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Cancun Intl (MMUN), Mexico with 11 crew members and 334 passengers on board. Approximately 90 minutes into the flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was unable to continue duties. The affected cabin crew member’s duties were reassigned to the remainder of the cabin crew for the rest of the flight.

C-FBEB, a privately registered Aviat Christen Husky A-1B aircraft, was conducting circuits on Runway 08R at Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC with only the pilot on board. During one of the landings, the left main wheel of the aircraft touched down, however the aircraft was not in line with the runway centerline. The pilot attempted to abort the landing and, as full power was being applied, the aircraft veered to the right and contacted snow to the right of the runway surface. The aircraft came to rest upside down, approximately 40 to 50 feet to the right of the runway surface. The pilot was not injured, and was able to vacate the aircraft without assistance. There was no post impact fire. The weather conditions at the time of the accident were a ceiling of 3000 feet, a visibility of 15 sm, and light winds from the east.

C-FJES, a Cessna 172R aircraft operated by Island Air Flight School & Charters, was conducting a local flight from Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON with only the student pilot on board. During the landing roll on Runway 08, the aircraft exited the left side of the runway, collided with a snow bank, and flipped over. The pilot was not injured; however the aircraft sustained substantial damage to the right main landing gear, the right wing, the propeller, and the tail. Runway 08/26 was closed until the aircraft was cleared from the runway area. Commercial flights were diverted during this time.

C-GVEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3111 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Kamloops (CYKA), BC with 4 crew members and 67 passengers on board. During the climb through 10 000 feet ASL after the departure from CYYC, the flight crew observed that the cabin was not pressurizing. The QRH was actioned, a PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft returned to CYYC where it landed without further incident.

C-GVEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3194 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 4 crew members and 45 passengers on board. Upon landing gear retraction shortly after the departure from CYZF, the left main landing gear doors remained open. The flight crew executed the QRH, and elected to continue to CYYC at a reduced airspeed of 185 knots. During the approach at CYYC, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced the left main landing gear door solenoid.

C-GLQZ, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par Porter Airlines, effectuait le vol POE471 en provenance de Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. Lors de la descente vers CYUL, l’ATC a assigné POE471 à un circuit d’attente au point de cheminement ARVIE, au niveau de vol FL200. C-GENM, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par WestJet Encore, effectuait le vol WEN3526 depuis Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON vers CYUL, et était également dans un circuit d’attente au point ARVIE, au niveau de vol FL210. Lorsque POE471 a été autorisé à quitter le circuit d’attente, ce dernier a été observé au niveau de vol FL203, ce qui a occasionné une perte d’espacement avec WEN3526. L'espacement a été réduit à 700 pieds sur le plan vertical et 3.3 nm sur le plan latéral, alors que la norme était de 1000 pieds ou 5 nm.

C-FDAO, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-8-100 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE846 depuis Kuujjuaq (CYVP), QC vers Puvirnituq (CYPX), QC avec 3 membres d'équipage et 3 passagers à bord. Alors qu’il se trouvait à environ 230 nm au nord-ouest de CYVP, le voyant ambre #2 HYD ISO VLV s'est allumé, suivi d’une perte totale du liquide hydraulique du système numéro 2. L'équipage de conduite a effectué la liste de vérification applicable, et une urgence a été déclarée. AIE846 est revenu se poser sans encombre à CYVP, après avoir descendu le train d'atterrissage manuellement. Personne n’a été blessé.

C-GJWE, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3307 from Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 4 crew members and 71 passengers on board. As boarding was almost completed at CYXJ, a baggage tug struck the fuselage, just aft of the cargo door. The corner of the tug caused a 6 x 26 cm hole in the outer skin of the aircraft. Passengers were deplaned, and a replacement aircraft was requested.The damaged aircraft was positioned to CYYC in a non-pressurized configuration, and the damage skin panels were repaired. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-GNAK, a Beech B200 King Air aircraft operated by Northern Air Charter (P.R.), was conducting a flight from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Peace River (CYPE), AB with 2 pilots and 7 passengers on board. As the aircraft was taxiing on Taxiway B at CYEG, passengers alerted the flight crew that there was smoke coming from the ceiling panel. The captain stopped the aircraft, and turned off the master switch. A passenger discharged a fire extinguisher on the smoking area, and the smoke stopped. Once the smoke cleared, the radiant heat switch was turned off, and the master switch was turned back on. There was no more smoke. The flight crew taxied the aircraft back to its point of departure, and shut down. The flight crew and passengers disembarked with no further incident.The operator’s maintenance removed the ceiling panels and determined the cause to be the radiant heat unit. The aircraft was further inspected, and no other damage was found. The radiant heat system was disabled, and the headliner panel was cleaned. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FMWV, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1999 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 8 crew members and 165 passengers on board. The flight had been dispatched under Minimum Equipment List (MEL) provisions for an inoperative right hand generator. During cruise flight, the left hand generator indications began to fluctuate. The flight crew consulted the QRH, and elected to declare a PAN PAN as a precaution during the descent to CYYZ, when the flight entered the Toronto FIR (CZYZ). The aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-GUJA, un appareil de type Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA8682 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination de Bagotville (CYBG), QC avec 4 membres d’équipage et 42 passagers à bord. Lors de la circulation au sol sur la piste 36 suivant l'atterrissage sur la piste 11 à CYBG, la roue de nez est sortie de la surface pavée pendant le virage vers la voie de circulation HOTEL, qui mène au terminal. L'équipage de conduite avait été avisé que la surface était glissante; par conséquent, l’appareil circulait lentement (8-10 kts). L'appareil n'a subi aucun dommage, et les passagers ont été transportés au terminal en autobus.

C-GGAH, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA8971 de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON avec à son bord 4 membres d'équipage et 41 passagers. Lors du refoulement de la barrière à CYUL, une légère fumée et odeur d'huile ont été constatés dans la cabine. En interrompant le prélèvement d'air sur les moteurs, la fumée et l'odeur ont cessé. L'appareil est revenu à la barrière et les passagers ont été transféré sur un autre appareil.

C-FMIX, a Bombardier BD-100-1A10 Challenger 350 aircraft operated by Sunwest Aviation, was conducting flight CNK350 from Orlando Intl (KMCO), FL to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL. As the aircraft was level at 6000 feet during the approach for Runway 27R at KFLL, the flight crew received a TCAS TA for traffic rapidly climbing/converging from the left side. The flight crew contacted KFLL approach control and were instructed to commence a right turn to a heading of 360°. While complying, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to DESCEND from the still converging traffic. The flight crew complied with the RA, and notified ATC. Through approximately 5500 feet, the flight crew received a CLEAR OF CONFLICT aural alert. ATC instructed the flight crew to climb back to 6000 feet, and vectored the aircraft for the ILS 27R approach. The rest of the approach and landing were uneventful. The TCAS traffic was never acquired visually.

C-GHKR, an Airbus 330-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA835 from Geneva-Cointrin (LSGG), Switzerland to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 11 crew members and 258 passengers on board. During the initial climb after the departure from LSGG, the control tower advised the flight crew that black smoke was observed coming from the number 1 engine (Rolls Royce UK RB211 Trent 772B-60). Simultaneously, the flight crew received a BLUE HYDRAULIC PUMP FAIL ECAM message. The flight crew requested a return to LSGG, declared a PAN PAN, and carried out an overweight landing without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced the Blue Ground Service Manifold, and the High Pressure (HP) & Low Pressure (LP) Filters as per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM). The Blue Hydraulic Reservoir was refilled in accordance with the AMM. After several checks and an overweight landing inspection, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FMZB, an Embraer ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA526 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl (KBOS), MA with 4 crew members and 84 passengers on board. During the final approach to Runway 32 at KBOS, the flight crew received a wind shear warning. The recovery procedure was executed and, since the approach was still stabilized, the flight crew continued. During the flare, the wind changed and the aircraft landed hard. After the landing was completed, the flight crew requested ARFF to inspect the aircraft; no damage was found. The flight crew taxied to the gate without further incident. There were no injuries.

C-GLQQ, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE122 from Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ to Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON with 4 crew members and 27 passengers on board. As power was reduced once the aircraft reached its initial cleared altitude of 14 000 feet after the departure from KEWR, the flight crew noticed an unusual noise coming from the engines. Simultaneously, a POWERPLANT message was received, which prompted the flight crew to execute the QRH. In the absence of abnormal engine indications, the flight crew continued to monitor the situation, and contacted the operator’s maintenance via ACARS.  Following a step climb to FL180, the number 2 Propeller Electronic Control (PEC) caution light illuminated, and the number 2 propeller RPM rose to 1060. The flight crew executed the QRH one more time, shut the number 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW150A) down, declared an emergency, and elected to divert the aircraft to Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Intl (KAVP), PA where it landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. Following an inspection, the aircraft taxied to the terminal building.Maintenance personnel determined that the number 2 Beta Feedback Transducer (BFT) failed, causing the propeller to initially go into an underspeed condition, followed by an overspeed condition. It was held at higher than normal propeller speeds (1060) by the Over Speed Governor (OSG) until the flight crew shut the engine down. The incident has been entered into the operator’s Safety Management System for further investigation.

C-GNKG, a Cessna 172M aircraft operated by Wetaskiwin Air Services, was conducting a local VFR training flight out of Wetaskiwin Regional (CEX3), AB with 2 persons on board. During the flight, the instructor decided to go to an ice strip that had been cleared on Gull Lake, approximately 10 nm west of Lacombe (CEG3), AB, to conduct a precautionary landing exercise for the student. The instructor took control of the aircraft on final approach, in order to conduct an inspection of the runway. Since the instructor was satisfied with the condition of the runway, it was decided to do a circuit, followed by a touch and go on the ice strip. The wind was light out of the west, directly down the runway. During the take-off portion of the touch and go, the aircraft began to drift to the right due to deeper snow. The instructor could not control the drift, and the aircraft departed the strip to the right. The instructor shut the engine down just before the aircraft struck a large snow bank, on the right side of the strip. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the nose and the left wing. Both the instructor and the student exited the aircraft with no injuries.

C-FDJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8850 from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON to Greater Moncton/Romeo Leblanc Intl (CYQM), NB. During the approach to CYQM, the aircraft descended through an area of clouds. The temperature was below 10°C, and the aircraft was flying above 230 kts. At airspeeds above 230 kts, the Aircraft Flight Manual (AFM) states that the selection of wing anti ice is not required. The ice detection system did not indicate the presence of ice. The flight crew conducted a visual approach and in the flare, the right wing suddenly dropped approximately 10 feet above the runway. The right main landing gear touched down first, followed by the left main and nose landing gears. After exiting the aircraft at the gate, the flight crew inspected the wings and noted an accumulation of ice on the leading edge of both wings. The flight crew consulted with maintenance, and confirmed that the ice detection system was functioning normally. The flight data recorder was removed and examined, and it was confirmed that the aircraft stalled in the flare. An SMS review and consultation with the manufacturer are ongoing.

N808FD, an Airbus 310-300 aircraft operated by Federal Express, was conducting flight FDX120 from Memphis Intl (KMEM), TN to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB with 2 pilots on board. During the approach to Runway 20 at CYEG, the flight crew received a flap indication issue, and discontinued the approach in order to complete the appropriate checklist. The flight crew dealt with the issue, and requested a second approach. After selecting the landing gear down, the flight crew noticed an unsafe nose landing gear indication. A missed approach was executed, the flight crew declared an emergency, and completed the appropriate checklist. The aircraft landed on Runway 20 without further incident. The aircraft stopped on the runway and required to be towed to the apron. The operator’s maintenance replaced the right hand nose door sequence valve and the right hand Krueger flap retract position switch. The systems were ground checked, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FUJR, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA2050 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Huatulco/Bahías de Huatulco Intl (MMBT), México with 6 crew members and 158 passengers on board. During cruise flight approximately 2 hours before the arrival at MMBT, a flight crew member became ill and was incapacitated. The other flight crew member contacted Medlink who suggested that the sick flight crew member take a specific medication. Just before the top of descent, the flight crew member was able to resume normal duties for the rest of the flight.

C-FNOG, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA859 from London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During the final approach to CYYZ, ATC instructed the flight crew to perform a go-around due to traffic on the runway. Prior to the go-around, the fuel quantity was indicating 4800 kgs. However, with the increased pitch up during the climb, the fuel quantity was observed to display 3200 kgs. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and the aircraft returned to land without further incident with ARFF standing by. When the aircraft reached the gate at the terminal, the fuel quantity displayed 3800 kgs.

C-FGFL, un appareil de type Pilatus PC-12/45 exploité par Chrono Aviation, effectuait le vol NDL654 selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de Nemiscau (CYHH), QC à destination de Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU), QC. Lorsque l’équipage de conduite a amorcé la descente initiale environ 100 miles nautiques au nord de CYHU, l’indication lumineuse d’attacher les ceintures de sécurité a été activée. Au moment de passer au travers les nuages, l’appareil a rencontré de la turbulence légère à modérée. Suivant l’épisode de turbulence, l’approche et l’atterrissage se sont déroulés normalement. Après le débarquement des passagers, un des passagers a mentionné à un représentant du service à la clientèle de Chrono Aviation que sa tête avait frappé le plafond de l’appareil lors de la turbulence, et qu’il ressentait une douleur à la tête depuis. Le représentant lui a offert d’appeler une ambulance, mais celui-ci a décliné l’offre. Le lendemain, l’exploitant a été avisé que le passager s’était rendu à l’hôpital et qu’il avait reçu un diagnostic d’entorse cervicale.

C-FQWK, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG596 from Cancun Intl (MMUN), Mexico to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 7 crew members and 187 passengers on board. Approximately 35 minutes before the landing at CYYC, a flight crew member felt sick and became incapacitated. Since there was a third pilot assigned to this flight, the flight was completed to destination without further incident. It is suspected that the cause of the sickness was food poisoning.

C-GJBV, un appareil de type Beech A100 King Air exploité par SkyJet M.G., effectuait le vol d’évacuation médicale (MEDEVAC) VSL512 selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de Lourdes-de-Blanc-Sablon (CYBX), QC à destination de Sept-îles (CYZV), QC. Environ 60 miles nautiques à l’est de CYZV, l’équipage a observé une défaillance du générateur droit, suivi de l’arrêt de l’alimentation électrique par le générateur gauche. Bien que la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée, l’équipage n’est pas parvenu à isoler le générateur gauche, et a dû poursuivre le vol avec la batterie comme unique source d’alimentation électrique. Les systèmes électriques non essentiels au vol ont été fermés afin de réduire la consommation électrique, et l’équipage a déclaré une urgence. L’atterrissage à CYZV s’est fait sans encombre. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

C-GUXF, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-8-100 exploité par Air Creebec, effectuait le vol CRQ922 selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de Waskaganish (CYKQ), QC à destination de Val-d'Or (CYVO), QC. Lors de l’approche finale à CYVO, l’équipage de conduite a reçu une indication anormale que les roues n’étaient pas verrouillées lorsque le train d’atterrissage a été sélectionné en position baissée. Une approche interrompue a été effectuée, la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée, et l’équipage a déclaré un PAN PAN. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

N305UP, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by United Parcel Service (UPS), was conducting flight UPS218 from Paris/Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France to Philadelphia Intl (KPHL), PA. During cruise flight approximately 175 nm north east of Goose Bay (CYYR), NL, the flight crew received several EICAS messages (IAS DISAGREE, RUDDER RATIO, AILERON LOCKOUT), in addition to several stall warning activations. A few minutes later, the EICAS message L/R EEC (Electronic Engine Control) was received. The flight crew declared an emergency and requested a diversion to CYYR, where the aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance personnel conducted a pitot static leak check, and inspected the pitot drains. No faults were found. The right Air Data Computer (ADC) was replaced, and the aircraft was released to service.

G-TCCF, an Airbus 330-200 aircraft operated by Thomas Cook Airlines, was conducting Condor Airlines flight CFG116 from Frankfurt/Rhein-Main (EDDF), Germany to Cancún Intl (MMUN), Mexico. During cruise flight, liquid was inadvertently spilled onto the number 1 Audio Control Panel (ACP), causing all lights on the unit to illuminate. Initially, the number 1 ACP, then the number 2 ACP became hot, and began to emit a burnt electrical odour. At approximate position 56°03'N/031°11'W, smoke started to come out from the number 1 ACP. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks, initiated a diversion to Shannon Intl (EINN), Ireland, and sent a MAYDAY message using ACARS. The flight crew jettisoned fuel in order to achieve maximum landing weight, and the aircraft landed at EINN without further incident. 1 passenger and 4 crew members were attended to by paramedics and sent to local medical facilities for a precautionary assessment before being released.

C-FOHG, a Bell 407 aircraft operated by Northern Shield Helicopters, was conducting heli-skiing operations approximately 22 nm east northeast of Revelstoke (CYRV), BC. While maneuvering to land the helicopter to pick up a group of skiers at an un-flagged/un-prepared landing site, the main rotor blades contacted the sloped snow covered ground. The pilot felt a vibration, maneuvered the helicopter to another landing site approximately 300 feet away, and landed without further incident. After shutting the helicopter down at the cross slope landing site, the pilot inspected the main rotor blades and noticed some damage.

C-GHPY, an Air Canada Boeing 787-8 aircraft was being operated as flight AC737 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to San Francisco Intl (KSFO), CA. During the approach, a TCAS RA warning was triggered. The crew followed the RA and the flight continued uneventfully.

C-FWAD, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA667 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 9 crew members and 187 passengers on board. As the aircraft was approaching its destination, a cabin crew member experienced a medical incident. The flight crew was advised of the situation, and duties were distributed to the remaining flight attendants for the remainder of the flight.

C-FSRY, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8185 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC with 4 crew members and 62 passengers on board. As the aircraft was climbing through FL220 after the departure from CYVR, the flight crew reported a hissing noise in the flight deck, simultaneously receiving a cabin pressure caution indication. As the cabin pressure began to climb, the flight crew donned their oxygen masks. An emergency descent was executed, and the aircraft returned to CYVR where it landed without further incident. A few passengers reported ear discomfort during the descent. The operator’s maintenance inspection revealed that the belly drain under the cockpit was leaking air. The valve and the cabin pressure controller were replaced. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GEWR, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3283 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR) BC, to Prince George (CYXS), BC with 4 crew members and 39 passengers on board. After the departure from CYVR, the flight crew received an unsafe nose landing gear indication. The flight crew confirmed that the nose landing gear was retracted, and continued to CYXS. During the approach to CYXS, the nose landing gear would not extend. The flight crew extended the landing gear manually, and declared a MAYDAY. The aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. There were no injuries. Subsequent maintenance actions revealed that the nose landing gear actuator had failed. The part was replaced, and the system tested serviceable. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFNC, un Boeing 737-406 exploité par Bradley Air Services / First Air sous l’indicatif FAB866, avec à son bord 4 membres d'équipage et 78 passagers, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP). Pendant l’approche vers la piste 25 de CYVP, l’équipage a reçu une indication d'assymétrie des volets. L’approche a été interrompue, l'équipage a suivi la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a demandé la présence des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) pour l'atterrissage. Le C-FFNC s’est posé sans encombre et s’est immobilisé sur la piste pour l’inspection des freins. L’aéronef a ensuite circulé jusqu’au terminal. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé. L'indicateur et le transmetteur de position des volets ont été changés et l'appareil a été remis en service.

C-FGRC, a de Havilland DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8766 from Quebec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC to Sept-Iles (CYZV), QC. As passengers had begun to board the aircraft at gate 25 at CYQB, the flight crew encountered issues with the lighting in the flight deck. After troubleshooting and resetting circuit breakers, an electrical smell came on, and smoke appeared in the flight deck. Two passengers had boarded the aircraft, and were deplaned. The flight was delayed.

N508MJ, un appareil de type Bombardier CL-600-2C10 CRJ700 exploité par Mesa Airlines, effectuait le vol ASH6259 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Washington/Dulles Intl (KIAD), VA à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. Lors de l’approche pour la piste 24R à CYUL, une anomalie du train d'atterrissage est survenue. L’équipage de conduite a effectué une remontée, et a déclaré une urgence. L'appareil est revenu se poser sans encombre, et a circulé jusqu'à la barrière.

C-GKVL, un appareil de type Boeing 737-800 exploité par Sunwing Airlines, effectuait le vol SWG193 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC à destination de Puerto Vallarta/Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz Intl (MMPR), Mexique avec 7 membres d'équipage et 162 passagers à bord. Lors de la montée initiale au départ de la piste 24 à CYQB, l’équipage de conduite a entendu un bruit fort au moment où le train d’atterrissage se rétractait. Bien qu’aucune indication ou anomalie n’était présente dans le poste de pilotage, l’équipage a cru initialement à l’éclatement d’un pneu, et en a avisé l’ATC. Toutefois, la tour de contrôle de CYQB a confirmé qu’aucun débris de pneu n’a été localisé. Le Centre de contrôle de l’entretien de l’exploitant fût par la suite contacté, et la décision de dérouter le vol vers Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC a été prise. L'équipage de conduite a déclaré un PAN PAN, et a demandé la présence des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). L’aéronef s’est posé sans encombre en surcharge sur la piste 24R, et a circulé jusqu’au terminal après l’inspection des freins par le SLIA. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé. L’aéronef a été remis en service la même journée.

C-FGKZ, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA119 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 6 crew members and 190 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew received multiple Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitor (ECAM) messages, including ELAC 1 FAULT (Elevator and Aileron Computer), RIGHT AILERON FAULT, and LEFT AILERON FAULT. The ELAC was successfully reset, however the faults returned while the aircraft was in cruise flight while in US airspace. The flight crew declared an emergency with US Air Traffic Control (ATC) because of the loss of aileron control, however continued the flight and subsequently declared a PAN PAN on initial contact with Vancouver ATC. The aircraft landed without further incident in CYVR. There were no injuries.The operator’s maintenance replaced the ELAC 1 and 2 units and, after the system was tested serviceable, the aircraft was returned to service. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) was submitted to Transport Canada.

C-FLHJ, a Boeing 737-400 aircraft operated by Flair Airlines, was conducting flight FLE416 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB with 6 crew members and 157 passengers on board. Passing FL260 during the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from CYVR, the number 2 engine (CFM56-3C1) began to surge. The flight crew actioned the QRH checklist, and reduced the thrust on the affected engine, which eliminated the surge. The flight crew elected to return to CYVR, and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. There were no injuries. The operator’s maintenance conducted a borescope inspection, engine run, and a test flight. However, the condition could not be duplicated. The aircraft was returned to service.

N902EV, un appareil de type Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 exploité par SkyWest Airlines, effectuait le vol SKW3130 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Chicago/O’Hare Intl (KORD), IL à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. Des opérations de déneigement avaient été effectuées sur la piste 24R, et le convoi de véhicules se dirigeait vers la piste 24L via la voie de circulation Alpha. Le convoi a reçu et relu correctement l’instruction de rester à l’écart de la piste 24L. SKW3130 était en courte finale pour la piste 24L lorsque le véhicule de tête a fait une incursion sur la piste 24L, suivi de 2 autres véhicules; le reste du convoi est resté à l’écart de la piste. Le contrôleur aérien a donné l’instruction à SKW3130 d’interrompre son approche. L’équipage du SKW3130 a effectué une remontée, et est revenu se poser sans encombre sur la piste 24R. Il n’y a pas eu de blessé.

C-GNJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7362 from Detroit/Metro Wayne County (KDTW), MI to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During the descent to CYYZ, the flight crew received a FLAP FAIL caution message upon selection of flaps down, while the flaps gauge was indicating fully retracted. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and the aircraft continued for the landing with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance replaced the Skew Detection Unit (SDU), flap actuators and flex drive shafts. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-GEZD, an Airbus 321-211 operated by Air Transat, was performing flight TSC782 from Quebec City / Jean Lesage Int’l (CYQB), QC to Fort Lauderdale / Hollywood Int’l (KFLL), FL with 6 crew members and 190 passengers onboard. During descent into KFLL, at around 6000 ft, the flight crew received a TCAS/TA warning, followed immediately by a TCAS/RA. The flight crew followed standard operating procedures, complied with the TCAS/RA, and advised ATC of the TCAS advisory.

C-FTVF, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC447 from Holguin/Frank País Intl (MUHG), Cuba to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 6 crew members and 183 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL290, approximately 90 nm east-southeast of Pittsburgh Intl (KPIT), PA, the flight encountered severe turbulence for approximately 30 seconds. Altitude and pitch variations were minor. Speed variations were +/- 10 kts, and the aircraft experienced rolls of approximately 30° that were managed by the auto-pilot. The flight crew requested and was authorized to FL270, and the aircraft continued to destination without further incident. There were no injuries.The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM). No defects were found, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GZEH, un Boeing 737-800 exploité par Air Transat A.T. inc. sous l’indicatif TSC437, avec à son bord 6 membres d'équipage et 173 passagers, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Cancún Intl, Mexique (MMUN) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Alors que le C-GZEH effectuait une approche pour la piste 24R, les volets sont restés bloqués à la position 2 avec une faible dissymétrie des volets. Une approche interrompue a été effectuée et la liste de vérification du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et l’intervention des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) a été requise. Le C-GZEH s’est posé sans encombre et a été remorqué jusqu’au terminal après inspection. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GIKN, a Sikorsky S-92 helicopter operated by Cougar Helicopters was conducting flight CGR62 on a local SAR training trip 20nm south of St John’s International Airport (CYYT), NL. After lowering rescue personnel onto a vessel during night operations, the helicopter moved to the rest position away from the vessel to prepare for departure. The hoist cable was fully retracted and stowed at this point. On departure, the hoist operator, as well as the rescue personnel on the vessel, saw an object falling from the helicopter into the ocean. It was discovered that the hook was missing from the inboard hoist. Upon inspection of the hoist after landing, it was determined that the cable shear had unintentionally been activated. The inbound hoist was changed out. The Hoist Control panel was tested with no fault found and remained on the aircraft. Post installation checks were completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FTID, an Aerospatiale ATR42-500 aircraft operated by First Air, was conducting flight FAB852 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NY to Cambridge Bay (CYCB), NT with 3 crew members and 22 passengers on board. Approximately 60nm NNE of CYZF, after leveling at FL230, the flight crew received a master warning indication for "EXCESS CABIN ALTITUDE". The crew completed the applicable memory items and carried out the applicable QRH procedure. An emergency was declared with ATS and the decision to return to CYZF was made where an uneventful landing was completed. Company maintenance found a damaged ground air conditioning duct check valve. The part was replaced, ground checks/runs were completed, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GLQR, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE938 from Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl (KBOS), MA to Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON with 4 crew members and 21 passengers on board. Upon selection of landing gear up after the departure from KBOS, the flight crew received a nose landing gear amber advisory light. The aircraft was configured to remain below 185 kts, and the flight crew stopped the climb at 12 000 feet to assess the situation. The QRH was executed and, after consultation with the operator, the decision to return to KBOS was chosen. ATC was notified of the situation, and the flight crew declared a PAN PAN. Following a successful alternate landing gear extension, the flight crew received 3 green lights. The aircraft landed without further incident on Runway 27, stopped on the runway, and shut down both engines. Following an inspection and after securing the landing gear, the aircraft was towed to the gate.The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and replaced the nose solenoid sequence valve. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTQX, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC703 from Roatán/Juan Manuel Gálvez Intl (MHRO), Honduras to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 6 crew members and 161 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL350, approximately 50 nm south southeast of Pittsburgh Intl (KPIT), PA, the aircraft experienced a pressurization problem, which prompted the flight crew to don their oxygen masks. An emergency was declared, and the flight crew executed a rapid descent to 10 000 feet. Once at 10 000 feet, the flight crew regained control of the pressurization, and cancelled the emergency. The flight continued to destination and landed at CYYZ without further incident. There were no injuries.The operator's maintenance is troubleshooting the problem.

C-FEKB, a Beech 200 King Air aircraft operated by Kenn Borek Air, was conducting flight KBA203 from Sachs Harbour (David Nasogaluak Jr Saaryuaq) (CYSY), NT to Inuvik (Mike Zubko) (CYEV), NT with 2 crew members on board. Shortly after take off from CYSY, the flight crew received a left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-41) fire indication. Before the flight crew could address the problem, the indication went out. A scan of the engine instruments revealed no anomalies, so the flight crew elected to continue the flight. Approximately 60 nm south west of CYSY, a second left engine fire warning indication was received. There was no physical indication of fire, and troubleshooting failed to correct the problem. The flight crew elected to shut the engine down, and activated the fire bottle. An emergency was declared, and the flight crew elected to return to CYSY where an uneventful landing was completed.Subsequent investigation by the operator’s maintenance determined that there was an unserviceable fire detector for the left hand engine, which was providing an erroneous fire indication.

C-FASF, an Embraer EMB-525 aircraft operated by Air Sprint, was conducting flight ASP827 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 2 crew members and 2 passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff from CYXE, the flight crew received a FLAP LEVER DISAG caution message upon selection of flaps up from the Flap 1 position. The applicable checklist was executed, and a FLAP FAIL CAS message was subsequently received. A visual inspection of the flaps by a flight crew member indicated that they were near the Flap 0 position. The decision was made to continue to CYYC, with speed and altitude restrictions. ATC was notified and a PAN PAN was declared. The aircraft landed without further incident in CYYC with ARFF on standby. The operator's maintenance cleared all active faults and performed a flap function test. The flap system tested serviceable, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GLWJ, a de Havilland DHC-8-402 operated by WestJet Encore as flight WEN3272 departed Regina Intl. (CYQR), SK for Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. On climbout from CYQR, the flight crew received a gear "INOP" caution light and they completed the QRH checklist. The flight continued to CYYC where the flight crew declared PAN PAN and requested ARFF. A manual extension of the landing gear was completed and the flight landed safety in CYYC. The aircraft was towed to the gate. The operator's maintenance found the nose landing gear #2 sensor was open. The sensor was replaced and gear swings were carried out.

C-GFAJ, un appareil de type Airbus A330-300 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA419 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl. (CYUL), QC à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl. (CYYZ), ON. En montée au niveau de vol FL200, l'équipage de conduite a été instruit de procéder direct MELTI.  50 secondes se sont écoulées avant le début du virage. Conséquemment, l'espacement avec C-GGJA, un appareil de type Bombardier CRJ-200 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuant le vol JZA851 à destination d’Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl. (CYOM), ON, a été réduit à 4.7 miles sur le plan latéral alors que la norme est de 5 miles. Les trajectoires des aéronefs étaient divergentes.

C-FSRN, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8416 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Kelowna (CYLW), BC. Upon selection of landing gear up after the departure from CYVR, the red nose gear unsafe advisory light illuminated for over a minute, and the amber nose gear door light remained illuminated. The flight crew declared an emergency, and returned to CYVR where the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance conducted multiple gear swings and inspections, however no defects were found. The aircraft was returned to service. The aircraft experienced the same problem the previous day, however the landing gear was extended via the alternate gear extension, and the aircraft returned to CYVR. No emergency had been declared. Gear swings were conducted as well, but no faults were found. The nose landing gear shock strut was serviced and the aircraft was returned to service.

At 0851 Mountain Standard Time on 30 January 2019, the Air Tindi Ltd. Beechcraft King Air 200 aircraft (registration C-GTUC, serial number BB-268) departed Yellowknife Airport (CYZF), Northwest Territories, as flight TIN503, on an instrument flight rules flight itinerary to Whatì Airport (CEM3), Northwest Territories, with 2 crew members on board. At 0912, as the aircraft began the approach to CEM3, it departed controlled flight during its initial descent from 12 000 feet above sea level, and impacted terrain approximately 21 nautical miles east-southeast of CEM3, at an elevation of 544 feet above sea level. The Canadian Mission Control Centre received a signal from the aircraft’s 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter and notified the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre in Trenton, Ontario. Search and rescue technicians arrived on site approximately 6 hours after the accident. The 2 flight crew members received fatal injuries on impact. The aircraft was destroyed.UPDATED: 12 MAY 2020

C-FEJB, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU, (operated by Sky Regional Airlines, flight 7665) was departing from runway 06L at Toronto/LBPIA (CYYZ) during snowy weather conditions. At the same time, a convoy of snow plows /sweeper vehicles were operating north of runway 06L and proceeding southbound on taxiway Echo. ATC instructed the vehicles to turn left on to taxiway Charlie (east), however the vehicles turned left on Charlie 2 (C2) towards Runway 06L and continued past the hold short position. Ground control instructed the vehicles to STOP, and they came to rest just prior to 06L. The tower controller instructed C-FEJB to abort; the flight crew rejected the take-off and the aircraft came to rest just prior to C2.

C-GFFL, a de Havilland DHC-7-100 aircraft operated by Air Tindi, was conducting flight TIN803 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Diavik (CDK2), NT with 3 crew members and 35 passengers on board. During the descent into CDK2, the flight crew observed sparks coming from the top of the number 4 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-50) cowling. The sparks were caused by the engine cowling making contact with the propeller spinner. The flight crew actioned the QRH, and shut the number 4 engine down. The aircraft landed at CDK2 without further incident.

C-FSLZ, a Swearingen SA226-TC aircraft operated Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting local maintenance flight PAG08 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. The flight crew conducted an intentional shut down of the left engine (Garrett TPE331-10UA) in order to test the Negative Torque Sensing (NTS) system. During the subsequent restart of the engine, there was no torque indication, and the RPM was fluctuating. The flight crew elected to secure the left engine, and returned to CYWG. The flight crew completed the applicable checklist, SOPs and QRH items. No emergency was declared, and the subsequent landing was conducted successfully with the left engine inoperative. After the landing, the flight crew were unable to taxi the aircraft from Runway 36, and elected to shut down at the intersection of Runway 13/31 and 36. The aircraft was then towed to Apron 4.

C-GGMU, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8946 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Saint John (CYSJ), NB. During the takeoff from CYYZ, the left hand engine cowl door separated from the nacelle, and struck the left wing leading edge, causing damage to the de-icing boot. The flight continued to CYSJ as the crew were not aware of the event, and there were no cockpit indications or engine vibrations. The flight proceeded uneventfully, and the missing door was only noticed after the aircraft was parked at the terminal. The door was found on Runway 24R at CYYZ. The operator’s maintenance had performed a pre-flight inspection before the departure from CYYZ, which included engine oil quantity checks in the area of the missing cowl. The operator is investigating.

C-FSEQ, a Boeing 737-8 MAX aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA534 from Kahului (PHOG), HI to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 6 crew members and 134 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL370, the flight crew noticed a low oil quantity and a low oil pressure on the right engine (CFM LEAP 1B27). The flight crew elected to continue the flight, while monitoring the oil level. At the top of descent into CYVR, the oil quantity for the right engine was near zero. The flight crew consulted the QRH, shut the right engine down, and declared a MAYDAY. The flight landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. There were no injuries. The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and found that the oil loss came from the starter. The starter malfunction also caused damage to the engine fan case. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) was filed with Transport Canada Civil Aviation (TCCA). The starter and engine were removed and replaced. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GSKG, a Beech 1900C aircraft operated by Skylink Express, was conducting flight SLQ7721 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK. Shortly after takeoff from CYWG, the left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-65B) shut down unexpectedly. The fight crew continued the climb to 2 000 feet ASL in VFR conditions, declared an emergency, and returned to CYWG. The subsequent landing was successful with the left engine inoperative.The operator's maintenance inspected the engine and no defects were noted. The fuel system was inspected and the left auxiliary fuel tank was found to contain water. The fuel system was serviced and a ground run was performed. Additionally, a test flight was conducted successfully. The fuel provider's bowsers were also inspected, and found to be free of contaminants.

C-GEZD, an Airbus A321-211 operated by Air Transat under flight number TSC782 with 6 crew members and 185 passengers on board, was carrying out a flight under instrument flight rules from Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl, FL (KFLL). While parked at the gate and undergoing de-icing, fumes were noticed in the flight deck as well as reported by the cabin crew. It was quickly attributed to de-icing fluid being ingested by the APU. The aircraft was deplaned and emergency services contacted. 11 passengers and 4 crew members were seen by paramedics and transported to the hospital for observations.

C-FLSS, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA795 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Los Angeles Intl (KLAX), CA with 5 crew members and 146 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL360, approximately 85 nm south west of Colorado Springs/Municipal (KCOS), CO, the aircraft passed through a mountain wave and the number 1 engine (CFM56-5A1) rolled back from 90% to 60% N1. The aircraft started to lose speed, and started to descent. The flight crew notified ATC and requested FL300. There was a slight vibration on the number 1 engine, however there were no ECAM warnings. Shortly thereafter, the engine recovered and the flight landed without further incident. No emergency was declared.The operator is troubleshooting to find the cause.

C-FMWI, a privately registered Piper PA-12 aircraft, was on a local flight and was preparing to land on a gravel bar on the Fraser River approximately 4 nm north of Chilliwack, BC. The aircraft touched down short of the gravel bar and the main wheels made contact with the water, causing the aircraft to nose over. The aircraft sustained a prop strike and airframe damage. The pilot, the sole occupant, was not injured. The ELT did not activate and there was no fire.

C-FZCV, a Gulfstream G280 aircraft operated by Skyservice Business Aviation, was conducting a flight from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. As the aircraft rotated off the runway during the takeoff from CYVR, the flight crew received multiple warning messages, including LEFT BATTERY DISCHARGE and STAB TRIM FAIL. Because the horizontal stabilizer could not be trimmed, the flight crew slowed the aircraft down in order to reduce the aerodynamic load required, declared an emergency, and returned to CYVR for an overweight landing. The were no injuries or damage. The aircraft's left battery had indicated a charging problem during engine shutdown after the previous flight. Consequently, the left battery had been selected off and the aircraft was released under MEL provisions for the occurrence flight. The operator’s maintenance is replacing the left battery.

C-GTFX, un Aérospatiale AS350 B3 exploité par Peak Aviation effectuait un vol de gestion de la faune dans la région du lac Manouane, QC depuis Chute des Passes, QC, avec 1 pilote et 3 agents de la faune à son bord. Suite au déploiement du filet afin de capturer un caribou, un son claquant a été entendu. Le pilote a effectué un atterrissage immédiat à une distance d’environ 100 pieds de l’animal. Une fois le rotor arrêté, il a été constaté que l’animal se trouvait sur un monticule de neige sur la berge. Le pilote a effectué une inspection de l’appareil et a constaté des dommages au rotor de queue, à la partie inférieure du stabilisateur, et à la partie basse de la fine. Le caribou a subi des blessures mortelles.

C-GRPF, a Bombardier CL600-2B16 Challenger 601-3R aircraft operated by Skyservice Business Aviation, was conducting a flight from Iquitos/Coronel FAP Francisco Secada Vignetta Intl (SPQT), Perú to Teterboro (KTEB), NJ with 3 crew members and 2 passengers on board. When they were closing in to destination, the flight crew inquired to ATC about possible delays at KTEB; ATC replied that they were not aware of any delays. As they were subsequently handed over to another controller, the flight was issued a 45 minute hold, with possible longer delays. Since the flight did not have the fuel to hold this long, the flight crew declared Minimum Fuel. The flight crew requested a diversion to Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ, which was granted by ATC. The flight landed at KEWR with 2000 lbs of fuel remaining, which was well above the requirement.

C-GTCO, un appareil de type DHC-8-102 exploité par Air Creebec, effectuait le vol CRQ926 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Rouyn-Noranda (CYUY), QC à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC avec 3 membres d’équipage et 6 passagers à bord. Lors de la course au décollage de la piste 26 à CYUY, l’appareil a dévié vers la gauche, s’éloignant  de plus en plus du centre de la piste. L'appareil a quitté la surface de la piste et le train principal gauche a pénétré un andain de neige de 18 pouces d'épaisseur. En voulant réduire la puissance sur les 2 moteurs, le pilote a réduit la puissance sur le  moteur de gauche et par accident augmenté la puissance sur le moteur de droite. La puissance asymétrique a créé une déviation encore plus importantevers la gauche et l’appareil s'est finalement immobilisé dans un amas de neige compact d’environ 3 pieds d’épaisseur situé à environ 40 pieds au sud de la piste. Une personne a subi des blessures mineures, et l'appareil a subi des dommages importants.

G-CIVO, a Boeing 747-400 aircraft operated by British Airways, was conducting flight BAW45 from Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl (KBOS), MA to London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK. During cruise fight approximately 100 nm north of Greater Moncton/Romeo Leblanc Intl (CYQM), NB, the flight crew reported fumes in the cockpit. A MAYDAY was declared, and the QRH for SMOKE/FIRE/FUMES was executed. During this process, one of the items on the checklist switches off the utility power, which removes most of the cabin lighting. The flight crew requested a diversion to KBOS, and donned their oxygen masks for the duration of the flight. The fumes only became noticeable in the cabin toward the end of the flight; however, the passenger masks were not used. The aircraft landed without further incident. One cabin crew member was admitted to the hospital. One flight crew and nine other cabin crew members also attended another hospital for medical check ups. Every crew member was released the same day, and went to the hotel. No passengers reported feeling ill.Extensive inspections and function checks were carried out on a number of systems/components on the aircraft. The fumes were found to have originated from a defect or contamination within air conditioning pack number 2. The pack has been locked out, and the aircraft returned to EGLL using DDG 21-51-01. The pack will be inspected within the 10 day period allowable for this defect in order to determine the exact cause of the issue.

C-FWSE, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1465 from Phoenix/Sky Harbor Intl (KPHX), AZ to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB with 6 crew members and 161 passengers on board. During cruise flight, a cabin crew member experienced a medical incident. The flight crew was advised, and medical personnel were contacted. The incapacitated flight attendant's duties were distributed to the remaining cabin crew for the landing. Emergency Medical Services transported the cabin crew member to the hospital.

N402LC, a Lockheed 382G-44K-30 Hercules aircraft operated by Lynden Air Cargo LLC, was conducting flight LYC402 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Anchorage/Ted Stevens Intl (PANC), AK. During the climb after the departure from CYZF, the number 2 propeller low oil light illuminated, followed by an RPM out of limit message. The QRH was executed, and arrangements were made for a fuel dump. The flight crew reported to the tower that they shut down one engine (Allison 501-D22A) and had to return to CYZF. Shortly after, the number 3 propeller low oil light illuminated, with RPM out of limits. They then declared an emergency and advised they had to shut a second engine down. The aircraft landed without further incident with emergency services attending. A maintenance crew was dispatched to CYZF, and the operator will report back to the TSB with their findings.

C-GSGT, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Wildcat Helicopters, was conducting heli-skiing operations in the vicinity of Carpenter Lake, BC. As the aircraft was on approach for a precautionary landing to wait for weather to pass at the bottom of the Slim Fast ski run, the main rotor contacted the tops of a few spruce trees. The pilot did not notice or feel the contact with the trees. The helicopter landed momentarily, then returned to the Tyax ski lodge due to weather. During the inspection after the helicopter was shut down, the damage to the main rotor blades was noticed. The helicopter was grounded at the ski lodge, and photos of the damage were sent to the manufacturer for assessment. The operator’s maintenance is awaiting further instruction for inspection and maintenance action.

C-GXFC, a Lockheed 188C Electra aircraft operated by Buffalo Airways, was conducting flight BFL1218 from Hope Bay (CHB3), NU to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT. The flight crew advised CYZF tower that they had shut down an engine (Allison 501-D13), did not require priority, and did not need assistance on arrival. The flight landed without further incident.

C-GANS, a de Havilland DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG985 from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON to Angling Lake/Wapekeka (CKB6), ON with 3 crew members and 28 passengers on board. Approximately 10 minutes after the departure from CYXL, the flight crew received a SMOKE warning indication. The flight crew called the flight attendant to verify the alarm, and declared an emergency with ATC requesting a return to CYXL. The flight attendant notified the flight crew that no smoke was visible, and prepared the cabin for a landing at CYXL. The aircraft landed without further incident, and stopped on the runway while ARFF assessed it. No evidence of smoke or fire was reported by ARFF. The aircraft taxied to the apron where passengers deplaned. The operator's maintenance found that the number 1 smoke detector would not test. The smoke detector was deferred as per the MEL, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FZUB, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA307 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. During cruise, the flight crew received a HYD 2 LO LVL message, followed subsequently by a Y ENG PUMP LO PR ECAM message. ATC was notified, and the flight crew indicated that they were in communication with their Maintenance Control Centre (MCC). ECAM actions were completed, and, during the approach to CYVR, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft then carried out an uneventful landing on Runway 08L, stopped on the runway for inspection, and taxied to the gate followed by the operator’s maintenance personnel and ARFF.The operator’s maintenance determined that there was a Yellow Hydraulic Pressure line leak in the aft pylon area. There was chaffing found on the line which caused the leak. Damaged parts were replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service the following day.

C-FHVX, a Dornier 328 operated by Central Mountain Air as flight GLR708 from Terrace was on approach to Prince George when the flight crew reported a cargo fire indication and declared an emergency. ARFF were on standby when the flight landed without further event. Company maintenance inspected the aircraft.Update 31-01-2019: A TC Civil Aviation Safety Inspector (CASI) looked into this occurrence. Maintenance boarded the aircraft and indicated that there was an electrical burning smell. Upon inspection of the cabin lighting ballast, it was found that the last left hand (LH) ballast had an electrical failure. The damage was contained to the ballast. Maintenance tracked the possible smoke path and concluded that the smoke travelled from the passenger compartment aft into the cargo hold filling the cargo hold with smoke and triggering the detector. The cargo hold was inspected for smoke/fire damage. There was no evidence of fire in the cargo hold. Cabin inspection revealed no cosmetic damage to interior furnishing or airframe. The cabin lighting system ballast was replaced and the system functioned without fault. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) was submitted.

C-FOHK, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Wildcat Helicopters, had departed from Kelowna (Wildcat Helicopters) (CWC2), BC, enroute to Penticton (CYYF), BC to conduct a pilot proficiency check ride. While heading south toward CYYF at 2500 feet ASL, the pilot observed an aircraft heading directly toward them. The pilot initiated a sudden turn to the right to avoid a collision. The unidentified, low wing aircraft flew past C-FOHK within 150 feet, at the same altitude. Unsuccessful attempts were made to contact the aircraft on 126.7. Once in the vicinity of CYYF, the pilot reported the risk of collision to ATC.

C-FWEP, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3265 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Kelowna (CYLW), BC. During cruise flight, the flight crew received a fuselage door warning light. Subsequently, a loud bang was heard and pressurization was lost during the descent. The flight crew declared an emergency, and continued to destination where ARFF met the flight. The aircraft landed without further event. The operator’s maintenance inspected the aft cargo door and found the lateral door handle in the extended position on arrival to the gate. The door handle had not been secured properly.

C-GLAT, an Airbus 310-300 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC801 from Samaná/El Catey Intl (MDCY), Dominican Republic, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During cruise flight, a cabin crew member became ill and was not able to perform assigned duties. These duties were redistributed to the rest of the cabin crew for the remainder of the flight.

C-FTXW, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC443 from Cancun Intl (MMUN), Mexico to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 6 crew members and 139 passengers on board. As ground personnel was loading the passenger bags into the holds, brown smoke could be seen coming out from one of them, and actually burning through the material. The suitcase was taken away from the gate area, and sprayed with a portable fire extinguisher. ARFF came over and inspected the bag. It was determined that the fire and smoke was caused by electronic cigarette batteries that were overheating. A second bag belonging to a travel companion was removed as a precaution.

C-GOWG, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing, was conducting flight SWG648 from Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC to Holguin/Frank Pais Intl (MUHG), Cuba with 6 crew members and 180 passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff from CYQB, the flight crew requested to return to the airport as they suspected that they may have experienced a tail strike during the rotation. The Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) checklist was carried out and, in consultation with the operator’s operational control centre (OCC), a decision was made to divert the flight to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed overweight without further incident at CYUL. ARFF and maintenance personnel inspected the aircraft before it was towed to the gate. The operator’s maintenance performed a tail strike inspection and no faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSKO, a Beech B200 King Air aircraft operated by Keewatin Air, was conducting medevac repositioning flight KEW204 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Churchill (CYYQ), MB. Climbing through 10 000 feet after the departure from CYWG, the flight crew observed fuel leaking from the left wing. The left fuel indication was also indicating 300 pounds less than the right fuel indicator, where both indicators were equal before the departure. The flight crew declared an emergency, and returned for an uneventful landing at CYWG. After landing, ARFF met the aircraft and confirmed the fuel leak under the left wing. The aircraft was shut down on the runway, and towed to the operator's maintenance facility.The operator's maintenance examined the aircraft and determined that fuel was leaking from the left wing tip air inlet vent. The fuel tank air inlet check valve was replaced, and no further leaks were detected. The aircraft was returned to service.
