C-GSCA, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1609 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 8 crew members and 282 passengers on board. During cruise flight less than 1 hour after the departure from KFLL, a cabin crew member felt ill and was unable to continue duties. Duties were reassigned for the remainder of the flight, and the aircraft continued to destination without further incident.

CNK657, a Learjet 45 aircraft operated by Sunwest Aviation, was on the approach for Runway 17R at Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB, and was instructed to descend to 5200 feet. ACA351, an Embraer 190 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was on the RNP Y approach to Runway 17L. Separation between the two aircraft was reduced to 1.8 miles laterally, where 3.0 miles or 1000 feet is required.

N555EF, a privately operated Bombardier CL-600-2B16 Challenger 604 aircraft, was conducting a flight from St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL to Miami-Opa Locka Executive (KOPF), FL. When taxiing for the departure at CYYT, N555EF had been given instructions to taxi via Runway 02 for a takeoff on Runway 29, with a restriction to hold short of Runway 29. ATC observed N555EF approaching the hold short line of Runway 29 without slowing down, and instructed the flight crew to stop. The aircraft stopped beyond the hold short line, 300 feet away from Runway 29. C-GMRS, a Beech 200 King Air aircraft operated by PAL Aerospace, was approaching to land on Runway 29 and had its landing clearance cancelled by ATC due to the encroachment into the protected area of Runway 29. Once N555EF vacated the area, C-GMRS circled around and landed on Runway 29 without further incident.

C-FPBJ, a de Havilland DHC-7-100 aircraft operated by Trans Capital Air, was conducting flight UNO657P from Wanlaweyn/Baledogle Airfield (HCBD), Somalia to Baidoa (HCMB), Somalia with 3 crew members and 17 passengers on board. During the descent to HCMB, the flight crew received a LOW OIL PRESSURE indication on the number 3 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-50). The flight crew initiated an immediate diversion to Mogadishu/Aden Adde Intl (HCMM), Somalia, and briefed the cabin crew of a potential in-flight shut down. During the flight to HCMM, the oil pressure was fluctuating continually. The flight crew executed the QRH, proceeded to shut the number 3 engine down, declared a PAN PAN, and requested ARFF to stand by. The aircraft landed at HCMM without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced a hydraulic garloc seal, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYHQ, a Bell 212 HP BLR aircraft operated by Yellowhead Helicopters, was conducting a local flight near Blue River (CYCP), BC. Upon completion of the day, it was noticed that a main rotor blade tie down tip was broken. The pilot reported that the blade tip may have contacted a cedar sapling, while the aircraft was settling in the snow. This was confirmed with a follow-up visit to the site, where a cedar sapling showed signs of rotor contact. The operator’s maintenance further inspected the helicopter and replaced the tip cap. No other damage was found on the aircraft. Company operations discussed clearing of the landing sites with the client.

C-GPTL, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 aircraft operated by Yellowhead Helicopters, was conducting external load operations at Mount Sheba, BC. When the external load was placed on the ground, the pilot pushed the wrong button and inadvertently released the belly hook, rather than the remote hook. The long line and clevis assembly fell approximately 90 feet. There were no injuries. The operator’s SMS documented the occurrence.

C-GKQI un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par Porter Airlines, effectuait le vol POE450 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination de Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City, ON avec 4 membres d'équipage et 32 passagers à bord. Alors que l'appareil était sur la montée initiale suite au décollage de la piste 24L à CYUL, l'équipage de conduite a reçu une indication à l’effet qu’une des portes du train d'atterrissage principal était demeurée ouverte. La liste de vérification applicable a été suivie, et l'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence avant de revenir atterrir à CYUL sans autres incidents. Personne n’a été blessé et l'appareil n'a subi aucun dommage.

C-FEAI un DHC-8-300 exploité par Air Inuit sous l'indicatif de vol AIE832 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau intl (CYUL), Québec, à destination de Québec/Jean-Lesage intl, Québec. Alors que l'appareil était en montée environ 10 miles nautiques au nord de CYUL, l'équipage de conduite a noté une indication de basse pression d'huile du moteur droit (PW123B). L'hélice du moteur a été mise en drapeau tel que requis par la liste de vérification applicable. L'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence (PAN PAN) et est revenu atterrir à CYUL sans problème.

C-GMSY, a Learjet 45 aircraft operated by Skyservice Business Aviation, was conducting a medevac flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Metropolitan Oakland Intl (KOAK), CA. During cruise flight approximately 80 minutes from KOAK, the flight crew received a R FUEL PRESSURE LOW CAS message, and the associated engine started to spool down. The flight crew followed the checklist and, when the right standby fuel pump was switched on, the fuel flow returned to normal and the engine ran normally. The aircraft continued to KOAK, and an emergency was declared as a precaution. The aircraft landed uneventfully; maintenance is investigating.

C-GGAH, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA8712 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC. Lors de son contact radio initial, l'équipage de conduite a indiqué qu'il était en descente jusqu’à 8000 pieds. L’ATC a observé JZA8712 à 7600 pieds et, après avoir questionné l’équipage sur son altitude, JZA8712 est remonté à 8000 pieds, invoquant un ennui technique qui a causé cette erreur de navigation. Conséquemment, l'espacement avec C-GLQP, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par Porter Airlines et effectuant le vol POE514 de CYQB vers Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON, a été réduit à 0.9 mile sur le plan latéral et 700 pieds sur le plan vertical, alors que la norme est de 3 miles ou 1000 pieds.

C-GTQF, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC943 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 8 crew members and 189 passengers on board. As the aircraft was passing 12 000 feet during the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from KFLL, the flight crew received a master caution warning associated with a BLEED TRIP OFF light on the number 2 engine, followed seconds later by an overheat indication for the same engine. The flight crew levelled off at 15 000 feet and declared an emergency. While performing the procedure for the engine overheat, the light extinguished; the flight crew elected to keep the engine at idle. The remainder of the checklist items were carried out, the aircraft returned at KFLL and landed overweight with ARFF standing by. The aircraft stopped on the runway and, after the flight crew shut the number 2 engine down, ARFF proceeded to inspect it. Subsequently, the aircraft was towed to the gate due to hot brakes.The operator’s maintenance found the number 2 engine duct supply from the 5th stage not secured correctly to the compressor case. The left hand side C duct & insulation were also found damaged.

C-FSCY, a Boeing 737-8 MAX aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1049 from Palm Springs Intl (KPSP), CA to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. During the takeoff roll on Runway 31L at KPSP, the flight crew received a Master Caution Light for the FWD Entry Door. At an indicated airspeed of approximately 110 kts, the flight crew rejected the takeoff, brought the aircraft to a full stop, declared a PAN PAN, and exited the runway. A flight attendant confirmed that the door appeared to be properly closed and locked. A brake inspection was done by a safety vehicle, and maintenance personnel inspected once the brakes cooled.

C-FSNQ, a Boeing 737-8 MAX aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA517 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Honolulu/Daniel K Inouye Intl (PHNL), HI. During cruise flight, continuous light turbulence was encountered as expected. Shortly after, flight conditions worsened to continuous moderate turbulence at FL360. As the flight subsequently encountered severe turbulence, a PAN PAN was declared, and the flight crew requested a lower altitude via Controller-Pilot Data Link Communications (CPDLC). The autopilot could not maintain the selected altitude or speed, as there were variations of at least +/- M.03 and +/- 500 feet observed. The aircraft descended to FL300 and continued to destination without further incident.

C-GMNL, un appareil de type Beech B100 King Air exploité par Max Aviation, effectuait le vol MAX180 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Waskaganish (CYKQ), QC à destination de Chibougamau/Chapais (CYMT), QC avec 2 pilotes et 6 passagers à bord. Lors de l'approche à CYMT, le train d'atterrissage n'est pas descendu lorsqu’activé. Le QRH a été activé, et une urgence a été déclarée. La procédure de sortie manuelle du train d’atterrissage a réussi, et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Le personnel de l’entretien a remis en service l'aéronef après avoir remplacé le moteur électrique du train d'atterrissage.

C-GKTA, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8408 from Kelowna (CYLW), BC to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 3 crew members and 13 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL230 approximately 115 nm south west of CYYC, the flight crew received a cabin pressure master warning light. The cabin altitude was at 12 500 feet and climbing; consequently, the flight crew initiated an emergency descent to 14 000 feet, and declared a PAN PAN. The QRH was executed, and the flight crew regained control of the cabin. Once the aircraft was clear of the mountains, the emergency was cancelled and the aircraft landed on Runway 35L without further incident. There were no injuries.The operator’s maintenance replaced the cabin pressure selector panel, and the cabin pressure controller in accordance with (IAW) the procedure. Functional pressurization check was performed IAW Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) 21-30-00. A test flight was completed and no faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKFR, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ100 aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7272 from Memphis Intl (KMEM), TN to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During the descent into CYYZ, both the captain's and co-pilot's airspeed and altitude became unreliable. The flight crew followed QRH procedures, and managed to recover the co-pilot's Flight Director (FD) and Flight Mode Annunciator (FMA). A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft proceeded to land using the co-pilot's instruments. ARFF was standing by for the landing. After fault verification, the operator’s maintenance replaced the number 1 Air Data Computer (ADC) and purged the pitot line. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-GURG, un appareil de type Bombardier CL600-2B16 Challenger 601-3R exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait le vol d'évacuation médicale QUE10 depuis Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC vert Gaspé (Michel Pouliot) (CYGP), QC avec 2 membres d’équipage et 2 passagers à bord. Lors de la sélection du train d'atterrissage en position rentrée après le départ de CYQB, un message WOW I/FAIL est apparu dans le cockpit et le train avant ne s'est pas rétracté. Une urgence a été déclarée, et l'appareil est revenu se poser à CYQB sans encombre. Le personnel de l’entretien a remis l'appareil en service après avoir remplacé un harnais électrique sur le train avant.

C-GUJZ, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA8792 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination de Saint John (CYSJ), NB avec 4 membres d'équipage et 66 passagers à bord. À environ 45 miles marins à l’est de CYUL alors que l'appareil était en montée à travers 16 000 pieds ASL, le personnel de cabine a observé de la fumée ainsi qu'une lueur rouge à l'arrière de la cafetière. L'utilisation d'un extincteur a permis de maitriser l’incendie. L'équipage de conduite a mis leur masque à oxygène, déclaré une urgence et demandé un retour vers CYUL où l'appareil s'est posé sans problème. L'appareil a circulé jusqu'à la passerelle, d'où les passagers ont pu débarquer normalement. Personne n'a été blessé et l'appareil n'a subi aucun dommage.

C-FSIP, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA205 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. During the descent into CYVR in icing conditions, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to the loss of the wing anti-ice system. The aircraft landed without further incident 9 minutes later.The operator’s maintenance found that when the wing anti-ice was selected on, the LEFT VALVE OPEN light illuminated. Trouble shooting was carried out, and the valve was satisfactorily tested using APU bleed air. The fault was determined to be intermittent.

C-GLXJ, a Piper PA-12 aircraft operated by Blue Sky Air, was conducting a flight from Manor, SK to Estevan (Blue Sky) (CBS2), SK with 1 pilot on board. During the takeoff roll from a farm field, the aircraft struck a snow drift, pitched forward, and came to a rest on its nose. The pilot was not injured, however the aircraft sustained substantial damage to the propeller, engine and engine cowling.

C-FTXW, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC089 from Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. Shortly after the departure, the flight crew received a HYD G RSVR LO LVL ECAM message. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, conducted an alternate landing gear extension, and landed at CYVR without further incident. The aircraft stopped on the runway and was towed to the gate.The operator’s maintenance found a loose B-nut on the green hydraulic system high pressure feed line, to the number 1 engine's thrust reverser hydraulic control unit. The B-nut was secured, the hydraulic reservoir was serviced, and an engine ground-run/leak check was carried out before the aircraft was returned to service. An SDR was submitted.

C-GHJP, a Sikorsky S-76A helicopter operated by Helijet International, was departing westbound from Pad 'C' at Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. VP-CNI, a privately operated Boeing MD87 aircraft, was conducting a flight from CYVR to Palm Springs Intl (KPSP), CA. As VP-CNI was departing off Runway 13 at CYVR, ATC issued a clearance to the flight crew of C-GHJP to cross Runway 13. The flight crew of C-GHJP queried ATC, and were subsequently instructed to hold short of the runway, to the east. A loss of wake turbulence separation occurred.

C-FNIZ, an Aerospatiale AS350 B3 aircraft operated by Canadian Helicopters, was conducting VFR helislinging operations approximately 30 nm west of Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC. During the final approach to the drill pad, the slung load (lumber) and long line released from the helicopter at an altitude of approximately 200 feet. An uneventful landing was completed at the heli-pad. A post flight inspection of the hook assembly by the pilot found that the outer sheath of the manual release cable was broken, and likely snagged on the electrical cable assembly to the hook as the load moved around during the flight. This likely caused the manual release to activate, resulting in the unintentional load release.

C-FSRJ, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8176 from Fort St. John (CYXJ), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 4 crew members on board. During the pre-flight preparation before passenger boarding, the flight crew attempted to start the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU). After a failed first attempt, a second attempt was made, and the flight crew received an APU Fire Bottle Low Pressure warning, along with an APU Fire Detection System warning. ARFF was requested to the aircraft, however no fire or smoke was visible when they arrived.The operator’s maintenance completed an inspection of the APU and its compartment, and no defects were noted. The APU was started, and function checks were carried out with no faults found. The aircraft was released back to service.

C-FHNC, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by North Cariboo Air, was conducting flight NCA4054 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Kirby Lake (CRL4), AB. Upon selection of landing gear up shortly after the departure from CYVR, the number 2 hydraulic pump light and the roll spoiler outboard hydraulic caution light illuminated. Additionally, the landing gear door amber lights illuminated, and the number 2 main hydraulic pressure read zero, while the quantity remained stable. The flight crew requested a return to CYVR, and accepted priority handling from ATC. The QRH checklist was executed, which resulted in the return of the hydraulic pressure with no caution lights. The flight returned to CYVR and performed a normal landing.

C-GPCI, a SAAB 340B aircraft operated by Pacific Coastal Airline, was conducting flight PCO3047 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies Intl (CYXC), BC with 3 crew members and 9 passengers on board. Approximately 54 nm south west of CYYC, the flight crew received a R BLD FAULT caution light. The QRH was executed, and it was determined that the right hand low pressure bleed valve had failed. The system was reset in flight and subsequently, the flight crew noticed an increase in cabin altitude approaching 9000 feet. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and requested a return to CYYC. During the descent, the crew elected to cancel the emergency, and completed an uneventful landing at CYYC. The operator’s maintenance replaced the R/H low pressure bleed air valve. The aircraft was released back into service.

C-FHMD, a privately operated Cessna 414A aircraft, was conducting a positioning flight from Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies Intl (CYXC), BC to Calgary/Springbank (CYBW), AB with only the pilot on board. During the final approach for Runway 17 at CYBW, the pilot heard a change in propeller sound for the right engine. A check of the engine instruments indicated that the oil pressure for the right engine (Teledyne Continental Motors TSIOL-550-A) was 0 PSI. The pilot proceeded to feather the right propeller, secured the engine, and declared an emergency. An uneventful single-engine approach and landing was completed.Maintenance personnel determined that the cause of the oil loss to be a worn bushing in the RH engine turbo charger.

C-FYJH, un appareil de type Airbus 319-114 exploité par Air Canada rouge, effectuait le vol ROU1745 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Samaná/El Catey Intl (MDCY), République Dominicaine et Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC avec 5 membres d'équipage et 134 passagers à bord. Alors que l'aéronef était en approche finale pour la piste 24R à CYUL, un message ECAM a avisé l'équipage de conduite d'une baisse du niveau de liquide hydraulique dans le système jaune. La liste de vérification applicable a été effectuée, et une urgence a été déclarée par précaution. Un atterrissage sans encombre a suivi. Le personnel de l’entretien de l’exploitant a trouvé une ligne hydraulique perforée suite au frottement. La ligne hydraulique a été réparée, et l'appareil fût remis en service.

C-FNAZ, a British Aerospace Jetstream 32 aircraft operated by Northwestern Air Lease, was conducting flight PLR599 from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Fort Smith (CYSM), NT with 2 crew members and 14 passengers on board. Approximately 100 nm south of CYSM, the flight crew established the first radio contact with CYSM’s Community Aerodrome Radio Station (CARS). The CARS operator advised PLR599 of the current weather, and the flight crew gave their Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA). The CARS operator then proceeded to advised Truck 80 (TK80), which was clearing snow on Runway 12/30, of the inbound traffic and provided its ETA. Approximately 28 nm south of CYSM, the CARS operator passed the aerodrome information and ground equipment traffic on the runway to PLR599. Upon entering the zone, the flight crew of PLR599 did not make a radio call, nor did they advised that they were on final approach for Runway 30. When the CARS operator realized that the aircraft was landing, they advised TK80 of the situation. TK80 saw PLR599’s landing lights behind him, and quickly proceeded to the equipment turn off loop near the threshold for Runway 12. TK80 then radioed that they were clear of all maneuvering areas. PLR599 landed on Runway 30 while TK80 was still on the runway.

N626CZ, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 aircraft operated by Compass Airlines, was conducting flight CPZ5762 from Seattle-Tacoma Intl (KSEA), WA to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. When CPZ5762 was inbound for Runway 29 via the IGVEP4 arrival at CYYC, the aircraft was observed to have closed the base leg segment from TEXIT to HENRI. CPZ5762 was then instructed to turn east, and to stop the descent at 7000 feet. C-GWGA, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7218 from Lethbridge (CYQL), AB to CYYC. GGN7218 was established on final approach for Runway 29 east of HENRI, and was instructed to descend to 6000 feet immediately. A loss of separation occurred when the lateral separation eroded to 2.5 nm laterally by the time a vertical separation of 1000 feet was established. The required separation was 3.0 nm lateral or 1000 feet vertical.

C-GTWS, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA428 from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. N572FX, a privately operated Bombardier BD-100-1A10 Challenger 350 aircraft, was conducting flight LXJ572 from Washington Dulles Intl (KIAD), VA to CYYZ. When both aircraft were being vectored for the landing at CYYZ, a loss of separation occurred approximately 11 nm south west of the airport. The separation between the 2 aircraft eroded to 100 feet vertically and 2.5 nm laterally, where 1000 feet or 3 nm is required. Both aircraft landed uneventfully and there was no operational impact.

N414YX, an Embraer ERJ 170-200LR aircraft operated by Republic Airlines, was conducting flight RPA4664 from New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During the approach at CYYZ, the flight crew declared an emergency due to a nose wheel steering fault. QRH procedures were carried out, and the aircraft landed uneventfully on Runway 23 with ARFF standing by.

C-FKJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 CRJ900 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA575 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. As the flight crew was authorized down to 9000 feet during the initial approach at CYVR, a Traffic Collision and Alerting System (TCAS) Resolution Advisory (RA) was received. The flight crew climbed 500 feet, and initiated a 20 degree turn to the left in response to a fast climbing Cessna 525B, registration C-GTSX, on departure from CYVR that was levelling off 1000 feet below. ATC relayed the traffic information to the flight crew after they had initiated the climb. The aircraft continued to destination without further incident.

C-FWEP, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3125 from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Kelowna (CYLW), BC. During the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from CYEG, the flight crew observed several caution messages related to various electrical systems, and observed a dual AC generator failure. The fight crew declared a PAN PAN, and executed the appropriate QRH checklists. Following the QRH checklist completion, the R TRU, PITOT HEAT 2, ENG ADAPT 2, DE ICE PRESS, and PUSHER SYST FAIL caution lights remained illuminated. The operator’s operational and maintenance control centres were consulted. As the aircraft de-icing systems were no longer functional due to the AC system failure, the flight crew decided to divert to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB where the aircraft landed without further incident. Upon inspection, the operator's maintenance found evidence of arching from a 115 Volt, 3-phase AC supply feeder in the RH wheel well at the AC Contactor Box, connector plug assembly (2421-P5-2).

C-GARG, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA295 from Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. As the aircraft had just started the descent approximately 120 nm east northeast of CYVR, the flight crew declared an emergency due to compressor stalls on the number 2 engine (CFM56-5A5). The flight crew executed the QRH, stabilized the affected engine, and continued to destination without further incident with the engine at idle.The operator’s maintenance replaced the Hydro Mechanical Unit (HMU), the fuel pump and the high pressure bleed valve. A high power run was completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FYJD, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG326 from Regina Intl (CYQR), SK to Punta Cana Intl (MDPC), Dominican Republic with 6 crew members and 187 passengers on board. Passing 2500 feet ASL as the aircraft was on final approach for Runway 08 at MDPC, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to LEVEL OFF, followed immediately by an RA to CLIMB. The conflicting traffic was a helicopter that was tracking towards SWG326, outbound from the field and approximately on the runway track. The flight crew executed the command, executed a missed approach, and returned for an uneventful landing.

C-GBHM, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA152 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During cruise flight at FL370, the flight crew received an LGCIU 1 & 2 FAIL ECAM message. The flight continued to destination and, on approach to CYYZ, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and extended the landing gear using the manual gear extension system. Additionally, the flight crew requested to be towed off the runway after landing. The aircraft landed without further incident on Runway 05 with ARFF standing by, and stopped on Taxiway E for inspection. Once ARFF released the aircraft, it was towed to the gate.

C-GONX, a de Havilland DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8282 from Timmins (Victor M. Power) (CYTS), ON to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. As the flight crew selected landing gear up after becoming airborne from CYTS, the right main landing gear did not retract. After consulting with the operator’s Operational Control Centre, the flight crew was provided with new fuel calculations for the flight at a lower airspeed and altitude, and the decision to continue to CYYZ with the right main landing gear extended was elected. Approaching CYYZ, the flight crew requested ARFF to be on standby for the landing. The aircraft landed uneventfully, and taxied to the gate. The operator’s maintenance determined that the landing gear pin had not been removed prior to the flight.

C-FRSE, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA85 from Tel Aviv/Ben Gurion (LLBG), Israel to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During cruise flight, the flight crew received a main landing gear low tire pressure indication. The flight continued to CYYZ and, during the descent, the flight crew requested ARFF on stand by to meet the aircraft upon landing. The aircraft landed uneventfully and stopped on the high-speed taxiway, waiting for maintenance to inspect aircraft. The operator’s maintenance found one tire deflated, and replaced both tires before allowing the aircraft to proceed to the gate.

C-FGKJ, a Boeing 757-200 aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways, was conducting flight CJT618 from Greater Moncton/Romeo Leblanc Intl (CYQM), NB to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. C-GORZ, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Services, was conducting flight EVS776 from Fredericton Intl (CYFC), NB to CYHZ. ATC had cleared CJT618 to land on Runway 23, while simultaneously clearing EVS776 to land on Runway 14 behind CJT618. The required 3 miles separation in a control zone was not met, as the 2 aircraft closed in to just over 1 mile separation. There was no risk of collision.

C-GZSG, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1245 from Tampa Intl (KTPA), FL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During the flight, the flight crew received a STAB OUT OF TRIM annunciator light. QRH procedures were executed, and the flight crew continued to CYYZ. Passing FL210 during the arrival sequence, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN as they entered Toronto Centre (CZYZ) airspace. The aircraft continued for an uneventful landing with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance replaced the Stabilizer Trim Motor, and the aircraft was returned to service after a successful test of the system.

C-FWVJ, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1791, from Las Vegas/McCarran Intl (KLAS), NV to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. During the top of descent, the first officer told the pilot-in-command (PIC) that he was not feeling well. A nurse, travelling as a passenger on board, assessed the first officer, and assisted the crew in administering oxygen as a precaution. The PIC declared an emergency, and the flight landed shortly thereafter at CYVR. Emergency Medical Services (EMS) met the aircraft to assess the first officer, and released him after the assessment.

C-GSJB, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1734 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Liberia/Daniel Oduber Qui Intl (MRLB), Costa Rica. As the aircraft was climbing out after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew received an ECAM message for a Blue Hydraulic System fluid leak. The aircraft was levelled off at 16 000 feet, the flight crew executed the QRH procedures and consulted with the operator’s Operational Control Centre; the decision was made to return to CYYZ. Out of precaution, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN, the aircraft landed overweight and taxied to the gate under its own power. The operator’s maintenance found a leak on a blue hydraulic system line, which powers the left hand aileron. The line was replaced, and an overweight landing inspection was carried out before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GAWS, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1722, from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Palm Springs Intl (KPSP), CA. As the aircraft was being pushed back from Gate E83 at CYVR during the departure procedure, it collided with a catering vehicle. The vehicle, which was parked within the safety area at Gate E83, was taller than prescribed limitations. ARFF responded and confirmed that there was no fire, and no fluid leaks. The aircraft sustained minor damage to the port side winglet, and was removed from service. There were no injuries, and passengers were deplaned into the boarding lounge until service was continued aboard an alternate aircraft.

On 03 January 2019, a WestJet Encore Bombardier DHC-8-402 (Q400) aircraft (registration C-FSWE, serial number 4517), operating as flight 3109 (WEN3109), was conducting an instrument flight rules flight from Calgary International Airport, Alberta, to Nanaimo Airport, British Columbia. At about the same time, a privately registered Piaggio P.180 aircraft (registration N990RS, serial number 1015) operated by Rainbow Sandals Retail Incorporated, was conducting an instrument flight rules flight from Spokane International Airport, Washington, United States, to Kamloops Airport, British Columbia.The Q400 was flying in a southwesterly direction from the northeast of Kelowna, British Columbia. The Piaggio was flying in a north-northwesterly direction from the south of Kelowna. Both aircraft were operating at flight level 220, and their flight paths would cross to the west of Kelowna.At 1021:11 Pacific Standard Time, when the aircraft were west of Kelowna, a loss of separation occurred when the required vertical separation minimum of 1000 feet or lateral separation minimum of 5 nautical miles was not maintained. At that time, the aircraft were at the same altitude and less than 5 nautical miles from each other on converging tracks. At 1021:20, the Q400 flight crew received and responded to a traffic alert and collision avoidance system resolution advisory to descend. At approximately the same time, the Piaggio P.180 received a traffic advisory. At 1021:49, there was 1000 feet of vertical separation and 0.9 nautical miles of lateral separation between the 2 aircraft. Both flights continued to their destinations without further incident.

C-FSRY, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8065 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC. When the landing gear was selected up after the departure from CYVR, the landing gear handle illuminated and the flight crew received a LANDING GEAR INOP caution light. The flight crew then selected the landing gear down, and received three green lights and an amber light on the nose landing gear door. The LANDING GEAR INOP light remained on. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and returned to CYVR where the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced the Proximity Sensor Electronic Unit (PSEU), performed gear swings, and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FLHJ, a Boeing 737-400 aircraft operated by Flair Airlines, was conducting flight FLE613 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB. As the flight crew expected turbulence passing FL310 during the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from CYVR, the FASTEN SEAT BELT sign was turned on and the captain instructed the cabin crew to be seated. Shortly thereafter when the aircraft was on autopilot, the aircraft pitched up 20° and the airspeed increased by 40 kts. The aircraft rolled 45° to the right, which required full left aileron deflection, then rolled 30° to the left, which was corrected with full right aileron deflection. The VSI displayed a speed of over 6000 fpm up. After a subsequent loss of 25 KIAS, the aircraft levelled off at FL350 with significant ongoing buffeting. The flight crew elected to leave the autopilot on the whole time, and let it make the corrections. There were no injuries; however, 14 passengers became ill as a result of the turbulence.The operator reported that the autopilot performed adequately, did not disengage throughout the event, and that no aircraft limitations were exceeded. An SMS report was filed.

C-GWJK, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3428 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to St John's Intl (CYYT), NL. Upon selection of landing gear up shortly after the takeoff, the nose landing gear failed to retract. The flight crew declared an emergency, and performed a low approach for a visual inspection by the control tower. Following a holding of approximately 1 hour to burn fuel, the aircraft landed without incident at CYHZ. The flight crew was able to taxi the aircraft to the gate under its own power. The operator’s maintenance determined that the rigging for the NGLK1 and NGLK2 sensors needed to be reset. A gear swing was completed, and the aircraft released to service.

C-FIYA, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1980 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to México City/Benito Juárez Intl (MMMX), México. Prior to the landing at MMMX, the flight crew was instructed to enter a hold in the vicinity of enroute waypoint PIVOL, approximately 90 nm north east of MMMX. During the hold, a flight crew member became ill and was unable to continue flight duties. The remaining flight crew member continued to operate the aircraft, and landed at destination without further incident.

C-FNNW, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA871 from Paris/Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. During cruise flight, 4 cabin crew members sustained minor injuries when the aircraft encountered moderate turbulence. 2 of them did not continue with duties. Duties were redistributed to the remaining cabin crew members. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GMWT, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG875 from Opapimiskan Lake (CKM8), ON to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON. Climbing through 9000 feet approximately 210 nm north of CYQT, the flight crew noticed that the number 2 engine (PW123B) oil pressure was indicating 50 PSIG. After consulting the QRH, the flight crew declared an emergency and carried out a precautionary engine shutdown. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYQT with ARFF on standby.  The operator's maintenance replaced the number 2 engine oil pressure transmitter, and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FOER, a de Havilland DHC-2T MK. III aircraft operated by the Ministry of Natural Resources of the Province of Ontario, was conducting touch and go’s on Runway 28 at Timmins (Victor M. Power) (CYTS), ON. The pilot advised the FSS that they would come to a full stop prior to the intersection of Runway 03/21, in order to accommodate other traffic. During the landing roll, the aircraft nosed over momentarily, and the propeller contacted the runway several times. As the aircraft dropped back onto its tail wheel, the impact was sufficient to activate the ELT. The pilot was not injured, and requested to be towed to the ramp. The ELT was manually turned off. The operator’s maintenance reported serious damage to the propeller, engine and empennage.

C-GKOE, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA261 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. Shortly after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew reported a plastic burning odour in the aft galley. The flight crew declared an emergency, and diverted back to CYYZ. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. After the aircraft was cleared by ARFF, the flight crew taxied back to the gate where passengers deplaned.

VQ-BQB, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Aeroflot Russian Airlines, was conducting flight AFL100 from Moscow/Sheremetyevo Intl (UUEE), Russia to New York/John F. Kennedy Intl (KJFK), NY. N613FE, a McDonnell Douglas MD-11F aircraft operated by Federal Express, was conducting flight FDX9001 from Memphis Intl (KMEM), TN to Cologne-Bonn/Konrad Adenauer (EDDK), Germany. At approximate position 56°13' N / 044°08' W, AFL100 descended from FL300 to FL280 without a clearance. Opposing traffic was FDX9001 at FL290. Since the 2 aircraft did not establish the required vertical separation for 15 minutes before and after crossing tracks, a loss of separation occurred.

C-GWSZ, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA391 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB. During the takeoff roll at CYHZ, the flight crew noticed fumes and smoke on the flight deck. The flight crew rejected the takeoff, and stopped the aircraft on the runway. ARFF was requested once the aircraft came to a full stop. After the aircraft was assessed, the flight crew taxied to the gate. The operator’s maintenance suspected that deice fluid was ingested before the takeoff. The aircraft was thoroughly inspected, and released back to service.

C-FHOY, an Embraer ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA501 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Chicago/O'Hare Intl (KORD), IL. During the short final phase of the approach at KORD, the flight crew executed a missed approach due to a WING ANTI ICE FAIL EICAS message, and climbed to 3000 feet. The QRH was actioned, however the message would not clear. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft positioned for another approach. On landing, the aircraft appeared to be free of any ice accretion. The operator’s maintenance was advised.

C-GBZS, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing, was conducting flight SWG516 from Cancún Intl (MMUN), Mexico to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During cruise flight approximately 80 nm west of Tampa Intl (KTPA), FL, heavy smoke came out and flames were observed inside the aft number 2 oven. A few seconds later, the flames self-extinguished. Food debris and burnt grease were found on the racks. The smoke in the galley lasted approximately 20 seconds. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FWGH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG783 from Río Hato/Scarlett Martínez Intl (MPSM), Panamá to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During cruise flight at FL360 in the vicinity of Cayo Largo/Vilo Acuña Intl (MUCL), Cuba, the flight crew received a TCAS TA, and an aircraft was seen climbing towards them. Subsequently, a TCAS RA – CLIMB sounded seconds later, which was immediately complied with by the flight crew up to FL366, until clear of conflict. SWG783 then continued to destination uneventfully. The conflicting traffic was observed to be as close as 400 feet below on TCAS, and had been cleared to FL350 by Havana Center; however, it continued the climb through FL350. ATC reported that the aircraft involved was a Falcon 900EX, registration YV2486.

C-GUJA, un appareil de type Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA8512 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Charlottetown (CYYG), PE, à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC avec 3 membres d’équipage et 49 passagers à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage sur la piste 06L à CYUL, l’ATC a donné l’instruction à l’équipage de conduite de sortir sur la voie de circulation B1. Bien que l'instruction ait été relue correctement, le pilote aux commandes a dirigé l'appareil vers la voie de circulation Echo, qui était fermée par NOTAM. Lorsqu'il s’est aperçu de l’erreur, le pilote aux commandes a appliqué les freins avec l’intention de ramener l’appareil sur la piste 06L. Toutefois, une couche de glace recouvrait le sol à l'intérieur de la zone protégée sur la voie de circulation Echo, ce qui a empêché l’appareil de freiner efficacement et de tourner. L’appareil a terminé sa course sur le gazon. La piste 06L a été fermée temporairement afin de permettre le remorquage. L’appareil n’a pas subi de dommage au train d’atterrissage, et personne n’a été blessé.

C-GPCW, a Beech 1900C aircraft operated by Pacific Coastal Airlines, was conducting flight PCO750 from Campbell River (CYBL), BC to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 2 pilots and 2 passengers on board. During the take-off roll, some water dripped from the cockpit ceiling, in close proximity of the compass. Prior to levelling out at 7000 feet after climb-out in instrument meteorological conditions, the instrument panel lighting and the side panel lighting were flickering on and off. The flight crew noted a very strong smell of electrical smoke. An emergency was declared, and the flight crew elected to divert to Comox (CYQQ), BC where an uneventful landing was made. During the taxi after the landing, the flight crew smelled electrical burning again; however, no smoke was visible. There were no popped circuit breakers.The operator’s maintenance found indication of water ingress through the left hand windshield retention screws, behind the standby compass cover. The windshield screws were torque checked, and tightened as required. Maintenance personnel could not duplicate the flickering panel lights, or the electrical burning smell. No damage was found.

C-FRYV, a Boeing 737-8 MAX aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA2245 from Puerto Vallarta/Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz Intl (MMPR), Mexico to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. During cruise flight, a flight attendant experienced a medical incident and became incapacitated. The associated duties were distributed to the remaining flight attendants for the landing. The aircraft landed without further incident, and medical assistance was awaiting at the gate.

C-FOQH, an AS350B2 helicopter operated by Blackcomb Helicopters, with only the pilot on board, was landing at the Lizzie Bay log sort near Lillooet Lake, BC in order to pick up a group of back country skiers to be flown to the Lizzie Lake hut. The landing area was covered with a few inches of fresh snow and the weather included low cloud, light snow, and flat light. Just prior to the skids touching down, the tail rotor struck a low snow-covered berm. The helicopter yawed 90 degrees but remained upright. There were no injuries, however the tail rotor, tail rotor gear box, tail rotor drive shaft, and tail boom were substantially damaged.

C-FLSS, an Air Canada Airbus A320-211, was operating as flight ACA223 from Calgary, AB (CYYC) to Vancouver Intl (CYVR). During cruise, approximately 150 nm SW of CYYC, a flight attendant reported that flames were visible from the exhaust of the # 1 engine (CFM International, CFM56-5A1). The flight crew actioned the QRH and shut down the # 1 engine. A PAN PAN was declared and the flight returned to CYYC and landed uneventfully. Company maintenance replaced the #1 engine hydromechanical unit (HMU) and fuel pump.

C-FOEN, a WestJet Encore de Havilland DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3307 from Fort Saint John, BC (CYXJ) to Calgary, AB (CYYC). During departure from CYXJ, the flight crew received caution lights and indications that the nose landing gear did not retract. The flight crew actioned the QRH and continued to CYYC. During descent the flight crew declared a PAN PAN. WEN3307 landed uneventfully. At the gate maintenance found the nose landing gear ground lock was in the extended (activated) position.

C-FDST, an Airbus A320-211 operating as Air Canada flight AC557 from Los Angeles, USA (KLAX) to Vancouver, BC (CYVR) was taxiing to the gate when flames were observed from the right main landing gear. ARFF was notified, and at the gate it was found that the parts of the right main landing gear brake assembly were missing. Airport operations found parts on the runway and taxiway. Company maintenance replaced the brake and wheel assemblies and the tachometer. Maintenance opened an investigation.

C-GGNY, a de Havilland DHC-8-400, operating as Jazz flight JZA8421 from Kelowna, BC (CYLW) to Vancouver, BC (CYVR), had arrived at the gate and was shutting down the #2 engine when the crew received a smoke master warning light from the aft cargo compartment. The crew discharged the fire bottles and called for fire trucks to assess the situation. The baggage was unloaded and the compartment was inspected but no indication of fire was found. Maintenance replaced the high and low rate pressure fire bottles and tested the aft baggage compartment detector circuit system. No fault was found and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GMWT, a de Havilland DHC-8-314 operated by Wasaya Airways operating as flight WSG884, departed Opapimiskan Lake (CKM8), ON for Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON. At approximately 60 north west of CYQT, the flight crew declared an emergency due to #2 hydraulic system depletion. The crew carried out a manual gear extension and landed uneventfully on Runway 07 at CYQT with ARFF on standby. The aircraft stopped on the runway and was shut down. Landing gear safety pins were installed, passengers were debriefed by the captain and the aircraft was towed to the terminal. The operator's maintenance found the #2 pressure line from the rudder pressure regulator was leaking; the line was replaced.

C-GBIM, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1779 from Cozumel Intl (MMCZ), Mexico to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 5 crew members and 78 passengers on board. Approximately 1 hour after the departure from MMCZ at FL370, a cabin crew member sustained a minor injury, and was unable to continue duties. A doctor travelling as a passenger attended to the crew member, and the flight continued to destination where Emergency Medical Services met the aircraft on arrival.The cabin crew member was admitted to the hospital and was released shortly after.

C-GHLQ, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1806 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to San José/Juan Santamaría Intl (MROC), Costa Rica with 8 crew members and 282 passengers on board. Less than 2 hours after the departure from CYYZ, a cabin crew member felt ill and was unable to continue duties. The flight continued to destination without further incident.The operator is following up on the condition of the cabin crew member.

C-FDSU, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA794 from Los Angeles Intl (KLAX), CA to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 5 crew members and 134 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from KLAX, the flight crew received an AFT EMERGENCY EXIT OPEN / MAXIMUM ALTITUDE 10000 ft ECAM message. The flight crew stopped the climb at 10 300 feet, declared a PAN PAN, and returned to KLAX where they landed overweight without further incident.The operator’s maintenance is investigating the cause.

C-FPDN, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA7055 from Phoenix/Sky Harbor Intl (KPHX), AZ to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with only the 2 flight crew members on board. During cruise flight at FL360, the flight crew received a PACK 1 + 2 FAULT ECAM message. The flight crew initiated a precautionary descent to 14 000 feet, declared a PAN PAN, and diverted the aircraft to Las Vegas/McCarran Intl (KLAS), NV where it landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance is investigating. The aircraft experienced a similar event the previous day, and had diverted to KPHX on its way from Mexico to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB (TSB occurrence A18F0297).

C-FDRH, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA717 from New York/LaGuardia (KLGA), NY to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During the flight, the flight crew noticed a depletion of the green hydraulic system fluid. Several green hydraulic powered systems were lost, including the nose wheel steering. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and requested Runway 33R for the landing. The aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. The aircraft stopped on the runway, and was towed to the gate due to the inoperative nose wheel steering.

C-GKEM, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7335 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Nashville Intl (KBNA), TN with 3 crew members and 46 passengers on board. During the approach at KBNA, the flight crew experienced a GEAR DISAGREE message as the nose landing gear indicated that it was not down and locked. The approach was interrupted, an emergency was declared, and the flight crew cycled the landing gear as per the QRH; however, it was unsuccessful. Subsequently, a manual release was executed, and a green indication was achieved. The flight crew performed a fly-past inspection by the control tower, and returned for a landing without further incident. ARFF followed the aircraft to the gate.The aircraft could not be flown back to CYYZ with the gear down due to known or forecasted icing conditions. Following an inspection by maintenance personnel, the aircraft was repositioned under MEL provision to Covington/Cincinnati-Northern Kentucky Intl (KCVG), KY for repairs.

C-GKGC, an Air Georgian Ltd. Bombardier CL-600-2B19 aircraft (GGN7349), was on route from Charlotte, NC (KCLT) to Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) and climbing through FL240 when the crew received a FLAPS FAIL message. The crew declared a PAN PAN and continued to CYYZ. The aircraft performed an uneventful flapless landing at CYYZ with ARFF standing by. Maintenance found a fault with the left Brake/Position Sensor Unit. The unit was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

N817SK, a Bombardier CRJ900 operated by SkyWest Airlines, was operating flight SKW4981 on a re-positioning flight with flight crew only from Minneapolis-Saint Paul Intl/Wold-Chamberlain Field (KMSP), MN. to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK. At approximately 25 nautical miles south east of CYXE, the flight crew received a "Smoke Aft lavatory" warning message. The flight crew was unable to verify if there was smoke and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed uneventfully in CYXE with ARFF on standby. After the aircraft came to a stop, ARFF indicated there were no signs of smoke or fire visible from the outside of the aircraft and a visual inspection of the aft lavatory by a flight crew member found no evidence of smoke. The aircraft taxied to the gate where ARFF boarded the aircraft and conducted an inspection. No signs of smoke or fire were found.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft, the aft lavatory, and smoke detector and were unable to duplicate the fault. Aircraft was returned to service.

C-FLEJ, a Boeing 737-400 aircraft operated by Flair Airlines, was conducting flight FLE137 from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 6 crew members and 118 passengers on board. As the aircraft was descending through 15 000 feet approximately 49 nm north east of CYVR, severe turbulence was encountered. The autopilot disconnected unintentionally, the aircraft entered an abrupt left bank of approximately 30 degrees, and a nose-down attitude of 8 degrees was also noted before control was regained by the flight crew. The flight continued to CYVR without further incident. There were no injures.

The Air Canada Airbus A320-211, C-FDCA, was operating as flight ACA244 from Vancouver, BC (CYVR) to Edmonton, AB (CYEG). During cruise, approximately 80 nm SW of CYEG the flight crew reduced engine power in anticipation of mountain wave turbulence. After the turbulence subsided, the flight crew increased engine power and Engine 1 (CFM International, CFM56-5A1) was observed running roughly. Engine 1 power was reduced to idle and the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and requested priority to descend. After descent, with all engine indications normal, the number 1 engine power was increased to 50%. ACA244 continued to land uneventfully and met by ARFF.

C-FNXN, un appareil de type DHC8-314 exploité par Air Creebec, effectuait le vol CRQ534 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, de l'aéroport de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC) à destination de l'aéroport de Mont-Joli, QC (CYYY) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 12 passagers à bord. Après l'embarquement des passagers, alors que les moteurs n'étaient pas encore en marche, la nacelle du véhicule qui appliquait le liquide de déglaçage a heurté une pale de l'hélice gauche. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-FENU, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3428 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL. During cruise flight, the flight crew noted the loss of fluid quantity on the number 1 hydraulic system. During the approach, the flaps operated normally, however during the landing roll on Runway 16 at CYYT, the flight crew received a number 1 ISO VALVE indication. Additionally, anti-skid braking was not available. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN as a precaution, and the aircraft stopped without further incident on the runway. After approximately 5 minutes, the aircraft taxied clear of the runway, and was towed to the gate.

C-GLEM, a privately operated Piaggio P-180 Avanti, departed Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto  (CYYZ) destined for the Montreal Saint-Hubert Longueuil Airport (CYHU). Shortly after departure the right engine was shut down, due to an un-commanded feather of the propeller. The crew declared an emergency and returned to CYYZ. The aircraft landed uneventfully; there were no injuries. This issue was associated with the Beta Ring.

MTC 682, a maintenance vehicle was operating at Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) and was instructed by ATC to taxi onto VICTOR taxiway and hold short of Runway 33R. A short time later, ATC observed MTC 682 crossing Runway 33R and proceeding on ALPHA taxiway without a clearance. At the time of the runway crossing, a Boeing 777-300, operated by China Eastern Airlines as flight 207 was on final approach for the runway, 5.8 miles from the threshold.

C-FGRC, a de Havilland DHC-8-102, operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight 653 departed Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) for London, Ontario (CYXU). Shortly after take-off the flight crew informed ATC that they were returning, due to a smoke indication in the cockpit. The aircraft landed uneventfully and ARFF met the aircraft and escorted it to the gate. There were no injuries.

C-GIUB, an Airbus A321, operated by Air Canada, as flight AC453, was parked at the gate at Lester B. Pearson Intl Toronto (CYYZ) with passengers on board in preparation for a flight to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), when a fuel spill occurred below the right engine. ARFF was called and passengers were rapidly deplaned through the normal exit. There were no injuries.

C-FVLX, a Boeing 787-900 operated by Air Canada as flight AC792 was on the approach to Runway 23 at Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) when a hydraulic system failure occurred during flap selection. A missed approach was performed and a PAN PAN declared. The aircraft landed on Runway 33R uneventfully and was towed to the gate.

C-GZEH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC041 from Paris/Orly (LFPO), France to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with only 2 flight crew members on board. Just before the flight crew set take-off thrust at the start of the take-off roll, a thick white smoke filled the cockpit. The flight crew rejected the takeoff, and the smoke dissipated as soon as the power was brought back to idle. The aircraft exited the runway. The aircraft was on its first flight with Air Transat, and was on a positioning flight as it was being delivered to CYYZ. The previous operator’s maintenance had prepared the aircraft, and it was found that both engine oil levels were over-serviced. Both engine oil reservoirs were drained as per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM), and an idle run leak check was completed. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTXO, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC491 from Cancún Intl (MMUN), Mexico to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 6 crew members and 141 passengers on board. During cruise flight in the vicinity of Kansas City Intl (KMCI), MO, the flight encountered severe turbulence that resulted in a loss of 400 feet. The flight crew notified ATC, and returned to their assigned flight level once the aircraft regained stability. The flight continued to destination without further incident. There were no injuries to the passengers or crew members.The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft as per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM), and no faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GSAT, an Airbus 310-300 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC973 from Samana/El Catey Intl (MDCY), Dominican Republic to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 9 crew members and 234 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure, approximately 45 nm north-northwest of MDCY, the cabin crew detected a burning smell. After investigation, an identification card from what appears to be an airport personnel was found melted in one of the ovens of the rear galley. The card was removed, and the oven was inspected. The flight continued to destination without further incident.The operator’s maintenance inspected the oven and found no further defects.

C-FMZU, an Embraer 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA592 from Houston/George Bush Intercontinental (KIAH), TX to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 4 crew members and 65 passengers on board. Passing FL280 during the climb to cruising altitude, approximately 110 nm northeast of KIAH, the flight experienced continuous moderate turbulence. As the flight passed through FL300, the turbulence became severe and the flight crew observed the vertical speed in excess of 2500 feet per minute. A higher level was requested, however it was denied by ATC due to heavy traffic at FL320. The flight crew levelled off at FL310 in continuous moderate turbulence, and subsequently climbed to FL350 a short while later.The operator’s maintenance carried out a phase one inspection and found no faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBHM, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA202 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR) BC, to Calgary Intl (CYYC) AB, with 5 crew members and 111 passengers on board. During the takeoff roll at approximately 100 kts, the number 2 engine (CFM56-5A5) ingested a bird. The flight crew rejected the takeoff, shut the number 2 engine down, and returned to the gate without further incident. No emergency was declared.The operator’s maintenance found damage to 3 fan blades. The damaged fan blades and 1 acoustic panel in the engine inlet were replaced. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-GAQL, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA202 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 5 crew members and 110 passengers on board. During the departure from CYVR, the flight crew reported smoke and an odour in the flight deck. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight crew returned to CYVR without further incident. The operator’s maintenance was unable to find the source of the problem. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GMCP, a Bombardier Learjet 45 operated by Skyservice Business Aviation, was conducting flight 119397 from Keflavík (BIKF), Iceland to Goosebay (CYYR), NL with 5 crew members onboard. After takeoff and retraction of landing gear, the flight crew received a nose-wheel steering fail light, with the two main gear door lights indicating they have failed to close properly. After review of the associated emergency checklist and consultation with maintenance, it was determined that the nose wheel was likely off-centered. The flight crew declared an emergency, burned off fuel, and flew-by the air traffic control tower to confirm the nose wheel was not centered. The flight crew then proceeded with the approach, landed at BIKF safely, and shut down the aircraft on the runway. During the landing, the flight crew experienced minimal loss of directional control.Maintenance found the nose landing gear strut to be deflated, therefore, did not self-center after takeoff (when fully extended, the nose landing gear strut sits on the centering cam). There was no damage to the aircraft.

C-GUSC, un appareil de type British Aerospace Jetstream 32 exploité par Pascan, effectuait le vol PSC824 selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis Sept-Îles (CYZV), QC à destination de Mont-Joli (CYYY), QC avec 2 membres d’équipage et 12 passagers à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage sur la piste 24 recouverte de neige à 90% à CYYY, l’appareil s’est immobilisé légèrement passé le bout de la piste 24. Le pilote a réussi à faire demi-tour et circuler jusqu’à l’aérogare. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé, et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage.

C-GEWQ, un Dash-8-300 (DH8C) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8699, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Wabush, NL (CYWK) à destination de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) avec 31 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, l’appareil a subi une panne du système hydraulique numéro 2. L’équipage a poursuivi le vol à CYZV et a déclaré un état d’urgence. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre à CYZV avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) déployés. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage.

C-FTIQ, un appareil de type Aérospatiale ATR-42-500 exploité par First Air, effectuait le vol FAB882 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Iqaluit (CYFB), NU à destination d’Arctic Bay (CYAB), NU avec 3 membres d’équipage et 12 passagers à bord. Environ 120 miles marins au sud de Pond Inlet (CYIO), NU alors que l’appareil était en vol de croisière dans l’espace aérien non contrôlé au FL220, l’équipage a aperçu un avion sur une trajectoire convergente, et à la même altitude. À ce moment, un ATR-72 exploité par Calm Air sous l’indicatif CAV484, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis CYIO à destination de Hall Beach (CYUX), NU, et était aussi en croisière au FL220. L’équipage du FAB882 a allumé les phares d’atterrissage et, au même moment, l’équipage du CAV484 s’est rapporté en palier au FL220 sur la fréquence 126.7 MHz. L’équipage du FAB882 a perçu le trafic sur le TCAS à la même altitude, a débranché l’autopilote, et a amorcé une montée au FL229. Les appareils se sont croisés à environ 2 miles marins sur le plan latéral et 900 pieds sur le plan vertical. Il n’y a eu aucun dommage ni blessé.

C-FENO, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3369 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. Just before commencing the inflight cabin service, a cabin crew member experienced a medical event and was unable to perform their duties. The cabin crew member occupied a passenger seat for the remainder of the flight to CYYC.

G-CIVY, a Boeing 747-400 aircraft operated by British Airways, was conducting flight BAW273 from London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK to San Diego Intl (KSAN), CA. During cruise flight approximately 195 nm north-northwest of Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB, a cabin crew member suffered a medical condition, and was unable to perform their duties. The crew member received assistance via medlink and two medical professionals on board travelling as passengers. The flight crew elected to divert the aircraft to CYWG, where the crew member was transported to a hospital. The flight continued to KSAN after refueling.

C-GARG, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA553 from Los Angeles Intl (KLAX), CA to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB with 5 crew members and 110 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from KLAX at approximately 9700 feet ASL, the flight encountered severe wake turbulence from N834AA, a preceding Boeing 787 aircraft operated by American Airlines, conducting flight AAL181 from KLAX to Beijing/Capital (ZBAA), China. ACA553 experienced an uncommanded roll of 37° when the turbulence was encountered, as the lateral separation between the 2 aircraft was 1 minute and 44 seconds, or approximately 10 nm apart. The aircraft was at 9700 feet at that point, while AAL181 had passed through this area at approximately 10 100 feet. The seatbelt sign was on at the time, and there were no reported injuries. Forecast winds for the area were less than 10 knots, from the southwest.

C-FSNJ, a Piper PA-18-150 aircraft operated by Mackenzie Mountain Aviation, was conducting a flight from Muskwa Ranch, BC to a hunting camp at Richards Creek, BC. During the landing at Richards Creek with its Tundra tires, the aircraft overturned after contact with the snow. The spinner, propeller, and right wing struts were damaged, however neither occupants were injured. There was no fire, and the ELT did not activate. The occupants were picked up by a helicopter working nearby.

C-FEKD, un appareil de type Embraer 170-200 exploité par Sky Regional Airlines, effectuait le vol SKV7642 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination de New York/La Guardia (KLGA), NY avec 4 membres d’équipage et 58 passagers à bord. Alors que l’appareil était stationné à la barrière 81 à CYUL, un camion a accroché le bout de l’aile droite. Les dommages ont été limités au couvercle transparent du feu de navigation de l’aile. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FWEW, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3358 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. During the approach at CYYC, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and conducted a missed approach due to a landing gear indication. A manual extension was carried out, and the aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by.

N407UA, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL1299 from Houston/George Bush Intercontinental (KIAH), TX to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. During the approach for Runway 17L at CYYC, the flight crew conducted a missed approach due to a landing gear issue. Subsequently, an emergency was declared due to a hydraulic problem. The flight was vectored around for another approach to Runway 17L, and landed without further incident. The aircraft taxied off the runway under its own power. Maintenance personnel is investigating the hydraulic issue and will report back to the TSB.

C-GNRP, un appareil privé de construction amateur de type Wagaero Sport Trainer équipé de skis, effectuait un vol récréatif selon les règles de vol à vue depuis St-Donat (CSY4), QC à destination du Lac du Pin Rouge, QC, situé à 2 miles marins au nord de Saint-Hippolyte, QC, avec seul un pilote à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage sur la glace, l’appareil a glissé jusqu’au bout du lac et a percuté des arbres. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé, toutefois l’appareil a subi des dommages importants à l’aile droite.

C-GJZD, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8533 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON. Upon extension of the landing gear during the approach at CYQT, the flight crew did not receive a down & locked indication for the left main landing gear, on both the advisory panel and the alternate indicator on the floor. A missed approach was conducted, and the flight crew performed an alternate landing gear extension; however, it was unsuccessful. In accordance with the QRH, the landing gear was pumped down 30 to 50 times with no effect. The flight crew declared an emergency, shut the number 1 engine down as per the procedure, and requested ARFF in attendance. The cabin was prepared for an emergency landing, and passengers were briefed. The subsequent landing was conducted without further incident with the left engine inoperative. The aircraft was towed to the gate.The operator's maintenance replaced the Proximity Sensor Electronic Unit (PSEU), and repaired wiring at the landing gear down-lock. Landing gear swings were performed with no further faults.

On 12 December 2018, a Pacific Coastal Airlines Ltd. Beechcraft 1900C aircraft (registration C-GIPC, serial number UC 110), operating as flight PCO451, was on a scheduled flight from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), British Columbia (BC), to Trail Airport (CAD4), BC, with 2 flight crew members and 19 passengers on board. While the aircraft was conducting an approach to land southbound on Runway 16, an airport vehicle was travelling northbound on the runway, performing a runway inspection. When the aircraft touched down, the airport vehicle was still on the runway. The airport vehicle exited the runway onto the taxiway before the aircraft reached the runway/taxiway intersection, avoiding a collision. Radio communications had not been established between the aircraft and the airport vehicle. There were no injuries, and there was no damage to the aircraft.UPDATED: 12 MAY 2020

C-GXCA, un appareil de type Beech 1900D exploité par Chrono Aviation inc. sous l'indicatif de vol NDL191 a été autorisé à monter au FL240 au départ de Bagotville (QC) en direction nord-ouest à destination de Nemiscau QC derrière C-GODE, un appareil de type PC-12/47 exploité par Kudlik Aviation Inc sous l'indicatif de vol KUK707 qui était en palier au FL230 en direction nord en route de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean-Lesage Intl QC à destination de Kuujjuaq QC. Une perte d'espacement est survenue lorsque la distance entre les deux appareils a été réduite à 3,5 milles à la même altitude alors que la norme est de 5 mille ou 1000 pieds. L'espacement a été rétabli une minute après avoir été perdu.

C-GWBL, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA2057 from Cancún Intl (MMUN), Mexico to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. During cruise flight, a cabin crew member experienced a medical incident. The number 2 position duties were distributed to the remaining flight attendants for the remainder of the flight.

C-GEHS, a Beech King Air 200 aircraft operated by PAL Aerospace Ltd, was conducting MEDEVAC flight SPR810 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Yarmouth (CYQI), NS. When the landing gear was selected down during the approach at CYQI, the flight crew did not receive a nose landing gear down & lock indication. The decision to return to CYHZ was elected, and the flight crew declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYHZ with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance replaced the nose landing gear down lock indicator switch, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GNAO, a Beech B200C King Air aircraft operated by Northern Air Charter, was conducting flight NL1067 from Victoria Intl (CYYJ), BC to Abbotsford (CYXX), BC with 2 crew members and 5 passengers on board. While inbound to CYXX, the right engine fire warning light illuminated for approximately 5 minutes. There was no other indication of fire. The flight crew declared an emergency, and emergency vehicles were called out for standby. Just before the landing, the fire indication light extinguished. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYXX. Maintenance personnel could not duplicate the fault on the ground after troubleshooting. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FEIX, an Embraer 170-200 aircraft operated by Sky Regional Airlines, was conducting flight SKV7503 from Baltimore/Washington Intl Thurgood Marshall (KBWI), MD to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. While the engines were running after the push back from KBWI, a flight attendant smelled a burning odour coming from the galley ovens. The flight attendant advised the flight crew who contacted dispatch to advise that they were returning to the gate for a burning odour. The oven was turned off and the flight attendant discharged a fire extinguisher into the oven. The passengers were deplaned. Maintenance personnel came on board, and determined that there was paper found in the oven, which caused the smoke. After a conference call, it was decided to MEL the oven and re-board the passengers. Upon arrival at CYYZ, the oven was removed from the aircraft for further inspection. The aircraft was returned to service with a replacement oven.

C-FITW, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA015 from Toronto / Lester B. Pearson Int’l (CYYZ), ON to Hong Kong / Chek Lap Kok Int’l (VHHH), Hong Kong. During landing on runway 07R, the aircraft experienced a tail strike due to a hard landing, resulting in structural damage requiring a major repair. There were no injuries. The Hong Kong Air Accident Investigation Authority completed an investigation and issued report AAIA 05-2021 on 31st December 2021 (URL: https://www.thb.gov.hk/aaia/doc/Air%20Canada%20AC15%20Final%20Report%2028%20Dec21.pdf) with the following:5. Safety Recommendations Safety Recommendation 12-2021It is recommended that Air Canada consider recognition and awareness training for Pilot Induced Oscillation (PIO) during the training process, in particular as a component for pilots converting across type. [3.1 (9)]Safety Recommendation Owner: Air Canada Safety Recommendation 13-2021It is recommended that Air Canada consider awareness training for crew qualifying as IOETC to emphasise the requirement to monitor and recognise situations where the control of the aircraft may be compromised. This should also include guidance when the trainee is new to the type. (3.3.4)Safety Recommendation Owner: Air Canada Safety Recommendation 14-2021It is recommended that Air Canada consider reviewing and where necessary revise the unstabilised approach criteria and the requirements for a go around to be carried out, setting out the requirements in a clear and unambiguous format to avoid any confusion that flight crew may have in interpreting them and the crew actions required. [3.1 (4)]Safety Recommendation Owner: Air Canada Safety Recommendation 15-2021It is recommended that Air Canada consider reviewing and where necessary revise the formal handover of control criteria contained in the FOM incorporating the method when a pilot takes over control “I have control/you have control” setting out the requirements in a clear and unambiguous format to avoid any confusion that flight crew may have in interpreting them. (2.3.7)Safety Recommendation Owner: Air Canada  Safety Recommendation 16-2021It is recommended that Air Canada consider reviewing and where necessary revise the Sterile Flight Deck criteria contained in the FOM incorporating setting out the requirements in a clear and unambiguous format to avoid any confusion that flight crew may have in interpreting them. [3.1 (10)]Safety Recommendation Owner: Air Canada Safety Recommendation 17-2021It is recommended that Air Canada consider reviewing and where necessary revise the removal of loose objects from the flight deck policy, including eating utensils and beverage containers, before the top of descent setting out the requirements in a clear and unambiguous format to avoid any confusion that cabin and flight crew may have in interpreting them. (2.3.8)Safety Recommendation Owner: Air Canada Safety Recommendation 18-2021It is recommended that Air Canada consider incorporating policy and guidelines in the company manual suite regarding the reporting of potentially hazardous occurrences, for example a tail strike, to the relevant Air Traffic Services in the most expeditious manner setting out the requirements in a clear and unambiguous format to avoid any confusion that flight crew may have in interpreting them. [3.1 (11)]Safety Recommendation Owner: Air Canada 6. Safety Recommendations Already ImplementedOn receipt of the draft report Air Canada proactively addressed all the Safety Recommendations made and after review by the AAIA they are considered closed. Safety Recommendation 12-2021 Air Canada has designed a module on PIO in their Pilot Indoctrination Training course for new pilots, so that every new pilot is aware of this phenomenon.
