This will be implemented prior to their next course. Additionally, since currently some pilots may not be aware of this phenomenon information will be included on PIO in their next Annual Recurrent Training (ART) cycle to ensure all pilots will see this material over a 12-month period. Safety Recommendation 13-2021 Air Canada has amended their training manual with guidance for training captains on taking control early in appropriate situations and to be alert for students freezing in tense situations. The simulator training for training captains includes practical training on taking control from a student pilot. Scenarios are included where the student candidate (a check pilot or instructor in this case) will intentionally operate the aircraft in a manner that will necessitate the IOETC to take control of the aircraft. Safety Recommendation 14-2021Air Canada incorporated a new Stable Approach, Landing and Go-Around Policy into their FOM in September 2020 which defines crew tasks and responsibilities including guidance for the requirement of a go-around. Safety Recommendation 15-2021Air Canada has amended their procedures to incorporate both cases of control handover. Safety Recommendation 16-2021Air Canada has amended their use of “sterile cockpit principles” and how they are employed during critical phases of flight.  Safety Recommendation 17-2021Air Canada has amended their procedures which now include the requirement to remove or secure loose objects for critical phases of flight. Safety Recommendation 18-2021Air Canada has amended their procedures which now include that in order to reduce the risk of potential safety risks to aircraft or flight operations, Flight Crews shall report as soon as possible any hazardous flight condition to ATC, such as any observed conditions or events that may cause Foreign Object Damage (FOD).

C-FSKA, a Beech A100 King Air aircraft operated by Beaver Air Services (dba Missinippi Airways), was conducting a flight York Landing (CZAC), MB to Thompson (CYTH), MB with 2 crew members and 2 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew smelled and observed electrical smoke and fumes in the cockpit. All unnecessary electrical equipment was turned off, and the smoke was evacuated. The flight crew advised ATC, however no emergency was declared. The flight continued to CYTH where an uneventful landing was conducted with emergency vehicles standing by as a precautionary measure. A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed that the aircraft's heater vent blower had seized. The vent blower motor was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GGPR un appareil de type PA-23-250 exploité par Cargair avec à son bord 2 pilotes effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Montréal/Saint-Hubert QC (CYHU) à destination de Brockville Regional Tackaberry ONT (CNL3). Peu de temps après le décollage une fuite de carburant a été observée suite à un bouchon de réservoir mal fermé. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil est revenu se poser à CYHU sans problème.

C-GSJB un Airbus 319-100 exploité par Air Canada Rouge sous l'indicatif de vol ROU1822 était stationné à la passerelle numéro 60 à l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl lorsqu'un camion de ravitaillement en carburant a frappé l'aile gauche de l'aéronef. Personne à bord n'a été blessé. L'appareil a subi des dommages mineurs. Il n'y a eu aucun déversement de carburant.

C-GBLJ un Cessna 340A en exploitation privée avec à son bord seul le pilote à bord, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l'aéroport de Fredericton NB à destination de Sept-Îles QC (CYZV). Alors que l'appareil était à son altitude de croisière, le pilote a observé une fluctuation au manomètre de pression d'admission du moteur gauche (Teledyne Continental TSIO-520-NB) ainsi qu'un bruit de retour de flamme. Le pilote a demandé un déroutement vers Charlo (NB) (CYCL). En route vers CYCL, le pilote a observé de nouveau des retours de flammes ainsi qu'une trainée de fumée derrière le moteur. Le pilote a coupé le moteur, a déclaré une urgence et demandé un déroutement vers Sainte-Anne-des-Monts (CYSZ) où l'appareil s'est posé sans problème en présence des services d'urgence. Le pilote n'a subi aucune blessure.

N813SK, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by SkyWest Airlines, was conducting flight SKW4718 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Minneapolis-Saint Paul Intl/Wold-Chamberlain (KMSP), MN. Shortly after the departure from CYWG, the flight crew observed a STEERING INOP caution message, followed by a GEAR DISAGREE warning message. The flight crew requested vectors while they conducted the QRH procedure for the GEAR DISAGREE. Upon completion of the procedure, the landing gear indicators showed three green lights in the down position. An emergency was declared, and vectors were requested for a low approach so that ATC could visually inspect the landing gear. The tower reported that the landing gear appeared down, and that the nose wheel was straight. An uneventful landing was then carried out with emergency vehicles standing by. The aircraft was subsequently towed to the gate.A post-flight inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed a leaking nose gear strut seal. The seal was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GQCA, an Airbus A320-200, was operating as Air Canada flight 568 from Vancouver Int'l (CYVR), BC to San Francisco Int'l (KSFO), CA. During the approach into KSFO, when the flight crew selected gear down, they received an ECAM message 'Landing Gear'. The flight crew then selected landing gear up, and, after 20 seconds, they received a 'gear not uplocked' message. After 120 seconds, they selected gear down and received a green indication but still had gear not uplocked noted on the ECAM. A Pan Pan was declared and the aircraft landed at KSFO uneventfully. The aircraft was then taxied to the gate with emergency vehicles following. Maintenance replaced the relay of LGCIU #2 and carried out full gear swing and associated tests.

C-GTQC, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC934 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL with 6 crew members and 192 passengers on board. During the descent to destination, TSC934 was instructed to hold at waypoint FATHR at FL330 due to heavy thunderstorms (+TS) at KFLL. The filed alternate airport, Miami Intl (KMIA), FL, was also experiencing +TS with an estimated holding time of 25 to 30 minutes. Since weather conditions were not improving at both the destination and the alternate after 38 minutes of holding, the flight crew declared a fuel emergency for priority handling at KFLL. ATC offered West Palm Beach Intl (KPBI), FL as an option, which the flight crew accepted. TSC934 landed at KPBI uneventfully with emergency vehicles in attendance, and with 1600 kgs of fuel on board, which was above the minimum reserve fuel required.

C-FNJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ 900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8668 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to San Diego Intl (KSAN), CA. Shortly after the departure from CYVR, the flight crew received a WING ANTI-ICE FAULT message, and noticed and electrical burning smell. The flight crew also observed a brief puff of smoke from the wing anti-ice circuit breaker (CB), however the smoke dissipated quickly. Masks were not required. The aircraft returned to CYVR and landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance found that the screw which secures both the DC BUS bar and the FEEDER BUS bar from CB D6 to CB D7, was several turns short of being fully tightened, which caused high resistance and arcing. Both CBs and BUS bars were replaced, and all attaching screws were torqued. An SDR was submitted.

C-GNDF, a Bell 206L helicopter operated by Héli Mistral Service was performing a slinging operation near Lac Barkmere, QC located approximately 28 nm SSE of La Macaza/Mont-Tremblant Intl airport (CYFJ), QC. The operation consisted of slinging several large slabs of granite to a cottage located on the shore of Lac Barkmere from the nearest road access. During the third and final load, the two granite slabs broke and pieces were released into the water. There were no injuries.

C-FLOR, a Beech C90A King Air aircraft operated by Montair Aviation, was conducting a training flight from Red Deer (CYQF), AB to Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC with two persons on board. During cruise flight approximately 10 nm northeast of Vancouver Harbour (CYHC), BC, the flight crew initiated an emergency descent below the minimum vectoring altitude (MVA) due to a loss of accurate airspeed indication. ATC vectored the aircraft over Indian Arm, BC to an area with a lower MVA for the aircraft to operate under Instrument Flight Rules (IFR). Upon reaching a lower altitude, the airspeed indication returned to normal. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYPK. It was determined that the pitot tube became blocked by ice.

C-FUKU, a privately registered Piper Cherokee PA-28-140, took off from Rivière-du-Loup (CYRI), QC, for a local VFR flight with two occupants onboard. Upon return to the airport and during landing on runway 05, the aircraft deviated from the runway centerline due to a gust of wind. During the attempt to go-around, the nose wheel contacted a snowbank and the aircraft drifted sideways into the adjacent ditch.  Both occupants were uninjured during the occurrence.  The aircraft sustained structural damage to the nose landing gear attachment points and fuselage aft of the engine firewall. The propeller contacted the ground, causing damage to the engine and propeller blades. Winds were reported at 325 degrees, 8-10 knots and gusting 20-22 knots.

C-FSDW, a Boeing 737 Max 8 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA321 from Montreal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl., QC (CYUL) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with 6 crew members and 125 passengers on board. Approximately 1/2 mile back, on final approach to Runway 35R, multiple birds were ingested in the #2 engine (CFM International Leap 1B). The crew continued the approach and an uneventful landing was accomplished. Abnormal vibrations were noted in the #2 engine and the crew elected to shut down the #2 engine as a precaution on the taxi from the runway. The aircraft was removed from service while maintenance conducted the appropriate inspection items.

N611AS, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by Alaska Airlines, was conducting flight ASA64 from Ketchikan Intl (PAKT), AK to Seattle-Tacoma Intl (KSEA), WA with 5 crew members and 37 passengers on board. During cruise flight just prior to the top of descent at KSEA, the flight crew felt a pressure change in their ears. The cabin altitude panel was observed climbing at 3000 feet per minute. Within 10 seconds, the cabin altitude warning horn activated. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks, declared an emergency, and initiated a rapid descent. The aircraft was levelled off at 10 000 feet ASL, and the flight continued to its destination where it landed without further incident.

N28912, a Boeing 787-8 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL807, from Washington Dulles Intl airport (KIAD) to Beijing Capital Intl Airport (ZBAA). After departure, the aircraft lost the L1 variable frequency starter/generator (VFSG). The applicable procedure for the VFSG failure requires the continuous use of the auxiliary power unit (APU) for the remainder of the flight. It was determined that the continuous use of the APU for the 12 remaining hours combined with the normal fuel burn of both engines would require more fuel to reach their destination than there was on board. The decision was made to divert to San Francisco Intl airport (KSFO) to refuel and change crew. The aircraft subsequently departed KFSO for ZBAA with the L1 VFSG deactivated as per the aircraft minimum equipment list (MEL).

C-GHLK, un appareil de type Boeing 767-300 exploité par Air Canada rouge, effectuait le vol ROU1603 entre Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL et Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. Durant l'approche finale pour la piste 06L à CYUL, le message LE SLAT DISAGREE est apparu sur le système d'affichage des paramètres réacteurs, de mise en garde et d'alarme (EICAS). Une remise des gaz a été effectuée, et l'équipage a complété la liste de vérification applicable. Un PAN PAN a été déclaré avant de revenir atterrir en configuration de volets réduits, et l'atterrissage a été complété sans encombre.

C-GMAS, a de Havilland Canada DHC-6 operated by Air Tindi Ltd. was conducting flight TIN601 from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Snare River, NT (CEV9) with 2 crew members and 5 passengers on board. Approximately 10 nm after departure, the crew turned on the internal instrument lighting and a faint electrical smoke smell was observed. The flight crew initiated a return to CYZF and the first officer proceeded to check the cabin and inform the passengers of the change in flight itinerary. An uneventful approach and landing were conducted.Company maintenance determined that the internal lighting board of the standby attitude indicator was burnt, which was the source of the smell. The instrument was replaced and the aircraft released for service.

C-FTCA, a Boeing 767-300 operated by Air Canada as flight AC446 was descending into MacDonald-Cartier Intl - Ottawa (CYOW) when the flight crew was advised by ATC of moderate turbulence in the area. The flight crew advised the cabin crew of the expected turbulence and to return to their seats. The aircraft experienced moderate to severe turbulence sooner than the flight crew expected, while the cabin crew were stowing galley equipment and not seated. Three flight attendants received minor injuries; there were no passenger injuries.

C-FCCJ, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Cargojet, was conducting flight CJT620 from Moncton/Greater Moncton Roméo Leblanc Intl (CYQM), NB to St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL. During the climb to cruise altitude, the autopilot disengaged and the flight director information became erroneous. The crew did not receive any EICAS messages or any STATUS messages. The crew declared a PAN PAN and held to burn fuel below the maximum landing weight. The crew elected to return to CYQM due to better weather conditions than CYYT, and landed without further incident. Maintenance replaced the Mode Control Panel and the aircraft returned to service.

C-FYNS, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1632 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Sarasota/Bradenton Intl (KSRQ), FL with 5 crew members and 125 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL380, ATC instructed ROU1632 to turn 20 degrees to the left, which was read back and complied with. Approximately 1 minute later, 35 nm north-northeast of Charlotte/Douglas Intl (KCLT), NC, the flight crew received a TCAS RA CLIMB aural warning. The flight crew responded to the RA and subsequently notified ATC. After the aircraft reached FL384, a CLEAR OF TRAFFIC message was heard. Shortly thereafter, ATC cleared ROU1632 to enroute waypoint SLOJO on course.   The conflicting aircraft is believed to be a Bombardier Global 6000 (GLEX) of unknown identification.

C-GTSO, an Airbus A330-300 aircraft operated by Air Transat A. T. Inc., was conducting flight TSC111 from Paris/Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. During cruise, approximately 2 hours prior to landing at CYUL, a flight attendant became incapacitated and could not complete their duties. The flight duties for landing were distributed amongst remaining flight attendants.

C-GONW, a DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP was conducting flight JZA757 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl Airport (CYUL), QC to Rouyn-Noranda Airport (CYUY), QC with 3 crew members and 32 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL190, the flight crew noticed that 3 of the 4 sequence lights of the horizontal stabilizer de-icing boots were not illuminating. As the flight was being conducted in icing conditions, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and requested a return to CYUL where an uneventful landing was carried out.

C-FMZW, an Embraer ERJ190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA595 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Houston/George Bush Intercontinental (KIAH), TX with 4 crew members and 64 passengers on board. During the cruise portion of the flight, the flight crew experienced an auto-pilot disconnect, while receiving an ADS 1 FAIL and AVNX MAU 1A FAIL EICAS messages. The flight crew reverted to manual control mode, referenced the QRH, and declared a PAN PAN during the initial descent. The flight continued to KIAH without further incident, and taxied to the gate.   The operator’s maintenance replaced the Module Assembly Control and carried out a few checks. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GARO, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1735 from Liberia/Daniel Oduber Quirós Intl (MRLB), Costa Rica to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 5 crew members and 131 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from MRLB, the landing gear failed to retract. Subsequently, a number of ECAM messages were displayed in the cockpit. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and initially requested vectors to facilitate troubleshooting. The QRH was executed, and ECAM messages began to clear. The flight crew was able to clear all ECAM messages, and successfully cycled the landing gear to the retracted position. The flight continued to CYYZ without further incident.The operator’s maintenance is troubleshooting the cause of the ECAM messages. The occurrence was captured in the operator’s SMS.

C-GLWN, a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by North Cariboo Air, was conducting flight NCA1420 from Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC) to Fort Mackay/Albian, AB (CAL4) with 3 crew members and 11 passengers on board. During the taxi for departure from CYYC, the flight crew received a "DC BUS" caution light and a "TOUCH RUNWAY" light. The flight crew actioned the appropriate checklist and returned to the apron. During the taxi in, smoke and a strong burning smell was detected. The aircraft was shut down at the hangar and all passengers were deplaned to the terminal.Company maintenance determined the source of the smell and smoke to be originating from the aircraft's APU, and completed the appropriate maintenance actions.

C-FACV, un appareil de type Dash-8-300 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA725 selon les règles de vol aux instruments à partir de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. Lors de l'approche ILS sur la piste 24R de CYUL, JZA725 été instruit par le CCA de réduire sa vitesse à 160 nœuds. Plus d’une minute plus tard, la vitesse sol de JZA725 restait inchangée et l’aéronef allait compromettre l’espacement nécessaire avec le trafic précédent. Le CCA a annulé l'autorisation d'approche et viré JZA725 à l'écart. Durant cette manœuvre, l'espacement a été réduit à 2.6 nm et 800 pieds avec C-GKQC, un appareil de type Dash-8-400 exploité par Porter Airlines sous l'indicatif POE483, alors que la norme est de 3 nm ou 1000 pieds. JZA725 a ensuite été guidé pour une seconde approche, et s’est posé sur la piste 24R à 2353Z.

C-FIJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (Series 100) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8788 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Saint John (CYSJ), NB. While en route to CYSJ, the crew received a “FLAP FAIL” caution. The crew determined that they would now require a longer runway than what was available at CYSJ and diverted to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. The crew did not declare an emergency but requested ARFF to be on standby. The aircraft landed without further incident. Maintenance reset the system and the aircraft was returned to service.

N525EZ, a Cessna 525C CitationJet aircraft, was conducting a flight from Gander Intl (CYQX), NL to Shannon Intl (EINN), Ireland. While taxing for departure, N525EZ was instructed by ATC to hold short of Runway 21. The flight crew read back the hold short clearance correctly. A military Airbus 330 (A330) aircraft conducting a flight from CYQX to Oxford/RAF Brize Norton (EGVN), UK, had been cleared for take off on Runway 03. N525EZ was observed crossing the hold line and entering Runway 21, which prompted ATC to cancel the take off clearance for the A330. The aircraft had just commenced its take off run, and was able to stop within the first 2000 feet of the runway. N525EZ taxied off Runway 21, while the A330 backtracked to position. The A330 departed with no further incident.

C-GBWS, a Boeing 737-600 aircraft operated by WestJet Airlines, was conducting flight WJA557 from Kitchener/Waterloo, ON (CYKF) to Calgary, AB (CYYC) with 5 crew members and 76 passengers on board. As the aircraft was taxiing into the arrival gate position on the lead in line at CYYC, a safety cone was ingested into the #1 engine (CFM International, CFM56-7B22). The flight crew immediately shut the engine down. There were no injuries to any ground personnel and damage to the aircraft was limited to the #1 engine. The aircraft was removed form service for maintenance investigation.The #1 engine was replaced with serviceable unit and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GGMU, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8995 from St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL, to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS with 4 crew members and 67 passengers on board. On approach into CYHZ, the flight crew experienced difficulty in controlling the aircraft due to severe turbulence, which caused the autopilot to disconnect and the stick shaker to momentarily activate. The flight crew conducted a missed approach and diverted to their alternate. Maintenance will be conducting an inspection of the aircraft.

C-FIWE, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3222 from Kelowna, BC (CYLW) to Edmonton Intl., AB (CYEG) with 4 crew members and 24 passengers on board. Enroute to CYEG, the crew received a landing gear inop caution light indication. Upon arrival into CYEG, the flight crew attempted to extend the landing gear using the manual extension system; the operator reported that excessive force was required to operate the system. A fly past of the control tower was completed and the tower reported that the nose landing gear was not extended. The flight crew made a second attempt at manually extending the landing gear which was successful in lowering all three landing gears. The flight crew declared an emergency and an uneventful landing was completed.Company maintenance determined that NLGK 1 bracket to be loose and NLGK 1, NGDN 1 and NGDN 2 sensors required adjustment. Corrective actions were completed, landing gear swings were carried out and the aircraft was released for service.

N89313, an Embraer ERJ-170-200, flight 6196, operated by Mesa Airlines, landed on runway 06R at Toronto/LPIA (CYYZ). The aircraft was instructed to exit on taxiway D5, a high-speed exit, and hold short of runway 06L. The flight crew did not read back the instructions correctly, so ATC reiterated the requirement to hold short of runway 06L, after which the flight crew correctly read back the instructions. At this time Air Canada flight 722, (Airbus A320) was cleared for departure from runway 06L. ATC observed N89313 rapidly approaching the hold-short line for runway 06L on D5, and instructed the aircraft to STOP STOP STOP. N89313 came to a stop past the hold short line, but not on the runway surface. Air Canada 722 was airborne prior to D5, between D1 and D3. It was reported that the flight crew of N89313, mistook the 06L hold short line for the 06R exit line.

C-GFAH, an Airbus 330-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA878 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Zürich-Kloten (LSZH), Switzerland with 11 crew members and 275 passengers on board. During the landing on Runway 14 at LSZH, the flight crew experienced a Nose Wheel Steering Fault and was unable to steer the aircraft. The aircraft needed to be towed off the runway, all the way to the gate.The operator’s maintenance replaced the hydraulic block in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual. Functional tests and leak checks were carried out, and no further faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FPWD, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1220 from Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl (KFLL), FL with 5 crew members and 134 passengers on board. During the approach to KFLL, the flight crew received a slat failure ECAM message. The checklist was executed, and the flight crew declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed at KFLL without further incident, and was met by ARFF who escorted the aircraft to the gate. The operator’s maintenance found the number 9 Torque Limiter had popped out. After a fix and operational checks, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FSNU, a Boeing 737 MAX 8, was parked at a gate in Ottawa (CYOW) in the boarding process when the flight and cabin crew noticed an odor throughout the aircraft. Visible haze was also noticed by the gate agent at the bridge. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, ARFF was notified and attended the scene. The passengers were deplaned normally at the gate.  A post-incident inspection determined there was air contamination from an external source.

C-GEWR, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3244 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl (CYXE), SK to Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with 4 crew members and 31 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to a medical issue with one of the flight attendants. After the aircraft landed, Emergency Medical Services took the flight attendant to a hospital for further examination.

C-GELP, a Helicopteres Guimbal Cabri G2 aircraft operated by British Columbia Helicopters, was conducting an autorotation training flight within the infield at Abbotsford (CYXX), BC with 1 instructor and 1 student on board. During the descent into the wind, the main rotor RPM decreased lower than anticipated. The Fenestron tail rotor became inefficient, and directional control was lost. As directional control was re-established in close proximity to the ground, the wind direction shifted, the helicopter skid tube contacted the ground and the helicopter rolled over. The instructor and the student exited the helicopter with minor injuries. The helicopter sustained substantial damage. The wind velocity at the time of the accident was 18 knots, gusting to 28 knots. There was no post impact fire.

C-FDRH, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA239 from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC. During the taxi to the runway for the departure, a flight attendant noticed smoke emanating from the galley. The flight crew isolated the circuit for the oven, and requested ARFF to attend to the aircraft as it returned to the gate. The operator’s maintenance replaced the oven, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FWJS, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA128 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. During the approach at CYYC, the flight crew noticed a flap disagree indication. The flight crew conducted a missed approach, and completed the applicable checklist. An emergency was declared, and the landing was executed with flaps 15 without further incident. Subsequent inspection by the operator’s maintenance found a faulty flap position transmitter. The transmitter was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FENO, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3188 from Grande Prairie (CYQU), AB to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. During cruise flight, the flight crew received an IOP (Input Output Processor) 1 fail advisory message. The flight crew declared an emergency and, due to weather conditions at CYYC, diverted the aircraft to Lethbridge (CYQL), AB where the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced the IOP 1 unit, and returned the aircraft to service.

C-GIZO, a Bell 206B aircraft operated by Highland Helicopters, was conducting slung load operations approximately 18 nm north-northeast of Helmet (CBH2), BC with only the pilot on board. While transitioning to forward flight, the cargo net became entangled with an object on the ground. The pilot attempted to release the load from the cargo hook, however was unable to do so. The aircraft pitched nose down and contacted terrain. The pilot evacuated the aircraft and sustained minor injuries. The helicopter was substantially damaged.

C-FLEN, a Boeing 737-400 aircraft operated by Flair Airlines, was conducting flight FLE463 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB. During the descent for the arrival into CYEG, the flight crew attempted to start the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU). Shortly after the EGT indicated a rise, the APU fire warning illuminated. The flight crew immediately actioned the appropriate QRH checklist, and the fire warning indication went out. The flight crew continued the approach, and the aircraft landed without further incident. No emergency was declared, and ARFF was not requested. The flight crew taxied the aircraft to the gate.  Subsequent inspection by the operator’s maintenance found damage to the EGT probe wires and determined that there was no damage to the APU mounts and other structural components. The APU was deferred in accordance with MEL 49-01, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKCH, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Canadian Helicopters, was returning to Kugaaruk (CYBB), NU when smoke became evident in the cockpit. The smoke dissipated after the flight crew turned off all major electrical systems, lights, heater blowers, and ventilation blower. During the approach, the systems were turned back on. The odour returned when the heating system was turned on. The heating system was shut down, and the helicopter landed without further incident.It was determined that a burnt out blower motor was the source of the odour. Pending repairs, the aircraft can be dispatched with the blower under MEL provision.

N8300G (US registration), a Dynamic Avlease Inc. DHC-8-300 aircraft, departed from North Bay (CYYB) destined for Erie Pennsylvania (KERI).  During the initial climb the #2 hydraulic system failed. The crew declared an emergency and returned to CYYB. The landing was uneventful with ARFF standing by.

C-FYAG, a Fairchild SA227-AC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting flight PAG223 from Deer Lake (CYVZ), ON  to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with 2 crew members on board. During the initial take off roll at CYVZ, the flight crew heard what sounded like gravel hitting the fuselage, and elected to continue the take off. All aircraft and engine indications appeared normal, and the flight crew decided to continue to CYWG, where the aircraft landed without incident. After deplaning, the flight crew inspected the aircraft and noticed substantial damage to the left propeller, left side fuselage, left passenger windows and right engine cowling. A TSB investigator was deployed to the operator’s maintenance facility to inspect the aircraft. It was determined that the damage was indicative of the propeller making contact with gravel.

C-FTIZ, an Aerospatiale ATR 42-500 aircraft operated by First Air, was conducting flight FAB852 from Taloyoak (CYYH), NU to Kugaaruk (CYBB), NU with 3 crew members and 21 passengers on board. After both engines had been started during the preparation for the departure, the flight crew noticed that the number 1 inverter and MFC 2B (Multi-Function Computer) displayed faults. The flight crew also noticed an electrical odour, elected to shut both engines down, and requested assistance from ARFF. The flight attendant was advised to deplane the passengers, as smoke was evident in the forward cargo and cabin areas. The operator's maintenance determined that the number 1 inverter was faulty, and proceeded to replace the unit. The number 2 DC generator, along with the main and emergency batteries, were also replaced.

N951DJ (US registration), a Falcon 50 aircraft inbound from Orlando Intl - Orlando (KMCO) was landing at Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ)when it was instructed by ATC to taxi via RWY 33R and hold short of RWY 23. The instruction was read back correctly by the flight crew. The aircraft was observed crossing the hold short line and was instructed by the controller to stop. WJA710 a WestJet Boeing 737-800 Max had just touched down on RWY 23 when the incursion took place.

MPE1560, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Canadian North, was operating a flight from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Fort MacKay/Albian (CAL4), AB. MPE1560 departed off Runway 02 on the GABET ONE departure from CYEG. C-GWRE, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was operating flight WEN3140 from CYEG to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. WEN3140 also departed off Runway 02, behind MPE1560. The climb performance of WEN3140 was greater than anticipated by ATC, which resulted in the separation being reduced to 2.7 nm horizontally and 1000 feet vertically, where 3 nm or 1000 feet are required. WEN3140 was given radar vectors to regain lateral separation.

C-GYPA, un appareil de type Beech B100 King Air exploité par Max Aviation, effectuait le vol MAX190 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Kuujjuaq (CYVP), QC à destination de Schefferville (CYKL), QC avec 2 membres d'équipage et 8 passagers à son bord. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, une odeur de brulé est apparue, accompagnée de fumée dans la cabine. L’équipage a décidé de revenir atterrir à CYVP, et les services d’urgences ont été activés. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 25 quelques minutes plus tard. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage, et les pompiers ont confirmés ne voir aucun feu ou fumée.

C-FSII, un appareil de type Eurocopter EC120B en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Rouyn-Noranda (CYUY), QC à destination de Montréal/Mirabel Hélico (CMH4), QC avec seul le pilote à bord. L’appareil s’est rapporté en passant Mont-Laurier, QC à 12h00 EST, toutefois il n’est jamais arrivé à sa destination. Il a été rapporté manquant au Centre conjoint de coordination des opérations de sauvetage (CCCOS) de Trenton vers 14h19 EST. Le CCCOS a déployé un hélicoptère Griffon et un avion C-130 Hercule pour tenter de localiser l’hélicoptère, mais aucun signal de la radiobalise de repérage de détresse (ELT) n’a été reçu. L’hélicoptère a été localisé le lendemain vers 16h00 EST dans un secteur boisé sur le flan d’un haut relief. L’appareil a subi des dommages importants et le pilote a subi des blessures mortelles. Il n’y a pas eu de feu post-impact.

C-FYKR, un appareil de type Airbus 319-100 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA386 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC avec 5 membres d’équipage et 120 passagers à bord. Alors qu’il était en vol de croisière, le moniteur électronique centralisé de bord (ECAM) a généré un message de faible quantité de liquide hydraulique du système jaune. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification et a par la suite déclaré un état d’urgence. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre avec les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) déployés. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé, ni dommage.

C-FHGG, un appareil de type Beech A100 exploité par Propair, effectuait le vol PRO4210 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Val d’Or (CYVO), QC à destination de Rouyn-Noranda (CYUY), QC. Alors que le vol avait été autorisé à 4000 pieds ASL par l’ATC après le départ de CYVO, l’appareil s’est retrouvé à 4400 pieds ASL. Une perte d’espacement est survenue avec CRQ531, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-8-100 exploité par Air Creebec, qui était en circuit d’attente au radiophare omnidirectionnel VHF (VOR) de Val-d’Or (YVO) à 5000 pieds ASL. La séparation requise était de 1000 pieds sur le plan vertical.

C-FPWD, un appareil de type Airbus 320-200 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA318 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC avec 7 membres d’équipage et 130 passagers à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en vol de croisière, le moniteur électronique centralisé de bord (ECAM) a généré un message de défectuosité du déporteur numéro 4 (SPLR 4 Fault). Lors de la descente, à environ 135 miles marins au nord-ouest de CYUL, l’ECAM a généré un message de défectuosité des déporteurs 3 et 4 (SPLR 3 + 4 Fault), ainsi qu’un désaccord entre les freins aérodynamiques (SPD BRK DISAGREE). L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification et a par la suite déclaré un état d’urgence. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre avec les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) déployés. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé, ni dommage.

C-GJZZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (CRJ200) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8033 from Philadelphia Intl (KPHL), PA to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC with 3 crew members and 41 passengers on board. Approximately 25 minutes after the departure during cruise flight at FL290, the flight crew received a fluctuating oil pressure indication on the number 2 engine. Passing through 15 000 feet during the descent to CYUL, the flight crew elected to shut the number 2 engine (General Electric CF34-3B1) down  since the oil pressure was decreasing and the oil pressure warning activated. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, briefed the passengers, and completed a successful landing at CYUL without further incident.The operator’s maintenance found that the O-ring behind the number 2 starter seal was missing. A new seal with the O-ring was installed as per GE’s maintenance manual 72-61-00. The number 2 engine oil tank was serviced, engine runs were performed, and no leaks were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GMXB, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG439 from Punta Cana Intl (MDPC), Dominican Republic to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON with 6 crew members and 176 passengers on board. While the aircraft was in cruise flight at FL350, the flight crew received erroneous indications on the captain's instruments. As a precaution, the flight crew elected to descend to FL250 in order to get out of Instrument Meteorological Conditions (IMC). Since the stand by and the first officer's instruments were functioning normally, control of the aircraft was handed to the first officer. As the aircraft passed through FL280, approximately 50 nm northwest of Washington/Dulles Intl (KIAD), VA, the weather radar and TCAS both failed. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and executed the QRH checklists. Subsequently, the left side IRS fault light illuminated. The flight continued to destination and landed without further incident.The operator's maintenance replaced the left Air Data Inertial Reference Unit (ADIRU) and performed functional checks to confirm that the fault was cleared. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GEHS, a Beech 200 King Air aircraft operated by PAL Aerospace, was conducting a test flight from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS with 4 crew members on board. Upon departure, sparks were noted exiting the number 1 engine. The flight crew suspected an engine fire, climbed to a safe altitude and declared an emergency. Since the flight was conducted during hours of darkness, sparks were highly visible. The engine was not shut down as all indications were normal. The flight crew returned to the airfield and conducted an uneventful landing. The operator’s maintenance inspected both engines and conducted run ups. However, they were unable to duplicate the sparking. Before the flight, both engines were washed, and it is suspected that some debris remained and created the sparks on takeoff.

C-GWCY, a Boeing 737-600 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA137 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 5 crew members and 99 passengers on board. Approximately 5 minutes prior to the top of descent, the lead flight attendant informed the pilots that a sulphur like smell was observed in the overhead bins, in the vicinity of Row 2. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and landed without further incident. Once at the gate, a fire crew proceeded on board and identified a smell from a WestJet commissary cooler bag in the overhead bin, above Row 2. The bag was removed and searched with no heat source identified. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GAIS, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-8-100 exploité par Air Creebec, effectuait le vol CRQ920 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Rouyn-Noranda (CYUY), QC à destination de Val-d’Or (CYVO), QC. C-GTUK, un appareil de type Boeing 737-200 exploité par Nolinor, effectuait le vol NRL950 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis CYVO à destination de Churchill (CYYQ), MB. NRL950 avait reçu une autorisation de départ de la piste 18. CRQ920 se trouvait alors en rapprochement pour CYVO, et avait été autorisé pour l’approche RNAV pour la piste 36 via le repère INOPU. Suite au décollage de NRL950, la séparation de 3 minutes entre les arrivées et les départs, dans un environnement de norme de contrôle procédurier non-radar, n’a pas été assurée.

C-GNVC, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Nav Canada, was conducting flight NVC201 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Saint John (CYSJ), NB. The aircraft was positioned at the de-icing bay and configured for spray with the parking brake set, both engines running and the APU shut down. The de-ice truck proceeded to spray the left wing, however as it moved to position rearward, the truck came into contact with the tail and jolted the aircraft. The flight crew shut the left engine down, and the flight engineer exited the aircraft to inspect it. There was visible damage to the horizontal tail section. ATC was advised, the aircraft was shut down and was towed to a hanger.

On 15 November 2018, the PAL Airlines Ltd. Bombardier DHC-8-315 aircraft (registration C FPAE, serial number 562) departed Churchill Falls (CZUM), Newfoundland and Labrador (NL) as flight PVL1922 on an instrument flight rules flight to Deer Lake (CYDF), NL with 4 crew members and 47 passengers on board. At 1057 Newfoundland Standard Time, during the approach at CYDF, the flight crew selected the landing gear down; however, the crew noticed a weight on wheels caution light as well as advisory lights indicating that the nose landing gear was not in the down and locked position. The flight crew executed a missed approach and entered a hold in order to troubleshoot the problem. At 1202 the flight crew requested a diversion to Stephenville (CYJT), NL and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed at CYJT at 1230 with the nose landing gear in a partially extended position. On touchdown the nose landing gear fully collapsed and the aircraft nose structure made contact with the runway surface. The aircraft slid to a stop approximately half way down the runway. All occupants on board egressed the aircraft with no reported injuries. The aircraft sustained minor damage. There was no post-impact fire. There were insufficient forward impact forces to automatically activate the emergency locator transmitter. The accident occurred during the hours of daylight.

C-FAMC, a Fairchild SA227-AC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting flight PAG912 from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON to Big Trout Lake (CYTL), ON. After the aircraft became airborne following the departure from CYXL, the flight crew noticed that the take-off roll required more runway than expected. During the retraction of the landing gear, the flight crew noticed that the parking brake control was not fully pushed in. The flight crew selected the landing gear down to provide cooling of the brakes, and elected to return to CYXL. An emergency was declared, and the flight crew executed a holding pattern to burn off fuel, in order to reduce the landing weight. Two fly overs were flown to allow ground personnel to visually inspect the aircraft and, after receiving a report that no damage was observed, a normal landing was conducted. The aircraft was brought to a stop on the runway, and was subsequently towed to the apron. The operator's maintenance inspected the brakes and wheels; no defects were noted.

C-FKGE, un appareil de type Pilatus PC-12/47 exploité par Kudlik Aviation sous l'indicatif de vol KUK761 et C-GECN, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-8-100 exploité par Canadian North sous l'indicatif de vol MPE611, effectuaient tous deux un vol depuis d'Igloolik (CYGT), NU  à destination d'Iqaluit (CYFB), NU. Peu de temps après le départ de CYGT, les deux appareils sont entrés dans l'espace aérien contrôlé à la même altitude avec 6.6 nm d'espacement latéral, alors que la norme est de 10 nm. L’ATC a appliqué l'ancienne norme de 5 nm, alors que la nouvelle norme de 10 nm est en vigueur depuis Juin 2018.

C-GWOX, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG714 from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON to Fort Severn (CYER), ON with 2 crew members and 7 passengers on board. During the final approach into CYER, the flight crew extended the landing gear and received an unsafe nose gear indication. The flight crew declared an emergency and decided to return to CYXL where the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator will notify the TSB of their findings.UPDATE 19 November 2018The operator advised that the NLG actuator was replaced and, after several successful gear swings, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GSNQ, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Exploit Valley Air Services, was conducting flight EVS601 from Sydney/JA Douglas McCurdy (CYQY), NS to Deer Lake (CYDF), NL. During cruise flight at FL190, the aircraft experienced a pressurization issue. The flight crew declared an emergency and began a descent to 9000 feet. The Cabin Decompression checklist was completed, and the flight crew discovered that they had inadvertently hit the cabin pressure dump switch. The emergency was cancelled, and the aircraft landed without further incident.

OY-MGA un appareil de type Dassault Falcon 2000EX exploité par Air Alsie, effectuait le vol MMD6467 selon les règles de vol aux instruments à partir de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC à destination de Londres Oxford (EGTK), England. Après le départ de CYUL, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence et a demandé un retour à CYUL, invoquant un problème de volets. À 0449Z, après avoir consommé du carburant, l'équipage a déclaré que le problème était résolu et a demandé de reprendre sa route vers Londres/Heathrow (EGLL), England. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GMLS, a privately registered Cessna 340A aircraft, was conducting an approach at Ponoka Industrial (Labrie Field) (CEH3), AB with only the pilot on board. The pilot missed the first approach due to autopilot malfunction issues, and decided to do a forced landing during the go-around due to the autopilot that would not disconnect as needed. As the forced landing in a field was executed, the aircraft struck a tree during the slide. The aircraft was substantially damaged, and the pilot walked away with a serious injury.

C-FPLS, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Swoop, was conducting flight WSW505 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB. During cruise flight, a flight attendant was no longer able to perform their duties due to their illness. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GDUM, a privately owned Piper PA-28R-200 aircraft, crashed at Brantford (CYFD), ON, at approximately 01h19 EST on 13 November 2018. The accident wasn't known until the aircraft was located on the airport infield area, adjacent to the threshold of Runway 05, during a routine airport inspection around 08h00 EST. The aircraft was substantially damaged during the accident, and the two occupants on board were fatally injured.

C-GRPP, an Amateur Built Denney Kitfox IV 1200 aircraft, was enroute from a private airstrip in Solsgirth, MB to Shoal Lake (CKL5), MB, with only the pilot on board. During cruise flight, the engine (Rotax 912 UL) began to lose power and the pilot decided to return to Solsgirth. During the final approach, the engine lost power completely, and the aircraft force landed in a field approximately 400 feet short of the runway. The aircraft touched down hard then overturned. The pilot was not injured and the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GPRU, un appareil de type Beech B100 King Air exploité par Max Aviation, effectuait le vol MAX130 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, depuis Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC avec 2 membres d'équipage et 3 passagers à bord. Lors de l'approche à CYUL, le voyant vert du train de nez refusait de s'illuminer lorsque que le train était en position baissée. L'équipage a alors déclaré une urgence et a demandé un espace aérien réservé afin d'effectuer des tests. Un passage bas près de la tour de contrôle a été effectué afin d'avoir une confirmation visuelle que le train étain déployé, et l’appareil s’est ensuite posé sans encombre sur la piste 24L à 0417Z. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.Une inspection subséquente du personnel de l’entretien a révélé un fil électrique au contact intermittent dans le compartiment du train d'atterrissage.

C-GBHO, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1735 from Liberia/Daniel Oduber Quirós Intl (MRLB), Costa Rica to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. During cruise flight, the flight crew received reports of significant turbulence in the vicinity of Pittsburgh Intl (KPIT), PA. As a result, the cabin was secured early, all passengers and crew were instructed to remain seated with seatbelts fastened, and an early descent to FL230 was initiated due to ride reports which indicated more favourable conditions at that altitude. In the vicinity of Erie Intl/Tom Ridge Field (KERI), PA, the flight encountered significant turbulence which caused an abrupt change in altitude and airspeed, with the aircraft climbing to FL235. ATC was notified, and a lower altitude was requested and granted. Upon reaching FL180, flight conditions were smooth and the flight was subsequently completed uneventfully. No persons were injured, nor was any damage caused to the aircraft as a result of the turbulence encounter. The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and found no faults.

C-FEJF, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 aircraft operated by Sky Regional Airlines, was performing flight SKV7634 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to New York/La Guardia (KLGA), NY with 4 crew members and 77 passengers on board. During cruise flight approximately 210 nm North of KLGA, in the vicinity of Saranac Lake, NY, the aircraft experienced severe turbulence. All passengers were seated at the time of the event, but the aircraft experienced violent shaking and banked to the side. Once the aircraft returned to wings level, the flight crew was able to confirm that no passengers had been injured, however both cabin crew members sustained minor injuries. Emergency medical services (EMS) was requested upon arrival at KLGA, and both cabin crew members were released after examination. The flight crew were relieved for the return leg back to CYUL. Following an inspection by the operator’s maintenance, the aircraft was returned to service.

N908AR, a Boeing 747-400 aircraft operated by Skylease Cargo, was conducting flight KYE4854 from Chicago/O’Hare Intl (KORD), IL to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS, with 4 crew members and no cargo onboard. The flight crew conducted the ILS Runway 14 approach, and touched down at 0906Z. During the landing, the aircraft overran the runway, continued past the RESA, and went through the approach lights of Runway 32. The aircraft came to a stop 695 feet (210 meters) past the end of the runway, and remained within the airport perimeter, sustaining substantial damage. There was a post impact fire in the tail section, caused by the number 2 engine separating from the wing. All occupants suffered minor injuries and were taken to the hospital. ARFF responded. The TSB deployed a team of investigators to the site.

C-FGCN, a Boeing 737-300 aircraft operated by Canadian North, was conducting flight MPE438 from Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT with 4 crew members and 24 passengers on board. As the aircraft was climbing through FL320 during the flight, the flight crew received a Cabin Altitude warning light. The QRH procedure was executed, however the flight crew was unable to control the cabin altitude. Therefore, a rapid descent to 10 000 feet was initiated, and the flight crew declared an emergency. The aircraft returned to CYEG without further incident. The operator’s maintenance discovered that an air regulator canon plug had become disconnected. The situation was rectified, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWEP, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3155 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Kelowna (CYLW), BC. During the departure from CYYC, the aircraft experienced a landing gear malfunction. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, levelled off at 7000 feet, and ran the relevant checklist items. After consulting with the operator’s maintenance, the aircraft returned to CYYC and landed uneventfully. ARFF was not required.The operator’s maintenance replaced the nose landing gear center electrical harness and rigged the proximity sensors. The system was tested with no further issues. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GAPY, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA352 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON. During the departure from CYYC off Runway 35L, the aircraft encountered a flock of birds. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight crew requested to return to CYYC where they landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance found damage to the number 1 engine intake leading edge at the 6 o'clock position, in addition to two fan blades that appeared to be bent. The number 2 engine suffered 7 bent fan blades at the mid-span point. The number 1 engine cowl was replaced, a borescope was carried out and no internal damage was found. Fan blades were inspected and were within limits. A borescope inspection was also carried out on the number 2 engine, and no internal damage was found. All fan blades were removed, and seven blades were replaced. Both engines were tested, and the aircraft was returned to service.

N281QS, a corporate Dassault Aviation Falcon 2000 aircraft operated by Constellation Productions Inc,  was conducting a flight from Shannon Intl (EINN), Ireland to Presque Isle/Northern Maine Regional (KPQI), ME. During cruise flight, the destination airport (KPQI) was impacted by a substantial storm and became unsuitable for a landing. Additionally, the flight experienced stronger headwinds during the oceanic crossing, which rendered their filed alternate airport of Quebec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC below minimum fuel requirements. The flight crew determined that an unplanned stop was required for refueling, and requested a diversion to Fredericton Intl (CYFC), NB. The aircraft landed, refueled, and continued on to its final destination of Washington/Dulles Intl (KIAD), VA.

C-FRTU, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA848 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to London/Heathrow (EGLL), England with 10 crew members and 298 passengers on board. When the aircraft was cruising at FL290 in the vicinity of Quebec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC, a passenger in the forward section of the aircraft inadvertently dropped an eReader down inside the seat mechanism. The seat was moved by the passenger, which caused damage to the eReader. Smoke was observed, heat began emanating from the unit’s battery, and the case started to melt. The cabin crew was able to retrieve the device and contained the risk of fire with the use of 2 fire extinguishers and 2 smoke hoods. The damaged unit was placed in a Portable Electronic Device Fire bag. The flight continued to destination without further incident.The operator’s maintenance replaced the seat cover, as well as the emergency equipment used. The aircraft was returned to service.

Approximately 70nm east of Lester B. Pearson Intl-Toronto (CYYZ) an Air Canada Airbus A330-300 aircraft (flight AC7140) was cleared by ATC to descend to 17,000 feet.  Approximately 3nm behind the A330 was a WestJet Encoure DHC-8-402 (flight WEN3533) descending through 17200 feet. Separation between the two aircraft reduced to 3nm in an area where 5nm or 1000 feet is required.

C-FUCS, a WestJet Boeing 737-800 operating as flight WJ547, was on route from St. John's Intl. (CYYT) to Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto  (CYYZ) when a flight attendant became incapacitated. The flight duties for landing were distributed amongst remaining flight attendants.

C-GNON, a DH8C aircraft operated Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8246 from Vancouver International Airport (CYVR), BC to Castlegar/West Kootenay Regional Airport (CYCG), BC. While in cruise flight at 125 nautical miles from CYCG, the oil pressure for the #1 engine dropped to zero with no associated caution or warning messages. The crew shut down the #1 engine, declared an emergency, and returned to Vancouver where the aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance found a pair of wires in the #1 engine oil pressure circuit that failed the insulation checks. The wires were replaced and the engine disconnect harness P29 to firewall connector 9811 P17 was also replaced due to corrosion.

C-FJCQ, an ATR 72-200 aircraft operated by Calm Air, was conducting flight CAV117 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with 4 crew members and 43 passengers on board. While en route, at approximately 150 nautical miles north of CYWG, the flight crew observed instrument fluctuations on the number 1 (right) engine and the torque rolled back to 37%. The flight crew then selected continuous relight and the engine torque slowly recovered to cruise value. Approximately 30 minutes later, the right engine dropped to 0% torque. The flight crew secured the engine and completed the ATR QRH checklist for "engine flame-out in flight". Included in the checklist is an option to attempt a re-start of the engine. The flight crew successfully restarted the engine and landed uneventfully at CYWG.During a subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance, the #1 engine EEC, the #1 engine high-pressure fuel pump and the MFCU were inspected and replaced. Ground runs were carried out with no faults found, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FCSL, a privately operated Piper PA-42 aircraft, was approaching Ottawa/Carp (CYRP), ON under visual flight rules (VFR) with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. C-FGMZ, a privately operated Cessna 150G aircraft, was also operating in the vicinity of CYRP with only the pilot on board. At approximately 1010 EST, both aircraft collided while they were in the circuit within the downwind area for Runway 28. One of the wings of the Cessna 150G was partially severed, which rendered the aircraft uncontrollable. The aircraft impacted the ground, and there was a post impact fire. The pilot was fatally injured, and the aircraft was destroyed. The pilot of C-FCSL notified ATC, and diverted to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON where the aircraft landed successfully on Runway 32. C-FCSL sustained damage to the wings, main landing gear, aft fuselage and rudder. The weather conditions at the time of the accident was a few clouds, and a visibility of 20 sm. The TSB is investigating.

C-GZOX, a Air Nunavut Ltd. Dassault Falcon FA20 (BFF20) was on route from Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT) to Oshawa Executive - Toronto (CYOO) when the crew received a warning for a left fuel boost pump failure. The crew followed the QRH procedures and declared an emergency. The aircraft was diverted to Sault Ste. Marie (CYAM). The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. Maintenance replaced the fuel boost pump and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GRFF, a privately operated Piper PA-46-350P aircraft, was conducting an IFR flight from Columbia/Metro (KCAE), SC to West Palm Beach/North Palm Beach County General Aviation (F45), FL with only the pilot on board. Upon receiving progressive taxi instructions to the active runway in good, daylight weather conditions and visibility, the pilot stopped the aircraft and asked Ground Control if he should turn left “here”. Ground Control confirmed, and the pilot proceeded without realizing that it was a service road and not a taxiway. Subsequently, the bottom of the aircraft’s left wing collided with a low stop sign. The pilot secured the aircraft, had it inspected, and continued to his destination. The aircraft was later flown to Canada where internal structural damage to the left wing and flap were found.

C-FKAU, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA90 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to São Paulo/Guarulhos Intl (SBGR), Brazil. During cruise flight at FL350, the flight crew reported severe turbulence that lasted approximately 2 minutes, with altitude excursions. There were no reported injuries, nor any damage to the aircraft. The flight continued to destination without further incident. Maintenance personnel performed the severe or unusual turbulence inspection, and no faults were found.

C-FSNS, a privately operated Murphy Renegade Spirit Advanced Ultra-light aircraft, was conducting a local flight from a private grass strip near Rochester, AB with only the pilot on board. During the approach phase of the flight with the intention to land, the pilot reportedly believed that the aircraft experienced a microburst on final approach. The pilot attempted to execute a go-around and applied full power. After the aircraft had past the end of the runway, a strong tail wind was encountered and effective control of the aircraft was lost. The pilot executed a forced landing into a wheat field, adjacent to the runway. During the landing, the aircraft nosed over onto its back and was substantially damaged. There were no injuries.

C-FIVQ, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA15 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Hong Kong/Chek Lap Kok Intl, (VHHH) Hong Kong with 17 crew members and 380 passengers on board. During cruise flight in the vicinity of Beijing/Capital Intl (ZBAA), China, the flight crew was advised that there was smoke and a strong burning smell in the cabin, in the area of seats 12 DEF, simultaneously receiving a RECIRC FAN message. The flight crew elected to divert to ZBAA, however did not declare an emergency. The Recirc Fan was turned off, and the smoke quickly dissipated. The aircraft landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance met the aircraft at ZBAA. The Upper Recirc Fan was identified as the source; the area was inspected and no damage was found. The unit was deactivated, and the aircraft was released under MEL provisions. The flight departed for VHHH without further incident, and there were no further reports of odour.

C-FIUA, a Boeing 777-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA34 from Sydney/Kingsford Smith (YSSY), Australia to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 14 crew members and 281 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL360, approximately 880 nm South West of CYVR, the aircraft experienced a right bleed failure. Since the flight had been released with the left bleed under Minimum Equipment List (MEL) provisions, the flight crew descended to FL220, started the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU), and successfully reset the right hand bleed. As a precaution, the flight crew elected to remain at FL220 for the remainder of the flight, and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident.

D-AIMJ, an Airbus 380-841 aircraft operated by Lufthansa, was conducting flight DLH401 from New York/John F. Kennedy Intl (KJFK), NY to Frankfurt/Rhein-Main Intl (EDDF), Germany with 23 crew members and 432 passengers on board. During cruise flight approximately 190 nm southeast of Gander Intl (CYQX), NL, the flight crew smelled smoke on board and requested a diversion to either KJFK or Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl (KBOS), MA. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks, while some of the cabin crew members donned their smoke hoods. The QRH procedure for smoke/fumes was executed, and the environmental system was suspected as a source of the smell; consequently, the number 1 environmental pack was shut off. Cabin crew members reported feeling sick, which prompted the flight crew to consider Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS as a possible diversion option. While the flight crew started to jettison fuel in preparation for the landing, KBOS was selected for the diversion as the air condition in the aircraft had improved. Enroute, the flight crew noticed that the number 2 engine (Rolls Royce Trent 970B-84) oil quantity was decreasing. Approaching KBOS, medical services were requested to meet the aircraft at the gate. The aircraft landed without further incident.  Two cabin crew members received medical attention following the landing at KBOS. Maintenance personnel determined that there had been an internal oil leak on the number 2 engine, which was the source of the smell. The operator proceeded to ferry the aircraft to its home base (EDDF) on a manufacturer-approved 3-engine ferry.

C-FHNV, an Embraer ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA502 from Chicago/O'Hare Intl (KORD), IL to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. Climbing through 3000 feet after the departure from KORD, the flight crew received a Pitch Trim Fail Message. A PAN PAN was declared, and a return to KORD was completed uneventfully. Maintenance performed ground tests, no faults were found.

C-GGTS, an Airbus 330-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC588 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Paris/Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), France with 11 crew members and 294 passengers on board. As the flight crew selected flaps to CONF 2 during the approach to Runway 27R at LFPG, they received a F/CTL FLAPS LOCKED ECAM message. A missed approach was executed, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN, and the aircraft was levelled off at 5000 feet in order to carry out ECAM and QRH actions. A second approach was executed and, following the landing on Runway 27L, the flight crew stopped the aircraft on a rapid exit taxiway to allow ARFF to inspect the landing gear and flaps. The aircraft subsequently taxied to the gate.The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and discovered the left hand Asymmetry Position Pick-Off Unit (APPU) outside of tolerance. The unit was adjusted in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM), and the aircraft was released back to service.

C-GLQN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE486 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC to Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON with 4 crew members and 17 passengers on board. Just prior to levelling off at FL220, the flight crew received a Fuselage Door warning, associated with a gradual climb indication in the cabin altitude. The flight crew decided to begin a descent to 14 000 feet, and declared a PAN PAN. During the descent, the cabin altitude began to increase. The flight crew decided to divert to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON, and declared an emergency. As the aircraft descended through 12 000 feet, the aircraft experienced a complete loss of pressurization. The flight crew briefed the passengers and proceeded to land uneventfully on Runway 07 with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance found the cargo door handle had become unstowed in flight, which deflated the door seal and depressurized the aircraft. The aircraft has been returned to service without further incident.

C-GJVW, a Fairchild SA227-DC aircraft operated by Bearskin Airlines, was conducting training flight BLS101T 25 nm North East of North Bay (CYYB), ON. During the training exercise, the landing gear was selected to the down position, but the nose gear did not indicate down and locked. The flight crew performed troubleshooting, and completed the emergency extension as per the SOPs and AFM; however, the nose gear continued to indicate unlocked. The aircraft initially proceeded to CYYB, but then rerouted to Sudbury (CYSB), ON for operational reasons. The flight crew declared an emergency and, approximately 2 nm on final to CYSB, the nose gear indicated down and locked. The landing was uneventful with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance completed landing gear swings, with no faults found. The nose gear down switch (R/H) was replaced for troubleshooting. A successful test flight was completed with no further faults.

C-FMPN, an Embraer EMB-505 300 Phenom aircraft operated by Aurora Jet Partners, was conducting a flight from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC, to Scottsdale (KSDL), AZ with 2 crew members and 2 passengers on board. During the climb from FL390 to FL410 south of the SEA VOR, the flight crew was alerted to multiple BATT EXCEEDANCE CAS messages that remained on briefly, and then extinguished. The messages appeared for a third time, and remained on. The flight crew requested a diversion to Yakima Air Terminal/McAllister Field (KYKM), WA, and declared a PAN PAN. A normal approach and landing on Runway 27 was conducted at KYKM without further incident, with ARFF standing by.As a precaution, ARFF scanned both aircraft batteries with a Thermal Imaging Camera (TIC), and no abnormal heat signatures were detected. Maintenance personnel replaced the number 1 Starter/Generator and the number 1 Generator Control Unit. Function tests were completed with no faults found and the aircraft was returned to service.

N15912, an Embraer EMB-145LR aircraft operated by Express Jet, was conducting flight ASQ4137 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS to Newark /Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ with 3 crew members and 36 passengers on board. Climbing through 1800 feet after the departure from CYHZ, the lavatory smoke detector indication activated, and the cabin crew and passengers indicated the presence of smoke. The flight crew actioned the checklist, and requested to return to CYHZ where an uneventful landing was conducted. No emergency was declared, and the flight crew did not use their oxygen masks. Once on the ground, the smoke could not be duplicated by maintenance. The aircraft was ferried to KEWR where further maintenance is being conducted.

N660UA, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL931 from Chicago/O'Hare Intl (KORD), IL to London/Heathrow (EGLL), UK with 11 crew members and 178 passengers on board. Approximately 100 nm southwest of Goose Bay (CYYR), NL, the flight crew declared an emergency and requested a diversion to CYYR due to a cracked windscreen. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYYR.

C-GMQZ, un appareil de type Pilatus PC-12/45 exploité par Chrono Aviation, effectuait le vol NDL432 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/St-Hubert (CYHU), QC à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB), QC avec 2 membres d’équipage et 1 passager à bord. Peu avant l’arrivée à CYQB, le voyant d’indication de défaillance du générateur numéro 1 (GEN 1 fail) s’est allumé. L’équipage a alors effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH). La procédure alternative de sortie des roues a été suivie, toutefois la roue de nez ne s’est pas verrouillée lors de l’approche pour la piste 29 à CYQB. L’équipage a déclaré un PAN PAN, et a interrompu l’approche en effectuant une remontée. La procédure alternative de sortie des roues a été suivie de nouveau avec succès, et l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 29.Le personnel de l’entretien a inspecté et remplacé le générateur (GEN 1).

C-GIGK, a de Havilland DHC-6 aircraft operated by Transwest Air LP, was conducting a flight from Pelican Narrows (CJW4), SK to Prince Albert (Glass Field) (CYPA), SK. Shortly after levelling off at 8 000 ft ASL, the flight crew noticed that the left engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-27) oil pressure was indicating 20 psi. The oil temperature was normal and the low oil pressure annunciator was not illuminated. The flight crew elected to shut the engine down and divert to La Ronge (Barber Field) (CYVC), SK. The memory and QRH checklist items were completed to secure the engine, and the passengers were briefed. The flight crew declared an emergency and requested ARFF response. The subsequent landing was successful with the left engine inoperative. The operator's maintenance replaced the left engine oil pressure indicator.

TF-CAT, un appareil de type Airbus 321-200 exploité par WOW Air EHF, effectuait le vol WOW251 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Reykjavík/Keflavík (BIKF), Islande à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. Après l’arrêt complet de l’appareil à la barrière A68 à CYUL, un membre du personnel de manutention a remarqué une échelle, ayant possiblement servi afin de brancher le groupe électrogène (GPU), coincée sous le nez de l’avion. Le débarquement des passagers et l’avitaillement de l’avion ont possiblement occasionné un déplacement du centre de gravité vers l’avant, provoquant ainsi un abaissement du nez sur l'échelle qui avait été laissée sur place. Le nez de l’avion a été soulevé avec un vérin hydraulique, ce qui a permis le retrait de l’échelle. Les dommages à l'appareil sont de nature mineure, et l’appareil a été remis en service. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FACV, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8345 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB for Regina Intl (CYQR), SK. Following the landing at CYQR, the aircraft was being marshalled to Gate 6 with the assistance of a ground crew when the aircraft was jolted. The flight crew did not receive a stop signal from the marshaller, and the left wing struck the canvas bridge canopy. There was no obvious visible damage to the aircraft. Upon investigation, it was determined that the bridge had not been reset to its position from the previous flight. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft prior to returning it to service.

C-GJGW, un appareil de type Cessna 310R exploité par Grondair, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis St-Frédéric (CSZ4), QC à destination de St-Georges (CYSG), QC avec 1 pilote-instructeur et 1 élève-pilote à bord. Au moment d’exécuter l’arrondi lors d’un posé-décollé sur la piste 24 de CYSG, l’appareil s’est mis à dériver vers la gauche. L’instructeur a pris les commandes pour ramener l’avion au centre de la piste et, suite à un atterrissage ferme, l’appareil a dérivé vers la droite. L’instructeur a manœuvré afin de corriger la dérive, mais l’appareil a effectué une embardée vers la gauche et a dérapé. Voyant que la sortie de piste était inévitable, l’instructeur a coupé l’arrivée d’essence aux moteurs, et l’appareil s’est immobilisé dans le fossé qui longe la piste 24. Les deux occupants n’ont pas été blessés et ont pu évacuer sans difficulté. L’avion a subi des dommages au train d’atterrissage, aux hélices et aux ailes.

C-FAMC, a Fairchild SA227-AC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting flight PAG416 from Shamattawa (CZTM), MB to Thompson (CYTH), MB. When the aircraft entered clouds during cruise flight, the flight crew selected the engine intake heat to the on position. Shortly after, the flight crew began to smell a toxic odour on the flight deck. Before the flight crew could determine the source of the smell, the aircraft exited clouds, and the engine intake heat was turned off. Subsequently, the aircraft re-entered clouds, and the flight crew re-selected the engine intake heat on again. Smoke coming from the J-box/left essential bus area was then noticed. The flight crew notified ATC, declared a PAN PAN, and completed the associated procedures in accordance with SOP's and the aircraft flight manual. Engine intake heat was then selected off as the aircraft was in VMC conditions, and the smoke dissipated from the aircraft. The flight landed at CYTH without further incident.The operator's maintenance replaced 2 current limiters and terminal blocks in the J-box. Ground runs were completed, and aircraft was returned to service.

C-FMWP, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU2363 from Shannon Intl (EINN), Ireland to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. When the flight crew selected Flaps 15 during the approach to Runway 23 at CYYZ, they received a TE FLAP DISAGREE EICAS message. The approach was discontinued, and the flight crew executed QRH procedures. The fault did not clear and, consequently, a PAN PAN was declared. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance determined the #1 RVDT was out of limits and subsequently proceeded to replace it. An operational check of the system revealed no further faults, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBHM, an Airbus 319-114 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA585 from Newark/Liberty Intl (KEWR), NJ to Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB. N34HP, a privately operated Piper PA-34-200T Seneca aircraft, was operating on an IFR flight plan from Great Falls Intl (KGTF), MT to CYYC. N34HP was instructed to fly the visual approach for Runway 35L. In the vicinity of Waypoint GABOL, ATC observed N34HP turning right toward the approach for Runway 35R, while ACA585 was established on the approach for that runway. The separation between N34HP and ACA585 reduced to 2.7 miles horizontally and 700 feet vertically, where 3.0 miles or 1000 feet is required. ATC subsequently recleared N34HP for the Runway 35L approach.

C-GSOT, a privately registered Kitfox S6 Amateur Built aircraft, was conducting a local flight from a private property, 2.3 nm North Northeast of Gull Lake (CJK5), SK with only the pilot onboard. The takeoff run was conducted up-hill, into wind, on a farm field. Immediately after liftoff, the aircraft began to drift to the left.
