Subsequently, the left wing dropped and the aircraft touched down, skidded, and then overturned. The pilot was wearing a four point restraint system, and was uninjured. The aircraft sustained damage to the wings, vertical stabilizer, propeller, and engine.

C-GKGC, a Bombardier CL 600-2B19 (CRJ200) aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7367 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Detroit/Metro Wayne County (KDTW), MI. After the landing gear was selected up shortly after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew received a NOSE GEAR DOOR OPEN warning message. The flight crew elected to return to CYYZ and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed uneventfully on Runway 23 with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance checked Proximity Switch Electronic Unit (PSEU) codes, which indicated that the nose landing gear was not fully extended. The oleo was serviced, and after the landing gear was swung, no further faults were detected. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GBUU, a de Havilland DHC-8-106 aircraft operated by Regional 1 Airlines Ltd., was conducting flight TSH141 from Lansdowne House (CYLH), ON to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON with 3 crew and 23 passengers on board. During descent, the flight crew noticed that the No. 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW121) torque indication had decreased to 0 foot-pounds, and the propeller revolutions per minute remained in the prohibited range. The flight crew evaluated the condition as an engine failure without the propeller auto-feathering. They shut down the engine in accordance with the company standard operating procedures and declared an emergency with ATC. The subsequent landing was conducted without further incident with the No. 1 engine inoperative. After ARFF conducted an inspection for fire, smoke, or damage, the aircraft was taxied to the apron. The operator's maintenance personnel inspected the engine. During an attempted ground run, the engine would not accelerate past 20% Nh. The engine was replaced due to a suspected turbine seizure.

C-FJTS, a Fairchild SA227-AC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting flight PAG118 from Cross Lake (Charlie Sinclair Memorial) (CYCR), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. During the climb out of CYCR, the RH Chip Detect annunciator light illuminated. The flight crew executed QRH actions, and monitored the annunciator during the climb. There were no other anomalous engine indications, and the annunciator extinguished when the aircraft levelled off at FL220. Approximately 140 nm North of CYWG, the right engine (Garrett TPE331-11U-612G) experienced a complete power loss. The flight crew carried out the related QRH actions, declared an emergency and selected transponder code 7700. The subsequent landing was uneventful with the right engine inoperative, and ARFF responding. The operator's maintenance examined the engine oil filter and a large quantity of metal particles was found. The engine was removed for repairs. During the engine tear down, it was determined that the Fuel Control Unit drive gear bearing had failed. An SDR was submitted.

C-GWFE, a DHC-8-400 operated by WestJet Encore as flight WEN3606 from Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ)  to General Edward Lawrence Logan IntL (KBOS) was struck by lightning during its descent through 6000 feet. A Pan Pan was declared. ARFF met the aircraft on the taxiway and at the gate; no issues were reported after the inspection.

C-FPPW, a de Havilland DHC-8-106 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting flight PAG664 from Sioux Lookout (CYXL), ON for Sandy Lake (CZSJ), ON with 3 crew members and 4 passengers on board. When the aircraft was approximately 60 nm North Northwest of CYXL, the flight crew received a Primary Inverter caution light. As the flight crew actioned the QRH, they detected a burning smell in the cockpit. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks, completed the QRH for smoke, declared an emergency and advised ATC that they were diverting to Red Lake (CYRL), ON. The flight attendant was informed of the situation, and confirmed that there was no smoke in the cabin. PAG664 landed in CYRL without further incident, with ARFF on standby. The flight crew shut the engines down on the taxiway, and passengers disembarked via the main cabin door. The operator's maintenance personnel were dispatched to CYXL. The aircraft was flown to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB under MEL 24-02-1. Subsequently, the primary inverter was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FGZI, an MD A4N aircraft operated by Top Aces, was conducting a local flight from Wittmund/Wittmundhafen (ETNT). During the approach the generator failed; no reset was possible. The emergency generator was deployed, an emergency declared, with an uneventful landing at ETNT.

C-GFEH, a Boeing 737-800 was being operated by Sunwing as flight SWG643 from Frank País International Airport - Holguín (MUHG) to Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ). At FL360 on B503 south of HANKX intersection, a TCAS Traffic Advisory was received for traffic climbing from the north west. The traffic continued to climb until showing -500 feet on the navigation display, at which point a TCAS Resolution Advisory, Climb, Climb, was received. The flight crew followed the TCAS RA to climb and advised ATC. 36500 feet was maintained until clear of conflict, then the aircraft returned to FL360. The flight continued uneventfully.

P4-LAS, a Lockheed L-382 (C130) Hercules aircraft operated by Lynden Air Cargo, was conducting flight LYC408 from Iqaluit (CYFB), NU to Anchorage/Ted Stevens Intl (PANC), AK with 4 crew members on board. During cruise flight at FL240, the flight crew received a Prop Oil warning light on the number 1 engine (Allison 501-D22A). The flight crew followed the appropriate checklist and elected to shut the engine down. An emergency was declared, and the flight crew elected to divert to Yellowknife (CYZF), NT where the aircraft landed without further incident. A subsequent inspection by the operator’s maintenance found that the propeller seal on the number 1 engine had failed.

N679SA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (CRJ200) aircraft operated by SkyWest Airlines, was conducting flight SKW5480 from Chicago/O’Hare Intl (KORD), IL to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW), ON with 3 crew members and 50 passengers on board. During the descent into CYOW, the flight attendant contacted the flight crew and reported an odour in the cabin, and fumes coming from the overhead bin in Row 9. The flight crew declared an emergency and initiated an expedited approach. The captain advised the flight attendant to prepare for a normal landing, and a possible evacuation if there was a fire. The passengers were briefed, and the aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. ARFF inspected the aircraft and found no indication of a fire or smoke. The aircraft was released, and the flight crew taxied to the gate. The operator’s maintenance operated both air conditioning packs, the APU and the two engines as per AMM 21-50-00 procedures, and determined the smoke was a result of water condensation from the lower air conditioning vent. The aircraft was released back into service.

C-FNOG, a Boeing 787-9 operated by Air Canada as flight AC845, from Rhein-Main - Frankfurt (EDDF) to Calgary Intl - Calgary (CYYC) encountered severe turbulence during its first hour of flight. There were no injuries; the aircraft continued to destination uneventfully.

C-FGFZ, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA754 from San Francisco Intl (KSFO), CA, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. When the flight was on the downwind for Runway 23 at CYYZ, the aircraft was struck by lightning. The flight crew declared an emergency and requested ARFF to be on standby for the landing. After the uneventful landing, ARFF released the aircraft to proceed to the gate. The operator’s maintenance performed a lightning strike inspection prior to releasing the aircraft back into service.

ACA7140, an Airbus 330-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting a flight from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, (CYUL), QC, to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON. WEN3533, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was also conducting a flight from CYUL to CYYZ. When both aircraft were in descent approximately 70 nm East of CYYZ, ACA7140 was at FL190 and was given clearance to descend to 17 000 feet. The separation was compromised when ACA7140 descended through FL180, 3 nm ahead of WEN3533 at 17200 feet, in an area where 1000 feet or 5 nm was the standard. Nav Canada has started an investigation into this event.

C-GIRE, un AutoGyro Cavalon en exploitation privée effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Trois-Rivières, QC (CYQR) à destination de La Tuque, QC (CYLQ) avec un pilote et un passager à son bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en croisière à une altitude de 2000 pieds au-dessus du sol (AGL), le pilote a rencontré des conditions météorologiques défavorables. Le pilote a choisi de faire demi-tour, et a modifié son plan de vol à destination de Victoriaville, QC (CSR3). Alors que l’appareil se trouvait à proximité de St-Luc-de-Vicennes, le pilote a effectué une descente et l’appareil s’est retrouvé en vol lent. En raison de sa basse altitude, le pilote n’a pas été en mesure de récupérer la vitesse nécessaire afin d’effectuer une remontée. L’appareil a percuté le sol et a subi des dommages importants. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FKPT, an A320-200, was operated by Air Canada as flight AC716 from Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) to LaGuardia (KLGA). After landing, C-FKPT was instructed by ATC to hold at Bravo and Gulf taxiways. N432YX, an Embraer 175 operated by Republic Airlines as flight RPA4589, from St. Louis Lambert International Airport (KSTL) to KLGA was instructed by ATC to hold at Romeo and Gulf when it clipped the left winglet of the stationary aircraft, C-FKPT. The Air Canada crew contacted ATC immediately and the Port Authority Operation, police and fire showed up to their gates (A7 and A5). There were no injuries; both aircraft sustained minor damage to their winglets. The CVR and DFDR were pulled from C-FKPT and reactivated. Maintenance is conducting the required inspections.

C-FEJD, an EMB170-200 was being operated by Sky Regional Airlines as flight SKV7672 from Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) to General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl - Boston (KBOS). During the climb through FL300 for FL310 the crew noticed the cabin altitude was at 8000 feet and in the amber caution range. A descent was requested and at FL290 the cabin altitude continued to rise with a Cabin Altitude High message. A full emergency descent was completed with a descent to 10000 feet. An emergency was declared by the crew with a request to divert to Albany International Airport (KALB). The aircraft landed on RWY28 KALB uneventfully with ARFF on standby. The aircraft was inspected and ferried to CYYZ for further maintenance.

C-FOGV, a Bell 206L-3 aircraft operated by Sky Helicopters, was conducting a sight-seeing flight from Pitt Meadows (CYPK), BC with 1 pilot and 4 passengers on board. Shortly after the helicopter decelerated below 30 knots during an approach to land at 4100 feet ASL on a mountain ridge, 17 nm North of CYPK, it began an uncommanded yaw to the right, despite full left pedal input by the pilot. The helicopter spun several times before it hit terrain short of the intended site, and subsequently rolled onto its right side. This sequence is consistent with a loss of tail rotor effectiveness (LTE). The pilot and 1 passenger received minor injuries, while the other 3 passengers were uninjured. Fuel began to spill from the helicopter, however there was no fire. The aircraft was damaged beyond economical repair. The pilot manually activated the ELT, and called the operator to report the accident. All occupants were airlifted to CYPK where ambulances transported them to the hospital.The operator’s weight and balance calculations indicated that the helicopter was 271 pounds below maximum takeoff weight when it departed CYPK. Density altitude at the accident site was about 5300 feet, and there was little or no wind at the time of the accident.

C-FZMD, a privately registered Cessna 172K aircraft, was conducting a flight in the vicinity of Westwold BC, for the purposes of filming a wing walking stunt for a music video, with 1 pilot and 2 skydivers on board.  At approximately 7000 feet ASL, one of the skydiving passengers climbed out of the right hand side of the aircraft and up onto the right wing. Shortly thereafter, the second skydiving passenger climbed out onto the right hand landing gear to film the first passenger. The passenger on the right wing laid down parallel to the direction of flight, and began to move slowly toward the tip of the wing. Suddenly, the aircraft entered a spiral dive, with the right wing low. The pilot then motioned to the second passenger to release from the aircraft's landing gear, while the aircraft continued to spiral to the right. C-GAGP, a Cessna 310Q aircraft registered to Eagle Eye Aviation, was filming the stunt and declared an emergency when the pilot noticed that C-FZMD was in the spiral dive. After an undetermined amount of revolutions to the right, the pilot of C-FZMD regained control of the aircraft at approximately 1500 feet AGL. It is unknown when the passenger on the top of the wing departed the wing surface; his parachute failed to open and he suffered fatal injuries. The second skydiving passenger deployed his parachute and landed without further incident. The aircraft returned to Vernon, BC (CYVK) and landed without further incident. The RH Aileron and the top wing surface were found damaged. The RCMP is investigating.

C-FCAU, a Cessna 172R aircraft operated by Leading Edge Enterprises, departed from Montreal/St-Hubert (CYHU), QC for a local VFR flight with two crew members on board. Climbing through 800 feet after the departure from CYHU, the pilot felt abnormal restrictions and limited roll deflection when using the ailerons. The pilot declared an emergency, and returned to CYHU where an uneventful landing was carried out. An inspection of the aircraft by an AME could not identify what the problem was, and could not duplicate the issue.

TF-ISJ un appareil de type Boeing 757-200 exploité par Icelandair sous l'indicatif de vol ICE688 avec à son bord 7 membres d'équipage et 155 passagers effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments d'Orlando Intl (Floride) à destination de Keflavik (Islande). Alors que l'appareil était environ 50 miles au sud-est de l'aéroport de Bagotville (CYBG) Québec au FL350 le commandant de bord a observé la présence d'un arc électrique dans le coin droit du parebrise avant gauche ( L FWD WINDOW). Le chauffe parbrise a été fermé et peu de temps après, un fort bruit de craquement s'est fait entendre. L'équipage de conduite a mis leur masque d'oxygène et a déclaré un MAYDAY dû à la fissure du pare-brise avant gauche et effectué une descente d'urgence. En passant le FL250 et constatant que la pression cabine était demeurée constante la descente d'urgence a été interrompue. Le commandant de bord a retiré son masque d'oxygène, mais le premier officier l'a gardé par précaution. Une descente normale a été poursuivie et l'équipage de conduite a demandé un déroutement vers CYBG où l'appareil s’est posé sans problème.

C-GFBW, un hélicoptère de type AS 350 B2 avec à son bord 1 pilote et 1 passager devait déposer une charge à la longue élingue dans un endroit restreint sur un site de télécommunication en forêt près de Poste Montagnais (QUE). Lors de l'approche finale, la charge s'est appuyée sur les fils de ligne de distribution électrique. Le pilote a interrompu l'approche, toute fois le fil neutre est resté accroché à la charge. Le pilote a donc déposé la charge sur place, a décroché l'élingue et s’est éloigné sans autres incidents. Personne n'a été blessé et l'hélicoptère n'a subi aucun dommage.

C-FHVO un hélicoptère de type EC130 T2 en exploitation privée décollait d'un espace restreint à environ 50 miles à l'est de Lebel-sur Quévillon (QUE) lorsque les pales du rotor principal sont entrées en contact avec des branches d'arbres environnants. Le pilote a réussi à poser l'appareil. Le pilote seul à bord n'a pas été blessé. Les 3 pales du rotor principal ont été endommagées.

C-FACT, a de Havilland DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8861 from Gander Intl (CYQX), NL, to Halifax/Stanfield Intl (CYHZ), NS. Shortly after the departure from CYQX, the number 2 engine went into an uncommanded feather. The flight crew shut the number 2 engine down in accordance with the QRH, declared an emergency and, since the weather at CYQX was at minimums, diverted to Deer Lake (CYDF), NL. The flight landed at CYDF without further incident.An analysis of the uncommanded auto-feather of the number 2 engine determined that it was caused by a loss of the number 2 engine torque signal. The related torque signal sensing/transmitting components have been sent to the manufacturer for further investigation.

C-GGJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 was being operated by Jazz as flight JZA8824 from Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl - Montreal (CYUL) to Ronald Reagan Washington D.C. (KDCA). During the approach the crew selected flaps and they failed at zero degrees. The QRH was followed and the flight crew  diverted the aircraft to Washington Dulles Intl - Washington, DC  (KIAD) for a longer runway. They declared an emergency, advised the passengers and the aircraft landed uneventfully. After taxing off the taxiway, AARF inspected the aircraft. The flaps could not be reset, the next flight was cancelled for maintenance.

C-GTMB, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Services (EVAS), was conducting flight EVS807 from Goose Bay (CYYR), NL to Gander Intl (CYQX), NL. Approximately 20 nm North of CYQX, the flight crew received a Right Engine Bleed Line failure warning. The flight crew executed the check list and switched the right bleed air valve off. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight landed at CYQX without further incident.The operator’s maintenance determined that a faulty bleed air warning temperature sensor caused the false indication.

C-GHDM, un appareil de type Aero Commander 112 exploité privément, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue de Ste-Hyacinthe, QC (CSU3) à destination de Joliette, QC (CSG3) avec seul le pilote à bord. Au moment de l'atterrissage le pilote a oublié de déployer le train d'atterrissage et l'aéronef a atterri sur le ventre. L'aéronef a subi des dommages importants. Le pilote n'a subi aucune blessure.

C-FMLZ a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1917 from Lisbon/Portela de Sacavem, Portugal (LPPT) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 8 crew members and 275 passengers on board. During cruise flight in the vicinity of St John's Intl, NL (CYYT), a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unfit for duty for the remainder of the flight. The aircraft continued to destination and the remaining cabin crew were reassigned to ensure the exits were manned for the landing in CYYZ.

C-FGZO, an MD A4N aircraft operated by Top Aces, was conducting a local flight from Wittmund/Wittmundhafen, Germany (ETNT). While climbing to FL300, overhead Nordholz Air Base (ETMN), the generator failed and no reset was possible. The emergency generator was deployed, the pilot declared an emergency and a return to ETNT was completed uneventfully. Maintenance found that the power connector of the generator was disconnected and the safety wire was broken.

C-FCBH, a private, Amateur Built Murphy Rebel aircraft, was landing on a privately owned grass airstrip near McKellar, ON. During the landing roll out, the aircraft went off the left side of the runway. The main wheels dug into soft mud, causing the aircraft to nose down into the mud, and settled back on its landing gear. There were no injuries, however the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FLRJ, a BAE Avro RJ85 aircraft operated by Summit Air, was conducting flight FAB956 from Yellowknife (CYZF), NT to Edmonton Intl (CYEG), AB with 4 crew members and 14 passengers on board. During cruise flight enroute to CYEG, the aircraft experienced a pressurization issue. An emergency descent was performed, and the flight crew declared an emergency. The QRH was actioned, and the flight crew elected to return to CYZF where the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance will advise the Transportation Safety Board of their findings.UPDATE January 22, 2019:Upon return to CYZF, the operator's maintenance deferred the aircraft pressurization system. The aircraft was flown unpressurized and without passengers to CYEG where maintenance personnel replaced the pressurization controller and returned the aircraft to service.

C-FHHH an Aerospatiale AS 350 BA helicopter operated by Helicoptères Transit, was operating under a contract with the Société de protection des forêts contre le feu (SOPFEU) to transport firefighters in and out of their assigned area. The pilot landed the helicopter in a remote staging area established for fire #368, located 50 nm South East of Lebel-sur-Quévillon (CSH4), QC, in order to pick up firefighters. While lowering the collective lever and awaiting for firefighters to board, the tail rotor impacted a 2 to 3 inch wood log, which immediately caused noticeable vibrations. The pilot shut the engine down, and subsequent inspection revealed substantial impact damage to the tail rotor blades. Repairs were carried out in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions, and the aircraft was returned to service a few days later. The selected landing site was reportedly unprepared and covered with fallen wood debris.

C-FNOH, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA833 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Tel Aviv/Ben Gurion, Israel (LLBG) with 12 crew members and 296 passengers on board. During cruise flight approximately 50 nm North West of Deer Lake, NL (CYDF), a cabin crew member noticed a galley oven in the economy class emitting smoke due to debris that had been left in the oven. The debris, which was not observed during the preflight safety checks, was removed from the oven, and the smoke and smell dissipated. The aircraft continued to destination without further incident.

C-GSAZ, a Piper PA-31 aircraft operated by Globe Hawk Survey, was conducting a flight from Grande Prairie (CYQU), AB to Kamloops (CYKA), BC with 2 persons on board. During cruise flight under Instrument Flight Rules (IFR), the pilot was informed that CYKA was closed to non-scheduled aircraft. The pilot was subsequently cleared to Salmon Arm (CZAM), BC. However, the pilot read a note in the Canada Flight Supplement (CFS) to the effect that “Only pilots familiar with local terrain should use this A/D dur hrs of darkness”. Since he was unfamiliar with CZAM, the pilot declared a fuel emergency and landed without further incident at CYKA.

N427QX, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Horizon Air, was conducting flight QXE2266 from Seattle-Tacoma Intl (KSEA), WA to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 4 crew members and 68 passengers on board. During the final approach to land at CYVR during the hours of darkness, the flight crew observed a large flock of Canadian geese passing in front of the aircraft. In order to avoid hitting the birds, the flight crew pitch the aircraft up and executed a missed approach. Still, the aircraft struck several birds, causing damage to the right wing inboard leading edge. The flight crew declared an emergency, and requested vectors to return to land. ARFF responded and the aircraft landed without further incident.  No injuries were reported.

C-FFZR, a privately registered Pipistrel VIRUS SW, was on a flight from Whitecourt, AB (CYZU) to an unprepared private field near Rich Valley, AB. During landing, the aircraft nosed over and came to rest inverted sustaining substantial damage. There was no post impact fire. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured.

C-FFWN, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft, operated by Air Canada as flight ACA416, with 5 crew members and 145 passengers on board, was conducting a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl), ON (CYYZ) to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). While on short final for Runway 24R at CYUL, an ECAM "AUTO BRK FAULT" caution message appeared. The crew initiated a go-around and requested to be vectored to an area clear of other traffic to perform verifications. Twenty minutes later, the crew declared an emergency and proceeded with the approach and landing which were uneventful. The Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting Services (ARFF) had been deployed.Troubleshooting carried out by the maintenance personnel revealed that contamination was present on pin "F" of connector 15GG-A of the brake servo valve #1. The pin was replaced and operational tests were performed satisfactorily. The aircraft was returned in service.

C-FSLZ, a Swearingen SA226-TC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was being prepared for a flight from St. Theresa Point (CYST), MB to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB. While starting the right engine, the flight crew noticed a burning plastic odour, followed by smoke. The flight crew aborted the start, shut off the batteries, and evacuated the aircraft. The flight crew verified that there was no fire, however noticed that the circuit breaker for the co-pilot's standby directional gyro had tripped. The operator's maintenance personnel replaced the affected directional gyro.

C-GMCP, a Bombardier Learjet 45 aircraft operated by Skyservice Business Aviation, was conducting a medevac flight from Terceira/Aeroporto das Lajes (LPLA), Portugal, to St. John’s Intl (CYYT), NL with 4 crew members and 2 passengers on board. During the climb through FL300 after the departure from LPLA, the flight crew noticed the cabin altitude was climbing at an abnormally high rate. The flight crew stopped the climb at FL330, and switched the pressurization to manual mode; however, there was no effect. The decision to return to LPLA was elected, and a PAN PAN was declared. The aircraft landed at LPLA uneventfully. An inspection revealed that the cockpit muffler assembly was cracked.

C-ILUX, a private Quad City Challenger II Advanced Ultra-light aircraft, departed Ottawa/Carp (CYRP), ON for Peterborough (CYPQ), ON with 1 pilot on board. During cruise flight approximately 3.6 nm South of CYRP, control of the aircraft was lost for undetermined reasons. During the uncontrolled descent, the aircraft contacted guy wires running along the side of a road, and collided with terrain. The aircraft was substantially damaged, and the pilot sustained serious injuries.

C-FIES, a private, float-equipped Piper PA-12 aircraft, was departing from Gilles Lake, near Cobalt, ON with 1 pilot and 2 passengers on board. Shortly after the aircraft became airborne, the pilot reportedly encountered rudder control difficulties. The pilot aborted the takeoff, and attempted to land straight ahead on the remaining portion of the lake. The aircraft landed hard, and as a result sustained substantial damage. There were no injuries to the three occupants.

C-GEAS, a Transwest Air Beech 300, was operating from La Ronge, SK (CYVC) to Yellowknife, NT (CYZF). C-GEAS was declared number 1 for the airport via Runway 34. The Buffalo Airways Beechcraft B-55, was operating as BFL55 from Hay River, NT (CYHY) to Yellowknife, NT (CYZF). BFL55 was to proceed behind GEAS on the approach. GEAS slowed faster than the controller anticipated and BLF55 came within 4.2 nm horizontally and 900 feet vertically where 5 nm or 1000 feet are required. Separation was re-established 30 seconds later.

C-GJZC, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA535 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Thunder Bay (CYQT), ON. When the flight crew selected landing gear down during the final approach to Runway 25 at CYQT, the nose-gear doors did not open and, consequently, the nose landing gear did not extend. The amber nose-gear door light did not illuminate, and the red nose-gear unsafe light remained illuminated. Additionally, the landing gear handle also remained illuminated. The flight crew conducted a go-around, and requested ARFF to stand by for the landing. QRH items were executed, and an alternate landing gear release and extension was performed. The subsequent landing on Runway 25 was successful, and the flight crew brought the aircraft to a full stop on the runway with ARFF responding. Gear pins were installed, and the aircraft was towed to the gate.The operator's maintenance replaced the Proximity Sensor Electronic Unit (PSEU), and the aircraft was returned to service.

N423MA, a Swearingen SA227-AC (Metroliner) aircraft operated by Ameriflight LLC, was conducting a cargo flight between Buffalo Niagara International Airport (KBUF) and Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) with 2 pilots on board. During cruise, Cleveland Center informed the flight crew that Airport Services at KBUF airport had found a 2 foot long rubber remain on the runway and that they suspected it came from their aircraft during their takeoff. Montreal ATC was advised and N423MA was authorized to perform a low pass - by in order for ATC to assess. There was no visible damage observed, an emergency was declared and the aircraft landed uneventfully at CYUL. Post flight inspection revealed that the retread of the right inboard main landing gear tire was completely missing.

C-FTLS, a Cessna 750 aircraft operated Telus Communications, was conducting a flight from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) with 5 persons on board. During the climb through FL180 after the departure from CYVR, the flight crew received a Hydraulic Low caution message, followed by subsequent hydraulic system failures including landing gear extension, anti-skid, braking, nose wheel steering, outboard roll spoilers, outboard speed brake panels and left thrust reverser. The flight crew actioned the checklist, declared an emergency and returned to land at CYVR. The aircraft landed on Runway 26L, and waited for ARFF to respond. Subsequently, the aircraft was towed clear of the runway without further incident. Subsequent maintenance actions revealed that an O-ring on the left slat valve had failed, causing the loss of the A side hydraulic fluid. While maintenance personnel were replacing the O-ring, they noticed the replacement part was of a larger diameter than the one that was removed. They confirmed that the replacement O-ring was the correct part number for that installation, and that the failed O-ring was not the right size. 5 other fittings were removed to check the O-ring sizes, and it was discovered that 4 of the 6 fittings (including the failed one) had incorrect O-rings installed. The aircraft was removed from service pending further inspection.

C-GJZX, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8181 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Fort St. John/North Peace Regional, BC (CYXJ) with 4 crew members and 33 passengers on board. While in the climb to 9000 feet, the crew responded to a TCAS RA due to C-CFBJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) inbound to CYVR from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) with 4 crew members and 76 passengers, that was in the descent to 10000 feet on the Whistler 5 arrival.  Both aircraft followed the appropriate guidance displayed by the TCAS avoidance instrumentation and continued without further incident.

C-FJOU, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1681 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Victoria Intl, BC (CYYJ) with 6 crew members and 200 passengers on board. During cruise flight in the vicinity of Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC), a cabin crew member became incapacitated due to a minor injury, and was deemed unfit to perform duties for the remainder of the flight. The associated duties were distributed among the remaining cabin crew members, and the aircraft landed without further incident.

The American Airlines Boeing 787-800, N814AA, was operating as flight AAL263 operating from Dallas-Fort Worth Int'l, TX (KDFW) to Beijing / Capital, China (ZBAA). During cruise flight, approximately 200 nm East of Fond-du-Lac, SK., the flight crew declared a passenger medical emergency and that AAL263 was diverting to Edmonton Int'l, AB (CYEG). On approach to CYEG, AAL263 experienced flap and slat issues and the flight crew declared an emergency. As the aircraft was above the maximum landing weight, the flight crew entered a hold to burn fuel. While assessing the technical issue, the flight crew elected to divert to Calgary Int'l, AB (CYYC) due to the availability of a longer runway. Upon landing, the flight crew reported nose landing gear steering issues. AAL263 stopped on the runway and was met by ARFF. The aircraft was towed from the runway. Company maintenance replaced the slat electric motor control unit (EMCU) and nose landing gear isolation valve.

C-GNLA, a Boeing 737-200 aircraft operated by Nolinor, was conducting flight NRL41 from Montreal Intl (Mirabel) (CYMX), QC to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB, with 7 crew members and no passengers on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew received a left engine (Pratt & Whitney USA JT8D-17) fire warning indication. The flight crew contacted the operator’s Maintenance Control Center (MCC), and it was determined that the alert was a false indication. The flight crew elected to complete a precautionary shutdown of the engine, and declared an emergency. The flight continued to CYWG where the aircraft landed without further incident. An inspection of the engine by the operator’s maintenance did not find any evidence of a fire or overheat. Inspection of the fire warning system revealed damage to the fire loop. The fire loop was repaired, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GURG, un appareil de type Bombardier CL600-2B16 Challenger 601-3R exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait le vol QUE10 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Alors que l’appareil se trouvait à proximité du repère UFX (Saint-Félix de Valois, QC) avec une restriction d’altitude au plus bas de 6000 pieds au passage de UFX, l’équipage a reçu un avis du système de surveillance du trafic et d'évitement des collisions (TCAS), indiquant un appareil à une altitude de 5000 pieds en montée. Quelques secondes plus tard, un avis de résolution fut émis, avisant l’équipage de monter. L’équipage a suivi les directives du TCAS et a immédiatement amorcé une montée pour une altitude de 6500 pieds. Un avis de trafic avait été transmis par l’ATC, pour un trafic qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue à une altitude de 5600 pieds.

C-FUZY, a Swearingen SA226-TC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting flight PAG771 from Thompson (CYTH), MB to Lac Brochet (CZWH), MB. While climbing through FL190, the left engine (Garrett TPE331-10UA-511G) fire-warning annunciator began to flicker, and then remained illuminated. The flight crew carried out the associated checklist items, proceeded to shut the engine down, declared an emergency and requested a return to CYTH where the subsequent landing was uneventful with ARFF responding. After the landing, the annunciator light was no longer illuminated, and there was no sign of smoke or fire. The flight crew elected not to evacuate, and the aircraft was taxied to the apron. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and confirmed that the 450° temperature probe was faulty. The probe was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJFR, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-6-300 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE698 depuis Salluit, QC (CYZG) à destination de Déception, QC (abandonné). Alors que l’appareil circulait pour prendre position pour le décollage sur la piste 03 à CYZG, l’équipage a rapporté un risque de collision avec une niveleuse. Bien que l’équipage ait effectué les appels requis sur la fréquence obligatoire (MF) 122.8 et sur la fréquence en route 126.7, le véhicule est demeuré sur la piste. L’équipage a tenté en vain de communiquer ses intentions à l’opérateur du véhicule, mais n’a reçu aucune réponse. Au moment où l’équipage a actionné les lumières de piste, le véhicule a circulé afin de dégager. L’équipage a annulé son décollage afin de discuter de la situation avec l’opérateur du véhicule. Celui-ci l’informe que l’opérateur de la station radio d’aérodrome communautaire (CARS) lui transmet les informations sur la position et intention des appareils, car il n’est pas équipé d’une radio à très haute fréquence (VHF) et ne peut donc pas entendre les communications effectuées par les équipages. En l’absence du CARS, il ne reçoit donc pas les informations. Comme ce type d’incident est croissant, Air Inuit effectue un suivi avec l’exploitant des aéroports situés au Nunavik, Kativik Regional Government (KRG).

N265WA, a privately operated CubCrafters CC11-160 aircraft, was conducting a VFR flight itinerary from Beaver Creek, YT (CYXQ) to Watson Lake, YT (CYQH) with one pilot and one passenger on board. The aircraft completed an uneventful landing at CYQH and during rollout, the pilot was unable to maintain directional control. The left brake was ineffective, and the aircraft experienced a ground loop. The right wing contacted the ground and received substantial damage. The two occupants received no injuries. A post-accident inspection found the left brake line leaking at the brake caliper.

C-GUMQ, un appareil de type Piper PA-31 (Navajo) exploité par Grondair, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à destination de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU). Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en rapprochement pour CYHU, l’équipage a déclaré une urgence en raison d’un problème avec le train d’atterrissage. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre.

C-FPSC, un appareil de type British Aerospace Jetstream 32 exploité par Pascan Aviation, effectuait le vol PSC999 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Baie Comeau, QC (CYBC) à destination de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV). C-FTJJ, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-6 Twin Otter exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE131 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Poste Montagnais (Mile 134), QC (CSF3) à CYZV. AIE131 était sous guidage radar via un vecteur de 180° afin d’intercepter l’ILS pour la piste 09 à CYZV. Alors que PSC999 se trouvait en approche finale pour la piste 09, l’équipage a reçu l’instruction de réduire sa vitesse d’approche et a effectué un palier à 4400 pieds afin de réduire sa vitesse à 120 kts. L’espacement avec AIE131 a alors été réduit à 4.6 nm sur le plan horizontal et 300 pieds sur le plan vertical. L’espacement requis est de 5 nm ou 1000 pieds.

C-FPCA, a Boeing 767-375 operated by Air Canada as flight ACA010, was enroute from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ).  The cabin crew reported a plastic, burning odour originating from an oven in the mid galley. The cabin crew turned off the oven and the odour dissipated. The flight continued to CYYZ without further incident. The source of the odour was determined to be plastic that was in contact with an oven coil. The oven was replaced.

C-FWRR, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (CRJ100) aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7335 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Nashville Intl (KBNA), TN. As the aircraft was climbing through FL270 in the vicinity of London (CYXU), ON, the flight crew received a CABIN ALT master caution message. The flight crew noted that the cabin altitude was at 8500 feet, and requested an immediate descent to 10 000 feet. However, the cabin altitude continued to increase to 10 000 feet, and the CABIN ALT master warning light illuminated. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks, and continued the emergency descent to 10 000 feet as per SOPs. The airspeed was reduced to 250 KIAS, and QRH procedures were followed. The decision was made to continue to destination, and the aircraft subsequently landed uneventfully at KNBA. The operator’s maintenance found the R/H pack duct blown out and deferred it as per MEL procedures. The L/H pack was checked and found to be operational. Part of the follow up actions included the replacement of the duct, as well as the duct check valve. The operator issued an SDR for the duct check valve.

C-FFPH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by TUI Airways as flight TOM5382, departed Norwich Intl. Airport, UK (EGSH) for Rhodos/Diagoras/Maritsa Airport (LGRP). During the climb, London ATC cleared TOM5382 to FL220 and advised of converging traffic leveling at FL230. The flight crew reduced the climb to less than 900 ft/min and at FL217 a TCAS Traffic Advisory was received. Almost immediately a TCAS Resolution Advisory "Descent, Descent" was received. The autopilot was disconnected, corrective action was taken to move the aircraft out of the red descent displayed on the PFD and ATC was advised. After having descended 300 feet a new TCAS RA was received to "Level off, Level off". A clear of conflict was received and then FL220 was resumed by the aircraft. The aircraft continued to LGRP uneventfully.

CN-RNT, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Royal Air Maroc, was conducting flight RAM208 from Casablanca/Mohammed V Intl, Morocco (GMMN) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). As the aircraft went through 22 000 feet during the descent for CYUL, the flight crew declared an emergency due to an engine power loss. The aircraft landed on Runway 24R without further incident.

C-GRIR, un appareil de type Beech A100 King Air exploité par Grondair, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis La Romaine, QC (CTT5) à destination de Natashquan, QC (CYNA). Lorsque le train d’atterrissage a été sorti lors de l’approche à CYNA, une indication que la roue de gauche n’était pas verrouillée est apparue. La liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) a été complétée et une urgence a été déclarée. L’équipage a effectué un déroutement vers Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) et la procédure d’extension manuelle du train d’atterrissage a été effectuée avec succès. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 31 et a circulé jusqu’au hangar de l’exploitant sans assistance.

C-FGQH, a float-equipped de Havilland DHC-6 aircraft operated by Harbour Air, was conducting flight HES2120 from Victoria Harbour, BC (CYWH) to Vancouver Harbour, BC (CYHC) with 2 pilots and 11 passengers on board. During the final approach at CYHC, the aircraft landed long due to traffic on the water. The aircraft contacted the water with a nose down attitude, which caused it to bounce. Reverse thrust was applied in an attempt to stabilize the aircraft; however, it bounced a second time before finally landing hard on the water. After landing, the flight crew heard noise and realized that something had broken. The aircraft was afloat, but the left float was loose. The pilot expedited the taxi to the dock, and contacted personnel ahead for assistance. The operator’s maintenance discovered that the LH front float strut (PN C3UF1014-3) had failed, the front spreader bar had buckled, and the top of the float strut had punctured the fuselage in two places. There were no injuries or fire. The ELT did not activate.

C-GWAZ, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA121 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC with 5 crew members and 125 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the cabin crew detected a burning smell in the aft galley. The smell dissipated, however the cabin crew was unable to find the source. The flight crew was notified and, during the descent, the smell could be detected again. The flight crew declared an emergency, and requested ARFF on standby. The aircraft landed without further incident, and there were no injuries. The operator’s maintenance found that the hydraulic system was at 104% of its capacity, and corrected it to the recommended level of 91%. Both engines were run with no faults found, and the aircraft was returned to service.

N733AR, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL79 from London/Heathrow, UK (EGLL) to Dallas-Fort Worth Intl, TX (KDFW) with 16 crew members and 266 passengers on board. As the flight was approximately 50 nm East of St John's Intl, NL (CYYT), an unruly passenger attempted to open one of the cabin doors in flight. The passenger was restrained, the flight crew declared an emergency and requested a diversion to Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl, MA (KBOS) for landing. The flight crew jettisoned fuel on their way to KBOS in order to reduce the weight for the landing. Upon arrival at KBOS, the flight was met by US authorities who removed the passenger from the aircraft. The flight then continued to destination without further incident.

C-FWCN, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA4153 from Sint Maarten/Princess Juliana Intl, Sint Maarten (TNCM) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During cruise flight, a flight attendant became incapacitated due to a minor injury. The captain was advised, the other flight attendants assumed remaining duties.

C-GFOL, a Beech 200 aircraft operated by Kississing Lake Lodge Ltd., was conducting a special visual flight rules flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB to St. Andrews (CYAV), MB. There was no reported visible contamination on the aircraft prior to taxi or departure. During the climb, after taking off from Runway 36, the flaps were retracted and the aircraft entered instrument meteorological conditions. As the aircraft climbed through approximately 2 000 feet ASL, the aircraft pitched up and entered an aerodynamic stall. The crew performed the stall recovery, during which both engines (Pratt and Whitney - Canada PT6A-41) were over-torqued. The flight crew elected to continue to CYAV.

C-GQBQ, un appareil de type Bombardier CL600-2B16 Challenger 601-3A exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait le vol QUE20 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de Gaspé (Michel-Pouliot), QC (CYGP). Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en montée initiale après le décollage de CYUL, une indication de panne des volets « Flaps Fail » est survenue. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification d’urgence et a décidé de dérouter vers Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB). Par mesure de précaution, l’équipage a demandé la présence des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre avec un volet à moins de 20 degrés d’angle. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GEWR, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3351 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) for Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG). Shortly after the departure from CYYC, the flight crew reported that the nose landing gear would not retract. The flight continued to CYEG and, on initial descent, the flight crew requested ARFF to be standing by for the landing as a precaution. The flight landed without further incident, and the landing gear was inspected prior to taxiing to the gate. The operator’s maintenance found the landing gear locked sensors out of rig and loose. They were rigged as required and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GAQN, a DHC-8-311 operating as North Cariboo Air flight NCB5109, was in cruise en route from Christina Lake, AB (CCL3) to Kelowna, BC (CYLW) when the left main landing gear aft door opened fully. The flight crew received a gear door light indication and a landing gear INOP caution light. The crew diverted to Vancouver, BC (CYVR), declared a PAN PAN PAN, and requested emergency services stand by. The landing gear was extended manually and the aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident.Company maintenance inspected the aircraft, swung the gear, and performed a test flight with no faults found. The Proximity Switch Electronics Unit (PSEU, p/n 8-586-01) was replaced as a precautionary measure.

C-FJZL, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 CRJ900 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA91 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Seattle-Tacoma Intl (KSEA), WA. N912NN, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL1415 from Dallas-Fort Worth Intl (KDFW), TX to CYVR. After the takeoff, JZA91 was cleared by the Terminal Departure controller to 12 000 feet, while AAL1415 was cleared by the Terminal Arrival controller down to 10 000 feet. The Departure controller noticed the conflict, and instructed JZA91 to stop the climb at 9000 feet. JZA91 was not able to stop climb until 9500 feet prior to descending back down to 9000 feet. Both aircraft experienced TCAS RAs and came within 900 feet and 2.6 nm of each other, when 1000 feet or 3 nm was required.

C-FLAP, a float-equipped de Havilland DHC-3T aircraft operated by Harbour Air, was conducting flight HES412 from Ganges, BC (CAX6) to Vancouver Harbour, BC (CYHC) with 1 pilot and 6 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure, the pilot turned on the bleed air for cabin heat when passengers advised that smoke was rising from the cabin floor. The aircraft returned to CAX6 and landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft, however no defects were found. It is suspected that the smoke could have been dust from the cabin heat ducts, which had not been used throughout the summer.

C-FNHT, a privately registered Cessna 172B aircraft, was en route from Birch Hills, SK (CJD3) to Tisdale, SK (CJY3). Prior to arriving at CJY3, the pilot attempted to land in a pasture, approximately 15 nm North East of the airport. During the landing roll, a gust of wind caught the right wing tip and the aircraft ground looped. Control could not be regained, the aircraft veered to the left and collided with trees at the end of the pasture. The pilot was not injured, however the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GITU, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA134 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 6 crew members and 183 passengers on board. During the taxi from the gate to the runway at CYYC, the flight crew observed a burning smell on the flight deck, in the vicinity of the ECAM control panel. The flight crew elected to return to the gate, and deplaned all passengers.The operator’s maintenance determined the fault to be the back lighting of the ECAM control panel. The panel was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FTJO, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA718 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to New York/La Guardia, NY (KLGA) with 5 crew members and 142 passengers on board. Inbound to KLGA, ACA718 was vectored between two helicopters which were at 4500 feet and 3500 feet. Descending through 4500 feet, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to DESCEND. The flight crew complied with the advisory and continued to KLGA for an uneventful landing on Runway 31.

N2578C, a privately operated Cessna 170B, was on a VFR flight from Manning, AB (CFX4), to Fort Nelson, BC (CYYE) with two crew members and one passenger on board. The aircraft successfully touched down on Runway 22 in CYYE but on the landing roll out, control of the aircraft was lost and the aircraft performed a ground loop. There were no injures and the aircraft taxied clear of the runway. There was substantial damage to the outer portion of the left wing, and minor damage to the left elevator and left main wheel assembly.

C-FEJF, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 aircraft operated by Sky Regional Airlines, was conducting flight SKV7595 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Chicago/O'Hare Intl, IL (KORD) with 4 crew members and 75 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL350, approximately 100 nm East Northeast from KORD, the flight crew received a FLAP FAIL EICAS message. The flight crew carried out the checklist, declared a PAN PAN and diverted to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) where it landed without further incident. The aircraft stopped on the runway and ARFF checked the brake temperature. Subsequently, the aircraft taxied to the gate under the supervision of ARFF.The operator’s maintenance replaced the skew sensor and the SF-Ace. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-FRYH, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Yellowhead Helicopters, had picked up a sling load of drill rod at a site located approximately 40 nm West of Stewart, BC (CZST). As the helicopter began its descent, the straps holding the drill rods to the shackle clipped into the hook on the end of the longline broke, and the load was released. The helicopter was not damaged and there were no injuries.

C-FGSJ, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways, was conducting flight CJT572 from Calgary Intl (CYYC), AB to Hamilton (CYHM), ON. Approximately 110 nm North West of CYHM, the flight crew reported a failure of the center hydraulic system. An emergency was declared, and the flight proceeded to land uneventfully at CYHM with ARFF standing by. The aircraft had to be towed off the runway to the operator’s hangar. The operator’s maintenance found the CTR HYD landing gear up line from the right hand brake metering valve ruptured. The line was replaced in accordance with Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) 20-10-09, and subsequent tests revealed no further faults. Additionally, the CTR 1 and 2 HYD pumps were replaced and tested satisfactorily.

C-FZEL, a private float-equipped Cessna A185E aircraft operated by Jennings River Wild Adventures, was en route from Hall Lake, BC to Coconino Lake, BC with 2 persons on board. Approximately 1.5 nm out on final at 700 feet AGL, the engine (Teledyne Continental IO-520-D) lost power abruptly. During the forced landing approach to a small lake, the aircraft struck trees and came to rest in approximately 7 feet of water. The pilot and the passenger received minor injuries, and swam to shore. However, the aircraft was substantially damaged. The ELT activated, and there was no fire. The two occupants were evacuated several hours later by Yukon EHS helicopter.

C-GFAT, an Airbus 310-300 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC258 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Barcelona/El Prat, Spain (LEBL) with 9 crew members and 205 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL340 in the vicinity of 52N/020W, the aircraft encountered severe Clear Air Turbulence (CAT). The auto-pilot disconnected, and the aircraft gained 300 feet very rapidly. The flight crew regained control of the aircraft and descended back down to FL340. Since the flight crew had no advanced indication, the seat belt sign was off at the time of the event. Two passengers and two cabin crew members received minor injuries, while another passenger received a serious injury, and was transported to the hospital upon arrival at LEBL. All four minor injuries were treated in flight, and the two cabin crew members were able to continue with their duties.The aircraft was inspected by the operator’s maintenance upon arrival at LEBL, and was released back to service.

N816SY, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sun Country Airlines, was conducting flight SCX8201 from Bullhead City/Laughlin Bullhead Intl, AZ (KIFP) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with 6 crew members and 154 passengers on board. During the intermediate approach at CYYC, the flight crew attempted to extend the flaps and received a FLAP DISAGREE message on the EICAS. The flight crew actioned the QRH and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without incident, and there were no injuries. Maintenance personnel replaced the number 3 flap skew sensor and the aircraft was released back to service.

C-GHAR, a float-equipped de Havilland DHC-3T aircraft operated by Harbour Air, was conducting flight HES1150 from Nanaimo Harbour, BC (CAC8) to Vancouver Harbour, BC (CYHC) with 1 pilot and 6 passengers on board. As the aircraft was taxiing into the sun after the landing at CYHC, approximately 45 minutes before sunset, the pilot did not see a boat at the 1 o'clock position. Consequently, the right wing tip of the aircraft struck the bow of the boat. There were no injuries and the damage was minor. The aircraft was ferried to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) for repairs.

C-FSKQ, un appareil de type Beech 200 exploité par Sky Jet M.G., effectuait le vol VSL443 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) avec 2 pilotes et 4 passagers à bord. Peu de temps après son décollage de CYUY, l’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence en raison d’un problème de pressurisation. L’équipage a poursuivi sa route en demeurant sous l’altitude de 10 000 pieds ASL, et s’est posé sans encombre à CYQB.

C-GAHK, un appareil de type Cessna 206H amphibie exploité par Charlevoix Aviation, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Charlevoix, QC (CYML) à destination du lac Nairne, QC, avec seulement un pilote à son bord. Lors de l’approche pour l’amerrissage sur le lac Nairne, le pilote a oublié de rétracter les roues. Lorsque les flotteurs ont fait contact avec la surface du lac, l’appareil s’est renversé. Le pilote a pu évacuer l’appareil et a été secouru par des témoins de l’accident avec l’aide d'une embarcation. La radiobalise d'urgence s'est déclenchée lors de l'impact, et le JRCC de Trenton a été avisé. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FSNU, a Boeing 737 Max 8 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA861 from London/Heathrow, UK (EGLL) to Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) with 6 crew members and 144 passengers on board. During boarding at Gate 223 at EGLL, the aircraft experienced a fuel spill off the right wing overflow vent. The 4 square meters spill was contained, and passengers were deplaned. ARFF attended. The aircraft subsequently departed.

C-FJZD, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ 900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8667 from San Diego Intl, CA (KSAN) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). As the aircraft was in the climb through 10 000 feet after the departure from KSAN, the DC Emergency Bus caution light illuminated. The QRH was referenced and the flight crew requested a return to KSAN. No emergency was declared, however ATC considered this event as an emergency due to the list of systems that could have been lost. Additionally, the flight crew requested the re-opening of Runway 09 (which was closed by Notam), so they could have the ILS approach versus the RNAV27 approach due to low ceilings below the operator’s limits. The aircraft landed on Runway 09 without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced the RH DC power center in accordance with 24-63-01-400-801.

C-GYKX, a Cessna 172N aircraft operated by Super T Aviation Academy, was conducting a maintenance run with the intention to complete a compass swing on the threshold of Runway 09 at Medicine Hat, AB (CYXH). C-GNAX, a Beech B200 King Air aircraft operated by Northern Air Charter, was conducting IFR flight NLI419 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to CYXH. The operator of C-GYKX contacted the Flight Service Station (FSS) and advised that they were taxiing for a maintenance run on the threshold of Runway 09.  The flight crew of NLI419 contacted the FSS and advised that they were inbound for a landing on Runway 27. Subsequently, NLI419 transmitted that they were downwind for Runway 27, then on final for Runway 27. The FSS was aware of C-GYKX’s position, however traffic information was not relayed to NLI419. Consequently, NLI419 proceeded to land on Runway 27, while C-GYKX was still in position on the threshold of Runway 09. During the landing roll, the flight crew of NLI419 noticed C-GYKX at the opposite end of the runway. Both aircraft then proceeded to exit the runway without further incident. There was no damage and there were no injuries.

C-FNAJ, an Embraer ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA651 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) to St. John’s Intl, NL (CYYT). C-GGJF, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by PAL Aerospace, was conducting flight SPR05 from Summerside, PE (CYSU) to CYHZ. ACA651 was given instruction to hold short of Runway 23 on Taxiway Delta. When SPR05 was 1 mile on final for Runway 05, ATC observed ACA651 beginning to cross the hold short line, and instructed to stop. Since ACA651 had already crossed the hold short line, ATC subsequently cleared them across Runway 23 prior to SPR05 landing Runway 05. NAV CANADA is investigating this runway incursion.

C-FOEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3138 from Fort McMurray, AB (CYMM) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). As the flight was in the process of deplaning passengers at the gate in CYYC, a cabin crew member became incapacitated due to illness. The second cabin crew member assumed duties until all passengers left the aircraft. The incapacitated cabin crew member sat in the rear galley and waited for EMS to arrive after the passengers had offloaded.

C-IMTN, a privately operated CLASS BushCaddy R-80 Basic Ultra-light aircraft, departed from South Cariboo/108 Mile, BC (CZML) on a local VFR flight with 2 persons on board. Approximately 25 minutes after the departure, the pilot observed the engine (Subaru series) oil pressure and electrical voltage indications fluctuating. The pilot and the passenger, who was also a pilot, elected to shut the engine down and performed a forced landing in a field along the VFR route, 30 nm South East of Williams Lake, BC (CYWL). The field turned out to be saturated with water, causing the tailwheel aircraft to come to an abrupt stop, and overturned. Both occupants were wearing a four point seat restraint system, and were not injured. However, the aircraft received substantial damage. Reportedly, the alternator belt had recently been replaced. The RCMP and Air Traffic Area Control Center Shift Manager were advised.

C-FEIQ, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 aircraft operated by Sky Regional Airlines, was conducting flight SKV7528 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Gander Intl (CYQX), NL with 4 crew members and 70 passengers on board. During the takeoff roll from CYYZ, the flight crew noted that the number 1 engine ITT indication was exceeding limitations, and was still increasing. The flight crew rejected the takeoff at 80 knots and exited the runway. While taxiing back to the gate, the flight crew noted that the number 1 engine fuel flow indication was significantly higher than the number 2 engine. The number 1 engine (General Electric CF34-8E5A1) was shut down, and ARFF was requested to inspect the engine and the brakes. Everything appeared to be normal, and the aircraft taxied to the gate on one engine.The operator’s maintenance carried out function checks, completed a compressor wash and returned the aircraft to service.

C-GMCT, a Robinson R44 II aircraft operated by Essential Helicopters, was conducting a flight from North Bay (CYYB), ON to Toronto/Buttonville Muni (CYKZ), ON with only the pilot on board. While approaching CYKZ, the pilot encountered IMC conditions and decided to turn northbound, away from the airport. Subsequently, radio contact was lost and a search was initiated. The helicopter was found destroyed in a bush, 9 nm North of CYKZ. The pilot was fatally injured. The TSB deployed two investigators to the site.

C-FTLB, a privately registered Cessna 175 Skylark aircraft, was conducting a VFR flight from a private airstrip near Dewberry, AB to Dawson Creek, BC (CYDQ) with only the pilot on board. Approximately 15 nautical miles North of Grande Prairie, AB (CYQU), the engine stopped as a result of fuel exhaustion. The pilot executed a forced landing onto a rural road and lost control of the aircraft during the roll out. The aircraft wing struck a berm beside the road, and the aircraft swerved into a ditch, causing the main landing gear to collapse. The pilot was uninjured; however, the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GUBH, an Airbus 330-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC708 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Paris/Charles de Gaulle, France (LFPG) with 11 crew members and 292 passengers on board. During cruise flight in the vicinity of London, UK, a Hand-Held device used for on-board sales by the cabin crew started to emit smoke. Procedures were followed and the device was secured. The flight continued to destination and landed without further incident. The cause is being investigated by the air operator.

RP-C3435, an Airbus 340-300 aircraft operated by Philippines Airlines, was conducting flight PAL117 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Manila/Ninoy Aquino Intl, Philippines (RPLL). As the aircraft was accelerating for take off on Runway 08R at CYVR, the air traffic tower controller heard a loud noise. The runway was closed for inspection, and tire and other debris were found on the runway. Runway 08R was closed for 15 minutes to clean it up; a few departures and arrivals were delayed. PAL117 continued its flight to RPLL where it landed without further incident.Following the landing at RPLL, several holes in the skin were found in the landing gear area. The aircraft received substantial damage to the belly, as well as the Center Landing Gear (CLG) fairing door.

C-FIVX, a Boeing 777 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA030 from Beijing/Capital, China (ZBAA) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). C-FIWE, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3323 from Kelowna, BC (CYLW) to CYVR. As ACA030 was on final approach to land on Runway 26R at CYVR, ATC instructed the flight crew to go around when the spacing reduced to 2 miles behind WEN3323. ACA030 was vectored for a subsequent approach with no further impact on operations.

C-GJWG, an amateur built Titan T-51 aircraft, departed from Collingwood (CNY3), ON for a local flight. During the flight, the engine (Suzuki V6) experienced a power loss, and the aircraft force landed on a field located approximately 10 nautical miles North East of the CNY3. The aircraft was substantially damaged, however the pilot, who was the sole occupant, was not injured.

C-GCCF, a privately registered Cessna 421B Golden Eagle aircraft, was conducting an IFR flight from Ponoka Industrial (Labrie Field), AB (CEH3) to Whitecourt, AB (CYZU). As the aircraft reached 12 000 feet after the departure from CEH3, the right engine (Teledyne Continental GTSIO-520-H) stopped abruptly. An emergency was declared, and the pilot requested a diversion to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) where an uneventful RNAV, single-engine approach and landing was made to Runway 02 with ARFF standing by. The aircraft taxied off the runway under its own power. A maintenance inspection revealed a failed magneto drive on the right engine.

C-GYFB, a Learjet 35A aircraft operated by Keewatin Air, was conducting medevac flight KEW101 from Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) to Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) with a crew of two and two passengers on board. During the descent through 20 000 feet, the flight crew received a fire aural and master warning indication for the right engine (Garrett TFE731-2C-2B). The flight crew discharged one fire bottle and completed a precautionary shutdown of the engine. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft landed without further incident.An inspection of the right engine by the operator's maintenance revealed no evidence of a fire. Further inspection of the fire warning system revealed an unsecured fire detection control unit connector and sensing element connections. The connections were secured and a successful ground run of the system was completed. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-FNNW, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA871 from Paris/Charles de Gaulle, France (LFPG) to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). During cruise flight, a cabin crew member was exiting the overhead crew rest area and fell, sustaining a serious injury. Doctors on board provided medical attention. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and diverted to Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ). The cabin crew member was met by medical staff and was sent to the hospital. The flight continued on to destination.

C-GJPY, an Aerospatiale ATR 72-202 aircraft operated by Summit Air, was conducting flight SU7122 from Gahcho Kue, NT (CGK2) to Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) with 3 crew members on board. During the descent, the flight crew received a LO LVL hydraulic caution light, 20 nautical miles inbound to CYZF. After reviewing the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH), the flight crew contacted ATC and requested Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) to be standing by. An emergency gear extension was performed, and the aircraft landed uneventfully. The operator’s maintenance is investigating.

C-GTSH, un appareil de type Airbus 310-300 exploité par Air Transat, effectuait le vol TSC299 depuis Basel-Mulhouse-Freiburg/EuroAirport, France (LFSB) à Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Alors que l’appareil était stationné pour le débarquement des passagers après l’atterrissage à CYUL, un transbordeur est entré en collision avec l'aile droite de l'appareil. Personne n'a été blessé. L'ampleur exacte des dommages est inconnue pour l'instant.

C-GMCP, un appareil de type Learjet 45 exploité par Skyservice Aviation d'Affaires, effectuait un vol depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) en route vers St-John's Intl, NL (CYYT) avec à son bord 2 membres d'équipage et 3 passagers. Alors qu’il était à environ 10 miles au sud de Bromont (Roland Désourdy), QC (CZBM), l’équipage a reçu le message L ENG PYLON OVHT. L'équipage a fermé le moteur gauche (GARRETT TFE731-20BR-1B) en accord avec la liste de vérification applicable, et a déclaré un PAN PAN. Des circuits d'attente ont dû être effectués afin de consommer du carburant, pour ainsi réduire le poids de l'appareil à sa masse maximale d'atterrissage autorisée avant de revenir se poser sans problème à CYUL. Personne n’a été blessé et l'appareil n'a subi aucun dommage.

C-FDRH, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA336 from Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) with 5 crew members and 146 passengers on board. The aircraft had been released with the Air Data Reference 3 (ADR3) inoperative, in conformity with the Minimum Equipment List (MEL). While approaching CYUL, the ADR1 failed. The flight crew carried out the appropriate check list, and declared a PAN PAN. After the landing, the aircraft was shut down, inspected by ARFF and was subsequently towed to the gate. There were no injuries, and the aircraft did not receive any damage. The operator’s maintenance replaced the Air Data Module 19FP4 and performed checks as per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM). The aircraft was returned in service.

C-GABO a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA717 from Quebec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). As the aircraft was 5 miles on the final approach to Runway 24L at CYUL, a drone flew overhead JZA717 by approximately 50 feet. The flight crew continued the approach and carried out an uneventful landing. No one was injured, and the aircraft sustained no damage. The type of drone and its operator are unknown.

C-GJOP, a de Haviland DHC-8-102 aircraft operated by Air Creebec, was conducting IFR flight CRQ906 from Waskaganish, QC (CYKQ) to Val d'Or, QC (CYVO) with 3 crew members and 20 passengers on board. Just after the rotation while taking off on Runway 24 at CYKQ, the right engine surged to a high torque, before going down to zero torque. The flight crew shut the affected engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW120A) down and carried out a VFR circuit to return to land at CYKQ without further incident. None of the occupants was injured. The aircraft sustained no damage.

C-FOFI, a Bombardier CL-415 aircraft operated by the Government of Newfoundland and Labrador, departed from Gander Intl, NL (CYQX) to conduct aerial firefighting operations near Whitehead Pond, NL. The flight crew inspected several lakes and selected Whitehead Pond for scooping water while fighting a fire approximately 8 nm to the South West. While making the sixth water scoop run along the lake, the flight crew heard a loud bang. The flight crew suspected that they had struck hidden rocks, so full power was applied and a go around was conducted. Both left water drop doors indicated open, and the hydraulic quantity indicated low. The hydraulic pressure was normal, and airspeed below maximum open door speed was maintained for the return to CYQX. While enroute, attempts to close the doors were unsuccessful. The flight crew completed the checklist related to the low hydraulic quantity, manually jettisoned the remaining water, and landed without further incident at CYQX.The aircraft's lower left hull sustained substantial damage.

C-GJAZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8737 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl, SK (CYXE) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 4 crew members and 75 passengers on board. During the approach at CYVR at approximately 9 nm North East and at 7100 feet, the flight crew observed a drone flying at the same altitude, approximately 200 feet to the left of the aircraft. No evasive manoeuvre was required. ATC was advised, and contacted RCMP. The aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident. No injuries were reported.

C-GZVJ, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG742 from Sioux Lookout, ON (CYXL) to Sachigo Lake, ON (CZPB). After levelling off at FL240, the flight crew operated the elevator trim toward nose down. However, the trim stuck short of what was required, and significant forward stick pressure was required to maintain level flight. The flight crew reduced engine power and airspeed in order to reduce the pressure required on the control column. After consulting with the operator's maintenance, the flight crew elected to return to CYXL. A MAYDAY was declared, and ARFF was required on standby. The passengers were briefed on the situation throughout the event. The subsequent landing at CYXL was uneventful.The operator's maintenance personnel carried out extensive inspection and troubleshooting of the elevator trim system, and carried out two unsuccessful test flights. The left and right elevator trim actuators were replaced, followed by a successful test flight.

C-GSWQ, a Learjet 45 aircraft operated by Sunwest Aviation, was conducting flight CNK657 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Fort Mackay/Albian, AB (CAL4) with 2 pilots and 7 passengers on board. During the initial climb after the departure from CYYC, the flight crew received a MAIN HYD QTY LO indication, followed by a MAIN HYD PRESS indication, associated with a decreasing hydraulic pressure. The flight crew actioned the QRH, declared an emergency, and elected to return to CYYC. A hold was requested in order to bring the weight of the aircraft down before the landing. The landing gear was lowered without issue and, after approximately 30 minutes of holding, the flight crew entered the approach, lowered the flaps and landed uneventfully. The aircraft retained sufficient braking capability and was able to taxi back to the operator’s facility under its own power. The operator’s maintenance found a faulty hydraulic pressure switch.

C-FHGA, a Cessna 208B aircraft operated by Skylink Express, was conducting a cargo flight from Victoria Intl, BC (CYYJ) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with one pilot on board. During the approach at CYVR, the pilot observed a HDG flag on the Horizontal Situation Indicator (HSI), followed by a HDG flag on the Radio Magnetic Indicator (RMI). Shortly after, there was a smell of burning wires, and the Directional Gyro circuit breaker popped. The pilot notified ATC of the situation, and ARFF was advised. The aircraft landed without further incident and taxied to the hangar. Subsequent maintenance action revealed that the Directional Gyro (P/N 060-0015-00) had a strong burnt smell. The part was replaced and the circuit breaker was reset. No injuries were reported.

C-GPTL, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 aircraft operated by Yellowhead Helicopters, was conducting external load operations approximately 25 nm South East of Mackenzie, BC (CYZY). As the net full of tools and snow survey equipment was being delivered to the ground crew, the pilot inadvertently released the longline and cargo hook from the belly hook. No injuries or damage were reported by the ground crew.

C-GKQD, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE481 from Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City (CYTZ), ON to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL), QC. During the climb after the departure from CYTZ, the speed of the aircraft reduced unexpectedly, which caused a loss of separation with C-GJZH, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft, which was conducting flight JZA958 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Fredericton Intl (CYFC), NB. The separation reduced to 4.8 nm horizontally, in an area that requires 5 nm.

C-FSRN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8242 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Terrace, BC (CYXT) with 4 crew members and 74 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYVR, one of the flight attendants began to feel unwell. The aircraft returned to CYVR and landed without further incident. Emergency Medical Services met the plane at the gate.

C-GEOH, a private Zenair CH-300 TRI Z Amateur Built Aircraft, had landed on the north-westbound grass runway at Smiths Falls-Montague (Russ Beach), ON (CYSH) when the aircraft started to veer to the right. The pilot was unable to stop the aircraft from veering to the right and the aircraft collided with C-GGQT, a Bellanca (Citabria) 7GCBC aircraft that was stopped with its engine running on the east side of the runway. The propeller of C-GGQT contacted the right wing leading edge of C-GEOH, causing the aircraft to swing into C-GGQT. The propeller of C-GEOH then cut into the right wing of C-GGQT. Both aircraft were substantially damaged, but there were no injuries to the occupants.

C-FAKN, a Beech 200 King Air aircraft operated by Alkan Air, was conducting a charter flight from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Nanaimo, BC (CYCD) with two pilots on board. Just after the touchdown at CYCD, the flight crew observed smoke in the cabin of the aircraft. The smoke appeared to be originating from the left hand flap motor.
