The flight crew taxied to the apron and shut the aircraft down without further incident. Subsequent maintenance action revealed that the flap motor up limit switch was malfunctioning. No injuries were reported.

C-FFWI, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA296 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl (CYWG), MB with 5 crew members and 107 passengers on board. At an approximate airspeed of 120 kts during the takeoff roll on Runway 26L at CYVR, the flight crew initiated a rejected takeoff and subsequently shut the number 1 engine (CFM56-5A1) down due to abnormal engine indications. A PAN PAN was declared, and ARFF responded to meet the aircraft. The 2 left-hand main landing gear tires were found flat. The passengers were deplaned, and bussed back to the terminal. There were no injuries. The aircraft was removed from the runway, and towed to the operator’s hangar. The operator's maintenance found bird remains in the left-hand engine. Airport Operations determined that the remains were of a Great Blue Heron. The engine sustained compressor damage and was removed from service.

C-FNBR, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 helicopter operated by Lakelse Air, was conducting external load operations approximately 10 nm East of Bronson Creek, BC (abandoned) with only the pilot on board. During the flight, the pilot encountered a high wind gust and observed the external load (empty fuel bladder) flying erratically and sailing up towards the tail rotor. The pilot released the load as a precautionary measure, returned to the staging area and landed without further incident.

C-FHKP, an Embraer ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA525 from Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl, MA (KBOS) to Toronto/Lester B. Parson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from KBOS, the flight crew noted a burning smell in the cockpit. The smell dissipated for a short time, but subsequently returned. Consequently, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN with Toronto Center. Descending through 1800 feet while on radar vectors for Runway 06L, the flight crew received an EICAS message PACK 1 FAULT and the smell dissipated. The flight landed without further incident, was inspected by AARF and then taxied to the gate.The operator’s maintenance replaced the L/H Air Cycle Machine (ACM) in accordance with the applicable Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM).

C-GXMG, a Robinson R44 II helicopter operated by Valley B Aviation, was enroute to a well site near Ring Border, BC. During the initial approach to the landing site, the pilot heard two bangs and yaw control was lost. The pilot lowered the collective to reduce the uncontrolled rotation, prior to colliding with trees. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was wearing a helmet and sustained no injuries. However, the helicopter received substantial damage. The ELT functioned and was shut off by the pilot after contacting the operator’s dispatch. A safety vest was found, along with some tail rotor blade pieces approximately 400-500 feet from the accident site. One of the cabin doors was found in the unlatched position.

C-FZJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (CRJ200) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8853 from Newark/Liberty Intl, NJ (KEWR) to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW). While the airplane was parked at the gate at KEWR, the flight crew heard a bang and felt the aircraft shake. A baggage cart struck the left wing tip of the aircraft, causing damage. There were no passengers on board at the time of the collision. The flight crew stopped the fueling process and contacted the operator's maintenance.The flight was subsequently cancelled. The operator's maintenance installed a new fairing (winglet).

C-GFPK, a privately registered Van’s RV 6 A aircraft, was conducting a flight from Edmonton/Parkland (CPL6), AB to Chilliwack (CYCW), BC with 2 persons on board. The aircraft departed CPL6 at 10:03 Mountain Time (MT) with a flight planned route from CPL6 to Hinton/Jasper-Hinton (CEC4), AB, Valemount (CAH4), BC, Kamloops (CYKA), BC, and finally CYCW. The last known position was calculated using a cellular phone location that was received at 12:29 Pacific Time (PT) in the vicinity of Blue River (CYCP), BC. The aircraft had approximately 4 hours of fuel onboard. The 121.5 MHz ELT did not transmit a signal. The aircraft was reported overdue at the destination airport. A search was initiated, and was discontinued by the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) after seven days. The aircraft's location remains unknown at this time.

CC177701, a military Boeing CC-177 aircraft operated by the Royal Canadian Air Force, was conducting flight CFC4010 from Trenton, ON (CYTR) to Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ). C-GOJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA638 from Ottawa/Macdonald–Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW) to CYHZ. CFC4010 was ahead of JZA638 on the approach at CYHZ; however, JZA638 was travelling approximately 50 kts faster than CFC4010. The speed remained constant, and when JZA638 was approximately 6 nm from the runway, the lateral separation was 4.4 nm, when 5 nm was required. NAV CANADA is investigating the occurrence.

C-GUON, a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA360 from Grande Prairie, AB (CYQU) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG). During the initial arrival into CYEG, JZA360 was cleared to 10 000 feet by the terminal controller. C-FMDW, a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft also operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA139 from CYEG to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC), and was cleared to maintain 9000 feet. A loss of separation occurred when a third aircraft, operating as JZA226, was cleared to descend to 5000 feet; JZA360 read that clearance back, and the terminal controller did not correct it. When JZA360 descended below 10 000 feet, the flight crew received a TCAS RA command to CLIMB, while the flight crew of JZA139 received a TCAS RA command to DESCEND. The separation was reduced to 1.7 nm laterally and 600 feet vertically, where 3 nm or 1000 feet is required.

EC-MYX, an Airbus 350-900 aircraft operated by Iberia, was conducting flight IBE6252 from New York/John F. Kennedy Intl, NY (KJFK) to Madrid/Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Intl, Spain (LEMD) with 265 passengers and 11 crew members on board. During cruise flight at FL410, approximately 70 nm South East of Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ), the flight crew received an ENG 1 EGT OVER LIMIT message, followed by an ENG 1 FAIL message. The engine (Rolls-Royce Trent XWB-84) was secured, and the flight crew declared a MAYDAY. The aircraft descended and diverted to Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl, MA (KBOS) where an uneventful landing was conducted.The operator’s maintenance replaced the engine, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GABO, a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting IFR flight JZA8907 from Greater Moncton Roméo Leblanc Intl, NB (CYQM) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) with 3 crew members and 31 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the ROLL SPLR INBD caution light illuminated, followed by a #1 ISO VLV caution light. The flight crew carried out the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) checklist and, as the flaps were selected during the approach into CYUL, the FLAP PWR caution light illuminated and the flaps remained at position 0. The flight crew performed a missed approach and carried out the QRH checklist for a flap 0 landing. As a precaution, ARFF was requested by the flight crew to be on standby. The aircraft landed without further incident with only emergency brakes available, and taxied onto Runway 10 where ARFF and maintenance personnel inspected it. The aircraft was subsequently towed to the gate. The operator’s maintenance replaced the number 1 hydraulic reservoir level switch, and returned the aircraft to service.

G-ZBKA, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by British Airways, was conducting flight BAW103 from London/Heathrow, England (EGLL) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with 201 passengers and 12 crew members on board. After the air conditioning had been surging periodically during cruise flight, the flight crew heard it one last time before going silent. At approximately the same time, the Senior Cabin Crew Member (SCCM) reported that the In-Flight Entertainment (IFE) system had failed throughout the aircraft, and that a system reset was being carried out. Shortly thereafter, the flight crew noticed an electric burning smell in the flight deck, followed by a haze coming from the first officer’s side. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks and initiated the SMOKE FIRE FUMES non-normal checklist. The flight crew member on rest was called back to the flight deck, along with the SCCM; both reported that the electric burning smell was still present. Approximately 5 minutes later, the SCCM returned to the flight deck and reported that the smell was subsiding, and the flight crew proceeded to remove their oxygen masks. However, the smell suddenly returned, accompanied by a haze on the captain’s side of the flight deck. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks once again and continued with the non-normal checklist procedures. In the vicinity of Pangnirtung, NU (CYXP), the flight crew declared an emergency and requested a diversion to Iqaluit, NU (CYFB). Fumes were present throughout the descent, increasing on final approach; however, it remained isolated to the flight deck throughout the flight. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYFB and stopped on the runway where it was met by ARFF. After the situation was assessed by the flight crew in conjunction with ARFF, the aircraft was cleared to proceed to the apron. A rescue flight was sent the following day and the passengers continued on to CYYC.

N858DP, a corporate Cessna 525 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Narsarsuaq, Greenland (BGBW) to Goose Bay, NL (CYYR). N506KM, a corporate CASA CN235-300 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Gander Intl, NL (CYQX) to Reykjavík/Keflavík, Iceland (BIKF). Upon the departure from BGBW, N858DP was cleared to FL220. N506KM was travelling in the opposite direction at FL320. N858DP initially levelled off at FL220, then requested to climb to FL400. However, the flight crew of N858DP continued to climb without a clearance from ATC. Subsequently, ATC stopped N858DP at FL300, and the flight crew reported to have mistakenly believed that they had been cleared to FL320. A loss of separation occurred when the closest lateral separation in time was 27 minutes, where 60 minutes was required for opposite traffic.

C-GXAI, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-300 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE821 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 3 membres d’équipage et 14 passagers à bord. Alors que l’équipage de conduite effectuait la liste de vérification pour la descente vers CYUL, l’indicateur de quantité de liquide hydraulique #2 indiquait près de 0. L’équipage de conduite a demandé et effectué un circuit d’attente au point OMBRE afin de procéder aux vérifications. La liste de vérifications du Manuel de référence rapide (QRH) pour «Loss of Hydraulic #2 Quantity» a été complétée, et une urgence a été déclarée. L'équipage a effectué une extension manuelle du train d’atterrissage et l’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 06L sans encombre. Les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d’aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés, et ont escorté l’appareil jusqu’à la barrière. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

CA22, a Swearingen SA-226 aircraft operated by Carson Air, was conducting a flight from Kelowna, BC (CYLW) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). WEN3265, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting a flight from CYYC to CYLW, and had been authorized to 11 000 feet after the departure. During the arrival at CYYC, CA22 was authorized by ATC to descend and to maintain 12 000 feet, which the flight crew read back correctly; however the flight crew continued the descent past 12 000 feet. ATC queried CA22 about the deviation, and re-cleared the flight to 12 000 feet. The separation eroded to 2.3 nm laterally and 700 feet vertically, where 3 nm or 1000 feet is required.

C-GUBD, an Airbus 330-243 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC464 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Marseille Provence, France (LFML). During cruise flight, a flight attendant became incapacitated and was unable to perform their duties; duties were assigned to the remaining cabin crew members.

C-GJJL, a Cessna 172M aircraft operated by Namao Flying Club, was conducting a local flight from Edmonton/Villeneuve, AB (CZVL). During the approach for landing at CZVL, the aircraft landed short of the runway and the nose wheel collided with the lip between the grass and asphalt. There was damage to the nose wheel, the landing gear, airframe structures and floor area.

C-GBNX, a Cessna 560 Citation V aircraft operated by the Province of Manitoba, was conducting a flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) to Brandon Muni, MB (CYBR). During the approach to CYBR, the flight crew checked the brake pedal function. The pedals felt spongy, and could be depressed almost to the floor. The flight crew elected to return to CYWG and requested ARFF to be on standby. The subsequent landing on Runway 18 was uneventful, and the aircraft was brought to a precautionary stop on Taxiway C. The operator's maintenance towed the aircraft to the apron.

C-GPMY, un hélicoptère de type Bell 206L-1 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Sainte-Madeleine, QC avec seul un pilote à son bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en vol de croisière dans la région de Saint-Pie, QC, une perte de puissance a été observée, et la procédure d’atterrissage d’urgence dans un champ de maïs a été effectuée. L’autorotation s’est terminée avec un atterrissage dur, et l’appareil s’est affaissé sur ses patins. L’inspection de l’appareil a révélé des dommages importants à la poutre de queue, et au stabilisateur vertical. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GJPY, an Aerospatiale ATR 72-202 aircraft operated by Summit Air, was conducting flight SU7141 from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Diavik, NT (CDK2) with only the 2 pilots on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew received a hydraulic caution warning light for low level green hydraulic system. The flight crew diverted back to CYZF and declared a PAN PAN, requesting ARFF to stand by. An emergency landing gear extension was executed, and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GFAT, an Airbus 310-300 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC261 from Barcelona/El Prat, Spain (LEBL) to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). At approximate position 49°44' N/051°16' W, the flight crew declared an emergency and requested a diversion to St. John’s Intl, NL (CYYT) due to smoke in the cockpit. The smoke subsequently dissipated on the descent however, a burnt plastic smell remained. The aircraft landed on Runway 29 without further incident. Emergency services met the aircraft on the runway and proceeded to an inspection; it was then released to taxi to the gate.The operator’s maintenance found an electrical fault in the first officer’s seat adjustment system.

C-GBTI, a Beech E90 King Air aircraft operated by SkyNorth Air, was conducting flight SN698 from Thompson, MB (CYTH) to Island lake, MB (CYIV). Shortly after the departure from CYTH, the flight crew selected the landing gear in the up position, however they did not receive a gear up indication and the GEAR UNSAFE light remained illuminated. The flight crew continued to climb to a safe altitude and leveled off. A gear down selection was made, and no change to the landing gear unsafe position was noticed. The flight crew declared an emergency, requested a return to CYTH, briefed the flight medic crew member, and completed the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) items. A manual extension of the landing gear was attempted, but was not successful. The flight crew carried out a low pass, and observations indicated that the landing gear appeared to be down. On approach to Runway 06, the flight crew selected full flaps and received the landing gear warning horn. Upon touchdown, the landing gear collapsed and the aircraft slid to a stop on the runway center line, with Thompson Fire and EMS on standby. There were no injuries. Thompson Fire did contain the fuel spill, which occurred as a result of aircraft structural damage.The operator's maintenance suspects a gear actuator had failed. The TSB will be notified of the subsequent findings.Update - 01 November 2018Update from the operator.  Teardown of the landing gear actuators. The right hand gear actuator failed and would not allow the gear to continue retract or extend.

N12163, an Embraer 145XR aircraft operated by ExpressJet Airlines, was conducting flight ASQ4137 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) to Newark/Liberty Intl, NJ (KEWR) with 3 crew members and 48 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYHZ, the flight crew declared an emergency due to a suspected fuel leak. The flight returned to CYHZ where a landing was made without further incident.The operator’s maintenance determined that the right wing fuel check valve was faulty. The part was replaced in accordance with manufacturer instructions, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJUU, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Campbell Helicopters, was conducting fire suppression activities near Vernon Lake, BC. During the final approach to a target on the side of a mountain, the helicopter began to settle in the down flowing air. The pilot released the long-line and bucket and returned to the staging area where it landed without further incident.

C-FEJL, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 aircraft operated by Sky Regional Airlines, was conducting flight SKV7678 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl, MA (KBOS). As the aircraft was being pushed back from Gate 162 at CYYZ, the two wing walkers were not prepared and were not in position. A catering vehicle was stopped behind the aircraft, waiting for another aircraft to arrive at the next gate. One of the wing walkers attempted to signal the mule driver to stop the pushback, however was unsuccessful. The tail section collided with the catering truck, resulting in damage to the aircraft and the truck. There were no injuries to the passengers, however the catering truck driver later complained of back and neck soreness, and was taken to the hospital as a precaution. The aircraft was brought back to the gate, and passengers deplaned normally.

C-FPDN, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA167 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG). During cruise flight in the vicinity of Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl, SK (CYXE), the flight crew received a HYD G ENG 1 PUMP LO PR ECAM warning indication for the number 1 engine hydraulic pump. The prescribed actions of the ECAM were carried out, and it was decided that the flight would continue to CYEG. Subsequently, the flight crew received a second ECAM message (HYD G RSVR LO LVL) for low fluid level in the same (green) system. A PAN PAN was declared, and the flight landed at CYEG without further incident.The operator’s maintenance replaced the green hydraulic system accumulator and released the aircraft back to service.

C-GTSY, an Airbus 310-304 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting IFR flight TSC547 from Bordeaux/Mérignac, France (LFBD) to Montreal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) with 223 passengers and 9 crew members on board. Approximately 5 hours after the departure from LFBD, a rapid depletion of the Green hydraulic system occurred, and was followed by a G SYS LO LEVEL message on the Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitor (ECAM). The flight crew executed initial ECAM actions and, approximately 120 nm North Northeast of CYUL, declared a PAN PAN. The remaining procedures were carried out before the landing, and the aircraft landed on Runway 06L without further incident. The aircraft was then shut down and towed to the gate. The operator’s maintenance determined the cause to be the number 1 Engine Hydraulic Engine Driven Pump (EDP) leaking. Both green EDP and case drain filters were replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYRD, a Swearingen SA226-TC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP, was conducting training flight PAG907T from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) to the northeast to train in a practice area. The training included a planned engine shutdown and air restart. The flight crew shut the number 2 engine (Garrett TPE331-10UA-511G) down, however they were unsuccessful in the air-start procedure. The flight crew advised ATC and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft returned to CYWG and landed without further incident with ARFF on standby. The operator's maintenance replaced the right hand inboard squat switch, the right hand speed stop/start switches and performed a right hand unfeather pump test. Ground runs were completed with no faults found and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GODA, a privately registered Cessna 180 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Toronto/Oshawa Executive, ON (CYOO) to Richmond Intl, VA (KRIC) with only the pilot on board. During the approach to KRIC, the aircraft encountered a fuel exhaustion situation and the engine stopped. During the forced landing to a baseball field short of Runway 20, the aircraft clipped power lines and collided with terrain. The pilot was uninjured, however there was substantial damage to the aircraft's right wing lift struts and floats.

C-FPOS, a privately registered Ayres S-2R agricultural aircraft, was on a local flight near Cupar, SK with only the pilot on board. After completing a pass over a wheat field, the aircraft was slow to respond to elevator input and collided with a tractor that was parked in the field. The aircraft struck the tractor with the right main landing gear, then landed under control in the field ahead. The aircraft came to a rest in an upright position. The pilot was not injured, however the aircraft sustained substantial damage. Reportedly, the aircraft flew next to a tree line and encountered some turbulent air.

C-GBHY, an Airbus 319-114 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1974 from Nanaimo, BC (CYCD) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 5 crew members and 135 passengers on board. During cruise flight, a flight attendant fell and sustained a minor injury. As the flight attendant was unable to continue with their duties, the remaining cabin crew members carried out the duties for the remainder of the flight.

C-GONX, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-100 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA758 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, à partir de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 30 passagers à bord. Alors qu’il se trouvait à 100 miles au nord-ouest de CYUL, l'équipage a reçu une indication de basse pression d'huile du moteur gauche (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW120A). L'équipage a fermé le moteur par précaution, a déclaré une urgence et l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre à CYUL à 0111Z. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GWWK, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by West Wind Aviation, was conducting flight WEW690 from Christina lake, AB (CCL3) to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl, SK (CYXE) and was level at 15 000 feet ASL in uncontrolled airspace. C-GSAV, a Beech B200 King Air aircraft operated by the Province of Saskatchewan, was conducting flight SLG4 from CYXE to Ile-a-la-Crosse, SK (CJF3) and was level at 16 000 feet in uncontrolled airspace. Both aircraft had made position reports, and were aware of conflicting traffic. The flight crew of SLG4 provided a positon report to WEW690, advising that they would be descending shortly into CJF3; however, they did not see WEW690 on their TCAS. At 25 nautical miles from CJF3, the flight crew of WEW690 received a TCAS RA to DESCEND, complied with the command and initiated a left hand turn. The flight crew of SLG4 did not receive any TCAS alert, however observed WEW690 in a descending left hand turn.

C-GADP, a privately operated Cessna T182T aircraft, was conducting an IFR flight from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl, SK (CYXE). During the departure off Runway 27, ATC instructed the pilot to climb on runway heading in order to allow a medevac flight to depart behind. The NAV CANADA controller then authorized TW911, a Beech 200 aircraft operated by Transwest Air, to depart from Runway 27 behind C-GADP with a right-turn northeast bound instruction. A loss of separation occurred when TW911 turned northeast later than anticipated. The separation decreased to 2 nm laterally and 900 feet vertically, where 3 nm or 1000 feet was required.

C-FXCA, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1712 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Punta Cana Intl, Dominican Republic (MDPC). During the climb after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew received a SPOILERS EICAS message. QRH procedures were followed, and it was decided to return to CYYZ. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN as a precaution, and the aircraft landed uneventfully below the Maximum Landing Weight with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance identified a fault within the Spoiler Control Module (SCM). The SCM was replaced and subsequent tests found no further faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GLKX, a Cessna 340A operated by Flex Air Services, was conducting a private flight from St. Thomas Muni, ON (CYQS) to Port Huron/St. Clair County Intl, MI (KPHN) with a single pilot on board. The pilot reported a right engine (Teledyne Continental TSIO-520-NB) power loss before radio communications and radar contact were lost. The wreckage of the aircraft was later found near a baseball field, in the vicinity of KPHN. The pilot was fatally injured, and the aircraft was destroyed. The NTSB is investigating (Ref: CEN18FA371).

C-FTDW, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG802 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). After the departure from CYVR, the flight crew were unable to trim the aircraft when using the electric trim switches. The flight crew completed the QRH and continued the flight using the manual trim. In coordination with the operator’s Operations Control Center (OCC) and ATC, it was determined that the aircraft could continue the flight to CYYZ at a lower altitude. During the descent into CYYZ, the flight crew was informed by ATC that the planned Runway 15L was no longer available, and that Runway 23 was now in use. Fuel calculations determined that the landing could be performed on minimum fuel, however ATC informed the flight crew that they were number 6 for the approach. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft was cleared for the ILS approach to Runway 15L where the aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by.

C-IKCJ, a float-equipped Merlin GT Basic Ultra-light aircraft, departed from Paddy's Pond, NL on a local flight with only the pilot on board. The aircraft landed on a pond near the township of Lower Island Cove, which is located 30 nm North Northwest of St. John's Intl, NL (CYYT). After refueling, the aircraft departed again for Paddy's Pond. During the initial climb, the aircraft collided with trees due to a loss of lift over the terrain, and crashed in a wooded area at the edge of the pond. The aircraft was substantially damaged, and the pilot egressed out of the aircraft with no reported injuries.

C-FNNU, a Boeing 777-333ER aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA890 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Rome/Leonardo da Vinci Intl, Italy (LIRF). During cruise flight in the vicinity of Prince Edward Island, the flight crew noticed that the fuel quantity in the centre tank was decreasing. The remaining fuel in the centre tank was transferred into the wings and the flight crew elected to return to CYYZ to have the aircraft inspected. No emergency was declared, however the flight crew requested ARFF to be present for the overweight landing. The aircraft landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance inspection determined that the left centre fuel discharge check valve was faulty, and replaced the unit in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions.

C-FGEI, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA61 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Seoul/Incheon Intl, South Korea (RKSI) with 13 crew members and 276 passengers on board. Approximately 2.5 hours into the flight over the Northwest Territories, all lavatories on the left hand side of the aircraft ceased draining or flushing. The flight crew elected to divert the aircraft to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) and declared a PAN PAN on arrival. The aircraft carried out an overweight landing without further incident. Subsequent maintenance actions involved de-clogging the left hand waste lines and carry out an enzyme treatment for the system. A valve purge command test, grey water/vacuum waste system test, and waste water system test were all successful. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-GAQZ, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA221 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). Upon arrival at CYVR, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to a hydraulic issue. The aircraft landed without further incident. Subsequent maintenance actions revealed that the number 2 Engine Driven Pump (EDP) failed, causing a hydraulic leak through the engine drain mast. The yellow hydraulic system quantity was at zero. The EDP was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FTID, an Aerospatiale/Aeritalia ATR 42-500 aircraft operated by First Air, was conducting flight FAB850  from Taloyoak, NU (CYYH) to Gjoa Haven, NU (CYHK). After an uneventful landing at CYHK, the aircraft was parked on the ramp with the number 1 engine shut down, and the number 2 engine in Hotel Mode (Propeller Brake engaged) in preparation for the subsequent flight. Shortly after shutting down the number 1 engine, the flight crew received a Master Warning for electrical smoke, followed with a strong smell in the cockpit and cabin. The flight crew carried out the emergency evacuation checklist and passengers were ordered to deplane the aircraft through the main cabin door. There were no injuries. The aircraft was removed from service to allow the operator’s maintenance to troubleshoot the source of the smoke. It was subsequently determined that the left hand turbo fan had seized. The left-hand pack was deferred per the MEL and the aircraft was ferried to Yellowknife, NU (CYZF) where the operator's maintenance replaced the left hand turbo fan. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GUSC, un appareil de type British Aerospace Jetstream 3212 exploité par Pascan Aviation, effectuait le vol PSC822 selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) à destination de Montréal/Saint-Hubert, QC (CYHU). Alors que l’appareil était à environ 72 miles au sud/sud-est de Val-d'Or, QC (CYVO), une perte d’espacement est survenue avec C-GHQL, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par Hydro-Québec, effectuant le vol HYD142 selon les règles de vol aux instruments, de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) vers CYUY. L’espacement entre les deux appareils a été réduit à 900 pieds sur le plan vertical et 4.8 miles sur le plan horizontal alors que la norme est 1000 pieds ou 5 miles. Toutefois, il n’y a eu aucun risque de collision. Une erreur au niveau du service de la circulation aérienne est à l'origine de la perte d'espacement.

C-GQBQ, un appareil de type Bombardier CL600-2B16 (Challenger 601-3A) exploité par le Service Aérien Gouvernemental (SAG) du Québec, effectuait le vol de transport médical QU20 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Bagotville, QC (CYBG) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 4 passagers à bord. Suite à une indication de problème du train d’atterrissage principal droit, l'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence et a demandé un réacheminement vers Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) où l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre. Le personnel de l’entretien a diagnostiqué le dysfonctionnement d'un poussoir du train droit et a remplacé les poussoirs des deux trains principaux. L’appareil a par la suite été remis en service.

C-GCKN, a privately operated Piper PA-23-160 aircraft, was conducting a local flight from Drayton Valley Industrial, AB (CER3) with a pilot and a passenger on board. While exiting the runway after an uneventful landing and rollout, the pilot inadvertently selected landing gear up, rather than retracting the flaps. Consequently, the right main landing gear collapsed. The right wing and propeller contacted the ground as the aircraft came to rest. The 2 occupants received no injuries.

C-FGWJ, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA328 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to St. John’s Intl, NL (CYYT). Some time after the departure, the flight crew was instructed by ATC to climb to FL390. During the climb, a loss of separation occurred between WJA328 and DAL2790, an Airbus 320 aircraft operated by Delta Airlines who was conducting a flight from Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl, MA (KBOS) to Minneapolis-St. Paul Intl/Wold-Chamberlain, MN (KMSP) at FL360. The separation between the two aircraft reduced to 4.7 nm laterally and 600 feet vertically, in airspace where 5 nm or 1000 feet is required.

C-GJWE, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3429 from St. John’s Intl, NL (CYYT) to Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ). Shortly after the departure from CYYT, the flight crew advised ATC that they were unable to retract the landing gear. The QRH was actioned and the flight crew requested to return to CYYT. No emergency was declared, however ARFF was requested to be on standby as a precaution. The flight landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance replaced both left hand main gear up lock actuator extension springs. A function check was completed with multiple gear swings with no faults found. A service difficulty report (SDR) has been filed.

C-FLHJ, a Boeing 737-400 aircraft operated by Flair Airlines, was conducting flight FLE127 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) to Hamilton, ON (CYHM). During the approach at CYHM, the flight crew did not receive a down and locked indication for the right main landing gear when landing gear down was selected. The flight crew initiated a missed approach and performed a fly-by the tower to confirm that the landing gear was down. Light bulbs were tested, and a visual check of the gear down indicator on the wing was also executed. However, due to the light condition, it was not possible to confirm that the landing gear was down. The flight crew declared an emergency and, upon touchdown, the right landing gear down and locked light illuminated. The remainder of the landing was uneventful. Once the operator’s maintenance verified that the landing gear was locked, the aircraft proceeded to the gate. The landing gear indicator switches were cleaned, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GEXY, a privately registered Found Brothers FBA-2C3 aircraft, was attempting to land on a private airstrip at Hudson Island, BC. During the final landing phase the aircraft's airspeed was higher than normal and the aircraft landed hard. After the initial touchdown the left main gear and nose gear collapsed causing the aircraft to nose over, coming to rest inverted. The ELT activated and search and rescue responded. The pilot sustained serious injuries and was medevac'd to hospital.  The three passengers sustained minor injuries.

C-FVVS, a Piper PA-31-350 aircraft operated by Island Express Air, was conducting flight IAX304 from Abbotsford, BC (CYXX) to Victoria Intl, BC (CYYJ) with 2 crew members and 2 passengers on board. While enroute, the flight crew observed an engine oil pressure caution light. Oil pressure and oil temperature on the right engine (Lycoming LTIO540-J2BD SN L-2222-68A) was rising. The flight crew notified ATC, declared and emergency and returned for landing at CYXX. The aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by.

C-FTIR, an Aerospatiale-Aeritalia ATR-42-500 aircraft operated by First Air, was conducting flight FAB892 from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) with 3 crew members and 37 passengers on board. While taxiing for departure at CYZF, the flight crew noted the smell of smoke in the flight deck. The aircraft was stopped on Taxiway Bravo when the smoke became visible. The flight crew contacted the flight attendant who confirmed the smell in the cabin. The flight crew actioned the QRH emergency evacuation checklist, shut down the engines, and ordered the passengers to evacuate. ARFF responded to the aircraft. The operator’s maintenance found the air extraction fan circuit board to be burnt, or overheated. No one was injured.

C-FACV, a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8426 from Kamloops, BC (CYKA) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with 3 crew members and 24 passengers on board. During the descent to CYYC, the aircraft flew through an area of moderate turbulence at 17 000 feet ASL, and the turbulence was worst at 15 000 feet ASL. The autopilot disengaged, and the flight crew momentarily lost control. Moderate turbulence continued until the aircraft descended below 7 000 feet ASL. All passengers were wearing their seat belts and received no injuries. The flight attendant experienced minor injuries, however was able to continue with their duties. The flight landed without further incident and the aircraft sustained no damage.

C-FFJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (CRJ200) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8457 from Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl, MA (KBOS) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) with 3 crew members and 48 passengers on board. When JZA8457 was cleared for takeoff from Runway 27 at KBOS, ATC warned the flight crew of a Cessna 172 north of the airport, heading southbound at 1500 feet. Shortly after takeoff and after intercepting track 234 to KIRAA, ATC advised the flight crew that the traffic was at their 1 o’clock position and 4 nm, and to maintain visual separation. Climbing through 1800 feet, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to MAINTAIN VERTICAL SPEED, which they complied with. The traffic passed 300 feet below JZA8457.

C-GSGF, a de Havilland DHC-6-300 aircraft operated by Sander Geophysics, was conducting a local survey flight from Killarney/Kerry, Ireland (EIKY) with Shannon Intl, Ireland (EINN) as the alternate. In the vicinity of Birr, Ireland, the flight crew smelled an overheating electrical odour. The flight crew initially decided to return to EIKY, and the onboard survey equipment was shut down. However, the odour continued, so the aircraft was flown to EINN, which was only 8 minutes away, where the aircraft landed uneventfully. The operator’s maintenance inspection performed in EINN determined that a faulty fuel gauge had overheated. The snag was rectified, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FKFZ, a Convair 340 aircraft operated by Kelowna Flightcraft, was conducting flight KFA578 from Prince George, BC (CYXS) to Kamloops, BC (CYKA). Shortly after the departure from CYXS, the aircraft cockpit would not pressurize normally and the flight crew observed a door open caution light. Upon visual inspection the flight crew found the R1 forward cargo door was slightly ajar and was secured in the secondary latch position. The door warning checklist was completed. The flight crew contacted ATC, declared an emergency and requested a return to land at CYXS.  The aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by.

C-GONX, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-102 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA8752 de Val-d’Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 35 passagers à bord. Quelques instants après le décollage de CYVO, l'équipage de conduite a observé une l’indication OIL PRESSURE MASTER WARNING pour le moteur gauche. Toutefois, l'indication de pression d'huile du même moteur indiquait une pression normale. Le moteur a été fermé par mesures de précaution et une urgence a été déclarée. L'appareil est revenu se poser sans encombre à CYVO.

C-GBZR, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1712 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Punta Cana Intl, Dominican Republic (MDPC) with 8 crew members and 250 passengers on board. Shortly after reaching cruising altitude following the departure from CYYZ, one of the pilots began to feel ill and subsequently became incapacitated. The other pilot elected to return to CYYZ and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed at CYYZ without further incident.

C-GMUU, a Mitsubishi MU-2B-60 aircraft operated by SkyNorth Air, departed Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) to conduct a maintenance check of the flight idle fuel flow system. During the approach into CYWG at the end of the maintenance check, the flight crew selected landing gear down; however, the landing gear did not extend. The flight crew conducted the emergency landing gear extension, notified ATC and requested ARFF on standby.  The aircraft subsequently landed without further incident. The operator's maintenance inspection revealed that the safety pin on the forward main landing gear door had sheared. The safety pin was replaced, functional tests of the landing gear were carried out, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FWEZ, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3500 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) to Gander Intl, NL (CYQX). During cruise flight, the flight crew noticed that the number 1 engine oil pressure was fluctuating, however it was still within operating limits. During the descent into CYQX, the oil pressure dropped below the lower operating limit of 61 psi, fluctuating between 50-61 psi. The flight crew actioned the QRH, and the number 1 engine was selected to start/feather, remaining in that selection for the remainder of the flight. An emergency was declared. During the RNAV approach for Runway 21, the flight crew had to execute a missed approach due to gusty winds. The aircraft returned for the RNAV approach for Runway 03, and the flight landed without further incident. The aircraft taxied to the gate and was shut down normally.The operator’s maintenance found the oil pump to be leaking from a transfer tube packing. All oil pump transfer tube packings were replaced and the aircraft was returned to service. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) has been filed.

C-FDYF, a privately registered amateur-built Murphy Elite on amphibious floats, took off from Runway 25 at Vancouver / Boundary Bay, BC (CZBB) for a local flight. The aircraft became airborne early and a gust of wind drifted the aircraft left until the left float contacted the ground. The aircraft cartwheeled and came to rest to the left of the runway. The pilot was not injured but the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GCTD, a privately operated Cessna 172N aircraft, landed westbound at the Sandpiper/Rowena's Airstrip at Harrison Mills, BC. During the landing phase, the aircraft encountered a crosswind from the north, which pushed it off the south edge of the runway, into foliage and other obstacles. The landing gear and the leading edge of the left wing were damaged; however, the pilot was not injured.

N981EV, un appareil de type CL-600-2B19 (Bombardier CRJ200) exploité par Endeavor Air sous l’indicatif de vol DAL5287 venait juste d'être repoussé de la passerelle d’embarquement 80 de l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl (CYUL) pour un vol à destination de John F Kennedy Intl (New York) KJFK , lorsque durant le démarrage du moteur droit, des flammes et de la fumée ont été observées par le personnel au sol. Après en avoir été avisé, le commandant de bord a demandé de ramener l’appareil à la passerelle où les passagers ont pu évacuer pendant l’intervention des services d’incendies. Des flammes résiduelles ont été éteintes dans la tuyère du moteur droit. Le personnel de maintenance à déterminer qu'une unité de contrôle de carburant (Fuel control unit) alimentait le moteur en surquantité et que le surplus de carburant éjecté dans la tuyère avait probablement été allumé par les gaz d'échappement chauds de l'unité de puissance auxiliaire (APU). Aucun dommage n'a été observé sur l'aéronef suite à ce bref incendie. Aucun passager ou membre d'équipage n'a été blessé.

N556NW, a Boeing 757-251 operating as Delta Airlines flight DAL1084 from Minneapolis-St. Paul Intl, USA (KMSP) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) was in cruise flight at FL380 when the crew observed a L HYD QTY LOW engine indication and EICAS message. The crew turned off the left hydraulic pumps and pulled the power transfer unit (PTU) circuit breaker. The fluid level subsequently stabilized. During approach to CYVR, when the crew selected hydraulic pumps ON before selecting flaps 1, they received a LE SLAT DISAGREE EICAS message. The crew declared an emergency, requested delay vectors, and extended the flaps using the alternate system. The aircraft landed without further incident.Maintenance personnel found the left landing gear retract actuator line (P/N AS116-08K0194) leaking. The line was replaced and the hydraulic system serviced.

C-GSTZ, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B3 aircraft operated by Star Helicopters, was on a VFR flight from the Elbow Ranger station near Bragg Creek, AB to Pincher Creek, AB (CZPC). As the visibility deteriorated to less than 2.0 nm in smoke during cruise flight, the pilot elected to follow Highway 22 south at approximately 500 feet AGL, making position reports on frequency 126.7 MHz. Just after passing abeam the town of Furman, AB, the pilot spotted another AS 350 helicopter in the opposite direction and at the same altitude, approximately 1500 feet ahead. The pilot made an evasive turn to the right, while the other helicopter also appeared to take evasive action. The two aircraft passed within 1000 feet of each other. The pilot of C-GSTZ could not positively identify the other aircraft, nor could communication be established with it. C-GSTZ continued to its destination and landed safely at CZPC.

C-GHQQ, un appareil de type Boeing 787-8 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA11 de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de Shanghai/Pudong Intl, China (ZSPD) avec 13 membres d'équipage et 248 passagers à bord. Peu de temps après le départ de CYUL, une défaillance d'un générateur-démarreur (Variable Frequency Starter Generator) est survenue. En conformité avec le manuel de référence rapide (QRH), le groupe auxiliaire de bord (APU) a été démarré. Toutefois, comme la procédure exigeait le fonctionnement de l'APU pour toute la durée du vol, l’exigence en carburant minimum était maintenant insuffisante pour se rendre à destination. Par conséquent, l'équipage de conduite a demandé une diversion vers l'aéroport de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ), où l'appareil a effectué un atterrissage en surcharge sans incident. Le personnel de l’entretien de l’exploitant a remplacé le générateur-démarreur et a effectué une inspection suite à un atterrissage en surcharge. Aucune anomalie n'a été observée.

C-GTGO, a de Havilland DHC-7-103 aircraft operated by Trans Capital Air, was conducting a ferry flight from Zagreb/Franjo Tudman, Croatia (LDZA) for Dortmund/Wickede, Germany (EDLW). Shortly after takeoff from LDZA, the number 2 HYD PUMP caution light illuminated. The flight crew declared an emergency and returned to LDZA. The landing was uneventful.

C-FIWT, a privately operated Piper PA-18-150 Super Cub aircraft, was on a VFR flight from Carcross, YT (CFA4) to a private strip known as Kiwi Lake, 102 nm NNE of Mayo, YT (CYMA) with only the pilot on board. While attempting to land on the turf runway, the pilot elected to abort the landing just after touchdown due to soft field conditions. By the time full power was reached and a positive climb was established, the aircraft impacted small trees at the end of the runway. The aircraft settled into the trees at the south end of the runway, sustaining substantial damage to the right wing and tail. The pilot was not inured.

C-FPWD, an Airbus 320-211 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA415 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During cruise flight, the flight crew received an ECAM message YELLOW HYDRAULIC LO PRESS. QRH procedures were followed and the flight crew declared an emergency. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by, and was subsequently towed to the gate from the runway. The operator’s maintenance determined that the "O" ring at the Power Transfer Unit (PTU) check valve was damaged and allowed for the depletion of the hydraulic liquid. The "O" ring was replaced and an operational check of the system found no further faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FIYA, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1650 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) Miami Intl, FL (KMIA). During cruise flight, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and could no longer perform their duties. Cabin crew positions were reassigned, and the flight continued to its destination uneventfully.

C-FJOK, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1886 from San Diego Intl, CA (KSAN) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 6 crew members and 192 passengers on board. During cruise flight, one of the flight attendant became incapacitated and was unable to perform their duties for the remainder of the flight. Duties were assigned to remaining cabin crew members for the landing.

C-GVED, un appareil de type Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 exploité par Hélicoptères Panorama, venait de livrer des isolateurs par charge à l'élingue à proximité du pylône 179, sur la grille 3001 au nord de Forestville, QC avec seul le pilote à bord. Lors de la manœuvre, un coup de vent a déporté l'appareil et le rotor principal est entré en contact avec le pylône. Le pilote a réussi à poser l'appareil sur place. Il n'y a eu aucune blessure.

C-GAHP, un hélicoptère de type Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 exploité par Hélicoptères Canadiens, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue au départ de Montréal/Les Cèdres, QC (CSH6) avec un pilote à bord. Alors qu’il se trouvait près de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU), le pilote a observé une indication de défaillance du système hydraulique. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre sur le gazon à CYHU, entre la piste 24L et la voie de circulation TANGO. L'appareil n'a subi aucun dommage et personne n'a été blessé. Le personnel de l’entretien a trouvé un capteur de pression hydraulique défaillant.

C-FJXW, a private, float equipped Piper PA-18-150 aircraft, was departing Kagianagami Lake, ON. During the takeoff in gusty wind conditions, the aircraft crashed and flipped over, becoming submerged. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, sustained serious injuries and was taken to hospital.

C-GITU, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA150 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). When the aircraft was on short final for Runway 06L at CYYZ, ATC instructed the aircraft to go around due to the previous arrival aircraft that was still on the runway. The go-around transmission was not acknowledged by the flight crew of ACA150, and the aircraft proceeded with the landing. The aircraft landed as normal and exited the runway without further incident.

C-GJVW, a Fairchild SA227-DC aircraft operated by Bearskin Airlines, was conducting flight BLS386 from Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT) to Sudbury, ON (CYSB) with 2 pilots and 9 passengers on board. Approximately 100 nm West of CYSB in cruise flight at FL190, there was a rapid decompression through the cabin door area. The flight crew advised ATC and commenced an emergency descent. The aircraft landed at CYSB without further incident.

N63886, a privately operated PA-23-250 aircraft, was taking off from Runway 06 at Sydney/J.A. Douglas McCurdy, NS (CYQY) for a local flight. On departure, exhaust gas and cylinder head temperatures dropped suddenly on the number 4 cylinder of the number 2 engine. The pilot initiated a left turn to return to the airport and made a PAN PAN call. ATS suggested a landing on Runway 18, and the aircraft landed without further incident.A post flight inspection revealed a broken engine ignition lead for the number 4 cylinder of the number 2 engine.

C-FMWV, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1940 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR), BC to Dublin Intl (EIDW), Ireland with 8 crew members and 257 passengers on board. As the aircraft was climbing through 10 000 feet shortly after the departure from CYVR, the flight crew heard a loud bang coming from the number 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney USA PW4060-3), associated with a power loss and abnormal engine indications. The number 2 engine was brought to idle, and a MAYDAY was declared. The flight subsequently returned to CYVR where an overweight landing was executed with ARFF on standby. There were no injuries. Following the landing, the Vancouver Intl Airport Authorities detected debris on Runway 08R/26L, and closed it to clean it up. An initial visual inspection of the engine revealed extensive damage to the aft-most turbine blades. The inboard aileron and the fuselage just aft of the baggage door were punctured by debris exiting the engine exhaust duct. The engine was sent to the manufacturer for teardown and inspection. The damage was limited to the Low Pressure Turbine (LPT) section, from the stage 4 vanes to the stage 6 turbine blades. Root cause analysis is on-going.

C-FNEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3476 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW). Following landing gear up selection after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew received a LDG GEAR INOP caution light. After contacting ATC and the operator, the flight crew decided to return to CYYZ. QRH procedures were completed and the landing gear was extended using the Alternate Gear Extension system. The flight crew received indication that the landing gear was down and locked, and proceeded to declare an emergency. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by, and stopped on the runway. Since nose wheel steering was no longer available, the aircraft needed to be towed to the gate. The operator’s maintenance found that the Nose Gear Lock Sensor 2 Bracket Mount was loose, allowing the sensor to move freely. The bracket was re-installed and subsequent landing gear retractions revealed no further faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FYTO, a privately operated Rotorway Exec 90 Amateur Built helicopter, was on a local VFR flight from a private residence north of Sherwood Park, AB. While conducting an autorotation with a power recovery, the pilot noticed the engine (Rotorway HC, RI162) had experienced a power loss. The autorotation was continued to touchdown, resulting in a hard landing. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the tail boom, the skid gear and the main rotor. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, sustained minor injuries.

The privately registered Piper PA-31 aircraft (C-GTEW) with the pilot and a passenger on board was on approach to runway 34 at Midland / Huronia, ON (CYEE), and the landing gear had not been extended.  Just prior to touchdown the pilot increased engine power and did not hear the landing gear unsafe horn until power was reduced just as the aircraft contacted the runway. The aircraft landed gear up and slid to a stop. Both occupants exited the aircraft and were not injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FHLL, an Amateur Built Storm 300 Special aircraft, was departing from Edenvale, ON (CNV8) with the pilot and a passenger on board. During the takeoff run from Runway 13, the aircraft veered to the right, exited the runway surface and impacted a bail of hay. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. There were no injuries.

C-IFZD, a privately owned Ultravia Pelican Sport Advanced Ultra-light aircraft, was landing at a private airstrip located approximately 8 nm South East of Tillsonburg, ON (CYTB) with only the pilot on board. During the touchdown, the aircraft landed hard, bounced, and the nose landing gear collapsed. The aircraft sustained substantial damage, however the pilot was not injured.

N18GB, a corporate Cessna 650 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Seattle/Boeing Field-King County Intl, WA (KBFI) to Kitchener/Waterloo, ON (CYKF). Shortly after the flight was handed off from Minneapolis Center (KZMP), the flight crew declared an emergency due to an engine issue. The aircraft continued to CYKF and landed without further incident. There were no injuries.

2-ODAY, a Bombardier CL600-2B16 Challenger 601 aircraft operated by Volare Aviation, was conducting flight VLZ595 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Cleveland/Burke Lakefront, OH (KBKL). As the aircraft was climbing to its cruising altitude after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew reported fumes in the cockpit. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft returned to CYYZ. There were no injuries, and the aircraft landed without further incident.The operator determined that the most likely cause of the fumes was leftover compressor wash agent in the engines.

C-IJGU, a privately owned float equipped Zenair STOL CH 701 SP Advanced Ultra-light aircraft, was being operated by a student pilot in the vicinity of Timmins, ON (CYTS). Following an approach on the Mattagami River, approximately 3 nautical miles South of CYTS, the aircraft experienced a hard landing. The sole occupant was not injured. It was reported that the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-FIVS, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA001 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Tokyo/Haneda, Japan (RJTT) with 15 crew members and 365 passengers on board. During cruise flight approximately 1200 nm North East of RJTT, the flight crew noted a decreasing oil quantity on the number 2 engine (GE90-115B). The flight crew continued to monitor the indication and subsequently elected to shut the engine down while in Tokyo airspace. A MAYDAY was declared, and the aircraft landed without incident 35 minutes later on Runway 23. The aircraft stopped on the runway for inspection, and was authorized to taxi to the gate.The operator’s maintenance found the oil pressure line from the fuel/oil heat exchanger to the number 4 bearing was leaking. The line was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GXYH, a Bell Helicopter 206B aircraft operated by Yellowhead Helicopters, was maneuvering with a long-line attached when the main rotor blades contacted the top of a tree. Since there was no change to the flight characteristics, torque or RPM noted, the pilot elected to return the helicopter to the staging area within a mile. After shutdown, damage was observed on the underside of both blades where the skin was pierced. The helicopter was grounded for further inspection and maintenance.

C-GZMN, a Cessna 172S aircraft operated by South Nahanni Airways, was on a VFR flight from Fort Simpson Island, NT (CET4) to Nahanni Butte, NT (CBD6) with one pilot and one passenger on board. While on short final to Runway 34 at CBD6, the pilot experienced a windshear and elected to go around. On the second attempt to land on Runway 34, the aircraft landed long. The pilot was unable to stop the aircraft on the runway and exited at the end, striking a runway end light. The aircraft was taxied to the apron and the pilot conducted an inspection; no damage was found. The pilot consulted with company management and the decision was made to return the aircraft to service. The incident and damage to runway lighting was reported to the airport manager.

C-FAVT, a Bell 407 helicopter operated by Canadian Helicopters, was conducting forest fire control operations and was on approach to release a load of water from the suspended Bambi bucket, when the long-line was inadvertently released from the helicopter belly hook. The operator’s maintenance suspected the mechanical emergency release mechanism was not fully retracted. Electrical wires at the disconnect plug were re-routed to offload pressure on the release cable.

C-GCJZ, a Boeing 727-200 aircraft operated by Cargojet, was conducting flight CJT245 from Newark/Liberty Intl, NJ (KEWR) to Bermuda/L.F. Wade Intl, Bermuda (TXKF) with 4 crew members on board. Shortly after the departure from KEWR, the flight crew levelled off the aircraft at 5000 feet and shut the number 3 engine (Pratt & Whitney USA JT8D-15A) down. A MAYDAY was declared, and the flight returned to KEWR without further incident.The operator’s maintenance found a pneumatic duct that was disconnected and proceeded to reconnect it.

C-FMZW, an Embraer ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1041 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Denver Intl, CO (KDEN) with 4 crew members and 97 passengers on board. As the flight crew was intercepting the glide slope for Runway 35R at KDEN, a TCAS RA to DESCEND was received. The instruction was followed and the flight landed without further incident.

C-FLHJ, a Boeing 737-400 aircraft operated by Flair Airlines, was conducting flight FLE137 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). C-FENO, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3153 from CYYC to Nanaimo, BC (CYCD). FLE137 was proceeding to the SIMTA intersection as authorized, however the flight crew did not intercept Airway Q894 and caused a loss of separation with WEN3153, who was tracking Airway T602. The separation eroded to 4.9 nm horizontally and 500 feet vertically, where 5 nm or 1000 feet is required.

C-FKYF, a privately operated Luscombe 8E aircraft, was conducting a local flight from Sundre, AB (CFN7) with one pilot and one passenger on board. During the flight, the pilot was practicing forced approaches to a cattle field, 5 nm South of CFN7. During the manoeuvre, the aircraft contacted the ground and struck a wire fence bordering the field. The aircraft flipped over and was substantially damaged. There were no injuries.

C-FJDQ, un appareil de type Beech B100 exploité par Max Aviation, effectuait le vol MAX100 à partir de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) vers Amos/Magny, QC (CYEY). C-FEYP, un appareil de type Beech A100 exploité par Propair, effectuait le vol PRO4500 depuis Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) vers CYEY. Les deux appareils ont été autorisés dans l'espace aérien non-contrôlé en prévision de leur approche à CYEY, et l'information sur le trafic a été échangée entre chacun des vols et l'ATC. En passant le repère d’approche finale URSOP, situé à 5 miles du seuil de la piste 32, PRO4500 a capté la transmission du MAX100 qui se rapportait en finale à 3 miles de la piste 32. PRO4500 a alors effectué une approche interrompue. N'ayant pas été en mesure d’établir le contact visuel avec la piste, MAX100 a effectué une remise des gaz quelques instants plus tard. Aucun des équipages de conduite n'a réussi à établir le contact visuel avec l’autre appareil. L'espacement minimum réel entre les deux appareils est inconnu. Le Centre de contrôle de Montréal a par la suite re-coordonné l'approche des deux appareils.

C-FFWI, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA718 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to New York/LaGuardia, NY (KLGA) with 5 crew members and 145 passengers on board. At approximately 4000 feet during the approach at KLGA, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to climb, and complied with it. The flight continued to KLGA and landed without further incident.

C-FMLV, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1967 from Berlin/Tegel, Germany (EDDT) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During cruise flight in the vicinity of Stavanger/Sola, Norway (ENZV), a flight attendant became incapacitated due to illness. The order of priority for the cabin crew was reassigned.

G-CLBA, a Boeing 747-400 aircraft operated by CargoLogicAir, was conducting flight CLU817 from Houston/George Bush Intercontinental, TX (KIAH) to Frankfurt/Rhein-Main, Germany (EDDF). Shortly after reaching cruising altitude out of KIAH, the flight crew received an ENG 2 FUEL FILT message. The checklist was executed, and the decision to continue to destination was taken. Approximately 630 nm East of Goose Bay, NL (CYYR), the flight crew received an ENG 1 FUEL FILT message. The flight crew decided to land at the nearest suitable airport, in accordance with the checklist. A PAN PAN was declared, and a diversion to CYYR was carried out without further incident. The aircraft was returned to service following the testing and inspection of the related fuel systems, including the replacement of both number 1 and 2 engine fuel filters.

C-GFAJ, un appareil de type Airbus 330-300 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA842 à partir de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) à destination de Dublin Intl, Irlande (EIDW) avec 10 membres d'équipage et 286 passagers à bord. Alors qu’il était en vol de croisière à 150 nm à l’est de CYUL, une défaillance du système hydraulique vert est survenue. L'équipage a demandé une diversion vers Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) et a déclaré un PAN PAN. L'appareil s'est posé sans problème à 0816Z. Le personnel de l’entretien de l’exploitant a remplacé un clapet de non-retour. L'aéronef a été remis en service.

C-GIUE, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA153 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). Shortly after the departure from CYYZ, the cabin crew noticed an electrical odour in the cabin. The In-flight Entertainment (IFE) System was switched off, and the smell dissipated. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and returned to CYYZ where the aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance followed the Fault Isolation Manual (FIM) procedures and checked different electrical circuits within the cabin; no faults were found. An engine run was carried out and no further faults were noted. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFJL un appareil de type Cessna 310 exploité par Grondair Transport inc effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Matagami (QC) à destination de Val-d'Or (CYVO), QC. En rapprochement de CYVO, le C-FFJL avait reçu l'instruction de l'unité de la circulation aérienne de demeurer hors de l'espace aérien contrôlé à plus de 25 miles de CYVO en raison du départ d'un appareil de type DHC-8-100 exploité par Air Creebec sous l'indicatif de vol CRQ203 en direction opposée en partance de CYVO à destination de Chisasibi QC à 11 000 pieds. Cependant, à 14 h 06Z, le C-FFJL avise être à 15 miles de CYVO en palier à 6000 pieds. À ce moment le CRQ203 était à 17 miles au travers de 6600 pieds. La distance séparant les deux aéronefs lors de leur croisement est inconnue.

C-FGJI, an Airbus A320 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA172 from Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with a crew of 5 and 126 passengers on board. While in cruise the aircraft was diverted to Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) due to a disruptive passenger. The crew declared a PAN PAN and the aircraft landed safely. The local authorities met the aircraft and removed the disruptive passenger. The aircraft continued to CYYZ.

C-FAIO, un Beech A100 exploité par Air Inuit Ltée sous l’indicatif AIE529, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) à destination de Schefferville, QC (CYKL) avec 2 membres d’équipage et aucun passager à bord. Sur la montée initiale de la piste 25 à environ 600 pieds, l’équipage a senti une odeur d’huile brûlée et a observé la présence de fumée dans le poste de pilotage. L’équipage a complété la liste de vérification d’urgence et a déclaré une urgence à la station de service en vol (FSS) à CYVP. Le C-FAIO s’est posé sur la piste 25 sans incident. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GTLS, a Beech 100 operated by Kississing Lake Lodge (dba Wings Over Kississing), was enroute from St. Andrews, MB (CYAV) to Silsby Lake Lodge, MB, with a crew of 2, and 9 passengers on board. While en route, the #2 engine (P&W PT6A-28) began losing oil pressure. The crew shut the engine down and diverted the aircraft to Thompson, MB (CYTH). An emergency was declared; the aircraft landed uneventfully. Inspection by the operator's maintenance of the #2 engine revealed failure of the carbon oil seal.

C-GEMZ, un appareil de type Beech 58P en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue au départ de Sherbrooke, QC (CYSC) à destination de Pembroke, ON (CYTA). Alors qu’il était en vol de croisière à une altitude de 15 000 pieds ASL, le moteur droit (Teledyne Continental Motor TSIO-520-WB) a démontré une perte de puissance significative, sans autre indication anormale. Le pilote a fermé le moteur par mesure préventive et a senti une odeur d’essence. Le pilote a déclaré une urgence et demandé un déroutement vers Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) où il s'est posé sans problème en présence des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). Il n'y a pas eu de blessé. L’inspection a révélé que l’attache d’une conduite d’arrivée de carburant du moteur droit était la cause de la fuite de carburant.

C-FGRC, un appareil de type DHC-8-102 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA764, effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de l’aéroport Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à destination de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV). Au moment d’amorcer la descente pour CYZV, des indications erratiques de surcouple du moteur #2 (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW120A) sont survenues. L’équipage a complété la liste de vérification d’urgence et a fermé le moteur #2 par mesure préventive. L’équipage a déclaré une urgence et demandé les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). Le C-FGRC s’est posé sans incident. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FDAO, un appareil de type Dash-8-102 exploité par Air Inuit sous l’indicatif AIE844 effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) à destination de Kangiqsualujjuaq (Georges River), QC (CYLU). Le C-FDAO circulait sur la rampe avec l’aide du personnel au sol pour se diriger vers la piste en vue de son décollage. Au moment de passer entre deux appareils stationnés, l’équipage a reçu un signal d’un membre du personnel au sol d’arrêter le C-FDAO. Le C-FDAO n’a pu être arrêté à temps et le bout de l’aile droite est entré en contact avec le gouvernail de direction d’un autre Dash-8 de la même compagnie (C-FOAI). Les 2 avions ont subi des dommages mineurs. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FRRQ, a Beech 200 aircraft operated by North Cariboo Flying Service, was conducting flight NCB1082 from Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with 2 flight crew members and no passengers on board. During the take-off roll on Runway 20 at CYEG, a yaw to the left was noticed, however it was controllable. As the aircraft lifted off, the yaw was more pronounced; the captain decided to abort the take-off and land on the remaining runway. The aircraft came to a stop just past Taxiway B1. The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and no issues were found.

On 16 August 2018, a Simpson Air (1981) Limited float-equipped Cessna U206G aircraft (registration C-FNEQ, serial number U20605036) was conducting a sightseeing flight from Fort Simpson Island Water Aerodrome, Northwest Territories, with stops at Virginia Falls and Little Doctor Lake, Northwest Territories. The pilot and 4 passengers were on board. At approximately 1830 Mountain Daylight Time, while the pilot was conducting a water landing at Little Doctor Lake, control of the aircraft was lost and the aircraft nosed over, coming to rest inverted and partially submerged. The pilot and 1 passenger were able to escape the submerged fuselage and climb up onto the floats; they were rescued by a nearby boater within 15 minutes. The 3 remaining occupants were unable to escape the fuselage and drowned. The emergency locator transmitter activated on impact; however, the signal was not received by the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre because the emergency locator transmitter was submerged.

C-FGQK, un appareil de type  DHC-8-100 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif AC8964, effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de l’aéroport de Mont-Joli, QC (CYYY) à destination de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC). Durant l’approche pour CYBC à 3500 pieds, l’équipage a reçu un avis de résolution du système de surveillance du trafic et d'évitement des collisions (TCAS) les avisant de descendre. L’équipage a suivi les directives du TCAS et a immédiatement augmenté le taux de descente à 1700 pieds par minute. L’équipage n’a pas eu de contact visuel avec le trafic en conflit. Le C-FGQK s’est posé sans incident. Aucun blessé.DHC

N622QX, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 aircraft operated by Horizon Air, was conducting flight QXE2569 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Seattle-Tacoma Intl, WA (KSEA). C-GAQL, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA227 from CYYC to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). Both aircraft were simultaneously cleared for takeoff on Runways 17L and 17R, and both were assigned runway heading for the initial climb. This situation resulted in a loss of separation.

C-FVJC, a Harv's Air Service, Beech D95A was on a local training flight at the Steinbach, MB airport (CJB3) with a student and instructor pilot on board. While on approach and the landing gear selected in the down position, the landing gear extended only half way. A manual gear extension was performed, but the gear did not extend fully. The aircraft then landed on grass with the landing gear partially extended and the aircraft eventually settled onto its belly. There were no injuries, the aircraft sustained substantial damage. An inspection by the operator's maintenance of the landing system revealed a failure of the landing gear actuator gearbox.

C-FZSJ, a Custom Helicopters Bell 206B-3, was enroute from Island Lake, MB (CYIV) to St. Theresa Point, MB (CYST) with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. During the short final approach into CYST, the engine (Allison 250-C20) began to decelerate and a hard landing was completed. There were no injuries and the aircraft is currently undergoing a hard landing inspection. The operator will advise the TSB of their findings.

C-FUWE, a Bombardier DHC 8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3212 from Edmonton Intl (CYEG) to Regina Intl (CYQR) with four crew members on board. On departure from CYEG, the aircraft was unable to pressurize and a door warning light illuminated. A PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft returned to CYEG. An uneventful landing was completed; the aircraft was removed from service and maintenance found a dislodged door vent seal on the L2 door.

C-GANE, a Cessna TU206G aircraft operated by South Nahanni Airways, was departing Nahanni Butte, NT (CBD6) for Ft. Simpson, NT (CYFS) with 1 pilot and 3 passengers on board. The flight departed at 1330 MDT from Runway 16 at CBD6 and shortly after liftoff, the aircraft experienced an engine power loss and was unable to climb. The pilot conducted a forced landing, and the aircraft came to a rest against the trees on the east side of the runway, perpendicular to the threshold of Runway 34. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. Two occupants sustained serious injuries, and two occupants received minor injuries. The ELT activated.Update 19 October 2018Subsequently, the aircraft engine was removed from the airframe and an examination occurred at the Edmonton, AB regional office of the TSB on 9 October 2018. Initial examination did not reveal any external anomalies with the engine. It was found that the timing of the LH magneto was unable to be checked due to the points appearing to be in an open state. The engine was taken to an overhaul facility for a test run on 10 Oct 2018. The engine was successfully started and run on a test stand on the RH magneto. During the course of the engine run the LH magneto began to operate. Post engine run, the LH magneto (Slick model 6300, P/N: 6310) was placed on a magneto test stand and its operation checked.  The intermittent operation was confirmed on the test stand. A detailed examination of the LH magneto was completed, and it was found that the carbon brush in the distributor gear that contacts the high tension contact of the coil, appeared to be contaminated with a slight oil residue and carbon dust resulting in sluggish operation of the carbon brush and an open circuit when not in contact with the coil. The LH magneto had accumulated 412.0 hrs. time in service since overhaul by Kelly Aerospace.

C-IJQP, a Challenger II ultralight on amphibious floats took off from the St. Lawrence River near Downie Island in a northerly direction. The aircraft had just become airborne as it passed the end of the island and gust of wind caused the aircraft to yaw to the right. The right float dug into the water followed by the right wing; and the aircraft flipped inverted. The pilot was able escape the aircraft and was not injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FRQN, un appareil de type Embraer ERJ 170-200 SU exploité par Sky Regional Airlines, effectuait le vol SKV7529 de St. John’s Intl, NL (CYYT) à Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Alors que l’appareil s'approchait de la passerelle numéro 7 après son atterrissage à CYUL, le moteur gauche est entré en collision avec la passerelle qui était mal positionnée. Personne n'a été blessé. La nacelle du moteur gauche a subi des dommages mineurs.

ACA829, un appareil de type Airbus 330-300 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait un vol de Lyon/St-Exupéry, France (LFLL) vers Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL).
