Lors de l’approche finale pour la piste 24R à CYUL, une perte d'espacement pour fin de turbulence de sillage est survenue avec WJA326, un Boeing 737-700 exploité par WestJet en provenance de Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG). L’incident s’est produit suite à une mauvaise planification du service de la circulation aérienne, alors que la distance entre les deux appareils a été réduite à 4,4 miles marins, la norme étant de 5 miles.

C-FJCP, a privately operated Cessna 172 aircraft, s/n 28956, was on a VFR flight from Edson, AB (CYET) to Westlock, AB (CES4) with only the student pilot on board. The aircraft departed CYET at 1642 Mountain Daylight Time (MDT) from Runway 07 on August 12th, and was declared missing on August 13th. The Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) conducted a search and the aircraft was found at 1611 on August 16th. The aircraft had collided with terrain and the student pilot was fatally injured. There was no post impact fire and the 121.5 MHz ELT did not activate; there was no flight plan filed with NAV CANADA.

C-FRHL, a Cessna 208B Caravan aircraft on amphibious floats operated by CFFI Ventures, was conducting a VFR flight from a fishing lodge on Eagle River, NL to Goose Bay, NL (CYYR) with one pilot and 8 passengers on board. The flight had departed from the water at the lodge and was on final approach at CYYR when the pilot noticed that the landing gear was still retracted. The pilot applied take off power, conducted a missed approach, and returned for a normal landing without incident. An inspection later identified that the float bottoms had contacted the runway surface and damage to the aft area of both float main keels had occurred. Maintenance personnel inspected and made repairs as per consultation with the float manufacturer. The damage to both left and right float main keel wear strips was dressed, and affected hardware was replaced.

C-GMXB, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG730 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Montego Bay/Sangster Intl, Jamaica (MKJS) with 8 crew members and 187 passengers on board. During cruise flight, 58 nm North West of Jacksonville Intl, FL (KJAX) at FL360, ATC passed 2 traffic information to SWG730 ahead; one aircraft was 1000 feet above, and one aircraft was 1000 feet below. Shortly after, the flight crew received a TCAS Traffic Advisory (TA), followed by a Resolution Advisory (RA) to DESCEND. The alert was triggered by the aircraft above that was descending toward SWG730. The flight crew complied with the RA and advised ATC. Subsequently, another TCAS RA to LEVEL OFF was received due to the aircraft below. ATC decided to turn SWG730 to the right in order to avoid both aircraft. Once clear of all traffic, SWG730 returned to the previously assigned altitude and continued to destination without further incident.

C-GCTS, an Airbus 330-300 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC510 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Paris/Charles de Gaulle, France (LFPG). During cruise flight, the flight crew received an ECAM FCMC number 1 fault. This was followed by a fuel imbalance ECAM message, and a loss of indication for the right inner tank with amber dashes on the other tanks. The flight crew confirmed that there was no fuel leak, and declared a PAN PAN inbound to LFPG due to unreliable fuel indications. The operator’s maintenance changed the number 1 FCMC before the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FIYA, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1947 from Lima/Jorge Chávez Intl, Perú (SPJC) to Toronto/Lester B. Person Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 9 crew members and 253 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL320, approximately 260 nm North Northwest of SPJC, the cabin crew reported an odour in the cabin described as “dirty socks”. The odour was not detected in the cockpit, however the flight crew elected to return to SPJC and declared a PAN PAN. During the descent to SPJC, approximately 7 tons of fuel were jettisoned, and the aircraft landed overweight without further incident.The operator’s maintenance is investigating the cause.

C-FKWM, un appareil de type Piper Aerostar 601P en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) à destination de Kitchener/Waterloo, ON (CYKF) avec seulement le pilote à bord. Lors du décollage de la piste 06L à CYHU, le pilote a perdu la maîtrise directionnelle de l'appareil. Le décollage a été interrompu, et l'appareil est sorti de piste du côté nord. Le train d'atterrissage principal gauche s'est affaissé. Le pilote n'a pas été blessé et a pu évacuer l'appareil qui a subi des dommages importants à l'aile gauche.

C-GHPT, un appareil de type Boeing 787-8 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA408 en provenance de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) à Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). ACA408 était sous guidage radar pour une approche vers la piste 06L à CYUL. Au même moment, C-FSES, un appareil de type Boeing 737 MAX 8 également exploité par Air Canada, et effectuant le vol ACA819 en provenance de Dublin Intl, Irlande (EIDW), était aussi sur guidage radar pour la piste 06L par le sud. Suite à une instruction tardive de virer, l'espacement entre les deux appareils a été réduit à 1.9 mile marin latéralement, et 800 pieds verticalement, alors que la norme est de 3 miles ou 1000 pieds.

N338NW, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL2278 from Minneapolis-St. Paul Intl/Wold-Chamberlain, MN (KMSP) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with 6 crew members and 156 passengers on board. DAL2278 had been given the EBGAL 4 arrival for RWY35R at CYYC. At the MATAV IAF, DAL2278 discontinued the STAR and commenced the RNAV Z. This resulted in a loss of separation with C-GTAG, a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, who was conducting flight JZA165. To regain the proper separation, the arrival controller turned DAL2278 outbound. The separation was reduced to 2.8 nm laterally and 400 feet vertically, where 3.0 nm or 1000 feet was required.

N762SU, a corporate PA-23-250 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Sept-Iles, QC (CYZV) to Charlottetown, PE (CYYG). During cruise flight, the pilot declared an emergency due to smoke in the cockpit, and requested to divert to Gaspe (Michel Pouliot), QC (CYGP) where an uneventful landing was carried out with ARFF on standby. The aircraft stopped on the runway to get inspected. It was determined that the source of the smoke was from the battery. The battery was disconnected, and the aircraft was towed to the ramp for further examination.

C-GFAT, un appareil de type Airbus 310-300 exploité par Air Transat, effectuait le vol TSC263 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Barcelone/EI Prat, Espagne (LEBL) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 9 membres d'équipage et 244 passagers à bord. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait à environ 135 miles marins à l'est de CYUL, l'équipage de conduite a déclaré un PAN PAN due à une baisse de la quantité de fluide hydraulique du système vert. Le TSC263 a poursuivi sa route et s'est posé sans problème à CYUL. Le personnel de l’entretien a déterminé que la fuite provenait de la pompe hydraulique. La pompe a été changée et l'appareil fût remis en service.

C-FENY, a WestJet Encore Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft (WEN3480) was on route from Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) to MacDonald-Cartier Intl - Ottawa (CYOW). As the aircraft climbed through 10000 feet ASL the crew received a #2 HYD ISO VLV message, followed by a zero fluid quantity indication. The QRH procedures were actioned and after contacting company maintenance and dispatch the flight continued to CYOW. On approach to CYOW the crew declared an emergency and landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. After the aircraft parked at the gate, smoke was noticed in the vicinity of the #2 engine and the captain ordered a rapid deplanement as a precaution. Maintenance found a hydraulic leak from the #2 HYD EDP. The pump was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service after the system was checked for leaks and contamination.

C-GJSZ, a Bell 206B Helicopter, operated by Expedition Helicopters was maneuvering at the operator’s base located in Cochrane, Ontario when a main rotor blade contacted a covered trailer. The main rotor and transmission separated from the helicopter. The helicopter stayed upright but sustained substantial damage. The two occupants were not injured.

C-GIJZ, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8417 from Kelowna, BC (CYLW) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 4 crew members and 76 passengers on board. After the departure from CYLW, the flight crew received a flap power caution message, and the flaps remained at the flap five position. The flight crew requested ARFF to meet the aircraft upon landing at CYVR, where it landed without further incident.

C-GODM, an amateur built Glastar on floats, was landing at Peninsula Lake with the pilot and one passenger on board.  During touchdown the right float dug in and the aircraft flipped. The pilot and passenger, who were wearing 3 point safety harnesses, exited the aircraft with minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

N683DH, a vintage De Havilland DH-89A MKIV 'Dragon Rapide' biplane operated by Historic Flight Foundation, was conducting air rides at the termination of the second day of the Abbotsford International Airshow, when it departed with four passengers off Runway 25 from the intersection of Taxiway Delta for a local flight to the South East. During the initial climb shortly after becoming airborne, the aircraft impacted the runway with its right wings, and came to rest on its nose on the right edge of the runway with approximately 3000 feet remaining. ARFF responded and were on scene within a few minutes. Three passengers suffered minor injuries and were taken to hospital for observation. One passenger received serious injuries, and was airlifted by helicopter. The pilot was seriously injured, and required to be extricated from the wreckage; he was also airlifted to the hospital. The airplane was substantially damaged.

C-FTIY, a privately operated Christavia MK I Amateur Built aircraft, was conducting a local flight from the Indus/Winters Aire Park, AB (CFY4) with only the pilot on board. This was the first flight after the installation of a new propeller and a cylinder in the Teledyne Continental O-200A engine. Shortly after lift-off from Runway 34, the performance wasn't as expected and the pilot reduced the power to land; however, directional control could not be maintained. The aircraft nosed over in a wheat field to the west of the runway, and came to rest on its back; the pilot was uninjured.

C-FCJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ 900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA840 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to San Francisco Intl, CA (KSFO) with 4 crew members and 77 passengers on board. During the climb after the departure from CYVR, the flight crew noted vibrations from the number 2 engine. An emergency was declared, and the decision to return to CYVR was elected. The aircraft carried out an uneventful, slightly overweight landing on Runway 08R with ARFF standing by.The operator’s maintenance replaced a fan blade pin 15. A vibration check was performed in accordance with Aircraft Maintenance Manual TASK 71-00-00-720-806. No further faults were found, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJPY, an Aerospatiale ATR-72-202 aircraft operated by Summit Air, was conducting flight SU7131 from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Hope Bay, NU (CHB3) with two crew members on board. During the initial portion of the approach into CHB3, the flight crew observed a LO LVL caution for the green hydraulic system. A decision was made to return to CYZF and the flight crew declared a PAN PAN to get ARFF on standby for the landing. An alternate landing gear extension procedure was used to lower the landing gear, and the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance found a cracked hydraulic fitting related to the green hydraulic system. A Service Difficulty Report (SDR) was submitted to Transport Canada.

C-GJTA, a Dassault-Breguet Dornier Alpha Jet Model A aircraft operated by Top Aces, was conducting flight FISHBED1 over Katherine/Tindal, Australia (YPTN). Upon landing gear retraction shortly after takeoff, the landing gear retraction failure indication illuminated. Simultaneously, the pilot heard a noise. After advising ATC of the situation, FISHBED1 orbited over YPTN to execute the Landing Gear Retraction Failure emergency checklist. After confirming that the landing gear was down and locked, burning off fuel to achieve the maximum landing weight and declaring an emergency, FISHBED1 returned to YPTN for an uneventful landing.

C-FPDK, a Piper PA-31-350 aircraft operated by K.D. Air Corporation, was conducting charter flight KDC730 from Qualicum Beech, BC (CAT4) to Bella Bella (Campbell Island), BC (CBBC) with 1 pilot and 6 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CAT4 while climbing through 1200 feet, the left engine (Avco Lycoming TIO-540-J2BD) surged, while the associated fuel flow gauge indicated fluctuations. The pilot then reduced the power to the engine and, consequently, the engine stopped. The pilot declared an emergency and circled to land at CAT4. The aircraft landed without further incident, and no injuries were reported. Subsequent maintenance action revealed that the engine had a loose elbow fitting on the fuel supply line for the fuel pump. The elbow was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFWN, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA559 from Los Angeles Intl, CA (KLAX) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 5 crew members and 145 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL320, approximately 7 nm North of the Salinas VOR (SNS), the flight crew received a TACAS TA, which was followed shortly thereafter by an RA to CLIMB. The flight crew executed the command until a CLEAR OF CONFLICT aural message was received, levelled off at FL345, and notified ATC of the situation. At the flight crew’s request, ATC cleared ACA559 back down to FL340, and the flight continued to destination without further incident. The other aircraft involved has been identified as N261WN, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by Southwest, who was conducting flight SWA554 from Oakland/Metropolitan Intl, CA (KOAK) to KLAX. The closest lateral/vertical distance recorded was 4.7 nm laterally and 775 feet vertically.

C-GTUK, a Boeing 737-200 aircraft operated by Nolinor, was conducting flight NRL950 from Churchill, MB (CYYQ) to Meadowbank, NU (CMB2) with 5 crew members and 76 passengers on board. During the take off roll at CYYQ, the flight crew noticed numerous Canada geese flying over the runway, and initiated a rejected takeoff at 120 knots. The aircraft collided with a goose on the runway, and was brought to a stop with 1200 feet of runway remaining. The flight crew set the parking brake to assess the situation prior to returning to the apron. Upon releasing the parking brake, the flight crew noticed that the brakes had seized. ARFF was requested to inspect the landing gear. Both tires on the left main landing gear had deflated due to melting of the fusible plugs, and the aircraft was unable to taxi. The operator's maintenance replaced all four tires and brakes and completed a High Energy Braking inspection.

C-GNQZ, a Pilatus PC-12/47E aircraft operated by North Star Air, was conducting flight BF711 from Pickle Lake, ON (CYPL) to Webequie, ON (CYWP). When the aircraft was in a climbing right turn after the departure from CYPL with the autopilot engaged, an un-commanded disconnect of the autopilot and yaw damper occurred. The flight crew attempted to re-trim the rudder to the left prior to re-engaging the autopilot and yaw damper, however the rudder trim remained stuck at approximately 80% nose-right and difficulty in maintaining straight flight was encountered. The flight crew elected to divert to Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT), and attempts to troubleshoot and rectify the problem by following the QRH and resetting the rudder trim circuit breaker were unsuccessful. Attempts to re-engage the autopilot and yaw damper generated a "YD (Yaw Damper) Hold Nose Left" Cockpit Alerting System message. The autopilot and yaw damper were left disengaged for the remainder of the flight. When the flight was approximately 120 nm North of CYQT, the flight crew declared an emergency. Since turning to the left was difficult, a right hand approach to Runway 25 was elected. The possibility of a compromised nose-wheel steering system was discussed, so it was decided to hold the nose-wheel off the ground as long as possible. The subsequent landing was uneventful and the nose-wheel steering operated normally. The operator's maintenance replaced the autopilot trim adapter.

C-GLQO, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE229 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) to St. John’s Intl, NL (CYYT). As the flight climbed through 11 000 feet after the departure, the flight crew received a message that the cargo door was unsafe. The flight crew contacted ATC and initiated a return for CYHZ. When descending through 4000 feet, the cabin depressurized rapidly. The flight crew requested emergency vehicles on stand by for the landing, and the aircraft landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance found that the cargo door handle had moved out of its flush, latched position, which allowed the cargo compartment pressurization to decrease. The aft cabin bulkhead blowout panel became dislodged because of the cargo compartment pressure loss.

C-GABP, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-300 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA735 des Îles-de-la-Madeleine, QC (CYGR) à Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). C-GKQC, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par Porter Airlines, effectuait le vol POE471 de Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City, ON (CYTZ) à CYUL. Suite à une erreur opérationnelle de l'unité ATC, la séparation entre les 2 appareils n'a pas été maintenue lors de l’approche à CYUL. L'espacement latéral entre les deux appareils a été réduit à 1.8 nm, et 800 pieds verticalement, alors que la norme d'espacement est de 3 nm ou 1000 pieds.

C-GHXO, a Cessna 180J aircraft operated by Trek Aerial Surveys, was conducting pipeline patrols approximately 30 nm East of Fort St. John, BC (CYXJ) with one pilot and one observer on board. The area of inspection features a significant amount of oil and gas production infrastructure. After flying for about 3 hours, the amount of forest fire smoke had increased significantly. Coincidentally, the pilot and the observer began to feel out of sorts; cognition was reduced. The pilot decided to head back to CYXJ out of precaution and while en route, the ability to concentrate became more difficult for both the pilot and the observer. ARFF was on standby for the landing, which was uneventful. Both the pilot and observer were met by EMS for observation and nothing significant was noted. The aircraft exhaust system was checked for leaks, and none were found.

C-FADF, a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA215 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies Intl, BC (CYXC). During the cruise section of the flight, the flight crew received a number 1 Hydraulic Isolation valve caution light. An emergency was declared and the flight crew elected to divert to Kelowna, BC (CYLW) where an uneventful landing was completed. The operator’s maintenance are troubleshooting to determine the cause.

C-GVWJ, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA653 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with 126 passengers and 5 crew members on board. While in cruise flight, a flight attendant became ill and was unable to complete their duties. The duties were distributed between the remaining flight attendants and the aircraft continued to CYYC without further incident.

C-FATW, a de Havilland DHC-6-300 aircraft operated by Air Tindi, was conducting flight TIN218 from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Whatì, NT (CEM3) with 2 pilots and 9 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew noticed smoke in the cockpit, which quickly dissipated. The flight crew actioned the QRH and declared an emergency. The flight returned to CYZF and landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. After the landing, the flight crew noted that the left-hand landing light was still on despite the switch being in the off position. The operator’s maintenance found the pulse light wiring connector shorted internally.

C-FHJU, a Embraer ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA547 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Portland Intl, OR (KPDX). During cruise flight, ten minutes prior to the top of descent, the aircraft experienced a failure of the secondary power distribution assembly that resulted in a fuel feed fault, as well as high cabin temperatures. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN just after commencing the descent when they were given a delay vector of 90° to the south. The flight subsequently landed uneventfully in KPDX. Troubleshooting was undertaken.

N853DN, a Boeing 737-900 aircraft operated by Delta Airlines, was conducting flight DAL1328 from Seattle-Tacoma Intl, WA (KSEA) to Anchorage/Ted Stevens Intl, AK (PANC). During cruise flight approximately 100 nm West of Prince Rupert, BC (CYPR), the flight crew received a number 1 engine fuel pressure warning light. Suspecting a fuel leak, the flight crew elected to shut the number 1 engine (CFM Intl CFM56-7B27EB3) down, declared an emergency and diverted to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) where the aircraft landed without further incident 96 minutes later.The operator’s maintenance is investigating the issue.

C-FJFR, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-6-300 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE3652 de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) à destination d’un camp situé à 68 miles marins au nord-est de CYVP avec 2 membres d’équipages et 4 passagers à bord. Lors de l'atterrissage, le patin de protection de la queue de l'appareil est entré en contact avec le sol. Une roche sous le sable a causé des dommages aux supports du patin de queue. Un permis de vol a été requis afin de ramener l'appareil à la base.

C-GCVE, a Bell 412EP helicopter operated by the Government of Canada, Department of Transport, was carrying out an external load operation near Shearwater, BC. As the aircraft was 6 to 7 minutes into the flight over water, the load released inadvertently. The pilot returned to the staging area where it was discovered that all three ropes holding the load had severed. The load was recovered and towed to shore.

C-FAFC, a Cessna 208B aircraft operated by Conair Group, was conducting fire-fighting operations from Edson, AB (CYET) with 2 persons on board. Approximately 35 nm North of CYET while returning to the firebase, the autopilot system disconnected. The flight crew attempted to re-engage the autopilot, however without success. At that time, a burning odour was detected in the cockpit. There was no sign of visible smoke and no other system failures were detected. The flight crew selected the battery master, standby power and main generator to the off position, and circuit breakers to the autopilot system were pulled. The odour then began to dissipate. The main electrical power was restored, and the aircraft proceeded to land at CYET without further issues.

C-FNOH, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA44 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to New Delhi/Indira Gandhi Intl, India (VIDP) with 14 crew members and 238 passengers on board. During cruise flight approximately 20 nm Northeast of Astana Intl, Kazakhstan (UACC), the left hand cabin air compressor (CAC) experienced an uncommanded shut down, resulting in a burning/plastic smell throughout the aircraft. The flight crew assessed the situation and elected to continue to destination. The smell did not dissipate during the remainder of the flight and, as a precaution, the flight crew used oxygen for about 30 minutes during descent to FL100.The operator’s maintenance replaced the L2 CAC, in addition to the check valve as per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM).

C-GKWJ, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1100 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Los Angeles Intl, CA (KLAX) with 6 crew members and 174 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL360 approximately 135 nm North West of Albuquerque Intl Sunport, NM (KABQ), the flight crew noticed smoke coming out of the radio panel. After executing the QRH and communicating with the operator’s maintenance, a diversion to KABQ was elected. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed at KABQ 27 minutes later without further incident.The operator reported that the smoke was caused by an accidental liquid spill on the communication panel. Maintenance personnel replaced the panel and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GZJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (CRJ200) aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7271 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Memphis Intl, TN (KMEM) with 3 crew members and 44 passengers on board. During the approach into KMEM, the cabin crew member became incapacitated. Emergency services were called to the aircraft after the landing, and the cabin crew member was sent to the hospital.

C-GTSR, an Airbus 330-243 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC446 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Bordeaux/Mérignac, France (LFBD) with 11 crew members and 273 passengers on board. When descending through FL210 approaching destination, as ATC had cleared TSC446 to a lower altitude, another aircraft unexpectedly came into its path. A TCAS TA was immediately triggered, followed shortly thereafter by an RA. The flight crew executed the memory items to resolve the conflict. ATC was informed of the situation and advised that they were investigating.

N198AA, a Boeing 757-200 aircraft operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL89 from Shannon Intl, Ireland (EINN) to Philadelphia Intl, PA (KPHL) with 166 passengers and 9 crew members on board. When the aircraft was established in cruise flight at FL380, just abeam Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ), the flight crew was informed of a smoke odour in the cabin. No emergency was declared, however the flight crew requested a diversion to CYHZ where the aircraft conducted an overweight landing without further incident. Maintenance personnel determined that the forward equipment supply fan was inoperative. The fan was replaced, and an overweight inspection was performed. The aircraft was subsequently released back to service.

C-FMZB, an Embraer ERJ 190-100 IGW aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting IFR flight ACA1113 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ), to Regina Intl, SK (CYQR). During cruise flight over Thunder Bay, ON, the flight crew observed a burning smell in the cockpit. Subsequently, in the vicinity of Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG), the aircraft experienced a brief failure of an avionics computer and a second event of the burning smell in the cockpit. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and elected to divert to CYWG where the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator's maintenance replaced the MAU 1 and 2 power supplies and the MAU 1 NIC processor. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-GKFO, a Convair 340/580 aircraft operated by Conair Group, was conducting local flight FGD453 in support of fire-fighting operations from Slave Lake, AB (CYZH) with only the 2 pilots on board. During the takeoff, observers on the ground noted that one of the nose wheel came off on departure, and the flight crew was notified by radio. The flight crew extended the flaps and the landing gear, and the missing nose wheel was confirmed by the pilot of the birddog aircraft that was accompanying FGD453. The fire retardant was jettisoned, and the flight diverted to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG). An emergency was declared, and the flight landed uneventfully. The aircraft stopped on the runway, and was towed to a maintenance facility.The nose wheel was recovered from CYZH. The operator’s maintenance is investigating.

C-GIVP, un appareil de construction amateur Abyla-1 équipé de flotteurs en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol récréatif selon les règles de vol à vue depuis la rivière des Montagnes Blanches, QC avec 1 pilote et 1 passager à bord. Lors du décollage suite à la sortie de l’eau des flotteurs, une rafale de vent a causé la remise à l’eau du flotteur gauche, causant ainsi une déviation de trajectoire. Le pilote a sécurisé l’appareil et a fermé le moteur, mais n’a pas été en mesure de modifier la trajectoire vers la droite; conséquemment, l’appareil a percuté des arbres en bordure de la rivière. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé, et les deux occupants ont évacué l’appareil. L’appareil a subi des dommages importants. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) s’est déclenchée, et le pilote a signalé sa condition par téléphone satellite. Le Centre conjoint de coordination des opérations de sauvetage – Trenton a évacué les deux occupants.

C-GLML, a privately registered Cessna P210N aircraft operated by Superior Airways, was conducting a flight from Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT) to Red Lake, ON (CYRL). Prior to departing from CYQT, the fuel gauges indicated approximately 3/4 full for the planned 1 hour and 45 minute flight. While descending through 3500 feet ASL toward CYRL, the engine (Teledyne Continental TSIO-520-P) began to lose power. The engine indications were normal, but the fuel pressure was decreasing. The pilot switched fuel tanks, and turned the auxiliary fuel pump on. The pilot declared a Mayday and informed Kenora radio that it was not possible for the aircraft to reach CYRL, and an attempt would be made to land on a road. The right fuel tank indicated empty, and the pilot switched to the left tank which was indicating more fuel. The pilot changed throttle settings to no effect. When the approach to the road was assured, the pilot lowered the landing gear and selected flaps 10. The forced landing was conducted successfully on a mine road. During the landing roll, the nose wheel contacted a speed bump, and the nose landing gear collapsed. The pilot and the passenger were uninjured. The aircraft sustained damage to the nose landing gear, propeller, engine, cowling, and right wing leading edge.An inspection of the aircraft revealed that there was no fuel remaining on board, however the left fuel quantity gauge was still indicating 3/4. Testing of the left fuel tank quantity indication system revealed that, when the fuel quantity sender was moved between empty and full, the indicator moved between 3/4 and full.

C-FCDQ, a float-equipped Cessna 180H aircraft operated by Fort Langley Air, was taking off from Tyaughton Lake, BC with 3 persons on board for a photography flight. As the aircraft was climbing through approximately 300 feet shortly after takeoff, the instructor pilot, who was seated in the back left seat, observed fuel leaking from the left wing. The instructor pilot informed the pilot flying about the fuel leak, and instructed to turn back and land on the lake. The pilot flying reduced the airspeed and initiated right turn. Shortly after the turn was initiated, control of the aircraft was lost and the aircraft impacted the surface of the lake. The aircraft came to rest inverted in water, approximately 10 to 15 feet deep, and 50 feet from the shore of the lake. The instructor pilot and the passenger were fatally injured; the pilot flying sustained serious injuries. The ELT did not transmit a signal and there was no post-impact fire.

On 01 August 2018, after completing 2 hours of survey work near Penticton, British Columbia (BC), an Aries Aviation International Piper PA-31 aircraft (registration C-FNCI, serial number 31-8112007) proceeded on an instrument flight rules flight plan from Penticton Airport (CYYF), BC, to Calgary/Springbank Airport (CYBW), Alberta, at 15 000 feet above sea level. The pilot and a survey technician were on board. When the aircraft was approximately 40 nautical miles southwest of CYBW, air traffic control began sequencing the aircraft for arrival into the Calgary airspace and requested that the pilot slow the aircraft to 150 knots indicated airspeed and descend to 13 000 feet above sea level. At this time, the right engine began operating at a lower power setting than the left engine. About 90 seconds later, at approximately 13 500 feet above sea level, the aircraft departed controlled flight. It collided with terrain near the summit of Mount Rae at 1336 Mountain Daylight Time. A brief impact explosion and fire occurred during the collision with terrain. The pilot and survey technician both received fatal injuries. The Canadian Mission Control Centre received a 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter signal from the occurrence aircraft and notified the Trenton Joint Rescue Coordination Centre. Search and rescue arrived on site approximately 1 hour after the accident.

SKW5462, an Embraer 175 aircraft operated by SkyWest Airlines, was conducting a flight from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Denver Intl, CO (KDEN). SKW5462 was instructed to fly a heading of 040° after the departure, however ATC observed the aircraft flying a heading of 090°. Consequently, ATC instructed SKW5462 to turn left to the correct heading of 040°. The separation between WJA1511, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft and SKW5462 was reduced to 2.3 miles laterally, where 3 miles is required.

C-FMZW, an Embrear ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1113 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Regina Intl, SK (CYQR). During the climb out of CYYZ after the departure, the flight crew noted a change in the sound, as well as a vibration, from the number 2 engine (General Electric CF34-10E5A1). The power was reduced on the affected engine, and the flight crew elected to return to CYYZ. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced the engine.

N7ZR, a privately registered Aviat A-1C-180 (Husky) aircraft, was on a VFR flight plan from Glasgow, MT to Lethbridge, AB (CYQL) with 2 persons on board. During the touchdown on Runway 23 at CYQL, directional control was lost and the aircraft swerved to the right. The left landing gear collapsed, and the left wing tip was bent; there was a fuel spill. There were no injuries to the pilot and passenger.

C-FSRY, a Dehavilland DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8240 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Terrace, BC (CYXT) with 4 crew members and 74 passengers on board. Just prior to touchdown to RWY 33 at CYXT the aircraft encountered low level windshear. The flight crew decided to reject the landing after the right wheel made contact with the runway. The aircraft entered the missed approach and circled for RWY 15. The aircraft landed without further incident.  No injuries were reported.

C-FKNS, a float equipped, Found Aircraft Canada FBA-2C1, commercially operated by Georgian Bay Airways, departed Toronto Billy Bishop Water Aerodrome destined for Parry Sound Harbour. During low level maneuvering in the Lake Muskoka area, the aircraft struck the water and then cartwheeled. The aircraft was significantly damaged and sank a short time after the accident. The two occupants egressed with minor injuries; the aircraft was destroyed. The TSB deployed two investigators to the scene.

On 31 July 2018, C-ITMF, a privately operated Kasper Kootenay Wings MS Special Basic Ultralight aircraft was conducting a flight from a private airfield, east of Grande Prairie, Alberta, to John G. Diefenbaker International Airport in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan (CYXE). Approximately 1.5 nm after takeoff, at an altitude of 500 feet, the aircraft entered a nose down attitude and collided with terrain. The pilot was fatally injured and there was a post-crash fire.UPDATED: 19 May 2020

C-FBWI, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1511 from Los Angeles Intl, CA (KLAX) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). During the approach to Runway 35R at CYYC, the flight crew received an aural warning for windshear. A missed approach was executed and the flight crew set up for a second approach to Runway 35R. During the second approach, an aural warning for windshear was heard again. The flight crew conducted another missed approach, and consulted with the operator’s operational control centre (OCC). The decision was then made to divert the flight to Lethbridge, AB (CYQL). Since the predicted fuel remaining at CYQL was below 3000 pounds, the flight crew declared a fuel emergency. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYQL with 3000 pounds of fuel remaining.

C-GRRS, a privately operated PA-60-602P aircraft, departed from Pembroke, ON (CYTA) to Charlottetown, PE (CYYG). During cruise flight, the pilot declared an emergency. A diversion to Greenville Municipal, ME (3B1) was initiated, and the aircraft impacted terrain during the approach, 0.25 nm from the threshold of Runway 14. The pilot and the 2 passengers were fatally injured; the aircraft was destroyed. The NTSB investigated (ERA18FA206).

C-GVZJ, a privately operated Piper PA-28-161 (Warrior II) aircraft, was departing from a cut hay field, approximately 2 nm East of Black Diamond, AB, with two persons on board.  During the takeoff, the aircraft collided with stacked hay bales and crashed; a post-impact fire ensued. The aircraft was destroyed. 1 person received fatal injuries and the other was taken to hospital with serious injuries.

ACA318, an Airbus 321 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting a flight from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). JZA221, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft, was conducting a flight from CYYC to Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) and departed behind ACA318. As ACA318 was climbing northbound to FL210 after the departure from CYYC, its slow rate of climb allowed JZA221 to overtake ACA318. The separation eroded to 2.8 nm laterally and 500 feet vertically, where 3 nm or 1000 feet was required.

C-GNWT, a Beech B200GT aircraft operated by Air Tindi, was conducting Medevac flight TIN512 from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Fort Smith, NT with 2 crew members and 2 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure off Runway 28 at CYZF, an odour was detected coming through the air vents, and the flight crew was informed of the presence of smoke in the cabin. The flight crew requested a return to CYZF, and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed shortly after on Runway 34 without further incident. The operator’s maintenance found that the smoke was actually an odour caused by an engine wash residual cleaner that had remained in the compressor.

C-GCPH, a Messerschmitt MBB-BK117 B-2D helicopter operated by Shock Trauma Air Rescue Service (STARS), had deployed from Grande Prairie, AB (CYQU) to a MEDEVAC scene in British Columbia. Approximately 14 minutes after the departure from the scene while enroute to CYQU, the number 1 engine (Avco Lycoming LTS-101-750B-1) chip light illuminated. The crew carried out an inflight shutdown, declared an emergency and diverted to Fort St. John, BC (CYXJ) where a single engine landing was conducted. There were no injuries.

PCO3014, a Saab 340 aircraft operated by Pacific Coastal Airlines, had departed off Runway 17R at Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC), and was issued a left turn direct to NOSIV after departure. CFG441, a Boeing 767 aircraft operated by Condor Airlines, was conducting a flight from CYYC to Stuttgart/Echterdingen, Germany (EDDS). Shortly after becoming airborne off Runway 17L at CYYC, CFG441 came within 300 feet vertically and 1.6 nm laterally from PCO3014, where 1000 feet or 3.0 nm was required.

C-FJJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8040 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Chicago/O'Hare Intl, IL (KORD) with 4 crew members and 58 passengers on board. Once the aircraft reached its cruising altitude of FL330 after the departure, the flight crew observed a loss of hydraulic pressure in the number 2 system. The flight crew elected to return to CYVR and requested ARFF to be present for the landing. The aircraft landed approximately 1900 lbs overweight at CYVR without further incident.The operator’s maintenance found a flex line unserviceable. The number 2 EDP and flex line were both replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-IGKT a privately operated Quad City Challenger II advanced ultralight aircraft, was en route from North Bay, ON (CYYB) to Ottawa/Rockcliffe, ON (CYRO). At approximately 1800 feet ASL, 14.3 nm East of CYYB, the right wing separated from the aircraft. The aircraft crashed in the trees near a cottage on Talon Lake. A post crash fire occurred and was extinguished by the cottage’s residents. The pilot was fatally injured at impact.

C-GDMP, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Swoop, was conducting flight WSW123 from Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) to Abbotsford, BC (CYXX). As the flight crew was conducting an RNP approach to Runway 25 at CYXX, ATC provided VFR traffic information to WSW123 that C-GBPT, a Cessna 172N aircraft operated by Langley Flying School, was approaching the RNP track at 3600 ASL. While descending through 4500 ASL, the flight crew of WSW123 received a TCAS TA, followed by an RA shortly thereafter. In response to the command, WSW123 climbed to avoid the conflict. Once clear of the conflict, WSW123 continued the approach visually and landed without further incident. The two aircraft conflicted approximately 2.5 nm North of the CYXX control zone boundary.

C-FJFM, a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8271 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Nanaimo, BC (CYCD) with 3 crew members and 46 passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff, the nose landing gear did not retract, and the HYD ISO caution light illuminated. The flight crew declared an emergency and elected to return to CYVR where the aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by.  The operator’s maintenance found a cracked nose landing gear strut actuator line. The line was replaced, and the aircraft was then returned to service.

C-FPPN, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 aircraft operated by Dam Helicopters, was conducting fire suppression activities approximately 17 nm Southeast of Trail, BC (CAD4). During the landing phase, while dropping off an initial crew, the pilot heard a loud buzzing noise and felt a vibration in the tail rotor system. The pilot landed and shut down the aircraft. A visual inspection of the tail rotor system did not find any abnormalities. After consultation with maintenance personnel, the pilot completed a ground run, flight test and then flew the aircraft back to Castlegar, BC (CYCG). Further inspection of the tail rotor revealed that contact with an unknown object had occurred. The tail rotor blade assembly was replaced in accordance with the manufacturer.

C-GHPE, a Boeing 767-33A operated by Air Canada Rouge, was on approach into Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Int'l, ON (CYYZ) when the flight crew declared an emergency due to a vibration from the nose gear area. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GEUA, a Piper PA-31 aircraft registered to Tintina Air, was conducting a flight from Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen Intl, YT (CYXY) for Ross River, YT (CYDM). Shortly after leveling off at cruise altitude, the upper cowling for the number 1 engine detached. The pilot reduced the airspeed, declared an emergency and returned for a landing at CYXY. There was no other damage to the aircraft, and no handling issues.

ExpressJet flight ASQ4318, an Embraer 145XR aircraft, was conducting a flight from Chicago/O’Hare Intl, IL (KORD) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During the approach into CYYZ, the flight crew reported an issue with the landing gear and, as a precaution, declared an emergency. The aircraft subsequently landed without further incident on Runway 05 with ARFF standing by.

C-FCIJ, an Aerospatiale ATR 42-300 aircraft operated by Calm Air, was conducting IFR flight CAV569 from Churchill, MB (CYYQ) to Thompson, MB (CYTH). During the descent into CYTH, the flight crew cancelled IFR and positioned the aircraft to join the left downwind for Runway 06. C-FUZY, a Swearingen SA226-TC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting VFR flight PAG781 from CYTH to South Indian Lake (CZSN), MB. When CAV569 was approximately 15 nm North of CYTH, PAG781 was departing off Runway 06 under VFR. The flight crew of PAG781 advised CAV569 that they would be turning to the North West and climbing to 5500 feet ASL. CAV569 levelled at 5200 feet, and the CYTH FSS specialist  requested that PAG781 level at 4500 feet. The flight crew of CAV569 subsequently climbed to 6000 feet in response to a TCAS RA to climb. The TCAS showed approximately 500 feet of vertical spacing as the two flights passed within ½ mile horizontally.

N824CC, a privately operated Learjet 55 aircraft, was departing from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) for a flight to Buffalo/Niagara Intl, NY (KBUF). Upon issuing the departure clearance, ATC authorized the flight crew for takeoff on Runway 05, from the intersection of Runway 15R. The flight crew took off from Runway 15R instead. ATC observed the aircraft departing from Runway 15R and instructed the flight crew to remain on runway heading after departure.

C-GVMX, an Agusta AW119 MK II helicopter operated by Geotech Aviation, was operating at a height of approximately 400 feet AGL near Uxbridge, ON, and was carrying a geophysical antenna system as a slung load. During the flight, a failure in the antenna rigging system occurred and, as a result, the antenna fell to the ground and landed on a house. There was minor damage to the house and no injuries.

C-FWAD, a Boeing 767-300ER aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA22 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to London/Gatwick, UK (EGKK). During cruise flight at FL320, approximately 37 nm East Southeast of Valemount, BC (CAH4), one of the cabin crew experienced a medical incident. Duties were distributed to the remaining flight attendants. The aircraft continued to EGKK and landed without further incident.

C-IMSL, a Moraine Saulnier Type L Ultra-light aircraft, was departing from Guelph, ON (CNC4) for a local flight. During the takeoff, control was lost and the aircraft crashed on the front lawn of a residence. The pilot was not injured, however the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

C-GAQL, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA585 from Newark/Liberty Intl, NJ (KEWR) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with 5 crew members and 107 passengers on board. During the taxi segment for a departure off Runway 22R at KEWR, the flight crew was authorized via Taxiways Alpha, Sierra, and to hold short of Yankee for an intersection departure at Whiskey. While approaching Taxiway Kilo on Sierra, the flight crew noticed a Boeing 757 aircraft operated by United Airlines coming from their left, and had to apply brakes to give way as the B757 was not stopping. The closest distance between the two aircraft was estimated to be approximately 80 feet. ATC was queried about the incident, and responded by asking the flight crew to contact Clearance for a change of routing. The flight carried on to destination without further incident.

C-GOSA, an Aerospatiale ATR 72-202 aircraft operated by Summit Air, was conducting a flight from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Resolute Bay, NU (CYRB) with 5 crew members on board. As the aircraft was climbing through 8000 feet ASL after the departure from CYZF, the number 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW124B) rolled back to 30% torque, and continued to decrease. The flight crew executed the checklist, performed an inflight shutdown, informed ATC and requested to return to CYZF with ARFF in attendance. The aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance found that an O-ring at the inlet to the fuel flow divider was leaking. The part was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FMLV, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1958 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Porto/Francisco Sá Carneiro, Portugal (LPPR). Shortly after reaching its cruising altitude of FL350, the flight crew received a L HYD QTY EICAS message. QRH procedures were executed and a hydraulic leak was identified. The flight crew elected to divert back to CYYZ and declared a PAN PAN as a precaution. The aircraft performed an uneventful overweight landing with ARFF standing by, and came to a stop on the runway. The aircraft was checked by ARFF before it taxied to the gate. The operator’s maintenance identified the leak coming from the left hydraulic system pressure switch coupling. Hydraulic seals were replaced, and after subsequent operational tests, the aircraft was returned to service.

OY-PAA, an Airbus 321-251N NEO aircraft operated by Primera Air, was conducting flight PRI45 from London/Stanstead, UK (EGSS) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During the descent into CYYZ, ATC informed the flight crew that they needed to hold at their present position due to thunderstorms in the area. Subsequently, the flight was vectored away from the arrival route and the landing runway, which prompted the flight crew to request priority due to fuel; however, the flight crew stated that they were not declaring an emergency. ATC provided priority handling for Runway 23, and the aircraft landed without incident at 0110Z, with 39 kgs above the requirement for minimum diversion fuel.

C-GBIP, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA243 from Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 5 crew members and 112 passengers on board. Shortly after turning final for Runway 26R at CYVR, 7.5 nm behind a Boeing 747 at 3500 ft AGL, the aircraft encountered momentary wake turbulence, which caused the aircraft to roll. The flight crew reported severe turbulence to ATC, and landed without further incident. No injuries or damage was reported.

C-GHLU, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1917 from Lisbon/Aeroporto da Portela de Sacavem, Portugal (LPPT) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 8 crew members and 261 passengers on board. During cruise flight, one of the cabin crew members became incapacitated and was unable to perform for the remainder of the flight.

C-FMZR, an Embraer ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA687 from St. John’s Intl, NL (CYYT) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). After reaching cruise altitude, the number 2 engine oil pressure indication began decreasing. The flight crew followed the QRH and shut the engine (General Electric CF34-10E5A1) down. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and requested a diversion to Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) where the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance is investigating.

C-GKLB, an Aerospatiale ATR 42-300 aircraft operated by First Air, was conducting flight FAB803 from Igloolik, NU (CYGT) to Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) with 3 crew members and 3 passengers on board. After retracting the landing gear during the initial climb, the flight crew began to smell smoke. Shortly thereafter while passing through 600 feet, smoke emitted from the captain's left panel. The flight crew elected to return to CYGT. During the downwind segment, the smoke subsided, however the smell remained. The aircraft landed without further incident and taxied to the ramp. An inspection by the operator's maintenance found that wiring associated with the #2 FMS CDU had chaffed. The #2 FMS circuit breaker was pulled and collared, then deferred in accordance with the MEL. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJZK, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1895 from Las Vegas/McCarran Intl, NV (KLAS) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 8 crew members and 202 passengers on board. During cruise flight approximately 140 nm South Southeast of Lovelock/Derby Field, NV (KLOL), a cabin crew member was seriously injured by an unattended cart, and became incapacited for the remainder of the flight.

C-FJOK, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1681 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Victoria Intl, BC (CYYJ) with 6 crew members and 191 passengers onboard. During cruise flight, one of the flight attendant became incapacitated and was unable to perform their duties for the remainder of the flight.

C-GENM, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3298 from Prince George, BC (CYXS) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). Shortly after departing CYXS, the fight crew reported a landing gear issue and elected to return to CYXS. ARFF was requested for the landing, which was made without further incident.After the takeoff, the left amber main gear door advisory light had illuminated. The operator’s maintenance determined that the LH MLG up-lock inboard spring was broken. The part was replaced and landing gear swings were carried out.

C-GWBL, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet Airlines, was conducting flight WJA182 from Kelowna, BC (CYLW) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with 6 crew members and 101 passengers on board. During the approach into CYYC, a cabin crew member experienced a medical incident and was unable to perform their duties. The captain was advised of the situation, and the duties were distributed to the remaining flight attendants for the landing.

C-FTSK, a Fairchild SA227-AC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation, was conducting flight PAG982 from Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) to Island Lake, MB (CYIV) with 2 crew members on board. While in cruise, the flight crew received a Fuel Filter Bypass indication on the left engine (Garrett TPE 331-11U-612G). Engine instruments indicated an engine roll back to minimum flow, however there were no associated sound or flight characteristic changes. The condition appeared to rectify itself and the flight crew elected to return to CYWG. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft landed without further incident with both engines operating. The operator's maintenance inspection of the engine indication system revealed a faulty number 1 Garmin Engine/Airframe (GEA71) unit and exhaust gas temperature (EGT) thermocouple. Both units were replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

OE-FIS, un appareil de type Piper PA-31T1 exploité par Redair Luftfahrt, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) à destination de Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City, ON (CYTZ). Lors de la montée après le départ de CYHU, l’équipage de conduite a déclaré un état d’urgence et a avisé qu’une diversion était nécessaire en raison d’un problème de carburant. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre à Montréal Intl (Mirabel), QC (CYMX). Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

N6ZR, a privately operated Piper PA60 Aerostar aircraft, was en route from Klawock, AK (PAKW) to Bellingham Intl, WA (KBLI). During cruise flight, the pilot declared an emergency at 1415Z due to an engine (Lycoming IO-540) power loss. The pilot elected to divert to Port Hardy, BC (CYZT) where the airplane landed without further event at 1440Z with ARFF on standby.

C-FGXR, un appareil de type Beech B200 exploité par Air Nunavut, effectuait le vol BFF203 selon les règles de vols aux instruments depuis Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) à destination de Sanikiluaq, NU (CYSK) avec 2 pilotes et 3 passagers à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en vol de croisière à environ 300 miles marins au sud-ouest de CYFB, une panne du moteur gauche est survenue. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a effectué un retour à CYFB. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre et il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FNND, a Boeing 777-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA033 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). While in cruise flight, the flight crew declared a MAYDAY and diverted the aircraft to Winnipeg/James Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) due to a medical emergency with a passenger. The aircraft landed without incident and was met by paramedics.

C-FGHM, a Cessna P206B aircraft operated by Southwestern Ontario Organization of Parachutists, was returning to land at Dundas Air Plaza, ON, after dropping parachutists. During the descent, the engine (Teledyne Continental IO-520-FCA) lost power and started to smoke. The pilot conducted a forced landing into a cornfield, near the Dundas Air Plaza. There was no damage to the aircraft during the landing, and the pilot was uninjured.Initial investigation by the pilot found the oil filter adapter had failed.

C-FWRR, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (CRJ100) operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7367 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Detroit/Metropolitan Wayne County, MI (KDTW). While taxiing for the departure in CYYZ, an electrical odour was noticed in the passenger cabin. The flight crew elected to return to the gate and requested emergency vehicles to attend. Passengers deplaned normally at the gate. The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and found a faulty ballast box at the entrance boarding lights.

C-FWBH, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Blackcomb Helicopters, was conducting external load operations approximately 4 nm South of Whistler (Municipal), BC (CBE9) with only the pilot on board. As a descent was initiated following the completion of the delivery of a full load of concrete, the pilot inadvertently touched the grapple Open/Close switch located on the head of the collective. A slight bump in the airframe was felt coming from the main cargo hook in the belly of the aircraft. The pilot observed that the empty bucket had released from the remote longline hook, and started to roll down slope on the hillside. The pilot alerted all workers about the situation. The bucket remained clear of the workers, and stopped downhill shortly thereafter. There were no injuries, and the bucket sustained minor damage. The aircraft returned to fuel staging.

C-GWSH, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA156 from Regina Intl, SK (CYQR) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 5 crew members and 122 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the flight crew noticed a fuel imbalance between the left and the right wings. After consultation with the QRH, the flight crew elected to shut the right engine (CFM56-7B24) down and declared a MAYDAY, as they suspected a fuel leak. A diversion to Winnipeg/James A. Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) was initiated, where the aircraft landed without further incident. The aircraft came to a stop on the runway, and the left engine was also shut down. Maintenance personnel then towed the aircraft to the parking area where passengers deplaned using the stairs.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and did not identify any fuel leaks or issues with the fuel system that would explain the imbalance. The aircraft was checked serviceable and was returned to service.

C-GJDA, an Airbus 330-243 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC429 from Paris/Charles de Gaulle, France (LFPG) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 11 crew members and 317 passengers on board. During the takeoff at LFPG, a bird was ingested in the right engine. No abnormal engine indications were observed in the cockpit however, the engine vibration increased and noise was heard from the engine. The flight crew returned to LFPG and conducted an overweight landing with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance is evaluating the damages and, at this time, one fan blade from the engine was found damaged.

C-GHKR, an Airbus 330-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA893 from Rome/Leonardo da Vinci Intl, Italy (LIRF) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) with 11 crew members and 291 passengers on board. Shortly after reaching their assigned cruising altitude of FL360, approximately 50 nm South of Milan/Malpensa, Italy (LIMC), the flight encountered severe turbulence. The aircraft lost approximately 2000’, before the flight crew climbed back to FL360. The flight then continued to destination without further incident. There were no injuries. The operator’s maintenance monitored data from the Quick Access Recorder (QAR) and found the parameters to be within AMM limitations. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FGDZ, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA793 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Los Angeles Intl, CA (KLAX) with 10 crew members and 293 passengers on board. While passing through 700 feet ASL on the approach to Runway 25L at KLAX, the flight crew received a TCAS TA, which quickly changed to a TCAS RA to CLIMB. The flight crew complied with the RA and executed a missed approach. ATC was notified of the situation, and vectored ACA793 for another approach to Runway 25L where they landed without further incident.

C-IKGC, a privately operated Spectrum Beaver basic ultra-light aircraft, had just departed for a sight-seeing flight from Indus/Winters Aire Park, AB (CFY4) with one person on board. As the aircraft was in the climb passing approximately 800 feet above the ground, the engine stopped. The pilot checked the fuel valves and tried to restart the engine, however with no success. Seeing a canola field below the aircraft, the pilot elected to activate a spring-loaded parachute device to slow down the descent. Unable to release the parachute with the left hand, the pilot slipped the right shoulder out of the harness, released the grip on the control stick, and tried to pull the parachute release with both hands. During this action, the aircraft experienced an aerodynamic stall of the wings. The pilot was unable to recover from the stall before the impact with the ground. The aircraft was substantially damaged, and the pilot sustained serious injuries. A witness called 911 and both fire services and ambulance attended. There was no fire, and the emergency locater transmitter (ELT) did not activate.

C-GARO, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1692 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) with a crew of 3 and 129 passengers on board. While in cruise flight, the flight crew encountered a pressurization problem and attempts to rectify the issue were unsuccessful. The flight crew declared an emergency and conducted an emergency descent to 10 000 feet. The aircraft was then diverted to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl, SK (CYXE) where the aircraft landed without further incident. The oxygen masks did not deploy.The operator's maintenance replaced the number 2 engine bleed air pressurization regulator valve and released the aircraft back to service.

C-FNAK, a Bell 407 aircraft operated by Sahtu Helicopters, was conducting a VFR flight from Norman Wells, NT (CYVQ) to the 108 mile marker of the Canol Trail with 1 crew member and 6 passengers on board. The flight was operated in support of the Canol Trail remediation project, and while approaching the destination, a bear was noted on the landscape by a passenger. The pilot initiated a right turn to facilitate a closer look and observed that the bear was not proceeding in the same direction as the intended landing zone. The helicopter then entered a descending right turn, from which the pilot was unable to arrest the rate of descent; the helicopter collided with terrain. Upon impact, the main rotor struck the tail boom and severed it from the fuselage. Additionally, the main rotor blades struck a rock outcropping to the left of the helicopter. The aircraft remained upright and was secured by the pilot. The passengers and crew exited the aircraft, which was substantially damaged.

C-GNYZ, a Sikorsky S-92A aircraft operated by Canadian Helicopters Offshore, was departing from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) for search-and-rescue training. During the take-off, the flight crew noticed a power loss on the number 2 engine. The flight crew executed a rejected take-off and performed an emergency shutdown of the engine. The aircraft was taxied back to the hangar without further incident. The operator’s maintenance found the number 1 variable inlet guide vanes (VIGV) link broken and is working with the manufacturer to complete the repair.

A6-EQC, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Emirates, was conducting flight UAE235 from Dubai Intl, United Arab Emirates (OMDB) to Chicago/O'Hare Intl, IL (KORD) with 18 crew members and 355 passengers on board. Approximately 65 nautical miles South East of Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) while cruising at FL360, the flight crew received the ENG FUEL VALVE R message on the EICAS, followed by ENG FAIL R message. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to the number 2 engine (GE 90-115B) power loss, and requested a diversion to Goose Bay, NL (CYYR) at FL250. An attempt to restart the engine was carried out, however unsuccessfully. The right engine was secured and the aircraft continued to CYYR where an uneventful landing was carried out at 1835Z. No one was injured. Maintenance personnel replaced the right fuel spar valve, and the aircraft was returned in service.

C-FZCS, a Lockheed 188A  aircraft operated by Air Spray (1967), was operating as Tanker 487 on fire LWF179, 25 nm West of Fort McMurray, AB (CYMM). During the flight, the number 4 engine propeller experienced an over speed. The flight crew executed the checklist and, once the propeller was regulating, the decision was taken to fly to the abort area to dump the remaining retardant in the tanks. Once this was completed, the flight crew shut the number 4 engine down. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft returned to CYMM where it landed without further incident with ARFF attending.The operator’s maintenance found the propeller governor O-ring damaged. The mounting pad O-ring was replaced, and the engine was successfully run. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FJJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8668 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to San Diego Intl, CA (KSAN) with 4 crew members and 63 passengers on board. Just prior to top of climb after the departure from CYVR, the flight crew received an Inboard Brake Pressure caution indication. The flight crew elected to return to CYVR and, due to increased landing distance requirements and potential for high brake temperatures, an emergency was declared. The aircraft landed on Runway 26L without further incident and stopped on the runway for inspection. Once ARFF confirmed that there were no signs of brake overheat, the aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.

C-FTOH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines on behalf of TUI fly Netherlands, was conducting flight TFL712 from Bodrum/Milas, Turkey (LTFE) to Amsterdam/Schiphol, Netherlands (EHAM). As the flight was authorized to descent to FL340, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to LEVEL OFF. The aircraft was leveled off as directed, followed by instructions from ATC to level off. ATC then advised TFL712 that they were clear of the conflict, and cleared the flight to further descent before being handed to the next sector. Due to congestion on the frequency, ATC was not notified of the RA.

C-GVJA, un appareil de type Cyclone 180 amphibie de construction amateur, s'est renversé sur le lac Lenôtre (QC) lors de l'amerrissage et a coulé. Le pilote, seule personne à bord, a pu évacuer l'appareil pour se rendre au rivage. À l'aide d'un téléphone satellite, le pilote a communiqué avec le Centre de recherche et sauvetage des Forces armées canadiennes pour demander du secours. Le pilote portait une veste de flottaison, et n'a subi aucune blessure. L'appareil a subi des dommages importants aux 2 ailes.

C-FXUS, a Fairchild SA227-CC aircraft operated by Bearskin Airlines, was conducting flight BLS384 from Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT) to Sault Ste. Marie, ON (CYAM). During cruise flight, the flight crew conducted an emergency descent due to a rapid increase in cabin altitude. The flight returned to CYQT and the subsequent landing was uneventful.The operator's maintenance personnel replaced the main cabin door seal.

C-FASN, a Beech B100 aircraft operated by Island Express Air, was conducting local training flight IAX100T from Abbotsford, BC (CYXX) with two pilots and two flight examiners on board. At approximately 1000 feet AGL on the initial climb after the departure, the flight crew received a Master Caution light, a BLEED AIR FAIL warning and the copilot smelled smoke. The flight crew declared an emergency, followed the checklist for BLEED AIR LIGHT, and returned to CYXX.The operator’s maintenance replaced a melted plastic bleed air line under the floor of the cockpit.

C-FIGX, a privately operated float-equipped Noorduyn Norseman MK. VI aircraft, was conducting a flight from Stein Lake, SK to Emma Lake, SK. While cruising at 3 500 feet ASL, the engine (Pratt & Whitney - USA, R-1340-AN-1) developed a vibration, and the oil pressure indication decreased from 90 psi to 60 psi. The pilot elected to divert and commenced a descent toward Montreal Lake, SK. The pilot selected the mixture to rich and carburetor heat on. The fuel selector was moved from the belly tank to the wing tanks and the magneto switch was checked. The pilot asked the passengers to secure the cabin, and the subsequent precautionary landing on Montreal Lake was uneventful. The pilot initiated a rescue using a cell phone and 121.5 radio transmissions. The occupants were transported to shore with a boat provided by RCMP. The aircraft was then towed to shore at Weyakwin Landing. Inspection of the engine revealed that the No. 4 cylinder had failed. The engine will be removed for inspection and repair.

C-GRSP, a Piper PA-25-235 aircraft operated by Miccar Aerial, was engaged in agricultural aerial application, 18 nm North East of Preeceville, SK (CJK9). During a spray pass, the aircraft contacted and severed a newly erected power line that serviced a nearby property. The pilot was able to maintain control and flew the aircraft to Yorkton Muni, SK (CYQV) for inspection. There were no injuries, however the aircraft sustained damage to the propeller and the leading edge of the left wing. The operator informed SaskPower of the incident.

C-FQWA, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG957 from Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT) to Sioux Lookout, ON (CYXL). As the aircraft was turning onto final approach for Runway 34 at CYXL, the landing gear failed to extend when selected down. The flight crew flew the aircraft to the west of the airport to complete the checklist. An emergency gear extension was performed, and the flight crew received down-and-locked indications for all 3 landing gears. The flight crew declared an emergency and activated the ISAT emergency feature. The flight orbited CYXL until emergency vehicles were in position. The subsequent landing was conducted without further incident. In accordance with the checklist, the aircraft was brought to a stop at the end of Runway 34, and was shut down. After verification that the landing gear was secure, the aircraft was towed to the apron.The operator's maintenance personnel discovered, and secured, a loose cannon plug on the landing-gear selector assembly. Gear swings were completed, and a verification flight was conducted satisfactorily. The aircraft was the subject of a similar event earlier that same day (A18C0067).

C-FIQR, un appareil de type ATR 42-300 exploité par First Air, effectuait le vol FAB802 selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ d'Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) à destination de Igloolik, NU (CYGT) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 7 passagers à bord. Alors que l'appareil était en vol de croisière au FL200, l'agent de bord a signalé à l'équipage de conduite une odeur anormale dans la cabine. L'équipage de conduite a signalé la présence de fumé au service la circulation aérienne et a demandé un retour vers CYFB, où l'appareil s'est posé sans problème. Aucune urgence n'a été déclarée, et personne n'a été blessé. Suite à une vérification effectuée par le personnel de l’entretien de l’exploitant, aucune anomalie n'a été trouvée. Lors de l'embarquement subséquent des passagers, il a été noté que l'odeur provenait des bottes d'un des passagers, lesquelles avaient trempé auparavant dans un solvant. L'appareil a été remis en service.

C-FHEZ, a privately operated amateur-built Mosquito XE helicopter, was on a flight from its home base 4 nm North of Indus/Winters Aire Park, AB (CFY4) to a location approximately 7 nm Southeast of CFY4 with only the pilot on board. During cruise flight, the pilot chose to follow the Highwood River westbound, just East of the Davisbruk bridge on highway 552 where it crosses the Highwood River. Approximately 1800 feet East of the bridge, the helicopter struck an unmarked power line that was strung across the river at approximately 75 feet above ground level. The helicopter departed controlled flight and impacted the ground on the river bank. The aircraft was destroyed, and the pilot was fatally injured. There was no post impact fire.

C-GDUK, a Bell 204B aircraft operated by Delta Helicopters, was conducting helislinging operations in support of tree planting operations, approximately 20 nm South West of La Crete, AB (CFN5). During cruise flight with a load of 63 boxes of trees in two nets, a lanyard broke and the load fell to the ground. There were no damages or injuries to people or property.

C-FLTS, un appareil de type Beech A100 King Air exploité par Exact Air, effectuait le vol ET823 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Amos/Magny, QC (CYEY) à destination de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) avec 2 pilotes à bord. Alors que l'appareil passait 9000 pieds ASL lors de la montée après le départ de CYEY, le voyant d'alarme indiquant un feu sur le moteur gauche s'est allumé. L'équipage de conduite a effectué la liste de vérification applicable et a fermé le moteur (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-28). Un PAN PAN a été signalé au service de la circulation aérienne et l'équipage a demandé un déroutement vers Val-d'Or, QC (CYVO) où l'appareil s'est posé sans problème avec la présence de l'unité de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). Le personnel de l’entretien de l’exploitant a effectué des vérifications au sol et en vol et aucune anomalie n'a été observée. L'appareil a été remis en service.

C-FQWA, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting local flight WSG1407 from Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT). While selecting landing gear down on final approach, the landing gear failed to extend. The flight crew declared an emergency, executed checklist items, and performed an emergency extension of the landing gear. ATC and the operator's maintenance personnel confirmed that the landing gear was down, and that the taxi light was on. The subsequent landing was uneventful.The operator's maintenance personnel replaced a solenoid switch assembly and carried out successful gear swings. The aircraft experienced a similar event later the same day (A18C0068).

C-GIQG, a Swearingen SA226-TC aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation LP., was conducting medevac flight PAG02 from Winnipeg James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) to Thompson, MB (CYTH). While descending for a landing at CYTH, the right-hand wing-overheat warning light illuminated. The crew performed the checklist items in the AFM and notified CYTH FSS of the issue. Subsequently, the crew performed a precautionary shutdown of the No. 2 engine (Garrett TPE331-10UA) and advised CYTH FSS of the emergency. The subsequent landing was conducted with the No. 2 engine inoperative. The aircraft was brought to a stop at the end of Runway 33 and an emergency evacuation was initiated. The crew requested an ambulance and ARFF. The aircraft was towed to the apron.The operator's maintenance personnel repaired a wire at the right-hand 450 degree thermal switch.

C-FEUR, an Aerospatiale ATR 72-202 aircraft operated by Summit Air, was conducting flight SU7313 from Arviat, NU (CYEK) to Thompson, MB (CYTH). During the descent through 8500’ ASL, the aircraft experienced an abrupt yaw. The flight crew then received a number 2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada - PW124B) oil pressure master warning, accompanied by a loss of High Pressure Gas Generator RPM (NH), and decreasing Inter-Turbine Temperature (ITT). The flight crew declared Pan Pan, and circled North East of CYTH to troubleshoot the problem and perform the checklist. The flight crew requested ARFF, and the subsequent landing was conducted with the number 2 engine inoperative. The operator's maintenance discovered metal contamination on a chip detector. The engine has been removed for examination and repair at an overhaul facility.

C-GDLP, a privately registered Bellanca 8KCAB, was conducting a flight from Buttonville Municipal (CYKZ), ON. Shortly after take-off from Runway 15 at CYKZ, the pilot declared a Mayday with ATC, and the aircraft entered a right hand turn.  The turn then steepened and the aircraft entered a nose down attitude before colliding with the ground in a field approximately 500 ft west of the departure end of Runway 15.  The aircraft was destroyed by a post impact fire and the single occupant was fatally injured.

N900YY, un appareil de type Falcon 900 exploité par Big Skyy Aviation, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments en provenance de Split/Kastel, Croatie (LDSP) à destination d'Iqaluit, NU (CYFB). Alors que l'appareil se trouvait à environ 145 nm à l'est de CYFB, l'équipage de conduite a demandé la priorité auprès du service de la circulation aérienne dû à une condition de carburant minimum. L'appareil a poursuivi sa route vers CYFB où il s'est posé sans problème.

C-FGJI, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA560 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to San Francisco Intl, CA (KSFO) with 5 crew members and 146 passengers on board. During the approach at KFSO, ATC cleared ACA560 for a visual approach for Runway 28L. ATC also advised the flight crew to monitor the separation with another aircraft located on their right side. While descending, the flight crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory (RA) message and immediately initiated a go around. The aircraft conducted a second approach and landed without further incident.

C-FYJD, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG707 from Aruba/Reina Beatrix Intl, Aruba (TNCA) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ).
