During the boarding at TNCA, the aft cabin crew noticed an electrical burning smell, which activated the smoke detector coming from the aft lavatory on the R/H side of the aircraft. A light gray layer of smoke was observed. The passengers were deplaned and emergency services were notified by the ground handling company. Maintenance personnel found that the source was a burned out ballast located in the mirror door inside the lavatory. The aircraft was released under MEL 38-02-A and, as per the aircraft maintenance manual (AMM), the lavatory was made inoperative and the mirror lights deactivated.

C-GMXO, a Cessna A188B Ag Truck aircraft operated by Clayton Air Service, had just completed a series of flights which involved applying fungicide to a flax field, East of Carrot River, SK, and was en route to the operator's mobile operations base at Arborfield, SK. The aircraft was reported overdue by ground personnel, and was later discovered in a wooded area, 8 nm East of Carrot River, SK. The aircraft had collided with terrain and trees, and was destroyed by a post-crash fire and impact forces. The pilot, the sole occupant, suffered fatal injuries. TSB investigators were deployed.

C-FNAJ, an Embraer ERJ190 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA651 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) to St John's Intl, NL (CYYT) with 97 passengers and 4 crew members on board. After the landing on Runway 29, the number 1 engine flamed out as the aircraft was back tracking on the runway. ARFF was called by ATC, however the flight crew did not require assistance. The flight crew continued taxing to the gate on engine number 2. The operator’s maintenance could not determine any faults and the engine, when run, operated normally. In the absence of any faults, the aircraft was released back to service.

C-FWEW, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 operated by WestJet Encore as flight WEN3214, was conducting an IFR flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl., MB (CYWG), Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT). In the vicinity of the QT NDB, while the aircraft was on final approach to Runway 07 at CYQT, a passenger observed a UAV approximately 100 feet from the aircraft. No information was available as to the precise location and altitude of the occurrence.

C-GBZR, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1677 from Orlando Intl, FL (KMCO) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During cruise flight, the flight crew received an EICAS message that indicated low hydraulic quantity in the centre system. The flight crew observed the associated quantity gauge at 45% and decreasing slowly. Applicable QRH items were executed and a PAN PAN was declared with Cleveland ATC. The aircraft landed and came to a full stop at CYYZ's RWY 33R where an external visual inspection was carried out by ARFF with no faults found. The aircraft taxied under its own power to the gate.

C-FNAJ, an Embraer ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1119 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Regina Intl, SK (CYQR) with 4 crew members and 90 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL380, the flight crew encountered severe turbulence. The aircraft continued to destination and landed at CYQR without further incident. A severe turbulence airframe check was carried out by the operator’s maintenance and no damage was found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FCOO, a de Havilland DHC-2 MK. I Beaver aircraft, was conducting float training operations at Goose (Otter Creek) water aerodrome, NL (CCB5) with 2 pilots on board. During the landing, the front of the float dug in and the aircraft rolled over, coming to rest inverted in the water. The aircraft was equipped with an Alaska door modification that did not have an interior door release latch. One of the pilots found themselves in the rear of the cabin and experienced difficulty to exit, requiring the assistance from the other pilot who had exited the front of the aircraft and opened the Alaska door. The two occupants were rescued by a nearby boat, with one pilot receiving serious injuries and the other minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GDJH, a Learjet 35A aircraft operated by Keewatin Air, was conducting a medevac flight from Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW). During the descent into CYOW, the flight crew received a LOW HYD indication. The flight crew declared an emergency and executed QRH procedures. The landing gear was lowered by using the alternate extension system and the flaps were lowered by operating the auxiliary hydraulic pump. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance performed an operational check of the landing gear and found a leak on the L/H main landing gear actuator up pressure line. The line was tightened and subsequent landing gear operations revealed no further faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FENO, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3278 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl, SK (CYXE). During cruise flight at FL250 while navigating around thunderstorm cells, the flight crew observed a TCAS target shown as 1000 feet below them, and on a course set to cross their current flight path. C-FKXC, a corporate Beech B200GT aircraft operated by Regional Aviation Campbell River, was conducting a flight from Medicine Hat, AB (CYXH) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG). The flight crew of C-FKXC requested the authorization to climb from ATC, due to weather. The request was denied as it conflicted with WEN3278. The flight crew of WEN3278 observed C-FKXC begin to climb, and received a TCAS traffic advisory (TA). Shortly thereafter, the TA became a resolution advisory to initiate a climb. The captain disengaged the autopilot and executed a climb until the TCAS advised to level off at FL255. When the TCAS indicated clear of conflict, and after observing C-FKXC pass on the display, the flight crew of WEN3278 descended back to FL250. The flight crew notified ATC of the deviation and subsequent return to their assigned altitude. At no time was WEN3278 in visual contact with C-FKXC.

C-FHOS, an Embraer 190 was being operated by Air Canada as flight ACA507 from Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ), ON to Chicago O'Hare Intl (KORD), IL. C-FHOS was descending to FL200, when a King Air that had departed KORD was climbing fast. C-FHOS received a TCAS RA "level off" that was followed by crew. The flight landed uneventfully.

C-FHNP, an Embraer 190 operated by Air Canada as flight ACA509 from Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Chicago O'Hare Intl, IL (KORD). On approach, approximately 15 nm from Runway 09, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to climb.  The crew initiated a climb, and the aircraft continued to land uneventfully.

C-GBHO, an Airbus 319-114 was operating as Air Canada rouge flight ROU1857 from Los Angeles Intl (KLAX) to McCarran Intl, Las Vegas (KLAS). After takeoff, upon the GEAR UP selection, the flight crew received indications of the green hydraulic system failure, and the gear did not retract as commanded. The flight crew executed the applicable QRH drills, confirmed the gear was down and locked, and declared a PAN PAN before returning to KLAX where a full stop landing was completed with ARFF on standby. ARFF conducted external visual inspection and noted no apparent fluid leaks, however the gear doors were open. The aircraft taxiied under its own power to the gate uneventfully.

N55CD, un appareil de type Beech P35 en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments à partir de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à destination d’Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW). Peu de temps après le décollage de la piste 29 à CYQB, l’appareil a été observé effectuant un virage par la gauche sur un cap de 253°, alors que la procédure de départ normalisé (SID) préconise une montée dans l'axe de piste. L'espacement avec ROU1793, un appareil de type Airbus 321-200 immatriculé C-FJQD qui décollait de la piste 24 à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ), a été réduit à 1.4 nm.

C-FUJZ, the Jazz Aviation Bombardier CRJ-705 (CL-600-2D15), was operating as flight JZA8103 from Houston, TX (KIAH) to Calgary, AB (CYYC). JZA8103 was declared number 1 and on the downwind for Runway 17L. The WestJet Boeing 737-600, C-GWSJ, was operating as WJA607 from Saskatoon, SK (CYXE) to Calgary, AB (CYYC). WJA607 was inbound from the northeast and was assigned Runway 17L. When JZA8103 was turning base, separation with WJA607 eroded to 1.3 nm horizontally and 300 feet vertically where 3 nm or 1000 feet are required.

N525QS, un appareil de type Cessna Citation 680A Sovereign exploité par Netjets Aviation, effectuait le vol EJA525 selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à destination de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC). L'équipage prévoyaient un atterrissage sur la piste 28, dont toute la portion sud sur sa pleine longueur était fermée en raison de travaux de réfection. Des feux de bord de piste temporaires ont été placés au centre habituel de la piste, et un avis aux aviateurs (NOTAM) avait été publié à cet effet. L’appareil a subi une crevaison à l'atterrissage lorsqu'il est entré en collision avec les feux de bord de piste temporaires. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. L’appareil a également subi des dommages mineurs aux bords d'attaque des volets droit et gauche.

C-GBQC, a de Havilland DHC3T aircraft operated by Ookpik Aviation, began takeoff on the sandy shoreline of Parker Lake, NU with the pilot and one passenger onboard. During the takeoff roll, the aircraft ran out of shore line and went into the water. The right main gear was torn off and the aircraft came to a rest in an upright position. The pilot and passenger were not injured and the aircraft sustained substantial damage. It was reported that the sandy shoreline was very soft.

C-FPNX, the Skyservice Business Aviation Inc. Beech B200, was operating from Prince Rupert, BC (CYPR) to Calgary, AB (CYYC). While on a 2 nm final approach to Rwy 17R, the flight crew selected landing gear down and the R/H main landing gear down and locked light failed to illuminate. The flight crew initiated a go-around and actioned the emergency landing gear extension checklist. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed uneventfully. There were no injuries. Company maintenance found the R/H main landing gear down and locked indicator lamp burnt out.

C-GKDR, an Aerospatiale AS350-B2 helicopter operated by Access Helicopters, was applying fungicide to a wheat field with only the pilot on board. During an application pass, the helicopter struck a powerline and then collided with terrain. The pilot received a serious injury and the helicopter was substantially damaged. There was no post-impact fire. Local RCMP and EMS responded to the scene.

C-FSSD, a privately operated Beech B60 Duke aircraft, was conducting a local flight from Peterborough, ON (CYOQ) with only the pilot on board. Upon selection of the landing gear down during the approach at CYPQ, the landing gear failed to extend. Shortly after, the landing gear motor circuit breaker popped. After unsuccessful troubleshooting, the pilot proceeded to land with the landing gear in the retracted position. The aircraft touched down and skidded on the runway, sustaining substantial damage. However, the pilot was not injured. This was the second flight following an annual inspection. On the first flight, the landing gear would not retract due to a micro switch out of rigging.

C-FXTJ, a privately operated float-equipped Champion 7GCAA aircraft, departed from Deer Lake, West Nipissing, ON with two persons on board. The aircraft was observed to be flying around the lake perimeter at low altitude when it pitched nose up, and then the wing dropped. The aircraft entered a spin and impacted a wooded terrain in a steep, nose down attitude. A fire erupted after the impact and both occupants were fatally injured. The TSB deployed two investigators to the site the following morning.

C-GORN, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7277 from Harrisburg Intl, PA (KMDT) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During the flight, the flight crew noticed an acrid smell in the cockpit. As there was smoke associated with the smell, the flight crew donned their oxygen masks, advised the passengers of the situation and requested priority landing. Shortly after, the flight crew noticed that COMM1 was unserviceable. The aircraft landed uneventfully at CYYZ with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance confirmed the smell was from the COMM1 control head and proceeded to replace it. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-KFIW, a Boeing 737-7CT aircraft operated by WestJet as flight WJA475, departed Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) for Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG). After departing CYYZ, the flight crew received an inoperative anti-skid indication. The flight crew completed the checklist, consulted with company operations and elected to continue to CYWG. The flight crew declared a PAN-PAN with Winnipeg ATC. The aircraft landed safely with ARFF on standby. The operator's maintenance replaced the left hand alternate anti-skid valve.

C-GCNO, a Boeing 737-36N operated by Canadian North Inc, departed Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Rankin Inlet, NU (CYRT). While unloading freight at CYRT, the flight crew was notified of a dangerous goods (UN# 3363) spill in pit number 5.  A box was found to be soaked from within containing aviation turbine fuel. The operator's DG coordinator was notified and a clean up was conducted prior to releasing the aircraft.

N388AA, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by American Airlines was conducting flight AAL52 from Philadelphia airport, PA (KPHL) to Vaclav Havel airport, Prague, Czech Republic (LKPR). While in cruise flight passing 49N 032W the crew received a "Cabin Auto Inop " EICAS message. The crew switched to manual pressurization but the pressurization could not be controlled. The crew completed the checklist, which called for the dropping of the oxygen masks, and declared a PAN PAN, requesting a precautionary descent to 10,000 feet. The aircraft diverted to St John's, NL, (CYYT) where the flight landed without further incident at 0629Z. Maintenance has replaced the outflow valve actuator, the # 1 cabin pressure controller and selector. All pressurization tests passed and the aircraft is being ferried to the USA for further maintenance testing before returning to service.

C-FODL, un Dash-8-106 exploité par Air Creebec Inc. sous l’indicatif CRQ231, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de l’aéroport de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) à destination de Vald’Or, QC (CYVO). Quelques minutes après être établi en vol de croisière à 16 000 pieds d’altitude, l’équipage observe une fluctuation de la pression d’huile du moteur numéro 2. L’équipage a arrêté le moteur (PW121) par mesure de précaution, a continué sa route vers CYVO et a déclaré une urgence. Le C-FODL s’est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé. Suite à l’inspection de l’aéronef, une défaillance du joint d’étanchéité de la conduite d’huile en amont du refroidisseur d’huile a été découverte.

C-FTXK, un appareil de type CL-215 exploité par le Service Aérien Gouvernemental du Québec, avec à son bord 2 membres d'équipage de conduite effectuait un vol de combat de feu de forêt selon les règles de vol à vue. Lors d'un écopage sur le lac Skokiaan l'équipage a senti une perte puissance du moteur droit (Pratt & Whitney Wasp R2800-CA3) attribuable à une mise en drapeau non commandé. Lors de la décélération qui a suivi, l'aéronef s'est échoué sur un haut fond et y est resté immobilisé. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GUON, a de Havilland DHC-8-301 operated by Jazz Aviation LP as flight JZA7076, departed Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) for Regina Intl, SK (CYQR). While departing CYWG, at an altitude between 1000 feet AGL and 1500 AGL, the left hand engine ( Pratt and Whitney Canada PW 123) torque dropped to zero followed by a decrease of Inter-stage Turbine Temperature (ITT) to 400 degrees Celsius before the flight crew was able to shut down the engine. The crew declared an emergency and completed the emergency checklist. C-GUON landed uneventfully in CYWG with ARFF on standby. The aircraft was on a maintenance ferry flight and no passengers were on board.  The operator's maintenance replaced the fuel pump and fuel control unit.

D-AIGP, un Airbus 340-300 exploité par Lufthansa sous l'indicatif DHL479, se préparait pour effectuer un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Francfort-sur-le-Main, Allemagne (FRA). Le D-AIGP était stationné à la barrière 63 avec à son bord tous les membres d’équipage et les passagers lorsqu’un véhicule pour le réapprovisionnement alimentaire est entré en collision avec la partie inférieure de la queue de l’appareil. Les dommages ont été évalués comme étant mineur par les techniciens d’entretien d’aéronef de la compagnie. L’avion a été remis en service et a pu décoller vers sa destination. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FSKA, a Beech A100 King Air aircraft operated by Wings Over Kississing, was conducting flight WN03 from St. Theresa Point, MB (CYST) to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG). At approximately 100 nautical miles North East of CYWG, the flight crew noticed that the left engine’s (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-28) oil pressure was fluctuating. The flight crew reduced the power on the affected engine, noticed torque indications began to fluctuate, followed by oil pressure drop below 40 PSIG, in addition to a burning smell in the cockpit. The flight crew briefed the passengers and performed a precautionary engine shutdown. ATC was advised and ARFF responded. The aircraft landed without further incident at CYWG. Following the landing, the other engine was shutdown and the aircraft was towed to the apron. The operator's maintenance is currently troubleshooting the engine.

C-FLRV, un Mooney M20A en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l’aéroport de Bromont (Roland Désourdy), QC (CZBM) à destination de Montréal/St-Lazare, QC (CST3) avec 2 personnes à son bord. Alors que le C-FLRV était en courte finale pour la piste 20, l’avion est descendu rapidement sous la pente d’approche en raison d’un changement important de la vitesse du vent. Le C-FLRV a atterri brutalement, environ 200 pieds avant la piste 20. Le train d’atterrissage de droite s’est affaissé occasionnant des dommages importants à l’appareil. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GPAU, a Bombardier DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Provincial Airlines, was operating as flight PVL410 from St. John’s Intl, NL (CYYT) to Gander Intl, NL (CYQX). During cruise, the flight attendant became incapacitated and could not perform their duties. The crew decided to return to CYYT and requested that an ambulance be available upon landing. While waiting for the ambulance, ARFF assisted and tended to the flight attendant.

C-GSCA, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1918 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Venice/Marco Polo, Italy (LIPZ). During cruise flight in the vicinity of 52N030W, the flight crew received an EICAS message indicating low hydraulic quantity in the centre system. The flight crew observed 46% quantity remaining, which dropped to 20% over the next hour. The system was deactivated in order to preserve the quantity and to protect the system from damage as per instruction from the operator’s Maintenance Control Centre (MCC). The flight crew continued to destination without further incident, and declared a PAN PAN with ATC when in range of LIPZ. The flight was briefly put in a hold to accommodate ATC requirements, then landed on Runway 04R. The flight crew taxied the aircraft to the gate.The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and found that the cause of the leak was a flex hose located on the LH MLG side brace. The part was replaced, and the aircraft was returned to service.

N5741D, a privately operated Piper PA-22-150, was conducting a VFR flight from Tok, AK (PFTO) to Whitehorse, YT (CYXY). N5741D conducted a straight in approach to CYXY Runway 14R. The ATIS information stated winds were 230° true at 5 knots. On landing, while in a tailwheel low attitude, N5741D touched down left main wheel first. When the right main wheel contacted the runway surface, the aircraft veered and pirouetted about the right main landing gear. The aircraft came to rest with the right main landing gear off the runway surface. The aircraft continued off the runway under its own power. The pilot, sole occupant was uninjured and the ELT was not activated. The aircraft received substantial damage to the right cockpit fuselage tubing and area of the right main gear attach point.

C-GVZP, a privately-operated Piper PA-28-140, departed runway 29 at the Sechelt Aerodrome (CAP3) on a local sight-seeing flight with the pilot and three passengers. The wind was variable and gusty, predominately from the west. The aircraft's rate of climb immediately after take-off was low. As it overflew the Chapman Creek ravine off the departure end of the runway, the aircraft stopped climbing and flew into trees on the side of the ravine. The pilot was fatally injured; the three passengers received minor injuries and the aircraft was destroyed.

C-FULE, an ATR 72-202 operated by Calm Air as flight CAV470, departed Thompson, MB (CYTH) for Rankin Inlet, NU (CYRT). At approximately 50 nautical miles north of Churchill, MB (CYYQ), the flight crew received a low oil pressure indication from the left hand engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW124B). The flight crew carried out the applicable checklists and performed a precautionary engine shut down. The crew declared an emergency and diverted the aircraft to CYYQ. The aircraft landed safely with ARFF on standby. The operator's maintenance is investigating to determine the cause and will advise the TSB of their findings.

The private PA28-161 C-GVDH was taking off from CNR4 Tobermory, destined for CYKF Kitchener/Waterloo, with the pilot and three passengers on board.  The weather was reported as very hot with gusty winds.  After initial lift off the pilot levelled the aircraft to gain sufficient speed to climb out, but in doing so contacted the runway. After the brief runway contact the pilot determined that the aircraft was unlikely to clear the trees at the end of the runway, and chose to abort the take-off.  Once the aircraft was back on the ground the pilot commenced heavy braking but was unable to stop the aircraft on the runway.  As the aircraft slid off the runway end, the left wing contacted a tree and was separated.  The aircraft then rolled upside down and came to a stop just short of the trees.  The four occupants were able to egress the aircraft without difficulty and had received only minor injuries during the accident.  The aircraft was significantly damaged.

The privately owned RANS S-7 COURIER aircraft (C-IIFS) was on a local flight from CYEE Midland with the pilot and one passenger on board. During a cross-wind landing the aircraft landed hard on the right main landing gear resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft. The pilot and passenger were not injured.

C-GRNE, a Piper PA-31-350 operated by the Province of Manitoba, departed Gimli/Industrial Park Airport, MB (CYGM) enroute to The Pas, MB (CYQD).  Approximately 30 nautical miles north of CYGM and leveling at 6000 feet, the pilot noticed a decrease in manifold pressure on the left engine. The pilot performed a precautionary shutdown of the left hand engine (Avco Lycoming LTIO-540-J2BD) and returned to CYGM. The aircraft landed safely. The operator's maintenance inspection revealed that the turbo charger waste gate had malfunctioned.

The Jazz DHC-8-100 aircraft (JZA8675, C-GJIG) was taxiing for take-off at Lester B. Pearson Intl (CYYZ).  Once stopped, waiting for clearance for the runway, the crew set the parking brake. Upon brake release the aircraft did not move forward even though engine power was applied. The flight attendant on board and the crew of the aircraft following C-GJIG reported smoke coming from the left hand brakes. The captain ordered an evacuation of the aircraft on the taxiway and ARFF responded to the scene. No injuries or damage to the aircraft was reported, and the passengers were bussed back to the terminal. Maintenance found the #1 left brake pressure would not fall to below 50 p.s.i. after brakes were released, and subsequent investigation determined the left Dual Skid Control Valve was at fault. The valve was replaced IAW AMM 32-46-11 and subsequent checks revealed no further faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GHGW, a privately registered SZD-50-3 Glider, operated by the Rideau Valley Soaring School was landing at the Kars Aerodrome (CPL3).  During the flare the left wing contacted a tree, the aircraft spun around and impacted the ground. The aircraft was substantially damaged; the pilot who was the sole occupant was not injured.

C-FZXU, a privately registered Cessna A185E, equipped with amphibious floats was departing Commanda Lake, located near Restoule Provincial Park. Shortly after lift off the left wing dropped and the aircraft descended and struck the water. During the impact sequence, the fuselage separated from the floats, and then sank in about 15 feet of water. The pilot and two passengers egressed safely from the aircraft. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The front seat occupants were wearing seatbelts equipped with shoulder harnesses, and the pilot had previously received egress training.

C-GWRJ, a Thrush Aircraft Inc. S2R-H80 aircraft operated by Prairie Dusters, was engaged in agricultural aerial application 6 nm southwest of Russell, MB (CJW5). The pilot was performing east west pattern swath runs, and noticed that the winds and gusts had increased in strength since takeoff from CJW5. The pilot elected to return to CJW5 and wait for more favourable conditions. During the flight back to CJW5, the winds and gusts increased in strength, and were from the west. The pilot considered diverting to Shoal Lake, MB (CKL5) for a more favourable runway, but decided to evaluate the rapidly changing wind conditions while attempting to land at CJW5. The touchdown on Runway 17 was made on one wheel initially, with a crosswind from the right. As the tail settled, the aircraft began to ground loop into the wind. The pilot attempted to control the aircraft with the brakes and added power in an attempt to abort the landing. Then the aircraft swung back to the left. As the aircraft was about to become airborne, the wheels contacted the surface of a slough. The aircraft came to rest inverted in a few feet of water. The pilot was submerged to chest level but was able to release the 5-point harness. With assistance from a pilot who had witnessed the crash, the pilot was able to release the emergency-exit latch and make an underwater egress from the aircraft. The pilot suffered minor injuries and the aircraft sustained substantial damage. The pilot had utilized a 5-point harness and was wearing a helmet.

C-GPUS, a float equipped de Havilland DHC-2, operated by Air Ivanhoe departed on a southerly heading from an unnamed lake near Biggs Lake, approximately 60 nm north east of Chapleau, Ontario. The pilot banked the aircraft steeply during the initial climb out to avoid terrain ahead, and was flying north bound when the aircraft collided with some tree tops and subsequently collided with the shoreline. The aircraft came to rest inverted, and was substantially damaged. There were no reported injuries to the two occupants, both were secured with lap belts only.

N278AY, an Airbus 330-300 operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL718 from Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (KPHL) to Rome, Italy  (LIRF) with 287 passengers, 14 crew members on board. While in cruise and nearing ELSIR fix about 120 NM NE of Gander, NL, (CYQX) the flight encountered moderate turbulence while the seatbelt sign was off. One flight attendant sustained a serious injury, and another a minor injury. Two passengers sustained minor injuries. The flight crew declared an emergency and diverted to Gander (CYQX) and met by EHS. One cabin crew member and the one passenger were transported to hospital.

C-GDUZ, un appareil de type Boeing 767-300 exploité par Air Canada rouge, effectuait le vol ROU1902 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination d’Athènes/Eleftherios Venizelos Intl, Grèce (LGAV) avec 8 membres d'équipage et 282 passagers à bord. Alors qu’il se trouvait en vol de croisière à 25 nm au nord-est de Charlevoix, QC (CYML), l'équipage a reçu des messages EICAS individuels tels que ELEV FEEL, R ENG HP SOV, WINDOW HEAT et FWD EQUIPT COOLING, sans toutefois observer d'anomalie au niveau du comportement de l'avion. L'équipage a alors demandé une diversion vers Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB). Dû aux conditions météorologiques qui se détérioraient à l'approche à CYQB, l'équipage a déclaré PAN PAN afin d'obtenir la priorité. Bien que 7 tonnes de carburant ont été larguées avant l’atterrissage, l'appareil s'est posé en surpoids sans encombre à CYQB. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

The Delta Helicopters Ltd. Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2, C-FWCL, Serial number 2869, was moving a tree planting crew from cut block 1516 to 1657 approximately 32 nautical miles to the northeast of Rainbow Lake, AB. On arrival to cut block 1657 the pilot performed an orbit to assess landing sites. On the approach to the chosen landing site the main rotor struck a tree. The pilot moved away from the tree to assess the situation. Vibrations were not too strong so he began to move to a more suitable landing site. Dropping to 10 feet above the ground with the vibrations increasing exponentially, the pilot was able to slide the aircraft onto a service road. The aircraft landed hard buckling the tail boom, but remained upright on its skids. The emergency locator beacon did not activate. There were no injuries.

C-FTJH, a Boeing 737-800 operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight 3Z7377 from Girona-Costa Brava, Spain (LEGE) to Frédéric Chopin Int’l, Poland (EPWA) with 6 crewmembers and 187 passengers onboard. The flight crew requested priority handling into EPWA and that emergency medical services meet the aircraft at the gate due to an ill passenger onboard.

C-GOJI, an Air Tractor AT402B aircraft operated by Fly On Ag Services Inc., was conducting a flight from Geraldton, ON (CYGQ) to Sioux Lookout, ON (CYXL). During the landing on Runway 34 directional control was lost. The aircraft exited the runway to the west, north of Taxiway A. The aircraft re-entered the runway and taxied to the apron. The winds were reported to be 260 degrees at 14 knots gusting to 27 knots. The tailwheel alignment required adjustment after a subsequent flight.

C-FKPA, a Pilatus PC-12/45 aircraft operated by North Star Air Ltd., was commencing flight BF709 from Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT) to Attawapiskat, ON (CYAT). At lift off from Runway 25, the flight crew encountered an inadvertent stick-shaker activation, accompanied by the illumination of the stick- pusher warning light. The stick-pusher interrupt button was depressed and held. Simultaneously the flight crew increased the angle of attack and maintained engine power at 42 psi. Due to the proximity to the ground the crew pulled out the stick-pusher circuit-breaker. The memory checklist items were completed and the checklist was consulted. The crew declared an emergency. About 3 to 5 minutes after the original stick-shaker operation commenced the J2 circuit breakers were pulled out and the operation of the stick-shaker ceased. However the stick-pusher warning light remained illuminated. The subsequent landing was uneventful. The operator's maintenance personnel performed tests of the stick-pusher system, engine ground runs and pre-flight stick-pusher test. No faults were found and troubleshooting is on-going.

C-GFLA, a Pilatus PC-12/45 aircraft was conducting a medical transport flight from Iqualuit, NU (CYFB) to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG). The aircraft was making a planned fuel stop in Coral Harbour, NU (CYZS) where the winds were reported to be 270 degrees at 15 knots. The touchdown on Runway 34T was firm and the aircraft bounced back into the air. The pilot flying, checked forward with the control column, and the  nose-down pitching moment resulted in propeller contact with the runway surface. The aircraft was taxied to the apron. The crew did not note any unusual vibrations or engine parameters. The damage assessment is on-going.

N255UP, a McDonnell Douglas MD-11F aircraft operated by United Parcel Service, was conducting flight UPS72 from San Antonio/Kelly Field, Texas (KSKF) to Anchorage/Ted Stevens Intl., Alaska (PANC). While in cruise, the flight crew received an "Indicated Airspeed" warning on the captain and co-pilot primary flight displays. The flight crew declared an emergency and the flight descended to FL320. The "Airspeed Unreliable" checklist was followed during which the No. 1 Air Data Computer (ADC) was determined to be unreliable. The No. 2 ADC was selected and all indications returned to normal. The "Indicated Airspeed" warning extinguished. The flight continued to destination without further incident. The No. 1 ADC was replaced and system checks were satisfactory.

C-FYYT, un appareil de type de Havilland DHC-2 MK. I (Beaver) exploité par Air Saguenay, se préparait à décoller du lac Jules, QC situé à 44 nm à l’ouest-sud-ouest de Manic-5, QC (CMN5) pour un vol selon les règles de vol à vue vers le lac Margane, QC, avec un pilote et 3 passagers à son bord. L’appareil a débuté sa course au décollage en direction sud. Lorsque le pilote a constaté qu’il ne pourrait être en vol avant le bout du lac, il a interrompu sa course au décollage. L’appareil est entré en collision avec les arbres de la rive sud du lac, causant des dommages importants à l’appareil. Les occupants ont pu évacuer l’avion sans difficulté et n’ont pas été blessés. L’ELT s’est déclenché suite à l’impact.

N821AE, un appareil de type Embraer EMB-135KL exploité par Envoy Air, effectuait le vol ENY3368 selon les règles de vol aux instruments à partir de New York/LaGuardia, NY (KLGA) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Lors de l'approche à CYUL, l'équipage a déclaré une urgence, invoquant un problème de déporteurs. Une remise des gaz a été effectuée et l’appareil est revenu se poser sans encombre sur la piste 06L à 1711Z. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GKKU, a privately operated Cessna 182P aircraft, was on a VFR flight plan from Calgary/Springbank, AB (CYBW) to Nanaimo, BC (CYCD) with two persons on board. The pilot was in contact initially with Kelowna sector Air Traffic Services to provide flight following. At a point during cruise flight, the pilot was advised that radar service was terminated. Approximately 30 minutes later, the aircraft collided with a mountain at an elevation of about 5800’ ASL. The aircraft had been observed following the Coquihalla Highway at very low altitude due to a ceiling of approximately 300’ AGL. The aircraft was equipped with a Garmin ADS-B antenna and was identified by the NavCanada Aireon satellite system. The last recorded target placed the aircraft in a climb at 5200’ feet ASL. It had turned right into a valley, away from the highway, and collided with a granite mountain slope. Both occupants were fatally injured. The aircraft was destroyed and mostly consumed by fire.

C-FWFZ, a privately operated Robinson R44 helicopter, was landing on a logging road approximately 39 nm North West of Prince George, BC (CYXS). Just prior to touchdown, a gust of wind pushed the helicopter sideways and the left skid contacted the ground, causing the helicopter to roll over. The helicopter sustained substantial damage, however the pilot suffered only minor injuries.

D-AIGV, an Airbus 340-300 aircraft operated by Lufthansa, was conducting flight DLH489 from San José/Norman Y. Mineta Intl, CA (KSJC) to Frankfurt/Rhein-Main, Germany (EDDF). During the cruise portion of the flight in Canadian airspace, a powerbank caught fire in the cabin, which was extinguished by the cabin crew. There was no damage to the aircraft, and no injuries. The aircraft continued to destination and landed without further incident. Germany’s Federal Bureau of Aircraft Accidents Investigation (BFU) notified the TSB of the occurrence and have retrieved the powerbank.

N525EZ, un avion d'affaire de type de Cessna 525C, effectuait un vol privé selon les règles de vol aux instruments à partir de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de Westchester County/White Plains, NY (KHPN). Peu de temps après le décollage de la piste 06R, N525EZ a dévié à gauche pour éviter une volée d'oiseaux. Ce faisant, il s'est rapproché de JZA716 un DHC8-300 de Jazz immatriculé C-FACF décollé précédemment en direction de l'aéroport Jean Lesage Intl de Québec, QC (CYQB) et qui était au nord de l'axe. ATS a donné l'instruction à N525EZ de virer vers la droite au cap 090 afin de rétablir l'espacement qui s'est retrouvé réduit à 1.8nm alors que la norme était de 2NM. Toutefois, il n'y a pas eu de risque réel de collision.

C-GHPR, a Cessna A188B aircraft operated by Air Greenway Ltd., was engaged in fungicide application 0.7 nm W of St. Alphonse, MB. During a spray run, the engine (Teledyne Continental Motors, IO-520-D) lost power. The pilot jettisoned the load and conducted a forced approach and landing on a grid road. During the landing, the main landing gear contacted a ditch and the aircraft came to rest on the roadway. The pilot received minor injuries. The aircraft sustained damage to the landing gear, tail, fuselage, left wing, and spray-boom.

C-FWGH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing on behalf of TUI Airways, was conducting flight TOM1148 from Dublin Intl, Ireland (EIDW) to Burgas Intl, Bulgaria (LBBG). Shortly after the departure off Runway 10 at EIDW, ATC authorized the flight direct to enroute waypoint RULOV, however the flight crew was unable to execute the command despite several attempts. The flight crew decided to return to EIDW as a precaution. An overweight landing was completed, and the aircraft taxied to a parking stand where ARFF met the aircraft to check the brakes for heat. The operator’s maintenance checked the Flight Management Computer (FMC) and all associated systems in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) and the Fault Isolation Manual (FIM), all checks were found satisfactory. The aircraft was returned to service, and no further occurrences have been reported.

C-GMNI, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 helicopter operated by Lakelse Air, was conducting external load operations approximately 10 nm East of Bronson Creek Airport, BC (abandoned) with only the pilot on board. As the helicopter began to transition into forward flight with ten propane tanks weighting 100 lbs each in a cargo net suspended by a 100 foot long line, the pilot noticed degraded performance due to unfavorable wind conditions and elected to release the external load. The pilot return to land without further incident. A minor over-torque was recorded on the helicopter’s torque gauge. Damage to the propane tanks resulted from the release.

C-FYHD, a Bell 205A-1 skid-equipped aircraft operated by Northern Shield Helicopters, was conducting belly-hook water bucket operations 24 nautical miles North West of Hudson Bay, SK (CYHB). The pilot was hovering the helicopter over Buckmayer Lake, SK with the bucket in the water while waiting for instructions from the bird dog aircraft when there was an abnormal noise, which was accompanied by a lateral vibration. The pilot began to manoeuvre the helicopter toward the shore and, after travelling approximately 100 metres, the vibration changed to a vertical vibration and worsened. The pilot informed the bird dog pilot that there was a drive train problem, then landed the aircraft in the lake close to shore. During the approach, the tail rotor contacted trees. Once on the water, the shaking caused both crew doors to pop open. The pilot shut the engine down and pulled collective pitch to slow the rotors. The helicopter floated and, after the rotor system came to a stop, the pilot exited the aircraft and swam about 15 metres to shore. The helicopter eventually rolled onto its side, and sank in about 6 feet of water. The bird dog aircraft was circling the site and initiated rescue operations. After firefighters cleared a landing pad, the pilot was recovered from the site. The pilot was uninjured, however was transported to hospital for observation. The helicopter sustained substantial damage and was recovered from the site. The investigation is ongoing.

N511CM, a privately operated de Havilland DHC-2T MK III aircraft, was conducting a flight from Kamloops, BC (CYKA) to Vancouver/Boundary Bay, BC (CZBB). During cruise flight, the aircraft encountered icing conditions while in instrument meteorological conditions (IMC). As the pilot was unable to cancel the IFR flight plan, a descent was requested and ATC issued the emergency descent profile into the Fraser Valley, BC.  The aircraft landed without further incident at CZBB.

The WestJet Airlines Boeing 767-300 ER, C-FOGJ, was operating as flight WJA27 from Gatwick, UK (EGKK) to Edmonton, AB (CYEG). While in cruise a flight attendant became incapacitated and was unable to continue with their duties.

C-GARF, un Cessna 150B en exploitation privé effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Joliette, QC (CSG3), à destination de Trois-Rivières, QC (CYRQ) avec 1 pilote et 1 passager à bord. Alors qu’il circulait au sol pour le décollage, l’aile gauche a percuté l’hélice du C-GTIR, un Cessna 172N stationné avec le moteur arrêté. L’aile du C-GARF a subi des dommages importants. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

A Piper PA-31-350, C-GBDN operated by Northern Skies Air Service as flight GS103, was conducting a VFR flight from Poplar Hill (CPV7), Ontario, to Pikangikum (CYPM), Ontario. The flight landed on Runway 09 at CYPM with the landing gear retracted and was substantially damaged. Three passengers received minor injuries. The other 2 passengers and the 2 pilots were not injured.Post-occurrence examination of the aircraft by the operator's maintenance staff determined all 3 landing gear were up and locked, and the landing gear handle was in the down position.

N154GJ, a Bombardier CL-600-2C10, operated by GoJet Airlines (flight number 4509), was inbound to Toronto (CYYZ). Due to an extended flight time for weather, the amount of fuel on board was less than planned when approaching CYYZ. It was reported that due to high traffic volume the aircraft was given delay vectors during the approach. The flight crew complied with the vectors but eventually declared a fuel emergency, and was subsequently cleared direct to CYYZ. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-IKIJ un paramoteur Per Il Volo, miniplane effectuait un vol local en exploitation privée avec seul le pilote à bord. Lors de la montée après le décollage d’une carrière de sable, à environ 70 pieds au-dessus du sol, un changement soudain de vent est survenu et la voilure a subi une fermeture frontale. L’appareil est descendu quasi vertical et a percuté le sol. Le pilote a subi des blessures graves et l’appareil a subi des dommages importants.

C-GFFI, a privately operated Piper PA31, was conducting an IFR flight from Edmonton, AB (CYEG) to Tofino, BC (CYAZ) with 1 pilot and 4 passengers on board. While in cruise in IMC at FL180 the left engine (Avco Lycoming TIO-540-A2C) lost power. The pilot attempted to restore power but was unsuccessful. The aircraft was unable to maintain altitude on one engine and a controlled descent and turn back to CYEG was initiated by the pilot. The area minimum altitude (AMA) in the area of the descent was 13 900 feet. The pilot declared an emergency by relaying a message through another aircraft as radio contact was lost with ATC due to terrain and being below 14 000 feet. The pilot relied on a synthetic vision terrain depiction on a personal electronic device to ensure adequate separation from terrain. While descending through 10 000 feet the pilot was able to restart the engine and the flight continued uneventfully to CYEG. Maintenance did not find any issues with the engine and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWEJ, a Bombardier DHC-8-402, operated by Westjet Encore (flight number 3415) was taxiing for departure at Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) when the left main brake seized which eventually caused both tires to blow. The flight crew declared an emergency. The passengers were off loaded and taken to the terminal by buses. There were no injuries.

C-FOWE, a Bombardier DHC-8-402, operated by Westjet Encore (flight number 3461) departed Ottawa (CYOW) destined for Toronto (CYYZ). While at FL220 the flight crew received a cabin pressure warning, and subsequently declared an emergency and returned to CYOW. The aircraft landed safely, there were no injuries.

The Northwestern Air Lease Ltd British Aerospace BA 32-12, C-GNAQ was operating as flight PLR598 from Fort Smith, NT (CYSM) to Edmonton, AB (CYEG). PLR598 was cleared for the RNAV Z approach to Runway 12 in CYEG via MIPOT. The Horizon Air Industries Inc. Embraer ERJ 170-200 LR, N633QX was operating as flight QXE2542 from Seattle, WA (KSEA) to CYEG. While on the ESKIE TWO arrival for Runway 12 in CYEG QXE2542 did not turn at the BEMIG waypoint as per the arrival. The controller noticed the deviation and instructed QXE2542 to turn. PLR598 had just switched to the tower frequency and by the time ATS instructed them to descend separation eroded to 600 feet and 2.5 nm when 1000 feet or 3.0 nm is required.

The Air Tindi Ltd de Havilland DHC-7-103, C-FWZV, was operating as flight TIN802 from Diavik, NT (CDK2) to Yellowknife, NT (CYZF). While on final approach to Runway 10 in CYZF the crew selected landing gear down and the nose gear unsafe light remained illuminated. The crew cycled the landing gear but the condition persisted. The crew then declared an emergency and conducted a low approach and requested ATC to visually inspect the gear. ATC told the crew that the gear appeared to be down but could not verify. The crew maneuvered west of the airport to reference the appropriate check list and consult with company operations. The crew then conducted another low approach and company maintenance visually confirmed the gear was down. The aircraft landed safely at CYZF with ARFF in attendance. Subsequent inspection by company maintenance found the nose gear downlock micro switch actuating lever was missing. The micro switch actuating lever was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service. The company has inspected the remainder of its fleet, but have found no other aircraft with this fault.

C-GBSV, un appareil de type Beech C 23 en exploitation privée, était au sol à l'aéroport de Trois-Rivières, QC (CYRQ) avec seul 1 pilote à bord. Après le démarrage, l’appareil a avancé et l’hélice a percuté l’aile de C-GAGN, un appareil de type Cessna 172N qui était stationné. L’hélice du C-GBSV a été endommagée et l’aile du C-GAGN a subi des dommages importants. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GETA, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-300 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol régulier JZA8964 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Mont-Joli, QC (CYYY), à destination de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC) avec 18 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage à bord. En raison des travaux de réfection de la piste à CYBC, la moitié sud (75 pieds) de la largeur de celle-ci était fermée sur toute sa longueur. Lorsque JZA8964 s’est posé sur la piste 10, l’appareil était aligné au centre de la piste; conséquemment, le train d'atterrissage droit s’est posé sur la partie fermée de la piste. Lorsque l’appareil s’est déplacé à gauche vers la partie ouverte de la piste, la roue interne du train principal droit a percuté une lumière temporaire de piste et a subi une crevaison. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil. Il n’y avait aucune marque de piste fermée sur la partie sud de la piste.

C-GBSC, un appareil de type Cessna R182 exploité par Exact Air, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Manic-5, QC (CMN5) à destination de Baie-Comeau, QC (CYBC) avec seul le pilote à bord. En raison des travaux de réfection de la piste à CYBC, la moitié sud (75 pieds) de la largeur de celle-ci était fermée sur toute sa longueur. Lors de l’atterrissage sur la piste 28, l’appareil a dévié à gauche et s’est posé sur la partie fermée de la piste. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage. Le personnel au sol a aidé l’appareil à retourner sur la partie nord de la piste qui était ouverte.

C-FLQY, a Bombardier, DHC-8-400, operated by Porter Airlines (flight 203) was on final approach for runway 07 at Ottawa MacDonald-Cartier Intl (CYOW). The left propeller feathered without input from the flight crew and then alternated between feather and unfeather until touchdown. The flight crew had difficulty controlling the aircraft but managed to land without further incident. There were no injuries. Maintenance determined the left propeller electronic control (PEC) unit was faulty and subsequently replaced it.

C-GNCH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines on behalf of TUI Airways, was conducting flight TOM1417 from Palma de Mallorca/Son Sant Joan, Spain (LEPA) to Belfast/Aldergrove Intl, UK (EGAA) with 6 crew members and 196 passengers on board. Shortly after the fuel truck finished the refueling at Stand 23B, a minor fuel spill occurred from the right wing fuel surge tank vent. The flight crew was notified and ARFF was requested to the aircraft. Boarding was temporarily suspended and resumed once the problem was resolved.The aircraft departed shortly thereafter without further incident.

C-FFPH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines on behalf of TUI Airways, was conducting flight TOM5483 from Paphos Intl, Cyprus (LCPH) to Norwich Intl, UK (EGSH). During cruise flight at FL360, an electrical odour was detected in the passenger cabin in the vicinity of Rows 2, 3, and 4. The flight crew made a precautionary diversion to Sofia Intl, Bulgaria (LBSF) where it landed uneventfully. The operator’s maintenance carried out an inspection and could not found any faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

G-VLNM, an Airbus 330-200 operated by Virgin Atlantic was conducting flight Vir110 from Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson International (KATL) Airport to Manchester Airport (EGCC) with 175 passengers and 12 crew. Approximately 100 NM NW of Stephenville NL (CYJT) the crew noted smoke in the galley area of the cabin. Cabin power was shut down and the smoke dissipated, the crew did not declare an emergency but did divert to Halifax (CYHZ) where a safe landing was conducted. Maintenance completed a galley inspection with no causal factors identified. The aircraft is being relocated to London, Gatwick for further inspection with two technicians and a full compliment of cabin crew to monitor for any further smoke enroute.

C-GAGE, a Cessna 441 operated by Lake Central Airways, was taxiing for departure at Toronto (CYYZ). The aircraft was cleared to taxi via taxiways ECHO and DELTA to the threshold of Runway 06L. While taxiing southbound on taxiway ECHO, the aircraft continued past taxiway DELTA and crossed the Runway 06L hold short line. ATC instructed C-GAGE to stop. At the time of the incursion a Westjet Boeing 737-800 (registration C-GWBL, flight number 1246) was on the take-off roll, departing from Runway 06L.

C-GWSI, a WestJet Boeing 737-600 aircraft, operating as flight WJA427, was taxiing for departure at Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ). The aircraft was instructed to taxi via taxiway Bravo to Hotel for departure on runway 23. The aircraft missed the right turn onto taxiway Hotel and continued on Bravo. ATC instructed the aircraft to stop when the aircraft crossed the hold short line at runway 05/23. Jazz flight JZA602, a De Havilland DHC-8-102 (C-GONX) aircraft, on approach to runway23 was instructed to go around.

C-GLLE, a Bush Caddy L164 amatuer built aircraft on floats, was on final approach to land in the south bay of Lake Nippissing when the pilot noticed a wasp in the cabin. The pilot became preoccupied with the wasp and the aircraft stalled at about 50 feet agl. During the recovery from the stall the right float made contact with the water and dug in and the aircraft began to spin around. The aircraft remained upright and sank due to the damaged floats. The pilot received minor injuries but egressed from the aircraft and was picked up by a boater. The pilot had previously taken underwater egress training, and was wearing a 4 point safety belt and inflatable PFD at the time of the accident.

C-FCSP, a Cessna 172S aircraft operated by Pacific Sky Aviation, was returning to Victoria, BC (CYYJ) from the Cowichan Lake flight training area with one student pilot on-board. During the approach to land at CYYJ, ATC requested the pilot increase their approach speed.  During the landing flare, the aircraft porpoised, and the touchdown was hard.  The pilot taxied the aircraft to the Pacific Sky Aviation Hanger.  Subsequent inspection revealed that the aircraft had sustained substantial damage including both propeller ends being bent, the nose wheel damaged and the bottom of the aircraft rippled.

C-FOIZ, a Cessna 182 on floats, was landing on Vixen Lake with one pilot and one passenger on board. During the landing there was a crosswind gust and the downwind float caught the water and dug in. The aircraft spun and flipped over, coming to rest inverted. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The pilot and passenger were both wearing 4 point harnesses and inflatable PFDs and were able to egress the cabin and inflate their PFDs. The pilot had received underwater egress training.

C-FTJC, a Cessna 560 Encore aircraft operated by Carson Air, was conducting a flight from Terrace, BC (CYXT) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). While climbing thru 17 000 feet, the flight crew turned on the engine and wing anti-ice systems. Shortly thereafter, the flight crew observed a right engine fire warning light. The flight crew leveled the aircraft at FL230 and completed the engine fire light checklist. After reducing power on the right engine as per the checklist, the engine fire light extinguished. The flight crew completed the checklist and advised ATC that they would continue the flight to CYVR with reduced power on the right engine. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident.

D2-TBO, a Boeing 737-200 aircraft owned by Angola Airlines, was operated by a ferry pilot, first officer and technician and was conducting a ferry flight from Luanda, Angola via Santa Maria, Azores (LPAZ) to St John's, NL, (CYYT) with final destination Mirabel, QC (CYMX). While approximately 200 nm east of CYYT the crew noted a loss of oil quantity in the #2 engine and shut the engine down. An emergency was declared and the aircraft continued to CYYT where a safe landing was conducted. The technician determined that the gear box oil pressure line had loosened and oil was escaping. The fitting was secured, the oil was replenished and after an engine test run the final leg to CYMX was conducted without incident.

N991BW, a privately operated amateur built Glasair Sportsman 2+2 aircraft, was conducting a local flight from Langley, BC (CYNJ). While in the Glen Valley training area the pilot observed an unusual noise coming from the engine (Aerosport IO375).  The pilot elected to return to CYNJ.  During the approach to CYNJ the pilot requested priority from ATC for landing on runway 25.  Shortly after priority was given the aircraft experienced a reduction in power.  The pilot made an emergency landing in a rhubarb field approximately 3.5 nm NE of CYNJ.  Just after initial touch down the aircraft nosed over in the soft field.  The aircraft came to rest inverted.  The pilot and passenger received minor injuries, the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FNRY, a privately registered Piper, PA-18-150, departed Sault Ste. Marie (CYAM) and was in the vicinity of Parisian Island, on Lake Superior, approximately 13 nm to the north west of CYAM. The pilot and an instructor were practicing forced approaches on a beach shoreline. It was reported that during the overshoot procedure, a wind shear occurred and the descent could not be arrested. The aircraft touched down on the beach and flipped over; eventually coming to rest partially in the water. The occupants were not injured however the aircraft was substantially damaged.

BWA600, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Caribbean Airlines, had just landed on Runway 24L at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ), and was instructed by ATC to hold short of Runway 24R. The flight crew read back the instruction correctly and exited Runway 24L on rapid exit Taxiway D6. Subsequently, ATC cleared WJA30, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, to takeoff from Runway 24R.  As WJA30 was on the takeoff roll, BWA600 crossed the hold short line on D6, and was instructed by ATC to stop. BWA600 stopped before reaching the runway surface.

C-GJKD, un Cessna 150K X (équipé de flotteurs) en exploitation privé effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis le Lac Noir situé à 4 miles marins au sud-est de Nominingue, QC avec un pilote et un passager à son bord. Après le décollage, à une hauteur d’environ 50 pieds au-dessus de la surface de l’eau, l’appareil a subi une panne motrice (Lycoming O-320-E2D X). Par la suite, un décrochage aérodynamique survenu, l’appareil a percuté la surface de l’eau et il a culbuté. Le C-GJKD est demeuré à la surface sur le dos et les 2 occupants ont réussi à quitter l’habitacle sans blessure. L’appareil a subi des dommages importants. La radiobalise de repérage d'urgence (ELT) ne s’est pas déclenchée.

C-GRPF, a Bombardier CL600-2B16 Challenger 601 aircraft operated by Skyservice Business Aviation, was conducting a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Fort Lauderdale Executive, FL (KFXE) with 3 crew members and 6 passengers on board. When the aircraft was level at 3000 feet on a westerly heading while on radar vectors for the ILS 09 at KFXE, ATC advised the flight crew of a traffic located 20 degrees to their left at 1800 feet. The flight crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory (RA) to initiate a climb. The flight crew complied with the RA and advised ATC of the deviation. When clear of the traffic, the flight crew descended back to 3000 feet and completed the approach with no further incident.

C-FEAK, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Thomson Airways on behalf of TUI Airways, was conducting flight TOM370 from Leeds/Bradford Intl, UK (EGNM) to Dalaman, Turkey (LTBS). Approximately 3 hours into the flight, within the Macedonia FIR at FL370, the flight crew was unable to reach FL390 within the cleared time limit and leveled off at FL380. ATC instructed the aircraft to turn right 5 degrees, and on the new heading, TOM370 received a "Climb" RA. TOM370 complied with the RA and advised ATC.

C-GVBI, a privately operated, float equipped Maule M-5-210C aircraft, was landing at Geraldton/Hutchison Lake, ON (CNE6). While on final approach to the glassy water surface, the pilot found the throttle to be stuck when power was needed to arrest the high rate of descent. The aircraft landed hard, bounced and dug in a float, causing the aircraft to overturn. The pilot, who was wearing a 4 point safety belt and an inflatable PFD, was able exit the aircraft and received minor injuries.

C-IGOC, a Rans S-6ES Coyote II Advanced Ultra-light aircraft, was inbound to land on Runway 12 at Omemee, ON (CME2). While the aircraft was approaching the threshold of the runway, a sandhill crane encroached on the flight path of the aircraft. The pilot attempted to avoid the collision with the bird and inadvertently went into a drainage ditch beside the runway. The aircraft flipped and came to rest inverted. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was not injured. However, the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FCLS, un DH8A exploité par Air Creebec sous l’indicatif CRQ461, effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Val d’Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) avec seuls 2 membres d’équipage. Alors que l’appareil est en croisière au niveau de vol 190, une dépressurisation est survenue. L’équipage a effectué une descente d’urgence et a poursuivi le vol à destination à 9000 pieds asl, où l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-GDZA, a Cessna 172G aircraft operated by FD Air Tours, was conducting a local VFR photo flight from Summerside, PE (CYSU) over the island. After approximately 4 hours and 10 minutes of flight, the aircraft returned for landing at CYSU. In the turn from right base to final approach for Runway 23, the engine lost power. The pilot set up for a short field landing and landed in the grass, approximately 500 feet short of the runway. There were no injuries or damage to the aircraft. The pilot noted that there was 20 litres of fuel in the right tank and the left tank was empty. Once the aircraft was refueled, the engine operated without any issues. The pilot believes that, in the turn, the engine experienced fuel starvation due to the low fuel level.

C-FCHE, a Bell 205A-1 aircraft operated by Custom Helicopters, was conducting a sling load VFR flight from Little Grand Rapids, MB (CZGR) to Pauingassi, MB. Approximately 5 nm North of CZGR during cruise flight, a refrigerator that was part of the sling load fell from the sling net. The helicopter continued to destination and landed uneventfully. The refrigerator fell in an uninhabited area.

C-GNIX, an Aerospatiale AS350 B3 aircraft operated by Hy-Ridge Helicopters, was on a VFR flight with a slung load of camp food provisions from Coleman, AB to a field 20 nm to the South East. While on final approach, the pilot attempted to transmit on the radio, however inadvertently pressed the remote hook release switch. The load was released and impacted the ground short of the landing area. There was no damage to property and the area was cleaned up by the company.

C-GKWE, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3395 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG). Shortly after the takeoff from CYYC, the flight crew noticed an unsafe landing gear indication following gear up selection, as the landing gear failed to retract. The flight crew followed the appropriate checklist and lowered the landing gear. The landing gear extended and indicated down and locked. The flight crew elected to return to CYYC and requested ARFF on standby. The aircraft landed without further incident. Subsequent inspection by the operator’s maintenance resulted in the replacement of the nose landing gear actuator. The aircraft was tested serviceable and was returned to service.

C-GJQG, un appareil de type Sikorsky S-61N exploité par Canadian Helicopters, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue à partir de Cape Hooper, NU à destination d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Pendant le vol, l'équipage a détecté de la fumée provenant du contrôleur de dégivrage du pare-brise, situé près des pieds du co-pilote. Le contrôleur de dégivrage du pare-brise a été mis hors-circuit, et la fumée s'est dissipée. Le personnel de l’entretien a par la suite confirmé une défaillance du contrôleur de dégivrage du pare-brise. L'aéronef a atterri sans encombre à CYFB peu de temps après. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GBBZ, a float-equipped Cessna 206 operated by Kississing Lake Lodge (dba Wings Over Kississing), was en route from Flin Flon, MB to Chatwin Lake, MB to pick up passengers. At the destination, the aircraft landed long on the lake surface and ran up onto a beach. The aircraft struck small trees and brush at the beach's edge and sustained damage to both left and right leading edges. The pilot was uninjured. The operator is coordinating to ferry the aircraft to a maintenance facility where it will removed from service until repaired.

C-FSMR, a privately registered, float-equipped Piper PA-11 aircraft, was conducting a VFR flight from Vermillion Bay, ON (CKH6) to Big Canyon Lake, ON. Upon landing at Big Canyon Lake, the aircraft's left float struck a rock. The damage sustained allowed water into the float and the aircraft subsequently sank. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was uninjured. The aircraft has been removed from service.

C-GKGA, a Beech 1900C aircraft operated by Skylink Express, was conducting cargo flight SLQ751 from Kamloops, BC (CYKA) to Kelowna, BC (CYLW) with two pilots on board. As the aircraft was taxiing across the main apron at CYKA prior to the departure, the flight crew received a right engine fire annunciator. The flight crew notified ATC, shut down the aircraft on the apron, and evacuated. ARFF responded, however no indication of fire was found and the aircraft was towed back to the parking area.The operator’s maintenance found a defective forward fire loop (p/n 244-12886). The fire loop was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GUBF, an Airbus 330-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC705 from London/Gatwick, UK (EGKK) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with 11 crew members and 283 passengers on board. Less than 1 hour after the departure in the vicinity of Glasgow/Abbotsinch, UK (EGPF), one of the cabin crew members became ill and was unable to continue their duties. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FEKB, a Beech 200 aircraft operated by Kenn Borek Air, was conducting flight KBA203 from Inuvik (Mike Zubko), NT (CYEV) to Paulatuk (Nora Aliqatchialuk Ruben), NT (CYPC) with 2 crew and 9 passengers on board. Shortly after levelling off at FL210, the right engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PT6A-41) torque reduced to zero and the T5 increased to 850°C. The flight crew set flight idle on the right engine, however the T5 continued to climb to 1100°C. The flight crew shut the engine down, declared an emergency and returned to CYEV where an uneventful single-engine approach and landing was performed with ARFF standing by.

C-FNEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3176 from Victoria Intl, BC (CYYJ) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) with 4 crew members and 50 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL250, south east of Kamloops, BC (CYKA), the aircraft encountered turbulence. As a result, a flight attendant sustained a serious injury and was unable to continue their duties.

C-FJKS, a privately operated Aviat Sky Intl A-1C-200 (Husky) aircraft, was on a local pleasure flight in the vicinity of Joseph Lake, AB. When the aircraft was at 300 feet above the lake, the engine (Avco Lycoming AEIO-360-A1D) began losing power. The pilot conducted a forced landing into the shallow lake and the aircraft nosed over upon touchdown. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was wearing a helmet and a four point harness, and egressed the aircraft quickly without injuries. The 406 ELT activated, and was detected by COSPAS/SARSAT. JRCC Trenton initiated search operations, and the pilot was recovered approximately 2 hours later.

F-GZNS, un appareil de type Boeing 777-328ER exploité par Air France, effectuait le vol AFR342 selon les règles de vol aux instruments à partir de Paris/Charles de Gaulle, France (LFPG) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Lors de l'approche à CYUL, AFR342 a été instruit par l’ATC d'effectuer une approche interrompue, car l'espacement était devenu insuffisant avec C-FEJB, un appareil de type Embraer 170 exploité par Sky Regional Airlines sous l'indicatif de vol SKV7639, provenant de New York/LaGuardia, NY (KLGA), qui était situé devant AFR342. L'espacement a été réduit à 2.6 nm sur le plan longitudinal, alors que la norme est de 3 nm. AFR342 a ensuite été guidé pour une seconde approche, et s’est posé sur la piste 24R à 2150Z.

C-GEOW, a Pilatus PC-12/45 aircraft operated by North Star Air, was conducting flight BF712 from Fort Hope, ON (CYFH) to Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT) with 2 crew members and 2 passengers on board. During the final approach for Runway 12 at CYQT, the flight crew observed an engine fire light. No emergency was declared, however the flight crew requested that fire trucks be placed on standby. The aircraft landed without further incident and taxied off the runway. The engine fire on ground checklist was then executed, and the passengers deplaned. A subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance revealed a faulty engine fire detection loop. The loop was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GONR, un appareil de type DHC-8-102 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA762 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 33 passagers à bord. Alors qu’il était en vol de croisière à 9000’ ASL, environ 40 miles marins (nm) au nord est de CYUL, l'équipage a reçu une alerte TCAS RA causé par un trafic VFR situé 300 pieds plus bas, juste à la sortie de l'espace aérien contrôlé de classe "C". Lorsque l'espacement a réduit à 1 nm, l’équipage de conduite a alors monté à 10 000’, et est ensuite redescendu à 9000’ une fois le trafic passé. JZA762 avait un contact visuel avec le trafic en tout temps, toutefois celui-ci n'a pu être identifié.

N942WD un appareil de type PA-31-310 exploité privément, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue, de l'aéroport de Montréal Intl-Mirabel (CYMX) à destination de Lachute, QC (CSE4). Suite au décollage, le pilote a signalé avoir des problèmes de train d'atterrissage et a déclaré une urgence. Après avoir passé près de la tour pour que le FSS observe la position du train d'atterrissage, l'aéronef a atterri sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GJZS, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 CRJ900 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8626 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Dallas-Fort Worth Intl, TX (KDFW) with 4 crew members and 72 passengers on board. As the landing gear was selected down during the intermediate approach for Runway 17R at KDFW, the flight crew received a NOSE WHEEL STEERING caution light. The landing gear was recycled, however this time a NOSE GEAR UNSAFE light came on. The flight crew executed a missed approach and declared a PAN PAN. While circling around for another approach, the landing gear was recycled several times and, finally, the flight crew received three green lights. The aircraft landed without further incident and stopped on the runway in order to be inspected. The aircraft was then cleared to taxi to the gate.The operator's maintenance found the lower bearing seal damaged at the nose landing gear. The seal was replaced as per CMM 32-21-06, task #12-12-32-610-804, AMM 32-30-00-710-801. The system was checked serviceable for revenue flight.

CN-RGC, a Boeing 787-8 aircraft operated by Royal Air Maroc, was conducting IFR flight RAM208 from Casablanca/Mohammed V Intl, Morocco (GMMN) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). During the descent upon arrival at CYUL, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to a damaged window. The aircraft landed on Runway 24R without further incident and taxied to the gate normally.

C-GXJZ, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting IFR flight JZA7972 from Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City, ON (CYTZ) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) with 3 crew members and 47 passengers on board. During the taxi phase after the landing at CYUL, the flight attendant noticed a burning electrical smell in the cabin. Shortly after, the flight crew noticed the electrical smell as well and turned the recirculation fan to the ON position; the intensity of the smell decreased. The flight crew requested assistance from Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) services who conducted a visual inspection of the aircraft. Use of thermal cameras did not reveal any sign of fire or smoke. Passengers deplaned normally.

C-FMSX, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA712 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to New York/La Guardia, NY (KLGA) with 5 crew members and 140 passengers on board. When the aircraft was on short final for Runway 31 at KLGA, the flight crew received a TCAS RA which was triggered by a helicopter. The flight crew executed a missed approach, returned for a second approach, and landed without further incident.

C-FYJD, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG516 from Cancún Intl, Mexico (MMUN) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 6 crew members and 162 passengers on board. As the flight was being vectored around weather during cruise flight at FL350, just to the east of Pittsburgh Intl, PA (KPIT), the flight crew was informed of a strong electrical burning smell from an aft lavatory. Approximately 20 minutes later, a PAN PAN was declared and a direct routing to CYYZ was requested. The aircraft then landed without further incident on Runway 33L. The flight crew coordinated the taxi in with ARFF following as precaution.The operator’s maintenance inspected the lavatory and found no faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FKCJ, a Boeing 757-236 aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd., was conducting flight CJT570 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) to Montreal/Mirabel Intl, QC (CYMX). During the climb through FL280 there was a strong odour of smoke in the cockpit and the crew elected to return to CYWG. During the descent, the crew ran the checklist items and declared an emergency. The smoke odour dissipated briefly but returned a short time later. The smoke odour was not bad enough to require donning of oxygen masks or smoke goggles. The subsequent landing was uneventful with ARFF responding as the aircraft taxied to the apron. The crew did not require medical attention.Subsequent inspections, operational checks, and engine ground runs by the operator's maintenance personnel did not reveal the source of the smoke odour. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYQT, a Fairchild SA227-AC aircraft operated by Bearskin Airlines, was conducting flight BLS373 from Sault Ste. Marie, ON (CYAM) to Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT) with 2 crew members and 14 passengers on board. As the flight crew was positioning the aircraft for takeoff at CYAM, smoke was noticed in the back of the cabin. The flight crew declared an emergency and started the evacuation. Emergency vehicles met the aircraft, however there were no signs of fire.The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and found that the left hand cooling turbine had an excessive oil residue on the exterior. It was suspected that an internal seal failed, allowing oil to enter the air passage of the cooling turbine which caused oily smoke to enter cabin via the air conditioning ducts.

C-GNWI, a Cessna 208 aircraft operated by Northway Aviation, had departed Little Grand Rapids, MB (CZGR) for Winnipeg/St. Andrews, MB (CYAV). Upon touchdown on Runway 18 at CYAV, the brakes failed and the aircraft veered left onto the grass adjacent to the runway. There was no damage as a result of the runway excursion, and no injuries. The runway was closed for approximately 20 minutes while the aircraft was towed to the operator's hangar.The operator's maintenance conducted a subsequent inspection and found that the brake bleeder screws were loose. The brake bleeder screws were tightened, the brake system was checked serviceable and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GWUX, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA689 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl, SK (CYXE) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). During cruise flight, a flight attendant experienced a medical incident. The flight crew was advised and the flight attendant’s duties were distributed to the remaining flight attendants for the landing.

On 14 June 2018, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA113 from Calgary, Alberta, to Vancouver, British Columbia, with 53 passengers and 5 crew members on board. While climbing through 9000 feet after departure, the flight crew received a cargo fire warning. An emergency was declared and a return to Calgary was requested. After landing, the cargo hold was inspected and evidence was found of a fire in passenger baggage.UPDATED: 19 May 2020

C-GTQF, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC127 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau, QC (CYUL) with 6 crew members and 136 passengers on board. During cruise flight at FL370 in the vicinity of Marathon, ON (CYSP), the flight crew received a SOURCE OFF indication for the number 1 Integrated Drive Generator (IDG). The flight crew executed the QRH procedures, which included starting the Auxilary Power Unit (APU). However, the APU failed to start and, since only one source of electricity was now available, the flight crew declared an emergency and initiated a diversion to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). The aircraft descended to FL250, and the flight crew was able to start the APU at that altitude. The emergency was cancelled, and the flight continued to CYUL where it landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance placed the number 1 IDG on MEL and returned the aircraft to service.

C-GCRU, a Bell 429 helicopter operated by the Canadian Coast Guard, was conducting external load operations to the Popes Harbour light from the shore at Popes Harbour, NS. While in transit slinging lumber, the load began to spin as the helicopter reached an airspeed of about 45 knots. Several boards from the slung load of lumber slipped out of the rigging and fell into the ocean near the intended drop site. No damage to the sling gear was noted, and no injury or aircraft damage occurred.Transport Canada Aircraft Services Directorate is conducting an investigation.

C-GAAT, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Services, was conducting flight EVS7791 from St. John's Intl, NL (CYYT) to Deer Lake, NL (CYDF). During the approach to CYDF, the flight crew noted that the nose landing gear did not indicate green (down and locked) after the landing gear was selected to the extended position. The flight crew reported the condition to air traffic services and requested that emergency vehicles be on stand by for the landing. A low overflight provided information that the landing gear appeared to be fully down.
