The flight crew switched light bulbs within the landing gear position display and determined that the nose landing gear was indicating down and locked; the aircraft then landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft and replaced bulbs that were burnt out in the landing gear position indication display.

TF-LLX, a Boeing 757-200 aircraft operated by Icelandair, was conducting flight ICE696 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Reykjavík/Keflavík, Iceland (BIKF) with 6 crew members and 120 passengers on board.  As the flight was about to reach its assigned flight level of FL350 after the departure from CYVR, the flight crew declared an emergency due to a left engine (Rolls Royce RB211-535E4-37/24B) overheat message. The QRH was executed and a return to CYVR was requested. The flight crew shut the left engine down as the overheat warning did not go out with the thrust lever at idle. The aircraft landed without further incident at 2350Z with ARFF on standby.After the landing, maintenance personnel performed an overweight inspection and no issues were found. The left engine was inspected, and high pressure bleed ducts HP2 and HP6, as well as heating system (HS) pilot were replaced. Following testing and run-up in accordance with B757 Aircraft Maintenance Manual 36-11-01, the aircraft was released back to service.

N787AL, a Boeing 777-200 aircraft operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL71 from Frankfurt/Rhein-Main, Germany (EDDF) to Chicago/O’Hare Intl, IL (KORD). During cruise flight 21 nm East of Iroquois Falls, ON (CNE4), the flight crew noticed a high oil consumption on the number 1 engine. The flight crew declared an emergency and the flight was cleared direct to KORD.

C-GHJW, a Sikorsky S-76A helicopter operated by Helijet International, was conducting VFR flight JBA851 between Vancouver/Harbour (Public), BC (CBC7) and Victoria Harbour (Camel Point), BC (CBF7) with 2 crew members and 12 passengers on board. During the descent to CBF7, the flight crew received an intermittent number 1 engine (Allison 250-C30S) fire annunciator warning light. ATC was notified and the flight crew elected to divert to Victoria Intl, BC (CYYJ) where they landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. After landing, ARFF escorted the aircraft to the gate. The operator’s maintenance was dispatched to CYYJ to inspect the helicopter’s fire warning system. An inspection of the aft fire detector cannon plug showed it was full of water and was the source of the false indication. The plug was cleaned out and an operational check of the system was carried out satisfactorily. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTSW, un appareil de type Airbus 310-304 exploité par Air Transat, effectuait le vol TSC729 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Londres/Gatwick, UK (EGKK) vers Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 218 passagers et 9 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors qu’il se trouvait en vol de croisière au niveau de vol FL360, à environ 200 miles marins au nord-est de Mont-Joli, QC (CYYY), l’appareil a rencontré de la turbulence modérée à sévère. La perte de contrôle momentanée a causé une montée de 400 pieds, suivie d’une descente de 700 pieds, soit 300 pieds sous l’altitude de croisière assignée. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’inspection post envolée n’a révélé aucun dommage à l’appareil.

C-GGOI, un Dash-8-402 (DH8D) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8906, effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) à destination de Moncton/Greater Moncton International, NB (CYQM) avec 56 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage. Alors que l’appareil se trouvait à 18 milles nautiques est-nord-est de Sherbrooke, QC, en croisière au niveau de vol 250, une dépressurisation est survenue. L’équipage a effectué une descente d’urgence et a poursuivi le vol à destination à 10 000 pieds, où l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-GSKW, un Beechcraft B1900C exploité par Skylink Express Inc. effectuait un vol cargo selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal Intl Mirabel (CYMX), QC à destination de l’aéroport de Québec Jean Lesage (CYQB), QC avec 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Lorsque l’appareil était en approche finale de la piste 06, l’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence en raison d’une indication anormale du train d’atterrissage gauche. L’appareil s'est posé sans encombre et les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés. L’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage et il n’y a eu aucun blessé. L’inspection post envolé a établi que l’ampoule de l’indication du train gauche était brulée.

C-GONJ, a Bombardier DHC-8-102 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8327 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Sault Ste. Marie, ON (CYAM) with 3 crew members and 33 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew felt a bump which was followed by a nose landing gear unsafe indication. After contacting the operator’s maintenance, the flight crew elected to return to CYYZ and declared an emergency. During the approach, the alternate landing gear extension was executed and the aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance performed several landing gear operations without being able to duplicate the fault. As a precaution, the Proximity Switch Electronics Unit (PSEU) and nose landing gear down lock sensor were replaced and the aircraft was returned to service. No further nose landing gear faults were reported on subsequent flights.

C-GPWE, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting IFR flight WEN3226 from Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl, SK (CYXE). WEN3226 was approximately 6 nautical miles northwest of CYXE, and descending on the KEBRU4 arrival for Runway 27. At approximately 8000 feet ASL, a TCAS traffic advisory alerted the flight crew to conflicting traffic followed by a TCAS resolution advisory (RA) to stop the descent. Conflicting traffic was C-GCSC, a Cessna 182 operated by Skydive Saskatoon, that was climbing through 6000 feet ASL for 10 000 feet ASL under VFR.  WEN3226 notified ATC of the TCAS RA and advised ATC the aircraft was stopping the descent. ATC advised to continue the descent to 7500 feet; however, the flight crew rejected the instructions and indicated WEN3226 would follow the TCAS RA. C-GCSC passed below WEN3226 by approximately 500 feet vertically. When WEN3226 was clear of the traffic, the descent was continued to Runway 27 for an uneventful landing. As one aircraft was VFR and the other IFR, no loss of separation occurred.

C-FWEZ, a Westjet Encore de Havilland DHC-8-400, was operating as WEN3258 from Edmonton, AB (CYEG) to Yellowknife, NT (CYZF). During the take-off roll on Runway 02, the number 3 tire of the main landing gear failed. During the initial climb the flight crew declared a MAYDAY emergency and returned to CYEG and landed uneventfully. The aircraft received damage to the right refuel/defuel panel and right main landing gear doors.

C-FPWC, a privately registered Piper PA-32-300 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Saskatoon/Corman Air Park, SK (CJN5) to Cree Lake/Crystal Lodge (Midgett Field), SK (CKS8) with only the pilot on board. During cruise flight, the pilot encountered a low ceiling and elected to turn back to CJN5. Approximately 95 nm from the destination, the engine (Avco Lycoming IO-540-K1A5) began to lose power. The pilot elected to conduct a precautionary landing onto a road and, upon touchdown, the aircraft pulled to the left and struck a sign post as the aircraft entered a ditch. During the ensuing skid, the nose landing gear collapsed, and the aircraft came to rest in an adjacent field. The pilot was uninjured, however the aircraft sustained substantial damage. The ELT did not activate and there was no fire.

GGN7372, a Bombardier CRJ200 aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was taxiing for take-off at Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ), and was instructed by ground control to hold short of Taxiway D4. The tower controller observed GGN7372 cross the hold short line at Taxiway D4 and instructed ROU1811, an Airbus 321 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge on final approach, to execute a missed approach.

C-FZRM, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1447 from Las Vegas/McCarran Intl, NV (KLAS) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG). During the approach into CYEG, WJA1447 was given the number 1 sequence via the RNAV Runway 12, and to intercept TULID at 7000 feet ASL. C-GFCD, a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Sunwest Aviation, was conducting flight CNK9403 from Conklin (Leismer), AB (CET2) to CYEG. CNK9403 had been authorized to descend down to 8000 feet ASL. A loss of separation occurred when the two aircraft came within 2.7 nm horizontally and 900 feet vertically of each other, where 3 nm or 1000 feet is required.

C-GJZX, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA584 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl, SK (CYXE). Upon arrival in CYXE, JZA584 was unable to land due to thunderstorms. As the planned alternate airport was Regina Intl, SK (CYQR) 130 nm to the South East, the flight crew evaluated that they could not get around the thunderstorms and made a request to the operator’s dispatch to change the alternate to CYYC. The operator’s dispatch produced a revised flight plan, which indicated that the aircraft had the required fuel on board to use CYYC as the new alternate. The flight crew then initiated the diversion to CYYC, however a fuel emergency was declared while on descent and the aircraft landed without further incident. The fuel on arrival was planned to be 1546 lbs; JZA584 landed with 1390 lbs of fuel remaining.

C-FOTX, a float equipped, amateur built, MAC CUB M1 aircraft (Piper PA18 replica), was departing Lake Huron, near Bruce Mines, ON. After take-off when the aircraft was about 200 feet AGL, the engine (Avco Lycoming, O-290-D2) lost power. Due to the perceived obstacles ahead, the pilot turned back toward the lake. An aerodynamic stall ensued, and the pilot lost control of the aircraft. The aircraft impacted the water in a steep nose down attitude, flipped over and became submerged in shallow water. The pilot, who was wearing a shoulder harness, was not injured and was able to egress the aircraft.

C-FRZE, un Cessna 182R exploité par Grondair, effectuait un vol de patrouille de feu selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Val d’Or, QC (CYVO) avec seul un pilote à bord. En croisière, le pilote remarque que l’alternateur ne charge pas la batterie et décide de revenir à CYVO. Au retour, la radio ne fonctionnait plus, donc le pilote communique avec Rouyn Radio par téléphone, déclare un état d’urgence et avise qu’il revient à CYVO sans radio. La procédure d’extension manuelle des roues est utilisée et l’appareil se pose avec les volets rentrés sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-FNOE, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA043 from New Delhi/Indira Gandhi Intl, India (VIDP) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 14 crew members and 297 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the aircraft experienced a number 1 engine (GE GENX-1B74/75/P2) flame out. The flight crew successfully conducted an engine restart, declared an emergency and diverted to Moscow/Domodedovo Intl, Russia (UUDD) where it landed without further incident. The Aircraft Incident Investigation Division within the Federal Air Transport Agency (FATA) is not conducting an ICAO Annex 13 investigation about this incident. The operator’s maintenance found a loose connector at the Fuel Metering Unit (FMU). The connector was tightened and an engine run was performed. No further faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFJL, un Cessna 310R exploité par Grondair Aviation, effectuait un vol d’aéropointage dans le cadre d’une opération d’extinction de feu de forêt selon les règles de vol à vue depuis l'aéroport de Val d’Or, QC (CYVO) avec un pilote et un coordinateur des opérations à bord. Lors du retour à environ 12 miles marins au sud-ouest de CYVO, la pression d’huile du moteur droit (Teledyne Continental IO-520-MB) a diminué à son minimum opérationnel et le pilote a fermé le moteur. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 36 sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-FWXJ, a privately registered, float equipped Cessna A185E aircraft, was landing at Crooked Lake, ON. During the flare, it was reported that a violent wind shear occurred. The aircraft touched down in a nose-down attitude, the front of the floats dug into the water, and the aircraft flipped over. The aircraft was submerged, however was held afloat by the aircraft floats. Both occupants were wearing inflatable personal flotation devices (PFD's) and seat belts equipped with shoulder harnesses; both egressed the aircraft safely. The pilot had previously received floatplane egress training.

C-FZJA, un CL-600-2B19 (CRJ2) exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8827, effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport Ronald Reagan Washington National aux États-Unis (KDCA) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL) avec 46 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage. Alors que l’appareil circulait au sol après l’atterrissage, un autre avion a rapporté apercevoir de la fumée qui provenait des roues du train d’atterrissage droit ainsi qu’une crevaison. L’équipage a immobilisé le JZA8827 dans l’aire de dégivrage et il a été rejoint par les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA). Aucun feu ne s’est déclaré, l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage. Les passagers ont été acheminés au terminal par autobus et il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FEKR, a privately registered Cessna 140 aircraft, departed from Deep River/Rolph, ON (CPH2) for a local flight. The aircraft was approximately 5 nm East of CPH2 when the engine (Teledyne Continental C-90-14F) began to lose power, and subsequently completely stopped. The pilot elected to ditch the aircraft into the river. The aircraft came to rest in about 8 feet of water and sustained substantial damage. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was not injured.

C-GNLW, un appareil de type Boeing 737-200 exploité par Les Investissements Nolinor, effectuait le vol NRL796 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal Intl (Mirabel), QC (CYMX) à destination d’Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) avec 3 membres d’équipage et aucun passager à bord. Lorsque les volets ont été sélectionnés à la position « Flaps 1 » en approche initiale à CYFB, les volets sont restés immobiles et l’équipage a effectué une approche interrompue. L’équipage a ensuite effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH), a déclaré un état d’urgence et a exécuté une deuxième approche avec les volets à la position « Flaps 15 ». L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 34 sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage. L’inspection par le technicien d'entretien de l'avion a révélé une fuite d’une conduite hydraulique du système « A ».

C-GGJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (CRJ200) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was operating flight JZA825 from Washington/Ronald Reagan National, DC (KDCA) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). When the flight crew selected flaps up shortly after the departure from KDCA, a FLAP FAIL caution message was received. The QRH was executed, and the flight crew requested a return to KDCA. An emergency was declared due to the higher approach speed. There was no injuries to the occupants and no damage to the aircraft.

C-GTSD, an Airbus 330-300 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC318 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Lisbon/Aeroporto da Portela de Sacavem, Portugal (LPPT) with 10 crew members and 316 passengers on board. During cruise flight approximately 180 nm East of CYUL, the aircraft experienced a hydraulic leak in the green system. The flight crew executed all ECAM actions and QRH checklist items, and declared an emergency. A return to CYUL was also requested where the aircraft landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance replaced a union and an O ring on the Green System High Pressure Filter Manifold. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-FGKZ, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA338 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW) with 6 crew members and 178 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure, the landing gear failed to retract. The flight crew advised ATC, declared a Pan Pan and returned for landing at CYVR. An overweight landing was accomplished without further incident with ARFF standing by. Subsequent maintenance actions revealed that the nose landing gear oleo had been over-serviced with hydraulic fluid. Maintenance personnel accomplished a nose landing gear service as per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) and the aircraft was returned to service.

N804NW, an Airbus 330-300 aircraft operated by Delta Airlines, was conducting flight DAL75 from Amsterdam/Schiphol, Netherlands (EHAM) to Atlanta/Hartsfield-Jackson Intl, GA (KATL) with 13 crew members and 293 passengers on board. While in cruise flight, the flight crew reported vibrations in the number 1 engine, which exceeded 10 units. The vibrations ceased when the power was reduced to idle. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and diverted to Goose Bay, NL (CYYR) where the flight landed without further incident with the number 1 engine remaining at idle. Maintenance personnel observed metal in the tailpipe and proceeded to change the engine. The faulty engine was sent for examination and failure identification. The aircraft was released back to service.

C-GWOX, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG843 from Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT) to Sioux Lookout, ON (CYXL) with 2 crew members and 18 passengers on board. When the landing gear was selected down during the final approach for Runway 34 at CYXL, the flight crew did not receive a nose gear down-and-locked indication. A missed approach was conducted and the flight crew completed the associated checklists, including the landing gear manual extension. However, the nose landing gear down-and-locked indication remained unlit. After conducting a fly-by where the nose landing gear was reported to be down, the flight crew requested that emergency services be placed on standby for the landing. Upon touchdown on Runway 34 after the subsequent approach, both engines were shut down as a precautionary measure and the aircraft came to a stop on the runway. The aircraft was then towed to the gate.The operator's maintenance inspection revealed that the nose landing gear indication bulbs were not illuminating. The bulbs were replaced, gear functionality was checked, a test flight was conducted, and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GYZK, a float-equipped Cessna 180K aircraft operated by Georgian Bay Airways, was taking off from Parry Sound Harbor, ON (CPS1) with one pilot and three passengers for a sightseeing tour. During the take-off run, the aircraft veered left and the left wing struck a harbor marker. The take-off was aborted, however the left wing was substantially damaged. There were no injuries to the occupants.

N37018, a Boeing 777-200 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL19 from Newark/Liberty Intl, NJ (KEWR) to Milan/Malpensa, Italy (LIMC) with 14 crew members and 251 passengers on board. While in cruise flight approximately 100 nm South West of Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ), the flight crew noted a decreasing oil pressure on the number 2 engine. An emergency was declared and the flight crew requested to divert to CYHZ where an uneventful landing was conducted. Engine power was reduced and remained at idle until the aircraft was clear of the runway, at which time it was shut down. Maintenance personnel determined that the starter on the number 2 engine had failed and was leaking oil at the gearbox pad. The number 2 engine starter was replaced and the aircraft was released back to service.

C-FRSO, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA844 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Frankfurt/Rhein-Main, Germany (EDDF) with 11 crew members and 196 passengers on board. During cruise flight at position N5940/W4626, approximately 550 nm North East of Goose Bay, NL (CYYR), the flight crew noted a loss of oil in the number 1 engine. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and requested a diversion to CYYR. The power on the engine was reduced to idle where it remained until the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance determined that the L2 Variable Frequency Starter Generator (VFSG) was leaking oil due to O rings damage on the shaft and the carbon seal. After the VFSG and the carbon seal were replaced, a successful leak check was carried out. Subsequently, the aircraft was released back to service.

C-GRHW, a Bell 205A-1 aircraft operated by Remote Helicopters, was conducting forest fire suppression operation South West of Loon River, AB (CFS6). When the pilot tried to release the load of water on fire SWF053, the water, bucket and longline were all released from the helicopter. No one was injured in the incident. Repairs to the long line and bucket wiring in the cargo hook area were carried out.

C-GSZL, a privately registered Yakovlev Yak-55M aircraft, was landing at Rocky Mountain House, AB (CYRM), when directional control was lost on the landing rollout. The aircraft rolled up onto its left main landing gear, allowing the left wingtip to strike the ground. Subsequently, the aircraft came to rest on its nose and was substantially damaged. The pilot was uninjured.

C-FYIP, a Hughes 369D aircraft operated by Bighorn Helicopters, was conducting external load operations approximately 1 nm North East of Elko/Lionel P. Demers Memorial Airpark, BC (CBE2) when the external load inadvertently released from the sling and flew back into the tail rotor. The pilot felt a vibration, entered autorotation, and made an emergency landing into a meadow. After touchdown, the main rotor contacted the tail boom, causing substantial damage. The pilot was uninjured.

C-FAJV, an Embraer EMB-505 Phenom 300 aircraft operated by Aurora Jet Partners, was departing on a flight from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG). Shortly after becoming airborne out of CYYC, the aircraft experienced a bird strike while climbing through 400 feet above ground. An emergency was declared, the aircraft remained in the circuit, and a landing was carried out on Runway 17R with ARFF attending. A subsequent inspection revealed traces of bird remains on the left forward windscreen. However, there were no damage to the aircraft.

C-FHNO, un appareil de type Cessna 172L exploité par Dorval Aviation, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue avec un élève-pilote à son bord qui effectuait des posé-décollés sur la piste 20 à Saint-Jean, QC (CYJN). Lors du troisième atterrissage, l’appareil s’est posé durement et a rebondi 2 fois. La roue de nez s'est détachée du train d'atterrissage, causant un impact de l'hélice avec le sol. L'avion s'est immobilisé et l'élève-pilote n'a pas été blessé. L'appareil a subi des dommages importants.

C-FFCE, a privately operated Aerospatiale AS 355 F2 helicopter, was on a local flight from Langley Regional, BC (CYNJ) to the Pitt Lake, BC area with the pilot and one passenger on board. The aircraft was landing on a forestry road and, as the aircraft touched down, the pilot lost control. The rotor blades contacted the ground and the aircraft rolled onto its side. The pilot and passenger sustained minor injuries and were able to egress the helicopter. The helicopter was substantially damaged.

C-GKDX, an L-23 Super Blanik glider operated by Edmonton Soaring Club, was doing a solo training flight at Chipman, AB (CFU3). Since the aircraft was high on the downwind leg, the student-pilot activated the  spoilers to assist the descent. However, the aircraft remained above the desired approach path throughout the approach, leading to a landing that was well above optimal landing speed. The aircraft touched down well down the runway, rolled off the end through a ditch, then over a road and finally came to rest in a field. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. The pilot was uninjured.

C-FHEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3329 from Kelowna, BC (CYLW) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 4 crew members and 28 passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff from CYLW, the flight crew observed the Landing Gear Inop caution light. The flight crew actioned the QRH and advised the operator’s operational and maintenance control centres. The decision was made to continue to CYVR. A Pan Pan was declared, and the aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident with ARFF standing by. Subsequent maintenance actions revealed that the nose landing gear proximity sensor was out of rig.

C-GJEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3183 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Victoria Intl, BC (CYYJ) with 4 crew members and 68 passengers on board. While on approach to CYYJ, the Flap Power caution light triggered when the flaps were selected. The flight crew actioned the QRH and decided to return to CYVR due to the availability of a longer runway. A Pan Pan was declared and the aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident with ARFF standing by. Subsequent maintenance actions resulted in the replacement of the flap power unit pressure switch.

C-GWQH, a privately registered Cessna A150L aircraft, was on a VFR flight from Ottawa/Carp, ON (CYRP) to North Bay, ON (CYYB) with 2 persons on board. As the aircraft was flying at an altitude of 4500 feet ASL over a remote area of Algonquin Park, ON, the engine (Teledyne Continental O-200-A) partially lost power. Subsequently, the engine completely stopped. The pilot declared MAYDAY and then executed a forced landing in a marshy area. During the touchdown, the nose wheel dug into soft ground and the aircraft nosed-over. The aircraft came to rest inverted and was substantially damaged. The pilot and the passenger received minor injuries. A search and rescue aircraft was dispatched from the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) in Trenton, ON and rescued the occupants.

C-FWSF, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1541 from Houston/George Bush Intercontinental, TX (KIAH) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). C-FTJS, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA321 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to CYYC. WJA1541 was assigned the TASBU arrival into CYYC, while ACA321 was assigned the BIRKO 3 STAR via LIBUX. As both aircraft were being routed for Runway 35R, a loss of separation occurred. The two aircraft came within 2.5 nm horizontally and 500 feet vertically where 3 nm or 1000 feet was required. Both aircraft landed without incident and there was no other impact to operations.

C-FRYP, un appareil de type Cessna R182 exploité par Grondin Transport, effectuait un vol local pour la SOPFEU selon les règles de vol à vue depuis St-Frédéric, QC (CSZ4) avec 2 personnes à bord. Lors de l'atterrissage au retour, le pilote a perdu la maîtrise de l'avion et a effectué une sortie de piste vers la gauche. L'avion a traversé un fossé et s'est immobilisé sur une butte. Les 2 occupants n'ont pas été blessés. L'avion a subi des dommages importants.

C-GJBQ, un appareil de type Beech A100 exploité par Strait Air, effectuait le vol NUK105T pour de la formation dans le circuit à Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) avec seulement 2 membres d’équipage à bord. C-FAIP, un appareil de type Beech A100 exploité par Air Inuit, effectuait le vol AIE527 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Schefferville, QC (CYKL) à destination de CYZV avec 3 passagers et 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Lors du contact initial sur la fréquence obligatoire de CYZV, AIE527 a avisé qu’il procèdait depuis sa position au nord pour une approche contact par la gauche pour la piste 09, derrière un DHC-8 également en approche pour la piste 09. Lorsque NUK105T était en vent arrière piste 09 à 1200 pieds ASL, l’équipage a annoncé son intention de suivre le DHC-8 qui était sur le point d’atterrir. À ce moment, AIE527 se trouvait en base gauche étendu pour la piste 09. Les tentatives de réconciliation du trafic afin d’établir l’ordre d’atterrissage n’ont pas fonctionné. AIE527 est monté à 1800 pieds ASL et a vu NUK105T quelques secondes avant de le croiser sur une trajectoire quasi perpendiculaire, environ 300 pieds en-dessous. Les 2 appareils se sont posés sans encombre, il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage. NAV CANADA effectue une enquête interne.

C-GMON, a Bombardier DHC-8-301 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8427 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Kamloops, BC (CYKA) with 3 crew members and 40 passengers on board. While on approach to CYKA at 4000 feet AGL, the flight crew reported severe turbulence, which resulted in a momentary loss of control. One of the flight crew members sustained a minor injury. The aircraft landed at CYKA without further incident.

C-GMMX, a Diamond DA 20-C1 aircraft operated by Canlink Aviation/Moncton Flight College, was conducting a cross country training flight from Fredericton Intl, NB (CYFC) with planned stops at Grand Manan, NB (CCN2) and Saint John,NB (CYSJ), before returning to CYFC. As the pilot was attempting to practice soft field take-off technique from Runway 15, the aircraft rolled to the left after take-off and the left wing struck the runway surface, causing the aircraft to exit the left side of the runway. The wind was reported to be variable from 170°-190° at 10 knots. The pilot was uninjured, however the aircraft was destroyed.

C-GFIQ, a float-equipped de Havilland DHC-2 MK. I aircraft operated by Elk Island Air, was conducting training circuits at Selkirk, MB waterdrome (CKC5). During one of the landings, the right front float tip dug into the water surface. The aircraft's right wing subsequently contacted the water, however the aircraft remained upright. The aircraft's right wing and aileron sustained damage. There were no injuries to the two occupants. The aircraft has been removed from service pending repairs.

C-GRHJ, an Aerospatiale AS 350 B-2 aircraft operated by Remote Helicopters, was conducting bucketing operations in support of forest fire suppression, 10 nm North of Calling Lake, AB (CFK4). While lifting the bucket from a water source, the engine (Avco Lycoming LTS-101-700D-2) experienced compressor stalls, followed by an engine deceleration. The engine RPM recovered during the landing on the shore of the lake.The operator’s maintenance replaced the power turbine governor and engine air flow modulator actuator before flying the aircraft back to CFK4.

C-FINB, an Aerospatiale-Alenia ATR 72-202 aircraft operated by Calm Air International, was conducting flight CAV771 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) to Sudbury, ON (CYSB). After levelling off at cruise altitude after the departure from CYWG, the low oil-pressure annunciator for the number 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW124B) began to flicker. The flight crew referenced the QRH low oil-pressure checklist. The oil pressure continued to decrease and the flight crew proceeded with the memory items for engine shutdown. The QRH checklist items were completed as the Master Caution light illuminated. The flight crew elected to return to CYWG and declared an emergency, advising ATC of the engine shutdown. The subsequent landing was made with one engine inoperative and ARFF standing by.Subsequent inspection by the operator's maintenance found the oil cap not properly secured on the number 1 engine. The chip detectors were inspected, as well as the oil filters were removed and inspected, with no faults found. Engine ground runs were completed and tested serviceable. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GOPW, a Boeing 737-200 aircraft operated by Canadian North, was conducting flight MPE9045 from Inuvik (Mike Zubko), NT (CYEV) to Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) with only 3 crew members on board. During the climb through FL250, the flight crew observed that the oil temperature for the number 1 engine (Pratt and Whitney - USA JT8D-17) had exceeded the upper limit. The flight crew executed the appropriate QRH, shut the engine down, declared an emergency and diverted into Normal Wells, NT (CYVQ) where an uneventful single-engine approach and landing was conducted.

C-FSRZ, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA153 from Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). During cruise flight, one of the flight attendants became unable to perform their duties. A dead heading flight crew member was designated an able body person for the landing.

C-GGCI, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8214 from Prince George, BC (CYXS) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 4 crew members and 17 passengers on board. While on approach to CYVR, the number 1 hydraulic system failed. The flight crew declared an emergency and landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance replaced the number 1 engine driven hydraulic pump. Additionally, the number 1 system pressure manifold, return manifold and number 1 case drain manifold filters were replaced. Engine runs were completed and the number 1 EDP functioned with no leaks. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-GMAN, a Rockwell Intl Aero Commander 690B aircraft operated by MAG Aerospace Canada, was conducting a Bird Dog operation from Red Lake, ON (CYRL) in support of aerial suppression of Red Lake Fire 23, 2.5 nautical miles North East of Pikangikum, ON (CYPM). The aircraft interior began to get warm regardless of the climate control selections and an odour and haze began to fill the cabin. The flight crew notified the Air Attack Officer that there was smoke in the cabin and that they needed to leave the wildfire. The flight crew depressurized the cabin, at which point the odour and haze cleared. The flight crew consulted the QRH and elected to continue to Red Lake, ON (CYRL).The operator's maintenance determined that the Blower Motor isolation switch was in the OFF position, allowing the climate control system to overheat. The switch, intended for use by maintenance personnel, is in a non-standard and exposed location on this particular aircraft. The switch has since been witness-wired to prevent inadvertent operation.

C-GNYH, a Bell 407 aircraft operated by Yellowhead Helicopters, was commencing water bucketing operations approximately 46 nm North West of Mackenzie, BC (CYZY) when the longline and bucket inadvertently released from the helicopter. Subsequent maintenance inspection revealed that the manual release cable was kinked.

C-GJEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3417 from Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT) to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG). Following landing gear retraction on departure, an unsafe nose landing gear (not retracted) indication was received. The flight crew requested radar vectors and to level off at 4000 feet while they actioned the QRH. An emergency was declared and a return to CYQT was requested. Prior to the landing, the Alternate Landing Gear Extension procedure was completed and the aircraft landed on Runway 07 with emergency vehicles standing by.The operator's maintenance replaced the nose landing gear door actuator and the landing gear system was checked serviceable. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKQE, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE388 from Chicago/Midway Intl, IL (KMDW) to Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City, ON (CYTZ) with 4 crew members and 41 passengers on board. During the approach into CYTZ, the flight crew noted that the number 2 hydraulic system quantity was indicating 25%. When the landing gear was selected down, the system dropped lower to 20%. The flight crew informed ATC to check the runway for hydraulic fluid after the aircraft lands. During the landing rollout, numerous caution lights associated with the hydraulic system illuminated. The aircraft was taxied clear of the runway and both engines were shut down. ARFF met the aircraft and confirmed hydraulic fluid leaking from the nose landing gear area. The aircraft was then towed to the gate.The operator’s maintenance found a flexible hydraulic line leaking on the nose landing gear.

C-GGDC, a Mitsubishi MU-2B-60 aircraft operated by Thunder Airlines, was conducting flight THU880 from Sudbury, ON (CYSB) to Earlton (Timiskaming Regional), ON (CYXR). Following the takeoff from CYSB, the landing gear retracted normally, however the red light remained illuminated, indicating that the landing gear door(s) were still open. The flight crew reduced the airspeed and cycled the landing gear down, at which time a shear pin broke and the front landing gear doors did not open. A manual landing gear extension was conducted, and the flight crew received the green down and locked indication. The flight returned to CYSB and ARFF was requested for an uneventful landing.

C-FIJA, un appareil de type Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA820 à partir d’Hamilton, ON (CYHM) vers Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 20 passagers à bord. Alors qu’il était en approche à CYUL, un membre du personnel de cabine a signalé à l'équipage de conduite une alarme sonore inhabituelle. Aucune indication anormale n’était apparente dans le poste de pilotage. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil s’est posé sans problème à CYUL. La source de l'alarme a été identifiée comme provenant d'un appareil électronique appartenant à un des passagers.

On 16 May 2018, an Air Transat Airbus A310-304 aircraft (registration C-GFAT, serial number 545), operating as flight 485 (TSC485), was conducting an instrument flight rules flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson International Airport, Ontario, to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport, Quebec. At about the same time, a privately owned Cessna 421-B aircraft (registration C-GADG, serial number 421B0802) conducting an instrument flight rules flight, was returning to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport from Trois-Rivières Airport, Quebec. The Airbus was inbound from the west, and its flight path would take it north of the airport to commence an approach to land on Runway 24R. The Cessna was inbound from the northeast to commence an approach to land on Runway 24L. At 1901:17 Eastern Daylight Time, when the aircraft were approximately 18 nautical miles northeast of Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport, a loss of separation occurred. Neither the required vertical separation minimum of 1000 feet nor the lateral separation minimum of 3 nautical miles was maintained. When the loss of separation occurred, they were 200 feet and 2.8 nautical miles from each other. At the closest point, the 2 aircraft came within 500 feet vertically and 1.7 nautical miles laterally of each other. At 1902:22, following instructions from the controllers, the required separation was re-established, and the 2 aircraft landed without incident.

C-GJZH, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA8917 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) à Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 78 passagers à bord. L'aéronef était à son altitude de croisière au FL240, à environ 47 miles marins au nord-ouest de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL), lorsqu'il y a eu survitesse de l'hélice du moteur droit. L'équipage de conduite a effectué la liste de vérification applicable et a fermé le moteur (PWC PW150A). Une urgence a été déclarée et l'aéronef a dérouté vers CYUL où il s'est posé sans problème.

C-GTCO, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-100 exploité par Air Creebec, effectuait le vol CRQ927 de Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) vers Chisasibi, QC (CSU2) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 4 passagers à son bord. Alors qu’il circulait au sol à CSU2 en vue de se stationner, le bout de son aile droite est entré en collision avec l'aile droite de C-GXCN, un autre DHC-8-100 du même exploitant aérien, qui était stationné. Personne ne se trouvait à bord du C-GXCN lors de la collision. Les 2 appareils ont subi des dommages mineurs aux extrémités des ailes. Personne n'a été blessé.

C-GVAL, a privately operated Piper PA-28-140 aircraft, was on a pleasure flight from Calgary/Okotoks Air Park, AB (CFX2) to High River, AB (CEN4). During the landing on Runway 25 at CEN4, the aircraft began to porpoise. On the fourth bounce, the nose landing gear failed, resulting in damage to the nose wheel assembly, firewall and propeller. The two occupants were uninjured.

C-FAWL, a privately operated amphibious float equipped Cessna 182R aircraft, was conducting a pleasure flight from Edmonton/Cooking Lake, AB (CEZ3) with only the pilot on board. While joining downwind for Runway 28 for a wheel landing at CEZ3, the pilot smelled an electrical burning odour. A short time later, black smoke was observed emanating from behind the rear cargo bulkhead. The pilot did not observe any abnormalities in the electrical system but elected to turn off the electrical master switch. The system was re-energized prior to landing in order to select full flaps, and the master switch was once again turned off. The smoke continued to increase until touchdown; touchdown was made with the wheels in the retracted position. The pilot evacuated the aircraft on the runway and, shortly after, the aircraft was engulfed in fire. The pilot received minor injuries while attempting to open the rear cargo door in order to discharge the fire extinguisher.

C-GOLM, a Cessna U206G aircraft operated by Mackenzie Mountain Aviation, was on a VFR flight from Fort Nelson, BC (CYYE) to Watson Lake, YT (CYQH). While established in cruise at 6500 feet ASL, the pilot became incapacitated. The aircraft descended 2500 feet and changed course approximately 270 degrees. Just prior to contacting a meadow on a ridge at 4000 feet ASL, the pilot was able to pitch the aircraft up enough that the main wheels contacted the meadow first. The aircraft bounced a few times prior to contacting some trees. The uninjured pilot exited the aircraft and contacted the company using a satellite phone. The pilot stayed with the aircraft overnight and was recovered the following morning by JRCC.

N692CA, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by SkyWest Airlines, was conducting flight SKW4137 from Philadelphia Intl, PA (KPHL) to Minneapolis-St. Paul Intl/Wold-Chamberlain, MN (KMSP). C-GHLT, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1804 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Montego Bay/Sangster Intl, Jamaica (MKJS) with 8 crew members and 234 passengers on board. While established in level flight at FL350 approximately 20 mns after the departure just west of Erie, PA, ROU1804 accepted and read back a clearance to climb to FL360 that was intended to ROU1802, which was on the same frequency. The mistake was not cognitively identified by ATC, and ROU1804 subsequently received a TCAS TA; the flight crew responded by reducing the rate of climb in order to mitigate the conflict. The separation between the two aircraft eroded to 2.72 nm laterally and 600 feet vertically, where 5 nm or 1000 feet is the requirement.

C-GKFF, a Convair 580F aircraft operated by Kelowna Flightcraft, was conducting flight KFA579 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Kamloops, BC (CYKA). Shortly after the departure from CYVR, the number 2 engine (Allison 501-D13D, s/n CAE500841) RPM began to increase above the normal range. The flight crew contacted ATC and requested vectors back to CYVR. During the return, the RPM began to decrease.  The flight crew performed a precautionary engine shutdown in accordance with the QRH and the operator’s SOPs. The aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by.  The operator’s maintenance replaced the propeller regulator.

C-FCJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 CRJ900 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8041 from Chicago/O'Hare Intl, IL (KORD) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 4 crew members and 75 passengers on board. While in cruise flight approximately 100 nm East of CYVR, the flight crew received the following messages: Rudder Limit Fault, Stall Fail, Mach Trim Caution and EFIS Comp Mon. The flight crew declared an emergency and landed without further incident at CYVR. The operator’s maintenance subsequently replaced the FWD Cabin Pressure Controller (which failed while troubleshooting) and the RH Air Data Computer. The P3 drain tube was discovered to be 2/3 full with water. The water was drained and a leak test was carried out. The MDC showed failure of the number 2 ADC. The component was replaced and tested. The rudder travel limit was also checked and found serviceable. All other messages were cleared in MDC and EICAS. No further faults were found and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FCJE, a Bombardier DHC-8-102 aircraft operated by Central Mountain Air, was conducting flight GLR758 from Prince George, BC (CYXS) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). Approximately 24 nm North of Pemberton, BC (CYPS), the flight crew observed a Master Warning indication, and a number 1 engine Oil Pressure caution light. The flight crew confirmed the low oil pressure with the analog gauge. The QRH was consulted and power was reduced on the number 1 engine (PWC PW121, S/N 121208). Shortly after the power reduction, the oil pressure dropped further. The flight crew subsequently shut the number 1 engine down as per company SOPs and QRH, and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident with ARFF standing by.  A post flight inspection revealed a substantial amount of oil on the lower portion of the number 1 engine.

HB-JHM, un appareil de type Airbus 330-300 exploité par Swiss International Air Lines, était stationné à la barrière 61 de l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) alors qu’un camion d’approvisionnement de nourriture a percuté le fuselage de l’appareil. Les dommages ont été limités à l’égratignure de la peinture et il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GLBW, a privately registered Cessna 180 aircraft, was enroute from North Battleford, SK (CYQW) to Moosomin/Marshall McLeod Field, SK (CJB5) with the pilot and one passenger on board. As the pilot flared the aircraft before touchdown on Runway 08 at CJB5, the aircraft dropped to the runway and bounced. The pilot elected to go around and applied full power. The aircraft veered to the right, and attempts to control the turn were unsuccessful. The aircraft continued to bank to the right and, as the pilot was about to regain control, the right wing struck the ground. The aircraft contacted the terrain and spun around. Both occupants had their seat belts and shoulder harnesses on and received minor injuries. However, the aircraft was destroyed. The ELT did not activate and there was no fire. The wind was reported to be from the east at 15 knots, gusting to 25 knots on the runway heading.

C-GMAN, a Rockwell Intl Aero Commander 690B aircraft operated by MAG Aerospace Canada, was conducting a Bird Dog operation from Red Lake, ON (CYRL) in support of aerial fire suppression 13 nautical miles South of Lac du Bonnet, MB (CYAX). During flight, there was an odour and associated smoke in the cockpit and cabin, that appeared to be unrelated to the smoke generated by the fire on the ground. The flight crew elected to divert to CYAX and noticed that, when the ground blower automatically shut down at 140 knots, the smoke cleared. The subsequent landing was uneventful. The operator's maintenance proceeded to replace the ground blower.

C-GCGQ, a Bell 412EP helicopter operated by the Canadian Coast Guard, was transporting a pole tower as a sling load from the Port Hawkesbury, NS jetty to Little Judique Harbour, NS. As the helicopter was approaching the destination, the slung load began to spin and released from the helicopter, falling into the ocean approximately 1/4 mile offshore. As there were no lifting rings, a strap had been secured to the tower and it is suspected the strap was cut as a result of the spinning motion. The tower was about 2 feet in diameter and weighed about 600 pounds. It is resting in several feet of water and recovery efforts are underway. The Coast Guard has halted any further transport by this method until proper and secure lifting mechanisms can be put in place.

C-GNJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8229 from Phoenix/Sky Harbor Intl, AZ (KPHX) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 4 crew members and 65 passengers on board. Upon selection of the landing gear up shortly after the departure from KPHX, the flight crew received a NOSE GEAR UNSAFE indication as the nose gear lights were alternating between amber and red. The flight crew executed the related checklist, declared a PAN PAN and requested a return to KPHX where the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FEXH, a Cessna 208B aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express, was conducting flight MAL7060 from Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT) to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG). During the descent from 10 000 feet ASL, the aircraft experienced moderate to severe turbulence. Severe turbulence was encountered at 6 000 feet ASL, as a downdraft caused a 2 000 to 2 500 feet per minute descent, with an associated airspeed exceedance. The pilot did not have control over the rate of descent and informed ATC that the flight would be unable to maintain 3 000 feet ASL to the initial fix. The subsequent landing was uneventful. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and no defects were noted.

C-FEKS, un appareil de type Embraer 170-200 exploité par Sky Regional Airlines, effectuait le vol SKV7599 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de Chicago/O’Hare Intl, IL (KORD) avec 60 passagers et 4 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’appareil était en montée à 9000 pieds ASL suivant le départ de CYUL, le système d'affichage des paramètres moteurs et d'alerte de l'équipage (EICAS) a diffusé plusieurs messages, dont AVNX MAU 2B FAIL. L’équipage a effectué la liste de vérification du manuel de référence rapide (QRH) et a exécuté un retour à l’aéroport de départ. Par la suite, l’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 06L sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage.

C-GBHY, un Airbus 319-114 exploité par Air Canada rouge, effectuait le vol ROU1855 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de Las Vegas/McCarran Intl, NV (KLAS) avec 133 passagers et 5 membres d’équipage à bord. Alors que l’appareil avait terminé son refoulement de la barrière au départ de CYUL, un membre d’équipage de conduite a subi une incapacité physique. L’appareil a été repositionné à la barrière afin de remplacer ledit membre d’équipage.

N31MG, un appareil de type Cessna 208B exploité par Castle Aviation, effectuait le vol CSJ915 selon les règles de vol aux instruments à partir de Montréal Intl (Mirabel), QC (CYMX) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Lors de la circulation au sol après l’atterrissage à CYUL, l'aéronef a heurté un feu de voie de circulation. L'hélice a été endommagée. Une capture d'écran du radar au sol à CYUL a démontré que l'aéronef a dévié de la trajectoire à suivre sur la voie de circulation. Personne n'a été blessé.

C-GJZD, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8150 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG). During the approach into CYEG, the flight crew noted that the number 2 hydraulic system was dropping below 45 percent. The flight crew elected to lower the landing gear early and the hydraulic fluid reading then fell to 25 percent. ATC was notified of the situation and ARFF was requested to standby. The flight landed normally without incident.The operator’s maintenance found a leaking ground servicing quick disconnect fitting. The fitting was repaired and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FIVQ, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA881 from Paris/Charles de Gaulle, France (LFPG) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 12 crew members and 249 passengers on board. As the aircraft was being pushed back from the gate at LFPG, Apron Control observed smoke and flames coming from the APU area, and dispatched ARFF. When attending to the aircraft, ARFF sprayed the fire retardant to the affected section. Although there was no APU fire warning, the flight crew discharged the APU fire extinguisher out of precaution. Passengers were deplaned from the aircraft. There were no injuries and no damage to the aircraft. Upon preliminary inspection, the operator’s maintenance found the APU oil level to be empty due to a leak. It was later determined that the flames and smoke were from the APU tailpipe, and not the APU compartment.

C-FRWI, a Robinson R44 Raven II helicopter operated by Synergy Aviation, had completed the days flying and was enroute to a fuel cache before returning to base. At approximately 1500 feet AGL while at cruising speed, the pilot experienced a yaw to the right, followed by a low rotor warning horn. The collective was lowered to regain rotor and engine speed. However, when power was brought back, a severe vibration developed, accompanied with a loud clacking noise. The pilot initiated an autorotation approach into a well site and, when power was brought back on short final, the vibrations increased. A full auto rotational landing was conducted. After the landing, the pilot visually inspected the aircraft for damage; none was found. The operator’s maintenance determined that an exhaust valve had failed on the Avco Lycoming IO-540-AE1A5 engine.

C-GHTA, a DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8148 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG). While taxiing to Runway 17R on Taxiway C6, ATC cleared JZA8148 to line-up on Runway 17R. The flight crew of JZA8148 declined the clearance due to a WestJet Encore DHC-8-400 (C-GTWE flight WEN3228) being on short final; WEN3228 had been cleared to land.

C-GWEF, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3131 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Fort McMurray, AB (CYMM). When the flight crew selected the landing gear down during the approach at CYMM, they observed only two green lights for the landing gear down position. A missed approach was executed and the flight crew ran the QRH for the landing gear indicator malfunction. ATC was notified, ARFF was requested and the aircraft landed without further issue.

C-GTYM, a privately operated, amphibious float equipped Cessna R172K aircraft, was landing on the Harrison River abeam Sandpiper Golf Course/Rowena's Inn, BC. After touchdown, the aircraft struck a boat wake which resulted in both wings contacting the water. The right and left ailerons were damaged and the left wing was bent. The aircraft was taxied to a dock. The pilot was not injured.

C-GAAP, a Pilatus PC-6/B-H2 Turbo Porter ski equipped aircraft operated by North-Wright Airways, was conducting a wildlife survey out of Ulukhaktok/Holman, NT (CYHI). After almost 3 hours of flying, it was decided to land on the snow to provide a pause for the observers. The pilot selected an appropriate area for a remote site landing in Minto Inlet, approximately 70 nm North of CYHI, and commenced the approach. Shortly after touchdown, the aircraft contacted a snow drift and the right landing gear leg collapsed. The right wing, strut and propeller were also damaged. There was 1 pilot and 6 observers on board, and no one was injured.

C-GYHQ, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Yellowhead Helicopters, was conducting water bucketing operations 50 nm North of Peace River, AB (CYPE), when the bucket and long line were unintentionally released. It is suspected that the manual release cable was rigged too short.

C-GLWS, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1469 from Palm Springs Intl, CA (KPSP) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with 5 crew members and 120 passengers on board. Just prior to the top of descent inbound to CYYC, the flight crew received an error message on the Flight Management Computer. It was then determined that the first officer’s Primary Flight Display (PFD) was displaying erroneous altitude and attitude information. The autopilot was also affected by this system fault. After completing the checklist associated with the condition, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and requested radar vectors for an approach. Subsequently, an uneventful landing was conducted. Upon inspection, the operator’s maintenance found fault with the right Air Data Inertial Reference Unit (ADIRU), and proceeded to replace the unit. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GSNQ, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Services, was conducting flight EVS601 from Sydney/J.A. Douglas McCurdy, NS (CYQY) to Deer Lake, NL (CYDF). When the flight crew selected landing gear down during the approach to CYDF, the left main landing gear light did not illuminate. A missed approach was conducted and the flight crew referenced the checklist. The landing gear was manually extended and the gear safe light illuminated. ARFF was requested on standby and the aircraft landed without further incident. A flight permit was obtained to fly the aircraft to Gander Intl, NL (CYQX) with the landing gear down to repair the fault. The operator’s maintenance inspected the connectors, rigging and wiring in accordance with the manufacturers requirements and could not duplicate the fault. The aircraft was released back to as service.

C-FDBD, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was performing flight SWG758 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Montego Bay/Sangster Intl, Jamaica (MKJS) with 191 passengers and 6 crew members on board. Upon arrival at the gate at MKJS, the flight crew was advised of hydraulic fluid leaking from the right main landing gear. After inspection of the landing gear and confirmation of the hydraulic leak, the flight crew requested ARFF to attend to the aircraft and proceeded to move all persons away from the aircraft. ARFF inspected the scene and advised it was safe to return to the aircraft. Normal operations resumed.

C-FEKS, un appareil de type Embraer ERJ 170-200 exploité par Sky Regional Airlines, effectuait le vol SKV7642 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de New York/LaGuardia, NY (KLGA) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 69 passagers à bord. Lors de la descente pour KLGA, l'équipage a reçu un message de défaillance de volets de bord d'attaque, accompagné d'une activation du vibreur de manche. L'équipage a déclaré une urgence et a demandé de revenir à CYUL afin de bénéficier d'une longueur de piste supérieure et de conditions VFR à l'atterrissage. Suite à l'atterrissage, l'équipage a noté une température élevée des freins du côté droit. L'aéronef a été immobilisé sur la piste où les services d'urgence ont refroidi les freins à l'aide de ventilateurs. L'aéronef a par la suite pu procéder à la barrière sur son propre pouvoir.

C-GMAY, un appareil de type Viking Aircraft DHC-3T exploité par Johnny May's Air Charters, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue à partir du lac Lemoine, QC à destination de Kuujjuaq, QC (CYVP) avec 1 membre d'équipage et 7 passagers à bord. Lors de l'atterrissage, l'aéronef a viré vers la gauche et a effectué une sortie de piste. Le pilote a fait demi-tour et est revenu sur la piste. Il n'y a pas eu de dommages ni de blessés. Un problème d'ajustement de la roue de queue serait à l'origine de l'évènement.

C-GHLV, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1945 from Bogotá/El Nuevo Dorado Intl, Colombia (SKBO) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 8 crew members and 229 passengers on board. During cruise flight in the vicinity of Orlando Intl, FL (KMCO), one of the cabin crew members became incapacitated and was unable to continue their duties. A cabin crew member employed by the operator was travelling as a passenger, and agreed to take on the duties. The flight continued to its destination without further incident.

N5587A, a Ryan Navion A aircraft operated by Kingdom Air Corps, was conducting a post maintenance local test flight from Fort Nelson, BC (CYYE) with one pilot on board. The aircraft departed from Runway 08 and, at an altitude of approximately 100 feet AGL, the engine (Teledyne Continental Motors E185) began to run rough. The aircraft continued the climb to an altitude of approximately 500 feet AGL, at which point the aircraft lost engine power for undetermined reasons. The pilot elected to return to the field and executed a left turn due to better landing area options and proximity of rescue personnel. However, there was insufficient altitude to make the airport and a forced landing was carried out in a grassy area, on the east side of the airport. ARFF and EMS responded to the scene. The pilot received serious injuries, and the aircraft was substantially damage.

C-FXCL, a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan aircraft operated by McMurray Aviation, was conducting a scheduled flight from Fort Chipewyan, AB (CYPY) to Fort McMurray, AB (CYMM) with 1 crew member and 9 passengers on board. While cruising at 5500 feet approximately 25 nm North of CYMM, the pilot noticed a change in sound, accompanied by a noticeable vibration in the aircraft. On approach to CYMM, the pilot requested an expedited landing. ATC asked if the pilot would like ARFF placed on standby, which the pilot agreed to. An uneventful landing was completed and the aircraft taxied to the ramp with no further issues.A post flight examination revealed that baggage pod door A had opened in flight. It appeared that the latch had been closed on the rubber door seal and not the baggage pod structure as designed. During flight, the rubber seal tore and the door opened, resulting in the change in noise and vibration. No other anomalies were found. As that section of the baggage pod contained no items, nothing was lost from the aircraft.

C-FNOE, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA026 from Shanghai/ Pudong Intl, China (ZSPD) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 12 crew members and 252 passengers on board. On taxi out from ZSPD, a smoke indication was noted in the cabin-crew rest cabin. The aircraft returned to the gate. The operator’s maintenance performed checks in accordance with the AMM and FIM with no faults found. The flight continued without further incident.

C-FIVX, a Boeing 777-333ER aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA890 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Rome/Leonardo da Vinci Intl, Italy (LIRF) with 14 crew members and 450 passengers onboard. During cruise flight approximately 720 nm West of London/Heathrow, UK (EGLL), a flight crew member became incapacitated. The other flight crew member contacted the operator’s operational control centre and the decision was made to divert the flight to EGLL. A PAN PAN was declared and the flight landed without further incident.

C-FNKZ, a privately operated Belair Raven Amateur Built aircraft, was conducting a flight from Sault Ste. Marie Municipal/Sanderson Field, MI (KANJ) with 2 persons on board. Shortly after becoming airborne, the aircraft was observed departing controlled flight, and nose-dived into the ground next to the runway. The 2 occupants were fatally injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged. The NTSB is investigating.

C-FPKW, a Viking Aircraft CL-215-6B11 (CL-215T) aircraft operated by the Ministry of the Environment of the Province of Saskatchewan, was conducting a local training flight from La Ronge/Barber Field, SK (CYVC). As part of the training matrix, the right engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW123AF) was feathered, shut down, and an air restart was performed using the checklist. After the engine was restarted, the propeller (Hamilton Standard 14SF-19) would not come out of feather. The flight crew elected to return to CYVC. The right engine was shut down and an emergency was declared. The aircraft landed without further incident. The operator's maintenance replaced the Propeller Pitch Control Valve.

C-GCIJ, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways, was conducting flight CJT620 from Greater Moncton/Romeo Leblanc Intl, NB (CYQM) to St. John's Intl, NL (CYYT). While unloading cargo after the landing in CYYT, the staff discovered a mail bag containing a liquid spill. Upon investigating, a package was discovered to have contained two cans with Evotherm M1. This substance is a Class 9 dangerous goods, Environmentally Hazardous Substance, Liquid, N.O.S. (Fatty Amine Derivatives) marine pollutant. One of the cans had leaked its entire content, equal to approximately one liter. The dangerous goods were not declared by the shipper.The operator’s maintenance inspected the cargo compartment and cleaned up the spill. The aircraft was then returned to service. The contracting company cleaned the unit load device and will conduct an undeclared dangerous goods follow up with the shipper.

C-GVXU, un appareil de type Cessna A185F exploité par le Centre québécois de formation aéronautique (CQFA), effectuait un vol local d'essai pour fins de certification sous l'autorité d'un permis de vol expérimental selon les règles de vol à vue, à partir de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Lors d'une descente à haute vitesse au-dessus du Lac Lamothe, QC, l'appareil s'est mis à vibrer et à tanguer. L'équipage a alors constaté que le ski et la roue du côté gauche s'étaient détachés de l'appareil et que le ski du côté droit avait quitté sa position initiale et pendait vers le bas. Le pilote a alors réduit la vitesse afin de ramener le ski droit à un angle acceptable. Une urgence a été déclarée et l’appareil est revenu atterrir à CYRC en présence des services d'urgence. Personne n’a été blessé. Un dossier SGS a été ouvert par l’exploitant.

C-GTSD, an Airbus A330-300 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC323 from London/Gatwick, UK (EGKK) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 11 crew members and 326 passengers on board. As the aircraft was accelerating past 100 kts during the take-off run, the flight crew heard a bang, which was followed with a yaw. A few seconds later, another bang was heard which was also associated with another yaw. The flight crew rejected the takeoff and stopped the aircraft on the runway. A number 2 ENGINE FAIL ECAM message appeared shortly after, followed by ENGINE STALL. ECAM action was executed, the flight crew shut the engine down, and ATC reported that there was black smoke coming out of the engine. As a precaution, the flight crew discharged the engine 2 fire bottle. ARFF inspected the aircraft and found no damage. The aircraft then taxied to the gate.The operator is currently investigating the incident.

C-GJZR, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8284 from Timmins (Victor M. Power), ON (CYTS) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During the climb out from CYTS through 6500 feet ASL, the number 1 propeller RPM decreased to 850, which was  followed by a master caution light. The propeller RPM then increased to 1060, an over speed condition, and the flight crew followed QRH procedures. The engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW150A) was shut down, a PAN PAN was declared and the flight crew requested to return to CYTS where the aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance replaced the propeller PCU and, following operational checks, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GSJB, un appareil de type Airbus 319-112 exploité par Air Canada rouge, effectuait le vol ROU1709 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Charlottetown, PEI (CYYG) à destination de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). Alors que l’appareil était en vol de croisière à environ 80 nm à l’est du radiophare omnidirectionnel (VOR) de Montréal (YUL), l’équipage a rapporté avoir un problème avec le système hydraulique. L’équipage a déclaré un PAN PAN et l’appareil a poursuivi le vol jusqu’à destination où il s’est posé sur la piste 33R sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-FWRS, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (CRJ100) aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7316 from Raleigh-Durham Intl, NC (KRDU) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 3 crew members and 50 passengers on board. As the aircraft was climbing through FL250 approximately 60 nautical miles South West of Washington/Dulles Intl, VA (KIAD), the flight crew received an R 14th DUCT OVHT message, accompanied by a Master Warning light. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and requested a diversion to KIAD where the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced the 14th stage bleed sensing element in accordance with Aircraft Maintenance Manual 36-21-04-00/400-807 and conducted an operational check. An engine run was carried out at high power (85% N2) with the 14th stage bleed ON and anti-ice ON. No further faults were found. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GSOC, a Cessna 680 aircraft operated by Sunwest Aviation, was conducting flight CNK771 from Duluth Intl, MN (KDLH) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with only 2 pilots on board. During the number 2 engine start in KDLH, the flew crew observed abnormal N2 acceleration. Smoke and some fire was observed emanating from the engine and the pilots were advised. The engine was shut down and motored for 10 seconds with no further issues. There were no flight crew warning system indications for fire and the fire suppression system was not activated. A post incident inspection discovered heat damage on the inlet fan blade shroud for the number 2 engine (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW306C).

C-FVLX, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA92 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Santiago/Arturo Merino Benítez Intl, Chile (SCEL) with 11 crew members and 208 passengers on board. When the aircraft was cruising at FL390 approximately 245 nautical miles North of SCEL, a passenger in the forward section of the aircraft inadvertently drop a cellular phone down inside the seat mechanism. Despite guidance to passengers on how to address this type of situation, the seat was moved by the passenger which caused damage to the phone. Smoke was then observed in the cabin, however there was no fire. The cabin crew was able to retrieve the device and placed it in a Portable Electronic Device Fire bag. The flight continued to destination without further incident.The seat area was inspected and no damage was found. The area was cleaned and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FDSN, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA224 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). Shortly after takeoff from CYVR, the landing gear doors failed to close upon selection of landing gear up. Following an unsuccessful ECAM reset, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and elected to return CYVR where the aircraft landed without further incident. Subsequent maintenance actions revealed a leaking nose landing gear actuator. The nose landing gear door safety valve and NLG door up-lock were replaced. Note: C-FDSN experienced a similar landing gear door issue while departing Los Angeles, CA (KLAX) on 30 April 2018 (see TSB Occurrence A18F0092).

C-GDAS, a privately registered Cessna A188B agriculture aircraft, departed from Bracken, SK to Swift Current, SK. (CYYN) with only the pilot on board. During the landing roll on Runway 12 at CYYN, directional control was lost, the aircraft swerved to the left and departed the runway surface. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the right landing gear and propeller. There were no injuries to the pilot. Winds were calm and the runway was bare and dry. A NOTAM was issued for the closure of Runway 12/30 until 2230Z when the aircraft was removed.

C-FCAE, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA010 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). While the aircraft was taxiing for the departure in CYYC, the flight crew experienced an uncommanded hard right turn; however, the aircraft remained on the taxiway. Following a preliminary inspection by the operator’s maintenance, the aircraft taxied back to the gate. Maintenance personnel could not identify any faults with the steering or braking system and, after taxi tests were performed, the aircraft was returned to service.

2-ODAY, a Bombardier CL-600-2B16 Challenger 601-3A aircraft operated by Volare Aviation, was conducting flight VLZ556 from San José/Norman Y. Mineta San José Intl, CA (KSJC) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During the approach at CYYZ, the left side Primary Flight Display (PFD) image became distorted and flickered. Moments later, the flight crew noted the smell of burning electrical wiring. EFIS 1 was then deselected and the burning electrical smell dissipated. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-INEL, un appareil Ultra-léger de type évolué Tecnam P2002 Sierra en exploitation privée, se préparait pour un décollage au départ de Lachute, QC (CSE4) en prévision d'un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue. Lors de sa course initiale au décollage, l’appareil a effectué un virage non contrôlé vers la droite et a terminé sa course dans le fossé, en bordure de la piste 28. Le pilote, qui était seul à bord, n'a pas été blessé. L'appareil a subi des dommages importants à l'aile droite.

C-FXCA, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1901 from Athens/Eleftherios Venizelos Intl, Greece (LGAV) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During the approach to CYYZ, the flight crew received an EICAS message for the slats upon selection of flaps/slats. A missed approach was executed and the flight crew declared a PAN PAN as a precaution. On the second approach, the aircraft landed without further event with ARFF standing by. During troubleshooting, the operator’s maintenance found several slat proximity sensors out of rig. Re-rigging was performed in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual and, after subsequent successful operations, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GLQN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE943 from Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City, ON (CYTZ). During the climb after the departure from CYTZ, the flight crew received a door open indication and was unable to pressurize aircraft. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and returned to CYTZ where the aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. A visual inspection of the aircraft determined that the cargo door handle had popped out or was inadvertently left unlocked by ground personnel during the previous stop. The operator’s maintenance inspected and lubricated the door handle and subsequent operational checks revealed no further faults.

C-FXIJ, a privately registered Cessna 150H aircraft, was conducting a local flight from an east/west grid road, 8.5 nm West of Swift Current, SK (CYYN) with the pilot and a passenger on board. Immediately after takeoff, the aircraft failed to attain a positive rate of climb. The pilot elected to conduct a forced landing into a field, during which the right wing and landing gear contacted a tree stump. The pilot and passenger were wearing seatbelts and shoulder harnesses and suffered minor injuries. The aircraft sustained substantial damage and the ELT activated. There was no post impact fire.

C-GDJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ705) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8668 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to San Diego Intl, CA (KSAN) with 4 crew members and 72 passengers on board. Shortly after the rotation off CYVR, the flight crew noticed a vibration on the number 1 engine (General Electric CF34-8C5). While climbing through 12 000 feet, the vibration intensified. The flight crew reduced the thrust on the affected engine to 75% and the vibration spiked into the amber caution range. The operator’s operational control and maintenance departments were consulted and the decision to return to CYVR was agreed. No emergency was declared, however ARFF was requested as a precaution. The aircraft landed at CYVR without further incident.

C-GZIX, a privately registered amphibious-float equipped Cessna A185F aircraft, departed from a road 8.5 nm South of Lintlaw, SK, enroute to Yorkton Muni, SK (CYQV). During the initial climb, the engine (Continental IO-520-L) had a partial power loss. The pilot attempted a forced landing in a field, however the aircraft collided with tree tops. The aircraft then spun around, and descended to the ground. The pilot, the sole occupant, sustained minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GAAT, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Services (EVAS), was conducting flight EVS7775 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) to Fredericton Intl, NB (CYFC) with 2 crew members and 13 passengers on board. While climbing through 5500 feet following the departure from Runway 05 at CYHZ, passengers alerted the flight crew of the presence of smoke in the cabin. The flight crew selected engine bleed air switches off and the smoke began to dissipate. An emergency was declared and vectors were requested for the return to CYHZ, where the ILS to Runway 14 was conducted. Neither the flight crew nor the passengers donned the available oxygen masks. Following the landing, the aircraft taxied onto Runway 23 where rescue vehicles were standing by. The engines were shut down, the first officer exited the aircraft to assist the evacuation of the passengers, and lead them away from the aircraft.
