A bus was subsequently sent to the location and the passengers were transported to the terminal.The operator’s maintenance conducted an inspection on site before the aircraft was towed to the hangar. Both runways at CYHZ were closed by Notam for approximately 30 minutes while the aircraft was removed. Maintenance personnel determined that the Air Cycle Machine (ACM) was the source of the smoke. This determination was confirmed by TSB investigators who deployed to the airport and spoke to both maintenance personnel and the flight crew, as well as conduct an independent inspection of the aircraft. The faulty ACM was replaced with a serviceable unit and was tested before flight to confirm the fault was rectified. Following the test, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GKHL, a Kamov KA-32A11BC aircraft operated by VIH Helicopters, was conducting a maintenance test flight from Victoria Intl, BC (CYYJ) with 1 pilot and 3 aircraft maintenance engineers on board. During liftoff, the helicopter yawed to the right despite the full application of the left pedal. After approximately four rotations, the pilot aligned the helicopter into the wind and landed firmly on the runway. The helicopter was taxied back to the hangar without further incident. Subsequent maintenance inspection revealed that, during the previous scheduled 600 hours drag hinge replacement which required the removal of the upper rotor head, the pitch links for the upper rotor head were not returned to the correct dimension upon reassembly.

C-GIHJ, a Sikorsky S-76C helicopter operated by Helijet International, was conducting a flight from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). During cruise flight, the transmission gearbox chip/hot annunciator light illuminated. The flight crew reviewed the checklist and, while locating the affected system circuit breaker to reset, they noticed the number 1 hydraulic servo jam circuit breaker had popped. The chip light extinguished once reset, however due to multiple unrelated malfunction indications, the flight crew declared an emergency and elected to return to CYVR where the helicopter landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance found chaffed electrical wires, and proceeded to replace them.

C-FCMN, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Central Mountain Air, was conducting flight GLR753 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Prince George, BC (CYXS) with 2 crew members and 11 passengers on board. After the departure from CYVR, the flight crew declared an emergency due to a fuel leak. The flight crew requested a return to CYVR and shut the number 1 engine down. The aircraft landed on Runway 26L with ARFF standing by. Upon touchdown, a tire was blown and the aircraft stopped at midfield on the runway. The passengers were deplaned and transported to the terminal building. The aircraft was subsequently towed off at 1826Z. Runway 26L was closed for a minor fuel cleanup, while Runway 26R remained active. Runway 26L was reopened at 1830Z.

C-GDMX a privately registered Cirrus SR22 aircraft, was landing on Runway 35 at Parry Sound Area Muni, ON (CNK4). During the landing roll, the aircraft veered to the left and struck a small snow bank. The nose landing gear collapsed, followed by the propeller striking the ground. There were no injuries.

C-FJJZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ705) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8890 from Whitehorse/Erik Nielsen Intl, YT (CYXY) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 4 crew members and 72 passengers on board. During cruise flight, one of the flight attendants began to feel unwell. The aircraft continued to destination and landed without further incident. Emergency Medical Services met the plane at the gate. The flight attendant was transported to a local hospital for further assessment and treatment.

C-GARO, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1671 from Orlando Intl, FL (KMCO) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). Approximately 125 nautical miles North of KMCO after the departure, the flight crew noted a loss in the green hydraulic fluid system quantity, followed by an ECAM indication. The flight crew elected to continue to CYYZ and declared a PAN PAN while on approach. The aircraft landed without further incident and was inspected by ARFF. Subsequently, the aircraft was towed from the taxiway to the gate.

C-FDST, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA615 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During cruise flight, the flight crew received an ECAM Yellow Hydraulic System loss of fluid indication. A PAN PAN was declared and the flight landed at CYYZ without further incident with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance found a leaking seal on the Filter Clogging Indicator and proceeded to replace it in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual procedures. A subsequent leak check found the system serviceable and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GANS, a Bombardier DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG823 from Sioux Lookout, ON (CYXL) to Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT). When the aircraft was approximately 12 nautical miles from CYQT, someone banged on the cockpit door. The flight crew called the cabin via the normal call intercom, and a passenger informed them that someone was having a medical event. During the read back of the landing clearance to ATC, the flight crew requested an ambulance. Subsequently, a PAN PAN was declared. The landing was uneventful and the aircraft taxied to the terminal. The flight crew requested that the passengers remain seated to facilitate first responder access to the patient. ARFF responded, followed a short time later by an ambulance. The flight crew then became aware that the sole flight attendant was the patient, and that two travelling nurses had rendered assistance.

C-GCJZ a Boeing 727-200 aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways, was conducting flight CJT570 from Hamilton, ON (CYHM) to Regina Intl, SK (CYQR). During the climb out after the departure from CYHM, the left engine reportedly experienced a compressor stall. The flight crew shut the engine down, declared an emergency and returned to CYHM. There were no injuries. The operator’s maintenance reported the engine sustained foreign object damage possibly from a chunk of ice.

C-GJVY, an Airbus A319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1740 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Varadero/Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl, Cuba (MUVR). During the taxi to takeoff position at CYYZ, the number 2 engine experienced a sudden flame out without warning. The flight crew taxied the aircraft back to the gate under its own power. The operator is investigating the cause of the engine flame out.

C-GTSZ, an Airbus 330-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC292 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Manchester/Ringway Intl, UK (EGCC) with 12 crew members and 269 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew received  a WHEEL TIRE LO PR (Tire # 7) ECAM message. Checklist items were executed and the flight crew continued the flight to destination. As the flight was approaching EGCC, ATC was notified that the aircraft needed to be inspected after the landing, and prior taxiing to the gate. Approximately one hour before touchdown, the flight crew called PAN PAN on all initial contacts with ATC. The flight crew was then informed that the flight would be treated as an emergency. Following the landing on Runway 23R, the aircraft stopped on an adjacent taxiway. The aircraft was inspected and subsequently towed to the gate.The operator's maintenance replaced the number 7 & 8 main wheel assembly in accordance with AMM 32-41-11/401. An axle and brake inspection did not reveal any damage.

C-FZUG, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU7097 from Tampa Intl, FL (KTPA) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). While inbound to CYYZ, the flight crew received a fault indication related to the aircraft braking system. As a precaution, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and the aircraft landed without further incident. Following an inspection by ARFF after the landing, the aircraft taxied to the gate.

C-FCWW, a Piper PA-31-350 aircraft operated by Super T Aviation Academy, was conducting a flight from Medicine Hat, AB (CYXH) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with 2 pilots and 4 passengers on board. After being cleared for the visual approach to Runway 35L at CYYC, the flight crew observed that the right fuel boost pump light had illuminated. The pilot requested a runway change to 35R and, a few minutes later, both engines (Avco Lycoming (L)TIO-540-J2BD) lost enough power that the pilot was unable to make the runway. A forced landing was conducted onto 36th Street NE, 2.8 nautical miles South of the threshold of Runway 35R. Shortly after touchdown just South of 16th Ave NE (Trans-Canada Highway), the outer right wing struck a pole and severed about 4 feet of wing. The left propeller struck some concrete structures, curling the outer portion of the three propeller blades. When the aircraft came to a complete stop, the first officer assisted the passengers in evacuating the aircraft. There were no injuries to the occupants or persons on the ground. The ELT did not activate.

C-GGGA, un appareil de type Beech 1900D exploité par Air Georgian, effectuait le vol GGN7305 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Hartford-Springfield/Bradley Intl, CT (KBDL) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en approche finale à CYUL, celui-ci a connu des indications de vitesse erratiques de sorte que l’espacement avec LOF4651, un Embraer 145 exploité par Trans State effectuant la liaison entre Washington/Dulles Intl, VA (KIAD)  et CYUL, a été réduit à 2.7 nm sur le plan horizontal alors que l’espacement requis est de 3 nm.

JZA8745, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-100 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Bathurst, NB (CZBF) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Alors que l’appareil se trouvait en approche finale avec une restriction de vitesse de 160 kts jusqu’au point BIRPO, JZA8745 a été observé à une vitesse de 90 kts. Cette déviation a mené à une perte d'espacement avec ACA416, un appareil de type Airbus 330-300 exploité par Air Canada, qui effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) à destination de CYUL. L'espacement a été réduit à 2.5 nm sur le plan horizontal alors que l’espacement requis est de 3 nm. JZA8745 a reçu l'instruction de faire une remontée et a été guidé pour une seconde approche.

C-FDND, a Bombardier Dash 8-100 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines, was conducting flight PVL1902 from Sept-Iles, QC (CYZV) to Wabush, NL (CYWK). During the approach into CYWK, the flight crew received a nose landing gear unsafe indication when the landing gear was selected down. The flight crew entered a hold over CYWK in order to complete the necessary checklists and to burn fuel. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed without further incident. After the landing, the aircraft remained on the runway to deplane passengers since the nose gear pin could not be secured in place. The operator’s maintenance discovered a cracked and broken support bracket which affected the actuator position. The nose landing gear was in motion, however it did not fully travel over the center and locked position. A repair plan is in progress for the aircraft to be returned to service.

C-GYQW, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC369 from Orlando Intl, FL (KMCO) to Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) with 6 crew members and 184 passengers on board. As the aircraft was rotating off Runway 36R on the takeoff, the flight crew noticed a flock of birds passing below the aircraft. No impact was felt, however ATC was notified that the aircraft might have hit birds. After a few minutes, Jacksonville Center contacted the flight crew and advised that a few birds were found on the runway. The flight continued to destination without further incident.The operator’s maintenance carried out a bird strike inspection in accordance with Aircraft Maintenance Manual 05-51-18-210-801. No dents or damage was found.

C-GMOB, a Piper PA-31-350 aircraft operated by Northern Skies Air Service, was conducting flight GS105 from Sioux Lookout, ON (CYXL) to Red Lake, ON (CYRL). While taxiing to the takeoff position, the right engine (Lycoming LTIO-540-J2BD) stopped. The pilot taxied back to the apron. The operator's maintenance determined that, with the electric boost pump operating, the engine was receiving extra fuel due to an internal leak in the engine driven fuel pump. The fuel pump was replaced.

C-IHZG, un appareil de type Ultra-léger de base motorisé pendulaire DTA Combo 912 S en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Saint-Ours, QC à destination de Saint-Marc-sur-Richelieu, QC avec un pilote et un passager à bord. Lors de l’atterrissage sur un chemin de terre battue dans un champ, l’appareil a dévié à droite de la route et a fait un cheval de bois lorsque la roue droite est entrée dans le fossé. Les deux occupants ont subi des blessures légères et l’appareil a subi des dommages importants à la voilure.

C-GCKR, un appareil de type Airbus 320-200 exploité par Air Transat, effectuait le vol TSC671 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Havana /José Martí Intl, Cuba (MUHA) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Lors de l’approche pour la piste 06R à CYUL, l’ATC a donné l’instruction à l’équipage de TSC671 d’effectuer une remontée car il rattrapait C-GTSO, un appareil de type Airbus 330-300 exploité par Air Transat, qui effectuait le vol TSC561 de Cancún Intl, Mexico (MMUN) à CYUL. L'espacement a été réduit à 4.8 nm sur le plan horizontal alors que l’espacement requis est de 5 nm.

C-GGCI, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8982 from Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). After the passengers had deplaned after the arrival in CYUL, the flight crew received a number 1 Engine Fire Warning indication. The number 1 fire handle was pulled; the indication stopped momentarily for a period of approximately 5 to 10 seconds. Subsequently, the number 1 Engine Fire Warning indication reappeared, which prompted the flight crew to discharge the fire bottles. ARFF services were requested for assistance. There were no visual evidence of fire, smoke or any other abnormalities.

C-GWWL, a Bell 212 aircraft operated by Ascent Helicopters, was conducting an external load training flight with a 100 feet long line and 300 lbs of gear, approximately 5 nm East of Salmon Arm, BC (CZAM). While manoeuvering the load, an uncommanded release of the belly hook occurred. No one was injured. Subsequent maintenance inspection revealed a split in the manual release cable casing.

C-GNCH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG429 from Punta Cana Intl, Dominican Republic (MDPC) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) with 6 crew members and 187 passengers on board. During refueling at MDPC before the departure, fuel began leaking out. ARFF was requested and attended to the aircraft until the situation was rectified. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FNOH, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA84 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Tel Aviv/Ben Gurion, Israel (LLBG). Less than one hour after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew reported a minor medical problem with the first officer and asked to return to CYYZ. The flight was directed to the north of Maniwaki, QC (CYMW) to dump fuel but was expected to be overweight for landing. The flight returned to CYYZ and landed without incident. The pilot did not declare an emergency, but requested the emergency equipment on standby.

C-GORZ, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Services (EVAS), was conducting flight EVS7774 from Fredericton Intl, NB (CYFC) to Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ). C-FENO, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3497 from Deer Lake, NL (CYDF) to CYHZ. EVS7774 was cleared to Runway 23 via the DUTIR transition, however the flight crew proceeded direct to LEROS. At the same time, WEN3497 was cleared for the ILS Runway 23 via LEROS. This caused a reduced lateral separation from the required 3 nm to 1.8 nm. EVS7774 was re-cleared to DUTIR, which increased the separation. Both aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GHFE, a privately registered Cessna 170 aircraft, was on a local VFR training flight out of Barrhead, AB (CEP3). During the take-off run on Runway 07, the aircraft began to drift to the right. The student corrected, but the aircraft swerved to the left. The instructor attempted to take control in order to keep the aircraft on the runway, however the aircraft departed the left side of the runway and struck a 3-foot high frozen snow bank. The left main landing gear collapsed and the propeller struck the snow bank. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. Both the instructor and the student exited the aircraft with no injuries.

C-GVPA, a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by PAL Airlines, was conducting flight PVL928 from Gander Intl, NL (CYQX) to St. John's Intl, NL (CYYT). As the flight prepared for the descent into CYYT, the flight crew noticed a fuel imbalance, with the right fuel quantity indicating approximately 350 lbs lower than the left. The flight crew requested that the flight attendant visually check for signs of fuel leaking from the right wing area; however, no fuel leak was observed. As a precaution, the flight crew declared PAN PAN and requested ARFF on standby to inspect the aircraft after landing. The flight landed at CYYT without further incident and shut down on the runway for ARFF inspection. No sign of leaking fuel was observed and the crew taxied the aircraft to the gate.The operator’s maintenance inspected and tested the aircraft fuel quantity system. The aircraft was then returned to service.

N4AT, a privately registered Cessna C550 Citation Bravo aircraft, was conducting a flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) to Bedford/Laurence G Hanscom Field, MA (KBED). After starting the engines on Apron II at CYWG while under the guidance of a ground marshaller, N4AT began to taxi for the departure. During the initial turn from the parking area, aircraft control was lost and N4AT's right wing collided with the nose gear of C-FXWT, a Bombardier CL-600-2B16 (Challenger 605) aircraft, which was parked. The pilot of N4AT subsequently shutdown the aircraft and exited with the passenger without injuries. The right wing of N4AT was substantially damaged, causing a fuel leak on the apron. The right wing of C-FXWT was also damaged in the collision by the nose of N4AT. Local 911 was advised of the collision and fuel leak. ARFF was dispatched to the site, and the fuel leak was contained.

C-FTJR, un appareil de type Airbus 320-200 exploité par Air Canada, effectuait le vol ACA481 au départ de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) en direction de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) avec à son bord 5 membres d'équipage et 146 passagers. Alors qu’il venait de décoller de CYUL, les pilotes ont rapporté une collision avec des oiseaux. L'équipage de conduite a par la suite observé une vibration du moteur numéro 2, a déclaré une urgence et l'appareil est revenu se poser à CYUL sans encombre.

C-FTJR, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1219 from Orlando Intl, FL (KMCO) to Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ). During the climb to cruising altitude after the departure from KMCO, the flight crew heard a thump from the belly as the aircraft climbed through FL240. Since no abnormal indications were noted on the flight deck, the flight continued to destination. When the landing gear was selected down on the approach to CYHZ, there was no response. The flight crew declared an emergency, executed a missed approach and performed a manual extension of the landing gear. The aircraft landed normally and the aircraft was brought to a full stop on the runway as the nose wheel steering is disabled in manual extension. The operator’s maintenance was called to tow the aircraft to the gate and observed that one of the left main tires was flat. Additionally, damage to the landing gear doors was observed. The tire had exploded in the climb causing the noise and damage to the landing gear doors. The tire is being analyzed to determine the cause.

C-GURG, un appareil de type Bombardier CL600-2B16 Challenger 601 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait le vol QUE10 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) pour un vol Medevac à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB). Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, un bruit sourd a été entendu, accompagné d’une vibration importante et anormale du moteur droit, suivi par une indication de température de la turbine interne excédant les limites. L’équipage a fermé le moteur (General Electric CF34-3A1) et effectué un retour à CYUL. L’appareil s’est posé sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage.

C-GCEV, a de Havilland DHC-7-100 aircraft operated by Air Tindi, was conducting ferry flight TIN801 from Muskoka, ON (CYQA) to Gillam, MB (CYGX) with 4 crew members on board. Approximately 265 nautical miles East of Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT), the flight crew noticed oil accumulating on the number 3 engine cowling. Subsequently, the number 3 engine oil pressure indication started to drop. The flight crew shut the number 3 engine down and the aircraft diverted to CYQT. There was no emergency declared and the landing was uneventful.

C-GGMN, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-400 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA722 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliot Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 78 passagers à bord. Lors de l'approche pour la piste 29 à CYQB, l'équipage de conduite a reçu le message FLAP POWER CAUTION lorsque les volets se sont bloqués à 15 degrés. L'équipage de conduite a effectué une remise des gaz en raison des averses de neige qui prévalaient à ce moment, a déclaré une urgence et demandé d'être réacheminé vers CYUL où l'appareil s'est posé sans problème avec les volets à 15 degrés.

C-GMDQ, a privately operated Cirrus SR22 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Bedford County, PA (KHMZ) to Massena Intl/Richards Field, NY (KMSS) with one pilot and 2 passengers on board. While flying on an Instrument Flight Plan (IFR) at 9000 feet ASL in the vicinity of Lowville, NY, the pilot inadvertently allowed the aircraft to enter an unusual attitude and got spatially disoriented. As a precaution, the Cirrus Airframe Parachute System (CAPS) was deployed. While the aircraft descended with the parachute, the pilot shut the engine down and declared a Mayday. The aircraft landed vertically upright and all 3 occupants evacuated the aircraft with minor injuries. Subsequently, the wind dragged the aircraft and flipped it inverted, causing substantial damage.

C-GJIG, a Bombardier DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA756 from Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) with 3 crew members and 33 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the cabin crew reported smoke coming out from the ceiling at Row 6AC. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks and declared an emergency which was later cancelled as the smoke had dissipated. The aircraft continued to destination where an uneventful landing was carried out. Following a post flight inspection, the cabin zone temperature sensor was found to be faulty. The sensor was replaced as per Aircraft Maintenance Manual 21-60-44 and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJZE, a de Havilland DHC-2 MK. I aircraft on floats operated by Air Cab, was enroute over Johnson Return Channel, BC, approximately 4 nautical miles East of Bella Bella (Campbell Island), BC (CBBC) when it experienced an engine power loss. The pilot conducted a forced landing on water. The marine vessel Shauna Marie responded to provide assistance. Three of the occupants were taken aboard the marine vessel while the pilot remained on board the aircraft. The aircraft was towed to Shearwater and arrived at that location without further incident. There were no injuries.

C-GLKY, a Bombardier DHC-8-314 aircraft operated by Perimeter Aviation Lp, was conducting flight PAG997 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl, SK (CYXE) to Regina Intl, SK (CYQR). When the aircraft was 3.8 nautical miles from Runway 31 at CYQR on final approach and at an altitude of 3300 feet ASL, the flight crew observed an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) pass by the left side of the aircraft. The UAV was estimated to be approximately 50 metres from the aircraft laterally and at the same altitude. The aircraft subsequently landed uneventfully and CYQR Tower was advised of the incident.

C-GZPA, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-100 exploité par Provincial Airlines, effectuait le vol PVL1932 selon les règles de vol aux instruments au départ de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) à destination de Wabush, NL (CYWK). Lors du départ de la piste 09 à CYZV, PVL1932 était autorisé à suivre le départ normalisé CYZV2, lequel consiste à maintenir un cap de 089°M jusqu'à 5000 pieds ASL. À ce moment, C-FSKQ, un appareil de type Beech 200 exploité par Sky Jet M.G. effectuant le vol VSL443 selon les règles de vol à vue de Natashquan, QC (CYNA) à CYZV, était à environ 6 miles marins à l'est de CYZV avec l'intention d'effectuer son atterrissage sur la piste 27. Afin de laisser passer PVL1932, VSL433 a effectué un virage de 360 degrés à une altitude de 2000 pieds ASL. Toutefois, les deux appareils se sont retrouvés à une distance d'un mile l'un de l'autre, de sorte que PVL1932 a dû répondre à un avis de résolution TCAS.

C-FTJV, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA619 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During the approach at CYYZ, the flight crew received an EICAS message for a HYDRAULIC SYSTEM B FAULT upon lowering the flaps. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN, followed the abnormal procedures checklist and executed an uneventful landing with ARFF standing by. The aircraft stopped on the runway while ARFF checked the aircraft and, after completion of the check, was cleared to proceed to the gate. The operator’s maintenance found a hydraulic leak on the number 2 engine hydraulic EDP pressure line. The pump and line were replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GGJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 CRJ200 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8031 from Philadelphia Intl, PA (KPHL) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) with 4 crew members and 33 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from KPHL, the flight crew noticed that the Air Driven Generator (ADG) had deployed. The flight crew requested to return to KPHL and declared a PAN PAN. The aircraft landed back in KPHL without further incident.

C-GBZS, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG702 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Freeport/Grand Bahamas Intl, Bahamas (MYGF) with 6 crew members and 173 passengers on board. As the flight had been authorized to descend to 15 000 feet approximately 60 nautical miles North West of MYGF, ATC notified the flight crew of a traffic at 14 000 feet, which was acknowledged by replying that they had it in sight. The other traffic was then cleared by ATC for a visual climb, and the flight crew also acknowledged that they had SWG702 in sight. When SWG702 passed 15 800 feet, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to CLIMB, which was executed. The traffic was visual the entire time and proper separation was maintained. SWG702 continued to destination without further incident.

C-FJQL, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1887 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to San Diego Intl, CA (KSAN) with 6 crew members and 182 passengers on board. During cruise flight in the vicinity of Hampton, IA, one of the cabin crew members became incapacitated due to illness and was unable to continue their duties. The flight continued to its destination without further incident.

C-FJQD, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1887 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to San Diego Intl, CA (KSAN) with 6 crew members and 174 passengers on board. During cruise flight in the vicinity of Hampton, IA, one of the cabin crew members sustained an injury and was unable to continue their duties. Medical assistance was provided through StatMD and the flight continued to its destination without further incident.

C-GZGA, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7228 from Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies Intl, BC (CYXC) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). Upon landing on Runway 17R at CYYC, the aircraft lost its nose wheel just after touchdown. The aircraft came to rest on the axle and lower nose gear casting as it slid some 1200 feet down the runway. The tower controller noticed the shower of sparks and ARFF was dispatched. Once the aircraft came to rest on the runway, the flight crew evacuated the passengers. There were no injuries. The aircraft was subsequently towed to the hangar.

C-GTQJ, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC679 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl, FL (KFLL) to Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ). While on approach to CYHZ with the flaps set to the Flaps 5 position, the flight crew selected Flaps 10 and received an indication that the flaps did not move. The flight crew carried out the applicable checklist and followed the alternate flap extension procedure to lower the flaps to the Flap 15 position. A PAN PAN was declared and ARFF responded. The flight landed at CYHZ without further incident.Maintenance personnel determined that the left-hand proximity sensor was operating intermittently. The sensor's connector was cleaned and the flap system was tested with no faults found. The airplane was returned to service.

C-FEJL, an Embraer ERJ-170-200 aircraft operated by Sky Regional Airlines, was conducting flight SKV7707 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Austin-Bergstrom Intl, TX (KAUS) with 4 crew members and 62 passengers on board. Shortly after becoming airborne from CYYZ, the flight crew received an EICAS SPOILER CONTROL FAULT followed almost immediately by a WING SHEAR caution message. The flight crew advised ATC and declared an emergency while levelling the aircraft at 5000 feet ASL. QRH procedures were executed and the cabin crew was notified that they were returning to CYYZ. The landing was uneventful with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance checked the flight spoiler operation and found no faults. The main landing gear was serviced due to the overweight landing and the inspection revealed no faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FUSF, a privately operated Piper PA-30 Twin Comanche aircraft, was conducting a flight from Morgantown/Municipal-Walter L Bill Hart Field, WV (KMGW) to Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City, ON (CYTZ) with 2 persons on board. Shortly after touchdown on Runway 26 at CYTZ, the aircraft veered to the right and departed the runway surface onto the grass. The nose gear collapsed and the aircraft came to rest on the main landing gear. There were no injuries, however the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GTIM, a Swearingen SA226-TC Metro II aircraft operated by Skycare Air Ambulance, was conducting a flight from Sault Ste. Marie, ON (CYAM) to Kitchener, ON (CYKF) with 3 crew members on board. During the flight, the flight crew was unable to control engine power on the number two engine. The flight continued to destination and, since reverse thrust was unavailable after touchdown, the flight crew proceeded to shut the number 2 engine (Garrett TPE331-10UA-511G) down once the landing was completed. The aircraft was difficult to steer, however the flight crew managed to taxi to the tarmac. There were no injuries or reported damage to the aircraft. The operator’s maintenance found the linkage to the FCU was lose. The linkage was re-tightened and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FDQQ, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA206 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). ACA206 had been cleared for the ILS Runway 17R approach in CYYC. C-GGOK, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA585 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl, SK (CYXE) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). JZA585 had been cleared for the ILS Runway 17L approach in CYYC. While both aircraft were being vectored, the separation between the two eroded to 2.6 nautical miles laterally and 500 feet vertically, where 3.0 nautical miles or 1000 feet is required.

N692DL, a Boeing 757-200 aircraft operated by Delta Airlines, was conducting flight DAL1601 from Minneapolis-St. Paul Intl/Wold-Chamberlain, MN (KMSP) to Anchorage/Ted Stevens Intl, AK (PANC) with 6 crew members and 180 passengers on board. While in cruise flight at FL360 approximately 25 nautical miles East of Fort St. John, BC (CYXJ), the flight crew noticed the LH Engine (Pratt & Whitney – USA PW2037) oil quantity indication decrease to zero. The indication was accompanied by a LH engine low oil pressure EICAS message. The oil pressure indication had decreased to 70 PSI. The flight crew referenced the QRH and reduced the LH engine to idle. No vibrations were noted. The flight crew then declared an emergency and requested a diversion to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) where the aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF in attendance. A preliminary inspection of the aircraft found fluid on the left engine cowl. A subsequent inspection by maintenance personnel found a leak in an oil pressure line between the main gearbox and the angle gearbox.

N648UA, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL908 from Amsterdam/Schiphol, Netherlands (EHAM) to Chicago/O'Hare Intl, IL (KORD) with 14 crew members and 205 passengers on board. While in cruise flight at FL320 nearing the coast of Labrador, the flight crew noted a bang, a yawing of the aircraft and the left engine N1 and N2 indications decreasing. As the aircraft was unable to maintain FL320 with one engine inoperative, it began to descend and the flight crew executed the engine checklist. An emergency was declared and ATC was advised that they were descending. Since the engine surged twice and EGT readings were erratic, a restart was abandoned and the engine was shut down. The flight crew leveled off at FL200 and diverted to Goose Bay, NL (CYYR) where the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced the left engine.

C-GSQQ, a privately operated Lancair IVP aircraft, was conducting a flight from Fort Myers/Buckingham Field, FL (FL59) to Sebring Regional, FL (KSEF) with one pilot and 3 passengers on board. The pilot-in-command reported that, after an uneventful landing on Runway 01 at KSEF, the aircraft continued to the end of the runway, and then turned left onto Taxiway A4. At that time, the pilot noticed a Boeing B737, which was facing to the south, with the left engine cowling removed. The pilot did not notice any indication that either engines were operating, so the pilot proceeded in a westerly direction with no aileron control input. Suddenly, the left wing lifted up and the right wing contacted the ground. The airplane cartwheeled and came to rest in grass, upright, at the north edge of the taxiway, facing north. The nose landing gear fork and wheel assembly separated. Reportedly at the time, the B737 was performing engine(s) run(s). The NTSB is investigated (ERA18LA117).

C-GTVG, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG685 from Varadero/Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl, Cuba (MUVR) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 6 crew members and 181 passengers on board. During an enroute climb from FL350 to FL370 approximately 30 nautical miles North East of Fort Myers/Southwest Florida Intl, FL (KRSW), the flight crew received an engine vibration that exceeded limitations on the number 1 engine. A PAN PAN was declared and the aircraft was levelled off at FL361, to subsequently return to FL350. The flight continued to destination without further incident.  The operator’s maintenance confirmed that the indication was false and was caused by a faulty Fan Frame Compressor Case Vibration Sensor. The aircraft was put on MEL until the part was replaced.

C-GWUE, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3404 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Fredericton Intl, NB (CYFC) with 4 crew members and 58 passengers on board. During the climb out after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew received a ROLL SPLR INBD HYD caution light passing through 14 000 feet ASL. An emergency was declared and a return to CYYZ was requested. The aircraft entered a holding pattern in order to reduce its weight for the landing, and the aircraft landed without further incident with ARFF standing by. After coming to a stop, the flight crew shut both engines down and the aircraft was towed to the terminal. The operator’s maintenance found the hydraulic return line for the inboard spoiler dump valve leaking. The line was replaced in accordance with the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FADF, a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA195 from Kamloops, BC (CYKA) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 3 crew members and 34 passengers on board. As the flight crew selected landing gear down during the approach into CYVR, the number 2 hydraulic quantity depleted. A missed approach was executed, the flight crew performed an alternate landing gear extension and subsequently declared an emergency. The aircraft landed on Runway 08R with ARFF on standby.

C-GWSZ, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA1701 from Los Angeles Intl, CA (KLAX) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). When the flight crew selected Flaps 30 during the approach sequence, the flaps did not move. A missed approach was initiated in order to complete the appropriate checklist and, once ready, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN. Runway 26L was requested for landing distance considerations, and an uneventful Flaps 15 landing was accomplished. Upon inspection, the operator’s maintenance found a fault with the left hand flap position transmitter. The unit was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GEEX, a privately operated Cessna A185E aircraft, was conducting a VFR flight itinerary when the pilot encountered deteriorating weather conditions and had to perform a forced landing on Highway 37, south of Bowser Lake, BC. After the touchdown on the wet pavement, the aircraft swerved and a loss of directional control ensued. The aircraft drifted to the right toward a ditch, and the right wing struck a snow bank causing the airplane to flip onto its roof. The pilot exited the aircraft and plugged the wing vent in order to prevent a fuel leak. With the assistance of motorists, the aircraft was redressed onto its wheels and was moved away to clear the highway. An ELT signal has been triggered.

C-FGEW, a Swearingen SA226-TC Metro II aircraft operated by Sunwest Aviation, was conducting local training flight CNK216 from Camrose, AB (CEQ3). The training flight was being conducted with the pilot flying (PF) seated in the right seat and the training pilot, pilot not flying (PNF), seated in the left seat. During the takeoff roll on Runway 32 while accelerating through 40 KIAS, the PF’s finger slipped off the nose wheel steering button on the power lever. While trying to press the button again, the PF didn’t notice the aircraft veering to the left. The PNF was not immediately aware of the deviation as they were both setting power. The PNF alerted the PF of the deviation and while the aircraft was accelerating through 60 KIAS, the PF rejected the takeoff. At that time, the aircraft was half way between the runway centerline and the runway edge. The PF was unable to regain directional control using nose wheel steering. The PNF took over and attempted to regain control by using differential power and braking. The left main wheels caught the snow, the aircraft departed the runway at an approximate 45° angle and came to rest approximately 150 feet from the runway edge. There were no injuries and the aircraft did not sustain any damage.

C-FUJA, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 aircraft operated by Sky Regional Airlines, was conducting flight SKV7618 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Washington/Ronald Reagan National, DC (KDCA) with 4 crew members and 63 passengers on board. Shortly after starting the descent into KDCA, the flight crew noticed a burning odour in the cockpit. The cabin crew confirmed that they could smell smoke in the cabin as well. Subsequently, smoke appeared at the first officer’s feet and at the bottom part of the windshield. The flight crew donned their oxygen masks, declared an emergency and requested a diversion to Washington/Dulles Intl, VA (KIAD). All through the approach and the landing, dark grey smoke was visible in the cockpit and was also noticed in the cabin coming from the overhead vents. Once the aircraft came to a full stop on Runway 19R, the aircraft was evacuated. ARFF attended, and passengers were taken to the terminal by bus.The operator’s maintenance found a burnt windshield terminal block ground wire. The left hand windshield was replaced, as well as the windshield wire terminal crimp. After several checks, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GJKL, a privately registered Cessna 421C aircraft, was conducting a flight from Kingston, ON (CYGK) to St. Catharines/Niagara District, ON (CYSN) with one pilot and 2 passengers on board. During cruise flight, the number 2 engine (Continental GTSIO-520-L) began to lose power. The flight continued to CYSN and the number 2 engine was shut down. During the final approach, the aircraft touched down on soft grass approximately 500 feet short of the runway threshold. The nose landing gear collapsed; the main landing gear, propellers and nose were substantially damaged. The three occupants on board were not injured.

C-FJUB, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG590 from Cancún Intl, Mexico (MMUN) to Calgary Intl, ON (CYYC) with 6 crew members and 178 passengers on board. During cruise flight in the vicinity of Rapid City, SD, one of the cabin crew members became ill and was unable to continue their duties. Medlink was contacted and advised the flight crew to continue to destination. Upon initial contact with ATC approaching CYYC, the flight crew declared an emergency in order to get priority handling.

C-GHLV, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1981 from México City/Benito Juárez Intl, México (MMMX) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 8 crew members and 269 passengers on board. While holding short of Runway 05R on Taxiway A1 in preparation for the takeoff, the flight crew received their takeoff clearance. After the clearance was read back, the aircraft started to taxi to position. Shortly thereafter, a possible conflicting target on final for Runway 05R was identified on the TCAS. As the aircraft had partially crossed the hold short line, the flight crew stopped. ATC was queried and the tower controller advised ROU1981 to hold short of 05R. The conflicting aircraft on final was subsequently observed in the go-around.

C-FBVH, a Hughes 369D aircraft operated by Oceanview Helicopters, was conducting animal capture work near Revelstoke, BC (CYRV). During a landing in deep snow, the tail rotor contacted the snow. The pilot, who was the only person on board, was not injured. The operator’s maintenance attended the site and found that only the tail rotor driveshaft had visible damage. The driveshaft was replaced and, as a precaution, the tail boom, tail rotor gearbox and tail rotor assembly were also replaced.

C-FNSA, a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Sunwest Aviation, was conducting flight CNK7124 from Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). During the intermediate approach to CYYC, the flight encountered severe turbulence in the vicinity of intersection MESKA, resulting in a momentary loss of control. No injuries were reported amongst the crew and passengers and the aircraft landed without further incident. The aircraft was not damaged.

C-GWRE, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3191 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Grand Prairie, AB (CYQU). During cruise, a cabin crew member was injured. EMS was called to meet and assess the person upon arrival in CYQU.

C-GJZG, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8936 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Greater Moncton/Roméo Leblanc Intl, NB (CYQM). During cruise, the flight crew noted a number 1 engine hydraulic caution message. This condition caused the loss of flaps, so a flapless landing was planned. No emergency was declared, however the flight crew requested to have ARFF on standby to check the brakes after landing. The aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GBIP, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA715 from New York/LaGuardia, NY (KLGA) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During the climb after the departure from KLGA, the cabin crew observed smoke in the cabin/galley section for a few moments. There was no alarm, no dirty pack smell and no electrical smell. The cabin was reported as very warm. The flight continued to CYYZ without further event. A post maintenance inspection of the forward and aft galleys was conducted on the related equipment. Contaminated heating pads were found in the aft galley and were cleaned.

C-FIQR, un appareil de type Aérospatiale ATR 42-300 exploité par First Air, effectuait le vol FAB5482 selon les règles de vol aux instruments d'Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) à destination de Pond Inlet, NU (CYIO) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. Alors qu’il était en vol de croisière vers CYIO, l'équipage a noté une indication de pression d'huile anormale du moteur gauche (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW120). Par mesures de précaution, l'équipage a pris la décision de fermer le moteur et a déclaré une urgence. L'appareil s'est posé sans problème à CYIO. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.

C-GMDP, un hélicoptère de type Robinson R44 exploité privément, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol à vue, de Sainte-Pétronille, QC à destination de l'aéroport Jean Lesage Intl de Québec, QC (CYQB) avec seul le pilote à bord, lorsqu'au décollage, le patin droit est resté pris dans la glace et l'aéronef a basculé sur le côté causant des dommages considérables. Le pilote a été blessé légèrement.

N641UA, a B767-300 operated by United Airlines was conducting flight 938 from Chicago O'Hare Intl., IL (KORD) to London Heathrow,UK (EGLL) with 11 crew and 178 passengers. While in cruise at FL350 and passing 58N and 050W the crew observed an EICAS "Low Fuel" caution message and noted a fuel imbalance. The EICAS message cleared but the imbalance remained. The crew consulted with both maintenance and dispatch, declared a MAYDAY and diverted to Keflavik Intl., Iceland (BIKFK). Ground maintenance checks found no fuel or fuel system issues. The aircraft was refueled and departed for destination after a several hour delay.

N928EV, un CRJ-200 exploité par SkyWest Airlines sous l'indicatif SKW3130, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Chicago, IL (KORD) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). L'équipage avise le centre de contrôle de Montréal qu'ils éprouvent des difficultés avec les volets et déclare une urgence. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre sur la piste 06L et il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-GKEK, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (CRJ200) aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7356 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Baltimore/Washington Intl Thurgood Marshall, MD (KBWI). Approximately 20 minutes after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew received a wing overheat message. An emergency was declared and the flight returned to CYYZ where it landed uneventfully.After several tests, the operator’s maintenance was unable to duplicate the problem, or find the source of the wing overheat indication.

C-GENM, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3115 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Kamloops, BC (CYKA). During the approach to CYKA, the landing gear did not extend when selected to the down position. The flight crew conducted a missed approach, declared a PAN PAN, climbed to a safe altitude and completed the landing gear alternate extension checklist. Subsequently, the landing gear was lowered successfully. The flight landed without further issue with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance replaced the nose landing gear actuator and the aircraft was returned to service.

N468QS, a NetJets Inc. Gulstream G450 aircraft was conducting a flight from Dallas/Love Intl, TX (KDAL) to London/Farnborough Intl, UK (EGLF). At about 49°00' N, 040°00' W the flight crew observed a 10 – 15 cm area of the co pilot’s windshield upper left corner glowing orange, with brighter arcing spots noted within this area. A PAN PAN was declared with a diversion to St. John’s, NL (CYYT). The flight landed uneventfully.

C-GGMN, a Dehavilland Dash 8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz was conducting flight 8960 from Toronto/ Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Fredericton, NB (CYFC). In descent from 22000 to 19000 feet, approximately 50 NM west of CYFC, the aircraft experienced severe turbulence. The aircraft exceeded the safe operation speed and had several roll upsets. The passengers and crew had their seatbelts fastened, there were no injuries.

C-FJCQ, an Aerospatiale ATR 72-202 aircraft operated by Calm Air International LP, was conducting flight CAV112 between Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) and Thompson, MB (CYTH). Approximately 75 nautical miles south of Norway House, MB (CYNE), the entire outer pane of the captain's windscreen cracked. The flight crew completed the checklist items, declared a Mayday and requested clearance to descend from FL220 to 9000 feet ASL. The flight continued to CYTH uneventfully.

C-FJNX, an Airbus 321-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1206 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to West Palm Beach Intl, FL (KPBI). As the flight was starting its take-off roll on Runway 06L at CYYZ, a maintenance vehicle crossed over the hold short line of Runway 06L at Taxiway D7, which is located at the end of the runway. The vehicle stopped approximately 200 feet short of the runway surface and ATC instructed the vehicle to return behind the hold short line. The vehicle was clear of the protected area before ACA1206 passed the intersection of Runway 06L and Taxiway D4.

C-GJEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3161 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Nanaimo, BC (CYCD) with 4 crew members and 57 passengers on board. During the approach at CYCD, the flight crew declared an emergency due to smoke in the cabin. The aircraft landed at CYCD and all on board evacuated on the runway. There were no reported injuries.Teardown of the left engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW150A) determined that the 2.5 bearing carbon seal (p/n 3071831-01) had failed which allowed turbine oil to enter the cabin air pressurization.

C-GSLX, a Beechcraft 1900D aircraft operated by Sunwest Aviation was conducting flight CNK448 from Edmonton Intl., AB (CYEG) to Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC) with 2 flight crew members and 8 passengers on board. During the approach to CYYC, the flight crew received a Master Warning for Low Oil Pressure on the #2 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada, PT6A-67D). The Oil pressure was confirmed to be decreasing and the flight crew elected to shut down the #2 engine. An emergency was declared, and CNK448 landed without further incident.The operator's maintenance found an oil leak originating on the RH engine accessory case drive pad for the low pressure fuel pump. The seal was replaced.

C-GPKM, a Cessna 150M aircraft registered to Aéroclub de Montreal and operated by Air Richelieu, was conducting a student solo day-VFR cross-country flight from Montreal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) to Kingston, ON (CYGK). During cruise flight at 4500 feet ASL, the aircraft experienced a complete engine power loss. The pilot attempted to restart the engine, however without success. After several orbits, the pilot elected to conduct a forced landing on a road, 1.5 nm North of Cardinal, ON. At the end of the landing roll, the aircraft collided with trees on the side of the road and sustained significant damage. The pilot was wearing the lap belt portion of the seat belt, but had not attached the shoulder harness. During the accident, the pilot received serious injuries and was transported to a local hospital. The ELT signal activated and was identified on frequency 121.5 by a commercial carrier flying overhead.The reported weather at CYGK at the time of the occurrence was suitable for VFR flight, with winds from the north-east at 11 knots, visibility greater than 15 statute miles, few clouds at 25 000 feet, air temperature of -4°C and the dew point of -14°C). Initial examination of the aircraft did not determine the cause of the engine power loss. A significant amount of fuel was found in the wing tanks.

C-GDEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore was conducting flight WEN3395 from Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC) to Edmonton Intl., AB (CYEG). During the approach for CYEG, an Embraer EMJ-190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA360 from CYEG to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl., ON (CYOW). ACA360 started the departure roll on Runway 12 before WEN3395 was on 2 miles final. WestJet initiated a missed approach at IFR minimums due to not obtaining visual contact with the runway. Radar separation was reduced to 1.9 nm horizontally where 3 nm is required. WestJet conducted another approach to CYEG, but at 14 miles final diverted to CYYC. Air Canada continued the departure with no further issues.

C-FLSO, a privately operated ski-equipped Cessna 180B, was conducting a flight from a property east of Nipawin, SK (CYBU) to Oskikebuk Lake, SK with the pilot and 1 passenger on board. The right landing gear leg failed during the takeoff run. The right wing contacted the snow and the aircraft turned to the right. The occupants were uninjured. The aircraft sustained damage to the right landing gear leg, right wing, right elevator, engine cowl and propeller.

C-FBJP, a privately operated Piper PA-28-140 aircraft was operating on a local flight from Hinton/Entrance, AB (CEE4) with 1 pilot and 1 passenger on board. At the time of the occurrence, the CEE4 runway surface condition was a mix of ice and slush. The pilot conducted the takeoff roll and rotated. The aircraft lifted a few feet off the ground and then descended onto the runway surface losing directional control. The aircraft deviated to the left and contacted a snow windrow along the side of the runway with the left wing tip. The pilot and passenger were not injured, and the ELT did not activate. The left wing tip and propeller were damaged.

C-FRFO, a Cessna 172M aircraft operated by Bancroft Flying Club, was conducting a flight from Brantford, ON (CYFD) to Kirkfield/Balsam Lake, ON (CKD8) with one pilot on board. During the landing at CKD8, the aircraft landed fast and the pilot realized the aircraft was not going to stop at the end of the runway. The decision was made to not conduct a go-around due to hydro wires. The aircraft went off the end of the runway, hit some cedars and came to rest in a ditch. The pilot was not injured, but there was substantial damage to the aircraft.

C-FZUB, an Airbus A320 aircraft operated by Air Canada as flight ACA1294, departed Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) for Reina Beatrix International Airport - Oranjestadwhen (TNCA). During the climb-out the flight crew received a NAV ADR 1 fault. The aircraft returned to CYYZ and a PAN PAN was declared. The aircraft landed uneventfully.Maintenance replaced ADIRU #1 as per the maintenance manual.

C-FCWW, a Piper PA-31-350 aircraft operated by Super T Aviation Academy was conducting a local training flight from Medicine Hat, AB (CYXH). While on final approach, following several simulated approaches, the first officer called for landing gear down. The captain selected landing gear down and placed a hand on the gear lever to prevent it from snapping up to the neutral position. The handle did not return to neutral, and landing gear indication showed 3 green. The captain took control of FCWW.  The emergency gear extension checklist was actioned with no change to the landing gear handle. A low fly pass was conducted for FSS to conduct visual verification of the landing gear position. The landing gear was confirmed to be down, however; FSS could not confirm landing gear door position. Another aircraft in the circuit broadcast that the gear doors were still open. The captain declared an emergency and landed without further incident.

C-GFAJ, an Air Canada Airbus A330-300 aircraft, operating as flight ACA 983, was en route from Sangster Intl - Montego Bay (MKJS) to Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) when the yellow hydraulic system failed. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN on approach to CYYZ and they requested a long runway due to an expected longer than normal rollout. The aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by.Maintenance removed and replaced the yellow high pressure manifold supply check valve packing and seal as per the appropriate maintenance manual procedures.

C-FDSN, an Airbus 320-211 aircraft operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA571 from San Francisco Intl., CA (KSFO) to Vancouver Intl., BC (CYVR) with 5 crew members and 54 passengers on board. During the takeoff from KSFO, at 500 feet the flight crew received a TCAS RA to monitor vertical speed, due to an aircraft 300 feet below. The crew followed RA and the flight continued without further incident.

C-FMWY, a Boeing 767-333 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1672 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) to Orlando Intl., FL (KMCO) with 8 crew members and 279 passengers on board. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated, and could no longer perform their duties. Cabin crew positions were reassigned, and the flight landed without incident.

C-FDJA, un appareil de type Bombardier CRJ-200 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA8032, était stationné à la barrière 78 avec l'équipage à bord en préparation pour un vol à destination de Philadelphie Intl., PA (KPHL). Un véhicule sanitaire de Swissport a heurté le JZA8032 causant des dommages substantiels à deux ailerons de l'aile droite ainsi qu'à un panneau en fibre de verre sous l'appareil. Le JZA8032 a été remorqué au hangar de maintenance pour effectuer les réparations. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FJVV, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-300 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP sous l'indicatif JZA717, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl., QC (CYQB) à Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl., QC (CYUL). C-FPSC, un Jetstream 32 exploité par Pascan sous l'indicatif PSC455, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl., QC (CYQB) à Îles-de-la-Madeleine, QC (CYGR). Le PSC455 a reçu et relu l'instruction de maintenir le cap 210 lors de son décollage de la piste 24. Cependant, lors de sa montée initiale, le PSC455 a dévié de son cap et a été instruit par l'ATC de procéder à un virage par la gauche au cap 210. L'espacement avec JZA717 a été réduit à 2.5 miles marins (nm) horizontalement et 900 pieds verticalement, alors que 3 nm et 1000 pieds étaient requis. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé ni dommage.

C-FKWE, un DHC-8-400 exploité par Westjet Encore Ltd sous l'indicatif WEN3433, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl., QC (CYUL). C-GTQC, un B737-800 exploité par Air Transat sous l'indicatif TSC502, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Québec/Jean Lesage, QC (CYQB) à Puerto Plata/Gregorio Luperón Intl., République Dominicaine (MDPP). Lors de la montée initiale après avoir décollé de la piste 29, le WEN3433 a effectué un virage vers la gauche au cap approximatif de 240 au lieu de 273 de sorte qu'une perte d'espacement est survenue avec TSC502 qui était en montée initiale au départ de la piste 24 malgré qu'il a reçu l'instruction de virer immédiatement au cap 210 en raison du WEN3433. L'espacement entre les deux aéronefs a été réduit à 2 miles marins (nm) horizontalement et 800 pieds verticalement alors que 3 nm et 1000 pieds étaient requis. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage.

C-GONW, a Bombardier DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8724 from Gaspe, QC (CYGP) to Iles-de-la-Madeleine, QC (CYGR). On approach into CYGR, JZA8724 encountered severe turbulence which required the crew to use full deflection on the controls. The crew executed a missed approach and continued to their alternate, Quebec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) without further incident. The operator's maintenance conducted a severe turbulence inspection and no damage was found.

D-ABUI, a Boeing 767-300ER aircraft operated by Condor Flugdienst, was conducting flight DE2185 from Havana/José Martí Intl., Cuba (MUHA) to Frankfurt/Rhein-Main, Germany (EDDF) with 10 crew members and 253 passengers on board. While in cruise flight, one of the flight crew members became incapacitated and the third pilot took over this member's duties. A mayday was declared and DE2185 continued on route while the flight crew member's condition was being assessed. Initially, a diversion to St. John's Intl airport, NL (CYYT) was requested, however due to the weather conditions at CYYT, DE2185 subsequently diverted to Halifax/Stanfield Intl Airport, NS (CYHZ). About 1 hour prior to landing, the mayday was cancelled and a Pan Pan was declared.DE2185 landed at CYHZ without further incident.

C-FPDK, a Piper PA-31-350 aircraft operated by KD Air Corporation, was conducting flight KD421 from Qualicum Beach, BC (CAT4) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). Shortly after the departure from CAT4 at 900 feet ASL, the right engine suffered a power loss. The pilot immediately initiated a return to CAT4 and, upon landing, the engine stopped completely. There were no reported injuries. The aircraft remained grounded at CAT4 until its replacement.

C-FOKX, a privately registered Bushmaster XP 230 aircraft, was conducting a flight from Sechelt, BC (CAP3) to Quamichan Lake (Raven Field), BC (CML2) with only the pilot on board. During the landing on Runway 34, the aircraft bounced and landed hard on the left landing gear, damaging the left hand landing gear strut. The aircraft veered to the left and impacted a large concrete fence located on the side of the runway. The aircraft sustained damage to the left hand landing gear, wing, horizontal stabilizer and propeller. The pilot was uninjured.

C-GJZK, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was operating flight JZA546 from Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT) to Toronto//Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ). C-FWXL, a Beech 1900D operated by Wasaya Airways, was operating flight WSG828 from Sioux Lookout, ON (CYXL) to CYQT. During taxi for departure, JZA546 had been cleared by CYQT Tower to position and hold on Runway 25 at CYQT while WSG828 was on short final with a landing clearance for Runway 12. CYQT tower observed JZA546 initiating a takeoff roll without a clearance and instructed JZA546 to stop. JZA546 stopped the takeoff roll and was instructed by tower to exit Runway 25 and wait on taxiway B as there was an inbound medevac flight (C-FPCL, a Pilatus PC-12 operated by Air Bravo as flight AB258) inbound to land on Runway 25.

C-FKLB, un appareil de type C550 exploité par Transports Canada effectuait le vol TGO857, selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl., QC (CYUL) à Rouyn-Noranda, QC (CYUY). N24128, un E145 exploité par Trans States Airlines sous l'indicatif LOF4668, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Washington Dulles Intl., DC (KIAD) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). Le TGO857 a été autorisé à monter à 7000 pieds au-dessus du niveau de la mer (ASL) après avoir décollé de la piste 06R. Le LOF4668 était en rapprochement à 8000 pieds ASL pour un atterrissage sur la piste 06R. Le TGO857 est monté à 7400 pieds ASL suite à un avis de résolution de monter du système de surveillance du trafic et d'évitement des collisions (TCAS), ce qui a réduit l'espacement à 600 pieds alors qu'un minimum de 1000 pieds était requis. Il n'y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage. LOF4668 en palier à 8000 pieds n'a eu aucun avis de résolution TCAS.

C-GJOA, a privately operated Piper PA-28-140 aircraft was conducting a familiarization flight from Indus/Winters Aire Park, AB (CFY4) to High River, AB (CEN4) with 2 souls on board. At the time of the occurrence, the turf runway was frozen with patches of ice and snow. GJOA began the take-off roll on Runway 16 with flaps set to 1 notch with the flight instructor as PIC. During the take-off roll, directional control was lost and the aircraft drifted to the right. GJOA contacted a snow windrow and the nose landing gear was sheared. Both the flight instructor and student pilot were wearing lap belts; the aircraft was not equipped with shoulder belts. The instructor and student pilot received no injuries. The ELT was not activated.

D-AIKG, an Airbus 330-300 aircraft operated by Lufthansa, was conducting flight DLH409 from Newark/Liberty Intl, NJ (KEWR) to Düsseldorf Intl, Germany (EDDL). At about 49°18' N, 037°18' W the captain contacted Gander ACC, declared a MAYDAY, and advised that the co-pilot had become incapacitated. The captain requested a diversion to a Canadian airport, and was recleared to Halifax/Stanfield, NS (CYHZ) due to poor weather at St. John’s Intl, NL (CYYT). The route was revised to land at CYYT when weather improved, and the captain requested medical services meet the flight on arrival. The flight landed single-pilot at CYYT without further incident.

C-FWSX, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet was conducting flight WJA190 from Abbotsford, BC (CYXX) to Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC). The flight was cleared to CYYC via RNAV Y Runway 17R. WestJet flight WJA2289, a Boeing 737-800 was operating from Los Cabos Intl., Mexico (MMSD) to Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC). WJA2289 was cleared to CYYC via RNAV Y Runway 17L. While both aircraft were on approach, before being established on final, aircraft separation decreased to 2.5 miles and 1000 feet when 3.0 miles is required.

C-FMZB, an Embraer 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA167 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) to Edmonton Intl., AB (CYEG)  with 4 crew members and 66 passengers on board. During descent from cruising altitude inbound to CYEG, the flight crew observed several engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS) warnings. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN emergency, and continued to CYEG where the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced the Actuator Input/Output Processor module.

C-FHMA, a Mitsubishi MU-2B-60 aircraft operated by Skynorth Air Ltd, was conducting a local flight from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl., MB (CYWG). While on final approach to Runway 31, the landing gear down was selected followed by a loud bang. The flight crew did not receive a landing gear down-and-locked indication. The approach was continued to perform a low-and-over fly-past during which ATC confirmed that the landing gear was not visible. The crew flew out to a hold and performed an emergency gear extension. The landing gear extended and the crew received a 3 green indication. The crew requested ARFF on standby and the subsequent landing was uneventful.The operator's maintenance replaced the safety shear pin, reset the emergency extension system and adjusted the forward actuator striker plate on the right hand door. Landing gear swings were carried out satisfactorily.

C-FPDN, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA970 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Puerto Vallarta/Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz Intl, México (MMPR). After the departure from CYVR, the flight crew received multiple Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitoring (ECAM) messages for smoke in the lavatory. The flight crew completed the appropriate checklist and declared a PAN PAN. There was no fire on board the aircraft, however the flight returned to CYVR where it landed without further incident. After an inspection, the Smoke Detection Control Unit (SDCU) and the lavatory smoke detector were replaced.

C-GFLA, a Pilatus PC12 aircraft operated by Keewatin Air was conducting flight KEW400 from Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) with a planned return to CYFB with 2 flight crew members on board. While conducting an approach to CYFB, the flight crew declared and emergency due to a left main gear unsafe indication. The aircraft landed without further incident, and remained on the runway until it was towed off.

C-FCDM, a privately operated Maule M-7-235C aircraft, was on a flight from Langley Regional, BC (CYNJ) with stops in Hope, Osoyoos and Beaverdell, BC before returning to CYNJ. The pilot had completed two passes over the airstrip at Beaverdell and determined that the snow-covered runway was suitable for landing. Shortly after the touchdown, the main wheels dug into the snow and the aircraft flipped over. The aircraft sustained damage to the wing, wing struts, propeller and windshield. The pilot was uninjured.

C-GSJB, an Airbus A319-112 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1875 from Havana/José Martí Intl., Cuba (MUHA) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) with 5 crew members and 136 passengers on board. During cruise, the flight crew identified an abnormal humming noise emanating from under the forward galley. The noise stopped abruptly, and an odour accompanied by a slight amount of smoke was detected in the flight deck. The flight crew diverted to Jacksonville Intl., FL (KJAX), declared a PAN PAN and completed the landing with ARFF on standby. The smoke and odour dissipated prior to landing, and the aircraft arrived at the gate without further incident.

C-GCQR, a Bell 429 helicopter operated by the Canadian Coast Guard, was conducting flight CTG443 from Port Hardy, BC (CYZT). During a slung load operation, several pieces of lumber fell from the load and landed in the ocean. CTG443 returned to CYZT where the load was repacked for later transport to Herbert Island.

N815AA, a Boeing 787-8 aircraft operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL90 from Chicago/O'Hare Intl., IL (KORD) to London/Heathrow, UK (EGLL). While in cruise flight, about 125 nautical miles SW of Gander Intl, NL (CYQX), a passenger medical emergency was reported. The flight crew declared a medical emergency and requested a diversion to CYQX. About 20 minutes later the crew declared a Mayday because the aircraft would be above its maximum allowable landing weight at the time of the emergency landing. The aircraft landed without incident.Company personnel determined that the landing was conducted within the aircraft maintenance manual limits, and no maintenance action was required.

C-GJZZ, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 (CRJ200) aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8462 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl, MA (KBOS) with 3 crew members and 29 passengers on board. During cruise with the autopilot on, the flight crew reported airframe buffeting at FL270 and operating at an airspeed of 300 knots. No anomalies were reported with the engines or the flight controls. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and elected to return to CYUL. The flight landed uneventfully.

C-FMKY, a Cessna 210A aircraft was conducting a local flight from Fort McMurray, AB (CYMM) with 1 pilot on board. After approximately one hour of flying, and having completed several circuits for Runway 07 the aircraft lost engine power (Teledyne Continental IO-470-E) on an extended final approach. The pilot continued the approach, but did not have sufficient altitude to make the runway. The pilot contacted the tower, informed them of the engine power loss, and the intention to perform a forced landing. An emergency was not declared. The forced landing was executed on a snow covered portion of the airfield, within the confines of the airport in the direction of Runway 07. Shortly after touchdown, the aircraft nosed over and came to a rest upside down, approximately 1000 feet short of the threshold of Runway 07. The pilot sustained minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. ARFF was dispatched to the scene.

C-GTSO, an Airbus 330-342 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC397 from Paris/Charles de Gaulle, France (LFPG) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) with 11 crew members and 308 passengers on board. After receiving their takeoff clearance and while lining up on Runway 27L at LFPG, the flight crew of TSC397 observed an Airbus 320 landing on Runway 27R. Before commencing their take off roll, both TSC397 flight crew heard ATC instruct the Airbus 320 flight crew to hold short of Runway 27L, and this restriction was read back correctly. During TSC397's takeoff roll, at approximately 120 knots, ATC asked the Airbus 320 flight crew if they were stopped and instructed them to hold short a second time to which the flight crew replied that they were stopped and holding short of Runway 27L. When TSC397 passed the Airbus 320, the flight crew observed that it had stopped on the wrong side of the hold line.

C-GLQG, a de Havilland DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Porter Airlines, was conducting flight POE1480 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) to Montreal/Trudeau, QC (CYUL) with 72 passengers and 4 crewmembers on board. While in cruise flight about 45 nm southwest Fredericton INTL airport, NB (CYFC), passengers alerted the cabin crew of burning odour and sparks emanating from behind overhead bin near cabin wall above seat 14A on left side of cabin. The cabin crew alerted the pilots of the condition and inspected the area further. The odour began to dissipate, and no further sign of fire was present. The pilots began the smoke drill and donned their oxygen masks, then declared a MAYDAY and initiated a diversion to CYFC. The pilots observed cautions related to the loss of LH AC power (TRU, windshield heat control, stick pusher and #1 pitot heat), and other caution lights flickered momentarily. Once on the approach at CYFC, the flight flew through an area of icing and observed IAS mismatch, AP disconnect, and YD fail caution messages consistent with a blocked pitot tube. The flight landed on runway 09 at CYFC uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The crew shut down the aircraft and conducted a rapid deplanement on the runway. No injuries were reported and passengers were transported to the terminal. The source of the smoke and heat was determined to be arcing of the 115 Volt, 3-phase AC supply feeder in the LH wing root to fuselage connector plug assembly (9811-J711). The 50-amp circuit breaker in the LH nacelle junction box was found tripped. The affected components were retained by the TSB for further examination.

C-GJTA, a Discovery Air Defence Services Dornier Alphajet, was on a night mission in the Williamtown-Newcastle airport flying area (YWLM) when the AHRS failed (toppled main AI with OFF flags, a loss of pitch information in the HUD and a loss of directional information on the EHSI). An emergency was declared and the standby AI and standby compass were used to return to return to YWLM.  At 1600 feet AGL and 7nm from the airfield, the aircraft broke out of clouds, flew a straight-in visual and landed uneventfully.

C-GBHY, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1650 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Miami Intl, FL (KMIA) with 129 passengers and 5 crew members on board. While in cruise flight in the vicinity of Philadelphia, PA, the flight crew identified a low oil quantity indication on the number 2 engine. After monitoring the indication for a period of time, the flight crew elected to shut the engine down as a precaution. A PAN PAN was declared and a diversion to Washington/Dulles Intl, VA (KIAD) was initiated where the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-FHNC , a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by North Cariboo, was conducting flight NCB3580 from Edmonton Intl., AB (CYEG) to Primrose, AB (CFN6) with 3 crew members and 31 passengers on board. During touch down, NCB3580 inadvertently landed on the west side of Runway 14, just beside the runway. The aircraft came to a stop 500 feet short of the PAPI lights for Runway 32, and the flight crew taxied to the apron. There was no damage to the aircraft, and no reported injuries to passengers or crew.

C-GDFF, a Beechcraft C90A aircraft operated by Moncton Flight College, was conducting a local training flight from Fredericton Intl, NB (CYFC). Shortly after departure, the crew noted fuel leaking from the left wing filler cap and requested to return to CYFC via radar vectors. The crew declared an emergency and landed at CYFC without further incident.The operator's maintenance determined that the fuel filler cap was not installed correctly after refueling.

C-GJDA, an Airbus 330-200 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting flight TSC664 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Port-au-Prince/Toussaint Louverture Intl, Haiti (MTPP) with 312 passengers and 11 crew members on board.
