During cruise flight approximately 350 nautical miles North-Northeast of MTPP, one of the cabin crew members sustained a minor injury and was unable to continue their duties. Positions were reassigned among the other cabin crew members for the remainder of the flight. The aircraft landed in MTPP without further incident.

C-GWSX, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA2057 from Cancún Intl, Mexico (MMUN) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with 6 crew members and 150 passengers on board. During the descent into CYVR, the flight crew observed a trailing edge flap asymmetry indication. The appropriate checklist items were completed and the flight crew declared an emergency. After requesting Runway 08R, the flight landed without further incident. A post flight inspection revealed a faulty left hand flap position transmitter. The component was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FRAM, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA027 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Shanghai/Pudong Intl, China (ZSPD) with 17 crew members and 396 passengers on board. During cruise flight approximately 600 nm North of CYYZ, the flight crew noted a hydraulic problem. After consultation with the operator’s operational and maintenance control centres, the aircraft was returned to CYYZ and landed without further event with ARFF standing by. The aircraft stopped on the runway and was inspected for hot brakes before proceeding to the gate.

C-FSBV, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by  Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA101 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) to Vancouver Intl., BC (CYVR) with 10 crew members and 267 passengers on board. While the aircraft was preparing to pushback from the gate, a passenger's mobile phone caught fire. The fire was extinguished by flight crew members and EMS attended to the passenger. There was no damage to the aircraft.

C-GAAR, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Air Georgian was conducting flight GGN7221 from Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC) to Lethbridge, AB (CYQL) with 2 flight crew members and 15 passengers on board. On approach into CYQL, the flight crew selected the landing gear to the down position. The crew did not receive a green, gear down and locked indication for the nose landing gear, and the landing gear handle red unsafe light remained illuminated. The crew executed a go around and requested to divert back to CYYC leaving the gear in the extended position. On the return to CYYC, the emergency landing gear extension procedure was performed with no change in the cockpit indication. An emergency was declared with ATS. An uneventful landing was completed, and the flight crew elected to shut down the aircraft on Runway 35L where ARFF met the aircraft on the runway. All passengers were deplaned and transported back to the airport terminal.The operator’s maintenance determined that the bracket on the NLG drag brace that actuates the plunger for the NLG down lock indication had detached. As a result, the switch was not actuated even though the NLG was down and locked.

TF-ISR, a Boeing 757-256 aircraft operated by Icelandair, was conducting flight ICE671 from Reykjavík/Keflavik, Iceland (BIKF) to Denver Intl., CO (KDEN) with 6 crew members and 113 passengers on board. At about 59°28' N, 058°00' W, the flight crew received a number 2 engine fire warning. The crew shut down the engine, carried out the QRH checklist, and declared a MAYDAY. The crew coordinated with ATC for descent and diversion to Goose Bay, NL (CYYR), and then briefed cabin crew and passengers. The flight landed at CYYR without further incident.The operator's maintenance repaired the defective number 2 engine fire detection system.

C-GKEZ, an Air Georgian Limited CL-600-2B19 aircraft was operating as flight 7388, from Kansas City International - Kansas City (KMCI) to Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ). While en route with the APU operating the flight crew noted a fuel odor in the cockpit and the cabin crew reported smoke in row 2. The flight crew shut down the APU and the odor and smoke subsided. The flight crew declared an emergency and an uneventful landing was performed with ARFF standing by. Maintenance checked the APU compartment and found no fuel leaks. The L/H and R/H pack coaleser bags were replaced and subsequent operational checks revealed no further faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GTMB, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Services, was conducting flight EVS7787 from St. John's, NL (CYYT) to Gander Intl, NL (CYQX). During the approach to CYQX, the flight crew noted that the right main landing gear did not indicate green (down and locked) after the landing gear was selected to the extended position. The flight crew carried out a missed approach and declared an emergency. The aircraft was vectored for an ILS approach at CYQX Runway 03, where it landed without further incident. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and determined that 2 bulbs were burnt out in the right landing gear DOWN indication display.

C-FGQK, un appareil de type DHC-8-100 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA697 selon les règles de vol aux instruments à partir de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) à Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl., QB (CYUL). Alors que JZA697 effectuait une approche visuelle vers la piste 06R de CYUL, JZA697 a dépassé l'axe d'approche de sorte que l'espacement avec N683AE, un E145 de Piedmont Airlines qui était en approche de la piste 06L a été réduit à 0.5 mille et 600 pieds alors que la norme est de 1000 pieds et 3 milles.

C-GVIJ, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Cargojet, was conducting flight CJT301 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). During the approach into CYVR, the flight crew declared an emergency due to a center hydraulic system issue. An alternate landing gear extension was executed and the aircraft landed without further event.The operator’s maintenance found that the number 8 spoiler PCA (P/N 1542500) was leaking. The actuator was replaced, the hydraulic fluid was replenished, and a Landing Gear Alternate Extension Inspection was performed.

C-GWEJ, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3110 from Vancouver Intl., BC (CYVR) to Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC) with 4 crew members and 69 passengers on board. On approach to CYYC, approximately 18 minutes prior to landing the flight crew declared a PAN PAN due to a flight control issue. ARFF services were dispatched. The aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance replaced the roll actuator, and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GLPJ, un appareil de type Beech 1900C exploité par Propair, effectuait le vol PRO4601 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Toronto/Buttonville, ON (CYKZ) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl., QC (CYUL). C-FNAD, un Boeing 737-800 exploité par Sunwing sous l'indicatif SWG123, effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Punta Cana Intl., (MDPC) à Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl., QC (CYUL). Alors que SWG123 amorçait son virage, pour intercepter la phase d’approche finale de la piste 06L de CYUL en descente pour 3000 pieds ASL, une perte d’espacement est survenue avec PRO4601 établi en approche finale pour la piste 06R à 4000 pieds ASL. Les 2 appareils se sont rapprochés à 2.5 mn et 500 pieds alors que le minimum d’espacement requis était 3 mn et 1000 pieds.

C-GHHG, a Bell 206B aircraft operated by Highland Helicopters, was recovering a snowmobile with a long line at Roundtop Mountain near Quesnel, BC (CYQZ). While on short final, an uncommanded release of the belly hook occurred, and the longline with the load fell from an approximate height of 50 feet. There were no injuries to persons. The aircraft has been restricted from any further external load operations pending examination of the cargo hook.

ROU1887, an Airbus 321 aircraft was conducting a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) to San Diego Intl., CA (KSAN). ROU1887 departed Runway 23 at CYYZ behind JZA865, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP that was conducting a flight from CYYZ to Windsor, ON (CYQG). During the departure, separation was reduced to 1.9 nautical miles and 900 feet, where 1000 feet or 3 miles is required.The air traffic controller issued a turn to ROU1887 to re-establish required clearance between the two aircraft.

C-GWIU, un appareil de type Cessna 172M en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local à partir d’Ottawa/Gatineau, QC (CYND) selon les règles de vol à vue avec seul un pilote à bord. Lors de l'atterrissage au retour à CYND, l'appareil s'est déporté vers la droite et le train principal droit a heurté la glace en bordure de piste. Le pilote a aussitôt remis les gaz et repris l'air. Le pilote a ensuite fait un passage à basse altitude au cours duquel on lui a communiqué que la jambe droite du train d’atterrissage paraissait endommagée. Les services d'urgence ont été offerts, mais le pilote a refusé et choisi de tenter un atterrissage. Lors de l'atterrissage, l'aéronef a bifurqué vers la droite et sorti de piste avant de s'immobiliser sur le dos. Les services d'urgence sont intervenus pour contenir la fuite du carburant. Le pilote n’a pas été blessé.

C-FKCI, a Bombardier BD-100-1A10 Challenger 300 aircraft operated by Irving Oil Transport, was conducting a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Saint John, NB (CYSJ) with 2 pilots and 10 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYYZ, the flight crew noticed high engine vibrations on the number 1 engine (Honeywell AS 907-1-1A). The aircraft diverted back to CYYZ and, on final approach, the flight crew shut the number 1 engine down. No emergency was declared and the aircraft landed without further incident. The cause of the engine vibrations has not been determined, however the operator contacted the manufacturer for assistance. The engine will be replaced prior to the fault being determined.

C-GANS, a Bombardier DHC-8-102 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG824 from Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT) to Sioux Lookout, ON (CYXL) with 3 crew members and 14 passengers on board. During the landing flare, the aircraft encountered a gusting crosswind and suddenly dropped. The aircraft bounced on the runway and, on the subsequent touchdown, the nose wheel came down hard with the main landing gear. There were no injuries and the aircraft then taxied to the ramp. The operator's maintenance revealed that the nose landing gear limiter ring had sheared; the nose gear assembly was replaced.

N801FD, an Airbus 310-324 aircraft operated by Federal Express, was conducting flight FDX134 from Memphis Intl, TN (KMEM) to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG) with a crew of two on board. During the final approach for Runway 18 at CYWG, the flight crew declared an emergency due to stuck slats. The aircraft then landed without incident. It was reported that the aircraft had departed KMEM in heavy rain conditions. An inspection by the operator's maintenance of the slats/flap system did not reveal any anomalies. The system was ground checked several times and the aircraft was returned to service.

A Boeing 747-400 aircraft operated by KLM was conducting flight KLM86 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) to Amsterdam/Schiphol, Netherlands (EHAM). During the taxi for departure, the aircraft was instructed to hold short of Runway 23, at taxiway "Q". The aircraft crossed the hold short line, incurring on the Runway 23 protected area of Taxiway "Q", however did not contact the runway surface. At the time of the incursion, an Airbus 330-200 operated by Air Transat was conducting flight TSC649 from Puerto Vallarta/Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz Intl, Mexico (MMPR) to CYYZ, and was on final approach for Runway 23. Air Traffic Control (ATC) instructed TSC649 to go around.

N807NW, an Airbus 330-323 aircraft operated by Delta Air Lines, was conducting flight DAL72 from Atlanta/Hartsfield – Jackson Intl, GA (KATL) to Amsterdam/Schiphol, Netherlands (EHAM). Approximately 46 nm North of Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ), the flight crew perceived an engine compressor stall, and then received an electronic centralized aircraft monitor (ECAM) ENG 1 STALL message, accompanied subsequently by an ENG 1 FAIL message. The flight crew noted that the number 1 engine was not rotating and did not indicate engine oil pressure. ECAM actions and QRH procedures were executed. The flight crew declared an emergency and initiated a diversion to CYHZ where the flight landed without further incident.Maintenance personnel recovered metal from number 1, 1.5, and 2 bearings chip detectors. The engine was removed and shipped to a maintenance facility for root cause determination.

C-FGEK, a Cessna 152 aircraft operated by Fly Kingston Airways, was on a local training flight from Kingston, ON (CYGK) with one student pilot on board. Upon completion of the training, the pilot returned to CYGK and during the landing, the propeller struck the ground; the nose wheel then collapsed. The student pilot was not injured, however the aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FNVU, an Airbus 320-211 aircraft operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA782 from Los Angeles Intl., CA (KLAX) to Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl., QC (CYUL) with 6 crew members and 143 passengers on board. During cruise, the lavatory smoke warning alerted the flight crew; however, the message self extinguished. No evidence of smoke or fire was found.The operator’s maintenance carried out an operational test of the Multi-Function Control and Display Unit (MCDU) for each lavatory. No faults were found.

C-GQRA, a Cessna 172S aircraft operated by Waterloo-Wellington Flying Club, departed from Kitchener/Waterloo, ON (CYKF) on a round robin night VFR flight to Tobermory, ON (CNR4). Since CNR4 does not have winter maintenance as indicated in the Canada Flight Supplement, there was no intention to land there. However, upon arrival at CNR4, the pilot elected to land. The aircraft touched down on the snow covered runway and flipped over. The pilot was wearing a shoulder harness and was not injured. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-FZUG, an Airbus 319-114 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1899 from Las Vegas/McCarran Intl., NV (KLAS) to Vancouver Intl., BC (CYVR) with 5 crew members and 136 passengers on board. During cruise, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN message due to a green hydraulic system failure. The flight landed in CYVR and was towed to the gate.

Le 26 février 2018, un Beechcraft King Air A100 (immatriculation C-GJXF, numéro de série B 159) exploité par Strait Air (2000) Ltd. effectuait le vol nolisé NUK107 selon les règles de vol aux instruments en provenance de l’aéroport de Sept-Îles (Québec) à destination de l’aéroport de Havre St-Pierre (Québec), avec 2 membres d'équipage et 6 passagers à bord. Alors que les conditions de visibilité étaient réduites en raison de fortes averses de neige, l’aéronef a effectué une approche vers la piste 08, qui était enneigée, et s’est posé environ 3800 pieds après le seuil, soit à environ 700 pieds de l’extrémité de la piste. Il a continué sa course à l’atterrissage au-delà de la piste, pour finalement aller s’immobiliser dans un banc de neige, à environ 220 pieds au-delà de l’extrémité de la piste. L’accident s’est produit de jour, à 11 h 20, heure normale de l’Est. La radiobalise de repérage d’urgence émettant sur 406 MHz ne s’est pas déclenchée. L'appareil a subi des dommages importants. Il y a eu 4 blessés légers.

N211RH, a Fairchild SA227-AC aircraft operated by McNeely Charter Services, was conducting flight MDS211 from Laredo Intl, TX (KLRD) to Windsor, ON (CYQG). During the landing roll out on Runway 25 at CYQG at a ground speed of approximately 40 knots, the flight crew selected the nose wheel steering switch to on; the aircraft immediately veered to the left, exited the runway and came to a stop on the grass. There were no injuries to the two crew members or any reported damage to the aircraft. The aircraft was towed from the infield and subsequently taxied under its own power to the local FBO.

C-GYGY, a Piper Lance PA32R aircraft was conducting a flight from Grand Junction/Grand Junction Regional, CO (KGJT) to Albuquerque, NM with 1 pilot and 3 passengers on board. The aircraft collided with terrain 18 nm south of Monticello, UT. All occupants were fatally injured.

On 23 February 2018, at 1204 Pacific Standard Time, an Island Express Air Inc. Beechcraft King Air B100 aircraft (registration C-GIAE, serial number BE-8), departed Runway 07 at Abbotsford Airport, British Columbia (BC), on a day instrument flight rules flight to San Bernardino International Airport, California, United States. On board were the pilot and 9 passengers. It was snowing at the time of departure. A few seconds after taking off, the pilot raised the landing gear. At that same moment, the aircraft veered to the left and struck the ground just north of Runway 07. Five passengers and the pilot were seriously injured. The other 4 passengers received minor injuries. The aircraft was destroyed by impact forces. The aircraft's emergency locator transmitter activated and was detected by the Cospas-Sarsat search and rescue satellite system.UPDATED: 12 MAY 2020

C-GCTR, un appareil de type Cessna 152 exploité par Cargair, effectuait un vol local d'entrainement selon les règles de vol à vue à partir de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec 1 élève-pilote à bord. Lors de l’approche finale, l'aéronef était à environ 600 pieds au-dessus du seuil de la piste. L’élève-pilote a effectué une glissade afin de perdre de l’altitude, toutefois l’appareil a rebondi sur la piste avant d’atterrir durement, endommageant l'hélice, le capot moteur et la roue de nez qui s'est affaissée. Il n'y a pas eu de blessé.

C-FIYE, un appareil de type Boeing 767-300 exploité par Air Canada rouge, effectuait le vol ROU1605 selon les règles de vol aux instruments à partir de Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl, FL (KFLL) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Lors de l’approche à CYUL à une vitesse de 190 nœuds, une perte d'espacement est survenue lorsque C-FLSX, un DHC-8-100 exploité par Air Creebec sous l'indicatif CRQ204, évoluait à une vitesse de 220 nœuds et s'est rapproché à 4.1 nm derrière ROU1605. L’espacement requis était de 5 nm.

C-FTZG, a Piper PA-28-160 aircraft was conducting a local flight from Hinton/Entrance, AB (CEE4) with 1 pilot on board. While landing on the frozen turf runway, which had approximately 2 inches of recent snow accumulation, FTZG touched down and during rollout drifted to the left. The aircraft contacted a snow berm along the side of the runway. The nose landing gear struck the snow berm lifting the aircraft, and the right wing was damaged as it made contact with the ground. The pilot was not injured, and the ELT was not activated. The aircraft was substantially damaged.

C-GURG, un  Canadair CL60 exploité par le Service aérien gouvernemental du Québec, effectuait le vol QUE10 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Québec/Jean-Lesage Intl., QC (CYQB) pour un vol Médévac à destination de Îles-de-la-Madeleine, QC (CYGR). Alors que l'appareil effectuait une approche pour CYGR,  une indication de  « Weight on Wheel (WOW) input fail. » est apparue. L'équipage de conduite a demandé un retour vers CYQB et, par mesure de précaution, a demandé que les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) soient déployés. L'appareil s'est posé sans encombre. Le personnel de l'entretien de l'exploitant a remplacé un détecteur de proximité.

C-FFWJ, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA177 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG). While on approach into CYEG, the flight crew declared an emergency due to a flap issue. Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) were requested to be standing by and the aircraft landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance changed several parts related to the flap system and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GHKW, an Airbus 330-343 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA874 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl., QC (CYUL) to Frankfurt/Rhein-Main Intl., Germany (EDDF) with 10 crew members and 268 passengers on board. During cruise, a cabin crew member was unable to perform their duties. Duties were reassigned and the flight landed uneventfully.

C-FIVK, a Boeing 777-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA46 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Mumbai/Chhatrapati Shivaji Intl, India (VABB) with 15 crew members and 228 passengers on board. During cruise at FL350 over the Atlantic ocean, the cabin crew reported a lavatory smoke indicator. White smoke could be observed coming from the aft wall panel due to ballast producing heat. The flight crew consulted with the operator’s maintenance and disconnected the cannon plugs to both aft lavatories. The ballast eventually cooled down and the flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-FGZS, a McDonnell Douglas A4N aircraft operated by Discovery Air Defence Services, was conducting tactical flight SKYHAWK2 from its base in Wittmund/Wittmundhafen, Germany (ETNT) with only the pilot on board. Shortly after the departure, the generator dropped offline. The pilot deployed the Ram Air Turbine (RAT), declared an emergency and proceeded to burn off some fuel before landing back at ETNT. The aircraft returned without further incident.The operator’s maintenance could not duplicate the error on the ground, despite a ground run and a check of the entire system. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-FFWJ, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA603 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During the approach to Runway 06L at CYYZ, the flight crew received a SLAT FAIL ECAM message. At the same moment, ATC advised that the active runway was being switched to 24R. Due to the slat fault, the flight crew was unable to accommodate the request; a PAN PAN was declared and the flight continued the approach to Runway 06L. The slats became operative just before touchdown and the aircraft continued with an uneventful landing. The operator's maintenance replaced the L/H #5 and R/H #9 Slat Track actuators as per troubleshooting procedures and, after a successful operational check, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FDRK, an Airbus 320-211 aircraft operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA1263 from Orlando Intl., FL (KMCO) to Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl., ON (CYOW) with 5 crew members and 117 passengers on board. When on the approach to CYOW the flight crew received a FLAP FAIL message on the ECAM. The landing was aborted, and the QRH procedures were followed as per the ECAM display. A PAN PAN was declared, and the aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The operator's maintenance determined that the R/H #3 Flap Rotary Actuator was at fault, and replaced it. The aircraft returned to service after successful operational checks.

N719FD, an Airbus 300 B4-622 aircraft operated by Federal Express, was conducting flight FDX142 from Memphis Intl, TN (KMEM) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) with only the two pilots on board. During the final approach to CYVR, the flight crew declared an emergency due to a landing gear issue. The aircraft performed two low level fly-past inspections by the tower to confirm that the landing gear was down. ARFF was requested and the aircraft landed on Runway 08R at 1552Z. The aircraft remained on the runway without steering power and was subsequently towed to its parking position.

C-FWGH, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG481 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Ixtapa/Zihuatanejo Intl, Mexico (MMZH) with 143 passengers and 7 crew members on board. During cruise flight at FL370 shortly after passing the Delicias (DEL) VOR on Airway UJ27, the flight was cleared to climb to FL390. Approaching FL380, ATC instructed SWG481 to level off at FL380. Shortly thereafter, the flight crew received a TCAS TA, followed by an RA to "Climb". The flight crew complied with the RA and advised ATC. The flight was immediately re-cleared to FL390, and continued to destination without further incident.

C-GSCA, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1603 from Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl, FL (KFLL) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) with 256 passengers and 8 crew members on board. During the climb through 10 000 feet after the departure from KFLL, the aircraft experienced a compressor stall on engine number 1 however, the flight crew observed no abnormal engine indications. A precautionary shut down of the engine was executed and the aircraft returned to KFLL. The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and landed without further incident.

C-FTQB, a Cessna A185E aircraft operated by South Nahanni Airways, was conducting a local VFR flight from Pitt Meadows, BC (CYPK). Shortly after departing from Runway 26L at CYPK, the pilot reported a rough-running engine. The pilot immediately returned and landed on Runway 08R. After coming to a complete stop, the engine was shut down to prevent fire. The aircraft was subsequently towed off the runway. The operator and its contracted maintenance organization discovered that the newly installed fuel selector valve was misplaced and that the lever had been selected upside down. As a result, the valve was closed instead of opened during pre-takeoff checks. There were no mechanical stops on the valve to prevent the full rotation of the lever. The operator issued a memo to all pilots to raise awareness of the situation.

C-FNNQ, a Boeing 777-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA855 from London/Heathrow, UK (EGLL) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). During the WHISTLER FOUR ARR approach to Runway 26R at CYVR, the flight crew was issued a vector in preparation for a turn to final, which they read back correctly. The aircraft inadvertently turned off the assigned heading and the flight crew received a TCAS alert. A loss of separation occurred when the aircraft came into conflict with ACA219, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, that was on final approach for the same runway. The flight crew of ACA855 advised ATC that they had the traffic ahead visual and took corrective action. The flight landed without further incident. The separation was reduced to 1.4 nm laterally and 300 feet vertically, where 5 nm or 1000 feet is required.

C-FOWU, a Bombardier CS300 aircraft operated by Bombardier, was conducting production flight BBA532 from Montreal/Mirabel, QC (CYMX) with 7 passengers and 5 crew members on board. While the aircraft was at an altitude between 15 000 and 16 000 feet, with a flap 4 and gear up configuration, a smell similar to that of a hot galley oven was noted in the flight deck. Immediately after the smell was detected, a light white smoke was noticed near the top of the cockpit door. The crew initiated a return to CYMX, and descended below 10 000 feet. The smoke dissipated immediately, and the Quick Reference Handbook (QRH) procedures for smoke removal were completed as a precaution. The oxygen masks were not donned, and no emergency was declared. The crew carried out a normal approach for runway 06 and the aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GVVZ, a Bombardier Learjet 45 aircraft operated by Sunwest Aviation, was conducting flight CNK645 from Scottsdale, AZ (KSDL) to Kelowna, BC (CYLW) with 2 flight crew members and 2 passengers on board. During cruise, the flight crew reported an aileron control jam. CNK645 diverted to Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC), and while on approach to land declared an emergency. CNK645 landed without further incident. The flight crew reported that the aircraft was exposed to a significant rain event a few hours prior to departure. The operator’s maintenance found no signs of mechanical failure or obstructions. De-ice fluid and frost were noted in the area of the aileron brush seals.

C-FERF un appareil de type Piper Aztec PA-23-250 exploité par Cargair Ltée, effectuait un vol d’entrainement selon les règles de vol à vue depuis et à destination de Montreal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU). En approche pour l’atterrissage, lorsque le train d’atterrissage a été sélectionné en position baissée, l’équipage a reçu une indication anormale que la roue de nez n’était pas verrouillée. La procédure d’extension du train par gravité a été tentée sans succès, et une urgence a été déclarée. Une inspection visuelle du train révéla que le train était en position verticale, cependant la procédure d’atterrissage avec un train principal en position anormale a quand même été effectuée. Les services de sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d’aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés, l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre sur la piste 24L et a été immobilisé sur la piste. L’appareil fut par la suite remorqué jusqu’à Cargair et l’inspection après vol a révélé qu’un câble de contrôle frottait sur un tuyau hydraulique provocant une fuite du liquide hydraulique.

C-GKMT, a Cessna 425 aircraft was conducting a flight from Salmon Arm, BC (CZAM) to Edmonton/Villeneuve, AB (CZVL). During cruise, at an altitude of 17000 feet above sea level (ASL) the right side flight compartment window failed, separating from the airframe and tearing off part of the glare shield covering the instrument panel. The pilot declared an emergency, initiated an emergency descent and elected to divert to Revelstoke, BC (CYRV). The aircraft landed without further event.

C-GOPW, a Boeing 737-200 aircraft operated by Canadian North was conducting flight MPE445 from Norman Wells, NT (CYVQ) to Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) with 4 crew members and 40 passengers on board. MPE445 was number 1 for the airport via a visual approach for Runway 34R to intercept the FAWP at MAVUG. C-GMPX, a Pilatus PC-12/47E aircraft operated by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP), was operating from Fort Liard, NT (CYJF) to Yellowknife, NT (CYZF). While MPE445 was maneuvering for the visual approach, a loss of separation occurred with GMPX. Separation was reduced to 3.9 nm horizontally and 100 feet vertically, where 5 nautical miles and 1000 feet are required.

C-FDSN, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA243 from Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) to Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR). During cruise flight, the flight crew declared an emergency due to a navigation system issue. Radar vectors were requested and the flight landed without further incident.

C-GAAV, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Alkan Air, was conducting a flight from Nanaimo, BC (CYCD) to Prince George, BC (CYXS). WEN3285, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting a flight from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to CYXS. A loss of separation occurred when the aircraft came within 2.6 nm laterally and 700 feet vertically of each other in an area where 5.0 nm or 1 000 feet is required. C-GAAV was issued radar vectors to increase the separation and, after reporting WEN3285 in sight, was cleared for a visual approach to Runway 15.

C-GXWJ, a Boeing 737-600 aircraft operated by WestJet was conducting flight WJA184 from Kelowna, BC (CYLW) to Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC) with 5 crew members and 73 passengers on board. The flight was on approach to CYYC, and was given direct to waypoint IGVEP. Meanwhile, C-FNEN a DHC-8-400 operated by WestJet Encore was conducting flight WEN3116 from Kamloops, BC (CYKA) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). WEN3116 was flying direct IGVEP following WJA184. The WJA184 flight crew selected direct to the fix, however; did not engage the LNAV mode causing the aircraft to deviate off course. Separation was reduced to 4.3 nm horizontally and 500 feet vertically, where 1000 feet is required. The WJA184 flight crew recognized the situation and corrected. Both aircraft landed without further incident.

C-GLUH, a Beech 200GT aircraft operated by Can-West Corporate Air Charters, was conducting flight  CWA924-M from Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC) to Medicine Hat, AB (CYXH) with 2 flight crew members and 2 passengers on board. On approach to CYXH, the flight crew selected landing gear down. Following the selection of gear down, the right main gear showed unlocked, the landing gear handle red unsafe light remained illuminated and the landing gear circuit breaker popped. A go-around was conducted, and the QRH was actioned. The flight crew decided to return to CYYC. On approach to CYYC the flight crew reset the landing gear circuit breaker and lowered the landing gear. The right main gear continued to indicate unlocked. A missed approach was conducted with a fly-by of the control tower where the tower controller confirmed that the right main gear was down. The flight crew declared an emergency and landed without issue. The operator’s maintenance found the right main gear position switch to be loose and missing lockwire.

C-GSWV, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Sunwest Aviation, was conducting flight CNK425 from Bonnyville, AB (CYBF) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). While climbing to cruise altitude after the departure from CYBF, the flight crew levelled off late for FL230 and exceeded the altitude by approximately 400 feet. While attempting to level off at FL230, the electronic trim did not operate and the manual one was stiff. Once leveled off at FL230, the flight continued to CYYC using manual trim. The electric trim system was intermittent throughout the flight. The operator's maintenance found the right elevator trim tab outboard pushrod binding.

C-GJZA, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8585 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl, SK (CYXE) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) with 4 crew members and 78 passengers on board. Prior to departure from CYXE, the aircraft was de-iced using Type I fluid to remove ice that had accumulated on the previous flight. Shortly after departing CYXE, a passenger reported to a cabin crew member that flames were coming from the left engine tailpipe (Pratt and Whitney Canada PW150A). The cabin crew member observed the flames and notified the flight crew. The flight crew had no fire warnings or indications and did not shutdown the engine. An emergency was declared and the aircraft returned to CYXE with ARFF on standby. JZA8585 landed on Runway 27, the engines were shutdown, and the flight crew initiated a rapid deplanement of the aircraft. ARFF checked the aircraft with thermal cameras and determined there was no fire, nor excessive heat in the left engine or brakes.The operator's maintenance subsequently inspected the aircraft and found no signs of a defect or source for the flames.

C-FXCA, a Boeing 767-375ER aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1806 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) to San José/Juan Santamaria Intl., Costa Rica (MROC) with 6 crew members and 267 passengers on board. The flight encountered turbulence during cruise, in the vicinity of Athens/Albany Ohio University, OH (KUNI). Two cabin crew members sustained minor injuries. The flight returned to CYYZ for priority landing, resulting in a delay for 2 other aircraft. The flight landed without further incident.

C-GWEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3299 from Regina Intl., SK (CYQR) to Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC) with 4 crew members and 78 passengers on board. During the initial climb from CYQR, the flight crew selected landing gear up and the nose gear did not retract. The flight crew continued to CYYC at FL150. During final approach, the flight crew declared a PAN PAN and landed without incident. The operator’s maintenance found a faulty nose landing gear door actuator. The actuator was replaced.

C-GWEF, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore was conducting flight WEN3259 from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Edmonton, AB (CYEG) with 4 crew members and 78 passengers on board. After de-icing, the flight crew attempted to shut off the auxiliary power unit (APU) and the start light illuminated. The crew actioned the QRH, shutdown the aircraft and initiated a rapid deplanement. ARFF was requested to inspect the aircraft. The operator's maintenance inspected the APU and applied a minimum equipment list deferral. The aircraft returned to service.

On 15 February 2018, an Aerospatiale AS-350-B2 aircraft operated by Sahtu Helicopters was conducting an engine warm-up run on a hilltop helipad approximately three nautical miles west-north-west of Tulita, Northwest Territories.After the engine was started and brought up to 70% gas generator speed (Ng), the helicopter began to vibrate, started to bounce and yaw to the left. In response, the pilot increased the Ng and just before it stabilized at 100%, he raised the collective to lift the helicopter off the helipad.The main rotor speed, which was outside the governing range, decreased, and the pilot could not maintain control. The helicopter contacted the ground, tumbling approximately 140 feet down the mountain. The pilot, who was the sole occupant, was seriously injured. He was wearing the lap and shoulder harness, but no helmet. The emergency locator transmitter (ELT) did not activate.UPDATED:19 May 2020

RSCU336, a Canadian Forces Lockheed CC130 Hercules aircraft, was conducting a flight from Trenton, ON (CYTR) to track an active ELT signal. The aircraft entered Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) Class C airspace approximately 24 nautical miles East of CYYZ at 6000 feet, without an active Mode C transponder code and without contacting air traffic control (ATC). TSC476, an Airbus 310-300 aircraft operated by Air Transat, was conducting a flight from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to CYYZ, and was on approach to Runway 06R at the time. The flight crew visually acquired the CC130 at the same altitude of 6000 feet and 2 nautical miles ahead of them while descending for the approach. The required separation was 1000 feet vertically or 3 nautical miles laterally. RSCU336 later contacted ATC and the required separation was reestablished.

C-FGZS, a Discovery Air Defence Services McDonnell Douglas A-4N Skyhawk, was on a local flight from Wittmundhafen - Wittmund, Lower Saxony Germany (ETNT). During the departure the generator dropped off line 3 times. After the third drop-off the Ram Air Turbine was pulled. A PanPan was declared, and fuel was burned off. The aircraft landed uneventfully at ETNT. Post - Maintenance identified that the converter had failed causing the generator to fail.

C-FCAE, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA889 from London/Heathrow, UK (EGLL) to Ottawa/MacDonald-Cartier Intl, ON (CYOW). As the flight was beginning its descent towards CYOW, the flight crew received an AFT LAV SMOKE detector warning. The cabin crew investigated the lavatory and could not find any signs of smoke. The flight crew elected to continue to CYOW and requested ARFF meet the aircraft at the gate as a precaution. The operator’s maintenance tested the lavatory A6 smoke detector and circuit, but found no faults. The smoke detector was cleaned of dust and debris and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GNOZ, a privately registered Piper PA-32RT-300T Turbo Lance aircraft, was conducting a flight from Brantford, ON (CYFD) to Toronto/Billy Bishop Toronto City, ON (CYTZ). During the landing on Runway 26 at CYTZ, the aircraft porpoised, bounced and landed back hard. The nose landing gear collapsed and the aircraft came to rest on the runway on its main landing gear. There were no injuries.

C-GWZB, a Cessna 172M aircraft operated by International Flight Centre, was on a night training flight from Vancouver/Boundary Bay, BC (CZBB) with only the pilot on board. During the approach to Runway 13 at CZBB, the aircraft collided with two birds. One bird broke through the windscreen and the other contacted the propeller and tail section. The pilot landed the aircraft and requested emergency services. The pilot was not injured, however the aircraft sustained damage to the windscreen, propeller and horizontal stabilizer.

C-FMEP, a Boeing 757-200 aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express, was conducting a flight from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During the takeoff run out of CYVR, the flight crew received a left engine limiter caution light. The flight crew continued the takeoff, adjusting the thrust manually, and subsequently executed the required checklist. Once at FL300, the flight crew noticed that the left engine EGT was rising. A PAN PAN was declared and a return to CYVR was requested where the flight landed without further incident. The operator’s maintenance is currently troubleshooting the issue.

C-FKCK, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA783 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Los Angeles Intl, CA (KLAX) with 129 passengers and 5 crew members on board. While in cruise flight approximately 140 nautical miles South East of Salt Lake City Intl, UT (KSLC), a very strong electrical smell was noticeable throughout the aircraft. The smell dissipated after 2 minutes, and the flight continued to KLAX where it landed without further incident.The operator reported that the left hand Recirc Fan breaker kept popping when reset. The unit was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

N808FD, an Airbus 310-300 aircraft operated by Federal Express, was conducting flight FDX120 from Memphis Intl, TN (KMEM) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG). Upon arriving at CYEG, the aircraft experienced a slat issue and the flight crew declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance found that the slat control computers registered a high torque condition and shut down. The departure airport experienced heavy rain the night before and water had penetrated the structure. The water then froze in the climb to cruising altitude and CYEG was below freezing on arrival. The system was thawed, dried, which then lead to a serviceable ground check. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GENM, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore was conducting flight WEN3205 from Fort St. John, BC (CYXJ) to Vancouver Intl., BC (CYVR) with 4 crew members and 44 passengers on board. After departing CYXJ enroute to Vancouver, the #2 engine fire warning illluminiated. The flight crew shut down the engine and activated the fire suppression system. Both extinguisher bottles were discharged, however the #2 engine fire warning persisted. The flight crew advised air traffic control, declared an emergency and diverted to Prince George, BC (CYXS). The aircraft landed uneventfully at with airport rescue and fire fighting (ARFF) crews standing by. The operator’s maintenance established that there had not been an engine fire. The warning had been the result of a damaged wire in a connector within the fire detection system. The system was repaired and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GVWE, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3235 from Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl, SK (CYXE) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG) with 4 crew members and 77 passengers on board. Upon arrival in CYEG, the flight crew observed a flap power caution light as the flaps were stuck at setting 10. Due to higher speeds and a low CRFI value, WEN3235 executed two missed approaches before declaring an emergency. The flight subsequently landed with ARFF standing by.

C-GXFC, a Lockheed 188C Electra aircraft operated by Buffalo Airways, was on a cargo flight from Tulita, NT (CZFN) to Déline, NT (CYWJ) with 3 crew members on board. Shortly after levelling off at 7 000 feet after the departure, the flight crew received a number 2 engine (Allison 501-D13) fire indication. The checklist was actioned and the engine was shut down. The flight crew elected to divert to Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) where they landed without further incident.

C-GYRC, an AutoGyro Cavalon Gyroplane aircraft, was on a local flight from Victoria Intl, BC (CYYJ) with only the pilot on board. Shortly after takeoff from Runway 09 at an altitude of approximately 20 feet above the ground, the pilot moved the controls aft and the main rotor blades contacted the vertical stabilizer. The aircraft descended, contacted the runway and rolled over on its side. The propeller, rotor blades and tail section were substantially damaged. The pilot sustained minor injuries.

C-GHLA, an Air Canada rouge Boeing 767-300, was being operated as flight ROU1851 from Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) to Mc Carran Intl, Las Vegas (KLAS). During cruise a flight attendant became incapacitated and was unable to continue duties. The remainding cabin crew assumed these duties and the aircraft continued uneventfully.

C-FNAP, an Embraer ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA594 from Houston/George Bush Intercontinental, TX (KIAH) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). During cruise flight, a cabin crew member was unable to continue duties. These duties were distributed amongst the rest of the cabin crew and the aircraft continued uneventfully. A medical emergency was declared upon arrival into CYYZ.

N173AN, a Boeing 757-200 aircraft operated by American Airlines, was conducting flight AAL204 from Philadelphia Intl, PA (KPHL) to Amsterdam/Schiphol, Netherlands (EHAM). While in cruise flight at FL350 above Stephenville, NL (CYJT), the flight crew noted erroneous number 1 Engine Pressure Ratio (EPR) input data. The flight crew declared an emergency and diverted back to KPHL for technical reasons. The operator's maintenance determined that an EPR hose chafed due to contact with a connector. The hose was replaced as well as a 3 way adaptor tube and valve assembly which was leaking. Following a leak test, the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GVPA, a Bombardier DHC-8-300 aircraft operated by Provincial Airlines, was conducting flight PVL902 from Deer Lake, NL (CYDF) to St. John's Intl, NL (CYYT). While holding short of the gate following a normal landing at CYYT, a cabin crew member observed smoke and a small fire in the area of the left main landing gear wheels. The captain exited the aircraft and used a fire extinguisher on the area. Airport emergency services responded to the call from the first officer and assessed to ensure that the fire was extinguished.The aircraft was moved to the gate where the passengers deplaned normally. There were no injuries. The operator’s maintenance determined that the source of the heat was due to a failed wheel bearing.

C-FIUF, a Boeing 777-200 operated by Air Canada as flight AC34 from Kingsford Smith - Sydney (YSSY) to  Vancouver Intl - Vancouver (CYVR) experienced a fire cargo aft warning and 2 bottles were discharged. The aircraft was diverted to Daniel K Inouye Intl - Honolulu (PHNL) and a Mayday was declared. The flight crew advised cabin crew to prepare for an abnormal landing. The landing was uneventful and emergency vehicles met aircraft. Post 1) Aft Lower Cargo Smoke Detector Replaced ref A/C Maintenance Manual (AMM) 26-16-01-401 up to subtask 26-16-01-860-003. 2) Cargo Smoke Detector (CSD) tube inspected per fleet request with no faults  3) Arinc signal gateway (ASG) in P84 A15 and A12 replaced per Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) 31-09-00 PB401. 4) Circuit Breakers (C/B'S) closed from Step 1, install test carried out per A/C Maintenance Manual (AMM) 26-16-01-401. 5) Regulator filter replaced as per A/C Maintenance Manual (AMM) 26-23-04-000-801. Due to cargo fire bottles discharge C/S system. 6) All 5 cargo fire bottles replaced in accordance with (IAW) Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) 26-23-01-401.

C-GSBR , a Vintage Wings of Canada F86E Saber, was enroute at FL280 from Gatineau-Ottawa Executive Airport, ON (CYND) to Akron-Canton Regional Airport, OH (KCAK). While completing the cruise checklist the pilot noted that there was no oxygen flow being supplied to the pilot's mask. ATC was advised and an emergency descent begun. C-GKQC, a Porter Airlines DHC-8-400, operating as flight POE471 from Toronto City Center, ON (CYTZ) to Montreal Trudeau, QC (CYUL) was at FL230 and converging with the F86. The air traffic controller issued vectors to POE471 to avoid the descending F86. The two aircraft came within 3.6 NM horizontally at FL230 where 5.0 NM of separation was required. Post - It was determined that the oxygen hose to the pilot's mask had been incorrectly attached. The F86 was pressurized to approximately 5.5 PSIG giving a cabin altitude of approximately 13 500'. The operator has since revised the preflight checklist to include an oxygen flow check.

C-GLQN, a Porter Airlines DHC-8-400 aircraft was being operated as flight POE 616, from Timmins, (Victor M. Power) (CYTS) to Billy Bishop Toronto City - Toronto (CYTS). During the climb out a master warning for an unsafe door indication was received. The crew followed the QRH procedures and continued to destination uneventfully. Upon descent to CYTZ, the crew noted the cabin altitude climbing at 3000 feet/min and cabin pressure differential decreasing. QRH procedures were re-actioned, and instructions were to land at the nearest suitable airport which was CYTZ. The crew declared a PanPan and the aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. The post flight walk around noted that the baggage door handle was unseated preventing the door seal from inflating and affecting pressurization. The door handle in this position does not unlock the door but does trigger a cockpit indication.

N637CZ, an Embraer ERJ 170-200 LR aircraft operated by Compass Airlines, was conducting flight CPZ5762 from Seattle-Tacoma Intl, WA (KSEA) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). During the approach, the flight crew declared an emergency due to an ENG 1 A-I Wing Leak EICAS message indicating that their anti-ice system was inoperative. The flight crew executed the QRH and declared an emergency. The aircraft landed without further incident at 1335 MST.The operator's maintenance removed and replaced the LH IB, LH OB #4 SLAT WAI sensor, #2 LH IB WAI sensor, LH OB WAI sensor wire. The aircraft was then returned to service.

C-FMSX, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA133 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). Approximately 75 nautical miles North West of Thunder Bay, ON (CYQT), one of the flight crew members became incapacitated and was attended to by a physician who was travelling as a passenger. After 45 minutes, the pilot returned to the cockpit but did not resume their duties. The flight continued to destination and landed without further incident.

C-GPMA, a Cessna 337H aircraft operated by Landa Aviation, was conducting a local survey flight from Hay River, NT (CYHY). Approximately 65 nautical miles North West of CYHY, C-GPMA descended from a cruise altitude of 1800 feet ASL to 900 feet ASL. The aircraft was configured for slow flight at 100 KIAS, with the landing gear extended and flaps lowered to 10 degrees. A few moments later, the pilot heard a loud bang and noticed that the number 1 engine (Teledyne Continental IO-360-GB) had lost oil pressure. The pilot actioned the emergency checklist and shut down the number 1 engine. The landing gear was retracted and the flight returned to CYHY where it landed without further incident. There were no injuries to the 5 occupants on board. The operator’s maintenance found the number 1 engine crankcase breather vent line outlet restricted by ice buildup.

C- FWRS, an Air Georgian Bombardier CL 600-2B19 operating as flight GGN7404, took off from Cleveland-Hopkins International (KCLE) for Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) when the flight crew was unable to retract the nose landing gear. The aircraft continued to CYYZ and on approach an emergency was declared. The main landing gear was lowered normally and the aircraft landed with ARFF standing by. Maintenance determined that the nose landing gear strut was in a stuck position and after discussion with the manufacturer the nose landing gear was replaced.

C-FLWH, an Embraer ERJ 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA609 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). On initial climb out the crew received a wind shear caution advisory. The wind shear escape procedure was completed. The flight continued uneventfully.

N403UA, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by United Airlines, was conducting flight UAL1780 from Houston/George Bush Intercontinental, TX (KIAH) to Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC). During the approach at CYYC, the flight crew observed an unsafe landing gear indication. A missed approach was initiated and an emergency was declared. The aircraft landed without further incident, but was unable to exit the runway. A tow was arranged and the aircraft was removed from the runway.The operator's maintenance replaced the 62GA relay and 49GA landing gear system isolation safety valve. The aircraft was jacked and the landing gear handle was moved 4 times in accordance with procedures. All doors and gears were checked and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FVTQ, un appareil de type Piper PA-31-350 exploité par Strait Air, effectuait le vol NUK651 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Havre St-Pierre, QC (CYGV) à destination de Port-Menier, QC (CYPN) avec 2 membres d'équipage et 1 passager à bord. Suite au démarrage des moteurs, l'équipage a détecté une odeur de brûlé dans le poste de pilotage lors de l'activation de la chaufferette avant. La chaufferette a été fermée et l'odeur s'est estompée alors que l'aéronef circulait en vue du décollage. La chaufferette a été remise en marche et, en l'absence d'odeur, l'équipage a procédé au décollage. À environ 300 pieds au-dessus du sol, l'équipage de conduite a remarqué la présence de fumée blanche aux pieds du commandant. L’équipage de conduite a fait demi-tour et l’appareil s’est posé sans problème à CYGV. Aucune urgence n'a été déclarée et il n'y a eu aucun blessé.L'équipe d'entretien n'a pu reproduire l'anomalie au sol et après un test en vol, l'aéronef a poursuivi son itinéraire sans problème.

C-FDQV, un appareil de type Airbus 320 exploité par Air Canada sous l'indicatif AC480 avec à son bord 6 membres d'équipage et 85 passagers effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, Ontario à destination de l'aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, Québec (CYUL). Alors que l'appareil était à une altitude de 20 000 pieds au-dessus du niveau de la mer en descente pour CYUL, l'appareil a rencontré une zone de turbulence modérée, de sorte qu'un membre du personnel de cabine a été blessé et incapable de poursuivre ses fonctions. Une fois au sol, le membre du personnel de cabine a été transporté à l'hôpital. La nature exacte des blessures est inconnue.

ACA418, an Airbus 320 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting a flight from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QB (CYUL). Upon departing from CYYZ, the flight was cleared to climb to 7000 feet. The aircraft was observed on radar at 7500 feet without authorization and came within 2.0 nautical miles laterally and 500 feet vertically from WJA1229, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by WestJet which was at 8000 feet. The required separation at the time was 3.0 nautical miles or 1000 feet.

C-FEJD, an Embraer 170-200 operated by Sky Regional Airlines was conducting flight ZX7538 from Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) to Philadelphia International (KPHL). During descent, passing through 13000 feet, a slat fail message appeared on the EICAS. The QRH was completed and vectors were requested by the crew. A PanPan was declared and the aircraft landed uneventfully. ARFF  met the aircraft. The aircraft taxied to the gate.

C-FGDT, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight AC869 from London/Heathrow, UK (EGLL) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) with 10 crew members and 117 passengers on board. During cruise a cabin crew member  was unable to perform their duties. These duties were reassigned and the flight landed uneventfully.

C-GVIJ, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Cargojet Airways, was conducting flight CJT621 from St. John's Intl, NL (CYYT) to Greater Moncton Romeo Leblanc Intl, NB (CYQM). C-FMEP, a Boeing 757-200 aircraft operated by Morningstar Air Express, was conducting flight MAL7054 from Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ) to CYQM.MAL7054 was conducting an instrument approach behind CJT621 – both aircraft were on instrument approaches for Runway 29 at CYQM. The distance between the two aircraft decreased to less than the required separation for wake turbulence. The closest lateral separation was 4.3 nautical miles, where 5 nautical miles is required. NAV CANADA is investigating.

C-FFAL, un Boeing 737-200 en exploitation privée venait de décoller de l'aéroport de Rouyn-Noranda (Québec) sous l'indicatif de vol RAG100 à destination de l'aéroport de Kattiniq/Donalson (Québec) lorsque l'équipage de conduite a observé une anomalie avec les volets. Une urgence a été déclarée et l’équipage de conduite a demandé une diversion vers l’aéroport de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Int, Ontario où l’aéronef a atterri sans encombre.

N12195, un appareil de type Embraer EMB-145XR exploité par ExpressJet Airlines Inc. sous l’indicatif de vol ASQ4341 était en phase de décollage sur la piste 24 droite de l’aéroport de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, Québec lorsque le pilote a interrompu le décollage en raison de la présence de fumée dans la cabine. L'alarme d'écrasement a été activée et les services d'urgence ont été déployés. L'aéronef est retourné à la barrière sans encombre.

N430SW, a Canadair CL-600-2B19 operated by Skywest Airlines as flight SKW4311, was conducting an IFR flight from Winnipeg/Richardson International (CYWG), MB, to Minneapolis-St. Paul International (KMSP), MN. SKW4311 taxied to the CYWG de-icing area and had Type I and Type IV fluid applied with the #1 engine (GE CF-34) shut down. As the flight taxied on Taxiway Hotel toward the departure runway, the crew attempted to start the #1 engine, but received a hot start indication with temperature stagnating at about 600 degrees C. The crew stopped the start sequence and carried out the hot start shutdown checklist procedure. CYWG Tower advised the crew that flames had been observed coming from the engine and that ARFF was being dispatched. Following a visual inspection, the aircraft returned to the gate where troubleshooting and a maintenance inspection were completed. No damage or indications of fire was noted but the operator's maintenance identified a significant amount of de-ice fluid in the number 1 engine. Once the maintenance borescope inspection, dry motoring, and a normal engine start was accomplished, the aircraft was released by maintenance and continued to KMSP with no further issues.

C-GGGA, un Beech 1900D exploité par Air Georgian sous l’indicatif de vol GGN7305 avec à son bord 5 passagers et 2 pilotes, était en approche pour la piste 24R à l’aéroport de Montréal/ Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, Québec, (CYUL) en provenance de l’aéroport de Bradley-Windsor Locks Intl, Connecticut E.-U, lorsque le pilote a effectué une approche interrompue en raison d'une indication de train d'atterrissage non sorti. Une urgence a été déclarée. La tour a été en mesure de vérifier visuellement que le train d'atterrissage était sorti et un atterrissage sans encombre a été effectué. Le personnel de maintenance a remplacé un interrupteur sur le train principal  droit ainsi qu'un disjoncteur.

C-GONR, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-100 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA711 à partir de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) vers Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 3 membres d'équipage et 37 passagers à bord. Alors qu’il était en vol de croisière, l’équipage a reçu une indication de défaillance du système hydraulique numéro 1, suivi d’une baisse de la quantité de fluide hydraulique jusqu'à 0.1 pinte. L’équipage de conduite a effectué la liste de vérification applicable et a déclaré un PAN PAN. L'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre sur la piste 24L à CYUL.

C-FIYE, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1831 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Honolulu/Daniel K Inouye Intl, HI (PHNL). Shortly after takeoff from Runway 26L at CYVR, the flight crew observed a bird strike the aircraft just below the nose. However, no unusual handling or abnormal engine indications were observed. The flight crew elected to continue to PHNL and landed without further incident. Upon further inspection by maintenance personnel in PHNL, evidence of bird impact was found to the left side of the nose, below the radome. Additionally, there were minor damage to the left engine.

C-FELL, a privately operated ski equipped Cessna 140X, was conducting a local flight from a private airfield 13 nm ESE of High Level, AB (CYOJ). A takeoff and landing was conducted from the snow covered runway; the snow depth was approximately 18 inches. During the second landing the left ski caught in the snow. The left main landing gear collapsed and the aircraft came to rest. The pilot, the sole occupant, was uninjured; the aircraft was substantially damaged. The ELT did not activate.

C-FPIJ, a Boeing 767-33A aircraft was operated by Cargojet Airways Ltd, as flight CJT 620 from Moncton, NB (CYQM) to St. John's Intl, NL (CYYT). Taxiing to the gate after landing at CYYT, the flight crew noted a strong odour and a main deck fire warning indication. An emergency was declared, ARFF responded and escorted the aircraft to the gate. Initial inspection revealed no evidence of fire and the emergency was terminated. Maintenance personnel noted a slight haze upon entering the aircraft. Tests determined that one of the air supply ducts was delivering excessively hot air due to a defective mixing valve.

C-GLWJ, a Westjet Encore de Havilland DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3145 from Calgary, AB (CYYC) to Edmonton, AB (CYEG). During takeoff, accelerating through 75 KIAS, the AC GEN caution light illuminated. The takeoff was rejected and the QRH actioned. ARFF checked the brake temperature and no issues were noted. The AC GEN fault was reset and the aircraft continued with the departure uneventfully.

N191MG, un appareil de type Cessna 441 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l’aéroport de Québec/Jean-Lesage Intl, Québec (CYQB) à destination de l’aéroport New Bedford Regional, Massachusetts, É.-U (KEWB). Alors que l’appareil était en montée vers le niveau de vol 240, le pilote a déclaré une urgence en raison de vibrations à l'arrière de l'appareil. Moins de deux minutes plus tard, le pilote avisait qu'il avait stabilisé la situation et qu'il n'était plus en état d'urgence, mais a demandé une diversion vers l’aéroport de Burlington Intl, Vermont É.-U. où l’appareil s’est posé sans problème.

N777QX, a Bombardier CL-600-2B16 aircraft, operated by Flexjet LLC, was conducting a flight from London, Stansted airport, UK (EGSS) to Bangor International airport, MA (KBGR). During cruise, approximately 450 nm from KBGR, the crew received a Hydraulic system #2 temperature warning message. The crew noted the hydraulic temperature was 98°C and continued to monitor. Within a few minutes the temperature had risen to 107°C. As per the company checklist, the crew performed a precautionary shutdown of the # 2 engine, declared an emergency and diverted to Halifax Stanfield International airport, NS (CYHZ) and landed uneventfully. The #2 engine driven hydraulic pump was replaced in accordance with the manufacturer.

C-GXJA, the Air Georgian CRJ 200 aircraft operating as flight GGN7338 was on approach to Lester B. Pearson Intl - Toronto (CYYZ) from Port Columbus - Columbus (KCMH) when the crew received GEN 1 OFF and IDG 1 DISC messages. QRH procedures were followed and a reset attempt failed to re-connect the generator. The APU generator was on MEL and was not available. A PanPan was declared and the aircraft landed uneventfully with ARFF standing by. Maintenance replaced the #1 IDG and the starter motor for the APU. Additional troubleshooting and parts replacement were required before the APU became serviceable. A successful operational test of both components was completed and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-FXEA, a Chinook Helicopters Ltd. Robinson R44 II, was approaching Abbotsford, BC (CYXX) on the published Northwest route. The CYXX controller notified the pilot of C-FXEA of a radar target (Hughes 369F, N530FF) operating in the control zone without clearance and not talking to the tower. The pilot of C-FXEA descended to avoid collision. N530FF passed 100' above C-FXEA and returned to Langley Regional Airport (CYNJ). Both aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-FAKN, the Alkan Air Ltd. Beech 200, was operating from Whitehorse, YT (CYXY) to Nanaimo, BC (CYCD). During the initial climb the flight crew retracted the landing gear and the gear handle remained illuminated red. The landing gear was cycled several times as the aircraft maintained the climb to cruising altitude. The QRH was actioned and a manual landing gear extension was conducted. An emergency was declared and the aircraft returned to CYXY. During the final approach the landing gear indicated down and locked with 3 green lights and the aircraft landed uneventfully. Company maintenance performed adjustments to the landing gear indication micro switches.

C-FLJZ, a CL-600 was being operated as flight 8103 by Air Canada Express (Jazz) from George Bush Intercontinental/Houston (KIAH) to Calgary Intl - Calgary (CYYC). Shortly after take off the crew noticed a steering inop caution message and upon the gear up selection, a nose gear disagree message after 20 seconds. A PanPan was declared with a return to KIAH. Once the gear was lowered again the crew advised that all the gear showed down and locked. To land under the max landing weight, the aircraft remained airborne and held for 2 hours in to burn fuel. The aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-FJUB, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing Airlines, was conducting flight SWG584 from Cancún Intl, Mexico (MMUN) to Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl, MB (CYWG). Approximately 40 minutes prior to landing at CYWG, the crew declared an emergency due to a passenger illness. The aircraft landed uneventfully at CYWG and emergency services met the aircraft at the gate.

C-GJZK, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP, was conducting flight JZA8160 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG). While on short final approach into CYEG at an altitude of approximately 500 feet AGL, the aircraft encountered severe turbulence. The aircraft was displaced into a 45 degree bank angle from which the crew was able to recover. The approach was continued and the aircraft landed without further incident. There were no injuries. The crew reported continuous light to moderate turbulence for the duration on the flight from CYYC to CYEG.The operator's maintenance conducted a post flight inspection of the aircraft for flight in severe turbulence. No faults were found.

C-GKHI, a Beech B200 aircraft operated by Transwest Air, was conducting a flight from Patuanak, SK (CKB2) to La Ronge (Barber Field), SK (CYVC). Upon selecting gear down on approach to CYVC, the red gear in-transit light remained illuminated and the left hand main gear green light did not illuminate. The flight crew consulted with the operator's maintenance and an emergency landing gear extension procedure was conducted. During the procedure, the in-transit light extinguished. The flight crew did not declare an emergency but emergency services were requested. After conducting a low pass to allow the operator's maintenance to visually check the landing gear, the aircraft landed without further incident. The flight crew shut down the aircraft on the runway to allow further inspection before the aircraft was moved.The operator's maintenance conducted an inspection and determined that the left-hand landing gear's down-lock switch was faulty.

C-GTQH, the Kluane Helicopters Aerospatiale (Airbus Helicopters) AS350-B1, was operating a local flight from Haines Junction, YT (CYHT). During final approach at a company helipad, the aft portion of the tail boom and lower vertical fin contacted a 6 foot high  fence. C-GTQH began to rotate to the left. As an attempt was made to set the helicopter on the ground, the left skid made contact with the ground and the helicopter rolled onto its left side. The pilot, the sole occupant, sustained minor injuries, the helicopter was substantially damaged. The ELT was not activated.

C-GHLU, a Boeing 767-333ER aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge was conducting flight ROU1892 from Calgary Intl, AB (CYYC) to Bahias de Huatulco Intl, Oaxaca, Mexico (MMBT) with 9 crew members and 250 passengers on board. While in a non radar environment in level flight at 16 000 feet ASL in the vicinity of enroute waypoint NUDOS, ATC authorized the flight to descend to 6000 feet ASL at pilot’s discretion. At 30 nm North of MMBT, the flight crew initiated the descent and, approximately 1 minute later at 11 800 feet ASL, an EGPWS "Caution Terrain" aural warning was received. The flight crew climbed back immediately to 13 500 feet ASL and continued to MMBT before commencing the descent and the approach. The aircraft landed at MMBT without further incident.The Mexican Secretaria de Comunicaciones y Transportes of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGAC) has opened an investigation on this serious incident in accordance with ICAO Annex 13.

C-GYMG, un hélicoptère de type Robinson R44 en exploitation privé effectuait un vol de nuit selon les règles de vol à vue, de St-George de Beauce, QC à destination de St-Alexis de-Montcalm, QC avec 1 pilote et 2 passagers à bord, lorsque que celui-ci s'est écrasé et a pris feu dans un champ de St-Joachim-de-Courval QC. La balise de détresse s'est déclenchée et l'incendie a consumé la cabine. Les trois occupants sont décédés.

C-FNVV, an Airbus 320-200 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA566 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to San Francisco Intl, CA (KSFO) with 5 crew members and 146 passengers on board. During the descent approximately 65 nautical miles from KSFO, the flight crew received a TCAS RA to climb. The instructions were followed and the aircraft landed uneventfully.

C-GHOZ, a Boeing 767-300 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA824 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Amsterdam/Schiphol, Netherlands (EHAM) with 8 crew members and 94 passengers on board. During cruise, when approximately 700 nm west of EHAM, both crew and passengers noticed fumes and an odour in the cabin and flight deck. The flight crew turned off the gasper fan and the odour dissipated. The flight continued to destination without further incident.

C-GHPT, a Boeing 787-8 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA833 from Brussels, Belgium (EBBR) to Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) with 10 crew members and 211 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from EBBR, the flight crew was advised of smoke in the galley. The oven was turned off, and the smoke dissipated. The flight continued to destination uneventfully.

C-GENU, a Westjet Encore de Havilland DHC-8-400, was operating as flight WEN3109 from Calgary, AB (CYYC) to Nanaimo, BC (CYCD). During the take-off roll the flight crew noted an AC generator caution light and rejected the takeoff. While taxiing from the runway, the flight attendant reported smoke was coming from the brakes. The flight crew actioned the QRH and requested ARFF. ARFF met the aircraft and followed WEN3109 to the gate. There were no further smoke issues.

C-GENV, a Bombardier DHC-8-400 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3713 from Boston/General Edward Lawrence Logan Intl, MA (KBOS) to Halifax/Stanfield Intl, NS (CYHZ). C-GSWL, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing, was conducting flight SWG455 from Punta Cana Intl, Dominican Republic (MDPC) to CYHZ. WEN3713 was cleared for the visual approach with instructions to follow the RNAV Y 32 track. WEN3713 deviated from the route by turning final further back, causing a loss of separation with SWG455. The aircraft came within 2.8 nautical miles (nm) when the required separation was 3 nm.

C-FPSI, un Jetstream 32 exploité par Pascan sous l’indicatif PSC468 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vols aux instruments de l’aéroport de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl (CYQB) à destination de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) avec 2 membres d’équipage à bord. Lorsque le train d’atterrissage a été descendu, une indication anormale de position de la roue de nez est apparue. La procédure d’urgence a été exécutée sans succès. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et effectué une diversion à Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 06R sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage.

C-GQHB, un appareil de type Convair 440 (580), effectuait un vol d'entraînement dans la région de Montréal Intl (Mirabel), QC (CYMX) lorsque l'équipage de conduite a entendu un son anormal provenant de l'hélice gauche. L'équipage a fermé le moteur gauche (Allison 501-D13D), toutefois l'hélice ne s'est pas mise en drapeau. Une urgence a été déclarée et l'appareil s'est posé sans encombre à CYMX. Une fuite d'huile au niveau de l'hélice et la défaillance du bouton de commande de mise en drapeau seraient à l'origine du problème.

C-FTIQ, an Aerospatiale/Aeritalia ATR 42-500 aircraft operated by First Air, was conducting flight FAB120 from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Hay River, NT (CYHY) with 3 crew members and 13 passengers on board. Shortly after the departure from CYZF, the flight crew received a number 1 engine (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW127E) low oil pressure alert on the crew alert system (CCAS). The flight crew declared a PAN PAN and requested a return to CYZF. The aircraft landed without further event and the engine was secured after landing. The flight crew proceeded to taxi to the gate. The operator’s maintenance determined that the oil filler port for the number 1 engine was not secured correctly, allowing engine oil to escape during operation leading to the loss of engine oil and, consequently, oil pressure indication.

C-FYJP, an Airbus 319-114 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1650 from Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Miami Intl, FL (KMIA) with 5 crew members and 107 passengers on board. During cruise, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and could no longer perform their duties. The flight continued to destination where it landed without further incident.

C-GTQY, un appareil de type Boeing 737-800 exploité par Air Transat, effectuait le vol TSC969 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Acapulco/General Juan N. Álvarez Intl, Mexique (MMAA) à destination de Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Bien qu'il ait reçu et relu l'autorisation d'évoluer à 160 KT jusqu'au point VOLAX lors de l’approche à CYUL, TSC969 a été observé sur radar 20 nœuds en-dessous de la vitesse demandée. Par conséquent, la distance avec C-GPWG, un appareil de type Airbus 320-200 exploité par Air Canada et effectuant le vol ACA798 de Los Angeles Intl, CA (KLAX) à CYUL qui le suivait derrière, a été réduite à 2,7 miles marin (nm), alors que l'espacement requis était de 3 nm. L’espacement a été rétabli suite à la transmission d’une instruction de réduction de vitesse à l’intention d’ACA798.

C-GMWN, a Boeing 737-800 aircraft operated by Sunwing, was conducting flight SWG432 from Quebec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) to Punta Cana Intl, Dominican Republic (MDPC) with 6 crew members and 178 passengers on board. During the approach to MDPC, the flight crew received a fire indication in the forward cargo hold. The emergency checklist was executed and the fire extinguisher bottle was discharged. The flight crew declared MAYDAY and the aircraft landed without further incident. After the landing, the aircraft remained on the runway for an inspection by fire services. No fire or smoke was observed and the aircraft taxied to a remote stand where all passengers and crew deplaned without incident. Fire services then opened and inspected the cargo holds and found no sign of fire.

C-GWBX, a Boeing 737-700 aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA2755 from Nassau/Lynden Pindling Intl, Bahamas (MYNN) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 5 crew members and 124 passengers on board. After receiving authorization to depart from ATC and commencing the take-off roll, the flight crew observed an unauthorized aircraft enter the runway. The flight crew rejected the takeoff at low speed and informed ATC. WJA2755 was subsequently reissued authorization to take off when the conflicting traffic was off the runway.

N989CG, a Lear 31A aircraft operated by Cometic Aviation, was conducting a flight from Willoughby/Lost Nation Municipal, OH (KLNN) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). As the aircraft was landing on Runway 24R at CYYZ, the south tower controller cleared ENY3702, an Embraer 145 aircraft operated by Envoy Air from CYYZ to New York/Laguardia, NY (KLGA), to taxi to position on Runway 24R behind the landing traffic. Once ENY3702 was in position at the threshold of Runway 24R, the south tower controller issued departure instructions that included an altitude and heading once airborne; however, the instructions did not include a take off clearance. As N989CG was approaching Taxiway C4 high speed exit, ENY3702 was observed starting its takeoff roll on Runway 24R without a clearance. The south tower controller issued an ABORT instruction to ENY3702 when the aircraft was at a speed of approximately 65 knots. ENY3702 rejected the takeoff and exited at Taxiway D5.

C-GWEF, a WestJet Encore Dash 8 Q-400 operating as flight WEN3118, was on initial descent for landing at Kelowna Airport (CYLW) from Victoria Intl - Victoria (CYYJ) when it encountered an area of severe turbulence. All passengers had their seatbelts fastened, however one flight attendant was injured. The aircraft landed uneventfully and emergency medical services met the aircraft. The aircraft was inspected and no damage was found.

C-FDOV, un Beechcraft A100 exploité par Grondair, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de St-Frédéric, QC (CSZ4) à destination de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl, QC (CYQB) avec 2 membres d'équipage à son bord. Lors de la montée après le décollage, l’équipage a constaté que le train d’atterrissage ne rentrait pas et que l’indication de la position des roues était anormale.
