L’équipage a poursuivi le vol à destination de CYQB et a déclaré un état d’urgence auprès du centre contrôle de la circulation aérienne (ATC). La liste de vérification en cas d’urgence a été complétée et le disjoncteur du contrôle du train d’atterrissage a été réenclenché. L'indication de train d’atterrissage sorti est revenue à la normale et l’appareil s’est posé sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage.

C-GMNL, un Beechcraft B100 exploité par Max Aviation inc. sous l’indicatif MAX180, effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis l’aéroport de Montréal/St-Hubert, QC (CYHU) à destination de Chicoutimi/St-Honoré, QC (CYRC) avec 9 passagers et 2 membres d’équipage. Lors de la montée, en passant le niveau de vol 180, la température inter turbine du moteur gauche (Garrett TPE331-6-252B) a augmenté au-dessus de la limite. L’équipage a réduit la puissance au minimum et effectué une diversion à CYHU. Le moteur a été gardé en marche et l’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 24R sans encombre avec les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) en alerte. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé ni dommage à l’appareil.

C-IPJB, un appareil de type Quad City Challenger II en exploitation privée, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue depuis Ottawa/Rockcliffe, ON (CYRO) avec un pilote à bord. Alors qu’il était en vol de croisière à environ 6 miles marins à l’ouest de CYRO à 1200 pieds au-dessus du niveau de la mer, une panne motrice est survenue (Rotax 503). Le pilote a effectué un atterrissage d’urgence dans un champ. Lors de la course au sol après l’atterrissage, le pylône de l’aile gauche a percuté un panneau. L’appareil a subi des dommages au pylône et à un ski, mais il n’y a eu aucun blessé.

C-FUAM, un appareil de type Pilatus PC-12/47E exploité par Private Air Inc. effectuait un vol régulier selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Val d’Or, QC (CYVO) à destination de  Chibougamau/Chapais, QC (CYMT) avec 2 pilotes et 2 passagers à bord. Lors de l'approche à CYMT, l’équipage de conduite a observé une indication anormale du train d’atterrissage et a demandé d’être réacheminé à Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL). Après avoir reçu une confirmation visuelle de la tour de contrôle que le train était sorti, l’équipage de conduite a demandé la présence des services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) et a déclaré une urgence. L’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 24L sans encombre, il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage.

C-GTAI, un appareil de type DHC-8-100 exploité par Jazz Aviation LP, effectuait le vol JZA682 selon les règles de vol aux instruments depuis Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) à destination de Bagotville, QC (CYBG) avec 26 passagers et 3 membres d’équipage à son bord. Lors de la montée initiale après le décollage, une panne de la génératrice à courant continu numéro 2 est survenue. L’équipage a déclaré un état d’urgence et a avisé l’ATC qu’il revenait à CYUL. Les services de Sauvetage et lutte contre les incendies d'aéronefs (SLIA) ont été déployés et l’appareil s’est posé sur la piste 06L sans encombre. Il n’y a eu aucun blessé et l’appareil n’a subi aucun dommage.

C-GWXL, a Piper PA-31-350 aircraft operated by Orca Airways, was conducting flight ORK444 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Powell River, BC (CYPW) with only the two pilots on board. Shortly after the departure from CYVR, the flight crew noticed a burning smell in the cockpit. After observing smoke coming from the instrument panel, the flight crew elected to return to CYVR. No emergency was declared, however fire services were put on standby at CYVR. The aircraft landed without further incident. A post flight inspection was carried out and electrical faults were repaired. The aircraft was then returned to service.

CUB182A, an Airbus 320 aircraft operated by Air Cubana, was conducting a flight from Varadero/Juan Gualberto Gómez Intl, Cuba (MUVR) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). As the flight crew started their initial approach into CYYZ via the NUBER2 STAR, the aircraft encountered strong winds and the Flight Management Computer (FMC) lateral navigation system initiated the planned turn over waypoint QWERI by approximately 5 nautical miles (nm). As a result of the early turn, a loss of separation occurred between CUB182A and ENY3765, an Embraer 145 aircraft operated by Envoy Air, conducting a flight from Chicago/O'Hare Intl, IL (KORD) to CYYZ. The closest lateral distance between the two aircraft was 4 nm, where 5 nm is required.

C-FMXC, a Boeing 767-333 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1624 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood Intl, FL (KFLL) with 8 crew members and 276 passengers on board. During the final approach to Runway 10L at KFLL, the flight crew observed a small UAV pass within 50 to 100 feet to the left of the aircraft and just below their altitude at about 2000' feet ASL. ATC was notified and the flight was completed uneventfully.

C-GGMC, a privately operated Beech King Air C90GTi aircraft, was conducting a flight from Fort McMurray, AB (CYMM) to Edmonton Intl, AB (CYEG). N955LR, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24 (CRJ900) aircraft operated by Mesa Airlines, was conducting flight ASH5779 from Phoenix/Sky Harbor Intl, AZ (KPHX) to CYEG. The ceiling was overcast at 700 feet and simultaneous approaches and automatic control transfer was not in effect. As C-GGMC was approximately 4 miles final for Runway 02, ASH5779 was approximately 1 mile final for Runway 12. Neither IFR nor wake turbulence separation was assured. ATC instructed C-GGMC to pull up and was re-sequenced for another approach. The aircraft landed without further event.

C-GJLZ, a Boeing 737-8CT aircraft operated by WestJet, was conducting flight WJA717 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) to Vancouver Intl., BC (CYVR) with 6 crew members and 151 passengers on board. During cruise, a cabin crew member sustained an injury and was unable to perform their duties. Cabin safety positions were reassigned, and the flight landed without incident.

C-FABA, a Bombardier DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Wasaya Airways, was conducting flight WSG815 from Big Trout Lake, ON (CYTL) to Weibenville, ON, with 2 flight crew on board. While on approach into Weibenville, the flight crew selected gear down and received a #2 hydraulic isolation valve caution light. The aircraft diverted to Pickle Lake, ON (CYPL), and an emergency landing gear extension was conducted. The crew declared an emergency, and the aircraft landed safely. The operator’s maintenance inspection of the hydraulic system revealed a broken hydraulic actuator line. The line was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.

C-GARG, an Airbus 319-114 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA720 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) to LaGuardia/New York, NY, (KLGA) with 5 crew members and 112 passengers on board. On approach at approximatively 2 nm of KLAG, the flight crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory (RA). The flight crew followed the command and descended 400 feet. Another aircraft passed overhead 800 feet above. The aircraft landed at KLGA without further incident.

C-FNAJ, an Embraer 190 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1037 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) to Denver/Denver Intl., CO (KDEN) with 4 crew members and 91 passengers on board. During the approach at KDEN, the flight crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory (RA). The flight crew followed the command and landed without further incident.

C-FLWH, an Embraer 190-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada, was conducting flight ACA1037 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) to Denver/Denver Intl., CO (KDEN) with 4 crew members and 64 passengers on board. During the final approach at KDEN, the flight crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory (RA). The flight crew followed the command and landed without further incident.

C-GBIM, an Airbus 319-114 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1636 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) to Orlando Intl, FL (KMCO) with 5 crew members and 101 passengers on board. Just before the descent into KMCO, a cabin crew member became incapacitated and was unable to continue duties. Duties were reassigned to the remainder of the cabin crew members and the flight landed without further incident.

C-GDEN, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by WestJet Encore, was conducting flight WEN3483 from Sydney/J.A. Douglas McCurdy airport, NS (CYQY) to Halifax/Stanfield Intl., NS (CYHZ) with 4 crew members and 22 passengers on board. After departing CYQY, the fuselage doors warning light illuminated. The flight crew referred to the QRH, pressurization remained normal, and the crew elected to continue with the flight. During descent, about 10 nm north of CYHZ at an altitude of 4000 feet the aircraft depressurized, and the crew declared a PAN PAN. WEN3483 landed on runway 05 without further incident; emergency response services responded. The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft, and observed that the AFT cargo door was in the unlocked position, with the AFT cargo canted panel blown out. The AFT cargo was locked, the door seal and indication system was function checked, and the canted bulkhead blow out panel was secured. An aircraft pressurized/leak check was carried with no faults found. The aircraft returned to service.

C-GJNL, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-300 exploité par Hydro-Québec, effectuait le vol HYD151 selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Bagotville, QC (CYBG) à Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl, QC (CYUL) avec 4 membres d'équipage et 12 passagers à bord. À environ 100 miles marins au nord-est de CYUL, l'équipage de conduite a reçu une indication de perte de pression d'huile du moteur droit (Pratt & Whitney Canada PW123). L'équipage de conduite a fermé le moteur et demandé la présence des services d'urgence pour l’atterrissage à CYUL, où l'aéronef s'est posé sans encombre sur la piste 24L à 00:13Z. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.Le service d'entretien a diagnostiqué une fuite d'huile au niveau du PCU.

C-FMEQ, a Morningstar Air Express Boeing 757-200, was on initial climb out from Calgary Intl. (CYYC). Just after Flap 1 was selected, the crew received an EICAS message that the right side generator was off and the same side AC bus also. The R AC BUS OFF checklist was carried out, followed by the R GEN OFF and the L/R UTILITY BUS OFF checklist. A PAN PAN was declared with ATC and the aircraft leveled off to ensure that the APU was on and functioning properly. The flight crew terminated the PAN PAN declaration and the flight continued to Vancouver. Company maintenance is currently troubleshooting the Integrated Drive Generator on the right hand engine.

C-FPQB, a Boeing 787-9 aircraft operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA064 from Seoul/Incheon Intl., South Korea (RKSI) to Vancouver/Vancouver Intl., (CYVR) with 11 crew members and 298 passengers on board. During cruise, a cabin crew member was unable to continue their duties. Cabin crew positions were reassigned for landing in CYVR.

C-GNXT, a Cessna 172 aircraft was parked on the apron at Toronto/Buttonville Municipal (CYKZ). The aircraft had been moved from its normal parking area for snow removal, and there were no tie downs at the new location. The pilot attempted to start the engine using battery power but was unsuccessful. The parking brake was set, and the pilot attempted to hand start the engine. The brakes did not hold, and the aircraft moved forward across the apron and struck a snowbank. The pilot attempted to enter the aircraft during its movement and received minor injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged during the impact.

C-GXJA, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 aircraft operated by Air Georgian was conducting flight GGN7375 from Washington/Dulles Intl, VA (KIAD) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 3 crew members and 21 passengers on board. When approximately 30 minutes prior to landing at CYYZ, the flight crew received a FLAP FAIL caution message. The flight crew declared an emergency, completed the appropriate QRH checklist and performed a flapless landing on Runway 23 without incident.

C-GYKI, the Air Tindi Beech 200GT, operating as TIN510-M, on a medevac flight from Yellowknife (CYZF) to Inuvik (CYEV) experienced a landing gear issue on arrival at CYEV. The flight circled to the west of CYEV to troubleshoot the issue and a manual gear extension was carried out and ARFF was requested. It was determined that multiple gear indicator light bulbs had burned out; the bulbs were swapped to confirm gear down and locked. The flight landed uneventfully.

C-FESG, a privately operated Beech Duke B60 was on a cross-country flight from Canada to Scottsdale, Arizona (KSDL), with only the pilot onboard. As the aircraft was approaching its destination behind a jet, the aircraft kept the airspeed 5 to 10 knots faster than normal on the final approach. During the rollout, the left main landing gear tire blew out and directional control was lost. The aircraft veered left and exited the left side of the runway and came to in the gravel. The nose landing gear collapsed. The pilot was not injured; the aircraft sustained substantial damage. This occurrence is a data collection case for the NTSB (GAA18CA109).

C-GHTA, a Bombardier DHC-8-301 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP was conducting flight JZA8426, from Kamloops, BC (CYKA) to Calgary Intl., AB (CYYC) with 3 crew members and 23 passengers on board. During the climb, when the landing gear was selected up, the flight crew received a red warning light and the No. 2 Hydraulic ISO valve caution light illuminated. The nose gear did not retract, and the crew noticed a loss of the #2 hydraulic quantity. The crew declared a PAN PAN, extended the gear manually, and returned to CYKA. The operator’s maintenance found that one hydraulic line (p/n DSC252B4-0124) associated with the down lock actuator was leaking. The line was replaced with a temporary flex line, the hydraulic fluid was replenished, and the system tested with no faults found. The aircraft returned to service.

C-FXJF, an Embraer 170 aircraft operated by Sky Regional Airlines was conducting flight ZX 7671 from Halifax Stanfield International, NS (CYHZ) to Montreal Trudeau International, QC (CYUL). On departure from CYHZ as the aircraft climbed through 500 feet the aircraft momentarily entered severe turbulence and began an uncommanded climb up to 7000 feet per minute and it rolled to a bank angle which reached 48 degrees. The "Bank angle" aural warning sounded. The FDR data was retrieved by the company and showed wind aloft at 2000 feet at 80 knots the time of the exceedance. The aircraft control was regained and the flight uneventfully.

C-GKWW, a Messerschmitt-Bolkow-Blohm (MBB) BO 105 LS helicopter, operated by Dam Helicopters,with the pilot and 3 passengers, was conducting rescue operations approximately 15 nm WNW of Trail airport (CAD4). During a toe-in landing the helicopter contacted terrain. The landing was aborted and the helicopter flew to the company's base of operations. The helicopter sustained damage to the landing light, nose skin and structure.

C-FCMO, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Central Mountain Air was conducting flight GLR721 from Kamloops, BC (CYKA) to Prince George, BC (CYXS) with 2 flight crew members and 9 passengers on board. When climbing through 10 000 feet after the departure from CYKA, the flight crew observed the right engine torque fluctuating, followed by a loss of oil pressure. The crew shut the engine down and returned to CYKA. The operator’s maintenance found that the propeller overspeed governor gasket had torn and blown out. The gasket was replaced, and the aircraft was ground run without further issue.

C-FYJG, an Airbus 319-114 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1731 from Basseterre/Robert L. Bradshaw Intl., Saint Kitts and Nevis (TKPK) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) with 5 crew members and 105 passengers on board. During cruise, at FL390 the flight crew reported a failure associated with the hydraulic system. The crew declared a PAN PAN, then upgraded to a MAYDAY. ROU1731 subsequently landed without incident.The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and identified the check valve of the green hydraulic system leaking. Associated parts were replaced, and the aircraft returned to service.

C-GJWO , an Airbus 321-211 aircraft operated by Air Canada was conducting flight ACA119 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) to Vancouver/Vancouver Intl., BC (CYVR) with 6 crew members and 140 passengers on board. During climb the flight crew received a HYD G RSVR LO LVL ECAM message. The crew declared a PAN PAN and returned to CYYZ. The nose wheel steering, number one thrust reverser and normal landing gear extension functions were unavailable. The alternate gear extension was successfully completed by the crew, and an uneventful landing was performed with ARFF standing by.  The operator’s maintenance found the green hydraulic pressure line within the #1 pylon leaking. The line was replaced, and subsequent testing found no further faults. The aircraft was returned to service.

C-GAAT a Beechcraft 1900D aircraft operated by Exploits Valley Air Services was conducting flight EV 7793 from St John's International (CYYT) to Deer Lake (CYDF) in Newfoundland and Labrador. On approach to RWY 25 the crew selected the gear down and received an unsafe nose gear indication. The gear was recycled with no change. An overshoot was conducted, and an emergency was declared. The emergency checklist was referenced and the gear was pumped down manually. The crew received three green landing gear indications and landed uneventfully. Maintenance conducted a gear contact switch replacement and found a broken wire in the process. The gear was tested and the aircraft released to service.

C-GORN, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by Air Georgian, was conducting flight GGN7298 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to Hartford/Springfield/Bradley Intl, CT (KBDL). When ATC cleared the flight for take off from Runway 06L at CYYZ, the flight crew lined up the aircraft with the left edge of the runway and commenced the take off. During the take off roll, the left main wheel entered the grass area on the north side of the runway and struck a runway edge marker. The flight crew heard a noise and felt the aircraft pulling to the left. The take off was aborted at approximately 65 knots, the aircraft exited on to Taxiway D4 and stopped. The flight crew shut the left engine down, notified ATC of their situation and requested that the operator’s maintenance meet the aircraft to assess damage. The right engine continued to operate and all passengers remained on board. After a visual inspection, maintenance personnel advised that the aircraft could taxi back to the gate. Further examination by maintenance personnel revealed minor damage to the propeller blades and minor indentations to the left side of the fuselage, aft of the entry door. There were no reported injuries. The FDR and CVR were recovered and downloaded by TSB Engineering. The takeoff roll began at 0147:41 UTC and the aircraft stopped at 0148:46 on the taxiway. When reviewed by the TSB, the 30 min CVR contained only data from 0224:28 to 0232:13. The portion of the recording which should have captured the time period between 0201:06 and 0224:28 was blank.

C-GJOD, un appareil de type Cessna 337G exploité par Sasair, effectuait un vol local selon les règles de vol à vue à partir de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl., QC (CYQB) avec 2 membres d'équipage à bord. L'équipage de conduite a déclaré une urgence en raison d'une indication anormale du train d'atterrissage avant. L'aéronef a atterri peu après sans encombre. Il n'y a pas eu de blessés.Le personnel de l'entretien de l'exploitant de la compagnie a pu reproduire le problème au sol et les portes du train d’atterrissage ont été ajustées.

C-GKON, un De Havilland DH8-100 exploité par Jazz sous l'indicatif de vol JZA705 effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, Québec (CYZV) à destination de l'aéroport de Québec/Jean-Lesage Intl avec à son bord 3 membres d'équipages et 9 passagers. Alors que l'aéronef venait de décoller, l'équipage de conduite a observé des sautes de régime du moteur droit (P&W CAN PW120A) et un son anormal. La puissance du moteur a été réduite et une urgence a été déclarée. L'appareil est revenu se poser à CYZV sans encombre. Le même appareil avait effectué un décollage interrompu précédemment dû à une fluctuation de l'affichage numérique du couple du moteur gauche.

C-FMWV, un appareil de type Boeing 767-300 exploité par Air Canada rouge, effectuait le vol ROU1883 de Cancún/Cancún Intl., Mexico (MMUN) à Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl., QC (CYUL). ROU1883 était en approche pour CYUL quand l’équipage de conduite avait relu correctement l’autorisation d'intercepter l’approche ILS 24R. ROU1883 a dirigé vers une approche visuelle 24L de sorte qu’une perte d’espacement est survenue avec C-GYCV, un appareil de type Bombardier DHC-8-314 exploité par Provincial Airlines sous l’indicatif de vol PVL1959 en provenance de Québec/Jean Lesage Intl., QC (CYQB) lorsque la distance entre les 2 aéronefs a été réduite à 2.5 miles.

C-GAJS, un Learjet 35A exploité par Lattitude Air Ambulance effectuait un vol selon les règles de vol aux instruments de Ottawa/Macdonald-Cartier Intl., ON (CYOW) à Iqaluit, NU (CYFB) avec 2 membres d’équipage et 2 passagers à bord. Alors que l'aéronef était en approche pour la piste 34 à CYFB l'équipage de conduite a constaté que les témoins lumineux de position du train d'atterrissage ne donnaient pas la bonne indication suite à la sélection train sorti. Après plusieurs tentatives, l'équipage a procédé à une extension manuelle et a déclaré une urgence. L'atterrissage s'est déroulé sans encombre avec la présence du SLIA. Suite à l'événement, le personnel de l’entretien de l’exploitant a effectué plusieurs essais afin de reproduire l'anomalie, mais sans succès. L'appareil a été remis en service.

C-GPPS, un appareil de type Jetstream 32 exploité par Pascan effectuait le vol PSC999 de Baie-Comeau QC (CYBC) à Wabush, NL (CYWK) avec 2 membres d’équipage et 5 passagers à bord. PSC999 était en approche pour l'aéroport de CYWK, lorsque l'équipage de conduite a décidé de faire une diversion vers Mont-Joli, QC (CYYY) en raison d'un coefficient de frottement de piste qui n'était pas favorable. Durant le segment de vol vers CYYY, l'équipage de conduite a noté une consommation de carburant supérieure à celle normalement prévue. L'équipage de conduite a déclaré une situation de carburant minimum et a demandé de dérouter vers l'aéroport de Sept-Îles, QC (CYZV) où l'appareil s'est posé sans problème. Suite à une vérification auprès du fournisseur qui génère les plans de vol, une erreur au niveau de la programmation se serait glissée de sorte que la consommation horaire prévue était inférieure à la normale.

C-FNCL, a Beech 1900D aircraft operated by North Cariboo Flying Service Ltd., was conducting flight NCB1903 from Points North Landing, SK (CYNL) to Prince Albert/Glass Field, SK (CYPA).  NCB1903 waited on the runway prior to takeoff due to bird activity. After the takeoff roll, the flight crew suspected a frozen brake or anti-skid system malfunction due to blowing snow during their wait on the runway. After consulting with company maintenance, the aircraft was diverted to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl. SK (CYXE). The crew requested that ARFF be placed on standby and the aircraft landed uneventfully. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft braking system and returned the aircraft to service.

C-GOPF, a Bell 206B operated by Highland Helicopters, was conducting a moose survey near Smithers, BC, with the pilot and three passengers on board. The helicopter landed on snow in a cut block near Chapman Lake for a rest break. A few moments after the pilot and front seat passenger exited the helicopter it tipped backward and the tail rotor struck the ground, breaking the tail rotor drive shaft. There were no injuries.

C-FPON, a Bombardier DHC-8-102 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP was conducting flight JZA8291 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) to Timmins/Victor M. Power, ON (CYTS) with 3 crew members and 19 passengers on board. During cruise at 22000 feet ASL and 190 knots, the autopilot disconnected and the control column started shaking fore and aft. Airspeed was reduced to 160 knots and controls returned to normal. The crew declared an emergency, and diverted to Sudbury, ON (CYSB) where an uneventful landing was performed with ARFF standing by. The operator’s maintenance inspected the flight controls and found no faults. The stall system was checked and maintenance found the #2 stall vane heater had failed. Maintenance suspected the issue was a false stick shaker, due to the failed vane heater. The system was disabled and after a test flight no further faults were found. The #2 stall system was placed on MEL and the aircraft was returned to service. Company issued an SDR with Transport Canada (SDR20180116007).

C-FCJK, a Piper PA-28-180 aircraft operated by the Olds Didsbury Flying Association, was on a local flight from Olds/Didsbury, AB (CEA3). C-FCJK was conducting touch and go landings during the hours of darkness. Three circuits were completed and during final approach for the last landing, approximately 800 feet from the Rwy 28 threshold, the aircraft contacted power lines. Airport power was lost and the runway lighting extinguished. C-FCJK landed uneventfully. The pilot, sole occupant, was uninjured; C-FCJK received damage to the propeller, windscreen and vertical stabilizer.

4X-ELA, a Boeing 747-400 aircraft operated by El Al, was conducting flight ELY008 from New York/John F Kennedy Intl airport (KJFK) to Tel Aviv/Ben Gurion, Israel (LLBG) with 22 crew members and 404 passengers on board. While in cruise about 220nm east of Goose Bay NL, the flightcrew received a fire warning for the wheel well. An emergency was declared and 4X-ELA diverted to Goose Bay, NL (CYYR). 4X-ELA landed without further incident. The aircraft stopped on the runway and firefighters confirmed that there was no fire. An additional examination was carried out by the firefighters after the aircraft had parked. The operator’s maintenance determined the warning to be an indication problem, and released the aircraft into service.

C-GBZR, a Boeing 767-38E aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1823 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) to Honolulu/Daniel K. Inouye Intl., Hawaii (PHNL) with 8 crew members and 274 passengers on board. During climb, the flight crew selected the landing gear up, and received a GEAR DISAGREE EICAS message. The crew noticed that the left main landing gear was indicating green, with a door open indication. The aircraft climbed to 9000 feet ASL, and orbited north of CYYZ where the crew declared a PAN PAN before returning to CYYZ. The operator’s maintenance performed several cycles of the landing gear, and determined that the left main landing gear actuator was unserviceable. The actuator was replaced and subsequent cycles determined that no further fault existed.

C-FTJQ, un appareil de type Airbus 320-211 exploité par Air Canada effectuait le vol ACA402 de Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl., ON (CYYZ) à Montréal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl., QC (CYUL). ACA402 était en phase de débarquement des passagers à la porte 1 de CYUL, lorsque le pont d'embarquement s'est déplacé de sorte qu'une charnière de la porte de l'appareil a été endommagée. Une accumulation de glace sur le système de nivellement automatique du pont d'embarquement est soupçonnée. Personne n'a été blessé.

C-GGMZ, a Jazz Aviation LP DHC-8-402 aircraft operating as flight 919, was enroute to Toronto Pearson Intl (CYYZ) from Jean Lesage Intl - Quebec City (CYQB) and was instructed to hold due to weather. During the hold the #1 hydraulic system failed. The aircraft diverted to MacDonald-Cartier Intl - Ottawa (CYOW). The crew requested ARFF to be on standby and the aircraft landed uneventfully. Maintenance replaced the #1 EDP, the case drain filter, and the pressure and return filters; the aircraft was returned to service (no evidence of metal particles in the filters found).

C-GZNB, a Piper PA31 was being operated by K D Air Corporation on a VFR flight plan as flight KDC412 from Vancouver Intl (CYVR) to Qualicum Beach (CAT4). Shortly after takeoff C-GZNB was struck by lightning south of the airport. ATC initiated an emergency standby and the aircraft returned to CYVR and landed uneventfully.

The Namao Flying Club Mooney M20D, C-FHHQ, was operating on a local training flight from Villeneuve, AB (CZVL) with 1 instructor and 1 student on board. FHHQ was conducting touch and go landings on Rwy 08. During the occurrence touchdown, the landing gear collapsed and FHHQ came to rest on the runway. There were no injuries and the ELT did not activate. Company maintenance will advise TSB of findings.UPDATE 06 February 2018The operator's maintenance found the landing gear handle left bolt (AN4-22A) sheared.

C-GIAE, a Beech B100 aircraft operated by Island Express Air, was conducting a flight IAX602 from Slave Lake, AB (CYZH) to Abbotsford, BC (CYXX). During cruise, the flight crew advised ATC that they had a cracked windshield, descended to FL170, and diverted to Kamloops, BC (CYKA). The aircraft was given priority handling and landed without incident with ARFF on standby.

C-GRGO, a Bombardier DHC-8-100 aircraft operated by Canadian North Inc, was conducting flight MPE478 from Kugluktuk, NU (CYCO) to Taloyoak, NU (CYYH) with 3 crew members and 14 passengers on board. On descent through FL180 into CYYH, the flight crew noticed a haze in the cockpit that was becoming light smoke. The crew declared an emergency and continued the approach. When the aircraft was descending though 10000 feet, the smoke started to clear. The aircraft landed without incident. After landing, no source of the smoke was found. The operator's maintenance inspected the aircraft and determined the aircraft was safe to ferry to Yellowknife, NU (CYZF) for further maintenance.

The Sunwest Aviation Ltd. Beech 1900D, C-GSWB, was operating as flight CNK432 from Calgary, AB (CYYC) to Grande Prairie, AB (CYQU), with 2 crew and 2 passengers on board. Shortly after leveling off at cruise altitude one of the flight crew members became ill and the other flight crew member assumed control of the aircraft. The aircraft landed uneventfully in CYQU.

C-GGOK, a Jazz Aviation LP de Havilland DHC-8-400, was operating as flight JZA8226 from Yellowknife, NT (CYZF) to Edmonton, AB (CYEG). While climbing through 4000 feet agl from CYZF, the flight crew heard the lavatory smoke detector activate and smelled an acrid odour. The flight attendant called the flight crew to notify that there was smoke in the cabin. The flight crew donned oxygen masks, declared an emergency, closed the bleed valves and returned to CYZF. The lavatory alarm stopped prior to an uneventful landing. Company maintenance conducted engine runs and did not receive any further smoke or smell in the cabin, lavatory or cockpit.

C-FMLZ, a Boeing 767-316ER aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1715 from Bridgetown/Grantley Adams Intl., Barbados (TBPB) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 8 crew members and 275 passengers on board. ROU1715 was climbing to cruise level when the flight crew received 'C HYD QTY' and 'C PRESS' warning light. The crew actioned the QRH, however were unable to resolve the issue. The aircraft continued to destination and declared a PAN PAN while approaching CYYZ. The aircraft landed without further incident.The operator’s maintenance inspected the aircraft, found no leaks, and hydraulic reservoir levels were normal. Maintenance removed and replaced the hydraulic quantity indicator and transmitter. The aircraft was released to service.

C-FYLC, a Boeing 737-8BK aircraft operated by Sunwing, was conducting flight SWG272 from Cancún/Cancún Intl, Mexico (MMUN) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 8 crew members and 184 passengers on board. During descent to CYYZ, SWG 272 experienced a trailing edge flap asymmetry. The flight crew carried out the QRH and declared a PAN PAN. The flight landed without further incident on Runway 23. ARFF performed an inspection of the tires and brakes, and escorted the aircraft to the gate.

C-GJVY, an Airbus 319-100 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1980 from Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) to México City/Benito Juárez Intl, México (MMMX) with 5 crew members and 135 passengers on board. After the landing on Runway 05R at MMEX, ATC instructed the flight to hold short of Runway 05L. Once taxi instructions were received, the flight crew applied power to commence rolling. However, the number 2 engine experienced an uncommanded shut down, followed by associated ECAM messages. The flight crew subsequently taxied the aircraft to the assigned gate under its own power without further incident.  The operator’s maintenance entered a defect in the Aircraft Journey Log in accordance with company policy and procedures. The occurrence has been captured in the operator’s Safety Management System (SMS).

C-FDMB, a Boeing 737-8CT aircraft operated by WestJet was conducting flight WJA2425 from Cancún/Cancún Intl, Mexico (MMUN) to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ) with 6 crew members and 168 passengers on board. Following the aircraft’s arrival from MMUN, WJA2425 was stopped with the engines and APU running, on Taxi-lane 2 on the north side of Pier B at Terminal 3.  C-FPRP, a Boeing 737-8FH aircraft operated by Sunwing, was parked at Gate B13, and was being prepared to be towed to an alternate position on the infield.  A Sunwing maintenance technician was in the cockpit of C-FPRP, and the aircraft’s APU was running. Two Swissport International ground personnel were in the cab of the tow vehicle.  The tow vehicle was informed by North Apron to pushback at their discretion.  The Sunwing aircraft (under tow) began to move back and the APU contacted the right wing of the stationary Westjet aircraft.  A fire rapidly ensued.  The WestJet flight crew immediately commenced the required steps for an evacuation, and an evacuation was ordered shortly after.  The Swissport tow vehicle operator pulled the Sunwing aircraft back towards the gate to separate the two aircraft.  The slides on the WestJet aircraft were utilized on doors L1, R1 and L2, along with the over-wing exits on the left side; all passengers evacuated safely.  The maintenance technician aboard the Sunwing aircraft exited the left cockpit window using the emergency rope and received minor injuries.     ARFF arrived at the scene, and extinguished the fire. The Sunwing aircraft sustained substantial damage. Westjet is evaluating the damage to their aircraft. TSB investigators deployed to the occurrence site.

C-FEAK, a Boeing 737-86Q aircraft operated by Sunwing, was conducting flight SWG519 from Montreal/Pierre Elliott Trudeau Intl., to Cancun/Cancun Intl., Mexico (MMUN) with 6 crew members and 188 passengers on board. During cruise, SWG was instructed to make a 25 degree right turn. The flight crew then received a TCAS RA to DESCEND, to which they responded. SWG519 obtained visual contact of the conflicting traffic, and when clear, notified ATC. The flight resumed cruise at FL340, and continued to destination without further incident.

C-GHJG, a privately registered Piper PA 24-260 Comanche, was conducting a local flight from Calgary/Springbank AB, (CYBW) with 1 pilot on board. On return to CYBW, the main gear would not extend and the circuit breakers were released. Several attempts were made to extend the gear normally, and manually. The pilot requested ARFF, and elected to conduct a main gear up landing. The landing was accomplished without injury.

C-GVJZ, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Jazz Aviation LP., was conducting flight JZA574 from Vancouver Intl., BC (CYVR) to Saskatoon/John G. Diefenbaker Intl., SK (CYXE) with 4 crew members and 64 passengers on board. On approach, when the landing gear was selected down, the left main landing gear did not indicate down and locked. The flight crew initiated a missed approach. The crew referenced the QRH and performed the alternate landing gear extension procedure. The alternate indication panel in the floor showed 2 landing gears down and locked with the left main landing gear not illuminated. A satisfactory test of the anti-skid system was an indication that all 3 landing gears were, in fact, down and locked. The cabin crew prepared the cabin and moved some passengers away from the left propeller region of the cabin. The flight crew declared PAN PAN and the aircraft landed safely with ARFF on standby. The aircraft was brought to a stop on the runway to facilitate installation of the landing gear ground-locking pins prior to proceeding to the terminal. The operator's maintenance personnel replaced a corroded sensor connector. The landing gear was tested with no further faults found.

N963SW, a Bombardier CL-600-2B19 aircraft operated by SkyWest, was conducting flight SKW5533 from Winnipeg/James Armstrong Richardson Intl., MB (CYWG) to Chicago/O'Hare Intl., (KORD) with 3 crew members and 48 passengers on board. During the climb out the flaps were selected up; however, the retraction stopped at 20 degrees and the "Flap Fail" annunciator illuminated. The flight crew elected to return to Winnipeg and requested ARFF to be on standby. The subsequent landing was uneventful and the aircraft taxied to the gate. The operator's maintenance personnel replaced the Brake and Position Sensing Unit (BPSU) and the right side Flap Electronic Control Unit (FECU).

C-FMWQ, a Boeing 767-333 aircraft operated by Air Canada rouge, was conducting flight ROU1718 from Vancouver Intl, BC (CYVR) to Cancun/Cancun Intl, Mexico (MMUN) with 8 crew members and 282 passengers on board. On takeoff, the flight crew observed an audible thump, at which time all engine parameters were normal. The takeoff was continued, however after becoming airborne an abnormal odour was detected within the flight deck. Due to the possibility that a landing gear tire may have been damaged on takeoff, the landing gear was left in the extended position. The flight crew advised air traffic control, that the aircraft would be returning for an overweight landing at CYVR. The flight landed uneventfully with airport ARFF resources standing by.The operator’s maintenance conducted an inspection and found evidence of a bird strike, possibly involving a Blue Heron, on the aircraft's right engine. Minor damage was limited to the outlet guide vane (OGV) outer platform, and found to be within manufacturer’s tolerance. The aircraft was returned to service.

N494UA, an Airbus 320-232 aircraft, operated by United was conducting flight UAL1599 from Calgary Intl., Calgary, AB (CYYC) to Houston/George Bush Intl., TX (KIAH) with 5 crew members and 145 passengers on board. During taxi to the active runway, the flight crew received a smoke warning for the aft cargo hold. The crew requested ARFF, and returned to the gate where an inspection was performed. No evidence of fire was found, and it was determined to be a false alarm.  It was suspected that aircraft de-icing fluid had leaked into the APU air intake, and into the cabin through the air conditioning system, causing the smoke alarm in the aft cargo compartment. The operator’s maintenance completed a BITE test of the Smoke Detection Control Unit (SDCU) and no faults were noted. After a short delay, the flight departed CYYC with no further issues.

C-GLQN, a Bombardier DHC-8-402 aircraft operated by Porter, was conducting flight POE127 from Toronto/Billy Bishop, ON (CYTZ) to Newark/Newark Liberty Intl., NJ (KEWR) with 4 crew members and 77 passengers on board. In the climb out of CYTZ, the flight crew noticed a fluctuation of the #1 engine oil pressure. The crew actioned the QRH, and elected to return to CYTZ. During descent, the oil pressure dropped into the red area on the gauge. The crew decided to shut down the engine (Pratt & Whitney-CAN PW 150 A), and divert to Toronto/Lester B. Pearson Intl, ON (CYYZ). The aircraft landed uneventfully on Runway 24R with ARFF standing by. Upon shutdown, the flight crew inspected the engine, finding evidence of a substantial oil leak. The operator’s maintenance found the oil cap missing. The back up check valve that prevents oil from leaking out when the cap is missing also failed, and as a result the engine was depleted of oil.
